1/Day Each: [[/item .Ct8BsfnckY97Z2f5]]{Comprehend Languages}, [[/item .zR16qsbYYWFCioKb]]{Zone of Truth}

Message.name: Message
Message.description:
You point toward a creature within range and whisper a message. The target (and only the target) hears the message and can reply in a whisper that only you can hear.

You can cast this spell through solid objects if you are familiar with the target and know it is beyond the barrier. Magical silence; 1 foot of stone, metal, or wood; or a thin sheet of lead blocks the spell.

Comprehend Languages.name: Comprehend Languages
Comprehend Languages.description: For the duration, you understand the literal meaning of any language that you hear or see signed. You also understand any written language that you see, but you must be touching the surface on which the words are written. It takes about 1 minute to read one page of text. This spell doesn't decode symbols or secret messages.

Zone of Truth.name: Zone of Truth
Zone of Truth.description:
You create a magical zone that guards against deception in a 15-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range. Until the spell ends, a creature that enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, a creature can't speak a deliberate lie while in the radius. You know whether a creature succeeds or fails on this save.

An affected creature is aware of the spell and can avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such a creature can be evasive yet must be truthful.

Corvana Vortest.biographyprivate:
The Signborn mage [[lookup @name]] has occupied Vortest Tower on the southeastern edge of the Golden Flats as long as she's been alive, having inherited the curious estate from her late parents. Indeed, House Vortest has been charged with the protection of the tower and its secrets for generations, stretching back to the time of the Forsaken War — when Daemos fought Daemos amdist the lightless realms of Signara. The nature of Corvana's inheritance and her arcane pedigree are rather surreptitious, and the cause of much speculation among other citizens of the Arctus Plateau.

Occasionally, those in search of abstruse answers to cabalistic questions will seek out [[lookup @name]] for spellcasting services. These would-be patrons are met with a variety of receptions, for Lady Vortest's agendas are ultimately known only to her and the Daemos @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.3ZDcyUW0ydYE84rj]{Nalgomith}, whom she serves in perpetuity. Despite the responsibilities of her birthright (or perhaps because of them), Corvana regards her duty with a healthy measure of skepticism, a trait which has only earned the mage a greater measure of respect from her Daemos lord.

Personality

A life of relative solitude has contributed to Corvana's eccentric tastes and cloistered personality, which are marked by measured ambition and unbridled perfectionism; and while she takes everything a bit too seriously, Corvana does enjoy conversation wrought with dry humor. She's her own worst enemy when it comes to peace of mind, and is often occupied with the memory of moments past.

Connections

Corvana Vortest is a covert operative allegiant to Nalgomith, the Daemos responsible for the creation of the Wirrun and a key character in the Forsaken War. One of Nalgomith's chief rivals in this conflict was another Daemos known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.aTy7db5ZGUnNDVL4]{Kerastes}, the Clandestine Arbiter, whose spheres of influence are Corruption and Secrecy. In the final days of the Forsaken War, House Vortest was charged with the protection of one of Nalgomith's most hallowed artifacts: a matrix of arcane knowledge known as the @UUID[Item.Qy8YeWMH8PmAxyS5]{Orphic Reliquary}.

Corvana's progenitors subsequently fled to the surface of Ember, where they might hide the artifact away from the prying eyes of Kerastes and his minions. Thus, the Orphic Reliquary has remained hidden for countless generations. To this day, Corvana Vortest guards the reliquary from the extraplanar confines of Vortest Tower — which is tethered to Signara itself via powerful Daemos magic.

Phrases

Information is a commodity we can't afford to waste.

Not for all the lore in Signara …

My ambitions are mine alone.
Corvana Vortest.biographypublic:
You regard a lithe woman with pale blue skin clad in the esoteric robes of a scholar. Her bald head is crowned with a pair of tall, curving horns that betray her Signborn heritage, as do the two ethereal limbs alongside her physical arms. Her corporeal right hand holds a wand made of crystal and silver; meanwhile, her spectral hands cradle the dog-eared pages of a leather-bound grimoire in search of some abstruse knowledge. There's a disarming, otherworldly elegance in the woman's gaze as she regards you with equal measures of suspicion and interest. Her crimson eyes are discerning, and her arms are inked in cryptic occult symbols. She is at once both alluring and intimidating, replete with mystery.

[[lookup @name]] is an eccentric mage with Signaran roots who lives in relative seclusion among the people of the Golden Flats. Well-learned and experienced in the ways of wizardry, Vortest's hermetic lifestyle is a result of her mysterious past — which persists as one of the Arctus Plateau's best kept secrets. Those who seek out Lady Vortest for her spellcasting services are known to approach Vortest Tower with fair amounts of hesitance and circumspection. Vortest's demeanor is said to be as fickle as the light of Ember's moons, but those who know her best understand this is simply a ruse to obscure her acute and calmly-measured focus.

Liestra Grann.name: Liestra Grann

Mace.name: Mace
Mace.descriptionpublic: A one-handed blunt weapon that features a heavy head, typically forged of metal, which converts the momentum of its wielder's swing into a bone-shattering impact.

Liestra's Bracer of Appraisal.name: Liestra's Bracer of Appraisal
Liestra's Bracer of Appraisal.descriptionprivate: An invested user of this bracer can activate its enchanment to cause it to unfold into a fully functional @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.jewelersPortable]{Jeweler's Portable Workbench}, and gain @Advantage[2] while using these tools for the purposes of appraising the value of an item.
Liestra's Bracer of Appraisal.descriptionpublic: This enchanted bracer is fitted with implements like clockwork calipers and tweezers, arcane spectroscopes, and a phantasmal scale.

Loupe.name: Loupe
Loupe.descriptionprivate: Although it has a very short range of focus (10 inches), this masterwork loupe provides @Advantage[2] on skill checks made to appraise items of value (like gemstones, art, and currency) or skill checks made to verify documents.
Loupe.descriptionpublic: Objects viewed through a loupe are magnified to twice their size.

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.descriptionpublic: Crafted from thick, boiled leather hardened into panels or a cuirass, leather armor offers lightweight protection ideal for scouts, rogues, and lightly armed skirmishers.

Kivahr Lineage.name: Kivahr Lineage
Kivahr Lineage.description:
Your body is strengthened with the lineage of giants. Your mind and your body work in harmony to solve problems and withstand physical strain.

You gain a bonus to your Fortitude and Willpower defenses equal to your Level divided by 4.
Kivahr Lineage.actiondesc:
You engage your supernatural ability to harmonize your mind and body. You enter a trance-like state which provides the following benefits at the start of your Turn.

  • You gain +1 Focus.

  • If your Morale is higher than your Health, you transfer up to your Presence ability score reducing Morale and gaining Health.

  • If your Health is higher than your Morale, you transfer up to your Toughness ability score, reducing Health and gaining Morale.

These transfers will not cause any resource to exceed it's maximum value.

Safecracker.name: Safecracker
Safecracker.description: You are skilled in the arts of disarming traps and picking locks. You gain +1 Boon on Stealth checks to disable a device or open a lock.

Diversionist.name: Diversionist
Diversionist.description: You specialize in using subterfuge to distract or trick your opponent during combat.
Diversionist.actiondesc: You make a Deception based Skill Attack against the Willpower defense of a target within 30 feet which can see or hear you. On a success, the target loses 1 Focus.

Skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
Skirmisher.description: You are adept at entering and exiting the fray. When moving out of the Engagement radius of an enemy, that enemy has 2 Banes to any Disengagement Strike against you.

Preternatural Instinct.name: Preternatural Instinct
Preternatural Instinct.description: Your quickness of mind and body are equally impressive. You gain +2 Boons to all Initiative checks.

Jeweler's Toolkit.name: Jeweler's Toolkit
Jeweler's Toolkit.descriptionpublic: A leather-bound wooden kitbag. Contains files, calipers, a small grindstone, polishing compounds and rags, and an assortment of inexpensive settings. The case can unfold completely to provide a smooth work surface.

Blue Gemstone Choker.name: Blue Gemstone Choker
Blue Gemstone Choker.descriptionprivate:
This necklace provides a bonus to Armor defense equal to the minimum of its Quality and Enchantment bonuses.

  • Fine quality and Minor enchantment: +1 Armor

  • Superior quality and Major enchantment: +2 Armor

  • Masterwork quality and Legendary enchantment: +3 Armor
Blue Gemstone Choker.descriptionpublic: The smoky blue gemstone that adorns this choker necklace seems to perpetually swirl within like the winds of Mayis, the Tempest Moon.

Scrivener's Toolkit.name: Scrivener's Toolkit
Scrivener's Toolkit.descriptionpublic: A leather-bound wooden kitbag. Contains a waxed document pouch for keeping papers dry, a packet of sealing wax, several quills and inks, and a flat wooden board to use as a writing surface.

Healing Tonic.name: Healing Tonic
Healing Tonic.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to gradually close wounds and improve bodily health.
Healing Tonic.actiondesc:
Immediately, and at the beginning of each of the next 5 Rounds, recover an amount of Health dependent on the quality of the tonic.

  • Shoddy - Heals 2 Health each Round

  • Standard - Heals 4 Health each Round

  • Fine - Heals 8 Health each Round

  • Superior - Heals 16 Health each Round

  • Masterwork - Heals 32 Health each Round

Rallying Tonic.name: Rallying Tonic
Rallying Tonic.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to gradually fortify the psyche and improve morale.
Rallying Tonic.actiondesc:
Immediately, and at the beginning of each of the next 5 Rounds, recover an amount of Morale dependent on the quality of the tonic.

  • Shoddy - Heals 2 Morale each Round

  • Standard - Heals 4 Morale each Round

  • Fine - Heals 8 Morale each Round

  • Superior - Heals 16 Morale each Round

  • Masterwork - Heals 32 Morale each Round

Diplomacy Journeyman.name: Diplomacy Journeyman
Diplomacy Journeyman.description: You gain the Journeyman rank in the Diplomacy skill, providing a +1 Skill Bonus.

Intimidation Novice.name: Intimidation Novice
Intimidation Novice.description:
You understand the fundamentals of how threats and coercion can achieve desired outcomes. You gain the Novice rank in the Intimidation skill and are no longer considered Untrained in that skill.

You know how to use simple displays of violence or overt threats to get others to follow your lead, but you aren't very subtle.

Athletics Novice.name: Athletics Novice
Athletics Novice.description:
You have received training in basic athletics. You gain the Novice rank in the Athletics skill and are no longer considered Untrained in that skill.

You know whether a surface can support your weight or not, how to find handholds while climbing, and how to distribute your weight for buoyancy when swimming. You know how to run for distance, and how to pace yourself to avoid exhaustion.

Society Novice.name: Society Novice
Society Novice.description:
You have learned the fundamental building blocks of Society, the mores, beliefs, history and politics which directly inform the growth of culture. You gain the Novice rank in the Society skill and are no longer considered Untrained in that skill.

You understand that history and politics contribute prominently to the way decisions are made at the highest and lowest levels of society, and how tradition frequently informs subgroups of society to place them in opposition to one another.

Liestra Grann.biographyprivate:
@ref[name] spends her days making a good living by orchestrating the trade of Shent and Varùn artifacts (alongside an array of illicit goods and services, which she only offers to vetted clientele). Her Understory storefront in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} (the Long Haul) offers a wide array of standard adventuring equipment and exploration gear, and serves as a perfect facade for her more clandestine dealings.

After an adventurous youth in Ordain, this Skybrush native focused her attention on the Wedgelands foothills near her hometown, where the ruins of ancient giantfolk are ripe for excavation (and the provincial locals were overdue for a good fleecing). Her deals aren't always fair; and neither is her sense of loyalty. Liestra has operated the Long Haul for the better part of ten years, and only occasionally takes a leave of absence in pursuit of new treasures to purloin.

Personality

Liestra aims to make enough wealth to expand her business ventures beyond Skybrush, including eventual plans for a storefront location in Ordain. She keeps relatively late hours, full of revelry and abandon or extreme focus on her work. Liestra would rather kick someone out of her shop than suffer their insults, and often curses in Pathward under her breath when frustrated or surprised. She has a soft spot for rare sweets like Ordani candies and seasonal Arcturian confections, and loves a good dare.

Connections

Opportunity led an adolescent Liestra from Skybrush to Ordain, where time spent galavanting with local street gangs was balanced alongside hours of practical study. One notable caper — in which Liestra attempted to steal a prized antique from the overstuffed home of a notoriously reclusive collector — ended with the young thief in manacles at the hands of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain}. The Drakon known as @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist} was instrumental in her release, and she owes the aged warrior a debt to this very day.

Liestra also maintains several contacts within @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{The Anachraenum} for the sale and distribution of rare artifacts. And the storied artificer @UUID[Actor.gBXPA4AerLzwSbi6]{Janix Mance} of Ordain endures as a lifelong friend.

Phrases

A penny for my thoughts?

Everything's negotiable.

Skybrush is no place for soft hands and sad hearts.
Liestra Grann.biographypublic: @ref[name] is a headstrong Arcturian pawn broker known for her witty banter and ability to suss out a killer deal. Standing 6 feet 9 inches tall, Liestra is a lean and muscular tradeswoman whose amber-hued eyes issue a commanding gaze and whose allusive grin betrays her penchant for snark.
Liestra Grann.biographyappearance: A muscular Kivahr femme clad in in loose layers of cloth and leather leans upon the wall with casual composure. A side-parted bob of tawny hair hangs just below her chin as she scrutinizes some curious trinket using a small eyepiece. A wry, expressive grin rises to meet you moments before she sizes you up with amber-colored eyes, and you can't help but spot a stony ersatz mace strapped to her side. It's quite evident she means business.

Mica Valaston.name: Mica Valaston

Skybrush Constable's Key.name: Skybrush Constable's Key
Skybrush Constable's Key.descriptionpublic: This simple bronze key opens the locked cells of the Blockhouse gaol in Skybrush, as well as the evidence locker.

Studded Leather Armor.name: Studded Leather Armor
Studded Leather Armor.descriptionpublic: A base of leather reinforced with small metal studs or riveted plates, this armor strikes a balance between mobility and modest protection against slashes.

Healing Elixir.name: Healing Elixir
Healing Elixir.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to rapidly close wounds and improve bodily health.
Healing Elixir.actiondesc:
Immediately recover an amount of Health dependant on the quality of the elixir.

  • Shoddy - Immediately heals 6 Health.

  • Standard - Immediately heals 12 Health.

  • Fine - Immediately heals 24 Health.

  • Superior - Immediately heals 48 Health.

  • Masterwork - Immediately heals 96 Health.

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.descriptionpublic: The shortsword is a straight-bladed weapon which is nimble to wield and quick to strike in close combat. It features a crossguard ideal for parrying incoming blows.

Heavy Crossbow.name: Heavy Crossbow
Heavy Crossbow.descriptionpublic: A powerful, steel-limbed crossbow requiring a crank or lever to draw, it delivers devastating bolts capable of punching through armor or pinning enemies to walls.

Hulg'run Lineage.name: Hulg'run Lineage
Hulg'run Lineage.description:
You are immune to the Asleep condition.

You can commune with the essence of Ember when you Rest. If you are resting upon solid ground, you do not require sleep and can remain conscious. You may not engage in any strenuous activity in order to gain the benefits of the rest.
Hulg'run Lineage.actiondesc:
Your form temporarily calcifies, providing enhanced protection against physical blows.

  • You gain resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage equal to your Level + 1.

  • Your Stride is reduced by -2.

  • You are immune to the Prone condition and cannot be involuntarily moved.

Intercept.name: Intercept
Intercept.description: You protect your allies, intercepting blows that might otherwise be directed towards your companions.
Intercept.actiondesc:
You intercept the path of an enemy which enters your Engagement radius, immediatly moving up to your Stride to interpose yourself and block their path.

If the enemy moves out of your Engagement radius or attacks any other creature during their turn, you may make a Disengagement Strike against them.

Projectile Weapon Training.name: Projectile Weapon Training
Projectile Weapon Training.description: You have a basic education in archery and other projectile weaponry. You are no longer treated as Untrained with weapons in the Projectile categories.
Projectile Weapon Training.actiondesc: You can loose a shot under pressure, although with decreased accuracy. You perform a Strike that is Difficult, but has a reduced Action cost.

Preparedness.name: Preparedness
Preparedness.description: You seem to always be prepared for the moment at hand. You may sacrifice your free movement for the Round to instead equip an Item from your inventory without spending any Action points.

Unarmed Combat Training.name: Unarmed Combat Training
Unarmed Combat Training.description: You are familiar with basic martial arts and hand-to-hand combat. You know how to subdue or restrain opponents using your physical Strength. You are Trained with weapons in the Unarmed category.
Unarmed Combat Training.actiondesc: You attempt to physically restrain or subdue an opponent. Perform a Athletics skill attack against an adjacent target. If successful, both you and your target are @Condition[restrained] for 1 Round.

Lantern.name: Lantern
Lantern.descriptionpublic: An oil-burning or magically illuminated lantern that sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius.

Rope.name: Rope
Rope.descriptionpublic: A 30' length of plant-fibre rope that can be used to assist climbing or for many other purposes.

Expanded Toolbelt.name: Expanded Toolbelt
Expanded Toolbelt.descriptionpublic:
An expanded toolbelt in the form of a utility belt, a bandolier, or an array of pockets stitched into your equipment.

This item provides a number of additional Toolbelt slots according to its quality tier:

  • Standard: +1 Toolbelt slot

  • Fine: +2 Toolbelt slots

  • Superior: +3 Toolbelt slots

  • Masterwork: +4 Toolbelt slots

Whistle.name: Whistle
Whistle.descriptionpublic: An instrument made from carved wood or bone that, when blown into, produces a single shrill sound that can be heard over long distances. Often used by hunters and fishers to signal one another when in the wilderness or at sea.

Intimidator.name: Intimidator
Intimidator.description: You specialize in exerting your intimidating presence to break the morale of your foes.
Intimidator.actiondesc: You physically intimidate an enemy that is within your engagement range, performing an Intimidation skill attack against your target. On a success they sustain Void damage to Morale.

Mark Prey.name: Mark Prey
Mark Prey.description: You fire a special shot which deals no damage, but explodes in luminous powder clearly marking your target.
Mark Prey.actiondesc: You Strike using a special shot. If your attack is successful the target is Exposed for the next 3 Turns.

Pinning Shot.name: Pinning Shot
Pinning Shot.description: You fire a tactically placed shot to pin your target against a nearby surface.
Pinning Shot.actiondesc: You Strike from distance. The attack is Difficult, however if your target is it it becomes Restrained until the end of their next Turn.

Disarming Strike.name: Disarming Strike
Disarming Strike.description: A martial technique designed to disarm your opponent, forcing them to drop an object held in one of their hands.
Disarming Strike.actiondesc: You make a Strike against a the Reflex defense of a single target. The technique is Difficult to perform and deals reduced damage. If successful, the target's mainhand weapon is Dropped.

Mica Valaston.biographyprivate:
Constable Mica Valaston (they/them) is Skybrush's sole authority in law enforcement, and maintains an office at the center of town within a building known as the Blockhouse — a two-story edifice that houses the gaol, along with an upstairs apartment for the Constable themself. This cynical Arcturian gendarme is a former soldier who served in the ranks of Ordain's militia, and is proud to apply the teachings of their heady cosmopolitan years in the remote setting of the Rustvar hinterlands.

Personality

Mica Valaston is straightforward, cynical, and proud. While kind and forthcoming, they are generally apprehensive of strangers — especially considering the latter day supernatural harrowing of Skybrush. And trust is something that must be earned, according to Constable Valaston, who prizes the concepts of truth and honor more than most.

Connections

A former soldier in service to Ordain's active militia, Mica maintains a handful of solid connections to old friends and colleagues in Ordain. But the Constable's cynical disposition and remote station have also led to a somewhat lonely life, where the comings-and-goings of small town folk offer little in the way of companionship for self-reliant outsiders like Valaston. In a certain sense, they see themselves as an older sibling for the people of Skybrush, who never seem to know better.

Phrases

If you're thinking about causing any trouble, think again.

Don't get ahead of yourself…

That's Skybrush for you.
Mica Valaston.biographypublic: Mica Valaston is the obdurate and cynical Constable of Skybrush. Mica is a gruff warrior whose no-nonsense disposition readies them to exercise the duties of their station at a moment's notice.
Mica Valaston.biographyappearance: You behold the skeptical countenance of a thirty-something Hulg'run warrior clad in studded leather armor, a ring of keys around their belt. Their hand hovers just above the hilt of a sheathed longsword, and they regard you with a healthy look of suspicion.

Kali Andrella.name: Kali Andrella

Fire Bolt.name: Fire Bolt
Fire Bolt.description:
You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell ignites if it isn't being worn or carried.

This spell's damage increases by 1d10 when you reach 5th level (2d10), 11th level (3d10), and 17th level (4d10).

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
This spell repairs a single break or tear in an object you touch, such as a broken chain link, two halves of a broken key, a torn cloak, or a leaking wineskin. As long as the break or tear is no larger than 1 foot in any dimension, you mend it, leaving no trace of the former damage.

This spell can physically repair a magic item or construct, but the spell can't restore magic to such an object.

Spike Growth.name: Spike Growth
Spike Growth.description:
The ground in a 20-foot radius centered on a point within range twists and sprouts hard spikes and thorns. The area becomes difficult terrain for the Duration. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes 2d4 piercing damage for every 5 feet it travels.

The transformation of the ground is camouflaged to look natural. Any creature that can't see the area at the time the spell is cast must make a Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC to recognize the terrain as hazardous before entering it.

Create Food and Water.name: Create Food and Water
Create Food and Water.description: You create 45 pounds of food and 30 gallons of water on the ground or in containers within range, enough to sustain up to fifteen humanoids or five steeds for 24 hours. The food is bland but nourishing, and spoils if uneaten after 24 hours. The water is clean and doesn't go bad.

Plant Growth.name: Plant Growth
Plant Growth.description:
This spell channels vitality into plants within a specific area. There are two possible uses for the spell, granting either immediate or long-term benefits.

If you cast this spell using 1 action, choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot radius centered on that point become thick and overgrown. A creature moving through the area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves.

You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

If you cast this spell over 8 hours, you enrich the land. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 1 year. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested.

Fabricate.name: Fabricate
Fabricate.description:
You convert raw materials into products of the same material. For example, you can fabricate a wooden bridge from a clump of trees, a rope from a patch of hemp, and clothes from flax or wool.

Choose raw materials that you can see within range. You can fabricate a Large or smaller object (contained within a 10-foot cube, or eight connected 5-foot cubes), given a sufficient quantity of raw material. If you are working with metal, stone, or another mineral substance, however, the fabricated object can be no larger than Medium (contained within a single 5-foot cube). The quality of Objects made by the spell is commensurate with the quality of the raw materials.

Creatures or Magic Items can't be created or transmuted by this spell. You also can't use it to create items that ordinarily require a high degree of craftsmanship, such as jewelry, Weapons, glass, or armor, unless you have proficiency with the type of artisan's tools used to craft such Objects.

Creation.name: Creation
Creation.description:
You pull wisps of shadow material from the Shadowfell to create a nonliving object of vegetable matter within 'range': soft goods, rope, wood, or something similar. You can also use this spell to create mineral objects such as stone, crystal, or metal. The object created must be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and the object must be of a form and material that you have seen before.

The duration depends on the object's material. If the object is composed of multiple materials, use the shortest duration.

  • Vegetable matter - 1 day
  • Stone or crystal - 12 hours
  • Precious metals - 1 hour
  • Gems - 10 minutes
  • Adamantine or mithral - 1 minute

Using any material created by this spell as another spell's material component causes that spell to fail.

Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the cube increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 5th.

The Kali Cutter.name: The Kali Cutter
The Kali Cutter.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

A short but wide metal blade mounted to a wooden hilt. Used primarily to cut back unwanted plant growth and to shovel dirt, the metal is stained by soil remnants that cannot be fully washed away. Can be wielded as a weapon if needed.

Web.name: Web
Web.description:
You conjure a mass of thick, sticky webbing at a point of your choice within range. The webs fill a 20-foot cube from that point for the Duration. The webs are difficult terrain and lightly obscure their area.

If the webs aren't anchored between two solid masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across a floor, wall, or ceiling, the conjured web collapses on itself, and the spell ends at the start of your next turn. Webs layered over a flat surface have a depth of 5 feet.

Each creature that starts its turn in the webs or that enters them during its turn must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is Restrained as long as it remains in the webs or until it breaks free.

A creature Restrained by the webs can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer Restrained.

The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot cube of webs exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing 2d4 fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in the fire.

Glyph of Warding.name: Glyph of Warding
Glyph of Warding.description:
When you cast this spell, you inscribe a glyph that later unleashes a magical effect. You inscribe it either on a surface (such as a table or a section of floor or wall) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book, a scroll, or a treasure chest) to conceal the glyph. The glyph can cover an area no larger than 10 feet in diameter. If the surface or object is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the glyph is broken, and the spell ends without being triggered.

The glyph is nearly invisible and requires a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to be found.

You decide what triggers the glyph when you cast the spell. For glyphs inscribed on a surface, the most typical triggers include touching or standing on the glyph, removing another object covering the glyph, approaching within a certain distance of the glyph, or manipulating the object on which the glyph is inscribed. For glyphs inscribed within an object, the most common triggers include opening that object, approaching within a certain distance of the object, or seeing or reading the glyph. Once a glyph is triggered, this spell ends.

You can further refine the trigger so the spell activates only under certain circumstances or according to physical characteristics (such as height or weight), creature kind (for example, the ward could be set to affect aberrations or drow), or alignment. You can also set conditions for creatures that don't trigger the glyph, such as those who say a certain password.

When you inscribe the glyph, choose explosive runes or a spell glyph.

Explosive Runes. When triggered, the glyph erupts with magical energy in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on the glyph. The sphere spreads around corners. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes [[/r 5d8]] acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage on a failed saving throw (your choice when you create the glyph), or half as much damage on a successful one.

Spell Glyph. You can store a prepared spell of 3rd level or lower in the glyph by casting it as part of creating the glyph. The spell must target a single creature or an area. The spell being stored has no immediate effect when cast in this way. When the glyph is triggered, the stored spell is cast. If the spell has a target, it targets the creature that triggered the glyph. If the spell affects an area, the area is centered on that creature. If the spell summons hostile creatures or creates harmful objects or traps, they appear as close as possible to the intruder and attack it. If the spell requires concentration, it lasts until the end of its full duration.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage of an explosive runes glyph increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd. If you create a spell glyph, you can store any spell of up to the same level as the slot you use for the glyph of warding.

Alarm.name: Alarm
Alarm.description:
You set an alarm against unwanted intrusion. Choose a door, a window, or an area within range that is no larger than a 20-foot cube. Until the spell ends, an alarm alerts you whenever a Tiny or larger creature touches or enters the warded area. When you cast the spell, you can designate creatures that won't set off the alarm. You also choose whether the alarm is mental or audible.

A mental alarm alerts you with a ping in your mind if you are within 1 mile of the warded area. This ping awakens you if you are sleeping.

An audible alarm produces the sound of a hand bell for 10 seconds within 60 feet.

Entangle.name: Entangle
Entangle.description:
Grasping weeds and vines sprout from the ground in a 20-foot square starting from a point within range. For the Duration, these Plants turn the ground in the area into difficult terrain.

A creature in the area when you cast the spell must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be &Reference[Restrained] by the entangling Plants until the spell ends. A creature restrained by the plants can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself.

When the spell ends, the conjured Plants wilt away.

Goodberry.name: Goodberry
Goodberry.description:
Up to ten berries appear in your hand and are infused with magic for the duration. A creature can use its action to eat one berry. Eating a berry restores 1 hit point, and the berry provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day.

The berries lose their potency if they have not been consumed within 24 hours of the casting of this spell.

Locate Animals or Plants.name: Locate Animals or Plants
Locate Animals or Plants.description: Describe or name a specific kind of beast or plant. Concentrating on the voice of nature in your surroundings, you learn the direction and distance to the closest creature or plant of that kind within 5 miles, if any are present.

Fear.name: Fear
Fear.description:
You project a phantasmal image of a creature's worst fears. Each creature in a 30-foot cone must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or drop whatever it is holding and become &Reference[Frightened] for the duration.

While Frightened by this spell, a creature must take the Dash action and move away from you by the safest available route on each of its turns, unless there is nowhere to move. If the creature ends its turn in a location where it doesn't have line of sight to you, the creature can make a Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, the spell ends for that creature.

Speak with Plants.name: Speak with Plants
Speak with Plants.description:
You imbue Plants within 30 feet of you with limited sentience and animation, giving them the ability to communicate with you and follow your simple commands. You can question plants about events in the spell's area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, weather, and other circumstances.

You can also turn difficult terrain caused by Plant Growth (such as thickets and undergrowth) into ordinary terrain that lasts for the Duration. Or you can turn ordinary terrain where Plants are present into difficult terrain that lasts for the duration, causing vines and branches to hinder pursuers, for example.

Plants might be able to perform other tasks on your behalf, at the DM's discretion. The spell doesn't enable Plants to uproot themselves and move about, but they can freely move branches, tendrils, and stalks.

If a plant creature is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a Common language, but you gain no magical ability to influence it.

This spell can cause the plants created by the Entangle spell to release a Restrained creature.

Private Sanctum.name: Private Sanctum
Private Sanctum.description:
You make an area within range magically secure. The area is a cube that can be as small as 5 feet to as large as 100 feet on each side. The spell lasts for the Duration or until you use an action to dismiss it.

When you cast the spell, you decide what sort of security the spell provides, choosing any or all of the following properties:

  • Sound can't pass through the barrier at the edge of the warded area.
  • The barrier of the warded area appears dark and foggy, preventing vision (including darkvision) through it.
  • Sensors created by Divination spells can't appear inside the protected area or pass through the barrier at its perimeter.
  • Creatures in the area can't be targeted by divination spells.
  • Nothing can Teleport into or out of the warded area.
  • Planar Travel is blocked within the warded area.

Casting this spell on the same spot every day for a year makes this effect permanent.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can increase the size of the cube by 100 feet for each slot level beyond 4th. Thus you could protect a cube that can be up to 200 feet on one side by using a spell slot of 5th level.

Guidance.name: Guidance
Guidance.description: You touch one willing creature. Once before the spell ends, the target can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to one ability check of its choice. It can roll the die before or after making the ability check. The spell then ends.

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description:
Whispering to the spirits of Nature, you create one of the following Effects within range:

  • You create a tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, Falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.
  • You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.
  • You create an Instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as Falling leaves, a puff of wind, the sound of a small animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot cube.
  • You instantly light or snuff out a Candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Produce Flame.name: Produce Flame
Produce Flame.description:
A flickering flame appears in your hand. The flame remains there for the Duration and harms neither you nor your Equipment. The flame sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. The spell ends if you dismiss it as an action or if you cast it again.

You can also Attack with the flame, although doing so ends the spell. When you cast this spell, or as an action on a later turn, you can hurl the flame at a creature within 30 feet of you. Make a ranged spell Attack. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 fire damage.

This spell's damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

Detect Poison and Disease.name: Detect Poison and Disease
Detect Poison and Disease.description:
For the duration, you can sense the presence and location of poisons, poisonous creatures, and diseases within 30 feet of you. You also identify the kind of poison, poisonous creature, or disease in each case.

The spell can penetrate most barriers, but it is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

Enhance Ability.name: Enhance Ability
Enhance Ability.description:
You touch a creature and bestow upon it a magical enhancement. Choose one of the following effects; the target gains that effect until the spell ends.

  • Bear's Endurance. The target has advantage on Constitution Checks. It also gains 2d6 Temporary Hit Points, which are lost when the spell ends.
  • Bull's Strength. The target has advantage on Strength Checks, and his or her carrying capacity doubles.
  • Cat's Grace. The target has advantage on Dexterity Checks. It also doesn't take damage from Falling 20 feet or less if it isn't Incapacitated.
  • Eagle's Splendor. The target has advantage on Charisma Checks.
  • Fox's Cunning. The target has advantage on Intelligence Checks.
  • Owl's Wisdom. The target has advantage on Wisdom Checks.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Gust of Wind.name: Gust of Wind
Gust of Wind.description:
A line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide blasts from you in a direction you choose for the spell's duration. Each creature that starts its turn in the line must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from you in a direction following the line.

Any creature in the line must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving closer to you.

The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles, torches, and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to extinguish them.

As a bonus action on each of your turns before the spell ends, you can change the direction in which the line blasts from you.

Black Tentacles.name: Black Tentacles
Black Tentacles.description:
Squirming, ebony tentacles fill a 20-foot square on ground that you can see within range. For the Duration, these tentacles turn the ground in the area into difficult terrain.

When a creature enters the affected area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, the creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage and be &Reference[Restrained] by the tentacles until the spell ends. A creature that starts its turn in the area and is already Restrained by the tentacles takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage.

A creature Restrained by the tentacles can use its action to make a Strength or Dexterity check (its choice) against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself.

Control Water.name: Control Water
Control Water.description:
Until the spell ends, you control any freestanding water inside an area you choose that is a cube up to 100 feet on a side. You can choose from any of the following effects when you cast this spell. As an action on your turn, you can repeat the same effect or choose a different one.

Flood. You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20 feet. If the area includes a shore, the flooding water spills over onto dry land, instead create a 20-foot tall wave that travels from one side of the area to the other and then crashes down. Any Huge or smaller vehicles in the wave's path are carried with it to the other side. Any Huge or smaller vehicles struck by the wave have a 25 percent chance of capsizing.

The water level remains elevated until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. If this effect produced a wave, the wave repeats on the start of your next turn while the flood effect lasts.

Part Water. You cause water in the area to move apart and create a trench. The trench extends across the spell's area, and the separated water forms a wall to either side. The trench remains until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. The water then slowly fills in the trench over the course of the next round until the normal water level is restored.

Redirect Flow. You cause flowing water in the area to move in a direction you choose, even if the water has to flow over obstacles, up walls, or in other unlikely directions. The water in the area moves as you direct it, but once it moves beyond the spell's area, it resumes its flow based on the terrain conditions. The water continues to move in the direction you chose until the spell ends or you choose a different effect.

Whirlpool. This effect requires a body of water at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep. You cause a whirlpool to form in the center of the area. The whirlpool forms a vortex that is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet tall. Any creature or object in the water and within 25 feet of the vortex is pulled 10 feet toward it. A creature can swim away from the vortex by making a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC.

When a creature enters the vortex for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage and is caught in the vortex until the spell ends. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage, and isn't caught in the vortex. A creature caught in the vortex can use its action to try to swim away from the vortex as described above, but has disadvantage on the Strength (Athletics) check to do so.

The first time each turn that an object enters the vortex, the object takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage; this damage occurs each round it remains in the vortex.

Awaken.name: Awaken
Awaken.description:
After spending the casting time tracing magical pathways within a precious gemstone, you touch a Huge or smaller beast or plant. The target must have either no Intelligence score or an Intelligence of 3 or less. The target gains an Intelligence of 10. The target also gains the ability to speak one language you know. If the target is a plant, it gains the ability to move its limbs, roots, vines, creepers, and so forth, and it gains senses similar to a human's. Your DM chooses statistics appropriate for the awakened plant, such as the statistics for the awakened shrub or the awakened tree.

The awakened beast or plant is charmed by you for 30 days or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it. When the charmed condition ends, the awakened creature chooses whether to remain friendly to you, based on how you treated it while it was charmed.

Commune with Nature.name: Commune with Nature
Commune with Nature.description:
You briefly become one with nature and gain knowledge of the surrounding territory. In the outdoors, the spell gives you knowledge of the land within 3 miles of you. In caves and other natural underground settings, the radius is limited to 300 feet. The spell doesn't function where nature has been replaced by construction, such as in dungeons and towns.

You instantly gain knowledge of up to three facts of your choice about any of the following subjects as they relate to the area:

  • terrain and bodies of water
  • prevalent plants, minerals, animals, or peoples
  • powerful celestials, fey, fiends, elementals, or undead
  • influence from other planes of existence
  • buildings

For example, you could determine the location of powerful undead in the area, the location of major sources of safe drinking water, and the location of any nearby towns.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor, and a protective magical force surrounds it until the spell ends. The target's base AC becomes 13 + its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends if the target dons armor or if you dismiss the spell as an action.

Agrimagical Artifact.name: Agrimagical Artifact
Agrimagical Artifact.description:
Once per day, an agrimage can touch a single stone, plant, or other natural item and imbue it with a specific agrimagical effect. Most of these effects are unique to the agrimage, but known effects include:

  • Barrier Stone. An individual barrier stone can be created to repel creatures of 4 intelligence or less that come near it, either physically (pushing them back) or mentally (compelling the subject to avoid the stone). The stone affects the area in a 1-foot radius around it and can be countered with a DC 10 save. With each new barrier stone placed within 10 feet, the stone becomes stronger, adding a DC of 1 and an additional 1-foot in radius for each additional stone.

  • Evergrowth. Ground within a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=um6uF8FxLGv955QQ]]-foot square of this artifact, traditionally created from newly fallen wood, doubles in productivity - all plants yield double their normal amount and gain one of the following effects:

    • Roots glow in the night, casting dim light within 10 feet of each root.

    • Plants produce a pleasing aroma that reminds each person who encounters them of a pleasant moment from their past.

    • Children conceived in the area have a high chance of being twins.

  • Good Seed. Once planted and fully grown, a plant from this seed has one of the following effects:

    • It produces a fruit or vegetable every 3 days, regardless of the season.

    • Its roots grow toward the nearest source of water, gaining 10 feet of length and/or depth per day.

    • Food made from it keeps for 7 days under any conditions and always tastes good, regardless of the recipe.

Foundry Note

Scaling is implemented in the Barrier Stone activities to adjust the save DC and the area of effect based on the number of stones created.

Kali Andrella.biographyprivate:
For many years, Kali Andrella could be found tackling the Arctus Plateau's most impossible agrimagical challenges, using her quick mind and magical talents to develop solutions that no one else would ever think of. Even after she settled down in Steed's Point, becoming a student and collaborator of the agrimage smith Bertron Steed, Kali remained a force for agrimagical innovation on the plateau, making and selling items for those in need and providing guidance to those interested in understanding the craft of agrimagic.

That all changed when Steed's Point fell, destroyed by a pack of jurtak who made their way to the surface after an earthquake. No one has seen or heard from the agrimage since, though the continued functioning of many of her agrimagical creations has reassured those who care about her that she is alive. Unbeknownst to anyone, including her own daughter, Kali has not moved an inch - she is still within Steed's Point, attempting to hold together what small part of it she still can and protect it from the jurtak. It is the challenge of a lifetime.

Personality

Kali is generally at her happiest when she's taken on a seemingly impossible problem and figured out some way to best it (including using vines to support and supplement the functions of the arm she burned during the defense of Steed's Point). Plain-spoken but compassionate, she likes to get to the root of a challenge quickly and will pursue it doggedly until she figures out some way to solve it, but there is a grace to the way she moves through the world that makes her seem less like a stubborn scrapper and more like a force of nature. Both are probably equally true.

While Kali has regrets, especially about the fall of Steed's Point and Bertron's death during the town's last stand, there is a small part of her that is thriving in her current situation as the one person keeping Steed's Point from being completely destroyed — a challenge worthy of her talents.

Connections

Kali Andrella is deeply connected to Steed's Point, which was built by her mentor and friend Bertron Steed, but has contacts throughout the Arctus Plateau thanks to her work in her youth, especially in Nain. In recent years, she has lost touch with many of these connections, and has not seen her own daughter, Moriah, since before the fall of Steed's Point.

Phrases

Mind my vines - they can get a little prickly.

Haven't found the problem that can best me yet.

Throw enough time, money, or dirt at a problem and you always get there in the end.
Kali Andrella.biographypublic:
While she is no longer a young woman, the Arcturian in front of you is a study in motion, moving gracefully from one task to the next as if dancing from one side of the room to the other. As she moves, the vines that wrap around her scarred arm also move and sway, almost seeming to reach out next to her fingertips, as if part brace and part magic. The woman's dance is not a light or carefree one, but her movements have determination and purpose. If she eyes the world appraisingly from time to time, she seems more than capable of tackling what it has to offer.

Kali Andrella is a renowned agrimage who once traveled extensively through the Arctus Plateau helping local communities thrive. Known for her single-minded determination to solve a problem once encountered, she was often brought to towns and farms when other agrimages encountered a challenge they couldn't overcome, and is credited with saving the local prysmid beetle population of Saundrine after a drought and developing soil that cures plants of blight, among other wonders. She has not been seen in several years, since the fall of her hometown to a jurtak attack.

Moriah Foxhaven.name: Moriah Foxhaven

Sorcery Points.name: Sorcery Points
Sorcery Points.description:
[[lookup @name]] has 3 sorcery points. She can spend 1 or more sorcery points as a bonus action to gain one of the following benefits:

Heightened Spell: When [[lookup @name]] casts a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist the spell’s effects, she can spend 3 sorcery points to give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw against the spell.

Subtle Spell: When [[lookup @name]] casts a spell, she can spend 1 sorcery point to cast the spell without any somatic or verbal components.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of her character sheet. She automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Agrimagical Artifact.name: Agrimagical Artifact
Agrimagical Artifact.description:
Once per day, an agrimage can touch a single stone, plant, or other natural item and imbue it with a specific agrimagical effect. Most of these effects are unique to the agrimage, but known effects include:

  • Barrier Stone. An individual barrier stone can be created to repel creatures of 4 intelligence or less that come near it, either physically (pushing them back) or mentally (compelling the subject to avoid the stone). The stone affects the area in a 1-foot radius around it and can be countered with a DC 10 save. With each new barrier stone placed within 10 feet, the stone becomes stronger, adding a DC of 1 and an additional 1-foot in radius for each additional stone.

  • Evergrowth. Ground within a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=um6uF8FxLGv955QQ]]-foot square of this artifact, traditionally created from newly fallen wood, doubles in productivity - all plants yield double their normal amount and gain one of the following effects:

    • Roots glow in the night, casting dim light within 10 feet of each root.

    • Plants produce a pleasing aroma that reminds each person who encounters them of a pleasant moment from their past.

    • Children conceived in the area have a high chance of being twins.

  • Good Seed. Once planted and fully grown, a plant from this seed has one of the following effects:

    • It produces a fruit or vegetable every 3 days, regardless of the season.

    • Its roots grow toward the nearest source of water, gaining 10 feet of length and/or depth per day.

    • Food made from it keeps for 7 days under any conditions and always tastes good, regardless of the recipe.

Foundry Note

Scaling is implemented in the Barrier Stone activities to adjust the save DC and the area of effect based on the number of stones created.

Walking Stick.name: Walking Stick
Walking Stick.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

A thick shaft of wood wrapped with a sturdy grip makes a highly functional weapon in addition to a stout walking stick.
Walking Stick.descriptionpublic: A thick shaft of wood wrapped with a sturdy grip makes a highly functional weapon in addition to a stout walking stick.

Ember Blaze.name: Ember Blaze
Ember Blaze.description: When [[lookup @name]] is reduced to 0 hit points, he rolls a d20. On a 16 or higher, [[lookup @name]] instead drops to 1 hit point, and it can immediately take an action. Until the end of its next turn, his Speed increases by 10 feet, and he has advantage on weapon attack rolls and spell attack rolls.

Abyssal Sensitivity.name: Abyssal Sensitivity
Abyssal Sensitivity.description:
When [[lookup @name]] takes necrotic damage, she makes a [[/save cha format=long]] with DC equal to either 10 or half the total necrotic damage taken - whichever value is greater.

  • On a success, apply the Abyssal Resistance effect, gaining resistance to necrotic damage until the end of your next long rest.

  • On a failure, apply the Abyssal Susceptibility effect, inflicting vulnerability to necrotic damage until the end of your next long rest. Each time you take additional necrotic damage you may repeat the saving throw, ending this effect immediately on a success.

This check is not repeated while either Abyssal Resistance or Abyssal Sensitivity are active.

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description:
Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range.

Weather Sensor. You create a Tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.

Bloom. You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.

Sensory Effect. You create a harmless sensory effect, such as falling leaves, spectral dancing fairies, a gentle breeze, the sound of an animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot Cube.

Fire Play. You light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a campfire.

Fire Bolt.name: Fire Bolt
Fire Bolt.description:
You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or an object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell starts burning if it isn't being worn or carried.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d10 when you reach levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10).

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
This spell repairs a single break or tear in an object you touch, such as a broken chain link, two halves of a broken key, a torn cloak, or a leaking wineskin. As long as the break or tear is no larger than 1 foot in any dimension, you mend it, leaving no trace of the former damage.

This spell can physically repair a magic item, but it can't restore magic to such an object.

Animal Friendship.name: Animal Friendship
Animal Friendship.description:
Target a Beast that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[charmed apply=false] condition for the duration. If you or one of your allies deals damage to the target, the spells ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional Beast for each spell slot level above 1.

Entangle.name: Entangle
Entangle.description:
Grasping plants sprout from the ground in a 20-foot square within range. For the duration, these plants turn the ground in the area into &Reference[difficultterrain]. They disappear when the spell ends.

Each creature (other than you) in the area when you cast the spell must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have the &Reference[restrained apply=false] condition until the spell ends. A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself from the grasping plants and is no longer Restrained by them.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Speak with Animals.name: Speak with Animals
Speak with Animals.description:
For the duration, you can comprehend and verbally communicate with Beasts, and you can use any of the Influence action's skill options with them.

Most Beasts have little to say about topics that don't pertain to survival or companionship, but at minimum, a Beast can give you information about nearby locations and monsters, including whatever it has perceived within the past day.

Gust of Wind.name: Gust of Wind
Gust of Wind.description:
A Line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide blasts from you in a direction you choose for the duration. Each creature in the Line must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from you in a direction following the Line. A creature that ends its turn in the Line must make the same save.

Any creature in the Line must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving closer to you.

The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to extinguish them.

As a Bonus Action on your later turns, you can change the direction in which the Line blasts from you.

Lesser Restoration.name: Lesser Restoration
Lesser Restoration.description: You touch a creature and end one condition on it: &Reference[blinded], &Reference[deafened], &Reference[paralyzed], or &Reference[poisoned].

Spike Growth.name: Spike Growth
Spike Growth.description:
The ground in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range sprouts hard spikes and thorns. The area becomes Difficult Terrain for the duration. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes [[/damage 2d4 type=piercing]] damage for every 5 feet it travels.

The transformation of the ground is camouflaged to look natural. Any creature that can't see the area when the spell is cast must take a Search action and succeed on a [[/check ability=wis skill=prc dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] or [[/check ability=wis skill=sur dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC to recognize the terrain as hazardous before entering it.

Haste.name: Haste
Haste.description:
Choose a willing creature that you can see within range. Until the spell ends, the target's Speed is doubled, it gains a +2 bonus to Armor Class, it has Advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and it gains an additional action on each of its turns. That action can be used to take only the Attack (one attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Utilize action.

When the spell ends, the target is &Reference[Incapacitated apply=false] and has a Speed of 0 until the end of its next turn, as a wave of lethargy washes over it.

Protection from Energy.name: Protection from Energy
Protection from Energy.description: For the duration, the willing creature you touch has Resistance to one damage type of your choice: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

Moriah Foxhaven.biographyprivate:
Moriah's stoicism stems from the curiosities of her youth as a misunderstood dreamer from the remote village of Steed's Point. In an effort to leave the burdens of the past behind, she set out to find a new place she could call home — ultimately settling on the proud life of a naturalistic vagabond.

Personality

While she's suspicious of strangers, Moriah is practical and a consummate survivor. And a profound curiosity has motivated her since her younger days. She's happy enough to welcome outsiders into her camp for a while if their intentions are pure (and their gold or barter is worthy).

Connections

Moriah is the daughter of the reclusive agrimage Kali Andrella, who still resides in the doomed ruination of Steed's Point, and is the adopted granddaughter of the village's blacksmith founder — the late Bertron Steed.

Following her exodus from Steed's Point, Moriah fell in with a group of like-minded rovers, eventually falling in love with a young Arcturian falconer named Evrest Foxhaven. Side-by-side, this found-family roams the Golden Flats in search of a better tomorrow and the right people to share it with.

Rattletrap, the Rickety Man, will send the party on a mission to find Moriah during the events of "The Book of Tales," so that they might procure a fabled Grassland Talisman from the young agrimage and stem the tide in Steed's Point.

Phrases

The plains provide.

If you live too firmly in the past, you'll rot along with it.

Life is what we make it. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.
Moriah Foxhaven.biographypublic:
A young Arcturian woman sits atop a magnificent four-legged yarnac, which she drives across the grassy plain with calm and ease. Her sun-kissed light brown skin is freckled from relentless exposure to the rays of Lantyr, and the details of her close-fitting garb reveal a healthy symbiosis with the nature around her — earth-tone garments made from cotton, straps and belts made from vine instead of leather, and an assortment of jewelry and trinkets lovingly culled from the natural world. There's a fire in her twenty-something auburn eyes that suggests an undeterred sense of self, and she regards you with unwavering composure as she dismounts the beast to entreat with you face-to-face.

[[lookup @name]] is a fierce-spirited agrimage who lives amongst an unnamed group of beast-riding nomads, who are known to roam among the Golden Flats in placid symbiosis with the land and its creatures. Warm-hearted to those she trusts most and curious to the bone, Moriah is a self-made sorcerer whose somewhat lonely past will never overshadow her hopeful future.

Rattletrap, the Rickety Man.name: Rattletrap, the Rickety Man

Greater Improvised Weaponry.name: Greater Improvised Weaponry
Greater Improvised Weaponry.description:
Rattletrap can use almost any object as a greater improvised weapon. A greater improvised weapon follows the rules below.

Proficiency. Add the [[lookup @name]]'s Proficiency Bonus to attack rolls with an improvised weapon.

Damage. On a hit, the weapon deals 1d6 damage of a type the DM thinks is appropriate for the object.

Range. If the [[lookup @name]] throws the weapon, it has a normal range of 40 feet and a long range of 80 feet.

Weapon Equivalents. If an improvised weapon resembles a Simple or Martial weapon, the DM may say it functions as that weapon and uses that weapon’s rules. For example, the DM could treat a table leg as a Club.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: Rattletrap makes two attacks with its [[/item Rusty Scythe]], two attacks with its [[/item Rusty Trowel]], or two attacks with its [[/item Greater Improvised Weaponry]].

Sure-Footed.name: Sure-Footed
Sure-Footed.description: Rattletrap has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made against effects that would knock it prone.

Gust of Brambles.name: Gust of Brambles
Gust of Brambles.description:
Rattletrap calls forth an arcane flurry of thorny brambles from the earth around it.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]]-foot [[lookup @target.template.type capitalize activity=dnd5eactivity000]] originating from Rattletrap.

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage, and the creature is pushed 10 feet away from Rattletrap.

Success: Half damage, and the creature isn’t pushed.

Rusty Scythe.name: Rusty Scythe
Rusty Scythe.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

A large curved blade mounted on the end of a tall curved shaft. This rusted polearm is primarily used to reap crops. It also provides the ability to attack with deadly efficiency from a greater range than typical melee weapons.
Rusty Scythe.descriptionpublic: A large curved blade mounted on the end of a tall curved shaft. This rusted polearm is primarily used for the reaping of crops. It also provides the ability to attack with deadly efficiency from greater range than typical melee weapons.

Rusty Trowel.name: Rusty Trowel
Rusty Trowel.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

This one-handed trowel resembles a rusty spade with a broad blade and upturned sides, and is primarily used for moving earth and other material. In the hands of a [[lookup @name]], it can be quite useful in hand combat.
Rusty Trowel.descriptionpublic: This one-handed trowel resembles a spade with a broad blade and upturned sides, and is primarily used for moving earth and other material. In the hands of a [[lookup @name]], it can be quite useful in hand combat..

Rattletrap, the Rickety Man.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

[[lookup @name]], is a ramshackle automaton crafted from wood and vine to resemble an Arcturian human with a wise and benevolent visage. Similar to other Woven Constructs, the once-proud artisanal quality of Rattletrap's form is evident in his carefully carved face and the finer details of his whittled garb; but this aged construct appears weathered and worn by countless years of exposure to the chaotic exterior climes of the Golden Flats.

As construct, Rattletrap doesn't require food, air, or sleep to survive. He can, however, be repaired by characters with adequate training and proficiency, or magical mending and artifice.

Behavior

Rattletrap toils alone amidst the overgrown ruins of Steed's Point, in constant turmoil with local predators like the Jurtak (and seemingly oblivious to the town's other isolated resident). He is a stoic and solemn fellow, who attempts to hide his bittersweet relationship with acute nostalgia behind an unmoving countenance and the rotes of his labor.

His greater improvised weaponry feature allows Rattletrap to wield all manner of tools and objects in combat with more precision. Meanwhile, a rusty scythe and trowel have served him well over the years as formidable weapons against aggressive Gore Birds and Jurtak that would threaten his small plot of land.

Lore

Unlike normal Woven Constructs, Rattletrap was granted the ability to speak (and a small measure of sentience) by his creator — a long-dead blacksmith-mage named Bertron Steed, the eponymous founder of Steed's Point. And when calamity came to Steed's Point, a calamity that would drive out most of the town's residents and spell the end for Bertron Steed himself, Rattletrap endured. The notorious "Rickety Man" has persisted in the ruins of the time-ravaged village to this very day, where he staves off incessant attacks from Gore Birds and Jurtak Warriors in an effort to one day carry out Bertron Steed's dying wishes: to somehow unite his estranged family, Kali Andrella and her daughter Moriah.

Standard Woven Constructs are relatively commonplace throughout the Arctus Plateau, and can be found in the service of many a Golden Flats farmstead. These automatons are known for the varied materials of their wooden construction, and are known to wear carved faces that reflect the temperaments of their respective households.
Rattletrap, the Rickety Man.biographypublic:
This humanoid figure is crafted from various scraps of wood, its ramshackle limbs held together with a skeleton made of timber and ligatures woven from vine. The masterful carving that comprises its wooden face is fixed in a perpetual look of mirthful stoicism as it labors away at the duteous task of reaping wild grain in a long-forgotten field.

Known as "The Rickety Man" of Steed's Point, Rattletrap is a unique Woven Construct that presides among the overgrown ruins of a doomed village, where he toils in quiet servitude to an endless task. Contrary to standard Woven Constructs, Rattletrap possesses the curious ability to speak.

Kendral Lowd.name: Kendral Lowd

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. HIs spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of his character sheet. He automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Fire Bolt.name: Fire Bolt
Fire Bolt.description:
You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or an object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell starts burning if it isn't being worn or carried.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d10 when you reach levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10).

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Minor Illusion.name: Minor Illusion
Minor Illusion.description:
You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

Detect Evil and Good.name: Detect Evil and Good
Detect Evil and Good.description:
For the duration, you sense the location of any Aberration, Celestial, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, or Undead within 30 feet of yourself. You also sense whether the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplHallow0000]{Hallow} spell is active there and, if so, where.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Magic Missile.name: Magic Missile
Magic Missile.description:
You create three glowing darts of magical force. Each dart strikes a creature of your choice that you can see within range. A dart deals 1d4 + 1 Force damage to its target. The darts all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The spell creates one more dart for each spell slot level above 1.

[[2 + @item.level]]{Level [[lookup @item.level]] darts}

Protection from Evil and Good.name: Protection from Evil and Good
Protection from Evil and Good.description: Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch is protected against creatures that are Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, or Undead. The protection grants several benefits. Creatures of those types have Disadvantage on attack rolls against the target. The target also can't be possessed by or gain the &Reference[Charmed apply=false] or &Reference[Frightened apply=false] conditions from them. If the target is already possessed, Charmed, or Frightened by such a creature, the target has Advantage on any new saving throw against the relevant effect.

Enhance Ability.name: Enhance Ability
Enhance Ability.description:
You touch a creature and choose Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. For the duration, the target has Advantage on ability checks using the chosen ability.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2. You can choose a different ability for each target.

Gust of Wind.name: Gust of Wind
Gust of Wind.description:
A Line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide blasts from you in a direction you choose for the duration. Each creature in the Line must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from you in a direction following the Line. A creature that ends its turn in the Line must make the same save.

Any creature in the Line must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving closer to you.

The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to extinguish them.

As a Bonus Action on your later turns, you can change the direction in which the Line blasts from you.

Mirror Image.name: Mirror Image
Mirror Image.description:
Three illusory duplicates of yourself appear in your space. Until the spell ends, the duplicates move with you and mimic your actions, shifting position so it's impossible to track which image is real.
