Jurtak Champion.name: Jurtak Champion

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes three attacks with its [[/item Claw]]{Claws}, [[/item Wicked Pike]], or [[/item Grotesque Longbow]].

Aggressive.name: Aggressive
Aggressive.description: As a bonus action, the [[lookup @name]] can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

Limited Telepathy.name: Limited Telepathy
Limited Telepathy.description: The [[lookup @name]] can telepathically communicate with any other Jurtak within 120 feet of it. This constant telepathic connection also makes them highly resistant to Psychic damage.

Jurtak Poison.name: Jurtak Poison
Jurtak Poison.description:
Jurtaks all carry containers of deadly poison that they use to coat their weapon and ammunition tips with. The first time it hits with a weapon attack in each encounter, the attack delivers this poison.

Jurtak Poison is a sticky mass of a foul-smelling compound wrapped in a crudely cut square of skin. Taken from the Jurtak and found coating their weapons, it is undoubtedly toxic and unsafe to handle or consume.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=CfHod0bLN500c2cm]], made by one creature hit by the [[lookup @name]]’s first weapon attack that hits in each encounter.

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage, and the target has the &Reference[poisoned] condition for 1 minute.

Success: Half damage.

Acid Spit.name: Acid Spit
Acid Spit.description:
The [[lookup @name]] spits acid in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]]-foot line that is [[lookup @target.template.width activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet wide.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], each creature in the line.

Failure: [[/damage average]]

Success: Half damage.

Sunlight Sensitivity.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
Sunlight Sensitivity.description: While in sunlight, the [[lookup @name lowercase]] has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

Spider Climb.name: Spider Climb
Spider Climb.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. Its hands must be empty to do this.

Jurtak Champion.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Jurtak are saurian humanoids that have become horribly warped by abyssal energies. They possess six eyes perfectly attuned to darkness, and their slender bodies are covered in scales that allow them to easily blend into the shadows of their surroundings.

Champions are much larger, much more heavily armored than any other Jurtak. They are covered in trophies taken from victims of all kinds, and adorn themselves with feathers, leaves, and other trophies taken from the various creatures that call the lightless depths home.

Behavior

Champions are leaders within the Jurtak, and gather groups of lesser Jutak around them to serve as lackeys and minions. Most Jurtak groups only have one Champion, but some larger groups may have additional leaders in the form of Geormancers, though this is rare due to inherently territorial nature of Jurtak.

Champions are hyper aggressive, leading charges into enemy lines, commanding raids on vulnerable settlements, and violently claiming as many trophies for themselves as they can.

Highly aggressive and territorial, Jurtak prefer ambushes from the shadows, leveraging their ability to climb and hide to overwhelm prey. They hunt in coordinated groups, often comprised of warriors supported by hunters, and launch swift, multi-pronged assaults on unwitting enemies.

Jurtak, build dens and nests deep in the Pathways, each one as dark as the abyss that created them. In these dens they gather in the dozens, often falling under the leadership of at least one, sometimes several leaders such as Champions or Geomancers.

Lore

Spawned from a primordial Abyssal incursion within Ember's hidden pathways, the Jurtak have steadily expanded across the shadowed expanses, adapting to the environment, laying traps, building dens and blinds from which to spawn and hunt. Scholars speculate the origin of these creatures ties directly to some abyssal entity in the pathways itself, as there is no other explanation for why their numbers have not dwindled over time.

Jurtak do not speak, not as far as anyone is aware. Save for the odd hiss or roar meant to intimidate foes they are almost entirely silent, but exhibit a shocking ability to coordinate without speech. It is believed that they possess some ability to communicate with each other telepathically or through some other means.

No Jurtak has ever uttered an intelligible word as far as any record or tale recalls.
Jurtak Champion.biographypublic:
You behold a lean, six-eyed saurian creature, its body clad in fragments of bone and its scales glinting in the dim light. The acrid scent of poison tinges the air, dripping from the bone blade held in its clawed hands. Its long, semi-prehensile tail moves with a predator's anticipation, and a forked tongue flicks across twisted lips as its eyes fix upon you with a predatory malice.

Jurtak Warriors are six-eyed saurian aberrations from the darkest depths of the pathways, armed with crude weapons and armor fashioned from the skeletal remains of their vanquished foes. They are swift and brutal, incapable of mercy.

Jurtak Geomancer.name: Jurtak Geomancer

Stoneblast.name: Stoneblast
Stoneblast.description:
The [[lookup @name]] projects a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=f6lqcGn0za2gvBhb]]-foot [[lookup @target.template.type capitalize activity=f6lqcGn0za2gvBhb]] of sharp rocks.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=f6lqcGn0za2gvBhb]], each creature in the cone (creatures with a shield equipped have advantage on the save).

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: Half damage. If the creature has a shield equipped, it takes no damage instead.

Unstable Ground.name: Unstable Ground
Unstable Ground.description:
The [[lookup @name]] emits a swift pulse of transmutation magic in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]]-foot cone. The ground in the area becomes briefly unstable and treacherous.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], each creature in the cone.

Failure: The creature’s Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.

Crystal Staff.name: Crystal Staff
Crystal Staff.descriptionpublic: This mage staff is a talisman to assist with spellcraft or hurl gouts of arcane flame at enemies.

Clinging Grip.name: Clinging Grip
Clinging Grip.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is able to cling to vertical or overhead surfaces with exceptional grip or adhesion. This creature can avoid falling as long as they are adjacent to any solid surface which can reasonably support them.
Clinging Grip.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can drop from overhead to Strike a creature below it. The target creature suffers an Empowered attack which, if successful, knocks them @Condition[prone] in addition to dealing damage.

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can suffer falling damage from this attack only if it misses its target.

Acid Spit.name: Acid Spit
Acid Spit.description: The creature has salivary glands which produce a caustic acid.
Acid Spit.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} spits a glob of acidic bile at a target within 20 feet.

On a Critical Hit, this attack causes the @Condition[corroding] condition for 3 Turns.

Thermal Vision.name: Thermal Vision
Thermal Vision.description: The @ref[actor.name]{Creature} perceives the world through differences in temperature with precision, allowing it to locate creatures which are warm-blooded or otherwise emit heat up to 60 feet away as long as they are not behind total cover and you are not Blinded or Incapacitated. A creature detected using this Thermal Vision is treated as visible for the purposes of actions which require you to see your target.

Bonded Mind.name: Bonded Mind
Bonded Mind.description: The mind of a @ref[actor.name]{creature} with this talent is inextricably bound to other members of its group. It is capable of instantaneous telepathic communication with any other @ref[actor.taxonomy.name]{creature of its taxonomy} within 60 feet.

Rune: Flame.name: Rune: Flame
Rune: Flame.description:
The chaotic force of elemental, thermal energy. The Flame rune governs fire and heat.

The Flame rune scales using Intellect, targets Reflex, and deals Fire damage to Health. It is opposed by the orderly rune of Frost.
Rune: Flame.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Flame allows you to manipulate fire and thermal energy in creative ways, producing one of the following effects:

  • Manifest a burst of elemental flame in one inch sphere which can ignite a candle, torch, or other flammable materials.

  • Imbue your body with momentary thermal shielding which provides you with immunity to fire damage on an immediately subsequent action that costs 1 Action or less.

  • Control the movement of flames within a small area, causing them to flicker, dance, or shift in an animated performance of light and shadow.

Enkindle may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Rune: Earth.name: Rune: Earth
Rune: Earth.description:
The orderly force of elemental earth, responsible for physical matter. The Earth rune governs minerals, metals, soils, and other physical compounds.

The Earth rune scales using Wisdom, targets Reflex, and deals Acid damage to Health. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Lightning.
Rune: Earth.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Earth allows you to manipulate raw forces of rock, mineral, and soil in basic ways, producing one of the following effects:

  • Quickly shape up to one cubic foot of available material into a simple geometric form like a cuboid, ellipsoid, or polyhedron.

  • Precisely copy the physical shape of a held object that is smaller than a 6-inch cube, reproducing it from available clay, stone, or metal. The replica retains no useful properties except for its physical form.

  • Separate and collect earthen particles from the surface of an object, creature, or liquid that you touch, rendering the subject completely cleaned or purified in moments.

Mould may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Gesture: Arrow.name: Gesture: Arrow
Gesture: Arrow.description:
You hurl a projectile imbued with the magical power of a Rune at a distant target.

The Arrow gesture scales using Intellect and targets a single creature up to a distance of 60 feet, dealing 8 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus.

Gesture: Influence.name: Gesture: Influence
Gesture: Influence.description:
You intensify the arcane power of a Rune into a concentrated direct contact which is generally a more powerful evolution of the basic Touch gesture.

The Influence gesture scales using Presence and targets a single adjacent creature. It deals 10 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus.

Talisman Weapon Training.name: Talisman Weapon Training
Talisman Weapon Training.description: You understand the arcane usage of talismans, orbs, foci, or other similar implements to channel magic or empower spellcraft. You are Trained with weapons in the Talisman categories.
Talisman Weapon Training.actiondesc:
You use your equipped Talisman to attempt to regain some Focus. You perform a Harmless Strike against your own Rallying threshold.

On a success you recover +1 Focus if using a one-handed Talisman and +2 Focus if using a two-handed Talisman. On a critical success the amount of Focus recovered increases by an additional +1.

Gesture: Strike.name: Gesture: Strike
Gesture: Strike.description:
You empower a direct close-range attack with the arcane essence of a Rune, performing a Strike with your equipped weapon.

The Strike gesture scales using Strength and deal damage based on your used weapon but with the damage type of the incorporated Rune. This gesture does not require any free hand and has a base cost of 1 Focus in addition to the cost of your weapon Strike.

Gesture: Ward.name: Gesture: Ward
Gesture: Ward.description:
You shape the arcane power of a Rune into a protective barrier used to shield yourself from harm.

The Ward gesture scales using Toughness and provides +6 Resistance against the damage type of the Rune used in the spell. This resistance lasts for 1 Round and you may only have a single Ward at a time. Casting another spell using the Ward gesture replaces your prior Ward. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 2 Action and 1 Focus.

Firestarter.name: Firestarter
Firestarter.descriptionpublic: A small waxed-leather pouch containing dry shredded plant fibre and wood shavings, with a little clasp inside for securing a piece of flint and a steel striking ring for the purposes of starting fires.

Rations.name: Rations
Rations.descriptionpublic: Dried bread, nuts, smoked cheese and meat suitable to serve as a rudimentary meal capable of sustaining life for a single day.

Wetskin.name: Wetskin
Wetskin.descriptionpublic: A leather-wrapped bladder that can be affixed to a belt or outside of a pack for convenient use. Can contain 26oz of liquid.

Mealkit.name: Mealkit
Mealkit.descriptionpublic: A leather pouch containing a metal cup, plate, fork, and a piece of cloth for wiping them clean.

Ragged armor.name: Ragged armor
Ragged armor.descriptionpublic: Crafted from thick, boiled leather hardened into panels or a cuirass, leather armor offers lightweight protection ideal for scouts, rogues, and lightly armed skirmishers.

Rune: Kinesis.name: Rune: Kinesis
Rune: Kinesis.description:
The chaotic force of space and physical movement. The Kinesis rune governs all things related to the act of movement and physicality.

The Kinesis rune scales using Presence, targets Physical defense, and deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage to Health. It is opposed by the orderly rune of Control.
Rune: Kinesis.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Kinesis allows you to exert local control over gravitational forces to perform basic telekinetic manipulations, producing one of the following effects:

  • Pull an unsecured object within 15 feet and with weight no greater than 1 towards you and catch it. An object that is equipped or possessed by a creature is never treated as unsecured unless that creature is willing to release it.

  • Flick an object that you hold with weight no greater than 1 towards a target up to 30 feet away. The object flies unerringly in a straight line towards that target at a moderate speed. Any creature along the object's path can react to catch it as long as they have a free hand with which to do so.

  • Suspend in midair an object or willing creature that you touch with weight less than or equal to 10 times your Presence, altering its position up to 20 feet in any direction from its original location. You can maintain this suspension indefinitely as long as you take no further Action and are not @Condition[incapacitated].

Propel may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch unless otherwise specified. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Gesture: Fan.name: Gesture: Fan
Gesture: Fan.description:
You shape the essence of a Rune into a sweeping or splintered arc to strike multiple targets in close proximity.

The Fan gesture scales using Intellect and targets a 120 degree arc with 6 foot radius. It deals 6 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus.

Jurtak Geomancer.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Jurtak are saurian humanoids that have become horribly warped by abyssal energies. They possess six eyes perfectly attuned to darkness, and their slender bodies are covered in scales that allow them to easily blend into the shadows of their surroundings. Generally, Geomancers are taller and stronger than regular Jurtak, but fall shy of the might of the Jurtak Champions.

Jurtak Geomancers are arcane spellcasters whose Sorcerous Origin stems from the Abyss itself, which they channel into and out of veins of corrupted earth.

Behavior

The cruel Jurtak Geomancers, like Champions and Sporebearers, often serve as sectional leaders of regular Jurtak Warriors and Hunters. Their heavily stone-shrouded forms make the Geomancer stand out within any given group of Jurtak.

Jurtak Geomancers use their magic to appear intimidating before and during battle and won’t hesitate to urge their lesser allies onward to engage opponents in melee combat while the Geomancers themselves target enemies from afar.

They, as all Jurtak, build dens and nests deep in the pathways, each one as dark as the abyss that created them. They are almost silent, seemingly able to communicate with each other through some other means.

Lore

Spawned from a primordial Abyssal incursion within Ember's hidden pathways, the Jurtak have steadily expanded across the shadowed expanses, adapting to the environment, laying traps, building dens and blinds from which to spawn and hunt. Scholars speculate the origin of these creatures ties directly to some abyssal entity in the pathways itself, as there is no other explanation for why their numbers have not dwindled over time. Geomancers have only rarely been identified from those fortunate enough to survive the most recent of Jurtak encounters.

Jurtak do not speak, not as far as anyone is aware. Save for the odd hiss or roar meant to intimidate foes they are almost entirely silent, but exhibit a shocking ability to coordinate without speech. It is believed that they possess some ability to communicate with each other telepathically or through some other means.

No Jurtak has ever uttered an intelligible word as far as any record or tale recalls.
Jurtak Geomancer.biographypublic: @ref[name]s are remarkably powerful spellcasters who harness the latent power of Ember’s terrain and use it to shape their surroundings as desired.
Jurtak Geomancer.biographyappearance: The tall, six-eyed saurian before you clutches a gnarled staff crowned in a jagged crystal of lambent crystal. This loathsome creature is coated in thick, jagged stone that appears to be growing out of its very hide, forming an unnatural armor.

Jurtak Hunter.name: Jurtak Hunter

Jurtak Light Armor.name: Jurtak Light Armor
Jurtak Light Armor.descriptionpublic: Tattered protective wear made of crudely cut pieces of hide, fastened with sharpened hooks of bone, and layered until it provides something resembling armor.

Grotesque Longbow.name: Grotesque Longbow
Grotesque Longbow.descriptionpublic: A tall, self-bow often taller than the archer who draws it, the longbow requires great strength and years of practice to master, sending arrows with deadly force across the battlefield.

Bonded Mind.name: Bonded Mind
Bonded Mind.description: The mind of a @ref[actor.name]{creature} with this talent is inextricably bound to other members of its group. It is capable of instantaneous telepathic communication with any other @ref[actor.taxonomy.name]{creature of its taxonomy} within 60'.

Dual Wield.name: Dual Wield
Dual Wield.description: You are adept at fighting with two weapons simultaneously. You can weave attacks together to strike more rapidly than possible with a single weapon.
Dual Wield.actiondesc: Immediately after you perform a basic Strike with your mainhand weapon, you make a reduced-cost fullow-up Strike with your offhand weapon.

Backstab.name: Backstab
Backstab.description: You focus your cunning instincts on exploiting the weak points of a flanked target. You identify an opportunity and strike with deadly efficiency.
Backstab.actiondesc: You Strike with your mainhand weapon against a Flanked target, dealing Deadly damage.

Pinning Shot.name: Pinning Shot
Pinning Shot.description: You fire a tactically placed shot to pin your target against a nearby surface.
Pinning Shot.actiondesc: You Strike from distance. The attack is Difficult, however if your target is it it becomes Restrained until the end of their next Turn.

Opportunist.name: Opportunist
Opportunist.description: You sieze any opportunity you can to capitalize on an enemy who turns their back on you. You may make a Disengagement Attack even if you are otherwise Fully Engaged, but you do so without the 2 Boons that would ordinarily apply to such an attack.

Weak Points.name: Weak Points
Weak Points.description: You identify moments of opportunity to strike at an enemy's weak points. When attacking a target that is Unaware, Flanked, or Exposed using Finesse weaponry, you gain +2 damage to any Strike.

Light Weapon Training.name: Light Weapon Training
Light Weapon Training.description: You know how to wield light weapons fluidly with a high degree of maneuverability and grace in combat. You are Trained with all weapons in the Light and Balanced categories.
Light Weapon Training.actiondesc:
You dart forward nimbly, making a strike with sudden and unexpected swiftness to perform a Strike with a Finesse weapon against a single target with an increased range of +2 feet.

The attack is Difficult, but you do not move from your current position nor does this attack provoke Disengagement.

Projectile Weapon Training.name: Projectile Weapon Training
Projectile Weapon Training.description: You have a basic education in archery and other projectile weaponry. You are no longer treated as Untrained with weapons in the Projectile categories.
Projectile Weapon Training.actiondesc: You can loose a shot under pressure, although with decreased accuracy. You perform a Strike that is Difficult, but has a reduced Action cost.

Clinging Grip.name: Clinging Grip
Clinging Grip.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is able to cling to vertical or overhead surfaces with exceptional grip or adhesion. This creature can avoid falling as long as they are adjacent to any solid surface which can reasonably support them.
Clinging Grip.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can drop from overhead to Strike a creature below it. The target creature suffers an Empowered attack which, if successful, knocks them @Condition[prone] in addition to dealing damage.

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can suffer falling damage from this attack only if it misses its target.

Dirty Tricks.name: Dirty Tricks
Dirty Tricks.description: You have pouches of sand and dust that you use to temporarily distract or blind an enemy.
Dirty Tricks.actiondesc: You fling debris into the eyes of an enemy. If the Strike is successful, they are Blinded until the end of their next Turn.

Firestarter.name: Firestarter
Firestarter.descriptionpublic: A small waxed-leather pouch containing dry shredded plant fibre and wood shavings, with a little clasp inside for securing a piece of flint and a steel striking ring for the purposes of starting fires.

Jurtak Poison.name: Jurtak Poison
Jurtak Poison.descriptionpublic: A sticky mass of foul-smelling compound wrapped in a crudely cut square of skin. Taken from the Jurtak, and found coating their weapons, it is undoubtedly toxic, and unsafe to handle or consume.
actiondesc:
When this toxin is ingested or otherwise enters the bloodstream of a creature, it is initially Harmless, but the target must defend an attack against its Fortitude or become @Condition[poisoned].

The amount of poison damage and its duration is dependent on the quality of the @ref[name]:

  • Shoddy - 2 damage for 4 rounds

  • Standard - 4 damage for 6 rounds

  • Fine - 6 damage for 8 rounds

  • Superior - 8 damage for 10 rounds

  • Masterwork - 10 damage for 12 rounds

This action should be used when the poison is ingested rather than when it is first applied.

The contents of this vial can be added to food, drink, smeared upon a bladed weapon, or combined with some alternative delivery mechanism.

This action, which consumes the available usage of the poison, should be used when it is first applied.

Mealkit.name: Mealkit
Mealkit.descriptionpublic: A leather pouch containing a metal cup, plate, fork, and a piece of cloth for wiping them clean.

Acid Spit.description: The creature has salivary glands which produce a caustic acid.

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} spits a glob of acidic bile at a target within 20 feet.

A creature detected using this Thermal Vision is treated as visible for the purposes of actions which require you to see your target.

Jurtak do not speak, not as far as anyone is aware. Save for the odd hiss or roar meant to intimidate foes they are almost entirely silent, but exhibit a shocking ability to coordinate without speech. It is believed that they possess some ability to communicate with each other telepathically or through some other means.

Limited Telepathy.description: The [[lookup @name]] can telepathically communicate with any other Jurtak within 120 feet of it. This constant telepathic connection also makes them highly resistant to Psychic damage.

Sporebearers are skinnier than their ilk, and covered in invasive fungus and lichen that seems to be growing out of their flesh as much as on it. Whether these beings are in constant pain or not is a question none have been able to ascertain, though it does appear some portion of their body has been permanently converted into fungus.

Behavior

Sporebearers are strange, addled beings, not quite as outwardly aware or mentally sharp as their ilk, possibly because of the haze of noxious spores that flow out of the numerous mushrooms growing out of them. However, what they lack in perception and willpower is made up for in speed and deadliness. Their long, twisted scythes are razor sharp and quite good at cleaving prey in two. More worrying than that, they don't seem to feel pain the same as other Jurtak.

Like all Jurtak, they are highly aggressive and territorial, Jurtak prefer ambushes from the shadows, leveraging their ability to climb and hide to overwhelm prey. They hunt in coordinated groups, often comprised of warriors supported by hunters, and launch swift, multi-pronged assaults on unwitting enemies.

Scholars speculate the origin of these creatures ties directly to some abyssal entity in the pathways itself, as there is no other explanation for why their numbers have not dwindled over time.

Sporebearers have become vessels for numerous colonies of Pathways native fungus, which feed off of the Sporebearer's flesh and blood, and become twisted by the Abyssal energies flowing through the Jurtak. The Jurtak in turn grows immune to poisons, enjoys increased physical resilience, and becomes all but inured to pain, living their lives in the darkness numb and detached.

Jurtak Warrior.biographyappearance: You behold a lean, six-eyed saurian creature, its body clad in fragments of bone and its scales glinting in the dim light. The acrid scent of poison tinges the air, dripping from the bone blade held in its clawed hands. Its long, semi-prehensile tail moves with a predator's anticipation, and a forked tongue flicks across twisted lips as its eyes fix upon you with a predatory malice.

Pale Whisperer.name: Pale Whisperer

Amorphous Entity.name: Amorphous Entity
Amorphous Entity.description:
The [[lookup @name]] can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing, and has no discernible, organs or weak points.

Additionally, it's amorphous form is almost impossible to get hold of, making it immune to being grappled, restrained, or knocked prone. It cannot bleed, and no terrestrial illness or poison can affect its abyssal physiology, such as it has.

It also has no eyes or sensory organs, and senses its surroundings in a manner that makes it immune to being blinded or deafened.

Sight Without.name: Sight Without
Sight Without.description: The [[lookup @name]] has no eyes, ears, or mouth. It cannot be blinded, silenced, or deafened. Instead, it has 60 feet of blindsight and can speak telepathically to anyone or all creatures within 120 feet of it.

Inscrutable.name: Inscrutable
Inscrutable.description: The [[lookup @name]] is an unknowable alien entity. It is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (Insight) checks made to ascertain the [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.

Legendary Resistance.name: Legendary Resistance
Legendary Resistance.description: If the [[lookup @name]] fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is Medium or smaller, it must make the following saving throw.

Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes one [[/item Shadow Tendril]]{Tendril} attack and, if it can, [[/item Abyssal Whip]].

Pale Whisperer.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Its form defies traditional description, a swirling mass of living darkness and shadow that slithers and writhes into and around itself with an unsettling impossibility. Its body lacks a definitive shape, constantly shifting and morphing, spawning countless tendrils of blackness that dissolve back into its form, or dissipate into a swirling mist that orbits the form like a nebula. The core of the creature is an incomprehensible void, a black sphere that the rest of the being seems to swirl and orbit.

Behavior

Whisperers have their own agendas, and personalities, each wanting something unique to itself but also aligned with the unknowable entities that spawned them. They are dangerously intelligent and manipulative, and seek to consume sources of magical power wherever they can find them, growing stronger with each meal. Their ultimate goals are unknown beyond the simple collection of strength, but there is certainly some grander design at world, and it is not one that Ember will benefit from seeing come to fruition.

Lore

This abyssal creature is functionally timeless. It has likely existed for ages uncountable, seen the birth and death of worlds no mortal minds ever held knowledge of. It was birthed from the deepest depths of the abyss beyond Ember, and resided there for longer than perhaps even Ember itself has existed in the cosmic fabric of the universe. If it has a name or a maker, such secrets are its alone to keep.

Upon death this abyssal creature quickly unravels, turning into a viscous, oil-like substance that is all but impossible to collect or get hold of. This fluid quickly evaporates, creating a cloud of noxious fumes which blind and choke any caught within. Within a few hours all that remains of its form will be a horrible dark spot of tainted earth and stone where its rotted form soaked in.

Any long term effects of exposure to its corpse are unknown, but surely best avoided.
Pale Whisperer.biographypublic:
Ever shifting and reshaping itself, producing new limbs as quickly as it retracts existing ones, occasionally you glimpse flickers of stars and lights swirling around under the surface, but they are always consumed by blackness a moment later.

It has no eyes, no mouth, no perceptible form that lets you ascribe humanity or awareness to it, and yet you can feel its alien intelligence, feel it probing your mind, trying to find ways in. You can sense it trying to understand what you are in much the same way you are trying to parse is inscrutable form in return.

The [[lookup @name]] is an Abyssal creature that has existed on Ember for millennia, and perhaps even longer before it's arrival during the Shattering.

Vhismara's Claw.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Vhismara's Claws are monsters that seem to be the disembodied large hands of an even greater monster; however, this is not accurate. Like many other Abyssal entities, they are merely concentrated amounts of Abyssal energy. Vhismara's Claws are nothing like other life forms and exist without internal organs. They are immune to various effects and do not require food, water, or sleep.

Behavior

It’s said that Vhismara's Claws are Abyssal monsters with a strong connection to the Outer God Vhismara. This may be true, or it may simply be a monster that Vhismara uses more often than not to do his bidding and to rip apart mortal creatures. Vhismara's Claws spend most of their existence hiding in dark places, often sticking to high vaulted ceilings. They drop down onto unsuspecting prey and use their considerable size to pin a creature before rending it apart with their other sharp-clawed fingers. They are particularly mindless monsters in most circumstances, but they also follow a dark willpower from far away and will toy with mortals in certain situations for the thrill of the chase.

Lore

Vhismara's Claws appeared in Ember during the Abyssal Shear, and while they are not powerful, they can cause unimaginable destruction to environments and areas if left unchecked.
Vhismara's Claw.biographypublic:
A massive, disembodied hand with six fingers emerges from the gloom, crawling with its nightmarish claws upon the ground with some unknown purpose or design. This grotesque hand is misshapen and sinewy, lacking the vibrancy of life, and coated in matted, foul-smelling fur. Each finger is tipped with large, crimson claws reminiscent of being drenched in blood.

Vhismara's Claws are not just one monster from a larger creature; instead, they seem to be a distinct embodiment of something far more deadly. Although they are less prevalent than some of the weaker Abyssal monsters, they can still gather large numbers in deep darkness to ambush unsuspecting beings and rip them to shreds.

Gohema's Eye.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The Gohema is a colossal Abyssal entity that has been trapped within a sealed chamber of the Lightless Halls for thousands of years. It has slowly fed upon Abyssal energy that has bled through the fabric of the Ember Cosmos during that time and has grown to fill the entire space. Its actual body is a formless mass of flesh that covers the whole floor of the chamber, but it also has several external appendages that creep and writhe in and out of its form, connected by long tendrils that reabsorb its mass and reappear in different places or move independently. The largest of these appendages appears like a huge head with an eyeless maw that attempts to swallow hapless foes; this head contains the central nervous system and, once destroyed, the entire monster would collapse. The Gohema also has several twisting tendrils that lash out and wrap around the central column. Its most crucial appendages, however, are its eyes, which contain sensitive nerve endings and allow the entire Gohema entity to see. This makes the eyes incredibly vulnerable to damage, and the Gohema often tries to hide them behind its head or in various darkened places around the chamber.

Behavior

The Gohema has no mind to speak of; it is an Abyssal Entity of great power and deadly hunger that acts primarily on instinct and a deep, unsettling, and ravenous rage towards any living creatures around it. Once it is unsealed, the Gohema will first attempt to destroy anyone who enters its prison, and if it succeeds, it will undoubtedly spread and grow larger, feeding on more living matter and energy until it can challenge the gods.

Lore

The Gohema may have been a much smaller Abyssal entity long ago, but after the events of the Unveiling, it became trapped in the Sealed Chamber for hundreds of thousands of years. It grew slowly over that time, gradually absorbing energy and gradually becoming a mass of writhing flesh. It is thankfully mindless, as such isolation would be a mind-numbing fate for any immortal creature of Ember.
Gohema's Eye.biographypublic:

The Gohema is a massive Abyssal monster that appears more like some kind of malignant growth than a creature with organs or legs. While the entire monster is one entity, its appendages are split between a Head, three Tendrils, a Tail, and an Eye.

Ram.name: Ram

They cannot move to or occupy any space outside of this area.

Abyssal Remains.name: Abyssal Remains
Abyssal Remains.description:
When the [[lookup @name]] dies, it dissolves into a thick liquid often described as “melted shadow,” which spreads in an oozing pour from the place where it died, soaking a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=0CtCrqPc5KbnIvoc]]-foot radius around it in viscous corruption.

Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=0CtCrqPc5KbnIvoc]], each creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=0CtCrqPc5KbnIvoc]] feet of the [[lookup @name]] when it dies.

Failure: The target is cursed with Cursed Vision until the end of its next long rest.

Cursed Vision. Shadowy film clings to the creature’s eyes. While afflicted, the creature has disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, and attack rolls against the creature have advantage. In addition, the creature can’t benefit from darkvision.

Note: After Alpha, Abyssal Residue may remain on the ground and/or be found in locations where an abyssal creature died, affecting anyone who moves through its space. When this feature is active, the residue will remain in place for 1 week before fading away. If located in an area without direct light from Lantyr, the residue will remain for 1 month.

Gohema's Tail.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The Gohema is a colossal Abyssal entity that has been trapped within a sealed chamber of the Lightless Halls for thousands of years. It has slowly fed upon Abyssal energy that has bled through the fabric of the Ember Cosmos during that time and has grown to fill the entire space. Its actual body is a formless mass of flesh that covers the whole floor of the chamber, but it also has several external appendages that creep and writhe in and out of its form, connected by long tendrils that reabsorb its mass and reappear in different places or move independently. The largest of these appendages appears like a huge head with an eyeless maw that attempts to swallow hapless foes; this head contains the central nervous system and, once destroyed, the entire monster would collapse. The Gohema also has several twisting tendrils that lash out and wrap around the central column. Its most crucial appendages, however, are its eyes, which contain sensitive nerve endings and allow the entire Gohema entity to see. This makes the eyes incredibly vulnerable to damage, and the Gohema often tries to hide them behind its head or in various darkened places around the chamber.

Behavior

The Gohema has no mind to speak of; it is an Abyssal Entity of great power and deadly hunger that acts primarily on instinct and a deep, unsettling, and ravenous rage towards any living creatures around it. Once it is unsealed, the Gohema will first attempt to destroy anyone who enters its prison, and if it succeeds, it will undoubtedly spread and grow larger, feeding on more living matter and energy until it can challenge the gods.

Lore

The Gohema may have been a much smaller Abyssal entity long ago, but after the events of the Unveiling, it became trapped in the Sealed Chamber for hundreds of thousands of years. It grew slowly over that time, gradually absorbing energy and gradually becoming a mass of writhing flesh. It is thankfully mindless, as such isolation would be a mind-numbing fate for any immortal creature of Ember.
Gohema's Tail.biographypublic:
A singular, much larger tendril with spiky, hard tips on the end slowly rises from below. Its movements are far slower than the other appendages of the terrifying monster below, but what it lacks in speed, this tendril seems far stronger and more durable.

The Gohema is a massive Abyssal monster that appears more like some kind of malignant growth than a creature with organs or legs. While the entire monster is one entity, its appendages are split between a Head, three Tendrils, a Tail, and an Eye.

Gohema's Tendril.name: Gohema's Tendril

Abyssal Monster.name: Abyssal Monster
Abyssal Monster.description:
The [[lookup @name]] is an unknowable alien entity. It is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (Insight) checks made to ascertain the [[lookup @name]]'s intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.

The [[lookup @name]] and all Abyssal creatures are opposed by Life and Light, making them vulnerable to radiant damage.

Defensive Shielding.name: Defensive Shielding
Defensive Shielding.description: When the @UUID[Actor.Q5iudLrTvVX7AeFF]{Gohema's Head} is within 15 feet of the [[lookup @name]], the [[lookup @name]] can use their reaction to take the damage instead.

A large tendril of flesh writhes upwards out of the body below, dripping with slimy excretions. Its horrifying mass is a deep crimson and black color, as if it were covered in ancient, dried blood. Its movements are lightning fast, and they seem to be able to unerringly seek out living creatures to crush or pull towards the maw in its head.

The Gohema is a massive Abyssal monster that appears more like some kind of malignant growth than a creature with organs or legs. While the entire monster is one entity, its appendages are split between a Head, three Tendrils, a Tail, and an Eye.

Baradom.name: Baradom

Baradom Plate.name: Baradom Plate
Baradom Plate.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{drake} has a rough hide of thick and inter-locking scales.

Tail.name: Tail
Tail.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can lash out with it's elongated and muscular tail.

Claw.name: Claw
Claw.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has formidable claws, each the size of a steel blade.

Burrower.name: Burrower
Burrower.description:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has a supernatural ability to rapidly burrow through solid surfaces which are not entirely impermeable.

Additionally, it can compress its body to pass through apertures that can accommodate ¼ of its Size.
Burrower.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} emerges from a subterranean position with surprising and sudden force. This action may only be activated immediately the creature leaves the @Condition[burrowing] state.

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} erupts to Strike against all enemies within its weapon range with an Empowered attack.

Immutable Form.name: Immutable Form
Immutable Form.description: The @ref[actor.name] is immune to any spell or effect which alters its physical form.

Extended Breath.name: Extended Breath
Extended Breath.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can hold its breath for 15 minutes.

Spellmute.name: Spellmute
Spellmute.description:
Currents of magic flow strangely around you, as if unaware of your presence.

You cannot perform any action with the Spell tag. Spells which target you suffer +2 Banes regardless of whether they impose harmful or beneficial effects.

Concussive Blows.name: Concussive Blows
Concussive Blows.description:
Your physical power wielding melee weapons which deal Bludgeoning damage can cause the Staggered condition on Critical Hits which deal damage to Health.

The Staggered effect lasts for 1 round and reduces your target's maximum Action by 1.

Restraining Chomp.name: Restraining Chomp
Restraining Chomp.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} uses its powerful jaws to bite and hold a target with a powerful chomp.
Restraining Chomp.actiondesc: The creature chomps down upon its target. If the attack is successful and the target is equal or lesser in Size, the target is also Restrained until this creature chooses to release it or the restraint is otherwise broken. Only one target may be restrained by this action at a given time.

Thrash.name: Thrash
Thrash.description: Once the @ref[actor.name]{creature} has an enemy restrained, it will thrash violently dealing terrible blows to the grasped victim.
Thrash.actiondesc: The creature deals Deadly damage to a target that it currently has Restrained.

Trampling Charge.name: Trampling Charge
Trampling Charge.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} uses its prodigious size to charge forward, trampling smaller creatures that stand in its way.
Trampling Charge.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} moves forward up to twice its Stride, attacking the Reflex defense of all creatures in its path. Targets who are half the creature's size or smaller are @Condition[stunned] until the end of their next turn as they are slammed aside.

Baradom.biographyprivate:
A gargantuan beast, the Baradom is perhaps the largest lizard on the whole of Ember, and they exist entirely within the sprawling underground of the Pathways.

Anatomy

The Baradom is covered in thick, hardened scales that provide exceptional natural armor, making it nearly impervious to most physical attacks. It has a massive, protruding belly that stores vast amounts of fat, allowing it to go long periods without needing to hunt or eat. The creature’s most distinctive feature is its oversized mouth, covered in immensely thick scales and capable of unhinging like a snake’s jaw to swallow smaller creatures whole. Within its maw are rows of sharp and blunt teeth capable of tearing through flesh and crushing bone with ease.

Behavior

The Baradom is an indolent creature, rarely exerting itself unless absolutely necessary. It typically spends all hours of the day sleeping, save for those rare moments when it decides to move to a new spot or go scrounging for something to eat. It is omnivorous, eating vast amounts of whatever organic material it can find, be it flora or unlucky fauna.

This reptilian giant is primarily indifferent to most creatures unless hunting, including adventurers, due to its exceptional natural defense; it perceives very few things as a legitimate threat and has no known predators except perhaps Dragons. When encountered, the Baradom often remains motionless or lazily observes newcomers, uninterested in confrontation. However, if threatened or persistently disturbed, it will defend itself by using its powerful jaws and sheer bulk to crush or consume aggressors.

Lore

Stories and legends state that Baradoms can live for centuries, if not longer, growing ever larger and acquiring near-total immunity to other dangers in the Pathways.

Poachers and hunters value the creature’s thick hide and formidable teeth and they would surely fetch a high price on any market if they ever appeared. However, because engaging with a Baradom is more trouble than the bounty is worth, few have attempted such dangerous ventures.
Baradom.biographypublic: The Baradom is a massive, lethargic lizard, both awe-inspiring and oddly endearing due to its prodigious size and laid-back demeanor. It often lies sprawled out in the darkness of the pathways, its enormous pot-belly rising and falling with each leisurely breath. Its dark, thick scales seem almost impenetrable, each one an armor plate rather than typical reptilian skin.
Baradom.biographyappearance: With scales thick as shields, this great beast regards you and the world at large with sleepy and indifferent detachment. Its mouth, alarmingly large and wide, droops open slightly, as though it has no energy to hold it shut. Just beyond its heavy, armored may are rows of massive teeth that look more than capable of rending apart anything they sink into.

Sitherian.name: Sitherian

Venomous Bite.name: Venomous Bite
Venomous Bite.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks, injects toxin which, if successful, inflicts the @Condition[poisoned] condition for 6 Turns.

Web Spinner.name: Web Spinner
Web Spinner.description:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can create powerfully adhesive webbing. It ignores any movement restrictions or restraints otherwise caused by webbing.

While in contact with a web, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} knows the precise location of any other creature in contact with the same web.
Web Spinner.actiondesc: The creature can spend 10 minutes to spin a new new section of webbing that covers a 5-foot area.

Pack Hunter.name: Pack Hunter
Pack Hunter.description:
This creature is a pack hunter, relying on its allies to flank and harrass a target to render it exposed to further harm.

This creature doubles number of Boons awarded from attacking a Flanked enemy.

Fangs.name: Fangs
Fangs.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has fangs that are both sharp and venomous.

Arachnid Chitin.name: Arachnid Chitin
Arachnid Chitin.descriptionpublic: Chitinous plates that provide natural protection for arachnids.

Clinging Grip.name: Clinging Grip
Clinging Grip.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is able to cling to vertical or overhead surfaces with exceptional grip or adhesion. This creature can avoid falling as long as they are adjacent to any solid surface which can reasonably support them.
Clinging Grip.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can drop from overhead to Strike a creature below it. The target creature suffers an Empowered attack which, if successful, knocks them @Condition[prone] in addition to dealing damage.

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can suffer falling damage from this attack only if it misses its target.

Sitherian.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Similar to a more traditional giant spider, a Sitherian's arachnid body is comprised of a large abdomen and a smaller cephalothorax, marked by spotted hues of dusky orange and a grotesque web of dark gray flesh between its eight spindly legs. Abyssal physiology has strengthened their survivability and bolstered their intelligence. Consequently, Children of Sitheera are rather cunning and can survive for an extremely long time on a considerably modest diet.

Behavior

Sitherian are extremely predatory, and will lair in a location or environment that caters to their rapacious nature. In combat, a Sitherian relies on the potency of its venomous bite after a victim has been woefully ensnared in the arachnid's intricate system of webs.

Lore

The genealogical connection of Sitherian to the Spider Goddess is a secret to the people of Ember, who generally regard these voracious arachnids as natural creatures. However, every spider on Ember is an aspect of Sitheera to some degree, as they are the true direct followers of the Watcher herself. Although they propagate and grow and die like other living creatures within the Cosmos, spiders of Ember possess a primordial link to their creator and seethe with latent Abyssal energy.

Since their introduction to the Cosmos, Sitherian and other spiders have spread out and settled in almost every corner of the world. Sitherian are particularly prevalent in the sprawling subterranea of the Pathways, where great nests and lairs are quite common.
Sitherian.biographypublic: A @ref[name] is an arachnid beast descended from their namesake — Sitheera, the Watcher. Heralded by the vibrations of their intricate lattice of webs, Sitherian are capable of injecting a potent venom from their chelicerae fangs, and can extrude silk from spinnerets located at the rear of their immense ovoid abdomens.
Sitherian.biographyappearance: This large eight-legged creature boasts two fanged chelicerae that appear to drip a viscous green venom. Its ten reflective eyes regard you with a keen animal maliciousness as it crawls forth from its web-shrouded hiding place.

Giant Kezus Jelly.name: Giant Kezus Jelly

Blindsense.name: Blindsense
Blindsense.description: The Kezus Jelly cannot see, hear, taste or smell, and perceives its environment through a natural blindsense, allowing it to perceive creatures even if they are hidden or invisible.

Contact Hazard.name: Contact Hazard
Contact Hazard.description: Creatures attempting to grapple, grab, carry, push, or otherwise make physical contact with the jelly automatically trigger its Debilitating Tendrils reaction.

Freedom of Movement.name: Freedom of Movement
Freedom of Movement.description: The jelly ignores magical effects that would reduce its speed or cause it to be restrained. It can spend 5 feet of movement to escape from nonmagical restraints or being grappled.

Reactive.name: Reactive
Reactive.description: The jelly can take one &Reference[Reaction] on every turn of combat, but only to use Debilitating Tendrils.

Special Adaptation.name: Special Adaptation
Special Adaptation.description: The Kezus Jelly has incredible resistance to high temperatures and fire damage. Additionally, the jelly is resistant to bludgeoning damage, and without a mind to speak of, is immune to psychic damage.

Confusing Patterns.name: Confusing Patterns
Confusing Patterns.description:
The jelly begins to pulse and flash in wild patterns of color and light. Whenever a creature that can see the jelly and isn’t incapacitated starts its turn within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet of the jelly, it must make the following saving throw.

Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]].

Failure: The creature can’t take reactions until the start of its next turn, and it has disadvantage on the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check it makes before then.

Scintillating Agony.name: Scintillating Agony
Scintillating Agony.description:
The jelly turns blood red and pulses with waves of darker and lighter crimson as it inflicts psychic harm on multiple targets. Each creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet of the [[lookup @name]] must make the following saving throw.

Charisma Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], each creature in the area.

Failure: The creature takes [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: Half damage.

Debilitating Tendrils.name: Debilitating Tendrils
Debilitating Tendrils.description:
Trigger: A creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet of the jelly makes an attack against it.

Response: The jelly recoils and whips its tendrils at the attacker.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], the attacker.

Failure: The attacker has the &Reference[poisoned] condition for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, it also has the &Reference[paralyzed] condition. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Giant Kezus Jelly.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Kezus Jelly are bioluminescent jellyfish ith long tendrils and tails that swirl behind them as they propel themselves through water by pulsing their heads. Kezus Jelly are uncomfortable in bright light and seek to avoid illumination.

Behavior

Kezus Jelly are generally gentle creatures, favoring evasion over confrontation. Unless provoked or threatened, these creatures tend to not be menacing to other species. Kezus Jelly are uncomfortable in bright light and seek to avoid illumination.

Even provoked, the jelly tends to be defensive, using its tendrils to inflict horrible pain on would-be attackers, and utilizing a special bioluminescent pattern to confuse and disrupt would-be attackers. If pressed, it can utilize powerful psychic attacks, but only does so as a last resort.

Lore

For centuries, the Kezus Jelly has been a part of the vibrant Kadisos ecosystem, having long adapted to the super heated waters of the caldera. They are considered one of the more beautiful creatures to live in the caldera lake, but a beauty which should be enjoyed from a distance.

Rarely, Kezus Jelly are found in the Pathways in large underwater lakes where darkness allows them to exist comfortably at all hours.
Giant Kezus Jelly.biographypublic:
You behold an ethereal display of bioluminescence and elegant fluidity. Its bulbous, umbrella-shaped body pulses with a translucent glow, revealing a mesmerizing dance of colors within its soft structure. Usually, a soft pink and calming blue light emanates from its organism, accentuated by a constellation of star-like points, shimmering in sync with the creature's rhythmic pulses. Delicate tentacles, stretching several feet in length, trail its body in an exquisite ballet, leaving a mesmerizing trail of luminary discharge in their wake.

Kezus Jelly are generally gentle creatures, favoring evasion over confrontation. Unless provoked or threatened, these creatures tend to not be menacing to other species. These jellies spend their days in deep and dark waters, only emerging into shallows once the sun has set.

Gore Bird.name: Gore Bird

Rot-Stained Beak.name: Rot-Stained Beak
Rot-Stained Beak.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity100]], if the target is hit.

Failure: [[/damage activity=dnd5eactivity100]]

Dying Call.name: Dying Call
Dying Call.description: When the gore bird has been reduced to 3 or fewer hit points, it calls out for another gore bird to consume and avenge it. The closest gore bird within 50 feet that is not currently engaged in combat immediately attempts to locate the dying gore bird and enter combat, whether or not the bird that used this ability has died.

Gore Bird.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The Kadisoan gore bird is easily recognized by the bright red coloration of its beak and rectrices. Male gore birds are typically decorated with subtle geometric patterns of black and gray on their breasts and the sides of their heads, while females of the species — which are generally darker in appearance — tend to exhibit more uniform mantles and undercoats.

Behavior

Gore birds tend to congregate in swarms, which greatly enhances their survivability. A flock of these tiny avian scavengers is commonly referred to as a "Ravage" of Gore Birds, and the opportunistic creatures are known to form symbiotic relationships with larger predators (such as suarroks, sisastl, and leviathans). Gore bird swarms prefer to use terrain or allies to their advantage when confronted — particularly when targeted by ranged attacks — and tend to focus their efforts on smaller foes in combat. If at all possible, a lone gore bird will usually avoid combat with a larger foe.

Wherever a gore bird swarm can be found, carnage and rot are most certainly nearby. Swarms of gore birds are often found dining on the fetid remains of ill-fated creatures; naturally, this sometimes includes the corpses of waylaid travelers and star-crossed adventurers. Typically, a solitary gore bird isn't too far from the rest of its flock.

Lore

Though native to the island of Kadisos, gore birds have made their way to the Arctus Plateau and beyond thanks to minor domestication efforts and the slow migration of their larger symbiotic partners. And while relatively uncommon, gore birds do make effective familiars for spellcasters who aren't deterred by the gore bird's unsavory reputation.
Gore Bird.biographypublic:
A tiny, keen-eyed bird appears to feast on the rotted carcass of some recently deceased creature. Its sharp red beaks tear at the putrid meat with abandon. The dark, charcoal-colored feathers of this carnivorous avian are offset by the brilliance of its crimson tail feathers. With a strip of sinew dangling from its bloody beak, the bird emits an unsettling caw to aptly remind you of its presence.

The tiny [[lookup @name]] is a swift, carnivorous carrion birds found all across Ember. Though they primarily feed on carcasses, they have been known to aggressively hunt down prey in great flocks when food is scarce.

Gore Bird Swarm.name: Gore Bird Swarm

Rot-Stained Beaks.name: Rot-Stained Beaks
Rot-Stained Beaks.descriptionprivate:
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]], reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: [[/damage average activity=dnd5eactivity000]] damage, or [[/damage average activity=P5QriPbtnLcW1Yux]] damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity100]], if the target is hit.

Failure: [[/damage average activity=dnd5eactivity100]] damage, and the target has the &Reference[poisoned] condition for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the target succeeds on the save or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to this poison effect for 24 hours.

Keen Sight and Smell.name: Keen Sight and Smell
Keen Sight and Smell.description: The gore bird swarm has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or smell.

Swarm.name: Swarm
Swarm.description: The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny bird. The swarm can’t regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

Mephitic Nature.name: Mephitic Nature
Mephitic Nature.description: The gore bird swarm doesn’t require air.

Though native to the island of Kadisos, gore birds have made their way to the Arctus Plateau and beyond thanks to minor domestication efforts and the slow migration of their larger symbiotic partners. And while relatively uncommon, gore birds do make effective familiars for spellcasters who aren't deterred by the gore bird's unsavory reputation.
Gore Bird Swarm.biographypublic:
A large swarm of tiny, keen-eyed birds circles above, their charcoal-colored feathers a stark contrast to their sharp red beaks. It is nearly impossible to see how many of them there are, but as they grow closer, making an unsettling cawing noise and rustling their crimson tailfeathers, you can smell the rot of the putrid flesh they so often feast on.

The [[lookup @name]] is a swift, dangerous thing found all across Ember. Though these tiny birds typically feed on existing carcasses, flocks such as these have been known to hunt down prey on their own instead.

Grey Hydroxol.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Exceptionally large predatory amphibians, Hydroxol are covered in slick, waterproof skin, long bioluminescent frills, and external gills that allow them to breathe water. Their thin legs are tipped with long, sharp claws, and their wide mouths are lined with tiny, razor sharp teeth. In their maws are also large, sticky tongues that they can use to latch onto distant prey and pull toward their mouths.

Hydroxol are typically blue in color, with pink tongues and pink-blue bioluminescent features, but there are larger Grey Hydroxol that have gray skin, and blue tongues. Grey Hydroxol are rarer, and can be significantly more aggressive.

Behavior

Hydroxols thrive in the freshwater springs, rivers, and subterranean lakes scattered throughout Ember, and specifically congregate wherever large amounts of elemental magic collect, or where the light and energies of Mayis are more heavily resonant. Their lairs, often hidden in the shadowy depths of underwater caves or beneath fallen logs, are unmistakably marked by a luminous glow, betraying their presence to those who know what to look for. They are largely nocturnal, using the cover of darkness to hunt and avoiding the harsher daylight.

Primarily ambush predators, Hydroxols lie in wait amongst rocks and submerged vegetation, using their bioluminescent markings to hypnotically lure prey closer. Once within striking distance, they lunge with swift, lethal precision, swallowing smaller creatures whole in a single gulp. Despite their predatory nature, Hydroxols are solitary beings, fiercely territorial and intolerant of rivals. They communicate through intricate light patterns along their bodies, which serve as both a warning to intruders and an alluring dance during the mating season.

When nesting, female Hydroxols deposit their eggs in secluded, well-guarded underwater alcoves. They are known to guard these nests ferociously until the hatchlings are self-sufficient, ensuring the continuation of their enigmatic lineage.

Additionally, the immense mouth and its formidable digestive tract often harbor the remains of swallowed prey, sometimes yielding unexpected treasures and relics from unfortunate victims.

Lore

Folklore and ancient texts suggest that the Hydroxol's origins are found on Mayis, and that they are terrestrial versions of larger, more fanciful elementals that exist on the greater water moon. There are also some that posit the Hydroxols were gifts from the water courts long ago, placed upon Ember to add to its rich tapestry of creatures, and to leave Mayis' mark upon its surface.

In truth, nobody actually knows where they came from, and many don't even know they exist until the first time they run into the creatures.

Hunters and explorers brave enough to confront a Hydroxol are often richly rewarded. The creature's bioluminescent markings can be harvested and used in the creation of radiant inks favored by artists and mages. Its external gills are highly prized for alchemical concoctions that grant enhanced underwater breathing.

The gelatinous hide of the Hydroxol, when properly treated, produces a durable, flexible material that remains waterproof, making it rare but sought after material for waterproof packs, water repellent cloaks, and similar.
Grey Hydroxol.biographypublic:
This huge creature watches its surroundings with keen eyes, its wide maw hanging open, prepared to snap at a moment's notice. A long tongue moves back and forth, like it is actively scenting the area. It's wide frame boasts an almost gelatinous sheen with threads of shimmering ethereal light running down its back from head to tail, and large glowing gills pulse with each breath it takes.

[[lookup @name]] are larger, more aggressive variants of the typical Hydroxol, and have bodies with a pronounced silver-gray hue and colorful markings that are more purple than pink. Their tongues and the insides of their mouths are also a striking blue color.

Gumtoad.name: Gumtoad

Adhesive.name: Adhesive
Adhesive.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] can adhere to vertical surfaces, including those of difficult terrain, without needing to make an ability check.

Barbed Tongue.name: Barbed Tongue
Barbed Tongue.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is Medium or smaller, it is also &Reference[Grappled apply=false] (escape DC [[lookup @check.dc.value activity=VV5bJucurCEESIzS]]).

Gumtoad Glue.name: Gumtoad Glue
Gumtoad Glue.descriptionprivate: The sticky secretions on a gumtoad's skin can be collected and used as an adhesive, a mild toxin, or a way to do painful medical procedures when no herbalist can be found - it helps to adhere things together but creates a mild paralyzing and sleep-inducing effect when consumed.

Tongue Boomerang.name: Tongue Boomerang

Strength Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=qEXLGM2HNlc4dO4K]]

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage.

Standing Leap.name: Standing Leap

Gumtoad.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Gumtoads have a large rounded belly and are brightly colored, with elaborate patterns that they can change at a moment's notice by shifting the colors on their skin. It is believed that they use the colors and patterns they display to communicate with other gumtoads in mating rituals and fights over territory, though this has never been proven. Their skin has a somewhat glossy appearance, caused by the stickiness of the substance they secrete, which they use to take down their prey and stick to surfaces. While their tongues are rarely seen unless they are hunting, they are quite long, reaching up to 30-40 feet away from their bodies.

Behavior

Gumtoads are amphibious creatures, able to thrive on land or sea. The stickiness of their bodies means that they can also be found on canyon walls and even the occasional cave ceiling, though they are rarely too far from some source of water. While they will use their tongues to clear out ketral lairs and feast on insects, they excel in and prefer attacking larger creatures by using the stickiness of their bodies and their long prehensile tongues to drag down birds and trip up creatures that move on land, but often do not hunt for weeks on end, making it easy for nearby creatures to forget about the threat they pose.

Once one gumtoad has landed a solid hit on a target, it attempts to either pull the prey to it or use its tongue to propel itself toward the creature as a weapon. The substance that helps gumtoads stick to their prey also has a mild paralyzing and soporific effect, making whoever the gumtoads affect sleepy and still. Once the prey is no longer moving, gumtoads use barbs on their tongue to slowly lick the flesh off of their prey, beginning while it is still alive.

Lore

Gumtoad secretions can be collected shortly after their death and used as a mild toxin or as a way to make painful medical procedures possible when there is no healer in the area by stopping someone who is injured from thrashing while temporary aid is rendered. Their tongues are also extraordinarily strong and can be dried out and turned into a leather-like material that is is sometimes used instead of ropes or fastenings.

Gumtoads are amphibious, and are found anywhere there are substantial inland rivers and a temperate or warm climate, including the Arctus Plateau. Their original origin is unknown.
Gumtoad.biographypublic:
The squat and colorful skin of bulk of these colorful frog-like amphibians is deceiving - while they might seem to be nothing more than odd decoration stuck to the canyon walls by their sticky skin, their long prehensile tongues dart back and forth, readying to shoot out and wrap themselves around the gumtoad's next unsuspecting target.

These brightly-colored large amphibians use their tongues to reach out and attach themselves to larger or flying prey, forcing it down with their weight or by impeding its movement. While they are animals, they appear to have some form of rudimentary communication via the colors and patterns they display on their skin, which they use for mating and to warn other gumtoads away from their prey.

The tail of the Hydroxol is long and paddle-like, adorned with a vibrant, membranous fin that give it super agility in water and a useful weapon outside of it.

Bestial Senses.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has finely honed senses and is particularly perceptive of their environment, all Awareness checks gain +2 Boons.

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can suffer falling damage from this attack only if it misses its target.
