Light Scales.name: Light Scales
Light Scales.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has skin that is covered in lightweight scales that provide some modest protection from harm.

Light Weapon Training.name: Light Weapon Training
Light Weapon Training.description: You know how to wield light weapons fluidly with a high degree of maneuverability and grace in combat. You are Trained with all weapons in the Light and Balanced categories.
Light Weapon Training.actiondesc:
You dart forward nimbly, making a strike with sudden and unexpected swiftness to perform a Strike with a Finesse weapon against a single target with an increased range of +2 feet.

The attack is Difficult, but you do not move from your current position nor does this attack provoke Disengagement.

Skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
Skirmisher.description: You are adept at entering and exiting the fray. When moving out of the Engagement radius of an enemy, that enemy has 2 Banes to any Disengagement Strike against you.

Jobri.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Evolution has been kind to these curious lizards, who have developed a canny sense of survivability over centuries and centuries of proliferation. The lithe, six-legged form of @ref[name] has contributed to a rather adaptable physiology, capable of inhabiting nearly any environment suited to their cold-blooded nature. The soles of the @ref[name]'s padded feet are covered with countless microscopic setae that allow it to climb and adhere to steep surfaces with ease.

Behavior

[[lookup @name]] are omnivorous, and are known to feed on insects, rodents, and fruits in equal measure. Reports of ornery and hostile @ref[name] are relatively few and far between, but rare incidents of feral @ref[name] aren't altogether unheard of. These amiable reptiles make worthy and capable companions, and are considered by many to be among of the Arctus Plateau's most genial of creatures.

Lore

@ref[name] can be found throughout the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} and beyond, where they are known to dwell in subterranean areas and surface biomes alike. In particular, @ref[name] are most ample among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}, and their implementation by denizens of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.SZq6RXsfxKownAN6]{Sinkhole Depths} is as commonplace as horses or @UUID[Actor.QGpM0XLtyG7zN76l]{rask} on the surface world.
Jobri.biographypublic: @ref[name] are six-legged lizards native to the Arctus Plateau, where they are commonly cultivated as riding mounts and beasts of burden. These docile reptilian creatures are generally considered to be more eccentric than other domesticated mounts like horses and rask, but are equally as gregarious as their mammalian contemporaries.
Jobri.biographyappearance: The eyes of this large reptilian beast are remarkably big, and the padded five-toed feet that accompany its six muscular legs only accentuate the creature's charming awkwardness. Fitted with tack and bridle, this riding lizard lurks with a measure of domesticated calm, absentmindedly hunting for insects with each flick of its prehensile tongue.

Kadhana Lizard.name: Kadhana Lizard

Aggressive.name: Aggressive
Aggressive.description: As a bonus action, the Kadhana Lizard can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

Numbing Saliva.name: Numbing Saliva
Numbing Saliva.description:
When charged, the [[lookup @name]]'s teeth are coated in a poisonous saliva, and the next time it hits a creature with its Bite and deals damage, it can expend 1 charge to inflict a debilitating poison on its prey.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12.

Failure: The target has the &Reference[poisoned] condition for 10 minutes.

While the target is affected by this trait, each time the [[lookup @name lowercase]] hits it with its @UUID[Actor.McN3C0nRW9WdLfQa.Item.OQzvoRNuRsyzjFA9]{Bite}, the condition from this trait is replaced with &Reference[restrained], then &Reference[incapacitated], and the duration resets to 10 minutes.

The [[lookup @name]] is immune to this poison, including poison from other kadhana.

Ambusher.name: Ambusher
Ambusher.description: In the first round of a combat, the [[lookup @name lowercase]] has advantage on attack rolls against any creature it has &reference[surprise]{surprised}.

Hold Breath.name: Hold Breath
Hold Breath.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] can hold its breath for 60 minutes.

Kadhana Lizard.biographyprivate:
Appearance

Kadhana Lizards are squat, stocky, long-bodied giant lizards with iridescent skin that glimmers in multiple colors under the sunlight. Their most prominent feature is a long, spiked dorsal fin. They also have large, clawed and webbed feet which makes them equally good at climbing and swimming, and a huge mouth full of razor sharp teeth suited to ripping apart prey.

In terms of dimorphism, males are more dull-coloured, tending to appear with greater concentrations of green, yellow and brown in their scales, giving them excellent camouflage against the sands, rocks, and grass of their habitat. With the brighter blue-green skin, females are best suited to aquatic environments, where their iridescent scales blend most effectively.

Behavior

A well-adapted creature, the Kadhana Lizard can be found all across the coastal environs of Kadisos. They are as adept at prowling the grasslands and cliff sides in search of nests to pilfer, as they are at gliding through the saltwater pursuing fish and crustaceans.

Female kadhana are primarily aquatic hunters, relying on their blue scales to help them blend in while chasing down fish, while males prefer prowling the bluffs looking for nests of easy prey, or run down animals on the coasts.

When mating, female kadhana rely on their colorful skin to attract males to their nests. Otherwise, they are solitary creatures, prone to defending their hunting grounds against fellow Kadhana.

History

An indigenous species of Kadisos, these creatures have thrived along the coasts, adapting and evolving with the changing environment over many generations. Before the arrival of Scoris and her Ashka, the Kadhana were much smaller, and duller looking, but the amount of magic that seeped into the land as a result of the Ashka caused these creatures to become warped, and gain new abilities which proved highly beneficial to them.

Loot

Kadhana scales and skin is prized as a material for clothing and decorative textiles, while their poison glands are useful for the production of pain medicines.

Kezus Jelly.name: Kezus Jelly

Blindsense.name: Blindsense
Blindsense.description: The Kezus Jelly cannot see, hear, taste or smell, and perceives its environment through a natural blindsense, allowing it to perceive creatures even if they are hidden or invisible.

Contact Hazard.name: Contact Hazard
Contact Hazard.description: Creatures attempting to grapple, grab, carry, push, or otherwise make physical contact with the jelly automatically trigger its Debilitating Tendrils reaction.

Freedom of Movement.name: Freedom of Movement
Freedom of Movement.description: The jelly ignores magical effects that would reduce its speed or cause it to be restrained. It can spend 5 feet of movement to escape from nonmagical restraints or being grappled.

Reactive.name: Reactive
Reactive.description: The jelly can take one &Reference[Reaction] on every turn of combat, but only to use Debilitating Tendrils.

Special Adaptation.name: Special Adaptation
Special Adaptation.description: The Kezus Jelly has incredible resistance to high temperatures and fire damage. Additionally, the jelly is resistant to bludgeoning damage, and without a mind to speak of, is immune to psychic damage.

Confusing Patterns.name: Confusing Patterns
Confusing Patterns.description:
The jelly begins to pulse and flash in wild patterns of color and light. Whenever a creature that can see the jelly and isn’t incapacitated starts its turn within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet of the jelly, it must make the following saving throw.

Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]].

Failure: The creature can’t take reactions until the start of its next turn, and it has disadvantage on the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check it makes before then.

Scintillating Agony.name: Scintillating Agony
Scintillating Agony.description:
The jelly turns blood red and pulses with waves of darker and lighter crimson as it inflicts psychic harm on multiple targets. Each creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet of the [[lookup @name]] must make the following saving throw.

Charisma Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], each creature in the area.

Failure: The creature takes [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: Half damage.

Debilitating Tendrils.name: Debilitating Tendrils
Debilitating Tendrils.description:
Trigger: A creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet of the jelly makes an attack against it.

Response: The jelly recoils and whips its tendrils at the attacker.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], the attacker.

Failure: The attacker has the &Reference[poisoned] condition for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, it also has the &Reference[paralyzed] condition. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Kezus Jelly.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Kezus Jelly are bioluminescent jellyfish ith long tendrils and tails that swirl behind them as they propel themselves through water by pulsing their heads. Kezus Jelly are uncomfortable in bright light and seek to avoid illumination.

Behavior

Kezus Jelly are generally gentle creatures, favoring evasion over confrontation. Unless provoked or threatened, these creatures tend to not be menacing to other species. Kezus Jelly are uncomfortable in bright light and seek to avoid illumination.

Even provoked, the jelly tends to be defensive, using its tendrils to inflict horrible pain on would-be attackers, and utilizing a special bioluminescent pattern to confuse and disrupt would-be attackers. If pressed, it can utilize powerful psychic attacks, but only does so as a last resort.

Lore

For centuries, the Kezus Jelly has been a part of the vibrant Kadisos ecosystem, having long adapted to the super heated waters of the caldera. They are considered one of the more beautiful creatures to live in the caldera lake, but a beauty which should be enjoyed from a distance.

Rarely, Kezus Jelly are found in the Pathways in large underwater lakes where darkness allows them to exist comfortably at all hours.
Kezus Jelly.biographypublic:
You behold an ethereal display of bioluminescence and elegant fluidity. Its bulbous, umbrella-shaped body pulses with a translucent glow, revealing a mesmerizing dance of colors within its soft structure. Usually, a soft pink and calming blue light emanates from its organism, accentuated by a constellation of star-like points, shimmering in sync with the creature's rhythmic pulses. Delicate tentacles, stretching several feet in length, trail its body in an exquisite ballet, leaving a mesmerizing trail of luminary discharge in their wake.

Kezus Jelly are generally gentle creatures, favoring evasion over confrontation. Unless provoked or threatened, these creatures tend to not be menacing to other species. These jellies spend their days in deep and dark waters, only emerging into shallows once the sun has set.

Rask.name: Rask

Pouncing Strike.name: Pouncing Strike
Pouncing Strike.description: This creature lunges forward, putting its whole weight behind a leaping strike.
Pouncing Strike.actiondesc:
This attack may be used after a Move that brings the @ref[actor.name]{creature} at least 10 feet closer to its target. If the creature was above the target, this attack gains +1 Boon per 10 feet of elevation decrease in that movement.

If this attack is a Critical Hit, the target of the attack is immediately knocked @Condition[prone].

Pack Hunter.name: Pack Hunter
Pack Hunter.description:
This creature is a pack hunter, relying on its allies to flank and harrass a target to render it exposed to further harm.

This creature doubles number of Boons awarded from attacking a Flanked enemy.

Bestial Senses.name: Bestial Senses
Bestial Senses.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has finely honed senses and is particularly perceptive of their environment, all Awareness checks gain +2 Boons.

Skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
Skirmisher.description: You are adept at entering and exiting the fray. When moving out of the Engagement radius of an enemy, that enemy has 2 Banes to any Disengagement Strike against you.

Anticipate Harm.name: Anticipate Harm
Anticipate Harm.description: Your keen reflexes and acuity allow you to anticipate imminent danger and react to avoid it.
Anticipate Harm.actiondesc: You may immediately move 4 feet after the area-of-effect of the attack is declared. If this movement escapes the area of the attack, you are unaffected.

Rask.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

@ref[name]s are three-toed, clawed mammals who possess an organ structure that resembles a hybrid of canine and feline species. The bearing of a @ref[name]'s head is like that of a great cat, and its quadruped body is like that of a lean dog. And while some morphological variation does exist among @ref[name]s, most exhibit the tall, athletic features that their kind is known for. The pelt of an adult @ref[name] is marked with a large stripe on its back that matches the light-colored stripe of its underside, and the spots that once marked its hind legs in youth have faded.

Behavior

@ref[name]s are understood to be mostly virtuous creatures, with a simple appreciation for benevolent coexistence. These noble beasts are known to exhibit unique and individual behaviors, however, often tinged with a measure of precociousness. Feral @ref[name]s are known to be more cautious than their domesticated cousins, but are never altogether unapproachable when the right animal handler is involved.

Lore

These beloved four-legged creatures are so ubiquitous throughout the Arctus Plateau, they have a tendency to find their way into many of the region's narratives.
Rask.biographypublic: @ref[name]s are domesticated four-legged mammals who frequent various biomes of the Arctus Plateau. Often used as animal companions and beasts of burden, @ref[name]s are known to be some of the region's most beloved and skillful animal mounts. They're known to be noble beasts, both generous of heart and direct of intention.
Rask.biographyappearance: The eyes of this majestic quadruped appear to glow with subtle phosphorescence. A lean mammal with features both canine and feline in nature, the large creature is marked by feathery tufts of fur, and appears as strong as it is dexterous. A striped pelt crowns the beast's regal head, and a short fluffy tail sways behind it with graceful intention.

Swarm of Cave Wasps.name: Swarm of Cave Wasps

Light Eater.name: Light Eater
Light Eater.description: If the swarm occupies the same space as a light source, the light source ceases to emit light. For 1 hour following this action, the [[lookup @name lowercase]] sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 ft.

Light Bites.name: Light Bites
Light Bites.description: Any creature who is bitten by the swarm sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius for 10 minutes. Multiple bites do not change the level of this illumination.

Extinguish.name: Extinguish
Extinguish.description: As an action, the [[lookup @name lowercase]] may fully extinguish their light, ending the effect of @UUID[Actor.v6ty5QZydZmZ7hrb.Item.6MjuFYBkOHPDKpLu]{Light Eater}. Any creature they have transferred light to via @UUID[.nJrzeAaYjbipxOVc]{Light Bites} continues to shed dim lighting and is unaffected.

Bites.name: Bites
Bites.description: Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. [[/damage average extended activity=gGceq8IeLNbJhk57]], or [[/damage average activity=bPpmYVTZj7fvMn46]] damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

Swarm.name: Swarm
Swarm.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

Swarm of Cave Wasps.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

These small flying insects differ from other forms of wasps and similar creatures for one main reason - they glow. While the cave wasps do not appear to be able to produce light on their own, they can take light from objects around them, swarming any source of light that they see and extinguishing it while transferring its glow to their own bodies. They can similarly transmit a bit of their glow to others, making those they bite glow dimly for a time.

Behavior

Cave wasps hate the light of Lantyr and tend to avoid even moonlight, sticking to dark corners of caves and shadowed sections of canyons. When handheld light, whether natural or magical, appears nearby, they swarm it, transferring its lights to their bodies and forming patterns in the darkness even as they attack whoever carried the light. Those they bite while lit emit a dim glow, which is thought to help them mark and find injured creatures after their initial flurry of bites.

Lore

As their name suggests, cave wasp swarms are most frequently found in caves and caverns, but they can also be found anywhere where the shadows are deep enough, and are often transported by adventurers who attempt to use them as a moving source of light while wandering. Some believe that giving a swarm the right source of magical light will cause them to reveal a path to a magical reward, but those who have followed the path they see in the cave wasps' lights are rarely heard from again.
Swarm of Cave Wasps.biographypublic:
In dark caves and shadowy canyon corners, a whirring sound is often your only warning before your light extinguishes, swarmed by the cave wasps that wait in crevices and corners, following any source of light that passes by to claim it for their own.

Cave wasp swarms are large groupings of tiny flying insects that travel in dark places in search of sources of light. While they avoid the light of Lantyr, they are quick to consume illumination from any lantern, glowing orb, or torch that they see, extinguishing it as they transfer its light to their bodies and become a constellation of light within the darkness.

Yarnac.name: Yarnac

Tail.name: Tail
Tail.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name] can lash out with it's hefty tail.

Thick Hide.name: Thick Hide
Thick Hide.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{beast} has a thick leathery hide that is resilient against attack.

Trampling Charge.name: Trampling Charge
Trampling Charge.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} uses its prodigious size to charge forward, trampling smaller creatures that stand in its way.
Trampling Charge.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} moves forward up to twice its Stride, attacking the Reflex defense of all creatures in its path. Targets who are half the creature's size or smaller are @Condition[stunned] until the end of their next turn as they are slammed aside.

Yarnac.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The Yarnac’s hardy anatomy is ideally suited for the harsh climates in which it thrives. Its shaggy woolen coat provides exceptional insulation against biting winds and low temperatures, while its dense muscle and fat layers make it capable of sustaining high levels of effort or long distance travel. The creature’s powerful legs and broad feet provide stability and traction on most any terrain, while its long tail aids in balance.

The distinctive antler-crest offers both a tool for fending off predators and a magnificent display for potential mates or rivals.

While Yarnac are mostly used was work animals, their hides are highly prized for their thickness and warmth and can be crafted into durable clothing and accessories. Yarnac meat is fatty and rich, and cooks well.

Behavior

Traveling in herds, Yarnacs are social creatures with a naturally gentle disposition. They’re naturally docile, easily adapting to humanoid presence, and are quick to respond to training as beasts of burden. When domesticated, they can tirelessly plow fields, transport goods, draw wagons, and power machines.

Despite their size, they are remarkably placid, with even temperament and long tempers under most circumstances. However, if they or their herd are threatened, their formidable size, power, and antler crests allow them to become incredibly dangerous.

Lore

The Yarnac is highly esteemed by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak} people, who cultivated relationships with them from the earliest days, hunting and herding them in equal measure to survive. Over time, the Bejak have perfected the art of domestication, turning Yarnacs into indispensable companions and work partners.

The introduction of Yarnacs to the Arctus Plateau via Bejak migration was seen as a boon for agricultural development and survival in the region as they become vital parts of the silt and mud extraction process for lakeside dredging operations. At this point, Yarnac are a largely domesticated beast and wild Yarnac are incredibly rare outside of their original northern homeland.
Yarnac.biographypublic: The huge, crest-horned creatures known as @ref[name] are one of the Arctus Plateau's most reliable beasts of burden, and — thanks to their even temperament and ease of training — @ref[name]s are actually celebrated in nearly every region of Ember as the world's premier pack animals. Thanks to their wooly hides, these majestic creatures can survive some of Ember's most frigid climes, and they're known to be hardy and trustworthy companions to those in need — from globe-spanning caravans to countryside farmers. Indeed, their role in daily life is both vital and ubiquitous.
Yarnac.biographyappearance: The squat body of this huge quadruped is covered in a dense fur, and its lumbering movements appear slow but deliberate. The shaggy creature's head is broad and powerful, crowned with a massive crest of majestic horns; and its three-toed feet are tipped with broad, bony hooves that serve as the foundations for the beast's wide, column-like legs. A long, plumed tail sways gently behind it, and a musky odor permeates the air nearby.

Aburyx.name: Aburyx

Gesture: Aspect.name: Gesture: Aspect
Gesture: Aspect.description:
You infuse the essence of a Rune into your body, empowering your own physical form or psyche.

When you assume a certain Aspect, you become more closely attuned to the damage type of the Rune used in your spell. You gain +2 Resistance to that damage type, and deal an additional +2 Damage whenever dealing damage of that type.

Your Aspect lasts for 6 Rounds. You may only have one active Aspect, casting another spell using the Aspect gesture replaces the previous effect. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 2 Action and 1 Focus.

Gesture: Ray.name: Gesture: Ray
Gesture: Ray.description:
You funnel the arcane power of a Rune into a point and project it outwards in a beam.

The Ray gesture scales using Wisdom and produces a line that is 1 foot wide and 30 feet long originating from the spellcaster, dealing 6 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. The gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 4 Action and 1 Focus.

Gesture: Strike.name: Gesture: Strike
Gesture: Strike.description:
You empower a direct close-range attack with the arcane essence of a Rune, performing a Strike with your equipped weapon.

The Strike gesture scales using Strength and deal damage based on your used weapon but with the damage type of the incorporated Rune. This gesture does not require any free hand and has a base cost of 1 Focus in addition to the cost of your weapon Strike.

Inflection: Compose.name: Inflection: Compose
Inflection: Compose.description: Enhance a spell by taking extra time in its formation, reducing other resource costs in exchange. The Compose inflection reduces the Focus cost of a spell by 1 while increasing its Action cost by 1 in exchange.

Mental Fortress.name: Mental Fortress
Mental Fortress.description: Your strong will makes you exceedingly difficult to influence. You gain +1 to your Willpower defense and +5 resistance to Psychic damage.

Radiant Absorption.name: Radiant Absorption
Radiant Absorption.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is no stranger to the chaotic force of light. Its Radiant resistance is doubled and if that resistance would reduce an amount of damage below zero, the negative amount is received as Healing instead.

Last Stand.name: Last Stand
Last Stand.description: You can muster the toughness and courage to fight on and stand your ground against improbable odds.
Last Stand.actiondesc: You expend Heroism to instantly recover two times your Toughness in Health. Your Healing Threshold is reduced by 2 for the next 3 Rounds.

Cleave.name: Cleave
Cleave.description: This martial technique is a specialized two-handed fighting maneuver which relies upon brute strength to swing your weapon in a wide arc, hitting multiple enemies in its path.
Cleave.actiondesc: A ferocious two-handed swing cleaves through foes in a 120 degree arc.

Armored Efficiency.name: Armored Efficiency
Armored Efficiency.description: You are trained in wearing the heaviest types of armor while still retaining mobility. You are able to use a free Movement action once per Turn while wearing Heavy armor.

Glowing Body.name: Glowing Body
Glowing Body.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} emits non-magical bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light in a 30 foot radius.

Call Skither.name: Call Skither
Call Skither.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} controls nearby Skither which act as its bound servitors.
Call Skither.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} calls for a servitor Skither which flies in from somewhere nearby, summoning the creature within 10 feet of the creature's location.

Splint Mail.name: Splint Mail
Splint Mail.descriptionpublic: A layer of vertical metal strips riveted to a backing of leather or mail, splint armor offers strong limb protection while sacrificing some flexibility.

Longsword.name: Longsword
Longsword.descriptionpublic: The longsword is a double-edged blade wielded with two hands for balance and strength, usually featuring a large crossguard used for parrying blows.

War Lance.name: War Lance
War Lance.descriptionpublic: Designed for mounted combat, the war lance is a long, tapered weapon used to shatter armor with the momentum of a charging steed, its shaft reinforced for devastating impact.

Rune: Illumination.name: Rune: Illumination
Rune: Illumination.description:
The orderly force of light and energy. The Illumination rune governs light and radiance.

The Illumination rune scales using Presence, targets Reflex, and deals Radiant damage to Health. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Illusion.
Rune: Illumination.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Illumination allows you to create light and exert basic control over its radiance, producing one of the following effects:

  • Create a ball of light called a "tosslight" which sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius. The light can hover near your body, be affixed to an item or surface, or be thrown up to a distance of 30 feet. You may dismiss your tosslight at any time and may only have a single tosslight at a time, casting this spell again causes your previous tosslight to disappear.

  • Inscribe up to 200 words of invisible text into paper like a scroll, page, or book. The text is written from light itself and hidden from non-magical detection. It can be made visible by yourself or another through use of this spell combined with a spoken passphrase that you define at the time of inscription.

  • Touch a physical object that produces dim light, causing it to become bright light for as long as you maintain physical contact. Only one light source may be intensified in this way at a given time.

Reveal may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Lightbringer.name: Lightbringer
Lightbringer.description:
You are highly skilled in weaving the Rune of Illumination. Spells which use this Rune cause the @Condition[irradiated] condition on Critical Hits.

The Irradiated effect lasts for 1 Round and deals your Presence score as Radiant damage to both Health and Morale.

Illumination Proficiency.name: Illumination Proficiency
Illumination Proficiency.description:
You have fluency in weaving spellcraft using the Rune of Illumination. You gain a +1 Skill Bonus for spells cast using this Rune.

Playtest Notes

This talent will eventually also provide an upgrade to the Reveal action, expanding its effectiveness or including new options for how to use it.

Iramancer.name: Iramancer
Iramancer.description: Your feats of arcana are fueled by anger. While Enraged you may still spend Focus and you deal 2 additional damage to all spell attacks.

Aburyx.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Like all creatures native to Luxarum, the Aburyx has a soul of powerful light encased within a constructed metal carapace. In the Aburyx's case, this body is vaguely humanoid in nature, and can be concealed by magic if the Aburyx is engaging in clandestine work on behalf of another, more powerful being. When fully revealed, the Aburyx's internal radiant flame can be clearly seen erupting from within its armor, showing its true Tyraphem nature.

Behavior

Despite the fearsomeness of their look and the fearlessness of their behavior, Aburyx are fairly dispensable on Luxarum, with armies of them sometimes clashing to the death over a minor dispute, so distinguishing themselves from their peers and being pulled off of the front lines is a high priority. They make themselves known to other, higher-status Tyraphem mostly by their willingness to sacrifice others for their own needs and the needs of their mission. Whether this ruthlessness is innate to the Aburyx or a result of their situation on Luxarum is unknown, but they are willing to do nearly anything to complete an assignment on behalf of those they work for.

Lore

Aburyx are some of the least powerful Tyraphem, and are often seen as disposable ground troops, admired more for their look when standing in a phalanx than celebrated individually. These days, having an Aburyx in your employment that stands out above the rest can be seen as a status symbol among higher-level Tyraphem, and they often work as personal aides, messengers, spies, and bodyguards to other Tyraphem.
Aburyx.biographypublic:
Aburyx are sometimes described as soldiers of flame and light, and can be found in several historical and mythical texts across Ember. From the work of scholars on these creatures, it is believed that their role (whether actual or metaphorical) is primarily as ground troops in larger battles on Luxarum, but descriptions of them as aides and messengers suggest that they have some way of elevating themselves in status by distinguishing themselves on and off the battlefield.

While accounts of the Aburyx are varied, a few commonalities appear across all of the tales — they are ruthless, loyal, and clever, both in their battle tactics and in their ability to sow seeds of dissent before and after combat.
Aburyx.biographyappearance: With a head of radiant yellow flame and the golden plate armor of a warrior, the Aburyx floats up from the ground it stands on, swiveling to face with you with a flare of light. Within moments, it it is hovering in front of you, a sword of light suddenly emerging from its hands as it readies to attack.

Skither.name: Skither

Talons.name: Talons
Talons.descriptionpublic: Finely articulated talons with needle tips for grasping prey or piercing flesh.

Pack Hunter.name: Pack Hunter
Pack Hunter.description:
This creature is a pack hunter, relying on its allies to flank and harrass a target to render it exposed to further harm.

This creature doubles number of Boons awarded from attacking a Flanked enemy.

Sacrifice Self.name: Sacrifice Self
Sacrifice Self.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} may intervene to take a blow instead of an adjacent ally.
Sacrifice Self.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} reacts, performing a Movement up to their Stride to interpose itself between a nearby ally and some source of harm which it can perceive.

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} becomes @Condition[dead], destroyed in their sacrifice, but the triggering action causes no effects to its original target.

Radiant Death Burst.name: Radiant Death Burst
Radiant Death Burst.description: When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} dies, it explodes in a volatile burst of radiant energy.
Radiant Death Burst.actiondesc: When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} becomes @Condition[dead], it explodes in a pulse of Radiant energy which attacks the Fortitude defense of all nearby creatures that fail to resist the effect.

Lightweight Carapace.name: Lightweight Carapace
Lightweight Carapace.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has a lightweight metallic exoskeleton which protects it from harm.

Servitor.name: Servitor
Servitor.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} serves the will of another and maintains a connection to that master that allows the transmission or messages or even the sharing of senses between the servitor and its controller.
Servitor.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can contact its master, sending inaudible communication which is instantaneously received by its controller as long as that other creature is capable of receiving messages.

False Appearance.name: False Appearance
False Appearance.description: While it remains motionless, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} is indistinguishable from some other object or material.

Skither.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Skithers, like most Luxarum creatures, have a bright radiant-yellow flame within a metal carapace. While most of their internal light is covered, giving them the ability to curl into a completely nondescript metal ball as needed to observe those around them, the heat and light that it generates is powerful, giving them the ability to generate heat in both their "eye" and pincers and to self-destruct if needed by overloading themselves beyond what their frames can handle.

Behavior

Skithers are messengers and spies, using their small size to follow simple directives on behalf of other tyraphem that often either require information gathering or the delivery of dramatic messages carved into walls and onto the bodies of the dead. Able to hold complicated routines and directives in their heads, but without the strength to pose a real threat, they are also often sent to fetch or fix things on Luxarum as needed, like a swiss-army knife of a creature who never ever says no.

Lore

It is said that Skithers were created as children's toys among the Tyraphem, with children being considered mature when they realized that the small toys they were playing with could be use to harm or help their peers and put this theory into practice. Whether or not this is true, the use of skithers among Tyraphem is somewhat widespread and they are sometimes treated as family pets., with some going so far as to have all within their service explode when they die.
Skither.biographypublic: Often used as a particularly destructive breed of messengers among tyraphem, who deploy them to leave burning messages on the property and bodies of their enemies, skithers use their small size and ability to camouflage themselves, putting themselves into positions where their chosen target will not be able to put up a defense. Dedicated to creating carnage where they can for the more powerful creatures they serve, skithers have known to follow a target for miles and will overload their bodies with radiant energy when they believe they have lost a fight, determined to harm the target even if they have to give up their own lives in the process.
Skither.biographyappearance: Small and fast-moving, this creature seems at first like something to ignore, little more than a piece of trash with jagged wings crudely shaped to look like a insect. The creature's solitary eye and claw-like appendages seem to surge with fiery radiance as it strikes, leaving streaks of amber light in its wake.

Burrower.name: Burrower

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has a supernatural ability to rapidly burrow through solid surfaces which are not entirely impermeable.

Radiant Death Burst.actiondesc: When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} becomes @Condition[dead], it explodes in a pulse of Radiant energy which attacks the Fortitude defense of all nearby creatures that fail to resist the effect.

Raking Talons.name: Raking Talons
Raking Talons.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks rapidly with its talons, dealing multiple raking blows against a single target.
Raking Talons.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks swiftly with both talons.

If at least one attack results in a Critical Success, it inflicts the @Condition[bleeding] condition for 2 Rounds.

Talons.name: Talons
Talons.descriptionpublic: Finely articulated talons with needle tips for grasping prey or piercing flesh.

Heavy Carapace.name: Heavy Carapace
Heavy Carapace.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has a heavy articulated exoskeleton which protects it from harm.

Whiptail.name: Whiptail
Whiptail.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.item]{creature} whips its body around, using its bulk to slam into nearby foes.

Vorg.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

As with many creatures of Luxarum, Vorg are composed of a metallic carapace and an inner glowing fire. They have the capacity to compress their long segmented body into a single segment that can move forward or sideways, giving them the ability to fit through spaces they would otherwise not be able to reach, and can use the compression and extension of their body to shoot themselves forward and pin their prey. The fire within their body also glows hot, burning those who grow too close.

Behavior

Wild Vorg are generally aggressive, and enjoy burrowing beneath surfaces only to emerge and immediately attack their prey. Drawn by sound, they are When tamed by a Tyraphem, they can be taught general behaviors and a rudimentary proto-language, enough to scratch out the layout of things that they see or alert the Tyraphem who has adopted them to dangers that lie beneath the surface.

Lore

Vorg are creatures of Luxarum, rarely found on Ember if not in the employ of some Celestial or Tyraphem. Vorg are often used as steeds on Luxarum, hitched to chariots and other carts that pull notable Tyraphem through the streets, but can also be used as a means of gathering information on others — while they have limited stealth capacity and language skills, they can bond with Tyraphem who take them on as pets and convey limited information about the layout of a building or depth of another Tyraphem's defenses. Some also use them as a form of defense, encouraging Vorg to burrow beneath their homes and attack any who come close.
Vorg.biographypublic: Vorg are centipede-like creatures whose metal carapace surrounds an endlessly glowing radiant light. Hot to the touch, and capable of climbing up walls, burrowing into the ground, and pulling themselves along the surface, they are often an unwelcome surprise to those who come across them in caves, caverns, and other subterranean locations.
Vorg.biographyappearance: Seemingly endless segments of metal speed across the ground, dragged by the clicking and clacking of countless legs on each side and multiple pairs of surprisingly dexterous pincers. Within this metallic body, a orange-yellow glow is visible from the creature's pointed spine and through what passes for eyes, burning with a heat that emanates from its body into the nearby air.

Broken Aedir Sentinel.name: Broken Aedir Sentinel

Deteriorated Plating.name: Deteriorated Plating
Deteriorated Plating.descriptionpublic: This once-impermeable reinforced plating has become deteriorated and weathered over centuries of neglect.

Sword-Arm.name: Sword-Arm
Sword-Arm.descriptionpublic: The arm of this creature once featured a wicked built-in armblade.

Greatsword.name: Greatsword
Greatsword.descriptionpublic: Longer and heavier than a standard longsword, the greatsword is a two-handed blade meant for powerful sweeping strikes, its length commanding both reach and awe.

Enhanced Shielding.name: Enhanced Shielding
Enhanced Shielding.description: The @ref[actor.name] channels alchemical fluid through its shielding plates, temporarily super-heating and reinforcing them against physical damage.

Powered Spin.name: Powered Spin
Powered Spin.description: The @ref[actor.name] unleashes an alchemically fueled spinning attack which strikes all nearby enemies.
Powered Spin.actiondesc: The Sentinel sweeps its Greatsword in a lighting-fast circular arc, striking all nearby foes.

Alchemical Recharge.name: Alchemical Recharge
Alchemical Recharge.description: The @ref[actor.name] interfaces with an Alchemical Charging Station to recover its supply of internal alchemical fluid.
Alchemical Recharge.actiondesc: The Sentinel connects with an Alchemical Charging Station that is powered and operational. Once connected, the construct becomes @Condition[restrained] but at the beginning of its next turn will recover up to 4 Focus if the charging process is not interrupted.

Self-Repair.name: Self-Repair
Self-Repair.description: The @ref[actor.name]{construct} activates internal repairing mechanisms to mitigate damage it has taken.

Repelling Kick.name: Repelling Kick
Repelling Kick.description: The @ref[actor.name] unleashes an alchemically fueled kick with ruthless concussive force.
Repelling Kick.actiondesc: The sentinel slams a single target with a concussive boot of force, dealing Bludgeoning damage, knocking the target backwards up to 15 feet, and leaving the target @Condition[staggered].

Aedir Construct Fluid.name: Aedir Construct Fluid
Aedir Construct Fluid.descriptionprivate: This alchemical contaminant, created from the runoff of a metal construct, holds a small amount of power, which appears to have been used as some sort of power source by the Aediri scientists in the lookout post in the hills of the Forest of Stone.
Aedir Construct Fluid.descriptionpublic: A strange alchemical compound with swirls with a yellow-orange color. The exterior of its cannister gives you the sensation of electrical charge that causes your hair to stand on end.

Immutable Form.name: Immutable Form
Immutable Form.description: The @ref[actor.name] is immune to any spell or effect which alters its physical form.

Broken Aedir Sentinel.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The construct has fallen into disrepair, but at its prime it was a large metal construct standing 12 feet tall with a humanoid form and four arms, powered by an orange glowing substance of unknown origins. In the many years since the construct was made, the metal has begun to wear away and chunks of it have either fallen off or been covered with spider webbing, mold, and the occasional bit of moss. After a recent fall, a hole has opened in one of its legs and orange fluid has begun to leak out of it onto the floor.

The orange substance within a damaged construct can be collected once it is defeated – this substance functions as a contaminant for most other living creatures, but its full properties have yet to be fully explored. It can be sold to alchemists and spellcasters looking for experimental reagents, as well as historians from groups like the Anaechraenum who want to use it to learn more about its potential creation by the Aediri.

Behavior

When under attack, the Sentinel uses the fluid in its system to bolster its attacks and protect itself, but the leaks in its system have greatly reduced how much fluid it can carry at any one time before being drained. As a result, the Sentinel must recharge itself at nearby fluid recharge stations frequently and uses blasts of steam and quick motion to throw enemies back and give it time to reach this goal.

Lore

The damaged construct was created by researchers in an outpost in the Forest of Stone which was created and staffed by Aediri. Evidence suggests that they were potentially spying on the Shent, who mined nearby, and though the contstruct is metal, it has features with some echoes of Shent workmanship, though there is no conclusive evidence to prove it. Recent earthquakes in the Forest of Stone have damaged the construct, which was left behind by their builders years ago - it is now leaking a fluid into the ground that is contaminating the mine below.
Broken Aedir Sentinel.biographypublic: The damaged construct is made of a dark metal and powered by strange Alchemical Fluid. Over time, it has fallen into disrepair but retained some basic functionality and defended its domain with absolute obedience.
Broken Aedir Sentinel.biographyappearance: This large metal creature once had four arms, but two have eroded, leaving them as crumbling stumps. The remaining arms hold a broad swordlike weapons, one whole and one broken, Both swat at the air in front of the creature as it staggers forward., leaking viscous orange fluid from within its body with every shaky step.

Chessman.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

@ref[name]s are built to resemble armored humanoids, and were originally crafted with extreme precision and attention to detail by the Arcturelian artificer Vartholomew Chess (and his associates). There is an artisanal quality to their design and embellishments, as evident in their embossed face masks and chest plates, almost like a suit of fine armor yet somehow more practical and commonplace.

As constructs, Chessian Constructs don’t require food, air, or sleep to survive. They can, however, be repaired by characters with adequate training and proficiency, or magical mending and artifice.

Behavior

@ref[name]s are often encountered in groups, and are often accompanied by one or more humanoid controllers. As such, they work together to the best of their abilities according to the commands of their living masters. Their greater improvised weaponry feature allows Chessian Constructs to wield all manner of tools and objects in combat with more precision. A Chessian Construct’s specific melee weapon attacks are generally determined according to their location and work assignment (with miners utilizing war picks and inkaro pool farmers utilizing spears and nets), although most @ref[name]s are equipped with enough armaments to handle nearly any job.

Lore

@ref[name]s are relatively commonplace throughout the Arctus Plateau, and are generally found in the service of businesses or middle-class and affluent households. These automatons are known for the precision of their design and artful embellishments, and are prized region-wide for their reliability and inherent display of Arcturian excellence.
Chessman.biographypublic: Scrappy automatons made of copper and steel, @ref[name]s are anthropomorphic constructs utilized by Arcturians for a variety of tasks — including dangerous labor like excavating, beast wrangling, security, and the hazardous harvesting of rare resources (like the inkaro pearls of Arcturel’s sinkhole depths).
Chessman.biographyappearance: A humanoid figure clad in copper armor before you moves with a smooth and mechanical precision, and you can’t help but notice that the limbs beneath its burnished mail look more like steel rods than living flesh. This construct, whose embellished countenance resembles an artistic expression of amused stoicism, barely regards you as it continues to toil.

Light Beam.name: Light Beam
Light Beam.description:
Any player character may stand next to the Light Energy Turret and make a [[/check arcana 11]]. On a successful check, the PC can spend an action to adjust the turret's aim and fire it in the same turn. You can choose a new line of effect for the turret, allowing you to target a different area within the range of its firing capabilities (60 feet long and 10 feet wide). Additionally, if you roll above 15 on the Arcana check, the PC can gain control over the turret, allowing them to manipulate its firing direction and fire it as a bonus action from now on.

When the [[lookup @name]] fires, it shoots an intense ray of radiant light in the direction it was aimed. All creatures in a line that is 60 feet long and 10 feet wide must make a Dexterity saving throw. They take 4d6 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Silver Beam Sentinel.biographyprivate:
Big, bad, and still undergoing testing, this dangerous automaton is not quite ready for release, but it's more than capable of destroying unwanted guests visiting the workshop where it's being built!

Anatomy

The @ref[name] bears a passing resemblance to the original construct it began life as, features a large number of ill-advised modifications. At its core are a pair of entropic inkaro pearls, and numerous other dubious mechanisms and arcane batteries sit ready to be tapped by the various tools and implements attached to it.

As constructs, they don’t require food, air, or sleep to survive, but do require an Inkaro Pearl to operate as a power source, which must be changed periodically. While they can't be healed with normal restorative magic, they can be repaired by characters with adequate training and proficiency, or magical mending and artifice.

Behavior

Like all other Silver Beam made constructs, the Sentinel is an emotionless machine that lacks any sense of self preservation. While they are not self-aware and have no personalities, they are highly intelligent and capable of tackling complex tasks with ease.

The Sentinel is highly dangerous as it has no concept of mercy to draw upon when fighting. While the company would claim otherwise if asked, this construct was built for violence and the various dangerous weapons integrated into it make that abundantly clear.

Lore

The Sentinel is the very latest automaton model in service of Larissa Toth’s consortium, and her first foray into building something almost entirely new. While it is based on the earlier Servitor design, it has been heavily modified into a mechanical monstrosity.

If this machine survives testing and trials and makes it to production it is slated to play a vital role in the Silver Beam Consortium’s future enterprises.
Silver Beam Sentinel.biographypublic: The @ref[name] is an iteration of the Silver Beam Consortium's servitor constructs, but features extensive modifications including a more robust frame, greater strength, and much more powerful offensive weaponry.
Silver Beam Sentinel.biographyappearance: You see a lumbering, armored humanoid figure clad in silver alloyed plate standing before you. It's burnished steel limbs and segmented body gleams with mechanical menace, and metallic tubes mounted on its forearms coil to some unseen source within its body.

Silver Beam Servitor.biographyprivate:
These constructs are built by the Silver Beam Consortium, and sold as an affordable, and adaptable automaton capable of taking on nearly any task one might need done.

Anatomy

@ref[name]s are built to resemble stylized humanoids, and are highly advanced, and precisely built constructs meant to do anything that a humanoid can do, within reason. As constructs, they don’t require food, air, or sleep to survive, but do require an Inkaro Pearl to operate as a power source, which must be changed periodically.

While they can't be healed with normal restorative magic, they can be repaired by characters with adequate training and proficiency, or magical mending and artifice.

Behavior

@ref[name]s are emotionless machines that lacks any sense of fear or self preservation. While they are not self-aware and have no personalities, they are highly intelligent and capable of tackling complex tasks with ease.

If threatened, these constructs don't defend themselves unless they have been given special lease to do so, and tend to be highly dangerous as they have no sense or mercy to draw upon when fighting.

Lore

@ref[name]s are relatively new additions to the construct markets in the Arctus Plateau, and have not yet become commonplace beyond Arcturel, their place of origin. However, since they are typically cheaper than competing constructs and just as reliable, they are poised to become popular across the region.
Silver Beam Servitor.biographypublic: Sleek, slender automatons made of brushed steel the @ref[name] is built and sold by the Silver Beam Consortium. Rugged, and adaptable, they are built to handle a variety of tasks from dangerous labor like excavating and harvesting rare materials to more mundane work like tending fields and waiting tables.
Silver Beam Servitor.biographyappearance: This humanoid construct is made of brushed silver steel with blue accents and bears the distinctive logo of the Silver Beam Consortium. It moves with a smooth precision punctuated with all the whirs and swishes of machinery hidden under it's glossy metal shell.

Woven Construct.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

@ref[name]s are crafted from wood and vine to resemble Arcturian humanoids, and are considered to be rustic implementations of original designs by the famed Arcturelian artificer Vartholomew Chess. And similar to a Chessian Construct, the artisanal quality of a @ref[name]'s form is evident in its carefully carved face and the finer details of its whittled garb.

As constructs, @ref[name]s don’t require food, air, or sleep to survive. They can, however, be repaired by characters with adequate training and proficiency, or magical mending and artifice.

Behavior

@ref[name]s can be encountered in groups, but can are also known to toil alone. They are often accompanied by one or more humanoid controllers. As such, they work together to the best of their abilities according to the commands of their living masters. Their greater improvised weaponry feature allows @ref[name]s to wield all manner of tools and objects in combat with more precision. A @ref[name]'s specific melee weapon attacks are generally determined according to their location and work assignment (with harvesters of the Golden Flats utilizing trowels and scythes).

Lore

@ref[name]s are relatively commonplace throughout the Arctus Plateau, and can be found in the service of many a Golden Flats farmstead. These automatons are known for the varied materials of their wooden construction, and are known to wear carved faces that reflect the temperaments of their respective households.
Woven Construct.biographypublic: @ref[name]s are dutiful automatons made of wood and vine that resemble timber humanoids. These anthropomorphic constructs are employed by Arcturians of the Golden Flats for a variety of tasks — including strenuous labor like farming, beast wrangling, construction, and defense.
Woven Construct.biographyappearance: This humanoid figure is crafted from various scraps of wood, its ramshackle limbs held together with a skeleton made of timber and ligatures woven from vine. The masterful carving that comprises its wooden face is fixed in a perpetual look of mirthful stoicism as it labors away at some duteous task.

Afflicted Pallid Drake.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Drakes bear a striking resemblance to the Vile Dragon, with long, thin bodies, two fore-legs and no other limbs. They often have horns and frills, and maws lined with thin, razor sharp teeth.

Drakes are capable of flight, though they lack wings, indicating their capacity for flight comes from some other means, likely magic. The precise nature of this ability is not known. Drakelings lack this ability, only developing it in adulthood.

Drakes are covered in robust scales which help protect their bodies from harm, though they rely more on their dexterity to evade attacks, rather than natural armor. This hide is similar to snake skin in texture and composition.

All drakes have intensely sharp eyesight and strong low-light vision.

Behavior

The newness of these creatures precludes the development of academic knowledge of drake behavior, so little is known beyond what direct observation may provide.

That said, drakes quickly assert themselves as apex predators in any biome they inhabit, and are naturally territorial, attacking anything that dares to enter the territory they've claimed.

Drakes are intelligent, capable of complex reasoning, and coordination in groups, even with humanoid allies despite being incapable of speech. However, since drakes are territorial and extremely willful, training them is difficult, if not impossible. Though not social by nature, drakes can and will hunt and nest together, with all members of that nest bowing to the will of largest among them.

Lore

There is little known about Drakes, as they are not naturally occurring on Ember and only began appearing in recent years. To the wider world of academics, they appear to be a chimerical blend of snake and dragon with an unknown but possibly magical origin.

The truth about them is that they were created in secret by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn], grown in a hidden blood forge, their forms patterned after @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.v6lXjfETDkrt0J7E]{Zerranyss}, a powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.EhQnCUxkJyxOSbf7]{Vile Dragon}. They were made to serve as a resources for Mutagists and their experiments, forced to become test subjects for the mutagenic compounds their numerous underground labs produce.

The ultimate goal of the mutagists was to find serums and alchemical treatments that would enhance, transform, and empower the draks, with the expectation that any such discoveries would also be applicable to the Vile Dragon they were spawned from.
Afflicted Pallid Drake.biographypublic: The Afflicted Pallid Drake is part of a newly discovered type of draconic monster that boasts impressive speed and strength. While they appear to be descended from or related to dragons, the true nature of their origin is presently unknown. They particular ones are riddled with some manner of wasting disease that is causing their bodies to rot from the inside out.
Afflicted Pallid Drake.biographyappearance: This large, serpentine creature is covered in pale white-green scales with a prominent flared tail adorned with ragged, green frills. Its draconic head is set with long horns tipped in the same pale green hue, and halfway down its body are more wide, damaged frills. The Drake's eyes are a cloudy white, hinting at blindness, and its body is marred by unsettling yellow pustules emerging from ragged wounds. Despite its obvious afflictions, it maneuvers with undeterred grace, periodically revealing rows of razor-sharp teeth within a saliva-dripping maw.

Mutated Ultra Drake.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Drakes bear a striking resemblance to the Vile Dragon, with long, thin bodies, two fore-legs and no other limbs. They often have horns and frills, and maws lined with thin, razor sharp teeth.

Drakes are covered in robust scales which help protect their bodies from harm, though they rely more on their dexterity to evade attacks, rather than natural armor. This hide is similar to snake skin in texture and composition.

The mutated drake has been affected by a powerful alchemical mutagen that has greatly enhanced their physical strength, at the cost of their dexterity. It has also caused intense physical damage, leaving them ravaged by a some manner of degenerative malady causing their bodies to become rotten and infected.

The anatomy of this mutated drake is robust, its hide considerably thicker and more impervious than smaller drakes. Its six arms grant it the ability to climb, grapple, swim, and fight with greater ferocity than more mundane creatures. While asymmetrical, its eye arrangement grants expanded visual fields, compensating for the impairment in its one blind eye. Its finger-like appendages which augment its already fearsome bite by grasping and dragging prey deeper into its maw.

Behavior

The newness of these creatures precludes the development of academic knowledge of drake behavior, so little is known beyond what direct observation may provide.

That said, drakes quickly assert themselves as apex predators in any biome they inhabit, and are naturally territorial, attacking anything that dares to enter the territory they've claimed.

Drakes are intelligent, capable of complex reasoning, and coordination in groups, even with humanoid allies despite being incapable of speech. However, since drakes are territorial and extremely willful, training them is difficult, if not impossible. Though not social by nature, drakes can and will hunt and nest together, with all members of that nest bowing to the will of largest among them.

With its enhanced size and resilience, and the fact is has been resigned to life in the pit of an underground quarry, this creature has become highly aggressive and territorial, proving to be an immense danger to anything that dares to come into its arena. Despite its grotesque mutations, it operates with surprising precision and cunning, leveraging its considerable intellect and power to rip apart anything foolish enough to get in its path.

Lore

There is little known about Drakes, as they are not naturally occurring on Ember and only began appearing in recent years. To the wider world of academics, they appear to be a chimerical blend of snake and dragon with an unknown but possibly magical origin.

The truth about them is that they were created in secret by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn], grown in a hidden blood forge, their forms patterned after @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.v6lXjfETDkrt0J7E]{Zerranyss}, a powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.EhQnCUxkJyxOSbf7]{Vile Dragon}. They were made to serve as a resources for Mutagists and their experiments, forced to become test subjects for the mutagenic compounds their numerous underground labs produce.

The ultimate goal of the mutagists was to find serums and alchemical treatments that would enhance, transform, and empower the draks, with the expectation that any such discoveries would also be applicable to the Vile Dragon they were spawned from.

This hyper-mutated drake is the byproduct of repeated exposure to advanced mutagenic serums developed in the clandestine laboratory where it is discovered. Born from experiments that often killed lesser subjects, it stands as one of the rare successes the Mutagists have achieved, showcasing superior strength, resilience, and size. The odd anatomical features, including extra limbs and asymmetrical eyes, were unforeseen consequences of the experimental process, and show that more work still needs to be done.
Mutated Ultra Drake.biographypublic: This huge mutated drake is comprehensively enhanced and perverted by mutagenic serums. It has a thick scaled hide, numerous extra limbs, and distinctive horns and eyes. Incapable of flight like it's smaller kin, it makes up for it with boundless aggression and physical power.
Mutated Ultra Drake.biographyappearance: Warped and misshapen, this monster is covered in thick scales, and scuttles forward on half a dozen limbs protruding haphazardly from its grotesque form. Its head is crowned with a flaring array of teal horns which extend into long, uneven spikes that run halfway down its spine. The creature's elongated mouth is framed by six finger-like appendages ready to guide pray into its jagged teeth. Scabbed over brown pustules blemish its body, hinting at an illness in remission.
