Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes four melee attacks: two with its [[/item Bladed Bracer]] and two with its [[/item Signaran Dagger]]. Alternatively, it can use [[/item Plasma Ray]] twice.

Penumbral Hide.name: Penumbral Hide
Penumbral Hide.description: At the start of each of its turns, the [[lookup @name]] deals [[/damage average]] damage to any creature grappling it.

Plasma Ray.name: Plasma Ray
Plasma Ray.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]] Hit: [[/damage average extended]].

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=mxdOtRIMZDFLZNLU]].

Failure: The target has the &Reference[poisoned] condition until the start of its next turn.

Success: If the save result is 15 or higher, the target is immune to this effect until it finishes a Long Rest.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name]]'s spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]]).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of its character sheet. It automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: Once on each of its turns, when the [[lookup @name]] hits a target with a melee weapon attack, the target takes an extra [[/damage average]] if the [[lookup @name]] has advantage on the attack roll or if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t incapacitated, and [[lookup @name the]] doesn’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.

Magic Resistance.name: Magic Resistance
Magic Resistance.description: The [[lookup @name]] has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Darkness.name: Darkness
Darkness.description:
For the duration, magical &Reference[darkness] spreads from a point within range and fills a 15-foot-radius Sphere. Darkvision can't see through it, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it.

Alternatively, you cast the spell on an object that isn't being worn or carried, causing the Darkness to fill a 15-foot Emanation originating from that object. Covering that object with something opaque, such as a bowl or helm, blocks the Darkness.

If any of this spell's area overlaps with an area of Bright Light or Dim Light created by a spell of level 2 or lower, that other spell is dispelled.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Detect Thoughts.name: Detect Thoughts
Detect Thoughts.description:
You activate one of the effects below. Until the spell ends, you can activate either effect as a Magic action on your later turns.

Sense Thoughts. You sense the presence of thoughts within 30 feet of yourself that belong to creatures that know languages or are telepathic. You don't read the thoughts, but you know that a thinking creature is present.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Read Thoughts. Target one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself or one creature within 30 feet of yourself that you detected with the Sense Thoughts option. You learn what is most on the target's mind right now. If the target doesn't know any languages and isn't telepathic, you learn nothing.

As a Magic action on your next turn, you can try to probe deeper into the target's mind. If you probe deeper, the target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, you discern the target's reasoning, emotions, and something that looms large in its mind (such as a worry, love, or hate). On a successful save, the spell ends. Either way, the target knows that you are probing into its mind, and until you shift your attention away from the target's mind, the target can take an action on its turn to make an [[/check ability=int skill=arc dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC, ending the spell on a success.

Invisibility.name: Invisibility
Invisibility.description:
A creature you touch has the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition until the spell ends. The spell ends early immediately after the target makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.

Minor Illusion.name: Minor Illusion
Minor Illusion.description:
You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

Plane Shift.name: Plane Shift
Plane Shift.description:
You and up to eight willing creatures who link hands in a circle are transported to a different plane of existence. You can specify a target destination in general terms, such as the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire or the palace of Dispater on the second level of the Nine Hells, and you appear in or near that destination, as determined by the DM.

Alternatively, if you know the sigil sequence of a teleportation circle on another plane of existence, this spell can take you to that circle. If the teleportation circle is too small to hold all the creatures you transported, they appear in the closest unoccupied spaces next to the circle.

Jahud.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

[[lookup @name]] are lithe and muscular assassins whose sleek profiles suit their murderous dispositions. The physiology of the [[lookup @name]] has been dictated by their creators: Signaran biomancers who designed the [[lookup @name]] to be effective and ceaseless killers throughout the cosmos (and very little else). Indeed, their penumbral hides and arcane spellcasting abilities are inherent to their fiendish anatomy; and the [[lookup @name]] form is ultimately inspired by the physiology of its Signaran makers — including four arms, an overall quality of anthropomorphism, and the readiness of its otherworldly eyes.

Behavior

[[lookup @name]] assassins possess formidable slyness, and take great efforts to veil their presence in foreign realms, such as the terrestrial lands of Ember. Fortunately, the metaphysical augmentations bestowed upon them provide tools like enhanced stealth, heightened speed, and innate spellcasting — traits they use to deadly effect when shadowing their quarry. And while they can speak Signaran (or any learned language) with ease, they prefer to infiltrate the minds of those they communicate with via their otherworldly telepathy.

In combat, [[lookup @name]] are known to wield their innate spells and the ability to conjure a beam of radioactive plasma with terrifying precision; these sorceries manifest through a series of arcane sigils and Signaran formulae, which the [[lookup @name]] trace into thin air with any of their four fiendish hands. However, once they meet an adversary in melee combat, [[lookup @name]] prefer to experience the visceral, tactile sensations of their various daggers and blades.

Lore

These fiendish killers were first created as servants of the Daemos lord Kerastes, whose domains of influence are corruption and secrecy. Originally culled from lesser ranks of roguish minions and subject to a variety of what their masters would refer to as "evolutional upgrades," [[lookup @name]] are grown by Signaran biomancers in a laboratory environment, and their physical alterations preside on a genetic scale. Like most fiends and outsiders, [[lookup @name]] defy standard classification by terrestrial scholars and naturalists; to the people of Ember, they are merciless outsiders, cruel and inscrutable.
Jahud.biographypublic:
A four-armed, blue-skinned cutthroat stands before you, armed with two viridian daggers and an array of bladed bracers crafted from dark gray bone. A black half-mask obscures most of the creature's face, exposing its pale blue eyes, a pair of wicked horns, and a mane of bright azure hair that roils like arcane fire. The rogue's strappy leather armor is wrapped tightly around its muscular flesh, and its shoulders boast overlapping plates of cerulean chitin like primeval pauldrons. A pointed tale lashes with ferocious cruelty behind this otherworldly menace, who looks ready to slay anything that moves.

[[lookup @name]] are otherworldly hunters and emissaries who embody murder as a fine art. These malevolent assassins wear sparse leather armor and wield exotic alien weaponry, which allow them to appear as lethal and intimidating as they are collected and poised. In addition to their innate magical defenses, [[lookup @name]] are learned in the ways of arcane spellcasting, and can summon forth a variety of esoteric sorcery for their insidious schemes.

Agrimage.name: Agrimage

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Their spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

The [[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of their character sheet. They automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Agrimagical Artifact.name: Agrimagical Artifact
Agrimagical Artifact.description:
Once per day, an agrimage can touch a single stone, plant, or other natural item and imbue it with a specific agrimagical effect. Most of these effects are unique to the agrimage, but known effects include:

  • Barrier Stone. An individual barrier stone can be created to repel creatures of 4 intelligence or less that come near it, either physically (pushing them back) or mentally (compelling the subject to avoid the stone). The stone affects the area in a 1-foot radius around it and can be countered with a DC 10 save. With each new barrier stone placed within 10 feet, the stone becomes stronger, adding a DC of 1 and an additional 1-foot in radius for each additional stone.

  • Evergrowth. Ground within a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=um6uF8FxLGv955QQ]]-foot square of this artifact, traditionally created from newly fallen wood, doubles in productivity - all plants yield double their normal amount and gain one of the following effects:

    • Roots glow in the night, casting dim light within 10 feet of each root.

    • Plants produce a pleasing aroma that reminds each person who encounters them of a pleasant moment from their past.

    • Children conceived in the area have a high chance of being twins.

  • Good Seed. Once planted and fully grown, a plant from this seed has one of the following effects:

    • It produces a fruit or vegetable every 3 days, regardless of the season.

    • Its roots grow toward the nearest source of water, gaining 10 feet of length and/or depth per day.

    • Food made from it keeps for 7 days under any conditions and always tastes good, regardless of the recipe.

Foundry Note

Scaling is implemented in the Barrier Stone activities to adjust the save DC and the area of effect based on the number of stones created.

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description:
Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range.

Weather Sensor. You create a Tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.

Bloom. You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.

Sensory Effect. You create a harmless sensory effect, such as falling leaves, spectral dancing fairies, a gentle breeze, the sound of an animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot Cube.

Fire Play. You light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a campfire.

Guidance.name: Guidance
Guidance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a skill. Until the spell ends, the creature adds 1d4 to any ability check using the chosen skill.

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
This spell repairs a single break or tear in an object you touch, such as a broken chain link, two halves of a broken key, a torn cloak, or a leaking wineskin. As long as the break or tear is no larger than 1 foot in any dimension, you mend it, leaving no trace of the former damage.

This spell can physically repair a magic item, but it can't restore magic to such an object.

Produce Flame.name: Produce Flame
Produce Flame.description:
A flickering flame appears in your hand and remains there for the duration. While there, the flame emits no heat and ignites nothing, and it sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Until the spell ends, you can take a Magic action to hurl fire at a creature or an object within 60 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 Fire damage.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

Detect Poison and Disease.name: Detect Poison and Disease
Detect Poison and Disease.description:
For the duration, you sense the location of poisons, poisonous or venomous creatures, and magical contagions within 30 feet of yourself. You sense the kind of poison, creature, or contagion in each case.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Entangle.name: Entangle
Entangle.description:
Grasping plants sprout from the ground in a 20-foot square within range. For the duration, these plants turn the ground in the area into &Reference[difficultterrain]. They disappear when the spell ends.

Each creature (other than you) in the area when you cast the spell must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have the &Reference[restrained apply=false] condition until the spell ends. A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself from the grasping plants and is no longer Restrained by them.

Goodberry.name: Goodberry
Goodberry.description:
@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbutlMagicalBer]{Ten berries} appear in your hand and are infused with magic for the duration. A creature can take a Bonus Action to eat one berry. Eating a berry restores 1 Hit Point, and the berry provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day.

Uneaten berries disappear when the spell ends.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Enhance Ability.name: Enhance Ability
Enhance Ability.description:
You touch a creature and choose Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. For the duration, the target has Advantage on ability checks using the chosen ability.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2. You can choose a different ability for each target.

Gust of Wind.name: Gust of Wind
Gust of Wind.description:
A Line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide blasts from you in a direction you choose for the duration. Each creature in the Line must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from you in a direction following the Line. A creature that ends its turn in the Line must make the same save.

Any creature in the Line must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving closer to you.

The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to extinguish them.

As a Bonus Action on your later turns, you can change the direction in which the Line blasts from you.

Spike Growth.name: Spike Growth
Spike Growth.description:
The ground in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range sprouts hard spikes and thorns. The area becomes Difficult Terrain for the duration. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes [[/damage 2d4 type=piercing]] damage for every 5 feet it travels.

The transformation of the ground is camouflaged to look natural. Any creature that can't see the area when the spell is cast must take a Search action and succeed on a [[/check ability=wis skill=prc dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] or [[/check ability=wis skill=sur dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC to recognize the terrain as hazardous before entering it.

Web.name: Web
Web.description:
You conjure a mass of sticky webbing at a point within range. The webs fill a 20-foot Cube there for the duration. The webs are &Reference[difficultterrain], and the area within them is &Reference[lightlyobscured].

If the webs aren't anchored between two solid masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across a floor, wall, or ceiling, the web collapses on itself, and the spell ends at the start of your next turn. Webs layered over a flat surface have a depth of 5 feet.

The first time a creature enters the webs on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the &Reference[restrained] condition while in the webs or until it breaks free.

A creature Restrained by the webs can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer Restrained.

The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot Cube of webs exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing [[/damage 2d4 type=fire]] damage to any creature that starts its turn in the fire.

Create Food and Water.name: Create Food and Water
Create Food and Water.description: You create 45 pounds of food and 30 gallons of fresh water on the ground or in containers within range—both useful in fending off the hazards of malnutrition and dehydration. The food is bland but nourishing and looks like a food of your choice, and the water is clean. The food spoils after 24 hours if uneaten.

Glyph of Warding.name: Glyph of Warding
Glyph of Warding.description:
You inscribe a glyph that later unleashes a magical effect. You inscribe it either on a surface (such as a table or a section of floor) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book or chest) to conceal the glyph. The glyph can cover an area no larger than 10 feet in diameter. If the surface or object is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the glyph is broken, and the spell ends without being triggered.

The glyph is nearly imperceptible and requires a successful [[/check ability=wis skill=prc dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC to notice.

When you inscribe the glyph, you set its trigger and choose whether it's an explosive rune or a spell glyph, as explained below.

Set the Trigger. You decide what triggers the glyph when you cast the spell. For glyphs inscribed on a surface, common triggers include touching or stepping on the glyph, removing another object covering it, or approaching within a certain distance of it. For glyphs inscribed within an object, common triggers include opening that object or seeing the glyph. Once a glyph is triggered, this spell ends.

You can refine the trigger so that only creatures of certain types activate it (for example, the glyph could be set to affect Aberrations). You can also set conditions for creatures that don't trigger the glyph, such as those who say a certain password.

Explosive Rune. When triggered, the glyph erupts with magical energy in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on the glyph. Each creature in the area makes a [[/save ability=dex dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] saving throw. A creature takes 5d8 [[/damage (@item.level + 2)d8 type=acid]]{Acid}, [[/damage (@item.level + 2)d8 type=acid]]{Cold}, [[/damage (@item.level + 2)d8 type=acid]]{Fire}, [[/damage (@item.level + 2)d8 type=acid]]{Lightning}, or [[/damage (@item.level + 2)d8 type=acid]]{Thunder} damage (your choice when you create the glyph) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Spell Glyph. You can store a prepared spell of level 3 or lower in the glyph by casting it as part of creating the glyph. The spell must target a single creature or an area. The spell being stored has no immediate effect when cast in this way.

When the glyph is triggered, the stored spell takes effect. If the spell has a target, it targets the creature that triggered the glyph. If the spell affects an area, the area is centered on that creature. If the spell summons Hostile creatures or creates harmful objects or traps, they appear as close as possible to the intruder and attack it. If the spell requires Concentration, it lasts until the end of its full duration.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage of an explosive rune increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3. If you create a spell glyph, you can store any spell of up to the same level as the spell slot you use for the Glyph of Warding.

Foundry Note

The Explosive Rune activity allows you to choose the damage type in the roll dialog.

Plant Growth.name: Plant Growth
Plant Growth.description:
Casting Time: Action (Overgrowth) or 8 hours (Enrichment)

This spell channels vitality into plants. The casting time you use determines whether the spell has the Overgrowth or the Enrichment effect below.

Overgrowth. Choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point become thick and overgrown. A creature moving through that area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves. You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

Enrichment. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 365 days. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested. They can benefit from only one Plant Growth per year.

Speak with Plants.name: Speak with Plants
Speak with Plants.description:
You imbue plants in an immobile 30-foot Emanation with limited sentience and animation, giving them the ability to communicate with you and follow your simple commands. You can question plants about events in the spell's area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, weather, and other circumstances.

You can also turn &Reference[difficultterrain] caused by plant growth (such as thickets and undergrowth) into ordinary terrain that lasts for the duration. Or you can turn ordinary terrain where plants are present into Difficult Terrain that lasts for the duration.

The spell doesn't enable plants to uproot themselves and move about, but they can move their branches, tendrils, and stalks for you.

If a Plant creature is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a common language.

Black Tentacles.name: Black Tentacles
Black Tentacles.description:
Squirming, ebony tentacles fill a 20-foot square on ground that you can see within range. For the duration, these tentacles turn the ground in that area into &Reference[DifficultTerrain].

Each creature in that area makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 3d6 Bludgeoning damage, and it has the &Reference[Restrained apply=false] condition until the spell ends. A creature also makes that save if it enters the area or ends it turn there. A creature makes that save only once per turn.

A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC, ending the condition on itself on a success.

Control Water.name: Control Water
Control Water.description:
Until the spell ends, you control any water inside an area you choose that is a Cube up to 100 feet on a side, using one of the following effects. As a Magic action on your later turns, you can repeat the same effect or choose a different one.

Flood. You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20 feet. If you choose an area in a large body of water, you instead create a 20-foot tall wave that travels from one side of the area to the other and then crashes. Any Huge or smaller vehicles in the wave's path are carried with it to the other side. Any Huge or smaller vehicles struck by the wave have a [[/r 1d100cs<26#Vehicle is capsized]]{25 percent} chance of capsizing.

The water level remains elevated until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. If this effect produced a wave, the wave repeats on the start of your next turn while the flood effect lasts.

Part Water. You part water in the area and create a trench. The trench extends across the spell's area, and the separated water forms a wall to either side. The trench remains until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. The water then slowly fills in the trench over the course of the next round until the normal water level is restored.

Redirect Flow. You cause flowing water in the area to move in a direction you choose, even if the water has to flow over obstacles, up walls, or in other unlikely directions. The water in the area moves as you direct it, but once it moves beyond the spell's area, it resumes its flow based on the terrain. The water continues to move in the direction you chose until the spell ends or you choose a different effect.

Whirlpool. You cause a whirlpool to form in the center of the area, which must be at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep. The whirlpool lasts until you choose a different effect or the spell ends. The whirlpool is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet tall. Any creature in the water and within 25 feet of the whirlpool is pulled 10 feet toward it. When a creature enters the whirlpool for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there, it makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 Bludgeoning damage. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage. A creature can swim away from the whirlpool only if it first takes an action to pull away and succeeds on a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC.

Fabricate.name: Fabricate
Fabricate.description:
You convert raw materials into products of the same material. For example, you can fabricate a wooden bridge from a clump of trees, a rope from a patch of hemp, or clothes from flax or wool.

Choose raw materials that you can see within range. You can fabricate a Large or smaller object (contained within a 10-foot Cube or eight connected 5-foot Cubes) given a sufficient quantity of material. If you're working with metal, stone, or another mineral substance, however, the fabricated object can be no larger than Medium (contained within a 5-foot Cube). The quality of any fabricated objects is based on the quality of the raw materials.

Creatures and magic items can't be created by this spell. You also can't use it to create items that require a high degree of skill—such as weapons and armor—unless you have proficiency with the type of Artisan's Tools used to craft such objects.

Awaken.name: Awaken
Awaken.description:
You spend the casting time tracing magical pathways within a precious gemstone, and then touch the target. The target must be either a Beast or Plant creature with an Intelligence of 3 or less or a natural plant that isn't a creature. The target gains an Intelligence of 10 and the ability to speak one language you know. If the target is a natural plant, it becomes a Plant creature and gains the ability to move its limbs, roots, vines, creepers, and so forth, and it gains senses similar to a human's. The DM chooses statistics appropriate for the awakened Plant, such as the statistics for the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.gaSTr7DFZJLmgI2J]{Awakened Shrub} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.UR2gWLFHmFwG7ReH]{Awakened Tree} in the Monster Manual.

The awakened target has the &Reference[Charmed] condition for 30 days or until you or your allies deal damage to it. When that condition ends, the awakened creature chooses its attitude toward you.

Creation.name: Creation
Creation.description:
You pull wisps of shadow material from the Shadowfell to create an object within range. It is either an object of vegetable matter (soft goods, rope, wood, and the like) or mineral matter (stone, crystal, metal, and the like). The object must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube, and the object must be of a form and material that you have seen.

The spell's duration depends on the object's material, as shown in the Materials table. If the object is composed of multiple materials, use the shortest duration. Using any object created by this spell as another spell's Material component causes the other spell to fail.

MaterialDuration
Vegetable matter24 hours
Stone or crystal12 hours
Precious metals1 hour
Gems10 minutes
Adamantine or mithral1 minute

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The Cube increases by 5 feet for each spell slot level above 5.

Walking Stick.name: Walking Stick
Walking Stick.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

A thick shaft of wood wrapped with a sturdy grip makes a highly functional weapon in addition to a stout walking stick.
Walking Stick.descriptionpublic: A thick shaft of wood wrapped with a sturdy grip makes a highly functional weapon in addition to a stout walking stick.

Agrimage.biographyprivate:
Agrimagic is deeply associated with the Arctus Plateau, and most agrimages, even if they were not raised in Arcturian culture, favor Arcturian dress and customs to help those they help feel at home. Still, they generally stand out from other farmers on the plateau. Whether it's a certain glow to the seeds they carry, a spellbook on their hip, or a construct in their company, there's usually some indication that magic plays a role in their lives.

As they are a broader character type, each individual agrimage will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

While there is no absolute personality trait associated with being an agrimage, most have some ability to travel well from place to place to determine where their skills can be most of use, whether they get by on survival instincts or charm. Even among the more industrial agrimages of the consortium, the ability to put others at ease helps when trying to ascertain what is happening and where they can be of value.

Connections

The most important connection that any agrimage has is to their craft. Whether they are a member of the Agrimage consortium, a traveling practitioner who visits and helps settlements in need, or a fixture of a specific local community, almost all agrimages carry the symbol of the agrimage somewhere on their person to identify themselves as a practicing agrimage. These symbols are given great weight and respect by Arcturians, but are not given out by any overarching authority, making word of mouth about any agrimage's talents almost as critical.
Agrimage.biographypublic:
An unfamiliar face comes around a corner, but the symbol they carry immediately identifies them as an agrimage. They carry things you recognize — a jug of water, handful of seeds, plant leaves and stems and roots, a shovel, maybe, on their hip, but there is an air of magic around it all, a feeling that they can make the everyday items of agriculture into something truly magical.

Agrimages use magic to support the tending and farming of the land by local communities, from helping crops grow faster and more productively to attracting and corralling livestock to making towns safer from the dangers of the wilderness around them. The scale of this work varies from one agrimage to the next; while the Agrimage Consortium focuses on massive agricultural endeavors, traveling agrimages serve the farms, towns, and small cities of the Arctus Plateau, helping a variety of Arcturians survive and thrive on the land around them.

Each agrimage has their own style and teachings, but most combine the practice of spellcasting and the creation of agrimagical items and devices, letting them use the power of their spells to solve immediate issues while also giving those they've helped the opportunity to help themselves for the long-term.

Arcturian.name: Arcturian

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Common Clothing.name: Common Clothing
Common Clothing.descriptionpublic: A shirt, pair of pants, undergarments, socks and shoes or boots suitable for menial labour or travel, cannot be worn with armor.

Firestarter.name: Firestarter
Firestarter.descriptionpublic: A small waxed-leather pouch containing dry shredded plant fibre and wood shavings, with a little clasp inside for securing a piece of flint and a steel striking ring for the purposes of starting fires.

Lantern.name: Lantern
Lantern.descriptionpublic: An oil-burning or magically illuminated lantern that sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius.

Club.name: Club
Club.descriptionpublic: A crude yet effective weapon, the club is a blunt length of wood or bone designed to crush rather than cut. It can be a dangerous implement in the hands of even untrained fighters.

Quarterstaff.name: Quarterstaff
Quarterstaff.descriptionpublic: A simple wooden staff around six to eight feet long, the quarterstaff is a deceptively balanced weapon that can be deadly in trained hands.

Wilderness Novice.name: Wilderness Novice
Wilderness Novice.description:
You have received training in the basics of wilderness survival and traversal. You gain the Novice rank in the Wilderness skill and are no longer considered Untrained in that skill.

You know how to find and construct safe shelter from the elements, to start a fire for warmth, to keep cool in hot environments. You can find safe, drinkable water in most places, and how to identify which plants and animals can serve as safe food sources.

Arcturian.biographyprivate:
Arcturians are covered in more detail here: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian}

Personality

The Arcturians are friendly to everyone and greet outsiders as if they were friends and family. They are not martial and possess few martial traits because the plateau they have inhabited for generations is largely peaceful and serene.

Connections

The Arcturians have a close relationship with the Ordani, who reside in Ordain, the large metropolis located on the northeastern shores of the Arctus Plateau.

Phrases

"Hello there, friend!"

"Creativity is the heartbeat of our community."
Arcturian.biographypublic: @ref[name] are simple, honest crafters who live in expertly crafted and maintained family homes across the Arctus Plateau
Arcturian.biographyappearance: Arcturians are warm, friendly, and weathered by their time spent in the golden fields and outlying regions of the Arctus Plateau. You notice their hands are always not far from crafting tools, wearing simple leathers, brown cloth with hints and accents of the famous soft green colored fabrics draped around them, many of their clothes are also carefully woven with beautiful, subtle patterns.

Arcturian Miner.name: Arcturian Miner

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Blast Flask.name: Blast Flask
Blast Flask.descriptionprivate: Primarily used to break apart large pieces of ore, these alchemical flasks pack a concentrated punch. If combined in a large enough quantity, they can also be used to create a chain reaction that results in larger explosions.
Blast Flask.descriptionpublic: A flask filled with a reddish liquid explodes when it breaks open, creating a small explosive fire that quickly dissipates.
Blast Flask.actiondesc:
You light and throw the @ref[name], dealing Fire damage to all enemies in the radius of the explosion. The radius of the Blast depends on the quality of the bomb:

  • Shoddy - 3 feet

  • Standard - 4 feet

  • Fine - 6 feet

  • Superior - 8 feet

  • Masterwork - 10 feet

Claw Hammer.name: Claw Hammer
Claw Hammer.descriptionpublic: A seemingly humble tool with a flat striking face and curved claw, the claw hammer can become a savage weapon in determined hands.

Padded Armor.name: Padded Armor
Padded Armor.descriptionpublic: Consisting of quilted layers of cloth stuffed with rags or wool, padded armor cushions the body against blunt force and serves as the foundation beneath heavier gear.

Pickaxe.name: Pickaxe
Pickaxe.descriptionpublic: A crescent spike mounted atop a sturdy haft, the pickaxe is conventionally a mining implement, but can be wielded in combat to deliver dangerous piercing blows.

Lantern.name: Lantern
Lantern.descriptionpublic: An oil-burning or magically illuminated lantern that sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius.

Resilient.name: Resilient
Resilient.description:
Your body responds eagerly to healing, demonstrating a remarkable ability to recover from wounds.

Your Wounds Threshold is reduced by 1, making you easier to heal.

Heavy Weapon Training.name: Heavy Weapon Training
Heavy Weapon Training.description: You know how to use a heavy weapon to deliver punishing blows, putting your entire strength behind every swing. You are Trained with all weapons in the Heavy and Balanced categories.
Heavy Weapon Training.actiondesc: You unleash a powerful Strike with your mainhand weapon. The attack is slower to execute, but is Empowered to deliver additional damage.

Arcturian Miner.biographyprivate:
Among one of the most numerous professions in the plateau, miners can be found almost anywhere. Their dangerous work is vital to the success and progress of their people.

Anatomy

Miners come from all backgrounds, and as long as one is able to wield a pick, crack open the ground, and move a mine cart, they can be a miner. Most miners are physically strong, with good endurance and strong backs.

Behavior

Miners are working class, no-nonsense sorts. They have a hard job that requires nerve and focus. When the next strike of your pick could bring the mine down on your head, one must have a steely resolve. Miners tend to band together, looking out for each other, though when vast sums of riches are on the table this can quickly divide them.

Lore

Mining has existed for longer than people have lived in the Arctus Plateau, and few on Ember have seen stranger sights than those delving below its surface. Miners across the world know just how odd things become the closer one gets to the heart of Ember itself.
Arcturian Miner.biographypublic: The @ref[name]{miner} is one of many such workers that can be found all over the region. They work for themselves and the success of the Yakoshta mine specifically. Regardless of allegiance or employ, at the end of the day they all have the same thing in common: they are just another hard working member of the Arcturian people.
Arcturian Miner.biographyappearance: This miner is covered in the dirt and dust of a hard shift pulling precious materials from the crust of Ember, and wear the protective gear and heavy tools necessary for the task.

Arcturian Sailor.name: Arcturian Sailor

Hand Axe.name: Hand Axe
Hand Axe.descriptionpublic: Compact and deadly, the hand axe is a one-handed chopper with a short haft and sharp blade, ideal for throwing or close-quarters strikes where speed outmatches reach.

Padded Armor.name: Padded Armor
Padded Armor.descriptionpublic: Consisting of quilted layers of cloth stuffed with rags or wool, padded armor cushions the body against blunt force and serves as the foundation beneath heavier gear.

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Rope.name: Rope
Rope.descriptionpublic: A 30' length of plant-fibre rope that can be used to assist climbing or for many other purposes.

Arcturian Sailor.biographyprivate:
With much of Ember covered by major waterways, sea travel is a common way to move both inhabitants and goods from one region of Ember to the next. The sailors who make this sea travel possible can be found at most of Ember's ports, usually with their current ship of employ, though there are usually a few more sailors than ships available for those looking to recruit or replace workers on incoming ships.

As this is a broader character type, each individual sailor will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that may supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

While the personality of sailors can vary widely, many are attracted to the sailing life because of their adaptability and desire for freedom - when the winds and currents may change at any moment, sailors must be ready to adapt to whatever the waves bring them. While many sailing captains, especially on larger ships, require absolute obedience in crisis situations or when decisions have to be made, tackling daily tasks can often be a group or individual decision, with latitude given to what is best for the ship over paperwork or following specific rules. As a result, sailors are often those who chafe at rules and regulations, or who hate the feeling of repetition, as well as those who prefer a life that is physically demanding and who don't mind risk, as sailing can be both strenuous and dangerous.

Connections

Sailors are bonded to those they sail with. Whether they have been on the seas with the same group of people time and time again, or are taking their first step onto a new ship, sailing can be dangerous, with risks of weather, fire, and piracy, and each sailor must put their faith into those who sail beside them. While sailing ships can sometimes be loose with rules of behavior, loyalty and dereliction of duty are taken seriously and serious breaches can be punished with death. After leaving a ship, the bonds between sailors may loosen somewhat, but unless there are personality conflicts between two sailors, often any two that served together on a ship consider themselves to have a bond that will drive them to go out on a limb for each other.
Arcturian Sailor.biographypublic: The @ref[name] can be found in any port in the Arctus Plateau and beyond. They work the numerous sailing vessels travels across the Reaper Ocean, and are vital to trade in the region.
Arcturian Sailor.biographyappearance: An able crewman of a vessel, this burly sailor has strong limbs, and looks to have weathered many long days under harsh sun and unforgiving ocean swells. Though lightly armored and lightly armed, they look able to look after themselves.

Arcturian Sea Captain.name: Arcturian Sea Captain

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.descriptionpublic: The shortsword is a straight-bladed weapon which is nimble to wield and quick to strike in close combat. It features a crossguard ideal for parrying incoming blows.

Padded Armor.name: Padded Armor
Padded Armor.descriptionpublic: Consisting of quilted layers of cloth stuffed with rags or wool, padded armor cushions the body against blunt force and serves as the foundation beneath heavier gear.

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Light Weapon Training.name: Light Weapon Training
Light Weapon Training.description: You know how to wield light weapons fluidly with a high degree of maneuverability and grace in combat. You are Trained with all weapons in the Light and Balanced categories.
Light Weapon Training.actiondesc:
You dart forward nimbly, making a strike with sudden and unexpected swiftness to perform a Strike with a Finesse weapon against a single target with an increased range of +2 feet.

The attack is Difficult, but you do not move from your current position nor does this attack provoke Disengagement.

Dual Wield.name: Dual Wield
Dual Wield.description: You are adept at fighting with two weapons simultaneously. You can weave attacks together to strike more rapidly than possible with a single weapon.
Dual Wield.actiondesc: Immediately after you perform a basic Strike with your mainhand weapon, you make a reduced-cost fullow-up Strike with your offhand weapon.

Inspire Heroism.name: Inspire Heroism
Inspire Heroism.description: Your courageous presence inspires your nearby allies to strike with confidence.
Inspire Heroism.actiondesc: Each ally, excluding yourself, within 10 Feet gains +1 Boon to actions performed until the end of their next Turn.

Rallying Cry.name: Rallying Cry
Rallying Cry.description: Your presence as a battlefield leader fortifies and restores the morale of your allies.
Rallying Cry.actiondesc: You emit a courageous bellow that inspires allies within 12 feet of you to remain stalwart in the face of peril. All allies within range immediately recover your Presence score in Morale and become @Condition[resolute] for 3 Rounds.

Swashbuckler.name: Swashbuckler
Swashbuckler.description: Your bravado inspires your allies and cowes your enemies. When you Dodge or Parry a Strike, the attacker loses Morale equal to your Presence attribute. When you achieve a Critical Hit, all nearby allies who can see you gain Morale equal to your Presence attribute.

Feinting Strike.name: Feinting Strike
Feinting Strike.description: A two-weapon technique which makes a feint with your primary weapon, exposing your target for an off-hand attack.
Feinting Strike.actiondesc:
You feint with your mainhand weapon, making a Deception attack against the target's Reflex defense. You immediately make a Strike with your offhand weapon.

If your Deception was successful, you gain +2 Boons to your Strike and it deals an additional +6 Damage.

Hand Crossbow.name: Hand Crossbow
Hand Crossbow.descriptionpublic: This palm-sized crossbow trades power for concealability, perfect for close-quarters surprise shots or the desperate last bolt of a cornered rogue.

Mechanical Weapon Training.name: Mechanical Weapon Training
Mechanical Weapon Training.description: You are familiar in the design and usage of crossbows, firearms, and other similar armaments. You are Trained with weapons in the Mechanical category.
Mechanical Weapon Training.actiondesc: You focus deeply and calm your nerves to quickly Reload your mechanical weapon with exceptional haste.

Expanded Toolbelt.name: Expanded Toolbelt
Expanded Toolbelt.descriptionpublic:
An expanded toolbelt in the form of a utility belt, a bandolier, or an array of pockets stitched into your equipment.

This item provides a number of additional Toolbelt slots according to its quality tier:

  • Standard: +1 Toolbelt slot

  • Fine: +2 Toolbelt slots

  • Superior: +3 Toolbelt slots

  • Masterwork: +4 Toolbelt slots

Ring of Evasion.name: Ring of Evasion
Ring of Evasion.descriptionprivate: This item is presented as a ring, but it can be any type of accessory like an amulet, cloak, bracers, or other type of trinket.
Ring of Evasion.descriptionpublic:
This elegant ornamented ring feels slightly slick and difficult to grasp. While held it vibrates almost imperceptibly.

This ring provides a bonus to Dodge defense equal to the minimum of its Quality and Enchantment bonuses.

  • Fine quality and Minor enchantment: +1 Dodge

  • Superior quality and Major enchantment: +2 Dodge

  • Masterwork quality and Legendary enchantment: +3 Dodge

Spyglass.name: Spyglass
Spyglass.descriptionpublic: A handheld telescope made of brass and wood with highly polished glass lenses. Used to magnify a distant view.

Razor.name: Razor
Razor.descriptionpublic: A particularly sharp blade used for shaving or, in some cases, surgery.

Fishing Pole.name: Fishing Pole
Fishing Pole.descriptionpublic: A collapsible wooden pole affixed with metal rings and a post to attach fishing line. Easily fits in or alongside a backpack.

Book.name: Book
Book.descriptionpublic: A wood-covered book bound in cloth or leather.

Arcturian Sea Captain.biographyprivate:
Nearly all Sea Captains gained their position in the same way - by making their way up the ranks of a ship from a sailor. While generally this is done through hard work, there are sea captains who ascend by force, or because they are one of the only remaining survivors of a disaster, though those who muscle or luck their way to being a captain are often thought to be sailing on borrowed time. The captain of any sailing vessel is the ultimate authority on their ship and can run it as they choose, bound only by how safe they are able to keep their crew and how successfully they are able to get sailors to stay loyal to them and their ship.

As this is a broader character type, each individual captain will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that may supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

Sea Captains, like sailors, enjoy the freedom of being out at sea, but those who wish to be the authority on a ship often also desire a bit of control. For some, this is out of a tyrannical nature. Others simply like to keep things organized the way that they see fit, or enjoy bringing those underneath them together in a common cause. Whatever their reasons, sea captains tend to be decisive leaders who are able to command the respect and loyalty of their crew. Those who don't, or who make poor decisions (or who simply get unlucky) are often lost along with their ships beneath the water's surface.

Connections

In many ways, sea captains are simply sailors with more authority, and they feel a bond with their fellow sailors that all do, but since they must have a certain amount of authority, there is sometimes a limit to how deeply they can bond with those who serve underneath them, lest they make decisions of the heart when they must make the choices that best serve the ship as a whole. Often, their closest bonds outside of their ship are to other captains, and to those who they once sailed with who are not currently on their ship. Still, most sea captains will do a great deal to help those who sailed on their ships, whether on the sea or on land.
Arcturian Sea Captain.biographypublic: The @ref[name] can be found in any port in the Arctus Plateau and beyond. They command the numerous sailing vessels traveling across the Reaper Ocean, and are vital to trade in the region.
Arcturian Sea Captain.biographyappearance: The commander of a vessel, this seasoned officer has strong limbs, and looks to have weathered many long days under harsh sun and unforgiving ocean swells. Though lightly armored and lightly armed, they look able to look after themselves and their crew.

Burnished Hand Protector.name: Burnished Hand Protector

Heavy Crossbow.name: Heavy Crossbow
Heavy Crossbow.descriptionpublic: A powerful, steel-limbed crossbow requiring a crank or lever to draw, it delivers devastating bolts capable of punching through armor or pinning enemies to walls.

Kite Shield.name: Kite Shield
Kite Shield.descriptionpublic: Tall and tapered for full-body protection, the kite shield curves around the wielder’s body and is favored by cavalry and infantry alike for its excellent coverage and iconic silhouette.

Splint Mail.name: Splint Mail
Splint Mail.descriptionpublic: A layer of vertical metal strips riveted to a backing of leather or mail, splint armor offers strong limb protection while sacrificing some flexibility.

Bastard Sword.name: Bastard Sword
Bastard Sword.descriptionpublic: A bastard sword, also known as a hand-and-a-half sword, is a versatile weapon with a straight, double-edged blade around 40 inches long. This weapon is forged for both single-handed agility and two-handed power.

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Shield Combat Training.name: Shield Combat Training
Shield Combat Training.description: You are practiced at fighting with shield, using it to slam into and imbalance your foes. You are Trained with weapons in the Shield category.
Shield Combat Training.actiondesc: Following a basic Strike with your mainhand weapon, you Strike with your shield, causing the @Condition[staggered] condition for one Round.

Bulwark.name: Bulwark
Bulwark.description:
You have expertise in using a Shield to defend yourself and others.

Once per Turn while you have a Shield equipped, you may use the Defend action at a reduced cost of 1 Action Point.

Intercept.name: Intercept
Intercept.description: You protect your allies, intercepting blows that might otherwise be directed towards your companions.
Intercept.actiondesc:
You intercept the path of an enemy which enters your Engagement radius, immediatly moving up to your Stride to interpose yourself and block their path.

If the enemy moves out of your Engagement radius or attacks any other creature during their turn, you may make a Disengagement Strike against them.

Hold Fast.name: Hold Fast
Hold Fast.description: You are a calm anchor in the swirling sea of combat. When you have a Shield equipped, your Engagement increases by +1, allowing you to simultaneously engage more adjacent foes.

Torch.name: Torch
Torch.descriptionpublic: Able to be used as either a light source or as an improvised weapon, a torch can illuminate dark places and ward off the foes that lurk there.

Healing Elixir.name: Healing Elixir
Healing Elixir.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to rapidly close wounds and improve bodily health.
Healing Elixir.actiondesc:
Immediately recover an amount of Health dependant on the quality of the elixir.

  • Shoddy - Immediately heals 6 Health.

  • Standard - Immediately heals 12 Health.

  • Fine - Immediately heals 24 Health.

  • Superior - Immediately heals 48 Health.

  • Masterwork - Immediately heals 96 Health.

Counter Strike.name: Counter Strike
Counter Strike.description: You are trained to transition between defending with your shield and a swift counter-attack.
Counter Strike.actiondesc: When you defend against a melee attack with a Block you may expend Focus to retaliate with a reduced-cost Strike using your mainhand weapon.

Disarming Strike.name: Disarming Strike
Disarming Strike.description: A martial technique designed to disarm your opponent, forcing them to drop an object held in one of their hands.
Disarming Strike.actiondesc: You make a Strike against a the Reflex defense of a single target. The technique is Difficult to perform and deals reduced damage. If successful, the target's mainhand weapon is Dropped.

Heavy Weapon Training.name: Heavy Weapon Training
Heavy Weapon Training.description: You know how to use a heavy weapon to deliver punishing blows, putting your entire strength behind every swing. You are Trained with all weapons in the Heavy and Balanced categories.
Heavy Weapon Training.actiondesc: You unleash a powerful Strike with your mainhand weapon. The attack is slower to execute, but is Empowered to deliver additional damage.

Burnished Hand Protector.biographyprivate:
Practiced in the ancient sword arts of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken}, Burnished Hand Protectors are low-ranking soldiers who pledge their service to the militant organization known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}, a well-armed and well-funded league of warriors who safeguard the great city of Ordain and its beloved @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}. Under the guidance of their leader, the honorable @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver}, the Burnished Hand Protectors and their fellow soldiers help maintain a steady peace for the prosperous city and its people.

Personality

There is no single defining personality trait among Burnished Hand, although a certain amount of grit is required to endure the training necessary to join their ranks. Camaraderie among Protectors is common, but these relationships tend to be shallow and jocular until strengthened via time and circumstance. As a whole, the Burnished Hand do possess a fair amount of respect for their leader Steros, and are known to follow his stoic example in public. And as their name suggests, Burnished Hand Protectors are also regarded for their relative kindness in battle, often choosing to disarm and subdue their opponents via intimidation rather than take their lives outright.

Connections

First and foremost, Burnished Hand Protectors are allegiant to their order and its members, including the skilled axe-master Steros Kraver. Secondly, the entire Burnished Hand serves at the mercy of the Cindaric Sages, whom they are duly sworn to protect. Burnished Hand soldiers of various skill levels are stationed at the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CVV5b22IksTdg7hy]{Rusted Fortress} on Bura Island, while others occupy the barracks known as Veneration Hall in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.86owx3lgvm2zLyv4]{Lower Ashvale} district. Burnished Hand Protectors rarely venture deep into the southern and western reaches of the Arctus Plateau, but occasional expeditions alongside Cindaric allies are known to happen.
Burnished Hand Protector.biographypublic: Burnished Hand Protectors serve as the rank-and-file troops of the eponymous Burnished Hand, a militant order tasked with protection of the Arctus Plateau and steeped in the ritualistic traditions of the Oaken. Armed and armored for battle, these well-trained humanoid soldiers are ready to handle any conflict thrust upon them, in times of war and peace alike. Protectors and other soldiers of the Burnished Hand are known for their allegiance to the venerable Cindaric Sages, whom they are duly sword to defend.
Burnished Hand Protector.biographyappearance: You regard a heavily-armored Ordani warrior, whose bronze splint mail gleams with a gorgeous russet luster. A symmetrical crimson hand with the roots of an oak tree decorates this soldier's chest piece, and the well-oiled longsword at their side looks poised and ready for action.

Carmin Anther.name: Carmin Anther

Keen Hearing & Sight.name: Keen Hearing & Sight
Keen Hearing & Sight.description: [[lookup @name]] has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or hearing.

Entangle.name: Entangle
Entangle.description:
Grasping weeds and vines sprout from the ground in a 20-foot square starting from a point within range. For the Duration, these Plants turn the ground in the area into difficult terrain.

A creature in the area when you cast the spell must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be &Reference[Restrained] by the entangling Plants until the spell ends. A creature restrained by the plants can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself.

When the spell ends, the conjured Plants wilt away.

Plant Growth.name: Plant Growth
Plant Growth.description:
This spell channels vitality into plants within a specific area. There are two possible uses for the spell, granting either immediate or long-term benefits.

If you cast this spell using 1 action, choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot radius centered on that point become thick and overgrown. A creature moving through the area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves.

You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

If you cast this spell over 8 hours, you enrich the land. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 1 year. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested.

Wall of Force.name: Wall of Force
Wall of Force.description:
An invisible wall of force springs into existence at a point you choose within range. The wall appears in any orientation you choose, as a horizontal or vertical barrier or at an angle. It can be free floating or resting on a solid surface. You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a sphere with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-by-10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. In any form, the wall is 1/4 inch thick. It lasts for the Duration. If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (your choice which side).

Nothing can physically pass through the wall. It is immune to all damage and can't be dispelled by Dispel Magic. A Disintegrate spell destroys the wall instantly, however. The wall also extends into the Ethereal Plane, blocking ethereal travel through the wall.

Eversmoking Bottle.name: Eversmoking Bottle
Eversmoking Bottle.description:
Wondrous item

Smoke leaks from the lead-stoppered mouth of this brass bottle, which weighs 1 pound. When you use an action to remove the stopper, a cloud of thick smoke pours out in a 60-foot radius from the bottle. The cloud's area is heavily obscured. Each minute the bottle remains open and within the cloud, the radius increases by 10 feet until it reaches its maximum radius of 120 feet.

The cloud persists as long as the bottle is open. Closing the bottle requires you to speak its command word as an action. Once the bottle is closed, the cloud disperses after 10 minutes. A moderate wind (11 to 20 miles per hour) can also disperse the smoke after 1 minute, and a strong wind (21 or more miles per hour) can do so after 1 round.

Thornbark.name: Thornbark
Thornbark.description:
Trigger: When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you erupt with thorny barbs for 1 minute.

While the barbs last, you gain the following benefits:

  • Retaliatory Barbs. When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack (including the attack that triggered this reaction), it takes [[/damage activity=dnd5eactivity000]] damage.

  • Hard to Handle. A creature has disadvantage on Strength (Athletics) checks it makes to Grapple or Shove you.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Fibrous Resilience.name: Fibrous Resilience
Fibrous Resilience.description:
The fibrous biology of Thornlings is incredibly resilient, providing the following benefits:

  • Your armor class cannot be less than 16 regardless of what type of armor you are wearing.

  • You have resistance to damage taken from falling.

  • You gain double the effects of healing from expended Hit Dice.

Carmin Anther.biographyprivate:
Carmin has always felt that they should be part of something special but has never been sure of exactly what. Raised by clothing designers who use natural materials to create fashion, they often tried on their parents' designs and imagined themselves in an alternate life of glamour or intrigue, but often struggled to make moves towards those lofty goals in real life. They wander a lot, driven by an ill-defined idea of what it means to be in an adventure and stand out from those around them, and have begun developing a larger than life persona as the Canyon Crawler to make themselves more "known."

Personality

Carmin was in the first generation of Thornlings to be fully raised in Brevin, but has never really felt attached to the city, preferring to spend time on the road and communing with nature solo. They sometimes feel that those in Brevin talk a lot about the natural world, but don't really take the opportunity to step outside of their manicured plant homes and orderly lives to really understand nature. Deep down, this is driven by their belief that they understand nature better than anyone else could, even the druids, and bitterness that their potential in this area has never been truly recognized or understood.

Connections

Carmin was once close friends with Edivel Sprout, and the two often went on walks together through the Arctus Plateau in search of adventure, but in recent years they’ve grown apart. Both are risktakers, but Edivel believes that their risks are necessary to gaining knowledge, while Carmin primarily wants an adrenaline rush and a bit of attention, even if it's negative.
Carmin Anther.biographypublic:
The young thornling's body is more spikes and crags than smooth wood, with a green and red coloring that could easily blend into the background in the right bit of deep tangled foliage. They keep their head up high and their shoulders back, but shift their weight from one foot to another, as if unsure of exactly how to stand as they make their presence known.

Carmin is a young thornling who prefers the solitude of the road and the forest to the company of others, but feels adrift even in the natural places they love, always wishing for a feeling of adventure and glory. Raised by clothier parents who catered to adventurers and dignitaries, they want to get the same level of respect and fame, but don't quite know how to get there. In recent years this has led to their development of a new persona, the brigand known as the Canyon Crawler, whose name they want to be known far and wide.

Cindaric Adherent.name: Cindaric Adherent

Quarterstaff.name: Quarterstaff
Quarterstaff.descriptionpublic: A simple wooden staff around six to eight feet long, the quarterstaff is a deceptively balanced weapon that can be deadly in trained hands.

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Rune: Life.name: Rune: Life
Rune: Life.description:
A chaotic force of creation, responsible for living matter. The Life rune governs health and matters relating to biological growth.

The Life rune scales using Wisdom and provides Restoration of Health or inflicts Poison damage opposed by Fortitude. It is opposed by the orderly rune of Death.
Rune: Life.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Life allows you to stimulate biological growth and nourish physical health, producing one of the following effects:

  • Cultivate 1 cubic foot of existing plants or fungus to rapidly grow to a healthy, blossoming, or harvestable state.

  • Identify a negative physical condition that is affecting a creature such as @Condition[diseased], @Condition[poisoned], @Condition[bleeding], or @Condition[weakened].

  • Verify whether a portion of food or drink is free of contamination from bacteria, parasites, or poison.

Bloom may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Gesture: Influence.name: Gesture: Influence
Gesture: Influence.description:
You intensify the arcane power of a Rune into a concentrated direct contact which is generally a more powerful evolution of the basic Touch gesture.

The Influence gesture scales using Presence and targets a single adjacent creature. It deals 10 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus.

Rune: Earth.name: Rune: Earth
Rune: Earth.description:
The orderly force of elemental earth, responsible for physical matter. The Earth rune governs minerals, metals, soils, and other physical compounds.

The Earth rune scales using Wisdom, targets Reflex, and deals Acid damage to Health. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Lightning.
Rune: Earth.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Earth allows you to manipulate raw forces of rock, mineral, and soil in basic ways, producing one of the following effects:

  • Quickly shape up to one cubic foot of available material into a simple geometric form like a cuboid, ellipsoid, or polyhedron.

  • Precisely copy the physical shape of a held object that is smaller than a 6-inch cube, reproducing it from available clay, stone, or metal. The replica retains no useful properties except for its physical form.

  • Separate and collect earthen particles from the surface of an object, creature, or liquid that you touch, rendering the subject completely cleaned or purified in moments.

Mould may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Talisman Weapon Training.name: Talisman Weapon Training
Talisman Weapon Training.description: You understand the arcane usage of talismans, orbs, foci, or other similar implements to channel magic or empower spellcraft. You are Trained with weapons in the Talisman categories.
Talisman Weapon Training.actiondesc:
You use your equipped Talisman to attempt to regain some Focus. You perform a Harmless Strike against your own Rallying threshold.

On a success you recover +1 Focus if using a one-handed Talisman and +2 Focus if using a two-handed Talisman. On a critical success the amount of Focus recovered increases by an additional +1.

Soothe.name: Soothe
Soothe.description: You administer a soothing Performance which rallies your allies, restoring Morale.
Soothe.actiondesc: You perform a calming verse, benefiting all allies who can perceive you within 12 feet. Make a Performance Check against the Madness threshold of each ally. On success, each ally's Morale is restored.

Lantern.name: Lantern
Lantern.descriptionpublic: An oil-burning or magically illuminated lantern that sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius.

Rallying Tonic.name: Rallying Tonic
Rallying Tonic.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to gradually fortify the psyche and improve morale.
Rallying Tonic.actiondesc:
Immediately, and at the beginning of each of the next 5 Rounds, recover an amount of Morale dependent on the quality of the tonic.

  • Shoddy - Heals 2 Morale each Round

  • Standard - Heals 4 Morale each Round

  • Fine - Heals 8 Morale each Round

  • Superior - Heals 16 Morale each Round

  • Masterwork - Heals 32 Morale each Round

Healing Tonic.name: Healing Tonic
Healing Tonic.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to gradually close wounds and improve bodily health.
Healing Tonic.actiondesc:
Immediately, and at the beginning of each of the next 5 Rounds, recover an amount of Health dependent on the quality of the tonic.

  • Shoddy - Heals 2 Health each Round

  • Standard - Heals 4 Health each Round

  • Fine - Heals 8 Health each Round

  • Superior - Heals 16 Health each Round

  • Masterwork - Heals 32 Health each Round

Padded Armor.name: Padded Armor
Padded Armor.descriptionpublic: Consisting of quilted layers of cloth stuffed with rags or wool, padded armor cushions the body against blunt force and serves as the foundation beneath heavier gear.

Steadfast.name: Steadfast
Steadfast.description: Your patient resolve allows you to endure psychologically grueling ordeals with steadfast determination.
Steadfast.actiondesc: You harden yourself against demoralization. Your Morale is increased by your Wisdom score and you temporarily gain the Resolute condition.

Gesture: Sense.name: Gesture: Sense
Gesture: Sense.description:
You attune your mind to the arcane power of a Rune to sense nearby sources of energy.

The Sense gesture scales with Presence and produces an emanation with 30 feet radius and position that remains centered upon the spellcaster. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus. It may optionally be Maintained at the additional cost of 1 Focus every subsequent round.

This spell allows the caster to detect the presence of spellcraft using the same Rune as the one incorporated in this spell. The sense will also momentarily detect the presence of creatures according to their type.

  • Control: Fiends

  • Death: Undead

  • Earth: Oozes and Earth Elementals

  • Flame: Dragons and Fire Elementals

  • Frost: Giants and Frost Elementals

  • Illumination: Celestials

  • Illusion: Fey

  • Kinesis: Monstrosities

  • Life: Plants and Beasts

  • Lightning: Constructs and Storm Elementals

  • Oblivion: Outsiders

  • Soul: Humanoids

Playtest Notes

There is no automation for the sense that is temporarily granted by this spell, but such automation can be provided in the future via a Detection Mode which temporarily reveals creatures of the appropriate type to the spellcaster while the spell is maintained.

Cindaric Adherent.biographyprivate:
Cindaric Adherents serve as the rank-and-file members of the Cindaric Sages, and are renowned throughout the Arctus Plateau as competent healers with kind-hearted souls. Their druidic magic is harnessed from the primal metaphysical forces of Ember, and they consider themselves as tireless caretakers of the living planet's preternatural Heartblood. Wherever trouble can be found throughout the Arctus Plateau, the Cindarics and their adherents aren't too far behind with timely aid and good intentions.

As they are a broader character type, each individual Cindaric Adherent will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

While there is no absolute personality trait associated with being a Cindaric Adherent, all walks of life make their way into the Cindaric order — whether to serve Ember's people or simply revere the living planet with time-honored Cindaric practices. Cindaric Adherents tend to be selfless people, with personalities that allow for gregarious interactions with the needy and the infirm.

Connections

The most important connection that any Cindaric Adherent has is to Ember itself. And a Cindaric Adherent's specific enclave sets the pace for their more intimate connections to other Sages, from the Ordani opulence of Cindarin Temple to the rural confines of Corpin Sanctuary. Furthermore, Cindaric Adherents aren't quite expected to leave their lives behind when they join the order, but their busy schedules allow little room for a conventional life marked by excessive individualism.
Cindaric Adherent.biographypublic: Cindaric Adherents are skilled healers and scholars who spend their lives in dedicated service to the Cindaric faith. Whether from the splendor of Cindarin Temple in Ordain, the remote heights of Corpin Sanctuary on Mial Mountain, or the hermetic reaches of another enclave, a Cindaric Adherent is always ready to feed the hungry, heal the sick, or clothe the poor. Cindaric Adherents are known for their compassion and goodwill, and each Adherent finds their own passion in the face of perpetual service. To facilitate their life of charity.
Cindaric Adherent.biographyappearance: This scholarly healer is clad in garments of bright gold and lush crimson, the colors of the famed Cindaric Sages of the Arctus Plateau. Their shoulders and tunic are marked with the familiar four-leafed diamond that signifies the Cindaric order, and their hands are marked and calloused by the wholesome abrasions of honest labor. The sage regards you with a benevolent smile.

Mutagist Bombardier.name: Mutagist Bombardier

Studded Leather Armor.name: Studded Leather Armor

Powerful Throw.name: Powerful Throw

This item provides a number of additional Toolbelt slots according to its quality tier:

Caustic Phial.descriptionpublic: Corrosive liquid swirls within this vial of intentionally thin glass, designed to shatter on impact and spill the caustic substance upon a target.

The amount of burning damage and its duration is dependent on the quality of the @ref[name]:

Alchemical Grenade.descriptionpublic: This small brass and glass canister weighs about a pound and contains a strange green fluid held at pressure. It has an obvious trigger on its side.

The amount of poison damage and its duration is dependent on the quality of the @ref[name]:

  • Shoddy - 2 damage for 2 rounds

Alchemist's Fire.name: Alchemist's Fire
Alchemist's Fire.descriptionpublic: A flammable concoction that ignites upon impact and burns intensely for a short time.
Alchemist's Fire.actiondesc:
