Fatal Contingency.actiondesc: @ref[actor.name]'s mouth begins to foam and hiss, emitting a noxious smell as acid rapidly corrodes their mouth and throat.

Mutagist Bombardier.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

@ref[name]s are typically disgraced alchemists shunned for their unethical and cruel practices. They are protected under layers of leather and chain, and don complicated gas masks to keep themselves safe from the worst effects of their chemicals.

Behavior

Loving nothing more than to test their creations on any victims that cross their paths, these maniacs gleefully hurl their handmade bombs and grenades where the explosions will have the greatest effect. Outside of combat they are consumed with tuning and perfecting their chemical designs, creating new compounds to test, and devising even more dangerous ways to maim and kill.

Lore

@ref[name]s are ranged shock troops used in defensive and offensive actions. They are not organized or trained, and are given unsettling leeway in how they prepare and deploy their various chemical weapons.
Mutagist Bombardier.biographypublic: The @ref[name] is an agile, unpredictable agent of chaos employed by the Mutagists. Prized for their knowledge of alchemy and feared for their love of mayhem, they are one of the more unpredictable elements found in the Mutagist ranks.
Mutagist Bombardier.biographyappearance: This wiry figure is clad in a studded leather vest caked with old stains, worn over a grimy apron looped around their waist. A bandolier loaded with glass vials and chemical canisters hangs across their chest. Their face is hidden behind a bulky, round-eyed gas mask, its filter puffing quietly with each breath. Chemical stained and burned fingers twitch restlessly at their sides, hovering near their arsenal and always ready to snatch up a bomb.

Mutagist Scout.name: Mutagist Scout

Mutagist Scout.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

@ref[name]s are typically humanoids chosen for their hardy constitution and astute senses. Their physique reflects the rigors of their environment, with athletic, lean builds adorned with scars and weathering from countless missions. Concealed beneath their adventurer's garb are tools for harvesting and trapping, including custom darts tipped with paralyzing toxins and snares designed to hold creatures alive. These scouts often carry small notebooks, inscribed with detailed observations or coded instructions, inked in alchemical solutions invisible to the naked eye.

Behavior

In the field they are indistinguishable from any other member of the Anachraenum or other ostensibly benign adventuring companies. Their operations are clandestine, always masked behind much more plausible tasks of exploration and adventure. Quick and calculating in combat, they prefer to work in concert with their allies to outmaneuver foes, either aiming to immobilize and kill their victims, or abduct them, ensuring specimens remain useful for future experimentation.

Lore

@ref[name]s are the eyes and ears of the Mutagists, though the faction is shrouded in enough secrecy that even the scouts don't actually know what their master's true aims are. As far as anyone else is concerned, these scouts are nothing more than adventurers and mercenaries traveling from job to job.
Mutagist Scout.biographypublic: The Mutagist Scout is a wily operative who blends into society by masquerading as an adventurer. In truth, they travel the lands with aim to track, capture, and gather creatures materials for their more malignant counterparts.
Mutagist Scout.biographyappearance: A rugged, sly-looking individual, clad in a patchwork cloak of leather and fabric, their attire a mismatched collection of adventure-worn gear. They have the bearing of a well traveled and road worn adventurer or mercenary. It is concerning how utterly nondescript they actually are.

Mutagist Vivisector.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The @ref[name] is always a humanoid and can be from any ancestry. They are typically scarred from constant contact with chemicals, their faces, arms and hands bearing the burns of haphazard experimentation. They are rarely seen outside their stained coats and aprons, and always carry belts filled with vials and needles filled with awful chemicals.

Behavior

They are cruel, aggressive and often entirely devoid of moral or ethical constraints. In truth, they are specifically chosen for these qualities, as their masters find this makes them more effective at getting desired results.

Their malnourished appearance is a testament to their dietary negligence, as they sacrifice their wellbeing for the consumption and creation of more potent medicinal and alchemical brews. If they ever stopped consuming their cocktails they might die on the spot. Luckily, that is not a problem they have to worry about often.

Lore

As relatively recent arrivals to the region of Arctus Plateau, Mutagists are shrouded in mystery, and the@ref[name] is only one of the many minions they employ. They are, at best, a clandestine association of vile chirurgeons devoted to grotesque and sinister ends. These faceless surgeons are nothing more than a limb of a much more obscured beast. Not even they know the true extent of the Mutagists or their full agenda, always working through middlemen and contacts that create layers of deniability.
Mutagist Vivisector.biographypublic: The @ref[name] is a dangerous surgeon obsessed with injecting subjects with chemicals, and then cutting open their corpses (if they are lucky) to see what effects those compounds had on their victims.
Mutagist Vivisector.biographyappearance: Clad in stained apron and coat, they regard you coolly from behind goggles and mask which make it impossibly to discern anything about them. They turn a razor sharp scalpel in their hand, as their off-hand rests on a pouch containing several vials of undoubtedly dangerous compounds. The air around them is thick with the scent of medicine and blood.

Otherhood Brigand.biographyprivate:
Brigands are front-line fighters found protecting Otherhood interests, or traveling to battles where hit-and-run tactics aren't advantageous.

Anatomy

The Otherhood recruits from all cultures and walks of life, though each and every one is selected for their prowess in combat or potential to become a dangerous fighter. Raiders are the Otherhood's frontline fighter, and are relied upon to handle the most dangerous missions. Their armor, though a patchwork of stolen, scavenged, repaired, and hand-me-down pieces, is more than sufficient to protect them in their brutal hit-and-run attacks.

Behavior

The Otherhood operates with a blend of strategy and opportunism. Trained to work seamlessly with each other, most raiders form dedicated squads that train and plan together to increase cohesion. In combat they engage targets with efficient precision, often laying traps to disorient their targets and provide them as many advantages in combat as possible. Raiders exhibit loyalty to their group and cause, often prioritizing the objective or the preservation of fellow raiders over their own safety.

Lore

The Otherhood is seen as one of the more prominent threats within the Arctus Plateau. Their unpredictable attack patterns, resourcefulness, and ferocity make them a constant danger that one can never truly prepare for sort of posting large numbers of defenders, which itself presents issues they can exploit. While their ultimate goals remain obscure to most raiders themselves, their actions nourish the unrest and instability upon which their organization thrives. To the local populations the Otherhood is often seen as little more than glorified bandits.
Otherhood Brigand.biographypublic: The @ref[name] is a dangerous combatant serving an order of criminal raiders and smugglers operating out of the city of Seawall. They are easily identified by their golden robes, though they have been known to travel in disguise.
Otherhood Brigand.biographyappearance: A well-armored, season fighter of the Otherhood wearing golden robes and scale armor. They look determined, disciplined and spoiling for a fight.

Otherhood Raider.name: Otherhood Raider

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Dual Wield.name: Dual Wield
Dual Wield.description: You are adept at fighting with two weapons simultaneously. You can weave attacks together to strike more rapidly than possible with a single weapon.
Dual Wield.actiondesc: Immediately after you perform a basic Strike with your mainhand weapon, you make a reduced-cost fullow-up Strike with your offhand weapon.

Backstab.name: Backstab
Backstab.description: You focus your cunning instincts on exploiting the weak points of a flanked target. You identify an opportunity and strike with deadly efficiency.
Backstab.actiondesc: You Strike with your mainhand weapon against a Flanked target, dealing Deadly damage.

Pinning Shot.name: Pinning Shot
Pinning Shot.description: You fire a tactically placed shot to pin your target against a nearby surface.
Pinning Shot.actiondesc: You Strike from distance. The attack is Difficult, however if your target is it it becomes Restrained until the end of their next Turn.

Opportunist.name: Opportunist
Opportunist.description: You sieze any opportunity you can to capitalize on an enemy who turns their back on you. You may make a Disengagement Attack even if you are otherwise Fully Engaged, but you do so without the 2 Boons that would ordinarily apply to such an attack.

Weak Points.name: Weak Points
Weak Points.description: You identify moments of opportunity to strike at an enemy's weak points. When attacking a target that is Unaware, Flanked, or Exposed using Finesse weaponry, you gain +2 damage to any Strike.

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.descriptionpublic: Tthe shortsword is a straight-bladed weapon which is nimble to wield and quick to strike in close combat. It features a crossguard ideal for parrying incoming blows.

Dagger.name: Dagger
Dagger.descriptionpublic: Small, swift, and deadly, the dagger slips between ribs or into gaps in armor with ease, its wicked edge favored by assassins, thieves, and those who prefer a silent kill.

Shortbow.name: Shortbow
Shortbow.descriptionpublic: Compact and quick to draw, the shortbow excels in rapid, close-quarters archery and skirmishes, favored by scouts, hunters, and swift-footed raiders.

Studded Leather Armor.name: Studded Leather Armor
Studded Leather Armor.descriptionpublic: A base of leather reinforced with small metal studs or riveted plates, this armor strikes a balance between mobility and modest protection against slashes.

Flaming Arrow.name: Flaming Arrow
Flaming Arrow.description: You take time to light and loose an arrow covered in flammable pitch. This shot takes longer but is very damaging to either creatures or structures.
Flaming Arrow.actiondesc: You loose a Empowered ranged strike using a Projectile weapon which deals Fire damage upon impact.

Projectile Weapon Training.name: Projectile Weapon Training
Projectile Weapon Training.description: You have a basic education in archery and other projectile weaponry. You are no longer treated as Untrained with weapons in the Projectile categories.
Projectile Weapon Training.actiondesc: You can loose a shot under pressure, although with decreased accuracy. You perform a Strike that is Difficult, but has a reduced Action cost.

Otherhood Raider.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Otherhood Raiders are recruited from all cultures and walks of life, though each and every one is selected for their prowess in combat or potential to become a dangerous fighter. Raiders are the Otherhood's frontline fighter, and are relied upon to handle the most dangerous missions. Their armor, though a patchwork of stolen, scavenged, repaired, and hand-me-down pieces, is more than sufficient to protect them in their brutal hit-and-run attacks.

Behavior

The Otherhood Raider operates with a blend of strategy and opportunism. Trained to work seamlessly with each other, most raiders form dedicated squads that train and plan together to increase cohesion. In combat they engage targets with efficient precision, often laying traps to disorient their targets and provide them as many advantages in combat as possible. Raiders exhibit loyalty to their group and cause, often prioritizing the objective or the preservation of fellow raiders over their own safety.

Lore

The Otherhood is seen as one of the more prominent threats within the Arctus Plateau. Their unpredictable attack patterns, resourcefulness, and ferocity make them a constant danger that one can never truly prepare for sort of posting large numbers of defenders, which itself presents issues they can exploit. While their ultimate goals remain obscure to most raiders themselves, their actions nourish the unrest and instability upon which their organization thrives. To the local populations the Otherhood is often seen as little more than glorified bandits.
Otherhood Raider.biographypublic: Otherhood Raiders are dangerous combatants belonging to order of anarchist raiders and smugglers operating out of the city of Seawall. They are easily identified by their golden robes, though they have been known to travel in disguise.
Otherhood Raider.biographyappearance: A lightly-armored, heavily armed fighter wearing golden robes and brown leather armor. They look determined, disciplined and spoiling for a fight.

Punch.name: Punch
Punch.descriptionprivate: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

Thornling Lineage.name: Thornling Lineage

The fibrous biology of Thornlings is incredibly resilient, providing the following benefits:

  • Your Armor defense cannot be below 6 regardless of what type of equipment you are wearing.

  • Damage taken from Falling is reduced by half before other resistances apply.
Thornling Lineage.actiondesc:
When you are targeted by a melee attack, you can cause thorny barbs to extrude from your body. For one minute you gain the following benefits.

  • Melee attacks which Hit or Glance you wound the attacker in retaliation who suffers damage equal to your Toughness ability score.

  • Attempts to Grapple or Push you suffer +2 Banes.

The effects of this Action apply to the attack which triggered the reaction.

ALPHA ONE: The effects of Thornbark are not yet fully automated.

Leg Sweep.name: Leg Sweep
Leg Sweep.description: You use a weapon which scales using Strength to sweep your enemy off balance, swinging low to knock them from their feet.
Leg Sweep.actiondesc: You make a Strike attack with your mainhand weapon. This technique is Difficult to execute and deals reduced damage, but if successful renders your target Prone.

Unarmed Combat Training.name: Unarmed Combat Training
Unarmed Combat Training.description: You are familiar with basic martial arts and hand-to-hand combat. You know how to subdue or restrain opponents using your physical Strength. You are Trained with weapons in the Unarmed category.
Unarmed Combat Training.actiondesc: You attempt to physically restrain or subdue an opponent. Perform a Athletics skill attack against an adjacent target. If successful, both you and your target are @Condition[restrained] for 1 Round.

Bonded Mind.name: Bonded Mind
Bonded Mind.description: The mind of a @ref[actor.name]{creature} with this talent is inextricably bound to other members of its group. It is capable of instantaneous telepathic communication with any other @ref[actor.taxonomy.name]{creature of its taxonomy} within 60 feet.

Death Spores.name: Death Spores
Death Spores.description: When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} dies, it explodes in a volatile burst of corrupting energy.
Death Spores.actiondesc: When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} becomes @Condition[dead], it explodes in a pulse of spores that deal Corruption damage, attacking the Fortitude defense of all nearby creatures that fail to resist the effect and afflicting them with the @Condition[decaying] condition for 3 rounds.

Sporix Host.biographyprivate:
These thornlings are afflicted with a magical fungus known as the Sporix, which has taken over their mind and seeks to spread itself to more and more plant life in the world. While the Sporix can spread to most plants, it only becomes truly dangerous when it manages to take over a Thornling, which itself is rare and difficult.

Anatomy

These afflicted Thornlings are still alive, but barely. Their flesh and foliage are withered and ill-colored, giving the appearance of death or undeath, though that is not actually the case. The fungus growing out of them splits open their bark and burrows as deeply as it can so that it can draw life out of them.

This leads to the withered, pale complexion that most afflicted thornlings have, and over time will result in the host's death.

Behavior

Sporix afflicted Thornlings are largely mindless, the host's personality and thoughts are suppressed to the point that even mind reading magic has great difficulty finding them. As a result, the afflicted are commanded entirely by the psychic network of fungi growing out of them.

The fungal intelligence is as smart, collectively, capable of using basic tactics, coordinating the hosts in action, and even limited communication though certain magical avenues (such as speak with plants).

Sporix colonies tend to be single-minded, though, focused on spreading their spores to more plants, especially ones that are capable of moving on their own, like Thornlings. This makes them dangerous and aggressive when encountering potential hosts.

Lore

Sporix are not well documented or well understood, and they have only been witnessed a few times; they are more myth than reality. In some rare instances, travelers with extensive knowledge of underground regions may have heard rumors, but little else.

The Sporix is a semi-sentient magical fungus that grows in the darkest, dampest regions of the Sinkhole Depths. The fungus specifically targets plants and works its way into the core of the afflicted plants, drawing out the flora's life force until it withers and dies.

Unfortunately, Sporix colonies are capable of afflicting Thornlings if said Thornlings are already weakened by sickness, starvation, and fatigue. Thankfully, the Sporix have not managed to spread very far, as it is only well suited to dark, damp regions. The fungal weakness to heat and light makes it hard for them to survive anywhere light touches, and greatly limits the spread of colonies.
Sporix Host.biographypublic: @ref[name] are an extremely rare sight, and found only in the Sinkhole Depths. Their bodies are covered in strange, glowing mushrooms and they appear to move in groups, only barely aware of their surroundings.
Sporix Host.biographyappearance: This thornling's bark is pale and withered, their foliage equally dry and dying. They appear to be on the brink of death, glassy-eyed, and in something of a stupor. Their body is covered in brightly colored, glowing fungus that pulses and shimmers in strange patterns.

Echolocation.description: The [[lookup @name]] can't use its blindsight while deafened.

Juvenile Garganthus.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The [[lookup @name]] is a vaguely reptilian, six-limbed monstrosity that hails from the lightless depths of Ember's subterranean Pathways, where its preternatural abilities help it thrive as an apex predator. Garganthi are scaled with exceptionally durable hides, and possess an agile strength that allows them to navigate cavernous expanses with ease. A cruel and ravening evolution has helped shaped the [[lookup @name]]'s capacity to track its prey without the benefit of light, as well its ability to emit an uncanny, primeval screeching sound vicious enough to make an enemy's brain bleed.

Behavior

Carnivorous to the bone, Juvenile Garganthi live to consume any living creatures they deem worthy of their fierce appetites. And the [[lookup @name]] is never one to shy away from challenging prey. To track said prey, the [[lookup @name]] utilizes acute echolocation abilities; two large, frilled ears are the outward signs of the creature's keen sense of hearing. Furthermore, this Pathways monstrosity is capable of navigating subterranean tunnels with ease, as evident in the agile girth of its hind legs and the tenacity of its primeval claws.

A [[lookup @name]] is also able to utilize its prehensile tail to great effect in combat. When the Garganthus isn't busy grappling its enemy, it can use anything from loose earth to uprooted timber as an improvised weapon.

Lore

Creatures similar to the [[lookup @name]] once populated the surface of Ember, but were driven underground into the Pathways where they languished in subterranean abandon, evolving and devolving for centuries untold.

The modern [[lookup @name]] is but one specimen amongst the numerous Pathways creatures that have found purchase near surface realms. Although the Juvenile members of the species are among the earliest encountered, larger adults are known to populate the lightless depths of Ember's subterranea and beyond.
Juvenile Garganthus.biographypublic:
You behold the pale and hulking form of a bipedal reptilian creature with a long prehensile tail. Its agile saurian head is marked by multiple sets of bulbous pearlescent eyes, two fan-shaped ears of prodigious length, and a mouth lined with spear-like fangs. The creature's massive arms end in three-fingered hands with formidable claws, and its muscular legs look as though they could mount the toughest terrain with ease.

A [[lookup @name]] is a malicious Pathways predator that embodies the cruel primordial savagery of Ember's prehistory. It has a vaguely humanoid torso, but its scaly, somewhat ophidian features are extreme, monstrous, and grotesque. It is horrible to behold, and inspires fear in any creature small enough to fall prey to its clawed grasp.

Mootap.name: Mootap

Swallow.name: Swallow
Swallow.description: @Ref[actor.name]{This creature} has the capability of swallowing creatures smaller than them whole, though only one creature may be affected by this action at a time.
Swallow.actiondesc:
You swallow a target enemy, effectively removing that foe from combat. The swallowed target is @Condition[blinded] and @Condition[restrained] until released.

If you take Severe damage, are Wounded, or are rendered @Condition[incapacitated] you regurgitate the swallowed creature.

Extended Breath.name: Extended Breath
Extended Breath.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can hold its breath for 15 minutes.

Glowing Body.name: Glowing Body

On a success you may move up to your Stride directly through the enemy's space. Your enemy is knocked Prone and may not make any attack of opportunity against you. On a failure your movement is blocked and your remain in your current position.

Tentacles.descriptionpublic: Slick writhing tendrils that can grasp and whip, exuding a natural toxin.

Mootap.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

This eyeless Pathways carnivore resembles a stubby eel crowned with a head of two dozen lambent tendrils like those of a giant anemone. These pale, writhing tendrils surround a gaping maw lined in soft bioluminescent tissue, from which the rare arcane stones known as @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{Inkaro Pearls} are produced. Inkaro Pearls nucleate within the soft tissue over the course of several months, and are harvested by the people of the Arctus Plateau as a valuable resource.

A mootap’s rubbery skin is covered in luminous mottled stripes similar to a tiger’s; and although this strange monstrosity moves rather slowly, its grip is resolute — which makes the cultivation of Inkaro Pearls a somewhat hazardous (yet profitable) trade. Fortunately, the Mootap's susceptibility to lightning presents Inkaro farmers with a somewhat reliable method of surviving these hazards.

Mootap proportions range from small and medium-sized varieties when they are young to large specimens which form the backbone of pearl harvesting operations in the Sinkhole Depths beneath Arcturel. Rarely, huge or even larger-sized exceptional specimens have been reported as encountered in the deeper areas of the Pathways.

Behavior

@ref[name]s inhabit subterranean freshwater environments like the Sinkhole Depths, Mycelian Expanse, and Fogbound Caverns of the Pathways — particularly above sites where Spirit Beast Blood festers deep within Ember's earthy crust. @ref[name]s are carnivorous, and usually feed on fish, mollusks, cephalopods, and crustaceans associated with their subterranean habitat. @ref[name]s have been known to attack smaller humanoids or other small-sized creatures on occasion, particularly outside of cultivated areas. Greater @ref[name]s of the deep pathways are rumored to have maws and tentacles large enough to swallow an adult Rask (or even yet, a full wagon).

@ref[name]s slowly track their prey via electromagnetic blindsight, often preferring to lay in wait using their invisibility to surprise attack targets that swim close enough to their long-reaching tentacles. Other times, @ref[name]s will approach their prey while cloaked, waiting until the perfect moment to spring a poisoned tentacle attack in an attempt to swallow the prey alive. Their bioluminescence is usually triggered during these moments, likely as an attempt to frighten prey and other would-be predators.@ref[name]s often hunt alone, but are known to swim in small groups when prey is bountiful (or large) enough.

Lore

Due to their abstruse connection to Spirit Beast Blood, the most learned of Pathways scholars speculate these monstrosities originated during the Age of Beasts — the result of some arcane manipulation by Giant sorcery. Others relate stories of Abyssal influences that came about during the Shattering, but these confabulations are tall tales at best.

Inkaro Pearls can be harvested from a Mootap's maw, but can be a challenging and dangerous task involving a skill check as described in the [[/eventState arcturelSidePool]] event.
Mootap.biographypublic: @ref[name]s are curious aquatic monstrosities that dwell in pools of the Sinkhole Depths below Arcturel and other subterranean areas of the Pathways. Capable of producing rare arcane stones known as an inkaro pearls, these bioluminescent amalgams of eel and anemone are cultivated by people of the Arctus Plateau in relatively small numbers with great effort.
Mootap.biographyappearance: An eyeless creature appears out of nowhere, resembling a stubby eel crowned with a head of two dozen luminous tendrils like those of a giant anemone. These photophore tentacles writhe with inhuman glee as it reaches blindly into the water ahead.

Suarrok Juvenile.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Suarrok are exceeding strange creatures, with singular eye, feathers, bat-like wings, two tails, and a long, piercing beak. They are surprisingly agile despite their strange form, and their eyes possess considerable magical power, capable of harming creatures through simple stares alone.

Behavior

Suarroks are highly territorial creatures, favoring rugged, high perches to build their nests and scout for prey below. Suarroks are primarily nocturnal hunters, but can be encountered at any time of day, and grow bolder the longer they go uncontested in their territory.

Relying on their uncanny eye and blinding gaze to disorient prey during ambushes, they descend rapidly upon unsuspecting targets, their piercing calls drawing the eye and often resulting in stunned prey. Their long, piercing beaks drive through stunned prey, killing them instantly, and allowing them to feed on the spot, or carry off the carcass for later consumption.

Suarrok are opportunistic feeders, primarily hunting unwary ground mammals or prowling coastlines and bodies of water where they can dive on unsuspecting sea life. They have been known to attack the occasional unwary traveler.

Solitary by nature, Suarroks fiercely defend their territory against any intruders, including others of their kind, even driving off their young as soon as they are old enough to fly. During mating season they communicate through a series of eerie, high-pitched calls and the flashes of their luminescent gaze.

For a cyclopean creature, the Suarrok has been observed hunting, flying, and fighting without any issue. It is speculated that the creature's single eye perceives the world differently, allowing it to see more, and compensate for a lack of depth perception.

Lore

The Suarrok is an ancient creature believed to have originated from Ragen, given their burning stare, thought there is little evidence otherwise to support this. There is a spirited debate about the Suarrok in the halls of academia and its true nature as a monstrosity. Most recognize that the Suarrok is not a natural creature, not a beast in the most classical sense, yet it does have the hallmarks of one, as the Suarrok have been observed to nest, mate, hunt, and generally act as a beast would.

Suarroks are generally left undisturbed due to their aggressive nature, though seasoned hunters and adventurers sometimes seek them out for the valuable resources they can provide. Their eyes are particularly valuable to alchemists and enchanters, believed to hold potent, magical properties associated with blindness and fire.

The large feathers from their wings are prized as materials for clothing, art, decoration, and for the larger ancestries — high-quality quills. Lastly, Suarrok leather is light and sturdy, but rare, making it valuable, as is fresh Suarrok meat, though the bitter aftertaste makes it an acquired taste at best.
Suarrok Juvenile.biographypublic: The Juvenile Suarrok is a one-eyed magical monstrosity that nests in high, rocky areas. It is primarily found in and around the Forest of Stone, making nests in high perches where its young are shielded from opportunistic predators like Drakes, Kadhana lizards, and Crag Raptors. The Suarrok has managed to spread itself far and wide, and as a result it can be encountered all across Ember's rocky regions, often serving as the apex flying predator in the region.
Suarrok Juvenile.biographyappearance: This creature is an unsettling thing, a strange mixture of bird and lizard, with massive, bat-like wings fringed with trailing feathers. A long, sinuous neck that coils and moves like a serpent holds a massive head with menacing, serrated beak that's perfectly designed for tearing through flesh. On this head rests a single, enormous eye that glows ominously, and as its gaze sweeps over you, a wash of stinging heat can be felt.

While in contact with a web, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} knows the precise location of any other creature in contact with the same web.
Web Spinner.actiondesc: The creature can spend 10 minutes to spin a new new section of webbing that covers a 5-foot area.

Venomous Bite.name: Venomous Bite
Venomous Bite.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks, injects toxin which, if successful, inflicts the @Condition[poisoned] condition for 6 Turns.

Bewildering Gaze.name: Bewildering Gaze
Bewildering Gaze.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is capable of mesmerizing and bewildering its prey with it's gaze.
Bewildering Gaze.actiondesc:
The creature focuses its supernatural gaze on a single target it can see within 60 feet which can also see it.

The target faces a Willpower attack which deals Void damage to Morale and inflicts the @Condition[confused] condition.

Young Cheliceraeth.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Cheliceraeths are carnivorous, and will feed on any living creature of suitable size; when necessary, their preternatural crystalline biology allows these wicked predators to go for months or even years without eating.

Behavior

Crystal spiders usually live in groups of 2 or more, and will use the intricate network of glittering webs that cover the crystalline walls of their lairs to sense, trap, and surprise their enemies. And while young cheliceraeths have yet to develop the talents, elder cheliceraeths are known to possess a kind of cruel intelligence. Quite often, one cheliceraeth will engage the quarry with a succession of vile or inane taunts while an allied spider approaches in secrecy for an ambush. Cheliceraeths prefer to web or magically bewilder their prey from afar before closing in.

Pathways areas rife with gemstone deposits — like the Forest of Stone’s Kaleidoscope Caverns or the tunnels beneath the Salt Flats — serve as the primary habitat of crystal spiders, who seem curiously at home amidst these particular kinds of strange and surreal landscapes.

Lore

Cheliceraeths are cruel children of Sitheera, the Outer God of Corruption and Domination, and came about during the earliest days of the Shattering — when they began to infest the lightless, crystalline corners of Ember’s expansive subterranea. Only the oldest and wisest of Cheliceraeths recall their lineage to the Spider Goddess, but all Crystal Spiders possess the same demented hubris brought about by their matron’s unearthly pride in her creations.
Young Cheliceraeth.biographypublic: Also known as a crystal spider, the Young Cheliceraeth is a juvenile form of a much larger arachnid monstrosity native to Ember’s crystal-laced subterranea that resembles a giant spider made of faceted purple moonstone. In addition to its poisonous bite, a cheliceraeth can entrance its prey with a bewildering gaze that warps the target's mind with psychedelic uncertainty.
Young Cheliceraeth.biographyappearance: A melodious, twinkling percussion fills the air — like the sound of softly cascading glass — as you notice a medium-sized growth of crystals transform into a ten-eyed creature with eight spindly legs and two large, articulated fangs. This horrible arachnid resembles an enormous semi-translucent spider made of faceted purple moonstone, which shimmers and scintillates in the scant light. Angry crystalline spikes decorate the extremities of its silicate form, and its ten loathsome eyes appear refracted with a dreadful arcane opalescence.

Giant Luminous Ooze.name: Giant Luminous Ooze

Amorphous.name: Amorphous
Amorphous.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} may move through a space as narrow as 1 inch in diameter without any penalty to its Stride. It gains a bonus to Dodge equal to half its Toughness score and is immune to the @Condition[restrained] condition.

Subdivide.name: Subdivide
Subdivide.description: The @ref[actor.name]{ooze} can divide itself into multiple parts, each an independent copy of the original.
Subdivide.actiondesc:
The ooze's cells rapidly divide and the creature splits in two! The original creature and its clone equally divide its remaining Health. The Size of each resulting creature is decreased by 1.

If in combat, the new creature acts as a Summon and joins at Initiative 1. This Action may only be used if the creature has Size larger than 2. The created ooze never has rank superior to Normal.

Multiply.name: Multiply
Multiply.description: The @ref[actor.name]{ooze} grows rapidly, increasing in health and size.
Multiply.actiondesc: The ooze's cells rapidly multiply as the creature grows. Its Size increases by 1 and its Health increases by its Toughness value.

False Appearance.name: False Appearance
False Appearance.description: While it remains motionless, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} is indistinguishable from some other object or material.

Corrode Weapon.name: Corrode Weapon
Corrode Weapon.description: The internal corrosive metabolism of the @ref[actor.name]{ooze} threatens to dissolve metal weapons that strike it.
Corrode Weapon.actiondesc:
When struck by a melee weapon made of metal, the ooze attempts to consume the weapon itself, potentially breaking it.

This attack is Harmless, but if successful the Quality of the weapon used in the attack is downgraded by one tier. On a Critical Success or if the weapon is already Shoddy, the weapon becomes entirely Broken. Enchanted weapons are protected against this effect.

Electrified Pseudopod.name: Electrified Pseudopod
Electrified Pseudopod.description: This @ref[actor.name]{ooze} courses with currents of electricity which it can emanate in a violent blast of electrical force.
Electrified Pseudopod.actiondesc:
A Strike which targets Fortitude and arcs between up to three targets that are within 3 feet of each other. This attack deals Electricity damage to Morale.

On a Critical Hit it inflicts the Shocked condition for 2 Turns.

Magnetic Disarm.name: Magnetic Disarm
Magnetic Disarm.description: The @ref[actor.name]{ooze} uses it's magnetically charged body to disarm an attacker of their metal weapon.
Magnetic Disarm.actiondesc:
When struck in melee by a metal weapon, the ooze can react to wrench the weapon free of its wielder's grasp using its magnetized body. It performs an Athletics skill attack against the target's Fortitude. On a success, the weapon is dropped and absorbed into the ooze's body.

The ooze gains its Toughness score in Health and the weapon cannot be retrieved unless the ooze is defeated.

Bewildering Gleam.name: Bewildering Gleam
Bewildering Gleam.description: The @ref[actor.name]{ooze} spreads itself into a gelatinous sheet that coats every nearby surface.
Bewildering Gleam.actiondesc: The ooze rapidly spreads itself to cover every surface within a 15 foot radius. Creatures other than oozes within this area must defend an attack against their Willpower or be overcome with a bewildering languor dealing Radiant damage to Morale and inflicting the Disoriented condition.

Pseudopod.name: Pseudopod
Pseudopod.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{ooze} lashes out with an amorphous tentacle of slime.

Crystal Carapace.name: Crystal Carapace
Crystal Carapace.descriptionpublic: This ooze is covered in crystal fragments and formations which protect it from harm.

Luminous Copper Flakes.name: Luminous Copper Flakes
Luminous Copper Flakes.descriptionprivate: Due to the strange biological process of luminous oozes, these copper flakes have some unique properties which can be used by spellcasters or alchemists to perform spellcraft or create specialized concoctions.
Luminous Copper Flakes.descriptionpublic: A pile of powdery copper flakes which have been internally metabolized by a Luminous Copper Ooze.

Luminous Liquid Silver.name: Luminous Liquid Silver
Luminous Liquid Silver.descriptionprivate: Due to the strange biological process of luminous oozes, this silver has some unique properties which can be used by spellcasters or alchemists to perform spellcraft or create specialized concoctions.
Luminous Liquid Silver.descriptionpublic: Silver in its liquid form. Usually, obtaining liquid ore requires heating silver to high temperatures, but it can occasionally be found in a liquid form cool enough to the touch to be gathered and carried in a vial or bottle. This silver is unique it has been internally metabolized by a Luminous Silver Ooze.

Luminous Iron Scraps.name: Luminous Iron Scraps
Luminous Iron Scraps.descriptionprivate: Due to the strange biological process of luminous oozes, these iron scraps have some unique properties which can be used by spellcasters or alchemists to perform spellcraft or create specialized concoctions.
Luminous Iron Scraps.descriptionpublic: A pile of iron slivers which have been internally metabolized and magnetized by a Luminous Iron Ooze.

Luminous Pooled Gold.name: Luminous Pooled Gold
Luminous Pooled Gold.descriptionprivate: Due to the strange biological process of luminous oozes, this gold has some unique properties which can be used by spellcasters or alchemists to perform spellcraft or create specialized concoctions.
Luminous Pooled Gold.descriptionpublic: Rumors about puddles of gold often take their truth from this substance, which is rare but valuable. While it takes some effort to gather and carry this slippery substance, usually found in very small quantities that fit, at most a single bottle. This gold is unique it has been internally metabolized by a Luminous Gold Ooze.

Giant Luminous Ooze.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The ooze's exact form changes depending on its actions, but it generally resembles a glowing gelatinous mass. Bits of gold, silver, and copper can be seen within, as well as the occasional piece of crystal, as if it absorbed everything in its path and is carrying all that it came across with it.

Behavior

The giant luminous ooze has some of the qualities of the smaller luminous oozes - like the iron ooze, it is magnetic, and metal items sometimes cling to it after hitting it, and its pseudopods are electrified like a silver ooze. Its most distinguishing feature, though, is its ability to split off pieces of itself into smaller oozes, which fight on its behalf, and to reabsorb those oozes into its main body as a form of healing.

Once defeated, the giant luminous ooze melts into a pool of different liquid ores - generating gold, silver, and copper ore that can be collected and sold.

Lore

The giant luminous ooze was created through combination of silver, gold, copper, and iron luminous oozes. Like these smaller oozes, it was created via a contaminant found in Yakoshta mine that leaked down into the mine from the broken Aedir Spypost above, but grew larger by absorbing and combining with several of the smaller oozes.
Giant Luminous Ooze.biographypublic: Formed from a combination of different luminous metallic oozes, kaleidoscope crystals, and an alchemical contaminant, the Giant Luminous Oozes uses its ability to spawn and absorb smaller metallic oozes alongside the powerful strikes made by its crystal-embedded tentacles.
Giant Luminous Ooze.biographyappearance: This amorphous blob of glowing gold seems to have endless numbers of tentacles that shift in shape, size, and number, each studded with bits of metal and pieces of kaleidoscope crystal, their sharp edges catching and reflecting the light.

The ooze's exact form changes depending on its actions, but it generally resembles a mass of gelatinous copper and has a slight glow to it, emitting dim light.

Behavior

The luminous copper ooze has the ability to heal a small amount of the damage it has taken in lieu of an attack and often uses hide and seek tactics, striking and then retreating to regroup.

Once defeated, the copper ooze becomes flaked copper of impeccable purity, which can be used to make coins and other copper objects. Some alchemists have also been known to use the copper flakes in healing potions.

Lore

The luminous copper oozes are a variation of the copper oozes sometimes used as companions by the Yakoshta miners due to their mild healing properties - the luminous variety are brighter, larger in size, and more aggressive than the originals. They have begun to spread through the Forest of Stone and have occasionally been seen as far as Helkas in the Arctus Peninsula.

The luminous oozes were formed by the interaction of metallic oozes and the runoff from a broken Aedir construct located in a defunct tower above Yakoshta mine.
Luminous Copper Ooze.biographypublic: Copper Luminous Oozes use the copper within their gelatinous bodies to heal themselves from injury, and have been known to pretend to be a pile of copper coins in an attempt to play dead while they recover.
Luminous Copper Ooze.biographyappearance: An amorphous slime of a creature slowly oozes forward, dragging bits of flaked copper and the occasional crystal within its gelatinous body. Though it seems formless as it moves, it reaches out in a long tentacle-like arm when confronted with a fight, readying itself to strike.

The gold luminous ooze is fast-moving, and often attempts to shift position quickly between attacks to confuse its intended target.

Once defeated, the gold ooze becomes liquid gold ore, which can be collected and used to make coins and other gold objects.

Lore

The gold luminous ooze was formed when dripstone oozes being used to mine gold interacted with the luminous runoff from the Yakoshta mine. They have begun to spread through the Forest of Stone and have occasionally been seen as far as Helkas in the Arctus Peninsula.
Luminous Gold Ooze.biographypublic: Gold luminous oozes resemble a pile of gold treasure when still, but are faster and more viscous than other oozes once they begin moving, able to not only squeeze through small openings and lash out with golden tentacles, but stretch out to trap and corral their prey.
Luminous Gold Ooze.biographyappearance: Like a puddle of congealing gold ore in motion, the creature elongates its gelatinous ooze of a body into a single slender viscous arm and pulling itself across the ground. Narrower and more willing to stretch than other luminous oozes, it moves more quickly than the average ooze as it moves in search of prey.

The ooze's exact form changes depending on its actions, but it generally resembles a mass of gelatinous iron and has a slight glow to it, emitting dim light.

Behavior

The luminous iron ooze exerts a slight magnetic field on the world around it. While it cannot control the effects of this magnetic energy, its magnetism draws metal items close to its body.

The luminous iron ooze can sometimes be found carrying metal weapons or tools that have stuck to it - while these eventually drop off of its body as it travels, enterprising miners have been known to use the non-luminous version of these oozes to keep track of their tools, while some thieves use this magnetic property as a way of stealing armor and weapons.

Lore

The luminous iron ooze are a variation of the iron oozes sometimes used as companions by the Yakoshta miners - the luminous variety are brighter, larger in size, and more aggressive than the originals. They have begun to spread through the Forest of Stone and have occasionally been seen as far as Helkas in the Arctus Peninsula.

The luminous iron oozes were formed by the interaction of iron oozes and the runoff from a broken Aedir construct located in a defunct tower above Yakoshta mine.
Luminous Iron Ooze.biographypublic: The iron luminous ooze exerts a small magnetic pull on metal objects in its vicinity, including weapons used against it, but relies on its amorphous pseudopod to pummel its victims, often drawing them with its ability to resemble a pile of iron scraps when still.
Luminous Iron Ooze.biographyappearance: The viscous body of the luminous iron ooze is a silvery gray, filled with small fragments of metal and the occasional piece of glittering crystal. As it moves, its body shapes and reshapes itself, stretching and contracting in a viscous pool that extends a single gray-iron tentacle.

Luminous Silver Ooze.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The ooze's exact form changes depending on its actions, but it generally resembles a mass of gelatinous silver and has a slight glow to it, emitting dim light.

Behavior

The silver luminous ooze gathers static electricity as it moves, which it can then emit as an attack. It often releases energy collected this way over the course of its natural movements at the beginning of a battle, then replenishes itself throughout the conflict to use at the end as a killing blow.

Once defeated, the silver ooze becomes liquid silver ore, which can be collected and used to make coins and other silver objects.

Lore

The silver luminous ooze was formed when dripstone oozes being used to mine silver interacted with the luminous runoff from the Yakoshta mine. They have begun to spread through the Forest of Stone and have occasionally been seen as far as Helkas in the Arctus Peninsula.
Luminous Silver Ooze.biographypublic: Though they are indistinguishable from silver coins when still, silver luminous oozes pick up static electricity as they move and can use it to shock liquid and creatures around them using the tentacles formed from their ever-shifting gelatinous bodies.
Luminous Silver Ooze.biographyappearance: Light reflects from what one moment looks like a heap of silver coins and the next moment like a slowly pulsing silver ooze of a creature, with sparkles of light emanating from the bits of metal dust and crystal trapped within its gelatinous center. It shifts shape as it edges forward, crackling with static electricity as it extends a long piece of itself like an arm poised to strike.

Sarracine.name: Sarracine
Sarracine.descriptionprivate: This fluid made from the contents of a Sarraceias' digestive sac can be used to dissolve substances from metal locks to centuries-old caked-on grime.

Grasping Vines.name: Grasping Vines
Grasping Vines.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is Large or smaller, it has the &Reference[Grappled apply=false] condition (escape DC [[lookup @check.dc.value activity=okSl0Ip6CA6yIzzc]]), and the [[lookup @name]] uses [[/item Engulf]] on it.

Engulf.name: Engulf
Engulf.description:
The [[lookup @name]] engulfs one Large or smaller creature it is grappling. The engulfed creature has the &Reference[Blinded apply=false] and &Reference[Restrained apply=false] conditions, and it can’t breathe.

At the start of each of the [[lookup @name]]’s turns, the engulfed creature must make a [[/save format=long]].

Failure: The creature takes [[/damage average]] damage. Once the [[lookup @name lowercase]] engulfs a creature, it can’t use Engulf again until the start of its next turn.

Sarracenias.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Sarracenias appear to be a mound of plant material at first glance, aided by their tendency to allow moss and grass to grow in and around their large carapace, but they are in fact a set of large stomach-like sacs surrounding powerful vines that drag creatures into the sacs for slow digestion.

Though it is extremely difficult to harvest, the acid within a Sarracenias sac is a powerful substance, able to dissolve nearly anything, and is highly desired both by thieves looking to use it to dissolve locks and members of the Anachraenum, who use it in small quantities to remove dirt and grime from artifacts.

Behavior

Sarracenias are patient, letting prey come to them instead of chasing it down, but when the time comes to strike, they are decisive, lashing out with their vines and drawing their victims into the sacs within their body that allow them to slowly digest creatures and keep themselves fed even during lean times.

Sarracenias are found most frequently in jungle terrains, but they travel well, and have been transported to a few places outside of their natural habitat by well-meaning adventurers. Once in a new location, they are adaptable and root down quickly, becoming nearly immovable parts of the landscape.

Lore

Sarracenias are naturally occurring carnivorous plants. It's not clear what specific situation or environment is necessary to spawn them, but they have been encountered all over the world, and come in a wide array of appearances based on the biomes they call home.
Sarracenias.biographypublic:
What at first glance seems to be a pile of plant debris spread across the ground moves, ever so slightly, at the hint of nearby motion, waiting for an opportunity to strike. Beneath the green and purple mass that blends into the scenery around it, its vines are ready to snatch up any who come too close and draw them into its waiting hungry maw.

Though often mistaken for a mound of vegetation or the rotting stump of a large tree when motionless, the Sarracenias waits patiently for unsuspecting creatures to walk within the grasp of the vines concealed within its large mass, which grab onto prey and drag them into the sack-like chambers within its body. Once within, escape is nearly impossible; whatever is captured within the Sarracenias is slowly dissolved and digested to feed its growing mass.

While in sunlight, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} suffers 2 Banes to all actions.

This mechanic is handled through an Active Effect that is easily toggled when applicable.

Abyssal Protection.name: Abyssal Protection
Abyssal Protection.description:
While in an area of dim light or darkness, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} gains a +2 bonus to their Armor defense and is @Condition[guarded].

This is implemented via an Active Effect which can easily be toggled to enable or disable the benefit.

Grave Mark.name: Grave Mark
Grave Mark.description: When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} achieves a Critical Hit with a melee attack, it leaves a baleful Grave Mark upon its target.
Grave Mark.actiondesc:
After achieving a Critical Hit with a melee attack, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks the target's Willpower defense, leaving a Grave Mark upon a success that inflicts the @Condition[exhausted] condition that persists until the target completes a Rest.

If a humanoid creature bearing a Grave Mark dies while under the effects of the mark, it rises from death on its subsequent Turn as a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.taxonomy.Item.ghoul00000000000]{Ghoul}.

Shadow Gait.name: Shadow Gait
Shadow Gait.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is able to step into and out of shadow itself to move in nightmarish and unpredictable ways.
Shadow Gait.actiondesc: While in dim light or darkness, the @ref[actor.name] can meld into shadow to disappear from view. It may Move and reappear within a different area which is also dim light or darkness. This is a Displace movement which provokes no disengagement.

Necrotic Bite.name: Necrotic Bite
Necrotic Bite.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} tears into flesh with a maw that is corrupted by pestilence and undeath.
Necrotic Bite.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks with a pestilent bite that is Empowered and deals Corruption damage.

On a Critical Success the attack causes the @Condition[decaying] condition for 3 Turns.

Bestial Senses.name: Bestial Senses
Bestial Senses.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has finely honed senses and is particularly perceptive of their environment, all Awareness checks gain +2 Boons.

Strike First.name: Strike First
Strike First.description: Shoot first, ask questions later. You gain +1 Boon on any Strike or Spell attack against an enemy whose initiative score is lower than your own.

Hold Fast.name: Hold Fast
Hold Fast.description: You are a calm anchor in the swirling sea of combat. When you have a Shield equipped, your Engagement increases by +1, allowing you to simultaneously engage more adjacent foes.

Corrupted Cadrithor.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Vulnerable to daylight and magical radiance, these malevolent hunters of the dark are known for their enervating spectral attacks and their ability to magically transport themselves between shadows. The shaded, canine form of a Corrupted Cadrithor resembles a bestial skeleton wreathed in black flame, whose wicked claws and mighty fangs are as incorporeal as they are deadly.

Behavior

Corrupted Cadrithors lurk in dark places, where shadows grow long and the influence of evil seems palpable. These spectral predators always hunt in groups of two or more, known as packs, and they are known to chuckle with an otherworldly, animalistic glee when the tide of battle suits their favor. Corrupted Cadrithors are undead creatures beholden to the unnatural corruptions of the Abyss; while Dusk Hounds consume the life force of living creatures, they do not need it to survive.

Lore

Not much is known about Corrupted Cadrithors in Ember's modern day, although sages speculate that true Cadrithors originated as celestial beasts of service for the ancient Shent; and evidently, the Abyssal force responsible for their corruption them has warped them resolutely. As the malevolent influence of the Abyss continues to seep into the world from beyond the Weave, these Dusk Hounds have begun to find their way into all corners of the Arctus Plateau, summoned from beyond the limits of physical space by conjurers with evil intents and long-dormant Abyssal artifacts.
Corrupted Cadrithor.biographypublic: Colloquially known as a Dusk Hound, the Corrupted Cadrithor is a vicious spectral predator made of pure shadow. These loathsome, four-eyed creatures bear resemblance to a decayed canine with wicked horns, wreathed in a terrible shroud of black flame.
Corrupted Cadrithor.biographyappearance: You behold a quadruped creature made of pure shadow. The curves of its tenebrous form unmistakably resemble the grotesque skeleton of some vaguely canine monstrosity, shrouded in a black and purple cloak of abyssal fire. It's cruel eyes shine with a ghostly radiance, and its otherworldly growl reeks of grave nitre.

Crumbling Skallith.name: Crumbling Skallith

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.descriptionpublic: The shortsword is a straight-bladed weapon which is nimble to wield and quick to strike in close combat. It features a crossguard ideal for parrying incoming blows.

Shortbow.name: Shortbow
Shortbow.descriptionpublic: Compact and quick to draw, the shortbow excels in rapid, close-quarters archery and skirmishes, favored by scouts, hunters, and swift-footed raiders.

Restless Dead.name: Restless Dead
Restless Dead.description:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature}'s life is sustained by necromantic magic or otherworldly forces. When it would be considered @Condition[dead] it is instead @Condition[incapacitated].

After the conclusion of combat, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} may begin to perform the Recover action, regaining consciousness after the recovery is complete. Recovery in this fashion may be prevented in one of the following ways:

  • The creature was incapacitated by a type of damage for which it is Vulnerable.

  • The magical forces which caused it to rise as undead are disrupted, countered, or otherwise dispelled.

  • The creature's body is destroyed to a degree that it can no longer maintain its physical form.

Rotten Ring Mail.name: Rotten Ring Mail
Rotten Ring Mail.descriptionpublic: Ring mail features metal rings sewn onto a padded base, offering a compromise of less protection than heavier mail options in exchange for greater mobility.

Crumbling Skallith.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

These lesser undead creatures are created by the malevolent unholy magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors} and their greater minions. Any humanoid skeleton is a valid candidate for the dreadful reanimation process that brings them back to life, and @ref[name] are known to take on the broad physical traits of their mortal counterparts — so long as those traits are reflected in the humanoid's skeletal system.

Behavior

@ref[name] are relentless killers, driven first and foremost by the loathsome whims of their evil masters. Armed with ancient weaponry, these skeletal undead maintain a vigilant adherence to whatever orders they're given, which usually involve unslakable attacks upon of the living. Occasionally, errant @ref[name] have been known to exist without the influence of a creator or commander; these rogue @ref[name] persist according to their own wants or needs.

Lore

@ref[name] are reanimated skeletons brought to life by certain unholy influences or esoteric necromancy. They act as servitors and foot soldiers of evil entities, and were first recorded on Ember several hundred years ago, in the wake of the Shattering and the Abyssal scourge that ensued.
Crumbling Skallith.biographypublic: @ref[name] are malevolent undying creatures brought to life by necromancy, created from the skeletal remains of long-dead humanoids. Driven by unholy forces beyond their control, @ref[name] rarely exist of their own accord, and are often encountered as the minions of evil spellcasters and greater undead.
Crumbling Skallith.biographyappearance: You behold the terrifying appearance of a reanimated humanoid skeleton, whose decrepit bones remain dreadfully assembled, despite the lack of sinew and flesh. This loathsome skeletal creature wields a timeworn blade, and a rotted shortbow is slung across its bony back.

Dereth's Notes.name: Dereth's Notes
Dereth's Notes.descriptionpublic: A collection of notes on folded parchment pages, including several drafts of song lyrics, a grocery list from Mrs. Erekos, and a bill of sale from Liestra Grann for the new lute.

Skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
Skirmisher.description: You are adept at entering and exiting the fray. When moving out of the Engagement radius of an enemy, that enemy has 2 Banes to any Disengagement Strike against you.

Raking Talons.name: Raking Talons
Raking Talons.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks rapidly with its talons, dealing multiple raking blows against a single target.
Raking Talons.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks swiftly with both talons.

If at least one attack results in a Critical Success, it inflicts the @Condition[bleeding] condition for 2 Rounds.

Necrotic Bite.name: Necrotic Bite
Necrotic Bite.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} tears into flesh with a maw that is corrupted by pestilence and undeath.
Necrotic Bite.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks with a pestilent bite that is Empowered and deals Corruption damage.

On a Critical Success the attack causes the @Condition[decaying] condition for 3 Turns.

Diversionist.name: Diversionist
Diversionist.description: You specialize in using subterfuge to distract or trick your opponent during combat.
Diversionist.actiondesc: You make a Deception based Skill Attack against the Willpower defense of a target within 30 feet which can see or hear you. On a success, the target loses 1 Focus.

Intimidator.name: Intimidator
Intimidator.description: You specialize in exerting your intimidating presence to break the morale of your foes.
Intimidator.actiondesc: You physically intimidate an enemy that is within your engagement range, performing an Intimidation skill attack against your target. On a success they sustain Void damage to Morale.

Defensive Roll.name: Defensive Roll
Defensive Roll.description: You are a nimble skirmisher, always in movement to stay one step ahead of your enemies in combat.
Defensive Roll.actiondesc: When you Dodge a melee attack you can expend Focus to leap into a defensive roll, moving up to your Size in any direction.

Intuit Weakness.name: Intuit Weakness
Intuit Weakness.description:
You calm your mind and study the physiology of your foe, seeking a vulnerability in its defenses.

Perform a Knowledge Test using an appropriate Skill chosen by the Gamemaster. On a success, you learn the Damage type that the creature has the greatest vulnerability towards, if any. On a Critical Success you learn the two Damage types which have the largest vulnerability.
Intuit Weakness.actiondesc: You still your mind and study the physiology of your foe, attempting to identify a vulnerability in its defenses.

Horrific Critical.name: Horrific Critical
Horrific Critical.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} delivers savage and grotesque blows that evoke fear within any who behold them.
Horrific Critical.actiondesc:
When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} achieves a Critical Hit using a melee attack it may exaggerate the blow in a way that evokes fear within those who behold the strike.

All the enemies within 30 feet who can see the creature face a Harmless attack against their Willpower or become @Condition[frightened] for 3 Turns.

Fetid Claws.name: Fetid Claws
Fetid Claws.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has terrible grasping claws which it uses to rip and tear.

Rune-Marked Knife.name: Rune-Marked Knife
Rune-Marked Knife.descriptionprivate:
Curse. When this item is invested it curses its user.

At the start of each hour, the character faces [[/hazard 6 willpower morale psychic]]{Creeping Confusion}, and if they do not pass the hazard they enter a brief state of delusion as described in @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}.

Additionally, each time the bearer of this curse awakes from a Rest they must face [[/hazard 4 willpower morale severe]]{Lost Dreams}. The third time this hazard deals damage, the GM should reference the article above for additional effect.

Once cursed, this curse may only be removed with a [[/counterspell rune=control gesture=aspect inflection=negate dc=16]].
Rune-Marked Knife.descriptionpublic:
This ancient rune-marked blade is a knife in name only, large enough to serve as a broadsword in medium-sized hands.

Forged long ago by Varùn giants, this ancient rune-marked blade is an arrowhead in name only, large enough to serve as a dagger in medium-sized hands. The light enchantments on this archaic @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{Varùn Artifact} have faded over time, but it retains enough magic for the purposes of overcoming damage immunities and resistances.

When invested, this weapon grants you the ability to mark a target, making it easier to attack.
Rune-Marked Knife.actiondesc: Choose a target, the next attack you make with the @ref[name] against that target has @Advantage[2].

Common Clothing.name: Common Clothing
Common Clothing.descriptionpublic: A shirt, pair of pants, undergarments, socks and shoes or boots suitable for menial labour or travel, cannot be worn with armor.

Dereth Erekos.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Horrendor are lesser undead creatures created by the malevolent eldritch magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors} and their greater minions. Whether decrepit or freshly reanimated, they resemble deceased versions of the people they were in life, with grotesquely distorted features that betray their sinister undead nature — such as pale or sallow skin, unsettling cataract-clouded eyes, protrusive claws of sharpened bone, and terrible mouths full of blood-drenched fangs.

Behavior

Horrendor are unspeakably cruel, and tend to mock their victims with an impossibly personal affectation. They love to strike fear, contempt, and outrage in their opponents; anything that might push their enemies towards emotionally impetuous and dangerous decisions. The ability of a horrendor to wreak mortal havoc is formidable; and to truly destroy one of these reanimated corpses, it must be burned, melted in acid, or ground to a pulp.

Quite often, Horrendor can be motivated from afar by a necromancer or other powerful entity, and will heed the commands of their controller to the most extreme limits of their physical form. They are fallible servants, however, and the control exerted upon them is not absolute; their commanders are less of puppet masters than they are a guiding influence.

Horrendor possess the equipment they carried in life. Roll 1d2 times on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot (Arctus Plateau)} table unless otherwise stated.

Lore

Horrendor are undying reanimated corpses brought to life by certain Abyssal influences or eldritch necromancy (such as the victims of the mysterious curse known as @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}). They act as servitors and foot soldiers of evil entities, and are relatively new to Ember's ecology. Their history is as young as the tall tales that have recently surrounded Skyrbush in the wake of the unseen influence of @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd]{Tethra Shùl}, but the impact of these ghoulish servitors may prove to be long-lasting.
Dereth Erekos.biographypublic: This ghoulish creature was once a young bard named Dereth Erekos before succumbing to a gruesome fate. Now, he persists as a sadistic undead @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendor}, and a twisted mockery of the joyous life he once led. Instead of a musical instrument, the former bard now wields an ancient blade marked with rune and blood.
Dereth Erekos.biographyappearance:
A disheveled corpse of a young man lurks before you, freshly reanimated from the grave. A wicked grin dripping an evil crimson ichor twists its way across the cadaver's pale, deathless face, and the exaggerated brows that frame its milky white eyes betray some kind of cruel intelligent menace.

Dressed in the clothes of an Arcturian commoner, the shambling corpse drags a heavy stone sword behind it with mock lethargy, rotating the tip of the blade in the dirt like some demented child with a new plaything.

You dart forward nimbly, making a strike with sudden and unexpected swiftness to perform a Strike with a Finesse weapon against a single target with an increased range of +2 feet.

Rusted Chain Mail.name: Rusted Chain Mail
Rusted Chain Mail.descriptionpublic: A mesh of interlinked steel rings worn over padding, chain mail provides excellent protection against cuts and decent defense against thrusts, though it distributes weight across the whole body.

Round Shield.name: Round Shield
Round Shield.descriptionpublic: A round metal shield nearly two feet in diameter which is the basic defensive armament of foot soldiers lacking specialized training in shield combat.

Bulwark.name: Bulwark
Bulwark.description:
You have expertise in using a Shield to defend yourself and others.

Once per Turn while you have a Shield equipped, you may use the Defend action at a reduced cost of 1 Action Point.
