Intimidator.actiondesc: You physically intimidate an enemy that is within your engagement range, performing an Intimidation skill attack against your target. On a success they sustain Void damage to Morale.

Armored Efficiency.name: Armored Efficiency
Armored Efficiency.description: You are trained in wearing the heaviest types of armor while still retaining mobility. You are able to use a free Movement action once per Turn while wearing Heavy armor.

Leg Sweep.name: Leg Sweep
Leg Sweep.description: You use a weapon which scales using Strength to sweep your enemy off balance, swinging low to knock them from their feet.
Leg Sweep.actiondesc: You make a Strike attack with your mainhand weapon. This technique is Difficult to execute and deals reduced damage, but if successful renders your target Prone.

Heavy Weapon Training.name: Heavy Weapon Training
Heavy Weapon Training.description: You know how to use a heavy weapon to deliver punishing blows, putting your entire strength behind every swing. You are Trained with all weapons in the Heavy and Balanced categories.
Heavy Weapon Training.actiondesc: You unleash a powerful Strike with your mainhand weapon. The attack is slower to execute, but is Empowered to deliver additional damage.

Skallith Warrior.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

These lesser undead creatures are created by the malevolent unholy magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors} and their greater minions. Any humanoid skeleton is a valid candidate for the dreadful reanimation process that brings them back to life, and @ref[name]s are known to take on the broad physical traits of their mortal counterparts — so long as those traits are reflected in the humanoid's skeletal system.

Behavior

[[lookup @name]]s are relentless killers, driven first and foremost by the loathsome whims of their evil masters. Armed with ancient weaponry and clad in corroded armor, these skeletal undead often lead scores of lesser Skallith into battle. Like lesser Skallith, these skeletal warriors maintain a vigilant adherence to whatever orders they're given, which usually involve unslakable attacks upon of the living. Occasionally, errant @ref[name]s have been known to exist without the influence of a creator or commander; these rogue @ref[name]s persist according to their own wants or needs.

Lore

@ref[name]s are reanimated skeletons brought to life by certain unholy influences or esoteric necromancy. They act as servitors and foot soldiers of evil entities, and were first recorded on Ember several hundred years ago, in the wake of the Shattering and the Abyssal scourge that ensued.
Skallith Warrior.biographypublic: @ref[name]s are undying skeletal creatures brought to life by necromantic magic, and are known to be formidable opponents in battle compared to lesser Skallith. With their superior arms and armor, @ref[name]s make horribly effective shock troops for undead battle companies and their macabre campaigns.
Skallith Warrior.biographyappearance: You behold the terrifying appearance of a reanimated humanoid skeleton, whose decrepit bones remain dreadfully assembled, despite the lack of sinew and flesh. This skeletal warrior is clad in corroded armor, rusted from untold centuries in the grave. A rusty longsword at the creature's side belies its noteworthy strength, and a helmet crowns its cracked and decaying skull.

Sodden Corpse.name: Sodden Corpse

Restless Dead.name: Restless Dead
Restless Dead.description:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature}'s life is sustained by necromantic magic or otherworldly forces. When it would be considered @Condition[dead] it is instead @Condition[incapacitated].

After the conclusion of combat, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} may begin to perform the Recover action, regaining consciousness after the recovery is complete. Recovery in this fashion may be prevented in one of the following ways:

  • The creature was incapacitated by a type of damage for which it is Vulnerable.

  • The magical forces which caused it to rise as undead are disrupted, countered, or otherwise dispelled.

  • The creature's body is destroyed to a degree that it can no longer maintain its physical form.

Powerful Physique.name: Powerful Physique
Powerful Physique.description: You can wield weapons with the Slow trait and wear Armor with the Bulky trait without suffering Banes to your Initiative rolls.

Leg Sweep.name: Leg Sweep
Leg Sweep.description: You use a weapon which scales using Strength to sweep your enemy off balance, swinging low to knock them from their feet.
Leg Sweep.actiondesc: You make a Strike attack with your mainhand weapon. This technique is Difficult to execute and deals reduced damage, but if successful renders your target Prone.

Unarmed Combat Training.name: Unarmed Combat Training
Unarmed Combat Training.description: You are familiar with basic martial arts and hand-to-hand combat. You know how to subdue or restrain opponents using your physical Strength. You are Trained with weapons in the Unarmed category.
Unarmed Combat Training.actiondesc: You attempt to physically restrain or subdue an opponent. Perform a Athletics skill attack against an adjacent target. If successful, both you and your target are @Condition[restrained] for 1 Round.

Mouldering Armor.name: Mouldering Armor
Mouldering Armor.descriptionpublic: Consisting of quilted layers of cloth stuffed with rags or wool, padded armor cushions the body against blunt force and serves as the foundation beneath heavier gear.

Acid Spit.name: Acid Spit
Acid Spit.description: The creature has salivary glands which produce a caustic acid.
Acid Spit.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} spits a glob of acidic bile at a target within 20 feet.

On a Critical Hit, this attack causes the @Condition[corroding] condition for 3 Turns.

Repugnant Pustules.name: Repugnant Pustules
Repugnant Pustules.description: A malodorous cloud hangs about this creature like a pall, the rank noxious scent that can only come from active decay. Striking this creature is likely to release repugnant and corrupting essence.
Repugnant Pustules.actiondesc:
When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} is hit by a Strike, it may partially burst to release a spray of sickening fluid that deals Corruption damage. This action scales with Toughness and targets the Reflex defense of any creature within 3 feet.

On a Critical Success, the affected target becomes temporarily @Condition[diseased] for 3 Rounds.

Thick Skin.name: Thick Skin
Thick Skin.description: Your physical toughness makes you more resistant to harm. You gain +2 Resistance to Bludgeoning, Slashing, and Piercing damage.

Sodden Corpse.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

@ref[name]s resemble the humanoids they were in life, now inundated with the rot and bloat of supernatural putrescence. Their sagging flesh is often covered in pustules, lesions, and boils, and their innards seem barely contained by their blanched and decaying skin.

Behavior

@ref[name]s have no real need for sustenance, but they do behaviorally subsist on a diet of flesh and organ matter culled from living creatures and the freshly-dead. Many clerics and occultists of Ember speculate that a @ref[name]'s innate need to consume stems from a lingering sense of humanity, some aspect of their former life that the corpse hasn’t quite managed to leave behind. Whatever motivates them – be it some supernatural hunger or the whims of a diabolical taskmaster – @ref[name]s are a pox upon the living and pose a noteworthy threat to humanoid survival wherever they may be found.

@ref[name]s are largely known to possess rotted versions of the equipment they had at the precise moment of their death, excluding any weaponry or other items in-hand at the time. However, some @ref[name]s have been seen wielding basic weapons or wearing slipshod armor; on occasion, these decorated specimens also carry loose treasure and other trinkets.

Lore

@ref[name]s were among the first undead to populate Ember following the events of The Shattering, according to many occult and religious texts. In modern times, @ref[name]s are a known element to the varied peoples of the world, and each culture has their own explanation for why these loathsome zombies endure. One thing is for certain: putrid walkers are often sign of a greater source of malevolence that is responsible for their unholy creation.
Sodden Corpse.biographypublic: @ref[name]s are hideous undead creatures born from the carrion of humanoids who’ve been cursed by foul circumstances or bedeviled sorcery. Akin to typical zombies, Sodden Corpses can be identified by the bloat of their rotten and distended flesh, which exudes a toxic stench of decay.
Sodden Corpse.biographyappearance: The fetid smell of corpse rot assaults your senses as a vaguely misshapen humanoid silhouette shambles into view. What appears to be a putrid, ambulatory cadaver shuffles your way, its soft and bloated flesh reeking of the grave. The clothes it wore in life are tattered and torn, stained by the toxic putrescence of its undead form. As the creature’s milky, moldering eyes regard you with a malevolent inhuman hunger, its rotted jaws gnash in rapacious anticipation.

Adelyne Goss.name: Adelyne Goss

Abyssal Sensitivity.name: Abyssal Sensitivity
Abyssal Sensitivity.description:
When [[lookup @name]] takes necrotic damage, she makes a [[/save cha format=long]] with DC equal to either 10 or half the total necrotic damage taken - whichever value is greater.

  • On a success, apply the Abyssal Resistance effect, gaining resistance to necrotic damage until the end of your next long rest.

  • On a failure, apply the Abyssal Susceptibility effect, inflicting vulnerability to necrotic damage until the end of your next long rest. Each time you take additional necrotic damage you may repeat the saving throw, ending this effect immediately on a success.

This check is not repeated while either Abyssal Resistance or Abyssal Sensitivity are active.

Font of Knowledge.name: Font of Knowledge
Font of Knowledge.description: [[lookup @name]] has expertise in History, Arcana, and Religion. Additionally, once every 24 hours, she can grant allies within 30 feet a +2 bonus on any History or Arcana check.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of her character sheet. She automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Fly.name: Fly
Fly.description:
You touch a willing creature. For the duration, the target gains a Fly Speed of 60 feet and can hover. When the spell ends, the target falls if it is still aloft unless it can stop the fall.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 3.

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
This spell repairs a single break or tear in an object you touch, such as a broken chain link, two halves of a broken key, a torn cloak, or a leaking wineskin. As long as the break or tear is no larger than 1 foot in any dimension, you mend it, leaving no trace of the former damage.

This spell can physically repair a magic item, but it can't restore magic to such an object.

Guidance.name: Guidance
Guidance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a skill. Until the spell ends, the creature adds 1d4 to any ability check using the chosen skill.

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Healing Word.name: Healing Word
Healing Word.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains Hit Points equal to 2d4 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 1.

Cure Wounds.name: Cure Wounds
Cure Wounds.description:
A creature you touch regains a number of Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

Arcane Lock.name: Arcane Lock
Arcane Lock.description: You touch a closed door, window, gate, container, or hatch and magically lock it for the duration. This lock can't be unlocked by any nonmagical means. You and any creatures you designate when you cast the spell can open and close the object despite the lock. You can also set a password that, when spoken within 5 feet of the object, unlocks it for 1 minute.

Silence.name: Silence
Silence.description: For the duration, no sound can be created within or pass through a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within range. Any creature or object entirely inside the Sphere has Immunity to Thunder damage, and creatures have the &Reference[deafened apply=false] condition while entirely inside it. Casting a spell that includes a Verbal component is impossible there.

Faerie Fire.name: Faerie Fire
Faerie Fire.description:
Objects in a 20-foot Cube within range are outlined in blue, green, or violet light (your choice). Each creature in the Cube is also outlined if it fails a Dexterity saving throw. For the duration, objects and affected creatures shed &Reference[dimlight] in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the Invisible condition.

Attack rolls against an affected creature or object have Advantage if the attacker can see it.

Invisibility.name: Invisibility
Invisibility.description:
A creature you touch has the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition until the spell ends. The spell ends early immediately after the target makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.

Anachraenum Member.name: Anachraenum Member
Anachraenum Member.description:
You have full access to the Anachraenum's, Amaranthine Archives, training facilities, and equipment. You can spend one hour researching in the restricted section of Archives, allowing you to gain advantage on one Intelligence (History) or Intelligence (Arcana) check you make in the next 24 hours.

In addition, when you are within a dungeon or ruin, you gain +4 on initiative rolls, and you can use the environment to your advantage. If you are surprised, you can make a [[/save format=long]] to act normally as if you were not &Reference[surprise]{surprised}.

Ember Blaze.name: Ember Blaze
Ember Blaze.description: When [[lookup @name]] is reduced to 0 hit points, he rolls a d20. On a 16 or higher, [[lookup @name]] instead drops to 1 hit point, and it can immediately take an action. Until the end of its next turn, his Speed increases by 10 feet, and he has advantage on weapon attack rolls and spell attack rolls.

Adelyne Goss.biographyprivate:
Adelyne has held the position of Loremistress in the Anachraenum for nearly sixty years, and she is a force of nature among the various parties that make up the guild. Many consider her to be on equal footing with the guildmaster and official leader of the Anachraenum, as she performs many administrative duties in addition to overseeing the vast Amaranthine Archives. It's not clear how old she is, as she tends to lie about her age, briskly admonishing and smacking the hands of anyone who asks repeatedly.

Personality

Adelyne’s demeanor is exceptionally confident and demanding despite her physical injuries, hinting at a fierce spirit that continues to drive her pursuits in scholarship and research. She is often unfriendly to outsiders and with people she hasn't met yet, asking a deluge of questions to ascertain thier merits or failings. However, once she gets to know someone, she can be a valuable ally in research and can direct people to hidden treasures among the archives she calls home.

Connections

Adelyne knows everyone, at least to some extent, and could likely formulate secrets and hidden motives for everyone in Ordain. These wouldn’t be based on truth but on her own opinions and reflections drawn from previously studied behaviors. While she may not literally know everyone in Ordain, she can provide obscure information about them nonetheless. She is a close personal friend of Arcos Sarinland, the current guildmaster, and feels genuinely sorry for him; she understands the burdens he carries.

She is also a follower of Sigil and has met the Shard God many times over the years.

Phrases

"You little whipper, how did you get down here! Get out of my Archives!"
Adelyne Goss.biographypublic:
A dour elderly woman sits before you, clad in a mixture of pale blue and green clothing accented by rich brown leather. She appraises you with a deep frown on her face, as if you have already been found wanting in some way. Her long, gray hair cascades in waves over her shoulders and frames a face that bears the scars of time and battle. Deep scars from blade, claw and fire can be seen on her bare, tattooed arms as well.

Loremistress [[lookup @name]] is a sarcastic and sharp scholar, and despite her extensive physical injuries sustained after battling a dragon deep in the Duskflare Jungles many years ago, she remains an intensely insightful and productive researcher and librarian. She is also extremely proud of her Waerd heritage and wears a combination of traditional Waerd clothing interwoven with ancient Sedyri trinkets.

Arcos Sarinland.name: Arcos Sarinland

Inheritors of Chaos.name: Inheritors of Chaos
Inheritors of Chaos.description:
You thrive on unpredictability and you have a penchant for turning a bad situation into an advantageous one.

  • After failing on a Deception, Persuasion, or Intimidation check you may immediately make another check with advantage using a different skill from this list. Be aware that the DC of the second check may change at the Gamemaster's discretion.

  • After rolling a 1 on an Attack Roll, you make your next attack roll against the same target with Advantage.

Keth Bite.name: Keth Bite
Keth Bite.descriptionprivate: You bite with your sharp Keth teeth.

Sudden Bite.name: Sudden Bite
Sudden Bite.description:
You may use a Bonus Action to make an attack with your sharp teeth. This is a special unarmed attack with the finesse property. You have proficiency with this attack which deals 1d6 piercing damage.

If you have levels in the Monk class, the damage of this attack may be improved by the size of your Martial Arts die.

Wayfinder.name: Wayfinder
Wayfinder.description: You can mark a route or point of significance within a 1-mile radius on any map or chart you are carrying. Until the end of your next long rest, you gain advantage on any navigation checks, such as navigating through wilderness, urban areas, or any other area relevant to adventuring. Additionally, allies within 30 feet gain a +1 bonus on their navigation rolls as well.

Anachraenum Member.name: Anachraenum Member
Anachraenum Member.description:
You have full access to the Anachraenum's, Amaranthine Archives, training facilities, and equipment. You can spend one hour researching in the restricted section of Archives, allowing you to gain advantage on one Intelligence (History) or Intelligence (Arcana) check you make in the next 24 hours.

In addition, when you are within a dungeon or ruin, you gain +4 on initiative rolls, and you can use the environment to your advantage. If you are surprised, you can make a [[/save format=long]] to act normally as if you were not &Reference[surprise]{surprised}.

Arcos Sarinland.biographyprivate:
Arcos Sarinland was once a promising young ranger who joined the Anachraenum forty years ago and became a close friend of Darion Bastilla. He was widely celebrated for his participation in the Battle of the Throat, where a combined fleet led by Darion destroyed the Blood Barons' assembling ships in Golden Bay; however, he retired from active adventuring not long after. For thirty years, he taught and guided new members in Ordain, always maintaining a friendly yet troubled demeanor. Recently thrust into the guild's leadership after Fernis Ossa declined the nomination, he faces a number of increasing challenges as Ordain slips further into unrest. He is maintaining the previous Guildmaster legacy with a new Expistion Challenge to further bolster the ranks of the Anachraenum and to bring the people of Ordain together in celebrating new members' successes, but secretly he fears that the challenge may lead to further division.

Personality

Arcos is generally friendly and smiles often, though he carries a hint of fatigue, indicative of the stress he faces in his leadership role. He is deeply afraid of losing control over the various aspects of his responsibilities, from overseeing All-Fable Keep to managing the disparate members spread across the world. Talking with Arcos reveals only small hints of his hidden stresses, but he will keenly, if not curtly, try to steer conversations to a close so that he can address the many issues piling up on his desk.

Connections

While Arcos has taught many of the Anachraenum members throughout the years and has relationships with several seasoned parties, his reputation is one of strict academic perfection, and he is regarded with a certain level of academic respect only. His inability to connect with people generally also means that he has few connections with any powerful heads of organizations or political leaders in the city, and mostly keeps to himself. He does have a close friendship with @UUID[Actor.GA8VFWysoIYfNWCL]{Adelyne Goss}, and the two of them tend to spend long hours together trying to muddle through the various administrative tasks of the organization.

Phrases

"The scars we carry remind us of our past battles, but the Anachraenum is strongest together!"
Arcos Sarinland.biographypublic:
The small figure before you has a rugged and weathered appearance that reflects his years of experience. His once luxurious Keth hair has long since disappeared, leaving a bald head covered in thin old scars. His piercing green eyes hold a mix of wisdom and stress, revealing the weight of his past traumas and current pressures. Many scars can be seen on his forearms and face, and his left hand is missing two fingers, remnants of battles fought and survived. He is clothed in a fur-lined dark purple leather coat and has the air of a professor and practical survivalist all rolled into one.

[[lookup @name]] is the recently appointed Guildmaster of the Anachraenum, a storied yet troubled Keth in his late fifties. He is a deeply learned and wise adventurer who spent his youth traversing many distant and dangerous environments with his friend and comrade Darion Bastilla. However, he retired from active adventuring many years ago to teach at All-Fable Keep. He still bears many scars from his battles in his youth, both physical and mental, and struggles with controlling his own fears and doubts. He did not resist the appointment to Guildmaster by the other Anachraenum members but was nevertheless surprised to find himself in this position, having expected the honor to fall upon the shoulders of the most likable and famous Fernis Ossa.

Fernis Ossa.name: Fernis Ossa

Backpack.name: Backpack
Backpack.description: A backpack can hold one cubic foot or 30 pounds of gear. You can also strap items, such as a bedroll or a coil of rope, to the outside of a backpack.

Crowbar.name: Crowbar
Crowbar.descriptionprivate: Using a crowbar grants advantage to Strength checks where the crowbar's leverage can be applied.

Hammer.name: Hammer
Hammer.descriptionprivate: A tool with a heavy metal head mounted at the end of its handle, used for jobs such as breaking things and driving in nails.

Torch x8.name: Torch x8
Torch x8.description: A torch burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a burning torch and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.

Tinderbox.name: Tinderbox
Tinderbox.descriptionprivate: This small container holds flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a torch - or anything else with abundant, exposed fuel - takes an action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

Waterskin.name: Waterskin
Waterskin.description: A leather hide sewn into an enclosed skin which can contain up to 4 pints of liquid. It weighs 5 pounds when full; a pint of water is approximately 1 pound.

Ink Bottle.name: Ink Bottle
Ink Bottle.descriptionprivate: A small bottle of ink for writing upon parchment.

Ink Pen.name: Ink Pen
Ink Pen.descriptionprivate: A deviced used in combination with ink to write or draw on a sheet of paper.

Silk Rope (50 ft.).name: Silk Rope (50 ft.)
Silk Rope (50 ft.).description: Rope, whether made of hemp or silk, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

Acid (vial).name: Acid (vial)
Acid (vial).description: As an action, you can splash the contents of this vial onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw the vial up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the acid as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 acid damage.

Potion of Healing.name: Potion of Healing
Potion of Healing.description:
The potion's red liquid glimmers when agitated.

You regain 2d4+2 hit points when you drink this potion.

Thermal Vision.name: Thermal Vision
Thermal Vision.description:
You can detect subtle differences in temperature with precision. You can locate creatures which are warm-blooded or otherwise emit heat up to 60 feet away as long as they are not behind total cover and you are not blinded or incapacitated.

This generally includes creatures of the following types: Beast, Celestial, Dragon, Fey, Fiend, Giant, Humanoid, Monstrosity. Certain exceptions may apply where creatures of these types do not emit heat, or creatures of other types do.

A creature detected using Thermal Vision is treated as visible for the purposes of actions which require you to see your target.

Amphibious Adaptability.name: Amphibious Adaptability
Amphibious Adaptability.description: You have a swim speed of 30 feet. You can hold your breath while underwater for up to twenty minutes.

Cyclonic.name: Cyclonic
Cyclonic.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. This weapon is considered magical for the purposes of overcoming damage resistances and immunity.

Whirlwind: As a bonus action, the wielder can spin Cyclonic and perform a melee attack against all creatures within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=Z24lBnBLSrLyRJxI]] feet. Each creature must make a [[/save format=long activity=Z24lBnBLSrLyRJxI]] or take [[/damage average activity=Z24lBnBLSrLyRJxI]] and be pushed back 10 feet. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is not pushed back.

Chain Control: When Cyclonic is thrown, the wielder can use a bonus action to magically recall it to their hand, regardless of its distance. This ability can even be triggered if the sickle is thrown through the air at a target that is out of reach.

Wind Magic: Upon hitting a creature with Cyclonic, the target must make a [[/save format=long activity=R8KUNWNsE5GWqASV]] or be pushed back 15 feet.

Forged in the heart of a storm by an ancient Zeph from the moon of Aura, Cyclonic was once a treasured relic of the Vaznor. [[lookup @name]] uncovered it during a foray into a Skyhold, and it's rumored that it only activates in her hands, granting her mastery over winds and storms in battle.

Amulet of Scoris.name: Amulet of Scoris
Amulet of Scoris.description:
Ability: Intelligence

Utilize: Elemental Resonance (DC 13)

Elemental Resonance: The Amulet grants you the ability to manipulate the environment as an action, creating a 15-foot-radius sphere of swirling elemental energies and motes of magic (fire and water) centered around you. This effect lasts for 1 minute, and while active, difficult terrain caused by either extreme heat or flooding can be traversed without penalty. You can use this ability once per long rest.

Elemental Resilience: While wearing the Amulet, you gain resistance to fire and cold damage.

The Amulet of Scoris was crafted by the ancient Sedyri to honour their creator goddess, Scoris. Fernis Ossa believes that the Amulet was forged during an ancient celestial impact event when the skies rained fire and the oceans surged, symbolizing the powerful union of fire and water.

Wayfinder.name: Wayfinder
Wayfinder.description: You can mark a route or point of significance within a 1-mile radius on any map or chart you are carrying. Until the end of your next long rest, you gain advantage on any navigation checks, such as navigating through wilderness, urban areas, or any other area relevant to adventuring. Additionally, allies within 30 feet gain a +1 bonus on their navigation rolls as well.

Elemental Balance.name: Elemental Balance
Elemental Balance.description:
You possess an innate connection to the elemental forces of fire and water, reflecting the legacy of the ancient Sedyri culture. Once during the next 24 hours, you may choose Fire or Water as your primary element.

Once per short rest, you can tap into your cultural understanding of elements to gain advantage on a Wisdom (Insight) or Intelligence (History) check related to environments, customs, or obstacles associated with your chosen element. For example, if you chose Water, you might gain insight into navigating a flooding area or understanding water-related rituals.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes two attacks with [[/item Cyclonic]] with one action.

Anachraenum Member.name: Anachraenum Member
Anachraenum Member.description:
You have full access to the Anachraenum's, Amaranthine Archives, training facilities, and equipment. You can spend one hour researching in the restricted section of Archives, allowing you to gain advantage on one Intelligence (History) or Intelligence (Arcana) check you make in the next 24 hours.

In addition, when you are within a dungeon or ruin, you gain +4 on initiative rolls, and you can use the environment to your advantage. If you are surprised, you can make a [[/save format=long]] to act normally as if you were not &Reference[surprise]{surprised}.

Veteran Explorer.name: Veteran Explorer
Veteran Explorer.description: [[lookup @name]] has Expertise in the Perception and Survival skills.

Uncanny Dodge.name: Uncanny Dodge
Uncanny Dodge.description:
When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

Foundry Note

With your token selected you can either right click on the damage roll's chat card and select Apply Half Damage or click the "1/2" button and then the Apply button.

Fernis Ossa.biographyprivate:
Fernos Ossa is a forty-one-year-old Ashka Anachraenum adventurer with a keen mind, quick reflexes, and plenty of luck. She is an expert on the ancient civilizations of the Aedir, Vaznor, and the Sedyri, with a very specific and passionate focus on the Sedyri. She is regarded as something of a celebrity in Ordain and is well known for her exploits and her ability to connect with people.

Fernis is not technically Ordani; instead, she grew up in the Ashka settlement of Tajor, which is a diverse mix of cultures from Arcturain, Ordani, and ancient Sedyi traditions. When she was seventeen, she made her way to Ordain with her family's blessing and immediately joined the Anachraenum as a trainee. She spent several years learning how to fight and developed a keen appetite for scholarly research. It was here that she focused her fascination with the Ashka culture of the Sedyri into a lifelong pursuit of knowledge. She tracks down snippets of ancient knowledge to piece together mythological tales and align them with historical facts. In particular, she is driven to discover the lost city of Rejarh, which, if the tales and legends are to be believed, was once a shining Sedyri city that floated upon the oceans of Ember.

One of her first official outings with the Anachraenum saw her visiting the Lumek city of Hearth, shadowing the veteran Wayfinder, @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift}, with a large group of Anachraenum Trainees. However, upon the return journey, their ship was attacked and pulled beneath the waves of the Yaning Sea by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.j9bIMMSCcMeHstz9]{Godkiller Orinoth}. Fernis managed to survive, along with a few other Anachraenum trainees. In the aftermath, they all became fast friends, forming the Skywarders, with Agraband joining the group as well. She served as a skilled Wayfinder within the Anachraenum for many years afterward, leading the Skywarders on many grand adventures. One of the Skywarders' missions involved investigating and studying a forgotten cistern beneath the Waterworks in Ordain itself, and it was here that Fernis discovered incredibly ancient Sedyri ruins. They claimed the area as their home base shortly after, naming it the Concourse Hideout, and transformed it into a spacious living space, complete with many useful additions for an adventuring party.

Five years ago [[/date AS2513]], she became even more famous among the people of Ordain after winning the Anachraenum's first Expedition Challenge with the now veteran Skywarders. Six months later, they successfully explored an ancient Vaznor Skyhold within the distant Shana Mountains. In fact, the enchanted blade that Fernos wields in battle to this day was obtained from the depths of that Skyhold. Although successful in thier mission, the dangers of the Skyhold left their mark on the group, with one of the Skywarders perishing inside its depths and another injured. When they returned to Ordain, they were showered with praise and accolades, but the party disbanded in the weeks that followed.

Fernis then began working directly for the Guildmaster of the Anachraenum, Veron Longspear, and traveling extensively as an emissary. With Fernis and the Skywarders no longer actively living in the Concourse Hideout, the base gradually collected dust until it was taken over by a gang of criminals called the Toothbreakers. One year ago, [[/date AS2522]], Guildmaster of the Anachraenum, Veron Longspear, died unexpectedly while visiting a research site in the Ruinous Crags. The cause of his death was very mysterious, with rumors and theories circulating among the members of the Anachraenum. His successor, Arcos Sarinland, is considered the alternate choice and only ascends to the role of Guildmaster after Fernis Ossa declined the responsibility.

Personality

Fernis Ossa has a vibrant and multifaceted personality that reflects her adventurous spirit and thirst for knowledge, but despite the challenges of her life, she is almost always smiling in some way. She is driven to explore and has a wanderlust that is hard to contain. This curiosity drives her to explore, research, and uncover forgotten ruins, unearth ancient relics, and delve into dangerous dungeons. Additionally, her ability to connect with people makes her a natural leader and a beloved figure among her peers. She effortlessly draws others into her adventures, and her natural charm is born from a deep empathetic ability to connect with people. Having faced challenges and losses throughout her career, Fernis exhibits remarkable strength and determination. She learns and grows from her experiences, allowing her to navigate difficult situations with grace and poise.

Connections

Both within the city of Ordain and across the known world, Fernis has established a network of allies and friends, ranging from ordinary people, historians, and scholars, to leaders of nations. In particular, she has visited the city of Hearth in the Lumek Firelands many times and is said to have a close relationship with the Shard Goddess, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka}. As she is extremely well-traveled and responsible for uncovering many lost secrets throughout her career, her name is well-known, and she can find just the right person to help in any situation. Many willingly assist her in her missions and adventures, without requiring payment.

Most of the members of her party, the Skywarders, have gone their separate ways. Fernis only stays in contact with @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift}, but only briefly when they happen to be in the same area. Of the previous three members, Haptek Korel is missing and presumed dead after traveling to the Koranda Barrens. Mesina Or was last seen in the Tayan Empire, and Rai Jare is the head of the Starshield Commission, amassing resources in the Waerd city of Wick.

Phrases

"Hello there, neighbor!"

"Every ancient ruin tells a story waiting to be uncovered; it’s our duty to listen and learn from the past."

"In every stranger, there’s a potential friend waiting to be discovered!"
Fernis Ossa.biographypublic:
A thin Ashka with scales that range in hue from hunter green to a shade of tea green stands before you. Her expression is a mix of curiosity and open friendliness that gives her a warm, likable demeanor. She wears loose-fitting clothes, reminiscent of an explorer, paired with pouches, leathers, and adventuring accessories. It seems she is dressed lightly enough to suggest a dynamic fighting style based on fast movements; this is reinforced by the strange curved weapon at her side, attached to a long thin chain.

[[lookup @name]] is one of the most well-known and admired Anachraenum members living in Ordain. She led a group of adventurers called the Skywarders many years ago before effectively becoming the envoy and deputy to the previous Guildmaster, Veron Longspear. She has spent many years among the people of Ordain, and her adventurous spirit is matched only by her dedication to her friends and comrades. Fernis often organizes gatherings and events in Ordain and travels to many nearby friendly cities like Luen, Wick, and the Lumek city of Hearth. She has a genuine interest in the stories and lives of the people she meets.

Amelia Naxan.name: Amelia Naxan

Lifeforce Siphon.name: Lifeforce Siphon
Lifeforce Siphon.description: As a Vampyre, [[lookup @name]] does not need to physically suck a mortal's blood to feed, but rather siphon their Lifeforce.

Legendary Resistance.name: Legendary Resistance
Legendary Resistance.description: If [[lookup @name]] fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

Misty Escape.name: Misty Escape
Misty Escape.description:
If [[lookup @name]] drops to 0 Hit Points outside her resting place, [[lookup @name]] uses [[/item Shape-Shift]] to become mist (no action required). If she can't use Shape-Shift, she is destroyed.

While she has 0 Hit Points in mist form, she can't return to her vampyre form, and she must reach her resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed. Once in her resting place, she returns to her vampire form and has the &Reference[Paralyzed apply=false] condition until she regains any Hit Points, and she regains 1 Hit Point after spending 1 hour there.

Spider Climb.name: Spider Climb
Spider Climb.description: [[lookup @name]] can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

Vampyre Weakness.name: Vampyre Weakness
Vampyre Weakness.description:
[[lookup @name]] has these weaknesses:

Lifeforce Sensitivity. [[lookup @name]] is acutely sensitive to Lifeforce energies from the Heart of Ember. When she is within 15 feet of a source of Lifeforce, such as a cleric’s channeling or a druid’s spells that harness nature's vitality, she must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC determined by the caster's spellcasting ability). On a failure, she takes radiant damage equal to twice the level of the spell cast and has disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of her next turn.

Holy Fire Vunerabilty. [[lookup @name]] is not harmed by fire in general, but she does have a unique vulnerability to magical flames that are fueled by pure intent or sacrifice. Any magical fire (like that from a spell or magical weapon) created with the desire to purge evil or protect the innocent deals an additional [[/damage average activity=d7v7gIWq2LYgV07E]] damage to [[lookup @name]]. Additionally, if the fire is cast with a spell of 3rd level or higher, [[lookup @name]] must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be momentarily &Reference[stunned] until the end of her next turn due to the burning purity.

Multiattack (Vampyre Form Only).name: Multiattack (Vampyre Form Only)
Multiattack (Vampyre Form Only).description: [[lookup @name]] makes two [[/item .mUPQwiNiyKhmSf49]]{Grave Strike} attacks and uses [[/item .GrveONDtU4WL5tBq]]{Bite}.

Grave Strike (Vampyre Form Only).name: Grave Strike (Vampyre Form Only)
Grave Strike (Vampyre Form Only).descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the &Reference[Grappled apply=false] condition (escape DC [[lookup @skills.ath.passive]]) from one of two hands.

Bite (Vampyre Form Only).name: Bite (Vampyre Form Only)
Bite (Vampyre Form Only).descriptionprivate:
Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=ngPzlEI5pVSdBv86]], one [[lookup @target.affects.type activity=ngPzlEI5pVSdBv86]] within [[lookup @range.value activity=ngPzlEI5pVSdBv86]] feet [[lookup @target.affects.special activity=ngPzlEI5pVSdBv86]].

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage. The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and [[lookup @name]] regains Hit Points equal to that amount. A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage and then buried rises the following sunset as a @UUID[Actor.j3B9TkGTc23Q6Ina]{Vampyre Spawn} under [[lookup @name]]'s control.

Charm.name: Charm
Charm.description: [[lookup @name]] casts [[/item .xecQm6abQI3Bp7XV]]{Charm Person} requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC [[lookup @abilities.cha.dc]]), and the duration is [[lookup @duration.value activity=fcRXSTOlFJShCl52]] hours. The &Reference[Charmed apply=false] target is a willing recipient of [[lookup @name]]'s [[/item .GrveONDtU4WL5tBq]]{Bite}, the damage of which doesn't end the spell. When the spell ends, the target is unaware it was Charmed by [[lookup @name]].

Charm Person.name: Charm Person
Charm Person.description:
One Humanoid you can see within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. It does so with Advantage if you or your allies are fighting it. On a failed save, the target has the &Reference[charmed apply=false] condition until the spell ends or until you or your allies damage it. The Charmed creature is Friendly to you. When the spell ends, the target knows it was Charmed by you.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Shape-Shift.name: Shape-Shift
Shape-Shift.description:
If [[lookup @name]] isn't in sunlight or running water, she shape-shifts into a Tiny @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmBat00000000000]{bat} (Speed 5 ft., Fly Speed 30 ft.) or a Medium cloud of mist (Speed 5 ft., Fly Speed 20 ft. [hover]), or she returns to her vampyre form. Anything she is wearing transforms with her.

While in bat form, [[lookup @name]] can't speak. Her game statistics, other than her size and Speed, are unchanged.

While in mist form, [[lookup @name]] can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. She is weightless and can enter an enemy's space and stop there. If air can pass through a space, the mist can do so, but it can't pass through liquid. It has Resistance to all damage, except the damage it takes from sunlight.

Beguile.name: Beguile
Beguile.description: [[lookup @name]] casts [[/item .ffmdbUBsKjZvv91U]]{Command}, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC [[lookup @abilities.cha.dc]]). [[lookup @name]] can't take this action again until the start of her next turn.

Command.name: Command
Command.description:
You speak a one-word command to a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or follow the command on its next turn. Choose the command from these options:

Approach. The target moves toward you by the shortest and most direct route, ending its turn if it moves within 5 feet of you.

Drop. The target drops whatever it is holding and then ends its turn.

Flee. The target spends its turn moving away from you by the fastest available means.

Grovel. The target has the Prone condition and then ends its turn.

Halt. On its turn, the target doesn't move and takes no action or Bonus Action.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can affect one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Deathless Strike.name: Deathless Strike
Deathless Strike.description: [[lookup @name]] moves up to half her Speed, and she makes one [[/item .mUPQwiNiyKhmSf49]]{Grave Strike} attack.

Lady Amelia Naxan is one of the infamous Moiran @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Blood Barons}. Additional details about this loathsome matriarch will become available as the campaign continues to develop.

Personality

Amelia Naxan.biographypublic:
Despite the dark cloak that enshrouds her, it's easy to tell that this mysterious woman is remarkably beautiful — her skin, the color of porcelain stained with essence of lavender; her hair, a waterfall of sleek obsidian locks. You regard a cruelty beneath her seductive smile, and a malevolence behind her inquisitive crimson eyes. Clad in stygian robes, the alluring woman moves with uncanny grace and inhuman precision — like a predator among so much prey.

Lady [[lookup @name]] is one of the infamous Moiran Blood Barons, insidious necromancers who rule their kingdom of undead servitors with ferocious cruelty and sensational cunning. She is as deadly as she is beautiful, and is known for her duplicitous nature and exceptional viciousness, even among the Blood Barons themselves.

Jon Vastil.name: Jon Vastil

Quarterstaff.name: Quarterstaff
Quarterstaff.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

Healer's Kit.name: Healer's Kit
Healer's Kit.description: A Healer's Kit has ten uses. As a Utilize action, you can expend one of its uses to stabilize an Unconscious creature that has 0 Hit Points without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes three attacks, using [[/item .5rHCbsklSKAB7A9u]] or [[/item .4GsPaTNwr7CUkPey]] in any combination.

Starry Wisp.name: Starry Wisp
Starry Wisp.description:
You launch a mote of light at one creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 Radiant damage, and until the end of your next turn, it emits Dim Light in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the &Reference[Invisible] condition.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description:
Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range.

Weather Sensor. You create a Tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.

Bloom. You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.

Sensory Effect. You create a harmless sensory effect, such as falling leaves, spectral dancing fairies, a gentle breeze, the sound of an animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot Cube.

Fire Play. You light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a campfire.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Resistance.name: Resistance
Resistance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a damage type: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Radiant, Slashing, or Thunder. When the creature takes damage of the chosen type before the spell ends, the creature reduces the total damage taken by 1d4. A creature can benefit from this spell only once per turn.

Gentle Repose.name: Gentle Repose
Gentle Repose.description:
You touch a corpse or other remains. For the duration, the target is protected from decay and can't become Undead.

The spell also effectively extends the time limit on raising the target from the dead, since days spent under the influence of this spell don't count against the time limit of spells such as Raise Dead.

Lesser Restoration.name: Lesser Restoration
Lesser Restoration.description: You touch a creature and end one condition on it: &Reference[blinded], &Reference[deafened], &Reference[paralyzed], or &Reference[poisoned].

Aura of Life.name: Aura of Life
Aura of Life.description: An aura radiates from you in a 30-foot Emanation for the duration. While in the aura, you and your allies have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and your Hit Point maximums can't be reduced. If an ally with 0 Hit Points starts its turn in the aura, that ally regains 1 Hit Point.

Mass Cure Wounds.name: Mass Cure Wounds
Mass Cure Wounds.description:
A wave of healing energy washes out from a point you can see within range. Choose up to six creatures in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point. Each target regains Hit Points equal to 5d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 5.

Cure Wounds.name: Cure Wounds
Cure Wounds.description:
A creature you touch regains a number of Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

Detect Poison and Disease.name: Detect Poison and Disease
Detect Poison and Disease.description:
For the duration, you sense the location of poisons, poisonous or venomous creatures, and magical contagions within 30 feet of yourself. You sense the kind of poison, creature, or contagion in each case.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Purify Food and Drink.name: Purify Food and Drink
Purify Food and Drink.description: You remove poison and rot from nonmagical food and drink in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range.

Protection from Poison.name: Protection from Poison
Protection from Poison.description: You touch a creature and end the &Reference[poisoned] condition on it. For the duration, the target has Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition, and it has Resistance to Poison damage.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a 9th level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of his character sheet. He automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Healing Word.name: Healing Word
Healing Word.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains Hit Points equal to 2d4 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 1.

Spirit Guardians.name: Spirit Guardians
Spirit Guardians.description:
Protective spirits flit around you in a 15-foot Emanation for the duration. If you are good or neutral, their spectral form appears angelic or fey (your choice). If you are evil, they appear fiendish.

When you cast this spell, you can designate creatures to be unaffected by it. Any other creature's Speed is halved in the Emanation, and whenever the Emanation enters a creature's space and whenever a creature enters the Emanation or ends its turn there, the creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 3d8 Radiant damage (if you are good or neutral) or 3d8 Necrotic damage (if you are evil). On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3.

Dispel Magic.name: Dispel Magic
Dispel Magic.description:
Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range. Any ongoing spell of level 3 or lower on the target ends. For each ongoing spell of level 4 or higher on the target, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 plus that spell's level). On a successful check, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You automatically end a spell on the target if the spell's level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you use.

Death Ward.name: Death Ward
Death Ward.description:
You touch a creature and grant it a measure of protection from death. The first time the target would drop to 0 Hit Points before the spell ends, the target instead drops to 1 Hit Point, and the spell ends.

If the spell is still in effect when the target is subjected to an effect that would kill it instantly without dealing damage, that effect is negated against the target, and the spell ends.

Protection from Energy.name: Protection from Energy
Protection from Energy.description: For the duration, the willing creature you touch has Resistance to one damage type of your choice: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

Flaming Sphere.name: Flaming Sphere
Flaming Sphere.description:
You create a 5-foot-diameter sphere of fire in an unoccupied space on the ground within range. It lasts for the duration. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of the sphere makes a [[/save ability=dex dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] saving throw, taking 2d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

As a Bonus Action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet, rolling it along the ground. If you move the sphere into a creature's space, that creature makes the save against the sphere, and the sphere stops moving for the turn.

When you move the sphere, you can direct it over barriers up to 5 feet tall and jump it across pits up to 10 feet wide. Flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried start burning if touched by the sphere, and it sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 2.

Shillelagh.name: Shillelagh
Shillelagh.description:
A Club or Quarterstaff you are holding is imbued with nature's power. For the duration, you can use your spellcasting ability instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of melee attacks using that weapon, and the weapon's damage die becomes a d8. If the attack deals damage, it can be Force damage or the weapon's normal damage type (your choice).

The spell ends early if you cast it again or if you let go of the weapon.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage die changes when you reach levels 5 (d10), 11 (d12), and 17 (2d6).

Jon Vastil.biographyprivate:
[[emberCharacterDetails]]

Jon Vastil was born in Ordain in 2,416 AS, around 107 years ago, in the Coinwealth Heights district of the city. He was originally a member of House Bastilla during his youth, and it wasn’t until his early twenties that he joined the Cindaric Sages as an initiate, rejecting the pursuit of wealth for a spiritual journey instead. Rumors swirl that his decision was based on a life-changing experience while crossing the Yawning Sea that made him change direction in life. Once he had joined the Cindaric Sages, however, he became increasingly popular among other sages for his impassioned and almost fanatical belief in the Heart of Ember. His pursuit of meditation, connection, and spiritual enlightenment with the world. In 2,448 AS, at only 32 years of age, he was perfectly positioned to take on the role of Holy Speaker after the previous Speaker went missing in mysterious circumstances in the Shard Caverns.

Personality

Jon exudes a quiet strength despite his increasingly dire illness, radiating an air of calm that encourages those around him to share their burdens. He listens intently, his sunken eyes betraying a depth of empathy that allows others to feel truly heard. However, this gentle exterior hides an iron will; when he believes in something, he is unwavering, fiercely defending his ideals with the conviction of a seasoned sage. At times, his stubbornness surfaces, leading him to reject offers of assistance that could alleviate his burdens. He tends to internalize his struggles, choosing to maintain an air of stoicism, which can alienate those who wish to help. He often brushes off his own well-being in favor of the duty he feels toward others, believing his wisdom is his most valuable asset.

Connections

As the Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages, Jon Vastil has connections with powers across the known world. Not only does he have relationships with numerous heads of state and organizations, but he also has long-standing agreements with various Shard Gods, such as Katua, Vekalla, and Raineka, and maintains diplomatic ties with Lumé from the Lumek. This gives him unprecedented reach, but he rarely requires or considers asking for aid with any problems. With his illness becoming worse and worse, however, he has begrudgingly begun to rely on Vinarith and Lilla Arien to take over much of his workload, and after learning of the appearance of Undead in the Arctus Plateau region, he secretly reached out to Lumé and requested that she send someone to investigate.

Phrases

I will soon join the Heart of Ember, and only then will my true journey begin.
Jon Vastil.biographypublic:
The Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages appears fragile and haggard, burdened by the weight of countless years. His skin has a parchment-like texture, stretched tight over protruding bones. Deep lines etch across his forehead, and his once-bright eyes are now dulled and sunken. A persistent cough punctuates his speech, each raspy breath a reminder of his frailty. He walks with a slow, deliberate gait, leaning heavily on a gnarled cane. The air around him is thick with the faint scent of herbs and potions, remnants of remedies that provide little solace against the illness that appears to be wracking his body.

[[lookup @name]] is the Holy Speaker of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, an ancient Human who has guided the order for nearly 75 years. While his leadership has been commendable, he has faced growing criticism in recent years for a perceived lack of compassion towards the people and their growing problems and issues, instead focusing on spiritual connections with the Heart of Ember. He has been battling an illness for several years without a known cause or cure, leading many to believe he may soon depart from the mortal realm.

Vinarith.name: Vinarith

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Rune: Life.name: Rune: Life
Rune: Life.description:
A chaotic force of creation, responsible for living matter. The Life rune governs health and matters relating to biological growth.

The Life rune scales using Wisdom and provides Restoration of Health or inflicts Poison damage opposed by Fortitude. It is opposed by the orderly rune of Death.
Rune: Life.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Life allows you to stimulate biological growth and nourish physical health, producing one of the following effects:

  • Cultivate 1 cubic foot of existing plants or fungus to rapidly grow to a healthy, blossoming, or harvestable state.

  • Identify a negative physical condition that is affecting a creature such as @Condition[diseased], @Condition[poisoned], @Condition[bleeding], or @Condition[weakened].

  • Verify whether a portion of food or drink is free of contamination from bacteria, parasites, or poison.

Bloom may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Rune: Soul.name: Rune: Soul
Rune: Soul.description:
An orderly force of creation and spiritual essence. The Soul rune governs the fundamental procession of souls through life and death and relates to matters of sapience, personality, and mental health.

The Soul rune scales using Presence and provides Restoration of Morale or inflicts Psychic damage opposed by Willpower. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Oblivion.
Rune: Soul.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Soul allows you to facilitate basic forms of spiritual influence, producing one of the following effects:

  • Enable yourself or another willing person to revisit a core memory of a moment from their past up to one minute in duration as if it happened recently.

  • Identify a negative spiritual condition that is affecting a person such as @Condition[broken], @Condition[frightened], @Condition[confused], or @Condition[insane].

  • Create a momentary spiritual connection with another willing creature that allows them to recognize an idea which can be expressed as a single word.

Uses of Evoke may only affect yourself or another creature which you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Gesture: Influence.name: Gesture: Influence
Gesture: Influence.description:
You intensify the arcane power of a Rune into a concentrated direct contact which is generally a more powerful evolution of the basic Touch gesture.

The Influence gesture scales using Presence and targets a single adjacent creature. It deals 10 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus.

Gesture: Sense.name: Gesture: Sense
Gesture: Sense.description:
You attune your mind to the arcane power of a Rune to sense nearby sources of energy.

The Sense gesture scales with Presence and produces an emanation with 30 feet radius and position that remains centered upon the spellcaster. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus. It may optionally be Maintained at the additional cost of 1 Focus every subsequent round.

This spell allows the caster to detect the presence of spellcraft using the same Rune as the one incorporated in this spell. The sense will also momentarily detect the presence of creatures according to their type.

  • Control: Fiends

  • Death: Undead

  • Earth: Oozes and Earth Elementals

  • Flame: Dragons and Fire Elementals

  • Frost: Giants and Frost Elementals

  • Illumination: Celestials

  • Illusion: Fey

  • Kinesis: Monstrosities

  • Life: Plants and Beasts

  • Lightning: Constructs and Storm Elementals

  • Oblivion: Outsiders

  • Soul: Humanoids

Playtest Notes

There is no automation for the sense that is temporarily granted by this spell, but such automation can be provided in the future via a Detection Mode which temporarily reveals creatures of the appropriate type to the spellcaster while the spell is maintained.

Gesture: Surge.name: Gesture: Surge
Gesture: Surge.description:
You channel the arcane power of a Rune into a rushing wave of energy that surges forward from your current position.

The Surge gesture scales with Wisdom and produces a line that is 10 feet wide and 15 feet long originating from the spellcaster, dealing 8 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. The gesture requires 2 Hands to cast and has a base cost of 5 Action and 2 Focus.

Playtest Notes

This talent is currently placed at a Tier 4 node. It will eventually only be attainable at a higher level (probably Level 6 required). It is currently available "early" for testing.

Gesture: Aura.name: Gesture: Aura
Gesture: Aura.description:
You concentrate the arcane power of a Rune to create a maintained field of energy that washes over allies and enemies near to you.

The Aura gesture scales with Presence and produces an emanation with 20 feet radius centered on the spellcaster. The center of this Aura moves with the spellcaster.

Depending on the Rune used, the Aura deals damage or provides healing to any creature which begins its turn inside the Aura. This gesture requires 2 Hands to cast, has a base cost of 5 Action and 1 Focus, and must be Maintained costing an additional 1 Focus every subsequent round.

Playtest Notes

This talent is currently placed at a Tier 4 node. It will eventually only be attainable at a higher level (probably Level 6 required). It is currently available "early" for testing.

Emanation templates which are linked to the Token and move when the Token moves are a feature coming in Foundry VTT version 14. Automation of the Aura gesture will occur once Crucible depends on Foundry VTT version 14.

Rune: Earth.name: Rune: Earth
Rune: Earth.description:
The orderly force of elemental earth, responsible for physical matter. The Earth rune governs minerals, metals, soils, and other physical compounds.

The Earth rune scales using Wisdom, targets Reflex, and deals Acid damage to Health. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Lightning.
Rune: Earth.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Earth allows you to manipulate raw forces of rock, mineral, and soil in basic ways, producing one of the following effects:

  • Quickly shape up to one cubic foot of available material into a simple geometric form like a cuboid, ellipsoid, or polyhedron.

  • Precisely copy the physical shape of a held object that is smaller than a 6-inch cube, reproducing it from available clay, stone, or metal. The replica retains no useful properties except for its physical form.

  • Separate and collect earthen particles from the surface of an object, creature, or liquid that you touch, rendering the subject completely cleaned or purified in moments.

Mould may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Rune: Frost.name: Rune: Frost
Rune: Frost.description:
The orderly force of water and cold. The Frost rune governs the creation of water or other fluids and their transfer between liquid and frozen states.

The Frost rune scales using Wisdom, targets Fortitude, and deals Cold damage to Health. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Flame.
Rune: Frost.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Frost allows you to manipulate liquids and their thermal properties, producing one of the following effects:

  • Draw up to one quarter gallon of fresh water from the atmosphere into a container or upon a surface you touch. The created water may be affected by relevant atmospheric properties of your current location.

  • Manipulate the temperature of up to 1 gallon of water, causing it to immediately freeze or thaw. The water need not be in a container; this technique can be used to coat a surface or join two objects together via regelation. Ice created in this way remains frozen for as long as the ambient temperature of the environment allows.

  • Gather up to a six-foot cube of nearby snow, forming it into a solidified sculpture, shape, or shelter.

Condense may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Talisman Weapon Training.name: Talisman Weapon Training
Talisman Weapon Training.description: You understand the arcane usage of talismans, orbs, foci, or other similar implements to channel magic or empower spellcraft. You are Trained with weapons in the Talisman categories.
Talisman Weapon Training.actiondesc:
You use your equipped Talisman to attempt to regain some Focus. You perform a Harmless Strike against your own Rallying threshold.

On a success you recover +1 Focus if using a one-handed Talisman and +2 Focus if using a two-handed Talisman. On a critical success the amount of Focus recovered increases by an additional +1.

Talisman Weapon Proficiency.name: Talisman Weapon Proficiency
Talisman Weapon Proficiency.description: You have a fluent education in the use of talismans, orbs, foci, or other similar weapons. You gain the Journeyman training rank and a +1 Skill Bonus with weapons in the Talisman category.

Soothe.name: Soothe
Soothe.description: You administer a soothing Performance which rallies your allies, restoring Morale.
Soothe.actiondesc: You perform a calming verse, benefiting all allies who can perceive you within 12 feet. Make a Performance Check against the Madness threshold of each ally. On success, each ally's Morale is restored.

Conserve Effort.name: Conserve Effort
Conserve Effort.description: You find calmness and focus in conserving your effort in battle. When you end your Turn with un-spent Action you gain +1 Focus.

Inflection: Compose.name: Inflection: Compose
Inflection: Compose.description: Enhance a spell by taking extra time in its formation, reducing other resource costs in exchange. The Compose inflection reduces the Focus cost of a spell by 1 while increasing its Action cost by 1 in exchange.

Rune: Control.name: Rune: Control
Rune: Control.description:
The orderly force of discipline and permanence. The Control rune governs thought, reason, and persistence.

The Control rune scales using Intellect, targets Willpower, and deals Psychic damage to Morale. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Kinesis.
Rune: Control.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Control allows you to affect the decision making of others in basic ways, producing one of the following effects:

  • Moderately intensify or dampen the primary emotion being felt by a creature you touch. If the creature is intelligent enough to be aware of the laws governing spellcraft, they are aware of your actions.

  • Understand the abstract motivations of another living creature which allows you to touch it. You are able to intuit their immediate goals expressed in the form of a single verb.

  • Intensely focus on your current objective and the means of achieving it. You receive a brief hint or reminder from the Gamemaster about that objective containing only information which you have previously learned.

Motivate may only affect a creature or object which you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Inflection: Extend.name: Inflection: Extend
Inflection: Extend.description:
Enhance the duration of a spell, increasing the duration of its effect. For spells which are instantaneous, any corresponding status conditions that they cause are increased in duration.

Effect duration increases from the Extend inflection are not yet automated in Playtest 1. This inflection is included as an example of the intended direction for the Spellcraft system.

Inflection: Push.name: Inflection: Push
Inflection: Push.description: Empower a spell to repel affected creatures away from the caster. Creatures affected by a spell with the Push inflection move 4 feet away from the spellcaster if that destination is unoccupied.

Sage's Staff.name: Sage's Staff
Sage's Staff.descriptionpublic: The iconic staff of a Cindaric Sage, which serves as a talisman which provides additional defensive capabilities.

Padded Armor.name: Padded Armor
Padded Armor.descriptionpublic: Consisting of quilted layers of cloth stuffed with rags or wool, padded armor cushions the body against blunt force and serves as the foundation beneath heavier gear.

Periapt of Determination.name: Periapt of Determination
Periapt of Determination.descriptionprivate: This item is presented as an amulet, but it can be any type of accessory like a ring, cloak, bracers, or other type of trinket.
Periapt of Determination.descriptionpublic:
A graceful silver amulet embedded with blue jewels imbues you with a feeling of steadfastness while you clutch it, prepared to weather any challenge.

This amulet provides a bonus to Willpower defense equal to the minimum of its Quality and Enchantment bonuses.

  • Fine quality and Minor enchantment: +1 Willpower

  • Superior quality and Major enchantment: +2 Willpower

  • Masterwork quality and Legendary enchantment: +3 Willpower

Rallying Elixir.name: Rallying Elixir
Rallying Elixir.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to rapidly fortify the psyche and improve morale.
Rallying Elixir.actiondesc:
Immediately recover an amount of Morale dependant on the quality of the elixir.

  • Shoddy - Immediately heals 6 Morale.

  • Standard - Immediately heals 12 Morale.

  • Fine - Immediately heals 24 Morale.

  • Superior - Immediately heals 48 Morale.

  • Masterwork - Immediately heals 96 Morale.

Healing Elixir.name: Healing Elixir
Healing Elixir.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to rapidly close wounds and improve bodily health.
Healing Elixir.actiondesc:
Immediately recover an amount of Health dependant on the quality of the elixir.

  • Shoddy - Immediately heals 6 Health.

  • Standard - Immediately heals 12 Health.

  • Fine - Immediately heals 24 Health.

  • Superior - Immediately heals 48 Health.

  • Masterwork - Immediately heals 96 Health.

Lantern.name: Lantern
Lantern.descriptionpublic: An oil-burning or magically illuminated lantern that sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius.

Vinarith.biographyprivate:
[[emberCharacterDetails]]

False Appearances

Note: This character is in truth a persona of the dragon @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss}. They have been masquerading as a Human in Ordain for nearly 25 years, having murdered the real Vinarith in 2498 AS. Everything apart from the early history of this character should therefore be considered part of Zerranyss's carefully constructed facade.

Under no circumstances should this information be revealed to the party, and no amount of insight checks, successful magical spell casting, or any other attempts to read this character will reveal who they truly are, as it is a pivotal aspect of the main story.

For decades, Vinarith Jurman has devoted himself to the Cindaric Order, climbing the ranks through dedication and selfless sacrifice. Having been born and raised in the Smokerie district of Ordain, he always viewed the Cindaric Sages and the distant temple on the horizon as a sacred calling to help his fellow Ordani. Since joining the order in his teenage years, he has held numerous positions across the city, serving in and out of the main Temple in Ordain, spending seven years in the Lumek Homelands aiding their cause against the undead, and he has never once faltered in his duties. By the time he ascended to the position of Steward to the Speaker, he was renowned for his unwavering service to the faith.

Many Sages consider him to be the natural successor to the ailing Jon Vastil and the next in line to inherit the title of Holy Speaker. His firm and uncompromising attitude towards recent events has helped many feel more secure as recent turmoils have engulfed the city.

When the Holy Speaker, Jon Vastil, fell ill, Vinarith was required to take over many critical duties, and the difficult role of stewardship was made even harder during a time when many in the city feel the Sages should be doing far more to confront the growing chaos in the region. He often clashes with another popular figure among the order, Lilla Arien, who advocates for calm, measured, and thoughtful responses focused on helping the people. While Vinarith believes in confronting chaos head-on by sending Sages out among the people to inspire them to stand strong, and a resurgent Burnished Hand to maintain order and peace.

Personality

Vinarith embodies a stern, unyielding leader, possessing an aura of resolute confidence that personifies the idealized image of a Sage who takes direct action. With his significant responsibilities, he still takes the time to speak with people in the city and often listens to their concerns personally with a warm smile, inspiring words, and speeches. He is deeply devoted to the principles of the Cindaric faith and fiercely believes that the Sages are a force for good in Ordain and can help shape the people and governance of the city into a brighter future.

His faithfulness and compassion for others mark him as a beloved figure among many in Ordain, with numerous unpopular decisions that the Sages seem to have enacted in recent years being blamed on the ancient and aloof Jon Vastil.

Connections

As the steward of the Holy Speaker, Vinarith is extremely well-connected throughout the Cindaric Order, having taught many initiates personally in the past and interacting with nearly every Sage in the Cindaric Temple on a weekly basis. He maintains broad connections with religious and community leaders throughout the city, including the High Priests of the larger temples, and many rely on his wisdom and guidance, particularly during the Speaker's absence. He has almost complete sway and influence over the Sages' council members, who sit on the Ordanite as well.

With the illness of the Holy Speaker, Vinarith is seen by many as the Speaker in waiting, though he treads as lightly as he can in this case, knowing that he does not have true authority. He must also contend with the Keeper of the Cindaric Sages, Lilla Arien, who has many supporters in the order and is often trying to place the brakes on his bold efforts to steer the Sages towards more direct involvement in Ordain's problems.

Phrases

Our faith shines brightest when nourished by kindness, compassion, and confidence in our convictions.

In service to others, we find the true strength of our convictions.
Vinarith.biographypublic:
A tall, middle-aged male human with gray-bronzed skin and a strong, muscular figure reveals a distant Kivahr ancestry.
