His once-rich brown hair is greying at the roots, and he has a variety of middle-aged wrinkles and lines across his face, especially around his eyes. Vinarith is a charismatic, firm, and, at first glance, serious figure. His angular, stern features are often softened by a kind smile, and his bright golden eyes hold a warmth that is instantly reassuring. Despite his impressive stature and imposing bearing from afar, he exudes a kindly and reassuring air. Unlike other Sages, he is clad in a practical tunic and trousers with a short cloak embossed with Cindaric symbols.

[[lookup @name]] is the Steward of the Holy Speaker within the Cindaric order, the right hand to the highest office of the Cindaric Sages. With the Holy Speaker having fallen ill, he now shoulders many responsibilities of leadership alongside Keeper @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien}.

Hephiss Wandren.name: Hephiss Wandren

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: Hephiss Wandren makes one [[/item Dagger]] attack and one [[/item Radiant Dagger]] attack.

Radiant Dagger.name: Radiant Dagger
Radiant Dagger.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. On a hit, the target is subjected to the following effect.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=VHStJ3hZGwHAHcUQ]].

Failure: [[/damage average activity=VHStJ3hZGwHAHcUQ]] damage and is &Reference[Blinded apply=false] for 1 minute.

Success: Half damage.

You can take a Bonus Action to charge the blade with radiant energy. The blade remains charged for 1 minute, or until an attack using this weapon hits a creature. The weapon can't be charged again until the next dawn.
Radiant Dagger.descriptionpublic: A short metal blade mounted to a small hilt and crossguard.

Chromatic Orb.name: Chromatic Orb
Chromatic Orb.description:
You hurl an orb of energy at a target within range. Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder for the type of orb you create, and then make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 3d8 damage of the chosen type.

If you roll the same number on two or more of the d8s, the orb leaps to a different target of your choice within 30 feet of the target. Make an attack roll against the new target, and make a new damage roll. The orb can't leap again unless you cast the spell with a level 2+ spell slot. [[@item.level]]{Number of leaps}

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1. The orb can leap a maximum number of times equal to the level of the slot expended, and a creature can be targeted only once by each casting of this spell.

Fog Cloud.name: Fog Cloud
Fog Cloud.description:
You create a 20-foot-radius Sphere of fog centered on a point within range. The Sphere is &Reference[heavilyobscured]. It lasts for the duration or until a strong wind (such as one created by @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGustofWind]{Gust of Wind}) disperses it.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The fog's radius increases by 20 feet for each spell slot level above 1.

Grease.name: Grease
Grease.description:
Nonflammable grease covers the ground in a 10-foot square centered on a point within range and turns it into &Reference[difficultterrain] for the duration.

When the grease appears, each creature standing in its area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the &Reference[prone] condition. A creature that enters the area or ends its turn there must also succeed on that save or fall Prone.

Hephiss' Keys.name: Hephiss' Keys
Hephiss' Keys.descriptionprivate: This set of keys, owned by Hephiss Wandren, can be used to open doors that would be otherwise inaccessible, even to thieves, shaping itself to fit the lock as needed. It also serves as a master key for Hephiss' more mundane locks, though these locks can be opened without it.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: Once on each of its turns, when [[lookup @name]] hits a target with a melee weapon attack, the target takes an extra [[/damage average]] if [[lookup @name]] has advantage on the attack roll or if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t incapacitated, and [[lookup @name]] doesn’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.

Hephiss Wandren.biographyprivate:
Hephiss Wandren has been the head of House Wandren for several years, which is longer than most are able to hold onto the position. She gained it by successfully becoming the confidante of both sides of a power struggle within the house that left several dead, then blackmailing the survivors with her knowledge of their crimes to amass wealth and power. Though she would never admit it, she worries that someone might do the same to her and is willing to go to great lengths to hold onto her title and station.

Hephiss' attempts to hold on to power have led her to ally with the celestial Pyix, who she believes will one day elevate her to be the sole leader of Ordain under a new world order.

Personality

Hephiss is deeply determined - she will do whatever she needs to do to reach her goals, which are to reshape House Wandren, and Ordain, to her liking. She believes that the control of information and manipulation of others is the best way to get ahead without putting yourself at risk or danger, and also secretly believes that she is smarter than most and thus cannot be manipulated herself. It bothers her that these traits that she sees as worthy are often looked down on by others, and believes this is because they are either jealous or foolish. She both wants and fears a true rival who will challenge her - while it would help her prove her worth once and for all, she isn't willing to risk the chance she'd lose on an equal playing field.

Connections

As the leader of House Wandren, most of Hephiss' connections are with other members of the house. Her parents were mid-level merchants who relocated from the Lumarian Homelands to Ordain for greater opportunity and raised her to outshine them in every aspect of their success.

She tends to disdain the other Trading Houses and see them as impediments to her ambition and to Ordain's future, as she thinks they are not ready to face any of the unsteadiness or unpleasantness that may be coming for the city, though she finds House Bastilla to be somewhat useful as an ally as needed. Within Wandren, she used blackmail and occasional violence to get ahead, and while members of Wandren do not necessarily like her, they do respect (and definitely fear) her.

Hephiss' association with Pyix has led her to turn on any members of House Wandren who she feels are disloyal to her cause, hollowing the Trading House out from the inside by killing a number of members and cowing the others.

Phrases

Do what you have to.

If you knew what I knew, you would do what I've done.

History rewards the competent, and the conquerors.
Hephiss Wandren.biographypublic:
The fej woman in front of you is dressed in sumptuous apparel and moves with a steady grace, but her eyes are steely and appraising, looking anyone she encounters up and down as if trying to gauge their true worth to her. The lines in her face give the sense that she has made this appraisal of many people, many times, and too often they have come up lacking.

Hephiss Wandren is the leader of House Wandren, one of the major Trading Houses of the Great City of Ordain. She has held onto the position longer than most by moving shrewdly but decisively in pursuit of power. While she does not often flex her power, preferring to seem a bit more above it all, when she does, it can be deadly, and several House Wandren members who have opposed her are now conveniently missing.

Cherish Ellerie.name: Cherish Ellerie

Exceptional Taste.name: Exceptional Taste
Exceptional Taste.description: Your attire is a more powerful a tool in your handling of social situations than any blade or spell. When you are wearing clean clothing instead of armor you may roll and add a 1d4 to any Deception, Persuasion, or Intimidation skill check.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Heroism.name: Heroism
Heroism.description:
A willing creature you touch is imbued with bravery. Until the spell ends, the creature is immune to the Frightened condition and gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your spellcasting ability modifier at the start of each of its turns.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]nd level spellcaster. Their spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of their character sheet. They automatically satisfy the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Message.name: Message
Message.description:
You point toward a creature within range and whisper a message. The target (and only the target) hears the message and can reply in a whisper that only you can hear.

You can cast this spell through solid objects if you are familiar with the target and know it is beyond the barrier. Magical silence; 1 foot of stone, metal, or wood; or a thin sheet of lead blocks the spell.

Healing Word.name: Healing Word
Healing Word.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains Hit Points equal to 2d4 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 1.

Cherish Ellerie.biographyprivate:
Cherish was born and raised in Ordain, grew up in and around House Salva, and developed a love for fashion at a very young age. As soon as she was old enough to pull away from her family's oversight and begin making her own decisions she set off to join the trading house, determined to make a name for herself.

Personality

Cherish is driven to succeed, and always remains focused on whatever her current goal is. This has allowed her to rise up the ranks of Salva quickly, though it has been at the cost of her relationships with family and friends.

Though she's neither cruel or criminal, Cherish is not above making difficult calls and hard decisions when other balk, even if it means someone's going to get hurt in the ensuing fallout. She believes that making progress to your goals takes sacrifice, sometimes your own, sometimes someone else's.

Connections

Cherish's ambition has caused her to rise up the ranks in house Salva quickly, and she now holds a position as a project overseer with several projects under her stewardship. What many don't know is that she also has a direct connection to Mistress Caberi, the head of House Salva itself, who acts as something of a mentor to her.

Phrases

Just because the sun's down doesn't mean the work's done!
Cherish Ellerie.biographypublic:
Covered head to toe in detailed ink, this tattooed Ordani woman is a walking art piece, a living mural of red, black and blue designs crawling across her skin in intricate, interlocking patterns. Like any Ordani, she is dressed in vibrant colors, her frame draped in the finest silk that the city can produce. To compliment her exquisite garb, and marked skin, she is further adorned with golden jewelry that glitters brightly with her every movement.

[[lookup @name]] is an up-and-coming member of House Salva that has already begun to distinguish herself from her peers. Young, ambitious, and driven, she'll do whatever it takes to succeed in the cutthroat world the trading house rules over.

Conaris Haid.name: Conaris Haid

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes four attacks, using [[/item Mace]] or [[/item Radiant Flame]] in any combination.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability:

At Will: [[/item .8ujpCzQz3847cYEo]]{Light} , [[/item .tPcPpB4rCtOWdMA0]]{Thaumaturgy}

1/Day: [[/item .FIwIBHsgjQlPPqR7]]{Spirit Guardians}

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Thaumaturgy.name: Thaumaturgy
Thaumaturgy.description:
You manifest a minor wonder within range. You create one of the effects below within range. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time.

Altered Eyes. You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.

Booming Voice. Your voice booms up to three times as loud as normal for 1 minute. For the duration, you have Advantage on [[/check ability=cha skill=itm]] checks.

Fire Play. You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.

Invisible Hand. You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.

Phantom Sound. You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point of your choice within range, such as a rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous whispers.

Tremors. You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.

Divine Aid.name: Divine Aid
Divine Aid.description: [[lookup @name]] casts [[/item .h81BQ3k18OO2Mp9i]]{Bless}, [[/item .2t5vgMjVxQyJXYCn]]{Dispel Magic}, [[/item .eriqBnwgrHqNLyzO]]{Healing Word}, or [[/item .ZmuOZkw6AM1nyGwG]]{Lesser Restoration}, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Bless.name: Bless
Bless.description:
You bless up to three creatures within range. Whenever a target makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target adds 1d4 to the attack roll or save.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Dispel Magic.name: Dispel Magic
Dispel Magic.description:
Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range. Any ongoing spell of level 3 or lower on the target ends. For each ongoing spell of level 4 or higher on the target, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 plus that spell's level). On a successful check, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You automatically end a spell on the target if the spell's level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you use.

Healing Word.name: Healing Word
Healing Word.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains Hit Points equal to 2d4 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 1.

Lesser Restoration.name: Lesser Restoration
Lesser Restoration.description: You touch a creature and end one condition on it: &Reference[blinded], &Reference[deafened], &Reference[paralyzed], or &Reference[poisoned].

Spirit Guardians.name: Spirit Guardians
Spirit Guardians.description:
Protective spirits flit around you in a 15-foot Emanation for the duration. If you are good or neutral, their spectral form appears angelic or fey (your choice). If you are evil, they appear fiendish.

When you cast this spell, you can designate creatures to be unaffected by it. Any other creature's Speed is halved in the Emanation, and whenever the Emanation enters a creature's space and whenever a creature enters the Emanation or ends its turn there, the creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 3d8 Radiant damage (if you are good or neutral) or 3d8 Necrotic damage (if you are evil). On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3.

Conaris Haid.biographyprivate:
[[lookup @name]] is a brilliant and eccentric 75-year-old philosopher who serves as the High Priest of the Temple of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} in @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}. And though he wears the guise of an affable, absent-minded codger in public, this expertly studied and accomplished cleric is one of the Arctus Plateau’s most trusted sources of information on Ember’s mysterious Soul Cycle. Despite his perpetually bemused and overtly scatterbrained demeanor, Haid is a skilled clergyman whose iron will and keen intellect have earned him the ultimate favor of his chosen deity, Sockets — the Elder God of death and souls. And while many of Ordain’s citizens have a rather narrow view of the aging cleric’s modern efficacy, the positive and lasting impacts of Conaris Haid’s fateful presence in the city come to bear relatively often (and when least expected).

Personality

Conaris often squints his bright blue eyes while talking to someone or observing something, and is known to run his narrow fingers methodically through his beard while lost in contemplation. Conaris purses his lips when he’s thinking, and instinctively smiles whenever someone asks him a question that intrigues him in the slightest. He likes to keep his hands clean, for impromptu handling of ancient texts and other precious artifacts. His vestments, on the other hand, are often dusty and dirty; he is clean but unkempt.

He’s opposed to unnecessary violence. He never goes back on his word. He gets lost in flights of fancy when discussing matters of passion and the heart. He takes Ember’s life and soul cycles very seriously.

Connections

Conaris Haid’s past is a storied one. In his childhood, he toiled as an assistant to his father, a talented Ordani fletcher. During his adolescence, however, Conaris would come to regret his role as an artisan of ballistic weaponry. As family, friends, and loved ones began to pass away, Conaris became more and more interested in Ember’s life cycle, eventually turning to a scholarly life of research and passive academia. One day, while scouring the dusty pages of some ancient religious text, Conaris was visited by an avatar of Sockets; this manifestation of the Elder God sent young Conaris on a quest to vanquish an unholy evil in the Farlands to the south — a mission that would seemingly fracture the young cleric’s mind while fortifying his spirit.

Upon returning to Ordain, Conaris became the first High Priest of the Temple of Sockets. Forever harrowed and enlightened by his experience in the Farlands, Conaris Haid is tasked with aiding the people of Ordain however his patron deity sees fit. The acolytes who serve beneath Conaris typically regard him with the reverence bestowed upon a favorite uncle or surrogate father figure; and the venerable old fool is all-too eager to treat them with an even greater admiration (once they’ve earned it, of course).

His goals: to shepherd lost souls of Ordain (and the Arctus Plateau) to the Bonelands through spiritual guidance and interpretation of the edicts of Sockets, and to one day find an acolyte worthy of his eventual replacement as the High Priest of Sockets.

Phrases

"Upward and onward, as they say!"

“Damnation is no laughing matter. But I'll give it a try!”

"Blame it on Sockets, kid. I just work here."
Conaris Haid.biographypublic:
If his tattered robes are any indication, the short, bald man before you is a priest of high station — an occupation at odds with the somewhat deranged look on his wizened face. This wild-eyed septuagenarian's beard is as chaotic as his crooked grin, which constantly shifts and wrinkles and sputters with every emotion under the sun. Missing one sandal and speaking to himself, the old cleric seems outright mad. At his side, however, a radiant tome bearing the holy symbol of the elder god Sockets seethes with divine energy, and you can't help but think this crazy old fool hides a power beyond measure.

[[lookup @name]] is the absent-minded High Priest of Sockets in Ordain, and is known far and wide for his unpredictable, often cantankerous nature. Located at the Temple of Sockets in the city's Temple Ward district, Conaris is regarded as one of Ordain's most beloved public figures (despite his wild eccentricities).

Funar Cevher.name: Funar Cevher

Unarmed Strike.name: Unarmed Strike
Unarmed Strike.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixDRule.JournalEntryPage.xJjJ4lhymAYXAOvO]{Unarmed Strike Rules}

Abyssal Sensitivity.name: Abyssal Sensitivity
Abyssal Sensitivity.description:
When you take necrotic damage, make a Charisma saving throw with DC equal to either 10 or half the total necrotic damage taken - whichever value is greater.

  • On a success, apply the Abyssal Resistance effect, gaining resistance to necrotic damage until the end of your next long rest.

  • On a failure, apply the Abyssal Susceptibility effect, inflicting vulnerability to necrotic damage until the end of your next long rest. Each time you take additional necrotic damage you may repeat the saving throw, ending this effect immediately on a success.

This check is not repeated while either Abyssal Resistance or Abyssal Sensitivity are active.

Ember Blaze.name: Ember Blaze
Ember Blaze.description: When [[lookup @name]] is reduced to 0 hit points, he rolls a d20. On a 16 or higher, [[lookup @name]] instead drops to 1 hit point, and it can immediately take an action. Until the end of its next turn, his Speed increases by 10 feet, and he has advantage on weapon attack rolls and spell attack rolls.

Funar Cevher.biographyprivate:
Funar has always been the dutiful son. Though he is quieter and shyer than the more rebellious Lyla, he is very passionate about House Cevher and believes that he should be one of the House's leaders going forward, as he will continue building the legacy developed by his father. Secretly, he does worry that he might be passed over in favor of Lyla, who has more natural charisma and leadership, but believes that his dedication to House Cevher while Lyla went to Casla-Brava to learn new ways will be rewarded.

Personality

Funar believes in the power of tradition, and often cites the past when trying to prove a point or make an argument. This can occasionally make him seem a little pedantic, but he means it earnestly, believing that to build on the accomplishments of the past is to truly honor them. This can be seen when he truly gets excited about a way in which he can bring something from the past into the present, lighting up with the excitement of the discovery.

Connections

Funar is deeply loyal to House Cevher. This loyalty is one of the reasons that he fears what will happen over time with House Cevher, as he knows that he would step down as one of the leaders of the house if someone else — like his sister — was better suited for it.

Phrases

Let's not remake the wheel now.

I think that's what father would have wanted.

What can I do to help?
Funar Cevher.biographypublic:
The young Ordani man walks more slowly than most, looking at everything around him, including you, as if either seeing it for the first time or making sure it hasn't changed since his last viewing. As you meet his eye, he pulls down on his vest and stands up a little straighter, as if he's just remember where he is and why.

Funar Cevher, the younger brother of Lyla Cevher, has always been the more studious and traditional of the two - where Lyla has always wanted to go off exploring or figuring out new ways of doing things, Funar prefers to stick to tradition, using the tried and true methods developed over House Cevher's many generations. He hopes to become one of the leaders of House Cevher one day, though he fears that he lacks the fun and fierce personality of his sister Lyla, who many think of as the future of the Trading House.

Janix Mance.name: Janix Mance

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: Janix Mance makes two attacks, using his [[/item Engineered Arm]] and [[/item Piercing Wrench]] in any combination.

Muscle Machinery.name: Muscle Machinery
Muscle Machinery.description:
Your maximum carrying capacity is doubled for your size.

You have advantage on Constitution saving throws to avoid Exhaustion when going without rest.

Foundry Note

This feature includes an Active Effect which automatically upgrades your size when determining carrying capacity.

Regulated Rhythm.name: Regulated Rhythm
Regulated Rhythm.description:
Your mind and your body work in harmony to solve problems and withstand physical strain. On your turn you may spend a Bonus Action to enter a trance-like state. While in this state you have the following benefits:

  • You have advantage to Insight, Investigation, Perception, and Athletics skill checks.

  • You have advantage on Concentration checks to maintain a spell.

  • If in combat, you recover your Constitution modifier in hit points at the start of each turn. If used outside of combat you instead gain 10 times your Constitution modifier in hit points over the course of 1 minute.

Casting a spell or making an attack roll immediately ends the trance. Once you have used this feature you may not use it again until you finish a long rest.

Janix Mance.biographyprivate:
Janix would never describe himself as a people person - he's always felt a bit more at home with metal and fire than flesh and blood, and after a difficult childhood, would rather put his trust and energy into the constructs he creates than personal connections. His passion — for them, for the art of creation, for the way that metal can be shaped into something that holds its own version of life — is contagious, and he has attracted a number of apprentices interested in learning from an artificer and forgemaster. Working out of Burnside Arms in the Smokerie, he and his team work together to create innovative solutions to fit their clients' needs and are ready to take on any challenge.

Personality

Janix loves coming up with new ideas and putting them into practice. Always innovating, he can easily become bored with the routine - a reason that he enjoys making and working with constructs, which stop him from becoming hyper-focused on his current projects with their pet-like antics. Outside of the excitement of his work, Janix works hard to maintain an even temperament and avoid letting his emotions get the better of him. While he has a quick wit and often uses humor to lighten the mood, he tries to treat everyone with kindness and cannot abide those who are nasty to others. This has made him a sought-after mentor, and while he sometimes keeps his apprentices at arms' length, he is secretly quite proud of helping to build the next generation of artificers.

Connections

Janix and his half-brother Manfryd were raised to compete against each other by their forgemaster father in Skybrush, who only paid attention to the son currently crafting the more impressive work. Ironically, Manfryd's greatest achievement came in his creation of metal replacement limbs for Janix after a fire nearly destroyed the forge and killed their father, but the two brothers had a falling out shortly afterward when Janix revealed he was partly responsible for the blaze.

With no real ties left, Janix decided to devote his energy to creating and animating constructs that would give him an outlet for his skills and a way to interact with others without disappointment. Beyond these creations, Janix generally only interacts with clients and apprentices - he is accommodating with the former and kind with the latter, though he is reluctant to let either group get too close.

Phrases

You give a little, you get a little.

Everybody's got a spark. Mine's just a little easier to see.

Don't worry, I love a challenge.
Janix Mance.biographypublic:
The kivahr has metal and heated fluid on one side of their body, and flesh and blood on the other, but both move as one, with a fluidity and precision that give the sense that each move they make is one they've made a thousand times before. As they move, they hum a little, under their breath - a steady rhythmic song - pausing every so often as if they are waiting for someone or something to join in.

Janix Mance is an innovative blacksmith and artificer whose metal prosthetics give him unique insight into how magic, metal, and flesh can work together as one. Often surrounded by one of the small metal constructs that he makes, animates, and treats as if they were a cross between a pet and a helper; or trailed by one of the apprentices he claims not to need but is always unfailingly kind to, he's always happy to take on a new challenge, whether it's for a client or to satisfy his own personal curiosity.

Eamon Mariflor.name: Eamon Mariflor

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
This spell repairs a single break or tear in an object you touch, such as a broken chain link, two halves of a broken key, a torn cloak, or a leaking wineskin. As long as the break or tear is no larger than 1 foot in any dimension, you mend it, leaving no trace of the former damage.

This spell can physically repair a magic item or construct, but the spell can't restore magic to such an object.

Produce Flame.name: Produce Flame
Produce Flame.description:
A flickering flame appears in your hand. The flame remains there for the Duration and harms neither you nor your Equipment. The flame sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. The spell ends if you dismiss it as an action or if you cast it again.

You can also Attack with the flame, although doing so ends the spell. When you cast this spell, or as an action on a later turn, you can hurl the flame at a creature within 30 feet of you. Make a ranged spell Attack. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 fire damage.

This spell's damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description:
Whispering to the spirits of Nature, you create one of the following Effects within range:

  • You create a tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, Falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.
  • You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.
  • You create an Instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as Falling leaves, a puff of wind, the sound of a small animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot cube.
  • You instantly light or snuff out a Candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Guidance.name: Guidance
Guidance.description: You touch one willing creature. Once before the spell ends, the target can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to one ability check of its choice. It can roll the die before or after making the ability check. The spell then ends.

Detect Poison and Disease.name: Detect Poison and Disease
Detect Poison and Disease.description:
For the duration, you can sense the presence and location of poisons, poisonous creatures, and diseases within 30 feet of you. You also identify the kind of poison, poisonous creature, or disease in each case.

The spell can penetrate most barriers, but it is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

Goodberry.name: Goodberry
Goodberry.description:
Up to ten berries appear in your hand and are infused with magic for the duration. A creature can use its action to eat one berry. Eating a berry restores 1 hit point, and the berry provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day.

The berries lose their potency if they have not been consumed within 24 hours of the casting of this spell.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor, and a protective magical force surrounds it until the spell ends. The target's base AC becomes 13 + its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends if the target dons armor or if you dismiss the spell as an action.

Entangle.name: Entangle
Entangle.description:
Grasping weeds and vines sprout from the ground in a 20-foot square starting from a point within range. For the Duration, these Plants turn the ground in the area into difficult terrain.

A creature in the area when you cast the spell must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be &Reference[Restrained] by the entangling Plants until the spell ends. A creature restrained by the plants can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself.

When the spell ends, the conjured Plants wilt away.

Spike Growth.name: Spike Growth
Spike Growth.description:
The ground in a 20-foot radius centered on a point within range twists and sprouts hard spikes and thorns. The area becomes difficult terrain for the Duration. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes 2d4 piercing damage for every 5 feet it travels.

The transformation of the ground is camouflaged to look natural. Any creature that can't see the area at the time the spell is cast must make a Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC to recognize the terrain as hazardous before entering it.

Web.name: Web
Web.description:
You conjure a mass of thick, sticky webbing at a point of your choice within range. The webs fill a 20-foot cube from that point for the Duration. The webs are difficult terrain and lightly obscure their area.

If the webs aren't anchored between two solid masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across a floor, wall, or ceiling, the conjured web collapses on itself, and the spell ends at the start of your next turn. Webs layered over a flat surface have a depth of 5 feet.

Each creature that starts its turn in the webs or that enters them during its turn must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is Restrained as long as it remains in the webs or until it breaks free.

A creature Restrained by the webs can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer Restrained.

The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot cube of webs exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing 2d4 fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in the fire.

Enhance Ability.name: Enhance Ability
Enhance Ability.description:
You touch a creature and bestow upon it a magical enhancement. Choose one of the following effects; the target gains that effect until the spell ends.

  • Bear's Endurance. The target has advantage on Constitution Checks. It also gains 2d6 Temporary Hit Points, which are lost when the spell ends.
  • Bull's Strength. The target has advantage on Strength Checks, and his or her carrying capacity doubles.
  • Cat's Grace. The target has advantage on Dexterity Checks. It also doesn't take damage from Falling 20 feet or less if it isn't Incapacitated.
  • Eagle's Splendor. The target has advantage on Charisma Checks.
  • Fox's Cunning. The target has advantage on Intelligence Checks.
  • Owl's Wisdom. The target has advantage on Wisdom Checks.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Gust of Wind.name: Gust of Wind
Gust of Wind.description:
A line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide blasts from you in a direction you choose for the spell's duration. Each creature that starts its turn in the line must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from you in a direction following the line.

Any creature in the line must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving closer to you.

The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles, torches, and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to extinguish them.

As a bonus action on each of your turns before the spell ends, you can change the direction in which the line blasts from you.

Create Food and Water.name: Create Food and Water
Create Food and Water.description: You create 45 pounds of food and 30 gallons of water on the ground or in containers within range, enough to sustain up to fifteen humanoids or five steeds for 24 hours. The food is bland but nourishing, and spoils if uneaten after 24 hours. The water is clean and doesn't go bad.

Plant Growth.name: Plant Growth
Plant Growth.description:
This spell channels vitality into plants within a specific area. There are two possible uses for the spell, granting either immediate or long-term benefits.

If you cast this spell using 1 action, choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot radius centered on that point become thick and overgrown. A creature moving through the area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves.

You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

If you cast this spell over 8 hours, you enrich the land. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 1 year. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested.

Glyph of Warding.name: Glyph of Warding
Glyph of Warding.description:
When you cast this spell, you inscribe a glyph that later unleashes a magical effect. You inscribe it either on a surface (such as a table or a section of floor or wall) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book, a scroll, or a treasure chest) to conceal the glyph. The glyph can cover an area no larger than 10 feet in diameter. If the surface or object is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the glyph is broken, and the spell ends without being triggered.

The glyph is nearly invisible and requires a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to be found.

You decide what triggers the glyph when you cast the spell. For glyphs inscribed on a surface, the most typical triggers include touching or standing on the glyph, removing another object covering the glyph, approaching within a certain distance of the glyph, or manipulating the object on which the glyph is inscribed. For glyphs inscribed within an object, the most common triggers include opening that object, approaching within a certain distance of the object, or seeing or reading the glyph. Once a glyph is triggered, this spell ends.

You can further refine the trigger so the spell activates only under certain circumstances or according to physical characteristics (such as height or weight), creature kind (for example, the ward could be set to affect aberrations or drow), or alignment. You can also set conditions for creatures that don't trigger the glyph, such as those who say a certain password.

When you inscribe the glyph, choose explosive runes or a spell glyph.

Explosive Runes. When triggered, the glyph erupts with magical energy in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on the glyph. The sphere spreads around corners. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes [[/r 5d8]] acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage on a failed saving throw (your choice when you create the glyph), or half as much damage on a successful one.

Spell Glyph. You can store a prepared spell of 3rd level or lower in the glyph by casting it as part of creating the glyph. The spell must target a single creature or an area. The spell being stored has no immediate effect when cast in this way. When the glyph is triggered, the stored spell is cast. If the spell has a target, it targets the creature that triggered the glyph. If the spell affects an area, the area is centered on that creature. If the spell summons hostile creatures or creates harmful objects or traps, they appear as close as possible to the intruder and attack it. If the spell requires concentration, it lasts until the end of its full duration.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage of an explosive runes glyph increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd. If you create a spell glyph, you can store any spell of up to the same level as the slot you use for the glyph of warding.

Speak with Plants.name: Speak with Plants
Speak with Plants.description:
You imbue Plants within 30 feet of you with limited sentience and animation, giving them the ability to communicate with you and follow your simple commands. You can question plants about events in the spell's area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, weather, and other circumstances.

You can also turn difficult terrain caused by Plant Growth (such as thickets and undergrowth) into ordinary terrain that lasts for the Duration. Or you can turn ordinary terrain where Plants are present into difficult terrain that lasts for the duration, causing vines and branches to hinder pursuers, for example.

Plants might be able to perform other tasks on your behalf, at the DM's discretion. The spell doesn't enable Plants to uproot themselves and move about, but they can freely move branches, tendrils, and stalks.

If a plant creature is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a Common language, but you gain no magical ability to influence it.

This spell can cause the plants created by the Entangle spell to release a Restrained creature.

Fabricate.name: Fabricate
Fabricate.description:
You convert raw materials into products of the same material. For example, you can fabricate a wooden bridge from a clump of trees, a rope from a patch of hemp, and clothes from flax or wool.

Choose raw materials that you can see within range. You can fabricate a Large or smaller object (contained within a 10-foot cube, or eight connected 5-foot cubes), given a sufficient quantity of raw material. If you are working with metal, stone, or another mineral substance, however, the fabricated object can be no larger than Medium (contained within a single 5-foot cube). The quality of Objects made by the spell is commensurate with the quality of the raw materials.

Creatures or Magic Items can't be created or transmuted by this spell. You also can't use it to create items that ordinarily require a high degree of craftsmanship, such as jewelry, Weapons, glass, or armor, unless you have proficiency with the type of artisan's tools used to craft such Objects.

Control Water.name: Control Water
Control Water.description:
Until the spell ends, you control any freestanding water inside an area you choose that is a cube up to 100 feet on a side. You can choose from any of the following effects when you cast this spell. As an action on your turn, you can repeat the same effect or choose a different one.

Flood. You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20 feet. If the area includes a shore, the flooding water spills over onto dry land, instead create a 20-foot tall wave that travels from one side of the area to the other and then crashes down. Any Huge or smaller vehicles in the wave's path are carried with it to the other side. Any Huge or smaller vehicles struck by the wave have a 25 percent chance of capsizing.

The water level remains elevated until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. If this effect produced a wave, the wave repeats on the start of your next turn while the flood effect lasts.

Part Water. You cause water in the area to move apart and create a trench. The trench extends across the spell's area, and the separated water forms a wall to either side. The trench remains until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. The water then slowly fills in the trench over the course of the next round until the normal water level is restored.

Redirect Flow. You cause flowing water in the area to move in a direction you choose, even if the water has to flow over obstacles, up walls, or in other unlikely directions. The water in the area moves as you direct it, but once it moves beyond the spell's area, it resumes its flow based on the terrain conditions. The water continues to move in the direction you chose until the spell ends or you choose a different effect.

Whirlpool. This effect requires a body of water at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep. You cause a whirlpool to form in the center of the area. The whirlpool forms a vortex that is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet tall. Any creature or object in the water and within 25 feet of the vortex is pulled 10 feet toward it. A creature can swim away from the vortex by making a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC.

When a creature enters the vortex for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage and is caught in the vortex until the spell ends. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage, and isn't caught in the vortex. A creature caught in the vortex can use its action to try to swim away from the vortex as described above, but has disadvantage on the Strength (Athletics) check to do so.

The first time each turn that an object enters the vortex, the object takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage; this damage occurs each round it remains in the vortex.

Black Tentacles.name: Black Tentacles
Black Tentacles.description:
Squirming, ebony tentacles fill a 20-foot square on ground that you can see within range. For the Duration, these tentacles turn the ground in the area into difficult terrain.

When a creature enters the affected area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, the creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage and be &Reference[Restrained] by the tentacles until the spell ends. A creature that starts its turn in the area and is already Restrained by the tentacles takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage.

A creature Restrained by the tentacles can use its action to make a Strength or Dexterity check (its choice) against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself.

Creation.name: Creation
Creation.description:
You pull wisps of shadow material from the Shadowfell to create a nonliving object of vegetable matter within 'range': soft goods, rope, wood, or something similar. You can also use this spell to create mineral objects such as stone, crystal, or metal. The object created must be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and the object must be of a form and material that you have seen before.

The duration depends on the object's material. If the object is composed of multiple materials, use the shortest duration.

  • Vegetable matter - 1 day
  • Stone or crystal - 12 hours
  • Precious metals - 1 hour
  • Gems - 10 minutes
  • Adamantine or mithral - 1 minute

Using any material created by this spell as another spell's material component causes that spell to fail.

Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the cube increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 5th.

Awaken.name: Awaken
Awaken.description:
After spending the casting time tracing magical pathways within a precious gemstone, you touch a Huge or smaller beast or plant. The target must have either no Intelligence score or an Intelligence of 3 or less. The target gains an Intelligence of 10. The target also gains the ability to speak one language you know. If the target is a plant, it gains the ability to move its limbs, roots, vines, creepers, and so forth, and it gains senses similar to a human's. Your DM chooses statistics appropriate for the awakened plant, such as the statistics for the awakened shrub or the awakened tree.

The awakened beast or plant is charmed by you for 30 days or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it. When the charmed condition ends, the awakened creature chooses whether to remain friendly to you, based on how you treated it while it was charmed.

Agrimagical Artifact.name: Agrimagical Artifact
Agrimagical Artifact.description:
Once per day, an agrimage can touch a single stone, plant, or other natural item and imbue it with a specific agrimagical effect. Most of these effects are unique to the agrimage, but known effects include:

  • Barrier Stone. An individual barrier stone can be created to repel creatures of 4 intelligence or less that come near it, either physically (pushing them back) or mentally (compelling the subject to avoid the stone). The stone affects the area in a 1-foot radius around it and can be countered with a DC 10 save. With each new barrier stone placed within 10 feet, the stone becomes stronger, adding a DC of 1 and an additional 1-foot in radius for each additional stone.

  • Evergrowth. Ground within a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=um6uF8FxLGv955QQ]]-foot square of this artifact, traditionally created from newly fallen wood, doubles in productivity - all plants yield double their normal amount and gain one of the following effects:

    • Roots glow in the night, casting dim light within 10 feet of each root.

    • Plants produce a pleasing aroma that reminds each person who encounters them of a pleasant moment from their past.

    • Children conceived in the area have a high chance of being twins.

  • Good Seed. Once planted and fully grown, a plant from this seed has one of the following effects:

    • It produces a fruit or vegetable every 3 days, regardless of the season.

    • Its roots grow toward the nearest source of water, gaining 10 feet of length and/or depth per day.

    • Food made from it keeps for 7 days under any conditions and always tastes good, regardless of the recipe.

Foundry Note

Scaling is implemented in the Barrier Stone activities to adjust the save DC and the area of effect based on the number of stones created.

Walking Stick.name: Walking Stick
Walking Stick.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

A thick shaft of wood wrapped with a sturdy grip makes a highly functional weapon in addition to a stout walking stick.
Walking Stick.descriptionpublic: A thick shaft of wood wrapped with a sturdy grip makes a highly functional weapon in addition to a stout walking stick.

Eamon Mariflor.biographyprivate:
Eamon Mariflor grew up among the farming communes of the Arctus Plateau, where stories of ancient Agrimagical breakthroughs inspired his early fascination with the craft. After apprenticing to a roving Agrimage he decided to commit himself fully to the cause, and moved east, to Redrak Fields. As a young, headstrong man he joined the Consortium ranks and was swiftly met with the jarring focus on commerce-first practices that it held.

Though he struggled for a while, and nearly became disillusioned, Eamon refused to accept his fate, or the slow decline of the Agrimage order. He threw himself into research, pored over the old magics held in the archives, all the while moving up the ranks in the Consortium.

He became a mentor to young mages, a merchant without equal, an administrator that missed nothing, and an expert in the industry of agriculture, until one day he found himself at the top, unchallenged, and able to truly make change.

Since taking charge, Eamon has made bold moves to separate scholarly work from business dealings, and has seen great success in this endeavor. He has seen the Consortium reopen and catalog the archives, extend invitations to wayward Agrimages who can contribute their knowledge, and fostered the teaching of the next generation of Agrimages.

His reforms have started a slow revival of magical study at the heart of the Consortium and in the Redrak Fields region, earning respect among arcane circles and mixed feelings from those invested in its old mercantile ways. He strives to maintain a balance between both interests as best he can.

Personality

Eamon is bright and endlessly curious, keen to hear new ideas and determined to find better ways of doing things. He speaks in a lively, approachable manner, always quick with a joke, but sharp with questions that aim at the heart of a problem. He prefers careful planning and thoughtful collaboration over rash action and is always keen to do some portion of the work himself, rather than delegating it all away to underlings.

Though generally cheerful and patient, Eamon often finds frustration in dealing with people who cling to tradition without question, or refuse to examine why something is done a certain way, especially if the tradition in question is no longer working. He tries to approach these situations with wisdom and grace, valuing all voices, but sometimes fails to see how comforting old routines are to others, especially during times of change he is dedicated to.

Connections

As leader of the Redrak Agrimage Consortium, Eamon is in close contact with scholars, merchants, surveyors, farmers alike, forging bonds between his order and the wider community of Redrak Fields and beyond. His reforms have drawn in a new generation of Agrimages that regard him as a father figure for the order and patron of the Agrimagical ways.

Phrases

If it’s always been done this way, let’s ask why see what we learn form the answer.

Magic and methodology, if grown together, can feed far more than either alone ever could.

A new harvest starts with a single daring seed.
Eamon Mariflor.biographypublic:
Before you stands a short figure with dusky, gray hair shimmering with tiny magical stars and crescent moons. Glowing orange lines coil up his arms and over his face, making his skin look like a bed of cooling lava. His amber eyes seem to always glint with keen interest, and his wide, sharp-toothed smile is overtly friendly. He is dressed practically, and wears the mark of the Redrak Agrimage Consortium pinned to his coat. He moves with lively energy.

[[lookup @name]] is the current head of the Agrimage Consortium in Redrak Fields and is known for his intelligence and approachability. He is admired in the region, and in his order, for leading the organization back toward magical research and learning without sacrificing the lucrative trade they need to sustain themselves and feed the region.

Eveis Brightstone.name: Eveis Brightstone

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of her character sheet. She automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Quadruple Arms.name: Quadruple Arms
Quadruple Arms.description: When [[lookup @name]] casts a spell, she can use her additional arms to manipulate multiple components, allowing her to cast two spells on the same turn. The second spell must have a casting time of 1 action and must be of 1st level or lower. She still uses her own spell slots for both spells, and she benefits from the regular limitations on casting spells (e.g., concentration).

Arcane Ward.name: Arcane Ward
Arcane Ward.description: When an attacker that [[lookup @name]] can see hits her with an attack, she can use her reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

Cast a Spell.name: Cast a Spell
Cast a Spell.description: [[lookup @name]] casts a spell of 3rd level or lower.

Teleport.name: Teleport
Teleport.description:
This spell instantly transports you and up to eight willing creatures that you can see within range, or a single object that you can see within range, to a destination you select. If you target an object, it must be Large or smaller, and it can't be held or carried by an unwilling creature.

The destination you choose must be known to you, and it must be on the same plane of existence as you. Your familiarity with the destination determines whether you arrive there successfully. The DM rolls [[/gmr 1d100]] and consults the Teleportation Outcome table and the explanations after it.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.tables24.RollTable.phbsplTeleportMi]{Teleportation Outcome}
FamiliarityMishapSimilar AreaOff TargetOn Target
Permanent circle———01–00
Linked object———01–00
Very familiar01–0506–1314–2425–00
Seen casually01–3334–4344–5354–00
Viewed once or described01–4344–5354–7374–00
False destination01–5051–00——

Familiarity. Here are the meanings of the terms in the table's Familiarity column:

  • "Permanent circle" means a permanent teleportation circle whose sigil sequence you know.
  • "Linked object" means you possess an object taken from the desired destination within the last six months, such as a book from a wizard's library.
  • "Very familiar" is a place you have visited often, a place you have carefully studied, or a place you can see when you cast the spell.
  • "Seen casually" is a place you have seen more than once but with which you aren't very familiar.
  • "Viewed once or described" is a place you have seen once, possibly using magic, or a place you know through someone else's description, perhaps from a map.
  • "False destination" is a place that doesn't exist. Perhaps you tried to scry an enemy's sanctum but instead viewed an illusion, or you are attempting to teleport to a location that no longer exists.

Mishap. The spell's unpredictable magic results in a difficult journey. Each teleporting creature (or the target object) takes [[/damage 3d10 type=force]] damage, and the DM rerolls on the table to see where you wind up (multiple mishaps can occur, dealing damage each time).

Similar Area. You and your group (or the target object) appear in a different area that's visually or thematically similar to the target area. You appear in the closest similar place. If you are heading for your home laboratory, for example, you might appear in another person's laboratory in the same city.

Off Target. You and your group (or the target object) appear [[/r 2d12]] miles away from the destination in a random direction. Roll [[/r 1d8]] for the direction: 1, east; 2, southeast; 3, south; 4, southwest; 5, west; 6, northwest; 7, north; or 8, northeast.

On Target. You and your group (or the target object) appear where you intended.

Arcane Burst.name: Arcane Burst
Arcane Burst.description: [[lookup @name]] releases a burst of magic in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=0eP9PG6HfqJkCuuL]]-foot radius around her. Each creature in that area must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or take [[/damage average]] damage and be knocked &Reference[prone].

Custodian Star Mage.name: Custodian Star Mage
Custodian Star Mage.description:
As a higher-ranking member of the Star Mages, [[lookup @name]] has unrestricted access to the Star Academy Vaults, Libraries, and Observatories.

In addition, due to the intense training and after passing the Star Mages final exams, you now gain advantage on all Arcana and Religion checks.

You can also cast [[/item .BBPH0UJLeCXu2fjG]]{Augury} as a ritual without using a spell slot or reduce its casting time to an Action by expending a 2nd-level spell slot.

Fire Bolt.name: Fire Bolt
Fire Bolt.description:
You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or an object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell starts burning if it isn't being worn or carried.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d10 when you reach levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10).

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Minor Illusion.name: Minor Illusion
Minor Illusion.description:
You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

Ray of Frost.name: Ray of Frost
Ray of Frost.description:
A frigid beam of blue-white light streaks toward a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, it takes 1d8 Cold damage, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Magic Missile.name: Magic Missile
Magic Missile.description:
You create three glowing darts of magical force. Each dart strikes a creature of your choice that you can see within range. A dart deals 1d4 + 1 Force damage to its target. The darts all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The spell creates one more dart for each spell slot level above 1.

[[2 + @item.level]]{Level [[lookup @item.level]] darts}

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description: An imperceptible barrier of magical force protects you. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack, and you take no damage from @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMagicMissi]{Magic Missile}.

Darkness.name: Darkness
Darkness.description:
For the duration, magical &Reference[darkness] spreads from a point within range and fills a 15-foot-radius Sphere. Darkvision can't see through it, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it.

Alternatively, you cast the spell on an object that isn't being worn or carried, causing the Darkness to fill a 15-foot Emanation originating from that object. Covering that object with something opaque, such as a bowl or helm, blocks the Darkness.

If any of this spell's area overlaps with an area of Bright Light or Dim Light created by a spell of level 2 or lower, that other spell is dispelled.

Mirror Image.name: Mirror Image
Mirror Image.description:
Three illusory duplicates of yourself appear in your space. Until the spell ends, the duplicates move with you and mimic your actions, shifting position so it's impossible to track which image is real.

Each time a creature hits you with an attack roll during the spell's duration, roll a [[/r (@flags.dnd-players-handbook.mirrorImages)d6kh1cs>2#Duplicate destroyed]]{d6 for each} of your remaining duplicates. If any of the d6s rolls a 3 or higher, one of the duplicates is hit instead of you, and the duplicate is destroyed. The duplicates otherwise ignore all other damage and effects. The spell ends when all three duplicates are destroyed.

A creature is unaffected by this spell if it has the &Reference[blinded apply=false] condition, &Reference[blindsight], or &Reference[truesight].

Misty Step.name: Misty Step
Misty Step.description: Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.

Fireball.name: Fireball
Fireball.description:
A bright streak flashes from you to a point you choose within range and then blossoms with a low roar into a fiery explosion. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried start burning.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

Magic Circle.name: Magic Circle
Magic Circle.description:
You create a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-tall Cylinder of magical energy centered on a point on the ground that you can see within range. Glowing runes appear wherever the Cylinder intersects with the floor or other surface.

Choose one or more of the following types of creatures: Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, or Undead. The circle affects a creature of the chosen type in the following ways:

  • The creature can't willingly enter the Cylinder by nonmagical means. If the creature tries to use teleportation or interplanar travel to do so, it must first succeed on a Charisma saving throw.
  • The creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls against targets within the Cylinder.
  • Targets within the Cylinder can't be possessed by or gain the &Reference[charmed apply=false] or &reference[frightened apply=false] condition from the creature.

Each time you cast this spell, you can cause its magic to operate in the reverse direction, preventing a creature of the specified type from leaving the Cylinder and protecting targets outside it.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The duration increases by 1 hour for each spell slot level above 3.

Dimension Door.name: Dimension Door
Dimension Door.description:
You teleport to a location within range. You arrive at exactly the spot desired. It can be a place you can see, one you can visualize, or one you can describe by stating distance and direction, such as "200 feet straight downward" or "300 feet upward to the northwest at a 45-degree angle."

You can also teleport one willing creature. The creature must be within 5 feet of you when you teleport, and it teleports to a space within 5 feet of your destination space.

If you, the other creature, or both would arrive in a space occupied by a creature or completely filled by one or more objects, you and any creature traveling with you each take 4d6 Force damage, and the teleportation fails.

Greater Invisibility.name: Greater Invisibility
Greater Invisibility.description: A creature you touch has the Invisible condition until the spell ends.

Phantasmal Killer.name: Phantasmal Killer
Phantasmal Killer.description:
You tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see within range and create an illusion of its deepest fears, visible only to that creature. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 4d10 Psychic damage and has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls for the duration. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and the spell ends.

For the duration, the target makes a [[/save ability=wis dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a failed save, it takes the Psychic damage again. On a successful save, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.The damage increases by 1d10 for each spell slot level above 4.

Cone of Cold.name: Cone of Cold
Cone of Cold.description:
You unleash a blast of cold air. Each creature in a 60-foot Cone originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 8d8 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature killed by this spell becomes a frozen statue until it thaws.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 5.

Telekinesis.name: Telekinesis
Telekinesis.description:
You gain the ability to move or manipulate creatures or objects by thought. When you cast the spell and as a Magic action on your later turns before the spell ends, you can exert your will on one creature or object that you can see within range, causing the appropriate effect below. You can affect the same target round after round or choose a new one at any time. If you switch targets, the prior target is no longer affected by the spell.

Creature. You can try to move a Huge or smaller creature. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or you move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range. Until the end of your next turn, the creature has the &Reference[Restrained] condition, and if you lift it into the air, it is suspended there. It falls at the end of your next turn unless you use this option on it again and it fails the save.

Object. You can try to move a Huge or smaller object. If the object isn't being worn or carried, you automatically move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range.

If the object is worn or carried by a creature, that creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or you pull the object away and move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range.

You can exert fine control on objects with your telekinetic grip, such as manipulating a simple tool, opening a door or a container, stowing or retrieving an item from an open container, or pouring the contents from a vial.

Wall of Force.name: Wall of Force
Wall of Force.description:
An Invisible wall of force springs into existence at a point you choose within range. The wall appears in any orientation you choose, as a horizontal or vertical barrier or at an angle. It can be free floating or resting on a solid surface. You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a globe with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-by-10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. In any form, the wall is 1/4 inch thick and lasts for the duration. If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (you choose which side).

Nothing can physically pass through the wall. It is immune to all damage and can't be dispelled by @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic}. A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDisintegra]{Disintegrate} spell destroys the wall instantly, however. The wall also extends into the Ethereal Plane and blocks ethereal travel through the wall.

Chain Lightning.name: Chain Lightning
Chain Lightning.description:
You launch a lightning bolt toward a target you can see within range. Three bolts then leap from that target to as many as three other targets of your choice, each of which must be within 30 feet of the first target. A target can be a creature or an object and can be targeted by only one of the bolts.

Each target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d8 Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. One additional bolt leaps from the first target to another target for each spell slot level above 6.

Contingency.name: Contingency
Contingency.description:
Choose a spell of level 5 or lower that you can cast, that has a casting time of an action, and that can target you. You cast that spell—called the contingent spell—as part of casting Contingency, expending spell slots for both, but the contingent spell doesn't come into effect. Instead, it takes effect when a certain trigger occurs. You describe that trigger when you cast the two spells. For example, a Contingency cast with Water Breathing might stipulate that Water Breathing comes into effect when you are engulfed in water or a similar liquid.

The contingent spell takes effect immediately after the trigger occurs for the first time, whether or not you want it to, and then Contingency ends.

The contingent spell takes effect only on you, even if it can normally target others. You can use only one Contingency spell at a time. If you cast this spell again, the effect of another Contingency spell on you ends. Also, Contingency ends on you if its material component is ever not on your person.

Foundry Note

The "create contingency" activity is configured to optionally enchant a Scroll to track and serve as the triggered spell. Create a spell scroll by right clicking on a spell in your spell list, expend a spell slot of the created scroll's level, and enchant the scroll.

Simulacrum.name: Simulacrum
Simulacrum.description:
You create a simulacrum of one Beast or Humanoid that is within 10 feet of you for the entire casting of the spell. You finish the casting by touching both the creature and a pile of ice or snow that is the same size as that creature, and the pile turns into the simulacrum, which is a creature. It uses the game statistics of the original creature at the time of casting, except it is a Construct, its Hit Point maximum is half as much, and it can't cast this spell.

The simulacrum is Friendly to you and creatures you designate. It obeys your commands and acts on your turn in combat. The simulacrum can't gain levels, and it can't take Short or Long Rests.

If the simulacrum takes damage, the only way to restore its Hit Points is to repair it as you take a Long Rest, during which you expend components worth 100 GP per Hit Point restored. The simulacrum must stay within 5 feet of you for the repair.

The simulacrum lasts until it drops to 0 Hit Points, at which point it reverts to snow and melts away. If you cast this spell again, any simulacrum you created with this spell is instantly destroyed.

Mind Blank.name: Mind Blank
Mind Blank.description: Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch has Immunity to Psychic damage and the Charmed condition. The target is also unaffected by anything that would sense its emotions or alignment, read its thoughts, or magically detect its location, and no spell—not even @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplWish000000]{Wish}—can gather information about the target, observe it remotely, or control its mind.

Power Word Stun.name: Power Word Stun
Power Word Stun.description:
You overwhelm the mind of one creature you can see within range. If the target has 150 Hit Points or fewer, it has the Stunned condition. Otherwise, its Speed is 0 until the start of your next turn.

The &Reference[Stunned apply=false] target makes a [[/save ability=con dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.

Foresight.name: Foresight
Foresight.description: You touch a willing creature and bestow a limited ability to see into the immediate future. For the duration, the target has Advantage on D20 Tests, and other creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls against it. The spell ends early if you cast it again.

Gate.name: Gate
Gate.description:
You conjure a portal linking an unoccupied space you can see within range to a precise location on a different plane of existence. The portal is a circular opening, which you can make 5 to 20 feet in diameter. You can orient the portal in any direction you choose. The portal lasts for the duration, and the portal's destination is visible through it.

The portal has a front and a back on each plane where it appears. Travel through the portal is possible only by moving through its front. Anything that does so is instantly transported to the other plane, appearing in the unoccupied space nearest to the portal.

Deities and other planar rulers can prevent portals created by this spell from opening in their presence or anywhere within their domains.

When you cast this spell, you can speak the name of a specific creature (a pseudonym, title, or nickname doesn't work). If that creature is on a plane other than the one you are on, the portal opens next to the named creature and transports it to the nearest unoccupied space on your side of the portal. You gain no special power over the creature, and it is free to act as the DM deems appropriate. It might leave, attack you, or help you.

Augury.name: Augury
Augury.description:
You receive an omen from an otherworldly entity about the results of a course of action that you plan to take within the next 30 minutes. The DM chooses the omen from the Omens table.

OmenFor Results That Will Be …
WealGood
WoeBad
Weal and woeGood and bad
IndifferenceNeither good nor bad

The spell doesn't account for circumstances, such as other spells, that might change the results.

If you cast the spell more than once before finishing a Long Rest, there is a cumulative 25 percent chance for each casting after the first that you get no answer.

Legendary Resistance.name: Legendary Resistance
