Legendary Resistance.description: If [[lookup @name]] fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

Seacrown.name: Seacrown
Seacrown.descriptionprivate:
Weapon (@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepQuartersta]{Quarterstaff}), Legendary (Requires Attunement)

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

Seacrown is a legendary staff crafted by Eveis Brightstone herself, which some say was crafted from the remains of a dead Shard God from her homeland. The staff stands at approximately eight feet tall, crafted from a rare, polished ebony coral that boasts a natural sheen reminiscent of glittering stars. The entire length is intricately carved to appear like the rising waters of ocean waves. Etheral magical waters swirl around the staff itself, glowing softly with a luminous blue hue when wielded by Eveis. At the top of Seacrown rests an exquisite round pearl, encased within a crown of bone.

You have a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Spellcasting Focus: You can use Seacrown as a spellcasting focus for your spells.

Water Manipulation: As an action, you can cast the spell [[/item .M0iC5JcAurp8stnq]]{Control Water} without expending a spell slot.

Legendary Actions: Seacrown grants you access to two legendary actions, which can be used at the end of another creature's turn, regaining all spent legendary actions at the start of your turn.

Tidal Wave (Costs 1 Action): You create a wave of water in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=qoITzdDVJVgx5yKR]]-foot line that is [[lookup @target.template.width activity=qoITzdDVJVgx5yKR]]-feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a [[/save format=long activity=qoITzdDVJVgx5yKR]] or take [[/damage average activity=qoITzdDVJVgx5yKR]] damage and be knocked &Reference[prone]. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is not knocked prone.

Call of the Stars (Costs 1 Action): You can cast [[/item .geJx8JBfDEfg65Ie]] or [[/item .7QkaKwunFyvuwffV]] without expending a spell slot. You can also choose an additional target to benefit from the Guidance spell.

Control Water.name: Control Water
Control Water.description:
Until the spell ends, you control any water inside an area you choose that is a Cube up to 100 feet on a side, using one of the following effects. As a Magic action on your later turns, you can repeat the same effect or choose a different one.

Flood. You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20 feet. If you choose an area in a large body of water, you instead create a 20-foot tall wave that travels from one side of the area to the other and then crashes. Any Huge or smaller vehicles in the wave's path are carried with it to the other side. Any Huge or smaller vehicles struck by the wave have a [[/r 1d100cs<26#Vehicle is capsized]]{25 percent} chance of capsizing.

The water level remains elevated until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. If this effect produced a wave, the wave repeats on the start of your next turn while the flood effect lasts.

Part Water. You part water in the area and create a trench. The trench extends across the spell's area, and the separated water forms a wall to either side. The trench remains until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. The water then slowly fills in the trench over the course of the next round until the normal water level is restored.

Redirect Flow. You cause flowing water in the area to move in a direction you choose, even if the water has to flow over obstacles, up walls, or in other unlikely directions. The water in the area moves as you direct it, but once it moves beyond the spell's area, it resumes its flow based on the terrain. The water continues to move in the direction you chose until the spell ends or you choose a different effect.

Whirlpool. You cause a whirlpool to form in the center of the area, which must be at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep. The whirlpool lasts until you choose a different effect or the spell ends. The whirlpool is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet tall. Any creature in the water and within 25 feet of the whirlpool is pulled 10 feet toward it. When a creature enters the whirlpool for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there, it makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 Bludgeoning damage. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage. A creature can swim away from the whirlpool only if it first takes an action to pull away and succeeds on a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC.

Guidance.name: Guidance
Guidance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a skill. Until the spell ends, the creature adds 1d4 to any ability check using the chosen skill.

Eveis Brightstone.biographyprivate:
Eveis is the Custodian Star Mage of Ordain who has held the position for thirty years. In her youth, she was considered a prodigy at the Star Academy, and it took her far less time to advance through the trials and tests to become a full Star Mage than almost any other member in living memory. After her ascent, however, she disappeared for many years, with some speculating that she returned to her people to aid them in various crises. Regardless, upon her return to the Star Academy, she was an even greater adept of the magical arts, and after long meetings with Director Albine Amar, she was surprisingly given the Custodian duty over the city of Ordain.

Eveis spends most of her time studying magic and delving into cosmological mysteries, in addition to keeping a close eye on the usage of the APN Gate in the city. The use of the gate is tightly controlled, and only important political figures, ambassadors, and licensed traders can access it. She routinely reviews and often denies requests from Trading Houses to use the Gate to transport goods.

Personality

Eveis is soft-spoken and reserved. Her calm demeanor often puts others at ease, enabling her to communicate complex ideas with clarity and patience. She possesses a keen intellect and is deeply curious, always seeking to expand her understanding of magic and the cosmos. Despite her friendly and calm personality, she is also deeply committed to the Star Mages’ policy of non-interference with the city of Ordain, a consequence of not changing the fate and direction that the people must walk on thier own. This means that to many, although she is powerful and wise, she can come across as very distant and unconcerned with others' problems, which is far from the truth in reality. Eveis will occasionally work with or aid others if the cause is minor or does not directly place her in a position of making decisions for the city. To that end, she often works with the Ancaharenum, helping them research odd or potentially dangerous magical artifacts.

Eveis is very aware that she is the only Carrow within Ordain and an extremely rare sight in the known world, as most of her people cannot survive on land. She therefore recognizes that she represents all Carrow to some extent and strives to answer any questions about her strange and wondrous physical appearance. However, she does not talk about her people and culture, keeping where she originally came from a secret. This may be because she doesnt want her people's knowledge or life to be known and is protecting them, or perhaps there is some other reason.

If a character in the party is a follower of Spectra, they will likely recognize that Eveis is one of her followers. Eveis herself is also aware that Spectra visits the Library of Spectra in Scholars Nook from time to time and will often spend time with her chosen deity discussing and arguing magical theory. Eveis will likely be much more engaged with anyone who is a follower of Spectra or a Rhivan and will be much more open to answering questions.

In contrast, any character with Abyssal influence, necrotic connections, or energies will be immediately suspect. Eveis will not attack any such character within the city, but she will not trust them and will be extremely clipped in her responses. She may even refuse to aid them entirely based on the level of corruption.

Connections

Eveis has interacted with and met nearly everyone at Ordain over the years and has developed deep personal relationships with the various heads of organizations and city leaders. She is also strangely loved by the people, even though she does little to aid them directly; many consider her presence a sign that the city is being watched over and protected.

She is also considered one of the most powerful and well-connected Star Mages overall and would be in a position to succeed Albine Amar should anything happen to the illustrious leader of the Star Mages.

Phrases

"Knowledge is a vast sea, and I strive to explore every corner of it."
Eveis Brightstone.biographypublic:
You take a moment to absorb the sight before you, your mind struggling to accept what you see. Hovering just above the ground is a mythical being, one of the fabled Carrow from the depths of Ember's oceans. The figure clearly finds your surprise amusing as she smiles slightly, her calm expression hiding more of her mirth. Her pale blue skin, elongated face, and sharp, webbed long ears, along with four arms and hands, seem extraordinary, and you note with some alarm that she towers over you. Far larger than even a Cor'ak, her figure remains elegant and lithe, moving gracefully through the air. Clothed in flowing robes that shift and swirl like ocean currents and adorned with intricate designs of stars and the moons of Ember, she gives off the aura of a creature that has just stepped from a legend.

[[lookup @name]] is the Custodian Star Mage assigned to the great city of Ordain thirty years ago and she is considered one of the strongest mortal mages in the Arctus Plateau. Many are shocked to discover that Eveis is a Carrow, a captivating ancestry that dwells in the deepest sections of Ember's oceans. She possesses a keen intellect and is deeply curious, yet calm and serious and always balancing her pursuit of magic and the arcane with her sense of duty.

Ix'erax.name: Ix'erax

Web Sense.name: Web Sense
Web Sense.description: While in contact with a web, [[lookup @name]] knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

Web Walker.name: Web Walker
Web Walker.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] ignores movement restrictions caused by webs, and the [[lookup @name lowercase]] knows the location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

Bite.name: Bite
Bite.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]], and the target must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or be &Reference[poisoned] for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes two attacks: one with her [[/item Bite]] and one with her [[/item Web]].

Web.name: Web
Web.descriptionprivate: Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range [[lookup @item.range.value]] ft., one Large or smaller creature. Hit: The target is &Reference[restrained] by magical webbing. A creature restrained by the web can use its action to make a [[/check format=long]], freeing itself on a success.

Move.name: Move
Move.description: [[lookup @name]] moves up to half her speed

Shadow Strike.name: Shadow Strike
Shadow Strike.description: [[lookup @name]] teleports to an unoccupied space she can see within 30 feet and makes one [[/item Bite]] attack.

Devoted Watcher.name: Devoted Watcher
Devoted Watcher.description: [[lookup @name]] has an inherent connection to the Outer Goddess The Watcher. Once per day, she can cast [[/item .fz6lURUaZW36ub8R]]{Fear} (spell save DC 16) centered on itself.

Dark Doorway.name: Dark Doorway
Dark Doorway.description: [[lookup @name]] can teleport from her current location to any other spot within 1 mile at will. She arrives at exactly the spot desired.

Legendary Resistance.name: Legendary Resistance
Legendary Resistance.description: If the [[lookup @name lowercase]] fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

Fear.name: Fear
Fear.description:
Each creature in a 30-foot Cone must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or drop whatever it is holding and have the &Reference[frightened apply=false] condition for the duration.

A Frightened creature takes the &Reference[dash] action and moves away from you by the safest route on each of its turns unless there is nowhere to move. If the creature ends its turn in a space where it doesn't have line of sight to you, the creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, the spell ends on that creature.

Spider Climb.name: Spider Climb
Spider Climb.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

Ix'erax.biographyprivate:
As a young spiderling, without much thought or understanding, Ix'erax was driven by a primal hunger to feed on the creatures and even mortals around her. Over the years, however, as she slowly gained sentience and then sapience, her perception of this hunger began to shift, and she started to resist the urge. At some point, she was captured and imprisoned by Agaseroes, and as she sat ensnared in his arcane chamber, surrounded by new knowledge and arcane secrets, the need to feed faded away. There are moments when her old hunger reemerges, but she is old enough to control it and finds that arcane magic can sustain her indefinitely. Her knowledge of the Abyss is particularly unique, and as a child of the Sitheera, she is able to glimpse into dark corners of the Abyss with little fear.

Personality

Ix'erax is a strange character, on the one hand, she is wise and calm, with a wealth of knowledge, but she also has a distant, almost sociopathic personality, where she finds mortals and people fascinating but cannot relate empathically to them in any way. She exhibits a quiet confidence and a patient demeanor, and speaks many different languages, including Common, with elegance and skill.

Connections

She was once a prionor of Agaseros, and wanted nothing more than to devour him for his actions, but she spent years trapped within the Chamber and eventually understood more about the aracen world from him than she ever thought possible. Her hatred faded, and it was replaced by respect. Today, she looks back at the memory of her former friend with fondness and wistfulness.

Phrases

"The pitter patter of small feet in my room, how delightful.. "

"What you perceive as danger, I see as an opportunity to learn. Do not shy away from the unknown."
Ix'erax.biographypublic:
At first, the green glow floating in the air before you resembles many of the candles scattered around the room, however, these lights grow larger, and emerging from the darkness is a creature of alien fear and terror. The massive black body of a giant spider glistens in the dim light as it moves slowly forward into your field of view. Upon its large abdomen looms a giant, demonic-looking skull, with the eyes of the skull erupting in green fire. As you stare into her emerald-green eyes, you realize they are filled with ancient wisdom and an unsettling intensity, and there seems to be no hostile intent behind them.

[[lookup @name]] is an ancient and colossal Spider, believed to be one of the offspring of the goddess known to mortals as the Watcher. She was once captured by Agaseros, but over the years, she became quite content with her captivity and began to appreciate the arcane talent and power of Agaseros, eventually sharing her knowledge and skills. While she can leave the Chamber of Agaseros at any time, she is content to remain and happily observes the city of Ordain.

Scalemaw.name: Scalemaw

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes one [[/item .oBEQdx6fnOgy15s3]] attack and one [[/item .OU7L8MxhcUuyHtv6]] attack

Hold Breath.name: Hold Breath
Hold Breath.description: The [[lookup @name]] can hold its breath for 1 hour.

Bite.name: Bite
Bite.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].If the target is a [[lookup @target.affects.special activity=xWlMeXFjELfSUWX9]] creature, it has the &Reference[Grappled apply=false] condition (escape DC [[lookup @skills.ath.passive]]). While Grappled, the target has the &Reference[Restrained apply=false] condition and can't be targeted by the [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s Tail.

Tail.name: Tail
Tail.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the &Reference[Prone apply=false] condition.

Abduct.name: Abduct
Abduct.description: The [[lookup @name]] needn't spend extra movement to move a creature it is grappling.

Scalemaw.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Adult Scalemaws grow to be as large as 15 feet in length, although half of this length is their reaching tail that provides them with balance on-land and control while moving quickly through water. The four eyes of the Scalemaw have evolved to allow them to perceive both above and below the surface of water simultaneously. One pair of eyes rests higher on their head and can be used to watch for prey while the other pair of eyes remains submerged and alert for underwater movement.

The heavy scaled hide of the Scalemaw is valued by certain crafters as a material for the creation of leather armor or durable heavy cloaks which offer a balance of intimidating style and worthy protection.

Behavior

Scalemaws are carnivorous predators who lurk in shallow water to ambush and abduct prey that approaches the water's shore or that swims within its depths. Upon siezing its prey, the Scalemaw will withdraw into the water, hauling it down to the bottom where it holds it in place and devours it.

Scalemaws are easily provoked and often undetected when they are lurking beneath the water's surface. Travelers in regions where Scalemaws thrive, especially those journeying near bodies of water, are urged to remain watchful and not stray too close to the water's edge unless they take active precautions.

Lore

Natural ecosystems where Scalemaw thrive are found in the Duskflare Jungles, Mazira, or distant Jurin.

Scalemaws are famously ferocious, but there have been rare efforts made by certain Waerds to domesticate and train them as companion beasts of war. Primalist druids often make pilgrimage to Scalemaws habitats to spend time communing with such creatures in order to master the arts of shapechanging into their powerful form.

One Waerd in particular, Raster Thorn, procured a shipment of Scalemaws from Kulrun in the Lowland Bastions which he brought to Ordain. Within the city, the subterranean waterworks of the Concourse are a friendly urban habitat for the creatures who have thrived and become domesticated under Raster's supervision.
Scalemaw.biographypublic:
A hulking scaled shape lies low to the ground, it's belly grazing the floor as four gleaming eyes move in unison to survey its surroundings. The creature's body is nearly fifteen feet long, although much of that is due to a sinuous tail that moves with a level of control that suggests finely honed muscle within. The bulk of the creature's frame is large enough to devour a man and the jaws of the creature are savage enough that such a process would be both gruesome and effective.

Scalemaws are hulking reptilian beasts who are carnivorous hunters from swamps or coastal habitats. They excel in lurking within shallow water and bursting forth with ferocious power capable of killing unwary prey even larger than themselves.

Kynryth.name: Kynryth

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] makes any combination of two [[/item Tentacle Grab]], [[/item Tentacle Swipe]], and [[/item Heated Swipe]] attacks.

Throw Fire.name: Throw Fire
Throw Fire.description:
As a bonus action, the Kynryth takes a portion of the radiant fire at its core and throws it as a weapon, dealing radiant damage to anyone in its path.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=nzpSllSvsoBUg5Vu]], each creature in the area.

Failure: [[/damage average]] radiant damage.

Success: Half damage.

This expends 1 portion of @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.MFcSuAhMSQo009S5]{The Light Within} and can’t be used while out of portions.

Kynryth Torch (Lit).name: Kynryth Torch (Lit)
Kynryth Torch (Lit).descriptionprivate: The kynryth torch is the source of life within each Kynryth — they cannot be separated from the creatures while alive, and their light fades within 10 minutes of the associated creatures' death.

Burst of Speed.name: Burst of Speed
Burst of Speed.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] uses its internal fire to move at double its normal speed until the end of its next turn. This action uses 1 portion of @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.MFcSuAhMSQo009S5]{The Light Within}.

Tentacle Grab.name: Tentacle Grab
Tentacle Grab.description:
The [[lookup @name lowercase]] reaches out with its tentacles and grabs a creature within range, pulling the creature into the flame at the center of its body.

Strength Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=H3ZUZ0Rdw56BuiP6]], a creature within [[lookup @range.value activity=H3ZUZ0Rdw56BuiP6]]-feet of the [[lookup @name lowercase]].

Failure: The target is pulled into the same space as the [[lookup @name lowercase]] and takes [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: The target isn’t pulled into the [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s space.

The [[lookup @name lowercase]] can grab up to two creatures at a time.

The Light Within.name: The Light Within
The Light Within.description:
The [[lookup @name lowercase]] uses some of its inner flame to take one of the following actions. Each action dims the flame somewhat - after taking 4 actions that use its inner light, the [[lookup @name lowercase]] becomes a shell of its normal self until one of the following occurs.

  • Its flame is reignited by a Tyraphem

  • It acquires a @UUID[Item.5ABf86cbSTOxtMcs]{Kynryth Torch (Lit)}

  • It receives a portion of flame from another [[lookup @name lowercase]]

  • The light of Lantyr touches it in the dawn.

Until this occurs, the [[lookup @name lowercase]] is limited to the actions of a @UUID[Actor.VyWFhpROA1S5Icsg]{Kynryth Husk}.

The following actions use a single portion of the [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s inner flame:

  • [[/item .QVyuVvQsMOfHFmZH]]

  • [[/item .lq7GsU73yDlkGRmn]]

  • [[/item .fYPeEMBxaxVwtLng]]

  • [[/item .tk64nySGm5puF89S]]

Heated Swipe.name: Heated Swipe
Heated Swipe.description:
The [[lookup @name lowercase]] uses a portion of its inner flame to heat its tentacles with radiant fire. All tentacle attacks ([[/item Tentacle Grab]], [[/item Tentacle Swipe]]) do an additional [[/damage average]] damage until the end of the [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s next turn.

This action uses 1 portion of @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.MFcSuAhMSQo009S5]{The Light Within}.

Share Flame.name: Share Flame
Share Flame.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] provides 1 or more portions of @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.MFcSuAhMSQo009S5]{The Light Within} to a fellow [[lookup @name lowercase]], reducing its own portion accordingly.

Dying Light.name: Dying Light
Dying Light.description:
If a [[lookup @name]] dies while it still has an active portion of @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.MFcSuAhMSQo009S5]{The Light Within}, its inner fire seeks out any [[lookup @name lowercase]] within 60 feet that has used some of its own Light Within, initiating the @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.tk64nySGm5puF89S]{Share Flame} with that [[lookup @name lowercase]]. The dying [[lookup @name lowercase]] can only share flame with a single [[lookup @name lowercase]] with this action.

If no [[lookup @name lowercase]] are found, the light explodes. Any creatures within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=MwRJiFJ6zVMnW0DK]] feet of the [[lookup @name lowercase]] must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or they take [[/damage average]] damage.

Kynryth.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Like all creatures native to Luxaurum, the Kynryth has a soul of powerful light encased within a constructed metal carapace. This body can be fully and magically concealed for clandestine activities, though all Kynryth carry a torch somewhere on them when in human form, and often use it as a weapon once fully revealed as being creatures of Luxaurum.

Behavior

Kynryth are seen as fairly interchangeable beasts on Luxaurum, functioning almost as guard dogs. Their ability to hide their true form is more useful outside of Luxaurum than within it, used for spying on those who are in a specific Tyraphem's way and destroying them.

Lore

Treated as something along the lines of a ferocious pet on Luxaurum, Kynryth have more use on Ember, and are being seen as part of a vanguard of creatures from Luxaurum that can help Tyraphem continue their eternal wars on new ground.
Kynryth.biographypublic:
A metallic mass of arms and tentacles that advances towards you, clutching a pulsing flame to its chest that glows throughout its body, shifting with each step as if it has a life of its own.

Kynryth appear at first to be humanoids, distinguishable only due to the fact that they always carry a torch. In truth, this torch is a radiant flame that is at the heart of their power, given to them by the Tyraphem in return for their violence and devotion.

Projection of Pyix.name: Projection of Pyix
Projection of Pyix.biographyprivate:
Though it is only a faint echo of the true power and form of the Luxaurun that created it, this projection of radiant energy hums with power and speaks with deep authority.

For more guidance, see@UUID[Actor.fcK7WLaLCCcMP9oL]{ Pyix}, as this projection is only a reflection of the Celestial creature.
Projection of Pyix.biographypublic:
The being before you appears as suddenly as a spell, filling the space with an image that is as insubstantial as it is powerful. The light within its long robes is bright and glorious, but it flickers here and there - the only imperfection in the midst of an overwhelming presence.

The projection is a manifestation of Pyix, a powerful Tyraphem who views Ember as a playground to entertain themselves in. Catching their attention is rarely wise, and understanding their full intentions is difficult in the best of circumstances. These are not the best of circumstances.

Anachraenum Aetherial.name: Anachraenum Aetherial

Antimagic Susceptibility.name: Antimagic Susceptibility
Antimagic Susceptibility.description:
The [[lookup @name]] is &Reference[incapacitated] while in the area of an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAntimagicF]{antimagic field}.

If targeted by @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{dispel magic}, the [[lookup @name]] must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against the caster's spell save DC or fall &Reference[unconscious] for 1 minute.

Immutable Form.name: Immutable Form
Immutable Form.description: The [[lookup @name]] is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

Anachraenum Aetherial.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Anachraenum Aetherials are made of a magically enhanced rock. It's not particularly powerful, but it does allow the Aetherial to hold a charge for a number of days. This strong charge is also used to produce a beam of lightning energy that it uses during its "Attack" mode. The damage caused by this attack, however, is rarely lethal and is specially designed to knock out rather than kill.

Behavior

Anachraenum Aetherial have no true behaviors, they are simply small entities created by the Anachraenum. Their three main modes are:

  • Stay - The Aetherial does not attack or move from its position.

  • Attack - The Aetherial will pursue any creature or entity that enters its sight range, moving around obstacles and firing its laser at them. It will continue to do so until it loses track of them or it is defeated.

  • Defend - The Aetherial will attack anyone within its sight range, but it will remain stationary.

Lore

Anachraenum Aetherials were created by the Mage Agaseros, an Anachraenum Guildmaster, nearly three hundred years ago.
Anachraenum Aetherial.biographypublic:
This small, iron-like rocky construct floats silently before you, moving eerily through the air without any propulsion. Its strange, geometric shapes seem to pulse very softly, and between the sharp corners and flat pieces, a glowing center contains a solid, dark core surrounded by glowing, white, magical symbols.

Anachraenum Aetherials are small constructs about two feet in width and height that the Anachraenum uses for training. They are programmed with a very limited set of actions, such as stay, attack, and defend. They can be "defeated," but this merely shuts down their magical core, they can be safely picked up and reactivated later.

Animated Rune Tome.name: Animated Rune Tome

False Appearance.name: False Appearance
False Appearance.description: While the [[lookup @name]] remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal book.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

The [[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of its character sheet. It automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

Starry Wisp.name: Starry Wisp
Starry Wisp.description:
You launch a mote of light at one creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 Radiant damage, and until the end of your next turn, it emits Dim Light in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the &Reference[Invisible] condition.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

Ray of Frost.name: Ray of Frost
Ray of Frost.description:
A frigid beam of blue-white light streaks toward a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, it takes 1d8 Cold damage, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description: An imperceptible barrier of magical force protects you. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack, and you take no damage from @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMagicMissi]{Magic Missile}.

Fog Cloud.name: Fog Cloud
Fog Cloud.description:
You create a 20-foot-radius Sphere of fog centered on a point within range. The Sphere is &Reference[heavilyobscured]. It lasts for the duration or until a strong wind (such as one created by @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGustofWind]{Gust of Wind}) disperses it.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The fog's radius increases by 20 feet for each spell slot level above 1.

Faerie Fire.name: Faerie Fire
Faerie Fire.description:
Objects in a 20-foot Cube within range are outlined in blue, green, or violet light (your choice). Each creature in the Cube is also outlined if it fails a Dexterity saving throw. For the duration, objects and affected creatures shed &Reference[dimlight] in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the Invisible condition.

Attack rolls against an affected creature or object have Advantage if the attacker can see it.

Blur.name: Blur
Blur.description: Your body becomes blurred. For the duration, any creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you. An attacker is immune to this effect if it perceives you with &Reference[blindsight] or &Reference[truesight].

Darkness.name: Darkness
Darkness.description:
For the duration, magical &Reference[darkness] spreads from a point within range and fills a 15-foot-radius Sphere. Darkvision can't see through it, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it.

Alternatively, you cast the spell on an object that isn't being worn or carried, causing the Darkness to fill a 15-foot Emanation originating from that object. Covering that object with something opaque, such as a bowl or helm, blocks the Darkness.

If any of this spell's area overlaps with an area of Bright Light or Dim Light created by a spell of level 2 or lower, that other spell is dispelled.

Ray of Enfeeblement.name: Ray of Enfeeblement
Ray of Enfeeblement.description:
A beam of enervating energy shoots from you toward a creature within range. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a successful save, the target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes until the start of your next turn.

On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests for the duration. During that time, it also subtracts 1d8 from all its damage rolls. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success.

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.

Blink.name: Blink
Blink.description:
[[/r 1d6]]{Roll 1d6} at the end of each of your turns for the duration. On a roll of 4–6, you vanish from your current plane of existence and appear in the Ethereal Plane (the spell ends instantly if you are already on that plane). While on the Ethereal Plane, you can perceive the plane you left, which is cast in shades of gray, but you can't see anything there more than 60 feet away. You can affect and be affected only by other creatures on the Ethereal Plane, and creatures on the other plane can't perceive you unless they have a special ability that lets them perceive things on the Ethereal Plane.

You return to the other plane at the start of your next turn and when the spell ends if you are on the Ethereal Plane. You return to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of the space you left. If no unoccupied space is available within that range, you appear in the nearest unoccupied space.

Animated Rune Tome.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The Animated Rune Tome was once an ordinary spellbook stored within the Chamber of Agaseroes, but over time, since Agaseroes died, it has slowly absorbed increasing amounts of arcane magic, and now it has gained a semblance of life. At its core, it is just a book, made of paper with a leather cover.

Behavior

The Rune Tome doesn't have enough of a mind to think and is generally only able to flap around the library within the Chamber when disturbed, also attacking with its little paper teeth. It can cast spells from its pages, but the effort is very taxing, and every time it does, it seems to take a moment to flap wearily in the air before recovering.

Lore

The Animated Rune Tomes within the library are not numerous, but there are a few of them clustered around the bookshelves of magical knowledge. They contain a relatively large amount of arcane energy but are otherwise simple entities that came to "life" recently and have little connection to Agaseroes himself.
Animated Rune Tome.biographypublic:
Flapping in the air in front of you is a small, leather-bound book, its cover etched with intricate, glowing runes. As it flits through the air, the pages quietly rustle and twist, forming sharp little paper teeth.

[[lookup @name]] is a magical spellbook that has slowly absorbed arcane magic over the years. It is not a creature created by Agaseroes and seems to be a magical pest of sorts.

Radiant Ultra Drake.name: Radiant Ultra Drake

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes two attacks with its [[/item Claw]]{Claws} and one attack with its [[/item Bite]].

Blood Sense.name: Blood Sense
Blood Sense.description: The [[lookup @name]] has blindsight within 20 feet, but only for creatures missing any hit points. Additionally, it has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to detect or locate wounded creatures within 20 feet, even if they are hidden.

Final Blaze.name: Final Blaze
Final Blaze.description: The first time the [[lookup @name]] is reduced to 0 hit points, it instead is reduced to 1 hit point, and immediately takes a free turn. During this turn it is empowered, becoming able to take the &reference[dash] action for free, and gaining advantage on all attack rolls made.

Radiant Blast.name: Radiant Blast
Radiant Blast.description:
The [[lookup @name]] emits a powerful blast of radiant fire.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=pZM3lRzi5yVqtv2h]], each creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=pZM3lRzi5yVqtv2h]] feet of it.

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage.

Sudden Rush.name: Sudden Rush
Sudden Rush.description: The [[lookup @name]] moves up to 30 feet its speed and makes one [[/item Claws]]{Claw} attack.

Hyper-Aggressive.name: Hyper-Aggressive
Hyper-Aggressive.description: The [[lookup @name]] has advantage on Initiative rolls due to its hyper-aggressive nature.

Control Collar.name: Control Collar
Control Collar.descriptionprivate: This large leather and steel collar was once wrapped around the neck of a large, mutated drake. The magical engravings in it were used to control where the creature was allowed to go. It seems the magic is mostly burned out, and wouldn't be any use any longer.

Mantle of Radiance.name: Mantle of Radiance
Mantle of Radiance.description: The [[lookup @name]] blazes with radiant flames; as a result, it is protected from certain dangers and is resistant to cold, fire, and radiant damage. In addition, its burning form causes [[/damage average]] damage to any creature that ends its turn grappling or grappled by the drake.

Speed Burst.name: Speed Burst
Speed Burst.description: The [[lookup @name]] takes the &reference[disengage] action and moves up to its speed.

Slender Form.name: Slender Form
Slender Form.description: The long, slender form of the [[lookup @name]] allows it to squeeze through spaces like a medium sized creature. It still suffers all movement cost increases and penalties related to squeezing through a tight space.

Radiant Ultra Drake.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Drakes bear a striking resemblance to the Vile Dragon, with long, thin bodies, two fore-legs and no other limbs. They often have horns and frills, and maws lined with thin, razor sharp teeth.

Drakes are capable of flight, though they lack wings, indicating their capacity for flight comes from some other means, likely magic. The precise nature of this ability is not known.

Drakes are covered in robust scales which help protect their bodies from harm, though they rely more on their dexterity to evade attacks, rather than natural armor. This hide is similar to snake skin in texture and composition.

All drakes have intensely sharp eyesight and strong low-light vision.

The Radiant Ultra Drake displays an optimized physiology meant for speed, marked by streamlined musculature and tightly fitted, almost lustrous scales that glow along seams with magical light. Its body contains and channels residual blaze energy, resulting in the ever-present fissures visible beneath its hide. It looks like a normal drake in most every way except for its sleek scales and glowing eyes. The intense internal blaze grants the drake an ability to rapidly recover from injuries that would kill lesser creatures and strengthens its vital organs.

Behavior

The newness of these creatures precludes the development of academic knowledge of drake behavior, so little is known beyond what direct observation may provide.

That said, drakes quickly assert themselves as apex predators in any biome they inhabit, and are naturally territorial, attacking anything that dares to enter the territory they've claimed.

Drakes are intelligent, capable of complex reasoning, and coordination in groups, even with humanoid allies despite being incapable of speech. However, since drakes are territorial and extremely willful, training them is difficult, if not impossible. Though not social by nature, drakes can and will hunt and nest together, with all members of that nest bowing to the will of largest among them.

Infused with unnatural quickness and intelligence, this Ultra Drake is swift and aggressive, favoring hit and run tactics that leave its foes staggered and incapable to reacting before it's out of reach. Bursts of speed, enhanced evasive capability and strategic retreats make it adept at harrying its chosen prey until exhaustion or opportunity allows for a killing blow.

Lore

There is little known about Drakes, as they are not naturally occurring on Ember and only began appearing in recent years. To the wider world of academics, they appear to be a chimerical blend of snake and dragon with an unknown but possibly magical origin.

The truth about them is that they were created in secret by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn], grown in a hidden blood forge, their forms patterned after @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.v6lXjfETDkrt0J7E]{Zerranyss}, a powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.EhQnCUxkJyxOSbf7]{Vile Dragon}. They were made to serve as a resources for Mutagists and their experiments, forced to become test subjects for the mutagenic compounds their numerous underground labs produce.

The ultimate goal of the mutagists was to find serums and alchemical treatments that would enhance, transform, and empower the draks, with the expectation that any such discoveries would also be applicable to the Vile Dragon they were spawned from.

A singular triumph for the Mutagists, the Radiant Ultra Drake is the result of their first successful injecting of a human’s inherent blaze energies into a drake’s formidable frame. This integration has elevated the drake beyond even their wildest hoping: now not only stronger and almost impossible to kill, but faster and more calculating than any of its predecessors. Wholly unique, the Radiant Ultra Drake is the deadly apex of the Mutagist craft... for now.
Radiant Ultra Drake.biographypublic:
A sleek, menacing silhouette, this creature's silvery scales are slick and between them pulse radiant fissures of light in hues of blue, pink, and violet, illuminating the creature from within as if it carries caged lightning in its blood. Glowing eyes, unnaturally bright, emit thin wisps of multicolored smoke. Twin forelimbs, powerfully muscled, end in wicked claws, and its long horns sweep elegantly back from its head, the tips of them seemingly on fire.

This huge drake is dangerously enhanced by mutagenic serums infused with blaze residuum. It has a thick scaled hide, distinctive horns and eyes, and incredible speed. It is many measures more dangerous than its smaller kin, possessing resilience and cunning far greater than them.

Shade of Agaseros.name: Shade of Agaseros

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of its character sheet. It automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes two attacks: one with its [[/item Arcane Beam]] and one with [[/item Spellcasting]].

Arcane Echo.name: Arcane Echo
Arcane Echo.description:
Trigger: The [[lookup @name]] takes damage.

Response: The [[lookup @name]] unleashes a wave of residual energy. Each creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=Z4MhSb9f0Wyb6yp7]] feet of it makes a [[/save format=long]].

Failure: The creature takes [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: Half damage.

Manisfestation of Magic.name: Manisfestation of Magic
Manisfestation of Magic.description: [[lookup @name]] can cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMageArmor0]{Mage Armor} spell on itself at will, without requiring material components.

Fire Bolt.name: Fire Bolt
Fire Bolt.description:
You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or an object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell starts burning if it isn't being worn or carried.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d10 when you reach levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10).

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Minor Illusion.name: Minor Illusion
Minor Illusion.description:
You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Magic Missile.name: Magic Missile
Magic Missile.description:
You create three glowing darts of magical force. Each dart strikes a creature of your choice that you can see within range. A dart deals 1d4 + 1 Force damage to its target. The darts all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The spell creates one more dart for each spell slot level above 1.

[[2 + @item.level]]{Level [[lookup @item.level]] darts}

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description: An imperceptible barrier of magical force protects you. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack, and you take no damage from @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMagicMissi]{Magic Missile}.

Misty Step.name: Misty Step
Misty Step.description: Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

See Invisibility.name: See Invisibility
See Invisibility.description: For the duration, you see creatures and objects that have the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition as if they were visible, and you can see into the Ethereal Plane. Creatures and objects there appear ghostly.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Shade of Agaseros.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The Shade is not a real being; instead, it is a magical manifestation of the Chamber of Agaseroes. It has no true body and is made of arcane elemental energy. It can cast spells mimicking the great mage Agaseroes, but in reality, this creature is just a shadow of Agaseroes himself.

Behavior

The Shade of Agaseros is not a sentient entity, and it has no thoughts other than the ones programmed into it by Agaseros and the Chamber. It can discern threats and will attack those it considers the most dangerous or threatening, but overall, it cannot act independently. It cannot speak, but it can understand speech in a variety of languages, and it is usually tasked with protecting certain locations in the chamber or carrying out tasks to keep the Chamber active.

Lore

Agaseros created the Chamber as his personal library, laboratory, and zoo, where he collected creatures, studied the arcane, and tried to understand the cosmos. To help him achieve this, he also needed a number of mundane servants, that he called Shades. These beings were arcane constructs, made entirely of magic, that could carry out simple tasks. After his death, they remained active within the Chamber.
Shade of Agaseros.biographypublic:
Floating in front of you is a strange, arcane being. It has four arms and a mechanical brass body, but it seems to shimmer in and out of existence, with glowing purple runes floating above its head. Arcane fire glows within its hands, and what you could only call its head tilts to one side to regard you dispassionately.

The [[lookup @name]] is an arcane manifestation of the mage Agaseros. In essence, it is an elemental arcane ghost created by the Chamber. While it possesses arcane abilities and shares some physical similarities, it is also different and far less powerful than Agaseros once was.

Meri.name: Meri

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of her character sheet. She automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description:
Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range.

Weather Sensor. You create a Tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.

Bloom. You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.

Sensory Effect. You create a harmless sensory effect, such as falling leaves, spectral dancing fairies, a gentle breeze, the sound of an animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot Cube.

Fire Play. You light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a campfire.

Minor Illusion.name: Minor Illusion
Minor Illusion.description:
You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

Shillelagh.name: Shillelagh
Shillelagh.description:
A Club or Quarterstaff you are holding is imbued with nature's power. For the duration, you can use your spellcasting ability instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of melee attacks using that weapon, and the weapon's damage die becomes a d8. If the attack deals damage, it can be Force damage or the weapon's normal damage type (your choice).

The spell ends early if you cast it again or if you let go of the weapon.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage die changes when you reach levels 5 (d10), 11 (d12), and 17 (2d6).

Vicious Mockery.name: Vicious Mockery
Vicious Mockery.description:
You unleash a string of insults laced with subtle enchantments at one creature you can see or hear within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take 1d6 Psychic damage and have Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach levels 5 (2d6), 11 (3d6), and 17 (4d6).

Dissonant Whispers.name: Dissonant Whispers
Dissonant Whispers.description:
One creature of your choice that you can see within range hears a discordant melody in its mind. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 3d6 Psychic damage and must immediately use its Reaction, if available, to move as far away from you as it can, using the safest route. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 1.

Faerie Fire.name: Faerie Fire
Faerie Fire.description:
Objects in a 20-foot Cube within range are outlined in blue, green, or violet light (your choice). Each creature in the Cube is also outlined if it fails a Dexterity saving throw. For the duration, objects and affected creatures shed &Reference[dimlight] in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the Invisible condition.

Attack rolls against an affected creature or object have Advantage if the attacker can see it.

Healing Word.name: Healing Word
Healing Word.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains Hit Points equal to 2d4 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 1.

Mirror Image.name: Mirror Image
Mirror Image.description:
Three illusory duplicates of yourself appear in your space. Until the spell ends, the duplicates move with you and mimic your actions, shifting position so it's impossible to track which image is real.

Each time a creature hits you with an attack roll during the spell's duration, roll a [[/r (@flags.dnd-players-handbook.mirrorImages)d6kh1cs>2#Duplicate destroyed]]{d6 for each} of your remaining duplicates. If any of the d6s rolls a 3 or higher, one of the duplicates is hit instead of you, and the duplicate is destroyed. The duplicates otherwise ignore all other damage and effects. The spell ends when all three duplicates are destroyed.

A creature is unaffected by this spell if it has the &Reference[blinded apply=false] condition, &Reference[blindsight], or &Reference[truesight].

Misty Step.name: Misty Step
Misty Step.description: Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

Hypnotic Pattern.name: Hypnotic Pattern
Hypnotic Pattern.description:
You create a twisting pattern of colors in a 30-foot Cube within range. The pattern appears for a moment and vanishes. Each creature in the area who can see the pattern must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[charmed apply=false] condition for the duration. While Charmed, the creature has the &Reference[incapacitated apply=false] condition and a Speed of 0.

The spell ends for an affected creature if it takes any damage or if someone else uses an action to shake the creature out of its stupor.

Lightning Bolt.name: Lightning Bolt
Lightning Bolt.description:
A stroke of lightning forming a 100-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line blasts out from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the Line makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

Greater Invisibility.name: Greater Invisibility
Greater Invisibility.description: A creature you touch has the Invisible condition until the spell ends.

Flower Pop.name: Flower Pop
Flower Pop.description: As an action, [[lookup @name]] can polymorph into a flower. In flower form, she cannot take actions but may choose to revert to her normal form as a bonus action.

Shadow Stealth.name: Shadow Stealth
Shadow Stealth.description: While in dim light or darkness, [[lookup @name]] can take the &Reference[Hide] action as a bonus action.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes two attacks: one with her [[/item Thorn Whip]] and one with [[/item Spellcasting]].

Thorn Whip.name: Thorn Whip
Thorn Whip.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]], and the target must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or become &Reference[frightened] until the end of Meri’s next turn.

Pollen Burst.name: Pollen Burst
Pollen Burst.description: [[lookup @name]] releases a burst of magical pollen in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]]-foot radius sphere centered on herself. Each creature in that area must make a [[/save format=long]], taking [[/damage average]] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, affected creatures are &Reference[blinded] until the end of their next turn.

Shadow Shift.name: Shadow Shift
Shadow Shift.description: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

Dimension Door.name: Dimension Door
Dimension Door.description:
You teleport to a location within range. You arrive at exactly the spot desired. It can be a place you can see, one you can visualize, or one you can describe by stating distance and direction, such as "200 feet straight downward" or "300 feet upward to the northwest at a 45-degree angle."

You can also teleport one willing creature. The creature must be within 5 feet of you when you teleport, and it teleports to a space within 5 feet of your destination space.

If you, the other creature, or both would arrive in a space occupied by a creature or completely filled by one or more objects, you and any creature traveling with you each take 4d6 Force damage, and the teleportation fails.

Magic Resistance.name: Magic Resistance
Magic Resistance.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Meri.biographyprivate:
Meri is a relatively powerful Fae, and although she is not one of the Casia, she can effortlessly enter and exit the Chamber by casting the spell Dimension Door, using the spell to cross from the surface world to the realm of Primordis instantly. Meri revels in the art of deception, taking delight in leading others astray, sometimes for sheer amusement, other times as a playful test of wit.

Personality

Meri is not inherently malevolent, but her love for mischief knows no bounds; she often finds herself orchestrating harmless pranks or, on occasion, whimsically stirring chaos, which can lead to painful or even harmful results. Meri’s curiosity is also insatiable, and she approaches everything with childlike wonder, eager to explore new places and meet intriguing individuals.

Connections

Meri was once an advisor to Agaseroes, although the exact nature of their relationship is a mystery and she isn't willing to discuss it. She has some connection to the Silent Pack, a group of Casia from Primorids, but whether she allies with them or opposes them remains unknown.

Phrases

"You know what they say! When life gives you thorns, just dance among the roses!"
Meri.biographypublic:
A small, flower-like creature with large petals for wings floats before you. Her body seems to be made of rich, black velvet, creating a stunning contrast with the vibrant, glowing red and pink petals that spring from her head, chest, and back. As she moves, the petals bounce and shimmer softly, giving her a magical and even whimsical charm. Her eyes are a mesmerizing fiery red, sparkling with mischief and intelligence. As you watch her move, you notice a faint trail of glowing petals trailing behind her.

[[lookup @name]] is a small Fae from the mystical Inner Realm of Primordis. She was once an advisor to the renowned Anachraenum mage Agaseros, offering him arcane knowledge in exchange for undisclosed favors, often as elusive as her own nature. Meri was among a host of beings gathered and collected by Agaserors over the years, and while Agaserors himself is long dead, Meri often travels to the Chamber to tend to her garden.

Flameguard Crusader.name: Flameguard Crusader

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Their spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

The [[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of their character sheet. They automatically satisfy the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: If @UUID[Actor.8ICWlEOQZFXd1rJP.Item.OIKlOSzC1FfwRilO]{Divine Kindling} is active, the [[lookup @name]] makes two [[/item Greatsword]] or two [[/item Javelin]] attacks.

Divine Kindling.name: Divine Kindling
Divine Kindling.description:
As a bonus action, the [[lookup @name]] harnesses the divine power of the shard goddess Lumé to wreath their weapons in holy flame. For 1 hour, the [[lookup @name]]’s weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 fire damage (the @UUID[Actor.8ICWlEOQZFXd1rJP.Item.KkRkIIhD17sL5x30]{Greatsword} and @UUID[Actor.8ICWlEOQZFXd1rJP.Item.iGY92Nbz8QftIVCh]{Javelin} are enkindled by default with the extra damage).

While enkindled, the weapon counts as a magic weapon.

The enkindled weapons also shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. The effect ends early if the [[lookup @name]] dismisses it (no action required).

Foundry Note

The damage bonuses are found in the Global Bonuses section of the Special Traits tab.

Guidance.name: Guidance
Guidance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a skill. Until the spell ends, the creature adds 1d4 to any ability check using the chosen skill.

Sacred Flame.name: Sacred Flame
Sacred Flame.description:
Flame-like radiance descends on a creature that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d8 Radiant damage. The target gains no benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover for this save.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

Divine Smite.name: Divine Smite
Divine Smite.description:
The target takes an extra 2d8 Radiant damage from the attack. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is a Fiend or an Undead.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

Gentle Repose.name: Gentle Repose
Gentle Repose.description:
You touch a corpse or other remains. For the duration, the target is protected from decay and can't become Undead.

The spell also effectively extends the time limit on raising the target from the dead, since days spent under the influence of this spell don't count against the time limit of spells such as Raise Dead.

Shield of Faith.name: Shield of Faith
Shield of Faith.description: A shimmering field surrounds a creature of your choice within range, granting it a +2 bonus to AC for the duration.

Healing Word.name: Healing Word
Healing Word.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains Hit Points equal to 2d4 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 1.

Continual Flame.name: Continual Flame
Continual Flame.description: A flame springs from an object that you touch. The effect casts &Reference[brightlight] in a 20-foot radius and &Reference[dimlight] for an additional 20 feet. It looks like a regular flame, but it creates no heat and consumes no fuel. The flame can be covered or hidden but not smothered or quenched.

Lumek War Torch.name: Lumek War Torch
Lumek War Torch.descriptionprivate:
This large steel sconce can be worn on your back, and burns Torches as a lantern burns oil. A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet.

As a Bonus Action, you can remove the War Torch from your back, enabling the ability to attack with the Torch when you take the Attack action (using it as a Simple Melee weapon). On a hit, the target takes 1d4 Bludgeoning damage plus 1d2 Fire damage.

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Foundry Note

The Kindling 1d8 damage bonus applied to the Greatsword and Javelin's attack is deducted from this attack's damage total.

Torch.name: Torch
Torch.description: A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. When you take the Attack action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.

Fireborn.name: Fireborn
Fireborn.description:
You have resistance to fire damage.

If you start your turn submerged, you must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of your next turn. This penalty ends early if you are no longer submerged. If you remain submerged, you repeat the saving throw at the start of each of your turns.

Submerged. You are submerged if you are in water deep enough that you must swim or tread water to stay afloat.

Flameguard Crusader.biographyprivate:
[[lookup @name]]s are experienced soldiers who pledge their blades to the service of the shard goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}, and the Flame Warden endows their weapons with divine flame in return. In addition to their martial prowess, [[lookup @name]]s are talented adherents of Lumé's tenets, and are capable divine spellcasters in their own right. As their name suggests, these Crusaders are members of @UUID[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]{Luna Karrowrath's} Flameguard, and occupy the higher ranks of this illustrious corps of undead slayers.

Most [[lookup @name]] warriors are Fej, but other ancestries have been known to pledge their blades to Lumé's cause. As they are a broader character type, each individual [[lookup @name]] will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

While there is no absolute personality trait associated with being a [[lookup @name]], these accomplished warriors tend to be brash, youthful in spirit, and perpetually eager to prove their mettle in combat with the undead. Like most members of the Flameguard, [[lookup @name]]s share a strong camaraderie and esprit de corps amongst each other. And while their loyalty is generally hard-won, their devotion to their allies is nigh unshakable.

Connections

[[lookup @name]]s are veteran members of the world-famous Flameguard, Luna Karrowrath's diverse company of righteous undead slayers who courageously pledge their blades and very lives to Lumé, the Flame Warden. They are the sworn enemies of the Moiran @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Blood Barons} and their evil ilk, and have recently established a foothold in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} in search of a furtive undead menace that exerts is terrible unseen influence over the Arctus Plateau.
Flameguard Crusader.biographypublic:
This armor-clad Fej warrior wears the scarlet and coral-hued garb of the fire-worshipping Lumek, and the greatsword at their side is marked with chaotic scorches of divine flame. An unmistakable air of experience and grit clings to this hardened solider, as if they've seen it all; and a torch on their back wreathes the area in the amber glow of firelight.

[[lookup @name]]s are experienced Lumek warriors who dedicate their lives to ridding Ember of the scourge of undeath. Blessed by the divine magic of the shard goddess Lumé, whom they serve as intrepid frontline paladins in the eponymous Flameguard, these Crusaders are known for their unflappable grit in the face of danger, an unrivaled sense of loyalty, and the holy conflagrations of their flame-shrouded weapons.

Brynna Verocorrt.name: Brynna Verocorrt

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes three attacks, using @UUID[.CjGEA68OpB1zPU0H] or @UUID[.VeLwk0u9lcUuNQj6] in any combination. These attacks may benefit from @UUID[Actor.UVncdPqmzpZLwGvK.Item.SkUIK7flMOemXmvk]{Limblock Toxin}.

Cunning Action.name: Cunning Action
Cunning Action.description: [[lookup @name]] takes the &Reference[Dash apply=false], the &Reference[Disengage apply=false], or &Reference[Hide apply=false] action.

Rope.name: Rope
Rope.description:
As a Utilize action, you can tie a knot with Rope if you succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The Rope can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check.

You can bind an unwilling creature with the Rope only if the creature has the &Reference[Grappled], &Reference[Incapacitated], or &Reference[Restrained] condition. If the creature's legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Rope requires the creature to make a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check as an action.

Nightstep.name: Nightstep
Nightstep.description: [[lookup @name]] can use her bonus action to teleport up to 20 feet in any direction to a point she can see. She must be in dim light or darkness, and the destination must be unoccupied, and also in dim light or darkness.

Limblock Toxin.name: Limblock Toxin
Limblock Toxin.description:
[[lookup @name]]'s weapons are coated in a dangerous poison. Each time the successfully damage a creature with either a dagger stab or thrown knife that creature must succeed on a [[/save extended format=long]].

Failure: Suffer the &reference[restrained] condition until the start of their next turn as their muscles seize up.

Success: The target is unaffected and becomes immune to the Limblock Toxin for 1 hour.

Evasion.name: Evasion
Evasion.description: If [[lookup @name]] is subjected to an effect that allows her to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, she instead takes no damage if she succeeds on the save and only half damage if she fails. Brynna can't use this trait if she has the Incapacitated condition.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: Once on each of its turns, when [[lookup @name]] hits a target with a melee weapon attack, the target takes an extra [[/damage average]] if [[lookup @name]] has advantage on the attack roll or if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t incapacitated, and [[lookup @name]] doesn’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.

Brynna Verocorrt.biographyprivate:
Though they are a small part of the Trading House, Wandern's cadre of assassins are well equipped, well trained, and very highly paid so as to guarantee their ongoing loyalty.

Anatomy

House Wandren hires any capable warriors with skill in stealth, infiltration. As a result, all of Wandren's assassins are fast, agile, and capable of getting into nearly any location unseen.

Behavior

Wandren's assassins favor discretion and speed over direct confrontation or open combat. They prefer to slip a blade between their target's ribs from the shadows, or slit the throats of sleeping victims in the dead of night.

Lore

The assassins found in House Wandred all hold positions of minor influence and modest respect. Their deadliness and the fact their loyalty needs to be maintained at all times means they occupy a higher position within the house's overall hierarchy, and enjoy more leeway than rank and file guards and enforcers.
Brynna Verocorrt.biographypublic:
A regal blonde human woman stands before you, wrapped in shadowy leather armor and layers of find cloth dyed in rich, dark colors. Golden metal accents and jewelry glint across their armor, belt, shoulders, and wrists but no insignia or mark gives away their allegiance. Her movement is soundless, and precise, suggesting careful training and deadly intent. Yet for the stealthy bearing she has a magnetic charisma about her.

[[lookup @name]] is a member of the Wandren Trading House who specializes in recruiting and kidnapping. As one of Wandren's elite Tracers, she is both highly paid and highly dangerous. She is known within the organization for her ability to persuade, manipulate and coerce others with a complete lack of mercy.

Vitt Wandren.name: Vitt Wandren
Vitt Wandren.biographypublic:
Though they have an easy smile and immediately extend a hand in greeting, there is a glint in the eyes of the Ordani in front of you, as if they know exactly what you're worth and will take it from you as soon as they are given a chance.

Vitt Wandren has long used their loose association with House Wandren to throw his weight around, corralling what would have otherwise been a group of small petty criminals into an organized protection racket known as the Beacon Brigade. While they enjoy feeling as if they are one of the crew, they rule the group tightly and enjoy the fruits of their labor, though they have dreams of one day moving all the way up into the Marlstone Manor.

Wandren Patroller.name: Wandren Patroller

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The patroller makes two melee attacks with their [[/item Hollowed Dagger]]{Dagger}.

Paralyzing Poison.name: Paralyzing Poison
Paralyzing Poison.description: Often placed on arrows and in traps, this poison paralyzes its target for 1 minute.

Slowing Serum.name: Slowing Serum
Slowing Serum.description: This serum halves the speed of any creature affected by it for 10 minutes.

Choking Fog Dust.name: Choking Fog Dust
Choking Fog Dust.description:
This weaponized version of Dust of Sneezing and Choking is usually packaged in a throwing bag that allows the carrier to throw it up to 30 feet away, where it activates on landing, filling a 10 foot cube surrounding it with a thick fog that functions as magical darkness for 1 minute and dim light for an additional 10 minutes.

In addition, the fog chokes anyone within range - any creature within the fog that needs to breathe must succeed on a [[/save 17 constitution]] saving throw or they begin to violently cough and suffocate, becoming incapacitated for 1 minute until the dust clears. A creature may retry this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Pack Tactics.name: Pack Tactics
Pack Tactics.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

Hollowed Dagger.name: Hollowed Dagger
Hollowed Dagger.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Often made of animal bone, this sharp dagger has a hollowed core, allowing it to carry three uses of a poison or potion without the substance needing to be reapplied.

Wandren Patroller.biographyprivate:
Though primarily found guarding important House Wandren properties, patrollers can be found anywhere that the house feels there might be a credible but low-level threat to its interests. Their reliance on items as part of their strength makes them easy to deploy — and to walk away from — though patrollers who show promise can sometimes advance as they become more powerful and dangerous.

Anatomy

Wandren Patrollers aren't much different than the average Ordani commoner — though they've generally been some training in basic fighting skills, their real power comes from the poisons and throwing dust they have at their disposal, which can quickly even the playing field between them and their targets.

Behavior

Patrollers often work in pairs, with each half carrying a slightly different poison in order to best foes who may have resistance to a particular form of damage. If a patroller is seen on their own, often they are paired with a Wandren Watcher, who provides sentry duty and can light up areas where enemies might be hiding.

Lore

While several of the trading houses have guards or staff that protect their interests, House Wandren's patrollers have become increasingly unmanaged as the house continues to grab power and align with thieves in Ordain. They can now be found as low-level muscle within a few different small criminal enterprises in the city, using their abilities to shake down storeowners for money or provide support for major thefts.
Wandren Patroller.biographypublic:
