Though they try to look as if they are casually walking around street corners and leaning against random doors, these Ordani keep a close eye on the world around them, ready to draw the knives and poisons on their belts at a moment's notice.

House Wandren's patrollers keep an eye on the interests of the house — guarding shipments, watching storehouses, and providing security at important buildings. What they lack in strength or training is usually made up for by the poisons, oils, and bags of choking dust given to them by House Wandren, which they can use to subdue anyone who gets in their way.

Wandren Tracer.name: Wandren Tracer

Evasion.name: Evasion
Evasion.description: If the [[lookup @name]] is subjected to an effect that allows them to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, they instead take no damage if they succeed on the save and only half damage if they fail. They can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes three attacks, using @UUID[.CjGEA68OpB1zPU0H] or @UUID[.VeLwk0u9lcUuNQj6] in any combination. These attacks may benefit from @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.sbuElZ85CrfTRADH].

Success: The target is unaffected and becomes immune to the Limblock Toxin for 1 hour.

Nightstep.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] can use their bonus action to teleport up to 20 feet in any direction to a point they can see. They must be in dim light or darkness, and the destination must be unoccupied, and also in dim light or darkness.

Sneak Attack.description: Once on each of its turns, when the [[lookup @name]] hits a target with a melee weapon attack, the target takes an extra [[/damage average]] if the [[lookup @name]] has advantage on the attack roll or if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t incapacitated, and the [[lookup @name]] doesn’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.

Anatomy

House Wandren hires any capable warriors with skill in stealth, infiltration. As a result, all of Wandren's assassins are fast, agile, and capable of getting into nearly any location unseen.

Behavior

Wandren's assassins favor discretion and speed over direct confrontation or open combat. They prefer to slip a blade between their target's ribs from the shadows, or slit the throats of sleeping victims in the dead of night.

Lore

The assassins found in House Wandred all hold positions of minor influence and modest respect. Their deadliness and the fact their loyalty needs to be maintained at all times means they occupy a higher position within the house's overall hierarchy, and enjoy more leeway than rank and file guards and enforcers.
Wandren Tracer.biographypublic:
A masked figure stands before you, wrapped in shadowy leather armor layered neatly over a deep purple tunic and matching pants. Subtle golden metal accents glint at their belt, shoulders, and wrists but no insignia or mark gives away their allegiance. Their face is hidden behind a smooth, featureless mask, revealing nothing of their identity, just the cold, focused stare of a killer. Their movement is soundless, and precise, suggesting careful training and deadly intent.

The [[lookup @name]] is a contract killer in service to the Wandren Trading House. As the unseen hand of the Wandren elite, they are both highly paid and highly dangerous, eliminating threats quietly and without question. Within the organization they are prized for their discretion, relentless skill, and complete lack of mercy.

Wandren Watcher.name: Wandren Watcher

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The watcher makes two attacks, using the [[/item Shortsword]] and [[/item Longbow]] in any combination.

Spotlight Shot.name: Spotlight Shot
Spotlight Shot.description:
Once on each of its turns, when the watcher makes a [[/item Longbow]] attack, it can forgo targeting a creature and instead choose a point within the weapon’s range. The arrow creates a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=9B5HuosDSNBcwUAJ]]-foot emanation of blinding light that lasts for [[lookup @duration.value activity=9B5HuosDSNBcwUAJ]] [[lookup @duration.units activity=9B5HuosDSNBcwUAJ]].

Constitution Saving Throw: [[/save format=long]], each creature in the emanation.

Failure: The creature has the &Reference[blinded] condition until the end of its next turn.

A creature that is hidden in the emanation must succeed on a [[/check format=long]] with disadvantage to remain hidden. While the light lasts, Stealth checks made in the emanation are made with disadvantage.

Wandren Watcher.biographyprivate:
Though anyone who is willing and loyal can be a Wandren Patroller, Wandren Watchers are promoted and trained because they show particular promise, either in their ability to observe, level of focus and dedication to their task, or skill with a bow and arrow, which is the Watcher's primary weapon. They are trained to keep an eye out for interlopers in Wandren affairs as to use their spotlight arrows to highlight those who may be causing trouble and give Wandren Patrollers a target on the ground.

Anatomy

Wandren Watchers are generally humans, but can be drawn from any ancestry. They tend to come from Wandren Patrollers that are either exceptionally observant or have the dexterity to excel with the bow and arrow.

Behavior

Watchers spend their time, as their names indicate, watching. Often stationed on buildings or roofs, they are given unofficial oversight of a group of Patrollers whose routes they can see from their position - if anything happens to those Patrollers, they are often made to pay for it, either financially or physically, so they try their best to keep their areas clear and safe.

Lore

As House Wandren has expanded its criminal enterprises, it has needed to have lookouts that pay attention to its operations and ensure that they are progressing without interference. When noticed, the number of Watchers that can be found across the city working for Wandren sometimes draws attention and concern, and they are instructed to do as much as they can to move stealthily and downplay their association with House Wandren when needed.
Wandren Watcher.biographypublic:
These sharp-eyed Ordani sentries are most often found on rooftops or balconies, scanning the streets below to spot dangers before anyone else knows they're there

Though they go by a few different names in Ordain, depending on which group they currently work for or represent, these lookouts all have similar training and gear - a mark of their general association with Trading House Wandren.

Kaftor Brenk.name: Kaftor Brenk

Antitoxin.name: Antitoxin
Antitoxin.description: A creature that drinks this vial of liquid gains advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour. It confers no benefit to undead or constructs.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a 5th level spellcaster. Their spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of their character sheet. They automatically satisfy the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes two attacks which can be a [[/item .sQ966YV5oMsRE6ln]] or [[/item .dxWWIcMBtQkqGOwX]] attack in any order.

Draining Swipe.name: Draining Swipe
Draining Swipe.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]], healing [[lookup @name]] for the amount of damage done.

Fatal Contingency.name: Fatal Contingency
Fatal Contingency.description:
When [[lookup @name]] dies, suspended magic is unleashed that causes their mouth and throat to erupt with a powerful corrosive, eating away both and leaving nothing behind but a rancid slurry of blood and flesh.

The damage is precise and intended to make it impossible to question the corpse after defeat.

Inject Blaze.name: Inject Blaze
Inject Blaze.description:
[[lookup @name]] grabs a preloaded syrette of a glowing alchemical solution, and injects it into his arm. It has the following effects:

  • Kaftor becomes immune to the &reference[frightened] condition until the end of his next turn.

  • Kaftor gains the effects of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplHaste00000]{Haste} spell for one round, ignoring the negative effects related to the spell ending.

He has four doses on his person. Any unconsumed doses looted from his body should be granted as @UUID[Item.GSCmA5aRvggTLWtV]{Blazing Distillation}.

False Ember Blaze.name: False Ember Blaze
False Ember Blaze.description:
Thanks to extensive experimentation, [[lookup @name]] has successfully given themselves a form of the Human Ember Blaze feature. When he is reduced to 0 hit points he experiences a burst of radiant energy, regains 1 hit point, and immediately takes a turn, interrupting the next combatant in combat order.

Until that turn his movement speed is increased by +10 feet and he has advantage on any weapon or spell attack rolls he makes. This triggers before his @UUID[Actor.8jqTLAW121XrQiTN.Item.6nHS0vPupbFPe1yc]{Fatal Contingency} feature does.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

Ray of Sickness.name: Ray of Sickness
Ray of Sickness.description:
You shoot a greenish ray at a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 Poison damage and has the &Reference[poisoned] condition until the end of your next turn.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

Ray of Enfeeblement.name: Ray of Enfeeblement
Ray of Enfeeblement.description:
A beam of enervating energy shoots from you toward a creature within range. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a successful save, the target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes until the start of your next turn.

On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests for the duration. During that time, it also subtracts 1d8 from all its damage rolls. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success.

Vampiric Touch.name: Vampiric Touch
Vampiric Touch.description:
The touch of your shadow-wreathed hand can siphon life force from others to heal your wounds. Make a melee spell attack against one creature within reach. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 Necrotic damage, and you regain Hit Points equal to half the amount of Necrotic damage dealt.

Until the spell ends, you can make the attack again on each of your turns as a Magic action, targeting the same creature or a different one.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

Kaftor Brenk.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Mutagist Excisors possess a wiry, muscular build hardened by their rigorous and dangerous arcane practices. Their bare arms, always visible, serve as living grimoires—etched and enchanted with intricate, glowing green tattoos that heighten their spellcasting and serve as arcane conduits. Their blood often carries faint traces of reagents, as they often enhance their bodies with alchemical solutions.

Behavior

Excisors are cold, analytical, and frighteningly methodical, treating every living creature as little more than raw material for their magical experiments. In combat, Excisors are brutal and proactive, hurling spells that wither flesh, sap vitality, and ignite the blood of living foes. Their obsessions leave them largely indifferent to suffering or morality.

Lore

Excisors are recognized internally as some of the most feared and dangerous members of the order, where they are afforded greater freedom to pursue experiments and carry out rituals so long as it feeds into the goals of the Mutagists as a whole. They earned their name for their affinity to "excise" life, both metaphorically and literally, with spells that rot tissue and siphon blood, pulling out valuable magical or elemental qualities in the process. Wherever they go is often stricken with disappearances, strange blights, and the appearance of worrying magical energies.
Kaftor Brenk.biographypublic:
This Fej man's bare, muscular arms are inscribed with elaborate, glowing green tattoos and fissures that glow with green light. The markings extend up their neck to across their face and bald head and pulse like a heartbeat. Unmasked, his face bears a permanent, cruel sneer.

The [[lookup @name]] is a ruthless, spellcasting ritualist in charge of the Mutagist lab under Ordain. His interest in experimental bio-magic, alchemy, and necromancy with flesh-withering spells inspire fear among all who witness their grim magic.

Mutagist Excisor.name: Mutagist Excisor

Acid (vial).name: Acid (vial)
Acid (vial).description: As an action, you can splash the contents of this vial onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw the vial up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the acid as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 acid damage.

Antitoxin.name: Antitoxin
Antitoxin.description: A creature that drinks this vial of liquid gains advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour. It confers no benefit to undead or constructs.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name lowercase]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Their spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

The [[lookup @name lowercase]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of their character sheet. They automatically satisfy the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] makes two [[/item .sQ966YV5oMsRE6ln]] attacks.

Fatal Contingency.name: Fatal Contingency
Fatal Contingency.description:
When [[lookup @name]] dies, suspended magic is unleashed that causes their mouth and throat to erupt with a powerful corrosive, eating away both and leaving nothing behind but a rancid slurry of blood and flesh.

The damage is precise and intended to make it impossible to question the corpse after defeat.

Vampiric Touch.name: Vampiric Touch
Vampiric Touch.description:
The touch of your shadow-wreathed hand can siphon life force from others to heal your wounds. Make a melee spell attack against one creature within reach. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 Necrotic damage, and you regain Hit Points equal to half the amount of Necrotic damage dealt.

Until the spell ends, you can make the attack again on each of your turns as a Magic action, targeting the same creature or a different one.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

Ray of Enfeeblement.name: Ray of Enfeeblement
Ray of Enfeeblement.description:
A beam of enervating energy shoots from you toward a creature within range. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a successful save, the target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes until the start of your next turn.

On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests for the duration. During that time, it also subtracts 1d8 from all its damage rolls. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

Mutagist Excisor.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Mutagist Excisors possess a wiry, muscular build hardened by their rigorous and dangerous arcane practices. Their bare arms, always visible, serve as living grimoires—etched and enchanted with intricate, glowing green tattoos that heighten their spellcasting and serve as arcane conduits. Their blood often carries faint traces of reagents, as they often enhance their bodies with alchemical solutions.

Behavior

Excisors are cold, analytical, and frighteningly methodical, treating every living creature as little more than raw material for their magical experiments. In combat, Excisors are brutal and proactive, hurling spells that wither flesh, sap vitality, and ignite the blood of living foes. Their obsessions leave them largely indifferent to suffering or morality.

Lore

Excisors are recognized internally as some of the most feared and dangerous members of the order, where they are afforded greater freedom to pursue experiments and carry out rituals so long as it feeds into the goals of the Mutagists as a whole. They earned their name for their affinity to "excise" life, both metaphorically and literally, with spells that rot tissue and siphon blood, pulling out valuable magical or elemental qualities in the process. Wherever they go is often stricken with disappearances, strange blights, and the appearance of worrying magical energies.
Mutagist Excisor.biographypublic:
Clad in a bloodstained vest under a leather apron, this figure's bare, muscular arms are inscribed with elaborate, glowing green tattoos that pulse and flicker with eerie light and their hands flickers with dark energy. Their face is obscured by a mask and spectacles, though their eyes broadcast a clear contempt for anyone they set on. A palpable sense of dread surrounds them, and the air prickles with the latent magical energy.

The [[lookup @name]] is a ruthless, spellcasting ritualist whose interest in experimental necromancy with flesh-withering spells inspire fear among all who witness their grim magic.

Mutagist Grenadier.name: Mutagist Grenadier

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes two attacks with its melee weapon.

Throw Gas Bomb.name: Throw Gas Bomb
Throw Gas Bomb.description:
The [[lookup @name]] throws a grenade filled with alchemical compounds at a point it can see within [[lookup @range.value activity=dnd5eactivity100]] feet of itself, creating a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity100]]-foot-radius cloud of blinding, choking gas.

At the start of a creature’s turn while it is in the cloud, it must make the following saving throw.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12.

Failure: The creature has the &Reference[blinded] and &Reference[poisoned] conditions until the start of its next turn. These conditions end early if the creature leaves the cloud.

[[lookup @name]] is unaffected by the gas.

Throw Fire Grenade.name: Throw Fire Grenade
Throw Fire Grenade.description:
The [[lookup @name]] throws a grenade filled with alchemical compounds at a point it can see within [[lookup @range.value activity=dnd5eactivity100]] feet of itself. Each creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity100]] feet of the grenade’s impact must make the following saving throw:

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity100]].

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: Half damage.

Fatal Contingency.name: Fatal Contingency
Fatal Contingency.description:
When the [[lookup @name lowercase]] dies, suspended magic is unleashed that causes their mouth and throat to erupt with a powerful corrosive, eating away both and leaving nothing behind but a rancid slurry of blood and flesh.

The damage is precise and intended to make it impossible to question the corpse after defeat.

Mutagist Grenadier.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

[[lookup @name]] are typically disgraced alchemists shunned for their unethical and cruel practices. They are protected under layers of leather and chain, and don complicated gas masks to keep themselves safe from the worst effects of their chemicals.

Behavior

Loving nothing more than to test their creations on any victims that cross their paths, these maniacs gleefully hurl their handmade bombs and grenades where the explosions will have the greatest effect. Outside of combat they are consumed with tuning and perfecting their chemical designs, creating new compounds to test, and devising even more dangerous ways to maim and kill.

Lore

[[lookup @name]] are ranged shock troops used in defensive and offensive actions. They are not organized or trained, and are given unsettling leeway in how they prepare and deploy their various chemical weapons.
Mutagist Grenadier.biographypublic:
Clad in sturdy chainmail and heavy metal pauldrons, this figure moves with surprising purpose for their bulk. Thick bands of chain and bandoliers loaded with volatile chemicals clink and clatter against their body as they go. Their face and eyes are concealed by a reinforced gas mask meant to protect them from their own tools.

The [[lookup @name]] serve the Mutagists as dangerous shock troops. Armored to survive their own devastating explosions, they wade into the thickest parts of battle, tossing grenades that fill the air with choking gas and shrapnel. Their job is simple: break the enemy, cause confusion, and leave a trail of agony in their wake.

Ordani.name: Ordani

Exceptional Taste.name: Exceptional Taste
Exceptional Taste.description: Your attire is a more powerful a tool in your handling of social situations than any blade or spell. When you are wearing clean clothing instead of armor you add +2 Boons to any Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation check.

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Dress Clothing.name: Dress Clothing
Dress Clothing.descriptionpublic: A regal set of fine vestments fit for attending celebrations and high society functions, includes an overcoat or dress, kerchief or necktie, a fine shirt or corset, a vest or bodice, trousers or petticoat, belt or braces, stockings and fine shoes.

Stiletto.name: Stiletto
Stiletto.descriptionpublic: Thin, tapered, and made for piercing, the stiletto is a killer’s weapon — designed to slide between ribs or gaps in armor and leave barely a trace.

Book.name: Book
Book.descriptionpublic: A wood-covered book bound in cloth or leather.

Pen.name: Pen
Pen.descriptionpublic: A common writing implement used by scribes, allows for a variety of tips to be interchanged for different stroke styles.

Lantern.name: Lantern
Lantern.descriptionpublic: An oil-burning or magically illuminated lantern that sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius.

Diplomacy Novice.name: Diplomacy Novice
Diplomacy Novice.description:
You know the basics of debate and how to use rhetorical devices to make your arguments more convincing. You gain the Novice rank in the Diplomacy skill and are no longer considered Untrained in that skill.

You know how to leverage emotion in your words to inspire others or sway their opinions. You can make a convincing argument, and you can generally steer others to agree with your point of view.

Ordani.biographyprivate:
Personality

The Ordani are laid back, and enjoy the fine things in life. They believe that everyone is entitled to being comfortable and happy, and that everyone should strive toward that goal. They are not martial and possess few martial traits because the plateau they have inhabited for generations is largely peaceful and serene.

Connections

The Ordani have a close relationship with the Arcturians of the plateau, who provide them food, textiles, and more. The large metropolis the Ordani occupy in term drives trade that benefits their neighbors in the Plateau.

Phrases

"Hail, stranger!"

"There is nothing finer in life than a cool drink on a warm day."
Ordani.biographypublic: @ref[name] are the varied and stylish occupants of the grand city of Ordain, they are renowned for their fine clothing and easy-going outlooks.
Ordani.biographyappearance: This person is stylishly dressed in layers of bright cloth with intricate patterns and differing weights, creating a lavish ensemble of texture and color. Their garb is accented with silvers and golds, and minor gems which glitter in the light, making them appear all the more dazzling.

Ordani Ruffian.name: Ordani Ruffian

Exceptional Taste.name: Exceptional Taste
Exceptional Taste.description: Your attire is a more powerful a tool in your handling of social situations than any blade or spell. When you are wearing clean clothing instead of armor you may roll and add a 1d4 to any Deception, Persuasion, or Intimidation skill check.

Brazen.name: Brazen
Brazen.description: The [[lookup @name]] is emboldened by its allies. As long as its side has the numerical advantage over its enemies in a battle, the [[lookup @name]] has advantage on any checks to resist being frightened and other effects that would result in fleeing from combat.

Ordani Ruffian.biographyprivate:
Personality

The Ordani are laid back, and joy the fine things in life. They believe that everyone is entitled to being comfortable and happy, and that everyone should strive toward that goal. They are not martial and possess few martial traits because the plateau they have inhabited for generations is largely peaceful and serene.

Connections

The Ordani have a close relationship with the Arcturians of the plateau, who provide them food, textiles, and more. The large metropolis the Ordani occupy in term drives trade that benefits their neighbors in the Plateau.
Ordani Ruffian.biographypublic:
Lightly armed and armored, this person looks a bit tougher, and a bit meaner than average Ordani cityfolk, and a bit more willing to do what's necessary to get what they want. While they lack the finery of the city's upper echelons, they are still stylishly dressed for one of the city's rogue's gallery.

[[lookup @name]] are rough handed, mean spirited folk that roam the streets of Ordain looking for trouble. They give the average Ordani citizen a bad name, but will never apologize for it.

Toothbreaker Scaletamer.name: Toothbreaker Scaletamer

Gang Grappler.name: Gang Grappler
Gang Grappler.description: The [[lookup @name]] has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature that is Grappled by it or one of its allies within 5 feet.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes two attacks, using [[/item .qQkoV8hc4wGRjsiC]] and [[/item .G3LS15ybcX1hTzJz]] in any combination.

Command Scalemaw.name: Command Scalemaw
Command Scalemaw.description:
The [[lookup @name]] speaks a command in Wyrdic to a Scalemaw within 20 feet that can hear it, directing the creature to attack a specific target.

The Scalemaw gains Advantage to the first attack it makes against that target until the end of its next turn.

Toothbreaker Security Key.name: Toothbreaker Security Key
Toothbreaker Security Key.descriptionprivate: A rusted key which unlocks the security doors at the entrance of the Toothbreaker Hideout.

Toothbreaker Scaletamer.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Toothbreaker Scaletamers may hail from any humanoid ancestry, although the majority are Human. To thrive within the gang's competitive environment requires strength and toughness, which are valued in prospective recruits above other attributes by Raster's ringleaders. Consequently the most common non-human ancestries among the gang are Kivahr, Cor'ak, and Drakon.

Behavior

Most Toothbreakers are not Waerds, but cultural traditions of the Waerds run strong throughout the gang. Raster Thorn runs the operation according to a clearly regimented set of rules and expectations that emphasizes tactical discipline and unflinching strength.

Many of the Toothbreakers were cast-offs or criminals who had no secure home, and Raster's oversight has created a place where they feel belonging and revel in their own power. The Toothbreakers are fiercely loyal and will die for each other and follow Raster's commands without question.

Toothbreaker Scaletamers, in particular, are rarely separated from the Scalemaws that they attend to. They have trained the beasts to recognize and follow a set of Wyrdic commands that only they have mastered.

Lore

The Toothbreakers were created six years ago after Raster Thorn arrived in Ordain. Originally they operated throughout the city, but in the past years Raster has tightened the scope of his operation to focus specifically on the Concourse and the adjacent waterfront distrinct. Their territory is limited in size, but ironclad in their control. The Toothbreakers have no rivals to speak of and run roughshod over any attempt by the Veiled Chain to restrict or combat their operations in the Concourse.
Toothbreaker Scaletamer.biographypublic:
The Toothbreaker before you has an ominous visage, heightened by the incorporation of bleached bone elements into their banded leather armor. They wear a fanged creature skull as a headpiece, and sections of their armor gleam with the cured leather of scaled hide. This imposing figure exudes a commanding presence, and you sense that they might hold higher station among the gang's hierarchy.

Toothbreaker Scaletamers are specialized ringleaders of Raster Thorn's lawless gang. Scaletamers are Toothbreakers who have risen through the ranks to earn the privilege to handle the domesticated fanged creatures which the gang breeds and trains to be their companions and protectors. Like all Toothbreakers, they are fiercely loyal to the group and are eager to bring violence against those who stand in their way.

Vespian Hydral.name: Vespian Hydral

Active Heads.name: Active Heads
Active Heads.description:
The Vespian Hydral begins with six active heads. Reduce this tracker by 1 whenever a head becomes incapacitated, and increase it by 1 when that head recovers. This tracker shows how many heads can be used as origins and how many count for Multiattack and Regeneration.

Foundry Note

Place one Vespian Hydral token and five Vespian Hydral Head tokens on the map. Only the main Vespian Hydral belongs in the combat tracker. Head tokens are positioning proxies only and don’t have separate turns, hit points, actions, reactions, or recharge resources.

Fire Vulnerability.name: Fire Vulnerability
Fire Vulnerability.description: The Vespian Hydral takes extra fire damage, as it is magically vulnerable to this element.

Keen Senses.name: Keen Senses
Keen Senses.description: The Vespian Hydral has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or smell.

Regeneration.name: Regeneration
Regeneration.description:
At the start of the Vespian Hydral’s turn, it regains 7 (2d6) hit points for each active head.

If it has taken fire damage since the end of its last turn, it instead regains 3 (1d6) hit points for each active head.

Resolve this trait once at the start of the Hydral’s turn.

Serpentine Movement.name: Serpentine Movement
Serpentine Movement.description:
The Vespian Hydral moves its main token up to its Speed. During this movement, or immediately before or after it, up to three active heads can each reposition up to 30 feet. Each head must end this movement within 60 feet of the main token.

Head repositioning is part of the Hydral’s movement and doesn’t create separate turns, opportunity attacks, or reactions.

Shared Health & Properties.name: Shared Health & Properties
Shared Health & Properties.description:
The Vespian Hydral is a single creature represented by multiple head tokens. All heads share one pool of hit points, and any damage dealt to a head token is dealt to the Hydral.

The Hydral has one action and one reaction each round, shared by all its heads. Roll recharge and resolve turn-start traits once at the start of the Hydral’s turn, not once per head.

The GM can choose any active head token as the origin for the Hydral’s attacks and effects.

If a head takes 20 or more damage from a single attack, that head is incapacitated until the end of the Hydral’s next turn. While incapacitated, that head can’t be used as the origin for the Hydral’s attacks or effects and doesn’t count as an active head for [[/item Multiattack]] or [[/item Regeneration]].

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The Vespian Hydral's heads make a number of [[/item Arcane Bite]] attacks equal to its number of active heads (maximum 3). It can replace one Arcane Bite attack with [[/item Steam Breath]] or [[/item Whirlpool]], if available.

Steam Breath.name: Steam Breath
Steam Breath.description:
The Vespian Hydral exhales a stream of boiling steam in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=KHmr2ve3oEl9H8bj]]-foot line that is [[lookup @target.template.width activity=KHmr2ve3oEl9H8bj]] feet wide.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=KHmr2ve3oEl9H8bj]], each creature in the line.

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: Half damage.

Whirlpool.name: Whirlpool
Whirlpool.description:
The Vespian Hydral creates a swirling vortex of water in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]]-foot-radius aura centered on itself that lasts for 1 minute or until Vespian Hydral is &Reference[incapacitated].

Strength Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], each creature in the aura.

Failure: The creature is pulled to the nearest unoccupied space adjacent to Vespian Hydral and is &Reference[grappled] (escape DC [[lookup @check.dc.value activity=tCVHmS4n52ADuHdD]]).

At the start of each of its turns while it is in the aura, a creature takes [[/damage average activity=00rwjg090CgZk4Ex]] damage.

A &Reference[grappled] creature can use its action to make a [[/check format=long]] ending the effect on itself on a success.

Rune Regeneration.name: Rune Regeneration
Rune Regeneration.description:
Trigger: The Vespian Hydral is hit by an attack.

Response: The Vespian Hydral activates a protective rune. If the attack deals more than one damage type, choose one of those types. The Hydral gains resistance to the chosen type until the end of its next turn, and it regains [[/heal average]].

Vespian Hydral.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The Vespian Hydral is not a real creature as such, it is an arcane manifestation of the Chamber of Agaseros. This manifestation emerges when the Chamber decides it's time, and it cannot be found randomly in the waters at the bottom of the Chamber complex. It almost always appears as a creature with six nearly identical heads floating in the water around the central column. It has no body beneath the water, as it is just a manifestation of a real creature, not the creature itself. In addition, the Hydral has unique traits that seem to suggest what its real counterpart might possess, such as vulnerability to fire and regeneration despite its arcane construction.

Behavior

The Vespian Hydral is a very dangerous creature, it has little regard for its own health or well-being and instead attacks with abandon. It has no ability to think or feel and barely reacts to damage. Although it reacts to fire, roaring in pain, this response is often delayed slightly, so it is safe to assume the creature might be mimicking pain rather than actually feeling it. It attacks creatures around it aggressively, with the intent to kill, and it doesn't hold back. It seems to have been designed this way, either as a guardian creature created by Agaseros or perhaps based on the nature of the real Hydrals from the Lowlands.

Lore

Agaseroes created this creature long ago, possibly after studying a real Hydral from the Lowlands. It's also possible that Agaseros captured and kept a real Hydral at the bottom of the Chamber to study, which might explain the large pool of water needed to contain such a creature. However, it likely died at some point and was recreated with arcane magic.
Vespian Hydral.biographypublic:
The fanged maw of a reptilian, snake-like creature emerges from the water next to you. Its head and body are scaled, but along its back, there is a large sail-like ridge that marks this as a creature that swims through the water. Between its eyes are a number of glowing runes that match the Chamber as they flicker in and out of existence, and it glares at you with deadly fury.

The [[lookup @name]] Vespian Hydral is a special kind of arcane construct, based on a real creature from the Lowland Bastions. However, it is a creature wholly created and reconstituted at will by the Chamber of Agaseros itself. It appears as a reptilian creature in appearance, with a sleek, scaled maw and glowing, rune-empowered purple eyes. Strangely, its main body seems to be missing or absent, and only its head appears floating in the water to strike at its foes.

Corpuleth.name: Corpuleth

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes two [[/item .mmClaw0000000000]] attacks and uses [[/item .mmBite0000000000]], or makes one [[/item .i3s7WEUkDTDNjs8H]] attack and one [[/item .mmClaw0000000000]] attack and uses [[/item .mmBite0000000000]].

Claw.name: Claw
Claw.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the &Reference[Grappled apply=false] condition (escape DC [[lookup @skills.ath.passive]]) from one of two claws.

Bloody Gorge.name: Bloody Gorge
Bloody Gorge.descriptionprivate:
Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=7mBlINHfcabm0DAr]], one creature within [[lookup @range.value activity=7mBlINHfcabm0DAr]] feet that is willing or that has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition.

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage. The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains Hit Points equal to that amount.

Precarious Armor.name: Precarious Armor
Precarious Armor.description: Whenever the [[lookup @name]] takes damage from a critical hit or takes 20 hit points of damage in a single turn, it must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or its Moiran Plate Armor and Moiran Helm become instantly unequipped.

Prehensile Tongues.name: Prehensile Tongues
Prehensile Tongues.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the &Reference[Grappled apply=false] condition (escape DC [[lookup @skills.ath.passive]]) from one of three tongues.

Hematic Spray.name: Hematic Spray
Hematic Spray.description:
Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=20GU2JBM5zJfNPD1]], each [[lookup @target.affects.type activity=20GU2JBM5zJfNPD1]] in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=20GU2JBM5zJfNPD1]]-[[lookup @target.template.units activity=20GU2JBM5zJfNPD1]]-long, [[lookup @target.template.width activity=20GU2JBM5zJfNPD1]]-[[lookup @target.template.units activity=20GU2JBM5zJfNPD1]]-wide [[lookup @target.template.type capitalize activity=20GU2JBM5zJfNPD1]].

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage, and the target is &Reference[Poisoned] for 3 turns.

Success: Half damage.

Fear Aura.name: Fear Aura
Fear Aura.description:
The [[lookup @name]] emanates an aura in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=oT8238p9jXwVy76c]]-foot Emanation while it doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=oT8238p9jXwVy76c]], [[lookup @target.affects.special activity=oT8238p9jXwVy76c]].

Failure: The target has the &Reference[Frightened apply=false] condition until the start of its next turn.

Success: The target is immune to this [[lookup @name]]'s aura for 24 hours.

Corpuleth.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

[[lookup @name]]s maintain the basic physiology of the humanoid creatures they were in life, with a few major distinctions: their size increases by one unit (most often from Medium to Large), their mouth mutates into a fanged vertical aperture capable of monstrous distention, and their tongue is replaced by three prehensile organs that end in blood-sucking orifices (like the mouths of lampreys). Additionally, [[lookup @name]]s take on the traditional aspects of other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.krye4A4iHch1wC9i]{vampyres}, such as remarkably pale skin, prodigiously large claws, and an overt bestial nature.

Behavior

These malevolent undead creatures are insatiable of appetite, and were duly created to gorge themselves senseless on the vital fluids and tender flesh of both the living and the dead. As [[lookup @name]]s feast, they can renew and enhance their own vitality; and the hunger for this unholy fuel is ceaseless. On the battlefield, [[lookup @name]]s can serve as elite foot soldiers, but their uncontrollably feral nature often prohibits them from serving in leadership roles among formal groups of vampyres and other undead.

Lore

The origin of [[lookup @name]]s can be attributed to the esoteric necromancy of the Blood Baron @UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan}, who derived the first of their kind from the cadavers of servants who had failed her in one way or another. [[lookup @name]]s are but one of the many kinds of vampyric foot soldiers with which the Blood Barons intend to bolster their ranks in the conflicts to come. Encounters with these blood-sucking brutes are considerably rare in the modern age, but rumors persist about the monstrous creations of the Blood Barons and their unholy realm in the west.
Corpuleth.biographypublic:
This hulking, pale-skinned brute is clad in an odd assortment of darkened plate armor festooned with spikes of rotted bone and rusted metal. The helmet atop the hideous creature’s head is fashioned to conceal the eyes but leave the entire mouth exposed.

The mouth itself is a freak of nature. While the presence of lips suggest a normal mouth, this facade is laid bare when the creature’s mandible splits vertically down the middle, revealing a splayed orifice that resembles the toothy chelicerae of some mammalian spider or crab. A trio of long, prehensile tongues lashes out from this horrible mouth, each of them tipped in its own fanged circular mouth like that of a fiendish lamprey.

[[lookup @name]]s are a brutish kind of vampyre spawn created from a peculiar and esoteric form of necromancy. In addition to the telltale signs of vampyrism, a [[lookup @name]] has a vicious vertical mouth capable of prodigious distention, and uses three prehensile tongues to draw the blood from its victims. These large hematophages are known to be more feral than their lesser counterparts, insatiable and unmeasurably malignant.

Harrower.name: Harrower

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes two [[/item .PKMiiEMs0C1hTvl9]] attacks, two [[/item .SBC9LE11MPeBvxE7]] attacks, or one Thanatic Blade attack and one Oblivion Beam attack.

Sunlight Sensitivity.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
Sunlight Sensitivity.description: While in sunlight, the [[lookup @name lowercase]] has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

Parry.name: Parry
Parry.description:
Trigger: The [[lookup @name]] is [[lookup @activation.condition activity=aLG3BRZL7P6OEjwd]].

Response: The [[lookup @name]] adds [[lookup @roll.formula activity=aLG3BRZL7P6OEjwd]] to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name]]'s spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of its character sheet. It automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Dispel Magic.name: Dispel Magic
Dispel Magic.description:
Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range. Any ongoing spell of level 3 or lower on the target ends. For each ongoing spell of level 4 or higher on the target, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 plus that spell's level). On a successful check, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You automatically end a spell on the target if the spell's level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you use.

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Withering Touch.name: Withering Touch
Withering Touch.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]], and the target must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] to avoid gaining 1 level of &Reference[Exhaustion].

Protective Magic.name: Protective Magic
Protective Magic.description: The [[lookup @name]] casts [[/item .vUlTwhx3fM4w1rzL]]{Shield} in response to the spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description: An imperceptible barrier of magical force protects you. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack, and you take no damage from @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMagicMissi]{Magic Missile}.

Command.name: Command
Command.description:
You speak a one-word command to a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or follow the command on its next turn. Choose the command from these options:

Approach. The target moves toward you by the shortest and most direct route, ending its turn if it moves within 5 feet of you.

Drop. The target drops whatever it is holding and then ends its turn.

Flee. The target spends its turn moving away from you by the fastest available means.

Grovel. The target has the Prone condition and then ends its turn.

Halt. On its turn, the target doesn't move and takes no action or Bonus Action.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can affect one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Bestow Curse.name: Bestow Curse
Bestow Curse.description:
You touch a creature, which must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become cursed for the duration. Until the curse ends, the target suffers one of the following effects of your choice:

  • Choose one ability. The target has Disadvantage on ability checks and saving throws made with that ability (Curse Ability activity).
  • The target has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you (Curse Attacks activity).
  • In combat, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw at the start of each of its turns or be forced to take the &Reference[Dodge] action on that turn (Curse Actions activity).
  • If you deal damage to the target with an attack roll or a spell, the target takes an extra 1d8 Necrotic damage (Curse Resilience activity).

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. If you cast this spell using a level 4 spell slot, you can maintain Concentration on it for up to 10 minutes. If you use a level 5+ spell slot, the spell doesn't require Concentration, and the duration becomes 8 hours (level 5–6 slot) or 24 hours (level 7–8 slot). If you use a level 9 spell slot, the spell lasts until dispelled.

Harrower.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

[[lookup @name]]s are created exclusively from the fresh corpses of humanoids, utilizing an accursed ritual that actually takes a person's life during the process. As a result, [[lookup @name]]s tend to retain a majority of the features they exhibited in life. Meanwhile, their skin grows pale and desiccated, their eyes cloud with inhuman cataract, and their left hand becomes stained from fingertips to forearm with pitch-black evil. A [[lookup @name]] can temporarily subdue this effect with magic, and will often dress accordingly to help disguise their unholy nature.

Behavior

Created to serve greater undead and other evil masters, these unholy warriors follow the commands of their leaders to the letter, gloriously wielding the weapons and armor they carried prior to their deaths. They are swift and effective killers, but won't shy away from intimidation tactics when it suits them. [[lookup @name]]s are quite capable in leadership roles for lesser undead, and are intended to serve the Blood Barons in perpetuity as they amass their dark and blasphemous power.

Lore

Foul artifice is responsible for the blasphemous creation of these unholy creatures. The first [[lookup @name]]s were forged in the dark lairs of the Blood Barons to the West, but a looming and furtive threat within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CVV5b22IksTdg7hy]{Rusted Fortress} on Bura Island — helmed by the minions of @UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan} herself — threatens to increase their numbers tenfold in the months and years to come. Thus, standard [[lookup @name]]s of Ember are actually the undying cadavers of cursed @UUID[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA]{Burnished Hand Protectors}. While formidable in their own right, [[lookup @name]]s are actually the lesser form of Death Knights on Ember, and will one day occupy that ill-omened role if the dark tides of fate flow their way.
Harrower.biographypublic:
The warrior before you is clad in burnished bronze mail. Despite the tattered gauze haphazardly wrapped around their face, you notice that the countenance of this solider is remarkably grim … their flesh has grown woefully emaciated, their skin pallid and taut. The warrior’s milk-white eyes occupy shadow-haunted recesses, and their shriveled mouth is twisted into a wry, toothy grin. In contrast, you notice the left hand of this withered solider is stained black like coal, and similar markings of corruption curl up their forearm like tenebrous flames suspended in time.

[[lookup @name]]s are undead warriors created by foul wizardry, cursed to inhabit their decaying corpses while serving the whims of their necromantic masters. Known for their stoic and relentless cruelty, [[lookup @name]]s can drain the living essence from warm-blooded creatures with their left hand — a withered appendage stained soot-black with evil.

Vampyre Spawn.name: Vampyre Spawn

Spider Climb.name: Spider Climb
Spider Climb.description: The [[lookup @name]] can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes two [[/item .mmClaw0000000000]] attacks and uses [[/item .mmBite0000000000]].

Claw.name: Claw
Claw.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the &Reference[Grappled apply=false] condition (escape DC [[lookup @skills.ath.passive]]) from one of two claws.

Bite.name: Bite
Bite.descriptionprivate:
Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=7mBlINHfcabm0DAr]], one creature within [[lookup @range.value activity=7mBlINHfcabm0DAr]] feet that is willing or that has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition.

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage. The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains Hit Points equal to that amount.

Leap.name: Leap
Leap.description: The [[lookup @name]] jumps up to [[lookup @range.value activity=C28C43DeD8iFtZMe]] feet by [[lookup @activation.condition activity=C28C43DeD8iFtZMe]].

Escape Artist.name: Escape Artist
Escape Artist.description: The [[lookup @name]] has advantage on Strength (Athletics) and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks made to end the Grappled condition, and can attempt to end a grapple as a bonus action.

Vampyre Spawn.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

[[lookup @name]] are birthed from the diseased bite of other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.krye4A4iHch1wC9i]{Vampyres} and their kin. Unlucky humanoids who are injured and killed by the ill-omened bite of a Vampyre may rise from the dead as a [[lookup @name]] within 24 hours, afflicted by the same loathsome urges that motivate their forebears. [[lookup @name]] retain most of the physiological features they had in life, with a few notable changes that occur during the advent of their unholy transformation: their skin grows pallid and vaguely translucent, talon-like claws burst from their fingertips, their fanged mouths become capable of distention, and their eyes grow a shade of crimson, yellow, or white. The longer a [[lookup @name]] exists, the more feral and monstrous it becomes. And while [[lookup @name]] are incapable of ever becoming true Vampyres, they can eventually grow in both power and status among their kin.

Behavior

[[lookup @name]] endure their undying existence for one thing and one thing only: the blood of the living. All other concerns are secondary to these feral undead predators, who spend their days resting before hunting at night. And although [[lookup @name]] are typically nocturnal, there are instances of diurnal specimens — particularly in darker, cloud-covered lands like the desolate @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} wastelands of their origin. In combat, [[lookup @name]] make use of their uncanny speed and mobility to control the battlefield with alacrity; and it isn't altogether uncommon for these cruel undead creatures to "play with their food," taunting and terrorizing their prey to better enjoy the hunt.

Lore

[[lookup @name]] and their ilk are the creation of the infamous Moiran @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Blood Barons}, who are easily the most powerful Vampyres ever seen on Ember. Some sages speculate that some strange arcane disease is the reason for the spread of vampyrism on Ember, while others blame the proliferation of their kind on a curse that stems from the tenebrous depths of Oblivion itself. No one, save the Blood Barons themselves, knows for sure. And as long as vampyrism persists on Ember, [[lookup @name]] will eek out a place of their own in the living planet's darkest shadows.
Vampyre Spawn.biographypublic:
The skin of this humanoid is impossibly pale, almost translucent. Their lack of humanity, however, is betrayed by a pair of beady crimson eyes and a prodigiously fanged mouth, the latter of which is marked by the presence of four hideously long canine teeth.

As the creature’s jaw opens to salivate in your direction, you notice how distorted it becomes, as if the bones and flesh have relocated to accommodate a horribly monstrous bite. Before you know it, this feral creature scuttles forward with alarming speed to attack.

[[lookup @name]] are the accursed progeny of vampyres and thier hematophagic kin, and are driven by the same malevolent thirst for blood as their wicked progenitors. These savage undead creatures are rarely seen outside of the Moiran wastelands far to the west, where the enigmatic Blood Barons preside over their unholy realm — a place of darkness, cruelty, and deceit.

Kynryth Husk.name: Kynryth Husk

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] makes any combination of two [[/item Tentacle Swipe]] or [[/item Tentacle Grab]] attacks.

Tentacle Grab.name: Tentacle Grab
Tentacle Grab.description:
The [[lookup @name lowercase]] reaches out with its tentacles and grabs a creature within [[lookup @range.value activity=H3ZUZ0Rdw56BuiP6]] feet of it, pulling the creature into the flame at the center of its body. The target must make the following saving throw.

Strength Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=H3ZUZ0Rdw56BuiP6]].

Failure: The target is pulled into the [[lookup @name lowercase]]’s space and takes [[/damage average]] damage.

The [[lookup @name lowercase]] can have up to two creatures pulled into its space by this action at a time.

Receive Flame.name: Receive Flame
Receive Flame.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] receives 1 or more portions of @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.MFcSuAhMSQo009S5]{The Light Within} from a Tyraphem, fellow Celestial creature, or other source (Blessing Fire, Lit Kynryth Torch, etc.)

Unlit Kynryth Torch.name: Unlit Kynryth Torch
Unlit Kynryth Torch.descriptionprivate: The torch held by this Kynryth has gone out, and cannot be used as a source of radiant fire.

Kynryth Husk.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Like all creatures native to Luxaurum, the Kynryth has a soul of powerful light encased within a constructed metal carapace. This body can be fully and magically concealed for clandestine activities, though all Kynryth carry a torch somewhere on them when in human form, and often use it as a weapon once fully revealed as being creatures of Luxaurum.

Behavior

Kynryth are seen as fairly interchangeable beasts on Luxaurum, functioning almost as guard dogs. Their ability to hide their true form is more useful outside of Luxaurum than within it, used for spying on those who are in a specific Tyraphem's way and destroying them.

Lore

Treated as something along the lines of a ferocious pet on Luxaurum, Kynryth have more use on Ember, and are being seen as part of a vanguard of creatures from Luxaurum that can help Tyraphem continue their eternal wars on new ground.
Kynryth Husk.biographypublic:
The metal frame of a monstrous creature stands still and hollow, leaning ever-so-slightly forward as if waiting for something.

Kynryth Husks are the carapaces of Kynryth, left as shells of themselves without an active internal flame. They have some basic instincts of attack and self-defense, but strike quickly and unthinkingly.

Anachraenum Adventurer.name: Anachraenum Adventurer

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes three attacks with their [[/item Longsword]] or two attack with their [[/item Light Crossbow]].

Bolts.name: Bolts
Bolts.description:
Storage: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCaseCrossbo]{Case}

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAmmunitionV]{Ammunition} is required by a weapon that has the Ammunition property. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon. The Ammunition table lists the different types and the amount you get when you buy them. The table also lists the item that is typically used to store each type; storage must be bought separately.

Explorer's Pack.name: Explorer's Pack
Explorer's Pack.description: An Explorer's Pack contains the following items: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBackpack000]{Backpack}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBedroll0000]{Bedroll}, 2 flasks of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagOil00000000]{Oil}, 10 days of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagRations0000]{Rations}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagRope0000000]{Rope}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagTinderbox00]{Tinderbox}, 10 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagTorch000000]{Torches}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagWaterskin00]{Waterskin}.

Rope.name: Rope
Rope.description:
As a Utilize action, you can tie a knot with Rope if you succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The Rope can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check.

You can bind an unwilling creature with the Rope only if the creature has the &Reference[Grappled], &Reference[Incapacitated], or &Reference[Restrained] condition. If the creature's legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Rope requires the creature to make a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check as an action.

Bedroll.name: Bedroll
Bedroll.descriptionprivate: A Bedroll sleeps one Small or Medium creature. While in a Bedroll, you automatically succeed on saving throws against extreme cold (see @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.dmgDmsToolbox000.JournalEntryPage.xgLA30rErlkjIPAK]{Gameplay Toolbox}).

Waterskin.name: Waterskin
Waterskin.description: A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints. If you don't drink sufficient water, you risk &Reference[dehydration].

Water (Pint).name: Water (Pint)
Water (Pint).description: If you don't drink sufficient water, you risk &Reference[dehydration].

Torch.name: Torch
Torch.description: A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. When you take the Attack action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.

Oil.name: Oil
Oil.description:
You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel, as detailed below.

Dousing a Creature or an Object. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing an Oil flask. Target one creature or object within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or be covered in oil. If the target takes Fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an extra [[/damage 5 type=fire]] damage from burning oil.

Dousing a Space. You can take the Utilize action to pour an Oil flask on level ground to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. If lit, the oil burns until the end of the turn 2 rounds from when the oil was lit (or 12 seconds) and deals 5 Fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

Fuel. Oil serves as fuel for Lamps and Lanterns. Once lit, a flask of Oil burns for 6 hours in a Lamp or Lantern. That duration doesn't need to be consecutive; you can extinguish the burning Oil (as a Utilize action) and rekindle it again until it has burned for a total of 6 hours.

Rations.name: Rations
Rations.description: Rations consist of travel-ready food, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts. See &Reference[Malnutrition] in the rules glossary for the risks of not eating.

Tactical Retreat.name: Tactical Retreat
Tactical Retreat.description: The [[lookup @name]] can immediately move up to half their speed without provoking &Reference[opportunity attacks].

Veteran Explorer.name: Veteran Explorer
Veteran Explorer.description: The [[lookup @name]] has Expertise in the Perception and Survival skills.

Roving.name: Roving
Roving.description: The [[lookup @name]] can move an additional 5 feet while not wearing Heavy armor. They also have a Climb Speed equal to their Speed.

Monstrous Insight.name: Monstrous Insight
Monstrous Insight.description:
When the [[lookup @name]] encounters a creature, they can spend a bonus action to analyze it, or recall their training or knowledge about the creature from the Amaranthine Archives.

On the following turns, the [[lookup @name]] gains an additional 2d6 damage on all successful attacks against that creature, reflecting their knowledge of where to strike effectively.

Longsword.name: Longsword
Longsword.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

Lore Hunter's Resilience.name: Lore Hunter's Resilience
Lore Hunter's Resilience.description:
Once the [[lookup @name]] has used @UUID[Actor.mNKKDsvvNi8f0Pel.Item.eEFAXDQEUJflZujJ]{Monstrous Insight} they gain advantage on saving throws against the frightened condition, representing their confidence drawn from deep knowledge and experience.

If a fear effect is successfully resisted due to this ability, the [[lookup @name]] next attack deals an extra [[/damage]] damage.

Anachraenum Member.name: Anachraenum Member
Anachraenum Member.description:
You have full access to the Anachraenum's, Amaranthine Archives, training facilities, and equipment. You can spend one hour researching in the restricted section of Archives, allowing you to gain advantage on one Intelligence (History) or Intelligence (Arcana) check you make in the next 24 hours.

In addition, when you are within a dungeon or ruin, you gain +4 on initiative rolls, and you can use the environment to your advantage. If you are surprised, you can make a [[/save format=long]] to act normally as if you were not &Reference[surprise]{surprised}.

Anachraenum Adventurer.biographyprivate:
[[lookup @name]]s are explorers of the Anachraenum, first and foremost, spending months or even years in the wilds or dungeons of Ember. They are often more militant and combat-focused than other members of the guild, and function as protectors and guides to some of the more academically inclined scholars.

As they are a broader character type, each individual [[lookup @name]] will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

While there is no single personality trait associated with being a [[lookup @name]], each member is incredibly varied and often has conflicting goals and ideas about ancient cultures and methods for retrieving artifacts or exploring. However, they are usually hardened by years in the field and can be dismissive of youngsters or trainees within the guild.

Connections

[[lookup @name]]s are members of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} guild of explorers, scholars, and treasure-seeking Wayfinders. They are based within the grand city of Ordain, inside All-Fable Keep, where they store and house the artifacts and knowledge they uncover from their expeditions and travels.
Anachraenum Adventurer.biographypublic:
This veteran explorer is covered in deep purple hues representing the guild known as the Lore Hunters. Their hood casts shadows across their face, revealing just enough to showcase the years of experience etched into their skin. Their studded leather armor is dented and weathered, revealing many years wandering the far corners of the world. At their side hangs a longsword, the blade worn yet well-maintained.

[[lookup @name]]s are seasoned members of the Anachraenum guild, having traveled the world of Ember in search of long-lost knowledge and ancient artifacts. They're battle-tested from countless run-ins with monsters and enemies in the many dungeons and wilderness areas they've had to navigate to reach their objectives.

Cindaric Sage.name: Cindaric Sage

Human Lineage.name: Human Lineage
Human Lineage.description: When you perform a Reaction which involves a Focus cost, you gain +1 Boon on any associated roll.
Human Lineage.actiondesc: When you become Weakened or sustain damage while Weakened, you can activate a burst of extraordinary adrenaline called Blaze. You immediately replenish your Action and Focus pools to their maximum value.

Rune: Life.name: Rune: Life
Rune: Life.description:
A chaotic force of creation, responsible for living matter. The Life rune governs health and matters relating to biological growth.

The Life rune scales using Wisdom and provides Restoration of Health or inflicts Poison damage opposed by Fortitude. It is opposed by the orderly rune of Death.
Rune: Life.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Life allows you to stimulate biological growth and nourish physical health, producing one of the following effects:

  • Cultivate 1 cubic foot of existing plants or fungus to rapidly grow to a healthy, blossoming, or harvestable state.

  • Identify a negative physical condition that is affecting a creature such as @Condition[diseased], @Condition[poisoned], @Condition[bleeding], or @Condition[weakened].

  • Verify whether a portion of food or drink is free of contamination from bacteria, parasites, or poison.

Bloom may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Rune: Soul.name: Rune: Soul
Rune: Soul.description:
An orderly force of creation and spiritual essence. The Soul rune governs the fundamental procession of souls through life and death and relates to matters of sapience, personality, and mental health.

The Soul rune scales using Presence and provides Restoration of Morale or inflicts Psychic damage opposed by Willpower. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Oblivion.
Rune: Soul.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Soul allows you to facilitate basic forms of spiritual influence, producing one of the following effects:

  • Enable yourself or another willing person to revisit a core memory of a moment from their past up to one minute in duration as if it happened recently.

  • Identify a negative spiritual condition that is affecting a person such as @Condition[broken], @Condition[frightened], @Condition[confused], or @Condition[insane].

  • Create a momentary spiritual connection with another willing creature that allows them to recognize an idea which can be expressed as a single word.

Uses of Evoke may only affect yourself or another creature which you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Gesture: Influence.name: Gesture: Influence
Gesture: Influence.description:
You intensify the arcane power of a Rune into a concentrated direct contact which is generally a more powerful evolution of the basic Touch gesture.

The Influence gesture scales using Presence and targets a single adjacent creature. It deals 10 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus.

Gesture: Sense.name: Gesture: Sense
Gesture: Sense.description:
You attune your mind to the arcane power of a Rune to sense nearby sources of energy.

The Sense gesture scales with Presence and produces an emanation with 30 feet radius and position that remains centered upon the spellcaster. This gesture requires 1 Hand to cast and has a base cost of 3 Action and 1 Focus. It may optionally be Maintained at the additional cost of 1 Focus every subsequent round.

This spell allows the caster to detect the presence of spellcraft using the same Rune as the one incorporated in this spell. The sense will also momentarily detect the presence of creatures according to their type.

  • Control: Fiends

  • Death: Undead

  • Earth: Oozes and Earth Elementals

  • Flame: Dragons and Fire Elementals

  • Frost: Giants and Frost Elementals

  • Illumination: Celestials

  • Illusion: Fey

  • Kinesis: Monstrosities

  • Life: Plants and Beasts

  • Lightning: Constructs and Storm Elementals

  • Oblivion: Outsiders

  • Soul: Humanoids

Playtest Notes

There is no automation for the sense that is temporarily granted by this spell, but such automation can be provided in the future via a Detection Mode which temporarily reveals creatures of the appropriate type to the spellcaster while the spell is maintained.

Gesture: Surge.name: Gesture: Surge
Gesture: Surge.description:
You channel the arcane power of a Rune into a rushing wave of energy that surges forward from your current position.

The Surge gesture scales with Wisdom and produces a line that is 10 feet wide and 15 feet long originating from the spellcaster, dealing 8 Base Damage to targets which fail to Resist the spell. The gesture requires 2 Hands to cast and has a base cost of 5 Action and 2 Focus.

Playtest Notes

This talent is currently placed at a Tier 4 node. It will eventually only be attainable at a higher level (probably Level 6 required). It is currently available "early" for testing.

Gesture: Aura.name: Gesture: Aura
Gesture: Aura.description:
You concentrate the arcane power of a Rune to create a maintained field of energy that washes over allies and enemies near to you.

The Aura gesture scales with Presence and produces an emanation with 20 feet radius centered on the spellcaster. The center of this Aura moves with the spellcaster.

Depending on the Rune used, the Aura deals damage or provides healing to any creature which begins its turn inside the Aura. This gesture requires 2 Hands to cast, has a base cost of 5 Action and 1 Focus, and must be Maintained costing an additional 1 Focus every subsequent round.

Playtest Notes

This talent is currently placed at a Tier 4 node. It will eventually only be attainable at a higher level (probably Level 6 required). It is currently available "early" for testing.

Emanation templates which are linked to the Token and move when the Token moves are a feature coming in Foundry VTT version 14. Automation of the Aura gesture will occur once Crucible depends on Foundry VTT version 14.

Rune: Earth.name: Rune: Earth
Rune: Earth.description:
The orderly force of elemental earth, responsible for physical matter. The Earth rune governs minerals, metals, soils, and other physical compounds.

The Earth rune scales using Wisdom, targets Reflex, and deals Acid damage to Health. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Lightning.
Rune: Earth.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Earth allows you to manipulate raw forces of rock, mineral, and soil in basic ways, producing one of the following effects:

  • Quickly shape up to one cubic foot of available material into a simple geometric form like a cuboid, ellipsoid, or polyhedron.

  • Precisely copy the physical shape of a held object that is smaller than a 6-inch cube, reproducing it from available clay, stone, or metal. The replica retains no useful properties except for its physical form.

  • Separate and collect earthen particles from the surface of an object, creature, or liquid that you touch, rendering the subject completely cleaned or purified in moments.
