Mould may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Rune: Frost.name: Rune: Frost
Rune: Frost.description:
The orderly force of water and cold. The Frost rune governs the creation of water or other fluids and their transfer between liquid and frozen states.

The Frost rune scales using Wisdom, targets Fortitude, and deals Cold damage to Health. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Flame.
Rune: Frost.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Frost allows you to manipulate liquids and their thermal properties, producing one of the following effects:

  • Draw up to one quarter gallon of fresh water from the atmosphere into a container or upon a surface you touch. The created water may be affected by relevant atmospheric properties of your current location.

  • Manipulate the temperature of up to 1 gallon of water, causing it to immediately freeze or thaw. The water need not be in a container; this technique can be used to coat a surface or join two objects together via regelation. Ice created in this way remains frozen for as long as the ambient temperature of the environment allows.

  • Gather up to a six-foot cube of nearby snow, forming it into a solidified sculpture, shape, or shelter.

Condense may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Talisman Weapon Training.name: Talisman Weapon Training
Talisman Weapon Training.description: You understand the arcane usage of talismans, orbs, foci, or other similar implements to channel magic or empower spellcraft. You are Trained with weapons in the Talisman categories.
Talisman Weapon Training.actiondesc:
You use your equipped Talisman to attempt to regain some Focus. You perform a Harmless Strike against your own Rallying threshold.

On a success you recover +1 Focus if using a one-handed Talisman and +2 Focus if using a two-handed Talisman. On a critical success the amount of Focus recovered increases by an additional +1.

Talisman Weapon Proficiency.name: Talisman Weapon Proficiency
Talisman Weapon Proficiency.description: You have a fluent education in the use of talismans, orbs, foci, or other similar weapons. You gain the Journeyman training rank and a +1 Skill Bonus with weapons in the Talisman category.

Soothe.name: Soothe
Soothe.description: You administer a soothing Performance which rallies your allies, restoring Morale.
Soothe.actiondesc: You perform a calming verse, benefiting all allies who can perceive you within 12 feet. Make a Performance Check against the Madness threshold of each ally. On success, each ally's Morale is restored.

Conserve Effort.name: Conserve Effort
Conserve Effort.description: You find calmness and focus in conserving your effort in battle. When you end your Turn with un-spent Action you gain +1 Focus.

Inflection: Compose.name: Inflection: Compose
Inflection: Compose.description: Enhance a spell by taking extra time in its formation, reducing other resource costs in exchange. The Compose inflection reduces the Focus cost of a spell by 1 while increasing its Action cost by 1 in exchange.

Padded Armor.name: Padded Armor
Padded Armor.descriptionpublic: Consisting of quilted layers of cloth stuffed with rags or wool, padded armor cushions the body against blunt force and serves as the foundation beneath heavier gear.

Sage's Staff.name: Sage's Staff
Sage's Staff.descriptionpublic: The iconic staff of a Cindaric Sage, which serves as a talisman which provides additional defensive capabilities.

Rallying Elixir.name: Rallying Elixir
Rallying Elixir.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to rapidly fortify the psyche and improve morale.
Rallying Elixir.actiondesc:
Immediately recover an amount of Morale dependant on the quality of the elixir.

  • Shoddy - Immediately heals 6 Morale.

  • Standard - Immediately heals 12 Morale.

  • Fine - Immediately heals 24 Morale.

  • Superior - Immediately heals 48 Morale.

  • Masterwork - Immediately heals 96 Morale.

Healing Elixir.name: Healing Elixir
Healing Elixir.descriptionpublic: This potion contains a specialized alchemical formula to rapidly close wounds and improve bodily health.
Healing Elixir.actiondesc:
Immediately recover an amount of Health dependant on the quality of the elixir.

  • Shoddy - Immediately heals 6 Health.

  • Standard - Immediately heals 12 Health.

  • Fine - Immediately heals 24 Health.

  • Superior - Immediately heals 48 Health.

  • Masterwork - Immediately heals 96 Health.

Periapt of Determination.name: Periapt of Determination
Periapt of Determination.descriptionprivate: This item is presented as an amulet, but it can be any type of accessory like a ring, cloak, bracers, or other type of trinket.
Periapt of Determination.descriptionpublic:
A graceful silver amulet embedded with blue jewels imbues you with a feeling of steadfastness while you clutch it, prepared to weather any challenge.

This amulet provides a bonus to Willpower defense equal to the minimum of its Quality and Enchantment bonuses.

  • Fine quality and Minor enchantment: +1 Willpower

  • Superior quality and Major enchantment: +2 Willpower

  • Masterwork quality and Legendary enchantment: +3 Willpower

Lantern.name: Lantern
Lantern.descriptionpublic: An oil-burning or magically illuminated lantern that sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius.

Rune: Control.name: Rune: Control
Rune: Control.description:
The orderly force of discipline and permanence. The Control rune governs thought, reason, and persistence.

The Control rune scales using Intellect, targets Willpower, and deals Psychic damage to Morale. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Kinesis.
Rune: Control.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Control allows you to affect the decision making of others in basic ways, producing one of the following effects:

  • Moderately intensify or dampen the primary emotion being felt by a creature you touch. If the creature is intelligent enough to be aware of the laws governing spellcraft, they are aware of your actions.

  • Understand the abstract motivations of another living creature which allows you to touch it. You are able to intuit their immediate goals expressed in the form of a single verb.

  • Intensely focus on your current objective and the means of achieving it. You receive a brief hint or reminder from the Gamemaster about that objective containing only information which you have previously learned.

Motivate may only affect a creature or object which you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Inflection: Extend.name: Inflection: Extend
Inflection: Extend.description:
Enhance the duration of a spell, increasing the duration of its effect. For spells which are instantaneous, any corresponding status conditions that they cause are increased in duration.

Effect duration increases from the Extend inflection are not yet automated in Playtest 1. This inflection is included as an example of the intended direction for the Spellcraft system.

Cindaric Sage.biographyprivate:
Cindaric Sages serve as the elite spellcasters of the Cindaric Order, and are renowned throughout the Arctus Plateau as competent healers with kind-hearted souls. Their druidic magic is harnessed from the primal metaphysical forces of Ember, and they consider themselves to be tireless caretakers of the living planet's preternatural Heartblood. Wherever trouble can be found throughout the Arctus Plateau, the Cindaric Sages aren't too far behind with timely aid and good intentions.

As they are a broader character type, each individual Cindaric Sage will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

While there is no absolute personality trait associated with being a Cindaric Sage, all walks of life make their way into the Cindaric Order — whether to serve Ember's people or simply revere the living planet with time-honored Cindaric practices. Cindaric Sages tend to be selfless people, with personalities that allow for gregarious and meaningful interactions with the needy and the infirm.

Connections

The most important connection that any Cindaric Sage has is to Ember itself. And a Cindaric Sage's specific enclave sets the pace for their more intimate connections to other Sages, Adherents, and Initiates, from the Ordani opulence of Cindarin Temple to the rural confines of Corpin Sanctuary. Furthermore, Cindaric Sages aren't quite expected to leave their lives behind when they join the order, but their busy schedules usually allow little room for a conventional life marked by excessive individualism.
Cindaric Sage.biographypublic: Cindaric Sages are skilled healers and scholars who spend their lives in dedicated service to the Cindaric faith. Whether from the splendor of Cindarin Temple in Ordain, the remote heights of Corpin Sanctuary on Mial Mountain, or the hermetic reaches of another enclave, a Cindaric Sage is always ready to feed the hungry, heal the sick, or clothe the poor. Cindaric Sages are known for their compassion and goodwill, and each sage finds their own passion in the face of perpetual service.
Cindaric Sage.biographyappearance: This scholarly healer is clad in garments of bright gold and lush crimson, the colors of the famed Cindaric Sages of the Arctus Plateau. Their shoulders and tunic are marked with the familiar four-leafed diamond that signifies the Cindaric order, and their hands are marked and calloused by the wholesome abrasions of honest labor. The sage regards you with a benevolent smile.

Flameguard Firebrand.name: Flameguard Firebrand

Longsword.name: Longsword
Longsword.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

Torch.name: Torch
Torch.description: A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. When you take the Attack action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.

Fireborn.name: Fireborn
Fireborn.description:
You have resistance to fire damage.

If you start your turn submerged, you must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of your next turn. This penalty ends early if you are no longer submerged. If you remain submerged, you repeat the saving throw at the start of each of your turns.

Submerged. You are submerged if you are in water deep enough that you must swim or tread water to stay afloat.

Lumek War Torch.name: Lumek War Torch
Lumek War Torch.descriptionprivate:
This large steel sconce can be worn on your back, and burns Torches as a lantern burns oil. A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet.

As a Bonus Action, you can remove the War Torch from your back, enabling the ability to attack with the Torch when you take the Attack action (using it as a Simple Melee weapon). On a hit, the target takes 1d4 Bludgeoning damage plus 1d2 Fire damage.

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Foundry Note

The Kindling 1d8 damage bonus applied to the Greatsword and Javelin's attack is deducted from this attack's damage total.

Divine Kindling.name: Divine Kindling
Divine Kindling.description:
As a bonus action, the [[lookup @name]] harnesses the divine power of the shard goddess Lumé to wreath their weapons in holy flame. For 1 hour, the [[lookup @name]]’s weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 fire damage (the @UUID[Actor.ewWe4YfFwu1Vktx9.Item.QWCiFtQ59NzhyZiL]{Longsword} and @UUID[Actor.ewWe4YfFwu1Vktx9.Item.hQDM86uAa7AX7Cfi]{Javelin} are enkindled by default with the extra damage).

While enkindled, the weapon counts as a magic weapon.

The enkindled weapons also shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. The effect ends early if the [[lookup @name]] dismisses it (no action required).

Foundry Note

The damage bonuses are found in the Global Bonuses section of the Special Traits tab.

Flameguard Firebrand.biographyprivate:
[[lookup @name]]s are among the youngest of the fabled soldiers who pledge their blades to the service of the shard goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}, and the Flame Warden endows their weapons with divine flame in return. As their name suggests, the Firebrands are members of @UUID[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]{Luna Karrowrath's} Flameguard, and occupy the lowest ranks of this illustrious corps of undead slayers. And while they have yet to learn the divine spellcasting methods of their @UUID[Actor.8ICWlEOQZFXd1rJP]{Flameguard Crusader} brethren, they are nevertheless effective frontline soldiers for the Hearthslayer's ongoing campaign.

Most [[lookup @name]] warriors are Fej, but other ancestries have been known to pledge their blades to Lumé's cause. As they are a broader character type, each individual [[lookup @name]] will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

While there is no absolute personality trait associated with being a [[lookup @name]], these headstrong warriors tend to be brash, young (in body and spirit), and eager to prove their mettle in combat with the undead. Like most members of the Flameguard, [[lookup @name]]s share a strong camaraderie and esprit de corps amongst each other. And while their loyalty is generally hard-won, their devotion to their allies is nigh unshakable.

Connections

[[lookup @name]]s are members of the world-famous Flameguard, Luna Karrowrath's diverse company of righteous undead slayers who courageously pledge their blades and very lives to Lumé, the Flame Warden. They are the sworn enemies of the Moiran @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Blood Barons} and their evil ilk, and have recently established a foothold in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} in search of a furtive undead menace that exerts is terrible unseen influence over the Arctus Plateau.
Flameguard Firebrand.biographypublic:
The first thing you notice about this headstrong Fej warrior is the flame-shrouded torch they wear upon their back, followed by the scorched markings of divine flame on the longsword at their side. A scarlet tunic protrudes from the folds of their studded leather armor. And upon their ashen face, unbridled passion, seething fury, and the impetuousness of youth appear to be worn in equal measures.

[[lookup @name]]s are reckless but effective Lumek warriors who dedicate their lives to ridding Ember of the scourge of undeath. These brash young soldiers serve as the lowest-ranking members of the eponymous Flameguard, a cohort of slayers blessed by the divine magic of the shard goddess Lumé; but despite their relative inexperience, the Firebrands are known for their unparalleled sense of derring-do — along with the holy conflagrations of their flame-shrouded weapons.

Triss Carpel.name: Triss Carpel

Personalized Crafting.name: Personalized Crafting
Personalized Crafting.description:
You personalize your own equipment by making small alterations or modifications to suit your precise usage requirements and preferences. You may allocate up to 2 hours per long rest towards customizing your equipment using an appropriate set of crafting tools. If you spend a cumulative 40 hours customizing a magic item which requires attunement, it gains the Personalized Attunement trait described below.

Personalized Attunement. This item is extensively personalized for your own use. It no longer consumes an attunement slot when you have it attuned, but neither can it be attuned by any other character. This personalization can be reversed if you or another crafter spends another 40 hours to remove your alterations. You may only attune to one item with the Personalized Attunement trait at a time

Constructed Companion.name: Constructed Companion
Constructed Companion.description:
You may spend 1 hour creating a tiny @UUID[Actor.oLu6qs3AYUu8eitR] from a natural material that comes from or grows in the ground, for example clay, stone, wood, or straw. The Constructed Companion is an animated construct which becomes a creature under your control, surviving for 8 hours or until it is reduced to 0 hit points.

While the Constructed Companion is animated, you can provide it with basic verbal instructions to issue simple commands, such as "fetch a key", "stand watch", or "stack some books". If you issue no commands the Constructed Companion will do nothing other than defend itself against hostile creatures, performing the Dodge action whenever appropriate. Once given an order, the Companion continues to follow that order until its task is complete or alternative instructions are given.

You may only have one Constructed Companion active at a time, creating a second companion causes the magic which animated your prior Constructed Companion to immediately fade.

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description:
Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range.

Weather Sensor. You create a Tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.

Bloom. You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.

Sensory Effect. You create a harmless sensory effect, such as falling leaves, spectral dancing fairies, a gentle breeze, the sound of an animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot Cube.

Fire Play. You light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a campfire.

Speak with Animals.name: Speak with Animals
Speak with Animals.description:
For the duration, you can comprehend and verbally communicate with Beasts, and you can use any of the Influence action's skill options with them.

Most Beasts have little to say about topics that don't pertain to survival or companionship, but at minimum, a Beast can give you information about nearby locations and monsters, including whatever it has perceived within the past day.

Entangle.name: Entangle
Entangle.description:
Grasping plants sprout from the ground in a 20-foot square within range. For the duration, these plants turn the ground in the area into &Reference[difficultterrain]. They disappear when the spell ends.

Each creature (other than you) in the area when you cast the spell must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have the &Reference[restrained apply=false] condition until the spell ends. A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself from the grasping plants and is no longer Restrained by them.

Thunderwave.name: Thunderwave
Thunderwave.description:
You unleash a wave of thunderous energy. Each creature in a 15-foot Cube originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d8 Thunder damage and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

In addition, unsecured objects that are entirely within the Cube are pushed 10 feet away from you, and a thunderous boom is audible within 300 feet.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

Animal Messenger.name: Animal Messenger
Animal Messenger.description:
A Tiny Beast of your choice that you can see within range must succeed on a Charisma saving throw, or it attempts to deliver a message for you (if the target's Challenge Rating isn't 0, it automatically succeeds). You specify a location you have visited and a recipient who matches a general description, such as "a person dressed in the uniform of the town guard" or "a red-haired dwarf wearing a pointed hat." You also communicate a message of up to twenty-five words. The Beast travels for the duration toward the specified location, covering about 25 miles per 24 hours or 50 miles if the Beast can fly.

When the Beast arrives, it delivers your message to the creature that you described, mimicking your communication. If the Beast doesn't reach its destination before the spell ends, the message is lost, and the Beast returns to where you cast the spell.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The spell's duration increases by 48 hours for each spell slot level above 2.

Plant Growth.name: Plant Growth
Plant Growth.description:
Casting Time: Action (Overgrowth) or 8 hours (Enrichment)

This spell channels vitality into plants. The casting time you use determines whether the spell has the Overgrowth or the Enrichment effect below.

Overgrowth. Choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point become thick and overgrown. A creature moving through that area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves. You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

Enrichment. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 365 days. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested. They can benefit from only one Plant Growth per year.

Speak with Plants.name: Speak with Plants
Speak with Plants.description:
You imbue plants in an immobile 30-foot Emanation with limited sentience and animation, giving them the ability to communicate with you and follow your simple commands. You can question plants about events in the spell's area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, weather, and other circumstances.

You can also turn &Reference[difficultterrain] caused by plant growth (such as thickets and undergrowth) into ordinary terrain that lasts for the duration. Or you can turn ordinary terrain where plants are present into Difficult Terrain that lasts for the duration.

The spell doesn't enable plants to uproot themselves and move about, but they can move their branches, tendrils, and stalks for you.

If a Plant creature is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a common language.

Fibrous Resilience.name: Fibrous Resilience
Fibrous Resilience.description:
The fibrous biology of Thornlings is incredibly resilient, providing the following benefits:

  • Your armor class cannot be less than 16 regardless of what type of armor you are wearing.

  • You have resistance to damage taken from falling.

  • You gain double the effects of healing from expended Hit Dice.

Thornbark.name: Thornbark
Thornbark.description:
Trigger: When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you erupt with thorny barbs for 1 minute.

While the barbs last, you gain the following benefits:

  • Retaliatory Barbs. When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack (including the attack that triggered this reaction), it takes [[/damage activity=dnd5eactivity000]] damage.

  • Hard to Handle. A creature has disadvantage on Strength (Athletics) checks it makes to Grapple or Shove you.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Triss Carpel.biographyprivate:
Trish was one of the seeders who helped to create Brevin, though she was fairly young when the original planting of Brevin happened, picked for the task because of her skill with both plants and urban planning - much of the design of Brevin's famous fountains came from her sketches. As Steward, the bridge project has been one of her big focuses, but she's also trying to balance between two different factions within Brevin - those who want the village to grow into a major city and those who want to use it as a test ground for new innovations in planting buildings before moving elsewhere. Triss can see the benefit of both approaches and sees them as complementary paths to growth, doing her best to give both their space.

Personality

Triss believes in living life the way that plants do - having clear and simple goals, adapting to the unknown, and bringing different approaches together to benefit the greater whole. She can also be a bit nosy, always checking in on everything to make sure that things are functioning the way that they should.

Connections

Triss knows pretty much everything that happens in Brevin - some joke that she spends her evenings listening to the roots of the plants and asking them to tell her everyone's business. She does her best to get everyone what they need - if not exactly what they want - so she is well liked, even if she occasionally meddles.

Phrases

"What can I do for you today? No, wait - I bet I know."

"As long as it doesn't hurt anyone, go ahead."

"What grows together is hard to tear apart."
Triss Carpel.biographypublic:
The thornling before you doesn't seem to ever stop moving, whether she's crouching down to look at the height of the grass, scanning the landscape around them, or walking softly but determinedly to take care of something, somewhere. Somehow, despite the constant motion, there a sense of peace around her that makes all of the activity seem less frantic and more like something that is simply necessary, like the coming of the tides or the rising of the sun.

Triss Carpel is the Steward of Brevin, the pioneering village that aims to be one of the first to be grown instead of built. With a lot of work to do and a relatively small population, Triss is always busy, but puts the welfare of her people before all else. Despite feeling a lot of responsibility for proving that seed cities can be part of the future of Ember, Triss believes that ultimately, you can't control nature - all you can do is be good to those around you, be as informed as you can about what's happening, and give the land your best.

Crevvet.name: Crevvet

Bite.name: Bite
Bite.descriptionpublic: The Crevvet has a gnawing, harrying bite.

Frenzied Claws.name: Frenzied Claws
Frenzied Claws.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks rapidly with its claws, dealing multiple raking blows against a single target.
Frenzied Claws.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} attacks in a frenzied flurry of sharp claws. It performs three Strikes with its claws. If any results in a Critical Success, it inflicts the @Condition[bleeding] condition.

Bestial Senses.name: Bestial Senses
Bestial Senses.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has finely honed senses and is particularly perceptive of their environment, all Awareness checks gain +2 Boons.

Skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
Skirmisher.description: You are adept at entering and exiting the fray. When moving out of the Engagement radius of an enemy, that enemy has 2 Banes to any Disengagement Strike against you.

Defensive Roll.name: Defensive Roll
Defensive Roll.description: You are a nimble skirmisher, always in movement to stay one step ahead of your enemies in combat.
Defensive Roll.actiondesc: When you Dodge a melee attack you can expend Focus to leap into a defensive roll, moving up to your Size in any direction.

Crevvet.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Crevvets are verminous rodents native to Aterica. They walk on all six of their murine legs, but are known to occasionally stand erect on their hind limbs when surveying their surroundings or interacting with each other on a social level. A crevvet's emerald-colored eyes glow ever-so-subtly in the darkness, and their tails are covered in an extremely light covering of semi-translucent fur.

Behavior

Found in groups of 1-100, crevvets are pack animals whose survival often depends on the cohesion of their social unit. And thanks to their preternatural excavation skills, crevvets have earned a reputation as some of Ember's most objectionable beasts; verily, their ability to successfully ruin a pantry, raid a farmhouse, or plunder a granary is downright legendary. These meddlesome rodents certainly aren't the smartest creatures on Ember, but they might be among the most tenacious.

Lore

crevvets are most commonly found throughout the subterranean realms from whence they originated, like the various corners of the lightless @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}. But thanks to their uncanny burrowing abilities, these six-limbed have found their way into nearly every biome Ember has to offer. Undoubtedly, every city of Aterica has a nest of crevvets lurking somewhere beneath.

Despite its foul taste, crevvet meat is edible, and is actually prized by some @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka} (whose unique biology allows them to metabolize the unsavory enzymes found within the vermin's flesh).
Crevvet.biographypublic: Found everywhere from the shores of Ordain to the furthest reaches of Akazea, Crevvets are obnoxious little beasts known for their exceptional digging skills and their ability to scatter out of harm's way at just the right moment. These ubiquitous rodents are voracious pack creatures, often encountered in large numbers, and will go to nearly any lengths necessary to ransack their latest meal.
Crevvet.biographyappearance: This tiny, six-legged rodent is covered in light gray fur and has four beady eyes the color of glittering emeralds. Its front limbs end in rather prodigious claws (especially for its size), which it apparently uses to burrow to and fro through the crumbling earth.

Oozeling.name: Oozeling

Amorphous.name: Amorphous
Amorphous.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} may move through a space as narrow as 1 inch in diameter without any penalty to its Stride. It gains a bonus to Dodge equal to half its Toughness score and is immune to the @Condition[restrained] condition.

Multiply.name: Multiply
Multiply.description: The @ref[actor.name]{ooze} grows rapidly, increasing in health and size.
Multiply.actiondesc: The ooze's cells rapidly multiply as the creature grows. Its Size increases by 1 and its Health increases by its Toughness value.

False Appearance.name: False Appearance
False Appearance.description: While it remains motionless, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} is indistinguishable from some other object or material.

Corrode Weapon.name: Corrode Weapon
Corrode Weapon.description: The internal corrosive metabolism of the @ref[actor.name]{ooze} threatens to dissolve metal weapons that strike it.
Corrode Weapon.actiondesc:
When struck by a melee weapon made of metal, the ooze attempts to consume the weapon itself, potentially breaking it.

This attack is Harmless, but if successful the Quality of the weapon used in the attack is downgraded by one tier. On a Critical Success or if the weapon is already Shoddy, the weapon becomes entirely Broken. Enchanted weapons are protected against this effect.

Pseudopod.name: Pseudopod
Pseudopod.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name]{ooze} lashes out with an amorphous tentacle of slime.

Oozeling.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The appearance of an @ref[name] varies according to the food it consumes to survive. Whenever a noteworthy hue is absent from the creature's diet, the @ref[name] appearance commonly reverts to a cerulean translucence with hints of gray.

Behavior

@ref[name]s are protective of the humanoids and other creatures they bond with, and tend to warn their allies of external threats whenever possible. Arcane spellcasters who summon otherworldly versions of these amorphous creatures as familiars tend to recognize their exceptional gifts in the realms of perception and mobility.

Lore

@ref[name] are native to Ember's subterranea and various hydrated landscapes, including areas like the hidden underground @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} and the aqueous @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.TB9sbU2LNziZKZWD]{Forest of Stone}. It's unclear why these tiny creatures are more gregarious than their kin, but sages speculate a relationship with the rune magic of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} is somehow to blame for their domestication.
Oozeling.biographypublic: Unlike most of Ember's oozes, these diminutive sentient blobs are overtly peaceful creatures who prefer to use their amorphous forms to communicate with others rather than for predatory gains. @ref[name] are known to form close bonds with other creatures like humanoids and beasts, providing companionship when it's least expected.
Oozeling.biographyappearance: You spy a tiny translucent ooze that appears to regard you with a measure of curiosity, if its cautious and gregarious movements are any indication. This strange creature extends its viscous form into a hand-like tendril, which waves to you in friendly salutation.

Jonico Daridane.name: Jonico Daridane

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a 9th level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of his character sheet. He automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes three attacks, using [[/item .yaMxKMfuj0Pf2rTY]] or [[/item .WyUflaA7hXuYGA8c]] in any combination.

Starry Wisp.name: Starry Wisp
Starry Wisp.description:
You launch a mote of light at one creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 Radiant damage, and until the end of your next turn, it emits Dim Light in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the &Reference[Invisible] condition.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

Shillelagh.name: Shillelagh
Shillelagh.description:
A Club or Quarterstaff you are holding is imbued with nature's power. For the duration, you can use your spellcasting ability instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of melee attacks using that weapon, and the weapon's damage die becomes a d8. If the attack deals damage, it can be Force damage or the weapon's normal damage type (your choice).

The spell ends early if you cast it again or if you let go of the weapon.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage die changes when you reach levels 5 (d10), 11 (d12), and 17 (2d6).

Resistance.name: Resistance
Resistance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a damage type: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Radiant, Slashing, or Thunder. When the creature takes damage of the chosen type before the spell ends, the creature reduces the total damage taken by 1d4. A creature can benefit from this spell only once per turn.

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description:
Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range.

Weather Sensor. You create a Tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.

Bloom. You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.

Sensory Effect. You create a harmless sensory effect, such as falling leaves, spectral dancing fairies, a gentle breeze, the sound of an animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot Cube.

Fire Play. You light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a campfire.

Purify Food and Drink.name: Purify Food and Drink
Purify Food and Drink.description: You remove poison and rot from nonmagical food and drink in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Healing Word.name: Healing Word
Healing Word.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains Hit Points equal to 2d4 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 1.

Detect Poison and Disease.name: Detect Poison and Disease
Detect Poison and Disease.description:
For the duration, you sense the location of poisons, poisonous or venomous creatures, and magical contagions within 30 feet of yourself. You sense the kind of poison, creature, or contagion in each case.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Cure Wounds.name: Cure Wounds
Cure Wounds.description:
A creature you touch regains a number of Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

Protection from Poison.name: Protection from Poison
Protection from Poison.description: You touch a creature and end the &Reference[poisoned] condition on it. For the duration, the target has Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition, and it has Resistance to Poison damage.

Lesser Restoration.name: Lesser Restoration
Lesser Restoration.description: You touch a creature and end one condition on it: &Reference[blinded], &Reference[deafened], &Reference[paralyzed], or &Reference[poisoned].

Flaming Sphere.name: Flaming Sphere
Flaming Sphere.description:
You create a 5-foot-diameter sphere of fire in an unoccupied space on the ground within range. It lasts for the duration. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of the sphere makes a [[/save ability=dex dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] saving throw, taking 2d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

As a Bonus Action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet, rolling it along the ground. If you move the sphere into a creature's space, that creature makes the save against the sphere, and the sphere stops moving for the turn.

When you move the sphere, you can direct it over barriers up to 5 feet tall and jump it across pits up to 10 feet wide. Flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried start burning if touched by the sphere, and it sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 2.

Gentle Repose.name: Gentle Repose
Gentle Repose.description:
You touch a corpse or other remains. For the duration, the target is protected from decay and can't become Undead.

The spell also effectively extends the time limit on raising the target from the dead, since days spent under the influence of this spell don't count against the time limit of spells such as Raise Dead.

Spirit Guardians.name: Spirit Guardians
Spirit Guardians.description:
Protective spirits flit around you in a 15-foot Emanation for the duration. If you are good or neutral, their spectral form appears angelic or fey (your choice). If you are evil, they appear fiendish.

When you cast this spell, you can designate creatures to be unaffected by it. Any other creature's Speed is halved in the Emanation, and whenever the Emanation enters a creature's space and whenever a creature enters the Emanation or ends its turn there, the creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 3d8 Radiant damage (if you are good or neutral) or 3d8 Necrotic damage (if you are evil). On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3.

Dispel Magic.name: Dispel Magic
Dispel Magic.description:
Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range. Any ongoing spell of level 3 or lower on the target ends. For each ongoing spell of level 4 or higher on the target, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 plus that spell's level). On a successful check, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You automatically end a spell on the target if the spell's level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you use.

Protection from Energy.name: Protection from Energy
Protection from Energy.description: For the duration, the willing creature you touch has Resistance to one damage type of your choice: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

Mass Cure Wounds.name: Mass Cure Wounds
Mass Cure Wounds.description:
A wave of healing energy washes out from a point you can see within range. Choose up to six creatures in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point. Each target regains Hit Points equal to 5d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 5.

Healer's Kit.name: Healer's Kit
Healer's Kit.description: A Healer's Kit has ten uses. As a Utilize action, you can expend one of its uses to stabilize an Unconscious creature that has 0 Hit Points without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

Aura of Life.name: Aura of Life
Aura of Life.description: An aura radiates from you in a 30-foot Emanation for the duration. While in the aura, you and your allies have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and your Hit Point maximums can't be reduced. If an ally with 0 Hit Points starts its turn in the aura, that ally regains 1 Hit Point.

Death Ward.name: Death Ward
Death Ward.description:
You touch a creature and grant it a measure of protection from death. The first time the target would drop to 0 Hit Points before the spell ends, the target instead drops to 1 Hit Point, and the spell ends.

If the spell is still in effect when the target is subjected to an effect that would kill it instantly without dealing damage, that effect is negated against the target, and the spell ends.

Jonico Daridane.biographyprivate:
Jonico grew up in Ordain in a crowded, struggling home. His grandmother, Arza, a Sage herself, taught him medicine at the kitchen table and brought him along as she tended to the countless sick and injured that call the Harborage home.

When a string of illnesses swept through the neighborhoods and ships around the Harborage, he and Arza worked tirelessly alongside the other Sages in the city. However, the illness was swift and merciless, and by the time it subsided hundreds were dead, including most of Jonico's family.

As a young man he joined the Cindaric Sages and apprenticed in healing houses across the city. He kept to method more than faith, building a reputation for exceptional judgment under pressure, but also became infamous for his dismissive, sometimes insulting bearing toward those he considers to be detrimental to whatever task is at hand.

Personality

Jonico is steady, precise, and habit-bound. He keeps immaculate logs, triages without flinching, and expects preparation from everyone around him. His bedside manner is blunt but careful, refusing to soften the truth, or withhold information for the sake of a patient's feelings. Though well versed in magic, and capable of it, he only uses it when he has no other options, or to augment practical methods first.

He is relentless and exacting, demanding excellence from his staff and himself, but is careful to make sure that his staff are well cared for and always ready for anything that comes their way. Praise is rare with Jonico; a nod means you did well.

He hates wasted time, dirty hands, and anyone playing politics inside a sickroom. His temper is well known and he never suffers fools well, growing deeply belligerent with people he perceives to be wasting time, ignoring important procedures, or trying to manipulate situations for their own end.

Deep down, Jonico is an isolated, bitter, and guilt-ridden man who misses his family, and bears the weight of every life he's ever failed to save. His desire for excellence is borne from this weight, and his tendency toward isolation and pushing people away is out of a fear of suffering further loss.

Connections

Jonico is a veteran member of the Cindaric Sages, and holds a fair amount of respect and influence due to his expertise and position in the Spellbreaker Tower, but is not well liked because of his difficult personality. He keeps clear of temple politics, and even when he was a member of the Ordinate Council, he rarely involved himself in the social machinations they got up to.

His history as an outspoken critic of Vinarith has earned him little good will, which ultimately lead to his dismissal from the council. However, he busies himself with the Spellbreaker Tower’s healing house and its oeprations.

Phrases

Faith doesn’t stitch a wound; thread does.

Hold still. This will hurt, and then it won’t.

Do your best, that is all anyone can ask. If it's not good enough, get better.
Jonico Daridane.biographypublic:
A lean, man in the red and gold robes of a Cindaric, though styled far more plainly than most. Crow's feet, laugh lines and silver-streaked hair betray the years he's lived. Despite his age he moves with crisp, economical purpose, his gray eyes sharp behind wire-thin lenses. A leather satchel clinks with vials and tools at his hip, and a clean apron is tied tight over his chest.

[[lookup @name]] is the no-nonsense head of the Spellbreaker Tower’s healing house. He has held the position for decades, and is among the city's greatest conventional healers. However, he is notorious for his lack of interpersonal skills and poor bedside manner.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes three attacks, using [[/Item .xEkBLidqK5T2nH9g]], [[/Item .SKWPm2YvpoTCNUvI]] or [[/Item .rYlGswxRPWsRepGy]] in any combination.

Feinted Strike.name: Feinted Strike
Feinted Strike.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]], and [[lookup @name]] has Advantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of this turn.

Captain's Charm.name: Captain's Charm
Captain's Charm.description:
Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=3o27u4Ww7SmCgc8k]], one creature the [[lookup @name lowercase]] can see within [[lookup @range.value activity=3o27u4Ww7SmCgc8k]] feet.

Failure: The target has the &Reference[Charmed apply=false] condition until the start of the [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s next turn.

Riposte.name: Riposte
Riposte.description:
Trigger: [[lookup @name]] is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon.

Response: [[lookup @name]] adds 3 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss. On a miss, [[lookup @name]] makes one Rapier attack against the triggering creature if within range.

Foundry Note

This feature also provides an Active Effect (AE) that will modify this creature's Armor Class when you utilize the reaction. You can enable the AE in the effects tab of the character sheet.

Staggering Punch.name: Staggering Punch
Staggering Punch.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. When [[lookup @name]] hits a creature with this attack, she can choose to push them backward 10 feet with the force of the punch.

Katerin Bastilla.biographyprivate:
Katerin was born and raised in Ordain in a home of great luxury and privilege. From a young age she was attended by tutors, forced to endure lectures and lessons that armed her for a future in politics and leadership.

Between lessons she would become her mother's shadow, watching how she managed the household, and the city district beyond its walls. She also learned the history of the Waerd, and the people that called their wild shores home, the very lands her mother came from.

Inspired by the descriptions of these barely tamed places, she never missed an opportunity to set sail with her father, who eagerly taught her the intricacies of sailing and command. Unlike her brother Darion, who fancied himself a roguish hero of a pirate, Bastilla knew that the sea had no place for hearts of gold. It was a cruel, merciless force that demanded respect and a watchful eye, lest it swallow you and your crew whole.

By the time Katerin was an adult she was an accomplished sailor and fearsome sea captain with her own crew and vessel. She roamed the seas with impunity, taking treasure as she willed, and forging trade deals all along the coasts of the waerd lands.

When her brother vanished she was chosen to lead the house Bastilla, and accepted the mantle readily, knowing that she had spent most of her life being prepared for just such a challenge.

Personality

Katerin is dangerously shrewd and tactical, always looking for angles she can exploit and advantages she can claim, whether that's in battle, or trade negotiations. Despite the often brash and boisterous appearance she presents, she rarely rushes into decisions, or risks her position needlessly.

Mercenary in her dealings with others, Katerin aims to maximize profit and gain for herself, her family and her Trade House, and never shies away from renegotiating if terms are no longer favorable to her.

Should anyone test her resolve or patience, they will quickly learn that she is a veteran countless sea battles, has nerves of steel, and is more than willing to use force to get what manipulation and negotiation fail to.

Connections

Katerin is the head of House Bastilla, and commands its numerous sailing ships, privateers, and merchants. She is legendary among her people as a sea captain, warrior, and leader, enjoying nearly ironclad loyalty from those that have served under her.

Katerin's mother, Matienne, hails from the coastal regions of the Waerd, and as a result, Katerin has deep familiar and cultural connections to that region, giving her a unique insight into the people there, and allowing her to obtain trade deals most others never get.

Among the Cascillians, Katerin is a divisive figure as she refused to join her brother Darion in the naval campaign against the Ossarchate some years ago. To her mind, there was nothing to gain, and she had no deeply seated desire to be a hero like her brother.

Phrases

A trade route that yields no profit is just a pleasure cruise.

In life and sailing you must never forget where you came from, and never lose sight of where you're going.

Being a hero is all well and good, but I'd rather be beloved and rich.
Katerin Bastilla.biographypublic:
A mountain of a woman, this towering Kivahr is covered in an array of scars and tattoos that speak of deeds, battles and glory only she truly knows. Her garb is fine and sturdy, accented with a great coat worn across her shoulders and trimmed with teeth pried from the maw of a great sea beast.

[[lookup @name]] is the head of the Trading House that bears her name, and commands the great armada of merchant vessels, warships, and marauding privateers that sail under its banner.

Loris Tezran.name: Loris Tezran

Foolsbane.name: Foolsbane
Foolsbane.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

This masterwork rapier is known as "Foolsbane" in Imperial circles, and has claimed countless lives. It was a personal gift to the Redfiend from the Empress just before he set out to start his posting as Ambassador to Ordain. It is lightly enchanted to have superior balance compared to normal rapiers.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes four [[/item .Vjng7ukm5ZyIw3gJ]] attacks.

Foundry Note

This feature also provides an Active Effect (AE) that will modify this creature's Armor Class when you utilize the reaction. You can enable the AE in the effects tab of the character sheet.

Legendary Resistance.name: Legendary Resistance
Legendary Resistance.description: If [[lookup @name]] fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

Command: Pounce.name: Command: Pounce
Command: Pounce.description: If Rakavi is present and not incapacitated, [[lookup @name]] commands him to use Toppling Pounce.

Command: Tail Swipe.name: Command: Tail Swipe
Command: Tail Swipe.description: If Rakavi is present and not incapacitated, [[lookup @name]] commands him to make one Sweeping Tail attack.

Lunging Strike.name: Lunging Strike
Lunging Strike.description: [[lookup @name]] moves up to half his Speed, and it makes one [[/item Foolsbane]] attack.

Abyssal Resistance.name: Abyssal Resistance
Abyssal Resistance.description: [[lookup @name]] has resistance to necrotic damage. Additionally, he may make death saving throws, and once per long rest if he rolls a 1 on a death saving throw, he may re-roll the save and keep the new result.

Drakonfire.name: Drakonfire
Drakonfire.description:
[[lookup @name]]'s spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks), and can cast the following spells, requiring no components:

At Will: [[/item .8TOdl9RQw66yIHY0]]{Produce Flame}

1/Day Each: [[/item .0mh6rFa0KmcrQr1r]]{Burning Hands}, [[/item .yRWu0YmiVS5ZyPlJ]]{Scorching Ray}

Produce Flame.name: Produce Flame
Produce Flame.description:
A flickering flame appears in your hand and remains there for the duration. While there, the flame emits no heat and ignites nothing, and it sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Until the spell ends, you can take a Magic action to hurl fire at a creature or an object within 60 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 Fire damage.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

Burning Hands.name: Burning Hands
Burning Hands.description:
A thin sheet of flames shoots forth from you. Each creature in a 15-foot Cone makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Flammable objects in the Cone that aren't being worn or carried start burning.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 1.

Scorching Ray.name: Scorching Ray
Scorching Ray.description:
You hurl three fiery rays. You can hurl them at one target within range or at several. Make a ranged spell attack for each ray. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 Fire damage.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You create one additional ray for each spell slot level above 2.

[[@item.level + 1]]{Total Rays}

Loris Tezran.biographyprivate:
Born into the noble Tezran house, Loris was raised amid luxury, war stories, and expectation. His mixed Drakon blood granted him a strength and focus that set him apart from his peers, and by the time he joined the Kirargy Knights he already bore the arrogance of someone destined for greatness. But it was service in the Order of the Veiled Star the molded him into a disciplined warrior and tactician. He proved himself repeatedly on the eastern frontiers, slaying monsters and leading patrols to protect the Empire’s most remote provinces.

Ambition soon drove him higher. After years of distinguished service, he rose to Commander and led a controversial but decisive campaign alongside the Tayan military, his forces sacking and razing the city state of Yarino, all to prove his unit's loyalty to the Empress. That act drew the attention of the Empress and the Vryn, a secretive order of spies and agents serving her interests.

It wasn't long before Commander Tezran was holding audience with the Empress and being named Redfiend for his deeds. A title by which he is known by across the Empire and Kelmezian territories, though with greatly different sentiments behind them.

In the years that followed, Loris served loyally both as a Kirargy Knight slaying monsters in the East, but also as an agent of the Vryn whose mandate was to keep the empire stable and noble houses in check by any means.

Eventually Loris was assigned a unique posting: Ordain, a distant Great City of Ember that had begun to draw the Empress' attention. Loris was to find out more about it, lay the groundwork for trade and begin finding their weaknesses in the event a campaign was deemed worthy of undertaking there.

Personality

Loris is driven, deliberate, and intensely loyal, but his loyalty comes with many complicated feelings. To others, he seems to serve because it rewards him: power, proximity to the Empress, and purpose. He possesses a calculating charm and is highly adept in social and political settings, but would likely rather be testing his mettle against monsters and threats to the Empire on the frontiers.

In private, his faith in Selai guides him greatly, her teachings of guidance and protection or core tenets of Lor's beliefs: the Empire must be guided, protected, and secured by any means required, and the strongest in the empire are in a unique position to accomplish this.

He despises disorder and altruistic idealism, considering them weaknesses to overcome, and that strength of spirit and arms is paramount. All progress must be paid for, be it military, industrial, or political, and if blood is the cost, then it must be paid.

Despite his calm, polished exterior and unquestioning obedience, Loris is deeply thoughtful and troubled by some of the Empire's more openly evil actions. Though he doesn't question his role, he believes he might bring his own sense of honor and justice to the Empire. His steel will and sworn oaths, however, mean that no matter the order, he is a man willing to burn a city to the ground to achieve the goals of his superiors.

Connections

Loris serves the Tayan Empress directly and reports to her on his actions and ongoing mission in Ordain.

Loris also retains his rank as a Commander in the Kirargy Knights and as a Veteran of the Veiled Star order in the south. His reputation among the Knights is complex, as many with the Empire consider him to be a paragon of their Order, while others consider him to be a butcher.

He is also an agent within Vryn’s ranks and is considered efficient and effective, willing to do anything to accomplish the Empire's goals.

Phrases

Loyalty is the purest form of ambition.

A crime done in service to the Empire is no crime at all.

The Empire does not need heroes. It needs people who can get it results.

Everyone serves something, or someone, whether they know it or not.
Loris Tezran.biographypublic:
Tall and immaculately composed, this man carries himself with the cool poise of a man too assured to ever feel threatened. His dark hair is trimmed close and swept neatly back between horns which betray his half-drakon heritage. His expertly tailored clothing is of an overtly Tayan military style, and a rapier hangs from his belt, likely more for ceremony than battle.

[[lookup @name]] is the Tayan Ambassador to Ordain. He is known for his charm, intelligence, and quiet menace, and is quite active in the city's political landscape.

Yeela Drevvin.name: Yeela Drevvin

Evasion.name: Evasion
Evasion.description: If [[lookup @name]] is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, she instead takes no damage if she succeeds on the save and only half damage if she fails. She can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

Nimble Escape.name: Nimble Escape
Nimble Escape.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] takes the &Reference[Disengage] or &Reference[Hide] action.

Veiled Presence.name: Veiled Presence
Veiled Presence.description: While moving through the streets of Ordain, [[lookup @name]] can utilize crowds as cover, gaining &reference[advantage] on &reference[stealth] checks while doing so. While hidden, she is indistinguishable from @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani Cityfolk}.

Manacles.name: Manacles
Manacles.description:
As a Utilize action, you can use Manacles to bind an unwilling Small or Medium creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the &Reference[Grappled], &Reference[Incapacitated], or &Reference[Restrained] condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. While bound, a creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls, and the creature is Restrained if the Manacles are attached to a chain or hook that is fixed in place. Escaping the Manacles requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check as an action. Bursting them requires a successful DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check as an action.

Each set of Manacles comes with a key. Without the key, a creature can use Thieves' Tools to pick the Manacles' lock with a successful [[/tool thief dex 15]] check.

Yeela Drevvin.biographyprivate:
Yeela joined the Hallows in her late teens, serving as a legal clerk and inspector for several years. Her natural knack for reading people made her very good at rooting out the truth when conducting investigations, but she found the work lacked any real challenge, despite knowing it was important.

By her early twenties she was already being watched by Veiled Chain recruiters, and was approached to assist with some investigations, where she ended up providing vital insights into figured involved in the cases.

It wasn't long after that she was a fully fledged member of the Chain. Yeela hasn't looked back, and is among the Chain's senior leadership now, with two decades of distinguished service under her belt. She is presently the Chain's head of profiling and recruitment.

Personality

Yeela has been working for the Veiled Chain for a long time, a little over two decades now, and has seen a lot of Ordain's best and worst elements. She's learned how its people think, and in some ways there's very little about Ordani and Arcturians that surprise her anymore.

Outwardly she appears a mixture of bored and borderline flippant, with professionalism often taking a backseat so that her more unfiltered opinions can come out. She is well versed in the official, stodgy language of the Chain, Hallows and Ordinate's paperwork, but she also knows that the average person doesn't trust that style of communication.

She prefers to be more personable, because helping and protecting people is the point of this job in her mind, even if she knows that's not always true on a organizational level.

Connections

Yeela is among the senior agents of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} responsible for recruiting, training, and coordinating agents. Her ability to read people and profile them has proven vital in making sure new recruits are going to be to the tasks the Chain sets for them.

Yeela also has informants and allies in the Trade Houses, most notable @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{House Lilifeld} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}. She mostly uses them for information and insights, and avoids becoming politically involved herself.

People tell you everything you need to know about them, you just need to watch and listen.

Gastern Faviyos.biographyprivate:
Gastern is Kessian, originally, and grew up poor in shadows of a great port city. Every day was living moment to moment on wits and grit alone. By the age of fourteen his parents were gone, or dead, and he was on his own. He took his first life a year later and was a hardened criminal by eighteen, having fallen in with a band of Kessian cutpurses and robbers.

His ambition drove him to try and take over the band, but failure necessitated his flight. He ended up on the coast, having barely escaped with his life. With little prospect in Kessia, and knowing that people would be looking for him, he boarded the first ship he could sneak onto and stole food from the crew while waiting for landfall.

This began a decade of wandering from port to port like a ghost, stowing away on ships, or cutting enough purses to buy passage when they felt the desire. Eventually Gastern learned enough about ships to begin working as a sailor, and he embraced that wind, believing that they would lead a zeph to whatever point they were meant to arrive at.

Sure enough, he arrived at the island of Kadisos, met a grizzled pirate captain name Rostol, and found himself part of a violent pirate crew marauding through the seas. That band was known as the Wind Raiders, and seeing this as confirmation that the winds were taking him to his destiny, he dedicated himself to this crew and quickly ascended to first mate.

However, his ambition would lead him once more to try usurping power, and once more he would be exiled, but not without taking some loyal sailors with him. Rather than running, he vowed to one day return, and have his revenge. This was his destiny, after all, to lead the Wind Raiders.

Personality

Gastern is quick-witted, opportunistic, and confident to the point of arrogance. He is blunt, and crass, using intimidation and threats over charm and diplomacy. He is more than willing to injure, maim and kill to get what he wants.

Though ruthless, he also knows how to bide his time when danger is too great, and refuses to take on fights he knows he can't win.

His belief in winds as fate guides many of his decisions. he sees the world as a series of shifting opportunities and obstacles to be navigated and often takes time each day to commune with the wind and decide his course of action.

Connections

Gastern’s past has left him with more enemies than friends, and he he remains infamous among the unsavory communities that exist along the shores of Ember. His greatest rivalry, however, is with Rostol, the captain who exiled him: Gastern’s ambition burns hot, and many suspect it’s only a matter of time before he returns to finish what he started.

Phrases

"The wind never waits for cowards, and neither do I."

"If you want something in this world, someone's going to have to bleed for it."

"That what you want, give nothing back, and kill anyone trying to do the same."

Ancara.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

An Ancara’s body is built for power and agility, not sustained flight, and Rakavi exemplifies that strength. His robust torso supports thick, leathery patagia connecting all four heavily clawed limbs, allowing for remarkable aerial control, gliding, and climbing ability.

Behavior

Ancara are patient, observant, and deliberate, a predator that wastes no motion until the perfect instant to strike arrives. Ancara prefer to perch in trees and other high places where they can watch their surroundings, conserving energy until prey are spotted.

These gliding predators use their patagia to glide long distances silently, descending on targets without warning. Ancara are known to hunt creatures as large as themselves and bigger, using their claws and beak to latch onto prey, grievously wound them, and hold fast until their prey succumbs to its wounds.

Ancara fiercely defend their kills, as they generally lack the capacity to relocate carcasses easily. Once an Ancara has had its fill it will return to a high perch, often using the remaining carcass as bait to draw in fresh prey.

Most Ancara are solitary creatures once they reach adulthood, but paired Ancara remain with their young until they are capable enough to hunt on their own, or their offspring decide to strike out on their own.

Lore

The true origin of the Ancara is not known and many scholars debate whether it should be classified as a naturally occurring creature or if its existence is owed to the wild energies of Ember playing havoc with the form of a creature. Some cede that it is possible for both to be true, and that the Ancara as it's known now is a far cry from what it began existence as.

Anydrath.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Anydraths are powerful, aquatic predators found in the waters around the Cascillian Republic. Their muscular limbs end in partially webbed feet tipped with short, curved claws, granting both exceptional swimming ability and strong traction on land.

Their double-coated fur repels water naturally, insulating them in cold seas and harsh weather alike. A series of specialized salt glands situated along the neck and jawline allow the creature to expel concentrated bursts of crystalline salt with shocking power.

Behavior

Highly social and loyal by nature, Anydraths travel in family groups known as “clans,” that have been known to range across large areas, incorporating multiple dens in water and on land. These clans are playful and social, with large groups of the creatures being found basking together on beaches or rocks.

Intelligent and observant, Anydraths have been observed communicating with each other using mixtures of hand and tail signals. These signals are used by groups of Anydrath while hunting, or when engaged in battles with predators and territorial interlopers.

Lore

Native to the southern coasts of the Cascillian Republic, Anydraths were once considered a nuisance for their constant raiding of fishing nets and seemingly coordinated disrupting of coastal villages. However, over countless generations, the fishers began to turn the Anydrath into allies, forging relationships with them and eventually partially domesticating them.

Now, Anydrath are uncommon companions, prized for their intelligence and ability to retain complex training. The largest body of domesticated Anydraths belongs to the Cascillian Republic's navy, which actively cultivates a full clan that are bred for military service.

It wears a leather harness fixed with military insignia of the Cascillian Navy.

The [[lookup @name]] is a military service animal trained by the Cascillian Republic Navy to augment its marines. Like all Anydraths, they are swift swimmers, intelligent, and capable of spraying deadly bursts of salt at foes.

Surge Walker.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The Cascilians built this machine in layers, the innermost parts being a mysterious Ortarec core that serves as a powerful energy source to drive the machinery built around it. Adjacent to the core is a heavily armored tank meant to hold the mangled remains of a fallen soldier, now sustained and given second chance to serve their nation.

This tank is wrapped in layers of machinery that obey the pilot's commands, and move hundreds of pounds of alchemically treated bronze limbs and armor. The body also features powerful lamps and underwater drives that allow the surge walker to move through water with shocking agility.

Behavior

The Surge Walker is a versatile fighting machine made to fight the undead forces of the Ossarchate alongside the Cascillian infantry. It is primarily meant to break fighting lines and control hordes so that more vulnerable infantry are put at less risk.

As a result, this machine is fast, strong, well armored, and features a mixture of weapons from long-range harpoon cannons, to brilliant sunlight-lamps and powerful crushing limbs. In concert, these weapons allow it to drive back and manage the undead better than any mortal soldier can.

Lore

Originally conceived by the Office of Arcane Assignments, a clandestine arm of the Casciliian Republic's armed forces, it was built in concjution with the help of the Corps of Machines, but its true nature remains a closely guarded secret, with parts of its construction being handled by carefully vetted engineering teams.

Only a few know that at the heart of the machine is a living soldier, and fewer still know that their presence is to ensure the loyalty of the machine, because early trials of the Surge Walker that were powered by only the Ortarec core and mechanical command circuits quickly became unpredictable and dangerous, with no loyalty to the Republic whatsoever.

Cascillian Marine.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Marines are a fully volunteer force recruited from the full range of ancestries found in the republic. To qualify for service as a Marine a potential recruit must be an determined enough to make it to the end of a grueling four-month training program. By the end of training all newly minted Marines are able swimmers and disciplined soldiers ready to serve in their nation's defense.

As part of a professional fighting force, they are all given the same equipment and trained to use it extensively. While on duty Marines have identical uniforms, armor, and weaponry with little physical variation beyond what their rank, station, and assignment allow for.

Behavior

Marines in service to the Navy of the Republic of Cascillia have the ideals of loyalty, service, and dedication hammered into their heads from the first day of training. They are taught to value the sanctity of the nation above all else, even being willing to sacrifice themselves for the good of the Cascillian people if necessary.

Most Marines are decently compensated and have good morale, making them loyal soldiers that are unlikely to turn on their own commanders or disobey orders. They are strongest in numbers, and most Marine teams consist of a dozen soldiers with a low ranking officer leading them.

Lore

Marines can be found defending most bases, warehouses, and ships that belong to the Cascillian government. They are numerous, dedicated, and valued for their ability to fight under almost any conditions, on nearly any terrain.

The Marines are part of the greater Cascilian navy, but have their own commanders, culture, and hierarchy, making them a sub-faction of the greater Navy.

Blue Block Inmate.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Spellbreaker Inmate can be anyone, young, old, hale or frail, of any ancestry or background found in Ordain. A handful may possess physically visible abnormalities or distortions arising from magical maladies, but most outwardly resemble any other citizen one might encounter in the city.

Behavior

The inmates of the Spellbreaker Prison are broken up into three groups: Blue Block, Yellow Block, and Red Block. Though there is no specific behavior tied to these groups, the reasons for their presence in the group often ties to their deeds and background.

Blue Block inmates are subject to the gentlest of the prison's restrictions as many are here not for crimes, but because their abilities or afflictions pose a persistent risk to themselves or those around them. Among these inmates, there is more hope than despair: a number eventually transition to become residents of the tower’s lower levels thanks to rehabilitation or the temporary nature of their conditions.

Yellow Block inmates live under greater scrutiny as they are responsible for violent or grave offenses, or their magical or mental instabilities have proven acute enough to require strict and continual oversight. Yellow Block is not devoid of opportunity for redemption; there are some who are only temporarily dangerous due to recurring maladies, and can be released when dormant or cure.

Red Block inmates are inherently dangerous at all times, and are kept locked away around the clock. While most are remorseless criminals responsible for horrible acts, some are victims of magical curses that have left them too dangerous to be let free. Many Red Block inmates can never be released, not even to the tower’s own internal society.

Lore

A significant portion are housed in the Spellbreaker simply because no other institution can safely harbor them or provide for their care. Some came unwillingly, others sought out the tower of their own accord to escape the havoc their abilities or conditions wrought.

Over time, it is not uncommon for blue and even yellow block prisoners to find a measure of freedom, transitioning into the roles of tenants, workers, or even aides within the lower levels of the tower, forming a strange but resilient community of those who cannot leave, but need not be locked away.

Red Block, however, holds a darker purpose: it is not only criminals, but unspeakably dangerous entities, some of them not even humanoid, whose destructive capabilities or alien natures are only kept in check by the divine aura of antimagic that surrounds the tower.

Spellbreaker Guard.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Spellbreaker Guards are drawn exclusively from candidates possessing a high standard of physical fitness and overall health, ensuring each individual can withstand the physical and mental demands of shifts within the priosn. There is no restriction on age or background as long as the recruit meets these criteria, resulting in a relatively diverse team pulled from the whole of Ordain.

Uniforms consist of padded blue tunics for comfort and mobility, reinforced by light leather armor that offers protection without sacrificing approachability. Each guard carries a stout, weighted club, though these rarely see service since intimidation and violence are strictly minimized.

Behavior

Unlike traditional jailers found elsewhere, the Spellbreaker Guards occupy a hybrid role or caretaker and sentinel. They are chosen as much for their character as their competency. Recruits must demonstrate a genuine empathy for others and a steadfast, even-tempered nature.

Each member of the guard is rigorously screened against tendencies toward aggression or cruelty, the goal being to create a time that is capable of maintaining firm containment and humane treatment at the same time.

Many members of the guards are also members of the Cindaric Sages, or adherents to the religion, and hoping to help others with their presence.

Lore

Spellbreaker Guards are a distinct and respected order within the Tower, trained and paid directly by its administration. The funding for these positions is secured from two major powers: the Cindaric Sages and the Hallows, who both also supply oversight and guidance in accordance with their respective purviews of treatment and justics.

This dual sponsorship ensures that the guards bind the spiritual and civic aims of the city in their daily work, but the ultimate authority remains with the Warden of the Spellbreaker, who alone has charge over hiring, instruction and dismissal.
