Nimble Escape.description: The [[lookup @name lowercase]] takes the &Reference[Disengage] or &Reference[Hide] action.

Veiled Presence.name: Veiled Presence
Veiled Presence.description: While moving through the streets of Ordain, the [[lookup @name]] can utilize crowds as cover, gaining &reference[advantage] on &reference[stealth] checks while doing so. While hidden, they are indistinguishable from @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani Cityfolk}.

Manacles.name: Manacles
Manacles.description:
As a Utilize action, you can use Manacles to bind an unwilling Small or Medium creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the &Reference[Grappled], &Reference[Incapacitated], or &Reference[Restrained] condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. While bound, a creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls, and the creature is Restrained if the Manacles are attached to a chain or hook that is fixed in place. Escaping the Manacles requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check as an action. Bursting them requires a successful DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check as an action.

Each set of Manacles comes with a key. Without the key, a creature can use Thieves' Tools to pick the Manacles' lock with a successful [[/tool thief dex 15]] check.

Veiled Chain Agent.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Since the Veiled Chain has no formal uniform, and it recruits from the citizenry of Ordain directly, its agents look identical to anyone else. Since almost anyone can be a [[lookup name]], they enjoy near invisibility unless they want to be seen.

Each [[lookup @name]] carries a badge with the organization's logo and their identification sigils on it, allow them to verify their authority, but otherwise they look like anyone else.

Behavior

The Veiled Chain selects the most inquisitive, keen-eyed, dedicated, and cunning of Ordain to fill its ranks. Each [[lookup @name]] is charged with the important duty of watching the city for danger and investigating situations as they arise. Should any threats to the city appear it is their job to determine a plan of action and make sure no harm comes to Ordain or its people.

Lore

See the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} page for detailed information on the organization this agent belongs to.
Veiled Chain Agent.biographypublic:
This person is stylishly dressed in layers of bright cloth with intricate patterns and differing weights, creating a lavish ensemble of texture and color. Their garb is accented with silvers and golds, and minor gems which glitter in the light, making them appear all the more dazzling.

The [[lookup @name]] serves the investigative arm of the Ordinate, and is drawn from the great city's populace. As a result, they look like any other citizen of Ordain, allowing them to move through the city unnoticed with ease.

Wind Raider Boarder.name: Wind Raider Boarder

Able Crewman.name: Able Crewman
Able Crewman.description: The [[lookup @name]] is proficient with vehicles (water) and a strong swimmer, with a swim speed of 20 feet.

Get 'em!.name: Get 'em!
Get 'em!.description: Once per day, as a bonus action, the [[lookup @name]] selects an enemy it can see and adds [[/r 1d4]] to their next attack against that enemy. If the attack hits, any other uses of Get 'Em! in that round are rolled with a [[/r 1d6]] instead of a d4.

Wind Raider Boarder.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

The typical Wind Raider is wiry but strong, shaped by years of sailing. Wind Raiders are not picky about their recruits, and pick up sailors at any port their ship makes dock at. In terms of equipment, their favored armor is crafted from padded cloth, offering enough protection to deflect a glancing blow while allowing free movement to climb, swim, or leap between decks.

All of their armor and weapons bear a wind-motif, with swirling lines of blue and gray making the shape of clouds, and currents of wind moving between them.

Behavior

Wind Raiders are all seasoned sailors, and each knows how to reef a sail as well as wield a blade. They are also well known for their cruelty, greed, and willingness to kill to get what they want. Wind Raiders are among some of the most wanted pirates on the seas as a result.

Lore

The Wind Raiders are actually split off from a larger group of corsairs of the same name. Once the larger crew was run by a renowned pirate by the name of Rostol Grash, but after a mutiny the band split. While little is known about Rostol's side of the Wind Raiders, these particular pirates are led by the brutal and ambitious Gastern Faviyos.
Wind Raider Boarder.biographypublic:
Rugged, weather-beaten, salt-streaked, and tanned from countless seasons braving the Reaper Ocean, this sailor is clad in shades of gray, brown and blue, with a vest painted with swirling wind and clouds. A curved sword hangs from their hip and they seem more than willing to use it if given a reason.

The [[lookup @name]] is part of a vicious band of pirates of the same name, and they are well-adapted to the hardships of a life of sailing the Reaper Ocean.

Toron.name: Toron

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes three attacks with any of the following abilities: [[/item .aCn7R3Y4Rrku9Bwq]], [[/item .n8jSBjkRCVnqubTt]], or [[/item .vjiAR4useCqvPEs3]].

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name]]'s spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of his character sheet. He automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

Fireball.name: Fireball
Fireball.description:
A bright streak flashes from you to a point you choose within range and then blossoms with a low roar into a fiery explosion. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried start burning.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

Invisibility.name: Invisibility
Invisibility.description:
A creature you touch has the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition until the spell ends. The spell ends early immediately after the target makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.

Cone of Cold.name: Cone of Cold
Cone of Cold.description:
You unleash a blast of cold air. Each creature in a 60-foot Cone originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 8d8 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature killed by this spell becomes a frozen statue until it thaws.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 5.

Fly.name: Fly
Fly.description:
You touch a willing creature. For the duration, the target gains a Fly Speed of 60 feet and can hover. When the spell ends, the target falls if it is still aloft unless it can stop the fall.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 3.

Misty Step.name: Misty Step
Misty Step.description: Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

Protective Magic.name: Protective Magic
Protective Magic.description: [[lookup @name]] casts [[/item .kAD0obPg65DOReOe]]{Shield} or [[/item .WXgViEXtdQo6BzZn]]{Counterspell} in response to the spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description: An imperceptible barrier of magical force protects you. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack, and you take no damage from @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMagicMissi]{Magic Missile}.

Evasion.name: Evasion
Evasion.description: If [[lookup @name]] is subjected to an effect that allows him to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, he instead takes no damage if he succeeds on the save and only half damage if he fails. He can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

Cunning Action.name: Cunning Action
Cunning Action.description: [[lookup @name]] takes the &Reference[Dash apply=false], the &Reference[Disengage apply=false], or &Reference[Hide apply=false] action.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: Once on each of its turns, when [[lookup @name]] hits a target with a melee weapon attack, the target takes an extra [[/damage average]] if [[lookup @name]] has advantage on the attack roll or if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t incapacitated, and [[lookup @name]] doesn’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.

Toron.biographyprivate:
Toron was raised in a comfortable but modest home in the Tayan Empire, his family serving a noble household as it had for generations. Ambitious and clever, he used this connection to secure a place in one of the Empire’s magical academies, where he discovered a knack not just for spellwork, but for manipulating people and information.

Spotted by a recruiter, Toron was brought into the Empress' Vryn, an elite espionage and sabotage force where he served for several decades.

Recently, his latest mission in Ordain went awry, and he was apprehended by local authorities. Now, Toron waits in the Spellbreaker Tower, calmly enduring interrogation and biding his time.

Personality

Toron is calm, patient, and extremely observant. He never rushes into anything, preferring to take the measure of a person or place before committing to a course of action. While he appears approachable and reasonable, years of service as a spy have made him suspicious and slow to trust. He always weighs his words and actions, seeing even casual encounters as small battles of wit.

His capture in Ordain is not the first time he's been compromised, and by far not the worst, but the ire of his overseer, Loris Tezran, may prove especially fatal. This is not a prospect he is happy about, and a problem he has not yet worked out a solution to.

Though he is fiercely loyal to the Empire, he knows that its might makes right attitudes and extensive misinformation and clandestine operations against its own populace will only lead to instability and corruption. However, he is not willing to turn his back on the nation that gave him everything.

Connections

Toron’s deepest connections are with the Empress’ Vryn, particularly other field agents he considers friends and protégés. He has many contacts throughout the Empire and rival nations, but these are mostly professional.

Phrases

You can’t second-guess every move, sometimes you've just got to act.

Everyone has a secret, what matters is who learns it first.
Toron.biographypublic:
A quiet, well-groomed man wearing prison garb. His sharp, calculating eyes size up everyone in view, betraying a sharp mind behind a calm, almost friendly mask. His neat black hair shows hints of gray at the temples.

[[lookup @name]] is a veteran spy for the Tayan Empire, he is also a formidable mage.

Servitor.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can contact its master, sending inaudible communication which is instantaneously received by its controller as long as that other creature is capable of receiving messages.

Self Destruct.actiondesc: When this creature triggers its self-destruct protocol, it is consumed in a fiery explosion that attacks the Fortitude defense of all nearby creatures that fail to resist the effect.

Self-Repair.actiondesc: The construct recovers its Toughness value in Health and immediately ends a single status condition of its choice that is currently affecting it.

Uncanny Eye.description:
The [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s fixates its eye on a creature that it can see within 120 feet of itself and chooses one of the options listed below. It cannot use the same option more than once per round.

Suarrok.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Suarrok are exceeding strange creatures, with singular eye, feathers, bat-like wings, two tails, and a long, piercing beak. They are surprisingly agile despite their strange form, and their eyes possess considerable magical power, capable of harming creatures through simple stares alone.

Behavior

Suarroks are highly territorial creatures, favoring rugged, high perches to build their nests and scout for prey below. Suarroks are primarily nocturnal hunters, but can be encountered at any time of day, and grow bolder the longer they go uncontested in their territory.

Relying on their uncanny eye and blinding gaze to disorient prey during ambushes, they descend rapidly upon unsuspecting targets, their piercing calls drawing the eye and often resulting in stunned prey. Their long, piercing beaks drive through stunned prey, killing them instantly, and allowing them to feed on the spot, or carry off the carcass for later consumption.

Suarrok are opportunistic feeders, primarily hunting unwary ground mammals or prowling coastlines and bodies of water where they can dive on unsuspecting sea life. They have been known to attack the occasional unwary traveler.

Solitary by nature, Suarroks fiercely defend their territory against any intruders, including others of their kind, even driving off their young as soon as they are old enough to fly. During mating season they communicate through a series of eerie, high-pitched calls and the flashes of their luminescent gaze.

For a cyclopean creature, the Suarrok has been observed hunting, flying, and fighting without any issue. It is speculated that the creature's single eye perceives the world differently, allowing it to see more, and compensate for a lack of depth perception.

Lore

The Suarrok is an ancient creature believed to have originated from Ragen, given their burning stare, thought there is little evidence otherwise to support this. There is a spirited debate about the Suarrok in the halls of academia and its true nature as a monstrosity. Most recognize that the Suarrok is not a natural creature, not a beast in the most classical sense, yet it does have the hallmarks of one, as the Suarrok have been observed to nest, mate, hunt, and generally act as a beast would.

Suarroks are generally left undisturbed due to their aggressive nature, though seasoned hunters and adventurers sometimes seek them out for the valuable resources they can provide. Their eyes are particularly valuable to alchemists and enchanters, believed to hold potent, magical properties associated with blindness and fire.

The large feathers from their wings are prized as materials for clothing, art, decoration, and for the larger ancestries — high-quality quills. Lastly, Suarrok leather is light and sturdy, but rare, making it valuable, as is fresh Suarrok meat, though the bitter aftertaste makes it an acquired taste at best.
Suarrok.biographypublic:
Seeing a juvenile was an unsettling encounter. Now, it borders on horrifying as this raptavian super-predator gazes down upon you. Its body, while enormous, is lithe, with webbed wings ending in razor sharp talons. Its long, serpentine neck ends in a head that has a spear-like beak the length of two fully grown men. Its eye is a singular gemstone of pure malice and predatory instinct, it radiates chaotic energy and arcane power. Gazing into it, you feel dizzy, nauseous, blinded all at once.

The [[lookup @name lowercase]] is the adult stage of its lesser suarrok juvenile. It has grown monstrous in size, with a wingspan that measures 40 feet, if not greater. This raptavian-super predator makes its homes in rocky regions like the Forest of Stone. As it has aged, the [[lookup @name lowercase]]'s eye has grown stronger, with a variable kaleidoscope of abilities that it can use and direct at its prey or would be intruders into its territory.

Unseen Servant.name: Unseen Servant
Unseen Servant.description:
This spell creates an Invisible, mindless, shapeless, Medium force that performs simple tasks at your command until the spell ends. The servant springs into existence in an unoccupied space on the ground within range. It has AC 10, 1 Hit Point, and a Strength of 2, and it can't attack. If it drops to 0 Hit Points, the spell ends.

Once on each of your turns as a Bonus Action, you can mentally command the servant to move up to 15 feet and interact with an object. The servant can perform simple tasks that a human could do, such as fetching things, cleaning, mending, folding clothes, lighting fires, serving food, and pouring drinks. Once you give the command, the servant performs the task to the best of its ability until it completes the task, then waits for your next command.

If you command the servant to perform a task that would move it more than 60 feet away from you, the spell ends.

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Brackus von Tet.biographyprivate:
This retired gladiator owns and operates a smithy in The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c]{Smokerie}, where he not only crafts noteworthy arms and armor — he forges a new life for himself in the wake of his affiliation with @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero} and her cult of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}-worshiping warriors known as @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{The Undaunted}. The circumstances of [[lookup @name]]'s departure from The Undaunted remain a mystery to most citizens of Ordain (including fans of the notorious Havoc Games at which Brackus excelled). Some say Brackus forged a rift between fellow members of The Undaunted (if not Zira herself), while others contend he simply aged out of his prime. Whatever the case, Brackus has a tendency to change subjects when the issue arises in conversation, and is always more eager to talk about the actual science of combat and associated tools of the trade.

Personality

[[lookup @name]]'s rugged looks match his demeanor, which represents the textbook definition of determination. With a desire for control as his guide, Brackus maintains an element of apprehension at nearly all times, letting his guard down only when surrounded by contemporaries he can trust (which are getting harder and harder to find these days). Brackus curbs the gruff aspects of his nature as much as possible for potential customers, but regulars get the brunt of his unfiltered pragmatism and thoughtful speculations.

Connections

[[lookup @name]] is a former member of the Undaunted, a team of daredevil athletes who are the current reigning champions of the Havoc Games held at Grand Kalion Stadium in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}. The Undaunted devote their lives to rigorous training under the leadership of Zira Hestidero, a power-hungry warlock of the shard god Ku'arta. Indeed, it was Zira's overzealous quest for power that first led Brackus to question her leadership in the arena — a confrontation that subsequently led to his estrangement. For nearly a year, Brackus has built up his small business using both his acumen with a hammer and his notoriety as one of the best Havoc Games athletes the city's ever known.

[[lookup @name]]'s lineage includes some of the first Altyrans to occupy Ordain during its construction; and while the von Tet house has diminished in stature throughout the years that followed, their qualities of pride and resilience have not.

Brackus von Tet.biographypublic:
This ruggedly handsome Altyra wears the trademark tools of a blacksmith upon his belt, and is clad in stylish-but-practical Ordani garb, with the slightest nod to western methods in the way he ties the long silver ropes of his dreadlocked hair. His medium-brown skin is patterned with a lattice of orange birthmarks the color of oak leaves in late autumn, but you also spy a palimpsest of scars that betray a history of danger or physical conflict. There is an unmistakable athleticism on display in the cords of his muscles and the focus of his movement, and you cant help but wonder about the previous lives this stoic craftsman has led.

[[lookup @name]] is a steady-handed smithy who operates a modest forge in Ordain's Smokerie district known as Untarnished Munitions. Although he's currently known for the quality of his craftsmanship, Brackus also carries the legacy of his former career as a player in the notorious Havoc Games of Grand Kalion Stadium. Indeed, some of von Tet's most valued customers are fans of his erstwhile occupation as a gladiator, and expect a tale or two from the rugged smithy as part of their transaction when they visit his shop.

Magic Initiate.name: Magic Initiate
Magic Initiate.description:
[[lookup @name]] has received knowledge from an elder entity of the cosmos, allowing her to gain the Magic Initiate Origin feat. She gains the following benefits.

Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbSpells0000000.JournalEntryPage.SkHptN2PTzFGDaEj]{Cleric}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbSpells0000000.JournalEntryPage.LhvuDQEyrCdg5EfU]{Druid}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbSpells0000000.JournalEntryPage.6AnqLUowgdsqMFvz]{Wizard} spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat's cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list.

Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.

Identify.name: Identify
Identify.description:
You touch an object throughout the spell’s casting. If the object is a magic item or some other magical object, you learn its properties and how to use them, whether it requires Attunement, and how many charges it has, if any. You learn whether any ongoing spells are affecting the item and what they are. If the item was created by a spell, you learn that spell’s name.

If you instead touch a creature throughout the casting, you learn which ongoing spells, if any, are currently affecting it.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

Message.name: Message
Message.description:
You point toward a creature within range and whisper a message. The target (and only the target) hears the message and can reply in a whisper that only you can hear.

You can cast this spell through solid objects if you are familiar with the target and know it is beyond the barrier. Magical silence; 1 foot of stone, metal, or wood; or a thin sheet of lead blocks the spell.

Helice Korsos.biographyprivate:
[[lookup @name]] works from home and isn’t afraid to use her natural charm and feminine guile during business negotiations. Her clothes are loose and revealing, worn with supreme confidence, shrouded in curious fey esoterica.

Personality

[[lookup @name]] is a mystifying woman, both in terms of her skill as a spellcaster and her ability to calm others. While affable and inviting, she also maintains an air of healthy suspicion at all times. Her resting expression is one of measured curiosity, accented by her constant presence of poise and grace.

Connections

Prior to her patronage by the Casia known as Vesper, [[lookup @name]] was a warlock of the shard god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}, an association that plagues her to this very day thanks to other ghosts of her past …

Helice was once the lover of @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero}, the two-fisted champion of the Undaunted. But Zira’s dangerous ambitions led their relationship to ruin, and a broken-hearted Helice had to reluctantly sever their intimate connection in order to maintain her own values and personal integrity.

Phrases

"Phrase 1."

"Phrase 2."

"Phrase 3.
Helice Korsos.biographypublic:
Shrouded in occult mystique and the sweet aroma of fresh lavender, this alluring woman of mixed ancestry is a breathtaking display of self-confidence on legs. With skin the color of ashen mauve and a sultry mane of ginger hair tied atop her thoughtful head, she appears quite comfortable in her unconventionally athletic skin. Furthermore, her eyes betray a keen mental acuity that her infectious charisma only accentuates. You take note of a few arcane baubles that decorate her delicate limbs and feminine curves, and can't help but wonder precisely which one of these trinkets she uses to focus the eldritch powers that have made her famous.

[[lookup @name]] is a congenial spellcaster-for-hire located in Ordain's Orchard Lanes district, where she utilizes the arcane patronage of a powerful Casia known as Vesper to provide services for locals in need. Known for her affable personality and the inviting qualities of her home parlor, Helice is a casual friend to many — but remains the close companion of only a select few.

Jorey Swift.biographyprivate:
[[lookup @name]] wears the trademark burgundy and gray clothing of his Undaunted comrades, lightly-inspired by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Maziran} martial arts taught to him by @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero}, and is instructed in the ways of unarmed combat. Like most of his allies, this audacious young warrior hopes to one day strike an arcane pact with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}, the Shard God of Torment. [[lookup @name]] wears the red sash that signifies his station as an @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]{Undaunted Trainee}, but he has yet to earn the signature cowl of his @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted Adept} counterparts.

Personality

Certain amounts of pride and ambition are necessary to join The Undaunted, and young [[lookup @name]] has both of these attributes in spades. Precocious at heart, Jorey has been calloused in recent years by the harsh dynamics of modern life as an orphan. Nevertheless, he remains a quick study — a quality that has served him well under Zira's unforgiving tutelage. Thanks to his own tireless perfectionism, Jorey is valued among his fellow teammates a natural-born-contender in the Havoc Games, and shows great promise for the seasons to come (as both an athlete and an eldritch spellcaster).

In combat, Jorey will work in tandem with his allies to quickly take down the most powerful foe or whomever the group might identify as a formidable spellcaster (as knowledgeable of the arcane as they are). Jorey's also eager to prove himself to more experienced Undaunted members (including, first and foremost, Zira herself), and will display excessive bravado on the battlefield whenever he can.

Connections

[[lookup @name]] is a member of the Undaunted, a team of daredevil athletes who are the current reigning champions of the Havoc Games held at Grand Kalion Stadium in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}. The Undaunted devote their lives to rigorous training under the leadership of Zira Hestidero, a power-hungry warlock of the shard god Ku'arta. As part of his training, [[lookup @name]] possesses relatively little in the way of personal treasures or resources (particularly compared to other arena athletes), but does retain at least one valuable or cherished possession from their previous lives: a wooden token from a city fair when he was five, etched with an image of a cartoon dragon. This trinket, like those owned by his compatriots, serves to remind Jorey of the life of weakness he's chosen to leave behind.

The most salient part of that former life is Jorey's uncle, the famed caravaneer @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift}, who Jorey only has fleeting memories of. Following the semi-recent death of Agraband's sister Selena, Jorey was consigned to a few tough years as an orphan alongside the other youths of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c]{Home Away From Home} hostel. It's here that Jorey met his Undaunted cohorts and started a new life for himself — a life that Agraband knows very little of.

Phrases

"You gotta be kidding me."

"I've got five good reasons for you to mind your own business …"

"Ordain is like a boiling kettle: as soon as you turn your back, you've got a real mess on your hands."
Jorey Swift.biographypublic:
You regard an agile Ordani teenager, no more than the age of sixteen, with a western-worn topknot of auburn hair. Dressed in the short-sleeved robes of a martial artist, the scrappy young athlete looks like he's ready to take on the whole world. A silver-stitched crimson sash is tied around his waist, and you spy the hilt of a dagger or two poking out from the fold of his garments. There's something familiar about his expression, a certain wanderlust in his eyes, but you can't readily place it.

[[lookup @name]] is a junior member of Zira Hestidero's cohort of athletes known as The Undaunted. Driven by the same zealous brinksmanship as their seniors, these headstrong youths are notorious amongst the people of Ordain, who know them to be the unchallenged champions of local arena combat. Many Atericans call the collective group of adepts and trainees under Zira Hestidero's brash leadership a "team" or "organization," while others would simply (if not dismissively) label them a gang. As one of the newer members of this so-called gang, Jorey has shown a great deal of promise — but a test of his loyalty is close at hand.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: [[lookup @name]] makes three [[/item Unarmed Strike]] attacks.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
[[lookup @name]] is an [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

[[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of her character sheet. She automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Parry.name: Parry
Parry.description:
Trigger: The [[lookup @name]] is [[lookup @activation.condition activity=aLG3BRZL7P6OEjwd]].

Response: The [[lookup @name]] adds [[lookup @roll.formula activity=aLG3BRZL7P6OEjwd]] to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

Thaumaturgy.name: Thaumaturgy
Thaumaturgy.description:
You manifest a minor wonder within range. You create one of the effects below within range. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time.

Altered Eyes. You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.

Booming Voice. Your voice booms up to three times as loud as normal for 1 minute. For the duration, you have Advantage on [[/check ability=cha skill=itm]] checks.

Fire Play. You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.

Invisible Hand. You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.

Phantom Sound. You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point of your choice within range, such as a rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous whispers.

Tremors. You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.

Bane.name: Bane
Bane.description:
Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within range must each make a Charisma saving throw. Whenever a target that fails this save makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must subtract 1d4 from the attack roll or save.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Expeditious Retreat.name: Expeditious Retreat
Expeditious Retreat.description: You take the Dash action, and until the spell ends, you can take that action again as a Bonus Action.

Hex.name: Hex
Hex.description:
You place a curse on a creature that you can see within range. Until the spell ends, you deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage to the target whenever you hit it with an attack roll. Also, choose one ability when you cast the spell. The target has Disadvantage on ability checks made with the chosen ability.

If the target drops to 0 Hit Points before this spell ends, you can take a Bonus Action on a later turn to curse a new creature.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. Your Concentration can last longer with a spell slot of level 2 (up to 4 hours), 3–4 (up to 8 hours), or 5+ (24 hours).

Hold Person.name: Hold Person
Hold Person.description:
Choose a Humanoid that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[paralyzed apply=false] condition for the duration. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional Humanoid for each spell slot level above 2.

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.

Mind Spike.name: Mind Spike
Mind Spike.description:
You drive a spike of psionic energy into the mind of one creature you can see within range. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw, taking 3d8 Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, you also always know the target's location until the spell ends, but only while the two of you are on the same plane of existence. While you have this knowledge, the target can't become hidden from you, and if it has the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition, it gains no benefit from that condition against you.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 2.

Eldritch Blast.name: Eldritch Blast
Eldritch Blast.description:
You hurl a beam of crackling energy. Make a ranged spell attack against one creature or object in range. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Force damage.

Cantrip Upgrade. The spell creates two beams at level 5, three beams at level 11, and four beams at level 17. You can direct the beams at the same target or at different ones. Make a separate attack roll for each beam.

[[(floor((@attributes.spell.level+1)/6)+1)]]{Total Beams}

Vampiric Touch.name: Vampiric Touch
Vampiric Touch.description:
The touch of your shadow-wreathed hand can siphon life force from others to heal your wounds. Make a melee spell attack against one creature within reach. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 Necrotic damage, and you regain Hit Points equal to half the amount of Necrotic damage dealt.

Until the spell ends, you can make the attack again on each of your turns as a Magic action, targeting the same creature or a different one.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

Black Tentacles.name: Black Tentacles
Black Tentacles.description:
Squirming, ebony tentacles fill a 20-foot square on ground that you can see within range. For the duration, these tentacles turn the ground in that area into &Reference[DifficultTerrain].

Each creature in that area makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 3d6 Bludgeoning damage, and it has the &Reference[Restrained apply=false] condition until the spell ends. A creature also makes that save if it enters the area or ends it turn there. A creature makes that save only once per turn.

A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC, ending the condition on itself on a success.

Phantasmal Killer.name: Phantasmal Killer
Phantasmal Killer.description:
You tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see within range and create an illusion of its deepest fears, visible only to that creature. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 4d10 Psychic damage and has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls for the duration. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and the spell ends.

For the duration, the target makes a [[/save ability=wis dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a failed save, it takes the Psychic damage again. On a successful save, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.The damage increases by 1d10 for each spell slot level above 4.

Eldritch Mind.name: Eldritch Mind
Eldritch Mind.description: [[lookup @name]] has Advantage on Constitution saving throws that she makes to maintain Concentration.

Magic Initiate.name: Magic Initiate
Magic Initiate.description:
[[lookup @name]] has received knowledge from an elder entity of the cosmos, allowing her to gain the Magic Initiate Origin feat. She gains the following benefits.

Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbSpells0000000.JournalEntryPage.SkHptN2PTzFGDaEj]{Cleric}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbSpells0000000.JournalEntryPage.LhvuDQEyrCdg5EfU]{Druid}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbSpells0000000.JournalEntryPage.6AnqLUowgdsqMFvz]{Wizard} spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat's cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list.

Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.

Command.name: Command
Command.description:
You speak a one-word command to a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or follow the command on its next turn. Choose the command from these options:

Approach. The target moves toward you by the shortest and most direct route, ending its turn if it moves within 5 feet of you.

Drop. The target drops whatever it is holding and then ends its turn.

Flee. The target spends its turn moving away from you by the fastest available means.

Grovel. The target has the Prone condition and then ends its turn.

Halt. On its turn, the target doesn't move and takes no action or Bonus Action.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can affect one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Resistance.name: Resistance
Resistance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a damage type: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Radiant, Slashing, or Thunder. When the creature takes damage of the chosen type before the spell ends, the creature reduces the total damage taken by 1d4. A creature can benefit from this spell only once per turn.

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Dark Devotion.name: Dark Devotion
Dark Devotion.description: [[lookup @name]] has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

Temple of Ku'arta Key.name: Temple of Ku'arta Key
Temple of Ku'arta Key.description: This gold and platinum key opens the locked doors inside the Kalion Stadium Underworks, including all secret doors.

Eldritch Defense.name: Eldritch Defense
Eldritch Defense.description: While [[lookup @name]] is wearing no armor and wielding no shield, her AC includes her Charisma modifier.

Lethal.name: Lethal
Lethal.description: The [[lookup @name]]'s melee and ranged weapon attacks deal an additional 1d4 damage of the base weapon's damage type.

Chill Touch.name: Chill Touch
Chill Touch.description:
Channeling the chill of the grave, make a melee spell attack against a target within reach. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Necrotic damage, and it can't regain Hit Points until the end of your next turn.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d10 when you reach levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10).

Zira Hestidero.biographyprivate:
Headquartered in Ordain after a challenging youth in the Kelmezian City State of Kalaxa, [[lookup @name]] is one of the most indomitable athletes the Solar Games have ever known. What nearly everyone doesn't know (including her Undaunted cohorts) is that ZIra utilizes the brinksmanship of her motley gang of daredevils as both front and fuel to pursue her own enigmatic goals — which include the forthcoming betrayal of her patron Ku'arta in favor of the eldritch power of an outer god.

Personality

Zira is both arrogant and cruel, but manages to turn these traits to her advantage by way of her intense charisma, echoed by the intense emerald shade of her eyes and the mystique of her well-honed arcane techniques. Zira’s lean and muscular physique is a testament to her youth spent in those fight clubs of Kalaxa to the west, and her current life of cruel ambition is her never-ending attempt to outrun the shadows of that troubling past.

As a former pit fighter, Zira has a masterful grasp of environmental hazards and the logic of the battlefield. She’s quick to use such things to her tactical advantage, and is fond of pushing her allies and enemies to their breaking points. Indeed, Zira is known to use aggressive spells like @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj.Item.DuD1KxoSSwGmcLiC], @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj.Item.AlbkwgyKp1C6BAQq], and @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj.Item.1IfWKKgb0u5dNPHm] to abusively manipulate friend and foe alike. She's also famous for bringing her opponents to the brink of death, only to spare them for the cruelty and humiliation of a future proving.

Connections

[[lookup @name]] is the team leader of the @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted}, a gang of daredevil athletes who are the current reigning champions of the Solar Games held at Grand Kalion Stadium in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}. The Undaunted devote their lives to rigorous training under Zira's leadership, and possesses relatively little in the way of personal treasures or resources — unlike Zira herself, who maintains a remarkable collection of arcane trinkets and eldritch lore.

Zira Hestidero cultivates a counterculture profile as something of an antihero to the people of Ordain, but keeps her private life relatively clandestine, conducting sensitive business either via proxies or using a clever disguise. The various members of the Undaunted whom Zira considers to be her acolytes view the senior warlock with a mix of respect and fear, but the awe they share for her abilities — and subsequent interest in her otherworldly patron — are equal in measure. Tall tales abound regarding the mythological triumphs of Zira's past (many of which may likely be true).

Phrases

"Prepare to learn a lesson you'll never forget."

"You can't change the world without rearranging a few faces first."

"A life without ambition is a life wasted."
Zira Hestidero.biographypublic:
The lean and muscular woman that stands before you is a paragon of physical acuity and raw charisma. Captivating from buzzed head to sandaled toe, this chiseled bruiser could easily handle herself in a brawl or command a crowded room. Her lean athletic form is clad in revealing gray and crimson robes, loosely cut like those of a martial artist or esoteric mystic. Whoever she is, you'll never forget those piercing emerald eyes and her unassailable smirk.

Opportunistic by nature and unrivaled in athleticism, [[lookup @name]] is a Kalaxan warlock of the undying shard god Ku'arta, and is known by most Ordani as the brash leader of The Undaunted — a ragtag enclave of scrappy adherents who are the reigning champions of Grand Kalion Stadium's famous Solar Games. Zira's bombastic antics (in the arena and otherwise), along with her team's nearly flawless record, have catapulted her to the role of local celebrity. And this notoriety shows no sign of slowing down.

Dark Devotion.description: The [[lookup @name]] has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

Pack Tactics.name: Pack Tactics
Pack Tactics.description: The [[lookup @name]] has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the [[lookup @name]]'s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

Fear Aura.name: Fear Aura

The [[lookup @name]] emanates an aura in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=oT8238p9jXwVy76c]]-foot Emanation while it doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.
