Abyss-Warped Undaunted.biographyprivate:
An [[lookup @name]] is the byproduct of an eldritch ritual in service of an abyssal entity, during which the humanoid warrior's literal flesh and bones are ripped from their body and replaced with gruesome tentacular growths and glistening disordered flesh. Scraps of burgundy and gray Undaunted uniform remain, but this misshapen creature is a far cry from the person it once was.

Anatomy

[[lookup @name]] are humanoid creatures that have been malformed by evil eldritch magic, and each limb that is severed during the ritual that creates them is replaced with a horrible growth of mangled tentacles and mutable flesh. These aberrations are the progeny of the void, misshapen and unholy, and feast on whatever organic material they deem worthy — be it blood or brains or worse.

Behavior

The mind of an [[lookup @name]] has been fractured by the insidious and unknowable metaphysics of the Abyss, and they no longer behave according to societal norms. In and out of combat, [[lookup @name]]s will obediently serve the whims and commands of any abyssal masters or eldritch spellcasters that might lord over them, working in tandem to dispatch those enemies deemed most threatening or savory for consumption.

Lore

[[lookup @name]] are are the result of a gruesome ritual known as The Coalescence — in which their flesh and bones are torn asunder to summon the grotesque melange known as the @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su]{Grim Assembly}, a horrendous eldritch creature that serves the inscrutable whims of the Outer God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VUhtOxDvWc3I7pY2]{Sha-Xotha}.

Prior to their gruesome transformations, [[lookup @name]] were members of the eponymous Undaunted, a team of daredevil athletes who are the current reigning champions of the Havoc Games held at Grand Kalion Stadium in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}. The Undaunted devote their lives to rigorous training under the leadership of Zira Hestidero, a power-hungry warlock of the shard god Ku'arta. As part of their training, [[lookup @name]]s possessed relatively little in the way of personal treasures or resources (particularly compared to other arena athletes), but did retain at least one valuable or cherished possession from their previous lives — a token to remind them of the life of weakness they’ve chosen to leave behind. Occasionally, a [[lookup @name]] still possesses these items after the advent of their abyssal transformation.
Abyss-Warped Undaunted.biographypublic:
This grotesque humanoid warrior appears horribly malformed. Where an arm should be, a mass of tentacles writhes in its place; instead of two normal legs, you find at least one gruesome stump tipped in fleshy pseudopodia. And the loathsome creature's singular bloodshot eye is a terrible sight to behold in its own right — pulsing angrier and redder than the fire moon itself. This monstrous entity is a freak of nature, an impossible arrangement of mutilation and regrowth and muscle that squelches with each hideous step.

[[lookup @name]] were once the headstrong warrior-acolytes of Zira Hestidero's cohort of athletes known as the Undaunted. Driven by zealous brinksmanship in service of the shard god Ku'arta, these headstrong gladiators were notorious amongst the people of Ordain, who knew them to be the unchallenged champions of local arena combat. Now, this gang of would-be legends are little more than the accursed pawns of abyssal entities, warped and reshaped into their chaotic image.

Grim Assembly.name: Grim Assembly

Abyssal Monster.name: Abyssal Monster
Abyssal Monster.description:
The [[lookup @name]] is an unknowable alien entity. It is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (Insight) checks made to ascertain the [[lookup @name]]'s intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.

The [[lookup @name]] and all Abyssal creatures are opposed by Life and Light, making them vulnerable to radiant damage.

Abyssal Remains.name: Abyssal Remains
Abyssal Remains.description:
When the [[lookup @name]] dies, it dissolves into a thick liquid often described as “melted shadow,” which spreads in an oozing pour from the place where it died, soaking a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=0CtCrqPc5KbnIvoc]]-foot radius around it in viscous corruption.

Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=0CtCrqPc5KbnIvoc]], each creature within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=0CtCrqPc5KbnIvoc]] feet of the [[lookup @name]] when it dies.

Failure: The target is cursed with Cursed Vision until the end of its next long rest.

Cursed Vision. Shadowy film clings to the creature’s eyes. While afflicted, the creature has disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, and attack rolls against the creature have advantage. In addition, the creature can’t benefit from darkvision.

Note: After Alpha, Abyssal Residue may remain on the ground and/or be found in locations where an abyssal creature died, affecting anyone who moves through its space. When this feature is active, the residue will remain in place for 1 week before fading away. If located in an area without direct light from Lantyr, the residue will remain for 1 month.

Eye Blast.name: Eye Blast
Eye Blast.description:
The [[lookup @name]] fires a concentrated beam of arcane energy in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=dnd5eactivity000]]-foot line that is [[lookup @target.template.width activity=dnd5eactivity000]] ft. wide.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], each creature in the area.

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage, and the target is pushed 10 feet away from the [[lookup @name]].

Success: Half damage.

Dreadful Glare.name: Dreadful Glare
Dreadful Glare.description:
Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], one creature it can see within [[lookup @range.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet that can see the [[lookup @name]]

Failure: The target has the &Reference[frightened] condition until the end of its next turn.

Unnerving Gaze.name: Unnerving Gaze
Unnerving Gaze.description:
Trigger: A [[lookup @target.affects.type activity=btp6NZvx465nxWTF]] the [[lookup @name]] can see starts its turn within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=btp6NZvx465nxWTF]] feet of the [[lookup @name]] and can see the [[lookup @name]].

Response—Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=btp6NZvx465nxWTF]], the triggering [[lookup @target.affects.type activity=btp6NZvx465nxWTF]].

Failure: The target has the &Reference[frightened] condition until the end of its turn.

Success: The target is immune to this [[lookup @name]]'s Unnerving Gaze for 24 hours.

Multiphased.name: Multiphased
Multiphased.description:
When the [[lookup @name]] loses half or more of its hit points, it absorbs its NPC summoner for a 2nd Phase of the encounter and gains the following attributes:

  • It regains HP equal to those it has lost during the encounter, returning to full health.

  • It gains the @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su.Item.Whfc2i6PDqqBX02h]{Magic Initiate (2nd Phase)} and @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su.Item.7BgT6T8ZlmNljgdA]{Spellcasting (2nd Phase)} features plus all associated spells and spell slots of the summoner.

  • It gains the [[/item Scuttle (2nd Phase)]] Legendary Action.

Scuttle (2nd Phase).name: Scuttle (2nd Phase)
Scuttle (2nd Phase).description: The [[lookup @name]] moves up to half its Speed without provoking an &Reference[Opportunity Attacks]{Opportunity Attack}.

Grab.name: Grab
Grab.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the &Reference[Grappled apply=false] condition (escape DC [[lookup @skills.ath.passive]]).

Eldritch Mind.name: Eldritch Mind
Eldritch Mind.description: The [[lookup @name]] has Advantage on Constitution saving throws that it makes to maintain Concentration.

Spellcasting (2nd Phase).name: Spellcasting (2nd Phase)
Spellcasting (2nd Phase).description:
The [[lookup @name]] is an [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

The [[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of its character sheet. It automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Eldritch Blast.name: Eldritch Blast
Eldritch Blast.description:
You hurl a beam of crackling energy. Make a ranged spell attack against one creature or object in range. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Force damage.

Cantrip Upgrade. The spell creates two beams at level 5, three beams at level 11, and four beams at level 17. You can direct the beams at the same target or at different ones. Make a separate attack roll for each beam.

[[(floor((@attributes.spell.level+1)/6)+1)]]{Total Beams}

Mage Hand.name: Mage Hand
Mage Hand.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

Resistance.name: Resistance
Resistance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a damage type: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Radiant, Slashing, or Thunder. When the creature takes damage of the chosen type before the spell ends, the creature reduces the total damage taken by 1d4. A creature can benefit from this spell only once per turn.

Thaumaturgy.name: Thaumaturgy
Thaumaturgy.description:
You manifest a minor wonder within range. You create one of the effects below within range. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time.

Altered Eyes. You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.

Booming Voice. Your voice booms up to three times as loud as normal for 1 minute. For the duration, you have Advantage on [[/check ability=cha skill=itm]] checks.

Fire Play. You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.

Invisible Hand. You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.

Phantom Sound. You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point of your choice within range, such as a rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous whispers.

Tremors. You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.

True Strike.name: True Strike
True Strike.description:
Guided by a flash of magical insight, you make one attack with the weapon used in the spell's casting. The attack uses your spellcasting ability for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity. If the attack deals damage, it can be Radiant damage or the weapon's normal damage type (your choice).

Cantrip Upgrade. Whether you deal Radiant damage or the weapon's normal damage type, the attack deals extra Radiant damage when you reach levels 5 (1d6), 11 (2d6), and 17 (3d6).

Bane.name: Bane
Bane.description:
Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within range must each make a Charisma saving throw. Whenever a target that fails this save makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must subtract 1d4 from the attack roll or save.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Black Tentacles.name: Black Tentacles
Black Tentacles.description:
Squirming, ebony tentacles fill a 20-foot square on ground that you can see within range. For the duration, these tentacles turn the ground in that area into &Reference[DifficultTerrain].

Each creature in that area makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 3d6 Bludgeoning damage, and it has the &Reference[Restrained apply=false] condition until the spell ends. A creature also makes that save if it enters the area or ends it turn there. A creature makes that save only once per turn.

A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC, ending the condition on itself on a success.

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.

Expeditious Retreat.name: Expeditious Retreat
Expeditious Retreat.description: You take the Dash action, and until the spell ends, you can take that action again as a Bonus Action.

Hex.name: Hex
Hex.description:
You place a curse on a creature that you can see within range. Until the spell ends, you deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage to the target whenever you hit it with an attack roll. Also, choose one ability when you cast the spell. The target has Disadvantage on ability checks made with the chosen ability.

If the target drops to 0 Hit Points before this spell ends, you can take a Bonus Action on a later turn to curse a new creature.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. Your Concentration can last longer with a spell slot of level 2 (up to 4 hours), 3–4 (up to 8 hours), or 5+ (24 hours).

Hold Person.name: Hold Person
Hold Person.description:
Choose a Humanoid that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[paralyzed apply=false] condition for the duration. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional Humanoid for each spell slot level above 2.

Mind Spike.name: Mind Spike
Mind Spike.description:
You drive a spike of psionic energy into the mind of one creature you can see within range. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw, taking 3d8 Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, you also always know the target's location until the spell ends, but only while the two of you are on the same plane of existence. While you have this knowledge, the target can't become hidden from you, and if it has the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition, it gains no benefit from that condition against you.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 2.

Phantasmal Killer.name: Phantasmal Killer
Phantasmal Killer.description:
You tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see within range and create an illusion of its deepest fears, visible only to that creature. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 4d10 Psychic damage and has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls for the duration. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and the spell ends.

For the duration, the target makes a [[/save ability=wis dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a failed save, it takes the Psychic damage again. On a successful save, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.The damage increases by 1d10 for each spell slot level above 4.

Vampiric Touch.name: Vampiric Touch
Vampiric Touch.description:
The touch of your shadow-wreathed hand can siphon life force from others to heal your wounds. Make a melee spell attack against one creature within reach. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 Necrotic damage, and you regain Hit Points equal to half the amount of Necrotic damage dealt.

Until the spell ends, you can make the attack again on each of your turns as a Magic action, targeting the same creature or a different one.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

Command.name: Command
Command.description:
You speak a one-word command to a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or follow the command on its next turn. Choose the command from these options:

Approach. The target moves toward you by the shortest and most direct route, ending its turn if it moves within 5 feet of you.

Drop. The target drops whatever it is holding and then ends its turn.

Flee. The target spends its turn moving away from you by the fastest available means.

Grovel. The target has the Prone condition and then ends its turn.

Halt. On its turn, the target doesn't move and takes no action or Bonus Action.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can affect one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes two [[/item .VMpHGSgWScoqfGgc]] attacks. It can replace one attack with a [[/item .ZEAiCr0gkEHljw3i]], [[/item .CRXmrlUmT9ur8h5y]], or [[/item .2NjkNnR4hMiz57Ix]] attack.

Magic Initiate (2nd Phase).name: Magic Initiate (2nd Phase)
Magic Initiate (2nd Phase).description: The [[lookup @name]] has received knowledge from an elder entity of the cosmos. They know @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplResistance]{Resistance} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMageHand00]{Mage Hand} and has @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCommand000]{Command} prepared. It can cast Command without expending a spell slot once per Long Rest. For it, these spells count as Warlock spells.

Enthralling Glare.name: Enthralling Glare
Enthralling Glare.description:
Wisdom Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]], one creature it can see within [[lookup @range.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet that can see the [[lookup @name]]

Failure: The target has the &Reference[charmed] condition until the end of its next turn.

Grim Assembly.biographyprivate:
Conjured from the depths of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss} using accursed terrestrial components and the skin and bone of foolhardy acolytes, the [[lookup @name]] is a formidable emissary of the outer gods, bearing the weight of cosmic doom and eldritch destruction with its countless gangly limbs.

Anatomy

The [[lookup @name]] is comprised of the body parts of several smaller humanoid creatures, including their flesh, limbs, organs, and viscera. All of these elements coalesce around one key feature: the enormous crimson eye that acts as a catalyst for the monster's creation. Regarded as a sacred relic by servants of outer gods, this profane artifact is integral to the [[lookup @name]]'s horrible advent. Meanwhile, the inscrutable workings of the [[lookup @name]]'s hideous eldritch biology are as unknowable as the void itself.

Behavior

Guided by the cryptic whims of its abyssal masters, the [[lookup @name]] is an aberrant creature with otherworldly motives. And while spellcasters of Ember may try to wrangle the chaotic devastation wrought by a blasphemous creature such as this, they will most likely never succeed.

Lore

The [[lookup @name]] is a horrendous eldritch creature that serves the inscrutable whims of the Outer God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VUhtOxDvWc3I7pY2]{Sha-Xotha}, and is brought to life during a gruesome ritual referred to in profane texts as "The Coalescence," in which the flesh and bones of several humanoid acolytes are torn asunder and reassembled into a grotesque melange. Traditionally, the summoner who conjures the Assembly is absorbed into the large creature's loathsome mass as well, often during combat when the [[lookup @name]]'s health has been compromised.
Grim Assembly.biographypublic:
You behold a hideous entity that appears to have been formed from the glistening excoriated flesh of more than a dozen different humanoids. Vaguely quadrupedal, this loathsome amalgamation of meat and sinew is held aloft by its monstrous forelimbs — two appendages made of a half-dozen smaller arms, each adorned with several bony protrusions swathed in ichor. The slavering monster's hind section is comprised of a hideous array of humanoid legs and fleshy tentacles, which it uses to scuttle across the ground with preternatural efficacy.

It has no proper head to speak of, but the mound of horrible flesh that crowns its torso is dominated by a central crimson eye — prodigious in size, alien in origin, and utterly evil in expression. An array of warped mouths is scattered beneath this vermillion orb, and they whisper and growl in some awful cacophony, speaking a grim language you're certain you've never heard. Aside from the pupil of its terrible crimson eye, there appears to be no symmetry to the abhorrent form of this repulsive otherworldly creature.

The aberrant creature known as the [[lookup @name]] is a revulsive horror summoned to Ember by the servants of some unknown Outer God via profane and eldritch ritualism. Defined primarily by the hideous crimson eye that serves as both its physical centerpiece and supernatural keystone, this loathsome unearthly amalgam is a terrible sight to behold, cobbled together from the sundered limbs of the very acolytes that brought it into being.

Writhing Whisperer Tendril.name: Writhing Whisperer Tendril

Inscrutable.name: Inscrutable
Inscrutable.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is an unknowable abyssal entity. It is immune to any effect or spell that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts. Any skill check to ascertain this creature's intentions is made with +4 Banes.

Sight Without.name: Sight Without
Sight Without.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} has no eyes, ears, or mouth. It cannot be @Condition[blinded], @Condition[silenced], or @Condition[deafened]. It has 60ft of blindsight and can speak telepathically to any one or all creatures within 120 feet of it.

Amorphous.name: Amorphous
Amorphous.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} may move through a space as narrow as 1 inch in diameter without any penalty to its Stride. It gains a bonus to Dodge equal to half its Toughness score and is immune to the @Condition[restrained] condition.

Abyssal Whip.name: Abyssal Whip
Abyssal Whip.description: A horrifyingly elongated tendril of darkness extends out from the @ref[actor.name]{creature} and strikes a distant target.
Abyssal Whip.actiondesc: An elongated whip of darkness strikes a creature that can be sensed and physically reached. It deals Cold damage if not resisted and grasps its target, knocking it @Condition[prone] and dragging it up to 30 feet closer to the creature.

Abyssal Whispers.name: Abyssal Whispers
Abyssal Whispers.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} telepathically intrudes into a creature's mind, and floods it with thoughts and images of the Abyss. It must be able to sense the creature, and not be incapacitated to do this.
Abyssal Whispers.actiondesc:
The creature penetrates the mind of its target, dealing Psychic damage to Morale and inflicting the @Condition[disoriented] condition.

On a Critical Hit the target is compelled to move towards the @ref[actor.name]{creature} immediately upon the beginning of its next turn, spending 2 Action to do so.

Grasping Form.name: Grasping Form
Grasping Form.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} causes the ground surrounding it to erupt in countless clinging and coiling tendrils of shadow that trip and slow nearby creatures.
Grasping Form.actiondesc:
The creature grasps all nearby creatures with a myriad mass of tendrils whose touch fills you with dreadful despair dealing Cold damage to Morale. Each target must use Reflex elude their grasp or become @Condition[restrained]] (escape 4 Action or [[/skillCheck athletics 17]]).

If the creature moves while it has targets grappled in this way, those targets are also moved to remain within 15 feet of the creature.

Abyssal Remains.name: Abyssal Remains
Abyssal Remains.description: Upon death, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} dissolves into a thick liquid often described as a "melted shadow," which spreads in an oozing pour from the place where it died, soaking the area around it in abyssal corruption.
Abyssal Remains.actiondesc:
Upon death, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} spreads into a melted pool of shadow spreading in a 4 foot radius from its position. This residue remains in place for one month or unless otherwise cleansed.

Any creature within the area or who enters it upon a subsequent turn must withstand an attack against their Reflex defense or suffer Corruption damage which also afflicts them with Cursed Vision.

While affected by Cursed Vision, they cannot perceive sources of dim light and sources of bright light appear dim.

Playtest Notes: Cursed Vision is not yet automated, but will be some time after Foundry VTT version 14 becomes stable.

Extrude Tendril.name: Extrude Tendril
Extrude Tendril.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} can reach through intervening space and extrude an independent copy of one if its tendrils which separates from the body of its progenitor.
Extrude Tendril.actiondesc:
The @ref[actor.name]{creature} summons a @UUID[Actor.UXpL07GsaMzGCUVh]{Writhing Whisperer Tendril} which appears within a vacant space within 60 feet.

The @ref[actor.name]{creature} may possess up to a maximum of 3 extruded tendrils at a given time and may dismiss any number of its tendrils for free upon its own turn.

Writhing Whisperer Tendril.biographyprivate: This tendril is a part of the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Writhing Whisperer}
Writhing Whisperer Tendril.biographypublic:
This coiling tendril seems to be a longer connected part of the Writhing Whisperer's main body.

The [[lookup @name]] is an extension of an Abyssal creature, a mere limb of something that has existed on Ember for millennia, and perhaps even longer before it's arrival during the Shattering.

Pallid Ultra Drake.name: Pallid Ultra Drake

Multiattack.name: Multiattack
Multiattack.description: The [[lookup @name]] makes one attack with its [[/item Charged Bite]] and one attack with its [[/item Claws]] in either order. It can replace its Bite attack with the usage of the [[/item Spit Lightning]] ability, if available.

Slender Form.name: Slender Form
Slender Form.description: The long, slender form of the [[lookup @name]] allows it to squeeze through spaces like a creature one size smaller than itself. It still suffers all movement cost increases and penalties related to squeezing through a tight space.

Elusive Flight.name: Elusive Flight
Elusive Flight.description: The [[lookup @name]] doesn't provoke &Reference[opportunity attacks] when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

Blood Sense.name: Blood Sense
Blood Sense.description: The [[lookup @name]] has blindsight within 20 feet, but only for creatures missing any hit points. Additionally, it has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to detect or locate wounded creatures within 20 feet, even if they are hidden.

Spit Lightning.name: Spit Lightning
Spit Lightning.descriptionprivate:
The [[lookup @name]] spits a bolt of abyssal lightning that spreads out, leaping between targets as it travels through the air.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=t4Yfj9SLOfb8V04C]], each [[lookup @target.affects.type activity=t4Yfj9SLOfb8V04C]] in a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=t4Yfj9SLOfb8V04C]]-foot Cone.

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: Half damage.

Recharge: 4+

Swooping Bite.name: Swooping Bite
Swooping Bite.description:
If the [[lookup @name ]] moves at least [[lookup @range.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a [[/item Rotten Bite]]{Bite} attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] saving throw or be knocked &Reference[prone].

The [[lookup @name]] can also use this feature if it flies or falls at least [[lookup @range.value activity=dnd5eactivity000]] feet downward from an elevated position onto a creature before making its attack.

Pallid Ultra Drake.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

Drakes bear a striking resemblance to the Vile Dragon, with long, thin bodies, two fore-legs and no other limbs. They often have horns and frills, and maws lined with thin, razor sharp teeth.

Drakes are capable of flight, though they lack wings, indicating their capacity for flight comes from some other means, likely magic. The precise nature of this ability is not known.

Drakes are covered in robust scales which help protect their bodies from harm, though they rely more on their dexterity to evade attacks, rather than natural armor. This hide is similar to snake skin in texture and composition.

All drakes have intensely sharp eyesight and strong low-light vision.

Behavior

The newness of these creatures precludes the development of academic knowledge of drake behavior, so little is known beyond what direct observation may provide.

That said, drakes quickly assert themselves as apex predators in any biome they inhabit, and are naturally territorial, attacking anything that dares to enter the territory they've claimed.

Drakes are intelligent, capable of complex reasoning, and coordination in groups, even with humanoid allies despite being incapable of speech. However, since drakes are territorial and extremely willful, training them is difficult, if not impossible. Though not social by nature, drakes can and will hunt and nest together, with all members of that nest bowing to the will of largest among them.

Lore

There is little known about Drakes, as they are not naturally occurring on Ember and only began appearing in recent years. To the wider world of academics, they appear to be a chimerical blend of snake and dragon with an unknown but possibly magical origin.

The truth about them is that they were created in secret by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn], grown in a hidden blood forge, their forms patterned after @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.v6lXjfETDkrt0J7E]{Zerranyss}, a powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.EhQnCUxkJyxOSbf7]{Vile Dragon}. They were made to serve as a resources for Mutagists and their experiments, forced to become test subjects for the mutagenic compounds their numerous underground labs produce.

The ultimate goal of the mutagists was to find serums and alchemical treatments that would enhance, transform, and empower the draks, with the expectation that any such discoveries would also be applicable to the Vile Dragon they were spawned from.
Pallid Ultra Drake.biographypublic:
This large drake boasts a long, coiling body adorned with olive-green scales that shimmer in the light, culminating in a flared tail with pristine teal frills. More of these elegant teal frills adorn its neck and back, complementing the long, gleaming teal horns that fan out gracefully from the back of its head. Its amber-orange eyes gleam with acute awareness and intelligence. Its maw is filled with rows of razor sharp teeth.

[[lookup @name]] are newly discovered draconic monsters that boast impressive speed and dexterity. While they appear to be descended from or related to dragons, the true nature of their origin is presently unknown.

Pit Trap Bouncer.name: Pit Trap Bouncer

Exceptional Taste.name: Exceptional Taste
Exceptional Taste.description: Your attire is a more powerful a tool in your handling of social situations than any blade or spell. When you are wearing clean clothing instead of armor you may roll and add a 1d4 to any Deception, Persuasion, or Intimidation skill check.

Quick Grapple.name: Quick Grapple
Quick Grapple.description:
Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=aDWVHpJgsNPPNrDs]], [[lookup @target.affects.special activity=aDWVHpJgsNPPNrDs]] the [[lookup @name lowercase]] can see within [[lookup @target.template.size activity=aDWVHpJgsNPPNrDs]] [[lookup @target.template.units activity=aDWVHpJgsNPPNrDs]].

Failure: The target has the &Reference[Grappled] condition (escape DC [[lookup @skills.ath.passive]]).

Pummel.name: Pummel
Pummel.description:
Dexterity Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=aae828c0Hue0XOMP]], one creature Grappled by the [[lookup @name lowercase]].

Failure: [[/damage average]] damage.

Success: Half damage.

Pit Trap Bouncer.biographyprivate:
Personality

The Ordani are laid back, and joy the fine things in life. They believe that everyone is entitled to being comfortable and happy, and that everyone should strive toward that goal. They are not martial and possess few martial traits because the plateau they have inhabited for generations is largely peaceful and serene.

Connections

The Ordani have a close relationship with the Arcturians of the plateau, who provide them food, textiles, and more. The large metropolis the Ordani occupy in term drives trade that benefits their neighbors in the Plateau.

Phrases

Sorry, can't let you in. You're not on the list.

Yeah, you want in? What's the password then?
Pit Trap Bouncer.biographypublic:
Despite being unarmed and dressed in street clothes, this person looks a bit tougher, and a bit meaner than average Ordani, and a bit more willing to let their fists do the talking for them. They watch their surroundings with keen eyes, wary of anyone that might start trouble.

[[lookup @name]] are the tough, rough handed, people paid to keep order in the Pit Trap.

Thayloc Courser.name: Thayloc Courser

Arrows.name: Arrows
Arrows.description:
Storage: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagQuiver00000]{Quiver}

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAmmunitionV]{Ammunition} is required by a weapon that has the Ammunition property. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon. The Ammunition table lists the different types and the amount you get when you buy them. The table also lists the item that is typically used to store each type; storage must be bought separately.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]th level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

The [[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of its character sheet. It automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Lesser Restoration.name: Lesser Restoration
Lesser Restoration.description: You touch a creature and end one condition on it: &Reference[blinded], &Reference[deafened], &Reference[paralyzed], or &Reference[poisoned].

Healing Word.name: Healing Word
Healing Word.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains Hit Points equal to 2d4 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 1.

Dispel Magic.name: Dispel Magic
Dispel Magic.description:
Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range. Any ongoing spell of level 3 or lower on the target ends. For each ongoing spell of level 4 or higher on the target, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 plus that spell's level). On a successful check, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You automatically end a spell on the target if the spell's level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you use.

Guidance.name: Guidance
Guidance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a skill. Until the spell ends, the creature adds 1d4 to any ability check using the chosen skill.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Spare the Dying.name: Spare the Dying
Spare the Dying.description:
Choose a creature within range that has 0 Hit Points and isn't dead. The creature becomes Stable.

Cantrip Upgrade. The range doubles when you reach levels 5 (30 feet), 11 (60 feet), and 17 (120 feet).

Resistance.name: Resistance
Resistance.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a damage type: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Radiant, Slashing, or Thunder. When the creature takes damage of the chosen type before the spell ends, the creature reduces the total damage taken by 1d4. A creature can benefit from this spell only once per turn.

Shield of Faith.name: Shield of Faith
Shield of Faith.description: A shimmering field surrounds a creature of your choice within range, granting it a +2 bonus to AC for the duration.

Protection from Evil and Good.name: Protection from Evil and Good
Protection from Evil and Good.description: Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch is protected against creatures that are Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, or Undead. The protection grants several benefits. Creatures of those types have Disadvantage on attack rolls against the target. The target also can't be possessed by or gain the &Reference[Charmed apply=false] or &Reference[Frightened apply=false] conditions from them. If the target is already possessed, Charmed, or Frightened by such a creature, the target has Advantage on any new saving throw against the relevant effect.

Cure Wounds.name: Cure Wounds
Cure Wounds.description:
A creature you touch regains a number of Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The healing increases by 2d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

Beacon of Hope.name: Beacon of Hope
Beacon of Hope.description: Choose any number of creatures within range. For the duration, each target has Advantage on Wisdom saving throws and Death Saving Throws and regains the maximum number of Hit Points possible from any healing.

Gentle Repose.name: Gentle Repose
Gentle Repose.description:
You touch a corpse or other remains. For the duration, the target is protected from decay and can't become Undead.

The spell also effectively extends the time limit on raising the target from the dead, since days spent under the influence of this spell don't count against the time limit of spells such as Raise Dead.

Enhance Ability.name: Enhance Ability
Enhance Ability.description:

Thayloc Courser.biographyprivate:
As they are a broader character type, each individual [[lookup @name]] will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

[[lookup @name]] are among some of the world's finest archers thanks to an almost fanatical devotion to the art and its practice. These warrior-priests consider mastery of archery second only to their mission to scourge undead from the world.

As servants of the god of retribution, these warriors feel strongly that justice must be served in one way or another, and that none are above justice. Most believe that if the laws and institutions of the land cannot deliver justice adequately, then it falls to them to take up the slack, and see things set right.

Connections

As servants and priests of the god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc}, the Coursers have connections to the faith at large, and hold positions of leadership and influence. It is not uncommon for individual Coursers to have their own following of faithful they tend to and protect.

With their pursuit of justice often placing them at odds with organizations and governments, there are many places where they are seen as unhinged zealots or dangerous vigilantes that should be avoided or arrested.

The Coursers have deep connections with the followers and faiths of both @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, and view them as allies in their war against the unnatural undead forces that plague the world.
Thayloc Courser.biographypublic:
Armed with a silver longbow covered in holy etchings, this daring humanoid is clad in the hooded cloak of a ranger, but wears the hallowed vestments of a warrior-cleric beneath. The silver cloak pin that binds their cowl is fashioned into the shape of a bow and broken arrow, and the quiver on their back is bedecked with a variety of strange arrows — missiles with esoteric purposes, set in motion by a sacred weapon.

[[lookup @name]]s are skilled warrior-priests who worship the shard god Thayloc, and are known as some of Aterica's most capable hunters of the undead. In addition to a light compliment of divine spells, these holy bowmen are equipped with several specialty arrows that greatly assist their ongoing efforts of righteous vengeance and holy purification.

Undaunted Adept.name: Undaunted Adept

Dark Devotion.name: Dark Devotion
Dark Devotion.description: The [[lookup @name]] has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

Pack Tactics.name: Pack Tactics
Pack Tactics.description: The [[lookup @name]] has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the [[lookup @name]]'s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
The [[lookup @name]] is a [[lookup @attributes.spell.level]]rd level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is [[lookup @attributes.spell.abilityLabel]] (spell save DC [[lookup @attributes.spell.dc]], +[[lookup @attributes.spell.attack]] to hit with spell attacks).

The [[lookup @name]] knows and has prepared the spells presented on the Spells tab of its character sheet. It automatically satisfies the material component requirements to cast these spells, if any.

Parry.description:

Expeditious Retreat.name: Expeditious Retreat
Expeditious Retreat.description: You take the Dash action, and until the spell ends, you can take that action again as a Bonus Action.

Bane.name: Bane
Bane.description:
Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within range must each make a Charisma saving throw. Whenever a target that fails this save makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must subtract 1d4 from the attack roll or save.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Thaumaturgy.name: Thaumaturgy
Thaumaturgy.description:
You manifest a minor wonder within range. You create one of the effects below within range. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time.

Altered Eyes. You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.

Booming Voice. Your voice booms up to three times as loud as normal for 1 minute. For the duration, you have Advantage on [[/check ability=cha skill=itm]] checks.

Fire Play. You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.

Invisible Hand. You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.

Phantom Sound. You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point of your choice within range, such as a rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous whispers.

Tremors. You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.

Lethal.name: Lethal
Lethal.description: The [[lookup @name]]'s melee and ranged weapon attacks deal an additional 1d4 damage of the base weapon's damage type.

Hex.name: Hex
Hex.description:
You place a curse on a creature that you can see within range. Until the spell ends, you deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage to the target whenever you hit it with an attack roll. Also, choose one ability when you cast the spell. The target has Disadvantage on ability checks made with the chosen ability.

If the target drops to 0 Hit Points before this spell ends, you can take a Bonus Action on a later turn to curse a new creature.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. Your Concentration can last longer with a spell slot of level 2 (up to 4 hours), 3–4 (up to 8 hours), or 5+ (24 hours).

Hold Person.name: Hold Person
Hold Person.description:
Choose a Humanoid that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[paralyzed apply=false] condition for the duration. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional Humanoid for each spell slot level above 2.

Eldritch Blast.name: Eldritch Blast
Eldritch Blast.description:
You hurl a beam of crackling energy. Make a ranged spell attack against one creature or object in range. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Force damage.

Cantrip Upgrade. The spell creates two beams at level 5, three beams at level 11, and four beams at level 17. You can direct the beams at the same target or at different ones. Make a separate attack roll for each beam.

[[(floor((@details.level+1)/6)+1)]]{Total Beams}

Undaunted Adept.biographyprivate:
Most [[lookup @name]]s wear burgundy and gray clothing lightly inspired by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Maziran} martial arts taught to them by their team captain @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero}, and are instructed in the ways of unarmed combat. Their training and experience, however, extends beyond standard fighting techniques. In addition to their physical prowess and athletic talents, [[lookup @name]]s are neophyte warlocks who serve @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}, the Shard God of Torment. Unlike the @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]{Undaunted Trainees} who have yet to earn them, [[lookup @name]]s are clad with a burgundy cowl that signifies their veteran or varsity rank.

As they are a broader character type, each individual [[lookup @name]] will have their own backstory, personality, and goals that supplement or replace the general notes below.

Personality

While there is no absolute personality trait associated with being a [[lookup @name]], these eldritch warrior-monks tend to be brash and reckless in their pursuit of accolades, whether the stuff of fame or notoriety. And despite their station as @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}'s reigning champions of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Grand Kalion Stadium}'s dangerous Solar Games, [[lookup @name]]s and their cohorts keep a relatively low profile amongst the city's other denizens. Zira & Co. often use this inherent mystique to their advantage when approaching potential recruits to take up the mantle as members of the Undaunted. And be they a "team" or a "gang" in practice, the Undaunted are well known amongst the city's moodier circles, where the disenfranchised and the downtrodden oft dwell. Indeed, joining their scrappy ranks can very well lead one to self-enlightenment (if the rumors are true).

In combat, [[lookup @name]]s will work in tandem to quickly take down the most powerful foe or whomever they might identify as a formidable spellcaster (as knowledgeable of the arcane as they are). They’re also eager to instruct other Undaunted members like @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]{Undaunted Trainees} in an effort to gain battlefield dominance and/or maintain a certain cruel edge throughout the fray.

Connections

[[lookup @name]]s are members of the homonymous Undaunted, a team of daredevil athletes who are the current reigning champions of the Solar Games held at Grand Kalion Stadium in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}. The Undaunted devote their lives to rigorous training under the leadership of Zira Hestidero, a power-hungry warlock of the shard god Ku'arta. As part of their training, [[lookup @name]]s possess relatively little in the way of personal treasures or resources (particularly compared to other arena athletes), but do retain at least one valuable or cherished possession from their previous lives — a token to remind them of the life of weakness they’ve chosen to leave behind.
Undaunted Adept.biographypublic:
This athletic streetwise humanoid is adorned with a patchwork of scars and bruises, and appears to be clad in the short-sleeved robes of a martial artist. A silver-stitched crimson cowl is draped across their shoulders, with a matching sash tied around their waist. This bruiser looks like they've seen more than a few fights, and wears the rough edges to prove it.

[[lookup @name]]s are the experienced warrior-acolytes of Zira Hestidero's cohort of athletes known as The Undaunted. Driven by zealous brinksmanship in service of the shard god Ku'arta, these headstrong gladiators are notorious amongst the people of Ordain, who know them to be the unchallenged champions of local arena combat. Many Atericans call the collective group of adepts and trainees under Zira Hestidero's brash leadership a "team" or "organization," while others would simply (if not dismissively) label them a gang.

Telekinesis.name: Telekinesis
Telekinesis.description:
You gain the ability to move or manipulate creatures or objects by thought. When you cast the spell and as a Magic action on your later turns before the spell ends, you can exert your will on one creature or object that you can see within range, causing the appropriate effect below. You can affect the same target round after round or choose a new one at any time. If you switch targets, the prior target is no longer affected by the spell.

Creature. You can try to move a Huge or smaller creature. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or you move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range. Until the end of your next turn, the creature has the &Reference[Restrained] condition, and if you lift it into the air, it is suspended there. It falls at the end of your next turn unless you use this option on it again and it fails the save.

Object. You can try to move a Huge or smaller object. If the object isn't being worn or carried, you automatically move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range.

If the object is worn or carried by a creature, that creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or you pull the object away and move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range.

You can exert fine control on objects with your telekinetic grip, such as manipulating a simple tool, opening a door or a container, stowing or retrieving an item from an open container, or pouring the contents from a vial.

Regus Halamattrix.biographyprivate:
The phantom known as [[lookup @name]] is the immortal steward of the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl]{Kalion Stadium Underworks}, where he haunts a monument that was erected in his honor long ago. A deviant of Ember's notorious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.5zekdrPxWYJGV9LT]{Wraiths}, Regus is a unique undead creature that still harnesses some of the arcane powers he utilized in life — including mastery of several varieties of magical damage via the deadly impact of his spectral fists.

Anatomy

[[lookup @name]] is wraith-like creature known as a phantom, and exhibits some of the qualities associated with its spectral cousins along with a bespoke array of physical and supernatural attributes. While Regus exudes a dim five-foot light (which he is capable of halting), he nevertheless remains sensitive to direct and magical sunlight — made of the same abyssal ectoplasm as other spectral undead. Rather than physical sustenance like flesh or blood, Regus feasts on the life energy of other creatures to replenish his own eldritch life force when necessary.

Behavior

Driven by an undying hubris in service to abusive oaths, [[lookup @name]] is truly one of the haughtiest characters to inhabit the great city of Ordain throughout its storied history. He entreats with curious contenders willingly and with some manner of civility, but is all-too-eager to teach poseurs a valuable lesson if they so recklessly desire. Regus allows gladiators, athletes, and warriors of all stripes to commune with his immortal spirit via the subterranean monument beneath Grand Kalion Stadium — but the inauthentic and the foolish are punished severely. If the phrase "hurt people hurt people" has any truth to it, the axiom is surely on display in the brutal and savage behavior of [[lookup @name]].

Lore

The stories of [[lookup @name]] tend to be as hushed as they are because of his historical allegiance to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta} — the shard god of torment. Thanks to the shard god's cruel inspiration and arcane patronage, Regus became a force to be reckoned with among the gladiators of Ordain's arena sports. But it was his endurance as one of Ember's mysterious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound} that allowed him to become as legendary as he is today.

Not many know precisely what the subject of Regus' so-called "unfinished business" was, but some correctly speculate that the warrior had an important promise to keep. In truth, [[lookup @name]] endured all three stages of life as a Soulbound character to fulfill an oath to his dying father — an abusive Ordani mercenary who threatened to haunt Regus from the afterlife if he failed in this self-aggrandizing mission. Ironically, Regus' transition to a wraith-like phantom was the end-result of an abyssal bargain his father made earlier in life.
Regus Halamattrix.biographypublic:
You behold the semi-translucent silhouette of a spectral humanoid warrior, clad in an array of light armor and Ordani garb that appears nearly two centuries out of style. The specter sheds a dim red light, and arcane vapors appear to waft from both of its hefty, clenched fists. While little more than an apparition, the grim visage of this gladiator bears signs of rot and decay, as if the man's body was riddled with decomposition long before it ever became the phantasm you see before you. The eyes of this specter blaze with crimson menace, and you can feel a shiver crawl up the back of your spine as he speaks — his voice a sepulchral noise like doom itself.

[[lookup @name]] is the undying phantom of a long-dead Ordani antihero, a gladiator of unparalleled skill and savagery who served as the original champion of Grand Kalion Stadium's Havoc Games. While his accolades are many, the story of [[lookup @name]] tends to be a whispered one. Regus rose to ranks unheard of in the local arena, and became something of a regional legend after several harrowing deaths on the field of battle (which proved to be temporary affairs, according to the tall tales of Ordani bards and raconteurs).

Vespian Hydral Head.name: Vespian Hydral Head

Hydral Head.name: Hydral Head
Hydral Head.description:
This actor represents one of the Vespian Hydral’s heads and is used only for positioning.

A Head token doesn’t have its own turn, hit points, actions, reactions, or recharge resources. Any damage dealt to a Head token is dealt to the main Vespian Hydral. Keep only the main Vespian Hydral in the combat tracker.

A Head token must remain within 60 feet of the main Vespian Hydral token. If a Head token is ever farther than 60 feet away, reposition it so that it is within 60 feet.

When the Vespian Hydral attacks or creates an effect, the GM chooses one active Head token as the point of origin.

If a Head token takes 20 or more damage from a single attack, that head is incapacitated until the end of the Vespian Hydral’s next turn. While incapacitated, it can’t be used as the origin for the Hydral’s attacks or effects and doesn’t count as an active head for Multiattack or Regeneration.

Vespian Hydral Head.biographyprivate: This Actor exists to assist the Gamemaster with running an encounter with the @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU]{Vespian Hydral}. Refer to that creature for full details.
Vespian Hydral Head.biographypublic:
The fanged maw of a reptilian, snake-like creature emerges from the water next to you. Its head and body are scaled, but along its back, there is a large sail-like ridge that marks this as a creature that swims through the water. Between its eyes are a number of glowing runes that match the Chamber as they flicker in and out of existence, and it glares at you with deadly fury.

The [[lookup @name]] Vespian Hydral is a special kind of arcane construct, based on a real creature from the Lowland Bastions. However, it is a creature wholly created and reconstituted at will by the Chamber of Agaseros itself. It appears as a reptilian creature in appearance, with a sleek, scaled maw and glowing, rune-empowered purple eyes. Strangely, its main body seems to be missing or absent, and only its head appears floating in the water to strike at its foes.

Minor Illusion.name: Minor Illusion
Minor Illusion.description:
You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

Vicious Mockery.name: Vicious Mockery
Vicious Mockery.description:
You unleash a string of insults laced with subtle enchantments at one creature you can see or hear within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take 1d6 Psychic damage and have Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach levels 5 (2d6), 11 (3d6), and 17 (4d6).

Charm Person.name: Charm Person
Charm Person.description:
One Humanoid you can see within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. It does so with Advantage if you or your allies are fighting it. On a failed save, the target has the &Reference[charmed apply=false] condition until the spell ends or until you or your allies damage it. The Charmed creature is Friendly to you. When the spell ends, the target knows it was Charmed by you.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

Disguise Self.name: Disguise Self
Disguise Self.description:
You make yourself—including your clothing, armor, weapons, and other belongings on your person—look different until the spell ends. You can seem 1 foot shorter or taller and can appear heavier or lighter. You must adopt a form that has the same basic arrangement of limbs as you have. Otherwise, the extent of the illusion is up to you.

The changes wrought by this spell fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, if you use this spell to add a hat to your outfit, objects pass through the hat, and anyone who touches it would feel nothing.

To discern that you are disguised, a creature must take the Study action to inspect your appearance and succeed on an [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC.

Illusory Script.name: Illusory Script
Illusory Script.description:
You write on parchment, paper, or another suitable material and imbue it with an illusion that lasts for the duration. To you and any creatures you designate when you cast the spell, the writing appears normal, seems to be written in your hand, and conveys whatever meaning you intended when you wrote the text. To all others, the writing appears as if it were written in an unknown or magical script that is unintelligible. Alternatively, the illusion can alter the meaning, handwriting, and language of the text, though the language must be one you know.

If the spell is dispelled, the original script and the illusion both disappear.

A creature that has &Reference[truesight] can read the hidden message.

Silent Image.name: Silent Image
Silent Image.description:
You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 15-foot Cube. The image appears at a spot within range and lasts for the duration. The image is purely visual; it isn't accompanied by sound, smell, or other sensory effects.

As a Magic action, you can cause the image to move to any spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image. For example, if you create an image of a creature and move it, you can alter the image so that it appears to be walking.

Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it. A creature that takes a Study action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.

Invisibility.name: Invisibility
Invisibility.description:
A creature you touch has the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition until the spell ends. The spell ends early immediately after the target makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.

Mind Spike.name: Mind Spike
Mind Spike.description:
You drive a spike of psionic energy into the mind of one creature you can see within range. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw, taking 3d8 Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, you also always know the target's location until the spell ends, but only while the two of you are on the same plane of existence. While you have this knowledge, the target can't become hidden from you, and if it has the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition, it gains no benefit from that condition against you.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 2.

Mirror Image.name: Mirror Image
Mirror Image.description:
Three illusory duplicates of yourself appear in your space. Until the spell ends, the duplicates move with you and mimic your actions, shifting position so it's impossible to track which image is real.

Each time a creature hits you with an attack roll during the spell's duration, roll a [[/r (@flags.dnd-players-handbook.mirrorImages)d6kh1cs>2#Duplicate destroyed]]{d6 for each} of your remaining duplicates. If any of the d6s rolls a 3 or higher, one of the duplicates is hit instead of you, and the duplicate is destroyed. The duplicates otherwise ignore all other damage and effects. The spell ends when all three duplicates are destroyed.

A creature is unaffected by this spell if it has the &Reference[blinded apply=false] condition, &Reference[blindsight], or &Reference[truesight].

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.

Hypnotic Pattern.name: Hypnotic Pattern
Hypnotic Pattern.description:
You create a twisting pattern of colors in a 30-foot Cube within range. The pattern appears for a moment and vanishes. Each creature in the area who can see the pattern must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[charmed apply=false] condition for the duration. While Charmed, the creature has the &Reference[incapacitated apply=false] condition and a Speed of 0.

The spell ends for an affected creature if it takes any damage or if someone else uses an action to shake the creature out of its stupor.

Major Image.name: Major Image
Major Image.description:
You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 20-foot Cube. The image appears at a spot that you can see within range and lasts for the duration. It seems real, including sounds, smells, and temperature appropriate to the thing depicted, but it can't deal damage or cause conditions.

If you are within range of the illusion, you can take a Magic action to cause the image to move to any other spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image. For example, if you create an image of a creature and move it, you can alter the image so that it appears to be walking. Similarly, you can cause the illusion to make different sounds at different times, even making it carry on a conversation, for example.

Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, for things can pass through it. A creature that takes a Study action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image, and its other sensory qualities become faint to the creature.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The spell lasts until dispelled, without requiring Concentration, if cast with a level 4+ spell slot.

Hallucinatory Terrain.name: Hallucinatory Terrain
Hallucinatory Terrain.description:
You make natural terrain in a 150-foot Cube in range look, sound, and smell like another sort of natural terrain. Thus, open fields or a road can be made to resemble a swamp, hill, crevasse, or some other difficult or impassable terrain. A pond can be made to seem like a grassy meadow, a precipice like a gentle slope, or a rock-strewn gully like a wide and smooth road. Manufactured structures, equipment, and creatures within the area aren't changed.

The tactile characteristics of the terrain are unchanged, so creatures entering the area are likely to notice the illusion. If the difference isn't obvious by touch, a creature examining the illusion can take the Study action to make an [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC to disbelieve it. If a creature discerns that the terrain is illusory, the creature sees a vague image superimposed on the real terrain.

Phantasmal Killer.name: Phantasmal Killer
Phantasmal Killer.description:
You tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see within range and create an illusion of its deepest fears, visible only to that creature. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 4d10 Psychic damage and has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls for the duration. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and the spell ends.

For the duration, the target makes a [[/save ability=wis dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a failed save, it takes the Psychic damage again. On a successful save, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.The damage increases by 1d10 for each spell slot level above 4.

Mage Armor.name: Mage Armor
Mage Armor.description: You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. Until the spell ends, the target's base AC becomes 13 plus its Dexterity modifier. The spell ends early if the target dons armor.

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description: An imperceptible barrier of magical force protects you. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack, and you take no damage from @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMagicMissi]{Magic Missile}.

Fortified Mind.name: Fortified Mind
Fortified Mind.description:
[[lookup @name]] has a powerful mind that has been honed against being manipulated by outside forces. He has advantage in the following situations:

  • When making saving throws to resist charm, fear, illusion or sleep effects.

  • When making checks to detect, investigate, or pierce magical illusions.

He is also resistant to psychic damage.

Falar.biographyprivate:
Long ago, Falar came to Ordain to become an adventurer, and found considerable success within the Anachraenum. Beyond its ranks he also found a knack for making himself useful to the right people.

Highly adaptable, dangerously creative, with a grasp of magic few of his peers could match, he quickly turned his aptitudes into a small fortune, and made himself invaluable to aspiring adventurers and wealthy clients alike. For a time, he did very well, built a strong reputation, gathered an impressive personal library, and secured a place in high society.

It did not last, however. A string of bad choices in allies and business partners led to strained alliances, and costly grudges that brought his fortunes crashing down. Failure after failure stripped him of almost everything, eventually forcing him to sell off the magical library that had once been the pride of his life. All he kept were a few miserable deeds in Flotsam and enough sense to disappear.
Since then, Falar has lived in near obscurity, selling paints and supplies, dabbling in art, and doing his best to never need Ordain again. He claims to be done with magic, adventuring, and Ordain as a whole, but the city’s old wounds still sit close to the surface.

Personality

At his best, Falar is clever, charming, and talented, with a deep desire to create within himself. However, a life of bad choices and poor allies has left him embittered toward the world, skeptical of everyone's motives, and dour beyond reason.

Beneath the bitterness, Falar still has some of the charm that once carried him through salons, guild halls, and expedition camps, but he is badly out of practice, and has trouble bringing it to bear most days. Deep down, he respects competence and intelligence, but is quick to become envious of those who succeed in the ways he previously failed.

Most people that meet him see a curt, burned out shopkeeper with little patience for nonsense, but that rough edge hides a wounded spirit that has never had time or opportunity to heal. Though he lies to himself, and pretends that he has left his old life behind, he still yearns to create, to engineer new spells, or paint scenes the various strange and majestic sights Ember has to offer an artist.

Connections

Falar has burned most of the bridges he once had, and now lives a deeply isolated life. There are few in Ordain who still remember his name, and even fewer among them who do so fondly.

Quotes

Ordain is built to grind people up as pigment for someone else's masterpiece.

Paint is honest: The color in the pot is the same as on the brush, and the canvas.
Falar.biographypublic:
Clad in well-tailored vintage clothing marked with intermittent paint stains, this gray-haired Ordani merchant has a world-weary look about him, accented by the wry look on his handsomely wrinkled face.

[[lookup @name]] is an old paint monger with a small shop in Flotsam where he sells paints to the local artist community there. Bitter from a long, difficult life, he has unflattering opinions on Ordain and what he perceives as its numerous failings.

Mistress Caberi.name: Mistress Caberi

Shard God.name: Shard God
Shard God.description:
[[lookup @name]] is a Shard God, Imbued with Lifeforce from the Heart of Ember after their interaction with one of Ember's Heart Crystals. They are not a typical opponent, as they can tap into massive amounts of power if needed to elevate the damage done by one of their typical features, destroying most non-shard gods without much effort.

It would be highly foolish for characters to try and fight a Shard God unless a quest event specifically calls for it and provides the party with specific means suitable for doing so.

Mistress Caberi.biographyprivate:
For more on Mistress Caberi's true nature, see the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.FaUiibd3k4gfrzry] article in the setting journal.

Personality

Mistress Caberi is supernaturally charming, carrying herself with an effortless grace and unassailable dignity. She knows full well how intimidating she is to others, and does all that she reasonably can to put people at ease, at least when she chooses to. If given cause, she can wield a terrible force of personality capable of cowing even the most stalwart and belligerent spirits.

Connections

As the head of house Salva, Caberi has connections throughout the fashion industry, and the highest halls of upper society and government. Her former posting as the Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages has only further deepened her connections to Ordain as a whole. It is rumored that she has eyes and ears everywhere, and this rumor is exactly true, though Mistress Caberi is quick to downplay just how well connected she is.

Quotes

Style is how we live, but substance is why we live. One should endeavor to never have more style than substance in their life.

There is no more powerful force than an inspired person!
Mistress Caberi.biographypublic:
This gorgeous human woman wears an impossible gown made from arches of vibrant fabric that defy gravity, layers of shimmering cloth seemingly made from woven metal, and layers of lace that seem to have starlight trapped in them. As she moves a train of glowing cloth flows behind her, never quite touching the floor. Swirls of light dance around her wrists in long, intertwining orbits, leaving colorful trails of dust in their path.

[[lookup @name]] is the glamorous head of House Salva. She is a paragon of fashion and style, guiding the house with a velvet hand. She's been a public figure for decades, having held high ranking positions in one organization or another for most of that time.

Light Mote.name: Light Mote

Radiant Death Burst.name: Radiant Death Burst
Radiant Death Burst.description: When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} dies, it explodes in a volatile burst of radiant energy.
Radiant Death Burst.actiondesc: When the @ref[actor.name]{creature} becomes @Condition[dead], it explodes in a pulse of Radiant energy which attacks the Fortitude defense of all nearby creatures that fail to resist the effect.

Radiant Absorption.name: Radiant Absorption
Radiant Absorption.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is no stranger to the chaotic force of light. Its Radiant resistance is doubled and if that resistance would reduce an amount of damage below zero, the negative amount is received as Healing instead.

Rune: Illumination.name: Rune: Illumination
Rune: Illumination.description:
The orderly force of light and energy. The Illumination rune governs light and radiance.

The Illumination rune scales using Presence, targets Reflex, and deals Radiant damage to Health. It is opposed by the chaotic rune of Illusion.
Rune: Illumination.actiondesc:
Your command of the Rune of Illumination allows you to create light and exert basic control over its radiance, producing one of the following effects:

  • Create a ball of light called a "tosslight" which sheds bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light in a 40 foot radius. The light can hover near your body, be affixed to an item or surface, or be thrown up to a distance of 30 feet. You may dismiss your tosslight at any time and may only have a single tosslight at a time, casting this spell again causes your previous tosslight to disappear.

  • Inscribe up to 200 words of invisible text into paper like a scroll, page, or book. The text is written from light itself and hidden from non-magical detection. It can be made visible by yourself or another through use of this spell combined with a spoken passphrase that you define at the time of inscription.

  • Touch a physical object that produces dim light, causing it to become bright light for as long as you maintain physical contact. Only one light source may be intensified in this way at a given time.

Reveal may only affect a creature or object you can physically touch. You may attempt other uses similar those above, the effectiveness of which is decided by the Gamemaster.

Luminous Transit.name: Luminous Transit
Luminous Transit.description: The @ref[actor.name]{creature} is able to move instantaneously across up to three visible waypoints.
Luminous Transit.actiondesc: The @ref[actor.name] is able to move instantaneously between in rapid succession. Its Move must end in an unoccupied space, but can be any distance provided each waypoint on its movement is visible from the last.

False Appearance.name: False Appearance
False Appearance.description: While it remains motionless, the @ref[actor.name]{creature} is indistinguishable from some other object or material.

Radiant Sear.name: Radiant Sear
Radiant Sear.descriptionpublic: The @ref[actor.name] focuses a sharp point of pure luminous energy upon a foe.

Light Mote.biographyprivate:
Anatomy

@ref[name]s are manifestations of pure light. They shine with an inner luminescence that gives them an almost ethereal appearance, and they are constantly in motion. They do not live for very long, and only maintain their form for several minutes or an hour at most, before flickering out of existence.

Behavior
