When using this pickaxe, you gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls against constructs, machines, and metal objects.

This damage bonus includes damage to Celestials, which have a metal carapace.

Shifting Ink.name: Shifting Ink
Shifting Ink.descriptionprivate:
Messages written in shifting ink are nearly impossible for those reading them to decode without performing a specific action known only to the person writing the messages and the intended recipient. These range from casting a specific spell to saying a key phrase to folding the ink-covered note in a particular way.

While this is good for secrecy, it is said that there are pieces of writing created in shifting ink whose true meaning has been lost forever.
Shifting Ink.descriptionpublic: The deep golden ink seems to shift as it sits, as if moved by some unseen current.

Sturdy Pickaxe.name: Sturdy Pickaxe
Sturdy Pickaxe.description: The Sturdy Pickaxe gives a +2 bonus to all Strength checks made while using it as a tool.

Suspicious Karal.name: Suspicious Karal
Suspicious Karal.descriptionprivate: The rancid smell is caused by the addition of a toxin. If consumed, the creature that consumes it suffers [[/hazard 13 fortitude health poison]]{Acute Gastrointestinal Distress} and is @Condition[poisoned] for 1 hour.
Suspicious Karal.descriptionpublic: This brew resembles normal Karal, but has a slightly rancid smell to it.

Troubling Reports.name: Troubling Reports
Troubling Reports.descriptionprivate:
This list of reports is dated within the year and has a number of notes about odd occurrences at the Level 3 mine. Three in particular catch your eye.

Report 1

Tools keep going missing and then turning up in odd places. I think I might have a prankster in one of the shifts. I'll keep an eye out for trouble.

Report 2

Jerick says that he heard a clattering sound in the newly dug out section the mine — even worse, he was going to look into it, but all the pearls went dead at once and he scampered out of there. I'll have to get the Lamplighters down here to check it out.

An addition to the note, in a more wobbly handwriting, reads:

Had the lamplighter Calandra down here to see what she could make of things. She found nothing wrong, but the pearls keep going dark and the wind gets cold at the oddest times. Might have to close down for a bit if we can't figure this out.

Report 3

Another commotion. I'm going to check out what the —

The report trails off from there, as if the writer was interrupted.
Troubling Reports.descriptionpublic: A loosely bound stack of papers containing a thorough accounting of reports received regarding Arcturel's Level 3 mine.

Examination Notes.name: Examination Notes
Examination Notes.descriptionprivate:
This folder of notes and diagrams details the work that was being on a drakeling by a vivisector and overseen by Kalasak.

The report states that the weakened but live specimen was slated for exploratory surgery to ascertain the state of its organs, and determine how badly afflicted it was compared to other drakes in its testing group.

It also notes that this subject was from the same batch that was removed from the quarry to be released into the wild near Helkas. This one was held back to judge the difference between a drake in the wild and one held in pens.

It also notes that it received a baseline injection of the mutagenic medium plus one of the more recent activator compounds, and that its blood needed to be extracted and tested against a fresh dose of mutagenic medium to determine how it reacted with their blood, and what the infection level was.

The final entry notes that the examination was halted due to Kalasak needing to speak with Professor Bleak, who arrived by teleportation specifically to see him.

The work was never resumed.

Experiment Reports.name: Experiment Reports
Experiment Reports.descriptionprivate:
A bundle of reports from various members of the quarry laboratory. These reports go over experiments or exploratory surgeries conducted on premises. The majority of them being drakes and drakelings, and in many cases the creatures were alive to begin with, though few survived.

In almost all cases these procedures were carried out to see what effects, if any, a particular alchemical compound or serum had on the creatures. The number of iterations in compounds borders on staggering, as does the absolute lack of care or compassion shown for the creatures subjected to these treatments.

Kalasak's Observations.name: Kalasak's Observations
Kalasak's Observations.descriptionprivate:
This journal contains the names of the workers staffing this laboratory, the scout teams, their personalities, assignments, assessments, and more. This alone could be useful in tracking down more about this lab's origins.

The most recent entries center around Kalasak's work refining some sort of mutagenic compound, and how the most recent iteration has been proving progressively more promising.

There are also numerous entries about Subject AD-M-98 which is supposedly larger, smarter, more aggressive, and longest lived of all subjects received. However, Kalasak is not satisfied, citing "unchecked mutations" as not being under control yet.

Kryz.name: Kryz
Kryz.descriptionprivate: Found in a pile of Baradom dung in the pathways, and reclaimed from Jurtak trying to steal it.
Kryz.descriptionpublic: A large crystal with a crude painted on face.

List of Chemicals.name: List of Chemicals
List of Chemicals.descriptionprivate: A list of alchemical compounds encountered in the alchemical storage room located in an underground quarry that had been turned into a lab. Can be turned in as evidence.
List of Chemicals.descriptionpublic: A single piece of paper containing what appears to be a list of alchemical compounds.

Manual of Drake Anatomy.name: Manual of Drake Anatomy
Manual of Drake Anatomy.descriptionprivate:
This journal of anatomical analysis notes the nature of healthy drakes arriving in the testing facility, their typical length, weight, and age. It also notes the developmental differences between drakes and the smaller drakelings, and potential lifespans of specimens being centuries long.

The back half of the journal notes the numerous mutations, maladies, defects, and afflictions that develop when the drakes are exposed to various alchemical mutagens. It seems until recently most drakes would not survive the administration of the mutagen in any case.

Drakes exposed to even small doses tended to go blind, become unpredictable, and aggressive. At the same time, they would develop lesions, infections, and organ failure resulting in their often painful demise.
Manual of Drake Anatomy.descriptionpublic: A well maintained journal cataloguing dates and analysis of what appears to be animal care.

Molted Dragon Skin.name: Molted Dragon Skin
Molted Dragon Skin.descriptionpublic: A large swatch of leathery dragon skin taken from the molt of a vile dragon found in the Pathways. Could be used to make wearable equipment.

Mutagenic Formulae.name: Mutagenic Formulae
Mutagenic Formulae.descriptionprivate:
The books go through numerous iterations of each formula, every single one pursuing similar aspects of transformation, fortification, and strengthening a living body. The entries are all dated, and most of the early formulae are marked as "Rejected" or "Approved for Iteration" with many of their alchemical successors being rejects as well.

A vast number of the combinations and compounds listed are immensely dangerous for living beings to be exposed to, and could result in horrific mutations and organ death in most cases, and severe poisoning in the best of situations.

It seems that the most recent formulae had strings of successes and were narrowing down the final formation that this lab was pursuing. Unfortunately, this final formula is not present in any of the books in this collection.
Mutagenic Formulae.descriptionpublic: A collection of books containing numerous complex, often incomprehensible alchemical formulae.

Pathways Scout Map.name: Pathways Scout Map
Pathways Scout Map.descriptionprivate:
Using the scout camp where the map was found as a reference point, the following locations are notable:

  • To the northwest the "Mythspire Overlook."

  • To the northwest, past the bridge a note for "Jurtak hunting grounds."

  • Over the bridge and to the north, on a plateau a note: "Baradom sighted."

  • A series of checkmarks in an area to the northeast, with a note "strange thornling."

  • Far to the northeast, a note for "the skin."
Pathways Scout Map.descriptionpublic: A piece of parchment with carefully detailed cartography detailing the area of the Pathways near the Mythspire Observatory.

Protective Goggles.name: Protective Goggles
Protective Goggles.descriptionpublic: A pair of tightly fitting protective goggles that keep liquids, gasses, shrapnel and other particles out of the eyes.

Protective Mask.name: Protective Mask
Protective Mask.descriptionpublic: A tightly fitting rubberized leather mask with built-in protective goggles that keep liquids, gasses, shrapnel and other particles out of the eyes, mouth and nose.

Rare Chemicals.name: Rare Chemicals
Rare Chemicals.descriptionprivate: These were claimed from the alchemical storage room located in an underground quarry that had been turned into a lab. Can be sold, used in crafting, or turned in as evidence.

Scout Journal.name: Scout Journal
Scout Journal.descriptionprivate:
The journal belonged to one of two dead men encountered in the Pathways, killed by traps hidden in a gruesome killing field you found. It has suffered some damage due to the natural moisture in the underground, causing much of the ink to run. However, many passages remain legible.

The last page is scribbled with shaky writing and reads:

Damn the jurtak. They came and moved our traps, set them specially for us. I told Kalasak that they wouldn't tolerate us poaching their kills and messing with their hunting grounds. We could've just let them alone, but no, Kalasak had to be right, didn't he? Tell Kalasak I told him so.

Well now Erd's dead, and I can't stand on my leg. I'm sure those accursed lizard men will be along soon, and if the bleeding doesn't get me, they will.

I hope they choke on my guts.

For further details on the contents of this journal, consult with the Gamemaster, as this item pertains to the Ancient Paths quest.
Scout Journal.descriptionpublic: A battered journal with a leather cover, it shows signs of water damage.

Testing Schedule.name: Testing Schedule
Testing Schedule.descriptionprivate:
This journal is a logbook of every lab attendant that ever worked on the slab, and what their general work was meant to be, and when it was scheduled. Each entry is also accompanied by a report number, which likely connects to more detailed notes.

Just going off of the simply summaries of the work being done here, drakes and drakelings were often lashed to the table, sedated or euthanized, and then work on, which could include draining their blood, extracting organs, or subjecting them to chemicals or other gruesome actions in pursuit of some piece of knowledge or outcome.
Testing Schedule.descriptionpublic: A journal that logs the names of lab attendants and duties.

Vial of Mutagenic Medium.name: Vial of Mutagenic Medium
Vial of Mutagenic Medium.descriptionprivate:
This is a strange alchemical medium which is mixed with "activator compounds" to create a powerful alchemical concoction that has any number of transformative and often fatal effects whatever poor creature is injected with it.

Without the alchemical activators it is little more than a highly potent toxin. It is also notably flammable, creating a hot flame and noxious fumes when burned.
Vial of Mutagenic Medium.descriptionpublic: An odd alchemical compound liquid contained within a carefully stoppered vial.

Avwynn's Journal.name: Avwynn's Journal
Avwynn's Journal.descriptionprivate:
This handwritten book is the private journal of Avwynn Taol, and presents elements of her clandestine history with the Bloodwoods @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries}.

Any character who spends at least 5 minutes studying this journal is able to learn about its contents.
Avwynn's Journal.descriptionpublic: This well-worn journal contains the private accounts of the life of Avwynn Taol.

Black Aspen Wand.name: Black Aspen Wand
Black Aspen Wand.descriptionpublic: This wand has been carved from the twisted branch of a black aspen tree, found only in the Bloodwoods of the Arctus Plateau. It appears to be inscribed with powerful runes to invoke the power of nature by those who heed its call.

Burnished Seal.name: Burnished Seal
Burnished Seal.descriptionprivate: This bronze emblem grants passage through the Burnished Hand blockades located at the Ordani Skywalk or at Ordain's outer gates.

Cindaric Writ.name: Cindaric Writ
Cindaric Writ.descriptionprivate: This handwritten note grants passage through the Burnished Hand blockades located at the Ordani Skywalk or at Ordain's outer gates.

Evesso's Note.name: Evesso's Note
Evesso's Note.descriptionpublic:
A discreet scrap of parchment, folded in half to conceal its message. It features a short phrase, written in common, followed by a sequence of four numbers and the sketch of an arcane sigil — a glyph that resembles a fractured circle of six interlocked rings.

"The path to madness is paved in knowledge."

19, 53, 16, 5

Letter from Lilla Arien.name: Letter from Lilla Arien
Letter from Lilla Arien.descriptionprivate:
Dated exactly one day ago, it reads:

Mira,

I appreciate your continued petition for Corpin Sanctuary to house the displaced citizens from recently troubled settlements like Helkas and Skybrush, but the Speaker's guidance on this is quite clear: as the unrest between the Trading Houses intensifies and the Bloodwoods threat continues to rise, our resources are spread woefully thin. The Cindaric Temple in Ordain simply cannot offer additional aid at this time, and the duty falls to you and the other sages at Corpin to harbor safe haven for the people we need to send to you from the city. We're running out of room over here as it is.

I know your intentions are good, Mira. And my soul aches for those poor refugees. But our hands are tied. Trust in the Speaker, and the people of Ember are sure to trust in us. The heartblood wills it.

Regards,

Lilla Arien, Ordain
Letter from Lilla Arien.descriptionpublic: A handwritten letter "From Sage Lilla Arien," addressed "To Sage Mira Wavehorn, Corpin Sanctuary." Scrawled with expensive ink on fine parchment.

Letter from Sigil.name: Letter from Sigil
Letter from Sigil.descriptionprivate:
Dated exactly one week ago, it reads:

Sage Mira,

I'll have you know: the doors of Oldcraft Lodge will always be open to those in need. But you should have seen the look on the faces of those poor Helkans when they had to explain that Corpin Sanctuary of all places turned them away.

I understand that seasons of change are upon us, but I implore you and the Cindarics to once again open your doors to the people of the Arctus Plateau. Please, Mira, reconsider your stance. These families are welcome here at the lodge as long as they need to stay; we'll help them find ways out of this mess. But Oldcraft — with its peculiar nooks and crannies — is no place for a family on the run from fire and tragedy.

For centuries, the Cindaric Sages have stood for compassion and hope in this fateful world of ours. I hope the Cindaric Sages still stand for something. Ember seems to need you now more than ever.

With Eternal Sincerity,

Sigil
Letter from Sigil.descriptionpublic: A handwritten letter "From S," addressed "To Mira Wavehorn," scrawled in a curious vermillion ink that glimmers with arcane iridescence.

Letter of Introduction.name: Letter of Introduction
Letter of Introduction.descriptionpublic:
A dog-eared piece of correspondence, inked on the official letterhead of the Cindaric Temple in Ordain. Labeled "From the Desk of the First Speaker." Dated exactly 175 days ago, it reads:

Sage Wavehorn,

This document serves as a letter of introduction for its bearer, a talented sage of remarkable experience named Evesso, whose studies here at the Cindaric Temple in Ordain have reached their zenith. I've asked Evesso to join you and the other sages at Corpin Sanctuary to share his extensive learnings about traditional Cindaric rites, so they might assist us in the woeful times that have been prophesied to come. Please accommodate him with one of your empty dormitory chambers.

I understand that Evesso's appointment to your enclave may come as a bit of a surprise, but his familiarity with the occult and his faith in the order promise to be extremely valuable assets for our ongoing efforts against the heartblood's enemies.

Thank you, once again, for the ongoing excellence of your service.

With Regards from Ordain,

-- V

Nineteen Nights in Haxim.name: Nineteen Nights in Haxim
Nineteen Nights in Haxim.descriptionprivate: Finding this particular book in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.eDlvJHr6FhKhY8ji]{Library}, and following the numbers to the specific page, line, and words of interest reveals a specific phrase that is used to open a secret door in Evesso's chamber.
Nineteen Nights in Haxim.descriptionpublic: A book containing historical accounts, information pertaining to a particular field of lore, myth, or legend.

Note to Sin.name: Note to Sin
Note to Sin.descriptionprivate:
The note's interior reads:

Heed my words, for they are astoundingly true. There is a necromancer lurking among the sages here at Corpin Sanctuary. As outsiders, it seems you and your party are the most capable to investigate this dangerous affair. Most importantly, your intentions here seem noble and just.

Please, rid the Sanctuary of this invader, for all our sakes. And be careful to avoid suspicion — the eyes of the necromancer are everywhere.
Note to Sin.descriptionpublic:
A mysterious note written in Common on a folded scrap of parchment. The text on the outer fold reads:

To: Initiate Marmot.
For your eyes only.

Chessian Souvenir.name: Chessian Souvenir
Chessian Souvenir.descriptionpublic: This brass keepsake resembles a coin-sized cog with a Chessman construct stamped on one side and a relief of Arcturel on the other.

Chessman Scrap Metal.name: Chessman Scrap Metal
Chessman Scrap Metal.descriptionpublic: This scrap of metal from the chassis of a Chessman construct bears the trademark of famed artificer Vartholomew Chess.

Inkaro Pool Mandate.name: Inkaro Pool Mandate
Inkaro Pool Mandate.descriptionpublic:
A folded piece of correspondence, inked on the official letterhead of the Silver Beam Consortium. Dated exactly 5 days ago, it reads:

Attn: Zirca Bronzebellow & Co.

Following recent shifts in security protocol, you are hereby ordered to comply with the following mandate: all Chessmen working the Inkaro Pools in this sector are required to be outfitted with pearls inspected directly by our Silver Beam engineers. Any unaltered Chessian constructs that are still on the line must be serviced by a trained Silver Beam technician, without delays. Failure to comply with this mandate will result in dismissal from the company, with potential financial damages assayed as necessary.

Thank you for your swift compliance,

Larissa Toth
Director, Silver Beam Consortium - Arcturel

Larissa Toth's Grimoire.name: Larissa Toth's Grimoire
Larissa Toth's Grimoire.descriptionpublic:
Bound in the primordial hide of some unknown Leviathan, this arcane spellbook is an archaic Shent tome with the following wizard spells recorded upon its crystal-inked pages.

Under Development

While Invested, this Tome grants the wielder access to @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.gestureConjure00]{Gesture: Conjure} and @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.inflectionReshap]{Inflection: Reshape}.

The magical effects of this item are not yet automated. These effects will be added when the Crucible enchanting affix system is added.

Larissa Toth's Memory Shard.name: Larissa Toth's Memory Shard
Larissa Toth's Memory Shard.descriptionpublic:
This 2-inch-long sliver of arcane crystal can be activated to project the small illusion of a moment in time it has previously recorded. Up to 3 recordings can be stored in the single memory shard.

This memory shard contains a recording from Larissa Toth (intended for delivery to an unknown recipient) that explains her nefarious plans for the Silver Beam Consortium in Arcturel. These plans reveal a desire to: undermine House Cevher operations, sabotage Chessmen construct production via corrupted inkaro pearls, and establish a chokehold on exports from Arcturel. In the hands of Silver Beam's enemies, this confession would be most incriminating.

Potion of Jumping.name: Potion of Jumping
Potion of Jumping.descriptionpublic:
Tiny motes of fluid jump upon the surface of this effervescent potion, a semi-translucent orange-colored solution that tastes of citrus.

When you drink this potion, your jump distance is tripled for 1 minute. During this time, you have @Advantage[2] on Athletics checks you make to jump.

Renegade Construct Scraps.name: Renegade Construct Scraps
Renegade Construct Scraps.descriptionprivate: A collection of scrap metal harvested from the cadaver of the renegade Chessman construct known as "Hew".

Silver Beam Schematics.name: Silver Beam Schematics
Silver Beam Schematics.descriptionprivate:
Annotated in the Scripta language, these somewhat inscrutable blueprints also diagram how arcane energy flows into the construct's chassis from the central inkaro pearl receptacle.

The schematics are signed with a name at the bottom:

Larissa Toth, Silver Beam Consortium
Silver Beam Schematics.descriptionpublic: This large, dog-eared piece of parchment features detailed technical instructions that propose a series of edits required to alter the internal structure of a Chessman construct.

Silver Beam Uniform.name: Silver Beam Uniform
Silver Beam Uniform.descriptionpublic: This standard-issue uniform of the Silver Beam Consortium bears a distinctly far-western design crafted from Railen silk.

Used Chessman Parts.name: Used Chessman Parts
Used Chessman Parts.descriptionpublic: Used parts from a refurbished Chessman construct, bearing the telltale components of artificer Vartholomew Chess.

Blade of Eriss Khan.name: Blade of Eriss Khan
Blade of Eriss Khan.descriptionprivate:
This longsword is forged from a rare alloy of steel and lunar ore.

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

MORE

You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, while you are attuned to this weapon, your hit point maximum increases by 1 for each level you have attained.

Curse. This longsword is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the longsword, keeping it within reach at all times. You also have disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons other than this one, unless no foe is within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear.

Whenever a hostile creature damages you while the longsword is in your possession, you must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or go berserk.

While berserk, you must use your action each round to attack the creature nearest to you with the longsword. If you can make extra attacks as part of the Attack action, you use those extra attacks, moving to attack the next nearest creature after you fell your current target.

If you have multiple possible targets, you attack one at random. You are berserk until you start your turn with no creatures within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear.
Blade of Eriss Khan.descriptionpublic: This longsword is expertly forged and well-balanced. Its surface holds a faint, silvery sheen that catches the light in a way ordinary steel doesn’t.

Fluorite Bracelet.name: Fluorite Bracelet
Fluorite Bracelet.descriptionprivate: A blue-green bracelet made of semi-precious gemstone. This Arcturian heirloom has been lovingly cared for over the course of generations, which is reflected in its value as an antique.

House Vortest Signet Ring.name: House Vortest Signet Ring
House Vortest Signet Ring.descriptionprivate: This amber-alloyed band is adorned with the sigil of House Vortest, a lineage of Signaran vassals allegiant to the Daemos Nalgomith.

Parchment Boat 1.name: Parchment Boat 1
Parchment Boat 1.descriptionprivate:
This parchment boat is crafted from a letter scrawled in a child's handwriting, which reads:

Hello. My name is Jo. I'm ten years old. I grew up in Storsa's Strand. But now I live in Calloway Cove. It's special here. There are no adults to tell us when to wake up or when to go to sleep. Nobody makes us wash our ears, and nobody tells us what to eat. My new brothers and sisters take care of me here. I hope you have a special place, too!
Parchment Boat 1.descriptionpublic: This parchment boat is crafted from a letter scrawled in a child's handwriting.

Parchment Boat 2.name: Parchment Boat 2
Parchment Boat 2.descriptionprivate:
This parchment boat is crafted from a letter scrawled in a child's handwriting, which reads:

Hello! My name is Jo and I live in a special cave by the river, which we call Calloway Cove. I've only been here for a few weeks. Some of the older kids say that they've been here for years and never get older. I don't know if I believe them, but everybody else seems to. There are lots of kids here and we all take care of each other. We don't need adults. They don't understand.
Parchment Boat 2.descriptionpublic: This parchment boat is crafted from a letter scrawled in a child's handwriting.

Parchment Boat 3.name: Parchment Boat 3
Parchment Boat 3.descriptionprivate:
This parchment boat is crafted from a letter scrawled in a child's handwriting, which reads:

Hello! My name is Jo and I'm looking for friends to join us in Calloway Cove. I'm ten years old and we have our own city here, where we make all the rules and nobody ever tells us no. Baxon says the water here is magic, and that we'll never get sick or old if we keep drinking it. Bax is my friend, so I believe him. But I miss my family sometimes. I guess it's okay to make a new family, isn't it?
Parchment Boat 3.descriptionpublic: This parchment boat is crafted from a letter scrawled in a child's handwriting.

Rustvar Valleys Map.name: Rustvar Valleys Map
Rustvar Valleys Map.descriptionprivate:
This map of the Rustvar Valleys indicates a few points of interest located in the northwest section of the Arctus Plateau.

Once a character reads it, this map reveals the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]{Storsa's Strand} Vantage Points on the Arctus Plateau Region Map.
Rustvar Valleys Map.descriptionpublic: This map of the Rustvar Valleys indicates a few points of interest located in the northwest section of the Arctus Plateau.

Scroll Case.name: Scroll Case
Scroll Case.description: This cylindrical leather case can hold up to ten rolled-up sheets of paper or five rolled-up sheets of parchment.

Shard of Sending.name: Shard of Sending
Shard of Sending.descriptionpublic:
This splintered crystal has been engraved and enchanted with a binding that allows for distant, instantaneous communication. When a user holds one of the pieces of this paired crystal close to their face and speaks, the other paired crystal resonates the speech at a conversational volume.

The tier of enchantment determines the range at which the magical affect allows communication.

  • Minor- 5 miles

  • Major - 50 miles

  • Legendary - Limitless

Shardsteel Hammer.name: Shardsteel Hammer
Shardsteel Hammer.descriptionprivate:
Requires attunement

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

The steel of this hefty, timeworn hammer appears to be laced with minuscule fragments of azure crystal, and the initials "B.S." are etched into the base of its wooden handle.

The hammer is magical for the purposes of overcoming damage reduction, but does not grant an attack or damage bonus. Additionally, the hammer can be used by spellcasters to hone their arcane focus.

Spellcasting Focus. An arcane focus is a special item designed to channel the power of arcane spells. A sorcerer, warlock, or wizard can use such an item as a spellcasting focus, using it in place of any material component that does not list a cost.
Shardsteel Hammer.descriptionpublic: The steel of this hefty timeworn hammer appears to be laced with minuscule fragments of azure crystal.

Silvered Longsword.name: Silvered Longsword
Silvered Longsword.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

Stonecraft Manuscript.name: Stonecraft Manuscript
Stonecraft Manuscript.descriptionprivate: A hand-written manuscript penned by the famed storyteller of Nain, Amalthea Stonecraft.
Stonecraft Manuscript.descriptionpublic: A hand-written manuscript penned by the famed storyteller of Nain, Amalthea Stonecraft.

Tiny Copper Key.name: Tiny Copper Key
Tiny Copper Key.descriptionprivate: This tiny copper key is paired with the lockbox found in Eb Hargrove's bedroom.
Tiny Copper Key.descriptionpublic: This tiny copper key is paired with an unknown lock.

Wayfarer's Staff.name: Wayfarer's Staff
Wayfarer's Staff.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

The staff made of gnarled and knotted wood has 6 charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplShillelagh]{Shillelagh} (1 charge), @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds} (2 charges), or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplShield0000]{Shield} (2 charges).

The staff regains [[/r 1d3]] expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a [[/r d20]]. On a 1, the staff turns to dust and is destroyed.

Spellcasting Focus. An arcane focus is a special item designed to channel the power of arcane spells. A sorcerer, warlock, or wizard can use such an item as a spellcasting focus, using it in place of any material component that does not list a cost
Wayfarer's Staff.descriptionpublic: A staff made of gnarled and knotted wood.

A Farewell Note.name: A Farewell Note
A Farewell Note.descriptionprivate:
A note found in a wooden box in Steed's Point. It reads:

I'm sorry Ma. I know you just want me to be safe, but I need to do this on my own. I can't always have you checking up on me. Case in point, did you really need to open this box, which is supposed to be keeping my things safe? I knew you wouldn't be able to resist. But don't worry - once I've proved myself, I'll come back for this, I promise. I may not want to live here but a part of me will always call it home. For now, I think I hear the Eastern River calling - maybe I'll listen to it. - Moriah

Everbloom.name: Everbloom
Everbloom.descriptionprivate: Everbloom is an alchemical and enchanting ingredient often used to add luminance.
Everbloom.descriptionpublic: This bright flower, found on the Everblooming Hedge from which it takes its name, seem to glow slightly when held, and its color shifts as your gaze moves across it.

Growing Thorns.name: Growing Thorns
Growing Thorns.description:
This bundle of dried thorns, which can be placed or tossed up to [[lookup @range.value activity=YH1t68iTZz9jSOLK]] feet away from the creature holding it, grows into a thorny hedge when it hits the ground. The hedge measures up to [[lookup @target.template.size activity=YH1t68iTZz9jSOLK]] feet long, [[lookup @target.template.height activity=YH1t68iTZz9jSOLK]] feet high, and [[lookup @target.template.width activity=YH1t68iTZz9jSOLK]] feet thick, at the discretion of the creature who activates it. The hedge [[lookup @target.template.type activity=YH1t68iTZz9jSOLK]] provides cover, but does not block the line of sight.

When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make a [[/save format=long]] saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes [[/damage average]] damage. On a successful save, they take half the damage.

Creatures can move through the hedge, but must spend 3 feet of movement for every foot they travel forward. If a creature enters the hedge or ends their turn within it, they must make a [[/save format=long]] saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes [[/damage average]] damage.

The wall dissipates after [[lookup @duration.value activity=YH1t68iTZz9jSOLK]] [[lookup @duration.units activity=YH1t68iTZz9jSOLK]], leaving a carpet of thorns that makes its former location difficult terrain.

Honey Jar.name: Honey Jar
Honey Jar.description:
This otherwise ordinary jar has been enchanted to be irresistible to any Tiny flying insects within 40 feet of it. It lures the insects in, but will not let them out, making it an ideal accessory for homes plagued by wasps and other flying nuisances. Though some insects do escape the honey jar, it is effective with the vast majority, and can hold up to a single swarm of insects within a single jar.

If a full honey jar is broken with an action, it releases the swarm of insects inside, which immediately attack the nearest target.

Temporary Tool.name: Temporary Tool
Temporary Tool.description: This tool can be used as a substitute for any Artisan's Tools and grants proficiency in that tool. After 3 uses, the temporary tool dulls and cannot be used again.

The Clever Fox (Engraved Sign).name: The Clever Fox (Engraved Sign)
The Clever Fox (Engraved Sign).descriptionprivate:
This enchanged metal sign, crafted by Bertron Steed, was created in honor of Kali Andrella's daughter, Moriah Foxhaven, and bears her crest.

The sign is a thin metal rectangle is engraved with the abstract image of a forest filled with leaves and vines - and at its center, a fox, who stares out with knowing eyes and a slight smirk. As you watch, the image of the fox moves, ever so slightly, and it dashes through the leaves before returning to the center and fading into the letters M and F.
The Clever Fox (Engraved Sign).descriptionpublic: A thin metal sign engraved with an image of a fox that appears to move and the letters M and F.

Woven Map, Steed's Point.name: Woven Map, Steed's Point
Woven Map, Steed's Point.descriptionprivate:
This cloth map of Steed's Point notes the location of several buildings of note, including:

  • a horseshoe on the building to the northeast

  • a pitchfork on the building to the far west

  • the outline of a fox on a building to the far north

  • the letter K made from vines on a building at the center

The buildings depicted, in order, are:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.nxcYkQrl7JRWmD3R]{The Blacksmith's Cottage}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.t5ac8c8mRcXlGh21]{The Barn}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.fr6fZdCaywZQjX0K]{The Ruined Home}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE]{Kali's Cottage}
Woven Map, Steed's Point.descriptionpublic:
This intricately woven piece of cloth resembles the buildings of Steed's Point, silhouetted against the light of Lantyr against the horizon of the Golden Flats.

Several of the buildings have small symbols woven into them, which stand out on the fabric like labels.

A Note For Pa.name: A Note For Pa
A Note For Pa.descriptionprivate:
A note covered in grime. The edges where it has been folded are worn, as if it were opened and closed many times while being carried, but the words are still clear on the page. It reads:

Pa,

If you're reading this, something went wrong and I couldn't make it through the Borehole and into the Pathways. Or I did make it to the Pathways and couldn't find Dailen's body. Or I found her body but I couldn't bring it back to you. Whatever happened, I'm sorry. I know you said not to go back there, but I couldn't leave her in that horrible place, not after I left you both to fend for yourselves against the darkness.

I hope you know that I love you and that I hope you feel the warmth of Lantyr's rays again - I miss seeing you smile, and though I will not see it again, the world is better for you.

I am sorry, Pa, for everything.

Aberin

Aberin Lowd's Medical Records.name: Aberin Lowd's Medical Records
Aberin Lowd's Medical Records.descriptionprivate:
An accounting of the failed healing of an adventurere named Aberin Lowd, whose mental state has been changed by prolonged exposure to some sort of magically corrupting force. Referred by his father, Kendral Lowd, of Storsa's Strand.

While at Corpin Sanctuary, Aberin repeatedly broke into the Sanctorum and attempted to wade into the pool at its center, eventually having to be restrained.

The records end with the following text:

Patient left of his own free will against the healers' recommendation to "find Daelin." Long-term prognosis is poor.
Aberin Lowd's Medical Records.descriptionpublic: An accounting of the failed healing of an adventurer named Aberin Lowd.

Beast Mark.name: Beast Mark
Beast Mark.description:
This horrific mark appears on the back of your left hand, the mark looks vaguely like a large curved fang or tooth and feels raw and tender to the touch.

At this time, it poses no mechanical downsides..

Giants Comfort Stone.name: Giants Comfort Stone
Giants Comfort Stone.descriptionprivate:
This smooth, palm-sized stone is etched with a single ancient rune and glows faintly with a blue light. Holding it feels warm to the touch, and during times of great stress, it seems to chime with a single note that comforts the holder.

Strength of Old: The holder of the stone gains a +1 bonus to saving throws against being frightened. Additionally, once per long rest, they can press the stone to them tightly to regain a number of hit points equal to their proficiency bonus (this ability does not require an action).

Inscribed Ring of Eternal Rest.name: Inscribed Ring of Eternal Rest
Inscribed Ring of Eternal Rest.descriptionprivate:
A green metal ring that seems designed to catch the eye. It clings tightly to the finger, but a clear inscription can be read along the outside of the outer band: Lowd.

If the wearer of the ring dies, the ring protects their remains from decay for one month and slows decay for the following year. They can't be made undead during the initial month.

Lantyr's Blade.name: Lantyr's Blade
Lantyr's Blade.descriptionprivate: [[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]] or [[/damage twoHanded average]] damage if used with two hands.

Skull of Merliota.name: Skull of Merliota
Skull of Merliota.descriptionprivate:
This fascinating ancient artifact is the skull of one of the First Giants, recovered from the rubble of the Primordial Bastion. While it is clearly a giant, the elongated teeth suggest some form of mutation or alteration.

Embedded within the skull and clearly responsible for the creature's death is a large, shining gold arrowhead that indicates this giant was killed by another in an ancient conflict. The arrowhead still radiates magic, making the skull resistant to decay and the ravages of time.

Sun Star.name: Sun Star
Sun Star.description:
The Sun Star is an ancient relic created by the First Giants to counter Abyssal energies and darkness. This small, toughened golden and glass orb glimmers with a warm glow, resembling a small sun in the palm of your hand.

Radiant Light. If the Sun Star is held up in the air with one hand, it emits bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet. This light is considered sunlight and lasts as long as the Sun Star is equipped.

Abyssal Repulsion. Any area of Abyssal Darkness within the light radius of the Sun Star is dispelled immediately. Creatures that thrive in Abyssal Darkness, such as aberrations and certain undead, find themselves pushed back, forcing them to retreat 5 feet from the sphere of light at the beginning of their turn, if they are within that radius.

The Final Days of Daelin Lowd.name: The Final Days of Daelin Lowd
The Final Days of Daelin Lowd.descriptionprivate:
This sodden journal has seen better days, but an enchantment put upon it has managed to keep some of the words visible. It recounts the final weeks of life of an adventurer, Daelin Lowd, who was lost in the Pathways alone before their death.

Entries include the following:

Entry 1: I am alone. I do not know where Pa or Mama or Aberin are. I do not know where I am. Down below, somewhere. I try to remember what happened but the scraps of memory seem to evade my mind.

Entry 4: There was a battle. I am sure about that now. We were in the Primordial Bastion, had made it all the way inside to find the light we needed to protect. And then we were overrun. We all scrambled in different directions and I thought they were with me, but everyone was gone. I know they will come back. I know they may not be able to find me.

Entry 7: I have spent too long here. I am hearing things. Aberin screaming my name, like a dream that becomes a nightmare because it is not true when I wake. My body aches and I am tired. I do not think I will make it out of this place.

Final Entry: I will die here, but it is okay. I will remember what I can of the past, and the ring will protect what is left behind. If you find me, if you find this, please go to Storsa's Strand. Tell my brother Aberin and my parents, Kendral and Sien, that I love them.

The remainder of the journal is filled with pictures of a family of kivahr, clearly 2 parents and 2 children, fighting against shadowy creatures underneath a bright light, and a few small sketches of kivahr faces that all look somewhat related and were clearly drawn with love.

Tome of Abyssal Histories.name: Tome of Abyssal Histories
Tome of Abyssal Histories.description:
Wondrous Item

This book — bound in the skin of a tenebrous Wyrm — contains esoteric lore about the eldritch Abyss, and its words are charged with magic. If you spend 48 hours over a period of 6 days or fewer studying the book's contents and learning its formulae, you gain advantage on all Intelligence (Arcana) or Intelligence (History) skill checks made to comprehend aspects or creatures of the Abyss. You also gain the ability to understand and speak Abyssal. The manual then loses its magic, but regains it in a century.

Cursed. This book is cursed. Reading to it curses you until you are targeted by the remove curse spell or similar magic, which negates all effects of reading the book.

Whenever you take a long rest, you have a [[/r 1d100cs<=5#On a result of 1, you experience a Dream of Nethehepticas]]{5% chance} of experiencing a Dream of Nethehepticas, after which you must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or gain @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsterfeatures24.Item.mmSunlightSensit]{sunlight sensitivity} until your next long rest.

Choking Fog Dust.name: Choking Fog Dust
Choking Fog Dust.description:
This weaponized version of Dust of Sneezing and Choking is usually packaged in a throwing bag that allows the carrier to throw it up to [[lookup @range.value activity=VngXIisnyHuRiiGk]] feet away, where it activates on landing, filling a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=VngXIisnyHuRiiGk]]-foot [[lookup @target.template.type capitalize activity=VngXIisnyHuRiiGk]] surrounding it with a thick fog that functions as magical darkness for [[lookup @duration.value activity=VngXIisnyHuRiiGk]] [[lookup @duration.units activity=VngXIisnyHuRiiGk]] and dim light for an additional 10 minutes.

In addition, the fog chokes anyone within range - any creature within the fog that needs to breathe must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or they begin to violently cough and &Reference[suffocating]{suffocate}, becoming &Reference[incapacitated] until the dust clears.

A creature may retry this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Lit Kynryth Torch.name: Lit Kynryth Torch
Lit Kynryth Torch.descriptionprivate: The kynryth torch is the source of life within each Kynryth — they cannot be separated from the creatures while alive, and their light fades within 10 minutes of the associated creatures' death.

Overheard In Ordain: A Stitch In Crime.name: Overheard In Ordain: A Stitch In Crime
Overheard In Ordain: A Stitch In Crime.descriptionprivate:
An article detailing the rumors and evidence surrounding the untimely murder of Darius Cevher. The article, written by an anonymous source that claims to have information from the Veiled Chain, details the following.

  • Many believe that Funar Cevher killed his uncle in a dispute over money, stealing Threadforge's profit to prop up a failing House Cevher.

  • The murder happened in the mid-afternoon - Darius' body was discovered by a client at 3 PM.

  • The murder was committed in a sudden act of rage, after which Funar fled in shame.

  • Investigators have yet to make any official determination about what happened but with Funar gone, his role in the murder is clear.

Paralyzing Poison.name: Paralyzing Poison
Paralyzing Poison.description:
Often placed on arrows and in traps, this poison paralyzes its target for 1 minute.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=89Vwo7uLjUYrELIQ]]

Failure: The target has the &Reference[paralyzed] condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the target’s turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Satchel of Marlstone Decor.name: Satchel of Marlstone Decor
Satchel of Marlstone Decor.descriptionprivate:
This apron marks the wearer as an official member of the gala decorating team of Marlstone Manor, with free access to any first floor rooms open to decorators

While wearing this apron, you have advantage on any stealth or persuasion checks made while on the First Floor of the Marlstone Manor before the Marlstone Gala begins.

Slowing Serum.name: Slowing Serum
Slowing Serum.description: When applied to a weapon or object, this slow-acting serum reduces the speed of any creature that touches it by 10 feet per round until the creature is no longer able to move. The creature may end the effect with a successful [[/save format=long]] and can reattempt the throw at the end of each round.

Withering Flesh Poison.name: Withering Flesh Poison
Withering Flesh Poison.description:
This contact poison spreads quickly through the body, rotting the flesh from the inside.

Any creature that takes damage from a weapon coated in the poison takes [[/damage average]] each turn. The poison can be counteracted with a healing potion or spell.

Burial Grounds Skeleton Key.name: Burial Grounds Skeleton Key
Burial Grounds Skeleton Key.descriptionprivate:
This curious key bears the emblem of the Cindaric Sages, and is used to unlock various doors in the Burial Grounds, including:

  • Various exterior mausoleums.

  • The interior doors of facilities like the Cindaric Crematorium.

  • Cindaric chests and sarcophagi.

Cindaric Crematorium Key.name: Cindaric Crematorium Key
Cindaric Crematorium Key.descriptionprivate: This curious key is decorated with a tiny shard of some arcane crystal, and is used to unlock the Cindaric Crematorium Gate in the Burial Grounds.

Ordan's Key.name: Ordan's Key
Ordan's Key.descriptionprivate: This small bronze key unlocks the front door to the apartment of the Burnished Hand Protector known as Ordan, whose residence is located in the Fallbrook district of Ordain.

Sionia's Blessing.name: Sionia's Blessing
Sionia's Blessing.description:
The next time you make a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.VtyVX7M159v6UVqG]{Death Saving Throw}, it counts as a critical success no matter the result rolled. This feature can only be used once before Sionia's Blessing fades.

Additionally, while Sionia's Blessing is active, you have advantage on Wisdom (Medicine) checks made to stabilize a creature with 0 Hit Points.

Blaze Residuum.name: Blaze Residuum
Blaze Residuum.description:
A bottle of distilled Ember Blaze extracted from human victims of the Mutagists. This concentrated compound is highly dangerous and if consumed by or injected into a living creature it causes painful convulsions and a sensation like being lit on fire.

Creatures must make a [[/save con 18]] saving throw, which non-humans have disadvantage on. Failure reduces a character to 1 hit point, and incapacitates them for 2 (1d4) hours while success gives them the effect of the @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.4J1U8piyFqYfWfc7]{Ember Blaze} ancestry feature.

The bottle bears a handwritten label:

Batch #4, Purity: 97%

The bottle contains enough residuum for 4 uses.

Blazing Distillation.name: Blazing Distillation
Blazing Distillation.description:
This vial contains an elixir resulting from a perfected blaze distillation process developed by the Mutagists in Ordain's Forgotten Cistern. If injected into the bloodstream, it causes the following known effects:

  • It produces a momentary, empowering effect on all humanoids, making them feel invulnerable and immune to the frightened condition for 1 round.

  • It produces a desire to move and act swiftly, granting the effects of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplHaste00000]{Haste} spell for one round.

  • It produces a deleterious weakening effect in Drakon that inflicts the &Reference[poisoned] condition for 1 hour if they fail a [[/save format=long]].

Injecting this into a humanoid with 0 hit points immediately gives them 1 hit point in addition to the normal elixir effects. If done while in an encounter, the humanoid acts next in the turn order.

This compound should be considered addictive, as the effects are powerful and enjoyable.

Cistern Stockpile Logbook.name: Cistern Stockpile Logbook
Cistern Stockpile Logbook.descriptionprivate:
Seized during a raid on a Mutagist base under Ordain, this logbook details the items coming in and out of this lab. Up to a week before the raid the lab was only importing materials, but then began exporting small batches of something initialed as "B.R."

The logbook does not list the source or destination for these shipments.

Fading Light Gem.name: Fading Light Gem
Fading Light Gem.description:
This magically imbued crystal emits an uneven blue Dim Light passively in a 10-foot radius. Characters that have the ability to cast spells can channel a little magical energy into the crystal to temporarily boost the effect, at the cost of burning out the gem.

A character that charges the crystal with their magic will cause it to glow brilliantly for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. Once that time as passed the gem burns out and ceases emitting light of any kind.

Infused Water.name: Infused Water
Infused Water.descriptionprivate: This sample of magically infused water was procured from an ancient cistern found in a Sedyri ruin. It gloes gently with a teal-blue light. Its specific magical qualities are unknown, and the process by which the ruins created it remains a mystery, but the Mutagists were using it as part of their experiments.

Kaftor's Research Logs.name: Kaftor's Research Logs
Kaftor's Research Logs.descriptionprivate:
Seized from the Mutagist lab hidden in an ancient Sedyri ruin, this collection of log books, papers, notes, and journals details the ongoing process that Kaftor Brenk and his excisors have been working on in the lab.

In the broadest of terms, it appears that they are attempting to synthesize a rare for of Ember life energy only found in humans. The most recent entries into this collection indicate that they achieved success, and had a working method for extracting and refining what they are calling "Blaze Residuum" which can be injected into humanoids to induce an Ember Blaze effect, albeit with some side effects.

They were also working to combine it with stable drake mutagens, and successfully created a mutant drake with similar capabilities, as well as enhanced speed, strength, and resilience.

Extensive knowledge in Alchemy is required to gather usable information from this collection, and even with said knowledge, it would take months of study and work to replicate their work.

Kaftor's Spellbook.name: Kaftor's Spellbook
Kaftor's Spellbook.descriptionprivate:
This leather bound spell book belongs to Kaftor Brenk, a Mutagist Excisor and lab overseer. It contains all the spells he knew, and prepared, which included:

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMageArmor0]{Mage Armor}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRayofSickn]{Ray of Sickness}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRayofEnfee]{Ray of Enfeeblement}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplVampiricTo]{Vampiric Touch}

Letter to Kaftor.name: Letter to Kaftor
Letter to Kaftor.descriptionprivate:
Seized from the Mutagist lab in a forgotten cistern under Ordain, this letter was addressed to the leader of the lab, and hints at a greater web of conspirators working with the foul alchemists and ritualists.

The letter reads:

Overseer,

I understand your frustration, you are right: hands are tied for now, and that will not be changing immediately. I expect you to make do with what resources you do have, and would prefer you be prepared for what comes next.

Eventually you'll have a fresh supply of test subjects and assistants to work with. The influx of refugees from the west has been beneficial to recruitment efforts being made by our allies in the city.

I will be sure you get the resources you need to do your work. You need only be patient.

Wisdom and cunning guide you.

Mutagist Alchemical Data.name: Mutagist Alchemical Data
Mutagist Alchemical Data.descriptionprivate:
Seized from the Mutagist lab hidden in an ancient Sedyri ruin, this collection of log books, papers, notes, and journals detail the precise, painstaking process the Mutagists were undertaking in this lab. The pages are packed with inscrutable formulas and lists of compounds.

Extensive knowledge in Alchemy is required to make sense of them, and even with said knowledge, it would take months of study to piece together just what they were trying to accomplish.

Personal Effects.name: Personal Effects
Personal Effects.descriptionprivate:
Recovered from the Mutagist lab found in an ancient, forgotten cistern, this is a small collection of personal journals, engraved jewelry, and letters (both sent and received), all belonging to various Arcturian refugees and Ordani locals, likely the personal effects of the lab's victims.

It should be turned in as evidence to the Veiled Chain, but could be sold for a modest sum to a willing fence.

Sedyri Fire Emblem.name: Sedyri Fire Emblem
Sedyri Fire Emblem.descriptionprivate: Claimed from the ruins of an ancient Sedyri ruin, a slow flame curls inside the crystal, thin and bright, flaring and glowing against the smooth surface of the front of the emblem face. It emits a faint orange light, barely bright as a candle, and about as warm as one.

Sedyri Lava Emblem.name: Sedyri Lava Emblem
Sedyri Lava Emblem.descriptionprivate: Claimed from the ruins of an ancient Sedyri ruin, the surface of the crystal roils with a molten stone that flows slowly in response to the emblem being tilted in-hand. The emblem feels gently hot, as if sun-warmed. It emits a faint glow only truly visible in darkness.

Sedyri Steam Emblem.name: Sedyri Steam Emblem
Sedyri Steam Emblem.descriptionprivate: Claimed from the ruins of an ancient Sedyri ruin, mist swirls within the surface of this crystalline disc, coiling in restless rings as the emblem is tilted. It sits pleasantly warm in the hand with a faint dampness to the air around it. It is much lighter than you expect it to be.

Sedyri Water Emblem.name: Sedyri Water Emblem
Sedyri Water Emblem.descriptionprivate: Claimed from the ruins of an ancient Sedyri ruin, the surface of this crystal emblem ripples as if it contains water. Tilting and shaking it causes the water to roil and churn appropriately. The crystal is perpetually cool to the touch, and strangely weighty.

Tainted Water Sample.name: Tainted Water Sample
Tainted Water Sample.descriptionprivate:
This sample of water was procured during a Veiled Chain investigation into a spreading sickness in Ordain. It is suspected to contain an unknown compound of illness making people sick.

The water has a strange green tinge to it.

Water Sample Results.name: Water Sample Results
Water Sample Results.descriptionprivate: A list of alchemical compounds found in a water sample taken from around the Burns in Ordain. The chemicals on this list are dangerous and should not be consumed or even touched by anyone.

Acid.name: Acid
Acid.description: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a vial of Acid. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d6 Acid damage.

Alchemist's Fire.name: Alchemist's Fire
Alchemist's Fire.description: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Alchemist's Fire. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take [[/damage 1d4 type=fire]] damage and start &Reference[burning].

Amulet of Proof against Detection and Lo.name: Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location

Book.name: Book
Book.descriptionprivate: A Book contains fiction or nonfiction. If you consult an accurate nonfiction Book about its topic, you gain a +5 bonus to Intelligence (Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion) checks you make about that topic.

Cinderspar Crystal.name: Cinderspar Crystal
Cinderspar Crystal.description:
Wondrous Item, Very Rare, (requires attunement)

The Cinderspar Crystal is a vibrant red and blue gemstone, thrumming with arcane energy. It is a remnant of the magic that supposedly once kept the legendary city of Rejarh afloat.

Buoyant Grace. The individual gains the ability to float effortlessly in water. They can move gracefully above or below the surface, gaining a swim speed equal to their walking speed. Additionally, they can remain buoyant without tiring, allowing them to rest on the water's surface for 1 hour without sinking.

Crowbar.name: Crowbar
Crowbar.descriptionprivate: Using a Crowbar gives you Advantage on Strength checks where the Crowbar's leverage can be applied.

Frozen Tear.name: Frozen Tear
Frozen Tear.description:
Wondrous Item, Very Rare, (Does not require attunement)

This exquisite crystalline tear glimmers with a cool blue light and feels cold to the touch. When you hold the Frozen Tear, you can sense a deep, protective magic within it.

Stasis Field Activation. When you are knocked unconscious or if you choose to activate it while conscious, the Frozen Tear encases you in a shimmering field of ice. This effect takes place instantaneously, and you become incapacitated for the duration, but you are also immune to all damage and all effects that would affect you while in this state. The stasis field lasts [[/r 1d4]] days or until someone within the Anachraenum or your own party breaks it. Upon breaking the cocoon, the ice shatters harmlessly, and you emerge unharmed.

Expedition Challenge Restrictions. This item is single-use. It only works within the specifically prepared Keystone Challenge locations and the Chamber of Agaseros. It will fail to activate but remain usable if you attempt to use it elsewhere or fall unconscious.

Gleaming Distillation.name: Gleaming Distillation
Gleaming Distillation.description:
This vial is the elixir resulting from an imperfect blaze distillation attempt by the Mutagists in Ordain's Forgotten Cistern. If injected into the bloodstream it causes the following known effects:

  • It produces a momentary empowering effect in [[/ancestry emberHuman]] that makes them feel invulnerable and spurred to action, benefitting from the effects of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplHaste00000]{Haste} spell for one round.

  • It produces a deleterious weakening effect in [[/ancestry emberDrakon]] that inflicts the &Reference[poisoned] condition for 24 hours.

  • In other ancestries, it acts as a narcotic that induces minor hallucinations followed by several hours of languor.

Hammer of She'lu.name: Hammer of She'lu
Hammer of She'lu.descriptionprivate:
Weapon @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepWarhammer0]{Warhammer}, Very Rare, (requires attunement)

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

The Hammer of She'lu is a formidable weapon crafted from mountain stone of the ancient Shent capital city of She'lu. Its head, a heavy, ornate block of grey stone carved with countless small runes, is embedded with shimmering blue shards that pulse with a faint ethereal glow. The Anachraenum believes that many of these weapons were created by the Shent in their last days, enchanted with power against the dark forces of the Abyss.

You gain +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Starshine Strike. When you hit a creature with the trait Abyssal Monster with this weapon, it takes an additional [[/damage average activity=1bWdYr8L5azfflEc]] damage. It must also succeed on a [[/save format=long activity=fr5WjG1poBDn1cPo]] or be &Reference[stunned] until the end of its next turn.

Shattering Resonance. As an action, you can slam the warhammer into the ground, creating a shockwave that disrupts nearby enemies. All creatures of your choice within a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=XvjDnihpIDhxUhqv]]-foot radius must make a [[/save format=long activity=XvjDnihpIDhxUhqv]] or take [[/damage average activity=XvjDnihpIDhxUhqv]] damage and be knocked &Reference[prone]. On a successful save, they take half damage and are not knocked prone. This ability can be used once per long rest.
Hammer of She'lu.descriptionpublic: A massive warhammer encrusted with shining blue gems, once wielded by the Shent Giants, now strangely reduced in size to fit a humanoid's hands.

Jekeroka's Ledger.name: Jekeroka's Ledger
Jekeroka's Ledger.descriptionprivate:
The First Attempt at Creating the Elemental Flux.
Astral Convergence Date: [[/date AT24021]]

Objective: To harness and synthesize the energies of the six elemental moons, Ragen (Fire), Mayis (Water), Cora (Earth), Aura (Air), Akon (Order), and Orbis (Chaos) in order to create Elemental Flux.

Materials Used: Pyrae Crystal, Thalassa Pearl, Terrafir Stone, Aerion Feather, Keteran Shard. Umbros Slate.

Procedure: Positioned the six elemental materials in a circular formation, oriented according to the cardinal directions that reflect the physical positions of the moons. Cleansed the area of any impurities and distractions to ensure a conducive environment for elemental interaction.

Arcane Empowerment - Begins with a gradual increase of arcane energy, focusing on intertwining individuals' elemental energies into the arcane itself.

Failures. Several attempts were made, but the delicate nature of the experiment warrants extreme caution. (My Eyebrows will surely grow back in time)

Achieved a breakthrough as energies began coalescing into a fluid mass. The amalgamation exhibited the following characteristics.

Visual Properties: A dynamic, deep blue fluid/solid.

Behavior: Pulsating and responsive to external stimuli, indicating a living magical essence with a permanent connection to all six elemental moons, keeping the connoction stable.

Analysis of the Elemental Flux: Collected a sample of the fluid for further experimentation. The Flux displays unique properties that suggest a high degree of magical potency, with potential ramifications for both elemental manipulation and crafting.

Journal of Agaseros: Page 11.name: Journal of Agaseros: Page 11
Journal of Agaseros: Page 11.descriptionprivate:
Today was a day of fear. The Abyssal Harbinger that has been haunting my dreams made its presence known. My wards were almost sufficient, but I underestimated the creature's cunning. It invaded the Chamber in a cloak of night that terrified me to my core. Many of my Anachraenum apprentices were killed in the ensuing battle, but through a blend of cunning strategy and sheer will, I managed to repel its advance and banished it back to the Abyss. The energy required for such a confrontation was incredibly taxing. I have since reinforced the protective wards tenfold; I will not allow my sanctuary to fall to darkness.

Agaseros - [[/date AS2306]]

Journal of Agaseros: Page 3.name: Journal of Agaseros: Page 3
Journal of Agaseros: Page 3.descriptionprivate:
Today marks the inception of the Chamber beneath All-Fable Keep, a sanctum dedicated to the arcane and the preservation of Ember’s most potent secrets. After much deliberation with my fellow Lore Hunters, we chose this hidden cavern under the city. The air is thick with Lifeforce magic, almost palpable. I can feel it stirring from below, and perhaps one day I will explore further into the depths. I shall begin by inscribing wards and protections around the perimeter to shield my work from prying eyes.

Agaseros - [[/date AS2270]]

Journal of Agaseros: Page 32.name: Journal of Agaseros: Page 32
Journal of Agaseros: Page 32.descriptionprivate:
This entry will likely be my last as the darkness encroaches upon me with the swift certainty of a predator stalking its prey. The Abyssal Harbinger was only the beginning of a greater threat that has now appeared—a creature so dreadful that its name sends shivers down my spine. A great howling in the dark that draws closer and closer with each passing night. Despite my preparations, I underestimated the depths of its hunger and the scope of its power. Each night, it claws at the barriers I have erected, seeking to breach my sanctuary and consume the secrets I have gathered in the Chamber.

If any of my fellow Lore Hunters find this journal, know that I faced the Abyss and trembled. Should I not return, carry on my work! Guard the knowledge within these hallowed walls and continue our pursuit of preserved history and knowledge in the face of great dangers. I leave behind my spirit, intertwined with the arcane energies of this Chamber. I have warded the Arcane Matrix as much as I could, and the Chamber will remain long after I'm gone.

Agaseros - [[/date AS2354]]

Journal of Agaseros: Page 6.name: Journal of Agaseros: Page 6
Journal of Agaseros: Page 6.descriptionprivate:
Today, I accomplished what many deemed impossible: a successful capture of a Skull Spider. Utilizing the enchanted nets I crafted in conjunction with a number of potent illusion traps, I was able to lure the beast into a snare. The creature was extremely angry, and I could feel its hatred, possessing an intelligence I did not anticipate. There’s a curious symbiosis between its magical nature and the greater darkness that I have glimpsed briefly in my studies. I must study its properties further.

Agaseros - [[/date AS2282]]

Journal of Agaseros: Page 8.name: Journal of Agaseros: Page 8
Journal of Agaseros: Page 8.descriptionprivate:
I find myself shocked by the revelation that the Skull Spider I thought was merely a monster is a thinking, feeling, and even speaking being! We have begun to converse and discuss many matters of the world. The arachnid shared insights on the darkness that blankets the cosmos, they named it the "Abyss". I listened intently as it recounted tales of powerful entities that had been lost to the allure of the Abyss, destroyed utterly by merely becoming intertwined in its powers. I must learn to shield myself and the Anachraenum from these forces as quickly as possible.

Agaseros - [[/date AS2284]]

Maze Challenge Key.name: Maze Challenge Key
Maze Challenge Key.descriptionprivate: This key is the reward for the Maze Challenge of the second Expedition Challenge hosted by the Anachraenum and used to open the Chamber of Agageros.

Mudflisk.name: Mudflisk
Mudflisk.descriptionprivate: A type of shelled fish that lurks within mud at the bottom of rivers, ponds, or canals in urban environments. Mudflisk provides a common source of food, although the unusual oils that it secretes are known to cause sometimes severe allergic responses.

Raster's Keyring.name: Raster's Keyring
Raster's Keyring.descriptionprivate:
A circular keyring bearing a variety of keys. This keyring contains keys that unlock every door within the Toothbreaker Hideout including:

  • @UUID[Item.DtffHxTR7BB6ogGT]{Toothbreaker Security Key}

  • @UUID[Item.okV1Ejy1uuRz7LvP]{Toothbreaker Planning Key}

  • @UUID[Item.g1iWZuiQq4snjmmZ]{Toothbreaker Prison Key}

  • @UUID[Item.YksTyoJCNfAj7oN5]{Toothbreaker Throneroom Key}

  • Raster's Chambers key

  • Raster's Vault key

Rations.name: Rations
Rations.description: Rations consist of travel-ready food, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts. See &Reference[Malnutrition] in the rules glossary for the risks of not eating.

Razorwire.name: Razorwire
Razorwire.descriptionprivate:
Weapon @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepWhip000000]{Whip}, Very Rare, (requires attunement)

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

This ancient thornling weapon resembles a long, flexible whip crafted from twisted fibers of dark, resilient vines. Throughout its length are sharp, barbed thorns that glisten with a faint, poisonous sheen.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature with it, the target takes an extra 1d6 poison damage.

The barbs can latch onto the target; when you hit a creature with Razorwire, the target makes a the following saving throw.

Strength Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=kJq0mMrVzhfAOkLQ]].

Failure: The target has the &Reference[restrained] condition for 1 minute. A creature can use its action to make a [[/check format=long]], ending the effect on itself on a success.
Razorwire.descriptionpublic: A long, thin, razor-like whip with sharp thorns that seems to glint with green, shiny sap.

Sekkir's Blade.name: Sekkir's Blade
Sekkir's Blade.descriptionprivate:
Weapon, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepGlaive0000]{Glaive}, Very Rare, (requires attunement)

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Sekkir's Blade is a magnificent glaive intricately forged from a shimmering golden metal that seems to be as strong as steel. Its shaft is made from a blend of black hardwood and thin metal reinforcement bands.

You gain +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Sekkir's Balde also deals an addtional 1d6 lightning on a hit.

Additionally, when the wielder successfully lands a hit with Sekkir's Blade, it begins to spin in the user's hand, and they can choose to create a shimmering protective barrier around them, granting +2 to AC until the start of their next turn.
Sekkir's Blade.descriptionpublic: A long golden glaive, with a thin, sharp blade, at its apex. Across its length are flowing carved patterns of ancient Aedir design.

Staff of the Seers.name: Staff of the Seers
Staff of the Seers.descriptionprivate:
Weapon @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepQuartersta]{Quarterstaff} , Very Rare, (requires attunement)

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

The Staff of the Seers is a mythical Shent artifact, carved from ancient wood and intricately inlaid with glowing blue runes that pulse softly with lunar energy. Its length is adorned with carved details depicting celestial bodies and stars.

You gain +1 bonus to spell attack rolls made with this magic weapon.

All-Knowing. You can use the staff to cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplClairvoyan]{Clairvoyance} spell once per long rest without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you do not require material components.

Knowledge of Ages. The staff's runes seem to hold rare lore passages that grant the user [[/knowledge shent]].

Curse. This relic is cursed, a fact that is revealed only when the Identify spell is cast on the relic, or you attempt to take ownership of it. Taking ownership of the relic by attuning to it curses you with a condition known as the Obsession for Knowledge until you are no longer attuned to it.

Obsession for Knowledge. Your mind becomes filled with an overwhelming desire for knowledge. Whenever you fail an Intelligence saving throw related to history, you take [[/damage average activity=aTiuBYC6OocIHApN]] damage, as you become lost in thoughts and theories. Additionally, you have disadvantage on Intelligence saving throws for the next hour, as your mind is clouded with distractions and the urge to uncover further secrets.

Unattuning to the Staff of Seers. A Character must travel to a Shent ruin and spend [[/r 1d4]] hours meditating.
Staff of the Seers.descriptionpublic: A long staff made from ancient driftwood, found deep in the mountains, it is inlaid with countless small glowing blue runes.

Toothbreaker Planning Key.name: Toothbreaker Planning Key
Toothbreaker Planning Key.descriptionprivate: A rusted key which unlocks the doors to the Planning Room in the Toothbreaker Hideout.

Toothbreaker Prison Key.name: Toothbreaker Prison Key
Toothbreaker Prison Key.descriptionprivate: A rusted key which unlocks the prison cages in the Toothbreaker Hideout.

Toothbreaker Security Key.name: Toothbreaker Security Key
Toothbreaker Security Key.descriptionprivate: A rusted key which unlocks the security doors at the entrance of the Toothbreaker Hideout.

Toothbreaker Storage Key.name: Toothbreaker Storage Key
Toothbreaker Storage Key.descriptionprivate: A brass key which unlocks the Contraband Storage room of the Toothbreaker Hideout.

Toothbreaker Throne Room Key.name: Toothbreaker Throne Room Key
Toothbreaker Throne Room Key.descriptionprivate: A rusted key which unlocks the doors to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.ZEEz2PVd0uRJHL5j]{Raster's Throne Room} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk]{Toothbreaker Hideout}.

Trial Challenge Key.name: Trial Challenge Key
Trial Challenge Key.descriptionprivate: This key is the reward for the Trial Challenge of the second Expedition Challenge hosted by the Anachraenum and used to open the Chamber of Agageros.

Water (Pint).name: Water (Pint)
Water (Pint).description: If you don't drink sufficient water, you risk &Reference[dehydration].

Waterskin.name: Waterskin
Waterskin.description: A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints. If you don't drink sufficient water, you risk &Reference[dehydration].

Well Challenge Key.name: Well Challenge Key
Well Challenge Key.descriptionprivate: This key is the reward for the Well Challenge of the second Expedition Challenge hosted by the Anachraenum and used to open the Chamber of Agageros.

Trickadee Egg.name: Trickadee Egg
Trickadee Egg.description:
This is the egg of a Trickadee, an invasive, parthenogenetic bird. These eggs are notoriously hard to find one laid, and rapidly hatch once laid, regardless of the environment they are left in.

These eggs are remarkable because they have a natural camouflage ability, and can reshape themselves to become nearly indistinguishable from its surroundings. These eggs take on the texture of rocks, dirt, or snow, and have even been found to sprout leaves to better blend in.

Like the bird itself, these eggs are consumed by people and animals all over Ember.

Thieves' Lament.name: Thieves' Lament
Thieves' Lament.description:
This sticky substance, often painted onto the doorknobs, windows, and other entry points of high-value targets for thieves, burns the skin of anyone who touches or grabs onto something coated with it.

It also marks whoever touches it to make it easier to find the thief, leaving a white X on their palm that remains until it fades and can only be removed with a healing potion or healing spell. While the mark is active, the creature marked is less able to use their hands dextrously.

While it is primarily used to guard locations from thieves, some con artists have been known to put it on items that they sell so that they can either accuse whoever buys from them of being a thief or convince their target that they have a new disease that can only be fixed with a rare (and expensive) cure.

Any creature who touches an item covered in Thieves' Lament must make a [[/save format=long]]. On a success, they carry the thieves' mark for 1 day and suffer no other consequences. On a failure, they carry the thieves' mark for 3 days and take [[/damage average]] damage.

Anyone who carries the thieves' mark has disadvantage on sleight of hand skill checks and dexterity saves until it fades away or is removed.

Nimbus Pitcher.name: Nimbus Pitcher
Nimbus Pitcher.descriptionprivate: A flowering plant which produces deep pitchers that contain effervescent moisture. The inside of these pitchers looks like they are perpetually emitting steam, although they generate no heat. The fluid contained within is valued by alchemists for its properties in creating certain potions or elixirs.

Bag of Bronze Coins.name: Bag of Bronze Coins
Bag of Bronze Coins.descriptionprivate: This large bag of bronze coins is heavy, and jingles when carried, making it easy to keep track of whoever is carrying it.

Radiant Dagger.name: Radiant Dagger
Radiant Dagger.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]]. On a hit, the target is subjected to the following effect.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC [[lookup @save.dc.value activity=C6IpBiNmWCdFySGD]].

Failure: [[/damage average activity=C6IpBiNmWCdFySGD]] damage and is &Reference[Blinded apply=false] for 1 minute.

Success: Half damage.

You can take a Bonus Action to charge the blade with radiant energy. The blade remains charged for 1 minute, or until an attack using this weapon hits a creature. The weapon can't be charged again until the next dawn.
Radiant Dagger.descriptionpublic: A short metal blade mounted to a small hilt and crossguard.

Bounty Writ.name: Bounty Writ
Bounty Writ.descriptionprivate:
This document describes a bounty in the amount of [[/award 500gp]] offered in exchange for the confirmed death of Tayan Abassador Loris Tezran.

Proof of deed must be brought to Salara in Seawall.

Healing House Script.name: Healing House Script
Healing House Script.descriptionprivate:
A form that bears the Cindaric sigil, evidently from one of their many healing houses throughout the city. Within this printed form some handwritten text is located inside a section labeled "Diagnosis".

Acute anaphylaxis resulting from shellfish response, unconfirmed variety, likely Mudflisk.

A following section labeled "Treatment" reads:

Prevention most important, avoid ingestion of Mudflisk.

If exposed seek immediate aid. Recommend ingestion of water breathing potion and immediate submersion liquid until effects of anaphylaxis subside.

Brigade Key.name: Brigade Key
Brigade Key.descriptionprivate: This key opens the door to several commonly-used back rooms within Beacon Brigade territory.

Copy of Hephiss' Keys.name: Copy of Hephiss' Keys
