Copy of Hephiss' Keys.descriptionprivate: Created by Janix Mance, this copy of @UUID[Item.tFVP9iFAgD0zEhtV]{Hephiss' Keys} is an exact duplicate, and can be used anywhere the originals can.

Courier Bag.name: Courier Bag
Courier Bag.descriptionprivate: This otherwise non-descript bag is engraved with the letters BB, marking it as the property of a courier for the Beacon Brigade. Those possessing this bag are generally allowed to move without restriction throughout Lantern Roads unless they are stealing or committing another suspicious act.

Diary of a Prisoner.name: Diary of a Prisoner
Diary of a Prisoner.descriptionprivate:
This document contains the daily entries of a prisoner held in the Wandren HQ underground facility. They clearly name Hephiss Wandren as the person who imprisoned them, after they questioned the greater affiliation between House Wandren and the criminal element in the city, including the Beacon Brigade and the muscle lent to nefarious groups across the city.

This can be used as evidence against Hephiss Wandren/House Wandren.

Gala Security To-Dos.name: Gala Security To-Dos
Gala Security To-Dos.descriptionprivate:
This list, found in Hephiss Wandren's study, contains her list of to-do items to ensure her security during the event. If found before the gala, only the top item has been checked off. If found during the gala, all but the last item have been checked off.

  • Station guard outside of "closet" for extra security.

  • Put Juro's ledger in the safe down here - there may be time to talk to him in the waning hours of the party.

  • Check that vault stairs are concealed - too easy to accidentally deactivate while getting ready.

  • Change safe passphrase - too many people know the name of my favorite artist.

Hephiss' Keys.name: Hephiss' Keys
Hephiss' Keys.descriptionprivate: This set of keys, owned by Hephiss Wandren, can be used to open doors that would be otherwise inaccessible, even to thieves, shaping itself to fit the lock as needed. It also serves as a master key for Hephiss' more mundane locks, though these locks can be opened without it.

Hollowed Dagger.name: Hollowed Dagger
Hollowed Dagger.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Often made of animal bone, this sharp dagger has a hollowed core, allowing it to carry three uses of a poison or potion without the substance needing to be reapplied.

Juro Wandren's Ledger.name: Juro Wandren's Ledger
Juro Wandren's Ledger.descriptionprivate: This book of accounts, which belongs to Juro Wandren, is written in a details cipher using @UUID[Item.sWmD7INuv2mMZABt]{Shifting Ink}, making it nearly impossible for anyone other than Juro to read.

Marlstone Staff Key.name: Marlstone Staff Key
Marlstone Staff Key.descriptionprivate: This key opens the door to rooms that are restricted to Marlstone Manor guests. It has no effect on the doors to rooms that are forbidden.

Slowing Dust.name: Slowing Dust
Slowing Dust.description:
Packaged in a throwing bag that allows the carrier to throw it up to 20 feet away, where it activates on landing, filling a [[lookup @target.template.size activity=sSp1Xij76SdckENa]] foot [[lookup @target.template.type activity=sSp1Xij76SdckENa]] with a swirling dust that slows the movement of any creature who inhales it.

Creatures who are within the dust cloud when it activates, or who end their turn within the dust cloud, must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or their speed is reduced by 10 feet for 2 rounds.

This effect can stack if the creature remains in the dust's area of effect.

Unlit Kynryth Torch.name: Unlit Kynryth Torch
Unlit Kynryth Torch.descriptionprivate: The torch held by this Kynryth has gone out, and cannot be used as a source of radiant fire.

Withering Dagger.name: Withering Dagger
Withering Dagger.descriptionprivate:
[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Made of animal bone, this @UUID[Item.UNlemxngfJ2aAuOp]{Hollowed Dagger} carries 3 samples of @UUID[Item.pyKB2u54RkGyCbdu]{Withering Flesh} poison, which can be used without needing to be reapplied.

House Cevher Signet Ring.name: House Cevher Signet Ring
House Cevher Signet Ring.descriptionprivate: This platinum band is adorned with the sigil of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}, one of the great city of Ordain's venerated Trading Houses.

Predators of the Prowling Death.name: Predators of the Prowling Death
Predators of the Prowling Death.descriptionprivate: This aged tome is bound in the curious hide of some unknown creature, and contains several accounts of ancient Oaken monster-hunting myths written in [[/language hardac]]. If you consult this Book about the various monsters known to the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken}, you gain a +5 bonus to Intelligence (Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion) checks you make about that topic.

Traveler's Rest Basement Key.name: Traveler's Rest Basement Key
Traveler's Rest Basement Key.descriptionprivate: This curious key is decorated with a tiny shard of some arcane crystal, and is used to unlock the Cindaric Crematorium Gate in the Burial Grounds.

Traveler's Rest Key.name: Traveler's Rest Key
Traveler's Rest Key.descriptionprivate: This curious key is decorated with a tiny shard of some arcane crystal, and is used to unlock the Cindaric Crematorium Gate in the Burial Grounds.

Bust of Avilla.name: Bust of Avilla
Bust of Avilla.descriptionprivate:
An exquisitely carved marble bust of an unassuming young woman. The expression on her face seems perpetually looking away, as if averting her gaze from the sculptor. Her hair is pulled back behind her ears and clasped with a fastener, carved into stone with intricate detail. Upon the clasp is etched the sun-like symbol of the Cindaric Sages.

The Bust of Avilla is a rare sculpture, one of the only ever created of Avilla the Spellbreaker. It was historically displayed in a museum in Lantiri Plaza in Skycrest. Several years ago it disappeared overnight in what is still viewed as one of Ordain's most puzzling unresolved thefts.

As purely a work of art, it would command a reasonable fee by a collector (150gp), but a buyer aware of the piece's story and a connoisseur of Ordani history, it could be worth a precious sum.
Bust of Avilla.descriptionpublic: An exquisitely carved marble bust of an unassuming young woman. The expression on her face seems perpetually looking away, as if averting her gaze from the sculptor. Her hair is pulled back behind her ears and clasped with a fastener, carved into stone with intricate detail. Upon the clasp is etched the sun-like symbol of the Cindaric Sages.

Distillation Notice.name: Distillation Notice
Distillation Notice.descriptionprivate:
A note written in a precise script:

Raster, I hope you find this shipment of distillation to your liking. While still not perfected, I think you will find the effects of this batch to be more euphoric than the initial samples.

The specimens you provided us have been valuable in improving our extraction techniques. Please keep the supply coming, I am confident that with continued experimentation our process will further improve.

KB

Raster's \"Gala Invitation\".name: Raster's "Gala Invitation"
Raster's \"Gala Invitation\".descriptionprivate:
This note is hand-written on heavy parchment in an irregular hand. Several smudges partially obscure some of the words;

To the most excellent Raster Thorn, hear ye, hear ye.

You are cordully invited to the supreme party event of the season the MARLSTONE GALA!

Join all the other highfartlutin people of Ordain for an evening of prancing around like festooned trickadees. You don't want to miss this chance to breathe the same air as a bunch of rich folk.

We look forward to your attendance.

Lumek War Torch.name: Lumek War Torch
Lumek War Torch.descriptionprivate:
This large steel sconce can be worn on your back and burns Torches as a lantern burns oil. A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet.

As a Bonus Action, you can remove the War Torch from your back, enabling the ability to attack with the Torch when you take the Attack action (using it as a Simple Melee weapon). On a hit, the target takes 1d4 Bludgeoning damage plus 1d2 Fire damage.

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Moldy Recipe Folder.name: Moldy Recipe Folder
Moldy Recipe Folder.descriptionprivate:
However, there are a few pages that can still be made out, and those pages detail a strange creature called a @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk] with rather crude diagrams of its body and possible useful parts.

Some of the pages even detail possible crafting combinations:

  • A hydroxol hide, bolt of canvas, and some clever tailoring allows for the creation of a waterpoof pack that can be sealed to keep items inside dry while even submerged. The writer also notes that one could also use the same materials to make a fully waterproof cloak.

  • Some dried, ground up hydroxol gills, dried frog skin, and alcohol will create a water breathing tincture that should give one the ability to breathe underwater for an hour or two.

  • Combining some fresh hydroxol bioluminescence with a bottle of ink creates radiant ink that glows bright pink for weeks before fading. The writer also notes that this could probably be used to create unique glowing dyes and paints, but doesn't give any specific guidance on how to do so.
Moldy Recipe Folder.descriptionpublic:
This old leather folder if covered in mold and mildew but still intact. The pages within are not in any better shape, and many of them are badly damaged from some combination of water damage or mold, and made unreadable as a result.

Work in Progress! This item is intended for use with the Ember crafting system that is still in development and may change in both description and function.

Spider-cap Mushroom.name: Spider-cap Mushroom
Spider-cap Mushroom.descriptionprivate: These rare mushrooms grow from the webbing and husks of certain arachnids of Ember, including the dreaded @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV], and can be used as a component for the crafting of certain items and consumables.
Spider-cap Mushroom.descriptionpublic: These rare bioluminescent blue mushrooms can be found in the presence of certain arachnids of Ember.

Quickwater.name: Quickwater
Quickwater.description: A sample of rare arcane water from Ember's aqueous realms and biomes.

Fisherman's Hook.name: Fisherman's Hook
Fisherman's Hook.descriptionprivate:
This platinum fish hook provides a +1 Boon to checks made to catch fish while hunting and gathering.

Due to the niche circumstances under which this Boon applies, it must be added manually to such checks.

Hunter's Spyglass.name: Hunter's Spyglass
Hunter's Spyglass.descriptionprivate:
This spyglass offers three-times magnification suitable for viewing distant objects on land, unlike those typically used at sea which often require higher magnification to compensate for greater distances.

(Requires Investment)

Additionally, while looking at a creature through this lens, the magic in this spyglass allows you to determine the creature’s type.
Hunter's Spyglass.descriptionpublic: A seemingly typical collapsing brass looking glass of the kind often used by hunters to spy prey at a safe distance so as not to alert them.

Mirror of Masking.name: Mirror of Masking
Mirror of Masking.descriptionprivate:
This handheld glass mirror contains an enchantment that allows its user to assume an illusory appearance once per Rest. This illusion does not allow for change of size or number of limbs, but any superficial aspect of appearance can be modified including clothing. The effect lasts for one hour.

While this effect alters visible appearance, it does not alter other physical characteristics such as voice.
Mirror of Masking.descriptionpublic: A simple handheld mirror of the kind often used in the application of cosmetics.

Moon Ring.name: Moon Ring
Moon Ring.descriptionprivate: The clear gem mounted on the face of this metal band changes color according to the lunar cycle. Additionally, while wearing this ring, the damage reduction provided by your Attunement is increased by 1.
Moon Ring.descriptionpublic: A relatively simple ring adorned with a smoothly polished clear gemstone sphere. Curiously, the gem seems to change its color nearly every week.

Sage's Pipe.name: Sage's Pipe
Sage's Pipe.descriptionprivate: This pipe is capable of lighting the tobacco or other dried leafy substance packed into it without the use of an external fire source, this does not require use of an action.
Sage's Pipe.descriptionpublic: A seemingly common, if stylish, smoking pipe.

Calming Water.name: Calming Water
Calming Water.description: Anyone within 20 feet of one of the fountains is affected as if @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCalmEmotio]{Calm Emotions} was used on them - they lose the charmed or frightened condition if they had it, and become Indifferent where they might have previously been Hostile.

Drakehead Spores.name: Drakehead Spores
Drakehead Spores.descriptionprivate:
A sample of otherworldly spores collected from the leaves of a Signaran Drakehead Fern.

A unit of these azure spores can be used as an alternative for any plant-based material spell component.

Heartmoss.name: Heartmoss
Heartmoss.descriptionprivate: A flowerless plant which often grows on the surface of felled trees throughout the forests of Ember. Compared to other common mosses, its higher iron content is responsible for the ruddy hue that gives it its name. Powdered, it is a common alchemical ingredient.

Nothrin Meat.name: Nothrin Meat
Nothrin Meat.descriptionprivate: This meat can be cooked during Recover, resulting in Rations sufficient to feed 4 people for two meals.
Nothrin Meat.descriptionpublic: This cut of fresh meat butchered from the corpse of a Nothrin will keep for 1 day without being preserved in a suitable fashion (i.e. stored in a cold place, magically treated, etc).

Terra Tree Leaves.name: Terra Tree Leaves
Terra Tree Leaves.descriptionprivate:
A sample of otherworldly spores collected from the leaves of a Signaran Drakehead Fern.

A unit of these azure spores can be used as an alternative for any plant-based material spell component.

Steelmarrow.name: Steelmarrow
Steelmarrow.descriptionprivate: This lambent arcane mineral sheds 5 feet of dim light, and is harvested from the ossified bones of various @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans} of Ember. Artisans and stonecrafters have developed a range of applications for this rare ore in their creation of weapons, armor, or other artisanal objects.
Steelmarrow.descriptionpublic: A rare mineral with arcane properties oft sought by metalworkers and other artisans, sheds 5 feet of dim light.

Jasper's Key Ring.name: Jasper's Key Ring
Jasper's Key Ring.description:
The large iron ring includes keys of various shapes and sizes:

  • Four large keys, which appear a bit sooty.

  • Six medium-sized keys, some more worn down than others.

  • One small key, warm to the touch.

The keyring includes keys for all locked doors or objects in the mine including the Elevator Key and Storage Key, although neither key is labeled.

Jasper's Notebook.name: Jasper's Notebook
Jasper's Notebook.descriptionprivate:
It is clear from the entries in this notebook that the author has been trying to decipher some sort of symbol — after several attempts with cryptic notes, one is clearly circled. It is the same as the symbol found at the bottom of the ooze pool in the Forest of Stone.

The notebook also contains notes on the aftermath of the earthquake. Two entries in particular catch your eye. The first reads:

Must clear the rubble in the Excavation Pit before we can start repairs. Will order some more Blast Flasks. This will cut into profits. Must tell Sellen.

A second entry, scribbled in an excited hand reads:

Blast Flasks arriving shortly. Just in time. Ooze attacks are bad enough without exits being blocked. Will lock it up and tell folks to be careful … last thing we need is some kind of chain reaction.

Abyssal Insights.name: Abyssal Insights
Abyssal Insights.description: Once per day you can reach out to the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Writhing Whisperer} to offer you guidance and insight.
Abyssal Insights.actiondesc:
You may pose a question towards this entity and it whispers in response, with a strength of connection that depends on your Abyssal Attunement rank. This invites the Abyssal entity into your mind which suffers decoherence from attempting to understand what you are experiencing.

  • Rank 1: A "yes" or "no" response, and you suffer [[/hazard 2 fortitude morale psychic deadly]]{Minor Decoherence}.

  • Rank 2: A short phrase, and you suffer [[/hazard 4 fortitude morale psychic deadly]]{Moderate Decoherence}.

  • Rank 3: A complete sentence, and you suffer [[/hazard 6 fortitude morale psychic deadly]]{Major Decoherence}.

  • Rank 4: Multiple sentences, and you suffer [[/hazard 8 fortitude morale psychic deadly]]{Extreme Decoherence}.

  • Rank 5: You may engage in conversation, issuing multiple queries and receiving multiple replies, however every time it replies you suffer [[/hazard 8 fortitude morale psychic deadly]]{Extreme Decoherence}.

Dustweed.name: Dustweed
Dustweed.descriptionpublic:
One dose of intoxicating dustweed, a dried herb that can be smoked to exploit its inebriating medicinal properties. Dustweed is known to both heighten awareness and relax the senses when inhaled.

Under Development

When consumed, a single dose of dustweed provides you with the following effects for a duration of 1 hour:

  • @Advantage[1] to Knowledge Skill checks

  • +1 Willpower

Additionally, you also gain the following adverse effects for the duration:

  • @Advantage[-1] to Awareness checks

  • -1 penalty to Initiative

Rapture.name: Rapture
Rapture.description:
One dose of intoxicating rapture, a synthetic liquid that can be consumed to exploit its inebriating medicinal properties. Rapture induces a state of euphoria for most users when taken orally.

When consumed, a single dose of rapture provides advantage on the next Constitution or Wisdom save for a duration of [[/roll 1d2+1]] hours.

Additionally, you must succeed on a [[/save format=long]] or gain one level of &Reference[Exhaustion]. The advantage provided by the dose of rapture cannot be used on this save.

Arcturian Tobacco Pipe.name: Arcturian Tobacco Pipe
Arcturian Tobacco Pipe.description: This simple yet elegant wooden pipe carved from Arcturian hardwood is used for the consumption of pipe weeds and tobaccos.

Maziran Water Pipe.name: Maziran Water Pipe
Maziran Water Pipe.description: This multi-chambered water pipe is of classic Maziran design, and is used for the refined consumption of various pipe weeds and tobaccos. Considered to be an item of relative luxury, this water pipe cools the smoke before inhalation, resulting in a more relaxed and comfortable imbibing experience.

Spellbreaker Shard.name: Spellbreaker Shard
Spellbreaker Shard.descriptionprivate:
This shard of pale purple stone was broken off of the larger central cluster of crystals found on the top of the Spellbreaker Tower. It has the same antimagical properties as the tower, but affects a much smaller area.

This crystal generates a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAntimagicF]{Antimagic Field} large enough to affect up to one medium sized creature or the space one would occupy.

The crystal contains enough divine energy to create this field for several months before becoming inert. Destroying the crystal causes the field to dissipate immediately, and can be accomplished with a strike from any bludgeoning weapon.

Aedir Wellstone.name: Aedir Wellstone
Aedir Wellstone.descriptionprivate:
A twelve-faceted citrine gemstone that has been specifically cut to size and shape for use as a focus in the center of an Aedir Sunwell. Such gems are required in order for a Sunwell to attract solar energy and allow it to accumulate within the well basin.

Wellstones eventually break after being drawn upon too many times and they generally needed to be replaced every few years. Consequently, the Aedir empire produced a great number of such Wellstones, constrained only by the local availability of materials.

There is some lost art, however, in the cutting of Wellstones that eludes modern lapidaries, as recent attempts to repopulate ancient Sunwells with replacement stones have been unsuccessful.
Aedir Wellstone.descriptionpublic: A twelve-sided citrine gemstone that has been cut with remarkable precision.

Clarion Fork.name: Clarion Fork
Clarion Fork.descriptionprivate:
A unique sort of key, crafted by the ancient Aedir. Each Clarion Fork is attuned to a specific Invisibility Field created by Aedir magi. These forks are used in conjunction with a Scrying Lens that is located somewhere physically nearby, but outside of, the field itself.

When the fork is struck by another metal object it produces a unique sound. Use of the correct fork in proximity to the correct Scrying Lens creates a counter-field that temporarily disrupts the invisibility effect, revealing secrets obscured through ancient magic.

There are thousands of Clarion Forks in existence, but they are rare enough to be valued by collectors and antiquarians. Even more valuable, however, are the secrets they might reveal. Treasure hunters or scholars covet such forks especially if accompanied by the knowledge of what Invisibility Field they control.
Clarion Fork.descriptionpublic: An elegant and slightly curved rod of silver metal, around 8 inches long, that splits near its midpoint into bifurcated and parallel prongs.

Golarne's Signet Ring.name: Golarne's Signet Ring
Golarne's Signet Ring.descriptionprivate: The ring bears a minor enchantment allowing it to function as an unlocking mechanism for companion devices enchanted to recognize it.
Golarne's Signet Ring.descriptionpublic: A gold band engraved with a spiraled design of concentric circles. Upon its flat face is inscribed a glyph in Towyr representing the modern letter "G".

Barrel Room Key.name: Barrel Room Key
Barrel Room Key.description: This unassuming iron key unlocks the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.xlo5aV0beGpvleTV]{Barrel Room} located on the main deck of the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT]{Ember's Bounty}.

Cascillian Autotool.name: Cascillian Autotool
Cascillian Autotool.description:
This compact, biomechanical device is an oxidized brass orb that opens up and contains what looks like a hermit crab mixed with machines, and modular tools. The device is capable of producing and using a myriad of tools to carry out a variety of tasks on its own. It bears the military symbol of the Cascillian Machine Corps.

When activated, this autotool intuits what the user wants, and can autonomously carry out an action from the list below. These tasks must be ones that a character with appropriate tools could attempt, otherwise the tool won't activate. The tool automatically succeeds on the task as long as it's given time to work and isn't interrupted or moved before it finishes.

If the autotool is interrupted the work is lost, the task is not completed, and the charge is refunded under most cases. However, for tasks that involve cutting through material, the work done is retained, and the charge remains expended if the tool is interrupted.

It can do the following:

  • Automatically succeed on a check to pick a lock or disarm a trap. Time taken is in minutes equal to the DC of the lock or trap. The lock or trap must be non-magical, and capable of being picked or disarmed with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools} normally.

  • Chisel symbols or holes in stone as per @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulMasonsTool]{Mason's Tools}, requiring 10 minutes to do so.

  • Cut through stone, wood or metal with a saw. This is noisy and time consuming, taking 1 minute to cut through one inch of material. The tool can make a cut up to 5 feet long, or several small cuts that add up to that length, but the material can't be more than an inch thick at any point.

  • Cut holes in glass up to an inch thick with little noise. It can cut a circular hole up to a foot in diameter, but it takes 1 minute per inch being cut.

  • Mend a single object as per the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMending000]{Mending} spell. This effect is not magical, rather the device produces whatever it needs to fix the object.

Activating this device requires an action, and consumes one of it's charges. It has 8 charges to start, and once all charges are depleted the object becomes inert and cannot be used again.

Damaged Tayan Satchel.name: Damaged Tayan Satchel
Damaged Tayan Satchel.descriptionprivate:
This red leather satchel is badly damaged and spattered with dried blood. Inside it is a collection of scrolls, folders, envelopes, and binders that bear the mark of the Tayan Empire. Many of them have also been damaged, or their seals broken as a result of the beating the satchel seems to have taken.

This bag was taken from a Tayan courier that was murdered in Ordain, and should be returned to the Tayan Embassy found in Embassy Rise, or the Veiled Chain found in the Hallows.

Report on Toron.name: Report on Toron
Report on Toron.descriptionprivate:
Toron, Prisoner number 15874, is a Tayan national, human male. Their record states they are trained in martial and magical combat, intrusion, and general skullduggery. Their magical capacity is noted as being significant, and combined with their reported skillset they have been assigned to cell #8 in Yellow Block.

They were arrested in the Ordinate when security wards went off, alerting the evening watch to their presence. The ensuing pursuit resulted in several minor injuries and one life threatening but nonfatal injury before they were cornered and captured. They were charged and convicted of assault with a weapon, assault with intent to maim, in addition to multiple counts of espionage and theft against the Ordinate and its member entities.

They are presently being held until the Ordinate determines a proper diplomatic response to the presence of a Tayan spy in the city. The Tayan Embassy has not yet been informed of this arrest, but will be once diplomatic channels are opened.

Spellbreaker Intel.name: Spellbreaker Intel
Spellbreaker Intel.descriptionprivate:
A packet of documents that details the internal layout, operations, and security of the upper levels of the Spellbreaker Tower where the high security prison is located. Information on the layout and security of the upper prison levels including the Guard Barracks, Visitation/Medical area, Blue Block, Yellow Block, Red Block, Warden's Office and Tower Roof.

Like the rest of the tower and district, the prison area is devoid of magic. Spells, magic items, and some magical abilities possessed by beings cease functioning entirely.

The prison is patrolled mostly by prison guards who are lightly armed at all times. In times of riot or crisis the guards can gear up with heavier equipment from the armory. There is also a Cascilian Surge Walker machine available if things get out of hand.

Wingsuit.name: Wingsuit
Wingsuit.descriptionprivate:
An expertly made wingsuit of sturdy cloth, leather, and fasteners. Worn over clothing (or armor), it allows the wearer to deploy the suit as an action, causing them to move 15ft forward for every 5ft they fall, covering long distances quickly.

Maneuvering while gliding in the suit requires a successful Dexterity (Acrobatics) check with the DC determined by how difficult the maneuver is. This wingsuit does not protect the wearer from impacts with objects or the ground, nor does it negate fall damage from a bad landing.

Lambent Gem.name: Lambent Gem
Lambent Gem.descriptionprivate: This faceted teal gem gleams with a soft inner light, casting 5ft of dim light in all directions. The source of the glow is not well understood, but is not inherently magical, but a natural quality of the gemstone itself.
Lambent Gem.descriptionpublic: This faceted teal gem gleams with a soft inner light, casting 5ft of dim light in all directions.

Muddy Logbook.name: Muddy Logbook
Muddy Logbook.descriptionprivate:
Many of the pages have been rendered illegible due to water damage and animal investigation. Some of the most recent entries in the middle of the book are undamaged, however, and yield the following information:

  • The team includes four members, and they all work for the same employer and are in the Pathways as official assignment. The book doesn't indicate who they work for.

  • The logbook notes that this team found a underground entrance to a tower, but failed to get past the doors. This sounds like it refers to the base of the Mythspire Observatory, which was locked until recently.

  • The team spent several days camped here on the overlook while they tried to find a way into the tower. However, once they concluded there was no way in they resolved to return to the central field camp just past the Voidspan Bridge.

  • The team noted they were going to see if there was a way to reach the ruins topside. If there is a passage between the surface and underground, they'd like to unlock it for future use. They'll head to Skybrush and start there.

  • There is also a note to ask about the missing team that went poaching Jurtak traps. They haven't checked in, or returned. The writer suspects they've become lost in the pathways, and are probably dead, either by starvation or from encountering the Jurtak.

Underworks Guidestone.name: Underworks Guidestone
Underworks Guidestone.description: This dull glass marble acts as a homing device for the entrance of the Kalion Stadium Underworks beneath Arena Ridge. The closer you get to the entrance, the brighter the marble will shine with a golden arcane light.

Pellucid Glaive.name: Pellucid Glaive
Pellucid Glaive.descriptionprivate:
Weapon (glaive), Uncommon (Requires Attunement)

The blade of this exquisite polearm is fashioned from translucent crystal, which appears remarkably unblemished despite its delicate design, and shimmers with arcane opalescence when its powers are invoked.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

As a Magic action, you can strike the butt of the weapon's handle against the ground to cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplResistance]{Resistance} spell. Once you use this property, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

[[/attack extended]]. [[/damage average extended]].

Temple of Ku'arta Key.name: Temple of Ku'arta Key
Temple of Ku'arta Key.description: This gold and platinum key opens the locked doors inside the Kalion Stadium Underworks, including all secret doors.

Cindaric Mint Tea.name: Cindaric Mint Tea
Cindaric Mint Tea.description: A creature that drinks this tea must make a [[/save con 14]] Saving Throw or fall @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule]{Unconscious} for [[/roll 1d4]] hours. If they remain Unconscious for the whole duration, they gain @Advantage[2] on Saving Throws made to resist @UUID[RollTable.cK0yaPfqWY4csCUx]{Aterican Diseases} for 24 hours.

Waterborne Whiskey.name: Waterborne Whiskey
Waterborne Whiskey.description:
Fine whiskey from the Waterborne Distillery in Arcturel.

Whenever you consume this beverage, you must make a [[/save con 12]] Saving Throw. The DC of this Saving Throw increases by 2 for every drink of Waterborne Whiskey you've taken since your last Long Rest.

On a success, you gain [[/roll 1d4]] Temporary Hit Points and Advantage on your next [[/skill persuasion]] check.

On a failure, you lose all Temporary Hit Points and gain the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule]{Poisoned} condition until you finish a Long Rest.

Anticoagulation Tonic.name: Anticoagulation Tonic
Anticoagulation Tonic.description: You gain advantage on Saving Throws made to cure yourself of @UUID[RollTable.cK0yaPfqWY4csCUx]{Scalevein}. This bonus lasts until you're cured of Scalevein.

Antifungal Draught.name: Antifungal Draught
Antifungal Draught.description: You gain advantage on Saving Throws made to cure yourself of @UUID[RollTable.cK0yaPfqWY4csCUx]{Red Cough}. This bonus lasts until you're cured of Red Cough.

Dissolution Tonic.name: Dissolution Tonic
Dissolution Tonic.description: You gain advantage on Saving Throws made to cure yourself of @UUID[RollTable.cK0yaPfqWY4csCUx]{Crystalline Rot}. This bonus lasts until you're cured of Crystalline Rot.

Heartward Elixir.name: Heartward Elixir
Heartward Elixir.description: You gain advantage on Saving Throws made to cure yourself of @UUID[RollTable.cK0yaPfqWY4csCUx]{Hollowing Parasite}. This bonus lasts until you're cured of Hollowing Parasite.

Sanguinary Correspondence.name: Sanguinary Correspondence
Sanguinary Correspondence.descriptionprivate: A private letter directing a woman named Eliren to research the Leshy and sow discord amongst the Cindaric Adherents at Traveler's Rest. The broken red wax seal vaguely resembles a cat's head, and the initial "K." is written in decorative script at the bottom.

Improved Alchemist's Supplies.name: Improved Alchemist's Supplies
Improved Alchemist's Supplies.description:
Ability: Intelligence

Utilize: Identify a substance (DC 13), or start a fire (DC 13)

Craft: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAcid0000000]{Acid}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAlchemistsF]{Alchemist's Fire}, @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flask}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagComponentPo]{Component Pouch}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagOil00000000]{Oil}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPaper000000]{Paper}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPerfume0000]{Perfume}, @UUID[Item.TwsLk1KC8SqDbL8G]{Thieves' Lament}

Ordani Wine (Common).name: Ordani Wine (Common)
Ordani Wine (Common).description: A bottle of common wine from the vineyards of Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.F7b8e10Thlz19yxw]{Orchard Lanes} district.

Ordani Wine (Fine).name: Ordani Wine (Fine)
Ordani Wine (Fine).description: A bottle of fine wine from the vineyards of Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.5B8aVQR0YlauttCH]{Grand Meadows} district.

Arcturian Respirator.name: Arcturian Respirator
Arcturian Respirator.descriptionpublic:
This esoteric mask is crafted from natural materials like stone, wood, and crystal, and though it almost never exceeds Shoddy quality allows characters to breathe safely in certain hazardous environments.

While wearing this mask, you gain the following:

  • @Advantage[2] to resist airborne Hazards (including spells and area-of-effect attacks).

  • Protection from the effects of the @UUID[Item.fJD7Nz7WyUPKlVTz]{Storm Pollen}.

Jurtak Poison.name: Jurtak Poison
Jurtak Poison.descriptionprivate:
This sticky mass of a foul-smelling compound is wrapped in a crudely cut square of skin. Taken from the Jurtak and found coating their weapons, it is undoubtedly toxic and unsafe to handle or consume.

The first time a creature hit by a weapon coated with this poison takes damage from that weapon, the hit creature makes a [[/save con 15 format=long]].

Failure: [[/damage 4d4 poison average]] damage, and the target has the &Reference[poisoned] condition for 1 minute.

Success: Half damage.

Storm Pollen.name: Storm Pollen
Storm Pollen.descriptionpublic: This pink powder is a potent allergen harvested from one of the Arctus Plateau's notorious Pollen Storms, and is known to be a useful ingredient for crafters, alchemists, and spellcasters alike.

Lumarin Steel.name: Lumarin Steel
Lumarin Steel.descriptionprivate: This rare, sacred metal is forged by the Lumek through ancient rites that transform the ashes of their honored dead into magical steel. Seldom permitted to leave the Firelands, a Lumarin Steel ingot is prized as both a holy trade good and a source material for exceptional weapons, armor, tools, and other finely wrought goods.

Fine Bouquet.name: Fine Bouquet
Fine Bouquet.descriptionprivate:
A finely constructed bouquet of cut flowers, arranged and wrapped so that it can be presented as a gift. If given to the right person it could provide a +1 bonus to a Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) check with them.

This bouquet has been magically treated and will remain fresh and attractive for [[/roll 1d4]] weeks after purchase, afterward it will rapidly wilt and rot away.

Potted Plant.name: Potted Plant
Potted Plant.descriptionprivate: A decorative plant in a fine earthenware pot, suitable for display in a window, on a shelf, or perhaps a balcony. The plant is healthy, and hardy, and was clearly well cared for.

Suspiciously Large Carrot.name: Suspiciously Large Carrot
Suspiciously Large Carrot.description: A large, slighty glowing carrot, given to you by a farmer at Oldcraft Lodge.

Falar's Curious Note.name: Falar's Curious Note
Falar's Curious Note.descriptionprivate: This official flyer for the upcoming Redwalk Art Ramble bears Falar's handwriting, the text a conspicuous note reminding himself to "have enough chalk ready for this" with the date underlined.

Falar's Studio Notes.name: Falar's Studio Notes
Falar's Studio Notes.descriptionprivate:
These old notes are dated from several years ago and have the most rudimentary musings on a spell meant to lure and trap elementals for use to power something, such as a construct, ward, or illusion.

What few solid designs are present primarily focus on the earth moon Cora, citing several earthen materials that might be suitable as spell components, but the designs are far from complete and wouldn't be useful to anyone as they are presented.

House Salva Art Missives.name: House Salva Art Missives
House Salva Art Missives.descriptionprivate:
This folio Includes several back-and-forth missives between Falar and House Salva, detailing a long-winded argument over costs of materials and unpaid work on a project that ultimately fell through.

Within the pages Falar asserts that he should be reimbursed for his materials and time, while the House Salva representative asserts that they owe nothing on the ground of the contract being terminated.

The whole argument culminates a court case in the Hallows which Falar ultimately lost.

Notes on Elemental Binding.name: Notes on Elemental Binding
Notes on Elemental Binding.descriptionprivate:
These notes appear to be recently dated, and contain rather extensive and inspired designs on how to lure and trap earth elementals from Cora in elaborate warding art using chalk and charcoal made of similarly infused minerals.

Notes in the margin indicate that this should be a bit more predictable and less chaotic than the paint suspension, but is much more time consuming to produce. Experiments have so far been strong enough to capture more powerful elementals, as well, making them quite suitable to powering larger, more complex spells.

The notes and diagrams incomplete, as though Falar has left key elements off the page, likely to ensure no prying eyes or opportunistic thieves could walk off with the full design.

Tattered Book.name: Tattered Book
Tattered Book.descriptionprivate:
This old book has seen better days. A broken spine, frayed cover, and fading print don't stop it from being a potentially useful source of knowledge, however.

A Tattered Book contains fiction or nonfiction. If you consult an accurate nonfiction Book about its topic, you gain a +1 bonus to Intelligence (Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion) checks you make about that topic.

Pipes of Bravado.name: Pipes of Bravado
Pipes of Bravado.descriptionpublic:
These pipes carefully and intricately carved from an ancient wooden branch seem almost to hum with a feeling of triumph.

Under Development

The features of this item may not yet be automated.

While Invested, these pipes may be played to instill Heroic effects in Allies within 30 feet provided they are not @Condition[deafened]. These affected:

  • Immediately remove the @Condition[frightened] and @Condition[prone] conditions if they are currently affected by them.

  • Gain +2 Stride until the end of their next turn.

  • Gain +2 Willpower until the end of their next turn.
Pipes of Bravado.actiondesc:
Provided they are not @Condition[deafened], Allies within 30 feet:

  • Immediately remove the @Condition[frightened] and @Condition[prone] conditions if they are currently affected by them

  • Gain +2 Stride until the end of their next turn.

  • Gain +2 Willpower until the end of their next turn.

Change of Direction.name: Change of Direction
Change of Direction.description: Whether due to tides, a river's current, or the shaking of the ground, you are thrown in a random direction.

Minor Abyssal Madness.name: Minor Abyssal Madness
Minor Abyssal Madness.description:
These effects occur when characters learn specific information about the Abyss, get too close to Abyssal entities, or spend too long in contact with Abyssal energies. Note that while none of these effects have explicit mechanical effects, the Gamemaster is encouraged to apply @Advantage[-2] to actions and adjust NPC reactions as they deem appropriate.

Ending the Madness: These effects last until the afflicted character completes a Long Rest, at which point they must make a [[/save charisma 12]]. On success, the madness dissipates. On failure the effect persists until the next time they complete a Long Rest, and they must roll again. Characters that fail twice will have the effects automatically dissipate once they complete their third Long Rest with an active madness effect. Characters with multiple madness effects will only clear one effect per long rest, with the oldest effects dissipating first.

Ending the Madness: These effects last until the afflicted character completes a Rest, at which point they must face [[/hazard 10 willpower morale harmless]]. If they resist the hazard successfully, the madness dissipates. Failure means the effect persists until the next time they complete a Rest, and they must roll again. Characters that fail twice will have the effects automatically dissipate once they complete their third Rest with an active madness effect. Characters with multiple madness effects will only clear one effect per Rest, with the oldest effects dissipating first.

Helkas Raider Moments.name: Helkas Raider Moments
Helkas Raider Moments.description: These dramatic moments occur during the events of Dusktide Rising during the Raider Assault.

Hydroxol Stomach Contents.name: Hydroxol Stomach Contents
Hydroxol Stomach Contents.description: Hydroxol tend to consume their prey whole, eating just about anything they think might be edible. As a result all manner of odd things can be found inside them. These items tend to be magical, as not much else survives their stomach acids.

Kaleidoscope Crystal Effects.name: Kaleidoscope Crystal Effects
Kaleidoscope Crystal Effects.description:
The light within a kaleidoscope crystal begins to move in a mesmerizing pattern, making it nearly impossible to look away, and a shudder runs through your body.

All effects last until the afflicted character completes a Rest.

Yakoshta Mine Track Switches.name: Yakoshta Mine Track Switches
Yakoshta Mine Track Switches.description: Hazards associated with manipulation of track switches in Yakoshta Mine.

Arcturian Trinkets.name: Arcturian Trinkets
Arcturian Trinkets.description: The following assortment of simple items are lightly touched by mystery. Use this table to help decorate a dungeon chamber or supplement a creature’s equipment and loot. Note: items for the trinkets listed here must be created ad hoc by the GM or player in order to populate a character sheet.

Corpse Loot.name: Corpse Loot
Corpse Loot.description: The following assortment of items and equipment are likely to be found on the cadavers of dead adventurers and various humanoid denizens of the Arctus Plateau. Use this table to determine what kind of loot a character finds when looting a corpse. Roll [[/roll 1d2+1]] times for a corpse unless otherwise stated. Re-roll duplicate or incongruous results when applicable.

Climbing Hazards.name: Climbing Hazards
Climbing Hazards.description:
This table can be used in the following ways:

  • To generate a hazard during a dangerous descent or while navigating treacherous mountain terrain

  • As a consequence for the party failing a group check during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.Ih0y4k6zcqLvYWBl]{Dangerous Descent} Standalone Event

By default, "Draw with Replacement" has been disabled, ensuring that each result will be unique until the table is reset. You may re-enable "Draw with Replacement" or reset the table at any time to allow repeated results.

Rushing Water Perils.name: Rushing Water Perils
Rushing Water Perils.description:
This table can be used in the following ways:

  • To generate a hazard during a perilous swim in rapid water

  • As a consequence for failing a group check during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200]{Flash Flood} Standalone Event

By default, "Draw with Replacement" has been disabled, ensuring that each result will be unique until the table is reset. You may re-enable "Draw with Replacement" or reset the table at any time to allow repeated results.

Group Climbing Hazards.name: Group Climbing Hazards
Group Climbing Hazards.description: Climbing the cliffs of the Splinter Canyons is rife with peril.

Lower Arcturel Mine Effects.name: Lower Arcturel Mine Effects
Lower Arcturel Mine Effects.description: Something is wrong in the mine in Lower Arcturel. Toxic breezes, sudden dips into darkness, and other negative effects sweep through the area with regular frequency.

Night Terrors.name: Night Terrors
Night Terrors.description: Use this table to determine which nightmare of Nethehepticas affects the character during the 'Night Terrors' event of "A Brush with Death." Nightmares can be repeated.

Sanctuary of Death Moments.name: Sanctuary of Death Moments
Sanctuary of Death Moments.description: Each of the following Dramatic Moments from the Sanctuary of Death event can only happen once. When appropriate, roll 1d12 on the table below and narrate the result.

Shrouded Borehole Challenges.name: Shrouded Borehole Challenges
Shrouded Borehole Challenges.description: As you try to make your way through the twists and turns of the Shrouded Borehole, you find yourself separated from your party and must find your way through its next challenge alone.

Silver Beam Sentinel Moments.name: Silver Beam Sentinel Moments
Silver Beam Sentinel Moments.description: These dramatic moments occur during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3.JournalEntryPage.NcFW8EXnMRdFekac]{Storming the Consortium} after the appearance of the Silver Beam Sentinel.

Amaranthine Archives Artifacts.name: Amaranthine Archives Artifacts
Amaranthine Archives Artifacts.description:
The Amaranthine Archives are the main repository for the Anachraenum's extensive collection of relics, artifacts, and magical items gathered over the centuries from adventurers and expeditions across the known world. It also contains a vast library of books, tomes, and other scholarly works, many written by Anachraenum members, while others have been retrieved from ruins or purchased from distant kingdoms and nations to fill the nearly endless shelves.

This collection of magical items is from the public display cases of the archives.

Toothbreaker Rumors.name: Toothbreaker Rumors
Toothbreaker Rumors.description: Rumors or information gleaned from Thoothbreakers while spectating on fights in the Cistern Bloodring.

Sage's Dormitory Loot.name: Sage's Dormitory Loot
Sage's Dormitory Loot.description: The following assortment of simple items can be found scattered through the cluttered shelves and wardrobes of the Corpin Sanctuary @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.EJHF2Q6cyKjtemHy]{Sage's Dormitory}. Roll on this table twice per search.

Ossuary Loot.name: Ossuary Loot
Ossuary Loot.description: A collection of random loot that can be obtained while searching graves and tombs.

Aterican Diseases.name: Aterican Diseases
Aterican Diseases.description:
This table can be used in the following ways:

  • To determine a patient's illness in Traveler's Rest

  • To introduce an environmental hazard (for example: consuming tainted water might prompt a roll)

Once exposed to a disease, the character must make a Constitution Saving Throw — the DC of the Saving Throw is determined by the disease. On a failure, they contract the disease. On a success, they become immune to that disease until they finish a Long Rest.

An infected character begins to experience the symptoms of the disease about 2d10 hours following infection. Note that a character may only be cured of the disease after the onset of symptoms, never before. Once symptoms manifest, the character immediately suffers 1 level of Exhaustion.

Whenever the character takes a Long Rest, they repeat the disease's Saving Throw. On a success, they recover 1 level of Exhaustion. On a failure, they suffer an additional level of Exhaustion. A character that recovers all levels of Exhaustion in this manner is cured of the disease.

Surgery.name: Surgery
Surgery.description: This table is used to determine the procedure currently being observed in the operating theater (area 12) of Traveler's Rest. These surgeries are necessitated by rare complications brought on by @UUID[RollTable.cK0yaPfqWY4csCUx]{Diseases} interacting with the unique physiology of certain @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.PSx7hfJjAtsASAap]{Ancestries}.

Traveler's Rest Itinerant.name: Traveler's Rest Itinerant
Traveler's Rest Itinerant.description: This table is used to determine the current occupant of the guest quarters (area 15) or recreation quarters (area 11) of Traveler's Rest. Each person hails from a specific biome that's recently undergone some kind of upheaval, compelling them to leave and come to Ordain.

Arcane Maelstrom Hazards.name: Arcane Maelstrom Hazards
Arcane Maelstrom Hazards.description: An arcane maelstrom is a hazardous weather-like phenomenon that channels one (if not several) of Ember's magical forces into a chaotic localized storm, infused with the raw magic of the Cosmos. This supernatural vortex is not only physically dangerous, it acts as a mystical siphon, drawing magic energy from nearby sources.

Golden Flats Ruins.description:

  • In conjunction with the @UUID[RollTable.EhmbWLCrjPdkdXRO]{Pathways Behemoth Encounters} table for the Standalone Event, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.56wHKxcvf0ImvWqU]{In the Behemoth's Wake}

Pollen Storm Encounters.description: If the party becomes trapped in a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh100.JournalEntryPage.EU66vg66ZfLCebqQ]{Pollen Storm}, they may be able to benefit from one of these unexpected methods of reilef.

Shent Moon Temple.name: Shent Moon Temple
Shent Moon Temple.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} in ⬢ s.3204.2870, as a massive ancient temple built by the Shent to worship Mayis and the elemental moons.

  • This location is depicted by the area map @UUID[Scene.emberShentWaterT]{Shent Moon Temple}.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState overMoonTemple]] event.

Environment

The lake measures approximately two miles in both length and width, forming a somewhat round and circular shape. Numerous small streams and rivers flow into and out of it, and a small island sits at its center. On the island stands an ancient temple, magically built from large stone blocks and bronze-like metal bands. The architecture was designed to fit Giants who are 15 feet tall, giving its doors, halls, and atrium an outsized, grandiose appearance suitable for larger beings.

Ecology

Especially verdant and lush, this area of the Dripstones is home to tiny creatures almost everywhere, including insects, fish, and small bats. However, the dominant creature type near the temple is elementals, beginning with countless small water motes that remain in the area, creating currents so thick in the air that they obscure the surroundings. The area is also rife with larger, more invasive water elementals. Although many of these creatures are harmless and non-hostile, the Temple Invader and its minions are highly protective of the font of magical energy they've claimed for themselves.

Lore

While most of the ruined structures in the Forest of Stone were built by the Shent over three thousand years ago, they were constructed near the end of the Shent era and are relatively new from a certain perspective. The Water Temple, however, is much older and was built close to eight thousand years ago. The Shent of that time worshipped the moons as deities in their own right and built many temples across the surface world. When they encountered the Forest of Stone, they correctly determined that the lush, clear, flowing waters were somehow connected to Mayis. Over time, Shent practices evolved, and the temple underwent several phases of abandonment, reconstruction, and repair; by the time of the Shattering, it had become a holy site of some renown. Within the temple rests an ancient machine that the Shent used to communicate with the moons and worship Mayis though the presice manner of its mechnisima is now lost. The central artifact, the Planisphere, is an especially complex and prized object, one that the Shent valued highly.

Due to thousands of years of worship and magical accumulation, the now long-abandoned temple still retains a deep connection to Mayis, and in recent years, an active connection between the temple and Mayis has allowed water elementals to take control of the site.
Shent Moon Temple.soverview: This spectacular temple of ancient Shent design sits upon a small island at the heart of the Dripstones. Its most distinguishing feature is a great lunarium suspended within the temple interior, its various orbs attuned to Ember's moons. The original purpose of the temple is lost to time, but it retains its powerful connection to the elemental energy of the moons — particularly the aqueous energy of Mayis.
Shent Moon Temple.sexposition: Your eyes are immediately drawn to the grand structure ahead, an ancient Shent temple rising majestically from a broad, glistening lake like a monolith of timeless power. Its two-tiered stonework foundation supports towering stone walls, each crafted from massive stone slabs. Slanted channels on each side channel water down into the surrounding area, filling the place with a constant roar of flowing water. The whole edifice is timeworn and weathered, with its foundations seemingly made of even older materials, but it remains a remarkably impressive sight.

Yakoshta Mine.name: Yakoshta Mine
Yakoshta Mine.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} in ⬢ s.3218.2868, and is a mine used by the nearby workers of Yakoshta to gather crystals and ore.

  • This location is depicted by the area map @UUID[Scene.emberYakoshtaMin]{Yakoshta Mine}.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState oozeControlMine]] event.

Environment

The area where Yakoshta mine has been built reflects its initial creation by a culture with a large population of giants: high ceilings, deep chasms, and a large entrance. The active section of the mine, where the current mining operations are focused, is filled with tools and ore, and now includes a set of mining tracks that help to move ore throughout the mine.

Ecology

Kaleidoscope crystals can be clearly seen throughout the mine, but they lack the power of crystals found in other location, likely due to some method of the clearing of the area done by the Shent. The upper parts of the mine (above the level where the new miners could reach) and chasms below the ground generally look more rundown than the middle section where Sellen and her miners have been doing their work.

Lore

Not much, if anything, is known about the Shent era of the mine — Yakoshta's leader, Sellen, became aware of its presence from a conversation with a trader who passed by the caves holding the mine when looking for a shortcut through the area and sheltered in them during a storm. Eager to find a mine that didn't need to be created from scratch, Sellen and the miners that she leads moved within the year, constructing a mining rail system that allows them to pass safely over the mine's large chasms.

As they have settled into life here, the miners have begun slowly gathering ore from places that the Shent either ignored or never reached, and have been helped by their relationship with docile oozes who exist in this area and can be fed metal to give them new abilities. Unfortunately, something has recently changed - shifting the oozes and making them larger, luminescent, and aggressive.
Yakoshta Mine.soverview: Yakoshta Mine is a previously-defunct Shent mine now being used by a small group of mostly Hulg'run miners, who have repurposed its large passageways and tunnels as the basis for their new mining ventures from their settlement just outside the mine in Yakoshta. This new group of miners have only been in the area a year or two, and see this as a temporary venture, but but they are attempting to make the area their own, starting with the construction of a rail system that helps to transport ore within the large natural caverns and the use of friendly oozes in the area as helpers during minework.
Yakoshta Mine.sexposition: Unlike many of the other winding passages lit by the shifting purple crystals found throughout the Forest of Stone, Yakoshta Mine was made with purpose, carved into the existing rock by the Shent before being abandoned when their culture largely vanished. Its ceilings reach to great heights and its chasms have seemingly endless-depths, diffusing the light and effect of the kaleidoscope crystals within. Between them stretch intentional stone passageways and mining tracks that lead towards the ore within.

Ooze Island.name: Ooze Island
Ooze Island.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} in ⬢ s.3215.2864, as an ancient Shent breeding ground for small friendly Oozes.

  • This location is depicted by the "Ooze Pool" composition of @UUID[Scene.emberVistaDripst]{Vista: Dripstones}.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState oozeControlPool]] event.

Environment

This location is known for its natural pools of viscous ooze. Several large ground depressions are filled with these thick pools. While evidence hints at past humanoid activity, nothing recent is apparent.

Ecology

The small island here once served as a natural gathering place for @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozelings}, who would mix and mingle throughout its shallow waters. Over the years, hostile oozes have caused the more docile ooze population to dwindle significantly.

Lore

Miners from the nearby @UUID[.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta} encampment once exploited this natural resource, transforming it into an ooze farm. They extracted oozes and fed them metallic dust to alter their physical characteristics for mining purposes.

However, new species of luminous oozes rose up from the primordial goo and attacked, decimating or absorbing most of the original docile oozes and scattering the survivors. The "farm" here has since been abandoned, leaving behind naught but empty pools and the walkways between them.
Ooze Island.soverview: Once utilized by locals as a wellspring of resources — or perhaps a farm for the ooze creatures themselves — these large pools currently sit abandoned. They are not altogether unoccupied, however, as numerous tiny oozes can be seen slithering about from pool to pool.
Ooze Island.sexposition:
The area here is marked by a series of large depressions in the ground, each filled with liquids that seem seem like water — but thicker, and more viscous. A few small, slug-like oozes migrate between the pools, oblivious to your presence.

A scattering of wooden planks and timber have been laid here and there to serve as as crude walkways that span the deepest patches of goo, along with various piles of detritus left behind by previous visitors.

Aedir Signalpost.name: Aedir Signalpost
Aedir Signalpost.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} in hex ⬢ s.3218.2870 , It was once a hidden signal tower built by the Aedir in the latter years of the Age of the Tower.

  • This location is depicted by the @UUID[Scene.emberAedirSpyEnt]{Aedir Signalpost - Entry} area map.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState signalIntentTower]] event.

Environment

The terrain surrounding the Aedir Signalpost is rugged and steep, showing signs of having been leveled during early construction phases. Though the remnants of a path can still be utilized to reach the tower's base, much of the terrain has become eroded by thousands of years of exposure to the elements. The tower itself, abandoned and crumbling, holds unknown hazards and dangers for would-be explorers.

Ecology

The Signalpost area has become a nesting site for @UUID[Actor.BQ0Ba1dNhQwg0zJM]{Suarrok}, large bird-like creatures that have claimed the tower pinnacle as their own. The florae in the immediate vicinity consist of hardy, wind-resistant shrubs and low plants adapted to the rocky soil. Small groups of @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvets} can also be found burrowed in small dens around the outside of the tower.

Lore

Known in imperial records as Aegis-Height 32, this watchtower was a vital border outpost during the Age of Sunlight, designed to monitor the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}, whose culture and cities lay further to the west and north. Originally, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} had no ill intent toward the Shent and merely wanted a strategic platform to observe them, but over time, the watchtower became increasingly militarized, and several sentinels and constructs were transported from elsewhere to protect and defend against the theorized Shent aggression. The watchtower was also equipped with sophisticated lenses and signal equipment that enabled the Aedir to observe the Shent from great distances.

When the Sun Tower shattered and the world was broken, Aegis-Height 32 was quickly abandoned. The Aedir fled or were killed by the approaching horrors of the Abyss, leaving behind the volatile substances that powered their machines and constructs. The resulting leak is a glowing, amber-colored contaminant that has begun to seep through the porous rock of the spire. Following natural fault lines in the rock, this toxic ooze has dripped directly into the Yakoshta Mine located in the caverns below.
Aedir Signalpost.soverview: Perched like a jagged crown atop a high plateau within the Forest of Stone sits an ancient, lonely watchtower, a ruin from the Aedir Empire. Though the Age of Sunlight ended two millennia ago, the spire’s stonework remains strangely pristine, as if the stones themselves refuse to forget the majesty of a bygone era. The ascent toward the tower is a grueling journey through winding paths, windswept brambles, and sharp rocks. However, those who reach the foot of the tower find a panoramic view of the surrounding landscape: to the west, the canopies and twisting passages of the Forest of Stone, and to the east, the shimmering yellows and oranges of the Golden Flats. From this height, the Broken Tower itself lies as a jagged splinter on the horizon, echoing the broken ruin still standing tall here.
Aedir Signalpost.sexposition: As you step into the clearing, the air thickens and the light shifts once again. The tower you once saw in the distance is suddenly here, now only steps ahead of you, looming over the landscape. Though it casts a long shadow across the ground, it has clearly seen better days - its surface is a patchwork of rust, moss, scorch marks, and gouges nearly deep enough to see whatever waits you inside.

Helkas.name: Helkas
Helkas.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

Helkas exists at ⬢ s.3209.2871 on the boundary between the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats} of the Arctus Plateau beyond.

  • This settlement is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberHelkasFesti]{Vista: Helkas}

  • This settlement can be explored in the @UUID[Scene.emberHelkasTown0]{Helkas} area map.

  • This settlement is featured in [[/eventState windingTrailRevelry]] or [[/eventState windingTrailDestruction]] and subsequent events.

At a Glance

  • Settlement Type: Mining Town

  • Size: Small (200 - 250)

  • Primary Cultures: [[/culture emberArcturian]]

  • Predominant Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]], [[/ancestry emberKivahr]]

  • Languages: [[/language common]], [[/language arcden]]

  • Religion: Minor temple to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}

  • Governance: Elected Town Council led by @UUID[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]{Sadri Zhalimorne}

  • Architecture: Arcturian dwellings blended with natural rock formations

  • Economy: Extraction of precious minerals, harvest of produce, trade of livestock

  • Organizations: Close ties to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}

Locations of Interest

Undoubtedly, the most remarkable landmark in Helkas is the hulking corpse of the Leviathan known as Q’ordreth, which casts a shadow across Helkas from the northern end of town. Throughout the years, an impressive scaffolding system has been erected within and around the so-called Duskmaw Leviathan’s stony remains (which is a strange sight to behold no matter how long you look at it).

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.c9BRPEfFfUlgNQyz]{The Cragside Tavern} Tavern

The aptly-named Cragside Tavern is a charming watering hole that caters first and foremost to travelers and the local working-class. Maintained by the lively barkeep Eveline Doss, the Cragside is a place where people from every corner of Aterica can rub elbows with the storied laborers of Leviathan Mine.

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.2Nm18ITo5StmzIt0]{Leviathan Mine}Mine

Leviathan Mine is the source of several rare arcane components — one of which is unique to Helkas, while another can only be harvested during the lunar conjunction known as Dusktide. This strange enchanted mine is sometimes referred to as "The Jewel of Helkas," and is responsible for the frontier settlement's enduring prosperity.

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.drnsVB8wB7mhlH3y]{The Armarium}General Store

This graciously-outfitted general store is owned by the shrewd entrepreneur Cordayne Kohle, one of Leviathan Mine’s key stakeholders. The Armarium has nearly anything a traveler of the Forest of Stone could need for a safe and successful expedition. Cordayne minds the store most of the day, along with his assistant shopkeep Thaddeus (Neutral, Human Arcturian, he/him).

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.BmnjRCSCsWNZAIyO]{Manfryd’s Anvil & Stone} Blacksmith

The forges at Manfryd's Anvil and Stone are owned and operated by the prodigious blacksmith/stoneworker Manfryd Grimm. In tandem with a traditional coal-heated forge, Manfryd utilizes a special Gloamstone forge powered by arcane Duskflame, which serves as a valuable asset during the precarious crafting of Steelmarrow armaments.

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.GL1EYjzoOTsbSV5H]{The Last Satchel} Arcanist Shop

The shelves of The Last Satchel are lined with an array of occult wares and arcane materials, including novel spell components developed by proprietor Lorettia Ben-Wren from the extracts of Leviathan Mine. Lorettia is a patron of her own alchemical arts, and is known for keeping late hours at the shop while studying her reagents with unfettered focus.

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.NXInoxatRO2KbzXV]{Glinthome} Temple

This modest temple is dedicated to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, the Elder Goddess of Magic. Lit by arcane braziers of cold Duskflame, this humble place of worship is decorated with an array of delicate Steelmarrow embellishments, and serves as an inviting sanctuary for the people of Helkas. It also provides its caretaker, the tender-hearted cleric Briannon Frost, with a sense of individual purpose.

Characters of Interest

Briannon Frost Lawful Good, Arcturian Wirrun, she/her

This teenage cleric of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} operates @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.NXInoxatRO2KbzXV]{Glinthome}, a local temple dedicated to the Elder Goddess of Magic. A fledgling diviner and a promising cleric, Briannon Frost is a tenderhearted young empath who appreciates acts of service and who is never discouraged from professing her profound enthusiasm for Ember’s marvelous cosmology. Treat Briannon Frost as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmPriest00000000]{Priest}.

Cordayne Kohle Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, he/him

One of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.2Nm18ITo5StmzIt0]{Leviathan Mine}’s key stakeholders, this shrewd 44-year-old entrepreneur owns and operates @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.drnsVB8wB7mhlH3y]{The Armarium} when he isn't serving as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}'s local liaison. Cordayne is regarded as one of the Ordani Trading House's most skilled brokers, and is known for his insatiable curiosity. Treat Cordayne Kohle as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmNoble000000000]{Noble}.

Eveline Doss Neutral Good, Arcturian Human, they/them

This lively twenty-something barkeep manages the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.c9BRPEfFfUlgNQyz]{The Cragside Tavern}. Despite their relatively young age, Eveline has a real soft spot for nostalgia and loves a good story about a time long-gone from someone who cherishes the past.

Hode Cinderhaft Lawful Neutral, Arcturian Fej, he/him

This forty-something Fej mineworker is a gregarious storyteller who oversees operation of the lifts and hoists of Leviathan Mine in Helkas. If a rumor has passed through Helkas, it’s danced into the longing ears of Hode Cinderhaft, working class hero and collector of myths. Treat Hode as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmWarriorInfantr]{Warrior Infantry} armed with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepWarPick000]{War Pick}.

Lorettia Ben-Wren Chaotic Neutral, Waerd Human, she/her

This terminally-preoccupied spellcaster owns the occultist's shop known as The Last Satchel. Despite her distracted demeanor, Lorettia is a passionate student of the supernatural wonders that constitute Ember and is often eager to trade anecdotal evidence with fellow enthusiasts. Treat Lorettia Ben-Wren as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmCultistFanatic]{Cultist Fanatic} armed with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmCultist0000000.Item.mmRitualSickle00]{Ritual Sickle}.

Manfryd Grimm Chaotic Good, Arcturian Kivahr, he/him

This handsome and soft-spoken blacksmith is the eponymous proprietor of Manfryd’s Anvil & Stone, the only major smithy in Helkas. One of Manfryd’s most notable physical features is his prosthetic right forearm, a simple tungsten-alloy innovation created by his brother @UUID[Actor.gBXPA4AerLzwSbi6]{Janix Mance} that enables the talented blacksmith to overcome a tragedy of his not-too-distant past. Treat Manfryd as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmWarriorVeteran]{Warrior Veteran} with a wide range of melee and ranged weapons at his disposal.

@UUID[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]{Sadri Zhalimorne} Neutral Good, Arcturian Altyra, she/her

Sadri Zhalimorne is the ambitious Magistrate of Helkas. A well-traveled lawmaker, she often wears a wry grin that reveals her gregarious nature with playfully sardonic flare. Sadri owes much of her success to prominent allies in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}, and has several debts to pay via her newfound station.

Life In Helkas

Living in Helkas can be as hard or as easy as one ultimately desires, depending almost entirely on what they seek out of life here at the edge of the Forest of Stone. Sure, there is opportunity aplenty — but favorable circumstances are hard-won, and the toil required to achieve is often mighty. This scrappy philosophy of rural industry means the people of Helkas work hard and play hard. Recreation is celebrated most thoroughly when it's earned, and one's social station often depends on how helpful they are to the community and/or its mining and trade endeavors. This is not as draconian as it seems, however, for the people of the Arctus Plateau consider "help" to be a rather wide array of goods and services — this includes everything from material resources, tools, and equipment; to general courtesy, warm company, and timely inspiration.

Culture

Its status as a frontier town of lucrative repute has turned Helkas into a veritable melting pot over time as more and more of Ember’s disparate ancestries and cultures began settling among its rocky environs. As one might expect, many of the local traditions pay heed to this prosperity, the most notable of which is the spectacular Dusktide Festival that only takes place when Ember’s Spirit Moon and Water Moon are in celestial alignment.

The most prominent holiday associated with Helkas is the annual Dusktide Festival, which celebrates the special alignment of Ember's lunar bodies needed to activate the arcane potential of Leviathan Mine's esoteric resources. Other traditions include an anniversary celebration of the town’s founding known as Hewer’s Eve.

Religion has a relatively minor presence in Helkas; a lone shrine to the Elder Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} (known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.NXInoxatRO2KbzXV]{Glinthome}) marks the only formal place of worship. Many citizens of Helkas celebrate their faith in their own ways, with private meetings of prayer and reverence taking place in homes or public areas like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.MRrbXWcRm5QNSZnL]{Helkas Green}.

Politics

Helkas is governed by a Town Council of eight volunteer representatives who are elected annually to their station. A loose set of laws and ordinances are recorded in the town’s founding manifesto: a hand-written tome known as the Helkas Missives (kept under glass at the Cragside Tavern, which serves as the Council’s periodical meeting place).

Helkas maintains close ties with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher} of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}. Serviced by continental logistics companies like @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift}’s Strayhearth Caravan, this alliance has proven valuable for both settlements, who benefit from steady access to each other’s bespoke goods and services.

Additionally, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} cultivates an ongoing relationship with Helkas that affords the treasure hunter’s guild a “first look” policy when it comes to exceptional artifacts discovered within and around the local mines. These two covenants don’t often find themselves in conflict with each other, but disagreements between the Trading Houses and the Anachraenum over precious resources from Helkas are not entirely unknown.

Defense

While some Helkas locals call for the implementation of an official constabulary, a volunteer militia of lightly-trained citizens forms the town’s primary defense force. These efforts are generally supplemented by the intervention of the countless adventurers, explorers, and armed traders who make their way through town.

Lore

It is speculated that the Leviathan of Helkas — referred to as Q’ordreth in ancient texts — emerged from the subterranean bowels of Ember during the Spirit Moon's Zenith; though its cause of death is unknown, archaeological examinations of its bones have revealed deep gouges suggestive of battle wounds. When Q’ordreth came to rest, it rapidly ossified, forming the valuable mineral clusters that are mined today. These arcane minerals leeched into the surrounding soil, and a copse of magenta aithus trees sprang up around the half-buried leviathan. When the Trading Houses of Ordain eventually caught wind of the settlement's unique landmark (roughly 300 years ago), settlers established a provisional camp to begin mining the strange materials found within. That humble camp eventually became the village of Helkas, a town whose reputation hinges on its valuable exports and an ongoing coincidental reputation for bad luck.
Helkas.soverview:
Helkas is a storied mining village on the eastern edge of the Forest of Stone that overlooks the western expanse of the Arctus Plateau. Nestled at the northwestern edge of the Golden Flats, this frontier town has a curious history that’s almost (but not quite) as rich as the precious ores extracted from the local mines. Indeed, the most lucrative mine in Helkas is actually the petrified gullet of a dead Leviathan, which stands as an unforgettable landmark on the northern end of town; and the strange arcane minerals extracted from the titan’s ossified remains — some of which can only be quarried during certain lunar cycles — are prized the entire continent over.

Known for the strange materials cut from the ancient, preserved remains of the long-dead Leviathan that looms over it, Helkas is a resourceful mining town on the eastern edge of the Forest of Stone that serves as a valuable trade hub to the western expanse of the Arctus Plateau. Helkas is a relatively small settlement, boasting less than 200 permanent residents along with a near-constant influx of dozens of additional visitors: traders on tour, tourists on leave, and migrant workers who hope to find prosperity in the local mines. In spite of its peculiar resources (or perhaps because of them), Helkas is predominantly a settlement full of honest, hard-working Arcturian people with relatable goals and intriguing customs; the kind of place you have to visit at least once.
Helkas.sexposition: This scrappy frontier town is marked by a truly remarkable sight: the lengthy, ossified corpse of some colossal creature winds its way around and above the settlement, a petrified sentinel. The gaping maw of this long-dead specimen hangs open like the entrance of a cave, and is lit by the lanterns of local activity. Railway lines crisscross the massive carcass and disappear into the jumble of Arcturian buildings built in and around it. Weathered signs leading in and out of the settlement read: "Welcome to Helkas, The Leviathan's Rest."

Ancient Door.name: Ancient Door
Ancient Door.text:
