Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} in ⬢ s.3202.2865, as a vast ancient doorway created by the Shent Giants.

  • This location is depicted by the "Ancient Shent Door" composition of @UUID[Scene.vistaForestedCli]{Vista: Verdant Paths}.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState overMoonDoor]] event.

  • Its appearance on the region map changes depending on the [[/eventState overMoonDoor opened]] outcome of that event.

Environment

Around the ancient door, the area appears completely overgrown with verdant plants, trees, and vines. An almost imperceptible hum is generated by the door itself, which seems to repel both moisture and natural decay, giving the door an almost ageless feel. The doorway links different areas of the @UUID[.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} to an isolated and unexplored section of @UUID[.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} that was sealed away by thousands of years ago.

Ecology

The doorway and the surrounding cliffs are overgrown with creeping tendrils, thick vines, and heavy growth of moss, which leaves the structure partially obscured and slick with moisture. Surrounding the door are several large trees with pink leaves of various shades.

Lore

This massive stone door blocking the path here is a colossal monument of reinforced stone and star-wrought bronze. It was constructed over three thousand years ago, before the Shattering by the Shent Giants. During the height of the Abyssal Shear, as the fabric of reality frayed, the Shent performed an act of desperate sacrifice: they lured a powerful Abyssal monster into these twisting passageways of the Forect of Stone and triggered a series of wards as they battled the monster to a standstill. Because of the airtight nature of the Shent door, the region beyond has remained a frozen snapshot of an era long thought lost.

Currently, an expedition from the Anachraenum, the Fulgerite Blades, has set up just outside the door and is attempting to gain access. The Fulgerite Blades are a trainee group hoping that the investigation into the Shent Door and the revelation of what lies inside will catapult their careers, unaware of the menace lurking in the shadows.
Ancient Door.soverview: In the northern reaches of the Forest of Stone, a colossal door of reinforced stone is built directly into the cliffside rock. Covered with large, circular crystals of various colors and swirling designs, it is an impressive sight, even as it is worn by the passage of time. It appears to be tightly sealed, and there is no obvious way to open it.
Ancient Door.sexposition: You spy a massive stone archway and a corresponding door of intricate design set into the rocky canyon walls. The vast stone door within the aperture is covered in blue crystal orbs and inlays, swirling designs, and metal bands that appear to be bronze at first glance. The door seems to have suffered damage along some of its edges, with deep gouges and marks visible in the stone itself, possibly from people attempting to open it.

Kaleidoscope Caverns.name: Kaleidoscope Caverns
Kaleidoscope Caverns.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the Forest of Stone, providing cavernous connections between the adjacent @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} and @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones}.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Difficult Terrain}.

  • This biome is visually depicted by the @UUID[Scene.emberKaleidoCave]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} area map.

  • On the region map, the Kaleidoscope Caverns are concealed by canopy tops which become hidden when hovering over them.

The Kaleidoscope Caverns are a system of meandering and dimly-lit caves interspersed throughout the Forest of Stone. The predominant feature of these caverns are the ubiquitous clusters of translucent crystals that reflect and refract any light they are exposed to, creating a bewildering landscape of shifting light and shadow.

Terrain and Environment

The ever-changing illumination makes it difficult to tell how large the caverns are or how far they extend. No matter how much light is shone within the caverns, they always appear to be dimly lit.

Travelers who move through these caverns often feel a sense of unease that they can't quite place — especially if they bear light with them which heightens the crystals’ effects. Those impacted by this bewilderment grow more deeply unsettled the longer they remain in the area, with effects ranging from hallucination of images that disappear when looked at directly, whispers that can only be heard when right at the edge of sleep, sudden moments of clarity about what to do with their lives, and a fascination with the light emitted by the crystals that can lead to them neglecting their own needs to stare into the crystals' depth. Occasionally, these deleterious effects linger even after departing the caverns.

Resources

The most notable resources present in this biome are fragments of @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal} which are plentiful within the area. Other resources include rare minerals, gemstone deposits, ooze formations, and a variety of mushrooms and fungal growth. It is not known whether any creatures are native to this habitat, and the stories told by travelers tend to vary wildly on this account.

Lore and History

Various legends speculate about the origins of the mysterious magic inherent in the Kaleidoscope Caverns; experimentation of sorcerous Nir’ae, an ancient war between the Shent and the Abyss, or other stranger tales. Sages continue to study the caverns and some ambitious scholars believe spending time within them is worth the risk in exchange for potential clarity offered by the crystals’ arcane influence. This research is dangerous, and slow to progress.
Kaleidoscope Caverns.soverview: The Kaleidoscope Caverns are widely regarded as the Forest of Stone's most curious habitat, distinguished by the strange, enchanted effects of the luminous crystals that lend the biome its name.
Kaleidoscope Caverns.sexposition:
A breathtaking sight unfolds before you — a vast system of interconnected caves filled with pockets of darkness and light that make it nearly impossible to gauge its full size. These caverns are adorned with strange, prismatic crystals that jut out from the ground and walls like the jagged teeth of a colossal beast.

The crystals shimmer with an otherworldly opalescence, the faint light from the mouth of the cave behind you reflects and refracts into a mesmerizing pattern of vivid color. The reflections dance hypnotically across the stone floor, creating an ever-shifting landscape of shadow and light.

Verdant Paths.name: Verdant Paths
Verdant Paths.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is the predominant biome of the Forest of Stone, located on the western side of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Normal Terrain}.

  • This biome is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.vistaForestedCli]{Vista: Verdant Paths} and the @UUID[Scene.emberForestedCli]{Verdant Paths} area map.

  • The Pollen Storm @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.HLQWWXHPxWPAXRDz]{Weather} event can originate in this biome.

The Verdant Paths are an expanse of stone cliffs and canyons whose rocky surfaces are coated with signs of life – crawling vines, shocks of color from local mosses, and trees with twisting branches covered in bright foliage. Ample shade from the overgrown cliffs creates numerous stretches of dim, dappled space to rest and hide. The paths are filled with wildlife as a result, with countless safe havens and habitats for all manner of creatures to flourish in.

Environment

Traveling through the winding passages is easy and comfortable in most cases, with plenty of shade, water, and well-worn terrain with minimal obstacles beyond the infrequent landslide or collapsed archway. Shade from dense overhead foliage creates a cool, dim environment that is often damp with condensation, but gives easy escape from the sun.

It is only vertical traversal that becomes slow and hazardous, as the mossy crags and overgrown cliffs make it hard to judge perches and handholds, many of which are slippery or unstable.

Ecology

The Verdant Paths abound in botanical and mineral wealth, and teems with curious animals suitable for hunting and trapping, and perhaps even domestication. Despite the richness of the region, there is only one active mine in the paths, as the remote and sometimes difficult to access nature of the paths makes accessing its treasures a trial.

Lore

The Verdant Paths, like the rest of the Forest of Stone. was created in a battle between two giant creatures – a Leviathan and a wurm – who tore through what was once one of the large foothills at the base of the Hersa Mountains, opening its caverns to the sky and leaving broad passageways through the newly-created Forest of Stone in their wake.

Over time, these passageways changed dramatically, their original forms being lost to the march of time. Through weathering of wind and rain, the movement of animals, the growth of local plants, and the cycling of the seasons the region was transformed into the Verdant Paths seen today.

In the past this region also fell under the frontier regions of the Shent culture, and was home to at least two mines and a temple, if not more. As a border region of their nation and the ever expanding Aedir empire, it was also home to a spy post used to monitor the area.
Verdant Paths.soverview: The Verdant Paths constitute the Forest of Stone's central and most hospitable biome. Lush with mountainous flora and fauna, these ancient canyon trails wind their way through the sub-region's neighboring environments and impassable rocky terrain like a craggy labyrinth.
Verdant Paths.sexposition: A maze-like network of narrow, rugged canyons and mossy crags obscures the horizon. The stony cliff sides and rocky overhangs of this spectacular landscape are decorated with lush flora — from fruit-bearing Wurmwood Trees overhead to sparse blankets of Heartmoss and Snakevine in the gulleys below. Travel here is likely slow-going and somewhat hazardous.

Dripstones.name: Dripstones
Dripstones.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the Forest of Stone, on the western side of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Difficult Terrain}.

  • This biome is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaDripst]{Vista: Dripstones} and the @UUID[Scene.emberDripstones0]{Dripstones} area map.

The meandering cliffs of the Forest of Stone occasionally conceal and support a mossy biome of glistening and mineral-rich lowland known as the Dripstones. These humid and vaporous areas are notable for precarious paths, cascading waterfalls, slick rock, cenotes, and gleaming pools bounded by sudoriferous erosions and teeming with semi-aquatic flora and other life.

Environment

The pond-dappled lowlands of the Dripstones are challenging and perilous to traverse, this biome is difficult terrain unless otherwise noted. Rain or fog is more common in this environment, resulting in an intermittent haze that can occasionally stifle long-range visibility of the area.

Ecology

There are abundant sources of potable water in the Dripstones, along with a variety of other resources such as oozes, arcane vegetation, and rare mineral deposits. Creatures native to this habitat are frequently amphibious. Water elementals are also more likely to be observed in this environment.

Lore

The Dripstones were shaped in part by the cataclysmic events of The Shattering, like much of Ember. Prior to that pivotal moment, the Forest of Stone played host to a handful of Shent landmarks and remote Aedir strongholds. Most notably, the Shent Moon Temple in the northern reaches of the Dripstones is noteworthy for its powerful attunement to Ember’s moons, and Mayis in particular. In the war following the Abyssal Shear, however, the Shent in this area were driven back, leaving behind only ruins and fallen guardians.
Dripstones.soverview: The Dripstones are a scattered collection of moist lowland areas that decorate the Forest of Stone's meandering landscape. Marked by preternatural humidity and semi-aquatic wildlife, the Dripstones comprise a biome unlike any other in this storied mountainous region.
Dripstones.sexposition: The lush wilderness of the Verdant Paths gives way to a mossy, mist-laden stretch of lowland canyon marked by glistening rocks and tepid ponds. Here and there, you identify the crumbling foundations of timeworn ruins peeking out beneath the overgrowth of this water-soaked preternatural landscape.

Yakoshta.name: Yakoshta
Yakoshta.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

Yakoshta exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} biome in ⬢ s.3217.2866 on the south side of the Forest of Stone.

  • This settlement is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaYakosh]{Vista: Yakoshta}.

  • This settlement is featured in [[/eventState oozeControlCamp]] and subsequent events.

At a Glance

  • Settlement Type: Mining Encampment

  • Size: Miniscule (30-60)

  • Primary Cultures: [[/culture emberArcturian]]

  • Predominant Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHulgrun]]

  • Languages: [[/language common]], [[/language arcden]]

  • Governance: Founder (@UUID[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]{Sellen}) and mine supervisor (@UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper})

  • Architecture: Stone-hewn cliffside dwellings

  • Economy: Mining and trade of precious metal ores

Landmarks

Patch's General Store

An armor and clothing repair shop run by Patch, a hulg'run whose body and clothing are both a patchwork of colors.

Mine Mixtures Alchemist

A potion shop run by Simar, a Thornling from Brevin (who sells about as many placebos as they do real potions - so far no one has noticed).

Day's End Lodging

A gathering point for the miners, where they come together to talk about the day, hang out, and occasionally hold social events.

Locals

@UUID[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]{Sellen} Neutral, Hulg'run, Arcturian, she/her

The leader of the Yakoshta mining community. Straightforward but friendly, she is excited about the future of the mine, but takes a slow and steady approach to progress. While she would never admit it to anyone, she sometimes feels isolated by her position, and brought her brother Tauric with her to Yakoshta in part because his love for her and lack of interest in mining keeps her grounded.

@UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper} Chaotic Neutral, Hulg'run, Arcturian, he/him

The mine supervisor, working underneath Sellen to ensure that the mine is as productive as possible. Jasper is aware that Sellen mostly gave him this position because he has been agitating about ways to make the mine more efficient, but sees his role as being a voice for progress (and making enough money to add more jewels as ornamentation).

@UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]{Tauric} Neutral Good, Hulg'run, Arcturian, he/him

Sellen's younger brother, who accompanied her to support her and get his chance to "explore the world." He found his passion when he discovered the friendly oozes in the area and he has become an ooze enthusiast, championing them as helpers of the miners and as a way to learn more about nature. He is convinced he can communicate with his ooze, Squish, and takes it everywhere.

Garil Neutral, Human, Ordani, they/them

A human trader who is loosely affiliated with the Ordani Trading Houses and the main source of income and supplies to Yakoshta. They provide the wagon and take requests for goods from Sellen in return for a higher than average fee and the opportunity to gossip freely about everything going on in the Arctus Plateau.

Culture

Nearly everyone in the encampment has a primary job within the mine, but there are a few friends, romantic partners, and family members who accompanied the group. Most of these supporters of the project primarily work to keep up the community by building new structures, harvesting the nearby area, or logging and tracking goods that come out of the mine. Others function as traders, meeting caravans that come through the Forest of Stone or transporting wagons of ore to the nearby town of @UUID[.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}.

An outlier resident of the town is @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]{Tauric}, who is focused on learning more about the oozes. While his early enthusiasm for this project led to the miners discovering the helpful properties of the metallic oozes, there are some who grumble that he is allowed to be a wanderer instead of contributing to the encampment because he is Sellen's brother. The mine supervisor, @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper}, is one of the main grumblers, as he wants the mine to make as much profit as possible.

Governance

The leader of the Yakoshta encampment and mining operation, @UUID[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]{Sellen}, brought the miners to Yakoshta to take advantage of the Shent ruins, mine as much as they can, and earn enough money to create a long-term mining community elsewhere.

Sellen is supported in her work by @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper}, the supervisor of the mine who handles most logistical operations related to mining activity.
Yakoshta.soverview:
This small encampment, located outside of Yakoshta Mine, houses the workers who have converted the old abandoned Shent mine into an active source of ore. Yakoshta is populated mostly by Hulg'run and Thornlings who don't need traditional agriculture in order to survive.

The encampment is seen by its inhabitants to be both temporary in nature — many of its workers hope to settle in Helkas or elsewhere after the mine becomes profitable — and as a place of great camaraderie. Living here makes for hard work, but is rewarded with good company and good cheer.
Yakoshta.sexposition:
A broad clearing is nestled beneath the overhanging rock above, protected from the elements on three sides by the tall cliffs around them and from any dangers of the Forest of Stone by a narrow stone wall in front of them. The stone that makes up each building appears to have been carved out of the side of the cliffs themselves and shaped together into rounded circular buildings surrounding a central, more open clearing.

Beyond the buildings, at the far end of the encampment, an arched opening has been carved into the cliff at the back of the settlement. While it is impossible to see exactly what lies beyond it, it glows with a faint purple light.

Writhing Grave.name: Writhing Grave
Writhing Grave.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} in ⬢ s.3206.2871, as a site of an ancient battle that still imprisons a terrible Abyssal monster.

  • This location is depicted by the area map @UUID[Scene.emberWrithingGrv]{Writhing Grave}.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer]] event.

Environment

This location bears invisible scars of a battle fought long ago, deep gouges in the earth concealed by millennia of natural growth. The area seems normal at first — aside from a subtle sense of unease — but as one nears the waterfall nexus, it becomes readily apparent that a sinister presence has befouled the land.

Ecology

The flora and fauna of this location resemble the rest of the Dripstones, although the area does feature some heavy decay and rot throughout — particularly where the Abyssal entity known as the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Writhing Whisperer} was fought and imprisoned long ago.

Lore

This ill-fated location was marked by destiny long ago, when an abyssal entity was all but defeated and trapped beneath the righteous blade of an ancient Shent warrior. And the region has not been seen or scouted for thousands of years. Hence, very little is known about this place. The lingering Abyssal presence of the Writhing Whisperer is known only to the Shent seer @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth} — whose arcane spirit monitors the malevolent creature from beyond time and space.
Writhing Grave.soverview: The gravesite here is a nexus of waterfalls both large and small, whose cascading paths converge into a large pool. The area's wild growth becomes more visibly withered and corrupted the closer one gets to the epicenter of its abyssal taint.
Writhing Grave.sexposition: The great cliffs that encircle the northern Dripstones valley converge here, creating a space where multiple waterfalls cascade down the rock and culminate in a shallow lake. The terraced shelves of rock and greenery bear the scars of an ancient battle, and are haunted by the pervasive scent of decay. Even the brilliant verdancy of vegetation and the percussive roar of the falls can't fully mask the gnawing sense that something here is amiss.

Giant's Moonstone.name: Giant's Moonstone
Giant's Moonstone.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} in ⬢ s.3209.2854.

  • This location is depicted by the "Shent Moonstone" composition of @UUID[Scene.vistaForestedCli]{Vista: Verdant Paths}.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState windingTrailMoonstone]] event.

Environment

The Moonstone is surrounded by dense, overgrown plants, trees, and vines, some of which have intertwined with the stone pillar and curled around it. Nearby, large reddish-pink bulbs can be seen, and most of the plants here appear exceptionally lush, nourished by water motes that constantly emerge and vanish around the blue crystal. Towards the base of the nearby cliffs are a series of small, shallow pools of incredibly clear water.

Ecology

The surrounding area seems to be filled with smaller creatures, beetles, flies, and various insects that scuttle and flit around the Moonstone itself. Several fish can be seen floating lazily in the nearby waters. When the elemental moon of Mayis is dominant, the Moonstone begins to radiate an increased amount of magical energy and is overrun with tiny, harmless swarms of water motes that dance and swirl around it like enchanted drops of rain.

Lore

This ancient monument is a moonstone, a marvel of Shent toechology and magic, constructed over three thousand years ago, long before the events of the Shattering. It comprises a thick, reinforced stone pillar with a huge crystal orb inset into the top. All moonstones are crafted to channel a specific moon's energy, and this one is built for the elemental moon of Mayis. The purpose of the moonstone was to monitor a certain area and relay information about local environmental conditions, such as humidity and temperature, but it also functioned as a communication relay. This moonstone is one of the few that remains active in the region, although its power has significantly faded; nevertheless, it still draws energy from the water moon. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis} and is especially potent when the moon is dominant in the sky, and can provide a unique boon for characters who are duly attuned.
Giant's Moonstone.soverview: This ancient monument is a relic from a bygone era, a moonstone crafted by the Shent Giants as a communication and monitoring device. Despite being worn, battered, and weathered by the elements, it somehow still functions. It's evident by the faint blue motes that surround the huge crystal orb atop the stone pillar that a potent magic still resides within, but its original purpose has been lost to history.
Giant's Moonstone.sexposition: You spy a large stone monument beyond the southern side of the road, standing above the overgrowth in ageless defiance. Crafted from weathered stone and a strange bronze-like metal, this curious landmark is crowned with a gleaming blue orb made of polished crystal. Upon further inspection, the orb seems to hold a swirling storm of energy inside of it, slowly turning and twisting, as if driven by some unseen force. A longer glance suggests that the ancient stone beneath the orb is etched with weathered runes and inscriptions.

Dry Outpost.name: Dry Outpost
Dry Outpost.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} in hex ⬢ s.3205.2861 and is used by various caravans and travelers who journey through the Forest of Stone.

  • This location is depicted by the "Dry Outpost" composition of @UUID[Scene.vistaForestedCli]{Vista: Verdant Paths}.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState windingTrailRestful]] event.

Environment

While the surroundings are filled with the lush plants and foliage typical of the Forest of Stone, some of the decaying buildings seem to be in various states of repair, and the area around them has been cleared. Numerous signs of refurbishment are evident: windows are boarded up, sagging roofs have been reinforced, and several new wooden planks have been installed in place of older ones.

Ecology

When travelers pass through, the area serves as a refuge for smaller creatures like rodents, birds, and lizards that live nearby and inside the structures. However, when caravans arrive, the area becomes somewhat quieter, and the only visible life consists of a swarm of flying and scurrying insects that seem to infest the area.

Lore

Once a bustling rest stop with a tavern and general store, this small homestead was established and operated by the Joyton family for nearly thirty years. After Varon Joyton’s death, his wife, now in her eighties, chose to relocate to Helkas, leaving the site abandoned. Over the past decade, neglect has taken a toll, evident through visible damage and deterioration. In another ten years, it’s possible that no structures will remain.
Dry Outpost.soverview: This once-bustling homestead was abandoned several years ago, leaving little evidence of its former inhabitants. Now, it endures as a makeshift outpost for various caravans and travelers who journey through the Forest of Stone. It is used by travelers often enough that some of the buildings have been reinforced and repaired, but no one lives here permanently.
Dry Outpost.sexposition: Nestled below the trail's towering verdant cliffs, you see a few ramshackle buildings of hand-laid stone and weathered timber. The largest building’s wattle roof sags and has partially collapsed, held up by the desperate efforts of thick vines that snake their way in and out of several holes in the crumbling structure. These dwellings still offer a small measure of shelter despite their derelict state, and are a welcome sight for travelers navigating the wet and winding canyon paths.

Crystal Carving Cavern.name: Crystal Carving Cavern
Crystal Carving Cavern.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} in ⬢ s.3198.2867, and was once used by the Shent to carve crystals for experimentation.

  • This location is explored in the "Arcane Machine" composition of the @UUID[Scene.emberKaleidoCave]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} area map.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState signalIntentCrystals]] event.

Environment

Throughout the cavern, signs of ancient industry are evident everywhere. Many of the larger crystals have small chips and cracks, likely from mining activities or samples taken for study. Some crystals are wrapped with bands of bronze metal for reinforcement or containment. Scattered, brittle tools, fading and crumbling, are found in piles or corners. The same can be said for bones and remains of ancient Giants; there are several scattered around the cavern, all of which seem to have met violent and terrible ends with twisted limbs, bones lying at odd angles, and skulls smashed by tremendous force.

Ecology

Initially, the cavern appears lifeless, but after a few moments, several small creatures become visible. Tiny, strange-looking lizards with crystal-like scales can be seen, and tiny nearly invisible, eels with transparent skin drift through the air, shimmering and vanishing in the faint light.

Lore

Long abandoned, there is no indication of how long the Shent visited and utilized the cavern to gather the crystals, though it's likely they only utilized the crystal technology around the time of the Shattering, roughly two and a half thousand years ago. In the center of the cave stands a now badly damaged brass machine. Originally created by the sage Mioroth, it was intended to protect the region from the confusing magic of the kaleidoscope crystals. The Shent used this cavern to carve runic symbols into crystals, transforming them into personal wards in their upcoming fight against the Abyss.
Crystal Carving Cavern.soverview: The Crystal Carving Cavern is a distant recess of the Kaiedoscope Caverns in the northern-most reaches of the Forest of Stone. This cave shows evidence of previous occupation, although the remains of its prior inhabitants suggest a grim fate.
Crystal Carving Cavern.sexposition: In the glittering gloom of these caves the remnants of activity can be found. The shadowed shapes of skeletal remains, discarded tools, and broken machinery are scattered about the cavern, bathed in nacreous light from the cave’s scintillating crystals.

Shard of Akon.name: Shard of Akon
Shard of Akon.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} in ⬢ s.3211.2872. The ruins are from the moon of Akon that fell to the surface after the events of the Shattering.

  • This location is depicted by the "Shard of Akon" composition of @UUID[Scene.vistaForestedCli]{Vista: Verdant Paths}.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState windingTrailCampsite]] event.

Environment

Scattered throughout the area are large, metallic-looking ruins that cast long shadows and hang at odd angles, blocking the sky. This cool, damp, sheltered space has been heavily used by travelers as a resting spot, with many newer bolts, hooks, and furnishings affixed to the metal ruins. Campsites have been cleared of underbrush, and old and discarded items are hidden among plants, such as rufuse, broken tools, and broken pottery. It's evident from a cursory glance that travelers often camp here, and there are small collections of fallen logs assembled around soot-stained fire pits among the ruins as well.

Ecology

The air beneath the Akon ruins is damp and still, with the structures providing ample shade from the overhead sun. Numerous insects scuttle around in the shadows and across the moist soil. Many plants, like bushes and vines, appear to have gradually crept over the metal ruins over centuries, accumulating and contributing to their decay.

Lore

During the Shattering two and a half thousand years ago, the moon of Akon was shattered, and numerous pieces, both large and small, fell onto the surface world. It is not entirely clear which part of the moon these shards originated from, but their design is extremely unusual, featuring twisting shapes and intricate markings. These shards are also heavily weathered, with rusted and dulled surfaces that make them appear more like twisted rocks than metal. However, scraping away the outer layer can reveal the truth. Very few people know the true nature of these ruins, and that they are a part of the moon of Akon. But as many caravans pass through the Forest of Stone each year, this sheltered campsite has become a key point of interest on the route to and from @UUID[.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas} in the east.
Shard of Akon.soverview: This massive fragment of strange rock is said to originate from the shattered moon Akon. It provides shelter from the unpredictable environs of the Forest of Stone and serves as an unusual campsite for travelers of the region.
Shard of Akon.sexposition: A jagged slab of dark rock protrudes out from the cliffside here, where it is wedged motionless. This rock provides an overhang underneath which travelers might seek shelter, but is inconsistent in both texture and color with the natural stone of the area. Visible within its mass are protrusive relics of ancient clockwork — centuries old, twisted, and weathered by the elements.

Overgrown Sunwell.name: Overgrown Sunwell
Overgrown Sunwell.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} in ⬢ s.3211.2872, three miles south of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}.

  • There is no area map or vista composition that visually depicts this location.

  • This location is featured in the [[/eventState signalIntentSunwell]] event.

  • Its appearance on the region map changes depending on the [[/eventState signalIntentSunwell restored]] outcome of that event.

This particular Sunwell is significantly overgrown by the lush flora of the Verdant Paths and missing its Wellstone, a central orb that attracts solar energy and allows it to gather within the Sunwell's shallow basin. Consequently, this Sunwell is inoperable unless the overgrowth is cleared and a replacement Wellstone is procured.

Environment

The Overgrown Sunwell exists in a broad dale with expansive views of the sky above. The perimeter of this dale is surrounded by rocky spires and chimneys that are typical of the Forest of Stone, but this location provides a rare clearing that is less claustrophobic than typical for the biome. It is likely because of this comparatively spacious setting that the Aedir constructed the Sunwell here.

Ecology

The clearing around the Sunwell is free of large obstacles, but the dale is still thick with low-lying trees, shrubs, vines, bushes, flowers, and other foliage. Many creatures who typically lurk in the rocky recesses of the Verdant Paths avoid such expansive sunlit areas, lest they fall prey to regional predators like Suarrok or Crag Raptors.

Lore

Shortly before the Shattering, this region of eastern Aterica marked the outlying boundary of the Aedir empire. Advanced scouts and imperial regiments were tasked with building a network of functional and defensive structures across this perimeter to help secure the Empire's foothold upon the continent. This Sunwell was one of thousands constructed across the continent. Most such wells have been destroyed, while a rare few function still to this day.
Overgrown Sunwell.soverview:
This structure was built by the Aedir thousands of years ago, before the Shattering, as a monument to the practice of spiritual and arcane communion with Lantyr, and to collect solar energy with which to infuse their artifice or empower their spellcraft. In its original operational form, the basin of this Sunwell would collect latent energy from the sun during daylight hours, allowing Aedir magi to gather and direct that daily battery of energy.

The architectural arcana to create such Sunwells has become lost knowledge, but there remain a number of surviving Sunwells scattered across Aterica where the Aedir constructed them, often near locations of strategic importance to the expansion of their flourishing empire.
Overgrown Sunwell.sexposition:
A spacious dale before you is dominated by a circular ruin that rises from the earth, ascending to a height of nearly forty feet. The structure is broad at the base and tapers towards its summit where it forms a shallow basin about twenty feet in diameter. There are no visible entrances, although the entire edifice is comprehensively overgrown by decades — if not centuries — of neglect.

The clearing offers a spectacular view of the sky in all directions and, consequently, plant life here has flourished beneath Lantyr's warming gaze. Heavy vines, thick mosses, and leafy ferns cover the stonework; it is only the precise geometry of the underlying architecture that reveals this to be an unnatural protrusion. There is no immediate context nor clue which suggests the structure's original purpose.

Region Overview.name: Region Overview
Region Overview.text:
Kadísos [Kah-DEE-sos] is a volcanic island located to the south of Ordain along one of Ember's primal arteries which extend towards the Lowland Kingdoms.

The cloudy island of Kadisos is a landmass that not many know much about, even to those that frequent its shores and sole settlement. It is as shrouded in mystery as it is fog, with much of its past having been lost to the march of time and collapse of civilizations. For those that visit it, Kadisos is a modestly sized tropical island in the midst of temperamental seas and surrounded by jagged rocks and reefs the hunger for the hulls of passing ships. It has little to offer the average soul, and little more to the brave and daring that seek to explore its heart.

Terrain and Biomes

Once a huge volcano dominated the center of the island, but it exploded ages ago. In its place is a large, bubbling caldera lake which exudes warmth and the stink of sulfur at all hours. This great central lake is the source of the island's perpetual fog, as well, as cooler winds drawn across the steaming caldera quickly create huge banks of fog. The great gray clouds hang low over the island, gutting themselves on the island's few remaining mountains, their whispy tatters drifting out to sea to menace ships that come too near.

While jungles dominate the center of the landmass, both sandy and rocky beaches can be found nesteled between tall, rocky bluffs, jagged rocky shorelines, and tidepools teeming with life big and small. To the north, the island is dominated by rough hills and rugged, mountainous terrain rising high above the sea.

Flora and Fauna

As a result of the great volcano's destruction, much of Kadisos is covered in heavy tropical rainforest nourished by rich volcanic soil, which makes for dense and fast growing foliage. The plant life on Kadisos hardy and thick, but due to the extensive damage the island has suffered in its past, it wants for diversity. Most of the plants are variations of palms, ferns, woody grasses and the like, but become more varied as they get deeper into the jungles where old Ashka and Aedir magic still lingers.

Given the remote and often ignored nature of Kadisos, many of these plants remain entirely unknown to the academic world, and are waiting to be discovered, studied, and written about. Unfortunately Kadisos makes for a particularly deadly expedition. The island teems with all manner of dangerous creatures that visitors would be wise to avoid.

Along the coasts are the Red-Breasted Gore Birds, which swarm corpses on the edges of the forest and along the shores, picking at old flesh to access the blood and innards beyond, Crag Raptors, magically infused flying lizards with huge claws and the ability to blend into their surroundings while perched on the bluffs, Kadhana Lizards, huge, clawed, cliff-climbing lizards with large frills and a taste for Crag Raptor eggs, fish, and anything too slow to escape its jaws, and Tidal Snails, massive scavenger mollusks with mouths filled with razor sharp teeth which they use to burrow into beached corpses.

In the jungles, travelers must contend with Stripe-Tailed Mud Snakes which can sit in wait for days, nestled under dead leaves or in mud puddles waiting for a creature to fill with their deadly venom, Geyser Frogs who sit on the banks of the boiling lake spitting jets of steam at prey, and Slinkers, huge centipedes with lemprey mouths which scuttle through the brush looking for warm bodies to burrow into.

If this weren't bad enough, even the rocks and waters teem with danger, including the Gravestone Goats known for creating landslides to kill predators, and turning to stone before butting would-be attackers off of cliffs, while the waters off of Kadisos are home to Mirror Sharks whose shiny scales make them almost impossible to distinguish from the natural glitter of sunlight on the ocean surface.

Cultures and Settlements

Kadisos is home to only one major settlement, though calling it "major" is rather generous. The port town of Graven's Rest is a small dockyard built into a sea cave and crammed with all manner of additional structures, many of them built on old the docks themselves. It is a rough frontier town largely supported by the steady flow of ships harboring from storms as they make their way to and from the lowland coasts or the ordain port.

Graven's Rest is small, and its main population is sailors on leave, making for repairs, or waiting out storms. Beyond this the town has a handful of locals that fish, hunt, forage, and make a tidy business serving the incoming ships. A minor trade office of House Bastilla is about the only notable part of the town to the outside world, and even so it's a minor office of minimal import.

The folks of Graven's Rest are hardy, no-nonsense, and have learned to avoid the greater dangers of the island. In the sea cave where their town is built they are safe from most every problem there is except for the odd mirror shark attracted by fish guts being dumped overboard.

Darkstone Ruins

Scattered across the island of Kadísos, but most concentrated around the northern shore of @UUID[.5jydYxd6imXEAjqT]{The Cauldron} are unusual ruins sculpted of crystallized volcanic rock. These remnants are found throughout the island but they are most prevalent and impressive within the waters of the lagoon itself where dark pillars of obsidian rise out of the sea bed forming dwellings, thoroughfares, and gathering places for a lost people who dwelled on Kadísos in ages past. These undersea ruins form a skeleton and foundation upon which a vibrant coral reef thrives, striking a beautiful contrast between the dark stone and the myriad coral. There is a mysterious intentionality in how the ruins are not lost to nature but rather augmented and decorated by it - perhaps becoming the foundation for the lagoon's reef was what their original architects had intended.

The origin and nature of these ruins are a source of fascination for historians and archaeologists who are drawn to Kadísos to study them. The scholars who study these ruins believe that they predate the Aedir Empire and were most likely created during the Age of Beasts. The ruins were built by an ancient culture of scale-folk known as the Ashka who constructed their civilization around an expansive temple complex dedicated to the goddess Soleil.

The ruins of note on the island are:

  • @UUID[.sJTK66EK2TiEQPPD]

  • @UUID[.w1xbZAhwjCwHUsjd]

  • @UUID[.Pk1UfvqZeFrAv4Bu]

  • @UUID[.Gsuf0M1B7acZ5DZQ]

Additional Points of Interest

There is much to see and find on Kadisos, though most of it is not present in the minds of those who visit. In truth, the ancient island holds all manner of secrets and curiosities for those brave enough to go searching.

Ruins: The jungles of Kadisos are littered with old ruins from the ancient Aedir empire and the Ashka people before it. Though much of it has crumbled away to nothingness by now, there are still small remnants of the thriving societies that once called this island home. Brave and keen-eyed adventurers who know their history are in for a treat if they survive long enough to find one of these sites.

The Boiling Lake: At the center of Kadisos is the great caldera filled with nearly boiling water heated by vents of lava from below the surface. This great lake has many names, most of them coined by visitors and sailors spying it from afar, such as the clouded eye, the gray caldera, the cloud-mother, and so forth. Locals simply refer to it as the lake or caldera, and it's actively avoided as most don't like being boiled alive.

The Great Storm Shrine: Once an elaborate temple to the god Katu, the storm shrine sits atop a mountain cliff that has half eroded into the sea. What remains of the temple is just a fraction of the larger structure, and still stands as an active worship site for Katu, the god of storms.

A Sunken City: Though not many know of it, and even fewer can hope to find it, there is a great sunken city beneath the superheated waters of the caldera. This city used to belong to the ancient Ashka people, and fell wholly beneath the waves millennia ago. Anyone clever enough to find a way inside might discover all manner of ancient secrets and forgotten magic.

Resources and Materials

It is largely believed that Kadisos has no real value or resources worth having, and to an extent this isn't incorrect. The effort required to exploit Kadisos is far higher than most companies and investors would be willing to undertake. From the danger to the remoteness of the island, most write the place off as being a waystation and little else.

But in reality there is quite a lot waiting to be discovered. There are all manner of strange plants that would make good medicines or poisons, wildlife which might make exotic pets or expensive delicacies. There is good stone waiting to be quarried, and rich earth which would grow most anything put into it.

More than this, there are old ruins of imperial and Ashka nature which might hold rare insights into magic, or yield resources whose production has been lost to time and collapse.

Historical Notes

While much of Kadisos' history has been lost to time, a few key events and connections include:

  • Ashka Homeland: Kadisos was the original homeland of the Ashka people, who now call much of the Lowland regions their home. The Ashka alive today are but a shadow of the magical society that once inhabited the island, and many of them have no interest in returning home, as the trek alone would be more trouble that it would be worth.
  • The Grave of Gods: Before the rise of the empire the shard goddess Scoris brought the Ashka people to this island and helped them build a home. It was on this island that the dreadful Bale sowed chaos by releasing demons into the populace. As a result the two gods warred, and slew each other over Kadisos. It is said that Scoris' remains lay under the caldera to this day.
  • Imperial Outpost: Before the shattering brought the empire of the Aedir low, Kadisos was home to a large garrison, and posting to it was considered desirable for its nearness to the great tower. However, when the the vampire collapsed, the island became subject to unchecked cruelty, the scars of which persist to this day.
  • Haunted Jungles: It might seem odd to consider a jungle haunted, and in truth that's probably not the most accurate statement, but the locals are quick to warn newcomers not to enter the jungles when the fog is heaviest, because something terrible stalks the mists.

Tidal Pools.name: Tidal Pools
Tidal Pools.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Alpha One Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

The tidal pools on the southern side of Kadisos offer a unique and treacherous landscape. As the tides roll in and out, these rocky beaches are constantly replenished with water, creating a dynamic ecosystem filled with life and perils.

Environment

The terrain of the tidal pools is characterized by large rocky outcrops scattered across the beaches the flood pools, creating natural barriers and hiding spots for both predators and prey. The rocks are often covered in seaweed, making them slippery and hazardous to traverse.

As the tide rolls in, hot sea water from @UUID[.5jydYxd6imXEAjqT]{The Cauldron} meets cooler water from the @UUID[.31S5xuKEKCV3nhFH]{Reaver Ocean}, creating huge plumes of steam and mist which shroud the island daily.

Ecology

Along the sandy areas of the beach, hardy plants such as beach grasses and dune shrubs can be found dug in and holding fast against the constant flow of sea water. These resilient plants have long roots that anchor them firmly in place.

In the tide pools themselves there are huge kelp beds, slime slicked rocks, bundles of collected debris and fishing nets, and all manner of sea life growing through them.

This biome teems with life both great and small, from starfish and crustaceans huddled between rocks to huge, invasive tidal snails, massive scavenging crustaceans, and lurking kadhana lizards looking for an easy meal.

Lore

The true terror of the tidal pools lies in the presence of Krasarioc, a lumbering behemoth that roams the area in search of food. Less an apex predator, and more a force of nature, few upon Ember's surface can confront it without meeting a grim fate. The remains of Krasarioc's kills, including the crushed shells from its prey, attract other opportunistic hunters and scavengers, while sea life teems in the deep depressions of its footsteps.
Tidal Pools.soverview: A teeming biome filled all manner of life both terrestrial and aquatic. This land is treacherous thanks to the ebb and flow of the tides, and unwary spirits may find themselves washed away if not careful.
Tidal Pools.sexposition: The The salty scent of the sea hangs heavy in the air, intermingling with the pungent aroma of seaweed and decomposing life. The terrain here is a captivating blend of chaos and beauty. Large rocky outcrops rise from the sandy shores, creating natural barriers that break the flow of water and crash of waves, forming the pockets of water that teem with life, each a miniature ecosystems nestled within a watery landscape.

The Teeth.name: The Teeth
The Teeth.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Alpha One Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

The Teeth of Kadisos is a treacherous and desolate region, characterized by its sharp, unforgiving cliffs and jagged rock formations. Located in the northwestern part of the island, this area is littered with the wreckage of unfortunate ships that have fallen victim to the powerful winds that constantly sweep along its length.

Environment

These broken remnants serve as a haunting reminder of the dangers that await those who venture too close to this cursed place. The beaches are muddy and inhospitable, offering no respite or shelter to survivors. Even those who manage to reach the safety of the rocky shores are not safe from danger, as the remote nature of this region presents an additional challenge for anyone attempting to escape.

Ecology

The treacherous cliffs and jagged rock formations offer little purchase for vegetation to take root, and is largely a gray, desolate wasteland of jagged stone. However, there are a few resilient plant species that have managed to adapt to this harsh terrain such as mosses and lichens which cling to the crevices of the rocks, their pale green hues contrasting against the rugged landscape. These hardy organisms are able to survive in the salt-laden air and withstand the strong winds that constantly buffet the area. Beyond this, some small shrubs and grasses can be found scattered sparingly along the coastline.

The Teeth make it difficult for most creatures to survive, with the treacherous rocks and limited presence of plant life further restricting the availability of resources for animals. As a result, the fauna in the Teeth biome is sparse and specialized, with mostly small lizards and rodents living between rocks and preying on each other and insects.

The only large predators of note are the crag raptor and kadhana lizard. These agile and stealthy predators make their nests among the cliffs, taking advantage of their superior mobility to hunt each other and their nests.

In addition to these predators, there is another macabre presence in the Teeth biome known as gore bird murders. These scavenging birds feast on carcasses littered along the beaches from shipwrecks, taking advantage of any unfortunate souls who meet their demise in this treacherous place.

Lore

Remnants of the great cataclysm that destroyed the ancient people of Kadisos the first time, the teeth are magically hardened shards of stone forced out of the earth. Though they are not themselves malevolent, the winds, tides, and teeth seemingly work together to drag ships into the stony maw. No story of sailing around Kadisos is complete without a tale of a close call or brush with the teeth and certain death they promise.
The Teeth.soverview: The "Teeth of Kadisos" are a bleak and foreboding place, feared by sailors and considered haunted by many, its name is earned through the ships it has eaten and the deaths of hundreds along with them. Its legend spread by those few that survived them in one way or another.
The Teeth.sexposition:
The landscape before you transforms into an unforgiving and desolate region of muddy beaches and unforgiving rocks. Jagged spires of stone jut out from the earth like sharp fangs, their imposing presence casting a somber shadow over the land.

Amongst the rocks lie the remnants of ill-fated ships, their shattered hulls serving as grim reminders of the perils that await those who venture too close and are caught by the hungry winds along this coast. The beaches are muddy and treacherous, offering no refuge to survivors, while the rocky shores provide only temporary respite from danger.

The Cauldron.name: The Cauldron
The Cauldron.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Alpha One Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

Nestled in the heart of Kadisos, the Cauldron Lake is a unique and treacherous biome that captivates and challenges adventurers with its ever-changing landscape.

Environment

The terrain of the Cauldron Lake is characterized by its volatile nature. The shores of the lake are composed of fine volcanic sand beaches that stretch out towards the churning waters. These beaches are hot to the touch day and night. The heat of the lake and surrounding shores mixed with the offshore sea air creates a near constant haze that hangs over the area which often turns into heavy gray fog that stinks of the sea.

Traversing through Cauldron Lake requires caution and adaptability due to its ever-changing conditions and extreme temperatures. Only those brave or foolish enough venture here in search of its rumored hidden city beneath its surface.

Ecology

Along the coast of the lake the flora is limited due to the intense heat and high salt content present in the volcanic sand. Only a few hardy grass species have managed to adapt and survive in this extreme environment, with the vast majority of plants stopping at the tree line.

The fauna of the Cauldron Lake is an enigmatic and bizarre assortment of creatures that have adapted to survive in the extreme conditions of the superheated water. The unique environment has given rise to species that are unlike anything found in other biomes on Kadisos.

Beneath the surface of the lake are strange variations of common sea plants, specially adapted to survive in the extreme heat. These strange plants are coiled around the shattered remains of the ancient people that once called this island home.

It is worth noting that more typical jungle life tends to avoid the beaches due to the intense heat and shifting terrain caused by geothermal activity. The strange and resilient fauna of the Cauldron Lake serves as a testament to the adaptability of life in even the most hostile environments.

Lore

Though one might mistake the natural pattern of the cauldron for the breathing of Ember itself, the cycle of superheating and cooling it sees is actually cause by an ancient structure deep within the lake. An out of control magical reactor leaks energy into the water, causing it to heat up in predictable cycles.

Legend holds that the great city of Rejarh can be found down there, the last great settlement of an ancient people whom the Ashka are descended from.
The Cauldron.soverview: This boiling lagoon, formed by a deep caldera at its center, is surrounded by unpleasantly hot seawater during the day, and and as the sun sets, begins to turn into a superheated lake capable of boiling most beings alive within seconds.
The Cauldron.sexposition:
Approaching the Cauldron Lake, you can feel the temperature rising with each step. The ground beneath your feet grows warmer, and a shimmering haze hangs in the air. The sandy shores stretch out before you, their fine volcanic particles radiating an intense heat that feels like standing in a firepit with the fuel removed. Steam rises in billowing plumes, mingling with the salty sea air and obscuring your view beyond a few feet.

Though the lake appears placid, there is a sense of foreboding here, a wrongness you cannot place your finger on. Looking along the shores you see minimal plant life, and almost no wildlife save for the odd creature here and there, adapted to survive in the superheated waters flowing from the heart of this caldera lake.

Clouded Jungle.name: Clouded Jungle
Clouded Jungle.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Alpha One Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

The lush, thick and verdant jungle of Kadisos is the largest biome on the island, and teems with life.

Environment

Travel through the jungle is slow and perilous as there are no paths or roads to follow, requiring expeditions to hack their way through the undergrowth to make any sort of progress. Here and there one can find crumbling ruins and markers of an ancient people that once called this island home. Even these ruins are treacherous, threatening to topple or collapse if not treated with care.

Flora

The jungles of Kadisos are diverse, and choked with plants. Large tropical foxglove trees, and palms blot out the sun as exotic plants and thick undergrowth make all but the most well trod paths a pain to travel. Scattered amongst the dense foliage are a number of ancient volcanic stone ruins, encrusted with moss, leaves or fungi, they seem small and broken against the ceaseless growth of nature. Numerous jungle plants grow in this biome that are hazardous, either through their toxic nature, or by their ability to strike the unwary without warning.

Many powerful creatures and monsters thrive in the humidity and heat of the jungle basin, travelling through its depths and making prey of anything in their path. Given the extreme density of ground cover, threats of ambush are high. To make matters worse, many of the island's natural predators and creatures are particularly adept at stalking through the fog that frequently settles over the island.

Lore

The locals at Graven's Rest openly recommend against going too deep into the jungles as that's where the greatest dangers reside. This is especially true when the fog rolls in and makes it impossible to travel with purpose. During this time a terrible monster, the "Mist Stalker" some call it, is said to hunt anyone who doesn't belong. Rational thinking would lead one to believe that anyone who vanishes into the jungles likely just got lost and died of exposure or wildlife, but this is an island steeped in old magic… so perhaps it's not entirely far fetched.

For all the danger and difficulty it presents, the jungles are also a great source of useful materials for anyone with the skills to extract them. There are numerous types of wood, plant material and vines which can be used for construction, as well as edible plants, medicinal herbs to sustain oneself with, not to mention countless wild animals to make use of.

Many of the creatures in this biome and on Kadisos as a whole are not found elsewhere, making knowledge of them rather uncommon. Given how generally unexplored the region is, even seasoned botanists and naturalists are likely to discover plants they have never seen before.
Clouded Jungle.soverview: The lush, thick and verdant jungle of Kadisos is the largest biome on the island, and teems with life. Travel through it is anything but safe, and only the prepared and experienced should attempt it.
Clouded Jungle.sexposition: The jungle is thick with emerald foliage and the air hums with the din of insects. Signs of life are everywhere. The ground is alive with the crawling throng of insects and small shapes dart through the tangled quilt of trees. Every now and then you glimpse something larger disturbing the foliage or stalking through the long shadows cast by the forest canopy.

Volcanic Bluffs.name: Volcanic Bluffs
Volcanic Bluffs.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Alpha One Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

The windswept rocky bluffs of Kadisos serve as a transitional zone, connecting the lush jungles to the towering mountains or the vast oceans that surround the island. These bluffs can be found along the entire perimeter of the island, with the exception of the southern edge where they give way to the enchanting Tidal Pools.

Environment

The bluffs are characterized by their rugged terrain and exposed rock formations. The strong ocean winds constantly batter against these cliffs, shaping them into majestic and imposing structures. It is a sight to behold as waves crash against the rocks, creating a mesmerizing display of spray and foam.

Ecology

Tall grasses, bushes and rocky outcrops are common in this biome, with large areas of open space dominated by unchecked growth. While hardier trees and palms can also be found scattered across the areas, they think out quickly as one leaves the edge of the jungle.

The flora of the bluffs is hardy and resilient, adapted to withstand the strong winds and rocky terrain. Tall grasses sway in the breeze, providing cover for small animals and insects. Hardy bushes cling to the cliffsides, their roots anchored deep into crevices in the rocks. Some of these bushes bear small, brightly colored berries that serve as a food source for birds and other creatures but not fit for people.

The most common predators in this biome are the stealthy crag raptors and agile kadhana lizards, both of whom use the bluffs for nesting and as their hunting grounds. Both rely on their superior mobility to reach prey that think they are safe. Their keen eyesight and ability to blend into the terrain let them watch for prey, while the climbing kadhana make easy meals of nests situated in sheer cliffs overlooking the sea.

Lore

Not much is known about the history of the bluffs, though much of their volcanic activity has ceased, they are named for the obvious hallmarks of that activity which formed them. Overall, the bluffs offer a unique ecosystem where both predator and prey coexist in a delicate balance between rock and sky, ocean and jungle.
Volcanic Bluffs.soverview: The rocky bluffs provide a stunning view of the ocean below and are home to a large variety of creatures both big and small, as it provides a relatively safe environment with ample cover. Travelers be warned: this makes it a rich hunting ground for predators of all kinds, and they are not particular about their prey.
Volcanic Bluffs.sexposition: Broad, flat plains and fields of rocky land spread out before you, dotted by hardy plants and dark stones jutting from the earth. The salt of the sea is thick in the air here, and the distant roar of crashing waves is like a far-off whisper in a language you don't speak.

Jade Mountains.name: Jade Mountains
Jade Mountains.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Alpha One Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

Rough mountains rise out of the land of Kadisos like a crown, casting long shadows over the lower regions, and capturing clouds so that their ran can pour down into the central bay of the island.

Environment

The sharp, rugged features make the mountains extremely challenging to navigate, and even traversing the rocky foothills is a daunting task for seasoned travelers. With no established paths or trails to guide the way, most opt to follow natural pathways created by the elements over time. These pathways offer some semblance of safety in an otherwise hazardous environment, so long as the weather doesn't turn them against you.

Ecology

Vegetation struggles to take root among the unforgiving slopes and jagged cliffs. Occasionally, small patches of stunted shrubs and hardy alpine flowers can be found in sheltered areas or where moisture collects. In the few areas where soil can accumulate, some resilient plant species manage to survive. Low-lying mosses and lichens cling to the crevices in the rocks, adding a touch of green amidst the barrenness.

The mountains appear barren at first glance, nothing but rocks and a few sparse plants but no shortage of small critters can also be found in this biome. The only truly large and notable creature to call this biome home is the Gravestone Goat, a large, mountain goat capable of navigating the difficulty terrain with ease, and also known for its ability to blend into its surroundings, appearing identical to stone. It is notorious for ambushing unwary travelers.

Lore

Driven up from the waters ages ago, the jade mountains were once a very different sight, but the destruction of the ancient Seydiri people by way of a massive magical explosion left the landscape of Kadisos changed forever. No living mortal remembers the old, softer, rolling mountains and hills of Kadisos, only the jagged, shattered stone that sit in their place now.
Jade Mountains.soverview: The Jade Mountains, located along the northern edges of Kadisos, are a formidable and treacherous terrain. Towering peaks of stone battered by relentless winds and rains dominate the landscape and pour water into the lowlands.
Jade Mountains.sexposition:
Towering peaks of black stone, weathered by time and battered by relentless winds and rains, dominate the landscape. The air grows colder and thinner as you ascend, urging you to brace yourself for the challenges that lie ahead.

Life is sparse, and little grows on the rough, dark stone here. What little vegetation manages to take root there is hardy though, refusing to be beaten by the unforgiving slopes. These little places of stunted shrubs and hardy flowers manage to create tiny pockets of beauty in an otherwise unwelcoming landscape.

Reaver Ocean.name: Reaver Ocean
Reaver Ocean.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Alpha One Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

The Reaver Ocean, surrounding Kadisos entirely, is a vast expanse of water that connects the island with numerous nearby regions.

Environment

The Reaver Ocean is known for its tumultuous nature, especially around Kadisos, with frequent natural and unnatural storms making navigation around the island treacherous at best, and deadly at worst. To seek refuge from these dangers, many vessels anchor in the relative safety of Graven's Rest sea cave. Here, they can find repairs offered by locals and gather necessary supplies for their journeys.

While there are shallow areas around the island, with sharp rocks meeting the water's edge, there are also rocky and sandy beaches scattered along the coast. However, as one ventures further from shore, the depth of the water plunges suddenly into an abyssal ocean plateau.

Ecology

The Reaver Ocean is a vast and diverse ecosystem, teeming with unique and resilient marine flora. Seaweed forests sway with the ebb and flow of the currents, providing shelter and food for a variety of sea creatures, and colorful coral reefs dot the ocean floor, creating vibrant undersea landscapes teeming with life.

Floating plants known as sea drifters can also be found in the Reaver Ocean. These plants have adapted to life on the open water, utilizing air-filled bladders to remain buoyant as they drift along with the ocean currents, often serving as perches for migratory birds or cover for lurking sea life.

The Reaver Ocean supports a rich diversity of marine life, ranging from small creatures to magnificent sea giants. Schools of shimmering fish dart through the water, their scales reflecting sunlight in a dazzling display, chased by nearly invisible slips of mercury-skinned sharks.

Lore

In addition to these familiar creatures, there are also mysterious and elusive beings that dwell in the depths of the Reaver Ocean. Deep-sea bioluminescent organisms light up the darkness with their ethereal glow, and much worse which no mortal has ever seen before.

Overall, the Reaver Ocean is a realm of wonder and danger where a diverse array of plants and animals coexist beneath its turbulent surface.
Reaver Ocean.soverview: From the Arctus Plateau and Ordain to the Lowlands and even the more distant realms, the Reaver Ocean serves as a vital link between lands, and a dangerous hazard to those that dare set sail on it.
Reaver Ocean.sexposition:
The Reaver Ocean stretches as far as the eye can see, its vast expanse of deep blue waters merging with the horizon in a seamless blend of sea and sky. The waves dance with an untamed energy, rising and falling in a mesmerizing rhythm that seems to echo the beating heart of Ember itself.

As you gaze out over the water, you can't help but feel a sense of both awe and trepidation for you know that beneath the beautiful, glimmering surface of the ocean lies a world of untold depths and hidden dangers.

Barrows.name: Barrows
Barrows.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of current Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located along the northwestern coast of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Bluffs Terrain}.

  • This biome is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaBarrow]{Vista: Barrows}.

Environment

The Barrows are a labyrinthine expanse of ancient burial mounds and forgotten ruins, perpetually shrouded in eerie fog. This realm of desolation stands as a testament to the haunting presence of the past, where the imprints of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Z8Nm4rnjqG3BJHSd]{Varún} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} Giants linger in stone and shadow.

The mist-cloaked landscape offers little visibility, masking the sinister secrets that lie beneath its surface. The remnants of the once-great civilization of the Shent play host to cryptic riddles and arcane mysteries that challenge even the most intrepid explorers. On top of these ancient ruins are more recent but still old and abandoned structures built by the Varún. A foreboding atmosphere envelops the area, drawing in those who seek to unravel its dark legacy or restore sanctity to its hallowed grounds.

Ecology

Other than a blanket of withered grasses and shrubbery, plant life in the Barrows is incredibly sparse, and is identified by its ashen color. Areas closest to the biome’s invisible necromantic fields occasionally host leafless, nearly petrified trees and decayed foliage, which have grown putrid with supernatural taint.

The living are few and far between. Undead creatures, fueled by the necromantic magics coursing unseen beneath the surface, roam the shadowy landscape with unsettling resolve. They are spurned ever onward by strange and sinister forces that lurk beneath the ruins.

Lore

The Barrows are steeped in history, with many scattered ruins and tombs of the ancient Shent dotting the landscape. After @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, the Varún visited the area and continued to bury their dead in mounds and cairns until the dead began to rise and the Mourning War erupted across the Arctus Plateau. Although this was never discovered during the war, its ultimate architect was a terrifying @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horror} known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas}, a harbinger of darkness and death that still sleeps in a hidden cavern in the northern Barrows.

Though many have tried to revive the legacy locked within the tombs, only cautionary tales and echoes of the past have emerged from the sepulchral shadows. The Barrows persist as a somber battlefield between those who fear its secrets and those who seek to understand them, with their unyielding presence standing as both a warning and an enticement to daring souls.
Barrows.soverview: This rolling, rocky wilderness at the northwestern edge of the Arctus Plateau is a desolate and haunting place, marked only by the giant tumuli of the ancient Varùn. Few willingly travel to this place, and the rugged terrain makes it all the more inhospitable to those who do.
Barrows.sexposition: This sullen land of rolling hinterlands and stark mountain peaks lies shrouded in thick mist; dark silhouettes of giant tumuli loom over its ashen grasslands. An eerie, unbroken silence underscores the strange absence of wildlife. Where there should be birdsong, there is only the skitter of dead leaves.

Bloodwoods.name: Bloodwoods
Bloodwoods.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of current Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the northeastern reach of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Normal Terrain}.

  • This biome can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberBloodwoods0]{Bloodwoods} area map.

Environment

The Bloodwoods possesses a faint, otherworldly energy that causes the forest to move physically in chaotic patterns; it is an ever-changing landscape that demands vigilance and adaptability from its inhabitants. The Black Aspens, all part of one living organism, rule the biome, as towering Marble Oaks, resembling stone statues, break up the dense aspen growth and serve as landmarks. The forest floor is a patchwork of crimson grass and russet colored variants of common plants, thriving in the dark earth enriched by magical residue. Only one settlement, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.i8a6VBrxUsZ2PaHo]{Talei}, clings to its southern edge, while failed expeditions, lost caravans, and overgrown camps serve as a grim testament to the land's hostility toward intruders.

Ecology

Within the Bloodwoods, common creatures are transformed by primordial magic into aggressive, formidable beasts. @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Birds}, Grass Runners, and more call this place home, and all are warped by it. Its most prominent native species, @UUID[Actor.pn9LliLM3cfP1GFG]{Amerasps} — black-and-gold, wasp-like creatures — burrow into Black Aspens and construct nests around amber deposits. In time, these colonies harden into @UUID[Actor.r9t5wVOmfEtIt10K]{Leshy} cocoons, from which humanoid sap creatures emerge. The Leshy, bound to one another in shared consciousness, embody the forest’s will and are met with caution, even when they do not show open hostility.

Lore

During @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering }and the subsequent @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, this area was the scene of a final confrontation between the Shent Shard God Kyra and an Abyssal Horror of Sha-Xotha. Their fierce battle decimated the region, rending a deep fissure into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} below. For many years, Abyssal energy fluctuated across the region until the Casia Nimaella attempted to mend the damage by planting a seed from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} in the wound. Over time, the Bloodwoods grew and covered the scar. Yet Abyssal wounds rarely heal properly, and the forest now festers with chaos, destruction, and ancient magic left untamed.
Bloodwoods.soverview: Named for the striking red foliage of its Black Aspens and Marble Oaks, the Bloodwoods is a rugged area of the northernmost Arctus Plateau that has thus far resisted all attempts to tame it. The forest’s presence extends beyond the physical, with the forest itself seeming to pulse with otherworldly magic that drives people mad. As stories warn, the Bloodwoods do not favor the unready and pose a challenge to all who venture into it.
Bloodwoods.sexposition: An intimidating sea of tangled crimson forest stretches before you. Black aspens dominate the horizon, their red leaves shivering under the faintest breeze, while massive white oaks stand sentinel over the canopy like stone towers. A faint energy pulses through the air here, irritating the skin and leaving a soft ringing in your ears.

Splinter Canyons.name: Splinter Canyons
Splinter Canyons.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located within a long canyon corridor that runs the length of the central region of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Difficult Terrain}.

  • This biome is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaCanyon]{Vista: Splinter Canyons}.

  • This biome can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberCanyonsBiom]{Splinter Canyons} area map.

The Splinter Canyons plunge from the Arctus Plateau in a near-vertical drop, traversable only via narrow switchbacks and occasional shelves and plateaus. Their depths are far enough from the surface of the Golden Flats to have their own unique mix of flora and fauna, which are either adapted to survival on the canyon walls or near the river on the canyon floor.

Environment

The Splinter Canyons combine three types of terrain: sheer rocky walls, the river that snakes through them, and the narrow strips of land between water and stone (the route most travelers follow once inside). The canyon walls conceal occasional caves that hold both hidden dangers and valuable resources; several of these caves have been transformed into mining operations by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}, who have invested heavily to clear natural predators and protect the entrances from flooding.

Ecology

The Splinter Canyons are prone to rockfalls, and water frequently upwells from subterranean springs, triggering sudden flash floods. As a result, the flora and fauna of the Splinter Canyons are well adapted to clinging to, burrowing through, or scaling the steep walls. The ubiquitous @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Bird} also plunges into the canyons in search of easy prey.
