One example of such adapted life is the Vale Vine, a deeply rooted, flowering plant that grows vertically, forming a thick netting along the rock face; in places it is sturdy enough to aid ascent or descent, though its fronds often conceal caverns and lurking predators. The @UUID[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl]{Gumtoad} uses powerful hind legs, sticky forelimbs, and a prehensile tongue to leap great distances and adhere to canyon walls during flooding. Finally, the Stone Lilly is a broad, floating plant that resembles a simple stone, but is actually a carnivorous plant that latches onto prey and sinks to the river floor. When dead, however, Stone Lillies form safe floating platforms.

Lore

While there are some communities in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} that use canyons and tunnels as places to live, like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel}, the Splinter Canyons are widely considered off-limits, as they were created during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} and are perceived as somewhat unnatural by Arcturians. The rising waters also became much more sporadic following the major earthquake that rocked the region twenty years ago. Some superstitious travelers and locals believe that their depths hold secret horrors, and point to difficulties at some of the mining concerns operated by House Cevher in shallower parts of the Canyons. In truth, the main threats to anyone who passes through are simply those of the natural environment: rockfalls, flash floods, steep paths, and predators used to using all three to their advantage.
Splinter Canyons.soverview: The Splinter Canyons, formed by the shaking of the land during the time of the Shattering, snake through the Arctus Plateau in the center of the Golden Flats. They form a steep, continuous gouge of stony walls, and though a small river flows through them from the Reaver Ocean, the canyons are too narrow to support an entire community without hollowing out its cliff face — and with earthquakes routinely wracking the Flats, none are too keen to stake their lot below a mountain of rock. Most avoid travel through the region unless they are especially adventurous, foolhardy, or have a specific purpose in mind.
Splinter Canyons.sexposition:
Immense cliffs of deep brown and tan rock rise in near-vertical walls, broken only by narrow shelves of land and hidden crags that shadow the ground beneath them. The rock is rough and jagged, as if the Golden Flats had been torn open by mighty hands, leaving nothing but sky above and canyon floor below.

Still, there is life here. Water appears from deep underground in the center of the canyon floor, lapping at the orange, red, and yellow grasses that spread from its banks up the canyon walls, rooting in rocky cracks and ledges in thin, wispy bands. Ahead, the canyon twists and turns with the water, making it near-impossible to know what might be around — or above — the next bend.

Redrak Fields.name: Redrak Fields
Redrak Fields.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Early Access gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the northcentral region of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Normal Terrain}.

  • This biome can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberRedrakField]{Redrak Fields} area map.

The region's land is naturally rich, and is further enhanced by the efforts of the local agrimages living in the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.UkNBiAA4l5PP891p]{Redrak}. These casters combine the soil and silt drawn out of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.iWZG0gUGUL76Dd3r]{Lake Orial} with the waste of livestock, and use magical processes to transform it into incredible topsoil capable of growing anything quickly.

The soil is sold back to the farmers of the region, who then use it to produce massive amounts of food that keeps the region — and Ordain — fed. This cycle has created a delicate balance of power between the Lake Orial Dredgers, the Redrak agrimages, and the farmers of Redrak Fields, who rely on and profit from their continued mutual cooperation.

Environment

Stretching from the coast of the @UUID[JournalEntry.UXWZgBVAzcNudIEa.JournalEntryPage.31S5xuKEKCV3nhFH]{Reaver Ocean} to the chaotic curves of the Tarca River and the shores of Lake Orial, Redrak Fields is a gently rolling landscape awash in broad seas of grain and grass that sway rhythmically with the wind. Travel across this land is easy, and what dangers exist are few and far between.

Ecology

This bountiful terrain is adorned with ubiquitous red grass, its hue ascribed to the rich soil derived from the nearby Lake Orial, and nourished by the Tarcas River running along the northern @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.TNPxd8ZlYQvJEXu6]{Bloodwoods}. Apart from this omnipresent grass, Redrak Fields is devoid of any significant tree population, except for the ones deliberately planted by the local residents.

Redrak Fields is home to various creatures found elsewhere in the Arctus Plateau region, such as Weaver Bugs, whose domed nests dot the grasses, and Tiller Birds, who make a nuisance of themselves on farms. Meanwhile, both wild and domesticated @UUID[Actor.N8NkRFQf752p2pWD]{Grassrunners}, Lodoxeros, and Docktail Lizards can be encountered here. Around Lake Orial, one can also find mighty @UUID[Actor.6HckJyV8TKc37xNT]{Yarnac} imported from distant @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak}.

Lore

Redrak Fields is a region shot through with magic that flows from the massive Lake Orial up north. Unknown to any in the region, this lake is the site of an elemental prison holding a fallen sage of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora}, and the magic of that prison seeps into the waters above. The folk of Redrak Fields unwittingly draw up the infused water and soil, and spread it across the land; this has made the region immensely productive in terms of agriculture, but leaves it vulnerable to a growing influence from the trapped earth sage under the lake — and its prison is not as sturdy as it once was.
Redrak Fields.soverview: Redrak Fields is a lively, agrarian heartland that provides cereals and essential food supplies to several regions. Long regarded as a rival to the Golden Flats, it has recently surpassed them as earthquakes continue to disrupt the region.
Redrak Fields.sexposition: Vibrant crops of red vines and gold leaves sway with the wind, each field growing from dark, rich earth, and hemmed in by seas of rich, blood-red grass that stretches over hill and field. The horizon is dotted with signs of agriculture — turning windmills, stoic silos, and the crowns of distant orchards lined up in perfect rows.

Golden Flats.name: Golden Flats
Golden Flats.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the central and northeastern expanse of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Normal Terrain}.

  • This biome is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.vistaGoldenFlats]{Vista: Golden Flats}.

  • This biome can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberGoldenFlats]{ Golden Flats} area map.

While the sprawling landscape of the Golden Flats seems inviting and serene at first glance, it has recently become rife with turmoil. Chaos and upheaval are now constant threats to those who once enjoyed calm, untroubled lives.

Most settlements in the Golden Flats are @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian}, built along established trading routes, with smaller towns and farms scattered across the plains. Many of these settlements were founded centuries ago to exploit valuable resources and fertile watercourses. A few settlements, however, were raised in recent years by @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain's} Trading Houses to serve more private ambitions. A steady trickle of merchant caravans — some from as far as Casla-Brava and Toraga — passes through the region, either traveling toward Ordain or circulating locally to supply the villages.

Environment

Most of the area is safe and quiet, featuring gentle breezes and light rains. However, for nearly two decades, mysterious geological upheavals have increasingly affected several unexpected locations. Residual earthquakes and mild aftershocks from the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.tuopdqO2JSeH1LeU]{Splinter Canyons} have altered the landscape, leading many to whisper that the land is now cursed or burdened by some great weight. The appearance of elemental and arcane energy has become common near places imbued with the forces of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.JUwFAaelI86yiscL]{the Cosmos}, growing larger with each new conjunction of the Elemental Moons.

Ecology

The Golden Flats is known for its rich soil and eponymous golden grasses, which range in color from muddy brown in its furthest reaches to a fiery orange or striking yellow in its centrality. Distinctive plants in the region include Sapgrass, a sweet-tasting yellow grass that can climb any stationary object and is often found trailing down into canyons, and the Waterwell Plant, whose stalks resemble long locks of hair and whose roots can find and hold water even in the driest places.

Animals found throughout the region include the tree-dwelling Docktail Lizard, the carnivorous @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Bird}, the crop-ravaging Tiller Bird, and the hive-dwelling Weaver Bug. Weaver Bugs in particular helped inspire the popular Acturian constructs known as Woven; these ramshackle automatons vary in construction materials, but are generally made of tightly wound materials (from vines to grass to cloth).

The persistent arcane and cataclysmic reshaping of Ember’s crust that occurs throughout the Golden Flats is responsible for the recent reemergence of ancient Arcturian megafauna, such as the six-legged Katherim, the pack-hunting avian Avir, the aberrantly nimble @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Garganthus}, and the ferociously brutish Urkon. These rare (and sometimes unique) @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} behemoths are creatures thought long extinct, and are viewed by the people of the Golden Flats with a healthy mix of reverence and fear.

Lore

The Golden Flats has been historically peaceful for thousands of years and was once claimed and tamed by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir}, who constructed several outposts and settlements on its shores. Since @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, however, it has been settled by the Arcturians, who reveled in a place with few dangers and mild weather. Unfortunately, twenty years ago, a massive earthquake tore through the Arctus Plateau, sundering the land and releasing an array of primeval creatures from the Pathways into the Golden Flats. The emergence of these megafauna specimens has had various effects on the biome; while some of the creatures live in tranquil cohabitation with the people of the Golden Flats, others have proven calamitous and continue to wreak havoc.
Golden Flats.soverview: The Golden Flats is the largest biome on the Arctus Plateau outside Ordain, named for its gilded orange and yellow tall grasses and its thriving overland trade route linking Ordain to the rest of Aterica. It is a historically peaceful region, and its Arcturian settlements are known for rich craftsmanship and inventive ambition.
Golden Flats.sexposition: An endless expanse of golden-hued grassland stretches before you, dotted with ambling crossroads, remote farmsteads, and breathtaking geological phenomena. A sense of peaceful, aged serenity pervades these amber plains, despite the occasional upheavals, both magical and mundane.

Wedgelands.name: Wedgelands
Wedgelands.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located within the northwest region of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Difficult Terrain}.

  • This biome is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaWedgel]{Vista: Wedgelands}.

The towering peaks referred to as the Wedgelands are known for their treacherous landslides, perilous alpine hazards, and brutally unpredictable wildlife. This biome defines the majority of the Arctus Plateau's mountainous terrain, which often plays host to preternatural creatures, awe-inspiring vistas, and timeless myths of the ancient Giants and their kin.

Few settlements manage to endure within the harsh mountain environs of the Wedgelands, but the presence of outlying camps is not altogether unheard of, along with a few well-known key points of interest — like Cevher Estate (owned by the eponymous Trading House) and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh]{Corpin Sanctuary} (famed citadel of the Cindaric Sages). Outside of such remote sanctuaries and precipitous estates, the scattered remains of ancient cities and outposts of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} Giants dominate these desolate lands.

Environment

The Wedgelands are known for a transitional mountain climate, and most of the biome can be identified by its steep hills of brown rhyolite and gray slate covered in amber moss and sporadic waterfalls. The exceedingly rare forests of the Wedgelands are marked by the russet hues of their rugged trees and shrubbery. The environment here is equal measures exalted and severe, and the unforgiving nature of Ember's primordial majesty is constantly on full display.

Ecology

The biome's steep rocky slopes offer less-than-favorable conditions for wildlife habitation aside from an infrequent grove or pasture near a potent water source. An array of wild beasts populate the Wedgelands (like bears, wild cats, goats, and more), along with a scattering of rare and uncommon monstrosities. Hardened creatures like the massively-winged Huntsman Vulture and the six-legged lupine Gurrath are known to prowl the mountainous biome's uncaring wilderness.

Although excessively rare, flora of the Wedgelands is suited to hot summers and mild winters alike; and few varieties of vegetation can survive here. Noteworthy specimens include the restorative Goldroot, the pernicious Gravelthorn, and the resilient Scragwood tree.

In those areas where the Wedgelands border upon fog-shrouded Barrows, undead creatures like those found in the legendary Varùn burial lands can also be encountered.

Lore

Despite the harsh landscape and unforgiving climes of the Wedgelands, these mountainous realms are laden with archaic legends and tales of historical significance — most notably, the myth-laden stories of the ancient Shent and their descendants, which linger among the ruins of their civilizations. Arcturian storytellers are known to spin epic yarns about the mythologies of these time-forgotten mountain people and their role in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.JUwFAaelI86yiscL]{the Cosmos}, and adventurers from every corner of Ember seek the fortune and glory these regional tales promise.

In addition to chronicles of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giants} and their kin, Arcturian folk tales are rich with stories about strange elemental spirits of earth and air that originate from the lowest of Wedgelands valleys and steepest of Wedgelands peaks. These narratives are often the stuff of fantasy, and commonly used by rural Arcturians to explain strange occurrences and keep ornery children in check; but they do occasionally possess some wondrous credence, as the cosmic influences of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora} are never far from hand.

The western Wedgelands are also steeped in the necromantic energy of an immortal @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horror} known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas}, who slumbers within a dark sanctum beneath the neighboring @UUID[.iQhYX8QCmDyBnhHP]{Barrows}. The influence of this ancient evil has permeated adjacent biomes like the Wedgelands and @UUID[.CgqmvuJ1NLfqaO3I]{Rustvar Valleys} to such an extent that the rising threat of undead malevolence draws nearer every day.
Wedgelands.soverview: The Wedgelands are a collection of precipitous ridges that dominate the craggy mountainous landscapes of the Arctus Plateau. Like most of the region, these mountains are steeped in legend and lore, but also play host to an intriguing (if sparse) array of indigenous flora and fauna. Few people call the unforgiving Wedgelands home, but remote locations like mountainside estates and lofty citadels are known to populate various corners of the Plateau.
Wedgelands.sexposition: An expanse of steep gray mountains and craggy ridges blocks the horizon’s edge, draped in thin pale blankets of wind-driven snow. There is an isolation to these colossal peaks, which tower above the Arctus Plateau with an archaic, somewhat primordial splendor. Surely, nothing can thrive here but the hardiest of wildlife and most intrepid of explorers.

Salt Flats.name: Salt Flats
Salt Flats.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Early Access Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the southeastern region of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Difficult Terrain}.

The only permanent residents of the Salt Flats reside on its offshore island, a few seasoned explorers who make their living preparing would-be adventurers for expeditions into the Flats. As such, most encounters in the region are with solo or paired travelers searching for Signaran crystals or unique ecological finds — more often, however, one comes across their bodies, mummified by the salt air and stripped of possessions.

Environment

Only the bravest (or most foolhardy) venture into the Salt Flats, usually for one of two purposes: to prove their mettle against the harsh environment, or to search for crystals with Signaran resonance found amid the stark expanse of white crystalline hills and acidic blue waters.

Ecology

Only a handful of tough, flowering plants have managed to survive the Salt Flats' unforgiving conditions, pushing roots past the mineral crust and deep into the earth. Most have white or silver flowers that make them hard to spot from a distance, their petals etched with crystalline, geometric patterns.

In addition to its stationary plants, the Salt Flats are also home to the Walking Grasses: a remnant of early explorers' attempts at settling the area by planting grass designed to thrive in the Flats. While the grass grew wild and plentiful for a short time, it eventually became dry and brittle; once dead, it became uprooted by the wind and blown into large, tumbleweed-like masses. Driven across the Flats at speed, these rolling thickets can knock out anyone in their path.

Animal life on the Flats has adapted to withstand the abrasive, particulate wind. The Shardmole — a small, armored mammal — survives by burrowing beneath the crust, its plated back shielding it from grit and debris. @UUID[Actor.St4ia61vbEcS3TrC]{Salt Spiders} dwell in the deep tunnels, relocating frequently enough to avoid eradication.

Frog-like aquatic creatures called Swelltoads inflate a primary air sac and cling to the bottom of pools to wait out windstorms. Above, Scourwings ride the violent thermals that rise from the Flats, their narrow, scythe-like wings slicing through the particulate air; their scaled hides resist abrasion, and a clear inner membrane shields their eyes, allowing them to hunt even during storms. They descend only when prey is exposed — Swelltoads forced to surface, or Shardmoles too old or sick to burrow in time.

Lore

This desolate expanse of salt-covered earth, raised from the Reaver Ocean by forces unknown thousands of years ago, is a treacherous region of natural and unnatural dangers. It is home to all manner of hostile life, and is one of the most unwelcoming places on the face of Ember.

Little is known about the place, but the cavernous spaces beneath the surface may hold valuable crystals, and countless lives have been lost venturing into those caverns in search of them.
Salt Flats.soverview: A flatland of dry, sulfurous earth where little grows, stunted by the salinity of the hard-packed soil and the acidity of the regional water table. The Salt Flats are hostile at the best of times; few willingly travel here, and none stay longer than is absolutely necessary.
Salt Flats.sexposition: A vast and desolate flatland — bleached white and veined with spiderweb cracks like ancient porcelain — stretches endlessly before you. Salt and sulfur linger on your tongue with each breath. Sparse pools of impossibly blue water dot the terrain, their surfaces reflecting the sky like polished glass. The silence of this place is broken only by the sudden rustling of tumbleweed-like walking grasses, driven swiftly across the flats by a ceaseless wind, as if fleeing the very earth.

Caryx Savanna.name: Caryx Savanna
Caryx Savanna.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Early Access Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the southwestern region of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Normal Terrain}.

The Caryx Savanna stretches its vast and untamed land south and west, from the coasts of the Reaper Ocean to the lands beyond the bluffs of the Golden Flats. This expanse of unyielding grassland is shaped by the elemental seasons of water and fire — life and death — dictated by the rise and fall of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}, respectively.

Environment

The Elenain River defines the Savanna's northern boundary, highlighting stark contrasts — lush floodplains near the river give way to increasingly dry, harsh stretches that test even the most experienced travelers and resilient inhabitants. Known for its extreme heat and intense rainfall, the area frequently experiences brush fires, which serve as both hazards and signs of change. These flames, seen as Ragen reaches its peak, often spread uncontrollably, forcing wildlife to migrate toward the Elenain River. This migration marks the start of movements across the plateau and sparks the emergence of thousands of vibrant Prisma Beetles from the soil. When the fires threaten to consume the Savanna in an endless blaze, Mayis reaches its zenith, bringing a powerful monsoon season. The rains flood the low plains, creating large mud lakes that nourish migrating animals. With renewed vitality, the land flourishes again — herds grow, hunters thrive, and the Savanna reverts to a chaotic, wild landscape, at least until Ragen waxes again.

Ecology

The Caryx Savanna is dominated by vast fields of resilient, golden grass that sway in unison under the relentless sun. Monumental Boarbark Trees serve as natural landmarks, and in some cases, as hollowed-out shelters. Along the riverbanks, more vibrant vegetation claims the floodplains and thrives unchecked, supported by the life-giving waters of the Elenain.

Life in the Caryx Savanna is a vivid tapestry of adaptation and survival. Grass Runners, Tiller Birds, and the annual migration of colorful insects represent the constant churn of migration and change in the region. Several predators stalk these migratory creatures, the most dangerous of which is the towering Caryxidar.

Lore

The Caryx Savanna has long been a wild area of the Arctus Plateau, home to many predators and ancient creatures from the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}. After @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, a few scattered families of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka} settled on the eastern and southern shores, establishing hidden villages and trying to tame the land around them. They brought with them deep cultural beliefs in the harmony between fire and water. However, despite their efforts, their ritual practices have disrupted the area's natural balance, causing extreme weather phenomena and moon zeniths that bring chaos, destruction, and intense intermittent magic to the region. The violent two-season system eventually led most of these villages to be abandoned, except for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.Iwh7BmLJKhYCiLcV]{Tajar}, a settlement on the Savanna's southern edge, which still clings on despite the dangers.
Caryx Savanna.soverview: The Caryx Savanna is a harsh but vibrant land of contrasts, defined by its two extreme seasons. When Ragen reaches its zenith, great swathes of the savanna are consumed by fire, burning a path for new growth later. When Mayis reaches its zenith, monsoon season overtakes the savanna, flooding the lowlands and coaxing life out of the ashes.
Caryx Savanna.sexposition: Expansive waves of golden grass ripple beneath the scorching sun, creating a mesmerizing sea across this sprawling savanna. Sparse, gnarled trees punctuate the horizon, marking upwells of life and sanctuary in an otherwise hostile land. The scent of burning grass comes and goes with the breeze, as do the sounds of wildlife calling out to each other in warning.

Sarin Strand.name: Sarin Strand
Sarin Strand.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located along the eastern coast of the Arctus Plateau and on Bura Island.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Bluffs Terrain}.

The Sarin Strand is a rough and unpleasant biome, with almost nothing to forage, hard-to-navigate terrain, and ample danger.

Environment

The Strand is broken into two distinct areas: the coastal bluffs, and the inland crags. In both cases, the terrain makes traveling in a straight line difficult, as the rocky land often bars passage, requiring travelers to either go around or undertake a risky climb to go over. Along the coast, these bluffs grow even more dangerous, as the uneven rock masks many sheer drops to the unforgiving seas below.

While there are ample outcrops and caves to camp under or in, these locations are also common gathering places for the more dangerous creatures and residents of the region, and can easily turn a quiet night in camp into a sudden midnight melee, with treacherous rock underfoot working against defenders at every step.

Ecology

The region has little in the way of plant life. There are no trees to speak of, only hardy grasses, shrubs, the odd flower, and knobby roots. The region is so rocky that there is little soil to grow in, leaving it quite desolate most of the time. Only the hardy Widow Thorn grows here naturally, with bright colorful blooms that beg to be picked — but hide needle-like thorns with exceptionally deadly poison, hence the flower's name.

While the crags and cliffs teem with hardy creatures, only one is synonymous with the Strand: the @UUID[Actor.lUtcCZ3fGrCDfIkE]{Orvidrath}. Once mistaken for dragons, these long-bodied, multi-legged creatures navigate the Sarin Strand with little difficulty, resting comfortably at the top of the food chain. Its mottling of dark reds, grays, and blacks allows it to easily blend with the stone; it prefers to nest in coastal caves, to which it drags prey.

Lore

There is only one notable settlement in this region, @UUID[.X1FzWfTYfe7JfD3P]{Seawall}, a fortified position that once served as a mining and supply outpost for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aediri} in older ages, and now is a bustling haven for travelers, pirates, smugglers, traders, and fishers. It is isolated and unwelcoming to strangers who do not have their wits about them.

While there is a highway that runs from Seawall up the coast toward @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}, it is rarely used, and in a terrible state of disrepair. Worse, it is often watched by bandits, and many sections run close to Orvidrath lairs. Both prey readily on travelers foolish enough to take the road without proper protection.
Sarin Strand.soverview: The Sarin Strand is an unforgiving expanse of rocky bluffs and cliffs lining the eastern coast of the Arctus Plateau and comprising the totality of Bura Island. Those who venture here must be wary of hazards concealed within its shadowed crevices and along its precarious cliffsides.
Sarin Strand.sexposition: A desolate coastline of jagged cliffs and rugged crags stretches before you. The salty breeze carries the roar of waves crashing against the outcrops. This harsh and unwelcoming landscape offers few comforts, save for a few scattered shrubs covered in bright, cheerful flowers.

Rustvar Valleys.name: Rustvar Valleys
Rustvar Valleys.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the northeastern region of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Normal Terrain}.

  • This biome is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaRustva]{Vista: Rustvar Valleys}.

  • This biome can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberRustvarMoun]{ Rustvar Valleys} area map.

The curious stretch of history-laden hinterlands known as the Rustvar Valleys offers a remote glimpse into the Arctus Plateau's storied past. Here, modern Arcturians live among the timeswept outskirts of ancient giant ruins and cultivate a frontier life defined by freewheeling ambition and tenacious grit.

Other than the famed settlement of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} and a few scattered points of interest hosting the hermetic and the lost, the northern reaches of the Rustvar Valleys are home to relatively few citizens of the Plateau. By comparison, the tributaries of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.JuuKQzqfLP4R33Dm]{Lake Mithra }to the south provide ample water for travel, fishing, and irrigation; as a result, a small number of households, camps, and farmsteads dot the landscapes near its banks.

Environment

The Rustvar Valleys are known for a transitional, somewhat arid climate, lying between the surrounding alpine highlands and the drier inland plains, with hot summers and mild winters. The Valleys are markedly less desolate than the Wedgeland mountains that encircle them, and certain aspects of the biome are known to reflect Ember's inherent arcane nature — from the enchanted vestiges of archaic civilizations to the peculiarity of its errant peaks and waterways.

Ecology

Forests of the Rustvar Valleys are marked by the russet hues of their trees and shrubbery, and a surprising diversity of vegetation — if sparse — can survive here. Although local agricultural potential is hampered, cultivation is possible on a moderate scale. Farmers here are known to grow corn, wheat, barley, sugar beets, peaches, tomatoes, cotton, tobacco, olives, grapes, melons, potatoes, and oranges. Flora unique to the area are known for their resilience and rustic beauty, like the hardy Scragwood Tree and the fruit-bearing Cinderseed Ivy.

The various settlements, farms, and homesteads of the Rustvar Valleys usually cultivate indigenous livestock, but the appearance of outland creatures is not altogether unheard of. A scattering of wild beasts (like bears, wild cats, goats, and more) proliferate the Eastern and Western Valleys, along with a modest array of creatures both mundane and mythical — from the four-horned, oryx-like Nothrin to the venomous, two-headed Vale Monitor. The biome's fauna is often a reflection of (or reaction to) the closest point-of-interest or preternatural phenomenon. And in areas where the Rustvar Valleys border upon the fog-shrouded Barrows, undead creatures like those found in the legendary Varùn burial lands can also be encountered.

Lore

The Rustvar Valleys are also steeped in the mysterious lore of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} and Varùn giants who once called these lands and the nearby Wedgelands home. Furthermore, the presence of other adjacent biomes have introduced a number of existential threats — including the maddening subterranean fauna of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} far below and the lingering threat of the Abyssal Horror known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas}. The emergence of these threats has given rise to a disconnected series of tall tales in recent years, originating from the ominous tongues of the most insightful Arcturian soothsayers.
Rustvar Valleys.soverview: The Rustvar Valleys are a pair of wide highland vales that carve their way down through the Wedgelands. The landscape is notably arid but remarkably hospitable, as evidenced by the impressive array of wildlife that occupies its borders. This is a remote biome decorated with the ancient legends (and occasional ruins) of the long-gone Shent giants, and defined by the hardiness of its resourceful outland people. Settlements of the Rustvar Valleys are considered by many to carry the essence of the Arctus Plateau itself in their storied frontier histories and ambitious hinterland architecture.
Rustvar Valleys.sexposition: The wind that sweeps through this broad mountain valley carries with it the halcyon scents of highland fields and hinterland wildflowers. You feel a sense of forgotten purpose in this gargantuan swale, which winds its way between the ancient Wedgeland peaks with aplomb. The steep rocky hillsides that frame the majestic valley stand resolute, having overlooked this region for time immemorial.

Elenain Delta.name: Elenain Delta
Elenain Delta.text:
Work In Progress! This biome and its accompanying entry are not in the scope of Early Access Gameplay. All text provided here is currently in development and incomplete. This entry will be revised and expanded on in future updates.

Gamemaster's Summary

This biome is located in the southcentral region of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Travel through this biome is generally @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Difficult Terrain}.

This perilous mire teems with dangerous flora and prowling beasts, making traversal a true test of resilience and cunning.

Environment

The environment of the Elenain Delta is varied and largely hazardous. At its safest reaches, small islands, farms and the settlement of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.ZBItrDrGoJXoX41x]{Saundrine} swell with vibrant economic activity linked to the moon-reactive Prisma Beetles. Beyond these havens, swamps, mires, peats, and twisting waterways prove an escalating challenge to navigation and survival. The true wild heart of the Delta is the most treacherous realm, where tangled, skeletal trees cast perpetual darkness over uneven, hazardous terrain teeming with all manner of dangers.

Ecology

The Elenain Delta is a crucible of vibrant plant life and cunning predators, each species having adapted ingeniously to this hostile environment. It is home to numerous carnivorous flora, from Bonebranches that resemble skeletal remains and snare prey with their hardy vines, to Skygrass which swiftly overtakes and consumes anything left sitting too long.

The fauna are equally adapted and dangerous, with wolf-like Bogbiters, poisonous Mudsnakes and horrible Slinkers waiting in the mud and undergrowth. Among the area's more curious inhabitants though, are the moon-reactive Prisma Beetles, which unwittingly create wild magic fields through their vibrant, color-shifting swarms.

Lore

The Elenain Delta's strange ecology stems from ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} aquaculture experiments that were carried out thousands of years prior. These experiments had proceeded without issue until suffering a critical disruption by the cosmic cataclysm of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}. Surviving remnants of these experiments were warped, imbued with unusual and sometimes deadly characteristics.

However, all of this is ancient and unknown history. There are countless stories from the locals and meandering academic theories about how the land came to be, why it is so dangerous, and why the creatures within are so strange, and few if any of them touch on the true cause. To most, the Elenain Delta is one of two things: home, or best avoided.
Elenain Delta.soverview: The Elenain Delta is a wild and lush wetland ecosystem bordering the Elenain River, the Reaver Ocean, the Sarin Strand, and the Caryx Savannah. While the town of Saundrine thrives on the savannah border and is famed for its unique dyes, the Delta's interior remains sparsely populated.
Elenain Delta.sexposition: A verdant labyrinth of dense wetlands unfurls before you. The air is thick with humidity, carrying the heady scent of mud and moss. Overhead, towering bone-white trees with skeletal branches form a twisted canopy, while patches of blue-tinged skygrass cling to rocks and outcroppings. There is a powerful sense of chaos in this wilderness, where things could go awry in seconds and survival is often determined by sharper instincts and quicker reflexes.

Skybrush.name: Skybrush
Skybrush.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This settlement exists at ⬢ s.3198.2885 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CgqmvuJ1NLfqaO3I]{Rustvar Valleys}, northwest of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]{Storsa's Strand}.

  • This settlement is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaSkybru]{Vista: Skybrush}.

  • This settlement is featured in @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death}, [[/eventState chain1Reunite]], and [[/eventState chain1Map]].

Said to “brush the sky,” this colloquially-named Rustvar settlement is known for being the Arcturian community at the highest elevation outside of the Hersa Mountains — a subject of pride for its citizens, who have acclimated to their high-altitude lifestyle with zeal. The people of Skybrush are predominantly an adventurous and self-made folk, with roots that spread as far as the roads of the Arctus Plateau can carry them.

Skybrush may be somewhat remote, but it stands protected and ready to accommodate. Both the vantage of the Canopy district's arboreal architecture and the ramparts of the ancient giantkin ruins have proven time and time again to thwart any would-be interlopers and errant wildlife alike. Meanwhile, outside the town limits, smaller homesteads dot a forested, suburban sprawl.

At a Glance

  • Settlement Type: Lumber and mining town; niche specialty in Shent & Varùn artifacts

  • Size: Small (100 - 150)

  • Primary Cultures: [[/culture emberArcturian]]

  • Predominant Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]], [[/ancestry emberHulgrun]], [[/ancestry emberKeth]], [[/ancestry emberKivahr]], [[/ancestry emberFej]], and [[/ancestry emberKiska]]

  • Languages: [[/language common]], [[/language arcden]]

  • Religion: Moderate; @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.LNFCxHtijBM7gh76]{Thoma}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae}

  • Governance: Elected Town Council

  • Architecture: Tiered arboreal housing (Canopy District) and modern Arcturian dwellings (Understory District) blended with natural caverns and ancient giantkin ruins

  • Economy: Harvest and trade of rare lumber; harvest and trade of produce (grapes, pears) and livestock (goats); extraction and trade of precious ores; black market export of rare Varùn artifacts; domestication of beasts as mounts

  • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}

Landmarks - The Canopy

The RoostTavern

An ale-soaked watering hole in the Canopy where spirits can be lifted during times of trouble, The Roost is one of the most reliable sources of information and rumors in Skybrush. Amenities are available here to those in need, including an all-hours kitchen and a half-dozen rooms for rent.

Invocation RowShrines

This Canopy-based cul-de-sac houses an array of five shrines to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.LNFCxHtijBM7gh76]{Thoma},@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{ Janar}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae}.

The Wystful ApothecaryApothecary

This frontier pharmacy owned and operated by Hescott Wyst is a reliable source of affordable spell components, natural herbal remedies, and common alchemical reagents.

Cradley's Uncanny BeastsMount Stables

Situated in a precipitous cavern on the northern edge of Skybrush, this eponymous collection of stables owned by Goose Cradley hosts an uncommon variety of domesticated beasts, including @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.SoK7l5zJQKxTVgLL]{Giant Bats} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.EYiQZ3rFL25fEJY5]{Dire Wolves}. These well-trained steeds command a rather hefty price of 500 gp each — unless the buyer is willing to take up a peculiar errand from the eponymous owner for a relative discount.

The Long HaulConsignment Shop

A consignment shop owned and operated by the pawn broker Liestra Grann, The Long Haul carries a wide variety of eccentric wares uncommon to more traditional retail outlets. Situated near the southeastern edge of town, The Long Haul's cylindrical two-story edifice is often a welcome sight for travelers in search of retail therapy and creature comforts.

Landmarks - The Understory

The BlockhousePrison & Constable's Office

This two-story edifice in the Understory district houses the Skybrush gaol and a guardhouse office for the town Constable, along with an apartment on the second floor. The gaol itself houses four iron-barred cells secured with heavy locks; characters without the @UUID[Item.DbWgoCxmEbS3ST7u]{Skybrush Constable's Key} must succeed on a [[/tool thief dex 18]] check or a [[/check str 20]] check to open.

HollowstoneNeighborhood

This Understory neighborhood of squat Arcturian houses is built in a small gulley on the southeastern edge of town. The homes of Qory Hult and Mrs. Lillium Estweather preside among the dwellings here, alongside several others.

The Rustic ForkRestaurant

Many residents of Skybrush consider The Rustic Fork to be a shining example of precisely how good a simple menu of rural Arcturian cuisine can be. The daily specials may change, but the charming, timeworn folk tales of its proprietor stay the same.

Skybrush General GoodsGeneral Goods Store

This aptly-named emporium of adventuring gear, tools, and trade goods also carries a modest variety of weapons and armor. An assortment of in-house smithies, led by an Arcturian craftsman named X, are available for simple repairs and commissions.

Tavoc's DeepQuarry

This subterranean quarry of ore and stone is the modern incarnation of an ancient Shent mine at the edge of town, and provides a few dozen Skybrush citizens with their hard-earned livelihoods.

Characters of Interest - The Canopy

@UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann}Chaotic Neutral, Kivahr, she/her

Liestra Grann is a headstrong Arcturian pawn broker known for her witty banter and ability to suss out a killer deal. She spends her days making a good living by orchestrating the trade of Shent and Varùn artifacts from her Understory storefront, the Long Haul (alongside an array of illicit goods and services, which she only offers to vetted clientele).

Kel KornanLawful Neutral, Kiska, she/her

This accomplished stone and timber broker maintains an apartment in Skybrush, from which she facilitates business matters for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}. She purchased a cursed @UUID[Item.OJRVuMrUlSAM3soe]{Rune-Marked Sash} from Liestra Grann, which has brought her under the damnable sway of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}.

Revelry WystChaotic Good, Aster/Human, she/her

This talented young jeweler was once the muse and "true love" of Dereth Erekos, but recent events have propelled the glamorous ingenue to a grim spotlight. Her days are now marked with sorrow and fear of the lingering evil that threatens Skybrush.

Hescott WystLawful Neutral, Human, he/him

This shrewd Arcturian apothecary is Revelry Wyst's overprotective father. Hescott operates The Wystful Apothecary from the boughs of Skybrush's Canopy district, and is exceptionally wary of outsiders in light of recent circumstances.

Gedron TathChaotic Good, Kivahr, he/him

Gedron Tath is an eccentric Arcturian artist whose macabre creations have earned him a somewhat dubious reputation among the citizens of Skybrush. He purchased a cursed @UUID[Item.tft5aeUE51jyKoqX]{Rune-Marked Band} from Liestra Grann, which he wears like a bracelet (and which has become responsible for his own affliction with @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}).

HadrasLawful Good, Kivahr, he/him

Hadras is a tenacious @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.PVD5wRdyO7iCJPs1]{Priest} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.LNFCxHtijBM7gh76]{Thoma}, learned in the ways of many faiths and generally welcoming of their practitioners. A true servant of the people, Hadras is eager to reflect the rites and rituals of those who come to him seeking divine succor.

Danton ShainChaotic Good, Human, they/them

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}'s most qualified expert on Shent artifacts, Danton Shain is a studious Ordani socialite who paradoxically likes to keep a low profile, preferring the privacy of their home parlour to the bustle of local gatherings.

Shax the SeeressChaotic Neutral, Kiska, she/they

This sly Witch of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae} harbors a curious appreciation for entropy and the arcane. Despite her relatively macabre interests, Shax is eager to help those who come to her with interesting need (and appropriate coin) in-hand.

Goose CradleyChaotic Neutral, Human/Kivahr, he/him

This madcap Kithil animal handler is the eponymous proprietor of Cradley's Uncanny Beasts. Unconventional to the core, Cradley is known for his tendency to strike up fair trades in exchange for rather peculiar errands.

Characters of Interest - The Understory

@UUID[Actor.cvyDEZu7WvSDLzAo]{Mica Valaston}Lawful Good, Hul'grun, they/them

Mica Valaston is Skybrush's obdurate and cynical Constable, and stands ready to exercise the duties of their station at a moment's notice. Despite their inherent skepticism, Mica is eager for the party's capable help, and is notably equipped with the @UUID[Item.DbWgoCxmEbS3ST7u]{Skybrush Constable's Key}.

Qory HultNeutral Good, Human, he/him

This twenty-something Arcturian is a once-proud mineworker who purchased the cursed @UUID[Item.w7jXkPu7MheM6bkw]{Rune-Marked Arrowhead} from Liestra Grann. Now, Qory anxiously awaits an untimely death in the Blockhouse gaol after murdering his wife (a result of the Confusion effect caused by the curse of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}).

Mrs. Lillium EstweatherNeutral Good, Keth, she/her

This elderly Skybrush local is Qory & Veera Hult's busybody neighbor. She wears her Kithil roots proudly and enjoys a life of retirement (which allows her to relentlessly exercise her rather nosy dispositions).

Gurty HoldstoneLawful Good, Human, she/her

Many locals consider this spirited thirty-something washerwoman to be the heart of Skybrush. Gurty chastises any visitors for the ill-fated timing of their arrival to the accursed treetop hamlet, but provides helpful guidance nonetheless.

Mr. Elyas ErekosNeutral Good, Human, he/him

The despondent father of Dereth and Branos Erekos, this retired mine worker's gregarious temperament has given way to grief. His attempts to remain stoic after the death of one son at the hands of another are rather tenuous.

Mrs. Chrysta ErekosNeutral Good, Human, she/her

The grief-stricken mother of Dereth and Branos Erekos, inconsolable in the wake of the violence that surrounds her family. Her selfless duties as an experienced governess have fallen to the wayside.

MattockNeutral Good, Fej, he/him

This grizzled, scar-covered mine worker has seen more action than most of Skybrush. A Lumek @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.J8xjoG4Dxb8WkHtV]{Veteran} who decided to settle down in a foreign land, the stout-hearted Mattock is rather protective of this treetop hamlet he calls home.

Life in Skybrush

The ardency of the town's settlers is evident in Skybrush via the resourceful artistry and enterprising craftsmanship of its people. Many Skybrush residents generate folk art and music as inspired as the work of any Ordani professional, and the treetop hamlet's homes and businesses are bedecked with various signs of this personal ingenuity and design. The people of Skybrush are proud of their connection to the ancient Shent and Varùn ways, and view their habitation of the ruin-marked landscape as a reverent one (despite the relative exploitation of the area's historical gravesites and monuments).

The mountain settlement is defined by 2 distinct districts: the Canopy and the Understory. There isn’t a great deal of societal stratification between these two districts; homes and places of commerce are generally located where they happen to be based on practical requirements (but there are certainly exceptions). These districts are built in and around the towering boughs of a grove of gravelbark pine trees as well as the cavernous ruins of decrepit Shent and Varùn monuments.

Culture

In addition to several holidays that honor the regular phases of Ember's moons, the people of Skybrush (both faithful and secular alike) observe an annual Hunter's Eve that marks a celebration of the Shard God Janar's many conquests and the various Leviathans he managed to slay.

Religion is of relatively low importance in Skybrush compared to a more secular reverence for the Cosmos, but a humble scattering of five shrines to various gods serve local citizens of faith. These shrines honor Alar, Spectra, Thoma, Janar, and Malae.

Defense

As remote as it is, Skybrush persists under recurring threat of encroachment by local wildlife both monstrous and mundane. Access points between the Canopy and Understory districts have been constructed with these assaults in mind, and offer a variety of quick escape or assault options for citizens if and when an attack occurs. Meanwhile, a cadre of bat-riding cavaliers and a volunteer ground force serve as Skybrush’s most capable defenders.

Politics

Skybrush is a relatively lawless settlement, with community decisions guided by silver and gold (with a small measure of the common good thrown in for safe measure). A town council of eight is elected annually, but is unofficially comprised of members from each of the eight top business enterprises in town rather than the voices of average citizens. Arguably, there are few “average” citizens in Skybrush — for it takes a certain kind of stoicism, inquisitiveness, or wanderlust to call this dangerous mountainside community home.

Lore

Skybrush began as a scrappy camp of Kivahr archaeologists and adventurers who established a base of operations in the foothills of the Varùn Lowlands, where ruins and vaults of the ancient Shent and other giantkin promised financial opportunity and cosmic enlightenment. Ingenious to the last, these settlers built some of their homes among the treetops — to both honor the ancient Shent accords with the moon, and be spared from the biome's most menacing ground predators. These treetop dwellings became the camp's trademark, and the name Skybrush was formally adopted by its flourishing people.

The earliest days of Skybrush actually precede the founding of Ordain by roughly 100 years, but the advent of the great Arcturian metropolis encouraged a rapid expansion of the frontier hamlet's modest sprawl. As Ordain's need for gravelbark pine and mineral ore grew (along with the private interests of groups like the Anachraenum and Ordain's Trading Houses), so did funding for Skybrush development, alongside a swift rise in the Human population.

Today, Skybrush not only serves as a profound historical waypoint for the ancient traditions of the Shent and Varùn giants, but as an important trading post for travelers and explorers of the western plateau.
Skybrush.soverview: The treetop hamlet known as Skybrush is a predominantly Human and Kivahr settlement in the western Rustvar Valleys that borders on the foothills of the mountainous Wedgelands, where the ruins of ancient giants color the lives of the proud locals who live there. Remote and self-sufficient, Skybrush is known throughout the Plateau for its exports of rugged gravelbark lumber and rare Shent artifacts.
Skybrush.sexposition:
A two-tiered frontier town of wood and stone stands before you, its houses not only built among the windswept lofts of towering trees but nestled into the giant timeworn ruins of some bygone civilization. Up above, rope bridges and wooden catwalks connect dozens of arboreal homes and business constructed by the very lumber that supports them; and down below, squat Arcturian buildings hug the ancient monuments of long-gone Giants and their kin. There is a rustic splendor here quite unlike any you've seen.

Yet, the mountain air grows cold as you step foot among the rural outskirts of this frontier town — where the stern hand of fate appears to hold the locals in its bleak grasp. Whatever pride that once resided here among the towering pines and scattered excavations has given way to somber desolation, made evident by the lack of vitality in this otherwise thriving hamlet.

Keeper's Crossing.name: Keeper's Crossing
Keeper's Crossing.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3209.2890 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, south of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.JuuKQzqfLP4R33Dm]{Lake Mithra}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberNainRiverCr]{Keeper's Crossing} area map.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState cindaric1Crossing]].

The ruined bridge known as Keeper’s Crossing was once a proud stone-and-timber viaduct that previously connected each bank of the River Elenain along the Golden Way, the region’s most frequently traveled mercantile road. However, naught but moss-covered rubble and river detritus can be found here after the great earthquakes that rocked the Golden Flats two decades ago; and the arcane waters of the notorious River Elenain remain unforgiving. Nevertheless, the moss-covered remains of the eastern and western abutments stand defiant and resolute.

Environment

Because of its ruinous condition and proximity to the River Elenain's turbulent and enchanted waters, Keeper's Crossing is a remarkably damp and sodden location, marked by muddy and overgrown earth that resulted from the bridge's destruction years ago. Footing here is unsure and slippery, even during the most benevolent of weather — conditions dictated by the arcane river's somewhat unpredictable currents.

The bridge itself once sat 40 feet above the water's surface level, where a ramshackle array of planks and ropes are now stretched across the swift runnel. Those who wish to cross the river without being washed downstream by the torrent must safely ford the river using the various rocks and makeshift bridges that span the watercourse.

Ecology

The ecology of Keeper's Crossing is similar to that of most other locations along the River Elenain in the Golden Flats, with an array of Arcturian flora like sapgrass and waterwells in abundance, alongside fauna including gore birds, tillers, and the iridescent trout that swim up- and downstream along the 'Nain.

Lore

Originally named for the Ordani shopkeep who commissioned its construction, Keeper’s Crossing became a major landmark along the region’s most traveled trade way, and was fundamental in Ordain’s early growth. A small array of docks beside the bridge — all but annihilated by the quakes — once catered to ferry captains and riverboats from Nain, and brought a long-forgotten vibrancy to this place that has been utterly lost to time.

Like much of the plateau, Keeper’s Crossing is steeped in local legend. Rumors abound of a still-hidden cache from the merchant caravan that was caught up in the earthquake’s tumult, lost somewhere in the rubble below the current. Whatever the accuracy of the landmark’s tall tales, the ruins of Keeper’s Crossing stand as a testament to Ember’s effortless ability to reclaim the land and sea for itself.
Keeper's Crossing.soverview: Once the site of a trade way bridge, Keeper's Crossing has been reduced to nothing but a pile of rubble, treacherous stones, and agglomerated detritus dragged from upriver. The remnants of the eastern and western abutments mark where the bridge once began, for what little that is worth.
Keeper's Crossing.sexposition: A soggy scattering of mossy flagstones and splintered timber comprise the ruins of a time-neglected bridge. The masonry and woodwork here that once spanned the River Elenain is now mostly submerged beneath its ceaseless southward flow, and the chances of crossing without great effort seem slim to none.

Ordani Skywalk.name: Ordani Skywalk
Ordani Skywalk.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3208.2901, spanning the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.tuopdqO2JSeH1LeU]{Splinter Canyons} west of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet]{Ordain}.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState cindaric1Bridge]].

The great Skywalk of Ordain a centuries old pathway bridging the two sides of the plateau, and is one of the most iconic and enduring sights in the region. Almost everyone traveling to or from Ordain will cross the Skywalk, and take in its magnificent view of the canyon below.

Environment

The bridge is made entirely of pale stone quarried from somewhere far beyond this region, as it's white color is unlike any of the stone found in the area. Underfoot the bridge is made of thousands of unevenly sized slabs pieced together and decorated in an vast array of styles. This extends up into the walls and watch towers of the bridge, each one unique in its own way.

At the midpoint of the bridge travelers gather to rest, take in the view and socialize. Here one can find impromptu swap meets, maker shows, concerts, and the like, though they never happen with any kind of predictable schedule.

Ecology

The bridge sees constant traffic at all hours, and their make consist of a varied sort. Locals walk the bridges at night, enjoying the glow, while trader caravans trundle across it, bound for one of Ordain's many markets or warehouses. The towers, manned by members of the city's Hallows keep watch over the bridge, helping travelers, and looking out for trouble.

Lore

The stone this bridge is made from was quarried from deep beneath Ordain, and was brought to the surface at great cost to the city, but the end result is nothing short of magnificent. The entire structure is centuries old, and embodies the meeting of Arcturian and Ordani cultures. The bridge features art, inscriptions, reliefs, makers marks of the countless artisans that contributed to its construction. Even today artists and crafters petition in the Hallows for the right to put their mark on the Skywalk, or performance maintenance in the hopes of putting their name alongside the others there.
Ordani Skywalk.soverview: This magnificent bridge stretches across the Splinter Canyon, spanning the gap between the Arctus Plateau and Ordain. The stone it is made from is unique, as it gently glows at night, becoming more pronounced as the Spirit Moon Orbis approaches its apex.
Ordani Skywalk.sexposition:
The dark earth and golden grasses around you give way to stunning white stone. Before you a truly massive bridge spans the vast canyon ahead. Easily thousand feet wide and over a mile long, this immense thoroughfare is the largest of its kind in the plateau.

Traffic flows across the bridge, a combination of pedestrians, mounted travelers and caravans, all under the watch of six pale watch towers running along the edges playing host to groups of Ordani, with banners of the Hallows hanging from them.

Nain.name: Nain
Nain.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This settlement exists at ⬢ s.3216.2893 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, northwest of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.X1FzWfTYfe7JfD3P]{Seawall}.

  • This settlement is featured in [[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]]. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book of Tales}, and [[/eventState canyonsSideKaliResettles]].

This weather-swept village is occupied by two main social groups of Arcturians — the Stone-hearted and the River Walkers — and serves as a small trade hub for the surrounding farmsteads.

At a Glance

  • Settlement Type: Fishing village and river trade hub

  • Size: Small (200 - 250)

  • Primary Cultures: [[/culture emberArcturian]]

  • Predominant Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]], [[/ancestry emberHulgrun]], [[/ancestry Kavir]], [[/ancestry emberKeth]], [[/ancestry emberFej]], [[/ancestry emberKiska]]

  • Languages: [[/language common]], [[/language arcden]]

  • Religion: Low/Moderate; primary deities include @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla}

  • Governance: Village Council, with outside influence from the Otherhood of Fortune

  • Architecture: Modern Arcturian (with an emphasis on stone and wood materials), featuring an elaborate network of water wheels, channels, and aqueducts

  • Economy: Fishing, shipping, travel; cultivation and trade of produce (rice, wheat) and livestock (horses, pigs, sheep, donkeys); smuggling

  • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{House Lilifeld}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{House Wandren}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune}

Landmarks - The Thruways

The Thruways serve as the settlement's central district, marked by a network of river channels and sturdy stone structures.

The Barrel BottomTavern

This seedy, ale-soaked tavern is frequented by adventurers, fisherman, and locals of all stripes, and plays host to noteworthy scoundrels like Juro Wandren and Helton Stath.

The EastwharfTavern

This market and docking bay on the eastern edge of town caters to local waterway commerce and hosts a variety of merchants peddling various Arcturian wares.

Zenodora's General GoodsGeneral Goods Store

When tools and provisions are what you need, Zenodora's General Goods has you covered. This moss-covered equipment store owned by Zenodora Vann is a favorite stop for adventurers and traveling merchants who make their way through Nain.

Landmarks - The Riverwinds

The surrounding Riverwinds district is distinguished by its floating wooden structures and weather-resistant agrarian marvels.

Angler's WayFishing Bridge

Angler's Way is a narrow stone bridge that spans several of Nain's channels and serves as a popular fishing area for urban piscators.

Old Northside MillSmithy

This waterwheel-powered smithy and granary of exceptional Arcturian design features a variety of semi-automated mechanisms that manage to increase its productive capabilities twofold. Elefield Beck is the head smithy.

The Stonecraft EstatePrivate Residence

This aged two-story townhouse is the residence of Amalthea Stonecraft, the Arctus Plateau's most accomplished storyteller. The estate is cluttered with art and literature of the Arctus Plateau and beyond, along with an accumulation of curiosities collected throughout several lifetimes. A detailed history of Ember can be found among the shelves if one knows precisely where to look.

Characters of Interest - The Thruways

@UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren}Chaotic Neutral, Wirrun, he/him

This twenty-something Wintermaned scoundrel makes his living as a black market smuggler, and is known to be an estranged childhood friend of Lyla Cevher.

Helton StathLawful Evil, Kiska, he/him

This sardonic bartender of the Barrel Bottom is an unscrupulous rogue, rumored to facilitate many an unsavory deal for Nain's most underhanded traders.

Zenodora VannChaotic Good, Arcturian Human, she/her

The eponymous proprietor of Zenodora's General Goods, Zenodora Vann is known as a shrewd but gregarious businesswoman with a passion for Nain history and a taste for foreign cuisine.

Characters of Interest - The Riverwinds

@UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft}Chaotic Good, Aster/Human, she/her

The violet-winged Aster known as Amalthea Stonecraft is the Arctus Plateau's most celebrated storyteller and historian of local legends.

Elefield BeckNeutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/they

The stoic head smithy of the Old Northside Mill. An exceptional ironsmith with an innate talent for agrimagic.

Life In Nain

The Arcturians of Nain are split between two main groups, separated by their survival-based ideologies: while the Stone-hearted believe in lasting structures that can withstand the test of disaster and time, the River Walkers have embraced an ideology of coexisting with nature's whims, living within wooden structures that ebb and flow with the River Elenain. Members of both social groups provide ferry services on the river, but the competition between them seems to customarily drive prices up rather than down (leaving some outsiders to believe that the two groups actually collude to benefit from the trade to Ordain).

Despite the dangers inherent in its waterways (or perhaps because of them), many people of Nain make use of a complex system of water wheels and aqueducts to help power their simple agrarian machinery. The constantly shifting arcane properties of the river's water make the maintenance of these systems routinely difficult. As a result, Stone-hearted locals are always searching for better resources and raw building materials.

Culture

The children of Nain are known to send parchment sailboats up and down the river. Hand-written stories and songs adorn these papercraft vessels, which have a bizarre way of washing ashore in remote places all throughout Ember. Some adults in Nain continue this tradition by placing messages in bottles or hollowed gourds rather than parchment boats.

Religion in Nain is of low-to-moderate importance to its people. While many of Nain's residents maintain lives of secular pragmatism, other citizens look to the gods to help shape the fortune of their relatively tumultuous days. Various shrines throughout town honor gods like Lantyr, Janar, and Vekalla.

The people of Nain observe several holidays, such as Trawler's Haul, an annual contest where ramshackle boats and homemade vessels are sent over the waterfall in a death-defying plunge. And Docking Day, when the Stone-hearted and the River Walkers put aside their disagreements to celebrate the founding of Nain.

Politics

Trade in Nain is the primary concern of the town's commercially-driven Town Council, which is comprised of several members from each group and a few neutral parties (along with a few covert operatives of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune}.

Defense

Like many Arcturian settlements, Nain relies on a voluntary militia to assist the town in times of trouble. Fortunately, the riverfront hamlet's stout bulwarks afford extra security against the region's aggressive fauna just as much as it protects Nain from the ceaseless assault of supernatural storms.

Lore

Arcane maelstroms regularly manifest along the banks of the River Elenain here, causing calamity both up- and downstream in their wake. Similarly, the water of the River Elenain is known to sometimes spontaneously transmute; this alchemical havoc can prove difficult for the people of Nain, who sometimes go to great lengths to protect their tools, structures, and vessels from preternatural wear.

Nain is routinely threatened by freak tornadoes and the unexplained transmutation of its local waters. Throughout the years, several smaller villages built along the banks of the River Elenain were lost to natural disaster, leaving little more than ruins behind. This unpredictability led to the development of Nain's social stratification.
Nain.soverview:
This tenacious riverside settlement, nestled in the heartland of the Golden Flats, spans the River Elenain and sits upon the edge of the Arctus Chasm.

Prone to flooding during rainier seasons (and at the unpredictable whims of the Biome's peculiar geological phenomena), Nain is characterized by its river channels, water wheels, and complex aqueducts.
Nain.sexposition: A scrappy riverside settlement is built here upon the banks of the River Elenain, marked by a network of stone aqueducts and channeled waterways. An inner district crafted from strong Arcturian stone is surrounded by a ring of ramshackle-yet-charming wooden structures; just as these timber buildings effortlessly sway with the river currents, the stone of the stoic inner city stands against them. The settlement is dotted with industrious water wheels and individual wharfs, and the roar of a grand waterfall to the south is ever-present.

Arcturel.name: Arcturel
Arcturel.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This settlement exists at ⬢ s.3221.2886 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, east of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.cHJSlRXSX9wvV7br]{Vortest Tower}.

  • This settlement is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaArctur]{Vista: Arcturel}.

  • This settlement can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelTra]{Arcturel Upper - Tradeway}, @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelUnd]{Arcturel Upper - Underbelly}, and @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelLow]{Arcturel Lower} area maps.

  • This settlement is featured in [[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel1]], [[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel2]], @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3.JournalEntryPage.ZThJu6HC10ohFR4v]{Glitter in the Dark}, and [[/eventState bookTalesQuarryman]].

Light in Arcturel is often scarce, and natural light is almost nonexistent but for one hour each day: beginning at noon, a narrow beam of Lantyr's light pierces the settlement’s depths from directly above, lighting it like a beacon. The rest of the time, the Sinkhole City is dim, lit mostly by the glow of the hundreds of luminous mushrooms that line the sinkhole walls. Where the light of the mushrooms cannot reach, Arcturel is illuminated by its best known export: lambent @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{Inkaro Pearls}, harvested from @UUID[Actor.AnhHlAMP5rsnH7wZ]{Mootaps} that live at the lowest levels of the settlement. These strange creatures are cared for by the Inkaro Lamplighters, who steward their subterranean environment with great care.

At a Glance

  • Settlement Type: Industrial mining settlement nestled in the walls of a sinkhole

  • Size: Large (1200 - 1500)

  • Primary Cultures: [[/culture emberArcturian]]

  • Predominant Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]], [[/ancestry emberHulgrun]], [[/ancestry emberKeth]], [[/ancestry emberFej]], and [[/ancestry emberKiska]]

  • Languages: [[/language common]], [[/language arcden]]

  • Religion: No central religion; household worship; common reverence for Lantyr

  • Governance: Loose trade alliance of local businesses

  • Architecture: Practical; homes, business, and mines are built within whatever space is available to them, using whatever materials are immediately available

  • Economy: Trade of @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{Inkaro Pearls}, ores, and minerals

  • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}; Inkaro Lamplighters; Silver Beam Consortium

Landmarks - Brimtown

Located on the surface of Ember at the northwestern edge of the sinkhole, Brimtown considers itself the gateway to Arcturel, but it's little more than a scattering of shops and homes, often seen by visitors as a place to pass through on their way into Arcturel proper. Most of its value to outsiders lies in the local stables and storage houses, where visitors and traveling merchants can keep certain assets and commodities in lieu of taking them into the sinkhole. Brimtown is also intended as the first line of defense against anyone who might think to attack Arcturel; its watchtowers are poised to warn the city in the advent of an attack, although this particular security measure has yet to be put to the test.

The Bird's NestSecurity Post

This security post is built into the remains of a desiccated tree at the sinkhole's edge. Its vigilant guards, known as the Brimtown Watchers, keep a keen eye on Arcturel's surface at all times of the day, although they are rarely called to action.

The Edge of CivilizationWaystation

A ramshackle waystation near the sinkhole’s edge that hosts a tavern alongside an assortment of stables. In recent years, The Edge has positioned itself to become a major tourist destination in the Arctus Plateau, but has yet to achieve lasting success. It is owned and operated by a congenial woman named Onsi Urganzi.

Landmarks - Upper Arcturel

Light is brighter in Upper Arcturel than anywhere else in the Sinkhole City, thanks to its relative proximity to the surface and the oversized ceilings of many of its buildings. While there are concerns about changing the natural layout of the caverns further down the sinkhole (and any instability that might occur as a result), those who live or work in here in "The Balconies" have been given permission to add flourishes to their homes and businesses. These modifications often include the installation of larger entrances or the lavish use of @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{Inkaro Pearls} as light sources (even when it isn't necessary). In addition to these more spacious homes, The Balconies are marked by the ornamentation of its bridges, which are often embedded with small bits of crystal or glass to create a light show during the midday hour when @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} shines down on the city.

@UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.K9z1CCM6zkDkIBOn]{Rallyhome}Tavern & Inn

A large communal meeting house built into the undulating eaves of a massive petrified mushroom, where many of Arcturel’s adventurers plot their next excursion (or recover from their last). Rallyhome hosts a small tavern and rooms for rent. Servers include the permanently disgruntled Felisa Waterborne, who is pretty bad at her job.

@UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.7wweAzTLYqshFH0d]{Arcturian Automatons}Workshop

The cluttered, curiosity-strewn workshop of the famed artificer Vartholomew Chess, maker of fine constructs. Built among and beneath a cluster of large, luminous crystals.

@UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.5IHmzA71p0Fd8F4l]{Silver Beam Foyer}Silver Beam Headquarters

The restricted headquarters of the Silver Beam Mining Consortium, the opportunistic group of Railen outsiders led by Larissa Toth. Hosts a barracks for Silver Beam personnel and a furtive workshop for Toth’s transmutation experiments.

@UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.vivtup8c9VWCcFTx]{Glimmer Lounge}Crystal Carving Shop

A crystal carving shop that holds frequent art exhibitions and dance parties, which feature prismatic light shows created using @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{Inkaro Pearls}; its clientele is a mix of visiting merchants and celebratory locals.

@UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.U6xx9KnEc5QsiNF1]{Briez Flywell's General Goods}General Store

A store run by shopkeeper Darvin Nolde, where characters may purchase various odds and ends, including equipment, tools, and trade goods.

@UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.iXV5jxIGjk6Yp4Qn]{Precipice}Restaurant

A fine dining establishment that caters to Arcturel's most sophisticated palates and special occasions.

Landmarks - Lower Arcturel

Located a mile below Upper Arcturel, Lower Arcturel is both the heart of the city's mining community and the core of its operations. A collection of mines, businesses, and homes comprise this lightless area, many of which are cut into the rock of the sinkhole itself. Thanks to its traditionally unsavory qualities, "The Dives" isn't exactly renowned as a place for tourists or visiting dignitaries; this industrial area of Arcturel consists of true locals, those who actually live and work within the city.

@UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.yXmLKvQfWjY5Nf9d]{Hob Korell's Unconventional Steeds}Stables

Modest stables owned and operated by the stilt-wearing frog herder named Hob Korell. Featuring a range of rare mounts, including frogs, lizards, and dragonflies of the giant variety.

@UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.rh4RdGCvghwWvPgR]{Zodi Trask's Apartment}Home
