The private residence of Zodi Trask, the current foreman of the Arcturel Mining Concern and chief contact in the area for House Cevher.

@UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.yObJp4josnr70zog]{Arvoda's Elixirs}Alchemical Shop

The residence, workshop, and storefront of Emelyn Arvoda, a matronly water mage who crafts scrolls, potions, and other magic items for travelers of the lightless depths.

@UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.crgIhy7BVETKJYHN]{Wrest Repairs}Blacksmith

A repair shop owned by Rennerie Wrest, former miner and current metal artist; the mining operations often rely on him for big jobs, but he always tries to make time for individuals and odds jobs. The shop changes its slogan frequently, but none have managed to catch on. The current iteration, "Not At Its Best? Come Get Some Wrest!" does not appear likely to change this track record.

@UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.QpHwyxq7yJZGhjFY]{Waterborne Family Distillery}Brewery

Waterborne Distillery, which is run by a family of trained distillers, primarily makes brews from water found in the Inkaro Pools, which improves the taste and is thought to put people in a good mood. The family is currently under the guidance of elder member Sevali Waterborne.

Landmarks - Rock Bottom

This ramshackle suburb of Arcturel sits on the floor of the sinkhole, a mile beneath Lower Arcturel, and is seen by locals as an ironic bookend to Brimtown above: whereas Brimtown is a bright gateway, Rock Bottom is a gloomy sprawl, a makeshift village of tent rows and canvas pavilions, piles of crates and industrial waste, and the detritus of the finer society overhead. @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{Inkaro Pearls} are scarce here, and most residents rely instead on oil and lambent mushrooms for lantern light. Rock Bottom shelters those who can't afford to live elsewhere — or choose not to, for one oft-illicit reason or another.

Big Cap's Mushroom StandDelicious Fungi Stand

Owned and operated by Buddy "Big Cap" Moss, this grimy mushroom vendor is one of the few places of noble repute in Rock Bottom, and is known for the remarkable quality of its savory fungi and candied insects.

The Inkaro PoolsPearl Extraction

The Inkaro Pools lie at the bottommost levels of Arcturel, deep within a cavern overgrown with phosphorescent fungi. These wide, shallow pools glow with the light of @UUID[Actor.AnhHlAMP5rsnH7wZ]{Mootaps}: large, lamprey-like creatures that scuttle along their beds and feed on the fungi's luminosity. @UUID[Actor.8nFz5CSPqhv6h1eI.Item.pvkcgxB5z38CSxmF]{Inkaro Pearls} are the hardened waste product of this process, their color reflecting the dominant band of phosphorescence consumed. A Mootap cannot shed this growth on its own; though it takes years for a pearl to form, it will eventually kill the creature if not removed. The Inkaro Lamplighters tend the pools, herding the Mootaps toward different bands of light and gently harvesting the pearls at the proper time. Their work often puts them at odds with Larissa Toth and the Silver Beam Consortium, as ecological stewardship clashes with the pursuit of profit.

Characters of Interest - Brimtown

Onsi UrganziNeutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/her

A former adventurer turned business owner, Onsi Urganzi possesses a friendliness that many locals describe as "aggressive." Still, The Edge is the only place in Brimtown with stables equipped to properly care for exotic mounts, and one can leave even the most ornery creature under Onsi's protection with confidence.

Characters of Interest - Upper Arcturel

Felisa WaterborneNeutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/her

Daughter of Sevali Waterborne, Felisa was forced out of the family distillery and into food service to teach her a valuable lesson in humility. She has not learned it — nor how to properly pour an ale.

Xofira AledendroNeutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/her

An Anachraenum scholar who specializes in histories and relics of the Pathways, she often be found frequenting the comforts and distractions of Rallyhome.

@UUID[Actor.nnTbrW4RdzudxxMT]{Vartholomew Chess}Lawful Good, Arcturian Wirrun, she/her

An ingenious artificer whose famed Chessmen constructs are known for their efficacy in the sinkhole depths.

@UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth}Neutral Evil, Altyra, she/her

This austere Railen industrialist serves as the Silver Beam Consortium's chief executive and the charismatic face of the organization's questionable dealings.

Nodrick StolasChaotic Good, Arcturian Human, he/him

A flamboyant crystal merchant and owner of the Glimmer Lounge, dutifully served by his Chessman construct Lucent.

Darvin NoldeNeutral Good, Arcturian Human, he/him

An absentminded shopkeeper who runs Briez Flywell's General Goods.

Characters of Interest - Lower Arcturel

Hob KorellChaotic Good, Waerd Keth, he/him

This stilt-legged mount trader's rambunctious nature is as unpredictable as his inventory of unconventional steeds — which can range from wall-climbing giant lizards to the occasional oversized dragonfly.

@UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask}Neutral Good, Kiska, he/him

This gregarious Kiska quarryman is a trusted head foreman for House Cevher, and serves as a de facto local leader for the people of Arcturel, who regard him as one of the Sinkhole City's few voices of reason.

Emelyn ArvodaNeutral Good, Arcturian Ashka, she/her

This matronly water mage crafts scrolls, potions, and other magic items for travelers of the lightless depths, but always keeps her eye on the bottom line.

Renneri WrestNeutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/her

A blacksmith as keen with a hammer as she is hopeless with a slogan, Renneri Wrest has nevertheless cornered the market on repair work for the local mines.

Sevali WaterborneNeutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/her

Sevali is the matron of the Waterborne family and the current operator of its distillery. Well connected within Arcturel and beyond, she is the person to seek out when something — or someone — must be handled discreetly.

Characters of Interest - Rock Bottom

Buddy "Big Cap" MossChaotic Neutral, Arcturian Thornling, they/them

A chummy merchant/spelunker clad in an oversized mushroom cap; owner and operator of Big Cap's Mushroom Stand in Rock Bottom.

CalandraNeutral Good, Arcturian Nir'ae, she/her

A convivial Inkaro Lamplighter whose love for subterranean nature shines through in her work.

Zirca BronzebellowNeutral Good, Hulg'run, she/her

The obdurate foreman of the Silver Beam Inkaro Pools.

Life In Arcturel

Where others would see only a hole in the ground, Arcturel sees opportunity: its culture is one of making do with what is at hand. In the mines, equipment is used, reused, and repurposed. This attitude is reflected also in its residents' small side trades, from art fashioned from ore scraps to food harvested from mushrooms that have lost their glow, alongside countless other practical crafts.

Culture

Self-reliance is prized in Arcturel. Those who look to a higher power for rescue or complain about their lot in life without acting are seen as unworthy of good fortune. As a result, cultural practices vary widely, shaped by individual and familial sensibilities. Yet there is one exception: when Lantyr shines down on Arcturel at midday, work halts, and the hour is given to rest, shared meals, and community before the light fades again.

Defense

Arcturel relies on its natural features to repel would-be raiders, preferring to invest in escape routes than fortification. Back tunnels to the surface, hidden by enchantments, wind throughout Arcturel, linking major caverns together in case the bridges become compromised. The bridges themselves are shielded with wards; when fully activated, these protections form a magical shell around the city that can deflect and disintegrate large projectiles.

Economy

Many who live in Arcturel make a living by working in the mines, which are laden with rich veins of ore and minerals. Below Rock Bottom, the Inkaro Pools are maintained by skilled Inkaro Lamplighters and Silver Beam laborers. The work is hard, but the city appeals to those who prefer to be left to their own devices. Outsiders care little for how Arcturel conducts its business, so long as trade remains steady — a climate that rewards both the entrepreneurial and the unscrupulous.

Politics

Because it is difficult to grow much food in the caverns, Arcturel depends on trade to survive; much of its politics focuses on satisfying the needs of its trading partners. Meeting the quota of goods demanded by House Cevher and other large trading partners is often paramount, and leadership generally falls to those who can extract a good yield from the mines and ensure a smooth operation. Each mine nominates one person to represent it in matters that concern all of Arcturel, alongside representatives from House Cevher, the Silver Beam Consortium, the local merchants' association, Brimtown, and the Inkaro Lamplighters.
Arcturel.soverview:
Arcturel is a sprawling settlement that consists of four mile-wide districts stacked between Ember's surface and the Pathways below: Brimtown (the village perched on the northwestern rim), Upper Arcturel (carved into the upper walls of the sinkhole), Lower Arcturel (a mile below, cut into deeper stone), and Rock Bottom (spread across the floor of the hollow).

Many of the Sinkhole City's living and working spaces occupy natural caves found within the hollow's walls. While some of these caves cut deep into the surrounding rock, most businesses and homes cluster around the perimeter, linked by a dense web of bridges and elevators where the light shines strongest.
Arcturel.sexposition:
A mile-wide sinkhole perforates the Golden Flats here, an impossibly large testament to Ember’s primeval curiosities. A stone-and-timber village clings to the northwestern brim, its unwalled perimeter watched over by a handful of wooden guard towers.

Two wooden platforms, suspended with iron chains and braided hemp, continuously rise and fall from the sinkhole's southeastern edge; they glide past a sprawling palimpsest of bridges, catwalks, and platforms before reaching the depths below, revealing a subterranean city carved into the hollow's rocky walls: Arcturel. Illuminated by phosphorescent fungi and arcane minerals, this gloam-shrouded place shelters a hardened community of miners and explorers. The air is heavy with the iron taste of metal, earth, and sweat, and the stone itself seems to tremble with the rhythm of the city beneath your feet.

Seawall.name: Seawall
Seawall.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This settlement exists at ⬢ s.3219.2897 on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fv5rtYdqx1cCbzcM]{Sarin Strand}, southwest of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet]{Ordain}.

  • This settlement is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaSeawal]{Vista: Seawall}.

  • This settlement can be explored in the @UUID[Scene.emberSeawallAlle]{Seawall Alleys} area map.

  • This settlement is featured in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu]{An Old Friend}.

Seawall, notably built on top of a previous Aedir colony known as Avadaol, is a formidable port city carved from the cliffs by the sea. Originally built as a safe haven against the unchecked and dangerous wilderness of the plateau, the city's ancient fortifications make it an almost impregnable stronghold.

At a Glance

  • Settlement Type: Port city

  • Size: Large (10,000 - 12,000)

  • Primary Cultures: [[/culture emberArcturian]]

  • Predominant Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]], [[/ancestry emberHulgrun]], [[/ancestry Kavir]], [[/ancestry emberKeth]], [[/ancestry emberFej]], [[/ancestry emberKiska]]

  • Languages: [[/language common]], [[/language arcden]]

  • Religion: Minimal

  • Governance: Otherhood of Fortune leads; various lieutenants manage aspects of city life

  • Architecture: Ancient Aediri, Modern Arcturian, and Ordani

  • Economy: Fishing, shipping, travel, smuggling

  • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{House Wandren}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune}

Landmarks - Tower Crags

The vast majority of the city exists in this upper district called the Tower Crags, and a mixture of residences, businesses, and the like.

The Ancient Tower Government Center

An ancient Aedir tower that serves as home of the city's watch, as well as its leadership and government offices.

The Cliffs Residential Area

A wealthy residential area built into the cliffs, overlooking Lower Seawall and Gray Harbor. Access is limited to a single bridge and a few lifts; its residents are the rich, connected, and influential.

The Rising Tide Inn Inn

Known for its comfortable rooms, fine food, and stunning views of the sea below.

Landmarks - Stone Haven

Directly below upper seawall, Stone Haven is partially built into the cliffs of the city, partially built on the water, and is the city's roughest neighborhood. In this part of the city the alleys are dark, hiding the worst elements of the city from the light of day.

The Old Door Inn Inn

A ratty building that offers cheap rooms and no questions asked.

The HolesInn

A series of artificial coves dug out of the cliff walls by the Aedir a millennia ago. From here, barges move cargo and people between Gray Harbor and Lower Seawall. The area also functions as a drydock for damaged ships in need of repair, and as a quiet place for more clandestine activities.

Landmarks - Gray Harbor

A sprawling dock caked with layers of long-dried sea salt, giving the district its name. This space is lined with warehouses and stores, providing a legitimate market and front for more illicit deals waiting to be made.

The Salted Anchor TavernTavern

A place for watered down drinks and shady business deals.

Merak's Trading OutpostTrading Hub

The central hub for all inbound and outbound oversea trade.

Life In Seawall

Culture

Seawall's people are a mix of smugglers, bandits, fences, and honest merchants united by a historic animosity toward the Trade Houses and the great city of Ordain. This shared distaste allows the masters of Seawall to keep attention focused outward, giving them cover for their own illegal and disruptive actions. This outward aggression also helps to mask the flow of bandits and raiders disguised as traders and merchants, as everyone knows that Seawall has no love for Ordain.

Economy

Since the rugged terrain surrounding the city forbids any possibility of agriculture, the city's survival relies on constant overland trade from nearby Nain and Molte, with more surreptitious dealings facilitated by its extensive, shadowy dock areas masked by a vigorous fishing industry.

Politics

Historically the city was overseen by a council of leaders that did their best to represent the needs of the various districts of the cities and their people. However this council was recently dissolved behind closed doors and replaced by a single charismatic leader and their inner circle of lackeys, sycophants, and lieutenants.

This change has rubbed many the wrong way, but little can be done about it without severe risk to life and limb, as the new leader is not as even-handed as the old council was. As a result, many have chosen the route of least resistance, keeping their head down and doing their work, though a few still fight back in their own ways.
Seawall.soverview: The rugged city of Seawall is a formidable port set opposite Ordain, and a haven for smugglers and pirates that can find no welcome docks across the bay. The city's fortifications make it an almost impregnable stronghold, well defended against sea and land.
Seawall.sexposition: Rising from the cliffs overlooking a rugged bay is the city of Seawall, its gray walls contrasting the warm tones of the Golden Flates. The great stone defense protect a teeming city of structures old and new, some Arcturian in style, some half-rebuilt ruins, and others ramshackle extensions of the former. At its heart, a spire of ancient stone from an era and people long gone.

Mythspire Observatory.name: Mythspire Observatory
Mythspire Observatory.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3195.2889 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands}, northeast of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberMythSpLower]{Mythspire Observatory - Lower} and @UUID[Scene.emberMythSpUpper]{Mythspire Observatory - Upper} area maps.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState chain1Guardian]].

Perched atop a harsh and barren mountain, the observatory ascent involves a treacherous path through rocky terrain, the air becoming biting and colder the higher one travels. Furious winds are a constant feature at this altitude, creating a desolate and awe-inspiring environment.

Environment

The mountains that hold this old ruin are inhospitable, difficult to traverse, and unwelcoming to interlopers, but do not significantly differ from the rest of the peaks in the region.

Ecology

The mountaintop is largely devoid of vegetation and wildlife, dominated instead by the winds and cold that hold sway. The harshness of the environment allows for little in the way of life to flourish here.

Lore

The Mythspire Observatory is an incredibly ancient structure, possibly the oldest structure the party will have encountered so far, built during the early days of the Age of Sunlight. It was a deeply significant site to Shent, and they carefully maintained and repaired it throughout their history. The Observatory was said to be one of the first places where Giants emerged above ground from the Pathways. Gazing at the cosmos, the moons and stars, for the first time, they marveled at the open skies, which they had never seen, and recorded their history in sprawling murals.

Throughout its long history during the Age of Sunlight, the Observatory was seen as both a historical and spiritual site. Shent would travel hundreds of miles across the Shana mountains to the north to reach the Observatory and mediate under its famous towering dome. It remained a significant location for them until the Shattering and the destruction of the Shent during the subsequent Abyssal Shear. Abandoned, left to the cruel, merciless winds and weather of the mountaintops, the observatory is now crumbling and ruined, a forgotten monument to Ember's grand history.
Mythspire Observatory.soverview: Atop the mountains far to the north lies the ruin of an observatory, though the truly ancient structure was once so more than that. The true depth of its history and what it meant to the people who built is lost to time, but even now its crumbling walls hold clues that those keen of eye and mind can discern.
Mythspire Observatory.sexposition:
The air grows colder and more biting as you approach, each breath a laborious effort, underscoring the observatory’s isolation and the daunting effort required to reach it. As you climb the treacherous path up the lonely mountain, the Mythspire Observatory comes into view, silhouetted against the sky.

The ancient structure is partially hewn from the living rock of the mountain, and masterfully cut pieces of stone, making it seem as though Ember itself helped form parts of the structure.

Despite its grandeur, the observatory appears crumbling and eroded, beaten down by the relentless winds that howl at this altitude. Its once-majestic dome now sits cracked open and crumbling. The surfaces of the stone are pitted and scarred by centuries of exposure to the elements.

Lake Orial.name: Lake Orial
Lake Orial.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3198.2916 in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.LcZ893eubbZrIOLX]{Redrak Fields}, northeast of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}.

Bookended by the Bloodwoods to the northwest and Redrak Fields to the southeast, Lake Orial is something of an oddity for the people who frequent its glittering purple waters. Although it sits at the edge of civilized territory, Orial is a place of copious natural riches maintained by a variety of Arcturians. While dredgers haul rich mud and silt from the lake, farmers work the fertile land, and fisherfolk cast their plentiful nets.

Environment

Lake Orial is fed by the waters of the Orial Tributary to the north and the Tarca River to the west, which are naturally enriched by the mineral-laden soil of the nearby Bloodwoods biome. Much like Lake Yrthain to the west, Lake Orial is the result of a synthesis between the primal growth of the Bloodwoods and the subtle sanctitude of Ember's waterways. These two woodland rivers constantly supply the lake with rich resources, making it a prosperous area for local settlers — and the key to the great productivity and prosperity of the entire @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.LcZ893eubbZrIOLX]{Redrak Fields} biome.

Ecology

Life around Lake Orial is not without its perils, rare though they may be. The proximity of the lake to the Bloodwoods means the occasional unplanned encounters with its strange lifeforms are a definite possibility for the otherwise peaceful settlers here. While incursions from Bloodwoods fauna like amerasps and bloodrunners are too frequent for comfort on the northwestern shores, domesticated animals like rask and yarnac also populate Orial's southern and eastern coasts. Meanwhile, Bloodwoods flora like redgrass and black aspens are abundant along the lake's northern perimeter, and give way to Redrak grassland the closer one gets to the southeast. Thanks to the industry here, fishing is not as abundant as it once was; but chordates like eels and mudfish can be found in constant supply.

Lore

The shores of Lake Orial are primarily inhabited by communities of hard-working Bejaki settlers. Daily life around the rural expanse of Lake Orial is difficult, but also cherished by the Kivahr, Keth, and others that call the land home. As such, the legends and lore of Lake Orial are infused with those of the Bejaki people. More than one sordid tale involving Trolls of the far north has been shared among storytellers who journey here, along with legends of odd cyptids that lurk among black aspen in the neighboring woods.
Lake Orial.soverview: Situated within the lush Redrak Fields but adjacent to the choking expanse of the Bloodwoods, Lake Orial is the Arctus Plateau's easternmost lake, marked by its tepid amethyst waters and the stark wilderness of the landscape that surrounds it. Orial is generous with its natural resources, which are harvested from the lake with regularity by local communities of rural workers and skilled laborers from Ordain to the south.
Lake Orial.sexposition: The amethyst-hued waters of this turbid lake are a sight to behold, and lightly scintillate with glittering particulate that seeps into the water from the rich circumjacent soil of the Bloodwoods. There is a proper sense of community here, despite the preternatural quality of the nearby wilderness, as evident in the signs of commerce that decorate the lake's southeastern shores.

Corpin Sanctuary.name: Corpin Sanctuary
Corpin Sanctuary.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3206.2893 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands}, west of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet]{Ordain}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberCorpinSanct]{Corpin Sanctuary} area map.

  • This location is heavily featured in [[/eventState cindaric1CorpinArrival]] and subsequent events.

Corpin Sanctuary features a quartet of connected buildings stacked upon the stony mountainside, the largest of which is a central rotunda marked by a massive cupola crowned with a sharp spire. Ruddy tiles cover the roofs of each edifice, with two chambers boasting open-air canopies — including the Entry Courtyard and the Meditation Pavillion. The structures here are all constructed from wood and a creamy white stone similar to the rock quarried in Ordain, although none of it bears the obvious hallmarks of magical reformation.

Environment

Built on rocky cliffs, access to the sanctuary involves traversing a large number of steps or specially built walkways. The location has a high vantage point with a stunning view of the surrounding land, but is perpetually struck by winds that make the outer areas especially blustery.

Ecology

The verdant gardens and foliage that decorate the interiors and exteriors of Corpin Sanctuary appear somewhat out of place amidst the stony mountainside terrain here; but those familiar with the Cindaric Sages and their connection to the Heart of Ember are unsurprised by the seemingly effortless proliferation of these otherwise dislocated plants, which include pink-petaled blush blossom tree and ample flowerbeds lined with an array of fruits, vegetables, herbs, and florets. Fauna here is somewhat sparse, with wild birds and rodents comprising the majority of wildlife. Meanwhile, domesticated animals like rask and birbs are always on hand, serving as faithful companions to the Sages who foster them.

Lore

Corpin Sanctuary was established in 2185 AS by an intrepid group of Ordani sages who sought a simpler place to practice their arts. Shortly after the Shard God Sigil's arrival in Ordain, a small enclave of Cindarics led by a sage named Janas Theed set out to find a new place of worship — one removed from the metropolitan clamor of city life. Their meditations eventually led them to the slopes of Mial Mountain, where careful construction of the Sanctuary took place over the course of two short years. In the decades that followed, Corpin Sanctuary steadily gained a favorable reputation as a safe haven for the Arctus Plateau's most lost and lonely citizens. Contact between Corpin Sanctuary and the Cindarin Temple in Ordain is constant, and sages are known to serve their faith for ample periods of time at both locations (based on the immediate needs of the Arcturian people and of the Order itself).
Corpin Sanctuary.soverview: This remote facility is home to an isolated enclave of Cindaric Sages, who — removed from the distraction of a bustling city and the chaos is brings — are able to cultivate their connection to the Heart of Ember in relative peace. Life at Corpin Sanctuary is simple and rustic, lacking most of the creature comforts of Ordain; yet, in these areas where the Sanctuary is lacking, one can instead find a serene and direct connection to the land itself. For some, this is all that's required.
Corpin Sanctuary.sexposition: A small complex of structures sits nestled in quiet isolation on the lower slopes of Mial Mountain, with a commanding view of the lands below and only the sound of empty skies around it. An aura of serenity blankets this remote location, where the harsh winds of the mountain slopes seemingly cannot reach.

Oldcraft Lodge.name: Oldcraft Lodge
Oldcraft Lodge.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3215.2882 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, on the eastern shore of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.Py8rh7u0Q5yFuuio]{Lake Jinro}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberOldcraftLod]{Oldcraft Lodge} area map.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState otherhood1Lodge]].

Only those who the Shard God Sigil mentors and trusts are allowed beyond the common areas of Oldcraft Lodge — as a result, the true size of its interior is unknown. Even the lodge's public spaces are hard to fully measure; they always appear to have just enough room for whoever is visiting, as if they are expanding and contracting to match the current number of guests.

While no one has been able to observe these changes when they occur, several researchers have confirmed differences in room sizes, orientations, and entrances over time. Some believe that these shifts are the result of the slight draft that runs through the halls, which has no clear origin point and has been known to blow papers across the room, scattering them in patterns that somehow reveal new insights to the scholars working on them.

Environment

The rooms of Oldcraft Lodge are lit by a soft warm light that resembles candlelight, but comes from no particular direction, as if the air itself was aglow. A slight breeze often drifts through the lodge with the sound of rustled pages and the faint smell of bound leather – some joke that it is the collected air from the sighs that Sigil sometimes lapses into while working, but no one knows its true origins.

Ecology

It is rumored that there is a greenhouse somewhere within the hidden arcane library, used for the study of herbalism and crafting, but no one has ever found it. Outside of this mythical room, Oldcraft Lodge is kept clear of anything that might threaten the books and knowledge inside of it, including insects and rodents.

Lore

Oldcraft Lodge was originally built for a trader, Jarith Imeron, as a second home outside of Ordain, but after their death it fell into disrepair. Sigil discovered the abandoned home while on a search for Jarith’s journals, which document some of the early days of Ordain, and remade it into the place it is today, using some of the power he holds as a Shard God to imbue the home with enough magic to hold more space and books than it otherwise would be able to.
Oldcraft Lodge.soverview: Oldcraft Lodge has long served as the home and library of Sigil, a Shard God committed to the pursuit of knowledge. Though it appears as a modest residence from the outside, it is rumored to contain a vast arcane library whose full extent only Sigil himself is truly aware of. Most visitors to Oldcraft Lodge never come close to seeing its entire interior. They typically work either in the communal spaces provided by Sigil or grounds outside.
Oldcraft Lodge.sexposition: A rustic single-story lodge sits on the banks of Lake Jinro, its grounds marked by the sweet scent of ripe berries and wild irises. While at first glance, its warm wood and lush grounds seem no different than those found at any other Arcturian waterfront home, the iridescent blue of its roof shifts colors ever so slightly each time as the light moves across it, and the faint sound of turning pages whispers on the breeze.

Bramble Gully.name: Bramble Gully
Bramble Gully.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3204.2898 within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.tuopdqO2JSeH1LeU]{Splinter Canyons}, south of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.qJlz7IOwWve46sLq]{Brevin}.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState canyonsSideGrowing]].

This small outcropping within the Splinter Canyons once held the only settlement within the biome — a small community of Thornlings known for their elaborate floral and plant displays — but it has since been abandoned, left behind after tremors in the area cracked the well that fed the community. In the years since, that water has run directly into the ground of the gully and the plants have grown lush and wild, providing food and shelter for a number of creatures in the area.

Environment

Bramble Gully is a small outcropping that forms a mini-plateau within the Splinter Canyons — while it, like much of the land against the side walls of the canyons, is somewhat shadowed, it is high up enough that it does receive some direct sunlight and rain from above, helping the plants in the area to thrive. Still, most of the water that feeds the area comes from the ruins of the well created by the Thornlings who once lived in the area, who are believed to have created channels that lead all the way down to the water source beneath the canyon's floor.

Ecology

Bramble Gully has one of the broadest varieties of plants in the Splinter Canyons, as many of the plants that were collected and tended by the Thornling community who lived in this area have continued to thrive and even intermix, creating new varieties not seen anywhere else. While the wild beauty of this gully is often admired from a distance, dangers abound for anyone who ventures close, as many creatures, and even some of the plants themselves, wait to prey on anyone who ventures within the tangle of plant life in the area, including gumtoads, sarracenias, and amerasp swarms. Despite these dangers, some ne'er-do-wells enjoy the area, as the cross-breeding of some of the flowers has led to the natural development of new potions, intoxicants, and poisons.

Lore

A small community of Thornlings, known for collecting and displaying colorful plants collected from across the Arctus Plateau and beyond, once lived in this small outcropping within the Splinter Canyons, using a hand-dug well to supply themselves and their crops with an abundant supply of water. When shifts in the land due to earthquakes cracked the well, the community similarly fractured and eventually abandoned the land. Many members resettled in nearby Brevin, but others scattered, joining communities from Helkas to Ordain. In their absence, the area has become overgrown with the far-flung plants favored by the community before their departure and remains one of the most colorful sections of the Splinter Canyons.
Bramble Gully.soverview: Nature has begun to reclaim this this small outcropping within the Splinter Canyons. Once it held a small community and likely thrived, but some event in its past rendered the location uninhabitable and it but now lays abandoned and half collapsed.
Bramble Gully.sexposition: Plants in reds, oranges, and yellows abound, their leaves and vines and flowers growing in and on and beside each other until it is difficult to tell where one plant ends and the next one begins. Though there are signs that houses or other buildings may have once existed here, they have long been overgrown, becoming part of the larger tangle of flower and leaf and stem.

Steed's Point.name: Steed's Point
Steed's Point.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This settlement exists at ⬢ s.3212.2898 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, southwest of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.NbPaM0jLKENCCQFQ]{Ordani Skywalk}.

  • This settlement can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberSteedsPoint]{Steed's Point} area map.

  • This settlement is featured in [[/eventState bookTalesSteedsPoint]] and @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM]{Thorny Predicaments}.

Steed's Point is named for its founder, Bertron Steed, an agrimage who moved from Nain to build a small village that would give him more opportunity to farm and experiment with his craft. Once a popular place for local trade and the swapping of agrimagical knowledge, the village was lost to a series of jurtak attacks. Today, the jurtak continue to fight over the ruins of Steed's Point with the seemingly endless flocks of gore birds hat famed agrimage Kali Andrella is rumored to have called to the village in a failed attempt at a final defense.

Environment

In its heyday, Steed's Point was a valuable stop for those crossing the Arctus Plateau due to its fertile fields, productive mill, and collection of oddities made by tinkerer and village founder Bertron Steed. Now, it lies in ruins. Most of its structures have been ruined either by Jurtak attacks or the ongoing battles between the Jurtak and Gore Birds in the area, and overgrown by hedges, vines, and thorns that are believed to be a reflection of the strong agrimagical resonance in the area.

Ecology

Steed's Point is dominated by three things: brambled hedges and vines that grow in, around, and over its central buildings; the jurtak who have set their sights on turning this into an aboveground shelter, and the gore birds that perch on the tops of those buildings that are not yet covered in thorns and vines, attacking the jurtak in large flocks when possible. Nothing else has been able to thrive or grow here since Steed's Point's fall.

Lore

After its founding by Bertron Steed, Steed's Point quickly became a small trading hub for other small settlements in the area looking for innovative items ranging from charmed seeds to enchanted equipment, drawn in by Bertron's piece de resistance, an impressive construct made of woven straw accented with metal parts, known as Rattletrap.

As knowledge of Steed's Point spread, it also became a place for agrimages outside of Redrak Fields' more formal Agrimage Consortium to learn and trade info, attracting those who liked to try new techniques and meld disciplines. It is rumored that Moss Ritherin got the idea for seed settlements after spending time in Steed's Point, and famed traveling agrimage Kali Andrella chose it as her place to settle down, becoming an adopted daughter of sorts to the aging Bertron.

This all changed after a series of earthquakes stranded a pack of jurtak in the area. Unable to return to their normal underground habitat after a tunnel collapse, the creatures targeted Steed's Point as a potential new shelter and attacked the village relentlessly. Kali Andrella rallied the town to fight back and await help, but the reinforcements she hoped for never came. In the final battle, Kali attempted to fend off the jurtak by calling down a wave of Gore Birds to attack on Steed's Point's behalf, but it was to no avail - Bertron died in the siege and the remaining villagers fled, leaving the gore birds and jurtak in a war to claim the lost village for their own that has been going on for at least the past decade.
Steed's Point.soverview: While this abandoned village is currently infested by the gore birds, jurtak, and other passing predators, this desolate and dangerous place could one day prove to be a welcome area of respite, learning, and trade once again, if only the creatures that prowl its ruins could be driven off and the dwellings that form the settlement salvaged and repaired.
Steed's Point.sexposition: The collection of buildings left in this overgrown field are all in varying stages of destruction and decay - here, a door has been ripped off of its hinges; there, a roof has caved in. Between the half-broken ruins and skeletal frames of what appear to have once been houses and barns, hedges grow everywhere. These massive brambles weave in and around each of the buildings, sprouting vines with thick spiky thorns like teeth, as if every available piece of unrestrained wildlife was trying to swallow what once lived here whole.

Storsa's Strand.name: Storsa's Strand
Storsa's Strand.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This settlement exists at ⬢ s.3205.2888 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CgqmvuJ1NLfqaO3I]{Rustvar Valleys}, on the western shore of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.JuuKQzqfLP4R33Dm]{Lake Mithra}.

  • This settlement is featured in [[/eventState fallAgainStrand]].

Storsa's Strand is a small fishing town on the western bank of Lake Mithra, known for its extravagant freshwater cuisine, bountiful exports of fish and fruit, and the strange tendency of its residents to drag curious treasures from the bottom of the lake. Sometimes, these treasures come with a small stroke of bad luck — a chance that many residents and visitors of Storsa's Strand are willing to take.

At a Glance

  • Settlement Type: Fishing hamlet

  • Size: Tiny (40 - 60)

  • Primary Cultures: [[/culture emberArcturian]]

  • Predominant Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]], [[/ancestry emberKivahr]]

  • Languages: [[/language common]], [[/language arcden]]

  • Religion: Cult of the Sun; worship of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}

  • Governance: Hamlet Elder

  • Architecture: Old Arcturian (with an emphasis on wood materials), featuring a large central dock on Lake Mithra

  • Economy: Fishing

  • Organizations: Cult of the Sun

Landmarks

Storsa's Strand is merely a small collection of old Arcturian homes and is located far enough away from the main route to Ordain to be isolated from most trade, but its position on the lake and reputation as an excellent source of both fish and fish stew does occasionally bring a trading caravan or traveling adventurer looking for a place to rest. The village includes:

The Far From HomeInn

An ale-soaked inn celebrated far and wide for the spicy flavors of their famous fish stew, which is served in edible bowls. Travelers from all about the continent talk about their visits here, with a select few celebrants and wayfarers who make their laketown visitations a habit. It is owned and operated by Chef Tama Tyne.

Storsa's ForgeSmithy

A smithy and equipment shop run by the descendants of Storsa herself, the Mondain Siblings, fueled by the primeval fires of an elemental fissure on the edge of town.

Kraddok's DockWharf

A solid timber wharf that once housed the infamous Qrag Kraddok, a cantankerous yet secretly well-meaning fisherman who had a knack for pulling some of the more interesting mysteries out of Lake Mithra. He has since vanished, leaving his daughter, Sielle Kraddok, to manage the wharf and his eclectic collection.

Lantyr ShrineShrine

A large, spherical shrine of overlapping bands of steel, forged by the Mondain Siblings in the elemental forge. Its hollow heart is filled with wood and set ablaze during the village's nightly rituals.

Characters of Interest

The Mondain SiblingsNeutral Good, Ordani Human, she/her & he/him

The Mondain Siblings — Cholni and Malcem — are the direct descendants of Storsa Mondain, for whom the village was named. Expert blacksmiths, they tend the elemental forge on the edge of town, but have rarely been seen since the village fell into its present gloom.

Chef Tama TyneChaotic Good, Ordani Vrjnhar, she/her

Chef Tama Tyne is the current proprietor of The Far From Home, and is constantly striving (but not often succeeding) in creating exotic fish dishes. Newcomers to Storsa's Strand are quickly warned never to order the "Tama Scramble."

Verdal FainLawful Good, Arcturian Human, they/them

This massive specimen of a Human may appear intimidating, but Verdal Fain is as gentle as they are large. Though dim, they are immensely kindhearted, quick to lend a hand whether it's delivering packages, pulling boats ashore, or testing their palette against Chef Tama Tyne's more interesting culinary experiments. Verdal is beloved by everyone in Storsa's Strand; outsiders who are unkind to them must make amends or leave.

Jak InsiterraLawful Neutral, Arcturian Fej, they/them

Jak Insiterra is an aspiring blacksmith, drawn to Storsa's Strand by the opportunity to smithy at its famous elemental forge. Unfortunately for them, the Mondain Siblings have grown reclusive as of late, and aren't entertaining visitors.

Sielle KraddokNeutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/her

Sielle Kraddok is the daughter of Qrag Kraddok, and the sudden (and unwilling) owner of Kraddok's Dock. Overwhelmed by the disappearance of her father, Sielle is struggling to manage her day-to-day responsibilities.

Kendral LowdLawful Good, Kivahr, he/him

Ex-adventurer and member of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}, he was once a devout follower of Spectra and a powerful wizard who traveled the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} with his family. With his daughter's death, son's disappearance, and wife's absence, he has put that time behind him and now spends his days fishing.

Nono CretzChaotic Good, Arcturian Human, she/her

Nono Cretz runs a secret Kingslayer card game for low stakes in the basement of her cozy split-level cottage home. She is more welcoming of outsiders than most but tries to size newcomers up before inviting them to her table, usually by challenging them to a quick game in The Far From Home.

Life in Storsa's Strand

Inhabited primarily by Human and Kivahr families who make their living farming and fishing, Storsa's Strand was once known as a welcoming place filled with happy people who loved to fish and relax. In recent years, however, something unsettling has crept over the hamlet; the people seem struck by a general sense of depression, making them more morose and glum. Most continue to do their best to stay cheerful, and their religious festivals of the sun are some of the few times when the old charm and cheerfulness of the settlement reveals itself once more.

Culture

Storsa's Strand is a beautiful, quaint, and seemingly undisturbed hamlet of Arcturian heritage and culture. Its people are generally friendly to outsiders, and they have maintained the same buildings since they were built hundreds of years ago, living peaceful lives for generations.

Religion in Storsa's Strand is fairly concentrated on Lantyr, with festivals, nightly rituals, and many different practices that involve light and fire. This ardent belief has become more intense in recent years among the people of the hamlet, who believe that their worship of Lantyr is the only thing holding back a more serious mental toll. A large central shrine, made of carefully woven metal strands, lies in the center of the village with a hollow core; it is often filled with wood, and a bonfire is lit during nightly rituals.

Defense

There are no military forces in the hamlet to speak of; the population is far too low. However, the Lowd Family has lived in the settlement for several generations and has often stepped in to solve local problems with aggressive animals or creatures when necessary. That protection has now faded away after Kendral Lowd retired and his two children went missing.

Politics

The small hamlet is completely self-governing, and while the people generally show deference to the older generations, no one in the settlement is technically in charge.

Lore

Storsa's Strand has stood for several hundred years and was named after the renowned Arcturian ranger Storsa Mondain, the celebrated traveler who first settled here following her decades of loyal service to Ordain's Trading Houses. Her original lodge was transformed into The Far From Home inn to preserve it. There are rumors that there may be artifacts from her days on the Arctus Plateau hidden somewhere in the house, though no one knows where.
Storsa's Strand.soverview: Storsa's Strand is a small fishing hamlet on the western bank of Lake Mithra, known for its freshwater cuisine, its bountiful exports of fish, and the strange nightly rituals to venerate the passing of Lantyr. The other peoples of the Arctus Plateau view Storsa's Strand residents as slightly odd, but they remain as friendly, open, and welcoming to outsiders as any other settlement you could find.
Storsa's Strand.sexposition: Ahead lies a quaint, peaceful fishing hamlet on the shores of Lake Mithra. Soft, muted sounds of village life drift upon the wind, and white smoke rises from among the scattered buildings. Fishermen and workers bustle about a large dock stretching out onto the water. Some seem to be preparing their boats, while others are offloading fish baskets onto small carts.

Vortest Tower.name: Vortest Tower
Vortest Tower.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3220.2891 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, west of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.X1FzWfTYfe7JfD3P]{Seawall}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberVortestTowe]{Vortest Tower} area map.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState bookTalesVortest]].

This lone tower is the remote dwelling and arcane workshop of the Signborn mage Corvana Vortest, an erstwhile purveyor of spells and oddities who lives a hermetic lifestyle near the eastern edge of the Golden Flats. The Vortest Homestead is open to visitors "by invitation only," and it is a rare occasion that lady Corvana issues such invitations willingly.

Environment

At a glance, Vortest Tower appears to be an 80-foot tall, 50-foot wide circular stone edifice with a single chamber located at its floor level. In reality, this circular antechamber serves as a method of otherworldly conveyance to a larger complex of eight separate chambers — all of which are located in a pocket of the shadow-haunted Inner Realm of Signara, and connected by a series of arcane bridges powered by esoteric magic.

The bone scarecrows that decorate the tower's exterior grounds on Ember are little more than slapdash wards meant to inspire fear and suggest the presence of some bleak entity or force of nature here. Simple illusion magics enhance this air of doom by supplementing Corvana Vortest's crude visuals with evocative sounds of softly-wailing despair.

Ecology

The gruesome effigies and illusion magics that persist here serve to keep visitors and wildlife away, but flora persists in abundance, as no one maintains the grounds with any regularity whatsoever; this neglect is so apparent, it borders on abandonment. Thus, Golden Flats vegetation like dawngrass and feverbloom are copious; and the only creatures to frequent the area include the occasional grassland rodents and avian raptors.

Lore

Vortest Tower was created by the Daemos Nalgomith many moons ago to serve as a dwelling and workshop for Corvana Vortest's great grandmother Eda Vortest, who was among the Daemos' most trusted of attachés. In the final days of the Forsaken War, House Vortest was charged with the protection of one of Nalgomith's most hallowed artifacts: a matrix of arcane knowledge known as the Orphic Reliquary. The creation of Vortest Tower has ultimately allowed House Vortest to hide the Reliquary far away from their enemies, while keeping it perpetually tethered to Nalgomith's otherworldly magic. And little do the citizens of the Golden Flats know, Corvana Vortest's isolated lifestyle is part of a clandestine effort to obscure her mysterious occupation: the ongoing protection of the Orphic Reliquary and the curation of its Signaran secrets.

Those bold enough to seek Corvana Vortest's spellcasting services have been met with silence in recent years, and it seems the Signborn mage isn't currently willing to offer her arts to the public. However, this silence is merely a prelude to the events of The Book of Tales, wherein characters may actually meet and aid Corvana Vortest in her cosmic task.
Vortest Tower.soverview: A lone tower situated on a remote stretch of land and surrounded by unsettling bone scarecrows, this location inspires fear and concern in any who venture to close, ensuring the structure never has more visitors than its occupant desires.
Vortest Tower.sexposition: An eighty-foot tall stone tower is perched upon the grassy hillside here, marked by a single fifteen-foot tall door to the southeast, crafted from some curious amethyst-hued alloy and adorned with bas-relief. An assortment of bone "scarecrows" surround the tower exterior, their sun-bleached skulls painted with esoteric symbols in blood and ichor. Meanwhile, the loosely cobbled path that leads up towards the southeastern gate is overgrown and riddled with neglect. As you take it all in, you swear you can almost hear the voices of all those skulls that loom within your view — their words are those of warning, and their songs are those of doom.

The Bleak Archive.name: The Bleak Archive
The Bleak Archive.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3194.2884 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands}, north of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberBleakArchiv]{The Bleak Archive} area map.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState brushWithDeathArchives]].

This uninviting edifice carved out of the mountainous Rustvar terrain is rumored to be an esoteric repository built by the ancient Shent giants. Few people of the region even know about the Bleak Archives or its whereabouts; thus, the remote timeworn vault sits here lonely and forgotten, its archaic contents unseen.

Environment

The Bleak Archive is carved into and out of ashen gray slate, which also comprises the craggy precipice that leads up to the vault's mist-shrouded entrance. The threshold is flanked by statues of two celestial hounds; and scattered cerulean moon blossoms decorate the ground here, lambent beneath the light of Ember's moons.

The interior consists of a false antechamber, a main gallery, an inner sanctum, and several corridors and smaller chambers that surround them. The gallery in particular was designed to serve as a "false tomb" to dissuade robbers and thieves who might plunder the location's infamous hoard, which actually lays locked behind a complex mechanism powered by revolving mirrors and arcane light. The Archive is also laden with a handful of traps and hazards installed by the Shent to punish would-be tomb robbers; meanwhile, the facility's true valuables lurk timelessly beyond the inner sanctum, which serves as the vault's most powerful containment area.

Ecology

The Bleak Archive was designed to act as a spiritual trap of sorts for the various artifacts, treasures, and trinkets contained therein — all of which have been polluted by Abyssal energies that predate the Shattering. It's quite difficult for living creatures to call this remote and forsaken place home.

The vault's main resident is a loathsome Varùn wraith named @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd]{Tethra Shùl}, who served in life as a devout warlock for an Abyssal Horror named Nethehepticas. Thanks to the power of an artifact known as the Stone Hand of Uroth, Tethra Shùl has also summoned undead minions to this place, quadrupedal creatures made of shadow known as @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithors}. Furthermore, an insidious @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendor} lurks within the northeastern study, eager to wreak havoc on unsuspecting interlopers; and a @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV]{Child of Sitheera} has made its home in the southeastern refectory, which is secretly exposed to the outside world via a small hole in the vault's exterior wall.

Lore

Known as Ebbok Zhùr by the ancient Shent artificers who built it prior to the Shattering, this trap-laden vault was originally constructed to contain a volatile repository of Abyssal artifacts and eldritch curiosities. Today, it covertly serves as the sepulchral lair of Tethra Shùl, who has made foul use of some of the Archive's most dreadful relics.

Tethra Shùl first came to the Bleak Archive in 5 AS, at the behest of otherworldly visions of Nethehepticas transmitted to her in fevered nightmares. A loyal cadre of five Varùn renegades came alongside her, but would perish in the Archive's trapped antechamber when the warlock sacrificed them to gain forbidden entry. Eager to solve the vault's riddle, Tethra Shùl was subsequently trapped alive within the Archive's inner sanctum, a prisoner of her own ambition.

In the face of death, the warlock made a bargain with her Abyssal master: she would serve Nethehepticas in perpetuity as an undying wraith, who would one day execute a clandestine and insidious plot. Meanwhile, the corpses of her minions spawned the eldritch curse known as the Bewilderment, which eventually spread to the residents of Skybrush after the fateful intrusion of Dereth Erekos. Centuries later, Tethra Shùl continues to weave her elaborate plans of chaos and murder from the confines of this ersatz tomb; and the remote settlement of Skybrush is the closest target of these malevolent schemes.
The Bleak Archive.soverview: This uninviting edifice cut out of the rugged terrain is remote and timeworn, its true purpose and origins subject of speculation and rumor for those precious few that even know of its existence. Only one thing is agreed upon: it was built by ancient folk far larger than typical humanoids, Shent giants.
The Bleak Archive.sexposition: Cerulean moon blossoms trail off into the crags of the Rustvar hinterlands ahead, where the signs of a strange and solitary edifice can be seen cut into the side of a mist-shrouded hill. A rough path winds its way up towards a small precipice, where you spy what could be a door or gate obscured within the mists.

Brevin.name: Brevin
Brevin.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This settlement exists at ⬢ s.3201.2898 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, north of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.FByC8hRZtRuAJgA8]{Bramble Gully}.

  • This location is visually depicted by @UUID[Scene.emberVistaBrevin]{Vista: Brevin}.

  • This location is featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM]{Thorny Predicaments} quest.

Brevin is one of the first of a new type of settlement known as “seed settlements." While the Arcturian druid Moss Ritherin, who pioneered this movement, often talks of having an entire city built from a single seed, Brevin is a smaller town, created by planting hundreds of them, each with its own part to play in the literal growth of the area. While Brevin sometimes appears to have been created somewhat haphazardly due to the overlapping natural materials, a closer look will find a delicate balance that allows for many different types of plant life to thrive and grow together.

At a Glance

  • Settlement Type: Seed settlement

  • Size: Small (200 - 300)

  • Primary Cultures: [[/culture emberArcturian]]

  • Predominant Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberThornling]], [[/ancestry emberKeth]], [[/ancestry emberHuman]]

  • Languages: [[/language common]], [[/language arcden]]

  • Religion: Slightly higher than average adherence to religious belief, with reverence for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.B987VijfeT6i9TEI]{Aythorn}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka} the most common, along with a few more recent worshippers of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta}

  • Governance: Council called the Central Branch

  • Architecture: Seed-grown buildings; smaller than average; each building has the ability to sprout additional rooms

  • Economy: Trade and tourism; the opening of the new Brevin bridge that spans the Splinter Canyons could grow the town into something larger and more prominent

  • Organizations: None yet; exploratory talks with Ordain Trading Houses forthcoming

After the events of Thorny Predicaments, if Aythorn blesses the settlement, skill checks within the settlement limits are made with advantage.

Landmarks - Moss

Brevin is centered on its Four Fountains, which sustain the local Thornlings, who draw most of their nourishment from drink. Though each fountain was shaped through the labor of Stonewalker Beetles and the planting of Hollow Reed piping, each of the Brevin fountains bears a unique aesthetic that shapes the quarter grown around it. Over time, each district adopted the name of its fountain as a colloquialism. One fountain stands at the very heart of Brevin, while the other three radiate outward, supporting clusters of homes and shops. Lighthearted debates about which of the fountains has the best water are common.

Moss FountainSustenance Fountain

This fountain stands at the very heart of Brevin, near the gathering area known as The Root. It appears simple, but has the largest variety of plants in its district — it is customary for visitors to scatter a few seeds around its base as a token of good luck.

The RootVillage Center

This large, trunk-like platform at Brevin's center serves as a communal gathering space. It is flanked by Moss Fountain, The Roost Inn, and a variety of merchant shops. To attract outside visitors, the buildings here have been enchanted to grow faster and larger than the average Brevin residence… and, as a consequence, more haphazardly.

Temi's TonicsPotion Shop

A pop-up shop that sells spices and spiced beverages. Owned and operated by the eponymous Temi.

The Seeds of FashionClothing & Armor Shop

The Seeds of Fashion is a clothing and armor shop that is pioneering "hand-grown clothing" that molds itself to the wearer. Its proprietors are Perri and Valein Anther.

The RoostInn

The Roost resembles a hollow tree with many windows, and is one of the few places that can easily accommodate travelers of all sizes due to its verticality. Triss Carpel, the Steward of Brevin, is often on hand to greet visitors here.

Landmarks - Bloomspray

Bloomspray FountainSustenance Fountain

This fountain is awash with colorful perennials. The district is home to decorative artisans and artists, drawn toward its bright foliage.

NectarTavern

A flower-themed bar in Bloomspray where all drinks are sipped from inside living flower glasses. Discounts are available for those who promise to plant the remnants of their cup in a location at least 10 miles from Brevin to help spread these floral varieties, and to those who bring a bloom from a Nectar Glass. The bar keeps a detailed map of where Nectar Glass flowers have been found in the Arctus Plateau, and can be a good place to learn local gossip.

Landmarks - Crossways

Crossways FountainSustenance Fountain

This fountain lies nearest to the Brevin Bridge and features complex lattice work at its base. Druidic architects tend this quarter, guiding and reinforcing Brevin's growth.

The Brevin Bridge(Eventual) Grass Bridge

A crowning feature of Brevin, this interwoven grass bridge has been trained to grow down into the Splinter Canyons and up to the other side. Once it reaches its destination, it will tighten into a permanent crossing, the first of its kind.

Landmarks - Riveril

Riveril FountainSustenance Fountain

This fountain is ringed by smaller cascading fountains, and is home to many of Brevin's original seeders. Some are anxious to found something larger and more ambitious, even if it means leaving Brevin unfinished.

Heart’s ClimbAythorn Shrine

A site of worship for Aythorn, consisting of an obelisk that has been fully consumed by vines and Heartmoss, making it climbable. A small hollow at the top can be used for rest and contemplation and is often thought to be a gift from the popular trickster god. While some climb to this perch, most worshippers spend their time at the sculpture's base, enjoying the way it casts shadows on the ground around it.

Notable Characters - Moss

TemiNeutral, Keth, she/her

Owner of Temi's Tonics. Her spice blends, which she claims are found nowhere else on the Arctus Plateau, are often showcased in food at The Roost. It is rumored that some of her spices, offered to select customers, have a variety of hallucinogenic, poisonous, or magical effects, but she staunchly denies this.

Perri & Valein AntherNeutral Good, Arcturian Thornling, she/her & he/him

This Thornling couple runs The Seeds of Fashion. Though eccentric, they are well-meaning and earnestly invested in the lives of their patrons. They've turned a blind eye to the misdeeds of their child, Carmin Anther, unwilling to believe that they've turned to a life of crime.

Notable Characters - Bloomways

@UUID[Actor.qW0lhTVZLQknOayq]{Carmin Anther}Chaotic Neutral, Arcturian Thornling, they/them

A ranger who has been influenced by the Otherhood of Fortune, Carmin Anther has secretly begun robbing travelers under the name "the Canyon Crawler." Son of Perri and Valein Anther, the brilliant but somewhat harried proprietors of clothing shop The Seeds of Fashion.

Notable Characters - Crossways

@UUID[Actor.AJuixWYxgoyEo3tf]{Triss Carpel}Neutral Good, Arcturian Thornling, she/her

The Steward of Brevin, elected by the people, who is attempting to grow Brevin's popularity in hopes of spreading the message that cities can be grown as easily as they can be built.

Notable Characters - Riveril

@UUID[Actor.hLvc42ruEEclRBCZ]{Edivel Sprout}Chaotic Good, Arcturian Thornling, they/them

An ambitious young wizard who seeks to be like the agrimage heroes they idolize. They will go to nearly any lengths to add a spell to their spell book.

Life in Brevin

Most of Brevin's residents are a group of Thornlings who left their previous home of Bramble Gully to build something new, and they share in a common ideal of communal effort. As they prepare for the unveiling of an ambitious hand-grown bridge stretching across the nearby Splinter Canyons, the community is now starting to grow beyond its original size and purpose — there are rumblings of disagreement between those who favor starting similar seed settlements elsewhere and those who want Brevin to grow into a major influence on the Arctus Plateau.

Culture

Like most Arcturians, Brevinites value hard work for mutual gain, but more often value effort over outcome. Many of the projects they work on will eventually die off when their season has ended, so they place less value on individual enduring objects than the average Acturian, focusing more on the cycle of life as a whole. Even the best tender of plants will have some that die due to weather or disease, and those living in Brevin believe that any difficulties in life are matters of circumstance that can be overcome with the support of those nearby, just as a sick plant might be staked to a healthier one as its roots regrow. Without the large multigenerational houses common elsewhere in the Arctus Plateau, Brevinites have created their own substitute — branches. These groupings of those with the same situation or outlook on life range in focus from the physical areas surrounding each of Brevin's fountains to groups that have aligned due to role or place in life, including parents, merchants, druids, the seeders who laid the groundwork for the town, and travelers who call Brevin home, but often spend long periods of time in Ordain or on the Arctus Plateau.

Defense

The seeds used to create Brevin were developed to be naturally repellant to dangerous local wildlife and many of its plants have natural defenses that can be triggered if the right substance is added into any of the local fountains, ranging from the ability of the grass to grab onto the feet of intruders to the large thorns hidden within many of Brevin’s vines. Despite creating these precautions, most in Brevin don’t think about them and generally feel they have nothing to fear. With their proximity to Ordain, even with its position on the other side of the Canyons, they feel generally protected, and occasionally reach out to the Veiled Chain if they stumble into anything that they aren't able to deal with. Even with the rising influence of the Otherhood of Fortune putting many on edge, there remains no organized militia or law enforcement group within the town — if worse comes to worst and something damages the place, Brevinites are sure they will be able to grow it again.

Politics

The politics of Brevin often resembles the intertwining vines found throughout the town — a central council known as the Central Branch consists of representatives of each of Brevin’s many branches. Though this can seem complex, Brevinites easily keep track of which branches they belong to and each resident is attached to at least 3 or 4 members of the council, ensuring that their voices are heard on local issues. Even amid growing philosophical conflict between those who want to create new versions of Brevin elsewhere and those who want to pour resources into making Brevin from a town into a thriving city, most residents belong to enough branches that they still remain connected to those they vehemently disagree with and can live harmoniously despite the conflict.
Brevin.soverview: Brevin is a "seed settlement," a place grown rather than built. Hundreds of natural and magically-enhanced seeds were planted, shaping the settlement from pliable wood, fast-growing grasses and vines, and tough interlacing roots. A recent addition to the Arctus Plateau, it is largely inhabited by Thornlings, who live comfortably in its undersized structures as the city slowly grows toward its full height.
Brevin.sexposition: The smell of fresh-tilled soil heralds the appearance of a knotted grove of stumpy, interlocked trees, their trunks vanishing into riotous hedges of color. Somewhere out of sight, a stream babbles. Only gradually does this mass of greenery resolve into the shape of a village: interwoven branches arch overhead, hedges stand as walls, and vines twist into signposts and doors. Small heads poke out from behind leaves and flowers, as if in greeting.

Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine.name: Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine
Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3214.2879 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, near the western shore of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.Py8rh7u0Q5yFuuio]{Lake Jinro}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberLakeJinro00]{Lake Jinro} area map.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState bookTalesMoonChild]].

This lonely lakeside island near the western shores of Lake Jinro is named after the archaic lunar shrine that sits upon its grassy hillside precipice. Dedicated to Ember's moons, the shrine was created by Arcturians who dwelled here many centuries ago, and its esoteric secrets have been lost to time.

Environment

This layered hill of sandstone and granite features a switchback path that winds its way towards the mound's grassy precipice, where the eponymous Lunar Shrine stands against time immemorial. Surrounded by the tranquil waters of Lake Jinro, the Lunar Shrine's island is a remote and solitary place, where remnants of civilization — like the shrine itself and a solemn beach strewn with rusty blades — are left to be forgotten.

Ecology

The remote nature of the Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine has resulted in a rather simple ecology, marked by sparse wildlife and natural overgrowth. A scattering of evergreen and deciduous trees dot the island's shaggy, shrub-dotted landscape, along with a covering of golden grass that grows bare near the water's edge. Wildlife here includes the varied fish and shellfish of Lake Jinro alongside avian species like kestrels and gulls, who visit the island to feed on the area's assorted fish and insects. Lately, the island has also become home to a Juvenile Garganthus, a brutal pathways predator that is most certainly out of place upon this otherwise tranquil isle.

Lore

The Lunar Shrine is is generally regarded as one of the Age of Discovery’s earliest innovations, and is said to have been created by an alliance of Arcturian druids and geomancers who sought to craft a powerful scrying tool for their cosmological rituals. Led by a soothsayer named Menodora Vhael, this alliance came to be known as the Selenic Order, and was regarded for nearly a century as one of the region’s most enigmatic if favorable organizations. Yet, whatever events caused the Shrine to be abandoned long ago are as mysterious as the inner workings of the landmark itself.

Beyond its historical context (or perhaps because of it), the Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine is purported to be a powerful spot for divinations and other rituals — particularly for those capable of weaving magic and transcending the mundane. A half dozen smaller altars line the path that winds its way upward to the island’s ascent, each of them keyed to one of Ember’s specific lunar bodies. Characters who offer the appropriate ritual elements or components at each shrine are granted a temporary cosmic boon, thanks to the potent Arcturian magic that lingers here.
Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine.soverview: A hallowed place revered by Arcturians of the Golden Flats and outlanders alike, the Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine endures as one of the region’s oldest landmarks.
Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine.sexposition: An air of ancient reverence lingers about this remote island, which appears overgrown and forgotten. From a blade-strewn beach to the southeast, a switchback path winds its way vertically, clockwise towards a 60-foot high precipice that towers over the waters edge. Some curious arrangement of weathered stone peeks out above the top of this hill, resolute against the ravages of time.

Shrouded Borehole.name: Shrouded Borehole
Shrouded Borehole.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3204.2888 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands}, outside of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]{Storsa's Strand}.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState fallAgainDescent]].

The borehole is a secret and well-hidden tunnel that winds its way down into the Pathways from the surface; very few are even aware of its existence. Its walls are jagged and sharp — passing through its tight gaps would require careful and slow maneuvering even under the best of circumstances, and traveling through the borehole is never the best of circumstances. Those who make their way through its narrow pathways find the passageway filled with a deep and unsettling darkness that begins to assault their mind. The horrifying sensation forces most to turn back. Those who continue experience greater and greater stress and intensity as they proceed through its depths, with voices, whispers, and snarls slowly flooding into their minds.

Environment

The sharp rocks of dark stone twist and appear almost carved as they snake around confusing bends and sudden drops in elevation. There are no life forms of any kind in the borehole, and it appears completely devoid of even dust and dirt. An intense and often screeching wind rushes through the tunnel, but it stops and starts in bursts, sounding to most like someone screaming in pain.

Ecology

There are no life forms, whether plant, animal, creature, or monster in the borehole. However, it could be said that the darkness within the borehole is alive, whether it is pooling unnaturally in recesses or converging into swirling, raging whirlwinds as the air moves swiftly through the passageway. The concentrated darkness is best avoided if possible, but often the tight space means that those who travel through the borehole's passageways have no choice but to pass directly through it. Those who do experience flashes of great pain, and deep gashes often appear on their bodies.

Lore

The borehole is so unusual in its shapes and path through Ember that it's hard to imagine that it was created by natural forces. Its origin may remain a mystery, but some believe hat it was created when an Abyssal Horror managed to claw its way out of the Pathways.
Shrouded Borehole.soverview: The Shrouded Borehole is a passageway down into the Pathways, located not far from the small hamlet of Storsa's Strand in the Arctus Plateau. It is extremely well hidden in a series of twisting canyons and gorges, and without knowledge of its existence, it's almost impossible to come across randomly.
Shrouded Borehole.sexposition: Among the rocky hillsides a small gorge cuts into the nearby stone ahead. The jagged walls rise steeply, and sunlight fails to penetrate through the narrow opening above, casting dark shadows along the ground that delvelop in a deep darkness the further you peer ahead. The air here feels thick with tension and you feel as if you are being watched.

Lake Argath.name: Lake Argath
Lake Argath.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3199.2876 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CgqmvuJ1NLfqaO3I]{Rustvar Valleys}, north of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.Py8rh7u0Q5yFuuio]{Lake Jinro}.

The tranquil waters of Lake Argath are fed by a small tributary that flows from the Wedgelands to the northeast, and act as the source for the River Vestus to the south, beyond the steep drop of an unnamed waterfall. Argath is a place known for its quietude as much as its vicinity to untamed wilderness, and — despite it lacking most hallmarks of civilization — is steeped in the legends and lore of yesteryear.

Environment

The environs of Lake Argath are remarkably clean, stirred by the constant flow of fresh mountain water that springs forth from the northeastern tributary, and siphoned off via the southern waterfall. The Wedgelands mountains that surround the valley where Lake Argath is situated invariably shield it from winds that would otherwise disturb the remote locale's cool and serene waters.

Ecology

Lake Argath's proximity to the mountainous hinterlands of the Wedgelands has resulted in a somewhat mixed ecology, marked by abundant wildlife and natural overgrowth. A scattering of evergreen and deciduous trees dot the lake's somewhat desolate perimeter, where the golden grass of the plains has given way to dustier footing, marked by gravel and brown rock. Wildlife here includes the varied fish and shellfish of Lake Argath alongside avian species like kestrels, gulls, hawks, and vultures. Indeed, thanks to the area's unbridled wilderness, the relationship between Argath's birds of prey and scavengers is quite a cooperative one. Meanwhile, mammalian creatures like wild rask and feral nothrin feed on the area's flora, while preyed upon by hinterland predators including crag lizards and abyss-warped beletors.

Lore

Adventurers and survivalists (along with those who can afford their professional employ) are known to journey to Lake Argath during their more whimsical and aimless excursions. However, the legends of the giants loom large over this area, where tall tales of Varùn folklore tend to become a memorable part of the visit. Such fireside narratives include the spooky ghost story known as "Old Tall Bones" and the whimsical legend known as "The Giantess and the Drake".
Lake Argath.soverview: Lake Argath is arguably the Plateau's most remote lake, and is known to sit beneath the shadow of the Wedgeland crags that surround all but its southern perimeter. This outlying body of water is a place where the majesty of the Rustvar Valleys and the primal wilderness of the Wedgelands meet, where echoes of the ancient giants run deep.
Lake Argath.sexposition: The waters of this large mountainside lake are noticeably calm, save for the frothing rapids near the top of a waterfall at the lake's southern edge. Scanning the horizon, you don't spot anything in the way of settlements or points of interest, just a lonely shore that meanders around the lake's leaf-shaped perimeter. Indeed, the lake is surrounded on nearly all sides by towering Wedgelands mountains, as if Ember itself sought to cradle this place in a furtive embrace.

Lake Jinro.name: Lake Jinro
Lake Jinro.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3215.2880 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, adjacent to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.sdIjbPRNIsJ3ApcU]{Oldcraft Lodge}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberLakeJinro00]{Lake Jinro} area map.

  • This location is heavily featured in [[/eventState bookTalesAwakens]] and subsequent events.

Formed in a basin from the River Vestus, Lake Jinro sits on the northern edge of the Arctus Canyon's westernmost reaches.
