The majestic tranquility of this place played no small role in the construction of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.sdIjbPRNIsJ3ApcU]{Oldcraft Lodge} on its eastern shores, and a scattering of farmsteads and rural holdings can be found by those exploring the rest of the lake's perimeter.

Environment

Lake Jinro is connected to the River Vestus to the north and south, and a small tributary runs from the westernmost edge of the lake into the hinterlands beyond. The environs of this massive lake reflect the majesty of the Golden Flats proper, from the tall grasses that surround Jinro's sandy perimeter, to the area's meandering weather patterns marked by windy sunshine and scattered precipitation. The surface of Lake Jinro is remarkably serene, and the locale is consequently a rather inviting one. Even during the hottest summers, the waters of Jinro remain cooler than air temperature — fed by a subterranean flow from one or more chasms that lurk unseen at the bottom of the lake.

Ecology

Lake Jinro's size and canyon-side placement provides for a marginally diverse array of flora and fauna. In addition to the rampant amber-hued grasses and shrubs of the Golden Flats that permeate the area, the lake's rural perimeter is decorated with a scattering of evergreen and deciduous trees made lush by Jinro's halcyon waters.

As one might imagine, Lake Jinro's placidity is a main attraction for regional wildlife, who can participate in the local ecosystem with aplomb. Fauna here includes varied fish and shellfish alongside avian species like kestrels and gulls, plus a variety of mammal wildlife like wild rask and feral nothrin. Deeper in the lake's depths, an impressive array of aquatic life can be found — with qualities curiously similar to those of the squamous creatures of the lightless Pathways.

Lore

Lake Jinro has a storied history for residents of the Golden Flats, who regard its tranquil waters and grassy shores with a healthy amount of reverence (as far as natural landmarks go). Much of this can simply be attributed to Jinro's natural majesty, while some of the esteem is due to the lake's prominence in legends and lore surrounding Oldcraft Lodge and its fabled assortment of occupants. Indeed, Lake Jinro has been the location of interest detailed in several Arcturian folk tales and creation myths, including the tall tale of "Nabb the Crab" and a sorcery myth from the Age of Sunlight known as "The Watery Graves of Phin Din'ae."

Furthermore, several narratives (both true and false) surround the source and function of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fHYfRhU3UKTc4HQl]{Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine}, which occupies a grass-strewn island near the center of the lake. Pilgrims and vacationers come from miles around to visit the island shrine, if only to gawk at it from the banal safety of the lake's far shores. And it goes without saying: stories about the lake's peculiar relationship to Oldcraft Lodge are never far from the tongue of any self-respecting Arcturian bard.
Lake Jinro.soverview: Lake Jinro, known for its calm fishing waters and the two small islands that dot its center, is the largest lake in the Golden Flats. Jinro is a source of pride and prosperity for the Arcturian people who frequent its shores, including the storied residents of Oldcraft Lodge and the countless fishermen who come and go with the tide.
Lake Jinro.sexposition: The halcyon waters of this large lake stretch across the Golden Flats for miles, stirred by the slow southward flow of water from the River Vestus. You spy two small islands near the northern mouth of the Vestus, one of them crowned with a wind-stepped hill. And even from the shore, you can tell the lake's water runs deep.

Lake Mithra.name: Lake Mithra
Lake Mithra.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3205.2890 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, adjacent to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]{Storsa's Strand}.

The waters of this lowland lake sway with the constant southern flow of the River Elenain, fed by two source tributaries in the mountains to the north. Lake Mithra stands as a bounteous signifier of Ember's preternatural abundance, and is regarded by some as one of the Arctus Plateau's most treasured natural resources.

Environment

While Lake Mithra embodies the dry summer climate of the rest of the Arctus Plateau, it also exhibits a range of unique environmental qualities that stem from the enchanted nature of the Lake's waters, which are infused with primordial energies that even the residents of nearby Storsa's Strand struggle to understand. Due to the humanoid population in the area, the environs here are relatively well kept, with less overgrowth than one might expect. The lake's perimeter is marked by a varying stretches of low sandy beaches and a surfeit of steep craggy overlooks.

Ecology

Lake Mithra is known far and wide for the extravagant freshwater cuisine harvested from its depths, and the intermittent arrangements of fruit trees that line its steep rocky shores. Despite the lake's relative compact size, it's an ecological cornucopia, one that provides ample resources for the region. Chief among these is the wide array of freshwater fish that populates the lake, from carp and trout to catfish and eels. Furthermore, avians and mammals can be seen lurking about Mithra's grassy circumference in steady supply, drawn here by the lake's generous natural food cycle.

Lore

Lake Mithra is celebrated as one of the Arctus Plateau's most curious sites of interest, and is known far and wide for the lightly enchanted nature of its waters — although the precise magical qualities of the lake are a source of contention. On top of Mithra's ecological abundance, locals have the odd tendency to drag curious treasures from the bottom of the lake. Sometimes, these treasures carry with them a small stroke of bad luck (a chance many residents and visitors of Lake Mithra are willing to take). No one quite knows how the magic of Lake Mithra functions or from whence it comes, but all are thankful for its confounding arcane bounties.
Lake Mithra.soverview: Among all of the Arctus Plateau's lakes, Lake Mithra is considered to be one of the most important bodies of water, particularly when it comes to the Plateau's quality of life. This synchrony is due in no small part to the thriving fishing industry that occupies the area, which operates out of countless lakeside homesteads and the docks of Storsa's Strand nearby.
Lake Mithra.sexposition: A diamond-shaped lake stretches out across the lowland valley here, sourced by a western river and two northern tributaries that appear to keep its tepid waters flowing with moderate gusto. If the fishermen and boats that dot the landscape here are any indication, this lake is a bountiful one for the locals. Lambent pyreflies skim the surface of the lake's constantly lapping waves; and before you can blink, a large carp jumps out of the water to swallow one the insects whole and lands back into the lake with a hearty splash.

Lake Yrthain.name: Lake Yrthain
Lake Yrthain.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3196.2908 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.TNPxd8ZlYQvJEXu6]{Bloodwoods}, north of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}.

Lake Yrthain comprises most of the expanse of the Tarca River, which flows from the Wedgeland mountains in the northwestern expanse of the Bloodwoods, and feeds a larger Lake Orial to the east. Yrthain is a cloistered place, choked by the oppressive growth of the biome’s tallest redgrass and oldest black aspens.

Environment

The environs of Lake Yrthain are rather unforgiving compared to the relative reachability of nearby Lake Orial. Here, deep within the Bloodwoods’ savage expanse, the soil is heartier and the stone is mightier. Weather in the local area is also subject to the primal whims of the biome, embodied by occasional fits of strong mountain gales from the north and the turbulent river rapids that result from them.

Ecology

Thanks to its relative sequestration, Lake Yrthain and the surrounding areas are a veritable crucible of preternatural Bloodwoods flora and fauna. Creatures like amerasps and bloodrunners frequent the lake’s overgrown shores, and the waters of the lake are inhabited by an array of freshwater fish and squamous amphibians — from benign catfish and carp to pernicious species of eels and daggerfish.

Lore

The legends that stem from Lake Yrthain are steeped in speculation and suspicion, and speak of dark supernatural forces that permeate the Bloodwoods themselves. One such tale is the legend of Ardan Vail, the story of a hunter who was drawn to Lake Yrthain by the alluring song of a Primordal enchantress. As the story goes, this otherworldly spellcaster fell to earth after her heart was broken by a powerful Casia, and seeks her revenge in the arms of countless unwitting lovers — who inevitably find their dooms at the center of the primal lake (like poor Ardan himself).
Lake Yrthain.soverview: Lake Yrthain is considered by many to be the “smaller sibling” of Lake Orial to the east, since the two bodies of water share so many characteristics along with their proximity to each other. But unlike Orial, Lake Yrthain stands as a testament to the primal nature of the area’s biome — all but cut-off from outsiders by the uncompromising foliage and fierce woodland hazards.
Lake Yrthain.sexposition: Surrounded by a vermillion expanse of obtrusive flora, this small lake is nestled between Wedgeland foothills and the unforgiving forested expanse of the Bloodwoods. The water that flows here is marked by its amethyst color and scintillating particulate, which roils ever-so-lightly within its tepid depths.

Aparon Bay.name: Aparon Bay
Aparon Bay.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3196.2898 on the northern coast of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet]{Arctus Plateau}, east of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.jL7yjWynI4u2ff2Z]{Mistwalk}.

Although it lacks any proper ports or docking stations, Aparon Bay has served as an important waterway for seafarers of the Arctus Plateau for centuries. The bay's perpetual fog and mountainous shelter make it a prime candidate for ships that need to lay low while navigating the northern coast of the Plateau. Some regard the area with suspicion, however, daunted by the oppressive nature of its atmospheric events — which often masquerade as supernatural phenomena or folklore made manifest.

Environment

The barometric pressure of Aparon Bay is constantly above average, caused by the ongoing clash of summery Wedgelands winds with the cold waters of the northern Reaver Ocean. The shores here mostly consist of the same rocky brown stone of the Wedgelands themselves, and the water is often less turbulent than one might expect — stilled by the incessant counterflow of deep ocean channels and the heavy fog-laden air.

Ecology

Moss growth is rampant among the rocky shores of Aparon Bay, but the relative lack of direct sunlight prevents saltwater flora like algae and kelp from blooming with much abundance. Coastal oceanic fish are plentiful, along with a variety of aqueous predators like sharks and sea snakes.

Lore

"Apparition Bay" earned its spectral nickname centuries ago when two naval vessels clashed off the northern coast — a pirate galley called The Havoc and an Imperial trireme known as the Leviathan's Tooth. The two ships disappeared in a magical conflagration when The Havoc's warmage let loose a powerful arcane blast, and it is said that any apparitions or figments of the imagination spotted here are the souls of those waylaid pirates and soldiers, who lurk in a metaphysical "otherworld" to this very day.
Aparon Bay.soverview: Colloquially known as "Apparition Bay" by the sailors and fishermen who frequent its fog-shrouded waters, Aparon Bay is regarded as a favorable waterway for pirates and smugglers, thanks to the incessant mist that coalesces near its rocky shores.
Aparon Bay.sexposition: The roily waters of this large bay are cloaked in a dense fog bank that obscures much of the area in a perpetual haze. Seaspray lines the rocky shores here, which are marked by impossibly step cliffs and promontories.

Dradley Grange.name: Dradley Grange
Dradley Grange.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3208.2885 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, southwest of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]{Storsa's Strand}.

  • This location is visually depicted by [Vista: Dradley Grange].

  • This location can be explored within the [Dradley Grange] area map(s).

  • This location is [heavily] featured in [[/eventState {Dradley Grange Event/Quest}]] [and subsequent events].

A former lava tube that descends into the dark stone around it, and has been transformed into a sunken stronghold of a group of witches who perform dark magic within. This location is almost impossible to spot as it sits nestled between rocks on the unforgiving and unwelcoming coast of a small island just east of Bura Island.

The current proprietor — a convivial homesteader named Egon Dradley — is known by equal measure for both his hospitality and his prowess with a flute; indeed, when the work day is done, the whimsical melody of Dradley's woodwind can oft be heard ambling throughout the tranquil holding.

Environment

Facilities of Dradley Grange include: the sprawling two-story farmhouse, a guest house with a half-dozen rooms for rent, four barns for locals and visitors alike, two stables, three fields, and a pear orchard that's stood here since the grange itself was founded.

Ecology

The crops and livestock cultivated at Dradley Grange are known to be as wholesome as the people who propagate them. Indeed, the residents of Dradley Grange are known for their exemplary hospitality and their respect for outsiders of all stripes.

Crops grown at the grange include tomatoes, lentils, and sugar cane; while livestock cultivated here primarily consists of cows, chickens, the goat-like nothrin, and domesticated rasks — who help to both tend the farm and curtail the chicanery of outsiders.

Lore

This rural farmstead was founded nearly a hundred years ago by Keleste and Bron Dradley, two young lovers from Ordain who sought a simpler, more holistic life than the one afforded them in the city. In the generations that have followed, their children and their children's children have kept the property and its sterling reputation in check.
Dradley Grange.soverview: Dradley Grange is a rural Arcturian farmstead that provides crops and livestock for various settlements of the Golden Flats. The grange also serves as an occasional rest stop for travelers of the Golden Way, who often find the rustic accoutrements of this place a warm welcome on their journeys to or from the metropolitan sprawl of Ordain.
Dradley Grange.sexposition: Nestled atop a wide grassland butte, this rural farmstead is walled in by sun-bleached timber fencing and a collection of weather-worn Arcturian buildings — including the large main farmhouse, a secondary edifice for guest lodging, and an assortment of ramshackle barns. The farm and fields appear well-tended, as if the cultivation of crops and livestock here occurs yearlong. You sense an air proudness to this quiet place, which smells of hearthfire, chrysanthemum, and hay.

Jekeroka Villa.name: Jekeroka Villa
Jekeroka Villa.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3214.2901 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, northeast of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.X1FzWfTYfe7JfD3P]{Seawall}.

  • This location can be explored within the @UUID[Scene.emberJekerokaVil]{Jekeroka Villa} area map.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState anachraenum1Villa]].

The site itself is relatively small, with only a few chambers adorned with remnants of ancient Aedir furniture slabs, mechanical apparatuses, and scrolls that have long since disintegrated into shells, crumbling at the slightest touch. Dust motes dance in the shafts of light that enter when the large entrance door is open, creating an ethereal, silent atmosphere. At the heart of the dig site lies a much larger central chamber, dominated by several large pools of elemental energy that bubble and boil quietly. Its properties have fascinated the Anachraenum for years, and no one is sure what exactly keeps the strange liquid active.

While the dig site is a common place for researchers, it has been designated for another purpose as the Anacrahem prepares to host the second Expedition Challenge. The dig site is also one of the locations where Anacharanum Trainees will face carefully constructed challenges and trials.

Environment

The Aedir Digsite is a lovingly preserved site by the Anachraenum. Most Aedir structures have been weathered and worn over the millennia, and many details have been lost, but as explorers enter the site, they are greeted by the sight of intricate patterns upon the walls and floors, and glyphs etched into the chambers’ geometric pillars, depicting scenes of arcane rituals and celestial alignments. The pale stone itself shimmers with a faint luminescence, hinting at the potent magic that once thrived here.

Ecology

The digsite is maintained by the Anacharenum as a place of study and research into the daily life and history of the Aedir Empire, but nothing lives within the chambers. The guild ensures the door is sealed with their own magic when no one is present, preserving everything within. Only the strong roots of trees snaking down from above have penetrated the structures and pressed through the ceiling and walls in some places.

Lore

The Anachraenum has determined that Jekeroka Villa was once the ancient home of the Aedir, one of the most powerful Magi of the Aedir Empire. He likely lived on the Arctus Plateau before the events of the Shattering. While this is true, the villa and Jekeroka lived roughly a thousand years before the Shattering itself. He sealed this location about three and a half thousand years ago before disappearing. Strangely, Jekeroka was somewhat of a scholar, historian, and explorer, which echoes the Anachraenum's goals. He collected and researched artifacts and cultures from history himself, such as the ancient Sedyri and Vaznor. He also pursued magical experimentation, and the elemental energy he produced and created is a strange mix of several cosmological concepts, still powered by a connection to distant and mysterious magical forces.
Jekeroka Villa.soverview: The Aedir Digsite, more commonly known as Jekeroka Villa, has been sealed for millennia and was only uncovered roughly ten years ago. It has been an active archaeological site ever since, carefully studied by many different scholars and researchers from the Anachraenum.
Jekeroka Villa.sexposition: Carefully tucked away on the side of a nearby cliff appears to be the entrance to a small cave or structure. Around the entrance, there are various boxes, crates, barrels, tools, and other objects. As you approach, you notice that the boxes are marked with a bladed compass symbol, and artifacts, such as pottery shards and stone pieces, are being stored and labeled with small tags.

Bramble Maze.name: Bramble Maze
Bramble Maze.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3202.2900 within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.tuopdqO2JSeH1LeU]{Splinter Canyons}, southeast of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.qJlz7IOwWve46sLq]{Brevin}.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState anachraenum1Brambles]].

The site itself is relatively small, and the maze grows within a small ravine that is mostly blocked at the surface, leaving only distant filtered light streaming down onto the brambles, which further block out the light even more. Navigation through the maze is possible, and a single route can be followed by using the natural markers in the brambles and flylight insects that call the maze home.

Environment

While the location is often visited by the Anachraenum, it is still an natural location and is not maintained permanently by the guild. Its path can change or adjust after one of the many flooding events that the Splinter Canyons experience, and even veteran Anachraenum members come to the maze to challenge their skills every few years.

Ecology

The predominant plant species in the maze are the extremely thick, often between two and five feet thick, tree-like barbed plants, which have evolved to thrive in the low-light conditions. The brambles are interspersed with vibrant glowing insects called Flylights, which have adapted to the dark by developing bioluminescence, creating a mesmerizing yet eerie atmosphere. Other plant life includes hardy mosses and fungi that cling to the damp surfaces. A few small, nocturnal creatures have adapted to the maze’s environment, using the dense thickets for camouflage and protection against predators. There may be occasional sightings of larger creatures that venture into the maze, but they are rare, as the thorns and brambles serve as a natural deterrent, limiting their movement.

Lore

Long before the Anachraenum discovered the maze, local Arcturian folklore spoke of it as a sacred site guarded by nature spirits known as the Bramble Wraiths. According to legend, these ethereal beings were tasked with protecting the delicate balance of the ecosystem. It is said that the Wraiths could manipulate the growth patterns of the brambles and thorns, reshaping the maze at will to trap those who would harm the land, while guiding those with pure intentions. Over the years, the Anachraenum have determined that this was likely an ancient tribe of Thornlings, possibly dating back nearly a thousand years. Nothing of their presence survives, as they likely built structures using purely natural materials, which explains the curious, maze-like structure that was probably grown to protect a hidden village at some point.
Bramble Maze.soverview: The Bramble Maze, which lies embedded into the walls of the Splinter Canyons outside Ordain, is a dark, labyrinthine natural structure discovered by the Anachraenum nearly a century ago. Its passages are mainly safe, with few creatures or dangerous entities inhabiting the location. However, exploring it is a different matter, as explorers can easily become lost among the thorns for days. The Anachraenum often uses the site as a testing ground for its trainees to assess their navigation skills and ability to remain calm under pressure.
Bramble Maze.sexposition: As you're moving through the canyons, you see in a small alcove in the rocks a twisting dark tunnel that seems to disappear into the earth. A few glowing insects, which seem to live among the massive brambles that make up the tunnel, and thick, tree-like, barbed plants. The entrance nearly impenetrable, and it would take hours, if not days, to simply cut your way through a small section.

Krator's Hall.name: Krator's Hall
Krator's Hall.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This location exists at ⬢ s.3197.2902 in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands}, northwest of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}.

  • This location is featured in [[/eventState anachraenum1Well]]

The Anachraenum came across this site several centuries ago, and it serves as a retreat and training location for Wayfinders within the guild. Traversing the depths of the Bloodwoods themselves can be extremely dangerous due to the many miles of twisting forest paths and the presence of overwhelming magical anomalies and effects. However, in this gorge, the Anachraenum found a secluded, self-contained area to train in an outdoor environment that was perfect for thier needs. In addition to the location itself, the Anachraenum also chose this site because of a strange object on the gorge's floor — a well of water with extremely mysterious properties they called the Well of Orbis.

The Well of Orbis is a striking feature just beyond the campsite, its surface shimmering with soft, white magical energy. Glowing stones encircle the well, casting light throughout the dark, shadow-filled gorge. The Anachraenum has studied it for many years, and interestingly, anyone trying to examine the well often encounters riddles and strange, puzzle-like challenges that appear in their minds at random. Sometimes, these provide new insights into their research or lead them to explore new places in the world. Most of the time, however, the riddles and puzzles are playful, nonsensical, or offer intriguing insights into the world.

Environment

Krators Hall is hidden deep within a mountain gorge, not far from the Bloodwoods, north of Ordain. It is exceptionally well concealed, and very few would be able to find it without being directed their or without a map or chart provided by the Anachraenum. For most of the year, the site is carefully locked up and left to the mercy of nature. Only during the Withering season do the Anachraenum members travel there as a kind of retreat and annual celebration event. It was also used previously during the first Expedition Challenge as a site that tested the mental resolve and problem-solving skills of the participants. It is likely that it will be used again in the upcoming second Expedition Challenge as well.

Ecology

The area of the gorge is very small, but it contains many of the same plants and trees present in the nearby Bloodwoods. Thankfully, however, apart from the Well of Orbis, there are no magical effects present within the environment here. There are also very few large creatures, and throughout the years, the Anachraenum has documented that most monsters and creatures tend to deliberately avoid the location.

Lore

The Anachraenum has studied the Well of Oribs for nearly two hundred years, but after all this time, they have little understanding of its true purpose or how it was created. It may not be connected to the moon of Orbis at all and is just a name that stuck.
Krator's Hall.soverview: The Anachraenum maintains a research site hidden deep within a gorge in the mountains north of Ordain. A series of tents, crafted from durable canvas, are pitched on the floor of the gorge itself, providing living quarters for the guild members. Only one large structure stands on the site: a lodge made of dark timber, surrounded by vines and standing two stories tall. This is Krator's Hall, where many Anachraenum members gather each year during the season of Withering. Located nearby is an extremely strange object that the Anachraenum have coined the Well of Orbis.
Krator's Hall.sexposition: As you make your way through the difficult mountain ridges and passes, you come across a deep gorge, surrounded by sharp-looking rocks and likely hidden in permanent shadows cast by the light of either the sun or moons passing overhead. Within the gorge, deep red foliage from the nearby Bloodwoods is abundant, and nestled among the plant life, a large wooden structure towers over the bushes and small trees.

Burial Grounds.name: Burial Grounds
Burial Grounds.text:
People of all faiths are laid to rest here in the Burial Grounds northeast of the city. However, most of Ordain’s citizens are ceremonially cremated in the cemetery’s subterranean magma pit (according to sacred Cindaric rites). If fate doesn’t choose for them, other citizens elect to leave their remains among the graveyard’s select repositories, from modest urns to elaborate mausoleums. Furthermore, a special cohort of priests from many different denominations maintains a sullen vigil here. These clerics also serve as lamplighters for the Burial Grounds — utilizing the rarest of inkaro pearls to stave off errant eldritch influences.

A sprawling subterranean complex beneath the crypt-strewn cemetery grounds houses an array of catacombs and vaults, the central magma pit, Cindaric ritual chambers, and a hallowed shrine to the Elder god Sockets.

Landmarks

Swiftbolt Spire

Near the center of the cemetery's haphazard sprawl, this venerated sentry tower houses a shrine to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc}, topped with a bow-wielding, silver-laced statue of the eponymous shard god. The entirety of the Burial Grounds can be seen from the Spire's lofty balcony, which also overlooks the whole city of Ordain to the southwest.

Foremother Fountain

This inviting shrine to the shard god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.LNFCxHtijBM7gh76]{Thoma} is marked by the purifying waters of a grand and holy fountain. Citizens who visit the Burial Grounds to honor the dead are known to stop by the fountain to make an offering, whether they worship "Grandmother Comfort" or not.

Eventide Hall

Marked by a shrine to the shard god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar}, the edifice known as Eventide Hall is a collection of grave-strewn courtyards and connected mausoleums that house the remains of celebrated warriors and hunters of Ordain. Several exquisite statues decorate the area, depicting scenes of legendary monster-slayers in mortal combat with terrible beasts and hulking leviathans.

The Cindaric Crematorium

This fortified subterranean facility houses various funerary chambers used for the ceremonial observance of deceased Ordani citizens, as well as the ritual preparation of their mortal remains for cremation. At the core of this facility, a deep magma pit known as the Heartblood Maw serves as the site for the final step of the Cindaric ceremony — when a fully-prepared cadaver is surrendered to Ember's fiery womb, so that their soul might travel freely to far-off Mort'oliss. Outside the Crematorium, various mausoleums and graves dot the uneven landscape, overgrown with the telltale crimson grass of the Redrak Fields.

Locals

Ruxandra Haeld (Lawful Neutral, Kiska Ordani, she/her)

This wily thirty-something cleric of Thayloc who maintains a majority of the evening vigils at Swiftbolt Spire. Like many adherents of the God of Ashes, Ruxandra can be a rather sullen and stoic individual when the situation calls for it; but a humorous spirit lurks at the core of her personality, which she tends to subvert in the name of duty and piety. Treat Ruxandra as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.PVD5wRdyO7iCJPs1]{Priest} with an expanded spell list.

Elder Jessos (Lawful Good, Human Ordani, he/him)

This stoic sage supervises the Cindaric acolytes who maintain the subterranean Cindaric Crematorium. A headstrong sellsword in his youth, the venerable Jessos has traded in his warring ways for the simple life of a Cindaric ritualist. Treat Elder Jessos as a @UUID[Actor.uIDDak2Oq8Qd9Mfx]{Cindaric Sage}.

Lamplighter Rabette (Chaotic Good, Kivahr + Aster Ordani, she/her)

The hairless Aster known as Rabette is a humorously droll devotee of Sockets who works as the cemetery’s senior lamplighter. Her uncommonly pale Kivahr skin shines with a dull glow like moonlight, which serves as a supernatural light source as she makes her way through the shadow-haunted corners of the Burial Grounds.

Lore

Ordain's Burial Grounds are perhaps steeped in more lore than the rest of the city, and rightfully so — considering the countless souls that are interred within, or who were surrendered to Ember's core via the Heartblood Maw. Some of the Arctus Plateau's most harrowing legends and ghost stories have roots or branches that stem from the Burial Grounds, where the histories of some of Ordain's most celebrated heroes and villains have been laid to rest along with their bones. Such tales include the legend of Qorahad the Cruel, an indomitable champion of the shard god Kuarta, whose remains were buried here in a fortified mausoleum long ago.
Burial Grounds.soverview: The colloquially-named Burial Grounds serve as Ordain’s largest cemetery, spanning nearly one mile from edge to edge. Located northeast of the city limits, the Burial Grounds endure as one of the most hallowed examples of Ordain’s intrinsic sense of community. Shrines to the shard gods Thoma, Theyloc, and Janar dot the landscape, and seem to keep watch over the cemetery’s aging masonry.
Burial Grounds.sexposition: This mile-wide cemetery is crowded with countless mausoleums and crypts, where the worldly remains of Ordain’s deceased linger for time immemorial. Near the center of the grounds, a tower crowned in a silver-laced statue of Thayloc attends this disordered but majestic sprawl. The air here is thick with reverence and gloom, and the dark hollows and low stairways of this awe-inspiring necropolis suggest the presence of a shadow-haunted catacomb beneath.

Cindarin Temple.name: Cindarin Temple
Cindarin Temple.text:
• District Type: Institutional

  • Population: 1,100 Inhabited solely by the Cindaric Sages and their allies).

  • Lifestyle: Monastic-but-Comfortable (Sages with means living in a lavish, historic temple).

  • Services: Spiritual guidance, healing, religious education and practice.

  • Influences: Built and maintained by the Cindaric Sages.

Visible from nearly any point in the city, the spired marble towers and red cupolae of Cindarin Temple are a venerated hallmark of the Ordain skyline, and serve as an inspiring sight for all who gaze upon their splendor. Only from up close can one truly regard the impressive details of this historical structure of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, featuring intricate embellishments, precise patterning, and uncanny stonework made possible through potent and artful magic. Huge slabs of stone — far too large and perfect to be quarried by hand — comprise the grand, sweeping lines and arches of this temple's countless walls, towers, and satellite structures. Each building stands as a testament to the measureless skill and cost that was surely required to erect it.

The multiple levels of the Cindarin Temple are spanned by grand stairways of precisely cut, time-worn stone. Each landing grants access to some section of the temple's services, archives, or the Cindaric Sages themselves. Each chamber and tower of this sprawling complex offers some specific service, or provides a dedicated space for a Cindaric ceremony or rite. Cindarin Temple is the tallest manmade structure in the city, rivaled only by the Ordinate to the west and the towering spires of Temple Ward to the north.

Landmarks

Emberhome

This large central spire serves as Cindarin Temple's primary sanctuary, and hosts a majority of the rites and ritual services that the Cindaric Sages participate in themselves (rather than the ones they conduct for the people of Ordain). Still, many of these services are open to the public — in the hopes that someday they'll grow curious or faithful enough to join the ranks of the Cindarics themselves. The massive curves of Emberhome's architecture are laid out in such a way that the voices and footsteps of the people within are reflected about every corner (making the entry hall often feel busier and more full than it actually is).

Cindarin Dormitories

Managed by the meddlesome caretaker Darrisa Sissos (Neutral Good, Human Ordani, she/her), the Cindarin Dormitories contain a variety of chambers that house the Cindaric Sages who dwell on the Temple grounds (which actually comprise most of the Cindaric Sages who live in Ordain). Treat Darrisa Sissos as a @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherent}.

Higher levels of the Dormitories house the organization's leaders; and a few of these chambers were constructed with sonic amplification of other chambers in mind, so that the inhabitants might be able to surreptitiously listen in on activity in the Temple's lower areas. But the truth of this particular detail is a rumor of perpetual discussion by Cindaric Sages and temple visitors alike.

The Murmuring Well

This stone well built in the rear garden north of Emberhome doesn't draw water, but is actually said to be a conduit that reaches all the way down to the burning heart of Ember, with voices of Ordani ancestors occasionally rising from below. By all accounts, it is a bottomless pit; indeed, no one (including many of the Cindaric Sages themselves) seems to know precisely how far the well reaches or where it terminates. Only the most senior of Sages understands the truth: powerful spells were cast upon the bottom of the well long ago to both mimic the behavior of a "bottomless" chute and emit the phantom sounds of Ordani voices — but things cast into the well are merely annihilated by the old magic, and the voices are simply an assortment of Cindaric tenets. Nevertheless, the Murmuring Well is venerated as a place of reflection, longing, and remorse.

Locals

@UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} (Lawful Good, Signborn Ordani, she/her)

Also known as the "Second Sage," the affable Signborn known as Lilla Arien serves as the "Keeper of Sages" at Cindarin Temple. This high-ranking position is tasked with overseeing the room, board, and wellbeing of all other sages in the order — duties which Lilla carries out with great respect and dedication, through good times and bad.

@UUID[Actor.KQ9uGdZu6zDlM66n]{Jon Vastil} (Lawful Good, Human Ordani, he/him)

Jon Vastil is the Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages, and has guided the order from a position of leeadership for nearly 75 years. Ancient in age and infirm of health, the once-commendable Vastil has faced growing criticism in recent years for a perceived lack of compassion towards the commonfolk and the city's mounting problems. An obsession with humanity's spiritual connection to the Heart of Ember is said to guide this aged leader, who battles a curious illness without cause or cure.

@UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith} (Lawful Good, Human + Kivahr Ordani, he/him)

Vinarith is the Steward of the Holy Speaker within the Cindaric order, the right hand to the highest office of the Cindaric Sages. With the Holy Speaker having fallen ill, he now shoulders many responsibilities of leadership alongside Keeper @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien}.

Lore

When it was constructed during Ordain's formative days by the very first Cindaric Sages under Speaker Adonia, Cindarin Temple was built to literally amplify the voices of the faithful. Indeed, the exquisite stonework of the Temple structures has been crafted to connect and inspire its occupants via sound; chambers built for sonic resonance or suppression, indirect conduits for remote communication, and grand recital halls serve as a testament to this philosophical legacy. And while this curious feature has its detractors, many adherents believe it accurately represents the cacophony of life on Ember (and is thusly close enough to the architect's original artistic and philosophical intents).
Cindarin Temple.soverview:
One of the oldest structures in Ordain, Cindarin Temple endures as the headquarters and beating heart of the Cindaric faith. Home to the Arcus Plateau's hundreds of famed Sages, this one of a kind edifice not only serves as the base of the Cindaric Order's power, where Sages toil in humble service to the Heart of Ember and the city of Ordain itself; indeed, most people who aspire to join the Cindaric faith or serve its goals wind up dwelling here within the Temple's ornate and hallowed walls.

The Temple grounds bustle with activity at every hour of the day; faithful citizens of Ordain come and go as they need, the Sages themselves tend to their duties of healing and counseling, and warriors of the Burnished Hand patrol the area in stoic observation.
Cindarin Temple.sexposition:
A titanic edifice of white stone with an enormous central spire crowned in a red-roofed cupola dominates this eastern district, which stands high above the entire city of Ordain. This monumental temple and its surrounding towers offer viewers an imposing yet tranquil sight. A great golden icon sits atop the temple's highest spire: a four-leafed diamond enclosed in a circle, the familiar emblem of the Cindaric Sages. This symbol shines brightly with the reflected light of Lantyr during the hours of dusk and dawn, marking each day's end and beginning for citizens throughout the restless city.

Here and there, you spot various people of Ordain going about their business — including faithful citizens who've come here in search of aid, the Cindaric Sages who serve them with humility, and a few soldiers of the Burnished Hand who appear to protect this most sacred of Ordani institutions. There's no mistaking it: the sense of community here seems as hallowed as the edifice itself.

Temple Ward.name: Temple Ward
Temple Ward.text:
• District Type: Institutional

  • Population: 1,012 (Low. Grand temples and religious institutions with heavy foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Respectable (Priests, acolytes, and followers of various faiths).

  • Services: Spiritual guidance, healing, religious education and practice.

The primary feature of this monumental district is a temple to the Elder God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}. Also known as the Graveflame Sanctuary, this edifice is recognized by its impressive gothic architecture and its eponymous flames — magical fires that burn with an eerie, spectral light. The grand front entrance of this primary temple is a sight to behold as well, yawning upon the city like some tenebrous maw. Meanwhile, dormitories for local priests and smaller temples that service other gods can be found lining the streets that surround the Sanctuary; and all are invited to participate in the Deathless god's ceremonies, regardless of their religion or past.

A temple to the sun goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} dominates the eastern corner of the district, a regal building marked with elaborate gilded runes that tell stories of "the Energy Moon" and her many triumphs via a palimpsest of ancient languages. And to the south, a large temple that honors the triumvirate of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka} stands in defiant simplicity compared to the rest of the district; this obelisk-shaped structure allows adherents of all three faiths to worship in proximity to one another.

The inkaro lanterns that light this hallowed neighborhood are distinguished by their pale purple light, which casts a gloomy and surrealistic tint upon the district's lurid stone buildings. Temple Ward is a solemn place, accompanied by a small citizenship of faithful priests and curates, along with the ambient sounds of sullen Ordani bards performing the Arctus Plateau’s most inspired dirges.

Landmarks

Temple of Sockets

This bastion stands proudly as Temple Ward's largest sanctum, marked by an impressive shrine to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} known as Graveflame Sanctuary — where braziers of magical flame burn eternal with a pale white light, and a magnificent statue of Sockets himself overlooks the solemn central chamber. The absent-minded @UUID[Actor.UEN4Lxa3qDqOAS5B]{Conaris Haid} serves as the Temple's High Priest, and is attended during most daylight hours by a small envoy of priests and acolytes who are eager to learn from him.

The Keeper's Ossuary

This hallowed crypt beneath the Temple of Sockets houses the worldly remains of some of the most venerated of the Elder God’s priests and champions. Protection and maintenance of the Ossuary has become a rite of passage for fledgling acolytes of the Temple, who must learn their rotes beneath the timeless gaze of their forerunners. Meanwhile, a series of secret passages connect various chambers and corridors of the crypt to unseen places, unbeknownst to all but Conaris Haid and his most trusted acolytes.

Remira's Bower

This huge public gazebo is crafted from the same pale white stone that defines most of Temple Ward, but is crowded in a notable overgrowth of budding vines and flowering brambles tinged with otherworldly glamor. Beneath this kaleidoscopic bloom, the stonework is adorned with romantic depictions of Primordis. Blessed by the obscure shard god Remira, this restful place is known to bestow divine boons on those who are willing to pay homage to the love goddess beneath its stony eaves.

Locals

@UUID[Actor.UEN4Lxa3qDqOAS5B]{Conaris Haid} (Neutral Good, Human Ordani, he/him)

This brilliant and eccentric philosopher serves as the High Priest of the Temple of Sockets in Ordain; and though he wears the guise of an affable, absent-minded codger in public, this expertly studied and accomplished cleric is one of the Arctus Plateau’s most trusted sources of information on Ember’s mysterious cycle of souls.

Yasmora Zaban (Neutral Good, Human Maziran, she/her)

Yasmora is the wry-witted keeper of the titular fires of Graveflame Sanctuary inside the Temple of Sockets. She takes her duties seriously, but is always ready to mete out a certain measure of gallows humor and good nature. Treat Yasmora as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.PVD5wRdyO7iCJPs1]{Priest}.

Merida Helestian (Chaotic Good, Human + Kivahr Cascilian, she/her)

A cleric of the wind goddess, this humorless priest serves as the keeper of Vekalla's sanctuary alongside allied adherents of Katu and Raineke. Although she can be uncomfortably earnest, Merida nevertheless remains a trusted advisor for the restless hearts and wayward sailors that are known to seek haven here. Treat Merida Helestian as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.PVD5wRdyO7iCJPs1]{Priest}.

Lore

Tellers of tall tales speak of how Sockets himself raised the stone towers of Graveflame Sanctuary from the cobbled streets of Ordain with his own divine inspiration — and these tales are mostly true. However, the godly will of Sockets was actually summoned to this corner of the city by his faithful worshippers, who originally erected a smaller, humbler shrine where the Temple of Sockets now stands. One of Conaris Haid's predecessors — an Arcturian Aster named Dorina Mariu — put part of her very soul into the creation of this shrine, and her selflessness was rewarded. To this day, some say they can hear the wise voice of the incorporeal priestess as they wander the amethyst light of Temple Ward's hallowed streets.
Temple Ward.soverview: The mile-wide expanse of Temple Ward is comprised of a variety of smaller structures that surround a massive central edifice known as Graveflame Sanctuary, where the devotees of the elder god Sockets practice their honored religion. And while the Keeper of Souls is the most celebrated of gods found in Temple Ward, he isn't the only member of the Arctus Plateau's pantheon to take up space here. Smaller temples and shrines to various other gods are scattered around the district's outlying areas, which tend to be more inviting for casual worshippers — if only for their lack of pomp, circumstance, and macabre architecture.
Temple Ward.sexposition: A grand municipal complex made of immaculate pale stone dominates this district of Ordain, marked by the presence of several places of worship. A large temple to the northwest stands out from the other structures nearby, a magnificent sanctuary decorated with portentous spires and flues crowned in ghostly flame. To the south, another large edifice stands proudly above the area, resembling an obelisk-shaped tower. And a temple decorated with gilded diagrams lies to the east, crowned with a bright golden orb. Here and there, you spy various robed figures clad in the telltale garments of religious devotees, who go about their local business with solemn reverence.

Assembly Hills.name: Assembly Hills
Assembly Hills.text:
• District Type: Institutional with some Commercial

  • Population: 1,098 (Low. Civil workers and bureaucrats, with moderate foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Comfortable-to-Wealthy (Civil servants and bureaucrats).

  • Services: Accounting and exchanges, deeds and titles, public records, legal services.

Built among the spires east of Spellbreaker Tower, Assembly Hills is a testament to classical Ordani architecture, and its majestic stone edifices should stand as enduring monuments for countless ages to come. These large, exalted buildings include public places like Commerce Hall and the Spiretop Commons, along with more restricted locations including Precept Hall and the various Trading House offices.

Ultimately, Assembly Hills serves the people of Ordain as the go-to district for all matters of a legally commercial nature. Lawmaking is not really proposed, passed, or carried out here in Assembly Hills, but this is certainly where much of the legislature of institutions like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows} begins. As they say: "a word-on-the-street in Assembly Hills is worth a hundred words elsewhere."

Landmarks

Commerce Hall

This large edifice serves as the central meeting place for Ordain's Trading Houses, and is dominated by a large meeting chamber surrounded by a variety of smaller offices (collectively known as The Stations). Trading House representatives congregate within Commerce Hall at least once a week to discuss region-wide issues and initiatives. Meanwhile, the Stations cater to the specialized needs and endeavors each of Ordain’s esteemed Trading Houses. Station Bastilla caters to the commerce of sea trade and arcane objects, Station Cevher focuses on the trade of ores and metals, Station Wandren maintains a catalogue of their luxury goods and services, Station Lilifeld is a source for all things agriculture in Ordain, and Station Salva facilitates the commerce of Ordani arts and entertainment.

Chamber of Records

This secure repository contains countless ledgers and tomes that detail an extensive history of Ordain’s civil and municipal information. Records here range from business registrations and trade deals to marriages, birth records, and an elaborate scholastic account of Ordain’s storied past. A network of secret passages below the Hall of Records is connected to similar chambers beneath Spiretop Commons, but only the Hall's attendants and a select few know about these covert tunnels.

Precept Hall

This municipal building hosts an elaborate archive of Ordain’s historical and modern legal codes, along with a small garrison of bailiffs and magistrates employed by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate}. Precept Hall is regarded by most Ordani citizens as a rather stodgy place, rife with the petty-yet-necessary evils of civic administration and sociopolitical red tape.

Spiretop Commons

The edifice known as Spiretop Commons serves Ordain as a public assembly house, with multiple meeting spaces and a large central plaza for special events and high-profile arbitrations. Every kind of public activity from legal hearings to secular marriages has been carried out on the steps of Spiretop Commons — a place truly deserving of its moniker.

Locals

Breccia Cobblestone (NG, Ordani Hulg'run, she/they)

Bookish and obsequious by nature, Breccia Cobblestone works as the primary front desk clerk at the Hall of Records, a job she takes quite seriously. A trashy romance novel is the way to Breccia's heart, which beats with hidden passion and wanderlust. Treat Breccia Cobblestone as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.SqZRuJ8lt2KGJBbq]{Commoner}.

Calahad Prinn (LN, Ordani Human, he/him)

This aged Ordani bookeeper is the stern but fatherly administrator of Precept Hall. The various staff members employed at Precept Hall regard the sixty-something widower with a great measure of genuine respect, and Calahad holds that esteem in high regard. But he also carries a troubling secret: his brother-in-law is a high-ranking member of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune}, a fact that privately haunts him to this very day. Treat Calahad Prinn as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.GlaCGcgIP6YjBjGc]{Noble}.

Evela Farfeld (CG, Arcturian Human, she/her)

A duly-initiated member of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{House Lilifeld}, the sagacious and comely Evala Farfeld serves as the Head Trading House Liaison at The Stations, where she assists each of Ordain's Trading Houses with their respective mercantile needs. Before she settled down in Ordain in her early forties, Evela adventured throughout the Plateau as an agent of fortune — and is known by many both far and wide as a reliable information broker. Treat Evela Farfeld as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.13K3XK2A3wwxVKLD]{Spy}.

Lore

The overt municipal nature of Assembly Hills means it is a place of commerce more than cultural activity, so narratives that surround the district tend to reflect the practical problems of the people of Ordain. Assembly Hills is less rich in its own local history, particularly given its relatively recent construction near the western perimeter of the city, but it is most certainly a place where rumors can often carry more weight than gold. When gathering rumors in Assembly Hills, it's not altogether uncommon to uncover a lot more about the city than one's expecting, along with poignant details about the latest trade disputes or transcontinental gossip.
Assembly Hills.soverview: The municipal sprawl of markets, record halls, and public buildings known as Assembly Hills is one of Ordain’s most respected neighborhoods, and caters to a wide range of the city’s inhabitants — from nameless Arcturian scholars to esteemed Trading House administrators. Assembly Hills stands as a testament to Ordain’s inherent sense of community and is a crucial component to the city’s democratic machinations. If there's a communal or neigbhorhood-spanning issue to be solved, Assembly Hills is most likely the place to do it.
Assembly Hills.sexposition: An array of majestic stone markets, meeting halls, and public offices occupy this hilltop neighborhood overlooking western Ordain. A large central structure appears to host a common plaza for the city's people, while other buildings are clearly marked with the various insignias of Ordain's illustrious Trading Houses. Ordani citizens of all stripes come and go in this active city square, where the locally-appointed municipalities of the great Arcturian metropolis have gathered in one convenient place.

The Hallows.name: The Hallows
The Hallows.text:
• District Type: Institutional and Residential

  • Population: 18,130 (High. Crowds come and go from dusk till well after dark; busiest during the day. Only a few caretakers and officials keep quarters within the halls. However, extensive housing around the central plazas are home to thousands.)

  • Lifestyle: Mixed. (While central gathering areas see many lobbyists, barristers, and magistrates, all of Ordain flows through here.)

  • Services: Mediation, public forums, theaters, guidance for civil affairs.

Here, columns of old Arcturian stone quarried centuries ago meet the new lines of modern Ordani aesthetic, with seams between these architectural movements masked or accented by ever-changing murals contributed by local artists. This bombast of color and pattern creates a visual chaos that somehow binds the ever shifting face of the Hallows into a recognizable if not cohesive identity. While the Hallows remains an architectural tangle, its disparate facades speak to a city ever in negotiation with itself, and a people determined to honor the outcome of that tradition.

Culture

The Hallows is a district of social and judicial tumult, where law and order are executed in the light of Lantyr for all to see, as much a performance as an affirmation that the systems of the Ordinate work and can be trusted.

Meetings are public; celebrations spring up around verdicts and reconciliations, and debates over current events rage like forest fires across the district, sometimes smoldering for days, never fully leaving the public discourse. Here, anyone may find a soapbox in Speaker’s Square, or a moment to shine in Songhall Theater.

Landmarks

Songhall Theater

This grand, multi-storied theater hosts an array of performances and panels, with a ground floor dedicated to showcasing the upcoming month's events and handling admission to the numerous stages and theaters held on higher levels. While most events are free to the public, it is not uncommon to find private and paid performances as well.

Speaker's Square

The open and cacophonous heart of the Hallows where the court of public opinion is held with no regard for order or ceremony. Its pale flagstones have been worn smooth by centuries of foot traffic as crowds shift around orators, singers, and passionate citizens making their presence known. It is said that you can hear a hundred opinions and witness half as many arguments just by walking from one end to the other.

The Scales

A venerable structure and vital institution in the city, the Scales is a building wholly dedicated to resolving disputes across the city, whether that is issue of business deals gone awry, crimes committed, or arguments unresolved. The councilors that roost here offer unbiased mediation for minor issues, while teams of barristers and magistrates wait on higher floors to address more major matters worthy of the courts and inspectors.

The Underfoot

A maze of stone corridors beneath the Hallows known to be older than the city itself, but with origins few fully known. Lantern-lit, signposted, and open by decree, the Underfoot serves as a shortcut for those in the know. Rumors abound of hidden chambers, forgotten passages, and hushed conspiracies away from the prying eyes above.

Locals

Marnis Vell (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

A senior magistrate of the Scales, Marnis is revered for his calm voice and tireless impartiality. He often lingers in Speaker's Square to engage locals in debate, and educate those needing to know the finer points of Ordani law.

Lisarra Pell (Neutral, Ordani Ashka, she/her)

A prominent and celebrated muralist whose artworks have become a signature feature of the Hallows’ walls in recent years. Lisarra is well known for creating sprawling pieces that she adds to over time to represent recent events, court rulings, or cultural movements that captured the minds of Ordain.

Jastor Riven (Chaotic Good, Ordani Altyran, they/them)

An outspoken advocate and barrister known for energetic speeches in Speaker’s Square and scrappy efforts to fight economic corruption in the city. Jastor only accepts clients they believe are in the right, and is notoriously happy to fight the Trading Houses in court if given a chance.

Zalend Ark (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

A no-nonsense city inspector that haunts the archives of The Scales, looking for inspection records that are out of date. He considers that pursuit of law and order to be the most noble of tasks, but has become a thorn in the side of local merchants and builders who aren't fastidious about their paperwork.

Lore

The Hallows is not the oldest district in Ordain's eight centuries of history, and was established only after the judicial systems of the city were properly codified by the Ordinate. Before its creation the city handles justice in the streets, often in broad view of the public, with local leaders serving as arbiters and judges.

Though this open-air justice system is formally gone, the Hallows has never stopped being a place where the unruly and vocal mobs of Ordain could gather to make their voices heard, and find out the fate of certain cases that matter to them.

The rumors that the underfoot conceals clandestine meeting halls and operations that the Hallows keeps away from public knowledge is quite true, and those that know the right sequence of turns to take will find themselves in hidden parlors, secret debate spots, and secure bolt holes for the Veiled Chain.
The Hallows.soverview: Situated prominently on the Spires and overlooking several vital districts in the city of Ordain, the Hallows serves as the cultural and communal heart of the city. Alive day and night with debate, performance, and the slow work of justice, here, the city’s communal bonds are forged and repaired in courts of law and peers.
The Hallows.sexposition:
Stone steps and shade trees frame the climb to the Hallows, where broad plazas unfurl before a cluster of grand halls and sweeping amphitheaters. Murals dance along facades in shifting patterns of paint and style, baring the city's creative soul for all visitors to see.

Crowds streaming up from the city’s arteries below fill the air with the din of a hundred voices all at once, some soft with laughter, others sharp with debate, or ringing with announcement, each floating above the city’s hum.

Quarry Run.name: Quarry Run
Quarry Run.text:
• District Type: Residential and Commercial

  • Population: 7,422 (Medium. Town homes, apartments, and shops with moderate foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Tight-knit (A community of "live together work together" quarry workers, haulers, and stone cutters).

  • Services: Stonemasonry (including education), Sentimental Trinkets, Hauling, Storage.

  • Influences: Closely tied to House Cevher, which has its headquarters in the area.

Culture

Quarry Run is still very much a place in recovery, after losing over 100 members of its tight-knit community of haulers, quarry workers, stone masons, and House Cevher-affiliated traders in the Stonehollow Quake of 2309, which brought down several of the district’s famous stone arches and decorative towers. In the afermath, locals came together to rebuild, creating memorial benches, new expressions of stoneworking prowess that emphasize safety, and the occasional dig at House Cevher, which was widely blamed for the quake.

Families that once guarded their trade and craft secrets from their neighbors started openly sharing as the community came together to clear the rubble, take down any structures that could possible collapse in the future, and create memorials to those who were lost. In the decades since the event, this spirit of communal sharing has remained part of Quarry Run.

Today, those who grow up in Quarry Run, or are simply interested in stonemasonry, metalworking, or mining, are brought through a series of apprenticeships with local experts that are intended to spread knowledge. The niches in the stone pillars at the community's center, while not created for this purpose, have been a great way to attract those who might be interested in trying their hand at some small work of craftsmanship. But not every rift has been healed by time. With House Cevher largely blamed for the Stonehollow Quake, relatives of those lost in the tragedy have demanded a series of reforms and payments that they believe will make House Cevher safer, but that the House believes is starting to feel like retribution for a tragic accident that they were not actually to blame for.

Landmarks

The Cevher Tradeway

A large stone edifice that holds the business offices of House Cevher. While it is carved from stone on the outside, to match the facades of the other buildings nearby, the inside is divided into rooms and areas that feature the different materials that House Cevher works with, from the grand Silver Staircase to a long hallway known as Iron Alley. This metal reinforcement protected the Tradeway from any damage during the Stonehollow Quake, leading some to believe that Cevher protected its members better than the public around it.

Folly Plaza

The gates and archways on the outskirts of Quarry Run end in this large plaza, which features a number of stone columns in varying styles, many of which include niches that can hold small items, good wishes, fortunes, and even coins. The Plaza also holds Quarry Run’s famous Whispering Columns, which take short messages whispered in one place and broadcast them, at random times and with distorted voices, at another. Though these were once used primarily for people to make frivolous confessions and a source of tips for the Veiled Chain, they now occasionally include accusations of House Cevher's negligence, even though it has been 2 decades since the Stonehollow disaster.

The Quarry Arches

Though the gate between Stonehollow Quarry and Ordain was once used to regulate traffic in and out of the city, the need for haulers to move large quantities of stone into Ordain on a regular basis led to it becoming permanently open and renamed locally to the Quarry Arch. Other arches soon followed, used primarily to direct quarry haulers to the proper warehouse and provide walking bridges for foot traffic when larger goods were moving through the streets. After several of the walking bridges collapsed during Stonehollow Quake, doing the majority of the damage, they were all taken down and reshaped into a number of benches throughout the district dedicated to the victims of the disaster. Their pillars still stand, and some argue that new magically-reinforced bridges should be created between them, but these have yet to be attempted.

Wrought Works

This metalworks shop focuses on the ways in which stone and metal can work together, and was created in part by a group of stone and metal workers who helped to build the Cevher Tradeway building. Wrought Works is known for its part in the apprenticeship program, which lures in new potential apprentices by working with passersby to weld small metal figurines that can be put into the niches in the Folly Plaza columns, representing recent accomplishments, odes to loved ones, and small works of art. It also offers work spaces to craft people who need specialized equipment, including the enterprising Darzeni Volle.

Locals

Kallie Cevher (Chaotic Good, Ordani Aster, she/her)

One of the younger members of House Cevher, Kallie has made it her mission to repair some of the rifts caused by the Stonehollow quake within the district by writing the “true story” of the incident for its 20-year anniversary. Though her more brash style is often at odds with older members of the house, and there are many who wish she would leave the subject of the disaster alone, she is convinced that she’s in the right and will one day mend enough fences to be considered for House Steward.

Elwin Lathel (Neutral Evil, Ordani Human, he/him)

Elwin worked for years as a hauler, moving goods to and from the quarry, and complained about it the entire time. Eventually, he managed to take over the Whitestone Storehouse after its previous manager was killed on the day of the Stonehollow Quake, though unbeknownst to most, Elwin simply killed the man during the chaos. Despite this, Elwin has become one of the loudest critics of House Cevher’s role in the quake, demanding payouts from House Cevher for victims that he distributes while skimming some of the money off the top.

Darzeni Volle (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

Darzeni, who trained as an ironshaper, lost the use of her legs to a rock crush during the Stonehollow Quake and dedicated herself to creating assistance devices that combine metals with magic to give mobility to those who suffer injuries that the Healing Houses are unable to heal. While she is most proficient with iron, she is always looking to expand her offerings, and has been seen following Silverbeam constructs through the city or quizzing Arcturian construct makers on their techniques in an attempt to broaden her skills.

Everly Wainsight (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, they/them)

Everly is technically employed by House Cevher to keep an eye on things in the district and prevent vandalism of the follies pillars, but they also report any major activities to the Veiled Chain and look for any structural issues in the stonework in the area on behalf of the Hallows. While getting paid by all three has brought them a decent amount of wealth, they give a good deal of it away, hiding coins in the Stone Folly niches for passersby to find.

Lore

While House Cevher was not, in fact, to blame for the earthquake known locally as the Stonehollow Quake, they have been unable to prove it, as the timing of the quake aligned with a push by the House to dig more deeply into the Quarry. The House briefly investigated internally, but eventually decided not to try to prove its innocence, instead focused on putting money towards repairs and working on the development of wards to prevent deaths if there are any future quakes.
Quarry Run.soverview: Quarry Run often claims that it is the "district that built Ordain," thanks to its proximity to the nearby quarries that give the area its name. While much of the district is taken up by residences for quarry workers and warehouses filled with quarry overflow, it's known for its Stone Follies — a series of decorative stone pillars spread across the district's wide streets and central plaza that showcase innovative stoneworking techniques and feature small niches filled with everything from small wooden carvings to good luck talismans to poems in glass bottles. The district has also been shaped by its resilience in the face of loss — hit hard by the tragic collapse of several of the follies in the Stonehollow Quake of 2503 that killed at least 100 in the district and forced it to rebuild.
Quarry Run.sexposition:
A bustle of activity fills a large plaza between ornately carved whitestone buildings and etched benches— small teams of haulers using combinations of rope and rune-inscribed wooden sleds drag blocks of uncut stone on paths in and around the district's many carved stone pillars while small stone stalls sell trinkets made of stone and iron. Some take these trinkets and place them in niches inside the walls of the pillars, no two of which are shaped exactly the same. Each has something distinctive about it— an intricate carving, an unexpected shape, a way that it plays with the nearby light — and if you stand between the long enough, a whisper will always reach your ear.

Remember the lost. Remember.

Westgate.name: Westgate
Westgate.text:
• District Type: Commercial (amenities for travel and trade)

  • Population: 17,554 (High. Businesses, depots, and info centers with extreme foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Audacious (Merchants, moneylenders, information brokers, tourists).

  • Services: Stables, lodging, food & drink, leisure, equipment sales, accounting.

Although the district of Westgate is named for the actual gate itself, several other structures define this neighborhood as much as the monumental edifice — from various inns, shops, and taverns inside the gate, to the scattered market stalls and stables located without. And while the district’s various shops and other businesses are duly sanctioned by Ordain's Trading Houses, they manage to operate with a relatively larger amount of autonomy than the rest of the city. Locations of note include the Pyrefly Lounge, Westgate Wares, and Traveler’s Rest, in addition to the Great Western Gate that houses the Watchbox and Information Office.

As one of Ordain's primary points of entry, Westgate is sometimes (if rarely) burdened with the need for increased community awareness, if only to defend the local caravans outside the gate from opportunistic thieves or errant natural predators. Since Ordain has stood for centuries without assault from the outside world, its citizens see little need for an overt security presence other than a few city-owned Chessmen constructs; nevertheless, agents of the Burnished Hand and the Veiled Chain are known to occupy the area, along with the scattered array of retired and furloughed adventurers who reside here. Full of opportunity and information, Westgate is a district where nearly anything is possible, and encounters are as diverse as the far-off travelers that walk its streets.

Culture

Life in Westgate is simultaneously an exemplary and atypical representation of life in Ordain. Despite it being one of the city's most well-traveled points of ingress, it's also a terminus for many travelers who don't manage to venture further into the city — and as a result, the outlying district is a small but potent example of the city's cultural melting pot. The languages of many people are spoken here, and the goods and services offered in Westgate (while often overpriced compared to other areas of the city) are plentiful.

The culture in Westgate has an element of transience to it, held together by the city's array of long-lasting institutions. As one of Ordain's outlying districts, Westgate is in a unique position to attract a wide array of cultural and ancestral backgrounds to its crowded urban confines. And like many of the city's districts, the politics of individuals here are as varied as their respective backgrounds.

Landmarks

The Great Western Gate

Also known as "Adonia's Pass," the Great Western Gate is more than a monument: it's a gatehouse structure that houses multiple smaller facilities with a variety of purposes. The northern Watchbox serves as a shared ready room for members of the Burnished Hand, the Veiled Chain, and the Ordinate who need a temporary base of operations in the area. Meanwhile, the southern Information Office is occupied by an Information Officer (appointed by the Hall of Records in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.1RJRU9XGC5WBm2Kq]{Assembly Hills}), and serves as a 24-hour kiosk for people in need of information about the city.

The very pillars of the structure itself are used as massive notice boards, and are decorated with layers upon layers of parchment posts and hand-scrawled messages of response. The towering stone archway is crowned with an Observation Post, and manned on the ground at all times by one or more @UUID[Actor.0xDU0k3l8V4movO8]{Chessman} constructs — owned by the Ordinate and paid for with taxpayer coin.

Traveler's Rest

One of many similar healing houses located throughout Ordain and the Plateau, Traveler’s Rest is a soothing place of relaxation and recovery operated by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}. This inviting wellness center specializes in healing the body (for physical ailments), the spirit (for magical ailments), and the spark (for ailments emotional and spiritual in nature). A variety of medicinal drugs and herbs are available for sale here, and a bright-eyed Cindaric healer named Jessa Aritou (LN, Arcturian Human, she/her) serves the patrons of Traveler’s Rest as the healing house's thoughtful Head Sage.

Pyrefly Lounge

The Pyrefly Lounge is a grungy, liquor-soaked tavern where unwitting outlanders often clash with a motley assortment of Ordain’s shadier and shiftier locals. Rumors run rampant here, but their veracity is often as watered down as the cheap wine. Patrons can frequently encounter Magda Marteth (Chaotic Good, Human Maziran, she/her), the Pyrefly's shrewd but sultry senior barkeep, who spends most of her time in the tavern — whether she's working or not.

Westgate Wares

Owned and operated by the retired adventurer Nesbit Silverbraid (Neutral Good, Vrjnhar Ordani, he/him), this busy emporium is often the first market encountered by travelers on their way into the city, and takes advantage of this convenient placement by overpricing its wide assortment of wares (an act considered somewhat garish by many, if not most, Ordani locals). Silverbraid's infamous affability allows Westgate Wares to get away with this opportunism, and everyone who walks out of the store tends to leave with something new in-hand — even if it's one of the emporium's coveted souvenir tokens.

Locals

Tolar Galanis (Lawful Good, Human Ordani, he/him)

This veteran of the Burnished Hand is a laconic warrior who can be found manning the Watchbox of The Great Western Gate when he isn't drowning his clandestine sorrows in ale at the Pyrefly Lounge. Rumors about about the source of Tolar's epic woes, but nobody has managed to convince the aged solider to share his miserable secrets.

Phoebe Stodd (Chaotic Good, Human Ordani, she/her)

Recognizable by her sleeves of Ordani tattoos and braided top-knot, this sardonic information broker serves as an opportunistic go-between for the caravans parked outside Westgate and the Trading Houses stationed within. For those who seek knowledge about Ordain without drawing the attention of local authorities or enterprise, Phoebe Stodd is happy to oblige (for the right amount of coin).

Jessa Aritou (Lawful Neutral, Human Arcturian, she/her)

Known for the adroitness of her problem-solving and the equanimity of her bedside manner, this thirty-something apothecary is the skilled head sage of the Traveler's Rest healing house. Locals and visitors alike regard Jessa as one of the most caring and considerate people the city has at its disposal, and her Arcturian roots make her an invaluable liaison for the Plateau's more rural patrons who seek succor within the city limits. The qualities people tend to remember most about Jessa are the kindness of her eyes and the wisdom of her words, despite her somewhat younger age.

Treat Jessa Aritou as a @UUID[Actor.uIDDak2Oq8Qd9Mfx]{Cindaric Sage} equipped with a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} and a @UUID[Item.HOL5fmggz6d8QMd4]{Traveler's Rest Basement Key}.

Nesbit Silverbraid (Neutral Good, Vrjnhar Ordani, he/him)

The affable general manager of Westgate Wares was an accomplished monster-hunting adventurer in a previous life, a fact that he keeps thinly veiled from his customers. If trouble were to break out in Westgate, you can trust that Nesbit Silverbraid and his handy blades will be the first to arrive — a notion that often serves as an adequate deterrent for would-be thieves and rabble rousers.

Treat Nesbit Silverbraid as an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmAssassin000000]{Assassin} armed with an additional @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepShortsword]{Shortsword}.

Lore

Because the construction of the city spread outward from its center over the course of several centuries, Westgate is remarkably one of Ordain's newest neighborhoods, a quality that is evident in the district's architecture, ethos, and people. Some say the name "Westgate" was once ascribed to another district that lies closer to the heart of the city, and that each generation the monumental Great Western Gate is relocated further westward to appease the city's expansion; but this is actually one of many tall tales that do little more than stoke the fires of unrest against aggressive Trading House and Ordinate development.

One legend with more than a shred of truth, however, is the tale concerning Nesbit Silverbraid of Westgate Wares — who is rumored to have slain a chimera in the Rustvar hinterlands during his youth as an adventurer. Indeed, the three skulls of the monstrous creature hang above the cabinet in his arcane trophy room, entrance to which is only permitted to the Vrjnhar merchant's most loyal (or affluent) customers.
Westgate.soverview:
This commercial district serves as the westernmost entrance to Ordain, and its eponymous landmark is known to be a welcome sight for many a far traveller.
