An exalted statue overlooks the stone threshold of Westgate, carved into the likeness of Adonia, the legendary Cindaric Sage who founded the proud city within. Each pillar of this monumental structure also houses chambers to accommodate various civic needs — including the Watchbox shared by various Ordani first responders, and an Information Office for those in need of directions, etiquette, or other local advice.

The further reaches of Westgate host a variety of businesses that cater to Ordani commercial interests, particularly those that support the city's extensive trade and tourism needs. From the outer threshold to its inner mercantile sprawl, Westgate is a neighborhood known for its welcoming attitude, its constant influx of travelers, and its "anything goes" lifestyle.
Westgate.sexposition:
A massive stone archway stands proudly above a main thoroughfare into the great city of Ordain, overlooked by a majestic statue fashioned into the likeness of a wise feminine sage. Both stone pillars of the archway are adorned with countless notices, bills, and bounties; and an ornamented lookout post stands atop the structure, equipped with an array of mounted telescopes. You notice at least one silhouette lurking amidst this observation perch, while a humanoid-looking automaton stands at calm attention beside the gate below — one hand clutches a flag pole bearing Ordain's sigil, and an elegant sword is hilted casually upon its steel hip.

Stables, caravans, and market stalls flank each side of the road leading up to this grand and welcoming threshold. And diverse crowds of locals and visitors alike make their way to and fro, caught up in the lively hustle and bustle of urban commerce. A neighborhood full of shops, taverns, and hostelries waits on the other side of the titular Westgate, inviting you to explore this sprawling metropolitan wonderland for yourself.

Ember's Bounty.name: Ember's Bounty
Ember's Bounty.text:
• District Type: Commercial

  • Density: Unknown (Crowded. Decks churn with pirates, merchants, and thrill-seekers day and night. The crew, hangers-on, and cutthroats number in the low hundreds.)

  • Lifestyle: Maritime (Sailors, merchants, pirates and the like are found here.)

  • Services: Sale and barter of stolen, exotic, or forbidden goods; rough food and drink for the daring. Provisions and drink are cheap, but rare or magical wares can be expensive.

Bastilla’s flagship, Ember’s Bounty dominates any harbor lucky (or unlucky) enough to host her. The Bounty rarely strays far from its fleet, and when it makes berth by a city it becomes the epicenter of vice and trade. While docked it offloads a small army of pirates looking for distraction on leave, and welcomes merchants and criminals of all stripes to come make deals and pick through the loot on offer.

Culture

Life on the Ember’s Bounty is chaos at the best of times, with hundreds of sailors and officers working together to keep the massive vessel afloat. While the Bounty’s leadership maintains some order while at sea, all bests are off when the ship docks. Drunken brawls, gambling, and wild revels are commonplace when the ship has nowhere to be, with consequence decided on the spot by whatever officers happens to be nearby.

The ship is crewed by a large number of sailors hailing from Ordain, all of them loyal to House Bastilla, or serving under mercenary contracts with their loyalty given to coin and treasure alone. Visiting crews of Bastilla ships always receive priority in all dealings, from accommodations and food to best deals on offered goods.

The ship is so large and the holds so crowded that the vessel runs with several Quartermasters, each in charge of their own sections of the hold. They alone handle negotiation and sale of the goods, and in cases where coin is not sufficient, can be bartered with directly.

Though the ship has a Captain, it at times feels less like any one person is in command, and more as though the ship itself is a living organism with many pieces working in concert.

Landmarks

The Heaving Stalls

When anchored, the sprawl of the ship's deck becomes covered in stalls and displays of goods, with pirate-merchants standing by to take coin or discuss barter. Many stalls also list items which are held below deck, which one of the ship Quartermasters are needed to view and purchase.

The Grand Galley

Amidships, this sheltered hall runs lengthwise and is stacked with plank-benches and tables that make up the ship's communal mess. Guests are welcome to come sit and eat, drink, and watch the chaos unfold. Prepared food and drink can be had here for a modest sum, and all manner of foodstuffs, from rare ingredients to uncommon vintages of foreign booze can be bought from the quartermaster here.

The Batteries

A deck unto itself, the Batteries is a gun-deck lined with converted ballistae meant to defend the ship. Each one is etched with magical runes and mystic symbols that allow them to fire rapidly without needing ammunition. These mystic ballistae can unleash bolts of magical fire, acid, lightning to keep enemies at bay. Its existence is kept a secret from the outside world, and the crew can count on one hand the number if times the gun ports have had to be opened.

The Endless Holds

This massive, compartmentalized cargo hold is like a maze, and many a soul have ended up lost amongst the countless stacks of crates, barrels, and chests. Nothing is labeled, and only the quartermasters aboard the ship truly know what each container holds. It is said that the masters of the hold have magical devices that allow them to know the contents of their sections at all times.

Locals

Captain Stonne Torish (Neutral, Cascillian Human, he/him)

Captain Torish carries himself with a reserved but ironclad dignity. Weather-burnished and silver-haired, he often oversees the Bounty from the immense quarterdeck, surrounded by his officers and most trusted crew. As most captains, Stonne leaves the day-to-day operation of the ship to his quartermasters and only truly takes commend when the vessel is sailing to a new destination.

First Quartermaster Lynet Sarrow (Lawful Neutral, Kelmezian Human, she/her)

Lynet is the ship’s logistics brain, strict and unflappable, overseeing all intake and movement of cargo. She primarily deals with the second quartermasters under her supervision, and otherwise leaves them to mind their goods. However, in the event that there is a dispute, she is regarded as the final judge of barter-worthiness of all items.

Quartermaster Tion Marvek (Lawful Neutral, Bejak Kivahr, he/him)

Tion is lean, sharp-featured, and famously unflappable. One rarely sees him without his arcane ledger — a thick, rune-bound tome said to magically update itself as his cargo holds change their contents. Tion deals primarily in magical items, magical reagents, spell components, scrolls, spell books, potions, and similar items of mystical power.

Maasathtar “Moss” Enki (Chaotic Good, Lumek Fej, he/him)

A broad-shouldered, tattooed man with an ear for gossip and a love of strange spice combinations, “Moss,” Maasathtar reigns supreme in the Grand Galley. He delights in sourcing the rarest ingredients the Bounty’s nomadic market can offer and inflicts the culinary experiments on any foolish enough to agree to try it. His kitchen is always open, brimming with experimental dishes and hearty stews that keep spirits buoyed in any weather. He oversees all trades in the Galley, not unlike a Quartermaster.

Lore

Most accounts state that the ship appeared roaming the seas about a century ago, but its actual origins remain a great mystery. Its size along makes it too large to have been built in any but the largest shipyards, and many believe that it is Cascillian in origin, but no record of its construction exists in any known shipyard.

The make and design of the great vessel are unique, lending further mystery to its history and creation. The ship also features extensive mystical reinforcement that would have taken great skill and resource to create, including alchemically treated iron that never rusts, transmuted wood that never leaks, and magically threaded sails that catch the wind like no other.

As a result, rumors about the ship are numerous, and range from plausible to insane. Some say that the ship was made by the Cascillian Republic in secret and that the ship was stolen by House Bastilla. Others claim that it was build by the Trading house directly, again, in secret. Some believe it was created by one or more gods, and given to a captain for some unknown purpose. However, the real origin of the ship remains unknown, and the crew are happy to feed the rumor mills and never tell the truth, likely because not even they know.

Given the piracy, crime, and debauchery it brings with it, elements in the Ordinate actively attempt to make Ordain itself hostile to the vessel, but House Bastilla always manages to bribe and intimidate the right people to keep the docks open to their flagship.
Ember's Bounty.soverview: The Ember's Bounty serves not only as House Bastilla's flagship, but also as the largest and most infamous pirate ship on the seas, serving as a haven for pirates, smugglers, and outcasts alike. The ship's sprawling market brims with goods and contraband, much of it procured at swordpoint. Wherever Bastilla’s flagship docks, she brings an eruption of chaos, crime, and coin.
Ember's Bounty.sexposition: A colossus among ships, this five-masted behemoth rests low in the water, her hull laden with a trove of unknown cargo. Its great crimson sails are drawn and secured, while long ruby pennants attached to her towering masts snap in the breeze. Narrow gangways teem with activity going to and from her main deck as a small flotilla of skiffs and flatboats ferry passengers and crates to and from the vessel.

Flotsam.name: Flotsam
Flotsam.text:
• District Type: Commercial (trade, finance) with some Residential

  • Population: 2,215 (Dense with shoppers and tourists during the day, with only a moderate population of merchants and artisans as full-time residents)

  • Lifestyle: Scrappy (Getting less for more and making something out of nothing are considered art forms)

  • Services: Financial Services (Banks, lenders, currency exchange) and Goods (Odds and ends, usually at a bargain)

Culture

While there are plenty of places in Ordain to buy goods, there's nothing quite like the clutter and buzz of Flotsam, which has a unique mix of rotating stalls for local Trading House merchants, rented stands for traders visiting Ordain with goods from foreign lands, and bankers happy to store and trade coin to keep the commerce flowing. Even Flotsam's residential housing is a bit of a mix, with both long-term residential housing for local merchants and artisans who want to be close to their merchandise and short-term roots for rent for visiting traders. Often, those who live here bring some flavor of what they do or sell with them, giving the residential streets behind the shops the feel of a mosaic of cultures and ways of life.

Despite the seeming chaos, with merchant after merchant offering goods and sales, Flotsam does have some method to its madness. The Trading House market is the most permanent fixture, with rows of fixed wooden stalls that are distributed evenly between the five Houses and generally sell the same goods every day. In the rotating market outside of the Trading House market, on the other hand, stalls and carts are generally rented, changing hands frequently. Flotsam's regular bazaars fall somewhere in the middle - during these high-energy all-day events, carts are given out for free by lottery, giving merchants who are just getting started or unsure about the value of Flotsam to show off their wares to Ordani buyers.

Landmarks

Levee

The facade of this riverside tavern is crafted entirely from driftwood culled from the bay south of Ordain, collected by its proprietors for generations. The Levee’s 5-star kitchen serves up Ordani versions of international cuisine; the flavorful menu is kept relatively short, but rotates each season. The popular tavern’s witty head chef Bodi Frumme is a well-traveled romantic who has a fondness for foreign chefs and employs at least 3 of his exes.

Slipknot

One of the largest cart rental shops in Flotsam, Slipknot is notable because it does a live auction for carts each morning instead of doing long-term reservations. Often, merchants can get the carts cheaper than they would elsewhere, but only if they don't bid too high. Owner Verix Andail (CG Ordani signborn, they/them) also uses the crowds that the auction generates to bring in merchants who might benefit from their other services, like coin changing and short-term storage, but has been dogged by recent rumors that they are fixing their auctions.

Trading House Market

This large stone building has rows of permanent stalls for each of Ordain's Trading Houses, where they showcase smaller goods related to their main area of interest, ranging from wearable accessories (House Salva) to unique spice blends (House Lillifeld) to ocean maps (House Bastilla). For Houses with fewer physical goods, stalls are often used for demonstrations of artisanship, with House Cevher putting on showcases of stoneworking and metalsmithing alongside the small trinkets they might put out for sale.

Waterfront Bazaar

The theme for the Waterfront Bazaar is always a little different, but its general appearance remains the same - a twisting network of stalls and tents that makes its way from Flotsam's main plaza to the floating docks on the river at the edge of the district and is one of the best places in the city to find goods from abroad. The market’s tents and awnings are haphazardly (if lovingly) fashioned from the sails of decommissioned ships, giving the entire area the appearance of a checkered blanket of recycled textile. It is said that there is some way to tell what is being sold by staring at the pattern but if that is true, the secret is not wildly known.

Locals

Chef Fancie Frumme (CN Lumek Fej, she/her)

The most recent of Bodi Frumme's exes to join the cooking staff of Levee, she has taken his last name in what she claims is a Fej custom, despite the short length of their courtship, which, like many of Bodi's romances, only lasted about 4 months. While some of the other staff at Levee claim that she is simply trying to elevate herself using Bodi Frumme's name, no one will deny that she can cook, and her Fej desserts — including her famous Sugared Smoke — are the talk of the town.

Mauny Setsun (N Arcturian human, he/him)

Retired from sailing after being cursed by a figurine that gave him crippling fear of the water, Mauny now sells maps in the Trading House market on behalf of House Bastilla. He hopes to one day break the curse and be able to sail again, working toward his goal both by working at a market not too far from the Destine River that flows into Ordain and by keeping an eye out for any items in Flotsam that might shake the curse and get him back on the water.

Hypatia Sissos (LN Ordani human, she/her)

Hypatia is in charge of administering the Trading House markets, which often consists mostly of convincing the merchants of one house that they are not being given a disadvantage compared to the merchants of another. As a result she knows much more about trading house relations than most, though she sincerely wishes she didn't. Hypatia routinely develops new rules and regulations for the markets, mostly to keep the merchants busy with something other than questioning her, and does not care in the least that most simply ignore them.

Tillamer Wins (CG Ordani human, she/her)

Sick of getting lost in the Flotsam markets, Tilamer has been working on a system of message stones attached to Flotsam carts that will allow her to know what is being sold each day and create fast-drawn maps for visiting tourists. The initiative is controversial, with some merchants believing that it will attract new customers to stalls that might not otherwise get attention and others convinced it will lessen overall foot traffic as buyers go to exactly the stall they need.

Lore

Legend has it that Flotsam was created after a merchant's boat capsized in the river, and rather than let their goods float away, the crew decided to sell the floating crates at a discount. While this is likely not true, nearly every shop in Flotsam claims to have a plank from that boat somewhere on their property that visitors can touch or take a shaving from, for a nominal price.
Flotsam.soverview: This bustling riverside market decorated with reclaimed ship timber is known for the sheer number and variety of goods being sold in its common shops, rotating markets, and seasonal bazaars. Always open for business and usually jam-packed with merchants, customers, and more than a little clutter, Flotsam can be overwhelming for first-time visitors, though locals swear it has the best prices in all of Ordain.
Flotsam.sexposition: As you make your way through the narrow aisles of impromptu merchant stalls and past the open doors of lenders offering fair trades for foreign coin, the voices of the shopkeeps and their customers blend into a steady hum. In and around them, the buildings are a mix of old wood, new stone, and generic metal; much like the goods on the carts surrounding you, no two pieces are ever quite the same.

Redwalk Ramble.name: Redwalk Ramble
Redwalk Ramble.text:
• District Type: Recreational

  • Population: 312 (Sparse population of artists, merchants, and nature lovers)

  • Lifestyle: Observational (Performance artists and paid fashion models supplement the natural beauty of the park)

  • Services: Performance (Impromptu fashion shows and performance art)

Culture

The Redwalk Ramble is a place of natural beauty, but despite its well-tended grassy knolls and abundant flowers, it is most well known as a place to see the latest and greatest in both Ordani fashion and entertainment, thanks to the influence of Trading House Salva. House Salva, which focuses on clothing, fashion, and the arts, encourages the designers from the nearby Gossamer District to use the Ramble as a display case of sorts, sending their work out on the backs or in the hands of trusted ramblers, whose job is to meet people, mingle, and encourage anyone who admires the goods they are wearing to visit the appropriate store. This arrangement gives the Ramble a lively atmosphere, as do the many performance troupes in the area, who often perform small pieces from larger shows in the hopes that they might catch the eye of a House Salva scout.

Despite the generally festive feeling to the Ramble, the meadows and other plant life within it are quite serene. The Hallows uses magically treated stone to make some areas of the Ramble, like the large open-air amphitheater at the heart of the district, more resonant, while others remain quiet corners for conversation or contemplation where loud performances and ramblers selling goods are strictly forbidden. There is also a certain order to even the busier sections of the Ramble, as locals in the district pride themselves on being able to display some of the best that Ordain has to offer without overwhelming those around them and are not hesitant to report any overenthusiastic performer or rambler to House Salva leadership for a dressing down.

Landmarks

Ettie's Exhibitions

This indoor space run by Ettie Salvari hosts events for House Salva that range from fine art gallery exhibitions to living fashion shows, often using its proximity to the open space of the Ramble to let the events spill out into public spaces and bring them additional recognition. Ettie is known for her eye for talent, and many wait with bated breath for her declaration at the end of exhibition of who to watch going forward.

The Ramble Amphitheater

This large tree-shaded performance space is occasional used for major events like fashion shows or performance showcases, but is open to foot traffic and public performance when not in active use. Performers looking to catch the eye of a new audience member, supporter, or patron perform small shows, while decadently attired ramblers serve as both walking displays of the goods they have been hired to sell and welcomers meant to put newcomers at ease.

80 Steps to Glory

This set of 83 steep steps would be fairly unremarkable if not for the encouragement of House Salva to make it a showcase for art and entertainment. Collaboratives of artists and designers across disciplines often work together on projects that utilize the steps and showcase their talents, with recent exhibitions ranging from a history of Ordani fashion expressed through dance to a mural made entirely of flowers that changed as they bloomed, grew, and died. House Salva scouts are known to spend time in the area, looking for those who might be worthy of funding for more permanent exhibitions.

Umber's Pass

A wooded arch that leads to one of the more secluded sections of Redwalk Ramble, as its opening is perpetually overgrown with vines. The vines have been cleared more than once, but always return, usually thicker than before. As it is popular with lovers looking for spots to meet in secret, it is believed that they replant the arch with vines anytime it is cleared to maintain their secret hideaway.

Locals

Arvin Spoole (True Neutral, Arcturian Human, he/him)

Arvin Spoole arrived in Ordain from the Arctus Plateau as a talented fabric repairer, but has reinvented himself with his ability to upgrade the outfits of those around him, setting up shop in the Amphitheater and making small tweaks to the clothes of passersby in return for generous tips. His only rule is that he will not “refashion” the clothes of any Arcturians, and he seems to actively avoid them, along with any questions about his past.

Ettie Salvari (Lawful Evil, Arcturian Human, he/him)

The head of Ettie's Exhibitions, she may have inherited her shameless pursuit of glory from her father Palo, who changed his last name to Salvari just in the hopes that it would make his ascension in House Salva faster. Unlike Palo, who never made it particularly far up in the House, Ettie is an excellent talent scout, and has a knack for spotting the one or two artists in her exhibitions who will ascend to great heights. Unfortunately for those she discovers, her stamp of approval comes with a price, and she collects favors from those she put on the map for the rest of their lives. Those who don't approve receive a visit from Palo Salvari, whose true talent lies in intimidation.

Kantella (Neutral Good, Ordani Signborn, she/her)

Retired rambler Kantella's weekly pamphlets highlighting the best fashion of the past week are well-loved in the Ramble, in part because she tends to weave them in with local news, gossip, and even the occasional matchmaking – she has a surprising ability to match people up based on their fashion sense that has led to several friendships and at least one romantic pairing.

Zanzi Felten (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

Zani Felten grew up at a time when the greenery of the Ramble dominated most of the district, and has watched as pieces of it have been given away to House Salva shops over the years, something that she deeply opposes. While her many many letters to both Hollows and House Salva are considered a bit of an annoyance, both value the care she brings to the remaining parkland, which she unofficially oversees maintenance of with the help of the Redwalk Rangers, a group of Ordani youth that she has recruited and are trying to teach to love nature's beauty over "artificial glamour."

Lore

Some claim that Redwalk Ramble’s name comes from an era when the color red became a fashion must-have in Ordain, causing every storefront to display its own version of the color, but in truth, it is named because of its proximity to Redrak Fields.
Redwalk Ramble.soverview: The Redwalk Ramble was once a single large park at the edge of the city, but over time, at the request of House Salva, pieces of the park were given to shopkeepers looking to showcase their wares to the public or provide entertainment to those enjoying the area. Today, the area is filled with shops that create and display the latest in Ordani fashion and cultural spaces that showcase performers and artists who are making a name for themselves in the city. The parkland that remains between these shops and homes is well-maintained but disjointed, containing many small cul-de-sacs and hidden corners that can be used for either secrecy or solitude.
Redwalk Ramble.sexposition: Though the performers and fashion mavens who frequent the stone amphitheater at the heart of the Ramble often grab most of the attention of visitors, a walk through the district reveals a more subtle mix of art, commerce and nature. Paved residential streets lead into and out of wooden glades. Unexpected wooden arches bridge the passageway between a small pond surrounded by flowers on one side and a small shop filled with fabrics on the other. Though it could be easy to get lost on one of these winding paths, welcoming guides dressed in some of the finest clothing seen in Ordain are often nearby, ready to direct you to anywhere you might need to go.

Performer's Plaza.name: Performer's Plaza
Performer's Plaza.text:
• District Type: Recreational and Institutional with Residential and Commercial

  • Population: 4,681 (Medium. Civic centers and apartments with heavy foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Modest-to-Comfortable (Artists, performers, civil servants, laborers, culinary pros).

  • Services: Public gathering facilities, information services, housing, food & drink.

Performer's Plaza is named after the large public commons at the district's center, which is capable of amplifying the voices of those who perform within the confines of its sweeping, convex stonework. The plaza lives up to its name daily, as countless musicians, artists, and street performers shuffle among its ample stone stages and airy palisades. Of course, only one artist may occupy the stage of honor at any given point in time; known as Exhibition Court, this small amphitheater makes the most use of the plaza's marvelous architecture, and is reserved for larger shows and whatever performances the local Performer's Guild deems the most worthy or adequate.

Most of the time, the central plaza is used for recreation and public gatherings, and the enclosing neighborhood caters to these gatherings with a variety of eateries, taverns, and market stalls. Noises emitted here travel farther than anywhere else in town; and while that means practically little in modern Ordain — where sounds are quickly swallowed by the din of the city — a certain belief that the music and voices of the people can inspire the whole of Ordain from one central location endures.

Culture

The people of Performer's Plaza are a proud lot, and while there is a fundamental contingent of Ordani locals, the lively neighborhood also attracts a fair amount of transplants to its progressive and welcoming streets. As one might imagine, several Arcturians populate the area, along with Imperial, Cascillian, and Luma expatriates. If Ordain has a "melting pot" outside of its most commercial districts, Performer's Plaza is most likely that place.

Landmarks

Exhibition Court

Exhibition Court is the name given to the central-most amphitheater of Performer's Plaza, where a convex stone commons is surrounded by dozens of rows of tiered stone benches. Outside of the public concerts and plays for which it is famous, Exhibition Court also serves as a public gathering area — a vivacious park made of elegant mortar and stone. Whether or not a show is happening, people can be found gathered around Exhibition Court at nearly all times of the day.

The People's Voice

This large edifice in Petitioner's Plaza is one of Ordain's famed Noticeries — public buildings where information is freely traded, including everything from job postings and solicitations for adventuring services to public compliments and complaints (anonymous and otherwise). Due to its location in Performer's Plaza, The People's Voice also provides information regarding citywide initiatives related to the arts, like details about concerts and live shows in other districts.

East Street Market

This sprawling indoor/outdoor complex hosts a score of different merchants and vendors, whose respective stalls and alcoves can be as diverse as the people of Ordain themselves. Nearly half of the circuitous place resembles a farmer's market, playing host to a variety of fresh fruit and meat vendors alongside a wide array of international eateries. Other merchants provide equipment and trade goods, often shifting their inventories and prices to take advantage of whatever notices might be posted this week at The People's Voice. If you can't find what you're looking for at the East Street Market, someone here can guide you in the right direction.

Locals

Ash Danwren (CG, Ordani Human, he/him)

This vociferous clerk for The People's Voice is known for his intense passion for Ordani gossip, which many locals find more humorous than engaging (often to his amusing chagrin). Nevertheless, Ash dutifully mans his post with a stalwart eye for news that might have an effect on local citizens and the people of the surrounding plateau. Ash believes music can be a powerful tool for change, and encourages most of the minstrels and bard he encounters to heed that call for progressivism.

Merida Hardbark (NG, Cascilian Thornling, she/her)

A retired smuggler who settled in Ordain nearly a decade ago, this wily old merchant runs a popular stall in the East Street Market that specializes in curious beneficial saps, alchemical herbs, and botanical spell components, alongside a small array of plant-based clothing and equipment. Merida is an experienced information broker, and always has an opinion about the jobs and notices posted at The People's Voice, as well as general Ordani and Arcturian gossip.

Eli Eld (CG, Ordani Human, he/they)

This moody young street musician is a kithara player known for his sonorous tenor voice, a soft and haunting sound that's perfectly at home within the amplified confines of Performer's Plaza. A relatively new talent, Eli's so incredibly charismatic and skilled that other local musicians and street performers tend to stand back and listen rather than compete for space. Many consider Eli to be the voice of a whole generation of young Ordani, and his compelling songwriting and relatable lyrics are beloved by all.

Lore

A community watch group known as the Street Sweepers is established in Performer's Plaza, made up of a cadre of concerned citizens of all stripes who strive to ensure the people and their interests stay protected. Merida Hardback of the East Street Market is one high profile member of this clandestine group, which is all but a mystery to most everyone outside of the district.
Performer's Plaza.soverview:
The district known as Performer's Plaza is named after the large municipal square at its center, which has historically served the people of Ordain as a free venue for exhibitions and public gatherings. Indeed, the place has given Ordani citizens a literal and figurative voice to speak up about what matters to them the most — albeit through art, discussion, and the power of live performance.

The eponymous Plaza was built by a talented engineer, who designed the concave area to amplify voices within it. To this day, the public makes tremendous and effective use of Performer's Plaza with a regular schedule of public shows, charitable exhibitions, and civic gatherings; and it remains a place where the people of Ordain can feel heard and seen, regardless of their particular walks of life.
Performer's Plaza.sexposition: As soon as you step foot in this roomy district, the cacophony of a hundred whispers seems to engulf you, along with the music of an unseen minstrel. Noise resounds throughout the broad and capacious streets here, which are copiously lined with small apartments and eateries, and soon enough you determine the origin of the melodic swell: a central public square, full of people, where the lone minstrel plays their inviting song. The architecture here seems capable of amplifying sound with uncanny ease, and you ponder what this marvelous design has afforded the performance artists and aficionados of Ordain.

Ordain Waterfront.name: Ordain Waterfront
Ordain Waterfront.text:
The Ordain Waterfront cuts through the heart of Ordain, offering views of the coursing river, and access to numerous docks and slips where cargo and people can be moved through the grand metropolis. The winding waterfront of Ordain is heavily weighted toward industrial and commercial districts, especially those of shipping and transport, as the mighty Destine was tamed long ago, and turned into a tool for the city's success.

Environment

Paved with white stones like the rest of Ordain, and accented with sturdy wooden docks, much of the Destine's natural form has vanished with the expansion of the city. The rushing waters flowing from the north been confined by sturdily constructed canals of stone, and directed through underground waterways built centuries ago.

Travel through and across the waterfront is swift, as countless ferries and barges can be found moving cargo, though visitors must be careful where they go. Most of the waterfront is meant for work, and the transit of goods above all else, so navigation requires vigilance, as the traffic of workers and materials creates plenty of hazards for the unwary.

Ecology

The heavy industrial nature of the waterfront means that little space has been dedicated for greenery and gardens, creating an often unwelcoming landscape for creatures that don't excel in urban and commercial sprawls. As a result, floral and faunal presence is minimal but comprises creatures familiar with dockside activity, such as seabirds, enterprising rodents, and invasive insects taking advantage of the crates, spilled materials, and moving vessels.

Lore

Significant portions of the waterfront's construction were necessitated by the gradual shifting of the river's flow over the centuries, and city planners worked tirelessly to create the final shape of the Destine's course. It took decades of work, and the plans had to be revised numerous times, including the addition of underwater canals and sewers to facilitate the flow of waters and waste, especially in rainy seasons, to make sure the river didn't overflow into the city.

Most citizens of Ordain won't give the river a second thought, seeing it as an obstacle to travel or just another part of their home. Yet it took many minds and countless hands to tame the swift waters and make it a mundane part of daily life.
Ordain Waterfront.soverview: The Ordain waterfront is the city's primary conduit for trade and travel, stretching from the river’s broad banks in the north of the city all the way down to the vast bay where ships from all over Ember dock in search of commerce or safe harbor. It is the center of transportation, a series of energetic districts marked by loading cranes, shops, ferries, warehouses and a veritable army of people who keep everything moving, from cargo to people.
Ordain Waterfront.sexposition: Docks and piers line the flowing waters of the Destine River as it carves a path through Ordain. From these docks, a fleet of small craft, barges, and ferries sails back and forth between the banks, moving people and materials day in and day out. As the Destine gives way to the great Bay of Ordain, these docks grow ever larger, more elaborate, with rows of warehouses standing behind them and cranes looming overhead. In these larger docks, great deep water trading ships are loaded down with goods or relieved of the bounties they bring.

The Ordinate.name: The Ordinate
The Ordinate.text:
• District Type: Governmental

  • Population: 38 (Very light permanent population of Ordinate employees, high traffic while the Ordinate is in session)

  • Lifestyle: Focused (the Ordinate is everything for those who live there)

  • Services: Law (citywide policy, development of laws)

Culture

Few live in the district that holds the Ordinate, but it never feels empty, filled with the many decision facilitators who help the Ordinate to function, including the proxies of important parties who bring petitions to the Ordinate, the clerks who present evidence of the potential impact of a decision (often in private sessions, though any impact reports are usually made public for those who care to read them), the scribes who capture what happens in an Ordinate session, and the Hallows representatives who uphold and enact the Ordinate's laws. On days when the Ordinate is in session, most of these parties are in the Ordinate itself to witness the session, leaving the streets of the district feeling somewhat still unless the Ordinate is making a decision about something that catches the public's fancy and brings more observers to the surrounding streets.

Once the Ordinate adjourns for the week, though, is when the real activity of the Ordinate district begins. The sprawling network of clerks, record keepers, and stewards is somewhat self-managing, kept in balance by a common interest in the continued functioning of the Ordinate and enough competing priorities that anyone who attempts to circumvent the system will have someone reporting on their activities. Tradition also holds a fair amount of weight in the Ordinate, influencing everything from where people sit when the Ordinate is in session to the order in which Presentations are scheduled by the Chief Clerk. While this keeps things moving at a steady hum and ensures that everyone knows what to expect from the Ordinate, there are those who wonder if the reliance on old ways makes the Ordinate unable to respond quickly to any new and unexpected problems.

Landmarks

Clerk's Row

This unofficial term for the stretch of offices outside of the Ordinate holds the few residences in the Ordinate, including a residence for the designee of each current member of the Ordinate and for the Chief Clerk, who deals with the administrative scheduling of Ordinate sessions. Most of these are used primarily as places to live only on the days the Ordinate is in session, but the Chief Clerk generally lives in theirs full-time. Several past Chief Clerks and influential scribes have also built or acquired homes along the row, hoping it will help them stay informed about Ordinate matters after retiring from their posts.

The Ordinate

A centerpiece not only of the district but of Ordain proper, the Ordinate is an architectural delight that also contains a myriad of rooms needed to conduct the business of the city, all centered around its magnificent atrium, where the Ordinate members publicly hear petitions and make decrees. Though not always full, the Ordinate usually has some number of observers when it is in session, and tours are given of the structure on its off days, usually by clerks and scribes in training.

The Underchambers

For most, the Underchambers are little more than a myth, rumored to be a place where overenthusiastic Ordinate clerks sleep during important debates, or a set of rooms that only members of the Ordinate know about where deals are struck between them in velvet-lined rooms filled with impossible luxuries. In truth, these tunnels beneath the Ordinate's main chamber, though constructed to provide a way out of the Ordinate if needed, have become cluttered, holding everything from gifts for Ordinate members (which they are honor-bound to turn over to the Ordinate for disposal) to supplies for the many scribes who capture each official decree. Some say that there is a way through the mess if you know where you're going, but the popular prank of setting up illusions of skeletons in dusty chairs in the Underchamber corridors makes it clear that most, at least, don't believe it.

Locals

Elwin Kirei (Lawful Neutral, Ordani human, he/him)

A former Chief Clerk of the Ordinate, and father of current chief clerk Winna, Elwin stayed neutral about every issue facing the Ordinate…up until his retirement after 40 years in his role. Now, he makes a living publishing books about his time at the Ordinate that seem calculated to make the role of the clerk one of a heroic public servant saving the Ordinate from their own mistaken ideas, though they are also so drily and confusingly written that most don't care. Elwin believes that his writing is helping his daughter Winna as she makes the role her own, but also enjoys being able to finally speak his mind, and ignores the fact that this has caused tension between them. Instead, he has thrown himself into his work and is hard at work on his next opus, focused on what he believes to be a scintillating discussion about grain pricing and storage from a decade ago.

Tiravan Elms (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani drakon, they/them)

Ordinate scribe turned journalist Tiravan keeps their ear to the ground and their quill to the page, reporting on Ordinate business day and night so that the rest of Ordain knows what the Ordinate is doing. Raised by parents who fled the Tayan Empire after falling out of favor, Tiravan tries to be a barrier against corruption in the city, despite having not yet found much of it. They spend much of their time cultivating sources within the Ordinate, enjoying being seen to be among the powerful and influential, but while Tiravan is a dogged pursuer of the truth, they're also easily swayed by the opinions of those they know and trust, and can be manipulated by those who wish their perspective to reported as the absolute truth. Given that few others know the ins and outs of the Ordinate as well as they do, Tiravan's word is often trusted by others without question, even if it is untrue.

Winna Kirei (True Neutral, Ordani human, she/her)

The current chief clerk of the Ordinate. Winna has only been in the role a few years, and is well-respected, having overcome those who believed she only got the job due to her father's influence and then those who were insulted in some fashion by her father's ongoing relitigation of former Ordinate business in his dry but detailed books. She's known for her near encyclopedic memory of dates, faces, and incidents from across Ordain, which she uses to determine which items the Ordinate needs to consider in its session and which will either resolve themselves or can be sent to another source of authority, like the Trading Houses or the Hallows. Among the pieces of information that Winna has collected are several incidents and issues that could be used to blackmail various members of the Ordinate, which she holds onto not to use them herself but to be aware of whether or not an Ordinate member is being unduly influenced by someone else. The secrets are meticulously filed and written in a shorthand that Winna developed herself, which is difficult but not impossible to decipher.

Lore

The ruling body known as the Ordinate came out of the ashes of the Veiled War, but it took time for the massive structure that houses its daily activities to be built. It is said that the building of the structure helped to cement the relationships between the Trading Houses (which provided supplies to construct the building that ranged from stone mined by House Cevher to fabrics created by House Salva to arcane protections carried in by Red Bastilla, founder of House Bastilla) as well as the mutual respect between the Ordinate and the Hallows, which helped supply the labor that turned the raw materials into the building that the Ordinate has now become.
The Ordinate.soverview: The Ordinate is more than a district — it is both the ruling body of Ordain and the massive building in which it makes its public decisions. Both dominate life in their immediate vicinity, but are surrounded by the web of officials, information, and decisions that make their authority possible, from smaller Ordani government offices to the homes of some of the residents who help to carry out the Ordinate's will.
The Ordinate.sexposition: Intricately carved out of gleaming white stone, the Ordinate towers over the city of Ordain, visible from every point in the city. In the entirety of Ordain's history, there has always been light in its windows, a symbol that the nine members of the Ordinate who steer the direction of the city are always there — or always watching — depending on whom you ask. But the nine members of the Ordinate do not do their work alone. In and among the Ordinate's decorative edifices and impossibly high doorways, those who turn the will of the Ordinate into action stay in steady motion, ensuring that the city functions the way that the Ordinate wills it to.

Restaurant Row.name: Restaurant Row
Restaurant Row.text:
• District Type: Commercial (restaurants) with some Residential

  • Population: 5,605 (Moderate population of service workers, dock workers, and other hands-on professions, along with a high density of visitors)

  • Lifestyle: Fast-Paced (Diners coming in and out of the area's restaurants create a sense of constant movement)

  • Services: Food (Restaurants, taverns, cafes)

  • Influences: Overseen by House Lillifeld, which runs the back-end storage and supplies of most of the restaurants in the district

While the workers of Restaurant Row tend to move together like a well-oiled machine in front of their guests, making sure that everyone feels well taken care of, Restaurant Row is a bundle of sometimes chaotic energy behind the scenes. The many workers who move through the backrooms, undercuts, and side passages that connect the restaurants to House Lilifeld food stores are often only steps or seconds away from disaster as they balance changing supplies, odd customer requests, and House Lilifeld's demands that one ingredient or another be showcased as the fresh new flavor of the moment.

Still, many would say that this level of chaos is what draws them to cooking or serving or preparing food in Restaurant Row over anywhere else in Ordain. In the world behind the cooktops, stakes are high, life can feel like it is on a knife's edge, and those who work (and often) live in the area love the fast pace, even if it means occasional fits of passion, dropped plates, and heightened emotions.

The residential housing in the area, which is tucked away, around corners that the average diner wouldn't explore, is mostly communal, with individual housing groups often focusing on a specific work-related skill or recreational interests. House Lillifeld set these units up initially in the hopes that it would lead to unofficial mentorship and a sense of teamwork, which has largely worked, though there are occasional feuds and fights that show up in the food on the Row in ways that only those who live in the district understand (and often reference in short hand with phrases like "a three fish fight" or "like a barrel of stilling wine").

Landmarks

Pancha's Pourhouse

No one knows who Pancha is or was - general consensus is that she may have never existed other than in some shared inside joke - but the Pourhouse that bears her name is one of the few places in Restaurant Row that exists as both a communal house and a tavern serving the public. Behind the scenes, Pancha's is often the first place that newcomers to Restaurant Row land, known for its late-night conversations and dedication to being able to make everything from a good semi-magical consumable elixir to a Blacksap infused picker-upper, and its small cafe storefront provides drinks to many of the nearby restaurants, as well as those passing through the district.

Odd Bites

When House Lillifeld is looking to try something new with one of their ingredients, or a chef has an idea that might or might not be good, it often ends up at Odd Bites, which serves limited portions of experimental food at a deep discount, but requires those who eat there to share their honest thoughts on what they've just consumed. Rumors that there is a truth stone embedded beneath their floor somewhere is just that, though it doesn't stop people from occasionally bringing friends or lovers there to ask the tough questions between bites of new concoctions.

Shine

Shine is all about the show, with food preparers who perform a variety of music between courses. The type of music performed varies based on who is running the shift, and it is not unusual to hear a bawdy group round at one time of day and a heartfelt soloist at another.

Whistler's Tavern

An inn and tavern that doubles as a Noticery—boards can be found there advertising jobs, leaving messages for people, sharing gossip, and the like, though most patrons use the ink and paper left at their tables to leave notes, thoughts, and even poems, which are attached to the walls, creating an overlapping mosaic of information, news, and silliness.

Locals

Pevin Draivel (Neutral, Ordani human, he/him)

Pevin oversees Whistler's Tavern and enjoys keeping it aa raucous but intimate environment, but he is very protective of the written scraps that he has patrons leave on the walls, and tends to scour over them at the end of the day, as if looking for something. Pevin won't reveal what it is that he is after, but patrons have come up with theories ranging from finding a lost love to avoiding the assassin who for some reason may be trying to kill him.

Faral the Fearless (Chaotic Good, Arcurian Cor'ak, he/him)

Faral has lots of stories to tell. A few may even be true, but that's not the point - he's a bit of an institution in the various establishments of Restaurant Row where he tells tales of his time as an adventurer that can somehow never be verified, though that never stops new adventurers from trying to repeat them. Faral is also helpful if there are any disputes in Restaurant Row, always willing to scoop up any angry customers and allow them to fight again "as soon as he finishes his tale." By the time he's done, most of the time, the desire to fight has been replaced by either amusement or incredulity.

Jemble Kane (Chaotic Good, Ordani human, she/her)

Though she is technically a server, not a chef, Jemble is always coming up with an idea for a new food fusion or magically imbued drink and often interrupts herself in the middle of serving to rush off and try to whip up something new. Though this can be disconcerting, her concoctions are delicious enough that she has been hired away from her current restaurant at least four times.

Tidwick Lassinger (Lawful Good, Ordani thornling, they/them)

As someone who does not eat food themselves, Tidwick is possibly the best choice Lillifeld could have made as their behind-the-scenes food store manager. Tidwick is organized, but more than that, they are fascinated by the idea of eating food and keep track of what Restaurant Row customers are having both by looking at what is in the Lillifeld food stores and by watching diners as they consume ffood. Their stare can be somewhat disconcerting, and they have a habit of occasionally going up to diners to ask why they've chosen a specific food combo, but they are generally thought to be harmless.

Lore

Once a set of food storage depots used by House Lilifeld, Restaurant Row was repurposed into a series of restaurants that showcase ingredients from the Trading House and its suppliers in the Arctus Plateau in an attempt to bring the House (which has always had less of a visible presence in Ordain than some of its counterparts) a bit of recognition. The ability to use it to try to control supply and demand has been a more recent — if welcome — discovery.
Restaurant Row.soverview: Restaurant Row is about more than the food served on the everchanging menus of the restaurants that line its streets - it's about the hospitality. While eagle-eyed diners can usually tell what food Trading House Lillifeld is trying to clear from its storehouses by what's being served up and down the street, the feel of each restaurant varies widely, ranging from the showmanship of freshly prepared catch of the day to the boisterous atmosphere of tavern snack stands to the whisper of contemplative tea houses.
Restaurant Row.sexposition: The smell of something cooking floats through the air as you enter the district they call Restaurant Row, but it’s hard to tell exactly what it is or where it’s coming from, given the number of eateries within view. They vary widely in style and offering, from stands offering quick hand-held takeaway food to open-air tables where diners can watch the world go by as they eat their meal to wooden doors that swing open every so often to reveal the sounds of sloshing drinks and hearty laughter.

The Trawl.name: The Trawl
The Trawl.text:
• District Type: Residential and Industry (shipping, cargo freight, warehouses)

  • Population: 17,639 (Fairly dense central location with mixed-use dwellings)

  • Lifestyle: Flashy (residents revere the pirate's life and earning reputation through bold action)

  • Services: Cargo ships (leasing, repairs, cargo storage)

  • Influence: House Bastilla's main base of operations for active members

Culture

Though much of the work in the Trawl involves the not-so-glamorous tasks of moving cargo onto and off of cargo ships, the influence of House Bastilla gives everything a bit of flair, as locals attempt to impress both the Trading House and the captains that dock at the Trawl with public expressions of their competence and bravery. House Bastilla encourages this action, as it keeps coin moving through the district and into the Trading House’s pockets, and uses its Tradeway not just as a place to store and sell goods, but a “see and be seen” area that gives anyone looking to make a name for themselves a literal platform on which to do it.

One side benefit of the flair and flash that the Trawl is known for is the distraction it provides from some of House Bastilla’s more illicit activities. The Trading House’s official stance is that there is nothing beneath the docks except for storage, but it is well known that the Underdocks are used to bring goods that might otherwise be examined by the Hallows for their potentially dangerous magic into the city. For a price, many workers at the Trawl will store these arcane goods in the Underdocks while unloading ships, coming back at night to move them further into the city. Unfortunately, with the Underdocks prone to occasional flooding, arcane items are sometimes lost to sea in the area, and some believe that the waters in this area have strange and arcane powers as a result.

In one of the city’s most exciting annual events, the Platform Plunge, a few brave souls jump from the platform outside of the House Bastilla Tradeway into these waters to prove their bravery and show off for ships looking for new crew. It is rare to take part in the plunge twice, and some claim to have come back changed by whatever arcane forces might be lurking in the water, though this has never been proven.

Landmarks

House Bastilla Tradeway

Located in a repurposed fish market that they’ve had on loan from Lillifeld for at least 100 years (an endless source of mild bickering between the two). The back half of the tradeway is reserved for goods going to the trading houses, other shops, and other major players in Ordain, but the front half offers a number of goods for sale directly to the public, and can be a great source for those looking for obscure arcane items or items from foreign ports.

Platform

This rowdy boardwalk and tavern, located outside of the House Bastilla Tradeway, is a popular place for merchants to gather, trade information, and look for new recruits. As a result, hopeful sailors often show off in the area, spending coin ostentatiously or showing off their knot tying skills in between drinks. The Platform Plunge takes place from this area each year, and is hyped up by the Tradway-owned bar, which rakes in a decent amount of coin selling seats to the spectacle each year.

Surrelli's Ships

The place to go if you want to either buy/lease a merchant or try to procure passage on one. The owners, Survan and Elli (each of whom took those names when they joined the shop - a requirement of the original owners), often try to suss out who can be taken advantage of by challenging those who want something from House Bastilla to "earn their way on board" with obscure items or challenges of strength and skill while they endlessly delay helping, but a simple bribe can smooth the way forward every time.

Locals

Telaviel “Three Hands” Ren (Neutral Evil, Ordani Human, he/him)

One of the main shopkeeps in the Tradeway, he retired from a career as a sailor after losing his taste for ship life during a particularly rough storm 20 years ago. He often refers to his exploits while on The Waterchaser, the ship he called home, which sank with all hands about 3 months after he left the sailing life behind. There are occasional rumors that he was thrown off of the ship for stealing and sank it himself out of vengeance, but nothing has or ever will be proven.

Irivani Andiva (Chaotic Neutral, Kithil Human, she/her)

Irivani Andiva was raised in Ordain, but always preferred life in the dark, becoming a devotee of Thoma and moving to the Kithil villages in her early teen years. Since her return to the city as an adult, she's worked her way up in House Bastilla, and claims to be a small-time merchant giving tours of the River Destine to new visitors. In truth, Irivani runs the traffic of arcane goods that the Hallows might frown on through the Underdocks, often sneaking goods under and past the watchful eye of Vala Surrel, her longtime counterpart in the trade of legitimate items. Irivani is very charming, using her personality to convince captains to work with her to get their goods into Ordain, and she has never lost a full shipment where the captain followed her exact orders, which often involve the use of magical decoys placed to lead Vala astray.

Vala Surrel (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Kiska, she/her)

The current Harbormaster of the Trawl, Vala is a fairly influential member of House Bastilla. She made her way to Ordain as a stowaway on the ship of the infamous Darion the Soulthief, and immediately began using her eye for arcane items to price items out and gain the coin needed to move up in the Trading House. Vala oversees all traffic and trade of legitimate goods through the docks, and is in a stalemate with her "counterpart," Irivani Andiva, who manages much of the traffic of less legitimate merchandise through the Underdocks. Though Vala generally works days and Irivani operates at night, the obvious chemistry between the two has led to a betting pool at local tavern Platform about if (and when) the two might become an item. While Vala ignores this, she has kept every magical decoy that Irivani has ever made to deceive her.

Lore

While the many local beliefs about the arcane-touched water in and around the Trawl are overblown by a large magnitude, in part to steer smugglers away from any thought of stealing from the ships under House Bastilla protection, those who have the ability to detect magic or have an ancestral resonance with it have been known to see a shimmer on the water in and around the Trawl. There are also persistent stories about those who have been somehow changed by the waters, though they will never quite say how, and it is unclear whether or not they are true.
The Trawl.soverview: The Trawl is the official dock for House Bastilla, used exclusively for its ships and those who agree to pay its docking fees to unload cargo. As it is nearly impossible for merchants to bring goods in and out of the city without agreeing to work with the powerful House Bastilla, the Trawl has become the arrival point for nearly all goods that make their into Ordain by sea. Much of what House Bastilla brings to port is brought to their nearby Tradeway for storage, sale, or trade, but rarer and more illicit items often make their way through the Underdocks beneath the Trawl to avoid the watchful eye of the Hallows, which worries about dangerous artifacts coming into the city.
The Trawl.sexposition: The flashiest boats in Ordain — which generally belong to Trading House Bastilla — often take a docking spot on the Trawl, drawing the eye as they unload their crates of arcane wonders. Those with a close eye, or who visit in the darker hours, may be able to spot some of the goods from each ship also make their way under the official docks through a winding set of floating wooden walkways. Locals claim that the water around the Trawl is somehow more electric in color because of the effects of these arcane treasures, but that claim has never been proven.

The Harborage.name: The Harborage
The Harborage.text:
• District Type: Residential with industry (dockwork, shipyards)

  • Population: 35,957 (Very dense population of newer residents and visitors arriving by sea)

  • Lifestyle: On The Move (New residents come and go as they get to know the city, and the dock is always open)

  • Services: Dock work and ships (ship construction and repair), New Resident Assistance (free and low-cost meals, housing boards, etc.)

Culture

The Harborage is one of the densest districts in Ordain, filled with those who are making their way to Ordain from afar by sea and those whose tireless efforts to build, maintain, and service both local and foreign ships keep trade and travel running smoothly. Ships can arrive at all hours, so there is always is a general hum of noise in the area, and the streets are rarely empty. Work in the dockyard and lights from incoming ships often shed light on the streets, and it is sometimes said by residents that the Harborage never rests.

For those who are new to Ordain, the Harborage can be overwhelming, but the many dock criers and greeters that spend time on the docks attempt to steer newcomers to the resources they need. Most of the time. There are always a few scam artists mixed in with the other criers, often offering a deal on foreign goods or a place to stay at what they claim is a low price but comes with punitive fees. No individual scammer lasts for too long, as the actual criers, who represent everything from the large Dockside Quarters residential complex to nearby restaurants on Restaurant Row the Harborage Healing House, are motivated to get rid of any imposters in their midst.

Between those selling goods, offering tours, and giving directions, the dockworkers of the Harborage come and go, working jobs that are steady but often far from routine. Some focus on ship repairs and others on construction of new sailing vessels, but they are most known for checking ships that come and go from Ordain to ensure that they're seaworthy enough to dock safely and leave Ordain smoothly. Someone must always be working at the docks, in case of an unexpected arrival, and shift workers come and go, often stopping in at the Harborage Seam for gossip and a free meal either before or after their daily shift. While their jobs are ostensibly just about keeping ships afloat, the dock workers also try not to let anyone fall through the cracks in Ordain, running a number of successful new resident programs out of the main Dockside Quarters complex, where decades-long residents and plucky newcomers often live side by side.

Landmarks

Dockside Quarters

This massive residential building in the center of the Harborage provides most of the housing in the district. While its living spaces can vary widely in size, shape, and utilization of magic, the true heart of the Quarters (as most locals call it) is its many communal spaces, where residents can enjoy views of the water, work on projects, and get to know more about the city. Though the Quarters' very active Working Committee is open to anyone who has lived in the Quarters for at least a season, it is generally run by retired Harborage dockworkers, who use their long connections in the city to bring special events and speakers to the Quarters for the residents' enjoyment.

The Dockyard

The dockyard is the major employer of the Harborage, and always has at least a partial crew on hand to deal with any unforeseen arrivals or sudden emergencies. Dockworkers start in the dockyard as general workers, learning ships in and out. Once they have proven their proficiency, they generally take a specialization in shipbuilding, ship repair, or inspection. Each of the three attracts a different set of workers — ship repairers often spend some time sailing, or are settling down on land after barely escaping with their lies at sea, while shipbuilders are known for their precision architecture and use of magic, and inspectors are generally the most boisterous, in part to counter the negativity that captains have when their ships are being looked over for seaworthiness.

The Harborage Seam

This large open-air plaza provides meals to Harborage workers and residents. The dining tables sit under a number of repurposed sails, which shield it from the worst of any inclement weather, and diners can choose whether to take a free meal, pay for it, or pay extra to provide food for others. The Cindaric Sages provide for any shortfall, and the Seam's chief supplier uses relationships with House Lillifeld and the restaurants of nearby Restaurant Row to procure ingredients that might otherwise go bad and provide a place to work for aspiring chefs who wish to try their hands at providing large quantities of food each day. Many well-known chefs are known to take shifts at the Seam, which helps to keep up its reputation for simple but filling meals. It also is one of the best places in the district to get news, as the large communal tables encourage conversation, welcome, and a lot of gossip.

Locals

Divonnay (Lawful Good, Ordani human, she/her)

Genial ship inspector Divonnay is determined that everyone in the Quarters be enjoying their lives, believing that any individual who is facing emotional distress is as much an issue as a crack in a ship's hull. Though she can be an overbearing busybody at times, determined to set up singles, write letters to bad managers, and otherwise interfere in the life of anyone in the Quarters who looks like they have a problem, the fact that she doesn't mean anything negative by it generally makes her a mild annoyance rather than a major Quarters problem. It doesn't hurt that Divonnay throws a really great party, and has helped to organize the criers on the docks to better direct new arrivals to places where they can get any help they need.

Elvar Andraad (Neutral Evil, Ordani Soulbound, he/him)

Elvar has been working on the docks for as long as he can remember — and he can remember a lot. It is said that Elvar has built at least 500 ships, which seems somewhat improbable, but his branded initials can be found on many ships, including those that have no record of being built in Ordain, or having been created recently. In truth, Elvar drowned as an apprentice shipbuilder over a century ago, but has refused to move on, becoming a Soulbound with a ddriving desire to build the perfect ship, at which point he believes he will move on. Unfortunately, over time, he has become increasingly corrupted by his state, and now creates a flaw in each ship he designs so that he can live forever, using enchantments and bribes to hide the truth of who he is from those around him.

Zale (True Neutral, Bejak Wirrun, they/them)

Though Zale is far from the only cook working at the Harborage Seam, they definitely have one of the strongest reputations for intriguing flavor combinations, and dockworkers have been known to switch shifts in order to schedule their meals for whenever Zale is in charge of the kitchen. While several Restaurant Row establishments have tried to lure Zale away from their current gig, they refuse, in part because they enjoy the work, and in part because their food includes all of the flavors favored by their sister Ivellia, who was separated from them at sea years ago, and who they hope will one day taste one of their meals and find them for a long-awaited reunion.

Lore

The Harborage grew fairly organically as the city did — when docks were needed, docks were built; when housing was needed, a warehouse was turned into housing; when a visitor to Ordain was found to be stealing food out of hunger, a place to eat was created. Or at least that's how the Harborage tells it. Nothing was quite as easy as that, often requiring deals to be made, systems to be set up, and information to be shared, but in each case, the dockworkers have been a strong voice, using their influence within the Hallows and importance to a portside city to insist on the things that they believed would make the Harborage a better and stronger community.
The Harborage.soverview: For those who make their way into Ordain by sea, the Harborage is often the first place they settle in Ordain. Unlike the Trawl, where House Bastilla focuses on the goods moving to and fro by sea, the Harborage is a place for the travelers who come to Ordain by sea, with docks for both larger ocean vessels and small skiffs. Many don't make it further in, settling into the dense residential complexes that advertise river views and sharing space with the workers who live and work adjacent to the docks to form an ever-changing but tight-knit community amidst the hustle and bustle.
The Harborage.sexposition: The broad docks of the Harborage are nearly always filled with folks coming and going, whether they are boarding a vessel, making their way deeper into the city, or settling in at home with their small view of the water. The smell of food wafts through the air in and around the crowds, luring people into a large covered plaza filled with simple food and boisterous conversation between well-established locals and curious newcomers.

Ordain Flats.name: Ordain Flats
Ordain Flats.text:
The Ordain Flats are comprised of numerous districts that tend to share a common social philosophy in addition to their relative geographical features: one of comfort and prosperity. The Flats contain several neighborhoods defined by their local businesses or the very people who live there, with a regular emphasis on safe and affordable residential housing — even in the most industrial of areas.

Environment

While the wide cobblestone streets of the Flats are considered standard terrain in most instances, they tend to be so full of urban traffic (from local citizens on foot, to the occasional hand-cart or beast of burden) that the avenues are justifiably difficult to navigate during peak hours of commerce and trade. Still, navigating the streets of the Flats remains a simple enough task; the city planners took this traffic into account, and the broad whitestone plazas between each district allow the tides of foot traffic to flow remarkably unhindered. Ordain is a city that's been built to be lived in, and the environment is a constant reflection of that intention.

Ecology

There are several places throughout the Ordain Flats where flora and fauna have been dutifully cultivated. Ample gardens and parks dot the landscape here, with an impressive array of supplemental efforts by locals; potted plants line countless storefronts and windows, carefully maintained courtyards are everywhere, and even a few entire districts are dedicated to the preservation of nearby flora and fauna from the Arctus Plateau. Nature is never far from the Flats, where birds are known to perch on the city's ornate ledges to sing their songs, and beloved pets accompany their owners during daily business.

Lore

The Ordain Flats are sprawling enough to be rather disconnected when it comes to the history of their development. However, the Cindaric Sages and the Ordinate were directly involved in the zoning of these districts as they were settled; a key interest throughout these historical expansions, and well on into the future, is the comfortable habitation of Ordain's citizens alongside their means for survival.

Because of the relative quietude and safety of the various districts that comprise this urban biome, the Ordain Flats are a place where one can potentially get away with anything. A few neighborhoods actually play host to clandestine locations, with denizens of unsavory or illicit aims. Yet, as small as these organizations tend to be, they rarely pose a severe threat to the people of Ordain at large (for now).
Ordain Flats.soverview: The districts of this sprawling urban biome are readily identified by the hustle and bustle of the people who live and work within. Neighborhoods defined by trade, artistry, culture, and the simple pleasures of day-to-day life can be found here, bedecked with intricate murals and ablaze with color from decorative Ordani banners. This area pulses with an unyielding energy and liveliness, where Ordani citizens can live their lives in spectacular fashion.
Ordain Flats.sexposition: Glittering flagstones of white stone weave their way through bustling city blocks, while the roads and alleyways crisscross between busy shops, tradeways, well-kept townhouses, and residential buildings. Colorful banners and expansive murals adorn the walls of the buildings as the city sprawls across the leveled areas of the great Ordani city. Foot traffic is high as most of the population goes about their daily lives, and the noise of metropolitan chatter surrounds you from nearly every direction. From almost any street corner, you can spy the towers and keeps of the Ordain Spires, which loom regally overhead.

Ordain Spires.name: Ordain Spires
Ordain Spires.text:
Ordain's spires form the outer edges of the city, taking advantage of the natural hills in the Arctus Plateau that likely convinced the travelers who first made their way to the inlet to choose it as their home. Though the spires are home to several districts dominated by Ordani government and administrative needs, the term spires is most commonly used to refer to the residential neighborhoods nestled between them, where city life is a little slower paced and often a bit more luxurious.

Environment

A set of well-maintained paths and interconnected platforms connect many of the spires districts, giving those who live there an easy way to move around the city without needing to cross from one side to the other. For those who work, shop, or enjoy the culture found in the Flats and Docks, most districts have at least one set of stairs or paved road that leads directly into the center of the city.

Ecology

The Spires have little plant or animal life to speak of outside of curated green spaces created by their residents, with one major exception. Many birds enjoy nesting in nooks and crannies found in the high places in the spires, and can be seen flying in and out of the area at all hours. Some districts in the spires even attempt to attract specific types of birds, seemingly for their beauty, though their ability to carry messages over long distances may add to their appeal.

Lore

Primarily built during Ordain's first big expansion, after key trading routes and materials were secured, the Spires are said to represent a city deciding how it should govern itself - though there are several residential districts within the Spires, which are often what is most closely associated with the word spires today, it is also the area that holds the Ordinate and Hallows (which make and manage the city's laws}, the Temple Ward and Cindarin Temple districts (which provide spiritual guidance), and All-Fable Keep (which holds many of the city's historical artifacts and knowledge).
Ordain Spires.soverview: The Ordain Spires dominate the skyline of Ordain and offer sweeping views of the bustling metropolis below while staying somewhat removed from the controlled chaos at the heart of the city. Though the spires do include the Hallows, where lively debate and performance can be found at all hours of the day and night, most of the other administrative and religious districts found in the area have a more formal feel, and the residential districts around them are often quieter and more settled than those found in the Flats or Docks.
Ordain Spires.sexposition: The first thing most visitors see of Ordain is its white stone spires, rising dramatically from the plateau around them as if reaching for the sky and able to be seen for miles. Caravans traveling over the golden flats of the Arctus Plateau make their way toward the spires as if they were beacons. Sailors glimpsing them over the horizon know their journey is coming to an end. Tall and proud, these symbols of Ordain stand on the natural cliffs that have shielded Ordain from danger since its earliest days, marking the outer edge of one of Ember's greatest cities.

All-Fable Keep.name: All-Fable Keep
All-Fable Keep.text:
• District Type: Institutional with some Commercial

  • Services: Treasure-hunting guild (historical research, artifacts, antiques, appraisal).

  • Population: 600

  • Languages: Common, Arcden, Imperial, Cascilian, Luma

  • Cost of Living: Comfortable-to-Wealthy

The aged and handsome edifice known as All-Fable Keep serves as the storied base of operations of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} in Ordain, where it occupies most of its local district. The Keep acts as both guildhall and training facility for its motley fellowship, who come and go like the wind while they attend to official guild business throughout the Arctus Plateau. All-Fable Keep also famously plays host to the Amaranthine Archives, an esteemed museum facility that houses a most impressive collection of distinct treasures and notable antiques.

The Anachraenum takes in more artifacts and antiques than they would like to maintain; so, naturally, they turn their surplus into profit when the occasion allows. Gift shops in the museum offer antique trinkets and common magic items for sale, while more sophisticated buyers are allowed back-room access for high-tier purchases and private consignments. And just as the districts of southeastern Ordain look to the Anachraenum for local support in times of trouble, the city's people consider All-Fable Keep to be a major cultural repository, where the most important relics of Aterica's past are kept safe and secure. As they say: "a hint of ev'ry legend ever told lies somewhere in All-Fable's countless holds."

Landmarks

Amaranthine Archives

Also known as the Relic House, this venerated museum serves as the primary repository for the Anachraenum's vast collection of artifacts and antiques. Guild members who maintain the Archives host a quarterly rotation of thoughtfully curated exhibits, offered at the cost of a small donation thanks to the generous sponsorship of the Anachraenum's most elite patrons. To wit, this kind of sponsorship from affluent members of society makes up the lion’s share of the guild’s regular income. Furthermore, rumors persist about a network of secret tunnels beneath the Archives that leads to various points of interest throughout Ordain — and there is indeed some truth to this, but public understanding of this surreptitious architecture is tenuous at best.

The Orrery

This large circular chamber is bedecked with a hulking mechanical model of Ember's cosmos, and is outfitted with a variety of scientific and arcane devices used for long-distance observation, including everything from telescopes to crystal balls.
