The model of the cosmos is an intricate mechanism that is capable of simulating the rotation of Ember's sun and moons, while some of the observatory equipment allows guild members to actually view those heavenly bodies from the confines of the Keep's top floor. The Orrery is maintained by a manic warlock of Volta named Barnabas Hilheth (CG, Kithil Kivahr, he/him), who is often consumed by his arcane research for excessively long hours of the day.

The Chamber of Agaseros

Powered by magic and esoteric technology, this massive arena in the lower levels of All-Fable Keep was made to train Anachraenum guild members in a variety of combat and exploration techniques. The dynamic features of this self-transforming chamber are designed to challenge the acrobatic and athletic capabilities of anyone who enters, along with their ability to think fast and react to immediate danger or complex puzzles. Occasionally, the Anachraenum will loosen the restrictions on this private room for those eager or impetuous enough to try their own turn at surviving the Risk Chamber's gauntlet (a privilege typically reserved for vetted allies or wealthy patrons).

The Risk Chamber is managed by the retired swashbuckler Aelen Morde (CG, Arcturian Human, he/him), who oversees the dangerous arena with madcap enthusiasm and sadistic glee. Treat Morde as an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmAssassin000000]{Assassin} with a Strength score of 15.

Locals

@UUID[Actor.FYprIclhoDOI8FI4]{Arcos Sarinland} (NG, Ordani Keth, he/him)

Arcos Sarinland was once a promising young ranger who joined the Anachraenum forty years ago and became a close friend of Darion Bastilla. He was widely celebrated for his participation in the Battle of the Throat, where a combined fleet led by Darion destroyed the Blood Barons' assembling ships in Golden Bay; however, he retired from active adventuring not long after. For thirty years, he taught and guided new members in Ordain, always maintaining a friendly yet troubled demeanor. Recently thrust into the guild's leadership after Fernis Ossa declined the nomination, he faces a number of increasing challenges as Ordain slips further into unrest.

@UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} (LG, Ordani Ashka, she/her)

Fernis Ossa is one of the most well-known and admired Anachraenum members living in Ordain. She led a group of adventurers called the Skywarders many years ago before effectively becoming the envoy and deputy to the previous guildmaster, Veron Longspear. She spent many years among the people of Ordain, and her adventurous spirit is matched only by her dedication to her friends and comrades. Fernis often organizes gatherings and events in Ordain and travels to many nearby friendly cities like Luen, Wick, and the Lumek city of Hearth. She has a genuine interest in the stories and lives of the people she meets.

@UUID[Actor.GA8VFWysoIYfNWCL]{Adelyne Goss}( NG, Waerd Human, she/her)

Loremistress Adelyne Goss is a sarcastic and sharp character, and despite her extensive physical injuries sustained after battling a dragon deep in the Duskflare Jungles many years ago, she remains an intensely insightful and productive scholar and librarian. She is also extremely proud of her Waerd heritage and wears a combination of traditional Waerd clothing interwoven with ancient Sedyri trinkets.

Lore

In addition to the organization's vast collection of antiques, the magical and technological assets of the Anachraenum are numerous. For nearly a hundred years, this storied group has successfully explored some of Ember’s most dangerous landscapes in search of legendary ruins from bygone ages; and the vaults of All-Fable Keep are lined with the most precious fruits of their antiquarian labors. For the hundreds of arcane relics and objets d'art that decorate their public displays, there are hundreds more hidden away from common view.

Some notable relics include: the Amethyst Skeleton of St. Prestyn, the Sword of Arctus, the Silver Raiment of Lost Aed’Orna, the fabled Entropy Stone, and the largest collection of paintings and illustrations from the late clairvoyant fantasist Varan Fel.
All-Fable Keep.soverview: This fortified stone keep serves as the primary headquarters of the treasure-hunting guild known as the Anachraenum, a tightly-knit organization of explorers, researchers, and historians stationed in Ordain. In addition to grand chambers like museums, libraries, and vaults that cater to the guild's ongoing interests, All-Fable Keep provides comfortable housing for most of the guild's local members, as well as semi-secret training facilities for Anachraenum operations. Several of the Keep's museum galleries are actually open to the public; and the venerated guildhall — despite the clandestine airs of the guild itself — has become a source of cultural pride for many citizens of Ordain, particularly those who prize scholasticism and adventure.
All-Fable Keep.sexposition:
A massive fortified keep draped in antiquity towers above the district here, standing nearly five stories high above the city's cobblestoned streets. Several smaller structures are built up around this central edifice, whose architecture seems curiously older than Ordain itself. Unlike most of the city's other landmark buildings, there is a relative quietude to this place, suggesting a gentle air of privacy within its furthest reaches.

In spite of this tranquility (or perhaps because of it), scholars, guild members, and visitors alike can be seen reposing among the district's exterior walkways and balconies. Furthermore, you spy a bronze emblem hanging above the tower's large front gate: a sextant fashioned into the likeness of a capital "A."

Lantern Roads.name: Lantern Roads
Lantern Roads.text:
• District Type: Residential with some commercial (niche shops, mail services, illicit goods)

  • Population: 8,512 (Moderately dense population of residents who appreciate privacy and thieves who use that privacy for contraband)

  • Lifestyle: Secretive (Both regular residents and thieves take advantage of the shadows and alleys in the district and don't ask too many questions)

  • Services: Lanterns, courier services, movement of illicit goods

  • Influences: Unofficially affiliated with Trading House Wandren

Culture

Lantern Roads is easy to get lost in, mostly by design. It was once a storage area that began working to deter thieves and bandits by keeping goods moving from place to place, and its residents usually own more than one space in the area, moving from one to the next over the course of the year and using the shadowboxes on their windows to provide clues about their current location. This has made the district an ideal place for those who move illicit goods through Ordain, though the area also attracts those who wish to keep a low profile or hide out from those who may wish them harm. Many of the otherwise small homes and shops have secret access to tunnels, false walls, and other ways to move people and goods from one place to the next without moving out in the open, which is complemented by the work of spellcasters who use magical light and darkness within the neighborhood’s winding streets to draw the eye of observers away from where important deliveries and pick-ups are happening.

In addition to their practical use in indicating what can be found inside of a particular home or establishment, or in sending messages to hidden contacts, the tableau windows of Lantern Roads have become a distinctive decorative element of the area, often shown off during local festivals, when they are used to tell stories of Ordain's history and share current gossip. Different groups within Lantern Roads use different strategies to create these shadowbox windows, with some preferring small mechanical devices called shadowcasters that create specific and elaborate scenes when backlit, some using ribbons and hand-made puppets, and others relying on illusion magic. This has also made the district somewhat popular with avant-garde theater houses, whose odd light shows and limited audiences fit in beside the other specialty shops in the region.

Landmarks

The Lighthouse

A safehouse operated by House Wandren that connects the alleys of Lantern Roads with the lofty heights of Marlstone via a network of back alleys. Named in jest because its ground floor entrance is found in a completely shadowed doorway. Currently occupied by Vitt Wandren.

The Prancing Goat

A tavern and waystation for gossip that moves throughout Lantern Road, hosted by whoever manages the property that it currently sits within. It can always be found by looking for a goat hidden within a tableau in the area - whichever shadowbox currently has it in the background holds the bar's current location.

Shadowbos Souvenirs

Believed to be one of the oldest buildings in Lantern Roads, it is one of the few that does not use light in its picture window, opting instead for a display of swirling shadows. It also does not move, making it a strong reference point for anyone visiting the area. Despite its somewhat foreboding facade, it holds only a small souvenir shop, which sells small shadowcasters to those who wish to make their own shadow displays at home and is a staging ground for locals who make their money on tours.

Terracini's Tavern

Taking its name from the legendary thief Terracini, and run by Penni Terracini, who is no relation and was born Penne Talarand before taking over an empty storefront in the area, this Tavern always looks completely empty, other than when it hosts a show by one of the avant-garde illusionist groups that use it as a theater space. That said, there are a number of deals that go down in the Tavern, which uses some of the same magic found throughout the Lantern Roads to hide a few corners and shadowy back rooms where the real action happens.

Locals

Cavilla Rossin (Neutral, Arcturian Human, she/her)

Cavilla relocated to Lantern Roads to hide out after inheriting a bunch of goods from a group of bandits that attacked her and died in the process, leaving her with all of their goods. Unsure what to do with the somewhat ill-gotten gains, she spends her time in Lantern Roads trying to move some of the goods and do "good works" that will assuage a bit of her guilt about some of the items, which include some sentimental treasures that the bandits once stole.

Fozil Dalm (Lawful Good, Ordani Signborn, he/him)

The owner of a barely successful watchmaking enterprise, Just in Time, which sells watches that are notoriously bad at consistently telling time. He has been trying to use his lack of business sense to become one of House Wandren's contraband runners for years, but it is well-known in the district that he is an informant for the Veiled Chain, and locals wishing to keep their enemies close periodically buy watches from him to keep his business afloat.

Penni Terracini (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human,she/her)

A failed thief who has rebranded themselves, taking on the name of the famed Lantern Roads scoundrel Terracini and running Terracini's Tavern, which serves drink but also hosts a group of illusionists who hold impromptu theater shows that showcase the latest in light and illusion magic.

Vitt Wandren (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, they/them)

Vitt keeps a general eye on how goods are moving through Lantern Roads as part of their role as a member of House Wandren. They take liberal bribes from those in the area in a protection racket that threatens to disassociate local residents and stores with House Wandren if they don't pay up. Vitt has noticed some of the recent changes within the House and is resistant to them, not because of any loyalty to Ordain or the House, but because they believe it will cut into their profits.

Lore

Lantern Roads was originally home only to storage areas for goods that came into Ordain by sea, but after a series of high-profile thefts during Ordain’s early days, many members of House Wandren began living in their storehouses and storing goods in their homes. To confuse thieves, groups of Wandren associates would work together to purchase properties and use them interchangeably for living, storage, and sales, making it unclear where valuable goods would be stored and could be intercepted.

The origin of the use of lightboxes is less clear, though some believe it was a ploy by the great thief Terracini, who agreed to turn himself into authorities by asking them to meet him at the "House of Shadows" on a specific day and then paid his neighbors to create shadowboxes so that they could not determine which house was the correct one.
Lantern Roads.soverview: Nestled between the high plateaus of Marlstone and Coinwealth Heights, two of Ordain’s wealthiest neighborhoods, Lantern Roads is an assortment of narrow streets and alleyways known for its tableau windows, which use light and shadow to create vignettes showcasing everything from daily life to local gossip— as well as a large assortment of hidden storage areas and internal tunnels used by House Wandren to store goods and transport them behind the scenes to its Tradeway in Marlstone.
Lantern Roads.sexposition: Lights dance through the narrow warren of streets in Lantern Roads, cast both by the lanterns hanging from the buildings and the many lightboxes that decorate the district's large picture windows. Each uses light and shadow to create an image that gives a small hint as to who resides inside — from a set of clasped hands to an abstract image of leaves in a forest to a family crest. While visitors stroll through the mostly quiet streets admiring their beauty, only the residents of the area seem to know what each one truly means, and they aren't often talking, moving quickly from one corner of the district to another as they slip from lit passageways into the many shadows of the district's twisting streets.

Marlstone.name: Marlstone
Marlstone.text:
• District Type: Residential

  • Population: 963 (Wealthy residents, especially if they are members of House Wandren)

  • Lifestyle: Lavish (Residents live in luxurious estates and show off their possessions as a way of bringing sales and attention to House Wandrens)

  • Services:: High-end Entertainment (Galas, Showcases of Luxury Goods)

  • Influences: House Wandren is based in Marlstone

Culture

Marlstone is more than the substance used to build the district - it is also key to its development. The swirling colors in the rock are said to hold magical resonance, though that has never been fully proven. The rock is also fairly porous, making it easy to create passages out of, including a direct tunnel from nearby Lantern Roads to Marlstone that has become a haven for the movement of illicit goods by House Wandren. Most homes in Marlstone also have underground passages to at least 2 or 3 neighboring homes, based on alliances in the early days of the neighborhood. These have now created a complex web of passageways, many filled either with traps or dead-ends, and are collectively known as the Marls.

Within Marlstone, the tight-knit community believes in keeping its own secrets and solving its own problems. While people from Marlstone will not say much about the neighborhood other than to talk about its fabulous parties or work raising funds for the city's betterment, within Marlstone, gossip is rife, with evergreen topics including whose business ventures are not going well, possibly forcing them to move out of the neighborhood, who is currently enabling House Wandren shenanigans (which all Marlstone residents claim to be against but often benefit from and participate in), and the back-and-forth of planning Marlstone's regular events, which include lunar celebrations, seasonal observations, and other excuses to show off.

Landmarks

The Arch

House Wandren's tradeway, known locally as the Arch, is the hub of the trading houses's activities and is made up of two buildings on either side of the top of the Beaconage. They are joined together by an arch whose materials and design changes seasonally, and House Wandren hosts regular contests to determine who will design the arch next, as it can be seen from high vantage points around the city. On either side of the arch, the Tradeway itself is made from marlstone. As the stone is porous and has a tendency to crumble, making it suitable mostly as a paving stone, the Tradeway's ability to maintain it is seen as a reflection of their strength. In truth, the buildings are made from veined marble and simply disguised to look as if they are marlstone — a classic House Wandren subterfuge.

Beaconage

Beaconage, which begins in Lantern Roads and runs uphill into and around Marlstone, is the only real street in the district - it loops through, crossing over itself, and is confusing for outsiders, as addresses on Beaconage are designated by the light feature in front of the home instead of by a specific number. These light features keep Beaconage lit, but can be extinguished at the desires of the residents, plunging all of Marlstone into darkness and fending off any unwanted intruders or outsiders.

The Marls

Small underground passageways in Marlstone that usually connect one or two estates to each other. It is said that the specific connections reveal something about early alliances between estate owners, but no one remembers exactly what they are, and the one comprehensive list of the marls, a project of local muckraker Jent Keritz, has conveniently gone missing. Though Jent is never shy to share their outrage at the latest goings-on in the neighborhood, they are oddly silent about where the project they once bragged about might have gone.

Marlstone Manor

The most prominent mansion in Marlstone due to its impressive height, Marlstone Manor has had other names over the years as it passed between different owners, but most eventually fell on hard times. Local superstition says that naming it anything other than Marlstone Manor brings bad luck to the owners. The manor is famous for its glass panels, which avoid fully blocking the views of any other building while catching the eye with their impressive water features. The building also plays host, every year, to the Marlstone Gala, an event where the powerful and influential mix and mingle while showing off the latest fashions.

Locals

Rathani Biquer (LN Ordani keth, she/her)

Rathani delivers mail and packages better than anyone else in Marlstone, easily making her way through the Beaconage and translating the addresses written by the senders to the complex set of lantern-based addresses within Marlstone. Several locals have attempted to take advantage of this and get her to carry extra packages, but she appears to be so straightforward in her understanding of the world that she doesn't know when she's being bribed. In truth, Rathani is a major informant for the Veiled Chain, keeping close tabs on what happens in the district during her daily mail runs.

Dina Kalfe (NE Ordani human, she/her)

Dina believes in that variety is the spice of life, and prefers to experience that variety in the form of high-end artifacts that will impress those who visit her at her lavish estate, especially those with extensive histories or that come from very distant ports. She is willing to provide funding to travelers that will bring her back the goods she wants, whether they are Anachraenum expeditions or House Wandren ventures. Where she got her money is a mystery, and those who ask don't last long.

Jent Keritz (CE Ordani human, they/them)

Though it is technically anonymous, Jent Keritz is widely known to be the publisher of The Beacon, a publication that only exists within Marlstone (the paper bursts into flame and crumbles to ash if taken outside of the neighborhood's boundary lines). The Beacon claims to "shine a light" on the important goings-on in the neighborhood, and is in fact a good source of local news, but is also deeply petty, as Jent appears to have a grudge against nearly everyone in the neighborhood and routinely skews coverage based on who they currently like, dislike, or fear.

Tevvan Wandren (CN Ordani human, he/him)

Tevvan Wandren is not a member of House Wandren at all, but has worked at the Wandren Tradeway for years organizing events and enjoys a certain amount of status as a result - status that he wants everyone to be fully aware of. Though usually the House would frown upon their name being used by someone who is not a member, he has learned a few secrets over his time at the Tradeway that the house would not want to come out and traded his silence for association with the house.

Lore

The history of the Marlstone district is shrouded in mystery. For one thing, no one knows where the marlstone that the district has been made out of came from. Rumor has it that House Wandren acquired it from House Bastilla during its earliest days, after leaving the House to form their own concern, but this can't be proven.

It is believed that a true history of Marlstone would reveal how to get into some of its wealthiest estates through hidden entrances now lost to time. As a result, historians who have tried to trace exactly how Marlstone came together or how its houses connect to each other are routinely given the cold shoulder throughout the district and often find their path forward plunged into darkness. Even attempts to officially map the beaconage are frowned upon.
Marlstone.soverview: Marlstone is one of the closest things that Ordain has to a gated community. Somewhat isolated from its surrounding neighborhoods due to its height, and in a desirable location in the city thanks to its views of both the harbor and the Arctus Plateau, it is filled with manors of those who have either wealth or desire privacy - usually both. While there are several routes into Marlstone, all are controlled by the residents on some level - the Marlstone Crossings are temporary bridges used primarily for events that can be quickly retracted from the Marlstone side if desired and the winding Beaconage road between Lantern Roads and Marlstone can be extinguished from Marlstone, making it difficult to move through the darkened street.
Marlstone.sexposition: Tucked away between high towers toward the edge of the city, this neighborhood of wealthy Ordani socialites is paved with marlstone, whose swirling colors are mirrored in the elaborate light fixtures in front of each home. Each lamppost or lantern provides dappled light that illuminates visitors and provides cover to the privacy-loving residents. Through the streets of Marlstone are often quiet, a murmur of music and conversation can often be heard from the House Wandren Tradeway, which sits at the end of the Marlstone's one winding street and plays host to elegant parties that often serve as showcases for hard-to-find luxury goods.

Scholar's Nook.name: Scholar's Nook
Scholar's Nook.text:
• District Type: Commercial with some Residential

  • Population: 7,662 (Medium. Book stores, shops, and housing with moderate foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Comfortable-to-Wealthy (Scholars, publication professionals, retired citizens).

  • Services: Book-making, libraries, education, spellcasting, consignment, lodging.

  • Influences: Early Signaran/Signborn influence.

Binder's Row is one of Ordain's most commercially-minded academic districts, where the private exchange of books and related goods is just as important as the neighborhood's public library and education services. Indeed, important landmarks like the Old City Library draw interested readers here from the entire Plateau over. Furthermore, the name Binder's Row is actually a double entendre that speaks to the district's origins.

A wealthy Signborn conjurer and book collector named Mordus Kôl helped settle and develop the district alongside the Cindaric Sages who built Old City Library. It is often said (but rarely known for certain) that Kôl summoned a powerful fiendish entity from Signara to help accumulate his esoteric collection of arcane tomes and manuals, and that this creature lurks beneath the streets of Binder's Row to this very day. Whether locals consider this tale to be rumor or truth, there's no mistaking that a certain legacy of conjuration in Binder's Row has endured.

Landmarks

Old City Library

Also known as Tomehold, this venerable library is maintained by a group of Cindaric Sages known as the Coalescents, and serves as a repository of all modern and historical knowledge regarding the planet Ember — including famous natural and supernatural landmarks, the ecology of Ember's metaphysical resources, and chronicles of the various shard gods. Many initiates of the Cindaric Order begin their training here, where the tenets of the Sages have been recorded since Adonia founded the great city of Ordain.

The Crooked Spine

This serpentine alleyway is named for its winding and circuitous streetscape, which is crowded with a variety of specialty bookshops, many of which are dingy havens for dusty, forgotten tomes. Used book stores, smut vendors, and printers of scandal rags are in ready supply here, where nearly two dozen ramshackle business are crammed on top of each other. Of particular note is Ashton's Rare Books, a bookshop that caters to collectors of rare tomes and specializes in the delicate restoration of aged texts; a capricious bookbinder named Ashton Smythe (CN, Waerd Human, he/him) owns and operates this sought-after establishment.

The Secret Shelf

Those in search of low-level conjuration and divination spellcasting services or rare arcane tomes need look no further than this eccentric magic shop on the northeast edge of the district, owned and operated by Kastilla Kôl (LN, Ordani Signborn, she/her) and her younger brother Yura (LN, Ordani Signborn, he/him). These capricious Signborn siblings each harbor a bit of their ancestor Mordus Kôl's proclivity for spellcasting — headstrong Kastilla with her conjurations, and apprehensive Yura with his divinations.

The Gadrick Estate

A modest but charming public library founded by the late fantasist Erison Gadrick. Maintained by his successors and funded by an array of wealthy Ordani philanthropists, several of which remain anonymous.

The Inkswell Bookshop

A bookshop with a small but loyal clientele, run by Darius Cevher. Famed for its selection of rare tomes and the gregariousness of its owner.

Librarium of Spectra

This grand temple was erected to honor @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, goddess of magic and knowledge, and is well-known throughout the continent for its elaborate display of arcanum and esoterica.

Scrivener's Den

A specialty equipment shop that caters to loremasters, cartographers, visual artists, and scribes. Many of the material components and fine inks needed to copy spells can be purchased here, along with a variety of amusing occult curios.

Locals

Miles Melfield (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

This precocious Cindaric Sage serves as the senior Coalescent at Old City Library, and is a generally helpful and attentive fellow despite his penchant for humorous protest. His extensive arcane research has also afforded Miles a small compliment of wizardly spellcasting.

Elden Jhonda (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

This aged fortune teller is a purveyor of false hopes and dreams, brought to life by little more than mind games and parlor tricks (with which she is most skilled). Despite an common understanding that Jhonda's prophecies and divinations are the stuff of fantasy, she remains a popular public figure — perhaps due to the flamboyant decor in the window of her shop and her own fun-loving, rambunctious personality.

Gregorius Prestyn (Chaotic Good, Arcturian Human, he/him)

A descendent of the legendary St. Prestyn, this famed Arcturian researcher occupies a humble apartment in Binder's Row, and is known to provide consultation services for organizations that value his extensive acumen (such as the Anachraenum and the Veiled Chain).

Lore

In addition to the legends concerning the late Mordus Kôl and his so-called fiendish servitor, rumors abound regarding the presence of a dungeon complex below the Old Town Library that's connected to the secret tunnels beneath the Anachraenum and other areas of southeastern Ordain. There is certainly some credence to these stories, but the Coalescents and other Cindaric Sages who attend Tomehold haven't actually used the dungeon passages in nearly a century.
Scholar's Nook.soverview: This academic district is defined by its commercial focus on the bookbinding trade, public and private libraries, bookstores, scholastic facilities, and the profitable exchange of information. A cozy residential sprawl can be found alongside these various businesses and community centers, whose residents — often absorbed in their intensive or erudite work — generally prefer to stay close to home. Scholar's Nook also enjoys wearing its love of learning and the written word on its sleeve; quotes are carved into the paving stones of the district's central plaza, carts of free books can be found around every other corner, and key moments from the history of Ordain are captured in friezes throughout the district.
Scholar's Nook.sexposition: A conspicuously cozy borough occupies this crowded corner of eastern Ordain, where the twisting cobbled streets are lined with countless timber shops and townhouses. If the wooden signs hanging above the myriad shops are any indication, many of the businesses here specialize in the book trade. Everything from used book stores to public libraries can be spotted among the cramped confines of this notably academic district. The aged neighborhood's lazy streets are full of shoppers, readers, and scholars — all going about their business with remarkable intention. And you'd wager more than a few interesting stories or secrets lurk in the dusty, unseen corners of this bookish part of town.

Stonework Hollow.name: Stonework Hollow
Stonework Hollow.text:
Though it was once a thriving quarry used by House Cevher, a catastrophic earthquake believed to have been tied to the deep drilling happening in the area led to its abandonment by the house. In the years since, the site has mostly gone back to nature, with wildlife taking over the sites that were once used by workers. Stonework Hollow is far enough from the city of Ordain that while it is closely intertwined with its history, its more natural threats pose no real danger to the city. Some enterprising businesses and workers have even taken to scavenging from what is left of the site, despite its potential dangers.

Environment

Stonework Hollow still shows some of the signs of the quarry it was when the earthquake hit, with carts smashed on the rocky floor and ropes that dangle to nowhere. Some of the fissures in the rock also show the promise of new veins of metal, though House Cevher has very strongly warned against digging any further into the area. Those who do face not only the natural threats that now exist in the area, but the threat of unstable rock outcroppings crushing them.

Ecology

Since being abandoned, Stonework Hollow has become occupied by several creatures common to rocky environments, including Cave Wasps, Ketral, Crag Raptors, and an occasional Suarrok.

Lore

While it is widely believed that House Cevher did something wrong in their safety protocols that led to the Stonehollow Quake, there is no evidence that this is actually true. In the days following the quake, some within the trading house argued that they should prove their innocence, but Ralton Cevher believed it would be disrespectful to the victims of the quake to argue about who was to blame, and the belief that House Cevher caused the disaster has now solidified, much to the joy of the Trading House's political foes.
Stonework Hollow.soverview: Stonework Hollow is the mostly-emptied rock quarry that was used to provide much of the stone of Ordain during its building boom. In recent years, it has been associated with the Stonehollow Quake, an earthquake that coincided with a push to remove more rock from the quarry that has been widely blamed on Trading House Cevher.
Stonework Hollow.sexposition: The large quarry of Stonework Hollow is silent more often than not these days - though it was once the source of much of the stone that built the city of Ordain, it was eventually emptied of most of its easily accessible resources. An attempt was made two decades ago to reopen Stonework Hollow and use new quarrying techniques to reach further into its depths, but this coincided with the Stonehollow Quake, a major earthquake that killed over 100 Ordin residents and caused the quarry to be largely shut down.

Sunhaven.name: Sunhaven
Sunhaven.text:
• District Type: Residential and Institutional

  • Population: 6,523 (Moderately dense population of residents and clerics of the Temple of Lantyr)

  • Lifestyle: Righoutsness (Clerics, officials, Kessian traders and settlers)

  • Services: Spiritual guidance, exaltation, religious education, and practice.

Sunhaven was once a sparsely populated part of the city, with a few scattered Ordani buildings on its edge, until a large group of Kessians arrived, traveling halfway across the world from the Kessian continent and settling in the area. Today, the district is home to a few scattered Kessian natives or travelers who have settled or arrived more recently, however, most inhabitants are descendants of Kessain families who now consider themselves more culturally Ordani or a mix of both cultures.

Alongside the cultural elements, the Kessian settlers brought with them their devout worship of the Sun Goddess Lantyr. The district not only maintains this tradition but has aggressively built upon it. Today, this worship falls under what is locally known as the "Radiant Eye." This group is considered fairly extreme, and some of the recently arriving Kessians believe the worshippers belong to a sect rather than the primary religion in Kessia, which is why many call it the Sect of the Radiant Eye. These worshippers are deeply fanatical and have connections with many powerful supporters from across the world, including groups from the Kessian homeland.

Culture

The district's population is a mix of Ordani and Kessian descendants, which means that a proud Kessian cultural element is visible throughout the district. The people are profoundly influenced daily by the worship of Lantyr, revered as the bringer of light, warmth, and life. Families often begin their day with morning rituals, lighting candles or lanterns to invoke her blessings or spending time in the sun among the community, seated or kneeling in the streets, or attending daily services in the Temple of Lantyr. Songs, exaltations, and the loud calls of those expressing their devotion are common.

Much like the Kessian culture itself, women hold important roles in both family and community leadership, making decisions and guiding those around them. Although the strict matrical leadership system is not enforced in the city, unlike distant Kessia, many of the district residents abide by these ideas at a family and community level, and the High Priestess of the Temple of Lantyr is one in a long line of feminine leaders.

Landmarks

The Grand Temple of Lantyr

A stunning architectural marvel made of whitestone and golden sheathed metal tiles. This massive temple is adorned with intricate carvings that tell the stories of the Kessian people, their mythology, and belief system. Inside, soft golden light filters through mesh-covered windows, creating thousands of small beams that reflect off the polished golden stone floors. The temple hosts daily worship services, one at dawn and another at midday, along with special ceremonies and festivals that draw people from all over the district to honor Lantyr at certain times of the year. The current High Priestess of the Radiant Eye is the venerated Okia Tyrwar, who leads both the clerics overseeing the temple and the majority of the district's population.

Kessian Embassy

A small, oddly quiet building hidden away in the depths of the district that is currently boarded up. Kessia itself does not maintain regular contact with Ordain, and its trading ships are few and far between. The previous ambassador passed away several years ago, and the only remaining official then decided to retire and open a café.

Golden Path

A serene walkway along the district's main road leading to the Temple of Lantyr, illuminated by warm orange lanterns that cast enough light in the evenings for the street to be considered as bright as daytime. This path is popular for evening strolls and is lined with benches and carpeted areas for kneeling in quiet reflection. Along the way, there are small altars dedicated to Lantyr where people can pay their respects or offer thanks for blessings received.

The Fabled Rift

This large tavern is a popular spot for adventurers, wanderers, and seekers of wisdom, as it features a deep rift in the earth that descends into a spiraling dark maze. Many believe that the rift is a gateway to the Pathways, and locals have many strange stories about the canyon, which is said to be a remnant of a battle between light and darkness, where one can feel the tangible tension of opposing forces. In truth, it is relatively shallow, and its passages have been mapped. At least, that's what most people say who have returned from exploring its depths, but every now and then, people or groups go missing and are never heard from again.

Locals

High Priestess Okia Tyrwar (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

Okia comes from a long line of clerics of the Radiant Eye, and her grandmother was also the high priestess during her time. She was raised in Sunhaven and has dedicated her life to worshipping Lantyr, becoming one of the temple's most outspoken figures in recent memory. Her leadership is marked by deep ties to the traditions of both Kessian and Ordani cultures, but she believes that the vast majority of the population is far too lax in their veneration of the gods and of Lantyr herself, seeing the recent troubles and increasingly turbulent times as a consequence of their inaction. She is ardently passionate about her followers taking measures to enact change and to help others, and her rousing speeches have reached beyond Sunhaven and into the city population as a whole, which recently led to her being elected by the Hallows to a seat on the Ordinate itself.

Kerit Malroth (Chaotic Neutral, Kessian Kiska, he/him)

Malroth comes from a strict Kessian family in the city of Red Rhuin, where they place great importance on devoted worship of the Sun Goddess, Lantyr. Unlike many in Ordain, he is originally from Kessia and traveled across the seas to join the clerics of the Radiant Eye when he arrived in the city a decade ago. However, unknown to many, he is actually a member of the Kessian Iquistorias and was assigned by the organization to report on both Ordain and the Sect of the Radiant Eye itself. Not only is he fanatical, but Malroth is also deeply mistrustful of others, seeing corruption by the outer darkness everywhere.

Lira Natus (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human/Nir'ae, she/her)

Mira is a passionate resident of Sunhaven who travels across the city attempting to expose the calmer and more measured teachings of Lantyr as she sees them. As a descendant of both Ordani and Kessian heritage, she deeply appreciates her eclectic background and seeks to promote coexistence and cultural celebration. Energetic and determined, Mira often rallies her friends and neighbors for sun parties, helps those in need, and maintains the city as a whole. Unfortunately, most within Sunhaven, including her own family, consider her to be a borderline heretic, and only the laws of Ordain prevent her from being targeted by violence or reprisals.

Lore

The district has gone through many changes over the years and started as a sparse area where a few Ordani families began to build on the edges of an expanding city. In [[/date AS2397]], a large group of Kessains arrived and settled in the area, increasing its population. They quickly set about constructing buildings in their own cultural design and erected a central temple for worship, which quickly became a place where Ordani residents themselves came to worship. This attracted the attention of several trading houses and the Hallows, who, realizing the potential this held for attracting support to their various causes through public opinion, began financially supporting the growing priesthood of Lantyr.

Nearly twenty years later, the first stones were laid for a vast grand temple to the Sun Goddess. That temple then took a further fifty-nine years to complete, during which time its scale and scope were expanded, leading to the huge edifice overlooking the city today.
Sunhaven.soverview: Sunhaven is one of the most visually striking places in Ordain, featuring a dazzling array of unique architectural elements, such as golden tiled orbs in place of rooftops and thick mesh openings that allow natural sunlight to pass through. The vibrant district buzzes with energy, drawing visitors and devotees alike with its stunning beauty and cultural richness. At the heart of Sunhaven, the majestic Temple of Lantyr stands majestically above the skyline, its golden-tiled facade glistening in the Sun’s embrace.
Sunhaven.sexposition: The buildings around you shimmer in the light, each one uniquely adorned with thick golden tiles that catch the light in a mesmerizing dance. Curved mesh-covered openings seem to replace windows here, and deep orange and yellow colors are present on many of the buildings. Towering over the bustling streets is a massive structure, its grandeur dominating the skyline and drawing your gaze upward in awe.

Arena Ridge.name: Arena Ridge
Arena Ridge.text:
• District Type: Entertainment, Retail, and Residential

  • Population: 13,460 (Moderately dense population of folks who love the central walkable location)

  • Lifestyle: High Energy (Fans of sporting teams, shoppers, and entertainment-focused locals)

  • Services: Sporting (Arena) and Retail (Mix of Food, Apparel, and Lodging)

Arena Ridge is dominated by the Grand Kalion Stadium, with many residents working within the bustling and lively entertainment industry that surrounds the various games, shows, and sports that are hosted there. There is also a huge demand for food, lodging, and space from visitors traveling from other districts for special events or games. Additionally, a significant number of residents are food stall owners, shopkeepers, or traders who serve the steady flow of Ordain's population.

The most popular game in Kalion Stadium is a more modern version of an ancient handball once played in the Kelmezian city-states known in Ordain as Thronefire. Nobles and royalty originally played it before spreading to the masses, who transformed it into a more contact-driven physical sport that requires several athletic qualities. The game is played with a ball enchanted with various fiery and energy-based elements, and the goal is to score by throwing the ball while standing still into an opening in a tall tower called the Throne. Of course, other players will attempt to push, grab, shove, or run into opponents at full speed, creating some dramatic moments that are talked about for weeks.

Many teams within Ordain compete each year in the sports season called the Crown's Cup, and the winning team receives a golden crown trophy that they keep until the next season, when it is passed to the new winners. The Crown's Cup only lasts for roughly four months during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.xu3TCWh4GPy18X4t]{Steading} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.pEg9yxklAGARjf2Q]{Gleaning} seasons, but throughout the rest of the year, many other events are held in the stadium, including Relayrun, Champions Duel, and smaller-scale sporting tournaments.

Culture

Arena Ridge is often lively with an electric atmosphere, especially during game days or major events, when the streets fill with fans wearing their teams' colors and chanting slogans. Street performers, artists, and vendors line the roads, creating a vibrant market where local food and crafts are celebrated. Sports play a central role in the community, and friendly rivalries are common, fostering camaraderie among residents. When events are not scheduled in the Stadium, the district becomes dramatically less busy, and residents tend to spend more time relaxing and slowly preparing their local businesses for the next surge of traffic.

Landmarks

Grand Kalion Stadium

The Grand Kalion Stadium, named after the legendary Crowns Cup eight-time champion Arcus Kalion, stands as the pride of the city of Ordain. It is an architectural marvel designed to host a variety of events and entertainment spectacles. With a seating capacity that rivals the largest arenas in the known world, it features state-of-the-art magic and technology, including a dynamic scoreboard and sound systems that enhance the viewing experience. The stadium features a versatile field that can accommodate a range of sports and events, and the floor of the stadium can be easily converted within a few hours.

Champions Square

Located right outside the Grand Kalion Stadium, Champions Square is a bustling hub of celebration and camaraderie. This vibrant plaza is adorned with sculptures, flags, and banners representing various local teams. It is a favored gathering spot for fans to share their excitement before and after events.

Lost Wod

Lost Wod is a hidden tavern tucked away in the heart of Arena Ridge, often shrouded in an air of mystery. It is a place that is almost exclusively reserved for Oaken who travel to Ordain with the express purpose of participating in the games and events held in the stadium nearby. It has an infamous reputation for being one of the most violent places in the city, with fights, tests of strength, and bruised egos causing fights and clashes on a near-constant basis. Luckily for the Ordani residents, the tavern is maintained by an Oaken elder called Wod, who erected wards, charms, and magic around the area to both hide the location from prying eyes and prevent noise or disruptions from escaping out into the city.

Saltrack Gymnasium

Saltrack Gymnasium is an elite training facility at the forefront of physical fitness and athletic development in Ordain, primarily funded and maintained by House Salva. Equipped with weight training areas, spacious courts for various sports, and training facilities, the gymnasium attracts both aspiring athletes and fitness enthusiasts who can afford the high prices alike.

Locals

Donavan "Doc" Reed (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

Donovan, affectionately known as "Doc," is the charismatic commentator for many of the major events held at the Grand Kalion Stadium, including the Crown's Cup, which he has hosted for nearly fifteen years. With a booming voice and an infectious enthusiasm, he brings an electrifying energy to every event he covers. A former athlete himself, Donovan possesses an intricate understanding of Thronefire, allowing him to provide insightful commentary and engaging anecdotes that captivate both live audiences and those watching from home. His trademark catchphrases and playful banter have made him a local celebrity, adored by fans and participants alike.

Rowan "Greenball" (Chaotic Good, Ordani Thornling, they/them)

Greenball is the champion of the Crown's Cup four years in a row and is an endlessly energetic character who delights in teasing the crowd with last-minute plays during games of Thronefire. Known for her agility and endurance, she excels at anchoring herself firmly and making excellent shots on the towertop as well.

Wod (Lawful Neutral, Oaken Vrjnhar, he/him)

Wod is a revered Oaken elder almost seven hundred years old, who commands respect and admiration throughout the city, especially among visiting Oakens. He resembles a gnarled tree, with a trunk-like body, and his fur looks patterned like hardwood or tree bark. He is an extremely friendly and easygoing Oaken who runs the tavern known as Lost Wod, which is well known among all Oakens who visit the city.

Lore

Initially, the area was a large open field slightly raised above the floodplain of the nearby river, used to host local competitions and informal games of Thronefire in the early days of the city. As the years went by, the city's population grew, attracting a diverse mix of artisans, traders, and fans eager to watch the games. With this growth, the need for a bigger venue to handle the increasing size and frequency of events became clear. This led to the ambitious plans for the Grand Kalion Stadium. The massive stadium was then built in [[/date AS2197]], becoming the centerpiece of entertainment in Ordain. Its opening marked a new chapter for Arena Ridge, turning it into a bustling hub.
Arena Ridge.soverview: The district known as Arena Ridge emerged as a bustling hub of activity after the construction of the Grand Kalion Stadium of Ordain, a massive stadium that serves as the heart of sports and entertainment in the city. Once an open field used for local competitions, the area has now transformed into a vibrant community that thrives on the excitement of events held within the stadium, while also offering a wide array of local food, shops and entertainment options along its bustling streets.
Arena Ridge.sexposition: As you stroll down the bustling central street, vendors hawk their wares from all sides, enticing you with the scent of delicious local street food. The aroma of spices, grilled meats, and sweet treats wafts through the air, and small groups of people stand and eat while chatting enthusiastically with one another. In the distance, you can see the backdrop of a huge circular structure, covered in flags and banners.

Orchard Lanes.name: Orchard Lanes
Orchard Lanes.text:
• District Type: Residential and Commercial (food, taverns, shops)

  • Population: 13,242 (Medium. Homes, apartments, and businesses with heavy foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Modest-to-Wealthy (Culinary professionals, craftspeople, service professionals, laborers, merchants).

  • Services: Lodging, housing, food & drink (fruit, tea, wine), leisure.

This quaint residential neighborhood’s eponymous orchards are rife with fruits culled from all corners of the Arctus Plateau, and the local streets are lined with verdant flower beds full of luscious vine fruits such as grapes, kiwis, and berries. This greenery is duly tended to by sages from Cindarin Temple along with local volunteers; and — as the seasons allow — the resultant produce serves as a complimentary food source for locals and the city at large.

The houses and apartments of Orchard Lanes are generally occupied by a wide array of Ordani citizens whose middle-class incomes afford them a relatively comfortable quality of life. Here and there, an inviting market or curiosity shop dots the arboreal landscape. A gentle breeze often sweeps through these whimsical lanes, where life tends to slow down just long enough to enjoy it.

Landmarks

Sweet Reliefs

A favorite haven for many citizens of Ordain, this local tavern is well known for its potent wines and refreshing ciders. Sweet Reliefs is a place where good times are paramount above all else, a hazy den of conversation, gameplay, and unwinding. Indeed, many teenagers and young adults of Orchard Lanes and neighboring districts set their sights on Sweet Reliefs as a place to start their careers (although the small confines of the tavern allow relatively few of these aspiring youths to claim a coveted job).

Briarhearth

This sagging, four-story edifice offers affordable apartment housing for locals of modest-to-comfortable means. Briarhearth is owned and operated by a former House Cevher executive of trustworthy repute named Wanel Loag (LG, Ordani Human, he/him), alongside his kindhearted agrimage wife Marinela (NG, Arcturian Human, she/her). Short- and long-term lodging is usually available for those in need, and the Loags are known to offer temporary clemency for those in desperate need.

Mystical Musings

A cluttered curio shop stocked with spell components and rare alchemical ingredients, Mystical Musings is maintained by the aged wizard Rory Fairweather (NG, Arcturian Human, he/him), who absent-mindedly offers his spellcasting services for remarkably fair prices.

The Hazard House

This secret clubhouse serves as the base of operations for The Undaunted, an underground league of daredevil exhibitionists led by the tenacious @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero}. The Hazard House's precise location is unknown to nearly everyone, but its reputation among Ordain's sordid underworld is slowly on the rise.

Locals

Rory Fairweather (NG, Arcturian Human, he/him)

A native of the remote mountainside village of Skybrush, this courteous and elderly wizard operates the cozy arcane emporium known as Mystical Musings. An absent-minded adherent to the traditions of enchantment magic, Rory is happy to offer his low-level spellcasting services to anyone in need (unless, of course, their agenda is measurably distasteful). Treat Rory as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.mQnsXanewsPiV7QE]{Mage} with a more comprehensive spell list for spellcasting services.

Jonda Ven'dara (CG, Waerd Human, she/her)

Tall tales and local legends surround this wizened Cindaric Sage who lives in hermetic seclusion amidst the confines of her aged Orchard Lanes townhouse. Neighborhood children weave endless tales about what she does inside the spooky old house, and actual visitors to the estate are few and far-between; but despite the wild rumors and accusations that surround her lonely lifestyle, she's a remarkable mind.

Brando Grath (CN, Ordani Human, he/him)

This gregarious thirty-something piker is an opportunistic clerk employed by the Ordinate who utilizes duplicitous methods to settle his numerous gambling debts. As a result of his activities (both illicit and otherwise), Brando is connected to more than a few interesting and unsavory characters in Ordain.

@UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero} (NE, Kelmezoan Human, she/her)

Zira Hestidero is a Kalaxan warlock of the undying shard god Kuarta who leads a ragtag enclave of scrappy Kuartan adherents known as The Undaunted.

Lore

Orchard Lanes has a warm reputation among most of Ordain's citizens, and tends to be the quiet kind of place where one can escape the hustle-and-bustle of the rest of the city with some measure of regularity. The eponymous lanes and their endless orchards are discreet places, perfect for afternoon reading or a romantic stroll. Naturally, this also provides a furtive haven for more clandestine activity, and nurtures fertile ground for tall tales and local legends. Several ghost stories are connected to the fledgling history of Orchard Lanes, and are celebrated with pride by its local denizens; such tales include "The Tale of Lost Darrisa" and "Steppler's Cat."
Orchard Lanes.soverview: Nestled between the eaves of Assembly Hills and the Ordinate high above, this sprawling residential district is marked by the proliferation of affordable, multi-storied housing and the ubiquity of its arboreal parks and lush municipal orchards. Orchard Lanes is regarded throughout Ordain as one of the most welcoming and arcadian neighborhoods the city has to offer.
Orchard Lanes.sexposition: Narrow orchards ripe with produce and flowerbeds lined with fruiting brambles decorate the winding streets of this winsome residential neighborhood. A smell of hearthfire dances on the wind, which aimlessly rustles through the shaded area’s leafy boughs. There is an unmistakable tranquility to this place, which seems like a perfect neighborhood for settling down.

The Burns.name: The Burns
The Burns.text:
• District Type: Commercial (alchemy, consumables) with some Residential

  • Population: 4,242 (Light population of alchemists, potionmakers, and a few poisoners)

  • Lifestyle: Experimental (amateur scientists and makers who will do anything to discover something new)

  • Services: Alchemy and Consumables (potions, poisons, salves, alchemical substances)

Culture

In the Burns, experimentation is everything. It was experimentation that led the famed alchemist Barbazi to develop his Barbazi balloons, which help to cleanse the air in the district of the smoke from the industrial work in nearby neighborhoods, and attracted many aspiring alchemists to the area. It was experimentation that led these students to stay and build up the district on the edge of the river, iterating on what they'd learned while developing new processes and substances of their own. Where some fear working with unknown substances and trying radical new ideas, especially when there is the potential for them to go wrong in dangerous ways, innovators and risk-takers came together in the Burns to create during an era of rapid-fire new inventions. And though now things have settled, somewhat, as the Burns both innovates and supports itself by selling its existing goods and materials to the rest of Ordain, the district still likes to think of itself as the place where the next genius alchemical idea will be born.

The Burns has always had a slight division between those focused on what can be created through innovation and those who care more about the process of experimentation itself, going back to the days of Barbazi a century ago. Some of Barbazi’s students chose to focus on the end result of his work – the fact that he was able to create something that made a positive impact on the district around him - and felt inspired by targeting their experimentation at specific goals that would help Ordain. Others focused on the innovation of his methods and used them to try out new alchemical concepts, with no end goal other than seeing if they would work at all.

This difference of opinion about the goal of alchemy persists in the Burns to this day. Those who focus on the end product often live closer to the docks, where they believe they can get a better sense of what visitors and locals need, while those who are more interested in the process of creation for its own sake often experiment in warehouses that aren’t currently being used to store products. Both sides respect and generally believe they need each other, though the Dockside alchemists worry about the dangers and frivolousness of the more outlandish experimentation and the Warehouse experimenters complain that their peers have lost their experimental zeal in a desire to meet unnecessary customer needs.

Landmarks

The Barbazi Bazaar

This series of open-air stalls is often called "the Barbazi Bizarre" by locals, as it is the best place to find the rare alchemical materials and oddities, from vessels made of scavenged bones to recipes for only partially tested concoctions. The Bazaar offers stalls on a first-come first-serve basis each day, and many of the sellers work on a trade system, swapping items with fellow sellers that will help them pursue their own goals or experiments. Though the atmosphere is lively, manager/owner Lizelle Endring (Chaotic Good, Ordani human, she/her) attempts to keep things relatively safe with her three rules of the Bazaar - all sales are final, all risks must be disclosed, and anyone who gets hurt due to the seller's negligence is banned for life. As a result, warnings about potential death and dismemberment from items in the Bazaar tend to be very thorough, if generally ignored.

Scorch's

On the surface, this shop sells hot sauce and "romantic aids" (which the many signs in the shop are careful to warn should not be mixed), but it is also one of the best suppliers of explosive alchemical ingredients in the Burns. Anything dangerous that comes into Scorch's is stored in an empty well in the basement, which is heavily shielded against damage and can be quickly refilled with water in case anything goes wrong. Scorch's purported owner, Flametongue, who lives above the shop, likes to tell stories about the fires and explosions created by his development of new hot sauce flavors, which he uses to build up the shop's reputation and hide any accidents from alchemical experimentation, but he has little to do with either. Both the shop and its trade remain under the control of Flametounge's long-time friend Aevin Sarl (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani human, he/him), who poses as the store assistant.

The Syderie

Drinks at the Syderie are known for never quite being what they seem, with alchemical ingredients that change the nature of a drink — making a hot drink taste cold, for instance — or have an unusual physical effect on whoever drinks them, ranging from making them lighter on their feet to temporarily changing the color of their hair or tongue. Sydronach Stout (Neutral Good, Arcturian Keth, she/her), the long-time owner of the wholesaler Syd's Liquids, which supplies commercial fluids like dyes, inks, oils, beverages, chemicals, and potions to businesses across Ordain, opened the to bring more customers into the large direct-to-consumer shop at the front of her warehouse, but its ever-growing popularity of the shop has been more than she expected. With the novelty of each new drink effect wearing off quickly, she wonders how she can either find a new showstopper or tamp down interest in the place.

Locals

Flametongue (Neutral Good, Ordani vrjnhar, he/him)

Flametongue, whose real name is Fazeel, is the face of Scorch's, despite the fact that he has absolutely no skills at alchemy whatsoever. What he does excel at is perfume making, creating scents that seem to capture emotions. To avoid any confusion with his day job, he sells his perfumes under the name Lee Za (created by spelling his name backwards), though he deeply wishes to get the recognition as a perfume maker that he believes he deserves.

Daurin Vediqili (True Neutral, Ordani human, he/him)

Daurin has grown in influence over the past few years thanks to the innovative alchemical concoctions he has debuted at the annual Showcase, a social event that also gives all shops in the area an opportunity to show off their best work. His works tend to use cutting-edge techniques that he honed in the Warehouse section of the Burns, but are firmly aimed at giving the Ordani people what they want, making him popular Dockside as well. The attention and popularity he's garnered over the last few years has begun to go to Daurin's head a bit, and he has promised to make his next invention something to rival Barbazi's genius, but he has had no new ideas and is becoming desperate to find some way to save face, even if that means stealing someone else's work and passing it off as his own.

Ylvo Indrane (Lawful Evil, Ordani human, he/him)

Ylvo represents the small but influential Poisoner's Guild in the Burns. Though not an officially recognized group, the self-proclaimed experts of the deadly arts meet for drinks at various local establishments (including the Syderie, one of Ylvo's personal faves, though its proprietor Syd really wishes he wouldn't) and go for strolls along the docks as they discuss their work. Ylvo is flamboyant in his appearance and demeanor, wearing a fluttering black cloak with singed edges and a necklace of bones of unknown origins, but this is somewhat affected as a way to draw attention to himself and allow many of his fellow guild members (including those who are never seen publicly with the guild) to operate without drawing attention to them. He personally is one of the least dangerous of the guild, as he operates by what he calls a strict code of ethics, only poisoning those within the guild as a way to maintain his skills and power.

Lore

Though locals in the Burns often play up the many accidents and conflagrations in the district, in truth there have been very few real accidents, thanks to a tacit agreement between the district guilds and the city that they be allowed to operate without any real oversight as long as they tend to their own safety protocols. Even during the Stonehollow Quake, when tremors shook the district, the alchemists were able to quickly clean up any alchemical spills with the safety guidelines they put in place and help quell fires in some of the nearby industrial districts, preventing disaster from spreading.
The Burns.soverview: Rich scents punctuate the sometimes-hazy air of The Burns, thanks to the work of the alchemists, glass blowers, and perfumers who call the district home. Originally a residential district formed to house the families of metalsmithing workers, a push by those in the district to prevent the air and streets from feeling dingy led to a number of alchemical breakthroughs. Chief among these are the Barbazi balloons, glass structures which attract and trap industrial smoke, convert it to alchemical light, and - in response to more than one unfortunate explosion and fire in the area - change color to warn of potential toxicity.
The Burns.sexposition: There is debate as to whether name The Burns comes from the faint haze of smoke and soot in the air from the many perfume shops in the area, the Barbazi balloons that float above doorways and windows that burn industrial waste in the air from nearby districts and convert it into light, or the fact that the many alchemists who call the area home have been known to accidentally blow themselves up or briefly set it on fire every couple of years.

Spellbreaker Tower.name: Spellbreaker Tower
Spellbreaker Tower.text:
• District Type: Institutional

  • Population: 300 (Low. Patients reside here temporarily, while prisoners are permanent residents. Overall population of both is presently low.)

  • Lifestyle: Controlled. (Veiled Chain officers, prison guards, Cindaric Healers and inmates occupy this location. Most activity is closely monitored.)

  • Services: Counseling, curse-breaking, magical suppression, high-security containment.

The massive tower serves a dual purpose as Ordain’s maximum-security prison, and as a place where people far and wide may come to shed magical maladies and curses. The structure’s inherent aura of anti-magic ensures that no spell may be cast, nor magical item work, nor curse hold sway for long as the Spellbreaker's aura holds to its name.

The structure’s inherent aura of anti-magic ensures that no spell may be cast, nor magical item work, nor curse hold sway for long, ensuring that the Spellbreaker tower holds to its name. While the lower levels of the tower, known as "The Foundation" tends to the cursed and enchanted, the upper levels of the tower are reserved for containing dangerous beings and items that could harm the city.

The entirety of this district is affected by a powerful @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAntimagicF]{Antimagic Field} that emanates from the central Spellbreaker Tower.

Culture

Life in the district is regimented, and methodical, whether that is working or being treated in the foundation levels of the tower, or as an inmate or guard in the higher prison levels. Visitors to the Spellbreaker must check in with the Sentinel Tower in the main courtyard before proceeding, and their every movement is watched.

The district is monitored and staffed by a small army of Cindarics, and members of the Veiled Chain, both supplemented by a small army of attendants and guards selected from the city.

Landmarks

Sentinel Tower

The broad, lowest levels of Spellbreaker Tower are devoted to patients seeking refuge from curses, magical traumas, or syndromes beyond the reach of city magics. Here, consultations and mundane treatments are dispensed by the Cindarics, with simple beds offered to any in need. While the Foundation is open to most everyone, the doorways to the upper levels are carefully guarded.

The Foundation

Forming the broad base of Spellbreaker Tower, the Foundation is the vast ground-level of the prison, itself incorporating several floors of cell blocks and security areas. Most non-critical prisoners are housed and processed here, with only special prisoners moving up the tower. The Foundation features its own medical wing, a utilitarian cafeteria, visitation galleries, and an intake ward that handles visitors and prisoners coming and going from the tower.

Overwatch Garrison

Affixed to one side of the tower’s core, the Overwatch Garrison is a secure, multi-story facility built to house the Spellbreaker’s guard force, attending sages, clerks, and support staff. It features an armory and barracks, a galley and small infirmary ensure staff remain rested and ready. The garrison also features a large, covered, rooftop recreation yard with sweeping views of the Arctus Plateau, giving the occupants a rare chance to breathe fresh air while on rotation.

The Gallery

Built high into the tower, the gallery is a heavily secured vault where magical items are stored for safekeeping. All manner of dangerous items are retained here, their effects suppressed by the divine force the permeates the tower. The Gallery is guarded round the clock, and only the head of the guards and the the tower's warden may enter it or take others inside.

Locals

Warden Cyran Holst (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

A gaunt, quiet leader, Holst has spent nearly three decades balancing the expectations of the Ordinate, the Cascillian Republics' demands, and the needs of the Tower's inmates. His commitment to routine and fairness underlies every decision, rendering him respected by Ordinate, Cindaric, Cascillians and Veiled Chain alike. There is no aspect of operation within the tower prison levels that he doesn't know about.

Marle Sinterra (Lawful Good, Ordani Drakon, she/her)

A Tayan ex-patriate, she is the leader in charge of training and overseeing the regular guards, and making sure that the items in the Gallery are safe. Marle’s seriousness is balanced by a genuine concern for her team’s wellbeing. She keeps a low profile outside the tower, rarely socializing with locals.

Security Specialist Barik Vell (Lawful Neutral, Cascilian Human, they/them)

A practical, unsentimental technician who is the most recent in a long line of academic specialists arriving from the Cascillian Republic to study the tower and maintain the security systems within. He is expertly versed in every lock, gate, machine, and mechanism in the prison, even those not of Cascillian origin.

“Mercy” (Chaotic Evil, Arcturian Human, they/them)

Occupying the most locked-down cell in the tower's Red Block, this inmate is legendary within the prison itself. Every other inmate and guard has heard of them and has a theory about their background and is happy to discuss it. Appearing to be nothing more than a middle-aged human woman, their rumored abilities change with each source; they might be are either a supernatural assassin, a rogue archmage, or something else entirely. Only Warden Holst and the Hallows know the truth, and neither of them are willing to release any details, not even their true name.

Lore

Rumors about the tower's nature and origin are are numerous, ranging from plausible to far fetched. Some swear that the Spellbreaker lives (or slumbers) under the tower, and that the goddess is consuming the magic in the area. Others say that the tower was built by the Cascillian Republic, who pays the Ordinate large sums to house its most foul spellcasters off-site.

In truth, the Spellbreaker Tower's history is not especially well known since most of the inciting events around its creation occurred nearly six centuries ago, and has largely passed out of living memory. However, a few pieces of knowledge endure, committed to history texts, and described by witness accounts:

The tower was raised almost six hundred years ago by the goddess known as the Spellbreaker, lifted from the very stone of the spire that it stands on. The divine power within the tower that unravels even the most powerful magic was placed there by the goddess for reasons only she knew, and the Cindaric order had some connection to the goddess and events related to the tower's creation and her vanishing.

Two centuries ago, a generation of master stonemasons clad the Tower with Avilla’s image, reshaping its silhouette into a grand tribute to the goddess that built the tower. The lack of mag made this a long, laborious process that required massive support cranes to be built to move the stone sections into place. About a decade ago the Stonehollow Quake left cracks in the tower’s decorative edifice, and required several years of dedicated work to repair.
Spellbreaker Tower.soverview: The Spellbreaker Tower is Ordain’s most infamous edifice, known for being both a place of healing for those afflicted by magical maladies, and the last line of confinement for individuals too dangerous to be allowed in the world. A powerful aura of divine power here nullifies magic in the tower and surrounding areas.
Spellbreaker Tower.sexposition: The Spellbreaker Tower rises stark and angular, in stark contrast to Ordain’s loftiest buildings, its sheer faces and sharp corners softened by the intricate sculpture of a hooded woman cloaked in a flowing robe that becomes part of vast, curling banners that wrap the exterior. Unlike the gleaming white of the rest of Ordain's skyline, the spellbreaker is a dark spire of stone pulled from the earth below the city, and shaped into a pillar stark reminder of a god's power.

Skycrest.name: Skycrest
Skycrest.text:
• District Type: Residential

  • Population: 4,620 (Moderate. Private townhomes and apartments rise up around the striking exhibit homes, many of which are lived in. Visitors and locals fill the streets at all hours, and the district has a healthy nightlife.)

  • Lifestyle: Bohemian. (A mixture of artists, merchants, nobles reside in this visually striking district.)

  • Services: Food and drink, private clubs, private galleries, architectural tours.

Homes in Skycrest are celebrated for their individuality — each a testament to the owner’s taste and the artisans or architects behind it. Most buildings are built with terraces, large windows and wide balconies that provide sweeping views and a sense of openness.

Culture

Residents of Skycrest may value aesthetics and refinement more than fortune or pedigree, as this district embraced the ideals of art and innovation as a badge of distinction in Ordain. The community is lively, intellectual, artistically inclined, with a distinct air of competition. Here, artists and patrons vie to set the next great trend.

Landmarks

Lantiri Plaza

A sun-drenched square encircled by columns and trimmed with luminous topiary imported from the Corebright forests. Lantiri Plaza is famous for its open-air recitals, sculpture unveilings, and art shows which draw onlookers from around the city.

The Skywall Gallery

A daring, cube of a building whose interior is entirely hollow and consists of numerous platforms and levels suspended from cables or held aloft by enchantment. The inner walls are covered in magically enchanted paint that renders the exterior skyline in a living fresco. Open to the public, admittance is not cheap, but the experience is considered worth the price.

Iridane House

Perhaps the most iconic of Skycrest’s private residences, Iridane House is renowned for its seamless blend of prismatic glasswork terrariums fed by fountains that descend through the building's various levels. No longer an active residence, its owner hosts legendary midnight artist salons and private art showings.

The Riverlight Steps

A long, winding avenue that runs through several neighborhoods in Skycrest, beginning at its highest terraces and ending at the descent to the waterfront districts below. It is named for the ample lanterns that line the way from start to finish and is a favorite place for contemplative strolls.

Locals

Rilan Verdane (Chaotic Neutral, Tayan Human, he/him)

An architect that fled his homeland to escape mounting debt, he now attempts to convince local patrons to support his next project. He hopes to use light and shadow to create a building with an ever evolving facade. He spends his evenings at the Wind Gallery, always sketching and drinking.

Myella Tarrie (Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

Hostess of Iridane House, Myella is famed for her exquisite taste in art and her sharp wit. Her midnight salons are the talk of the district, and she quietly champions emerging artists with the ample endowment offered by her position.

Cavran Ellisar (Lawful Good, Ordani Cor'ak, he/him)

A master gardener responsible for the design of several gardens and topiary sculptures in the district, and his personal collection of miniature trees. Patient and soft-spoken, Cavran is beloved for his generosity in sharing rare seeds and techniques with others.

Pelin Dratch (Neutral Good, Lumek Fej, she/her)

A renowned glass artist with a studio tucked into a hillside along the Riverlight, Pelin’s creations are prized for their vibrant colors and exacting detail. She can often be found working with her doors open so folk passing by can see her latest piece taking shape.

Lore

Skycrest was once an unremarkable spur of the bluffs until vibrant white stone was found within. In short order numerous quarries were build to supply the growing city, and lasted until the cliff face was reduced to the level it stands at now.

A century after it served the construction of the city, those quarries were torn down and the land taken over by sculptors and masons who wanted easy access to the discarded stone, sand and gravel left in the old quarry sites.

Eventually the studios and brickyards became homes, and those homes became statements by the local artists and architects, stood on the bluffs for all to see. This drew wealthy patrons, their coin fueling growth and development that made Skycrest what it is today.
Skycrest.soverview: Skycrest is a district defined by its striking architectural invention and understated wealth. This district is home to a myriad of homes and estates built to serve more as art installations than as abodes. As a result, this district attracts the wealthy and creative in equal measure, making it a cultural hotspot.
Skycrest.sexposition: High atop the bluffs overlooking the sprawling cityscape of Ordain is the vibrant haven of culture and affluence that is Skycrest. Bold façades and sculpted rooftop gardens climb into the sky itself, looming over winding stone stairways and streets that stretch across the district between large stone plazas. Avant-garde homes of glass, marble, polished metals and carved woods line these avenues, every building a demonstration of artistry and craftmanship.

Koto Springs.name: Koto Springs
Koto Springs.text:
• District Type: Residential and Commercial

  • Populations: 2,590 (Low-Moderate. Koto Springs features many wealthy private homes built around spas, inns, clubs, and shops. The district is thick with foot traffic at all hours.)

  • Lifestyle: Mixed. (Nobles and merchants life here, but all of Ordain visits to enjoy the springs.)

  • Services: Bathhouses, hospitality, fine dining.

Koto Springs flourished around its namesake natural springs — deep, ancient wells of hot water that bubble up through stone and earth. The city’s finest engineers have tamed these waters, weaving networks of aqueducts and copper piping across streets and courtyards. Here, residents enjoy private steam baths and indoor plumbing that not even the noble manors elsewhere in the city can rival.

Culture
