Life in Koto Springs centers around public bathing and leisurely socializing, whether with friends or with clients. Business is often negotiated in the mosaic-tiled saunas of bathhouses or in vibrant private gardens draped in shade and greenery.

While some springs feed exclusive clubs or secretive spas, others are open to travelers and commoners who come to soak away troubles and gather news among the restorative waters.

Service trades — masseurs, cooks, cleaners, plumbers — are held in high esteem here as they are often in demand. Though outsiders flock to the springs, the long-settled families who maintain the pipes and operate the oldest inns are respected as the district’s heart.

Landmarks

Koto Springs Bathhouse

Ornate columns and flowering hedges mark the entrance to the oldest and most famous bathouse in the city. Here the polished marble floors and mineral pools host the city’s most influential figures. Cost to enter is high, but the quality is second to none.

The Copper Cauldron

This bustling café, perched atop a steaming fissure, prepares its vegetarian fare using ingenious steam-powered ovens and spits, filling the air with the scents of roasted herbs and bubbling broths. The Copper Cauldron is an expensive but well-loved eatery in the district.

The Vapor Room

A luxurious, lantern-lit social club and sauna where the well-to-do mingle in privacy, relaxing in crystal-tiled steam baths. The Vapor Room greedily scoops up all the second-rung clients that aren't important or rich enough to get into the famed Koto Springs Bathhouse.

Gajak's Rest

Built shortly after the district's namesake, Gajak's Rest is the oldest inn the district has, and is a sprawling collection of buildings with a tavern, multiple inn buildings, stables, and its own small restaurant. Prices are modest, and service is good here.

Locals

Rilano Mestrin (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

Chief steward of the Koto Springs Bathhouse, Rilano is known for his dignified manner and frightening, encyclopedic memory for guests’ preferences and secrets. He has connections with merchants, vendors, and Trading House officials throughout the city, and uses them to keep the bathhouse running smoothly.

Parne Valitaine (Chaotic Good, Tayan Human, she/her)

The bright and chipper proprietor of the Copper Cauldron, Parne’s an expatriate of the Tayan Empire who left to explore Ember's culinary landscape. While she's presently settled in Koto Springs, she has plans to move on eventually.

Rocklin Darix (Neutral, Ordani Hulg'run, they/them)

This patient, nearly silent caretaker tends the public moss gardens and pipes around the district with a backpack of tools and spare materials. Taciturn and more interested in their work that chatting, they have lived in Koto Springs for as long as anyone can remember. They have a standing agreement with district leadership to do their work.

Festra Yod (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

The matronly hostess of Gajak’s Rest and its current owner. She is the heart and soul of the inn, and is a highly respected fixture of the district after decades in the business. Festra wields kindness and hot meals like a fencer does a rapier.

Lore

Although many believe the district was named after its famed bathhouse, the truth is the reverse: the springs and their first great bath preceded the neighborhood, which slowly grew into a hub for both visitors and those seeking the springs’ rumored healing powers.

Whether the waters truly cure aches is a subject of friendly debate, but the legend itself is actively perpetuated by numerous merchants and bath owners that want to maintain the air of mystique around their venues.
Koto Springs.soverview: Home to numerous hot springs, small geysers, and geothermal hotspots, this district is one of the city's most popular, and sees intense foot traffic at all hours. There are always businesses and spas open, and street venders jockey for the best places to hock their wares to the passing crowds.
Koto Springs.sexposition: The air here is damp and rich with the scent of minerals, and a gentle haze of steam hangs over the entire district. It billows up from elegant stone aqueducts and winding pipes that crisscross overhead, channeling hot water into homes and bathhouses alike. The buildings around you are understated but give off subtle signs of wealth, with clean lines, immaculate gardens, and well-tended walkways.

Gossamer.name: Gossamer
Gossamer.text:
• District Type: Commercial (fashion) and Residential (fashion industry workers)

  • Population: 12,851 (Moderately dense population of workers in the fashion industry, along with a steady stream of both commercial and personal customers)

  • Lifestyle: Competitive (Hard-working fashion workers who like to publicly show off their skills and compete for local glory)

  • Services: Fashion (Fabrics, Clothing, Thread)

  • Influences: Closely tied to House Salva, the Trading House responsible for garments

Culture

Despite most of Gossamer being dedicated to the creation and design of fabrics, and the deep respect for all parts of the craft, there is occasional tension between the "makers" who spool thread and make raw fabric and the "drapers" who turn that fabric into fashion about who is more vital in the creation of the clothes Ordain wears. Both sides, though, have roughly the same values - work hard, try to make beautiful things, and take pride in seeing their work every time they walk through the streets of Ordain.

Gossamer often likes to think of itself as the hardest working district in Ordain, with most living not far from their workplaces and taking every opportunity to show off their skill. While Gossamer isn't about flashing wealth, many who work and live in the neighborhood will wear or carry something that shows how they contribute to the neighborhood, whether it's a pair of spool earrings, a raw-fabric scarf, or a piece of clothing made with fabric they wove.

Though work and fashion are important in Gossamer, they are not the only pastime. Friendly competition - between neighbors, coworkers, and shops - is common. The competitions take different forms, but tend to have some element of ridiculousness or silliness to they m and often use the materials of the district in ways they weren't intended to be used, ranging from tightrope walking on tightly braided threads to the annual "Spin to Win," where two groups compete to move heavy iron spinning wheels as far down the neighborhood's Threadfall Alley as they can without using magic. While most of the competition happens within Gossamer, they have a friendly rivalry with Highgate's Arcturian craftsfolk that shows up in occasional intermural games.

Landmarks

The Awlry

The Awlry specializes in fashion accessories that reflect the cosmos, ornamenting the scarves and belts they sell with small metal beads that are designed to catch the light and resemble stars in the sky and using fabric that changes color to mimic the changing of the moons over time. One of the secrets to this finery is in a hidden garden that can only be accessed by walking through the Awlry, which holds enchanted flowers believed to originate in Rhivan.

Snips

A bar where your clothes can be altered by the servers while you wait. Newcomers are not allowed to pick who alters their garment, though they are sometimes asked questions that supposedly connect them to the fitter who will work the best for them. Several of the servers also make clothes for stealth - it is said that if you find their card in your pocket, they've decided that you have promise as a spy or thief and want to attach themselves to you early.

Threadfall Alley

A long and narrow street that contains most of the weaving shops in Ordain. They advertise themselves to clients by weaving flags that show some aspect of their work and letting them fly in front of their shops. The use of air and wind spells to make the flags catch the breeze is common, but with so many people attempting the same effect, it can become a bit of a maelstrom. Any attempts to create rules to stop this have been rejected by all involved, who believe that the whipping winds of the alley are part of its charm.

The Wheel

A thread-spinning shop whose main spinning wheel (which takes several people to operate) has never slowed to a halt since the shop began. It is strongly believed that stopping the wheel will lead to some citywide calamity, and locals often feel that they are both saving the city through their work with the wheel and being ground down by it, depending on the day.

Locals

Vijin Barriq (Lawful Evil, Ordani Human, he/him)

Vijin spent his career cultivating his reputation as a weaver and has risen steadily over time through House Salva, using his influence to make connections within the district (making sure a certain threadmaker connects with a specific weaver, etc). It is well known within the district that those who gift him some of their goods (or their sewing time) are likely to have more buyers for their product, and he can often be seen wearing an array of fine clothing that doesn’t quite match but looks very expensive.

Tazhira Dyre (Chaotic Good, Ordani Kiska, she/her)

Tazhira is a talented cobbler who has been trying to get an official shop on Threadwalk Alley for years, but has yet to catch the attention of any Salva influencers with her “functional but not flashy” footwear. To try to get then to notice her products, which she walks in as she makes her way from her home across the city each day, she has begun adding magical effects to her shoes which range from creating an effect of mist as the wearer walks to leaving footprints that make them easier to track.

Jintal Aveniri (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, they/them)

The current three-year champion at Spin to Win, Jintal is somewhat famous in Gossamer for their incredible ingenuity in finding ways to get the iron spinning wheel moving without breaking any of the competition rules. Despite having been approached by a recruiter from the Anachraenum and an administrator from the Hallows about possibly putting their skills to a different use, Jintal has remained in their job collecting scraps that the various fabric shops of Gossamer no longer need, which they're trying to use to create a fabric construct.

Lore

The competitive nature of Gossamer is no accident - it was encouraged by House Salva to create camaraderie among workplaces, give the locals something to do as an outlet, and (if you ask the right people) prevent the vital workers who create Ordain's clothing from banding together and wanting more relaxed work conditions. The more intense that Gossamer's residents become at all aspects of life, the thinking goes, the more productive they will ultimately be.
Gossamer.soverview: This hardworking neighborhood is the heart of the fashion industry in Ordain. Not only does it produce much of the fabric and thread used and worn throughout Ordain, but it also houses the clothing shops responsible for much of the everyday clothing of the city. With so much to create and produce, long hours are common here, but the great respect that Ordain holds for fashion means that a fabric maker or button sewer can become a local celebrity alongside a dressmaker or designer, if they can distinguish themselves from their peers.
Gossamer.sexposition: A low but distinct hum of sound fills the air as soon as you enter Gossamer, made up of spinning wheels turning, scissors flying, and the movement of fabrics - being folded and measured, draped and redraped. While there are shops here, and eateries, this district is one of creation, with fabrics and accessories created in the spinneries and weaving shops on one side of the district and those materials transformed into the fashions and outfits that Ordain is known for on the other.

Embassy Rise.name: Embassy Rise
Embassy Rise.text:
• District Type: Institutional

  • Population: 2,368, (Low, district is busiest during the day, with frequent with diplomatic functions.)

  • Lifestyle: Political (Diplomats, clerks, and guards are semi-permanent residents.)

  • Services: Embassy offices, diplomatic lodgings, interpreters, meeting halls, access to Ordinate.

  • Influences: Outside cultures are concentrated within embassies, and the locals here are varied.

The district's embassies are imposing but elegant, each designed to showcase the prestige of the nation it represents. These buildings often blend ornate local stone with imported architectural styles and materials, making for a district unlike any other in the city.

High perimeter walls and iron gates are a common sight here, as are quiet courtyards shaded by imported trees and dotted with fountains. The district’s political weight means that only the well-connected — be they residents or visitors —move through it unchallenged.

Culture

Life in Embassy Rise is one of formality, and ever-present observation, whether by foreign officials or by embedded security. Dignitaries and diplomats keep careful schedules with meetings often running late into the evening, intermixed with banquets and garden receptions, all in service to political aims.

Security is omnipresent but discreet: nearly every embassy employs its own detail of guards, drawn from mercenary bands or the home nation's military, and many properties feature integrated residences for staff and their families.

In addition, the Veiled Chain's presence here is an open secret, and any long standing resident or worker in this district likely knows how to spot a few of the more obvious watchers placed here to keep tabs on things. As a result, there is an air of intrigue that one cannot deny in the district, as though the forces here play games with the delicate balance of power in Ordain.

Landmarks

The Council Ascent

The tallest structure in the district, this multi-storied structure not only grants a commanding view of the district, but is one of two ways into the Ordinate, and the one used by the envoys and ambassadors that live here in Embassy Rise.

Tayan Embassy

Regal and imposing, the imperial lines of the Tayan embassy's architecture stand in sharp contrast against the rest of the Ordani structures around it. The grounds are dotted with bubbling fountains and decorative waterfalls meant to remind the occupants of home and make eavesdropping all the more difficult.

Lumek Embassy

Distinctly square, and built out of a golden stone, this embassy is distinctly Lumekian in origin, a trait made all the more obvious by the massive brazier of black iron sitting out front, featuring a magical, ever-burning flame. A faint haze of acrid smoke hangs long around the grounds here, and the air is perpetually dry. Unlike most embassies, this one features a small guardhouse and contingent of Flameguard protectors at all times.

The Blue Lantern

A refined teahouse built on a steep overlook with a view of the lower waterfront districts, famed as a place for quiet parley and confidential discussion in its back rooms. The lantern that gives the spot its name glows with a striking blue radiance during business hours and is said to be nearly two centuries old.

Hall of Seals

An old, unassuming building of white stone, the Hall of Seals is the longest standing structure in the district, and one of great historical significance. Inside it displays the insignias, crests, flags and seals of every recognized delegation to Ordain. In addition it houses rare tomes of law, etiquette, and foreign customs for various nations and cultures. Here, visiting envoys and locals alike can consult texts on embark on knowledge-gathering pursuits in the hushed, marbled reading chambers within, along with any treaties they may hold with the city. While open the public, the documents contained within are accessible by city officials only.

Locals

Oathkeeper Orson Malv (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, they/them)

A senior archivist in the Hall of Seals, they track all comings and goings in the building, and personally oversee the small number of personnel tasked with guarding and maintaining the items within. They would die to protect the Hall of Seals.

Mira Solastis (Neutral Good, Ordani Signborn, she/her)

Owner of the Blue Lantern teahouse, Mira is quietly trusted by diplomats who seek neutral ground for private meetings. She maintains a collections of rare, imported teas from all over the world.

Vaeren Crosset (Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

A seasoned interpreter and master of seven language, Vaeren facilitates communication between embassies. She’s respected for her impartiality, though rumors suggest she keeps a private ledger of favors owed and owed to her.

Lore

In all cases the land here is provided by Ordain and broadly treated as foreign soil, allowing the members of the hill to have some measure of safety and autonomy. However, the Ordinate reserves the right to expel any member of the hill should it feel that the state's presence is no longer beneficial to the city. Though it is rarely necessary, all nations coming to do business in Ordain know they are there at the pleasure of the city alone.

As thinly hidden as the Veiled Chain’s presence is, most consider the surveillance the price of doing business here. The chain ensures peace while quietly cataloguing the ambitions of those who would shape Ordain’s path in the wider world, and those wishing to take advantage of Ordain's wealth and resources know they will be watched.
Embassy Rise.soverview: Embassy Rise is Ordain’s diplomatic heart: a wealthy and highly-guarded enclave of embassies and delegations from far-off nations, perched just below the Ordinate Spire. Here, foreign dignitaries, ambitious negotiators, and city officials meet to influence the policies that shape Ordain and its neighbors.
Embassy Rise.sexposition: Resting on a small plateau, this eclectic district sits above most of the city around it, but still under the imperious shadow of the great Ordinate Spire. The structures here are a mixture of classic Ordani design and elements of foreign cultures and aesthetics, making it one of the most visually discordant regions in the city. Its white-stone avenues flanked by high-walled estates and discreetly patrolled gates. Banners and crests from distant lands flutter above well-tended gardens, while carriages and footmen ferry dignitaries between towering embassies.

Lourd's Depot.name: Lourd's Depot
Lourd's Depot.text:
• District Type: Commercial and Transport

  • Population: 2,219 (Low. The depot is busy at all hours as ferries travel across the river.)

  • Lifestyle: Maritime. (Dock workers’ dormitories and sailors-only inns are common.)

  • Services: Cargo handling, storage, passenger ferries, dockside markets, maritime lodging.

Straddling the bustling docks of Lourd's Depot is the Destine river, the eastern branch heading off toward the bay of Ordain, while the eastern branch flows into what used to be a lake but has since become a meticulously maintained waterfront for the depot itself, Restaurant Row, and Pine Harbor to the west.

The district handles much of the northbound goods and is famed as the point where heavy cargo is sorted and disbursed to smaller wagons or ferries. Stacks of crates, merchant banners, and busy cranes define the skyline, while dockside markets overflow with provisions for sailors, travelers, and the city’s working class.

Culture

Life in Lourd’s Depot revolves around steady work and swift turnarounds. Crews of laborers come and go with the tides, unloading goods day and night, while small-time merchants, and porters stocking up along the piers.

The locals here maintain a rigid sense of duty and honor where a handshake is as good as a written contract, so long as you don’t break your word. Welshers quickly find that their word is worth nothing, and every deal must be in writing, even if they later make amends.

Landmarks

Walking Tours

A small kiosk run by members of the Anachraenum offers local history tours of the district. Guides gather in the central plaza, collecting groups and recounting tales of Lourd’s landing, the vanished lake, and the city’s early days.

Fork's Ferry

The oldest ferry operation on the plateau, Fork’s Ferry is famed for its reliability and ability to transport you to any of the adjacent waterfront location for only a silver. Veteran crews work in rotating shifts to ensure that passengers are getting moved across the city’s waterways in regular intervals. The old wooden hulls the crews run aren't fast, or particularly agile, but they are never late.

The Southern Hold

A large, secure warehouse that rents out storage by the month for a modest fee. Items stored here are kept secure and can only be accessed by the client and the hold's staff. The Hold is known for its efficiency and discretion.

Old Crane Tavern

Located in a a narrow avenue just off the main plaza, the Old Crane Tavern rings with the sound of music and revelry from midday to the evening hours as dock workers and ferrymen pack into its hall. The tavern takes its name from the district’s oldest hand-cranked crane which holds up the tavern's sign.

Locals

Vestra Lumar (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Fej, she/her)

Dockmaster of Lourd’s Depot, Vestre is a brisk, fire-eyed woman who manages scheduling and disputes with a firm, fair hand. She walks the piers at dawn and dusk, keeping careful track of incoming and outgoing cargo. She is known and somewhat infamous for her excellent memory and refusal to cut corners on paperwork.

Hario Harrick (Chaotic Good, Ordani Kivahr, he/him)

The most seasoned ferryman on the Fork’s Ferry line, Harrick is an affable, bearded veteran who leads his crew with skill and confidence. A former merchant captain, he retired to a quieter life as a ferryman, though one would argue his life is just as hectic now. He takes pride in the fact he can greet all his regular passengers by name.

Aldin Farrow (Neutral, Ordani Human, they/them)

Head clerk of the Southern Hold, Aldin is mild-mannered and precise, easily overlooked among the bustling dockworkers. They are known and somewhat infamous for their numerous relationships with House Bastilla captains, and rumors abound they keep track of numerous pirate treasures.

Udurin Peck (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

A chatty, gray-haired tour guide for the Anachraenum kiosk, he's been with the guild for decades, and is a dedicated scholar that knows a little bit about almost everything in the city. Peck is a font of obscure city lore and always ready to greet a visitor and show them around.

Lore

Besides its primary function as a commercial and ferry dock, Lourd's Depot also serves as a historical landmark. Named for being the landing site of Zuryx Lourd, an ambitious merchant looking to establish a foothold in the region and capitalize on the young Ordain's growth.

They arrived with several ships, built a series of warehouses in what was once a natural lake, and began to operate or fund ventures on the eastern banks of the city.

Though Lourd and their original depots are long gone and most have forgotten the origin of the name, the district still serves the same purpose: collecting and moving vital supplies to feed the various ventures and operations in the area.
Lourd's Depot.soverview: Lourd’s Depot is a busy and vital distribution hub on Ordain’s main waterfront, welcoming both cargo and passenger boats from every reach of the city and distant trade routes. Its ever-active piers, storied ferries, and reliable warehouses keep the wheels of commerce turning day and night.
Lourd's Depot.sexposition: Lourd's Depot bustles with steady movement that matches the flow of the river it sits by, as barges and small boats of goods and passengers come and go. Warehouses, docks, and looming cranes line the waterfronts and open plazas, each alive with clattering carts, shouted orders, and the rhythmic creak of timber and rope. No matter the hour or weather, the depot never truly sleeps.

Pine Harbor.name: Pine Harbor
Pine Harbor.text:
• District Type: Commercial (Docks, Marine Shipping and Warehousing)

  • Population: 2,288. (Light. Docks work all day, but house is limited to quarters for sailors and dockworkers.)

  • Lifestyle: Maritime. (Dockworkers, sailors, foremen, private guards and merchants are common.)

  • Services: Cargo handling, shipping administration, warehousing, haulers, weather reports.

Pine Harbor is the city’s busiest eastern-bank harbor and is often the first taste of Ordain for foreign traders and travelers. Its docks connect the bustling Lourd’s Depot to the north and the tiered sprawl of Highcrane to the south, serving as the vital anchor for Ordain’s daily trade.

Culture

The docklands of Pine Harbor is a place of relentless labor, strict schedules, and a tightly knit community. Here, the Trading Houses grind against independent foremen, unyielding Dockmasters, and the inescapable cost of commerce.

The entire district runs to an order dictated by the Pine Harbor Dock Office and the Dockmasters there. Though aligned with the Trading Houses in purpose, they are beholden to no master. Through them schedules are decided, and Trading House agents negotiate dock assignments, work fees and tariffs.

On the docks though, they must yield their authority to the army of independent longshoreman without whom nothing would move. Operating from cranes to wagons, these workers organize into unions lead by trusted foremen who in turn negotiate pay and shifts with Dockmasters. Enterprising captains may strike deals with foremen for preferred rates, and the Trading Houses retain the services of private stevedores to ensure their ships are never left waiting.

Landmarks

Pine Harbor Dock Offices

An imposing structure overlooking the harbor’s docks, this multi-storied building houses the schedules, shipping manifests, and team of dockmasters who orchestrate every arrival and departure in Pine Harbor.

Pine Crescent Warehouses

A stretching semicircle of stout, stone-and-timber warehouses equipped with iron-barred windows and watchful lanterns, storing everything from rare spices and silks to mundane grain and lumber. The warehouse section is named for and built over the land where pine timber used to accumulate from the eastern mill runs, forming a haphazard crescent of logs.

The Shellback Station

A rowdy dockside tavern and boarding house perched on the edge of the main quay. Each evening it fills with sailors and dock workers, laborers looking for a hot meal and a strong drink. with laughing sailors, grumbling laborers, and the warm glow of torches.

Harborwatch Spire

A tall, weather-stained watchtower that looms over the docks and allows the harbormasters to keep watch over the coming and going of ships. It also serves as a weather station where meteorological diviners prepare reports for captains looking to take specific trade routes.

Locals

Dockmaster Yolen Brack (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

Sharp and analytical, Yolen oversees docking schedules and takes pride in running a tight, incident-free harbor. She knows every incoming ship for the day and what dock team will be slated to handle it. She has plans for any delays that might threaten the day’s order, and believes being prepared is the key to success.

Haxton Narm (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, they/them)

A meticulous manifest clerk in the Dock Office, Haxton is the person to see for lost cargo or obscure paperwork. They keep a careful ledger of everything that passes through Pine Harbor and go out of their way to help honest traders navigate the bureaucracy.

Berrin Lathe (Neutral, Ordani Vrjnhar, he/him)

Owner of The River’s Rest, Berrin is burly, welcoming, and fiercely protective of both patrons and staff. Rumor holds he used to be a pirate but developed a conscience and prefers pouring ale and sharing news now.

Abel Howls (Neutral, Arcturian Zeph, he/him)

A devout follower of Vekalla, Abel is the chief diviner and weatherman of the Harborwatch Spire. He is laconic, only speaking when he must, and preferring to let his reports speak for themselves. When not poring over the day's forecast he can be found on the upper balconies of the tower watching the skies.

Lore

Named for the masses of wood that would accumulate from the mills to the North-East, the Pine Harbor's dock area initially extended out of Lourd's Depot to accommodate the ever increasing traffic coming into Ordain. Naturally, the accumulating timber was used to build the first sections of the docks.

Over time, the old wooden docks were reinforced with stone and packed earth, the sodden logs replaced with newer, treated wood, and supporting structures erected to facilitate the docking of larger and larger vessels which other docks were ill suited for.

The unionized longshoremen of Pine Harbor (and adjoining districts) came about after disputes between captains, Trading Houses, and local merchants lead to the dock workers suffering unreasonable hours and pay for backbreaking work. Though they are all quite competitive in their pursuit of contracts, at the end of the day they are all dedicated to the collective good of Ordain's vital longshoreman community.
Pine Harbor.soverview: Pine Harbor is the city’s principal dockyard, featuring immense piers and cranes built to facilitate the loading and unloading of the largest ships on Ember. Packed with rows of warehouses, the district makes the ceaseless movement of goods in and out of the city possible day and night.
Pine Harbor.sexposition:
Here, ships of all sizes crowd the docks, their hulls groaning beneath mountains of crates and barrels from distant lands or the bounty of Ordain’s hinterlands. The air carries the brine of the sea, mingled with the sharp tang of pitch and timber.

Dockworkers bellow orders above the screech of seabirds, while cranes wheel overhead, hoisting loads from bustling piers to waiting warehouses. Pine planks creak underfoot, never dry and never silent, as endless cargo moves across the wharves.

Numinous Shrines.name: Numinous Shrines
Numinous Shrines.text:
• District Type: Institutional with some Commercial and Residential

  • Population: 327 (Low. Shrines and temples with heavy-to-moderate foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Reverent (Modest homes for religious professionals and city workers).

  • Services: Spiritual guidance, healing, religious education and practice.

A central gallery known as the "Mall of the Nineteen" hosts individual shrines that serve each god in the eponymous local pantheon; and a few smaller altars and temples dedicated to more obscure deities can also be found here, erected somewhat haphazardly over the years as newer faiths gained purchase in Ordain. Occasionally, an errant doomsayer or fortune-teller can be found on a cobbled street corner within the Shrines, but these dogmatic opportunists are relatively few and far between. It's also not uncommon to see a few barges moored alongside the district's river channel to the south, where pilgrims have stopped to pay reverence to one or more gods, or passengers await chartered passage to other riverside areas of the city.

The Numinous Shrines are wholly open to the public, and are maintained by locals with assistance from the Hallows when necessary. This district is a popular spot for travelers and locals alike — not only as a venerated site for religious worship, but also as a place of simple respite where they might escape the metropolitan hustle and bustle (if only for a moment).

Landmarks

Mall of The Nineteen

This sprawling three story arcade connects nineteen distinct and individual shrines dedicated to one of the various gods in the revered Aterican pantheon. Most of the shrines to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen} here are housed within a gazebo or beneath the awning of a walkway, with few exceptions: the Shrine of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} and the Shrine of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka} each sit beneath an open sky, so that the sun and rain might fall upon their respective stone altars without obstruction. Servants of each of the faiths associated with The Nineteen regularly tend to their shrines, while three designated Shrinekeepers maintain a perpetual vigil over the Mall area as a whole. Remarkably, the shrine erected here for the elder god Sockets is a rather modest one compared to others (a direct result of the cultural and spiritual emphasis that's been placed on the Temple of Sockets in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.XUn8UELVkQmnCI78]{Temple Ward} by his adherents).

Piety Hall

Facilitated by the Ordinate and managed by a paid Resident Advisor, this large edifice houses dormitories and apartments for short- and long-term lodging here among the Numinous Shrines. Adherents to the various faiths of The Nineteen are afforded preferential treatment and discount rates, although any and all lawful citizens are actually welcome to take residence here. Yet, given Piety Hall's inherent aura of stoicism and selflessness, many find its confines to be a bit droll and lackluster compared to the opportunity and fervor found elsewhere in the city. Nevertheless, the Hall offers local clerics and priests some of the area's most reliable and affordable housing.

Destine Promenade

The Promenade is a public thoroughfare along the bank of the Destine in the southeastern edge of the district, where a modest array of market stalls and tents are erected around a small riverside concourse. Locals make use of this landmark as a convenient and valued stop on their way to or from the neighborhood's titular shrines. Destine Promenade isn't merely a public rest area, it provides a few commercial services for the pious — prayer books, holy symbols, and sacred materials are sold here for much more reasonable prices than elsewhere in the city, and information brokers cater to local specifics and the specific needs of Ordain's faithful.

Locals

Shrinekeeper Bolara Tol (Neutral Good, Human Ordani, she/her)

One of three duly-appointed Shrinekeepers, this kind-hearted cleric of Thoma serves as the senior custodian of the Mall of the Nineteen. The child of two Ordaini priests, she dutifully stepped into her role as Shrinekeeper at the earliest possible age. Treat Bolara Tol as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmPriest00000000]{Priest}.

Norrin Caertaris (Lawful Neutral, Human Waerd, he/they)

This scholarly adherent of Sigil works as the Resident Advisor of Piety Hall, and is known to regale visitors with Arcturian legends and capricious tales of "old Ordain" when they aren't buried in the pages of a good book.

Geb Navik (Chaotic Good, Keth Kithil, he/him)

Originally from the Kithil village of Hillhome north of Luen, Geb Navik is a whimsical merchant stationed at the Destine Promenade who caters to devotees of The Nineteen and their specific material needs. And while it remains close to his heart, Geb's nostalgia for his small-town youth is far exceeded by his passion for worldly people and Ordani commerce.

Lore

Ordani historians have well-traced accounts of the development of the Numinous Shrines and the Mall of the Nineteen that house most of them. However, several mysteries and legends lie at the heart of the district's eponymous landmarks. The most ubiquitous of these tall tales is perhaps the legend of "The Silent Acolyte," which chronicles the story of an apparition who visits the shrines of the four Elder Gods erected here; some say this apparition is a manifestation of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{Ven'avé}, while others maintain the Acolyte is a servant of Sockets who refuses the Soul Cycle for one reason or another. The most wizened of local adherents know the truth: the sightings are real, but the Silent Acolyte's motivations remain inscrutable to this day.
Numinous Shrines.soverview: Nestled between the River Destine and the eastern shadows of the Ordinate Spire, the Numinous Shrines district is one defined by its overt serenity and the welcoming nature of its varied practitioners of faith. The Numinous Shrines are generally regarded as a sacred space by all denizens of Ordain, who are free to worship the gods as they choose.
Numinous Shrines.sexposition: The soothing sounds of wind chimes and muttered prayer greet you as you enter a neighborhood marked by the austerity of holy shrines and the natural beauty manicured gardens. An aura of reverence hangs about this central city district, where countless stone pathways crisscross between more than two dozen places of worship. Each of these shrines, temples, or altars is rather distinct in its own way, and a wondrous array of priest, pilgrims, and acolytes pay homage to their respective faiths here. To the east, one can hear the low roar of the River Destine, which finds its way into the Numinous Shrines by way of a series of smaller channels at the southern edge of the district.

Lilifeld Stations.name: Lilifeld Stations
Lilifeld Stations.text:
• District Type: Industrial and Commercial

  • Population: 2,490 (Moderate-to-High, always busiest during market hours, dawn to dusk.)

  • Lifestyle: Industrial-Commercial. (Warehouse workers, caravaneers, traders, house Lillifeld associates.)

  • Services: Agricultural warehousing, milling, produce markets, roadside eateries.

Lilifeld Stations is dominated by sturdy granaries and busy mills, all watched over by the banners of Trading House Lilifeld. These warehouses secure all the city’s grain, flour, and harvested goods coming in from Redrak Fields before they’re sent to other markets or stored for future need. The district’s heart is its celebrated Lilifeld Granary, a landmark of both pride and practical importance.

The surrounding streets are tightly woven with depots and shops, all offering work to haulers, clerks, and barrowmen who ferry foodstuffs through the city. Though House Lilifeld is the district’s namesake, other trading houses — most notably Salva — keep offices and agents here to take advantage of the markets and keep watch over operations.

Culture

The Station’s culture is professional, neighborly, and fiercely loyal to House Lilifeld which has done its level best to take care of the people here. Everybody is well fed here, partially paid in grain and produce, which helps keep the workforce strong and dedicated. That loyalty even extends to the numerous merchants and restauranteurs that come directly to the Stations to procure their goods, rather than seeking supplies elsewhere.

Lilifeld Stations is less forgiving to smuggling and mischief than other districts in this part of the city: House Lilifeld keeps scrupulous records, and local law is enforced with an even hand by a small army of house officers and guards.

Landmarks

Lilifeld Granary

The city’s largest and most vital warehouse: a colossal, domed structure of pale stone and timber, filled floor to rafters with the stores of Ordain's bread supply. Teams of grain porters and tall grain elevators bustle from dawn till midnight. It is protected day and night by Trading House guards.

Willow Street Farmer’s Market

A patchwork sprawl of produce stalls and crate-filled booths, this daily open-air market offers the best vegetables, fruit, and nuts brought in from the eastern fields. Packed during the day by locals trying to get their staples, the prices are reasonable and stocks ample. However it is all but empty by sundown.

Liliman’s Bar & Grille

Named after one of the smaller Trading Houses that preceded House Lilifeld, this low, brick-walled tavern is adorned with faded field banners of old houses hung from ancient wooden beams. Liliman's is a working-class establishment that prides itself on being an accessible lunch and dinner spot, and sees heavy traffic from workers and merchants alike. It serves hearty meals and strong spirits at all hours.

Riverwall Depot

An old riverside warehouse converted to a bustling transit and weighing station for barges moving between districts. Owned and operated by House Lilifeld, nothing leaves here before paperwork is processed, loads are weighed, and arrival points are settled by posted clerks.

Locals

Darissa Liliman (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

The stalwart, matronly barkeep of Liliman’s Bar & Grille, Darissa is trusted by all and knows everyone who calls the Stations home. She often mediates neighborly disputes and is a source of quiet wisdom for newcomers. She is well known for making sure nobody goes hungry in her bar, even if they can't pay.

Jurlan Savas (Neutral, Ordani Cor'ak, he/him)

A pragmatic foreman at the Lilifeld Granary, Jurlan oversees shifting crews and storage records. He is known for his tireless energy, sharp memory, and clean-handed honesty in all dealings. As foremen go, he prefers to mix it up with his teams, and can be found moving shipments and goods when not handling paperwork.

Paela Tern (Chaotic Good, Ordani Signborn, she/her)

A cheerful market overseer of Willow Street's market, Paela manages the stalls and allots space to merchants that will sell during the daily hours. With a booming laugh and easy manner, she spins stories out of thin air, and constantly jokes that she missed her calling as a bard.

Matin Folke (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

A quiet, meticulous warehouse clerk stationed at the Riverwall Depot, Matin is responsible for keeping all incoming grain accounts balanced. He is known for his patience, discretion, and ability to spot irregularities others might miss.

Lore

The importance of the Lilifeld Granary cannot be overstated: any threat to its supply or integrity is met with swift response from both the Trading House and the Ordinate. Each year, the Stations’ market and storerooms feed thousands and in lean seasons, have staved off disaster more than once. The district’s order and prosperity remain a quiet backbone to the city’s vibrant daily life.

Additionally, in a bed to leverage this importance, House Lilifeld has begun investing in local restaurants on the waterfront, specifically in Restaurant Row, with intent to influence the markets through food culture, supply and demand, and price fixing. Though some within the House frown on this practice, it has substantially grown the profitability of the district's markets, which has benefitted the house and city alike.
Lilifeld Stations.soverview: Named after the neighborhood’s presiding Trading House, this welcoming mercantile district is the hub of agricultural commerce in Ordain. Almost everything the city eats passes through this bustling district.
Lilifeld Stations.sexposition: Broad avenues track between soaring granaries and squat, weathered mills as wagons, brimming with sacks of grain and baskets of vegetables, rumble past on cobbled streets. The air hangs thick with the sweetness of ripe produce, flour dust, and tang of work animals.

Fallbrook.name: Fallbrook
Fallbrook.text:
• District Type: Residential with some entertainment

  • Population: 19,606 (Dense population of younger residents supplemented by an active nightlife scene)

  • Lifestyle: Fun-loving (Young and energetic residents willing to try new things and accept all comers)

  • Services: Entertainment (Nightclubs, theaters, bars, and the occasional bordello)

  • Influences: Has the largest Kithil community in Ordain.

Culture

Fallbrook was once a fairly unremarkable residential neighborhood known mostly for its river views, but after a small community of Kithil settled in the area, they worked to make it more comfortable for their nocturnal lifestyle, designing awnings that generate shadow and darkness so that they could avoid Lantyr’s direct gaze when possible. While the district looks similar to any other at a distance, a walk through its streets leads to unexpected nightfalls and patches of dusky shadow that have been called dangerous, romantic, and “very easy to trip and fall in,” depending on who you ask.

The dim lighting, coupled with a number of overnight businesses that catered to Kithil clients, slowly began to make Fallbrook a destination for nightlife in Ordain. Soon, dance halls and taverns were beginning to crowd the district’s streets, leading locals, with the permission of the Ordinate, to declare that all new ventures had to have some tie to Kithil culture or have a strong nightlife purpose to be in the district. Although there are still some older establishments in the district that predate this rule, most of the popular venues are either run by Kithil or have an agreement with the locals to operate a business with their support.

Landmarks

The Bronze Rask Theater

This long-standing theater came into its name when a visiting noble donated a large bronze statue of a Rask to the theater as thanks for a performance they especially liked. Lacking anywhere else to put it, the statue ended up in the lobby, where it stands to this day. Though small in size and prestige, the local Fallbrook Performers that call this place home welcome all aspiring artists and performers of Ordain. From repertory theater to avant garde musical concerts, the Bronze Rask is a haven for anyone and everyone who is a bard at heart. Owned and operated by Dory "Dangerous" Doss, a former adventurer and mercenary who has rebranded himself as a wealthy, bohemian raconteur

Moonrise

The collective name for a series of clubs in one of the waterworks that once brought water from the river into the Ordain, but was cut off by the Big Shake of 20 years earlier. It has been transformed to look like Ember's night sky, with its side passages transformed into small clubs themed after the different moons of Ordain.

The Shading

Many buildings in the district feature awnings that generate darkness or cast a shadow, hiding those beneath them from Lantyr's light. The Shading is a path, marked by glowing stones, that takes locals from one shadowed awning to the next so they can avoid sunlight if they want to. At night, when the effects of the awnings are more minimal, it is often used as a walking route through the district in a tradition known as a Shading Stroll.

The Sunnery

A lightbathing spa and cafe that uses a series of mirrors and a bit of magic to heighten the brightness of Lantyr's light. Created to help counter the belief that the district is all shadows and dark, it is only rarely used by locals, but has become popular with visitors to Ordain as a place to watch boats go by on the river.

Tatters

Billed as a place of "natural debauchery," Tatters is a small park that has turned into a 24-hour club. Planted with a number of thickets and bushes that work together to create an atmosphere of fevered partying, it features thorns that snag clothing but not flesh (giving the area its name), duskberries that create pockets of darkness, a number of Rubita blooms, which are said to give off a slightly euphoric scent (though this has never been proven). At the new year, this is the local site for the traditional and adults-only Kithil welcoming of the New Year.

Locals

Ivreain Coravi (true neutral, Kithil keth, they/them)

Ivreain Coravi (ihv-RAIN core-AH-vee) is the leader of the Kithil community within Ordain and a bit of a stick-in-the-mud. Though he is happy that the district has been able to become a welcoming home for those who feel, as he does, that Lantyr's light is an oppressive force, and enjoys looking for ways to imbue the area with Kithil culture, he does not like that the district has become so synonymous with wild partying, fearing that it is giving visitors the wrong impression about the beliefs and priorities of the Kithil villages.

Xiantille Luenne (neutral good, Kithil human, she/her)

Xiantille (ZHAWN-til LOO-enn) was born with another name but changed it, as well as everything else about her, after traveling to the Kithil villages as a teenager and becoming obsessed with Kithil culture and the moons. Determined to make others see the beauty of Ember’s moons in a new way, she returned to Ordain and opened a fortune telling and tattoo business based on an individual’s lunar attunement. Viewed with a bit of suspicion by Kithil who feel that she only has a surface-level understanding of their culture, Xiantille can often be found in whichever of Moonrise's clubs corresponds to the current moon that is brightest in the sky.

Ellrie Tincer (lawful neutral, Ordani keth, she/her)

Ellrie has always been curious about what others were up to, spending much of her time even before joining the Hallows hanging out under one of the district's awnings and hoping to be hidden enough by its shadows to listen in to the local conversation. While she aspires to be part of the Veiled Chain, Ellrie likes to show off, dropping bits of whatever knowledge she’s gained into conversation, which makes her a less than ideal operative. Instead, she has been relegated to making sure that the many clubs in the area don’t overcrowd – a position she uses to continue to mine the area for gossip.

Lore

The reliance on the Kithil villages for some of its food supply has generally made the Ordinate more willing to make deals and concessions to local Kithil in the city who have ties back to their homelands, lest a hard stance create an issue for the Trading Houses or the Ordani people. Some politicians and Ordinite council members like to bring up the bad harvest of 18 years ago (known in the Kithil Villages as Lantyr's Scorn) and the cities' bending of norms to facilitate Kithil practices as an erosion of Ordani cultural dominance, but people don't take these complaints seriously.
Fallbrook.soverview: These days, Fallbrook is known not for the relatively calm currents that allow for passing over the river, but the shadows within its streets — placed there purposefully by the Kithil residents of the district who wish to live in Ordain while avoiding the bright light of day. This dedication to nocturnal living has made Fallbrook a popular spot for late night dancing and carousing, with establishments that tend to take some aspect of Kithil culture and shift it to create a theme for their decor and entertainment.
Fallbrook.sexposition: If not for the shadows and the thrum of music beneath your feet, this could be any residential district in Ordain, but both are unexpectedly present wherever you turn. Patches of dusky light that seem to have no origin source linger in the air and cast shadows on the paved ground, you can hear the faint sound of drumming, and occasionally a group emerges from some dark corner that is anything but natural, rushing off in excitement toward some place you aren't sure you were invited to.

Hunter's Wood.name: Hunter's Wood
Hunter's Wood.text:
• District Type: Residential (villas, lodging houses) with some commercial (tours, creature parts)

  • Population: 7,979 (Moderately dense mix of transient hunters and trackers, alongside wealthier locals who enjoy living close to nature)

  • Lifestyle: Outdoorsy (Whether out in the nearby Arctus Plateau or in their manicured gsrdens, locals appreciate and value the natural world)

  • Services: Tourism (monster hunting tours) and materials (creature parts)

Culture

While the dirt streets of Hunter's Wood don't appeal to everyone, the district remains popular among locals who want the feeling of being away from it all while still remaining in close proximity to the Hallows, Ordinate, and other places of influence in Ordain.

Those who prefer the aesthetic of the wilds to the reality live in majestic second-story villas that use illusion magic and clever construction to appear as if they are sunlit glades or moon-touched grottos, while those who hunt, track, or explore in the Plateau outside of the city live in the basic but serviceable lodgings camouflaged within the trees in the district's forested ground level. Many of these local hunters and druids are quite talented, and Hunter's Wood has become known in Ordain as a place to find rare creature parts, take tours into the Plateau, or train in the use of nature magic with the help of the Anachraenum.

Despite the residents' very different approaches to natural living, they generally get along well, in part because keys to the Hunter's Gate are limited in number. While many are passed down through families, especially among the villa residents, a few change hands each year, given to those who have made significant contributions to the district at an annual gathering called the Call of the Wild that is well-known in neighboring districts for its liberal use of birdcalls as an expression of celebration.

Landmarks

The Bottomless Grotto

A local tavern and impromptu trading post hidden behind an illusion of a waterfall. Decorated with furniture shaped to look like tree roots and wild vines, it features a wall carved with a map of the nearby section of the Arctus Plateau. Dangers and treasures have been marked on the map by trackers, using a shorthand not well understood outside of the district.

The Hunter's Gate

A small gate that connects this section of Ordain to a "wild" section of the Arctus Plateau frequented by Ordani hunters, trappers, and trackers. A protective enchantment designed by the Anachraenum prevents its location from being found by anyone without a key, even if they have previously traveled through it, and is believed to attract enough wild creatures to the area that it is impossible to overhunt.

Logroll

This low-cost lodging area in the center of Hunter's Wood offers places to rest for those who don't have much coin or need much comfort. Its offerings range from bedrolls in weatherproofed tubes decorated to look like fallen logs to tree-slung hammocks for those who prefer sleeping in the open air. Though all of its beds are known for producing less than restful nights, proprietor Pavel Lenai (Ordani human, he/him) claims this is a purposeful feature that prevents hunters from accidentally sleeping too deeply while out in the wild.

Villa Renari

A lavish villa that uses a combination of elaborate illusions and water spells to create a babbling brook running through the center of a sunny glade. The brook distorts conversations, making eavesdropping difficult. As a result, the villa a popular place to talk about confidential cases or share secrets among Hallows officials in the area.

Locals

Dariana (true neutral, Ordani keth, she/her)

Dariana runs the Bottomless Grotto and is determined to make it one of the top taverns in Ordain. Recently introduced season-long scorecards for hunters to use to prove their prowess by capturing particularly dangerous creatures of the Plateau. Though this is leading some groups to take excessive risks, it is also driving business to the Grotto, especially since she started offering side bets to patrons on which hunter will take the prize.

Jalik Blaines (chaotic neutral, Waerd human, she/her)

Jalik has tried for multiple years to make her walking tour business, "Plants: A Waerd's eye view," into a success, but customers find her more surly than personable. This, along with a few non-fatal poisonings caused by her policy of letting her customers taste whatever they want as long as it won't kill them, has caused her to lose her Hunter's Gate key to more tourist-friendly businesses. Bitter over the loss, Jalik has been introducing dangerous plant life into hidden corners of the district, hoping that she will be able to run to the rescue of anyone who stumbles upon them and be given a new key as a hero of the district.

Filp Kindering (lawful neutral, Ordani human, he/him)

A prominent judge within the Hallows who inherited Villa Renari despite not particularly liking nature. Has been trying to get in the spirit by frequenting the Bottomless Grotto, to the dismay of those who like to get raucous in the tavern and worry that he is judging them.

Desty Lam (chaotic good, Ordani human, they/them)

A merchant who regularly ambles through Hunter's Wood looking for those going through the gate to offer potions and other supplies. Desty fancies themselves a brilliant hunter in the making, though their "tips for the wilderness" are always wrong. Will give a deep discount to anyone who can get them a key to Hunter's Gate.

Lore

Hunters' Gate was used in the early days of Ordain by those who provided food and natural materials to the growing city, including some of the traders who would go on to found the agriculturally-minded House Lillifeld. While Ordani policy might have normally walled it off to prevent against creature attacks, it is home to several prominent members of the Hallows who like the idea that they could quickly escape the city if they ever needed to. The current key system, which limits who has access to the gate, was developed as a compromise.

The existence of Hunter's Wood is also seen as a defense against any escapees from Spellbreaker Tower, who could theoretically be tracked and hunted down by any locals in the area in an environment they might not be otherwise expecting.
Hunter's Wood.soverview: Favored by those who want to live as close to nature as they do to the hustle and bustle of the city, Hunter's Wood is a mix of high-end "nature villas" for those who like the appearance of the wilderness and no-nonsense lodging for those who spend much of their time outside of the city limits as hunters, trackers, and tour guides. It is notable both for its appearance, which resembles a wild forest, and for Hunter's Gate, an exit to the Arctus Plateau through the district that is accessible only to locals with a key.
Hunter's Wood.sexposition: As you enter Hunter's Wood, the stone buildings of Ordain seem to disappear, covered over by patches of thick leaves in the gold and red colors of the Arctus Plateau. Beneath your feet, densely packed dirt replaces the normal Ordani stone, creating a winding path through the bushes and trees of the district. This is no park, evenly spaced or gently arranged, but a half-wild expression of nature, as if the stones of Ordain had decided to grow a forest of their own accord. Along with the babbling of running water and the wind shifting through the trees, it is filled with the murmurings of sales pitches, as hunters in traveling leathers make their pitches to each newcomer about their "tours of the Arctus Plateau" and the world beyond the nearby Hunter's Gate.

Palisade Cross.name: Palisade Cross
Palisade Cross.text:
• District Type: Residential with some Commercial

  • Population: 25,939 (High. Historical and redeveloped homes with heavy foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Modest-to-Comfortable (Hirelings, sellswords, laborers, craftspeople, opportunists).

  • Services: Lodging, housing, grocery, equipment, hirelings.

This rough-and-tumble district was historically one of Ordain's more affluent neighborhoods, but the endless march of time has slowly robbed the area of that status. As time goes by, the once-proud stone buildings sag a bit more than they used to, and the splinters of the timber dwellings become harder and harder to hide. Today, Palisade Cross is much more a representation of the city's transplants than its settlers — a disparate sprawl of people from various places who come together under a united promise of achievement and growth.

Despite its outward looks, Palisade Cross is a rather progressive neighborhood, whose people tend to have a forward-facing approach to their existence here (rather than a painstaking examination of Ordain's past). In fact, many of the denizens of Palisade Cross make their living (and often a good one that) as hirelings for various adventurers, explorers, or profiteers. If you need an extra hand for a profitable escapade, Palisade Cross is a good place to look for one.

Landmarks

Fletcher's

This imposing timber edifice on the western edge of the district is what remains of a once-proud manse known as Fletcher's Community Home for Wayward Youths, a place where Ordain's lost and abandoned adolescents could find the simple pleasures of home, hearth, kith, and kin. But Fletcher's days as an orphanage of warm repute have long fallen by the wayside. Now, this rickety wooden behemoth lies dark and abandoned, and its skeletal eaves of splintered lumber loom above the rest of the district like some monolith of time forgotten. Fletcher's casts a pall over the people of Palisade Cross, who believe various tall tales and legends that surround the place — like the story of the spectral orphans that haunt the mansion's darkest corridors, or the tale of a roguish wizard who sought a place to hide but found his doom instead.

The Cracked Flagon

The tower-shaped vestibule of this dingy watering hole resembles a massive stone flagon, embellished with steel and copper fineries; notably, it bears a large crack down the vertical length of its front side, from the roof's edge to the top of the front door jamb. Employees (and a plaque next to the front door) are quick to inform newcomers of the crack's origin during the Great Stonework Quake of 2503, and there is a distinct air of novelty throughout the tavern's musty interior, despite its relative age. The Cracked Flagon known city-wide as a great place to soak up a good story while sipping on a frosty ale.

The Hayren Arms

This huge, multi-story apartment building provides ample housing for the locals. Originally built by the Hayren noble house for their personal army of servants and guards, it eventually became a dwelling for rent by the people of Ordain at large. The apartments here are small, and plain, with only room for the basics, but the cost is low. The people of Hayren Arms are good and decent, providing a packed community that looks out for its own.

Rylo's Rooms

A large inn partially build into the massive stone pillar found in the district, Rylo's Rooms is the largest inn to be found in Ordain, with several hundred rooms, all offered at low prices. What it lacks in creature comforts and quality it makes up for in affordability. Founded by Erban Rylo several decades ago, it's now run by his children.

Locals

Lady Wells (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

This retired schoolmarm serves as the reclusive caretaker for the estate upon which Fletcher's resides; however, she actually plays very little part in the landmark's preservation or maintenance, and has fallen to the wayside as much as the abandoned estate itself. Considered by many to be a "crazy old hermit," the absentminded Lady Wells is shunned by most of the denizens of Palisade Cross, and rarely seen outside of her own ramshackle apartment (situated in the shadows of Fletcher's, at the end of a row of similar low-income housing).

Hafton Tradd (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

This congenial patriarch is the owner and head barkeep of The Cracked Flagon, which he almost fully staffs with members of his rather jubilant family. The cousin of a venerated Anachraenum alumnus, Hafton offers steep discounts and complimentary beverages to members of Ordain's famed guild of treasure hunters; as a result, a lot of interesting rumors and legends find their way to the gregarious barkeep's ears (which are always open for more).

Lore

The eponymous palisades of Palisade Cross were erected during the district's earliest days, and have been all but forgotten as the neighborhood was slowly built upon and around them. Indeed, much of the original palisade serves as the architectural foundation for what became Fletcher's — so west-side denizens of Ordain tend to usually have an eye on the neighborhood's namesake, whether they know it or not.
Palisade Cross.soverview: Palisade Cross is a residential district known primarily for its low profile, its affordable housing, and the historical significance of a few of its local landmarks — including the abandoned schoolhouse known as Fletcher's, which is rumored to be haunted by strange spectral entities and woeful phantoms of the city's past. Thanks to the considerably affordable cost of living here, Palisade Cross attracts a great deal of Ordain newcomers, as well as scrappy adventuring types like sellswords and spellcasters-for-hire. This is a neighborhood where people go to be left alone, and where unwanted attention can often disappear like a bad dream — out of sight, but never fully out of mind.
Palisade Cross.sexposition: A cramped neighborhood of stone and timber buildings is laid out before you, resembling some massive stack of ramshackle crates, piled three stories high. Here and there, a modest tower or spire rises out of the sprawl, hinting at the presence of a few older, affluent structures among the modern. One curious edifice looms higher than the rest: a rickety, time-worn mansion crafted from a strange soot-colored lumber, pockmarked with ruin and painted with crooked shadows. The people of this teeming residential district pay this aged monument little heed as they go about their daily business; you spy a measurable amount of world-weariness upon several faces, as if the disinterested locals here have seen it all.

Trader's Corner.name: Trader's Corner
Trader's Corner.text:
• District Type: Commercial with some Residential.

  • Population: 12, 130. (High. Fine townhomes house the wealthy on main streets while middle and low income housing can be found on side streets in historic neighborhoods off the main avenues.)

  • Lifestyle: Mixed. (Locals are wealthy merchants and nobility, but outside foot and wagon traffic is constant throughout the day.)

  • Services: High-end retail, fine dining, exclusive goods.

Trader’s Corner is an old, historic district that has undergone expansion, reconstruction, and revitalization many times throughout its existence. In the shadows of new construction and shining white stone are older, stoic structures of rock and wood that hearken back to earlier days of the district. Though even these markers of history are vanishing behind new facades of stone, or face outright replacement.

Culture

Trader's Corner is a place of affluence, commerce, and leisure, at least for those who visit it as customers. Operating around the throngs of shoppers, entourages of elite hangers-on, and visiting elite from beyond the city is an army of shopkeepers, tailors, jewelers, painters, and Trading House funded guards that keep things running.

Trader's Corner relies on the sweat, skill, and dedication of the common folk, but its clientele prefer not to be reminded of it. As a result, this divide is a clear one, but deliberately painted over with the finery crisp uniforms, and mercantile etiquette.

Landmarks

Crossway Plaza

A broad public plaza connecting major avenues between other districts, this plaza sees intense traffic at almost all hours of the day. Capitalizing on the constant traffic, the plaza holds most of the district's most popular shops, offering art, food, drink, and fashion at a high premium. Whether the quality is truly better remains a matter of opinion, but the sellers here swear their offerings are second to none.

Goldwire Avenue

This cluster of jewelry shops and metalsmiths sit tucked into a single, winding side street, and is considered the single best place in all the city to acquire accents, accessories and statement pieces for one's wardrobe. Inside each storefront are secured cases of expertly made and perilously overpriced pieces that can be had by any with the coin.

Silver Street Market

Located just a few minutes away from Crossway Plaza, this small market is where the various servants and house stewards working for the elites of Marlstone come to refill pantries. The good here are overpriced to take advantage of the clientele, like much of Trader's Corner, leaving locals to look elsewhere for their needs.

The Laurel Table

An elegant restaurant set within a historic townhouse, famous for its seasonal menus and rooftop garden. Meals are extravagant and expensive at the invite only establishment, and its head chef is notorious for turning away guests for improper conduct.

Sarmell Wharf

Named for someone history has long forgotten, the tiny wharf of Trader's Corner practically disappears into the greater waterfront area of Ordain, but the few docks and warehouses there almost exclusively serve this district and its businesses. The wharf maintains a private stevedore team.

Locals

Lirma Grell (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

Lirma runs the tiny wharf on the south end of the district. She is exacting and composed, adept at managing the expectations of wealthy patrons, local merchants, and her crew. She mostly handles private deliveries from other locations on the waterfront, and knows not to ask questions.

Yerig Fenmarch (Neutral, Ordani Nir'ae, he/him)

A local healer that travels between businesses and homes taking care of folks who may have become injured or fallen ill. He is in charge of the local noticerie and has close ties with the Cindarics, of which he is a devout follower. Yerig is a trusted and beloved figure throughout the district.

Shevra Tassel (Lawful Good, Ordani Kivahr, she/her)

Captain of the local House Bastilla funded guard contingent, Shevra coordinates patrols across the affluent parts of the the district with vigilance. Though she knows her guards are only there to protect the commercial interests of her House, she makes sure that her guards look after the shopkeepers and workers as best they can, if only to keep things running smoothly.

Hestyl Drein (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Signborn, he/him)

The brilliant and often tempestuous head chef at The Laurel Table. Hestyl mixes tradition with innovation, drawing patrons from every corner of the city with dishes and flavors found nowhere else. He is notoriously hard to work with, firing cooks and servers often for whatever failure he cannot stand that week.

Lore

While the public face of Trader's Corner is new and elite, a smaller, lesser known community exists behind it, in the shadows. The few historic streets that remain have been relegated to housing for middle and lower income families that work in the district. The businesses in these historic areas are smaller, much more modest, and serve just the locals. Most that visit the district will never see them.
Trader's Corner.soverview: Trader’s Corner is a nexus of affluence and commerce where fine boutiques provide high end goods and services to the wealthy neighborhoods nearby. Though mostly catering to the wealthy in the area, Trader's Corner also consists of a few hidden streets of historic buildings and shops behind the glitz and glitter of the main roads.
Trader's Corner.sexposition:
Broad avenues of white stone stretch out before you, lined with gorgeous structures featuring the sweeping lines and elegant curves of Ordain's newest architectural movements. Shops display their wares in carefully curated arrangements that catch the eye and dare you to come purchase something.

Just once glance at the listed prices in a shop window tells you this is a district of wealth and affluence, or taking advantage of it at least.

Exile's Landing.name: Exile's Landing
Exile's Landing.text:
• District Type: Commercial with some Residential.

  • Population: 19,000 (High, busiest during daylight, remains lively in the evenings due to taverns and inns.)

  • Lifestyle: Eclectic (Waves of visiting merchants and tourists mingle with the numerous locals .)

  • Services: Docking, cargo exchange, river shipping, inns, historical harbor, taverns, and docks.

Exile’s Landing hugs the western riverbank of the Destine, and the district’s working harbor remains vital, alive with cargo ships and fishing boats alike, their arrivals counted as they have been for centuries.

At the district’s core, preservation and progress mingle: historic facades and brickwork stand beside new shops and warehouses, as centuries of rebuilding and renewal slowly overtake the oldest pieces of Ordain's history.

Culture

Exile’s Landing is the city’s soul laid bare: a place where centuries of history, and historians fight against the needs of industry and commerce demanding expansion and renovation. Hanging in the balance is the first pieces of Ordain's founding.

While the district committees work closely with the Anachraenum to preserve old buildings, document the history of the place, the immense prosperity from the affluent Marlstone and Coinwealth Heights districts has inevitably flowed downhill and brought an ongoing wave of gentrification with it.

Facing the loss of the district and city's history, locals and historians have begun to resist, if only to buy themselves enough time to preserve some of Ordain's oldest structures, though some view it as a lost cause.

Landmarks

Ten Step Tavern

A sleek and modern structure of smooth, white stone, this tavern rests in the middle of two roads leading up to more affluent districts. A placard declares it to be the district's oldest pub, but it looks anything but old. The original structure was torn down a few years back, and replaced with a much more modern building, and reworked to cater to richer clientele.

Old Refuge Inn

Among the city’s oldest operating inns, albeit rebuilt numerous times, this old structure is weathered, and still bears smudges of smoke damage in places. Inside, its floors are paved with some of the original stones that lined the district's streets, and it reportedly has timbers taken from the first ships that landed, though nobody knows if that's true.

Wid Street Market

A small but vibrant marketplace where vendors hawk wares and locals acquire their staples. Once the district's central market, it has since become geared to tourists and visitors. Now, much of the market has become overpriced and choked with souvenirs and baubles exalting the historic district

Yarin Hall

A stately, columned structure standing at the top of a rise, overlooking a good portion of the district. Once made of recovered ship timber, and local wood, it was rebuilt in gleaming white stone after a devastating fire claimed the original structure. It is now maintained as a small museum and event space. Yarin Hall is a center for district meetings, civic celebrations, the First Landing Historical Society.

Locals

Darik Volst (Lawful Evil, Ordani Human, he/him)

An enterprising owner of the Ten Step Tavern, Darik bought the old structure, tore it down, and built new. He heads the local business association, and actively champions the modernization of Exile's Landing to benefit local merchants and noble.

Navir Chari (Lawful Neutral, Lumek Fej, he/him)

Navir is the wizened keeper of the Old Refuge Inn, and has been running the inn since he was a young man. He dislikes the rich and wealthy injecting themselves into the area, and intends to run the inn until he keels over just to spite the people trying to buy it.

Salla Embral (Neutral, Ordani Ashka, she/her)

An Anachraenum preservation architect overseeing restoration projects in the district, Salla has strong ideas about what must be saved — and what can be adapted. She is equally at home in archival records and negotiating with wealthy merchants.

Paddock Vale (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, they/them)

A local street performer, storyteller, and veteran of the Anachraenum. Paddock is the head of the First Landing Historical Society, and spends all his time bringing to life the saga of the city’s founding for anyone willing to listed.

Lore

Eight centuries ago refugees made landfall at the mouth of the Destine river on the western shores. The settlers broke up their vessels for timber, using the planks and spars to raise the first crude shelters, piers, and watch-posts that would anchor their new home. The settlement was known as Exile’s Landing — a place where hope could be kindled, and a new beginning found.

This district is there the great collaborative dream of Ordain was born. For decades it was the center of all commerce and government, and it grew outward in rings, not unlike the trunk of a tree. As it did, Exile's Landing went from a sparse village to a town, to a city. Eventually the district's authority was shifted elsewhere, but the history remained.

Four centuries ago a fire swept through the dock front, consuming much of the historic wharves and crowding riverfront. The fire’s scars remain today, with a few buildings still bearing smoke damage, and a handful of fire-blackened pilings sunk deep beneath the modern piers.
Exile's Landing.soverview: Exile’s Landing is Ordain’s point of origin, the site where the city’s first settlers landed, and from which the city grew. Exile's Landing is a mixture of old and new, its docks bustling and modern, but just beyond it, old stones, historic buildings, and relics of the past can be found.
Exile's Landing.sexposition:
Weathered timber wharves stretch into the river’s path, where broad, venerable ships take shelter against the deep, steady flow of the Destine. The crash and chatter of cargo routines echo off walls and buildings along the water.

Amongst the bustle of people and the movement of goods you glimpse piece of history: venerable buildings still stained by smoke, old stone walls patched a dozen times over, and polished brass plaques declaring age and pedigree.

Yet amongst the old structures and built atop centuries of memory are new buildings, signs of progress, and change.

Coinwealth Heights.name: Coinwealth Heights
Coinwealth Heights.text:
• District Type: Residential with some Commercial.

  • Population: 2,332 (Low. Expansive manors take up most of the space, foot traffic is light.)

  • Lifestyle: Exclusive. (The district hosts numerous wealthy families and their retinues in expansive homes..)

  • Services: High-end retail, dining, clubs, and private warehouses.

  • Influences: As a stronghold for House Bastilla, members and associates of the house are common here.

Coinwealth Heights occupies a secluded corner of the south-western slopes of the Ordain Spires, a buffer of elevation separating it from the city’s bustle. It enjoys access to private docks in the south, has its own lighthouse, and extends its influence into the surrounding districts with impunity. It is also the historic stronghold of House Bastilla, whose influence is often felt but rarely seen by the locals here.

Culture

Coinwealth Heights is ruled by money and legacy. Most residents are old merchant blood or those whose fortunes have purchased entrance and place. Everything that happens in Coinwealth Heights is done behind layers of luxurious privacy.

House Bastilla governs the district with a firm yet invisible hand, as this districts is the seat of its power and home to its leaders. An expensive and loyal security force of private guards preserve the district’s impeccable calm, turning back the uninvited and tending to everything from garden parties to the subtle affairs of house politics.

Landmarks

The South Gate

One of the many ways into the city, this heavy gate is guarded day and night by house Bastilla’s elite retainers. Unlike other entrances to Ordain, here access is tightly restricted, with admission requiring invitation or favor with house Bastilla. The gate is an evergreen point of friction as city officials contest Bastilla’s claim to sole control of these lucrative southbound arrivals, but cannot break their hold over it.

Gilded Stems

Hidden behind opaque glass and black marble façades, the Gilded Stems is an exclusive wine bar and tasting house serving vintages from private cellars around the plateau and even beyond. Patrons are hand-selected and may be admitted only by the direct sponsorship of another patron. Inside, crystal sconces shimmer above deep velvet seating, and private alcoves allow for discreet discussions of business or pleasure.

The Risers
