A massive, two-tiered warehouse complex that hangs off the bluff’s edge with huge pillars rising up to hold it aloft. This warehouse unites the manors above with the private harbor below. Here, a collection of elevators move cargo up and down the bluffs.

Scintella Lighthouse

Set atop the lower bluffs near the private stone docks, this elegant lighthouse of marbled white bricks serves as the city's beacon. Its glass lantern burns ever-bright with magical flames, guiding ships of all kinds toward the mouth of the Destine.

Locals

Matienne Bastilla (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

A stoic figurehead of House Bastilla and the Heights itself, Matienne is not what most expect of the normally bombastic Bastilla members. She rarely appears in public, preferring to run district affairs from her estate or the private lounges of the Gilded Stem. She is known for cultivating cordial ties with those useful to her house and enforcing district order with an iron hand slipped into a velvet glove.

Dalbin Grell (Lawful Evil, Ordani Human, he/him)

Head of Bastilla’s private security force at the South Gate, Dalbin is a precise, hawk-eyed man renowned for his utter professionalism and stubborn resistance to interference from outside authorities. He maintains detailed records on every entrant and adheres strictly to House Bastilla’s command, though he and his men can be bribed if one is willing to part with enough coin.

Forella Meycor (Neutral Good, Cascillian Human, she/her)

The master steward of the The Risers, Forella oversees every shipment and staff rotation. Though not a member of House Bastilla, she is well paid to ensure that house reputations and client privacy are preserved. She is generally pleasant to staff, but ruthless toward incompetence, and unfailingly discreet in all transactions.

Brennet Vossin (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

Owner and sommelier of the Gilded Stem, Brennet is as theatrical as he is discerning. With an encyclopedic memory for faces and wine labels alike, he delights in reciting the histories of rare bottles if only to justify the exorbitant prices they command. Though he'd never admit it, he detests House Bastilla and its countless sea captains that think wealth can buy culture and standing.

Galen Scrit (Chaotic Neutral, Arcturian Signborn, he/him)

A witty tailor recently granted a permanent atelier in Coinwealth Heights, Galen’s developed a scandalous reputation for incendiary gossip and relationships alike. Despite this, he is beloved for his clever conversation and revolutionary designs.

Lore

Coinwealth Heights began as a humble extension of early Ordain back when it was known as Exile's Landing. Over the years it was built up, serving as a point for hunters to travel out into the grasslands, or a location where lumber could be brought down to the city.

Eventually house Bastilla selected it as the future enclave of its influential trading captains seeking respite from the city’s bustle. As the house's fortunes swelled, so too did their estates here, and the district’s character forever shifted toward exclusivity, wealth, and secrecty.

House Bastilla’s command over the district was historically tenuous, but was cemented a century ago when they brokered and enforced agreements to create an extensive estate management network. This network now sets standards and expectations of residents, provides private security, and controls who can be hired to work in the district. Since then, entry has remained tightly controlled, and all services within the Heights are either sanctioned or run by associates of Bastilla.
Coinwealth Heights.soverview: Coinwealth Heights is the pinnacle of luxury in Ordain, an exclusive residential district that is home to the opulent merchant families and overseers of the city’s economic fortunes. Here, grand estates and private villas form exclusive enclaves closed off to all but the city's most wealthy and elite.
Coinwealth Heights.sexposition: Gleaming carriageways wind through gentle rises, flanked by ornate ironwork gates and walls shrouded in carefully tended hedges. Marble fountains murmur in grand courtyards, and the scent of trimmed cedar and expensive perfumes hangs on the air. This is a district of money, built for those with it, and inaccessible only to those that can pay the high price of entry.

Trident's Point.name: Trident's Point
Trident's Point.text:
• District Type: Residential

  • Population: 2,475 (Small population of mainly Cascilian families, traders, and various officials)

  • Lifestyle: Maritime (Sailors, marines, and diplomats that travel to and from the Casilian Republic)

  • Services: City Defense, cargo transfer, training

Trident's Points is a recently expanded section of Ordain, a result of the good relations with the distant Cascilian Republic, with the majority of its inhabitants hailing from there. The district is one of the city's newest developments, and construction is still ongoing on certain streets as settlers from the republic arrive each year. Most of the buildings are based on a unique mix of traditional Ordani architecture and Cascilian aesthetics, with the city's usual deep reds replaced by Cascilian ocean blues and cyans.

At first glance, Tridents Point is oddly situated away from the water's edge directly. Instead, it is built upon the same large plateau that houses All-Fable Keep on the southern edge of the city. The Cascillians, however, often build their own cities this way, keeping their citizens safe from coastal predators in their homeland while constructing large lifts, cranes, and platforms to lower goods and people down to their awaiting navy.

Culture

Tridents Point community is small and tight-knit, with sailors, dock workers, and crane operators often sharing midday meals and swapping gossip near the waterfront cliffside. Cascillian officials are a common sight moving to and from the large Cascilian embassy, and many adventuring types stay at the large Achorside Alehouse while training at the Azor Academy.

While the district is still young, the Cascilians wasted no time since their arrival in constructing a large lighthouse that now towers over the entrance to the city bay. This lighthouse was approved by the Ordinate 30 years ago, and at the time the members believed the lighthouse would be largely symbolic, but the Casicallisn take their duty to protect the city extremely seriously. A number of well-trained Casicallisn Marines are housed in the lighthouse's lower levels, and they often stage mock scenarios in case the city is attacked by outside forces.

Landmarks

Azor Academy

Established by the renowned and now retired Azor "Stormbringer" Dane (Chaotic Good, Human Cascillian, he/him), the academy offers a variety of classes and courses for aspiring weapon fighters. Dane is known to train anyone in the art of "Si-sho," an elegant fighting technique used by the Cascilian Marines on the high seas. It requires a great deal of discipline with a long-bladed weapon, often a spear or, more commonly, a trident. The academy is large, but individual classes are available for those who want to sharpen their skills with other weapons or fighting styles, along with more extensive courses that provide a broader knowledge of sea-fighting techniques.

Casilian Embassy

Dominating the cliff edge next to the commanding Farsight Lighthouse, the Cascilian embassy consists of a central building with two long wings, each several stories tall, all containing offices and various bureaucratic stations where many officials write reports, send missives, and trade details back to the republic. The embassy features a large central pond, which is actually a map of the local region, showing the position of all trading vessels of the Republic which is kept off limits from the general public.

Achorside Alehouse

An extensive hostel and eatery for those traveling through the district or for those currently enrolled in the nearby Azor Academy, with several open patios filled with tables and chairs, the alehouse is the best spot to find a delicious Casclilian meal, which is often the famous spiced fish dish known as Asa. It's also a great place to chat with locals or fellow adventurers from the Anachraenum who pass through the alehouse or stay within its walls instead of All-Fable Keep itself. The alehouse is currently owned and operated by a married Casclilian couple, Lydia and Mira Lantell.

Farsight Lighthouse

The massive Casilian-built lighthouse took roughly 5 years to construct using local stonemasons from House Cehver, but it was almost entirely funded by the Casilian republic after it was approved by the Ordanite in [[/date AS2493]]. It now stands over the bay and helps ships find their way through the waters late at night by constantly shining a large beam of focused light through a series of complex mirrors at the lighthouse apex. Around fifty Casilian Marines live in the lower floors, with rumors that the Casilian special forces also have an office in the lighthouse and operate clandestinely in Ordain.

Locals

Narisa Ress (Lawful Good, Cascilian Ashka, she/her)

The Cascilian Ambassador is a retired member of the Casilian Navy. Her previous rank is unknown, but she holds a prominent position in the district, with many regarding her as the community's overall leader. She is an avid historian and personally fond of the Anachraenum, maintaining close ties with the organization to foster a healthy partnership on local issues. They are a patient teacher and captivating storyteller who delights in regaling people with her own personal adventures and past while sailing across the world.

Vice-Admiral Laskin Vix (Lawful Neutral, Cascilian Human/Wirrun, they/them)

Most are unaware of the Vice-Admiral's presence in Ordain, as they tend to keep to themselves within the Farsight Lighthouse. However, the rugged veteran is a capable commander who was posted to Ordain nearly a decade ago. Laskin takes the protection of the city very seriously but harbors a personal hatred for House Bastilla, and Katerin Bastilla especially, as they consider the trading house to be full of worthless pirates and murderers. They keep these feelings close to their chest, however, and while they are gruff and do not talk much with strangers, they have an impressively strategic mind and are deeply involved in Ordain's inner workings and politics.

Lydia & Mira Lantell (Chaotic Good, Cascilian Humans, she/her)

Former crane operators from the capital city of the Casicilian Republic, Alavai, Lydia, and Mira moved to the city twenty years ago and opened an alehouse with a desire to produce traditional Cascilian dishes for the local Ordani population. Since then, their small operation expanded after achieving a huge demand for lodging and food from academy trainees and Anchraenum members, and the construction of the much larger alehouse was finished only 8 years ago. They run the alehouse as a team and are ardently supportive of the mainly martial crowd they cater to, with much of the furnishings designed and built to allow for the "hot tempers" that flare up in such company.

Azor "Stormbringer" Dane (Chaotic Good, Cascilian Human/Nir'ae, he/him)

Azor Dane was born into a humble fishing family in the coastal town of Cascadia, in what was then the Cascilian Kingdoms. He lived a peaceful life until a chance encounter with the Shard God Katu while fishing in his late teens. Although he never became a follower of Katu in the traditional sense, many believe that Katu saw something in the young teen and blessed him in some way. When an undead raiding party attacked his village, Dane charged into the fight with his fishing spear, moving with such speed and grace that many in his community claimed he was a whirling blur of iron and wind. He soon left his village, vowing to protect all people from the threat of undeath. Throughout his adventures, he became a near-legendary figure, fighting in some of the most important battles of the last century, including the Battle of the Throat. However, his age has begun to slow him in combat, and he has semi-retired now, having built the Azor Academy in Ordain 10 years ago to help train new adventurers and fighters.

Lore

Tridents Point is among the newest districts in Ordain and was officially approved by the Ordinate to better align and ally with the Cascilian Republic. It features some of the latest construction in the city and is partly vibrant and fresh, with construction still ongoing in some areas. Now, with the district's large lifts, some goods can bypass longer routes and go directly to the warehouses to the east. It is also the most direct route for many Anachraenums members to enter and leave the city.
Trident's Point.soverview: This new district of Ordain is mainly composed of settlers and citizens from the distant Cascilian Republic who have started arriving and building in the city within the last 50 years. While they are eager to integrate into the city, they take pride in their roots, and many consider themselves representatives of their Republic, promoting its values of independent thought and freedom to anyone willing to listen. The district has also become a kind of beacon for those interested in learning more about martial pursuits, and the Cascilians have established a large academy for training in the art of "Si-sho," an elegant fighting technique that the Cascilian Marines use on the high seas.
Trident's Point.sexposition: The whitewashed buildings around you are adorned with beautiful blue and cyan nautical wave patterns, their curves and white-tipped edges resembling the ocean itself. The dome-shaped roofs rise above you, and several towers topped with wooden platforms display large blue flags with a large anchor symbol proudly sewn into the fabric. As you stroll through the lively streets, you notice that many of the residents do not appear to be Ordani, instead wearing stiffer, hard-looking leathers and blue-patterned shirts and short trousers.

Lastgate.name: Lastgate
Lastgate.text:
• District Type: Commercial with Residential

  • Population: 20,619 (High. Estates, homes, and shops with heavy foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Modest-to-Comfortable (Merchants, information brokers, retired professionals).

  • Services: Lodging, stables, secondhand goods, consignment, food & drink, leisure.

Lastgate has affectionately earned its name as the place where many of Ordain's retired and pensioned move to settle down. The district isn't merely a retirement community, however, as much as it overtly caters to a simple, slower lifestyle (which can often be lacking in many of the city's other residential neighborhoods). This is a district of thrift stores, consignment shops, and estate sales; and several of the citizens here live on fixed incomes. Of course, Lastgate also has a thriving community of younger Ordani who like the pace of the wayward district. And more recently, Lastgate provides a convenient point of ingress to the city for soldiers of the Burnished Hand stationed on Bura Island nearby.

As one of Ordain's primary points of entry, Lastgate is sometimes (if very rarely) burdened with the need for increased community awareness, if only to defend the local caravans outside the gate from opportunistic thieves or errant natural predators. Since Ordain has stood for centuries without assault from the outside world, its citizens see little need for an overt security presence other than a few city-owned Chessmen constructs; nevertheless, agents of the Burnished Hand and the Veiled Chain are known to occupy the area, along with the scattered array of retired and furloughed adventurers who reside here.

Culture

Lastgate's population is a remarkably diverse one, thanks to its proliferation as a commercial thoroughfare and its aged citizenship of assorted retirees. People of all walks of life from all corners of the Arctus Plateau are known to settle in Lastgate, where one's identity as an urbanite is often secondary to one's desire to get along. The shops and assorted business that occupy the district cater to a wide variety of needs and interests, both niche and commonplace; indeed, a robust assortment of Ordani and Arcturian cultural cornerstones can be found throughout the neighborhood's crowded nooks and crannies.

Landmarks

The Southern Gatehouse

This gatehouse structure houses multiple smaller facilities with a variety of purposes. A southern Watchbox serves as a shared ready room for members of the Burnished Hand, the Veiled Chain, and the Ordinate who need a temporary base of operations in the area. Meanwhile, the Information Office to the north is occupied by an Information Officer (appointed by the Hall of Records in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.1RJRU9XGC5WBm2Kq]{Assembly Hills}), and serves as a 24-hour kiosk for people in need of information about the city.

The very pillars of the structure itself are used as massive notice boards, and are decorated with layers upon layers of parchment posts and hand-scrawled messages of response. The gate here is manned on the ground at all times by one or more @UUID[Actor.0xDU0k3l8V4movO8]{Chessman} constructs — owned by the Ordinate and paid for with taxpayer coin.

Agatha's Curiosities & Consignments

Owned and operated by the matronly collector Agatha Zimm (NG, Ordani Human, she/her), this thrift shop features a staggering variety of storied curios and secondhand oddities on its dusty and cluttered shelves. Whether or not the tales are true, Agatha has a story for every item in the shop, which she gleefully orates to pressure would-be customers. Indeed, locals find it hard to leave Agatha's curiosity shop each time they visit without a little something to show for it.

The Rusty Rivet

This busy repair shop is the pride and joy of Gordi Grynfeather (LN, Ordani Nir'ae, he/him), a part-time music teacher who dabbles in artifice. When Gordi can't work the shop himself, he leaves its management to his irreverant son Brodi (CG, Ordani Nir'ae, he/him) and his sardonic daughter Kat (CG Ordani Nir'ae, she/her), who swap shifts as often as they trade playful insults. A variety of other younger family members are known to help out with smaller tasks around the shop, which is known for handling a wide array of repairs — from musical instruments and miscellaneous equipment to arms and armor. With a welcoming parlor and a convivial all-ages staff, The Rusty Rivet has a warm reputation for being a place where strangers often become fast friends.

The Rask & The Rider

A quaint bed and breakfast located near the Southern Gatehouse, The Rask & The Rider is owned and operated by the intrepid young innkeeper Etheria Matsaros (NG, Ordani Human, she/her) and her brash husband Solias (CG, Ordani Human, he/him). This three-story townhouse features a half-dozen modest-to-comfortable rooms for rent and a luxurious honeymoon suite, which is reserved for special occasions and larger parties when it isn't being rented out to young lovers (which, given the nature of Lastgate's relatively aged community, is more often than not).

Locals

Agatha Zimm (NG, Ordani Human, she/her)

This elderly collector of curios and antiquities is the proprietor of the aptly-named Agatha's Curiosities & Consignments, a secondhand shop the retired sorceress treats like an extended collection. Her matronly demeanor and penchant for gossip have earned her a reputation among locals as a quidnunc of the highest order; but her curiousness is rarely meddlesome, and her authenticity tends to inspire purchases from those who least expect it.

Gordi Grynfeather (LN, Ordani Nir'ae, he/him)

This part-time music teacher and repair specialist is the owner of The Rusted Rivet, and is considered to be Lastgate's consummate family man. Known for his wide range of skillful abilities, proclivity for artifice, and playful sense of humor, the convivial Mr. Grynfeather has a knack for remembering the name of every customer that enters his shop.

"The Judge" (CN, Arcturian Kivahr, he/him)

Not much is known about this wizened retiree other than his role as a former investigator of the Veiled Chain and his madcap manner of speech. A relative curiosity himself, with a muddled past and a dearth of intimates or relatives, The Judge is an affordable information broker — albeit one known to dispense questionable advice to the desperate and the gullible. The wily octogenarian lives in a rickety townhouse across the street from Agatha Zimm's shop, which he keeps a good eye on for safe measure.

Lore

Unbeknownst to all, one of the unassuming curios in Agatha Zimm's shop is secretly a powerful Primordis artifact capable of cosmological scrying. Furthermore, a mysterious connection ties this Fey relic to The Judge and his lunatic temperaments — although the specific nature of the connection eludes even the wily Judge himself. Is the former investigator cursed by the strange otherworldly object, is his mind under the control of an unseen Fey entity, or is the supernatural connection a sign of something altogether worse? Perhaps time and fate may tell.
Lastgate.soverview: Bereft of the spectacles of Westgate or the austerity of Highgate to the north, this unassuming commercial district on the southeastern edge of Ordain is known for its prospering retirement community and emphasis on the robust trading of secondhand goods. The inner reaches of Lastgate host a variety of businesses that cater to Ordani commercial interests, while a small collection of independent vendors and market stalls flank the outer walls.
Lastgate.sexposition:
At the eastern edge of this busy district, an impressive stone archway stands proudly above a main thoroughfare, flanked by two braziers that gleam with a ceaseless azure light. An automaton stands at calm attention beside the gate, humanoid in stature, clutching a flag pole topped with the city's sigil. An elegant sword is hilted casually upon its bronze hip.

Stables and market stalls flank each side of the road leading up to this grand and welcoming threshold. Diverse crowds of come and go, caught up in the lively hustle and bustle of urban commerce. The neighborhood streets are marked by the presence of countless apartment buildings, townhouses, and shops — the latter of which seem to cater to the sale of secondhand goods, with several thrift and consignment stores among them.

Lower Ashvale.name: Lower Ashvale
Lower Ashvale.text:
• District Type: Residential with Institutional and Commercial.

  • Population: 26,259 (High. Homes, apartments, and barracks with heavy foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Modest-to-Wealthy (Career Cindarics, Burnished Hand, other professionals).

  • Services: Healing, lodging, housing, food & drink, commercial trade, leisure.

  • Influences: Heavy Cindaric and Burnished Hand presence.

Lower Ashvale sits at the foundation of Cindarin Temple, and its people do their best to live up to the principles the benevolent sages preach. Home to the largest Healing House in all of Ordain, Lower Ashvale also contains several smaller homes and organizations that do their best to help those in need — whether they are providing free housing, low-cost subsidized goods, or access to jobs. Citizens who need any or all of these three elements tend to settle in Lower Ashvale, often taking advantage of these services before providing them or subsidizing them in return.

One of Lower Ashvale's main attractions is Highroad Sanatorium, a venerated Cindaric healing house whose exceptionally learned Sages cater to a wide variety of ailments. This is a welcome boon for the district's elderly citizens, which are ample (and lively, despite their age). Lower Ashvale also hosts a fortified edifice known as Veneration Hall, the defensible headquarters of the Burnished Hand.

Landmarks

Veneration Hall

This squat fortified structure serves as the headquarters of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} in Ordain. Ample barracks here provide duly-designated housing for the Burnished Hand's local forces, and vaults within contain a modest arsenal stocked with powerful arms and armor (both mundane and enchanted alike). While the true seat of the military organization's power is the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.b3WE7KCtxoJdPDzR]{Burnished Hand Fortress} of Bura Island, Veneration Hall plays a pivotal role in the ongoing security of Ordain, and is known city-wide as a bastion of law, order, and peacefulness.

Ashvale Sanatorium

This large tower structure is one of the most esteemed of healing houses maintained by the Cindaric Sages in Ordain. The upstanding reputation of the Sanatorium is not only the result of its extremely accommodating facilities (which are modern, spacious, and well-equipped), but of the timeless expertise of the Sages who work here — veritable masters of their respective healing trades.

Valenhome

A bustling inn and tavern owned by Midnight Max (CG, Ordani Kiska, he/him), a retired wayfinder of the Anachraenum. Known for its lively front room and its unflinching comfort in times of trouble, Valenhome offers some of the most affordable and welcoming rooms in town.

Locals

@UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver} (LN, Ordani Human, he/him)

Steros Kraver is the stalwart commander of the Burnished Hand, the order sworn to protect the Cindaric Sages. Steros is a skilled warrior and a charismatic leader, and is quickly becoming regarded by many to be one of the most competent young military leaders in Ordain's history.

Hathnan Tholos (LG, Ordani Kivahr, he/him)

An @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik]{Aster} druid with a metaphysical connection to Ember's water moon, this considerate healer serves the people of east Ordain as the Head Sage of Highroad Sanatorium. Hathnan's prolific abilities as an unflappable sage are humorously matched by his remarkably handsome countenance and striking physique, qualities that have endeared him with many starstruck patients throughout the years.

Gabi Greenbriar (CN, Arcturian Human, she/her)

This 15-year-old streetwise urchin has made a name for herself busking throughout Lower Ashvale, playing her Arcturian and Ordani folk tunes for coin. A skilled player of the vielle, Gabi is known for her stirring renditions of rural dirges, and for emerging talent as a songwriter in her own right. Fortunately, the charity of Lower Ashvale affords her a modest lifestyle as a transient; but her ambitions are far brighter than her checkered past, and the young bard aims to raise enough money to open a venue of her own one day soon.

Lore

A unique arcane construct of huge proportions and indomitable power lurks in the dungeons beneath Veneration Hall, crafted from wood and crystal and stone by the skilled Cindaric Sages of Highroad Sanatorium and the celebrated blacksmith Delos Travertine (LN, Arcturian Hulg'run, he/him). Not many know of the existence of this enormous sentinel, which the Burnished Hand has promised to only call forth in the most desperate of hours. Some remain skeptical about the massive construct and its clandestine nature, fearful of the potential threats it could pose to the city and its people if control of the automaton fell into the wrong hands (or, worse yet, if the Burnished Hand itself fell under the influence of less-scrupulous leadership).
Lower Ashvale.soverview: Lower Ashvale is a residential neighborhood in central Ordain that largely caters to institutions led by the Cindaric Sages and their allies in the Burnished Hand. Naturally, a variety of commercial and residential businesses also comprise the neighborhood's local industry, but many of these tend to specialize in interests related to healing, charity, and social reform. While many of the Cindaric Sages live in and around the temple itself, most of those who don't often live nearby in Lower Ashvale alongside others who believe in the charity of the their work. The result is a district known for its strivers and healers, as well as one of the largest aid networks in all of Ordain.
Lower Ashvale.sexposition: The spires of Cindarin Temple cast their shadows upon this quaint residential neighborhood, where several institutions of the city's benevolent orders can be seen stablished among the sprawl. Here, you spy an impressive healing house of the Cindaric sages; there, a fortified barracks bearing the emblem of the Burnished Hand. And all about them, apartments, inns, and townhouses are filled with the day-to-day lives of some of the city's most selfless citizens. People you pass on the street here seem remarkably kind, and there is an unmistakable mood of safety, security, and calm. By day, the laughter of children fills the wide streets. And by night, a chorus of Ordani folk songs dance through the evening air.

Highgate.name: Highgate
Highgate.text:
• District Type: Residential with some Commercial

  • Population: 2,570 (Moderate-to-Low, traffic is low after dark when work crews leave.)

  • Lifestyle: Holdouts (Residents who refuse to give up on their district and plan to rebuild one day.)

  • Services: Lodging, crafts, trade, food and drink.

Highgate once stood as a proud northern portal to the Redrak Fields, but the earthquake that struck some ten years ago fractured more than stone: it destroyed homes, ruined businesses and scattered much of the population elsewhere.

Culture

Those who remain in Highgate are its most stubborn or dedicated, those who refuse to abandon their homes or businesses, or simply can't. A small community persists through the hardship even though they often feel like the city gave up on them years ago.

Landmarks

Highgate Plaza

Once the district’s bustling heart, the plaza is now an uneven stretch of cracked stone and collapsed arches that once helped shade market stalls. What few vendors return here sell only to locals, as there is almost no road traffic to speak of.

The Dryblade

A battered old pub standing defiantly on the road to the old gate. Despite heavily spackled walls and a sagging roof, it remains open nightly. Its sign, a wooden sword, hangs over a slightly bent door. Inside the ale is cheap and the food simple, but there is always a chair for a vistor.

The Roadhouses

A line of inns that once welcomed travelers from Redrak, each one little more than private homes converted to welcome visitors and their coin. Now, most are shuttered and empty, their signs missing or faded to the point of being unreadable. Squatters, ruffians, and refugees have taken up residence in a few of them, making this area especially tricky to navigate.

The Tayan Worksite

Encircled by high wooden palisades and locked except when work is being carried out, the construction yard bears no signage or public plans. Wagons bearing stone and wood enter frequently, and laborers under contract seldom speak of their work or stay in the district after sundown.

Locals

Harn Veltrin (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

An aging mason overseeing the last of the public restoration projects in the plaza. Harn has spent his entire life in Highgate and refuses to leave until the work is finished, though funds have largely dried up.

Mirro Dane (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

Owner of the Dryblade, Mirro keeps her pub open more out of pride than profit. Gruff, sharp-eyed, and fiercely loyal, she knows every soul that still walks these streets and looks out for all of them as best she can.

Tessan Kord (Neutral Good, Arcturian Human, he/him)

A former caravan guard who now roams the broken streets trying to keep peace. Tessan has taken it upon himself to organize the braver locals to keep ruffians and thieves at bay. Tessan was born and raised in Highgate, and hates the current state of things.

Aric Talve (Lawful Neutral, Tayan Human, they/them)

As foreman for the Tayan project, Aric is the first to arrive on-site and the last to leave. Always crisply dressed on arrival, they often leave dusty, showing signs of hard work. When interacting with locals, Aric always chooses a stern silence in lieu of socializing or answering questions.

Lore

Highgate was once home to thousands of residents and numerous very profitable businesses. As the main road in from Redrak and the lands around it, the district used to see constant traffic and trade. However, once the quake devastated it traffic dwindled rapidly. Once bandits and thieves began to haunt the ruined streets the remaining traffic diverted south to Lastgate, all but sealing Highgate's doom.

In the years since, officials have declared their intent to fully reclaim the district, though little progress has been made. However, the Tayan Empire has purchased several adjacent lots in the fractured district and have begun breaking ground on some new structure, but no public record is available, and workers refuse speak of what they build, if they even know.
Highgate.soverview: Once a thriving gate district connecting Ordain to the Redrak Fields, Highgate now lies mostly deserted, a place of ruin, theft, and half-restored potential. Rebuilding efforts are slow, and with trade diverted elsewhere, the district lingers in uneasy limbo.
Highgate.sexposition: Cracked cobbles wind through a district that once bustled with life but now stands half-silent, half collapsed, and nearly abandoned. The remnants of once-proud structures lean over empty streets that have been cleared of rubble, but only just. Shattered masonry and half-repaired walls bear the deep marks of a decade-old quake that the district never quite recovered from. Weed-choked lots mingle with scaffolds and stacks of new stone where slow rebuilding creeps forward.

Grand Meadows.name: Grand Meadows
Grand Meadows.text:
• District Type: Recreational with Commercial and Institutional

  • Population: 37 (Very Low. Groundskeepers, with moderate-to-heavy foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Modest-to-Comfortable (Paid groundskeepers and career Cindarics).

  • Services: Leisure, food & drink, souvenirs.

The mile-wide park complex known as Grand Meadows is defined by an assortment of exterior landmarks, including the expansive Nestor Field, the verdant Springside Arbor, and the tranquil Abbot's Pond, alongside beloved structures like Adonia's Gazebo, the Wayroot Greenhouse, and the Vonwyn Playscape. The stone paths that weave through and around these locations of interest are often lined with street vendors and ambling citizens, which instantly betrays the Grand Meadows as an inviting place of organic harmony.

Historically, the swath of land that comprises Grand Meadows was identified by Adonia herself as an area worthy of conservation, and one of her seminal edicts as the first Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages catered precisely to this effort. Ever since, the terrain northwest of Cindarin Temple has been protected and tended to by the sages themselves alongside a guild comprised of select residents from surrounding districts (both paid and volunteer alike); and a small collection of dormitories and apartments near the district's perimeter cater to these munificent folks.

Culture

The culture of Grand Meadows tends to be defined by its visitors rather than its local inhabitants, which are few and far between. As a shared common space, the Meadows represent all the diversity Ordain has to offer. And thanks to the district's intrinsic sense of harmony and natural balance, the people who populate and visit this historic neighborhood tend to be warm in spirit and welcoming in disposition.

Landmarks

Nestor Field

"Slow your wheels in Nestor Field," they say. This urban stretch of grassland represents the largest of the eponymous Grand Meadows, and is marked by its wide, sweeping hills and the presence of a trio of sacred trees — known collectively as the Sagetrees — located in equidistant isolation throughout the meadow. Nestor Field is large enough to accommodate gatherings like weddings and organized sporting events alongside the scores of Ordani locals who simply enjoy lounging and relaxing among the meadow's grassy expanse.

Adonia's Gazebo

This beautiful stone and glass gazebo sits near the shores of Abbot's Pond at the end of a short pier, and was built to honor the city's founder Adonia, the first Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages who also established the Grand Meadows and its conservancy. Adonia's Gazebo is used for various purposes, including religious and cultural ceremonies, local gatherings, and civic meetings; when it's not in use for some other official purpose, the Gazebo is often home to relaxed readers who appreciate the historical edifice for its tranquil shade.

The Vonwyn Playscape

Designed by the famed sorcerer-architect Adlas Vonwyn, this modern playground was created as a recreational space for the children and adolescents of Ordain, who proudly enjoy the Playscape's subtle implementation of low-tier enchantments — recognizable in such features as the location's faerie fountain, living topiary, and musical trampolines.

Locals

Karsen Stole (LG, Ordani Human, he/him)

This aged Cindaric Sage serves as the dutiful Senior Groundskeeper of Grand Meadows, and is responsible for the administration of local staffing and the conservancy of the Meadows themselves. Although some regard the even-tempered Sage Stole to be a rather prickly fellow, those who know him well understand this tough exterior to be a ruse.

Neverly Phandren (LN, Ordani Human, she/her)

Neverly is a boisterous Events Planner who works under the attentive guidance of Ordain's Greensmans Guild. When she isn't wandering the Meadows, she can often be found stationed near Adonia's Gazebo and the surrounding waterways, which she takes great inspiration from.

Brina Thoulios (NG, Arcturian Human, she/her)

This kind-hearted street vendor makes a good living in Grand Meadows selling fresh fruit and Arcturian flowercraft dolls as keepsakes and souvenirs. A native of Helkas, Brina is well-learned in nearly every plant species that can be found in the gardens and conservatories of the Meadows.

Lore

A variety of tall tales and rumors surround the three Sagetrees that grow within the confines of Nestor Field, ranging from harmless urban legends to barmy conspiracy theories. One of the more popular tales is the legend of The Sage's Suitor, the story of a Waerd druid of the Duskflare Jungles who fell in unrequited love with Adonia; as the story goes, the Suitor had nothing to offer Adonia for her hand in marriage, so he planted three seeds in her beloved Grand Meadows to represent the potential for love between them. Another well-known tale is the story of the Oaken Aster named Kassus Brak; they say when Kassus passed away, all that remained of him were three enchanted seeds — which eventually became the regal Sagetrees recognized today.
Grand Meadows.soverview: The collection of urban parks, gardens, and conservatories known as Grand Meadows was developed as a place of shared recreation for local citizens, and serves as a haven for regional fauna who also call the city home. It is a place of calm, tranquility, and natural splendor (albeit cultivated). The Cindaric Sages of nearby Corpin Sanctuary are known to tend the pastoral expanse of Grand Meadows, which is also maintained by a guild of paid locals and volunteers.
Grand Meadows.sexposition: A verdant expanse of well-tended gardens and grassy fields stretch out across several city blocks here, where a moderate slice of nature has been cultivated beneath the shadows of Temple Ward to the northwest and Cindarin Temple to the southeast. Several greenhouses and conservatory structures dot and frame the thriving landscape, and the copious fauna that grows here appears to be tended to by a few Ordani citizens, some of them clad in the crimson robes of the Cindaric Sages. The air here is sweet with the smells of fresh grass, flower beds, and the savory grills of street vendors.

The Concourse.name: The Concourse
The Concourse.text:
• District Type: Commercial, City Management

  • Services: Storage, Boathouses, Water Management

  • Population: 400

  • Lifestyle: Impoverished (dockworkers, migrants, ruffians, and drifters)

The Concourse district is characterized by its unique blend of water and urban decay. The marinas are dotted with a mix of well-kept yachts, trading vessels, and weather-beaten fishing boats, and many store their vessels here but have little interest in the rest of the district itself. The gentle lapping of the water against the docks creates a serene backdrop, starkly contrasting with the crumbling infrastructure surrounding it. Some of the warehouses remain functioning while many are now derelict, some simply shells of their former selves. Their broken windows and graffiti-covered walls tell stories of minor criminal activity. The district also houses a few scattered families and residential buildings, but these residents are isolated, with more leaving the area every year. As daylight fades, the district becomes eerily quiet, isolating the few souls who venture here. They often ignore the hidden dangers lurking in the shadows, but a sense of palpable tension lingers in the air.

Landmarks

The Waterworks

Beneath the district is a meandering labyrinth of canals and tunnels called "The Waterworks". Portions of the subterranean architecture here predate the founding of Ordain and are attributed to prior Seydiri culture. The remaining canals and tunnels were excavated relatively early in the development of the city to provide crucial infrastructure and transportation between the eastern spires and Ordain's central waterfront districts.

The Waterworks Office

The city's Waterworks Office stands barely upright among old jetties, a crumbling stone wharf, and a number of ancient-looking bronze joists interlocking together to form a kind of outer structure around wooden beams and boards. Its weathered facade tells a story of years spent battling the elements with very little active maintenance or repair. The building has patches of peeling paint, moss creeping along the edges, and its rotting boards give off a damp, unpleasant smell in the sun. Tall, narrow windows, clouded with dust and grime, offer a glimpse into the dimly lit interior but obscure the activities happening inside. A large sign hangs above the entrance, its lettering faded and barely legible: "City Waterworks Office."

The Concourse Hideout

The Concourse Hideout is the current headquarters of the Toothbreaker Gang, a group of disenfranchised locals, Ordani criminals, and thugs, led by @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn}. The hideout is positioned at the eastern end of The Waterworks that span the district. It is built into the side of a large plateau that rises above the Concourse at the border of the Grand Meadows district behind it. It was once a cistern used to direct water flow throughout the city and was also the original base of operations for the Skywarders, a party of adventurers from the Anachraenum led by @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa}. After the Skywarders disbanded and Fernis began trading abroad, however, the Toothbreakers took over, and the base has become increasingly grim, filled with criminal elements and desperation.

Locals

Esta Fromp (true neutral, Ordani Ashka, she/her)

Esta Fromp is a shrewd and calculating Ashka woman in her late 40s, with an air of confidence that masks a deeper ambition. As the manager of the waterworks office in the Concourse, she presents herself as a diligent and responsible leader, dedicated to maintaining the River Destine. However, beneath this facade lies a more complex moral compass. She is well aware of the Toothbreaker Gang's activities, but she sees them as assets rather than adversaries. Underneath the surface, she allows their activities to flourish, often hiding their criminal acts from Veiled Chain investigators.

Lore

Historically, the Concourse was once a bustling harbor on the edge of the Ordain city itself, where boats from throughout the city would dock and deliver goods. However, as the city expanded, more northern and more accessible areas became more desirable, and over time, the Concourse fell into neglect. Much of the city's population started to view the Concourse as little more than a transit point—a place to pass through rather than a community to inhabit. This perception led more and more people to leave the area for other parts of the city, resulting in an increase in abandoned buildings and overgrown docks, which eventually became breeding grounds for local crime.
The Concourse.soverview: The Concourse is one of the least populated districts in Ordain, despite being a central location in the city with most of the area taken up by open water, marinas, boathouses, and storage yards. This once bustling waterfront is now mostly comprised of derelict warehouses and a large singular local water management office used by the Hallows to maintain the River Destine. Most people pass through the area without giving it a second thought, and over the last several years, this lack of attention has allowed a local gang called the Toothbreakers to establish a base in the largely overlooked district.
The Concourse.sexposition: A strange sense of stillness hangs in the air, despite walking through the middle of such a massive city. The distant sound of water lapping against the marinas fills your ears, accompanied by the faint creaking of old boathouses swaying gently in the breeze. As you move further into the district, you notice the large expanses of open water shimmering under the sun, but it feels oddly deserted, almost forgotten, with few people among the buildings.

Cutter's Passage.name: Cutter's Passage
Cutter's Passage.text:
• District Type: Recreational with Commercial and Institutional

  • Population: 40,407 (Very High. Quarry workers, laborers, et al., with heavy foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Melting Pot (modest-to-comfortable lodging and amenities; sporadic small parks and civic walkways; shops and equipment stores).

  • Services: Housing, lodging, food & drink, clothes, equipment, misc.

Cutter's Passage is one of the most densely-populated districts in all of Ordain, largely due to the expert planning of its neatly-stacked and phenomenally spacious architecture. The eponymous stone cutters who settled this area took it upon themselves to help further develop the neighborhood as the city continued to grow around it, and the result is a bustling district where the pride of its people can be seen in every brick and on every street corner.

Thanks to the quality of the architecture in Cutter's Passage, several of its structures have taken on landmark status, including The Danwren Building and Mason's tavern. And with so many people occupying its streets, whether full-time residents or visitors, Cutter's Passage is ultimately home to some of the best eateries and taverns in town — not to mention the formidable options in general stores and specialty shops.

Culture

Cultural touchstones in Cutter's Passage are predictably varied, thanks to the district's extraordinarily dense population. People from all walks of life and all realms of Ember have settled in Cutter's Passage at one time or another, although most of the people in this busy neighborhood consider themselves to be Ordani through and through — no matter their origins. The people of Cutter's Passage tend to be a proud lot, full of the kinds of boundless hopes and dreams one might expect to find in a city as grand and metropolitan as Ordain (even if and when their lives are full of inevitable hardship).

Landmarks

The Danwren Building

Built by the celebrated engineer Horatio Danwren, this famed apartment complex is instantly recognizable by its distinct architecture, which borrows a few aesthetic choices from ancient Shent designs. Throughout the years, several noteworthy Ordani have taken residence in this renowned abode, which continues to rise in prominence thanks to the celebrity of its executive clientele, its ample units for rent, and its storied history as a place where inspiration rubs elbows with everyday people. Some well-known residents of The Danwren include the cynical private investigator Samwyse Strath (Chaotic Good, Human Ordani, he/him), the devious girl genius Brinica Thax (Lawful Evil, Signborn Ordani, she/her), and the retired bard Venna Ydorius (Neutral Good, Human Ordani, she/they) — whose lavish parties tend to invite a rather chaotic element to the Danwren's top floor from time to time.

Mason's

This lively tavern is one of the most popular watering holes in Ordain. In fact, its reputation is so upstanding, folks will come from miles around to taste Mason's coveted array of beers, spirits, and bar food. Specialties include the Redgrass Ale, their semi-sweet pan-fried yams, and Colwren's famous Six Bean Stew. The staff of Mason's — including its playful manager Lynus Colwren (Chaotic Good, Human Ordani, he/him) — enjoy a light atmosphere, including the jocular and near-constant admission that there is, in fact, no one named "Mason" here, and the name of the place is simply a time-honored pun.

Hewer's Square

Hewer's Square is the most traveled intersection among the many wide thoroughfares of Cutter's Passage, a place where eager street vendors, brash news kids, and questionable job postings can be found by the handful. Activity here swells during dawn and dusk, as people are rushing to and from work, and peaks at lunchtime — when countless food carts and corner salesmen gather to tirelessly hawk their wares. There is an organized chaos to this busy place, where the Ordani people come and go like the ceaseless pulse of the city itself.

Locals

Venna Ydorius (Chaotic Neutral, Human Ordani, she/her)

This aged and retired actress lives in The Danwren. She's gained a reputation for being something of a curmudgeon in her later years, but those who know Venna best understand she's actually a softy at heart. Thanks to the considerable pile of wealth that she saved up throughout her successful years, the incredible Ms. Ydorius has decided to become a benefactor for her more eccentric interests — including research into lost Aterican legends and the collecting of rare Arcturian, Cascilian, and Waerd jewelry and artifacts. Indeed, an intrepid party could likely find themselves benefitting from Venna's patronage from time to time.

Stessos "Stessy" Thrasher (Chaotic Good, Human Ordani, he/him)

With an unkempt mop of raven-colored hair and a messy attitude to match, this brash seventeen-year-old is a stonemason's apprentice by day and a fledgling street vigilante by night (or aims to be, at least). Stessy is convinced that an underbelly of crime and corruption lurks outside the watchful gaze of organizations like the Veiled Chain, and hopes to personally support their efforts with his own local brand of street justice. Unfortunately, no one takes him seriously. (Yet). One thing is certain: young Mr. Thrasher's heart is certainly in the right place, whether his efforts and focus have found their proper footing or not.

Cora Nylos (Neutral Good, Kivahr Ordani, she/her)

Cora Nylos is the headstrong senior bouncer at Mason's, where her smug and impudent personality is a regular hit with the jocular crowd. What most customers don't outright know is that she's also a part-time adventurer and fist-for-hire, if the job is just and the crew are the proper people for it. Covered in elegant tattoos of Arcturian monsters, Cora wears her dark hair in a braided knot, and keeps a sleek dagger in her boot for unexpected combat encounters.

Lore

The expert stonemasons who settled this area are rumored to have carved a network of secret tunnels that run beneath the district (separate from, but connected to, its subterranean waterways). Of course, the more accessible areas of these tunnels have become host to an assortment of entities of various means and origins — from transients and street urchins, to rogues and the occasional sewer crevit.
Cutter's Passage.soverview: This drafty residential district is named for the early stonecutters of Stonework Hollow who originally settled here. Today, Cutter's Passage provides its many locals with fundamental resources like commercial retail, food, and lodging. Indeed, the neighborhood has accommodated quite a large amount of Ordain's citizens throughout the years with affordable and comfortable housing, a trait which has resulted in a rather diverse collection of folks who hail from various corners of Aterica.
Cutter's Passage.sexposition: The wide streets of this crowded residential district seem to carve their way effortlessly through the city, as if ingress deeper into Ordain was part of the architect's grand design, along with the impressive density of its various edifices. The city blocks here are flanked by tiered stone and timber housing, piled up nice and neat like carefully quarried rock. A few small businesses dot the urban landscape, which thrums with the activity of commonplace Ordani. And whether returning or setting off, the people of this highly-interconnected neighborhood seem to come and go with a steady pace.

Throughway.name: Throughway
Throughway.text:
• District Type: Commercial and Residential

  • Population: 14,100 (High. Businesses, depots, and trade centers with extreme foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Working-class (Merchants, moneylenders, logistics professionals).

  • Services: Warehouse rental, imports and exports, housing, general trade.

Throughway is one of Ordain's most overlooked districts in terms of local color or historical significance, but it nevertheless endures as one of the most valued neighborhoods when it comes to the city's commercial and socio-political affairs. Whether it's Throughway's importance to Ordani trade systems or the reliability of its community-based information network, it's a neighborhood where things are constantly happening.

Because of the district's advantageous proximity to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.nS7kj8wZ5eFq6pcy]{Westgate} and the bounteous trade it constantly brings the city, Throughway has also become a haven for hucksters and profiteers eager to make their coin via the exploitation of Ordain's more impressionable denizens. Verily, every third street corner plays host to some guide or salesperson of questionable repute; and while most of the locals know to steer clear of these unsavory vendors and their dubious wares, the neighborhood has elevated the status of these hawkers to the domain of local legend — tall tales abound about weird and wild happenings that have resulted from a chance encounter with one of Throughway's storied street hustlers.

Culture

Throughway's local culture is a synthesis of Westgate's diverse trade sector and the inner city's historical eccentricities. The people here — comprised of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani} with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} roots (among others) — tend to focus on the art of commerce and relationships of convenience, due largely to the hustle and bustle brought about by the district's varied goods and services. People often joke that "Throughway" is also a euphemism for the attitude of the opportunistic people who tend to live here, who view each other as assets rather than contemporaries. But this presumption is ultimately a misconception like any other, confirmed by the district's lively atmosphere and gregarious people.

Landmarks

Depot Square

This large public commons hosts a dozen commercial warehouses of various shapes and sizes, primarily used by Ordani businesses and foreign traders for the ongoing import and export of valued goods. Each of Ordain's Trading Houses has ample office and warehouse space here, and a central information kiosk is manned by duly-appointed employees of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate}. Depot Square is also famed throughout the city for its weekend market, where a score of Ordani vendors congregate to trade their fresh and novel wares.

The Here & There House

This extended-stay inn owned by the convivial Dorna Thassilhaft (Neutral Good, Human Ordani, she/her) features an adjoining warehouse with rental units for the short term storage of bulk goods. While she tends to be otherwise law-abiding, Dorna is known for looking the other way if a friend or regular needs to move some goods of questionable origin through her warehouses every once in a while. Meanwhile, The Here & There has a sterling reputation for their savory meat pies, which are prized the city over.

The Hub

Resembling a warehouse in its own right, The Hub is a spacious tavern where "the ale is never watered down" and the floors are always covered in sawdust — ready to soak up the rough-and-tumble spills of the establishment's rowdy clientele. Owned and operated by the lovably irascible Logar Halfhelm (Chaotic Good, Kivahr Ordani, he/him), The Hub is the kind of anything-goes venue where you can either have a spirited homecoming with old acquaintances or break bread (and maybe a few bottles) with someone new.

Locals

Zeela Marh (Chaotic Neutral, Human Ordani, she/her)

This wily twenty-something cutpurse is a regular patron of The Hub, where she likes to hone her pickpocketing skills as well as her aptitude for meaningless small talk. Always up for fun and lucrative trouble, Zeela most often hires out her thieving abilities to those patrons who manage to entice her with an exciting challenge, a noteworthy reward, or both.

Gaphne Greyfeld (Neutral Good, Kiska Ordani, she/they)

This young hedge wizard is a sedate, yet sharp-minded mage who works as a trusted hireling for several businesses within Throughway and nearby. Where brute strength falls short, Gaphne's spells often rise to the occasion — making her an invaluable asset to clients who might need or want the industrial potential of magic on their side.

Jonathas Nab (Neutral Good, Human Arcturian, he/him)

Truly his own worst enemy, this ornery day laborer never left his rural proclivities behind, despite decades of living in Ordain. Nab's mood swings and penchant for self-destruction are nearly legendary, and he's known among Throughway and neighboring districts for screwing up almost every job he's ever had. As a result, he's worked at nearly every warehouse and shipyard in the city — and has the personal contacts and information network to match. Whether or not his associates have tired of his chaotic tendencies, however, always remains to be seen.

Lore

It's a little known secret, but a handful of businesses and homes in Throughway play host to a secret fight club, where the anonymous attendees engage in rigorous bouts of bare-knuckle brawling for nothing more than camaraderie and the thrill of it all. Indeed, an agent or two of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} and several soldiers of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} are even said to participate in these events, free of the burden of their official duties. But citizens who stumble upon rumors of this macabre pastime can rest assured: the fights in this nameless underground circuit are fair and never, ever fatal.
Throughway.soverview: Known for its countless mercantile facilities and colorful street vendors, this industrial district acts as a distribution hub for the innumerable goods that make their way into the city via neighboring Westgate. Throughway earned its name from the wares that constantly come and go, and from the ample folks who only settle here for a short time before finding more suitable lodging elsewhere in the city. It's a busy neighborhood full of countless warehouses, depots, surplus stores, tenement buildings, and corner merchants.
Throughway.sexposition: The wooden cranes and scaffolding of this industrial sprawl are piled high with crates of mercantile goods, likely hauled into the city from nearby Westgate. Merchants and laborers swarm about the neighborhood's various structures like ants, grabbing as much as they can before heading off to some other corner of the sprawling metropolis. And with so many goods coming and going here, it's no surprise to see such a wide variety of retail locations scattered throughout the district, their storefronts stacked high with fresh goods and half-packed parcels.

Foxlairs.name: Foxlairs
Foxlairs.text:
• District Type: Commercial and Residential

  • Population: 7,330 (Medium. Comfortable town homes with lawns and stables).

  • Lifestyle: Affluent (animal handlers, home owners, etc).

  • Services: Lodging, housing, domesticated animals, livestock, stables, gardens.

  • Influences: Expertise in animal handling via early Kithil settlers.

A great deal of the commercial real estate in Foxlairs is dedicated to the lawns, gardens, aviaries, and stables that comprise the district's beast trade. Aside from the ever-ubiquitous house cat, if there's a domesticated animal to be found on the surface of the Arctus Plateau, it can probably be located here — bred and raised by some of the best animal handlers in the business. Beasts ranging from horses, rask, and nothrin to hawks, serpents, and monkeys can be found here in ample supply (along with the district's titular foxes, which have been cultivated in the city of Ordain since its settling).

And while much of the residential sector of this neighborhood is defined by its "comfortable" cost of living, several town houses in the district belong to more aristocratic members of Ordani society (and this affluence is immediately recognizable in the architecture and size of the estate). An influx of Kithil immigrants during the neighborhood's formative days have also resulted in a sizable population of transplants from places like Luen and Hillhome, who are known for their deft skills when it comes to handling avians and various tree-climbing species found in Foxlairs.

Landmarks

Jessos Station

This assortment of stables, aviaries, and animal pens is one of the oldest establishments in Foxlairs, comprised of over a dozen enclosures for the breeding, growth, and training of an impressive variety of domesticated animals. Thanks to the venerated historical nature of the Station and its remarkably comprehensive facilities, prices here can range a little high compared to other areas of the Arctus Plateau (or even Ordain). But, as the spry Nathira Jessos (Neutral Good, Human Ordani, she/her) loves to say, "when you hand your gold over to Jessos Station, you're paying for the pedigree," a phrase that has assured customers quite adequately for over four generations.

Elefield Training & Sales Stables

Owned and operated by the stolid and dependable animal handler Cosmo Elefield (Lawful Good, Human Ordani, he/him), this assortment of a half-dozen stables is famed for the quality of the rask and horses that are bred and raised here. The animals of Elefield Stables aren't simply known for their tenacity, they tend to be the noblest of domesticated creatures — traits passed down by the ever-considerate Cosmo and his loyal staff of trainers and stablehands. And whether it's true or not, there are some Ordani that swear by the so-called fact that rask raised by Cosmo Elefield are the fastest on the Plateau.

Cloverleaf Bed & Breakfast Inn

This rustic bed & breakfast hostelry is known city-wide for the unparalleled deliciousness of their savory local cuisine, lovingly cooked by its chatty proprietor Bramba Cloverleaf (Neutral Good, Keth Ordani, she/her) and her socially-awkward husband Dorin (Neutral Good, Human Arcturian, he/him). The prices here are surprisingly moderate, given the excellent quality of the food and amenities; and no one has ever left a bad review. Patrons are invited to write anonymous well-wishes, intimate hopes, and fond remembrances on small slips of parchment before hanging them on a tree in the inn's foyer — a sort of ritualistic and asynchronous communication between the kind souls who stay here.

Locals

Anika Rouge (Lawful Good, Human Ordani, she/they)

This aged local actor and storyteller is known to wander the district with pockets full of seeds, nuts, dried fruits, and grains, which she lovingly distributes to the animals of Foxlairs (wild and domesticated alike) while she ambles through the district each midday and dusk. Anika has long been known as one of the finest thespians to grace an Ordani stage, capable of remarkable scene studies, moving orations, and soul-stirring musical performances. Anika's many decades of storytelling experience and countless fans provide an unparalleled network of knowledge, which she rarely uses aside from the dissemination of hot gossip.

Aezra "Racer" Sissos (Chaotic Good, Ashka Ordani, he/him)

This lithe rask-jockey is considered to be one of the Arctus Plateau's most skilled professional riders, capable of mounting and handling any saddled beast known to Ember. When he isn't busy earning coin or accolades in some prestigious competition, he lends his services to Jessos Station — whose patrons are most likely able to afford his handsome training fees.

Talion Graves (Neutral Evil, Human Tayan, he/him)

This retired cavalier works as a stablehand for Elefield Training & Sales Stables, where he's (so far) been able to fade into an obscurity he so desperately desires. While Talion maintains the guise of a genial laborer, he's secretly a murderer on the lam from Imperial authorities, and a deserter of the famed Kriagry Knights of the Dragon Empress. Talion keeps the cause for his treason close at all times — a gemstone artifact known as the Vermilion Tear of Caren’ac, which allows its owner to read the minds of others.

Lore

Foxlairs was initially developed by a consortium of independent investors led by the famed animal trainer Bastian Jessos, who came into the possession of a large inheritance following the untimely death of a family member. With newfound funds in-hand, the headstrong handler established the first stables that would eventually become Jessos Station, an institution that is largely responsible for the overall conservancy of domesticated animal life in Ordain.
Foxlairs.soverview: Foxlairs is a commercial and residential district known for its proliferation of stables and shops that cater to the sale of a variety of domesticated animals — rask, hawks, nothrin, and eponymous Ordani foxes among them. Much like Hunter's Wood to its west, this relatively affluent borough is a place of lush gardens and contained wilderness, where the noble beasts that are cultivated here can be raised and trained in habitats more becoming of their nature. In addition to its posh stables and well-kempt barn yards, Foxlairs also plays host to a variety of permanent lodging, from modest townhouses to elegant mansions.
Foxlairs.sexposition: The stoney expanse of Ordain begins to give way to verdant pockets of foliage in this slightly-rustic but well-kempt part of town. Townhouses of both modest and affluent means dot this welcoming landscape, which is also checkered with plots of overgrown gardens, barn yards, and small manicured parks. You can't help but notice an increase in the number of domesticated animals in this charming district, which seems to be one of the city's primary sources for beasts of burden and the like. Indeed, you spy several gray Ordani foxes running about the neighborhood unattended, as if the wilderness also pays rent in this endearing part of town.

Smokerie.name: Smokerie
Smokerie.text:
• District Type: Commercial and Residential

  • Population: 2,524 (Medium. Smithies, forges, and homes with moderate foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Poor-to-Comfortable (Smiths, metalworkers, apprentices, laborers).

  • Services: Smithing, manufacturing, material processing, skill training.

When it comes to laying low in Ordain, the Smokerie is a great place to begin (that is, if you can handle the incessant cacophony and the smell of scorched air). Despite the neighborhood’s less-savory qualities, it nevertheless plays home to several upstanding citizens and artisans of influence; many of Ordain’s best blacksmiths happen to be some of the city’s finest people, and here in The Smokerie they're known to take on apprentices in larger numbers. Locals colloquially refer to these mentorships as "Academies" (but this stewardship is rather informal compared to the pomp and circumstance of other Ordani institutions).

They say the Smokerie has a way of keeping you warm when the rest of the city grows cold. But, then again, they say a lot of things in Ordain.

Landmarks

Burnside Arms

The celebrated workshop, forge, and storehouse of the famed Kivahr artificer @UUID[Actor.gBXPA4AerLzwSbi6]{Janix Mance}. Known far and wide for the skillful work of its apprentices as well as its forgemaster, the Burnside Arms is also manned by a cadre of construct helpers — who are ready to assist Janix (or the entire neighborhood) at a moment's notice.

The Edge of the World

This 24-hour forge and armory operated by the blacksmith Eilo Vark (Chaotic Good, Hulg'run Arcturian, he/him) is known for the keen quality of its assorted blades and its skilled proprietor's appetite for rare foreign tales. If there is an exotic weapon to be found anywhere in Ordain's urban confines, certainly it will be found here.

The Parched Lark

This beer-soaked tavern of ill-repute is managed by a retired privateer named Tomnas Grey (Chaotic Neutral, Human Arcturian, she/her), and serves up some of the cheapest rooms and trashiest talk in town.

Home Away From Home Hostel

This resilient and ramshackle youth hostel is run by the irascible caretaker Celesta Poe (Chaotic Neutral, Human Ordani, she/her), whose enigmatic past is a subject of constant and entertaining debate. The Home Away From Home keeps its doors perpetually open for the wayward and the aimless, even if the soot-stained hostel isn't always the safest place in the city for them to foster good habits or healthy relationships.

The Pit Trap

Inconspicuously situated in some unremarkable alley on the Smokerie's west side, The Pit Trap is a seedy warehouse nightclub of questionable repute. The Pit Trap is known for its sultry environment, and caters to a wide range of clientele — from casual locals in search of an unexpected good time, to big spenders who enjoy the location's impeccable sense of discretion. Fortunately for the regulars, the location of this sordid establishment remains a well-kept secret throughout the city (as does the weekly password for entry).

Locals

@UUID[Actor.gBXPA4AerLzwSbi6]{Janix Mance} (Neutral Good, Human Kivahr, he/they)

This artful blacksmith operates a forge in the heart of the Smokerie called The Burnside Arms. Not only is Janix a proud and competent artificer and blacksmith, the Skybrush native is also a collector of antique arms and armor from all four corners of Ember (a passion he cultivated as a young Kivahr among the giant hinterlands back home in the Rustvar Valleys).

Eilo Vark (Lawful Good, Hulg'run Ordani, he/him)

This friendly fifty-something blacksmith operates the Edge of the World forge and armory, and possesses an extensive knowledge of arms and armor the world over. If there's a niche interest or curious detail about modern and historical weaponry to be known, Eilo will most certainly familiar with it.

Tomnas Grey (Chaotic Good, Human Ordani, she/her)

Known for her provocative worldly tattoos and her revolving door of would-be suitors, this retired privateer is the proprietor of the Parched Lark tavern. Although she exudes an air of strictness with new acquaintances, Tomnas Grey is a bawdy, adventurous woman at heart who never turns down a good time (unless it inconveniences her peace of mind).

Lore

The Smokerie is aptly named after the embers of its countless foundries and the slag and cinders of the nearby Dustforge. Some denizens of other, more affluent districts of Ordain are known to deride The Smokerie for its begrimed industrialism, and false rumors about regarding fiery accidents and citizens scarred by molten metal are not uncommon — but these tall and troublesome tales hold very little credence. Not all is fair in The Smokerie, however, as illicit deeds are fostered behind the closed doors of the Home Away From Home by its Kuarta-worshipping owners (who tend to train the unsuspecting youths in their eldritch ways).
Smokerie.soverview: The Smokerie is a grimy, ash-stained neighborhood defined by its assortment of smithies, its lower-income housing, and its proximity to the slag and cinders of the nearby Dustforge district. Yet, in spite of these relatively harsh conditions, The Smokerie is a place where opportunity abounds and friends can be made from the least likely of strangers. The rhythmic sound of countless hammers striking their anvils echoes through each crooked street and twisted alley of this dingy sector of Ordain, where people of modest means settle in to either start chasing their dreams or forget about them altogether.
Smokerie.sexposition: Nestled beneath fuming smoke stacks and ashen clouds of perpetual exhaust, this grimy district is marked by soot-stained windows and the ambient staccato clanging of countless steel anvils. Here and there, you notice local denizens going about their business amidst the area's incessant haze, which cloaks the cobbled streets and alleys in a sweaty aura of curious intent. It's easy to understand how this place came to be known as The Smokerie, a neighborhood where the forges and the people alike smolder with anticipation.

Dustforge.name: Dustforge
Dustforge.text:
• District Type: Industrial with some Commercial

  • Population: 1,029 (Low. Forge workers, metalsmiths, and customers, with low foot traffic).

  • Lifestyle: Comfortable-to-Wealthy (The Dustforge provides a steady influx of wealth).

  • Services: Processing and refinement of ore, minerals, and raw arcane materials.

Dustforge serves as Ordain's primary foundry and processing plant for the refinement of ores, minerals, stones, and a wide assortment of arcane materials. A few town homes and apartment buildings allow the workers of Dustforge and associated endeavors to live close by, but more than a few of these places are occupied with locals who simply like the moody inspiration or noisy escape the industrial district so readily provides. Indeed, a small community of avant-garde Ordani artists has taken shape here over the past year; some of these dreamers claim that the mechanical clamor of the neighborhood is part of their creative process (along with similar musings), and their general lust for life is a welcome addition to the neighborhood.

House Cevher's commercial interests in ore and arcane materials necessitates their heavy involvement with the district's business concerns, but the Dustforge is ultimately operated by an group of independent smithies under House Cevher's employ. The Ordinate provides minor oversight, particularly when it comes to the distribution and regulation of the materials that come and go through this massive foundry complex.

Landmarks

The Dustforge

The district's namesake is a massive forge and an adjoining refinery complex maintained by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}, where most of the stone, ore, and crystals that are mined from beneath Ordain are brought for processing and refinement. A tireless guild of laborers known as the Dustforgers work the refinery, comprised of a diverse group of talented blacksmiths and geologists from all walks of life, including several Vjrnhar, Kivahr, and humans among them. For an added element of security, the Dustforge is manned by a pair of @UUID[Actor.0xDU0k3l8V4movO8]{Chessmen} at all times.

Cevher Station

Nestled below the eaves of the Dustforge, this office complex serves as a base of business operations for agents and allies of House Cevher, whose vested interest in the Dustforge stems from their designated purview over ores, minerals, and arcane materials. Most of the facility is built to house various meeting rooms, workshops, and private offices. A small barracks on site affords over a dozen employees and guests of House Cevher enough accommodations for week-long stays when necessary, while other long-term housing is available from the company nearby.

Discount Minerals

This cluttered crystal emporium is supplied directly from Dustforge surplus, and offers traditional retail opportunities for regular individuals in addition to affordable bulk prices for licensed local businesses. Managed by the laconic appraiser Broonan Pebblesmith (NG, Ordani Hulg'run, he/him), Discount Minerals is a great place for consolidating coin into precious gemstones, for crystal artisans to find superior raw materials, and for arcane casters to procure distinct spell components.

Locals

Fineas Stonecrow (NG, Ordani Kivahr, he/him)

This slag-scarred blacksmith serves as Forgemaster General of the Dustforge, duly appointed by House Cevher and a coalition of senior Dustforger blacksmiths. Known for his assuring baritone voice and a fierce hometown pride in Ordani culture, Stonecrow is one of the city's most respected leaders, and is frequently called upon by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate} as an arbiter for local disputes. Naturally, the tall Forgemaster's expertise precedes him, and his ruggedly handsome silhouette is unmistakable.

Elora Pholthos (LN, Arcturian Human, she/her)

Prodigiously talented and advanced well beyond her years, this cheeky young artificer is the Lead Engineer responsible for analyzing the various raw materials that are delivered to the Dustforge for processing. Supported by a small team of other professionals (many of which are jealous of her talents), Elora is quickly becoming one of the Arctus Plateau's preeminent specialists on arcane elements and precious stones.

Moira Madrigale (CG, Ordani Zeph, she/her)

This would-be wayfinder is a cantankerous administrator for House Cevher, relegated to serving the esteemed Trading House as one of their key liaisons at Cevher Station. Anyone who wishes to tour the Dustforge refinery and surrounding facilities is beholden to Moira's permissions, which can often be purchased with a small bribe or a favor in kind. An amateur archaeologist, Moira is fond of wiling away her free time amidst the public museums of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0]{All-Fable Keep}, daydreaming of her own adventurous escapades.

Lore

The foundry of Dustforge is actually inhabited by a huge Magma Golem, a construct of molten ore that helps power the massive refinery — and that the Forgemaster can command when necessary. The Forgemaster's enchanted hammer is actually the control rod for the construct; and the dutiful Fineas Stonecrow is known to sleep with the hammer at his bedside (when it isn't beneath his pillow).
Dustforge.soverview: The district known as Dustforge is named after the massive edifice that dominates this industrial neighborhood at the northwestern edge of Ordain. An enchanted foundry and refinery for the processing of various ores, metals, minerals, and arcane materials, Dustforge plays a vital role in the ongoing expansion of Ordain and excavation of the quarries and caverns beneath the great city.
