Resultantly, several support structures have been erected around the Dustforge, including a few retail locations and ample offices for House Cevher business.
Dustforge.sexposition: Plumes of scintillating exhaust can be seen billowing out of the hollow smoke stacks and spires that rise from this dusty industrial district, which appears to be dominated by an enormous foundry made of stone and steel. This proud edifice stands over the neighborhood like a tireless sentinel, its forges never slowing, its lights never dimming. Workers, blacksmiths, and engineers can be seen coming and going, covered in grime and cinder burns and arcane dust. A few supporting structures indicate the presence of commerce here, and you can't help but notice the soft glittering sheen of the strange soot that has settled on this place.

Lumiere Wharf.name: Lumiere Wharf
Lumiere Wharf.text:
• District Type: Commercial with some Residential

  • Population: 1,000 (Low. Crowds gather for trade, spectacle, and business at all hours but few live here.)

  • Lifestyle: Eclectic (Rhivan residents, wandering visitors, and cityfolk flood the district daily)

  • Service: Lodging, Retail shops, trinkets and souvenirs, restaurants, teleportation services.

  • Influences: The presence of numerous Rhivan visitors, merchants, and transplanted citizens has created a small enclave of Rhivan culture not found anywhere else in the city.

Defined by the interplay of Ordani and Rhivan culture, the constant flow of traffic from within and city and beyond, and ever present glow of magic, Lumiere Wharf is Ordain’s symbolic and literal portal to the Rhivan realms.

Across Lumiere Wharf, Ordani stone construction is layered with elements of the Rhivans: numerous windows, crystalline lamps, and flourishes of blue and gold that contrast the white and red of Ordain. Most striking are the levitating sapphire crystals: some small as a lantern, others the size of a wagon, with the largest standing two stories high. Each crystal casts azure light across the avenues at all hours, lending the wharf the sensation of perpetual twilight in the darker hours of the day.

Culture

Locals in the district are a mixture of Ordani and Rhivan transplants, which has lead to the district becoming a self-contained pocket of Rhivan culture. These assorted locals and foreign visitors mingle in the gem-lit streets of the district every day, creating a lively and eclectic atmosphere unlike anywhere else in the city.

It is not uncommon to encounter impromptu musical performances, magical demonstrations, market stalls offering goods both mundane and arcane, and the exchange of half a dozen languages in any crowd.

The Rhivan staff of the Destine Sanctum work closely with the city’s Trading Houses and bureaucrats to smooth potential conflicts and keep incidents to a minimum. Permission for portal travel is strictly regulated, and even the boldest smugglers think twice about crossing the Sanctum’s ever-present watchers.

Landmarks

The Rhivan Gateway

An immense teleportation circle inlaid into the wharf’s central plaza, this fixture connects Ordain to the Arcanic Portal Network run by the Rhivan Star Mages. It was built and is maintained by a local contingent from the Starsworn Academy and is large enough to accommodate entire caravans of goods. When the gateway activates, the nearby crystals flare bright blue, pulsing in tune and time with the gateway's energy.

The Destine Sanctum

A multi-tiered structure blending pale Ordani stone with Rhivan love of high-peaked rooves and numerous windows, it is home to a multitude of offices as well as private residences. Serving as embassy, trade consulate, and home for the Rhivan Star Mage that oversees the portal, this structure is busy at almost all hours. Visitors are constant, with petitioners, bureaucrats, tourists and traders flowing through it like the tides. Its upper levels are closed via magical wards and serve as residence to the Rhivans that operate the location.

The Roundshore Market

A bustling row of market pavilions laid out along the river wall and overlooking the Destine. The Roundshore Market is home to merchants, performers, cooks and more gathered to peddle a mixture of local good and Rhivan imports. All manner of things can be found here, and its proximity to a bridge and local ferry docks means it sees heavy traffic at all hours.

Celestinian Hall

Once a historic Ordani estate belonging to a now forgotten great house, it was renovated extensively to become a mixture of tavern, inn, and temple. This mulit-story building serves as a popular stopping point for newly arrived and local Rhivans alike. The shrines to Spectra and The Weaver are well cared for by its owners, and the building is never empty of patrons.

Locals

@UUID[Actor.XrFDJNn1Fa7hopqR]{Eveis Brightstone} (Lawful Neutral, Rhivan Carrow, she/they)

Assigned to Ordain some time ago by the Starsworn Academy, the aquatic Carrow oversees the day to day operations of the Gate and Sanctum in the district. She is both a magical consultant for the Ordinate and local Rhivan mages, and the leader of the team responsible for keeping the gate calibrated and stable.

Tillan Harke (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

A clever interpreter and guide, Tillan offers his services to new arrivals, providing translation, cultural advice, guidance and arrangements for touring Ordain. He is always ready with a recommendation for his cousin’s restaurant across the river for those that want a bite.

Cassan Vey (Lawful Good, Rhivan Human, he/him)

Head of the Destine Sanctum's trade offices, Cassan oversees operations with a cool and detached demeanor. He spends his day mediating disputes, certifying foreign wares, and ensuring taxes are paid on time and in full. He is known and regarded well for his fairness and rigid adherence to trade law.

Nestos Narvo (Lawful Good, Rhivan Human, he/him)

Owner and operator of the Celestinian Hall, Nestos is both a highly dedicated and religious Rhivan, and a fastidiously dedicated businessman. He bought and founded the hall decades ago with his two sisters, and they still operate it to this day.

Vella Seriane (Chaotic Neutral, Rhivan Signborn, she/her)

A flamboyant Rhivan entertainer and illusionist, Vella retired to Ordain in her old age and bought a stake in the Celestinian Hall where she is a familiar sight. She spends her evenings dazzling crowds with stories, illusions, and elaborate light displays.

Lore

Long ago, this district was the site of a faltering riverside market and dockland. Once part of a coastal spur leading from Exile's landing meant to facilitate movement of goods from the eastern shore of the river, it quickly was bypassed by ongoing development.

Larger, newer market spaces closer to the residents drew away merchants, while modern wharfs and docks on nearby shores diverted ferries and barges with their superior capacity. While attempts were made on more than one occasion to revitalize the district, nothing ever stuck, and it was left as a mish-mash of houses, businesses, old waterlogged docks, and empty lots.

The district limped along for decades until a treaty granting Rhivan access to the land for development was signed. All at once the district became a flurry of activity, buildings were leveled, locals were bought out and displaced and the massive Arcanic Portal Network gateway was constructed. Before long, trade and new residents flowed into the city, followed by coin and resources. The district swiftly transformed in the following decades, becoming the beacon of trade and culture that it is now.

A little known fact about the district is that the numerous floating blue crystals were engineered as stabilizers for the Gateway’s surges, blending function with beauty in classic Rhivan fashion. Each one is tuned to reflect magical energy back toward the gateway, both protecting the city from potentially disruptive energy, and feeding the portal so that its function remains constant and predictable.
Lumiere Wharf.soverview: A thriving commercial marketplace, tourism hub, and nexus of travel, Lumiere Wharf is a figurative and literal portal to the rest of the world. It holds numerous services and merchants, and imported goods from all over the world arrive via a local magical gateway overseen by Rhivan Star Mages.
Lumiere Wharf.sexposition: Shimmering blue light dances along the waterfront, thrown from floating crystals that drift lazily above paved promenades and rest on sturdy stone piers. All along this district Ordani structures of white stone and red rooves are contrasted by the gray and blue of Rhivan architecture, each foreign edifice adorned with numerous windows that blaze with light at all hours. The air here tingles with energy, and swirls with dormant magic that flows through the district like a sea breeze.

Dragon Skin.name: Dragon Skin
Dragon Skin.text:
Left in a somewhat remote part of the Pathways, the skin of an ancient dragon molders in the dark corner of the mycelian expanse, though its presence is all but impossibly to miss if one travels through the massive tunnel where it rests.

Environment

The ground around it was torn up and dug out as the dragon struggled to pull itself free of its skin. However, the area is not remarkable otherwise.

Ecology

There is a stark absence of both plant and animal life around the skin, suggesting an unwelcoming aura, ensuring no living things dare grow or linger here.

Lore

This massive skin once belonged to the dragon Zeranyss, and was abruptly deserted after the massive being shed it. Over the years, the lair has become a site of interest for Mutagist scientists seeking unique resources for their research. Simultaneously, it has attracted at least one lunatic who pays homage to Zeranyss, worshiping the dragon with a shrine resting beneath the dead of the discarded skin.
Dragon Skin.soverview: The origin of this massive, mysterious draconic molt remains unknown, but such a find is significant regardless. The huge skin has drawn interest from all manner of parties below the surface of Ember, some taking academic interest, others religious.
Dragon Skin.sexposition: Your eyes are drawn toward a shape in the dark — a colossal draconic visage frozen in the final moments of life. As you peer at its massive, misshapen form in the gloom clarity reveals its truth: this is an immense, hollow shell, discarded and abandoned. It is lifeless yet horrible to behold, with great claw marks gouged into stone and shifted rubble framing it, as though the dragon fought ferociously to tear itself free of its old skin.

Repurposed Quarry.name: Repurposed Quarry
Repurposed Quarry.text:
Nestled in the pale stone of the north eastern corner of the mycelian expanse, this old quarry has become something more than a place to acquire slabs of rock.

Environment

The quarry's terrain is primarily composed of pale white stone cut deep into the subterranean expanse. The walls feature a fast-moving waterfall flowing into the center, flooding the lowest depths. Structures of decaying metal and weathered wood traverse the pit, connected with a series of moving platforms suspended from rails. The 40-foot drops and sheer cliffs demand caution from those navigating its confines.

Ecology

Void of fauna, the quarry is colonized by typical Pathways flora. Slime and moss cling to walls, making surfaces slick and treacherous as low ground cover, flowers, and strange grasses find purchase anywhere they can.

Lore

Adopted by the Mutagists, the quarry serves as a clandestine lab where their experimental work to develop some sort of mutagenic compound takes place. With animal pens, labs, mixing stations and copious chemicals, the lab space is as fully featured a work space as any specialist could want.

Little is known of their intentions or the nature of their research, and when the location is first discovered it will be in the throes of destruction. Whatever work was being carried out here has been completed, or terminated, and is slated to be moved elsewhere.
Repurposed Quarry.soverview: Once a simple source of stone, this subterranean site has been transformed into a sprawling laboratory. Hidden deep in the Pathways, dubious experiments and alchemical ventures abound here, shrouded in secrecy and shadows.
Repurposed Quarry.sexposition: A gaping maw cut into the pathways bustles with activity in the darkness. Shadows flit back and forth against the rock face, and figures move across the metal catwalks between structures. Pillars of smoke rise in plumes, dissolving into the gloom overhead. A narrow tunnel cut into the stone appears to be the only way to access it.

Sinkhole Depths.name: Sinkhole Depths
Sinkhole Depths.text:
Home to the sprawling multilevel settlement of Arcturel, the Sinkhole Depths is the most easily accessed part of the Pathways in the Arctus Plateau, and as a result is the most well known and well studied of the vast underground regions in the world. It is a landscape rife with natural and unnatural resources, not to mention untold dangers lurking in the shadows.

Environment

Though downright treacherous in places, much of the terrain is easy enough to travel, and can even support the use of drawn wagons if routes are chosen carefully. Unlike other locations beneath the surface of Ember, the depths are mostly open, without winding tunnels to make navigation confusing. However, the rocky, uneven ground is not entirely yielding, and the presence of long fissures in the earth means that traveling aimlessly through the depths can quickly become fatal if one is not paying attention.

Ecology

Mammoth broadleaf trees with shimmering leaves tower over patches of rust-colored mushrooms, creating a unique ecosystem that thrives in the absence of reliable sunlight. The denizens of the depths are numerous, and dangerous, with countless minor Inkaro pools dotting the landscape, many of them home to lurking Mootaps, while packs of savage Jurtak prowl the lightless spaces, looking for unwary prey that have wandered too far from the light.

Scattered throughout the rocky terrain are low places that have formed natural basins where mineral rich water can collect and feed local plant life and sustain the various creatures that roam the area. Though not every pool is host to them, Mootaps can frequently be found within, preying on any creatures that get too complacent in the water.

Though the dense spore content in the air below the depths is harmless to humanoids, it does tend to coat everything, and can't be easily avoided. These spores can spoil unprotected food and water supplies, cause rot and mold to take root very easily, and even cause difficulty breathing when especially dense. This only adds to the dangers and difficulties of long-term survival in the region.

Lore

The Sinkhole Depths have long been a source of fascination and mystery. It is the shallowest point of the Pathways in the Arctus Plateau, and thus was able to be accessed when a massive sinkhole opened up overhead. Over the years it has been home to mining operations, hunting expeditions, failed attempts to establish camps and settlements, and any number of surveys. This makes it the most well mapped and well traveled section of Ember's subterranean expanses.

However, the depths are no less dangerous than any other section of Pathways, and many expeditions and ill-planned endeavors have come to swift, tragic ends as a result of the Sinkhole's many hazards. To date, only Arcturel and its nearby camps and operations have withstood the trials of the Sinkhole Depths. These settlements serve as the starting point for any new ventures into the spore coated gloom around it.
Sinkhole Depths.soverview: Vast trees with bioluminescent teal leaves illuminate the depths alongside patches of rust-hued mushrooms which constantly drop waves of glimmering spores into the air. In between these patches of overgrowth and fungal colonies are stretches of forbidding, rocky ground and natural pools of spring water fed from unseen sources below.
Sinkhole Depths.sexposition:
A vast, sunless chasm sprawls before you, its roof a sea of shadow pierced by towering stalactites of rust-streaked stone. The ground rises and dips unpredictably around thee massive columns, and in between them you glimpse gaping sinkholes plunging into fathomless darkness below.

Massive roots, thick as ancient oaks and armored in wicked thorns, burst from the earth and arc overhead, shaping natural arches of living wood and shadow before they plunge again into the ruddy earth of the cavern floor.

Speckled throughout the gloom are great stands of broad-leafed foliage of teal and orange that grow out of rock and earth. These trees are pushed aside by giant, glowing bulbs or expansive crowns of mushrooms with burnished brass caps. These collections of mega fungus cast a broad spectrum of colors across the foliage around them, the light coming in reds, golds, teal, and pink.

The air itself glitters with countless drifting spores — each glimmer like flecks of gold and silver caught in the air. Each breath in this place is accompanied by the earthy tang of mushrooms, wet earth, and minerals. Spores settle everywhere, clinging to every root, rocky shelf, and outstretched leaf, dusting the entire expanse and its inhabitants in a sparkling shroud.

Mycelian Expanse.name: Mycelian Expanse
Mycelian Expanse.text:
The Mycelian Expanse is mostly flat ground with few changes in elevation of note save for a few plateaus and winding tunnels. However, the area is home to several rivers that flow toward a massive central chasm which descends abruptly into the core of Ember and presents the main navigational obstacle of the region.

Environment

Travel through the fungal groves of the expanse is challenging and disorienting, as the region has no discernible sense of night or day, leaving travelers in a perpetual twilight. Despite the name, this area of the Pathways has little in the way of useful landmarks or unique terrain to aid travel, making it very easy to become lost.

Ecology

This region is overgrown with life of all shapes, kinds, and dispositions. The most abundant life in the expanse is fungal in nature, though many plants live in these lightless caves without any difficulty, seemingly surviving despite lack of sunlight. The fauna of the region is equally varied and in many ways utterly alien to anything seen on the surface.

Lore

Once, the burning blood of Ember flowed through these massive caverns, bringing with it the powerful life magic that shaped the whole of the world. Over time the currents of magically charged magma shifted, and diverted to other regions, leaving behind massive tubes and chambers of stone.

Over time the stone cooled and the lingering magic began to affect the region. Ancient remnants of matter and life left behind when the expanse pulsed with life began to grow and warp, changed by the ambient magic swirling in the dark spaces. Before long glowing mushrooms forms, fields of strange grasses sprouted up, and gnarled trees with glowing leaves became home to an ever growing menagerie of strange life forms.
Mycelian Expanse.soverview: This region is covered in massive fungal growth with bioluminescent mushrooms growing in patches not unlike forests. In between and underneath these fungal groves are untold numbers of strange flora and fauna that feed of the ancient magic flowing through this area.
Mycelian Expanse.sexposition:
An expanse of vast caverns unfolds before you. Gigantic stalks of mushrooms as tall as ancient trees spread out in the gloom, their luminescent caps and funnels casting an ethereal glow across the caverns at their lowest points, while yawning darkness consumes the rest.

All around you the glowing flora shifts their colors through shades of blues and and greens, teasing shapes and forms that shift in and out of the foliage with every blink. Strange yet harmonious sounds fill the air, the calls of unseen creatures, some warning of unexpected intruders in their world.

Inkaro Pools.name: Inkaro Pools
Inkaro Pools.text:
This particular acreage of pools is owned and operated by the Silver Beam Consortium. Like other Silver Beam holdings, the Inkaro Pools are strictly off-limits to interlopers and uninvited guests. A small team of Silver Beam guards patrol the perimeter surrounding the Pools and drive off trespassers without a second thought.

Environment

The large pools are deep and naturally roiling thanks to the gasses bubbling up from the rocks that cover the bottom of them. While some of the pools here are accessible by wooden decks and walkways, many of them are lined by wet stones and nothing more.

Ecology

This collection of subterranean water basins serves as natural habitats for Pathways creatures known as Mootaps — monstrous, crustacean-like predators who produce the luminous spheres known as Inkaro Pearls. Beyond this the pools are host to all manner of much smaller, much less dangerous aquatic and amphibious life such as Puddle Scuttlers, Acid Dart Eels, and schools of diminutive of Bubble Fish.

Lore

These pools have been worked by Arcturel for decades, first by locals, then by House Cevher, and most recently by the Silver Beam Consortium. While they are not the only pools in this region that host Mootaps, these are the closest to Arcturel, and the most productive that have been found thus far. As a result, whenever anyone from Arcturel talks about "the Inarko Pools" they almost certainly mean this location specifically.

The work of harvesting Inkaro pearls from the gullets of Mootaps is dangerous work at the best of times and has claimed numerous lives over the decades. The task requires the Mootap be restrained and stunned before a worker can dig out the large pearls. Any misstep in this process can prove fatal, and that danger has led to the rise of automation as a means of making it safer. Now, teams of constructs work the pools, overseen by flesh and blood supervisors, with minimal risk to mortal life.

The magically infused Inkaro pearls are Arcturel’s most prominent export, as they have many uses and are utilized across the plateau as sources of power for constructs, reagents for spells, and powerful light sources to beat back the dark.
Inkaro Pools.soverview: This work site is home to dangerous Mootaps, creatures that produce valuable Inkaro Pearls. This site is actively worked by the Silver Beam Consortium, which moves those pearls through the town of Arcturel.
Inkaro Pools.sexposition:
A collection of bubbling pools covers a broad area here in the depths, the majority of them built up with small docks, wooden sidewalks, and sheds roofed with large fronds cut from the surrounding wilderness. While some of the pools sit unattended and unworked by the people here, they all are home to strange creatures moving under the surfaces of the water.

As you draw closer, the unpleasant stink of sulfur and other acrid gasses becomes hard to ignore. A long rope fence surrounds much of this area, and bears the sign:

Silver Beam Work Site — Authorized Personnel Only!

Aberin's Folly.name: Aberin's Folly
Aberin's Folly.text:
Located several miles east of Rock Bottom, this ramshackle campground endures as a rundown relic of Arcturel's past, choked with abundant mushroom growth and the ink-black darkness of the Depths. Once known as Aberin's Hold, Aberin's Folly is what remains of an ill-fated mining camp that unfortunately fell prey to the area's natural (and supernatural) hazards. And thanks to the subterranean biome's lack of a meteorological weather system, the essence of the camp's "temporary" structures and abandoned inventory have remarkably stood the test of time.

Aberin's Folly has fallen into total disregard by the people of Arcturel and will only be found on the oldest of local maps. Nevertheless, the camp's accoutrements and geographical vantage make it a suitable enough place for rest or surreptitiousness. Made of various treated leathers, the tents are still quite functional and duly represent the pride inherent in classic Arcturian craftsmanship. A splintered array of crates, barrels, and bins decorate the tent-side areas, alongside a handful of tool-littered tables and rickety wooden chairs. A bygone scattering of grime-covered mining equipment has also been left here, but a small fire pit smolders at the camp's center — suggesting recent occupancy and a sign of life.

Environment

The campsite itself sits upon a low rocky butte above an overgrown gully, marked by uneven tiers of craggy brown stone. The soil here is hard and compact, which makes matters of sure-footing and solid construction relatively safe. And while some of the area's bioluminescent vegetation sheds a welcoming dim light, the local environment mirrors that of the Sinkhole Depths at large — where timeless, foreboding shadows paint the outskirts and areas between.

Ecology

The flora and fauna at Aberin's Folly aren't altogether unique from other areas of the Sinkhole Depths. The large awnings of countless rust-cap mushrooms dominate the area, alongside a few modest specimens of lambent broadleaf trees and smaller species of fungi. Meanwhile, ample patches of Bristlevine weave their way through the area's valley — posing a somewhat hazardous traversal if one isn't careful while crossing them.

Wildlife here includes the ubiquitous @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvet}, which lair in small dens among the camp's refuse, and various insects, arachnids, and reptiles native to the biome's furthest reaches. Visitations from larger, more dangerous creatures of the Sinkhole Depths are infrequent, but do happen (indeed, one such incursion is responsible for the location's woeful renaming). Predatory creatures like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.tLSBe3kfPlvqmnH2]{Jurtak} and @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Garganthi} have occasionally been known to prowl these grounds and pose an imminent threat whenever they do.

Lore

Despite its meager and slipshod appearance, Aberin's Folly has a storied history tethered to the earliest days of Arcturel, when a prospector named Aberin Hyle established a mining post here known as Aberin's Hold. In partnership with House Cevher and various stakeholders of Arcturel, this enterprise flourished for two seasons before calamity beset the modest camp.

As the story goes, a large six-limbed aberration crawled from somewhere out of the darkness one unassuming night to wreak havoc on the tiny settlement. Before the denizens of Aberin's Hold even knew what hit them, this terrible and malefic creature took several lives, slaughtering livestock and humanoids alike. The survivors quickly fled, abandoning the remote encampment for the years to come. In the wake of its demise, the ill-fated camp has come to be remembered as Aberin's Folly, if indeed it is remembered at all. What the settlers of Aberin's Hold didn't know is that the malefic creature in question was a Garganthus, which prowls the Sinkhole Depths to this very day — along with other unsavory denizens of the Pathways.

Lately, the camp serves as a makeshift hideaway for a group of awakened Chessmen known as the "Downsiders", who conceal themselves here far away from the prying eyes of their humanoid masters in Arcturel. And the brambles of the gulley hide their own secret: the forgotten remains of a few slain settlers and the rusted chassis of several nameless automatons.
Aberin's Folly.soverview: The mushroom-shrouded encampment known as Aberin's Folly is what remains of an abandoned mining post originally established during the early days of Arcturel. Once, this tumbledown place was a lively waystation for excavators of the eastern Sinkhole Depths. Today, it's a near-forgotten haven for itinerants and outsiders who seek shelter among the tattered tents and moldering wares that surround them.
Aberin's Folly.sexposition: Out of the subterranean darkness, you spy a tiny source of light nestled atop a craggy hillock, where the silhouette of a ramshackle encampment looms over this forgotten corner of the Pathways. A half-dozen tattered tents and stacks of splintered crates surround a small fire pit at the camp’s center — which can be reached by way of a pair of rickety bridges that hang above the area’s rocky terrain and overgrown fungal sprawl.

The Scrapyard.name: The Scrapyard
The Scrapyard.text:
The Scrapyard is a cruel and uninviting place where constructs go to die, and Silver Beam can conduct their most unsavory operations in secrecy. As with any Silver Beam operation, visitors are unwelcome, and workers will use force if necessary to drive off interlopers.

Environment

This open-air forge and junkyard is nestled in a narrow stretch of high, rocky walls covered in the Sinkhole's natural flora. Navigating the area requires significant climbing to avoid being funneled by natural stone pathways and barriers of old, rusting metal.

Ecology

Rocky and overgrown with local flora, the scrapyard is home to all manner of little critters and creatures that make nests in the rocks and heaps of scrap. Even the rock burrowing Crevvet can be found here, the skinny little rat-like beings having invaded the depths long ago. Here, these creatures can hide out safely, as larger predators are unlikely to approach a site actively occupied by humanoids and constructs.

Lore

This site was established by the Silver Beam Consortium out in the Sinkhole Depths to hide the untoward activities of those assigned to work the forge and scrap heaps. The work here is all done in support of the larger operation being undertaken in the Silver Beam headquarters found in Arcturel.

Here a team of Silver Beam engineers and constructs take apart Chessian constructs, repurposing their parts and melting down their scrap to be re-forged into material for creating new Silver Beam constructs. The internal corpses of the doomed constructs are also altered before being shipped back to Arcturel for final assembly, programming, and activation.
The Scrapyard.soverview: This scrapyard is hidden amongst the rocks and plants of the Sinkhole Depths and is owned by the Silver Beam Consortium. Its purpose seems fairly evident — to collect the remains of machines and constructs, which are then dismantled and repurposed.
The Scrapyard.sexposition:
A wrenching sound of scraping metal echoes off the stone, emitting a screeching tone that makes you wince in discomfort. You scan the environment to identify the source and your eyes catch sight of coiling tendrils of smoke hovering overhead before you in the gloom. As you cast your gaze downwards you see shifting forms of shadow, their silhouettes dancing in front of the flickering glow of firelight.

Drawing closer, you survey an unexpected landscape: battered iron drums, heaps of rusting metal, and twisted remnants of strange machines discarded carelessly or accumulated into disorganized piles. In the center of the space an large smelting furnace glows angrily, hungry for salvage fed into its all-consuming crucible eye.

Primordial Bastion.name: Primordial Bastion
Primordial Bastion.text:
The Bastion is undoubtedly a masterful construction from a people that have long since vanished from Ember. One of the most interesting aspects of this structure is that it seems to have been carefully and meticulously preserved, left in a deliberate state to repel intruders. Traps are carefully laid out; puzzles and the interpretation of runic script require access to inner areas. However, there are hints that the structure was once used for a different purpose, such as small empty holes in some of the walls and areas where the design of the floor’s patterns has clearly been cut away to accommodate defensive features.

The Lightless Halls

Within the Bastion, there are a series of large chambers and halls, connected by enormous, soaring hallways that rise nearly 60 feet to the ceilings. This colossal edifice has endured countless years without any noticeable faults or cracks; when carefully observed, it seems to shimmer slightly from magical reinforcement. Only a thick layer of dark gray dust covers the floors of the chambers. Throughout the dim halls, some rooms are filled with ancient runic carvings, machines, traps, softly glimmering golden adornments, and a deep unsettling silence.

Ecology

There is little, if anything, growing within or around the Bastion. Even the sickly pale plants and mushrooms of the surrounding biome of the Fogbound caverns seem to avoid encroaching too closely to the smooth stone walls.

Lore

The Bastion was constructed by the first Giants of Ember long ago during the Age of Beasts. This ancient era of the world remains nearly entirely unknown, but it’s evident that at some point, the Giants who built this structure abandoned it. One particularly curious aspect of the Bastion is especially mysterious, given what is known about the Giants of this period. They had little, if any, contact with or knowledge of the surface and were believed to have stayed underground until they emerged to see the skies for the first time after the Unveiling. So how then could they have possessed knowledge of Lantyr to build or create an artifact that harnesses some of her power?
Primordial Bastion.soverview: The Primordial Bastion is likely not its true name, as it is a structure of truly ancient origin dating back to the first Giants. Its age and lasting impact on this part of the world cannot be overstated, and its purpose remains ultimately unclear. Although it appears to be some kind of light source for the area at first glance, it may also serve as a form of protection or warding against forces of evil. The glowing light at the apex of the central obelisk-like tower resembles a miniature sun and seems connected to Lantyr in some inscrutable way. Clerics or followers of Lantyr will find the light warming when they gaze into its radiance.
Primordial Bastion.sexposition: You see a distant glittering light, akin to a miniature sun atop a tower of dark stone. The light shines across the dim section of the Pathways, barely illuminating anything beyond its immediate surroundings but perfectly visible on its own. As your eyes adjust to the light and darkness, you can also see a sprawling settlement or a series of large buildings surrounding the base of the large obelisk-like tower, hidden in the gloom.

Fogbound Caverns.name: Fogbound Caverns
Fogbound Caverns.text:
The Fogbound caverns are a small biome deep within the pathways, lying below the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.FJNYRa0cGLlizwYY]{Mycelian Expanse} by several miles. It is an eerie, deeply unpleasant, and ultimately horrifying place that few dare to tread, even with the promise of extensive rewards. It is a place where soft, unsettling words or screams creep into the mind, and some believe the whispers are echoes of long-forgotten secrets, carried on tendrils of entangled darkness. Though few have dared to explore deeply, the caverns hold a prominent place in some circles as a realm best left undisturbed except for the truly brave, with rich rewards somewhere hidden within.

Environment

Navigating the Fogbound Caverns is a challenging endeavor. The slick, damp rock from the heavy fog makes navigation treacherous, and the prevailing darkness is made all the worse by the thick fog itself, which limits visibility and masks terrain features like sudden drops and narrow paths. Dripping stalactites far above quickly add to the damp and wet environment, creating additional perils by coating surfaces with a slick, hazardous layer of gelatinous ooze. The ever-shifting shadows in this darkened landscape contribute to the feeling of intense disquiet and foreboding. While the caverns are eerily silent and seemingly free of immediate dangers, the occasional horrifying soft scream or snarl can be heard in the distance.

Ecology

There are no natural creatures or plants living in the Fogbound Caverns; everything that exists in the gloom is a twisted form of something else or an entity from beyond Ember entirely. Misshapen fungi cling to dark rocks, their pale, ghostly glow offering minimal light. The blighted earth supports little else, and the fog creates a damp, moldy environment that is both cold and inhospitable.

Some creatures venture into the caverns from elsewhere, becoming corrupted by the twisting forces and energies present and beginning to blend into the fog and stone. These creatures, while elusive, pose a constant threat, as stealth and surprise are their favored tactics. One of the most common entities encountered in the biome are Abyssal Eels that roam in large swarms and devour whatever life they encounter.

Lore

This is a place rife with Abyssal corruption and energy which has seeped into the stone, poisoned the wildlife and plants here, and turned a once vibrant stretch of the Mycelian Expanse into a withered and foreboding hole that no wise being should ever venture into. It was once home to a shining outpost of the First Giants, and the lake that now exists in the center of the Fogbound Caverns was once a traversable tunnel leading to other First Giant settlements. Unfortunately, during the Unveiling, this part of the Pathways suffered greatly, and the Orb of Lantyr became a crucial relic in stopping the spread of corruption.
Fogbound Caverns.soverview: This is not a place for the faint-hearted, as the darkness, obscuring mist and warped terrain make travel difficult in the most ideal of situation. Questions of what caused this malformation in the area remain unanswered to this day.
Fogbound Caverns.sexposition: Twisted, nightmarish rocks thrust upwards around you, imparting the sensation of being stuck in a cage, or the grasp of some malicious entity. The air grows dense and unnaturally heavy, thick with mist that causes every sound to carry farther than expected, and echo in strange, unsettling ways. Now and then, there are sounds of things moving in the mist but they are never seen. Colossal stalactites drip a viscous dark liquid, forming steaming puddles that merge into the thick fog swirling around your ankles. Twisted, withered mushrooms here emit only the faintest of glows, leaving this region mired in an oppressive shadow and darkness.

Voidspan Bridge.name: Voidspan Bridge
Voidspan Bridge.text:
This massive bridge crosses an underground chasm that plunges into the dark depths of Ember. Without it, crossing the gap would take much longer.

Environment

Slung across a monumentally large chasm in the center of the vast mushroom caverns in the Pathways, the Voidspan Bridge stands out with its glowing chains and levitating stone. The stone itself is clean but worn, the ancient stone preserved by the powerful magic flowing through it. The air is filled with a powerful hum and periodic rumbling that stem from the energy flowing through the chains and the occasional grinding of the stone sections moving against each other.

Ecology

The bridge itself remains devoid of typical plant or animal life using it as a habitat, and the magical hum of this space almost certainly wards off any creatures that might consider crossing it.

Lore

The Voidspan Bridge is one of the many great mysteries found in the Pathways beneath Ember. Built by Giants that predate even the Shent, the size and enduring nature of the construction hint at advanced magical technology that has withstood eons of weathering.
Voidspan Bridge.soverview: The Voidspan Bridge is an incredibly ancient structure that has stood for countless years in the deep, dark caverns of the Pathways. Its origins are a mystery, though it is believed to predate the ancient Shent.
Voidspan Bridge.sexposition: Nearly a mile wide and extending for twice as far at least, this bridge is supported by great cubes of stone fixed in the air by glowing runes of power etched into their sides. Glimmering chains of light hold the sections of stone over the great, lightless chasm below.

Mythspire Overlook.name: Mythspire Overlook
Mythspire Overlook.text:
This wide plateau covers a mile of level, elevated land, and has been marked by the footsteps of countless travelers now all long forgotten by time. Signs of these travelers can still be found here, but they are scattered and insignificant, with any items of value having long been removed.

Environment

The raise area is no different from the rest of the Myceliean Expanse, though entrance to it is accomplished by way of massive stairs to the south, their scale fit for giants, or via a massive lava tube that winds its way up to the Mthspire Observatory.

Ecology

While the cleared and built up space remains largely undisturbed, nature is slowly reclaiming the space, and plenty of plant growth and signs of animals can be found in the area.

Lore

This overlook was a brief stopping point for the migrations to the surface by the ancient Giants, where they first breached the surface of Ember and saw the skies for the first time. This is now a small area where visitors from the surface are able to take in the enormity of the Pathways and their vast underground caverns. Its commanding view of the space also make it good for spotting landmarks and plotting courses through the gloom.
Mythspire Overlook.soverview: At the foot of the great Mythspire Observatory this landing is the first place one can view the expansive underground space of the Pathways, and truly grasp the enormity of the region that spreads out under the surface of Ember. This location has long been used as a base camp and gathering point for travelers both ancient and modern in the region.
Mythspire Overlook.sexposition: You stand on a sizable plateau overlooking a cavern of unimaginable scale, stretching for miles in all directions, its farthest reaches claimed by perpetual shadow dotted with the fading glow of the Myceclian Forest's great fungal growths. From this vantage you can see twisting rivers of water rushing toward a massive hypogean chasm in the center of this region.

Silent Ossuaries.name: Silent Ossuaries
Silent Ossuaries.text:
Nestled in the caves are a collection of man-made spaces where the remains of ancient humans are stored.

Environment

While not inherently difference from the rest of the Myceliean Expanse, this secluded area is extensively populated with artifacts, creations, and decorations of a long-lost society that once ventured into these depths.

Ecology

This area is densely overgrown with the natural flora of the expanse, and no signs of curation are visible anywhere. This site has sat abandoned and forgotten for centuries at least, allowing nature to reclaim the space.

Lore

Long ago, before the great cities were built, ancient Arcturians built tombs in natural caves all over the plateau. This silent ossuary is nearly identical to those ancient tombs, though its placement is unexpected.

It's unknown if these tombs were established by the ancient Arcturian peoples the ventured into the pathways using the mechanisms of an even older people, or if they were built by an offshoot that resided down in the dark below ember Surface. In either case, they found a secluded space where they could lay their dead to rest, and generations of bones now are interred there.
Silent Ossuaries.soverview: Nestled in the caves are a collection of man-made spaces where the remains of ancient humans are stored. Once a place of rest and silent repose in the darkness, this site was disturbed by grave robbers, or worse, as many of the corpses have been removed.
Silent Ossuaries.sexposition:
Massive stalagnate columns rise from the ground into the shadowed reaches overhead, each one surrounded with rich bends of fungus and plant life. These ancient pillars are marked with numerous holes that appear to have been carved into them at regular intervals.

As you draw closer you notice the collection of carved shrine stones, hanging decorations of ancient, rotting textiles, and massive candles in various stages of melt. All around these and the ancient offering bowls are the scattered remnants of bones and death shrouds.

This space was once a place of rest of the dead, but was despoiled by grave robbers somewhat recently by the looks of things.

Lake of Whispers.name: Lake of Whispers
Lake of Whispers.text:
This large lake lies deep underground within the Pathways of Ember. Very little light illuminates its dark waters, and a soft, almost imperceptible whisper lingers over its surface.

Environment

The lake itself is calm, and a low fog constantly clings to the surface of the water. Aside from the rare swirl or eddy from below, the lake is utterly devoid of life. No fish swim in the water, no insects can be seen hovering above, and the water is so clear that even smaller creatures and flora are absent. It is an eerie and chilling place, and while it seems safe to cross at first glance, its depth could conceal any number of aquatic dangers.

Ecology

There are no fish living in the lake and no natural life forms of any kind. However, during certain times of the year, abyssal entities like the Abyssal Eels swarm above the waters in large numbers.

Lore

The Lake of Whispers is at one end of a much larger pathway that is completely filled with water. It runs deep into the depths of the world, and while at some point the twists and turns of the sections below curve and split in such a way that prevents water from flowing in large amounts into the Fogbound Caverns, just enough reaches the lake to prevent stagnation. At some point, this lake was likely used by the first Giants, but any trace of their presence has long since disappeared.
Lake of Whispers.soverview: The Lake of Whispers is an ancient section of the Pathways that was once a tunnel leading deeper into the depths of Ember. Its true depth is unknown, but water does not flow in from above or from any streams or rivers. Instead, the water is kept from becoming stagnant and brackish by a constant current that flows from below.
Lake of Whispers.sexposition: The waters of the lake in the middle of the Fogbound Caverns are exceptionally dark. Barely a ripple flows across the surface, and the air above it is still and thick with fog. Looking down into the water, a slow current swirls just visible in the gloom, and you sense immediately that falling or attempting to swim in these waters would be a perilous mistake.

Main Quest Overview.name: Main Quest Overview
Main Quest Overview.text:
Significant Spoilers

This page contains major spoilers for the plot of Ember, A Shard of Fear. We recommend all Gamemasters read through it thoroughly, however, because it's important to have a clear understanding of the overarching storyline of the campaign that you'll be orchestrating for your players.

On the other hand, some Gamemasters may strongly prefer to not arm themselves with full knowledge of the campaign's events. Proceed only if you wish to have all of the information available to you up-front instead of learning things as you play.

A Shard of Fear

The title of Ember's main story is A Shard of Fear, a deliberate moniker that acts as a bit of a spoiler once certain narrative information becomes available to the players. What the player characters of this grand adventure will eventually learn is one of the world's best kept secrets: many of the events that have swept them into the chaos and fatefulness of an emergent conflict in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} revolve around the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.EhQnCUxkJyxOSbf7]{Vile Dragon} known as @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss} — a powerful spellcaster who has their insidious sights set upon godhood.

The machinations of Zerranyss are not readily apparent at first, and early events will serve to establish the lore of the Ember world (its @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0]{Ancestries}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000]{Cultures}, places, and paradigms), gently exposing players to this dazzling new setting and its associated gameplay. The first few chapters of the game focus on a slow reveal of early plot elements while foreshadowing the greater story. However, by the end of Chapter 2, it becomes clear that there is something very sinister behind the calamitous and destructive events that have ravaged the Arctus Plateau in recent years.

Zerranyss is first encountered during Chapter 3, although indirectly via the humanoid guise of @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith}. Zerranyss' actions and ambitions directly cause the central plotline of the Ember campaign. The vile dragon is a cunning and strategic villain, and has orchestrated a complex plan to undermine and usurp the seats of power in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} — one of the great cities of the world and (most importantly) an access point to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.0jWlGgl5wkijM77v]{Shard Caverns}, where Zerranyss believes a powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal} may be found. Such an artifact would allow Zerranyss to undertake an ascension ritual which, if successful, would imbue the dragon with the power of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God}.

Chapter 1

The Chapter 1 Main Quest in Ember is called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai]{The Winding Trail} and covers the party's journey to the frontier mining town of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}, traveling with the eccentric caravanner @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} and the @UUID[Actor.emberStrayhearth]{Strayhearth Caravan}. Chapter 1 introduces the player characters to the following key allies, who will become a large part of the story to come:

@Embed[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP readaloud="Lyla Cevher is a savvy human from Ordain, poised to inherit both the prestige and problems of House Cevher — one of the famed Ordani Trading Houses."]

@Embed[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs readaloud="Ankarist is a skilled and stoic Drakon warlock. Originally hailing from the Tayan Empire, Ankarist now lives in Ordain and is a dedicated and determined investigator within the secretive ranks of the Veiled Chain."]

@Embed[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv readaloud="Sin Marmot is a wide-eyed Keth druid from the Corebright Forest, known for her aptitude with nature and enthusiasm to join the ranks of the benevolent Cindaric Sages."]

The journey takes an unexpected turn when the caravan's progress is obstructed by a massive rockfall, requiring the party to identify an alternative route that can be followed through the region. Upon reaching Helkas, the revelry of the Dusktide Festival turns deadly as a cohort of mutated drake-kin attacks the town alongside a marauding band of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune} raiders.

The aftermath of this attack provides clues and ill omens that set the stage for the epic campaign that follows.

Chapter 2

Following their fateful encounter in Helkas, the party now has a singular goal: to reach the great city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} to the east. However, the characters have a choice of three paths corresponding to each of the three companion allies, who undertake separate journeys toward the metropolis.

Traveling with Lyla

If the characters depart Helkas with Lyla Cevher, they undertake the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu]{An Old Friend}. Their journey will first lead them to a reunion and consultation with a powerful mentor to Lyla, the Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE]{Sigil}. From there, the path of clues leads to the industrial town of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel}, the settlement of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fBPE6UWg6EOO2WFH]{Nain}, and eventually the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.X1FzWfTYfe7JfD3P]{Seawall}. Along the way, the party gathers clues towards the identity of the mysterious Otherhood of Fortune.

Traveling with Ankarist

If the characters depart Helkas with Ankarist, they experience the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100]{Ancient Paths} and journey northward in search of a legendary Shent tower called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.RWj91gQguWOQcflB]{Mythspire Observatory} wherein an entrance to the vast subterranean @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} may be found. As Ankarist and the characters explore the lightless depths, they'll uncover schemes of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]{Mutagists} — a group of sinister alchemists whose twisted experiments are conducted within the secrecy of their underground laboratory.

Traveling with Sin

If the characters depart Helkas with Sin, they experience the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1]{Crumbling Sanctuary}. The road ahead will initially take them to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh]{Corpin Sanctuary} on the slopes of Mial Mountain, where Sin will make her first contact with the devoted @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}. However, this introduction is waylaid by the presence of a villainous necromancer, whose unholy machinations will lead to a siege on the Sanctuary by a horde of skeletal undead.

Eventually, all three paths lead to the city of Ordain and the beginning of Chapter 3.

Chapter 3

Having reached the great city of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet]{Ordain}, the party is now faced with three Main Quests associated with the key NPCs they met at Helkas (Ankarist, Lyla, and Sin). Throughout these adventures, the party will start to see the effects of Zerranyss' machinations on Ordani society. While exploring the city's bustling streets, the characters will begin learning about the insidious forces responsible for the problems at hand.

Although the party can initiate all three of these Main Quests, each quest has a "point of no return" event where the party must decide which of the three they'll continue to completion — once the characters finish such a Quest Event, they become locked out of the other two Quests for good.

Chapter 3 also introduces the player characters to a new key NPC, Fernis Ossa, whose associated Quest will become available as the party explores Ordain.

@Embed[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0 readaloud="Fernis Ossa is a seasoned Ashka Ranger who is something of a celebrity in Ordain, known for her storied affiliation with the Anachraenum — the city's esteemed guild of archaeologists, lore-seekers, and treasure hunters."]

Fernis and the Anachraenum

Fernis Ossa approaches the party with a proposal to ally in response to recent concerns about the operations of the Anachraenum. In the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1]{The Expedition Challenge} Quest, the heroes are sponsored by the fabled explorer as entrants in the grand Expedition Challenge — an extensive test of skill and capability that serves as a trial and competition for aspiring Anachraenum initiates. Fernis will also arrange for the party to reclaim possession of a secure and strategic hideout hidden within the derelict district of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.0RX8vLjKjRjf3JSj]{The Concourse}.

Ankarist and the Veiled Chain

If the characters choose to help Ankarist with his investigation into the clandestine Mutagists, they'll encounter the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness}Qquest — a mystery that begins with some poisoned granaries in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.s7O0qBepuI89HKUU]{Lilifeld Stations} before spanning the entire city of Ordain, eventually leading to a hidden laboratory in the Sedyri ruins of the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h]{Forgotten Cistern}. And all the while, the party members are being manipulated by the machinations of @UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]{Serethus} — one of Zerranyss' devoted lieutenants — which culminate in a perilous ambush the characters must narrowly escape.

Lyla and House Cevher

Parties which reconnect with Lyla Cevher in Chapter 3 may assist her with an intricate maneuver in the @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1]{Disgraced House} Quest to expose and oust the enemies of House Cevher responsible for their downfall. They will investigate the death of Lyla's uncle Darius and become embroiled in the planning of an epic and dangerous heist against the rival @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{House Wandren} during the backdrop of the the prestigious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.uVodk7tLiG3pZMTq]{Marlstone Gala}.

Sin and the Cindaric Sages

If the characters choose to assist Sin Marmot with her initiation to the Cindaric Sages, they will experience the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders} and help the young druid to uncover further details of the insidious necromantic plot which was first revealed in the depths beneath Corpin Sanctuary. This investigation eventually leads to a climactic battle in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.cvUD3Rj9MLXLwpAb]{Burial Grounds} where Zerranyss' ally and Blood Baron necromancer @UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan} has unleashed a hematophage abomination to prey upon and wreak terror among the citizens of Ordain.

Chapter 4 and Beyond

Chapters 4, 5, and 6 are not yet included, but will be added during a subsequent test phase. If you reach the end of Chapter 3 before this further content is added, we recommend taking a short hiatus from the campaign or spending time to explore the world and experience the many Side Quests which are available.

The events of Chapter 4 will compel the party to journey back out into various reaches of the Arctus Plateau, where certain people and places of Ember have been impacted by the deviant orchestrations of Zerranyss. Depending on which key NPC the characters have chosen to ally themselves with, these journeys could lead them to a variety of dangerous and intriguing locations in search of adventure.

Lyla and House Cevher

If the characters continue their adventures with @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla}, they must respond urgently to the troubling disappearance of the shard god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE]{Sigil}, Lyla's mentor and a powerful ally of House Cevher. This quest will follow a bloody trail of clues from the Shard God's extradimensional lodge to the lawless streets of Seawall on a hunt for answers that culminates in a operation to take down the Otherhood of Fortune.

Ankarist and the Mutagists

The party faces a race against time to save @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist} from the wasting effects of the mutagen inflicted upon him by the traitor Serethus. Their search for answers will lead the party to a remote island northeast of the Arctus Plateau and the seaside town of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fMje6qlhxYMnAbZR]{Caste} in search of clues to the Mutagists' location. The clues they discover lead towards a terrible laboratory where blood-based experimentation has produced abominable revelations.

Sin and the Cindaric Sages

If the characters continue their adventures with @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin}, they will be charged to join the Lumek paladin @UUID[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]{Luna Karrowrath} and her Flameguard warriors on a crusade into the northwestern @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands} where long-forgotten tombs of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Varún} giants may hold answers about the looming undead threat. The discovery of an ancient evil from the time of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering} will challenge everything the characters think they know about undeath.

Fernis and the Anachraenum

Meanwhile, continued adventure with @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} will compel the party to join her on a dangerous expedition in the southwest to explore the Crumbling Spire — an enormous fragment of the famed Broken Tower of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire, sundered into countless pieces during the calamitous events of The Shattering. Puzzles, mystery, monsters, and more await the party beyond the gates of this massive dungeon.

Towards Endgame

After completion of these Chapter 4 quests, the party will find themselves propelled towards the final arc of Ember's campaign (Chapters 5 and 6) via the revealed identity of Zerranyss and their terrible scheme to pursue ascension to godhood via communion with a Heart Crystal.

Faced with near impossible odds, the party must prepare to confront Zerranyss by completing what plotlines they can as well as by exploring lost and ancient places of the world to recover the knowledge and power to stand against a would-be deity.

Additionally, as a Gamemaster we recommend you review the pages in the Gamemaster's Guide to understand how the various systems of the game function and interact.

Vistas for Gamemasters.name: Vistas for Gamemasters
Vistas for Gamemasters.text:
A Vista is a special environment used for storytelling in Ember. Vistas present an in-character view of the world where you can look around and interact with other characters or aspects of the environment.

Work In Progress

The Vista System is actively evolving as part of Ember's development. This page is not yet complete, but will be updated accordingly as the Vista System and its features are further developed.

Most importantly, Vistas are used for conversation with non-player characters (NPCs). Events which transpire inside a Vista are often designed for dialog and conversation between player characters and the various NPCs which inhabit the vista.

Player characters can ask NPCs any number of questions and receive answers. Ember typically provides prewritten responses to overarching questions that the Gamemaster can read aloud, however, these prewritten responses are not exhaustive and the party should feel comfortable asking questions and receiving answers given directly by the Gamemaster as well. If a player's questions align with one of the overarching questions the Gamemaster can also choose to display the answer via the Vista which will be displayed as subtitles or a chat bubble within the Vista itself and saved in the Chat Log.

Each Vista scene depicts an in-world Biome or broad Location area, such as the grassy moors of the Golden Flats or the bustling city of Ordain. Within each Vista scene, there are multiple available Compositions that represent locations within that region. Compositions range from specific places, such as a notable point of interest, to more generic locales that could exist anywhere within the Vista's range.

Many Quest Events are set up to use particular Compositions that have been crafted specifically for the moment at hand. However, all Compositions within a Vista can be visited freely should the party find themselves in an impromptu social situation. And for moments that don't quite match the currently available Compositions, it is possible to construct new custom Compositions from premade templates or from scratch.

Overview

Vistas are located in the Scenes tab within a "Vistas" folder. There are two subfolders that further categorize the available vistas:

  • Locations: These Vistas use specialized art to represent specific points of interest and typically include only one or two compositions.

  • Biomes: These vistas use modular assets to represent broader areas or regions and typically contain multiple compositions as well as templates for creating custom compositions.

Quest Events with preconfigured Vista usage will load the specified Composition upon activating the event, but to view or activate a Vista outside of a quest, simply choose the desired Vista from either subfolder. Upon viewing or activating a vista outside of a Quest, it will display the first available Composition or the most recently viewed Composition if the Vista has already been visited.

To change the active Composition, view the basic layer controls and select the button with the repeating arrows icon — this button is located second from the bottom. Hovering above this button displays a "Change Composition" tooltip. Clicking this button will open a dialog box with a dropdown menu. Within this menu there are three categories:

  • Core Compositions: Premade, complete Compositions crafted by the Ember team.

  • Custom Compositions: An initially empty folder, where Compositions created by users are listed.

  • Template Compositions: Premade "blank" templates created by the Ember team for users who wish to create their own Compositions.

Select the desired composition and press "Change" to update the Composition that is displayed. Since only one Composition can be viewed at a time, all users viewing the Vista will be affected by this change.

Custom Compositions

For Gamemasters who wish to create their own custom Compositions, the Vista Configuration Tool will allow them to do so. Before accessing the tool, it is strongly suggested you first change the active Composition to a template.

Work In Progress

While creating custom Vista Compositions via the Vista Configuration Tool is possible, users should keep in mind that this feature is in active development. The UI/UX are actively evolving, and bugs are expected.

Please also be aware that future updates that improve functionality may have limited compatibility with Compositions created using the current framework.

To access the Vista Configuration Tool, view the basic layer controls and select the button with the dual cogwheels icon. This button is at the bottom of the basic controls and hovering this button displays a "Configure Vista" tooltip. Clicking this button will place the Vista into "debug view" and open a new menu. There are two tabs within the tool's menu: Assets and Scene.

Assets

This is the primary tab you will use to build Compositions. Toggle lists on the left contain categorized Assets that can be placed by clicking the crosshairs to the right of each asset name. Once an Asset has been placed and selected, the parameters of that Asset can be edited using the fields located on the right.

Scenes

This tab can be used to define your custom Compositions, edit advanced scene information, and toggle the visibility of shader effects. Entering data into the fields under "Composition" will allow the current configuration to be saved as a custom Composition. It is not advised for users to change the Token Scaling data.

At the bottom of the menu are additional controls:

  • Clear: Resets the active composition. For Core and Template Compositions, this means reverting to the preconfigured settings. For Custom Compositions, this means reverting to the most recent save point.

  • Import: Opens a dialog allowing the manual input or pasting of configuration data.

  • Export: Copies the current configuration data to your clipboard.

  • Save: Saves the current configuration as a Custom Composition. The "Identifier" and "Label" fields of the Scene tab must be filled out for this to work. A popup will inform you if saving the Composition has been successful.

  • Delete: Only visible on Custom Compositions. Clicking this will delete the active Custom Composition and remove it from the list.

Configuration Tips

  • When creating Custom Compositions, it is best to start with the desired template, save a Custom Composition, then change to the newly created Custom Composition and complete further edits there.

  • Saving frequently is recommended to help prevent the loss of progress.

  • Periodically exporting snapshots can also be useful, as those can be imported to revert to a version of the Composition that has been saved over.

  • If something seems amiss with asset placement or layering, try saving your progress before pressing "Clear," which should resolve a variety of minor placement issues.

Starting the Game.name: Starting the Game
Starting the Game.text:
Before beginning play in Ember, there are several pieces of information that the Gamemaster should review, and activities that you should undertake along with your players.

Review the Story

Unless you're particularly averse to spoilers, you may wish to read the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberGameGuide00.JournalEntryPage.Ajl2mEpagPebOYJx]{Main Quest Overview} in order to understand the scope of the main quest storyline, which will unfold over months (if not years) of gameplay.

Character Creation

Before the game begins, take time for every member of the party to create a player character of the Player Character type. If you want players to be able to do this themselves, you will need to ensure that players have the Create Actors permission granted to them in the User Permission Configuration screen.

Once each player has completed the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.UJLt0kE0pFZlUkJQ]{Character Creation} process, you should add their created character to the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party} group, which defines the set of characters who are currently traveling together.

Session Zero

We recommend beginning your experience with Ember by spending time on a preparatory session, often called "Session Zero," rather than jumping into the story immediately.

Character creation will take some time to complete; it involves presenting new information about Ember as a setting, and requires each player at the table to make important creative decisions about their character. These campaign-spanning decisions should not be rushed.

The first session of Ember's main story will likely feel more complete and satisfying if everyone has already created a new character beforehand. Furthermore, "Session Zero" is a valuable opportunity to establish shared expectations among your group regarding specific gameplay elements, social norms, and personal boundaries that are important to each player at the table.

Starting Play

When you are ready to start play, activate the @UUID[Scene.emberWorldRegion]{The Arctus Plateau} region map Scene. The first gameplay event @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.VG3DRsbDuG43cV01]{Sheltered Campsite} in the Chapter 1 main quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai]{The Winding Trail} will automatically begin and present you with a prompt at the top-center of the screen.

At the beginning of this, and every other event, you will encounter readaloud text presented inside a parchment block that is intended to be narrated aloud to players before clicking the Begin Event button.

Text presented in this type of stylized block represents a "readaloud" which should be narrated aloud to the players.

Once you have narrated the initial event exposition, clicking the Begin Event button will transport you and your players into the first Scene of the game, a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberGameGuide00.JournalEntryPage.U7QcWsGAbENffGAk]{Vista} depicting the campsite where your caravan is spending the night.

After you have completed the gameplay described within the event text, click the Complete Event button to mark the event as concluded, which will automatically return you to the Region Map.

The Strayhearth Caravan

For the first leg of the adventure, players are not in control of the movement of the caravan on the region map. The Strayhearth Caravan makes its way towards Helkas using the most direct route, with stops at the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.40qvRRe30tQVsAiJ]{Giants' Moonstone} and @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.0IsGP3Ar0XvIYoMZ]{Dry Outpost} where the caravan will spend the night on Day 1.

Automatic Caravan Movement

Automatic movement of the Strayhearth Caravan is not yet implemented in Beta. We eventually envision a guided tutorial experience for this first passage of gameplay that helps the GM automatically direct the caravan.

For now, Gamemasters will need to manually move the Strayhearth Caravan up until the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.VzlG3TTOny9a5b1M]{The Collapsed Cairn} event, after which point the players will take control of their own Party token. The caravan should follow the annotated map shown below to reach this point at around noon on Day 2.

Audio Engine.name: Audio Engine
Audio Engine.text:
Instead of managing multiple playlists and sounds of audio, there is only one playlist, the @UUID[Playlist.EmberPlaylist000]{Ember Soundscape}, which is always playing. There are four different sound channels inside this playlist:

  1. Music — which conveys the musical feeling and mood of the world. Music volume can be controlled by each player individually using the Music Volume Control.

  2. Environment — which conveys the soundscape of the world and the places that you visit. Environment volume can be controlled by each player individually using the Environment Volume Control.

  3. Weather — which adds certain weather effects or other intermittent environmental cues and is also played in the Environment volume control layer.

  4. Effects — which include interaction sounds like dice rolls, clicks, or notifications which are not in-world audio. The volume of these Effects can be controlled by each player using the Interface Volume Control.

Ember's dynamic audio engine is designed to adapt to gameplay without requiring direct input from the Gamemaster. The following sections detail the primary ways in which the engine adapts.

Region Map Location

Each biome in Ember is configured with a specific music and environment arrangement. Moving the party token from a hex with one biome to a hex with another will trigger this change automatically.

Specific locations on the region map have their own designated music or environment arrangements that supersede the default audio of the biome within which they are located. For example, the town of Helkas has its own distinct music and environment arrangements which override the default arrangements of its biome, the Verdant Paths, when the party token is located within Helkas.

Time of Day

Where appropriate for the location or biome, the music and environment arrangements will change depending on whether it is currently day or night according to Ember’s world time.

Mood

Music arrangements change depending on the currently selected mood, “calm” or “tension”. This can be controlled manually by the gamemaster from the Playlists tab, but is dynamically controlled by the audio engine during some events.

Events

Some events are configured to automatically change the music and/or environment arrangements at the start of an event, or when a particular outcome is selected by the gamemaster within that event. With some exceptions, events configured in this way reset to the default arrangements for the location or biome and reset the mood to “calm” upon ending the event.

Scenes

Some scenes are configured to automatically change the music and/or environment arrangements whilst active. For example, the Helkas Festival vista uses its own music and environmental arrangements which are distinct from the default Helkas arrangements.

Combat Encounters

Music in Ember automatically changes to appropriate combat music during encounters. The specific music is dictated by the composition of foes the party is facing. Each round of combat, the chosen theme may change as the composition of the surviving enemies in the combat encounter evolves.

Only visible tokens with the "Hostile" disposition which are not already defeated are considered. The determination of which combat theme is made using the following criteria in order, resolving ties with the next criteria:

  1. Cumulative challenge rating.

  2. Number of creatures.

  3. Largest sized creature.

The audio arrangement which was previously playing before combat began automatically resumes once the combat encounter is ended.

Stronghold.name: Stronghold
Stronghold.text:
The Stronghold is a special location in Ordain acquired starting in Chapter 3 which gives the players a home base which they can invest in, develop, and progress.

Work In Progress

The Stronghold system is not yet implemented and will be added during a later phase of game development.

Welcome to Early Access.name: Welcome to Early Access
Welcome to Early Access.text:
Hello, and welcome everyone to Early Access! This is an incredibly exciting milestone for the Ember team as we open the doors to a wider audience, and we're thrilled that more of our wonderful backers and supporters can now experience our game. Since launching Ember with Alpha and Beta testers, we've made significant progress—adding entire systems, questlines, hundreds of actors and items, maps, and artwork. Despite this progress, Ember still has a long journey ahead and is far from finished, but if you're looking for a truly unique and one-of-a-kind roleplay experience with your group, welcome!

About Early Access

The Ember team is creating the game through an open development process, which allows you, our supporters and backers, to see and experience an early version of the game while it is still under construction. Traditionally, Early Access denotes a project that is playable but still far from finished, which is exactly where we are with Ember. Almost every cornerstone feature of Ember is implemented in some form, but some features are still partially underdeveloped. Furthermore, significant portions of the game content are not yet designed or rigorously play-tested.

Under Construction

Please remember that the overall Ember Early Access experience is a work in progress. You will almost certainly encounter bugs, missing features, or content, and while we hope these deficiencies will not ruin your experience, it is important to expect a certain level of "Jankiness" compared to the final product.

Early Access Rules

When you play Ember, you'll likely have many comments and thoughts about the storylines, mechanics, balancing, or even your pure enjoyment of the experience. We would love to hear your impressions. Here are a few guidelines we ask you to follow:

  • You are free to invite players who don't have Ember Early Access to join your game.

  • You are free to talk about Ember Early Access; there is no NDA.

  • You are free to post screenshots, make videos, or livestream your experience.

  • If sharing content about Ember Early Access, please remind your audience that what they are seeing is still an early stage of development! If your players discover bugs or issues, please encourage them to report or share their feedback with the team!

Early ACcess Goals

As we move from Beta to Early Access, our goals remain the same with a slight shift in focus. We are very close to implementing all of our major gameplay and software systems. As of the start of Early Access, most of these systems are close to complete, while others are still in their infancy. We are deeply committed to finishing these systems as quickly as possible over the next few patches.

Furthermore, over the course of Early Access, we will be adding new game content, refining existing content with balance adjustments or clarifications, and expanding support for the Crucible system by converting more of our gameplay to be Crucible-enabled.
