Our goal is to complete our remaining systems first, then shift focus to content production for the latter half of the game. We plan to launch Ember once this content is finished, although we anticipate ongoing creation and refinement even after the launch.

Should I Play Ember Now?

If you are debating whether to begin an Ember campaign now or to wait for the game to be more complete, you should consider the following guidance:

Early Access is playable and fun! But the game is not yet done, and the game experience that you will have playing Ember at this stage will be inferior to the quality and scope of what the final game will deliver. If you would rather play a fully polished and playtested experience, then you should wait.

However, if you or your group want to experience the game now and are interested and excited to help with the playtesting process — assisting us to make the game better for future groups, then jump in, familiarize yourself with the content, and remember to take notes for feedback!

Providing Feedback.name: Providing Feedback
Providing Feedback.text:
During this phase of development and testing, our team will be focused on continuing to develop and refine the major systems of Ember while actively reviewing and prioritizing feedback from our community of tester players. Your input is invaluable to us and every report, suggestion, and observation helps shape the game and ensures that the final product is as polished, engaging, and enjoyable as possible.

Where to Submit Feedback

All feedback that you have about the game should be submitted through our official Discord server: https://discord.gg/foundryvtt . We have set up a dedicated channel, #ember-test-feedback, specifically for this purpose. Within this channel are a number of individual posts where you can submit feedback. These are specific to systems, quests, or aspects of the game that we have highlighted as needing extra scrutiny. You can create a post yourself to highlight a topic; however, before you do so, please ensure that you have checked to see if there is already a post that discusses that topic.

Using this channel enables our team to track feedback efficiently, discuss issues internally, and respond to your questions or requests for clarification more effectively.

Submitting Feeback

When providing feedback, please try to be as detailed and clear as possible. Useful feedback often includes:

  • Steps to reproduce issues or bugs – This helps us understand exactly what happened and how to fix it.

  • Screenshots or recordings – Visual examples can make it much easier for the team to identify and address issues.

  • Your experience or suggestions – Share how something felt, what worked well, and what could be improved.

  • Prioritization or severity – If something is a critical bug or a minor annoyance, let us know so we can address the most urgent matters first.

We encourage constructive, respectful, and thoughtful feedback. Remember, this is a collaborative process, and your input directly influences the development of Ember. While we may not be able to implement every suggestion immediately, we carefully review all feedback and use it to guide our updates.

Thank you for helping us make Ember the best it can be. Your participation, enthusiasm, and insights are what drive the project forward, and we deeply appreciate the time and effort you put into testing and sharing your thoughts with us.

Patch 0.1.1.name: Patch 0.1.1
Patch 0.1.1.text:
Ember Alpha patch 0.1.1 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.337 or higher and D&D5E system version 4.3.5 or higher.

New Features

  • Implement basic framework allowing for custom Standalone Events to be added to the game
  • Implement an EmberVistaToken subclass of the Token placeable which improves the code quality for special Vista-specific Token workflows
  • Re-enable click+drag Token movement in Vista scenes in a way that integrates the dragged Token position with the Vista environment.
  • Changing region map elevation should advance time and trigger events or discoveries in the destination hex
  • Improve presentation of event outcomes UI and/or make an outcome embeddable lower in the quest where narratively that outcome is likely to occur
  • Add control buttons to the header of each event allowing you to manually initiate or reset an event. Prompt the user with warnings if initiating or resetting an event could be inconsistent with Ember game state and event prerequisites.
  • Saving changes to the dynamic token for a player character should replace the static file stored in World data.
  • Add guidance to the GM Guide suggesting the nature of the player character's relationship to each other at the start of the game
  • Impose restrictions that only allow setting specific valid elevations and transitioning to a different elevation at specific valid hexes on the Region Map
  • Use location overview text as part of the "Involved Locations" block of the Quest Overview page.
  • Add support for hierrarchical categories in the VistaConfig sidebar instead of just used vs. unused assets
  • Add a keyboard modifier H which flips vista assets horizontally during placement or editing
  • Holding SHIFT during vista asset placement will lock elevation so you can move an asset vertically at a given elevation
  • When selecting a placement of an asset in the vista, highlight and pan to its location so it is clearly visible
  • Add custom Ember cursors using the new V13 cursors API with a client setting to optionally disable them
  • Use biome overview HTML as auto-generated biomes section in Location pages
  • The Fulgurite Blades caravan should be auto-added to the region map after Untouched Wilds.
  • Add ability to save a custom vista composition to Scene flags which are preserved upon adventure import

Content Improvements

  • Numerous typography updates and improvements for Ember Journal Entries.
  • Clarify exact timing and arrival time expectations in The Winding Trail
  • Revisit the Helkas area map to add support for parallax layers that weren't possible when it was first created
  • Revisit Roll Tables and move HTML descriptions back into tables and out of events
  • Skallith actors in the Bestiary are not correctly using TokenMaker static exports
  • Fixing general typos in the Setting Compendium
  • New Setting Setting Compendium Content
  • Add more water to Mycelian Expanse environment
  • Improved the rendering quality of a number of vista assets across multiple vistas
  • Add 3 "Background NPC" portraits of Cindaric Sages
  • Add support for the Wirrun ancestry into the Ember Token Maker for player characters and NPCs
  • Add new Mycelian Expanse vista compositions "Overgrowth" and "Scout Camp"
  • Add Rask and Rask Juvenile creatures to the world and Codex
  • Add audio environment layers for Arcturel
  • Add vista asset categorization for all existing vistas
  • Configure the Strayhearth Caravan character sheets to display properties such as languages, walking speed, etc, on the left sidebar.

Bug Fixes

  • Improve the final steps of character creation with a more integrated advancement flow and an approach to saving dynamic token portraits that does not require the FILES_UPLOAD permission
  • Correct issue with duplicating geometryMeshes and particleEmitters when redrawing a vista (like in the vista-config)
  • Address bugs in the adventure export process which failed to properly cull data like emptying the party or removing tokens from scenes.
  • Convert all maps that use legacy Ember doors to use new core V13 doors and delete Ember doors code
  • Fix an issue which caused the region map pathfinder to prefer impossible routes to possible ones
  • Prevent the page links in the Events Control UI from being draggable
  • Ensure that Ember scene environment and lighting effects are re-applied whenever changes to the Scene cause the canvas to be updated.
  • Resolve bugs and improve user experience of the Vista Config tool to be more accurate and easier to use.
  • Ensure that scene regions which automated changes in elevation (Mythspire, Yakoshta) correctly only handle your own token movements and not all tokens
  • Ensure the Yakoshta Mine track graph is properly cleaned up when that scene is deconstructed
  • Switch to using dnd5e.registry.classes for detection of available character creation classes
  • Fix the water layer animation shader in the Arctus Plateau Mega Region.

Patch 0.1.2.name: Patch 0.1.2
Patch 0.1.2.text:
Ember Alpha patch 0.1.2 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.339 or higher and D&D5E system version 4.3.7 or higher.

New Features

  • Add the Ashka ancestry template to the Ember Dynamic Token framework. This means that now all 16 of Ember's playable ancestries are supported! We still have big plans for the token maker, more parts, more variety, and more features - but this is a big milestone in terms of completing the foundation.

  • Begin converting Ember scenes to use KTX2 textures for superior GPU performance, memory management, and minor improvements in visual fidelity.

  • Updated the Ember Region Map ruler to use new v13 TokenRuler labels API.

  • Add Scene and Composition tags to the header of each Event, and include select tags in the Event Overview section of the Quest Overview page.

  • Refactor timekeeping framework to use new core v13 CalendarData API

  • Refactor dnd5e system-specific code into the ember.dnd5e submodule so it can be compartmentalized when using Ember with Crucible.

  • Add support for Location discoverability restrictions which allows certain gazetteer POI locations to be only conditionally discoverable.

  • Add configuration to each Location for discoveryHexes which define other hexes in the world from which this location may be discovered.

  • Add software integration support for the forthcoming ember-lunar-dice module which causes those dice to interact with the current in-world lunar phase.

  • Add support to attach programmatic light sources to region map locations so that those light sources are automatically disabled or enabled based on the location discovery state.

  • Suppress presentation of the Token elevation tooltip if the token is at the default "land elevation" for the region map slice, for example -1 in the Pathways.

  • Add a confirmation prompt when selecting an Event Outcome which confirms it is an intentional selection to avoid mis-clicks.

  • Add custom EmberDynamicTokenConfig header option to reset all custom offsets and angles.

Content Improvements

  • Added artwork for several new locations of interest to the mega-region map including: Arcturel, Inkaro Pools, Scrapyard, Construct Camp, Primordial Bastion, Shrouded Borehole, Storsa's Strand, and the Smouldering Tent.

  • Added a new Area Map for the Fogbound Caverns biome with several different compositions to explore.

  • Added a new Area map for the Bastion Apex, part of the Primordial Bastion dungeon that will feature prominently in a forthcoming quest.

  • Added a new musical soundscape for the City of Arcturel.

  • Added new combat music for Construct Combat.

  • Added new Golden Flats vista composition: Camped Merchants.

  • Added a new Sinkhole Depths vista composition: Fortified Camp.

  • Add waterfall flow shaders to vista compositions which feature a waterfall asset.

  • Add Verdant Paths and Dripstones leaf particle emitters.

  • Added many new vista assets in the Golden Flats, Rustvar Valleys, Wedgelands, and Sinkhole Depths biomes.

Bug Fixes

  • Correct some errors with the initial orientation of moons after the world time changes made in 0.1.1.

  • Fix a bug which prevented the surface of Ember in the Cosmos Map from being properly illuminated by the sun and affected by lunar phases.

  • Fixed a bug which caused caravan tokens to have a vision distance different than their EmberHexSightPolygon result.

  • Fix a bug which incorrectly required Location pages to explicitly declare a Terrain type. The default behavior for Locations is to inherit their terrain type from the Biome within which they exist.

  • Correct rendering size for the EmberDynamicToken for tokens which have width and height other than 1

  • Resolve some issues that prevented the Yakoshta Mine scene from tearing down properly.

  • Fix the coordinates of the Voidspan Bridge POI in the Pathways.

Patch 0.1.3.name: Patch 0.1.3
Patch 0.1.3.text:
Ember Alpha patch 0.1.3 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.339 or higher and D&D5E system version 4.3.8 or higher.

This is a minor patch which adds bug fixes for blocking or problematic issues in the 0.1.2 update.

New Features

  • Only display the "Change Composition" scene controls button for Vistas which have multiple compositions to choose between.

  • Refine the logic used to detect patch notes for the current Ember version in the appropriate journal so the CONST doesn't need to be manually updated every release.

  • Suppress the "Configure Vista" button if the vista is not manually configurable.

Content Improvements

  • Refine and re-balance the lighting in the starting Shard of Akon Campsite vista composition to be more dramatic and warm.

  • Remove the Impassable Ground page from the Pathways gazetteer and handle this biome purely programmatically.

Bug Fixes

  • Correct failure to load Character Creation due to typo in ember.character pack document retrieval.

  • Audio soundscape shuffling applied during Character Creation sometimes continues after character creation has concluded.

    Correct the font size of discovery scrolling text which is now oversized due to new v13 canvas UI scaling rules.

  • Fix bug with programmatic creation of region map light sources.

  • The Arctus Plateau region map was incorrectly configured with Global Illumination off.

  • Fix the rendering of Ember passive check tooltips which changed due to v13 core tooltip changes.

  • Improve the reliability with which activating the Arctus Plateau region map will begin the first game event.

  • Fix a bug which prevented audio from playing in the Pathways in 0.1.2.

  • Correct some issues with identification of the region map slice and current hex due to manual slice cycling.

Patch 0.2.0.name: Patch 0.2.0
Patch 0.2.0.text:
Welcome to a major Ember content release as part of our ongoing Alpha One test process. This major update includes new quests, new areas to explore, new characters to encounter, and way more!

Compatibility

Ember patch 0.2.0 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.341 or higher and D&D5E system version 5.0.0 or higher.

Important Playtest Instructions!

If you are actively playtesting Ember it will be important for you to manually trigger the newly added @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.wL4CB6fnuy0XJziF]{Leavetakings} event and select the correct event outcome in this event. If you do not do this, certain Chapter 2 content will not function correctly!

New Quests

This update adds the final two Chapter 2 side-quests to the game.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3]{Glitter in the Dark}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi]{To Fall and Fall Again}

Glitter in the Dark

Rumors are sweeping through the Golden Flats about an unsolved crime in the sinkhole city of Arcturel, a place where lawlessness has a loose foothold and lost things are seldom found. It seems one of the ubiquitous constructs used for manual labor in Lower Arcturel's industrial sector went haywire and killed an innocent bystander, and now the murderous automaton is missing — having fled the scene of the crime to places unknown in or around the Sinkhole City itself.

Naturally, a pall of paranoia and civil unrest has settled on the various districts of Arcturel, whose citizens live in mounting fear of the errant "Renegade Construct" and its homicidal tendencies. In an effort to stem this tide of turmoil, House Cevher and other businesses of Arcturel have teamed up to hire some outside investigators to track down the missing construct and mete out some proper recompense. Enter the party, who may very well discover a new definition of justice before Arcturel's score with the Renegade Construct is settled.

"Glitter in the Dark" will task the party with tracking down the so-called Renegade Construct and examining the mysterious events that surround the incident with the deceased citizen, a miner named Kellen Lorde. This investigation will lead the characters from the upper reaches of Arcturel to the darkest subterranean corners of the Sinkhole Depths — where the party will come face-to-face not only with their quarry, but with their very sense of right and wrong.

To Fall and Fall Again

An ancient attack. A mysterious body. A whisper in the night. Something is changing deep in the Pathways beneath Ember that has begun to affect the lives of those on the surface — and attracted the attention of powerful forces locked in an age-old struggle.

In the midst of these larger than life events, a family has suffered an unthinkable loss. One child has fallen in the darkness of the Pathways, another to the anguish of trying to find her. Their father now lives a simple life, but even his daily existence is tainted by the effects of the corruption that has begun to make its way up from the deep.

In “To Fall and Fall Again,” your path will head into the Pathways below Ember toward a light in the darkness, facing monsters, temptations, and ancient powers. As you make your way to millennia-old ruins, you can learn some of the secrets of those who built them, uncover the power that still remains hidden deep within, and confront a corruption as old as time.

Quest Changes

In addition to these new quests, there are some significant quest changes for the main quests in Chapter 1 and the beginning of Chapter 2:

The Winding Trail

The end of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai]{The Winding Trail} has been reworked.

  • Parties which arrive late to Helkas experience @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.YfJF8Z5XAXFcKmiU]{Dusktide Destruction} before also experiencing @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.fFtsG83gvrlyz3KY]{The Smoke Clears} as all other parties do.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.fFtsG83gvrlyz3KY]{The Smoke Clears} has been rewritten to be appropriate for all groups. During this event, Sadri Zhalimorne pushes the party more emphatically to return to the Forest of Stone and clear up the Chapter 1 side quest they did not experience on the way to Helkas before journeying onwards into Chapter 2.

  • A new event, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.wL4CB6fnuy0XJziF]{Leavetakings}, now concludes Chapter 1 wherein the party will gain their final milestone point and make a decision about which main quest companion to journey onwards with into Chapter 2.

If you are actively playtesting Ember it will be important for you to manually trigger @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.wL4CB6fnuy0XJziF]{Leavetakings} and select the correct event outcome in this event. If you do not do this, certain Chapter 2 content will not function correctly!

Chapter 2 Main Quests

The chapter 2 main quests with Ankarist, Sin, and Lyla have also been reworked:

  • All 3 quests now depend on the outcome selected in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.wL4CB6fnuy0XJziF]{Leavetakings}

  • The "Departing With …" events have been removed from these quests, as that content is now covered by the Leavetakings event.

  • Each of these 3 quests has a new "Traveling With …" event: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100.JournalEntryPage.keJtcQkmLrbCNrXX]{Traveling with Ankarist}, @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.2iUwaNqn7Eo168Rl]{Traveling with Lyla}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.41dlrDZuVo04zQJT]{Traveling with Sin} which are repeating events that can happen throughout Chapter 2 to strengthen your relationship with your companion by discussing ongoing events with them and learning their perspectives on the evolving world and the characters you meet.

  • Each of these 3 quests has a new "Reuniting With …" event which standardizes the mechanism by which a party can reconnect with that companion if they did not travel with them initially in Leavetakings.

    • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100.JournalEntryPage.59ICMZ4XfBJ5tMQh]{Reuniting with Ankarist} occurs in Skybrush

    • @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.BbqdZ43p5aVGPG2i]{Reuniting with Lyla} occurs in Nain

    • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.tZt7uMs1zOt5jwXF]{Reuniting with Sin} occurs at Corpin Sanctuary

New Areas

There are numerous new or significantly improved areas to explore in patch 0.2.0 including:

Area Maps

  • @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelTra]{Arcturel Upper - Tradeway}

  • @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelUnd]{Arcturel Upper - Underbelly}

  • @UUID[Scene.emberLightlessHa]{Lightless Halls}

  • @UUID[Scene.emberBastionApex]{Bastion Apex}

  • @UUID[Scene.emberFogboundCav]{Fogbound Caverns}

  • @UUID[Scene.emberSinkholeDep]{Sinkhole Depths}

  • @UUID[Scene.emberMythSpUpper]{Mythspire Observatory - Upper}

Vistas

  • @UUID[Scene.emberVistaArctur]{Vista - Arcturel}

  • @UUID[Scene.emberVistaPathFC]{Vista: Fogbound Caverns}

  • @UUID[Scene.emberVistaPathSD]{Vista: Sinkhole Depths}

Gazetteer locations

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.6nRFXEspxMJd6AQ8]{Aberin's Folly}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.iciVMv0WWYPKkp97]{Inkaro Pools}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.CPBGxUJqmL8o4XsG]{Lake of Whispers}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.EUcIZPY7x0qFHe3c]{The Scrapyard}

Characters and Creatures

As part of these quests, there are a number of notable characters you can meet or creatures you can encounter including:

Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth}

  • @UUID[Actor.OYdqWs17RvL7ntbf]{Lucent}

  • @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A]{Nadin}

  • @UUID[Actor.GuuohJfDx6gifCH5]{Kendral Lowd}

  • @UUID[Actor.bEMPCjG9mFc1d93U]{Issa Sunsword}

  • @UUID[Actor.d0mSoQozEIKozWVe]{Luxaroth}

Creatures

  • @UUID[Actor.0xDU0k3l8V4movO8]{Chessman}

  • @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU]{Silver Beam Servitor}

  • @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE]{Silver Beam Sentinel}

  • @UUID[Actor.vyN7FNbPEw6KsuGw]{Silver Beam Engineer}

  • @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7]{Silver Beam Guard}

  • @UUID[Actor.AnhHlAMP5rsnH7wZ]{Mootap}

  • @UUID[Actor.m86FIWDHh47htZNy]{Jurtak Geomancer}

  • @UUID[Actor.PO4036qpja149J7E]{Sporix Host}

  • @UUID[Actor.IZ1XuA12PN7L7DYE]{Pale Whisperer}

  • @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE]{Abyssal Echo}

  • @UUID[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ]{Abyssal Eye}

  • @UUID[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM]{Abyssal Eel}

  • @UUID[Actor.Q5iudLrTvVX7AeFF]{Gohema}

  • @UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A]{Vhismara's Claw}

  • @UUID[Actor.jXhgSnAtBX8gHBah]{Kezus Jelly}

  • @UUID[Actor.1OhTZgynGs9x5wFe]{Giant Kezus Jelly}

  • @UUID[Actor.Va3xPZVUrdOTb73X]{Corrupted Kezus Jelly}

  • @UUID[Actor.P4mkMkXH6KK6WBoz]{Giant Corrupted Kezus Jelly}

Other Content

In addition to these major pieces of content, there are numerous other content improvements featured in patch 0.2.0.

  • Added a suite of audio for the metropolis of Ordain including both music and environment sound for Ordain's three major biomes: Ordain Flats, Ordain Spires, and Ordain Docks!

  • Arcturian Constructs have been added as a non-playable template to the Ember Dynamic Token maker with support for woven, chessian, and silver beam variations.

  • The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberSignalInten.JournalEntryPage.signalIntentSunw]{Well Enough Alone} event in "Signal of Intent" now has a tracked outcome which governs the party's success (or not) in ascending the bluffs. A hex-to-hex boundary now prevents movement unless the event is successful.

  • The @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.yWP8ZAyLMGIWpaRU]{Bridging the Gap} event in "Thorny Predicaments" now visually toggles the appearance of Brevin and enables or disables an impassible hex-to-hex barrier depending on whether the Brevin Bridge is active or not.

  • Added a number of creature portraits for Yarnac, Rask, Tricket, and Ooze which allow these commonly domesticated creatures to be used in Vistas as non-humanoid tokens. These portraits are found under modules/ember/assets/portrait/creatures.

  • Added numerous "background characters" which can be used as miscellaneous crowd or background actors in vistas. This artwork is found under modules/ember/assets/portrait/background.

  • Add particle effects to the Splinter Canyons vista with the Water Surge composition.

  • Improve the rendering of the Sea of Stars in the Cosmos Map to appear more infinite and animated using a custom shader.

  • Improve the rendered quality of a large number of vista assets and backgrounds.

  • Improve the Corpin Sanctuary area map to feature the Pathways elevator and Evesso's profane altar.

  • Balance changes for Svala and Gafto the Howler in the "Ambushed Refugees" event in "Crumbling Sanctuary".

  • Added a Profane Altar active effect to Evesso which applies during "Sanctuary of Death" in "Crumbling Sanctuary".

  • Added standalone events which can occur in the Fogbound Caverns or Sinkhole Depths biomes.

Software Features

  • Differentiate the control icon or highlight color for GM-only interactables vs. interactables which can be controlled by players.

  • Restore D&D system specific short and long rest event logic so that Ember gameplay events can properly interrupt a Short Rest or Long Rest. Remove the restriction that prevented events of the social or exploration type for triggering during this context.

  • Capture explicit Dynamic Token configuration for unlinked tokens as part of Event encounter setup.

  • Update EmberRegionTokenRuler for new v13 waypoint label changes.

  • Add a custom journal enricher that can reference a specific event or event outcome and render it as a link with a checkbox for whether it has been completed or not.

  • Allow deleting a Caravan token as long as it is not the primary ember.partyToken

  • Better align ProseMirror WYSIWIG styles with Ember journals.

  • Implement new EmberNarrativeEvent#spawnEncounter method which can spawn the configured encounter for an event in the background, independent of the active Scene on the canvas.

  • Support custom token texture src and scale in EmberAreaMap#getActorSpawns

  • Automate adding the chosen main quest companion to the Party actor as an event hook in the Leavetakings event.

  • Allow EmberBeamLightSource to be occludable.

  • Add support for new event coefficients for chapter completion progress and main quest companion party membership.

  • Added a reusableMagicalPlatformShader, to create magical platforms or bridges with a lot of options (glow, patterns, resolution, colors, etc.) for visual effects.

  • Optimized the light sources in the Ember Cosmos Map to be more performant since they are not reliant on walls or collision.

  • Adapted the rendering complexity of the Ember Cosmos Map depending on the client's configured Performance Mode.

Bug Fixes

  • Improve rules around the visibility of gazetteer pages and their Note objects on the region map canvas. Players should be able to see the pinned locations of any gazetteer location that they have discovered, but not other undiscovered locations.

  • Fix a bug which caused completed Standalone Events to break the Codex display because they have no root quest node.

  • Adjust for CONFIG.Canvas.fogManager for V13 stable changes and fix restoration of CONFIG variables in Ember managed scenes.

  • Improve game state flags for chapter completion progress so that it automatically recomputes upon event state changes.

  • Fixed a bug in the WaterSamplerShader which caused the processed texture to be offset in the incorrect direction.

Patch 0.2.1.name: Patch 0.2.1
Patch 0.2.1.text:
Welcome to an Ember content release as part of our ongoing Alpha One test process. This update focuses on the city of Ordain and support for the Crucible game system.

Compatibility

Ember patch 0.2.0 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.344 or higher and either:

  • D&D5E system version 5.0.3 or higher.

  • Crucible system version 0.7.0 or higher.

Re-Import Required

It is essential to re-import the Ember adventure after installing this update. If you are actively playtesting Ember, be sure to use the Preserve World State option when you re-import.

Important Playtest Instructions

If you are actively playtesting Ember it may be necessary for you to manually trigger the newly added @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.wL4CB6fnuy0XJziF]{Leavetakings} event and select the correct event outcome in this event. If you do not do this, certain Chapter 2 content will not function correctly!

Ordain

The focus of our team's work from May through the end of September is the metropolis of Ordain and our Chapter 3 game content which takes place there. This first release in that sequence adds major improvements to Ordain as the first step in that process.

  • Introduce a major update to the artwork for Ordain on the region map. There is still a ton more work to do here, but this update redesigns the linework and begins to add color to the city, making it feel much more vibrant and alive.

  • Write @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet]{Ordain Gazetteer} pages for each of Ordain's 3 biomes and 51 distinct locations ("districts"). Every single hex of Ordain is it's own district with it's own unique history, culture, lore, landmarks, locals, and more.

  • Add new setting compendium articles for significant topics related to Ordain, including:

    • Geography: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}

    • Geography: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}

    • History: @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}

    • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}

    • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}

    • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}

    • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{House Salva}

    • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{House Wandren}

    • Organizations: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain}

Much more Ordain content is on the way as we continue to work on Chapter 3!

Crucible Character Creation

This release is the first on the long journey towards comprehensive Crucible game system support for Ember! Ember can now be installed, activated, and imported (with limited content) into a World that is running the Crucible system.

Crucible is not yet playable, BUT this release does add support for testing Ember's wonderful character creation process in the Crucible game system. We are closing in on Alpha Two, which will enable Crucible to be playable for Chapter 1.

  • Enable Ember to be used in a Crucible world.

  • Integrate Crucible and Ember character creation using a beautiful guided creation interface featureing all of the Ember setting-specific Ancestries, Attunements, Cultures, and Paths.

Other Content

  • Added water particle spray and foam to the @UUID[Scene.emberCanyonsBiom]{Splinter Canyons} vista in the "Water Surge" composition.

  • Completed the Area Walkthrough for @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI]{Mythspire Observatory} upper level.

  • Add a new deity portrait for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu}.

  • Add a new Culture banner illustration for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir}.

  • Add a brand new music orchestration for "Celestial Combat" which is used when fighting adversaries of the celestial type.

  • Created new biome-specific asset variants for the Mycelian Expanse and Sinkhole Depths biome vistas.

Software Features

  • Introduce a super-optimization for light source rendering on maps where light sources are unimpeded by Walls. Most notably in the Arctus Plateau mega-region map, light sources are now rendered using a fully batched shader that should provide a noticeable performance improvement while viewing this scene and will be able to accomodate the thousands of tiny light sources that the mega-region will eventually contain.

  • Refactor and rename all journal entry page sheets for better standardized design. A consequence of this change is that you MUST re-import the Ember adventure.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a bug with the interactive light bridges in Vortest Tower.

  • Correct an issue with the directional water flow in the Shent Moon Temple.

  • Added Issa Sunsword who was missing from the prior build as well as her missing equipment.

Patch 0.2.2.name: Patch 0.2.2
Patch 0.2.2.text:
Welcome to an Ember content release as part of our ongoing Alpha One test process. This update focuses on the city of Ordain and support for the Crucible game system.

Compatibility

Ember patch 0.2.2 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.346 or higher and either:

  • D&D5E system version 5.0.4 or higher.

  • Crucible system version 0.7.5 or higher.

Important Playtest Instructions

The major focus of this release is the addition of preliminary Crucible support to Ember's Chapter 1 gameplay experience!

Read the Crucible Playtest information for some context and recommendations about the current focus of Crucible system testing!

This update is a little light on additions of major new game content because:

  1. The core focus for this update was on Crucible Chapter 1 compatibility and Crucible system improvement.

  2. The creative team has been very hard at work creating Chapter 3 main quests which are well underway. Stay tuned near the end of July or early August for a big Chapter 3 content drop!

Crucible support

Gameplay support for playing portions of Chapter 1 using Crucible has been added to the Ember experience! Each of the three Chapter 1 quests has certain events that are designated as "Phase 2+ Crucible" with a P2C development tag. These events are ones that are intentionally converted and designed to be experienced using the Crucible system. We hope that by the end of July the entirety of Chapter 1 will be Crucible-enabled.

Crucible Specific Changes

  • Convert a significant number of events from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai]{The Winding Trail}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl]{Ooze Control}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon} quests to be designed specifically for Crucible play.

  • Convert a large number of Actors that appear in Chapter 1 to be designed specifically for Crucible.

  • Extensive additions to the Crucible Adversary Options compendium pack for building Ember creatures in Crucible. (this pack is only visible if you are using the Crucible system).

  • Improve the actor spawn algorithm used to place tokens into area maps to account for creature size (required for Crucible) and obtain better results.

Content Improvements

  • Clarify the identity of the Adult Suarrok and the Adult Pallid Drake in the Collapsed Cairn event.

  • Add interactivity to Corpin Sanctuary for destroying the Profane Altar and for interacting with the Pathways Elevator.

  • Improve the rune-lock puzzle in the Lightless Halls to properly shuffle the runes on the floor.

  • Correct naming of "Kelmezian" culture throughout.

  • Correct the sizing of the Aedir Signalpost maps to include the extra 200px of map background that was incorrectly omitted.

  • Automatically start "Dusktide Rising" upon the completion of "Dusktide Revelry".

  • Automatically discover Helkas upon the completion of "Arrival at Helkas".

  • Three new background character portraits for Burnished Hand members.

Technical Improvements

  • Implement extensible framework for one-time world data migrations.

  • Downsize assets in the Golden Flats spritesheet which are unnecessarily large.

  • When character creation is completed for a new character, prompt online GM users whether they want to add that new PC to the Party.

  • Migrate dnd5e attunement identifiers to conform with crucible ones, i.e. emberMayis rather than emberAttunementMayis.

  • Continued functionality and performance improvements for region map batched light sources.

  • Fix a bug with D&D background feature creation which prevented them from being correctly associated with background advancement

Patch 0.3.0.name: Patch 0.3.0
Patch 0.3.0.text:
Welcome to an Ember content release as part of our ongoing Alpha Two test process. This update focuses on the city of Ordain and support for the Crucible game system.

Compatibility

Ember patch 0.3.0 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.347 or higher and either:

  • D&D5E system version 5.1.8 or higher.

  • Crucible system version 0.7.8 or higher.

Welcome to Alpha Two!

With this patch, we are now in the "Alpha Two" phase of Ember's development. In practice, this isn't that different from Alpha One, it just means we are marginally closer to where we need to be in order to welcome our Kickstarter beta backers.

Updated Timelines

Beta One will begin once we have completed the entirety of Chapter 3 content and added some of the other foundational game systems that are necessary for Ember gameplay. We are anticipating that we can begin Beta One sometime in October (initially stated as September).

After our Kickstarter backers have had a period of exclusive Beta access, we will begin selling optional paid beta test access upgrades for Kickstarter backers or other pre-purchasers who do not have Beta access. This period of buy-in Beta access will likely begin in late November around which time our team will be at PAX Unplugged in Philadelphia showing off Ember to the masses!

Chapter 3

The pinnacle feature of this big update is the addition of four main quests which form the heart of Chapter 3 gameplay. These four quests are summarized below. These quests are implemented (for now) with support for D&D5E play, with Crucible support for them coming later in our development process. Our team is incredibly proud of what we've put together with this section of gameplay and we hope you love playing these incredible quests as much as our team loved creating them.

Minor Spoilers

The following summaries contain light spoilers for chapter 3 main quests. If you are wanting to avoid any information about the main plot you should skip reading the next few paragraphs and advance to the "Area Maps" section of the patch notes.

The Expedition Challenge

Shortly after the party reaches the glittering city of Ordain and begins exploring the metropolis, they are approached by the famous Anachraenum adventurer Fernis Ossa, who has been keeping track of their exploits in the Arctus Plateau. Fernis is impressed by the party's skills and convictions, but more importantly, she has a task and request for the party that no one else in the city can complete.

Fernis reveals that two years ago, the Guildmaster of the Anachraenum died under mysterious circumstances. Since that time, changes among the Anachraenum organization have left Fernis feeling troubled. To discover what happened, she needs outsiders to join the Anachraenum and help her. A timely opportunity to do this presents itself in the form of the upcoming "Expedition Challenge", a spectacular celebration and test for aspiring Anachraenum members to prove their adventuring mettle. In exchange for their assistance, Fernis offers the party access to her former stronghold called the Concourse Hideout. This reward does not come freely, however. The Concourse has recently become overrun by the "Toothbreakers", a violent criminal organization that now controls that waterfront district.

In "The Expedition Challenge", the party learns of Fernis' suspicions, aids the famous adventurer by reclaiming the Concourse Hideout, and enters the Expedition Challenge to compete alongside rival teams of Anachraenum aspirants. Should the party prevail and prove victorious in that challenge they will forge their names in history alongside the Anachraenum's most famous members.

Disgraced House

In the wake of her uncle Darius' murder, the disappearance of her brother Funar, and the expulsion of Trading House Cevher from the Ordinate, Lyla Cevher is determined to right the wrongs done to her family and repair the damage to House Cevher's good name. But she can't do it alone. Lyla reaches out to your party for help - to investigate the murder, track down her brother's whereabouts, and find who or what is behind the assault on all things Cevher.

After investigating the scene of the crime, tracking Funar Cevher's current whereabouts, and learning more about the head of a rival Trading House, the place to help Lyla accomplish all her goals is clear- the annual Marlstone Gala, an event where the who's who of Ordain comes out to see and be seen. Together with Lyla and any allies they can recruit, the party will have to pull off a heist, right underneath their enemy's nose.

No heist is easy, especially not under the bright lights of Ordain - the party must scout the location, find a way into the party, use the glitz and glamour as a cover to move throughout the massive Marlstone Manor, and make their way into its hidden depths and their incredible dangers. Along the way, they can uncover not only what is truly happening to House Cevher, but also what lies beneath the glittering surface of one of Ordain's most exclusive nights.

Spreading Sickness

During their time in Ordain, the party is duly summoned to the Hallows to once again join forces with Ankarist of the Veiled Chain. Their mission: to investigate a new and dangerous sickness that has appeared in the city. This situation is of critical importance, and the characters must learn of a new, dangerous sickness that has appeared in Ordain. Already spread thin due to other issues in the city, the Veiled Chain now relies on the help of the party to make the difference where they can't. However, this problem is not as simple as it seems, and old enemies lurk in dark, forgotten places within Ordain.

Vetted by Ankarist and proven by their previous actions, the party is given the autonomy to conduct their investigation as they see fit. The Chain is stretched thin, and Ankarist will conduct his own investigation while the party chases down their leads. Will the party make the right choices? Can they find every clue needed to stop the plots of foes hidden in Ordain’s alleys and parlors, or will they find themselves in over their heads?

In “Spreading Sickness,” the party is drawn into a troubling web of plots meant to destabilize and destroy Ordain from within. As their investigation unfolds, they begin to uncover a deeper conspiracy that seeks to manipulate, kidnap, and turn the people of Ordain against each other. Allies are few, support is thin, and danger grows in every shadow and alley as the party draws closer to the source the spreading sickness.

Smoldering Cinders

Strange things are afoot in the great city of Ordain, and it's up to the party to find out precisely why … Shortly after their arrival to the Arctus Plateau's storied metropolis, the characters join their ally Sin Marmot at Cindarin Temple to witness the eager druid's timely initiation into the order of Cindaric Sages. It is a triumphant day for the adventurers — full of pomp, celebration, and warm welcomes. And while Sin is ushered into her first official assignment at the Old City Library, the characters are invited to explore Ordain on their own, where new opportunities await discovery within the city's magnificent urban sprawl.

A few days later, however, the characters will receive a distressed message from one of the Cindarics that sets them on a collision course with one of the most devious plots the Plateau has ever reckoned with. Two separate encounters with the living dead in two disparate city districts will propel Sin Marmot and the party on a mission to unravel a mystery that lurks at the heart of her beloved order of Cindaric Sages. Along the way, they'll meet priests, gods, and monsters the likes of which they've never seen.

What begins with the druid's initiation into the Cindaric order ends in a perilous confrontation with a surreptitious enemy from a foreign land. During the course of this adventure, the party will learn about the Cindaric Sages and their tenets, and will quickly find themselves at the forefront of Sin's struggles as a novice Cindaric. Do the characters have what it takes to aid the young druid in her most desperate time of need and halt the rise of this furtive undead menace? The party's timely intervention will be crucial to stem the tide of unforeseen change within the ranks of Ordain's most trusted sages.

Other New Content

These four new quests are supported by a ton of content that is involved in their gameplay and exploration of Ordain.

Area Maps

14 spectacular explorable areas with gorgeous maps, special visual effects, interactive elements, and compelling mechanical gameplay. Each of the following scenes is designed to pull you into the lore and world of Ember as you explore the city of Ordain.

  • Biome Map: Ordain Docks (13 composition variants)

  • Biome Map: Ordain Flats (two compositions, many more coming!)

  • Biome Map: Ordain Spires (one composition, many more coming!)

  • Location Map: Oldcraft Lodge

  • Location Map: Toothbreaker Hideout

  • Location Map: Jekeroka Villa

  • Location Map: Chamber of Agaseros (x3 levels of an interconnected dungeon)

  • Location Map: Forgotten Cistern

  • Location Map: Lantern Roads

  • Location Map: Marlstone (x2 levels of an interconnected area)

  • Location Map: Ordain Burial Grounds

These and several other pre-existing area maps have been converted to use KTX2 textures instead of the prior format we were using, improving their rendering performance.

Audio

Five beautiful new music themes that you will encounter during Chapter 3 or can listen to by manually playing them in the Ember soundscape controls.

  • Seydiri Theme music

  • Marlstone Gala music

  • Tension variants for Ordain Flats, Ordain Spires, and Ordain Docks.

Each new area map (mentioned above) features an environment ambience that immerses you and your players in the exploration of that scene.

Added special audio cues for a number of interactive elements.

Creatures

A swathe of 23 inventive and devious new creatures with which to torment your party:

  • Anachraenum Aetherial

  • Animated Rune Tome

  • Corpuleth

  • Harrower

  • Ix'erax

  • Meri

  • Mutagist Excisor

  • Mutagist Grenadier

  • Mutagist Bombardier

  • Mutagist Vivisector

  • Ordani Ruffian

  • Radiant Ultra Drake

  • Raster Thorn

  • Scalemaw

  • Shade of Agaseros

  • Toothbreaker Thug

  • Toothbreaker Scaletamer

  • Vampyre Spawn

  • Vespian Hydral

  • Wandren Patroller

  • Wandren Tracer

  • Wandren Watcher

Characters

A host of 18 exceptional new characters, each with corresponding artwork, biographies, and more!

  • Adelyne Goss

  • Arcos Sarinland

  • Fernis Ossa

  • Amelia Naxan

  • Jon Vastil

  • Vinarith

  • Lilla Arien

  • Sionia

  • Hephiss Wandren

  • Conaris Haid

  • Funar Cevher

  • Janix Mance

  • Eamon Mariflor

  • Eveis Brightstone

  • Raster Thorn

  • Del Kalais

  • Desham Phos

  • Serethus

Vistas

The spectacular new "Ordain Streets" vista depicts a wide variety of outdoor areas in the city of Ordain. This vista initially offers six different compositions, each of which are beautiful ways to showcase Ordain, but we'll be adding many more Ordain Streets compositions as we continue developing content in the city. The spritesheet used for this vista contains a ridiculous 629 individual assets which can be placed!

The beautiful "Arbore Sanctorus" vista is added to the game, this scene isn't used during Chapter 3 content, but the artwork is finished so we're letting you have it early. Be inspired! Be teased! Be … slightly spoilered.

Other vista improvements include:

  • Added three new high-detail and 25 distant detail Ordani commonfolk portraits who can be included in Vistas.

  • Added the adorable "Sunflower Bush Thornling" as a background character that can be included in Vistas to delight your players.

New Features

In addition to these massive content additions, the 0.3.0 update has a bunch of new features to note:

Dynamic Tokens

  • When placing a new Token which has a random dynamic token configuration into a Scene, pre-randomize the appearance of that Token so that all players experience the same appearance for each Token in the Scene. This includes the tokens placed when a gameplay event is spawned, so now you and all your players will see the same looking characters rather than seeing aesthetically different randomizations.

  • Human-type hairstlyes (used by Human, Drakon, Altyra, Fej, Kivahr, Nir'ae, and Signborn) now have two-tone color combinations allowing for a highlight color in addition to the hair's base color.

  • The animation framework for the dynamic token has been optimized for better performance across a variety of performance modes. This makes including a large number of dynamic tokens in your scenes more realistic from a performance perspective.

  • Add a framework for the Dynamic Token Maker to migrate preexisting dynamic token data for part name changes or other alterations which require data compatibility.

Event System

  • Configured encounter spawn groups can now condition on specific event outcomes for more fine-grained control over how an event spawns.

D&D Integration

  • Improved resting integration with the new D&D party sheet added in system version 5.2.0.

  • Automatically configure some D&D system settings on first Ember import, like using milestone progression or requiring party rest rather than individual character rest.

  • Integrate Ember's travel paces into the D&D party sheet, now allowing each caravan to choose between Hidden, Slow, Normal, Fast, and Reckless paces - which have impacts on your group's movement speed but also the probability of certain events happening!

Crucible Integration

  • Dynamic tokens for small ancestries like Thornling and Keth are now upscaled in Crucible to compensate for the size of their mechanical hitbox (3x3) being smaller than a medium sized creature.

Codex

  • Complete creature and character biographies are now visible to gamemasters in the Codex instead of only the public player-facing summaries. This allows GMs to use the Codex as a reading and review tool to learn about all the creatures and characters in Ember.

  • Improve the Codex to present Gamemasters with full text details for Biomes and Locations in the Discoveries tab.

  • Improve the layout of the Codex to ensure that the central panel is scrollable to support long-form text.

Content Creation

  • Manually placed AmbientLight documents now automatically link to the closest parallax layer based on their configured elevation!

  • Improve the workflow for replacing static Actor portrait and prototype token texture files when an Ember Dynamic Token is updated.

UI Changes

  • Eliminate the EmberEventsControl application (the event prompt window at the bottom of the screen) in favor of folding discovery and event controls into the EmberCalendarNavigation application (the Ember-specific calendar and timekeeping UI element at the top of the screen).

Bug Fixes

This update also fixes a number of bugs:

  • Blood Sense (Crucible) now correctly removes the banes that were otherwise accrued from the blinded condition.

  • When spawning an event that automatically creates a combat encounter, ensure that the actorId of each Combatant is populated so that players have permission to roll their own initiative.

  • The Fulgurite Blades were not automatically spawned in the Lunar Awakenings scene (now they are).

  • Fix an audio bug with compositions configured to possibly use zero layers which prevented zero from ever being chosen.

  • Fix bug related to parallax transformation of a light source that had no background mesh.

  • When initializing the Ember game make sure that all players have Ownership of the Party actor.

  • Fixed an issue which occured when closing and then re-opening character creation on the token configuration tab.

  • Fix bug which prevented the Codex from rendering properly in Crucible due to differences in its Actor data model.

Patch 0.3.1.name: Patch 0.3.1
Patch 0.3.1.text:
Welcome to an Ember content release as part of our ongoing Alpha Two test process. This update focuses on adding some missing features and bug fixes from our prior 0.3.0 update. We are focused on stability and polish as we work towards the start of Beta testing later in the year.

Compatibility

Ember patch 0.3.1 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.348 or higher and either:

  • D&D5E system version 5.1.8 or higher.

  • Crucible system version 0.7.8 or higher.

New Features

The 0.3.1 update has a bunch of new features to note:

Actors

Several new or updated Actors which are ready to use including:

  • Anachraenum Adventurer (CR4)

  • Burnished Hand Protector (CR3)

  • Cindaric Sage (CR6)

  • Flameguard Crusader (CR3)

  • Flameguard Firebrand (CR1)

  • Trickadee (CR0)

  • Vampyre Spawn (CR5)

Additionally, some new character portrait artwork is available in the game for the following characters:

  • Eveis Brightstone

  • Mug & Cap - Named variants of the Anachraenum Adventurer

  • Sin Marmot - Alternate outfit wearing Cindaric Initiate regalia

  • Luna Kerrowrath - Updated portrait to reflect new Lumek styles

  • Fernis Ossa - Updated portrait to reflect a less youthful appearance

Area Maps

  • A brand new two-level area map: Traveler's Rest Healing House and the corresponding Traveler's Rest Basement. This map depicts a notable landmark in the Westgate district of Ordain which appears specifically in the gameplay of "The Secret Autopsy" event in the "Smoldering Cinders" quest line.

  • The framework used to automatically adjust the appearance of placed light sources according to the time of day has been ported from Vistas to be generally usable in Area Maps also. This allows us to finely tune the lighting palette for exterior maps depending on the darkness level with smooth interpolation of light source animation instead of relying on abrupt on/off thresholds.

  • Added water flow and foam particles to the Water Rising and Flood composition variants of the Splinter Canyons area map.

  • Prototype two new light source coloration techniques: "Adaptive Attenuation" and "Natural Attenuation" which can produce more realistic (subjectively) looking light sources. We will be refining and perfecting these new coloration techniques to become core Foundry VTT options in Version 14.

Audio

  • Added "Ankarist's Theme", our first specialized Character Theme to Ember's soundtrack! This musical theme will be used in events and moments where the party is specifically interacting with Ankarist during social moments. Similar character themes for Lyla and Sin are coming soon!

  • Add some new and improved sound effects to The Lightless Halls for use when exploring that area map or interacting with objects within it.

Crucible

  • Add new Crucible conversion support to a number of additional events in Chapter 1, largely focused on the beginning events of "The Winding Trail" and "Over the Moon" quest lines.

  • Add forward-compatible configuration of crucible languages and configure Cultures to grant languages as part of Crucible character creation. This feature will require Crucible version 0.8.0 (not yet released) to fully function.

Codex

  • Improve the sizing rules used for portraits in the codex to better accommodate character portraits that are especially wide.

Dynamic Tokens

  • We now automatically associate the randomized appearance of a dynamic token with the image presented on the character sheet for that unlinked synthetic actor, ensuring that when you open the character sheet for a token placed on the map, its appearance matches what is depicted in the Scene.

  • Add support for part rarities and exclusivity in Dynamic Token configuration which controls the visibility and adjusts the randomization weight of specific part options. For example, without this feature it would be the case that randomized characters would almost always be wearing some form of eyewear. Now, with this change, eyewear is relatively more rare such that "None" is now more likely to be chosen.

Event System

  • Redesign the way that all EmberSceneManager subclasses declare biome and location information to ensure that the correct location audio is playing for all scenes. Currently some vistas are bugged and don't play the right audio.

  • Improve the rendering of the Flowchart page of every quest to differentiate certain connections depending on the prerequisite mode of the target event using solid (prerequisite ALL), dashed (prerequisite ANY), or dotted lines (prerequisite NONE).

Quests and Events

  • Substantial cleaning up of loose ends in the newly released Chapter 3 main quests including: "Disgraced House", "Smoldering Cinders", "Spreading Sickness", and "The Expedition Challenge".

  • "Clearing the Rubble" and "Lending A Hand" now automatically prompt the GM offering a choice to automatically re-combine the party with the Strayhearth Caravan upon event completion.

  • "The Smoke Clears" event now should ensures that the Party token is placed on the region map in Helkas if it was not previously present.

  • In the "Ancient Door" event of "The Winding Trail", automatically switch the vista composition to the open doorway once the relevant event outcome has been marked as complete.

  • Ensure that the "Sealed Passage" event in "Over the Moon" can no longer happen if the party has already completed "A Promised Exit" in "The Winding Trail".

  • Add a Macro that can be used to destroy and remove certain pieces of Corpuleth equipment (Helm or Chestplate) during combat. This macro is especially useful during the "Grave Assignments" event of the "Smoldering Cinders" quest.

  • Ensure that the newly placed Party token at the end of "The Collapsed Cairn" also becomes automatically controlled.

Region Map

  • Convert rendering of the region map from using WEBP tiles to instead using ultra-optimized KTX2 tiles using high quality UASTC format. This change results in the region map files being larger and therefore requiring more loading time over network, but we feel strongly that the visual improvement of fidelity on the region map is absolutely worth it as the rendered quality of the megaregion is now sharper and more beautiful than ever!

  • Convert the dashed lines visualized in the EmberEventsLayer to use the built-in PIXI dashed line shader instead of manually managed dashed graphics.

  • Add animation to the dashed lines that connect quest events in the EmberEventsLayer to more elegantly visualize the directional flow of quest content.

Vistas

  • Added a beautiful new location vista for "Caste". This is a remote settlement in the northeast of the Arctus Plateau which you cannot visit during this phase of Alpha testing yet, but you can enjoy the moody visuals of the vista as something to look forward to as our gameplay content progresses.

  • Added day/night cycle appearance rules for the Ordain Streets vista as well as light sources to various vista compositions which adapt to the time of day.

Bug Fixes

This update also fixes a number of bugs:

  • Corrected the color alignment of the visible ooze in Yakoshta Mine to shift from green to orange to match the contamination in the Aedir Signalpost.

  • D&D5E: Wirrun characters now properly obtain Cold resistance from their ancestry progression.

  • Crucible: Correct bug with Crucible implementation of Kivahr Regulated Rhythm which caused it to apply every turn regardless of whether the effect was active or not.

  • Crucible: Add automation for the Vrjnhar ancestral passive that properly allows them to ignore glancing blows.

  • Crucible: Fix a lingering bug that prevented rendering of the Codex.

Patch 0.3.2.name: Patch 0.3.2
Patch 0.3.2.text:
Welcome to an Ember content release as part of our ongoing Alpha Two test process.

Our team is working hard to get Ember ready for Beta One which we expect will begin with the next major patch, version 0.4.0. Much of our work in this update 0.3.2 involves getting the game ready for beta testing by adding missing features, material, and game systems that are needed for Beta.

Compatibility

Ember patch 0.3.2 requires core Foundry VTT version 13.348 or higher (version 13.350 is recommended) and:

  • D&D5E system version 5.1.9 or higher.

  • Crucible system version 0.7.9 or higher.

Highlights

The most significant highlights of this new release are the following:

  • The region map of Ordain is brought to life in beautiful high-resolution detail.

  • Implement a brand new Dynamic Weather Engine for Ember which simulates the evolution of local weather effects that vary across the mega-region.

  • Overhaul the Ember-specific Calendar UI element at the top of the screen with a new beautiful aesthetic which is also more functional.

  • Significant expansions and refinements of our Setting Compendium with a focus on Ancestries, Organizations, and Cultures.

New Features

All the new features included in this update are detailed in the sections below.

Area Maps

  • Add a new area map called "The Bronze Rask", which depicts a theater in the Ordain district of Fallbrook. This area is used in the final segment of Ankarist's Chapter 3 main quest.

  • Added a full area walkthrough for all rooms and sections of "The Bronze Rask" area map.

Audio

  • Add a beautiful new musical theme for Sin Marmot, one of the game's main quest companion characters, which is used during events where interaction with Sin is the central focus.

  • Implement a framework for region map caravan movement sound effects which help annotate the environmental sound composition while the party is moving. Currently there is only one experimental sound effect used here, but eventually the audio side of this system will evolve to provide different sound effects according to the party's method of travel and the terrain over which they are traveling.

Characters and Creatures

  • Update the character portrait for Sigil with a new version which better reflects the unique attributes of "The Elder Scholar".

  • Add background character artwork for Gabi and Brandt Hargrove, the Arcturian farmers encountered during "The Boy Who Played With Boats" event of the "Book of Tales" quest. Further work on this event is anticipated in the subsequent patch to implement a vista configuration which showcases these portraits effectively.

Quests

  • Expanded the dialog and Q&A sections of the first few events of "The Winding Trail" to add more characterization to our main quest companion NPCs.

Region Map

  • The region map of Ordain is brought to life in beautiful high-resolution detail with customized illustrated detail for every district.

  • The lighting of Ordain has been updated to reflect the new artwork and utilize new beautiful and vibrant light source coloration techniques.

  • Implement a brand new "Dynamic Weather Engine" for Ember which simulates the evolution of local weather effects that vary across the mega-region.

  • Regional weather effects can be visualized and controlled (to a degree) by the Gamemaster using the new "Toggle Weather Overlay" control in the Scene Controls palette on the left side of the screen.

  • Add attenuated coloration techniques to region map optimized light sources.

  • Improve the technical framework used to evolve the global light angle according to the time of day, enabling us to deploy this same system for vistas and area maps in addition to the region map.

Players/Gamemasters Guide

  • Write the "Main Quest Overview" page of the Gamemaster's Guide to improve existing structure, add section for Chapter 3, and "Chapter 4 and Beyond" section.

  • Update the Player's Guide writing for the Ember Region map with expansions and corrections to existing material as well as new written rules explaining how travel pace selection works.

Setting Compendium

  • Add a beautiful new banner for Luxarum that depicts the "Realm of Endless War".

  • Add support for Ember Lore pages to define secondary titles used for monikers or epithets which are displayed as subtitles underneath their page title.

  • Updates to the Organization: Ordinate article with new material about the composition of the Ordinate and its functions.

  • Ongoing work to overhaul and expand the "Character Classes" entry of the Setting Compendium with more information that pertains to how D&D system classes would manifest within the Ember setting.

Tokens

  • Prototype a new "Undead Monster" token maker template with parts that consolidate Horrendor, Sodden Corpse, Skallith, and Corpuleth parts into a single shared structure.

  • Add new splint mail armor pieces to the Token Maker.

UI and UX

  • Overhaul the Ember-specific Calendar UI element at the top of the screen with a new beautiful aesthetic which is also more functional. The calendar now reports individual local weather events and your current location.

  • Prompt the Gamemaster and require reimport the Ember Adventure when migrating from a prior Ember world version.

  • Prompt the Gamemaster to conclude or cancel an in-progress Ember gameplay event before re-importing the Ember adventure.

  • Add support for flag-based development status tags for page types that are not owned by Ember.

  • Allow using the Hex HUD to target a hex as the target for a Teleport Destination or Weather Creation dialog.

Vistas

  • Support skewing vista assets with an alternative skew model (shear) better suited for this 2d use case.

  • Asset improvements for the Verdant Paths vista with new improved terrain, ground cover, and some prefab assets.

  • Implement the "Dry Outpost" and "Dry Outpost Camp" vista compositions in the "Verdant Paths" vista which are used in the "Skies Above" event of "The Winding Trail".

Crucible System

  • Ongoing conversion efforts to refine and polish Chapter 1 gameplay content for Crucible. Most game events are now fully converted, although need final review and balancing passes.

  • Design integration between Ember's envisioned Gathering and Crafting system with the new Schematic item type introduced in the Crucible system with update version 0.7.9.

D&D System

  • Upgrade the way that Knowledge areas are provided via D&D background components with a new bespoke advancement type that more seamlessly integrates that feature with the game system.

  • Extend the D&D character sheet to report Knowledge areas that the character possesses alongside other traits like Languages.

Bug Fixes

  • The Ordani Skywalk artwork needs to be always visible or revealed from one hex away so that players know there is a crossing point over the canyons.

  • Completion of "Amazing Brambles" should unlock the ability to travel to/from the pathways in that particular hex.

  • Fix an issue which caused the underground lake section of the Mycelian Expanse is incorrectly closed in by walls and impassable hexes such that the party cannot enter or exit it.

The Villains.name: The Villains
The Villains.text:
Significant Spoilers

This page contains significant spoilers for the plot of Ember, A Shard of Fear. We recommend for a Gamemaster to read it so that you have an understanding of the primary villains of the campaign and their motivations.

Some Gamemasters, however, may prefer not to have this full knowledge — so proceed only if you wish to have all the available information up-front instead of learning things as you play.

Zerranyss

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.EhQnCUxkJyxOSbf7]{Vile Dragon} known as @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss} is the principal antagonist and central villain of our story. Zerranyss is motivated above all else by a cruel and selfish desire to accumulate vast power, which he would use to establish a malicious dominion over Ember and its denizens.

Zerranyss also seeks revenge against the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}, who once nearly killed the Vile Dragon in a battle at the frontier of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Homelands. After being defeated and disgraced in this way, Zerranyss has grown more disdainful and cruel, using bitter resentment against Lumé and others to drive them down the path of conquest. Zerranyss is a cunning and conniving villain, forming and orchestrating a complex strategy to undermine and subvert power in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} — one of the great cities of the world and most importantly an access point to the underground Shard Caverns wherein Zerranyss believes a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal} of Ember may be found. Such a crystal would allow Zerranyss to perform an ascension ritual which — if successful — would imbue the formidable dragon with the untold power of a Shard God.

Zerranyss is first encountered in his human guise as @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith} during Chapter 3. Vinarith does not come across as a villain; in fact, he could be roleplayed as an earnest and hardworking man. While it's important that the characters don't immediately suspect Vinarith as a villain, it's nearly impossible for the party to understand just how critical this character is in the grand scheme of the overarching story. So some suspicion of his actions is perfectly acceptable if they question some of his actions.

A Complex Strategy

The player characters enter the story at a point where @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss} has already been hard at work, carefully constructing a strategy that would see him triumph over his enemies. Each of the schemes in this elaborate plot plays some particular role in the plan to usurp Ordain and the surrounding region. Zerranyss has several primary goals:

  1. Seize control over the Great City of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, its resources, power, and influence, and gain unrestricted access to the Shard Caverns below.

  2. Locate an elusive @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal} within the vast Shard Caverns by capturing and enslaving mortals and forcing them to mine the Pathways beneath the city.

  3. Obtain secret knowledge on how to undertake what Zerranyss calls "the Ritual of Ascension," by procuring knowledge from other beings who possess an extensive understanding of the process.

  4. Grow in strength to withstand the traumatic and deadly Ritual using experimentation and the formulation of the Mutagen by his @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]{Mutagist} followers.

The Inner Circle

These nefarious machinations are overseen by a cadre of loyal lieutenants pledged to serve Zerranyss. The most impactful of which are listed below, but others willingly serve the dragon or are keen to exploit the chaos his plans will bring about.

  • @UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]{Serethus}, an ingenious alchemist and leader of the nefarious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]{Mutagists}.

  • @UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan}, a Blood Baron necromancer and fellow enemy of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}.

  • @UUID[Actor.fcK7WLaLCCcMP9oL]{Pyix}, an inscrutable Tyraphem mage from Luxarum.

  • @UUID[Actor.z1Ttp0q6CAtjDphl]{Sticks}, the roguish figurehead of the mysterious Otherhood of Fortune.

  • @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver}, the stoic commander of the Burnished Hand, who Zerranyss will attempt to corrupt throughout the campaign's events.

Controlling the Ordinate

Gaining control of Ordain is a complex challenge, because the city is governed by a triarchy of organizations called the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate}, which is comprised of representatives from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}, and the Combined Trading Houses comprised of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{House Lilifeld}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{House Salva} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{House Wandren}. Controlling Ordain requires controlling the Ordinate — or a sufficient majority of it to wrest control from any remaining opposition. Zerranyss' strategy to control the Ordinate involves the following crucial steps:

  1. Gain a seat on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate} personally under the guise of @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith}, a leading member of the Cindaric Sages. At the start of the story, under his disguise as Vinarith, Zerranyss has already taken control over this seat, taking the place of the elderly current Holy Speaker of the Sages who is too ill to leave the Cindaric Temple.

  2. Secure another of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} seats through the corruption of @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver}, commander of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}. At the beginning of the story, this has not yet been accomplished, but as events unfold, it is virtually inevitable, as Steros is, unfortunately, highly susceptible to manipulation.

  3. Destabilize the Trading Houses by provoking infighting among the houses through lies, manipulation, and outright violence. Zerranyss uses the Tyraphem @UUID[Actor.fcK7WLaLCCcMP9oL]{Pyix} to gain control over @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{House Wandren}, while using @UUID[Actor.z1Ttp0q6CAtjDphl]{Sticks} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune} to gain leverage over @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}. As the story unfolds, Pyix manages to implicate @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher} in a grand conspiracy that causes chaos among the trading houses.

  4. Use @UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]{Serethus} to misinform and misdirect among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} to prevent law enforcement from interrupting or thwarting the scheme and keep the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows} distracted.
