Foundry Virtual Tabletop version 14 is not yet stable, although it is close. It is in the final stages of "User Testing" with the most recent release https://foundryvtt.com/releases/14.358 being similar to this one as potentially a final pre-stable test.

You should absolutely not immediately update your main Foundry VTT environment to version 14. Instead, testing version 14 and this version of Ember should happen in a separate test environment.

Version 13

It is not possible to test Ember version 0.4.7 with Version 13. If you want to remain testing in Version 13, you should stay on Ember version 0.4.6 or earlier.

Compatibility

Ember patch 0.4.7 requires core Foundry VTT version 14.358 or higher and:

  • D&D5E system pre-release version 5.3.0 or higher. Currently at the time of this release, there is no public installation option for this D&D system pre-release, but it can be manually installed from manifest URL https://github.com/foundryvtt/dnd5e/releases/download/release-5.3.0/system.json

  • Crucible system version 0.9.0 or higher which already implements support for Version 14.

Team News

Before getting into all the great content in this update, we have exciting team news to share. As many of you know, we conducted a hiring process earlier in the year to recruit a new full-time writer and designer for Ember. I am thrilled to announce the outcome of that search and welcome Jess Levine.

Jess Levine is an author, TTRPG designer, kindergarten teacher, and communist organizer. Her diverse creative interests are united by one theme: lesbians. She resides in Pittsburgh, on the occupied land of the Shawandasse Tula, Osage, and Monongahela peoples. She publishes TTRPGs as Jumpgate Games, including the CRIT Awards 2023 Best GMless Game of the Year going rogue 2e, a game of war, rebellion, and sacrifice. I Have the High Ground—her tabletop roleplaying game of banter, posturing, and capes—and her satirical scifi skirmish storytelling game PLANET FIST have been met with industry praise and player acclaim. You can find her on Bluesky as @jessfrom.online.

Jess joined up with our team this month and has already been hard at work improving the structure, presentation, and completeness of our Ember Player's Guide.

Highlights

Ember has been comprehensively overhauled to feature compatibility with Foundry VTT version 14. Some of the most notable changes that are part of this include:

  • Support for V14 Scene Levels. Not all scenes are converted yet. We are prioritizing new scenes, and conversions for old scenes as we revisit them for other gameplay reasons. Notes on which scenes have been converted are reported in the full patch notes below.

  • Region map Fog of War now uses shared fog that allows all players to share the same region exploration progress, even if someone misses a game session.

  • Ember has a new Adventure Quickstart option that makes it easy to create and jump straight into a new Ember game using either D&D or Crucible.

  • Ember is now integrated with both the D&D and Crucible game systems, especially noteworthy is that Crucible is fully V14 compatible, with a large number of new V14 features already integrated into its gameplay and automation.

Other major highlights in this update version include:

  • Complete a massive overhaul of the Ember Dynamic Token infrastructure to switch from individual ancestry-specific spritesheets to a single "mega-spritesheet" which includes all equipment and anatomy parts across all ancestries. For simple scenes, this creates a small additional performance overhead, but for complex scenes with many tokens it is a huge performance improvement.

More details on each of these highlights appear in the full notes, below.

Thank You!

Before getting into the full patch note details, I'd like to conclude by expressing a very sincere thanks to everyone who participated in our Alpha and Beta test phases. Your engagement, feedback, and encouragement have made it possible for Ember to be where it is now and will be fueling our team to keep going as we strive to complete this unprecedented game.

Features and Fixes

All the new features included in this update are detailed in the sections below.

Actors

  • Introduce several new adversaries including the Paint Globlin and the Chiaroscuran Beast.

  • Introduce several new notable characters including Mistress Caberi, Falar, and Cherish Ellerie.

  • Update language identifiers used in Ember to feature new lore-appropriate language identifiers and names. An automatic migration is in place that should auto-correct your existing playtest characters, but just in case be sure to double check your known languages. You can find updated information on the Languages page in the Players' Guide.

Area Maps

  • Introduce an expansive multi-level area map named Flotsam Canal Market. This is the first scene we worked on specifically with Version 14 levels, it features 3 levels of gameplay: Dockside, Stoneside, and Promenade. This area is beautifully animated with flowing water, bobbling boats, and all of the advantages that are unlocked by having multiple vertical slices separated as different gameplay Levels. If you are new to Version 14 this is an excellent scene to explore and discover how Scene Levels work in practice.

  • Introduce a large new area map for Redwalk Ramble which depicts a beautiful outdoor park space in Ordain's eponymous district. The map is beautifully animated with swaying trees, blustering leaves which respond to global wind conditions, flowing water, fountains, and more.

  • Create an expansive area walkthrough for Flotsam Market which is largely experienced during the Local Color quest but can be explored independently.

  • Add a water bobble sprite mesh that can be used to depict a sprite with a continuous animated bobble effect, typically used for boats or other floating objects.

  • The Verdant Paths biome area map is converted to Version 14 Scene Levels.

  • The Ordain Flats biome area map is converted to Version 14 Scene Levels.

Audio

  • Fix a bug which could cause multiple music or environment arrangements to play overtop of each other at the same time, resulting from a workflow problem during scene changes.

Crucible

  • Implement compatibility with Crucible version 0.9.0 focusing on Foundry VTT version 14.

D&D5E

  • Display pronouns configured via Ember Actor Flags on the D&D NPC sheet in the header.

  • Implement a (previously missing) bidirectional sync between D&D group actor sheet and token HUD for movement actions.

Guides

  • Accomplish a significant revision and restructuring of the Players' Guide to reorganize the way that it presents information. The new guide structure separates the presentation of information into logically separate categories for "Character Creation", "Playing the Game", and "Exploring the Setting". We have also revised the introduction and added a new "How to Use This Guide" page that should make it easier for new players to orient themselves. We aren't quite yet ready to distribute the Players' Guide in PDF format, but this is a big step on the path towards that goal.

Quests and Events

  • Introduce an entire new quest named Local Color that takes place in Chapter 3 in the city of Ordain. See the highlights section above for more detail about this quest and its narrative.

  • The Glitter in the Dark quest in Chapter 2 has been fully converted to Crucible and is ready for playtesting in the Crucible system.

  • Implemented significant refinement and rewrites to the Chapter 2 main quest An Old Friend to improve the quality and consistency of its gameplay.

  • Add 9 new standalone events ranging from Chapter 1 to Chapter 3 that provide bite-sized elements of gameplay to better populate areas of the world and reinforce gameplay themes. These events are specifically: Pollen Storm, In the Behemoth's Wake, Arcane Maelstrom, Sanguinary Salutations, Dangerous Descent, Flash Flood, The Giants' Span, Shent Observatory, and Voices in the Square.

  • Fix a bug which silently prevented adding tracked outcomes to standalone events.

  • Allow encounter configurations attached to quest and standalone events to spawn actors across multiple levels of a scene to fully populate multi-level environments where we previously had to rely on special case logic.

Region Map

  • The Ember Region Map has been converted to Version 14 Scene Levels! Instead of having a bespoke system for "slices" — vertical layers for the Surface and the Pathways — we now use native Levels for this. This changes the UI/UX for how the Gamemaster and Players can navigate levels. You can now easily swap your viewed level using the Scene Navigation element. Players can see which level others are viewing. The Gamemaster can move a token between levels using the Token HUD.

  • Scene Regions and Notes are now associated with the specific level they pertain to. This has the advantage of showing — in the Pathways — which points of interest allow an opportunity to return to the Surface.

  • Fix a bug with double shadows created by dynamic party tokens on the Region Map, groups using a dynamic token for their party banner will now properly produce only a single shadow.

Tokens

  • Complete a massive overhaul of the Ember Dynamic Token infrastructure to switch from individual ancestry-specific spritesheets to a single "mega-spritesheet" which includes all equipment and anatomy parts across all ancestries. For simple scenes, this creates a small additional performance overhead, but for complex scenes with many tokens it is a huge performance improvement. Our new mega-spritesheet textures are optimized in GPU-friendly UASTC format and scenes which a large number of dynamic tokens will experience both improved rendering performance AND increased visual quality. A significant consequence of this is that part names used in the token maker have changed their naming conventions somewhat. We apply automatic migrations to convert old token data into the new specification, but its definitely a good idea to check your own characters' dynamic token configurations to make sure they are still rendered properly.

  • Complete the process of re-assigning held token equipment to all characters and humanoid creatures. The characters you encounter and adversaries you face should now be holding sensible items.

  • Dynamic party banner tokens now support different "stances" for land and water movement, and will perform an automatic base swap between a land base and a water base depending on the terrain of the hex they move through.

  • Fix a bug which caused customization of the Party banner token to be incorrectly saved to the Ember module directory instead of to the user's custom World asset path.

Vistas

  • Implement a spectacular new vista for Cindarin Temple, a cornerstone landmark in Ordain and an essential location for one of our main quest arcs (Sin Marmot).

  • Add a new Golden Flats vista composition for "Nain Outskirts".

  • Add a new Ordain Streets vista composition for "Dockside Street".

  • Add a new Ordain Streets vista composition for "Huge Mural".

  • Add a new Ordain Interiors vista composition for "Cherish's Office".

  • Redesign the way that Vista Compositions work to instead become Version 14 Scene Levels. Each composition is a different level of the vista scene (parallel slices of the world, rather than vertically stacked ones), and custom vista compositions can be created and customized as custom levels.

  • Convert the Verdant Paths vista to use Version 14 levels instead of bespoke compositions.

  • Convert the Dripstones vista to use Version 14 levels instead of bespoke compositions.

  • Refactor and redesign the custom Vista Configuration tool to work with the Version 14 levels-based approach to vista compositions.

Other

  • Perform a thorough HTML cleaning pass to strip inline style tags, naked span elements, non-breaking spaces, and more.

Setting Compendium

  • Updated the Cultures -> Languages page with new language names.

Patch 0.5.0.name: Patch 0.5.0
Patch 0.5.0.text:
Welcome to Ember Early Access! This update, version 0.5.0, is a minor patch that adds some final bugfixes and features added to our initial early access release.

Beginning Early Access is a huge milestone for our team and the culmination of many years of work creating Ember. We are far from done, but we can see clearly how to get from here to the final product we all dreamed of when beginning this endeavor.

For those of you who participated in our Alpha and Beta test phases, thank you so much for your feedback and encouragement. For those of you who are just beginning your Ember journey now with Early Access, welcome and we are thrilled to have you here.

Compatibility

Ember patch 0.5.0 requires core Foundry VTT version 14.359 or higher and one of:

  • D&D5E system pre-release version 5.3.0 or higher.

  • Crucible system version 0.9.0 or higher.

Version 14

Foundry Virtual Tabletop version 14 is now Stable and Ember version 0.5.0 requires Foundry VTT version 14.

Version 13

It is not possible to test Ember version 0.5.0 with Version 13. If you want to remain testing in Version 13, you should stay on Ember version 0.4.6 or earlier.

Highlights

The major highlights in this update version include:

  • 70 beautiful new illustrated token maker part options.

  • A more polished Ember import experience that integrates seamlessly with Version 14 quickstart.

  • Setting Compendium expansions with major updates to Culture pages.

More details on each of these highlights appear in the full notes, below.

Features and Fixes

All the new features included in this update are detailed in the sections below.

Actors

  • Begin loading the token maker mega spritesheet in the background when beginning character creation so that by the time you get to the Token Maker step it is available instantaneously.

  • Update Vartholomew Chess to have a more complete biography and backstory.

Area Maps

  • Provide a way in Ember to configure both default and wall-specific animation elevations for DoorMesh instances on a per-level basis.

  • Improve computation of token move speed animation in area maps, customizing the movement speed based on dominant movement action and system action economy.

  • For scenes configured with lunarAmbience: false, only reject lunar hue changes while still keeping darkness level changes (unless darkness is locked).

Crucible

  • Fix a bug with door meshes in Crucible being unreasonably oversized due to a miscalculation with the microgrid.

Quests and Events

  • Improve the reliability of the "Shadowed Depths" Event triggering after taking the Corpin Sanctuary elevator.

  • Update several encounter configurations to have better starting conditions: Sickly Drakelings, Saving Jasper, Poolside Predicaments.

Region Map

  • Restore the specialized Note visibility control that was responsible for restricting Region Map note visibility to locations that have been discovered.

  • Preserve, or re-acquire correct Token levels when re-importing the Region Map scene.

  • Harden an edge case around canvas notification for discoveries or Events that did not have a designated hex.

Tokens

  • Add 70 new dynamic token part options for equipment.

  • Improve the illustration of Keth hairstyles and collars to be more whimsical.

  • Fix scaling issues with Keth hand-held equipment.

  • Fix hair placement for Hulg'run tokens.

  • Assign better randomization probabilities to hand-held equipment so that tokens will more often have empty hands.

User Interface

  • Convert the Calendar UI to report times with "am" and "pm" designations instead of 24h time.

  • Swap the order of Calendar scene buttons to be Cosmos -> World -> Region.

Vistas

  • Improve the Dripstones Vista compositions with rebalanced lighting and more placed assets to give them a more vibrant and living feel.

  • Improve the Helkas and Yakoshta Vistas with improved lighting and corrections for certain layers that did not interact well with token movement.

  • Implement mechanics-accurate token movement speeds in Vista scenes based on the physicalVvista dimensions and perspective.

  • Convert the Helkas Vista to V14 levels.

  • Convert the Yakoshta Vista to V14 levels.

  • Improve behavior for importing and exporting custom Vista configurations.

Other

  • Implement the new V14 core feature that allows the Ember adventure importer to be eagerly rendered while the (large) adventure data is lazily loaded. This creates a much more responsive experience that is clear to the user that the importer is loading.

  • When creating an Ember quickstart world, display the "Welcome to Ember" page rather than the current version of patch notes.

  • Improve the framework for initial Ember migration on world launch to have better prevention of edge cases that could cause migration to fail.

  • Integrate Ember with a new V14 change that will allow the Ember module to remain active in the world when upgrading from V13 to V14 instead of being automatically deactivated.

Setting Compendium

General

Most culture pages have been finished, except for some of the Ancient cultures! Culture details have all been updated.

Cosmos

  • Akon, added additional information.

  • Aura, added additional information.

  • Cora, added additional information.

  • Ragen, added additional information.

  • Orbis, added additional information.

Deities

  • Themis, written and ready for playtesting.

Culture

  • Culture Overview rewritten, included a lore summary.

  • Languages revised with several changes based on cultures.

    • Kithil now speak Mithia

    • Cascilian now speak Cascal

    • Kessian now speak Solical

    • Morian now speak Moiré

    • Maziran now speak Kaziric

    • NEW Jarn speak Veax

    • NEW Theroch speak Judega

    • Daemos and Fiends now speak Eonic

    • Tyraphem and Celestials now speak Harmos

    • Casia and Fae now speak Caligon

    • NEW Carrow speak Ocana

    • NEW Xaxin speak Xaxin

  • Cascilian, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Waerd, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Tayan, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Strider, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Bejak, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Oaken, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Rhivan, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Kelmezian, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Kessian, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Varún, written and ready for playtesting.

  • Kithil, reworked.

Creation Overview.name: Creation Overview
Creation Overview.text:
Character creation is one of the most important and enjoyable parts of any tabletop roleplaying experience. Choosing your starting attributes, @UUID[.PSx7hfJjAtsASAap]{Ancestry}, @UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC]{Ember Background}, and appearance are essential choices made at the beginning of the game that influence many aspects of gameplay as well as your character's persona.

Character creation in Ember is designed to be seamless, allowing you to select options from a one list after another, but with a few important alterations from the default process for the game system you are playing.

Character Creation Process

To create a character in Ember, you will select:

@UUID[.PSx7hfJjAtsASAap]{Ancestry} which defines your character's biological heritage.

@UUID[.OvOfdskIknYM9BNr]{Character Class} which determines your heroic approach to problem solving.

@UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC#attunement]{Attunement} which selects the cosmological body your character has an affinity towards.

@UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC#culture]{Culture} which identifies the culture of the world that your character came from.

@UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC#path]{Path} which contributes to your backstory prior to the game's beginning.

@UUID[.PSx7hfJjAtsASAap]{Ancestry} which defines your character's biological heritage.

@UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC#attunement]{Attunement} which selects the cosmological entity your character has an affinity towards.

@UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC#culture]{Culture} which identifies the culture of the world that your character came from.

@UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC#path]{Path} which contributes to your backstory prior to the game's beginning.

Talents that select your character's initial capabilities.

Character Appearance

Finally, you will customize the appearance of your @UUID[.yVLwgqQAgSrEfei3]{Dynamic Token} which visually represents your character within the world.

Creating a Character

You can spend time reading about all the available character options, but our recommendation is to simply enter the character creation interface and explore as you go.

To create a new player character, click the Create Actor button at the top of the Actors sidebar tab. Created characters of the "Player Character" type will automatically enter the Character Creation workflow.

Permissions Required

If you do not have permission to perform this action, instead ask your Gamemaster to create an Actor on your behalf and assign it to you as an Owner.

Character Connections

During or after the Character Creation process, each player should decide upon their character's reason for traveling with the Strayhearth Caravan and whether or not they have any pre-existing relationship with the other players. It's not required for the player characters to know each other already — in fact, our writing assumes that they are strangers who have met upon the road.

The Strayhearth Caravan consists of three massive six-wheeled wagons, the huge @UUID[Actor.6HckJyV8TKc37xNT]{Yarnac} that serve as beasts of burden, the caravaner @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} who owns and operates the enterprise, the Signborn merchant @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]{Clipper}, and a number of @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians} along for the ride (including merchants, passengers, and the like).

Members of the Strayhearth Caravan have already been traveling together for several days, so it can be assumed that each of the player characters have already been introduced and know each other's names and likenesses. You may find it creates less pressure for the group by encouraging them to share character names and appearances out-of-character before the beginning of play; this way, everyone is already acquainted when roleplaying begins in earnest.

Choices of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000]{Culture}, @UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC#path]{Path}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0]{Ancestry}, and @UUID[.3enOmC4M2HoyTXcg]{Attunement} can inform these decisions, but you should feel free to craft a unique backstory with connections that speak directly to the character you want to portray. For instance, your character could be an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian} @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.caravanner000000]{Caravanner} on a journey back to @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}, or even a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.starDreamer00000]{Star Dreamer} from far-off @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7iZDVtrBO7326XZY]{Caren'ac} — the sky's the limit.

Once you have a rough idea for a backstory, your Character Sheet includes a Biography tab where you can write down notes or entire paragraphs of text.

It's Your Story

Please don't feel forced into making immediate backstory decisions! If you want to spend a little more time in-game trying to figure out the specifics of these inter-character connections, by all means do so. There will be plenty of time to add elements to your character's backstory while you explore the Arctus Plateau and get to know the setting more.

Gameplay Overview.name: Gameplay Overview
Gameplay Overview.text:
Ember contains a number of unique mechanics that are added on top of the game system used to play it. The most important of those mechanics are summarized below, then expanded upon in the following pages.

Gameplay Pillars

Like most tabletop roleplaying games, the fundamental experience of Ember is one in which you are presented with a situation, and asked, as your character: what do you do?

Ember's gameplay emphasizes three pillars: exploration, social interaction, and combat. The exploration pillar is the gateway by which the rest of Ember's gameplay is experienced. We have designed the World of Ember to be immersive and inviting, and your exploration of it will uniquely determine what story you experience.

Ember's core gameplay loop is:

  1. In order to discover Ember's story, accomplish your party's goals, and advance in power, you must explore the world by moving your party around Ember's massive hex-based Region Map.

  2. Whenever you move your party or otherwise pass time in the game world, there is a chance that this will trigger an Event — a specific challenge or narrative moment in Ember’s story, typically focused on one of the three pillars of exploration, social interaction, or combat.

  3. As you complete Events, you will discover important people and places, and uncover long-term mysteries.

  4. Completing Events (and the Quests that many Events belong to) will cause the story and world to evolve and your characters to increase in Level, opening doors to new gameplay.

  5. Events and their outcomes will be recorded in your Codex, leaving you with clues to pursue to continue your journey.

This loop repeats over and over, with hundreds of hours of prewritten encounters, narrative moments, and lore to discover.

The Events themselves are not just the written story moments you might expect from a prewritten adventure, but also illustrated and interactive pieces of on-screen gameplay, unique to Ember's deep integration with Foundry. Events might include, among other features:

  • @UUID[.lNMkySfNYWS3EvIk]{Area Maps} which are top-down maps that you can explore and interact with as your individual character.

  • @UUID[.5U1FpueYTnRKzYiS]{Vistas} which are front-facing backdrops upon which characters can move about and talk to other characters.

  • Other illustrated (and even sometimes animated) creatures, characters, and environments.

Below, we'll learn a bit more about how Events are encountered through the process of exploration, and how they impact both your character and the World of Ember at large.

Region Exploration

One of the most important decisions your party will regularly make is where to travel on the Region Map, which can be viewed by clicking the ​​ icon at the top of the screen.

Your position on this map — made up of over ten thousand hexes across two vertical slices — impacts who you can talk to, where you can go next, and most importantly, what Events you might encounter.

Hexes and Fog of War

The position of your party on this map is depicted by a moveable Token with a customizable banner. While you can always see the hex that your party is in, many other hexes begin the campaign shrouded by Fog of War, which obscures the contents of that hex until your party moves close enough to see it. The terrain and elevation of a hex can affect both how far you can see, and the speed and danger of movement through that hex.

Many hexes have an associated Location to explore, or a recommended Area Map or Vista to use for scenes that take place in that hex.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.JMfEjsAuL2w9g7w5.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc]{Region Exploration} page of this guide has further details on the information above. While your Gamemaster and the Ember game itself will handle most of the details, when making decisions about movement on the Region Map, it can be useful for to fully understand what's on the map, how to interact with it, and other mechanical implications of your movement through it.

Quests and Events

Gameplay in Ember happens through Events — prewritten plot moments that involve exploration, social, or combat challenges. Events are broadly categorized as one of two types: Quest Events and Standalone Events.

Quest Events

These Events are part of a larger Quest — a series of linked Events with meaningful choices through which you forge your own unique path through the Quest. The primary story of Ember, A Shard of Fear, is told through a series of Main Quests (though your party will also have the option to engage in Side Quests along the way). Quest Events are the only source of @UUID[JournalEntry.JMfEjsAuL2w9g7w5.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points} by which you can increase your character's Level — though not all Quest Events award a Milestone Point.

Standalone Events

Standalone Events are individual encounters not directly linked to a larger thread. They do not award Milestone Points, but may benefit you in other ways.

Additionally, Events might bring you to particular illustrated scenes: Area Maps and Vistas.

Area Maps

Events that take place in an Area Map allow you move your individual Character Token around in their immediate environment, and interact directly with elements you see on screen, like puzzles and traps.

Vistas

Events that take place in a Vista show you a portrait of your character and any others nearby — all moving around on an illustrated backdrop of the local environment. Within a Vista, dialogue from an important character can even appear on screen alongside their portrait.

The@UUID[JournalEntry.JMfEjsAuL2w9g7w5.JournalEntryPage.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Quests and Events} page of this guide has further details on the information above, but as a player, you don’t need to worry about whether you’re in a Quest Event, Standalone Event, Main Quest, or Side Quest. In fact, Ember never directly tells you whether you’ve finished every Event for a particular Quest — the choices you make can have far-reaching consequences, and whether you’ve ever truly finished addressing a particular story is up to you to figure out.

The Codex

The Events you've encountered and the choices you made within them will be recorded in the Codex, alongside other important discoveries from your journey. You can view the Codex by clicking the ​​ icon at the top of the screen. The Codex has five important tabs:

Journal

The Journal tab in the Codex — separate from the Journal entries in the Foundry sidebar — tracks completed Events, including the time the party completed them, and a short summary of what happened, including important decisions made by the party.

Quest Log

The Quest Log tab displays summaries of completed Quest Events specifically, grouped by Quest, rather than a chronological list of all completed Events.

Discoveries

The Discoveries tab lists Biomes and Locations that you have encountered while exploring the Region Map, including when you first encountered them, and some detailed information on the Biome or Location.

Bestiary

The Bestiary tab lists creatures and monsters you've encountered during your game, including when you first encountered them, and some detailed information on the Biome or Location.

Characters

The Characters tab lists important characters you've met during your game, including when you first encountered them, and some biographical information, such as name, pronouns, Ancestry, Culture, their character portrait, and more.

Vistas.name: Vistas
Vistas.text:
Throughout gameplay, you will be pulled into scenes called Vistas. Vistas serve as visual representations of a place on the @UUID[.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc]{Region Map}, usually focusing on a very particular part of that place, such as a small campsite, a building, or a street within a city. For characters present in the scene, Vistas include character portraits — art that depicts the characters from a first-person perspective, as if your player character is viewing those characters.

Every Vista in Ember is made using a complex set of Assets. These Assets are layered so that when you right-click and hold, you can move the viewpoints around. Additionally, the layering of Assets and perspective-shifting in the Vista creates a parallax effect that gives an illusion of depth.

First-Person Perspective

Vistas are designed to be first person, in which you are looking at the scene through your own eyes, with the viewpoint directly in front of your face. Every design — from how characters are portrayed to the Assets and objects — takes this into account, including the overall angular perspective.

Character Portraits

Character portraits depict many of the wonderful and diverse Non-Playable Characters that are part of @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8#quests-and-milestones]{Quests} and storylines in the Ember game. These character portraits are loaded automatically when an @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Event} is started and a Vista scene is loaded.

Character portraits within a Vista can be moved around the scene by dragging them with a mouse click and hold, or by clicking on the character portrait to select it, then using the WASD keys to move it left, right, up, or down — up and down move the character portrait forward and backward in the Vista's layers, potentially shifting them in front of or behind preconfigured assets.

If you wish to add a character to the Vista, simply drag them from the Actors sidebar on the right. If a character has a portrait assigned, they will automatically appear in the Vista. By default, only a Gamemaster can add an Actor to a Vista, but the Gamemaster can allow players to do so by granting them the "Create Token" permission.

Adding Your Own Portraits.

You may also insert your own custom character portraits into the game world. We do not make this process immediately obvious, as we believe that the barrier to creating artwork for custom Ember characters is high, and not every player will have access to such artwork. If you wish to use a piece of custom artwork and place it in a view, you need to ask your GM to add the artwork to their Assets folder, then assign the artwork to your character by editing your character sheet and clicking on the portrait. This will bring up a list of Assets you can select.

Asset Overwrites Following Ember Updates

Be careful when adding Assets through a folder, as — depending on the placement of the Assets in the folder structure — these Assets may be overwritten by future Ember updates.

Area Maps.name: Area Maps
Area Maps.text:
Area Maps are explorable scenes viewed from a top-down perspective, incorporating player character Token Actors, Creature Actors, and NPC Actors, all within a preconfigured scene that typically includes walls, lights, sounds, and Interactable Objects.

Area Maps represent explorable areas within a @UUID[.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Location} on the Region Map, and allow players to move the Token representing their character around the scene by selecting their Token and using the WASD keys on their keyboard.

Player Character Tokens automatically incorporate the sight ranges from their character sheet. Sight is blocked by walls, but not by windows — map features like walls and windows come preconfigured in all Ember Area Maps.

Scene Levels

Scene Levels represent significant elevation within an Area Map, such as floors of a building or cliffs in a wilderness area. Scene Levels allow a Token to change elevation smoothly, such as traversing up and down a set of stairs without changing to a new scene.

Scene Regions

Area Maps in Ember are often configured with several Scene Regions, which are used to create interesting and dynamic effects. For example, an Scene Region might be designated as wood, such that when a Token moves across it, the sound of wooden footsteps is heard.

Scene Regions are also used for game elements like traps, so that when a character moves over a trap with their Token, they automatically trigger an effect. Typically, these effects include sounds and animations, such as the trap springing out from a wall. The exact nature of the trap or effect is described in the Chat Log.

Interactable Objects

Interactable Objects are elements of an Area Map that can be clicked on to change something on that map. Often, this includes an animation or sound.

Doors are common Interactable Objects, visible on Area Maps as small door icons. Clicking a door icon will cause that door to open, a small sound to play, and allow the vision of nearby Character Tokens to extend through the area behind that door.

Some Interactable Objects may be visible to players but not interactable until the Gamemaster engages with them on their end. For example, a locked door might require a Skill Check specified by the currently ongoing Event. After a successful Check, the Gamemaster unlocks the door, allowing players to open it normally by clicking on the icon.

Dynamic Tokens

Many Tokens on Area Maps are dynamic, meaning they animate with moving arms and legs.

Setting Overview.name: Setting Overview
Setting Overview.text:
Ember is an original imaginative fantasy setting for online roleplaying using Foundry Virtual Tabletop. Ember is vast, diverse, and self-contained. There are no alternative planes or parallel dimensions — the Cosmos of Ember and its World are the entirety of the game's universe. Choices here matter and can have major consequences that may not be recognizable at first.

The Ember Setting

The Ember Cosmos is a singular bubble of reality, meaning every location is accessible by travel or teleportation, from the moons in the sky, to the Spiritlands, to the Inner Realms on the surface of the Weave — which protects everything within it from the alien evils from without. This means Ember is not part of some vast multiverse; it is the only plane or dimension in existence. In the center of this bubble is Eiru, known as the World of Ember, home to a host of diverse cultures and distinct ancestries living upon its surface. Deep inside lies the Heart of Ember, a mysterious entity shaping the Cosmos.

Across Eiru, hundreds of powerful ascendant deities, called Shard Gods, influence events — some ancient, others new, but each is a complex, fallible character with their own goals and ambitions. In addition, five Elder Gods maintain Cosmic Balance and often intervene in mortal affairs. History spans beyond memory, with civilizations dating back hundreds of thousands of years, blending myth with truth, and the world suffers from ancient mistakes and cataclysms made by cultures that came before. The world features colossal structures of crumbling empires, vast wilds of untamed nature, and cities of towering stone. Above, glittering moons drift across the sky. Yet beauty exists alongside horror. A cataclysmic event known as the Shattering allowed the maddening influence from beyond the Weave to flow freely into the world. New terrors emerged, such as Undeath, Oblivion, and Dragons, ravaging the cosmos and reshaping mortal and divine pantheons alike. With all of these cosmic influences, magic permeates every corner of the world. It can be as subtle as drifting motes in the air or as forceful as the elemental energies channeled from the moons.

Ember is a setting of immense scale and wonder, a place where gods walk, magic breathes, and history stretches beyond comprehension, a setting designed to reward exploration, imagination, and storytelling on a truly epic scale.

Setting Compendium

The Ember Setting Compendium is extensive and offers a wealth of information for those who wish to explore the world in greater depth, whether for character creation and developing a backstory, or for Gamemasters who want to understand every detail and nuance of the lore. That said, the content in the Setting Compendium is entirely optional and not required to play Ember. It provides a rich and detailed foundation for the Ember: A Shard of Fear storyline and potential future content, but players are welcome to enjoy the game without reading a single page. The choice to delve deeper is yours, and the world is designed to be fully playable regardless.

Spoilers & General Information

The Setting Compendium is organized to provide different levels of information depending on the reader’s role and purpose. Content is categorized into three tiers of visibility: Player-Facing, Gamemaster-Facing, and Secret Lore.

Player sections are always visible and contain information that is generally known by most, if not all, inhabitants of Ember. This includes cultural norms, geography, major historical events, and widely recognized lore. Players are encouraged to explore these sections to understand the world their characters inhabit, without encountering spoilers for hidden plotlines or advanced mysteries.

Gamemaster sections are expanded to contain more specialized information that is only known to select individuals (such as scholars, experts, or key figures within the setting). These sections provide deeper context, hidden histories, and the inner workings of various factions, organizations, and deities. Access to this material allows Gamemasters to craft richer narratives, foreshadow events, and present secrets to players in organic ways.

For players interested in learning more beyond what is covered in this guide, the following pages detail various cornerstones of the setting, and serve as great places to start learning more about Ember as a whole.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.JUwFAaelI86yiscL]{The Cosmos}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.yOGZUX0Ld9ZnwAO4]{The History}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.39KjcVdySqOz1oSU]{The Deities}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.JrvMifpl4FgJ7PmF]{The Cultures}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{The Ancestries}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCharClasses]{Character Classes}

Welcome to Ember.name: Welcome to Ember
Welcome to Ember.text:
Ember is a vast world of rich history, vibrant cultures, imaginative places, and dramatic conflicts. The Ember game itself is both an original fantasy setting and a long-form campaign of epic scale.

Whether you're playing through Ember's canonical story or simply using the setting as a backdrop for your own narrative adventures, we hope you find it sets new and higher standards for immersive gameplay, mechanical innovation, player engagement, and memorable storytelling!

What's It Like to Play Ember?

The Ember game is more than what one might expect from a traditional roleplaying game setting or adventure; it is an interactive world that lives and changes around your characters. While playing Ember, your party will:

  • Travel across a vast region with tens of thousands of hexes and hundreds of discoverable locations.

  • Explore detailed area maps with interactive on-screen elements like traps, puzzles, and dynamic lighting, using animated and dynamically generated character tokens.

  • Encounter random events and overarching quests whose outcomes depend on the choices you make.

  • Play through over four hundred hours of handcrafted events, taking place in a unique setting with deep worldbuilding, and with a Codex that automatically records your journey along the way.

All the details of your journey — from the position of your caravan on Ember's surface to the orbit of Ember's mystical moons above — are illustrated and depicted in the game world, updating continuously to reflect the passage of time.

As days, months, and seasons pass, Ember will live and breathe around you, its fate dependent on what you choose to do (or not to do). Where you go, whose calls to action you heed, and what obstacles you overcome will impact not just the events that transpire in directly front of you, but the whole of Ember's vast world.

Plot Synopsis

This campaign is set upon the eastern coast of Aterica, the largest continent of the world of Ember, where a great rocky shelf known as the Arctus Plateau meets Ember's singular great ocean. The crown jewel of the Arctus Plateau is the metropolis of Ordain, one of the eleven great cities of the world.

You begin your story traveling with the Strayhearth Caravan — a group of traders traversing a route from the city of Casla-Brava (now several days to your west) to the great city of Ordain to your east. Your journey will take you through the winding trails of the Forest of Stone, open expanses of the Arctus Plateau, and ancient depths far below the surface, before you finally arrive to the bustling metropolis of Ordain.

Once you reach Ordain, you will become embroiled in a complex and far-reaching conspiracy involving powerful factions, shadowy and malevolent forces, iconic heroes, and gods themselves. Your approach to this conflict and the meaningful choices you make will forever alter the trajectory of Ember's story.

Game Systems

Ember is a setting designed for use with one of two game systems:

Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition

You can experience playing Ember using a familiar d20 rule engine with well understood character options and mechanics. The Ember implementation for D&D is designed to support the modern 2024-era rules revisions.

Crucible

Crucible is an original game system made by our team specifically and exclusively for the Foundry Virtual Tabletop platform. It is a dice pool system with free-form classless character progression.

Which system is right for our group?

Crucible is our own game system of choice and our favorite way to play Ember, as it lets us be bolder and take bigger swings with more interesting mechanics and design. However, because the ruleset of Dungeons and Dragons Fifth Edition is a mature, closed-loop ecosystem, it is more approachable for a broad range of players.

Crucible Beta Testing

Crucible is, like Ember itself, at an early stage of development, so choosing to play Ember with Crucible will result in a less polished and less complete experience than playing for D&D at this time.

Be Warned!

Testing Crucible in Ember is still preliminary. Many combat encounters are likely to be unbalanced — often against the player's favor.

Moreover, it is not yet possible to guarantee continuity of play with Crucible in Ember. Any characters created or testing done at this stage may need to be discarded with a subsequent update.

Thank You!

The Crucible system is a true passion to work on, and it will only achieve its potential with your help to evaluate the gameplay and enjoyment of using it. The team and I are very appreciative to those of you who take the time to try things out and share your feedback with us.

Getting Started

To start playing Ember, there are two main paths:

  • Discover more about the game's overall setting, beginning with the @UUID[.Bikr3BuyOCZpc8lL]{Setting Overview}.

  • Learn about Ember's @UUID[.UJLt0kE0pFZlUkJQ]{Character Creation} process to begin forging your hero.

Magic and Spellcraft.name: Magic and Spellcraft
Magic and Spellcraft.text:
Contextual Information

The material presented on this page differs depending on whether you are playing using the Dungeons & Dragons or Crucible game system.

Because of the unique nature of the Ember setting, there are certain limitations or features of the various @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0DQdqtsLn3M1ZZA2]{Magical Forces} which govern the cosmos that differ from other popular fantasy settings. Some of these important nuances are described below.

Magical Runes

Each of the twelve @UUID[Compendium.crucible.rules.JournalEntry.qjTSKlh59JhtUuEr.JournalEntryPage.p3hKRiZN3x0DEtyG]{Runes} of @UUID[Compendium.crucible.rules.JournalEntry.qjTSKlh59JhtUuEr]{Spellcraft} draw upon certain fundamental forces of the cosmos to empower magic shaped using that rune.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeControl00000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Control invoke specific glyphs intrinsically used by the fiends of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}. Only @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos} are able to manipulate the full power of such glyphs, but other spellcasters have learned to harness a measure of their power.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeDeath0000000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Death are crafted by tapping into dangerous @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{Abyssal} energy. This magic flows directly from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.E1Un2zZFUupMkmSQ]{Kinalathi}, although the provenance of undeath is unknown to all except a handful of Ember's most enlightened minds.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeEarth0000000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Earth draw upon fundamental elemental energy of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora}, allowing powerful spellcasters to control gravitational, tectonic, and corrosive forces. Some of the most dangerous and volatile practitioners of caustic magic are devotees of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QzJveYdQLi1LHHci]{Slinerak}.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeFlame0000000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Flame draw upon fundamental elemental energy of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}. Some of the most fervent pyromancers are devotees of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WMO5VwobQNmjaXQA]{Ravela}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KQF9QommtN6ITiLW]{Lorgi}, and in the most extreme cases @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ZvsMcVcESynKQn8d]{Fiyara}.@UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.GRs2vgeVsDpWPqjh]{Drakon}, and other types of dragonkind also utilize the Rune of Flame, although their connection to it is shrouded in mystery

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeFrost0000000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Frost draw upon fundamental elemental energy of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}. The Lady @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HhLvlcy84LAKTFWh]{Areyter} is said to be the most powerful user, as are the ferocious Behemoths that live upon Mayis. During the Age of Beasts, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giants} of the Shent harnessed and mastered the Rune of Frost to construct their towering mountain cities, and even today, many Giants maintain a close affinity to this Rune.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeIllumination]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Illumination draw upon the light of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} itself. The most fervent practitioners of radiant magic are the countless @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} that dwell in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}. Before the Shattering, the world-spanning empire of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} were also said to master and harness the Rune of Illumination.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeIllusion0000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Illusion draw upon the elusive shadow magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia} who are masters of its arts. A dangerous perversion of this rune has been observed among servants or followers of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.K0aRZjUnxqqxswAu]{Kyasifer} whose illusions twist and torment the mind.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeKinesis00000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Kinesis use gravitational manipulation to infuse objects with kinetic energy, one of the most fundamental forces in the cosmos. Kinesis powers @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{The Weave} and manifests in myriad ways. The Elder Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} is believed to be its most powerful wielder, although some speculate that her strength may be rivaled or even surpassed by the Outer God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.dapPg66vgvLnwgcp]{Vhismara}.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeLife00000000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Life draw upon the ever-present resonance of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.1jb9zDsRFMXo7Je0]{Wildsong} to manipulate primal natural energy. Channelers of this rune are most notably found among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Strider} culture or as devotees to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild Gods} who act as custodians of the natural order.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeLightning000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Lightning conduct the voltaic energy of storms. These currents flow from the fundamental elemental energy of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura} and the Elemental Sovereign @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Wfy3RfrQNFW8JWOv]{Nymbohr}, who is known as the Lord of Lightning. Many believe that the Rune of Lightning is a critical component in the construction of constructs and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.CNUDzx1WE09XXJZ8]{Wyrms} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon} once mastered its mysteries.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeOblivion0000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Oblivion dare to touch the entropic energy of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss} and its pure forces of destruction. Recognized usage of this rune is universally reviled by all cultures of Ember, who forbid such spellcraft. Occultists who dare to channel such power are often — either directly or unknowingly — servants of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VUhtOxDvWc3I7pY2]{Sha-Xotha}.

@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeSoul00000000]

Spells crafted using the Rune of Soul can subtly manipulate the ever-flowing current of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} originating from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. Most usage of this rune is culturally accepted throughout Ember, but major works of spellcraft that interfere with the current of souls draw the attention and ire of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} who presides over its continual flow.

Divine Smite

The additional damage from @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDivineSmit]{Divine Smite} can be applied to Abyssal and Undead enemies, but is not applied to Fiends which are not inherently evil or corrupted.

Teleportation

Teleportation magic is tightly restricted and controlled by the Rhivan @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages}, who limit its use. Long-distance teleportation magic is likely to be unavailable to you as players, though some shorter distance spells are commonly used.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMistyStep0]{Misty Step}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplBlink00000]{Blink}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDimensionD]{Dimension Door}

These spells provide short-distance translocation which falls outside the purview of the Star Mages. These arts are commonly practiced by spellcasters without restriction.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplTeleportat]{Teleportation Circle}

Teleportation Circles are tightly controlled by the Star Mages. Unauthorized travel to a controlled Teleportation Circle is a serious offense, and only sanctioned magical practitioners are authorized to use this network. There is one known Teleportation Circle in Ordain, called the Arcanic Portal Network Gate. Similar teleportation magic is otherwise not possible within the scope of this campaign.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplTeleport00]{Teleport}

Knowledge of this spell is tightly controlled and the Rhivan Star Mages proactively seek to prevent understanding of these arts from spreading outside the tight control of their order. It is exceedingly rare to encounter a mage who is capable of teleportation outside of the Star Mages.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplTransportv]{Transport via Plants}

These druidic arts fall outside of the purview of the Rhivan Star Mages. In the Ember game, however, not just any large plant may be used as a target for this transportation. Only specific trees grown from Seeds of Primordis may afford this type of transportation. There are two such trees in our game region.

Reviled Magic

Necromancy is nearly universally reviled on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}. Undeath is a fundamentally corrupting force of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, only introduced to Ember through the events of the Shattering, and has horrified every known Ember culture. No peoples, cultures, or nations tolerate the existence of necromancers, or of anyone who seeks to defile or corrupt the cycle of life.

Not all spells that belong to the Necromancy spell schools are reviled, nor are all spells that deal Necrotic damage. Only spells that draw upon the power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss} or the corruption of undeath are believed to be abhorrent to the natural order. Player characters who are observed wielding such magics on the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}, and in most other places on Ember, are likely to be treated as a malevolent threat. Other spells invite debate between scholars regarding the morality of their use and, as with any spell, can be used for good or evil according to the actions of their caster.

Reviled Spells

The following spells specifically are unanimously reviled and will not be viewed as acceptable to anyone who witnesses their casting and understands what they observed. Using them will likely lead either to immediate conflict or immediate reports to local authority figures. It could also cause pivotal characters in the game to loathe or become hostile towards the party.

Cantrips

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplChillTouch]{Chill Touch}

1st Level

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplFalseLife0]{False Life}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplInflictWou]{Inflict Wounds}

3rd Level

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAnimateDea]{Animate Dead}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplVampiricTo]{Vampiric Touch}

  • Spirit Shroud

  • Summon Undead

4th Level

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplBlight0000]{Blight}

5th Level

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAntilifeSh]{Antilife Shell}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRaiseDead0]{Raise Dead}

6th Level

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCircleofDe]{Circle of Death}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCreateUnde]{Create Undead}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplHarm000000]{Harm}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMagicJar00]{Magic Jar}

7th Level

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplFingerofDe]{Finger of Death}

9th Level

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplPowerWordK]{Power Word Kill}

Abyssal Corruption & Necromancy

While the peoples and cultures of Ember strictly forbid the practice of Necromancy and Abyssal Magic, we believe the best stories come from difficult choices. If your actions lead to evil outcomes or the use of reviled magic, you will accumulate corruption both narratively and through the @UUID[.3enOmC4M2HoyTXcg]{Attunement} system. We encourage you to embrace this if it suits your character! Just keep in mind that the full narrative weight and mechanical consequences of this corruption are far reaching and their full weight needs to be managed by your Gamemaster.

Resurrection

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} in Ember is one of the fundamental laws of the Cosmos. Resurrection magic is possible, but only if it does not directly oppose the natural order of the Soul Cycle. It is considered to be an acceptable form of intervention, rather than subversion, as long as:

  1. The person has died very recently.

  2. Their Soul has not yet made the conscious choice to move on to the Spiritlands.

The following spells may be used in this way:

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRevivify00]{Revivify}

Revivify may be used because the target has only very recently perished. The soul has not passed to the Spiritlands yet and may be restored to the body.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRaiseDead0]{Raise Dead}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplReincarnat]{Reincarnate}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplResurrecti]{Resurrection}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplTrueResurr]{True Resurrection}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplWish000000]{Wish}

Any of these spells can be used to restore life to a creature whose soul has not yet entered the Spiritlands. However, if this magic is used to recall a creature to life whose Soul has already entered the Spiritlands, it is considered a perversion of the Soul Cycle and will incur the wrath of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} and his followers.

Communication with the Departed

Use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithD]{Speak with Dead} ability to speak with the dead may or may not be deemed acceptable depending on the context. It is not reviled for priests or mages to use Speak with Dead to communicate with the departed, provided it is done respectfully.

In Ember, Speak With Dead magically communing with the dead works by pulling a small fragment of the soul back into its former body. This shade of the creature's former consciousness can impart portions of its past knowledge.

Using Speak with Dead Speaking with the dead imposes an undeathly facsimile of life upon the target which might be easily misconstrued as a reviled spell like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAnimateDea]{Animate Dead} if its usage is misunderstood by the observer.

Ancestry.name: Ancestry
Ancestry.text:
Ancestry describes your biological heritage, defines certain physical attributes of your character, and provides some signature features which are unique to characters of that Ancestry. There are 16 Ancestries available to choose from in Ember which are described in detail in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0]{Ancestries} entry of the Setting Compendium.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.tkGzfnJkkLZ3cgpG]{Altyra}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.blm7nVaaSYLZX3C9]{Cor'ak}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.GRs2vgeVsDpWPqjh]{Drakon}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.fmhP7pxXIXV0BM2r]{Fej}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.K28cb1q6tvU8FP8B]{Hulg'run}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Human}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.bOPreM2lwc0iB46X]{Keth}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.tyum0IGWIODRfitO]{Kiska}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.rl7QgGAIaYqAxLYq]{Kivahr}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p6DGVnaLHZfLvGem]{Signborn}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.3s9YujjWpwPJntGa]{Thornling}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.0YvoRkcs1BxtRiQz]{Vrjnhar}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.PYCLsQgKclg5toxT]{Wirrun}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.eyvVaX4c1rMos0ws]{Zeph}

As the first step of character creation you will select your Ancestry. Each Ancestry has its own unique origin story. Some ancestries are biologically compatible and it is not uncommon for characters in Ember to have a mixed ancestral heritage. You are welcome to describe your character as having mixed ancestry, however you must still select one Ancestry which defines the mechanical benefits and features that apply to your character.

Aster

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik overview inline]

During the Ancestry step of character creation, you may also select that your character has @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik]{Aster} heritage. This Aster trait is non-mechanical, but indicates that your character is different from others of your base Ancestry due to the particular qualities of their Aster alterations — you will still need to choose a base Ancestry to determine the relevant mechanical effects.

Special Gameplay Notes

Ashka Thermal Vision

The Ashka ancestry @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.ut16i65JiiErumq9]{Thermal Vision} feature is implemented in Foundry Virtual Tabletop as a Detection Mode. Be sure to configure the Prototype Token for any Ashka character and assign them the Thermal Vision detection mode with 60 feet of range. This is not currently automated but may be in a future update.

Ember Background.name: Ember Background
Ember Background.text:
Rather than choosing from a set of pre-defined backgrounds, you create a Background during character creation in Ember by combining your choice of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.jc7TEnx3yMnUcILK]{Attunement}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000]{Culture}, and @UUID[.#path]{Path}. Selecting these features during character creation automatically populates the Background section of your character sheet.

Attunement

Individuals in Ember can demonstrate an exceptional resonance to Ember's cosmological forces, a phenomenon called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.jc7TEnx3yMnUcILK]{Cosmological Attunement}. As part of character creation, you will select one of these Attunements — you will begin your journey with one Rank in that Attunement.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon - The Shattered Moon}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura - The Hollow Moon}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora - The Blasted Moon}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis - The Tempest Moon}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis - The Spirit Moon}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen - The Charred Moon}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum - The Realm of Endless War}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis - The Realm of Capricious Sorcery}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara - The Realm of Insatiable Curiosity}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{The Heart of Ember}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss}

You will begin your adventure at Rank 1 of your chosen initial Attunement with the abilities granted by that Attunement already active. During the course of your adventure, you will have abundant opportunities to further develop your chosen Attunement or to acquire Attunement with other forces via the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.3enOmC4M2HoyTXcg]{Attunement Progression} system.

Culture

Your Culture describes the region and peoples of Ember whom you most closely identify with as "home". This does not necessarily describe where you were born, although it can. Your chosen Culture will grant you a traditional Skill Proficiency, an Ember @UUID[.gd4Y1OVpcNAAK0MB]{Knowledge Area}, and a signature feature unique to that culture.

Certain Cultures may have predominant Ancestries which compose them, but every Ancestry is compatible with every Culture. There are eight cultures available to choose from:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd}

These cultures are those which are geographically closest to and most prominent in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} where the Ember game takes place.

Path

Your Path describes a facet of your character's history: what deeds you have accomplished, what training you have received, or what organizations you are affiliated with. Your chosen Path will grant you a choice of Skill Proficiencies and Tool Proficiencies based on the core competencies of that path.

There are currently 22 Path options available. Each Path option provides a backstory seed, two Skill Proficiencies, and one Ember Knowledge Area, all hallmarks of that Path. Additionally each Path provides a Tool Proficiency or an additional known language, and starting equipment (on top of to what was granted by your chosen Class).

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.academyDropout00]{Academy Dropout}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.anchoriteMarine0]{Anchorite Marine}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.caravanner000000]{Caravanner}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.cindaricInitiate]{Cindaric Initiate}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.cosmopolitanFash]{Cosmopolitan Fashionista}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.crownApothecary0]{Crown Apothecary}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.flameguardMiliti]{Flameguard Militia}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.imperialConscrip]{Imperial Conscript}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.lightsworn000000]{Lightsworn}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.lunarEmpath00000]{Lunar Empath}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.monsterHunter000]{Monster Hunter}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.naturalArtisan00]{Natural Artisan}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.nightwatch000000]{Nightwatch}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.obsidianAntiquar]{Obsidian Antiquary}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.primalistDiscipl]{Primalist Disciple}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.scionOfDarkness0]{Scion of Darkness}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.shadowWalker0000]{Shadow Walker}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.shardGodDevotee0]{Shard God Devotee}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.skyWanderer00000]{Sky Wanderer}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.starDreamer00000]{Star Dreamer}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.sunfireDescendan]{Sunfire Descendant}

  • @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.underworldMechan]{Underworld Mechanic}

Telling Your Own Story

The provided Path options in Ember suggest some backstory seeds which will be compatible with Ember's narrative and provide frequent opportunities to engage with it. We recommend using one if it is your first time playing Ember. However, if you want to change or entirely replace some suggested details of your Path, you should feel empowered to do so.

In this case, you should choose whichever Path provides a set of proficiencies and knowledges that you find appealing, but change the backstory details or even name of that Path to represent the story you want to tell for your own character.

Soulbound

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q overview inline]

During the Path step of character creation, you may choose to undertake the exceptional challenge of beginning your character's journey as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound}. Being Soulbound will make your character's journey more difficult, as there are meaningful mechanical penalties which this feature imposes upon your character.

Hard Mode

Undertaking this challenge is equivalent to playing Ember in "hard mode" and is not recommended for first-time players.

Dynamic Token.name: Dynamic Token
Dynamic Token.text:
The final step of the Character Creation process involves customizing your Character Token's appearance. This Token can be used as the main visual reference of your character, but more importantly, it represents your character on the @UUID[.lNMkySfNYWS3EvIk]{Area Maps} you will explore during the game.

When using the Token Maker during the Character Creation process, the choices you made in previous steps automatically determines the set of anatomy and equipment options that are available to you. For example, if you select a particular Ancestry, you will only be able to choose anatomical parts from that Ancestry.

Anatomy

First, you will choose your Token's anatomy, which determines your character's basic physical features. Anatomy includes body shape, face, eyes, arms, feet, and hands. To change these parts, click on the arrows on either side of the name displayed on the left side.

Equipment

Secondly, you will choose equipment, which can be selected above the visual Token appearance. This allows you to choose items, objects, and clothing for your character to wear. Once again, to change these parts, click the arrows on either side of the name displayed on the left.

Colors

Each anatomy or equipment piece can be colored via the small box on the right side of the Character Creation interface. Clicking this box reveals a color palette with hex codes for each color option. For some aspects of your character, you can select multiple colors. If you see options labeled 1 and 2, such as "Skin 1" or "Skin 2," this typically means you can assign different colors to different sides of the same part.

Random Appearances

There is a small Randomize button with two interlocking arrows next to Equipment. This button randomizes your anatomy and equipment, using pre-selected color choices that make the most sense for the Ember setting.

To configure your Token appearance after Character Creation, click the three small vertical dots in the top right corner of the Character Sheet, then select Ember Dynamic Token.

Milestone Progression.name: Milestone Progression
Milestone Progression.text:
Ember uses a system called Milestone Points to determine how and when the player characters advance in Level. Instead of acquiring traditional XP by defeating monsters, advancement in Ember is based on completing specific @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Events} within our many @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Quests}.

Expectations

Generally, a Main Quest awards 2 Milestone Points while a Side Quest awards a 1 Milestone Point — though there are some exceptions to this rule. You can learn more about Main and Side Quests on the @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Quests and Events} page of this guide.

Expected Progression

It is expected that player characters in the full Ember campaign will reach Level 11 by the end of the campaign. Parties which are comprehensive in their exploration and completion of content may reach Level 12. A party which pursues only the main story will finish the game at around Level 9.

Current Progression

During the current scope of the game, players can expect to reach Level 5 if they complete the main quest through the end of Chapter 3 and explore to locate and pursue available side quests along the way.

Progression Table

Leveling Up

Milestones earned apply to the entire party, even if certain characters or players were not present when the Milestone was achieved. When reaching the number of Milestone Points required to level-up, the entire party advances in Level. Only player characters advance in Level — non-player companions and allies either do not progress or have separate progression mechanics.

D&D Advancement

Rules Override

This section recommends some specific rules that apply to how leveling up should function when playing Ember with the Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition game system. These rules supersede and replace those written in the system.

When the party advances in Level, each member of the party should increase the Level of one of their chosen character classes by 1 or add a new Class at Level 1. Any traits, attributes, or features granted by this new Class Level are immediately acquired. In addition, each character who advances in Level also obtains the following immediate benefits:

  • Gained Hit Points are applied to both current and maximum totals.

  • All expended Hit Dice are recovered.

  • All expended Spell Slots are recovered.

  • All expended uses of a feature which recovers on Short or Long Rest are recovered.

  • Additional spells may be prepared if the maximum number of Prepared Spells increased.

The party is not required to perform a Long Rest to obtain these benefits, but neither is this equivalent to performing a Long Rest. Importantly:

  • Items with limited uses do not recharge.

  • Previously Prepared Spells may not be unprepared.

  • Features which are used during a Long Rest may not be performed.

Crucible Advancement

When the party advances in Level, each member of the party should increase their Level by one. Each player character may immediately advance their Ability Scores and Talents as normal and immediately benefit from that progression.

Rules Override

When the party advances Level in Ember, performing a Rest in order to advance in Level is not required.t.

Timekeeping.name: Timekeeping
Timekeeping.text:
@Embed[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.MzKx9e6HNy5I0cFD inline]

Gameplay Mechanics

The Ember game begins during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.R97NAeTio76VFKWI]{Age of Rediscovery} in year [[/date AS2523]].

We use the following terms to convey mechanical meaning about the time of the day:

  • Dawn is the period between 5am and 9am. Areas exposed to sunlight are affected by dim light unless otherwise noted.

  • Day is the period between 9am and 5pm. Areas exposed to sunlight are affected by bright light unless otherwise noted.

  • Dusk is the period between 5pm and 9pm. Areas exposed to sunlight are affected by dim light unless otherwise noted.

  • Night is the period between 9pm and 5am. Areas are affected by non-magical darkness unless otherwise noted.
