System Requirements.name: System Requirements
System Requirements.text:
Server Requirements

For the server or computer which is hosting the Foundry Virtual Tabletop game to perform well with Ember we recommend the following specifications.

  • The Hosting Requirements listed on the Foundry Virtual Tabletop website.

  • Foundry Virtual Tabletop version 14.358 or greater.

  • The Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition game system version 5.3.0 or greater.

  • OR the Crucible game system version 0.9.0 or greater.

  • At least 4GB of RAM and 5GB of available disk space on the server which hosts the game.

  • An internet upload speed of at least 24mbps (3MB/s) is recommended because Ember requires transferring large media files to all connected clients.

Player Requirements

For the gamemaster and players to have a great experience in Ember we require and recommend the following specifications.

  • The Recommended Client Specifications listed on the Foundry Virtual Tabletop website.

For players with a less powerful computer we recommend reducing the Performance Mode — which is configurable in game settings — to either Medium or Low. Reducing the performance mode will downgrade certain effects in-game resulting in improved performance for low-powered machines.

The Codex.name: The Codex
The Codex.text:
The Codex is a compendium of knowledge that you have accumulated while playing Ember. The Codex tracks the Events that have happened to you, the Quests you are progressing, the Locations and Biomes in the world that you have discovered, the creatures you have encountered, and the characters you have met.

The Codex can be viewed at any time by clicking the ​​ icon in the Calendar interface element at the top of the screen.

Journal

The Journal in the Codex — separate from the Journal entries in the Foundry sidebar — automatically tracks completed @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Events} as the party moves across the @UUID[.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc]{Region Map}. The Journal tracks the time and day a given Event was completed, and provides a small summary of what happened during the Event. This is a way to reflect on your journey and see when and where Events took place.

Quest Log

The Quest Log records completed Events in an identical fashion to those logged in the Journal, but filtered to include only @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Quest Events} (not Standalone Events), and displays these logs sorted by @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8#quests-and-milestones]{Quest}, rather than chronologically.

Discoveries

When the party moves into a hex with a @UUID[.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Location} or @UUID[.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Biome} that they have not previously encountered, this new discovery will be noted automatically in the Codex. These Codex entries include further information about the newly encountered Location or Biome, and the day and time that Location or Biome was first encountered.

Bestiary

The Bestiary automatically tracks encountered creatures and monsters that the party encounters in the game. This happens mostly inside @UUID[.lNMkySfNYWS3EvIk]{Area Maps}. Once discovered, a small summary will be recorded alongside an image and the day and time that creature was first encountered.

Characters

When the party discovers a new character for the first time, that character is recorded here alongside a small summary, including their name, pronouns, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0]{Ancestry}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000]{Culture}, character portrait, the day and time that character was first encountered, and other details.

Region Exploration.name: Region Exploration
Region Exploration.text:
Exploration of the Region Map — which can be accessed via the ​​ icon at the top of the screen — forms the backbone of Ember gameplay. It is how new Locations to explore are discovered, and how @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Quests and Events} are encountered. When making decisions about when and how to move on the Region Map, keep the following in mind.

Hex-Based Exploration

The Region Map is divided into hexes. Individual hexes can be inspected using the ​​ tool found in the Scene Controls interface element on the left side of the screen. Clicking on a hex while this tool is active will display the Hex HUD interface element for that hex.​ You may only inspect details of hexes that you've already explored.

Each hex has several important features:

Hex Key

The hex key uniquely identifies the specific hex, such as s.3209.2871. The letter prefix of the key describes the vertical slice the hex belongs to: s for Surface or p for Pathways — these are further explained in Region Levels below. The subsequent numbers of the key represent the hexagonal offset column and row of the hex, respectively.

Terrain Type

A hex's Terrain type can be viewed by hovering over the ​​ icon in the Hex HUD. The details of Ember's various Terrain types are described below.

Biome

A hex's Biome can be viewed by hovering over the ​​ icon in the Hex HUD. Each hex belongs to one (and only one) biome.

Location

Optionally, a hex may also contain a special Location, the name of which can be viewed by hovering over the ​​ icon in the Hex HUD. Locations are places with specific prewritten lore and gameplay — you can learn more about them in the @UUID[.#locations]{Locations} section below.

Hexes can have one of eight different Terrain types, the basic four of which simply modify the Land movement speed of your party when moving through that hex — an explanation party movement speeds can be found in the Party Movement section below.

Basic Terrain Types

Land Movement Speed Per Hour

Extreme

One-quarter

Difficult

Half

Normal

Unchanged

Road

Double

Additionally, there are four special Terrain types with more specific mechanics:

Impassable

Impassable Terrain is used to exclude hexes which cannot be occupied by a caravan. You may not move into an Impassable hex.

Water

Water Terrain is used to represent oceans, lakes, or other hexes which are mostly aqueous in nature. In water Terrain, a caravan travels using its full Water movement speed per hour.

Bluffs

Bluffs Terrain is used to classify special hexes that feature sheer cliffs adjacent to some other lower Terrain. Bluffs hexes count as Difficult for the purposes of movement, with the added rule that you cannot move from a Water hex into a Bluffs hex.

Canyons

Canyons Terrain is used to classify special hexes that feature deep elevation relative to their neighbors. Canyons hexes count as Extreme for the purposes of movement. Additionally, any movement into a Canyons hex also counts as Extreme, regardless of the Terrain of the origin hex.

You can also view the Terrain of the Region Map by toggling on the Terrain Overlay by clicking the ​​ icon in the Scene Controls interface element found on the left side of the screen.

When this overlay is active, it displays a legend of Biomes and Terrain types in the world, each with an associated are coded by color or texture displayed on the Region Map. Impassable edges between hexes are also depicted with solid black lines.

Locations

Locations are places with specific prewritten lore and gameplay, and may feature their own unique @UUID[.tR6hBroBjcKb7yG8]{Events}, @UUID[.5U1FpueYTnRKzYiS]{Vistas}, or @UUID[.lNMkySfNYWS3EvIk]{Area Maps}.

Most Locations are initially undiscovered — meaning that they do not appear in the Hex HUD, nor is the artwork that represents them visible on the Region Map. Locations can be discovered in one of two ways:

  1. You can encounter the Location directly by traveling to a hex where that location exists. When you enter a hex with a location, it is discovered automatically before any additional narrative events occur.

  2. The Gamemaster can individually mark locations as discovered using a button found at the top of each Gazetteer page or on the location view in @UUID[.rLYH6SWbKRtA3X8W]{The Codex}.

Region Levels

The Region Map contains two vertical slices, the Surface and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}. The party begins play on the Surface, but can move between these two elevation levels by visiting predefined transition points in specific hexes (after first discovering these transition points via exploration).

Each vertical slice has its own unique properties:

Surface

The Surface of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} is the entire overland region, which includes oceans, mountains, canyons, plains, and the city of Ordain. Your party must have its elevation set to 0 to travel on the Surface.

Pathways

The Pathways comprise the vast subterranean realms far below the Surface of Ember, which include unique underground Biomes and Locations to discover. Not all hexes on the Surface are explorable in the Pathways. A caravan must have its elevation set to -1 to travel throughout the Pathways.

To temporarily view a different slice of the Region Map without moving a caravan there, you can use the ​​ tool in the Scene Controls interface element found on the left side of the screen. This will change your own view of the Region Map without changing the position of your party or what other players see.

Party Movement

Moving through the Region Map takes an amount of time based on your party's Travel Pace, Land or Water movement speed, and the Terrain type of the tile your party is moving out of. For these purposes, a hex is always considered 1 mile wide.

Tile Category

Base Party Movement Speed

Land

2 miles per hour

Water

½ mile per hour

Parties possessing specialized vehicles may travel at different speeds over certain Terrain types. Additionally, exiting a Tile with a given Terrain type may modify your party's movement speed, as explained in Hex-Based Exploration above.

The party also sets a Travel Pace, which may be changed in the Party Sheet (which can be found via the ​ icon at the top of the screen). You may not change a party's Travel Pace while an Event is in progress. Your party's Travel Pace must be set before any Event resulting from travel occurs.

The following Travel Pace options are available, along with their respective advantages and consequences:

Normal

You move at your party's normal speed based on the Terrain type. Traveling at this pace has a neutral effect on the probability of Events occurring. This is the standard pace at which non-player caravans will travel.

Hidden

You move extremely slowly at ¼ of your party's normal speed. While moving this way, you are much less likely to trigger Combat or Social Events, but much more likely to trigger Exploration Events. If an encounter does occur, each party member is permitted to make a [[/skill stealth]] [[/skillCheck stealth]] check at the beginning of the Event to avoid initial detection. Unless otherwise stated, the difficulty of this check will be determined by the [[/skill perception passive]] [[/skillCheck perception passive]] Skill of other creatures that are simultaneously present in the area.

Slow

You move slowly at ½ of your party's normal speed. While moving this way, you are more likely to trigger Exploration and Social events. If an encounter does occur, each party member is permitted to make a [[/skill stealth]] [[/skillCheck stealth]] check with @Advantage[-2] at the beginning of the Event to avoid initial detection. Unless otherwise stated, the difficulty of this check will be determined by the [[/skill perception passive]] [[/skillCheck perception passive]] Skill of other creatures that are simultaneously present in the area.

Fast

You move quickly at 1.5× your party's normal speed. While moving this way, you are more likely to trigger Combat events and less likely to trigger Exploration events. Each hour of travel at this pace counts as 90 minutes of travel for the purposes of determining &Reference[exhaustion] @Condition[exhaustion].

Reckless

You move extremely quickly at 2× your party's normal speed. While moving this way, you are far more likely to trigger Combat events and far less likely to trigger Exploration or Social events. Each hour of travel at this pace counts as 2 hours of travel for the purposes of determining &Reference[exhaustion] @Condition[exhaustion.

Some additional rules for travel apply specifically when playing using the Dungeons & Dragons game system.

Equivalent Travel Paces and Skill Check Modifiers

The Ember game defines its own Travel Paces. The "Distance Traveled Per … " table in the Player's Handbook should be ignored. For the purposes of Skill Check modifiers (@Advantage[2] or @Advantage[-2] on certain Skill Checks based on Travel Pace as defined in the Player's Handbook) use the following equivalencies:

Ember Travel Pace

D&D Travel Pace

Hidden

Slow

Slow, Normal, Fast

Normal

Reckless

Fast

Extended Travel

Tests for &Reference[exhaustion], as described in the Dungeon Master's Guide, should be made for each hour of travel beyond 8 hours per day specifically when traveling on foot. When traveling as part of a caravan which has vehicles suitable for riding, such checks may be ignored.

Time Progression

Actions you take in Ember cause time to progress in the game world. The passage of time can have a number of important consequences:

  • Triggered Events: Whenever time passes, there is a probabilistic chance of triggering an Event. The ensuing Event could be beneficial, harmful, or both, and will typically involve social interaction, combat encounters, and/or exploration challenges.

  • Branching Quests: Some Quests in Ember depend on how quickly you reach a specific Event along that Quest. The clock is always ticking; how you choose to spend your time may effect the outcome or availability of Events within current and future Quests.

  • Miscellaneous: Time passing can also have other minor effects, such as the movement and evolution of @UUID[.HLQWWXHPxWPAXRDz]{Weather} on the Region Map.

For this reason, it's important to understand what exactly causes time to pass:

Action

Time Passed

Horizontal Movement: Moving between two hexes on the same vertical slice of the Region Map.

Dependent on your party's movement speed, Travel Pace, and the Terrain of the hex you're moving out of — see Party Movement above.

In Normal Terrain at a Normal Travel Pace and without a vehicle, moving one hex takes 30 minutes.

Vertical Movement: Moving between two vertical slices of the Region Map at a predefined transition point.

1 hour.

Resting: Taking a Short or Long Rest Rest or Recovery via the Party Sheet ​ .

10 hours for a Long Rest, and 1 hour for a Short Rest. 10 minutes for a Recovery.

Gamemaster's Choice: Whenever you take actions in the game world, the Gamemaster may choose to progress the current time.

Up to the Gamemaster's judgement.

Visibility and Fog

An essential component of region map exploration is the party's interaction with the Fog of War, which obscures the content of a hex until your party moves close enough to see it.

Every hex on the map has a certain visibility distance, which defines the number of adjacent hexes that can be seen from that location. A hex's Biome and Terrain type can affect the party's visibility distance. There are also barriers between hexes in certain locations which prevent visibility due to a natural or man-made obstacle.

These restricted movement and visibility edges between hexes are visualized in the Terrain Overlay, which can be toggled on via the ​​ icon in the Scene Controls interface element found on the left side of the screen.

Vantage Points

A Vantage Point is a special and rarely-encountered location or interactable object within the game world which has the effect of revealing a large area of Fog of War on the Region Map. Vantage Point reveals might happen as a result of certain Event outcomes, or as a byproduct of interacting with certain @UUID[.lNMkySfNYWS3EvIk]{Interactable Object} during exploration of an Area Map.

Shared Fog of War (Work In Progress)

For the time being, all players (and the Gamemaster) have their own independent copies of Fog of War exploration, meaning that the duly revealed areas are not guaranteed to be synchronized across all players.

The Fog of War exploration will be appropriately synchronized when all players are actively connected to the game server; but if a player is either absent for a session or disconnects during a session, they can miss moments of exploration — which will result in the fog of those areas not being revealed for them. This is a temporary limitation, and one objective for us during our continued development of Ember is to eventually feature a fully-synchronized Fog of War system for all players.

Quests and Events.name: Quests and Events
Quests and Events.text:
Gameplay in Ember happens through Events — prewritten plot moments that involve exploration, social, or combat challenges. Events come in two types:

Quest Events

Events that take place as part of a Quest. These Events are individual moments in an overarching storyline.

Standalone Events

Events that provide one-off moments of gameplay that may reference Quests, but are not specifically part of their narrative.

Events are the primary way you engage with the world of Ember and its adventures. They provide challenges and potential hardship, but also opportunities for advancement and rewards in the form of @UUID[.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}, @UUID[.3enOmC4M2HoyTXcg]{Attunement Points}, items, equipment, and more.

The Event Engine

Events occur in response to a sophisticated probabilistic model which determines the probability of any given Event occuring at a given time and in a given @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc]{hex}— and, in the case of Quest Events, any necessary prerequisites.

Events can be triggered one of three ways:

  1. When the party remains in its current location for one hour or longer, based on the relative probabilities of possible Events in the currently occupied hex.

  2. When the party completes a move into a new hex, based on the relative probabilities of possible Events in the destination hex.

  3. A Gamemaster may choose to manually initiate an Event regardless of its probability or prerequisites.

When an Event is selected to occur, that selection takes the form of a recommendation to the Gamemaster. The Gamemaster has the ability to accept that recommendation and begin the Event, to decline it in which case no Event occurs, or to request an alternative suggestion which proposes a different Event from the set of possibilities. While you won't have to worry about any of this as a player, it can be helpful to understand what's happening behind the scenes — discovering and initiating Events is key to progressing in Ember.

In particular, Quest Events may award @UUID[.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points} which are necessary for player characters in Ember to increase their Level, while any Event may grant @UUID[.3enOmC4M2HoyTXcg]{Attunement Points}.

Quests and Milestones

Quests in Ember are overarching narratives that connect multiple Events to tell a complex story. Quests are long sections of content — each Quest is likely to require between four to eight game sessions to complete. Completing Quests earns @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points} to advance the Level of player characters, so it is advisable for you to actively seek out quests and endeavor to complete them.

There are two categories of quests in Ember:

  1. Main Quests, which tell the central story of our campaign, A Shard of Fear. Main Quests typically award 2 Milestone Points each — 1 Milestone Point near the middle of the quest and the other near its conclusion.

  2. Side Quests, which provide supporting narrative to enrich exploration of the world. Side Quests typically award 1 Milestone Point near the conclusion of the Quest.

Discovering Quests

The first Main Quest of the game is called "The Winding Trail." It commences automatically at the beginning of the game. Other Quests have to be sought out by exploring the world and visiting new Locations. You may also encounter rumors that point the way to places where Quests can be encountered.

Quests are intentionally designed to be easy to find, so don't fret that you are missing them by failing to investigate subtle clues. Every Quest has multiple on-ramps that lead to the beginning of its narrative.

Progressing Quests

As you experience Quests, a record of the Quest's Events is recorded in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.rLYH6SWbKRtA3X8W]{Codex} in two ways — chronologically on the Journal tab and organized by Quest in the Quest Log tab.

It's important to note that quests in Ember are intentionally never marked as "complete." There are often downstream consequences of the decisions you make in a Quest, and we purposefully do not reveal whether a particular storyline is ever truly over.

Knowledge Areas.name: Knowledge Areas
Knowledge Areas.text:
Your character begins with two Knowledge Areas. In the context of the Ember game, Knowledge Areas represent everything your character has learned from those who raised them, the Culture they grew up in, and the choices that they have made in their life to date. Knowledge Areas are determined by the character's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000]{Culture} and @UUID[.T7maxaxoH8IvgWqC#path]{Path}, as noted in the list below, and are unrelated to their Ability Scores or Skills.

Knowledge Areas In Gameplay

While playing the game, Knowledge Areas have several impacts and can be used for the following purposes:

  • A substitute for a Skill Check. If your character has the necessary knowledge, they can gain related information without the need to roll.

  • A bonus to a Skill Check. If your character has the necessary knowledge, they may receive @Advantage[2] to a related roll.

  • As a prerequisite to a Skill Check. Some Skill Checks cannot be attempted unless your character has a base of knowledge about the subject in question.

Knowledge Areas are incorporated into the events that a Game Master uses to run the game. They have already been carefully configured, but ultimately, the GM has the final say on how a Knowledge Area may be used.

Knowledge Area List

You may want to choose a specific Knowledge Area because it is a subject that you would like to gain @Advantage[2] with during gameplay, or you might be interested in that specific subject and would like to gain more information from Skill Checks or gameplay moments. The following list makes it clear which Knowledge Area is associated with certain Cultures and Paths.

Missing Knowledge Areas

At this point in development, there is no way to start with certain Knowledge Areas, as there is no Culture or Path associated with them. Eventually, more Cultures and Paths will be available that will close these gaps. You will eventually also be able to gain additional Knowledge Areas as you play.

Attunement Progression.name: Attunement Progression
Attunement Progression.text:
Cosmological @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.jc7TEnx3yMnUcILK]{Attunements} grant unique features depending on how closely your character align with important celestial forces in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.JUwFAaelI86yiscL]{The Cosmos} of Ember.

You begin play with Rank 1 in a single Attunement. Through play, you will be able to progress multiple Attunements, granting you access to a wider range of Attunement features, but only one of these Attunements may be active (granting you its features based on your Rank) at a given time.

Your Attunement progression and the ability to change which Attunement is active can be found on an special Ember-specific tab on the character sheet for player characters — these Ember Attunements are wholly separate from item attunements in Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition. .

Attunement Progression

Attunement is progressed by acquiring Attunement Points which occur as a result of decisions you make during the course of play that are ideologically or philosophically aligned with the principle Ideal of a Cosmological Attunement. The table below describes the number of points needed to obtain or progress an attunement rank.

Attunement Rank

Points Required

Cumulative Points

Rank 1

3

3

Rank 2

4

7

Rank 3

5

12

Rank 4

6

18

Rank 5

7

25

Gamemaster Judgement

There are a large number of recommended Attunement progression moments scattered throughout the gameplay events of Ember. It is also possible for a Gamemaster to grant additional custom Attunement Points when a character takes some action that is strongly aligned with the Ideal of a specific Attunement. We encourage Gamemasters to consider Attunement progression as a way to reward exceptional roleplay or to add weight to climactic moments.

Expected Progression

You should expect for the Attunement which is most closely aligned with your character's personality and ideology to reach Rank 5 by the end of the Ember campaign. You may also expect to progress several other Attunements to lesser Ranks, providing you with additional tactical options which may be situationally useful.

Active Attunement

The Attunement that you currently have marked as "active" provides you with various mechanical benefits, which may include both passive bonuses as well as active features or actions.

Please note: when an Attunement becomes active, it causes all other Attunements to become inactive. Players can change which Attunement is currently active in one of two ways:

  1. Whenever you acquire an Attunement Point that progresses one of your Attunements, you may designate that Attunement as active.

  2. Certain shrines and other locations exist throughout the setting that allow you to commune with a specific cosmological force. Performing this communion will allow you to activate the associated Attunement.

Attunement Features

The Attunement system is still a work in progress. There is still work remaining to develop Attunement features and their progression paths.

Attunement Shrines are not yet added to the game world, but will be defined in a future update.

Gathering and Crafting.name: Gathering and Crafting
Gathering and Crafting.text:
The gathering and crafting system in Ember is a system designed to amplify and enhance the gameplay experience.

Work In Progress

The Gathering and Crafting system is not yet implemented and will be added during a later phase of game development.

Gathering

Through gathering, you can acquire materials from around the world through exploration, events, or defeating specific enemies.

Crafting

Through crafting, you may then take these gathered materials and craft items, objects, common weapons, and armor.

World Map.name: World Map
World Map.text:
Ember includes a World Map which depicts the major geographical features of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}. You can navigate to the world map easily at any time by clicking the ​ icon in the Calendar interface element at the top of the screen.

This World Map is used only for reference, not for gameplay. All gameplay pertaining to the party's in-world location is handled by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.hLp3EAST47aVpwVW]{Region Map}.

Using the World Map

The Ember World Map includes prewritten annotations that you can access to learn more about places within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}. Place names with associated information in the Setting Compendium will increase in size when you mouseover them — double-clicking these place names will bring you to the relevant Journal entry in the Setting Compendium.

Search and Discoverability

In the future, the World Map will include interface elements to search and more easily explore elements of the World Map.

Cosmos Map.name: Cosmos Map
Cosmos Map.text:
Ember includes a map of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{The Cosmos} which can be viewed at any time by clicking the ​ icon in the Calendar interface element at the top of the screen.

This visual representation of the Cosmos is accurate to the current world time. As time progresses, so too do the positions of the sun, moons, and inner realms that make up the Cosmos.

Each of the inner realms is depicted around the perimeter of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{The Weave}. The realm or realms closest to the top of the visualization are those which exert the greatest influence upon Ember itself.

Meanwhile, each moon has a different orbital path depicted on the Cosmos Map. The solid dot at one end of this path represents the position where this moon is closest to Ember and thus exerts the greatest influence.

Using the Cosmos Map

The visualizations of the orbits of Ember's moons are of particular importance. As a particular moon reaches its zenith, Ember is bathed in the elemental energy associated with that lunar body, which can have strange effects upon items, attuned individuals, and more — you can always check how close a moon's orbit is to apex via the Cosmos Map.

Death and Soulbound.name: Death and Soulbound
Death and Soulbound.text:
@Embed[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q overview inline]

When a player character dies in Ember, they're presented with an existential choice: leave the mortal world behind (resulting in the creation of a new character), or remain tethered to their body by becoming @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound}. Becoming Soulbound grants them a Soulmark, binding their souls to the mortal plane until their unfinished business is resolved.

Soulmark Progression

The are three categorical severities of the Soulbound @UUID[Compendium.ember.crucible-character.Item.emberSoulbound00] condition that have been observed. Mechanically, these are expressed as Soulbound Ranks. When a Soulbound character dies and subsequently clings to life, the rank of their Soulbound Rank increases and the effects of their Soulmark intensify.

As a Soulmark progresses, the negative mechanical properties of the feature continue to escalate — taking a dangerous and volatile toll on the character's body and mind as they struggle to resist the cosmic pull of Eternas.

Soulbound Rank

Soulmark

1

@UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.emberSoulbound00]

2

@UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.emberSoulbound20]

3

@UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.emberSoulbound30]

Creating a Soulbound Character

Players can optionally elect to be Soulbound immediately during character creation, in which case they begin their story under the effects of the@UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.emberSoulbound00]@UUID[Compendium.ember.crucible-character.Item.emberSoulbound00].

Assuming this burden will add difficulty and hardship for the character and for the party as a whole, so it should not be undertaken lightly. The only benefits from doing so are for narrative reasons in seeking a compelling or potentially tragic tale for your hero.

Becoming Soulbound

If a player character dies during the course of gameplay, a conversation with the GM can illuminate their next steps, including whether or not the deceased character is destined to become Soulbound. Should that character decide to persist until their unfinished business is complete, they'll gain a @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.emberSoulbound00]@UUID[Compendium.ember.crucible-character.Item.emberSoulbound00] instead of remaining &Reference[dead] @Condition[dead].

Once Soulbound, such a character can die a total of two more times before their tether to the mortal world grows too insubstantial to sustain. With each death, the intensity of their Soulmark deepens.

Extreme Situations

If the manner of a character's death is extreme to the degree that the character's body is no longer available (for instance, via disintegration or by falling into magma) they can't become Soulbound — their soul lacks a sufficient corporeal vessel to occupy. Otherwise, the Soulbound affliction can overcome even the most grievous of wounds (with extreme visual markers of their Soulmark to match).

Final Outcomes

When a Soulbound character with a @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.emberSoulbound30]{Deathly Soulmark} experiences their final death, that character's soul is corrupted by loathsome forces beyond the fabric of reality — resulting in their grim and unholy transformation into an undead creature.

If a Soulbound character can find contentment by completing their unfinished business, they may relinquish their tenuous hold on mortality before meeting this terrible fate. At any time outside of an active combat encounter, the player of a Soulbound character may choose to end their journey, accepting their end and allowing their soul to rejoin the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} and pass on.

How to Use This Guide.name: How to Use This Guide
How to Use This Guide.text:
Welcome to the Ember Players' Guide! This document is your main companion while playing the Ember game. Whether you’re setting up your first character or looking up a specific rule during a session, the information in this guide will be very helpful — but is not mandatory to read.

There are many ways to play roleplaying games, and instead of reading everything first, you can jump straight into Character Creation and learn about Ember as you play. The Ember game includes a guided Character Creation interface (which you can access via instructions on the @UUID[.UJLt0kE0pFZlUkJQ]{Creation Overview }page).

That interface will show you all available character options as you step through the process. Reading this guide in addition to using that interface will provide helpful additional context about Ember's world, and the unique changes that Ember makes to the rules of the game system you are using, but you can also simply work through the Character Creation interface and learn the rest as you play!

Guide Structure

The Players' Guide has three main categories, each explaining a fundamental part of the Ember game:

  • Character Creation: What you should know when creating a character

  • Playing the Game: What you should know before starting play or during play

  • Exploring the Setting: Story and reference material that will come up again and again as you explore.

    Navigation & Formatting

To help you find what you need quickly, we use specific formatting styles throughout this guide. You will also find this formatting used in the same way throughout the Ember game.

These yellow-bordered blocks are called Gamemaster Blocks, and typically contain important information or notes that directly address the Gamemaster — though sometimes also the player! They can contain mechanics, rules, and important summaries. These blocks convey meta information that a player or Gamemaster should know, but that a character within the game world wouldn't.

These red-bordered blocks are called Hazards. They are typically used to highlight extremely important information, or information about dangerous obstacles, such combat mechanics, combat tactics, and traps.

These beige-background blocks are called readalouds, and are typically used to indicate that the information comes directly from a character's voice within the world. Readalouds are also extensively used by the Gamemaster to read Quest and Event text during the game.

Throughout this guide, you will see many links formatted like @UUID[.]{this}. They can be clicked on, and will take you to another page, or a different section within the current page. Some of the links in the Players' Guide will direct you to other pages within this guide, while others will open game content such as the Setting Compendium.

User Interface.name: User Interface
User Interface.text:
Ember includes a number of unique interface elements at the top of the screen that may not be familiar, even to experienced Foundry users.

Calendar

In the middle of the interface element at the top of the screen, you can find the current time, date, season, and year as well as the position of important celestial bodies in the Ember @UUID[.fMNz9J9lFs5u0Plh]{Cosmology}. You can expand and collapse detailed information about the calendar and cosmos by clicking the carat to the right of the current time of day.

Maps

At the top of the screen,to the left of the time, you can find the different Maps used to play Ember. You can access the @UUID[.scq0o7cvwNlFENzr]{World Map} via the ​ icon, the @UUID[.EExZpAVbJ2JdbNzn]{Cosmos Map} via the ​ icon, and the @UUID[.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc]{Region Map} via the ​​ icon.

Party Sheet

At the top of the screen to the right of the time, you can find the Party Sheet via the ​ icon. This popup has information about the characters in your party, as well as your party's Level, Travel Pace, and banner.

The Codex

At the top of the screen to the right of the Party Sheet, you can find The Codex via the ​​ icon. The Codex contains information about Events you've completed, places you've discovered, and creatures and characters that you've met.

Weather.name: Weather
Weather.text:
While exploring the Region Map, you will encounter random Weather Formations affecting a group of hexes. Weather Formations modify the gameplay experience, and change their shape and position over time. Examples of common Weather Formations are listed below, although there are other more rare Weather Formations. Each Weather Formation has the following attributes:

Type

The type of event, such as Rain, Fog, Dust Storm, Wildfire, or others. Different types of Weather Formations may have different mechanical effects or impact on Event probabilities. On the Weather Overlay and its corresponding legend, different types of Weather Formation are presented using different colors.

Strength

Weather Formations have multiple strength tiers and generally are the strongest at their center with gradually tapering strength as you move towards the outer fringes of the event area. On the Weather Overlay, the size of round dots which visualize the Weather Formation represent its strength. For example, for the Rain Weather Formation, the weakest strength is a Drizzle while the greatest strength is a Tempest

Size

Weather Formations have a certain size specified in miles as a radius from their origin. The size of a Weather Formation varies over its lifetime. Some Weather Formations grow in size while others shrink.

Speed

Most Weather Formations move across the region according to the global Wind speed, though Weather Formations generally move somewhat slower than this base wind speed. The speed of a Weather Formation is a factor which adjusts how much slower it moves relative to the prevailing Wind speed.

The Weather Overlay provides a visualization tool that can allow you to understand the current weather mechanics that you are experiencing. The Weather Overlay can be toggled on or off by clicking the ​​ icon in the Scene Controls interface element found on the left side of the screen. While this overlay is active, it displays a legend of Weather Formations which are currently active within the Region Map. Each Weather Formation is color-coded on the Region Map with dark lines that separate attenuated strength levels within that Weather Formation area.

Geography.name: Geography
Geography.text:
This game is set upon the eastern coast of Aterica, Ember's largest continent, where a great rocky shelf known as the Arctus Plateau meets Ember's singular great ocean. The crown jewel of the Arctus Plateau is the metropolis of Ordain, one of the eleven great cities of the world. This region is home to two cultures. The Arcturians are an innovative and hardworking people, with a long history and rich traditions. The Ordani are colorful, inquisitive, proud, and creative.

Work In Progress

This page provides an abbreviated summary of information for Early Access and will be expanded as a more complete section of the Setting Compendium in the future.

Continents

The world of Ember has 8 major continents. The largest of these is called @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica}, a supercontinent to the northwest of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Op5BD9XSlmb7l6NN]{Starshield} — a smaller continent upon which the Aedir Sun Tower was built that marks the center of the world and from which cardinal directions are defined.

The Arctus Plateau

The windswept lands in eastern Aterica that border the ocean — and within them, the great city of Ordain — together make up the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}. Populated by a few isolated highland villages and towns, this highland plateau is rife with rocky outcrops and long winding roads between fields of dry grasses and isolated trees. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian} people who inhabit this land are practical and innovative with a deep love of tradition, creativity, and community.

Ordain

@UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} is one of the largest Great Cities of Ember, a glittering white and red jewel on the far eastern edge of the Arctus Plateau. Ordain is a vast and strategically located metropolis that is also one of the largest hubs of trade in the known world and the seat of several powerful organizations. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani} culture and influence is felt worldwide and the Ordani language called "Coins", once used primarily for trade, is now considered the common tongue for many cultures.

Siodread.name: Siodread
Siodread.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Siodread.scoverview: Siodread is a colossal Carnal Dragon that controls a massive region of bone-scattered lands and twisted spires between the Blood Barons and the Cascilian Republic. They are frequently appeased in secret by the Republic through sacrifices to abate their relentless hunger.

Ryleir.name: Ryleir
Ryleir.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Ryleir.scoverview: A young Carnal Dragon that lives in the shallow tunnels of the Pathways beneath the Arctus Plateau. Cunning and intelligent, they are a manipulator rather than a fighter and are shockingly happy to talk with mortals when they encounter them in return for information about the surface world. Strangely they have a keen desire to keep their word and although they do kill mortals they do so only when they have been betrayed or lied to in some way.

Karaxsus.name: Karaxsus
Karaxsus.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Karaxsus.scoverview: Karaxsus is a legendary Dragon known as the Flaming Dread that is said to live in the mountains north of the Corebright Forest. Various stories tell tales of a wingspan so large that they engulf entire towns and a maw large enough to swallow ships. Such stories are now told as legends, however, and it is not known if they are still alive, with the last sighting nearly two hundred years ago.

Calyn Kariset.name: Calyn Kariset
Calyn Kariset.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Calyn Kariset.scoverview: Calyn Kariset is the ruler of the Tayan Empire. She is known as the Dragon Empress or the Dragon Queen due to her fierce bond with the Dragon Velestrix.

Velestrix.name: Velestrix
Velestrix.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Velestrix.scoverview: Velestrix is a powerful Dragon of unknown age and lineage, she is bonded to the Empress of the Tayan Empire, Calyn Kariset. Velestrix is the largest Dragon even ridden by a Kirargy Knight and is often compared to the legendary Karaxsus in size.

Corwin Kawn.name: Corwin Kawn
Corwin Kawn.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Corwin Kawn.scoverview: Husband of Calyn Kariset, killed during the sacking of Yarino in 2,508 AS. Corwin was dashing, cunning, and extremely deadly with a single-bladed sword, one of the early supporters of Calyln's newly formed Tayan Empire. He was quick to secure power over the city of Kawn before pledging his services to the new Empress.

Mournax.name: Mournax
Mournax.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Mournax.scoverview: Mournax is a horrifying monster of nightmares that is said to prey upon the ships and settlements of the Lowlands and has been said to roam across the entire world in pursuit of relics and power. They are a Vile Dragon of impressive age and power that resides upon the Starshield continent and have survived by effectively hiding in one of the few places the deities of Ember refuse to tread.

Erisagosa.name: Erisagosa
Erisagosa.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Erisagosa.scoverview: Erisagosa is a sapient Leviathan who resides in the far north of the world. She is said to be the offspring of one of the ancient Wyrms of Akon and a Leviathan. She takes the form of a great ice wyrm that can fly through the air effortlessly. She is considered a minor deity by the Fikost.

Kalos Kariset.name: Kalos Kariset
Kalos Kariset.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.

Ankarist Talken.name: Ankarist Talken
Ankarist Talken.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Ankarist Talken.scoverview: A stern Drakon with a determined expression and piercing golden eyes. Their martial training is immediately apparent, with thick leathers, padding, and armor covering almost their entire body. A huge two-handed sword, forged in a strange style, with a flared wide square tip is typically clipped to the back without a sheath.

Renara Talken.name: Renara Talken
Renara Talken.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Renara Talken.scoverview: Renara Talken is the leader of the Vanguard and daughter of Ankarist Talken.

Cronaric Tezran.name: Cronaric Tezran
Cronaric Tezran.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Cronaric Tezran.scoverview: Lord Cronaric Tezran is the head of House Tezran in the Tayan Empire and leader of the Drakon faction that follows Empress Calyn Kariset. He is a stern, unyielding Drakon who is unflinching in his loyalty to the Empress and leads the internal security of the Empire as the head of the mysterious and deadly Talon.

Albine Amar.name: Albine Amar
Albine Amar.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Albine Amar.scoverview: Albine Amar is the current Director of the Rhivan Star Mages, one of the most esteemed, brilliant, and powerful Star Mages of his generation. Amar often teaches students personally at the Star Academy for most of the year. However, they are known to travel extensively, and it would not be unusual to find them in far-flung locations of the world.

\"Redfiend\" Loris Tezran.name: "Redfiend" Loris Tezran
\"Redfiend\" Loris Tezran.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
\"Redfiend\" Loris Tezran.scoverview: Tall, imposing, and with a powerful frame, "Redfiend" Loris Tezran somehow manages to appear sleek and refined despite the blatant strength and power he wields. As the official Ambassador to the Tayan Empire, Loris commands a small contingent of personal Tayan guards, and his ferocious mount Rakavi is never far from his side. He has a mane of dark hair, and dresses to impress, wearing only the finest clothing that the Tayan Empire produces.

Haldia.name: Haldia
Haldia.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Haldia.scoverview: The Ancient Keth Druid who wanders the Corebright forest and technically leads the Primalists, though they have become lost among their animal form of a Greater Pratax for over a thousand years and only other druids can communicate with them.

Norzi Ashigurin.name: Norzi Ashigurin
Norzi Ashigurin.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Norzi Ashigurin.scoverview: Norzi Ashigurin is the Shenin of the city of Lunari and the Lord of Storms, one of the most powerful rulers of the Maziran Kingdoms.

Avwynn Taol.name: Avwynn Taol
Avwynn Taol.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Avwynn Taol.scoverview: Avwynn Taol is mysterious figure that has a surprising and deep knowledge of the Heart of Ember and magic.

Pathgar Aztia.name: Pathgar Aztia
Pathgar Aztia.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Pathgar Aztia.scoverview: The Great Mender of the Bejak, Pathgar Aztia is an ancient Hulg'run that is over three thousand years old and fondly remembers the Shent. They are greatly revered by all Bejak but serve as more of a spiritual leader that helps kind the Tribes rather than directly give commands.

Rathern Orian.name: Rathern Orian
Rathern Orian.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Rathern Orian.scoverview: Rathern Orian is the current High King of the Wardcall, a position he has held for the last 43 years since the ending of the vicious civil war that ravaged the Kingdoms of Wintec, Katic, and Pertta. Once a powerful and well-respected leader, his falling health has reignited tensions across the Wardcall.

Luna Karrowrath.name: Luna Karrowrath
Luna Karrowrath.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Luna Karrowrath.scoverview: Luna Karrowrath is the Champion of Lumé, the highest-ranking warrior in service to the Shard Goddess and her most trusted confidant and friend. She is often tasked with investigating undead threats beyond the border of the Lumek Homelands.

Caster Tusk.name: Caster Tusk
Caster Tusk.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Caster Tusk.scoverview: Hunter extraordinaire, he previously prowled the depths of the Duskflare Jungles of the Lowlands but has been drawn to the Arctus Plateau to hunt the emerging megafauna for trophies. He is a boisterous, headstrong and powerful Kavir originally from the Bejak Tribelands, at 80 he is considered middle aged and wields a long spear like harpoon.

Briana Brewer.name: Briana Brewer
Briana Brewer.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Briana Brewer.scoverview: The famous travelling Bard who hails from the distant Great City of Kasarain in Kessia. Currently residing in Ordain she is a fun-loving and carefree traveller and is guarded by her friend Kroma a Bjordan Vrjnhar.

Viola Key.name: Viola Key
Viola Key.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Viola Key.scoverview: Mistress of the Arcing, the leader of the Arcageris warrior monks. She currently resides in the Iron Bastion of Wick in the Lowlands. A renowned elderly warrior, she somehow managed to kill a Fire Dragon named Voradaess in her youth and now trains future monks in all manner of martial forms.

Drevin Markus.name: Drevin Markus
Drevin Markus.text:
• Occupation: Historian

  • Period: (2310- 2402 AS.)

  • Affiliation: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}

  • Ancestry: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.PYCLsQgKclg5toxT]{Wirrun}

  • Famous Works: The Complete Works of History, Post Shattering by Drevin Markus

Professor Drevin Markus was a prominent and influential member of the Anachraenum that died a hundred years ago. He authored several works that are still used as the basis of knowledge for events after the@UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering} around the Arctus Plateau and beyond. He was famous for being bookish, cowardly, and difficult to work with. This meant he rarely traveled outside of Ordain and instead sent members of the Anachranum all across the known world in search of seemingly unimportant pieces of information to collaborate on his own theories and opinions. He lived his entire life in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} and only left All-Fable Keep to give talks and public speeches on history.

Personality

Professor Markus was said to be a singular intellect with a vast knowledge that seemed to connect seemingly unrelated snippets of information into wild ideas and stunning leaps of the imagination. Despite his brilliance, he was also said to be a cantankerous, lecherous, and thoroughly dislikable character who often clashed with other members of the Anachraenum. He was famously short of temper and spent the last few years buried so deeply into his books it was little surprise to anyone when he was found quite dead amidst a mountain of books, but none of his students had wanted to interact with his slumped form.

Connections

During his time, Drevin Markus was considered a towering figure of historical study; he spoke often and loudly about his own works and was well-regarded publicly. His lectures and public talks were extremely captivating, and he was responsible for spreading knowledge of history throughout Ordain. He had many intellectual admirers who supported his work from across the known world, and he was able to amass a sizeable fortune that he passed onto the Anachraenum upon his death, smoothing over some of his rougher edges in the minds of his fellows.
Drevin Markus.scoverview: One of the most distinguished historians of the Anachraenum, authoring hundreds of books attempting to understand ancient historical events post-Shattering. Their writings are famously second-hand, gathered from scattered pieces of combined information to create more complete pictures of the past, but surprisingly accurate once verified.

Itakurius.name: Itakurius
Itakurius.text:
• Occupation: Philosopher, Historian

  • Period: Unknown (Possibly around 2,000-3,000 years before the Shattering)

  • Affiliation: Unknown

  • Ancestry: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka}

  • Famous Works: Itakurius's Theory of Universals, Embrace of Tyrants, The Lost Empire

Itakurius was an ancient Ashka philosopher and historian. Her writings cover various subjects, including the natural sciences, philosophy, magical experimentation, history, and the arts. Very little is known about the life of Itakurius except that she was an extremely prolific writer who seemed to have also been an accomplished Wizard. Her writings have survived partly because many of her enchanted and protected tomes resist decay. Even so, every record so far recovered is a priceless tome, and only eight complete works exist; the rest are scattered pages and incomplete scrolls discovered in remote ruins.

Personality

Very little is known about her personality other than what can be conveyed through their writings. By her own accounts, they were meticulous and extremely thorough in their analysis of the things around them and extremely technically minded. Many of her recovered works are filled with as many diagrams, mathematical computations, and magical formula as they are words. She did not seem to show personal opinion on matters except in rare cases where they reference the Sunfire Empire of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir}. Here, a slight edge of contempt and dislike creeps into some of her phrases.

Connections

There are a few references to Itakurius living within a great city on a jungle island, but these are often brief. In these references, she sometimes refers to herself as a magical adept of some fame. Given the context, lack of hubris, and humble nature of the rest of her writing, it could be inferred that she was likely an exceptional, even legendary figure in her time.
Itakurius.scoverview: An ancient Ashka philosopher and historian from before the events of the Shattering. They are considered a particularly reliable writer on several matters but are thought to have a particular bias and dislike for the Aedir.

Auria Fisher.name: Auria Fisher
Auria Fisher.text:
• Occupation: Adventurer, Scholar

  • Period: (2494- Present)

  • Affiliation: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Qd6EE6pvR97O1OmH]{Kirargy Knights}

  • Ancestry: Human

  • Famous Works: Shards of Power, The Ancients of Ember.

Auria Fisher is an independent scholar and adventurer from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire. She is an associate member of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Qd6EE6pvR97O1OmH]{Kirargy Knights} Order of the Spear. She is accompanied on her adventures by her companion, Jerius Steel, a senior member of the Knights. She is an extraordinarily charismatic and dynamic researcher passionate about discovering lost information and gathering spoken tales and sagas from local inhabitants. She has been active for only twelve years but possesses a skill or lucky knack for tracking down obscure and fascinating subjects, revelations, and lost relics. She is also a powerful sorceress who follows the edicts of well.. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QDRFnVBZ1jy3YiD0]{me}.

Personality

Auria is quickly becoming a celebrated hero of the Tayan Empire, and her daring exploits are the stuff of rowdy tavern songs and spoken of among the ranks of various Tayan Armies for her determined and unrelenting spirit in the face of danger. She was assigned male at birth but transitioned with the support of her parents sometime in her adolescent years, embracing a vibrant, joyful demeanor, and she is happy to indulge her fans with exuberant expressions and catchphrases.

Connections

I first became aware of Auira not long after her nineteenth birthday. Her prayers and requests for knowledge intrigued me, especially considering her station in the Tayan Empire. Few would have dared to reach out to me as she did. Our bond has become closer over the years, and I do my best to protect our relationship. If The @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l5SNwXC8t3Qp3Ut3]{Empress} were to discover that Auria is one of my followers, I'm sure she would be put to death as a traitor. Still, she seems unconcerned by the danger and continues her exploits with my aid occasionally. Jerius may be aware of our connection, but so far keeps this information to himself.
Auria Fisher.scoverview: Auria Fisher is a young, energetic, determined adventurer and scholar from the Tayan Empire. Her works are written without interpretation or wild leaps of imagination, and she focuses on the facts that she can determine first hand and record.

Original Sorrow.name: Original Sorrow
Original Sorrow.text:
• Origin: Early Human

  • Knowledge: Well known by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian}@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessian}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian} & @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}.

The young @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen} King Mathwe sails to Venbrec to speak with its ruler, the ancient king Harloc, and asks for his daughter Sorrow’s hand in marriage, thus forging an alliance between the two human Kingdoms. Harloc agrees to the match and alliance and arranges a great feast, with the celebrations lasting for two days, until tragedy strikes and Mathwe’s half-brother Morol, kills the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} ambassador to King Harloc while drunk. Harloc is outraged and demands the head of Morol until Mathwe offers to bring the old king a magic bracelet that will allow its wielder to turn anything they wish into silver.

Mathwe sails east and sets ashore on a small island to resupply but the island proves to be a sleeping Leviathan and it dives into the ocean, nearly drawing Mathwe. He is only saved by the grace of the passing Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla}. Who warns Mathwe of the dangers of traveling east and that he must seek the Clouded Mountain upon which birds nest in great numbers, there he would find the bracelet he seeks.

Alas, while Mathwe is gone, his half-brother Morol, who was tasked with the protection of Prnicess Sorrow grows restless and jealous of his brother, he attempts to seize the throne with his group of followers and takes over the city of Ancalen. He arrives outside the doors of Princess Sorrow’s apartment, but she refuses to let him enter, he tries for three days and nights, using threats, promises and carefully placed words but the princess refuses all his advances. Eventually, Morol grows tired with her refusals and breaks down the door only to find Sorrow standing upon the window sill. Morol rushes forward, but with a cry, she throws herself into the air, wishing to be with Mathwe in death. Her pleas are heard by the God Taleisan, who turns her into an eagle as she falls.

Mathwe arrives at the great Clouded Mountains and travels upwards, braving the harsh winds and monsters on the path. He reaches the top of the mountains and a great nest filled with birds of many different types, all with smaller nests scattered within and filled with eggs of every size and color. Mathwe reaches the center of the nest and finds a mound of treasures and the bracelet he seeks glittering in the sunlight. As he reaches out, however, the countless birds around him screech, cry angrily and attack Mathwe and his men. At this moment, Princess Sorrow finds Mathwe upon the mountains and attempts to embrace him but Mathwe only seeing a great eagle, strikes out with his sword and cuts the bird flying at him in two. As he does so, the birds retreat and fly away into the sky. Mathwe returns to his boat and sails back to Venbrac with the bracelet he promised King Harloc.

With King Harlock satisfied, Mathwe returns to Ancalen to find the city in chaos. He learns of his half-brother's betrayal and storms the palace. He finds his half-brother weeping, and with a cry, he tells Mathwe that the princess was turned into a great eagle because of his jealousy, ambition, and anger. Mathwe realizes with horror that the bird he killed on the Clouded Mountain was his bride and falls to the floor broken. Mathwe then sets sail once again, leaving his regretful half-brother alone upon the throne of Ancalen, and is never seen again. King Morol is later murdered by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} assassins in his sleep.
Original Sorrow.scoverview: A myth from the time when Ancalen was inhabited by Humans, likely well before the Shattering. The city of Venbrec no longer exists in any records and it may be fictitious entirely.

The Knight & The Dragon.name: The Knight & The Dragon
The Knight & The Dragon.text:
• Origin: Between 500 & 1000 AS. Human

  • Knowledge: Well Known by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, & @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}.

In the legend, Isota, a Knight of Verador kills a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.0CquHJco0yougg3S]{Cruel Dragon} in the forests of Vanthar. The story goes that the Dragon inhabited the mountains nearby and would regularly fly across the area, attacking the villages and peoples indiscriminately. The villagers had begun to leave offerings to the Dragon hoping that it would be satisfied with livestock and whatever meager treasures they could find. Alas the Dragon was only emboldened and landed with a great roar in front of the village of Kayhurn demanding that once a month the villagers bring it young adolescents as a sacrifice. One day a young knight named Isota, rode north and heard the horrific stories of the dragon’s atrocities and proclaimed that they would slay the beast.

As Isota entered the Forests of Vanthar they came across a large glade where one of the young villagers lay bound awaiting the coming of the dragon. The villager asked Isota to flee and leave them to their fate but Isota refused and hid between the trees. When the dragon landed in the clearing, savouring the sacrifice in front of them, Isota charged from the side and managed to piece the thick dragon scales with a long spear of iron. This wounded the dragon but did not kill it and it roared in fury, spinning its wing and long tail around like a whip. A great battle ensued and though wounded, Isota emerged triumphant, cutting off the head of the Dragon and securing it to their mounts saddle* They returned to Kaythun in victory and were given a lavish celebration.**

*In some versions of the legend Isota removes the head but it bursts into flame, igniting the body of the dragon which burns down to blackened bone.

**Some early versions of the story claim that Isota marries the young villager they rescued, which caused some dispute in the region, as the villager was the village chieftain's son or daughter and gave Kaythun a considerable boost in prestige which other cities removed/ignored in later versions.
The Knight & The Dragon.scoverview: Though to be the original Kirargy Knight who went on to found the first order of Knights, however, the term Knight is not used until much later in history so this is likely a more modern change to the language. Isota is described in some stories as male while in others as female. It's also unknown whether they killed a dragon or some other creature as it's unlikely a mortal human would have been able to kill a Cruel Dragon alone.

The High King.name: The High King
The High King.text:
• Origin: Early Human

  • First Recorded: Directly after the Shattering, the modern account was transcribed in [[/date AS979]] by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QDRFnVBZ1jy3YiD0]{Laeora}.

  • Knowledge: Well known by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian}@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessian}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian} & @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}.

In the blackened dawn of the sunless age, a mythical warrior figure of legend strode the surface world. When the Shattering turned the clouds to cinders, the High King stood unbowed, a shield for the weak and a terror to the Malvorn. Alongside his Sorceress wife, the Lady Jena Frostfire, they held back the shroud from the beyond, unbowed by terror. Fenra raised the First Throne from the wreckage of the Sun Tower and cast down the first dragon, ensuring that mortals would endure forevermore. Now, though his crown is lost to the sands, his One Heroic Spirit remains, a phantom that flickers into existence in our darkest hours, to answer the cries of those facing insurmountable evil.

~Laeora

King @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.YNMxNE2TbhObyKMp]{Fenra Irdragon} was the legendary leader of the proto-@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} culture and the early Human Kingdoms following the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}. Born in 20 SY, Fenra was the only son of Fentwe Irdran, King of Masia, and his wife, Queen Leonor. He grew quickly, becoming a skilled scholar even while being schooled in swordcraft and weaponry by his father. His early life was happy enough, as his parents shielded him within the palace, yet a shadow had lain upon Masia for many years. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} kept a firm hand over King Fentwe and forced him to enact unpopular laws, including a yearly tithe to prevent the Aedir from deploying a garrison to the city.

In 2 SY, Queen Leonor was killed openly by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} for organizing a resistance movement among the people of Masia. King Fentwe was outraged and beyond reason; despite his advisors warning him that it would mean certain death for his people, he declared war upon the Sunfire Empire, executing its advisors and diplomats within the palace. Prince Fenra was then tasked with bolstering the city's defenses and training its people for war, a role in which he blossomed into a fearless leader and commander.

He traveled across the Aran Peninsula to Kortra, Lortu, @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen}, Nasjar, and even to distant @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.HN2Zimps4w5XniZe]{Carinth} in secret to strengthen ties between the Human Kingdoms. He often spoke publicly within city squares and towns, preaching of justice, honor, and freedom. It is said that Prince Fenra encountered the Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae} during these travels and he unknowingly helped her with simple tasks. Retrieving water, bringing food, and clearing her home of debris, while she hid her powers and true nature. Malae eventually revealed herself to Fenra and, thanking him for his kindness, gifted him a powerful charm of protection: a silver necklace set with a glowing red stone.

While in Nasjar, Prince Fenra encountered Lady Jena Frostfire, a skilled @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p6DGVnaLHZfLvGem]{Signborn} mage, and her small school of students. They were at first combative and were said to dislike each other immensely. However, after Fenra spent several weeks in the city attempting to convince the King of Nasjar to join their efforts, Lady Jena became enamored with his youthful ideals and sense of justice. It is thought that the two became lovers the night before Prince Fenra left Nasjar, although some believe this happened later.

Returning to Masia in 0 AS, Fenra and his father heard news of a great fleet being arrayed upon the shores of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Op5BD9XSlmb7l6NN]{Starshield} by the Aedir to the east, and that doom would soon fall upon them. While his father despaired, hearing that the forces deploying against Masia were the 1st Host, legendary imperial warriors commanded by the heir to the Sunfire Throne, Fenra remained resolute. He was bolstered by the commitment of the other Human Kingdoms and the fury his people felt toward the tyranny from across the seas.

Late one night, he was joined by Lady Jena, who brought him to a large palace chamber filled with hundreds of cowled figures. Jena revealed that she had found and convinced many fellow mages, wizards, and sorcerers to aid their cause. Standing within the center of the chamber, Prince Fenra was shocked to discover that the assembly knelt before him, pledging their loyalty to him personally. Many had heard his words and ideals as he traveled from city to city, and his legend had already begun to spread.

The Shattering

In 0 AS, during the height of summer, the greatest calamity in history struck the Aedir in a night of unimaginable destruction. The @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering} annihilated the Aedir nearly instantaneously, including the 1st Host arrayed upon their ships along the coastline of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Op5BD9XSlmb7l6NN]{the Starshield}. Masia, which lay upon the eastern edges of the Aran Peninsula, suffered greatly in the immediate aftermath, as earthquakes and shards of the Sun tower fell upon the city, yet a sense of satisfaction spread throughout the population. After all, had the Aedir not been stopped by some great force or fate? Alas, this feeling of relief and triumph lasted only a few weeks.

As the forces of the young nations stood allied together to face a common foe, they were, by some stroke of fate or design, perfectly positioned to confront a new coming shadow. While the sky still burned, Masia was attacked by creatures of utter evil and terror. The city was engulfed in a black fog that the people called the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{Shroud} as horrific Monsters arrived upon the World of Ember for the first time, quickly becoming known as the Malvorn. Overwhelmed and dismayed, the people watched as only the combined strength of the magical adepts arrayed within the city prevented a total collapse. In the fighting, King Fentwe was killed in front of the palace, his body mutilated and carried away by the horrors.

During this battle, a strange calm seemed to surround the young Prince Fenra; those around him were shocked to discover he had become akin to a tightly controlled, raging fire. The alien monsters died wherever he walked, and his presence even gave them pause as he sprang from one front to another, defeating one after another with incredible feats of strength and skill. He rallied the people of Masia, and after a terrible night of fighting and slaughter, the Shroud finally cleared.

While the initial attack on Masia had been repelled, the attackers by the Malvorn did not relent, and as the days and weeks passed, they attacked again and again. With the help of the assembly of magical adepts, Prince Fenra aided the other cities of the Aran Peninsula, appearing where he was most needed alongside his core group of fellow heroes and warriors. At some point in the fighting, he was joined by the young Shard God Maltkasa, who struggled mightily to aid their cause. However, the power arrayed against them was unrelenting, and Fenra’s friends began to fall, one after another, until at last only Prince Fenra and Lady Jena stood back-to-back against the monsters surrounding them.

It was then that the unexpected occurred: a strange red and golden glow began to shine forth in the sky above. It spread across the heavens to encompass the world, and its strength banished the Shroud utterly. The surviving Malvorn cowered and despaired, fleeing into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} of Ember.

The First Throne

With the immediate threat of the Malvorn seemingly banished, Prince Fenra turned his gaze toward the monumental task of rebuilding. The @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.NdqwtFoFAw85Gstr]{Aran Peninsula} was a landscape of broken monuments, hidden monsters, maddened creatures, and displaced peoples; yet, under Fenra’s guidance, a new era of cooperation and slow reconciliation began. After he was crowned with a simple iron band as the King of Masia, a hasty ceremony devoid of trapping or fanfare, he traveled once more between the battered walls of Kortra, Lortu, and Nasjar, @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen}, and the distant cities of the north not as a warrior, but as an architect of peace. He organized the clearing of the Shrouds' residue and oversaw the restoration of vital trade routes and farmlands, ensuring that the famine following the Shattering and the arrival of monsters did not claim the lives of those who had survived the slaughter.

During the following winter, however, monsters emerged from the Pathways to attack the city of Masia and other cities, and Fenra realized that desperate measures were required. After consulting with his gathered allies, he decided to undertake one of his most mythical feats. Recognizing that a new age required a new foundation, Fenra led a daring expedition to the Starshield. He was joined by Lady Jena, the Shard Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka}, and the Historian @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QDRFnVBZ1jy3YiD0]{Laeora}.

The journey across the seas was long and arduous, aided in part by the ancient god of the storms, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu}. The small party of heroes landed upon the broken shores of the once glittering realm. What they encountered there was said to be a host of nightmares, newly created undead spirits and ghosts, terrifying new monsters, and the still-smoking ruins of a people laid low. Seeking to reclaim what remained of the Aedir’s power, Fenra traveled deep into the Starshield to the ancient city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.kpLyA8T7vbOvn35H]{Towir}, within the Sun Tower itself. The journey was a harrowing descent into evil and the lingering corruption of the Shroud. His party of companions prevailed, however, and Fenra discovered a small artifact, one that some say was a lingering echo of the Aedir’s last Emperor or a fragment of their lost power.

Fenra returned to Masia in triumph. Using the artifact and scattered fragments of the Sun Tower, he forged the First Throne, a massive structure and fortress on the eastern shores of the Aran Peninsula. This seat was more than a symbol of power; it was a metaphysical bastion. By binding the artifact's magical power to the throne's stones, Fenra created a sanctuary that radiated a subtle ward of protection that seemed to repel the Shroud and monsters of all kinds.
