This ward could be replicated, and a portion of its strength was lent to all the other human kingdoms in the Aran Peninsula and beyond, and it even imbued humans of that era with even greater strength, magics, and abilities. After the completion of the First Throne, Fenra Irdragon was honored to accept the title of High King after a unanimous vote was held in the great chamber by the other kings. It was also here that Fenra publicly recognized Lady Jena as his wife and partner, much to her chagrin and shy embarrassment. Alas, while Fenra celebrated and the young human kingdoms began to finally recover, there was one last threat that threatened the human realms, and few had the foresight to see it.

Emergence of Dragons

In 7 AS, a few years after the peace of the First Throne had begun to settle, a terror of unimaginable proportions descended upon the world. Tamorderin, the first of the great @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{dragons} of Ember, appeared in the summer sky. The beast was so immense that it blotted out the sun, casting a shadow of doom over the land. In a single night of fire and blood, Tamorderin sacked and burned the city of Lortu, massacring its people and leaving the proud walls a smoldering ruin. No one could have known that such horrific beasts of evil and unparalleled strength and power could possibly exist, as Tamorderin dwarfed the ancient powers of Leviathans and even the Shard Gods that tried to stand against it.

Refusing to let the young kingdoms be extinguished, Fenra and Lady Jena led a vast army forth from the First Throne. With a sound said to echo into the halls of legend, this host of humanity rode like thunder, with the hooves of Kitnen rising and falling like the drums of clashing gods. Arrayed against the first dragon, they finally found it feasting on the remains of a large town in the northern lands, and with the blaring of great horns, they charged the beast of fire and blood.

The clash was said to be cataclysmic as the greatest army of humanity, bolstered by the magic of the First Throne, stood against the primeval fury of the first great dragon. Swathes of mighty warriors perished with every fiery breath of the beast, but the mortals fought on. Spears rained down upon its hide like iron needles, and arrows ripped through its wings, shredding them in tatters. Magic swirled in chaotic vortexes, and lightning thundered through the smoke-choked air as the mages of the Assembly threw every spell of destruction they could muster at the roaring, snarling beast.

At the center of the carnage stood Fenra. Witnesses claimed he seemed to shine with an inner golden light, a radiance that matched the ferocity of the dragon’s flames. In the final, shattering confrontation, Fenra faced the monster head-on, standing alone as warriors of the Throne lay dead and dying around him. Lady Jena, gravely injured and watching in horror, looked on as Fenra delivered the killing blow, slaying Tamorderin and ending its reign of terror. But the victory came at a terrible cost. His crown broken and shattered, Fenra lay mortally wounded, his lifeblood spilling onto the scorched earth alongside that of the dragon.

A slow, somber procession brought the dying King back to the eastern shores, to the sanctuary of the First Throne. There, surrounded by his remaining allies and his beloved Jena, Fenra passed peacefully. Yet, death did not claim him as it did others, and his spirit did not rise and travel to the Spiritlands. Instead, as his final breath left him, his body dissolved into a bright, golden mist that shimmered in the air before disappearing entirely.

One Heroic Spirit

In the years following his death, and in the centuries that have unfolded since, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.YNMxNE2TbhObyKMp]{Fenra Irdragon} has been sighted again and again across the World of Ember. His manifestation is described as a vision of stillness, grace, and immense power; he appears not as a ghost, but as a calming presence that defies the darkness. He is not a deity to be worshipped from afar, nor is he a restless undead bound by sorrow. Instead, Fenra has crystallized into an entity of profound strength, a warrior-king of justice who retains all his mortal memories and his tireless willingness to aid those in dire need.

Across the ages, he has appeared on crumbling battlements when all hope was lost, or stood beside a lone traveler facing a monster in the dark. He does not speak, but his presence acts grants them the courage to stand unbowed against the impossible. To this day, many across the scattered kingdoms still regard him as the one and true High King of their people. They believe that while crowns break and cities may fall, the King of Masia still walks the hidden paths of the world, waiting for the moment when a hero's cry reaches across the veil.

He is the reminder that even when the world shatters, and the sky burns, a single man can hold the pieces together if his heart is true. He does not come for the kings or the powerful; he comes for the person who refuses to kneel before evil.

~Laeora
The High King.scoverview: A legend from the time just after the Shattering two and a half thousand years ago. Modern scholars dispute many of the place names and peoples involved, as they no longer exist and may have been fictitious additions to the legends. Masia was abandoned during the events of the Virulent Plague, but it's rumored to still exist as a colossal ruin buried beneath earth and sand somewhere in the southern Aran Peninsula. High King Fenra was a real figure who appears repeatedly throughout history, but accounts are few and far between, and many accounts are not considered reliable.

The Spellbreaker.name: The Spellbreaker
The Spellbreaker.text:
• Origin: Ordani

  • Knowledge: Well known by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian} & @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}.

The founding of Ordain is well recorded, with many detailed firsthand accounts that have survived throughout the centuries. However, a less well-documented event and tale from around 600 years ago tells of Avilla, the First Shard God of Ordain. Her story has become akin to a folktale and legend for the people of Ordain, but many of the details and true facts remain unknown.

Historiain Drevin Markus - [[/date AS2403]]

Avilla of Ordain

During the construction of the grand Cindarin Temple in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} allegedly* discovered an earth-shattering secret. The tall plateau upon which the temple was being built concealed a mythical @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal}, lodged in the black basalt foundations. The Sages kept the discovery secret for many years and treated the Heart Crystal as a sacred relic, hiding it away in a deep chamber. Over time, many attempted to attune to its radiant Lifeforce, but all who tried were consumed in the process.

One day, a child initiate sought comfort and quietude at the foot of the Heart Crystal. The young girl was named @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Q0iioq0o2q011r8x]{Avilla}, and she was raised almost entirely by the Sages themselves after a cruel warlock had killed her family. As an orphan, she became an initiate of the Sages out of necessity, and she was said to have been a gloomy and withdrawn figure. No one outside of the Cindaric Sages knew of the Heart Crystal's existence, but she often sat within the chamber to be alone with her thoughts, as did many other Sages at the time. Over the course of several years, an inexplicable understanding seems to have formed between Avilla and the Heart Crystal, without anyone within the Sages noticing. As the sun rose one day over the city, the Sages were shocked to discover Avilla calmly sitting within the chamber, with a now inert and lifeless Heart Crystal in front of her. She had become the first @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God} of their order and of Ordain.

Avilla had little interest in using her divinity at first and had not communed with the Heart Crystal to gain power, merely engaging in meditation and attempting to find peace. While the Sages rejoiced and proclaimed her ascension to the people, asking her to help them, she struggled with her newfound gifts. Over time, the divine power that she now controlled became an uncomfortable weight, and she began to withdraw even further from those around her. She sought anonymity where she could and refused any attempts by the people of Ordain to venerate her.

The Spellbreaker

As Ordain grew, it drew the attention of distant hostile forces, and dark storm clouds gathered on the horizon. Strange ships of unknown design** and make sailed into the bay of Ordain, driven forth by winged creatures of the sea. In an instant, the city erupted in chaos as spellcraft and magery sprang forth, smashing into the buildings and ships across the bay. The fledgling @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} rose to combat the threat but had little answer to the magical forces arrayed against them. The city itself seemed lost until Avilla walked out upon the water into the middle of the battle and drew upon her divine power. For miles around, magic was silenced; no spellcraft nor artifact had any effect, and mages of all kinds clutched their heads in pain. Protected from the mages' evocations, the Burnished Hand turned the battle by firing fire arrows into the helpless foreign ships, and the entire fleet sank into the dark waters***.

In playing this crucial role in defense of the city, Avilla displayed a shocking amount of power that caused the city's population to recoil in fear. Whispers began during the battle's aftermath that she was internally fighting her own gifts and that she was losing control. The whispers and rumors spread rapidly, and Avilla made the decision to leave the city. Before she left, she met with the Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages at the time and made a secret pact. She raised a tower on a plateau on the western end of the city and infused this tower with the essence of her power. Throughout its halls, the wild currents of magic stilled, spells having no effect. This tower became a place of solitude and silence, where those haunted by magical afflictions could find respite and where dangerous magics could be contained.

Avilla then disappeared without comment or ceremony. She had no desire to remain in a city that saw her as a hero, a deity, and a menace all at once. However, the tower she built remains a lasting tribute to her legacy as the first Shard God of Ordain. Her story serves as a cautionary tale about the unchecked threats posed by both mages and Shard Gods in general, leading many in the city to perceive her as a tragic individual who sought solitude and had untameable power thrust upon her.

* My own research into the tale suggests that the Sages found the Heart Crystal somewhere else in the world, and there are hints that they had to bring it up to the plateau where the temple was being built.
** No one is entirely sure who was in control of the strange ships that attacked Ordain. My own theory is that they came from the extremely distant continent of Atou, based on a few scattered artifacts dredged from the Bay of Ordain over the years.
*** No records exist of any survivors, and the tales and stories do not mention anyone being held captive after the battle.
The Spellbreaker.scoverview: The tale of Avilla the Spellbreaker is the story of the first Ordani Shard God, who rejected their own divine power while saving the city in a climactic battle with invading mages from across the sea. Avilla left Ordain with an enduring legacy, a great tower on its eastern edge where weavings of magic fail and spells cease to function.

Foreword.name: Foreword
Foreword.text:
Creating a living world as expansive and detailed as Ember is a lifelong dream for myself and others on our team. Each aspect of Ember’s lore; its geography, cosmology, cartography, history, ancestries, cultures, and more has been carefully developed so that every design choice is meaningful. While the Ember Setting is a wondrous and immersive piece of fiction in its own right, one of the fundamental goals behind its creation was to design a sprawling open-world game for Foundry Virtual Tabletop where its worldbuilding features and cosmology affect the day-to-day and even moment-to-moment mechanics of the game itself.

Author of the Setting Compendium

The Historian @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QDRFnVBZ1jy3YiD0]{Laeora} is responsible for writing the majority of the Settign Compendium in an in-universe voice, drawing on her own perspective, gathered notes, and experiences across the ages. Throughout the writing, there are also a few 1st-person notes from her that offer a new perspective on the lore, history, and events.

Mysteries of the Living Cosmos

As you delve into the lore and the intricacies of the setting, you'll notice the term 'Ember' frequently repeated. This is a deliberate design choice, “Ember” serves as the title, the name for the Cosmos, the world, and most intriguingly the enigmatic object at the very center of it all: the Heart of Ember. This serves as a solid foundation, a point of reference before the complexity of the setting begins to unfold.

Ember’s lore is a powerful foundation that supports and enhances gameplay with worldbuilding themes that appear consistently throughout the story from session one until the story’s ultimate conclusion. These worldbuilding concepts will be gradually unveiled to players as the game progresses without the need to master these topics beforehand. We hope you find the setting and incredible attention to detail as cool as we do, so if you are excited to learn about this lore and how Ember's cosmology interacts with gameplay, keep reading!

Caeora
Creative Director and Lorekeeper
Foreword.scoverview:
During the continuing development of the Ember Game and beyond, the Ember Setting will continue to evolve alongside it. It is regrettable and unfortunate that so many of my ideas and thoughts around the setting remain tied up in my head or in note form, which is too rough to share publicly. It has also become clear to me that the way ive written certain pieces of information or lore is sometimes not entirely the way I intended it to come across, and my writing ability itself is at fault.

If you come across information that is not clear or ideas and lore that references other pieces of content that seem critical to the understanding of that piece, it may be intentional, or it may be a mistake or simply unintended. Reach out and provide feedback if you can, and I will do my best to improve things so that what I have written really shines for everyone!

Setting Introduction.name: Setting Introduction
Setting Introduction.text:
Manifest Deities

The Ember Setting is filled with hundreds of Ascendant Deities called Shard Gods, who walk upon the surface world and live among the mortal peoples. They are very real, tangible beings with huge impacts as they express their ideas, fight among themselves, and change the outcomes of events around them. Some Shard Gods are truly ancient, having existed since the first peoples arose on Ember. Others are incredibly young and have ascended much more recently. Every deity is a complex character with their own motivations and goals, and they are just as fallible and susceptible to mistakes and failures as the mortals around them are.

Even the Elder Gods of the Cosmos, of which only five exist, reside within the cosmos itself and walk the surface talking to mortals, maintaining their ideas of Cosmic Balance and safeguarding the world.

Singular Cosmos

The Ember Cosmos is exactly as described: a singular Cosmos where everything exists in Physical Space. There are no other planes of existence, parallel universes, or dimensions. This means that everything can be reached through conventional travel or teleportation magic, even the most esoteric and mysterious realms of Ember such as the Spiritlands, where a mortal Soul travels to when they die, or the wonderous and deadly Inner Realms that rest upon the inner surface of the Weave.

The World Within

The Ember Cosmos is like a multifaceted gem. It has a protective bubble called the Weave that shields everything within from the horrors and madness of the Abyss. At the center of the Cosmos is the World of Ember, where numerous cultures, mortal peoples, and deities live and survive. Then, deep within the world itself resides the Heart of Ember, some say the entity or object that created the cosmos long ago.

Portentous History

Many cultures on Ember today have histories dating back two-and-a-half thousand years, either before or after the Shattering — when the colossal Aedir Empire ruled over vast territories and built the astounding structure of the Sun Tower before its cataclysmic destruction. However, the history of Ember stretches back long before the Aedir. Indeed, Ember's oldest cultures have histories that reach back into a past so deep and unknowable, all that remains are the myths and legends of the forgotten people who founded them.

Breathtaking Scale

Ember is a very different kind of setting that offers characters new definitions for discovery and scale. As the world's six moons drift across the sky, the colossal Broken Tower looms above everything — visible no matter where one might be on the surface of the living planet. Even Ember's ancestries and cultures are all unique to the setting, and are deeply tied to its vast history, innovative worldbuilding, and imaginative storytelling. Everywhere you look, the world of Ember serves as a potent reminder about precisely how fantastical and wondrous a setting can be.

New Horrors

During the Abyssal Shear that occurred not long after the Shattering, the protective barrier of the Weave was breached, allowing the maddening and terrifying influence of the Abyss to flow into the Cosmos directly. This event was arguably even worse for the Cosmos than the preceding Shattering, and Abyssal Monsters were able to spread across the cosmos physically for the first time. The Abyssal Shear also introduced entirely new concepts into the Cosmos, such as Undeath and Oblivion. After the Shear, Dragons, terrifying scaled monsters linked intrinsically to abyssal energy, were created and have ravaged the cosmos ever since.

Magical Omnipresence

Magic is everywhere in the Ember Setting; it is so common, depending on certain circumstances, that it can be seen crystallized into visible motes that drift through the air. There are many types of Magic, from the Lifeforce of the Heart of Ember, the mystical magic of Light, Darkness, and Shadow of the three Inner Realms, the elemental magic directed from the Elemental Moons, and even the combinations of these forces known as Arcane magic.
Setting Introduction.scoverview: The Ember setting is, in essence, a High Fantasy setting, where magical forces, gods, strange creatures, and epic storytelling are everywhere. Early on in development, we coined the phrase Imaginative fantasy to express our desire for a very different kind of setting, one where the scale, breadth, and fantastical elements of the setting defied conventional ideas and pushed a wilder and grander vision for the world and storytelling. This does not mean smaller and more grounded stories do not exist; they simply occur in the context of a very strange and imaginative world.

Identity, Sex & Gender.name: Identity, Sex & Gender
Identity, Sex & Gender.text:
The Ember Setting is fantasy. Imaginative, wondrous fantasy, and it is doing its best to create something new while paying homage to older ideas and concepts. The world of Ember is massive, and features a variety of cultures with differing beliefs that may be controversial, some of the ideas and beliefs held by certain cultures are not universal. This game may, at times, present themes of hatred and intolerance that may affect certain characters based on their sex, gender, or other aspects of their identity. When dealing with topics of this nature it is important to be clear that the ember team does not condone nor accept such intolerant viewpoints; rather, we want to confront these topics head-on.

The Ember Setting as a whole is not built upon modern oppositional ideas surrounding identity, sex, or gender. Racism, homophobia, and transphobia do not exist in the same way in Ember as they do in our world. In fact, across almost every culture in the setting, there is no societal hatred nor persecution of anyone perceived as "different". The setting has been carefully constructed from the ground up with these things in mind.

The massive variety of Ancestries means that any differences in physical appearance simply aren't seen the same way as it is on Earth. Racism does not exist in Ember. People see one another as people or mortals rather than as their specific ancestry, and there is a shared understanding of what it means to struggle in a world filled with monsters and chaos. This goes a step further with the Aster, who, while rarer among the world's cultures and peoples, are never, in any case, considered oddities or different in any negative way but are seen as blessed by the Heart of Ember. Tensions related to Ancestry that may appear have far more to do with cultural conflict than mere appearance.

Homophobia does not exist in Ember; lacking earth's post-puritanical concepts of sexuality, love between consenting partners is viewed as part of the societal norm, regardless of gender. This draws inspiration from many ancient earth cultures. Some cultures of Ember have patriarchal societies but also matriarchal ones as well with most cultures having no particular bias or inequality between genders. Transphobia does not exist in Ember; many cultures have widely-celebrated heroes or deities have that have either transitioned or present genderless identities. Most notable among these is @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, who is principally the Goddess of Creation and the most powerful being in the Cosmos.

With this in mind, stories in Ember that present queer issues do so not as struggles against systemic oppression and prejudice, as this is something that doesn't exist except in extremely specific, more character-driven examples, instead and unfortunately for them, there are simply many other struggles in Ember that people need to overcome.

There are areas of Ember where hatred and intolerance do exist among people who have deeply rooted historical biases for specific groups. One example of such is the prejudice among many cultures toward the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} who caused the calamity known as the Shattering. There are other more modern examples as well; for instance, in the present, as the Tayan Empire is attempting to conquer the Kalmezian City States there is dislike and even hatred held between the peoples of both cultures. Overall, however, discrimination stems from the conflict between peoples, cultures, and individuals whose actions are their own and specific to Ember.

For those Gamemasters who wish to engage with topics of hatred and prejudice in Ember, it is important to remember that people do not form hatred in a vacuum. Hatred and prejudice are learned behaviors, and they do not start on a global or societal level. The average person in a world like Ember does not care about wider global sociopolitical issues as they are not directly affected by them, they care more about issues that have a direct impact on their own lives.
Identity, Sex & Gender.scoverview: Ember was built by a multicultural team of creative individuals from a wide variety of backgrounds and with diverse views. Ember's writing and design intentionally embraces diversity and acceptance in all things.

Ashka.name: Ashka
Ashka.text:
Ashka are a slender snake-like ancestry with several aquatic traits that make them ideally suited for semi-aquatic environments such as swamps, coastlines, and humid jungles. They can also breathe underwater for extended periods, far more than most other ancestries. Their most prominent physical trait is their hooded and flared head shape that falls across their shoulders and often connects to their back muscles. These hoods are not always present but the majority of Ashka exhibit them in some form. Their bodies are covered in delicate scales and softer facial skin with intricate and colorful patterns intertwining their entire bodies and heads. Some Ashka break these conventions, and their appearance is less smooth and rougher overall with pronounced scales, ridged brows, and rougher, completely scaled bodies even on the face. Their necks are slightly longer than those of many other ancestors, and coupled with their flexibility, they have the ability to quickly twist and turn, observing the world around them in all directions. Ashka also possess long thick tails that are partially prehensile and sometimes capable of impressive feats of dexterity and propel them through the water.

Ashka possess several less obvious but key traits, such as webbed hands and feet that allow them to swim more efficently and nostril slits with heat-sensing pits that allow them to track and sense warm-blooded creatures. It is thought that Ashka may have been created as proficient and adaptable hunters for semi-forested mangroves and jungles as they are exceptionally well suited to those wetter environments. Unfortunately, this makes them sensitive in other areas, and they are far less comfortable in dry climates and biomes, experiencing dry skin, scale conditions and lung diseases.

An Ashka eye deviates from most serpentine creatures and are not commonly slit like a snake, instead possessing a round pupil and coming in a wide range of colors. Their sclera is rarely white and instead a rich yellow or orange, giving Ashka a slightly predatory appearance. Ashka are known to be able to sense creatures with their thermal imaging pits on their face. Still, it's not known if this is somehow connected to their eyes, as they have exceptional vision overall. The combination may be responsible for their remarkable ability to perceive nearby and distant objects under extremely difficult conditions.

Biology

Ashka biology uniquely differs from other ancestries and seems carefully and tightly controlled or crafted in several aspects. Their skeletons have many hundreds of thin bones, which gives them incredible flexibility, and the position of the key organs is neatly organized with their hearts resting in the center of their chests between large lungs. Ashka are also mesotherms, a strange cross between cold-blooded and warm-blooded creatures. They can raise their body temperatures consciously but typically run their bodies cold-blooded, making them fond of warmer temperatures and fire. However, this comes at some cost, and an Ashka’s body requires a certain amount of humidity to remain healthy as their bodies use and require more water than other ancestries.

Ashka are particularly adept at underwater movement with many physical traits such as webbed hands and feet and thick muscular tails, which aid them in underwater movement. Their blood is also able to hold onto more oxygen than other ancestries, giving them the ability to hold their breaths for long periods, but this comes at a cost, and Ashka are vulnerable to air pollutants that can affect the lungs and prone to lasting lung damage that affects them permanently.

Ashka Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information. Ashka are Humanoids derived from the Jarn ancestry and are thus compatible with other Humanoids.

Cultural Connections

The Ashka do not currently have any significant cultural dominance they can call their own on the surface of Ember. However, it is claimed that long ago, during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of Sunlight}, they had their own rich and storied culture called the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.4RM8MIiCDWMFv2yr]{Sedyri}. This is something that most Ashka are taught by their parents, which may seem ancestry-based from the outside but can sometimes include others and may indeed originate from this incredibly ancient culture. Most Ashka live in small family groups, and as part of larger cultures, they often form small enclaves and try to maintain some semblance of their own cultural identity. These enclaves try to keep the history and traditions alive as best they can, but each successive generation becomes increasingly integrated into the cultures around them. Ashka are rare among most cultures but not unheard of and can be found in many far-off lands, more often as sailors, traders, or adventurers.
Ashka.scoverview: Ashka are an ancient serpentine, amphibious ancestry originally created by the goddess Scoris during the Age of Beasts. They are now scattered across the World of Ember and are integrated into many different cultures, clinging on to some of their ancestral traditions and beliefs. Ashka are generally tall and slender with scaled skin, remarkable eyesight, and innate adaptability to aquatic environments. Because of their rarity and snakelike appearance, they are occasionally mistaken for Aster by those unfamiliar with their unique history.
Ashka.sgamemaster: The Ashka were created from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.V1gzeX0JWSOCQ7LD]{Jarn} by the Shard Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.sa5TtcQvRnu3NbtN]{Scoris}, who was particularly fascinated with serpents and snakes. According to legend, when Scoris ascended during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}, she transformed many of her loved ones and family members into a new ancestry called the Ashka and quickly set about creating an idyllic place for them on the island of Sedyra, which would one day be known as @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.dx4RuTFlrsNTsBw3]{Kadísos}. The age and legacy of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.4RM8MIiCDWMFv2yr]{Sedyri} culture and the Ashka is impressive, and the ruins of their lasting presence on Ember's surface cannot be understated. Much of the true history of the Sedyri remains lost, forgotten, and buried, but it's thought that the Ashka once covered much of the southern regions of Aterica with several distinct cultures and nations. The legends of numerous floating cities, mighty empires, and kingdoms persist among treasure seekers and scholars today, and the artifacts and relics found in strange, incredibly ancient ruins tell a tantalizing tale of a once mighty people.

Zeph.name: Zeph
Zeph.text:
Zeph are magical winds that have coalesced into human form, made from the primeval gales of the hollow Wind Moon, Aura. Their semi-corporeal and semi-translucent form can vary, but is generally soft and light, with the clothing a Zeph wears and the items they carry creating much of their physical silhouette. A Zeph's core body is generally stormcloud gray, but their extremities can be a wider range of colors and illuminations. Often, the brightest color is seen in their hair, which extends from behind their mask in elaborate (and sometimes gravity-defying) configurations.

Each Zeph is born with a mask, which changes as the Zeph themself does. The masks may appear to others to hover in the air in front of a Zeph, but it is in fact the core of who each Zeph is, both biologically and spiritually. While Zeph are corporeal enough to take damage from direct physical contact, they are particularly vulnerable if their mask is damaged in any way, and do their best to deflect or avoid any blows that would harm it, often using the wind magic that comes from their connection with Aura. Zeph can also use their masks to express emotion, shifting them at will to reflect the Zeph's current personality.

Biology

A Zeph’s mask is their source of physical constitution and spiritual potency. The more damaged or exhausted a Zeph becomes, the more insubstantial their physical form generally becomes, but the mask endures. The mask is believed to help Zeph recover physically from injury, as Zeph are especially vulnerable if their masks are damaged in any way, and their masks remain behind when they die, unlike the rest of their body, which dissipates over time.

The form behind a Zeph's masks is partially translucent and partially non-corporeal — a reflection of the wind magic that they possess from their link with Aura. While they have enough physical form to wear clothing, carry items, and take damage, Zeph's ability to shift the edges of their swirling form can make them difficult targets to hit during combat scenarios.

Unlike many of Ember’s humanoid ancestries, Zeph do not reproduce naturally. New Zeph generally generate spontaneously from the winds of Aura, finding their way to the city of Conundrum by instinct. Zeph propagation on Ember has been noted to have happened on Ember, but is not well known, other than the fact that their emergence generally corresponds with the Wind Moon's Zenith.

Zeph Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more.

Zeph are not corporeal in a traditional sense, and thus not able to reproduce with any other ancestries, though some cultures do have legends that revolve around the star-crossed romance between a Zeph and a more corporeal ancestry. Depicting the offspring of a Zeph would likely be best expressed via an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik]{Aster} ancestry.

Cultural Connections

The majority of Zeph occupy the city-state of Conundrum, located at the hollow core of the Wind Moon, but in the modern age, some have sought their purpose elsewhere, with some exploring the depths of the Inner Realm of Primordis and others traveling across the face of Ember itself. As they occur on Ember fairly rarely, and often come to Ember in pursuit of something that they could not find in Conundrum or on Aura more broadly, Zeph on Ember generally either live solitary lives or focus on making connections with those of other ancestries and cultural backgrounds on Ember, using their personal connections as the measure of how they should live their lives and interact with the world around them.
Zeph.scoverview: Zeph hail from Aura, the elemental moon of air, and are only very rarely seen on the surface of Ember. Their swirling vaporous forms are vaguely humanoid in shape and known for their arcane masks — unique physical representation of their soul that can evolve in size, shape, or pattern over the course of their lives. Zeph are able to control their masks, using them to show emotions, communicate with other ancestries, and, in some cases, hide their identities. A Zeph's mask is also the only piece of themselves left behind physically when they die, though some believe that the air within a Zeph somehow returns to Aura, as they remain tied to the moon even when on Ember, and generally possess some of Aura's wind magic.

Nir'ae.name: Nir'ae
Nir'ae.text:
Though the Aedir Empire stretched across Ember at its height, encompassing many different ancestries, it was most closely tied to the Nir'ae, an ancestry whose magical energy could be clearly seen in their iridescent birthmarks and skin patterns. These patterns, caused by exposure to the arcane artifacts under the Empire's control, were often seen as a mark of someone favored by the Empire. That changed when the Empire fell, bringing about the cataclysmic Shattering. Many Nir'ae were killed, the world plunged into chaos, and the markings that were once a point of pride began to be viewed with mistrust.

In the present day, Nir'ae are very rare but can be found throughout Ember. They remain tied to the forces of the cosmos and have retained their connection to magic despite the many generations that have passed since the fall of the Aedir Empire. Nir'ae may draw power from great arcane artifacts and, though it has been generations since the Aedir Empire was lost, they can still commune with Ember, gaining some measure of power during the moons' zeniths.

Biology

Nir'ae are tall, lithe humanoids whose long, tapered ears frame their wide-eyed countenance. These ears can be moved independently from the rest of the Nir'ae face and from each other, and can be used to express emotion or add extra meaning. Similarly, the color of the irises in a Nir'ae’s large eyes are known to change several times throughout the seasons of their lifespan, often tied to major moments of magical expression or personal change. Their skin tones and hair colors, which remain the same throughout their lifetimes, come from a wide palette of shades, with hues that reflect their proximity to Lantyr at the time of their birth.

The most striking physical feature of the Nir'ae is their iridescent birthmarks, which generally run across the sharp angles of their face and torso. The patterns appear on a Nir'ae at birth and can grow and shift with age. They're also more than cosmetic, generating a magical effect that provide the Nir'ae some protection from spells and harmful magic, and allowing them to draw upon the magical forces of Ember at times and places where they are especially potent, such as during a moon zenith.

These markings, along with the ancestry's inherent connection to magic, comes from the Nir'ae's long exposure to the arcane influence of the Eye of Aedon and Heart of Ember during the many thousands of years that the Aedir Empire made their home in the Starshield.

Nir'ae Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information.

Nir'ae are Humanoid and thus able to reproduce with other Humanoid ancestries. Due to the relative rarity of the ancestry and the fact that some Nir'ae hide their origins when within the broader world, little is known about their descendants.

Cultural Connections

For most on Ember, Nir'ae are an ancient memory. Most of the Nir'ae were killed when the Sun Tower built by the Aedir Empire exploded, killing everyone on the Starshield and beginning the era known as the Shattering. Though the Aedir Empire contained members of a variety of ancestries, many of their more visible and well-known leaders were Nir'ae, leading some to tie the ancestry to the Empire's hubris and view them with suspicion or distrust.

Several cultural expressions popular during the Aedir Empire's heyday, including the use of cosmetics to emphasize or substitute for Nir'ae skin markings, became deeply unpopular overnight, and many Nir'ae joined new cultural communities and distanced themselves from anything having to do with Aediri culture. The largest exception is the hidden people of the Lorai, who left the Starshield long before the Shattering for a life underground, deep beneath the mountains of northern Oakengard. Most Nir'ae who can be found in the present day come from that area, though there are small isolated groups elsewhere in Ember.

When living outside of the mountains, some Nir'ae still hide their true ancestry and lineage, even though the present day reaction to them tends more towards fascination and surprise than prejudice, especially on the Arctus Plateau and in Ordain. Others have become interested in the past of the Aedir Empire, traveling Ember in search of the Empire's lost history, and others have no real tie to what they view as ancient history and have fully integrated themselves into another modern culture.

Playing as a Nir'ae Character

Nir'ae are the rarest of the playable ancestries in Ember, and their tendency to isolate themselves could make them more challenging to play. We suggest that the GM and player discuss the decision to ensure that both are comfortable before choosing this route. With that mind, it can be a rewarding choice, as there is a great deal of lost lore about both the Nir'ae, and the Aedir Empire that they were once the dominant ancestry of, to be found within Ember as written.
Nir'ae.scoverview: Nir’ae, who have a biological tie to magic and an affinity with the energies of the cosmos, once formed the backbone of the world-spanning Aedir Empire. In the aftermath of the Shattering, a global cataclysm caused by Aediri hubris, the Nir'ae became a rare and scattered ancestry that is at times incorrectly blamed for the devastation caused by the empire. For those who know of them, Nir'ae are easy to recognize — their bodies are covered in iridescent birthmarks that reflect their prowess with magic and often glow when they cast spells — but some Nir'ae hide these markings, not wanting to be tied to the misguided deeds of their distant ancestors.

Kiska.name: Kiska
Kiska.text:
Though it has been eons since the Kiska left their Casia ancestors in the Inner Realm of Primordis and came to Ember, they still retain many connections to their ancestral roots. Physically, they have several cat-like features, including furred ears and shoulders, claw-like fingers, long thick tails, and mane-like hair. This hair is often worn long to showcase both its glowing roots and dramatic length, and is generally found in shades of red, yellow, and orange that match the colors of Kiska eyes.

Beyond their appearance, all Kiska retain some connection to the shadow magic common on Primordis, giving them the ability to fade into the shadows or blend into a crowd without being noticed, despite their striking looks. Many are drawn to spellcasting, feeling a sense of familiarity when they practice magic, especially with spells that utilize darkness, shadow, or illusion. Even those Kiska who do not use magic have a general sense of when it is being used around them and an instinct for when they might be under threat, though this is rarely specific or targeted enough for them to pinpoint its exact source.

Biology

Kiska are humanoid, though they have several adaptations that make them both tough and nimble. Their hyperflexible joints allow them to turn and bend in ways that many others cannot, and they are capable of short bursts of speed when needed, though this does not often translate into long-term endurance. This, like their cat-like physical features, is thought to be a result of their Casia ancestors, who are known ambush predators. Kiska also have light-sensitive eyes, which give them the ability to see well in the darkness and dim light, and, for some, see the resonance of magic in the world when it is intense enough, as happens during moon zeniths or in the presence of powerful artifacts.

Though Kiska often stand out on Ember, thanks to their relative rarity, boldly colored hair, and long tails, they have the ability to obscure their physical form when they wish to, blurring the edges of their bodies and hair to blend into the shadows and becoming almost invisible to those who are not fully focusing on them.

Kiska Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information.

Kiska are compatible with other Humanoids on Ember and can reproduce with any other Humanoid ancestry. Their relative rarity and occasional standoffishness mean that little is known about the impact of Kiska heritage on their descendants.

Cultural Connections

Kiska have been on Ember for generations, since the days of the Shattering, but have a small enough population that they have always been more likely to blend into other cultures than create a set culture of their own. Their connection to the magic of the Inner Planes, which few others share, can also give Kiska the sense that they are more evolved than other ancestries and should observe them rather than truly integrating with them, though this attitude differs widely from one Kiska to the next.
Kiska.scoverview: Kiska descend from the cat-like Casia of Primordis, inheriting both their dense shimmering manes of hair and their connection to shadow magic from their ancestors in the Inner Realm. Powerful and tough, with brightly colored hair and eyes, their connection to this magic gives them the ability to blend into the shadows around them and an innate sense of danger that lets them react quickly and decisively to any unexpected threats.

Vrjnhar.name: Vrjnhar
Vrjnhar.text:
Oakengarde is a region filled with deadly creatures and plants, many of which prowl beneath the region's icy mountain slopes waiting for prey. To survive in this harsh land, the Vrjnhar body has adapted over time, becoming stocky and well-muscled, with redundant organs, thick fur and beards that are resistant to physical and magical damage, and a spine with an exaggerated spinal curve that puts the vrjnhar's shoulders in the path of danger instead of their more vulnerable necks. This resilience, as well as their stamina, make Vrjnhar some of the toughest humanoids in all of Ember. Even their beards, which they usually keep meticulously trimmed, cannot be cut with normal barbering tools, requiring gemstones or specially designed tools to maintain.

Biology

Vrjnhar have many biological adaptations for surviving the extremely harsh environment of Oakengard. Their thick leathery skin is difficult to pierce even with sharpened steel and their bones are denser than average, with greater amounts of iron, making them tough and very durable. Within their bodies Vrjnhar possess twin hearts, three lungs and a fully encased rib cage and stomach, protected by small bone plates that allow for a full range of athletic movements but acting almost like chainmail under the skin.

Their digestion is equally strong, with an additional sulfuric gall bladder that produces powerful acids, breaking down even the foulest or most inedible materials. As a result, Vrjnhar are able to eat foods that others might find unpalatable, dangerous, or deadly, and often take a heavy hand with spices when preparing food. There are varieties of hot pepper, for example, that have such a powerful effect on other ancestries that only vrjnhar are able to truly appreciate their taste.

A Vrjnhar beard is usually thick and full in appearance, and has the same tensile strength as steel. It, like their fur, also has anti-magical effects, with spells sometimes (but not always) dissipating on contact.

Vrjnhar Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information.

Vrjnhar are compatible with other Humanoids on Ember and can reproduce with any other Humanoid ancestry. The hardiness of the vrjnhar manifests differently in each offspring, but many have either redundant lungs or a larger than average heart.

Cultural Connections

Most Vrjnhar in Ember belong to the Oaken culture, which is centered in the continent Oakengard. Much as Oakengard has shaped the Vrjnhar ancestry, it is also shaped the Oaken culture, which reveres survival, adventure, monster hunting, and martial prowess. Beyond Oakengarde, many Vrjnhar leave Oakengarde and travel, secure in their physical hardiness to keep them safe as they travel. While many Vrjnhar eventually return to Oakengard after their adventuring, craving the challenge of this dangerous land, some settle in small groups in other places and among other cultures. One of the most long-standing groups of this type is an enclave in Ordain, which has maintained a strong trading relationship with the Oaken for hundreds of years.
Vrjnhar.scoverview: Known for their ability to survive in the harsh land of Oakengarde, Vrjnhar have been changed by their relationship with the land around them, as if Ember itself willed them to be able to survive. Outwardly, they are most easily distinguished by their broad, hunched shoulders, which protect their necks from direct injury, and full coat of fur, which generally matches their prominent (and self-protective) beards. Beneath the surface, every part of their body helps to contribute to their survival, from their twin hearts and triple lungs, which provide stamina and survivability, to the strength of their beards, which have the toughness and hardness of steel.

Human.name: Human
Human.text:
Humans are direct descendants and inheritors of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.V1gzeX0JWSOCQ7LD]{Jarn} and thus take on many of their physical characteristics. They are, however, incredibly varied across the surface world, with many regional differences depending on environments, history, or close connections to other ancestries with which they may have integrated or mixed. In many ways, a "standard" human does not exist. Skin, hair, and eye color have a truly massive range of tones with every type and combination possible. That said, some things set Humans apart; compared to many other ancestries, humans are the most adaptable to the world's hardships and have excellent stamina and endurance.

At a basic level, Humans follow the same shape and form as their Jarn predecessors, with two arms and legs, five fingers on their hands, and five toes on their feet. The only actual difference between the Jarn and Humans outwardly is the reduction of hair across the body, but apart from that, they are remarkably similar. Because Humans don't tend to have any distinguishing characteristics like other ancestries, such as sweeping horns, intricate scales, or thick fur, they are often considered tame and uninteresting by some. However, due to their drive to expand and explore, Humans frequently encounter other ancestries and incorporate them into their cultures and nations, increasing diversity and becoming even more powerful as a result. This may explain the remarkable expansion and growth of human kingdoms since the events of the Shattering, and if they continue, they will one day surpass the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir}.

Biology

Human biology is not very different from their predecessors the Jarn; their inner organs, such as a single heart, lungs, and digestive system, are the same. Human skin is thin and easy to cut or damage, and their bones are strong but generally not as strong as those of other ancestors. Humans, however, have a distinct lack of body hair, which comes with the ability to sweat profusely during exertion. This means that Humans can regulate their body temperatures much more efficiently than other ancestries and are capable of incredible feats of stamina and endurance. In fact, Humans have been known to outrun almost all other creatures and are the last ancestries to remain fighting during battles.

However, another key difference from other ancestries on Ember is the Human soul, which is often described as "Radiant" by anyone who studies such things. A Human soul is curiously potent, and Humans seem to have a much closer connection to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}; this often manifests as an intense passion for life, strong willpower, and a desire to experience everything possible in their lives. This, combined with an extremely tough and resolute mental fortitude, is one of the Human's greatest strengths.

A consequence of the Human's radiant soul is that they are sensitive to the effects of the Abyss and the aura of Undeath. This mean some Humans may be particularly resilient to its effects or, conversely, more easily corrupted by such influences.

In rare instances, and somehow linked to a Human's radiant soul, an individual can experience a supercharged boost to their bodies, known as a "Blaze". This ability is very difficult to control and not at all common but it empowers a Human with vastly increased strength, speed, and magical abilities for a short duration in dangerous or life-threatening situations. Humans call this Super-Adrenaline, and it is responsible for some of the most legendary feats imaginable, such as the slaying of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} and monsters.

Human Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information. Humans are Humanoids descended from the ancient Jarn, and are thus compatible with other Humanoids.

Cultural Connections

Human history began in the Aran Peninsula around three thousand years ago. Since then, they have spread across most of the continent of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica} and a large part of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia} as well. The ancient city-states of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} are the oldest known settlements. Many cultures now claim a distant origin back to those surviving Humans who stood against the darkness during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}. Today, the aggressive and constantly expanding @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire} is a prominent example of just how overwhelming the Human ancestry has become. The gleaming metropolis of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} is another more peaceful example, but it is equally remarkable that such a great city has risen in such a short period of time. It also seems to be a cultural successor to the Aedir in ages past, a vast melting pot of ancestries and cultures all living together and linking the known world.

Many other existing cultures and ancestries of the world are astounded by Human expansion, and most also view them as possibly the greatest force for good in the world, potentially capable of conquering the countless threats and challenges of the Ember Cosmos. Many such cultures are enthusiastic and eager to work with Humans; the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} especially are more than happy to teach Humans survival tricks and help them in their struggles, viewing them as a younger version of themselves but with greater drive.
Human.scoverview: The Human ancestry is the most numerous of all ancestries in the world of Ember in the present age. Humans are dynamic, capable, and unfaltering, thriving and adapting quickly to new environments, situations, and problems. Over the past three thousand years, humans have spread across the majority of the Aterican supercontinent and beyond. They have accomplished tremendous feats in a relatively short time, creating massive cities, establishing kingdoms and empires, and exploring uncharted regions of the world. Much like the Aedir Empire before them, humans have integrated numerous other ancestries into their cultures and created many varied, diverse, and flourishing nations.
Human.sgamemaster:
Humans are one of the younger ancestries that exist upon the surface of Ember, emerging roughly three thousand years ago, during the later years of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of Sunlight}. Humans have a particularly mysterious origin, as they are the direct transformed descendants of the remaining @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.V1gzeX0JWSOCQ7LD]{Jarn} upon the Aran Peninsula. The entire population of Jarn awoke one day to find themselves changed, and the Jarn as an ancestry was now extinct, replaced entirely by Humans. Though they retained memories and personalities, it quickly became apparent that they now had a spark of something else that pushed them forward. The Sunfire Empire of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} was a dominant force in the world during this time, and according to legend, they were utterly confused by the events and could not trace what had occurred even with the assistance of their pantheon.

Humans would almost instantly begin expanding outwards from the Aran Peninsula and learned all manner of things from the Aedir, who quickly grew somewhat wary of the speed and ferociousness of Humans. The Aedir would often implant helpful advisors into these early human kingdoms to try and curtail and prevent them from advancing too quickly. Some of the oldest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} city-states were founded and settled during this time. Humans also built ships and began exploring the nearby oceans, sailing south to the continent of Kessia and founding the coastal kingdoms of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessian} people. Many humans would join the Aedir culture, traveling to the Starshield or becoming part of their many colonies, but unfortunately, the events of the Shattering occurred not long afterward.

During the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}, Humans were hard-pressed and only survived thanks to the efforts of the legendary @UUID[JournalEntry.SXu41X2NifZaSVqh.JournalEntryPage.zpCnphwcwMcVOOmW]{High King} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.YNMxNE2TbhObyKMp]{Fenra Irdragon}. This event was extremely harrowing, however, and wiped out many human cities and settlements, leaving a lasting memory on the ancestry that many still recall with fear. Thankfully, Humans emerged from the Shattering with an unbowed spirit and continued onwards, no longer constrained by the distant dominant culture of the Aedir. Human kingdoms took over many Aedir ruins over time and welcomed surviving refugees. They pushed forward, settling the regions north of the Kelmezian city-states, crossed the seas to the west, and discovered the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Mazira}. Humans have continued to spread across Aterica, settling the outer reaches of the Corebright Forest and eventually the distant Cascaal Peninsula and the Arctus Plateau. Currently, Humans are advancing further north into Atercia, crossing and exploiting both the Corebright Forest and the Shana Mountains at the heart of the continent. Small outposts and settlements have been settled in these areas, and Humans have encountered @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.t0uXEiiy4hN4XBeX]{Trolls} for the first time.

Hulg'run.name: Hulg'run
Hulg'run.text:
Hulg'run are one of the more unusual and distinct ancestries upon the surface @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember.} They originated as squat stone constructs that the ancient Giant culture of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} used for mining, exploring, and construction. They often squeezed into small spaces to manipulate delicate machinery and navigate small passages and, even today, remain diminutive in size and scale compared to other ancestries. After their awakening, they ceased to have a unified form, and their variety and general appearance exploded with diversity. A Hulg'run's primary physical characteristic is the stone choice used to create their bodies. This can be almost anything from the geological record, from granites, sandstones, igneous rock, or even gemstones. This can lead to a wide variety of appearances, and some families of Hulg'run return to ancestral quarries for symbolic, ritualistic practices and communion with certain rock types they find alluring or beautiful. Sometimes, Hulgrun will eschew wearable jewelry and instead adorn their bodies with inset precious stones and metallic inlays and patterns.

Hulg’run are often described as incredibly slow shapeshifters, and each individual can choose how they appear, changing the structure of their bodies, face shapes, colors, materials, and gender on a whim. This process is slow, however, and may take several weeks or months to settle and morph fully. They may also require a physical connection to a rocky element to transform into it, with some Hulgrun carrying small rocks and gemstones for future use. Hulg'run faces and bodies are often rendered with angular, simple shapes, appearing more like carved statues rather than smooth biological skin. Some Hulg'run instead shape intricate details so fine that they seem like living organic stone. It is not uncommon for a Hulg'run to take on the appearance of the people around them or to be deliberately made in the image of others.

A Hulg’run’s eyes are among their most detailed areas and, in almost all cases, are contrasting precious stones or gemstones that glow softly in the darkness. This glow is linked to their spiritual connection with the world around them and fades upon their death. Their eyes may also be faceted instead of round and appear carved like a polished jewel with a darker pupil and a shining geometric iris and sclera.

Biology

Hulg'run are made entirely of stone without any inner organs except an inner core of magical material called a Spirit Core. This is an extremely potent magical element infused with Lifeforce and a Soul from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} and the reason Hulg’run became a sapient ancestry. Because Hulg’run are infused with magical energy, they can move their stone bodies in an almost unimaginable way, stretching, shifting, and twisting without cracking or damaging themselves. Because they do not possess organs of any kind, they do not consume food like most organic life forms; instead, they can absorb minerals and energy from materials by holding them in their hands, and they can do this with practically anything, such as traditional foodstuff, rocks, woods, and metals. They also do not breathe and can survive underwater and in some incredibly dangerous environments. When they “sleep”, they can sit quietly and slowly draw upon Lifeforce directly through the ground to energize themselves. This process can help injured Hulg’run regenerate their body but may take them several days or weeks to fully heal, depending on the injury.

In almost all cases, a Hulg'run will live for a respectable three hundred years before their bodies begin to wear down and their Spirit Core starts to fade. An older Hulg’run may experience “cracking”, where small chips and cracks will appear in their joints, causing movement to become painful and slow. In rare cases, especially spiritual Hulg'run that develop a close connection to Lifeforce, can reenergize their Spirit Core indefinitely, and they become effectively immortal. This often elevates that individual's power and usually results in the creation of what is frequently referred to as a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild God.}

Because Hulg’run are made of stone, they are incredibly hardy and strong and have an impressive resistance to some physical attacks. However, this comes at a heavy price, and a Hulg’run has a number of weaknesses in certain situations. They are especially prone to bludgeoning attacks, and when hit with enough physical force, their limbs can shatter and break away. Thankfully, a Hulg’run can survive extreme injuries, and there are even reports of Hulgr’un managing to survive having their heads shattered. They can regrow limbs slowly over time, even while meditating. Hulg'run are very heavy and cannot jump very far, often only a foot or so into the air or across gaps. Hulg’run do not breathe, but they require contact with air to survive and are damaged slowly by a lack of oxygen, as oxygen is imperceptibly absorbed through pores and cracks to sustain their Spirit Core. Its efficiency allows it to survive in thin atmospheres for extremely long periods. However, they cannot ignore gas-based hazards, complete oxygen deprivation, or complete submersion in water, as it would quickly choke the Spirit Core. This makes large bodies of water especially perilous, as Hulg’run cannot swim and would sink quickly to the bottom, where they would slowly suffocate.

Hulg'run Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry, but Hulg'run cannot reproduce with other ancestries — they create their own children with one another, using a process through which they slowly craft a Spirit Core from stone and infuse it with Lifeforce over several days. When crafting their children, Hulg’run deliberately create basic and blocky shapes and as a Hulg’run child matures, they begin to refine and adapt their own bodies as they see fit.

Cultural Connections

Hulg'run were created long before the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering} and were allied with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} Giants for thousands of years. As such, they were deeply ingrained in their culture, and many Hulg'run were destroyed along with their creators during the Shattering itself. Those that survived were aware of Shent's plans to create two new ancestries, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.bOPreM2lwc0iB46X]{Keth} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.rl7QgGAIaYqAxLYq]{Kivhar}, and they became the teachers and protectors of these young ancestries for many hundreds of years, surviving in enough numbers to continue reproducing themselves. Since that time, Hulg’run are still heavily incorporated within Keth and Kivahr cultures across the continent of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica}, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil}, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak}. There are even some incredibly ancient Hulg’run that remember the Shent and still teach their lessons and spread their wisdom to younger generations.

Beyond these cultures, the Hulg'run are sometimes found in small family or clan groups, as miners and explorers or simply living peacefully in remote locations, some still holding onto the cultural practices of the Shent. A small number can be found across the Arctus Plateau among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturians} and within the glittering great city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}. There is only one place where Hulg’run refuse live, alongside the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Z8Nm4rnjqG3BJHSd]{Varún} Giants in the hinterlands and lowlands of the Spine of Ember. All Hulg'run seem to have an instinctual resistance that borders on disgust for the Varún culture, believing they betrayed the Shent Legacy.
Hulg'run.scoverview: The Hulg’run were once small stone constructs created by the Shent, to navigate the smaller spaces and tunnels beneath the mountains that Giants could not reach themselves. Hulg’run all share aspects of their original rock-like appearance, but each Hulg’run can slowly transform their bodies to assume different shapes, hues, and adornments over a long period of time. Hulg’run maintain a deep spiritual connection to the Heart of Ember itself and instinctually infuse themselves with energy to restore their bodies and spirit.
Hulg'run.sgamemaster:
The ancestors of the Hulg'run were created roughly seven thousand years ago by the Shent @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God} Hulgaddoth. They served admirably as servants and workers for several thousand years, but at some point, they began to show signs of self-replication and sapience. When Hulgaddoth realized what was happening, he immediately called upon the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} to release them from any bonds of servitude, and he spent the rest of his life making sure they were protected and taught them all manner of knowledge and wisdom. To their credit, the Shent were partly horrified that they may have been controlling sapient creatures in that way but also oddly proud of the Hulg’run and quickly began regarding them as their children. As a result, these stone constructs were named the Hulg'run (Small Friends of the Giants), and they began living alongside the Shent or traveling the world as they saw fit.

During the Shattering, the Shent culture was destroyed by Abyssal @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.zaLrsSK495BEAUki]{Monsters} and a series of disasters, ruining their ancient cities and killing close to the entire population. This destroyed the vast majority of Hulg’run alive at that time. Still, a few of their number managed to survive among the fledging ancestries of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.bOPreM2lwc0iB46X]{Keth} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.rl7QgGAIaYqAxLYq]{Kivahr} that had escaped the Shent mountains a few hundred years before the Shattering itself. Those Hulg'run settled among their sibling ancestries as they developed their own cultures, slowly teaching them of the Shent's ways and traditions while accepting that these new ancestries needed to find their own path. These stony folk can now be found across Aterica, living in larger numbers among the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak}. While most of the Hulg'run live in or around these regions, they have traveled to almost every corner of the world and can be encountered in almost every nation and city. Despite their widespread nature, they are still a somewhat uncommon sight.

Kivahr.name: Kivahr
Kivahr.text:
Created by the Giants of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}, the Kivahr are powerfully built and extremely strong, with gray skin, dense bones, thick muscles, and taller than average stature. Though their dense musculature makes their physical power apparent, they are also durable, capable of withstanding large amounts of physical pain and duress, and of retaining focus even in deeply trying situations. This may have been the result of an intentional design decision by the Shent to help the Kivahr survive the dangers of the Shattering, but the details of their creation have long been lost to time.

In addition to their physical endurance and strength, Kivahr have a connection to the Shattered Moon of Akon that provides them mental focus — something which should be impossible. Akon appears to give Kivahr an ability to concentrate when at its zenith, which many Kivahr have learned to replicate to some extent in their daily life. For Kivahr who are able to tap into it, this focus can provide added concentration, the ability to make logical deductions more rapidly, and, in rare cases, even the ability to rapidly heal their own bodies.

Biology

Kivahr are a large, muscular ancestry with exceptionally dense bones, thick and wiry muscles, and tough skin that heals quickly after injury and is prone to developing scars in the process. Kivahr biology also makes it nearly impossible for them to retain fat and gives them a greater ability to build muscle than most other ancestries, regardless of their body type. As a result, Kivahr often carry muscle in places that others do not, including as a layer around their ribcages and in their wrists, giving them the appearance of having longer than average arms and a slightly hunched posture.

Kivahr eat and consume the same food as most other humanoid ancestries, but tend to eat in greater quantities and do not process or store fat in a typical manner, instead storing energy in their muscles that can be drawn on to sustain them during prolonged periods of caloric deficit. This allows Kivahr to survive for several months without food if needed and gives them great endurance.

In addition to their musculature, the most distinctive biological features of Kivahr are their gray skin, which often gives them a chiseled, stone-like appearance. Kivahr blood is similar in consistency to that of other ancestries, but it resembles liquid copper, with a bright orange tinge and slightly metallic appearance. When dry, their blood is a stark green/cyan color, resembling oxidized copper. While the glittering eyes of Kivahr appear on the surface to be different than other ancestries only in the way they sparkle, a closer look at their pupils reveals small components that move together in a steady rhythm — a relic, perhaps, of the way they were constructed.

Kivahr Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information.

Though Kivahr are a created ancestry, and do not descend directly from the ancient Jarn, they are compatible with other Humanoids on Ember. Individuals with Kivahr heritage, while not as muscled as their Kivahr ancestors, often retain some of the ancestry's dense musculature and above-average height.

Cultural Connections

Kivahr are the dominant ancestry in two cultures that live adjacent to the Giants Mountains that the Shent once called home — the knowledge-seeking @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak} to the North and the more warlike @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.xImbz6Nf4mMxtKF1]{Wardcall} to the East. Both cultures draw from elements of Shent culture, including a belief in thinking before acting. These beliefs have been reinforced by several ancient Hul'grun who live in cities with large Kivahr populations, where their knowledge of Shent culture is prized. In addition to their connections with some Hul'grun, the Kivahr have also retained some ties to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.bOPreM2lwc0iB46X]{Keth}, another ancestry created by the Shent, and both Bejak and Wardcall cultures trade readily with cities dominated by the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{ Kithil }culture, which was founded by the Keth.

Beyond the Bejak and Wardcall communities on the outskirts of the Giants Mountains, the confines of the Great City of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.qkFDffiLfGCd0RCs]{The Sphere}, and, in recent years, in the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.giaDQErIafhgueop]{Fallbrook} district of Ordain and the Arctus Plateau in general.
Kivahr.scoverview: Kivahr are direct descendants of the ancient Giants of the Shent culture, created after the Shent foresaw the calamitous events of the Abyssal Shear. Muscular by nature, and physically powerful, they show signs of their intentional design not just in their height and build, but in their ability to withstand physical duress and to focus their minds during stressful situations, using their connection to the shattered moon Akon to reach new levels of understanding.

Wirrun.name: Wirrun
Wirrun.text:
Though they are tall and slender, with long limbs and somewhat delicate appendages, Wirrun are well adapted to life in the coldest and uninhabitable lands of Ember. Their light bones and ability to walk effectively either on the balls or soles of their feet make it easy for them to traverse both slippery ice and thick snowbanks, and their innate elemental magic helps them retain their footing even when conditions are at their iciest. Their eyes, which range in color but have no visible pupils or irises, can see clearly even during extreme weather, working alongside their flexible and sensitive ears to navigate blizzards and heavy fog with ease. In warmer climates, Wirrun often feel vaguely uncomfortable, and though they can be found throughout Ember, often create cold environments where they can feel more at ease.

Wirrun retain some physical traits from their original role as servants of the fiendish Daemos, including their generally lanky frames, claws, and sharp teeth, but most of their most dominant traits come from their creation by Sokali, including their thin but unfreezable hair. Though their skin ranges from pale white to purple to charcoal grey, Wirrun all share the same hair color — a stark white that echoes Sokali's long mane— and sometimes call themselves the Wintermaned in her honor.

Biology

Wirrun are not only cold-blooded, but also supernaturally resistant to cold temperatures, perhaps as a result of the motes of silver found in their lavender colored blood. They can reportedly walk through raging blizzards with no ill effects. In warmer climates, on the other hand, they often feel some discomfort, with the severity ranging from one individual to the next. Especially high temperatures can make some nauseous and weakened. Wirrun who settle in warmer areas are said to acclimate to the temperature eventually — some more successfully than others.

Wirrun are omnivores with a strong preference for meat, which is generally their most reliable food source in far-off northern Aterica. Those who travel south and spend time in warmer climates vary their diets, but it is rare to find a Wirrun who does not eat meat as some major part of their diet.
