Though their creator, Sokali, helped to adapt their digestion to be able to thrive on this diet, their sharp teeth come from their original role as servants of the fiendish Daemos of Signara. This, among their adaptations for hunting — sharp claws, keen eyesight, an ability to pursue their prey across snowy terrain — can make them appear frightening to others, even when they do not intend any harm.

The Wirrun adaptation to cold is well known, but their origin with the Daemos of Signara is an affinity for symbol magic and words of power. In particular, Wirrun voices are strong and have a slight magic to them, which allows them to be heard through fierce blizzards, in the midst of raging storms, and across vast distances.

Wirrun Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information.

Though Wirrun are a created ancestry, and do not descend directly from the ancient Jarn, Sokali ensured that they are compatible with other Humanoids on Ember. Individuals with Wirrun heritage have been known to prefer cooler temperatures, even if they do not inherit their parent's cold adaptation.

Cultural Connections

The Fikost culture is made up primarily of Wirrun in and around the northern Hoarfrost Sea, with its center in the great floating city of Rimefrost. The presence of trolls and other creatures in the area, which the Wirrun hunt but also are wary of attacks from, tend to keep most Wirrun in and around this northern area. Some Wirrun, though, do travel further south and into warmer climates, either becoming accustomed to the warmer temperatures or using magic to keep themselves cool despite the weather around them, shielding their bodies from some of the heat of these regions.

Among Wirrun that travel further south, they are most likely to be found among the Bejak and Wardcall culture, as their environments are colder than those frequented by other cultures and they share the Wirrun and Fikost dislike of trolls. Elements of Fikost culture can sometimes be found in Bejack and Wardcall cities and settlements with large enough Wirrun populations. Some Wirrun will also venture further south to trade, often ending up in Ordain, where there is a large enough population that one of its districts has an ice spa designed for Wirrun merchants.
Wirrun.scoverview: Wirrun are a tall and slender ancestry created to be fiendish servants of the inner plane of Signara before being given mortal life by the goddess Sokali, who wanders the coldest northern lands of Ember. Both of their origins remain clear in the present day — they retain a predator's sharp teeth, lanky limbs, and fearsome claws, but have been adapted to survive even in the coldest regions, with thick fur across their heads, oversized ears that can be used for navigation even in the driving show, and a form of elemental magic that gives them additional balance and mobility even in thick snow banks. Most at home in the cold, most Wirrun remain either in the far north of Ember or the migratory city of Rimedrift, but some have traveled further south and can be found in warmer lands.

Thornling.name: Thornling
Thornling.text:
Thornlings are a very small plant-like ancestry with, large round heads and equally large eyes. Their facial features, combined with their small stature, can make them appear "cute" and delicate to others, but Thornlings are natural survivors — tough, adaptable, and hard to kill. Their skin is made of a resilient bark and the thorns that sprout from their body when they age are a strong defense mechanism against predators. They are also able to gradually adapt and transform their outward appearance to blend into their surroundings, though their bodies and heads almost always feature leaves and other plant-like shapes. The healthier these appear, the better the emotional state of the Thornling.

Though some Thornlings have been known to live incredibly long lives, on the whole Thornling lives are shorter than average. This, along with their ability to survive encounters and experiences that might do serious damage to other ancestries, has given them a reputation of being free-wheeling and risk-taking, whether they are on their own in the wilderness, often in communities centered around the large bodies of water they use for sustenance, or living among other ancestries across Ember.

Biology

Thornlings have no organs or bones — their internal structure is akin to tree or plant with tough fibrous internal structures. This makes them extremely hardy — a Thornling's skin-bark is nearly impenetrable, and their limbs have tree-like strength regardless of the thickness. They also take little damage even in situations that might harm others, recovering instantly after falls from large heights, for example, and can regrow lost limbs. Thornlings have no blood, but do contain a yellowish viscous liquid. This functions more like sap than blood, and leaking the substance is not a sign of danger or a grievous wound. Despite this, Thornlings always appear wide-eyed and youthful — the coloration of Thornling skin rarely changes from birth unless it has adapted to its surroundings in some way, and a Thornling's age is reflected solely in the number of thorns on their head.

Thornlings do not have the capacity to consume solid food, instead getting all of their nutrients from liquids. They have a great need for water, drinking more of it than any other humanoid, and it can have a somewhat intoxicating effect on them, making them feel more optimistic, lively, and outgoing. This can lead to celebrations and light-hearted pranks after heavy rains, or when at the edges of large bodies of water. Baths are a particularly enjoyable luxury for most Thornlings, and traditional baths known as Taro generally involve cooling water followed by warm water soaks infused with minerals or flowery scents. Thornlings also greatly enjoy flavorful drinks with a high water content, including alcoholic spirits and teas. Sharing a drink with a companion that hasn't had it before is considered a great sign of trust and friendship.

Because of their need for water, Thornlings are vulnerable to dry conditions and generally avoid dry environments like deserts or tundra unless there are scattered water sources. If kept away from water for too long, their leaves and bark will slowly shrivel, causing exhaustion and pain in the short term and dessication and collapse in the long term, though this takes many years and can be reversed if enough water is poured over them.

Thornling Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information.

Thornling are not humanoid, and thus not able to reproduce with any other ancestries. Some believe that the blessing of life that makes Thornlings possible can incorporate physical aspects of any ancestry who involved in their creation, but not much is known of the process outside of Thornling circles and such changes would be best expressed via an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik]{Aster} ancestry.

Cultural Connections

Thornlings generally live in small family groups, centering their lives around a fresh body of water. Able to successfully thrive in places that others can't, some Thornling settlements live in relative isolation. They generally ignore those who pass them in the wilderness unless the travelers interfere with their lives or limit their access to water in some way, but travelers may still be wary of them, as it can be hard to know what action might trigger a response from the Thornlings, who care about the natural world around them and are fearsome in their near indestructibility.

The ability of Thornlings to survive on their own is countered by a deep personal wanderlust that may have been instilled by some design of their creator. The spread of Thornlings to places across Ember is due in part to this love of exploration and adventure which often centers around the discovery of some new source of water. Once a Thornling settles down in a new place, a small community often grows around them and the source of water they have found, with the new Thornling community taking on the culture of those around them.
Thornling.scoverview: Thornlings are an ancestry derived from plants rather than any typical humanoid origin. Their bulbous forms, large heads, and bright eyes often make others view them as childlike, but they are far from helpless. Highly resilient and tough, with thick thorny bark that protects them from most dangers, Thornlings adapt to their surroundings, and can thrive not only in woods and plains, but also deep forests, swamps, river basins, and other watery environments.
Thornling.sgamemaster:
Thornling history and origin is rooted in mystery, with a great deal of confusion regarding their creation. Many Thornlings revere the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta}, and claim that Volta once traveled to a far-off place, teaming with massive wildlife and created Thornlings as tiny little explorers that could serve as their messengers. Many tribes and clans of wild Thornlings have little shrines to Volta and complex water-based rituals that occur at dawn or dusk during certain seasons to venerate their creator deity. Many cultures however, think that Thornlings simply popped out of the ground at some point in the ancient past, long before the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}, and slowly spread across the world. While others think Thornlings are monsters that only began appearing recently and they have slowly adapted to Ember enough to become peaceful. It's often surprising to many that Thornling are perhaps one of the most numerous ancestries living upon the World of Ember today, but they are usually spread across large distances and hidden in wild places.

In truth, Thornlings were indeed created by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta} from the Leafia, a massive plant-based ancestor from the Jurin continent. Volta often visits Thornling tribes and families and answers their prayers, but they are strangely bemused and amused by their creations and treat them with the kind of fascination a scholar would show towards a pet or experiment. It's clear that Volta adores the Thornlings, however, and works hard to protect them from dangers and threats whenever they can.

Keth.name: Keth
Keth.text:
Though the ancient Giants of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} culture have long been gone from the surface of Ember, many view the Keth as their spiritual successors, made by the Shent to survive and thrive where the ancient Giants could not. Physically, they are a sharp contrast to their creators, usually standing about three feet tall on average and rarely growing taller than four feet, with large eyes and an orange-red undertone to their skin.

Physically, the most distinctive feature of the Keth is their unsettling facial structure. They talk, eat, and speak similarly to other ancestries, with only a hint of large teeth behind their smiling lips, but the two lines below their cheekbones allow them to open their mouths impossibly wide, revealing a maw of large, sharp teeth. Many who are unaware of this trait find the revelation disturbing or frightening, and Keth across cultures generally keep this aspect of themselves hidden behind wraps, masks, or coverings.

Keth appear to share some of the Shent connection to the Elemental Moons of Ember. Their hair often changes depending on the moon cycle, glowing or glittering with tiny stars that augment its natural colors of black, grey, and white. The swirling patterns created by this glow are believed to be linked both to the current lunar movements and an individual Keth's spiritual state or moods. Their moods are also known to be affected by the moons, with the strongest effects generated by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis}, the Spirit Moon. When it is at its zenith, Keth are often more excitable, passionate, and prone to seemingly chaotic behavior. That this rarely ends poorly for them is often thought to be tied to the moons as well, as if they give the Keth some sort of preternatural luck.

Biology

Keth are short, squat, and slightly more blocky than @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Humans}. Their bones and internal organs are similar to Humans, but their smaller size and lesser endurance makes them slightly weaker and more susceptible to physical attacks. Their large teeth and jaws, while impressive and intimidating visually, are not particularly powerful, and may have been designed by the Shent as a way for the Keth to scare off larger predators.

Their blood, like their hair, glitters — it is a sparkling white with tiny flecks of an unidentifiable shiny material that appear to serve no true purpose, and shines more brightly when any moon is at its zenith. No scholars have yet been able to determine why, as it functions in the same way as blood from any other ancestry.

Whether due to their blood or not, Keth have an aversion to complex machinery, and often feel a physical repulsion when in the presence of complex constructs. The more complex the machine, the greater this aversion becomes, with some Keth feeling burns and other pain simply by holding complex construct parts. As a result, it is rare, though not impossible, for Keth to become artificers.

Keth Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information.

Though Keth are a created ancestry, and do not descend directly from the ancient Jarn, they are compatible with other Humanoids on Ember. Some believe this was a purposeful choice by the Shent to give the Keth the best chance to thrive and spread their connections with the moons. Indeed, individuals with Keth heritage often report feeling a connection to the moons of Ember, though it may not be as visible or as strong as in their Keth ancestors.

Cultural Connections

The Keth were created by the Shent for unknown reasons shortly before the events of the Shattering. Many presume that it was a way for the Shent to continue their spiritual traditions and preserve some of their culture before dying out, but their reasons are lost to history. During the Shattering, the Keth survived, fleeing in all directions from the Spine of Ember. Those who traveled East founded the lunar-focused Kithil culture, which functions almost exclusively during nocturnal hours, while those who traveled West settled in the massive trees of the Corebright Forest, founding the nature-focused Striders.

During the present age, Keth are a common sight across the Human kingdoms and nations of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Atercia}. They are pretty happy to integrate themselves into a wide variety of cultures, and many have made their way to the Arctus Plateau and @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}. In a testament to their ubiquity, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturians} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani} have no issues with a Keth’s strange wide smiles and teeth, and Keth don't tend to hide their faces in any way among those cultures.
Keth.scoverview: Small in stature, with monstrous jaws hidden behind their wide smiles, the Keth were created by the ancient Giants of the Shent in the face of a coming cataclysm. Aware that they would not survive the destruction themselves, the Shent created the Keth ancestry as their spiritual inheritors, seemingly giving them a connection to magic and the cycles of the moon that persists to this day. From the glow in their hair to their apparent ability to turn even impossible situations to their advantage, the Keth have a reputation for being unpredictable, with their moods and fortunes as changeable as the position of Ember's many moons.
Keth.sgamemaster:
Long before the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} foresaw the coming cataclysm in great detail, recognizing that their own culture would be completely destroyed in the conflict. This future sight gave the Shent great insight and allowed them to attempt many different paths to avoid what was coming, and they even tried to warn the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir}, but their pleas for caution fell on deaf ears. They then proposed a different path. Instead of trying to survive, they should instead pass on what made them Shent in the first place and thus created two new ancestries called the Keth and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.rl7QgGAIaYqAxLYq]{Kivahr}. This plan went ahead and was completed not long before the Shattering. The Shent had just enough time to teach the young ancestries what they could before sending them away from their cities and using the last of their magic and power to hide them.

Thanks to this effort, the Keth survived the Shattering in small numbers hidden among the trees and plains on either side of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.VxA0UsGvDbDn8SdO]{Spine of Ember}, where the Shent Cities resided. Since that time, their population has slowly increased, and they have managed to triumph over many evils and monsters. During the present, the Keth are widely recognized as a bright, inquisitive ancestry that often bring joy and deep spiritual connection to the world and cosmos around them.

Drakon.name: Drakon
Drakon.text:
Drakon are the only ancestry on Ember to derive directly from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Humans}. They share many physical characteristics, both in shape and form, but most importantly, a Drakon's face is remarkably human. However, their most prominent features are entirely unsettling and can only be described as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Draconic}, with long sweeping horns, scaled skin, and long-scaled tails. Thankfully, their Human traits are often more dominant and, combined with the inherent innocence of the very young; this has enabled them to be accepted and welcomed by the majority of cultures despite some of their other more monstrous physical features.

Drakon grow thick, protruding scales that cover almost their entire bodies. On the lower arms, legs, and tails, these scales do not simply follow the body's contours but are large, angular, and dangerous. On the face, the front of the neck, and the chest, the scales change dramatically, and although they are still present, they become almost invisible and look like Human skin. When touched, these facial and chest scales feel soft and leathery and are much less capable of deflecting blows than elsewhere, making Drakon particularly vulnerable to attacks in these areas. This weakness is often compensated for with armor that only covers the chest, neck, and face, usually leaving the arms and legs bare, as the incredible natural strength and thickness of the scales make those areas almost impossible to harm. Drakon have heavily scaled tails, with varying lengths and thickness, but are often heavy and thick at the base. Their arms, hands, feet, and legs are usually longer than Humans, appearing slender and elegant with claws upon their fingers and toes. A Drakon's scales are surprisingly kaleidoscopic; muted reds, oranges, blues, and purples are the most common, but other rarer colors also appear. The more pronounced scales of the body are almost always darker towards the base and lighter towards the tip and can also range in tone and hue. Facial and chest scales are often starkly different from the rest of the body, taking on traditional human skin pigments.

While the scales are a significant aspect of a Drakons appearance, the most striking physical feature are the large sweeping and elaborate horns that grow upon the top of their heads. Multiple sets of larger and smaller symmetrical horns are common, covering almost the entire head. These horns are not present at birth and may only appear as small nubs protruding from the skull, but as Drakon age, the horns continue to grow. This is often a clear indicator of how old an individual Drakon is by the size and amount of horns. Among the horns, hair is also common but is drastically different in texture from human hair as it is tough, metallic, and heavy.

Biology

Drakon’s inner biology and organ structure are almost identical to that of humans. However, they have much richer and more oxygenated high-temperature blood and cores that can metabolize and enrich even tiny amounts of air, keeping their bodies running under extreme conditions. This means a Drakon is very resistant to intense temperatures and comfortable in freezing and searing environments. They can also breathe normally in thick smoke, choking gases, and at high altitudes where the air is thinner, such as the tallest mountains and even the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars} without any additional aid. Unfortunately, this significantly impacts Drakon's stamina, requiring breaks and moments to catch their breath during intense bouts of activity. If a Drakon pushes themselves too hard, they can even cause self-inflicted blackouts and fall unconscious for several hours.

It's unknown if there is some kind of biological trait at work here but all Drakon have an inherent ability to manipulate a particular form of magic called Drakonfire. Some believe this red and purple flame causes no harm to a Drakon, and they can also choose whether the fire is harmful to others. Still, generally, Drakonfire is extraordinarily dangerous and burns unnaturally even when entirely immersed in water. Drakonfire can manifest in various ways depending on the Drakon; some can blast hot plumes or beams toward their enemies, while others can surround their bodies with a fiery shield that protects them from harm.

Drakon Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information. Drakon are Humanoids descended directly from Humans, and are thus compatible with other Humanoids.

Cultural Connections

Drakon arose very recently in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire} during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.Fze49xRKzbsO5qNq]{Night of Swords} from a very small number of Humans. They have a total of three generations: the first, their children, and their grandchildren, with the youngest generation's oldest members ranging from newborns to late teenagers. Most Drakons, therefore, are concentrated in the Tayan empire as this is where they were created. Still, Drakons are extremely curious, capable, and adventurous and over the last seventy-two years, they have begun to explore and discover many distant lands. They can now be found almost everywhere on both Atercia and Kessia.

Drakon arose without any memories of their previous lives and seemed unconcerned about their mysterious origins. The fact that they are connected in some way to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons} is of little relevance to most, but some are fascinated by their origins and seek any and all information regarding their creation and Dragons themselves. Most people who encounter Drakon for the first time are surprised by their appearance but are not particularly concerned or view them in any negative light, as many believe they are Aster.
Drakon.scoverview: Drakon are an incredibly young ancestry, emerging less than a century ago in the aftermath of the infamous Night of Swords that took place in the heart of the Tayan Empire. Drakon tend to be inquisitive and fearless as they possess both an inherent innocence and a resolute ability to withstand hardship. It is clear to the other people of Ember that Drakon are Draconic in some way, but it is also clear they have little in common apart from the physical characteristics of scales, horns, and tails.
Drakon.sgamemaster:
Drakon were created during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.Fze49xRKzbsO5qNq]{Night of Swords} by the Elder Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} herself in mysterious circumstances that are still shrouded and unclear. Perhaps it was an attempt to set things right and create an ancestry strong enough and capable enough to resist corruption and darkness. Still, her true motivations may never be fully understood. This is because while humans are sensitive to the Abyss, Drakon take this one step further and are seemingly very resistant to Abyssal energies. So far, this has meant no reported corruption of Drakon into undeath, which is a fascinating and powerful revelation.

Since Drakon history is so new, there are several first-generation Drakon that have begun to carve a name for themselves and are highly revered and regarded, including @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.uKgqDFNhh8Ll7iv8]{Ankarist Talken} and @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.Q6mGfHYIDKK3gfzs]{Cronaric Tezran}.

Fej.name: Fej
Fej.text:
Fej are Humanoid in appearance but have a strong resemblance to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae}, with some striking differences. Their rough-looking skin is finely cracked and banded in places with alternating bands of dull and bright material, and it often appears glassy yet dull at the same time. This skin is marred, pitted, and even rougher around the joints and the face, with this effect becoming much more pronounced on older Fej. The skin is almost always dark gray or black, with some rare individuals exhibiting lighter skin tones, such as light gray or white. Still, there is no indication of color except for a slight shine, which may sometimes suggest a slight blue or purple coloration.

While their skin is colorless, traces of glowing fire are unmistakable and can be seen glowing beneath the skin's surface as if the Fej are powered by an intense internal furnace. This fiery glow that can be seen flickering beneath the skin is a trait that all Fej universally share. In almost all cases, this fire is red or orange, sometimes making Fej appear monstrous and malicious. However, different fiery colors are recorded and considered exceptionally fortuitous, with those individuals often seen as blessed and pushed into leadership roles. The fire commonly brightens and is more visible in places where their skin is thinner, such as around the eyes, under the nail beds, or within the mouth. Fej hair is almost always black and greyscale in tone, like their skin; however, some individuals find that their hair has a mysterious smoke-like property that causes it to fade away into nothing towards the tips of the hair. This isn't something a Fej is born with but happens to Fej as a consequence of acute emotional distress or anger and can last for many years.

The eyes of a Fej glow with a burning intensity and are often the first feature that others are drawn to. Their eyes are always the same color as their internal glow, with a burning pupil, slightly less intense iris, and finally, a dimmer yet still gleaming sclera. It's rumored that Fej can see through fire itself and innately recognize the temperature of materials and objects around them, helping them construct weapons, armor, and other metallic objects.

Biology

Fej are, in many ways, a fire made manifest in a Humanoid body, closely tied to the fire moon @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}. They are primal and strangely elemental, with their internal biology almost entirely replaced by magical energies instead of organic tissue. Their blood is a rich, thin, molten fire and flows within their bodies at high pressure from their core, a rhythmic ball of fiery energy that acts as the Fej heart. This means that even minor wounds cause a spray of fiery blood to erupt from the Fej before their fast metabolism and magical energy closes the wound. When wounds are severe enough or savage in nature, Fej have been known to explode into a fiery ball of destruction, casting fire across the area. Fej do have skeletons to hold their forms upright, but it's thought they are akin to obsidian glass. Unfortunately, this cannot be confirmed, as when a Fej dies, its form bursts into flame and turns to ash over only several minutes.

Fej metabolisms are much higher than other ancestries, making them strong, agile, and capable of great bursts of elegant, almost otherworldly speed powered by their fiery core. This makes them exceptional warriors and fighters but comes with a cost, as they require their own special food types that are either calorie-dense or infused with magical energy. They can eat and drink regular food, such as plain bread or rice, but this often doesnt fuel them enough to maintain their peak efficiency.

Famously, Fej are almost entirely immune to the typical dangerous effects of fire; they are fire resistant to such a degree that walking into a raging bonfire only tickles the skin and makes a Fej slightly uncomfortable. Only extremely high temperatures, such as molten lava or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragon} flame, is capable of bypassing this resistance. As a consequence of their fiery bodies and biology, Fej are particularly weak to water. They do not drink liquids in any significant quantities, prefer solid foods, and become burnt out if immersed in water, quickly becoming exhausted, which makes them slow swimmers.

Fej Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information. Fej are Humanoids descended from the Nir'ae and are thus compatible with other Humanoids.

Cultural Connections

Fej rarely leave their homelands, and the Fej ancestry is almost indistinguishable from the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{ Lumek} culture in many ways. They are the dominant ancestry of the Lumek and have lived in the Lumarin Forelands since ancient days. They only barely managed to survive the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering} but clung on and rebuilt their culture. Since the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.Q59ZUVNaeBoZl9nJ]{Evernight}, they have been remade into a fighting force of unparalleled efficacy and determination under the direct leadership of the Shard Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}. The Lumek have now been battling the undead @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Blood Barons} to their north in the Cycles of Fire & Death for generations, and their is no sign of the stalemate ending soon.

Some Fej do travel and explore, more often to recruit allies and to confront undeath wherever it may be found. Fej are a somewhat common sight in the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} as the city has a close trading connection to the Lumek, supporting them in their struggle. Some Fej spend time in the city to learn about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} and their teaching, which they find fascinating. Most Fej found in places around the world would likely have a close connection to their homelands, but it's possible to find small family groups incorporated and integrated into many of the cultures of Aterica. The largest population of Fej outside of the Lumek is found across the oceans in Kessia, and they work closely with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessians} in their struggle against the horrors of the Obsidian Desert.
Fej.scoverview: Fej were originally created by the ancient goddess Naor from the fires of Ragen to spread beauty and passion throughout Ember. Naor's daughter Lumé has since taken over the Fej culture of the Lumek and turned the Fej into stalwart warriors of flame and fury against the horrors of undeath. Fej are known for the fiery glow in their veins and the coal-like sheen of their skin. Fej are remarkable for their ability to withstand heat and rapidly metabolize energy into preternatural bursts of movement, although they have a notable weakness to the water and rarely travel by ship beyond their homelands.
Fej.sgamemaster:
Fej are considered by many to be an ancient ancestry but this is not entirely true. They may have originated around twenty thousand years ago, but this makes them relatively young compared to others. Most Fej have inhabited the same area of the world since they arose but as a people and culture, they have gone through many significant changes, and they have never had a strong tradition of accurately recording history or information about themselves. According to their own legends, however, the first Fej were @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae}, who arrived upon the shores of the Lumarin Foreland and began constructing small colonies in the volcanic soil. Sometime later, a Nir'ae called Naor from the Lumarin colonies ascended as a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Goddess} who used the elemental energy and fires of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen} to change the people around her and create the Fej. This legend is called the Birth of Fire by the Lumek today and is still sung as a special ballad during festivals. The Fej were much more at home among the fiery, volcanic environments, in fact, they thrived and became a much more relaxed and peaceful society. This created a distinct break from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir}, and as the early Lumek culture formed, they distanced themselves from their ancestors. At some point during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of Sunlight}, Naor helped a number of her cherished people ascend, helping them find @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystals} in the numerous volcanoes nearby; among them was @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}, a fiery, hot-headed dancer from the city of Aurtej that Noar named her daughter.

It was during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering} that the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} culture was sorely tested. Naor taught them to be peaceful and gentle for countless generations, seeking only beauty and joy in the world. But the events after the Shattering and the emergence of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.zaLrsSK495BEAUki]{monsters} devastated the Lumarin Homelands of the Lumek, and many cities and settlements fell to the darkness; it was thought that the Fej were annihilated entirely on the mainland of Atercia during this time, only surviving on a few islands off the coast. Many of the Shard Gods of the Lumek were also killed, and only Naor and Lumé survived. Fortunately, the Lumek managed to hold on until the final moments of the Abyssal Shear. It was thought that after the Shattering, the Lumek resettled and recaptured much of their former lands, and it was perhaps during this time that Lumé became much more war-like and aggressive.

In 869 AS, as the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.Q59ZUVNaeBoZl9nJ]{Evernight} swept across the region. The Lumek were horrified to learn that the once peaceful co-existence they had maintained with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moirans} to their north would soon spell their doom as undead legions of the newly formed Blood Barons rampaged across their realm. It was here that the nature of the culture shifted dramatically. Lumé, overwhelmed by rage, fear, and determination, took control of the entire culture personally. This act remains shrouded in mystery, but Naor died during this time, with many blaming Lumé in secret for killing her own mother. Once again, the Lumek fought against the darkness, but this time, Lumé rallied them into a total war mindset. Amphitheaters, gardens, and places of beauty were ripped up, and in their place, the Lumek constructed fortresses, smithies, and areas of industry and war. The effort was successful, and Lumé and the Lumek held the city of Ash against the Blood Barons' advances. This victory was short-lived as it soon became apparent that no power on Ember could entirely displace the Blood Barons, and the Lumek and the Fej would be trapped in an unending war that would come to be called the Cycles of Fire and Death.

Cor'ak.name: Cor'ak
Cor'ak.text:
The Cor’ak are unique among the ancestries of Ember, descending from primordial @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans} and inheriting their considerable strength and power. Their flesh is tough, leathery, and infused with elemental earthly energies and primal might. This is not just limited to their outer skin, which is hard and tough, but also the softer skin on their inner arms, hands, and chest. Their entire bodies have a remarkable resistance to physical attacks, and this resistance is so strong in certain individuals that they often feel little need for armor. A Cor’aks skin is also commonly marked by subtle swirling patterns of various colors corresponding to volcanic rocky crystals. These markings are not always obvious from a distance, but small crisscrossing lines encompass their chest, midriff, and core, appearing like fine fissures in rock. Overall, Cor'ak are large, bulky, and stocky, often able to retain impressive muscles with little effort, thanks to their unique metabolisms. In addition, they only exhibit three thick fingers and toes on their hands and feet.

A Cor'ak's most distinguishing feature is their strange facial structures and large, often circular crowns of rocky material on top of their heads. This crown or crest frequently appears bone-like or horn-like in color and tone, but its vastly more durable and small crystalline rock formations glitter across the surface. Usually, smaller rocky protrusions or vestigial spikes of the same almost unbreakable material can emerge alongside the main crowns across the cheek, neck, shoulders, and forearms as a Cor'ak ages.

A Cor'ak eye is a glittering crystalline orb, often a bright singular color that matches the tiny crystalline materials embedded in their head crowns. Cor'ak have poor vision overall, finding it challenging to track quick movements and faster attacks. This often worsens as they age, and they become slow and methodical in their movement overall and prefer to take their time performing all manner of daily tasks.

Biology

Cor’ak possess a dense structure of internal organs that more closely resemble their Leviathan progenitors, this helps them withstand extreme physical forces and strong gravitational effects, shrugging off overwhelming blows with ease. Even if a Cor'aks tough hide is pierced, they are not particularly vulnerable and feel only minor amounts of pain. When significantly injured, their rich crystalline-infused blood can expand around the wound, creating a rocky, crystalline shell. This shell helps seal the wound quickly and protects the Cor'ak from any further damage. It's also said that when Cor'ak are killed, this shell can sometimes cover their entire bodies and the Cor'ak can choose to remain within their bodies as slumbering spirits instead of moving on to the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Rn0WQchGPVYCTExP]{Spiritlands}. It's rumored that after thousands of years, they can be reborn and walk the surface of Ember once more.

Cor'ak are one of the largest and bulkiest ancestries on Ember, and among the cities and cultures of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica}, they often feel out of place and uncomfortable. This is elevated by their primordial origin and instinctual dislike of urban environments, leading them to generally avoid such places. Although rarely studied in detail, Cor'ak also seem to possess a rare ability to cause fear in other ancestries, especially when appearing suddenly from the dark. Though this fear often quickly passes, it is thought that a Cor'ak's appearance is akin to viewing an ancient predator made flesh, which is somewhat true in many ways.

Cor'ak Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information. Cor'ak do not have any common origin with other Ancestries, but can reproduce with other Humanoids in extremely rare situations, possibly due to their origin as creatures.

Cultural Connections

The Cor’ak ancestry is responsible for establishing one of the oldest cultures Ember has ever known: the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Mazira}. The Mazira persisted untold thousands of years on the distant lands of Akazea. They lived in relative peace alongside Leviathans as sages and custodians of the earth. Eventually, at some points during @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Human's} early expansion out of the Aran Peninsula, they sailed across the Crossing Sea and encountered the Mazira for the first time. Over centuries, humans have become the dominant ancestry, growing in population and constructing cities and entire nations, but they did so alongside the native Cor'ak. This meant the Mazira culture remained culturally prevalent. While there are differences from more ancient beliefs, many Cor'ak believe the Mazira culture today continues their original traditions. Today, Mazira culture is represented by a relatively disparate array of ancestries with a large population of Humans, but the Cor’ak are still greatly revered and respected.

Outside of Akazea, Cor’aks are exceedingly rare. They seldom travel outside their homeland, but recently, small numbers of curious explorers and more adventurous Cor'ak have been seen in distant realms such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Homelands, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian Republic}, or glittering @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}. However, most Cor'ak found in such places can usually trace their family history back to their moon-struck continent.
Cor'ak.scoverview: Cor’ak are a formidable ancestry descended from a primordial leviathan that ruled the distant mountainous continent of Akazea. Large in size and stout of constitution, they are among Ember's eldest and most resilient ancestries. Cor’ak are rare outside of Akazea but immediately recognizable by their hulking proportions, dense hide, and radial crowns of crystal-infused stone. A Cor’aks fortitude stems from their thick, resistant muscles and skin, infused with crystalline flecks and earthen energy, as well as their extraordinary ability to heal themselves from grievous wounds.
Cor'ak.sgamemaster:
According to Legend, long ago, during the early years of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}, before even the first @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} walked the surface of Ember, a seismic event on the blasted Moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora} ripped a colossal fragment from the surface of the moon. This fragment flew across the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars} and slammed into the surface of Ember, creating a massive geological fissure called The Akazean Breach.

For many long years, a fierce @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan} known as the Slumbering One had claimed much of Akazea as its territory, and the creature was said to be one of the oldest and possibly even the first of its kind. As the fragment of Cora fell, the Slumbering One lay directly beneath the impact, and as the blazing meteor struck, the colossal Leviathan was shattered into thousands of smaller pieces. As the effects subsided, these pieces shuddered and twisted into upright shapes, creating the first Cor'ak.

Luckily, the fluctuating gravity of the Cora fragment slowed its descent just enough to spare the continent of Akazea from a more devastating impact, and its form remained primarily intact. This monument quickly became a sacred ritual site for the Cor’ak ancestry, and today it remains one of the most treasured and revered places in the world, protected and safeguarded by nearly all Mazirans.

Altyra.name: Altyra
Altyra.text:
Altyra were created from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Humans} and follow the basic humanoid shape and form closely. From a distance, this ancestry is often confused with Humans, and it's only when examining them closely that the somewhat alarming differences begin to appear. Their skin is often unmarred, with few blemishes or defects, it's also strangely textureless, and it has a slight metallic sheen that seems to shimmer under direct light and glows slightly at night. Their skin colors range from silvers, golds, whites, creams, dark iron greys, and, in rare individuals, more intense colors such as vibrant copper. Faint lines, swirling patterns, or seams intersect and crisscross an Altyra's body, following the contours of the muscles in some cases giving them an almost constructed appearance as if the limbs have been stitched together.

The Altyra ancestry has the remarkable ability to transform their bodies into metallic constructs, if only for a short time; this transformation is stunning, unnerving, and fascinating in equal measure. Altyra bodies store large amounts of liquid metal content in the form of their "blood," and they can temporarily draw on that metal to fuel their transformations. Their alternative form varies greatly between Altyra, such as a protective metal casing surrounding the body, increasing size and strength, manifesting weapons, or even sprouting wings. In some rare cases, the limbs can disconnect and float next to the main body but cannot travel far without causing great pain. Finally, their faces are often covered by strange light-emitting symbols. These symbols are often @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}-based words, but the meaning is extremely difficult to decipher, even for the owner. Individual Altyra typically have a set form they can generate, which manifests for the first time during late puberty.

An Altyra's eyes are the most prominent physical feature when not transformed. They glow with an intense golden, orange, or white light, and with no iris or pupil, they can often appear intensely piercing or even frightening when immersed in darkness. As the Altyrans grow and manifest their transformative powers during puberty, their previously smooth and hairless heads are often adorned with new hairstyles matching local trends. The fine metallic hair itself is an adaptable aspect of their transformation and remains purely cosmetic.

Biology

An Altyra's "blood" is often described as liquid metal and is the same color as their skin and hair, though much more vibrant. When transforming, the liquid metal blood is manipulated to enhance and create new forms. Still, the process is draining for most, so it can only be done periodically and briefly. Even when not being manipulated, their metallic blood is greatly responsible for various traits, making Altyra hardier and tougher to kill, and they can regenerate lost limbs over long periods of time. Unfortunately, their metallic nature comes with a cost; when subjected to freezing temperatures, Altyra slow considerably, and their flexible forms become almost impossible to express. In addition, their form becomes brittle, and they are rumored to shatter and crack apart, with pieces of their body falling away entirely.

The metal content in their skin does gives them a slight shimmer under daylight and moonlight and a low level of bioluminescence at night. Their blood is responsible for regeneration over long periods, and an Altyra can even regrow lost limbs, but this process is slow and takes many years.

Altyra have only vestigial bones in their arms and legs, and their muscles do most of the work, both in keeping the body structure together and standing upright. Their muscles are metallic and far stronger than normal flesh, which is part of how an Altyra can transform. Because of the lack of purely organic tissue and flesh, Altyra have a strong poison and disease resistance. This was both a critical factor during their creation and early years and has also served them well in the centuries since.

Altyra Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information. Altyra are Humanoids derived from the Jarn ancestry and are thus compatible with other Humanoids.

Cultural Connections

The majority of Altyra upon the surface of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} live in the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen}, whose @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.y4WHE3TEr6Of13SL]{Railen} culture is militaristic and isolationist and whose wealth was partly built on their ability to repurpose the treasures and resources of surrounding cities that fell during the time of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.hbO7NeNeouXYkx9t]{Virulent plague}. Ancalen is one of the Great Cities of the world, but it is a city that has been closed to outsiders until relatively recently, and even today, sections of the city are restricted.

As time has passed, Altyra have spread elsewhere on Ember in small numbers. Many who leave the confines of Ancalen do so to escape the dogmatic and restrictive ideals of the Ancalen council of three. They try to reject such teachings and endeavor to interact with, learn from, and assimilate into other cultures. Most other cultures in Ember view Altyra in a positive light, with slight trepidation only if they learn that the Altyra in question is from the city of Ancalen.
Altyra.scoverview: Altyra came into being during the events of the Virulent Plague which mysteriously transformed large numbers of Humans into a strange new ancestry. This transmutation somehow hardened Altyra against afflictions, leaving them extremely resilient against diseases and poisons that typically affect other mortals of the world. Altyra have burnished skin that shimmers subtly with a metallic gleam and is often unmarred by blemishes or age. Even more remarkably, in moments of great stress an Altyra can alter their bodies into an awe inspiring or terrible transformation, where shining symbols of light appear over their faces and their limbs assume dangerous or practical forms.
Altyra.sgamemaster:
During the outbreak of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.hbO7NeNeouXYkx9t]{Virulent Plague}, which killed much of the population of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.NdqwtFoFAw85Gstr]{Aran Peninsula}, a few outcast @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} saw an opportunity to experiment with new tools of war. They had observed the creation and spread of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Humans} with both curiosity and a sense of unease, as Humans were different to other ancestries in ways they could not fully explain or understand. Thus, they began running magical tests in the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen}. For the Tyraphem, these experiments were both an act of arrogant mercy in order to save lesser beings and one of cold curiosity. They succeeded in their goals and created the Altyra, who were immune to the effects of the Virulent Plague and able to thrive as most of the places around them crumbled. They quickly came to view the Tyraphem as creators and absorbed much of their ignorance and disdain for others in addition to their warlike and zealous nature.

The first few generations of Altyra isolated themselves in Ancalen, only admitting and associating with those descended from the Tyraphem, such as other celestials, and publicly refused to “sully” themselves with different ancestries, creating the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.y4WHE3TEr6Of13SL]{Railen} culture that exists today. However, this deep cultural touchstone of arrogance was centered in Ancalen only rather than something all Altyra believed, and some Altyra left the strict confines of the city to live in distant realms and other cultures. The Tyraphem that had created the Altyra disappeared shortly after the transformations. Whether they view the Altyra as wondrous children and successful experiments or abominations is unknown. Little, if any, contact between the Tyraphem and the Altyra has occurred in the centuries since; but the Altyra tend to venerate the Tyraphem above all other entities as their creators, and are eager (if not fanatical) to learn more about their progenitors.

Signborn.name: Signborn
Signborn.text:
The Signborn were created by the Daemos from Nir’ae for purposes that are as of yet unknown, but their fiendish influence can be seen in the Signborn’s mix of the ethereal and the dangerous. Signborn all possess at least one additional set of limbs, which may be incorporeal, ethereal, or both. Their thin pointed horns and long whip-like tails can appear ghostlike and hazy at their edges, a contrast to their vibrant hair of cyan and purple. Outside of their extra limbs, their skin is muted, often in varying shades of gray

Signborn limbs may be ethereal, but they are also effective – though some are incorporeal, most are able to be used either physically or magically, if not both. They are also capable fighters – many have delicately thin but dangerously sharp claws instead of nails, or fanged teeth that are easily wielded as weapons. These, in addition to the angularity of their faces, can give them a harsh and foreboding appearance despite the hazy ghostlike nature of their extremities.

Biology

Signborn's internal organs are comparable to their ancestors, the Nir'ae, and other descendants of the ancient Jarn. Any internal systems that connect to their ethereal limbs simply fade away at the connection point with the rest of the body, with no loss of functionality. In fact, the ethereal limbs of Signborn are generally immune to physical harm, though magical damage to these same limbs can affect them drastically, causing excruciating pain.

Some Signborn bear markings that echo those on their original Daemos creators, showing up as vivid patterns or symbols, while others gain additional ethereal limbs, including limbs that seem almost disconnected from the main body of the Signborn in question. These are usually arms, but can manifest as tails, legs, or even heads. These connections to the original Daemos are not passed on through family lines, instead appearing randomly on Signborn at birth. A few scholars have attempted to determine a pattern to the manifestations, but they have yet to find any definitive connection other than general Signborn ancestry.

Signborn Heritage

Sexual reproduction between different ancestries is very possible and can result in children with mixed ancestry. Players can play as characters with mixed ancestry, but this requires consultation with the GM and may not be ideal for first-time players or GMs. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.KfTUoUg81hAB3jZC]{Biology} for more information.

Signborn are Humanoid and thus able to reproduce with other Humanoid ancestries. Though not all with Signborn ancestry have ethereal limbs, it is generally thought wise to have a magically-trained healer on hand if another ancestry has a child with a Signborn, as the ethereal nature of their limbs can make birthing complex.

Cultural Connections

Signborn's visible ties to their Daemos creators can make others view them with apprehension or suspicion, and their numbers are small and widespread enough that they have never created a culture of their own, instead generally choosing to adapt to the cultures around them. Signborn can generally be found anywhere on Ember, and while some have made a name for themselves as adventurers and warriors, others disguise themselves with magic or clothing so as not to invite questions about their appearance or intentions from strangers.
Signborn.scoverview: Created by the Daemos, who reside in the shadowy Inner Realm of Signara, the Signborn are known for their sets of extra limbs, which are ethereal but functional, able to be used for both physical and magical tasks. Though these extra limbs, along with their horns, whip-like tail, and sharpened teeth, can make them appear somewhat monstrous, their true inheritance from the Daemos is their magical ability. Signborn have an affinity for Glyphs, a form of written magic used by the Daemos, and can use them both for communication and to learn magic, giving even non-spellcasters the opportunity to have a few spells at their disposal.

Aster.name: Aster
Aster.text:
At the moment of their birth, some individuals are altered by the life force of Ember, changing at a fundamental and biological level into a completely new form. Though these individuals are collectively known as Aster, each change is different, and can occur to any living thing on Ember, whether humanoid or not, and whether sapient or not. Some Aster are changed cosmetically, while others are altered internally, but all have been fundamentally transformed in some way.

Other than the fact of their transformation at birth and the sapience held by all Aster regardless of their origin, there is no rule or observable pattern in how an Aster has been transformed or why. Speculation about either is considered to be a questioning of Ember itself and thus verboten in nearly all polite society.

Biology

The biology of Aster varies widely, and can contain biological variations and alterations found nowhere else on Ember, or simply not found in the original biology of the Aster in question. While some Aster share biological traits, no two are ever exactly alike. Even in the extremely rare case of Aster twins, each is affected differently by the lifeforce of Ember and changed in their own unique way.

Aster Heritage

Aster reproduction differs from one individual to the next, but Aster are generally sexually compatible with humanoids. Being Aster is not an inherited or inheritable trait — the children of an Aster inherit the biological traits of that Aster's parents.

Cultural Connections

Aster can be found across cultures, ancestries, and locations on Ember. Reaction to them varies widely. Some cultures view being Aster as a blessing, and others a curse. Some welcome Aster among them, while others view them with suspicion. Some Aster remain with their communities of birth, while others leave to find and create new definitions of family.

As Aster are rare, they are usually found with those of other ancestries, backgrounds, and cultures, though there are occasional small settlements and neighborhoods within larger cities that predominately contain Aster from across Ember, drawn together by the shared experience of having been made fundamentally different than those around them. In [[/date AS2512]]A massive earthquake hits the Arctus Plateau and the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, centred below the city in the Shard Caverns, the quake topples many buildings and kills roughly a thousand citizens across the city. New building codes are enforced and magical wards are employed across the city to protect against such events in the future. Building repairs are still ongoing for some of the larger structures damaged by the event. After the quake, Aster children are born more frequently in the following decade. This event comes to be known by a few names within Ordain, including the Stonehollow Quake.
Aster.scoverview: Aster are individuals who were changed by the life force of Ember at their birth into something wholly unique. This change can be cosmetic — adding quills, feathers, tails, or other physical features not found in the Aster's ancestry — but it can also shift the individual's internal biology on the deepest level. Changes manifest differently in each Aster, and they can be created from any creature, regardless of its ancestry, culture, or sapience. The one commonality between Aster is that they're always changed at birth and that the change is always a permanent one.

Soulbound.name: Soulbound
Soulbound.text:
Most souls on Ember leave their physical forms behind when they die, moving on to the City of Eternas and going through the Rite of Passage that transitions them into the Spiritlands. The Soulbound are the rare exception, remaining tethered to their bodies by a deeply important goal that must be completed before they can leave their former mortal life behind. The tether between a Soulbound's immortal soul and their unliving mortal form is represented by a physical soulmark, which restricts their existence while allowing it to continue long enough for them to set their Unfinished Business to rest and willingly move on.

The willingness to leave the mortal world behind distinguishes Soulbound from the undead of Ember, whose corrupted spirits and souls seek to stay on Ember forever. But being Soulbound is not without its dangers — Soulbound feel a constant pull towards Eternas. Resisting this pull, and the cosmic order that it represents, can corrupt a Soulbound over time, leading to them becoming one of the undead.

Becoming Soulbound is extremely rare, and forces the character to live with the Soulmark in addition to the attributes gained from their original ancestral origin. The effects can be difficult at the best of times, making becoming Soulbound a double-edged blessing - as arduous and draining as it is appealing, and only found in the rarest of circumstances.
Soulbound.scoverview: The Soulbound are mortals whose souls cannot or will not move on after death. Soulbound characters can hail from any ancestry, culture, or walk of life, but they are all united by a common element: every Soulbound has some Unfinished Business that tethers the living essence of their soul to their unliving mortal form. Unlike the undead, who are corrupted or twisted by evil forces, these souls simply defy the constant pull towards the city Eternas and its Rite of Passage until they have completed their final tasks.

The Ancestries.name: The Ancestries
The Ancestries.text:
Diverse Possibilities

Every Ancestry in Ember is deeply tied to the world's cosmology, history, and geography, with boundless opportunities for customization and expression. Making a choice of which Ancestry to play is a critical choice for a player and we wanted that choice to have both meaning and a way to immerse someone new into the world. The sixteen playable Ancestries all have different ways to experience the story, with custom abilities and features that continue our central theme, an imaginative setting filled with wonder.

Aster - Creative Expression

Due to the nature of the Ancestries and their connection to the creative Lifeforce of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}, there is a seventeenth option for anyone that would like to play a completely original character, an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik]{Aster}. Aster are individuals who are changed by the Heart of Ember at birth, making them wholly unique. This change is sometimes simply cosmetic, with spines, feathers, or extra limbs or appendages, but it can also change the individual’s internal biology. Aster can be found across ancestries, creatures, and within any culture; it always occurs at birth and is a permanent choice that allows players to decide for themselves how they would like to present themselves. With this in mind, it's perfectly acceptable for someone to grab a character from another setting and explain their appearance as an Aster!

Mixed Ancestries

Among mortal ancestries, the subtle and complex weaving of ancestries often results in children of mixed ancestry who may display a wide range of physical characteristics reflecting their parents' appearances and traits. Mixed-ancestry individuals are relatively common, if not widespread, across Ember, and as cultures and ancestries have become more intertwined in the current age, they are becoming increasingly common still.

Mixed Ancestries In Game

For practical purposes, players may choose to create characters of mixed ancestry; however, it is recommended to consult with the GM beforehand, as such characters may introduce unique roleplaying and mechanical considerations. Mechanically, you must still select one Ancestry which defines the mechanical benefits and features that apply to your character, as noted in@UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.PSx7hfJjAtsASAap].
The Ancestries.scoverview: Ancestries is the term used to describe the unique and varied sentient and sapient species that exist within the Ember Cosmos. We make a deliberate choice to differentiate between an Ancestry (Sapience), a Creature (Natural Animal), and a Monster (Abyssal Connection). There are sixteen playable Ancestries in the game, but the setting itself has many more; some are incredibly rare or exist in far-off distant places of the world.

Dragons.name: Dragons
Dragons.text:
• Keywords: Destruction, Fire, Scaled

  • Ember Type: Monster

  • Type: Dragon [See @UUID[.55d3H7q4hiNxePoL]{Carnal Dragons}, @UUID[.0CquHJco0yougg3S]{Cruel Dragons}, @UUID[.EhQnCUxkJyxOSbf7]{Vile Dragons}]

It is said that Dragons are malice and hatred in physical form. Indeed, the very word is known to strike fear into the hearts of mortals, most of whom have been told countless tales of these monstrous creatures since birth — stories filled with terror, and mystery, and doom. A key history lesson that almost everyone learns from these tales is that Dragons of Ember are all unique creatures; no two Dragons are the same in terms of their exact physiology and motivations, but three main subtypes of categorization do exist. Dragons are also relatively new to Ember (the most ancient of their kin having arrived nearly twenty-five hundred years ago during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering}).

Many of Ember's denizens believe Dragons to be a punishment wrought by the folly and hubris of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} after the Shattering, and pray the whole draconic scourge will be banished from the world if and when the Sun Tower is rebuilt. Others know the true origin of these powerful creatures to be a thing of divine inspiration, for the first Dragons were the progeny of the Elder Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, who brought the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.0CquHJco0yougg3S]{Cruel Dragons} into being alongside the Abyssal Shear as descendants of her ill-fated Wyrms. But while Alar sought to create a Wyrm-like creature that could resist the influential taint of the Abyss, abyssal corruption would unfortunately become a hallmark of draconic nature.

Collectively and colloquially known as "True Dragons" to help distinguish them from drakes and lesser dragonkin, three specific subtypes of Dragon are known to populate Ember and the Cosmos. The aforementioned Cruel Dragons were the first Dragons brought into the world, and are known to be massive creatures of winged destruction — with breath of dragonfyre so hot, it can melt metal and stone with ease. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.55d3H7q4hiNxePoL]{Carnal Dragons} are smaller and more feral than their elder siblings, and are known to be some of the world's most aggressively powerful hunters and predators, dominating their local biomes with primeval lethality. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.EhQnCUxkJyxOSbf7]{Vile Dragons}, on the other hand, are creatures of inscrutable cunning and otherworldly wit, and are known to be some of the most powerful spellcasters in the Cosmos (verily, the mere idea of this sorcerous offshoot is considered a farce by Emberites who refuse to reckon with the awful possibilities of their being).
Dragons.scoverview: Throughout the Cosmos, no creatures are perhaps more feared or reviled as the otherworldly reptilian predators known as Dragons. These unruly outsiders are most often considered to be beings of evil, chaos, and destruction — but this is not entirely true. While Dragons are rarely friendly or helpful towards other creatures, only a few of their kind seek to impose abject doom on the denizens of Ember. Most Dragons are driven by unknowable desires, as deeply connected to the enigmatic influences of The Abyss as they are. Whatever their motivations, Dragons endure as one of the most terrifying and alien species of Ember's modern age.

Vile Dragons.name: Vile Dragons
Vile Dragons.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Vile Dragons.scoverview: Vile dragons are the most vicious and dangerous type of Dragon present on the surface of Ember. They are universally reviled by mortals, natural creatures, and the gods. Vile Dragons almost exclusively desire the accumulation of power in various forms. They are not only destructive but sadistic and remorseless and pursue any means to control those around them. Thankfully they are also extremely rare if not mythical monsters and most cultures and mortals are unaware of their existence.

Carnal Dragons.name: Carnal Dragons
Carnal Dragons.text: Carnal Dragons are the scaled @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.zaLrsSK495BEAUki]{monsters} of fang and claw, the apex predators of large wilderness territories. They are four-legged and wingless, with thick scales and powerful muscles that allow them to leap, run, and hunt at high speeds. They are unnerving in their movement, with strange otherworldly abilities and innate magic. Some can slip between shadows to ambush their prey, others can blend entirely into their environments, while others can remain motionless for months, waiting for the perfect moment to strike.
Carnal Dragons.scoverview: Carnal dragons are bestial, predatory monsters that are often mistaken for natural creatures. They are exceptionally intelligent but are not traditionally cruel or evil; rather, they simply view mortals as food. They kill to eat or simply to remove a perceived threat, but in rare cases they can be bartered with and they will not seek out or kill mortals outside of their lands.
Carnal Dragons.sgamemaster:
• Keywords: Predatory, Adaptable, Primal

  • Ember Type: Monster

  • Type: Dragon - See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons}

  • Other Names: Fanged Wyrms

Carnal Dragons are exceptionally intelligent, with distinct complex personalities that can vary widely. They can be reasoned with in rare situations and conversed with, but ultimately, Carnal Dragons see little reason to talk with mortals unless it involves their places of power or something that concerns them. They are often dismissive and arrogant towards others in such cases, and horrifyingly direct in their desires to hunt and kill — which can cause many mortals to run in fear after only a few short words have been exchanged. Legends do persist, however, of Carnal Dragons treating with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} or exceptionally brave mortals, working towards common goals and a shared understanding of the world. But whether or not these tales are true, no one alive (and willing to speak of it) has seen such an alliance.

Carnal Dragons have little interest in anything other than their claimed territory. They are less interested in gold, treasure, or the accumulation of power and more keen on patrolling their territory and dominating those within it. They value natural places such as caves, caverns, or even raised outcrops in dense forests and make their lairs there, surrounded by the bones of impressive kills. However, Carnal Dragon territories are only marked by the kills and carcasses of the creatures they hunt, and doomed mortals may unwittingly enter their lands without knowing and find themselves hunted and eaten within a matter of hours or days.

There is nothing a Carnal Dragon fears except perhaps @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors}, and even then, they will still attack them out of fury and desperation. These clashes are rare and not fully understood, but Abyssal Horrors cannot control dragons like they can other monsters, and there seems to be an intense hatred and loathing between them. Similarly, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans} and Carnal Dragons' territories sometimes overlap, as they both seek out wild and primal places of the world, and these encounters inevitably lead to confrontations. Carnal Dragons are often massively disadvantaged in size compared to Leviathans, but this doesn't stop them from attacking, and a Carnal Dragon's speed and determination usually result in conflicts of equal footing.

Biology

Carnal Dragons are inherently magical beings infused with elemental forces and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{Abyssal} energies. This makes them both incredibly powerful but also unnerving, alien, and terrifying to behold. To some, they look like giant-scaled reptiles with long, thick tails, and while they do lay eggs to reproduce, they are unimaginably different in all other respects. Their movements are sinuous and disconcerting, often twisting and gliding across the ground in strange ways. Their mouths are filled with large, sharp teeth, and their eyes are silted like a feline and shine with burning intensity.

Carnal Dragon's bodies are thickly muscled with four strong limbs that end in razor-sharp claws. They possess long, thick, sinuous tails that are often crucial in their ability to move effortlessly across various environments and contribute to their ability to leap between trees and jump across great distances. Unlike other Dragon Types, Carnal Dragons do not possess wings of any kind. Every Carnal Dragon is unique as they can adapt their physical appearance to their chosen environment over the centuries, developing feathers, rocky scales, toxic hides, or a multitude of other traits to slide perfectly into the ecosystem they control. This means it's easy to confuse a Carnal Dragon with a natural, possibly more docile creature from a distance, much to the dismay of those who discover otherwise.

Carnal Dragons are thought to be immortal and there are accounts of some reaching over a thousand years in age. Others believe they reach a natural end to their existence but this remains unconfirmed.

Reproduction

Carnal Dragons only reproduce among their own kind, and there is no evidence that they can reproduce with other dragons or creatures. It's not known precisely how the process occurs or how two Carnal Dragons find one other as its unlikely they would leave their own territories. It's rumored that Carnal Dragons feel an innate urge to reproduce at some point, and (with explicit permission) will use their arcane magic to travel and enter another Carnal Dragon's territory. Carnal Dragons have male and female genders, but there is barely any dimorphism difference between the two — both sexes can lay eggs, but only one partner will do so, while the other is responsible for fertilization. The eggs are always kept with the Carnal Dragon that laid them; there is no real concept of mother or father, merely two parents and their offspring.

Carnal Dragons lay an average clutch of around three eggs and will tend to them over several years as they mature exceptionally slowly. Once they hatch the parent typically watches them for several months as they grow, bringing them food. They are caring and strangely tender to their children and will protect them with a burning fury that is near impossible to describe. However, they do allow the clutch to fight and kill one another in the lair, which happens often. Surviving Carnal Dragons children are said to have an innate desire to claim their own territory, so they leave in search of one after only a few months.

Abilities

Carnal Dragons are incredibly efficient primal hunters and have innate powers of movement, stealth, and concealment.
