They can slip silently into a shadow in one area and appear somewhere else as if the physical space itself does not exist, and this form of magic and power makes them all but inescapable. As they adapt their forms to their chosen environments as they age, they often appear completely hidden among forested foliage, mountains, deserts, or tundras, and despite their size, a Carnal Dragon appearing seemingly in front of you without any indication of movement is said to be bone-chilling. They become stronger and larger as they grow older, becoming more resistant to damage and magic, with some ancient carnal dragons reaching gargantuan sizes. Typically, however, they remain relatively small at around 15-30 feet long.

Unlike other dragon types in Ember, Carnal Dragons do not breathe fire, nor can they cast spells or use magic externally. Instead, they often exhibit powerful, unique magical abilities, such as enhancing their speed and the destructive nature of their claws and teeth, among others. They also tend to adapt and absorb natural abilities from creatures around them and can slowly transform their bodies, such as growing toxic scales, a venomous bite, or becoming cold and heat resistant.

History

Carnal Dragons are indeed monsters that emerged after the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear} at the tail end of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering} but are not as overwhelmingly destructive or evil as others. They slip into wild and natural places and become the apex predators, displacing other beasts and creatures that may have held that role. They are often more destructive to the environment and will aggressively and relentlessly hunt creatures, but they do so to maintain dominance and to feed. They may be monsters, but they also contain some semblance of Lifeforce and connection to the cosmos, with some idea surrounding the natural order, and are not always seen as evil or negative forces by mortals or gods. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} do not actively hunt or confront them because doing so is often unnecessary as they live far outside civilized realms, but also, older Carnal Dragons can challenge Shard Gods in power, and the risk for a Shard God is often too high of a price to pay.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.LpJYtlg2nxWbfylH]{Ryleir}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.P2bBo8cyh95XhWew]{Siodread}

Cruel Dragons.name: Cruel Dragons
Cruel Dragons.text: No other monsters on the World of Ember are as justifiably feared and reviled as Cruel Dragons. Among mortals, they are infamous for destructive, malicious rampages, and they are so well known that their eradication is the sole objective for entire kingdoms. With four main limbs, two massive wings, and maws of sword-like teeth, Cruel Dragons are fire-breathing, monstrous entities that grow to colossal sizes. Living in remote mountainous regions and the far north among the ice-capped northern reaches, they sometimes sleep within their lairs for centuries before emerging to cause chaos.
Cruel Dragons.scoverview: Cruel Dragons are the winged terrors of the Ember Cosmos, to some, they are the ultimate monsters, striking fear and dread into mortals the world over. They are fire-breathing destroyers that lie beneath snow-capped towering mountains, and they are often worshipped or revered by lesser monsters for their terrible power. Thankfully, Cruel Dragons are rare in southern Atercia and they usually spend centuries hibernating in their lairs.
Cruel Dragons.sgamemaster:
• Keywords: Mighty, Colossal, Flying

  • Ember Type: Monster

  • Type: Dragon - See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons}

  • Other Names: Fire Wyrms

Cruel Dragons are extremely intelligent beings and are cunning and brutal in the pursuit of the materials they deem to be valuable, which are almost exclusively precious metals such as gold, silver, or gemstones. They could even be described as obsessive and fixated on their desires and they are focused so heavily on themselves that they view all others as secondary or lesser. They will more often than not attempt to manipulate or coerce mortals into bringing them more of what they seek, recognizing that mortal peoples are especially efficient at gathering what they desire. Cruel Dragons are not purely evil, and although some delight in causing chaos and destruction, they care little for domination and the amassing of power. Instead, they are mostly motivated by greed. Some will gladly burn a city full of humanoids to the ground to sift through the ashes for trinkets, metals, and gems. Cruel Dragons, like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.55d3H7q4hiNxePoL]{Carnal Dragons}, can be bartered with, however, and their lust for metals is their only true weakness. Tributes to satiate their desires will typically keep a destructive Cruel Dragon in check for a time

Cruel Dragons overall spend much of their lives beneath mountains and volcanoes or deep within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} of Ember, seeking veins of metal. They are exceptionally proficient at mining these veins by melting through rock with their incredibly hot Dragonfyre. They don't often care about refining these metallic veins but will collect great quantities of metal together, creating immense lairs of fused metal. It is not uncommon to find abandoned Cruel Dragon nests made of threads of gold, iron, copper, and silver, dotted with precious gems of all kinds. Dragonfyre tunnels are often obvious in their construction and appearance, crisscrossing beneath mountains and a good indicator of a Cruel Dragon lair nearby. Finding an abandoned Cruel Dragon nest is a fantastic windfall for prospectors, miners, and adventuring types — though it is tempered with significant amounts of fear and caution as the owner is not necessarily dead and may return at any time.

Cruel Dragons have few concerns or competitors; they surpass @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} at older stages of their lives and are far more powerful than other dragons in terms of raw strength. They are some of the few entities in the Ember Cosmos who do not fear @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors}, and there are rumors that clashes between the two often result in the Abyssal Horror being defeated. This terrifying concept would suggest older Cruel Dragons are the most powerful monsters in the cosmos and stand above all others. They don't tend to concern themselves with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans} as equals either, viewing them with the same contempt as any other creature, though they do sometimes hunt them for food and could be described as the only beings that prey upon Leviathans.

Biology

Cruel Dragons are considered to be the quintessential monsters, and while they share a vague resemblance to reptiles there are far more differences, than similarities. They are not natural creatures, but monsters infused with magical fire and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{Abyssal energy} to the extent that fire oozes from their bodies and glows in the darkness like a raging forest fire. A Cruel Dragon has especially thick large powerful wings and extremely hard scales, with four muscled limbs that allow them to move around on the ground with a grace and speed that belies their size. Cruel Dragons also have long tails that can be brutish and deadly, with huge dangerous spikes, and whip-like speed. Their mouths and jaws are perhaps their most deadly weapons and are filled with razor-sharp teeth the size of fully grown mortals.

Cruel Dragons scales are almost always black, dark brown, or red and fully encase them in thick impenetrable armor. Intense fiery cracks and seams between the scales of the jaw, throat, and underbelly emit intensely glowing fire that drips from and burns the ground beneath them. Sometimes this fiery glow spreads to the claws and tails and they are known to be incredibly hot creatures that are comfortable swimming through lava.

Cruel Dragons are thought to live for a thousand years or so, growing so large they cannot sustain themselves and eventually, they burn themselves out from within. There are some rumored exceptions to this however and some Cruel Dragons somehow surpass this limitation. @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l2UZCjkk0lRAlcTZ]{Karaxsus}, the flaming dread is said to be one of the original dragons created by Alar and was active in the world for two thousand years.

Reproduction

Cruel Dragons only mate among their own kind and cannot produce eggs with other dragon types or creatures. They are strangely fond of their mates, though they never live within the same lair, and live alone for most of their lives. Once they do find a mate however, they mate for life and will travel to one another homes to spend time with one another every few centuries. This is often another layer of danger when encountering a Cruel Dragon, and if you slay one, you had better make sure they don't have a living mate, or it will seek you out and take revenge. Cruel Dragons have male and female genders, but there is barely any dimorphism difference between the two — both sexes can lay eggs, but only one partner will do so, while the other is responsible for fertilization. The eggs are always kept with the Cruel Dragon that laid them; there is no real concept of mother or father, merely two parents and their offspring.

Cruel Dragons only lay a single egg and will tend to them over several years as they mature exceptionally slowly. Once they hatch, the parent typically watches them for several months as they grow, bringing them food. They are caring and strangely tender to their children and will protect them with a burning fury that is near impossible to describe. Cruel Dragon children sometimes stay with their parents for many years, learning and helping them build their piles of precious metals. This affection among their own kind is bizarre but common behavior, and even unrelated Cruel Dragosn treat each other with respect. When a young dragon does leave to find a place of their own, their parents will usually gift them some metal for them to start their lairs and this is the only time Cruel Dragons willingly part with their hoards.

Abilities

Cruel Dragons are magical monsters of strength and power that are essentially unrivaled within the Ember Cosmos. They have many abilities that make them absolute masters of fire and play with its effects in the same way a child plays with a wooden toy. Among their most feared abilities is their fiery breath known as Dragonfyre. This unimaginably hot magical fire melts through stone and metals with ease and it is controllable in its strength and the way that it behaves. Very few beings can survive the full force of an elder Crual Dragons Dragonfyre.

Cruel Dragons are among the largest entities on Ember and rival @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans} in size. They grow rapidly once hatched and quickly reach hundreds of feet in length over the course of a few hundred years. Older Cruel Dragons are reopened to reach sizes of nearly a mile in length, and their wingspans can block out the sun across entire towns. Cruel Dragons of this size however are truly infamous individuals and do not appear randomly, many are recorded in history books or guides for regional threats and mortals leave them well alone.

Curiously Cruel Dragons have some innate ability to cast spells of an arcane nature, though they rarely do so. This mastery over magic extends over time and its thought that some of the older Cruel Dragons begin to master some extremely powerful magic that can begin warping the lands around their lairs. Some legends insist that elder Cruel Dragons can change their forms and walk among mortals, though it's not clear why they would choose to do so.

History

Cruel Dragons were created during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, at the end of the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering} by the Elder Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}. Since that time, they have descended upon the World of Ember and become some of the most dangerous threats against mortals imaginable. Cruel Dragons live mostly in distant and remote areas of the world and are far more common in the far north of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterican} Continent. Cruel Dragons also inhabit the Spine of Ember in large numbers, and many of these specimens have established lairs within the crumbling ruins of ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} cities (thanks to their vacancy following the events of the Shattering and the annihilation of the Shent culture). Most Cruel Dragons can be found lairing deep beneath the ground and throughout the Pathways, carving massive tunnels through the earth as they voraciously search for precious metals.

The most famous Cruel Dragon is perhaps @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l2UZCjkk0lRAlcTZ]{Karaxsus}, the flaming dread who destroyed the Oderita Kingdom in its entirety nearly a thousand years ago. It's not currently known if he still lives or has burned away, as his last appearance was several hundred years ago.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l2UZCjkk0lRAlcTZ]{Karaxsus}

Giant.name: Giant
Giant.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Giant.scoverview: "Giant" is a broad term that has various uses throughout Ember, but it's most commonly used to describe the ancestry of towering humanoids who originated long ago during the Age of Beasts. The most ancient of these peoples — known as True Giants — no longer exist, having been driven from the Pathways after The Unveiling. Furthermore, the Elder Giants that established the Shent culture have also largely vanished from the world. Only the Inheritor Giants that comprise the Varún and Tolvor Kohatai clans are present in Ember today; and these large folk are quite smaller than their ancient predecessors.

Trolls.name: Trolls
Trolls.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Trolls.scoverview: Trolls are vicious, brutal creatures that were once beasts and animals but were transformed into terrifying brutes early on during the Age of Beasts by an ancient Shard God named Savaris. Trolls are a plague upon the northern lands of the Aterican Continent and the only thing keeping them in check are the near-constant clashes between themselves.

Leviathans.name: Leviathans
Leviathans.text:
• Keywords: Primordial, Colossal, Strong

  • Ember Type: Creature

  • Type: Beasts

  • Other Names: Ancient Beasts

Leviathans are some of the most ancient creatures to ever exist, or so people believe. In many tales and stories, they are guardians of ancient places and creatures of the world and of nature. This is very far from the truth, however, and some groups and mortals in the world today know the truth. Leviathans are natural creatures, yes, but they are often ruinous, deadly, and destructive forces that kill, eat, and lay waste to the environments around them. They were once prevented from destroying the world by primordial heroes like the Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar}, who hunted them and protected mortals from their destructive wrath.

A few extremely rare Leviathans seem to have transcended their bestial nature and ascended as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} like the great bone serpent, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rmMWMD9iFRm6Nl3x]{Obrisire}. However, this is incredibly rare, and few examples of such creatures exist despite the time periods involved.

Today, Leviathans can be found across the whole world of Ember; they are rare but not entirely uncommon either, and if you explore the wild places of the world, it's likely that you may find one hidden in the deepest of forests or striding across the boundless plains or tundra. They are best avoided, however, and have fearsome reputations, and many nearby cultures will even protect them or at least make sure no one enters their territories and disturbs them.

Leviathans have no true basic appearance; they take the form of huge, often gargantuan, or even colossal creatures and animals that are wilder, fiercer, and absolutely deadly. Some Leviathans are said to be many miles in length and size and are the greatest forces in the region simply because no other forces can destroy them. They are known to kill Dragons and even @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} and there are mythological tales of Shard Gods falling in battle to them in the case of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.j9bIMMSCcMeHstz9]{Godkiller Orinoth}.
Leviathans.scoverview: Colossal in both size and influence, Leviathans are primeval creatures of Ember that have roamed the surface world since the earliest days of the Age of Beasts. These ancient creatures often vary widely in shape and appearance — but they all tend to follow natural, animalistic forms, often with enlarged or impressively-accentuated features. Some Leviathans subsume themselves into specific ecosystems to become the apex predators of those areas; others can be far more destructive, and tend to affect the land around them in strange ways as they strip away life itself.
Leviathans.sgamemaster:
Leviathans are forces of nature themselves and are often equal in power to the Shard Gods of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}. Their origin is mysterious, apparently hailing from the distant continent of Jurin; they were once a plague upon the world and were so numerous that they posed a dire threat to the precursor ancestry of the Jarn. At some point, however, the flood of Leviathans across the world slowed to a trickle, and they seem primarily confined in significant number upon Jurin itself. Today, new Leviathans arriving upon the shores of Ateria or Kessia are rare; the majority are ancient creatures living in the same areas and territories for many thousands of years. Thornlings will claim that they come from a great ancestor called the Leafia, who hold the Leviathans at bay. However, scholars do not take this particularly seriously as no one has ever traveled or confirmed that Jurin exists.

It is thought that Leviathans grow with age, and the older the Leviathan, the stronger and larger it becomes. This may well be true across extremely long periods, or something else might be at work because scholars have yet to fully confirm this.

The glade was dark, near pitch black, as Lantyr fell below the horizon. Beneath the bowes of the trees around me, the air was still, soft and quiet. As I stared between the great trunks of the Jukata Trees, whose size rivaled entire buildings, two massive red eyes emerged from the gloom. The vapor from the throat of an equally colossal mouth drifted through the air and framed a terrifying face fixed in a vicious snarl. I fought to keep my own breathing steady and calm as my vision adjusted, and as it did so, the full extent of the creature in front of me was revealed. It had a combination of black scales, black fur, and a series of feathers down each of its four deeply muscled arms, giving it the look and style of a predatory feline of colossal size and strength. Its gaze held my own for what seemed an eternity, studying and judging me for entering its territory. After what had perhaps only been a moment in truth, with a shake of its head, it sank slowly into the darkness behind it without a sound and left me blissfully alone once more..

The World Beyond, Volume 27; Laeora [erased].

Leviathans are known to be incredibly territorial. They attack and kill any that dare set foot on land they claim. This has led to many mortals avoiding Leviathans and their lands entirely, and for good reason, as while Leviathans may be creatures, they possess a keen intelligence. While they might not be fully sapient, they can hold absolutely hold grudges. Leviathans have been known to destroy mortal hunting parties, track the party's path, and wipe out entire settlements as revenge, traveling outside their normal range.

While most Leveithans are intelligent, only a few rare cases of actual sapient thinking ability have been confirmed. The greatest example of this is Godkiller Orinith, who killed a Shard God, and not only that, but Orinoth also killed perhaps the most extraordinary Leviathan-hunting Shard God ever to exist. Leviathans do not discriminate either and will confront, kill, and even eat Dragons. Battles between Leviathans and Dragons are said to split the very ground and world around them and are terrible, destructive confrontations that can last for hours or even days.

Known Leviathans

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rmMWMD9iFRm6Nl3x]{Obrisire}

  • @UUID[Actor.q4ekelPqHPwteauF]{Krasarioc}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.j9bIMMSCcMeHstz9]{Godkiller Orinoth}

Hassratch.text:
Under Construction

Hassratch.scoverview: Hassratch are monsters that are said to have been created by an evil god and released in large numbers upon Ember during the time of the Shattering. They tend to gather in dark, hidden places where they can hoard secrets, using these discretions to manipulate mortals into servitude; these minions are known to perform a variety of tasks, from the collection of knowledge to the execution of heinous acts. Hassratch are deceptive creatures, often portraying themselves as priestesses or acolytes of noble deities.

Casia.text:
Under Construction

Casia.scoverview: Casia are the powerful feline-like beings that rule over the realm of Primordis.

Tyraphem.name: Tyraphem
Tyraphem.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Tyraphem.scoverview: Tyraphem are the powerful beings that reside upon the Inner Realm of Luxarum. Not only are the Tyraphem powerful but they are extremely numerous and combined with an incredibly warlike and martial nature they could become a major threat to the entire Cosmos. Thankfully they have been engaged in a never-ending war with themselves since Creation.

Daemos.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Daemos.scoverview: The Daemos are the extremely powerful beings that rule the Inner Realm of Signara, they are few in number but each is capable of great feats of power.

Wyrms.name: Wyrms
Wyrms.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Wyrms.scoverview: Wyrms are the mythical creatures that once populated the Order moon of Akon. Long-dead since the events of the Shattering, these enigmatic serpents gave rise to Ember's three species of Dragons.

Skum.name: Skum
Skum.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Skum.scoverview: Skum are terrifying creatures that resemble a horrific blend of humanoid and fish. They are monsters that first appeared after the events of the Abyssal Shear, since then they have spread across the surface world of Ember like a malignant plague.

Nepkela.name: Nepkela
Nepkela.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Nepkela.scoverview: Monstrous crustacean-like humanoid creatures that arose during the events of the Abyssal Shear. They are carnivorous, cannibalistic, and extremely dangerous.

Fiend.name: Fiend

Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Fiend.scoverview: Fiends are the servants of the Daemos and live primarily upon Signara, though a few are given tasks by their masters and pursue their own goals upon the surface world.

Celestials.name: Celestials
Celestials.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Celestials.scoverview: Celestials are otherworldly beings from Luxarum that serve the Tyraphem. Much like their masters, they are aggressive and martial in nature, and are often zealous (if not fanatical) in their service to the Luxaran religion known as the "The Light".

Fae.name: Fae

Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Fae.scoverview: Fae are the children of the Casia, a vastly varied and complex group that will sometimes serve a Casia with fierce loyalty while others are chaotic, wild and dangerous to mortals.

V'Mar.name: V'Mar
V'Mar.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
V'Mar.scoverview: Once humanoids, these beings were warped into monstrous creatures. They may or not be winged but are almost always thin and disjointed monsters with maws a thin sharp teeth. They may also bear magical markings or visual indicators of Malae's magical curse that still affects them.

Naga.name: Naga
Naga.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Naga.scoverview: Naga are a snakelike monster that came into being upon the continent of Kessia after the destruction of the Aedir Colonies.

Jurtak.name: Jurtak
Jurtak.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Jurtak.scoverview: Abyssal corrupted Lizard-like creatures with long tails, and sharp teeth. They are capable of constructing basic tools and settlements, they wear primitive armor and are highly aggressive and xenophobic.

Chimera.name: Chimera
Chimera.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Chimera.scoverview: Chimera are monstrous creatures, typically infused with Abyssal energy though some kinds are amalgamations of various natural creatures created by mages of Ember in the distant past. They are often violent, aggressive, and extremely dangerous monsters that are either territorial or predatory towards mortals.

Delvers.name: Delvers
Delvers.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Delvers.scoverview: Delvers are small bipedal monsters with strong arms and thick claws. They are found beneath the surface of Ember, where they maintain surprisingly complex societies, creating machines, weapons, and armor.

Wargs.name: Wargs
Wargs.text:
Under Construction

Wargs.scoverview: Wargs are corrupted wolf like creatures that prowl dark forests and wild places of the world.

Lamia.name: Lamia
Lamia.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Lamia.scoverview: The upper torso of a Lamia is Human or Jarn-like while the lower body is four-limbed and appears cat-like. They are said to be a strange experiment by the ancient Casia and are mysterious and strange beings. They are said to hail from the distant lands of Kessia and among the Fae upon the Inner Realm of Primordis.

Hydral.name: Hydral
Hydral.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Hydral.scoverview: The reptilian Hydral are large abyssal monsters that possess numerous heads upon their scaled muscular bodies. They are most commonly encountered in Ember's swamps or dense jungles, and are a veritable plague upon the Lowlands subcontinent.

Kraken.name: Kraken
Kraken.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Kraken.scoverview: Kraken are colossal, extremely powerful, Abyssal Monsters that are said to be abyss-corrupted Leviathans. They are said to dwell in some of the deepest areas of the World's oceans and are also common within the Pathways, having traveled along watery tunnels to lurk in dark places.

Wraiths.name: Wraiths
Wraiths.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Wraiths.scoverview: Wraiths are powerful, apparitions that feed upon the fear and misery of the living.

Wights.name: Wights
Wights.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Wights.scoverview: Wights are a powerful type of undead warrior. Physically strong and slow-moving, these vengeful entities are extremely hateful of Ember's mortals, driven by an undying rage and a thirst for destruction. Fortunately for the living, these vile creatures are repelled by sunlight and fire, providing some measure of hope amidst the darkest of nights.

Ghouls.name: Ghouls
Ghouls.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Ghouls.scoverview: Ghouls are a voracious type of undead that are cursed with an insatiable hunger for the flesh of the living. This drives them to wage wars on bordering lands, emerging from the dark, to rip the living out of their homes. Those they kill but do not eat quickly rise to become new ghouls, and join the ranks.

Theroch.name: Theroch
Theroch.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Theroch.scoverview: The Theroch were reportedly among the first sapient mortal creatures that came into being on the surface of Ember. They are rumored to still exist in the far northern continent Jekaros much diminished by the events of the Forsaken War. Very little is now known about the Theroch in the present age but records and lost knowledge of the Aedir are sometimes recovered leading to great speculation among scholars.

Carrow.name: Carrow
Carrow.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Carrow.scoverview: The Carrow are one of the most mysterious ancestries to live upon the Surface of Ember, mainly found in the deepest parts of the vast oceans. During the Age of Beasts a recently ascended Shard god named Karlow was shunned by her husband and sons after revealing her transformation into godhood. She took her daughters and any willing Jarn women from her tribe into the oceans. The Carrow have chosen to dwell among the cold, dark and beautiful underwater regions of Ember ever since.

Akonites.name: Akonites
Akonites.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Akonites.scoverview: Akonites are constructs that reside upon the dead moon of Akon. They once served the Wyrms of Akon but since their destruction, they have had little purpose. Some continue to protect and maintain the various Wyrm-made machinery, upon Akon itself and in remote locations across the Cosmos, others have broken down and decayed, becoming violent and insane.

Elementals.name: Elementals
Elementals.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Elementals.scoverview: Elementals are creatures of raw primeval power native to the Elemental Moons of the Cosmos (Aura, Akon, Cora, Mayis, Orbis, and Ragen) and the Inner Realms (Luxarum, Primordis, and Signara). Embodiments of the respective forces of these cosmic landscapes, elementals are as varied as they are unknowable — ranging in both size and power from the tiniest mote to the most colossal destructor, including the remarkably powerful Elemental Sages. Ultimately, the various Elemental Sovereigns of the cosmos are the supreme expression of a particular elemental force, and there is usually only one of these godlike beings in creation at any given point in time.

Leafia.name: Leafia
Leafia.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Leafia.scoverview: Leafia are a massive plant-based ancestry found only on the distant primal continent of Jurin. They are an ancestry created long ago during the early Age of Beasts by the Shard God Janar to combat and stop Leviathans. For the most part, they have been highly successful, thus the name they call themselves is Leviathan Hunters.

Spiders.name: Spiders
Spiders.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Spiders.scoverview: Every spider in existence is a monster, and Spiders came into the Ember world during the Shattering. Curiously, they are neither good nor evil, though some are predatory with a terrifying amount of intelligence. This includes tiny house spiders that mortals tend to see in their daily lives to massive monstrous creatures that live in the most remote wilderness.

Spirit Beasts.name: Spirit Beasts
Spirit Beasts.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Spirit Beasts.scoverview: Ive always been fascinated by the Moon of Orbis, but unlike many other bodies of the cosmos, I have never set foot upon its surface. I was planning to do so long ago, but was advised against it by Alar during one of our many chance encounters, and although she was most unwilling to share her reasons it was the first time that I learned of the name Spirit Beasts.

Jarn.name: Jarn
Jarn.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Jarn.scoverview: The Jarn, are considered the first true humanoid peoples on the surface world, though some records and legends dispute this. They were the first makers of tools, clothing and language and became the precursor people of the world that almost all other humanoid peoples on the surface of Ember are descended from. They went extinct after the creation of Humans.

Abyssal Horrors.name: Abyssal Horrors
Abyssal Horrors.text: Most mortals on Ember do not consider Abyssal Horrors to be real. Only a few scholars believe they may have once existed due to the prevalence of information and consistent tales of individual Abyssal Horrors from various places in the World. However, to most, they are simply part of the myths and legends surrounding the Shattering and the collapse of civilizations long ago.
Abyssal Horrors.scoverview: Abyssal Horrors are terrifying, and eldritch beings that are part of many whispered myths and legends from the times after the Shattering. Said to be vaguely humanoid but utterly horrific in every other respect, with many eyes, limbs, and the ability to control the minds of mortals. Most cultures have laws or cultural taboos around even mentioning their existence, and if they are spoken of, they are the principal villains in horror stories and tales.
Abyssal Horrors.sgamemaster:
• Keywords: Evil, Corruption, Destruction

  • Type: Aberration

  • Other Names: Zairoths, Xaré'ans

WARNING

References to the Abyss, the Abyssal Shear or Abyssal Horrors etc are not things that the player characters would learn about before gameplay begins unless under very specific circumstances for background purposes. This absolutely includes all Outer Gods as well.

Abyssal Horrors are terrifying and eldritch beings from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{the Abyss}. They are the principal servants of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.hq1cXdVHjFbQxfys]{Outer Gods} in general, but every Abyssal Horror has an Outer God that it ultimately serves above the others. They are utterly terrifying to behold, with gaping maws of needle teeth, multiple eyes, many limbs, and grasping hands that end in sharp claws. Thought to be the result of an Outer God or one of their Herald's curiosity with Ember, they are a twisted reflection of mortal peoples.

While their basic appearance is frightening enough, they vary wildly, and no two Abyssal Horrors are alike. Some may sprout humanoid arms and legs, while others may sprout varying numbers of tentacle-like appendices with dark pink, purple, or grey skin tones. The eyes of an Abyssal Horror seem optional, as they "see" the world around them through some unknown means. Twisted horns and spikes may adorn thin, elongated heads with gaping maws of pointed sharp teeth or strange toothless holes stretching wide enough to swallow a mortal's head. Abyssal Horrors also vary in size; some are towering figures nearly 25 feet tall, while others will be smaller and stand at the same height as an average mortal. The reason for such unparalleled fear and hatred by the beings of Ember is the Abyssal Horrors' unique and terrifying ability to corrupt and take over the minds of countless mortals within days in any given area. They are also capable of controlling other lesser monsters by force and enslaving them to their will.

Abyssal Horrors are incredibly cruel, destructive, and thoroughly evil creatures. They have free will and are not merely extensions of their masters. Still, they act in their ultimate interests in every sense. They are committed to the destruction and corruption of all life within the cosmos of Ember, and they cannot be reasoned with or convinced to ally themselves with the goals of mortals or beings created by the Heart of Ember, like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods}.

They first made their way past the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{Weave} and entered the Ember Cosmos during the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, causing unimaginable destruction. They were the direct causes of much of the woes inflicted upon the cosmos during this time. Since then, however, they have diminished, and their numbers have significantly reduced. Hiding in the dark places, they wait or plot to bring about their master’s will, which almost always means destroying all life. Whenever they are found, all creatures and beings born of the Heart of Ember, including the Shard Gods and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} will focus their attention on annihilating their places of power beyond any other concern. Abyssal Horrors can kill most Shard Gods, and it often takes several Shards together or the intervention of an Elder God to destroy them.

The only saving grace for the people of Ember is that Abyssal Horrors do not collaborate with one another, and are extremely independent in their efforts to destroy and corrupt the cosmos around them. Whether due to innate pride, disdain for others of their kind, or perhaps a failing from the Outer Gods themselves, these motives are as inscrutable as the otherworldly villains themselves.

Known Abyssal Horrors

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas}

Bestiary Overview.name: Bestiary Overview
Bestiary Overview.text:
There are three broad classifications of life forms in Ember, based upon some key differences between them in a number of areas. Within these broad classifications, there can be a massive variation in type, shape, appearance, and behavior. The First classification is Ancestries, the Second is Creatures, and the third is Monsters.

Ancestries

These life forms exhibit both sentience and sapience in one form or another. Sentience is the ability to experience feelings and have some kind of awareness of oneself, in addition to the ability to feel pain and grief. While Sapience is the ability to think, the capacity for intelligence, and the ability to reason. There are many Ancestries in the Ember Cosmos and some numbers in the millions, as is the case with humans in the current age. It is possible to be both an Ancestry and a Creature or an Ancestry and a Monster, but this is only a small distinction and rarely used except for perhaps a historical origin or connection. For example, Dragons are technically an Ancestry, but they are regarded as Monsters due to their origin and behavior. Examples of Ancestries include but are not limited to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Human}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.uYINWy1xgnIkCVaC]{Carrow} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia}.

Creatures

Creatures are life forms created by the effects of the Heart of Ember and Lifeforce. In almost every case, Creatures are referred to as natural, which means animals, beasts, reptiles, birds, and a host of insects and other smaller beings. Technically speaking, this also includes Plants and Fungi as although these life forms do not move they are still natural creatures originating from the Heart of Ember. Creatures may be natural but this does not mean they are peaceful or passive; they can be incredibly aggressive, carnivorous, and deadly. Examples of Creatures include but are not limited to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.0Hdrg5LbCh0XaLGp]{Ancara} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.k7OqrgNIwwPJf33w]{Yarnac}.

Monsters

Monsters, on the other hand, are beings introduced during the events of the Shattering. They are young compared to the natural creatures of Ember having only existed for a few thousand years and they are considered "alien" to the cosmos, and almost all are evil, dangerous, and corrupting in various ways. Undead are also classified as Monsters in this sense as they are connected to the alien energies despite them being also connected to once living Creatures or Ancestries. Examples of Monsters include but are not limited to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.efXX30CpuVqlWblK]{Hassratch}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.krye4A4iHch1wC9i]{Vampyres} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.UIXhmx3iwyk52raz]{Spiders}.
Bestiary Overview.scoverview: Since Creation, the Ember Cosmos has been teaming with life in every form imaginable. Some are as ancient as the world and others are so young that they are still trying to find a place to survive and call thier own. Exploring the World of Ember is a dangerous, difficult, and often deadly ordeal; its environments can be extreme and hostile, but they are often overshadowed by the threats posed by natural creatures and monsters. It takes the strength of an extraordinary will to leave the confines of a safe village or city and strike out into the wilds, and sometimes, the monsters in the dark can be very close to home indeed.

Vampyres.name: Vampyres
Vampyres.text:
• Keywords: Blood, Death, Immortal

  • Ember Type: Monster

  • Type: Undead

Mortal ancestors on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} know a great deal about Vampyres from the tales and stories of Moiran refugees who fled the Evernight and from the continuing experience of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, who regularly encounter them during the cycles of Fire and death. This shared knowledge contains many truths but also a few misconceptions and exaggerations.

A Vampyre retains its appearance from life; it can appear extraordinarily hale and healthy, almost pristine, without marks, and the appearance of aging appears graceful and firm. This does not mean all Vampyres are youthful-looking, and their appearances range across the age ranges of every ancestry. This serene appearance can change dramatically on a whim, however, and when a Vampyre is hunting, or angry or upon command its facial features twist unnaturally, as its regular teeth extend and grow sharp, especially the canines that elongate dramatically. Often, this means a slight distortion of the entire jaw to fit the new row of more prominent, sharper teeth.

A Vampyre is said to have no heartbeat and requires blood from mortals to survive. This is primarily true from my own accounts, and Vampyres are undead in every sense of the word, but they do not require blood to survive and do eat and consume normal food types like bread and fruits when needed. Unfortunately, the transformation into a Vampyre has a dramatic mental effect and causes the vast majority of Vampyres to become extremely predatory. This results in them feeding and hunting mortals and consuming them. It's said that a Vampyre has an unending hunger for blood only, but in reality, some Vampyres only feel the need to kill and the thrill of the hunt, while others seek to consume flesh instead.

It's said that Vampyres are created by allowing a mortal to feed from them instead, offering their own tainted blood that transforms the mortal into an immortal monster. This is partly true, but the process is more complex and requires the original Vampyre to imbue a certain amount of its power into the process, which drains them for days or even months. Thus, despite what many believe, the act of creating more Vampyres is not performed regularly, and most Vampyres tend to avoid creating more of their kind unless a situation requires it.

Vampyrism is thought to be a curse upon the living and a curse specifically created to target and punish the Moiran people for some ancient folly or injustice. Surviving Moiran families believe this wholeheartedly despite some evidence to suggest that it may be a magical process created by some ancient being. Regardless of the origin, Vampyres are not only undead and immortal but are extremely powerful monsters and among the strongest undead. They can move incredibly quickly, with some mortals believing that they have an innate ability to teleport and move instantly through space. They are also greater strength than mortals with skin that cannot be pieced with ordinary metals.
Vampyres.scoverview: Vampyres are monsters of blood and undeath. They feed upon the blood of mortal creatures and are considered malicious, evil, and utterly without remorse. They are rare outside of the Moiran lands in the south of the Aterican continent but can be found among many cultures preying upon the helpless. Most of their fearsome reputation comes from their first appearances in Ember around the time of the Evernight, and they are greatly feared by all mortals.
Vampyres.sgamemaster:
Among monsters and especially undead, Vampyres, are incredibly unusual in that they are not consumed by evil upon being inflicted by undeath. Vampyres are generally considered to be sane and possess free will from the monent the are transformed. Unfortunately, The majority lean towards evil due to their instinctual changes and desires that occur during the transformation process. Still, there are rare examples of Vampyres in Ember that have rejected evil in every form and fought against their nature or even combat their own kind and other undead.

It's not known precisely how or why Vampyre came into existence, but it's believed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.P2Xu1anbZwADenvM]{Elwin Davos} is the original Vampyre that created all the others. Though some Vampyres dispute this and suggest that there were, in fact, several Vampyres at first that spread the curse.

Weaknesses

Some people believe that Vampyres cannot stand the light of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} and that sunlight somehow burns them. Unfortunately, this is untrue; Vampyres can stride through sunlight without damage or aversion. Despite what some think, they have no innate weaknesses to fire or silver either. Vampyres have very few actual weaknesses, and they are terrifying entities that, once they fixate on a hunt, can be single-minded and almost impossible to destroy.

The little-known but only true weakness of Vampyres is that they are repelled and extremely sensitive to Lifeforce. Lifeforce is often the origin of many holy spells used by clerics, priests, and druids, and it can greatly harm a Vampyre if used directly against them.

Known Vampyres

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.P2Xu1anbZwADenvM]{Elwin Davos}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.sZ7WbCZE3811qQrD]{Menis Valegar}

  • @UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan}

Ancara.name: Ancara
Ancara.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Ancara.scoverview: A ferocious creature from the Corebright Forest, they are common mounts of Kirargy Knights.

Yarnac.name: Yarnac
Yarnac.text:
The Yarnac is a large, woolly creatures highly valued as a work animal by the Bejak people, and came with them when they immigrated to the Arctus Plateau. Because of their even temperament and ease of training, the Yarnac is a celebrated beast for its loyalty, and vital role in daily life and labor across numerous regions.

Anatomy

The Yarnac’s hardy anatomy is ideally suited for the harsh climates in which it thrives. Its shaggy woolen coat provides exceptional insulation against biting winds and low temperatures, while its dense muscle and fat layers make it capable of sustaining high levels of effort or long distance travel. The creature’s powerful legs and broad feet provide stability and traction on most any terrain, while its long tail aids in balance.

The distinctive antler-crest offers both a tool for fending off predators and a magnificent display for potential mates or rivals.

While Yarnac are mostly used was work animals, their hides are highly prized for their thickness and warmth and can be crafted into durable clothing and accessories. Yarnac meat is fatty and rich, and cooks well.

Behaviour

Traveling in herds, Yarnacs are social creatures with a naturally gentle disposition. They’re naturally docile, easily adapting to humanoid presence, and are quick to respond to training as beasts of burden. When domesticated, they can tirelessly plow fields, transport goods, draw wagons, and power machines.

Despite their size, they are remarkably placid, with even temperament and long tempers under most circumstances. However, if they or their herd are threatened, their formidable size, power, and antler crests allow them to become incredibly dangerous.
Yarnac.scoverview: This behemoth of a creature is squat, and slow moving, its huge body covered in dense, shaggy. Its head is broad and powerful, crowned with an impressive crest of bone forming an antler shield. It lumbers along on short, pillar-like legs ending in broad, flat feet meant to distribute it's enormous weight. A long, plume-like tail sways gently behind it, providing a counterbalance to its movement.
Yarnac.sgamemaster:
The Yarnac is highly esteemed by the Bejak people, who cultivated relationships with them from the earliest days, hunting and herding them in equal measure to survive. Over time, the Bejak have perfected the art of domestication, turning Yarnacs into indispensable companions and work partners.

The introduction of Yarnacs to the Arctus Plateau was seen as a boon for agricultural development and survival in the region as they become vital parts of the silt and mud extraction process for lakeside dredging operations. At this point, Yarnac are a largely domesticated beast and wild Yarnac are incredibly rare outside of their original northern homeland.

Oozes.name: Oozes
Oozes.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Beta.
Oozes.scoverview: Oozes originally come from the Blasted Moon of Cora, and while they are often not considered Elementals, they have some incredibly unique and mysterious magical biology.

Artificer.name: Artificer
Artificer.text:
Ember has more than its fair share of Artificers, whose marvelous creations can be found throughout the world — from the technocratic innovations of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire, to the arcane marvels of the mysterious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.lOu3Wwh34SH6uqV1]{Lorai}, or the masterful folk constructs of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturians}. Some say the ubiquity of arcane artifice throughout Ember's cosmos owes much to the perpetual clockwork influence of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, the Shattered Moon — which has become a much larger part of daily life on the living planet since the advent of The Shattering. Others maintain that these arcane innovators have been around for ages untold, as far back as the time of the ancient Shent and beyond (and they would be quite correct to do so).

Premium Content Required

The Artificer class is only available to use in Ember if you also have Tasha's Cauldron of Everything by Wizards of the Coast installed and activated.

Alchemist

Alchemist Artificers of Ember are a cut above the world's standard apothecaries or chemists. These specialists are practitioners of elevated alchemical arts that infuse their reagents with remarkable magic potential, and are capable of chemical masteries that can both harm and heal. The practice of alchemy is common to many of Ember's cultures, but the most famed Alchemists of the living planet tend to hail from cultures like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Strider} peoples, who each prize the study and innovation of chemical sciences in their own unique ways. Furthermore, Artificers of Ember are also known to inhabit and originate from places of extreme weather and preternatural strife — such as the lightless depths of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}, the blistering deserts of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia}, or the frigid expanse of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UeziKENAQNnY5lYj]{Rimedrift}.

Armorer

Armorers are those Artificers who specialize in the creation and use of enchanted armor, and are welcome in nearly all cultures of Ember — particularly those that have a greater need to defend themselves. Indisputably, this area of study is most honored among Ember's warring nations and cultures, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan}, or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} peoples. And as one might expect, Armorer Artificers are extremely rare among the seafaring @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilians}, whose mistrust of arcane magic leads them to put more faith in actual physical technology rather than the metaphysical arcana of enchanted artifice.

Artillerist

Artillerist Artificers specialize in the powerful magic of enchanted weaponry, and are capable of developing some of the world's most potent methods of ranged arcane attacks. Despite being notably sparse in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire (where the use of explosive chemical compounds reigns supreme), Artillerists can be found throughout Ember's most war-torn and dangerous lands — including the shadow-haunted reaches of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.y4WHE3TEr6Of13SL]{Railen}-controlled realms of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.NdqwtFoFAw85Gstr]{Aran Peninsula}, and the Bloodworm-ridden expanses of northern @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia}. Furthermore, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} people are known to cultivate Artillerists among their ranks in larger numbers than most, as are the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.lOu3Wwh34SH6uqV1]{Lorai} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.oFaQK5PcWivfuOx3]{Nalvani} descendants of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir}.

Battle Smith

Arcane healers and protectors, Battle Smiths are valued members of society throughout Ember, no matter where they dwell. Battle Smiths and their steel defenders are a rather common sight among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Maziran} people of far-off @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.3ImHPBYTX7u3OqEQ]{Akazea}. However, these Maziran steel defenders are typically "steel" in name only, having been created using an exquisite array of more esoteric materials like semi-precious gemstone stone and arcane glass. Naturally, their @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} neighbors beyond The Crossing Sea have grown quite accustomed to this area of study as well.

Cartographer

In the Ember Cosmos, the Cartographer is more than a simple mapmaker; they are dedicated archivists and chroniclers of the world's changing, expanding reality. Within the Tayan Empire, Cartographers are highly regimented and organized under the direct authority of the Tayan Cartographers' Guild. They focus their efforts on validating and extending the Empire's territorial claims, and their magical practices center on the precise manipulation of arcana and Aethyra, enabling them to survey vast distances with unerring accuracy, create magically anchored boundary markers, and uncover hidden natural resources valuable to the Empire. They are less concerned with lore and more with concrete political power, with many also working within the ranks of the feared Vyrn.
Artificer.scoverview: Artificers are inventive creators who blend physical creation with arcane skill to create amazing magical devices. An experienced Artificer is capable of achieving many wonders, limited only by the quality of their tools and the limits of their innovation. Whether by infusing pre-existing materials with magical essence or creating enchanted items whole cloth, Artificers shape the world around them using their expert grasp of arcane technology.

Barbarian.name: Barbarian
Barbarian.text:
A Barbarian's Rage can originate from a variety of sources — whether it stems from the blood of the Barbarian's ancestors, the cosmic influence of a shard god, or the primeval Heart of Ember itself. The Paths a Barbarian can walk are numerous, and often carry these indomitable warriors to places unseen by their kith and kin. Barbarians of Ember need not be uneducated brutes with provincial attitudes, but they do tend to shirk many elements of local propriety wherever they may roam.

Path of the Beast

Barbarians who follow the Path of the Beast are bestial warriors whose souls are infused with primal, animalistic traits. These feral traits manifest during the Barbarian's Rage, physically transforming the warrior and enhancing their destructive potential. Many of those who walk the Path of the Beast on Ember hail from some of the world's most distant and ancient cultures, whose histories are deeply connected to the wild, untamed legacies of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}. Choose the thematic origin of these powers and abilities, or determine it by rolling on the table below.

1d6

Origin of the Beast

1

Your ancestors originate from the cold reaches of northern @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica}, and your people occasionally possess various traits of the Vartic Lycanthropes. You are more likely to hail from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.xImbz6Nf4mMxtKF1]{Wardcall}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.TUt9EUMWp8pV1wXe]{Fikost}, or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} cultures than others.

2

You are descended from one of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.d1bHKAOnvoumeL7p]{Primalists} from the Corebright Forest and inherited the ability to partially change shape. You are likely to hail from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Strider} culture.

3

You were gifted strange powers by an otherworldly @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia} from the Inner Realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}. Most likely, your features are predominantly feline — muscular, ferocious, and predatory.

4

Your soul is infused with the ancient power of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan}, granting you primal access to unmatched strength and fortitude. You are likely to hail from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} Culture.

5

You were experimented upon by a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos} or other fiend from the Inner Realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}. These abstruse manipulations have granted your body the ability to undergo strange and powerful biological transformations.

6

You soul is cursed with monstrous influence from the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles}. When your Rage transforms you, hard scales cover your skin and your innate hatred for monstrosities intensifies. You are likely to hail from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} Culture.

Path of the Berserker

Barbarians who walk the Path of the Berserker are violent warriors defined by their natural born fury. Their Rage manifests via an unquenchable thirst for battle — a frenzy that drives them to deal greater damage, which can eventually reach a level of mindlessness that effectively steels the Barbarian against sources of charm or fear. Berserkers are known to hail from nearly every culture on the face of Ember, which leads some scholars to believe that the primal Rage that fuels Barbarians is innate to many (if not all) creatures of the cosmos — no matter how minuscule, whether they harness it or not.

Path of the Wild Heart

Barbarians who tread the Path of the Wild Heart possess a metaphysical kinship to the various animals and beasts of Ember, and their Rage is a supernatural manifestation of this primal connection. Path of the Wild Heart Barbarians can not only communicate with beasts, they can eventually take on their physical aspects — harnessing the power of wild animals via magical means. What most people don't fully comprehend is that the Path of the Wild Heart is guided by the very Heart of Ember itself, which is tethered to the soul of every living creature on the planet, beasts and Barbarians alike.

Path of Wild Magic

Barbarians who walk the Path of Wild Magic possess souls shaped by the raw, untamed forces of Ember's Cosmos. Their Rage is harnessed from the chaotic and uncontrollable supernatural essence of the universe, and manifests itself via a random array of wild and uncanny magic effects. This connection also grants Path of Wild Magic Barbarians the innate ability to sense magic around them, and eventually allows them to bolster themselves and their allies in kind.

Path of the World Tree

The term "Yggdrasil" is not used in Ember, but this doesn't mean that Barbarians who walk the Path of the World Tree are not present in the setting. Rather than a connection to Norse mythology, Path of the World Tree Barbarians in Ember are metaphysically linked to the ancient forests of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.dm5FW6EbHBGhJweI]{Jurin} — a distant continent located to the southeast of Aterica, far across the Carrow Ocean, known to many as "The Leviathan Preserve."

Barbarians who tread the Path of the World Tree are extremely rare individuals who possess a unique ancestral connection to a far-distant land known as Jurin, the Leviathan Preserve. Path of the World Tree Barbarians tend to be more frequent among @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.blm7nVaaSYLZX3C9]{Cor’ak} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.3s9YujjWpwPJntGa]{Thornling} peoples, whose origins in Jurin are noteworthy. The so-called Leviathan Preserve is a place of ancient primordial forests and towering trees of unimaginable scale; a tree known as the Root-father stands at the heart of this distant realm, a singular tree of such power and scale that it rivals even the height of the Broken Tower itself. Barbarians who walk the Path of the World Tree are able to draw upon the primordial power of this tree to fuel their primal Rage, which manifests via the spectral branches of the Root-father itself.

Path of the Zealot

Barbarians who walk the Path of the Zealot gain their powers from one of Ember's deities, particularly those who prize qualities of passion and avidity among their adherents. For a Path of the Zealot Barbarian, their fanatical Rage is a moment of holy (or unholy) communion, which manifests itself via a powerful transformation of divine transcendence. Numerous shard gods and pantheons hold sway throughout the world of Ember, but some cultures tend to foster more fanatical dispositions than others — such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessians}, or the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerds}. Within these cultures, Path of the Zealot Barbarians tend to fight alongside clerics and priests of their respective faiths.
Barbarian.scoverview: Barbarians are fierce warriors capable of channeling the primal energies of the cosmos via a mighty Rage, a semi-supernatural force that grants the Barbarian extraordinary strength and resilience. Eventually, this Rage manifests according to the Path a Barbarian chooses when they select their subclass, and is personified by the various traits and abilities associated with that chosen specialization.

Bard.name: Bard
Bard.text:
The Bard Colleges of Ember — whether organized or scattered to the winds — help define the various ways a Bard's artistry is able to come to life via their magic. Bards are ultimately drawn to their respective Colleges by any number of reasons, but this call to adventure is often rooted in the glamorous and awe-inspiring magic of the cosmos. Many of Ember's Bard Colleges began as terrestrial schools of artistic study, where hopefuls would learn beneath the tutelage of talented experts; however, as the years have passed, so too have the traditions of these private institutions — into the hands of errant bards the world over.

College of Creation

Ember's College of Creation originates with the fabled @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, who believe that the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} is the prime mover and central force of the cosmos. Those who follow Cindaric teachings learn songs, harmonies, and meditative chants that connect them back to the first days of creation itself. Some Creation Bards have studied under this storied tradition with the Cindaric Sages (also known as Heart Singers), while others have managed to find their way to the Heart of Ember's primeval song without the Sages — via folk music or ancient words and melodies handed down through centuries untold.

College of Eloquence

The first College of Eloquence on Ember was established by Grand Retorician Molnar, a powerful Bard of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} Republic who founded the oratory College within the bayside city of Hoist. For generations, the Eloquence Bards here have been taught to hone their craft within the Halls of Virtue — where the art of persuasion is considered a fundamental and powerful skill. Nevertheless, these teachings have recently spread beyond the borders of the republic. Thanks to the intrepid seafaring that defines Cascilian society, teachings from the College of Eloquence have made their way to Bards from Akazea to Oakengarde (and everywhere between).

College of Dance

Inspired by the constant shifting of Ember's cosmos, Bards who study from the College of Dance manifest their arcane magic via the preternatural power of physical movement. Their artistic expression through motion is a terrestrial reflection of the cosmic harmony that binds and reinforces the universe and all things in it. Naturally, Dance Bards are dexterous performers, whose speed and agility are keenly augmented by the metaphysical power of their craft. The College of Dance finds its roots in several cultures throughout Ember, including the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Fire Dancers of the Lumarin Homelands and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Maziran} Zarsa Weavers of World's End. More than any other Bard College, these disparate traditions have many elements in common - stemming from an unprecedented amount of shared respect for each other's style, values, and heritage.

College of Glamour

Ember's College of Glamour originates from the Fey-fraught Inner Realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, where the metaphysical concepts of shadow and illusion reign supreme. Founded by powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia} and their Feyfolk allies, the College of Glamour is steeped in magic both inspirational and beguiling. Bards of this College — also known as Shadow Bards — are capable of weaving powerful spells infused with the chaos and whimsy of "The First Forest," and are known to frequent all corners of Ember's expansive cosmos. And while this College's fundamental origins can be traced back to Primordis, nearly every culture of Ember plays host to their own College of Glamour, with regional traditions and artistic mainstays that reflect their particular roles in society.

College of Lore

Bards associated with the College of Lore are Ember's great collectors and purveyors of stories, whose magic is manifested via the recitation of myths, legends, folk tales, and such that reach back time immemorial. A scholarly approach to their craft allows Lore Bards to study magic that would otherwise be inaccessible to them, and they weave these esoteric spells with the same natural ease as their songs. Bards of the College of Lore tend to revere the mysterious entity known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QDRFnVBZ1jy3YiD0]{Laeora}, and the most dedicated of her adherents refer to themselves as "Truth Speakers." The College of Lore has a foothold in several of Ember's great cities, often aligned with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} strongholds and the like. The devout academics who comprise the ranks of the College of Lore throughout Ember are known as the world's most accomplished storytellers, skilled raconteurs who spin yarns like a sorcerer shapes reality.

College of the Moon

Ember's College of the Moon is steeped in the legends and lore of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles}, the homeland of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd}, where the influence of ancient and mysterious magic runs deep. Bards who study the teachings of the College of the Moon are capable of channeling the primal power of the Duskflare wilderness through their art, which is also subtly and curiously tinged by the Fey magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}. Duskflare Folktales and Blessings of the Waerdwells are common manifestations of this College's teachings, which have begun to spread beyond the borders of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowland} Bastions in recent centuries.

College of Valor

Bards who learn their craft from the College of Valor study the heroic deeds of Ember's ancient champions, and carry their bardic talents into battle. Some of the most celebrated Valor Bards hail from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken}, a culture of proud monster-hunters and dauntless survivors, whose storied myths and legends date back to the mystery-laden @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}. The Oaken's Skalds of Valor are known the world over as keepers of legend whose songs can stir their allies to perform incredible deeds. But the College of Valor is not restricted to the traditions of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.u7CDTzcmggsA1wYL]{Oakengarde}; Valor Bards are frequent among many of Ember's cultures, from the folk raconteurs of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} to the learned remainders of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire.
Bard.scoverview: Bards are skilled storytellers who manifest arcane magic through music, song, and dance. Not only can these consummate performers affect the emotions of their allies and enemies with their bardic spells, they can reshape the very world around them as any magic user could. And while all Bards tend to be jacks- and jills-of-all trade, capable of displaying prowess with nearly any skill under the sun, each Bard's specialization stems from the teachings of their Bard College — one of the numerous traditions of bardic knowledge.

Cleric.name: Cleric
Cleric.text:
Clerics in Ember emerge from the followers and priesthoods of the various @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} in Ember's pantheons. While most Clerics don't have a direct relationship with their deity of choice (such as persistent one-on-one communication), some Shard Gods in particular maintain a retinue of faithful Clerics with whom they hold close communion.

The following entries on Cleric Subclasses feature suggestions for which @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000]{Deities} would be most likely to favor a Cleric of a certain domain. Because faith is a personal belief unique to each character, we've featured a list of the various deities and their associated domains — leaving the character's "call to faith" entirely up to you.

Knowledge Domain

When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as the source of your character's divine power.

Sigil

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE overview inline]

Knowledge Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE]{Sigil} tend to be scholars and academics themselves, in addition to whatever other roles they occupy in life. Clerics of Sigil who adhere to this domain are not uncommon to the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}, home to Sigil's terrestrial residence known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.sdIjbPRNIsJ3ApcU]{Oldcraft Lodge}. Students of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy} and the Obsidian Antiquaries of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessia} are also known to host several Clerics of Sigil amongst their ranks.

Spectra

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC overview inline]

Knowledge Clerics who venerate or admire the world's most esoteric mysteries tend to be worshippers of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, who rewards her most faithful servants with blessings of divine knowledge and a greater understanding of arcane lore. Knowledge Clerics of Spectra are often appointed as protectors of the world's most influential mages and arcanists, and will invariably seek out relationships that strengthen their own connection to the living planet's magical forces.

Life Domain

When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as the source of your character's divine power.

Alar

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn overview inline]

Life Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} honor the elder god's role in creation by helping to sustain the positive energies she has fostered for centuries untold. Because she walks the terrestrial corners of Ember so frequently, worshippers of Alar can be found anywhere from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire to the shores of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordain}.

Lantyr

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH overview inline]

Life Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} generally consider themselves to be the mortal vessels of her unearthly light, and live their lives in holy veneration of her role as one of the most profound life-sustaining forces in the cosmos. Clerics of Lantyr are common to all corners of Ember, but are perhaps most prevalent throughout the sun-marked reaches of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia}, the Radiant Continent.

Nite

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.DskILHKPngH3FVa7 overview inline]

Life Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.DskILHKPngH3FVa7]{Nite} revere the primal essence of creation, and view the emergence and persistence of life (however chaotic it may be) as the most sacred force of the cosmos.
