Clerics of Nite emerge from all walks of life, but can often be found in those places where strife meets resolve — like the primal wilderness of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ntef4M02D50Y8BlE]{Corebright Forest} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles}, or the northern reaches of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.TUt9EUMWp8pV1wXe]{Fikost} (where Nite's calamitous warmth is most welcome).

Raineka

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ overview inline]

Life Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka} are known to be some of Ember's most prestigious healers and diplomats, and revere the Rainbringer herself as one of the most calming and restorative forces in the cosmos. Because of Raineka's relative youth, her worshippers throughout Ember are fewer in number than other gods of The Nineteen; but while the adherents of Raineka may be harder to find, they are certainly easier to befriend, and always eager to broker peace and communion.

Remira

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.9qLVBh0lSY0mOpLD overview inline]

Life Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.9qLVBh0lSY0mOpLD]{Remira} are known for the intimacy of their succor, and their rites and rituals tend to be sensual, rapturous occasions welcoming to all. Remira is popular among Clerics who also have a penchant for artistic skill or appreciation, and her influence is on a steady rise throughout Aterica in places of storied art and industry — like @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}, @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.HN2Zimps4w5XniZe]{Old Carinth}, or far-off @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Pn6NT1oZqpYisyjp]{Kalvard}.

Vekalla

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt overview inline]

Life Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla} are some of Ember's most intrepid healers, and tend to find themselves on the forefront of travel, exploration, and conflict — things in life where a swift resolve is usually the most beneficial one. As servants of The Whispering Wind, these Life Clerics are as widespread as the winds of Ember themselves; but it's no surprise to find the highest concentration of Vekalla worshippers among seafaring people like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}, or mountainside folk such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} of the Kaustic Hinterlands.

Light Domain

When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as the source of your character's divine power.

Lantyr

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH overview inline]

Light Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} generally consider themselves to be the mortal vessels of her unearthly light, and revere The Sun's role in the cosmos as an unmatched force of revelation. Clerics of Lantyr are common to all corners of Ember, but are perhaps most prevalent throughout the sun-marked reaches of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia}, the Radiant Continent.

Lumé

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd overview inline]

Light Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé} are generally regarded as the most generous and benevolent of her faithful, and stand as stalwart guards against the encroaching evil of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} Evernight. Indeed, the Flame Warden's physical presence in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Homelands ensures her servants feel connected and safeguarded by her holy light. Clerics of Lumé can communicate with her from afar, but she also welcomes any adherent who would seek her personal counsel.

Steelsong

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.CBreAnaMxOim355U overview inline]

Light Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.CBreAnaMxOim355U]{Steelsong} recognize their goddess in every spark of creation and each ember of a blacksmith's forge. Arguably less militaristic than other Clerics of the domain, these joyous priests tend to be a more celebratory force in the world, and praise their goddess as a champion of integrity and revelation. Steelsong's worshippers are numerous, but most of them can be found among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} peoples.

Volta

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84 overview inline]

Light Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta} are often explorers of unseen places and revealers of the unknown. Volta is a well-recognized deity, and is popular among cultures who respect progress, change, and globalism — like the gregariously industrious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}, the sea-faring merchants of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} Republic, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} peoples of the far-off @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy}. And Volta's origins during the Age of Sunlight have contributed to a lasting legacy within @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.oFaQK5PcWivfuOx3]{Nalvani} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.lOu3Wwh34SH6uqV1]{Lorai} societies as well.

Order Domain

When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as the source of your character's divine power.

Lanespear

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6dEDqbOX2xuQLUgZ overview inline]

Order Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6dEDqbOX2xuQLUgZ]{Lanespear} tend to strive for perfection in everything they do, and work to embody the shard god's immaculate sense of precision when it comes to matters of discipline and martial combat. Clerics of Lanespear are most popular among the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowlands}, where the chaotic southern reaches of the Duskflare Jungles are overrun with monstrous inhabitants in dire need of law and order.

Obrisire

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rmMWMD9iFRm6Nl3x overview inline]

Order Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rmMWMD9iFRm6Nl3x]{Obrisire} revere the Bone Serpent's penchant for measured survival, and their rites and rituals are said to be symbolic recreations of Obrisire's immaculate patterns of logic and reason. Communion with Obrisire is remarkably more esoteric than fellowship with other shard and elder gods of Ember, but the Ancient Beast manages to find ways of communicating with the faithful when they least expect it. Clerics of Obrisire are most common amongst the people of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} Republic and the ancient mystery-laden @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.4RM8MIiCDWMFv2yr]{Sedyri}.

Sockets

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX overview inline]

Order Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} venerate the elder god's stewardship of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} above all else, and their faith is a reflection of the painstaking structure the Soul Cycle must maintain for Ember's cosmos to endure. Because of this rather dogmatic philosophy, Order Clerics of Sockets are often just as rigorous in their practices. These Clerics generally consider themselves to be terrestrial extensions of the elder god's divine will, live their lives accordingly — marked by rote, routine, and tireless dedication to the Soul Cycle itself.

Vekalla

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt overview inline]

Order Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla} strive to embody the immaculate discipline of their goddess via their worship of the living planet's primal weather patterns. As servants of The Whispering Wind, these Life Clerics are as widespread as the winds of Ember themselves; but it's no surprise to find the highest concentration of Vekalla worshippers among seafaring people like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}, or mountainside folk such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} of the Kaustic Hinterlands.

Peace Domain

When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as the source of your character's divine power.

Raineka

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ overview inline]

Peace Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka} are known to be some of Ember's most prestigious healers and diplomats, and revere the Rainbringer herself as one of the most calming and restorative forces in the cosmos. Because of Raineka's relative youth, her worshippers throughout Ember are fewer in number than other gods of The Nineteen; but while the adherents of Raineka may be harder to find, they are certainly easier to befriend, and always eager to broker peace and communion.

Sigil

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE overview inline]

Peace Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE]{Sigil} tend to be learned diplomats and masters of tranquility. Clerics of Sigil who adhere to this domain are not uncommon to the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}, home to Sigil's terrestrial residence known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.sdIjbPRNIsJ3ApcU]{Oldcraft Lodge}. Students of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy} and the Obsidian Antiquaries of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessia} are also known to host several Clerics of Sigil amongst their ranks.

Trickery Domain

When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as the source of your character's divine power.

Aythorn

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.B987VijfeT6i9TEI overview inline]

Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.B987VijfeT6i9TEI]{Aythorn} tend to be Trickery Clerics first and foremost. And while "The Trickster Thorn" isn't the only entity in the cosmos associate with this domain, Aythorn is the only real public-facing deity for Clerics of this ilk in modern day Ember. Aythorn tends to reward those followers who show the most interest and initiative in their efforts, and is eager to foster grand achievements from humble beginnings — as long as a little chicanery is manifested along the way. These days, Aythorn is popular throughout Aterica, but their oldest churches reside in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire (where Aythorn ascended to power).

Twilight Domain

When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as the source of your character's divine power.

Malae

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi overview inline]

Twilight Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae} are somewhat rare among mortal of Ember, as most of her latter-day faithful tend to be monstrous in nature or otherworldly in origin. Nevertheless, the Queen of Curses is known to bless those who worship her with a divine mastery of the dusk. Twilight Clerics of Malae most often dwell on the fringes of society, but enclaves of her worshippers are known to exist where darkness holds sway — like the dreadful expanses of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7zFmCJqtAp32EaI1]{Moiran Bonelands} and the lightless reaches of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles}.

Sionia

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gT5S5ncAEUvkYYYg overview inline]

Twilight Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gT5S5ncAEUvkYYYg]{Sionia} are exceptionally rare throughout Ember, and dedication to her faith comes at the cost of becoming a social pariah amongst most of Aterican society. Nevertheless, the Deathbinder has earned a reputation in recent years for bestowing her faithful Clerics with magnificent powers over light and dark. Just as Sionia dwells between the profound radiance of life and the cloying darkness of death, so do her Clerics become custodians of a liminal reality — where the apparent is obscured and the furtive is made seen.

Thayloc

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f overview inline]

Twilight Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc} are stewards of holy light, locked in a constant conflict with the countless forces of darkness that threaten to extinguish it. Following Thayloc's exodus from the Lumarin Homelands at the hands of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Blood Barons}, The Silver Bowman has become increasingly popular throughout Aterica — with militant temples and churches to be found everywhere from @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain} to @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.HN2Zimps4w5XniZe]{Old Carinth}.

Thoma

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.LNFCxHtijBM7gh76 overview inline]

Twilight Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.LNFCxHtijBM7gh76]{Thoma} are the veritable firesides that the lost and lonely of the world can gather next to when the darkness of the cosmos is too much to bear. These vigilant Clerics can be servants of calm when restlessness strikes, but they're also champions of obscurity when guile is needed most. And thanks to Thoma's own graciousness and personal curiosity, her Twilight Clerics actually end up meeting her in person for tea at one time or another. As the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} of the Kaustic Hinterlands are fond of saying, "There's always time for a visit from Grandmother Comfort."

Volta

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84 overview inline]

Twilight Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta} are often explorers of unseen places and revealers of the unknown. Volta is a well-recognized deity, and is popular among cultures who respect progress, change, and globalism — like the gregariously industrious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}, the sea-faring merchants of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} Republic, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} peoples of the far-off @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy}. And Volta's origins during the Age of Sunlight have contributed to a lasting legacy within @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.oFaQK5PcWivfuOx3]{Nalvani} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.lOu3Wwh34SH6uqV1]{Lorai} societies as well.

War Domain

When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as the source of your character's divine power.

Janar

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb overview inline]

War Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar} view the art of the hunt as a sacred phenomenon, and manage to apply a similar reverence to all life's tasks — viewing each challenge through a lens of "predator versus prey," with the faithful serving as a mortal extension of Janar's primal will. Due to his legendary history stretching back to the Age of Beasts, Janar is worshipped in some fashion among nearly all of Aterica's people; but Janar's War Clerics in particular have historically stood out as noteworthy practitioners of divine magic in times of conflict.

Katu

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4 overview inline]

War Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu} seek to embody the cold temperament of their shard god with their own icy, pragmatic approach to conflict. And Katu's chaotic personality is made manifest by the awesome might that his War Clerics wield in battle, each one of them another stone in the shard god's eternal hail storm. Katu is tremendously popular throughout all of Aterica's seafaring nations, from the peninsulas of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} Republic to the shores of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.u7CDTzcmggsA1wYL]{Oakengarde}.

Lanespear

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6dEDqbOX2xuQLUgZ overview inline]

War Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6dEDqbOX2xuQLUgZ]{Lanespear} tend to strive for perfection in everything they do, and work to embody the shard god's immaculate sense of precision when it comes to matters of discipline and martial combat. Clerics of Lanespear are most popular among the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowlands}, where the chaotic southern reaches of the Duskflare Jungles are overrun with monstrous inhabitants in dire need of law and order.

Lumé

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd overview inline]

War Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé} are regarded as some of her most dedicated and tireless followers, and are heralded for their crucial frontline role in the ongoing war against the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Blood Barons}. The Flame Warden's physical presence in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Homelands ensures her servants feel connected and safeguarded by her holy light. And while Clerics of Lumé can communicate with her from afar, she also welcomes any adherent who would seek her personal counsel.

Thayloc

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f overview inline]

War Clerics of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc} dedicate their lives to the concept of safety through retribution, and are known to be some of the world's most effective slayers of undead creatures. Following Thayloc's exodus from the Lumarin Homelands at the hands of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Blood Barons}, The Silver Bowman has become increasingly popular throughout Aterica — with militant temples and churches to be found everywhere from @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain} to @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.HN2Zimps4w5XniZe]{Old Carinth}.

Other
Cleric.scoverview: Clerics are divine spellcasters whose magic is powered by the Cleric's personal faith in their god, and the deific blessings that god provides in return. Different from normal priests and acolytes, Clerics are adventurers who carry their particular brand of spiritualism throughout the world, spreading the word of their god and proselytizing through their heroic (or villanous) actions.

Druid.name: Druid
Druid.text:
The primal magic of Ember's Druids stems directly from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} itself, and is a manifestation of the living planet's Lifeforce. Each Druid's connection to nature is an extension of this phenomenon, and the various druidic circles of Ember champion their own methods regarding how best to serve the Heart and its cosmic needs. Anyone on Ember can become a Druid if their connection to the world's deific core is strong enough, but some of the most powerful and prolific Druids throughout time have been @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik]{Aster} by birth — a notable coincidence for circles who seek to cultivate a prominent (and powerful) membership.

Beasts of Ember

The world of Ember has a number of novel creatures that occupy its various biomes. Among these, a handful of Beasts exist that are compatible with a Druid's Wild Shape feature. When choosing a Druid's "Known Forms," you may select Beasts from the following list (in addition to any standard options or those provided by the Gamemaster):

  • @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvet}

  • @UUID[Actor.T6YcptpxcCLx4yLx]{Jobri}

  • @UUID[Actor.D0Ws1Flk2fF48bBf]{Rask Juvenile}

Circle of the Land

Circle of the Land Druids throughout Ember are known to hail from a wide variety of peoples and places, but the groups most readily associated with the traditions of this order are perhaps the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.d1bHKAOnvoumeL7p]{Primalists} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ntef4M02D50Y8BlE]{Corebright Forest}. While the Cindaric Sages are not generally considered by to be Druids in the traditional sense, their teachings and tenets run unmistakably parallel to the primal spellcasting paradigms of other Circle of the Land Druids throughout Ember. Furthermore, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders} of the Corebright Forest are known for the Primalists who hold important stations within their woodland society; and these life-affirming druids are acknowledged far and wide for their innate spellcasting talents.

Circle of the Moon

Circle of the Moon Druids have learned to harness the power of Ember's six moons to fuel their magical transformations and spells. This relationship with the lunar bodies of the cosmos enhances a Moon Druid's shapechanging abilities beyond their normal ken, and contributes to their comparatively untamed dispositions. The Circle of the Moon has countless orders throughout Ember of various shapes and sizes, which are prone to as much change and migration as the lunar bodies they revere. One of the more prominent associations of Circle of the Moon Druids stems from the shapechanging @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.d1bHKAOnvoumeL7p]{Primalist} traditions of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders}. Indeed, a new sect has arisen among the Druids of the Corebright Forest; referred to as the Moonstruck, these particular Circle of the Moon adherents are known for their reclusive lifestyles and their proclivity for spending a great deal of time in their wild shape forms.

Additional Beasts of Ember

When choosing a Circle of the Moon Druid's "Circle Forms," you may select Beasts from the following list (in addition to those detailed in "Beasts of Ember" above, any standard options, or those provided by the Gamemaster), per the level-appropriate Challenge Rating:

  • @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV]{Child of Sitheera}

  • @UUID[Actor.EXu53Ax88rWm8YOM]{Grey Hydroxol}

  • @UUID[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl]{Gumtoad}

  • @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk]{Hydroxol}

  • @UUID[Actor.McN3C0nRW9WdLfQa]{Kadhana Lizard}

  • @UUID[Actor.jXhgSnAtBX8gHBah]{Kezus Jelly}

  • @UUID[Actor.QGpM0XLtyG7zN76l]{Rask}

  • @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]{Scalemaw}

  • @UUID[Actor.7LUoANZTizlXTCB2]{Yarnac Juvenile}

Circle of the Sea

Druids who join the Circle of the Sea draw their power from the ceaseless ebb and flow of Ember's tides — from the calm of the gentle lakes and streams, to the ferocious energy of the deepest ocean currents. These rare, but often powerful, individuals are known to tap into the primal power of Ember's storms. Some become particularly adept with seafaring and maritime activities, like guiding ships through dangerous seas or serving as stalwart protectors of Ember's aquatic wildlife. One notable sect of Circle of the Sea Druids is the infamous "Special Forces" of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} Republic, who are widely recognized as masters of the oceans (despite their relative secrecy).

Circle of Spores

Druids who become one with the Circle of Spores venerate rot and decay, and their primal magic is powered by the cosmic energies associated with entropy, change, and decomposition. Since death plays such a large part of the natural order of the cosmos (including Ember's mysterious Soul Cycle), Circle of Spores Druids are intimately familiar with the metaphysical potential that lingers in mortal forms, and the capacity for putrefaction to create new life and new forms of energy. Various orders dedicated to the Circle of Spores can be found throughout Ember — including the reclusive Grimbriar sect of the treebound @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders}, the intrepid Rotfinders of the undead @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} legions, and the resourceful Mycons of the subterranean @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}.

Circle of the Stars

Ember's modern Circle of the Stars originates within the foothills and peaks of the Kaustic Hinterlands, where the ancestors of the world's oldest cultures of star-worshippers still endure today. While some of the traditions associated with Circle of the Stars Druids were founded by the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} Giants, most latter-day folks associate this sect of seers and dreamers with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil}, who often pair their devotion to the night and stars with heady worship of the Elder Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{Ven'avé}. Beyond the reclusive Druids that inhabit this area east of the Shana Mountains, Ember's Circle of the Stars has also found purchase in lands far afield of the order's origins — with sects operating out of places like the lofty canopies of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles} and the wide-open spaces of the Awakened Savanna.

Circle of Wildfire

Circle of Wildfire Druids are somewhat rare throughout Ember, and are most commonly found among a fervent sect moon-worshipping @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} known as the Ustrinas. These Druids ultimately seek to restore life to the ravaged fire moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}, and their assorted rituals and prophecies revolve around the advent of this most cosmic of conflagrations. Other Circle of Wildfire sects can be found scattered across the world in likely (and unlikely) places, including the Firewardens of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Hearthguard of the Lumarin Homelands, and the Sun-seers of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia}.
Druid.scoverview: Druids are primal spellcasters and shapechangers who belong to ancient, primeval orders that revere — and protect — various aspects of nature and its beasts. Each Druid is part of an association that caters to one of these aspects, which are known as circles. A Druid's circle informs which particular facet of the natural world they're cosmically in tune with the most, as well as the general kind of spellcaster they'll become (or more precisely, which bonus spells they'll have access to throughout their career).

Fighter.name: Fighter
Fighter.text:
Warriors from nearly every walk of life on Ember have the potential to become a Fighter, which is arguably the world's most ubiquitous character class. Throughout the eons of the living planet's evolution, the various peoples of Ember have taken arms against some would-be foe at one time or another. And whether a Fighter is part of a traditional faction's teachings — like those of the undead slayers of the Lumarin Homelands or the salaried soldiers of the Tayan Empire — or merely a warrior of their own device, these paragons of martial combat are capable of wielding almost any weapon known to humanoid kind.

Battle Master

Ember's Battle Masters are called such with good reason. Through rigorous study and application of Ember's numerous combat traditions — often using techniques that stretch back to the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} masters of eons past — Battle Masters have become supremely proficient at the art of war. This warfare acumen allows these martial strategists to control the field of battle with a deftness and precision unheard of, enabling them to outmaneuver foes with powerful demonstrations of their vast combat knowledge. Battle Masters are known to take leadership positions in all manner of armies and war parties throughout Ember — from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} tacticians of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowland} Bastions, to captains of armed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} vessels. And, in addition to their inherent value to military groups the world over, Battle Masters are celebrated throughout the Arctus Plateau for their ability to keep organized groups of ruffians and monsters at bay where it matters most.

Champion

Champions in Ember constitute a broad category of individuals that can be found in every culture throughout the cosmos. These deadly warriors seek victory above all else, and this pursuit of triumph is what drives their potent combat mastery. Champions typically possess a single-minded focus for martial perfection, which supersedes any other concerns. Naturally, this means they tend to act individually rather than working in teams, and are celebrated for their lethal effectiveness in duels and other one-on-one encounters. Thanks to their daring deeds, many Champions of Ember eventually rise to prominent positions of power, fame, and influence — and their accomplishments become the stuff of legend, writ in stories and song to inspire the people of Ember for generations to come.

Eldritch Knight

The term "Eldritch Knight" does not exist in Ember. However, the concept of traditional Eldritch Knight Fighters persists via the alternatives listed below (among others).

Arcane Knights of Ember balance their combat prowess with the traditional study of arcane magic, resulting in a powerful combination of martial skill and spellcasting abilities. Arcane Knights learn from the same repository of magical knowledge as Wizards, and devise their spell lists accordingly — often with an emphasis on spells that will complement their combat expertise. Arcane Knights are not a specific order, nor do they belong to a specific organization. Instead, these magic-wielding Fighters tend to appear among many cultures throughout the world (even ever-so-rarely among those places where magic itself might be shunned).

Chosen of Spectra are a variant of Arcane Knight, similar in almost every respect. More specifically, these magical Fighters worship and revere the Elder Goddess Spectra, and gain their magical insight from her divine mysteries. Chosen of Spectra are often confused with clerics or priests, and this error is an understandable one, since the Chosen of Spectra are known to proselytize the word of the Elder Goddess far and wide. These specialists are far less common than standard Arcane Knights, and tend to only arise after a chance meeting with the goddess herself.

Purple Dragon Knight

The term "Purple Dragon Knight" does not exist in Ember. However, the concept of traditional Purple Dragon Knight Fighters persists via the alternative listed below (among others).

Dragon Companion

A Purple Dragon Knight's Purple Dragon Companion is referred to as a "Tayan Wyvern" for the purposes of a Kirargy Knight character.

The Kirargy Knights of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire is a stalwart force of formidable warriors known for their unrivaled devotion to the Dragon Empress herself, who bestows a select few with impressive Wyvern mounts, which they raise from hatchlings to "adulthood" — becoming large enough for the Kirargy Knights to ride them into battle. In exchange for this gift and other magical boons, most Knights enforce the Empire's strict justice via service in its vast and powerful military. Occasionally, errant Kirargy Knights are sent on missions far afield from the Tayan Empire, with orders that service the intricate gamut of the Dragon Empress' machinations; often, this means protection for the Empire's allies — or envoys to its enemies.

Psi Warrior

Psi Warriors of Ember harness the metaphysical power of their minds to enhance their fighting prowess and push their physical might to its very limits. And while the modern practice of this sophisticated combat tradition can be found throughout Ember, the first Psi Warriors are said to have originated within the ranks of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire — where a cunning Maejis set out to "improve" the Empire's warriors by gifting them with an enhanced mental aptitude and the ability to change reality itself with their very minds. This cruel experimentation resulted in an entire generation of Psi Warriors, trained from birth and conscripted into the Empire's Hosts once they reached adolescence. Many modern Psi Warriors are the descendants of these ancient Fighters. However, the defunct Aedir Empire is not the only source of Psi Warriors on Ember; thanks to the living planet's inscrutable magic, Psi Warriors (as rare as they may be) come from all walks of life, and often hail from Signaran or Aster lineages.

Rune Knight

Rune Knights of Ember have incorporated the runes of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} Giants into their fighting styles. Because the genesis of these magic-laden symbols originates in a time long gone, the source of a Rune Knight's runic mastery is a source of particular interest; perhaps the Fighter found an ancient weapon or piece of armor inscribed with the runes, or maybe they stumbled onto a stone tablet or menhir etched with ancient Shent text. Whatever the source of this knowledge, Rune Knights have learned to carve magic runes to enhance their own gear and abilities — a practice they're keen to use as often as their experience allows.

Bonus Proficiencies

3rd-level Rune Knights of Ember gain proficiency with smith’s tools, and learn to speak, read, and write Pathward (rather than Giant).

Rune names and the associated lore text for their meanings have been slightly reworked for Ember to align them with the cultural tenets and writing of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} Giants. They function the same as traditional Rune Fighter runes.

Eclipse

(Cloud)

This rune depicts the shadow of one of Ember's moons as it obscures another.

Mastery

(Fire)

This rune focuses one's understanding of materials and elements, granting overwhelming skill and knowledge.

Mind

(Frost)

This rune redirects a person's own inner strength and mental fortitude.

Solar

(Stone)

This rune channels Lantyr's radiant energy; it disrupts and pierces darkness and shadow.

Dream

(Hill)

This rune evokes magical tranquility, resilience, and legacy, bestowing the ability to resist disruptive forces.

Star

(Storm)

This rune channels the magic of stars directly from the Sea of Stars and the Weave. It is one of the most important Shent runes, which they used to perceive magical auras and the future itself.
Fighter.scoverview: Whether their talents stem from might or agility, Fighters are warriors of Ember that are known for their exceptional skill in the ways of combat. Athleticism, nimbleness, bravado — these qualities and more are among the key traits exhibited by Ember's wide array of accomplished slayers, who train their entire lives to further develop their innate proclivity for physical conflict.

Monk.name: Monk
Monk.text:
Whether they understand the specific wellspring of their abilities or not, Monks of Ember are powered by the cosmic energy of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0DQdqtsLn3M1ZZA2#fundamental-forces]{Lifeforce}, which manifests itself in many ways to these elite warriors of mind and body. And while they may or may not venerate the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} that provides this metaphyiscal power, each Monk on the living planet benefits from its inscrutable glory. Monk subclasses of Ember represent various cultural and historical traditions that have shaped the way their associated warriors interact with the world, and affect how a Monk's spiritual Focus is able to help them reshape reality itself.

Warrior of the Astral Self

Warriors of the Astral Self on Ember believe that their body is an apparition, a spiritual tether to the Heart of Ember that persists as an illusory manifestation of their soul's ideal physical form. Most of the Astral Self Monks that walk the earth of Ember are ascetics who consider the pollution of their terrestrial apparition to be a threat to their entire sense of self; and many of the warriors who study this tradition's teachings end up living solitary lifestyles marked by reclusiveness or disarrangement. One of Ember's most prominent monastic schools for Astral Self Monks is the Arcageris — a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} temple in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowland Bastions}, whose "arcing" Monks adventure to places of power throughout the world in search of metaphysical wellsprings that will help them Focus their concept of the great "Cosmic Force."

Warrior of the Elements

Warrior of the Elements Monks channel their Focus via the metaphysical wellsprings of Ember's six moons, and are capable of tapping into the magic of each of these lunar bodies to enhance their fighting. Some warriors who study this monastic tradition have a patron moon they tend to favor in their techniques, while others embrace a holistic view of all six moons and their relationship to the cosmos. The earliest monasteries dedicated to the Elements can be traced back to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.u7CDTzcmggsA1wYL]{Oakengarde}, who have subsequently established temples and schools throughout Aterica that cater to would-be adherents of their time-honored ways.

Warrior of the Open Hand

There are no finer masters of unarmed fighting than Ember's Warriors of the Open Hand, whose nimble melee combat techniques can be as graceful as they are deadly. Open Hand Monks are known throughout the world, but their monasteries are exceptionally few. The most venerated institution of this monastic tradition is Swiftwind Temple, located in the foothills of the Runa Highlands, where an ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.K28cb1q6tvU8FP8B]{Hulg'run} master named Kyan the Swift-fist still teaches the Open Hand techniques he began developing during the time of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}. Furthermore, a handful of master Kyan's students have set off into the world and formed monasteries of their own, where new hopefuls can learn the ways of the ancient unarmed experts.

Warrior of Mercy

Warriors of Mercy are capable of using their spiritual Focus to manipulate the ebb and flow of Ember's metaphysical Lifeforce, enabling them to both heal and harm others. It comes as little surprise to learn that this monastic tradition therefore originates from one of the lunar bodies that orbit Ember rather than from its terrestrial earth. Indeed, the first Warrior of Mercy monks were a group of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.eyvVaX4c1rMos0ws]{Zeph} siblings named the Sisu Sisters, who founded a legendary martial arts school on the hollow surface of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura}, the Air Moon. In the centuries since the Sisu School's inception, the teachings of this monastic tradition have made their way to various temples and schools on the surface of Ember, where they persist to this day. And even when they aren't of Zeph ancestry, modern Mercy Monks wear ceremonial masks to honor their lunar forerunners.

Warrior of Shadow

Warriors of Shadow are Ember's most disparate group of Monks, capable of channeling the tenebrous essence of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} through their spiritual Focus. These clandestine warriors don't often belong to a public-facing tradition or organization, preferring to navigate the world via their own subtle, unseen methods — engaging in activities reserved for the furtive and the obscure. Shadow Monks often study under the secret tutelage of a powerful master, who learned the ways of Shadow from another master before them. This cycle continues in modern day Ember, with networks of Shadow Monks scattered across the face of Aterica and beyond.
Monk.scoverview: Monks are spiritual warriors who balance their combat training with a discipline of the mind so powerful, it allows them to channel inner metaphysical energies to augment their physical prowess. Monks achieve this cosmic harmony via a number of methods and monastic traditions, most often taught to them by masters of the craft who preceded them. Authorities in the use of light weapons, Monks are known to be as deadly as they are deft in the ways of form and movement, and tend to be driven by goals connected to a greater purpose than themselves.

Paladin.name: Paladin
Paladin.text:
Ember's Paladins receive their divine power from one or more of the world's Elder Gods or Shard Gods, who grant the holy warriors various deific boons based on their respective domains of influence. Anyone on Ember can become a Paladin, if their faith and desire are strong enough. In fact, some Paladins take up oaths that defy categorization or fealty to a god, and are instead driven by some inner conviction that perhaps only the Paladin themself might understand.

Oath of the Ancients

Paladins who take the Oath of the Ancients are rare individuals of Ember who have have a holy connection to one of the ageless @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}. Among the oldest entities in creation, the enigmatic Casia bestow their mortal champions with the primordial magic of their native Inner Realm; and these boons allow Oath of the Ancients Paladins to channel the arcane essence of Primordis itself, to protect both themselves and those around them. Precisely how this bond between Paladin and Casia is formed is often a source of mystery itself, although various sects of Oath of the Ancients Paladins are known to reside within the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowland Bastions} of the Waerd — where the holy warriors of Primordis can subtly influence terrestrial events relatively unnoticed.

Associated Deities: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2FA1FO5P0G83sjt9]{Nimaelle}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.vKU4RfzoCeBJ9sNB]{The Silent Pack}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.RPVn1KLLcutCzYcv]{Vesper}

Oath of Devotion

As stewards of justice and order, Oath of Devotion Paladins tend to serve gods and organizations of Ember who embody the same heroic ideals. More often than not, these virtuous holy warriors serve at the behest of one of the world's more noble and benevolent @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000]{Deities}, such as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}, or the elder god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} (among others). Oath of Devotion Paladins also tend to find themselves allied with organizations whose tenets and goals are aligned with Ember's nobler pursuits — like the heroic protectors of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} who serve the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, or the holy @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} warriors of the Lumarin Flameguard.

Associated Deities: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.LNFCxHtijBM7gh76]{Thoma}

Oath of Glory

The call of destiny is incessantly strong for Paladins who take the Oath of Glory, and this type of headstrong, star-crossed warrior has existed on the face of Ember since time immemorial. Nearly anyone who can wield a sword has the potential to take up an Oath of Glory and become one of these stalwart holy warriors, but the most storied among them are blessed by the gods or Ember itself with qualities that serve their cause — like preternatural strength, raw charisma, and unerring courage. In one way or another, most (if not all) of Ember's shard gods, elder gods, and god-like beings seek out champions to serve as conduits for their own deific prestige; Oath of Glory Paladins are the heroes and antiheroes that answer this call, and can hail from any walk of life. Paladins such as these can also often be found among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd}, who prize the undertaking of glorious deeds, to be celebrated in legends for ages untold.

Associated Deities: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6dEDqbOX2xuQLUgZ]{Lanespear}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.cVcA9liudzvcYgZc]{Lorex}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rmMWMD9iFRm6Nl3x]{Obrisire}

Oath of the Noble Genies

The term "Genie" does not exist in Ember. However, the concept of traditional Oath of the Noble Genies Paladins persists via Ember's "Oath of the Elemental Moons."

Paladins who take up the Oath of the Elemental Moons in Ember have sworn allegiance to the cosmos itself, and place their fealty in the metaphysical arms of the planet's quartet of elemental moons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}. The four abilities of the Elemental Smite trait learned by these Paladins at Level 3 have been renamed as following: Crush of Cora, Escape of Aura, Fury of Ragen, and Surge of Mayis. Meanwhile, the "Lunar Spells" and "Lunar Splendor" also granted at Level 3 behave as originally intended, with no changes to the spell list, etc. Elemental Moon paladins hail from all corners of Ember, but are most commonly encountered throughout the lands of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Z8Nm4rnjqG3BJHSd]{Varún}.

Oath of Vengeance

Righteous punishers driven by the desire for retribution, Paladins who take the Oath of Vengeance embody their sworn vendetta through their everyday actions and the grander paths they walk in life. A Paladin's vengeance can take a wide variety of forms throughout Ember — from a sworn dedication to right some cosmic wrong, to something as relatively simple as an innate need for personal retribution. As a result, Oath of Vengeance Paladins can be as loyal to a metaphysical cause or concept as they are to a specific deity and their tenets. The temples of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc}, however, are noteworthy for their high concentration of Paladins who swear by this Oath, and bastions dedicated to this loose affiliation of Vengeance warriors can be found throughout Aterica.

Associated Deities: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.DskILHKPngH3FVa7]{Nite}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc}

Oath of the Watchers

Paladins who swear by the Oath of the Watchers dedicate their lives to protecting Ember from the persistent and malevolent encroachment of otherworldly influences — whether that extraterrestrial power stems from the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyss}, or the curious depths of the Inner Realms (@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}). Most of the Paladins who swear by this oath protect Ember's mortal realms from the loathsome, unknowable chaos of the Abyss, and the horrors that lurk beyond the Weave (like the Paladins of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Flameguard. Some, however, oppose the influence of the Inner Realms, and stand proud against the celestials of Luxarum, the fiends of Signara, or the fey of Primordis. Whatever motivates these hostilities, Watcher Paladins are sure to extend their divine aid to others in times of need.
Paladin.scoverview: Holy warriors bound by sacred oaths, Paladins are empowered with divine magic to carry out the will of their patron deity, and tend to do so with unmatched conviction and loyalty to their cause. Less versatile than Fighters and not as spell-oriented as Clerics, Paladins exist as something of a fusion of these two roles — able to command the battlefield with purpose, driven by divine resolve.

Ranger.name: Ranger
Ranger.text:
The world of Ember is a primal place, full of constant change and unknowable dangers. One of the most capable self-defense mechanisms the living planet has at its disposal are the disparate heroes known as Rangers, who appear like diamonds in the rough — and emerge as some of the world's most noble and selfless protectors. Whatever calls a Ranger to duty, they persist as some of the realm's most prized slayers of monsters and tyrants.

Beast Master

Rangers of this type specialize in a deep and lasting bond with a Primal Companion, a magical beast that appears as a physical manifestation of a legendary animal from a bygone age of the living planet. Many of Ember's Rangers strive to become Beast Masters, and these beast-bonded warriors can be found among nearly all of Ember's societies — from the agrarian @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturians} of the eponymous Plateau, to the imperialist @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayans} of western Canasia. Most notably, symbiotic enclaves of Beast Master Rangers and their allies can be found frequently among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak} peoples northeast of Aterica, where a demanding nomadic lifestyle benefits from the perpetual comforts and security of primal companionship.

Fey Wanderer

The term "Feywild" does not exist in Ember. However, certain concepts of the Feywild persist via the Inner Realm known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} — also known as the Realm of Capricious Magic, or the Shadowlands.

For one reason or another, these enigmatic Rangers possess a strong connection to the arcane wilds of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, where the shadowy glamour of fey magic is most potent. Fey Wanderers can find their way to this subclass through any number of methods — be it a lineage that stems from The First Forest, a fateful encounter with a powerful fey artifact, or via the whims of an ambitious or influential @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia}. Like most Rangers, Fey Wanderers tend to be outcasts, but their capacity for illusion magic often makes up for their societal shortcomings. And these masters of glamourous subterfuge are capable of utilizing their Fey Wanderer Spells and "Primordial Gifts" to astonishing effect.

Gloom Stalker

The term "Shadowfell" does not exist in Ember. However, certain concepts of the Shadowfell persist via the Inner Realm known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} — also known as the Realm of Ferocious Curiosity, or The Endless Dark.

Gloom Stalkers of Ember are more commonly known as the "Somber Guard," and draw upon the ethereal, otherworldly magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} to fell their enemies and traverse the tenebrous wilds of the living planet. Whether a Ranger has encountered a technological wonder of The Endless Dark, has reasoned with a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos}, or is the product of a fiendish lineage, something mysterious has drawn them to the natural and supernatural darkness of the cosmos. Members of the Somber Guard tend to be at home among the darker recesses of Ember, such as the subterranean @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} and the lightless canopies of places like the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles} or the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7zFmCJqtAp32EaI1]{Moiran Bonelands}.

Hunter

Hunters are perhaps the most common type of Ranger to be found on Ember, but their combat and survival acumen remain unmatched — particularly when set against a foe that's been marked by their supernatural tracking skills. According to legends passed down throughout the ages, the esoteric techniques of Ember's Hunters originated long ago among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles}, who've had to maintain a stalwart vigil against the ceaseless assault of monstrous creatures and preternatural villains for centuries. These days, Rangers who excel in battlefield tactics and the lore of the wilderness make the strongest candidates for effective Hunters of the living planet.

Swarmkeeper

The swarm of nature spirits that empower these esoteric Rangers stem from a deep and plentiful connection to the Heart of Ember itself, which is connected to all things that inhabit the metaphysical ecosystem of the living planet. Swarmkeeper Rangers can hail from any walk of life, but the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries} of the Arcturian @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.TNPxd8ZlYQvJEXu6]{Bloodwoods} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ntef4M02D50Y8BlE]{Corebright Forest} tend to actively cultivate these skilled weavers of spiritual current. When it comes to the physical manifestation a Swarmkeeper's swarm takes when it appears, it's not uncommon for the Swarming Insects common to Rangers of this type to resemble Ember's benevolent Pyreflies — which are coincidentally revered by the druidic @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} and Sanguinaries in many of their rituals.

Winter Walker

Winter Walkers are Rangers who excel in the frigid, unforgiving temperatures of Ember's coldest biomes — such as the hoary expanse of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.636CDJ8h9RNVKLCj]{Desolation of Vaznor}, the glittering domains of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} southwest of Kessia, the jagged peaks of the Spine of Ember, or even the haunted unknown wilderness of far-off @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.SVA2mEPwehsfWViM]{Jekaros}. Notably, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.TUt9EUMWp8pV1wXe]{Fikost} people of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UeziKENAQNnY5lYj]{Rimedrift} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.xImbz6Nf4mMxtKF1]{Wardcall} people of the Wintec, Katic, and Pertta kingdoms are known to venerate Winter Walkers among their ranks. Winter Walkers of Ember are also known to be familiar with the strange arcana related to these glacial areas as well, like the powerful Wardscale armor of the Wardcall and the portal technology of the Rhivan @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages}.
Ranger.scoverview: Rangers are the tireless guardians of Ember's wilds. These watchful warriors often live far from bustling cities, where they form close connections to the natural world and the animals around them. Almost all Rangers on Ember are dedicated enemies of the world's monsters, which they help quell using their innate proclivities for hunting and tracking. A combination of physical prowess and primal magic are the tools of a Ranger's trade, and their affinity with nature is only rivaled by the most powerful druids.

Rogue.name: Rogue
Rogue.text:
Rogues of Ember are a resourceful lot, marked by disparate backgrounds but united by one great fascination: opportunity. Rogues rely on their wide array of skills to fulfill their often equally varied goals. Stealth and chicanery are often employed by any given Rogue in pursuit of their own personal agenda, but they also tend to offer their expertise to larger groups (where profit or favor can be found in steady measure). Anyone in Ember can become a Rogue, and nearly every town in Aterica has at least one of these adaptable scoundrels in their midsts.

Arcane Trickster

Arcane Tricksters supplement their abilities of stealth and subterfuge with spells and other magical enhancements, and are known to exist among almost every civilization on Ember. Organizations like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} thieves' guilds of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.HN2Zimps4w5XniZe]{Old Carinth} are known to employ Arcane Tricksters within their ranks, who serve these groups as frontline explorers and deft invaders of enchanted places. Throughout the Arctus Plateau, a great deal of these sorcerous Rogues are also followers of the shard god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.B987VijfeT6i9TEI]{Aythorn}, a wily deity of mischief and trickery.

Assassin

The deadly Rogues known as Assassins are formidable killers, masters of surprise whose trade is murder. Rogues of this type are known to occupy most civilized places of Aterica, where they go relatively unseen and unheard by the masses. Assassins are most common, however, within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} City States — where the most dangerous Rogues in the world can be found (if you know who to ask). Assassins are also skilled in the ways of poison, and utilize it with deadly effect; it's no wonder, then, that these murderous Rogues are sometimes hired by villains of Ember's high society who wish to keep a low profile themselves.

Phantom

A Phantom Rogue's mystical connection with death gives them preternatural insight into Ember's Soul Cycle, a knowledge they use to stunning effect both offensively and defensively throughout the course of adventuring. Rogues of this type are exceedingly rare, and can learn the supernatural tools of their trade through a variety of ways. The most common touchpoint for these macabre Rogues is their introduction to one of countless secret organizations that serve @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, the Elder God of Death — helping to manifest his divine balance of life and death (whether they know it or not).

Phantoms of Ember can roll on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} Table to determine their various Tokens of the Departed at Level 9.

Scion of the Three

The trio of evil gods known as the "Dead Three" do not exist in Ember. However, the concept of the Scion of the Three subclass persists via a select triumvirate of Ember's god-like beings: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.sZ7WbCZE3811qQrD]{Menis Valegar}, the Lord of Torment; @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HAAY0z8U2EIWOjCr]{Sitheera}, The Spider Goddess; and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.kuzrxa7DiSrhMtq9]{Xalarax}, Omen of the Evernight.

The occult gifts of this macabre Rogue subclass come from a trio of malevolent God-Like Beings. Many Scions don't know much at all about the specific deities who power their macabre boons, but these unholy Rogues pay their fealty in illicit deeds nevertheless, learning what they can as long as their luck holds out. Furthermore, the triumvirate of deities who comprise a Scion's eponymous "Three" have little in common other than their inscrutable otherworldly nature — the aims and methods of Ember's gods are each their own.

At Level 3, Scions of the Three in Ember choose one of the following for their Dread Allegiance: Menis Valegar, Sitheera, or Xalarax. The corresponding Damage Resistances and Cantrips gained by this feature are detailed below.

Deity

Menis Valegar

Soulknife

These rare and peculiar Rogues are capable of using psionic mind power to bolster their attacks and enhance their slyness. The origins of a Soulknife's psionic powers can be varied and mysterious; but whatever the source of this power, it is usually esoteric or uncanny in nature. Soulknife Rogues are extremely rare throughout Ember, and tend to be servants of one of the fiendish @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} — who "bless" these mindful Rogues with supernatural alien psionics to serve their inscrutable ambitions. Soulknife Rogues have also surfaced from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} Republic, where their anti-magic philosophies have cultivated new ways of wielding the metaphysical energies of the cosmos.

Thief

Thieves are the most ubiquitous type of Rogue to be found on Ember. Wherever there are valuables worth stealing, purses worth cutting, or traps worth springing, a Thief can be found nearby. These ambitious Rogues are relatively common in bustling settlements of industry like @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel} — and are actually quite prevalent areas such as the dangerous @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} slums of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7iZDVtrBO7326XZY]{Caren’ac}, or the lawless reaches of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kalmezian} City States. As members of the @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.nightwatch000000]{Nightwatch} are fond of saying, "all the thieves in Old Carinth couldn't make it happen" and nothing's "fleeter than a Kelmezian thief."
Rogue.scoverview: Armed with deception, wit, and lethal precision, Rogues are adventurers who rely on their cunning and stealth to exploit an enemy's weaknesses. These scoundrels are extraordinarily skillful, and are capable of more nimble approaches to combat than other classes — succeeding most when they strike from places unseen, clad in light armor, and equipped with swift weaponry. Masters of subterfuge and versatility, Rogues form the backbone of any party who aims excel at the arts of trap-springing and trickery.

Sorcerer.name: Sorcerer
Sorcerer.text:
Sorcerers have a welcome place in Ember, where the entire cosmos is suffused with the eternal magic of the living planet's preternatural @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart}. These instinctual magic users are more common on Ember than one might think, and Sorcerers tend to occupy notable roles in all levels of society. Whether a Sorcerer's power stems from their unique heritage, a metaphysical connection to some part of the cosmos, or a supernatural boon from a powerful being, their innate font of magic and penchant for metamagic adaptability are prized traits the world over.

Familiars of Ember

The world of Ember has a number of novel creatures that occupy its various biomes. Among these, a handful of animals exist that are compatible with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplFindFamili]{Find Familiar} spell. When choosing the spell's "animal forms," you may select one of the CR 0 animals from the following list (in addition to those listed in the spell's description):

  • @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvet}

  • @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Bird}

  • @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozeling}

  • @UUID[Actor.5f6yFaP9gpprOu0w]{Trickadee}

Aberrant

Reviled Sorcery

Aberrant Sorcerers gain their arcane power from the eldritch magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss}. First and foremost, familiarize yourself with the concept of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.0RXUc08I2fOUESTL#reviled-magic]{Reviled Magic} in Ember, and discuss your character concept and background with the Gamemaster. The Reviled Magic of an Aberrant Sorcerer will have dramatic effects on gameplay, which should be considered before creating such a character.

While all Aberrant Sorcerers aren't inherently evil, the Abyssal magic that they wield is reviled among most people of Ember (much like the Wizard's arcane tradition of Necromancy). As a result, life in normal society is difficult for an Aberrant Sorcerer, no matter their origins or motivations. Ultimately, many Sorcerers who dabble in Aberrant magic throughout Ember are evil in nature, thanks to the malevolent and chaotic influence of the Abyss — but there are exceptions to this paradigm. Some Aberrant Sorcerers spend their entire lives attempting to outrun the otherworldly weight of their Abyssal origins (to varying degrees of success). An Aberrant Sorcerer's origin could stem from any number of sources, such as a fateful encounter with an Abyssal artifact, or ancestry marked with alien corruption.

Clockwork

The terms "Mechanus" and "Modron" do not exist in Ember. However, certain concepts of Mechanus persist via the lunar body known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, the Shattered Moon.

Naturally, a curious relationship persists between Ember's Clockwork Sorcerers and those whose origins are more Draconic in nature, since Akon is the true birthplace of Ember's Dragons as well as the preternatural Wyrms of old.

Clockwork Sorcerers of Ember channel their arcane magic through the cosmological influence of Akon, the Shattered Moon — where countless constructs toil in unknown servitude to long-dead masters, and the concept of Order reigns supreme. Manifestations of Clockwork Sorcery on Ember appear as one of Akon's various constructs or mechanical creations, and can be as esoteric as the Shattered Planet itself. A Sorcerer's Clockwork origin could hail from any number of sources, such as the influence of a lunar monolith, exposure to a powerful mechanical artifact, or ancestral ties to Akon's long-forgotten @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.CNUDzx1WE09XXJZ8]{Wyrms}. And whatever that source might be, the cosmic force of order that was once maintained by Akon lives on via the arcane methods of these custodians of law and balance.

Draconic

Sorcerers with Draconic origins possess strange arcane powers that emulate those of Ember's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons}. A Draconic origin comes with its fair share of stigma, given the troubled history of these wyrm-like creatures in the cosmos — including their problematic beginnings and enduring legacy of malevolence. However, not all Dragons in the annals of the cosmos have been evil creatures, and even those who do bear the ancestral legacy of Ember's malignant Dragons can often shirk the mantle of their progenitors. Thus, Draconic Sorcerers of Ember tend to be as unique and peculiar as the legendary creatures of their namesake. The fateful path that leads to a Sorcerer's Draconic origin can be one of many potentialities: perhaps your ancestors were experimented upon by a Vile Dragon, or maybe you were born within the accursed aura of a Cruel Dragon's remote lair. The possibilities, like a Dragon's wrath, are endless. And of all societies on Ember, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} people of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy} tend to find a home for these wayward Sorcerers, whose primeval Draconic magic is always welcome among the world's most elite arcanists.

Associated Deities: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}

Spellfire

The term "Spellfire" does not exist in Ember. However, the concept of Spellfire persists via the metaphysical arcane phenomenon known as "Heartfire," which is derived from the preternatural @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}.

Those who wield the rare phenomenon known as "Heartfire" throughout Ember harness the raw magic potential of the Heart of Ember to cast their spells. Unlike most arcane spellcasters, Heartfire Sorcerers are able to heal others with their magic — and they can innately counter and absorb spells, feeding their own pool of Sorcery Points in the process. Heartfire Sorcerers tend to feel at home anywhere the strands of fate can carry them, since they're directly connected to the living planet itself via the central force of the cosmos. Many of Ember's militaristic societies (like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.nightwatch000000]{Nightwatch} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Flameguard of Hearth) prize Heartfire Sorcerers as potent battle mages who can bolster the front lines without the need for divine aid. Heartfire Sorcerers are also known to dwell among the benevolent @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}, as well as the enigmatic @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries} of the famed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.TNPxd8ZlYQvJEXu6]{Bloodwoods}, and the noble @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ntef4M02D50Y8BlE]{Corebright Forest}.

Associated Deities: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.DskILHKPngH3FVa7]{Nite}

Wild Magic

Wild Magic Sorcerers cast their arcane spells by tapping into the cosmological influence of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis}, the Spirit Moon — the most singular and influential force of Chaos in the cosmos. Wild Magic Sorcerers are viewed with suspicion and distrust by many of Ember's societies, if only for the unpredictable destruction and calamity they can cause in their wake. However, among the moon-worshipping peoples of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Z8Nm4rnjqG3BJHSd]{Varún}, they are often welcomed as earthly avatars of The Spirit Moon's mercurial will. Wild Magic Sorcerers are also known to emerge from places where the veil of reality has been torn asunder by @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering} — like the fragmented ruins of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.XXMizY6WTIsL0swx]{The Broken Tower} scattered throughout the known world.

Associated Deities: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.DskILHKPngH3FVa7]{Nite}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}

Wild Magic Surge

Some results of a Wild Magic Sorcerer's Wild Magic Surge require slight adjustment to fit the Ember cosmos. Replace the appropriate text of the original Wild Magic Surge table with the following:

05–08

Roll [[/roll 1d4]] to determine the creature: on a 1, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmSprite00000000]{Sprite} of Primordis appears; on a 2, a fiendish @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmFlyingSnake000]{Flying Snake} of Signara appears; on a 3, a fey @UUID[Actor.D0Ws1Flk2fF48bBf]{Rask Juvenile} appears; on a 4, a fey @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmUnicorn0000000]{Unicorn} appears.

25–28

Instead of the Astral Plane, the Wild Magic Sorcerer is transported to a realm of Orbis until the end of their next turn.
Sorcerer.scoverview: Sorcerers are arcane spellcasters who can innately call forth the power of their magic from their very being. They need not study a grimoire like wizards, nor make a pact with an otherworldly being like warlocks; a Sorcerer's origin drives their arcane abilities. Whatever the source of that sorcerous potential might be, these magic users tend to be more versatile than other arcane casters, and serve as terrific candidates for multiclassing as a result.

Warlock.name: Warlock
Warlock.text:
Warlocks in Ember are those who have communed with powerful entities and have been granted incredible power but at a great cost. Warlocks can form pacts with any number of entities in Ember even the Gods themselves but there are several "others' who will gladly treat with mortals upon the surface world.

The following entries on Warlock Subclasses feature suggestions for which @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000]{Deities} might be the most suitable to engage with as patrons in the Ember setting.

Familiars of Ember

The world of Ember has a number of novel creatures that occupy its various biomes. Among these, a handful of animals exist that are compatible with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplFindFamili]{Find Familiar} spell. When choosing the spell's "animal forms," you may select one of the CR 0 animals from the following list (in addition to those listed in the spell's description):

  • @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvet}

  • @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Bird}

  • @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozeling}

  • @UUID[Actor.5f6yFaP9gpprOu0w]{Trickadee}

Archfey Patron

Warlocks of Ember who choose an Archfey patron can harness the power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} for their spells, drawing upon the obscure magic of the Realm of Capricious Sorcery. When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as your character's Archfey patron.

The Silent Pack

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.vKU4RfzoCeBJ9sNB overview inline]

Warlocks who bargain with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.vKU4RfzoCeBJ9sNB]{The Silent Pack} are no strangers to cruelty or peril. The primordial members of the Silent Pack are known to toy with their mortal servants, and a bond with this enigmatic coterie of Archfey will undoubtedly lead one on dangerous hunting missions full of impossible cat-and-mouse games. Whatever a Warlock's original point of contact with The Silent Pack — be it a run-in with a roving member of the Pack or a timely encounter with a primordial artifact — The Silent Pack is sure to make their servant's patronage a challenging one.

Vesper

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.RPVn1KLLcutCzYcv overview inline]

Warlocks who enter a covenant with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.RPVn1KLLcutCzYcv]{Vesper} know this mysterious Casia to be a soft-spoken entity, full of puzzling subtlety. Vesper is said to visit her Warlocks in their dreams, where she leads them on wild and curious escapades through illusory corners of The First Forest. To seek arcane power through Vesper is to learn your spellcasting through her otherwordly riddles, her own curious proclivities, and her endless tests of wit.

Raineka
