@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka} are uncommon, but not altogether unheard of. Although Raineka is one of Ember's shard gods — with a host of divine adherents at her service — her influence reaches to arcane spellcasters as well. Warlocks of Raineka astutely recognize her primordial qualities, and strike their otherworldly pacts to beseech her for arcane abilities beyond mortal ken.

Celestial Patron

Warlocks who make their pact with a Celestial patron harness the otherworldy power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} with their spells, drawing upon the radiant magic of the Realm of Endless War. When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as your character's Celestial patron.

Juriel

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2NXPu79uxzDh1Z0x overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2NXPu79uxzDh1Z0x]{Juriel} are often brought into the Tyraphem Lord's loosely-organized fold via a sequence of fateful events — such as the discovery of a Luxaran artifact, an encounter with a mysterious celestial creature, or as the anointed descendent of a powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.y4WHE3TEr6Of13SL]{Railen} dynasty. Much like Juriel themself, Warlocks who make a pact with this fair-minded celestial tend to be people of poise and integrity (even if their personal definitions of these concepts appear to differ from popular or local opinions). Juriel's requirement for his servants is simple: they must swear allegiance to his cause and take up arms against all other Tyraphem Lords.

Taryakel

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.XXyU4kvrBPceEoz2 overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.XXyU4kvrBPceEoz2]{Taryakel} have been known to walk the surface of Ember as long as the Inner Realms themselves have existed. Indeed, Taryakel claims to be one of the oldest celestials of the cosmos, and the subtle impact of this longevity can be seen throughout the known world. Warlocks who strike a pact with this ageless Tyraphem Lord are known for their patience, because they must surely contend with Taryakel's inscrutable wisdom when they least expect it — a challenge that can take most mortals a lifetime to master.

Lantyr

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} are rare, but not altogether unheard of. Although Lantyr is one of Ember's Elder Gods — with a host of divine adherents at her service — her influence reaches to arcane spellcasters as well. Warlocks of Alar astutely recognize the celestial qualities of The Sun, and strike their otherworldly pacts to beseech her for arcane abilities beyond mortal ken.

Fathomless Patron

Warlocks of Ember who choose a Fathomless patron can harness the power of Ember's deep, preternatural waterways for their spells, drawing upon the aqueous magic of the living planet's circulatory system. When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as your character's Fathomless patron.

Godkiller Orinoth

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.j9bIMMSCcMeHstz9 overview inline]

Warlocks who make a pact with the beguiling leviathan known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.j9bIMMSCcMeHstz9]{Godkiller Orinoth} are some of Ember's most insatiable arcane spellcasters, driven by their own allegiance to the unfathomable yearning of Orinoth's preternatural hunger. The first lesson a Warlock of Godkiller Orinoth usually learns is how casually cruel the leviathan can be, for the disembodied conversations with this legendary serpent are riddled with manipulation and abuse — qualities the Warlocks tend to further exhibit themselves as their otherworldly covenant with Orinoth grows stronger.

Fiend Patron

Warlocks of Ember who choose an Fiend patron can harness the uncanny power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} for their spells, drawing upon the esoteric magic of the Realm of Ferocious Curiosity. When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as your character's Fiend patron.

Kerastes

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.aTy7db5ZGUnNDVL4 overview inline]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.aTy7db5ZGUnNDVL4]{Kerastes} enjoys pitting his various servants against each other (fiend and mortal alike), a trait Warlocks of Kerastes must learn to embrace if they wish to know the powerful arcane secrets of the duplicitous Daemos mastermind. Kerastes possesses a keen and rather cruel intelligence, which colors every interaction with this wily Daemos with a certain amount of conflict. Warlocks who make a pact with Kerastes find themselves in his service via a number of ways — like a fateful Signborn bloodline, the otherworldly mysteries of an alien text, or the receipt of a cursed Signaran artifact.

Nalgomith

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.3ZDcyUW0ydYE84rj overview inline]

Unlike many of Ember's otherworldly patrons, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.3ZDcyUW0ydYE84rj]{Nalgomith} is commonly known to sometimes walk the surface of the living planet to commune with his followers. However, this gregariousness is no substitute for common courtesy — a quality the fiendish Daemos seems to lack, despite his relative patriarchal generosity. While Nalgomith is overtly fair to his Warlocks, he still views them as pawns on a chess board; and this air of utility becomes readily apparent to those who might benefit from Nalgomith's patronage.

Alar

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} are uncommon, but not altogether unheard of. Although Alar is one of Ember's Elder Gods — with a host of divine adherents at her service — her influence reaches to arcane spellcasters as well. Warlocks of Alar astutely recognize the eldritch and draconic qualities of The First, and strike their otherworldly pacts to beseech her for arcane abilities beyond mortal ken.

Genie Patron

The term "Genie" is not used in Ember. However, the concept of Genie Patrons persists via the Elemental Sovereigns — a group of deities who preside over Ember's elemental moons.

Warlocks of Ember who choose an Elemental Sovereign as their patron are able to summon the preternatural power of one the living planet's elemental moons. When choosing this subclass, pick one of the following Deities to serve as your character's Elemental Sovereign patron.

Areyter

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HhLvlcy84LAKTFWh overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HhLvlcy84LAKTFWh]{Areyter} can harness the aqueous power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}, thanks to the Elemental Sovereign's cosmic association with the Water Moon. Because of the ubiquity of Ember's moons and the common phenomenon of lunar attunement, Areyter will often make herself known to Mayis-attuend mortals who possess a measurable affinity for arcane spellcasting. Aryeter communicates with her followers and servants via mystical apparitions, such as a phantasmagorical image appearing in a cascade of sea spray or a reflective pool of water. She is regarded for her ceaseless calm.

Lorgi

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KQF9QommtN6ITiLW overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KQF9QommtN6ITiLW]{Lorgi} can harness the incendiary power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}, thanks to the Elemental Sovereign's cosmic association with the Fire Moon. Thanks to the ubiquity of Ember's moons and the common phenomenon of lunar attunement, Lorgi will often make himself known to Ragen-attuned mortals who possess a measurable affinity for arcane spellcasting. Lorgi will often appear to his followers and servants as mystical apparitions in the flickering flames of ritual fires or the torchlight of the chosen. He's known to be friendly, helpful, and involved.

Nymbohr

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Wfy3RfrQNFW8JWOv overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Wfy3RfrQNFW8JWOv]{Nymbohr} can harness the formless power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura}, thanks to the Elemental Sovereign's cosmic association with the Air Moon. Despite the ubiquity of Ember's moons and the common phenomenon of lunar attunement, Nymbohr remains a somewhat elusive entity, but will certainly make himself known to those he deems most worthy. Nymbohr manifests to his followers as a disembodied voice on the wind. He is known to be vague, aloof, and relatively indifferent.

Slinerak

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QzJveYdQLi1LHHci overview inline]

Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QzJveYdQLi1LHHci]{Slinerak} can harness the primal power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora}, thanks to the Elemental Sovereign's cosmic association with the Earth Moon. Because of the ubiquity of Ember's moons and the common phenomenon of lunar attunement, Slinerak will often make himself known to Cora-attuend mortals who possess a measurable affinity for arcane spellcasting. Slinerak is a vulgar entity, and has no qualms about appearing to his followers and servants (or their enemies) by momentarily reshaping the earthly terrain around them — which often appears as mutable and inconsistent as his values.

Great Old One Patron

Warlocks of Ember who choose an Great Old One patron can harness the alien power of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss} for their spells, drawing upon the eldritch magic of the Far Outside. When choosing this subclass, pick one or more of the following Deities to serve as your character's Great Old One patron.

Sitheera

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HAAY0z8U2EIWOjCr overview inline]

No matter their alliances or personal agendas, Warlocks of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HAAY0z8U2EIWOjCr]{Sitheera} are all connected by the fateful web of the Spider Goddess' inscrutable otherworldly whims. To serve the Watcher is to become one with her furtive network of acolytes and adherents, even if a Warlock pursues this service in relative solitude. Sitheera is known to speak to her Warlocks via the mundane arachnids of Ember (among other, more mystical methods), and treats each arcane spellcaster in her service as one of her own children. Whether matronly support or manipulation in disguise, Sitheera's otherworldly encouragement is something each Warlock of her loose order must content with.

Herald of the Whispering Choir

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rxr72Zmt6eUOFg5B overview inline]

Warlocks who make a pact with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rxr72Zmt6eUOFg5B]{Herald of the Whispering Choir} are often driven by an unparalleled curiosity, a trait held in high esteem by the Herald itself. Furthermore, these eldritch spellcasters tend to stand out as pariahs of normal society, even when they hold positions of relative influence or power. And whatever their occupation, many Warlocks of the Herald find themselves called to venture to the Obsidian Desert at least once in their lifetimes on a pilgrimage to commune with the Herald's undying corpse — which mysteriously lingers somewhere beneath the region's blistering sands.
Warlock.scoverview: Warlocks are arcane spellcasters who gain their magic power from a fateful pact made with a mysterious, often otherworldly entity. Whatever causes a Warlock to seek out the knowledge they so desire, they manage to procure it at a great cost — for the whims of a Warlock's patrons must be met if the spellcaster's own power is to grow. Thus, a Warlock and their otherworldly patron are bound by a cosmic thread that connects each of their destinies to one another (for better and worse).

Wizard.name: Wizard
Wizard.text:
Ember is a world steeped in magic, so it's no wonder that Wizards occupy a rather important place among the various occupations that player characters can take up. Whether their mystical knowledge comes from the study of Ember's most venerated libraries or the exploration of long-forgotten places, these arcane spellcasters tend to achieve remarkable positions of power throughout the cosmos. Perhaps more than anything, a Wizard's subclass helps them find their way towards this cosmic destiny, whatever it might be.

Familiars of Ember

The world of Ember has a number of novel creatures that occupy its various biomes. Among these, a handful of animals exist that are compatible with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplFindFamili]{Find Familiar} spell. When choosing the spell's "animal forms," you may select one of the CR 0 animals from the following list (in addition to those listed in the spell's description):

  • @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvet}

  • @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Bird}

  • @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozeling}

  • @UUID[Actor.5f6yFaP9gpprOu0w]{Trickadee}

Abjurer

Protection and banishment spells are the tools of the Abjurer, who primarily uses their magic to defend and redirect. Abjurers of Ember learn their most potent spells from the Abjuration school of magic, which is transparently one of the world's more ubiquitous arcane traditions. Although they can be found all throughout Ember, Abjurers are remarkably common among the war-torn @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} city states, the Signara-savvy @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles}, and the moon-worshipping @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} villages of the Kaustic Hinterlands.

Bladesinger

The history of Bladesingers on Ember is an enigmatic one, with roots stretching far back to the ancient days of the long-forgotten @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire. And while the originators of this esoteric school of magic are long gone, the arcane tradition endures through the teachings of the Aedir's descendants (like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.lOu3Wwh34SH6uqV1]{Lorai} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.oFaQK5PcWivfuOx3]{Nalvani} peoples) as well as ancient texts, manuals, and illusory diagrams that have survived the ages. Bladesinging is one of the rarest arcane subclasses on Ember, and is only learned by a select few Wizards — whether they've inherited the traditions's esoteric techniques or sought them out.

Diviner

Diviners utilize their magic to perceive the hidden and see the unseen, utilizing the so-called "sixth sense" of legend to detect that which has been obscured. Diviners of Ember are a somewhat rare lot, and many of the spells that comprise their school of study are relatively hard to find in the wild. The knowledge of Divination magic is rather guarded throughout many of Ember's realms, and the perceptive specialists who practice this tradition tend to go by names specific to their order or origin. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} Star Mages of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy} are among the most celebrated of Diviners in the cosmos, and their arcane predictions — known for their keen precision and uncanny foresight — are held in high regard by the hopeful and the hidden alike (for equal but opposite reasons, of course).

Evoker

Also known as Elementalists throughout most of Ember, Evokers are Wizards whose arcane spellcasting harnesses the metaphysical power of the elements. Naturally, Evokers of Ember have a strong relationship, reverence, or fascination with one or more of Ember's six moons, and weave spells that literally evoke the elemental magic of the living planet's lunar bodies. Furthermore, Elementalists are often combat-focused, finding opportunity in realms where their aggressive spells can see practical use. Some of Ember's most powerful Elementalists have emerged from places like the Kaustic Hinterlands, where the moon-worshipping @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} live among the ruins of the ancient giants; or the ports of coastal cities like @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7iZDVtrBO7326XZY]{Caren'ac} and @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Pn6NT1oZqpYisyjp]{Kalvard}.

Illusionist

Illusionists are Wizards who specialize in magic that obscures the senses and warps the mind. And since spells from the school of Illusion are cosmically rooted in the tenebrous magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, Illusionists of Ember are often colloquially known as "Shade Mages." One of the more ubiquitous of Ember's arcane traditions, Illusionists are often dismissed as too playful or unnecessary (much like the Inner Realm of Primordis itself); but learned adventurers and sages alike know that Illusionists can become just as powerful as any Wizard, if not more so. After all, the mind is perhaps the most important of one's faculties; and Ember's Illusionists are masters of mind control. And wherever civilization or intrigue can be found — from the industrial corners of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7iZDVtrBO7326XZY]{Caren'ac} to the bustling districts of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} — so too can a competent Illusionist.

Order of Scribes

Ember's Order of Scribes was founded by one of the world's oldest champions of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, the Elder Goddess of Magic. This champion — a powerful Kiska Wizard named Breña Vhast — established the Order's first sanctuary long ago in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowland Bastions} during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of the Tower}. In the millenia since, casters of all stripes have sought out the Order's curious and esoteric traditions, so that they too might unravel the immortal cosmic mysteries of Ember's arcane Weave; thus, these arcane spellcasters end up serving the inscrutable whims of the elder goddess, whether they know it or not. Indeed, by merely perpetuating the Order and its teachings, each Order of Scribe Wizard on Ember becomes a historical part of Spectra's legacy. And in the years since the Order's inception, other strongholds have been established throughout Ember — such as the remote Palimpsest Tower of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Rg25PSayVhEQEpNe]{Cascaal Peninsula}, and the venerated @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.iphMPgtJv5eQjGaR]{Librarium of Spectra} in Ordain.
Wizard.scoverview: Wizards harness the power of arcane magic through years of careful research, intense study, and tireless dedication. Because of this potent esoteric training, Wizards can eventually become some of the most powerful beings in the world — but a rare few actually possess the talent, commitment, or resources needed to plumb the deepest depths of Ember's arcane mysteries.

Classes Overview.name: Classes Overview
Classes Overview.text:
Ember uses the standard classes from Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition for player character creation. The twelve core classes featured in the 2024 Player's Handbook are available to all players. Additionally, the Artificer class is only available if you have Tasha's Cauldron of Everything by Wizards of the Coast installed.

Each of these character classes has been carefully incorporated into the lore and setting of Ember, with various levels of adjustment for narrative and gameplay considerations. These changes are recommended for anyone who would like to immerse themselves more fully in the game world, but they are not required — the Ember experience should emphasize freedom of expression and personal choice among its ideals, beginning here during character creation.

Character progression for each of these classes in Ember follows the same rules as it does in any other Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition (2024) game.

  • @UUID[.emberBarbarian00]{Barbarian}

  • @UUID[.emberBard0000000]{Bard}

  • @UUID[.emberCleric00000]{Cleric}

  • @UUID[.emberDruid000000]{Druid}

  • @UUID[.emberFighter0000]{Fighter}

  • @UUID[.emberMonk0000000]{Monk}

  • @UUID[.emberPaladin0000]{Paladin}

  • @UUID[.emberRanger00000]{Ranger}

  • @UUID[.emberRogue000000]{Rogue}

  • @UUID[.emberSorcerer000]{Sorcerer}

  • @UUID[.emberWarlock0000]{Warlock}

  • @UUID[.emberWizard00000]{Wizard}

Expansion Classes

  • @UUID[.emberArtificer00]{Artificer}

Reviled Magic

Some Necromancy spells within Ember are fueled by the eldritch magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss}. The accumulation and use of certain spells can have dramatic effects on gameplay, which should be considered before creating a spellcasting character. During character creation, we recommend you familiarize yourself with the concept of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.0RXUc08I2fOUESTL#reviled-magic]{Reviled Magic} in Ember, and discuss your character concept and background with the Gamemaster.

Regarding Subclasses

Because of Ember's unique setting and lore — including its novel ancestries, cultures, and history — a substantial amount of the text regarding the game's various subclasses has been reworked and rewritten to accommodate this brand new world. The character class pages throughout this journal feature a new description for each subclass that has been affected by Ember's setting and narrative, while a few subclasses remain relatively untouched. We encourage players and gamemasters alike to embrace the narrative opportunities these modified subclasses have to offer.

These advised changes should be presented to players during character creation as a starting point to enhance their immersion within Ember's distinct narrative, but they aren't the only paths PCs can take during advancement. Ultimately, these tweaks to the original subclasses are optional, and players should be allowed to create the characters they want to portray the most.
Classes Overview.scoverview: All of the character classes supported by the Fifth Edition game system are compatible with and represented in Ember. For most of these classes and their subclasses, specific narrative considerations have been indicated to provide players and gamemasters alike with recommendations on how the creation of these characters can intersect with the unique lore and worldbuilding of the Ember setting.

Mayis.name: Mayis
Mayis.text:
• Keywords: Water, Survial, Storms

  • Ideal: Patience

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: The Tempest Moon, The Fathomless, The Eternal Tide

Eternal grey, white, and blue storms shroud Mayis in a permanent cloak of howling, unstoppable hurricanes. Yet beneath this turbulent atmosphere lies a dark, roiling ocean, broken by shattered floating islands that rise and fall with the moon’s heaving waves. Immense and untamed, Mayis is a perilous, elemental expanse where otherworldly water elementals swim through the currents, and enormous behemoths lie in wait behind floating underwater islands of ice.

Mayis is a world defined by a singular element: water. Its single vast ocean is a wild and lethal expanse where survival requires not only contending with crushing pressures and unpredictable currents but also with dangerous denizens of the deep. Though the moon has remained untamed throughout its existence, it has long been home to the Typhic, smaller cousins of the moon's other legendary inhabitants, the Behemonths. While most of the Typhic population resides within the monumental city of Tohr, anchored to the back of the Elemental Sovereign @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HhLvlcy84LAKTFWh]{Areyter}, others survive in nomadic floating villages that drift through the dark waters. These outposts are often tucked away in the jagged cracks and ice-chasms of the moon’s wandering frozen islands, hidden from the larger predators.

To mortals on Ember, Mayis embodies both awe and caution. Its relentless storms and vast, unpredictable oceans are seen as symbols of the undying strength and power of the waves. Sailors, travelers, and seers speak of the moon as a place that tests the mind and spirit alike, offering insight and reward only to those willing to wait, observe, and respect its rhythms.
Mayis.scoverview: Mayis is a world of endless motion, wrapped in titanic storms that have raged since Creation. Its surface is a single, heaving ocean of dark and glimmering water where fragments of shattered islands drift both across and above the waves. The depths are alive with countless creatures, rising out of the gloom, their forms glimpsed only through flashes of lightning. Somewhere deep within the moon drifts the fabled city of Tohr, a place of calm serenity amid the dangers, where calm waters mirror the patience that defines the moon itself.
Mayis.sgamemaster:
The geography of Mayis is a vertical labyrinth. Though almost entirely fluid, the moon is divided into numerous levels, differentiated by light and depth. Near the surface, the light of the Lantyr filters through to support massive, sprawling coral reefs and sun-drenched kelp fields that either float entirely or rest upon floating islands. As one descends, the water grows colder, and the light fades, giving way to hardier flora and larger, more deadly creatures. In these twilight depths, the waters are most often lit by glimmering bioluminescent plants and entire forests that pulse in time with the moon’s heartbeat.

At the absolute center of Mayis lies the Core of Ice. Here, the pressure is so immense that the water has crystallized into a frozen heart. Near the core, light from Lantyr is entirely absent, and the landscape is full of cold ice islands, most of which are miles in size and covered in lightless caves and jagged underwater ice mountains. From the Core of Ice, the Force of Water itself flows out into the water of Myais and even beyond into the Sea of Stars and the Cosmos as a whole.

Flora & Fauna

On Mayis, the plant life can range from tiny to absolutely gigantic, with some areas of the moon overgrown with underwater flora. The massive, vine-like Siphon-Stalks extend down from the floating islands, dropping miles into the deeper currents. Bioluminescent forests of Glow-Grip trees cling to passing debris to create mobile, glowing ecosystems. These natural structures provide much-needed protection from its many predators, often used as hiding places, nurseries, or resting places. Most creatures on Mayis are intricately linked to the Force of Water and are elemental by nature or magical to some extent, but they are also heavily armored, fast, or deadly in their own ways.

At the absolute peak of this food chain are the Behemoths, the oldest and most powerful entities on Mayis save for Areyter herself. These colossal predators treat the entire moon as their playground, possessing such immense strength, size, and power that their territorial disputes can trigger current shifts felt throughout every depth. While smaller creatures fight for survival among themselves, the Behemoths move through the deeps with total impunity, answering only to one another.

Notable Locations

  • The City of Tohr. An ancient masterpiece of architecture and living coral, the capital of Mayis is built directly upon the back of Lady Areyter. It serves as the Typhic's primary home.

  • Norvirim's Wreck. The shattered remains of a massive, ancient vessel, now floating in the mid-depths. It has become a haunted labyrinth of rusted metal and shadows.

  • The Ice Core. At the absolute heart of the moon, the water is crushed into a crystalline, frozen sphere that radiates the Force of Water into the Cosmos.

  • Maedrift Forest. A vast, wandering ecosystem of Glow-Grip trees and Siphon-Stalks that drifts through the twilight currents. It serves as a vital nursery for the moon's more peaceful aquatic life, though it is frequently shadowed by Behemoths who treat the forest as a seasonal hunting ground.

  • Cave of Bwagaw. A legendary, pressure-warped cavern located near the Ice Core where the water is said to scream with the echoes of the Abyss. It is the rumored den of a corrupted, ancient Behemoth.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HhLvlcy84LAKTFWh]{Areyter}

Cora.name: Cora
Cora.text:
• Keywords: Earth, Endurance, Cataclysm

  • Ideal: Pragmatism

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: The Blasted Moon, The Stone Mother, The Crashing World

The fearsome earth moon is a lunar body of restless, yet predictable forces. Cora's gravitational pull is both erratic and fierce, capable of powerful surges that can tear the very mountains from the surface of the moon and cast them into the Sea of Stars — and drag them back down again to impact the lunar surface with terrifying force. These unending upheavals have formed a ring of debris that orbits the moon like a jagged crown, a monument to Cora's relentless, self-inflicted destruction. Yet, throughout this endless cycle of ruin, new formations arise and the moon endures.

In the earliest ages, as the cosmos of Ember took shape, Cora emerged from the Sea of Stars as a molten mass of ore and stone. It was said that from her body came the bones of the world of ember itself, and some believe Cora may have once been part of the world itself before being torn free. Over time, the moon's surface became a crucible of violent transformation: mountains rising quickly and collapsing in moments, canyons yawning wide and then sealing shut again within hours. Few beings can endure such fury, and the moon’s main inhabitants are the Korvathi, elemental creatures of stone and crystal, who survive by sheer adaptability.

To mortals on Ember, Cora is both revered and seen with some caution. Many assign a feminine personality to the moon despite no evidence to support the idea. Farmers, miners, and builders alike whisper her name in quiet prayers before working the soil or striking the ground, acknowledging the moon's temper as much as her generosity. Scholars see Cora as the embodiment of harsh necessity, the understanding that survival requires acceptance of hardship. While other moons may inspire faith or wonder, Cora teaches endurance: that the world does not bend to one’s will, but one must meet its challenge regardless.
Cora.scoverview: The fearsome moon of earth has been wracked by wild and untamed change since Creation. Its powerful gravitational forces fluctuate erratically, causing dramatic fissures and changes to its topography, while flinging rock into the moon’s orbiting ring of debris. This debris is often trapped above for a short time before Cora’s gravitational surges cause these meteors to plummet and slam unrelentingly into the moon’s pockmarked surface.
Cora.sgamemaster:
Cora is a world of change, its surface is a chaotic mosaic of fresh scars and ancient ridges, where gravity behaves like a wild beast, surging and ebbing without warning. One moment, a traveler may feel as light as a feather; the next, they are pressed to the ground by forces capable of cracking bones. The environment hosts one of the most intense and relentless battlefields in the Cosmos, where native Korvathi and earth elementals fight against terrible spiders skittering from the moon's core. This ongoing battle is further complicated by both sides attacking and trying to destroy malignant oozes that emerge from every crack and tear in the moon, led by the corrupted Elemental Sovereign Slinerak.

Flora & Fauna

The biology of Cora is defined by armor and density, as anything fragile is instantly shattered by the shifting moon or impacts. Obsidian Vines extend through fissures, their stone thorns able to anchor into solid rock to withstand gravitational surges. The only structures called Iron Palms are mineral deposits that grow upward during low-gravity cycles and harden into indestructible columns. The Korvathi, the moon's main inhabitants, are armored elementals with crystalline nervous systems that can sense gravitational shifts seconds before they happen. The moon is also filled with massive web-filled lairs, inhabited by spiders, some as large as buildings.

Notable Locations

  • The Palace of Rust: The home of the corrupted Sovereign of Earth, the debaunced Slinerak.

  • The Iron Forge: A subterranean city built within a massive geode of Iron, where the pressure of the moon is harnessed to craft tools that can cut through any material.

  • The Crystal Core: The shuddering centre of the moon, said to be home to the largest spider lair in existence, and the home of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HAAY0z8U2EIWOjCr]{Sitheera}.

  • The Resonating Monoliths: A circle of twelve obsidian towers that hum with a deep, subsonic frequency, serving as the only places on the moon where gravity remains perfectly stable.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.QzJveYdQLi1LHHci]{Slinerak}

Aura.name: Aura
Aura.text:
• Keywords: Air, Knowledge, Paradox

  • Ideal: Individualism

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: The Hollow Moon, The Veiled Sphere, The Breath of the Cosmos

From the surface of Ember, Aura appears as a gentle, pale pink orb streaked with white lights and dark bands of swirling clouds. Yet this serene face conceals a mesmerizing world within a hollow sphere of shifting gases, luminous storms, and an endless sky. Its thin outer crust conceals vast layers of mists and vapor, where titanic creatures of the air drift and soar. Among them are the Xarcaledons, feathered leviathans said to be as old as the cosmos and the moons' true guardians, whose songs echo like thunder through the Hollow Moon’s unseen reaches.

At the heart of Aura floats the mythical city of Conundrum, a place of impossible geometry, floating structures, and ageless wisdom. Scholars believe it to be a convergence of lost knowledge, a citadel of the mind where creative thoughts and the winds themselves intertwine. The city is said to drift in the exact center of the moon and is the only place on Aura that remains constantly stable. To many, Aura embodies the pursuit of personal truth, freedom, and the pursuit of one's own destiny, but it is also a window into the dangers of pride, isolation, and the abandonment of responsibility; for just as air gives breath, it can just as easily suffocate.

To mortals on Ember, Aura symbolizes freedom of mind and self-determination. Philosophers see it as the domain of independent thinkers and those who dare to chart their own course. When its faint pink glow appears in the night sky, travelers report visions and inspirations carried by unseen winds.
Aura.scoverview: From the surface world of Ember the moon of air seems solid, but a thin surface of pale pink rock shrouds a mesmerizing hollow world within. Aura is a world of gasses, clouds, and floating dangers that few mortals can safely navigate. In addition to the environment, Aura contains a plethora of monstrous creatures such as the mythical and enormous feathered Xarcaledons. Legend tells that in the center of Aura hovers the floating city of Conundrum, a bastion of learning and knowledge of the Cosmos.
Aura.sgamemaster:
Aura is a world of endless skies, enclosed within a shell no thicker than half a mile and composed of a material similar to glass, making it slightly transparent. Within its hollow interior, gravity pulls slightly outward toward the shell and inward toward the center, creating a vast, dense, and complex atmosphere filled with luminous voids, thick storms, and vast stretches of empty shimmering sky. At the center, where atmospheric pressure becomes extraordinarily high, lies the legendary city of Conundrum. It is inhabited by Zeph, although legends suggest they may not have been its original inhabitants. Following the events of the Abyssal Shear, Conundrum is still plagued by corruption and darkness. Despite numerous efforts to destroy and push back the monsters emerging from its stones, they keep returning, causing endless battles to break out in the city's streets.

Flora & Fauna

Life on Aura is dominated by floating plants and creatures, such as the Sky-Lilies, massive floating plants with translucent petals that serve as sails to catch the wind. These plants extend long, bioluminescent "roots" into clouds and storms, drawing minerals and water. Among the clouds, vast swarms of Mist-Rays move silently through the air, camouflaging themselves against the white and pink cloud layers. The legendary Xarcaledons are the moon's true rulers, and their shadows strike fear into even the most experienced Zeph, their maws glittering with long teeth and their iridescent feathers humming with energy.

Notable Locations

  • Mesatrons Folly: A massive pocket of superheated steam created by a strange object at its center, that defies the clouds and gravity around, hanging motionless among the clouds.

  • The Hurricane Gallery: A stable, circular storm front where the lightning has been magically frozen into jagged, permanent sculptures of light.

  • The Forest of Jep: A massive collection of floating Sky-Lilies that drifts close to the inner surface of the shell.

  • The Echoing Atrium: A massive hollowed-out asteroid trapped within the moon, home to odd creatures that slip between the shadows.

  • The Well of Gravity: A terrifying "hole" in the clouds near the center where the winds fail entirely, causing anything caught within it to fall towards the mythical city of Conundrum, accelerated at insane speeds.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Wfy3RfrQNFW8JWOv]{Nymbohr}

Ragen.name: Ragen
Ragen.text:
• Keywords: Fire, Betrayal, Rebirth

  • Ideal: Directness

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: The Charred Moon, The Ember Crown, The Broken Flame

Ragen was once a breathtaking world of living fire, where molten forests and rivers of flame burned with life. The Pyrrhen, beings of fire given form, tended this incandescent realm, believing that through flame they could express the truth of the cosmos, the endless cycle of death, life, and rebirth. They forged cities of unburning wood and glass, their spires rising upwards to cover the surface of the moon.

When the cosmos fractured during the Shattering, Ragen’s brilliance blazed defiantly against the encroaching dark. Yet its life-giving flame was seen as a challenge, and so it was targeted by forces of terrifying power with hatred and malice. Its said that the moon erupted in storms of black alien ash as magic from beyond tore into its surface, its continents burning away during a war that ripped the moon apart. Amid the chaos, the Pyrrhen seemed to turn upon one another, some striving to preserve their radiant home, others surrendering to the corruption that flooded their world. When the flames at last subsided, Ragen was little more than a scar upon the cosmos, its once-living forests reduced to wastelands of ash and cinders.

From Ember’s surface, Ragen now burns faintly, a wounded flame that refuses to die. Its dim red glow reminds mortals of its former glimmering glory and its unfortunate fate. To the people of Ember, the Charred Moon is both a warning and a lesson: fire provides warmth, life, and clarity, but when it’s left unchecked, it consumes everything in its path.
Ragen.scoverview: Legend tells that the surface of Ragen was once covered in flame-wreathed groves of living fire, where radiant beings and creatures of fire and smoke thrived amid burning forests. When the cosmos was torn apart during the Shattering, Ragen’s brilliance drew the malice of the dark, and its once-flourishing realm was engulfed in storms of ash. The Pyrrhen fought to preserve their world, but the fire turned upon itself, and their cities were lost beneath waves of deadly magic. Now, only a few flickering remnants of those eternal groves remain, surrounded by a wasteland of blackened glass haunted by echoes of flame and shadow.
Ragen.sgamemaster:
Ragen is one of the most heavily corrupted elemental moons in the Cosmos. During the Abyssal Shear, its surface was overwhelmed by hordes of Abyssal monsters. Even now, the pockmarked and scorched terrain hosts numerous horrors hiding in the ash and deep caves. The air is filled with the stench of death and decay, and occasional roars break the eerie silence among the ash wastelands. A few small pockets of life remain, including the Garden of Ravela, which survived and resisted the hordes of the Abyss. These pockets of life are the sole remaining habitats for elemental creatures that still survive, and a few scattered settlements of the Pyrrhen that try to cling on amid attacks and assaults from the wastelands.

Flora & Fauna

The vegetation on Ragen within its surviving native pockets consists of Cinderasc, trees with bark like cooling magma, and leaves that are literally dancing tongues of flame. Beneath their canopy, thick fields of Fiern Ferns blanket the ground, providing further shelter for small ground-dwelling birds called the Ciptec. Birds are among the most common elemental creatures on Ragen, with the legendary Phoenix being the most famous. The Phoenix lives in the wastelands, trying to restore the flames of its ancient forts before it dies and is reborn through a fiery, life-giving explosion.

Notable Locations

  • Garden of Ravela. The refuge and sanctuary of the Elemental Sovereign Ravela, her garden remains one of the few remaining places on the moon that embody Ragen's pre-Shattering state—a vibrant, lush forest of immense scale.

  • The Obsidian Ribs: A massive, fossilized ribcage of an ancient creature that defies imagination, that now serves as a jagged mountain range and a haven for the Pyrrhen.

  • Fitaci Spire. Once the home of Fiyara, this blackened and hollow spire of melted rock and glass now houses her remaining fanatical followers, corrupted elementals, and monsters.

  • The Fountain of White Flame: A shimmering pool of pure, radiant heat in the center of a grove that is said to heal those who are brave enough to touch its blinding waters.

  • The Den of Evil. A massive tunnel that burrows deep into the surface of Ragen is said to extend into large caverns beneath the moon. These tunnels are believed to house some of the most vicious abyssal monsters in the cosmos.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WMO5VwobQNmjaXQA]{Ravela}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KQF9QommtN6ITiLW]{Lorgi}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ZvsMcVcESynKQn8d]{Fiyara}

Orbis.name: Orbis
Orbis.text:
• Keywords: Chaos, Change, Emotion

  • Ideal: Spontaneity

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: The Spirit Moon, The Maelstrom, The Unbound Halo

Orbis is unlike any other moon in the cosmos. It is composed of vast, luminous bands that spiral and cross one another in an ever-shifting lattice of color and light. These colossal ribbons weave layer upon layer, encircling a roaring maelstrom at the moon’s heart. At first glance, each band appears smooth and white, but the longer one gazes upon them, the more they fracture into iridescent patterns, kaleidoscopic hues that twist and shimmer as though alive. No layer follows a constant orbit; they drift and bend around each other in a slow, almost hypnotic dance.

No life stirs within Orbis. There are no creatures, no elemental beings, and nothing stirs across its ever-twisting lands. Winds scream between the shifting layers, and faint echoes can be heard where the bands brush together, forming chords that have driven countless seers to madness. Many scholars claim that this music is thought itself, the raw expression of creation or chaos. Some believe the truly ancient tales that Orbis is a prison, a shell built to contain a terrifying ancient power that should never again awaken.

From Ember’s surface, Orbis gleams as a restless jewel, its colors waxing and fading without rhythm or reason. It embodies a person's raw spirit, emotion, and unpredictability. Orbis has no patterns, no single truth, but is always in constant motion.
Orbis.scoverview: Mind-twisting arrays of white and multi-colored geometric bands surround the roiling maelstrom at the heart of the chaos moon of Orbis. It is said that at first glance, each band appears as solid white matter, but anomalous pearlescent patterns appear with increasing intensity the longer they are observed. An ancient myth told throughout the ages is that surrounding the maelstrom at the heart of Orbis is an eternal prison built to contain the most dangerous and calamitous force of the Cosmos.
Orbis.sgamemaster:
Orbis is a place of breathtaking beauty and profound psychological peril, where the bizarre and alien nature of the environment can break even the strongest minds. The atmosphere is a shimmering haze of psychic static, where colors have weight and shadows hum with discarded thoughts. While extremely few people from the surface of Ember have ever traveled to Orbis or recorded anything about its history, it is said that the moon was the only place in the Cosmos ignored by the Abyss during the Abyssal Shear.

Flora & Fauna

Biologically, Orbis is a wasteland, as no organic or elemental life can take root on its shifting plane like bands. In place of plants, the bands are encrusted with Refraction-Clusters—crystalline growths that grow by absorbing the stray emotions of those who gaze upon the moon from the surface of Ember. These clusters do not breathe; they pulse in sync with the central maelstrom, occasionally shattering into Prism-Dust that drifts between the layers. The only "inhabitants" are the Chromatic Echoes, visual after-images of historical events trapped within the light of the bands, playing out silent, looping tragedies for eternity.

Notable Locations

  • The Maelstrom. The central core of Orbis, a roaring white hole of raw chaotic energy that is visible through the gaps in the lattice. Said to be enclosed by solid bars of an indestructible prison.

  • The Knot: A rare junction where seven of the moons' bands have tangled into a stationary, multi-colored mountain of light that serves as the only "stable" landing point on the moon.

  • The Well of Silent Screams: A localized vacuum between two fast-moving bands where sound is utterly erased.

  • The Fortress of Pandemonium. A massive castle structure made of white crystal-like stone, said to be inhabited by creatures that defy reality itself and are older than the Ember Cosmos.

Akon.name: Akon
Akon.text:
• Keywords: Order, Regret, Ruin

  • Ideal: Discipline

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: The Shattered Moon, The Broken Crown, The Silent Architect

Akon was once a bastion of symmetry and reason, its surface covered in vast geometric plains of metal and glass where the ancient Wyrms crafted monuments and machines that reflected the perfect harmony of creation. The Wyrms, beings of immense wisdom, sought to understand the architecture that shaped all existence, believing that through pure logic and discipline they might one day mirror the perfection of the cosmos itself.

Today, Akon is a graveyard. Its shattered remains drift through the sky above Ember like a frozen storm, with massive fragments orbiting the now-broken and lifeless moon. The endless debris fields, sharp with the edges of crystals and metal, whisper to those who watch them for too long, voices of regret, mourning the loss of a once pure and noble people.

The tragedy of Akon is discussed endlessly by scholars and historians; many claim that its destruction marked the first great fall of cosmic reason, and every year, Ember falls further into chaos. The Wyrms, for all their brilliance, were blinded by their faith in structures and logic, unable to grasp the dangers of unmanaged chaos. Yet even now, the broken fragments of Akon shimmer faintly in the night sky, a silent reminder that Order, though wounded, still binds the cosmos together, frail, but enduring. Among the people of Ember, Akon is regarded with fear and sorrow. When its splintered chunks reach thier apex in the night sky, many see it as an omen of misfortune. Some claim that the Shattering and the destruction of the moon was some kind of divine punishment, while others argue it was merely in the wrong place at the wrong time and was hit by shards of the Sun Tower completely at random.
Akon.scoverview: Once a glimmering orb of darkened bronze, the moon of order is now gray, broken, and lifeless. It is said that the wise and ancient Wyrms had tunneled beneath its surface since Creation, where they magically forged wondrous and delicate machines to safeguard the cosmos. The Shattering was catastrophic for Akon, breaking the moon into thousands of fragments and scouring life from its surface and passageways. Now, constructs, machines, and undead monsters prowl the crisscrossing tunnels and passageways of its intact sections.
Akon.sgamemaster:
Akon now exists as a hollowed, broken graveyard, surrounded by jagged fragments. The air is thin and metallic, with a taste of copper and dust. Silence is only broken by the grinding of drifting metal and machinery tectonic plates. Many of the Wyrms' machines and structures are broken, but some still seem operational, slowly ticking or turning in strange patterns without any visible source of energy or control. Interestingly, very few Abyssal monsters are present on the moon; they tend to avoid it, as if there's little left to corrupt, which is probably true.

Flora & Fauna

It's said that nothing living still walks on the surface of Akon, but that's not entirely true. While there are no large plants, small patches of hardy moss cling to the walls of some of the deepest recesses and caves. Among these tiny Solder-Mites, small insect-like creatures also cling on. Although they may not be truly alive, the last remnants and legacy of the Wyrmns still wander the moon in the form of strange constructs called the Akonites. Elsewhere on the moon, only the dead and ghosts roam the ruins. It's said that terrifying creatures known as Echo-Worms can be found in the dark, incorporeal remnants of the Wyrms—gliding through the air between fragments.

Notable Locations

  • The Great Orrery: A floating cluster of metallic spheres that once tracked the movement of souls in the cosmos, now spinning erratically and showing only visions of the Shattering.

  • Plains of Dust: The vast stretches of lifeless surface, home to countless undead monsters that were once elemental creatures of the moon and servants of the Wyrms of Akon.

  • The Engine of Dead Thought: A gargantuan, rusted gear-work heart embedded in the moon’s surface that still beats once every century, causing a localized surge of gravity that pulls nearby debris into its maw.

  • Kestalon's Burial Mound: A colossal pile of broken metal, broken machinery, and rusted tools, said to be one of the last structures built by the Wyrms as they buried their last great ruler, who fell defending Akon against the forces of the Abyss during the Abyssal Shear. Countless desiccated corpses of massive Wyrms lie scattered across the surface of the mound.

Primordis.name: Primordis
Primordis.text:
• Keywords: Shadow, Illusion, Predatory

  • Ideal: Cunning

  • Age: Countless Years

  • Other Names: Realm of Capricious Shadows, Shadowlands, The First Forest

Primordis is a violently dangerous realm for mortals. Ancient entities, deadly creatures and the realm itself treat all visitors as prey, and you are just as likely to be hunted as you are to become a toy in some twisted game. Like the other Inner Realms of @UUID[.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} and@UUID[.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{ Signara}, Primordis is the pinnacle of an otherworldly realm. It feels utterly alien for any mortals who dare tread its paths. Fortunately, it lies so far from the @UUID[.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} that it has remained isolated and mysterious throughout every age of the Cosmos, and mortal visitors or explorers are practically unheard of.

Mortals connected Primorids and the Blooming season long ago as Primordis slowly drifted above the surface world and Luxarum waned. Primordis is also visible in the night sky, glimmering with a soft red glow roughly the same size as one of the Moons of Ember, highlighting its importance to ordinary people. In truth, all the Inner Realms are much larger than most mortals know and are comparable in size to the World of Ember itself, in addition to having even more powerful effects on the surface world than the Elemental Moons.

Very little is known of the realm itself among mortals beyond whispered tales and ancient stories of its strange, predatory inhabitants. Like the other Inner Realms, for most, it simply forms part of the tapestry of the night sky and the seasonal and yearly change. Arcane spellcasters tend to revere and study the distant secrets of Primordis during their lifelong quests for esoteric knowledge; otherwise, the realm simply forms the basis of a wide variety of cultural celebrations and stories surrounding the passing of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.loBTA2Ahpf2nMgIY]{Seeding} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.8chE39ioICfZw3jU]{Blooming}.
Primordis.scoverview: Since Creation, the shadowed land known as Primordis has been one of the most untamed and dangerous realms in all the Cosmos. Intense shadowy sorcery and primeval magic swirl beneath the crimson boughs of the colossal tree-like plants. This is a place where mortals become lost amidst towering foliage, fall prey to silent creatures, or are driven mad by twisted illusions that mock their every turn. Despite its many threats, Primordis is the home to the capricious yet often compassionate Casia, beings of concentrated ancient magic, and their sundry kin the fey.
Primordis.sgamemaster:
Primordis is an alien, primordial place and home to extremely aggressive and lethal predators. Every creature on Primordis is a fey, a classification of creature type deeply tied to Shadow Magic. Most fey have some inherent feline characteristics; these traits actually originated from Primordis and are not native to the World of Ember: large eyes, sleek fur, claws, fangs, and agile builds. Fey are nevertheless incredibly varied in type, with different forms and personalities that make them hard to recognize as a connected group. Unfortunately, many fey are hostile towards mortals, and tend to view them with aggressive curiosity. While the term fey refers to their creature type, the word "Primordian" is also used to describe the collective inhabitants of Primordis. In sporadic cases, some beings that live within the realm are not fey (and may actually be mortal). Many fey are sapient and more than capable of rational thought, but some that stalk the immense forest of Primordis are creatures of habit and insatiable hunger.

The original inhabitants of Primordis are the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia}, who are said to have emerged during Creation. Most of the Casia found within Primordis today are incredibly ancient beings, far older than the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} of Ember. Still, they are not as powerful as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods}, but there are far more numerous, possibly numbering in the hundreds. An exact number of Casia is almost impossible to find, as many remain hidden or have changed forms and names over the ages. Casia are the original fey of Primordis and can be just as varied as their lesser kin in personalities. They tend to be slightly more benign, helpful, and caring towards mortals, possibly due to their age and experiences. It's unknown if the Casia created the rest of the fey who inhabit Primordis or if they arose naturally. Still, the Casia themselves are actually significantly outnumbered compared to the other fey and only control smaller pockets of the wilder Primordis.

While many fey are born and are completely natural creatures of Primordis, some fey did not begin that way, and instead, they were once mortals. Mortal souls can be bound, coerced, or tricked into eternal service and turned into fey, and some mortals even choose this option willingly. This is one of the core concepts of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7#eternal-souls]{Eternal Soul}.

Shadow magic originates from Primordis, but of all the magical forces in the Cosmos, Shadow is considered the hardest to both understand and master. Only the fey can use it innately, and the Casia are its ultimate practitioners. Throughout Primordis Shadow magic is everywhere and it affects everything and everyone. Illusions and twisting echoes are common, and the realm often hunts its own inhabitants with living shadows. Arcane magic is also widespread throughout Primordis, and its presence is often responsible for powerful effects and anomalies. All the inhabitants of the Inner Realms are suffused with magic to some degree. Still, the fey and Casia are perhaps the most significant examples of true magical beings living within the Ember Cosmos. As an additional consequence of this all-encompassing magic, most spells are amplified in power or duration when cast in Primordis.

Flora & Fauna

Primordis is home to a colossal range of unique plant varieties and is considered by many to be the First Forest from which the ideas of plants themselves came. Its trees are among the most titanic lifeforms in the Cosmos, towering hundreds, if not thousands, of meters into the sky. Twisting vines, dense foliage, and plants often as large as the trees themselves mean that Primordis is a realm unlike any other. On this vertical hunting ground, navigating the environments quickly can be the deciding factor between life or death.

Notable Locations

Primordis is a vast primordial realm. While much of its surface is covered by immense trees and plant life a few notable locations and even settlements exist hidden in the deepest shadows. Unlike @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}, most of Primordis is home to the Casia and fey with very few outsiders. The events of the Abyssal Shear did not severely affect its inhabitants, but they were still profoundly affected, and remnants can still be found in desolate, forbidden areas.

  • Naloria Vale. Home to Vesper, one of the more prominent and well-known Casia and the creator of the Zeph in ancient days.

  • Shimatrix Pools. A distant part of Primordis that lies upon the edge of the realm facing Signara, where the body of one of the Daemos has been lying since her destruction during Creation.

  • Fin’ian Crags. A splitting line of mountains barely visible above the all-encompassing plant life, Fin'ian Crags are crisscrossed with countless tunnels created by some unknown and extremely secretive fey.

  • Keron’s Lodge. A lonely Kiska and Human settlement on the edge of Primordis, home to hardened survivors and fey hunters.

  • Jinam’s Spike. A Thornling City built inside the fossilized remains of an ancient plant covered in colossal thorns. The Thornlings here are just as predatory as the fey around them and seem quite at home on Primordis.

  • The Shadow Thicket. Some say the location from where the Casia emerged in Primordis at the center of Primordis. It is also the home to several Casia who call themselves the Silent Pack; combined, they are a terrifyingly dangerous group.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2FA1FO5P0G83sjt9]{Nimaelle}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.RPVn1KLLcutCzYcv]{Vesper}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.vKU4RfzoCeBJ9sNB]{The Silent Pack}

Luxarum.name: Luxarum
Luxarum.text:
• Keywords: Zeal, Faith, Light

  • Ideal: Ambition

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: The Realm of Endless War, Golden Realm, Land of Light

Luxarum is a realm of unbelievable contradictions, where golden, warming light is used to end lives and cause untold devastation. Luxarum has fewer cosmological dangers than @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, and its magic is straightforward in its raw destructive potential but the real dangers of the Golden Realm lie with its inhabitants, the unwavering and relentless @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} who view mortals as mere tools and objects to further their personal war efforts. The most fascinating aspect of Luxarum is that for the vast majority of mortals on Ember, the realm is considered to be a warming, hopeful place that brings life and light after the darkness of winter. This is partly due to the connection between light and the energy given off by Lantyr. Throughout countless myths and legends, the Tyraphem are often viewed as guiding forces of goodness and help guide mortals but nothing could be further from the truth.

Luxarum is a deeply disturbing and alien realm. Indeed, it lies so far from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} that it has remained isolated and mysterious throughout every age of the Cosmos, and mortal visitors or explorers here are practically unheard of. Mortals do, however, have a clear understanding of the role that Luxarum plays in the yearly calendar, associating its passage in the sky as a marker for the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.xu3TCWh4GPy18X4t]{Steading} and @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.pEg9yxklAGARjf2Q]{Gleaning}. Luxarum is also known as the Golden Realm, because (unlike the furtive shadows of Signara or the soft red glimmer of Primordis) Luxarum glows with an intense golden light in the night sky, and is quite visible with the naked eye even when obscured by clouds. Mortals generally have little knowledge of Luxarum itself other than the realm's importance in the cosmological order.
Luxarum.scoverview: Since Creation, Luxarum has been considered a brilliant realm of eternal summer — an otherworldly place full of hope, light, and beauty. In reality, it is a realm of constant warfare, where ceaseless battles rage on ferociously, viciously, and without pause. Mortals who traverse Luxarum often become forcibly recruited for the Inner Realm's eternal wars waged by its formidable inhabitants, the zealous Tyraphem — powerful entities who glorify Lantyr and preside over countless fanatical servants known as Celestials, which comprise each Tyraphem's uncanny legion of soliders.
Luxarum.sgamemaster:
Luxarum is a realm of war, destruction, and unending brutality. Unimaginable clashes between armies numbering in the tens of thousands smash into one another day and night. Massive sieges and intense skirmishes are commonplace as the various @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} Lords battle one another in complex struggles for dominance. Tyraphem are the powerful beings that originated on Luxarum and rule over it, claiming numerous domains and petty states. Tyraphem are incredibly numerous, numbering in the millions, and new Tyraphem are born or created in never-ending cycles to fuel the war effort. Its thought that the Tyraphem were the greatest combined force in the Cosmos and would be able to defeat any other group or force with relative ease. This is partly due to their number, which dwarfs beings like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia}, who number in the hundreds or the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos} of which there are sixteen, or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods}, who also number in the hundreds. Tyraphem are innately talented combatants and some of the best tacticians in the Cosmos. Unfortunately, Tyraphem are petty, selfish, and blinded by a twisted faith in Lantyr and have little (if any) interest in helping other beings, each other, or, least of all, mortals, who they generally consider to be cattle at best. Tyraphem Lords are a title, for those Tyraphem old enough and experienced enough to claim dominion over others of their kind.

While the Tyraphem are extremely numerous, there are many other creatures on Luxarum known as Celestials. Many serve in support roles in the constant battles, but some are equally aggressive and warlike in nature. These creatures and beings are treated poorly by the Tyraphem and are merely tools but some are powerful enough to survive in the wilderness between the battlefields and engagements, and the Tyraphem often try to capture them to use as mounts or as part of war engines. Celestials are native to Luxarum, but a mortal can also become one. Becoming a Celestial is relatively easy, if a mortal soul swears to fight for a Tyraphem Lord then upon their death they are reborn as a Celestial. Celestials vary significantly in appearance, but almost all are made up of strange, dull metallic crystal much like the Tyraphem themselves.

The motivations and goals of various Tyraphem Lords are often surprisingly simple yet convoluted simultaneously as they seek to rule over all of Luxarum. This has never happened before, but they all strive for it regardless. For lesser Tyraphem they seek to become Lords themselves and then rule over all of Luxarum. Such a committed and dedicated belief in their manifest destiny to rule is due to their deep and ingrained religious fervor. All Tyraphem worship @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}, in a fanatical unyielding way that leaves no room for doubt or questions. It would be considered very unwise to mention to a Tyraphem that Lantyr herself has been disgusted by their behavior and actions since Creation, but the Tyraphem are so blinded by their faith and their own representation of what Lantyr is and wants that they ignore everything else.

Flora & Fauna

Luxarum has a hardy yet fast-growing flora, primarily grasses and small bushes that scatter the wide-ranging fields, hills, and inclines. Its golden-shining grasses cover the battlefields and glow softly during the long nights, bathing the realm in eternal light. There are a few scattered groves of thorny gnarled trees, but these are often guarded, revered, and maintained carefully by the Tyraphem, who value the incredible strength and magical qualities the wood offers. Underneath the seemingly endless grasslands lie mountains of bodies and corpses and a virulent and complex system of fungi that feeds upon it all. There are even said to be caves, caverns, and entire tunnel systems cutting through the overwhelming amount of bodies

Notable Locations

Luxarum is a realm of endless destruction, where its settlements are constantly under attack and then frantically repaired and reinforced daily. Its battlefields are thick with the corpses of the dead, and there are scattered decaying weapons and broken engines of war lying in mounds across its entire surface. Between the fields of death and glory are rearing fortifications surrounding bustling settlements of activity. The hammering of weapons and armor is constant, as are the battle hymns and prayers for victory, faith in Lantyr, and glory unending. During the Abyssal Shear, forces from beyond attacked Luxarum and claimed a small section facing Signara. While the attack devastated the realm, this was nothing new to the Tyraphem, and they ignored the blasted, corrupted areas after annihilating the Abyssal entities in a remarkable yet brief realm-wide ceasefire.

  • Taryakel’s Seat. One of the most powerful Tyraphem Lords in the Cosmos, Taryakel is rare among the Tyraphem and claims to be as ancient as Luxarum itself.

  • Halls of Faith. A vast series of halls and chambers situated within the ring of mountains surrounding the center of Luxarum. Various Tyraphem and Celestials travel here on pilgrimages to test their faith in cosmic trials.

  • Temple of Radiance. A forlorn structure that stands on the edge of Luxarum facing Primordis, its towering spires are silent and the Tyraphem believe it is a cursed, unholy temple to some long-lost forgotten deity.

  • Tyraranis Excantor. A massive machine of war that moves across the battlefields of Luxarum, some say it has a mind of its own and uses the corpses and armor it moves over to fuel its very being.

  • Palace of Eternity. At the center of Luxarum is a colossal palace structure surrounding a deep opening. Within resides a massive ball of light and energy that the Tyraphem believe was once a gift from Lantyr.

  • Castillian’s Redoubt. Unlike most Tyraphem Lords, the Castillian Juriel attempted to broker a lasting peace, which led to a massive attack on his Redoubt, which has continued for nearly a thousand years.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Aburyx}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2NXPu79uxzDh1Z0x]{Juriel}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.illZO15u6gbz338u]{Pyix}

  • @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{Skither}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.XXyU4kvrBPceEoz2]{Taryakel}

  • @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR]{Vorg}

Signara.name: Signara
Signara.text:
• Keywords: Science, Technology, Darkness

  • Ideal: Curiosity

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: Realm of Ferocious Curiosity, The Endless Dark

Signara is an incredibly unpredictable place for a mortal from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}. It is the realm of ancient fundamental ideas and concepts made manifest by only a suggestion of tangible reality. A mortal's mind can quickly become shredded if they interact with something they shouldn't have. Like the other Inner Realms of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, Signara is the pinnacle of an otherworldly realm. Fortunately, it lies so far from the World of Ember that it has remained isolated and mysterious throughout every age of the Cosmos, and mortal visitors or explorers are practically unheard of. Mortals have a clear understanding of the role that Signara plays in the yearly calendar, long ago associating its passage in the sky as the marker for the colder months of the year. Signara is often called the Dark Realm as, unlike Luxarum, which shines brightly, and Primordis, which glimmers softly in the skies above, Signara is frequently lost amid the darkness of the Sea of Stars. Even during the months of@UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.MEfKfW6rZMdpFhwf]{Withering} and the@UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.qwv1GJoa18AnS05c]{Stilling}, its light is barely visible to the naked eye.

Mortals have little knowledge of Signara itself other than its importance in the cosmological order. They do, however understand and are aware of Fiends and their nature to entrap and sign pacts with mortals in exchange for their souls. As a result, Signara has the worst reputation among the Inner Realms, seen as both a dark and evil place and a place where evil creatures come from. Signara and Fiends are often the villains in countless tales and myths, even though many Fiends have noble — or at least neutral — intentions and simply adhere to the ideas of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7#eternal-souls]{Eternal Soul}.
Signara.scoverview: The azure, ethereal, and otherworldly realm of Signara is both intensely beautiful and incredibly disorienting to outsiders bold enough to navigate its eternally-feuding factions. It is a place governed by laws of nature fundamentally different to those of Ember, blending incomprehensible arcana with esoteric science. The inscrutable language of Signarans was formed over eons and is impossible for most mortals to comprehend. Magical experiments run wild throughout Signara's dark and twisting laboratories and workshops, fueling the subtle and complex feuds between the incredibly powerful Daemos and their eternally-bound retainers, the Fiends.
Signara.sgamemaster:
Signara is an extraordinary and yet inexplicable place for a mortal. It is a realm of disorienting natural laws that defy deeply held conventions and ideas taken as universal on the World of Ember. Some say it was where the first concepts of words and song originated during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.0bkmoi8aSFvbaCi0]{Creation}, and language is a fundamental part of Signarans' daily life. The spoken and written word is a complex basis of every interaction, but it uses an almost indescribable amount of complexity with runic symbols and terms that take countless years to learn. Almost every creature on Signara is a Fiend, engaging in thousand-year feuds among various factions in strange word-driven or song-infused confrontations that are so complex that violence is only a small part of how you succeed or claim victory. Most Fiends are servants of the powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos}, but there are independent factions that act in their own interests. Signara is not an evil place, however, and the culture is far more neutral or balanced overall, with some Fiends caring deeply about each other, their work, and even mortals. In contrast, others are dismissive, rude, or actively hostile and cruel.

The original inhabitants of Signara and its principal rulers are the sixteen @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos}. Each is a powerful being that has existed since Creation, with more power than that held by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods}. They are somewhat akin to deities, but functionally, they do not involve themselves very often, if at all, with the surface World of Ember and personally care very little for mortals in most cases. Daemos are unrelenting in their curiosity and have been studying and attempting to master the cosmos since they arose; their desires and motivations to learn about specific avenues of science, technology, and how the cosmos functions has led to some dangerous and often catastrophic experiments. One of the Daemos is said to have created Fiends at some point not long after Creation which led to the majority of the other Daemos following suit and creating their own Fiendish servants. The most defining characteristic of both the Daemos and Fiends are multiple arms and long, thin horns and tails, this is thought to originate from the Daemos themselves and are traits that the mortal Signborn found on the World of Ember inherited as well.

Fiends are creatures that live upon Signara, but they are incredibly varied in overall appearance, with some taking on humanoid shapes while others are more bestial. Some are incredibly ancient, while others have been created more recently from mortal Souls. Darkness Magic originates from Signara, but it's often called either Pact Magic or Rune Magic. Its principal users, the Daemos and their servants, the Fiends, write words and runes in the air to create powerful magical effects. The most common usage of Pact Magic is the ability to form contracts with mortals. Fiends do this to safeguard a mortal soul and turn them into a fiend, following the ideas of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7#eternal-souls]{Eternal Soul}.

Flora & Fauna

Signara is home to some of the most bewildering and strange flora and objects in the cosmos. In many respects, everything on Signara is a raw, unrefined idea with a thin veneer of mass and structure. The waters glow a brilliant crystalline blue and, when drunk, give mortals intense visions of connections forming between fundamental aspects of magic, or they may envision a single drop of water falling into an ocean over thousands of years. Some of its flora include glimmering delicate stalks and grasses made of blue and purple magic, which, when brushed against, convey meanings, concepts, or ideas. Many different types of larger bushes and trees contain the essence of a single word, often murmuring in the wind in a soft, endless song.

Notable Locations

Signara is a huge primordial realm containing testing grounds, colossal experiments, magical darkness, and dark strongholds inhabited by countless Fiends. The events of the Abyssal Shear smashed apart much of the realm facing Luxarum, and the Abyssal influence in Signara remains high and constant. Unfortunately, the Daemos are slaves to their nature and cannot help but try to understand and study the Abyss in secret, which continues to permeate the very danger they are seeking to destroy.

  • Infinite Workshop. Beneath Signara is said to lie the Infinite Workshop, a complex somehow larger than the realm above, containing hidden rooms filled with constructs, machines, and experiments with various sections owned by different Daemos.

  • Oar’arc Hollow. The home of Nalgomith and his small cohort of Fiendish retainers.

  • Cerulean Vats. A complex of interconnected pipes, containers and vats filled with Fiendish ichor that is overrun by strange oozes and slimes.

  • The Rune Fields. The Rune Fields of Signara are said to be the birthplace of the Daemos. The original language and writing of Signara stretches across miles and can be seen from the surface of the World of Ember with telescopes.

  • Halls of Steam. An ancient museum containing ancient machines.

  • Lortea’s Whirlwind. A massive eternal experiment of unknown purpose and designs that sweeps across the surface of Signara at random, said to be millions of years old.

  • Libarrus, The Black Spire. A vast structure at the center of Signara that contains all the knowledge of Creation. Unfortunately, it is entirely overrun by Fiends from various antagonist factions, and the twisting, ever-changing corridors are a constant battlefield.

Known Entities

  • @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK]{Jahud}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.aTy7db5ZGUnNDVL4]{Kerastes}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.3ZDcyUW0ydYE84rj]{Nalgomith}

  • Shimatrix

Pathways.name: Pathways
