Pathways.scoverview: Beneath the surface of the World of Ember lies the Pathways, the colossal underground passages, tunnels, and caverns that crisscross, intertwine and weave throughout the world. Some are vast open spaces, filled with curious and otherworldly life, while many are filled with streaming currents of magma, water, or gas that flow from the Heart of Ember to the very edges of the world and back again. The Pathways are largely unexplored, and very few mortals attempt to descend to its depths; they can be extremely dangerous and full of ancient hidden dangers in addition to hostile and deadly environments.
Pathways.sgamemaster:
• Keywords: Underground, Caverns, Tunnels

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: World Arteries, Earthway, Paths, World Below

The Pathways are as old as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} itself, forming alongside the world during Creation. What makes the Pathways so interesting is that when taken as a whole, they are not merely natural or random tunnels but seem to be carefully designed in a complex pattern that is nearly impossible to understand fully. The Heart of Ember's influence over the structure of the World and Pathways is unmistakable. If the entire Pathways could be viewed at once and mapped accurately, it would almost act like a biological breathing or nervous system. While many of the paths are filled with flowing rivers of magma, water, gas, or other rarer elements, many are also empty and contain strange lifeforms and complex environments. Even more remarkably, entire sections of this epic subterranean expanse were created by unknown means and powers, forming vast structures and designs that twist their way through the world.

Despite the massive amounts of magma and the age of the World, the Pathways are not overwhelmingly hot; in fact, the temperature is relatively stable in most areas. The heat is somehow expelled out into the Sea of Stars instead and is mainly responsible for the pleasant conditions across the cosmos, in addition to the warming light of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}. Even the Pathways full of water act in strange, unconventional, and confusing ways. Water flows through the Pathways at slightly colder temperatures and emerges from underwater vents in the deep oceans barely above freezing. Given the amount of water involved, it's currently unknown how this is even remotely possible.

Entrances down into habitable sections of the Pathways are very rare, and traveling or even falling down into the immense depths is often considered a death sentence. There are a few famous examples of mapped sections. However, one is the Gallery of Blood in the Kelmezian Great City of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.HN2Zimps4w5XniZe]{Old Carinth} but comparatively few mortals have journeyed into the depths and survived to tell the tale.

The Heart Chamber

One of the most important parts of the Pathways is the legendary Heart Chamber, which contains the Heart of Ember. The Heart Chamber is a cavernous area that is so large it has its own oceans and underground weather system and sky. The pressure, energy, and magic emitted by the Heart make this chamber incredibly dangerous and deadly, to the extent that mortals would likely be killed instantly by fierce and unconfined energy. Even powerful beings like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} would find the experience challenging. The various elements like magma and water that flow throughout the Pathways all lead back to the Heart Chamber, though this process can be extremely long, in some cases taking hundreds if not thousands of years. Elements then travel outwards to the world's edges and back through the unstable passageways, creating a continuous cycle which is one of the ways in which the oceans refill themselves.

Dissecting the Heart Chamber is the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.cBBj0IFFc7BhtphK#gravitational-line]{Gravitational Line}, a strange force that fluctuates in its positioning but is responsible for the Gravity exerted upon the entire world. Passing through the Heart Chamber would not necessarily mean that you would be crushed by the forces involved either, and you may even experience complete weightlessness. The Line does seem to be emitted by the Heart of Ember in some way, but its effect is not consistent over large periods of time; during the Age of Sunlight, for some unknown reason, Gravity across the entire world was slightly less than today.

The Abyss.name: The Abyss
The Abyss.scoverview: The Abyss is a term that fills the mind with a sense of dread. Its existence is not something any mortal on Ember should be familiar with, and knowledge of even the word itself is exceptionally perilous. Any contact with Abyssal energies should be treated as an existential threat, and if possible, try to inform a nearby Shard God about the location or energy uncovered. In extremely rare situations, some mortals claim to be born without attunement to one of the Elemental Moons, though they often do not understand what this means. They may, horrifically, be influenced by the Abyss and lead lives of incredible suffering.
The Abyss.sgamemaster:
• Keywords: Malignant, Evil, Alien

  • Ideal: Nihilism

  • Age: Unknown

  • Other Names: The Shroud, Far Outside

WARNING

References to the Abyss, the Abyssal Shear, Abyssal Horrors, Outer Gods etc are not things that the player characters would learn about before gameplay begins unless under very specific circumstances for background purposes.

The following information is highly sensitive and should not be read or shared except under extreme circumstances. Mortals and the vast majority of immortals including most Shard Gods have no knowledge of the Abyss and learning names, concepts or ideas causes significant mental stress and can damage a person's mind.

The Abyss exists outside of the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} beyond the barrier of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{The Weave}. It is outside the reality exerted by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} and the cosmological forces that form the underlying existence that we understand. Gravity, electromagnetic forces, or Ember's many different types of magic either function in odd, often explosive and destructive ways or do not work at all. Understanding the Abyss is impossible; it is not a place of logic, rules, and laws, and to try is to invite madness, death, and destruction. Not only is its nature alien to all concepts mortals and beings of Ember recognize, but it is said to be an infinite realm without borders, barriers, edges, or an end containing eldritch and alien creatures of terrible power and merely learning of its existence can be a corrupting influence that drives mortals insane.

Despite the incredible dangers that surround even the knowledge of the Abyss, it can be a source of power for the foolish mortals upon the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}, the kind of power that comes at a terrible price. Abyssal Energy or Abyssal Magic is a very different kind of power. It is inherently malignant and destructive, insidious and tempting to use again and again by those exposed to its whispering intrusions. It is a twisted kind of magic that warps the user — even when used unwittingly or without restraint or simply for long enough, it will eat away at their logic and restraint until they're essentially just mindless conduits of the raw power of the Abyss. During the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear} the most dangerous effect on the Cosmos was the spreading corruption that at first exploded out of control, ripping through entire nations or bastions of strength from within. For example, the effect on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen} to this day has been cataclysmic, turning almost an entire realm into a charred, horrific landscape and corrupting one of its @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Tl4gvmUGThkZdrUd]{Elemental Sovereigns} so utterly they now burn with an unquenchable rage and hatred for all life.

Combating the Abyss is something that almost all within the Ember Cosmos seem to understand, and it is something that, strangely, one of the youngest ancestries on Ember, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Humanity} is uniquely good at. Not only are they particularly sensitive to Abyssal influence, but they are even somewhat resistant to it. Generally, though, mortals cannot combat the Abyss directly, and while they may be able to stop or even destroy weaker entities the Abyss is a relentlessly corrupting and malignant force, and so the threat of spreading and continuing to corrupt people and things after the fact is very high. During the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} and even@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{ Elder Gods} fought directly as an almost unified force to protect the Cosmos. Many were killed, but some unlocked strange anti-Abyssal abilities that helped them fight back with greater ferocity and power, discovering that the Lifeforce that imbues Shard Gods is an opposing power to Abyssal Energy. To this day, the deities of Ember are incredibly wary of Abyssal Energy and influence, and it is the one thing that will force them to band together even with hated rivals to confront and destroy.

In [Redacted], I made the greatest, most foolish decision of my life: I entered the [Erased]. Words cannot accurately portray the terrifying feelings of despair, overwhelming destruction, and mental anguish that I experienced. So utterly alien and vast was the power that assaulted my senses and strained my sanity to its very edges. I spent only [Redacted], but upon returning to the [Erased], close to a year had passed, and the effect on my mind took nearly a century to recover from. Today, I am thankful for my mind's ability to compartmentalize information. Still, even the knowledge that I could recall from my journey if so needed or required, makes me shudder with fear.

[Redacted], The Shroud of Madness; Laeora [erased].

Entities of Evil

While Abyssal Energy and its effects and even the mere existence of the Abyss is bad enough, it is also home to terrifying eldritch and alien beings that are twisted, horrific and abhorrent to the Ember Cosmos. At the pinnacle of power within the Abyss lie the entities commonly referred to as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.hq1cXdVHjFbQxfys]{Outer Gods}, beings of such unfathomable destructive power that they create, distort, or remake reality within the Abyss on a whim. Every single Outer God is vastly more powerful than the gods of Ember, and while more detail on the Outer Gods is unfortunately covered in other pages, the most important thing to note regarding their existence is that their hatred for the Ember Cosmos is absolute. Attracting their attention not only invokes calamity but presents a singular and terrible threat to the entire Cosmos.

The only good thing I'm aware of regarding the Outer God's nature is that they are so alien that they are unable to focus on Ember, and their attention slips away before they can direct their true power at destroying us.

Even though the Outer Gods may often be distracted, they have plenty of terrible servants; among them are their Heralds, who are said to be on par with the Elder Gods of Ember. During the Abyssal Shear, only one entered the Cosmos directly and was destroyed personally by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, who was the only one who could damage it. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors} are the foot soldiers of the Outer Gods, and these invaded the Cosmos in great numbers during the Abyssal Shear; many were killed but not before inflicting monumental damage and destruction, destroying entire societies and civilizations like the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{ Shent}. Since then, the few survivors have hidden in dark places of the Cosmos, attempting to bring about destruction and chaos or another Abyssal Shear. In terms of power, most Abyssal Horrors are more powerful than Shard Gods one-on-one. More recently, the emergence of an Abyssal Horror caused @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.Q59ZUVNaeBoZl9nJ]{the Evernight}, dooming the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moirans} to undeath and ripping apart an entire realm. There are smaller, weaker servants of the Outer Gods as well, or beings that slipped into the Ember Cosmos during the Abyssal Shear. Creatures like the Whisperers are far less destructive and psychically powerful but perhaps even more dangerous due to their ability to control, corrupt, and take over the minds of mortals.

Abyssal Corruption

Entities from the Abyss, such as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors}, are beings formed out of the Abyss itself and are in many ways antithetical to Ember Lifeforms; this means they are not part of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} and do not have souls. When significantly damaged, however, they can be killed and destroyed like Ember Lifeforms, but unfortunately, this is not the end of their existence. Upon death, several things can happen; the first is that the Abyssal monster dissolves into Abyssal Energy, which then soaks into the earth, rock, plants, and creatures around it, transforming them into monsters. Abyssal corruption is a terrifying transformation that can happen rapidly or extremely slowly, but it alters physical or biological forms, twisting them into foul and abhorrent abominations. If they are a sapient ancestry or creature, the mind is broken and distorted, aligning their thoughts with destruction, chaos, and death. Because of this, Abyssal Corruption can spread over and over again; as mortals or beings kill Abyssal entities, it creates new monsters which, when killed, leave more minor but still potentially deadly and dangerous corruption behind as they dissolve, repeating the cycle.

Although spreading corruption is one consequence of an Abyssal entity or monster's death, the other is perhaps even more horrifying, as the being might refuse to disperse. This can lead to the formation of a concentrated Abyssal Nexus, which efficiently collects the power of the slain monster into a small, extremely durable object that is nearly impossible to destroy. This Abyssal Nexus can then be transported to distant locations. Over time, it will slowly seep Abyssal Corruption into the surrounding area, potentially over hundreds of years. While it may not pose an immediate threat, this subtle corruption can cause the destruction of entire families, settlements, or even nations.

Abyssal corruption itself is almost impossible to remove or destroy once it's diffused into objects or creatures. The only known remedy is [Erased]

The Weave.name: The Weave
The Weave.text:
• Keywords: Barrier, Shield

  • Age: Millions of Years

  • Other Names: Woven Barrier, Shield of the Cosmos

The Weave is a distant field of energy that encases the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} of Ember in a protective bubble. Among the peoples of Ember, where magical, mystical, and more obvious cosmological forces affect them daily, it typically ranks lower on the list of importance. Despite this, most mortals are aware of its existence to some degree and have a variety of beliefs about its purpose as a barrier, a structure that holds the stars in place, or as simply the edge of the Cosmos. Its distant glimmering purple and blue mesh-like structure and light are often particularly clear on cloudless nights, and add to the breathtaking majesty of Ember skies. Some groups, however, do give the Weave much greater respect, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}, who both venerate the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Goddess} they call @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{Ven'avé} and study, record, and use the power of stars and the Weave for spells and a distinct type of magic.

The three Inner Realms of the Cosmos, @UUID[.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, @UUID[.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} and @UUID[.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} all rest upon the surface of the Weave and drift slowly across its surface. These realms are vast and comparable in size to the surface @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}. As such, they are extremely visible despite the distance, and mortals on Ember are aware of the distinct difference between the Inner Realms and Moons. One of the most essential functions of the Inner Realms that mortals have discovered is that they are seemingly responsible for the seasons and, as such, are often venerated for their power. Strangely, most people are warier of the Inner Realms for historical reasons or some innate sense that they are particularly strange and distant forces that are perhaps best left alone.
The Weave.scoverview: The Weave is a breathtaking wonder of power, purpose, and protection created during the expansion of the Ember Cosmos itself. It surrounds the entire Ember Cosmos with a mystical barrier that appears to be a perfectly rounded bubble. The Weave can be easily seen at night from the World of Ember, softly glimmering with purple and blue lattice lines like a colossal woven cloth. Many of the world's cultures revere and venerate its power, believing fate and prophecy are entwined into its very nature.
The Weave.sgamemaster:
Approaching the Weave by traveling through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars} reveals a glowing lattice of purple and blue lines of mystical energy emerging from a background of a purest black void. At intervals of several hundred or even thousands of miles, static Stars are embedded into the lattice, shining brilliantly with red, white, yellow, or blue energy. These stars are the static kind and have not moved since @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.0bkmoi8aSFvbaCi0]{the First Dawn}. Though in extremely rare circumstances, stars will burn out and disappear, no one is sure why this occurs. Stars are curious entities in the Cosmos as they exist in large quantities but have little if any obvious effects on the cosmos and have puzzled scholars for untold ages. However, these bright spots of strange matter and energy did lead to the development of Star Theurgy by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}. They use the power of Stars to cast spells and study fate, though their practices are as convoluted and mysterious as the Weave itself.

The Weave was said to be explosively created during the process of the First Dawn, expanding outwards at speeds that defy belief. It formed the barrier around the Cosmos incredibly quickly in order to protect the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} and what lay within from the powers of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{the Abyss}. Without its protection, the alien energies of the Abyss would bleed through into the Sea of Stars and spread out to corrupt the Cosmos, causing untold destruction. The Weave was devastatingly breached during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}but reformed and healed quickly, continuing to provide a complete barrier against the Abyss that remains in place in the present. Since that time, the Star Mages of Rhivan now hold an even greater responsibility and have charged themselves with protecting the Weave to ensure a breach never happens again.

Sea of Stars.name: Sea of Stars
Sea of Stars.scoverview: The Sea of Stars is the name for the vast and mostly empty space between the World of Ember and the protective barrier known as the Weave. Lantyr, the Elemental Moons, the three Inner Realms, various objects, ruins, and Stars float, orbit and move through its Ethereal Currents. The peoples of Ember use the term Sea of Stars to explain the motion and movement of objects they can see in the sky, and the belief that the Sea of Stars acts like a celestial ocean is actually not far from the truth.
Sea of Stars.sgamemaster:
• Keywords: Space, Ethereal

  • Age: Millions of Years

  • Other Names: The Great Sea, The Ether, Ethereal Ocean

The Sea of Stars is not an empty void or vacuum, and although it is mostly empty, it contains a host of matter, energy, magic, and heat. The air within the Sea of Stars is thin, but mortals on Ember would find the environment merely challenging rather than deadly and could comfortably travel its vast depths with some preparation. In addition, it contains near-invisible currents of energy and raw magic that flow from and around the larger cosmological bodies like the World, the Moons, and the Inner Realms. These Ethereal Currents are the true danger of the Sea of Stars and can be treacherous to navigate accurately as they are both colossal in size and extremely powerful. Once caught up in a current without the means to control your movement, you may find yourself slammed into a moon, the Weave or Lantyr herself at tremendous speeds.

The massive objects and realms of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, such as the Moons, move through the Sea of Stars, orbiting the World of Ember in complex patterns. The Sun rotates around the world in a single day, or 24 hours, with the 12 hours where the Sun is visible from the surface considered the day and the time when it passes below the horizon starting the night. This is flipped for the undersurface of the world. This is the most predictable of the objects that float through the Sea of Stars, and most of the other elements have changed their orbits throughout history or have been affected by events in various ways. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, known as the Shattered Moon was thrown out of its orbit and is now much closer to the World of Ember after the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}.

During the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.0bkmoi8aSFvbaCi0]{the First Dawn}, the mystical barrier known as the Weave captured many objects, materials, and elements that were present within @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{the Abyss}. Despite the Abyss being a realm of unknown and alien energies, for some reason, the maliciousness did not persist within the growing Ember Cosmos or, even more curiously, may not have been present at all during the First Dawn. Some objects have been discovered in the ages since, and remain complete anomalies, seemingly neither Abyssal nor created by Ember. One such object is @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.qkFDffiLfGCd0RCs]{The Sphere}.

Wandering Objects

There are two kinds of Stars within the Ember Cosmos, the static and unchanging kind that are held in place by the energies of the Weave and also the roaming, orbiting Stars that wander randomly or orbit the world like the Moons. Static Stars have been present during the First Dawn, and may indeed have been formed upon the Weave as it expanded, whereas roaming Stars tend to be much younger. Stars themselves are very mysterious in nature and what they are made of and how they function within the Cosmos is a hotly debated topic. They give out very subtle and distinct magical energy that is difficult for most mortals to use, but some mages and wizards can tap into it for divination purposes. Both kinds of Stars are used and studied using the practice of Star Theurgy by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}.

Smaller elements such as asteroids, comets, and dust that drift across the Cosmos are either ancient, dating back to the First Dawn, or they were created more recently from places like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora} which sometimes displaces its mass. Beings such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} or even a few @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} have also been known to construct objects or places of power that drift across the Sea of Stars. Since the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, numerous pieces of the Sun Tower, both larger chunks containing entire sections and smaller debris drift aimlessly or are caught in the orbit of either the world itself or the Moons. Some of these pieces are also lodged into the surface of the Weave and although they did not contain enough energy at the moment of impact to breach the barrier, they do allow elements of the Abyss to latch on and pass through into the Ember Cosmos. This makes such places extremely dangerous where distortions of reality occur, twisting or reshaping natural laws and swallowing nearby Stars and other elements.

World of Ember.name: World of Ember
World of Ember.text:
• Keywords: World

  • Age: Countless Ages

  • Other Names: The World, Ember, The Surface

Most mortals today who live upon the surface World of Ember live in relative ignorance and have little regard nor concern for larger cosmological questions or problems. The fact that the World they live upon is considered the largest, most auspicious, and important realm in the Cosmos is of no consequence. It's a fair outlook; the scale of such things is beyond the farmer trying to make ends meet by selling their harvests in the nearby town each fall or even ambitious leaders looking to expand their influence and power. Every Mortal on Ember is affected in various ways by the world's strange nature, but more often than not, people tend to consider such things the work of gods, monsters, or, more simply, the way it has always been.

While the distant Inner Realms have a comparative surface size, the traversable and habitable landmass of Ember exceeds that of any other body within @UUID[.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{the Weave}. Especially when considering the size and scale of the @UUID[.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}, not to mention the mythical "undersurface" a place just as large and diverse as the surface itself. No living Mortal has traveled to the undersurface, and it remains one of the most obscure and mysterious realms by being cut off from people's cosmological viewpoint in the skies. Mortals have more knowledge of the Moons and even the Inner Realms than the collosal twin realm that they share a celestial body with.

The Broken Tower

The largest Structure on the surface of Ember is the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.XXMizY6WTIsL0swx]{Broken Tower}. Once called the Sun Tower before the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}, it is now a titanic gleaming reminder of the cataclysmic destruction wrought upon both the World of Ember and the Cosmos. The exact nature of the Shattering (precisely what caused the upper two-thirds of the tower to explode with such overwhelming intensity) remains unknown — a prevailing mystery that many say is best left alone. Nevertheless, countless theories, myths, and legends pervade places like Ember's libraries, academies, and taverns; but these tales are so widespread and fanciful, most scholars and sages consider the very pursuit of them to be a fool's errand.

The size of the Broken Tower is not simply impressive, it's utterly breathtaking (even with most of the structure missing and scattered across the planet). It is not only visible from every corner of the surface, the ruined structure is so vast that it often dominates the horizon, casting deep shadows across the entire continent of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Op5BD9XSlmb7l6NN]{Starshield} during dusk and dawn. Due to the cataclysmic nature of the Shattering, the presence of such a structure on the horizon is an often painful reminder of the chaos and destruction of that time — a deep wound that many cultures and peoples still struggle with. The tower is not entirely static either; massive chunks of debris still orbit the tower's apex, hinting at the extreme magical forces that remain active and almost all mortals on Ember consider the Broken Tower to be cursed in some way or another.

Geography

If you were able to view the World of Ember from a great distance, i.e., from one of the Elemental Moons, it would look strangely squat, like a stocky disc with a large flat surface with a few odd protruding spikes of land extending from the disc into the Sea of Stars. From such a viewpoint, the surface would be relatively smooth and flat, with a massive connecting ocean surrounding eight primary continents. At the center of the world's surface is the Starshield, a central continent upon which the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} built their empire and the Sun Tower during the Age of Sunlight.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Op5BD9XSlmb7l6NN]{The Starshield} is one of the smallest continents positioned at the exact center of Ember's surface with eight points that follow the same rough alignment of the world itself. The Starshield was once the center of everything, where the Aedir built their empire thousands of years ago and built their crowing achievement, the Sun Tower.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica} is the largest continent on the surface, often called the Shardstone Continent; it is both the largest and the most storied in its history and peoples. Home to no less than five subcontinents, one of which is the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.NdqwtFoFAw85Gstr]{Aran Penisula}, which gave rise to the ancient Jarn, the precursor ancestry. Aterica also has a veritable wealth of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} that have found and communed with @UUID[.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystals}, and there are so many separate cultures and realms that currently, no less than six different entire pantheons exist at once.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia} is the only continent deeply connected to Aterica, with burdening trade routes, diplomatic ties, and a history of shared struggles. Kessia was once said to be home to the largest Aedir colonies, but they were completely annihilated during the Shattering. Within the heart of the continent, the great Obsidian Desert formed and spread to cover the vast majority of its landmass. . The Shadiel sub-continent, home to the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy} of the Rhivan, is considered a part of Kessia in some circles, though it remains an extremely distant and far away realm.

  • Across the vast Reaver Ocean lies @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Rn0WQchGPVYCTExP]{Mort'oliss}, often called The Spiritlands; it is a continent realm presided over by the Elder God Sockets and where the Souls of Mortal peoples travel to when they die. The Spiritlands are not connected physically to any other continent, as they are separated by a barrier that supposedly prevents the living from crossing over, not to mention no one is particularly keen to visit the realm of the dead.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.dm5FW6EbHBGhJweI]{Jurin} is an ancient and untamed continent as far away from Atercia as is possible on the surface world. Very little is known about its nature, except many Thornlings tell a surprisingly consistent myth surrounding their origins and a towering ancestry of peoples that hunt and kill Leviathans upon the distant continent..

  • Jekaros is spoken of in hushed tones as the "Cursed Continent," a place so reviled that most people of Ember don't speak of it at all. Much like the Spiritlands, Jekaros is a metaphysical place that you can physically travel to; but unlike the Spiritlands, the Cursed Continent is considered to be a realm of such fear and terror that no one dares disturb it.

  • Atuo is one of the most mysterious places on the surface, surrounded by powerful esoteric energies, hidden from view by swirling blue mists; even powerful scrying magic fails to penetrate far. Some of the most powerful entities in the cosmos, including deities, have been repelled by its power.

Forces Unknown

Mortals of Ember tend to live their relatively short lives completely absorbed by personal issues and matters of local import. To a large extent, most of the grander forces and concepts of the Cosmos remain unknown to them, and the realms that contain the people of Ember are far, far stranger than they actually know. Various cosmological forces, magical effects, and metaphysical energies affect mortals on a daily basis, and their lives are governed by a cosmic balance that's enforced and upheld by cornerstones of immeasurable power: six elemental moons drift across the sky in complex patterns and orbits, the Inner Realms create the world's seasons as they wander slowly across the glimmering weave of Stars, the Broken Tower serves as a constant reminder of the scale and majesty of what can be achieved, and even the gods themselves walk among mortal beings … Many of these forces may seem disjointed or chaotic when viewed separately, but when combined (and a broader view of the Cosmos as a whole is considered), there appears to be an overarching balance to all things.

Some believe this balance is a grand design or purpose enforced by the Heart of Ember, and many consider the world itself to be “alive.” The world contains a heart and a complex system of lava, water, and gaseous arteries that flow and breathe like a living being. There is even a limb-like geography and structure to the world that flows outwards from the center like spokes on a wheel. The world's edges are particularly fascinating, where the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.cBBj0IFFc7BhtphK#gravitational-line]{Gravitational Line} emitted by the Heart of Ember starts to break down and dissipate unpredictably, suggesting the concept of Gravity itself is not a force but rather something maintained.
World of Ember.scoverview: Sitting immobile at the center of the Cosmos is the World of Ember, a colossal realm of rocky earth, oceans, and life that surrounds the Heart of Ember. It is mainly referred to as simply the world, the surface, or even simply as Ember itself. Throughout the ages of the Cosmos, the World of Ember has always hosted the largest number of diverse and divergent forms of life, from the smallest creatures to massive earth-shattering Leviathans that stalk across the lands and waters. Its environments and realms, from towering mountains, deep forests, and wind-swept barrens, are ancient, awe-inspiring, and formidable; it is a place of unparalleled beauty and wonder.
World of Ember.sgamemaster:
History

Much of the History of the World of Ember is covered in other pages, but given the extreme scale of the time periods involved, one of the most notable things about the World today is how truly ancient some things are. Mortals today believe that they are inventing, progressing, and experiencing the world in new ways, and while sometimes that may be true, they live upon the countless bones, kingdoms, and empires of cultures long turned to dust. A prime example of this unfathomable scale is the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} culture, a people who have maintained a relatively consistent cultural base for hundreds of thousands of years, a feat that defies comprehension.

Ancient in Ember is relative. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} — who were destroyed by the Shattering two and a half thousand years ago — are considered by most to be ancient, despite the fact that the Aedir arose tens of thousands of years prior and endured seismic cultural changes with distinct periods of growth, collapse, and reorganization. In fact, the term Empire was only used to describe the culture around four thousand years ago. Before that, it was considered to be more of a Theocratic Dynasty.

Ultimately, the truth of things has been largely lost, remembered by a scant few via unreliable myths, tales, and legends told around Ember's campfires. Despite the lack of knowledge surrounding the history of the World, the evidence of ancient peoples remains omnipresent, in ancient structures and places of power. Upon the World of Ember, ancient cities or dungeons could be Aedir, in which case they are thousands of years old, or they could be far, far older and date back hundreds of thousands of years to primordial cultures that no longer have names. This is all to say that the scale of the world is geographically vast, but so is its history, and so much is lost, forgotten, and unknown in the present age of the world.

Heart of Ember.name: Heart of Ember
Heart of Ember.text:
• Keywords: Life

  • Ideal: Creation, Vitality, Hope

  • Age: Unknown

  • Other Names: World Heart, World Crystal, Heart of the Cosmos

The Heart of Ember is by far the greatest of the forces in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, and some believe it to be some kind of creator entity that created everything with some grand design or purpose. The Heart is a limitless reservoir of energy called Lifeforce, the pure, undiluted energy of creation that is extremely potent and is responsible for many great wonders, including the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle}, the formation of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystals} and the constant flow of lava, water, and energies throughout the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} beneath the surface of the world. Throughout the History of the cosmos, the Heart of Ember has often been at the center of cosmological events, and its importance cannot be understated, as without its presence, the cosmos itself would cease to be.
Heart of Ember.scoverview: The Heart of Ember is said to be a titanic shard of crimson crystalline material, infused with mystical energy that rests at the center of the Ember Cosmos within a colossal cavern called the Heart Chamber. Its true size is difficult to determine with any accuracy as it is impossible to approach without being utterly consumed in red and golden energy. The Heart Chamber itself is colossal in size, and the Heart floats unerringly within its center.
Heart of Ember.sgamemaster:
The Heart's history and origin is one of the greatest mysteries imaginable, and very few beings are even aware that the Heart existed before Creation. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} believe that the Heart wandered the endless and unknowable expanse of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss} for unknown eons before it collided with strange energies, causing an extraordinary reaction and the formation of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{The Weave}. This expansion of space resulted in a safely enclosed cosmos which is often referred to as the Ember Cosmos. Everything within, all the forces, matter and beings exist in this space also called the Sea of Stars, set apart from the eldritch indescribable energies and beings of The Abyss.

While this belief is based upon uncounted ages of understanding and spiritual connection to the world by the Oaken and it does seem to be credible, it does contain several inaccuracies that I have personally uncovered. Thus the exact formation of the Cosmos is not known by anyone except @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}.

Intentionality

It is worth noting that few mortals are even aware of the Heart of Ember today. Few believe that the Heart of Ember is a thinking sapient being with intent or motivations; or perhaps it is instead some kind of creationary engine or object, or an echo of an even greater beings purpose. Most mortals dismiss its impact and ability to affect the world and that it may just be a name for some ancient Shard God.

A few groups and cultures, however, believe that the Heart of Ember is a being with a strange, unknowable personality, the most famous example of which are the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} of Ordain, who worship the Heart much like a deity. They believe that the creation of the Ember Cosmos by the Heart is a deliberate act by an entity or being with awareness and purpose. The Ember Cosmos is so grand, so complex, and vast that it must obviously have some directed intent or purpose.

When ruminating on the Heart of Ember, there always seem to be greater mysteries and unknowns when considering its purpose or history. Where did it come from? What kind of power does the Heart truly hold? What is the purpose of a soul? Why does its power not remain completely consistent across the ages? Answers to these questions and many others are maddeningly illusive and some may hold hidden secrets that extend far beyond the Ember Cosmos into the darkness beyond that will never be answered.

Ascendancy.name: Ascendancy
Ascendancy.scoverview: The ultimate ambition for many mortals in the Ember Cosmos is to Ascend, through absorbing Lifeforce and imbuing themselves with vast power. It's widely believed that this is only possible through the discovery of Heart Crystals. These giant crystal formations, often as large as a building, are not mere objects, but rather highly concentrated reserves of raw Lifeforce, diluted remnants of the Heart of Ember left over from the First Dawn or created through a mysterious process that few are aware of. It's said that merely touching one grants a mortal the power to become a Shard God. Some Shard Gods who have survived the process have reported that the Heart Crystals possess a strange, enigmatic sense of being, able to interact with mortal creatures and the world around them in ways that defy explanation.
Ascendancy.sgamemaster:
• Keywords: Power, Crystals

  • Age: Variable

  • Other Names: Heart Shards, Heart Fragments

In ages past, when the energy and power of the First Dawn were at their height, many Heart Crystals were formed and were more easily found by mortals all over the surface world. It's said that they are created deep within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} somehow connected to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} and are more easily found there but throughout the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}, Heart Crystals were sometimes flung from these pathways onto the surface of Ember by eruptions. Discovering one in those primordial days was said to be a fairly well-known occurrence, and there are plenty of creator myths and legends surrounding the discovery of Heart Crystals in ancient tales.

As the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} has settled and calmed from the intensity of the First Dawn, fewer and fewer Heart Crystals have been discovered. During the present, discovering a Heart Crystal is a rare, world-changing event.

Ascendancy

One of the most well-known results of interacting with a Heart Crystal is the creation of a new Shard God through a process known as Ascendancy. During this process, an individual creature absorbs the energy of a Heart Crystal, giving them godlike power. It's worth noting that most mortals assume that people and sapience is required in order to ascend, but that its not entirely true. Creatures and other beings have been known to become Shard Gods and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rmMWMD9iFRm6Nl3x]{Obrisire}is one of the more famous examples. How exactly this occurs is a mystery, however.

Due to the rarity of Heart Crystals during the present age, the exact nature of Ascendancy is not fully understood. Scholars of the process believe that it takes a set amount of time to complete, though their estimates range from a few hours to several days. The process is also believed to involve a complex series of attunements and communions requiring an immense level of willpower and mental resolve. Despite what most people believe, simply touching a Heart Crystal is not enough. Once the Ascendancy process is begun, it cannot be interrupted – while there are rumors of half-Ascended creatures, all documented examples of an interrupted Ascendancy led to massive energy explosions that annihilated the individual attempting to ascend and anyone or anything nearby.

For those who successfully ascend, including beasts and other non-sentient creatures, the process has been said to cause irreversible physical and mental changes. The amount of Lifeforce infused into a mortal's being is remarkable. Shard Gods, who have explained how they felt after the process, describe feelings of overwhelming understanding and overstimulation of the senses. Despite the increase in power and the changes that inevitably occur, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} are not changed at any basic level and remain similar to their mortal selves, with the same feelings, ideas, motivations, and flaws. More information regarding Shard Gods can be found on other pages, but it is worth noting that Shard Gods are not granted any particular aspected power upon ascension; instead, they tend to gravitate towards concepts that resonate with their own personalities, which means that Shard Gods can have competing titles and areas of concern. When describing a Shard God, it's more accurate to call them "a God of" rather than "the god of" in this respect, i.e., in the present, there are currently three Shard Gods of Fire and four of Battle in various places of the world.

The Cosmos.name: The Cosmos
The Cosmos.text:
The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} is known as Eiru and sits at the center of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars}, a vast expanse that stretches to the edges of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}. At the core of Eiru rests the Heart of Ember. Eiru is a vast world, but it is not spherical; instead, it appears like a thick disc, with a surface on one side, an under-surface on the other, and twisting underground Pathways that are home to myriad environments within. Each day, Eiru is bathed in the radiant light of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}, a celestial body and Elder Goddess also called “the Sun."

The Weave and The Abyss

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars} is the name for the space within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{The Weave} , enveloping Eiru, the Moons, and Realms contained within. The Weave is a mystical barrier that glimmers with blue, purple, and pink light in the darkness and can even be seen from the surface of Eiru on clear nights. This strange barrier marks the perimeter of the Ember Cosmos and is the bubble that shields everything within from the eldritch madness from beyond.

Beyond the barrier of the Weave is a place called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{The Abyss}, a word that is itself barely spoken or well understood by those living in Ember. It is the terrible and unimaginable outside, so alien that few can comprehend its secrets or even attempt to understand it. The Abyss is believed to be an infinite realm of impossible, mind-warping corruption. Thankfully, the Weave's constant protection prevents these maddening energies from flooding into the Sea of Stars to cause untold destruction.

The Moons of Ember

As the Weave formed around Eiru during Creation, so too did six moons — each of which encapsulates the essence of certain elemental and primeval forces: fire, water, earth, air, order, and chaos. These moons are massive spherical objects with distinct orbital patterns. Each moon also gave life to its own denizens, beings of energy and matter, from the tiniest elemental motes to the mighty Elemental Sovereigns.

Each moon serves as the physical, spiritual, and cosmological origin of its own elemental energy; the dispersal of these energies throughout the Sea of Stars has a major influence on the world of Ember and its denizens. As a particular moon reaches its zenith, directly overhead Eiru, the world is bathed in elemental energy.

The Inner Realms

Alongside Eiru and the moons are a trio of realms that float just barely upon the surface of The Weave itself. Each was influenced differently during Creation by their proximity to The Abyss, meaning that, while the Inner Realm is part of the Cosmos, it is among the most alien and otherworldly places imaginable. Their influence cannot be overstated, and the effect they have upon Eiru is even more intense than that of the Elemental Moons.

Each Realm has its own distinct magical force that plays a vital role in maintaining the cosmic balance and forms a mysterious link to the inhabitants of the World of Ember. These forces are Light tied to the realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}, Darkness tied to the realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}, and Shadow to the realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, and, like Eiru and the moons, these realms are inhabited by their own unique beings and creatures.
The Cosmos.scoverview: The Ember Cosmos is a singular universe, a bubble of life, with complex forces that exist as bastions of balance and order. The Cosmos is contained and protected by a cosmological barrier of incalculable power called the Weave; beyond the Weave lay the eldritch and maddening energies that seek the annihilation of the Ember Cosmos at all costs. At the center of this bubble is a world called Eiru, and within its core rests the Heart of Ember, a force so powerful that some believe it to be the source of all Creation.

Attunement.name: Attunement
Attunement.text:
Different souls within the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} occasionally exhibit varying degrees of attunement, and only a rare few are capable of resonating with more than one cosmological force at a time. Those who achieve such alignment may occasionally manifest extraordinary capabilities, their thoughts, senses, and actions subtly influenced by the essence of the forces they reflect.

The exact process by which a soul becomes attuned is not known, but leading scholars theorize that such attunement develops when a person lives their life according to a fundamental Ideal: an underlying philosophy or tenet which guides the soul to harmonize with the metaphysical nature of the cosmological force.

Careful observation of attuned souls has allowed Ember’s sages to discern recurring patterns of thought, behavior, and ideology. These patterns have been codified into the currently accepted classification of Ideals, each of which represents a distinct philosophical or metaphysical path through which the soul may resonate with one part or aspect of the cosmos. Some Ideals encourage discipline, cunning, or patience, while others call for spontaneity, ambition, or the preservation of life itself.

Though these classifications are widely accepted among the learned, attunement remains a deeply personal and often unpredictable phenomenon. The strength, expression, and effects of a soul’s resonance can wax and wane across a lifetime, and even the most careful study cannot fully predict the consequences of deep or prolonged attunement. The eleven accessible attunements in Ember and their Ideals are presented below.

Akon

@Embed[.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon} resonate with a harmony to The Shattered Moon and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Discipline.

The Ideal of Discipline

To be attuned to Akon is to bind oneself to the remnants of a broken perfection. Though the moon lies in ruin, its ideal of order and discipline endures, a quiet purpose that calls to those who live by code and conviction. People on Ember consider Akon to be most associated with discipline, but this is not mere obedience to rules but the mastery of one’s will: the strength to act with purpose, duty, and to remain steadfast in the face of chaos.

Aura

@Embed[.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura} resonate with harmony to The Hollow Moon and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Individualism.

The Ideal of Individualism

To be attuned to Aura is to embrace one’s own path. Those aligned with the Hollow Moon act according to their own desires, guided by personal insight and the urge to seek new horizons or experiences. Their minds are restless, alive with ideas, reflections, and creativity that often diverge from tradition. Yet such independence carries the risk of obsession or relentless ambition. True attunement to Aura lies in balancing freedom with responsibility, knowing when to soar and when to anchor oneself amidst the shifting winds.

Cora

@Embed[.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora} resonate with harmony to The Blasted Moon and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Pragmatism.

The Ideal of Pragmatism

To be attuned to Cora is to see the world through the lens of what must be done. Those who follow her ideal embrace practicality over perfection, acting not from hope or despair, but from a clear understanding that the world just is, and a person must ultimately carry on with firm resolve in the face of every challenge. They are steadfast and unsentimental, grounded by experience. Yet such pragmatism can harden the heart, for the path of endurance often leaves little room for gentleness. True attunement to Cora lies in knowing when to stand firm and when to yield.

Mayis

@Embed[.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2 overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis} resonate with harmony to The Tempest Moon and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Patience.

The Ideal of Patience

To be attuned to Mayis is to embrace patience, understanding that not all storms may be faced at once, and it's often better to let the currents swirl around you. Their actions are deliberate, measured, and they persevere where rashness would lead to ruin. True attunement lies not in controlling the waters, but in moving with them, accepting the cycles of turmoil and calm, and finding clarity while waiting for the perils to pass, or waiting until the right moment to act.

Orbis

@Embed[.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis} resonate with harmony to The Spirit Moon and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Spontaneity.

The Ideal of Spontaneity

To be attuned to Orbis is to surrender to the pure random chance of the cosmos, to trust impulse, to act without hesitation, and to find strength in the moment rather than in the plan. Those guided by the Spirit Moon’s ideal of Spontaneity embrace chaos, knowing that meaning is found not in what may happen but in what happens now. They are the dancers of chaos, the voices of chance, the souls who refuse stillness.

Ragen

@Embed[.LKptgmc56euSOb0G overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen} resonate with harmony to The Charred Moon and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Directness.

The Ideal of Directness

To be attuned to Ragen is to embrace the virtues of direct action: the unflinching drive to act, to confront truth without disguise. Those who follow Ragens' ideal do not waver or hide behind pretense; they burn through uncertainty and forge the most direct path possible, favoring bold action over hesitation. Fire often destroys what lies before it; it burns, flares, and destroys until it has achieved its goal.

Luxarum

@Embed[.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} resonate with harmony to The Realm of Endless War and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Ambition.

The Ideal of Ambition

To be attuned to Luxarum is to burn with unyielding purpose. Its burning light calls to those who seek greatness, driving them toward perfection through willpower and ambition. Such individuals see every obstacle as fuel, every failure as proof that they must shine brighter still, often at the expense of others, driving them towards selfish actions. The light of Luxarum is not gentle. It consumes as much as it empowers, and those who chase its brilliance too far often lose themselves to the same zeal that once lifted them.

Primordis

@Embed[.16sqn71JsCkghaTt overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} resonate with harmony to The Realm of Capricious Sorcery and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Cunning.

The Ideal of Cunning

To be attuned to Primordis is to think five steps ahead, to move unseen, and to act with subtlety, precision, and deception. Primordis favors those who are both careful and clever, turning obstacles into opportunities. Yet the shadows of Primordis are never static; the unobservant are easily ensnared, and even the clever can be misled by the realm’s ever-shifting tricks. Its lessons are gained in stealth and observation, and the rewards belong only to those who can outsmart others.

Signara

@Embed[.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} resonate with harmony to The Realm of Insatiable Curiosity and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Curiosity.

The Ideal of Curiosity

To be attuned to Signara is to seek knowledge, drawn to the mundane curiosities of the world as much as the mysteries that lie beyond mortal understanding. Signara inspires curiosity, daring its followers to question, explore, and probe the boundaries of what is known. Yet Signara’s truths are dangerous, and the unprepared risk being consumed by what they discover. To follow its path is to embrace understanding and peril in equal measure.

Heart

@Embed[.0anKTKgOav9sXox1 overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart} resonate with harmony to The Heart of Ember and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Vitalism.

The Ideal of Vitalism

To be attuned to the Heart of Ember and its Lifeforce is to feel the pulse of existence, the quiet rhythm that binds every living thing across the cosmos. Such individuals often act as unseen anchors in times of despair, their presence is a calm barrier of hope that steadies the living world against entropy and decay.

Those driven by an instinctive need to protect, to nurture, and to preserve are those most likely to be attuned to the Heart of Ember. Yet this primordial devotion is not without burden, for to feel life so keenly is also to feel its loss in equal measure. Being attuned to Ember itself means carrying the weight of every dying breath and every fading spirit, their souls burning with the unending duty to keep the flame of existence from guttering out.

Abyss

@Embed[.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV overview inline]

Souls attuned to @UUID[.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{Abyss} resonate with harmony to The Abyss and generally exhibit adherence to the Ideal of Nihilism.

The Ideal of Nihilism

To be attuned to the Abyss is to surrender meaning itself. Those who find resonance with its whispers do not seek power, only release from purpose, from the unbearable weight of order, consequence, and life itself. The Abyss does not offer guidance, only the reflection of a truth so vast and indifferent that it unmakes all others.

Such attunement is not chosen; it seeps in. It begins as a quiet erosion of conviction, a thought that nothing truly matters, that Creation itself is an error, that the Cosmos is but a momentary flicker in an eternal dark. A mortal may see the value in thoughtless destruction or the corruption of life into undeath, and those who walk too long with these thoughts find themselves untethered from reality, their dreams invaded by monstrous ideas and beings that drive them to madness. And yet, there is a strange peace in the greater darkness: the stillness of surrender, the quiet knowledge that all things, great and small, are equally meaningless.
Attunement.scoverview: There are thirteen known cosmological forces within the cosmos, each bound to a distinct metaphysical attribute. Of these, only eleven appear to be accessible to mortals. Scholars of Ember have long observed that certain souls resonate in subtle harmony with these forces, their essence shifting with the waxing and waning of each power’s strength. The nature of this resonance remains a matter of great debate among Ember’s foremost sages, yet most have come to call it Attunement.

Biology.name: Biology
Biology.text:
While the shared Lifeforce from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} ensures that most species are magically compatible, often due to common origins, this rule is not absolute, as compatibility breaks down in certain extreme situations.

Fundamental Incompatibility

The primary limit to compatibility is the vast difference in physiology. If two creatures have fundamentally different reproductive methods or exhibit a significant difference in their physical nature, the process cannot succeed. For example, a creature that lays eggs cannot reproduce with one that utilizes a womb. Just as a small insect cannot reproduce with a large warm-blooded creature.

Another limit to compatibility stems from the influence and introduction of monsters during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}. The alien nature of monsters seems to prevent reproduction in all but the rarest cases, and typically, the resulting offspring from such a merging is considered a monster itself.

A less permanent but still profound incompatibility arises when a creature or its ancestry undergoes extreme, targeted changes driven by powerful entities such is the case with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.K28cb1q6tvU8FP8B]{Hulg'run}. If a creature or ancestry is changed to the point that they can no longer reproduce with any other creature, then they become isolated to their own type. This specialized incompatibility can sometimes be bypassed through magical intervention, but is often insurmountable.

The Adaptation of Life

The evolution of creatures within the Ember Setting occurs through radical diversification of the life-giving power that the Heart of Ember imbues into every new soul through a process called Divergent Alteration. The Heart of Ember unpredictably bestows new traits upon the offspring of an existing species or manifests entirely new life forms. Scholars speculate that these alterations are not random mutations, but rather that the Heart of Ember is intentionally experimenting with new forms of life in order to ensure the continuation of existence. Regardless of the truth of this process, all cultures understand that it is not uncommon for children to be wildly different from their parents. Offspring bearing these changes are often called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik]{Aster}, however sometimes such changes simultaneously affect a wide group or are reinforced over a prolonged period of time, resulting in new species with a large enough population to sustain their unique traits.

In addition to the unique traits imprinted upon new life by the Heart of Ember, creatures on Ember are also shaped by the exerted will of powerful entities. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} have been known to also introduce fundamental or sweeping changes to groups of creatures. The most prominent recorded example of this involves @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} and the creation of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons}. More frequently, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild Gods} direct the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.1jb9zDsRFMXo7Je0]{Wildsong} to nurture flora and fauna of Ember towards more resilient or adaptive traits. Most of the current mortal ancestries of Ember were in some way shaped or directly created by powerful gods, for example the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae}.
Biology.scoverview: All creatures, from the tiniest insect to the largest Leviathans, ultimately originate from the Lifeforce exuded by the Heart of Ember; countless physical variations and adaptations seem possible while maintaining a kind of strange core identity. Because of this shared common origin, the various ancestries and creatures of Ember, despite being wildly different in appearance, physiology, and abilities, are also mostly compatible.

Soul Cycle.name: Soul Cycle
Soul Cycle.scoverview: Every creature on Ember is born with a soul, a unique spark straight from the Heart of Ember. While there have been many religious beliefs throughout the history of the world, it is widely believed that when you die, your soul, containing every memory and a lifetime of experiences, is pulled by a subtle cosmic influence towards the Spiritlands. This afterlife resides upon the world itself, far to the east, and many intrepid explorers, despairing lovers, or those wishing to conquer death itself have even attempted to reach its hallowed shores. While some particularly greedy deities or beings from the Inner Realms might try to hoard a person's soul, eventually they all return to the Heart.
Soul Cycle.sgamemaster:
The existence of all life on Ember comes from the mysterious and enigmatic Heart of Ember through a continuous process known as the Soul Cycle. Upon the birth of every creature native to the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, a unique spark of Lifeforce flashes forth from the Heart, instantaneously forming that being's soul. A Soul is much like a reservoir of existence, storing a being's memories and experiences. This accumulated experience is not merely personal; it is vital to the Heart of Ember as a whole, as the primary purpose of the Soul Cycle is to gather Souls enriched by long lives, sending them first to the Spiritlands and then back to the Heart of Ember itself. The Heart uses the Souls to invigorate and sustain itself, allowing it to continue fueling life on Ember in a continuous cycle.

The Journey to the Spiritlands

Upon death, a being's soul begins to slowly condense into something known as a Spirit, a being that appears much like a ghostly version of themselves, and the Spirit, with its Soul forming most of its essence, begins its slow, ethereal drift eastward towards the Spiritlands, the realm where sentient souls experience the afterlife. Spirits cannot be seen, heard, or observed in any tangible way by those living unless by some magical means. Among the priests and followers of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, once a spirit reaches the Spiritlands, the afterlife is known as Mor-ai and is a process to be celebrated, a second chance where the Spirit can live forever in eternal peace and happiness. In rare circumstances, this pull towards the Spiritlands is not immediate, but rather takes a number of days, weeks, or even months after a person's death.

The journey itself is not fully understood, and those brought back from the dead do not retain any memories of their experiences or travels when dead, as if they existed in some trance-like state. However, many believe that the entire Soul Cycle is maintained by and guided by the influence of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder God} Sockets. Once the Spirit arrives, it must wait to enter the grand doorway of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WmwoaJUw9oosRtS5]{Eternas}, the city of the dead on the border of the Spiritlands realm. Once they pass through the door, they "awaken" and begin their afterlife.

Sentience

All life on Ember, including animals and non-sentient creatures, possesses a soul. However, non-sentient souls are subtly different; in almost all cases, they are not drawn to the Spiritlands by Sockets. Instead, they typically fade away within a few days and rejoin the Heart of Ember directly upon death.

Rejoining the Heart

While it is believed that a person's Soul and Spirit may remain within the Spiritlands for an indefinite period, processing their life and gaining new experiences as they live in happiness. Almost no one in Ember, save the Elder Gods, is aware that there is something else, beyond the realms of the Spiritlands and the afterlife. While a soul's time in the Spiritlands can be eternal, they are not trapped within the realm of the dead and can instead choose of their own free will to move on, fading away entirely, returning everything they are to the Heart of Ember.

Upon rejoining the Heart, a person's essence laden with the totality of memories, emotions, and experiences from both life and the afterlife, becomes one with the Heart's vast ocean of Lifeforce. At this point, nothing is known for certain. Some believe that a person's soul helps shape the Heart of Embers' role and guide it in some way, and while the person's soul is gone, something small always remains. But the precise nature of this final unification is one of the deepest mysteries of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} and likely will never be fully understood by mortals or gods.

Claimed or Consumed

While the ultimate fate of all souls is to return to the Heart of Ember, this journey can be interrupted, and Elder Gods, certain @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods}, and the three major entities of the Inner Realms, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nXYB7d7ZBsWV1chY]{Fiends}, possess the ability to "claim" souls. Through various, often complex methods, these powerful beings prevent the souls from moving on, keeping them sequestered for their own purposes. This process is seen as highly immoral and even evil by certain religions on Ember, and there are two competing philosophies of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7#eternal-souls]{The Eternal Soul} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7#mortal-souls]{Soul Transference} that mortals and the gods from various pantheons tend to align with.

Eternal Souls

The Eternal Soul is a competing belief system with the idea of Soul Transference, regarding the nature of life after death. While the reality of the Soul Cycle remains a common theme, followers and believers of the Eternal Soul maintain that the best way to safeguard the Cosmos and an individual experience is to try and live forever instead of moving on after death. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} created the belief system during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.0bkmoi8aSFvbaCi0]{the First Dawn}, and her strong opinion on the nature of souls and her opposition to the more common belief of Soul Transference is one of the key reasons Alar is held in lower regard by mortals. Alar firmly believes that experiences in the wider world and across the Cosmos for a Soul are eventually more fulfilling for the Heart of Ember than an afterlife in the Spiritlands. Followers of the Eternal Soul and Alar herself help mortals become immortal by becoming Fae, Fiends, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.qtxBDYBNwKhD7nWd]{Celestials} or extending life in other ways.

It should be noted that a key part of this belief is that all Immortals will eventually die. Any Immortal in Ember, including Shard Gods, are not indestructible and can be killed or choose to die, and Alar believes that when this occurs, the resulting merging with the Heart of Ember is significantly more impactful and meaningful.

Unlike believers of Soul Transference, Alar actively supports the idea of resurrection no matter how much time has passed since their death. This belief is one of the more controversial and hostile for the followers of Soul Transference, as resurrection directly fights against the power of Sockets himself and forcibly removes a Soul from the Spiritlands.

Mortal Souls

Soul Transference is a belief system held by the vast majority of cultures on Ember's surface. It is a key part of many of the world's Pantheons and is a commonly held conviction of how a mortal's soul should experience an afterlife when they die. The Elder God Sockets created Soul Transference during the First Dawn as he believed souls should move on from their mortal lives, experience an afterlife in the Spiritlands, and come to terms with their existence before finally passing on to become one with Ember itself. Almost all cultures have some understanding of Soul Transference, though it may be called different names. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} call it "The Last Hunt," while the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessian} people call it "Becoming One with the Light." The basic principle that a mortal being has a soul and that it moves on from its body after death, however, is seemingly intrinsic and believed to be tied to the power of the Elder God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}.

Soul Transference begrudgingly accepts the concept of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound}, considering such individuals are exceptionally rare and traditionally move on to the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WmwoaJUw9oosRtS5]{Spiritlands} after some worthy measure of time, regardless of their situation. But the adherents of some deities have conflicting opinions on the matter — such as the Coursers of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc}, who argue that being Soulbound is merely one step removed from true undead, and are known to forcibly help Soulbound characters move on (whether their business on Ember is finished or not).

Believers of Soul Transference do not readily accept resurrection spells, especially if a significant amount of time has passed since the individual's death. They do sometimes make exceptions with the direct blessing of Sockets, but they believe that once a Soul has reached the Spiritlands, it should not be touched. Spells that reach out to Souls such as Speak with Dead are perfectly acceptable as doing so merely makes a connection to the Soul in the Spiritlands.

Reincarnation?

While extremely rare, it is believed that as new souls flash forth from the Creational Energy, they may carry subtle imprints, memories, emotional echoes, or even fragments of skill from Souls that collided with them during the union within the Heart. This may explain certain inexplicable talents or deep-seated fears witnessed in the newly born.

Wildsong.name: Wildsong
Wildsong.text:
Deep Vibrations

The Wildsong is not an audible force but a profound, magical field that connects the various @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild Gods} of Ember. It is experienced deep within the soul and through the body's physical connection to nature, often amplified in places bursting with natural energy, and the sensation becomes especially strong in the presence of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild God}. Some mortals are drawn to this deep thrum and feel it as a slow, inexorable vibration rising from the natural world around them. By attuning to this sensation, mortals like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCharClasses.JournalEntryPage.emberDruid000000]{Druids} and Shamans learn to channel the Wild Gods’ Wildsong, manipulating nature itself. This can instantly promote rapid growth or summon localized weather patterns, control or animals and beasts, and even allow them to shapeshift into natural creatures.

The Natural World

Some of the most ardent believers in the Wildsong as a force are the Striders of the Corebright Forest. Their culture is deeply religious, centered on Druidism, communing with the wilderness, and the sacred belief that everything around them is playing a part in the wider symphony of life. While some of the more astute and experienced Striders recognize Lifeforce as the powerful magical energy stemming from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}, they view the Heart only as a reservoir of power, which the Wild Gods around them then interpret. For them, true wisdom lies in listening, worshipping, and revering the different Wild Gods and the natural cycles of the world.

It is common for believers in nature and in the origin of life across the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{world of Ember} to have widely different ideas about how the Wildsong can manifest or help them in their daily lives, which is a significant point of contention and conflict between cultures or groups. For example, while the Striders consider the Wildsong created by the combined existence of the Wild Gods to be paramount and the ultimate expression of life, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain} focus almost solely on the Lifeforce that stems directly from the Heart of Ember.
