They see the Wild Gods and the Wildsong as mere distractions or a lesser, filtered version of the true power, choosing instead to focus on the raw, life-giving and radiant energy of the soul.
Wildsong.scoverview: While the Heart of Ember is the limitless source of all Lifeforce in the Cosmos and the spark that ignites every soul, the flow of the natural world is guided by The Wildsong. This force is driven by primordial entities called Wild Gods. Through them, Lifeforce is refined and shaped into the Wildsong, an invisible network of interconnected magic, which dictates the laws of growth, decay, and animal instinct. Those who practice nature magic learn to listen to and attune themselves to the Wildsong and develop a deep connection to plants and animals.

Metaphysics.name: Metaphysics
Metaphysics.text:
Gravitational Line

The World of Ember is a thick, flat disk, and its primary force of attraction is governed by the Gravitational Line: an invisible, plane running horizontally through the center of the disk. Gravity on Ember operates by pulling all things perpendicularly toward this central plane, establishing a consistent sense of down" for inhabitants on both the upper and lower surfaces. The Gravitational Line's unique characteristic is the deliberate weakening of its field strength as one approaches the edges of the world. As you approach the edges, vast sections or entire regions experience lower gravity, and structures can be built higher into the sky, and creatures may grow taller and more slender. You can "fall" if you step out into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars}, but slowly, and eventually, you will be pulled down and into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} just like the water from the world's oceans. This also explains the perpetual maintenance of the world's hydrological and material balance, as any water that falls from the oceans inevitably reemerges further within the oceans at deeper levels.

It takes conscious effort to stay grounded here, and the air is thin and remarkably clear. I have seen several small, winged creatures, with tiny gliding membranes stretched between their hands and shoulders, slip and tumble over the edge, only to glide back safely to the rocks. It’s a frightening end to the world as the Sea of Stars glimmers in front of me, clearer and darker than even the blackest nights.

~ Laeora

Teleportation

Within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, cosmic travel is achieved exclusively through the mastery of teleportation magic. This method of travel is not simple, and those who try to misuse it or lack a certain level of understanding find that moving themselves or others over vast distances in Ember is both difficult and dangerous. Moving between distant points, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{world of Ember} and the Elemental Moons, demands not only immense magical power but also flawless spatial calculations and knowledge. Miscalculation results in instant, often fatal consequences. The secrets to generating stable and long-range portals are tightly guarded, primarily held by deities or the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages}.

Strength of Conviction

The esoteric magical nature of the Ember cosmos results in various mysterious facets that currently lie beyond scholarly understanding. One particularly curious element is the observable truth that an individual's strength of conviction, or willpower, can enable powerful magical feats and allow individuals to connect with the same magical systems as those that have learned, studied, and understood magic at a deeper level. This suggests an underlying metaphysical fabric, or perhaps a deep connection to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}, that links the power of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul} directly to reality.

Determined and dedicated individuals, often those with heroic levels of willpower, can manifest power through belief alone, bypassing traditional arcane training. This feat is exceptionally rare and extremely difficult to achieve, but such individuals are capable of incredible feats of strength. Consequently, most inhabitants of Ember pursue faster and more reliable routes to power, such as the direct worship of deities or the channeling of the tangible cosmological forces and beings that are found throughout the cosmos.

Atheists in Ember

Outright denial of deities or major cosmological forces is virtually nonexistent, given the overwhelming abundance of historical and everyday evidence. The various deities of Ember have a profound and undeniable influence, and many walk among mortals. However, this tangible presence does not eliminate debate; indeed, given the immense scale and fractured history of the Cosmos, a great deal of conflict and discussion exists among groups and cultures over the true nature, domains, and motives of specific deities or forces.
Metaphysics.scoverview: The Cosmos of Ember is a mixing bowl of such staggering complexity that its interconnectivity cannot be overstated. While the Elemental Moons, the Inner Realms, and the primal forces within and beyond are obvious, striking, and shine brightly in people's minds, there exists a multitude of smaller, essential laws and quieter forces that govern the daily functioning of reality. These are the subtle threads and minor metaphysical constants that truly hold the reality of the Ember Cosmos together.

Time.name: Time
Time.scoverview: Time in the Ember Cosmos moves forward inexorably, and for most inhabitants, it is accepted as an integral part of how things are and have always been, scarcely given a second thought. To scholars, however, it is recognized as a fundamental and pervasive force, distinct from any of the other magical forces in the Cosmos. Its true origin and its underlying ability to govern reality remain a profound mystery, making it one of the least understood yet most crucial forces in existence.
Time.sgamemaster:
Time is perhaps the least understood of all the forces woven into the fabric of the Ember Cosmos and remains largely an enigma. Unlike the Elemental Moons or Inner Realms, which are tangible places and embody powerful, easily understood concepts like fire, light, dark, or earth, Time acts as a silent, overarching, and mysterious presence deeply integrated with all aspects of the Cosmos. This inherent cosmic complexity renders Chronomancy exceptionally rare, and the ability to manipulate temporal flow is considered the rarest discipline practiced by perhaps a handful of beings in the known world. It requires the deepest possible understanding of the cosmos that few mortals, or even deities, can sustainably manage.

Rules of Time

While the inherent mystery of time in the Ember Setting means that few, if anyone, will ever interact with it, let alone master it, there are a number of rules that make sure things don't get too complex.

  • No Paradoxes: The fundamental flow of time is too powerful to be truly broken. Even if someone is able to travel to the past or future, this does not create paradoxes that erase the traveler's present. The lost @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.BP2QN2S6fFOfwp3U]{deity} responsible for time corrects it; they will always find the path of least resistance to ensure the traveler's timeline remains intact.

  • The Law of Minimal Change: Significant changes to the past are virtually impossible. The more significant a change, the more resistance is exerted. Changes are usually minimal, often resulting in small shifts or temporary delays to the inevitable.

  • Chronal Backlash: All temporal magic, even perceiving the past through Chronal Resonance, carries a mental and physical cost. The greater the desired manipulation, the more severe the Chronal Backlash will be. This can manifest as rapid aging, memory loss, or fragmentation of the soul.

  • The Future is Fluid: While the past is resistant to change, the future is highly volatile and complex due to the interplay of multiple forces and free will. Predictions of the future, even by the most skilled augurs, are never guaranteed and are usually only accurate up to a certain point.

It saddens me deeply to reflect on the nature of time.

Once there was an Elder who presided over this aspect of the Cosmos, but he perished long ago. But what is truly heartbreaking is that his death had practically no impact on time itself. Remarkable really. The clock did not stop. The passing of time continued, only now it seems to run unsupervised, governed solely by the relentless momentum he gave it eons ago.

~Laeora

Chronal Resonance

A rare manifestation of Time's influence in Ember is Chronal Resonance. This phenomenon dictates that moments of extreme historical, emotional, or magical consequence leave behind a powerful echo in the flow of reality. These resonances are not memories; they are temporal distortions where the past subtly bleeds into the present or the present bleeds into he past. Areas marked by ancient events, such as battlegrounds fought by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire or fractures in reality caused by the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, can become unstable. Curiously, if you were to find a rare individual who could manipulate time, while they could not actively alter the timeline, they would be able to perceive these echoes, providing fragmented glimpses into history.

Arcturian.name: Arcturian
Arcturian.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language arcden]]

  • Capital City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.STo5BdBzDmGZChCw]{Toraga}.

  • Technology: Late bronze, early iron/steel production, enhanced with Agrimagic.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}.

  • Names: Dorin, Darius, Hasdeu, Costel, Simu, Sandul, Tiberiu, Abel, Savu, Sandu, Arcos, Gabi, Aurika, Ruxandra, Flavi, Mihaela, Draguta, Marinela, Laurentia, Eveline, Aberin, Auriu, Tibel, Evela, Mariu.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (75%) + [[/ancestry emberKeth]] (5%), [[/ancestry emberKivahr]] (5%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers).

Innovative Crafters

After a long journey across Ember fleeing the undead, the early Arcturians decided that if they were to put down roots in the Arctus Plateau, those roots would be deep ones. Taking inspiration from the enduring strength of nature, they built their community for the long-term, crafting lasting homes and tools made in harmony with the land around them.

To this day, Arcturians believe strongly in craftsmanship, passing well-crafted items and the knowledge of how to create them from one generation to the next. Though they respect tradition, they think of themselves as flexible innovators, celebrating the progress of each new generation both for its connection to the past and its ability to build for the future. The practice of agrimagic, which Arcturians created as a melding between spellcasting and their work with the land, comes from this type of creative innovation, as does the Arcturian practice of creating small constructs out of natural materials to help protect or support their communities by doing routine tasks.

Though they are sometimes seen by other cultures as naive or untouched by hardship, Arcturians believe that their years of peaceful coexistence with the cultures around them have given them a deep strength, centered in tight-knit communities that make use of the fertile land of the Arctus Plateau. They have little patience for unnecessary conflict, or for anything they see as frivolous, preferring to focus on what is needed to get things done and nothing more. For the parts of life that are thought of as practical, though, Arcturians love to add embellishments that show the care they've put into their actions, and take great pride in expressing that care through the items they make or share.

Related Cultures

Arcturians are a peaceful and non-confrontational society that has existed in peace for many generations. They have good relations with everyone around them, especially the Ordani, who live nearby in the great city of Ordain. Some cultures view Arcturians as complacent because of their long history of peace, with more conflict-driven cultures like the Waerds, Lumek, and Oaken believing that the Arcturians are naive when it comes to world events and will require help in defending themselves if they ever face real struggles. Aside from this dismissiveness, Cascilians are the only nearby culture with a less than positive view of the Arcturians, as they do not approve of the practice of Agrimagic.

Customs & Tradition

The home is one of the centers of Arcturian life, with most homes holding multiple generations within their walls. Each new generation changes and adds to the home they live in, which can make the interior of an Arcturian home feel like a hodgpodge to outsiders, but makes Arcturians feel physically grounded in their history and relationships. Many Arcturian customs feature the making, giving, and exchanging of handcrafted items, from family members providing hand-stitched clothes for each year of a newborn's future life to close friends or lovers trading everyday items as a way to show intimacy and affection. Returning an item that was given in good faith is considered extremely rude, which some traders use to their advantage by giving an item to a customer and then demanding payment for the kindness.

For those who are new to a community, or times when an appropriate existing item isn't available, buying or trading for items is considered equal to inheriting, receiving, or creating them — Arcturians work hard to make sure that those who pass through their lands generally feel welcome and know that not everyone shares their love of craft. That said, it is considered polite for someone who brings or gifts a purchased item to either know who the original crafter of the item was or put in some effort to haggle for it - something considered an art in and of itself.

Religion & Beliefs

The grouping of gods known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen} gained their name as a result of the help they provided the early Arcturians when they faced off against undead Varun giants during the Mourning War. By the end of the conflict, nineteen deities had stepped in to help the newcomers to the Arctus Plateau, from those who fought alongside the Arcturians to those who helped them rebuild after the conflict. The grateful Arcturians deemed them The Nineteen and have had some reverence for the group ever since.

Among the Nineteen, the most popular on the Arctus Plateau are @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}, who is popular in many communities on Ember, but especially loved in the Arctus Plateau for the sun's role in agriculture; @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE]{Sigil}, who makes his home in the middle of the Plateau at the Oldcraft Lodge; and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta}, who often visits the Plateau during his travels across Ember. Though not one of the Nineteen, @UUID[Actor.HUIhXv1i0eywY5Q5]{Aythorn} is also gaining some popularity with Arcturians, as they often accompany Volta on his journeys through the region.

Beyond the Nineteen, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} are fairly popular on the Arctus Plateau, especially in the region immediately surrounding @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS]{Corpin Sanctuary}, which has long been home to a group of Cindaric Sages who combine their worship with acts of kindness in the community.

Clothing & Adornments

The Arcturian love for craft extends to their clothing, which often seems straightforward or plain, but contain intricate craftsmanship that only fellow Arcturians or artisans might notice. Even the color of Arcturian garments, which often feature a shade of green, is a nod to craftsmanship — creating the color from the naturally orange and yellow materials of the Arctus Plateau takes the work of skilled fabric makers. Arcturians also favor detailed stitching and ornamental elements made from natural ingredients, like grass or tree sap, but tend towards simple silhouettes that are easy to move in and fabrics that stand the test of time.

Among Arcturians, it is considered a mark of sophistication to be able to identify the region or specific artisan associated with the clothing of anyone you meet. Shoddily-crafted clothing is generally considered to have been a gift and isn’t looked down upon, but any form of mass-crafted clothing, or clothing that is impractical for movement (including many of the styles worn by their neighbors in Ordain) is seen as a mark of either arrogance or carelessness on the part of both the maker and the wearer.

Cuisine & Diet

Most Arcturians have a garden of some kind near or incorporated into their home (often built around over time so that it is difficult to see or access by anyone who does not live there) and tend to favor grain and vegetable agriculture over raising animals for meat. Meat is seen more often in larger settlements, especially those that are visited regularly by caravans and traders, and is often associated more strongly with festivals and large gatherings than daily cuisine.

Ture, a yellow-kerneled grain that grows in pods in most Arcturian gardens, is a staple of traditional Arcturian cuisine. It is combined with liquids and spices to make a stew, turel, that is filling and nourishing, but very bland while on its own, typically becoming a showcase for a dominant ingredient or flavor. While Arcturians can speak eloquently about the way a specific herb or vegetable changes the flavor of turel, they tend towards subtle flavorings, and their cuisine has been dubbed by an outsider or two as "plain grains." In settlements on the trade routes, this is less the case, as Arcturians are quick to embrace the influence of other culture's cuisines and add new herbs and spices to their gardens where they can.

Technology & Magic

Arcturians are known for their practice of agrimagic, a form of spellcasting that supports local agriculture by imbuing items with magic for the growth and protection of the community. This practice has driven a good deal of their technological development, as it allows them to remain connected to the land while still pushing for innovations that help crops grow more freely, prevent infestations by nearby creatures, purify water sources, and perform other acts that, while magical, are focused on making the land and community as strong and fruitful as possible.

The other notable technology developed by Arcturians is in itself a type of agrimagic - many Arcturian settlements use small constructed companions made from natural materials. While these figures are not fully sentient and are not designed for combat, they are able to follow smaller commands and can help smaller settlements continue to thrive, even if their population is limited.

Social Structure & Government

Most Arcturian communities grew out of settlements formed during one of three major events in the history of the Arcturian experience — the initial settlement of the Arctus Plateau by travelers seeking a new home, the resettlement of the Arctus Plateau in the aftermath of the Mourning War between the Arcturians and the undead Varun giants, and the shift to take advantage of the caravans that make their way to the city of Ordain from beyond the Plateau. In each case, communities developed around a group of Arcturians who decided to make a specific place their home, building on that home until it became large enough to split off into an an entire community, often centered around a shared farm or garden.

Today, homes are still the centers of most Arcturian settlements, with individual homes acting and voting as a unit when it comes to making decisions about major town matters. During these decisions, deference is often given to the homes that have been around the longest, and those that have the most generations under their roof, as they are thought to have the greatest stake in what the community will become. In addition to the typical Arcturian settlement, artisan settlements often spring up around a particularly talented crafter, who will build homes for the apprentices and colleagues who become their chosen family. Tradeways tend to be a bit larger, as stopping points for the trading caravans that travel through the plateau.

Though they operate independently, individual settlements know and communicate with each other, avoiding conflict — if any disagreement threatens, the oldest home in both settlements sends a representative to a neutral location, where a compromise is usually (eventually) worked out.

Language & Communication

The Arcturian language is known as Arcden, or Old Speak. Known for its variety of descriptive words, it is used by Arcturians to craft intricate sentences that have their own element of craft, especially in their poetry and song. Most speak the Common Coin in daily life, as it is the language of trade and travel, but Arcturian poetry and folk songs, which are often shared during celebrations, use Arcden to celebrate the natural world. Some believe that their lyrics hide information about the location of old relics and hidden sites, but this has never been proven.

Some scholars have noted the use of words in Arcden that appear to come from the time of the Shent, and may have been learned by the Arcturians from some of the last surviving Shent, or during their travels across Ember. Though the exact origin of these loanwords is still unknown, their existence has occasionally helped those who study Shent ruins make some sense of artifacts whose purpose has long since been forgotten.
Arcturian.scoverview: Arcturians are a practical and innovative agrarian people who live in the Arctus Plateau. Descended from refugees who crossed the Yawning Sea following the traumatic events of the Evernight, they care deeply about crafting tangible items that are as enduring as the natural materials they are made from. Arcturians cultivate traditions that honor creativity and build legacy, relying upon them during both difficult and joyful times. Whatever comes, the people of the Arctus Plateau view themselves as a living bridge between the past and a future they aspire to create.

Sedyri.name: Sedyri
Sedyri.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language scor]]

  • Capital City: None

  • Technology: Cinderspar production, enhanced with Fire & Water magic.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.sa5TtcQvRnu3NbtN]{Scoris}

  • Names: Acor, Akari, Alon, Aras, Atan, Axil, Belan, Covan, Elan, Ignis, Inari, Isu, Joran, Kael, Kairo, Koven, Luran, Maris, Miri, Nilus, Oris, Pyra, Solan, Talan, Thal, Toran, Vash, Vira, Xalo, Zari, Zun.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberAshka]] (99%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers).
Sedyri.scoverview: In the legends, after the Shard Goddess Scoris created the Ashka, she brought them to an idyllic island called Sedyra, or Paradise, where the Sedyri culture flourished. During the events of the Shattering, the island was decimated, and the legendary floating city of Rejarh sank beneath the waves. Only a few of their cultural practices survive in small Ashka enclaves but the culture as a whole no longer exists.

Aedir.name: Aedir
Aedir.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language towyr]]

  • Great City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.kpLyA8T7vbOvn35H]{Ruined Towir}

  • Technology: Extremely advanced, the Aedir achieved higher technology levels than any other culture in the Ember cosmos. However, most of their advancements and technology were destroyed after The Shattering. Remnants of Aedir technology that remain are their colossal structures, such as the ruins of Towir and rusting metal constructs, left to rust in their crumbling halls.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Solaru}

  • Names: Akshan, Amashar, Amelzar, Amorash, Ashuran, Eleuvan, Kalanesh, Kalnash, Loamar, Lomirah, Malnara, Moruvan, Rumanar, Shalvan, Talmaris, Tashiran, Timarash, Toaniel, Tochnara, Toctaniel, Ulmaran, Zimara, Zumara, Zumran.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberNirae]] (65%) + [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (5%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in large numbers).

Vestiges of the Aedir

The Aedir, also known as the Aedir Empire or the Sunfire Empire, was an ancient culture that fell two and half thousand years ago during the end of a time known as the Age of Sunlight. Despite the passing of years, the name Aedir is still very well known by the peoples of the Aterican continent. This is due to the lasting impact that the Aedir had on many foundational cultures but also because their once crowning achievement, the colossal Sun Tower (now known as the Broken Tower), looms above the horizon from almost everywhere on the surface of Ember.

Common Cascilian phrase, while sailing in the direction of the Broken Tower, "Breakers of light." followed by spitting to one side.

Some view the Aedir as conquerors, others as sages who help guide their people in their early days, but generally, the events of The Shattering and the breaking of the world in the aftermath have meant that even after thousands of years, the peoples of the world view the Aedir in a negative light. According to myth, the Aedir tried to build the Sun Tower to ascend into the heavens, commune directly with Lantyr, and harness her power. However, their pride and arrogance blinded them, and the tower became unstable, ultimately destroying itself. This event is called The Shattering because of the cataclysmic destruction of the Aedir capital of Towir and the moon Akon, which was destroyed by a piece of the tower in the following days. Many scholars and historians claim that this is not the full story, and it's almost impossible to determine what really happened; nevertheless, the people of the world believe that the Aedir deserved their terrible fate.

Today, ruins and relics of the Aedir remain scattered across the shores and lands of the Aterican supercontinent and in many other distant places, such as Kessia and the shores of Jurin. Many Aedir structures on Aterica were left abandoned by their peoples who fled the horrors of the Abyssal Shear, while others are fallen chunks of the Sun Tower itself that fell back to the surface world after the Shattering.

Identity

Aedir were said to be extremely positive, wildly extroverted, and capable of pushing themselves and others to new heights. This often meant that others saw them as arrogant and untroubled by consequences, and there are numerous stories of Aedir who involved themselves in dangerous situations. This viewpoint is often reinforced by decisions the Aedir made that impacted cultures and peoples without seemingly considering the impact that those decisions would bring. There are even myths and legends about the Aedir that have been passed down as fables that teach moral lessons, and it's common for the Aedir to appear foolish or unthinking and would often meet justified ends. This, however, is not backed up by the few historical records that have survived, and the Aedir were rarely caught off guard; in fact, they are recorded as being unusually capable, powerful, and able to deal with almost any situation. This is perhaps the reason why their fall was so shocking to the world and certainly to the surviving Aedir after the Shattering.

Daily Life

Legends state that the Starshield before the Shattering was a place of complete paradise, where every Aedir lived in titanic mansions, with machine servants of silver and gold that completed every menial task, leaving the people to endlessly practice art, music, and dance. These stories have perhaps a grain of truth, but as an outwardly looking and driven people, tales of endless parties and limitless excess seem more akin to gross exaggeration than truth. Very little accurate information remains on the daily life of the Aedir; however, they were clearly keen traders, builders, and explorers, as evidenced by their massively successful spread across the world.

Language

The language of the Aedir was called Towyr, and it was said to be beautiful, extremely fast-paced, and difficult to learn. Speaking Towyr is a lost art that has disappeared almost completely from the world. Even historians cannot speak the language entirely, and only a few words and phrases that are directly translatable have survived. The written form of the language has survived, however, and is something that takes years to learn as there are four distinct alphabets, said to be used for different circumstances, such as formal, informal, and ceremonial, in addition to an imperial, later stage amalgamation that was used to try and simplify the language's complexity.
Aedir.scoverview: The Aedir are one of the most well-known but also most reviled peoples that have ever existed on Ember. They lived several thousand years ago, falling into ruin after causing the events of The Shattering. During the height of their power, the Aedir became a diverse empire, one that spread across the surface world from their homeland on the Starshield continent, both guiding others and subjecting them to satisfy their pride. Very little remains of the people themselves, but their actions and legacy, left a devasting impact upon the world that many still struggle with today.

Ordani.name: Ordani
Ordani.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language common]]

  • Great City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}

  • Technology: Late bronze, early iron/steel production.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}

  • Names: Jonica, Wanel, Bassa, Vastilla, Lilla, Sissos, Melin, Lillin, Shisa, Elita, Darrisa, Adone, Elefield, Elin, Elisa, Melfield, Vassra, Arissa, Jessa, Jessos, Danwren, Jondak, Meld, May, Bassar, Arien, Jonia, Melisa.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (65%) + [[/ancestry emberKeth]](5%), [[/ancestry emberKivahr]](5%), [[/ancestry emberAshka]](5%), and [[/ancestry emberFej]](5%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers)

Velvet Icons

Ordain is one of Ember's great cities, known for its embrace of trade and acceptance of cultures from beyond its borders. The Ordani take pride in their ability and willingness to get along with others, and are always willing to give those they deal with the benefit of the doubt, but they are as shrewd as they are friendly, ensuring that they're getting the best deal they can for themselves and avoiding being taken advantage of in any way.

Bolstered by years of peace, most Ordani believe that they can settle anything, even major conflicts, all on their own. Within Ordain, most districts have groups that are ready to jump into action in the rare times of trouble that disturb the overall peace of the city, handling issues on their own before reaching out to higher authorities. Even outside of Ordain, the cultural value of getting involved and getting things done remains strong.

Ordani pride in their city, while sometimes grating on those from other places, has stopped Ordain from trying to expand its reach beyond its current location — most Ordani are interested more in making Ordain culturally (and financially) richer through deals and trade than in trying to extend their physical borders. That richness, and Ordani pride in the city, are both expressed most clearly through Ordani fashion, which tends to be bold and colorful.

Related Cultures

Due to their many similarities, Ordani and Arcturians who often live in intertwined proximity to each other tend to form strong connections with one another. This connection may be both a shared passionate bond and love for the art of fashion and intricate designs or it can be a fervent rivalry between what is too functional and what is too glamorous.

Customs & Tradition

Shaped by life in one of Ember's safest and most cosmopolitan cities, Ordani pride themselves on being welcoming, warm, and cultured, and are eager to show it. Many know a smattering of words in many different languages and a range of greeting customs, so they can greet strangers in the manner they are accustomed. Similarly, when traveling, Ordani favor cultural exchange when possible, sharing stories of Ordain and asking those whose lands they are visiting about what makes their part of Ember special. Though Ordani are known for talking about their city more than most, even if they haven't lived there in some time, they value treating others with admiration, appreciation, and deep respect, and are generally seen as well-meaning and friendly.

While the Ordani will rush in to help in times of trouble, they prefer to take everything else at a leisurely pace, especially when it comes to shopping, trading, and buying goods. They often ask question after question while shopping, inquiring about the materials made to make an object or its method of construction, and use that information to make the best trade or purchase they can. Somewhat consumerist in nature, Ordani are often keen to trade, viewing the objects they acquire and sell as markers of their cultural exchange with others as well as a way to stay ahead of changing trends and fashions. While this can make them seem acquisitive and shallow to critics, residents of Ordain are used to having many of their basic needs met and being able to express themselves through what they own, wear, and display, and they often see their very visible use of goods as a way to enhance the city's trade position and showcase their relative comfort and peace.

Religion & Beliefs

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} are a major force in the governance of Ordain, providing social services across the city that range from medical care to basic food provisions — all part of their devotion to Ember as a whole. Despite this large presence, following the Cindarics is often thought of as a calling or role as much as it is a religious faith, and is seen as separate and more formal than the devotion or worship any individual might offer to a god of their choosing. It tends to be less popular among Ordani communities outside of the city than it is within Ordain.

With the Cindaric Sages focused on honoring and communing with Ember as a whole, those who follow individual deities generally choose from among @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{the Nineteen}, who are well known in the area thanks to the influence of the Arcturians. Religious tolerance is high in Ordain, and worship of nearly and/or all deities is seen as a personal matter, rather than something that outsiders should have an opinion on. Those who do worship within the city are often seen in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.aLXuhuWQdislrPnJ]{Numinous Shrines} district, which has a variety of temples, altars, and shrines. Popular Ordani include @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, who has a large shrine dedicated to him in the Temple Ward; @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}, who is broadly popular across Ember; and@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{ Vekalla}, whose blessings are sought by the many sailors and traders that come to and from the port city, as well as those who bring Ordani culture to other cities.

Some might say that the worship of fashion in Ordain almost rises to a religious level among some, and people in the city often refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.FaUiibd3k4gfrzry]{Soul of Fashion} as a concept that falls somewhere between general cultural belief and an actual religious faith. A few take the concept more seriously, seeing the act of wearing fine clothes as a type of religious devotion, but they are relatively rare.

Clothing & Adornments

Ordani clothes are a vibrant rainbow of color in the midst of the dazzling white of their city's architecture — wearing sashes, robes, and even armor in a variety of bright and bold colors. While the moderate heat of the city often means loose and light garments, Ordani also try to use a variety of fabrics, incorporating materials and designs that come to the city through its trade with other groups and nations. Keeping up with fashion is often seen as a citywide hobby, with local gatherings and assemblies providing as much opportunity to investigate and analyze the fashion choices of their peers as to meet.

When traveling, Ordani are often much more practical, wearing splashes of color in otherwise utilitarian outfits that are focused on the task at hand — and can often be spotted outside of Ordain by the addition of a particularly colorful scarf, hat, or handkerchief in what is an otherwise business-first get-up.

Cuisine & Diet

There is no lack of intriguing cuisine within Ordain, and its status as a great trading city has allowed those within the city access to a wide variety of foods and ingredients. House Lilifeld, the Ordani trading house responsible for much of the trade of food items in Ordain, is renowned for its chefs, partnering with the seafaring House Bastilla to procure spices and ingredients from across Ember. As a result, Ordani culture tends to prize variety in food, as well as unexpected combinations of cuisines that originate elsewhere and are only made possible because of Ordain's role as a hub city.

As Ordain's Cindaric Sages also provide basic sustenance in the city to those who need it, eating out is fairly common, and those with talent in the kitchen often end up taking their talents to one of the city's many restaurants. Outside of the city, Ordani travelers are known for seeking the most interesting cuisine in the places they visit, and though they sometimes annoy those they encounter with their talk of the food in Ordain, they often single-handedly keep the restaurant industry alive in the places they call home.

Technology & Magic

As Ordain has continued to grow as a city, it's embraced the use of technology and magic, including those from afar, and is a place where dazzling feats of both artifice and magic can be found. The Ordani are open-minded about it all, willing to use magic or technology across disciplines with no real concerns. The general belief is that if a magical practice or new technology is dangerous in any way, it will be found and handled by either the individual who brings it into the city, their local community, or, if needed, the Hallows, who run the city's inspection and safety departments. This attitude remains even for Ordani outside of the city, who tend to look at technology and magic as opportunities for discovery and trade, even if they are of no direct or immediate use.

Social Structure & Government

Life in Ordain is overseen by three groups - the Cindaric Sages, the Hallows, and the Trading Houses. The three share power and responsibility for daily life within Ordain, and while they have their power struggles, they generally are able to maintain an even balance of power between them. As a result, the Ordani have fairly high trust in the government to take care of any issues to large to be handled by individuals. Despite the general openness and cultural curiosity of the Ordani, it can be hard for them to relate to the idea of a government that is in opposition to or oppressive of its people, and when found in situations where those in charge oppose their actions or goals, they tend to be more trustful of authority than ready to revolt against it.

Language & Communication

The traditional greeting of Ordani merchants across the world is:

Do you speak the Common Coin my Friend?

This is both a reference to their language but has a double meaning as they are also asking whether someone is happy to trade. Thus, most refer to the Ordani language as Coins but is also known as Common.

The language is derived from the original language of the ancient Kelmezian City States and so at its root, it shares many similarities with most other human-dominated cultures. Unlike other cultures however common is considered a beautiful language with its descriptive and emotional words flowing with singing-like quality whilst more common terms for things have sharper, shorter, and faster notes for easy-to-understand interactions.
Ordani.scoverview: The industrious and vibrant Ordani primarily reside within the great metropolis of Ordain or upon the Isle of Kortos across the sea to the northeast. With little interest in geographical expansion or settling outside of Ordain itself, they live harmoniously alongside the older Arcturian culture that thrives in the lands surrounding the city. Many Ordani travel extensively, reinforcing their strong traditions of trading and cultural exchange. They are known for their diversity of heritage, pride in their city, and colorful garb. The role of Ordain as one of the world’s great cities and most significant ports upon the Aterican continent position the Ordani as one of the most influential cultures active in the world.

Bejak.name: Bejak
Bejak.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language borel]]

  • Captial City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.v0ahUcYp5dHh6kvM]{Vellatagé}

  • Technology: Early Bronze, enhanced with Beast Taming magic.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor}

  • Names: Arghun, Batkhan, Bayar, Chuluun, Dorj, Elchi, Galdan, Jochi, Kadan, Kassar, Khagan, Khanis, Khorchi, Khulan, Mundzuk, Naran, Ochir, Qara, Qasar, Rugila, Saran, Subot, Tamer, Tayan, Temur, Tergel, Toghrul, Tsok, Tulga, Uldin, Yesui.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberKivahr]] (85%) + [[/ancestry emberKeth]] (5%), [[/ancestry emberHulgrun]] (5%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers)

Beast Tamers

The Bejak are primarily a nomadic people, traveling great distances across the northern plains of Aterica. They hunt massive beasts and creatures in a seasonal dance that has been ongoing since the Shattering. While they maintain a capital in the northernmost part of their lands, called Vellatagé, this ancient city is a place dedicated to their gods and serves as a spiritual connection. However, the heart of their culture remains mobile. They are also a deeply pacifist society on the surface, with a strong cultural aversion to direct physical violence among each other. This doesn't mean they are not violent or capable of defending themselves against monsters or outsiders, but the idea of attacking or killing each other is inconceivable. Because of this, the Bejak have developed a workaround: the Beast Clash. Nearly every Bejak is bonded to a tame creature of some kind, ranging from small to large, and these beasts act in their stead whenever a conflict between two Bejak arises. These clashes between tamed beasts are rarely bloody; instead, they are displays of tactics and control, used to settle everything from arguments to violations of Bejak law.

To many, the idea of a society without violence in this way verges on societal bliss; however, this is unfortunately untrue. Social life for the Bejak is a constant tug-of-war between the direct family members who travel together and the Greater Family of the nation. While family bonds are ironclad and exert immense pressure to prioritize kin, the Bejak recognize that isolation is a death sentence. They celebrate the departure of youth to join new families with joyous ceremonies, yet this outward harmony masks a bitter competitive streak. Families frequently find themselves at odds over prime foraging grounds or ancestral migration routes. These resource wars are the primary catalyst for Beast Clashes, where the pressure to provide for one's family creates deep friction that bubbles away under the surface.

Taming a creature for the Bejak is not a simple process and goes far beyond merely feeding it to make it a pet. Instead, it is a sacred, transformative rite. Through a complex ritual of mutual agreement, a Bejak forms a magical bond with a creature, granting the beast a spark of true sentience and magical power. This partnership is a two-way street, as it also enhances the physical or magical abilities of the Bejak.

Related Cultures

The Bejak are seasonal migratory traders and herds that travel across the vast expanses of the Hente Plains by nature, they are not opposed to traveling even further afield, though they do not have a fondness for ocean travel which restricts their range. They have a strong cultural connection to the Wardcall due to their shared history, a love for the Oaken who aid them in thier struggles with Trolls each year, and a great relationship with the Fikost to their north as well. Perhaps the only culture the Bejak tend to ignore is the Kithil, as they have opposing beliefs that make it hard to relate to one another, but they are still perfectly cordial. Finally, the Bejak culture surrounds the Great City of the Sphere and many Bejak has slowly been incorporated into more urban life. Most Bejak view the Sphere as a valid alternative despite its less-than-stellar reputation on the world stage.
Bejak.scoverview: The Bejak are peaceful beast-taming seasonal nomads, that range across the vast plains of northeastern Aterica upon giant Megatheria. The Bejak are primarily made up of Kivahr ancestries, having fled from the Giants Mountains during the Shattering, but in recent centuries, Humans have started adapting to seasonal life as well. Although the Bejak are peaceful with each other and their neighbors, they are one of the few people who actively resist the incursions of Trolls and train their younger generations to always prepare for especially harsh winters when the wind begins to howl.

Oaken.name: Oaken
Oaken.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language hardac]]

  • Great City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Pn6NT1oZqpYisyjp]{Kalvard}

  • Technology: Copper/@UUID[Item.L1TdyHNyomGh8H3I]{Amberal Bronze} production, enhanced with Folklór magic.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor}.

  • Names: Aegir, Alvis, Asbjorn, Bragi, Dagmar, Elif, Fannar, Geir, Gils, Gudrun, Hakon, Hallbi, Halvar, Harek, Hrafn, Ivar, Jora, Joris, Kjell, Leif, Lif, Njall, Skuld, Snorri, Solveig, Thora, Thrain, Valdis, Var, Viggo, Yngvi.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberVrjnjar]] (85%) + [[/ancestry emberThornling]] (10%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers).

Sacred Elders

The Oaken are among the oldest cultures on the surface of Ember, maintaining an unbroken lineage since the early days of the Age of Beasts. This longevity is remarkable for several reasons: it spans not just hundreds or thousands of years, but an estimated several hundred thousand years of continuous existence. Their longevity as a culture is impressive, but the fact that the Oaken also live on the small continent of Oakengarde, considered a "Death Realm" due to its extreme hostility, makes this feat almost unimaginable. The environment, flora, fauna, and weather on Oakengarde are incredibly lethal, where merely stepping onto the forested floor is considered a lethal hazard. Consequently, the Oaken cannot reside permanently on the mainland of Oakengarde. Instead, they establish seasonal or temporary settlements that they abandon and rebuild every few years or decades.

Oakengarde is also one of the few places in the Ember Cosmos that did not become infested with monsters after the Shattering. The native creatures were so hostile that even horrific entities from beyond could not slide their way into the ecosystems or threaten the dominance of the apex predators living there. When an Oaken tracks an Elder Behemoth or Jeterio through the jagged forests, their goal is not to tame the land around them or protect themselves. Instead, they hunt to facilitate a violent adaptation. By slaying a dominant predator, they create a power vacuum that forces the surrounding ecosystem to adapt, change, and produce something even more terrifying to fill the void. To the Oaken, this cycle is a religious duty; they believe that by forcing the environment to adapt, they are forging themselves into the ultimate lifeforms.

The Oaken are primarily composed of the Vrjnhar, who are the longest-living ancestors on Ember. As a result, their warriors and hardy survivors live long lives, engage in epic battles, and become incredibly powerful. They rarely stay confined to their homeland either, often venturing into the world to hunt monsters and massive creatures. When the Oaken traverse the seas, they do so in sleek hulls of harvested fossilized wood, reinforced with iron-hard timbers infused with @UUID[Item.L1TdyHNyomGh8H3I]{Amberal}—a magical mineral mined from the forests, fossil-veins, and mountains of Oakengarde. Amberal is also incorporated into their clothing and armor, forging heavy plates that blend the prehistoric spirit of their land with their bodies, enhancing their durability.

Related Cultures

The Oaken have a positive relationship with the Ordani, the Arcturians, and the Kithil; all these cultures have historically enjoyed the help and aid of small groups of Oaken warriors over the centuries. However, the Wardcall have a far less enthusiastic response to the Oaken, they believe the Oaken are responsible for creating their greatest enemies, the Vartic. The Oaken are firm friends with the Bejak, who regularly help with Troll packs and invasions.

Both the Waerds and the Oaken have an intense curiosity about each other, believing that their respective beliefs and the practice of slaying monsters are remarkably similar yet different in several ways.
Oaken.scoverview: The Oaken are an ancient culture of hardened survivors that enthusiastically reside upon the deadly continent of Oakengarde. Oakengarde is considered to be one of the most extreme, hostile, and dangerous places in the known world, with a terrifying ecosystem of deadly creatures and plants that prowl beneath the region’s colossal taigas and icy mountain slopes. The Oaken view their homeland as a proving ground and constantly pit themselves against the natural forces inland; and while the Oaken claim to have inhabited these lands since the Age of Beasts, even they cannot live permanently on the mainland. Instead, they occupy Kalvard, a towering Great City built upon a great spire of ice in Oakengarde's largest fjord.

Cascilian.name: Cascilian
Cascilian.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language cascal]]

  • Capital City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.eVJXxKGmHUutFYjo]{Hoist}

  • Technology: Late bronze, early iron/steel production, enhanced with Ochanic technology.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: Deptism

  • Names: Coral, Coraline, Maht, Mott, Merida, Seaor, Trite, Trow, Torwin, Siren, Siran, Marisea, Narisea, Neroos, Nereus, Tia, Tiam, Torule.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (95%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers)

Free Mariners

The Cascilian Republic is a young seafaring nation that broke free from tyranny three hundred years ago. Historically, the Cascaal region was governed by powerful Mage Kings who ruled over city-states with despotic glee. After a brutal and bloody uprising, the survivors of the Cascilian people established a nation led by themselves, who attempt to govern fairly and uphold just laws. This history and its aftermath led to a deep and enduring hatred of mages of any kind. This animosity drives them to seek out and punish powerful mages, leading to their current fierce conflict with the Star Mages of Rhiva, whom they see as lying manipulators. Within the republic's borders, all magic is banned, and while executions of magic users are rare, imprisonment is common, and the republic maintains a large prison on the Isle of Coral.

Just as the nation is known for its hatred of mages, it is perhaps more famous for its mastery of the ocean. The Cascilian Navy and its Marine branch are among the most formidable forces on Ember. When the Mage Kings ruled the area, they enchanted their ships with ocean magic to prevent the undead from Ossarchate from landing on their shores. However, since the republic's founding, the Navy and Marines have evolved into something new. They still actively repel the undead, but now employ a technology called Ochanic, inspired by biomimicry, with ship designs modeled after the overlapping scales of deep-sea fish, sail designs inspired by the shapes of fins, and sleek hulls based on shark bodies. They also use strange "engines" that move with undulating pulses like those of a squid. While the navy continues to maintain surface fleets, much of its recent strength lies beneath the waves, with many powerful ships capable of striking from the depths.

In addition to their formidable Navy and ships, the Cascilians utilize a magic-absorbing mineral called Ortarec, which can be infused into wood, stone, and metal. Ortarec is mined from the Burial Plains, Dustlands, and the edges of the Giants Mountains. Ortarec is carefully controlled. An open secret kept by the Republic is that Ortarec's absorption only works up to a certain point; once that threshold is surpassed, Ortarec explodes in a colossal blast.

Related Cultures

The Cascilian Republic is closely aligned with the Lumek to the south across the Yawning Sea; both cultures and nations stand firm against the creeping expansion of the Blood Barons and their undead armies. The Cascilians are distant and even standoffish with Arcturians to their west, who they view as careless and unmindful, but they have a positive attitude toward the Ordani, who they believe are much more capable of recognizing the dangers of magic; in fact, the Cascilian Senate is very much in favor of forging closer ties with Ordain. However, they are fiercely, even fanatically, opposed to the Rhiven culture, which hosts the Star Mages of the Starsworn Academy. This is due to historical and political reasons but anti-magic sentiments and distrust are deeply ingrained within the Cascilian society.

Customs & Tradition

Life in the republic is characterized by community unity, a history of oppression, and a strong desire to stay free in a world dominated by powerful forces they desperately try to hold at bay. While the republic appears strong, both militarily and culturally, controlling its borders and keeping its citizens safe from within and without, it is actually encircled by forces that constantly challenge its authority. This instills in Cascilians a deep-seated sense of vigilance, always preparing for any eventuality. This attitude extends beyond simple gut feelings, influencing all of Cascilian society, including their coming-of-age trials at sixteen, when every Cascilian learns to navigate a small ship alone through treacherous waters, known as a Salt-Trial. There is a strong belief in self-reliance, and seeking divine help is seen as a sign of mental weakness.

Religion & Beliefs

Cascilians hold no faith in gods, even the Shard Gods who occasionally visit to offer help or guidance. Instead, they follow a spiritual philosophy called Deptism, which emphasizes strength, honesty, and resolve. This belief is widespread, and although small groups of worshippers for gods or powerful beings exist secretly, most Cascilians consider reliance on divine intervention a sign of weakness. They acknowledge these powerful entities exist, but that a mortal should not worship or venerate them. As a democracy, Cascilians strongly believe their families, communities, and nation are entirely capable of making important decisions, and that the collective strength of their republic can guide them through any challenge or crisis.

Clothing & Adornments

Throughout the republic, the ocean is regarded not only as a vital provider of safety and material goods but also as a symbol of power and strength. This view influences Cascilian fashion, which emphasizes materials that shed water, resist rust, and visually connect wearers to the sea. As a result, Cascilians wear clothing and armor inspired by fish and marine life, crafted from rust- and rot-resistant metal alloys or cloth and featuring sleek designs. These clothes are often incredibly long-lasting, and handed-down elements are passed between families, upgraded, and adapted to individual preferences. Most citizens also wear a small Ortarec shard on chains, serving as a talisman that hums or warms in the presence of active magic, acting as a personal alarm.

Cuisine & Diet

Almost their entire diet is dictated by the waters of Golden Bay and the Yawning Sea to the south. While they do grow vast fields of golden corn on land to feed their population, Cascilians consider any foods gathered from the ocean as far more important. Fish is considered one of the primary ingredients, and Cascilian fishing ships and fleets traverse the waters and oceans around the republic, with some even crossing the Yawning Sea in defiance of Godkiller Orinth. How they manage to appease his wrath or remain hidden from his gaze is unknown. In the capital of Hoist, one of the most famous recipes is Bisam, a hearty, salty broth made from rendered fatty fish bones, char-grilled vegetables as a garnish, and a large serving of slow-cooked Jurk Fish on top, the skin blistered and made crisp by direct flame.

Technology & Magic

The republic strongly despises any form of magic, resisting anything that cannot be fully explained by logic, mathematics, or material understanding. Among Ember's cultures, the Cascilians are unique in their pursuit of science without any magical aid whatsoever. They instead observe the world around them, particularly the oceans and seas, and see the strength and power of its creatures and plants as something they can emulate and refine to meet their needs. Consequently, their ships, buildings, clothing, and various objects reflect this approach, leading them down a path of biomimicry. Cascilian technology mimics the forms and functions of natural creatures and elements. Instead of magic, they depend on the wind, waves, and, in rare modern cases, mechanical pulses and hydrostatic pressure.

Social Structure & Government

Life in the republic revolves around community service, often requiring several years in the Navy or Marines. This creates a Stratocratic Democracy where only those currently enlisted or retired veterans can vote or run for office. Although this might seem restrictive, nearly the entire population serves in either organization for at least a short period, making participation in elections almost universal. The head of the republic is called the Grand Admiral, a position held by the commander of both the Marines and the Navy. They act as the head of state and are advised by a council of elected representatives from major port cities. While the Grand Admiral handles most daily decisions and military matters, the Cascilian Senate is responsible for passing laws and debating reforms that affect daily life. Legislation tends to be strict, emphasizing the "Common Good" of all Cascilians over individual freedoms.

Language & Communication

The Cascal language is called Cascal and is often seen as terse and guttural by outsiders. Words are often sharp and percussive, and its citizens converse in short sentences filled with nautical jargon and slang derived from naval operations.
Cascilian.scoverview: The Cascilian Republic is a relatively young maritime nation located on the shores of the Yawning Sea to the west of Ordain. The Republic was formed nearly three centuries ago following a bloody uprising against tyrannical local Mage Kings. The Republic expanded to encompass the entire Cascaal Peninsula and now provides the Arctus Plateau with a strong bulwark against the relentless undead of the Blood Barons. The Cascilian people are notoriously mistrustful of magic, viewing it as a treacherous tool of manipulators and power-hungry tyrants who threaten their otherwise progressive society.

Lorai.name: Lorai
Lorai.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language towyr]]

  • Capital City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.JOQEUVlchjySDKzy]{Oneir}

  • Technology: The Lorai retain a great deal of technology from the Aedir Empire, but it has stagnated.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Solaru}

  • Names: Akshan, Amashar, Amelzar, Amorash, Ashuran, Eleuvan, Kalanesh, Kalnash, Loamar, Lomirah, Malnara, Moruvan, Rumanar, Shalvan, Talmaris, Tashiran, Timarash, Toaniel, Tochnara, Toctaniel, Ulmaran, Zimara, Zumara, Zumran.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberNirae]] (99%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in tiny numbers).

Legacy of the Sun

Beneath the jagged peaks of northern @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.u7CDTzcmggsA1wYL]{Oakengarde}, the Lorai dwell in deep, hidden enclaves, remnants of the ancient Aedir civilization and the last true heirs of the Sunfire Empire. Their cities are carved from stone and lit by glowing crystals and carefully tended conduits fueled by the Lifeforce of Ember. Outsiders rarely gain entry, and those Lorai who venture into the world above are bound by oaths of blood and magic to conceal the location of their homes.

The Lorai are a people burdened with shame and responsibility. They carry the legacy of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, the cataclysm that fractured their once world-spanning empire and scarred the cosmos. Unlike simple isolationists, the Lorai seek to understand the disaster and, where possible, repair the damage it caused. Their efforts are focused on restoring the moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, which was shattered by the cataclysm. While the task itself is daunting, they remain undeterred. For the Lorai, this task borders on a spiritual redemption as they pursue the knowledge and practical means to mend the cosmos and redeem the overwhelming failures of their ancestors.

Lorai society is defined by study, ritual, and the careful preservation of knowledge. Scholars of the Shattering dedicate their lives to understanding history, magic, cosmology, and, in particular, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. They meticulously record both arcane and mundane observations, seeking patterns that might illuminate the path to Akon’s restoration. Libraries, observatories, and underground laboratories form the heart of every enclave, while art and craftsmanship, particularly metalwork, sun-forged glass, and stone-grown architecture, honor the aesthetic legacy of the Sunfire Empire.

Complementing the Lorai’s scholarly pursuits are the Shattered Blades, a warrior order forged from guilt and determination. Named in memory of Aedir’s failure during the Shattering, they are tasked with defending the enclaves, confronting Abyssal threats, and safeguarding knowledge vital to the restoration of Akon. Shattered Blades train in both martial skill and celestial-imbued techniques. Their weapons, often fractured and reforged from relics of the empire, symbolize the world’s current broken state and the hope that it can be remade. Many rituals accompany their combat: ceremonial duels, the lighting of sunfire beacons, and meditative practices designed to harmonize body, mind, and the cosmic forces they strive to restore. While fearsome in battle, their actions are guided by a code of restraint, humility, and devotion to the penance of their people.

Related Cultures

The Lorai do not exist, at least on the world stage, and very few know of them. Individual Lorai researchers are present in the world but hide their origins. Thus the Lorai have no connections with other cultures.
Lorai.scoverview: Beneath the mountains of northern Oakengarde lies one of the last remnants of ancient Aedir culture and the last true successors of the Sunfire Empire. They have now closed themselves off from the world and hidden away from the sun, few if any outsiders are ever permitted to visit their hidden society. Thankfully the continent of Oakengarde makes sure that few if any know that the city exists and while some Nir'ae leave the confines of the enclave they still keep the exact location a closely held secret to protect their passive kin.

Nalvani.name: Nalvani
Nalvani.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language towyr]]

  • Capital City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.AvHqypTJUqpXBP7z]{Oramar}

  • Technology: The Nalvani retain a great deal of technology from the Aedir Empire, but it has stagnated.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Solaru}

  • Names: Akshan, Amashar, Amelzar, Amorath, Ashurak, Elevahn, Kalanesh, Kalnath, Loamyr, Lomirath, Malnar, Moruvan, Rumanar, Shalvahn, Talmaris, Tashiran, Timarash, Toaniel, Tochnar, Tocthiel, Ulmaran, Zimarah, Zumarah, Zumvrah.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberNirae]] (75%) + [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (5%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers).

Twisted Heirs

The Nalvani are a people forged in the shadow of ruin. They are among the last heirs of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire, clinging to an ancient world that seeks only to forget them. They are secretive, unyielding, and obsessed with the majesty and power of their once-vast civilization. They venerate the dead Gods of the Solura, debasing themselves and outsiders in blood-fueled rituals. They are a terrible, cruel, and relentless culture, only prevented from expanding to encompass others by their furious and deadly infighting among their numerous noble houses. To cross a Nalvani is to risk death, betrayal, or worse, as their patience is endless, and their vengeance is cruel.

Unfortunately, the Nalvani practice a horrific form of slavery, which they call Reclaiming, which is seen by other cultures and kingdoms as disgusting and dehumanizing. Slavery is not economic; it’s political and ideological. It is used as a punishment for failure, dissent, or defiance. A Nalvani or outsider who disobeys or underperforms may be “reassigned” to servitude, emphasizing obedience and fear of the system in which the Nalvani live. The Nalvani noble houses regard their slaves as instruments of their "empire." In the hidden halls of their enclaves, entire wings are dedicated to those "reclaimed" and then trained, conditioned, and exploited to rebuild the Aedir legacy. Names are stripped, and magical bonds are carved into flesh, while the fear of reprisal or rebellion is seared from the Reclaimed minds.

Related Cultures

The Nalvani are known to other cultures at least at a surface level, but with their reputation as slavers and worshippers of blood they are whispered about as if they are monsters of myth rather than a living people. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessians}, however, are all too aware of the Nalvani’s presence and harbor an unrelenting hatred. Any Nalvani who attempts to infiltrate Kessian lands is captured without hesitation, and few ever survive their imprisonment.
Nalvani.scoverview: The Nalvani are the hidden inheritors of the shattered Aedir Empire, a secretive and ruthless people devoted to restoring their lost civilization at any cost. Power is concentrated in their many ancient noble houses, which dominate politics, enforce loyalty, and maintain control over the population. They worship the dead Gods of the Solaru in dark, sadistic rituals. Feared as slavers and blood worshippers, the Nalvani are patient predators, striking with precision and leaving ruin in their wake.

Rhivan.name: Rhivan
Rhivan.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language arcden]]

  • Great City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy}

  • Technology: Steel production, enhanced with Star magic.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} & @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{The Weaver}.

  • Names: Amonthal, Arcanis, Azureth, Balthazar, Belphos, Elara-Zun, Ethereos, Ignathis, Jorthal, Kaelith, Korthas, Luvion, Lyris-Var, Malakor, Mistralis, Myrennos, Nythari, Omnis, Orithar, Qystra, Rholandis, Seralith, Silvyr, Thalmus, Xalith, Xeron.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (35%) + (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in large numbers).

Vibrant Academics

The Rhivan are a society of scholars, academics, historians, and teachers living in one of the strangest places on the surface of Ember. Most people confuse the Rhivan people with Star Mages, though the latter are a specific organization, and the Rhivan society includes many ordinary individuals. Their population consists of those without magical abilities, as well as those with minor talents or abilities, or those who attended the renowned Star Academy for a few years before leaving for various reasons. Dropping out of the Academy is regarded as a significant achievement, as it recognizes someone’s talent, skill, or drive to reach that stage and be accepted. The Rhivan are a highly expressive and scholarly society that values knowledge and deep thinking across numerous subjects. Besides the magical elements of the Star Academy, libraries, research centers, and knowledge repositories are widespread in Rhivan settlements and cities. Wandering Rhivan scholars are as common as the Star Mages who run the Portal Network.

Despite the focus on learned and academic pursuits, Rhivans are also deeply religious and particularly venerate @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{The Weaver}& @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} with a number of magical ceremonies and customs. The Weaver herself, who is typically never seen anywhere else on Ember, regularly visits and spends time in the Star Academy, and she is even rumored to play a crucial role in Star Mages's graduation. Spectra is another deity that often visits the Star Mages in a far more casual fashion, seen eating, drinking, and arguing about various theories.

One of the most unique challenges the Rhivan must face is their attachment to the ground itself. Living on one of Embers' spines means that the Gravitational line is incredibly weak; even the simple tasks like walking are difficult. The Rhivan have adapted to this problem through various methods, such as wearing specialized metal-weighted boots and enchanted anchors to stay grounded. Large gravitational zones are maintained by Star Mages and arcane machines, allowing the Rhivan people to cultivate food.

Related Cultures

Due to their strong magic, especially the ability to create and maintain a portal network that crisscrosses the world, the Rhivan are connected to almost every culture and have good relations with almost all of them. Most cultures and nations believe the Star Mages of Rhiva positively impact their lives by helping to negotiate trade and impolitic relations, calming tensions or simply sharing news and information. The only culture that truly dislikes the Rhivans is the Cascillians.
Rhivan.scoverview: The Rhivan live in the strangest and most extraordinary lands on Ember, with their small ice-bound settlements on the very edge of the world, on one of the Spines of Ember overlooking the Sea of Stars. They are so far and distant that they would be utterly isolated if not for an exceptionally strong tradition of arcane magic and the cultural dominance of the Star Academy and its Star Mages. Star Mages are so ingrained in the Rhivan culture that the culture and the organization are effectively one and the same.

Kithil.name: Kithil
Kithil.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language mithia]]

  • Capital City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.YRvKJW3wtFPCg37H]{Luen}

  • Technology: Bronze, enhanced with Lunaral magic.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen} & Moon Cycle Worship.

  • Names: Aris, Astro, Caelis, Caelum, Esthel, Gebra, Gebis, Geyzhra, Lipsis, Nethal, Nythe, Nythra, Nyxara, Nyxos, Orbis, Orbith, Selit, Serath, Seraz, Skara, Skathi, Vesphora, Vespir, Zenora, Zenthia

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberKeth]] (65%) + [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (15%, [[/ancestry emberKivahr]] (5%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers)

Nocturnal Worshippers

The Kithil are a reculsive culture of moon worshippers and farmers who reject the radiant light of the sun. While most cultures glory in the light of Lantyr, the Kithil see her presence in the sky as unwelcome, intrusive, and dangerous. To Kithil, Lantyr is the blinding light that drowns out the power of Ember's moons and makes it easier for fabled creatures known as the Voracta to hunt them. Their aversion to the sun and reverence towards Ember's moons has made them an almost wholly nocturnal culture, sleeping during the day and working at night, with evenings that begin with a shared meal around a communal flame.

Kithil live in a region where the landscape constantly shifts due to frequent eruptions of geologically active vents, geysers, and earthquakes. They perceive the world beneath them as chaotic but seek peace by looking up to the sky, which deeply influences their culture and construction methods. They usually build their settlements and other structures on long stilts made from a material called Nupti, which bends and sways with movement, bringing them closer to the sky. This also applies to their farms, which are large structures built above the ground instead of being cemented into it, with plants extending their roots into volcanically enriched water.

As a people, the Kithil care deeply about knowing, learning from, and sharing with those around them, and despite thier strange habits, they are deeply committed to the ideal of family and community. To that extent, they reject the cosmopolitan life, which they see as isolating, and instead favor connected villages, each a large unit that works together to farm, solve problems, and enjoy life as best they can. Kithil also strongly believes in enjoying the moment, and their adoration of the night sky leads to large celebrations and frequent festivals, with dances and songs that correspond to whichever moon is currently highest in the Ember sky.

Related Cultures

Kithil are somewhat isolationist, as they find many other cultures fundamentally different, but this does not mean they are not open to exploring other ideas. They tend to abandon some of their stricter social conventions when traveling outside of their villages, especially their nocturnal practices. Kithil are generally very welcoming of others and have great relations with the Ordani and good relations with all other cultures around them.

Customs & Tradition

The deep bond between Kithil and the moons is worn on their bodies through intricate tattoos that trace their life's journey. A Kithil's first tattoo is given by those who raise them, but they choose the rest themselves, including their Marking—the first tattoo they select for themselves, signifying their status as an adult in the community. Other tattoos may reflect their connection to a specific moon of Ember or commemorate significant events, experiences, and relationships. Usually, the true meaning of each tattoo is only known to the Kithil who wears it, and sharing that meaning happens only with those they trust most.

Kithil's communal spirit influences their views on sex and love — while many Kithil are romantically monogamous, deep bonds between friends often have a level of intimacy that other cultures might consider romantic, and sharing sexual intimacy is often seen as no more special — or taboo — than sharing a secret or a good meal. This is especially true during the new year, when Kithil traditionally celebrate having survived another year by "sharing life" with each other, which can range from giving someone a plant to participating in a communal sexual experience around a campfire. Other cultures sometimes judge the Kithil culture as debaucherous, which Kithil find more amusing than concerning, though they usually tone down the new year celebrations when away from the villages to avoid causing issues with the locals.

Kithil are fascinated by the cultural norms of those who live under Lantyr's gaze, and many take part in the Kithil practice known as Sunning in their late teens — going out to explore the world during the daytime and learn about other cultures and places before returning home. While sunning, Kithil tend to be deeply curious about even the most mundane tasks performed by other cultures, eager to experience a new way of life and absorb all they can of it before returning to their village to share what they have learned with those around them.

Religion & BelieFS

Most Kithil worship @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.LNFCxHtijBM7gh76]{Thoma}, who became a shard god while leading a group of Keth away from danger during the Shattering, as the group that she led to safety eventually became one of the founders of Kithil culture. Like the Kithil, Thoma is strongly associated with the night, and many Kithil believe that she can provide guidance in the dark, whether it is about the right physical path to take or the correct way to move forward in life. In addition to Thoma, popular deities within Kithil communities are often those who are either associated with night or with revelry, including @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.9qLVBh0lSY0mOpLD]{Remira}, who seeks both pleasure and consent, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84], who is seen by some as Thoma's counterpart — the dawn to her dusk.

Clothing & Adornments
