Fikost.scoverview: In the far north of Ember, amid the freezing oceans and howling winds of the Hoarfrost Sea, dwell the resolute Fikost. Composed almost entirely of Wirrun ancestry, they endure and even prosper within one of the most hostile regions of the world. Although the cold is an ever-present peril, the Fikost have learned to harness the snow and ice that surround them, shaping it into a source of strength and survival. Their greatest triumph is the Great City of Rimedrift, a colossal floating metropolis of ice and living hulls that drifts with the currents of the Hoarfrost Sea, moving in slow, deliberate patterns with the changing seasons.
Fikost.sgamemaster:
The Fikost present themselves as a hardy, stoic people, hunters and sailors who thrive amid the endless cold. To most outsiders, they appear pragmatic and somewhat strange, viewing the world through a lens shaped by fear of the land and deep spiritual devotion. Yet beneath their calm endurance lies something far older, and far more alien.

The Fikost do not truly command their living ships, they are part of them. Bonding with a vessel is neither symbolic nor merely spiritual; it is biological. Each ship contains an Ir’tesh, a core grown from frozen marrow and Deepstrand harvested from ocean Leviathans. To become a captain, a Fikost must pierce their own chest, allowing threads of cold marrow to weave into their body. From that moment onward, the ship and its captain are one. The captain feels the cold waters along its hull, the wind across the sails. While they may leave the ship for hunts, over time the bond deepens, until eventually they can no longer part from it at all.

Kost is unique among Ember languages for its near-total absence of sound. It is primarily made up of complex hand signals and subtle gestures, perfectly suited to the north, where furious blizzards and howling winds can sweep away even the loudest cries. This silent language allows the Fikost to coordinate their hunts, maintain control of their vessels, and speak across distances in ways that outsiders cannot hope to understand.

Shent.name: Shent
Shent.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language pathward]]

  • Great City:@UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.pJzZDDC6dzjTgeqo]{She'lu}

  • Technology: Koritha Stone, enhanced Lunar and Runic magic.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.isH9tuxCUUP4GfWN]{Sentina}

  • Names: Aramorth, Elorthon, Ishtor, Jiroth, Jomalor, Jonoc, Karoth, Kiom, Kiroh, Korthas, Lorth, Lorthian, Malorth, Marm, Monoth, Mortax, Morth, Morthul, Olstor, Ormark, Rathoc, Storamir, Tholoth, Valorth, Virom, Zorthon.

  • Ancestries:@UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giant} (75%) + [[/ancestry emberKeth]] (5%), [[/ancestry emberKivahr]] (5%)

Echoes of Majesty

The Shent (or Tunori, in Pathward) were an enlightened and wise society that met its end during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering} two and a half thousand years ago. Despite the passage of time and the catastrophic events of The Shattering, many of their ruined and towering cities still stand defiantly among the biting cold and shimmering mountains, forever immortalized with the name the Giants Mountains.

The modern cultures of Ember and its people are far less aware of the Shent than their peers of the period, the Aedir. However, many cultures surrounding the Giants Mountains have deep ancestral and formative connections to the Shent. In addition to deeply held respect and appreciation for their actions during The Shattering itself, many of these people believe the Shent sacrificed themselves to protect the world of Ember. It is believed that the Shent held powers of foresight that allowed them to see the events of The Shattering coming, but they decided they would stand against the evils seeking to destroy the world even if it meant their end. They created the Keth and Kivahr ancestries to carry forward different aspects of their beliefs and ideals; this, in turn, created the Bejak, Kithil, and Strider cultures directly, in addition to the Wardcall, which arose much later.

While the Shent culture no longer exists, there are ancient members of the society that have wondrously survived. Long before the Shattering, perhaps before the powers of foresight manifested, the Shent built small stone servants to help them maintain their settlements upon, between, and below the mountains. Eventually, these servants, perhaps due to the Shent's benevolent miscalculation, gained both sentience and sapience, becoming the Hulg'run. A great many Hulg'run remained with the Shent as they fell, but some fled and joined the fledging cultures and peoples to the east and west. In rare cases, Hulg'run can live extremely long lives, and some still remember the Shent as they were, though they seem to hoard their secrets closely and speak little of what the Shent were truly like.

Today, the Shent are gone, with only memories, tales, and legends remaining of their once beautiful and ancient culture. Their ruins bear terrible scars, displaying acts of unimaginable power, where lingering Abyssal magic and the horrors of The Shattering still echo across time.

Identity

The Shent were said to be extremely peaceful and wise, focused on gaining a measure of the world around them by deeply reflecting one's self and purpose as part of the greater whole. They held a deep fascination with the cosmos, specifically the lunar cycle of the Elemental Moons and the Stars. This is evidenced by many preserved ruins that display intricate and detailed carvings of the moon cycles in various ways, with giant figures studying and worshipping.

Daily Life

Very little accurate information is known about the daily life of the Shent; some stories speak of their reference for the world around them and how they would not eat the flesh of animals, while others speak of great feasts, with roaring fires and food of every kind imaginable. Part of the problem seems to stem from the differing beliefs and stories from separate cultures derived from the Shent and a lack of any clear written history (likely all destroyed during the Shear). What is known is that they were a people who constructed some of the largest structures in the world aside from the Aedir, and their great halls and spires would have meant trade, social gatherings, and ceremonies would have been extremely grand affairs.

Language

Pathward is no longer a spoken language; at least, it is no longer shared or taught by its remaining speakers. There are extremely old Hug'run who know how to speak Pathward, but they don't tend to have any reason to share its secrets. Pathward is said to be a very slow, measured, and thoughtful language with a strange emphasis on rhetorical questions.
Shent.scoverview: Shrouded in mystery amid the towering mountains cutting across the spine of the Aterican continent lie the ruins of the Shent. Said to be wise, powerful, and gifted with strange powers of foresight, they fell long ago after the events of The Shattering. Their titanic edifices and cities of stone, tower upwards into the sky, broken and shattered by terrible forces of magic and raw strength.

Vaznor.name: Vaznor
Vaznor.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language windclaw]]

  • Capital City: Unknown

  • Technology: Unknown

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: Unknown

  • Names: Akee, Chay-Oh, Enwy, Hallow, Iska, Kawel, Kiah, Koel, Miwak, Nahele, Nye, Ohari, Okwa, Pahu, Shiye, Tahke, Walo, Woyak, Wunne, Xawi, Yahli

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (75%) + [[/ancestry emberKeth]] (5%), [[/ancestry emberKivahr]] (5%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers).
Vaznor.scoverview: Among the legends and myths of the peoples and cultures of Ember, especially the Oaken, there are tales of flying cities and a winged people who soared between the clouds. Many believe these people, known as the Vaznor, lived in the far north of the continent of Aterica, and their fallen cities are sometimes uncovered in distant realms. Virtually nothing is known about the Vaznor themselves, and no one is sure what caused their destruction.

Varún.name: Varún
Varún.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language pathward]]

  • Capital City: None

  • Technology: Bronze production, enhanced with Bone with Runic Magic.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: Sacrifice

  • Names: Akroth, Balthor, Gorthax, Jiroth, Jonoc, Karoth, Kharn, Kiom, Kiroh, Korm, Lorth, Marm, Mortax, Morth, Raxoc, Skarn, Stor, Throm, Varkas, Vornak, Zorth

  • Ancestries: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giant} (100%)

Violent Ritualists

The Varún are a culture of Giants hidden in the jagged shadows of the Runa Highlands and the Ruinous Crags in southern Aterica. It is thought that they are the violent remnants of the ancient Shent, survivors who chose to trade peace and the gift of foresight for a desperate primal rage rather than face destruction during the Shattering. Based on the rare encounters with the Varún, it's clear that they have descended into a state of xenophobic brutality, and they seem to attack anyone whom they encounter. Travelers who have ventured too close to the clans tell of dark rituals conducted under the light of the elemental moons, where the Varún are said to bind twisted runes to massive weapons carved from bone and stone.

Related Cultures

The Varún border the lands of the Cascilians to the west, the Arcturians to the south, and the Kithil to the east. In every case, the Varún have little interest in peaceful coexistence or trade and attack anyone who enters their territories.
Varún.scoverview: The Varún are the violent descendants of the Shent, the last survivors who decided to resist and fight back against their destruction rather than meekly accept annihilation. They did so by abandoning peace and their power of foresight and instead they began worshipping the cosmos' primal nature. Over time, the Varún became xenophobic, aggressive, and brutal. Building their settlements in the Highlands and around the Ruinous Crags, they keep to themselves and conduct dark rituals worshipping the elemental moons and binding twisted runes to great weapons of bone.

Niethun.name: Niethun
Niethun.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language pathward]]

  • Great City: Unknown

  • Technology: Unknown

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors}

  • Names: Agnash, Dagonis, Ghal-Xath, Hyliss, Ithal-Qun, Kul-Vog, Lythos, Myrkul, Nhag, Nythos, Olthara, Phul, Rhogog, Shath, Thol, Thul-Kesh, Tulu, Ul-Qath, Vahl, Vash-Nir, Xoth, Zeghos

  • Ancestries: Giant (75%)

Horrifying Abyssalists

Virtually nothing is known about the Niethun, other than the name, and that the term appears in ancient texts of the Shent and the Aedir. It is believed that they may have been an ancient terrible people who lived deep within the Pathways, but no evidence to suggest their existence has ever been found.

Learning about or knowing about the Niethun is an Abyssal connection.
Niethun.scoverview: Very little is known about this culture, aside from the fact that they exist somewhere in the vast, deeper regions of the Pathways.

Moiran.name: Moiran
Moiran.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language moiré]]

  • Capital City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.xi238vVZAOIsyqNr]{Miris}

  • Technology: Late bronze, early iron/steel production

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc} + Other gods.

  • Names: Abelin, Adelance, Arcosse, Aurielle, Aurivon, Costelle, Darien, Dorance, Dragant, Evelien, Evelore, Flavien, Gabrielne, Hasdeul, Laurentine, Marinel, Mariun, Mihaelle, Ruxant, Sandure, Savien, Simuen, Tiberien, Tibere, Varian.

  • Ancestries: [[/ancestry emberHuman]] (85%) (Other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.yc1bRBrDsyaIi2C6]{Ancestries} exist in small numbers).
Moiran.scoverview: The Moiran culture was once a peaceful and almost idyllic society that established itself in the rolling grassy hills and scarred forests of the Moiran Plains. However, as the events of the Evernight unfolded, the vast majority of the culture was enslaved by the blood barons or killed outright and transformed into the undead. Some ancestors of the few refugees still cling to old traditions from their now-lost culture, but these traditions have become increasingly rare over time.

The Cultures.name: The Cultures
The Cultures.text:
Lore Summary

  1. Cultures in Ember include colossal city-states, sprawling kingdoms, merchant theocracies, or wandering nomadic clans. This is because in the Ember setting, culture focuses more on people, food, identity, etc, rather than lines on a map.

  2. Cultures are further split into four sub-categories: Prominent, Regional, Distant, or Ancient.

    • Prominent Cultures are those next to Ordain.

    • Regional Cultures are those closely related through trade.

    • Distant Cultures are barely recognized or unknown in Ordain

    • Ancient Cultures have fallen and are no longer active in Ember.

  3. The two most important cultures for the Shard of Fear game, are @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}. Both of which are present on the Region Map itself.

Cultures on Ember form an incredibly diverse tapestry, from vast, multi-ancestry empires and kingdoms where numerous languages flourish in vast markets, to isolated, xenophobic communities that have protected their secrets for thousands of years. Some cultures resemble traditional kingdoms led by monarchs or regents, while others are nomadic clans, meritocratic magocracies, or loose alliances of tribal elders, and some are fully developed democracies.

In many cultures in present-day Ember, you will find metropolitan hubs where ancestries coexist in a range of fragile or comfortable multicultural unity. This is historical, as the ancient Aedir empire, which ruled for most of the Age of the Tower, encouraged multicultural cultural harmony, a philosophy that seems deeply ingrained within many societies today.

Some cultures are characterized by their impressive stone architecture and written laws, while others survive solely through oral traditions of traveling caravans or the rhythmic chants of forest dwellers. However, every culture is profoundly influenced by the history of the Shattering, their neighbors, and the existence of gods, dragons, and powerful entities that strive to impose their own agendas.
The Cultures.scoverview: Cultures in Ember consist of groups of people united by common traditions, language, beliefs, and social systems. These cultures are intricate and ever-changing, shaped by their history, geography, and interactions with others. While the Setting Compendium offers a good overview of cultures generally, more detailed information is available in the questlines and stories of the Ember Game for two of the cultures discussed here.

Languages.name: Languages
Languages.text:
Lore Summary

The people of Ember speak many languages. These Languages replace the standard set of languages used in Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition.

  1. The most common language in Ember is literally called Common, though among its creators, the Ordani, it is actually known as Coins. This language is used because it is both a derivative of the older human language of Arcden, which is still spoken in many places, and incorporates many words from the ancient Aedir, making it understandable at a basic level to a wide range of cultures.

  2. Most people speak the language of their specific culture and community. This is because 'Common' is considered the trading language, and most cultures in Ember are multicultural. This means there are very few languages tied to ancestries or creatures, although these do exist. Notably, dragons speak their own secret language.

It's said that the Inner Realm of Signara was the first place in Ember where words were both spoken and understood for the first time. Over time, this knowledge extended to other Inner Realms and eventually to the entire World of Ember. Today’s dialects are echoes of earlier forms, shaped either by the intentions of gods or fractured by the violent tremors of world-altering cataclysms such as the Shattering. In some areas, a single word can carry the melodic resonance of a celestial blessing, inherited from Luxarum, while in others, the language is rough and sparse, born from the desperate necessity of survival and the need for faster communication.

Ossarchate.name: Ossarchate
Ossarchate.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language moiré]]

  • Capital City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.3k1PiJ9EXzMCox0M]{Elwin's Seat}

  • Technology: Late Iron/Steel production, Soul Forges, Cloning, and Flesh Engines.

  • Major Religions/Beliefs: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.E1Un2zZFUupMkmSQ]{The Howling One}

  • Names: Djorvra, Drejaal, Eryndra, Halvenn, Kaelnir, Kormaen, Korveth, Nadreth, Myrkaen, Osvketh, Rethvar, Saelnith, Skaarith, Thalnor, Thaynok, Tornaal, Vaskra, Velraen, Vornikra, Vorraktar.

  • Ancestries: Majority Undead.

Dominion of Death

Shrouded beneath the eternal gloom of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.Q59ZUVNaeBoZl9nJ]{the Evernight}, the Ossarchate is a realm where death has triumphed utterly over life. The skies above are sealed by a permanent veil of black, magical clouds, casting the land below into a grey half-light where neither sun nor moon is ever seen. It is a place of silence and decay, a necrotic dominion where the dead rule over vast kingdoms without end.

The Ossarchate sprawls across a blasted wasteland known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7zFmCJqtAp32EaI1]{Moiran Bonelands}, eternally scarred by the cataclysm called Moira’s Lament. Across these grey wastes, immense limbs, most often hands, seem to burst from the ground, thrusting upward as if fleeing from the depths below. Each of these titanic limbs appears to be made of a white, stone-like material, yet is utterly impervious to harm or mark. These pale monoliths are worshipped by the undead and feared by any living soul foolish enough to venture into the Bonelands, for they exude a terrible aura that erodes the mind, draining hope, purpose, and memory, until nothing remains but madness and despair.

The realm is divided among a host of independent rulers known as the Blood Barons, lords of undeath who carved their territories from the living and from each other as the Evernight descended. Each Baron rules with absolute power, their castles rising from the mist like jagged tombs, glowing with ethereal lights and the sound of crackling machinery. Within these fortress-laboratories, the living are bred, harvested, and transformed; necromantic fields keep the captive populations docile while their flesh and souls are shaped into new soldiers for the Ossarchate’s ever-growing armies.

Traditionally, the Blood Barons are in a constant state of war with every neighboring culture, nation, and kingdom. However, they are equally eager to absorb the territories, cities, and resources of their rivals, often turning their foes against one another through cunning or corruption. Yet despite their endless rivalries, all of the Blood Barons remain bound by a shared devotion to the Ossarchate’s grim ideal: the perfection of existence through the denial of mortality. To them, life is weakness, an error in the greater cosmos that can only be corrected through undeath and the destruction of all life.

The Ossarchate is regarded by nearly all as a stain upon the cosmos, a blight so abhorrent that every living being instinctively recoils from it. Even @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} oppose its existence, viewing it as a violation of the natural order and an affront to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos }and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. Yet the Ossarchate endures, and the true terror lies in the scale of its power. Among the Blood Barons, some are merely formidable commanders, but others are unfathomably powerful beings whose mastery of necromantic energy rivals or even surpasses that of Shard Gods. Four of these Barons are said to possess strength so potent that their wills bend reality itself to their command.

The sheer necromantic power of these individuals flows outward, empowering their generals, lieutenants, and the countless armies under their control. It is whispered that their combined might is so immense that the Ossarchate could stand against entire pantheons, and even many Shard Gods regard it with fear or even terror.

Related Cultures

The Ossarchate stands in direct opposition to nearly every living power in the world. Its borders are shunned by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezians}, Striders, and even the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayans}, all of whom view it as a festering blight. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} wage a constant and unrelenting war against the Ossarchate, fought in brutal cycles of Fire and Death. To the Lumek, the Ossarchate is not merely an enemy, but a stain upon creation itself. The Ossarchate is also openly at war with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} Republic, though this conflict typically erupts only when the Blood Barons’ armies attempt to cross the Golden Bay by water. Despite this, the Ossarchate influence leaks beyond its shadow-shrouded lands, through necromantic relics, cults, and whispers of eternal life sold to desperate mortals.
Ossarchate.scoverview: The Ossarchate is a realm of perpetual night and death, ruled by the Blood Barons. Its undead armies march across the Moiran Bonelands, a grey wasteland haunted by towering white monoliths that warp reality itself. Even gods fear the Ossarchate, and all who enter risk madness, death, or becoming part of its endless necrotic hordes. Horrifically, there are countless living mortals bound within the Blood Baron territories, trapped in breeding vats, cloned in vast laboratory-like facilities, and imprisoned in vast castle cities.
Ossarchate.sgamemaster: In Ember, undeath is a manifestation of Abyss, a twisting of the natural order that seeks the oblivion of life itself, driven by the will of the Outer God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.E1Un2zZFUupMkmSQ]{Kinalathi}. The Blood Barons are not simply powerful necromancers, they are beings who have been transformed into immortals of undeath, and Abyssal power flows through them just as easily as entities from the Abyss itself, such as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors}. The Moiran Bonelands are a reflection of this corruption: the grey, unmoving mists, perpetual night, and titanic white monoliths are not just environmental hazards; they are both remnants of previous bursts of Abyssal power and signs of the increasingly powerful and growing influences of the Abyss upon the surface of Ember. Some of these colossal white limb monoliths are partially sentient and are directly linked to Kinalathi, perhaps even functioning as extensions of his will, exerting both psychic influence and reality-warping power over the land and its inhabitants.

Oderita.text:
At a Glance

  • Language: [[/language pathward]]

  • Capital City: @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.IRN93J8zYGAnxP3W]{Oderita}

  • Technology: Late bronze, early iron/steel production

Oderita.scoverview: The Oderita Kingdom was a wealthy and prosperous culture of Keth miners and jewelers who built a large citadel in the Northern Shana Mountains. They had a flair for creating glittering and powerful artifacts and encouraged traders from across the world to visit their gleaming city. Unfortunately, this obsession with wealth and precious metals attracted the attention of Karaxsus the Flaming Dread, and in a single night of fiery destruction, the Oderita Kingdom was utterly destroyed and its riches consumed by the Dragon.

Katu.name: Katu
Katu.text:
Areas of Concern: Storms, Wrath

Typical Followers: Sailors, Fishers, Fighters

Domains: War, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}

Symbol: A roiling cloud cut through by lightning

Edict of Katu

Respect the fury of the storm.

Though the storms Katu is known for are impressive and often destructive, they (like his moods) often pass quickly. He has threatened, more than once, to destroy Ember and all who live upon it. However, he has neither the patience (nor truthfully, the power) to act on these threats. The temperamental god must instead satisfy himself with haphazard calamity — such as the wrecking of a boat, the flooding of a city, or the creation of an errant storm.

Oddly, Katu has respect for those who survive his onslaughts, and will often act protectively towards those who manage to pilot a ship through one of his storms or withstand the wind that lashes their city. This wind is often made more potent by Katu's wife @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla}, the Whispering Wind, who enjoys taking the opportunity to show her power if she believes that Katu's anger is justified.

Though Katu can at times be ruled by his anger, he has taken steps over the years to blunt its effect on the world around him. Every few years he selects one mortal, called the Stormheart, to imbue with part of his anger and wrath as a way of helping to calm his temper - passing the title on to someone else when that person grows too weary or angry to continue in the role. While this arrangement can weigh heavily on the mortal who takes it, it is also considered a great honor, and whoever takes it on can generally count on fairer skies and gentler winds after stepping down from the position.

Appearance

Katu appears as a statuesque and chiseled man whose blue body calls to mind the color of a darkening sky. Blue lightning bolts extend from his body, crackling unpredictably, and he often appears to be in the center of a windstorm, with clouds circling around him and his hair, beard, and clothes in motion. Though it is said that there are times that the winds and clouds and lightning that he is known for dissipate around him, replaced by a gentle breeze, his storms are intensified by his anger, and most mortals only encounter him when he is already enraged.

Katu's clothing is often simple, but framed with precious metals that bring to mind the flash of lightning in the sky. He changes these ornamental trappings frequently — switching out bracers, belts, and the like as suits his mood — and some believe that the nature of the storms he generates can somehow be predicted by the size and shine of the accessories he wears (although this knowledge likely comes far too late for whomever he uses them against).

Influence and Followers

Sailors and fishers can be found loudly singing and toasting to Katu's health and mercy, or visiting shrines to make offerings when preparing for voyages in the hope that he will view them positively if he passes by. As a result, every port city has at least a small shrine to Katu attended by an Acolyte of Storms, with larger temples appearing in bigger cities.

The Acolytes of Storms are Katu's most devoted followers, and are known for creating the Litany of Storms, a series of books that hold a detailed list of Katu’s moods, storms, and grievances and are believed to help predict storms. Each Litany is closely guarded and shielded from the weather by physical and magical protections, and is guarded by the Stormblades, a group devoted to the physical protection of Katu's shrines and acolytes. They are also dedicated to keeping the Litanies from Katu, out of the fear that if he ever reads one, he will recall all of his old grudges and attempt to drown the world in his anger.

In recent years, the Acolytes have begun expanding their definition of storms, including geopolitical and personal conflicts into their records. A group of Acolytes that call themselves the Stormbreakers use this information to help mediate conflicts and broker peace agreements, asking only that those they help set up a large shrine to Katu once the conflict has been smoothed over.

Using Katu as a Deity

Using Katu as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or general devotion is common, especially for those who travel by sea. With altars to Katu at most ports, keeping up with devotion to the mercurial god is generally easily done — and considered to be a wise idea lest a follower get on the god's bad side and bring a storm down upon them. For those who wish a more formal devotion to Katu, becoming an Acolyte of the Storm, Stormblade, or Stormbreaker are all worthy options, though Katu tends not to interact with followers other than his chosen Stormheart unless they have angered him — his silence is often considered his deepest blessing.

Katu is deeply close to his family, who are all shard gods in their own right — his wife Vekalla is associated with the wind, while daughters Raineka and Sokali favor rain and snow respectively. Outside of this tight family circle, Katu is passingly friendly with Nite, though he sometimes finds her desire to stop him from raging against a place that he believes deserves his fury trying.
Katu.scoverview: Proud, unpredictable, and unbelievably petty, the Shard God Katu has a deep connection to the storms and blizzards of Ember, bringing their chaos to the land whenever he is enraged. Unfortunately for those around him, Katu is easily driven to anger by the acts of mortals, taking offense at the smallest of slights and starting disputes over issues that another god would barely notice, much less rage against.
Katu.sgamemaster:
Katu was short-tempered even as a young man, but he was also the best sailor that anyone in his village had ever seen, with an uncanny intuition about the skies and the changing of the weather that earned him the nickname Stormheart. But despite his prowess at sailing, Katu had no particular interest in trade, exploration, and discovery. What he loved was movement, being driven across the seas by the wind while using his skills and mastery of sailing to stay afloat.

For years, Katu traveled the seas with little care for his destination, avoiding time on shore when possible, as his short temper still led to fights with many around him. This changed when he met Vekalla, a woman with a desire to wander and explore who was as fiery at heart as Katu. Together, they sailed Ember as friends, and later lovers, with Katu driving his ship in whichever direction Vekalla was interested in going, finding the spirit of adventure in seeing the world alongside her and debating with her endlessly about the nature of the world and those they met during their explorations.

Eventually, the pair stumbled upon Heart Crystals in a cave on a far-flung island, and through them ascended into gods — while Vekalla tied herself to the wind, Katu hearkened back to his nickname and sought the challenge of a storm.

Nite.name: Nite
Nite.text:
Moniker: Nature's Wrath

Areas of Concern: Natural Disasters, Preparedness, Recovery

Typical Followers: Diviners, Builders, Aid Workers

Domains: Life, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}

Symbol: A footprint made of lava

Edict of Nite

Prepare for the worst.

Though Nite is largely regarded as a bringer of calamity, her true focus is on teaching the people of Ember that in every disaster there is an opportunity for preparation, survival, and recovery. She monitors Ember closely and is often the first to know of an impending natural disaster, whether it is a random occurrence or one caused by the actions of a fellow god, alerting her followers through visions and dreams. Though this has only added to the perception of her as a bringer of calamity, she uses the fear that she instills in some mortals to ensure that they take her warnings seriously and are better prepared for disasters that she has been unable to prevent.

During disasters, Nite attempts to save those who she can, and bears witness to the effects of the destruction, doing her best to note where help is most needed and where greater injury or loss of life could have been prevented with better preparation. This has only added to the perception of her as the cause of calamity, but she cares little for her reputation, focusing instead on the work at hand.

In the aftermath of disaster, Nite and her followers promote community and healing, with many members of her faith helping to provide relief and coordinate recovery efforts. These actions are often seen publicly as evidence of Nite's guilt about her destructive nature, and while she remains feared for her power, many have grudging respect for practitioners of her faith and pray to her in the hopes that she will take mercy on them and show them compassion, sparing them from the worst of a disaster.

Appearance

Nite appears as if she is made from volcanic basalt, streaked with threads of white and gray, with eyes and hair that appear to be the color of molten lava. She exudes a physical warmth that increases as she becomes excited or agitated, but is never hot enough to burn or injure any mortal nearby. Nite dresses simply and unpretentiously, in unadorned grey robes, and generally walks barefoot, with her footfalls leaving fleeting prints of burning lava that vanish after she passes.

Influence and Followers

Nite is a well-known shard god, with many praying to her as a way of preventing impending doom. While many offer her veneration simply so she will spare them from what they believe to be her destructive nature, builders and architects follow her in the hopes that their work will withstand any disasters that befall the buildings they create, and often leave the imprint of a single footprint hidden in the mortar or metalwork of a building as a way of attracting her good favor.

Nite's most ardent and organized followers are the Seers of Calamity — diviners who receive her visions about upcoming disasters and attempt to warn those who may be at risk. The Seers are dedicated both to divination and communication, with networks that run across Ember, spreading Nite's messages and directing aid to those who need it. Though Nite often communicates with the Seers indirectly in her own form, when she walks among mortals she is generally in disguise, crafting a persona to interact with her faithful who is unknown to everyone except her most senior priestesses and diviners.

Using Nite as a Deity

Using Nite as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or general devotion is fairly common, though it is more common to pray to her idly to avoid destruction than to be one of her permanent followers. For diviners, or those who aspire to be, Nite will send visions and warnings if a disaster is imminent. Her other followers, including builders, healers, and aid workers, generally follow her principles of preparation, restoration, and recovery without guidance, though it is said that Nite will sometimes leave footprints in the ground leading one of her followers to what they need.

Nite watches the world, and the other deities, for potential disaster, but does not interact with many other shard gods unless she is asking them for help with a current or potential crisis. As a result, the shard god she sees most often is Katu, who has a tendency to visit unnatural disasters on those who earn his ire. She is occasionally successful in dissuading him from destroying parts of Ember, but not nearly as often as she would like.
Nite.scoverview: Nite, often described as the epitome of nature's wrath, is a shard god associated with earthquakes, volcanoes, and other natural disasters. Though she is sometimes thought of as a harbinger of ruin, with calamity trailing in her wake, her true role is one of tracker and observer of natural disaster, as well as someone who helps those suffering in the wake of calamity as they heal and rebuild. She also cares little for her reputation, content to busy herself with safeguarding mortals from unexpected danger and helping them recover from its aftermath.
Nite.sgamemaster:
Once, ages ago, Nite was born a mortal to the ancient people known as the Jarn, in the shadow of a towering volcano. Introspective and curious by nature, she became fascinated by the volcano, collecting stones from its edges and interpreting the shapes she saw in its smoky plumes. When an earthquake shook the volcano, causing new fissures to appear, her curiosity overcame her trepidation and she went into the volcano to see what she could find in its depths. What she found was a Heart Crystal.

On touching the Heart Crystal, Nite gained enough power to amplify the earthquake and cause the volcano to erupt, threatening her people and village beside it. Nite was able to redirect the deadly lava flow with her newfound power, showcasing her new abilities to those who had known her as a quiet collector of rocks. While at first, this made many regard her as a savior, even Nite could not prevent every misfortune; many blamed her for the ancillary disasters she couldn't stop, and the various people she couldn't save. When the people turned on Nite, she left to wander the world and seek her own purpose. When she returned, she'd decided not to directly intervene to prevent every disaster, but to watch for them, warn the mortals of their coming, and aid them where she could, giving them the best possible chance to survive.

Scoris.scoverview: Scoris is a Shard God associated with knowledge, magic, and creation. She created the Ashka people and styled them in her image, helping them create a society on Kadisos. Tragically, an ill-informed feud with the force of entropy known as Bale led to her demise.

Domains: Peace, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: A full sail, with wind lines blowing behind it.

Edict of Vekalla

Ever onwards, like the wind.

Vekalla is a luminous deity of bargains and barter, often called The Mediator. She has a rich history of calming conflicts and fostering peace. One of her most renowned stories involves her approaching the two warring Kelmezian Kingdoms of Korta and Ancalen in the days before the Shattering, ending a three-hundred-year rivalry. Many associate her with trading and ask for her blessing and guidance in commerce. She is equally revered by sailors and traders. Nearly all sailors and ship captains of the Ordani, Arcturians, and Waerds carry charms or taliams with her symbol. This is partly because Vekalla is a highly active and approachable Shard Goddess who enjoys conversations and problem-solving with her followers. It's common to find her floating beside ships along coasts or open waters, chatting and gossiping with crews. Though she is never portrayed as old, she is older than most realize, having once been a Jarn and witnessing many pivotal events in Ember's history.

Vekalla is the wife of Katu, with a long history together spanning hundreds of thousands of years, and is considered a member of the 'Family of Storms' and lives on the elusive, wandering Isle of Storms itself. Despite occasional arguments that can cause localized typhoons, they remain deeply in love with each other and dote on one another. She is the mother of Sokali and her adopted daughter Raineka, and she often travels great distances to visit and check on them. Both daughters find this somewhat embarrassing if they are among mortals at the time. Vekalla sometimes quarrels with Katu because they often have conflicting views on the natural world. She tends to be much more compassionate toward mortal concerns than her husband, and when Katu causes storms or threatens sailors, Vekalla can become especially wrathful toward her husband.

Appearance

Vekalla is a deity with numerous shifting forms, much like the winds and storms themselves. Sometimes she appears as a Human dressed in white with dark grey skin and long, flowing white hair, often when relaxing on the Isle of Storms or when she wishes to blend in unnoticed among mortals. More frequently, she manifests in her impressive Windform to bless ships. In this form, Vekalla stands over a hundred feet tall, resembling a vast cloud of white, blue, and pink in a vaguely humanoid shape.

Influence and Followers

Vekalla's followers mainly include sailors, caravaneers, traders, travelers, and merchants. Sailors, especially those crossing the Yawning Sea, regularly pray to her and offer her rare charms or objects. They believe this devotion is worth the cost, as they think her attention can ward off the Leviathan Godkiller Orinoth, who roams the region, or simply keep them safe from storms. She frequently visits her temples along the southeastern edge of the Aterican continent, often bringing gifts and rare goods. She also spends days engaging in conversations and chats with mortals.

Using Vekalla as a Deity

Using Vekalla as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is for those longing for new experiences and a strong desire for personal freedom. Vekalla appreciates anyone willing to travel in search of meaning, believing that exploring new lands, peoples, and ideas fosters growth and wisdom. She values understanding and those eager to learn how to apply themselves. When communicating with Vekalla, she can be very expressive, often chatting about random topics for hours, but she also enjoys listening to others. Her voice is clear and steady, often tinged with excitement or a reflective depth.

Relationships

Vekalla is the wife of the Shard God Katu and one of Ember's oldest married couples, having met hundreds of thousands of years ago. They share a very enduring and loving relationship that, while sometimes tumultuous, is rooted in deep mutual affection. Together, while still mortal, they had a child called Sokali, and the three of them discovered the legendary Isle of Storms, a floating, wandering island reputed to contain many radiant Heart Crystals embedded in its stone. The entire family then ascended and has remained close ever since.

Along with Katu, Vekalla adopted Raineka, who became their adopted daughter and shares many personality traits. They both love each other deeply and spend long days together on the Isle of Storms.

Vekalla is close friends with the Wild God Nite, and the two are said to value each other's wisdom. It's said that Vekalla once saved Nite's life thousands of years ago during the Shattering, but no one knows the full extent of the story.

Vekalla has a strong dislike for the Shard Goddess Malae. It's thought that the two of them don't see eye to eye on several issues, namely being kind toward mortals in general, but it may be more personal.

Several old sailor stories claim that Vekalla sometimes rides upon the back of Obrisire, but most consider these tales to be fiction.
Vekalla.scoverview: Vekalla is known as the Trader's Goddess, the Whispering Wind, or the Mediator, and is venerated by sailors, traders, and travelers all across the known world. As one of the older Shard Gods of Ember, Vekalla is known to many cultures and is revered as a goddess of protection and peace. She is the wife of the Shard God Katu and the mother to two other Shard Gods, Sokali and Raineka.

Raineka.name: Raineka
Raineka.text:
Areas of Concern: Rain, Healing

Typical Followers: Healers, Diplomats

Domains: Life, Peace

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: Raindrops in the shape of a rainbow

Edict of Raineka

Breathe slowly and know peace.

Raineka is a reserved and reclusive @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God}, known for her healing abilities and deep empathy. She prefers one-on-one conversations over the attention of crowds. Despite her social anxiety around mortals, she has been known to be fearless in the face of danger, appearing during conflicts between the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} factions in the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowlands} to aid the fallen. She also actively confronts monsters and seems to hold a tightly reined contempt for the undead. For this reason, to the Waerds she is a highly respected deity, with many shrines and followers across the Lowlands. Many warriors carry charms or talismans believed to invoke her divine protection, especially when they are injured.

Many believe she is a young Shard God who arose relatively recently, but evidence suggests she is older than her followers know. She is part of the 'Family of Storms' and is considered the daughter of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla}, both of whom adore her. She spends much of her time on the southeastern shores of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}, among the scattered villages and tribes of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka}, at her home alongside Katu and Vekalla on the floating Isle of Storms, or within the Lowlands. She rarely visits the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}, finding the confines of a bustling city too much to bear.

Raineka is also worshipped by many across the region as a bringer of rain for the harvest, a role she greatly enjoys. This is even more prominent among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} villages, who worship her ability to bring the calm, nurturing rains much more than her healing abilities. For the Kithil, however, Raineka is a distant force, and she is rarely found on their shores.

Appearance

Raineka is a very curious deity in many ways, appearing most often as a watery, elemental woman with dark blue skin and strange lighter patterns and color blends crisscrossing her form. She tends to hide most of this and wears a vibrant blue cloak with a deep hood, its patterns shimmering like raindrops across the surface. Under her hood, she often hides swirling, glowing blue eyes and a wry, playful smile. She can be very nondescript when she chooses to blend in among crowds and prefers not to be noticed. When healing the sick or performing a larger blessing, she reveals much more of her divinity and lifts her hood, revealing a shining, tumultuous mass of watery hair that seems to flow and twist like falling water in hues of blue, pink, and white.

Influence and Followers

Despite being part of the Nineteen for as long as it has existed, she has no formal priesthood or any major temple built to venerate her. Raineka has many followers who revere her peaceful healing abilities and her desire to help others. They follow her example by tending to the sick regardless of circumstances. Many can be found within Healing Houses or as local doctors, settling in villages, towns, or cities and spending their lives caring for the well-being of ordinary people. Some take a different path and wade into battles instead, risking their own lives to spare and aid those at the brink of death. She tends not to form close relationships with most of her followers, possibly influenced by her anxieties, but she does occasionally find a particularly worthy follower with whom she forms a deeper bond.

Using Raineka as a Deity

Using Raineka as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is a path rooted in deep empathy, reserved for those who genuinely seek to help others. Raineka highly values self-sacrifice and shares her power with anyone committed to healing. She also embodies hope, attracting positive influences that aim to preserve it even in the toughest environments. When communicating with Raineka, she tends not to speak much, but her voice is soft and calming, making her intentions easier to understand through her reassuring presence.

Relationships

Raineka is the daughter of Katu and Vekalla and the sister of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lc2ZMAGsL7pH1wEF]{Sokali}. She has a very close relationship with her parents and lives with them on the Isle of Storms. She sees her sister Sokali less frequently, but they adore each other and try to meet at least once a year during Ember's winter seasons.

Rumors suggest Raineka is in a relationship with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}. It is an intriguing pairing since the two deities are radically different: Lumé is associated with war, battle, and command, while Raineka is a goddess of healing. Reports indicate they have spent considerable time together over the past few years, with Raineka increasingly seen in Hearth, the capital city of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, granting blessings to its citizens.

Among the other Nineteen, she regards @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE]{Sigil} as a close friend and jokingly refers to him as 'Uncle Beardface' and sometimes visits him at his home in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.sdIjbPRNIsJ3ApcU]{Oldcraft Lodge}. She calls @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.9qLVBh0lSY0mOpLD]{Remira} her aunt, and despite their differences, Remira often tries to involve Raineka in public events and encourages her to have fun.

Though it's unclear why, she does not seem to like @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gT5S5ncAEUvkYYYg]{Sionia} or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta}.
Raineka.scoverview: Raineka is a Shard God of healing and hope. She is dedicated to aiding others and restoring the world after storms, often worshipped as a deity who brings essential rains for crops. Some say Raineka can be seen dancing in rainstorms, but only when the rain falls gently without wind, under a peaceful and calm sky.
Raineka.sgamemaster:
Despite what many of her followers during the Age of Rediscovery believe, Raineka is a very old deity. Very little is known of Raineka's true history among even the most learned scholars. It's said she was once a mortal around twelve thousand years ago during the Age of Tower, a time when the Aedir was just beginning to rise on the central continent of the Starshield. In truth, Raineka was once an Ashka and grew up on the island of Kadisos when the Sedyri culture was a powerful force in the world. Some believe she was once a follower or even a child of an even older deity named Scoris. It's unclear exactly how she became a Shard God, but not long after she ascended, she was adopted by Katu and Vekalla.

If Raineka was indeed an Ashka before she ascended, it would add some interesting depth to her link with Lumé despite their apparently radical differences, as the Sedyri highly value the complex relationship between fire and water.

~Laeora

Sokali.name: Sokali
Sokali.text:
Areas of Concern: Winter, Snow, Voyages

Typical Followers: Scouts, Mystics

Domains: Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor}

Symbol: A silver feline eye peering through a frost-cloud

Edict of Sokali

Step softly, leave no imprint upon the snow.

Sokali is an ancient Shard God of snow, winter, and predation, who ascended long ago during the Age of Beasts. She is the creator of the Wirrun ancestry and the wife of the deity Vólun, and is considered one of the most important deities in the Auris Bor pantheon. She is seen as a wild force that rarely interacts with people, including her own followers. Instead, she roams the snowy tundra, observing the migratory herds and sometimes preying upon them herself. Despite her wild nature, she is quite good-natured when encountered unexpectedly or when she chooses to interact with others. She simply enjoys spending long periods alone and is very at peace with her solitude. Sokali isn't worshipped by followers of the Nineteen or the Tanir, despite some mortals in those regions knowing of her, but she is sometimes vaguely referenced or prayed to by travelers or those who traverse the colder areas of the Wedgelands in the Arctus Plateau. She is a much more prominent deity among the Bejak and the Wardcall, and the principal deity among the Fikost.

She is the daughter of Katu and Vekalla and is well known among mortals who worship the northern pantheon of Auris Bor as a goddess of winter, snow, and hunting. However, this worship often takes on a more animalistic, predatory slant. Many worship her as a natural deity who brings or follows the winter months, while others are suspicious of her existence and see blizzards as her domain, a domain they could well do without. Sokali gets along well with her family, but since her birth, she has always been distant and has sought out remote places. After her ascension, she does not see her mother and father very often, but she makes a point of traveling south every winter to see her sister Raineka.

Appearance

Most of Ember's Shard Gods resemble mortals, often walking among them as influential leaders or guiding figures. However, Sokali is an exception; she prefers to appear as a massive snow leopard, with an icy mane and sharp fangs made of a strange, solid white metal. When she chooses to present herself in a more approachable form to her followers, she appears as an elemental-like figure, a Wirrun woman composed of snow, with long, flowing white hair and clothing made of ice.

Influence and Followers

Sokali is revered by almost all of the Wirrun, who view her as their creator. They offer her meat from their kills and build enchanted markers and monuments of ice in the most desolate regions of northern Aterica to venerate her wild nature. The Wirrun do not have a priesthood as such, but they do have a group that calls itself the Wildclaws. These half-priests and half-druids transform primarily into snow leopards, and they teach other Wirrun about the natural world and survival skills. They also participate in the yearly Spirit Hunt, a ritual said to cross the boundary between life and death, where the Wildclaws somehow travel to the Spiritlands and stalk the ancient spirits of the dead as a test of skill.

Elsewhere in the world, she has a more traditional following among the Bejak and Wardcall cultures. Her followers in those places venerate her for her supposed ability to control the winters and to bless people's voyages and travel across vast distances.

Using Sokali as a Deity

Using Vekalla as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is for anyone who rejects traditional society and seeks a closer bond with nature. Sokali is a primal deity who values those who explore the natural world and develop deep relationships with nature itself. While she is not a Wild God, she is closely associated with their principles, attracting many druids and hermits who adopt animal and beast forms. Sokali regards her followers with a distant affection, never quite forming genuine bonds but still guiding and supporting them. She gently tries to teach them about the world's harsh realities. Her communication often uses visual scenes of hunts, nature, or life to convey meaning, leaving followers to interpret her messages.

Relationships

Sokali is the daughter of the Shard Gods, Katu and Vekalla. She was always a distant child who preferred the outdoors and nature. For a time, she lived with her parents on the Isle of Storms after her ascension, but she later moved on to explore the colder regions of the world, where she felt more comfortable in the harsh wilds. She often visits her family, where she met and formed a close bond with her sister, Raineka, and the two make sure to see each other at least once a year.

While in the north, after creating the Wirrun, she met the Shard God Vólun, and the two were initially fierce rivals. A long saga is sung of their relationship, but suffice it to say, eventually the two fell in love and had many children, including their two sons, Hrymer and Astric, and their daughter, Eirun. While she is often traveling, she can sometimes be found in the Kindred Hall in the Bejak city of Vellatagé, the official home of the Auris Bor itself.

Sokali has a strained relationship with her adopted daughter, Nerrissae. The two are often at each other's throats, literally, but they sometimes reconcile enough to be cordial.

It's said that Sokali has been attempting to hunt and kill Erisagosa for thousands of years, but the ancient Ice Wyrm has always escaped or fought her off. The true nature of their relationship, however, may be more complex.
Sokali.scoverview: Sokali is a Shard Goddess residing in the far north of the Aterican continent, associated with snow, winter, and journeys. She roams the coldest parts of the world, migrating southward as winter begins each year. Sokali is renowned for storms and shattered ice, with her gentle footsteps barely leaving a trace on the snow. As a deity of primal nature and is most comfortable appearing as a great snow leopard, observing the actions of her children, the Wirrun, from afar.

Spectra.name: Spectra
Spectra.text:
Areas of Concern: Magic, Knowledge, Mystery

Typical Followers: Scholars, Spellcasters

Domains: Knowledge, Other

Pantheons:@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.SXks9PsVzNyIPuDH]{Tanir}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6cMQOhdBouTFJlSl]{Sunalins}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Solaru}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.isH9tuxCUUP4GfWN]{Sentina}

Symbol: Swirling motes of magic, which never quite look the same twice.

Edict of Spectra

Embrace the knowledge of magic and the magic of knowledge.

While other entities might govern specific elements, Spectra is the Elder Goddess of Magic, who represents the delicate, high-level synthesis of the arcane and the craft of magic alongside the combination of the fundamental forces. Spectra is traditionally regarded as the patron of passionate scholars, exceptionally gifted mages, and those who have dedicated centuries to unraveling the nature of the cosmos. To the average mortal, she often appears aloof or utterly uninterested in the world’s affairs, as her edicts and ideas are notoriously dense, requiring obscure knowledge and a level of theoretical understanding that many cannot grasp even after a lifetime of study. However, this perceived coldness is merely a side effect of her intense focus. In truth, Spectra is a remarkably warm and excitable figure. When she finds a mind capable of following her logic, she becomes a tireless conversationalist, often found in the great libraries of the world, losing herself in ancient texts and the exchange of radical new ideas.

Spectra sees herself as a researcher, and her journey as a tireless pursuit of understanding. She is content to dedicate an unbelievable amount of resources, attention, and time to a new project, but is often undone by her lack of concentration and her inability to see a project through to the end. To many, this makes her appear wildly unfocused, hyper-fixating on one problem only to pivot and dive into another without a moment's notice.

Spectra makes the air taste like ozone, old parchment, and an unidentified flower in full bloom. The magic gets so thick you can practically stir it with a spoon. It’s wonderful for your spells, but terrible for your head. Everything around her just... vibrates.

~Laeora

Among the other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} and even among many @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods}, Spectra is very active and approachable, frequently walking the surface world in various guises to satisfy her endless curiosity. Despite this, she remains largely detached from the ordinary problems of mortals. Wars, successions, and petty politics rarely catch her eye, and her attention is drawn only to magical phenomena. On the rare occasions she offers direct assistance or power, it is almost never to resolve a local conflict, but rather to solve a magical mystery that has piqued her hyper-fixated interest. For Spectra, the preservation of mystical knowledge and the solving of a good puzzle will always take precedence over the rise and fall of empires.

Appearance


Spectra appears as a breathtaking convergence of arcane colors and symbols. As an Elder Goddess, she can take any form she wishes, but consistently prefers a feminine humanoid form that towers over mortal ancestors. She appears wrapped in a dress of the deepest midnight black, a darkness so profound it seems more like a light-absorbing void than woven fabric. At the nape and hem, constellations and swirling magical colors pulse and flash, twisting in complex and mesmerizing patterns of raw magical arcana. Fragments of uncast spells swirl in a perpetual, humming dance around her, as she moves, flickering into existence and then disappearing just as quickly. Her skin is as dark as polished obsidian with wide, glowing eyes of golden, glittering amber. Crowning this somber visage is her hair, a brilliant corona of pure arcane energy that matches the shifting colors of the magic on her dress. It is not styled but rather frames her head like the flares given off by a raging fire, shedding bright sparks of magic when she turns her head in excitement.

Influence and Followers

Spectra has a large following among scholars, librarians, and researchers, but mages and wizards are often her primary followers throughout Ember and the Cosmos. In some respects, she is a more "present" Elder God than her peers, and she can often be found in libraries, academies, and magical schools in equal measure. Her visits to these places are rare in the grand scheme of things, with many years or even centuries between them, but they are often documented with precision. Perhaps her most visited library is the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages} in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhiva}, where she has her own vast complex chambers, where she likes to surround herself with adoring followers, each attempting to gain her attention with a new discovery or idea. She is likely partially responsible for many leaps forward in magical understanding and the creation of new spells, and she forms close bonds with many bright Star Mages dedicated to knowledge and magic.

Her status as an Elder Goddess is rarely questioned among mortals due to both her long history and detailed accounts of her visits, as well as to her often widely disproportionate display of power. This was the case when she "removed" an exceptionally deadly monster of the Shroud from the Kaustic Hinterlands in [[/date AS1107]], alongside three mountains. Unlike many other deities, Spectra has a well-established personality, and mortals know she doesn't get involved in everyday affairs. This means that even if people are aware she is in the area, very few will seek her out. Instead, her arrival carries a dual reputation: she is a source of wonder, but also a harbinger of disaster. To see Spectra in the streets, or to hear that she is in the area, is a sign that a profound magical phenomenon or a catastrophic magical event is imminent. She doesn't cause the disaster; she is there to research it or see how things play out.

Spectra is very close to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia} and Fey of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, whose magical nature and mystery have always been deeply fascinating. Equally strong is her bond with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos} and Fiends of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}. While she remains indifferent to the bloody conflicts or the political maneuvering of the various Fiendish factions, she finds their fanatical, almost obsessive approach to research deeply relatable. She spends a great deal of her time on Signara itself, openly supporting several Fiends in their private laboratories. To Spectra, a Fiend’s willingness to spend a thousand years perfecting a single, obscure Sign is not a sign of madness, but a trait of a kindred spirit.

Using Spectra as a Deity

Using Spectra as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is to enter into an intense, high-level apprenticeship with a mentor who is as brilliant as she is distracted. Following her is less about rituals and worship and more about engaging in a continuous, frantic dialogue regarding the nature of the cosmos. She grants power to those who can provide her with fresh insights on magic, solve complex magical puzzles, or act as field testers for her latest theorems. Interacting with her is warm but chaotic. For a follower, this relationship requires a high degree of self-sufficiency and a thick skin, as Spectra’s hyper-fixated attention can drift as she engages with something else. She is the ultimate peer patron, supporting growth with genuine excitement, provided you can keep her interested.
Spectra.scoverview: Spectra is the Elder Goddess of the Magic, a passionate, enigmatic deity who wields her power in subtle and often difficult-to-understand ways. To the average mortal, she seems aloof, but scholars know her as a warm, hyper-focused intellectual who loves to discuss ideas in libraries and academies. Spectra is immensely powerful but easily distracted by the next great mystery.
Spectra.sgamemaster:
Like her fellow Elder Gods, Spectra emerged during the dawn of creation, a time when the world was still cooling, and the Heart of Ember pulsed with raw, violent bursts of energy. Her birth appears to have been a direct cosmic response to the disparate forces of the universe, and she acts as the "universal glue" or binder between these concepts. Many scholars believe her very existence is the reason arcane magic transitioned from raw energy into a structured force that mortals could eventually harness.

Throughout the history of the Cosmos, Spectra has been present for, or responsible for, numerous pivotal events. She typically prefers to observe magical phenomena from the background, rarely intervening directly, though not always. During the height of the Aedir, a group of Maegis attempted to summon a second sun to banish the night and create a literal empire of the sun. Though the Maegis viewed the experiment as a purely theoretical exercise, Spectra, upon noticing the attempt, began "tweaking" its parameters because she found the complex formula inefficient. In a flare of Magical energy that spread across the cosmos, and for two harrowing hours, seven suns of varying colors scorched the skies of Ember. The resulting empire-spanning chaos was immense but short-lived, and scholars still debate whether these suns were physical or merely localized echoes or illusions. Spectra, ever the academic, reportedly dismissed the catastrophe as a successful "trial run."

During the Shattering, Spectra was watching the events unfold, though her presence among the increasingly arrogant Aedir had become unwelcome. Observing from a distance, she narrowly avoided the horrific fate that befell the other deities caught within the tower at the moment of detonation. Despite her vast power, she found herself unable to prevent the cataclysmic forces unleashed by the Aedir’s hubris from spreading. As the world broke, Spectra was quickly overwhelmed by the sheer scale of the cataclysm.

However, as the subsequent Abyssal Shear threatened to tear reality apart entirely, Spectra took a painfully direct and desperate course of action. Unbeknownst to most, it was Spectra who stood at the ragged edge of the Weave, facing the Abyss alone. She prevented the complete erasure of the Cosmos by physically and magically holding the fabric of reality together, providing the vital stability Ven'avé required to weave the Shear shut. Throughout this agonizing process, Spectra simultaneously battled hosts of emerging Abyssal monsters that poured through the rift.

Following the closure of the Shear, Spectra vanished. She remained missing for nearly five hundred years, eventually reappearing as if no time had passed at all, save for one chilling difference: a cold, furious hatred for the Abyss and hidden scars that she refuses to speak of. While she remains warm in common conversation, her demeanor shifts dramatically at the mere mention of monsters. A deep flash of pain and visceral concern haunts her eyes, and she has been known to hunt down Abyssal Horrors personally, destroying them with a ruthless efficiency that stands in stark contrast to her usual scholarly whimsy.

People think mages and wizards are powerful, but the truth is, they are all just children playing in a yard with a very high fence. You don't feel the wind from the Abyss because Spectra is standing in the gap. Every time you look beyond and don't hear the void screaming back at you, that’s her. She’s the voice that keeps us sane.

Laeora

Prismardia Ward

While Spectra’s focus often seems scattered, she maintains a constant, subconscious shield across the cosmos. Since the Abyssal Shear, Spectra has maintained a singular spell that protects most mortal minds from the maddening effects of the Abyss. For mages and wizards, this acts as a kind of buffer; without it, attempting to research or learn about the Abyss or use abyssal energies like necromancy would be devastating and would immediately expose a caster’s consciousness to the cold, hungry echoes of the Abyss. While the danger is always present, there is a safety net in place. No one is truly aware of it, but it is present nonetheless.

Ven'avé.name: Ven'avé
Ven'avé.text:
Areas of Concern: Fate, Stars, The Weave

Typical Followers: Seers, Oracles

Domains: Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.isH9tuxCUUP4GfWN]{Sentina}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor}

Symbol: A star surround by glittering threads

Edict of Ven'avé

Playing with the intricate and complex paths of fate.

Ven'avé, the Weaver of the Sea of Stars, is the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Goddess} of fate, prophecy, and the intricate patterns of luck. Among her fellow Elder Gods, she is perhaps the most elusive, characterized by a shy, whimsical nature that keeps her far removed from mortals on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}. She is said to see @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.JUwFAaelI86yiscL]{the Cosmos} differently than any other being, viewing the world around her as a woven mass of threads that twist, turn, and disappear and reappear in tiny flashes of light. Through this rich tapestry, she can glimpse possible future events, which makes her appear distant and out of touch with reality to those who encounter her. Despite her reclusive nature, she shares a profound and ancient bond with all the other Elder Gods, all of whom view Ven'avé as the little sister. She is especially close to both @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, and when she is not playing with the paths of fate, she can sometimes be found pestering @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} with cryptic foretellings or trying to "help" @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} with her new magical obsession.

Ven'avé sees herself as a curator, or a creator, and, while others like to watch the cosmos, she prefers to play with fate itself, focusing on a specific past event and exploring could-have-beens and what-ifs. She has a notably relaxed, almost sedentary personality. She appears to others as lazy and unconcerned, but only because she is deeply occupied with her own very specific form of entertainment.

Ven'avé spends the vast majority of her existence within her hidden sanctum, the Vesvstar Loom, a massive, ancient asteroid that drifts through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars}. This workshop is sometimes anchored directly onto @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{the Weave} itself, much like the Inner Realms. Inside, the asteroid is rumored to house the Tapestry of Fate: a cosmic wonder created by Ven'avé, which serves as both a record of the past and a constantly shifting reflection of what Ven'avé herself creates by predicting the future and creating alternate versions of events long past. The Vesvstar Loom is a place of profound secrets, and few have ever set foot on its sacred floors, guarded by numerous safeguards, wards, and defenses created and maintained by every other Elder God. It is considered one of the safest places in the cosmos.

You’d think a Goddess of Fate and an Elder Goddess, someone with a direct line to every past event and the future, would be a historian’s dream, a walking library of perfect clarity. That is, until you meet her.. and you realize she’s less of a grand oracle and more of a jumbled mess who looks like she’s just rolled out of bed on the wrong side of the cosmos. She isn't interested in recording history; she’s too busy trying to remember what she did yesterday and whether her current game is shaping up to be a "good" one.

~Laeora

Appearance

Ven'avé appears as a wisp-like figure of gentle, glowing starlight. Her small stature often leads people to mistake her for a teenager rather than an Elder Goddess. Her long white hair gradually dissolves into shimmering threads of starlight, which can be cut to reveal glimpses of fate. She typically speaks in soft, sleepy tones, but prefers to communicate through subtle shifts in her motions and lights, understood only by other Elder Gods. She glides through the air with a weightless, curious grace, and in her presence, mortals often feel both instantly calm and strangely intimidated, as if she can see through them and glimpse their future choices.

Influence and Followers

Ven'avé is not a principal deity per se, with no large temples or large groups of followers anywhere in Ember or even the cosmos. (Except by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhiva} people, who regard her as a somewhat distant patron, overall, though, they are more closely linked to Spectra) This is not because she is an unknown force but rather because she is so well known that people generally understand her complex nature. Luck and fate are not forces that can be relied upon, and although mortals may hold the odd charm of luck or fate and may ask the Weaver for her blessing in desperate situations, such prayers are rarely, if ever, answered.

Using Ven'avé as a Deity

Using Ven'avé as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is an exercise in immense patience. Unlike more active gods, Ven'avé is almost unusable for the average devotee. She does not seek people out, ignores the calls of even the most desperate, and doesn't see things like mortals do. Following her is a path usually reserved for the Star Mages or obsessive seers, and oracles who are comfortable with a deity who feels more like a distant memory than an active patron. In extremely rare occurrences, she might offer a cryptic, half-muttered observation about a thread of fate that hasn't even happened yet, which can make following her extremely frustrating.
Ven'avé.scoverview: Ven'avé is the Elder Goddess of fate and prophecy, overseeing the protective barrier of the Weave and stars upon its surface. She sees the Ember cosmos through a lens of millions of tiny threads representing every possible outcome in existence, and doesnt seem to be able to see the world like any other being. Despite her immense power, she is a very relaxed, if not lazy, deity, not out of apathy but out of profound contentment, viewing fate as a whimsical, ever-changing game.
Ven'avé.sgamemaster:
While Ven'avé has been present since creation and is deeply tied to the Weave and Stars, she doesnt seem to be have been impactful in any significant events, mainly staying to herself. She sometimes appears in the surface world, but her visits are extremely rare. During the Shattering, Ven'avé’s role was a silent, nearly unobserved struggle in the background. To Ven'avé, the Shattering wasn't just an explosion, it was as if a jagged blade had been run through her, severing millions of threads and causing the entire Tapestry of Fate to begin unraveling. It's said that Ven'avé was one of the few who knew what was coming, but couldn't see the exact nature of the cataclysm, and while she was able to warn and guide the Shent seers of the time, she could do little else but wait until the Shattering occurred.

When the Abyssal Shear began, the literal tearing of the Weave wounded Ven'avé so severely that the other Elder Gods believed she had been killed. However, as Spectra stood at the edge of the rift and Alara swept across the cosmos like a burning fury, Ven'avé appeared at last, working in the shadow of Spectra's protection, carefully repairing the delicate cosmic barrier of the Weave.

Sigil.name: Sigil
Sigil.text:
Areas of Concern: Research, Knowledge Preservation

Typical Followers: Librarians, Researchers

Domains: Knowledge, Peace

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}

Symbol: A quill tip in a circle of ink

Edict of Sigil

Preserve knowledge for future generations.

Sigil prizes knowledge and information above all other things, and has dedicated his life and his divinity to collecting and parsing the world's knowledge. Born during an era of great violence, he believes that knowledge, if well-maintained and protected, can create legacies of understanding and information that outlive and honor those who created them.

Even for a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{shard god}, trying to capture the knowledge of the world is a monumental task, and Sigil has used much of the magic he gained during his ascension to help him find, absorb, and catalogue as much information as possible.
