His set of magical tools and helpers include his living beard, which helps to catalogue books and scrolls; his home of @UUID[JournalEntry.tZhj2UzXEN4cw4nl]{Oldcraft Lodge}, which hides an ever-expanding library within its simple riverbank frame; and the ink he uses, which translates his passing thoughts and research ideas into notes that he always vows to go through later and never seems to get around to.

Though Sigil can at times appear small and frail, and has less pure power than many of the other shard gods, his shrewd understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of the people, items, and places around him is not to be underestimated. Sigil became a shard god in part because of his willingness to combine pure research with adventure, and while he is now more focused on collecting knowledge from books and scholars than unearthing it in distant lands, he retains a keen insight into others. He often uses this to find and mentor those rare mortals who he believes are true seekers and protectors of knowledge, encouraging them to continue to pursue their love of knowledge and share all that they find with him in deep and often meandering conversations about the nature of the world and life itself.

Appearance

Sigil takes the guise of an elderly human man whose small body is nearly dwarfed by the enormous white beard that wraps around him, glowing from within as if it has a life of its own. Sigil often uses his beard as a second pair of hands, storing scrolls within it and using it to grab books from the shelf. This, along with the magical ink that often spills from his work, flying into the air to arrange itself into letters on one of his parchments, gives him the appearance of someone who is very still while the world is in motion around them. Some speculate that Sigil's choice of an elderly human speaks to the wisdom and knowledge that those who are advanced in age are assumed to have, but he has never confirmed or denied his reasons.

Influence & Followers

Thanks in part to the reputation of the Oldcraft Lodge as a place for knowledge and study, Sigil is well known and well regarded across the Arctus Plateau. His Lodge is notable for being larger on the inside than it is on the outside, and holds a number of carefully catalogued books, tomes, scrolls, and treatises on any manner of subjects. Though Sigil is fond of the written word, he also captures stories, using magic to transcribe a tale as it was told and store it among his other files.

Despite his popularity on the Arctus Plateau, Sigil has relatively few direct followers. Even those he mentors or who spend time in Oldcraft Lodge learning from his library often do not count themselves as his followers, seeing him as more of a peer than a deity. This suits Sigil well, as he has no desire to give of his divine power to others, preferring to keep his relationships with mortals to a meeting of the minds than an imparting of divinity.

Using Sigil as a Deity

Using Sigil as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or general devotion is more common in the Arctus Plateau than elsewhere, but is still relatively rare. For those who do follow Sigil, he is more likely to provide the knowledge of what is needed to win a battle than to participate in it directly. Outside of his followers, Sigil is most well known on the Arctus Plateau, but his pursuit of knowledge puts him in touch with scholars elsewhere and ensures that his name is at least somewhat familiar, even in places where he is not commonly discussed.

While Sigil's closest relationships have been with the mortals that he mentors, he welcomes any of the members of the Nineteen who wish to stop by Oldcraft Lodge and share their understanding of the world with him. He is particularly fond of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé}, despite her association with fire and his with vellum, because of her ongoing fight for the homelands his parents fled from, and occasionally meets @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae} in secret for midnight tea to discuss whether or not the legends of her vengeful ways are true knowledge or false gossip.
Sigil.scoverview: Sigil prizes knowledge and information above all else. Small and bookish, the shard god often called the Elder Scholar is rarely wrong about anything and can be an excellent source of information for those who need it. He's also known on the Arctus Plateau for his home, the Oldcraft Lodge, which has an extensive library. Open to anyone who would visit in the pursuit of knowledge or because they need a safe haven, it is one of the most extensive collections of written knowledge on Ember. Though he is often too busy with research to delve deeply into mortal problems, and can be most often found bent over a large book, he has a few favorite mortals, mentoring those whose love for learning resonate with his own.
Sigil.sgamemaster:
Surprisingly for a god of information and knowledge, Sigil does not often speak much about his own path to becoming a Shard God, though rumor holds that there is a book in his library that notes every element of his past life, filed in such a way that only the most determined researcher would ever find it.

What is more commonly known about Sigil is that he was born in Moiran Lands to refugees who fled the nation as it was being consumed by undeath. Though he aspires to value all knowledge equally, Sigil has a slight resistance towards knowledge that could be use to create more undeath, and a soft spot for all those who are forced to flee their homelands. His creation of Oldcraft Lodge in the center of Arctus Plateau gave him a place to store the knowledge and books that he collects, but also to provide a place of refuge to those who might need it.

Driven to learn more about the homeland that his parents left behind , and seeking a place of security in an insecure time and place, Sigil turned to facts and knowledge as his bedrock. He became a researcher, fascinated by ancient and lost knowledge, and often accompanied adventuring groups in search of artifacts to help him build his collection of ancient scrolls and manuscripts. During one of these adventures, he followed a text tracking the location of a powerful artifact to the Heart Crystal that transformed him into a god.

Alar.name: Alar
Alar.text:
Areas of Concern: Creation, Mortality, Protection

Typical Followers: Dragons, Beings of the Inner Realms

Domains: Life, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.SXks9PsVzNyIPuDH]{Tanir}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6cMQOhdBouTFJlSl]{Sunalins}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Solaru}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.isH9tuxCUUP4GfWN]{Sentina}

Symbol: An ascending comet

Edict of Alar

Protect those in need.

Alar is a supremely powerful being, the first @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder God}. Unlike the Other Elders, Alar does not have a singular cosmic aspect that she seems to be associated with. While some call her the Goddess of Life and Creation, she is also associated with various other ideas, such as Tyranny, Deception, Ambition, and Protection. However, she often rejects such rigid labels and categories, finding them too restrictive for a cosmos that is ever-changing. She uses this ambiguity to her advantage, wielding her powers with masterful subtlety and nuance, preferring to mask herself behind a myriad of mortal guises and shifting personas to better navigate the complexities of existence.

Alar sees herself as a guardian of life and a protector of mortals and ancestries across the cosmos. She is a figure of immense resilience and deep empathy, becoming emotionally attached to mortals and seeking to understand their complex lives. However, she is often her own harshest critic, often replaying the choices and mistakes she made eons ago in her mind, wondering if a kinder word or a swifter action would have resulted in a different outcome. When she fails to protect a mortal she cares about or a people she adores, she doesn't just feel regret, she feels a profound, personal failure that can trigger her volatile temper or send her into periods of mournful isolation and withdrawal. She is a guardian who desperately wants to save everyone, struggling with the reality that even a goddess cannot fix every broken thing.

Outwardly, Alar masks this internal turmoil with a distinctly confident and expressive personality. Her identity is a complex tapestry that has evolved across the ages, allowing her to be both chaotic and lawful, compassionate and capricious. She often indulges in the games and stories of mortal kingdoms and empires, limiting her vast power to engage in petty conflicts or interfering with the plans of other deities, sometimes for no reason other than to distract herself from her own heavy thoughts. While she is more than capable of using her knowledge and physical form to manipulate or appeal to mortals' desires, this calculated exterior is governed by a strict personal code. She abides by clear rules and draws firm lines regarding how she engages with others, ensuring that even her most capricious whims never violate her fundamental duty as a protector of life.

Ancient Form

Alar was once a very different deity. In the years after she arose, extending throughout creation and the entire @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}, she used her power more openly to stoke conflicts, manipulating events in her favor as she saw fit and at a whim. During this time, she appeared in a masculine form and was worshiped by few upon the surface, sometimes attacking or confronting both other deities and mortals in the pursuit of her goals. Her only true followers during this time were the beings of the Inner Realms, especially the Fiends, and her influence shaped mortals' perceptions so much that even today, many distrust and fear her. She slowly changed throughout the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of the Tower}, becoming far less antagonistic. It was after @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} that her feminine form appeared in full, and references to her masculine aspects are extremely rare in the present.

People get confused when they find those old stone carvings of a male horned figure with Alar’s eyes. Many believe it’s a different god entirely… but it’s her.

I think that’s why she’s so hard on herself. I've spent many an evening sipping wine with Alar since the Shattering, and she is deeply remorseful of her actions in eons past. She remembers how it felt to just do what she wanted and break anyone in her way. She has changed in so many ways, and every time she cares and attempts to understand, she’s simply trying to make up for ancient mistakes. She isn't just seeking forgiveness from the world; she’s seeking it from herself.

~Laeora

Appearance

Alar is quite comfortable changing her form, often appearing as a member of any mortal ancestry upon Ember to wander the world unnoticed. When she chooses to reveal her power more openly, she appears as a towering figure, sometimes reaching twelve feet in height, resembling a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Human}-@UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae} mixed ancestry with an incredibly extensive crown of horns sprouting from her head. Her elegant arms and legs possess an unnatural flexibility, flowing with a strange, otherworldly grace as she moves. Her eyes are said to glow intensely with the raw power of creation, shining with the brilliance of gold and deep red fire. Across her pale skin and hair, twisting patterns of gold and silver constantly shift and flow, tracing the path of her movements.

In the most ancient stories, it is said that when Alar truly wishes to unleash her full power, she assumes a colossal, draconic form known as the Wyrm of Creation. In this aspect, she is described as possessing six wings, three tails, and a fanged maw of razor-sharp teeth, spanning many miles in size. However, it is worth noting that tales of this form are largely based on surviving accounts from the chaotic aftermath of the Shattering, and scholars debate whether these descriptions are literal truths, over exaggerations, or entirely fictitious myths.

Influence and Followers

Alar is loved, worshipped, hated, and cursed by all kinds of beings across the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}. She is a divisive figure who can often split opinions within societies, cultures, and even individual families. As such, Alar is rarely worshipped openly, with only a few shrines and temples dotted about the world. Most of her followers are clerics and priests who preach her teaching under the guise of working with other gods. In some cultures, Alar is culturally disliked, and her worship can lead to persecution as they view her as a breaker of the natural cycle and name her Soul Stealer. Alar spends most of her time among mortals and, in rare situations, reveals her divinity as an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Goddess}. Still, she prefers working with individuals rather than organizations or nations. Several first-generation @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.GRs2vgeVsDpWPqjh]{Drakons} have worked with her since their creation, understanding and revering her in ways few other mortals have been privy to.

She is also worshipped with a strange fanaticism by the beings from the Inner Realms, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos}, as many believe she is their creator. While they would do practically anything Alar commands, she tends to stay out of their circles of concern and doesn't align with their goals, ambitions, or politics. This control and devotion has its uses, and techinically, Alar could control the most powerful combined force in the cosmos if she so desired. However, she has little interest and has largely stayed away from the Inner Realms other than bringing souls to them as part of her ideas around the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7#eternal-souls]{Eternal Soul}.

Using Alar as a Deity.

Using Alar as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is a path of empathy and redemption. Alar is an intensely personal and expressive presence, and she expects her followers to act as her eyes and hands in the world, seeking out conflict to resolve it, protecting the sanctity of Ember, and defending life wherever it is threatened by true evil. Alar is a deeply supportive patron who genuinely cares for her followers, but she can also be demanding; she is her own harshest critic, and she often pushes her champions to be equally self-reflective and resilient.

Her magic is said to be vibrant and fluid, often carrying a warmth that feels like a physical embrace. However, this connection is not without its weight. Because she carries the remorse of her ancient, aggressive past, her power can sometimes flare with a volatile temper if her followers witness cruelty or injustice. Most importantly, Alar is the only Elder God who will directly intervene on behalf of her followers in times of great need.
Alar.scoverview: The first of the Elder Gods is the ancient deity known as Alar, who (according to her own memory) was born before the formation of The Weave during the process of Creation. An entity that has lived countless years, Alar is known to actively walk the surface world, interacting with mortals and solving their individual problems where she can. Known by many names and forms, Alar's complex nature and history — including her creation of Ember's inscrutable Dragons — mean that she is often blessed and cursed by mortals in equal measure.
Alar.sgamemaster:
Ive often spoken with Alar about her own creation, a subject I find personally fascinating.

She believes she was formed before the Weave even took shape, speaking of those void-black memories with a terrifying glint in her golden eyes, with a casualness that chills me to the bone. If this is true, it suggests something remarkable about her role in the Cosmos, and Alar may only an Elder God in name.

What fascinates me is that if Alar was created or formed before existence as we know it, how exactly was she born? Is her essence, life, and protection, or something else entirely? She already seems to hide a great deal of her powers from mortals; could she not hide more from other deities, even her brothers and sisters?

~Laeora

The history and story of Alar is vast, woven with countless accounts of her meddling in mortal affairs and steering the course of numerous cultures. Some of her most enduring legends include the Seduction of the King of Oderita, where she reportedly donned a mortal guise to manipulate a lustful king, and her role as the hidden puppeteer behind the Brothers Hexan and Jori, orchestrating a rivalry that reshaped the political landscape of the ancient Oaken. Beyond these, she is whispered to be the founder of the Aedir Maegis and the entity responsible for creating the Silent Hold.

While the title "Horned Mother" is frequently used by mortals on Ember to describe Alar, driven by the common belief that she is the creator of the Daemos and Fiends. This is not strictly accurate, but the confusion is understandable, as she deliberately based her original, ancient form on the aesthetics of the Daemos and the Wyrms of Akon. Despite this, Alar does align more closely with the beings of the Inner Realms regarding the fundamental nature of the soul. This shared perspective has led to a historic disagreement with Sockets over the nature of mortality itself. Rejecting the idea of souls traveling to the Spiritlands, Alar believes that guiding souls to the Inner Realms of Primordis, Signara, and Luxarum (making them immortal) is a purer and more revitalizing way to preserve the reality of the Cosmos. Many powerful beings within these Inner Realms share her philosophy, frequently traveling to the surface world to convince, deceive, or strike pacts with mortals to achieve this goal.

She is also said to have been instrumental in the preservation of Leviathans and other prehistoric creatures at the end of the Age of Beasts. Instead of allowing them to simply fade into obscurity or be trapped within the confines of Jurin, it was Alar who ensured gaps remained and hid many creatures within the Pathways in hidden enclaves.

The Shattering

By far, her most important role in recent history was after the Shattering. While Alar had been vaguely aware of the Aedir and their scheming atop the Apex of the Sun Tower, she was relatively unconcerned. Unfortunately, she was tragically wrong as the sudden, violent shock of the Shattering tore through the fabric of reality. Caught completely off guard, Alar was struck by a profound and paralyzing despair at the sheer devastation the blow dealt to the Cosmos and the millions of souls that perished in moments in the aftermath.

The Abyssal Shear

The Shattering was only the beginning; the Abyssal Shear followed swiftly, tearing open the fabric of the protective Weave and allowing the destructive, alien forces of the Abyss and the Outer Gods to flood into the cosmos. Alar describes her feelings during this time as "a fury beyond reason," viewing these entities as utterly evil and an "alien rot" within "her" universe. Unleashing her most terrifying aspect, Alar took the form of the Wyrm of Creation and flew into the Sea of Stars to meet the invasion head-on. She smashed through the invading ranks time and again, obliterating countless horrors until she finally clashed with a terrifying entity above the Moon of Akon: the Herald of the Whispering Choir. On the surface of Ember, cultures recorded the battle in myths as violent flashes of golden and black magic flickering across the night sky. The Herald, despite its cosmic dread, was no match for Alar’s raw creative power and was utterly destroyed.

In the aftermath, Alar continued onwards, hunting down large pockets of Abyssal monsters lingering on the surface world, the moons, and the Inner Realms. However, it soon became clear that monsters were adapting, sliding into the dark, forgotten corners of the cosmos where they could no longer be easily reached. While the Abyssal Shear was a moment of absolute terror for the universe, it drastically altered Alar’s perspective. Witnessing true, unthinking evil gave her a deeper, more profound belief in the value of life on Ember. Through this reflection, she became significantly kinder and more curious about mortal affairs, transitioning fully into her feminine form. Consequently, her ancient masculine names and titles have since faded into the shadows of history.

As the Abyssal Shear was finally closed by Ven'avé, Alar witnessed the horrific toll the conflict had taken; the moon of Akon was broken, and its native Wyrms were dead or dying in droves. Desperate to preserve their legacy and provide the cosmos with guardians against future incursions, Alar decided to act. She sought to create a new creature that would use the Wyrms' immense strength while possessing the resilience to resist the Abyss. She called these new creatures Dragons. However, in her urgency to heal the world, Alar was perhaps too rash. She failed to fully account for the lingering, corrupting influence of the Abyss that had already seeped into the essence of the fallen Wyrms and the Cosmos. Rather than being the noble protectors she envisioned, almost all Dragons have since become beings of untold destruction. Alar has been working tirelessly to correct this mistake ever since. While she does not hate her children, she openly admits that her lack of foresight has cost the lives of countless mortals over the ages. This failure remains one of her deepest burdens, a lingering shadow that fuels her modern-day self-criticism and her drive to be more careful when unleashing her full powers.

Pathwalker.name: Pathwalker
Pathwalker.scoverview: Pathwalker is a name known to very few, having resurfaced only recently after the discovery and translation of ancient Shent texts by members of the Anachraenum. Due to the lack of information, a debate rages regarding Pathwalker's status as a deity: some argue their age implies they must be an Elder God, while many believe they were simply one of the Shent's many lesser deities.
Pathwalker.sgamemaster:
Pathwalker is the most enigmatic of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods}, often referred to by scholars as "The Lost." While the other Elder Gods claimed the heavens, the stars, or the afterlife, Pathwalker seems to have been created to guard the tangible matter of existence itself. He is the guardian of the material @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, serving as the architect of the subterranean @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} that bear his name.

Pathwalker eternally roams these underground passageways, controlling, protecting, and shaping the flow of energy and power from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. Very few are aware of his existence, and even the most ancient cultures possessed little knowledge of his purpose, save for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giants}. As their creator, the Giants both learned from and revered Pathwalker, acting as his hands in the deep places of the world. In the present age, knowledge of Pathwalker has only recently reemerged following the translation of ancient texts by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}. However, a fierce debate rages regarding his status; many scholars believe he was merely a lesser deity of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}, rather than a true Elder.

Pathwalker is the youngest of the Elder Gods, often called The Last Elder. During @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.0bkmoi8aSFvbaCi0]{the First Dawn}, the Pathways were volatile and chaotic, constantly shifting course and triggering cataclysmic disruptions on the surface. Pathwalker, aided by his Giant servants, worked tirelessly to settle this turmoil, calming the elemental chaos into the stable, static network known today. These Pathways have remained unchanging for thousands of years, yet they remain vital. Should a Pathway shift its course now, it would likely result in a localized cataclysm or a disaster of global proportions, and Pathwalker continues his primordial task to keep these events from happening.

The lonely god, the wanderer in the dark. He trusted his children with boundless knowledge, and they used that knowledge to hurt him. Every tremor in the earth feels like an anguished cry of a failed father.

~Laeora

Appearance

In the rare texts that describe them, Pathwalker is said to have no true fixed form. But he is often described as towering, being made of the very layers of the earth. A colossal giant-like figure, with a body made of an intricate blend of stone, rock, and metal. Long bands of black hair hang limply from a lowered head, and he trudges among the countless caverns and tunnels of the Pathways. Great plumes of steam swirl and seethe from cracks and crevices in his chest, and an almost unbearable heat surrounds him at all times. When he moves through the Pathways, the ground doesn't break; it parts for him like water, sealing behind him as if he were never there.

Influence and Followers

Pathwalker has no followers to speak of any longer, as he no longer responds to prayers nor seemingly cares much for mortal life. He was once worshipped as the only deity by the Primordial Giants and then as a minor deity by the ancient Pantheon of the Shent Giants, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.isH9tuxCUUP4GfWN]{Sentina}, but since the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} and @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, he disappeared from all records, and any remaining followers are lone Giant hermits.

Using Pathwalker

Using Pathwalker as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is a near-impossible task. Pathwalker is an inaccessible deity, and few, if anyone, would ever be able to get through his vast guilt and distrust of mortal beings.

Sockets.name: Sockets
Sockets.text:
Areas of Concern: The Soul, Death, Rebirth

Typical Followers: Scholars, Gravekeepers, the Mourning

Domains: Peace, Order

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.isH9tuxCUUP4GfWN]{Sentina}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Solaru}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6cMQOhdBouTFJlSl]{Sunalins}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.SXks9PsVzNyIPuDH]{Tanir}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor}

Symbol: An abstract symbol representing the soul

Edict of Sockets

Safeguard the passage of souls.

Sockets is, to put it mildly, a stubborn, cantankerous, and sarcastic personality who delights in sharp wit and playful banter. On the surface, he frequently makes light of his station, cracking jokes about death and the afterlife, yet he remains meticulously careful with his wording and actions. Beneath this openly quarrelsome persona lies a deity deeply committed to his role as the Keeper of Souls. While other gods might demand worship, build sprawling empires, or maintain a cold distance from the living, Sockets is a professional who carries out his duties with tireless dedication. He is an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder God} who has seen every story, every tragedy, and every joke the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} has to offer, yet even after eons, he still offers a smile and a wink to those who need a small measure of comfort in the face of the end.

This fierce protectiveness defines his existence. Sockets views every soul as a precious fragment of the cosmos and sees himself more as a humble shepherd than the shadowy, frightening figure mortals often imagine. This approachability is reflected not only in his mannerisms but also in his appearance; he frequently shifts his form to blend into various cultures. Though he is the master of Mort’olis (The Spiritlands), he spends as much time walking the surface of Ember as he does his own realm, observing the living with the keen, patient interest of a gardener watching over a particularly rowdy patch of weeds.

Sockets does not hunt wayward spirits or drag them to the afterlife by force; instead, he possesses a seemingly limitless cosmic gravity. This spiritual pull serves as the natural destination for every soul that leaves its body, creating the path that leads inevitably to the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WmwoaJUw9oosRtS5]{Eternas} on the shores of the Spiritlands. Through his constant presence, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} itself functions, though it remains a mystery whether Sockets is the true architect of this cycle or if he is simply the hands-on steward for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. He also serves as the living battery for the Soul Barrier that keeps Mort'olis contained. He ensures the dead remain in their realm, not out of cruelty, but out of the firm belief that a spirit lingering too long in the living world would merely exist in a rotting limbo. While his principal servants, the Servants of the Deathless, handle the bulk of the Rite of Passing, Sockets is known to personally appear for souls of particular note. If a mortal has done something truly extraordinary, funny, or brave, they might find a man in a dusty coat waiting for them at the threshold, offering a joke instead of judgment as he walks them toward the gates of Eternas.

People call him grumpy, but I call him honest. Alar is too busy being a hero. Spectra gives me a headache, and Lantyr isn’t exactly a thrilling conversationalist. Sockets is the only one who feels like a friend. I love the crusty old fart, truly. He’s the kind of person who understands you at a glance, shows real empathy, and places a gentle hand on your shoulder.

~Laeora

Appearance

Sockets can take many shapes and forms, often appearing as various different ancestries, but most commonly he appears as a sharply dressed older Human with a short, neatly trimmed white beard and short-cropped hair. His skin is aged, leathery, and worn, with laugh lines and wrinkles in the corners of his eyes. Wearing a worn short coat, long trousers, and a high-neck shirt in an unknown ancient style. His most striking feature, however, is his eyes, which appear as inky, bottomless black voids with the spinning light of an orange star as a pupil.

Influence and Followers

Sockets enjoys a sprawling following across the surface of Ember. His followers often form local communities or monastic orders dedicated to assisting their neighbors with the transition from life to death. These priests and caretakers teach that the end of life is not a tragedy to be feared, but a natural passage to the next life, a place of reflection where the soul can gain new experiences and process their old life. Usually, Sockets priests and clerics are also focused on guiding and helping people through trials, teaching that new experiences, both good and bad, and the challenges of a long life are something to be celebrated.

Sockets himself is a rare visitor to these temples. His visits are often separated by centuries or even millennia, leading to a cycle in which his grandest cathedrals fall into ruin and are rebuilt by new generations, without him ever noticing the gap. He is famously hands-off with his organized religious order, preferring to communicate with individual followers and priests. He is well-known for his fondness for certain individuals and on very rare occasions, Sockets finds a particular mortal’s wit, perspective, or spirit so worthy that he grants them a reprieve from the Soul Cycle. These individuals continue to experience the world for hundreds of years, bypassing death until they are finally ready to move on.

While Sockets wanders the surface, the daily administration of the afterlife falls to his principal followers, called the Servants of the Deathless. Residing within the towering, pearlescent spires of Eternas, these entities are no longer mortal, but their exact nature remains mysterious. Many are the extraordinary souls who, upon reaching the Spiritlands, chose to stay and serve rather than move toward oblivion.

Using Sockets as a Deity

Using Sockets as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron is a path for the pragmatic and the empathetic. Unlike the distant silence of other Elder Gods, Sockets is a conversationalist who offers his followers small snippets of wisdom, witty barbs, and sharp-tongued observations. He rarely provides direct intervention, preferring to act as a reliable guide. While he may mock your mistakes or groan about the extra work you’re causing him, there is a profound, hidden warmth behind his words. To follow him is to have a partner in the tireless labor of life. A patron who treats you like a friend and ensures that even in the darkest hour, you’ll at least have a good joke to lean on.
Sockets.scoverview: Sockets is one of the younger Elder Gods born in the later stages of creation, as the Heart of Ember was being encased in the rocky matter that would form the world. He is the master of the Souls Cycle and is worshipped as the God of Death and Souls upon the World of Ember. He is known by many names and almost every culture across the ages has some knowledge and reference to his role and place in the cosmos. No being on Ember, save himself, and perhaps Alar are immune to death, eventually, all beings end up in his care and Sockets is a patient god.
Sockets.sgamemaster:
Sockets came into being shortly after the Heart of Ember was encased within the rocky shell that would become the world. Though he is an Elder God, he is technically younger than many of his peers, a fact that Alar finds incredibly amusing and frequently teases him about. Sockets instinctively understood his role in the cosmos from the moment of his creation. He set about carving the Spiritlands from the still-forming surface of the world, raising the pearlescent spires of Eternas and weaving the Soul Barrier. It was during these eons of quiet stewardship that the Soul Cycle was perfected, ensuring that every spark of life had a safe harbor to return to.

When the Shattering occurred, Sockets was within the Spiritlands, tending to the city of Eternas. The metaphysical shockwave of the Shattering and the death of millions in an instant struck him like a physical blow, leaving him dazed and confused for hours as the very foundations of the cosmos trembled. Yet, the worst was yet to come. As the Abyssal Shear tore into reality, it introduced the horrifying new corruption called the Undeath. For the first time, the dead did not flow toward Eternas; they twisted, rotted, and their spirits warped, losing themselves in madness, and finally rising again as undead. Seeing the great Aedir cities and the defenders of the Starshield turn into shambling husks enraged Sockets beyond reason. For the first time in his existence, the sarcastic guide vanished, replaced by a vengeful Elder God who felt personally responsible for ending the threat himself.

Sockets spent the following years in tireless battles, one after another, walking the surface of Ember to personally incinerate pockets of undead and annihilate Abyssal Horrors and monsters. However, this prolonged, direct intervention took a devastating toll. Whether from the sheer exhaustion of the task or the corruptive nature of the undead themselves, Sockets was gradually drained. He slowly realized with grim clarity that his powers had been significantly diminished, and he drew back, heartbroken and defeated by the weight of his own perceived failure to eradicate such a threat. In the present age, Sockets no longer fights the undead directly, despite wishing he could. He prefers to empower mortal champions to do the fighting for him. He harbors a private, lingering fear that should he ever lose his temper and unleash his full power again, he might lose control, and his powers would disrupt his spiritual pull or shatter the Soul Barrier, causing untold chaos.

Finor.name: Finor
Finor.scoverview: Very little is known of this deity except for ancient texts and long, sad songs.
Finor.sgamemaster:
Finor is the only @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder God} considered truly dead by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}. As the God of Time and the Steward of Continuity, he was a resolute, knightly figure who walked the world with a profound sense of duty and honor. Finor was never a passive observer; he was an active participant in mortal affairs, spending centuries living among common people. He guided their growth, taught them the arts of building and philosophy, and shared in their joy. In times of pain and hardship, he was a constant comfort, ensuring that even the darkest nights eventually gave way to the dawn.

In the ancient days, Finor was said to have spent countless ages in the company of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.CNUDzx1WE09XXJZ8]{Wyrms} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, sharing the secrets of the temporal flow and the intricacies of cosmic order. He served as the moral conscience of the Elder Gods, often clashing with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, who was, at that time, a much more aggressive and often destructive deity. Through his patience and wisdom, Finor often tempered Alar’s conflict-driven nature.

However, his unwavering desire for peace ultimately led to his destruction. During the onset of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4v37uAs6nY1Pc00M]{Forsaken War}, Finor attempted to mediate a truce between the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.186yO79YKDxPh0qT]{Theroch}. He held a fundamental belief that with enough time, any wound could be healed and any enmity settled. He was tragically wrong. The Theroch struck him down, and for the first and only time in existence, an Elder God died.

The shock of his murder enraged the Cosmos. In the wake of his fall, a colossal and unprecedented alliance was formed. The Aedir, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.o38uqC8NLxOWxA4i]{Vaznor}, and Seydri stood alongside a host of various deities. Even the Wyrms of Akon, and forces of the Inner Realms, Such as a legion of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.qtxBDYBNwKhD7nWd]{Celestials} from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}, descended to join the fray, all unified by a single, burning purpose: to avenge the Knight of Time.

You have to understand, Finor wasn't like the other Elders of that age. He was a gentle soul who defended the helpless, cooked in people's kitchens, and worked alongside ordinary people on farms or in smithies. He was the god who helped fix the roof of your house and then stayed for the stew. So when the Theroch betrayed him... they didn't just kill a deity. They murdered a friend.

~Laeora

WARNING

Finor is a complex character beyond even the context of the Setting Compendium and has a great deal of secret lore associated with him, so spoilers ahead. The following is a brief summary of some of the hidden truths about the character, but further details will come in time.

  • He is the creator of Jarn.

  • He is the creator of Humanity.

  • He is responsible for the existence of Soulbound.

  • He may not be dead, as the God of Time, he may exist beyond the known Cosmos.

Appearance

In his true form, Finor appeared as a noble, knightly figure with short silvery hair shot through with threads of copper and bronze. He wore armor of impossibly complex machinery that shifted and clicked as he moved, a living manifestation of time’s intricate workings, and upon his back, he wielded a massive two-handed blade named Eternities End. He would often transform and appear as one of the many mortal ancestries, and according to Aedir texts, he was most fond of his @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae} persona.

Influence and Followers

Finor has few followers on the surface of Ember. His very existence is disputed, and very few are even aware of him. He was worshipped by some ancient cultures, and there are depictions and mentions of him in many Aedir, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}, and Vaznor tales and stories, but no present-day cultures consider him to be a deity of renown.

Using Finor

Using Finor as a source of power is fundamentally different from any other deity, as he is an Absent God. Because Finor is dead, he is inaccessible to the living; he cannot hear prayers, grant direct boons, or speak to mortal followers.

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound}, however, can choose to worship him if they become aware of his existence through lost Aedir texts or Chronal Resonance events. There is no divine guidance, however, as Finor seems more like a lingering ghost. Worshipping him is a lonely, scholarly, and often tragic path, as any Soulbound followers are essentially trying to draw water from a dry well, relying on their own discipline to harness the fading fragments of a once-glorious deity.

Lanespear.name: Lanespear
Lanespear.text:
Areas of Concern: War, Martial Strength, Monster Fighting

Typical Followers: Soldiers, Fighters, Waerds

Domains: War, Order

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: A war spear with a long banner wrapped around it.

Edict of Lanespear

Strength through battle.

Lanespear is a deity associated with relentless war, survival, and strength. Her demeanor is harsh and unforgiving, disapproving of failure and laziness, encouraging her followers to train their martial skills while urging them to remain vigilant against the constant monster attacks from the Duskflare Jungles. She is considered the leader of the diverse Lowland Bastions, but she does not rule them as a queen or some kind of ultimate leader. Instead, she offers guidance, teachings, and the occasional interference in their various conflicts. Although very little is known about her past or how she became a Shard God, she is rumored to have been a follower of the hunter god Janar, but is now seen as a more warlike deity. She encourages the Bastions to resolve conflicts through honorable combat, in order to steady their resolve, train thier bodies and minds, and allow them to defend against monsters from the Duskflare Jungles.

She seldom travels beyond the Lowland shores, as she views the peaceful Arctus Plateau, Ordani, Arcturains, and even Kithil as weak and cowardly. More frequently, she is seen battling monsters and traveling between the Bastions. Since Lanepsear does not govern the Bastions directly, she rarely interacts with ordinary people, often appearing aloof or distant. However, she is approachable to renowned warriors, monster hunters, or adventurers, with whom she enjoys discussing martial techniques, monster behaviors, and combat strategies. For those who truly excel, she will personally bless and guide them, many of whom become her followers. These followers, known as the Kinthyr, are often praised as some of the most honorable and skilled warriors within the Lowlands.

Appearance

Lanespear is a whirlwind deity of un-flinching morals, willpower, and mental fortitude. Combined with a blazing strength of arms with her long-bladed runic spear, she is often seen by many to be unstoppable. She appears as a very tall Signborn with dark brown skin, four arms, and long black hair. Two slender, glowing horns sit atop her head, their tips emitting a red and purple hue that matches her intense eyes. Her body is adorned with intricate purple and red Waerd Tattoos, complemented by her elaborate runic scale mail.

Influence and Followers

Lanespear has a fervent following in the Lowlands, and most of the Waerd Culture worships her in various ways. Some follow her teachings, others adhere to the Codes of War she established, or dedicate trophies of monster kills at various fortified shrines and temples within and around the Bastions. She is also revered by many warrior-priests who form Companies, wielding spears and tattooed like their goddess, fighting for the side in Bastion conflicts that promises the greatest glory.

Those who have personally met Lanespear and earned her favor through great deeds are called the Kinthyr. They are bestowed with wings and wear runic armor crafted from powerful creatures and monsters. Like their Mistress, they mediate in the conflicts of the Lowlands, fighting for both sides. They also heal and restore fallen warriors and, in the event of a great warrior falling to monstrous incursions, carry their bodies back for veneration in fiery ceremonies.

Using Lanespear as a Deity

Using Lanespear as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is not for the faint of heart or those lacking willpower. She can be extremely demanding of her followers and expects them to endure life's harsh realities alone. She may occasionally intervene when her followers fight a powerful monster, but otherwise, she expects them to struggle, strive, learn, and grow stronger by themselves. She is famously known to reject her followers' calls for assistance, even in desperate situations. When she does appear, she speaks in a commanding, authoritative voice.

Relationships

Lanespear remains distinctly apart from many of the other deities of the Nineteen. She actively dislikes and is greatly dismissive of the more passive and peaceful gods, like Sigil, Thoma, and Volta. She sees them as weak and believes they could be doing much more with their powers to safeguard mortal lives.

She has a close bond with Malae, and the two of them are good friends. While they do not see each other often, they both have a deep respect for one another.

Lanespear is also allied with the 'Family of Storms'. Although Raineka is known as a goddess of healing and peace, she is frequently seen in the Lowlands, assisting people in surviving monster attacks and healing the sick. Because of this, Lanespear tends to become much more gentle around Raineka and often takes on a nearly motherly demeanor.

For some reason, she hates Thayloc with a passion that is frightening to behold, although the reason for this rivalry is not understood.
Lanespear.scoverview: Lanespear is a strict, unyielding Shard God who demands a great deal from her followers in pursuit of flawless combat prowess. The Lowlands region where she resides is a region teeming with monsters, ever-changing conflicts between the Bastions, and a constant state of survival. In such a hostile land, Lanespear is revered as one of the principal deities of the Nineteen above all others.
Lanespear.sgamemaster:
Very little else is known about how Lanespear became a Shard God, but she was once a follower of Janar, and when asked about her past, she fondly recalls Janar personally. This is particularly surprising because this would make Lanespear an extremely old deity, much older than the Waerd culture, and a Jarn-based Signborn rather than a Human one. How she found a Heart Crystal or what she was doing in those ancient days is something she doesn't speak of and seems saddened by.

The Lowlands region itself was settled only a few hundred years after the Virulent Plague swept across the Aran subcontinent. In Waerd songs and legends of their history, Lanespear was already a Shard Goddess when she arrived on the Lowland shores with refugees and survivors in large ocean-crossing logboats. Over the next two thousand years, she helped build and develop their culture, playing a crucial role in protecting the people from monsters and strengthening their resolve and fighting ability against the constant tides.

Sionia.name: Sionia
Sionia.text:
Areas of Concern: Death and the Undead, Solitude, Scientific Research

Typical Followers: Necromancers, The Undead

Domains: Twilight, Knowledge

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}

Symbol: A face made of swirling dust

Edict of Sionia

Seek to understand, not to be understood.

Though Sionia is considered to be evil by most mortals and almost all cultures repudiate her and what they consider to be her practice of necromancy, she is firmly aligned against the corruption and evil of true undeath. Sionia uses her powers with care, only animating the long dead and avoiding any interference with the Soul Cycle of Ember. Her continued work with the dead is born from a desire for understanding — she wants to know how the soul cycle works and is willing to sacrifice personally for the answers she seeks. This sacrifice has left her estranged, lonely, and deeply concerned with self-protection, but she still feels that it is worth the cost, especially as it leaves her able to help those who few others will — the Soulbound.

Sionia attempts to help the souls of those who remain bound to their physical form and free them if she can. Many Soulbound worship her, as do necromancers and the undead, but she avoids their love as much as she avoids others' hate, instead withdrawing from the world to remote places and spending centuries in isolation and meditation. She is most often found in forgotten ruins and hidden places, where she feels at peace and is safe from being hunted by those who revile her, including the priests and followers of Sockets, Elder God of Souls.

Appearance

Sionia appears as a beautiful human woman, whose long white hair seems to dissipate into ghostly mist. She generally dresses in white and golden silks and is sometimes mistaken for a ghost at a distance, seeming to float ethereally on the horizon. She generally has a kind, if deeply sorrowful, expression on her face. Staring too long into her eyes is known to bring most mortals to tears.

Influence and Followers

Sionia has very few true followers who actively reach out to commune with her, in part because she ignores those who do and in part because the worship of her is so thoroughly reviled. She does have a few chosen followers who she will answer, but they are generally those who have met and interacted with her personally, and understand her true nature as someone who wants to understand the cosmos, including the process of life and death.

Despite her apparent disinterest and general lack of response, there are many who worship Sionia and do deeds in her name, including individual necromancers, cults that worship undeath, and the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{ Blood Barons}, who are undead themselves. Sionia finds this worship offensive and has been known to hunt down and kill these followers if words of their deeds reaches her — a fact that has yet to dissuade others from following in their stead. A few have even attempted to catch her attention with vile acts that will lead her to kill them as an act of twisted worship.

Using Sionia as a Deity

Using Sionia as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or general devotion is very rare and usually hidden — a follower of Sionia will generally be reviled by all but a few necromancers and the undead, and is in danger of being hunted down by Sionia if their acts of necromancy go against her personal code. The one exception to this rule is those who have interacted with Sionia directly, often by coming across her while she communes in some hidden corner of Ember. Those who treat her with respect find her to be kind, despite her sometimes acerbic tone, and may have their prayers answered in future.

Despite his followers hunting her relentlessly, the only shard god who generally has any contact with Sionia is Sockets, Keeper of Souls. He periodically attempts to persuade her to help him watch over the Spiritlands, where the souls of those on Ember migrate when they die, but she has always refused. Beyond Sockets, shard gods generally either avoid Sionia or actively denounce her.
Sionia.scoverview: Sionia is a powerful mage reviled by many other shard gods because of her willingness to reanimate the dead. Though her practice of animating the dead comes not out of any love for undeath but a desire to understand the passage of souls, and she is careful not to endanger the soul of any mortal, she is considered to be a powerful necromancer and has been shunned by most on Ember, spending much of her time alone. For those who do encounter Sionia, she can be acerbic and cutting in her language out of a desire for self-protection, but this masks a deep sorrow that can overwhelm those who meet her, and she will not hesitate to come to the aid of those who truly need her.
Sionia.sgamemaster:
Sionia first appeared in the world after the Shattering and was considered to be a wandering mage, not a deity. She gained her reputation for necromancy after being seen in some of the many ruins of this era surrounded by walking corpses. Many drove her away from their settlements, leaving her to wander even farther afield into isolated and lonely places. Though unbeknownst to them, she ascended to divinity during the Shattering, as she was once a member of the Aedir royal family. Having lost everyone she ever knew to the power of the cataclysm, she became focused on understanding death and souls as a way to try to conquer her immense guilt over the destruction wrought by her people.

Sionia's designation as a god in the eyes of others came much later than her ascension, after she was confronted by a massive contingent of Lumek Fej warriors and walked away unscathed, despite their use of magic against her. Though she did not kill any of the Lumek who faced her, her reputation as a necromancer only grew after the confrontation, and many vowed to be the ones to destroy her once and for all.

Steelsong.name: Steelsong
Steelsong.text:
Areas of Concern: Craftsmanship, Invention, Fire

Typical Followers: Artificers, Smiths, Inventors

Domains: Light, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: A forge embedded with a hammer

Edict of Steelsong

The hammer strikes hardest when hot.

Steelsong is a diligent and warmhearted deity who delights in the company of mortals, often spending her days working, laughing, and drinking with them. She is considered a young Shard God, having risen among the Arcturian people roughly a thousand years ago. Her legend is celebrated as a grand epic by bards and storytellers, depicting her as a determined woman who was driven forward by destiny and fate, who braved the ancient underground ruins beneath the Shana Mountains and communed with a Heart Crystal, which was entrusted to her by the last surviving Shent Seer. Whether such tales are entirely accurate is up for debate, though Steelsong herself often sings variations of them while drinking among her followers. Since her ascension, she has been captivated by ancient Shent teachings and has encouraged the recovery of lost Shent knowledge. Even a few giant families descended from the Shent that had hidden themselves away in the Shana Mountains since the Shattering were drawn to her forge, where she used their great strength to build even greater and more powerful machines and structures.

Steelsong lives in the Krackos Enclave deep within the Ruinous Crags. Her massive forge is a wondrous, awe-inspiring sight, a shining jewel in an otherwise hellish landscape. Fed by lava connected to the Pathways, the forge is a blend of fortress, city, and smithy dedicated to craftsmanship and invention. Steelsong herself is a towering, giant-like figure, which puts her on par with some of her Giant followers. The Krackos Enclave is a bulwark against the Varún, who view the Goddess as an upstart. It is often attacked by various tribes over the centuries in great, bloody conflicts, but the city is defended by dedicated, well-trained followers who are equally devoted to protecting it at all costs.

Appearance

Steelsong appears as a young, muscular woman towering over most mortals at nearly twelve feet tall. Her dark, steel-like skin gleams under the light, and her glowing blue eyes give her a piercing, almost otherworldly appearance. Elegant bands of golden and bronze metal twist and curl around her entire form, emphasizing her impressive physique. She wields a massive great hammer named Ruenfoe, forged from ancient Shent metal and crackling with energy. She often uses this formidable weapon in battle against Varún Giants, with a roaring fury that few can match.

Influence and Followers

Steelsong has many followers in the Arcturian, Ordani, Kithil, and Waerd cultures. Among the Nineteen, she is considered the deity of progress and invention, which garners her a great deal of support among those willing to push society and culture forward. Her temples and places of worship are often forges, workshops, or foundries, where rituals and worship are conducted alongside the crafting of goods. Her followers outside the Krackos Enclave tend to be less militant and more focused on crafting and building. Within the enclave, however, her direct followers are much more focused on every aspect of warfare, including weapons and armor, as well as inventions that will help against the Varún Giant threat.

Using Steelsong as a Deity

Using Steelsong as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron reflects her friendly, easygoing spirit. She doesn't demand much from her followers and is pleased to support those passionate about invention, crafting, and a relaxed attitude. However, she also greatly respects warriors who confront evil, and she has been known to manifest formidable weapons for followers who choose a more combative path. It is said that becoming a follower of Steelsong is simple: just spend a night drinking with her. Her jokes, charm, and warm nature easily attract many to her side.

Relationships

Steelsong is good friends with the bookish Shard God Sigil, and Sigil himself has a magical way to transport himself to the Krackos Enclave, where he imparts knowledge and information to Steelsong and her followers. It's said that Sigil helped during a Varún attack on the forge, which would be a remarkable effort by the typically cowardly deity.

Steelsong dislikes the 'Family of Storms,' which includes Katu, Vekalla, Raineka, and Sokali. The Varún often use natural elements like storms, blizzards, and other phenomena to their benefit, especially during winter, to attack Krackos Enclave. This dislike, therefore, might not be directly related to the gods themselves but rather to their claimed aspects and areas of concern being linked to her enemies.
Steelsong.scoverview: Her voice the thunderous hammer on the anvil, Steelsong is a laughing, roaring Shard God of good humor and friendly excitement for all things crafted and made by working hands. She is a fluid yet unrelenting deity that does not suffer fools lightly and appears as a young muscled woman with dark steel-like skin, molten dripping hair and glowing fiery eyes.

Janar.name: Janar
Janar.text:
Areas of Concern: Protection, Hunting

Typical Followers: Hunters

Domains: War, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.SXks9PsVzNyIPuDH]{The Tanir}

Symbol: A spear piercing a fanged mouth

Edict of Janar

Slay those who would harm your kin.

Janar is dead, or so it seems to almost everyone on Ember's surface. As an ancient Shard God from the early Jarn days, he was one of their principal deities and protectors. He hunted Leviathans and safeguarded many Jarn villagers and tribes from their fury. Despite Leviathans causing widespread damage to the Jarn, Janar reportedly did not harbor hatred towards them or other beasts, but he did hunt them relentlessly, believing a hunter's role is to provide for and defend his family. As an ascended Jarn himself, he saw it as his duty to protect the entire Jarn population. Battles were intense, often lasting hours or days, but Janar typically succeeded in either slaying these colossal creatures or driving them off. Such victories often meant abundant meat or materials for nearby tribes, and Janar became especially revered.

In one of the most legendary tales since the Shattering and his final hunt, Janar faced the intelligent Leviathan Orinoth. After an epic battle across the shorelines and open ocean, Janar ultimately met his end. The story is often told as a great epic, but the exact circumstances of Janar's death remain mysterious and largely unknown.

In the present, Janar is still greatly revered, and despite his followers knowing he died, his worship has not faded like that of other gods. In fact, his followers still draw divine power from somewhere, and it is a matter of great debate among scholars, Janar's followers, and mortals across the surface on how this is even possible. It is said that Malae somehow recovered his body, which, in itself, is unheard of for a dead Shard God (typically they explode or dissipate into energy on death), and she enshrined it in a hidden temple on the Aran Subcontinent.

Appearance

According to legends and stories, Janar never changed his form from when he was a Jarn, except to grow larger when necessary to combat Leviathans. He appeared as a middle-aged Jarn male, with a body largely covered in hair and a short-trimmed beard. His leathery, weathered skin was covered in many horrific scars, which he wore proudly as signs of his successful hunts. He wore simple, practical hunting leathers and wielded a long spear tipped with a long shard of black obsidian. When depicted in imagery or statues among humans today, his ancestry is typically updated to show a Human, but all other aspects remain the same.

Influence and Followers

Janar has a large number of active followers and priesthoods throughout the world of Ember, though they often call themselves Hunters rather than priests and follow Janar's teachings to confront beasts and monsters and protect their loved ones from threats. This became much more pressing after the events of the Abyssal Shear, when monstrosities, dragons, and many other horrors entered the Cosmos for the first time. In some cases, his followers band together to form organizations designed to confront specific threats, such as the Serpent Hunters in the northeast of the Arctus Plateau, who hunt Sea Serpents of the

Using Janar as a Diety

Using Janar as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron is for those with a strong sense of duty and responsibility. Although Janar has been long dead, his followers uphold his legacy and philosophy, which include core tenets like strength, duty to family, and respect for the natural world despite its harsh and unrelenting aspects. Followers of Janar are often hunters of beasts and animals, as well as those dedicated to eliminating monsters to preserve the natural environment. Janar does not communicate directly with his followers; rather, his power manifests from an unknown source.

Relationships

Janar had a long and storied relationship with the Shard Goddess Malae. After his death, she supposedly recovered his body and concealed it within a temple on the Aran Subcontinent. Malae still mourns Janar, and many of his followers believe they were lovers at one point.

Janar was also the teacher for the Shard Goddess Lanespear, although she doesnt speak much, her now dead mentor and the two were close friends and allies.

Although it's not exactly what the relationship was at the time, Janar was said to intensely dislike Ku'arta, and some believe Jnar even tried to kill Ku'arta at one point. To this day, Jnar's followers hunt down Ku'arta's followers with equal hatred and passion, believing that Ku'arta is a detestable being that twists the natural world.
Janar.scoverview: Janar is a very old, human-centric Shard God, though his time came and went well before Humans even arose: his legacy and story is an ancestral thread from when Humans were Jarn. As a primal god of Hunting and nature, many still worship him today and strangely he has a surprising amount of active priests and followers, despite dying at the claws of a Leviathan during the Age of Beasts many thousands of years ago.

Thayloc.name: Thayloc
Thayloc.text:
Areas of Concern: Loss, Retribution, Death of the Undead

Typical Followers: Warriors, Refugees

Domains: Twilight, War

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: A broken silver arrow, still in flight

Edict of Thayloc

Swift is my arrow for rotting hearts.

Thayloc is a deity consumed by anger, regret, and loss. Once, he was a god of merriment, archery, and festivals, mainly concerned with organizing feasts and celebrations for the following day. His exceptional skill with the bow was well-known, and as a former adventurer with a storied history of fighting monsters, he was often lavished with praise by the people of Moria. However, because he was somewhat vain and irreverent, he was not taken particularly seriously. He often claimed to have "retired" from danger and peril, and only those seeking a skillful teacher or those who enjoyed his renowned feasts worshipped and loved him in those days.

While Thayloc enjoyed many hundreds of years of peace after his ascension, the events of the Evernight changed him almost completely. He somehow survived the cataclysmic destruction of the city of Miris and fled the Morian kingdoms, attempting to protect a host of refugees, but ultimately, he and many of the Morian people were cornered by Elwin Davos. In that encounter, Thayloc was almost killed, and nearly everyone he was protecting was massacred. In the aftermath, Thayloc recovered among the Lumek, bitterly lamenting his failure to do more and to see the events unfolding in his own city. He began helping the Lumek and the Goddess Lumé defend the firelands, but his anger and hatred for the undead were all-consuming, and he soon left to hunt them down on his own, spending long months within the now Morian Bonelands, preying on and destroying countless undead.

Thayloc became a beacon for those affected by the Evernight and for many surviving Morians who fled to other kingdoms and nations. Soon, his we joined his endless battles, small groups of loyal, fanatical, and displaced hunters, all of whom shared his hatred for the corrupted monsters of undeath and the Ossarchate in particular. Across the southern parts of Aterica, Thayloc is now revered by many, though most consider him an extreme and reclusive god. His uncompromising focus and otherworldly ability with his mythical Heartbow are the stuff of legends.

Appearance

Thayloc is a very tall Human, approximately seven feet in height, with soft brown hair that has silver roots. His skin is extremely pale and muted, nearing a light grey. His eyes are said to emit a silver glow in darkness but usually look dark grey. He wears durable black leather armor, partially covered by a shining silver mail. On his back is his great Heartbow, a legendary weapon believed to be older than the world. It doesn't need arrows and fires bolts of silver energy and force. When normal undead are struck, they often burst into flames of silver fire.

Influence and Followers

Thayloc has many followers across southeastern America, especially among the Lumek, but also among the Acturians, Ordani, Cascilians, and even the Kithil. After the Evernight and the rise of the Ossarchate, many feared that a tide of undeath was about to sweep over the world, but Thayloc, alongside Lumé, helped to calm such fears. As such, Thayloc is worshipped as a god of resolve, retribution, and revenge. He is often invoked after terrible events or tragedies and receives a constant stream of prayers asking for blessings in the face of great trials. His priests are often at the forefront of the world's effort to destroy the undead. They arm themselves with bows made of silver and are always the first to charge into darkened tombs and cursed ruins.

Using Thaylock as a Deity

Choosing Thayloc as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron appeals to those who have endured profound losses, seek justice and revenge, and are overwhelmed by anger and hatred. Making a pact with Thayloc is less about true justice and more about being driven by such intense fury that other concerns fade away. Many of his most loyal followers find this path ultimately leads to their doom as they push themselves into increasingly dangerous situations. Interacting with Thayloc himself is often difficult, as he is brooding and despondent, yet strangely brilliant, which fosters fanaticism and deep reverence among his followers.

Relationships

A resolute friend and ally of Lumé, Thayloc often fights side by side with Lumé, and the Lumek consider him one of the greatest destroyers of undead in the world, next to Lumé herself. Thayloc spends most of his time fighting the undead in hit-and-run attacks along the eastern coast of the Moiran Bonelands with a small band of his followers, but when the Undead attack the Lumek Firelands as part of the cycles of Fire & Death, he is often on the front lines.

Thayloc despises Sionia. The two have come to blows in the past in massive conflagrations of power. It's said that although Sionia is the stronger, she refuses to harm Thayloc, something he finds incredibly frustrating, and he bitterly resents her "mercy".

Thayloc is firmly aligned with Sockets and believes that all beings must follow the natural Soul Cycle. He believes this perhaps more strongly than Sockets himself and is dangerously fanatical. Soulbound are no exception, and Thayloc often demands that they release their souls to the afterlife if they meet in person.
Thayloc.scoverview: Thayloc is a Shard God of tragedy, loss, and retribution combined with a furious hatred for the undead. He is a deity that was once worshipped as the god of athleticism, archery, and feasts, but when the doom of Moira swept across the Casscal Peninsula, and the Evernight settled upon the region, Thayloc was forced to flee alongside mortal survivors. Afterward, he was overcome by a burning fury to rid the world of undeath in all its forms.

Obrisire.name: Obrisire
Obrisire.text:
Areas of Concern: Beasts, Survival

Typical Followers: Monster Hunters, Scouts

Domains: Order, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor}

Symbol: A triangle of fangs.

Edict of Obrisire

All creatures must do what they can to survive.
Obrisire.scoverview: The colossal Shard God that swims between the oceans of Ember, Obrisire takes the form of a massive bony serpent with scales harder and thicker than mountains. He has very little interest in mortals or even other gods and swims slowly around the world in seemingly random patterns over thousands of years. He does have a vague interest in beings that venerate him in specific ways, most notably Obrisire is greatly entertained by anyone who tries to kill him.

Thoma.name: Thoma
Thoma.text:
Areas of Concern: Night, Divination, Resilience

Typical Followers: Kithil, Night Shift Workers, Diviners

Domains: Twilight, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: A full moon shadow

Edict of Thoma

Find your way in the dark.

When the Keth fled from the Spine of Ember during the Shattering, Thoma emerged as a leader, helping to guide a group towards the area that the Kithil now inhabit. Unlike others, Thoma's group traveled almost exclusively at night, staying safe from predators and using her uncanny sense to find a safe passage forward in the dark. As she scouted one night, Thoma found a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal} and became a shard god, using her newfound power to find those paths more clearly and look into the future just enough to find a safe way forward for her charges.

Thoma's immediate thought after ascending was to ensure the safety of those traveling with her, and she channeled her power into finding somewhere that they could be safe from the dangers of the Shattering, enhancing her ability to find a safe path forward into a form of divination that allowed her to know which way would lead towards safety. This ability only worked in the darkness, perhaps as a result of her resonance with the moons from her Keth heritage, and Thoma dedicated herself to the idea of moving forward through the darkness.

Once the Keth reached the lands that would become the Kithil villages, Thoma withdrew somewhat, going on journeys through the world in the night to try to help those who felt lost in the dark to find comfort and determination instead. But no matter how far she travels, she always returns to the place that she guided her people to, and continues to try to provide them with guidance, making her one of the deities most directly involved in the mortal world.

Appearance

Thoma appears as an older Keth woman whose skin is covered in glowing tattoo-like markings that are constantly shifting, and thought to provide insight into possible futures. There is a moonlit glow to her teeth, and swirls of motes that look almost like stars briefly appear around her footsteps. Among her followers, finding and following these motes is often called "following Thoma's path," and the dappled light of the moon in the woods is sometimes referred to as Thoma's smile.

Influence and Followers

While Thoma is not worshiped much outside of the Kithil villages, her influence with the Kithil culture is significant. She has feared in the past that they might rely too much on her guidance, and is known to withdraw from time to time to avoid the Kithil using her too heavily to determine their future; nevertheless, she still visits frequently to check in, and an appearance from the Seer of the Stars is considered to be a sign of good luck.

Using Thoma as a Deity

Using Thoma as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or general devotion is common among Kithil, but can be found in others who have a particular resonance with night or the moons. Thoma is known for being more responsive to her followers than most, perhaps due to her relative youth as a shard god or her personal stake in the survival of the Kithil as a culture. While she does not like to interfere with the paths that her followers are taking, she often uses some of her power to look into the future and send obscure signs about which might be the best path to follow.

Between Thoma's nocturnal nature and the time she spends looking after the well-being of her followers, she hasn't been able to cultivate as many friendships and accords with other shard gods as she'd like. She does have a friendly relationship with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lc2ZMAGsL7pH1wEF]{Sokali} (who has a similar connection to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.PYCLsQgKclg5toxT]{Wirrun} people as Thoma does with the Kithil), and she enjoys spending time with some of the other solitary shard gods to offer them comfort and community — periodically checking up on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gT5S5ncAEUvkYYYg]{Sionia} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae}, in particular. Her most significant relationship is with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta}, a shard god she has never met. Even though the two prefer very different times of day, they've established a unique correspondence: leaving each other messages in hidden corners of the world, featuring their observations about life and various issues of the day.
Thoma.scoverview: Thoma is a shard god whose presence and power are only felt in the darkest hours of the night. Worshiped by many Kithil, who call upon her for guidance, clarity, and direction, she lives an exclusively nocturnal life, using the stillness of the night hours to travel across the land and discern what the future may bring. While some fear the nighttime as a time of danger and uncertainty, for Thoma it is a moment when the truth of the world is at its clearest, undiluted by the distraction of Lantyr's light and ready to be shared with those who are open to it.

Aythorn.name: Aythorn
Aythorn.text:
Moniker: The Trickster Thorn

Areas of Concern: Endurance, Plants, Trickery

Typical Followers:

Domains: Trickery

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: A flower made of thorns

Edict of Aythorn

Joy is best when it is shared — and unexpected.

Aythorn is a young, energetic, and friendly @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God} who moves throughout the world, meeting new people and playing small pranks to lift their spirits and forge personal connections. They are a very young Shard God, having ascended only three hundred years ago in the Tayan hinterlands, in what is now the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire}. Since arriving in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} twenty-six years ago, they have become an overnight celebrity, quickly charming the population of Toraga by hosting parties, events, and helping to solve local problems. Their incredibly captivating and charming persona is deeply attractive to many mortals, who have become enamored with a highly empathic and personal deity who seems to genuinely care about their lives. They have quickly become recognized as a member of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{Nineteen}, with many starting to refer to the Pantheon of the Arctus Plateau and surrounding regions as "The Twenty."

While Aythorn is happy to talk and tell all kinds of stories, their identity and origin remain a mystery. They are quick to call themselves an ascended @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.3s9YujjWpwPJntGa]{Thornling}.
