They are proudly non-gendered and chaotic, and they don't really understand gender or other social or cultural norms that most humans abide by. However, Aythorn also has some very curious characteristics that run counter to this idea. To begin with, they don’t look like other Thornlings and their skin is a greenish organic material rather than rough bark, and unlike other Thornlings, they greatly enjoy food rather than simply needing liquids to survive.

As they have settled more into the Arctus Plateau, Aythorn has become good friends with the Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.0SzX9C6HainzuV84]{Volta}. Aythorn usually invites them to parties and gatherings, and the two get along famously both enjoying celebrations, music, and good food. Aythorn calls Volta "Boba," a Thornling expression of close family. However, this is generally not seen as a true familial relation but rather a measure of respect and friendliness. With many other deities, Aythorn has a very positive relationship and spent several years living with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla’s} family on the Isle of Storms.

Aythorn is a Shard God of increasingly great renown; their fame is spreading through their eagerness to help people's daily lives and bring them joy, in addition to throwing some legendary parties that last for days. Unlike other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} or notable heroes, Aythorn steers clear of conflict or battles. One of the main reasons they left the Tayan hinterlands was that the area was volatile and dangerous, and the culture was increasingly focused on militaristic goals. Aythorn prefers charm, trickery, or even stealth when confronted with a hostile entity, and most of their stories revolve around them doing just that to all kinds of powerful foes.

Appearance

A vibrant, colorful deity, Aythorn appears to be some kind of mixed being between a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.3s9YujjWpwPJntGa]{Thornling} and a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Human}, or possibly some other ancestry, proudly commenting that they are a "big" Thornling. They are generally very tall for a Thornling, standing at nearly five and a half feet, and they can increase or decrease this even further when the situation calls for it. They have large, glowing, colorful flowering petals as hair and a wide, charming smile. They easily attract attention with their expressive gestures and strong, soft voice. Unlike most gods, Aythorn doesn't shy away from their divinity or try to disguise themselves and happily wanders among adoring crowds, giving out little blessings, playing pranks, and dispensing advice.

Influence and Followers

Aythorn has a large and growing number of followers, especially in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire}, who remember Aythorn fondly from the many years they spent traveling from settlement to settlement. In the Arctus Plateau, their followers are also growing in number, but they are concentrated around settlements where Aythorn has previously spent time. Most of Aythorn's followers might not be considered priests or clerics; however, they certainly pray and ask their god for guidance, especially if they have met Aythorn personally, although they prefer to think of themselves as just good friends instead.

Using Aythorn As A Deity

Using Aythorn as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or general devotion is common in specific regions of the World of Ember, such as the Tayan Empire and the Arctus Plateau. Outside these areas, worship or knowledge of Aythorn is virtually nonexistent, though not entirely out of the question. Aythorn's attention for their followers or friends is almost immediate, and they answer calls personally almost every time. They are unlikely to help their followers directly in battle by intervening personally, but they might assist them in escaping or finding another path to victory.
Aythorn.scoverview: Aythorn is a Shard God of mischief and happiness in the face of great trials, a deity that was once a Thornling but has since ascended and become much more involved with human-dominated cultures and concerns, they primarily appear as a mix between a Human and a Thornling. Aythorn is currently one of the most visible, active, and newest members of the Nineteen, the loose Pantheon of gods of the Eastern known world.
Aythorn.sgamemaster: Aythorn loves to tell stories and talk about themselves, but every tale is more grandiose, exaggerated, and hyperbolic. For their own ascendancy, Aythorn likes to tell the story of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan} basking on a sunbaked coastline, and how they managed to trick it into giving the once-tiny Thornling one of its massive, shining @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal} teeth. In another tale, Aythorn came across a wounded @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giant} who gave them a map to a lost city deep beneath the surface. Inside lay a terrible @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragon} guarding a trove of Heart Crystals, and Aythorn stole one and became a god. It's safe to assume that none of these are accurate versions of their history or origin, and they are merely tall tales. However, what is true is that Aythorn appeared on the western edges of the Tayan kingdoms as an ascended deity about three hundred years ago. For many years, they traveled and began hosting celebrations. Ultimately, they left the area after the rise of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire} and traveled by ship to the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}, a region considered one of the safest and most prosperous in the world. Twenty-six years ago, they arrived in the southern Arcturian city of Toraga and have been wandering the plateau ever since, with the ultimate goal of reaching @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} and seeing its glittering halls.

Volta.name: Volta
Volta.text:
Areas of Concern: Change, the Dawn, Secrets

Typical Followers: Travelers, Anyone going through a change

Domains: Twilight, Light

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: The horizon line with the rays of dawn above and the dusk colors below.

Edict of Volta

Moving at the speed of change.
Volta.scoverview: Volta is an unpredictable Shard God that enjoys traveling the skies of Ember and viewing the mortal world from above. They are one of the fastest beings in existence, known to run through the air at lightning speeds. Volta is worshipped as the bringer of the dawn and dusk, and while they rarely spend time on the surface of Ember, they are a very well-known deity due to being frequently seen racing across the sky, particularly at dawn.

Malae.name: Malae
Malae.text:
Areas of Concern: Curses, Herbalism, Vengeance

Typical Followers: Gardeners, Witches, the Wronged

Domains: Twilight, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.SXks9PsVzNyIPuDH]{The Tanir}

Symbol: A bundle of herbs bound with thorn

Edict of Malae

Punish those who wrong you.

Malae is seen by many as a merciless and uncompromising deity. While she is worshipped as one of the first truly ancient and great powers in the world of Ember, she is also greatly feared, and her very name is often spoken in hushed tones. While Malae is not evil, far from it, she has garnered an extremely negative, some would say villainous, reputation over many thousands of years of myths and stories that highlight her wrathful and terrible nature. Few speak of her warmer, more benevolent side or of her opposition to those who are oppressive or unjust. It is, however, true that she is a deity with an extremely waspish and wrathful attitude, and when angered she is a very alarming and even terrifying being.

Some believe that Malae is the first Shard God to walk the surface of Ember. This is not entirely true, but she is likely the first Jarn Shard God, and thus she is possibly hundreds of thousands of years old. By all accounts, she was a very normal woman with a loving family. There are many variations of the story of how Malae became the being she is today, but most are terrible tales of death, betrayal, and loss, often with Malae temporarily helpless to assist those she loved. At some point, according to the legends, she became a Shard God by communing with a Heart Crystal that was exposed to the sky, jutting out of the ground in those elder days. She has always been followed by tragedy, violence, and anger, but the events of those days are so long ago that only Malae herself likely knows the truth.

Malae believes strongly in being ready to take action when the moment comes. She spends most of her time wandering the world, studying and collecting plants, and has vast knowledge of herbalism and potions, part of her preparedness to strike when needed. Some of her devotees believe that she was once unable to act at a critical moment, now lost to time, and that both her wrath and her devotion to preparation stem from this incident.

One myth about her wrathful nature is that she cursed an entire ancient Kelmezian city after they tried to kill one of her devoted followers. She then went to great lengths to transform the entire city into Harpies, and such creatures have been called "Children" of Malae ever since.

Appearance

Malae appears as a short, beautiful human woman with a presence some call chilling. She has pure black hair that flows smoothly around her shoulders, framing a delicate face with two yellow piercing eyes. Her slender frame moves gracefully, and she wears flowing black clothing that seems to ripple gently with her movements, hugging her form. These garments are often adorned with intricate, ghost-like flowers and plants that seem to shimmer and fade in and out of existence.

Influence and Followers

Malae has few priesthoods or large temples dedicated to her worship, but most human-dominated cultures are aware of her and the old stories and legends. If they give her any thought, most ward against drawing her attention and whisper her name to prevent her from cursing them. A few notable followers venerate her as the goddess of herbs and plants for the deep knowledge she has cultivated over the years, and they understand that her more wrathful side is a consequence of the harsh world of Ember. These followers are often referred to as Witches by others and given a wide berth, though they are shunned. Very few people in the world will interfere or trifle with a follower of Malae.

Some monsters, notably Hassratch, will sometimes worship Malae as well, idolizing her wrathful and cruel side, but Male herself wants nothing to do with such beings and finds their existence to be an affront to nature.

Using Malae as a Deity

Using Malae as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron is an extremely rare pursuit among the peoples of Ember. While she is not the evil deity many believe her to be, Malae remains a prickly, difficult goddess with few followers who truly understand her nature. Nearly all her followers are considered Witches. While Witches are neither banned nor hunted across the surface world, they are often shunned—meaning followers of Malae tend to have thick skin, are deeply committed to justice, and seek vengeance for the wronged at all costs. Malae herself treats her Witches with care and love, granting them often greater power than other gods do. When she speaks to her followers, Malae is known for her kindness, speaking softly and soothingly.

Relationships

Malae's closest relationship was with the ancient Shard God Janar. They were said to be extremely close in ancient times, but after Janar was apparently killed, Malae slipped into a furious, cold rage that lasted for weeks. She is rumored to have recovered his body from the jaws of Godkiller Orinoth personally, although how this is possible is unknown. Other rumors persist that Malae was far more than simple friends with Janar and that they were lovers, but few would risk the Queen of Curses' wrath to ask her directly about the matter.

She is friendly with the Shard God Lanespear, and Malae is most often seen in the Lowlands, traversing the Duskflare Jungles and studying the ever-changing plants there.

Malae has a long, and some say ancient, relationship with the strange entity known as Laeora. The exact nature of their relationship is unknown, but the two are very close, and it's not uncommon for them to meet and exchange knowledge about the world.

It's said that Malae is searching for a way to permanently kill the sapient Leviathan Godkiller Orinoth, but so far her efforts have not been successful.
Malae.scoverview: Malae is known by many names, most commonly the Witch Queen of Curses, and she was the first Jarn Shard God to ascend after communing with a Heart Crystal. She is worshipped by few mortals on the surface world. Most regard her with a sensible amount of fear, seeing her as a cruel and heartless being. This is not entirely accurate, however, and she has a warmer side that only her true followers are aware of.

Lorex.scoverview: Lorex is a Shard God that has been active on the world stage for only a few hundred years. His godhood was at first disputed by many, but as his legend grew and he began responding to those worshipping him, it became irrefutable. Lorex is considered the greatest fighter in the world, nothing and no one can resists his thunderous fists and he spends most of his time making sure people know it. He is a laughing, singing, and exuberant deity that has just as much fun, drinking and singing as he does and fighting.

Kyasifer.name: Kyasifer
Kyasifer.scoverview: Hearing or reading this name immediately drowns your mind in a thick, kaleidoscopic haze. As you shake yourself out of the disorienting sensation, you cannot help but feel a sense of loss, as if the world is no longer as beautiful and true as it was before.
Kyasifer.sgamemaster:
WARNING

References to the Abyss, the Abyssal Shear, Abyssal Horrors, Outer Gods, etc, are not things that the player characters would typically learn about before gameplay begins, unless under very specific circumstances for background purposes. A more in-universe name for the Abyss among mortals is "The Shroud", with Abyssal monsters often called the Malvorn.

If you value the integrity of your own mind, do not look at this page. The entities and concepts here do not exist within the Weave; they exist beyond it. Even the act of naming them, or speaking them aloud, provides a tether, a thin, insidious thread that allows them to look back at you. I have seen scholars lose the ability to speak their own names after a single hour of research into the Abyss. This is not knowledge; it is a corruption of the mind and soul.

~Laeora

Areas of Concern: Dreams, Nightmares, Illusions

Typical Followers: None

Domains: Lies

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A formless purple triangle

Kyasifer, the Outer God of Tranquil Dreams, is perhaps the most insidious of all the entities from beyond @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{the Weave}. While the other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.hq1cXdVHjFbQxfys]{Outer Gods} appear as engines of destruction, Kyasifer manifests as a seductive promise of sanctuary. Known as the Lord of Comfort, they lure mortals into a realm called the Tranquil Dream, a realm only accessible when a mortal is unconscious. On the surface, the Tranquil Dream is a place of eternal bliss and endless beauty. To those exhausted by the hardships of life on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{Ember}, Kyasifer offers a world without pain, where the sun never sets, the resources are plentiful, and all dreams are possible. However, this beauty is an illusion, and over time, the dreamer becomes trapped in a horrifying prison of madness and delusion from which there is no awakening.

Kyasifer’s touch is subtle, often appearing as a sudden, obsessive preference for sleep, a detachment from reality, or a strange, purple-hued clarity in one's eyes. His tendrils creep through the minds of the lonely, the grieving, and the terminally ambitious. Lost cults of dreamers, swallowed by the realm's allure, operate in the shadows of great cities, while nobles and esteemed merchants seek the dreamscape as a shortcut to a blessed existence beyond pain and suffering. To fall into Kyasifer’s embrace is to suffer a fate arguably worse than death. A mortal mind trapped within the Tranquil Dream eventually breaks, becoming a hollow vessel that serves the Outer God without question or independent thought.

Appearance

Even among Outer Gods, Kyasifer's appearance is largely a mystery, his followers and cults tend to worship the Tranquil Dream itself rather than any personified deity-type figure. When Kyasifer is depicted, they are usually formless, a golden purple triangle or rectangle.

Influence and Followers

Followers of Kyasifer are more prevalent than many other Outer God worshippers, they can function normally within society right up until their minds finally become trapped for all time within the Tranquil Dream. The corruption of a mortal mind can take many years, during which time they enjoy their dreams each night, fully aware and able to experience unearthly delights. This becomes such a drain on a person's mind during their waking hours that they slowly become withdrawn and despondent.

Using Kyasifer as a Deity

Direct interaction with Kyasifer doesn't seem possible, and there are no recorded instances of this occurring. Instead, mortals may become aware of the Tanquil Dream. This usually begins when a mortal is introduced to the idea of the dream by someone already hooked and beholden to its dangerous allure. This person acts as a carrier, sharing their love and ideas of the Dream through intoxicating stories, billowing incense, or shared meditative rituals. Once a mortal attempts to access it, even for a second as they drift to sleep, Kyasifer has a hook in their subconscious that can never be fully removed.

Shattered One.scoverview: A mysterious entity with immense power that very few in the world even know exists. Very little is known about their intentions, personality or goals, and the only beings that seem to worship them are the fanatical Malicae.

Sha-Xotha.name: Sha-Xotha
Sha-Xotha.scoverview: Hearing or reading this name sends blinding red pain shooting through your mind. You recoil with terror and a sense of dread falls over you, your mind desperately trying to ignore and forget that which threatens to twist its sanity into something nightmarish.
Sha-Xotha.sgamemaster:
WARNING

References to the Abyss, the Abyssal Shear, Abyssal Horrors, Outer Gods, etc, are not things that the player characters would typically learn about before gameplay begins, unless under very specific circumstances for background purposes. A more in-universe name for the Abyss among mortals is "The Shroud", with Abyssal monsters often called the Malvorn.

If you value the integrity of your own mind, do not look at this page. The entities and concepts here do not exist within the Weave; they exist beyond it. Even the act of naming them, or speaking them aloud, provides a tether, a thin, insidious thread that allows them to look back at you. I have seen scholars lose the ability to speak their own names after a single hour of research into the Abyss. This is not knowledge; it is a corruption of the mind and soul.

~Laeora

Areas of Concern: Rage, Destruction, Anniliation

Typical Followers: None

Domains: Destruction

Pantheons: None

Symbol: An immense red eye.

Sha-Xotha is an immensely powerful and savage @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.hq1cXdVHjFbQxfys]{Outer God} of pure destruction. The few beings within the Ember Cosmos aware of her existence, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods}, never willingly speak of her, and she is possibly the most powerful entity of the Abyss. She is the Mindless Eye, the Red Ruin, and the Voice of Annihilation. Her presence within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{Abyss} is said to be a stain upon the concept of reality, an unstoppable force that even the other Outer Gods seem to avoid and fear. As very few on Ember are aware of her existence and learning her true name causes immense pain and madness, instead the term "The Red Eye" is used to invoke her power by her twisted and fanatical followers.

It's not thought that she is aware of the Ember Cosmos, but if she were, it's possible she could easily break through the protective barrier of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{Weave} entirely and cause the utter destruction of the Ember Cosmos. So vast and terrible is the danger associated with her existence that those who come across the cults of the Red Eye and learn their beliefs consider the destruction of the Ember Cosmos to be inevitable, and it causes such despair in mortals that it twists their minds, causing them to try and bring about this very event.

Sha-Xotha is a being of immeasurable power and energy, and as an Outer God, very little is known of her true mind, with most of her essence seemingly focused on the destruction of all things. Her motivations seem simplistic and even mindless, but as an Outer God, her very existence is inexplicable, so this may not be entirely accurate.

Sha-Xotha is said to be responsible for the Blood Moons, an event that affects the Ember Cosmos every few years. Sometimes, decades may pass without an event occurring, but they have affected Ember since living memory. They begin with darkness unlike any other, as night settles over the Cosmos entirely, and the light of Lantyr dims. Every moon visible in the sky turns a deep crimson color, lasting for several days. Elder Gods believe this is the gaze of Sha-Xotha passing over the cosmos, but she cannot focus her attention, and eventually, it passes. During the Blood Moons, nightmares plague mortals, and the veil of the world that separates the cosmos from the Abyss grows thin. The servants of the Outer Gods become empowered, monsters become more ravenous, and the world reveals the eldritch abominations it has been hiding in the darkness. Various cultures have many different interpretations of the Blood Moons and various names, but all consider them the work of pure evil, and they often cause untold destruction, anguish, and death.

Appearance

An Outer God is more of a concept than a being; they shift, twist, and reform themselves constantly, and within the Abyss, they are more akin to a vast concentrated force of energy. However, a mind viewing Sha-Xotha within the Abyss itself would likely see a black and red stain of cosmic size bleeding through the concept of space and distance with a vast singular eye burning through their soul. Among her cults and followers on Ember, “The Red Eye” is sometimes depicted as a humanoid of immense size, with intense swirling chaotic black and white mist covering her body and with a cycloptic single eye of burning red energy set into a large head crowned with black mist. These cults also seem almost universally to express her form as feminine, but it's unknown why this is the case, given that the idea of sex and gender is meaningless to an Outer God.

Influence and Followers

Somewhat paradoxically, Outer Gods can be worshiped, and Sha-Xotha is no exception. But this is not a connection that attracts her attention in any way. Instead, followers are more like parasites, feeding on a sliver of her power without her knowledge. Her followers do not know her true name and do not attempt to learn, as doing so would bring about their instant annihilation. Instead, the term “The Red Eye” and a number of her other titles are used, which helps prevent instant destruction. However, even obfuscating her name in this way does not shield her followers from the concepts of the Abyss and the maddening effects this causes within their minds. It is a violent, painful, and tearing revelation, and very few are able to resist these effects completely. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} and some other powerful beings would be able to withstand this madness to some degree, though there is still a risk. It would seem that only the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} and a few others can learn about Sha-Xotha without any damaging effects.

Using Sha-Xotha as a Deity

Interaction with Sha-Xotha is almost impossible. There is no such thing as a "Cleric of Sha-Xotha". Attempting a direct, conscious connection with her alien mind is to invite immediate backlash and a swift death. The raw, Abyssal energy of an Outer God's attention is toxic to beings from the Ember Cosmos, and any mortal who manages to catch Sha-Xotha's direct attention is usually reduced to a mindless, gibbering husk or a mutated thrall within seconds.

Instead, mortals may become aware of Sha-Xotha through the lens of the Cults of the Red Eye. Although this cult is rare and hides in some of the darkest, most remote locations in the Cosmos. They are considered incredibly dangerous by anyone with knowledge of their existence. Many actively hunt the cult, including some Elder Gods, who will intervene personally or task their greatest champions to scour them from the Cosmos without delay.

As these cults form, after some deranged or corrupt mortal comes into possession of secret and forbidden knowledge, what they are worshipping is usually hidden and obscured for some time. Only slow and careful probing into Abyssal mysteries will unveil more, but this always comes at a heavy price. The being that creates the cult will slowly reveal more knowledge to those they can convince to join them, resulting in very real and powerful magical abilities. These cults almost all revolve around destruction in one form or another, entire nations, or the killing of many people or beings. This ultimately leads to the cult destroying itself, but how much damage they cause before this happens, or if some other force stops them, is always unknown.

Notable Followers

  • @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A]{Nadin}

Kinalathi.name: Kinalathi
Kinalathi.scoverview: Hearing or reading this name drenches you in a feeling of unnatural, inescapable fear. This horrifying sensation feels as if it will slowly eat away at your mind until nothing remains, yet despite this terror you cannot help but feel a smile playing on the corners of your mouth.
Kinalathi.sgamemaster:
WARNING

References to the Abyss, the Abyssal Shear, Abyssal Horrors, Outer Gods, etc, are not things that the player characters would typically learn about before gameplay begins, unless under very specific circumstances for background purposes. A more in-universe name for the Abyss among mortals is "The Shroud", with Abyssal monsters often called the Malvorn.

If you value the integrity of your own mind, do not look at this page. The entities and concepts here do not exist within the Weave; they exist beyond it. Even the act of naming them, or speaking them aloud, provides a tether, a thin, insidious thread that allows them to look back at you. I have seen scholars lose the ability to speak their own names after a single hour of research into the Abyss. This is not knowledge; it is a corruption of the mind and soul.

~Laeora

Areas of Concern: Death, Unmaking, Undeath

Typical Followers: None

Domains: Oblivion

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A ghastly smiling face, strechted and distorted beyond reason

Kinalathi is the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.hq1cXdVHjFbQxfys]{Outer God} responsible for introducing the concept of Undeath into the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} during the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}. Like the other Outer Gods, they are not fully aware of the Ember Cosmos but their avowed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors} spread undeath like a malignant blight. Kinalathi is synonymous with the absolute cessation of the natural order. They are the force causing the slow, malignant decay of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} itself, with the ultimate goal of erasing the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. Undeath is not their end goal, but rather the weapon they use, ensuring that souls can neither move on to the Spiritlands nor find sanctuary in the Inner Realms.

Before the Abyssal Shear, the concept of an "undead" was non-existent, which means all undead within the Cosmos are no more than 2,573 years old. This makes the undead a relatively recent and terrifyingly unnatural blight upon the world. Kinalathi’s influence is spread by their Abyssal Horrors, who act as vectors for a spiritual plague that anchors a soul to its rotting vessel. Strangely, the Outer God appears largely indifferent to the individual struggles or triumphs of the undead they create.

The true name of Kinalathi is almost entirely unknown among mortals, but the entity is widely worshipped by undead and death-obsessed mortals, such as necromancers, as "The Howling One." This figure is actively revered by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Ossarchate}. Some scholars believe The Howling One is merely a lesser servant or an Abyssal herald, while others suggest it is an aspect of Kinalathi designed to facilitate the spread of Oblivion.

Appearance

In their guise as The Howling One, Kinalathi is depicted across the lands of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7zFmCJqtAp32EaI1]{Moira} and throughout the wider world. These depictions most commonly take the form of massive, blank-faced humanoid statues carved with smooth precision. In many regions of Moira, gigantic, disconnected humanoid body parts, colossal hands or heads, are a hauntingly common sight, jutting from the earth like the remains of a buried giant. These monuments are almost always magically constructed through grueling rituals and blood sacrifices, yet they remain unnervingly dormant and unmoving.

The terror of these monuments lies in the rare accounts of their awakening. Legends whisper of dormant statues suddenly stirring to life, with dark, hollow eye sockets illuminated by pinpricks of freezing white light, while a ghastly, jagged grin spreads across the face from ear to ear. It is not known what these effigies do once they have awakened, nor what purpose they serve in the physical world. History records no survivors from such an encounter.

Influence and Followers

Kinalathi is never worshipped openly, nor are they a being that would tolerate such a thing, as they seem to care little for the ideas, concepts, or actions of mortal sapient life. Should a person become aware of them and shield their mind enough to commune with Kinalathi directly, then the mortal soul would be vaporized instantly.

They do have several powerful avowed Abyssal Horrors that are much more well-known and active in the Cosmos today, in addition, several once mortal beings have some measure of Kinalathi's power. These beings are known as the Blood Barons of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Ossarchate}, and they are equal in power to older Shard Gods and even weaker @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} and present a malevolent threat like none other to the peoples of the world. Its not known whether the Blood Barons worship Kinalathi directly or to what degree they are aware of him and vice versa. Still, his depiction as the Howling One is very common in the undead cities of the Ossarchate and the lands themselves, and a great many undead worship and follow the Howling One.

Using Kinalathi as a Deity

Direct communion with Kinalathi is impossible for the mortal mind; if a mortal were to touch his consciousness, they would be instantly erased. Kinalathi does not possess a personality that can be bargained with or a will that can be understood. They are a metaphysical oblivion of all things, drawing all toward a silent end. Because of this, cults of Kinalathi do not exist on Ember; the name itself acts as a cognitive hazard that most minds instinctively reject.

Instead, the hunger for immortality and the fear of the Spiritlands drive mortals toward the worship of The Howling One. The Howling One is considered the deity of the undead. Necromancers, desperate monarchs, and nihilistic death-cults revere this figure, believing they are striking a bargain with a god of eternal life. They do not realize that every prayer to the Howling One acts as a chisel, chipping away at the Cosmos and allowing the entropic influence of Kinalathi to leak into the world and cause further corruption.

Lantyr.name: Lantyr
Lantyr.text:
Areas of Concern: Energy, Light, Life

Typical Followers: All

Domains: Light, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.isH9tuxCUUP4GfWN]{Sentina}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Solaru}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6cMQOhdBouTFJlSl]{Sunalins}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.SXks9PsVzNyIPuDH]{Tanir}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor}

Symbol: A roaring ball of yellow cosmic fire.

Edict of Lantyr

Life thrives in the light.

Lantyr is one of the strangest entities in the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}; she is both an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Goddess} and has a physical presence that serves as the literal sun for the world. While mortals look up and see a comforting orb of yellow fire, this is merely a refractive illusion caused by the atmosphere and magic. Her true form is a colossal, roiling sphere of intense light-blue plasma, which only becomes clear once you get uncomfortably close to her in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars}. The surface of Lantyr is an intensely dangerous landscape of pure energy. While it primarily exists as a churning sea of fire, Lantyr can solidify her essence, creating translucent, glowing platforms. These solid islands allow a rare few to walk on their surface and even support strange creatures and life forms. Within these zones, the temperature is remarkably mild, and the air is breathable, as Lantyr intentionally creates safe spaces to host her strange creations. However, should a traveler step off the edge of these sanctioned paths, they would instantly plummet into the burning, blue sea of pure energy below.

Lantyr's exact nature is paradoxical to many, as she appears to be the origin of light and life but is, in fact, the singular source of all energy within the Cosmos. Lantyr is a fierce nexus of power that keeps the Cosmos balanced and moving behind the scenes, and the light and heat she generates are merely the waste products of her existence. The fact that mortals grow and stay warm by her presence is a secondary consequence of her being. This actually defines her completely, as to many, she has a distant, calm, and seemingly uncaring personality. She doesn't see herself as a motherly figure or a caretaker, but as a perpetual cosmic regulator, spending every moment focused inward, keeping her energy in check so that the rest of the Cosmos can thrive in safety. Lantyr’s withdrawn nature also comes from her awareness of her own volatility, as she understands that being close to anything or anyone would consume them. Her deep kindness is an act of perpetual restraint.

To that end, Lantyr is perhaps one of the most well-known Elder Deities, the one worshipped and adored by every culture and people of Ember since the dawn of sentient thought. Looking up and seeing her glide gracefully across the sky, bringing warmth from the dark, is hard to miss, and mortals, as well as those upon the Moons and in the Inner Realms, hold Lantyr in the highest regard. She grants her powers freely to those who follow her but never interacts with them, meaning countless temples, priesthoods, cults, and groups have formed to worship her divine light and life-giving nature throughout history, despite receiving total silence in return.

I've always personally found Lantyr's light to be a comfort, as if she's shone upon me with a measure of kindness and care. Throughout my travels, I've certainly met people and groups with different interpretations. I’ve seen fanatics who want to burn the world just to purify it, doomsayers waiting for the day she finally goes cold, and oppressive tyrants who think her light is nothing but a weapon to cancel out the dark.

~Laeora

Appearance

Lantyr is an entity of staggering proportions, a roiling, spherical mass of energy that rivals the size of the Elemental Moons. To look upon her from the Sea of Stars is to see a churning ocean of cerulean fire, where tectonic-sized plates of solidified energy drift across seas of screaming plasma. While she appears as a comforting golden orb from the surface of Ember, this is merely an illusion cast by the atmosphere and a certain degree of magic of unknown nature that seems to shield the world from her true color and nature.

Influence and Followers

Sun worship is one of the most historically common ways of communing with a deity on Ember, across numerous cultures and ancestries, and it is an easy path to divine power, as Lantyr does not discriminate among her followers. From the most ancient days to the present, Lantyr has enjoyed large numbers of worshippers, with practices that take many forms. Beyond the grand temples, Lantyr’s silence has given rise to a vast spectrum of isolated faiths and local traditions. These range from entire city-states like Anacalen, which worship her divine power and strength, to the Heralds of the Dawn, an ancient sect of mountain-dwellers who view the rare glimpse of her unrefracted blue light as a moment of ultimate mental clarity. Elsewhere, solitary Sun-Watchers watch over ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Sunwells and protect them from the ravages of time. There are also many nomadic tribes, travelers, or sailors, who treat her as a beacon and constant marker in the sky.

Lantyr's largest current priesthood is the Clerics of the Radiant Eye, who form the cornerstone of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6cMQOhdBouTFJlSl]{Sunalin Pantheon}, where she is revered as the Sun Mother. For the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessian} people, her worship is less about philosophical meditation and more about societal structure and enforcing a strict, near-fanatical opposition to forces of evil and monsters.

During the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of the Tower}, the Aedir began worshipping Lantyr as a primary deity during their initial rise as a civilization and culture. They saw her warmth and light as a great affirmation of life itself and regarded her almost as much as their creator, Keia. Over time, their interpretation and knowledge of Lantyr increased, and they began to regard her as a glorious partner in their advancement. They did not just worship her but built their entire society and technology around her power, creating Sunwells that tapped directly into her divine energy. By the time the Aedir Empire reached its height, their faith had transformed into a doctrine. They no longer saw Lantyr's light simply as a blessing or a divine patron to worship, but as a tool to be mastered. The Aedir became convinced that they were destined to use her boundless energy to propel the Sunfire Empire forward, viewing the Sun not as a remote mother but as the engine of their own transcendence.

The most terrifying manifestation of her faith is found in the Inner realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} worship her as the creator of Light, despite this being a grand lie. Most of their worship is funneled through a religion known as the Blinding Truth, a philosophy that holds only a Tyraphem Lord called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.XXyU4kvrBPceEoz2]{Taryakel} can interpret Lantyr, and that all other beings are merely shadows waiting to be consumed or cast aside. Lantyr is generally considered by the Tyraphem to be a furious, angry, and burning deity, and anything that is not "of the Light" is to be purged.

Using Lantyr as a Deity

Using Lantyr as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is for the disciplined and the fanatical, or for those who seek to tap into raw energy without constraint. While Lantyr does grant her power to anyone under the right circumstances, she does so without guidance or personality, simply because it is in her nature to do so. Lantyr never speaks to her followers, which makes her unique among the deities on Ember, and her followers often become disillusioned by her lack of true warmth or attention. Worshipping Lantyr is also a dangerous path for a would-be follower, as there is no safety valve and no divine intervention if the power she grants begins to consume the user.
Lantyr.scoverview: Lantyr is both an Elder Goddess and a lunar body of cosmic size. Although her true name is well known, she is more commonly referred to throughout the cosmos and in the world of Ember as simply The Sun. Lantyr is the most recognizable and beloved of the Elder Deities, the radiant goddess who has watched over Ember since the dawn of creation. To every culture across the world, she is a graceful, golden presence that glides across the sky, banishing the cold and bringing the gift of each new day.
Lantyr.sgamemaster:
Lantyr, along with her brother Finor, came into being during the early moments of Creation, after Alar, Spectra, and Ven'avé. Since this time, she has remained remarkably content with her purpose and form, barely changing for eons. Only after her brother Finor's death did her output of light and warmth change for the first time, plunging the cosmos into years of winter, which eventually ended when Lantyr seemed to come to terms with his passing.

During the Shattering, Lantyr was deeply wounded, and her carefully maintained balance was thrown into chaos. Because the Aedir had tethered their civilization so deeply to her energy via the Sunwells and various other technologies, the physical Shattering of the Sun Tower caused a massive backflow of energy. Lantyr had to exert all of her will to dampen her own output, preventing her energy from exploding and incinerating Cosmos. For the first time since the death of Finor, Lantyr’s light flickered. Lantyr spent years grappling with the intense fluctuations, retreating into herself. She pulled her energy back, and her light and warmth grew dim. While this ultimately saved her, it left the World of Ember in a terrifying, twilight-like dimness for many years. a period of vulnerability that coincided with the Abyssal Shear. Consequently, her followers found themselves bereft of power or severely weakened precisely when they needed the light most to combat the encroaching dark.

At the height of the Abyssal Shear, Lantyr faced a physical threat unlike any other: a monstrous entity known as the Sun-Eater clawed its way into the cosmos. It attempted to engulf and devour Lantyr entirely, seeking to extinguish the light of the cosmos. While the historical records are fragmented and nothing is truly known about the battle, it is known that the catastrophic end of the Sun was narrowly averted. Someone, or something, intervened at the final moment to drive the Sun-Eater back, though the encounter left Lantyr more distant and reserved, spending many years recovering from the ordeal.

When the Sun Tower Shattered and the Sunwells blackened, the sky above faded and dimmed. While Lantyrs' light still shone, its warmth disappeared, and it was obvious that the Sun Goddess herself had pulled back in pain. She went cold and quiet, retreating into herself to keep from blowing the whole cosmos to cinders. And that...was the worst possible timing. Just as the world was cracking open, and chunks of the broken tower rained down upon the world, the first monsters crawled from the Shroud. I remember the last great Aedir warriors, stumbling across barren and broken lands, desperately trying to access their source of power and beseeching the grey sky above. But every spell sputtered, and every Divine Blade went dull. We all needed a hopeful light, and all we had was a dim ember in the sky. It makes sense in hindsight, she was too busy trying to keep herself alive to notice her followers being eaten in the dark.

~Laeora

Sitheera.name: Sitheera
Sitheera.text:
Moniker: The Watcher, The Spider Goddess

Typical Followers: Scholars, Historians, Academics

Domains: Unknown

Pantheons: None

Symbol: Six large green eyes within a black void.

Edict of Sitheera

This world has such fascinating little creatures.

Sitheera is one of the most subtly unsettling and potentially dangerous entities within the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, yet thankfully, most mortals remain blissfully unaware of her existence. The name Sitheera is seldom used or known by mortals save for a chosen few; instead, the name The Watcher is used instead. While her true nature is not known with any certainty, Sitheera seems to meticulously record events rather than attempt to interfere with or disrupt the natural order. Her attention is consuming and focused on all aspects of the world and of mortal affairs, and her deep fascination can sometimes manifest as an obsession with specific individuals. Those few researchers foolish enough to delve deeply into occult and esoteric lore sometimes stumble into her waiting embrace.

Sitheera is also strongly associated with the multitude of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.UIXhmx3iwyk52raz]{Spiders} found across Ember, with some scholars postulating that she is the Mother of all Spiders, the source of any widespread knowledge of her existence. If this is true, it suggests that Sitheera is an ancient entity of terrifying power, likely introduced during the tumultuous era of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, when Spiders first began to appear on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}.

Historians and scholars are often naturally drawn to her embrace and to her followers, Sitheera is surprisingly patient and kind. She rarely communicates with words, instead guiding her servants through a potent, innate subconscious desire. This "pull" compels her followers to seek out and record greater, more unusual, and more meaningful events, often leading them to stride into increasingly complex and dangerous encounters. To serve Sitheera is to commit oneself to a lifetime of witnessing the world's strangest and most catastrophic moments, always from the best, or worst, possible vantage point. Sitheera demands absolute, unyielding loyalty from her patrons, where disobedience is unacceptable. Attempting to resist her directions is met with the swift appearance of her children, as she begins sending spiders to enforce compliance. If compliance still fails, her patience snaps, and she becomes direct: dragging the Warlock into dark, inescapable pits within their own dreams, and holding them there until they can no longer resist her relentless, green-glowing gaze. A follower of Sitheera always serves, and always watches.

Appearance

Not much is known about Sitheera's true appearance; she is often depicted by her Spider children as an amorphous mass with countless green, shining eyes and a multitude of long, spider-like limbs. But her mortal followers tend to also depict her as a more humanoid being, albeit in a monstrous feminine form with a mass of insect or spider-like limbs as hair and six glittering green eyes.

Influence and Followers

Sitheera attracts certain scholars, historians, and diehard explorers obsessed with the world's greatest mysteries, and these are also the kinds of individuals she actively seeks out, valuing their ability to perceive, categorize, and archive the unusual events she demands to witness. These chosen followers are driven less by a desire for power and more by an insatiable need to know and record the hidden truths of the Ember Cosmos.

Outside of her select scholars, Sitheera's reputation as the Mother of Spiders and her potential origins during the Shattering make her widely regarded as a primordial monster and an evil being. Due to this association, she is also worshipped by various cults, malignant covens, and secretive groups who seek her power to unleash dark, uncontrolled forces upon the world. These cults venerate the spider as a symbol of patience, deadly silence, and the inescapable snare of fate, seeing Sitheera as the ultimate embodiment of cosmic malice.

Using Sitheera as a Deity

Using Sitheera as a deity for a Cleric, a Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron is extremely rare across the surface world. This is primarily because her connection to spiders and her assumed role as a progenitor of such monsters introduced during the Shattering leads the vast majority of societies and established religions to view her as a monster herself. Any open devotion to Sitheera is met with immediate suspicion, persecution, and the swift attention of local authorities or religious groups seeking to purge her influence.
Sitheera.scoverview: Hearing or reading this name feels innately violating, like pinpricks from needles as something crawls across the very essence of your being. You cannot shake the terrifying feeling that you are now being watched by something that will never look away.
Sitheera.sgamemaster:
Sitheera is, in truth, an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.hq1cXdVHjFbQxfys]{Outer God} from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{the Abyss}. The implications of this knowledge are staggering, as Sitheera should logically be a horrific blight upon the Cosmos, and yet, she is curiously not. Sitheera herself seems to be an outlier or an exception to an otherwise immutable rule, and instead, she appears to view the existence of the Ember Cosmos as fascinating. Although she may seek to dominate and control the Cosmos in her own way, this startling benevolence is often a confusing contradiction to the other Outer Gods' extremely destructive and alien natures.

It's also worth noting that, typically, Outer Gods cannot be worshipped or communed with directly; doing so destroys a mortal's mind instantly. If a mortal has contact with even lesser servants of the Outer Gods, it also results in madness, but at a slower rate. Sitheera, however, seems to be the exception, and an individual can communicate with her directly without their sanity being destroyed, further cementing her unusual nature.

The only thing more terrifying than boundless, immediate cosmic rage is boundless, immediate cosmic patience. Sitheera is not waiting to destroy the Ember Cosmos; she seems to be waiting for it to reveal its final, most interesting secret.

~Laeora

Another startling fact regarding Sitheera is that she is physically present within the Ember Cosmos, currently inhabiting the center of the Blasted Moon, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora}. This is a shocking revelation as Sitheera could easily destroy the Cosmos. However, they are not doing so and seem quite content to sit inside the moon and watch events roll by. She did not enter the Ember Cosmos during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} either and has been present in Ember since @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.10gWEDeJX8aj4L3u]{the Unveiling} at the end of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}. While largely passive for tens of thousands of years, she did, fascinatingly, confront and annihilate several @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors} that attempted to destroy Cora during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear} and seems to have created Spiders in response to other Abyssal threats. With this in mind, it's somewhat understandable that many mortals in Ember have an instinctual fear and terror of Spiders, as it is a logical aversion to entities that an Outer God has directly created.

Elder Gods.name: Elder Gods
Elder Gods.text:
Lore Summary

  • Origin: Created at the birth of the Cosmos.

  • Cosmic Aspects: They are cosmically empowered but have physical bodies.

  • Worship: They can hear and grant distant prayers, intervening from anywhere in the cosmos.

  • Soul Anchors: They can safeguard their followers' souls, taking them to the Inner Realms.

  • Destruction: Strangely, they can be killed. Or perhaps not; what exactly happens is unclear.

As most mortals on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} don't see much difference between @UUID[.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} and Elder Gods, they are not treated any differently. Elder Gods can gift power to their followers and answer prayers, and some Elders are just as visible and active on the surface as Shard Gods. @UUID[.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, the Elder Goddess of Magic, is often found in academies and libraries across the surface world, and she often speaks with mortals on a daily basis; she is also considered one of the principal deities of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}, who are among the few mortals who know her true age and nature.

Typically most elders are not actively worshipped today due to their more esoteric nature and tend to govern some of the more obscure aspects of reality that mortals do not pay attention to in their daily lives. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, for example, the Elder God of the Soul is also considered the God of Death and would be the most popular and well-known of the Elder Gods, consistently across most cultures in Aterica. But even he is not as actively worshipped or revered as much as local Shard Gods who impact people's lives in more direct ways. The idea of an afterlife comes from mortals' understanding of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7#mortal-souls]{Soul Transference} which is technically the domain of Sockets, but many mortals understand this concept in the context of their local pantheons and deities with distinct beliefs across cultures surrounding death, rituals for burial, offerings, and prayer.
Elder Gods.scoverview: Elder Gods are the most powerful and ancient entities within the Ember Cosmos, they are primordial forces of creation that maintain fundamental ideas of reality. They were born during Creation and inextricably linked to the Heart of Ember. They now maintain the fundamental reality of the Cosmos, and while their power is vast, they are often distracted by cosmological issues rather than daily mortal concerns. Elder Gods embody fundamental concepts (Space, Souls, Time)
Elder Gods.sgamemaster:
An Elder God is a being that is far more unknowable and mysterious than a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God}, they do not tend to share the same concerns that mortals do over what happens upon the surface of Ember as they typically have a particular aspect of creation that they oversee. Some can be more connected to mortals in various ways, but they might come across as strange, otherworldly, and distant. The key difference is that Elder Gods were created or possibly self-actualized during the creation of the Ember Cosmos. Their minds are not mortal in any way, although a few have absorbed a great deal of information about mortals and have empathy and compassion for their struggles.

According to Spectra, Elder Gods are the beings that were created during the creation of the Cosmos. As the Weave took shape and matter coalesced around the Heart of Ember, beings began to emerge from wild surges of Lifeforce emanating from the Heart of Ember. Apparently, the exact same process led to the creation of many of the cosmological bodies of Ember, such as the elemental Moons or the Inner Realms as well.

~Laeora

Among even the other Elder Gods accounts, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} was the very first being in creation. Many vain deities claim to be creators or the first god in their own little mythologies they preach to their followers, but in Alar's case, it's very likely true. In fact, according to her own memory and account, she was born before the formation of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{Weave} itself during the process of creation and, as such, has bore witness to almost the entire history of Ember. Alar is one of the Elder Gods who is often overlooked by mortals and even reviled in certain cultures despite her age and legacy. Alar does not have any temples nor numerous priesthoods, and her followers are often individuals. Generally, temples and worshippers of the Elder Gods are rare, except for Sockets and Lantyr, who are both well-known across the surface world and have larger followings in major cities such as @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}. Unlike local Shard Gods, Elder Gods dont typically tend to remain in one area long enough to develop a large following of clerics or priests.

The Elder Gods consider themselves a small family group of sorts and do their best to support and keep in contact with one another, albeit staying in touch could mean thousands of years between exchanges. Alar considers @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{Ven'avé} to be her daughters, and in turn both of them consider each other sisters and sometimes call Sockets "little brother". @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} is also considered an Elder God by the others and among those who study such things extensively, and this would make sense as she is one of the more obvious deities worshipped by mortals who have been a fundamental force of the cosmos since creation. The other Elder Gods consider Lantyr to be their aunt, which suggests the Elders do have some idea about the differing age and creation between them.

Perhaps one of the strangest concepts surrounding the Elders is that they can apparently be killed, and several Elder Gods have apparently disappeared from records or collective knowledge. Such is the case with@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.BP2QN2S6fFOfwp3U]{Finor} who was famously killed by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.186yO79YKDxPh0qT]{Theroch} during the Forsaken War events in the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} stories. This is particularly puzzling as Elder Gods are not Shard Gods; their power and very being are part of the reality of the Ember Cosmos, so if they were to die, then what exactly would happen to the forces they contained and watched over? Alar herself claims she cannot be killed or die in the traditional sense, but this area of lore is incredibly mysterious, and the truth may never be known.

The Nineteen.name: The Nineteen
The Nineteen.text:
Elder Gods Alar and Sockets have disagreed for eons about the nature of mortal souls on Ember, but when undead Varun began spreading across the Arctus Plateau, both recognized the fundamental danger the undead posed to the mortals fighting against them. Together, the two gods called for aid from their fellow deities — a call heeded by gods across Ember, each with their own reason for jumping into the fray.

Ultimately, nineteen deities helped to end the Arcturian-undead conflict known as the Mourning War, each assisting in their own way. Some gathered information and helped to strategize. Others jumped into battle, fighting side by side with the Arcturians. Still others helped to heal the wounded and rebuild the places destroyed by the conflict. While all took different roles and joined the battle for their own reasons, they ultimately worked together to eliminate the undead threat in the area— a powerful symbol of cooperation that became an inspiration for the early Arcturians.

Though thousands of years have passed since the Mourning War, the Arcturians have continued to uplift and venerate the Nineteen, putting aside any harsh feelings they might have towards individual members of the pantheon to celebrate what they were able to do together. Though it is not used as frequently in modern times, the phrase "Honor the Nineteen" was common in earlier eras to quell disputes and remind Arcturians what can be accomplished when disparate interests pull together as one.

The Nineteen.scoverview: The Nineteen is the collective name for a pantheon of gods well known to and celebrated by cultures in the southeastern region of the Aterican continent, including the Ordani, Arcturian, Waerd, and Kithil cultures. Though the gods of the Nineteen have many different areas of concern, the group came together to help defend the Arctus Plateau from an incursion of undead during the region's earliest days, ending a conflict known as the Mourning War. The grateful Arcturians have never forgotten this act of divine intervention, celebrating the Nineteen as a group for the thousands of years since.

Solaru.name: Solaru
Solaru.text:
The Solaru began with a single member, Keia, creator of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae} ancestry. After creating the Nir'ae on the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.NdqwtFoFAw85Gstr]{Aran Subcontinent}, she magically transported them to @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Op5BD9XSlmb7l6NN]{the Starshield} and ruled her people directly for many years. Following her marriage to the charismatic warrior Oryn, she later helped him to ascend, and he became the first @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir King}. Over time, they had many children, some of whom also ascended, like Aursia and Valen. These children married and had children of their own, continuing the lineage and forming a complex family tree of deities. Eventually, the Solaru pantheon ceased direct rule over the Aedir and delegated governance to the Imperial family, the mortal descendants of Keia and Oryn and their children, but the gods continued to guide events from behind the scenes. Over time, the Solura pantheon expanded, becoming the largest in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Ember Cosmos}. The strength of the Aedir people grew with their gods, and when the Aedir Empire was established and expanded across the surface world, the deities spread with them.

Eventually, as the Sun Tower reached its final heights and the Aedir rejoiced, the Solaru pantheon gathered, and the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} unfolded. In a single instant, the vast family of gods was ended with a finality that shocked the Cosmos. Very few of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods }and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild Gods} that made up the Solura survived the Cataclysm, but among them was Aursia, who founded the Sunalin pantheon upon the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessian} continent.

Solaru.scoverview: The Solaru was the ancient Pantheon of the Aedir, co-ruling alongside the Imperial Family for thousands of years. Like the Aedir themselves, the pantheon consisted of a diverse range of charismatic explorers, builders, artists, warriors, and conquerors who led their people with grace and strength. The Solaru was bound together by familial ties and complex relationships. Nearly all its members were killed during The Shattering. Today, it is an extinct pantheon studied by historians and scholars.

Sunalin.name: Sunalin
Sunalin.text:
The Sunalin pantheon is the radiant heartbeat of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia}, and while @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} remains the most prominent entity of worship, the pantheon was forged by Aursia. Originally part of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Solaru}, Aursia abandoned her peers after witnessing them descend into tyranny that failed to uphold the true tenets of righteousness and faith. After @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, Aursia’s zeal and opposition to monsters and evil gathered many scattered @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} and unified them to protect the remaining ancestries on the northern shore of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessian} continent. Today, this faith is so deeply integrated into @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessian} identity that it is no longer merely a religion but a total social and military ideology.

The relationship among the gods of the Sunalin is based on necessity and military commitment rather than any true family ties or deeper bonds. Aursia resides in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.BYvYIdN1bQH4UIvR]{Kasarain} and helps lead the Kessian people, while many of the other Shard Gods live in nearby cities, such as Pyriou'sasa, who resides in the city of Iktae. Korvak resides with the Bjordans to the east, while Vin'osul rules over the great city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.zk7jkfc35IBulYB4]{Tempest}. In the years after the Shattering, the Shard God Etarra was ripped apart by his own people, who had turned into undead ghouls, and now presides over a nation of undead and is reviled by the other gods.

Sunalin.scoverview: The Pantheon of the Sunalins is the dominant religion throughout the Kessian continent. Lantyr, known by the people there as the High Sun, is at the heart of the cultural and spiritual faith. Her worship is so widespread that almost every part of daily life, from market transactions to military organization, is influenced by the "Solar Vestarum", or more commonly, "The will of the Sun".

The Tanir.name: The Tanir
The Tanir.text:
The Tanir pantheon is not a unified family; rather, it consists of a system of Temple Houses, with power residing in the capitals of three distinct cultures: the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayans}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Mazirans}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezians}. In Tanir, divinity is intertwined with politics; weaker or newer @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} often pledge loyalty to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ZTZ8d8E7BPE8S6zX]{Selai}, Noduro, or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.aRQpUyfhVUie1Jan]{Tirass}, serving as their lieutenants or becoming their children to ensure their worship. Each House has its own goals and motives. In the Tayan Empire, the faith is refined and regal, centered around @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7iZDVtrBO7326XZY]{Caren'ac}, where Selai and her Court of Silver mostly align with the Empire’s interests. In the Kelmezian City-States to the south, the attitude becomes melancholic and pragmatic; Tirass is seen as a stern ruler of ancient seas, and his associated gods oppose the expansion of the Tayan Empire. Meanwhile, in Lunarai, the Mazirans view Tanir through the lens of Noduro’s iron-clad logistics, treating worship as a formal petition to a ruler.

Despite this, the gods are deeply interconnected: a Maziran merchant might offer a tithe to Noduro for his caravan’s success, but he will also whisper a prayer to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ZCI33WO5GIuAPg3p]{Verador} for winds, or silently plead with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ne6lFuJsytNGiyxK]{Orru} to safeguard the night-roads. This interconnectedness means all gods are worshipped in some form or for various reasons.

The Tanir.scoverview: The Tanir is the name for the pantheon of gods known to Western cultures of the Aterican continent, mainly centered around the Tayan Empire, the Kelmezian City-States, and the Mazirans across the Crossing Sea. Several key deities in the Tanir have vast temple complexes and priestly orders with thousands of members, making them highly influential. Other gods tend to gravitate toward these major deities, such as Selai in Tayan, capital of Caren'ac, Noduro in the Maziran city of Lunarai, and Tirass in Old Carinth, the Kelmezian city-state.

Sentina.name: Sentina
Sentina.text:
The Sentina slowly emerged as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} culture formed following the events of Unveiling, when the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giants} left @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} and began to settle the jagged @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.VxA0UsGvDbDn8SdO]{Shana Mountains}. At the staggering height of Mount K’hente, they founded the colossal city of She’lu, a city of silver, stone, and celestial geometry. For thousands of years, the Sentina oversaw the Shent culture, with many of its members living among the people in the city of She'lu itself. I was an age of quiet contemplation, with countless star-gazers, seers, and scholars living among the freezing peaks at the heart of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterican} continent. At the head of the Sentina was @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{Ven'avé}, whom the Shent considered the most important deity in existence despite her often infuriating silence, followed swiftly by Orizon, who lived in the Grand Temple of the Stars within She'lu and helped guide the Shent on a more daily basis.

This age of peace and reflection ended violently during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, as the Shent came under direct attack by forces of the Shroud. As horrific monsters tore through the city of She’lu, many of its @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} perished alongside their people. However, whispers remain that the Sentina did not vanish entirely. Vesta'ec had already parted from his fellow Sentina gods before the events of the Shattering, and his followers, known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Z8Nm4rnjqG3BJHSd]{Varún}, managed to survive the conflict. It is not known exactly what happened to Vesta'ec, however.

Sentina.scoverview: The Shent were a civilization of seers, architects, and lunar mystics. They believed that through the study of the stars, geometry, and observation, one could understand the very fabric of reality. Their gods were deeply embedded in these beliefs, and the Sentina was an ancient Pantheon that guided thier cultures for tens of thousands of years. Alas, most of its Shard God members were destroyed during The Shattering. Today, it is an extinct Pantheon extensively studied by historians and scholars.

Outer Gods.name: Outer Gods
Outer Gods.scoverview: These entities originate beyond the cosmos itself. Their powers are utterly alien and incomprehensible, often manifesting as paradoxes, impossible geometries, the unraveling of minds and the creators of monsters. They are the ultimate existential threat, and their followers often seek power through forbidden knowledge that drives them mad. Outer Gods embody destructive concepts (Oblivion, Annihilation, Terror)
Outer Gods.sgamemaster:
WARNING

References to the Abyss, the Abyssal Shear, Abyssal Horrors, Outer Gods, etc, are not things that the player characters would typically learn about before gameplay begins, unless under very specific circumstances for background purposes. A more in-universe name for the Abyss among mortals is "The Shroud", with Abyssal monsters often called the Malvorn.

If you value the integrity of your own mind, do not look at this page. The entities and concepts here do not exist within the Weave; they exist beyond it. Even the act of naming them, or speaking them aloud, provides a tether, a thin, insidious thread that allows them to look back at you. I have seen scholars lose the ability to speak their own names after a single hour of research into the Abyss. This is not knowledge; it is a corruption of the mind and soul.

~Laeora

Lore Summary

  • Origin: Unknown.

  • Alien Aspects: It's not clear if they have physical bodies.

  • Worship: They can hear prayers, but this almost always results in the praying mortal's mind being destroyed.

  • Soul Destruction: They are the greatest threat to the Soul Cycle. An Outer God does not recycle or guide a soul. They consume it.

  • Destruction: They cannot be killed.

The Outer Gods are the utterly alien cosmic entities of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{Abyss}. In the context of Ember and the beings within, they are vastly more powerful and could destroy life on a massive scale or, should they wish, destroy @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.JUwFAaelI86yiscL]{the Cosmos} entirely. Their mere existence is so unfathomable that mortals upon Ember can be driven insane merely by being introduced to their names or concepts. Very few beings in Ember can even fathom communication, let alone combating their powers, and it takes a mind of incredible willpower to survive contact with them for only a few moments.

The intentions, motivations, and goals of the Outer Gods are beyond the knowledge and understanding of others. Some, at one point or another, have viewed Ember with a fleeting emotion akin to mild curiosity; these are the most dangerous of their kind. When even a fraction of their attention is directed at a chattering mortal fanatic on Ember, desperate for power or favor, the result is often catastrophic. Not only would the foolish mortal be annihilated, but their souls would be dragged into the Abyss, doomed to an eternity of unimaginable torture and twisted beyond recognition, and the surrounding area is often infused with Abyssal corruption permanently. In almost all cases, however, the Outer Gods have vast cosmic concerns and cannot focus upon Ember for more than a few moments. Even these brief moments can have massive impacts, resulting in concentrated abyssal intrusions, unknown effects, and Abyssal energies exploding with unimaginable force.

While the term Outer Gods is as good as any, they are not gods in any traditional sense. Somewhat paradoxically, Outer Gods can be worshipped. But this is not a connection of mutual understanding that attracts their attention in any way. Instead, followers are more like parasites, feeding on a sliver of their power through aspects without their knowledge.

I have a few of my own theories and research that suggests the Outer Gods possess rivals within the Abyss that command their full, terrifying attention. I suspect this is merely wishful thinking. It is unlikely anything exists with the power to challenge such entities, save for another of its own kind. If they are distracted, it is not because they are being fought, but because they are busy devouring one another.

~Laeora

While the Outer Gods cannot seemingly interact with the Ember Cosmos, this has not stopped them from sending or rather imbuing servants with their will to dominate and destroy. Among their most powerful servants are the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horrors}, who might be considered the generals and commanders of the various Outer Gods. However, during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, another entity called the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rxr72Zmt6eUOFg5B]{Herald of Whispering Choir} physically made its way into the Ember Cosmos. Its size was cosmic and on par with one of the Elemental Moons of Ember, and it could be described as a Supreme Commander of the Abyssal Forces. Its power and ability to destroy would have likely caused the destruction of the cosmos in time if not for the intervention of the Elder Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}.

It's not known how many Outer Gods or Heralds exist within the Abyss, but there are currently records of five Outer Gods, with several others speculated to exist based on their effects and servants. Many more could exist within the Abyss, and the true number may be a horrifying revelation.

Vhismara.name: Vhismara
Vhismara.scoverview: Hearing or reading this name fills your mind with a ferocious burning sensation. It's all you can do to fight the violent feeling as it rips and tears at the fragile corners of your mind with disturbing precision, dredging up your deepest fears and darkest thoughts.
