Vhismara is known as the Great Wolf and the entity responsible for the countless monsters that crept into the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}. Vhismara is seemingly pure evil, a cruel, dreadful, and vast power from beyond the Cosmos. Yet, they also seem to be genuinely fascinated by the creatures, mortals, and peoples of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{Ember}. To encounter Vhismara is to face two distinct and terrifying identities: the first is the Great Wolf, a colossal engine of mindless rage and unyielding destruction that seeks only to rend the fabric of the cosmos. The second, however, is far more insidious, a cold, calculating entity possessed of a sharp, alien rationality. While the wolf howls at the boundaries of our world, the Rational Mind whispers into the cracks, displaying a capacity for forethought and patience that is rare among the chaotic forces of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{the Abyss}.

Appearance

Vhismara's true form like any Outer God is unknown. They are often depicted by their followers as a wolf-like being, a beast of terrible size, power, and cruelty. Shining orange eyes that glow from the darkness of the Abyss and a colossal maw of countless sharp fangs. Various monsters that are aware of Vhismara may depict him in other ways, typically a form that is closest to their own.

Influence and Followers

Few mortal peoples of Ember follow, worship, or are even aware of Vhismara; those that learn of their existence are often in grave danger, as once you know of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.hq1cXdVHjFbQxfys]{Outer Gods} name and being, he may eventually focus upon you. Should such a thing happen, there are various outcomes. Vhismara may annihilate your mind instantly, or break a person's body and twist it into a monster. Sometimes, however, Vhismara may begin whispering his desires and hatreds unceasingly into a person's mind, but this is perhaps the worst outcome as Vhismara will twist a person into a monster in spirit & soul, slowly causing a mortal to betray, kill, and consume their loved ones.

Monsters typically regard Vhismara with awe, reverence, and joy, believing he is the ultimate expression of their existence and purpose to hate, destroy, kill, and maim. True worshippers of Vhismara are still rare, however, as most monsters are not truly capable of sapient thought, and if they are, they will often be drawn towards Heralds or Abyssal Horrors of Vhismara instead, as they tend to be more tangible.

Using Vhismara as a Deity

Interaction with Vhismara is incredibly dangerous. There is no such thing as a "Cleric of Vhismara" or a "Warlock of the Great Wolf" in the traditional sense. Attempting a direct, conscious connection with his alien mind is to invite immediate backlash and a swift death. The raw, Abyssal energy of an Outer God's attention is toxic to beings from the Ember Cosmos, and any mortal who manages to catch Vhismara’s direct attention is usually reduced to a mindless, gibbering husk or a mutated thrall within seconds.

Instead, mortals may become aware of Vhismara through a lens of profound ignorance. They do not latch onto the entity itself, but onto the vague concepts he leaves in stories and nightmares. Tribes, cults, and desperate outcasts often venerate him under a dozen different names: The Vast Hunger, or The Father of Fangs, or The Great Wolf, believing they are praying to a primal spirit or a vengeful Wild God. This worship doesnt connect to Vhismara directly so they do not gain direct powers but may start down a very slippery slope towards corruption.

Lumé.name: Lumé
Lumé.text:
Areas of Concern: War, Fire, Murder

Typical Followers: Paladins, Soldiers, Fanatics

Domains: Fire, Other

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A crown of fire, pierced by multiple swords

Edict of Lumé

Only fire reveals a person's true nature

Lumé is the radiant fire goddess queen of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, a steadfast, uncompromising deity of compassion and strength, regarded by many as one of the most skilled warriors in the world. While she now rules over the Lumek and most of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.fmhP7pxXIXV0BM2r]{Fej } ancestry in Ember, she is not the original creator of the Fej; that was her mother, Naor, an ancient deity, who crafted them long ago during the early days of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of the Tower}. Controversy surrounds Lumé regarding whether she deliberately murdered her mother after the events of the Evernight. Some believe it was accidental, others think she had no choice. During the Evernight, when undead swarmed the Lumek, Lumé was among the first to act, leading her people in battle after battle. She succeeded in pushing back the emerging @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Ossarchate} at great cost but appeared frustrated with her mother's inaction and focus. What transpired between the two deities remains uncertain, but Naor died shortly afterward, and Lumé took over leadership of the Lumek. The people, frightened and angry over the ongoing undead assaults, rallied around Lumé despite the rumors and renamed their realm the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.02ZsG2X7epHZGOcq]{Lumek Firelands}.

Appearance

Lumé is a remarkably beautiful deity who adopts two primary forms. During the recovery period after undead assaults, she takes on a regal form, resembling a tall Fej woman with coal-black skin and an inner fire that emanates from her shoulders and head, wearing a plain golden crown. Despite her formidable appearance, her eyes remain calm and compassionate. Her attire blends intricate regalia with practical, form-fitting clothing suitable for rebuilding and aiding her people.

When the undead swarm into Moriran's Lament, targeting her children and nation, her appearance changes dramatically. The once gentle and thoughtful ruler becomes a fierce and deadly warrior. Her crown transforms into an elaborate helm, and her body is encased in blackened armor. Her form becomes more elemental as her skin ignites into blazing flames, and her eyes turn into white-hot pits within her fiery face. Lumé wields a long, slender obsidian sword, which glows with intense white-hot heat as she fights the undead.

Influence and Followers

Nearly the entire culture of the Lumek follows and worships Lumé to some degree. Even among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} who are accessible and approachable, Lumé is especially present in her people's lives. As a ruler, she makes time for her subjects and is often seen walking the streets of her cities and towns, helping where she can. In many cases, she offers blessings and gives people gifts. She seems well aware that the cycles of war that swept across the region are a constant pressure and tries hard to relieve her people's burdens. This makes her especially beloved and revered on a personal level, as her people can see firsthand how hard she works to keep them safe.

Direct followers of Lumé are peerless warriors and among the most powerful opponents of the undead in the world, imbued with power from Lumé personally. Many are based in the city of Ash on the western edge of the Firelands and guard the mountains to the north against any encroaching undead.

Using Lumé as a Deity

Using Lumé as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is a path of fierce, unrelenting resilience and a desire to live up to greater ideals. Lumé is a deeply passionate and present deity who cares greatly for her people. She never seems to show doubt but often expresses her grief and sadness over the burden her people carry. Because of her empathy, she rarely pushes anyone, except herself, to extremes, which often makes her followers try even harder to match her. She rarely leaves the Lumek Firelands but communes with her followers in other lands when they reach out to her, offering guidance and soft words of encouragement.

Relationships

Lumé is a steadfast friend of the Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc}, as both are passionately opposed to the undead, and they even employ similar methods, directly opposing threats head-on. Their bond is strengthened by past trauma and sadness, and they are often seen reminiscing and sharing memories together.

Rumors suggest Lumé is in a relationship with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka}, the Shard God, which has shocked many of her followers. It is an intriguing pairing since the two deities are radically different: Lumé is associated with war, battle and command, while Raineka is a goddess of peace and healing. Reports indicate they have spent considerable time together over the past few years, with Raineka increasingly seen in Hearth, the capital city of the Lumek, granting blessings to its citizens.

Lumé detests Ku'arta and it's rumoured she even tried to kill him in the past, long before the Evernight. However, she does begrudingly accept that he is aligned with her against the undead.

Lumé has a complex and often strained relationship with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KQF9QommtN6ITiLW]{Lorgi}, who shares many of her concerns. The two align on so many things that, at first glance, they would seem to be steadfast allies. Instead, the two have conflicting personalities and clash not over what needs to be done but over the manner in which it is achieved.
Lumé.scoverview: Unlike most Shard Gods, Lumé does not lead her followers from a distance. Instead, she governs the entire Lumek Firelands and stands as one of the most influential and powerful leaders in the known world. Lumé remains a controversial figure; some admire and worship her, others mourn her tragic past, while some view her as a cold-blooded killer. Revered by many as the goddess of fire, she is also famous for her relentless war against the undead Blood Barons of the Ossarchate.

Xalarax.scoverview: Xalarax is a name few know and that instills horror and dread in those that hear it. Those unfortunate enough to bear that burden associate it with the Evernight which saw the city of Moira destroyed, the Fractured Lands that were created in its wake, and the Blood Barons who rule there now.

Menis Valegar.scoverview: Menis Valegar, also known as the Lord of Torment, is one of the powerful Blood Barons, a group of undead beings that are on par with Shard Gods.

Deliverance through agony.

Nethehepticas.scoverview: To those caught in the thrall of a nightmare, the name Nethehepticas may manifest like a subconscious whisper. The name fades with the nightmare upon waking, which is for the best as to recall it in the waking world would bring nothing but misfortune.

Areyter.name: Areyter
Areyter.text:
Areas of Concern: Water, Patience

Typical Followers: Typhic, Water Elementals

Domains: Water

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A see-through water droplet, with a blue core, and city built above

Upon Lady Areyter's back lies the massive underwater city of Tohr, one of the oldest settlements in existence. Tohr is a masterwork of ancient architecture, characterized by hidden, winding paths, lush buildings of living coral, and the soft, haunting glow of bioluminescent lights. The original builders of the city, the Typhic, still walk its glowing streets, alongside water elementals and other watery denizens.

Tohr is the only city in the cosmos where the ground has a pulse. I spent a week in the Coral District, and I couldn't sleep. The vibration of her heartbeat through the stones feels like the drums of the raging tempest on the surface of the moon. It’s a stunningly beautiful city, though, and I found the entire experience both surreal and calming.

~Laeora

Despite her immense power, she is famously known for her laid-back, relaxed personality. She is a being of quiet contemplation, largely unconcerned with the finer details that rise and fall within her waters. Her presence has been felt at every major turning point in the history of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}, though she rarely takes an active role in the outcome. She presided over the creation and eventual dissolution of the first Court of Typhos, as well as the emergence of its second iteration. Yet, she always remained a silent witness to the political strife. The last time her voice was recorded was to bless the ancient union of Adrefton and Bathyios.

Appearance

Lady Areyter is a being of staggering size, a gargantuan entity measuring roughly six miles from her blunted snout to her massive tail. In silhouette, she bears a striking resemblance to the colossal whales found in the oceans of Ember. However, up close, her anatomy reveals a much more ancient, fish-like physiology that predates modern aquatic life. Her vast back is covered in a mottled, rugged armor. This hard skin is both tough hide and part vitrified stone. In stark contrast to her armored back, Areyter’s underside is composed of a semi-transparent elemental membrane. Through this glass-skin, observers can see the rhythmic pulse of her internal Lifeforce, which glows with a soft, bioluminescent blue light. Her twelve eyes are vast, swirling orbs that mirror the storms of Mayis.

Influence and Followers

Areyter is the absolute ruler of the moon of Mayis and, by extension, water elementals of all kinds. She is not particularly interested in getting involved with everyday concerns and is happy to lazily drift through the moon's vast ocean. However, the Typhic and water elementals generally adore her and treat her with the utmost respect. Her philosophy of laid-back acceptance and taking everything in before acting has a profound effect on her followers.

Very few mortals in the world of Ember are aware of the Elemental Sovereigns generally, and thus Areyter is not a commonly worshipped being. However, there are some exceptions. Notably, the mysterious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.uYINWy1xgnIkCVaC]{Carrow} dwelling deep within the oceans of Ember.

Using Areyter as a Deity

Using Areyter as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is extremely difficult for mortals in the world of Ember. Areyter is technically a Wild God of immense age, and therefore, she cannot hear prayers or the pleas from her followers remotely. To harness her power, a mortal must forgo the safety of the temple and seek her out personally, crossing the vacuum of the Sea of Stars and stand before her. Once a bond is forged, the follower will find that Areyter is a deeply patient and undemanding patron. She does not command, but instead encourages "going with the flow" to wash over them and to wait with the stillness of the deep sea.
Areyter.scoverview: Lady Areyter is a primordial force of the Ember Cosmos, an Elemental Sovereign who arose during the mythical days of Creation. She is the undisputed mistress of Mayis, the Tempest Moon. Areyter is not merely a ruler of the elemental moon; she seems to be the physical embodiment of the Force of Water itself, a massive, behemoth-like creature that swims through the moon's cold waters on a never-ending journey.
Areyter.sgamemaster: Areyter has existed ever since the moon of Mayis formed during Creation. She has a deep, thoughtful memory of all that has happened on the moon, but less so of the cosmos as a whole. She played very little part in some of the significant events of history, but she was roused to anger during the Abyssal Shear. It's not known what exactly transpired on Mayis during those tumultuous days, but Mayis remains somewhat corrupted by Abyssal energies to this day. It's rumored that Areyter herself annihilated numerous Abyssal monsters that attempted to ravage the moon, and the city of Tohr became a glittering fortress of wrath for a short time.

Slinerak.name: Slinerak
Slinerak.text:
Areas of Concern: Oppression, Ooozes

Typical Followers: Cultists

Domains: Earth

Pantheons: None

Symbol: An oozing mass of multicoloured slime with a large rusted spike thrust through it.

Slinerak is both a tragic and terrifying figure among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Tl4gvmUGThkZdrUd]{Elemental Sovereigns}, a primordial being whose descent into tyranny serves as a cautionary tale. Originally, he was a Lord of Earth, characterized by pragmatism and fairness, who ruled over the moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora} and its denizens with steadfast reliability. However, something twisted his mind beyond recognition, and his personality shifted into an obsessive need to control every aspect of his life. He began to overlook the individual lives of the beings beneath him and forced his need for control onto his followers, eventually transforming into an oppressive, insane overlord who seeks to subjugate everything within his reach.

Though his status as an Elemental Sovereign has never diminished, Slinerak has completely hidden himself away from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} since his fall. He resides deep within the Palace of Rust, a monumental fortress of rusting metals and corrupting liquids. While he remains the Sovereign of Earth, his corruption eventually gave rise to the creatures known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.SDNg4JYpXKIPptav]{Oozes}, which he is said to control utterly. Some Scholars suggest that Oozes represent earth that has lost its structure, a stagnant sludge that mirrors the Slinerak's own moral decay. Thankfully, the vast majority of elemental beings upon Cora resist the corruption of their once Lord, seemingly working to contain him within the Palace of Rust. They are somewhat successful but at great cost, and the effort has made Cora extremely unstable and chaotic.

Some people find Oozes to be friendly, cute little critters, but I find them revolting. Not only are they unnatural perversions of the earth, but knowing that Slinerak could be watching from behind their eyes is uniquely horrifying.

~Laeora

Appearance

Although he likely had another form in ages past, Slinerak now appears as an enormous slime creature with a barely visible core of earth and rusted metal. His size and girth are legendary, and while his form has no eyes, he often extends a colossal jaw-like structure that swallows anyone who displeases him.

Influence and Followers

Slinerak himself is a depraved individual; his only interest is spreading his form across the Cosmos and dissolving it in the process to make it his own. He is, however, aware that many other powerful entities in the Cosmos resist him and could even challenge his power, so he is content for the time being to play the long game. His influence and schemes ooze across the surface world, and he is a fundamentally malicious force that ultimately desires dominion and control over all things.

Using Slinerak as a Diety.

Using Slinerak as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron is to bind oneself to a force of unyielding stagnation and control. Slinerak is a Wild God of immense age who cannot hear prayers or traditional worship offered by mortals upon the surface of Ember. Therefore, to forge a connection with the Lord of Slime, a mortal must travel to the moon of Cora and reach the Palace of Rust. There, they must endure the Sovereign's oppressive presence and forge a suffocating contract of total submission. Strangely, all Oozes in existence seem to share an innate connection with Slinerk, and although he doesnt control every Ooze, a mortal could make a connection with Slinerk through them instead.
Slinerak.scoverview: Slinerak is an Elemental Sovereign and one of the most powerful Wild Gods in existence, having existed since Creation. He is also known as the Slime Lord and is considered the corrupted Elemental Lord of Earth. He is said to reside within the Palace of Rust upon the moon of Cora. Slinerak became a disgusting, shameful being long ago during the Age of Beasts and has been a malicious and rotten influence on the Cosmos ever since.

Ravela.name: Ravela
Ravela.text:
Areas of Concern: Fire, Healing

Typical Followers: Pyrrhen, Fire Elementals, Healers

Domains: Fire

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A serene face raised to the sky with both palms raised, surrounded by swirling flames.

Ravela is one of the three Elemental Sovereigns of Fire, a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild God } who embodies fire as a tool of restoration, nature, and healing. Following the cataclysmic events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering}, she single-handedly prevented the Fire Moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen} from descending into a total, lifeless wasteland. During the Shattering itself, her sister @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ZvsMcVcESynKQn8d]{Fiyara} turned on Ravela in a fit of corrupted rage. Even though she was also reportedly killed outright in the conflict, Ravela somehow survived. Because of this, she is often considered a goddess of rebirth through this miraculous, self-directed resurrection, yet she remains one of the few deities in Ember who visibly appears crippled by her wounds.

Throughout the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, Ravela is now well known as a powerful healer who wields a unique Healing Flame, a shimmering, golden-white flame that lacks the heat to burn but possesses the power to knit flesh, purge blight, and coax life from the earth. While this Healing Flame is powerful, ironically, it seems to be unable to fully heal Ravela herself, as she is by far the weakest of Elemental Sovereigns. Despite her weakened state, she is deeply revered by those who live in the harshest environments of Ember and on the Charred Moon itserlf.

Appearance

Ravela's pale body bears extensive scars from blackened, charred skin, with deep fissures that emit a soft white light. She appears visibly crippled, with thin, unused legs that prevent her from walking. While some in her situation might radiate agony or resentment, Ravela is calm and serene. Her face, though scarred, remains composed, and her eyes hold a steady, patient warmth. Dominating her broken silhouette are two magnificent wings of pure, golden-white flame. These wings ripple with the fluid grace of silk in the wind, casting a gentle, restorative light around her. They are the only parts of her that seem untouched by her conflict with her sister. These wings give rise to her most well-known moniker as the Firebird of Ragen.

Influence and Followers

Ravela is deeply loved by the remaining Pyrrhen and Fire elementals on Ragen; she is seen as both a saviour and a motherly figure. Following the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, much of the moon remains a wasteland full of lingering monsters and terrors. In this brutal environment, Ravela and her dedicated followers act as both guardians and gardeners. They maintain hearth-sites, massive bastions of warmth and light where the healing fire of Ravela keeps the monsters at bay while tirelessly working to purge the abyssal rot from the moon’s crust. It is said that the Phoenix, the legendary bird that resurrects itself in flame, was created by Ravela, and anyone who speaks with one is able to speak to Ravela as well.

On the surface of Ember, her followers are far fewer but no less devoted. They are typically found in the most scarred landscapes or places that desperately need healing, such as among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} attempting to resist the undead plague of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Ossarchate}.

Using Ravela as a Deity

Using Ravela as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron is an act of embracing resilience over power. Ravela provides a fundamentally nurturing source of power, and her magic doesn't just mend flesh; it targets trauma and corruption, making her the premier choice for those combating Abyssal monsters. A devotee of Ravela often plays the role of the traditional healer, someone who wants to fix the world and those around her. Thankfully for the mortals on the surface world, despite Ravela never leaving the moon of Ragen, she can connect with mortals through creatures known as Phoenixes.
Ravela.scoverview: Ravela is one of the Elemental Sovereigns of fire, and she resides upon the Charred Moon of Ragen. Ravela has been instrumental is preventing the Charred Moon from becoming a total wasteland after the events of The Shattering. She is a nurturing and compassionate being who was nearly destroyed by her corrupted sibling Fiyara and is associated with rebirth and restoration due to her miraculous recovery.

Lorgi.name: Lorgi
Lorgi.text:
Areas of Concern: Directness, Technology

Typical Followers: Alchemists, Scientists

Domains: Fire

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.SXks9PsVzNyIPuDH]{Tanir}

Symbol: A fiery steam furnace overflowing with flames, surrounded by gears and pipes.

Lorgi is one of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Tl4gvmUGThkZdrUd]{Elemental Sovereigns of Fire}, an extremely ancient, some say primordial, being that arose during creation. He is known as either the Fire Shaper or the Blast Lord, depending on who you ask, and he has an intense fascination with technology and progress. Unlike other @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild Gods}, who remain aloof, Lorgi is a remarkably approachable entity with a long-storied connection to the mortals of Ember. He is frequently credited with guiding fledgling cultures toward technological enlightenment, serving as a charismatic mentor who delights in conversation and genuinely cares about the daily lives of mortals. Despite his vast power, he remains well-informed about current events, often proving more knowledgeable about local politics than the people he is talking with.

Curiously, although he seems to be a Wild God bound to the moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}, he is not physically confined to it. Instead, he wanders the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} and has spent countless millennia walking the surface of Ember. Exactly how he is able to do this is unclear. Scholars and researchers suggest that he has discovered a way to maintain a connection to his domain through some invention or advanced magical knowledge. In recent years, Lorgi has settled within the Tayan Empire. Establishing a monumental workshop in the capital city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7iZDVtrBO7326XZY]{Caren'ac} and assuming leadership of the Mechanica, an organization dedicated to the creation of Aethyra.

Appearance

Lorgi appears Human, albeit with a strangely animalistic face and two horns resembling those of a beast. His skin is a deep, earthy red, patterned with rippling dark brown markings that shift across his form like cooling magma. In certain areas, his skin appears cracked, revealing an intense, pressurized fire that sputters and hisses beneath the surface, as if he is a living engine perpetually on the verge of an eruption.

His eyes are typically a calm, dark brown, but they are said to ignite with a fierce, predatory red whenever he hunts or is pushed to battle. He dresses in a sophisticated blend of intricate, deep-black clothing and heavy armor, accented with rich crimson. Upon his hips rest his twin Fire Lancers. These two curious magical weapons are masterpieces of both engineering and elemental power, acting as direct conduits that channel the raw power of the Force of Fire.

Influence and Followers

Lorgi maintains a diverse and widespread following, ranging from the Fire Elementals and Pyrrhen upon the Charred Moon of Ragen to the many mortals across the surface of Ember. To the Pyrrhen, Lorgi is a figure of profound awe and strength; he is seen as a savior who held the world together following the devastation of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear} and the tragic corruption of his sibling, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ZvsMcVcESynKQn8d]{Fiyara}. However, his reputation varies widely by geography. In regions outside the Tayan Empire, Lorgi is often viewed through a more fearful lens as a god of war or a warmonger, fueled by his close association with the militaristic Tayans and his own personal destructive exploits.

Despite his terrifying power, Lorgi remains remarkably approachable and conversational, a trait rarely seen in beings of his experience. He deliberately keeps his circle of direct followers small, as he is an exacting and grueling mentor. He expects those he grants power to be as strong-willed and ruthless in their defense of others as he is himself. His influence is most visible within the Tayan Empire, where he has found a society whose principles and goals mirror his own fascination with progress and the defense of the Cosmos. By leading the Mechanica, Lorgi has personally overseen the development of the Tayan Empire’s most significant technological marvels. Most notable among these is the infamous Aethyra.

Using Lorgi as a Deity.

Using Lorgi as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron is to enter a demanding partnership with a master engineer who favors industrial progress in the pursuit of defending the Cosmos. Unlike other deities who communicate through visions or distant voices, Lorgi connects with his followers through a singular, magically infused object known as The Firex. This intricate piece of machinery, which looks like a brass-cased pocket watch, serves as a direct two-way communication device, allowing his followers to contact him. Lorgi deliberately keeps his circle of direct followers small, selecting only those with the ruthless willpower to act and to pursue technology and science with a clear mind and steady pair of hands.

I like Lorgi. He's direct and honest, but I can't stand that he's working with the Tayan Empire. He’s turned half of Caren'ac into a clockwork heart full of machinery, pipes, and mist and steam. Lorgi thinks he’s guiding them toward progress, but he’s forgotten that mortals can manipulate gods just as easily as one another.

~Laeora
Lorgi.scoverview: Lorgi is one of the three Elemental Sovereigns of Fire from the Charred Moon of Ragen. They are known as the Blast Lord, and patrol Ragen and even other realms in the Cosmos on guard against forces of corruption and darkness. Lorgi is well known among mortals and is one of the only Elemental Sovereigns to be worshipped as a fully-fledged deity on the surface within the Tayan Empire.
Lorgi.sgamemaster:
Lorgi has been an active member of the pantheons of various cultures since the elder days; he was worshipped by the Aedir and played a crucial role in their advanced technological expansion. He was, however, stunned by the Shattering and was said to spend hours staring into space in disbelief. As the consequences of the Shattering unfolded and the Abyssal Shear tore itself open, Lorgi was one of the first beings to spring into action.

The Charred Moon of Ragen played a critical role during the events of the Abyssal Shear, coming under direct attack by a large number of Abyssal monsters. The exact accounts are unclear, but the three united Lords of Fire, Friyara, Lorgi, and Rarvela, resisted for a time before Friyara shockingly turned upon her siblings and grievously wounded Rarvela. As the Fire moon of Ragen burned and became the charred wasteland it is today, it was Lorgi who managed to trap his rampaging sister in a rift in reality, banishing her to the surface world and hiding her away in the volcano Hekkiro.

Since that time, Lorgi has been a relentless champion against the forces of the Abyss, not only engaging directly but also encouraging and guiding mortals to resist such threats.

Fiyara.name: Fiyara
Fiyara.text:
Areas of Concern: Hatred, Spite, Destruction.

Typical Followers: Cultists

Domains: Fire

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A charred burning claw, surrounded by orange and purple smoke.

Fiyara was once the radiant protector of the moon @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}, a goddess of warmth who nurtured the Pyrrhen and the moon's many creatures with maternal ferocity. However, the catastrophic events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} changed her beyond recognition, devastating her realm and fracturing her mind. Driven to insanity by the loss of her @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild God} domain, Fiyara turned upon her own siblings, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KQF9QommtN6ITiLW]{Lorgi} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WMO5VwobQNmjaXQA]{Ravela}, in a civil war that physically tore Ragen apart. Now banished from the moon and imprisoned within the Volcano of Hekkiro on the surface of Ember by her brother, she has transformed into a deity of pure destruction. She now seeks to consume life in a conflagration of Voidfire, a dark, ethereal flame capable of burning through a mortal’s soul and awakening their deepest impulses of jealousy, wrath, and spite.

Since her imprisonment within the Volcano of Hekkiro, Fiyara has not been idle, constructing a sprawling fortress of black metal and churning lava. Ever since the Shattering, her corrupting influence has twisted countless creatures and peoples nearby, creating an army of hate-filled elementals. She is a desperate, caged animal with the power of a star, slowly leaking her influence into the surrounding lands.

A mysterious and ancient connection exists between Fiyara and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons} of Ember. The breath of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.0CquHJco0yougg3S]{Cruel Dragons} bears a striking resemblance to her Voidfire, leading scholars to believe she may have played a role in their creation. Dragons have been known to venerate Fiyara with a fanatical reverence, viewing her as the source of their destructive fire and power. There may also be a connection between @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.GRs2vgeVsDpWPqjh]{Drakons} and Fiyara, but this is even less clearly understood.

Fire can be a source of warmth, life, and progress. But what about its darker, hungrier, more destructive side? That’s what Voidfire is. It doesn't just consume. It burns away your reasons for being kind and patient, leaving nothing behind but hate. It’s not an element. It’s an infection.

~Laeora

Appearance

Fiyara is a titanic entity of shifting, dark-violet flame. She appears as a massive humanoid torso of fire, emerging from the jagged, glowing rift at her waist, which keeps her trapped beneath the Volcano of Hekkiro. Upon her head rests a blackened, twisted metal crown, and her two arms are similarly charred, ending in massive claws.

Influence and Followers

Across the Cosmos, Fiyara is seen as a loathsome figure, a betrayer who attacked and attempted to kill her own family. Most mortals are unaware of her, but those who uncover her history are universally horrified by her existence and the unnatural properties of her Voidfire. This soul-burning flame does not ignite on its own; instead, it tends to manifest in blighted regions already weakened by decay or the lingering corruption of other monsters. In these dark pockets of the world, mortals already consumed by their own grievances find themselves susceptible to her influence.

Using Fiyara as a Deity.

Using Fiyara as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron is an especially dangerous path of slow inenitable corruption, where a follower will slowly slip into uncontrollable hatred and rage as time passes. To receive her power, a mortal would typically make a pilgrimage to the outskirts of the Hekkiro Volcano and be close enough to her influence to become enthralled. Or if a mortal is unlucky enough to find a place where Voidfire already burns, Fiyara finds the cracks in the mortal’s mind, such as unresolved grudges, jealousy, or a desire for vengeance. Once they devote themselves to Fiyara, the mortal becomes a conduit for Voidfire, becoming more consumed by hate and rage. Over time, her followers begin to resemble their goddess; their skin becomes ashen and cracked, their eyes glow with a dim light, and they find it increasingly difficult to feel any emotion other than a cold, simmering rage.
Fiyara.scoverview: Fiyara is known as the Elemental Mistress of Hatred. Once an Elemental Sovereign of fire, she is now infused with corrupted energy and a deeply evil being. She lies deep beneath Hekkiro the largest volcano on the surface of Ember, trapped halfway through a rift in the Cosmos. She is said to control Corrupted Fire, capable of burning through a mortal's soul and awakening spite, jealousy and wrath and a desire to destroy and consume.
Fiyara.sgamemaster:
During the chaotic events of the Abyssal Shear, as the Cosmos burned, Fiyara battled the Abyssal monsters assaulting the moon of Ragen alongside her brother Lorgi and her sister Ravela. The ferocity of the conflict on Ragen was breathtaking, as armies of the Pyrrhen held back hosts of Abyssal monsters, repelling their advances again and again. But the strength and scale of the assault soon took its toll. Tragically, Fiyara's domain fell under an unstoppable assault, with some accounts claiming that a Herald of an Outer God was present. As she witnessed the destruction on her domain, something snapped in her mind, driving her into an uncontrollable rage. Her rage gave her the power to annihilate the Abyssal forces, but she could not stop, and her newfound abilities made her nearly unstoppable.

She continued her furious path of annihilation, this time setting her sights on the rest of Ragen, attacking her sister directly when Ravela tried to heal her. Some ancient records insist that Ravela was slain on the spot, while others claim she was merely wounded. Afterwards, Lorgi stepped in to engage his sister in a climactic battle that shook Ragen to its core. Unable to kill his sister, Lorgi used the last of his strength to banish Fiyara from the Ragen, casting her down to the surface of Ember, where she remains imprisoned within the molten heart of Hekkiro.

Herald of the Whispering Choir.text:

Herald of the Whispering Choir.scoverview: A cacophony of silence fills the empty spaces of your mind, an absence that reverberates through you like a precursor to something you just can't remember.

Godkiller Orinoth.name: Godkiller Orinoth
Godkiller Orinoth.text:
• Keywords: Serpent, Maw, Hunger

  • Category: God-Like Being (Leviathan)

  • Areas of Concern: Knowledge, Power, Hunger

  • Sacred Weapon: Fanged Blade

  • Other Names: Godkiller, Hunger in the Deep

  • Pantheons: None

Edict of Godkiller Orinoth

Come to me, so that I may feed.

Orinoth is an unusually intelligent and beguiling @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan} that has become one of the most feared and dangerous of its kind in the known world. He primarily resides within the Yawning Sea, an area that covers essential trade routes between the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian Republic}, and the Lowlands and the primary shipping lane to the great city of Ordain from the west. Orinoth's lair is said to exist within a deep trench, and he can sense when brave and foolhardy ships pass by overhead. He greatly enjoys sinking such vessels on a whim, consuming the reckless sailors flailing in the dark water. However, he can also breathe upon land and drag himself along coastlines to attack villages and anyone slow enough to remain on their path. He is also known to bask in the sun upon rocky coastlines or beaches, especially when nearby creatures or mortals arrive to offer him food or sacrifices.

Orinoth is well known for his eternal hunger, not only to satisfy their unquenchable desire for nourishment, but he also greatly desires knowledge and information about the world. He is rumored to absorb memories after slowly digesting whatever he consumes over many weeks. For creatures like animals and beasts, this is instinctual, animalistic knowledge. For sapient creatures like mortal humanoids, or especially cunning creatures like monsters or other Leviathans, he can access their deepest thoughts and desires. Orinoth often uses this information to reach out to deceive the consumed ones' relatives or loved ones and convince them to serve him.

He is often described as utterly malicious in his actions; he is greedy and extremely possessive of his knowledge, but mortals can speak with him over vast distances if they have a connection. He may be willing to gift power to such mortals if they serve him and further his agenda, but his only true goal is to further his understanding of the world by consuming and eating everything he can. He is only limited by his fear of being caught by several @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} at once upon land, and he is well aware that he needs to moderate his actions just enough so that powerful entities do not seek him out above other concerns.

Appearance

Orinoth is a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan}, but they are an extremely unusual and mysterious example of their kind. He is terrifyingly intelligent and manipulative and has amassed vast knowledge throughout his long life thanks to his innate ability to absorb memories of those he consumes. Their form is akin to a colossal eel or serpent, albeit one with a face that is strangely forward-facing. They possess many rows of extremely sharp teeth and two eyes of burning blue light and glittering fin rays that glow blue, deep red, and pink. In the darkness of the seas, countless shimmering bioluminescence strands flow behind their main body, glittering in pulsing patterns that are said to captivate and enthrall anyone who stares too long at them. Orinoth also bears strong arms along his massive length with powerful dexterous hands that they greatly enjoy using to accentuate their speech.

Influence and Followers

Few beings on Ember are as depraved or as cunning as Orinoth. In pursuit of their eternal hunger, Orinoth spends their time scheming and plotting in decades-long efforts to enthrall mortals and trick them into venturing over his lair. This may mean becoming a helpful, almost kindly source of information for scholars or taking on a more dominant and overpowering persona to force weak-minded fools into betraying their friends and people. Regardless, Orinoth is insidious and is capable of speaking into the minds of beings many hundreds or even thousands of miles from their physical location in the same way a deity might. Many mortal beings can become tricked into serving them, and Orinoth uses his vast knowledge as bait to mass even more over time.

Some follow Orinoth willingly, usually aquatic monsters such as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.qCdveLhf5tJuFvNC]{Skum} or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XjJZj935v0dxoyWg]{Nepkela}, who build shrines and crude temples underwater or along coastlines to venerate Orinoth like a deity. Blood sacrifices to Orinoth by such creatures are common, and they will attack, raid, and pillage the lands around them to satisfy their master's needs.

Various @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} have hunted Godkiller Orinoth since his emergence, and he is currently a target for many more, though often lower down on the list of current threats. Most fail in their attempts to kill him, as he always finds a way to escape or kill anyone who ventures into his lair. However, he is hated beyond measure by the Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae}, who wants nothing more than to see him slain. She was close friends, and some say even lovers, with the Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar,} who Orinoth slew. Followers of Malae, otherwise known as Witches, will often take it upon themselves to hunt down and destroy followers of Orinoth.
Godkiller Orinoth.scoverview: Godkiller Orinoth is the beguiling and powerful sapient Leviathan that earned their title after killing the Shard God Janar. They are a vicious and depraved being that enjoys consuming mortal creatures and absorbing their memories, and currently reside deep within the Yawning Sea between the Lumek Firelands and the Lowlands. Orinoth is worshipped by monsters such as Skum and Nepkela, but other mortal beings can be enthralled by Orinoth's whispered promises of power.
Godkiller Orinoth.sgamemaster:
Orinoth was once a normal Leviathan in the ancient days of the Age of Beasts, an eel-like creature that was both large and powerful and swam without thought between the world's oceans. In those ancient days, Orinoth was not particularly powerful nor the most cunning; instead, it was a carrion feeder and scavenger often outclassed by other Leviathans. It did, however, have a mysterious ability that set it apart; whenever it ate a creature's nervous system, Orinoth would gain some of its awareness and knowledge. It's said that Orinoth continued to exist like this for many thousands of years, all the while becoming smarter and more cunning.

At some point, its predation and lust for mortal creatures drew the ire of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar}, the ancient Jarn deity of the hunt, and the two engaged in a legendary battle that is still sung in taverns across Ember. For many days and nights, the two fought, each inflicting grievous wounds upon the other across beaches and shallow seas, until it's said that Janar slipped upon slick rocks and fell into deeper water. Orinoth surged with their last ounce of strength to wrap their long body around Janar and dragged him underwater. Some say that the crushing depths finally proved too much for Janar, and Orinoth utterly consumed him. Others say that Orinoth was too wounded and weak to feed and spent years recovering. Meanwhile, Janar's body was found by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae}, who enshrined it in a hidden temple. Regardless, after the battle, Orinoth would forever be known as the Godkiller, and they have been hated and reviled by most beings ever since.

Orinoth is deathly afraid of only one being on Ember, the Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rmMWMD9iFRm6Nl3x]{Obrisire}. No known interaction has ever been recorded between the two of them but Obrisire’s followers maintain that their god greatly detests Orinoth and would kill him if the opportunity ever presented itself.

Vesper.name: Vesper
Vesper.text:
Moniker: Mother Mask

Areas of Concern: Illusions, Obsession, Longing

Typical Followers: Fey

Domains: Unknown

Pantheons: None.

Symbol: A cracked feline mask, surrounded by swirling mists and shadows.

Edict of Vesper

Reality is a burden my dears; let my veil be your comfort.

Vesper is one of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia} and the ruler of Naloria Vale, a region of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} where shadows have weight and both light and darkness are mere afterthoughts. She is a true mistress of illusions, to such an extent that she can make things real by simply believing them so. Her magic is so ancient that other Casia consider it thick, dense, and even unsettling, seemingly woven from the raw essence of the Shadow Realm itself.

She presents herself as a kind being, but only at a surface level. While her open kindness and empathy are not a mask, they are only the first layer of her personality. She speaks to those who need comfort and protection from the harsh reality of the world, providing exactly what you want to hear, crafting magical illusions that comfort the soul. But her gifts always come with a price, as mortals' desires will keep them locked in lies until they lose the ability to discern illusion from reality. She finds mortals eternally fascinating, in part because she wants to help them, but more so because she is obsessed with their imaginations and fantasies. She will pluck a secret desire from a mortal's mind and manifest it, a dead lover, a lost parent, or a pile of unimaginable riches, just so she can weave a new illusion into her complex web.

Vesper’s most enduring legacy is the creation of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.eyvVaX4c1rMos0ws]{Zeph} during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}. Her heart was once ensnared by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Wfy3RfrQNFW8JWOv]{Nymbohr}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Tl4gvmUGThkZdrUd]{Elemental Lord of Air}. In a desperate bid to enthrall him, Vesper traveled to the Wind Moon, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura}, where she studied the primal nature of the winds and began weaving increasingly dense illusions to enhance the moon's elemental beauty.

Almost by happenstance, she manifested the first Zeph, beings born from the marriage of shadow-magic and the untamed winds of Aura. For a time, Vesper and Nymbohr doted on their children, but the Zeph were never meant to be playthings. Their inherent need for freedom clashed with Vesper’s desire to control every thread of their existence. When Nymbohr and the Zeph ultimately spurned her love to claim their own independence, Vesper retreated to Primordis, broken and enveloped in sadness, leaving her children to build a society on Aura, a civilization born of her magic, yet forever wary of her reach.

Appearance

As a Casia, Vesper moves with a feline, predatory grace, her form draped in liquid shadows and translucent silks that shift and whirl in unending patterns that reflect the dreams of her followers. Her fur is completely black, but when she exerts her power, it shimmers with the violet-grey hue of a rainstorm, battered by raging winds. Her eyes are unblinking sapphire stars that seem to shimmer with an impossible number of reflected pinpricks of light. When she moves, a faint ghostly resonance, like the sound of a hundred soft flutes, can be heard playing from the echoes just behind the listener's line of sight.

Influence and Followers

Within the Shadow Realm of Primordis, Vesper rules the shifting landscapes of Naloria Vale from a throne of shadows, and she has a number of dedicated fey followers. While she is outnumbered by the more aggressive Casia of Primordis, her absolute mastery over shadow-magic and illusions ensures that few dare to encroach upon her borders. On the surface world, Vesper’s influence manifests as a haunting call to the grieving, the broken, and those who find the "real" world unbearable. Many of these followers are unintentional as they stumble into her influence through dreams or where portals to the Shadow Realm bleed into Ember. Mortals tend to see her as a maternal, empathetic savior who offers a sanctuary from pain, unaware that her empathy is a slow path towards losing themselves in illusions.

Using Vesper as Deity

Using Vesper as a deity for a Cleric or Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron, is a rare and dangerous path. First, it requires a mortal to be aware of her, sufficiently creative yet broken, to attract her attention, as Vesper grants power only to those who connect with her deep need to aid those who are desperate. Mortals gradually give more and more of themselves to Vesper, slowly losing memories they might find dear to them, even if they are painful. Her demands are often simple, but she cannot help but push her mortal followers toward interesting, often dangerous paths in order to later reap the seeds she has sown and claim the dark, painful memories that doing so might bring.
Vesper.scoverview: Vesper is a very old and powerful Casia from Primordis who speaks in a purring resonance that calms the most fractured soul. She is a patron for those who seek to weave beauty from shadows and for the broken-hearted who wish to turn their memories into living magic and healing. To serve Vesper is to be seen, comforted, and understood, wrapped in the warmth of an ancient grace that protects you from the harsh coldness of reality.

Nalgomith.scoverview: Nalgomith is one of the Sixteen Daemos, the powerful beings that rule Signara, known for creating the fiends that would later become the Wirrun. He is a deeply curious and knowledgeable entity who has researched a vast amount of esoteric lore and arcane phenomena over his unimaginably long life, making his mannerisms seem alien and otherworldly. He is lost in schemes, machinations, and plans that are so mysterious, layered, and complex that he appears almost random in his actions.

Nymbohr.name: Nymbohr
Nymbohr.text:
Areas of Concern: Wind, Peace

Typical Followers: Zeph, Air Elementals

Domains: Air

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A soft, hazy mist with almost invisible clasped hands within.

Nymbohr was once a being of immense strength and calm who ruled over the Hollow Moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura}. However, he has long since faded into seemingly nothingness. He now seems to exist as a ghost in the breath of the world, lacking the will to speak or perhaps the agency to intervene. To those who know of his existence, he is thought to be present in every pocket of air and a being that exists in every corner of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}. For those sensitive to the elemental force of Air, Nymbohr can be felt as a lingering pressure in the air around them rather than a divine voice. These individuals do not receive visions nor can they hear a voice that helps or guides them; instead, they experience the Sovereign's presence as a literal pressure, as if a faint hand were pressing down on their shoulder.

Once a primordial @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild God} of immense power, Nymbohr no longer appears to have a domain or a place of power, yet he has somehow kept his sanity. This perplexes many scholars, with some believing he has transcended the typical capabilities of a Wild God, while others argue that he has indeed descended into madness, with his insanity manifesting as a cold indifference to life.

Appearance

Nymbohr lacks a tangible body; he manifests as a shimmering distortion in the atmosphere, spread across the entire Cosmos. This lack of body means that he cannot be injured and may as well not exist for any practical purpose.

Influence and Followers

Nymbohr has very few followers on the surface of Ember. But the few who are rare typically find comfort in silence and isolation. Rather than priests seeking divine favor or intervention, his devotees are often master navigators, stoic philosophers, or hermits who interpret Nymbohr's state of mind through the rigorous study of weather patterns and shifts in the surrounding air's pressure. Because Nymbohr no longer has a domain or seat of power, his followers are often nomadic or dwell in isolated mountain caves.

On Aura, Nymbohr is venerated by various sects and groups among the creatures and air elementals of the moon. Among the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.eyvVaX4c1rMos0ws]{Zeph} in the city of Condundrum, he remains highly respected and worshipped to this day. As Nymbohr has no temples and no physical presence, potential followers often attempt to bind themselves to his power by ritually blindfolding themselves in isolated places of the world. Once blindfolded, the initiate shifts their perception and reaches out to the air and wind, attempting to achieve a perfect equilibrium. The process is difficult and may take many years, but followers often speak of a true connection when they first feel something akin to a hidden hand on their shoulder, a literal, physical pressure that anchors the follower to Nymbohr’s elemental power and allows them to read the air's intent.

Using Nymbohr as a Deity.

Using Nymbohr as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron is to enter a pact with an entity that does not seem to exist in the traditional sense. Any followers walk the path of complete independence, as their deity will give them no answers and has little care for their goals or dreams. Mortals are granted power in a very abstract sense, and they must find their own way through the chaos of life, knowing that the Sovereign of Air is always watching but will never act on their behalf.
Nymbohr.scoverview: Nymbohr is the Elemental Sovereign of Air, a being that is curiously absent from all conscious concerns. They are said to drift through the skies of Aura the Hollow Moon, but spend vast amounts of time drifting throughout the Sea of Stars as well. While they are indisputably a powerful force of creation, there are no known examples of them ever interacting with others, and they are famously aloof.

Ku'arta.name: Ku'arta
Ku'arta.text:
Areas of Concern: Bargains, Suffering, Power

Typical Followers: Monks, Criminals, The Desperate

Domains: Other

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A chain made of glowing symbols

Edict of Ku'arta

If you can do it, prove it

Ku'arta is an ancient deity from a time long before the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.R97NAeTio76VFKWI]{Age of Rediscovery}. Some believe he was once @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.V1gzeX0JWSOCQ7LD]{Jarn}, while others suggest he predates even that and is connected to the mythical and infamous @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.186yO79YKDxPh0qT]{Theroch}. He has a long history of conflicts, exploits, and malevolent acts. Though not actively worshipped today, he is feared and well known throughout the world in dark underworlds and seedy taverns. One famous story recounts how Ku'arta personally murdered the high priestess of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.HN2Zimps4w5XniZe]{Old Carinth} thousands of years ago, simply because she was widely beloved and beautiful, igniting a permanent feud with Lantyr and her followers. Many attempts have been made by other gods to kill Ku'arta, but he has survived them all.

Ku'arta is indifferent to concepts of good and evil, caring only about direct actions that achieve interesting, outlandish results through increasingly difficult challenges. This attracts a diverse group of followers, outcasts, fugitives, criminals, and some just seeking power. To many, he is a stereotypical villain and someone who promotes evil acts, but despite this vilification, Ku'arta has some redeeming qualities. He seems to genuinely care for his followers and has a nearly parental fondness for those who complete his tasks and grow stronger. He is seldom angry or vindictive; if a follower fails a task, he remains understanding and calm. If someone can no longer worship him or fulfill their duties, he strips them of the power he granted and moves on with a strange sense of regret. Unfortunately, he does not ignore them entirely and may send another follower to hunt down and eliminate a failure due to a sense of `putting them out of their misery`.

Following the rise of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Ossarchate} and the undead in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7zFmCJqtAp32EaI1]{Moiran Bonelands}, Ku'arta became an unusual protector against the undead invading the eastern lands of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian city-states}. Initially, the undead crossing the mountains disappeared, and the Blood Barons lost contact with entire armies. It was later discovered that Ku'arta possessed a secret method of destroying undead in a terrifying manner. The exact nature of his power is unknown, but the Blood Barons fear him and his followers. Ku'arta often sends his followers to kill large groups of undead in the Ossarchate as part of a challenge, which is oddly a beneficial act given his reputation.

Appearance

Ku'arta appears as a tall, masculine human with a slender build and an inviting, wide smile. His hair is described as nearly fluorescent white, complemented by pale skin and striking purple eyes. He often wears a grin and has a mischievous, playful nature. However, his mood can quickly shift to twisted and darker tones the more time you spend with him. His most noticeable feature is a prosthetic metal jaw with sharp fanged lower teeth. His followers are often encouraged to mutilate themselves similarly by replacing their jaws in the same manner.

Influence and Followers

Following Ku'arta is said to be a double-edged sword. He is a god who delights in worship, perhaps more than any other, and rewards his followers with great power, but only if they can accomplish increasingly difficult and progressively more sadistic challenges. These challenges may start relatively mundane, such as searching out a hidden place or killing a certain monster, but gradually become harder to accomplish and increasingly evil until Ku'arta begins demanding extreme acts of cruelty, such as competing against other followers to see how many people they can kill before being caught. Most mortals who start worshipping Ku'arta eventually end up killing themselves while trying to carry out an impossible task, and Ku'arta finds this incredibly satisfying in a way that is hard to describe. Followers of Ku'arta are rare because of this and are hunted, outlawed, and even executed when discovered, depending on the culture.

Using Ku'arta as a Deity

Using Ku'arta as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron is a path of pain and suffering. Ku'arta is inherently manipulative and abusive, and his followers are at his mercy, dancing to his whims. He regards his followers as treasured playthings, appearing to care for them on one hand, yet pushing them toward actions that may ultimately lead to their death. He speaks to his followers with a kind, warm voice, and he is a very present and active deity, one of the few that will intervene if necessary directly, but doing so always comes with a price. Any public display of devotion to Ku'arta is swiftly met with suspicion, persecution, and immediate intervention from local authorities or religious groups aiming to eliminate his influence, and most of his followers tend together in secret cults.
Ku'arta.scoverview: Ku'arta is a Shard God spoken of in whispers, he is a god of torment, suffering, and manipulation. He is such a terrifying force in the world that the undead Blood Barons of Moiran are said to fear him. Residing in the Far'rent Mountains to the east of the Kelmezian City States he is said to rule over a hidden city of worshippers that he takes great pleasure in controlling.

Auris Bor.name: Auris Bor
Auris Bor.text:
At the heart of the Auris Bor is Vólun, the Father Bear. A truly ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God}, Vólun is a primordial being whose origins predate @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, stretching back to the era of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.o38uqC8NLxOWxA4i]{Vaznor} during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}. It's said that even when the Vaznor encountered Vólun, he was already an ancient being, but most consider such stories myths. His transition from a Vaznor deity to the Father of the Auris Bor meant that he eventually became a symbol for strength and endurance in the face of great trials, and ever since, he has been a bedrock of the north.

The relationship between the thirteen gods of the Auris Bor is intensely personal. They are siblings, children, and rivals, and while they may bicker or hide secrets, they are deeply protective of one another and their people. Most of the members reside in a single city at the northern end of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak} triblelands, called Vellatagé. This is home to the Kistrind, the Kindred Hall, a vast structure made of stone and ancient wood, constructed by Hrymer. Both Vólun and his wife, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lc2ZMAGsL7pH1wEF]{Sokali}, reside in the hall alongside their two sons, Hrymer and Astric, and their daughter, Eirun. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.pEeJhnepW0PzeN9X]{Themis} is wed to Eirun, and they have two children, Varros and Gildaré, though Gildaré is lost. Nerrissae was once Sokali's adopted daughter and lived in Kistrind until her father drove her from the hall. The other deities of the Northern Host either travel to Vellatagé seasonally or at random, or are closely associated with the pantheon due to intense rivalry, as is the case with @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.PnF3A28nmu3caMgq]{Erisagosa}.

While the Bejak culture is most closely associated with the Auris Bor pantheon, both the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.TUt9EUMWp8pV1wXe]{Fikost} and Vartic clans honor the Northern Host. The nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.xImbz6Nf4mMxtKF1]{Wardcall} has shifted from the Auris Bor to the Trine of Wards, although many still build small shrines dedicated to the ancient deities of their ancestors in secret. In ancient times, many of the oldest Auris Bor gods were worshipped by the Vaznor, but this changed after the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.6thz1HFNCR4W3doS]{Troll Invasions}.
