Auris Bor.scoverview: The Auris Bor, often called the Northern Host, is a pantheon defined by blood and the relentless need for survival. They operate as a close-knit, sometimes volatile divine family. These gods oversee the hearth and tundra, where the boundary between life and death is as fragile as ice. For the Northern inhabitants of Aterica, their gods are more than distant voices; they are ancient ancestors living among them, offering protection and guidance.

Laeora.name: Laeora
Laeora.text:
Author of the Setting Compendium

Laeora is responsible for the majority of the Setting Compendium writing, drawing on her own perspective, gathered notes, and experiences across the ages. While not everything is written by her, the Setting Compendium of the Ember setting could be considered her Amber Historie, said to contain a largely accurate account of the world's forces, creatures, monsters, and beings, even those found on the Elemental Moons and the distant Inner Realms.

Laeora is an extremely well-known figure within the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}. She has been a celebrated hero of renown since long before the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire, with records of her appearance going back to the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}. Her identity is something of a mystery as she doesnt seem to be a deity, nor does she seem to be mortal. She is focused on history, recording events, and learning about the world. However, the way people view her has begun to shift recently, as she seems to be taking more opinionated stances on political and social issues. Many scrolls, accounts, and hidden and secret texts are sometimes recovered from ancient days, with her name appearing as the author. Even today, Laeora is credited with numerous historical records. She appears in the most unlikely of places, and while some consider her to be a strange tale or myth, most scholars agree that she is as long-lived and as knowledgeable as she claims.

Many believe Laeora to be a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God}, something she corrects whenever the opportunity arises. Despite her denials, her appearances are rare enough that debates regarding her true nature and her striking similarity to known deities can persist for decades. Even other Shard Gods are often perplexed by her true longevity and source of power, as she offers few explanations for either when she surfaces in populated areas.

Despite her immense age and wisdom, Laeora's memory is not a perfect historical record. Paradoxically, while she can recall the broad origins of something like the Aedir Empire, she struggles with the details of those distant eras. She tends to forget highly specific, localized events that occurred in ages past, particularly the mundane ones, as well as emotional contexts she never properly processed. This vulnerability is the singular reason she keeps the Amber Historie, a small, plain leather tome that serves as her personal, external memory. This tome is meticulously filled with her own observations, theories, and accounts from across millennia. It is her most treasured possession; without the detailed, physical record provided by the Amber Historie, the truth of many foundational events in Ember's history would be irrevocably lost.

Laeora is vehemently opposed to the rise of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire and views @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l5SNwXC8t3Qp3Ut3]{Calyn Kariset} as a tyrant. This has put her in a very unique situation, and she doesn't seem to hold back from helping repel the Tayan armies' advances, either by attempting to interfere with their many conquests or by exposing the Tayan imperial ambitions and evils through her writing, and is a key member of the organization known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.AXuTFye24hV7ciae]{Vanguard}. Curiously, her opposition seems somewhat personal, but Laeora has never elaborated on her motivations.

I have stood before cruel Emperors, brutal Queens, and mages of unparalleled power. I have strode across the ruins of great empires and powerful kingdoms that spanned worlds far beyond our own. I have met vain, power-hungry gods, resisted their tirades, and withstood their searing attempts to destroy my mind. I have witnessed the greatest magics and untamed sorceries lay waste to cities, armies, and entire nations, enough devastation to break the earth and tear the very sky asunder.

But never before have I laid eyes upon a being that resonated with such pure malice and absolute madness. I understood, in that immediate, agonizing moment, the full breadth of its unending hatred, its terrible power, and its desire for utter domination. With a horror that seized my very core, and for the briefest instant, I realized it was entirely aware of me. Not only was I completely at its mercy, my power stripped from me in an instant, but I knew without question that any lesser being would have been destroyed, and it took all of my willpower to resist. I realized that this.. thing.. was far greater, more dangerous, and more powerful than I could have possibly imagined.

The Shadow Within the Mists. Laeora, 1387 AS.

Appearance

Laeora appears as a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Human} woman of medium height, with an athletic build. Her most distinctive features are her soft, mousy-brown hair, which mysteriously shines like gold at the ends, and her glittering, bright-blue eyes with dark black shadows framing them. She is otherwise perfectly ordinary in all other physical aspects. Her attire is practical and understated; she favors a plain brown coat with traveler boots of exceptional quality. Across her chest, she wears crisscrossing leather bands over a dark shirt, which often serve as a makeshift harness for her pouches, small scrolls, and notes bound tightly to these straps for security. Strapped to her side is a seemingly simple, single-bladed sword of plain steel. On her other side is the Amber Historie, a small, plain leather tome with a small black pen attached by a blue ribbon. This tome is said to be an ancient artifact of legendary power, as it contains the written words of Laeora's entire life and her experiences of the world.

Laeora does not tend to wear armor, but she compensates for her lack of defense with incredible speed and agility. Accounts of her prowess with her blade are common in both ancient legends and recent reports from her battles against the Tayan Empire, where her sword skills are legendary. In combat, a soft glow can be seen surrounding her body and her sword. This distinct white and blue expression of her power grows stronger the longer she fights.

Influence and Followers

Her appearances over the last several decades fighting against the Tayan Empire have led many @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezians} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Mazirans} to adopt her symbol, and she has gathered a small, dedicated following. While her militant followers focus on her excellent tactical knowledge and martial power, she is also considered an extremely compassionate leader who genuinely cares about those under her command; thus, her followers adore her and fight furiously in her name. However, she is not always present at the front lines and still seems to wander a great deal, often giving warnings to other nations and peoples regarding the threat posed by the Tayan Empire's expansion.

It's also said that during the Sunfire Aedir Empire, Laeora had a large cult-like priesthood that worshipped her aspect of wisdom, but very little is known about this group. The few scraps of information do speak of how this group was also capable warriors, and it seems Laeora is no stranger to conflict.

Imperialism and arrogance often go hand in hand; as such, it's difficult to pin down the exact moment when the ruling family of ancient Towir first allowed themselves the grand, self-important delusion of the term 'empire.' It was never a single day of conquest, but a slow, quiet rot of hubris that set in. The transition from a dynasty of benign rulers to an empire was never about the scale of Aedir's influence but far more about the size of their ego.

The Sunfire Empire, Volume 4. Laeora 2351 AS.
Laeora.scoverview: I suppose I should start with the simplest truth: Laeora is me. I am a storyteller and a keeper of lost knowledge, a chronicler who has watched Ember spin through countless eons. Indeed. It is a curious thing, but some even worship me as a Goddess of History, which, quite frankly, I find absolutely laughable. Remarkable, the things mortals will believe! My memories, stories, and tales stretch across every single age of this world, from Creation to the present day. But after all this time, I must confess, my memories and notes are often incomplete.

Taryakel.name: Taryakel
Taryakel.text:
Moniker: The Solar Tyrant

Areas of Concern: War, Deception, Vanity

Typical Followers: Tyraphem

Domains: Unknown

Pantheons: The Blinding Truth

Symbol: Radiant wings surrounding a golden mirror.

Edict of Taryakel

Perfection is a light that leaves no shadows, nor darkness untouched.

Taryakel is perhaps the most dangerous being on the Inner Realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}, and an entity as old as @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.0bkmoi8aSFvbaCi0]{the First Dawn}. He views the millions of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} as his own reflected light and has a vanity that seems to surpass all others. To Taryakel, the faith of his kind is a resource to be harvested; he has spent eons subtly altering the rites and prayers of the Tyraphem so that every ounce of devotion intended for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} is instead directed towards himself and his own ego.

Taryakel does not possess the frantic ambition of the younger Tyraphem Lords; he possesses the absolute certainty of a true narcissist. He is soft-spoken, radiating a calm, terrifying, and warm persona that belies his inner cruelty, his self-importance, and deep need for attention and admiration. He treats the eternal war of Luxarum as a holy performance where every death is a sacrifice to his own glory and the glory of light. He is the master and leader of the main religion of Luxarum, known as the Blinding Truth, a philosophy that suggests only he is able to interpret the light from Lantyr, and all other beings are merely shadows waiting to be consumed or cast aside.

When it comes to his personal relationships, Taryakel is a being of cold, calculated interest. He recognizes the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods}, but views each and every one as lesser than himself. Even Lantyr, who he publicly venerates, but in truth he believes her to also be a lesser being. He holds a deep, visceral loathing for entities from the other inner realms, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia}, viewing them as creatures directly opposed to his shining light. However, his most active hatred is reserved for@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{ the Abyss}. While he is a narcissist, he is no coward, and he views the Abyss as the ultimate enemy, a glitch in the fabric of existence that threatens to dim his radiance. During the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}, he personally led his legions to the borders of Luxarum and beyond into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}, not out of a desire to save the lives of others, but to ensure the filth of the Abyss did not smudge the pristine Light of his domain.

Appearance

Taryakel is a blindingly radiant entity whose physical form is often obscured by the sheer intensity of his wings, which are not wings at all but more like roaring solar flares that lash out and incinerate anything that enters his personal space. His face is a featureless, polished Golden Plane so that when other Tyraphem kneel before him, they see only their own desperate, flawed reflections. His golden armor is flawless, ornate, overdesigned, and breathtaking to behold.

Influence and Followers

On Luxarum, Taryakel rules legions of other Tyraphem and celestials from his high seat within the Palace of Eternity, and his rule is questioned only by other Tyraphem Lords. On the surface world, Taryakel’s influence manifests as a form of righteousness that attracts misguided zealots, paladins, and those who oppose the great evils of the world, such as the undead. Many of these followers carry out his demands, assuming they are serving a righteous, warm entity, but ultimately, he possesses zero empathy or understanding of them. He operates from a state of absolute narcissism, viewing himself as a divine entity of light in a cosmos of distorted echoes and lesser lights. To Taryakel, his Tyraphem and the mortal followers of the surface are not individuals but instruments to further his own ends. One of his fervent beliefs is that history is irrelevant; only the present and the future matter, and he compels his followers to erase historical records or artifacts that do not highlight his own radiance.

Using Taryakel as a Deity

Using Taryakel as a deity for a Cleric, a Paladin, or as a Warlock Patron is rare across the surface world for two reasons. First, such devotion requires knowledge of Luxarum and a specific understanding of Taryakel, even if that knowledge is based on half-truths or outright lies about his benevolence. Second, Taryakel is only interested in communing with mortals who spark his curiosity or reflect his own vanity. To earn his support, a mortal must be fanatical enough to accept his absolute demands without hesitation, even when those commands are of questionable morality or require acts of profound cruelty.
Taryakel.scoverview: Taryakel is an ancient Tyraphem Lord from Luxarum and appears as a beacon of ultimate salvation, a radiant presence whose soft voice fills those who hear it with warmth. He offers a promise of absolute clarity and divine protection against the monsters and darkness of the Cosmos. His voice is a soothing, melodic resonance that calms the soul, and he invites his followers to see their own highest potential reflected within his golden, featureless brilliance.

Shard Gods.name: Shard Gods
Shard Gods.text:
Lore Summary

  • Origin: Created by communing with a Heart Crystal.

  • Mortal Aspects: They are ascended mortals that retain their physical bodies.

  • Worship: They can hear and grant distant prayers, intervening from anywhere in the cosmos, but are severely limited in power based on distance.

  • Soul Anchors: They have no impact on the Soul Cycle.

  • Destruction: They can be killed.

The Shard Gods of Ember are exceptionally powerful immortal individuals who gained their power through ascension. They are often part of sprawling webs of ancient ties, pantheons, and shared interests across thousands if not hundreds of thousands of years. Each Shard God has its own motivations surrounding the governance of their chosen aspects of power and domains and the people they hold dear. They can be fickle, resolute, charming, manipulative, or dangerously direct, and there is as much variation between Shard Gods as there is between mortals.

In the present age, hundreds of Shard Gods live upon the World of Ember, less now than before the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, but there are still six major pantheons containing multiple Shard Gods upon @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica} alone. Shard Gods can only be found upon the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}, and while some may travel to places like the Elemental Moons or the Inner Realms, this is rare. The vast majority of Shard Gods live among the cultures and peoples that worship them, sometimes hidden and guiding events from behind the scenes or openly displaying their power. Often, a Shard God will remain to guide their people or descendants, staying and living in the same area for millennia.

Shards Gods are not created as such; they are ascended mortals (or, in extremely rare cases, ascended creatures) that achieve godhood by touching and communing with a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal}. This process is not well understood, and the vast majority of mortals believe that to become a Shard God, all that is required is to discover a Heart Crystal and touch it. This is not accurate, however, and there are mysterious and obscure steps upon the path to ascension. Purity and goodness are seemingly not required, as there are many Shard Gods who are greedy, malicious, and foul. In fact, the criteria for Ascension is something that many spend their entire lives studying. Talking to a Shard God about what they experienced might be one of the first steps of that process, but unfortunately, few, if any, are able to describe the process in any detail, and it varies wildly enough that a single point of view cannot be trusted.

Mortals on the surface of Ember are well aware that while Shard Gods are extremely powerful beings, they can be killed or wounded, and there are many tales and stories of Shard Gods dying in conflict with cosmological forces, against one another, or even powerful mortals in a few rare situations. Despite this, many mortals dream of becoming a Shard God, which fuels their exploration and adventuring spirit to new heights as they search for Heart Crystals, some spending their entire lives pursuing power. Some of the Shards Gods active in the world today are very young, younger than some living mortals. @UUID[.B987VijfeT6i9TEI]{Aythorn}, a member of the @UUID[.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{Nineteen}, is roughly three hundred years old and ascended so recently that they barely have any followers other than the people they have directly interacted with. There is no strict overarching hierarchy within the ranks of Shard Gods, but some Pantheons have more strict and ordered roles for their members. The ancient pantheon of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} was partially ordered among family lineage and age.

Aspected Power

The chosen power of a Shard God over a particular element, force, or essence is often their most defining trait. But this isn't something that the Shard God actually has any special power or control over. Shard Gods are not granted any specific aspected power or domain upon ascension; instead, they tend to gravitate towards concepts that resonate with their own personalities. This means that Shard Gods can have competing titles and areas of concern. When describing a Shard God, it's more accurate to call them "a God of" rather than "the God of" in this respect, i.e., in the present, there are currently three Shard Gods of Fire and four of Battle in various places of the world. Some believe that Shard Gods are not Gods at all, but this opinion is considered heretical and blasphemous; after all, Shard Gods are common enough that almost all mortals worship them in some form or another.

However, this thought exercise may have some basis in truth; the worship of followers and belief does not create nor ascend a Shard God, and many do not require temples or priests. Though some Shard Gods insist worship is necessary for their survival, they are merely vain and capricious beings who enjoy devotion. Praying and worshiping a deity is simply a convenient way for Ember's mortals to connect with the gods who are aligned with an aspect they devote themselves to. Some Shard Gods reject this premise entirely and do not even play the game, instead insisting that they are just powerful beings and no gods at all, but this a mysterious theological argument among scholars as Shard Gods can answer prayers and grant power to their followers, indirectly in small amount or in large amount to mortals they treasure. In addition, they possess several strange abilities and powers that suggest they are not merely powerful immortals.

A Shard God's power is typically a set amount dictated by the age of the Heart Crystal they ascended with, and they are imbued with vast amounts of what many refer to as Lifeforce that originates from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. It does not increase with age after ascension nor from the belief of their followers. However, Shard Gods can grant this power and blessings to their followers. While this has an extremely minor effect on their total power, and it only diminishes them by a small amount, with enough followers, a Shard God's power can noticeably reduce. However, this is just borrowed power, and if the Shard God chooses or upon their follower's death the Shard God receives this power in return.

Every Shard God can imbue followers with power; the most common are priests, clerics, paladins, and ordinary mortals who pray to them. But a Shard God is not merely a distant figure to be worshipped, and making personal connections is fully possible. Meeting and serving a Shard God directly has several benefits, and in rarer cases, it's likely that a mortal will be imbued with greater power and will make a pact with their chosen deity.

Mortality & Destruction

Shard Gods are immortal and do not age but they are not invulnerable and can be killed. This is extremely difficult not only because of the pure power that would be required but Shard Gods are imbued with Lifeforce and this gives them remarkable abilities to resist damage and regenerate. If a Shard God is killed, their Lifeforce will be reabsorbed back into the Heart of Ember.

Shards Gods are imbued with Lifeforce and fundamentally oppose Abyssal Energy. They cannot be corrupted in the same way that mortals can, though in rare cases, they can be "twisted." This is still so rare that only one case is known, and the information should not be shared.
Shard Gods.scoverview: Shard Gods of Ember are among the most recognized, celebrated, and powerful entities that walk the surface World of Ember. In almost all cases, they are ascendant mortals imbued with the remarkable power of Lifeforce after discovering and touching a Heart Crystal. Some Shard Gods are ancient, or even primordial in age, while others are far younger and have arisen recently. All are distinct personalities with complex goals, motivations, and flaws, and at a very basic level, they are just as prone to mistakes as the mortals that venerate them. Shard Gods embody mortal concepts (War, Love, Trade)

Fenra Irdragon.name: Fenra Irdragon
Fenra Irdragon.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Fenra Irdragon.scoverview: Fenra Irdragon is known as the One Heroic Spirit, they were once the High King of the proto Kelmezian culture and died thousands of years ago. However legends and stories are told of them appearing in times of need to defend mortal ancestries against the darkness.

Wild Gods.name: Wild Gods
Wild Gods.text:
Lore Summary

  • Origin: Slowly created through centuries of soaking in Lifeforce from the Heart of Ember.

  • Natural Aspects: They are geographically anchored in their own domains. They rarely, if ever, leave their place of power.

  • Worship: They do not hear distant prayers. To gain their power, you must stand in their presence and receive a literal fragment of their essence.

  • Soul Anchors: They can safeguard their followers' souls, weaving them into the land as Nature Spirits.

  • Destruction: They can be killed, but if their domain is destroyed, they don't necessarily die; they are severed from the Wildsong, which results in violent, unpredictable insanity.

The Wild Gods are the ancient, mysterious stewards of the natural order in Ember, born from the world itself rather than through ascension or the birth of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.JUwFAaelI86yiscL]{the Cosmos}. They are powered by the pure Lifeforce that flows from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} into the soil, water, and air. Over centuries, or even millennia, a creature that remains in a place where Lifeforce flows particularly strongly will slowly absorb this creational energy. Typically, mortal ancestries are not long-lived enough to complete this process; therefore, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Tl4gvmUGThkZdrUd]{Elementals}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans}, and other exceptionally long-lived creatures are the most common beings to reach this state.

Once this infusion reaches a tipping point, the being connects with and also shapes the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.1jb9zDsRFMXo7Je0]{Wildsong}, a broad, cosmos-spanning field of energy that forms the natural world and binds all living things within the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} together. Through the Wildsong, they oversee the turning of the seasons, the adaptation of wildlife, and the protection of their domains from destruction. Because their power is drawn directly from the natural flow of Lifeforce within a given region, they are inextricably linked to the areas they protect and rarely leave their specific places of power.

Divine Power

The Wild Gods do not grant power through prayers or remote divine guidance. Unlike the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods} or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods}, who may hear a distant plea, the Wild Gods are so deeply woven into the Wildsong that the individual voices of mortals are often lost. Instead, their patronage is an intimate, physical act. To empower a follower, a Wild God must ritually bestow a fragment of their own Lifeforce in person. This sacrifice of essence creates a direct, tangible link between the deity and the mortal, a spark of the Wild God and the Wildsong that the follower carries within them.

As the living embodiments of nature, Wild Gods are both the creators and the subjects of the wild spaces they inhabit. They do not merely rule the forests, jungles, swamps, and rivers; they are the spiritual manifestation of those ecosystems. While most represent the vibrancy of growth and the turning of seasons, their influence can occasionally manifest through the darker, harsher aspects of the natural order, such as decay, the necessity of hunger, or the brutality of survival. Interestingly, Wild Gods can manifest in the same areas, overlapping and co-existing, but each typically represents a different aspect of nature.

Soul Cycle Connection

Wild Gods interact with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} in much the same way that an Elder God can. They can anchor mortal souls within their own wild domains, preventing their followers from being drawn to the Spiritlands. When a mortal dies as a servant of a Wild God, the divine essence and the imbued Lifeforce they carried return directly to the Wild God. The Wild God then anchors their followers’ souls to the local ecosystem, weaving the spirit into the very fabric of the land.

These anchored souls do not become ghosts; instead, they become Nature Spirits. In this state, manifesting as sentient flora, animals with ancient wisdom, or protective whispers in the wind that guide travelers through the wilds. While all souls eventually return to the Heart of Ember, for a Nature Spirit, this process is slowed to a primordial crawl, often taking hundreds, if not thousands, of years.

Mortality & Destruction

Wild Gods possess physical forms, ancient bodies of flesh, stone, or elemental energy, and can be slain. While a Wild God does not instantly perish if their domain is destroyed, the loss of their land is a fate often considered worse than death. A Wild God whose domain has been razed or corrupted remains physically as it was, but it loses the ability to draw new Lifeforce from around it. This can be catastrophic, and the Wild God almost inevitably falls into a state of violent insanity.
Wild Gods.scoverview: The Wild Gods are ancient shapers of Lifeforce, creating the natural world and maintaining the vast, complex ecosystems through their combined force, known as Wildsong. They are the keepers of the natural world and help keep the cosmos in balance, often coming into conflict with the ambitions of the Shard Gods. Wild Gods embody natural concepts (Growth, Seasons, Weather)

The Deities.name: The Deities
The Deities.text:
Lore Summary

  1. Four Types of Deity: Gods in Ember fall under four types; some are somewhere in between.

  2. Alien Entities: Outer Gods are real and powerful, but rarely, if ever, worshipped directly.

  3. Static Power: Gods have their own power; they are not empowered via worship or prayers.

  4. Political Worship: Worship is a social and political tool used to gain favor, not a necessity for the divine.

  5. Independence: Forgotten or independent deities are still incredibly dangerous, even without followers.

The deities of Ember do not rely on mortal faith or worship to sustain themselves or fuel their abilities. Their power is not a resource tied to prayers; instead, the amount of power they hold is fixed. For a Shard God, their power is determined at the moment of ascension by the purity and size of the Heart Crystal they touched. For an Elder God, their power is an immutable consequence of their role in the creation of the Cosmos.

The presence of hundreds of Shard Gods walking the surface world means that cultures venerate and constantly worship varied pantheons composed of many deity types, from Elder Gods to Wild Gods and Shard Gods, but few make any distinctions between them, and for most mortals, gods are gods. Lastly, many mortals build grand temples and offer sacrifices to appease a deity's temper or seek their favor, but no amount of collective belief can increase a god’s power.

Quick Reference: Four Deity Types

Within the Ember setting itself, there are four types of deities, all of which are subtly different from one another in various ways. Often, a deity's true categorization may not be clear or immediately apparent, even when placed in categories within the Setting Compendium itself, as the Setting Compendium is not an entirely true and accurate source of knowledge.

Outer Gods

These entities originate beyond the cosmos itself. Their powers are utterly alien and incomprehensible, often manifesting as paradoxes, impossible geometries, the unraveling of minds and the creators of monsters. They are the ultimate existential threat, and their followers often seek power through forbidden knowledge that drives them mad. Outer Gods embody destructive concepts (Oblivion, Annihilation, Terror)

Elder Gods

The Elder Gods are the primordial architects of the Cosmos, born during Creation and inextricably linked to the Heart of Ember. They maintain the fundamental reality of the Cosmos, and while their power is vast, they are often distracted by cosmological issues rather than daily mortal concerns. Elder Gods embody fundamental concepts (Space, Souls, Time)

Wild Gods

The Wild Gods are ancient shapers of Lifeforce, creating the natural world and maintaining the vast, complex ecosystems through their combined force, known as Wildsong. They are the keepers of the natural world and help keep the cosmos in balance, often coming into conflict with the ambitions of the Shard Gods. Wild Gods embody natural concepts (Growth, Seasons, Weather)

Shard Gods

Shard Gods are mortal ascendants, having communed with a Heart Crystal to ascend. Some Shard Gods are ancient, while others are far younger and have arisen recently. All are distinct personalities with complex goals, motivations, and flaws. Shard Gods embody mortal concepts (War, Love, Trade)
The Deities.scoverview: The Cosmos of Ember is not governed by distant, unreachable gods. Instead, it is a world where the divine is tangible, walking among mortals and influencing the flow of history and events through direct intervention. Every deity within the Ember Cosmos possesses a physical body; ruling over sprawling kingdoms, wandering the wilds as nomads, or secluding themselves in hidden enclaves. Divinity in this setting falls into four distinct categories: horrific entities from beyond known as Outer Gods, the primordial Elder Gods, strange nature-based Wild Gods, and the numerous, ascended Shard Gods who were once mortals.

Verador.scoverview: Verador is an ancient Shard God of chaotic charm and is well known for being unpredictable and spontaneous.
Verador.sgamemaster: • Verador, The Laughing Sky, is the Shard God of chaos, cunning, and freedom.

The Silent Pack.name: The Silent Pack
The Silent Pack.text:
Under Construction

The Silent Pack.scoverview: Deep within the heart of the Inner Realm of Primordis lies the Shadow Thicket. The primordial location from where the Casia first emerged during creation. It is one of the most dangerous places in the cosmos as not only is it a place of raw, untamed magical energy, but it is also home to a malicious group of Casia called the Silent Pack. Whether the pack is one entity with many different physical bodies is unknown. They appear in the minds of their followers as a collection of red burning eyes glimmering in the shadows, and if you see these eyes in the waking world, there is little point in running as you are likely already dead.

Juriel.name: Juriel
Juriel.text:
Under Construction

Juriel.scoverview: Juriel is a relatively new Tyraphem Lord from the Inner Realm of Luxarum. They claimed their position only a thousand years ago, and since then, they have faced pressure from other, more powerful Lords to defend and maintain their territory. Unlike other Lords, Juriel acts reasonably and possesses keen practical intelligence. He is also renowned for being calm, controlled, and fair, qualities that the vast majority of Tyraphem struggle to embody.

Orvaath.name: Orvaath
Orvaath.text:
Areas of Concern: The Soul, Death, Deception

Typical Followers: Alchemists, Scholars, Outcasts

Domains: Twilight, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6cMQOhdBouTFJlSl]{Sunalins}

Symbol: A strange ancient machine or contraption, wreathed in fire.

Edict of Orvaath

Fear death not for yourself, but for the promises left undone.
Orvaath.scoverview: Orvaath is a god born of grief and defiance, a being who could not accept the quiet ending of life. Once mortal, they are said to have reached beyond what any soul should touch, seeking to preserve life forever and end the tyranny of death. Now Orvaath is said to brood in a distant cavern somewhere on the continent of Kessia, plotting to resurrect old heroes and the long dead. To the Nalvani, he is both redeemer and curse, the Life Tyrant whose mercy consumes. Worship of him persists in secret, carried by those who reject the Soul Cycle and yearn for permanence in flesh. Elsewhere, his name is spoken only in fear.

Remira.name: Remira
Remira.text:
Areas of Concern: Consent, Autonomy, Passion

Typical Followers: Artists and Writers, Prisoners, Pleasure Workers

Domains: Life, Other

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ The Nineteen}

Symbol: Two fingers hooked together.

Edict of Remira

Choose your pleasure.
Remira.scoverview: Appearing to her followers as an alluring Kiska with pink and white fur, Remira is a shard god whose spheres of influence revolve around the romantic world. Consent, autonomy, and passion are the concepts she is most concerned with, and she is Ember's most important advocate for the pursuit of ethical pleasure.

Themis.name: Themis
Themis.text:
Areas of Concern: Justice, Vengeance, Battle

Typical Followers: Champions, Warriors, Scouts

Domains: Twilight, Light

Pantheons: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor}

Symbol: Radiant wings encompassed by swirling darkness.

Edict of Themis

Mercy without judgment is weakness; judgment without mercy is corruption.

Themis is an ancient deity, a close friend of the Shard God Volún and the husband of the goddess Eirun, and has two children, Varros and Gildaré, both of whom are also Shard Gods. He is thought to be older than the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wMAfwOrjwk0izpxC]{Auris Bor} pantheon, and many believe he was once a Varak. He embodies the concept of impartial fairness and necessary retribution. Unlike deities who watch from afar, Themis operates on a deterministic philosophy: once he perceives an imbalance or an injustice against the vulnerable, his intervention is swift and absolute. Despite his ancient origins, Themis was also said to have a close bond with the deity @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.BP2QN2S6fFOfwp3U]{Finor}, becoming enraged by his death.

During the Forsaken War, following the death of Finor, Themis served as a commander of the forces of the Aedir and the Luxarum, often leading his troops on the front lines. It was during the war that he was grievously wounded, and many believe this was when the darker side of his personality began to show as he became overwhelmed by grief and rage, unable to fight, protect, and save the mortals and other deities around him. This trauma shifted his divinity toward a self-sacrificial obsession with mortal preservation.

In the wake of the Shattering, Themis became a shield for isolated pockets of survivors, especially the young Kivahr ancestry who eventually founded the cultures of the Bejak and the Wardcall. To both, Themis is a very active part of their cultures, a being that shows little interest in slow ceremonies, adoration, or in watching things unfold; he often clashes with other members of the Auris Bor, as he views their non-interventionalist stance as a betrayal of their duty. He was blind sided by the formation of the Trine of Wards among the Wardcall, and despite many still worshipping him in secret, Themis does not openly travel in his deific form. It's not entirely clear why he would do this either. It's thought that every member of the Ironfrost Templars still carries his symbol, and he aids them on many occasions against the Vartic. He is also responsible for bringing Humans across the Shana Mountains and integrating them among the Bejak and the Wardcall.

Appearance

Themis manifests as a towering, winged human figure clad in slate-gray plate armor, with a tall helm and a full-face guard that seems to absorb the light around it. His six radiant, feathered wings flicker in the light and shadows that bleed from his hands and fingertips. He is rarely seen without his twin relics: The Blade Inumbrate, a greatsword that hums with a cold light, and The Mourning Star, a spear that leaves trails of starlight in its wake. His voice is low and controlled, speaking with the weary, grounded cadence of a veteran commander

Influence and Followers

Themis has many followers in the northern parts of Atercia, especially among the Bejak and the Wardcall. He is the patron of the Ironfrost Templars, an order of warriors who see themselves not just as his servants but as his children, even though officially Themis has no place among the Wardcall because of the influence of the Trine of Wards. Themis has few priests or clerics, as he prefers soldiers and warriors who take direct action. Those who do follow him are often fanatical in their belief in his divine will. Worship of Themis involves the Ritual of the Names, where warriors recite the names of their fallen comrades to him, believing that he carries their memories within his own heavy heart.

Using Themis as a Deity

Choosing Themis as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or Warlock Patron appeals to those who feel a profound, heavy sense of duty toward the defenseless. A pact or oath with Themis is not a pursuit of glory, but an acceptance of a burden; his followers are expected to be an impenetrable shield, absorbing the world’s darkness so that others may live in the light. This path often leads to a life of extreme self-sacrifice, as Themis drives his followers to stand their ground in even the most hopeless sieges. Interacting with Themis is humbling, as he speaks as a weary commander who knows the name of every soldier under his care. This fosters an intense, familial loyalty among his followers, who view themselves as his sons and daughters, willing to die alongside him.

Relationships

His closest connection is with his wife Eirun, as she remains his closest confidant, though his obsessive duty to the mortals often keeps him estranged from her side. She, on the other hand, adores and understands his nature and supports him as much as she can.
Themis.scoverview: Hailing from the ancient northern pantheon of Auris Bor, Themis is a Shard God of justice and balance. His wings shimmer with radiance interlaced with darkness, and his very presence can inspire awe or fear in equal measure. Themis wields justice like a weapon, rewarding virtue and punishing those he deems have failed, yet even his most disciplined judgment can be swayed by vengeance or whim. Themis often leads mortals in the fight against encroaching monsters, often on the front lines against trolls, striking with precision and inspiring courage.

Avilla.name: Avilla
Avilla.text:
• Keywords: Lost, Untamed, Ordani

  • Areas of Concern: Anti-Magic, Protection, Healing

  • Sacred Weapon: Sling

  • Other Names: The Spellbreaker

  • Pantheons: None

Avilla is a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God}, who has no presence in the present-day age of the world, disappearing from all records roughly six hundred years ago. Her story is told by many in Ordain as the story of @UUID[JournalEntry.SXu41X2NifZaSVqh.JournalEntryPage.wBfEdFXGf2pE20MF]{The Spellbreaker.}

Appearance

Avilla is currently a lost deity and has no known present-day appearance. Before she left Ordain, however, she was said to be unremarkable in almost every aspect. She had unkempt, loose, dark brown hair and a slightly slumped figure, preferring to wear simple Cindaric Sage robes. On her way out of Ordain, Avilla was said to carry an ethereal staff, carved from ancient wood but somehow removed from the physical world. At its tip rested a void of nothingness that shone softly with pale blue and orange light.

Influence and Followers

No one in Ordain actively worships Avilla as a deity, and she has no shrines or temples, but the Ordani venerate and remember her in stories and tales as part of their history. In some regards, she is a cautionary tale, and the Ordani as a people have a lingering apathy towards magic as a result. They do not fear or distrust magic users in any way, but they tend to use magic in small ways and as part of daily life rather than studying elemental or destructive paths as a result.

Strangely, Avilla has a large following among the lands of the Cascilian Republic. Although she has no clerics or priests, many view her in a much more positive light, using her story as further justification for their anti-magic stance.

Using Avilla as a deity for a Cleric, Paladin, or general devotion is not possible. The most likely reason is that Avilla is long dead, or perhaps she still lives but refuses to recognize any true followers.
Avilla.scoverview: Avilla the Spellbreaker was the first Ordani Shard God who ultimately rejected her divine power and wandered into the wilds of the world, only a few hundred or so years after the founding of Ordain. She saved the city from the Cabal, a sect of mages from Atou, in a climactic battle in the waters of the Bay of Ordain, just outside the city. Today, she is remembered with a mix of gratitude and fear by the Ordani people.

Soul of Fashion.name: Soul of Fashion
Soul of Fashion.text:
• Keywords: Clothing, Styles, Secrets

  • Areas of Concern: Clothing, Fashion, Ordain

  • Sacred Weapon: Rapier

  • Other Names: Prisma

  • Pantheons: None

Little is understood about the "Soul of Fashion." The people of Ordain often refer to this entity similarly to how one might speak of a guiding concept or principle, but they do not actively worship it. Instead, the term is frequently used to describe the Ordani's unique sense of style and their pursuit of clothing trends.

A few fervent believers assert that its influence is a real force, felt throughout the city, where dressing in beautiful garments becomes an expression of the soul itself. The vast majority in Ordain believe is is a collective cultural expression of thier culture. Regardless of whether the Soul of Fashion is a genuine force, it undeniably plays a crucial role in shaping the identity of Ordain, as its people prioritize fashion and stylistic expression in their clothing above many other concerns.

Appearance

No appearance is associated with the "Soul of Fashion".

Influence and Followers

Most Ordani, and even those outside the city, have heard of the "Soul of Fashion," and all Ordani have some connection to it in some way. Though it is not considered a person or entity, it is part of daily life. Many speak of the Soul as part of themselves or others, especially when they are particularly active in social fashion scenes.

The Soul of Fashion cannot be worshipped as a deity by a Cleric, Paladin, or for general devotion; it is not considered a deity.
Soul of Fashion.scoverview: The Soul of Fashion is an implied force of creativity within the great city of Ordain. The Ordani people typically evoke the term to describe a part of themselves or others who exhibit particularly strong creative or fashionable characteristics. Very few worship it like a deity, and instead, it is considered a part of the culture of the Ordani itself.
Soul of Fashion.sgamemaster:
In truth, the "Soul of Fashion" is a real person, Mistress Caberi, a seamstress who resides in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.0V2KtTURXT8WaxfX]{Gossamer} district of Ordain. She was once a devout member of the Cindaric Sages and rose to the position of Holy Speaker over four hundred years ago. However, after she communed with a Shard Crystal within the Shard Caverns, she decided to fake her own death and retire, hiding her newfound divine powers. Very few in Ordain know of her true nature, but she is a subtle yet driving force behind the scenes for the Ordani people.

Mistress Caberi is a warm, friendly seamstress who is often surrounded by bolts of luxurious cloth and textiles, vibrant colors of every hue, and a large following of adoring fans. Her long, silvery hair flows like shimmering threads of yarn, pinned and styled in mesmerizing patterns. Her hair is often adorned with delicate silver and golden jewelry entwined with precious gems. Her eyes, a deep shade of emerald green, sparkle and glitter under moonlight. She never seems to wear the same outfit or article of clothing, but loves to wear rich fabrics that seem to change hue as she moves, much like the colors of a delicate rainbow. These fabrics are meticulously tailored, showcasing her seamstress skills, with intricate embroidery woven throughout.

She welcomes all who enter her quaint shop with a radiant smile, where the aroma of fresh clean fabric mingles with soft laughter and cheerful conversations about the latest trends in Ordain. With her nimble fingers, she weaves magical threads of various hues, crafting exquisite and unique pieces of clothing for the city's most passionate fashionistas.

Although Caberi was once one of the Holy Speakers of the Cindaric Speakers who ascended nearly four hundred years ago, she is remarkably secretive about her past and divinity. She maintains near-perfect control over her powers and shows little interest in threats to the city, but she does enjoy getting involved in politics. In fact, she is currently serving as one of the members of the Ordinate in Ordain. Although a few question her long-lived nature, and there are several local legends and stories about her, no one assumes she is a deity. In her own quiet way, Mistress Caberi is an unseen champion, uplifting those around her through creative expression.

Adair.name: Adair
Adair.text:
Areas of Concern: Change & Chaos; Logic & Law

Typical Followers: Bureaucrats, Lawyers, Councilors

Domains: Twilight, Other

Pantheons: None

Symbol: A two-faced mask

Edict of Adair

Hold two truths close and let neither win.
Adair.scoverview: Known among mortals as a capricious and two-faced Shard God, who very recently seemed to ascend, Adair embodies the duality of thought and emotion, reason and logic in conflict with chaos, change, and the disruption of order itself. Many come to them seeking counsel, hoping to find clarity, yet few leave without confronting their own contradictions. Adair has few places of worship, but those that do follow them often gather around fires or quiet rooms, endlessly discussing the merits of one topic only to turn around and argue the opposite in later meetings.

Anachraenum.name: Anachraenum
Anachraenum.text:
Headquartered in Ordain, the Anachraenum is a relatively young organization compared to some of the city's other groups. For the most part, they see Ember as a chaotic but wondrous world where "treasure" means much more than material wealth. The carefully curated discoveries of the Anachraenum are numerous, and for nearly two hundred years, this storied group has successfully explored some of Ember's most perilous landscapes in search of legendary ruins from bygone ages. The vaults of the Anachraenum's All-Fable Keep and its archives are filled with all manner of arcane relics, artifacts of long-dead cultures, and curious unearthed oddities.

  • Enterprising Excavations: Archaeology is perhaps what the Anachraenum is best known for, and the organization's unique approach to nontraditional dungeon diving stems from their tendency to search extensively for the strangest and most fascinating historical oddities with an almost complete disregard for rules or oversight.

  • Archive Operations: The Anachraenum maintains the extensive Amaranthine Archives within the All-Fable Keep, a sprawling museum of relics, artifacts, and curated displays that is available for viewing year-round. Admission is offered at the cost of a small donation thanks to the generous sponsorship of wealthy elite patrons, typically members of the various Trading Houses.

  • Political Distance: Both the leaders and members of the Anachraenum stay as far away from political matters in the city as possible. While All-Fable Keep is their home and headquarters, they tend to think of themselves as a more global organization and act independently in many aspects of their work.However, they do sometimes work with the Trading Houses, particularly House Cevher.

  • Wayfinders: Most members abide by the same tenet: that cultural and intellectual enlightenment await those with enough bravery and wits to survive the most devious dungeons of Ember's ancient civilizations. As such, while the focus of the Anachraenum is officially scholarly, a great many adventuring types are drawn to join for the fame, glory, and prospect of uncovering treasure. These types are typically distinguished by the term "Wayfinders".

Operations

Members of the Anachraenum rarely work alone and tend to form groups and parties within the guild itself to pursue their own interests, whether it’s archaeology, anthropology, or treasure hunting. These teams often conduct fieldwork in some of the most dangerous areas in the world, often facing logistical challenges, treacherous terrain, deadly monsters, creatures, and ancient traps. It is not uncommon for communication with groups in the field to be lost for many months, and some disappear entirely, presumed killed in action. Despite the danger and the drive to explore ancient sites in search of relics and artifacts, most Anachraenum members maintain a strong desire to preserve whatever artifacts they uncover, carefully documenting them.

Once back at the All-Fable Keep, the work continues as members categorize and analyze their discoveries. This involves meticulous cataloging within the Amaranthine Archives, where each artifact is studied for its historical, cultural, and magical properties. Some members spend their days restoring damaged relics or conducting research to uncover the history and events behind them.

The guild traditionally allows anyone to join, though membership is earned through years of dedication and proof of skill. Some members devote their lives to scholarly pursuits within the safety of the All-Fable Keep, studying ancient cultures and forgotten lore, while others take to the field, braving ruins, dungeons, and untamed lands in search of relics.

Trainee

Entry-level members, often scholars or explorers in training. They assist senior members in cataloging, restoration, and research while learning the fundamentals of safe adventuring.

Scholar

Academically trained members who conduct research, translation, and theoretical study within the All-Fable Keep. Some begin assisting expeditions in limited support roles.

Adventurer

Trusted Adventurers and explorers who venture into ruins, retrieve relics, and conduct initial documentation. Skilled in survival, excavation, and magical containment.

Wayfinder

Veteran adventurers and expedition guides who specialize in navigation, logistics, and survival in the most dangerous environments.

Curator

Senior scholars and expedition leaders who manage research wings Archives. They review and verify all recovered materials and determine which relics are safe to study or display.

Loremaster

The overseer of the Amaranthine Archives, responsible for the preservation, classification, and academic integrity of all recorded knowledge and artifacts. Serves as the intellectual heart of the Anachraenum.

Guildmaster

The head of the Anachraenum, who governs both the academic and exploratory branches. The Guildmaster ensures that the guild’s work stays true to its purpose of research and preservation.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.FYprIclhoDOI8FI4]{Arcos Sarinland} (NG, Ordani Keth, he/him)

Arcos Sarinland was once a promising young ranger who joined the Anachraenum forty years ago and became a close friend of Darion Bastilla. He was widely celebrated for his participation in the Battle of the Throat, where a combined fleet led by Darion destroyed the Blood Barons' assembling ships in Golden Bay; however, he retired from active adventuring not long after. For thirty years, he taught and guided new members in Ordain, always maintaining a friendly yet troubled demeanor. Recently thrust into the guild's leadership after Fernis Ossa declined the nomination, he faces a number of increasing challenges as Ordain slips further into unrest.

@UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} (LG, Ordani Ashka, she/her)

Fernis Ossa is one of the most well-known and admired Anachraenum members living in Ordain. She led a group of adventurers called the Skywarders many years ago before effectively becoming the envoy and deputy to the previous guildmaster, Veron Longspear. She spent many years among the people of Ordain, and her adventurous spirit is matched only by her dedication to her friends and comrades. Fernis often organizes gatherings and events in Ordain and travels to many nearby friendly cities like Luen, Wick, and the Lumek city of Hearth. She has a genuine interest in the stories and lives of the people she meets.

@UUID[Actor.GA8VFWysoIYfNWCL]{Adelyne Goss} (NG, Waerd Human, she/her)

Loremistress Adelyne Goss is a sarcastic and sharp character, and despite her extensive physical injuries sustained after battling a dragon deep in the Duskflare Jungles many years ago, she remains an intensely insightful and productive scholar and librarian. She is also extremely proud of her Waerd heritage and wears a combination of traditional Waerd clothing interwoven with ancient Sedyri trinkets.

@UUID[Actor.vNN1EXVZkMWPcP8r]{Haruspex} (LG, Ordani Signborn, they/them)

One of the most famed Wayfinders of the Anachraenum currently operating in the Arctus Plateau is the ranger known as Haruspex, a ruthless solo adventurer whose unparalleled scouting skills and prowess with a longbow have earned them the reputation as one of Ember’s most successful treasure hunters.
Anachraenum.scoverview: The Anachraenum - also referred to as the Lore Hunters by its members and by common folk - is an organization of archaeologists, explorers, treasure seekers, and adventurers, whose primary goals include the location, preservation, and curation of Ember's most significant historical artifacts. Much like the scope of their operations, the shared knowledge and experience among its members is extensive, and they are granted a certain autonomy to pursue their individual goals.
Anachraenum.sgamemaster:
The Anachraenum's relatively short history stretches back nearly three hundred years, where it began as a loose association of five adventurers from diverse backgrounds and allegiances. This motley group of scholarly explorers and adventurers, known as the Five Founders, was united in their mission to uncover the dragon Harathraxes and its fabled lair. Legends spoke of a secret cavern deep beneath the Arctus Plateau, but Harathraxes themselves hadn't been seen since the settlement of the region over a thousand years prior.

While the exact nature of their discovery remains a mystery, the Founders seemingly discovered what they sought and found a treasure hoard large enough to fund the construction of All-Fable Keep in Ordain and found the Anachraenum. For many years afterward the Five Founders led the Anachraenum as part of a small unified group but by either disagreement or innate wanderlust, four of the founders left Ordain to pursue their own agendas, only Rexan Krist remained and led the Anachraenum until his death in [[/date AS2282]]

The Anachraenum has remained incredibly stable and resistant to outside influences for most of its history, but after the death of Veron Longspear, it was thrown into chaos. While everything seems normal on the surface and to outsiders, many parties within the guild are increasingly distrustful of one another, and the spirit of collaboration among its members has begun to fade.

Timeline

[[/date AS2522]]

The venerable Guildmaster of the Anachraenum, Veron Longspear, dies unexpectedly while visiting a research site in the Ruinous Crags. The cause of his death remains mysterious, with rumors and theories circulating among the Anachraenum members. His successor, Arcos Sarinland, is untested and only gains the title of Guildmaster after Fernis Ossa declines the responsibility.

[[/date AS2518]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} hosts the first Expedition Challenge, an intense competition where several young adventuring teams are pitted against one another in various challenges across the city of Ordain and the Arctus Plateau. @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} becomes a well-known celebrity in the city after winning with her team, and the following year, she explores an ancient fallen Skyhold of the Vaznor in the distant Shana Mountains to the north.

[[/date AS2245]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} organization begins as a loose affiliation of five adventurers and scholarly explorers – known as the Five Founders, unite in a mission to uncover the fabled lair of the carnal dragon Harathraxes that claimed a section of the Pathways under the Arctus Plateau. After this point, the group decided to dedicate their efforts to understanding the world of Ember's ancient history.

Burnished Hand.name: Burnished Hand
Burnished Hand.text:
The Burnished Hand is a military order of exceptional warriors clad in suits of thick bronze armor and furs who reside on the Rusted Fortress of Bura Island. The organization started out as a small group of Vrjnhar from the Oaken culture, but for the last several hundred years the order has consisted mostly of Ordani and Arcturian people (with a smaller number of other ancestries from across the world). The fortress itself was once the location of the largest concentration of Oaken within the Arctus Plateau, but the Vrjnhar who built it left many years ago; meanwhile, the trainees and other members who remained coalesced into a more official organization and eventually adopted their famed moniker.

For a long time, the Burnished Hand was the only organized military group in the region, and were known as a stalwart organization of monster hunters and justiciars when the Plateau was a much wilder and more primal place. Members of the order are not commonly seen inside the city limits of Ordain, but can often rather be found serving the needs of the Sages as protectors in more dangerous areas of the Plateau (and beyond).

  • Oaken Roots: With deep cultural ties to the Oaken — who helped with the building and protection of Ordain during its early years — the Rusted Fortress on Bura Island was built to protect the bay and to serve as a fortified home for scores of Oaken warriors. Oaken Vrjnhar are extremely long-lived, however, they have a deep sense of restlessness and urge to explore dangerous places; so as the Arctus Plateau calmed, most of these warriors departed, leaving the fortress in the hands of Ember's younger Ancestries.

  • Cindaric Guardians: Since the Cindaric Sages are not a militarized group, Oaken Warriors have historically protected and guarded the Sages on longer journeys, and a small elite group was often assigned to the Holy Speaker for protection. This close bond was aided by the connection many Oaken feel to the Cindaric belief system, and their legacy endures to this day via the Burnished Hand.

  • Ritualistic Techniques: The Burnished Hand are a close-knit organization trained in ancient Oaken techniques, martial styles that involve ritualistic pre-combat preparations capable of enhancing their bodies and minds. Such focus gives these warriors the ability to briefly shrug off their wounds, increase their strength, or banish their fears and doubts.

Operations

The Burnished Hand is helmed by the organization's Commander, the honorable warrior Steros Kraver, who presides over the order with a stern sense of rule and a keen realization of the organization's potential and limitations. A retinue of six Lieutenant Commanders serve beneath Steros, along with a battalion of 500 soldiers (including at least 100 initiates). These adherents are all learned in the ways of the Cindaric Sages, who they have solemnly sworn to protect.

While the Arctus Plateau has seen brief periods of unrest (such as the Mourning War), for the past several hundred years the organization diminished in prevalence, with most of the Rusted Fortress on Bura Island lying empty and abandoned. With the recent increase in threats, many are drawn to the fortress for a chance to fight back, drive away emerging monsters, and help return the region to its once peaceful state. As such they have become a more common sight in Ordain.

Initiate

New recruits who train rigorously in combat, discipline, and the teachings of the Oaken and the Cindaric Sages. Many serve as attendants or apprentices under more seasoned members.

Axebearer

Fully sworn members who have completed their initiation. They serve as the rank-and-file defenders of the order, guarding the faithful and the Rusted Fortress alike.

Carver

Keepers of the Rusted Fortress’s armories and traditions. They oversee the crafting of sacred weapons and train the younger ranks in both combat and the meditations of Ember.

Rust Warden

Senior officers responsible for maintaining the armories, relics, and martial traditions of the Burnished Hand. They are scholars of warfare and teachers of the next generation.

Lieutenant

One of six appointed leaders beneath the Commander, each responsible for overseeing a wing of the order’s operations, from recruitment to defense.

Commander

The leader the Burnished Hand. Currently held by Steros Kraver, a steadfast and disciplined warrior devoted to preserving the order’s legacy and ensuring its resurgence.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver}

Steros is the stalwart Commander of the Burnished Hand. He is also a loyal adherent to the edicts of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.GlbJezRw2ecnVIsx]{Cindarin Temple} in Ordain, where the Holy Speaker presides over the Cindaric Sages and their closest allies. Steros is a skilled warrior and a charismatic leader, and is regarded by many to be one of the most competent military leaders in Arcturian history.

@UUID[Actor.yLwrlq7nzkFYkRYc]{Aldath}

This ancient Vrjnhar warrior was a member of the Burnished Hand long ago, and has only recently returned to Ordain to investigate the once-proud organization. He resides in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.isjEWrS8Qv8gq8A2]{Nurk's Hollow} near Bura Island, alongside a group of other exiled members he's gathered together for his cause. Aldath is a legendary warrior who is losing his edge to old age.
Burnished Hand.scoverview: This fierce military order was born out of an ancient alliance of Vrjnhar warriors and the first Ordani who settled Ordain. The Burnished Hand now serves as the sworn protector of Ordain's venerated Cindaric Sages, but still manage to keep to themselves — rarely leaving the confines of the Rusted Fortress on Bura Island, which the organization calls home. With a new leader and a renewed determination to honor the legacy of their founders, the Burnished Hand has recently intensified its recruitment efforts and has begun to appear more frequently within the city once again.
Burnished Hand.sgamemaster:
Even before the founding of Ordain the Oaken had made brief contact with the Arcturians in small numbers, landing upon the shores of the Arctus Plateau to aid them in battles against monsters that roamed the region. After the arrival of the refugees and the founding of the city, however, the Oaken arrived in greater numbers to help build the city and protect the vulnerable. Constructing a Fortress on Bura Island, the Oaken were celebrated and renowned for their "selfless" aid (In reality, Oaken also loved a good challenge). Over time, the Oaken Vrjnhar began to leave the region as the monsters were slain and peace descended. With many of the Oaken leaving the area, the Burnished Hand is now made up of younger ancestries, such as Humans, Keth, Kavir, etc. They now continue as a more official organization with their name coming from the bronze coloration of the Fortress.

Recently, the Burnished Hand has experienced a resurgence and is now led by a new Commander, @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver}. Unfortunately, the dragon @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss} is pulling the strings behind the scenes, and the organization is becoming firmly under his control. Over the course of the questlines and story, much of the Burnished Hand is corrupted and turned into Death Knights by @UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan} or are killed during the course of the Chapter 4 questline Horror Rising.

Timeline

[[/date AS2213]]

As threats to the city of Ordain diminish and the area becomes increasingly peaceful, many of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.0YvoRkcs1BxtRiQz]{Vrjnhar}, who founded the organization, leave the region. The number of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} members drops to record lows in the subsequent years, and much of the Rusted Fortress on Bura Island outside Ordain is left abandoned.

[[/date AS1734]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} Explorers arrive in Ordain. Although they have made contact with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturians} in the past, they are more impressed and curious about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani} people's resolve to survive. They assist in some of the initial construction and expansion of the fledgling city, and the relationship between the two peoples has been friendly ever since. They also begin construction of a fortified keep several miles from the city at the mouth of the Ordain Bay, as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}, an organization that combats monsters and threats, forms.

Cindaric Sages.name: Cindaric Sages
Cindaric Sages.text:
The Cindaric Sages are one of the three main political powers of Ordain, focused on the spiritual, emotional, and physical well-being of those who live within the city. Cindarics believe that all life in the cosmos has a destined role guided by the unconscious will of the Heart of Ember — the prime mover that resides at the center of the world. Often considered to be the living spirit of Ordain, the Cindaric Sages focus on tending to the city and its people; they view themselves as stewards and caretakers, driven by the Heart of Ember's virtuous and inscrutable intentions.

  • For the Heart. Cindaric Sages believe that all life in the cosmos stems from (and is guided by) the unseen, unconscious will of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. This peaceful organization is often seen as a priestly order, a comparison which has some element of truth to it — but rather than a specific deity, the thoughtful Cindarics are connected to the foundational life force of Ember itself.

  • For the People. While the Sages spend a great deal of time meditating and communing with the Heart of Ember, they also play a pivotal role in the ongoing health and healing of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain} and its people. They provide healing of the body (physical), mind (emotional), and spirit (magical) from the sanctuary of their various Healing Houses located around Ordain and the Arctus Plateau.

  • No Power Without Balance. The Sages maintain a steady but sometimes uneasy political balance with Ordain's Trading Houses and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}. Each of these organizations sends three representatives each to the nine-person @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate}, the bureaucratic decision-making body of Ordain.

  • For Cindaric Eyes Only. A feeling of spiritual unrest has led the Cindaric Sages to become progressively withdrawn from the people and other immediate concerns. And while the Sages have always been protective of their secret lore and traditions, this inclination for privacy has only amplified in recent years, with no signs of stopping. As the Cindarics steadily turn their focus inward, they've begun to lose sight of some plights of the people.

Operations

Traditionally, the Cindarics are led by the head of their order, known as the Holy Speaker, who presides over the Sages from Cindarin Temple in Ordain. A Steward of the Holy Speaker serves as their right hand, with a focus on more practical and administrative duties. Furthermore, a Keeper of the Sages is appointed to supervise all other sages in the organization, along with the resources needed to facilitate their wellbeing. Other Cindarics are assigned tasks according to their abilities and the needs of the people, and younger Sages are afforded training at one of the order's several healing houses. Many operations of the Cindaric Sages are supported by a militaristic organization known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}, whose legacy of monster-hunting and certifiable martial prowess serve the peaceful Cindarics well.

Their weighty responsibilities have led the Cindarics to occasionally overstep their bounds when it comes to deciding what is best for Ordain, especially regarding the privatization of knowledge. In recent years, the Cindaric Sages have become increasingly concerned with ritualistic communion with Ember and its divine core. This concern has eclipsed the order's relationship with Ordain and its people, leading many denizens of the Arctus Plateau to regard the modern Cindarics as distant and withdrawn. And while the Sages remain generally well-meaning and progressive, their historically-esteemed reputation and influence has started to wane. Indeed, many within the city of Ordain consider them ineffective at handling the bigger issues.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} (LG, Ordani Signborn, she/her)

Also known as the "Second Sage," the affable Signborn known as Lilla Arien serves as the "Keeper of Sages" at Cindarin Temple. This high-ranking position is tasked with overseeing the room, board, and wellbeing of all other sages in the order — duties which Lilla carries out with great respect and dedication, through good times and bad.

@UUID[Actor.KQ9uGdZu6zDlM66n]{Jon Vastil} (LG, Ordani Human, he/him)

Jon Vastil is the Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages, and has guided the order from a position of leadership for nearly 75 years. Ancient in age and infirm of health, the once commendable Vastil has faced growing criticism in recent years for a perceived lack of compassion towards the commonfolk and the city's mounting problems. An obsession with humanity's spiritual connection to the Heart of Ember is said to guide this aged leader, who battles a curious illness without cause or cure.

@UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith} (NE, Ordani Human, he/him)

Vinarith is the charismatic Steward of the Holy Speaker, and serves as the proverbial right hand to the highest office of the Cindaric Sages. Now that Jon Vastil has fallen ill, Vinarith has had to shoulder many of the Holy Speaker's responsibilities alongside Keeper Lilla Arien, which the enterprising Steward has accomplished with fervor and success.

@UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}

Mira Wavehorn is the duly designated leader of the enclave of Cindaric Sages as Corpin Sanctuary, situated in the crags of Mial Mountain west of Ordain. An experienced sea captain from the Cascilian Republic, Mira manages to find ways to exercise her key learnings from those years on the high seas throughout her daily life as Corpin Sanctuary's chief steward.
Cindaric Sages.scoverview: This monastic order of benevolent healers and learned ritualists serves as one of the three main political powers of Ordain. The Cindaric Sages see themselves as the spiritual and physical caretakers of the great city — fateful wardens who carry out the preternatural wishes of the Heart of Ember itself and maintain the legacy of the city's founder, Adonia. Those in need of succor can find it at one of the many Cindaric healing houses located throughout Ordain and the Arctus Plateau, places focused on providing sanctuary and divine communion with Ember's supernatural core.
Cindaric Sages.sgamemaster:
The Cindaric Sages began with the first Holy Speaker, the legendary Adonia, who both saved the fledgling Ordani people from annihilation and founded the city of Ordain. While navigating a fleet of refugees across the Reaver Ocean from disparate parts of the world, Adonia was driven towards the eastern shores of the Arctus Plateau after an intense spiritual communion with the Heart of Ember. Some modern Sages believe Adonia saw a vision of the far future during that spiritual concord, and beheld the magnificent urban sprawl that Ordain would one day become.

Following the settlement of Ordain, a select few acolytes chose to follow Adonia's teachings more directly, and this group of adherents eventually became known as the Cindaric Sages, adopting rites, traditions, and rituals becoming of their leader's visions and goals. Near the end of her life, Adonia bore witness to the laying of the first cornerstone of Cindarin Temple — which stands as an eternal testament to her life's work.

Recently, the Cindaric Sages reputation, once held in the highest esteem by the people for their guidance and aid in everyday issues, has begun to wane. A combination of events orchestrated by @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss}, as he enacts his grand plan, has caused the common people of the city to view the Cindaric Sages as distant and unreachable. @UUID[Actor.KQ9uGdZu6zDlM66n]{Jon Vastil}, the current Holy Speaker, is slowly poisoned by Zerranyss, and his failing health means that Zerranyss has mostly free rein in taking over the organization; however, he is still opposed by @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} on some crucial issues. At the end of Chapter 3 of the campaign, Jon Vastil is finally killed by Zerranyss, and his human guise, Vinarith, is elected as the new Holy Speaker of the Sages.

Timeline

[[/date AS2448]]

@UUID[Actor.KQ9uGdZu6zDlM66n]{Jon Vastil} is made the Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages and enjoys a long tenure of peace for many years. His deeply spiritual attitude towards problems, however, begins to slowly erode the faith of the common people in the sage's ability to respond to problems.

[[/date AS2313]]

Darik Melsbow, a priest of the Cindaric Sages, discovers a dangerous truth: the power of the Heart of Ember is gradually weakening over time. He brings his concerns to the Holy Speaker but is ignored and eventually stripped of his rank within the order for trying to spread this knowledge. Bitter and angry, Darik leaves and heads to the town of Talei in the Bloodwoods, north of the city. There, working in secret, he founds the much more active organization of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries}.

[[/date AS2103]]

Holy Speaker @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.FaUiibd3k4gfrzry]{Caberi} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} discovers another @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal} within the Shard Caverns. She keeps her ascension a secret, faking her own death, and moves to the Traders Corner district in Ordain to open a tailoring shop.

[[/date AS1925]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Q0iioq0o2q011r8x]{Avilla} the Spellbreaker ascends as Shard God and is revealed to the city by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}. Her story and fate are told by many across Ordain as a cautionary tale regarding the misuse of magic and power, and her legacy looms over Ordain as Spellbreaker Tower, which stands over its western edge. Her story "@UUID[JournalEntry.SXu41X2NifZaSVqh.JournalEntryPage.wBfEdFXGf2pE20MF]{The Spellbreaker}," is told to all young Ordani, and Avilla herself disappears from all records.

[[/date AS1892]]
