The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} discover the Shard Caverns beneath the city, after this point, the Sages become increasingly rich and powerful, using the crystal shards and gemstones found within to compete with the Trading Houses to some extent, though the Trading Houses still dominate the trade and growing prosperity that the city enjoys.

[[/date AS1716]]

The Yarino refugees fleeing the Kingdom of Reysta from Yarino arrive in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} and begin building the foundations of the city that will one day become @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}. They settle at the mouth of the River Destine, and at first, the people call their settlement Exile's Landing before eventually adopting the name Ordain after several years. Adonia and the Cindaric Sages, as they are now called, begin the construction of Cindarin Temple on one of the tallest plateaus in the area.

[[/date AS1715]]

A small group of mystics and sages forms under the leadership of Adonia. She preaches that the creator of the world lies at its very center and begins calling it the Heart of Ember. She also speaks out against the corrupt leadership of the ruling prince of Yarino.

House Bastilla.name: House Bastilla
House Bastilla.text:
House Bastilla is one of the five great Trading Houses of Ordain, and it commands exclusive control over the city's sea trade. Unlike the other houses, which focus on land-based industries and politics, Bastilla cares only for the open sea. Their fleets handle nearly all maritime trade, and even rival houses must rely on Bastilla ships to move their goods overseas. The arrangement is simple: Bastilla builds, maintains, and commissions merchant vessels, which are then leased to other houses in exchange for a cut of their profits. This gives Bastilla enormous leverage in Ordain, and everyone respects House Bastilla, even if they don’t trust them.

Audacious and daring, House Bastilla members buy their way into power within the house and tend to value flashy displays of power. This leads to most members emphasizing a similar attitude of Big Risks for Big Rewards.While they have been accused of piracy, the general consensus is that if Bastilla breaks the rules, they are quick to admit it.

  • Money Is Power: Power within the house is neither inherited nor earned by merit, it is bought. Wealth is the key to influence, and members flaunt it proudly through extravagant fashion, opulent jewelry, and lavish displays of excess. In House Bastilla, status is not subtle—it is worn like armor, sailed like a flagship, and spent like water.

  • Show Your Stuff: Flamboyance and derring-do are valued in House Bastilla, with ship captains and shop owners attracting others to be part of their crews by sharing over-the-top tales of their daring antics of the past and bold plans for the future.

  • Experimental Magery: Competition between House Bastilla's ships and captains is fierce. To gain an advantage, ships and their sailors use a variety of means to achieve their goals or win a fight. Ships are often covered in arcane symbols, and sailors wear tattoos and talismans believed to protect them or bring luck. The house as a whole is highly superstitious, with rituals, omens, and magical rites playing a major role in daily life.

Operations

Progression through the ranks of House Bastilla depends on one thing: cold, hard coin. In House Bastilla, you buy your way into power, and when positions and captaincies open up, the wealthy sailors and more experienced individuals move up to higher positions. While this sociopolitical climb can be achieved with some intrigue and flair, the main driver remains wealth.

Most major decisions in House Bastilla are made by vote, with each ship and, by extension, its captain holding one vote. Additional votes can be bought, often leading to odd bidding wars and side deals. Beyond these large all-hands votes, the house’s interests are managed by their leader who heads the house itself. Although this leader is sometimes a descendant of Red Bastilla, as the name carries significant weight, other captains have led the house in the past.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.yztzqRozoEkbiO2K]{Katerin Bastilla}(Lawful Neutral, Ordani Kivahr, she/her)

The current leader of House Bastilla.

@UUID[Actor.4OrF9O1B8xcRJ0tG]{Darion the Soulthief} (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Signborn, he/him)

Darion is one of the most famous Ordani in recent memory, a legendary swashbuckler, explorer, and warrior whose life reads like something torn from the pages of an embellished myth rather than something true. Equal parts rogue and hero, Darion carved his name into history through daring feats, impossible escapes, and a seemingly endless string of near-suicidal adventures. His fame rose to glittering heights when he joined forces with the Cascilian Navy to take on a massive fleet commanded by the Blood Barons. While details of the Battle of the Throat are still debated in taverns and around campfires, it’s agreed that Darion played a crucial role in the confrontation and that he moved through the battle, grinning, laughing, and destroying the undead.

@UUID[Actor.z5Covcb509jE01ka]{Bortusk Flamebeard} (Neutral, Ordani Vrjnhar, he/him)

A large, cheerful Vrjnhar who captains the ship The Razorcrumb. Like many captains in House Bastilla, Bortusk is an extremely wealthy individual. They are rarely in Ordain and instead primarily trade with the Lumek and the Waerds, spending long months and years in foreign ports.

Matienne Bastilla (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

A stoic figurehead of House Bastilla and overseer of Coinwealth Heights, Matienne is not what most expect of the normally bombastic Bastilla members. She rarely appears in public, preferring to run district affairs from her estate or the private lounges of the Gilded Stem. She is known for cultivating cordial ties with those useful to her house and enforcing district order with an iron hand slipped into a velvet glove.
House Bastilla.scoverview: One of the five powerful Trading Houses of Ordain, House Bastilla rose from the early chaotic years of Ordain's founding to become a dominant force in the city’s commerce. Its origins lie in the hands of a few disgruntled ship captains who banded together to oppose House Komric. Though they are a legitimate part of the city, the house still carries the scent of its past, a reputation for ruthlessness, cunning, and a tendency to bend or break the rules when convenient. Today, House Bastilla commands Ordain’s merchant navy, overseeing the city’s sea trade routes, foreign ports, and on occasion, more discreet ventures. Outsiders and rivals often accuse them of being little more than gilded pirates, cloaking dubious dealings in silk and ceremony.
House Bastilla.sgamemaster:
House Bastilla officially formed [[/date AS1832]], but it was in operation before this date under the banner of the infamous Captain Red Bastilla. She was initially imprisoned in [[/date AS1800]] before escaping thanks to help from her crew and fled Ordain. She begins a violent campaign of revenge against ships sailing under the flag of Komric. In exile, she found fertile ground among other captains and ships that House Komric owned. These were not common brigands or outcasts but loyal citizens of the city, driven by shared anger over bad pay, and growing wealth inequality. Over the years, her fleet grew into a loose coalition of renegade captains, answering only to Red Bastilla's orders. They operated from hidden coves, forgotten ruins, and drifting sea camps. Some called them pirates, others mere raiders, but their power continued to grow until the vents of the Veiled War, which saw the downfall of House Komric, and the house was recognised as the Third Trading House of Ordain.

House Bastilla, under Katerin's leadership, appears ruthless and potentially villainous in some aspects. As the story unfolds, it's clear that Katerin's actions serve the goals of @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss}. However, this is not intentional, Katerin is an unwilling pawn in a larger game, and House Bastilla is neither corrupted nor trying to deliberately bring about the city's destruction.

Timeline

[[/date AS2511]]

@UUID[Actor.yztzqRozoEkbiO2K]{Katerin Bastilla} assumes leadership of House Bastilla, backed strongly by her house and captains. She is sharp, resourceful, and very wealthy, recognized for her straightforward dealings and focus on profit above other matters. Her rise is further facilitated by her being a descendant of Red Bastilla herself.

[[/date AS2493]]

Darion the Soulthief of House Bastilla proclaims his intention to sail to the Spiritlands and sets off from Ordain. He is not heard from again, though rumors persist that his ship, the Silence, was last seen off the coast of Oakengarde. Not long after, a band of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.vOQKJHlJKyhaAz68]{Flame Guard} arrive, hunting Darion and his crew for crimes they never publicly disclose. They depart in frustration once its clear that Darion is not within the city.

[[/date AS2488]]

Darion the Soulthief of House Bastilla returns from the Cascilian Republic after helping to destroy a large undead fleet being constructed by the Blood Barons before they are able to set sail in the Battle of the Dawn. He returns To better make his exploits known, he showers the city in riches. For several years he hosts parties, parades, and commissions song and painting about his greatest accomplishments. This helps drive House Bastilla into a position of power and influence in the city which it had previously lacked.

[[/date AS1832]]

Following intensive calls for reform in the city from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}, the governing body of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate} is established, comprising three members from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}, and the combined members of the Trading Houses. During the formation of the first Ordinate, Captain Red Bastilla returns to the city at the head of her fleet and demands a seat on the ruling council. After tense negotiations, she forms @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla} as a permanent addition to the city's organizations, and Ember's Bounty, her flagship, remains docked in the city for many years.

[[/date AS1800]]

The independent Captain Red Bastilla is accused of smuggling goods into Ordain by House Komric. She is initially imprisoned before escaping thanks to help from her crew and flees the city. She begins a violent campaign of revenge against ships sailing under the flag of Komric, and for many years, she remains a fugitive from the city. In her exile, she hires and recruits more disillusioned or disenfranchised Ordani who seek her out and forms a coalition of ships under her banner.

House Cevher.name: House Cevher
House Cevher.text:
House Cevher is the trading house generally responsible for metals, stone, and any arcane materials that can be mined or quarried. The potential for something to go horribly wrong if these operations fail makes House Cevher very risk-averse; their nickname is “House Never” for how often they shoot things down in the Trading House Assembly.

  • Family Comes First: House Cevher is all about family - most of its leaders are related to the original founders somehow, and quarries and mines tend to be passed down from one generation of a family to the next. Occasionally, someone marries into the family simply for the access to power, but the family generally allows it as it helps to bring in new blood.

  • If It Ain't Broke: House Cevher is all about doing things slowly and methodically, using time-tested methods. They also like everything by-the-book and above board. This has led to some animosity between Cevher and houses that are a bit more sneaky in their dealings, like Wandren and Bastilla.

  • Avoiding Disaster: There are a few large quarry and mining accidents in House Cevher's past, and while it has always changed its practices in response and taken care of survivors and the families of the dead (even creating a special memorial graveyard and garden for them just outside of Ordain), some still feel uneasy and worry that the house is either foolish or cursed.

Operations

All leaders of House Cevher are related to the original two friends who started the trading house by blood or marriage, and the House is still managed by a pair - the Steward and the Advocate. The Steward focuses on internal matters (pricing, productivity, disturbances in the mines, etc) and tends to be more bookish, while the Advocate focuses on relationships with outsiders (the other Trading Houses, the Ordinate) and tends to be more personable.

Outside of the leadership of the House, its members include those who oversee mining and quarry operations, create trade deals for its materials, or are experts at a craft that involves transforming and using its materials, such as masons, and metalworkers. The House uses the traditional method of generally referring to these members as inked (those who make deals and oversee projects), silvered (those who trade), and guilded (those who specialize in a craft). Individual miners and haulers are thought of as associated with House Cevher, but aren't full members who are privy to the House's dealings, a point of some contention that was exacerbated after they suffered many of the losses in the Stonehollow Quake that was widely blamed on House Cevher.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher} (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human she/her)

Lyla, who has spent the last few years learning new innovative business techniques in Casla-Brava, is returning to Ordain after the death of her father Ralton, the most recent House Cevher Advocate. She intends to support her brother Funar as he takes over some of Ralton's duties and responsibilities.

@UUID[Actor.E701HRk9vreXMUhl]{Funar Cevher} (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

Lyla's brother is much shyer and more withdrawn than his sister. He is passionate about House Cevher and is currently sitting in his father's seat in the Trading House Assembly. He is hoping to take his father's title of Advocate as well, but is worried that he doesn't have the charisma and might be passed over in favor of the returning Lyla.

Darius Cevher (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

Lyla's uncle, and Ralton's brother, Darius has always more interested in books than trade and spent most of his time "learning the business" trying to find intriguing arcane objects buried in the mines that he could research. Ralton helped to set him up with a bookshop, in part to convince him to stay in Ordain instead of joining the Anachraenum, and he has successfully run it for several years. It is rumored that he offers a "family" discount to all House Cevher members.
House Cevher.scoverview: If there is a substance on the Arctus Plateau that can be mined or quarried, Ordain’s House Cevher is likely involved. One of the five Trading Houses that make up the mercantile leg of Ordain’s triangle of power, House Cevher focuses on stone and metals, though it also trades any arcane materials found in its mines and quarries. Risk-averse and family-oriented, House Cevher is the most traditionalist of all the Trading Houses, and always draws its leaders from the Cevher family line.
House Cevher.sgamemaster: House Cevher is the only Trading House founded by Arcturians—best friends Lottie and Cael left Arcturel in the early days of Ordain to offer expertise to the city’s builders and soon became the go-to trading house for stone and metal mining. In the generations since, House Cevher has become a family affair, with nearly every prominent member able to trace themselves back to one or both of the founders. This has sometimes led to poor leadership as unqualified family members take over key roles, and there have been a few isolated but tragic disasters over the years at Cevher sites, including the Stonehollow Quake disaster, which killed over a thousand Ordain residents. The House does not believe it is to blame for the quake, but cannot prove its innocence.

House Lilifeld.name: House Lilifeld
House Lilifeld.text:
Among the five great Trading Houses, House Lilifeld is known as the living heartbeat of Ordain, the force that keeps the city fed and growing. Uniquely, Lilifeld is the only House whose seat of power lies outside the city proper, not even on the Arctus Plateau, but across the sea on the vine-wrapped Isle of Kortos. When it became clear that the Arcturian people nearby could only ever grow enough to sustain their own scattered communities, the rising urban sprawl of Ordain faced a crisis of hunger. In search of fertile lands beyond the plateau, interprising traders came across the lush, fertile Isle of Kortos, and among its rolling fields roamed the Terracant: massive, vine-horned beasts with mossy coats and eyes like slow-burning amber.

These ancient creatures, part beast and part natural force, seemed to be the perfect solution to the growing cities food problem. Through a special bond with the Terracants and their innate abilities to boost crop yields, House Lilifeld emerged not only as a merchant power but as the cornerstone of Ordain’s survival.

  • Bread and Wine: Among House Lilifeld’s sprawling estates on the Isle of Kortos, colossal golden terraces of wheat ripple gently alongside endless rows of grapevines. The terraced fields climb the hillsides in graceful steps, each plot tended to by Lilifeld workers and faithful, well-cared-for Terracent herds. Harvested wheat becomes the bread that fills the tables in Ordain, a humble yet vital counterpart to Lilifeld’s famed vintages for delicious wine.

  • Decadent Dishes: House Lilifeld is famous not only for what it grows but also for what it creates, with many legendary chefs among their ranks. The culinary arts are taught to all Lilifeld members, trained to coax extraordinary flavor from humble crops, vegetables, meats, and fruits sourced from across the known world. Within Ordain, Lilifeld has taken over nearly the entire Restaurant Row and owns stakes in many cafes, taverns, inns, and restaurants throughout the city. Their partnership with House Bastilla brings in exotic spices, seafood, and arcane delicacies from distant shores.

  • Foundation of Fashion: The lush, mossy fleece of the Terracant is spun into fine wool with a subtle shimmer and remarkable durability, and within Ordain it forms the foundation of everything from everyday cloaks to enchanted finery. House Lilifeld does not personally make these clothing items but instead has a close partnership with House Salva, the premier weavers and designers of the city.

Operations

House Lilifeld has a subtle but far-reaching influence. Its members are resourceful, hardy folk who spend most of their time in Ordain, distributing food throughout the city's markets, running restaurants, and cooking. On Kortos, they oversee the cultivation of wheat, grapes, and the care of their prized Terracants. Every harvest is carefully timed with the seasons, while wool shearing, food preparation, and trade coordination are handled with near-ritual precision. Lilifeld’s operations blend curated and carefully crafted magic with generational know-how, ensuring that every barrel, bushel, and bale is ready for market, whether bound for local tables or the grand halls of Ordain.

Unfortunately, while House Lilifeld has close relationships with every other house and is generally beloved by the people, despite being a commercial enterprise, their relationship with Arcturians and the Agrimages Circle is far from glowing. Agrimages dislike House Lilifeld's commercialization and industrialization, finding their techniques to grow food using the Terracant to be widely disruptive to natural ecosystems. As a result, Lilifeld is one of the only major houses that struggles to gain stable footing within the Arctus Plateau, often facing resistance from local Arcturian communities who view them as outsiders disrupting the old ways.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.fJ4WogeI4O64Ry1T]{Krafton Lilifeld} (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

The current head of House Lilifeld, Krafton is a shrewd, hard-working statesman known as much for his relentless work ethic as for his legendary obsession with alcoholic drink. Not merely a connoisseur, Krafton treats winemaking and distillation as high art, personally overseeing new blends, commissioning experimental brews, and hosting long, boisterous tastings that double as political negotiations. Beneath his easy charm and wine-stained grin lies a calculating mind, one constantly working to expand Lilifeld’s influence across Ordain. He is often found in the Lockstop Winery in Lastgate, overseeing production.

Torin Lilifeld (Neutral Good, Ordani Keth, he/him)

Overseer of Lilifeld’s estates on the Isle of Kortos, Torin is a commanding presence who walks the fields in finely dyed Terracant wool, equal parts farmer, strategist, and businessman. He keeps Lilifeld’s harvests flowing smoothly, even in drought or political unrest, and is firmly at work in the background of the house.

Serenna Ryes (Chaotic Good, Ordani Drakon, she/her)

Serenna is a brilliant and celebrated chef, the visionary behind Lilifeld’s most renowned recipes. She is currently cooking in the lavish Odd Bites restaurant, which has a waiting list of nearly two weeks to get a table. Her dishes blend rare spices from the Lumek Firelands, exotic meats from the Lowlands, and vegetables from the Kithil Highlands. Serenna also personally trains many new Lilifeld members and is whispered to possess a recipe book sealed with a spell that only opens under the moon of Orbis.
House Lilifeld.scoverview: House Lilifeld is the beating heart of Ordain, made up of farmers, vintners, herders, and culinary chefs who turn land and sea bounty into stunning dishes and rich alcoholic drinks. Primarily based in the lush hills of the Isle of Kortos, they cultivate wheat, vegetables, and flavorful grapevines, while raising the goat-like Terracants, whose enchanted fleece and soil-turning hooves shape the land itself.
House Lilifeld.sgamemaster: Long before House Lilifeld rose to prominence, they were little more than a ragged band of explorers and backwater merchants from Ordain. But fate, or perhaps luck, changed everything when a storm blew their ships off course into the pristine harbors of the Isle of Kortos. There, they discovered vine-covered hills rich with ancient soil, natural terraces ideal for farming, and the slow-moving, moss-covered creatures now known as Terracants. Recognizing a rare opportunity, the settlers made a pact to keep the land both fertile, pristine, and profitable. House Lilifeld was born, not by blood but through shared ambition and a little luck.

House Salva.name: House Salva
House Salva.text:
House Salva presents itself as a patron of high fashion, fine art, and rising entertainers, curating culture and taste for the entire city. But behind this refined image lies a more practical and far-reaching operation. Salva is the primary supplier of textiles and clothing across Ordain, ranging from everyday garments to elite gowns and shimmering, magically enhanced fabrics. Additionally, thanks to their access to canvas and a wide-reaching network of talent scouts, Salva is also a major, although somewhat secretive, producer and trader of maps. House Salva agents gather more than just artistic talent; they collect geographic and social intelligence used by the House to guide both fashion trends and strategic ventures.

  • Reputation is Everything: With so much of House Salva's public face focused on areas like art and style that are more about subjective judgment than objective measure, reputation is seen as a tangible representation of trustworthiness.

  • Image First: The appearance of things is important within Salva - this doesn't necessarily mean that Salva members are flashy, but they often make sure to have a touch of glamour about them in some way shape or form to mark themselves as influencers and tastemakers.

  • Proving Ground: Within Ordain, Salva is considered one of the most important houses due to its cultural fascination with clothing and styles. While this serves the house as a whole, different House Salva members deal with this differently, with some trying extra hard to prove themselves at all times and others getting a chip on their shoulders about their worth being constantly questioned. As such, members of House Salva are often treated to a higher standard than other houses, but consequently are judged far more harshly for their missteps amongst their fellow members and the people of Ordain.

Operations

Within House Salva, reputation and trustworthiness are essential and are measured through the use of a magical thread, given to prospective members of the house by their first mentor. The more a person has been vouched for by others in the house, the brighter the glow and the longer the thread, with newer members of the house trying their hardest to “shine” within the house both literally and figuratively. The thread is used differently by each member of the house, with some weaving it into clothing, others using it in the signage in their shop, and still others displaying the spool as is on their person. Any method is acceptable as long as the thread can be clearly seen.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.8f0lPTNdipyTDkX4]{Nix Salvar} (Neutral Good, Ordani Kiska, she/her)

Nix Salvar is the current leader of House Salva, a name she adopted when she became its head. She was once a renowned actress who impressed the city’s residents with her emotional depth and played a wide range of roles in theater performances throughout the city. Using her considerable charm and business acumen, she has secured several major deals for House Salva, including a partnership with Bastilla to place agents on several of their ships so they can produce more accurate sea charts.

@UUID[Actor.i5jXHUyZCPBJDb2k]{Mistress Caberi} (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

Mistress Caberi is a warm, friendly seamstress often surrounded by bolts of luxurious cloth, textiles in vibrant colors, and a large following of adoring fans. Her fame is so widespread that she has become a member of the Ordanite after being elected by the Hallows and through her connections with House Salva, and although she is not technically a member of the house, she is so closely connected that she might as well be. She welcomes all who enter her quaint shop in Gossamar with a radiant smile, where the aroma of fresh clean fabric mingles with soft laughter and cheerful conversations about the latest trends in Ordain. With her nimble fingers, she weaves magical threads of various hues, crafting exquisite and unique pieces of clothing for the city's most passionate fashionistas.

@UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]{Cherish Ellerie} (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

An up-and-comer who doesn't want to wait and earn her reputation piece by piece. Instead, she wants to grab it. Cherish befriends new artists in the city in unexpected locations, from the clubs of Kencleft to the altars at the Numinous Shrines, and pushes them to do big things, with her as their sponsor.

Vujin Barriq (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Fej, he/him)

Vujin ascended through House Salva because of his reputation as a scout and mapmaker, and has become the person within that house who almost exclusively deals with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} and adventures from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}.
House Salva.scoverview: House Salva is a prestigious and influential house within the great city of Ordain, known for its dominance in beauty, fashion, and the arts. It is a house built on image and reputation, shaping the city’s style trends while quietly pulling strings behind the scenes. House Salva is often seen as one of the most important trading houses by the people, as its impact is closely tied to how the Ordani perceive themselves as a culture. Interestingly, Salva allows the other trading houses to underestimate its significance in broader city affairs, putting them in the unique position as the deciding swing vote in many Trading House disputes; Salva takes advantage of this position to its own benefit, with the other trade houses being none the wiser.
House Salva.sgamemaster:
Publicly House Salva was started by the Salva acrobatics troupe from the Lumek city of Hearth, who sailed to Ordain in its early years in search of new audiences. While their act was only a moderate success, they made a fortune remaking and selling their costumes, quickly establishing themselves as a textile trading house while trying to raise money to build a theater. Known for both their over-the-top antics and their discerning eye for fashion and talent, they quickly attracted other performers, fashionistas, and shrewd merchants as they built their name. Their current focus on reputation and name can be traced back to the love for publicity of the original Salva troupe and the need to prevent scandals like the beetle belt incident, which almost saw the entire house fall due to the unscrupulous dealings of one silk merchant.

Timeline

[[/date AS2097]]

A traveling eccentric troupe of acrobatics from the Lumek city of Hearth visits Ordain and causes a social uproar in the city by exhibiting new fashions and ideas, and making a fortune selling new clothing items based on their costumes, all the while hosting extravagant parties and galas. They are soon sponsored by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.FaUiibd3k4gfrzry]{Mistress Caberi}, who creates magical garments and clothing for the group, and gives them enough prestige to remain in the city, forming a Trading House called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{Salva}.

House Wandren.name: House Wandren
House Wandren.text:
As the go-to trader for hard-to-acquire luxury items in Ordain, House Wandren relies on contacts and relationships to track down and move the goods that it sells. These relationships also help Wandren collect and trade on information and secrets, which they use to help incentivize those they deal with to either give them good deals or look the other way when they inevitably bring a few items into the city that they shouldn't.

  • Gilded Masks: House Wandren thrives on contradiction. To the public, they are charming hosts, draped in fine silks and perfumes, curating the rarest luxuries for Ordain’s elite. Yet behind that polished smile lies a ruthless engine of vice and profit, their every gesture calculated to conceal the smuggling, blackmail, and shadow deals that fund their true power. To deal with House Wandren is to never quite know whether you’re being courted—or ensnared.

  • Information is Everything: Whether it is knowing who to go to to get an obscure artifact, how to sneak contraband into the city, or who can be relied on to look the other way, members of House Wandren keep close tabs on information. Many carry small books that keep track of the information that they know, written in code that is indecipherable to anyone but their heirs.

  • Rules Are For Breaking: From its earliest days, House Wandren has been about breaking the rules, though some iterations of the organization are more aboveboard than others, depending on the current leader. In recent years, Wandren has appeared to abandon much of its legitimate business in favor of its more secretive operations and has been collecting more information than in previous iterations, for unknown reasons that may point to a shift in power.

Operations

House Wandren's power structure is both concentrated and chaotic - whoever knows the most damaging information about the other members of the house rises to the top, able to use their knowledge to force their potential rivals to do their bidding. Often, this leads to a cycle of change as new leaders unseat the current head of the house simply by finding information that they can hold over the leaders' head.

It is considered mandatory for any member of House Wandren to know who is currently in charge, but the frequent changes can make this difficult. To combat this, Wandren holds regular auctions in their Tradeway, which are considered the only proper place to make a dramatic power play. The current head of Wandren, Hephiss Wandren, gained his position by auctioning off the bottle of poison used to kill former Wandren leader Orena Wandren instead of providing it to the Veiled Chain or Hallows, a sign that he knew who was to blame but would let them escape if they supported his bid to run House Wandren. Hephiss has been in charge of the Trading House ever since.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.OOO380zs3xZYG9PI]{Hephiss Wandren} (CE Ordani Fej, she/her)

Hephiss Wandren has been the head of House Wandren for several years, which is longer than most are able to hold onto the position. She gained it by successfully blackmailing the killers of the last two major leaders of the house, though her tight grip on House Wandren is helped by the fact that anyone who tries to learn information about her ends up dead.

@UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren} (CG Ordani Wirrun, he/him)

Juro Wandren prefers the smuggling side of House Wandren's trade to the secret keeping side, perhaps in part because he once revealed a secret about his good friend Lyla Cevher that led to a serious rift between them. Uneasy in the presence of Hephiss Wandren, he has decided to make his base of operations out on the Arctus Plateau instead of in Ordain proper.
House Wandren.scoverview: House Wandren presents itself as the purveyor of luxury goods in Ordain, boasting refined tastes and access to wealthy clients. But this polished image hides their true nature. Beneath the silk, perfumes, and wide smiles lies a sprawling network of informants and brokers, trading not just in finery but in secrets. Their webs of contacts run so deep that even the Veiled Chain occasionally turns to them for intelligence. Yet it is not information alone that fills their coffers—the true profit comes from their shadow trade in stolen and illicit goods. House Wandren moves what others cannot: stolen treasures, dangerous magical artifacts, and materials that bypass the city’s laws.
House Wandren.sgamemaster:
House Wandren is the youngest of the trading houses, originally formed by the sailors of the Wandren, a ship that stumbled onto a cache of riches while sailing for House Bastilla. Instead of returning to Ordain and paying their dues to the house, the crew decided to use their newfound wealth and ship to bring in goods from afar that they could resell in the city.

The Wandren’s plan worked - they used the luxury goods that they brought back to build wealth and reputation in Ordain and established themselves as the final Trading House, taking Wandren as their name. But while House Wandren made a big splash in its earlier years, securing luxuries can be a difficult business, and the house soon ran into difficulties, kept afloat only by through the efforts of Dini Wandren, who forced the other Trading Houses to lend Wandren money in order to keep their secrets safe after her wife Myna broke into their strongholds to find information to bribe them with. Since that time, Wandren has continued to trade in luxuries, but has made as much money and impact trading in information and securing illegal merchandise – the only rule being that the house would only use its secrets on outsiders. Until now.

After the death of elderly leader Kore Wandren, a clandestine war began taking place, with factions led by his heirs. Two groups within the Trading House quickly emerged as the dominant players in the conflict. The Cryars, led by Orena Wandren, believed the house should get back to its roots and stamp out illegal activity and the Whispers, led by Tamis Wandren, believed the house should slip into the shadows and embrace more direct activities of the underworld, including thievery, assassination, and smuggling. The dispute ended with Tamis Wandren dead in an ambush and Orena Wandren dying suspiciously in her bath, fracturing the house. Hephiss Wandren has so far been the only one able to keep it together, in part because he routinely suggests that he knows who is behind both killings.

Many of the House Wandren Whisper faction members who were pushed out of the city at the end of the House Wandren War fled into the Arctus Plateau proper. They continued smuggling operations and thievery, many turning bandit and forming the foundations of the Otherhood of Fortune.

Sanguinaries.name: Sanguinaries
Sanguinaries.text:
The Sanguinaries are far smaller in number than the Cindaric Sages, with little influence beyond a handful of scattered pockets across the known world. They lack organized defenders or formal security, relying instead on improvised measures and the vigilance of individual members. Their hierarchy is loose, centered on a symbolic leader whose role is more to guide than to command. What strengthens them, however, is their deep connection to magic. Many of their number are skilled sorcerers and druids, and the order as a whole maintains a profound tie to the ancient and powerful Casia, and the realm of Primordis, drawing on that bond to further their studies and fuel their cause.

  • Heart of the World: Like the Cindaric Sages, the Sanguinaries believe all life in the cosmos exists as part of the unconscious will of the Heart of Ember—the creationary force at the center of the world.

  • The Burden of Truth: The Sanguinaries differ from the Sages in one crucial way: they believe the Heart of Ember is dying. This conviction is the cornerstone of their faith, shaping their worldview and driving their actions. Each member must grapple with this shared burden and the responsibility to act against such an end. How best to achieve this varies widely, but all pursue it with relentless determination.

  • Defiant Independence: Born from suppression by the Cindaric Sages, the Sanguinaries place great value on freedom of belief and expression. Their order is highly dispersed, with members scattered across the known world—even as far as the distant Tayan Empire. Leadership provides little formal doctrine, leaving individuals and groups to interpret their cause as they see fit.

  • Radical Elements: A small faction within the Sanguinaries believes awareness of Ember’s decline must be spread at all costs. These zealots push for decisive, often disruptive action, and pursue it whenever they can. Among their own, they are tolerated as fanatics; to outsiders, they are little more than doomsayers and madmen.

Operations

Though small and scattered, the Sanguinaries take an active role in defending Ember from threats they see as symptoms of its decline. Their efforts vary widely from cell to cell, but certain patterns are common. Many devote themselves to the destruction of the undead, whom they regard as abominations that gnaw at the strength of the living world. Others turn their focus to the encroaching corruption of monsters and threats from beyond the cosmos. Some Sanguinaries speak of combating the Great Darkness or one of its forms in many fragmented terms: the Hollow, the Famine, the Blight, but what they mean by this is unclear.

Most do not set out to become Sanguinaries. Members are usually drawn in after uncovering fragments of truth about the Heart of Ember or being approached by a wandering believer. Initiation is informal, like an invitation to a ritual, a trusted secret, or a test to destroy an undead or a monster. Each path is personal, with commitment born from conviction rather than oath, leaving the order diverse but united by a shared burden.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol} (Neutral Good, Maziran Human/Nir'ae, she/her)

Avwynn Taol is the iron heart of the Sanguinaries, a mystic-scholar whose power and presence command attention wherever she goes. Exceptionally well-read and insatiably curious, she has spent her life chasing the truths buried in Ember’s histories, cultures, and legacies, piecing together patterns others overlook.
Sanguinaries.scoverview: The Sanguinaries are a breakaway sect from the Cindaric Sages, formed when a horrified sage revealed the supposed truth that the order had long tried to hide: the Heart of Ember is not just weakened after long eons of keeping the cosmos intact, but is dying. Where the Sages deny and suppress, the Sanguinaries act. They are scattered, lacking central leadership, and place a high value on individual freedom, which gives them the flexibility to approach their cause in different ways. Some groups or individuals search for answers quietly, while others take desperate or extreme action, convinced that only direct action can save Ember.
Sanguinaries.sgamemaster:
The origins of the Sanguinaries trace back nearly three centuries to Darik Melsbow, a scholarly member of the Cindaric Sages. During his expeditions into the Bloodwoods, Darik encountered Nimaelle, a powerful Casia whose insights shattered his understanding of the world. From her, he learned a dire truth: the Heart of Ember was not merely weakened, but slowly dying, and with it the very fabric of the cosmos would one day unravel.

Upon realizing the gravity of his discovery, he sought to inform his peers in the Cindaric Sages. However, his warnings fell on deaf ears as the Holy Speaker of that time, in an attempt to avert widespread panic, dismissed the claims to maintain unity. Bitterness and anger led Darik to leave Ordain in search of evidence to prove their discovery and gain a deeper understanding of the Heart's affliction. In their wake, the Cindaric leadership exiled both Darik and his close group of followers, calling him and any who would follow harbingers of disunity and alarmists trying to spread fear and drive people into pointless panic.

From that split grew the Sanguinaries, a small but unyielding order that has since embedded itself within many lands beyond Ordain. Over time, they have learned to temper their message, avoiding the image of doomsayers while pursuing both discovery and the defense of the cosmos itself.

Timeline

[[/date AS2505]]

A poor harvest in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kethil} Villages across the sea and the unease following the recent quake led to a period of minor unrest and rationing for several months in Ordain. Though the situation is rare and resolved quickly by the Trading Houses with the purchase of food from several of the Southern Waerd Bastions, as a result, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries} gain momentum among the angry populace in the city.

Otherhood of Fortune.name: Otherhood of Fortune
Otherhood of Fortune.text:
Spoilers

The Otherhood of Fortune is a villainous organization, and the content within this page contains spoilers for the story of Shard of Fear.

The Otherhood of Fortune is a loose organization of bandits, outlaws, and ruffians, typically acting outside of the city of Ordain and led by various independent leaders of extremely questionable morality. The actual name Otherhood is rarely used as connections between these smaller groups is a secret within a mystery and the name is used by its principal leaders and high-ranking members with more understanding of the "Grand Plan" rather than its more rank-and-file grunts. Spread out across the Arctus Plateau the Otherhood is perfectly situated to take full advantage of the chaos, disruption, and unrest that has emerged over recent years. The various smaller groups have each taken on specific areas of opportunity. Banditry, theft, robberies, and even full-on occupation of abandoned villages and farms and resource-rich locations.

  • Rich Opportunities: The Otherhood thrives on chaos, drawing recruits from desperate refugees, displaced farmers, and idle workers, then seizing abandoned or vulnerable assets such as mills, mines, and supply routes. Their reach is so broad that the Trading Houses, the Veiled Chain, and other organizations cannot stamp them out; every victory against one group is undercut by the rise of another elsewhere.

  • Seawall Stands: A powerful faction of the Otherhood has coalesced around the seaside town of Seawall, where the charismatic outlaw “Sticks” has convinced the populace that the Trading Houses are the root of the Plateau’s suffering. His propaganda is laced with lies, yet his message carries enough truth to resonate with those desperate for stability, giving the Otherhood a rare stronghold within a settled town.

  • Unseen Strings: Though fragmented, the Otherhood’s scattered bands show uncanny coordination, often striking in ways that weaken supply chains, destabilize markets, or exploit unrest at opportune moments. This suggests that someone, or something, is quietly guiding their actions toward a larger, more dangerous goal.
Otherhood of Fortune.scoverview: The Otherhood of Fortune is a loose and elusive network of opportunists who style themselves as champions of the common folk on the Arctus Plateau. They claim to break the stranglehold of the Trading Houses, redistributing wealth and creating space for ordinary people to thrive. To most, however, the Otherhood looks little different from scattered bands of thieves and highwaymen, preying on trade routes and merchants alike. True coordination between these cells is rare and deliberately hidden, with many members carrying out raids or tasks without realizing how their actions serve broader Otherhood goals.
Otherhood of Fortune.sgamemaster:
The roots of the Otherhood of Fortune lie in brutal civil war within House Wandren. Beset by infighting following the death of Kore Wandren, its elderly leader at the time. A clandestine war unfolds across the city as factions form under his children. Two groups within the Trading House quickly emerge as the dominant players in the conflict: the Cryars, led by Orena Wandren, who believes the house should be legitimate and stamp out illegal activity; and the Whispers, led by Tamis Wandren, who believe the house should slip into the shadows and embrace undercity elements such as thievery, assassination, and smuggling.

After a particularly bloody conflict, the war officially ends with the death of Tamis. However, since then, House Wandren has been plagued by internal disputes, and many believe that the Whispers stopped fighting openly and now engage in illegal activities in the shadows. Orena Wandren's death, twenty years later, was especially suspicious after she was found dead in her bath.

Many of the Whisper faction members fled into the Arctus Plateau proper. They continue their smuggling operations and thievery, and many turn to banditry, going on to form the foundations of the Otherhood of Fortune, a loose group of thieves and bandits that still has many links to the darker side of House Wandren.

Operations

The Otherhood maintains its veneer as a disorganized rabble of bandits, but in truth, it operates with deliberate coordination shaped by hidden alliances. Its scattered bands are quietly supported and directed through connections with lingering ties to House Wandren. The knowledge of which would likely bring House Wandren itself to its knees. Unbeknownst to most, even within the Otherhood itself, the group is guided by three principal leaders: Sticks, Grimclaw, and Hephiss Wandren.

The Otherhood sustains itself through opportunistic recruitment. Many of its rank-and-file are drawn from the desperate, refugees, indebted farmers, failed merchants, and displaced workers, who are offered protection or the promise of wealth in exchange for service. Some are lured in with the illusion of fighting for justice against the Trading Houses, while others are simply forced to choose between starvation and or joing the organization. Funding comes from a patchwork of illicit activities: smuggling contraband across the plateau, extorting villages, raiding caravans, and seizing abandoned farms and mines to funnel resources into black markets.

The Otherhood is secretly controlled almost entirely by its three major leaders, Sticks, Grimclaw, and Hephiss Wandren who in turn are being commanded by the dragon Zerranyss. The ultimate goal beyond causing chaos, disruption, and weakening the region, is the eventual takeover and domination of the region and the city of Ordain by Zerranyss after they have ascended.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.z1Ttp0q6CAtjDphl]{Sticks} (Chaotic Evil, Kessian Kiska, he/him)

Once a pirate of considerable renown, Sticks earned his name after being rescued as a shipwrecked child, found clinging to little more than a bundle of driftwood. Rising through the ranks of the crew that saved him, he built a reputation for cunning, charm, and an unshakable will to survive. Once he arrived in the coastal town of Seawall, he became a self-styled champion of the common folk, positioning himself and his city as an alternative to Ordain’s rigid control and the Trading Houses’ suffocating dominance.

@UUID[Actor.OOO380zs3xZYG9PI]{Hephiss Wandren}(Lawful Evil, Ordani Fej, she/her)

Hephiss Wandren is the leader of House Wandren, one of the major Trading Houses of the Great City of Ordain. She has held onto the position longer than most by moving shrewdly but decisively in pursuit of power. While she does not often flex her power, preferring to seem a bit more above it all, when she does, it can be deadly, and several House Wandren members who have opposed her are now conveniently missing.

@UUID[Actor.T0s8ttP4GO1morn3]{Grimclaw} (Neutral Evil, Arcturian Signborn, he/him)

A towering figure of muscle and menace, Grimclaw earned his name from the jagged iron prosthetic that replaced his left hand after a pit-fight gone wrong. Once a mercenary commander under the Tayan Empire, he now leads one of the most violent arms of the Otherhood. He rules through fear and spectacle, his raids marked by brutality and blood. Despite his savage demeanor, Grimclaw is no fool, he’s a cunning tactician who understands that terror is a powerful tool.

Mutagists.name: Mutagists
Mutagists.text:
Spoilers

The Mutagists are a villainous organization; nothing about them is known publicly, and the content within this page contains spoilers for the story of Shard of Fear.
Mutagists.scoverview: The Mutagists are less of an organization than a following, devoted manics that seem to follow a mysterious master. The promises that have been made to them about the power they will receive in return drive them as a whole, though they each also have their own individual sadistic and destructive desires.
Mutagists.sgamemaster:
As organizations go, the Mutagists are barely aligned on even basic ideas or principles and barely tolerate one another; each of the five members is an individualistic, arrogant, self-absorbed megalomaniac with a penchant for cruelty, destruction, and sadism. The name itself was coined as more of a joke as they work towards the same overall goal, to create a Mutagenic Formula stable enough to empower their master so they can achieve ascension, though each member has their own complex motivations and reasons for doing so. While the number of Mutagists is limited to a mere handful of main members, their impact is immense, and their zealous individual pursuits and areas of influence often place them in positions of great political and social importance.

  • The Mutagenic Dream: At the heart of the Mutagists’ obsession lies their pursuit of the perfect Mutagenic Formula, an alchemical creation capable of reshaping flesh, mind, and spirit with the ultimate goal of achieving something akin to immortality. Each Mutagist interprets this goal differently, experimenting with their own unstable blends of magic and science. The results are often monstrous, leaving behind warped abominations and corrupted landscapes.

  • Power Through Discord: The Mutagists are not a unified organization but five rival egomaniacs bound by fragile necessity. Their constant infighting makes them unpredictable, but it also spreads their influence wide. Each commands their own networks of followers, failed experiments, and political connections, ensuring their presence is felt in multiple corners of society.

  • Fear as Influence: Though few in number, the Mutagists wield disproportionate power as they are connected, powerful, and wield immense influence. Each of the five tends to surround themselves with loyalists, fanatics, and warped creations, building small armies of minions who toil away either in hidden laboratories or among the general public, gathering information. The main Mutagists remain completely hidden, their existence unknown to most.

The Mutagists did not form by accident. They were gathered, piece by piece, by the will of @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss}. Through careful research and observation, he studied the habits, ambitions, and weaknesses of those who would become his chosen five. When the time was right, he approached each one in turn, tailoring his words to their vanity and ambition. Some were seduced with promises of power and ascension, others manipulated with flattery or the illusion of partnership. Zerranyss never asked for loyalty outright—he made them believe the alliance was their idea, that they stood to gain most from it.

What none of them realized was that they were already ensnared in his design. United, however reluctantly, these five fractured egomaniacs became something far more dangerous than they could have achieved alone.

Operations

The Mutagists operate in secrecy, each pursuing their own twisted schemes while feeding their work into Zerranyss’s grand design. Their methods vary, abductions for grotesque experiments, enthralling minions to spread terror, or subverting organizations and nations through manipulation. Though they rarely act in unison, their scattered atrocities form a hidden network of cruelty and corruption, with Zerranyss at its dark center.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]{Serethus} (Neutral Evil, Maziran Cor'ak, he/him)

Serethus is a master conversationalist, able to disarm with wit and dazzle with his vast scholarly knowledge. Yet behind the charm lies an insatiable hunger for forbidden truths and personal power. His humor often carries a cruel undercurrent, though he knows when to veil it for effect. Patient and calculating, Serethus delights in shaping people and events to serve his designs, treating morality as little more than an obstacle for lesser minds. When his mask slips, the warmth vanishes, revealing a cold intellect devoted wholly to the Mutagists’ pursuit of twisted ascension.

@UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan} (Neutral Evil, Moiran Vampyre, she/her)

Though counted among the weakest of the Moiran Blood Barons, Amelia Naxan has secured a place of influence through sheer cunning and a dangerous alliance with Zerranyss, dating back nearly a century. Where her peers rely on brute force and immense armies of the undead, Amelia has bound her ambitions to Zerranyss and the Mutagists, serving as both informant and collaborator. In exchange for knowledge and fragments of their mutagenic craft, she lends her vampiric talents to their schemes, providing networks of spies, expendable undead, and a ruthless mind for manipulation.

@UUID[Actor.fcK7WLaLCCcMP9oL]{Pyix} (Neutral Evil, Tyraphem, he/they)

Among the Mutagists, Pyix is perhaps the most alien in thought, a Tyraphem who views Ember as nothing more than a stage for their ambitions. Pyix sees the mutagenic formula as a tool not only to elevate themselves, but to prove the Tyraphem way of dominance and endless struggle. Though sworn in service to the stronger Tyraphem, Taryakel, Pyix’s loyalty is pragmatic and self-serving, and after being approached by Zerranyss, he joined his cause with great enthusiasm.

@UUID[Actor.CHMpij2geo5pTwoy]{Xeyrith} (Chaotic Evil, Dragon, he/they)

Among the five Mutagists, none embodies the raw hunger and primal ruin of destruction and gleeful sadism as Xeyrith, a Carnal Dragon of immense age and power. Known throughout the Lowlands and by the Waerds as The Red Maw, Xeyrith is a creature of insatiable appetite, his scales glimmering with a deep crimson sheen and his breath reeking of blood. Unlike the others, he did not need manipulation to join Zerranyss’s cause. Xeyrith came willingly, drawn to the promise of ascension and the mutagenic formula that might remake him into something greater.

@UUID[Actor.qIvuaK5p0319oWko]{Viviae Starsworn} (Chaotic Evil, Kessian Human, she/her)

Once a devout cleric of Ven’avé, Mistress of Fate, Viviae devoted their life to unraveling destiny’s threads. That devotion ended in madness when they peered too far, attempting to read not only mortal fates but the unraveling of Ember itself. Their visions shattered their mind, leaving them a broken vessel, yet Zerranyss saw use in their ruin. Twisted into a Mutagist, Viviae now serves as both prophet and enchantress, wielding fragments of divine power warped by mutagenic experiments.

Malicae.name: Malicae
Malicae.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.

The Malicae is one of the most furtive and clandestine organizations on Ember, yet it holds incredible power and maintains countless troves of hidden knowledge throughout Ember, the Sea of Stars above, and even the distant Inner Realms. Since the fall of the Aedir Empire and the annihilation of their pantheon, the Malicae has been secretly working to restore what was lost.

Ages ago, when the Aedir Empire was at its zenith, the Malicae served many purposes. Over time, however, its goals have shifted most dramatically. Now, the only path ahead for this abstruse organization is a bloody one, paved in ruin. Fraught with bitterness, anger, and dread, the surviving members of the Malicae were devastated by the near-annihilation of their world-spanning populace and the collapse of their once-mighty civilization. As a result, the Malicae of the modern age has no interest in saving anyone. It only cares for one thing: the rebirth of a malicious Aedir Empire, with the Malicae as its ultimate rulers. Dominion over all, at any cost.
Malicae.scoverview:
The Malicae was formed from the remnants of the once-dominant Aedir Empire. Devastated by the loss of their domain and the death of the Aedir pantheon, the members of this clandestine order have dedicated themselves to restoring the Empire by destroying all that came after it — all while reinstating themselves as the dominant leaders of the land.

As the Maelicae works towards this ultimate end, it accumulates knowledge gained through extensive research and a vast spy network. This disconnected hoard of information is only accessible by those the Malicae deems worthy, and members of the Malicae guard this covert intelligence with their very lives.
Malicae.sgamemaster: The Sunfire Empire of the Aedir once stretched across the world, discovering and settling upon the sun-bathed continent of Kessia long before the Shattering. Great cities arose, and the population exploded over thousands of years. The Aedir colonies paid only lip service to the imperial family on the Starshield. Like the Aedir Empire itself, however, the Shattering devasted the Kessian colonies and they were almost completely destroyed by the formation of the Obsidian Desert. Today the remnants of those colonies call themselves the Nalvani, or the inheritors of the empire, and extremely secretive and reclusive culture that remains hidden from the rest of the world.

Veiled Chain.name: Veiled Chain
Veiled Chain.text:
At its core, the Veiled Chain aims to protect Ordain from threats by investigating problems before they become crises. Its agents are expert fact-finders and investigators hand-picked from the best and brightest the city has to offer. Each member of the chain is expected to be independently effective and resourceful, but also capable of interlinking with the rest of the organization to support any and all operations they have ongoing.

  • Clandestine Operations. The Veiled Chain maintains a roster of highly trained, driven and dedicated agents who go above and beyond to investigate issues, take preemptive action, and ensure the safety of the city. While they are technically still beholden to the Ordinate, not everything the Veiled Chain does reaches their ears, and not everything done would please the Hallows.

  • Proactive Engagement. The Veiled Chain thrives on prediction and preempting problems. While it does spend a large portion of time responding to ongoing issues, it spends just as much time looking into brewing problems that might turn bad. Rather than waiting for disasters to happen, the Chain attempts to stay ahead of issues, catching them before they can threaten the city and its populace.

  • Unbroken Links. Above all else, the Chain's agents are loyal to each other, and their cause of protecting the city from all dangers. This cohesion is vital to not only maintaining the level of secrecy they need to work in the shadows, but ensuring that the agency is capable of working together effectively.

Operations

The Veiled Chain values discretion, resourcefulness, and unwavering loyalty, demanding nothing less than excellence from its agents. Members are expected to act independently, make difficult calls, and do whatever is necessary to shield the city from its gravest threats. Recruitment often begins with adventurers, tested on a trial basis before being offered full membership—though only a select few ever rise to the rank. The true roster of the Chain is known only to its own leadership and a handful of trusted officials, ensuring their work remains shrouded in secrecy.

At its head stands the Chief Investigator, who reports directly to the Hallows and manages the city’s most sensitive cases. Beneath them, senior investigators coordinate networks of field agents and informants, assigning missions and overseeing daily operations. From the shadows, the Chain strikes at corruption, conspiracy, and danger wherever it hides.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.m7bwxaSeiblzYyJw]{Shaar} (Neutral, Ordani Fej, they/them)

The enigmatic head of the Veiled Chain, Shaar has developed a near legendary reputation within the organization as a peerless investigator who never misses a detail. Their careful leadership and dedication to the Chain has earned them the respect and loyalty of every agent that serves under them.

@UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist} (Neutral Good, Tayan Drakon, he/him)

An expatriate from the Tayan empire, Ankarist has become a respected member of the Chain after years of dedicated service. Known for their physical prowess as much as mental, they often handle cases with heightened levels of danger that less sturdy agents avoid. Ankarist is especially good at working independently, and rarely requests active support in the field.

@UUID[Actor.RLFMnPbPwqW4SEKr]{Del Kalais} (Neutral, Ordani Signborn, he/him)

A veteran investigator that has seen more than their share of troubles in Ordain, Del Kalais is admired for their calm demeanor and track record of solving complex cases swiftly. Easygoing yet highly skilled, Del is often assigned to mentor less experienced inspectors and resolve particularly sensitive investigations.
Veiled Chain.scoverview: The Veiled Chain is the clandestine investigative arm of the Hallows, charged with uncovering threats that endanger the city of Ordain from within and without. Its agents are handpicked for loyalty, cunning, and discretion, empowered to pursue crimes and conspiracies that lesser officials dare not touch. They operate in silence, gathering intelligence, infiltrating dangerous circles, and unmasking enemies of the city. With the authority to issue charges and present cases directly to the Hallows, the Veiled Chain is as feared as it is respected.
Veiled Chain.sgamemaster:
The Veiled Chain was born in the hidden conflict later known as the Veiled War, a struggle that nearly tore Ordain apart. What began as simmering resentment against House Komric and its noble allies from Yarino erupted into a shadowy war, fought not with armies but through espionage and assassination. For nearly a year, the city bled quietly in alleys and backrooms while ordinary citizens remained unaware of the scale of the struggle. At the heart of the resistance against the overwhelming power of House Komric was a coalition of ordinary citizens who called themselves the Hallows. To combat the entrenched power of the Komric nobles, they turned to a band of adventurers, skilled in investigation, infiltration, and subterfuge, who became known as the Veiled Chain. Through cunning and relentless strikes, the Chain dismantled Komric's power from within. By the war’s end, House Komric and the old noble families of Yarino were destroyed, their legacies erased.

In the aftermath, both the Hallows and the Veiled Chain solidified into permanent institutions: the Hallows taking on the mantle of Ordain’s moral and judicial authority, and the Chain as their invisible arm of enforcement.

Kirargy Knights.name: Kirargy Knights
Kirargy Knights.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Kirargy Knights.scoverview: The fabled Kirargy Knights are the protectors of the law and defenders of the people of old Caran’ac and, by extension, many now serve the newly established Tayan Empire. They ride various creatures, from ground-based beasts to winged creatures and in extremely rare cases Dragons. These honorable warriors follow a strict code to maintain order even if that means carrying out questionable acts of morality.

The Arcageris.name: The Arcageris
The Arcageris.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
The Arcageris.scoverview: A centralized organization based in the Lowland Bastions, they seek to master the art of Arcing, a martial art designed to imbue physical strikes with cosmic forces. They seek out places of power in the world suffused with energy in order to bring them closer to their idea of the Cosmic Force.

Agrimage Circle.name: Agrimage Circle
Agrimage Circle.text:
Agrimages can be found throughout the Arctus Plateau, within private schools and halls known as Enclaves. Within these halls, knowledge is passed not only through books or scrolls, but also through ritual, craft, and lived experience. Students may spend as much time tending rootbeds or listening to riverstones as they do studying ancient books. The magic taught here is quiet and powerful, woven into tools, into food, into the rhythms of nature itself. Enclaves also serve as sanctuaries during times of strife, offering shelter and guidance to those in need, whether they be wandering travelers, troubled farmers, or young folk called to the old ways.

  • Natural Stewardship: The Circle exists to watch over the Arctus Plateau, treating the land not as something to be used up but as a partner to be respected. Through their practical magic, they help crops grow stronger, keep water clean, and mend the damage left by storms, monsters, or other troubles.

  • Quiet Council: Though not rulers, the Circle shapes the Arcturian people through counsel and quiet influence. They guide festivals, mediate disputes, and serve as anchors of identity, reminding people of who they are and their connection to one another.

  • Regional Unity: Though each Arcturian settlement across the Arctus Plateau is its own distinct community, shaped by local customs, concerns, and needs, it is the Agrimages who serve as the quiet thread weaving them all into a greater whole. While they hold no formal authority, Agrimages are deeply respected in every village, hamlet, and town, often acting as trusted advisors and cultural anchors. Through their guidance, settlements are encouraged to look beyond their borders, recognizing the shared rhythms of the land and the mutual challenges they face. In times of drought, migration, or seasonal shift, it is often the Agrimages who bring local leaders together.

Operations

Across the Arctus Plateau, much of the Agrimages’ work is quietly practical and often unglamorous. They spend their days repairing weather wards that protect settlements from storms, blessing the harvests to ensure bounty, mediating disputes between neighbors, and helping to repair buildings or teaching traditional methods of crafting durable structures and tools. In their quiet Enclaves, elder Agrimages pass on their knowledge to younger students, guiding them in crafts like seed-binding, an art of nurturing tough, dependable crops; storekeeping magic to preserve food and knowledge, and practical enchantment magic, the practice of imbuing everyday tools with a touch of magic to make life easier.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.X2nmQ7Ewt14lSR6g]{Eamon Mariflor} (Lawful Good, Arcturian Keth, he/they)

Eamon is a gentle presence with a sharp mind and a deep love for the land. Known for his intelligence and approachability, Eamon is admired not only in Redrak but across the surrounding Arctus Plateau for his unwavering compassion and his gift for bridging differences between people. He has a calming presence in tense situations, often resolving conflicts with wisdom rather than authority, and is especially beloved by students for his patient, story-rich teaching style and his passion for understanding magic.
Agrimage Circle.scoverview: The Agrimage Circle is an ancient organization of wise folk and practical mages devoted to caring for the Arcturian people and their homeland. Spread across the Arctus Plateau, they live and teach in carefully tended Enclaves, sturdy halls where the old ways of Agrimagic are preserved and passed down. This magic is rooted in common sense, skill, and a deep understanding of the land’s cycles, focusing on crafts such as growing food, preserving resources, and creating practical tools. Though they hold no official power, Agrimages are respected in every settlement, offering guidance through their knowledge and traditions
Agrimage Circle.sgamemaster: In the earliest days on the Arctus Plateau, the people later known as the Arcturians found the region peaceful and full of potential. They settled widely in isolated communities, living carefree. They knew that to preserve their peaceful way of life, they had to connect with the land and safeguard their growing knowledge. The first Agrimages started recording and sharing what various communities learned, traveling between them to exchange ideas. Over generations, the Agrimages established Enclaves, not temples or towers, but solid wooden halls built into hillsides or nestled into local communities, where knowledge was slowly accumulated into vast libraries. From these centers, they trained and taught new students, leaving to advise leaders and help the people through changing seasons and tough times.

Hallows.name: Hallows
Hallows.text:
Of all the great organizations within Ordain, none work harder, or care more deeply, than the Hallows. Composed of thousands of dedicated Ordani, the Hallows is the tireless, subtle heartbeat of the city, ensuring that life runs smoothly for all who call it home. From the humble clerk sorting petitions in an office, to the magistrate presiding over a bustling court, to the countless city inspectors and workers repairing shattered lampposts and crumbling infrastructure, the Hallows never stop working for Ordain.

  • Protectors & Investigators: Whether settling a dispute before it gets out of hand, walking someone home after too much to drink, or fixing a section of loose cobblestone, the Hallows make sure that the city is a good place to live. In those rare times of trouble and disaster they also form and organize first responders and emergency teams to help keep order and preserve lives.

  • Of the People: The Hallows draws its ranks directly from the city’s populace, from bakers and artisans to scholars, dockhands, and masons, reflecting the full spectrum of Ordain’s soul. The organization not only serves the people, it ensures their voices are heard. From managing civic petitions to overseeing Ordain’s public elections, the Hallows safeguards the right of every citizen to shape the city’s future. While some within Ordain see it as little more than a political body, others regard it as a true bastion of freedom, where every hand and every voice can help guide the city’s destiny.

  • Lively & Personal: Since the Hallows recruits from the streets, it is rife with personality and character. It is not uncommon to find a Noticerie or Hallows office doubling as a candy shop or lunch spot, Lookout Posts play music, or offer local youths games or classes, and most every location is decorated with small pieces of the personality and culture of the people assigned there.

Operations

The Hallows operates primarily from its namesake district, where a network of interconnected offices and sprawling chambers manages everything from civic regulation and public safety to law, infrastructure, and business records. It is one of the busiest institutions in Ordain, not only because of the vast number of officials and clerks it employs, but also due to the steady flow of citizens who arrive daily seeking resolutions, permits, or guidance.

Throughout the city, community waystations known as Noticeries or Offices serve as the Hallows’ public face. Staffed by ordinary citizens who proudly display their affiliation, these local volunteers keep residents informed about new laws, civic updates, and neighborhood events, and often provide a place to gather and socialize. Many are based within local establishments such as cafés, taverns, or workshops, while others stand on their own as proud symbols of community life.

While independent, the Veiled Chain operates under the oversight of the Hallows. The two maintain a carefully balanced relationship: the Chain conducts sensitive investigations and intelligence work, while the Hallows ensures those actions remain accountable to the city’s laws and values. Together, they form the quiet foundation of Ordain’s stability.

Key Members

@UUID[Actor.fNQpsNKKmLuYP6H7]{Calin Oren} (Lawful Good, Ordani Altyra, he/him)

Once the brightest star in Ordain’s musical scene, Calin was once a member of House Salva. His performances were legendary, and his charm and ability to communicate with dazzling speeches and oratory make him one of the most recognizable figures in the city. Though he claims to have left the stage behind, every public appearance is still a performance; his words are perfectly timed, his smile as dangerous as it is mesmerizing. To the people of Ordain, he is a beloved and admired scion, yet those closest to him whisper that behind the glamour and the gilded charm lies a calculating mind that knows precisely how to strike the right note to keep the city dancing to his tune.

@UUID[Actor.yUmnUZcCut8tTH5B]{Okia Tyrwar} (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

Okia comes from a long line of clerics of the Radiant Eye, and her grandmother was also the high priestess during her time. She was raised in Sunhaven and has dedicated her life to worshipping Lantyr, becoming one of the temple's most outspoken figures in recent memory. Her leadership is marked by deep ties to the traditions of both Kessian and Ordani cultures, but she believes that the vast majority of the population is far too lax in their veneration of the gods and of Lantyr herself, seeing the recent troubles and increasingly turbulent times as a consequence of their inaction. She is ardently passionate about her followers taking measures to enact change and to help others, and her rousing speeches have reached beyond Sunhaven and into the city population as a whole, which recently led to her being elected by the Hallows to a seat on the Ordinate itself.

@UUID[Actor.i5jXHUyZCPBJDb2k]{Mistress Caberi} (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

Mistress Caberi is a warm, friendly seamstress often surrounded by bolts of luxurious cloth, textiles in vibrant colors, and a small following of adoring fans. Her fame is so widespread that she has become a member of the Ordanite after being elected by the Hallows and through her connections with House Salva, and although she is not technically a member of the house, she is so closely connected that she might as well be. She welcomes all who enter her quaint shop in Gossamar with a radiant smile, where the aroma of fresh clean fabric mingles with soft laughter and cheerful conversations about the latest trends in Ordain. With her nimble fingers, she weaves magical threads of various hues, crafting exquisite and unique pieces of clothing for the city's most passionate fashionistas.
Hallows.scoverview: The Hallows is one of three major arms of the Ordinate, who see themselves as the city’s unseen custodians, the hands that build, mend, and move all that keeps Ordain thriving. From the masons and engineers who raise its towers, to the city inspectors who enforce its edicts, to the unseen eyes of the Veiled Chain who they oversee, every layer of Ordani life is touched by the Hallows’ influence. Yet beneath this veneer of public service lies something older and more calculating. They manage chaos with a craftsman’s precision, subtly steering the city’s fortunes while others take the credit. Their leadership, composed of shrewd magistrates and silver-tongued orators, maintains a delicate balance between the piety of the Cindaric Sages and the greed of the Trading Houses.
Hallows.sgamemaster:
The Hallows began over seven centuries ago as an armed resistance of ordinary Ordani citizens who rose against the tyranny of House Komric and the old nobility of Yarino. Tired of exploitation and manipulation, farmers, laborers, and scholars alike took up arms to remove the blatant corruption that was infecting their city. For two grueling years, they fought in the shadows to weaken, disrupt, and destroy House Komric interests. In the aftermath, the victors faced a profound question: what should become of the city they had bled to free?

Rejecting the greed and cruelty of those they had overthrown, the leaders of the Hallows chose to share power rather than hoard it. From that decision was born the Ordinate, a tripartite government composed of the Hallows, the Trading Houses, and the Cindaric Sages, each balancing the other to preserve the city’s future. Though centuries have passed and the Hallows is a peaceful organization, it remains the voice of the people and the safeguard of Ordain’s freedom.

Ordinate.name: Ordinate
Ordinate.text:
The Ordinate is the ruling council of Ordain, a nine-member body responsible for shaping the city’s laws, policies, and long-term vision. It stands as the final arbiter in disputes too large or complex for any single organization to resolve.
