While many of the city’s major powers, such as the Trading Houses, the Cindaric Sages, or the Anachraenum, manage their internal affairs autonomously, matters that cross boundaries or affect the city as a whole ultimately fall under the Ordinate’s jurisdiction. These include trade tariffs, infrastructure, and city-wide budget allocations, public health initiatives, and the maintenance of civic harmony.

  • Balance of Power: The Ordinate is divided evenly among three factions: the Cindaric Sages, the Trading Houses, and the Hallows, each holding three seats on the council. This balance prevents any one interest from overwhelming the others. The Trading Houses push for economic freedom and prosperity; the Hallows advocate for fairness, labor rights, and the will of the people; and the Cindaric Sages act as a moral and intellectual counterweight, emphasizing the greater good and long-term stability. Though this structure promotes debate and compromise, it also fosters rivalry and maneuvering behind the scenes as each faction seeks to guide policy to its advantage.

  • Advisory Groups: While only the nine seated members possess voting rights, several advisory groups exert significant influence over the Ordinate’s decisions. Representatives from the Anachraenum, the Burnished Hand, and the Veiled Chain are often invited to consult on specialized matters—ranging from arcane discovery to defense, intelligence, and security. As these groups have influence over their members and those around them, they are also asked to help enforce whatever new rules have been established within the areas where they hold power or sway.

  • The Will of the People: Ordain’s citizens place deep trust in the Ordinate, viewing it as the living embodiment of their collective will. Once a ruling is made, compliance is swift and rarely contested; communities often take it upon themselves to ensure adherence without the need for force. For those who knowingly defy an edict, however, the Hallows serve as both judge and executor of the city’s justice. For those who are unaware of a change, or unwilling to abide by it, they may be taken in hand by the organization they belong to, or judged by the Hallows if they knowingly break a rule, though violation for violation's sake is rare.

Operations

The Ordinate functions through a sprawling network of clerks, recordkeepers, and stewards who manage the daily flow of petitions, reports, and proposals from across the city. Every week, the Ordinate council convenes within the Ordinate, a vast marble chamber at the heart of Ordain, to debate, draft, and vote upon laws. These meetings are public by tradition, with citizens permitted to observe from the gallery—though the most sensitive discussions occur in private sessions known as Closed Deliberations.

When a proposal reaches the Ordinate floor, it passes through a three-stage process: Presentation, where the case is argued; Review, during which evidence and testimony are heard; and Judgment, where the nine members cast their votes. In the event of a stalemate, the Speaker of the Ordinate, chosen by unanimous agreement at the start of each term, is granted a deciding vote.

Once a ruling is ratified, it is disseminated throughout the city via the Hallows’ network of Noticeries, as well as through public orators and scribed bulletins. Enforcement is coordinated jointly between the Hallows and the organization most affected by the ruling—be it the Trading Houses, the Cindaric Sages, or another civic body.

Key Members

The Ordinate’s nine seats are currently held by a blend of visionaries, pragmatists, and schemers whose influence shapes the fate of Ordain. While each represents their own faction, alliances within the chamber shift as often as the city’s tides. Recently, the newest members include @UUID[Actor.yztzqRozoEkbiO2K]{Katerin Bastilla}, who took over from Ralton Cevher, and @UUID[Actor.yUmnUZcCut8tTH5B]{Okia Tyrwar}, who won an election against @UUID[Actor.UEN4Lxa3qDqOAS5B]{Conaris Haid} and @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver }who replaced @UUID[Actor.LxNdaYC9hKg9QSZN]{Jonico Daridane}.

Ordinate.scoverview: The Great City of Ordain has three pillars of power — the Trading Houses, the Cindaric Sages, and the Hallows. The Ordinate is the public body of leadership that works to balance these groups and give each of them a say in keeping Ordain strong, stable, and sustainable. Made up of nine members — three from each of the major pillars — it is their job to deal with citywide policy, including major changes to laws, policy, and budget.
Ordinate.sgamemaster:
The Ordinate was born out of turmoil. In the aftermath of the Veiled War, a shadowy conflict that pitted the noble House Komric against the citizen coalition known as the Hallows, Ordain was left leaderless and fractured. The old noble families of Yarino lay in ruin, their stranglehold on the city broken, but the question of who would rebuild its governance remained.

In the wake of victory, the Hallows called for sweeping reform. Their leaders, recognizing that absolute rule by any one faction would only invite future corruption, proposed a new system: a tripartite council that would balance civic duty, commerce, and faith. Thus, the Ordinate was formed, composed of three representatives each from the Hallows, the Cindaric Sages, and the city’s Trading Houses.

It was during these early negotiations that Captain Red Bastilla, famed privateer, returned to Ordain at the head of her fleet. Docking her flagship, Ember’s Bounty, in the city’s harbor, she demanded formal recognition for her efforts and a seat within the new order. After a tense debate, her claim was honored, and House Bastilla was founded, cementing the Trading Houses’ influence within the Ordinate and ensuring that the city’s maritime power would never again be overlooked.

Star Mages.name: Star Mages
Star Mages.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Star Mages.scoverview: The Star Mages of Rhivan are an incredibly famous organization that is renowned across not only the known world but far beyond it as well. They have traveled and explored some of the most distant places in the cosmos but are often limited by their lack of full members who only number in the hundreds. A Star Mage is not a typical wizard, sorcerer, or arcanist but a learned academic studying a specialized magical philosophy. This strict focus and commitment grants Star Mages impressive abilities and far greater power over magic than other magic users.

Warded Blades.name: Warded Blades
Warded Blades.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Warded Blades.scoverview: The Warded Blades are a powerful warrior class of the Wardcall, strictly defined by moral codes and firm resolve. They defend towering fortress holdouts in the cold northern realms and refuse to fight one another; instead, they are principled guardians who protect against the Vartic shapeshifters. Their members are extremely rare outside of the Wardcall kingdoms, but occasionally, they may be seen hunting shapeshifters and upholding their own personal honor through combat.

Moiran Warders.name: Moiran Warders
Moiran Warders.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Moiran Warders.scoverview: Moiran Warders were once a group of skilled and knowledgeable defenders of the Moiran Kingdom, but after the events of the Evernight, they now live in exile in various places across the world, specifically the Lumek and Cascilian cultures. They practice a unique method of archery that weaves innate magic into bows and arrows, enhancing their skills and power to deal devastating long-range attacks. They are a small, rare group of stalwart fighters that pass their techniques down from generation to generation and have a burning hatred for undeath and the Blood Barons that took over their homeland. They are also the direct followers of the Shard God Thayloc and have a fanatical, unwavering belief in his cause.

Primalists.name: Primalists
Primalists.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Primalists.scoverview: The Primalists are an ancient druidic organization that resides within the Corebright Forest. They are deeply tied to the Strider culture, but unlike the Striders, the Primalists become one with the natural world around them by transforming into animals, creatures, or beasts, and spend most of their lives safeguarding the wilds and nature itself. They rarely come together to achieve a common purpose other than their overarching goal of defending the forest, but they sometimes venture beyond their borders to seek out natural knowledge.

Vanguard.name: Vanguard
Vanguard.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Vanguard.scoverview: The Vanguard is a somewhat secretive organization that vehemently opposes the Tayan Empire. Many of its members are exiled Tayan citizens, including many Kirargy Knights, Drakon who fled the empire, and various powerful figures who have banded together to slow or stop the Tayan Empire's ceaseless advances. They also believe that the Tayan Empire is sinister or malicious in some way and that some darker purpose is fueling their power and ambition.

Muzseri.name: Muzseri
Muzseri.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Muzseri.scoverview: The Muzseri, are a mythical order of warriors who hail from a remote mountain temple said to hang over the edge of the world. They are powerful guardians of order and justice who, with rigorous training and intensive self-discipline, mold their strength of will and spirit into physical weapons. These manifest as long blades of white-hot fire and they are capable of impressive feats of stamina and agility. They avoid violence except as a last resort, often trying to find alternative solutions before fighting. They are exceptionally rare outside of Mazira and are largely unknown across the world.

Flame Guard.name: Flame Guard
Flame Guard.text:
Operations

Within the Flame Guard, which is the principal organization responsible for the protection of the Lumek, there are a number of ranks depending on experience and skill. The Flame Guard is not composed solely of warriors. It includes healers, engineers, fire-mages, scouts, and even farmers trained to defend their settlements with torches and Lumarin steel blades. It embodies the unified front of Lumek culture: everyone contributes, and all roles are vital. In the eyes of Lumé, there is no "lesser" sacrifice.

High Command

Pyre Lord

Commander of the Flame, the supreme leader of the Flame Guard. Oversees all crusades against the undead. Wields ancient relics of fire and is a close personal friend with Lumé.

High Command

Marshal

Responsible for strategy, alliances, and the coordination of Flame Guard in the Lumek Homelands.

Senior Officers

Flamebearer

An elite rank given to seasoned warriors or mages. Blessed directly by Lumé. Often sent on solo missions to destroy undead strongholds or targets deep within the Moiran Lands.

Senior Officers

Captain

Commands multiple Fireteams. Leads major offensives against vampire strongholds and undead hordes within the Moiran Lands.

Junior Officers

Cinder Warden

Leaders of the various smaller forts, keeps, or defensive placements in the Ash Peaks.

Junior Officers

Redcloak

Leads small units in battles or missions. Usually oversees a Fireteam.

Soldiers

Crusader

Veteran soldier or spellcaster. Trusted in battle and often assigned special tasks or front-line leadership.

Soldiers

Torchbearer

Newly promoted soldier. Carries the literal and symbolic torch into battle. Often assigned to defensive duties or patrols.

Soldiers

Firebrand

Fanatical, untrained members who often throw themselves into the front lines.

Trainees

Ashrunner

Scouts and soldiers in training that are often used for carrying messages in battle.

Key Members
Flame Guard.scoverview: The Flame Guard serves as the sword and shield of Lumek society, a sacred order of warriors devoted to the eternal war against undeath. Guided by the divine will of Lumé, its members stand as both soldiers and stewards, defending the Firelands and Homelands. Between the devastating Cycles of Fire and Death, the Flame Guard rebuilds, trains, and prepares for the next great assault, their unity and faith binding them as tightly as their steel. To the Lumek, the Guard is more than an army; it is the embodiment of survival, sacrifice, and divine purpose.

Silver Beam Consortium.name: Silver Beam Consortium
Silver Beam Consortium.text:
In @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen} the Silver Beam C0nsortium are a formidable enterprise, and in many ways on-par with the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani} Trade Houses from@UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} in terms of influence and financial might. Their offices are vast, and they oversee a broad set of activities ranging from transport, farming, construction, and mining. They employ large numbers of people, and over the last century have begun opening subsidiary branches across the known world.

Scope of Operations

Beyond the numerous industries that the Silver Beam Consortium carries out in Railen, it has the following notable endeavors underway beyond its home country:

  • Mining and transport operations in the Kelmezian borders.

  • Extensive logging operations in the Last Grove near Nasjar.

  • Logging, trapping, and surveying in the Southern @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ntef4M02D50Y8BlE]{Corebright Forest}, specially around the Zancol expanse.

  • Fishing operations in the Restless Bay, as well as in the numerous lakes in and around the Border Heathlands.

  • Farming and ranching operations in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Rg25PSayVhEQEpNe]{Cascaal} Golds, partially subsidized by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} government as a part of an agricultural revitalization program.

  • Fishing in the Golden Bay and along the shores of the Cascaal Peninsula.

  • Rare plant harvesting in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ESzK0uQM5ZsL6o0i]{Duskflare Jungles} with the tenuous blessing of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd}.

The Arcturel Branch

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel} office is headed by @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth}, an @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen} noblewoman who ascended to prominence in both the city and the Silver Beam ranks after her husband met his untimely demise. Rumors abound that his death was orchestrated to her benefit, but Larissa has been careful to make sure no proof exists to make such claims stick.
Silver Beam Consortium.scoverview: Established in the far-flung lands of Aran Peninsula, the Silver Beam Consortium is a major name in the luminous city of Ancalen and a major part of the Railen culture. They began as a small mining company, but quickly and aggressively expanded into other fields, consuming merchants and mining stakes and trade caravans as they went.
Silver Beam Consortium.sgamemaster: Barely a year old, this operation is the newest of the Silver Beam branches, and is one that is not expected to succeed. Its creation was ordered by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.illZO15u6gbz338u]{Pyix}, and it was established with the express intend to destabilize the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}, gain access to Inkaro Pearls, and develop trust with the dragon@UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.v6lXjfETDkrt0J7E]{Zerranyss}.

The First Dawn.name: The First Dawn
The First Dawn.text:
Lore Summary

The First Dawn is the first and longest eon of the Ember Cosmos; the period is sometimes referred to as the Creation or the Longest Age, and it includes not only the beginning of the Cosmos but also the formation and creation of many of the first life forms across the Inner Realms, Moons, and the surface world.

  • Cosmic Creation: Formation of the Inner Realms, the Elemental Moons, the World of Ember, and the protective barrier of the Weave.

  • Elders: The Emergence of the Elder Gods, Alar, Spectra, Ven'avé, Sockets, and Lantyr.

  • The First Life: The arrival of elemental spirits, primitive plants, and terrestrial animals.

  • Early Sapience: The first sapient species, the Xaxin on one side and the Theroch on the other side of the World of Ember.

The First Dawn is a period of the world that is almost entirely unknown and rarely considered or discussed among the mortals of Ember. Anyone discussing or attempting to describe events during Creation should be treated with the highest degree of doubt and scrutiny, as their statements are likely fiction. A few older, more established cultures are aware of certain pivotal events, yet there may be contradictory information, with numerous creationary myths they believe are part of their religious or spiritual beliefs.

Some of the only real facts of the period include the idea that the First Dawn is when the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} itself coalesced, giving birth to the Inner Realms and forming the Elemental Moons, and eventually the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}. It was during this expansion that the protective Barrier of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{the Weave} first rippled outward, acting as a cosmic shield to protect the newborn reality from the hostile, alien energies beyond. During this period, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{Ven'avé}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr}, manifested, establishing the metaphysical laws that would govern existence.

As the Cosmos stabilized, the first flickers of life began to stir. Primitive @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Tl4gvmUGThkZdrUd]{elemental} spirits and strange lunar creatures appeared first, followed by the emergence of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} and their celestial kin on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nXYB7d7ZBsWV1chY]{fiends} on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia} and Fey within the wild forests of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}. On the surface of Ember, life blossomed from simple flora into a complex ecosystem, with simple creatures and animals. Eventually, the long silence of the world was broken by the rise of the first, sentient and sapient mortal ancestries, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Eze09wAxj7pf7VZd]{Xaxin} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.186yO79YKDxPh0qT]{Theroch}, who emerged on opposite sides of the world.

Few know of the first peoples of Ember; by luck, design, or some other blessing. Both were two different flavors of poison, and we have thankfully stripped them of their power over this world long ago.

~Laeora
The First Dawn.scoverview: The First Dawn, known also as Creation, is both a singular event and a lasting period of time. So expansive and distant are the events that took place in ages long past that they are beyond the knowledge and memory of even the oldest of mortal ancestries. Some of the eldest beings in the Cosmos, such as the Elder Gods and Elemental Sovereigns, came into being during this time, but their memories are hazy and clouded by the vast number of years that have passed since.

Age of Beasts.name: Age of Beasts
Age of Beasts.text:
Lore Summary

The Age of Beasts was an era of Ember'sHistroy that lasted for hundreds of thousands of years and saw the rise of some of the largest, most primal beasts and animals, in addition to some of the older mortal ancestries.

  • Primordial Creatures: Emergence of the Leviathans as the dominant lifeform on the surface of Ember.

  • Mortal Ancestries: The Creation of the Co'ark, Jarn, Giants, Varak, Vrjnhar, Saurvek, Ashka, Carrow, Leafia, Zeph, and Wirrun.

  • Ascendants: The first Shard Gods arise after communing with Heart Crystals buried in the world.

The Age of Beasts is so far removed from the memories of mortal ancestries alive today that it may as well be fiction. So much of the history is entirely unknown, and while some of the earliest cultures arose during this time, almost nothing is known about their struggles. These cultures and corresponding ancestries are thought to have created and maintained vast kingdoms and nations of their own. Still, this period was so extraordinarily long that almost everything has been lost, buried, or crumbled into nothing. There remains a few ancient stories, sagas, creationary myths, and legends that are told of this age, handed down through countless generations, but most cannot be verified for accuracy or truth.
Age of Beasts.scoverview: The Age of Beasts was a primordial era that followed The First Dawn. The World of Ember was an untamed, wild, and dangerous place, dominated by the Leviathans, raging elementals, primal creatures, and the earliest known ancestries. The creative essence of the Heart of Ember produced a dazzling array of beings during this time, and large megafauna was so common the surface shook with their every step and clashes for territory.
Age of Beasts.sgamemaster:
The Age of Beasts was long in the history of the world, taking place over several hundred thousand years. It was a primal time that still echoed with the Lifeforce of creation. This energy created new ancestries and creatures at first with explosive variety, great creatures and small, and then over time, this process slowed. Some creatures died out and were lost forever, while others changed over time to adapt to different environments. Others were changed again and again by the creative energy and became something new. The Age was dominated by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans}, whose arrival or creation heralded the beginning of the period. These creatures exploded outwards from the continent of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.dm5FW6EbHBGhJweI]{Jurin} and claimed large territories across the World of Ember. It's said that Leviathans were so numerous during this time that it was not unusual to see them living more harmoniously together in great packs or herds. At some point during this age, the Leviathans were curtailed and confined within Jurin, and after countless conflicts with each other and the emerging @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} and ancestries, their number dwindled.

During this prehistoric era, the mortal ancestry known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.V1gzeX0JWSOCQ7LD]{Jarn} appeared in the Aran Peninsula. The Jarn were not particularly strong, they were not especially fast, they could not soar towards the heavens, nor could they burrow into the earth - but of all the creatures of Ember, the Jarn were clever, resourceful, and aware. The Jarn crafted tools and built dwellings and settlements, eventually becoming the progenitor species of many other ancestries across the World of Ember. As the Age of Beasts came to a close, many of the peoples known today had settled into shapes, sizes, and forms that suited them best or had been gifted to them by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} or their Gods. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Ni'rae} were brought to the Starshield by their creator, who eventually founded the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} culture. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.0YvoRkcs1BxtRiQz]{Vrjnhar} arrived upon the inhospitable continent of Oakengarde and began their long, grueling struggle to survive. Many other ancestries and cultures were said to have arisen during this time as well, including the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.blm7nVaaSYLZX3C9]{Cor'ak}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.PYCLsQgKclg5toxT]{Wirrun} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.eyvVaX4c1rMos0ws]{Zeph}.

The Primitive Gods

It is unclear when this first occurred, but as Ember's fledging ancestors began to spread across the world, they encountered @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystals} for the first time. It’s thought that the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.V1gzeX0JWSOCQ7LD]{Jarn} were the first to ascend, with some claiming that @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae} was the first ever @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God} to exist in Ember. As time passed, other Jarn discovered Heart Crystals through intrepid curiosity or random happenstance. Taming the power within was exceptionally rare. However, over time, the first Pantheon of divine beings who walked the surface of Ember emerged and wielded power that allowed them to remake the world and its creatures as they desired. These early Shard Gods contained far more power and strength of Lifeforce than Shard Gods that arose later. This enabled them to achieve extraordinary feats, such as changing large groups of creatures into desired shapes and forms so that they could survive in distant, varied environments.

Age of the Tower.name: Age of the Tower
Age of the Tower.text:
Lore Summary

The Age of the Tower, also known as the Age of Sunlight, was an era in Ember's history that lasted tens of thousands of years and saw the rise of the first global empire, the Aedir. The Aedir explored most of the surface world and even traveled into the Sea of Stars, eventually building the colossal Sun Tower at the center of the Starshield continent. It was also the period when cultures, peoples, and ancestries began to interact with one another in more meaningful ways, resulting in collaboration, alliances, but also major conflicts and wars.

  • Mortal Ancestries: The Creation of the Aedir, Fej, Thornlings, Hulg'run, and Humans.

  • Global Conflict: The first global conflict occurred between the Aedir and the Theroch. This conflict spread and involved many deities, cultures, and peoples, and even involved forces from the Cosmos, such as the Tyraphem and the Wyrms of Akon.

The Age of Tower was the period in which the Sunfire Empire of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} reigned over nearly all of Ember and wrought great wonders across the world. They established a near-universal dominant culture and a dynastic empire of scholarship, arcane supremacy, and technological mastery.

This age of the world is shrouded in mystery, myth, and legend. Still, many of the details and specific events were once meticulously recorded and documented by the Aedir and some other cultures active at the time. This means that ancient scrolls and tomes found in crumbling ruins may speak in detail about the Age of Tower and the majesty and power of the Aedir; such treasures are priceless to collectors and historians.
Age of the Tower.scoverview: The Age of the Tower was the era of time that saw the blinding rise of the Aedir upon the central continent of the Starshield. The Aedir were also known by many as the Sunfire Empire, reigning supreme across nearly every continent of the world, constructing cities, colonies, and outposts to claim and oversee vast territories. Their crowning achievement was the construction of the colossal Sun Tower upon the Starshield, which is said to have taken nearly six thousand years to complete. The Age ended with the cataclysmic destruction of the Aedir and the Sun Tower in an event known as the Shattering.
Age of the Tower.sgamemaster:
The Age of Sunlight took place over roughly twenty-five thousand years, and some say it began with the settling of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae} upon the central continent of the Starshield. Others believe the age began when the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giants} emerged from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} after an event known as the Unveiling. It was a distinctive period that saw the rise of incredible feats of progress, technology, and magic, and cultures worldwide began constructing massive structures and settlements and experimenting with new concepts and ideas. The wilderness and dominance of nature and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans} were pushed further and further back into the deeper reaches of the world, but they were never truly extinguished or removed. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} often found themselves combating primal creatures and battling Leviathans for territory as they expanded. This is perhaps why the primary reason the Aedir began establishing a greater and more powerful military over time. Something that made little sense in the context of the world at that time, as the Aedir had very few primary competitors or rivals. Unfortunately, as their viewpoint changed, many believe the Aedir culture overall and its government structures became much more aggressive, complacent, and overbearing.

Most, if not all, cultures of this age underwent significant cultural change over time, switching government types, experiencing periods of growth and collapse, and even infighting or civil unrest that reorganized how they thought about the world. The Aedir were not an Empire in the traditional sense for many thousands of years but after the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4v37uAs6nY1Pc00M]{Forsaken War} they became much more aggressive in their attempts to master and control their colonies and territories beyond the Starshield. This was also when the Aedir began the construction of the Sun Tower, using the mountain peaks at the very center of the world on the Starshield as a base. The construction was an unimaginable challenge and cultural commitment, but its thought its principal architects were the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.wWvTZjC2103uKJsc]{Aedir Pantheon} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} and not a mortal design.

The Shattering

Eventually, however, the Aedir Sunfire Empire was at its height, and the Sun Tower was complete. Many records suggest that the Sun Tower was complete for several centuries before the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}, but others say that the Shattering occurred as soon as the final piece was placed upon the tallest point. The Shattering was not only a cataclysmic event of unbelievable power, magnitude, and destruction, but also the point at which the Age of Sunlight ended and the Aedir were annihilated, never to recover again.

Age of Rediscovery.name: Age of Rediscovery
Age of Rediscovery.text:
Lore Summary

The Age of Rediscovery is the era following the Shattering and the Abyssal Shear, marked by the slow rebuilding of many surviving cultures and peoples in a changed, far more dangerous world. Much of the history immediately after the Abyssal Shear is shrouded in lost records, chaos, and desperation, but over time, nations and kingdoms begin to rebuild and flourish, rediscovering knowledge of the Aedir and other ancient cultures.

  • Mortal Ancestries: The creation of the Kiska, Keth*, Kivahr* & Drakon.

  • Human Expansion: Much like the ancient Aedir, Human ancestry has spread across much of the known surface world on the continent of Aterica, founding many diverse kingdoms and nations. These include cultures of the Tayans, Moirans, Cascilians, Arcturians, Ordani, and Kessians.

* The creation of both the Keth and Kivahr may have occurred just before the Shattering.

Roughly two and half thousand years have passed since the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{Shattering}, and in the years following, destruction, chaos, and death on a large scale affected nearly every existing culture and ancestry. Every single @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} colony overseas from the Starshield fell. Its peoples either fled or were destroyed, and only a few cultures remained intact and rode out the storm of darkness and the emergence of monsters. The early @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} peoples, made up primarily of Humans, resisted the onslaught, as did the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken}, who were spared much of the destruction due to their already tenacious nature. The young ancestors of the Keth and Kivahr, who had only recently founded cultures such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak}, miraculously escaped unscathed. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} who had existed in the center of Aterica, living across the spine of Ember, were also utterly destroyed. Only a few of its people escaped the cataclysm and now either live in isolation in hidden remote settlements or joined the defiant Varún culture.

Many@UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{ Leviathans}, who had claimed much of the world since the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}, were also affected and killed by the emerging monsters and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons} or forced from their ancient territories. Some remained, but these beings were perhaps the strongest, largest, and most dangerous of their kind, and most Leviathan survivors remain unchallenged by mortals even today.

The Shattering saw the death of countless @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods}, including the entire pantheon of the Aedir. Many Shard Gods were confronted by monsters and dragons after the events of the Shattering itself and were hard-pressed to resist. Those caught alone without aid often fell to the darkness and chaos that swallowed the world during that time. Shard God families or pantheons managed to survive more easily, such as the family of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla}.

Most cultures and nations agree that the time period after the shattering is the beginning of a new age. Many proposed names are suggested, such as the Age of Rediscovery or the Age of Humanity, but some scholars insist that the world now resides in the shadow of the Broken Tower and thus should be named the Age of Shadow.

One of the most devastating early consequences of the Shattering was the emergence of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.zaLrsSK495BEAUki]{monsters}. Monsters is a broad term that encapsulates a wide variety of horrific and terrifying foes that eagerly dug their way into the fabric of the world. So omnipresent have monsters become that cultures in the present are always on guard against overwhelming forces that seek to destroy them. In some cases, this has destroyed entire realms and peoples throughout the current age, including perhaps most famously, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} nation, which became consumed by undeath and created the Blood Barons. The emergence of Dragons is included within the monster category in many ways. Beings of such overwhelming strength and fury that they caused the death of Shard Gods and smashed apart nations, such was the case with the Oderita Kingdom, which fell to @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l2UZCjkk0lRAlcTZ]{Karaxsus} the Flaming Dread.

Today, most of the younger kingdoms, nations, and cultures of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica} and @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia} are still expanding, growing, and spreading throughout the world. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Humans} are often the driving force of these realms, but they are not alone in their ability to adapt and overcome the ever-present dangers and challenges of the world. The most impressive example is the rapidly advancing @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire}, which in the last seventy-two years has conquered and seized lands from the Vathar Forests across the Crossing Sea in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Mazira} and began its conquest of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} city-states in the south. While Humans are often seen as responsible for expansion, this is a narrow viewpoint, and many other ancestries are both welcomed and critical to the success of human-dominated cultures. In some cultures and nations, humans may be the largest single group, but other ancestries combined make up a far greater percentage of the population. They are often instrumental in presenting diverse viewpoints that fuel further expansion, and the idea that Humans alone are responsible for growth is laughable. There are many other dynamic and expanding cultures that are not human-dominated, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.xImbz6Nf4mMxtKF1]{Wardcall} Kingdoms of Kivahr, The Jaedith Dominion of Kiska, The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.y4WHE3TEr6Of13SL]{Railen} of Altyra, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerds} of Signborn. Overall, the world is still recovering from the Shattering in many different ways, and there remains countless opportunities for nations, organizations, and even individuals to strike out into wilder and untamed or lost regions to found new kingdoms and recover lost knowledge.
Age of Rediscovery.scoverview: Around two and a half thousand years have passed since the events of the Shattering. The World of Ember is now in a period of great change as the Human ancestry extends further and further, discovering new lands and founding new cultures and kingdoms. Monsters are now a permanent part of the cosmos, as is the threat of Undeath and terror of Dragons. The newer and rising cultures of Ember has much to learn from the hubris of the Aedir, and there are countless lost ruins, relics, and secrets to discover but the world today is perhaps more dangerous and hostile than ever before.
Age of Rediscovery.sgamemaster:
The World of Ember is home to many different ancestries and cultures, but overall the focus of recorded events and history is on the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica} continent. There are many other cultures and even entirely different ancestries living in more distant realms, but these are generally not highlighted because of the lack of knowledge regarding their existence by those on Aterica.

Timeline

[[/date AS20]]

The island city of Crown is settled on a lush rainforest island of Vita’ri south-east of the Aran Peninsula by the legendary High King @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.YNMxNE2TbhObyKMp]{Fenra Ordragon}.

[[/date AS110]]

The foundation of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} nation as Humans migrate across the shallow water of the Folded Sea. The people find a lush forested realm that borders the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Homelands to the south, and the two peoples quickly become friends.

[[/date AS272]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.hbO7NeNeouXYkx9t]{Virulent Plague} erupts across the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.NdqwtFoFAw85Gstr]{Aran Peninsula}, and humans are especially affected, dying in droves as the disease rips apart cities and turns some into echoing ruins. Ghostly undead arise and complete the decimation of the region.

[[/date AS869]]

Without warning, a being of ancient power emerges from the Pathways, and the sheltered, peaceful capital of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} is annihilated, along with most of the region around it, creating the Moiran Bonelands. This event is known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.Q59ZUVNaeBoZl9nJ]{Evernight} as a permanent night falls over the Moiran lands, and undeath runs rampant, turning thousands into monsters. The Blood Barons are formed around this time as well.

[[/date AS902]]

Fury of Fire -@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{ Lumé} takes control of the Lumek, apparently murdering her mother, the Goddess Naor, in a disagreement over the fate of their people. Lumé then holds the undead's advance to the north, and the cycles of Fire & Death begin.

[[/date AS1234]]

Heracas the Mage discovers portal magic and construction begins on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} Academy in the far southwest of the World of Ember.

[[/date AS1716]]

Refugees from the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{ Kelmezian} city of Yarino cross a vast stretch of the Yawning Sea, eventually discovering the far eastern edge of the Arctus Plateau and settling the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, and forming the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}.

[[/date AS1722]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Blood Barons} attempt to invade the Corebright Forest led by Kira Hetanya. In a stunning display of capability, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Striders} destroy the force utterly and halt any advances into the area. No attempt to move into the Corebright Forest by the Blood Barons has been made since.

[[/date AS1734]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} arrive in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, establishing ties with the city and forming the Burnished Hand as an organization that combats monsters and threats.

[[/date AS1958]]

The Dustlands and the Burial Plains form in the southern Arctus Plateau after the unhinged wizard Leatic attempts to commune with Akon and brings forth an infestation of machines that decimate the nearby biomes.

[[/date AS2215]]

Summer of Blood - The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian} city states erupt in protest and revolution, openly attacking sorcerers, wizards and mages of all kinds. The Shard God Mendal is torn apart in the streets of Alavai in a rare example of a group of mortals killing an ascended deity. The Cascilian Republic forms in the aftermath.

[[/date AS2234]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.B987VijfeT6i9TEI]{Aythorn} appears in the Western edges of the Tayan empire as an ascended Shard God for the first time. They then begin to build a small group of loving followers that constantly surround them.

[[/date AS2245]]

Coral Prison is constructed in the large bay north of the Yanwing Sea. Its main purpose is to hold and contain mages of all kinds. It quickly becomes a site of undeniable horror that the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian Republic} actively hides from the public.

[[/date AS2320]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mages} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} establish a gate in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} connecting Ordain to the Arcanic Portal Network, or APN. This act affirms Ordain’s status as one of the world's Great Cities.

[[/date AS2419]]

The City of Ash falls to the undead in a stunning loss for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, hope seems lost until a host of Shard Gods from@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{ the Nineteen} including @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Hw10ll6tklqdzaXt]{Vekalla} arrive to push the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Blood Barons} back in an event known as the Tides of Rain. The relationship between @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KkM8FZKL2R3whKEQ]{Raineka} becomes openly discussed among the population in the aftermath.

[[/date AS2427]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} ruins are unearthed in the eastern Cascaal Golds close to the Runa Highlands causing a treasure seeking boom in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian Republic}.

[[/date AS2436]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascilian Republic} miners and explorers trespass upon the Varun Highlands and caused a massive incursion by enraged @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Z8Nm4rnjqG3BJHSd]{Varún} Berserkers. The city of Caxko is sacked, but a small holdout protects the majority of the city's hidden populace until relief arrives.

[[/date AS2439]]

The hive of gang violence and villainy in the Great City of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.qkFDffiLfGCd0RCs]{Sphere} spills over, and the Red Hammers gang attacks and destroys the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mage} Portal Gate. This plunges the Sphere into chaos and disorder.

[[/date AS2446]]

The destruction of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} city Korma by the dragon Fiharax causes a period of cultural fervor among the people and a temporary truce is announced in order to hunt down the monster and slay it.

[[/date AS2451]]

The royal house of Caran’ac is assassinated amidst the murder of nobility and the ruling class in a night of blood and chaos. The @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.Fze49xRKzbsO5qNq]{Night of Swords} results in the formation of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire} and the crowning of @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l5SNwXC8t3Qp3Ut3]{Calyn Kariset}. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.GRs2vgeVsDpWPqjh]{Drakon} emerge as a new ancestry in the aftermath as well.

[[/date AS2454]]

A @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Z8Nm4rnjqG3BJHSd]{Varún} Moonwalker appears in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} city of Luen, and the cult of the Blooded Sky forms around her teachings in secret.

[[/date AS2455]]

A new @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan} is discovered on the southern shores of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Homelands. Its two-legged gait is ponderous and slow, but its thick hide and great oversized maw make it ideally suited for the harsh conditions of the peninsula. It also appears relatively docile towards mortals.

[[/date AS2458]]

The Shard God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.cVcA9liudzvcYgZc]{Lorex} ascends in Kessia after finding a long-rumored Heart Crystal hidden in the Pathways of the Obsidian Desert.

[[/date AS2494]]

The twin children of the Shard Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6dEDqbOX2xuQLUgZ]{Lanespear} attack one another during peace negotiations in the City of Oshclaw, sparking a new round of conflict between Oshclaw, Kulrun, and Chimeras.

[[/date AS2469]]

The outpost known as Graven’s Rest is founded by Kallo Graven, gaining notoriety as a safe (if surly) way station for ships moving throughout the region’s treacherous coastal waterways.

[[/date AS2481]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.uKgqDFNhh8Ll7iv8]{Ankarist} was seen in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} Homelands, as a guest of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Goddess-Queen Lumé}. He was instrumental in the defense of the city of Ash the following year in AS2482.

[[/date AS2496]]

A massive half-eaten @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan} carcass is found washed up on the shores of the Dustlands and is discovered by passing ships. The length of its body is recorded at over three miles. Fears mount throughout the region once even larger teeth marks are found across its skull.

[[/date AS2508]]

Fall of Yarino. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire} ends the siege on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} City State of Yarino after 3 years in a climactic confrontation of soldiers and magery that rips apart the main wall and sacks the city, killing many inhabitants. The fighting sees the death of @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.6fQJsIMTYKypB0Xp]{Corwin Kawn}, husband of Empress @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l5SNwXC8t3Qp3Ut3]{Calyn Kariset}.

[[/date AS2511]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} city of Wick Launches the Seventh Star expedition and lands upon the Starshield. This marks the first time anyone from Aterica or Kessia has stepped foot upon the central continent in over two and a half thousand years.

[[/date AS2520]]

Rumors swirl that the Colossal Carnal Dragon @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.P2bBo8cyh95XhWew]{Siodread} has been killed by the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{ Blood Barons} of Moiran, opening a land route to attack the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Ed7ttdIwKm95IdUG]{Cascillian Republic} directly.

[[/date AS2522]]

Ambassador @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.68Deh9LMWYnPjeX0]{Loris Tezran} travels to @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain }as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire's} Ambassador to facilitate an open trade agreement between the city and the Empire. This marks the first official ties between the two nations.

Abyssal Shear.name: Abyssal Shear
Abyssal Shear.text:
WARNING

References to the Abyss, the Abyssal Shear, Abyssal Horrors, Outer Gods, etc, are not things that the player characters would typically learn about before gameplay begins, unless under very specific circumstances for background purposes. A more in-universe name for the Abyss among mortals is "The Shroud", with Abyssal monsters often called the Malvorn.
Abyssal Shear.scoverview: As the Shattering ripped across the surface world, another equally and possibly even more significant event occurred in the aftermath. Triggered by a violent rupture in the fabric of reality, the entropic forces from beyond poured into the Sea of Stars, targeting the Inner Realms, Moons, and the surface world with malice and destruction. While many of the Gods scrambled to organize a defense, the sheer scale of the invasion meant that every corner of existence had to fight for its own survival. To the cultures or peoples of the surface world, the Abyssal Shear is considered part of the Shattering, and the details of the cosmic conflict are heavily shrouded in mystery.
Abyssal Shear.sgamemaster:
Lore Summary

The Abyssal Shear was a cosmic invasion that occurred only a few days after the Shattering, when a rift to the Abyss opened in the Sea of Stars. While Ven'avé eventually sealed the breach, the event fundamentally broke the spiritual order of the cosmos.

  • Divine War: The Elder Gods desperately defend the Cosmos, Alar, Spectra, and Sockets, held the line while Lantyr recovers from the Shattering and Ven'avé seals the Shear itself.

  • The Moons: Ragen became a wasteland, Mayis drowned its invaders, and Cora was saved by a temporary truce between Spiders and elementals. Aura was besieged, and no one is entirely sure what happened to Orbis.

  • Fallen Empires: The remnants of the Aedir were decimated by the appearance of Undead, the Shent were hunted to extinction, and the Sedyri culture collapsed.

  • Surface Survivors: High King Fenra Irdragon unified the humans, the Fikost fled permanently into the sea, and the Lumek survived a desperate siege in their last city.

  • Terrible Legacy: The Herald of the Whispering Choir crashed onto Kessia, creating the Obsidian Desert, while the dying Wyrms of Akon were transformed by Alar into the first Dragons. Monsters filled the dark places of the world, and the Pathways. Many Wild Gods, Shard Gods, and other powerful entities were killed or driven insane.

Since its creation, Ember shone like a raging signal pyre amidst the blackness of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{the Abyss}. Attracted by this beacon of life and energy, incomprehensible and alien energies coalesced into a dark nebula enshrouding @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{the Weave}, held at bay by the energy and magic of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.JUwFAaelI86yiscL]{the Cosmos}. As @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} tore apart the Sun Tower, rocketing large sections outwards into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars}, one of the largest pieces collided with the Weave itself and, with a titanic eruption, a great tear opened in the protective barrier. This shear in the Weave allowed alien energies to breach Ember's protective barrier, giving birth to numerous evils: perversion of life into undeath, corruption of the mind into madness, and mutation of the flesh into abominations and monsters.

Combined with the effects of the Shattering, the Abyssal Shear had unimaginable effects upon the cosmos of Ember. The corrupting influence, along with eldritch horrors that emerged from the Shear, felled Gods, decimated the radiant power of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}, and caused widespread monster and dragon attacks as they settled into the surface world. Those who perished during the crisis were corrupted into terrible forms of undeath for the first time, and those who survived were often twisted to succumb to their darkest impulses of rage, hatred, jealousy, and spite.

To the average mortal on the surface of Ember, the Abyssal Shear is another rare, seldom-used name for the Shattering. Because the details of the cosmic conflict are heavily shrouded in mystery, most surface cultures view the falling Sun tower fragments, the darkening sky, and the rising horrors of that time as a singular apocalypse. However, this is dangerously reductive. While the Shattering was a physical breaking of the Sun Tower and a magical apocalypse of unimaginable destruction, the Shear was a literal invasion by alien monsters from a reality beyond our own.

~Laeora

The Bleeding Stars

As the Abyssal Shear tore through the Weave and reality warped on its surface, no other beings felt the impact more keenly than the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods}, and they rushed to defend the Cosmos. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} leaped into the Sea of Stars, smashing into the hordes of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal monsters} again and again, while @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} took up a harrowing position directly above the jagged rift of the Shear above the Weave, preventing even more horrors from gaining entry. On the surface world, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} was a whirlwind of fury, battling monsters that slipped through and attacked mortals. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} had suffered greatly during the Shattering itself, and she was withdrawn for most of the conflict, her energy reduced and dimmed, causing the sky itself to darken. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.UNMWwZTkjz2AdhhP]{Ven'avé} stood hidden behind Spectra during the conflict, slowly weaving the fabric of existence back together, repairing the Weave and closing the Shear itself.

The Elemental Moons were attacked by seemingly unending swarms as they emerged from the Shear, none more so than @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen}, where a concentrated Abyssal assault drove the Elemental Wild God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ZvsMcVcESynKQn8d]{Fiyara} into a sanity-shattering rage, leaving her moon a charred, lifeless wasteland. On @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, the horrors continued to devastate the broken remains, lodging themselves deep within the now lifeless tunnels, while on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}, the invading forces were largely dragged down and swallowed by the moon's terrifying inhabitants, but many Abyssal monsters hid in the dark waters, evading detection. In a bizarre display of temporary pragmatism, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora} was held against the darkness by an unprecedented alliance between the Spiders of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.HAAY0z8U2EIWOjCr]{Sitheera} and the moon's native Korvathi, a truce that evaporated the instant the threat was neutralized. The city of Conundrum on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura} was surrounded by Abyssal horrors but managed to withstand a grueling battle for survival, leaving the city itself scarred and corrupted. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis}, meanwhile, remained an unnerving enigma, its fate during the crisis unknown.

As the hordes of Abyssal monsters spread throughout the Sea of Stars, they prioritized the radiant Inner Realm of Luxarum above all others. In a display of fatal arrogance, the various @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} factions refused to unify, choosing instead to engage the Abyssal horrors independently. Although individually formidable, this lack of cohesion led to the total erasure of several old Tyraphem Lords and their forces, and to the permanent desecration of the region now known as The Lights Lost, a blighted wasteland forever tainted by Abyssal corruption. On @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.Sk9SPYMoDwduuPph]{Daemos} and their fiendish servants banded together in a rare show of cooperation, although whispers and rumors suggest some of the Daemos attempted to make pacts with Abyssal entities that forever damned them. Amidst this widespread carnage, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} remained an anomaly. It was seemingly ignored by the main forces of the Abyss, and while some horrors did spread through the primordial forests, overall, the realm somehow hid itself away, likely masked by illusions.

Fallen Empires

Upon the burning @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Op5BD9XSlmb7l6NN]{Starshield}, the dead population of the once mighty @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} began to rise as some of the first forms of undead, as Abyssal energies reanimated the fallen. The few desperate survivors are wiped out by monsters and undead in the following weeks. Elsewhere, the Aedir colonies across the seas begin to fall one by one, including on @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia}, the Kaedem Colonies, the Vaerdawn Cities, and the Juriea Outposts. Most fall into ruin, as monsters, undead, and a terrifying unknown threat that targets what was left of the Aedir's Legacy.

On the Isle of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GLjKDhOphB9yNW1n]{Kadisos}, the remaining remnants of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.4RM8MIiCDWMFv2yr]{Sedyri} culture faced an equally brutal fate as the chaos of the Shattering rained fire from the heavens, followed immediately by a tide of Abyssal monsters. The Sedyri civilization was functionally annihilated, its grand structures crumbled, and its people hunted across the scorched landscape. Only a few scattered families managed to evade extinction, disappearing into the dense cover of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.OrHRk1Juzyz2gmnd]{Lowland} jungles or seeking refuge along the treacherous shorelines of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}.

The Shent were fully aware of the coming Shroud but could do nothing to withstand the malice, hatred, and utter destruction unleashed upon them by Abyssal Horrors. The Abyss seemed to target the Shent with particular cruelty, seeking vengeance for the primordial Giants who had recklessly toyed with Abyssal forces during the Unveiling eons ago. The Shent resisted mightily, but the ancient colossal mountain cities fell one by one. In only a few short weeks, their entire pantheon was shattered, and the Giants were brought to the precipice of total extinction, leaving only ruins where a proud culture once stood.

The Surface Wars

While the conflict in the Sea of Stars raged, the mortals of the surface world found themselves trapped beneath the Shroud of the Abyss, a period of unnatural darkness, created in part by the dimming of Lantyr and a literal Shroud created by the countless Abyssal Horrors attacking the Cosmos. Pushed back from their ancestral lands by encroaching horrors, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} were forced into a desperate last stand within the island city of Aurtej, where they clung on until the end of the Shear. Simultaneously, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian Kingdoms} teetered on the brink of collapse, saved only by the legendary resolve of High King @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.YNMxNE2TbhObyKMp]{Fenra Irdragon}, who managed the impossible feat of rallying the fractured human kingdoms into a unified wall of iron against the tide. This era also marked the arrival of the Jagkat, terrifying new predators that forced the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Maziran} people to abandon the open plains for the claustrophobic safety of their fortified sky keeps.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken}, who had been resisting the Aedir only weeks earlier, meant that they were in a uniquely strong position to withstand the Abyssal monsters that fell upon their homeland. Meanwhile, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.TUt9EUMWp8pV1wXe]{Fikost} in the north were mercilessly driven from the ice sheets and tundra and into the oceans. Fleeing into the deep seas, they transitioned into a fully maritime culture, never to settle on permanent land again. In contrast, the fledgling Human cities on the northern shores of Kessia managed a miraculous survival, their defenses bolstered by a desperate influx of Aedir refugees and elite warriors from the Vaerdawn Cities who brought with them just enough battered strength to resist until the last moments of the Shear.

The Final Hours

Exact Timeline

The exact length of the Abyssal Shear is vague. Historical accounts within the setting are notoriously fractured on the matter; some surface cultures, traumatized by the speed of the onslaught, claim that the "Shattering" lasted only a few harrowing days. Conversely, others contend that the period lasted several agonizing weeks. The reality likely lies somewhere in between and is deliberately kept vague to maintain a certain level of mystery.

In the final hours of the conflict, the resistance across the Ember Cosmos had reached a breaking point; magical energies were spent, and many powerful forces, peoples, and nations had been annihilated. The tide only began to turn with the harrowing destruction of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.rxr72Zmt6eUOFg5B]{Herald of the Whispering Choir} above the shattered remains of Akon by Alar in a climactic battle that sent a shockwave across the surface world. The death of this colossal Abyssal entity was so violent that its massive remains were catapulted toward the surface world, plummeting through the atmosphere like a dark comet. The impact on the Kessian continent was a geological catastrophe in its own right, creating a wasteland of permanent Abyssal corruption, the Obsidian Desert, where the Herald’s toxic essence continues to seep into the earth to this day.

As the Herald fell, the war finally reached its exhausted conclusion when Ven'avé, drawing upon the combined essence of the other Elder Gods, completed her ritual to seal the Shear itself by weaving together the frayed edges of reality. The sealing of the Shear did not destroy the Abyssal monsters and horrors already present within, but it halted the endless reinforcements. Those that remained inside the Weave were hunted down and destroyed; others hid in dark places, scheming and emerging to cause chaos and destruction whenever they could.

Legacy of Ruin

One effect of the Abyssal Shear at the time was the slow death of the last remaining @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.CNUDzx1WE09XXJZ8]{Wyrms} of Akon. The Wyrms were an old and unchanging species that were choking in their fractured tunnels, meaning the entire species would have been slowly destroyed in a matter of months. As Alar ended the Herald of the Whispering Choir above Akon, Alar discovered a world in its final death throes and, as she struggled with her own inner turmoil, decided to save the Wyrms dying beneath her, changing their forms so they could survive and creating the first @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.XZUGUc4DpPiB30b0]{Dragons}.

As the Abyssal Shear ended, the aftermath and impact on the Cosmos were unimaginable, and Ember changed in countless ways. The Cosmos remains infested with Monsters, Abyssals, and Horrors, which still lurk in the deep darkness, while the Undead occupy forgotten ruins. The wilderness on the surface of Ember became far more treacherous, as the combination of the Shattering and the Shear left the lands broken and changed, with the carcasses of dead @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans}, monster lairs, Dragon nests, and insane @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8BRLwv29l3AKFTMV]{Wild Gods} lurking in the remote corners of the world.

Night of Swords.name: Night of Swords
Night of Swords.text:
Lore Summary

The Night of Swords was a coup enacted by an ambitious Kirargy Knight named Calyn Kariset seventy two years ago in the city of Caren'ac. The insurrection was seen by many as justified, and Calyn used the initial support to found the Tayan Empire. One unintended consequence of the Night of Swords was the origin of Ember's youngest ancestry, the Drakon.

The Night of Swords is an infamous coup that occurred only seventy-two years ago in the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.7iZDVtrBO7326XZY]{Caren'ac}. The event was spearheaded by @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.l5SNwXC8t3Qp3Ut3]{Calyn Kariset}, a renowned and formidable @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Qd6EE6pvR97O1OmH]{Kirargy Knight}, who, backed by her loyal Order of the Dragon, orchestrated a swift execution of the Caren'ac Kingdom's nobility. Calyn had been the only Kirargy Knight to ever bond with a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.0CquHJco0yougg3S]{Cruel Dragon} in the history of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Kingdoms}, and she was famous as an honorable and fierce warrior. At some point, she must have become disillusioned with the political landscape of the Tayan Kingdoms, especially within Caren'ac, which arguably had become a cesspool of decadence, excess, and corruption. In a single, blood-drenched night, the despotic King Vardegan, his entire family, and the majority of the ruling caste of nobles, including their families, were systematically dragged from their estates and murdered.

The fallout of the slaughter sent shockwaves through the region, including among the other Kirargy Orders and Noble Holds in nearby cities. Half of the Knightly orders viewed Calyn’s actions as an act of madness, moving immediately to disavow her. However, Calyn was more than prepared, and as the dust settled that morning within the city of Caren'ac and with the pre-arranged support of the remaining Kirargy orders across the region, she seized the vacant throne and declared herself Empress, transforming the remnants of the Caren'ac Kingdom into the Tayan Empire.

The First Days

In the aftermath, Calyn became an extremely divisive figure. To the common people, she was a transformative hero; she immediately enacted sweeping reforms, granted new freedoms, and established a series of surprisingly just laws. On the other hand, she was brutal in her methods to maintain order and had little patience for dissent. The Temple of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.ZTZ8d8E7BPE8S6zX]{Selai} within Caren'ac, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Goddess} Selai herself, viewed the formation of the Tayan Empire with cautious acceptance. Seeing the previous King Vardegan as a corrupt despot, Selai felt that the coup was a path toward stability and renewed purpose for the people, and her passive endorsement provided just enough legitimacy for Calyn to cement her rule.

This religious backing was mirrored by several of the Great Noble Holds, which chose to align rather than risk future destruction. Calix Hold, Tyren Hold, and Vyssar Hold, active in the cities of Braken, Vence, and Corla, were among the first to pivot, accepting the formation of the Tayan Empire without opposition. These nobles traded their independence for high-ranking positions and safety within the new Imperial hierarchy, becoming the mercantile backbone of Calyn’s reign. However, Oryn Hold, a fortress-estate centered in the city of Point, refused to work with the emerging Empire. Although too far removed for Calyn to crush immediately, the Oryn family began setting the stage for more organized resistance and the eventual formation of the organization known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.AXuTFye24hV7ciae]{Vanguard}.

The origin of the Tayan Empire was paved in blood and murder. A despicable night of slaughter was followed by decades of silent, underhanded opposition, secret executions, and a pervasive undercurrent of fear. I find the Empire reprehensible for reasons that go far deeper than a coup, but its beginning was the ultimate dark omen.

~Laeora

Calyn's Folly & The Origin of Drakons

Another event, kept secret by the Empress (she became aware of it much later), is known as Calyn's Folly, which took place alongside the Night of Swords. Calyn did not discriminate in the destruction of the noble families. One family, the Talmonts of Talmont Hold, was killed as well, despite remaining largely above the corruption of the city and the Caren'ac Kingdom at large. Unknown to Calyn, the Talmonts were responsible for containing an ancient seal deep beneath their estate, just outside the city of Caren'ac, from the time of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} through their bloodline. When the last Talmont was killed, it released a long-dormant monster of incredible power. Before long, the Kirargy Knights assigned to kill the Talmonts had been killed and enslaved, and the dead Talmonts had been raised to assault the city. It was at this point that several powerful entities stepped in, including, eventually, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Goddess} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar} and the Shard God Hestol.

The alien monster was killed in a massive magical conflagration, something most of the city saw and heard but never fully understood. Hestol was slain in the conflict, but in a final, sympathetic act of preservation, Alar gathered the dying Shard God's fading energy and used it to catch the souls of the Talmonts, Kirargy Knights of the Dragon, and innocent people caught in the crossfire. She forged them into entirely new forms, imbued with draconic resilience and the fading light of Hestol, and created the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.GRs2vgeVsDpWPqjh]{Drakon }ancestry.
Night of Swords.scoverview: Taking place seventy-two years ago, the Night of Swords was a brutal coup that saw the murder of the royal family of Caren'ac and many noble families across the city by the Kirargy Knights of the Order of the Dragon. In the aftermath, the Tayan Empire was founded by Calyn Kariset, whose meteoric rise and lust for power and control have continued unabated ever since. It also saw the emergence of the Drakon ancestry in a parallel yet connected series of events on the same night.

The Shattering.name: The Shattering
The Shattering.text:
Lore Summary

The Sun Tower of the Aedir explodes with cataclysmic force, wiping out the entire continent of the Starshield and ending thousands of years of Aedir supremacy over the surface world. A section of the Sun Tower rockets outwards and shatters the Elemental Moon of Akon, breaking it apart.

In a single moment of unimaginable destruction, the apex of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.XXMizY6WTIsL0swx]{Sun Tower} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} exploded with such force and power that it appeared to shine with the full force of the sun, blinding those facing it directly. The explosion shattered the upper sections, expelling colossal chunks of stone and rock into the cosmos. For the Aedir living on the Starshield, close to nearly the entire population of millions, was annihilated instantly as the force of the explosion and magical energy radiated across the continent. Across the oceans, around the Starshield, the blast struck with less force, but depending on the distance, it was still powerful enough to smash aside buildings and lay waste to entire cities. The skies of Ember became choked by fiery red and orange storm clouds as fire seemed to engulf the world, casting the surface into glimmering darkness for several months. In the chaos and destruction that followed, the terrifying emergence of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.zaLrsSK495BEAUki]{Monsters} completed the devastation in many places, seemingly materializing out of nothingness to kill, consume, and destroy everything around them.
The Shattering.scoverview: The Shattering was the most cataclysmic event that has ever affected the Ember Cosmos. Its impact and consequences cannot be understated, and it has had a lasting influence on almost every area of the world, from the death of countless Shard Gods to the rearranging or emergence of entire cosmological forces to the deaths of millions of mortal lives. It was an event so universal and destructive that it has become ingrained into the cultural memory of nearly every nation or kingdom on the surface of Ember, even two and half thousand years later.
The Shattering.sgamemaster:
It's said that the arrogance and the hubris of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} led to a great reckoning, and they were fully responsible for their own destruction. Others maintain that something else must have caused such a massive cataclysm and that even the Aedir could not have summoned the level of power that caused the Shattering by themselves. It is a point in history that is universally acknowledged yet retains a level of mystery and confusion that causes some scholars and historians to spend their entire lives searching for answers. Ultimately, no one alive today knows the truth, not even the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods}, and what caused the Shattering may remain a mystery forever.

Many of the fragments and sections of the Sun Tower were expelled into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9e2b7awJ2yQVR4yZ]{Sea of Stars} as the Shattering occurred, causing some of the most damaging effects on the cosmos.
