One such fragment collided with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, one of Ember's elemental moons. It was so large and traveling with such force that it slammed into Akon and shattered the moon's surface. Since the creation, Akon had been the domain of an ancient race of serpentine Wyrms that dwelt within the labyrinthine tunnels of the mostly hollow moon. The near-complete destruction of Akon during the Shattering rendered these Wyrms nearly extinct, only a few remained in the darkest depths of the moon's tunnels. Other sections and pieces flew out and struck other realms with catastrophic consequences or were caught by the gravity of the World of Ember, eventually falling back onto the surface and causing further destruction. Many chunks remain floating across the Sea of Stars today and are said to contain secrets and lost technology of the Sunfire Empire at the height of their power, preserved and protected from decay.

The consequences of the Shattering itself were instant and far-reaching. While its effects were felt immediately, it also caused another event in the following hours that was as equally profound, called the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}. This event is not well understood by mortals today and is seen as part of the Shattering itself. Still, its effects were even more deadly and impactful in the aftermath of the Shattering, and its consequences have plagued mortals ever since.

The Evernight.name: The Evernight
The Evernight.text:
Lore Summary

The city of Miris is suddenly annihilated in a titanic explosion caused by an abhorrent magical ritual. In the aftermath, a vast cloud of impenetrable darkness — the Evernight — settles in the sky, covering the lands that would become known as the Moiran Bonelands. The region is then overrun by powerful undead hosts, crushing nearby cities and settlements.

  • The Unholy Kingdom: Emergence of the Ossarchate and the Blood Barons.

In the weeks leading up to the event that would become known as the Evernight, nothing amiss was reported in the city of Miris. Life continued in one of the largest human kingdoms, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran}, in the world at the time. The people of Moiran were a strong, dignified people who had allied themselves with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} to the east and had spread across the region. Alas, in the waning of [[/date AS869]], without any warning, Miris and the entire royal bloodline were annihilated, leaving behind a scarred, magical wasteland now known as the Desolation.

Some survivors contend that the explosion was the result of a high-level magical ritual gone catastrophically awry, while others believe the Moiran inadvertently unsealed an ancient, primordial evil buried beneath the city. Regardless of the cause, the consequences were immediate. A thick, impenetrable shroud of unnatural black clouds settled over the region, blotting out the sun and plunging the land into a permanent, freezing twilight. This "Evernight" acted as a conductor for necromantic energies, allowing undeath to run rampant, turning thousands into monsters. From this sea of carnage arose the Blood Barons, undead lords of immense magical power. The Blood Barons seized control of the vacuum left by the fallen Moiran Kingdom, forging the region into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Ossarchate}, an empire of the dead.

Valiant Defenders

To the east, the Lumek watched the collapse of their allies with horror, quickly realizing that the Evernight was a monumental threat to be contained. The initial waves of mindless undead, throwing themselves at hastily organized Lumek defenders, were soon replaced by legions led by the Blood Barons themselves. What followed was a series of grueling battles. Though the Lumek eventually emerged victorious, the cost was staggering; their strength was so thoroughly depleted that any hope of a counter-offensive into the heart of the Ossarchate was abandoned.

Retreating to a strategic bottleneck, the Lumek focused their remaining resources on fortifying the City of Ash. This fortress-city became the final bulkhead against the encroaching tide of the dead. For centuries, the two powers have remained locked in a stalemate of attrition known as the Cycles of Fire and Death. These are not mere skirmishes, but periodic, high-intensity wars where the Lumek’s mastery of flame and steel is pitted against the inexhaustible might of the Ossarchate.
The Evernight.scoverview: The Evernight was a devastating event one thousand-six hundred years ago that destroyed and transformed the peaceful Moiran nation and culture into the undead Blood Barons. A sickening and permanent night fell upon the region as undeath and darkness became an unassailable threat to mortal life.

Forsaken War.name: Forsaken War
Forsaken War.text: The Forsaken War stands as the first truly global conflict in the history of the surface world, a war of such staggering scale that it defies belief. Occurring roughly eight thousand years ago, it pitted the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} against the ancient, predatory dominance of creatures known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.186yO79YKDxPh0qT]{Theroch}. However, the war has largely drifted into the realm of myth. Scholars remain bitterly divided over its details, and the passage of millennia has eroded the records so thoroughly that many aren't even certain if the war ever occurred at all.
Forsaken War.scoverview: Recovered Aedir scrolls and history record an event that seems akin to fiction. So unimaginable was the scale of this conflict, that many today dismiss it ever took place on the surface world.
Forsaken War.sgamemaster:
Lore Summary

The Forsaken War pitted the Aedir against the primal power of the Theroch. The war itself was fought mainly on the continent of Jekaros, but many battles occurred across the surface world. The Aedir were joined in the war by many powerful allies, including:

  • Known Deities: Alar, Sockets, Spectra, Lorgi, Katu, Nite, Ku'arta, Scoris, Malae, Janar, Themis.

The war ended with the Theroch losing, and the Aedir replacing them as the dominant power on the surface world. Many cultures believe that Jekaros is cursed, and no one has visited its shores in thousands of years to confirm whether the Theroch still exist.

At the onset of the war, the Theroch, according to accounts, had already been attacking many of the younger ancestries in smaller-scale conflicts for millennia. However, tensions reached a breaking point when the Theroch allegedly murdered the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder God} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.BP2QN2S6fFOfwp3U]{Finor}, who had been attempting to broker a peace. The shock of his murder enraged the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos}. In the wake of his fall, an unprecedented alliance was formed. The Aedir, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.o38uqC8NLxOWxA4i]{Vaznor}, and Seydri stood alongside a host of various deities. Even the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.CNUDzx1WE09XXJZ8]{Wyrms} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon} and forces of the Inner Realms, such as a legion of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.qtxBDYBNwKhD7nWd]{Celestials} from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}, descended to join the fray, all unified by a single, burning purpose: to avenge the Knight of Time.

History of Cruelty

At the onset of the war, the Theroch could be found across the surface world. Though they were always found in small numbers or even as solitary individuals, they exerted a terrifying dominion over the landscape. A single Theroch would often "cordon off" vast areas of land, preventing any other ancestry from entering their territory. Not only was this an ever-present danger for anyone exploring the wilderness, but the Theroch would also often shift the size or location of these zones at random. This meant that even a thriving settlement could find itself suddenly placed within a Theroch’s territory, facing certain destruction as the creature enforced its claim.

Thus, when the Forsaken War erupted, many cultures leapt at the chance to finally rid their lands of Theroch control, and even though the vast majority of the war took place upon the cold northern continent of Jekaros, additional campaigns against a small number of Theroch were fought across the surface world of Ember at the same time.

The Alliance of Light

At the time, the Aedir pantheon, especially the creator goddess of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QgnKHUryvNrNqRfN]{Nir'ae} Keia, had some insight into the Theroch's plans. Over centuries, it became increasingly clear that the Theroch were evolving; their motivations were darkening, shifting to something far more sinister. In response the Aedir upon @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Op5BD9XSlmb7l6NN]{the Starshield} began slowly arming themselves over hundreds of years, continuously improving their martial strength and creating the 1st Host. Such a force had never existed on the surface world and even today has yet to be surpassed; its warriors were highly trained, led by Sun-Bladed champions with cadres of Maejis to provide support and firepower. When Finor was murdered, the Aedir were outraged and led the efforts to join forces with other powerful forces and entities.

They immediately moved to galvanize the world's fragmented nations and cultures, intending to lead a unified front against the Theroch threat. However, even the disciplined Aedir were stunned when an emissary from Luxarum suddenly appeared floating in their midst. The shock only deepened when the emissary offered the Aedir an alliance against the Theroch. The Aedir, recognizing that they desperately required the aid, accepted without hesitation.

Legends state that the arrival of the Luxarum forces remains one of the most staggering sights in history. Under the command of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.XXyU4kvrBPceEoz2]{Lord Taryakel}, Celestial Legions began to descend upon the Starshield in preparation for the war to come. They kept coming, day after day, a seemingly infinite stream of golden armor and shimmering light. While the 1st Host was the largest army ever assembled by the surface kingdoms of Ember, it was dwarfed by the Legions of Luxarum. Once assembled, the colossal force was said to cover the freezing tundras of Jekaros like a rising tide, turning the white snow into a sea of gold and radiant energy.

As this massive coalition prepared for the march, they were joined by reinforcements from the cultures the Theroch had long oppressed. Elements from the Vaznor, the Seydri, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} arrived to lend their strength, as did strangely many Wyrms from the moon of Akon. Even the divine presence was overwhelming as countless Gods from across the Cosmos joined the alliance. Most notably, the Elder Goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}, alongside @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.KQF9QommtN6ITiLW]{Lorgi}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q13vkYPSDBkSLRI4]{Katu}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.DskILHKPngH3FVa7]{Nite}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.sa5TtcQvRnu3NbtN]{Scoris}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.7IA3oPJOMyKqnYpb]{Janar}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.pEeJhnepW0PzeN9X]{Themis}, as well as the enigmatic @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}. It was a gathering of powers so dense that the very air around the encampments hummed with the magical power.

A World War

Many ancient accounts have been written of the battles and skirmishes of the war in full, each a saga in its own right. Ancient chronicles speak of the Red Landing, where the Alliance first spilled its blood upon the frozen shores of Jekaros; Ashkins Rise and the Fall of Vandras; and the Battle of the Seven, where seven @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods} stood against a single Deafic Theroch.

Throughout the war, despite the strength of the Tyraphem Legions and the Aedir 1st Host, and the deities arrayed against them, the Theroch were a terrifyingly powerful enemy, able to match the Alliance time and again. It was only through immense sacrifice and dogged attrition that the Alliance gained ground. Thankfully, the Theroch, even upon their home continent, were incredibly few in number, and their birth cycles took place over hundreds of years. Thus, slowly and surely, the Alliance inched closer to the Theroch's sacred city of Jaea.

It was on the slopes of Jaea that the war ended, and the Theroch were finally and bitterly defeated. True to their nature, not a single adult Theroch surrendered; they fought with a cold, unrelenting ferocity until the last of their kind was extinguished. It is whispered that even the Theroch’s own dark gods were hunted down and slain in the final hours of the siege. The cost of this "victory" was so high that it nearly shattered the Aedir as a race, requiring over a thousand years of isolation to recover their strength. Across the surface world, Theroch were hunted down and destroyed, often causing massive casualties and scarred landscapes. However, some were believed to be sealed away instead, as their power was too great to be fully destroyed.

Curse of Eternity

One of the most chilling consequences of the war was the rumored curse enacted by Keia and the Aedir Pantheon. Despite many of the other gods' resistance, Keia led the effort to cast what became known as the Curse of Eternity. Although never confirmed, many believe the Curse of Eternity permanently severed the Theroch from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. By cutting their connection to the source of all life, the Aedir ensured the Theroch could never again ascend, grow in power, or replenish their population, effectively ending their threat to the Cosmos for all time.

In the millennia since the fall of Jaea, a profound and terrifying isolation has settled over the north. It is widely believed that any Theroch survivors of the war remain confined to the cursed continent of Jekaros, trapped within the frozen wasteland they once called home. However, the truth of their fate remains a mystery; the waters surrounding the continent are treacherous, and the air itself is said to be heavy with magical fissures. No ship has successfully landed upon its frozen shores in centuries, leaving the world to wonder if the Theroch still linger in the shadows of their ruined cities.

Virulent Plague.name: Virulent Plague
Virulent Plague.text:
Lore Summary

As the Age of Rediscovery unfolds, the Aran sub-continent is hit by a devastating contagion known as the Virulent Plague. It sweeps through the bustling Human settlements of the Kelmezian Kingdoms, and a mass exodus occurs. Many of the affected cities are entirely abandoned in the aftermath, and Humans begin spreading across the Aterican continent.

According to accounts, the Virulent Plague began in the Fortress city of the First Throne in [[/date AS272]]. Theories regarding its origin remain a subject of intense debate: some scholars suggest a malevolent entity or force, others believe it was a targeted curse, while many maintain it was simply a natural (though uniquely vicious) pathogen that proved resistant to the healing magics of the era. Regardless of its source, the plague’s lethality was absolute. Transmission occurred through both physical contact and air exposure, but its most devastating trait was a fluctuating dormant period. Lasting several days to several weeks, this window of asymptomatic infection allowed carriers to travel far and wide before realizing they were ill, resulting in rapid, uncontrollable regional transmission before the full extent of the plague was recognized.

The progression of the disease was as agonizing as it was swift. Once the symptoms manifested, individuals suffered from sudden fevers, chills, nausea, and debilitating pain in the throat and chest. As the infection reached its terminal phase, the extremities, the fingers, toes, and nose, would turn a bruised, dark blue. The most horrific symptom, however, was the expulsion of a fine, dark blue and green mist known as the Virulence. This mist was caustic, rapidly burning organic matter, including the victim’s own skin, nearby foliage, and animals. This Virulence would accumulate on surfaces, sprouting small, pulsating bulbs and growths that were extremely caustic to the touch. The substance proved nearly impossible to eradicate; it was highly resistant to magic and could be removed only by extremely high temperatures and sustained flame.

The Virulent Plague is one of the most horrific contagions that I've ever had the misfortune of witnessing in all my long years of existence. There is a sound you never forget, the wet, rattling scream of a person begging for water while their own skin melts in that abominable blue mist.

Even now, those ancient Kelmezian cities are choked with centuries-old Virulence, dormant but waiting. People talk about lost treasures in the ruins of the First Throne, but believe me: only the truly insane or the already dead would try to breathe that air.

~Laeora

Destruction of the Kingdoms

Prior to the outbreak, the region's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Human} settlements were divided into a network of small, independent kingdoms. While they ostensibly recognized the authority of the First Throne and High King Kostros Irdragon, a descendant of the legendary @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.YNMxNE2TbhObyKMp]{Fenra Irdragon}, this fealty was symbolic at best. In truth, the kingdoms were fully independent, and when the plague emerged, this disunity proved fatal. The initial refusal to coordinate or share resources led to a total breakdown of order. As a result, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} Kingdoms fractured, and within several months, once-vibrant cities were silenced and filled with the dead, their streets choked by the blue-green mist of the Virulence.

To the north, a few city-states on the periphery managed to survive by enacting ruthless measures. They shuttered their borders and enforced absolute quarantines on all arriving refugees, aided by powerful entities like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Goddess} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.GIX4ViCk2Vr9NWDi]{Malae}, capable of sensing the dormant infection. However, even this assistance offered little comfort; the power of many other Shard Gods proved insufficient to cure the disease, and reports suggest that at least three such deities were themselves consumed and killed by the plague's effects. Ultimately, the Kelmezian kingdoms were shattered forever within the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.NdqwtFoFAw85Gstr]{Aran} sub-continent. Of the great city-states of that era, only Nasjar, Carinth, and Verena survived the devastation, taking on the name of the Kelmezian City-States instead.

Origin of the Altyra

Amid the height of the outbreak, as the population of the Aran Peninsula was decimated, several @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} outcasts saw a unique opportunity to study the newly created humanity. They had observed the creation and spread of Humans with both curiosity and unease, as Humans were different from other ancestries on the surface in ways they could not fully explain or understand. Thus, the Tyraphem began a series of clandestine experiments within the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen} during the height of the plague, capturing infected and non-infected humans alike. These experiments, which the Tyraphem viewed as both an act of mercy to save Human lives and an expression of their own curiosity, resulted in the creation of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.tkGzfnJkkLZ3cgpG]{Altyra} ancestry.

The newly formed Altyra were immune to the effects of the Virulent Plague and able to thrive as most of the places around them crumbled. They quickly came to view the Tyraphem’s experiments as a blessing from Ember that elevated them above the other “weaker” ancestries. They sent parties to acquire goods and technology from neighboring cities abandoned due to the outbreak, and over many years the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.y4WHE3TEr6Of13SL]{Railen} culture formed, centered in Ancalen.
Virulent Plague.scoverview: A terrible plague erupts across the Aran Sub-Continent, humans are especially affected, dying in droves as the disease rips apart cities and turns many into echoing ruins. Ghostly undead arise and complete the decimation of the region. Many Humans flee north, towards some of the distant human city-states, resisting the plague, while others flee across the oceans in hastily assembled fleets.

Seeding.name: Seeding
Seeding.text:
The Seeding is known throughout Ember as the Season of Restlessness, or the first season of spring, a sixty-day period during which the world of Ember awakens from the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.qwv1GJoa18AnS05c]{Stilling}. As @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} begins to wane in the sky and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} becomes more prominent, mortals find themselves grappling with a frantic internal "itch" that defies easy explanation. Sleep becomes restless, and settlements hum with nervous energy as people spring-clean their homes or make plans for the year ahead.

Across the surface world, the transition from the Stilling is rarely gentle; the Stilling's snow and ice does not merely melt but often shatters under sudden pressure. Travel becomes harder due to sudden meltwater, flash floods, and roads turning into mud. Yet the restlessness benefits traders and merchants, who often use the feeling of unrest to set out on new journeys. Life also begins to awaken from dormancy over the winter as plants sprout once more. Predators, starved by the long winter and emboldened by the seasonal unrest, can be at their most dangerous, hunting with a desperate intensity, making the Seeding a time of both vibrant renewal and profound, erratic peril.
Seeding.scoverview: Seeding is often called the season of restlessness when Primordis begins to dominate the sky above. During this time of year, mortals may feel anxious, sleep fitfully, or find themselves grappling with problems that offer no immediate solutions.

Blooming.name: Blooming
Blooming.text:
The Blooming is known as the Season of Optimism, or the Second Season of Spring, when the restlessness of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.loBTA2Ahpf2nMgIY]{Seeding} matures into a sense of boundless, abundant possibility. Under the full light of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, mortals often find themselves swept up in a tide of ambition, making plans that sometimes ignore the harsh realities of logic. This is a season of boundless creativity, where builders may break ground on new projects, artists learn new techniques, and musicians learn new songs.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} mirrors this surge with a frantic, often explosive vitality that can be nearly overwhelming to the senses. Plants not only grow but often erupt in a frenzied burst of untamed growth. Wilderness paths through forests and grasslands become clogged or swallowed by thickets or rapid-growing vines, making navigation a constant struggle. The air itself seems to hum with more motes, making magic feel effortless yet dangerously volatile.
Blooming.scoverview: The Blooming is often called the Season of Optimism, when primroses are at their height in the sky and are associated with a period when people feel abundant possibilities, often concocting grandiose or impractical plans.

Steading.name: Steading
Steading.text:
The Steading is known as the Season of Industry, or the first Season of Summer, where the frantic pace of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.8chE39ioICfZw3jU]{Blooming} settles into contentment. With @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis} in balance, mortals begin to feel a profound satisfaction in manual labor and progress. People find themselves happiest when engaged in meaningful work, leading to a surge in craftsmanship, infrastructure repair, and the quiet domestic joys of tending to one’s community and home.

The world reflects this newfound stability as the wild growth of the spring slows into a predictable, lush maturity. The weather tends toward a reliable warmth, and the violent flash floods of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.loBTA2Ahpf2nMgIY]{Seeding} give way to calm rivers and clear, navigable trade routes. This is the golden age of the Ember year for travel and commerce, as the roads are dry and the people are at their most hospitable and level-headed. Even the wilderness seems to settle down, and predators are well-fed and less prone to the aggression of other seasons, allowing for a rare window of relative peace.
Steading.scoverview: The Steading is known as the Season of Industry, when Luxarum begins to replace Primordis in the sky above and as the period of the year when people are happiest being productive and working with their hands.

Gleaning.name: Gleaning
Gleaning.text:
The Gleaning is known as the Season of Passion, or the Second Season of Summer, when the steady productivity of the previous months gives way to emotional fervor. As @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} dominates the sky, the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.xu3TCWh4GPy18X4t]{Steading's} grounded nature evaporates, replaced by flights of fancy and spontaneous, often rash decisions. It is a time of sudden romances, fiery political movements, and spiritual awakenings that flare up with little warning. Common wisdom holds that any contract signed or vow spoken during the Gleaning should be viewed with skepticism, and some cultures even disallow pacts or contracts altogether during this time.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} is bathed in what seems to be extra light, and the season projects golden, shimmering luminance during the day and soft golden light at night. The air often feels electrically charged, and the sunsets stretch into long tapestries of crimson and gold. Farmers and laborers work with additional speed, not out of the quiet duty found in the Steading, but out of a sudden, zealous drive to secure the year’s bounty before the light fades. This creates an atmosphere of high-stakes energy in every settlement, where the pressure to succeed and the desire to indulge in life’s pleasures collide, leading to grand festivals and fabulous summer parties.
Gleaning.scoverview: The Gleaning is the period of the year when mortals are swept away in feelings of passion, zeal, or rashness when Luxarum is at its height in the sky. During Gleaning, folk may be prone to flights of fancy or spontaneous decisions that they might think twice about during other seasons.

Withering.name: Withering
Withering.text:
The Withering is known as the Season of Understanding, or the First Season of Winter, during which people experience surges of regret, wistfulness, and nostalgia. As the golden light of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum} fades, the passions of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.pEg9yxklAGARjf2Q]{Gleaning} are replaced by a somber, reflective mood. Mortals find themselves looking backward, mourning lost opportunities, or dwelling on the past. Despite this heavy sense of longing, the season brings a strange, restorative peace to the mind; people tend to sleep more soundly than at any other time of year, and they are visited by dreams that are exceptionally clear and often seen as prophetic.

Across the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}, the vibrant colors of the earlier year begin to fade; leaves turn orange, brown, and red, eventually falling in piles. Persistent mists often cling to the hills or rise from shorelines, making the world feel more oppressive. In many cultures, the Withering is also the season of the harvest, where people gather what remains in farms and gardens and preserve it for the coming winter season. Settlements become quiet, and the air is filled with the scent of woodsmoke as the temperatures fall.
Withering.scoverview: The Withering is the period of the year when mortals feel regret, wistfulness, or nostalgia more keenly, as the additional light from Luxaurum fades and the darkness of Signara replaces it in the sky. During this season, folk tend to sleep soundly with clear, vivid dreams.

Stilling.name: Stilling
Stilling.text:
The Stilling is revered as the Season of the Quiet, or the Second Season of Winter, a period of profound calm and stillness where the heat and passions of the earlier year are extinguished. Shrouded in the darkness of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara}, mortals find themselves at their most rational and contemplative. Traditionally, this is the most productive period for academic research, complex innovation, and the birth of new ideas. Scholars, engineers, and philosophers retreat to their libraries and workshops, and common people like farmers and traders retreat indoors to find solace with their families and communities.

Across Ember, the Stilling is a time of calm, as the world falls into a heavy silence, and most of the landscape is locked beneath layers of frost and snow. Travel becomes almost impossible in many places; harsh cold and deep snow make travel treacherous, and the "Stilling Hush" makes even the sound of a footfall carry for miles in the frozen air. Communities bond over stories and rigorous debates, using the long, dark nights to recuperate and rest before the start of the next year.
Stilling.scoverview: The Stilling is the season when mortals are said to be most rational and thoughtful, and when the darkness of Signara dominates the sky. Traditionally, Stilling is a productive period for academic work, research, innovation, and new ideas.

Timekeeping.name: Timekeeping
Timekeeping.text:
Time in Ember is divided into the seasons of the year, and further subdivided into days, hours, minutes, and seconds. The seasons are dictated by the dominance of one or two of the Inner Realms in the sky and their movement around @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{the Weave} in a predictable pattern. Days are calculated by how long it takes @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} to make a single rotation around the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember}.

Years

Each year in Ember has 360 days, which are divided into six seasons. The turn of each year occurs between the end of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.qwv1GJoa18AnS05c]{Stilling} and the beginning of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.loBTA2Ahpf2nMgIY]{Seeding}.

Years are numbered according to the historical age that particular year is a part of, and there have been several ages throughout the course of Ember's history — defined by the precise year they began. Ages of Ember's history are annotated as:

  • AC = After Creation

  • AB = @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts}

  • AT = @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of the Tower}

  • AS = After Shattering (also known as the "@UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.R97NAeTio76VFKWI]{"Age of Rediscovery"})

After Shattering (AS)

Historical ages of Ember can actually be categorized differently based on the specific culture that is referencing a certain event. Generally speaking, though, most people of Ember use the AS calendar — which is used to label the years that have taken place after the cataclysmic event of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} two-and-a-half-thousand years ago. AS is used with regularity throughout the continents of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica}, @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.2eLAE5AF2iAMlc0e]{Kessia}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}, though some distant cultures have a different time scale (such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken}, who currently track time approximately and are in their 27th Era).

Example Years

  • [[/date AB200451]] = 200,451 years after the beginning of the Age of Beasts

  • [[/date AT0]] = The start of the Age of the Tower

  • [[/date AT11021]] = 11,021 years after the beginning of the Age of the Tower

  • [[/date AS0]] = The year of the Shattering

  • [[/date AS-200]] = 200 years before the Shattering

  • [[/date AS2523]] = Present day

Seasons

As the Inner Realms of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordis}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} drift across the sky, their influence can be felt upon the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} in the form of seasons. These seasons affect more than just the weather, temperature, and plant life on Ember's surface. As the balance between the Inner Realms shifts and changes, so do the moods of Ember's people — anxious and fitful during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.loBTA2Ahpf2nMgIY]{Seeding}, rational and thoughtful during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.qwv1GJoa18AnS05c]{Stilling}, and everything in between.

You can read more about each season in the Setting Compendium:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.loBTA2Ahpf2nMgIY]

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.8chE39ioICfZw3jU]

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.xu3TCWh4GPy18X4t]

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.pEg9yxklAGARjf2Q]

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.MEfKfW6rZMdpFhwf]

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.qwv1GJoa18AnS05c]

Days

A day in Ember consists of 24 hours. Each hour consists of 60 minutes, and each minute is a standard 60 seconds in length.

Lunar Cycles

The cycles of Ember's Elemental Moons also play an important role for timekeeping. The orbital durations of these lunar bodies are well-known by nearly everyone on the planet, so most @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000]{Cultures} in Ember can understand and anticipate when forthcoming zeniths or conjunctions will occur. Ember's lunar cycles are as following:

  • Aura: 28 days

  • Akon: 33 days

  • Cora: 32 days

  • Mayis: 32 days

  • Orbis: 29 days

  • Ragen: 29 days
Timekeeping.scoverview: The study of time is the domain of the wise. Keeping time and tracking it accurately is for the mad and the foolish. If anyone sits in towers with brass gears and ticking pendulums, trying to measure the world down to the nearest second, they might as well be measuring a waterfall with a thimble. By the time they’ve calibrated their machines to the pulse of Primordis, Signara, Luxarum, and, most importantly, Lantyr, the world has already shifted under their feet.

The Unveiling.name: The Unveiling
The Unveiling.text: Even during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} culture's prime, the knowledge of "The Unveiling" was a closely guarded secret. Since thier fall during @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering}, the knowledge has all but disappeared entirely.
The Unveiling.scoverview: Marking the end of the Age of Beasts the Unveiling was an ancient event that took place in the Pathways. Records of the Shent reference the event with secretive and mysterious undertones.
The Unveiling.sgamemaster:
Lore Summary

The primordial Giants that once lived deep within the Pathways go to war with one another. The effects are far-reaching, but the survivors flee the Pathways, emerging onto the Surface world and forming the Shent culture.

Whatever happened during the Unveiling, it wasn't just a simple civil war. You don't abandon an underground paradise and the love of a creator deity to flee into a strange new land. There is a hollow look in a Shent’s eyes when they talk about 'The Great Descent.' They’re terrified that whatever they left behind in the dark is still down there, waiting.

~Laeora

The Unveiling was an ancient apocalypse and one of the most transformative turning points in the history of the world, bringing the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.OXodus5uIOGlL9xZ]{Age of Beasts} to a close and ushering in the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of the Tower}. This ancient event unfolded within the lightless depths of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}, centered in the legendary Lost City of the First Giants. Long ago, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giants} had established a sprawling, sophisticated culture. They shaped and helped tame the Pathways with the help of an ancient deity called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.RMKcfiSM5c565Dh8]{Pathwalker}, building many great structures and cities. Their primary purpose was to serve as custodians, safeguarding the world from the volatile, destructive bursts of raw Lifeforce that periodically surged from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember} and guiding lava and water through and around one another to tame earthquakes, seismic shifts, and natural "merges" when lava and water tunnels would unite and cause catastrophic explosions underground.

The era of subterranean dominance was shattered when a cataclysmic civil war erupted among the Giants, a conflict so devastating that it fractured their civilization, killing much of their kind and annihilating their way of life. In the wake of the carnage, the survivors were forced to abandon their home, and the majority fled to the sunlit surface to adapt and eventually found the Shent. However, a stubborn remnant refused to leave the dark, retreating further into the labyrinthine Pathways to form the dark and reclusive @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.7i1MQodKiQNxOuyl]{Niethun}. The Giants' exodus had an immediate, destabilizing impact on the surface world and its inhabitants. As the Giants abandoned their posts in the deep, the unregulated surges of Lifeforce began to warp the landscape. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathans} weakened, and their stranglehold on the surface began to wane. Finally, as the Shent emerged onto the surface, they displaced the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.t0uXEiiy4hN4XBeX]{Trolls} living in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.VxA0UsGvDbDn8SdO]{Shana Mountains}, inadvertently causing the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.6thz1HFNCR4W3doS]{Troll Invasions}.

The History.name: The History
The History.text:
Lore Summary

The history of Ember is divided into four distinct ages, with each era lasting less time than the one before it. This accelerating timeline seems to be increasing volatility and chaos as the World moves toward the present day.

Due to the sheer scale of world history and the cataclysms that have reset civilizations, much of the past remains shrouded in mystery. The further back one looks, the more lost history there is to uncover, with ancient records eventually dissolving into myth and legends.

  • The First Dawn: The creation of the Ember Cosmos, the Inner Realms, the Elemental Moons, and the Elder Gods. In addition, the first sapient ancestries arise, the Theroch and the Xaxin.

  • Age of Beasts: The age of the Leviathans and the creation of many mortal ancestries, such as the Co'ark, Jarn, Giants, Varak, Vrjnhar, Saurvek, Ashka, Carrow, Leafia, Zeph, and Wirrun. In addition, the First Shard Gods appear. This age ends with the Unveiling.

  • Age of the Tower: The Nir'ae appear and eventually create the Aedir Empire, which spans the world. This age also sees the creation of Fej, Thornlings, Hulg'run, and Humans. This age ends with the cataclysm known as the Shattering.

  • Age of Rediscovery: The present age and the creation of the Kiska, Keth, Kivahr & Drakon ancestries.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.9aUFzpVzfkJ1UIZX]{World of Ember} in the present age is a land of staggering contrasts, defined by the weight of ancient secrets. It is a place where epic myths are not merely stories, where vast, sunless ruins and silent monuments whisper of a long-lost majesty of kingdoms and empires long dead. Yet atop these remnants stand vibrant, dynamic kingdoms and young nations, fiercely determined to carve out a future amid ever-present dangers. In some cities, it's easy to forget that dangers grow perceptibly darker just beyond thier walls. Beyond the flickering torchlight of civilization, the wilds are reclaimed by monsters that roam the dark, while ancient evils hide deep within the Pathways below.
The History.scoverview: The history of the Ember setting is vast, taking place over millions of years with some cultural memories dating back hundreds of thousands of years. Countless places, peoples, and events have been lost to the ravages of time, and the discovery of ancient artifacts in unexpected places is common. Myths and legends are also extremely prominent parts of many cultures in the world. Still, these spoken records are unreliable, and it can sometimes be hard to differentiate between truth and fiction.

Ordain.name: Ordain
Ordain.text:
• Keywords: Regional History, Present Day

  • Length: 807 Years

  • Other Names: The Foundation of Ordain.

Eight hundred and seven years ago, the citizens of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} city-state of Yarino were invaded from the north by the Kingdom Reysta, originating from the Tayan Heathlands. The people of Yarino at the time were led by a timid and ineffectual prince who had wasted his people's riches on extravagant palaces and lavish feasts for other nobles. As the war escalated and the poorly funded army of Yarino retreated to the city walls, a largely overlooked group of mystics who had begun calling themselves the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} began criticizing the prince, attributing the city's plight to his reckless greed.

When the Reysta armies reached the city, the terrified populace spiraled into a frenzy as the prince attempted to escape on ships chartered with the last of the city's wealth. The Speaker of the Sages, Adonia, had garnered immense respect for her impassioned speeches and sermons. She claimed that salvation for the people lay far to the east. Enraged and inspired, the common people assaulted the fleeing prince before he could board his ship. By all accounts, the prince was torn apart by a mob at the harbor and his name was lost to the annals of history. Adonia then rallied as many people as possible onto the waiting ships and set sail eastward. Miraculously, their journey into the Silken Sea and northward along the coast lasted many weeks, yet not one ship from the fleet was lost. Upon spotting the towering cliffs and blood-red fields of grass north of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}'s shores, the fleet anchored and began establishing a new settlement.

Soon after, the fledgling town was named @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, an ancient Yarino term that means "heart-born," and its inhabitants began calling themselves the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}. The Cindaric Sages emerged as a significant political force in the newly founded city, with many, if not all, citizens viewing Adonia as a holy saint sent by the heart of the world to guide them toward a greater destiny.

After the vast majority of the population fled Yarino, it was sacked and abandoned for several generations. However, in 1817 AS, Verena sent an expedition to reclaim the ruined city and begin rebuilding. The modern city of Yarino is therefore only related to the Ordani people in a vague historical context.

For the large majority of its history, Ordain has remained exceptionally stable and peaceful, with very few major events affecting its rise as one of the greatest cities in the known world. It has grown steadily in both population and scale. Due in part to the cooperation and shared governance across multiple organizations, no one group ever gained enough control over elements of the city to cripple progress. In addition, Ordain's position in the world was secure and entirely unthreatened by its neighbors, who largely supported the city's successes.

Regrettably, Ordain's recent history over the last twenty years has begun to turn the dial in the opposite direction and has been filled with increasingly turbulent events. The once peaceful and thriving city, is now confronting numerous issues that threaten and or place extreme pressures on the systems that many residents depend on to secure their futures.
Ordain.scoverview: Ordain was founded 807 years ago when refugees from the Kelmezian city-state of Yarino navigated far to the east in search of a peaceful and prosperous land. The history of the city is intricately tied to these founding people, who eventually called themselves the Ordani. Over time, Ordain transformed from a small encampment into a burgeoning town and then into a sprawling, colossal metropolis, expanding across several miles and housing a vast, diverse population.
Ordain.sgamemaster:
Timeline

[[/date AS1716]]

The Yarino refugees fleeing the Kingdom of Reysta arrive in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} and begin building the foundations of the city that will one day become @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}. They settle at the mouth of the River Destine, and at first, the people call their settlement @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.ZVtXK6l76dBvJLm0]{Exile's Landing} before eventually adopting the name Ordain after several years.

[[/date AS1722]]

In the early days of the city, many of the nobles who fled Yarino banded together to form House Komric, a trading powerhouse with enough capital to restrict and control the markets. At first, their intentions aligned with those of the common people, prioritizing growth and the security of the fledgling settlement; however, over time thier greed began to show, and they hoard wealth for themselves. This begins a slow-burning resentment for House Kormic under the surface.

[[/date AS1728]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher} is the only Trading House of Ordain, originally founded by Arcturians. Best friends Lottie and Cael left Arcturel in the early days of Ordain to offer expertise to the city’s builders and soon became the go-to trading house for stone and metal mining. In the generations since, House Cevher has become a family affair, with nearly every prominent member able to trace themselves back to one or both of the founders.

[[/date AS1734]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} Explorers arrive in Ordain. Although they have made contact with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturians} in the past, they are more impressed and curious about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani} people's resolve to survive. They assist in some of the initial construction and expansion of the fledgling city, and the relationship between the two peoples has been friendly ever since. They also begin construction of a fortified keep several miles from the city at the mouth of the Ordain Bay, as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}, an organization that combats monsters and threats, forms.

[[/date AS1800]]

The independent Captain Red Bastilla is accused of smuggling goods into Ordain by House Komric. She is initially imprisoned before escaping thanks to help from her crew and flees the city. She begins a violent campaign of revenge against ships sailing under the flag of Kormic, and for many years, she remains a fugitive from the city. In her exile, she hires and recruits more disillusioned or disenfranchised Ordani who seek her out and forms a coalition of ships under her banner.

[[/date AS1831]]

The Veiled War, A clandestine war erupts in Ordain between House Komric and agents employed by a group of citizens in the city. This conflict, fought in shadows and back alleys, involved sabotage, espionage, and deception, tearing apart the very fabric of Ordani society without anyone ever realizing the scale of the conflict. The citizens opposed to the nobles in the city call themselves the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows} and eventually succeed in defeating House Komric, naming the agents that helped them the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain}. In the aftermath of the conflict, after nearly a year, House Komric and the old noble families from Yarino are wiped out, and both the Hallows and the Veiled Chain emerge as permanent organizations in the city.

[[/date AS1832]]

Following intensive calls for reform in the city from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}, the governing body of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate} is established, comprising three members from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}, and the combined members of the Trading Houses. During the formation of the first Ordinate, Captain Red Bastilla returns to the city at the head of her fleet and demands a seat on the ruling council. After tense negotiations, she forms @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla} as a permanent addition to the city's organizations, and Embers Bounty, her flagship, remains docked in the city for many years.

[[/date AS1892]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} discover the Shard Caverns beneath the city, after this point, the Sages become increasingly rich and powerful, using the crystal shards and gemstones found within to compete with the Trading Houses to some extent, though the Trading Houses still dominate the trade and growing prosperity that the city enjoys.

[[/date AS1900]]

The city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} celebrates the turning of the century with a once-in-a-lifetime festival called the Bloodruby Burning. Such is the fervor and excess of its people that the streets of Ordain, originally a brilliant white, are forever stained a dark red with both Bloodwood smoke and sap, as well as the blood of citizens crushed by the heaving crowds. The festival continues every year afterward, though on a much smaller scale and more tightly controlled by the city’s officials.

[[/date AS1925]]

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.Q0iioq0o2q011r8x]{Avilla} the Spellbreaker ascends as Shard God and is revealed to the city by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}. Six years later, in [[/date AS1931]], the city of Ordain is attacked, and a massive battle takes place in the Bay of Ordain. Although the attacking forces are defeated, the story of those events regarding the misuse of magic and power remains a @UUID[JournalEntry.SXu41X2NifZaSVqh.JournalEntryPage.wBfEdFXGf2pE20MF]{cautionary tale} for the people of Ordain. In the following year [[/date AS1932]] Avilla builds Spellbreaker Tower and afterwards, leaves the city and is never heard from again.

[[/date AS1973]]

Long before @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{House Lilifeld} rose to prominence, they were little more than a ragged band of explorers and backwater merchants from Ordain. But fate, or perhaps luck, changed everything when a storm blew their ships off course into the pristine harbors of the Isle of Kortos. There, they discovered vine-covered hills rich with ancient soil, natural terraces ideal for farming, and the slow-moving, moss-covered creatures now known as Terracants. Recognizing a rare opportunity, the settlers made a pact to keep the land both fertile, pristine, and profitable. House Lilifeld was born, not by blood but through shared ambition and a little luck.

[[/date AS2103]]

Holy Speaker @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.FaUiibd3k4gfrzry]{Caberi} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} discovers another @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystal} within the Shard Caverns. She keeps her ascension a secret, faking her own death, and moves to the Traders Corner district in Ordain to open a tailoring shop.

[[/date AS2097]]

A traveling eccentric troupe of artists from the Lumek visit Ordain and cause a social uproar in the city, exhibiting new fashions and ideas while hosting extravagant parties and galas. They are soon sponsored by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.FaUiibd3k4gfrzry]{Mistress Caberi}, who creates magical garments and clothing for the group, and they decide to remain in the city, forming a Trading House called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{Salva}.

[[/date AS2145]]

A @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.Ss3VAfrwO5B5qGHk]{Star Mage} enters Ordain and treats with the Ordinate, establishing a Gate in the city, after this point Ordain becomes more connected to many other distant places in the world and although the Gate cannot be used for large amounts of trade, many new lands and peoples become known to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}.

[[/date AS2213]]

As threats to the city of Ordain diminish and the area becomes increasingly peaceful, many of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.0YvoRkcs1BxtRiQz]{Vrjnhar}, who founded the organization, leave the region. The number of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} members drops to record lows in the subsequent years, and much of the Rusted Fortress on Bura Island outside Ordain is left abandoned.

[[/date AS2245]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} organization begins as a loose affiliation of five adventurers and scholarly explorers – known as the Five Founders– they unite in a mission to kill the carnal dragon Harathraxes that claimed a section of the Pathways under the Arctus Plateau. After this point, the group decided to dedicate their efforts to understanding the world of Ember's ancient history.

[[/date AS2313]]

Darik Melsbow, a priest of the Cindaric Sages, discovers a dangerous truth: the power of the Heart of Ember is gradually weakening over time. He brings his concerns to the Holy Speaker but is ignored and eventually stripped of his rank within the order for trying to spread this knowledge. Bitter and angry, Darik leaves and heads to the town of Talei in the Bloodwoods, north of the city. There, working in secret, he founds the much more active organization of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries}.

[[/date AS2448]]

@UUID[Actor.KQ9uGdZu6zDlM66n]{Jon Vastil} is made the Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages and enjoys a long tenure of peace for many years. His deeply spiritual attitude towards problems, however, begins to slowly erode the faith of the common people in the sage's ability to respond to problems.

[[/date AS2488]]

Darion the Soulthief of House Bastilla returns from the Cascilian Republic after helping to destroy a large undead fleet constructed by the Blood Barons. To better make his exploits known, he showers the city in riches. For several years he hosts parties, parades, and commissions song and painting about his greatest accomplishments. This helps drive House Bastilla into a position of power and influence in the city which it had previously lacked.

[[/date AS2493]]

Darion the Soulthief of House Bastilla proclaims his intention to sail to the Spiritlands and sets off from Ordain. He is not heard from again. Not long after, a fleet of warships from the Lumek arrive hunting Darion and his crew for crimes they never publicly disclose. The fleet departs once its captains conclude that Darion is not within the city.

[[/date AS2505]]

A poor harvest in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kethil} Villages across the sea and the unease following the recent quake led to a period of minor unrest and rationing for several months in Ordain. Though the situation is rare and resolved quickly by the Trading Houses with the purchase of food from several of the Southern Waerd Bastions, as a result, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries} gain momentum among the angry populace in the city.

[[/date AS2507]]

@UUID[Actor.oGmkdFWZjiawZpbK]{Alar} passes through Ordain, she stays for several months, interacting with ordinary citizens and her own temple followers in the city in secret. Few in the city are aware of her presence. She leaves just as mysteriously, leaving behind a glowing orb upon the altar of her temple.

[[/date AS2512]]

A massive earthquake hits the Arctus Plateau and the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, centred below the city in the Shard Caverns, the quake topples many buildings and kills roughly a thousand citizens across the city. New building codes are enforced and magical wards are employed across the city to protect against such events in the future. Building repairs are still ongoing for some of the larger structures damaged by the event. After the quake, Aster children are born more frequently in the following decade. This event comes to be known by a few names within Ordain, including the Stonehollow Quake.

[[/date AS2513]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} hosts the first Expedition Challenge, an intense competition where several young adventuring teams are pitted against one another in various challenges across the city of Ordain and the Arctus Plateau. @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} becomes a well-known celebrity in the city after winning with her team, and the following year, she explores an ancient fallen Skyhold of the Vaznor in the distant Shana Mountains to the north.

[[/date AS2514]]

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune} is approached by @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss}, although only its current leaders, @UUID[Actor.z1Ttp0q6CAtjDphl]{Sticks}, @UUID[Actor.OOO380zs3xZYG9PI]{Hephiss Wandren}, and Grimclaw are aware of Zerranyss's identity; even they are not privy to the entire story and are used as willing pawns in the Pale Dragons' schemes.

[[/date AS2519]]

@UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss}'s actions and schemes begin to have an increasing effect on Ordain and across the Arctus Plateau as the various relationships between the Trading Houses, the Cindaric Sages, and the Hallows begin to break down, with tensions rising. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune} ramps up bandit attacks across the region, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]{Mutagists} begin to expand operations, building new laboratories for experimentation.

[[/date AS2520]]

@UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerrnayss}'s schemes begin to fall into place. In his human guise as @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith}, he becomes the Steward to the Holy Speaker of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}. While not in control of the sages officially, his power over the organization is now overwhelming, and he has many supporters.

[[/date AS2522]]

The venerable Guildmaster of the Anachraenum, Veron Longspear, dies unexpectedly while visiting a research site in the Ruinous Crags. The cause of his death remains mysterious, with rumors and theories circulating among the Anachraenum members. His successor, @UUID[Actor.FYprIclhoDOI8FI4]{Arcos Sarinland}, is untested and only gains the title of Guildmaster after @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} declines the responsibility.

[[/date AS2522]]

Ambassador @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.68Deh9LMWYnPjeX0]{Loris Tezran} travels to @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain }as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire's} Ambassador to facilitate an open trade agreement between the city and the Empire. This marks the first official ties between the two nations.

[[/date AS2523]]

The second Expedition Challenge is set to take place this year, even though the city is becoming increasingly fractured, @UUID[Actor.FYprIclhoDOI8FI4]{Arcos Sarinland} hopes it will bring people together and calm tensions.

Troll Invasions.name: Troll Invasions
Troll Invasions.text:
Lore Summary

After the Unveiling, the Giants slowly push the small packs of Trolls out of the Shana Mountains in the center of the Aterican continent. Unfortunately, this causes the Trolls to swarm in massive numbers and attack the ancient cultures of the Vaznor and the Windbare, utterly annihilating them over the course of five hundred years.

In the aftermath of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.10gWEDeJX8aj4L3u]{The Unveiling}, which saw the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.n8XfdXtjFxvpAE7a]{Giants} begin to settle in the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.VxA0UsGvDbDn8SdO]{Shana Mountains}, they soon found that the cold, perilous peaks were already inhabited by small packs of creatures called @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.t0uXEiiy4hN4XBeX]{Trolls}. Possessing both ancient magical abilities and vast physical strength, along with a considerable height difference, the Giants were nearly invulnerable to the Trolls' attempts to resist. Over the course of a few decades, the Trolls were pushed out of their ancestral peaks and forced into the northern lowlands, and with unimaginable fury, they surged like a tide into the territories of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.o38uqC8NLxOWxA4i]{Vaznor} and Windbare. It is thought that before the displacement, the Trolls were vicious but never truly united in any great numbers. Unfortunately, the northern lowlands proved to be an abundant breeding ground, and their population exploded.

What followed was a brutal, one-sided conflict that spanned half a millennium. The Trolls were relentless, driven by a primal need for new territory. As the invasions unfolded, it became clear that whenever the Troll packs found or took over an area or settlement with abundant food resources their population would quickly multiply in a matter of months. While the Varak (the people of the Vaznor cities) held significant advantages, most notably their advanced technology and their ability to fly, they lacked the raw physical strength to hold ground against the sheer mass and power of a Troll horde. The Varak could harass from the skies, but they could not stop the trolls from overrunning their streets and tearing down their flying settlements whenever they attempted to land.

One by one, the shining jewels of the north were extinguished, and the vast Vaznor kingdoms fell into ruins. The last great Vaznor bastion, the city of Kettera, stood as a defiant island in a sea of Trolls for centuries, but it eventually succumbed, marking the functional end of the Vaznor. After the fall of the last Vaznor city, the northern reaches became the territory of the Trolls, and they have claimed the vast region ever since. Over time, Trolls have pushed further south, often clashing with emerging cultures and nations, and while the Trolls are often a terrible blight, they have yet to boil over into an unending swarm, at least so far.
Troll Invasions.scoverview: As the Giants emerged from the Pathways, abandoning their ancestral homes and cities in the darkness, they encountered small packs of vicious Trolls, living among the towering peaks of the Shana Mountains. The Giants that would become the Shent were not yet adept at foreseeing future events and, without realising the consequences, drove the Trolls from the mountains into the north of the world. Unfortunately, this act had a devastating effect on the northern regions of Aterica, destroying many ancient kingdoms and entire cultures over the next several centuries.

Aran.name: Aran
Aran.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Aran.scoverview: The Aran Sub-Continent, also known as the Aran Peninsula, is a pivotal region in the history of Ember, as it is the birthplace of the ancient Jarn and then Humanity. It is an extremely ancient land filled with lost and forgotten ruins, incredible artifacts, and dangerous creatures. Although it was the birthplace of Humanity almost three and a half thousand years ago, its relevance has diminished greatly, and humans are no longer the dominant species in the region. Instead, the ancient city of Ancalen is ruled by the Railen people, who treat human relics and history with considerable disdain.

Shana Mountains.name: Shana Mountains
Shana Mountains.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Shana Mountains.scoverview: The Shana Mountains are a massive range of peaks that spans across Aterica, which are otherwise commonly referred to as the Giants Mountains or the Spine of Ember. These peaks were home to the ancient Shent culture, which built many wondrous structures across and beneath its peaks. The Shana Mountains are often categorized into three ranges: southern, middle, and northern.

Corebright Forest.text:
Under Construction

Corebright Forest.scoverview: The Corebright Forest is made up of many towering Elderbark trees that cover a colossal expanse at the centre of the Aterican continent.

Lowlands.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Lowlands.scoverview: The Lowlands are a small subcontinent of Aterica that lies to the south-east, separated by the thin Strait of Smoke that allows ships to pass from the west to the east. The Lowlands are a hot, humid, and dangerous land with thick jungles and deep, impassable swamps covering most of its landmass.

Revis.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Revis.scoverview: Revis is also known as the Reaver Ocean and is a vast stretch of deep water between Aterica and the Spiritlands. Crossing to the Spiritlands physically is almost impossible due to the massive waves, storms, and dangerous monsters lurking in the deep.

Yawning Sea.text:
Under Construction

Yawning Sea.scoverview: The Yawning Sea lies between the Lumek Homelands and the Lowlands, with the Cascaal Peninsula to the north. Deep trenches and dark waters are home to terrible ancient monsters that often rise to the surface and attack passing ships.

Duskflare Jungles.text:
Under Construction

Duskflare Jungles.scoverview: The murky jungles of the Lowlands are home to some of the most savage, and brutal monsters in the world, ancient crocodilian retpiles, ambushing Spiders and vicious predatory insects.

Dracanis Peaks.text:

Dracanis Peaks.scoverview: The Dracanis Peaks are home to a large population of Cruel Dragons, with reports of over ten fully grown adults living among the towering mountains peaks.

Burial Plains.scoverview: The Dustlands and the Burial Plains lie to the south of the Arctus Plateau after the unhinged wizard Leatic attempted to commune with Akon and brings forth an infestation of machines.

Arctus Plateau.name: Arctus Plateau
Arctus Plateau.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and subject to change in future updates.

  • Cultures: The primary culture group in the region is @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian}, but pockets of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.A1uPGhtaDifW8Sph]{Bejak}. In the city of Ordain the primary culture group is @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}, a metropolitan offshoot of Arcturian culture influenced by the steady foreign trade the city sees.

  • Settlements: Numerous small communities, towns, and villages dot the region. Major population centers include Ordaine, Seawall, Redrak, and Arcturel.

  • Economy: Agriculture and Livestock are primary industries in the region, textiles, stone, and gems make up secondary industries, all of which see regular export from major ports such as Ordain and Seawall. Ordain stands as the largest economic power in the region.

  • Politics: While numerous smaller political organizations and ideologies exist, the dominant political power in the plateau is the city-state of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, which exerts considerable pressure on surrounding communities by way of the organizations that operate under its auspices, including the Trading Houses, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}. While smaller organizations exist and wield considerable power in their respective realms, they are considered secondary to the influence of Ordain.

Environment

The Arctus Plateau features extraordinary diversity of terrains including mountains and highlands, windswept grasslands and forbidding forests, down to lush coastal wetlands and rocky oceanside cliffs. Despite this variance, the region shares some unifying qualities: The land is often rugged, and rocky, with plateaus and cliffs constantly breaking the skyline, forcing inhabitants to take winding routes as they travel. The region itself is even surrounded by jagged, inhospitable terrain that makes entry and exit difficult outside of specific locations.

Canyons and valleys carved by ancient events both geological and mythical cut across the plateau, while sprawling plains and river systems define the region’s more habitable expanses. Across these varied landscapes environmental hazards such as flooding, wildfires, and rockfalls are common, creating countless challenges for the locals to overcome.

The land’s climate is predominantly shaped by its elevation and ruggedness, giving rise to distinct dry summers in the majority of biomes, with pockets of microclimates influenced by nearby bodies of water, sudden elevation changes, and the residual effects of mystic upheaval.

Ecology

The flora and fauna of the Arctus Plateau are marked by resilience, adaptability, and, magical traits that grant them unique edges in their respective environments. The vast environmental diversity of the plateau demands the beings that inhabit it to be equally as diverse or perish when meeting some predator that has. This makes for an unpredictable, and often perilous region for the beings that call it home.

Plant life across the region is dominated by hardy grasses and shrubs adapted to their localized biomes, but capable of spreading far and wide no matter the conditions. Here, tall grasses thrive in fire-scorched savannas, and crowd out weaker plants in magically tainted forests, while the verdant river valleys, deltas, and lakes become overgrown with wild plants taking advantage of the rich soil and ample water.

Animal life is equally diverse and competitive, with each biome hosting species adapted to its specific challenges and unique dangers under threat of eradication. Predators are prominent and specialized here, with the boundaries between biomes only serving to create new opportunities for these creatures to adapt their hunting methods to the expanded prey on offer.

Lore

The Arctus Plateau was settled in pieces and waves across the centuries. Numerous societies have risen and fallen in this time, including the ancient Aediri, Shent, and Sedyri people who all had settlements in this region at one point or another before their respective collapses.

Records, ruins, and burial sites still persist in far-flung corners of the Plateau and speak of settlers that arrived thousands of years ago on the heels of mystical cataclysm and upheaval to claim pieces of the plateau for themselves.
Arctus Plateau.scoverview: The Arctus Plateau, the windswept lands that lie to the west of the great city of Ordain, populated by a few isolated highland villages and towns. This barren and isolated highland plateau is rife with rocky outcrops, and long winding roads between fields of dry grasses and isolated trees.

Dead Mire.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Dead Mire.scoverview: The Dead Mire is a the small region of swamplands that lies to the south of the Arctus Plateau.

Kadísos.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Kadísos.scoverview: The mistbound island of Kadisos is a mysterious, ancient island that lies between the Lowlands and the Arctus Plateau. It is a small tropical island, covered in jungle in the midst of tempestuous seas and surrounded by jagged rocks and reefs, with a hunger for the hulls of passing ships. It has little to offer the average soul, and little more to the brave and daring that seek to explore its heart.
