Cascaal Peninsula.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Cascaal Peninsula.scoverview: The Cascaal Peninsula is a golden land filled with soft grasses, gentle hills, and scattered groves of forests. It is surrounded by waters, bays, shallow seas, and lakes, with plenty of natural resources to support the burgeoning Cascilian Republic.

Moiran Bonelands.name: Moiran Bonelands
Moiran Bonelands.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Moiran Bonelands.scoverview: The Moiran Bonelands are a region that was once home to temperate forests and a gentle climate of soft winds and light rains. Today, however, it is a place of death, fear, and terrible nightmares. The land itself is cursed and broken, where the light of Lantyr no longer penetrates an ever-present blanket of black clouds.

Sinkhole Depths.name: Sinkhole Depths
Sinkhole Depths.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Sinkhole Depths.scoverview: The Sinkhole Depths are an extremely deep section of the Pathways that drops down several miles into pitch-black darkness and an almost otherworldly environment. Layers of increasingly dangerous, dark, and bleak areas that become more and more challenging to survive. The full descent has never been accomplished and no one is entirely sure what lies at the very bottom of the depths, but the town of Arcturel and the people that make the strange town their home regularly descend into the upper areas to farm a material known as Inkaro Pearls.

The Broken Tower.name: The Broken Tower
The Broken Tower.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
The Broken Tower.scoverview: The colossal Broken Tower is a gleaming reminder of the cataclysmic destruction of the Shattering. Massive chunks still orbit the apex of the tower, hinting at the extreme magical forces that remain active to this day. Visible from every corner of the surface, the ruined structure is so vast that it often dominates the horizon, casting deep shadows across the entire continent of the Starshield during dusk and dawn.

The Starshield.name: The Starshield
The Starshield.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
The Starshield.scoverview: The Starshield is one of the smallest continents, located at the precise center of the world's surface, with eight points that roughly align with the cardinal and intermediate directions of Ember itself. The Starshield was once the center of everything. It is here that the ancient Aedir built their vainglorious empire thousands of years ago, along with their crowning achievement — the Sun Tower.

Aterica.name: Aterica
Aterica.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Aterica.scoverview: Aterica is the largest continent on the surface, often called the Shardstone Continent; it is both the largest and the most storied in its history and peoples. Home to no less than five subcontinents, one of which is the Aran Peninsula, which gave rise to the ancient Jarn, the precursor ancestry. Aterica also has a veritable wealth of Shard Gods that have found and communed with Heart Crystals, and there are so many separate cultures and realms that, currently, no less than six different entire pantheons exist at once.

Kessia.name: Kessia
Kessia.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Kessia.scoverview: Kessia is the only continent deeply connected to Aterica, with burgeoning trade routes, diplomatic ties, and a history of shared struggles. Kessia was once said to be home to the largest Aedir colonies, but they were completely annihilated during the Shattering. Within the heart of the continent, the great Obsidian Desert formed and spread to cover the vast majority of its landmass.

Mort'oliss.name: Mort'oliss
Mort'oliss.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Mort'oliss.scoverview: Across the vast Reaver Ocean lies Mort'oliss, often called The Spiritlands; it is a continent realm presided over by the Elder God Sockets and where the Souls of Mortal peoples travel to when they die. The Spiritlands are not connected physically to any other continent, as they are separated by a barrier that supposedly prevents the living from crossing over, not to mention no one is particularly keen to visit the realm of the dead.

Jurin.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Jurin.scoverview: Jurin is an ancient and untamed continent as far away from Atercia as is possible on the surface world. Very little is known about its nature, except that many Thornlings tell a surprisingly consistent myth surrounding their origins and of a towering ancestry of peoples that hunt and kill Leviathans upon the distant continent.

Oakengarde.name: Oakengarde
Oakengarde.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.
Oakengarde.scoverview: Oakengarde is considered to be one of the most extreme, hostile, and dangerous places in the known world, with a terrifying ecosystem of deadly creatures and plants that prowl beneath the region’s colossal taigas and icy mountain slopes.

Akazea.text:
Under Construction

This page is currently being developed and no further information is available for Early Access.

Akazea is one of the largest subcontinents on Ember's surface, and it is home to many different biomes and environments. The lands are extremely mountainous, with many towering peaks and plateaus, gorges, and ravines.

Tai'or.text:

Ordain.name: Ordain
Ordain.text:
• Keywords: Grand, Beautiful, Peaceful

  • Dominant Ancestry: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z]{Human}

  • Secondary Ancestries: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.rl7QgGAIaYqAxLYq]{Kivahr}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.0YvoRkcs1BxtRiQz]{Vrjnhar}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.bOPreM2lwc0iB46X]{Keth}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.K28cb1q6tvU8FP8B]{Hulg'run}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.QIC15zfqh4Ndzgha]{Ashka}

  • Technology: Late Bronze Age, early iron/steel production, enhanced with magic

  • Religion: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}.

  • Politics: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate Council}, Shared Power between the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, Trading Houses, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}.

  • Architecture: Rounded red rooftops, glittering white stone with faint rain staining and red foliage, black volcanic rock foundations.

  • Settlement Type: Metropolis

  • Population: 575,000

Ordain is a vast and diverse city that has grown quickly into a powerhouse of influence in the eastern known world. Its various political frameworks are intentionally designed to ensure stability both in the short and long term, supported by a responsible and proactive population committed to maintaining order. As a result, the city is safe, peaceful, and often focused more on local matters such as trade disputes, taxes, construction, and the social well-being of its citizens rather than any expansionist or militaristic matters.. There is minimal interest in allocating the city's resources or focus to external issues, and the city government almost never interferes with other nations’ problems or issues, except in specific compassionate circumstances, such as providing assistance after monster attacks or natural disasters.

Governance & Laws

Ordain has three major political groups: the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, the Trading Houses, (@UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{Bastilla}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{Cevher}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{Lilifeld}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{Salva} & @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{Wandren}) and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}, with elected representatives sitting on the governing body called the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate} or the Ordinate Council. There are also many other organizations that make up the city, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain}, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}, and these groups also follow the city's overarching rule of law. Fundamentally, the city operates under a strange system of representative democracy, where the three major factions elect three representatives to the Ordinate, resulting in nine members who legislate, adjudicate legal conflicts, and manage the city’s overall budget, which includes managing taxes across the city.

Traditionally, this sharing of power across different groups has led to a highly stable government, as no one group or individual is ever in a position to enforce unjust or disruptive laws alone. This, however, does not mean that conflict between the groups and their representatives does not exist, as discussions often flare into long, heated arguments and political maneuvering to sway others to certain causes. As the Trading House representatives are often solely concerned with the city's economy and their own houses' wealth, they are frequently at the forefront of increasing tax discussions, while the Hallows, which represents the ordinary people of the city, are vehemently opposed. The Cindaric Sages representatives are often neutral in these matters and are swayed or convinced through various means.

The process of electing representatives differs for each of the major groups. For the Trading Houses, each greatly desires a representative to be elected from their own house, and every five years, intense campaigns erupt behind closed doors among the Trading Houses' members in the Assembly on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.1RJRU9XGC5WBm2Kq]{Assembly Hill}. Representatives are chosen through a series of votes, with the top three candidates receiving the most votes being elected. In contrast, the Hallows also hold elections for three members every five years, but the general populace of the city votes for candidates in very public elections where political campaigning is heavily regulated so that it is as fair and open as possible. It is deemed highly inappropriate for Hallows representatives to highlight their individual character traits, and instead, they tend to focus on appearing connected and compassionate with people's current concerns as possbile in order to garner the most votes. Finally, Cindaric Sage representatives are chosen from among their own members in secret, and in most cases, unless it would otherwise cause dissent, the Holy Speaker appoints three of the most competent individuals, who sit on the Ordinate for a decade.

Once the ruling council of the Ordinate has eventually agreed upon a new law, it's the responsibility of the various other groups in the city to enforce it. This is also aided by the city’s overall high degree of societal well-being and community involvement, which means ordinary citizens often take the law seriously and help with enforcement on an individual level. Several of the city’s organizations are also key parts of the process, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain}, which ensures threats like violent crime or organized crime are investigated, and the Hallows itself, where people are taken to be judged and sentenced for any crimes they commit. Other organizations, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}, and the guards of the various Trading Houses, act in official capacities when required to arrest and maintain order directly on the streets of the city, although this is rare.

Ordain enforces a structured yet measured system of justice, guided by the Hallows and overseen by the Ordinate. Punishments emphasize restitution and civic responsibility over cruelty, though grave offenses are met with severity.

  • Theft and Fraud: Offenders are required to return stolen property or its full value and serve a period of compulsory community labor.

  • Assault: Penalties range from home or Hallows detention to formal trial and restitution, depending on the severity of the act.

  • Misuse of Magic: Charges are determined by the nature of the offense. Offenders may be temporarily restrained under abjuration wards and held in Spellbreaker Tower or face standard criminal proceedings.

  • Necromancy: Outright forbidden within the city. Practitioners face imprisonment within the Spellbreaker Tower or exile pending trial.

  • Disturbing the Peace: Typically punished with fines and, in repeated or severe cases, a short-term peace-binding enchantment such as geas or command.

  • Smuggling: Confiscation of goods and fines equivalent to their market value are standard. Repeat offenders risk exile following trial.

  • Murder or Attempted Murder: Tried before the highest Hallows courts. Conviction carries long-term Spellbreaker imprisonment or, in exceptional cases, capital punishment.

  • Violation of City Ordinance: First offenses receive formal warnings; subsequent violations result in fines or enforced community labor. Severe or repeated breaches may lead to trial and exile.

  • Vandalism: Offenders must repair or pay for damages and serve community labor. Repeat or malicious cases may result in enchantment bindings or exile.

Magic & Technology

In Ordain, magic is an intrinsic part of life, embraced by the people in everyday life without any formal structures such as schools or strict academic institutions. Instead, the practice and understanding of magic is shared among individuals. Magical items and objects are widespread across the city as Ordain imports large quantities of magical tools or objects from cultures such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan}, or the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{ Kithil}. Markets are filled with merchants showcasing magically enhanced goods, tools, and even weaponry. Finding someone within the city who can help with a magical problem is not difficult, as several shops and stores run by wizards or mages exist throughout the various districts, trading in services and goods to help with everyday issues.

Finding more advanced magical aid is slightly more challenging but follows the same pattern. Throughout the city are various powerful entities that may be able to assist with a dire situation or problem. The resident Custodian Star Mage of Ordain, @UUID[Actor.XrFDJNn1Fa7hopqR]{Eveis Brightstone}, is one such entity. She is responsible for the APN connection and resides in Lumiere Wharf. Eveis is primarily concerned with the maintenance, protection, and use of the teleportation gate, but they are known to help those in great need occasionally. Other powerful magic users include several of the high priests of the larger temples in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.XUn8UELVkQmnCI78]{Temple Ward} district, and the Curator of the Anachraenum@UUID[Actor.GA8VFWysoIYfNWCL]{Adelyne Goss}.

Culture & Society

Culture in Ordain is overwhelmingly @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.RxhlhTWqJqB1cZxY]{Ordani}, with communities of other cultures scattered throughout the various districts. While Ordain as a city and the Ordani are extremely supportive of other cultures, and the city is a diverse multicultural hub to some degree, other cultures tend to be largely self-contained, and the dominance of the Ordani way of life is evident across the city as a whole. This means that Ordani festivals or holidays, such as the Bloodruby Burning, Seasons End, Worker's Day, and Hearts Feast, are celebrated throughout the city regardless of cultural background. Additionally, other cultures adopt Ordani cultural practices, including strong social interactions and interest in various clothing and shopping trends.

Bloodruby Burning

Seasons End

Worker's Day

Carnival of Remira

Hearts Feast

Within the city, there is a strong emphasis on community involvement, with festivals, markets, and a vibrant nightlife being crucial social events where citizens connect, share ideas, and celebrate. Culinary arts and diverse dishes are an integral part of Ordani culture, influenced by traders and travelers. Local cuisine prioritizes fresh ingredients and exhibits bold spices or sweetness, with creative and interesting new concepts emerging constantly. Communal meals are common, where families and friends gather in restaurants or outside brasseries to share dishes and drinks that highlight flavors, colors, and the occasional touch of magic, such as foods that may glitter under moonlight or change flavor.

Perhaps the most important cultural touchstone of Ordain is the almost omnipresent fascination among the Ordani with clothing and fashion. To the Ordani, attire is not merely a matter of practicality or aesthetics—it is the purest expression of identity, artistry, and social philosophy. Every fold, color, and fabric carries meaning, communicating profession, faith, or mood with subtle precision. Styles shift with the seasons and with political or spiritual trends, and the skilled artisans who craft garments are held in the highest regard, their creations treated as both personal statements and living art.

Religion in Ordain is centered around the teachings of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, a predominantly passive belief system that traditionally works seamlessly with the Ordani lifestyle. The Cindaric Sages do not attempt to convert or convince others; instead, helping and supporting the people of Ordain is seen as their primary duty. In addition, many residents worship various individual deities from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}, a pantheon of deities representing various aspects of life, nature, and magic that are all accepted and followed by people in the eastern regions of the known world.

Landmarks & Districts

Ordain is a vast city spread over multiple miles of the Arctus Plateau and encompassing over fifty distinct districts. These districts vary significantly, with many serving specific functions, such as being the home territory of one of the Trading Houses or the base of operations for an organization like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0]{All-Fable Keep} for the Anchraenum. Some districts are dedicated to trade, featuring warehouses, storerooms, granaries, and transport offices, while others cater to residential life or reflect Ordain's passion for clothing, offering countless shops, eateries, and venues for socializing over fine wines in the evenings. The river Destine runs through the middle of the city and flows into the Bay of Ordain, and many of the districts next to the river feature large, expansive canal systems to move people, goods, and services quickly and efficently.

Beneath the city, Ordain has miles of sprawling sewers, drainage channels, and waterways carved deep into the black basalt rock foundations. These are far removed from the traditional, dirty, and foul-smelling sewers found elsewhere in the world; they are largely clean, massive in size and depth, and are maintained by a combination of manual labor and magic by the city's inspectors, who are employed by the Hallows.

Ordain is not only home to thousands of houses and everyday buildings but also to a number of colossal mega structures that took years or even centuries to complete. These include the two largest structures in the city, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Mnh1EGR4ir1wpumM]{Ordinate}, which stands atop the city's central plateau, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.GlbJezRw2ecnVIsx]{Cindarin Temple}, the home of the Cindaric Sages and the center for the religion. Other large and impressive structures include the vast All-Fable Keep at the southern end of the city, home to the Anachraenum, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.ThsrAwMhXhmowirO]{Hallows} complex in the north of the city, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.J37jJxiegQk11IcL]{Spellbreaker Tower}, the city's prison facility in the west.

Currency & Economy

The majority of Ordain's economy relies on the Trading Houses and their impressive holdings across the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} and beyond. Within Ordain itself, a vast array of valuable goods is produced through local manufacturing in workshops and specific districts, which transform raw materials into luxury items. Key exports and items include exquisite textiles and clothing, high-quality ceramics, and finely crafted jewelry, which are highly sought after in distant markets and within the city itself. Additionally, the city is famous for its spices and herbs, known for their unique flavors and medicinal properties, gathered from across the world and refined to create a rich culinary landscape. Ordain is also home to many forges and smithies in the northern part of the city, which gather and refine precious metals and gemstones mined from nearby and distant regions.

Ordain is a massive importer of raw foodstuffs to feed its large population and has a strong trading relationship with nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.8cGPxMRewkagoIvc]{Arcturian} settlements such as Toraga, which exports significant quantities of wheat and barley, as well as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} city of Luen, which exports large quantities of fruits and vegetables to Ordain. The city also imports goods such as fine wines from Kortos Isle vineyards, luxury crafted wooden and stone items from various Arcturian settlements, and technological innovations from other cultures, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire.

Ordain's five coins are considered the standardized currency not only in Ordain or the Arctus Plateau but also in the Lowlands, amongst the Kithil, and traded in large quantities in many other nations, kingdoms, and cultures in far-off places.

In addition, Ordain also trades and uses various precious Shards, which are gemstones mined in secret from the Shard Caverns. The Cindaric Sages explain the usage and appearance of these Shards as sacred abilities that only Sages can manifest and form after many years of deep contemplation and connections with the Heart of Ember. These Shards are used extensively by the Cindaric Sages as currency, but much of the population uses them in lieu of coinage as well, if they can get their hands on them.

Ordain.scoverview: Ordain is a vast and strategically located metropolis, regarded as one of the largest hubs of trade and commerce in the known world. Constructed from glittering white stone, Ordain sits on the far northeastern edge of the Arctus Plateau, and its crimson-red rooftops have a slight reflective quality, often giving the impression that the city itself shines with light. The inhabitants of Ordain are known as the Ordani. They are generally uninterested in expansion or military conquest, displaying contentment in residing solely within the city rather than spreading out to settle in other regions. Despite their tranquility, Ordani culture and influence extend worldwide, as they travel far and wide to seek out goods for trade. Additionally, the Ordani language has become the common language for many across the known world.

Old Carinth.scoverview: Old Carinth is one of the oldest cities in the world, having been inhabited for nearly three thousand years. It was founded by some of the first migrating humans from the Aran Penisula as they moved north to explore the continent of Aterica. Today, it is ostensibly the most powerful of the Kelmezian city-states and a truly colossal edifice of architecture with thousands of residential, farming, and industrial layers of the city stacked on top of one another. It is an artificial mountain that is considered by many to be one of the most populated settlements on the surface of Ember, with millions calling the city home.

Star Academy.scoverview: The Star Academy is a distant Great City far from the continent of Aterica that rests upon the very edge of the world. It is the home of the Rhivan people and the powerful Star Mages organization. The entire city is considered part of the academy in many ways, with scattered libraries, research centers, and magical experiments all interconnected into the everyday lives of its inhabitants. The towering Main Academy structure at the city center houses some of the most important, secretive, and dangerous knowledge in existence, and it is also where the Star Mages portal network resides.

Ruined Towir.scoverview: The ruins of the capital city of the Aedir inside the Broken Tower at the center of the Starshield. Since the Shattering, the massive structure of the Broken Tower and the city within has been a mostly empty shell of its former glory. While none of the previous inhabitants survived the massive apocalyptic destruction that spread across the continent, souls of the Aedir that died afterward have been drawn here in the thousands of years since.

Caren'ac.scoverview: Caren’ac is a vast Great City of industry, military might, and technological innovation built around the edges of a long-dormant volcano. Its circular structures contain many concentric rings of aqueducts and bridges and countless waterfalls that spill over the edges and into a central deep lake, for this reason, the city is often called the Falling City. The origin of the initial structures and ruins discovered by humans thousands of years ago remains a mystery, but they are truly ancient and resistant to weathering and decay. It has comparatively recently become the capital of the Tayan Empire ever since the empire's foundation seventy-two years ago.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fHYfRhU3UKTc4HQl]{Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine} depicts an island at the center of Lake Jinro, where the climactic events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book of Tales} occur. An ancient Lunar Shine occupies the center of the island's hilltop precipice, which still seethes with primal magic to this very day.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fHYfRhU3UKTc4HQl inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The island known as Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine serves as the location for the climactic finale of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book of Tales}, in which the storyteller @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft} has tasked the party with the transcribing of five curious Arcturian stories — including her own.

Objectives

The area must be reached by water or air, and is surrounded on all sides by the aqueous terrain of Lake Jinro. The party will most likely arrive here via boat, along with the Amalthea Stonecraft herself, who they must escort to the precipice for an esoteric ritual of rejuvenation.

Once the characters reach the Lake Jinro Shrine, they must:

  • Ascend the switchback path to the island's precipice, where the eponymous Lunar Shrine awaits.

  • Help the Aster storyteller Amalthea Stonecraft complete her ritual of rejuvenation.

  • Survive a surprise attack from a Juvenile Garganthus, which has made its way to the surface of Ember from the Pathways deep below.

Illumination

Illumination here is mostly dependent on the time of day, since the location is fully open to the sky above. Additionally, when the six Altar Stones along the switchback path have been lit, each one of them radiates bright light for 10 feet and dim light for an additional 10 feet. And when the Lunar Shrine itself is active, each of its six menhirs radiates dim light for 10 feet.

Terrain

Most of the terrain here is treated as normal terrain. The waters of Lake Jinro are typically calm, with an extremely slow current that laps the shore with lazy regularity.

Elevation

Other than the recessed burrow of the Garganthus Tunnel and the scant areas beneath the boughs of the island's handful of trees, the island is open to the sky above. The hilly landmass winds its way upwards a total of 60 feet in elevation at the island's precipice (where the Shrine itself is located), with a 30-foot high halfway mark along the switchback path at the far eastern side.

Characters who wish to climb the steep rocky hillsides must succeed on a [[/skill ath 15]] check to scale the sheer and craggy earth. Critical failure results in [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage for every 10 feet the character falls during the attempt. Characters with a climb speed succeed on this check automatically. Any character who fails this check can repeat it as many times as they'd like.

Grave Blade Shore.name: Grave Blade Shore
Grave Blade Shore.text:
This rocky beach is decorated with an array of rusty swords, which jut from the water-lapped ground in solemn reverence to the unnamed warriors who once wielded them. Many of these ancient blades hang lurched in the sodden earth with aged resignation, while others stand resolute and unbothered by the relentless assault of time.

The Armory Beach

This nameless graveyard of rusted blades is a rather enigmatic feature of the island, and is the source of various rumors among people who speak of this storied place. The characters may examine this unnamed monument to fallen warriors to discover various clues about the island's ancient history, including the origin of the blades.

The Forgotten Armory

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check his 12]] check has heard rumors of this place while traveling the Golden Flats. Some say it's an essential part of one of the Shrine’s lunar rituals, while others maintain that the presence of this forgotten armory suggests the spellcasters of the Selenic Order who built this place were known for their martial prowess as much as their magical gifts.

  • Result of 15+: Studies have revealed the true origin of this beachside monument. The first blade left here was driven into the earth by the Selenic Order's leader, a soothsayer named Menodora Vhael, as a vow to her deceased partner — the brilliant Maziran swordmaster Eriss Khan. In the years that followed, each time the Selenic Order came to this place, an acolyte would leave a blade of their own here upon the beach. And on and on it went, until today.

Examining the Blades

A few of the blades adorning the beach here are considerably more interesting than their rusted mundane counterparts.

Any character with a [[/check prc 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check prc 13]] check while searching the armory beach is able to locate the following:

  • An assortment of 15 rusty @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepLongsword0]{Longswords}, 6 rusty @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepRapier0000]{Rapiers}, and 5 rusty @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepShortsword]{Shortswords}. These corroded, rust-covered blades are in extremely poor condition and worth only 10% of their listed value.

  • A relatively untarnished iron @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepShortsword]{Shortsword}.

  • An untarnished @UUID[Item.cdrBwNgq7TELiAb5]{Silvered Longsword}.

  • A curious blade at the center of the beach made of some strange alloy. This is in fact the @UUID[Item.ccEnySAwfrSnkvWS]{Blade of Eriss Khan}. If any character attempts to remove the Blade of Eriss Khan from its resting place, they are subject to the hazardous effects of the magical blade's violent curse. See "Removing the Blade of Eriss Khan" below.

Characters who succeed on the Intelligence (History) skill check above or who possess the [[/culture emberMaziran]] background can spot the telltale signs of Maziran smithing in the qualities of the Blade of Eriss Khan.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check arc 15]] check is able to notice a significant arcane component to the nature of the Blade of Eriss Khan and its creation.

Any character with a [[/check rel 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check rel 13]] check has heard dozens of tall tales about what happens when the sanctity of shrines and monuments are disturbed, and extends the same consideration to this place.

Furthermore, if @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft} is with the party, she strongly advises them against disturbing the blades strewn here upon the shore, but has little to offer in the way of explanation and is focused on the task at hand.

Removing a Blade from the Beach

Any character who removes any of the blades here (silvered, magical, or not) cannot benefit from the blessings of the Altar Stones along the @UUID[.KErwRkMymJdmM42p]{Switchback Path} or from the boons associated with Leaving an Offering (see below), nor can they use the mehirs at the @UUID[.CUBZWXArz36FtriO]{Ancient Lunar Shrine} as a spellcasting focus.

Removing the Blade of Eriss Khan

If the @UUID[Item.ccEnySAwfrSnkvWS]{Blade of Eriss Khan} is removed from its resting place, it adopts the Curse property and extends this hostile curse to whichever character takes it from the beach. The curse is exceptionally powerful, and a character does not have to attune to the Blade of Eriss Khan to become cursed by it.

Leaving an Offering

If the party members decide to leave offerings of their own here, they can each receive a temporary magical boon.

Any character who drives a blade of personal significance* into the ground here, to leave in perpetuity, becomes the target of both the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGuidance00]{Guidance} spell and the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplResistance]{Resistance} spell. The duration of this spell is 24 hours rather than 1 minute.

*A blade of personal significance could be an heirloom, a sword the character has used for more than one level, or simply a blade the character covets.

Forgotten Wreckage.name: Forgotten Wreckage
Forgotten Wreckage.text:
The splintered hull of a small rowboat is washed up on the stony beach here, split in twain alongside a scattered array of water-soaked flotsam.

The Sundered Rowboat

Overturned during its wreckage, the splintered hull of the damaged rowboat here provides a meager amount of shade for the gulls and crustaceans who intermittently call it home.

Searching the Wreckage

A few items of interest can be found among the splintered wreckage of the sundered rowboat here.

The eroded remains of a humanoid skeleton are tucked away inside the eastern section of the wreckage. The first character to search these remains can roll twice on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot (Arctus Plateau)} table to reveal what they find.

Any character with a [[/check prc 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check prc 13]] while searching the wreckage is able to locate a locked strongbox buried in the sand. The stongbox contains 8 @UUID[Item.hMeljYMb7OxbfNKv]{Iolite} gemstones worth 15 gp each and three @UUID[Item.iLPJi71wt1qECwkQ]{Bronze Ingots} worth 50 sp each.

Switchback Path.name: Switchback Path
Switchback Path.text:
An overgrown path winds its way up and around the forgotten hilltop island. You notice a small rune-marked altar made of rugged stone at the base of the switchback, and a handful of similar altars along the path as it curves upward.

The Altar Stones

This collection of six stone altars hewn from rough umber serves a mysterious purpose for most visitors of the shrine. However, legends hold true that those who pay proper ritualistic respects at each of these six altars will be blessed with a temporary cosmic boon.

As the party ascends the slow vertical incline that wraps itself counterclockwise up towards the island's hilly precipice, they may examine and interact with this tertiary collection of monuments to Ember's moons — and possibly receive a metaphysical boon by observing all six sacred rites associated with them.

Examining the Altars

Characters who solve the mystery of the Altar Stones will be able to grant the party a boon for the rest of their time here.

Any character who properly observes the ritual by placing the correct offering in all six altar bowls is able to activate a special magical effect. Once the sixth and final offering has been placed in its requisite bowl, each creature within 15 feet becomes the target of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.jZ6JNykRtdQ90MOo]{Shield of Faith} spell. The duration of this spell is 4 hours. This effect can only be activated once per week.

A successful [[/check arc 15]] allows a character to decipher the general purpose of the altars: observation of the complete ritual awards some kind of metaphysical boon, likely channeled through ancient abjuration magic that sits latent in the stone here.

The inscriptions etched on each of the altars are written in [[/language arcden]].

Ancient Lunar Shrine.name: Ancient Lunar Shrine
Ancient Lunar Shrine.text:
You come upon a circle of six large standing stones, each of them adorned with markings that evoke imagery of one of Ember's six moons. At the center of this circle of menhirs sits a huge stone dais, overgrown with grass and fractured by time and the elements. There is a welcoming tranquility here unlike any you've known, as if the standing stones themselves were waiting for the very moment of your arrival.

The Lunar Shrine

The island’s eponymous shrine is its most notable feature, and is a famed landmark region-wide. The menhirs that comprise the Shrine’s circle of standing stones correspond to each of Ember's six moons and are laced with their own peculiar veins of crystal or ore (rumored to have been hewn from the very moons themselves). Whatever the substances, these rare elements serve to focus potent magical energies both arcane and divine, and invite strangers the world over to come and behold their enigmatic splendor.

Exploring the Shrine

The Lunar Shrine is comprised of six standing stone menhirs and a circular stone dais that sits between them, overgrown and forgotten by time. Each of the menhirs corresponds to one of Ember's six moons — @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.smc0OuMxsxfcSdhR]{Aura}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.LKptgmc56euSOb0G]{Ragen} — and is laced with a small amount of ore that hails from is respective lunar body.

Any character with a [[/check prc 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check prc 13]] check while examining the menhirs is able to notice the curious ore woven into the stone. Additionally, a successful [[/check nat 15]] check confirms the lunar nature of the ore.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check his 13]] check can identify the standing stones as ancient Arcturian in origin, with trace elements of Shent design.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check arc 13]] is able to realize the purpose of the Lunar Shrine: to serve as a potent spellcasting focus for arcane, divine, or druidic rituals that harness the power of abjuration, divination, and transmutation magic.

  • [[/culture emberArcturian]] and [[/culture emberKithil]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] and [[/knowledge rituals]] also have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Characters who succeed on this check can decipher and understand the Shrine's potential as outlined below in The Shrine's Enchantments.

The Shrine's Enchantments

Arcane, divine, and druidic spellcasters alike can use the Lunar Shrine as a spellcasting focus in place of the components specified for any abjuration, divination, or transmutation spell. A character must be located within the circumference of the six menhirs to utilize the Shrine as a spellcasting focus.

The Lunar Shrine has additional properties, which can only be activated simultaneously once per week:

  • Until the character completes a long rest, saving throws against abjuration, divination, and transmutation spells cast by the character have @Advantage[-2].

  • A single spellcaster (chosen by the players or the GM) gains one bonus spell slot up to 5th level that can only be used to cast an abjuration, divination, or transmutation spell. This bonus spell slot is expended after the character completes a long rest, whether the spell was cast or not.

  • Additionally, the first character to use the Lunar Shrine as a spellcasting focus and succeed on another [[/check arc 13]] check is able to cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAugury0000]{Augury} spell until they complete a long rest, whether they know the spell or not.

  • After they complete a long rest, characters who utilize the Lunar Shrine's enchanted properties add one point of Lunar Attunement to their current Lunar Attunement level. A character cannot benefit from this effect more than once.

Garganthus Attack!

If the party lingers here for any reason, they must survive an attack from a Juvenile Garganthus — a savage subterranean predator that has recently emerged from the Pathways below the island, instinctively drawn to the magic of the Shrine's menhirs.

Once the party has had sufficient time to conduct an initial survey of the Shrine and its features, read the following aloud:

Just then, the earth below your feet rumbles and the trees nearby shudder in response. Before you can blink, a huge creature leaps from below to take its own place on the island's grassy precipice…

@Embed[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]

The Thing from the Pathways

The @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Juvenile Garganthus} that currently resides here is out of place in an ecological sense. Once slain, it's quite unlikely the Garganthus or another predator of the Pathways would inhabit the area.

Garganthus Tactics

As the @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Juvenile Garganthus} appears, it will attempt to use its @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI.Item.CRzOLEFazWl0RTjv]{Deadly Leap} early on, and will continue to use it while bounding around the area map.

Whenever targeted by a spellcaster or other ranged attacker, the Juvenile Garganthus will attempt to use its @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI.Item.SoSvzyNL9N64RnDq]{Improvised Missiles} action to disrupt the oncoming attacks.

As soon as possible, the Juvenile Garganthus will position itself to use its @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI.Item.WUynvoWXEsWcHyDl]{Maddening Screech} on the largest possible number of enemies, including spellcasters and any allied NPCs that might be present.

If any allied NPCs are left unattended, the Juvenile Garganthus will move towards them and engage one or more allies in melee combat. The Garganthus will redirect its attention to any other attacking party members or characters when and if they join the fray.

Looting the Garganthus Corpse

Once the Juvenile Garganthus is slain, a few items of interest can be found on its corpse or harvested from its remains:

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/check sur 13]] is able to harvest one @UUID[Item.6MkixQ3Kud91T4ng]{Garganthus Hide}, which can be used to fashion a dark leather armor that absorbs light.

  • The stomach of the Juvenile Garganthus can be searched for undigested loot. Any character who searches the corpse can roll [[/roll 1d2+1]] times on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot (Arctus Plateau)} table to reveal what they find in the monster's distended belly.

Loot-Lined Hollow.name: Loot-Lined Hollow
Loot-Lined Hollow.text:
You notice a sizable hollow in the trunk of the aged olive tree here. The dark opening seems like the perfect lair for some small creature, if only this remote island could sustain such wildlife.

Inside the Olive Tree

Characters who take a moment to examine the hollow cavity inside this ancient olive tree may be rewarded for their effort.

Examining the Hollow

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check prc 15]] check while searching the hollowed-out tree's interior is able to locate a dirt-covered @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.6eMHIQ2CGKpjTtWC]{Scroll Case} concealed deep within the mulch-lined insides of the rotting hollow.

The scroll case contains a @UUID[Item.v6MH11f5ByrHsHQy]{Rustvar Valleys Map} wrapped around a @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ.Item.oFkmR4GWboLHhAfJ]{Potion of Healing}.

Once a character reads it, the Rustvar Valleys Map reveals the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]{Storsa's Strand} Points of Interest on the Arctus Plateau Region Map.

Garganthus Tunnel.name: Garganthus Tunnel
Garganthus Tunnel.text:
A huge cave opening has been violently carved out of the earth here. Claw marks adorn the edges of the cave's dark and rugged mouth, which constantly exhales a hollow baritone wind.

The Garganthus Lair

This small cave is where the Juvenile Garganthus first emerged upon the surface of Ember. If the characters search the cave interior, they'll discover a few details about how and why it came to be — including hints of the inaccessible Pathways caverns that lurk beneath. Little else of value can be found here.

The cave interior, lined with the skeletal remains of various lake-dwelling creatures, tells a story of a hungry abomination that made its way to the surface world from somewhere dark and terrible far below. Your stomach tightens and your eyes sting as they confront a fetid, ammonia-laced odor left behind by the subterranean monstrosity.

Examining the Cave

Any character with a [[/check prc 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check prc 13]] check while searching the cave can recognize the persistence of huge claw marks throughout most of the cave's interior, as if the Juvenile Garganthus clawed its way out of the earth.

  • Result of 15+: The character can also detect the presence of collapsed earth at the rear end of the cave, with little chance of detecting what lies far beyond.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check nat 13]] check is able to identify the skeletal remains of the various creatures the Juvenile Garganthus has consumed here, which include the skeletons of beavers, grassland herons, and giant catfish (among others).

  • Result of 15+: An impassible cave-in lurks at the rear of the cave. While it once led somewhere far below the island, the collapsed earth currently obstructs this bygone passage for at least 50 or more feet. Any attempt to traverse the wall-to-wall rubble would prove overwhelmingly dangerous or futile. Most likely, the Juvenile Garganthus attempted to traverse a narrow fissure here smaller than itself, and destroyed the earthen tunnel in the process.

Altar of Akon.name: Altar of Akon
Altar of Akon.text:
Hewn from rough umber, the stone altar at the foot of the switchback path appears to be scribed with runic markings and adorned with a shallow stone bowl.

For details about the properties of the altar stones, consult "Examining the Altars" in the @UUID[JournalEntry.5sSPjtjFWhTo8dmZ.JournalEntryPage.KErwRkMymJdmM42p]{Switchback Path} section of the walkthrough.

Honoring the Shattered Moon

Any character with a [[/check prc 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check prc 13]] check while searching the altar is able to notice the tiniest of scratches on the surface of the bottom of the bowl.

Characters with [[/attunement emberAkon]] can feel a strong connection to the altar, as if it calls to them. They also feel a slight arcane vibration emanating from any bronze in their possession.

  • Inscription: "Honor the Sundered"

  • Offering: A broken item or something made of raw bronze.

Any character with a [[/check nat 12 passive format=long]] who succeeds on a [[/check ins 15]] check is able to associate the phrase "Honor the Sundered" with the Shattered Moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon} in the context of the island's history.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for Mythspire Observatory encountered in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100]{Ancient Paths} quest.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.RWj91gQguWOQcflB inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Illumination

Direct and diffuse light from the torn open ceilings of the structure provide dim light throughout the structure, with the deepest pockets of darkness being banished by wall-mounted lanterns burning with eternal blue light.

Terrain

Though once an enclosed structure with a massive dome of stone and glass, some catastrophic failure in the past has left these ruins open to the sky. The mountain winds howl through the gaps in ancient stone, making the ruins gloomy and cold at all times.

The high altitudes and dry air make the environment feel harsher than it is. Nothing lives here — no plants, no animals, the top of the mountain is barren and devoid of life.

The terrain is ancient ruins. Crumbling stone, uneven footing, and scattered debris make travel difficult in many places. The scale alone of this place makes it clear that this place was not built by or for conventional humanoids, but giants.

Elevation

The distance between levels is 30ft in most places, and stairways serve as difficult terrain due to the height of steps. Due to damage and decay in the structure, only the upper chambers and lower chambers are available, with the intervening levels too choked with debris to be accessible.

The central space of the ruins features a 300 foot descent to the lowest level.

Additional Gameplay

Falling Hazard

In the event that a character gets too close to any of the open edges of the scene the stone crumbles over foot. This results in a [[/save dexterity 14]] to jump back before being caught in the collapse. Failure leaves the character hanging from the edge.

A follow up [[/save strength 14]] allows the character to pull themselves up. If someone helps them, no check is needed.

Failure results in them falling again, causing them to land on a stone catwalk some 20 feet down, suffering [[/damage 20 bludgeoning]] damage as a result of falling.

Characters can climb back up from there with a successful [[/skill athletics 12]] check. If they have help of a rope or other climbing tools no check is needed.

Failure causes them to fall to the lower catwalk again.

In the event that a character gets too close to any of the open edges of the scene the stone crumbles over foot. A character can make a successful [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] to jump back before being caught in the collapse. Failure leaves the character hanging from the edge.

A follow up [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] allows the character to pull themselves up. If someone helps them, no check is needed.

Failure results in them falling again, causing them to land on a stone catwalk some 20 feet down, if they aren't able to tuck and roll to land safely, they'll suffer a [[/hazard 20 reflex health bludgeoning]]{Dangerous Fall}.

Characters can climb back up from there with a successful [[/skillCheck athletics 12]] check. If they have help of a rope or other climbing tools no check is needed.

Failure causes them to fall to the lower catwalk again.

Tower Descent.name: Tower Descent
Tower Descent.text:
As you descend into the darkness you can see a vast chamber awaiting you, large glimmering rune-stones affixed to the wall serving as the only source of light. The space is square, and adorned with ancient reliefs of towering figures twice your height at least.

The stone lift thuds abruptly at the end of its descent, the impact resounding through the dim chamber beyond. Your arrival disturbs the cool, dry air here, causing the scent of rot to drift in to greet you from somewhere nearby.

Familiar Wall Crystals

Glimmering, rune-carved crystals embedded in the wall faintly glow, their fading magic still powering the lift and providing contrast for the carvings in the stone.

Characters that completed the Over the Moon quest recognize these crystals as the runed crystals being made in the forest of stone ruins. They were likely being used to power the lift here.

A successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check here notes that these crystals are all nearly depleted, but haven't failed yet. While they could be removed, they would make returning to the upper chambers impossible if taken out.

Ancient Carvings

A successful [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] while looking over the carvings notes that there are seven figures, and each bear a large gem around their neck. They all appear to be directing their attention skyward, though damage to the upper sections of this chamber and the inherent darkness make it impossible to tell what they are looking at.

Examining the carvings with a successful[[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check leads you to believe these are priests of these ancient people, whom you suspect were Shent. Given what you know of Shent religion, this is probably depicting seven priests of the sky venerating or communing with the seven major celestial bodies. Why is a mystery, as there's not enough context in the carving.

Looking over the carvings while making a successful [[/skill history 16]] [[/skillCheck society 16]] check leads you to believe that these are not actually the Shent. The depictions of them are wrong in small ways, from poses, to garb, to the general style of the carving. You suspect these may actually be ancestors of the Shent.

Characters proficient with [[/language pathward]] recognize an engraving at the base of the reliefs stating:

The seven sky watchers observe the motions of the cosmos as honored Vanexis stand guard. Blessed are those born beneath the skies of Ember, may they never walk in starless voids again.

Unfamliar Creatures

Depicted alongside the giant figures in the stone are numerous graceful yet lanky cat-like beings with long feathered tails and similarly feathered wings. They do not look up as the humanoid figures do, but instead keep their eyes level, as though watching over the figures.

These creatures are unfamiliar, and don't appear in any lore, history, or religion of the Shent people.

  • Characters proficient with [[/language pathward]] that read the above inscription can infer that the creatures depicted are "Vanexis."

Mythspire Entrance.name: Mythspire Entrance
Mythspire Entrance.text:
Crossing the threshold of the Mythspire Observatory, you are greeted by an almost oppressive silence, punctuated only by the whispering wind sneaking through gaps in the ancient stonework. The air within feels heavy, and colder than outside, as if the timeless stone greedily absorbs all the heat it can.

Rubble lies strewn across the floor, the entire structure continuing its slow spiral toward oblivion. Sunlight pierces through the great shattered dome above, casting stark, uneven beams that illuminate the otherwise dark interior.

Opening the Way

The doors are heavy stone and require a successful [[/check strength 20]] [[/skillCheck athletics 20]]check to open by a single character. However, if two or more characters attempt to push open the door then only a successful [[/check strength 16]] [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] is required.

Automatic Doors

Characters making a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check while examining the doors note that there is a large recessed area in the center of the door, situated about six feet up. It has the shape of a hand.

Pressing one's hand to the recessed area causes the doors to open automatically, sliding open smoothly, moved by an invisible force.

General Ruins Lore

Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] or who make a successful [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] check spot the hallmarks of Shent construction.

Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] or who make a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check notice that the construction appears new in comparison to the even more ancient stonework, indicating this structure has been repaired or rebuilt more than once in its life.

Central Room.name: Central Room
Central Room.text:
This massive space is round, and broken into two levels, with oversized stairs bridging them. Along the curve of the upper level are numerous glowing gems in bronze cages, suspended over the floor by unseen magic, but anchored in place with heavy bronze chains.

The central space of this area is spattered with blood and the shredded remains of multiple humanoids. Each body is rent into pieces, limbs detached from torsos, and heads from necks, yet horribly, these corpses still squirm and move as though not quite dead.

At the center of this space is a large winged being with luminous dust falling from its wings. Its eyes burn with anger, and that ire is directed at you.

Meeting The Guardian

Once the party moves down into the lower area they will be confronted by the guardian. Until then, the Guardian remains out of sight and observes the party, preparing to strike. This guardian is a Vanexis, as depicted in the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.ZjTkzkMwJiKTzbPc]{Tower Descent}

@embed[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC]

The being speaks, its pained voice betraying the agony its wounds inflict.

You corpses should know better than to rise again. How many times must I put you down?

It winces in pain, and shakes its head. For a moment it seems confused, but composes itself, finding its anger anew.

You come bearing false pretense, lying about your motives, I smell the lies, the falsehoods. You are not Shent, or Anachaenum, you are interlopers, enemies! You walk hallowed ground without leave! The passage shall remain closed, and your bodies shall join those of your allies at my feet!

The being crouches down, preparing its assault, but is overtaken by a fit of hacking coughs and shudders of pain no doubt caused by the wounds it bears.

Optional Combat Encounter

This encounter can be avoided by attempting to placate the guardian, and convince them that the party is not their enemy. In its current state it is mistrustful and volatile, readily finding enemies where they may not be any, but it is not beyond reason.

Placating the Guardian

The ancient Mythspire Guardian is clearly unwell. The burns and scars on its face and neck are covered in weeping boils. It seems out of sorts, confused and easily agitated. Parties interacting with it should take care.

The party may attempt to engage the guardian in conversation rather than attacking it outright, doing so is initially simple, but grows harder over time. Placating the guardian may allow them to befriend the creature, but any slip up could prove fatal.

A Dangerous Conversation

It is possible to placate the creature, though it is not easy.

A successful [[/skill persuasion 12]] or [[/skill deception 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] or [[/skillCheck deception 12]]check to either soothe or trick the guardian into believing the party isn't hostile will give it pause. Attempting to use Intimidate will not work, inciting to violence immediately.

This success is brief, allowing the party to ask questions, or examine the creature without risk. The window is brief though, and the guardian quickly becomes suspicious and agitated again.

Each new attempt to placate the guardian suffers a cumulative +2 DC increase whether it succeeds or fails, and after a total of three failures the guardian attacks the party.

Optionally, critical failure while trying to placate the guardian can count as two failures, at your discretion. We only recommend this if your party has especially strong social skill and the risk of failure is inherently lower or you want to make the encounter more tenuous.

With some concerted effort, it is possible to completely mollify the guardian.

Successful Defusal

If the party manages to successfully delay combat by placating the guardian 4 times, then it will calm down enough that it can be convinced the party is not a threat at all, and will begin to fully relax.

Examining the Guardian

The Ancient Guardian

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check reveals that the guardian is deeply unwell, easily agitated, and seems unable to tell friend from foe. It likely views all visitors as possible enemies, perhaps the same as those that attacked it.

Examining the guardian with a successful [[/skill medicine 13]] [[/skillCheck medicine 13]] check reveals that they have suffered wounds from some alchemical attack and are likely poisoned by contact with the toxin. However, given the creature is not a terrestrial beast, it is impossibly to render proper medical aide to the being.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success (or a further[[/skill medicine 16]] or [[/skill insight 17]] [[/skillCheck medicine 16]] check) leads you to believe this creature is dying from whatever the attackers hit it with. It is likely growing weaker by the day, and won't live much longer.

Examining the Guardian is possible, but only while it is placated. See the rules in the following section for how that might be accomplished. If the guardian is examined, the party can learn:

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.2skfDtglk1mGrb3l]{Detect Poison and Disease} also reveals the presence of a powerful lethal toxin in the creature.

  • Spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.F0GsG0SJzsIOacwV]{Lesser Restoration}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.MAxM77CDUu8dgIRQ]{Protection from Poison} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.XZhdgVK3cLoxNCQl]{Remove Curse} and similar healing or curative spells prove ineffective at combating the toxin.

  • However, Protection from Poison does reduce the potency of the poison long enough for the guardian to regain some of its mind. This grants @Advantage[2] on attempts to placate the guardian (see below) as long as the effect lasts.

  • @Spell[life.sense] or @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeLife00000000] reveals the presence of a powerful lethal toxin in the creature, and suggests its progression has advanced beyond the point where intervention will be successful.

  • Curative items like @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.antitoxin0000000] and similar healing or curative spells prove ineffective at combating the toxin.

  • However, use of magics can reduce the potency of the poison long enough for the guardian to regain some of its mind. This grants @Advantage[2] on attempts to placate the guardian (see below) as long as the effect lasts.

The Fate Of The Guardian

If the party doesn't kill the Guardian, and lingers long enough, it will rest somewhat peacefully, and then eventually die. When this occurs, the creature's form crumbles into swirls of light and energy in brilliant reds, pinks, purples, and blues. These ribbons of light fade away to nothing, with only a few guardian feathers remaining.

If the party leaves before this occurs, they will return to an empty Mythspire Observatory, and a few guardian feathers left where they last saw it.

Fighting the Guardian

Guardian Tactics

If the @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC]{Mythspire Guardian} enters combat with the party it immediately casts @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.rL15aLoprdZh7WYp]{Mirror Image} to improve its defense.

The guardian prefers to utilize speed and close-combat ability, using its its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.RxdmByLFjVOk8K06]{Cunning Action} to Dash or Disengage, and @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.LJDe0C4mJNDwV4kR]{Running Leap} allowing it to get space to move, or close on potential enemies, and make use of its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.wQkln56L0P0ahtkt]{Pounce} ability to knock down foes.

Once in melee range it savages enemies with its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.ocnwVK7ckLH0KAgM]{Bite} and @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.nYfPTVPJayLEYdu0]{Claw} via its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.B5yQZrkvCodscc5P]{Multiattack}.

At range, the guardian can resort to its powerful @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.Ks2KKuWvHh4diKVP]{Luminous Sting}, but only does so if it must.

If facing spellcasters it uses its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.Z4G7AYBpuYDUpavy]{Silence}, @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.J86nb6jzjH5jldhu]{Counterspell}, and @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.uVPftgomfuPem9cL]{Dispel Magic} spells to limit the effectiveness of their spells.

Cosmic Gems

The area features seven cosmic gems that represent important bodies in the cosmos of Ember: Lantyr, Akon, Orbis, Ragen, Mayis, Cora, and Aura. The Vanexis can use its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.YJrlVRbsV0T0ofIV]{Cosmic Gems} lair action (on Initiative Count 20) to strike these gems, charging it with light.

Once a gem is charged, place its measured template in the scene (if it has one). The gem's effect will go off as a Lair Action at the end of the round (on Initiative Count 0). When a gem's effect goes off the gem stops being charged.

It is possible to disable a charged gem before its effect is activated by interacting with the stone and pressing the runes on the floor in the correct sequence. This requires an action and a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check to spot and match the sequence that the runes are pulsing in. Failing this check has no repercussions.

Inescapable Fate

The Vanexis has been poisoned fatally and as a result its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.K2YkUlI9E0Qd60mT] feature it takes ongoing damage at the beginning of each of its turns. This effect will eventually kill it if the fight lasts long enough.

If the Mythspire Guardian enters combat with the party it immediately casts @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.protectiveMirage] to improve its defense.

The guardian prefers to utilize speed and its flight to reposition itself and take advantage of its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.ferociousleap000] , @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.swoopingStrike00], and @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.pouncingStrike00] in order to maneuver swiftly between targets.

Once in melee range it savages enemies with its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.BOM6vsI9jOJWlGxi]{Bite} and @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.vvugXHtoDV7KWPCl]{Claw},

At range, the guardian can resort to its powerful @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.7oTO4kdEfLh4AKRh]{Luminous Sting}, but only does so if it must.

If facing spellcasters it relies on counterspell spells to limit the effectiveness of their spells.

Cosmic Gems

The area features seven cosmic gems that represent important bodies in the cosmos of Ember: Lantyr, Akon, Orbis, Ragen, Mayis, Cora, and Aura. The Vanexis can use its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.YJrlVRbsV0T0ofIV]{Charge Gem} action to direct a beam of light into one of these gems, charging it with light.

Once a gem is charged, place its measured template in the scene (if it has one). The gem's effect will activate at the end of the round. When a gem's effect activates, the gem stops being charged.

It is possible to disable a charged gem before its effect is activated by interacting with the stone and pressing the runes on the floor in the correct sequence. This requires an action and a successful [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check to spot and match the sequence that the runes are pulsing in. Failing this check has no repercussions.

Inescapable Fate

The Vanexis has been poisoned fatally and as a result its @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC.Item.K2YkUlI9E0Qd60mT] talent, it takes ongoing damage at the beginning of each of its turns. This effect will eventually kill it if the fight lasts long enough.

Speaking with the Guardian

About the Dead Adventurers

The Vanexis views the dead adventurers as fallen foes, enemies, and has this to say about them if asked:

The corpses scattered at my feet were interlopers attempting to open the sacred passage to the Pathways. Only visitors seeking to know the history of the Giants and their path are allowed. Liars, invaders, and killers are not!

They said they were of the "Anachraenum" but they were unlike others of that order I have met. They threatened to use acids and tools to carve open the way below if I would not give them access. When I acted to remove them, they turned those implements on me.

The Vanexis can also explain why their remains are mutilated so badly, and why they are wriggling and moving stills: The adventurers kept rising from the dead.

Bidden to wake again and again by the Sleeper, I put them down countless times. Eventually their remains were savaged so thoroughly so that they could not rise again… but you can see their rotting forms still writhe and wriggle, trying.

If asked about the Sleeper:

The sleeper wakes. It slumbers in Ember now, but not for much longer. Its voice has been growing louder and louder in my ears. It promises me life after my death, but it does not know that I am beyond its reach. Still… the light of this place has grown more dim.

About The Mythspire and Guardian

The Guardian has quite a bit to say about itself and its purpose if asked.

Primordial Giants built this place when they emerged from the pathways so long ago. They built this place to study the skies which they had never seen before. I was sent here to serve as their guide, to teach them many things about magic and the cosmos, and welcome them to the surface.

The Guardian believes it was forgotten, but it is content with its place in the world.

The Casia of Primordis put me here, to protect the knowledge of this place, to preserve the memory of its builders and to keep this observatory safe. However, it seems the Casia have forgotten about me, and all who had connection to this place passed into history, I have watched over this crumbling space. One day it will turn to dust, and there will be nothing to protect, and I will return home.

If asked about the builders, the Guardian saw much of it, and can share what it knows:

I witness the growth of the Shent. Though, they didn't really grow, more they changed, become different as they reached the surface. I watched this place turn from observatory to a place of reverence and history, where Shent came to connect with their cultural heritage. I witnessed them come here in dark times, when the Abyss was destroying them, to gaze at the old mosaics and try to find purpose or solace. I remember when I last saw the Shent, and they told me they would soon be no more. I miss them.

About The Pathways Passage

The Vanexis can talk at length about the passage, and is even willing to explain about how to open it, if asked!

The passage is a great lift that descends to the base of this great tower. Opening it begins with Lantyr, but requires a traveler to reach all the other moons before they can set themselves onto the Pathways proper.

The passage has been opened a few times by visitors over the last few thousand years, but not often. It leads down into the ancient pathways beneath the surface. I have only seen what lies below a time or two, and it seems a wild place.

If asked to clarify on the solution to open the passage, the Vanexis is somewhat cryptic.

The ancient mosaics here on the walls hold the secrets you need. You can find the path through the cosmos there. Follow the ancients, they will guide you.

Examining the Walls

Ancient Carvings

Examining the ancient carvings of this lower area you can easily make out the progression, even through the damage: Long ago a people burrowed out of the body of Ember and through the mountains. They peered at the sky overhead, and were awed.

They built a great structure at their emergence point, likely this very building, and in it sat another feline guardian. From this structure many more of their kind ascended to the surface of Ember, each awed by the stars and moons overhead.

The mural further depicts the spread of these people across the mountains, and the construction of many homes high and low.

Interpreting the Stone

A successful[[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck history 14]] check connects some dots: The lack of heavy Shent construction markers means that this structure likely predates the Shent, and as a result this is possibly the emergence point of their precursors. The ancient guardian is possible tens of thousands of years old! Also the presence of the cat-like beings might be reference to the magical Casia, who could have provided them the basis of their magical knowledge.

A successful [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck religion 14]] check connects some dots: The reverence of the sky and moons feels like a classical marker of the Shent. This was likely an ancient and important sight (for the Shent) and served as the starting point of their worship of the heavens. The cat-like beings are possibly Casia, which are known to stem from Primordis. They might have served as guardians and guides to the early Shent.

Examining the Undead

The party may way to examine the remains of the adventuring party. While they are in a horrible state, a little bit can still be gleaned from them.

Undead Remnants

The scattered remnants of the dead here are in rough shape. Limbs have been carved from rotting torso, and heads split open and scattered on stone. Still there is an unseemly life in them as digits twitch and arms curl, trying to grab for anything nearby.

The dead here do not rest, and examining them is made all the more unpleasant for it.

Examining the remains with a successful [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check allows characters to find interesting details.

  • Result 13+ Success The corpses all had legitimate looking Anachraenum badges, pins, or crests, making them recognized members of the guild. This is almost certainly the group that Liestra helped in Skybrush.

  • Result 15+ Critical Success There are several shattered canisters in the possessions of the deceased, each previously holding noxious alchemical compounds. Though it's impossible to know what the compound was, it is green, and corrosive based on the remnants.

A successful [[/skill medicine 12]] [[/skillCheck medicine 12]] while examining the bodies yields insights into their deaths and current states.

  • Result of 12+ The bodies are still relatively fresh, preserved by the cold, dry air of this place. You would estimate they are only about two or three weeks old. However, there is a strange, discolored cast to the skin and muscle, as though something more is tainting it.

  • Result of 14+ The wounds are not all the same age, it appears that these bodies were savaged multiple times to get them into the state they presently hold. If you had to guess, the corpses kept getting up, and the guardian kept cutting them down until they were in a state they could not rise any longer.

  • Result of 16+ Several of the dead have old wounds akin to burns, and by the look of them you would guess from contact with corrosive chemicals. While none of them were fatal, all of them seem to have regularly handled dangerous alchemical substances while they lived.

  • Success The bodies are still relatively fresh, preserved by the cold, dry air of this place. You would estimate they are only about two or three weeks old. However, there is a strange, discolored cast to the skin and muscle, as though something more is tainting it.

  • Critical Success The wounds are not all the same age, it appears that these bodies were savaged multiple times to get them into the state they presently hold. If you had to guess, the corpses kept getting up, and the guardian kept cutting them down until they were in a state they could not rise any longer. Several of the dead have old wounds akin to burns, and by the look of them you would guess from contact with corrosive chemicals. While none of them were fatal, all of them seem to have regularly handled dangerous alchemical substances while they lived.

A successful [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check in regards to the undead yield the following: Undeath is uncommon, and there are no obvious sources or signs of such magic being worked in the area, so whatever is causing the dead to rise is coming from somewhere else. What is concerning about that though, is you're not sure how powerful a being or magical source you're dealing with. It could be nearby but weak, or worst case, miles away and powerful.

Balcony Perimeter.name: Balcony Perimeter
Balcony Perimeter.text:
A wide balcony extends around the open space here, and along this curve of the upper level are numerous glowing gems suspended over the floor by unseen magic, each anchored in place with heavy bronze chains.

Universal Fittings

The gems are are set in bronze fitting, and held above the ground by unseen forces, likely magic, with heavy chains keeping them in place. The chains themselves are anchored to cog-like tiles set into the stone which are carved with numerous runs of a peculiar make.

A successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check leaves you believing they are Shent in origin.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success At first glance they appear Shent, but the designs are strange and deviate in places. You suspect these are the runes of a different people, yielding different magic, but related to the Shent magic you're aware of.

Cosmic Gems

A successful [[/skill history 14]] or [[/skill religion 15]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] recognizes that each of the gems in this upper area coincide with the moons of Ember, and the sun Lantyr. Their specific order along the balcony doesn't seem to be important, but their presence here does.

  • The Gem of Lantyr is as golden and warm as the sun itself.

  • The Gem of Akon gem is nearly black, and featureless with a faint hint of green.

  • The Gem of Orbis is a chaotic shifting mess of pinks, blues, and purples.
