  • The Gem of Ragen is a deep red and radiates warmth even when dim.

  • The Gem of Mayis is deep blue, and beneath its facets are dim currents of light.

  • The Gem of Cora is a rich green and it exudes a palpable sensation of heaviness.

  • The Gem of Aura is an ethereal pink gem with facets that swirl with clouds.

Theft Averse

The gems are all magically fixed in their fittings and the chains are reinforced many times over with magic. It should be functionally impossible for the fittings or their chains to be damaged or broken, making theft of these ancient gems beyond the party.

All attempts to do so automatically fail.

Interactable Gems

Each of the gems have an interactable element that when clicked will turn the gem's lighting effect on or off. This is used both for the combat in the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.uQdyUS2DDyiaeu62] and the puzzle detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.G7YQat34HVQ6tspr].

Ancient Lift.name: Ancient Lift
Ancient Lift.text:
You step into a spacious, square chamber dominated by a broad stone platform at its very center. Measuring twenty feet to each side, the platform is slightly raised from the floor, and its edges are smoothed, as though well traveled.

A raised pedestal stands just next to it and is set with a large crystal plate bearing the shallow imprint of a humanoid hand.

Mounted on opposite walls, large crystals of pale white stone rest within rune-etched metal fixtures. A few of these crystals are cracked straight through, and a few slots in the wall are outright empty.

At the center of the room is the lift, the shape and pattern of the stone clear different from the rest of the floor.

A Way Down

The crystals set into the wall appear to powered the lift.

  • Characters that did [[/eventState overMoonTemple]] recognize these as carved crystals utilized by the Shent to power magical devices.

The party can descend to the lower level by pressing their hand to the pedestal.

Activating the Lift

Once the elevator has been reactivated, it can be used to descend to the lower area.

The stone platform shudders as magical energy rushes through it. A moment later the lift begins to descend, smoothly sliding down into the darkness. Though the shaft is enclosed, gaps in the crumbling stone give you fleeting glimpses of the numerous levels in between the upper level and your destination.

The lift slides past each one, as though it is aware the entrances are blocked by piles of rubble, collapsed walkways, and rusting iron. Instead you descend further into the darkness, toward the lowest levels of the Mythspire.

At this point the party will be transported to the Mythspire Observatory's lower area.

Manual Scene Transition

For the time being, you will need to manually load the @UUID[Scene.emberMythSpLower] scene and move the party characters to it.

Orb Room.name: Orb Room
Orb Room.text:
At the center of this space you see a large, circular frame. Though not too badly damaged itself, the room around it is littered with further pieces of metal, gears, oversized tools, lengths of braided steel cable, and more that seem to have come from some machinery and racks overhead.

Above the large steel cradle, metal rails run into the ceiling. Some stretch northward over a now-collapsed bridge, while the rest continue up into the gloom overhead, supported by cables anchored to high points on the walls.

This chamber holds the mechanisms needed to move large glass orbs in the observatory, however, time and the elements have caused it all to collapse to the point of being useless.

Orb Apparatus

Characters that noticed the suspended orb in the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.PWM9H3I4Hk79Rxll]{Chamber Overlook} would recognize this apparatus was meant to deal with those orbs specifically.

Otherwise, [[/knowledge machines]] or a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check while studying the machinery surmises that the central cradle was used to hold large circular orbs, possibly to work on them, affix mounting hardware, or similar.

Off the Rails

The rails overhead would have allowed the Shent here to move orbs back up into the ceiling area, or run them north to another space nearby. However, the rails have become partially detached from the ceiling in places, or are simply missing in others.

Beyond Repair

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] recognize that the damage is far too extensive to repair without considerable resources and support.

Characters looking around the room would also note that there are various carved stone plaques fixed to the wall featuring some sort of language. Additionally, among the rubble and wreckage are old tools.

Writing On the Wall

Characters that understand [[/language pathward]] can parse instructions cut into stone plates on the walls stating the followings things:

  • Warning: Improper suspension may result in the loss of projection orbs, injury or death.

  • Ensure that all projection orbs are secured in cradle before undergoing movement or etching work. Orbs may become dislodged and could break or fall on you.

  • Please return all etching and cutting tools to their associated racks.

Old Equipment

What at first appeared to be pieces of old machinery or rusting debris turns out to be ancient tools. Though rusted and pitted beyond use, they might lend some insight into the purpose of the room.

Characters with [[/knowledge Shent]] or making a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check recognize that the oversized tools feature ancient runs for transmutation and evocation that would have been used to cut and carve materials.

  • Characters gaining this insight via their knowledge of the Shent also know that similar tools like this existed for cutting and shaping stone, but were not quite as delicate as these appear to be.

Collapsed Archives.name: Collapsed Archives
Collapsed Archives.text:
You find yourself in a chamber shrouded in gloom. The air is heavy with the scent of stone dust and rotten paper. The only light is thin and uncertain, slipping in through the gaps in the broken stone overhead. Everywhere, piles of rubble and fallen masonry fill the space, choking most of the floor and leaving only narrow paths to pick through the ruin.

Along the battered walls you can see the shattered remnants of massive shelving, the stone broken and buried beneath debris that has fallen from the ceiling and upper levels. In the rubble, you spot the remains of scrolls and tablets, all long since pulverized into ruin.

Records of the Past

A successful [[/skill investigation 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check will find one ancient scroll that is still somewhat legible; it is covered in constellations and notations in Pathward. It appears to track celestial movements over a set time period.

Sadly, no other documents or records survived the collapse of this space.

A Lone Record

Characters that understand [[/language pathward]] can read the discovered scroll, determining that it was a printed record of a season's worth of celestial tracking. The subject is Akon, and no notable events or deviations are recorded in this period.

The dating schema on the scroll is indecipherable, but it likely dates back several thousand years. Further notations mark it as one of a series of such records.

Mystic Preservation

Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or making a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check recognize the hallmarks of magical protection runes on the scroll. While badly damaged and nearly burned out, they've still done the job of preserving the scroll over the centuries.

Crumbling Walkway.name: Crumbling Walkway
Crumbling Walkway.text:
You find yourself on a broad, curved walkway, partially buried beneath piles of broken stone and ancient debris. The outer edge is protected by a chest-high stone barrier, cracked in several places, which keeps you from a long, fatal fall to the lower levels.

The balcony leads only in one direction; the rest is blocked by collapsed sections. At the far end, a set of broad and unusually tall steps rises up to the level above.

Short Hop

This walkway is 30 feet below the upper, broken walkway that exits the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.H1FUd4Nd5MW7Z3Jh]{Orb Room}. Characters can jump down to this area without a roll, but it is a one-way trip.

Projection Room.name: Projection Room
Projection Room.text:
You enter a broad chamber where the floor is dominated by a pair of long metal rails, fixed firmly into the ancient stone and stretching in parallel from the room’s center to a nearby balcony. At either end of the rails is a circular recess etched with runes.

Set into the walls are two crystalline fixtures with large chest-high surfaces: one holds an array of blue and red gems set into the walls. Both clusters are fixed over extensively rune-covered structures of stone. One of them appears to have been badly burned.

Opposite these fixtures, the room curves into a long, smooth wall, utterly unbroken save for a border of runes at its outermost edges.

Ancient Projectors

A successful [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check while examining the runes around the crystal machines, the recess at the end of the rails, and the curved wall determines that they all worked in concert.

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] suspect that this may have been used for a variety of tasks — testing orbs, charging them, or extracting precise information from them.

The gems would project magical light, which was meant to hit something sitting in the cradle, and project light onto the wall beyond.

The presence of illusion and divination runes present on the crystal likely provided some predictive and visual elements to the projection.

  • Characters with [[/language pathward]] can read the controls and determine that this was once used to project light through crystal orbs onto the large, curved wall and had several modes including knowledge retrieval, surface inspection, and attunement. The instructions do not elaborate on how these states worked, or what they did.

Powerless Ruins

A successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check while examining the rune-covered machines here determines information based on the result.

  • Result of 14+ Success Though you're not sure what caused it, at some point a portion of the machinery on this wall suffered a catastrophic failure that left the stone badly burned, destroying several of the runes carved into it. The gems as well have suffered cracks, rendering them inert.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success Attempting to fill in the gaps left by the destruction, you believe this machine was meant to control the flow of magical energy through the room. Extensive evocation and abjuration runes were used to dampen and control the energy; if they failed, it could have resulted in the damage you see here.

  • Characters with [[/language pathward]] can read around the scarring and damage and surmise that this controlled all of the power for the central dome's projection system.

Chamber Overlook.name: Chamber Overlook
Chamber Overlook.text:
You step onto a broad, open platform bounded by a chest-high railing of shaped stone. Beyond the railing, the view plunges down into the vast, central void of the Mythspire — a breathtaking drop of hundreds of feet that reveals level upon level of ruined walkways, shattered stairwells, and inaccessible spaces in between.

Overhead, the remnants of a massive dome arch high above, with large gaps in its structure letting the brutal mountain winds in unabated. The constant sigh and howl of the mountain winds threading through ancient gaps can be heard here, echoing off the old stone like a ghostly chorus.

Ruins Overhead

A [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check reveals that the remains of the massive central dome were once etched with constellations, though much of this has been worn away by wind or crumbled with age.

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or [[/knowledge shent]] note there is an immense amount of bent metal and precariously hanging structures overhead that looks like it was once host to a massive orrery or telescope of some sort.

  • A successful [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] while peering up at the remains above leads one to suspect that something grabbed and wrenched a large portion of the building off the top. Not many things could do that on Ember.

Familiar Shapes

Characters that completed [[/eventState overMoonTemple]] or have [[/knowledge shent]] recognize the remains of a planetarium projector similar to the one hanging in the Mayis temple, though this one is heavily damaged and many parts are missing.

Otherwise a successful [[/skill arcana 16]] check reveals the magical runes in the walls and the machinery in the center of the space would have been used to magically project a vision of the cosmos.

Loose Change

Characters with [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check notice an old silver coin on the ground.

Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] or making a successful [[/skill history 16]] [[/skillCheck society 16]] check recognize it is an @UUID[Item.xn7QNEGmQG0ti8RZ]{Ancient Aediri Coin} that might be worth something to a collector or historian.

Character that spend some time looking up at the dome may also notice a solitary glass orb in the ruins.

Lost amongst the wreckage of the ruins at first, your eyes catch a flash of light and are drawn to a large glass orb swaying with the winds.

One Lonely Sphere

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] note where the orb once connected to the observatory's upper rails. Unfortunately, the damage to the structure as a whole has left the sphere isolated, and impossible to reach.

Characters looking down can also attempt to glimpse insight from the ruins below, though the distance and darkness does limit what they can see.

Ruins Below

A successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check notes that the lower levels are badly damaged, with the various walkways and balconies having collapsed on themselves, or fallen away entirely.

There might be half a dozen other levels to explore in this tower, but there is no clear or remotely safe way to reach them. Even if one could levitate or fly it looks like the entrances are choked with rubble.

Maintenance Balcony.name: Maintenance Balcony
Maintenance Balcony.text:
From where you stand on this square balcony you can see the skeletal remains of ancient machinery and rails looming overhead. Once used to guide enormous orbs down onto the rails fixed to the floor nearby, now they hang from their fixtures in ancient stone, twisted from their own weight, and filled with irreparable gaps.

Against the wall is a cracked stone diagram of a humanoid figure utilizing pulleys and handles to draw an orb down and set it on the floor rails.

Orb Access

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or who make a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck science 15]] check recognize that this balcony was used to pull orbs down from above and roll them into the nearby space, possibly to be worked on or used. However, none of this machinery would function at this point in its existence.

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] notices that going by the diagram of how to work the old machine here, none of the controls are reachable, and were clearly meant for people substantially taller — like everything else in this ruin.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] would know that this makes sense given who made the locations. The Shent were substantially taller than most ancestries on Ember.

Characters with [[/language pathward]] recognize the instructions on the diagram as those used to bring down a celestial orb from the racks overhead for examination in the nearby work room.

Characters might want to try to repair the railing and movement systems overhead to access the orb. While this isn't intended gameplay, or advised, it is certainly something possible for a sufficiently resourceful party.

There are two things to consider about the orb, and any possible solutions the party comes up with:

  • The orb is solid crystal-glass and immensely heavy. It weighs several thousand pounds, and is beyond the lifting capacity of most spells. It is also especially delicate, and would shatter if not carefully handled.

  • The railing and recall systems of Mythspire are so damaged that even if they were utilized, the weight of the orb would cause the rails to break away, and fall into the abyss below it, where it would be destroyed.

Etched Glass

Bringing the glass orb into the Projection Room, or examining the orb up close (via flight, levitation, or similar) allows the party to examine the magical inscriptions in the glass.

Characters with [[/knowledge cosmology]] know that this orb was meant to track the movement of Orbis across the sky, and has been etched with the figures necessary to plot its movements for near eternity, barring some celestial event changing its movement through the sky.

A successful [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] recognizes that extensive divination, illusion, and evocation magic was etched into the glass of this orb. It is all in the form of ancient runes that characters with [[/knowledge shent]] recognize as belonging to their library of symbols.

  • A result of 20+ Critical Success knows that the magic would have stored the knowledge of the moon's movements, major celestial events, deviations from its normal cycles, and even its inherent energy levels. However, there is no clear way to access this information, or any indication where it would be stored.

Mythspire Approach.name: Mythspire Approach
Mythspire Approach.text:
The ruins of Mythspire rise up out of the mountains, in some places looking as though they were carved from the ancient stone directly.

Layers of massive bricks form outer walls that curve around ridges of stone, and meet immense, rune-covered pillars. Everything is oversized here, even the great stone doors which provide entrance to the place.

The ruins reach upward for a hundred feet or more, presenting the shape of a jagged, half-collapsed dome which the mountain winds play with to create a mournful howl that cuts through the silence here.

Crumbling Ruins

Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] or making a successful a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check suspect this place is a Shent ruin, given the size and style, though it does break from some of the establish elements one would expect to see.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success you suspect that these ruins might be early Shent, given the prevalence of large stone bricks versus mostly contiguous stonework found in newer ruins.

Rallyhome.name: Rallyhome
Rallyhome.text:
This structure is made of sturdy blocks of golden stone that match the color and cut of the rest of the plaza. The façade is simple — a series of wide stone pieces forming an arch over modest wooden doors. The location's name is carved into that arch:

Rallyhome

Operating Hours

Rallyhome opens around midday and operates until well into late hours. It serves food until the evening, after that it's only whatever the bartender is willing to scrounge up.

Through the doors is the upper balcony area which provides a view of the lower bar, and a place to sit and enjoy the music below without being caught in the crowds.

Through the double doors you are met with the raucous din of Rallyhome filtering up through the open space just beyond the entryway's wide balcony.

Several smaller tables and well-cushioned chairs are set about the perimeter of this balcony, providing a commanding view of the stage and tables below.

A narrow stairwell in the far corner descends to the lower area. By the sound of things, all of the bar's life is contained down there.

Party Down Under

The stairs lead down to the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.ldg0L6T01PNsue0R]{Lower Bar} where drinks and food are sold.

Arcturian Automatons.name: Arcturian Automatons
Arcturian Automatons.text:
Arcturian Automatons presents itself as a boxy, striking building made entirely of weathered bronze. Its surface is burnished to a muted sheen, panels joined with visible rivets and seams. A weathered sign beside the door bears the painting of a humanoid construct and the words:

The Chessman: Tackles any task. Works any post.

Each one made to order.

Inquire within!

Operating Hours

Arcturian Automatons is open until sundown, afterward the doors are locked and the Chessmen inside will act as security.

It is possible the the proprieter, Vortholomew Chess is present after work hours, tinkering with designs or working to fulfill an order, but he doesn't let anyone in without a prior appointment.

Inside the building, one finds a collection of constructs for sale.

Set throughout the shop floor, tall and slender automatons, each a wonder of precise craftsmanship, their limbs and torsos sheathed in overlapping metallic shells. Some of them are wrapped in warm, rosy copper, others the rich gleam brass, while others bear the gray shadow of hammered iron.

A long wooden table and shelves of scrolls sit toward the back of this shop where the shop's owner conducts business.

Acquiring Automatons

Each Chessman automaton costs 15,000 gold pieces 1500 gold pieces and takes 30 days to be built to the buyer's specifications, and all new orders are put on a waitlist. The current waiting time for a new construct is half a year.

There is no means to expedite this. The floor models are for display and demonstration only.

Examining Automatons

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] recognize that these constructs are incredibly well made, with precise construction tolerances and a keen eye for detail. They are masterwork automatons.

Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] recognize the style of the machines is more akin to that of Aedir constructs and automatons than classical Arcturian designs which tend to feature more natural materials like wood and cloth.

If the party enters the back area, which is generally off-limits to customers, they will find Chess' workspace.

A long wooden bench stretches along one wall, its scarred surface crowded with gears, rods, and curious lengths of interlocking metal. Partially assembled components, fine tools, and discarded sketches are scattered across the workspace here.
At the back of this room is a door leading to crowded storage area where every available space is filled with something: boxes of bolts and springs, trays of washers and pins, battered tins of grease and oilcloth, spare tools slipped into a rack wedged against a wall and forgotten behind unmarked crated.

Lots to See, Nothing to Find

These back room areas are packed with items and pieces of machinery to examine, but there is nothing of particular note in this space. These parts and materials are all meant to create or maintain constructs, and are utterly mundane, even if the machines they go into are anything but.

Silver Beam Foyer.name: Silver Beam Foyer
Silver Beam Foyer.text:
Built directly into the rich brown stone, this dark structure reaches out across the gap to contact the plaza. There, the dark stone and curved walls are a sharp contrast to the warm, golden angles of the tradeway.

The steps up to the structure bear a sign that declares:

The Silver Beam Consortium

Arcturel Branch

Not From Round These Parts

Chracters with the [[/culture emberArcturian]] or [[/culture emberOrdani]] recognize that this structure reads is unmistakably foreign, not bearing any local sensibilities of design or aesthetic.

Characters making a successful [[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check recognize the building as having Railen sensibilities in places.

Operating Hours

The Silver Beam offices are open until sundown, then the front doors are closed and locked.

Inside the double doors is reception, though access to the building beyond this point is limited.

You find yourself in a grand, circular lobby dedicated to the Silver Beam Consortium's offices here in Arcturel. Tall windows allow light to pour in through the glass. This, paired with the gleaming white marble that's been polished to a fine sheen makes the space feel impossibly clean and bright.

At the very center stands a broad desk of ornately worked grey metal, its filigreed surface catching the light with each subtle movement. Here, the receptionist sits, their posture formal and welcoming at once.

On either side of this desk, two slender constructs fashioned of shining silver and painted with blue livery stand perfectly still upon raised stone daises.

The Silver Beam Consortium offices in Arcturel are accessed by appointment only. The Receptionist (an @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturian}) will not allow anyone inside that isn't an employee or arriving with authorization of someone inside.

Do You Know Who I Am?

Attempting to persuade or deceive the receptionist fails as they are infinitely more afraid of upsetting their boss (@UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth}) then letting someone in who isn't on their appointment list.

Attempting to gain access to the offices is intentionally difficult, and not something characters will be able to do outside of certain events. Attempting to intimidate the receptionist will result in her calling security via the security button on her desk.

Dress For The Job You Want

If the party manages to @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.Xi8DSOxh18XVrkep#consortium-disguises]{disguise} themselves as Silver Beam employees, they can walk right through the front doors and the receptionist won't spare them a second thought.

What's That Do?

Characters with a [[/skill perception 10 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 10 passive]] note there is a moderately sized red button on the desk. It's easily in reach of the receptionist, and is probably a button meant to summon security.

Display Only?

A pair of @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU]{Silver Beam Servitors} stand on the daises on either side of the desk. While they aren't armed, and don't seem to be active, they don't feel like they are just for display purposes.

Pushing Buttons

If the party acts in a hostile, disruptive, or criminal way, the receptionist will ask the party to leave. If it's clear they won't, or the danger they present is too great, the receptionist will hit the red button to alert security.

See: @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.Xi8DSOxh18XVrkep#activating-alerts]{Activating Alerts} in @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.Xi8DSOxh18XVrkep]{Gameplay Details} for how this works.

Glimmer.name: Glimmer
Glimmer.text:
Built from broad slabs of golden stone, matching the refined paving of the plaza itself, this squat and unassuming building is accented with wide, clear windows set evenly along the walls. The entrance is a sturdy stone door, faced with the same golden stone as the rest.

Above that door, a sign:

Glimmer

Operating Hours

Glimmer is open until sundown, afterward the doors are locked. The doors appear to be made of stone, but they have steel cores and advanced locks. A successful [[/skill sleightofhand 20 t00l=thief]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 20]] check requiring @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000]{Lockpicks} is required to open them.

The door, walls and windows are all magically reinforced.They have have an AC of 18 and a damage threshold of 10 when attempting to damage them.

Inside the shop, one finds a mixture of art gallery and gem shop.

Inside, Glimmer opens into a single, spacious chamber paved with fine stone tiles. The light within dances off countless displays lining the walls, where both raw crystals and brilliantly cut gems are set on shelves and nestled in cases for easy browsing.

Statues and busts of polished stone occupy the corners, and are joined by large, richly framed paintings. The busts and art combined with the constant glimmer of precious stones ensures that there’s always something to catch the eye.

Along the wall a stairwell of plain wood descends quietly out of sight, leading to some deeper and unmarked room below.

All That Glimmers

Glimmer is owned and operated by the flamboyant and gregarious Nodrick Stolas (CG, Arcturian Human, he/him). He operates Glimmer as a mixture of gem store, art gallery, and night club. He is happy to identify and appraise gems on request.

Characters can acquire nearly any kind of gem they might want here at typical market prices, and can even sell any gems or crystals they've acquired for a modest profit.

Nodrick's prices are fair, and fixed, he doesn't haggle.

Nightlife

In the evenings Glimmer serves as a club, the lower area serving as a lounge for clients, friends, and other esteemed associates. As Glimmer closes after sundown, the only way into the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.hPNx5zJWyySGYFjE]{Glimmer lounge} after closing time is from under the Tradeway.

Precipice.name: Precipice
Precipice.text:
An unassuming wooden structure stands here, set just at the outer edge of the plaza and bearing a sign declaring this location to be:

Precipice

A blackboard sign out front displaying the day's offerings and specials. The tantalizing scent of freshly cooked food hangs in the air here.

Operating Hours

Precipice opens around midday and operates until well into the evening. It closes late at night after the dinner rush has ended.

Inside the eatery, a warm, intimate atmosphere awaits.

You are greeted by the quiet elegance of what may be Arcturel's nicest restaurant. Fine art hangs from the wall, as polished wood parquet flooring set against a border of gleaming brass grating spreads out underfoot. The intimate dining room features numerous small, linen-draped tables, each set for two and softly lit by a single burning candle.

Through a broad archway beyond the dining area is a a long communal table set against a wall of tall windows that stretch from floor to ceiling and offering a breathtaking view out over the tradeway’s edge. This is the very view that gives Precipice its name.

Fine Dining

Given the small size, individual tables only seat two guests, but the larger communal table can take larger groups, and for 8 GP 8 SPcan be reserved for a larger group.

Precipice's meals cost about 2 GP 2 SP, and are served hot. Appetizes, Sides and Dessert all cost 1 GP 1 SP. The menu is small, with only a handful of options, but they are varied enough to fit all diets. It takes about twenty minutes to be served, but the wait is always worth it as the quality of the food is always excellent.

Characters that get into the kitchen are greeted by a cramped, hectic space.

Precipice’s kitchen is cramped and busy, lacking all the elegance of the dining area. A messy prep area sits beside a cramped stove, and both are overseen by racks and shelves packed with ingredients destined for a plate.

Suspended Paths.name: Suspended Paths
Suspended Paths.text:
Avenues lined with brass railings, diamond-pattered plates, and warm golden stone stretch out before you. Massive metal cables attach at regular intervals along each of them, and extend upward to anchor points all along the mouth of the great sinkhole cliffs.

Ample stairwells and ramps allow for traversal up and down between levels, leading to Brimtown above, or depths below.

Beyond the tradeway you can see numerous homes and other businesses sitting on suspended platforms just like this one, though none of them are especially remarkable from here.

Abstract Avenues

This area has no specific gameplay purpose but can be used as a transition point to other parts of the Arcturel location, such as heading to the @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelUnd] or down to @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelLow].

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text: @Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Arcturel Verticality

The distance between the Tradeway and Underbelly levels of upper Arcturel is 20 feet in most places, with some rooftops providing shorter 10 foot drops.

A Long Way Down

Characters that jump or fall off of upper Arcturel and don't land on a lower level will find themselves falling hundreds upon hundreds of feet to the Sinkhole Depths below.

Without a spell like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.pub0OWVEB71XQx1n]{Feather Fall}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.MRxldJd6C4bsBo3O]{Levitate}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.yfbK8gZqESlaoY5t]{Fly} or similar to save them, most characters will not survive this fall.

Without some magical means to float or fly, most characters will not survive this fall.

We recommend giving characters one or more [[/save dexterity 14]] or [[/save strength 14]] saving throws [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] checks to catch ledges, suspension cables, walkways, outstretched hands, or hastily thrown ropes to potentially save themselves from an early demise.

Silver Beam Consortium Offices

Activating Alerts

There are a few places in the offices where security buttons exist, some are obvious, others a hidden. They all have the same general functionality based on the number of times they are pressed:

  • First Press: Alert. The @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7] in the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.VCLZw6TSFNglHRMW] are alerted, drawing one or two of them to the area to investigate.

  • Second Press: Alarm. An alarm bell sounds, bringing all members of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.VCLZw6TSFNglHRMW] to that area. If there are any nearby dormant Servitor constructs, they activate and assist Security in subduing intruders.

  • Third Press: Lockdown. Metal security doors seal the offices, and more security are summoned to the level, arriving via any available elevators. It usually takes about 3 minutes for security to arrive once a Lockdown occurs.

Disabling Alerts

Holding the button for 10 seconds cancels the alert and unseals the doors, though security will still come to investigate and the constructs will remain active until ordered to stand down by a Silver Beam employee.

Idle Servitors

Located all over the Silver Beam offices there are @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU] that appear to be dormant and meant for display. These servitors are waiting for instructions, or an alert at which point they become active. They only follow orders from Silver Beam personnel, and always listen to the highest-ranking person they are aware of.

The ranking order is: Larissa Toth > Engineers > Guards > Receptionist > All Other Employees

Consortium Disguises

While interacting with Silver Beam personnel, visiting their operations, and getting involved in quests that feature them there is a chance for the players to acquire one or more @UUID[Item.LZAFIWKck47hrjRt].

While wearing these uniforms they are able to move through Silver Beam controlled areas with relative ease as long as they aren't caught doing anything suspicious or hostile.

Use of magic, such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.A3q2gTNqG6fvNGrv] Use of a magical disguise would also suffice.

Dubious Hiring Practices

Silver Beam only hires @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.tkGzfnJkkLZ3cgpG] and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.p7n66fVhfJCkGd4z] employees, and many of them are imported from other Silver Beam operations from abroad. This means that any other ancestries trying to pass themselves off as employees will stand out sharply and draw attention.

Bypassing Doors

All doors in the Silver Beam offices are of a higher quality and require a [[/tool thief 15]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] with lockpicks to successfully open.

Forcing doors open with tools (such as a prybar) requires a successful [[/check strength 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]]check and makes enough noise to alert any Silver Beam personnel within 60 feet.

The doors are not specially reinforced or armored, and can be destroyed with sufficient damage.

Heavy Doors

There are heavy metal and glass doors that limit access to the offices via the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.5IHmzA71p0Fd8F4l]{Silver Beam Foyer} and also can close off the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.r3qQuNmGgOfkPzpo]{Director's Office}.

These doors have no obvious locks, and the recessed mechanisms require a [[/tool thief 20]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 20]] with lockpicks to successfully open by bypassing. However, characters making a successful [[/tool tinker 15]] check can bypass the door mechanisms. Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

Prying them open requires a successful [[/check str 21]] check [[/skillCheck athletics 21]] check while using a crow bar. The doors are otherwise magically protected from harm, and have a natural damage threshold of 10 \highly resistant to physical damage.

Alarmed Doors

Attempting to force open or break down a door, or failing a tool check by 5 or more triggers a security alert. This causes the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.VCLZw6TSFNglHRMW]{Security Room} guards to become aware of an intrusion attempt, drawing one or two of them to the area to investigate.

Reinforced Walls

The walls of the Silver Beam offices are reinforced stone and steal and have a natural damage threshold of 10 are highly resistant to physical damage. They are designed to resist being breached. Even internal walls are much more resilient than most.

Assembly Area.name: Assembly Area
Assembly Area.text:
You see a long conveyor belt running the length of the marble wall, its surface crowded with a neat procession of mechanical parts — gears, rods, construct arms and heads, and curved metal plates — each piece moving along with the hum of the belt, and meant for some part of this company's new servitor line.

Employees carefully sort the shift parts, fitting smaller pieces together and setting aside incomplete assemblies. Each finished component is placed into a wire basket set beside them.

The workers here are all @UUID[Actor.vyN7FNbPEw6KsuGw]{Silver Beam Engineers}.

Watchful Guards

There is a lone member of the Silver Beam Security team posted up against the wall at all hours, watching over the workers. Any attempts to steal or tamper with the assembly line will get characters thrown out and barred reentry.

If a fight breaks out, the Engineers will join the Security in the fight.

Side Offices.name: Side Offices
Side Offices.text:
Here a slender desk of brushed metal sits to one side of the office, opposite a pale, gray wooden bookstand against the wall. A sliding door exits this office, leading out to a private balcony that overlooks the lower reaches of Arcturel spread out below.

Note: this description applies to all three offices in this area.

General Office Supplies

For the curious, the desk and cabinet contain the following items:

  • A nice @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.uVm7MiB71QblfnoY]{Ink Pen} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.pen0000000000000]

  • An @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.dP7jMKyHTTgVb3ii]{Ink Bottle} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.ink0000000000000]{Ink Bottle}

  • Ample blank @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.fNMkFCOvMiW2Rh3t]{Paper} paper

  • Several @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.RMi9efrW9ouHVLI2]{Books} with titles like: "Beg, Borrow & Steal", "Leveling Up Your Character" and "Lawful Ambitious: Systems of Success." Skimming the pages of these books, it's clear the content is not worth anyone's time.

Silver Beam Schematics

Characters who examine the westernmost Side Office will find a copy of the @UUID[Item.ZQs3ejY6m150wKs7]{Silver Beam Schematics}.

Gathering Evidence: Silver Beam Schematics

Important evidence can be gathered here that can be used in support of Hew the Renegade Construct's exoneration in @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3]{Glitter in the Dark}.

If the characters loot the Silver Beam Schematics, record the appropriate Event Outcome. This physical clue plays a major role in the forthcoming @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3.JournalEntryPage.Vc4ocR8zdKM8wO7i]{Presenting the Evidence} event.

Director's Office.name: Director's Office
Director's Office.text:
You step into a vast, circular office, its enormous glass window arcing across half the room and offering a breathtaking view of Arcturel. In each corner of the room, a broad stone dais supports a silent gray-metal construct.

Collected to one side are a white couches and some chairs, their pale upholstery blending in with the gray and white of the room's marble. Opposite the seating area a curved desk fashioned from brushed steel commands attention. Its surface is strewn with maps and layers of documents, the placard before it reading:

Larissa Toth, Director

Furthest from the entrance, against the window, stands a broad, immaculate conference table of silver metal, ringed with deep blue chairs whose cushions mirror the sky just beyond the glass.

Pressing Buttons

The Director's desk features a hidden buttons that can be spotted with a successful [[/skill perception 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16]] check. The button is unlabeled, and only @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth} knows what it does.

Predictably, it is used to alert security.

See: @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.Xi8DSOxh18XVrkep#activating-alerts]{Activating Alerts} in @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.Xi8DSOxh18XVrkep]{Gameplay Details} for how this works.

Office Staples

Searching the director's desk yields the same items as the desks in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.tgGJNYt0wynV4PIV]{Side Offices}.

@UUID[Item.otPv3LhRyg5KHh1u]{Larissa Toth's Memory Shard}

Waiting Room.name: Waiting Room
Waiting Room.text:
You enter a spacious waiting room with four tall, decorative columns in each corner, their surfaces wrapped with delicate silver accents. Along the pristine walls, a collection of grand paintings displays the distant, wild landscapes of Railen — vast plains, wave-swept coasts, and forbidding mountains rendered in vivid detail. Each frame is set in polished silver, drawing your eye from scene to scene.

A deep-cushioned couch and two plush chairs offer a comfortable place to sit.

To one side are double doors and a placard declaring:

Security — Employees Only

Standing By

During operating hours, there is always one member of @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7]{Silver Beam Security} in this room, standing in front of the security door. They are not hostile, but they are alert and watchful for trouble.

Beyond them, there are several more on standby in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.VCLZw6TSFNglHRMW]{Security Room}.

Security Room.name: Security Room
Security Room.text:
You find yourself in a low-lit chamber of cold gray stone, here some chairs and a sturdy stone table anchor the space, its surface bare save for a couple half-full tankards and a forgotten dagger in its sheath. The room is stark and functional, free from any decoration or finery, built for purpose rather than comfort.

Along one wall, racks display weapons of varying make—swords, hammers, axes, a handful of shields arranged for quick access. At the back, a narrow, unmarked stairwell descends to some lower level.

The stairwell here descends to the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.AbndV9j7m2yUX5On]{Barracks} found in the @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelUnd]{Arcturel Upper - Underbelly} area map.

On Guard

There are 2-4 members of @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7]{Silver Beam Security} in this room at all hours. It is their job to respond to alerts, investigate disturbances, and patrol the area.

If an alert is raised from either of the desks in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.5IHmzA71p0Fd8F4l]{Silver Beam Foyer} or @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.r3qQuNmGgOfkPzpo]{Director's Office}, this is the security team that will respond to it.

Standard Issue

The racks here have a selection of well made but otherwise unremarkable martial weapons including swords, axes, picks, hammers, and maces.

Main Plaza.name: Main Plaza
Main Plaza.text:
A broad expanse paved with golden stone cut into tidy squares stretches out before you, bands of bright brass trace the edges of walkways and create threads of gleaming gold that weave throughout the area.

At the center of the plaza is a large stone fountain, broad and tiered. Water burbles up from its crown before spilling down each tier, filling the air with a steady, cheerful rush and cooling mist.

Arranged around the fountain are a small number of open-air market stalls, each canopied with materials of bright color and pattern. Vendors call out in friendly chorus, each eager to draw a crowd beneath their shaded awnings.

Beyond the bustle of stalls, the plaza is bordered by shops that see steady foot traffic. Signs proclaim the presence of Arcturian Automatons, Rallyhome, the Silver Beam Consortium, Glimmer, and a restaurant called Precipice.

Tradeway Stalls

The things being offered in this open-air stalls vary often, with merchants coming and going as they choose. In general these stalls will sell fresh produce, hot food, preserved rations, hand-made clothing, dried herbs and spices, and sometimes even spell components.

Prices are usually very reasonable, and when they aren't the merchants are willing to haggle with a [[/skill persuasion 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] check being enough to bring them down to average market price for the item being offered.

Good Luck

The fountain contains a bevy of coins tossed into the water for good luck. Characters without a sense of decorum or shame can take a few minutes to fish coins out of the fountain. This yields a fistful of assorted coins worth [[/roll 1d6]] gold silver and can be done once.

The various onlookers and passers by will cast disapproving looks at any characters that do this.

Briez Flywell's General Goods.name: Briez Flywell's General Goods
Briez Flywell's General Goods.text:
You see a sturdy structure of heavy wood covered in a patchwork of pale plaster. The exposed wood is dark and worn, betraying the age of the structure. The double doors are fitted with handles worn smooth by countless hands. A sign over the door bears the smiling mask of a Zeph and the name of the establishment:

Briez Flywell's General Goods

Operating Hours

Briez Flywell's opens mid-morning and is open into the evening. The doors are strongly secured outside of business hours, and require a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 14 t00l=thief]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] check requiring @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000]{Lockpicks} to bypass.

Inside the structure is an eclectic assortment of goods, many imported from all over the region.

Stepping through the doors, you are greeted by immediate warmth and the mingled smells of leather, oiled steel, dried fruit, and parchment. The shop is packed at every turn. Shelves bow beneath books, boots, sacks of goods, helmets, and more. Racks and cases bristle with weapons of all kinds, and the walls are decorated with hanging items, all with prices.

On the wall is a map of the world of Ember, and a portrait of a zeph. The placard on the painted claims this is Briez Flywell, renowned treasure hunter and entrepreneur. The map is marked with numerous places, all locations that Flywell has visited and procured items for sale.

Assorted Inventory

Flywell's provides a little bit of everything, and most every kind of mundane equipment can be procured here without too much issue. In most cases the items are Arcturian in origin, but there are a high number of foreign-made versions of things, and a wide selection of books in different languages.

Good Help

Briez Flywell's is run by Darvin Nolde (Arcturian, he/him, 40s) who was hired by Flywell years ago. He has near absolute freedom to run this place as he sees fit.

Shoot the Briez

According to Darvin, Briez Flywell is a veteran member of the adventurer's guild in Ordain, an explorer, treasure hunter, and merchant. He comes and goes almost at random, and often sends back crates of items procured while on the road.

Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] or [[/knowledge artifacts]] have likely heard the name, but have never met them personally.

Elevator.name: Elevator
Elevator.text:
A small metal plate on the wall reads:

Lift Platform — Upper Offices

The heavy metal grates of the elevator mask the heavy machinery underneath. A raised control panel with a lever and lights someone to move the lift to other levels.

The Eastern Elevator is slightly different, as it has direct access to the conveyer line found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.7IJDUv3t6zlLRWsV]{Assembly Area}.

Scuffs and scrapes on the grating underfoot betray the heavier traffic this lift has seen. An input sits on the wall here where pieces can be dumped. From there, they are rolled onto the conveyer belt to be sorted and assembled by the workers down the line.

Scale of Operations

The elevators on this area map descend to the level below, contained within @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelUnd]{Arcturel Upper - Underbelly} as part of the intended gameplay of this area and its related quests.

However, narratively speaking, these elevators can access far more than just the two levels presented, and may hint at a larger Silver Beam operation "off-screen." They can be used to deliver reinforcements in combat, serve as an escape point for fleeing NPCs, and potentially access other levels of Arcturel if needed.

Washroom.name: Washroom
Washroom.text:
You open the door to a small washroom lined with white marble. The space is bright and plain, its walls and floor spotlessly clean. The air carries the faint scent of cleaning chemicals.

Occupied!

The door to this space can be locked from the inside, and can be opened with a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 10 t00l=thief]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 10]] check requiring @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000]{Lockpicks} .

Lounge Space.name: Lounge Space
Lounge Space.text:
This open-air lounge features chairs and couches arranged for comfort, offering a place for employees to pause and rest. Landscapes of some distant city hang on the wall, each held in a silver frame.

Familiar Places

Characters with [[/culture emberRailen]] or either [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/knowledge trade]] immediately recognize the city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.m4UyLxbFrbiONIb8]{Ancalen}, the home city of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.y7o8dKT1yxdnh2Pz]{Silver Beam Consortium}. Characters without the above traits need to succeed on a[[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check.

Glimmer Lounge.name: Glimmer Lounge
Glimmer Lounge.text:
You find yourself in a modest lounge awash in deep red tones, from the crimson wallpaper to the finely pattered burgundy carpet underfoot, to the richly upholstered seating all around. Even the candles cast a gentle, rosy light into this space.

A small wet bar occupies one corner, its polished wood counter set with a few waiting drinks while its shelves hold a small trove of gleaming decanters, goblets, and jars of dried fruit and everything else necessary to offer luxurious hospitality to those who visit here.

Crimson Club

During evening hours the Glimmer Lounge is open to all who know to come by. Since the upstairs store is often locked up, the only way in is through the door on this level.

Guests are welcome to mingle, explore the space, purchase drinks (3gp 3sp each), and even browse the art and gem displays upstairs in case they want to make an evening purchase.

The club is open a few hours after midnight, after that guests are ushered out and the building is locked up.

Characters that explore the side doors will find the balconies.

At either end of the lounge, sliding doors lead out to balconies. One holds a commanding view of the lower reaches of Arcturel and the sinkhole below, while the other is private, and decorated with vibrant potted plants.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
Rallyhome’s kitchen is a compact space that is busy and warm. The wood floors are well cared for but stained from years of bustling use. Heat radiates from a squat iron stove nestled against one wall. Beside the stove, a prep table is crowded with sprigs of fresh herbs, half-chopped vegetables, and various utensils.

On the opposite side, occupying nearly the entire wall, are stout shelves sagging under the weight of food. Jars filled with spices, preserved fruits, and pickles stand beside loaves of bread, wheels of cheese, and all manner of other ingredients that the cook might need.

Staff Only

The kitchen is off-limits to patrons and almost always occupied by the bar's cook. Not only this, but the bar's staff come through this area often, so windows to steal things will be few and brief.

If caught, guests are ushered back out to the bar after being relieved of any items they have in their hands. If the characters continue to be problematic, they will be removed, with guards being called if necessary.

Underbelly Alleys.name: Underbelly Alleys
Underbelly Alleys.text:
You find yourself in a secluded quarter of Arcturel situated just under the main plaza and tradeway. Here, sturdy platforms of broad metal plates and latticed grates stretch out over the yawning sinkhole below.

The spaces between these metal walkways are crowded with a wild tangle of unmarked and unremarkable buildings that could be any mixture of homes, private shops, and unseen businesses. Together they form a network of alleys connecting without pattern or plan to other passages that themselves go on to connect again and again.

You get the sensation that only locals know how to get around down here easily.

Abstract Alleyways

This area is full of buildings and places that are used by the locals but have no specific gameplay purpose. You may use this space as a transition point to other parts of the location, such as heading to the @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelTra] or down to @UUID[Scene.emberArcturelLow].

Lower Bar.name: Lower Bar
Lower Bar.text:
As you descend into the lower bar you are met with air that is rich with the scent of malt, sharp citrus, and the heavier sweetness of fruit-laden liquors mixed with the faint sting of smoke.

The centerpiece of the tavern is a truly massive circular table were patrons gather to share a drink. It dominates the common floor — its broad surface crafted from rings of contrasting stone, each band a different color. At its center is a brick-lined opening not unlike a well.

In the corner is a raised stage of worn planks, a modest raised stage sits ready for music or tales. The day's performers do their best to compete with the din of Rallyhome's occupants, but only those closest to the stage truly get to enjoy whatever show is being put on.

Against one wall stands a lengthy bar topped with golden stone, behind it, shelves spill over with bottles and crafted decanters filled with spirits in every hue. Both ends of the bar feature brass-bound taps ready to dispense liquid merriment.

The Rallyhome Well

At first glance this hole looks like the mouth of any other well, but its placement is curious and it features a funnel-like mouth meant to direct items into it.

A successful [[/skill perception 12 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12 passive]]notices that now and then patrons throw coins into the well, often before leaving the tavern, or just as they are sitting down to drink.

  • A further [[/skill insight 12 passive]] [[/skillCheck society 12 passive]] expects there is some local ritual or custom at play here that the locals might know more about.

Local History

Asking the locals, or any of the bar staff about the Rallyhome Well yields some insight into its history and purpose:

During the construction of Rallyhome this well was placed to let patrons throw coins or other tokens down into the sinkhole way down below.

As the city grew, and new levels were added, the town agreed to respect the Rallyhome well, and continued to extend the well downward through each level, ensuring that it always allowed for the full descent.

It's considered good luck to toss a coin into the well before beginning or ending any outing into the Sinkhole Depths below. Failing to do so, or worse, refusing, not only earns you a miserly reputation in the bar, but will curse you to suffer misfortune and bad luck belowground.

Characters with [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] suspect that this had to have caused some considerable headache to sort out, since building a well between suspended levels is no simple feat.

Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] know that the well would descend for hundreds of feet then open up into a freefall of several hundreds more at least. Such a fall would be utterly fatal.

Lost Treasure

Characters that ask about the fate of things thrown down the well receive a further bit of legend and color:

Just where all the coins, gems, and tokens thrown down the well end up is an enduring mystery. Many adventurers have gone into the depths looking, working out maps and search patterns with the hope of finding some pile of riches, but nobody ever has.

Rumor has it that unscrupulous individuals have even tried to intercept items thrown down by setting nets or catches, but they never find any success, as though the well bypasses their traps entirely out of spite!

Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] or [[/skill investigation 16 passive]] [[/skillCheck science 16 passive]] suspect that the scatter range of items would create a very large search area, and would make finding more than the odd coin or gem largely impossible.

Matters of Safety

Characters asking about the danger of falling down the well receive assurances they aren't the first to wonder about that:

The well has feather fall protections places in it that keeps living folk from falling to their deaths. In fact, each level has an outlet where people can get free of the well.

Every now and then some fool jumps in as a dare after one too many Open Veins, and their friends have to go fish them out of an access gate. They never get hurt, though.

Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] or [[/skill arcana 16 passive]] [[/skillCheck arcana 16 passive]] know that weaving such magic into the stone and making sure it lasts without needing constant upkeep or replacement would have been quite an undertaking. The effect itself might not be terrible complex, but making the magic robust enough to be repeatedly triggered takes a skilled mage.

Mixed to Order

Rallyhome offers a wide variety of wines and spirits, and most prices are modest, somewhere between a few copper and a couple silver for a single serving. They also have a few specialty drinks:

  • Fool's Gold — Served in a crystal goblet, this pale gold liqueur swirls with glimmering gold flecks. The drink is syrupy and sweet, with a metallic aftertaste. It's 10gp 1gp and twice the price it should be on purpose.

  • The Open Vein —Served in a tall glass that's cold as ice, the drink features layers of gold, red, brown, and amber liquors. It's sweet up front, becoming bitter, then has a smoky finish. It's 5gp 5sp a glass, and hits harder than a miner's pick. Drinking one requires a [[/save con 15]] save against poison, failure leaves a character &reference[poisoned] for an hour a [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] or [[/skillCheck science 15]] to space the consumption out sufficiently for safe consumption, failure leaves a character @Condition[poisoned] .

  • Sinkhole Draught — Served in a squat, round cup, the liquid within is blue and slightly glittering. It smells of the earth, and when stirred, glows faintly. It's bright and floral at first, then develops a salty, earthy flavor that numbs the tongue slightly. It's made with a bioluminescent mushroom liquor made in Arcturel. Costs 6gp 6sp per cup.

  • Druid's Draught — Served in an earthenware mug, this murky green-brown mixture of beer, spirits and muddled herbs has a deeply herbal flavor that lingers long after the mug is empty. Locals swear that it'll cure whatever ails you, costs 1gp 1sp per mug.

Warehousing.name: Warehousing
Warehousing.text:
This warehouse is lined with rows of towering steel shelves, each reaching to the stone ceiling and laden with stacks and baskets of metal — polished plates, rods, gears, and half-assembled construct frames, and more. The air carries the sharp tang of iron and oil.

Wandering Workers

There is at least one Silver Beam Engineer and one member of Silver Beam Security in this area at all hours of the day. While the engineer is distracted with examining and cataloguing the collection of materials and construct parts here, the guard is actively patrolling and watching for signs of trouble.

The guard's path takes them outside often, and the Engineer takes ample breaks, getting some fresh air out on the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.nWLqXV24uNbDYkTS]{Walkways} every five minutes or so. If both the guard and engineer happen to be outside at the same time, they may chat for several minutes.

Work Orders

Near the elevator are parts packed in sturdy crates or loaded into wire baskets. All of them bear bright tags, marking them for transport to distant assembly areas located elsewhere in the Silver Beam headquarters.

Characters with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check notice that some of the crates are staged near the elevator and are marked for the floor right above them.

Stacks and Shelves

Characters that examine the shelves who also visited @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.EUcIZPY7x0qFHe3c]{the Scrapyard} location as part of the @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3.JournalEntryPage.HSTCVHrXQN0q2wFw]{Junkyard Cogs} event will recognize the processed pieces of @UUID[Actor.0xDU0k3l8V4movO8]{Chessman} constructs. However, these have been properly converted to Servitor pieces, and no longer bear any damning marks.

Barracks.name: Barracks
Barracks.text:
You enter a barracks meant to house off-duty security and other personnel, the floor made of riveted iron plates that echo each step. Five sturdy bunkbeds line the walls, their sturdy iron frames bolted to the walls. Each bed is fitted with a thin mattress, white linens, and dark blue sheets.

In the center of the room stands a table, surrounded by chairs. The place is dimly lit by a single lantern hung from a ceiling bracket, the air cool and heavy with the scent of metal and stone. Everything here is built for function and endurance, leaving little room for comfort.

Distracted Defenders

Almost all hours of the day there are at least two off-duty members of @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7]{Silver Beam Security} here, chatting with each other. They aren't expecting trouble, and are not especially alert or wary unless given a reason to be.

Useful Items

Investigating the footlockers here yields two @UUID[Item.LZAFIWKck47hrjRt]{Silver Beam Uniforms} which can help characters blend in if they want to utilize stealth.

Cubicles.name: Cubicles
Cubicles.text:
You find a small, utilitarian area tucked beside the lift platform. Four simple cubicles stand together, each walled off by this panels fixed with iron bolts. Within each cramped work space are the signs of constant busyness — thick ledgers, sprawling survey reports, mining maps, and stacks of unfiled work orders, all needing attention.

Wary Workers

During operating hours consortium employees can be found here doing their thankless jobs. They ignore anyone walking past unless they are acting strangely or doing things to draw attention. Characters wearing Silver Beam uniforms won't get a second glance if they leave these clerks alone.

However, if characters do happen to draw attention, the clerks will immediately cry out, trying to draw attention from security in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.RspNcNYsYXsfDcL3]{Warehousing} and @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.AbndV9j7m2yUX5On]{Barracks} areas if they can.

They will flee if fighting breaks out.

Walkways.name: Walkways
Walkways.text:
You stand on an external walkway, its grated floor and pipe rails all that keep you from the long drop into the sinkhole depths. The walkways stretch across the face of the structure, connecting to distant doors and platforms. The wind whistles through the open iron, and there is little here to block the sweep of air or the feeling of height.

Well Traveled

The Silver Beam personnel inside this level have a tendency to come out here to smoke, take in some fresh air, patrol, and take breaks. Every five minutes or so someone will come out here. The general lack of cover means that hiding is next to impossible here.

Storage.name: Storage
Storage.text:
This cramped storage room is packed with crates stacked two-high, clusters of kegs and barrels, and burlap sacks filled with flour, dried beans, and other staples bound for the kitchen.

Rising from floor to ceiling opposite the entrance is a shelf unit crafted from rough-cut planks and thick iron brackets fixed to the brick walls.

The shelves hold an assortment of bar necessities: stacks of pewter mugs and sturdy plates, jars of pickled vegetables, dusty bottles of syrup and tonic, spare candles and lantern oil, and more not worthy of mention.

Packed Larder

While this supply room is packed with goods necessary to operate Rallyhome, nothing on these shelves is especially eye-catching or valuable looking. The materials here are mundane at best, worthless at worst.

Employees Only

There's a large amount of fresh food, small amounts of commodities, and a few spare bottles of alcohol here to be taken if desired. However, this area is off-limits to patrons and the bar's staff come through this area often, so windows to steal things will be few and brief.

If caught, guests are ushered back out to the bar after being relieved of any items they have in their hands. If the characters continue to be problematic, they will be removed, with guards being called if necessary.

Sentinel Display.name: Sentinel Display
Sentinel Display.text:
You see a broad, raised dais of spotless white, at its center rests an imposing statue — a heavy automaton clad in of overlapping plates of brushed steel. One hand bears a massive claw, the other arm is fixed with a long blade. Its back features two projectors of unknown purpose.

Though the statue is motionless, every part of it radiates one purpose alone: war.

At the base of the dais, a polished plaque reads:

The Silver Beam Sentinel

The next generation in combat constructs.

Examining Automatons

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] recognize that this massive constructs was probably functional at some point. Some of the construction looks haphazard, with gaps in the armor, and crude, probably underpowered servos. This was likely an early prototype turned into a display.

Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] recognize the style of the machine, as with the rest of the Servitors in this place, is more akin to that of Aedir constructs and automatons than classical Arcturian designs.

Contents Under Pressure

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] or making a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check on the construct notice a poorly protected tank of fuel just under this the construct's left shoulder. Going by the gauge there, it is still mostly full and pressurized.

This is not only an indication that the construct once was operational, but is a considerable fire hazard. If compromised, that tank would probably fill the surrounding area with a large explosion of fire and shrapnel.

Explosive Hazard

Characters that noticed the fuel tank on the construct can attack that fuel tank to cause it to explode.The tank itself has an AC of 10, and 10 hit points. If destroyed, it explodes in a 20ft area centered on the construct and deals [[/damage 3d6 piercing]] damage to any creature in that area. Those who do at least 10 damage with attacks against the specific target of the fuel tank cause the fuel tank to explode in a 20ft area centered on the construct. Those caught in the blast suffer [[/hazard 9 fortitude health piercing]]{Shrapnel Blast}.

If the tank is destroyed by an attack or spell that deals lightning or fire damage the tank explodes more violently and in a larger area. This creates a 40ft area centered on the construct that deals [[/damage 3d6 piercing]] and [[/damage 3d6 fire]] damage to any creature in that area , anyone caught in this area suffer [[/hazard 9 fortitude health piercing]]{Shrapnel…}[[/hazard 9 fortitude health piercing]]{…Flaming Sharpnel}

.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for Lower Arcturel depicts a small section of Lower Arcturel — like many of the other developed caverns that exists throughout this section of the city, it contains mining operations (the Level 3 Mine, which specializes in iron ore), a few businesses that cater to locals (an apothecary, a distillery, a repair shop, and a stable), and the residence of mine foreman Zodi Trask.

Gazetteer Entry

Located in the depths of the sinkhole that the city has been built into, the lower section of Arcturel is both the heart of the city's mining operation and the core of its operations. It descends over many levels, but the area is collectively known as the Dives, with collections of businesses and residences found at all levels within the lower section of the city's sinkhole walls. While there are plenty of supplies and work to be found in the area, the Dives are not for tourists or visiting dignitaries — this section of Arcturel is of and for those who live and work in the city.

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
This section of Lower Arcturel has been infiltrated by an Aburyx named Kilner, who is using the mine at its heart as his base of operations. Many of the recent troubles within Arcturel have been caused by Kilner to discredit House Cevher and drive locals away from the area surrounding the mine.

Illumination

At this level of the sinkhole, traditional fires do not stay lit without help — all unprotected candles are quickly extinguished. Instead, locals use the glowing mushrooms on the sinkhole walls, @UUID[Item.pCl2T09DRBETkkbZ]{Chasm Candles}, and the occasional Inkaro pearl for lighting.

Within the Dives section of Lower Arcturel, lighting is dim but steady.

Within the mine, lighting is bright, coming primarily from Inkaro pearls, which are hung like lanterns throughout the mine. These can be temporarily affected by the actions of the Device in the center of the mine (see The Device below).

Terrain

Terrain in the Dives section of Lower Arcturel is normal. Terrain within the mines is generally normal unless otherwise stated (it can be affected by actions of the Device or of the Vorg that burrow in the ground beneath it).

Elevation

Ceilings in the Dives section of Lower Arcturel are 10-feet high. Ceilings in the mine are 20-feet high.

Additional Gameplay

Infested Tunnels

Many of the tunnels of the mine have been overrun by Vorg, which often bury themselves beneath the surface of the ground. For more, see @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.MyIYNT8LU0HjQgT7]{The Tunnels}.

The Device

The Device is a large metallic machine located in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.eApuNVjHrvwXGB8C]{The Hub} at the center of the mine. Built by the Tyraphem @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Kilner} who now inhabits the mine, it is being actively tended and defended by a pack of @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{Skither}. Eventually, if fully activated, it would collapse part of the tunnel system in Lower Arcturel, creating a large disaster that can be blamed on House Cevher.

When the Device is powered and active, it periodically creates a @UUID[RollTable.XrY0Hys2AjCMJP8i]{Mine Effect}, as indicated in the room information throughout the Area Walkthrough.

The Device can be destroyed directly by an attack or by cutting its power using the hidden switch in the @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.byNiHbuGQAyGerNQ]{Empty Room}.

Level 3 Mine Office.name: Level 3 Mine Office
Level 3 Mine Office.text:
This office is one that could be found in any standard mining concern. Papers sit on the middle of the desk in relatively neat piles and the books around the office are organized in orderly fashion on nearby shelves. Only the slight hint of dust in the air gives the sense that this place hasn't been used in some time.

When the mine is active, this room serves as the on-site office for the foreman. A look at the books on the shelves yields nothing specific - they are primarily books about mining and records from previous years about ore quotas and other mine-related business.

Characters can find a note on the desk about recent occurrences in the mine, @UUID[Item.SjKt5G50dmCSOgbH]{Troubling Reports}, without a check.

The Storage Room.name: The Storage Room
The Storage Room.text:
The remains of an experiment of some kind — shattered test tubes and vials, abandoned papers and beakers — are scattered across two tables and the floor. Whatever happened here, it has left an acrid scent at the air that seems to claw at your senses with each step.

Entering The Storage Room

Toxic Air

The air in this room is toxic — any character who enters the room must make a successful [[/save constitution 14]] save[[/skillCheck medicine 14]] or [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] to take precautions against the toxins,ortake [[/damage 1d6 poison]] damage. On a success, damage is halved. If characters enter combat while in this room, they must reattempt this save on each turn that they begin while in this room or they are @Condition[poisoned] until they leave the room.

The Device Activates

If the Device in the Hub is powered, it activates once the first party member enters the room. Roll on the @UUID[RollTable.XrY0Hys2AjCMJP8i]{Lower Arcturel Mine Effect} table for the action taken by the device.

Finding the Source

Characters who make a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check can confirm that they heard no sound before the strange effect came through the mine. If they previously heard any sound in another room, it is absent here.

Toxic Substances

Characters that search the substances left behind by whoever was experimenting in this room discover the following without a check:

  • A pile of mining ore dust.

  • A container with @UUID[Item.4bmOJe7s9TwbHbvC]{Concentrated Ore Dust}.

  • A thick whitish gloop (@UUID[Item.qvLD88iUi3FBdkdc]{Metal Crumbler}).

Identifying the Substances

Characters can identify any of the substances as follows. They can also be identified by the apothecary, Emelyn Arvoda, who sells her wares in nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.yObJp4josnr70zog].

  • Characters can identify the regular mining ore dust without a check.

  • The Gray Dust in the Container: Characters who have a sample of @UUID[Item.Pwr7R7tZOhltCXiB]{Suspicious Karal} identify the dust as smelling identical to the odd smell in the sample. Characters that make a successful [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]], have [[/knowledge monsters]], [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.alchemyNovice000]], or that are already familiar with the substance from the distillery can identify it as @UUID[Item.4bmOJe7s9TwbHbvC]{Concentrated Ore Dust}.

  • The Whitish Goop: Characters who have visited @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.crgIhy7BVETKJYHN]{Wrestful Repairs} can identify it as being similar but not identical to the "glue" compound used to repair many of Arcturel's machines. WIth a successful [[/knowledge machines]] , [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.alchemyNovice000]] or [[/knowledge alchemy]] they know that it is an alchemical gel that breaks down metals. Emelyn Arvoda can identify it as @UUID[Item.qvLD88iUi3FBdkdc]{Metal Crumbler}.

Searching The Room

The Passageway

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check to search the room spot an odd trick of the light in the northwest corner — the hallmark of an illusion that covers the entrance to the passageway with the image of a solid wall. Any character who has Truesight, or who disrupts the magic using Dispel Magic, an anti-magic item or spell, or similar, uses @Spell[illusion.sense], or who uses some sort of anti-magic item or spell,

clearly sees as passageway instead of the wall. This passage leads to @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.QpHwyxq7yJZGhjFY]{Waterborne Family Distillery}.

Characters can also take an action to Study that corner and try to spot the origin of the odd light. If they succeed on a[[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, they can tell that the wall in that corner is an illusion. If a character fails the investigation check by 4 or more critically fails, they become convinced that the wall is real for the next hour and will not change their minds even in the face of evidence to the contrary.

The Hub.name: The Hub
The Hub.text:
A tall metallic cylinder sits in the middle of the room. It is covered with balls of what appear to be attached metal, but as you enter the room, the small metal objects detach themselves with a whir and turn towards you, eyes glowing and metallic claws extended.

Gamemaster Note: The Device

The device in the center of this room has AC 20, 30 HP, and a damage threshold of 10 (any attack that deals it 9 or fewer HP of damage has no effect). When it reaches 0 HP, it is destroyed. It is immune to Poison, Psychic, and Radiant Damage.

The device in the center of this room may be powered or unpowered.

If the device is powered up, it takes a turn at the end of each round of combat, triggering a @UUID[RollTable.XrY0Hys2AjCMJP8i]{Lower Arcturel Mine Effect}. If it takes damage at any time, the closest Skither redirects to the Device and attempts to repair it, restoring [[/roll 1d6]] in HP to the device per round.

If the machine is powered down or deactivated, it takes no actions and is not repaired by the Skithers. The device can be powered down by interacting with the hidden switch hidden behind a false wall found in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.byNiHbuGQAyGerNQ].

@Embed[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]

Skithers Attack!

The skithers are more powerful as a group and usually attempt to congregate around a single target unless they are low in HP Health.

When a Skither's Hit Points are reduced to half their maximum it begins looking for ways to use its @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.hZGnt69Mp5meOQlq]{Self Sacrifice} to deal as much damage to as many enemies as possible, or turn the tide of a battle. If it can, it avoids harming its own side with its @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.bXttKphal9Z1FHk5]{Dying Burst} feature.
