The Dying Burst does no damage to the Device and does not factor into the Skithers' decision of where to position themselves.

Skithers may lack self-preservation instincts, but when they begin to grow low on Health, especially if they are @Condition[weakened], they will seek an optimal position to trigger its @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.sacrificeSelf000] and @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.radiantDeathBurs]. The ideal position for it is one that places it between an ally and opponent in such a way that its burst will hit enemies but not allies.

Investigating the Machine

Once the machine has been deactivated, characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] can tell from the patterns of wear on the device that the Skithers were most interested in repairing/defending one particular section of it, which is marked with the symbol of an explosion. Characters who have [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check, and can tell without a check that the device was likely rigged to explode at some point.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check can find a marking scratched into the metal of the machine between the other marks of damage. It says Wandren.

The Gathering Place.name: The Gathering Place
The Gathering Place.text:
Once, this might have been a place where people gathered before heading deeper into the mine to put on equipment, grab a tool, or sit down for a shared meal during a break, but it has clearly been left in a hurry, with tools laying wherever they were dropped and chairs and benches overturned.

This room is used as a gathering place for those who work in the mines — a place to store tools, have meals, and socialize.

Note: The Device In The Mine

Once characters enter the mine, they will be subjected to periodic effects from the device that has been built at the center of the mine. Each room description will note when to trigger another mine effect if the device is still active (it can be deactivated by cutting power or by destroying it directly).

Once the entire party has entered the area, a wind blows from deeper inside the mine:

Suddenly, a whooshing sound fills the air and a strong wind blows through the room from deeper within the mine, knocking over a cup on one of the tables and toppling one of the remaining standing chairs before battering against you where you stand.

A Stiff Wind

Characters must make a successful [[/save strength 15]] saving throw [[/skillCheck athletics 15]], or they are pushed backwards 20 feet.

  • If characters are pushed into a wall or gate as a result of this action, they take [[/damage 1d10 bludgeoning]] damage suffer [[/hazard 6 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Terrain Impact}.

  • If characters fail the check by 5 or more critically fail, they also fall prone @Condition[prone], taking [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] from the hard fall suffering [[/hazard 3 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{A Hard Fall} in addition to any other damage.

Finding the Source

The strong wind has definitely come from within the mine, but beyond that, its origin is unclear.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check can tell that this gust of wind is not a natural in origin.

    • If characters succeed by 3 or more critically succeed, they know that the effect is being generated by someone or something in the center of the mine.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check sense that magic is involved in whatever has created this effect, but don't know more about what it is or how it works. Given that there is no one in sight, is unlikely to be a conventional spell.

    • If characters succeed by 3 or more critically succeed, they know that this is magic is not of Ember, in fact it somehow feels like it was generated forces from Luxarum.

    • A character with [[/path emberLightsworn]] automatically succeeds on this check.

The Empty Pit.name: The Empty Pit
The Empty Pit.text:
The ground of the cavern is rough and pockmarked, and clumps of dirt and rock are spread haphazardly across the ground, as if flung in all directions. Between them, pieces of metal from carts and other mining equipment have been spread out across the uneven ground, separated into collections of pipes, sockets, gears, and wheels.

This cavern was once a mining pit, but has been largely mined out and instead was most recently used as a place to store vehicles and other mining equipment, all of which has been torn apart since the mine was abandoned.

The Device Activates

If the Device in the Hub is powered, it activates once the first party member enters the room.

A distinct clicking sound can be heard in the distance, followed by a slight whir.

Roll on the @UUID[RollTable.XrY0Hys2AjCMJP8i]{Lower Arcturel Mine Effect} table for the action taken by the device.

Finding the Source

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check know that the sound of clicking comes from immediately north of them.

Spare Parts

Characters may take a closer look at the metal parts spread on the ground.

  • With a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]]check, characters see small markings on the metal, made by something metal repeatedly scraping against it.

    • If they succeed by 3 or more critically succeed, they can tell that the marks have been made by metal pincers or a creature with metallic hands. If the party has already encountered a @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{Skither}, the pincer markings match the creature's claws.

  • With a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, characters know that something or someone arranged these metal pieces into different piles.

    • If they succeed by 3 or more critically succeed, it is clear that a machine was disassembled to create the piles, as if the someone or something that made the pile was collecting spare parts.

Rocky Ground

Characters may try to determine what has caused the unevenness in the ground. If they previously investigated the uneven ground in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.B6g7UeoE2Md4qIZa]{The Active Mine Pit}, they can confirm without a check that this disturbance in the ground is identical to what they discovered there.

  • With a successful [[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check, characters know that the roughness of the ground was caused by a creature or object — it did not occur naturally. The disturbances in the ground were caused by something burrowing beneath it.

    • If they succeed by 3 or more critically succeed, they know that this creature or object is large, has a serpentine shape and has emerged in this room in the past, causing the spray of dirt across the room.

    • If the party has already encountered a @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR]{Vorg}, they know that the disturbance was caused by one.

The Last Pit.name: The Last Pit
The Last Pit.text:
In the center of the vast cavern before you, a radiant figure stands with a face of yellow light and a form composed of alien-looking metal bands. It appears to have its head lowered, gazing down at a desk, tapping its gauntleted hand against the wood. A long sword, crafted from concentrated light, rests against the desk, easily within reach at any moment.

After a moment, it jerks its head up and immediately grabs its sword, with its face flaring with what you assume is an expression of anger or intense emotion. Its voice then rings out like a deep musical instrument, whistling slightly as if the words themselves are hard to pronounce.

Why aren't you dead yet?

The figure appears to enunciate each syllable clearly, then steps away from behind the desk and twirls its blade around with practiced skill.

Nevermind. Soon enough..

@Embed[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]

Kilner Attacks!

Kilner immediately attacks as the party enters its presence, without hesitation. Kilner is a Tyraphem from the Inner Realm of Luxarum and is fiercely intelligent and cruel, and will attack the party in different ways.

  • It will attack anyone who attempts to stay at range rather than engage it in melee; this might include casters or healers, or an archer. It will do this even if he provokes an attack of opportunity from a character attempting to pin him down.

  • He will use his summoned minions and creatures to pin down melee characters.

Kilner has command over a pet Vorg at the back of the room and can use his @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0.Item.2sV9jgOZ9nL7oT2d]{Beckoning} ability to summon pairs of fast-moving Skithers, which attack the party directly and when they are injured Kilner uses his @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0.Item.o073sZpHxpgrYyCA]{Reckoning} ability, to make them explode, causing to everyone around them.

This Aburyx has command over a pet Vorg and can use his @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0.Item.callSkither00000] action to summon fast-moving Skithers to aid him in combat, whether by attacking the party directly or to make use of the Skither's @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.sacrificeSelf000] ability.

The Aburyx otherwise will fight the party to the death, its zeal driving it to fight even when @Condition[weakened] or @Condition[broken]. In combat, it leans heavily on its mastery of the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeIllumination]] and passive effects from @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0.Item.lightbringer0000] as its primary form of attacks. It will begin combat by buffing itself with @Spell[illumination.aspect] before settling into a rotation of @Spell[illumination.ray] for ranged combatants and @Spell[illumination.strike] for close combat.

The Aburyx is not merely resistant to radiant damage, it also regains health in cases where the resistance would reduce the incoming damage to a negative amount, it regains Health thanks to @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0.Item.radiantAbsorptio].

The Aburyx fights to the death. On its demise, its carapace condenses into a molten pile of an unknown metal.

The Device

If the Device found in the Mine Hub is still active, it takes a turn at the end of each round, causing a @UUID[RollTable.XrY0Hys2AjCMJP8i]{Mine Effect}. If all mine effects are expended, the Device pauses for 1 round then begins again. Clear all results from the rollable table (making all available again) and begin re-rolling.

After the Battle

Once Kilner and its minons have been defeated, the party is welcome to explore the area. The desk and a display shelf are readily visible.

Kilner's Desk

A map of Lower Arcturel has been spread out on the center of the table, held down by paperweights and a large bottle of ink. Each of the rooms that held a business has a symbol on it as follows:

  • The Distillery: The skull and crossbones symbol and a red X.

  • Hob's Steeds: A picture of a lizard splayed on its side, a flame, and a red X.

  • Zodi Trask's House: A piece of crystal. There is no other symbol.

  • Wrestful Repairs: A broken machine and a red X.

  • Arvoda's Elixirs: A question mark.

The mine is also depicted, with the following symbols:

  • The Hub: A picture of a cylinder surrounded by smaller orbs

  • The Last Pit: A flaming sword

  • A room to the left of the Last Pit: Book shelves

  • A room immediately below the room with the book shelves: Test Tubes

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] know that the map was a tracker of actions taken by Kilner against the local businesses, and suggests that there is a room with papers or books to the west of the pit.

The large bottle of ink is @UUID[Item.sWmD7INuv2mMZABt]{shifting ink.} Characters who succeed on a [[/check arcana 15]][[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check, use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify} spell , or have [[/knowledge alchemy]] can identify it.

The other papers and items on the desk have no particular meaning to the party.

Kilner's Display Shelves

The Aburyx's display shelf holds a number of items of note, including:

  • A @UUID[Item.omZrpwjq5FJuyffF]{Blue Inkaro Pearl}.

  • A few pieces of odd crystal that seem as if they glow slightly from the inside.

  • Several metal tools used for dismantling things, including a crowbar and wrench.

  • A skull of a creature that resembles one of Hob's riding lizards

  • Broken heating lamps, similar to those found in Hob Korell's lizard enclosure. Characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check can tell that they were intentionally broken.

If characters succeed on a [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] while searching the room, they find an oddly placed wooden wall in the western section of this pit. If they have seen the map on Kilner's Desk, they have @Advantage[2] on this check. With a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, characters spot wooden hinges on one side of the wall. If characters push on the wall, it swings open, revealing a room behind it, filled with papers.

The Hidden Room

A large number of books and papers sits strewn across the room. Other than these documents, the room is empty of everything but an opulent velvet cloak (a @UUID[Item.l2Oc7eBtvb9rsNus]) that hangs from a coat rack against the wall. If characters search the pockets, they find @UUID[Item.hFBEeNSQct3Tgkhc]{A Message to Tantrin} inside.

On a search of the books for anything of note, characters with a successful [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] check can note handwriting identical to that on the desk on one small book, titled @UUID[Item.AYDgFBnsqMR51Uqt]{Kilner Notes}.

If characters go through the other papers, they discover three things that are apparent from the many overlapping notes:

  • The figure that they just deafted was named Kilner, and was sent here by someone else, who is only referred to in the correspondence in the room as "Bright Lord."

  • There are several references to House Wandren in the correspondence; it doesn't necessarily suggest they are behind the disruptions and creatures here in the mine, but rather that Kilner was tracking some of their movements and receiving goods from a Wandren contact.

  • The words "For Other Fortunes" appear on one of the documents, providing a tie to the otherhood bandits that Lyla is attempting to track down.

Secondary Storage.name: Secondary Storage
Secondary Storage.text:
The room may have held something once, but it has since been stripped down to nothing more than a set of bare walls and smooth, solid ground. The entryways ahead and behind you are ordinary wooden archways, and a similar archway to the south has been filled in with a thick gray metal.

This room never held much while the mine was active, serving as a place for people to rest or store temporary objects. The Aburyx controlling the mine used the passageway behind the room for the power source and switch to the device, hiding it behind a false metal wall in the south of the room.

Investigating the Room

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check see nothing immediately out of the ordinary. The room is empty and the ground is flat and smooth. However, if they have previously encountered the uneven ground in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.B6g7UeoE2Md4qIZa]{The Active Mine Pit} or @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.UATwymF7nTN09TAZ]{The Empty Pit}, they notice that this ground has been undisturbed by whatever went through those areas.

  • Characters who make a successful on [[/skill nature 14]] or [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check know that the avoidance of this particular room is odd given the behavior of the creatures elsewhere and may point to there being something special or different about this room.

  • Characters who dig into the ground in this room or move it with a spell like Mold Earth find coiled wiring beneath the room, which prevents any creatures from burrowing through the area. Characters that make a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check can tell that the wiring originates to the south of their current location, where the metal wall stands.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check of the room note that the metal-filled opening to the south is the only archway they have seen of this type that is not an open entryway.

  • Characters who succeed by 2 or more can also tell that the metal has been poured recently, likely around or after the time the mine was abandoned by the miners.

The Metal "Wall"

The wall to the south of the room is a false one, which is used by the Skithers to reach the power to the nearby Device and shut it down for maintenance. It can be opened by cutting through the metal or by applying heat to the wall in two specific locations simultaneously (which is how it is opened by the Skithers).

Characters who knock on or strike the wall find that it appears solid, but also fairly thin. Characters who succeed on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check, are proficient in @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.KndVe2insuctjIaj]{Smith's Tools} have at least [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.smithingNovice00]], or have [[/knowledge crafts]] know that the metal can be cut through with acid or fire, but not broken with traditional weapons.

  • The wall can be sliced through by a metal weapon exposed to heat (whether by a flame or through a spelllike Heat Metal @Spell[flame.touch] ) or a tool dipped in acid (including the acid found in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.o06g8caWK9wvMvSR].

  • The wall can also be either cut through or melted by a spell of level 1 or above that does fire or acid damage (like Acid Arrow or Burning Sphere) like @Spell[flame.arrow] or by using a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.causticPhial0000].

Characters who make a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] or [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check to examine the wall find two slight circular dents in the upper section of the wall. The dents are equally shaped and perfectly round.

  • Applying direct force to the dents in the wall has no effect, but characters who touch the dents find them to be hot to the touch.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check, are are proficient in @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.KndVe2insuctjIaj]{Smith's Tools} have at least [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.smithingNovice00]], or have [[/knowledge crafts]] can tell that the dents have recently had heat or fire applied to them.

  • The wall will open if heat or fire is applied to both dents at the same time, either through physical or magical flame (including flame from Fire Bolt, Produce Flame, and similar cantrips) . If heat or fire is applied to only one of the dents, the wall rises slightly to reveal an entryway behind it, then slams shut.

The Hidden Switch

Behind the wall is a switch that controls the flow of power to The Device nearby in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.eApuNVjHrvwXGB8C]{The Hub}.

The wall gives way to reveal a small cluster of gleaming gold brass made of intricately formed segments and sections. The most prominent part of its design is a sliding switch below a glowing glass orb that pulses with yellow light.

There are no labels, no instructions, no indication toward what this controls or influences.

If the party flips the switch this changes @UUID[Actor.NavjdvoV2CLsRAij] in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.eApuNVjHrvwXGB8C] to a powered down state. Read the following:

The glass orb over the switch goes dark. You hear a sudden high-pitched whirring hum that rapidly descends in pitch as if diving off of a cliff, followed by a loud thumping noise to the east of you and an almost total silence.

What Comes Next

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]]check can hear a slight whirring in the silence like the fluttering of wings. It is also coming from the east.

The Active Mine Pit.name: The Active Mine Pit
The Active Mine Pit.text:
Veins of iron ore can be seen on the rocks in the room, but the pickaxes used to mine them and the cart used to move them have been tossed aside and left behind. The pit is otherwise empty, though there are furrows and pockmarks in the ground that seem to hint at some recent activity.

When the mine was active, this was a cavern being actively used for mining and retrieving iron ore.

The Device Activates

If the Device in the Hub is powered, it activates once the first party member enters the room. Roll on the @UUID[RollTable.XrY0Hys2AjCMJP8i]{Lower Arcturel Mine Effect} table for the action taken by the device.

Finding the Source

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check can confirm that they heard no sound before the strange effect came through the mine. If they previously heard any sound in another room, it is absent here.

Hidden Tracks

Characters may try to determine what has caused the unevenness in the ground. If they previously investigated the uneven ground in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.UATwymF7nTN09TAZ]{The Empty Pit}, they can confirm without a check that this disturbance in the ground is identical to what they discovered there.

  • With a successful [[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check, characters know that the roughness of the ground was caused by a creature or object — it did not occur naturally. The disturbances in the ground were caused by something burrowing beneath it.

    • If they succeed by 3 or more critically succeed, they know that this creature or object is large, has a serpentine shape and has emerged in this room in the past, causing the spray of dirt across the room.

    • If the party has already encountered a @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR]{Vorg}, they know that the disturbance was caused by one.

The Tunnels.name: The Tunnels
The Tunnels.text:
The tunnels of the mine are narrow, and while tracks can be clearly seen in the ground, it doesn't seem as if they are being actively used. Despite that, there is a shuddering of the ground from time to time, with no obvious cause or explanation.

Gamemaster's Note

Vorg lurk both in and beneath the tunnels of the mine. While empty passageways may appear safe to traverse, the Vorg are drawn to sound and will investigate any group traveling through their territory.

Avoiding the Vorg

Each time 2 or more characters are within a tunnel in Lower Arcturel, they must make a group [[/skill stealth 15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check. If half or more of the characters within the tunnel passes the check, the group crosses the tunnel without issue. If the group fails the check, two Vorg make their way toward the party, attempting to trap them within the tunnel by approaching from each entrance.

The ground beneath you begins to shake, ever so slightly, and a faint clacking sound emanates from the ground. muffled by the dirt beneath your feet. Something is underneath you, and it is growing closer.

Vorg Combat

@Embed[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR]

Vorg Attack!

Vorg on the surface attack anything they see on sight and often attempt to herd their prey into narrower passageways to make escape more difficult.

Once they have emerged, Vorg target those who they perceive to be either largest or strongest, beginning with a @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR.Item.QwM0QfEeSuZ8437H]{Slam} attack, and try to remain close enough to their prey that their heated bodies can do extra damage.

Vorg are opportunistic predators that work the terrain of their hunting territory to their advantage. They will harry and herd their prey toward narrower passageways in order to make escape more difficult, and so they can better use their ability to burrow.

A Vorg will typically initiate combat by either:

  • Emerging from a borrow very close to its prey to take advantage of its @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR.Item.burrower00000000] feature.

  • Dropping on its from above with a @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR.Item.clingingGrip0000]

A Vorg will attempt to flee if it is @Condition[weakened] or @Condition[broken], but if it cannot escape, it will attempt to position itself as close to as many enemies as possible to ensure its @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR.Item.radiantDeathBurs] is effective.

Arvoda's Elixirs.name: Arvoda's Elixirs
Arvoda's Elixirs.text:
Bowls, glasses, and pans of what seem to be hundreds of different substances crowd the tables of Arvoda's Elixirs. Between them, the proprietor, Emelyn Arvoda, a middle-aged kivahr woman wearing fine Ordani dress, leans her large body over a handful of herbs, studying them through what appears to be a gold-rimmed magnifying glass.

How can I help you in these troubling times?

Emelyn Arvoda is a pleasant — if quite mercenary — proprietor, always willing to help if you need anything, so long as you either buy something from her shop or pay her for her expertise. With a bit of persuasion, she can sometimes be convinced to lower her prices, but she does not believe in giving something for nothing.

If characters are visiting Arvoda as part of An Old Friend, they can ask her about what she knows in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.niW0x73bUCnjmHqn#asking-the-apothecary]{Asking the Apothecary}.

Goods for Sale

Arvoda's Elixirs is stocked with alchemical supplies, potions, and other consumables that are common or rare, all at a 20% markup, including:

  • @UUID[Item.QwzYLBnZ1PjLFEuI]{Alchemical Silver}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.Fc6UfFNOnW80XMzi]{Antitoxin} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.antitoxin0000000]

  • @UUID[Item.FXNnFGmbtvZrJEhq]{Everbloom}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPotionofHea]{Potion of Healing}
    @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingElixir000]

With a successful [[/skill persuasion 17]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 17]] check, she will lower them to normal prices.

Wrestful Repairs.name: Wrestful Repairs
Wrestful Repairs.text:
Gamemaster Note

If characters are visiting the repair shop as part of An Old Friend, read @UUID[..CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.niW0x73bUCnjmHqn#investigating-the-repair-shop]{Investigating the Repair Shop} on the event page.

In addition to half-broken machines and tools, various bibs and bobs are scattered around the shop, and it seems as if many things have piled up in recent days. Notes are scattered around the shop, many with the word "Completed" on them, which has often been amended to read "To Be Completed." Toward the front of the shop, a sign next to a doorway reads "Please put items to be repaired here. Thank you! -Rennerie"

The shop has a number of spare tools and items and a set of papers on a bench that reads "Repair Log." Locals come in and out regularly, dropping off and picking up items freely.

Hob Korell's Unconventional Steeds.name: Hob Korell's Unconventional Steeds
Hob Korell's Unconventional Steeds.text:
Gamemaster Note

If characters are visiting the repair shop as part of An Old Friend, read @UUID[..CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.niW0x73bUCnjmHqn#investigating-the-stables]{Investigating the Stables} on the event page.

The dulcet sound of ambient music surrounds you as you enter this lavishly-decorated stable. The musty but welcoming space is inhabited by a trio of large companionable reptiles, attended by a stablehand who casually prepares them a meal of assorted fruits and meats.

While Hob Korell sells a variety of uncommon steeds throughout the city, this location primarily caters to the large lizards known as @UUID[Actor.T6YcptpxcCLx4yLx]{Jobri}.

The stables are a point of pride, and are decorated somewhat opulently: magically-infused stones play music, the desk is decorated with several books about magical and mundane reptile care (including one called "The Lizard Life"), and there are a number of peculiar grooming tools scattered throughout.

@Embed[Actor.T6YcptpxcCLx4yLx]

At any given point in time, Hob Korell (CG, Waerd Keth, he/him) can be found working here alongside his stablehands Kaol (CG, Arcturian Human, he/him) or Jann (CG, Arcturian Nir'ae, she/her). Treat Hob and the stablehands as @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians}.

At any given point in time, Hob Korell (Waerd Keth, he/him) can be found working here alongside his stablehands Kaol (Arcturian Human, he/him) or Jann (Arcturian Nir'ae, she/her). Treat Hob and the stablehands as though they are @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians}.

The Lizard Trade

Characters can purchase @UUID[Actor.T6YcptpxcCLx4yLx]{Jobri} as mounts. Jobri cost 100 gp each and have a carrying capacity of 480 lb.

Waterborne Family Distillery.name: Waterborne Family Distillery
Waterborne Family Distillery.text:
Gamemaster Note

If characters are visiting the distillery as part of An Old Friend, they find it locked, and can attempt to enter in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.niW0x73bUCnjmHqn#investigating-in-the-distillery]{Investigating in the Distillery}.

The smell of earthy liquor fills the air, emanating from the barrels around the room. A sign above a stack of barrels in the corner reads " Do not disturb until fully aged. That includes sips. Yes, we mean you," while another, scrawled on the divider between the front and back rooms, shows the full process for creating karal, which includes water from the sinkhole and several locally-grown plants and grains.

This room holds typical supplies for a distillery — empty and full barrels, distilling pipes, and a cooking fire.

The Hidden Passageway

Any character who looks at the back half of the distillery and succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check can see that the barrels are piled up oddly, leaving a small gap between them as if leaving room for something to get through. With a further successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, characters can spot a curve in the wall that suggests a passageway behind the barrels.

While there is a gap between the barrels, it is a tight fit.

  • A character of small or medium size can attempt to squeeze through with a [[/skill acrobatics 15]] [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] check. Characters of medium size must make the check with @Advantage[-2].

  • Characters can widen the gap between the barrels by succeeding on a [[/skill athletics 15]] [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] check to push the very full barrels apart. If they succeed, the DC of the check to squeeze through lowers to a [[/skillacrobatics 12]] /skillCheck athletics 12. If they succeed by 3 or more Critically Succeed, no check is needed to move between the barrels.

Behind the barrels is a passageway, which leads to @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.o06g8caWK9wvMvSR]{The Storage Room}.

Zodi Trask's Apartment.name: Zodi Trask's Apartment
Zodi Trask's Apartment.text:
Zodi Trask's apartment is warmly appointed, but seems to be a bit of a work in progress, with construction in progress in the living room and items, including a fair number of sparkly rocks and oddly shaped artifacts, in a bit of a haphazard arrangement. The home feels no less welcoming for it.

Zodi has an apartment near the entrance to the mine that he oversees, but has not spent much time in it in recent months, due to his tendency to live his work, his hobby of going deeper into the sinkhole in search of new mining locations and trinkets, and the odd happenings in the Dives around the time of the Level 3 mine shutdown.

If Zodi is home, he welcomes the party in. If not, a search of the contents of the room reveals nothing of real note, though there are a number of small artifacts tucked into the corners of drawers and underneath chairs. If characters succeed on a [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, roll twice on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} table to determine what they find.

The Dining Area.name: The Dining Area
The Dining Area.text:
On the two long tables in this impromptu dining area, food has hardened onto plates, cups are filled with nothing more than residue, and cards are scattered on the table from an abandoned game. Beyond them, tools are scattered across the floor — some old and rusty, some sharp enough that they could be used as a weapon.

The playing cards on the table have a sinkhole design on the back and the four suits have been relabeled as Waterborne, Cevher, Silverbeam, and Lamplighters. The face cards of each suit showcase local luminaries, including Zodi Trask.

If characters wish, they can collect the cards from the table to create a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.YwlHI3BVJapz4a3E]{Playing Cards Set} to make a full set of playing cards, but they must first succeed on a [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check to spot all the cards from where they have been scattered.

Searching Through The Tools

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, or have [[/knowledge trade]], find a @UUID[Item.tAIz3XxOXKogxm4N]{Sturdy Pickaxe}.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, or have [[/knowledge warfare]] spot the gleam of a @UUID[Item.TafPASzoLKKoY8MI]{Sharpened Pickaxe}.

The Lockers.name: The Lockers
The Lockers.text:
Several of the metal lockers in what appears to be some sort of changing and storage area hang open, but a quick glance at the belongings reveals them to be nothing special — mining cloths, gloves, personal goods. While most are either ajar or unlocked, a couple of the lockers have remained firmly closed, their contents a mystery.

This locker area is generally used for storage of daily clothes and outside goods during the mining day.

Opening the Lockers

Characters can break into the closed lockers with a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 14 t00l=thief]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] check requiring @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000]{Lockpicks} or force the closed lockers open with a successful [[/skill athletics 17]] [[/skillCheck athletics 17]] check. If they use a @UUID[Item.tAIz3XxOXKogxm4N]{Sturdy Pickaxe} prying tool such as a crow bar or pickaxe to do this, they have @Advantage[2] on the check.

Characters who open the locked lockers find a bag of coins totaling [[/award 10gp]] [[/award 1gp]] .

Back Office.name: Back Office
Back Office.text:
The back office of this mine has seen better days — beneath the stone of the floor, patches of ground peek through, and dirt from the mine sits in clumps that are spread across the floor. A few sets of tools are scattered between crates and ropes labeled Level 3, but otherwise there is no real sign of life.

This room is attached to the main mining office and usually contains storage or extra tools, but it looks as if it has been damaged or ransacked in some way. Characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check can tell that the damage to the floors comes from being pushed up from below in some way.

Crates in the back of the office can be opened with a successful [[/skill athletics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check. Most have nothing of interest in them, but one holds a few minor items. Roll twice on @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} for the items found.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ljp2XpfiaGudD3wZ] depicts the center of the village of Steed's Point. While Steed's Point was once a slightly larger settlement, the outskirts have fallen to attacks by jurtaks, gore birds, and local wildlife, and it is covered with overgrown hedges, leaving only the center area somewhat recognizable as the collection of homes, barns, and fields that it once was.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ljp2XpfiaGudD3wZ inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Illumination

As most of Steed's Point is open to the sky above, its illumination is dependent on the time of day in the area. For houses that are closed off, lighting is generally dim unless there is a specific light source noted.

Terrain

The terrain varies throughout Steed's Point, but should be treated as normal terrain as a baseline. Areas of difficult terrain are noted throughout.

Elevation

Most of Steed's Point is open to the sky above - where there are areas with roofs, the roofs are 10-feet high.

Additional Gameplay

Two Quests, One Location

Two different quests use this area map - The Book of Tales, which has the characters attempting to retrieve an important sentimental item from the Blacksmith's Cottage in the Northeast corner of the map, and Thorny Predicaments, in which characters are attempting to get to the center of the village to talk with Kali Andrella, the agrimage who is still holed up in Kali's Cottage.

While both quests suggest a direction for characters to follow that makes the most sense for that quest, parties are free to move about the area as they see fit, with or without a quest, and clear all enemies if they wish. In most cases, parties will encounter the same information, enemies, and hazards regardless of what brought them to Steed's Point, but there are occasional differences based on their current quest. These are noted in the area in which they occur: @UUID[.X6okKjJy1vST39Cg]{Steed's Point Fields}, @UUID[.P1W4PJ9uBVdqwZ99]{The Watering Hole}, @UUID[.nxcYkQrl7JRWmD3R]{The Blacksmith's Cottage}, and @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE]{Kali's Cottage}.

If parties stick to the path given to them by one of the two quests, they will proceed as follows:

Book of Tales

Characters get their quest from Rattletrap at @UUID[.X6okKjJy1vST39Cg]{Steed's Point Fields}. The woven construct will only give them a tale if they retrieve a sentimental item from @UUID[.nxcYkQrl7JRWmD3R]{The Blacksmith's Cottage}.

To reach the cottage, characters must:

  • Make their way past @UUID[.KGZwWbro6n9O5EYQ]{the Supply Shed} (where 2 jurtak lurk) and through @UUID[.fLLusi2e39ohsfns]{The Vine Path} (a hidden trap that can leave them exposed to jurtak attacks.

  • Make their way past any remaining jurtak waiting to attack in @UUID[.7DvOSapwjP6cHYa8]{The Southern Clearing}.

  • Make their way to @UUID[.nxcYkQrl7JRWmD3R]{The Blacksmith's Cottage} - along the way they can investigate @UUID[.OFc4Zd295mntYrAS]{The House on the Left} and @UUID[.RhDoNPJHDYXTVj18]{The House on the Right} to find out what happened here and use what they find in those houses to help them cross @UUID[.7uBOsPDyQ7lcES8U]{The Broken Bridge}. Once at the cottage, they retrieve the item, possibly fight off one more jurtak inside and head back.

  • As a bonus, characters can explore the Eastern half of @UUID[.fr6fZdCaywZQjX0K]{The Ruined Home} - there is no way through the middle

Thorny Predicaments

Edivel immediately sees signs of Kali Andrella's signature hedge technique and wants to find her in the center of the village at @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE]{Kali's Cottage}. They believe the best way to go is to the north west.

Getting to the hedge maze takes characters through:

  • A gore bird attack under the ruined roof of @UUID[.t5ac8c8mRcXlGh21]{The Barn}, made more complicated by Kali's hedge traps, which trap you between them.

  • A broken bridge at @UUID[.P1W4PJ9uBVdqwZ99]{The Watering Hole}, which holds evidence of Kali's involvement via another trap and where the construct Rattletrap can share some information about the area.

  • A swarm of gore birds perched on top of @UUID[.ZCxNd4aZ3atHZ3AY]{The Mill} that swarms anything it sees moving

  • The complexities of @UUID[.NiukHJ7qPlIpTXfN]{The Hedge Maze}, which Kali has made as difficult as possible to traverse.

  • If desired, @UUID[.fr6fZdCaywZQjX0K]{The Ruined Home}, though they can only make it through the Western half of the building - there is no way to the other side.

  • A final trap outside of @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE]{Kali's Cottage}, where she can question them about their motives before letting them in.

Kali's Cottage.name: Kali's Cottage
Kali's Cottage.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

The encounter in the cottage depends on how the players reach it:

  • If players are on their first visit and come through the hedge maze, see @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE#hedge-maze-entrance]{Hedge Maze Entrance} below

  • If players come via the Secret Passage in the Northeast corner of Steed's Point, see @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE#secret-passage-entrance]{Secret Passage Entrance} below.

  • If players are returning to the cottage after having previously spoken to Kali, see @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE#return-visit]{Return Visit} below.

@Embed[Actor.FAWXlZTU8syDdRFy]

If characters came to Kali's cottage via the hedge maze, she lets them in via the side door from the maze:

Unlike the rest of Steed's Point, Kali's cottage is in perfect condition, almost as if it isn't in the center of a town under attack. The agrimage stands in the center of the room next to a full containers of blooming flowers that vaguely resemble the blooms on Steed's Point's many brambled hedges. A light rain is falling on the flowers as if out of nowhere, and as you enter, she makes a gesture, dismissing them.

"Welcome to Steed's Point," she says, with a bitter laugh and a shrug of her shoulders. "I suppose I should be glad to have visitors after all this time, especially such determined ones. I only wish you could've seen Steed's Point the way it used to be."

Proceed to @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE#a-conversation-with-kali]{A Conversation with Kali}.

The Secret Passage

If characters discover the @UUID[.P9WnJNPnXltMoYU3]{Overgrown Trapdoor} in the Northeast corner of Steed's Point, they may use the Secret Passage beneath to go directly to the back door of Kali's Cottage:

The door above your head feels less wooden than thatched, almost grassy, as if you are lifting a section of overgrown moss with your hands. As you push up, the darkness of the tunnel that you have been walking through is replaced by a faint light. There is no breeze here, and also no destruction.

Wherever this is, it is inside and somehow protected from the violence and ruin around it. Before you can fully take in the scenery, the moss of the trap door begins to grow and reach out for you, grabbing hands and legs as it attempts to prevent you from going any further. A door to a small home swings open and a woman stands in the doorway, staring you down.

You would come ready to sneak into my house with no warning? Do not let the half-ruined buildings around here fool you. I know how to defend myself. But first, what gives you the audacity to try to sneak up to and into my home?

The party can calm Kali down with a successful [[/check 17 persuasion]] check. If the check fails, they have @Advantage[-2] on further charisma checks with Kali. Proceed to @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE#a-conversation-with-kali]{A Conversation with Kali}.

Conversation with Kali

Kali is willing, if not eager, to speak with the party - if for no other reason than she has not had visitors in some time. While she is often cagey with information, the items that characters have collected while in Steed's Point can help convince her to talk more openly.

Getting Kali to Open Up

As noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.NiukHJ7qPlIpTXfN#the-final-questioning]{The Final Questioning} in the Hedge Maze, Kali's attitude toward characters who entered via the Hedge Maze varies based on their response to her question.

  • Fame-seekers have @Advantage[-2] on charisma checks

  • Money seekers have @Advantage[-2] on insight checks

  • Those who seek to protect and preserve have @Advantage[2] on charisma checks

  • Knowledge seekers have @Advantage[2] on insight checks

Characters who share an item of Steed's Point with her - the @UUID[Item.6iMqi1oF0KxY80kd]{Map of Steed's Point} or @UUID[Item.M7u5PC2kMgthtrQA]{The Clever Fox (Engraved Sign)} - can retry a single failed persuasion check, as she is appreciative and willing to hear them out.

What Kali Knows

Kali has been living in the cottage since the fall of Steed's Point, protecting it against the jurtak. She believes that she is the only one who has stood by Steed's Point, except maybe for Bertron Steed's construct Rattletrap. With a successful [[/check insight 17]] check, characters can sense some guilt around the fall of Steed's Point.

With a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] check, characters can get Kali to share what happened when Steed's Point fell - an earthquake brought the jurtak to the village and it was overrun. All efforts to fight back failed.

  • If they succeed by 2 or more on the check, Kali adds that she is the one who led the charge to defend Steed's Point, even after others believed it should be left behind.

Kali is attached to Steed's Point because she thought of its founder, Bertron Steed, like a father and raised her daughter Moriah there - Moriah then left to become a famed traveling hunter. With a successful [[/check insight 17]] check, characters can tell that there is some hurt or bitterness regarding Kali's relationship with Moriah.

  • With a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] check, characters can get Kali to admit that she and Moriah parted on bad terms.

  • If they succeed by 2 or more on the check, Kali shares that she regrets the bad parting.

  • If they succeed by 4 or more on the check, she adds that she also feels guilty, as she had no way to ask Moriah for help when Steed's Point was attacked.

Kali is the reason for the infestation of gore birds - a last gasp attempt to save Steed's Point that has continued keeping the Jurtak at bay. With a successful [[/check insight 17]] check, characters are aware that Kali is still somewhat afraid of the jurtak because of how viciously they overran Steed's Point when it fell.

A question?

Who Kali Is:

The great Kali Andrella, or at least that's what they once called me. Traveling agrimage, helping towns and cities across the Arctus Plateau thrive. Bit of a knack for getting into trouble - that's why there were so many stories about me. But I always found a way out…until the jurtak came.

Why are you here?

I ask myself that now and then. My being here is what keeps at least this little corner of it safe, and I owe the place that much.

Who else is going to do it? Rattletrap? Maybe, but he doesn't have my skills.

There might be some amount of self-inflicted suffering in the act, too, being alone in the rotting corpse of a town you used to love, and all.

The Fall of Steed's Point?

Not sure if you're from around here, but if you are, you know the earth shakes every so often.

I was even trying to figure out why, just as a side project. Maybe If I'd focused on that, I would have known that we were all just one big shake away from a hole to the pathways opening up, and Jurtak decided to pay us a visit.

With additional persuasion success:

People begged me to run, but I wanted to stay and fight. They believed me when I said we had a shot at driving them back.

We ended up running anyway, well, the survivors did.

Kali's Relationship with Moriah?

My daughter is almost as stubborn as her mother. And not here, so not much more to tell you.

With additional persuasion success:

We were never gonna see eye to eye, not with her wanting to run hither and yon and me wanting her to stay put and learn from my tales of when I was the one out wandering.

We're a little alike in that way - wish I'd had the chance to tell her that, before she left. I don't think she's ever coming back.

With full persuasion success:

I could use her help though… we could save this place.

What do you know about the Gore Birds?

I brought 'em here, at the end, when Bertron was gone and… and I didn't want to lose everything else. I don't like the things particularly, but they work in a pinch.

Been fighting the jurtak ever since.

Hope they didn't give you too much trouble.

Kali is willing to keep talking to the group, but doesn't know much of what is going on outside of her cottage. She does offer a better way out of the cottage than the way they came in, lowering the previously hedges that lead back toward @UUID[.X6okKjJy1vST39Cg]{Steed's Point Fields}. Going forward, the party can use this entrance as a way to reach Kali's Cottage.

Note: If the party contains Edivel, the young agrimage is eager to learn from Kali, and follows up with additional questions in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu#additional-questions-for-kali]{Additional Questions for Kali}. Any benefits that the characters carry from the conversation with Kali above (@Advantage[2]/@Advantage[-2] on a roll, for example) apply to this additional conversation as well.

On Return Visits

If characters have previously visited Kali, they may enter through the front door, which was previously covered in brambles. She also asks them how things have been going and is willing to prepare an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.i89okN7GFTWHsvPy]{Herbalism Kit} for the group, but has no other real information.

Steed's Point Fields.name: Steed's Point Fields
Steed's Point Fields.text:
Gamemaster Note

The construct Rattletrap can most often be found in this area. When Rattletrap encounters the party, there are three different potential scenarios:

  • If the party is visiting Steed's Point on their own, they are generally limited to the conversation topics below.

  • If the party is on the Book of Tales quest, in addition to the conversation below, they may have additional dialogue as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000.JournalEntryPage.hJn9ofVtP4DxSTLe]{The Rickety Man}.

  • If the party is on the Thorny Predicaments quest, in addition to the conversation below, they may have additional dialogue as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu#encountering-rattletrap]{Encountering Rattletrap}.

If parties return to Steed's Point after some time away, they can skip the introduction to the character and proceed to @UUID[.X6okKjJy1vST39Cg#speaking-with-rattletrap-again]{Speaking with Rattletrap Again} below.

Meeting Rattletrap

In the midst of all the destruction of Steed's Point, a gangly figure made of wood and straw walks carefully and steadily through the fields, weeding and digging and keeping things orderly, while carrying a large scythe. After a moment it seems to notice you.

Well that explains it.

The figure says, its voice sounding like wind whipping through a field.

I thought I heard the gore birds screaming about something, they do get a bit aggravated whenever they see anyone new these days.

The construct starts toward you, but pauses a short distance away, seeming to realize something all of a sudden. It speaks:

Before I draw closer, let me introduce myself: Rattletrap, pleased to meet you. And yes, I am talking. Part of the magic of Steed's Point. What's left of it, anyway. It's been so long since I've seen anyone come through here, what brings you this way? Not much left to see in old Steed's Point…

@Embed[Actor.wI4zsTgX2eIy4VtQ]

A Conversation with Rattletrap

Rattletrap is generally happy to talk about his life at Steed's Point, though he doesn't remember that much of it. Characters who succeed on an [[/check 17 insight]] check can tell that he legitimately doesn't recall much.

  • Rattletrap is able to talk, which is rare for a construct, but he doesn't know why.

  • Rattletrap's first clear memories are on the day of Steed's Point's fall to Jurtak, but he has a few snatches of memory from before that.

  • Rattletrap attempts to keep as much of the place up and running as he can, because it feels like home and because he is generally safe from the gore birds (who ignore him) and the jurtak (who he can hide from).

  • Rattletrap stays away from the eastern side of Steed's Point, as there is a large concentration of Jurtak there and he is worried he would be ripped apart if he faced them alone.

Full responses below.

Why can you talk?

Good question!

No idea.

I only know it's weird because a while back a group of hunters came through here and told me so. Apparently my kind normally don't have the ability. Couldn't tell you why I'm different, I just am!

What happened to Steed's Point?

Couldn't tell you, not precisely anyhow. I want to say there was a battle, since my earliest memory is of the town filled with dead, blood everywhere, buildings burned down, all that. I buried the dead a while ago, and do my best to keep the fields in order, but it's just me out here.

Unless you count the birds and lizard people, but I avoid them.

Why are you here?

Rattletrap shrugs, the movement bringing with it the creak of wood and rustling of hay.

Feels like home. There's bits about the place that are familiar. I woke up here, I think this is where I was made.

Any Other Memories of Steed's Point?

My memory isn't too good anymore, at least not the way back part of it. I don't remember anything about this place, though… sometimes, when I stare at the ruins, I feel like I can see what this place once was. I get flashes of canopies and banners fluttering in the wind, or hear the steady ringing of a forge hammer.

The construct's shoulders slump suddenly.

Sometimes… I remember waking up to the death, like it just happened again, or see fresh blood on the ground… or hear people screaming for help.

Probably for the best I can't really remember anything anymore.

Speaking with Rattletrap Again

As you make your return to Steed's Point, Rattletrap is once again in the fields, this time harvesting bunches of grain that look not that different from the straw of his own body. He waves a hand in your direction as you walk by, but does not approach, instead simply shouting:

Welcome back! Just let me know if you need anything!

The party may have additional conversation with Rattletrap about any conversations not covered in their initial meeting above, or as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu#encountering-rattletrap]{Encountering Rattletrap} (while playing the "Thorny Predicaments" quest) or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000.JournalEntryPage.hJn9ofVtP4DxSTLe]{The Wooden Sentinel} (while playing the "Book of Tales" quest).

The Old Barn.name: The Old Barn
The Old Barn.text:
Past a trampled set of hedges sits the remains of an old barn. A large portion of its roof is gone, as if the tiles and wood had been relentlessly torn off of it piece by piece, leaving sections of splintered wood that are scattered on one side of the ground.

Crossing into the barn triggers the Briar Hedge Trap detailed below. If characters trigger the trap, read or paraphrase the following:

As you step inside, the flattened vines in the entrance behind you begin to rustle, lifting from the ground in a tangle of leaf and vine, becoming thick and impassable. Ahead, what was once an exit is similarly blocked by a hedge that has grown as if from nowhere, thick and thorny and as high as your head.

Gamemaster Note

The trampled vines are interactable map features! Trigger them when the trap is sprung.

Briar Hedge Trap

The trampled vines are a Briar Hedge trap set in place by Kali Andrella.

Detecting the Trap

Characters can detect the trap with a @UUID[Actor.fuL7YqC7eENDtHeJ.Item.Momq8AedoWUozyDh]{Find Traps} spell. Any other checks to examine the trampled vines cannot distinguish between them and a normal set of vines.

Trap Trigger

The trap activates at both exits from the barn as soon as characters cross into the barn from either direction.

Trap Effects

An impassible hedge of briars covers all movable space in its path. The hedge prevents forward movement, but does no damage unless it is touched or attacked. If touched, its thorns rapidly extend. Any character within 5 feet of the hedge must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 17]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d10 piercing]] damage.

Examining the Trap

Once the trap is activated, it can be identified as a Briar Hedge Trap by Edivel (if with the party), any character with [[/knowledge plants]], and/or any character who succeeds on a [[/check arcana 17]] check. Characters who have identified the trap know that it can be deactivated by locating and pushing on a branch within the hedge that appears out of place and that it is vulnerable to fire damage. They have @Advantage[2] on all other checks involving the trap.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check nature 17]] or [[/check investigation 17]] check to examine the hedge can see that the hedge has a specific pattern of branches that seem different than those around them and aren't typical for this type of hedge. If they succeed by 2 or more, they can identify the specific branch that breaks the pattern.

Deactivating/Destroying the Trap

The briar hedge trap can be deactivated by carefully pushing against the branch that deactivates the trap with a successful [[/check 18 sleightofhand]] check. On a failure, the character triggers the hedge's physical attack (see Trap Effects above) and has @Advantage[-2] on the saving throw to counter it.

While the hedge repels physical attacks, it can be destroyed with fire. Any spell of second level or higher that deals fire damage (such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.7u2obDvuvtZBkTfq]{Scorching Ray}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ztgcdrWPshKRpFd0]{Fireball}, or similar) will destroy a single hedge. The magical hedge can also be countered with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} against the trap's DC of 15.

Disarming the hedge trap is only temporary - after 10 minutes, the hedge reactivates (if the party is still within the barn) or resets (ready to retrigger if crossed over again). If a hedge is magically destroyed, it slowly grows back over the course of 24 hours.

As soon as the party is trapped inside by the hedges, a pair of gore birds attacks.

@Embed[Actor.ZuWduzUSGS6i4NZm inline count=2]

Gore Birds

Gore Bird often attack in waves, using their @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G.Item.UafhSUneNOqxQ1gj]{Dying Call} to alert other gore birds nearby to join the fight if they are close to death.

Searching the Barn

With a successful [[/check investigation 16]] to search the barn after the Gore Birds are dispatched, parties find a bag of copper and silver coins worth [[/award 2gp]] buried beneath a haystack.

Old Damaged Bridge.name: Old Damaged Bridge
Old Damaged Bridge.text:
A Drowned Vines trap hides below a wooden bridge.

A battered wooden bridge spans the rocky, half-dry basin below. The planks and beams are old and weathered, and despite the rather extensive damage in places, it still looks sturdy enough to cross without much concern.

Over the sides, the craggy walls of stone descend to a rocky bed where a few pools of stagnant water collect.

Drowned Vines

Lurking beneath the broken bridge are Drowned Vines, set in place by Kali Andrella, which function as a trap for any creature that sets foot on the bridge.

The vines can grab up to three creatures at once when triggered. Creatures targeted by the vines must make a [[/save dexterity 18]] saving throw. On failure, the character is dragged off the bridge and to the gulley below, and suffer [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] as the vines constrict them.

A character can escape the vines with an action and a successful [[/save dexterity 18]] or [[/save strength 16]] saving throw. Characters with access to a slashing weapon have @Advantage[2] on their save.

After triggering, the vines become dormant for 10 minutes before they can attack again.

Detecting the Vines

A character with a [[/check passive perception 19 long]] or making a successful [[/check perception 17]] check spots the vines in the water beneath the bridge starting to move as the party gets near the bridge. This movement is unnatural.

The Mill.name: The Mill
The Mill.text:
At first glance, the clumped dark mass on top of the stone mill could almost be a massive accumulation of hardened dirt, but the hint of red beaks and tails paints a clearer picture – a massive mound of gore birds is perched on top of the bulding, their bodies so tightly packed together that it is hard to distinguish one from the next. It’s impossible to count how many swarms might be among them, but they all seem focused on a single task – pecking and clawing at the tile roof beneath them. If they note your presence, they do not show it.

The gore bird swarms can be directly engaged in combat or avoided via stealth.

Gore Bird Swarm Combat

If the gore birds are directly engaged by the party in combat, 2 of the 7 swarms attack. The rest come in waves. Each new wave of gore birds should be added whenever a swarm currently engaged in combat is defeated or after 3 rounds of combat, whichever happens first.

Once engaged in combat, characters can get respite by entering @UUID[.fr6fZdCaywZQjX0K]{The Ruined Home} or @UUID[.NiukHJ7qPlIpTXfN]{The Hedge Maze} - the gore birds avoid these areas because of Kali's hedges and will fall back, waiting to see if the party emerges. They can also avoid the attack by entering the Mill itself, though this brings them into conflict with the Jurtak inside (see @UUID[.ZCxNd4aZ3atHZ3AY#cornered-jurtak-combat]{Cornered Jurtak Combat} below).

@Embed[Actor.ZuWduzUSGS6i4NZm inline count=7]

Evading the Gore Birds

Characters can sneak past the gore birds by succeeding on a [[/check stealth 16]] check. If characters fail their stealth check, a single gore bird will fly toward them to investigate. Characters can placate the bird with a successful [[/check 16 animalhandling]] check, kill the bird in a single hit (if it the bird is injured, it immediately cries out, triggering the swarm attacks), or silence the bird (using @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSilence000]{Silence} or a technique at the GM's discretion). If they are unsuccessful, the bird calls out an alarm and 2 swarms attack the party.

If parties enter the Mill, they encounter a single jurtak warrior, which cowers in the corner.

@Embed[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]

For a moment, the creature doesn't move. Huddled in the back corner of the mill, its eyes dart from you to the frenzied scratching and tapping from gore bird beaks and claws on the roof above. Hissing at the air, it raises a claw towards you and bares its razor-sharp teeth.

Cornered Jurtak Combat

The jurtak hunter has been cornered in the mill by the gore birds and is angry and hungry - it attacks viciously on sight. The jurtak will attempt to push members of the party outside of the mill in the hopes that the gore birds will spot them and attack, creating commotion and confusion that it can use to escape.

Hedge Maze.name: Hedge Maze
Hedge Maze.text:
The hedges in this section of Steed's Point narrow into wall-like structures, on each side of a winding path ahead of you. As you step between them, they seem to somehow get taller, looming on each side of the slippery grass of the overgrown path beneath your feet. It does not seem as if anyone has stepped foot here in some time.

There are three chokepoints within the hedge maze, each with its own dangers:

  • The first bend (@UUID[.NiukHJ7qPlIpTXfN#the-dreaded-corner]{The Dreaded Corner})creates a sense of dread meant to prevent anyone in the maze form coming any closer.

  • The second bend (@UUID[.NiukHJ7qPlIpTXfN#the-flower-trap]{The Flower Trap}) restricts movement with large thorns and contains flowers that emit a poison gas.

  • The final section leading up to the door (@UUID[.NiukHJ7qPlIpTXfN#the-final-questioning]{The Final Questioning}) is an impassable trap that allows Kali to question anyone who has made it that far.

Slippery Grass

The slippery grass within the hedge maze is difficult terrain. In addition, characters have a chance to slip each time they move forward. Whenever characters take a movement action, roll a d4 [[/roll d4]]. On a 1, the character slips on the grass and falls into the hedges on each side. They must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 18]] saving throw or they are scratched by the hedges, taking [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] and [[/damage 1d6 slashing]] damage.

The Dreaded Corner

Somehow the hedges seem to get even taller as you round the corner. They move as if they have a mind of their own, sprouting thorns and reaching out to do something cruel and unspeakable.

Fearful Growth

The hedges at this corner are designed to create fear. Each creature who passes the corner must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 17]] saving throw or drop whatever they are holding, become frightened, and immediately begin walking back the way they came. They can be convinced to move past the corner despite being afraid with a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] or [[/check intimidation 16]] check, or with a spell like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3MYDjS6k9IYL0aTj]{Calm Emotions}.

Repeated exposure to the hedges lessens their effect; each time the same character passes the corner, the DC of the wisdom save lessens by 1.

The Flower Trap

Thorned vines extend in front of you, creating a makeshift wall - the gaps are large enough that smaller creatures might be able to get through, but not without scraping against the thorns. As you begin looking for a way forward, flowers along the hedges bloom and begin spraying a pungent pollen directly on you.

Impenetrable Foliage

While the flower wall may appear to be impenetrable, characters can figure out a way through with a successful [[/check survival 17]] or [[/check perception 17]] check. If those checks are failed or they do not attempt them, they are subject to the pollen from the flowers nearby. They must succeed on a [[/save constitution 17]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d8 poison]] damage.

The Final Questioning

As you step into a small clearing, vines come down around you, as if you have been imprisoned in a cage of leaf and thorn. As you survey the flowers and grass of your prison, a whispered voice comes to your ears as if from on the breeze.

Well I will give you this, you are persistent. What I don't understand is why? What has brought you to the remains of what was once Steed's Point? Why do you visit the once great agrimage Kali Andrella?

A Simple Question

Kali will give the characters a single opportunity to share what brought them to Steed's Point. If they try to ask her any questions, she refuses to answer until they do. With a successful [[/check insight 17]] check, characters know that Kali is most interested in protecting Steed's Point and will respond well to arguments about saving or preserving something important to the world.

Kali responds as follows to the following broad reasons for the party's arrival:

  • Fame & Glory: Kali is not impressed by the group’s desire for fame as an end unto itself. They have @Advantage[-2] on all charisma checks for the entirety of their next conversation with Kali.

  • Money: Kali is dismissive of the group, believing that they do not know what is truly important, and becomes closed off. Characters have @Advantage[-2] on all insight checks for the entirety of their conversation with her.

  • Knowledge/Curiosity: Kali is bitter, believing that all her knowledge was ultimately not good enough to permanently save Steed's Point. With this revelation, characters understand Kali better and have @Advantage[2] on all insight checks for the entirety of their next conversation with her.

  • Protection/Preservation: Kali is inclined towards the party's point of view. They have @Advantage[2] on all charisma checks with Kali for the entirety of their next conversation with her.

Regardless of how the party answers, Kali lets the party into her cottage after responding back.

The party seeks Fame

Hoping that people will use your name after you are dead and buried?

Why?

Does hearing the name Steed’s Point bring Bertron Steed back to life?

Did being the great Kali Andrella help me save him? Or did it just attract vultures like you looking to pick from his corpse and my brain?

Come, tell me what you plan to pluck from the remains of the town I loved.

The party seeks Riches

Collecting riches.

Of course.

If nothing else, they will last when our names are lost and our deeds forgotten, though that is cold comfort. But as I am sure you can tell, I am surrounded by riches so please, come in.

Tell me how I can make your coinpurses that much heavier to carry.

The party seeks Knowledge

Ah yes. I remember when all I wanted to do was collect knowledge like bits of shiny rock. Just as useful really, in the end.

Did knowledge save the people of Steed’s Point? All my knowledge certainly did not. Though maybe it is the knowledge they held that I am truly trying to save.

A thought worthy of a conversation, I think.

The party seeks to Protect

You've heard of Steed's Point, then?

From before all this started?

I am surprised, but maybe because it feels like it's been so long keeping jurtak at bay that I've forgotten there's anyone else out there keeping our memory alive.

I appreciate the reminder that there's more to life than what is in these four walls – the least I can do is let you inside of them.

Ruined Home.name: Ruined Home
Ruined Home.text:
Like many of the houses of Steed's Point, the roof of this home has been ripped away, leaving destroyed beams of wood on the floor, but many of the open gaps in the roof have been covered by tendrils of vine, as if the winding vines and their green and purple leaves were trying either to protect or consume what remains inside.

As you enter, the vines shift, but do not react, as if waiting to see what you will do in the ruins.

The wall immediately facing the characters when they enter is covered in vines - if cut or burned, they immediately grow back even thicker - there is no way past it to the other side

The Placard

With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check or [[/check perception 19 long]], characters spot an @UUID[Item.M7u5PC2kMgthtrQA]{engraved metal sign} nestled in a pile of vines.

Among the ripped and destroyed bits of wood, a metal placard sits in a nest of vines, seemingly untouched by any of the destruction around it.

With a successful [[/check arcana 15]] check, characters know that this placard was created using a form of metallurgical enchantment that might be practiced by an Arcturian agrimage or artificer, and has been enchanted to remain unaffected by physical damage. The sign has no other magical qualities or abilities.

Characters who possess the @UUID[Item.6iMqi1oF0KxY80kd]{Woven Map of Steed's Point} see that the fox symbol on the map matches the symbol on the placard. If characters have met Moriah Foxhaven, they know that this placard was hers and the letters are her initials. If they have not, they can determine that the letters are initials with a successful [[/check investigation 16]] check - if Edivel is with them, the young agrimage will then remember that Kali Andrella's daughter had the last name "Foxsomething."

The Memento Box

With a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check to search the house, characters notice a floorboard the Southwest corner of the room is oddly ajar. The floorboard can be lifted using a tool like a crowbar with no check required - if pried up by hand, the character must succeed on a [[/check athletics 18]] check to raise it.

Beneath the floorboard is a small wooden box. It has a carved symbol of a fox and the initials MF on it, which matches both the metal placard found in the room and the symbol on the @UUID[Item.6iMqi1oF0KxY80kd]{woven map of Steed's Point}.

The wooden box looks as if it has been carved by many different hands using different tools - the styles are similar, but there are subtle differences in the depth of a cut or the turn of a line that give the sense that this has been passed down and added to over time.

The wooden box is locked shut, but can be opened with a successful [[/check sleightofhand 17]] check using Thieves' Tools. Inside is a jeweled necklace containing a @UUID[Item.Srp2AsMNBDxu61V3]{Shard of Sending} and a note, written in [[/language common]] titled @UUID[Item.vLYGD46oaA7xcXXC]{ A Fond Farewell}.

Vine Path.name: Vine Path
Vine Path.text:
While the path here is overgrown with vines and brambles, it nevertheless seems a reasonable way to traverse the southern expanse of the village, as a clearing awaits on the far end.

The overgrown alleyway here is fitted with a magical Entangling Vine Trap that can ensnare characters and creatures who traverse it without care.

Examining the Path

The area here is Difficult Terrain.

A [[/check perception 15 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill perception 14]] check allows a character to notice the long-dead skeletal remains of a bipedal saurian creature, half-buried deep within the bramble.

In addition, a successful [[/check inv 15]] check allows a character to surmise that the saurian creature's cause of death involved getting caught up in the brambles themselves. This is the party's primary clue to notice the Entangling Vine Trap that hides here amidst the brier-laden snarl (see below).

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check nat 16]] check is able to identify the skeletal remains as those of an adult @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.tLSBe3kfPlvqmnH2]{Jurtak} — a species of predatory aberrations that usually inhabit subterranean biomes, which puts these remains somewhat out of place. This check is made with @Advantage[-2] if the character doesn't inspect the remains closely enough.

  • The character also finds remnants of the dead Jurtak's belongings, including a crude bone-tipped @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.DWLMnODrnHn8IbAG]{Javelin} and a weathered suit of @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.NlXaa4Kk5JOxgiSM]{Jutak Medium Armor}.

Retrieving these items or getting close enough to the skeletal remains to inspect them risks triggering the Entangling Vine Trap.

Entangling Vine Trap

The alley south of the Dilapidated Shed is dominated by a magical Entangling Vine Trap that was planted here by the agrimage Kali Andrella.

Any character who moves through the area must make a [[/save dex 16]] saving throw or trigger the trap. A creature doesn't need to step on the ground to trigger the trap; the brambles and vines can detect intruders up to a height of 5 feet.

Any creature in the area when the trap is triggered must succeed on a [[/save strength 15]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d4 piercing]] damage and have the Restrained condition until the trap resets. A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check athletics 15]] check. On a success, it frees itself from the entangling vines and is no longer Restrained by them.

The trap resets each morning at dawn. The @UUID[Actor.ZuWduzUSGS6i4NZm]{Gore Birds} infesting neighboring areas make short work of any living creature who gets caught here for very long.

Jurtak Attack!

After the trap is triggered, the @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]{Jurtak Warrior} and @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd]{Jurtak Hunter} in the @UUID[.7DvOSapwjP6cHYa8]{Southern Clearing} will sneak up to attack the party, utilizing the same strategies found in "Jurtak Tactics".

Additionally, if the 2 Jurtak Warriors in the @UUID[.KGZwWbro6n9O5EYQ]{Dilapidated Shed} have avoided detection, they will attempt to sneak in behind the characters to flank them.

Southern Clearing.name: Southern Clearing
Southern Clearing.text:
This rough clearing is marked by the presence of two weathered chicken coops and a dead-end path of loosely-cobbled stone, but is otherwise unremarkable.

A @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]{Jurtak Warrior} and a @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd]{Jurtak Hunter} lay in wait here, ready to ambush any interlopers who might pass through this way.

Lurking Danger

Any character with a [[/check prc 16 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check prc 14]] check while examining the shed's interior is able to spot a Jurtak Warrior and a Jurtak Hunter hiding on opposite sides of the clearing.

@Embed[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]

@Embed[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd]

Jurtak Tactics

If possible, the Jurtak Warrior and Jurtak Hunter that hide here wait for the party to get caught in the Vine Path trap before springing their attack. If the party bypasses the agrimage trap, the Jurtak will continue to hide until the party has moved further into the clearing before attacking from behind.

The Jurtak Warrior will utilize its @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.WewF6d4OX0PjEE2j]{Acid Spit} ability before closing in on the party to fight in melee with its @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.TIJUbDlyqjxfKyrH]{Wicked Pike}.

Meanwhile, the Jurtak Hunter will take aim with its @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.PR4gST1hHcztH2wO]{Grotesque Longbow}, targeting characters who are caught in the Vine Path trap or who are engaged in melee combat with one or more Jurtak Warriors.

Both will use their @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.bB7URAM1YmHHD3oP]{Jurtak Poison} as soon as possible, and reapply the poison during combat when most convenient, especially if their numbers are bolstered by nearby reinforcements.

Nearby Reinforcements

If they've avoided detection, the 2 Jurtak Warriors that hide nearby in the @UUID[.KGZwWbro6n9O5EYQ]{Dilapidated Shed} will close in to flank the party from behind when the Jurtak Warrior and Jurtak Hunter here in the Southern Clearing initiate combat.

Exploring the Clearing

If the characters take time to search the chicken coops along the eastern edge of the clearing, they'll discover a forgotten @UUID[Item.Qc1MDLAykgWfbNQc]{Silver Flask} of @UUID[Item.4mIj4qrLgMompEZG]{Arcturian Liquor} tucked away in the chicken coop to the north.

Abandoned Home.name: Abandoned Home
Abandoned Home.text:
Leaves cover the floor of this unassuming house, which seems relatively unaffected by the ravages of time and weather compared to most of the village. While most of the structure remains unharmed, the dust-covered furniture is splintered and overturned, and a quick glance suggests the occupants that once lived here were normal Arcturian folks with normal Arcturian sensibilities.

The characters can search this abandoned home for signs of what happened to this remote, overgrown village.

Exploring the Home

Characters who search the house are able to locate a few details that suggest what life was once like here, including:

  • A table, still set with empty dishes and cutlery for a family of three.

  • Shelves along the northern wall stocked with kitchenware and cutlery.

  • A splintered bookshelf, toppled and windswept.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check per 12]] check while searching the house is able to find a Moth-Eaten Diary among the scattered detritus that once decorated the splintered bookshelf.

  • Penned by an amateur artist named Ruxandra Markos, the diary details what life was like in Steed's Point before its unfortunate demise. Sketches of some of the village's buildings accompany journal entries about the people that once lived here, alongside Ruxandra's account of her day to day life.

Cobwebbed Workshop.name: Cobwebbed Workshop
Cobwebbed Workshop.text:
