The battered door of this cobwebbed workshop has been torn from its hinges and lays flat on the dusty ground. A scattered assortment of tools and equipment is strewn about the one-room shop in complete disarray, and most of the furniture — like Steed's Point itself — is demolished and destroyed.

The characters can search this cobwebbed workshop for evidence of what happened to Steed's Point during its mysterious downfall.

Exploring the Workshop

Signs of distress adorn this dusty, cobwebbed workshop, which appears to be littered with splintered debris and evidence of a violent Jurtak incursion.

A few pieces of equipment remain scattered about the room, including:

  • A cracked and rusted @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj.Item.oftqGnLgZaKTt5ku]{Hooded Lantern}.

  • A chipped @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepHandaxe000]{Handaxe}.

  • A rusty @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.i4NeNZ30ycwPDHMx]{Sickle}.

A character with a [[/check perception 14 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check allows a character to notice two distinct sets of blood stains on the wooden floor, including the crimson blood of humanoids and another dark ichor.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check sur 13]] check is able to notice or locate the remnants of several clawed footprints from a curious bipedal creature, along with claw and spear marks on the door and interior.

  • Result of 16+: The claws are recognizable as those of a saurian, and the dark ichor that stains the floor (seen now, if it wasn't noticed before) most likely comes from some aberration or subterranean monstrosity.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check inv 14]] check can deduce the rough series of events that occurred here:

  • The people that lived and worked here took a stand against some other kind of clawed, bipedal creature — which forced its way in through the front door. There may have been more than one of these creatures.

  • Combat ensued between the two parties, and blood was spilled on both sides. Based on the disarray and the proportions of blood, the humanoids of Steed's Point did not fare well during the assault.

Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] easily recognize this building as the workshop of some artisan, and have @Advantage[2] on any checks made to assess the area.

The Ersatz Bridge.name: The Ersatz Bridge
The Ersatz Bridge.text:
The splintered wall of some Steed's Point dwelling spans the small ravine here as a rickety ersatz bridge. Although the timbers are weathered and worn, it looks safe enough to cross the expanse without concern of hazard or hindrance.

The characters can cross the splintered bridge with little effort, although a surprise attack from Jurtak raiders awaits them on the other side.

The small ravine beneath the bridge is roughly 15 feet deep, and is lined with the splintered, dust-covered debris of a demolished house.

Examining the Bridge

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check inv 13]] check or a [[/check nat 13]] check is able to identify evidence that suggests this hastily-erected bridge was placed here following an earthquake or other natural disaster, a testament to the tenacity of the village's citizens.

Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Jurtak Attack!

Once most or all of the party members have crossed the bridge to the northern landing, a group of enemies scurries out of the ravine from their unseen hiding places, including: a @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]{Jurtak Warrior}, a @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd]{Jurtak Hunter}, and a @UUID[Actor.m86FIWDHh47htZNy]{Jurtak Geomancer}.

Without the benefit of spells or other special abilities, these Jurtak cannot be detected by the party until they emerge from their hiding places.

@Embed[Actor.m86FIWDHh47htZNy]

Jurtak Tactics

The Jurtak Warrior and Jurtak Hunter will attempt to focus their attacks against the party member with the least amount of hit points.

The Jurtak Geomancer will target another spellcaster, if possible, using its own Innate Spellcasting.

Steed's Smithy.name: Steed's Smithy
Steed's Smithy.text:
The crumbling stonework of this squat, square smithy seems to have suffered the most brutal tests of time. Light streams through its rickety, perforated roof from above, cascading across a scattered array of weather-worn blacksmith's tools and other forgotten supplies. The forge at the center of the dilapidated chamber has likely been cold since the fall of Steed's Point so long ago.

This ruined edifice is what remains of Bertron Steed's once-proud forge, where he crafted a countless array of ingenious creations — including the sentient construct known as @UUID[Actor.wI4zsTgX2eIy4VtQ]{Rattletrap}, the Rickety Man.

Here, the characters can discover vague details about Bertron Steed himself from the various tools and accoutrements he left behind during the village's untimely demise.

Exploring the Smithy

If the characters take the time to explore the interior of the ruined smithy, they may find a few items of note:

  • An array of tools and trinkets scattered about the area, including a rusty set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.KndVe2insuctjIaj]{Smith's Tools} and a disorganized set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.xKErqkLo4ASYr5EP]{Woodcarver's Tools}.

  • A hammer stand located in the northeast corner of the smithy. 12 ordinary @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0.Item.dgOm4QAOpwSQ3Zjl]{Hammers} of various shapes and sizes are still stored here, moss-covered and forgotten. These hammers are all marked with the initials "B.S.", which are etched into the bottom of the handle on each.

  • Alongside these mundane tools, an item of particular interest rests on the hammer stand: the lightly-enchanted @UUID[Item.kmShhWv8eU9cHwfx]{Shardsteel Hammer}, which is integral to the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book of Tales} and is also marked with Bertron Steed's initials.

The forge itself is perhaps the most striking feature here, despite its aging dormancy. A large, hammer-worn anvil nearby shows aged signs of ample use. And the meager coals within the forge have weathered away to little more than blackened soot.

Analyzing the Scene

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check inv 13]] check or a [[/check prc 13]] check can accurately deduce that this place was hastily abandoned long ago (as evident by the weathering on the edifice and tools within, as much as from the lingering signs of damage from attacking Gore Birds).

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check arc 13]] check is able to recognize several esoteric accoutrements of an agrimage spellcaster among the otherwise standard array of tools, including the vaguest traces of spell components and the like.

  • Result of 15+: The Shardsteel Hammer is more than meets the eye, and bears obscure runic markings that indicate a connection to agrimagic, suggesting that it can be used as a spellcasting focus for agrimage casters.

Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] and [[/knowledge machines]] can tell that the blacksmith that once worked here practiced classic smithing and artisanal woodcarving in tandem, based on the way the tools are so completely intermingled and organized (among those that are organized, that is).

Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] and [[/knowledge rituals]] can recognize the Shardsteel Hammer as a potential spellcasting focus without identifying any of its other properties.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check ins 15]] check or a [[/check nat 15]] while pondering the location is inspired to wonder what it was like for the excessive amount of local flora when Steed's Point was besieged. Characters with [[/knowledge plants]] or any number of druid spell levels have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Speak with Plants

Some of the brambles and shrubs that grow nearby are old enough to have been here when Steed's Point met its untimely fate.

Any character who uses the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithP]{Speak With Plants} spell to communicate with this elder vegetation is able to learn a few firsthand details about what transpired here long ago.

From the plant's perspective, the rise of Steed's Point is likely more of a mystery than its demise, which the plant will be able to recall with precise detail (from its limited point of view).

What Happened Here?

You sense the ground rippling, shaking, and shuddering, the feeling of roots uncomfortably straining as the earth around them moves. You feel the pain of broken branches and snapped limbs as heavy things fall upon them.

You taste the tang of iron becoming rich in the earth, feeding your roots. You feel the cycles come and go where nothing of note happens.

About the Blacksmith?

You sense heat, taste the strong minerals in the water that spills over your earth and filters to your roots. You feel the vibrations of footsteps as beasts move around you. You feel the cycles pass where the waters and footsteps are missing.

Other things here?

You sense the withering of strange energies that was over your branches as something dark passes by in the dark hours. You feel your branches bend and shift as little things climb within, leaving rich droppings on your soil.

You feel the ebb and flow of magic in the land, an old and familiar magic, a magic that was common many cycles ago, and was missing, but came back.

About Rattletrap?

You feel strange kinship, but also revulsion at what was once like you, living plant, not dead, and wrought into something else. The construct uses the dead limbs of your fellows, but is something else!

Dilapidated Shed.name: Dilapidated Shed
Dilapidated Shed.text:
Like most of Steed's Point, this ramshackle shed near the southern edge of town has seen better days. Only the rear third of its roof seems to remain somewhat intact, and you spy a rusty array of farm equipment scattered about the front end, which hangs wide open in the stark absence of a wall or door.

The party can inspect the shed's interior, where weather-worn farm tools might distract them from noticing the two Jurtak Warriors who lurk in a filth pit at the far end.

Exploring the Shed

The missing roof of the Dilapidated Shed reveals a few pieces of aged farming equipment, including:

  • A sun-bleached wooden Cart.

  • 2 rusty Pitchforks (treat as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.OG4nBBydvmfWYXIk]{Spears}).

  • A 50 ft. length of @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F.Item.Hxda94WZnDT9APJA]{Hempen Rope}.

The Filth Pit

This pit of filth located at the eastern end of the shed plunges 5 feet into the earth, and provides Total Cover for any creatures who attempt to hide there.

Any character with a [[/check prc 14 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check prc 12]] check while examining the shallow pit is able to find the dessicated remains of an unfortunate Steed's Point citizen among the filth. Roll twice on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot (Arctus Plateau)} table and once on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} table.

Lurking Danger

Any character with a [[/check prc 16 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/check prc 14]] check while examining the shed's interior is able to spot the 2 Jurtak Warriors hiding down in the Filth Pit at the rear.

@Embed[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud inline count=2]

Jurtak Tactics

If possible, the 2 Jurtak Warriors that hide here wait for the party to pass through the Vine Path south of the shed before springing their attack. If discovered by the party, these two Jurtak will immediately engage the characters in combat.

The Jurtak Warriors will utilize their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.WewF6d4OX0PjEE2j]{Acid Spit} ability before closing in on the party to fight in melee with their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.TIJUbDlyqjxfKyrH]{Wicked Pikes}.

If the Jurtak Warriors are far away from the characters when combat begins, they will most likely use their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.Fx4xHMplkj1kO9DD]{Aggressive} bonus action to close the distance.

Both will use their @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.bB7URAM1YmHHD3oP]{Jurtak Poison} as soon as possible, and reapply the poison during combat when most convenient.

Nearby Reinforcements

The Jurtak Warrior and Jurtak Hunter located in the @UUID[.7DvOSapwjP6cHYa8]{Southern Clearing} do not rush to join combat if it breaks out here. Instead, they wait for the party to potentially spring the trap concealed along the @UUID[.fLLusi2e39ohsfns]{Vine Path}.

If they can avoid getting spotted by the characters, the 2 Jurtak Warriors that hide here at the Dilapidated Shed also wait for the party to spring the trap or engage their Jurtak allies before closing in to flank the characters in combat.

An Empty Shell of a House.name: An Empty Shell of a House
An Empty Shell of a House.text:
An old damp bed and empty fire pit are all that remain under what was once a home, its roof now ripped and torn away. Deep scratches are embedded in its walls and dried liquids of an unknown substance are scattered across the ground, some smeared by what appears to be footprints.

Characters can search what remains of the house or investigate the scratches and dried liquid on the ground.

Examining the Remains

Characters who succeed on a [[/check survival 17]] check know that the dried liquids on the ground are a mix of blood and saliva. Most of what is here is years old and has mostly faded away, but the smeared blood in the footprints is more recent.

  • With a success of 3 or more, or by succeeding on a secondary [[/check nature 15]] check, characters can identify the footprints as belonging to a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.tLSBe3kfPlvqmnH2]{Jurtak} of some type.

Searching the House

Characters that succeed on a [[/check investigation 16]] check to thoroughly search the home find an@UUID[Item.6iMqi1oF0KxY80kd]{intricately woven piece of cloth}, a @UUID[Item.MsaSOAqoBBqlpo7F]{wooden brooch} under a now-moldy pillow, and a feather on top of the ashes in the fire pit.

The image on the cloth resembles the buildings of Steed's Point against the horizon, and several of the buildings have small symbols on them. Any character who succeeds on a [[/check investigation 15]] check knows that this cloth is a vague map of Steed's Point, with the horseshoe and pitchfork indicating a blacksmith's workshop and barn, respectively. If Edivel is with the party, they recognize the K as Kali Andrella's symbol.

With a successful [[/check nature 16]] check, characters know that the feather belongs to a @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Bird}. With a successful [[/check survival 16]] check, characters know that the feather is more recent than the cold ash of the pit and likely fell from above.

Overgrown Trapdoor.name: Overgrown Trapdoor
Overgrown Trapdoor.text:
You spot a sun-bleached and weather-worn trap door beneath the overgrown tangle of wild brambles here, large enough to grant ingress to a cellar or basement.

The wooden trapdoor here reveals a Secret Passage that connects this remote, northwestern corner of Steed's Point to a Secret Passage Entrance south of Kali's Cottage.

Examining the Trapdoor

The wooden trapdoor here is made from sturdy, weather-work oak bound with rusted iron hardware. It is locked but not trapped.

Any character who has already visited the @UUID[.nxcYkQrl7JRWmD3R]{Steed's Smithy} who also succeeds on either a [[/check inv 12]] check or a [[/check prc 14]] check while examining the trapdoor can accurately speculate that the hardware was crafted in the Smithy's forge.

Opening the Trapdoor

The trapdoor can be unlocked by any character who uses Thieves' Tools and succeeds on a [[/check dex 14]] check.

Alternately, the trapdoor can be opened with brute force. A successful [[/check str 18]] check is required to pry the iron hardware from the weather-worn wood.

Opening the trapdoor reveals a rickety wooden ladder that stretches down into the darkness below. Remarkably, it lacks the musty odors that linger about the rest of Steed's Point, offering a scent of cool, dry earthiness instead.

The Passage to Kali's Cottage

Any character that chooses to navigate the length of the Secret Passage can use their entire turn to move from one end to the other. At the beginning of their next turn, the character emerges at either the Secret Passage Entrance south of @UUID[.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE]{Kali's Cottage} or the Overgrown Trapdoor here.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh] depicts the entirety of the sanctuary with the exception of some minor outlying buildings.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The tranquil mountainside complex known as Corpin Sanctuary serves as one of the primary locations of the Crumbling Sanctuary main quest, in which the party accompanies the druid Sin Marmot on her fated mission to join the Cindaric Sages.

Corpin Sanctuary is a remote headquarters for @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}'s unorthodox enclave of Cindarics, who prefer to practice their mystical arts away from the hustle and bustle of Ordain.

Once the characters reach Corpin Sanctuary with Sin, they must:

  • Learn about the rise of doubt and mistrust among some of the Sindaric Sages here.

  • Investigate a rumor that one of the Cindaric Sages at Corpin Sanctuary is actually a necromancer in disguise.

  • Discover a secret elevator to the Pathways below the floor of the Sanctorum chamber and explore the tombs beneath.

  • Help defend the Sanctuary from an undead onslaught, led by the necromancer known as @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso}.

The Abyssal Plot

After they explore the tombs beneath Corpin Sanctuary and return to the surface, the characters will participate in an epic battle against a shambling cadre of undead monsters.

Illumination

Illumination here is largely dependent on the time of day, since the location's exterior is fully open to the sky above and several of the Sanctuary's buildings feature moon roofs with open or glassed ceilings.

Inside the Sanctuary, lighting conditions are dependent on the specific illumination used from chamber to chamber. Most interior chambers feature the warm luminosity of lantern or candle light, which sheds bright light in a 15 foot radius and dim light in a 30 foot radius.

Terrain

Unless otherwise indicated, the landscape throughout Corpin Sanctuary counts as normal terrain. Several of the exterior mountainside areas are treated as difficult terrain because of the sheer rocky surfaces of their craggy heights.

Doors within the Sanctuary are crafted from sturdy oak, and can be bashed in or destroyed with a successful [[/check str 18]] [[/skillCheck athletics 18]] check. Most of the facility's doors are unlocked, however, resulting in a rather rare need for forced entry. Locked doors will be noted where applicable.

Elevation

Corpin Sanctuary is situated several hundred feet above sea level, and the ravines that immediately surround the complex run nearly 60 feet deep in certain areas.

Characters who fall from one of the elevated ledges surrounding the Sanctuary suffer [[/roll 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage for every 10 feet they happen to fall.

Entry Courtyard.name: Entry Courtyard
Entry Courtyard.text:
The sweet smell of blush blossom leaves fill the calm air of this tranquil courtyard, where one of these pink-petaled trees grows from the moist earth of a central pit. The courtyard is lined in benches, where a crimson-robed sage sits in casual attendance. The open roof overhead invites you to gaze at the sky in all its splendor.

The Entry Courtyard offers residents and visitors of Corpin Sanctuary a semi-outdoor haven where they might idle the time in a meaningful or relaxing way. During daylight and evening hours alike, it serves as a commons of sorts for the Sanctuary, and is guaranteed to offer guests a welcoming scene upon arrival.

@Embed[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]

Courtyard Conversation

The Entry Courtyard is a favorable spot for local Cindaric Sages and visitors alike, and serves as a welcoming place for those who seek inspired study, tranquil relaxation, or friendly discussion.

At any given moment, someone is present in the Entry Courtyard, including at least one @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Sage} who serves as a steward of the area. These stewards maintain a watchful eye over the Courtyard, but generally keep to themselves unless approached — providing an air of trust and gentle security. The stewards work in 4 hour shifts, and each of the Corpin Sanctuary Sages who lives here (including major and minor NPCs) is committed to at least one shift a week.

If the characters attempt to start a conversation with one of the Cindaric Sages here, topics of discussion include the following:

  • The history of Corpin Sanctuary and the Cindaric Sages who dwell here.

  • Current rumors of the Golden Flats and the Arctus Plateau at large.

  • A genuine interest in the party's journey to the Sanctuary, and what they plan to do next.

Exploring the Courtyard

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] is aware of how relatively irregular it is that a blush blossom tree blooms in the mountainous climate and dry rocky terrain here, and attributes the tree's lush growth to some leyline of Ember's heartblood or the tenacity of the Cindaric Sages themselves.

Refectory.name: Refectory
Refectory.text:
The smell of fresh-baked bread and hearty spices greets you as you enter this large refectory, where four long tables sit decorated with a scattered array of half-empty plates and a buffet of various foods — from fresh fruits to salted meats and plenty in between.

This large chamber serves as the Sanctuary's communal refectory, which hosts daily meals, recreational gatherings, and other events.

Rather than scheduled eating times, meals that are prepared daily in the adjoining @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.zJl2ZxpXGLzOVr3b]{Kitchen} are set out for consumption throughout the day at the leisure of the Sages who live and work here; several times a week, however, the Cindarics of Corpin Sanctuary gather here for a communal lunch or dinner.

Examining the Refectory

Characters who search the Refectory and wish to plunder its supply of food can find up to 5 days of preserved or dry @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.f4w4GxBi0nYXmhX4]{Rations} Rations each.

Wandering Sages

If a character idles here long enough, they'll likely encounter at least one @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Sage} (or another NPC) who visits the refectory for a snack.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
The embers of the hearthfire in this kitchen burn low, but the inviting scents of sweet and savory foods are as fresh as the loaf of bread that cools on the countertop.

This wide chamber hosts the Sanctuary's kitchen facilities, and is laid out in a rather professional manner despite the rustic, amateur approach to cuisine adopted by the Sages here. However, the lack of culinary ceremony does very little to undermine the deliciousness of the food that is regularly prepared here.

Examining the Kitchen

Any character who takes a moment to search the kitchen is able to find:

  • Multiple @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.V13fjV5oSmvbRdgP]{Mess Kits}

  • Several sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.Gflnp29aEv5Lc1ZM]{Cook's Utensils}.

  • 2 days worth of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.f4w4GxBi0nYXmhX4]{Rations} Rations per character.

Mira's Office.name: Mira's Office
Mira's Office.text:
The symmetry of this sparsely-decorated chamber and the presence of a desk cluttered with parchment suggests this room is an office of relative import. A bookcase on the eastern wall, lined with various encyclopedic texts and collections of Kelmezian lore, is flanked by two display cases whose esoteric contents linger timelessly beneath glass lids.

This small chamber serves as an office for the Sanctuary's leader, @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}, and is most often used for private meetings and consultations of a sensitive nature (when it is used at all). Mira is more likely to be found in other parts of the facility, and generally reserves this chamber for the execution of her administrative duties.

Exploring Mira's Office

The books that line the shelf on the eastern wall include various encyclopedic texts and collections of Kelmezian lore, including historical accounts of the Cindaric Sages and the founding of the great city of Ordain.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check locates a rare @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.l794iywHk8Wc6Uvi]{Book of Lore} book among the tomes titled "The Ghosts of Yarinu." Any character who takes the time to read this book during a short or long rest a Recovery or Rest gains @Advantage[2] on their next Intelligence (History) Society check.

  • [[/culture emberKelmezian]] characters and those with [[/knowledge souls]] or [[/knowledge undeath]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 14]] check or a [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skill society 14]] check while exploring the office is able to identify the antique art pieces located in the unlocked display cases here.

  • The fossil in the northernmost display case is the ossified shell of a Kelmezian Ammonoid — a "shard-finding" gastropod that was considered to be sacred by the early Cindarics, due to its overt connections to the Heartblood of Ember.

  • The parchment scroll in the southernmost display case bears a copy of the "Chant of Adonia" — a key religious text of the Cindaric Sages, the Chant is known to explain the divine vision that led Adonia to establish the great city of Ordain alongside the refugees that already called the place home.

Desktop Evidence

Any character who spends at least 5 minutes searching the desk is able to spot several documents and letters of correspondence, including the following:

  • A @UUID[Item.MB5aIlZdYZgJdZwM]{Letter from Sigil}, a document that erroneously makes it look as if Mira is turning away refugees.

  • The @UUID[Item.kc2AKDWVnHLTY3Z8]{Letter of Introduction}, a document that describes how Evesso came to join the ranks of Corpin Sanctuary under unusual circumstances.

  • A copy of @UUID[Item.HLuTRoOpNSmD3PTW]{Aberin Lowd's Medical Records}, the medical records of Aberin Lowd. Possessing this item relates directly to the event [[/eventState fallAgainThreads]], in which the body of Aberin is discovered.

Hidden Lockbox

If the party takes a moment to search the office, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] is able to locate a hidden lockbox in a secret compartment beneath Mira's desk. The lockbox contains the Sanctuary's reserves of petty cash, including [[/award 22pp 88gp]] [[/award 2pp 28gp 80sp]] .

Library.name: Library
Library.text:
The earthy smells of parchment and paper assail your senses as you enter this cozy library, which is furnished with multiple shelves stocked with a variety of books and tomes.

This chamber serves as Corpin Sanctuary's public library, although visits from outsiders are rather infrequent. The three shelves on the eastern wall contain an array of books about Arcturian history, while the free-standing shelves to the northwest are lined with a variety of religious texts. Meanwhile, the smaller shelf in the southwest corner of the room contains a more diverse selection of texts, including several works of modern fiction.

Exploring the Library

Characters who take a moment to inspect the tomes spread out on the chamber's reading table notice:

  • The smaller book is the Library Journal, which contains a log of texts that have been checked-out or reserved from the library. The Library Journal is a red herring, and contains no clues related to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.4rR7KxEbu3RXbzuQ]{Corpin Investigation} event.

  • The larger book is titled "The Druid's Almanac", and is opened to a page in a chapter that provides detailed advice for the cultivation of many of the plants currently found on the Sanctuary grounds. Any character who studies this book during a short or long rest Recovery or Rest gains @Advantage[2] on their next Intelligence (Nature) skill Wilderness check.

Any character who is familiar with @UUID[Item.5sDslKMjZXB18yNm]{Evesso's Note} who also makes a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check while searching the room is able to locate a curious tome on the shelf titled @UUID[Item.wlTZjyyW8K69yf56]{Nineteen Nights in Haxim}, which contains the passphrase needed to open the Secret Door to the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.jPYv3Z4n7vOswB7z]{Profane Altar}.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] and [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this skill check.

  • Any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} spell while searching the room is also drawn to "Nineteen Nights of Haxim," which radiates a faint aura of Abjuration magic.

Winding Stairs.name: Winding Stairs
Winding Stairs.text:
This wooden stairway zig-zags its way between the western refectory and the Sanctuary's northern dormitories. The narrow gap between the two buildings catches and channels the mountain wind into a steady and powerful gust that both dries your eyes and sweeps the stairs clean.

The gradual climb of the winding stairs here twists its way between the dorms and the refectory, two of the Sanctuary's most frequented areas. Sages are known to linger here after meals for a quick conversation or a casual pipe smoking.

The stair steps themselves count as difficult terrain — which several of the Sages consider to be a minor inconvenience when their stomachs seek a late night snack.

Cliffside Path.name: Cliffside Path
Cliffside Path.text:
The large alcove formed by the Sanctuary shields you from the mountain wind as you navigate this narrow cliffside path, which is well worn from the sandaled footsteps of the countless Sages who've lived and worked here throughout the centuries.

The cliffside path here is relatively unremarkable, but offers residents and visitors of Corpin Sanctuary a place to enjoy the rustic features of the mountain without going too far afield of the Sanctuary grounds.

A Dangerous Precipice

The Cliffside Path is situated at the same "ground level" as the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.WHdKr6CkT5xF7lqr]{Entry Courtyard}, and 60 feet above the floor of the ravine below.

Characters who happen to occupy the Cliffside Path during combat situations will find themselves in a more dangerous situation than the Sanctuary's other areas, due to the precipitous elevation and narrowness of the Path's walkways.

  • Any character without a flying speed who is pushed or shoved off the Cliffside Path must succeed on a [[/skill acrobatics 14]] or [[/skill athletics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check to avoid falling off the ledge.

  • Characters who fall from the Cliffside Path ledge suffer [[/roll 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage for every 10 feet they fall.

Sanctorum Entrance.name: Sanctorum Entrance
Sanctorum Entrance.text:
You behold an exalted set of double doors decorated with a bright mosaic that depicts a wizened femme sage clad in the robes of a Cindaric. A great city of white stone stands proud behind this figure, who holds her arms out in dutiful supplication to a throng of needy and hopeful Arcturians in her attendance.

An array of what appear to be holy offerings are scattered on the stone footsteps here — including rare flowers, copper coins, and curios crafted from natural materials.

The doors here at the grand entrance to the Sanctuary's largest chamber depict the first Holy Speaker, Adonia — the founder of Ordain and the Cindaric Sages themselves.

Meant to inspire and embolden those who look upon them, these doors usually stand closed and attended by a Cindaric steward stationed on the other side (in the Sanctorum proper); and the inspiration this place provides is evident in the countless windswept offerings that have been gathered at the footsteps below Adonia's feet.

Examining the Entrance

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check recognizes the figure in the mosaic as Adonia, the first Holy Speaker and founder of the Cindaric order.

  • The character is also convinced that leaving an offering here on the footsteps is a worthy endeavor, based on tales of Cindaric blessings afforded to those who pay proper respects.

  • [[/path emberCindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Characters who take a moment to leave an offering of their own on the footsteps of the Sanctorum Entrance gain @Advantage[2] on their next saving throw roll against any spell or effect that would cause the &Reference[Frightened] @Condition[frightened] condition.

Security Measures

In times of trouble, the Cindaric Sage that happens to be on duty as steward within the Sanctorum will barricade the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.Jj4lbzMBB7OBFM05]{Sanctuary Entrance} with a crossbeam of sturdy oak reinforced with steel. A combined Strength score of 20 and a series of 2 successful [[/check strength 24]] checks are required to break the barricaded door Breaking the door requires a series of 2 successful [[/skillCheck athletics 24]] checks . Once the Entrance has been barricaded, the Sage will alert the other denizens of the Sanctuary using a special @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.aa9KuBy4dst7WIW9]{Horn} hung on a beam nearby.

Sanctorum.name: Sanctorum
Sanctorum.text:
The domed ceiling of this large circular chamber is crowned with a roof made of glass, which allows sun- and moonlight to shine down into the sanctorum with a perpetual and natural elegance. The chamber itself is a remarkable monument to the natural world: four tiers of moss-covered earthen steps are stacked in ascending concentric circles around a shallow pool in a basin at the room's center. A loose arrangement of benches and pillows on these steps confirms the purpose of this place as a gathering and meditation chamber. Meanwhile, a wooden platform overlooks the southwestern edge of the basin like a tiny pier, adorned with a wide altar that appears to be decorated with druidic accoutrements and half-burned candles.

This large circular chamber serves as Corpin Sanctuary's main place of worship, and is generally reserved for Cindaric communion, sacred rites, and other special occasions.

Sanctuary Conversation

At any given moment, someone is present in the Sanctorum, including at least one @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Sage} who serves as a steward of the area. These stewards maintain a watchful eye over the Chamber, and will readily approach any visitors to the area with warm greetings The stewards work in 4 hour shifts, and each of the Corpin Sanctuary Sages who lives here (including major and minor NPCs) is committed to at least one shift a week.

If the characters attempt to start a conversation with one of the Cindaric Sages here, topics of discussion include the following:

  • The history of Corpin Sanctuary and the Cindaric Sages who dwell here.

  • Current rumors of the Golden Flats and the Arctus Plateau at large.

  • A genuine interest in the party's journey to the Sanctuary, and what they plan to do next.

Searching the Sanctorum

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13 check while searching the Sanctorum is able to locate 6 Cindaric @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.odV5cq2HSLSCH69k]{Prayer Books} prayer books strewn about the seats here.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success: The character is also able to spot a curious circular seam at the bottom of the pool at the center of the room, and may suspect it conceals a door or passage, but a proper understanding of what lurks beneath eludes them.

A successful [[/skill religion 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check while searching the area confirms that this chamber is where the Cindaric Sages usually conduct their tradition's ceremonies and rituals. The chosen leader of any given ceremony would take their place on the wooden platform in front of the altar, where they would conduct the sacred rites.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

A successful [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check allows a character to recognize some of the species of flora in the chamber to be of significant cultural or historical import to the Arctus Plateau.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success: The character recognizes some of these plants as beneficial and ethically sustainable. They can take 15 minutes to harvest enough flora to replenish [[/roll 1d4+2]] uses of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.6rocoBx5jdzG1QQH]{Healer's Kit} Healer's Kit.

  • [[/culture emberArcturian]] characters or characters with [[/knowledge plants]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Secret Elevator

A secret stone trapdoor is expertly concealed beneath the pool at the center of the chamber, which hides a clandestine elevator that connects the Sanctorum with the Pathways far below.

Security Measures

In times of trouble, the Cindaric Sage that happens to be on duty as steward here will barricade the Sanctorum Entrance with a crossbeam of sturdy oak reinforced with steel and alert the other denizens of the sanctuary. See @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.Jj4lbzMBB7OBFM05]{Sanctorum Entrance} for further details.

Balcony Overlook.name: Balcony Overlook
Balcony Overlook.text:
This stone balcony presents an impressive view of the mountainside and the terrain below, where the Golden Flats stretch out as far as the eye can see — including the edge of the Arctus Chasm to the east, and the banks of the River Elenain to the west. The decision to construct the sanctuary here was truly an inspired one, if the noble breeze that rustles your garments and stirs your imagination has anything to say about it.

In times of peace, the Balcony Overlook here is an interesting piece of architecture that embraces the majesty of the Sanctuary's mountainside setting; in times of trouble, however, it becomes a dangerous location where gravity can be a liability.

A Dangerous Precipice

The Balcony Overlook is situated 15 feet above the "ground level" of the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.9aygktOAMoTJoeBf]{Cliffside Path}, and 85 feet above the floor of the ravine below.

Characters who happen to occupy the Balcony Overlook during combat situations will find themselves in a more dangerous situation than the Sanctuary's other areas, due to the precipitous elevation and narrowness of the Overlook's walkways.

  • Any character without a flying speed who is pushed or shoved off the Balcony Overlook must make a successful [[/skill acrobatics 14]] or [[/skill athletics 14]] [[/skill athletics 14]] check to avoid falling off the ledge.

  • Characters who fall from the Balcony Overlook ledge suffer [[/roll 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage[[/hazard 3 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{falling damage} for every 10 feet they fall.

Meditation Pavilion.name: Meditation Pavilion
Meditation Pavilion.text:
The balcony overlook leads you to an isolated pavilion that stands high above the gulleys below. At the center of this open-roofed area, a smaller blush blossom tree sways gently in the mountain breeze. The comfortable wooden benches here and the perpetual air of majesty suggest this place would be a perfect spot for meditation or lunar communion.

This indoor-outdoor annex serves as a Meditation Pavilion for the Sages of Corpin Sanctuary, and offers a more secluded area from which to enjoy the majestic splendor of the Sanctuary's mountainside environs.

Exploring the Pavilion

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] is aware of how relatively irregular it is that a blush blossom tree blooms in the mountainous climate and dry rocky terrain here, and attributes the tree's lush growth to some leyline of Ember's heartblood or the tenacity of the Cindaric Sages themselves.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] discover a curious trinket that has grown into the twisting trunk of the tree, as if it was placed there long ago, clutched by the knotted bark like a warm embrace.

  • A closer look at the embedded trinket reveals it to be a tiny statuette of an otherworldly bird, crafted from some meteoric alloy.

  • If any of the Cindaric Sages here are asked about the trinket in the tree, they reveal its origin story: the trinket was crafted from a meteorite of Aura, and one of the founders of Corpin Sanctuary — a Zeph scholar named Zhulian Rha — planted it with the tree long ago in the hopes that it would bless the Sanctuary with the cosmic inspiration of the Wind Moon.

Dormitories.name: Dormitories
Dormitories.text:
A short series of stone steps leads northward to intersect with a narrow perpendicular corridor. Seven doors on the north wall and a trio of doors to the south suggest this collection of rooms serves as the lodging for the Cindaric Sages who live here.

The ten chambers assembled in this northern wing of the Sanctuary comprise the facility's dormitories, where the Cindaric Sages and overnight guests can find comfortable but modest lodging.

Each of the dormitory chambers, excluding the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.xp3AuG8ZJbRwm1us]{Washroom}, features a small wooden balcony; the Sages and their guests are known to utilize these for meditation and study beneath the satellites of Ember's ever-swirling cosmos.

Wandering Sages

If a character idles here long enough, they'll likely encounter at least one @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Sage} (or another NPC) on their way to or from the Washroom nearby.

Mira's Chamber.name: Mira's Chamber
Mira's Chamber.text:
The size of this dormitory chamber and the presence of a stately document-strewn desk betray it as the private bedroom of Corpin Sanctuary's most esteemed sage. Several household items decorate the room's shelves, scuffed by perpetual use, alongside years of charitable gifts in the form of simple Arcturian keepsakes.

This room serves as the private chamber of @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}, the Sanctuary's leader. Although the bed is no larger than those found in other dormitory rooms, the rest of the furniture here is somewhat larger, and indicative of the occupant's relative importance among the residents of Corpin Sanctuary.

Mira stores her vestments and day-to-day equipment in the large footlocker west of the bed, and the wardrobe on the northern wall is lined with a variety of femme garments that cater to each of Ember's seasons.

Exploring Mira's Chamber

The relatively cluttered and dust-free nature of this chamber suggests that Mira spends more time here than in her @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.OnKJslXqG9NYJCI6]{Office} (a fact that can be easily confirmed by the head Sage herself).

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check is able to locate one random @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinket} of interest.

Desktop Evidence

Any character who spends at least 5 minutes searching the desk is able to spot several documents and letters of correspondence, including the following:

  • A @UUID[Item.NOQ9M9ktPU35XtHU]{Letter from Lilla Arien}. (The 2nd set of evidence found will clarify that Mira is reluctantly following instruction provided to her by a superior in Ordain).

The first character to succeed on either a [[/skill perception 15]] or [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] or [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check while searching the desk are also able to locate a @UUID[Item.3VgiukLxEImUNOL6]{Spell Scroll of Locate Object} buried beneath the layers of parchment.

Washroom.name: Washroom
Washroom.text:
This trapezoidal chamber is fitted with wash basins, a wooden tub, and two latrines divided by folding partitions. A mirror in the corner and an array of towels and other textiles all but confirm that this is the Sanctuary's communal washroom.

This washroom provides the Sages and visitors of Corpin Sanctuary with a semi-private place for excretory movements and matters of personal hygiene. While there is no running water, a well nearby and the druidic magic of the Cindarics are the reliable methods used to supply the washroom with fresh water daily (or when otherwise necessary).

If a character idles here long enough, they'll likely encounter at least one @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Sage} (or another NPC) on their way to or from the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.XNmFfrViLKfVJiM8]{Dormitories} nearby.

Keeping it Clean

Custodial duties for the washroom are assigned to each of the Cindaric Sages on a weekly basis, with each sage being responsible for cleaning duties roughly one day a week. Waste is disposed of via a refuse pit concealed beneath one of the floor's central tiles, and is often recycled by the Cindaric Sages for use as compost in the Sanctuary's garden beds.

Evesso's Chamber.name: Evesso's Chamber
Evesso's Chamber.text:
This small square chamber is sparsely decorated with the simple accoutrements of a private bedroom, including a rustic wooden wardrobe on the eastern wall and shelves lined with tools of the Cindaric trade to the west.

This room serves as the private chamber of @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso}, the necromancer masquerading as a Cindaric Sage. Like the dormitory's other chambers, this room is equipped with a comfortable bed stuffed with down feathers, a footlocker full of personal effects, a rustic wooden wardrobe, and shelves stocked with druidic miscellany.

Evesso's Chamber is rather stark and draconian compared to the other rooms here, and hides a few details that hint at the necromancer's secret identity.

Exploring Evesso's Chamber

Any character who searches the room finds @UUID[Item.5sDslKMjZXB18yNm]{Evesso's Note} pinned beneath a stone bowl on the bedside shelf.

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] or [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check uncovers the presence of some other interesting items and features of the chamber, including:

  • The seams of a secret door on the western wall, which leads to the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.jPYv3Z4n7vOswB7z]{Profane Altar}. Further inspection reveals the residual presence of an arcane glyph on the secret door that resembles a fractured circle of six interlocked rings, which is also found inscribed on Evesso's Note.

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.eZGmdOhaTWMicXPW]{Component Pouch} on the shelves. A pouch containing various ritual magic components.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 18]] [[/skillCheck arcana 18]]check is able to associate some of the material components in the Component Pouch with various arcane spells that (curiously or coincidentally) belong to the schools of Divination and Necromancy magical rites and spells that would (curiously or coincidentally) be associated with necromancy or divination.

Secret Door

Characters with a [[/skill perception 15 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] are able to locate the seams of the secret door if they didn't actively search the room. There is no apparent keyhole or button on or near the door, and a successful [[/skill inv 15]] check assuages any doubts about this .

The secret door can only be opened by reciting the passphrase "malediction" in Common (the 5th word on the 16th line of the 53rd page).

  • This phrase can be found on the Page 53 in @UUID[Item.wlTZjyyW8K69yf56]{Nineteen Nights in Haxim}, the page that corresponds to the 2nd number written on Evesso's Note.

  • "Nineteen Nights in Haxim" is currently located in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.eDlvJHr6FhKhY8ji]{Library}.

Any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} spell while inspecting the chamber perceives a faint aura of Abjuration magic surrounding the entirety of the secret door, and the glyph inscribed upon it scintillates with brilliant arcane lambency.

Any character that uses the @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr] talent is able to discern traces of Abjuration magic surrounding the secret door, and identify the glyphs inscribed upon it as an arcane lock designed to await a spoken passphrase.

Avwynn's Chamber.name: Avwynn's Chamber
Avwynn's Chamber.text:
This small square chamber is sparsely decorated with the simple accoutrements of a private bedroom, including a rustic wooden wardrobe on the western wall and shelves lined with tools of the Cindaric trade to the east.

This room serves as the private chamber of @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}, the Sanguinary masquerading as a Cindaric Sage. Like the dormitory's other chambers, this room is equipped with a comfortable bed stuffed with down feathers, a footlocker full of personal effects, a rustic wooden wardrobe, and shelves stocked with druidic miscellany.

Yet, there are subtle signs of Avwynn's more rough-and-tumble attitudes about life and her history as a Sanguinary, if the characters know what to look for.

Exploring Avwynn's Chamber

Characters who take a closer look at the contents of the room find Avwynn's chamber to be relatively unkempt compared to other areas of the Dormitory.

A successful [[/skill prc 14]] or [[/skill inv 14]] [[/skill perception 14]] or [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awarness 14]] check uncovers the presence of some interesting items within the chamber, including:

  • A@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.il2GNi8C0DvGLL9P]{Poisoner's Kit} kit containing a number of alchemical ingredients typically used in the creation of poisons tucked behind an array of bottled herbs and dried specimens.

  • A @UUID[Item.AgmNUa9um9RGlEoP]{Black Aspen Wand} in the footlocker, a druidic spellcasting focus talisman crafted from the twisted branch of a black aspen tree.

  • @UUID[Item.Y3Z5Xq6TtwPVE8IP]{Avwynn's Journal}, concealed beneath the bed's down-stuffed mattress.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill nature 16]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 16]] check knows the Black Aspen tree to be a native plant of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.TNPxd8ZlYQvJEXu6]{Bloodwoods} located north of Ordain.

Any character that makes a successful [[/skill religion 16]] [[/skillCheck society 16]] check is able to identify the wand as a spellcasting focus utlized talisman commonly carried by fringe druidic groups like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries}. The party can speculate as to why a Cindaric Sage would collect such a taboo instrument, but the wand offers no direct evidence that would expose Avwynn's true affiliation with the Sanguinaries.

Empty Dormitory.name: Empty Dormitory
Empty Dormitory.text:
A layer of dust has settled on the surfaces of this simple square chamber, which appears to be some sort of guest room for visitors to Corpin Sanctuary. While a scattering of basic accoutrements can be found here, like a wooden wardrobe on the western wall and dusty shelves to the east, they appear relatively unused.

The empty dormitories of Corpin Sanctuary remain vacant and are generally reserved for visitors to the remote Cindaric facility. Albeit dusty, a comfortable bed stuffed with down feathers adjoins an empty footlocker here, and the wardrobe is bare — save for a single sage's robe and two sets of towels. Whatever miscellany lines the shelves here is mostly decorative.

Sage's Dormitory.name: Sage's Dormitory
Sage's Dormitory.text:
This small square chamber is sparsely decorated with the simple accoutrements of a private bedroom, including a rustic wooden wardrobe on the eastern wall and shelves lined with tools of the Cindaric trade to the west.

This modest chamber serves as a dormitory for one of the unnamed Cindaric Sages that lives and works here in the Sanctuary. A comfortable bed stuffed with down feathers adjoins a footlocker full of personal effects, and the wardrobe on the eastern wall is lined with vestments and clothes for various seasons. Shelves on the western wall are stocked with druidic miscellany and a variety of practical tools and equipment.

Searching the Dormitory

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]]check while searching the Sage's Dormitory locates an item of interest amongst the clutter on the shelves or stashed in the wardrobe. The following rollable table can be used to determine what they find. The party can continue to search until they have exhausted the contents of the table.

@Embed[RollTable.QJfpKhhkQAk0l5pm rollable]

Profane Altar.name: Profane Altar
Profane Altar.text:
The stone wall of the dormitory slides down into the floor, revealing a darkened alcove steeped in the iron smell of semi-fresh blood. At the far end of this secret chamber, an enigmatic altar crafted from black stone looms in the shadows.

Unbeknownst to nearly everyone at Corpin Sanctuary, this hidden chamber contains a Profane Altar that unambiguously identifies @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso} as the necromancer at the heart of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.4rR7KxEbu3RXbzuQ]{Corpin Investigation} plot.

The Profane Altar itself is a 3-foot high hexagonal lectern, asymmetrically carved from a solid slab of black jade and embellished with the likeness of screaming undead spirits on each side. Blood stains this unholy relic, which is obviously an instrument of evil.

Properties of the Profane Altar

Clerics, Sorcerers, Warlocks, and Wizards can attune to the Profane Altar, which grants the @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx.Item.kuKhl8K4JSGWsJAi]{Profane Blessing} feature if the attuned spellcaster spends a short rest performing the necessary unholy rites:

  • Allied undead creatures within 30 feet gain @Advantage[2] on all saving throws.

  • The caster gains a +2 bonus to their spell save DC for Necromancy spells.

  • The caster gains the ability to speak Abyssal.

Those with at least one Rune talent can take the time during a Recovery to attune to the Profane Altar, which grants the @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx.ActiveEffect.nuil54pScyOnc0Sj] feature.

Due to the weight of the altar, it is effectively immobile. Attempts to forcefully remove the altar are met with frustration and calamity.

These bonuses remain active until the attuned character finishes a long rest Rest. The necromancer @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso} is attuned to the Profane Altar unless otherwise stated.

Examining the Altar

Any character with [[/knowledge undeath]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] while inspecting the profane altar is able to confirm its nature as an arcane focus (albeit an immobile one) magical nature, and accurately identifies its potential to enhance necromancy spells.

  • Result of 19+ Critical Success or [[/knowledge rituals]]: You suspect that the blood here is the necromancer's own, and that a ceremonial dagger associated with the rites performed here (which is, in fact, Evesso's @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx.Item.NE0JzBn89TiREQQ0]{Black Jade Dagger}) must be located elsewhere.

Destroying the Profane Altar

Characters can destroy the Profane Altar by inflicting 10 hit points of magical damage to it. If the altar is destroyed, all creatures within 10 feet must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 13]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 2d4 psychic]] damage.

Consecrating the Profane Altar

Characters can consecrate the Profane Altar by casting either the @UUID[Actor.fuL7YqC7eENDtHeJ.Item.BE6ec6v5AVnSxz2R]{Bless} spell or the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.xmDBqZhRVrtLP8h2]{Protection from Evil and Good} spell using the altar as the target (the remains count as a willing creature for the purposes of this effect). Alternately, a cleric can use their @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.classfeatures.Item.r91UIgwFdHwkXdia]{Channel Divinity} ability to Turn Undead within 30 feet of the altar to consecrate it.

The Altar is imbued with a persistent enchantment from @Spell[spell.death.aura.extend].

Destroying the Profane Altar

The Profane Altar can be destroyed by using dealing 20 magical damage to it. When the altar is destroyed, all creatures within 10 feet suffer the effects of [[/hazard 8 willpower morale psychic]]{Profane Backlash}.

Dispelling the Profane Altar

A character with the capability to [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.counterspell0000]] can neutralize the Profane Altar by succeeding on a [[/skillCheck arcana 17]] check.

  • The nature of the enchantment can be recognized with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]].

  • Attempts to dispel using the Life rune gain +2 Boons.

  • Attempts to dispel using the Aura gesture gain +2 Boons.

  • Attempts to dispel using the Death rune suffer +2 Banes.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CS82h91RP59553vr]{The Bleak Archive} depicts the entirety of the location when it is discovered during the @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.mERlrM63Ioo7UrlO]{Where Evil Lurks} event of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death}.

  • The Bleak Archive features two points of entry: the front doors that lead to the @UUID[.8eyTxNv1M3lnR3eH]{Antechamber} from the @UUID[.5spyNIZFOSvpHkmn]{Mist-Veiled Approach}, and the nearby @UUID[.bnA4fGGRaYOsSOjJ]{Hidden Breach} that leads to the @UUID[.Nsvsx26sWAxGNY7x]{Webbed Mausoleum}.

  • Additional information about the Archive's arcane locks and the rotating mirrors that control them are located in the Gameplay Details section of this walkthrough.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CS82h91RP59553vr inline]

Western Corridor.name: Western Corridor
Western Corridor.text:
A slight current of air flows southward down the brief length of the short corridor here, and you spot a small aperture in the stone of the western wall, situated twenty feet in to the north.

An unassuming hallway wraps around towards the southern Ossuary where the party may advance the light beam puzzle and locate a secret door that provides access to the Reflector Array and its network of mirrors.

Spinning Blade Trap

The pressure plate which activates this trap is located at the south end of a short hallway, refer to the West Blade Trap Trigger Scene Region.

A character with a[[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] and is close enough to clearly see the pressure plate can notice it and the wall seams from which the spinning blades would emerge.

  • The plate can be disarmed with successful use of [[/check dexterity 15 tool=thief]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] using a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.disarmingToolkit].

The Spinning Blade Trap is triggered when 10 or more pounds of weight are applied to the pressure plate. When the trap is triggered, several whirling blades erupt from the nearby wall and sweep through the hallway.

  • Any character who is within the area of the trap immediately or at the start of a subsequent turn must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw or take [[/damage 2d6 slashing]] damage or half damage on a successful save faces [[/hazard 6 fortitude health slashing]].

A secret door into the @UUID[.gRLQzRFEKVu15Lzp]{Reflector Array} is located to the west of the Spinning Blade Trap can only be opened and closed using the inconspicuous lever to the southeast.

Reflector Array Door

Characters with a[[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] can detect the seams of the secret door itself.

  • Any character who succeeds on a[[/check intelligence 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] check can determine the mechanical nature of the secret door and confirm the presence of a remote lever.

Additionally, characters with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] can detect the lever while exploring the Western Corridor.

Progressing the Beam

In order to correctly advance the beam of light, it must be first routed south-west through a small gap in the wall into the Ossuary, then channeled around to this hallway where it passes through another gap into the Reflector Array.

Main Gallery.name: Main Gallery
Main Gallery.text:
This sizable gallery is cluttered with an esoteric array of odd antiquities — from clockwork globes and arcane baubles to iron-bound tomes and eldritch trinkets. A thin gray blanket of cobwebs and dust covers the room and all it contains. The air is musty and laden with the acrid scent of ozone.

One feature in particular here commands your attention: the stone statue of a large humanoid on a dais at the northern end of the chamber, which stands behind a wide altar paired with a strange orb at the front and a radiant crystal lens on each side. The orb, hewn from some pale azure crystal, features the indentation or etching of a large five-fingered hand on its surface.

In this area, the characters will discover a dusty vault that serves as a false terminus for would-be plunderers of the Bleak Archive. This gallery contains a variety of esoteric antiquities meant to dissuade invaders pillagers from finding the Archive's real treasures deeper within.

Antiquities of a Bygone Age

The gallery here is decorated with a dusty array of Shent antiques and assorted oddities from the Age of Sunlight, alongside some minor Abyssal relics. As the party interacts with the reclics stored in this ersatz vault, they'll be visited by an apparition of the Shent Sage known as @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth}, whom they may have encountered in the Forest of Stone during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.yzgUD9WX351fihbU]{Lunar Awakenings} event of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over the Moon}.

Searching the Room

Assorted crates, jugs, barrels, and boxes are stored throughout this large chamber, all covered in a blanket of cobweb and dust. Most of these vessels are curiously empty, or their ancient (and often rotted) contents are altogether unremarkable.

  • Nine stone plinths etched with runic Pathward markings stand out from the rest, each of them bearing a Shent relic of particular interest upon it. Any character who attempts to examine the various @UUID[Item.3kcd1E5aXjMi1NhB]{Bleak Archive Relics} stored on these plinths can spend an action to inspect one of the relics. These relics may include (listed clockwise from the Antechamber door): Alloyed Circlet, Alloyed Necklace, Scale-Bound Tome, Alloyed Jug, Alloyed Manacles, Alloyed Clockwork, Crystal-Faced Tome, Crystal-Lensed Spyglass, Crystal-Lensed Microscope.

  • A tenth plinth in the northeast corner of the chamber stands empty. A dusty blanket is draped off of one side, suggesting that whatever once sat here was removed long ago.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check while inspecting the items is able to confidently suspect that each of the nine Bleak Archive Relics has been tainted by its presence in the Bleak Archive or by the Abyss itself, and is cursed with a tenebrous sickness of the endless void. Removing these items will likely come with a hidden price.

Mioroth the Sage

Whenever a character interacts with or closely inspects one of the Crystal Relics or the Alloyed Clockwork, the spectral memory of Mioroth appears.

As you inspect the odd crystalline relic, it releases a brilliant flash of arcane light. The semi-spectral form of some large apparition begins to appear before your very eyes …

@Embed[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]

Old Acquaintances

The party may have met Mioroth previously, potentially multiple times. Mioroth's projection is aware of and remembers the party from those prior encounters, so be sure to adapt the dialog accordingly depending on whether the party is already familiar with the Shent sage or whether this is a first encounter.

Reference other Mioroth encounters in:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.yzgUD9WX351fihbU]

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.LyNcEPtA6HA1XvQZ]

Mioroth addresses the party immediately:

Hark, travelers. You find yourself among the vaults of Ebbok Zhùr. Whatever has brought you here, I hope your intentions are pure. This is a hallowed place, where the evils that lurk beyond this world are restrained by the work of our most honorable artificers.

The allure of precious metal and glimmering stone may tempt you, but beware the call of the Abyss and its minions, lest you fall to its insidious sway. Turn back now, or proceed with the truest of purposes.

The characters have a few moments to beseech the Sage's memory before they continue.

A Conversation with Mioroth

Mioroth can readily offer the party information on a variety of topics, with several examples in the dialogue below.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 16]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 16]] check are able to convince Mioroth of the veracity of their cause, and may elicit some additional help from the Sage (at the Gamemaster's discretion).

Once the characters have completed their exchange with Mioroth, he bids them farewell before his apparition dissipates with a fluttering of arcane light.

Moons guide you.

On the Bleak Archive?

Known as Ebbok Zhùr by the ancient Shent artificers who built it prior to the Shattering, this trap-laden vault was originally constructed to contain a volatile repository of Abyssal artifacts and eldritch curiosities.

Regarding the Vault's Hazards?

Beware the blade traps that protect the far eastern and western corridors. And take care when navigating the vault's darker chambers — the minions of the Abyss have strange relationships with the shadows.

About the Relics?

The Shent and Varùn relics that reside here are all corrupted with the eldritch taint of the Abyss. Embrace them at your own peril.

On the Shent?

The Shent were members an enlightened and wise society that met its end during the events of the Abyssal Shear two and a half thousand years ago. Shent sages foretold this cataclysm that came to Ember, and were paragons of lunar and runic magic.

The Statue's Contraptions

When the characters examine the stone statue on the dais, read the following aloud:

The statue here is made of the same ashen gray slate that comprises the rest of the vault, and features the likeness of a large, wizened humanoid with a mane of jagged hair, a magnificent beard to match, and two prodigiously curved horns atop his stony head. The statue's fingers are tipped in sharp claws, and his outstretched hands appear to be caught up in some kind of dramatic gesticulation that's been frozen in time.

Examining the Statue

The crystal orb in front of the statue altar generates the beams of light necessary to control the room's pair of retractable walls (one located to the east and the other to the west).

  • A living humanoid creature must place their left hand on the orb to correspond with the large handprint etched upon it in order to activate the beams of light.

  • Simultaneously, when the beams of light appear, both of the retractable walls are activated and lower into the ground.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] skill check recognizes the subject of the statue as a Shent artificer from the Age of Sunlight.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] skill check is able to comprehend the design of the statue's altar, the purpose of the arcane beams of light that emanate from the crystals to each side, how the beams of light relate to the mirrors, and how the front-facing orb interacts with the receding walls.

Retractible Walls

The crystal orb located in front of the statue is capable of lowering the retractible walls here. A character can place their hand upon the crystal orb as part of their move action.

The retractible wall located to the north of the @UUID[.k1DMt6QutPVqSxGJ]{Inner Antechamber} can only be opened by the completion of the mirror array puzzle throughout the Bleak Archive that redirects these two beams of arcane light. The key to opening the @UUID[.TfjCELA7w5tj5ybN]{True Vault} begins here.

Rotating Mirrors

Using the mirrors to redirect the beam of arcane light using the rules described in @UUID[.B9icKNDZQmOO2hnq#mirrors-and-walls]{Mirrors and Walls}, the party can gain access to the @UUID[.XVzHtK88QaL9cmOg]{Western Corridor} to the west and the @UUID[.Nsvsx26sWAxGNY7x]{Webbed Mausoleum} to the east.

Corrupted Guardians

Two Corrupted Cadrithor, the abyssally twisted and deathless remnants of once-noble guardian beasts, stand watch here on the far side of the retractable walls to the east and west of this chamber.

@Embed[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1 count=2]

Corrupted Cadrithor Tactics

The Cadrithor will engage the characters in melee combat as soon as the retractable wall nearest each of them recedes into the floor. They will frequently use @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.VUblphglrRmicBvR]{Shadow Gait} to navigate the dimly-lit environment and close on a vulnerable character which they can @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.LGzpxppyJKpAETxV]{Multiattack}. They will always fight to the death.

While in dim light or darkness, the Cadrithor benefit from @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.XuBzmC2SUOaOq8k0]{Blessing of the Abyss}, the effects of which can be easily toggled using an Active Effect on their character sheet.

The Cadrithor have a notable vulnerability to radiant damage, and especially the concentrated radiance of the light beams reflected by Shent mirrors throughout the complex. A Cadrithor will never voluntarily walk through these beams. If they are struck directly by a beam they are instantly destroyed as described in @UUID[.B9icKNDZQmOO2hnq#mirrors-and-walls]{Mirrors and Walls}.

The Cadrithor will engage the characters in melee combat as soon as the retractable wall nearest each of them recedes into the floor. They will frequently use @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.shadowGait000000] to navigate the dimly-lit environment and close on a vulnerable character which they then dedicatedly target with @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.necroticBite0000] and pursue repeated brutal attacks with their claws and bites to take @Advantage[2] of @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.graveMark0000000].

The Cadrithor lack any sense of self-preservation and will always fight to the death.

While in dim light or darkness, the Cadrithor benefit from @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.abyssalProtectio]{Abyssal Protection}, and conversely suffer from @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.sunlightWeakness.ActiveEffect.sunlightWeakness], the effects of either can be easily toggled using an Active Effect on their character sheet.

The Cadrithor have a notable vulnerability to radiant damage, and especially the concentrated radiance of the light beams reflected by Shent mirrors throughout the complex. A Cadrithor will never voluntarily walk through these beams. If they are struck directly by a beam they are instantly destroyed as described in @UUID[.B9icKNDZQmOO2hnq#mirrors-and-walls]{Mirrors and Walls}.

  • A character with [[/skill insight 16 passive]] or a successful [[/skill insight 14]] check[[/skillCheck diplomacy 16 passive]] recognizes the creature's extreme aversion to these beams and can intuit that the beams might be used to harm the Cadrithor.

Antechamber.name: Antechamber
Antechamber.text:
This hexagonal antechamber is illuminated by the pale, blue glow of three crystal lanterns that seem to cast a perpetual arcane light. The skeletal remains of five large humanoids lie upon the floor here, covered in countless layers of dust. Clad in tarnished armor and rotted vestments, these ancient warriors seem to have suffered an untimely and mysterious fate. The room is otherwise decorated with a scattered array of urns and canopic jars that line the cobwebbed walls.

A set of double doors to the north is etched with curious imagery: a geometric palimpsest of runic markings and archaic text surround the figure of some wizened sage, who holds aloft a staff crowned in six crystals that plainly resemble Ember's moons.

In this area, the characters may locate clues about a previous group of visitors that came to the Bleak Archive long ago, a raiding party led by Tethra Shùl themselves. These raiders were ultimately betrayed and killed by the Varùn warlock.

The Doomed Giants

You perceive five distinct skeletons of large sized humanoids scattered about the Antechamber. Each of the skeletal corpses is adorned with tattered tunics, and they seem to possess the telltale equipment of warriors — now moldering with verdigris and covered in countless layers of dust.

Examining the Remains

Characters with a [[/skill perception 12 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 10]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12 passive]] check will notice that the skeletons look out of place here, as if they were visitors to the Bleak Archive themselves. The style of their rotten garments and the make of their archaic weaponry is unlike the esoteric architecture of the vault's Antechamber.

  • A successful [[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check allows a character to identify the tattered rags adorning the skeletal corpses as ancient Varùn in origin.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck medicine 13]] check can determine the various causes of death for the Varùn warriors:

  • Two of the Varùn warriors seem to have simultaneously stabbed each other with their swords, which still protrude from their respective ribcages. These swords resemble larger versions of the @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z.Item.orNQU0QNPJo4jKue]{Rune-Marked Knife} wielded by Dereth Erekos.

  • Two of the Varùn warriors appear to have simultaneously shot each other with their shortbows. A half-dozen oversized arrows are scattered about each of these skeletons, with one or two protruding from skull and bone. One of the arrowheads is missing: the cursed @UUID[Item.w7jXkPu7MheM6bkw]{Rune-Marked Arrowhead}.

  • One of the Varùn warriors, located near the northern doors, appears to have been burned to death by some powerful incineration. The bones still bear signs of ancient scorching. Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check is able to identify the incinerated skeleton as the likely target of a potent Evocation Flame rune spell.

Speaking with the Dead

If a character uses the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithD]{Speak with Dead} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.SoulProficiency0] to communicate with the Varùn skeletons, they can learn the following information:

  • They came to this place as aides to the warlock Tethra Shùl.

  • Tethra Shùl betrayed them using strange eldritch magic that turned them against each other.

  • Tethra Shùl was granted new forms of eldritch power by some unknown or otherworldly being.

  • There is a dangerous magical trap on the Palimpsest Doors, and how it incinerated one of them in a horrible death.

  • Various recollections about the pre-Shattering era of Ember during the Age of Sunlight, as well as the Shattering itself.

Additional details about the Tethra Shùl's Varùn raiding party can be found in the "Lore" section of the @UUID[.JcGOyaCzImvAie1Z]{Area Overview}.

Ashes of the Ancient Shent

The urns and vases in this room contain the ashes of Shent heroes from long ago, including the dusty remains of sages and spellswords who battled the Abyss in the days before The Shattering.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 15]] or [[/skill religion 13]][[/skillCheck society 14]] check while examining the urns recognizes inscriptions and etchings on the vessels to be honorific in nature.

The Palimpsest Doors

The two stone doors to the north are covered in layers upon layers of runic etchings. This palimpsest of carvings displays the image of a wizened Shent sage bearing an arcane staff in one hand and a blank tome in the other. The staff, held aloft at the seam between the monolithic doors, is crowned with an inverted Holy Symbol of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}.

The doors are locked and trapped by powerful magic. When Tethra Shùl came to this place long ago, she sacrificed the five members of her raiding party to gain entrance unscathed. The party must solve the door's riddle and contend with its enchantments if they wish to do the same.

Deciphering the Doors

Characters who can understand [[/language pathward]], [[/language eonic]], [[/language harmos]], or [[/language caligon]] are able to discern the following phrases within the overlapping etchings of the palimpsest in the characters of their respective languages:

THE WAY IS BARRED FOR EVIL HEARTS

  • A hint regarding the arcane trap affixed to the doors. See "Fiery Doorway Trap" below.

SCRIBE YOUR NAME WITH THE DUST OF DEVOTION

  • A clue that points to the Shent ashes contained in the urns scattered about the room, the method for disarming the Fiery Doorway Trap.

A successful [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check also allows a character to notice the enchanted nature of the trapped door. It's also clear that the various phrases etched upon the door (whether they understand them or not) are related to a command or key.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]]] check recognizes the sage's pre-Shattering garb and iconography as Shent in origin.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 16]] further [[/skillCheck society 16]] check is able to identify the holy symbol of the Elder god Sockets at the head of the Sage's staff, as well as the dangerous connotation of its inversion — an omen to heretics who might challenge the so-called Keeper of Souls.

Any character who spends at least 10 minutes studying @UUID[Item.jlmAciSoBLtSdIaB]{Dereth's Journal} is able to find handwritten notes that feverishly describe the method of opening the door, a vision that came to the bard in a dream.

Fiery Doorway Trap

Characters with a [[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] check will notice that the doors here are magically trapped, detecting the faint glimmer of dangerous arcane luminance deep within the beveled grooves of the etchings.

Any character who traces their true name upon the door using ashes from the urns in the chamber here disarms the trap for 24 hours. Alternately, the trap can be disabled for 8 hours if it becomes the target of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} spell.
