The trap can be disabled for 24 hours if someone conducts a successful [[/counterspell rune=flame gesture=cone inflection=react dc=18]]. A character who uses @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr] receives +2 Boons to attempt this.

Any character who attempts to open the doors without disabling the trap activates a @UUID[Actor.a0eioTwCkcvXsQwE.Item.B0Y8A0oziDVw9BnI]{Burning Hands} @Spell[[flame.cone] spell which emanates in a 15-foot cone from the etching of the sage's staff located near the center of the two doors. Each affected character must make a [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 3d6 fire]] damage. Evil characters have Vulnerability to the damage caused by this effect.

Mist-Veiled Approach.name: Mist-Veiled Approach
Mist-Veiled Approach.text:
After navigating the steep hillside precipice, you come to a rocky promontory that overlooks a craggy, mist-veiled crevasse below. Two large doors — decorated with runic markings and crafted from a curious flaxen alloy — are cut into the hillside here, flanked by two statues of canine creatures bearing a regal, almost celestial presence. Above each statue, a blue crystal lantern shaped like a dodecahedron shines a pale light. And all around you, lambent cerulean moon blossoms decorate the ground, despite the presence of fertile soil. There is an ominous air to this bleak and lonely place.

Archive Exterior

In the side of this mountain stand the ominous gates of Ebbok Zhùr, the Bleak Archive.

The stony ground here is swathed in a low-hanging blanket of mist, along with a scattered array of lambent cerulean moon blossoms — which seem to grow brighter the closer they get to the entrance.

Characters who look more closely at the doors leading to the Archive are able to notice a few details: runic etchings traced all along the door's surface, and a bit of esoteric graffiti carved in a wicked-looking language. The doors have no handles, and — other than the esoteric graffiti — are totally unmarred, as if the ravages time and weather have passed them by.

Surveying the Vault Exterior

A successful [[/skill religion 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check reveals the esoteric holy symbol of the Elder god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} hidden within the etchings on the doors.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 16]] further [[/skillCheck society 16]]] check is able to recognize the architecture here as the expert work of the bygone Shent. They also recognize iconography in the door's etchings that depict a legendary Shent sage known as Heroth, the Harrow-Hearted.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: In addition to his arcane prowess, Heroth was known to be a war priest of the Elder God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, and stood proudly and successfully against many Abyssal incursions of the ancient past. This proximity to the Abyss came with rumors about Heroth's corruption — rumors staunchly denied by his disciples and allies.

Characters who understand [[/language pathward]] can decipher various runes within the door's etchings, revealing the phrase:

THE DEVOUT TRACE THE DEATHLESS PATH

Meanwhile, characters who understand [[/language abyssal]] are able to translate a phrase that has been graffitied here:

SPEAK THE WORDS TO SUMMON THE MASTER

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 18]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 18]] check can identify the statues here as diminutive sculptures of celestial hounds known as Cadrithors, which were known to be loyal companions to the Shent and their allies, often serving as guardians and protectors.

The entrance to this place is secured using an arcane trap.

Baneful Doorway Trap

Characters with a [[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] check will notice that the doors here are magically trapped, detecting the faint glimmer of dangerous arcane luminance deep within the beveled grooves of the etchings.

  • Result of 15+ Success: The character identifies the shape of the Holy Symbol of Sockets (whether they recognize it or not) as a centerpiece to the etchings and of some importance to the door's mechanism.

A successful [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check also allows a character to notice the enchanted nature of the trapped door. It's also clear that the Pathward phrase etched upon the door (whether they recognize it or not) is related to a command or key.

  • Result of 15+ Critical Success: The character recognizes the Abyssal graffiti as another command-related clue, despite its alien nature.

Any creature who attempts to open the door without performing a gesture of the holy symbol of Sockets must succeed on a [[/save wis 15]] saving throw or become affected by the @UUID[Actor.fuL7YqC7eENDtHeJ.Item.NCgR9uNJNsxEaxE0]{Bane} spell until they finish a long rest. Evil creatures have @Advantage[-2] on this roll.

Any creature who attempts to open the door without performing a gesture of the holy symbol of Sockets must face [[/hazard 4 willpower morale corruption]]{Judgment of Sockets} and are @Condition[weakened] until they finish a Rest.

The front doorway to the Bleak Archive is locked by powerful magic, and can be opened by two primary methods: recognition of archaic Shent rites or Abyssal assistance from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas}.

Opening the Gates

Any character who traces a gesture of the Holy Symbol of Sockets into the air or upon the surface of the door is able to open the door via the proper method. Once the gesture is traced, the Baneful Doorway Trap is disarmed, and the runic etchings on the doors swell with arcane brilliance as the portal slowly opens.

Alternately, any character who speaks one of the Abyssal phrases from the @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.O1u2YfjEcHhFRezW]{Night Terrors} of Nethehepticas is granted entry via the Abyssal Horror's distant otherworldly influence:

  • "Away to Ebbok Zhùr."

  • "The Night Terror beckons the brave."

  • "The Sleeper walks in Skybrush."

  • "The Bleak Seed has been sewn."

As soon as a character speaks one of these phrases aloud in Abyssal, four spectral claws of amethyst shadow coalesce and pry open the arcane doors — overriding the aged Shent magic that has kept them shut.

Any character who spends at least 10 minutes studying @UUID[Item.jlmAciSoBLtSdIaB]{Dereth's Journal} is able to find handwritten notes that feverishly describe the method of opening the door, a vision that came to the bard in a dream.

Alternate Entrance

Navigating the ravine to the east of the front gate allows the party to reach a covert secondary entrance to the Bleak Archives via the @UUID[.bnA4fGGRaYOsSOjJ]{Hidden Breach}.

Spotting the Hidden Breach

A character with [[/skill perception 16 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 14]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] notices an inconspicuous hole in the cliff face, obscured by shadow and a bramble of ash-colored vine.

Ossuary.name: Ossuary
Ossuary.text:
Countless humanoid skulls of various sizes adorn the cluttered alcoves of this grim ossuary, and an assortment of bones both large and small lies scattered across the stone floor. If you didn't know better, you'd swear the pitch black sockets of those skulls were staring right back at you…

In this area, the characters will encounter the Archive's ossuary, where the bones of countless Abyssal heretics have been collected for safe keeping. The party must manipulate the mirrors to advance the beam of light while braving the psychic hazards of a ghostly miasma that haunts the bones here.

The Haunted Charnel House

The skeletal remains here consist of the scattered bones of unnamed Abyssal heretics.

Heretical Remains

Any character who disturbs the bones here must succeed on a [[/save wis 16]] saving throw to avoid suffering [[/roll 1d2]] points of Wisdom damage as a ghostly miasma assaults their senses. This damage is restored after a long rest.

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.classfeatures.Item.r91UIgwFdHwkXdia]{Channel Divinity: Turn Undead} class feature and similar effects that Turn Undead suppress this effect for 8 hours.

Any character who disturbs the bones here suffers [[/hazard 8 willpower morale void]]{Ghostly Miasma}.

The remains are horribly decomposed and mostly crumbling into bone dust, however the ossuary compartments do contain some forgotten baubles.

Searching the Remains

There are ample bones here which could be used as spell components for arcana which require such.

Each character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] or [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check while searching the bones finds one of the following:

@Embed[RollTable.ku1tHDCPVktnPLsR inline rollable=true]

Spellcasters may endeavor to communicate with the long-deceased remains.

Speaking with the Dead

Characters who use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithD]{Speak with Dead} spell @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.SoulProficiency0] to communicate with the assorted skeletons can learn the following information:

  • Assorted tales of pre-Shattering Abyssal incursions.

  • Misleading hints about what lurks in the Archive's Inner Sanctum.

  • Cryptic revelations about the influence of Nethehepticas and other Abyssal Horrors.

Out of the Shadows

A Corrupted Cadrithor lurks unseen within the shadows of the Ossuary's crowded passages, ready to strike once the characters are occupied with the Heretical Remains.

A terrible canine growl fills the bone-strewn chamber, and the semi-spectral apparition of a hound made of pure shadow rushes forth from the dusky gloom.

Watchdog of Tethra Shùl

Once the characters are occupied with inspecting the remains in this chamber or manipulating the rotating mirrors, a @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor} emerges from the ossuary walls using its @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.lrfk5XIgWOSwND8P]{Amorphous} feature.

It will following the tactics described in @UUID[.1ZvVg4pODC7wjnxo#corrupted-guardians]{Corrupted Guardians} and fight to the death.

Once the characters are occupied with inspecting the remains in this chamber or manipulating the rotating mirrors, a @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor} emerges from the ossuary walls using its @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1.Item.lrfk5XIgWOSwND8P]{Amorphous} feature.

It will following the tactics described in @UUID[.1ZvVg4pODC7wjnxo#corrupted-guardians]{Corrupted Guardians} and fight to the death.

Reflector Array.name: Reflector Array
Reflector Array.text:
A half-dozen platforms of grated metal here are suspended high above what appears to be a bottomless pit. The air below is cold, and carries with it the hollow sound of fathomless subterranea.

This chamber serves as a crucial hub for the system of rotating mirrors that unlock the Bleak Archive's Inner Sanctum. Characters must navigate the grated metallic platforms as they rotate the mirrors to their proper alignments.

The Fear-Shrouded Pit

The pit in this room is 40 feet deep, but so shrouded in darkness that it appears to be bottomless.

Any character who falls into the pit suffers [[/damage 4d6 bludgeoning]] damage and must succeed on a [[/save cha 13]] saving throw or become &Reference[Frightened] for [[/roll 1d4]] hours by unseen Abyssal whispers. All undead creatures including Corrupted Cadrithors, Horrendors, and Tethra Shùl count as sources of this fear.

Any character who falls into the pit suffers a [[/hazard 12 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Great Fall} and must also face [[/hazard 4 willpower morale void]{Abyssal Whispers}, becoming @Condition[frightened] for [[/roll 1d4]] hours.

The northern exit from the reflector array is concealed and controlled by an inconspicuous lever on the east side of the northern wall.

Secret Door

Characters with a[[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] can detect the seams of the secret door itself.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill intelligence 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] check can determine the mechanical nature of the secret door and confirm the presence of a remote lever.

Additionally, after the door has been identified, characters with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] can detect the lever while exploring the Reflector Array.

Progressing the Beam

In order to correctly advance the beam of light, it must be routed around the array using all 7 mirrors, ending in the top-center mirror that directs the light northwards towards the Study Chamber.

Study Chamber.name: Study Chamber
Study Chamber.text:
Bookcases jam-packed with dusty scrolls and moldering tomes line the walls of this small two-room chamber, which appears to be an ancient study. Several books are strewn across the floor, and the faint smell of incense accompanies the stale scent of musty parchment and worm-eaten pages.

In this area, the characters can discover a small repository of ancient books and scrolls. They must survive combat with a malevolent Horrendor, whose corpse has lurked here for time immemorial.

Retractable Wall

The Study Chamber is only accessible via a retractible wall. The corresponding lever to this retractible wall is located in the shallow 5-foot alcove just outside the Study Chamber to the west.

A Horrendor lurks here, having risen from the long-dead corpse of a medium-sized Shent scholar.

@Embed[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]

Horrendor Tactics

The Horrendor will play dead until one of the characters moves close enough for a melee attack. A character with [[/skill perception 15 passive]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check will notice a subtle clue that the corpse may not be inanimate.

Once in range, the Horrendor will attack gleefully and without remorse using a combination of @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.CFHyyTtMRhrwaJ51]{Multiattack}, @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.Vna5GyoBUJhBtV1f]{Gruesome Mockery}, and @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.gldnENV6nrtpTlkH]{Cunning Escape}. The creature fights to the death. Note that @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.tx3NnbSgPml71Q20]{Undeathly Fortitude} makes the Horrendor exceptionally difficult to fully defeat.

Corrupted Cadrithor

If the confrontation with the Horrendor makes audible noise, which is likely as it uses its Gruesome Mockery, it may attract a @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor} which joins the fray from the hallway to the southeast.

The Horrendor will play dead until one of the characters moves close enough for a melee attack. A character with [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] or who succeeds on an [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check will notice a subtle clue that the corpse may not be inanimate.

Once in range, the Horrendor will attack gleefully and without remorse using a combination of @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.rakingTalons0000], @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.necroticBite0000], and a series of mocking efforts at @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.intimidator00000]{Intimidation} emphasized through its @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.horrificCritical].

The creature fights to the death. Note that @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.restlessDead0000] makes the Horrendor exceptionally difficult to fully defeat.

Corrupted Cadrithor

If the confrontation with the Horrendor makes audible noise, which is likely as it uses its Gruesome Mockery, it may attract a @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor} which joins the fray from the hallway to the southeast.

The Undead Scholar

Any character who searches the Horrendor remains is able to find a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.UOE8RGOpgv2oWIvM]{Scholar's Pack} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.scrivenersPortab] and a @UUID[Item.AxkavzAgou9VudO6]{Shent Signet Ring}.

The Forgotten Library

The walls here are lined with dusty shelves full of moth-eaten scrolls and moldering books. Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] or [[/skill investigation 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check while examining the shelves is able to locate the following items of interest amongst the detritus:

@Embed[RollTable.nKIsb5438ydfwV9C inline rollable=true]

Progressing the Beam

In order to correctly advance the beam of light, it must be routed through all four mirrors of the Study Chamber, ending in the mirror to the southwest of the chamber's entrance.

Accessing the Inner Antechamber

The @UUID[.k1DMt6QutPVqSxGJ]{Inner Antechamber} and the vault beyond can be acceesed by engaging a lever on the wall of the hallway to the southeast. This causes a large section of wall to descend that makes travel within the eastern half of the Archive less restricted.

Webbed Mausoleum.name: Webbed Mausoleum
Webbed Mausoleum.text:
Dusty layers of crisscrossing spiderwebs diffuse the azure light of the arcane lantern that illuminates this irregular chamber, and you notice the distinct bulge of egg sacs scattered here and there throughout the viscid, semitranslucent lattice.

In this area, the characters will traverse an arged mausoleum that has become the ersatz lair of a giant spider.

The Arachnid Interloper

A devious @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV]{Child of Sitheera} has taken residence in this irregularly-shaped chamber after discovering the Hidden Breach, and has managed to capture a handful of would-be tomb robbers throughout the years who crawled into its webs. The creature is initially hidden from view perched upon the ceiling and concealed among thick webs.

Navigating the Web

Any character who moves throughout the webbed sections of the chamber will unavoidably activate the Child of Sitheera's @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.1LTl2RCToU6ZLZdi]{Web Sense}, informing it of their presence.

Moreover, characters who move through the webbed area must succeed on a [[/save dex 12]] saving throw to avoid becoming &Reference[Restrained] by the webbing.

  • As an action, the restrained target can attempt escape using a [[/check athletics 12]] or [[/check acrobatics 12]] check.

  • The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10; 5 hit points; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).

Lurking Danger

The Child of Sitheera will attempt to remain hidden from the party until one of them is caught in the nearby webbing or until all characters have crossed to a far end of the room. It lurks in the center of the chamber on the ceiling amidst webs, 30 feet above.

Characters with a [[/skill perception 17]] or who succeed on a [[/skill prc 15]] check are able to detect the Child of Sitheera in its hiding place. Otherwise, the Child of Sitheera benefits from surprise when attacking. Once the creature is detected, or once it chooses to attack the party, combat begins!

Any character who moves throughout the webbed sections of the chamber will unavoidably make the Sitherian aware of their presence.

Moreover, characters who move through the webbed area must face a [[/hazard 1 reflex morale bludgeoning]] or become @Condition[restrained] by the webbing.

The restrained target can escape with a successful [[/skillCheck athletics 12]] check.

The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed using slashing weapons or fire.

Lurking Danger

The Child of Sitheera will attempt to remain hidden from the party until one of them is caught in the nearby webbing or until all characters have crossed to a far end of the room. It lurks in the center of the chamber on the ceiling amidst webs, 30 feet above.

Characters with a [[/skillCheck awareness 17 passive]] or who succeed on a [[/skillCheck awareness 17]] check are able to detect the Child of Sitheera in its hiding place. Otherwise, the Child of Sitheera benefits from surprise when attacking. Once the creature is detected, or once it chooses to attack the party, combat begins!

@Embed[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV]

Child of Sitheera Tactics

Once combat begins, the Child of Sitheera will immediately use its @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.U0Ydv7sK1ImlRpFD]{Web} action before engaging the character with the lowest Hit Points in melee. The creature is relatively intelligent, using its climb speed and the webbing throughout its lair to gain situational advantages against restrained characters.

The creature has instincts for self preservation and will attempt to escape once its life is meaningfully threatened.

Once combat begins, the Child of Sitheera will immediately use its @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.webSpinner000000Searching the Webs] action before engaging the character with the lowest Hit Points in melee. The creature is relatively intelligent, using its climb speed and the webbing throughout its lair to gain situational advantages against restrained characters.

The creature has instincts for self preservation and will attempt to escape once its life is meaningfully threatened.

After combat has concluded, the party may wish to investigate the area further.

Victims of the Venomous Steward

The first four characters who attempt to search the corpses and egg sacs wrapped up in the webbing here can roll twice on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot (Arctus Plateau)} table.

Additionally, the first character to succeed on a[[/skill nature 13]] or [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]]check is able to locate a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potion of Healing} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rallyingElixir00] concealed among the webbed detritus.

A character with [[/skill perception 16 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] check notices a concealed control lever covered in webbing upon the north wall of the room.

Retractible Column

In order to progress the mirror and light beam puzzle through this section of the dungeon, the party must find and activate a hidden lever which causes pillars in this room to alternate in height.

Darkroom.name: Darkroom
Darkroom.text:
This junction is adorned with another set of the vault's revolving mirrors. Swaddled in a tattered cloak, the skeletal remains of some long-dead humanoid appear seated upon the ground against the chamber's central column in a pose of ancient abandon.

The Darkroom serves as a junction for the Bleak Archive's complex system of mirrors, and is relatively sparse — save for the presence of a magical Darkness trap installed to ward off trespassers, and a single Corrupted Cadrithor that rises from the skeletal corpse of a Shent sage. In this area, the characters may operate several mirrors and doors necessary access the Inner Antechamber.

Magical Darkness Trap

Whenever at least 10 pounds of weight are applied to a pressure plate at the southern end of the Darkroom chamber, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDarkness00]{Darkness} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.engulfingDarknes] spell is cast on the area. The duration for this effect is 1 hour, after which time the trap resets.

  • A character with a[[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] who is close enough to clearly see the pressure plate can notice it.

  • This effect is subdued for 1 hour after becoming the target of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} spell [[/counterspell rune=oblivion gesture=pulse inflection=push dc=16]].

Once the trap has been triggered, any @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor} within 60 feet sense the magical darkness and are immediately drawn towards it. See @UUID[.1ZvVg4pODC7wjnxo]{Main Gallery} for information on Cadrithor tactics.

Arcane shadow fills the chamber, but you manage to catch the briefest of glimpses of some strange spectral vapor rising from the skeletal remains. As night surrounds you, you hear the telltale growl of some canine creature in the darkness and the ominous scraping of claws upon stone growing ever closer.

The Skeletal Remains

The aged skeleton that sits on the floor near the center of the chamber is a long-dead Shent scholar who presided over this place as a journeyman trapsmith.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck medicine 13]] check is able to recognize the tattered robes on the skeleton as Shent in origin.

  • Any character who searches the skeleton finds an ancient set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000] and a @UUID[Item.AxkavzAgou9VudO6]{Shent Signet Ring}.

Once they solve the puzzle of the Darkroom's mirrors, the party can travel to the @UUID[.k1DMt6QutPVqSxGJ]{Inner Antechamber} to the southwest, completing half of the mirror puzzle required to breach the inner vault.

Progressing the Beam

In order to correctly advance the beam of light, the darkness trap must be deactivated or disabled, since its magical darkness counteracts the beam of light. Then the beam must be routed through five of the six mirrors in the chamber.

Accessing the Inner Antechamber

The @UUID[.k1DMt6QutPVqSxGJ]{Inner Antechamber} and the vault beyond can be accessed by engaging a lever on the wall of the hallway to the southwest. This causes a large section of wall to descend that makes travel within the western half of the Archive less restricted.

Inner Antechamber.name: Inner Antechamber
Inner Antechamber.text:
The mechanical walls descend to reveal a wide room containing two mirrors and little else — save the shadow-ensorcelled forms of a pair of tenebrous dusk hounds. The luminous purple eyes of these creatures regard you with malice as they bare their hideously prodigious fangs.

This oblong room serves as an antechamber for the True Vault of the Bleak Archive. In this area, the characters will encounter a duo of Corrupted Cadrithors before making their way into the Inner Sanctum. The party must survive before they can complete the puzzle and unlock the True Vault.

@Embed[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1 count=2]

The Watchdogs of Tethra Shùl

A pair of @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithors} stand watch here, and will engage the characters as soon as they reach the Inner Antechamber or adjacent areas.

The two Corrupted Cadrithor follow the tactics described in @UUID[.1ZvVg4pODC7wjnxo#corrupted-guardians]{Corrupted Guardians} and fight to the death.

Unsealing the True Vault

Imminent Danger

Direct confrontation with Tethra Shùl, who awaits the party within the True Vault, is especially dangerous for lower level characters.

If the party is only level 2 at this point or not at full strength and resources, it is strongly suggested to remind them that a source of true evil is likely to be encountered beyond these doors. The party may wish to further prepare themselves or seek help in facing this deadly foe.

Directing the Beams

The Inner Sanctum is only accessible via a retractible wall. The corresponding key to this retractible wall is the completion of the mirror array puzzle that originates in the @UUID[.1ZvVg4pODC7wjnxo]{Main Gallery}, wherein the two beams of arcane light are redirected to the crystal receptacles located in the @UUID[.k1DMt6QutPVqSxGJ]{Inner Antechamber}.

Taking a closer look at the northern wall, you notice that the central forty-foot section is bookended by two seams that run the vertical length of the wall. The two crystal sconces on each side of this curious threshold all but confirm the presence of another retractable partition here. The northern wall itself feels cold to the touch, and you can almost hear a faint whisper in the back of your mind as you draw near to it.

The final vault door opens only in response to the completion of the puzzle, connecting both beams of light to their respective receptors on either side of the door.

As the two beams of bright light strike the crystals on the northern wall, the entire Inner Antechamber begins to tremble as the mechanism of one final retractable door shudders to life. The northern wall slowly retreats into the floor, revealing a secret vault on the other side. The large form of some gloom-shrouded creature lurks with intense preoccupation at the center of this darkened chamber.

Locked Mirrors

Once the True Vault door is open, all mirrors throughout the Bleak Archive become locked in position and none can be rotated further unless the entire apparatus is reset using the original levers in the @UUID[.1ZvVg4pODC7wjnxo]{Main Gallery}.

True Vault.name: True Vault
True Vault.text:
This large octagonal chamber is marked by a central platform surrounded by a ten-foot-wide bottomless pit. Upon this platform, a large figure cloaked in shadow appears to be caressing a statuette made of dark stone. A raspy femme voice thick with an unfamiliar accent cuts through the air like a blade made of grim whispers.

I've been waiting a very long time for you, my lambs. Welcome to the slaughter.

This area is the Bleak Archive's most hallowed repository. Before exploring it the party must survive combat with the wraithlike Varùn warlock Tethra Shùl, the eldritch villain behind Skybrush's accursed maladies. Combat with Tethra Shùl begins as soon as the players discover the room and hear the readaloud text above.

@Embed[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd]

Read the following aloud at the start of Tethra Shùl's first turn:

The spectral giantess holds forth a dark wand, which resembles the large desiccated finger of some hideous otherworldly creature. An opalescent sheen shimmers across its dusky surface, and the wraith utters something beneath her breath… A plume of tenebrous vapor pours out of the hand before coalescing into the awful form of another dusk hound.

And now, a pet for you to play with, my precious things … Devour these tender morsels!

Tactics of the Varùn Warlock

Throughout combat, Tethra Shùl will rely upon @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.RojHz4gSoAFJOMO6]{Incorporeal Movement} and her fly speed to navigate the battlefield with ease and avoid danger.

Upon their first turn of combat, Tethra Shùl uses the @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.2PE7yxXP4feQn6sx]{Finger of Nethehepticas} to summon a @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor}. On subsequent turns, Tethra Shùl will rely upon the following spells:

  • Mirror Image for self-protection

  • @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.r2G0m800EaKOo1ki]{Darkness} to deny visibility to the party and to take advantage of her own @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.HhedQaEJNk7JWZav]{Devil Sight} feature.

  • @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.NMMG9V23zBM0Vna5]{Dispel Magic} to counteract beneficial magics of the party.

In addition to spell slots, Tethra Shul will utilize:

  • The Waking Nightmares ability of the Finger of Nethehepticas.

  • @UUID[Actor.MJfOzwa6uawHDhHA.Item.f0ilya8ujxFSwuRj]{Life Drain} to ruthlessly kill weakened characters.

Tethra Shùl does not fear death and believes rather firmly that she cannot be defeated, and as a result her arrogance will encourage her to fight to the death.

During combat, Tethra Shùl will taunt the party with a variety of threats and insults (featured below).

Throughout combat, Tethra Shùl will rely upon her @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.amorphous0000000] nature and @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.shadowGait000000] to navigate the battlefield with ease and avoid danger.

Upon their first turn of combat, Tethra Shùl uses the @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.2PE7yxXP4feQn6sx]{Finger of Nethehepticas} to summon a @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor}. On subsequent turns, Tethra Shùl will rely upon the following spells and abilities:

  • @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.engulfingDarknes] to deny visibility to the party and to take advantage of her own @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.gloomSight000000] talent.

  • @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.curseDelusion000], and @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.curseAtrophy0000] to burden party members with difficult to overcome curses.

  • @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.2PE7yxXP4feQn6sx] to draw additional life from those she harms with magic, and she will ruthlessly Counterspell party attempts at magic if she is able.

In addition to these abilities, Tethra Shul will utilize:

  • The @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.2PE7yxXP4feQn6sx] ability of the Finger of Nethehepticas.

  • additional composed spells from the Death, Control, and Oblivion runes as required.

Tethra Shùl does not fear death and believes rather firmly that she cannot be defeated, and as a result her arrogance will encourage her to fight to the death. Perhaps justified by her nature as one of the @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd.Item.restlessDead0000].

During combat, Tethra Shùl will taunt the party with a variety of threats and insults (featured below).

When she casts a powerful spell:

Behold the horrors of Tethra Shùl, and embrace your unmaking!

A general threat:

Your cadavers will join me in this tomb, and your souls will succumb to the Bleak Seed. Till the ends of eternity.

If a character attacks Tethra Shùl with a nonmagical weapon:

Your pitiful weapons have no power here.

If one of the characters mentions the Night Terrors:

You were summoned to Ebbok Zùr by the whispers of our great and terrible master. I’m so glad you can hear them, my little lamb. Your destiny has been waiting for you… longing for you. And here you are.

If one of the characters is already attuned to the Abyss:

If you lay down to die in service of our master, I may spare your pitiful souls. But if you choose to fight, your false hope and primal fear will taste all the more succulent to my hounds.

Once Tethra Shùl has been defeated, read the following aloud:

With a shriek horrible enough to pierce The Weave, the wraithlike warlock is rent asunder. The two motes of crimson light that lurked inside her umbral eye sockets drift slowly to the ground, where they settle as bright gemstones next to her tattered robes and bony remains.

Furthermore, the warlock's tenebrous wand sits beside her naked skull, which appears to seethe with latent eldritch magic. As you behold the warlock's worldly remains, you can almost hear her raspy voice taunting you from beyond the grave…

Treasures of Tethra Shùl

The two motes of crimson light inside Tethra Shùl's umbral eye sockets slowly drift to the ground once she's slain, becoming a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.thkvJ5QBRORIwkkV]{Gem of Brightness} and an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.dsjke4vPPsc9gsxH]{Elemental Gem of Fire}. The Finger of Nethehepticas also lies next to Tethra Shùl's remains.

Quest Progression

If the party wishes to dispel the lingering effects of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment} in Skybrush, as encountered in the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death}, Tethra Shùl's remains must be destroyed with brute force or consecrated by divine magic.

If her remains are not destroyed, the Abyssal magic that has corrupted the Bleak Archive will continue to seep necromantic energy into the nearby Rustvar hinterlands and Wedeglands peaks — and the cursed citizens of Skybrush will remain afflicted by The Bewilderment in the days, weeks, and months to come.

Full details of this procedure are detailed in the "Cleansing the Wraith's Remains" section of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.mERlrM63Ioo7UrlO]{Where Evil Lurks}.

Speaking with the Dead

Should the party be brave or foolish enough to cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.I2LUSF5ogc7Bj62e]{Speak with Dead} spell on try to communicate with the dead using Tethra Shùl's remains, the former wraith has but one response:

A horrible, raspy voice seeps out of the wraith's loathsome skull.

"I’m so glad you found a way to speak with me, my pretty little lamb. I’ve one last reminder for your sweet little head to ponder… there will never come a day when you do not live in fear of my enduring shadow, and the adumbration of my liege Nethehepticas — the Bleak Seed that grows even now within the naive confines of your fragile, mortal minds. Despair! And know that your souls will never be cleansed of this immortal stain. I have foreseen it… Or do you doubt the testament of Tethra Shùl?"

The formless wraith laughs a terrible, tenebrous laugh as her voice trails off into oblivion.

Relics of the Inner Sanctum

A few items of import are scattered throughout this chamber, the most notable of which — the @UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas} — has already been procured by Tethra Shùl for her own insidious purposes. The rest lurks in shadow, waiting to be discovered.

Eldritch Antiquities of the Abyss

Plinths etched with runic [[/language pathward]] markings line the chamber, bearing Shent relics of particular interest upon them. Any character who attempts to examine the various @UUID[Item.3kcd1E5aXjMi1NhB]{Bleak Archive Relics} stored on these plinths can spend an action to inspect one of the relics. These relics may include (listed clockwise from the retractable wall): Broken Mirror, Sundered Shield, Alloyed Spyglass, Druid's Mantle, Alloyed Scroll Tube, Crystal Orb.

Accursed Treasures

Items stored in the True Vault are ancient relics that predate the Shattering, from a time when the Abyss first began its incursions upon the face of Ember.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check while inspecting the items is able to confidently suspect that each of the Bleak Archive Relics here has been tainted by its presence in the Bleak Archive or by the Abyss itself, and is cursed with a tenebrous sickness of the endless void. Removing these items will likely come with a hidden price.

Western Treasure Chamber.name: Western Treasure Chamber
Western Treasure Chamber.text:
Two central pedestals define this small chamber. A beaded necklace sits upon one of them, while the other bears a circlet made of bright silver. Several ancient earthen vases are also stored here, along with an iron-clad chest containing a bounty of lustrous coins. The air here is remarkably cold and uncomfortably quiet.

In this area, the characters may discover a handful of relics from the Age of Sunlight, which have been stowed away behind arcane lock and key.

Abyssal Adornments

The iron bound chest here contains[[/award 1000sp]] [[/award 100sp]]worth of archaic Primordial coins.

Two wondrous items of Abyssal origin sit atop the stone pedestals in this chamber:

  • @UUID[Item.6qVb3h1819xalpYc]{Darkflame Circlet}, a cursed circlet that allows its wearer to cast a necrotic ray.

  • @UUID[Item.xKX4QAIjKbBo3N4F]{Darkstride Amulet}, a cursed amulet that hides its wearer against divination magic.

Eastern Treasure Chamber.name: Eastern Treasure Chamber
Eastern Treasure Chamber.text:
This small chamber houses two central pedestals, upon which rest two large and musty tomes bound in dark leather. A variety of ancient earthen vases are also stored here, along with an iron-clad chest bearing a wealth of lustrous coins.

In this area, the characters may discover a handful of relics from the Age of Sunlight, which have been stowed away behind arcane lock and key.

Literature of the Ancients

The iron bound chest here contains [[/award 1000sp]] [[/award 100sp]] worth of archaic Shent coins.

The two tomes that sit atop the pair of stone pedestals in this chamber are notable treasures in their own right:

  • @UUID[Item.qK28ApJwHCmRyUMi]{Sage's Grimoire}, a collection of various spells used by Shent sages to thwart the Abyss.

  • @UUID[Item.Yc3xYAwVcNnu3t4m]{Tome of Eldritch Symbols}, a cursed volume of ancient eldritch lore pertaining to the Abyss.

Hidden Breach.name: Hidden Breach
Hidden Breach.text:
A small alcove situated above the narrow ledge here is doused in shadow and overgrown with ash-colored vine, making it difficult to see what, if anything, is inside.

This Hidden Breach provides an alternate entrance to the Bleak Archive via the Webbed Mausoleum on the other side. The cavernous ravine to the east of the front gate presents a considerable hazard for characters who draw too closely to its edge without care.

Navigating the Ravine

Characters who linger for 5 minutes or more at the ravine's edge must succeed on a [[/save str 12]] to avoid being shoved off the precipice by an intermittent gust of strong mountain wind.

Any character who falls while standing here or attempting to cross the ravine must succeed on a [[/save dex 15]] saving throw to avoid [[/damage 2d6 bludgeoning]] damage as they land on another stony ledge in the mist below.

Characters who linger for 5 minutes or more at the ravine's edge must succeed on a [[/skillCheck athletics 12]]to avoid being shoved off the precipice by an intermittent gust of strong mountain wind.

Any character who falls while standing here or attempting to cross the ravine suffers a [[/hazard 6 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Minor Fall} as they land on another stony ledge in the mist below.

A character who falls here must succeed on a [[/skill athletics 13]] [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check to climb back up to the highest ledge without assistance. A grappling hook attached to a length of rope at least 20 feet long provides @Advantage[n] on this check.

Into the Breach

The Hidden Breach is concealed by a bramble of ash-colored vine atop a narrow ledge of natural stone, east of the Archive's front doors. If characters can manage to safely reach the Breach from the Mist-Veiled Approach, read the following aloud:

Drawing closer to the stony alcove, you can't help but notice a dull, malodorous scent wafting from within; and with it, the somnolent whisper of a soft and steady current of air.

Webbing & Whispers

A character with [[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] notices a blanket of cobwebs lining the far end of the small tunnel that comprises the Hidden Breach.

  • Result of 15+ Success: The character is able to identify the malodorous scent as the pungent reek of carrion rot.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The character can also hear a faint scraping sound.

A Tight Squeeze

Characters who attempt to traverse the Hidden Breach must succeed on either a[[/skill acrobatics 14]] check or a [[/skill athletics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check or suffer [[/damage 1d2 slashing]] damage from abrasions and lacerations [[/hazard 2 fortitude health slashing]]{Scrapes and Abrasions} caused by protruding roots and rocks. Small characters have @Advantage[2] on this check, and Tiny characters automatically succeed.

Eastern Corridor.name: Eastern Corridor
Eastern Corridor.text:
A subtle current of air stirs southward down the length of this dusty corridor. A mirror decorates each end of the short hallway, while a third adorns an alcove to the east.

This long hallway east of the Main Gallery is trapped with nefarious blades and a sequence of platforms suspended above a deep pit.

Spinning Blade Trap

The pressure plate which activates this trap is at the north end of the hallway. Refer to the East Blade Trap Trigger Scene Region. Activation of the trap is likely to separate characters on either side of the hazard.

A character with a[[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] who is close enough to clearly see the pressure plate can notice it and the wall seams from which the spinning blades would issue.

  • The plate can be disarmed with successful use of [[/check dexterity 15 tool=thief]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000] .

The Spinning Blade Trap is triggered when 10 or more pounds of weight are applied to the pressure plate. When the trap is triggered, several whirling blades erupt from the nearby wall and sweep through the hallway.

  • Any character who is within the area of the trap immediately or at the start of a subsequent turn must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw or take [[/damage 2d6 slashing]] damage or half damage on a successful save faces [[/hazard 6 fortitude health slashing]].

After surmounting the hazard of the blade trap, the party is faced crossing a deep pit using small metal platforms in alcoves on either side, circling around to a triangular area with three mirrors just before the entrance to the @UUID[.ztLZVTsPe4VKByvQ]{Darkroom}.

Beam Direction

In order to correctly advance the beam of light, it must be routed to the south-eastern mirror of these three from which it is directed north through a small gap in the stonework.

This gap is too small for any small or larger sized creature to pass through, but a Tiny creature could move through it freely.

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The Bleak Archive not only serves as a containment facility for ancient Abyssal relics, it acts as the ersatz tomb of the Varùn wraith known as Tethra Shùl.

Objectives

If the party wishes to help release Skybrush from the eldritch affliction of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}, they must trace the origin of the curse to this dark place and put Tethra Shul to rest. Once the characters reach the Bleak Archive, they must:

  • Solve the puzzle of the facility's revolving mirrors, sequentially accessing each chamber and corridor until they reach the Inner Sanctum.

  • Avoid an untimely death at the hands of the area's traps and hazards.

  • Survive a series of encounters with shadowy minions who lurk these ancient halls.

  • Defeat the ancient Varùn wraith, Tethra Shùl.

Repopulating Minions

@UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd]{Tethra Shùl} can summon a @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor} once per day at midnight to replace any that may have been slain, up to a maximum of 6 Corrupted Cadrithors.

Illumination

Light and dark play rather important roles in The Bleak Archive. Beams of arcane light are responsible for triggering the various arcane doors via the facility's revolving mirrors, and the Corrupted Cadrithor minions of Tethra Shùl navigate the vault's mundane and magical shadows with supernatural ease.

The beams of arcane light shed dim light in a 5 foot radius. The primary sources of illumination here are the crystal dodecahedrons set within wall-mounted stone sconces throughout the vault. These pale blue crystals shed bright light in a 15 foot radius and dim light in a 30 foot radius.

Terrain

The flagstone floors of the Bleak Archive are crafted from magically-treated slate, and are resistant to all damage types other than the most powerful of magic. The ground here should be treated as normal terrain unless otherwise noted.

The interior walls of the vault are crafted from similar stone. Meanwhile, the grated metallic platform floors located within the @UUID[.gRLQzRFEKVu15Lzp]{Reflector Array} and the @UUID[.KvVDsn3rz90j4xC3]{Eastern Corridor} are crafted from an unknown adamantine alloy.

Elevation

The ceilings within the Bleak Archive are 30 feet high, unless otherwise stated.

In some cases, a pit descends into darkness. These depths are 40 feet deep. Any creature that falls from the main floor or a metallic platform to the pit floor takes [[/damage 4d6 bludgeoning]] damage. suffers a [[/hazard 12 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Serious Fall}. Climbing the pit walls requires a successful [[/skill athletics 16]] [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check.

Mirrors and Walls

A mirror array puzzle located throughout the Bleak Archive is responsible for reflecting two narrow beams of arcane light from the @UUID[.1ZvVg4pODC7wjnxo]{Main Gallery} towards the vault's Inner Sanctum. The beams of light originate from the two crystals mounted on the statue in the Main Gallery, and can be redirected through a series of various passages to eventually reach the @UUID[.k1DMt6QutPVqSxGJ]{Inner Antechamber}, where the two beams in tandem serve as a magical key to the Inner Sanctum.

Each mirror stands 8 feet tall, and can be rotated 360 degrees on a y-axis. The beams of arcane light originate from powerful Shent lunar magic and create dim light in a 5 foot line.

Action Economy

Characters may rotate a mirror once (one single 60-degree turn) using a free object interaction on their turn. They may rotate a single mirror an unlimited number of times by performing the Use an Object action

Light Banishes Evil

Whenever a @UUID[Actor.oNP6JkB5Me8gYrc1]{Corrupted Cadrithor} is struck by one of the beams, it is instantly destroyed — leaving naught but a wisp of tenebrous smoke in its wake.

Other evil creatures with Sunlight Sensitivity who are struck by one of the beams must succeed on a [[/save con 15]] saving throw or take [[/damage 2d10 radiant]] damage.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.cHJSlRXSX9wvV7br]{Vortest Tower}depicts two locations: the bottom floor of the tower as it resides on the Arctus Plateau, and a transdimensional pocket of the Inner Realm of Signara. The tower itself serves as a sort of transporter to and from this transdimensional pocket, which is powered and protected by the otherworldly magic of the Daemos known as Nalgomith.

Characters may journey to Vortest Tower during The Signborn Secret event of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book of Tales}, where they must save the Signborn mage Corvana Vortest from a cohort of Jahud assassins if they wish to earn her favor.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.cHJSlRXSX9wvV7br inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The remote edifice and otherworldly complex known as Vortest Tower serves as one of the primary locations of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book of Tales}, in which the storyteller @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft} has tasked the party with the transcribing of five curious Arcturian stories — including her own.

Vortest Tower is the transdimensional dwelling of the Signborn Mage known as @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0]{Corvana Vortest}, who is trapped in a state of magical suspension in the Master Bedroom of the area when the characters arrive.

Once the characters reach Vortest Tower, they must:

  • Figure out how to travel to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} via the Tower Antechamber's secret trigger — a mechanism disguised as a book located on the chamber's northeastern bookshelf.

  • Journey room-by-room through the complex, activating the lambent arcane bridges necessary to traverse the area while surviving attacks from fiendish assassins known as @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK]{Jahud}, interlopers sent here by the malefic Daemos @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.aTy7db5ZGUnNDVL4]{Kerastes}.

  • Reach the Master Bedroom and save Corvana Vortest, who is caught in a magical state of suspended animation along with a handful of Jahud assassins.

The Signaran Assassins

The Jahud who currently occupy various chambers here are otherworldly invaders from the Inner Realm of Signara. Once these alien intruders are slain, Vortest Tower reverts to a safe location for Corvana Vortest and her allies (including the characters, if they aid Vortest in her struggle).

Illumination

On Ember, illumination here is mostly dependent on the time of day, since the location exterior is fully open to the sky above.

On Signara, the entire area is illuminated with dim light that radiates from the lambent pools of arcane energy that roil in perpetuity below the complex. Additionally, each of the lambent bridges radiates bright light in a 5 foot aura once activated.

Terrain

On Ember, most of the terrain outside the tower is treated as difficult terrain because of the extreme overgrowth and cluttered macabre lawn decoration. The Tower Antechamber and all other rooms of the Signaran complex are treated as normal terrain, except where otherwise noted. The areas surrounding the Signaran complex chambers on the map are situated below them, and are defined by the presence of a translucent arcane miasma that can be traversed using one's mind.

Doors within the complex are made from a similar manifestation of solid arcane light, and are effectively indestructible. Each of these Energy Doors can be opened or closed with an item known as the @UUID[Item.koFSf2ZyCPoBR9Sh]{Jaunt Manipulator}, or via a paired Control Panel. Additionally, each Energy Door can be disabled for [[/roll 1d3 + 1]] hours by casting the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} spell and succeeding on the appropriate spellcasting ability check: [[/check cha 20]], [[/check int 20]], or [[/check wis 20]] (per the spellcaster's class).

  • Unless otherwise stated, each chamber of the complex features a Control Panel inside next to each of its doors.

  • Like regular doors, Energy Doors can be opened or closed as part of a character's Move action.

The various chambers of the Signaran complex are connected by a series of lambent arcane bridges made of solid light, most of which are deactivated when the characters first arrive. These Light Bridges can be activated or deactivated at the same Control Panels that manipulate the Energy Doors.

Elevation

Vortest Tower is situated at ground level on Ember. Meanwhile, the various chambers and lambent bridges of the Signaran pocket section of the location are situated roughly 60 feet above an alien expanse marked by luminous pools of magical energy that release a strange arcane miasma.

Characters who fall from one of the elevated chambers or bridges must succeed on a [[/skill acr 15]] check or a [[/skill ath 15]] check to avoid immediately plummeting into the arcane miasma below.

Navigating the Arcane Miasma

Characters who plummet into the arcane miasma can spend an action on their turn to attempt a [[/skill int 13]] check; success allows them to gain a flying speed of 30 until the beginning of their next turn, which can only be used to traverse the area defined by the arcane miasma. Any character who fails this check can repeat it as many times as they'd like, but can only make the attempt once per turn.

Metaphysics of Signara

The exploration of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3OvueRrGcFnwtnmw]{Signara} can be a disorienting experience for those unaccustomed to its arcane peculiarities. Characters must steel themselves against the potential psychic threats of Signaran entities or enchantments, which present themselves both immediately and over the course of time; and the very fabric of reality is different in Signara, exposing characters to a world both dark and fascinating, full of tenebrous secrets and mind-staggering revelations.

Encounters in Signara are subject to the following metaphysical changes and effects:

  • Signborn characters and characters with Attunement: Signara have @Advantage[2] on Intelligence saving throws.

  • All characters have @Advantage[-2] on saving throws against Illusion magic.

  • Intelligence (Arcana) checks are made with @Advantage[2].

  • Celestial and fey creatures are vulnerable to psychic damage.

Otherworldly Hallucinations of Signara

Any mortal humanoid who spends enough time in Signara — including the transdimensional Signaran pocket accessed by Vortest Tower — is likely to encounter the threat of otherworldly hallucinations.

The first time a character sets foot in the otherworldly realm of Signara and every 4 hours after their arrival, they must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 13]] saving throw or succumb to the effects of Otherworldly Hallucinations.

  • Signborn characters and characters with Attunement: Signara have @Advantage[2] on this saving throw.

  • Characters who succeed on this saving throw are immune to the effects of Otherworldly Hallucinations until the next dusk.

  • The effects of Otherworldly Hallucination last until the character completes a long rest.

Any character who fails this saving throw must roll [[/roll 1d12]] on the following Otherworldly Hallucinations Table once every four hours to determine how the metaphysical psychedelia manifests itself.

  1. Incessant retching makes it quite difficult to function. You gain the Poisoned condition for [[/roll 1d4]] hours.

  2. Psychedelic tracers and phantom noises surround you. You have @Advantage[-2] on Wisdom (Perception) checks.

  3. You hear a stirring music in your head, and feel compelled to hum or sing its rousing melody. You have @Advantage[-2] on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

  4. Your skin itches terribly, and you can't help but scratch it. You lose [[/roll 1d2]] hit points every hour from self-inflicted abrasions.

  5. Illusory patterns of light emanate from every magical item or effect you behold. You have @Advantage[-2] on concentration checks made for spellcasting.

  6. You feel incredibly thirsty, and nothing tastes clean or safe to consume.

  7. The sound of your own voice feels deafening. You speak in whispers to avoid being heard.

  8. You believe your skin has grown sensitive to bright light, and you stick to the shadows to avoid contact.

  9. You become irrationally afraid or superstitious of your own weapons, and are reluctant to use them.

  10. You're convinced that your fellow party members are up to no good. You can hear their conspiratorial conversations in your mind.

  11. You can see fractal patterns in everything you behold. You have @Advantage[2] on Wisdom (Perception) checks and @Advantage[-2] on Intelligence (Investigation) checks.

  12. A feeling of euphoria washes over you. You have @Advantage[2] on Charisma saving throws.

Tower Antechamber.name: Tower Antechamber
Tower Antechamber.text:
The southeastern gate of Vortest Tower welcomes you into a single circular chamber whose tall ceiling stretches into darkness. A round table made of some curious stone sits at the center of the room, surrounded by eight chairs padded in strange blue leather; in the middle of this table, a small round fire pit crackles with softly-glowing azure embers.

An assortment of other furniture decorates the tower chamber, all of it somewhat esoteric to your eyes and made from an peculiar ash-colored wood — as if the style and structures were inspired by a foreign culture you can't readily place.

The Tower Antechamber has been decorated to look like the sparse and esoteric dwelling of a hermetic spellcaster. In fact, it serves as an ersatz waiting room for Corvana's would-be guests, and is actually an arcane method of otherworldly travel that can transport characters to a remotely-contained pocket of the Inner Realm of Signara.

The method of using this arcane transportation is hidden among the chamber's book-laden shelves to the northeast, where one peculiar tome conceals a lever used to activate the otherworldly transportation device.

Searching the Antechamber

Characters who use the Search action to explore the room and its contents notice the following after a few moments of examination:

  • The table at the center of the room is made of a petrified version of the same ash-colored wood the rest of the furniture is crafted from. The enchanted azure embers that glow in the fire pit burn with no heat, but do regulate the temperature of the chamber to remain a calm 70° Fahrenheit; the coals radiate dim light in a 10 foot radius.

  • The potted plants that decorate the western wall are especially curious, and don't resemble any flora the characters have seen on the surface of Ember.

  • The eastern bookshelf is stocked with a collection of tomes related to the academic study of various esoteric subjects, including: mythical creatures of Ember, anecdotes and essays on the Pathways, and voluminous encyclopedias regarding the world's flora and fauna. Whenever a character attempts to remove any of these tomes from the Tower Antechamber, the books magically disappear from the character's possession and reappear on the shelves in their original location.

  • The northeastern bookshelf is lined with a collection of tomes — written in a variety of languages — that pertain to the cosmos, Signaran history, and the afterlife. As with the other bookshelf, whenever a character attempts to remove any of these tomes from the Tower Antechamber, the books magically disappear from the character's possession and reappear on the shelves in their original location.

  • The dark gray stone that comprises the walls and tiled floors of the antechamber is fascinating in its own right, and shines with a luster that seems almost enchanted; it's as if the veins of mineral ore in the stone are ever-so-subtly and perpetually moving.

The following skill checks can illuminate more information about this search:

[[/check his 15]]. The character is able to identify the origin of the furniture as Signaran in both material and design, and notes the particular presence of aged and rarified tomes on the northeastern bookshelf — recognized by the archaic modes of language used in their text. Craftsperson characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

[[/check nat 15]]. The character can identify the plants as Signaran in origin. Agrimage Apprentice characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

[[/check sur 13]]. Faint footprints of one or more medium-sized creatures with taloned, three-toed feet can be found throughout the room, with a distinct terminus at the northeastern bookshelf along with comings and goings from the Front Gate. A Ranger whose favored enemy is Fiends has @Advantage[2] on this check, and can identify the tracks as fiendish in nature.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check prc 13]] check while searching the bookshelves is able to locate the presence of a Curious Tome on the northeastern shelf, labeled "House Vortest" in Eonic like the one in the relief on the front gate. This check can be repeated.

The Curious Tome

The Curious Tome labeled "House Vortest" is actually not a tome at all, but rather a lever used to activate the transdimensional magic ascribed to the Tower Antechamber. Characters who take a closer look at the Curious Tome note the following text written in Common upon its spine:

A House's Creed is Its Compass.

Pulling on the book while speaking House Vortest's creed — "Enlightenment And Beyond" — activates the Curious Tome and results in immediate Transport to Signara (see below). Pulling on the book without speaking the House Vortest creed has no result, and the book is magically immovable.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/check inv 13]] check while searching the bookshelves is able to locate an aged tome labeled "Heraldry of Signara," which details the House Vortest creed (among others). Obsidian Researcher characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Alternately, any character who succeeds on a [[/check his 18]] check is able to recall the House Vortest creed from previous study of famous mages of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Additionally, any character who consults the Stonecraft Manuscript is able to find a curious new passage in the otherwise blank section of "The Signborn's Secret" that mentions the creed.

Transport to Signara

Once the characters have activated the Curious Tome, read the following aloud:

The entire tower begins to shudder and shake as the room grows dark. Arcane runes start to glow beneath your feet, casting narrow beams of a bright blue light up towards the umbral ceiling. The entire front gate begins to glow with a similar azure brilliance, and — to your amazement — two matching doors of soft blue light appear at opposite intervals around the room.

Your head swells with nauseating discombobulation, and a moment later you come to your senses … Where the front gate once stood, an open portal to what seems like another world awaits; beyond, a bridge made of pure blue light stretches out to another platformed chamber.

Meanwhile, the two new doors of blue light remain, revealing more of this remarkable otherworldly terrain on the other sides of their translucent arcane thresholds; a bewildering landscape marked by luminous azure enchantment and shimmering darkness.

All characters located inside the Tower Antechamber when the Curious Tome is activated are transported to a remote pocket of Signara, where the eight-chamber sprawl of the Vortest Tower complex is connected by a series of arcane bridges made of solid, indestructible light.

Opening the Energy Doors

The two new doors located at even intervals around the antechamber can only be opened from other chambers or devices located throughout the transdimensional complex:

  • The door to the west can be opened by a panel located on a wall in the Western Causeway.

  • The door to the north can be opened by a panel located on a wall in the Northern Sitting Room.

  • Alternately, the @UUID[Item.koFSf2ZyCPoBR9Sh]{Jaunt Manipulator} can open or close all three doors.

The Front Gate now stands wide open, wreathed in a halo of blue light that matches the luminance of the other doors.

Returning to Ember

Once the Curious Tome has been activated and the Tower Antechamber has transported the characters to Signara, they cannot return to the Arctus Plateau without first resetting the transdimensional mechanism via the Jaunt Manipulator device located in the Master Bedroom with Corvana Vortest herself.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
This cozy circular chamber appears to house a kitchen and dining room area. A small amount of food remains forgotten on the table — including rancid tea in silver receptacles, a brown and rotted sliced pear on a small plate, and a loaf of bread covered in a fuzzy veneer of viridian mold. A solitary teacup sits on the table, suggesting that whoever once dined here was doing it alone.

A sweet smell of decay wafts towards you from the opposite side of the room, where a metal stove is surrounded by crates of spoiled food.

This 30-foot diameter chamber serves as a kitchen and dining room area for Vortest Tower, and is equipped with a stove range, storage cabinets and crates, and an engraved table made of fine petrified ashwood.

The food on the table appears half-eaten and has started to rot. Similarly, other food found in the storage areas near the stove — like produce and bread — has also gone bad. This room currently reflects a state of normalcy that was interrupted when the Jahud infiltrated the Tower, and the questionable span of time that has passed in the interim.

Examining the Kitchen

Characters who attempt to Search the kitchen note the following:

  • The pots and pans scattered on the stove top appear to have been quickly abandoned, and contain the rotted ingredients of a meal that was prepared but never cooked.

  • Some of the rotted foods and ingredients are curious and strange compared to standard Arcturian cuisine.

A successful [[/check inv 13]] or [[/check per 13]] check allows a character to detect that some of the foodstuffs and cutlery is in a state of disarray, suggesting that the contents of the room were quickly searched and rifled through.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check sur 15]] check is able to discover evidence of footprints that match those found in the Tower Antechamber, which seem to belong to one or more medium-sized creatures with taloned, three-toed feet. The dust here is less evident than the previous chamber, and the tracks appear to travel from the northwestern door into the chamber, where they circle about before heading westward out of the room. A Ranger whose favored enemy is Fiends has @Advantage[2] on this check, and can identify the tracks as fiendish in nature.

Although much of the food in the kitchen area has rotted, characters who wish to pilfer the pantry are able to salvage [[/roll 2d4]] days worth of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.f4w4GxBi0nYXmhX4]{Rations} each.

Southern Sitting Room.name: Southern Sitting Room
Southern Sitting Room.text:
This small circular sitting room is decorated with a padded sofa and a hefty stone pot holding a curious plum-colored plant. Much of the floor here is transparent, and seems to be crafted from some kind of durable glass or crystal, permitting one to sit and view the arcane splendor that swirls beneath this sprawling, otherworldly complex.

This unassuming chamber serves a variety of roles — from a sitting room, to an isolated study, or an observation deck. An azure rug detailed with golden line-work adorns the floor at the center of the chamber, and can be removed at leisure.

When the characters arrive, the Energy Doors at the eastern and western edges of the chamber are deactivated and open.

Examining the Sitting Room

Characters who attempt to Search the southern sitting room note the following:

  • The padded sofa's frame is constructed from fine ashwood, and the textiles used in its padding are exquisite; it is readily apparent that this couch is slightly more posh and preserved than the similar furniture in the Tower Antechamber.

  • The strange potted plant here is similar to those found in the Tower Antechamber. However, this plant appears more vibrant, and emits a soft electrostatic hum.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check nat 14]] or [[/check arc 14]] check is able to discern that the plant's perpetual proximity to Signara keeps it infused with latent enchantment that is otherwise missing from the antechamber flora.

  • Result of 17+: The character is able to identify the plant as a Drakehead Fern. When the plant is healthy and present in Signara, @UUID[Item.ssFZuI6v5OmfIoMw]{Drakehead Spores} can be harvested from its otherworldly leaves and used as an alternative for any plant-based material spell component.

The first character to succeeds on a [[/skill survival 13]] check is able to harvest [[/roll 1d2 + 1]] units of @UUID[Item.ssFZuI6v5OmfIoMw]{Drakehead Spores} from the fern. After the spores are harvested, it takes 30 days for them to regrow.

Living Quarters.name: Living Quarters
Living Quarters.text:
This oblong chamber appears to be some kind of den or living quarters, as suggested by the sprawl of comfortable furniture, a pair of lovingly cluttered bookshelves, and an adjoining room. An air of leisure pervades this chamber, which is sealed off by a door made of solid, lapis-colored energy.

The Living Quarters here consist of a collection of three smaller chambers, including a Den, a Guest Bedroom, and a Guest Bathroom.

Once the characters open the doors to this area, they'll be attacked by two Jahud assassins from the realm of Signara, who've been sent here to slay Corvana Vortest and extract the item known as the Orphic Reliquary for their Daemos master Kerastes. Unfortunately for the Jahud, several chambers of Vortest Tower — including this one — were outfitted with powerful temporal traps, and the fiends are currently incapacitated in a state of suspended animation.

The party's timely arrival to the chamber inadvertently deactivates the temporal trap, and releases the Jahud — who leap into action and attack.

Opening the Energy Doors

The two Energy Doors that lead to the Living Quarters den are closed and locked, and can be opened via the following methods in addition to those described in @UUID[JournalEntry.tdpdWJgLONFmRPKI]{Gameplay Details}:

  • An exterior Control Panel is located on the rightmost column next to these doors, which features a luminous touch pad in the shape of a five-fingered humanoid hand. Any character who is an ally to Corvana Vortest, including the party members, can gain entry by placing their hand upon the touch pad and speaking the House Vortest creed as featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.tdpdWJgLONFmRPKI.JournalEntryPage.oHcWGpU9pAuvskJ1]{Tower Antechamber}: "Enlightenment and Beyond.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/check prc 14]] check is able to locate a crack in the stonework left of the eastern door large enough to allow a Tiny or smaller-sized creature to enter the bedroom section of the Living Quarters. Larger creatures cannot squeeze through this crack, but alternative methods of travel — such as the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.wqfAVANuQonNBgnL]{Misty Step} spell — can be applied.

Spotting the Assassins

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check prc 17]] check while peering through the lapis translucence of the closed Energy Door is able to notice the 2 Jahud assassins lurking inside, who were attempting to furtively sneak through the den when the temporal trap captured them.

@Embed[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK count=2]

Suspended Animation

2 @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK]{Jahud} lurk here in a state of suspended animation caused by the magic of a temporal trap located in the Living Quarters. The trap has already been triggered and cannot be reset by the characters.

This state of suspended animation ends as soon as the doors to the chamber are opened, releasing the Jahud — who emerge from the temporal suspension relatively ignorant of the reason for party's arrival, but generally aware of the threat they pose to the mission for Kerastes.

Jahud Tactics

Once combat begins, the Jahud will begin by targeting multiple characters with their @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.m7lbBW96pDxIrHqN]{Plasma Ray} attacks before closing in to engage the party in melee. In melee, each Jahud makes use of its @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.Dg3lskenea8pFw2I]{Multiattack} to attempt @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.qjliQmgUMeu0j23I]{Signaran Dagger} and @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.Lb7pwESJqDlgcICs]{Bladed Bracer} attacks against an individual target until that target is rendered unconscious.

The Jahud fight to the death in service of their interplanar mission for Kerastes, eager to continue their relentless pursuit of Corvana Vortest.

Examining the Living Quarters

Characters who use an action to Search the Living Quarters will be able to discover the following:

  • The furniture is mostly crafted of petrified ashwood and appears posh and well-kept, if somewhat dusty and ignored.

  • The bookshelves are lined with a variety of mythological tomes and keepsakes. Any character who spends at least 5 minutes to search the shelves more extensively will find [[/roll 2d2]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Books} with eccentric titles, and can roll twice on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} table.

  • The tome on the lectern to the north is an aged book of otherworldly fairy tales written in Eonic labeled "Veerad's Fables." It sits open to two dusty pages featuring a story called "The Fletcher and the Fiend," which has no apparent connection to the events at hand. Any character who takes the 15 minutes necessary to read this story gains @Advantage[2] on skill checks made to identify the Jahud or their motives.

  • The potted plants here, while native to Signara, are relatively mundane.

  • The door to the Bedroom section of the Living Quarters is unlocked. The Bedroom is dusty and neglected, and the dresser cabinet on the southern wall is empty, save for a half-dozen coat hangers and one set of .

  • The door to the Bathroom section of the Living Quarters is unlocked. The Bathroom is clean and well-kept. The facilities are made with semi-enchanted plumbing technology that conjures potable water and allows waste to be expelled to an unknown location.

Western Sitting Room.name: Western Sitting Room
Western Sitting Room.text:
A bench and chair adorn this modest sitting room, which faces the Tower Antechamber from a door-sized opening to the east. A lush, plum-colored plant sits next to the chair, which exudes the pleasant scent of ozone from its large lavender leaves.

This sitting room resembles the Southern Sitting Room in most regards, but features a 15-foot floor extension that also serves as a causeway between the Living Quarters and the Workshop. The azure rug that adorns the floor at the center of the chamber features a detail golden line-work, and can be removed at leisure.

When the characters arrive, the Energy Doors to the north and south of the chamber are activated and closed. A Control Panel in this chamber opens the westernmost door to the Tower Antechamber.

Examining the Sitting Room

Characters who attempt to Search the western sitting room note the following:

  • The bench and chair are constructed from fine ashwood, and the textiles used in their padding are exquisite.

  • The strange potted plant here is similar to those found elsewhere in the complex. It appears vibrant and emits a soft electrostatic hum, along with a distinct odor of ozone.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check nat 14]] or [[/check arc 14]] check is able to discern that the plant's perpetual proximity to Signara keeps it infused with latent enchantment.

  • Result of 17+: The character is able to identify the plant as a Terra Tree. When the plant is healthy and present in Signara, Terra Trees can purify the air in a 30-foot radius, making it cleaner and more pleasant — and ultimately more reminiscent of the atmosphere on Ember and its chemical components (or lack thereof).

The first character to succeeds on a [[/skill survival 13]] check is able to harvest [[/roll 1d4 + 1]] matured units of @UUID[Item.wq7vlgRbDhfczoqA]{Terra Tree Leaves} from the fern. After the leaves are harvested, it takes 30 days for them to regrow.

Workshop.name: Workshop
Workshop.text:
The chamber here seems to be some kind of study or storage room, as suggested by the expanse of shelves that line the western wall, along with another smaller shelf to the northeast — all of them stocked with a dusty array of books and jars full of dried goods. Most of the floor here appears to be made of glass, and the azure glow of Signara below shines up into the room through its pellucid surface.

This L-shaped corner chamber serves as Corvana Vortest's arcane workshop, and hosts three smaller rooms and a wedge-shaped storage closet within its walls. These smaller rooms include a Front Room stocked with tomes and components, a Workstation equipped with esoteric accoutrements, and a Forge fitted with an anvil and blacksmith's tools.

Once the characters open the doors to this area, they'll be attacked by a total of three Jahud assassins, one of which lurks unseen in the Forge. Unfortunately for the Jahud, the chamber's temporal trap has incapacitated them, and they remain in a state of suspended animation.

As with the Living Quarters, the party's timely arrival to the chamber inadvertently deactivates the temporal trap, and releases the Jahud — who leap into action and attack.

Opening the Energy Doors

The two Energy Doors that lead to the Living Quarters den are closed and locked, and can be opened via the following methods in addition to those described in @UUID[JournalEntry.tdpdWJgLONFmRPKI]{Gameplay Details}:

  • An exterior Control Panel is located on the rightmost column next to these doors, which features a luminous touch pad in the shape of a five-fingered humanoid hand. Any character who is an ally to Corvana Vortest, including the party members, can gain entry by placing their hand upon the touch pad and speaking the House Vortest creed as featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.tdpdWJgLONFmRPKI.JournalEntryPage.oHcWGpU9pAuvskJ1]{Tower Antechamber}: "Enlightenment and Beyond.
