  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/check prc 15]] check while surveying the Workshop exterior is able to locate an extremely narrow flume on the rooftop above the Forge that is large enough to allow a Tiny or smaller-sized creature to enter. Larger creatures cannot squeeze through this crack, but alternative methods of travel — such as the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.wqfAVANuQonNBgnL]{Misty Step} spell — can be applied.

Spotting the Assassins

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check prc 17]] check while peering through the lapis translucence of the closed Energy Door is able to notice 2 of the Jahud assassins lurking inside, who were attempting to furtively sneak through the front room when the temporal trap captured them. The 3rd Jahud is well out of sight, and can only be perceived by supernatural means from outside the Workshop.

Suspended Animation

3 @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK]{Jahud} lurk here in a state of suspended animation caused by the magic of a temporal trap located in the Living Quarters. The trap has already been triggered and cannot be reset by the characters.

This state of suspended animation ends as soon as the doors to the chamber are opened, releasing the Jahud — who emerge from the temporal suspension relatively ignorant of the reason for party's arrival, but generally aware of the threat they pose to the mission for Kerastes.

Jahud Tactics

Once combat begins, the 2 Jahud in the front room will begin by targeting multiple characters with their @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.m7lbBW96pDxIrHqN]{Plasma Ray} attacks before closing in to engage the party in melee. In melee, each Jahud makes use of its @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.Dg3lskenea8pFw2I]{Multiattack} to attempt @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.qjliQmgUMeu0j23I]{Signaran Dagger} and @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.Lb7pwESJqDlgcICs]{Bladed Bracer} attacks against an individual target until that target is rendered unconscious.

Meanwhile, the 3rd Jahud located in the Forge will cast the @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.LTyRhOPQuHId8dWH]{Invisibility} spell and attempt to use their @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.AFWninogtcHHeuIB]{Sneak Attack} on one of the characters from an unseen vantage point.

The Jahud fight to the death in service of their interplanar mission for Kerastes, eager to continue their relentless pursuit of Corvana Vortest.

Examining the Workshop

Characters who use an action to Search the Workshop will be able to discover the following:

  • The bookshelves in the Front Room are lined with a variety of encyclopedic tomes and dried goods. Any character who spends at least 5 minutes to search the shelves more extensively will find [[/roll 2d2]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Books} of lore related to Signara and the arcane.

  • The dried goods on the shelves in the Front Room — from jars of desiccated insects, to vials of granulated mineral ore, and everything in between — can be identified with a successful [[/check arc 13]] check as an array of spell components. Per Gamemaster discretion, any character who succeeds on an additional [[/check prc 15]] check can find almost any material component for an arcane spell of 3rd Level or lower in their list of known spells, but only if that component doesn't have a gp value associated with it.

  • The doors to the Workstation and Forge areas are unlocked.

  • The two desks in the Workstation area are bedecked with several projects in various stages of examination or completion. The majority of these tools and components are inscrutable to anyone other than Corvana Vortest, but any character who spends a few moments to search the area finds a set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.0d08g1i5WXnNrCNA]{Tinker's Tools} and a set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.YfBwELTgPFHmQdHh]{Jeweler's Tools} among the assortment, along with a random @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinket}.

  • The Forge area is stocked with an anvil and enough equipment for 2 sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.KndVe2insuctjIaj]{Smith's Tools}.

  • The vibrant potted plant in the Front Room is a Drakehead Fern (which can be harvested for @UUID[Item.ssFZuI6v5OmfIoMw]{Drakehead Spores}), as featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.tdpdWJgLONFmRPKI.JournalEntryPage.X1zxCgs3pGfMvXm6]{Southern Sitting Room}.

Northern Sitting Room.name: Northern Sitting Room
Northern Sitting Room.text:
This glass-floored chamber features a variety of furniture for lounging and relaxation, from an assortment of individual chairs to a lush, pleated lounge sofa. A trio of bookshelves adorn the walls, lined with what appear to be the fanciful titles of various works of fiction, written in a countless variety of languages. The southern threshold of this chamber faces the Tower Antechamber to the south, nearly close enough for one to reach out and touch it.

This large circular chamber serves as Corvana Vortest's most frequented sitting room, and boasts one of the facility's largest transparent floors — allowing those who lounge here to lavishly bask in the majesty of Signara's terrain as they study or sit.

A Control Panel in this chamber opens the northernmost door to the Tower Antechamber.

Examining the Sitting Room

Characters who attempt to Search the western sitting room note the following:

  • The furniture constructed from fine ashwood, and the textiles used in their padding are exquisite.

  • The potted plants here, while native to Signara, are relatively mundane.

  • The books that line the shelves are mostly works of fiction; an assortment of interesting titles can be found, written in nearly every language known to Emberites, but they offer relatively little in terms of gainful knowledge or revelations about the matter at hand.

Any character that succeeds on a [[/check prc 13]] check while searching the shelves is able to locate a @UUID[Item.BWiF73we37qDj9VJ]{Spell Scroll of Detect Magic} folded into the pages of a book labeled "Warlocks at the Gate."

Primary Bedroom.name: Primary Bedroom
Primary Bedroom.text:
This edifice appears to host a primary bedroom adjoined by a glass-floored foyer. Therein, behind the lapis glow and electrostatic thrum of an energy door, a four-armed figure appears frozen in suspended animation, locked in timeless combat with a trio of fiendish assailants who approach her with a fixed and petrified ferocity — their weapons raised in motionless aggression.

This area serves as the Primary Bedroom of Vortest Tower, and contains the Bedroom, an adjoining Bathroom, and a Foyer — where Corvana Vortest is trapped in suspended animation along with two Jahud assassins, thanks to the effects of a temporal trap.

Once the characters open the door to this area, combat between Corvana and the Jahud will begin, with the party caught up in the mix. The characters must help Corvana survive the attack and explain their reason for being here if they wish to gain her allegiance.

Opening the Energy Doors

The Energy Door that leads to the Primary Bedroom's Foyer is closed and locked, and can be opened via the following methods in addition to those described in @UUID[JournalEntry.tdpdWJgLONFmRPKI]{Gameplay Details}:

  • An exterior Control Panel is located on the rightmost column next to the door, which features a luminous touch pad in the shape of a five-fingered humanoid hand. Any character who is an ally to Corvana Vortest, including the party members, can gain entry by placing their hand upon the touch pad and speaking the House Vortest creed as featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.tdpdWJgLONFmRPKI.JournalEntryPage.oHcWGpU9pAuvskJ1]{Tower Antechamber}: "Enlightenment and Beyond."

@Embed[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0]

@Embed[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK count=3]

Suspended Animation

The 3 @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK]{Jahud} here and @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0]{Corvana Vortest} are all in a state of suspended animation caused by the magic of a temporal trap. The trap has already been triggered and cannot be reset by the characters.

This state of suspended animation ends as soon as the doors to the chamber are opened, releasing Corvana and the Jahud — who all emerge from the temporal suspension relatively ignorant of the reason for party's arrival. The characters will need to act fast if they wish to convince Corvana of the veracity of their cause.

Jahud Tactics

Once the temporal suspension is released, 2 of the Jahud here will focus their attacks on Corvana Vortest in an attempt to slay her and take the Orphic Reliquary. One Jahud will attempt to grapple Corvana and utilize its @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.QRirlSSUHZXEqCfu]{Penumbral Hide}, while the other makes use of its @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.Dg3lskenea8pFw2I]{Multiattack} to attempt @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.qjliQmgUMeu0j23I]{Signaran Dagger} and @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.Lb7pwESJqDlgcICs]{Bladed Bracer} attacks. When and if the party intervenes, one of these Jahud will break away to engage the intervening characters in melee.

Meanwhile, the 3rd Jahud located here will cast @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.To7Dbcv7IOrDfrzx]{Darkness} upon the area in the first round of combat. In the following round, it will target one or more of the party members with its @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.m7lbBW96pDxIrHqN]{Plasma Ray}, focusing efforts on spellcasters or the first characters to join the others in melee.

The Jahud fight to the death in service of their interplanar mission for Kerastes, eager to continue their relentless pursuit of Corvana Vortest.

Corvana's Tactics

When combat begins, Corvana will either attempt to cast @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0.Item.qDQfBzMWQjur5V1B]{Banishment} on one of the Jahud in the first round, or position herself to cast @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0.Item.KpxMKg3HZkPfwOCQ]{Lightning Bolt} at one or more of the fiends (based on the location of the party when they arrive). If one of the Jahud casts @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK.Item.To7Dbcv7IOrDfrzx]{Darkness} on the area, Corvana will attempt to prevent it via @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0.Item.AkHOuRTa7581Rz9I]{Counterspell} or remove it via @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0.Item.lTA3padSQP9WhEJP]{Dispel Magic}.

Meeting Corvana Vortest

After combat, the party must adequately explain the reason for their visit if they desire the Signborn mage's hard-earned trust. If the characters are forthcoming and honest with their answers (and prove to her that they don't pose any threats), Corvana will most likely oblige them with answers to any questions they might have.

Are you Corvana Vortest?

Well met, visitor. I am Corvana Vortest, and this is my home — a place usually reserved for intimates and my thoughts alone. I truly appreciate your intervention with the Jahud, but I hope your visit is one with purpose.

About the Jahud

Those malevolent fiends are assassins from the Inner Realm of Signara, sent to slay me and plunder the tower. Fortunately, they were unsuccessful in these endeavors.

About Vortest Tower & Signara

I see you managed to make your way into the heart of the facility … Welcome to my own little pocket of Signara, friend. Vortest Tower has served as a conduit to the inner realm for generations, and I am merely the latest to steward this place and its responsibilities. Tell me: have you come in search of spells? Or portents, perhaps? What, precisely, do you desire?

Returning to Ember

The journey back to the Arctus Plateau is a mere trifle.

Corvana produces a small metallic cylinder from her pocket, adorned with crystalline buttons full of scintillating light.

The Jaunt Manipulator allows me to control the facility's accoutrements. Once you're ready to leave, I'll help you see your way back to the antechamber, where we'll all make the trip back to Ember.

If the party has come here in search of Corvana Vortest's story for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book of Tales}, additional details about the mage's tale can be found in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000.JournalEntryPage.QwGONBUR04vwnj8k]{The Signborn's Secret} event.

Examining the Bedroom

Characters who use an action to Search the Primary Bedroom will be able to discover the following:

  • The furniture throughout is crafted of petrified ashwood and appears posh, well-kept, and well-used.

  • The Foyer area contains a small wardrobe cabinet, a modest bookshelf, and a potted Signaran plant. An Arcturian wicker basket sits near the front door, used for the impromptu storage of gloves and boots.

  • The Bedroom area is lavishly comfortable and well-decorated, adorned with a variety of ashwood furniture. It's easy to tell that the room feels only half lived-in, as if Corvana spends much of her time elsewhere (such as the confines of the Workshop).

  • The door to the Bathroom section of the Primary Bedroom is unlocked. The Bathroom is clean and well-kept. The facilities are made with semi-enchanted plumbing technology that conjures potable water and allows waste to be expelled to an unknown location.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check prc 18]] check while searching the Bedroom is able to find a hidden lockbox in the vanity containing Corvana Vortest's most valuable personal effects and heirlooms, which include:

  • 3 @UUID[Item.TKinFp8DoVau7DPY]{Signaran Opals} worth 100 gp each.

  • A @UUID[Item.EDGQMnXjEvAz7Y3H]{House Vortest Signet Ring} worth 50 gp.

  • A hollow obsidian pendant containing the ashes of a dead lover.

Corvana does not take kindly to anyone who would defile the sanctity of her private chambers, and will react accordingly to sneak-thieves and cutpurses.

Front Gate.name: Front Gate
Front Gate.text:
An artistic relief depicting a cloaked four-armed mage surrounded by embellishments of arcane splendor decorates the tower's main gate. The figure at the center of the relief studies a grimoire with intensity, and a phrase written in an obscure language appears to be etched upon the tome's stony cover.

Entering the Tower

The first time the characters arrive at Vortest Tower, the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000.JournalEntryPage.QwGONBUR04vwnj8k]{The Signborn's Secret} are in-progress, and the integrity of the front gate's security measures have been compromised.

Unbeknownst to the party, the tower has very recently been infiltrated by a gang of fiendish @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK]{Jahud} assassins, who sundered the locking mechanisms and protective magics used to keep the gate secure. The Jahud lurk elsewhere, and the broken lock seems to be the only clue they've left behind.

Read the following aloud once the party gets close enough to the front gate to survey the damage:

The front gate stands ever-so-slightly ajar, and the intricate mechanism that once served as the door's handle appears to have been rent in twain by the supremely keen edge of some blade or claw, allowing you to enter the tower remarkably unimpeded.

Examining the Door

Characters within 5 feet of the door can use the Search action to note the following:

  • The door is effectively unlocked and stands ready to open wider.

  • Upon closer inspection, the mage featured in the bas-relief appears to be a Signborn femme.

  • Characters who understand Eonic are able to identify the obscure language written on the tome in the relief as Eonic. It reads: "House Vortest."

  • The amethyst-hued alloy the door appears to be made from is unlike any metal or ore the characters have seen.

Characters can determine the Signaran origin of this alloy with a successful [[/check arc 16]] check or a successful [[/check nat 18]] check.

A successful [[/check prc 13]] check or a successful [[/check inv 13]] check reveals some additional details about the lock and the damage that has recently occurred to it:

  • The metal used in the creation of the lock appears to be adamantine or an alloy of it.

  • The damage to the lock was caused by the blade of a similar substance, if not one more naturally (or supernaturally) durable.

  • Any tracks left by the vandal have been worn away by time and weather. It's hard to tell precisely how long ago this occurred, but it must have been at least a week or two.

Once they're ready to enter the tower, the characters can simply open the compromised door and proceed.

Return Visits

Following the successful conclusion of The Signborn's Secret event of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book of Tales} side quest, Corvana Vortest will quickly take steps to repair the locking mechanisms on the front gate. The front gate is sealed with locks both magical and mechanical, and its "normal" conditions from now on are detailed below.

Examining the Door

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check prc 13]] check while examining the door and its locking mechanism is able to tell the following:

  • The embellishments surrounding the mage in the relief have been augmented, and appear to feature a peculiar assortment of arcane glyphs.

  • The locking mechanisms and the door handle are made of freshly-forged adamantine.

A successful [[/check arc 16]] check allows a character to ascertain that the arcane glyphs mean "secure" and "slumber."

A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} spell reveals the presence of powerful abjuration and enchantment magic on the door.

  • A powerful @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.8cse7rit0oswRPUP]{Arcane Lock} spell has been cast upon the door by Nalgomith. The password for this arcane lock is the phrase "knowledge unbound" spoken in Eonic.

  • The front gate has also been trapped with a powerful enchantment dubbed the "Sleep of Ages" (see below).

In order to open the door without the password, a successful [[/check dex 20]] check with thieves' tools is required to pick the lock, and the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} spell must be cast on the door with a successful spellcasting ability check: [[/check cha 20]], [[/check int 20]], or [[/check wis 20]] (per the spellcaster's class).

Sleep of Ages Trap

Any character who attempts to pick the lock of the front gate without speaking the Arcane Lock's password becomes the target of a powerful @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.KhwiSi9fwVfUPtku]{Sleep} spell, and must succeed on a [[/check wis 20]] saving throw to avoid its effects.

  • This unique Sleep spell has a duration of 12 hours.

  • A creature is affected by the spell regardless of their Hit Point total.

  • Creatures that don't sleep are still subject to the effects of this spell.

  • The magical sleep induced by this spell doesn't count as a long rest, and doesn't satisfy the criteria necessary for the recovery of hit dice, hit points, or spell slots.

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The following gameplay features apply to the entire Aedir Signalpost area unless stated otherwise in a specific room description.

Elevation

Ceilings within the tower are generally 40 feet high unless otherwise noted.

Illumination

The Entry, Basement, and Underforge areas of the Signalpost are entirely dark except for the presence of a few remaining flickering lights which produce dim illumination. The Top level is outdoors and subject to the illumination level of the surface world.

The interior lighting of the Signalpost will be repaired if the generator in the @UUID[.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4]{Secret Basement Room} is recharged and reactivated. In this case, the area is entirely illuminated by bright light.

Terrain

While the ground of the Signalpost is in disrepair, it should be treated as normal terrain unless otherwise noted.

Enemies

There are several adversaries of note within the tower:

  1. In the upper levels, packs of @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvet} burrow and scavenge.

  2. A @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]{Suarrok Juvenile} nests upon the tower roof.

  3. A @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v]{Broken Aedir Sentinel} survives and guards the Underforge.

Translating Towyr

Throughout the tower, the party will encounter writings in Towyr, the language used by the Aedir. Due to the incorporation of some of these words into modern Common, it may be possible for characters to understand their basic meaning: throughout the tower, texts that can be translated are presented in a table, with the words that can be identified in the text on the left and the fully translated meaning on the right, as seen below:

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

Simplified words or concepts that can be extracted from the text.

Full translated text known to anyone who speaks or properly translates from ancient Towyr.

Understanding Towyr

Characters who speak [[/language towyr]] or use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplComprehend]{Comprehend Languages} spell [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.versatileTransla]] talent achieve a full translation.

Characters who can understand [[/language common]] can interpret the basic meaning of a passage of text by making a successful [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] check.

  • Failure: Translation of a passage may not be re-attempted until the party successfully translates some other passage of text that shares certain key words in common.

If the party fails on a translation attempt, read the following to help explain how they might improve their chances:

Try as you might, you cannot quite make sense of the words in front of you. The roots of Common in ancient Towyr are too distant and tenuous for you to make sense of, and there is not enough to work with. If you were able to successfully translate some other passages you might be able to identify certain words in common.

The Secret Room

The secret @UUID[.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4]{Generator Room} contains the power source for the tower and can be opened only by activating 4 levers hidden throughout the tower:

  1. Embedded in the chess board in the @UUID[.FgHIm1VCjV3NJuxV].

  2. Attached to the bed within the empty @UUID[.ErF4VR5n7Nel3zFF].

  3. In the @UUID[.lwhzDpQvSO6BO4nX] workshop.

  4. Hidden within a bookshelf in @UUID[.O7FXBvoQmrlp8IDf].

The following clues to the locations of these levers can be discovered:

  1. A sketch of the basement that includes the Generator Room in @UUID[.4T3mt9zYLyiqlafI].

  2. Notes from Golarne that emphasize the word power, found in each room where a lever is located.

Activating the Levers

If characters activate a single lever, but have not activated all 4 of them, they hear a click, but nothing else.

A quiet click echoes from nearby. In the distance, somewhere in the tower, a gear creakily turns for a moment and then goes silent.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]]check knows the general direction of the grinding stone (if not on the basement level, they know if it is above or below them, and if on the basement level, they know which direction it is from them).

The door to this chamber now stands halfway open. Tiny creatures can enter the room while it is in this state. Any character who makes a successful [[/skill athletics 16]] [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check forces the door the rest of the way open. Alternatively, the characters can use a @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flask} to blow the door open.

If characters have activated all 4 levers, the sound of dragging is heard again, and this secret chamber is now fully opened.

The gear clicks, and not only does a distant gear turn, but you hear the groaning, scraping sound of marble against rock followed by a louder final fastening of some ancient mechanism. You may have found what you are looking for.

Entrance Alcove.name: Entrance Alcove
Entrance Alcove.text:
Two large metal doors stand recessed within a pair of entrance alcoves. If they were locked at some point, time has worn away whatever kept them closed — you can see spiderwebs and pieces of greenery growing through the cracks between them.

A Dark Entryway

The doors from the front swing inward and open easily, without lock or bar.

The heavy stone doors of the tower swing inward with surprisingly little effort. You peer within the gloom of the tower's interior. It is dark and empty, exuding a sense of long abandonment.

Regarding Traps

This area introduces one of the first traps in Ember's explorable Area Maps. As a Gamemaster, you will see a red rectangle on your screen just inside the tower doors. This indicates the area of the trap.

Each trap will have a corresponding Hazard block in the gameplay text (see the "Darkness Trap!" block below) which identifies the triggering mechanism and consequences of a trap.

Whether the trap is armed (or disarmed) is controlled via the Trap Trigger behavior of the relevant Scene Region. Most traps like this one are "pressure plates" which are triggered automatically when a Token moves over it.

A pressure plate inside the tower entryway is connected to an orb of magical @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.S7VbUetIfVT7B6Eq]{Darkness} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.engulfingDarknes] which suffuses the area in magical gloom. If a player steps on the triggering plate:

A tile clicks beneath your feet, and it instantly grows dark inside of the tower. Utterly and completely dark, as if all light around you has been swallowed by an deep and eternal shadow.

Darkness Trap!

The Entrance Alcove is trapped by a magical darkness trap, which is triggered when a character steps on the 60-foot-wide, 10-foot-long pressure plate at the eastern end of the chamber. This pressure plate cannot be disabled.

Characters with a [[/skill perception 16 passive format=long]] or who succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] are able to spot the pressure plate.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 16]] [[/skillCheck arcana 16]] check knows that magical darkness spells were used as a defensive measure by the Aedir and that there would typically be a physical disarming mechanism somewhere nearby.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Tripping Hazard

As characters make their way through the dark, they may trip over the ground, which is rough from years of disuse. While in darkness, the entryway area is considered Difficult Terrain.

Each time a character moves through the room, roll a [[/gmroll 1d4]]. On a result of 1, they stumble over something on the floor and must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] from falling awkwardly. suffer damage from the [[/hazard 4 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Tripping Hazard}.

Disabling the Darkness

The Darkness field is disabled by the control lever behind the fortified barricade on the west side of the room.

Alternatively, the Darkness may be dispelled by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.BP3GCwa66IAw1yTG]{Daylight} spells.

Alternatively, the Darkness may be dispelled using the @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.dawnBeacon000000]{Dawn Beacon} Iconic spell.

The magical darkness emanates from a circular orb mounted atop the east wall of the room and fills the space completely. The orb itself is totally obscured while the Darkness effect is active, has an Armor Class of 18, and 20 hit points.

Departure Notes

Once there is light in the room, the wall in its center can be clearly seen:

A gray metal wall stands in the center of the room. Pieces of paper, largely faded, have been taped to it — one has bold red writing, one in a thin and neat blocky blue, and one in green that varies in thickness and color, as if written by someone whose hands were currently shaking.

Inspecting the Notes

Of the pieces of paper on the wall, only the notes in red, blue, and green can be clearly made out. Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check or is fluent in [[/language towyr]] knows that the writing is from the Aedir Empire. Those who succeed on the history check are also aware that the language is no longer used, but that there are several words in Common that come from the language because of how widespread it was when the Aedir Empire fell in the wake of the Shattering.

With a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check, characters know that these pieces of writing were either written with @UUID[Item.17IzJQ0rWmZ3cdNQ]{Spellwrought Pens}, or on paper that has been magically treated to resist fading and disintegration. As a result, determining exactly when they were written is not possible.

Deciphering the Text

Rules for translating these notes are provided in @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#translating-aediri]{Towyr Translation}.

Three Perspectives

The written perspectives of the three Aedir researchers can be found both in the entryway and throughout the tower. Any character can tell that the three sets of handwriting are different without a check.

  • Red Ink. Text written in red ink with bold and blocky text is by Remel. Remel's writing is also usually accompanied by sketches.

  • Blue Ink. Text written in blue ink with precise thin lines is by Bejai. Bejai has clear-cut to-do lists.

  • Green Ink. Text written in green ink with chaotic and sloppy handwriting is by Golarne. Golarne's memory aids point to the location of the levers to the Secret Basement Room that can be found throughout the tower.

The Red Note

Each scarlet red glyph that fills the page is drawn with paint instead of ink, in bold artistic strokes that give the line and curve of words a sense of depth and motion. In the corner of the page, still bold but drawn at smaller scale, is a small model of the tower, much as it looks today but without depicted damage or deterioration.

Deciphering the Red Note

The red note was drawn by an artist, which can be determined by any character without a check.

Any character who examines the model of the tower drawn on the page and makes a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check lines up the image with what they see around them. They learn that the tower has four total levels, and that the entry level that the party now occupies is the second highest of the group.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

Protection and preservation

Protect the Tower. Activate concealment. Preserve the Aedir Empire.

The Blue Note

The sets of glyphs on this page are written in a thin blue ink, one below the other. Several are crossed out or faded and can no longer be read, but four remain legible and untouched.

Deciphering the Blue Note

The blue note looks like a to-do list, which can be determined by any character without a check.

Any character who reads the blue note and makes a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check can also identify the author as someone who is precise and organized.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

Science and sight

Leave the laboratory. Take the elevator up to the top. Keep watching. Record audio for any intruders.

The Green Note

The note is written in a forest green and has several false starts — glyphs that have been written down and scribbled out and replaced with similar ones, then underlined. The ink is also quite uneven: thicker lines can be seen in some places and thinner ones in others, though they all appear to be by the same hand.

Deciphering the Green Note

Any character who examines the green note and makes a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check can determine that one word in particular in the note is the one that has been emphasized most strongly; it is similar to the Common word for power.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

Power and memory

Note the recipe for power. Remember and stay safe.

Rotating Elevator.name: Rotating Elevator
Rotating Elevator.text:
If closed, the elevator can be opened from the outside by pulling a lever located next to the lever that disables the magical darkness, on the freestanding wall in the center of the entryway.

The metal walls of the inside of the elevator are copper-colored, with a hand-shaped indentation in the wall by the door as if someone had forced their palm into the metal. Below the indentation is a panel with four circular niches, arranged as if they were the top, bottom, left, and right points of a diamond. The top, left, and right niches all hold metal discs inscribed with different glyphs. The bottom niche is empty.

Any character who takes a look at the glyphs can tell that the left and right discs are mirror images of each other.

Position

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

Left

Left Turn

Rotate Clockwise

Right

Right Turn

Rotate Counter-Clockwise

Top

Sky

Ascend

Operating the Elevator

Interactive Object

The elevator is an ​​ Interactable Object which can be rotated, raised, or lowered by the Gamemaster only.

Disabled Functions

Before finding the @UUID[Item.WQQEvyrN62iXctqi]{Elevator Glyphstone} and restoring it to the elevator control panel, the elevator can only be rotated to visit other areas of the Entry level or ascend to the Top level.

As the Gamemaster, you will be prompted with an option to descend, but this should not be used until the party has repaired the elevator's functionality.

Entering and Exiting

Characters open and close the elevator doors by placing their hands against the hand-shaped indentation in the elevator wall.

As you place your hand against the indentation in the wall, the metal shifts, feeling suddenly soft and pliable under your touch, and molds itself around your touch as the doors move. When you take your hand off of the metal, the indentation remains, fitted to the shape of your hand.

Rotating

Touching the inscribed circular discs on the left or right side of the diamond of niches rotates the elevator by a quarter turn. The elevator will only rotate properly when it is closed.

The glyph in the center of the metal disc you press glows and the disc warms slightly to the touch. With a soft hum, the elevator slowly begins to rotate in a gentle but constant motion, stopping when it has moved a quarter of the way around the circle. As it ceases moving, the glyph ends its glow and returns to normal.

Changing Floors

Touching the disc at the top of the diamond raises the elevator one floor. This has no effect if the elevator door is open.

The glyph in the metal disc glows beneath your fingertips, and the elevator creaks as it begins to ascend, slowly rising inch by inch until it comes to a stop.

Characters can only make the elevator descend if they find the elevator Descent Disc and put it into the empty slot in the elevator panel as noted below.

The glyph in the metal disc is slow to warm this time, and the elevator jerks as it descends, shaking you as it lowers to the floor below.

Repairing the Elevator

To fully operate the elevator, the party must find and replace the @UUID[Item.WQQEvyrN62iXctqi]{Elevator Glyphstone} that has been removed from the elevator's control panel.

Finding the Missing Disc

The missing glyphstone that controls the elevator's descent can be found in the nest of a suarrok that has been collecting jewels, coins, and other objects of value and storing them in its nest in the @UUID[.rmlW0jNwmDevov5W]{Lookout Post}. It can be easily identified by its size and shape, as well as the glyph written on it, which is a mirror image of the glyph that raises the elevator.

Anyone who knows Common can identify the word "Below," while those able to translate basic Towyr identify its meaning as "Descend".

No Substitutions

The function of the disc is tied to the glyph written on it, not its positioning in the panel. Characters can pry one of the existing discs out of its niche and slide it into the bottom niche, but it will perform the same function that it did previously (if the left disc is moved to the bottom, for example, it still turns the elevator left).

The glyph eagerly gravitates into position in the empty socket. A subtle humming sound and gentle light emit from it; you get the sense that it is once again functional.

Living Quarters.name: Living Quarters
Living Quarters.text:
Metal plaques are affixed to three of the four doors visible from the elevator entrance, each etched with a name in different handwriting — "Remel" is inscribed in block letters on the one to the west, "Bejai" in thin and neat lettering on the one next to it, and "Golarne" in sweeping script with swirls and flourishes on the door farthest east. The remaining door is empty.

Characters who have seen the writing of the three inhabitants of the tower can match them to the writing found elsewhere in the tower. Generally, Remel writes in red, Bejai in blue, and Golarne in green.

From the foyer, characters can investigate the following:

  • @UUID[.4T3mt9zYLyiqlafI] (West)

  • @UUID[.R29NTurbvFLdFcua] (Center-West)

  • @UUID[.SQ0bfGVXY3RltrVd] (Center-East)

  • @UUID[.OJfN8ULdcIFFSkC8] (East)

Locked Chambers

Both Golarne's and Bejai's rooms are locked with heavy stone doors that cannot be easily demolished or forced open. The doors do appear to have a traditional keyhole, however, on the side of their exterior surface.

The door can be unlocked with a successful[[/skill sleightOfHand tool=thief dc=15]]. [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000].

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who makes a [[/skill perception 11]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] notices an elliptical indentation in the same place on each doorframe near where the conventional keyhole is located.

  • Golarne's room in particular may be opened by pressing @UUID[Item.oZTYuDbSnIyy9atT]{Golarne's Signet Ring} into this indentation.

Dining Hall.name: Dining Hall
Dining Hall.text:
The room looks as if whoever lived here was interrupted mid-meal: plates and cups are still on the tables, chairs are pushed back as if someone is about to return, and a game board in the corner of the room is still set as if it is the middle of a game.

Golarne's Reminders

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who makes a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 12 passive]] notices a piece of paper on the wall above the game board. On it, in green writing, is a note that can be translated using the rules in @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#translating-towyr]{Translating Towyr}.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

Power Game

A POWERFUL Game

The Chessboard

Anyone who examines the immediate area of the game board sees the following:

The board is less dusty than the rest of the room, though not by much, and it appears to have been abandoned mid-match. While the pieces are different than those seen in modern times, it appears to be a game of chess.

This game is, in fact, one of the keys used to open the secret @UUID[.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4].

Identifying the Game

The game in progress is an Aedir variant of chess called "Seas and Spires," which contains an alternate defeat condition: if your opponent is ever up by more than two pieces, you lose the game.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 17]] [[/skillCheck society 17]] check can recognize the game as "Seas and Spires" and recall the alternate defeat condition.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] and characters with experience playing chess have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The Board State

A decorative piece — a soldier holding a flag — stands on the side of black, indicating that it's black's turn to move. The Towyr word engraved on its base carries the Basic Meaning of "Turn" and a Full Translation of "To Mark Order."

Any character who analyzes the board state and makes a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check deduces that black is currently down two pieces, and white stands poised to take black's most powerful piece on its next turn, which would cause black to lose the game. Black has two legal moves: to capture one of white's weakest pieces, or to move their most powerful piece out of harm's way.

  • Characters with experience playing chess have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Solving the Puzzle

The game pieces can only be moved by speaking a command phrase: the piece's name — engraved on its base — plus its destination on the board.

To solve the puzzle, the characters must make the only move that would allow the game to continue: capturing white's weakest piece. Whenever a character moves the wrong piece, a jolt of electricity arcs from its base and strikes them for [[/damage 1d4 Lightning]] damage. Then, the puzzle resets.

Any character that uses @UUID[Actor.MJfOzwa6uawHDhHA.Item.iCaiYRPxSxowvFJa]{Detect Magic}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify}, or a similar spell the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] talent can tell that there is some enchantment on the board that connects to a distant mechanism.

Once the characters have made the correct move, they activate one of the levers needed to unlock the hidden basement room: refer to @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#the-secret-room]{The Secret Room} for details.

Brute Force

If the characters — through the unfortunate combination of bad rolls and poor deductive reasoning — are unable to solve the puzzle, they may brute force it by moving every piece on black's side.

There are seven black pieces remaining, and only one correct piece. Therefore, divide [[/damage 6d4 Lightning]] damage between the entire party to represent their failed attempts.

Equipment Storage.name: Equipment Storage
Equipment Storage.text:
The floor ahead of you is littered with damp crates, covered in a blanket of mold and dusty spiderwebs. A half-dozen tiny creatures skitter and scuffle across the floor between them, squeaking as they go. Catching sight of you, these six-legged rodents flee to the west, scampering into an alcove behind a curtain of overlapping cobwebs.

Scurrying Critters

Before the characters have time to react, the 6 @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvets} located here scurry away into the @UUID[.rwL2EwQH5AV1sFJI]{Western Storage Alcove}, quickly disappearing from the party's view. The characters won't be able to interact with these creatures directly, but they have just enough time to catch a meaningful glimpse.

@Embed[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X count=6]

There are four separate alcoves within this larger storage area:

  • @UUID[.rwL2EwQH5AV1sFJI]{Western Storage Alcove}

  • @UUID[.ag0qVoqjpYWFgzC0]{Center-West Storage Alcove}

  • @UUID[.ix4VFt1Y2KIDwIvL]{Center-East Storage Alcove}

  • @UUID[.5MbPQ5vWzvFanhzy]{Eastern Storage Alcove}

The Cliff Face.name: The Cliff Face
The Cliff Face.text:
The narrow passageway from the tower's storage area emerges onto a small cliff. Below, the Forest of Stone stretches out beneath you, its greens and grays and blues inviting, but so far down that a fall would likely kill you. The cliff is blocked by the tower's structure to your right, but appears to continue to your left to some unknown destination for those willing to brave the treacherous heights.

The path is narrow, and must be carefully navigated to avoid a potential fall.

Treacherous Path

For each party member who moves along the cliff, roll a [[/gmroll 1d6 # Cliff Face Challenge]] on the Cliff Face Challenges table below.

Any character who moves to the western tip of the tower and makes a successful [[/skill acrobatics 16]] [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check climbs down to the level below.

  • Characters who use proper equipment (rope, grappling hook, etc.) have @Advantage[2] on this check.

If the check is failed, they fall 20 feet to the ledge below, taking [[/damage 2d6 bludgeoning]] damage and landing Pronethey face a [[/hazard 5 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Twenty Foot Fall}.

@Embed[RollTable.XFwhh8fq216JIFo4 inline rollable=true]

Scene Transition

Players can automatically transition to the lower scene by moving into the Scene Region titled Transition: Descend to Basement.

Alternatively, you can manually activate the @UUID[Scene.emberAedirSpyBmt]{Aedir Spypost - Basement} Scene.

Lookout Post.name: Lookout Post
Lookout Post.text:
As you exit the elevator your breath catches for a moment as you realize that you can see for what seems like miles from here, across the canopy of the Forest of Stone and into the orange-yellow of the Golden Flats in the center of the Arctus Plateau.

Whoever once lived here took advantage of those views — telescopes line the outer edge of the tower's rooftop, and tracks in the center of the tower seem to indicate some kind of signaling system that may have used mirrors and glass.

While searching the area, characters may inspect the circular track and system of lenses installed atop the lookout post.

Searching the Area

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check faintly hears the distant flapping of wings from some creature far overhead.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] check recalls that the ancient Aedir were rumored to be able to communicate instantaneously across vast distances by encoding messages within beams of light using a sophisticated set of directed mirrors and lenses.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Observation Lens

One telescopic lens in the northwest edge of the lookout post remains functional. Its lens is scratched and blurry from centuries of neglect, but peering through it you can still survey a considerable stretch of the Forest of Stone from this lofty perch.

Vantage Point

The Observation Lens described above is the first Vantage Point that can be discovered in the game. Interacting with this telescope clears the Fog of War from a large section of the Forest of Stone on the Region Map.

Suarrok Nest

Once the nest comes into the party's view, read or paraphrase the following:

A large nest of straw, branches, and paper sits in the far corner, sparkling with the reflection of light on gem and glass and metal. The creature is nowhere to be seen, but it has not gone far. Just then, you hear a shrill cry as a shadow passes overhead, and you can even feel the breeze upon your face from the beating of massive wings.

The party can carefully search for the missing @UUID[Item.WQQEvyrN62iXctqi]{Elevator Glyphstone} in the suarrok's nest without calling attention to themselves.

Inspecting the Nest

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check identifies the nest as likely belonging to a suarrok; these creatures are known to tuck their treasures against the back wall of their nest, underneath piles of straw.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who makes a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] can spot the glint of metal within the nest, and knows precisely where to search.

Searching the Nest

To adequately search the ramshackle nest, the party must sneak into the nest, locate the disc, and pull it out without attracting attention.

If the party fails any of the following checks, the suarrok immediately notices them and lands, initiating combat.

  • To enter the nest without being detected, a character must succeed on a [[/skill stealth 15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check.

  • To find the disc, a character must succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check while Searching the nest. This step can be bypassed if the party already knows precisely where it is from the previous check described in "Inspecting the Nest" above.

  • To remove the disc, characters must succeed on a [[/skill sleightofhand 15]] [[/skillCheck performance 15]] check to remove it without disturbing other nearby items.

Any character who takes the Search action to survey the nest is able to find the following:

  • The @UUID[Item.WQQEvyrN62iXctqi]{Elevator Glyphstone}

  • A weathered @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmChainShirt]{Chain Shirt} shoddy @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.chainMail0000000] covered in moss and mildew

  • [[/roll 1d3 + 1]] random items from the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot} Table

Fighting the Suarrok

If at any time while exploring the Lookout Post the party makes loud noise or is detected while investigating the Suarrok Nest, the creature itself swoops down and attacks.

@Embed[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]

Suarrok Tactics

The giant bird's attacks don't completely make sense — it switches targets frequently and seems to favor aggression over any sort of practical attack strategy.

  • It uses @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.T2ZNQKTKt3TyWvYg]{Searing Stare} to blind any character that gets close to it.

  • It relies upon @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.z0zk5kCBd8tSuH64]{Flyby} and the 10 foot reach of its @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.6vURSsPqR8UTQan4]{Long Beak} to harass the party and avoid being pinned down.

  • It uses @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.T2ZNQKTKt3TyWvYg]{Searing Stare} to blind any character that gets close to it.

  • @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.elusiveFlight000]{Elusive Flight} and its @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.swoopingStrike00]{Swooping Strike} to harass the party and avoid being pinned down.

The suarrok's main focus is on protecting its nest — it will attempt to keep itself between the party and the nest if at all possible.

Survival Instinct

Once reduced below half its Hit Point maximum, the suarrok attempts to flee, flying off into the distant clouds. If it escapes, combat ends and the creature does not return until the following day.

The Saurrok will fight aggressively until @Condition[broken], at which point it will attempt to flee toward the distant clouds. If it escapes, combat ends and the creature does not return until the following day.

Basement West.name: Basement West
Basement West.text:
An assortment of tools and supplies are strewn across nearly every elevated surface of the room, from the circular worktable that lines the outside wall to the bronze tables in the center. The supplies are a mix of familiar and strange, common and wondrous, but none are rusted — unlike most other things in the tower, they appear to have been recently cleaned.

The party may wish to peruse through the tools on these workbenches, although tampering with them initiates the hazard of the Steam Trap described below.

Signs of Danger

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check can confirm that the tools on the tables were recently cleaned by the application of a substance that likely covered the entire room, as the worktables and barrels in the room show the same level of cleaning.

  • The trap can be discovered before it is triggered with a successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check to note the drops of condensation on the long table of tools beneath each of the bronze spouts,

    or by using the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.KrM3oHVv13RAALrS]{Find Traps} or similar, or with the use of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} or similar, which reveals an aura of magic around both the worktables and the bronze spouts.

    or through the use of the @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]{Recognize Spellcraft} talent, which reveals an aura of magic around both the worktables and the bronze spouts.

Sorting through the Tools

Most of the tools found in the Basement are of no real use to the party, but there are some standout items.

  • [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] The character can identify the bulk of the tools as metalworking tools that would have been used by the Aediri. Those with [[/knowledge aedir]] know that they have no real monetary value currently.

  • [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] The character can identify a @UUID[Item.17IzJQ0rWmZ3cdNQ]{Spellwrought Pen} among the items on the table.

  • [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] The character can spot a few scattered gems on the table, likely used as component pieces in magical works. In total, the gems are worth 50 gp. They also notice that all of the papers and books on the table have the same symbol either on or near them.

Any character who examines the symbol and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] or [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] or [[/skillCheck society 14]] check identifies it as one that shields the item it is on from environmental damage.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] can use the supplies to create or refresh @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.SztwZhbhZeCqyAes]{Alchemist's Supplies}.

Steam Cleansing Trap

This trap uses the natural steam cleaning functions of the basement (meant to keep tools sterile) and uses them against intruders by flooding the area with super-heated caustic steam.

Steam Cleansing Trap

This room contains a complex Steam Cleansing Trap which, once activated, becomes worse as more steam and caustic chemicals are released into the air.

Once triggered, place all characters who are inside the area of the trap into a Combat encounter and have them act in initiative order. The trap acts as described below on both initiative count 20 and 10.

Trap Trigger

This trap is triggered when the weight on any of the three worktables in this section changes (by objects being removed or added).

Trap Actions

The trap acts on initiative count 20, when it releases more steam into the room and on initiative count 10, when it adds cleaning agents to the steam that are harmful to the party.

Steam Release (Initiative 20). Hot steam is released from the spouts in the wall and begins filling the room. Characters within the room must make a Constitution saving throw or take fire damage. The difficulty and danger of this trap escalates the longer it is active, the DC of the Saving Throw increases by 1 and the damage increases by a die size Characters within the room must make a series of checks to avoid the injurious release of steam. The difficulty and danger of this trap escalates the longer it is active:

  • Round 1:[[/save constitution 14]] Saving Throw or [[/damage 1d4 fire]] damage [[/hazard 2 fortitude health]]{Mild Steam Burn}

  • Round 2: [[/save constitution 15]] Saving Throw or [[/damage 1d6 fire]] damage [[/hazard 3 fortitude health]]{Minor Steam Burn}

  • Round 3: [[/save constitution 16]] Saving Throw or [[/damage 1d8 fire]] damage [[/hazard 5 fortitude health]]{Steam Burn}

  • Round 4+: [[/save constitution 17]] Saving Throw or [[/damage 1d10 fire]] damage [[/hazard 6 fortitude health]]{Major Steam Burn}

Alchemical Cleaning Agents (Initiative 10). Alchemical cleaning agents are released into the steam. Any creature that ends their turn within range of the steam must make a [[/save constitution 15]] Saving Throw. On a failure, the creature is Poisoned. If they are already Poisoned when making this save, they suffer a coughing fit and are knocked Prone. make a successful [[/skillCheck medicine 15]] to take precautionary measures against breathing in the toxic air. Failing this check results in the character being @Condition[Poisoned]. If the character is already poisoned when making this check, they suffer a coughing fit and are knocked @Condition[Prone]. The cleaning agents disperse into the steam and become harmless after 1 round.

Deactivating the Trap

The trap can be deactivated by activating two cutoff valves located against the wall on either side of the elevator. Characters can spot the valves if they are within 10 feet, have clear line-of-sight, and have a [[/skill perception 16 passive format=long]] or make a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]].

Activating the valve requires a character to perform the Use an Object action. The trap is disabled once both cutoff valves have been turned.

The trap can also be neutralized by disabling the heating elements that produce the steam. Those heating elements are magical, but can be disabled by casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} (DC 13). by freezing it using the Condense action from [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeFrost0000000]].

Trapped Inside

When the trap begins, the doors to the other half of the basement and to the elevator close and lock automatically. The basement doors can only be opened in one of the following ways:

  • Unlocked with a successful [[/skill sleightOfHand tool=thief dc=15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check using Lockpicks

  • Forced open using a prybar or similar tool (one of which can be found among the tools on the table) and a successful [[/skill athletics 16]] [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check.

Once a door is opened, the steam dissipates over the larger space and becomes harmless beyond its initial 5 foot radius.

Secret Room Lever

One of the four levers required to open the @UUID[.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4]{Generator Room} is found in this area.

A Powerful Tool

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16]] while looking around the room notices one note in particular, which has been wedged between tools so that it sits up straight on the table. It reads:

"Use a POWERful Tool." It also has a sketch of a rectangular table on it, along with several items: a spring, a length of pipe, and a circular gear with a hole in its center.

Through roleplay, or after a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck science 15]] check, characters can identify each of these items as belonging to the table to the left-hand side of the elevator when facing the elevator. The only item not accounted for in the drawing is a lever that is attached to the outer edge of that table.

If a character pulls the correct lever, refer to @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#the-secret-room]{The Secret Room} for details. Interacting with this lever does not trigger the Steam Cleansing trap.

Basement East.name: Basement East
Basement East.text:
Between the small tool-covered metal tables and the set of stairs that lead further down into the lower levels of the tower, a half-made metal construct sits in a heap on the floor. Orange liquid has congealed beneath its pile of copper-colored limbs, none of which fully match each other. It is impossible to tell at a glance whether this is a failed project, a pile of scraps, or the remains of some violent experiment. A small note affixed to its chest reads: "Add Shielding." It is not the only one — similar small notes are scattered across the room.

Any character who visited Golarne's room will recognize the notes as being by the same person and serving the same general function — reminders of things to do.

Notable Notes

Golarne has written many, many notes, and it is not immediately clear which, if any, are helpful. To identify notes which may have important information for them, characters must succeed on an [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check.

The First Note

This note has a large down arrow on it in addition to the words.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

clean, silver

Clean alchemical spills with silver decontamination powder.

The Second Note

The note has only words on it, and matches similar notes about power found elsewhere.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

power, book

A POWERful read

The Third Note

The note has a picture of piping and two small wheels.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

heat, caution

Beware of steam cleansing, remember cutoff valves.

A Hidden Lever

One of the levers to open the @UUID[.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4]{Generator Room} is found in this section of the basement and can be activated by pulling any book off a specific bookshelf to the south of the stairs.

A Powerful Read

If the party has found Golarne's clue or has reason to suspect that the bookshelves contain a secret, they can determine what they need to do with a successful [[/skill investigation 17]] [[/skillCheck awareness 17]] check or through roleplay. The DC of this check is reduced by 2 for each of the following successful checks: This check gains +1 boons for each of the following successful checks:

  • [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] The character can determine that the bookcase containing the lever has a slight dusting of a glittering crushed crystal on it.

  • [[/skill arcana 15]] or [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] or [[/skillCheck society 15]] The character identifies the dust as a substance popular in magical enchantments during the time of the Aedir Empire. If characters have encountered the substance elsewhere, they can recognize it without a check.

  • [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] The character can tell that the books on each shelf are arranged by title, with the exception of the bookcase holding the lever, which appears to have books arranged in random order.

  • [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] The character can make out a symbol traced across the spine of the books — it is the symbol for power.

If a character manipulates the correct bookshelf, refer to @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#the-secret-room]{The Secret Room} for details.

Underforge.name: Underforge
Underforge.text:
A large metallic humanoid stands in the center of the room; the room is filled with large metal vats. Several have begun to leak fluid, creating patches of bubbling liquid. As you enter the room from the staircase, the metal figure jerks as if startling to life, and the orange fluid within its body begins to glow.

The humanoid is a Broken Aedir Sentinel. Though it is partially destroyed, it maintains and adheres strictly to its designated instructions of defending the Underforge and defeating any who enter.

@Embed[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v]

Broken Aedir Sentinel Tactics

In addition to its dangerous @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.90dfhrI5KDGETGmv]{Multiattack} combination, the construct uses @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.2tVeIS6H0Lem0A5A]{Aedir Construct Fluid} to power additional special abilities:

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.PtIxg3j5xCFJJWn7]{Powered Spin}

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.Af0gVweXcUrWvGFN]{Enhanced Shielding}

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.0oxUW5r3PhZHsDDO]{Self Repair}

Each use of Construct Fluid depletes its current stores. It can only restore the spent fluid in the Recharge Stations located in the side rooms of the underforge, and uses its legendary actions to procure more construct fluid when needed:

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.NNUbM9Qm0kNZfoWf]{Repelling Kick} knocks back enemies so the construct can move safely.

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.gg6sS2kF5M7BncTM]{Charge} increases speed and moves towards a recharge station to begin charging fluid.

If the Sentinel reaches a recharge station, the @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.GgAvK0QQ4ugXnpKd]{Recharge} lair action automatically occurs on Initiative count 20.

In addition to its dangerous capacity for multiple attacks, the construct is empowered by alchemical fluid and can expend Focus on several special abilities:

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.sentinelSpin0000]{Powered Spin}

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.sentinelshieldin]{Enhanced Shielding}

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.selfrepair000000]{Self Repair}

Each use of Alchemical Fluid depletes its current stores. It can only restore the spent fluid in the Recharge Stations located in the side rooms of the underforge, and if it requires more fluid will make use of its @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.sentinelKick0000]{Repelling Kick} to knock enemies back and then spend all available actions on movement toward the nearest Recharge station.

If the Sentinel reaches a recharge station, it will use its @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v.Item.sentinelRecharge]{Alchemical Recharge} ability at the first possible opportunity and begin refilling its Alchemical Fluid.

The Sentinel places no priority on self-preservation and will continue its stalwart defense until it is no longer physically capable of resisting.

The spills on the floor of Construct Fluid have no effect on the Sentinel, but pose a hazard to the party, as noted below.

Caustic Spill

Any character who passes through a pool of construct fluid must make a [[/save dexterity 13]] saving throw [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check to avoid getting some on their feet or clothing.

Those who fail become coated in the slick and caustic substance. If such a character moves more than half their speed on their turn or as a single action, they immediately slip and fall &Reference[prone] @Condition[prone]. To remove the viscous coating from equipment requires spending 1 minute cleaning and is impractical to do within the context of a Combat encounter.

The party can eliminate the construct's access to Alchemical Fluid off by turning off the valves at each of the @UUID[.WoToQ2QSKdq7CEGp]{Recharge Stations}.

Cutting Off The Supply

If the party can reach the valves located at each of the alchemical recharge stations in the room, they can turn them off, giving the construct no way to recharge.

To find the valves before they are used by the construct, characters must make a successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check.

  • If they have seen the Sketch of the Underforge found in Remel's Room the DC of this check is reduced by 4 this check gains a +2 Boons.

  • If they have translated Golarne's Reminder Notes in the Basement, the DC of this check is reduced by 4 this check gains a +2 Boons.

Once one valve has been located or once they have witnessed the Sentinel using one of the charging stations first-hand, they can locate other valves without a check.

Turning the valves requires a successful [[/skill athletics 13]] [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check. In addition, the valves are heated — if physically touched without gloves or other protection, the character that turns them must make a successful [[/save constitution 14]] saving throw [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check or take [[/damage 1d6 fire]] damage suffer a [[/hazard 4 fortitude health]]{Minor Steam Burn}. Once a valve is turned off, the recharge stations on that side of the room are no longer supplied with fluid.

Once the construct has been defeated, the party can explore the rest of the room.

The puddles of orange alchemical fluid soaking into the ground have only gotten deeper over the course of the battle, slowly seeping their way into the groundwater and down to Yakoshta Mine. Collecting a sample would be easy here, but stopping the leak as the miners requested is a job for more than a mop and broom. The parts, labor, and understanding of ancient Aedir mechanisms that would be required to fully repair the leak make repair seem prohibitively difficult — some other way to address the leaking fluid will need to be found if the miners' troubles are to be solved.

Quest Event

For details on the party cleaning, decontaminating, or collecting samples from the tower, see @UUID[JournalEntry.emberSignalInten.JournalEntryPage.signalIntentTowe#resolving-the-contamination]{Resolving the Contamination} in the corresponding Quest Event.

Generator Room.name: Generator Room
Generator Room.text:
The light flickers an eerie yellowish orange, bouncing off of piles of books and tools, including several fully functioning metal limbs, which hang from stands as if waiting to be brought to life. The light comes from several large glass tubes in the back of the room, which have a small amount of orange fluid coating their bottoms. They are attached to a contraption that is a combination of metal and stonework and enough magic that it feels like it has a heartbeat. A gentle voice whispers in your ear as you cross the threshold, repetitive and insistent:

Fluid low. Recharge required. Fluid low. Replenish immediately. Fluid low.

The generator in this room is the source of arcane power for the Signalpost. It is currently empty of the alchemical substance which powers it. Characters who examine the residue of fluid in the canisters and are familiar with the substance already will recognize it as @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0].

Gaining Access

Review the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn.JournalEntryPage.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#the-secret-room]{The Secret Room} section of the Gameplay Details page for details on how this secret room may be opened.

Restoring Power

In order to restore power to the generator, the canisters in the back of the room must be refilled using the @UUID[.ndbokyeEFn2XBDSf#recharge-station]{Recharge Stations} in the Underforge. By replacing filled canisters in the ports on the north wall of the room, the generator will spring back into life:

Brightness. Everywhere. Lights you could not see before glow from the walls, lighting the entire tower in a warm glow. The gentle voice whispers again:

Power restored. Our work continues.

If whatever powers the voice is aware that the post has been long-abandoned, it does not mention it.

Restoring power to the generator causes all interior lights throughout the Aedir Signalpost to turn on, suffusing the area with bright illumination. Additionally, the stealth field which conceals the tower from view returns to full operation, no longer flickering intermittently.

Event Outcome

If the party restores power to the generator, mark the Power Restored outcome of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberSignalInten.JournalEntryPage.signalIntentTowe]{Traversing the Tower} Event as completed.

Remel's Room.name: Remel's Room
Remel's Room.text:
This is a room in a state of suspended motion — the cover has been dragged off of the bed, clothes are strewn about, and a cup of long-evaporated liquid, now home to a clutch of spider eggs, sits with a spoon still in it on the dresser in the sleeping area. Papers are scattered across the desk, including several sketches. You recognize one as being of the entryway you came through to enter the tower. One word is written on it, which vaguely translates as "dark".

There are a number of sketches on the desk, which include faraway landscapes, portions of the Forest of Stone, and rooms within several towers, all of which have notes on them.

Identifying the Sketches

Any character who makes a [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check can identify three of the sketches as architectural drawings of this tower.

The First Sketch

This sketch depicts a half-circle of a room with two desks in its center.

The area depicted by this sketch is the left half of the basement level of the tower. One phrase is written on it in Towyr. Characters who successfully translate the phrase have @Advantage[2] on checks to deactivate the Steam Heat trap in the basement.

Basic Meaning

Translation

clean, turn

The cleansing steam will protect, but turning the lever will stop.

The Second Sketch

This sketch depicts a half-circle room with a square-shaped room adjoining it.

The area depicted by this sketch is the right half of the basement level. Two phrases are written in Towyr. Characters who successfully translate the phrases have @Advantage[2] on checks to locate the levers that open the Secret Basement room throughout the tower.

Basic Meaning

Translation

power, hidden

Secure the power source in a concealed chamber.

four, safe

Four separate switches required for access to ensure secrecy and protection.

The Third Sketch

This sketch depicts a large circular room, filled with large circular vats and square pads.

The area depicted by this sketch is the Underforge. A metallic helmet is drawn in the center of the room. No notes are written on this sketch, but orange lines with arrows trace from the vats to the square pads.

Bejai's Room.name: Bejai's Room
Bejai's Room.text:
The room is sparsely decorated, but the items that can be seen from the door are evenly spaced and precisely placed; the bed is made, and everything smells mildly of antiseptic. A small metal sign on the desk reads “Plan. Honor. Execute. Repeat.” The only thing in the room that does not appear to be in a state of well-organized rest is the small glowing cube that rests on a disc in the center of the desk, which pulses with a soft light.

The Message Cube

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check can identify the cube as a Message Cube that allows for someone to record their voice and have it play back at a later date.

If characters touch the illuminated cube, it glows more strongly and plays a message.

The recording begins with the shuffling of papers and the sound of a voice in the distance that you cannot make out. A voice closer to you says, as if irritated:

Golarne, if you're that worried that you'll forget how to get into the power room, leave yourself notes or something. I'm recording.

The voice then clears their throat and begins again:

If you are listening to this, then I am either dead or have abandoned the tower. I hope and trust that you are of the Aedir Empire, but in case you are Shent, or from some other group that does not share our tongue, I have enchanted this message to reach all ears.

Please know, the research in this tower is for the Aedir alone. If you are not one of us, it is not meant for you. If you disregard this message, only death awaits you below. Choose your next moves wisely.

Parting Jab

As the recording ends, the cube pulses brightly and sends out a blast of force energy. All characters in the room must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 14]] Saving Throw or suffer [[/damage 1d8 force]] damage suffer the effects of a [[/hazard 5 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Forceful Blast}.

Empty Room.name: Empty Room
Empty Room.text:
There is no sign of occupancy in this room — the bed and desk are empty, and there is a layer of dust on the wood that is deeper than you have seen anywhere else in the tower. Only the bed seems slightly less dusty and abandoned.

Golarne's Reminders

Any character who makes a [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check notices a small piece of paper under one of the legs of the bed, which can be translated using the @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#translating-aediri]{Towyr Translation} rules.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

power, sleep

A POWERFUL Rest

One of the levers that opens the secret @UUID[.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4] is activated by putting weight on the bed in this room, triggering a pressure plate.

A Powerful Rest

The party can activate the lever to the hidden basement room by laying down on the bed. They can figure this out with a successful [[/skill investigation 17]] check or through roleplay. For each of the following checks they successfully make, reduce the DC of the Investigation check by 2.

  • [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] The character notices that the bed isn't fully made — it appears to have been purposefully set so that someone can easily get in and out of it.

  • [[/skill arcana 15]] or [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] or [[/skillCheck society 15]] The character discovers a dusting of a crystalline substance, and can identify it as a substance popular in magical enchantments during the time of the Aedir Empire.

Spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify} may be used to learn that the bed is enchanted to respond to weight being placed upon it. The @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]{Recognize Spellcraft} talent may be used to learn that the bed is enchanted to respond to weight being placed upon it.

If a character activates the lever by lying down on the bed, refer to @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#the-secret-room]{The Secret Room} for details.

Golarne's Room.name: Golarne's Room
Golarne's Room.text:
Notes in green writing are affixed to nearly every surface in this room — objects, papers, even the door. Many have faded away, but one piece of paper, in the center of the desk, has words large enough to be read from across the room.

Golarne has left notes throughout the room as a reminder of daily tasks. Translation of these notes reveals that most are about mundane things: reminders to eat and sleep, to go to the top of the tower and enjoy the view, and more. The prominent piece of paper in the center of the desk can be translated using the @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#translating-aediri]{Towyr Translation} rules.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

memory, paper

Remember the notes of POWER.

Golarne's Reminders

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check can confirm that the handwriting on these notes matches the handwriting found on notes about "power" that are located elsewhere throughout the complex.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] automatically succeed on this check.

Western Storage Alcove.name: Western Storage Alcove
Western Storage Alcove.text:
Behind the spider-webbed entrance, this alcove is filled with boxes that have been knocked over and gnawed on. The crevvets you previously spotted are nowhere in sight, having disappeared through some crack or crevice to another part of the tower, but the evidence of their presence is everywhere, from the dusty footprints to the holes gnawed into the stone floor.

The boxes in this alcove contain shelf-stable food items, like flour and sugar, most of which have been eaten by the @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvets} — which have all escaped to places unknown.

Crevvet Crevices

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check can confirm that the gnaw marks on the boxes are made by the crevvets. Parties may investigate the room to figure out where the vermin have gone off to.

The pests have been entering and exiting the storage area of the tower through a large crevice in the wall in this section of storage. Party members can locate it by searching the room thoroughly with a successful [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check.

This check is made easier if they use the evidence of the crevvets' activity. If characters succeed on one of the checks below, they gain the relevant information and @Advantage[2] on the Investigation check. If they succeed on a second check, they get a +2 circumstance bonus they gain an additional @Advantage[1] to that check. If they succeed on all three, they automatically notice the crevice in the wall without a check.

  • [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] The character notices a breeze in this room that appears stronger than in other locations in the tower. Somewhere, there's a crack leading to the outside.

  • [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] The character recalls that crevvets can chew through stone — they likely found a crack on the outside of the tower and widened it to give themselves access to these supplies and a location safe from predators.

  • [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] The character notices tracks that show the rodents have been both coming and going. they must have access to the outside world. The tracks leads to a cracked portion in the floor toward the back corner.

The crevice is slightly hidden behind a sheet of fallen slate.

The slab of rock leans against the opening behind it — from a distance, it looks indistinguishable from the rock wall on either side of it, but up close, it is clear that the crevvets have chewed away at enough of it for it to be easily moved, exposing a narrow dark passageway behind it.

Heavy Slab
