Any character who makes a successful [[/skill athletics 16]] [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check can move the rock slab without special equipment.

  • Characters who use a crowbar or other suitable equipment have @Advantage[2] on this check

If the check is failed, it can be retried, but the party member in question must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 13]] saving throw [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] or the heavy rock shifts unexpectedly and deals [[/damage 1d8 bludgeoning]] damage. suffer [[/hazard 5 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{The Shifting Rock}

Secret Door

A "secret door" on the map is used to represent the rock slab described above. Open the secret door once the party has successfully moved the rock.

Once party members have cleared the blockage, they can go through the passageway, leading to @UUID[.jBd5CnAhQ2Zxf3o7]{The Cliff Face}.

Center-West Storage Alcove.name: Center-West Storage Alcove
Center-West Storage Alcove.text:
This storage alcove is somewhat more organized than the scattered goods elsewhere. Boxes are well-labeled, and there is a list of items on a piece of paper on top of the largest storage crate, lettered in precise blue handwriting. On the bottom corners of the page are two separate sketches, in red ink.

The paper on top of the storage crate is Bejai's "Final Tower Storage" list, which gives the location and basic description of several items in storage. The storage list can be translated using the @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#translating-aediri]{Towyr Translation} rules.

Basic Meaning

Full Translation

metal, piece

Metal construct parts can be found in these boxes.

machine, water, bottom

Construct Fluid is stored in the Underforge.

water, clean, bottom

Construct Fluid Neutralizer is stored in the Underforge.

power, tower, down

Tower can be recharged on Basement Level with Construct Fluid.

Remel's Sketches

Additionally, characters may attempt to use Remel's sketches to figure out more about the list. She has drawn the following sketches:

  1. A small golden-brown abstract head with glowing eyes. Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck social 14]] check connects this with the metal constructs that the Aedir Empire was known to use in its structures.

  2. A battery filled with a liquid of some kind. Any character who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check recalls that the power in the tower is connected to a fluid of some kind.

Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

Center-East Storage Alcove.name: Center-East Storage Alcove
Center-East Storage Alcove.text:
This boxes in this storage alcove are covered in dust and spiderwebs. A crowbar lies against the wall, but it seems unlikely that anyone has been in this area in some time.

This storage area contains mostly clothing items. If any are opened, they reveal everyday clothes, bed linens, and other similar items. Some of these boxes appear to have been re-packed with items they did not originally come with.

Contaminating Evidence

Any character who investigates the boxes discovers one that smells vaguely of something alchemical — its source appears to be an orange stain that has soaked into the box's side. The orange stain was produced by @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0]{Aedir Construct Fluid}.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 20]] [[/skillCheck arcana 20]] check can identify the substance.

  • If the party has encountered this contaminant during their travels — in Yakoshta Mine, for example — they can identify it without a check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Eastern Storage Alcove.name: Eastern Storage Alcove
Eastern Storage Alcove.text:
Much like the others, this alcove is filled with boxes, distinguished only by a stand of rusted weapons against the wall.

The boxes in this storage alcove are filled with various supplies: containers, vials, screws, pieces of piping, cleaning fluid, crow bars, and adhesive. The weapons on this rack are practical and not exotic, and are difficult to distinguish in quality due to their extensive rusting.

Ancient Weaponry

Any character with a [[/skill perception 15 passive format=long]] or who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 13]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] notices one of the swords in particular appears to be made of an exceptional material. This blade is a @UUID[Item.84MTJGlTj9OyKGY1] and is obviously a weapon of value notable for its exceptional hardness and sharp edge.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The Area Map for the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC] depicts all four levels of the ancient fortification.

  • Entry - Ground level where characters enter from the bluffs overlooking the Forest of Stone. The Entry level is divided into the Main Entryway, Storage Rooms, a Dining Area, and Living Quarters.

  • Top - The tower summit which was once used by the Aedir to gather information from those nearby. It can only be reached via the elevator inside of the tower.

  • Basement - A lower level where the inhabitants of the tower kept their records and supplies. It is initially inaccessible via the elevator until the control disc is recovered from the Lookout Post atop the tower. Otherwise this level can be accessed via a crack in the wall found both in the Basement and in the Storage Room on the Entry Level.

  • Underforge - The lowest level of the tower where servitor constructs were manufactured, tested, and housed.

Overall gameplay information about the area is described in @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg]{Gameplay Details}.

Scene Levels

Currently this environment is implemented as four separate Scenes, one for each level of the tower. Once Foundry Virtual Tabletop version 14 is used in Ember, this will be redesigned to a single Scene with multiple Levels for a more inter-connected gameplay experience.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC inline]

Decontamination Station.name: Decontamination Station
Decontamination Station.text:
Cylindrical tanks colored red, yellow, and green sit on top of a cabinet against the wall. A few Towyr words are etched in large letters on the cabinet, along with a sign that you immediately recognize as the word "Emergency."

The decontamination station is located north of the stairs, on the easternmost wall.

In Case of Emergency

The station is labeled with the following message, which can be understood using the rules for @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#translating-towyr]{Translating Towyr}.

Basic Meaning

Translation

Emergency, Clean

Alchemical Decontamination Station — Use only in case of emergency for immediate neutralization of active reagent.

If characters open the cabinet, they see a pile of supplies, including several vials of @UUID[Item.QwzYLBnZ1PjLFEuI]{Alchemical Silver} and empty @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.lHS63sC6bypENNlR]{Flasks} flasks that can be used to collect liquids.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] check can identify the powder as Alchemical Silver, a substance that can act as a decontaminant for certain alchemical agents and poisons.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] automatically succeed on this check.

The cabinet opens to reveal a shelf covered with vials, flasks, and spare materials, next to an indentation that matches the size and shape of a hand.

If any character places their hand within the indentation and holds it there for 6 seconds, the decontamination station comes to life.

The tanks begin to pump fluid into the pipes, and before your eyes, the bubbling orange of the broken and rusty vats shifts in color and becomes more still, turning from its previous electric color to a silvery gray.

Irreversible Cleansing

If the alchemical fluid is neutralized in this way, it can no longer be used by the @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v]{Broken Aedir Sentinel} nor can it be used to refill the canisters required to restore power to the @UUID[.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4]{Generator Room}.

Any character who makes a successful[[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] check will understand that performing the decontamination procedure will render the alchemical substance inert.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] get @Advantage[2] on this check.

Recharge Stations.name: Recharge Stations
Recharge Stations.text:
Between the crumbling stone, the brass hexagonal platforms on the floor remain almost untouched, each waiting for something that fits between the pipe that juts out from above and the winding plug around the base below. A small sign written in Towyr hangs from the brass wheel in the center of each pipe.

A diagram beneath the label shows a length of hose connecting one large hexagon to smaller hexagons on items, including the construct, a power tube, and a large cylindrical tube that resembles the elevator. A foot can be seen on the large hexagon, and hands hold each of the items with smaller hexagons. Wavy lines around the hands seem to indicate some sort of motion, but there is no written detail.

Station Labels

Each station has an advisory label written in Towyr which can be translated using the rules for @UUID[.lrabLmAzis4i49wg#translating-towyr]{Translating Towyr}.

Basic Meaning

Translation

water, power

Alchemical Recharge for construct and power cannister refueling.

Recharging Generator Cells

The Recharge Station can be used to refill the power cells found in the secret @UUID[.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4]. In order to be used, the Recharge Station must have a full supply of @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0].

  • If the party turned off the supply between the vats and the Recharge Stations during their battle with the construct, they must first turn it back on.

  • If the party neutralized the contamination by using the @UUID[.pWdw77wVIhK1b4Hq]{Decontamination Station} it is impossible to refill the canisters with viable fluid.

When placed in the Recharge Station in the Undercroft, they refill with fluid:

The recharge machine hums to life, turning the empty tubes a deep green as it fills them with the alchemical fluid.

Exterior.name: Exterior
Exterior.text:
The exterior facade of the tower looms over you, its ancient architecture both impressive and foreboding.

Surveying the flora surrounding the entrance of the tower, you notice a strange desiccation that diminishes the lushness of the environment somewhat. The fringes of usually vibrant heartmoss assume a withered hue and the long reeds that protrude from tiny gaps in the masonry have yellow and wilted fronds.

Inspecting the Exterior

Characters can get the following information from examining the exterior of the tower and its architecture.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14 passive]] check realizes that the tower is likely Aedir in origin due to its use of metal and stone, the shape of the tower, and its age. This location, though, is a long way from the bulk of Aedir territory.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The character also recalls that the Aedir were known to gather information on those around them in signalposts which used mirrors, light, and magic to gather and send information across vast distances.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]][[/skillCheck arcana 14 passive]] check infers that they may now be within the radius of whatever stealth field was intermittently concealing the tower, and that they should be able to see the structure clearly as long as they remain near or within it.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 13]][[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] check notices that light glints off of specific spots in the ring at the top of the tower. It is likely that there is some sort of mirror or glass there, possibly used to observe the area around the tower.

The plants surrounding the tower have no ill effects if touched, but they do offer some clues about the source of trouble below.

Contamination Clues

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill nature 13]][[/skillCheck wilderness 13 passive]] check deduces that the plants have likely come into contact with the contaminant.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge plants]] succeed on this check automatically.

  • Result of 18+Critical Success : You recognize that such contamination is likely present in the groundwater and, given the deep roots of plants in this ecosystem, the source of the contamination is probably somewhere below you.

Temple Exterior.name: Temple Exterior
Temple Exterior.text:
This massive Shent temple bears two long walls of stone per door, each one bearing two short columns of chipped, weathered stonework. Each of these columns holds floating orbs of water held aloft by an unseen force. The orbs themselves glow brilliantly, casting rays of blue light in all directions, illuminating the grounds.

Four massive artificial waterfalls sit at the corners of the structure, pouring large amounts of water down onto long stone channels that guide it toward the greater body of water around the structure. The noise is considerable, and drowns out the world beyond the temple.

Massive stone doors sit on each wall of the temple, each covered in the symbols of Mayis, the water moon in grand detail, and the rest of the cosmos of Ember is secondary form.

The party may inspect the architecture or exterior details of the structure before entering.

History in Stone

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check notices that this structure was built for people that were substantially larger than average-sized humanoids of Ember. Judging by the size of the stairs alone, one might guess that the ancient Shent were at least fifteen feet tall.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check while examining the architecture surmises that the main structure was constructed by the Shent at least 2,500 years ago. It could very well be older, since the Shent are one of the oldest cultures to exist on Ember.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The character can also identify some of the patterning in the stonework here as that of the final era of Shent culture — likely built a short time before the entire culture collapsed and mysteriously vanished from the world.

Once the party has concluded an investigation of the exterior, they must proceed into the temple by opening one of the four sets of double doors which frame each side of the temple. All doors are unlocked and can be opened through the combined effort of two characters pulling in opposite directions from their central seam.

The doors open into the spacious @UUID[JournalEntry.dCExfRYP8KRVogO2.JournalEntryPage.xDXhEZOud6pfrfNY]{Temple Interior}, where the party is immediately greeted by the peril within.

Temple Interior.name: Temple Interior
Temple Interior.text:
Encounter Overview

There is a major encounter with the @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty]{Temple Invader} that takes place in this area, designed to occur in two phases.

Phase One

The first phase is a trial of endurance. The Invader begins combat shielded from all harm by a protective barrier that is powered by six elemental orbs. The Invader will deplete one orb every round of combat in order to empower dangerous abilities which threaten the party while the creature itself remains invulnerable. Assuming the Invader depletes one orb every round of combat, this phase should last 6 rounds.

Phase Two

The second phase of the fight begins once the Invader depletes the sixth and final orb, causing their protective shield to disperse. This allows the creature to join the battle directly, but also leaves it vulnerable to harm. It is also at the beginning of this phase that the @UUID[Actor.emberFulgrBlades]{Fulgurite Blades} arrive to join the battle as impromptu allies of the party.

Summoning Elementals

During both phases, the Invader relies on the ability to summon additional elementals into the arena, conjuring either a @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V]{Water Sprite} or occasionally a more dangerous @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS]{Water Visitor}.

Water Temple Interactivity

Each time the Temple Invader uses its @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.fvOXfL6PG7Z85aUx]{Deplete Orb} @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.muERZZ4Crfqg7VIH]{Deplete Orb} action, one of the six overhead elemental orbs is depleted, resulting in its visual removal from the area map. After the sixth and final orb is depleted, the shield effect protecting the Invader from harm becomes automatically deactivated.

If you need to manually control the number of elemental orbs which remain in play, you can do so by interacting (using the ​ Interaction Tool) with the pedestal of the Lunarium in the center of the area. Note that the Temple Invader is formed around and on top of this pedestal, so it is not initially visible, but you can still interact with it (press the ALT key to display its ​ control icon).

For more details on Interactable Objects and how they work, review the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.lNMkySfNYWS3EvIk#interactable-objects]{Interactable Objects} section of the Player's Guide.

Inside the temple, a massive well of swirling water churns under a central platform; the water is propelled by a mass of gears and cogs that scythe around the central platform, a death trap. Flowing into the well at each of its corners are smaller basins of water, each fed from channels of water rushing from large fonts on the walls.

Four bridges reach across the central basin to a slightly elevated platform surrounded by a glowing shell of energy being fed from unstable swirls and beams of energy which originate from a massive, clattering array of machinery overhead.

Six orbs race around the temple interior on rails, propelled by machinery with an unknown power source. Above it all, a flickering, half-realized projection of Ember and its cosmos hangs in the air. The projection flickers in and out of view, as the majority of the energy meant for it is being siphoned into the shield formed around the elemental on the central platform.

The Temple Invader

The large elemental in the center of the area has no name other than the "Temple Invader," and is an elementally overcharged variant of a @UUID[Actor.jfY4JW1VVPxyMMG8]{Water Wanderer}.

@Embed[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty]

It is reinforced by the presence of three lesser sprites who patrol about the area.

@Embed[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V count=3]

The elementals are hostile toward any intruders. They automatically notice the opening of temple doors — however, they may not notice the party immediately if every character makes a successful [[/skill stealth 15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check. If any character in the party is detected, combat begins immediately.

Temple Invader Tactics (Phase One)

The Invader is aggressive in its desire to protect its domain and hoard the elemental energy that coalesces here. It is sealed, however, behind its @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.fvOXfL6PG7Z85aUx.ActiveEffect.v4aHyBnlJzkiten9]{Impenetrable Shield} @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.ActiveEffect.KvaQIInA8mYrv8De]{Impenetrable Shield}. While shielded, it is immune to all damage types immune to all damage types except Psychic or Void and has a significant bonus to its Physical Defense. During this phase, the Invader is &Reference[restrained] @Condition[restrained] and can perform only a limited set of actions.

The Invader will use its Bonus Action every turn to draw upon the power of an elemental orb using the @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.fvOXfL6PG7Z85aUx]{Deplete Orb} action under the "Elemental Surge" feature. Each usage destroys one of the orbs, but grants the Invader a charge which can be expended in one of the following ways:

  • @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.klzFNbi4ycW4QnFk]{Tidal Wave} (Action)

  • @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.trAjww6k1wMjo7kP]{Freezing Fog} (Action)

  • @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.mP0hckfkpa58vaxy]{Summon Elemental} (Legendary Action)

The Invader will use its Legendary Action every round to summon forth an additional elemental. The Invader will prioritize summoning a @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS]{Water Visitor}, however it can only have one water visitor summoned at any given time. Once a Visitor is already present, the Invader will summon a @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V]{Water Sprite} instead.

The Invader will begin each turn by drawing upon the power of an elemental orb using @Action[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty lunariumDepleteOrb]. Each usage destroys one of the orbs, but immediately grants the Invader a point of Heroism which it can expend in one of the following ways:

  • @Action[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty lunariumTidalWave] to push characters out of the temple or slam them against obstacles.

  • @Action[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty lunariumFreezingFog] to slow characters' movement and make them more vulnerable to attack.

  • @Action[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty elementalSummonVisitor] to conjure a powerful @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS]{Water Visitor} servant.

The Invader will prioritize summoning a water visitor — however, it can only have one such elemental summoned at a given time. Once a water visitor is already present, the Invader will also use @Action[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty elementalSummonSprite] to conjure a lesser minion.

Water Sprite Tactics

Water sprites are weak, but numerous and single-minded in their searching out of nearby targets.

  • Sprites use @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V.Item.eDqzYY8AfoBMv4qD] as their primary attack.

  • If they cannot reach a target to strike, they will use @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V.Item.BQ6leX4yhOPox6ce] to quickly relocate.

Sprites fight to the death and have a disregard for their own safety.

  • Sprites use @Action[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V aqueousTransmission] to quickly relocate into position to Strike.

  • Sprites spend remaining focus on @Spell[frost.fan] if multiple targets are adjacent.

Water Visitor Tactics

Water visitors are smarter, tougher, and more dangerous elementals than their lesser sprite kin. They have a stronger grasp of combat tactics, using sprites as a frontline screen, preferring to instead attack from a distance.

  • Visitors use @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS.Item.wkbIEFj1xGE0cXGw]{Icy Projection} as their primary attack, preferring to maintain distance.

  • If engaged in melee, they make two @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS.Item.eDqzYY8AfoBMv4qD]{Watery Strike} attacks.

  • They will proactively use @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS.Item.BQ6leX4yhOPox6ce]{Aqueous Transmission} to reposition, taking advantage of opportunities to flank enemies or elude attackers.

  • Visitors prefer to maintain distance and Strike from afar using @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS.Item.1W0Ze2SkSAajExco]{Frigid Projection}.

  • Visitors can empower their Cold damage using @Spell[frost.aspect].

  • They will protectively use @Action[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS aqueousTransmission] to reposition, taking advantage of opportunities to flank enemies or elude attackers.

  • Visitors spend remaining focus on @Spell[frost.fan] if multiple targets are adjacent.

Once the Invader has depleted the sixth and final elemental orb, narrate the following development:

The whole structure shudders as vibrations travel through the floor and walls of the temple from the dying machine. The screeching, roaring sound of the machine coming to a halt is terrible but brief, and leaves your ears ringing.

On the central platform over the well itself, the shimmering shield loses cohesion and comes apart, the strands of magical energy vaporizing like mist in the air.

The elemental in the center of the platform writhes in an abstract expression of anger and rears upwards, swelling to fill the space with a mass of frigid malice.

Fulgurite Arrival

Before the beginning of the next combat round, introduce the sudden arrival of the @UUID[Actor.emberFulgrBlades]{Fulgurite Blades} who join the battle as impromptu allies of the party.

As you brace for the impending attack of the now liberated and palpably enraged elemental, the far doors of the temple grind open, drawing the attention of both elemental and heroes alike.

A group of well-armed figures come charging up the steps into the temple and you immediately recognize the familiar faces of the "Fulgurite Blades". Their leader, Sajor, spots you and calls out:

Well, well, look who it is! Looks like you owe Kazra a silver, Leeph.

Kazra pipes up:

I figured they would beat us here. I'll collect after the fight. Be careful, I'll do my best to keep you alive, but I can't be everywhere, and my magic isn't bottomless.

Rorhim grins as he hefts the great sword in his hands.

You heard the priestess, we can't all be reckless fools. Some of us will have to pretend like we're competent!

Enraged by the appearance of yet more interlopers, the large elemental undulates with what can only be rage, its form frothing and foaming as it surges forward.

Add all four of the Fulgurite Blades to the Combat encounter and to initiative order.

@Embed[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu inline]

@Embed[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28 inline]

@Embed[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj inline]

@Embed[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR inline]

With the Temple Invader now free of its shielded enclosure, the battle escalates towards its climax.

Temple Invader Tactics (Phase 2)

In the second phase of the battle the Invader is liberated to engage directly in combat. The Invader will spend any remaining Elemental Surge charges Heroism on the actions described during Phase 1.

  • The Invader uses its @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.BQ6leX4yhOPox6ce] to throw itself into the fray where it can use its @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.eDqzYY8AfoBMv4qD] attack to harm enemies.

  • If it needs to attack distant foes, it can use its @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty.Item.G6UdBarNC2Y4Iqfw] ranged attack to do so.

  • The Invader uses @Spell[frost.aspect] to increase its own damage-dealing potential and @Action[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty aqueousTransmission] to efficiently traverse the battlefield where it can Strike interchangeably from distance or melee.

  • The Invader will continue to use @Action[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty elementalSummonSprite] whenever its current minion expires or perishes.

  • The Invader can cast dangerous spells, using @Spell[frost.strike] and @Spell[frost.pulse] to threaten nearby foes.

The Temple Invader is drunk upon the elemental energy which it has feasted upon for centuries. It craves nothing except the continued torrent of that power. It has no concern for self-preservation and will fight to the death on even if @Condition[broken] .

Sajor Tactics

Sajor is the leader of the Fulgurite Blades. She is a capable spellcaster and tactically shrewd, making intelligent choices about which spells to use that most benefit herself or her allies.

  • Sajor will lean heavily on her extensive repertoire of arcane spells, ideally lining up multiple adversaries in a row to unleash a @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu.Item.zsNZCMgQ1sq7051U]{Lightning Bolt}.

  • Sajor refrains from casting spells above 3rd level, reserving her most powerful spells in case she or her team is at risk of death.

  • Sajor will rely primarily on the Arrow gesture, hurling @Spell[flame.arrow] and @Spell[lightning.arrow] from afar.

  • If threatened in melee, she can use @Spell[flame.fan.push] to knock multiple adversaries backwards or @Spell[lightning.step] to escape from harm.

  • Sajor does not know the Rune of Frost, but nevertheless as a War Mage she may attempt to @Action[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu counterspell] the Invader if it attempts a dangerous spell.

Fulgurite Tactics

The other members of the Fulgurite Blades employ effective teamwork, each specializing in different areas.

  • Rorhim will wade fearlessly into harm, relying on his heavy armor and @UUID[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28.Item.zt1Boed6A1nYh0B8]{Multiattack} to threaten foes.

  • Kazra will focus on sustaining the resources of her allies using restorative spells like @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj.Item.S835C3xtdWDAhpgn]{Cure Wounds} and @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj.Item.45dVk3RJw1bgKtjC]{Healing Word}.

  • Leeph will use @UUID[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR.Item.93TfWPoMzBoaneMx]{Cunning Action} to maneuver into position to unleash @UUID[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR.Item.frhxADwLETnOdKl8]{Sneak Attack} against vulnerable targets.

  • Rorhim will wade fearlessly into harm, making active use of @Action[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28 defend], @Action[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28 legSweep], and @Action[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28 counterStrike].

  • Kazra will focus on sustaining the resources of her allies using restorative spells like @Spell[life.ray] and @Spell[soul.influence].

  • Leeph will maneuver into advantageous positions, using @Action[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR pinningShot] to hinder foes and @Action[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR backstab] to eliminate vulnerable targets.

The Fulgurites will do their best to assist the party and keep them alive, although not at the total expense of their own safety.

After the Battle

Shortly after the conclusion of the battle, before the party or the Fulgurites have time to begin debriefing or investigating the area, an ancient apparition appears to acknowledge their achievement.

Mioroth's Appearance

Return to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.yzgUD9WX351fihbU#the-memory-remains]{The Memory Remains} section in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.yzgUD9WX351fihbU]{Lunar Awakenings} event and engage in this follow-up social encounter before continuing with other exploration.

After the party has met and conversed with Mioroth, they are free to further investigate the temple. These details are presented in the following page, the @UUID[JournalEntry.dCExfRYP8KRVogO2.JournalEntryPage.lMbC6i5ooadxm33z]{Central Lunarium}.

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The following gameplay features apply to the entire Shent Moon Temple area unless stated otherwise in a room description.

Sound

The temple features a constant roar of flowing water and cascading waterfalls inside and outside its walls. As a consequence, hearing in this environment is more challenging. Characters need to raise their voices to speak over the din of flowing water.

Illumination

The exterior areas of the map are exposed to direct sun and moonlight and follow typical expectations for outdoor areas. The exterior of the temple also features several ancient Shent water lights, which cast 5 feet of bright blue light and 10 feet of dim blue light. They are obviously magic.

Inside the temple, the central platform is brightly lit thanks to a large glowing bubble shield. The rest of the temple is dimly lit with swirling blue light and energy being slowly directed into the center of the temple.

Terrain

The area is broken up into the @UUID[.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp], which covers all spaces outside the central structure, and the @UUID[.xDXhEZOud6pfrfNY], which covers everything within the doors of the central structure.

Wading In

The area around the temple is surrounded by knee-deep water (for Medium creatures) and presents &reference[difficult terrain] limits movement due to @UUID[Compendium.crucible.rules.JournalEntry.QhZgmBrdLAGwYy5c#movement-cost-calculation]{a terrain effect} for characters wading through it.

Creatures that end up &reference[prone] @Condition[prone] in this water are submerged, suffering the &reference[suffocating]@Condition[drowning] condition until they stand up again. Characters that can breathe water will not have this problem.

Slippery Slopes

The four aqueduct channels flowing out of the temple can be freely climbed and traversed without issue, though crossing the rushing water is Difficult Terrain.

Attempting to climb, fight, or rush across the water may cause creatures to lose their footing, resulting in falls and sliding down toward the water, but this is left to the GM's discretion.

Elevation

The ceilings of this temple are at 70 feet. Just below that, a ring with rotating machinery is situated at 60 feet. At ground level is a large central platform. In the corners, stairs rise up to 10 feet.

The surface of the water around the central platform is at Height 0. Applying any negative height to a token will place it underwater. The water itself reaches down as far as -30 feet. Anything lower than that places tokens under the ground level of the map entirely.

Submerged Machinery

The spinning machinery presents a danger to any characters between a depth of -15 to -30 feet.

Characters that begin their turn in the water surrounding the central platform must make a successful [[/skill athletics 13]] [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check or be pulled 10 feet downward and moved 10 feet clockwise by the machinery churning the water.

Between -15 and -30 feet below the surface of the water the machines sweep past rapidly, and risk catching creatures in them. Any character who ends their turn at or between these depths must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 13]] Saving Throw [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] or suffer [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage as the machines hit them while going around take damage from a [[/hazard 4 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Machine Impact}.

Characters with a Swim Speed have @Advantage[2] for this hazard.

Enemies

This temple is rich with elemental energy that has attracted the attention of water elementals in the region. As a consequence, the temple has become a hotbed of water elemental activity, and the amorphous beings now infest the place.

  • @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty]

  • At least 3 @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V]{Water Sprites}

  • Possibly 1 or more @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS]{Water Visitors}

Resting

It is possible to rest outside the temple as long as the temple doors have not been opened. Once the temple is opened, however, the elementals within will become hostile and attempt to drive the party off if they refuse to leave.

Fleeing

Should the party need to flee the area, they may do so by retreating from the temple interior toward the edges of the map. The elementals will not pursue them beyond the immediate area around the temple that the map covers.

Central Lunarium.name: Central Lunarium
Central Lunarium.text:
Unavailable During Combat

Investigation of the environment and other details on this page are unavailable until the combat encounter described in the @UUID[JournalEntry.dCExfRYP8KRVogO2.JournalEntryPage.xDXhEZOud6pfrfNY]{Temple Interior} is resolved.

Rising out of the center of the platform is a large stone pillar with a dozen unlabeled stone dials around a large central basin now filled with water. With the destruction of the greater machinery it is connected to, the pillar and its controls are rendered inert.

It seems the central column had several spaces for pieces of stone, crystal, and metal to be slotted into it, possibly manipulating how the machine functions. Many of these slots are empty now, and likely have been for centuries.

Exploring the Temple

Once the elementals are defeated, the party can explore the temple in relative peace. Examination of the grand machinery that spans throughout the temple can reveal some clues towards its history or purpose.

Examining the Interior

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] reveals the presence of subtle inclusions of Abjuration, Transmutation, and Divination symbols throughout the structure, albeit very old and archaic ones. Perhaps these were meant to shape and channel energy through the structure, and reinforce weak points in its construction, keeping the sunken machine from shaking the whole building apart over time.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or [[/knowledge shent]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill religion 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check recognizes the typical, deep reverence for the cosmos that permeates all @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} construction that has been found so far. Symbols, images, reliefs, and such depict the Shent people using this structure to chart the path of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}, to predict tides and rains for the nourishment of crops. This location is part-temple, part-scientific outpost.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge cosmology]] or [[/knowledge shent]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

[[/ancestry emberHulgrun]] characters feel a special connection to this place:

The energy that flows through the ancient stonework of this temple resonates with the very core of your being. Although you don't have a physical heart, the thrumming you currently feel in your chest is perhaps as close to a heartbeat you'll ever know. There's no mistaking that this place was made with the same ancient magic used to create the Hulg'run people.

Giant Cogs

Any character who spends time surveying the remains of the ancient machinery and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check can determine that this machine was a massive planetarium dedicated to a single celestial body: Mayis. It drew power in from an external source, converted it and used it to power the extensive magical markings. This machine used a mixture of illusion, conjuration, divination and evocation magic to draw energy from Mayis and turn it into an illusory projection of the cosmos with a focus on the cycle of Mayis.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or [[/knowledge cosmology]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The damage to the machine is so extensive that repairing it would be a considerable effort. Even with the effort and resources necessary, it's possible there's vital Shent magic, materials, or components which would end up impossible to recreate. It seems that the extensive Abjuration warding on the machine failed long ago, leaving the magical energy unregulated. This failure, coupled with something going awry in the temple's connection to Mayis, effectively turned the machine into a massive beacon for elementals to gather around.

Fulgurites In the Lunarium

While the party is examining the temple, Sajor and the Fulgurite Blades begin actively investigating the most prominent artifact within the temple — the pillar that sits upon the central pedestal of the temple lunarium and the @UUID[Item.yiT683ZD41E18OUh]{Shent Planisphere} it contains. If they are attentive, the party may notice Sajor and the Fulgurite Blades rooting around in the ancient machinery.

Eyes on the Prize

Any character with a [[/skill perception 16 passive format=long]] or who makes a [[/skill perception 14]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] notices the Fulgurites converging on this artifact before they get a chance to pry it free from its housing.

Sajor has recognized its value and intends to claim the object before the party has a chance to interfere. If asked, Sajor is open about her intentions. She states plainly that their group is here specifically to recover artifacts of archaeological significance, and she is not open to dividing or sharing such a find.

If confronted, success on an [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15]] check suggests that Sajor's motives are genuine, if somewhat self-interested. She seeks renown and prestige among the Anachraenum and views this find as one that will elevate her reputation within that guild.

If the party notices the Fulgurites paying special attention to this pillar, they may wish to investigate it themselves.

Examining the Lunarium Pillar

Any character who examines the pillar and makes a [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check discovers an assortment of @UUID[Item.zNtuueUpOtPQX3mR] and a socket which houses the @UUID[Item.yiT683ZD41E18OUh]{Shent Planisphere} (if it has not already been taken).

  • Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: Looking at how it connects to the central pillar, you suspect that the removed disc was likely responsible for controlling the timing of the machine. Without significant repair and this unique artifact, the temple will never function again.

If the party does not notice the Fulgurites examination of the central pillar, or if they do not stop them from removing its contents, read the following aloud:

The grunt of exertion and the scrape of stone draws your attention. Bent over the central pillar of the machine is Rorhim being assisted by Sajor. The pair are muscling a cover off of the central column of the machine.

Rorhim grunts out a confirmation while straining:

Definitely got deformed when this thing broke down.

With a final, heavy pull the cover snaps off, nearly sending Rorhim to the ground. As he tosses the cover into the water he asks:

That what you expected, Sajor?

Sajor's smile is broad and pleased.

Paydirt.

She kneels down, pulling out some fractured cogs and discs, eventually followed by a series of interlocking discs. Rorhim peers over her shoulder easily, actually curious for once.

What is it?

Sajor turns the thing over in her hands, sliding the discs around to see how their notches and holes and carvings line up. She utters a huh to herself.

It's a planisphere, pretty archaic device meant for tracking stars. But this one is special. Obviously because it's Shent, but also because it looks like they accounted for Mayis specifically. Either way, it'll do the trick.

She tucks it away into her pack looking well pleased with herself.

Looting Dissuaded

If the party notices the Fulgurites they can attempt to stop them from taking further actions with one of the following methods:

  • [[/skill persuasion 16]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 16]] to convince them to slow down and talk first.

  • [[/skill deception 18]] [[/skillCheck deception 18]] to distract them by diverting their attention to some other focus.

  • [[/skill intimidation 20]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 20]] to urge them via guilt, obligation, or threat to stop.

If the Fulgurites are successfully deterred, the party can claim the @UUID[Item.yiT683ZD41E18OUh]{Shent Planisphere} themselves, although soon after Sajor will confront them and ask for it. She intends to keep it in her possession because it is potentially a very valuable archaeological find, and she doesn't want to lose sight of it. This item will allow her to pay her team, keep the group afloat, and gain needed stature within the Anachraenum.

Conversing with the Fulgurites

There are a number of topics that the party can speak with the Fulgurite Blades about, including any topics presented in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.Xtmd5E8yiRsnnS6X]{Lightning in a Bottle} which were not already covered.

If the party made a favorable impression on Sajor and the Fulgurite Blades, read the following aloud:

Sajor considers you for a moment and says:

You know, it was interesting working with you, you'd make a decent adventuring team.

You should drop by the All-Fable Keep if you ever make it to Ordain and see about joining the Anachraenum. I'll put in a word for you when I get there.

What is the Planisphere?

It's a planisphere, which itself isn't new. They are used to track time and celestial bodies in that time. They are actually pretty common, and not very special.

This one, however, is very special: It came out of a Shent machine that's thousands of years old. Did they make them the same, did they track the same bodies in the sky? I don't know, but this thing can tell us!

Why do you want it?

I will return it to Ordain, to All Fable Keep, where the Anachraenum will pay for its return. These funds will provide supplies, materials, spellcraft components, and more that our group needs.

Exploration and academic discovery don't pay the wages by themselves. Coin must come from somewhere, and today that somewhere is an ancient Shent ruin.

Is selling it right?

Well look, I'm not just selling it on the open market. It will go through the curators in the Anachraenum so it can be studied. It will either end up in our long-term vaults or sold to an interested scholar or collector who specializes in Shent artifacts.

It will be studied and any knowledge we learn will add to the body of knowledge we have about the Shent.

What can we have?

Sajor shrugs.

Have a look around, see what you can scavenge. Maybe scoop up some of the ice left behind by the elementals. I believe that has some alchemical properties, and might be worth something.

What are you going to do?

Sajor looks at her team, then back to you.

Oh, that's easy — patch up wounds, survey the location, and take notes until Kazra's satisfied. We'll also scoop up anything else of interest, then head back to camp.

What should we do?

Sajor shrugs at you.

I don't know. I'm not your boss. Are you out here for a reason?

Help for the Strayhearth Caravan? If on good terms

Sajor contemplates the request and exchanges glances with Rorhim.

Well … alright, you've been fair to us and we need that road cleared anyway so we can get back to Helkas once we're done here. We can double back the way we came and find your caravan on the road. Between my spells and Rorhim's muscles I suspect we can have that rubble cleared in no time.

Sajor coughs skeptically, saying:

Do you want to come with us? Or are you intent to throw your lives away tracking down some ancient abyssal?

Help for the Strayhearth Caravan? If on poor terms

Sajor scoffs loudly and rolls her eyes in Rorhim's direction.

Yeah … sure. We'll just go lift rocks for you while you run around . Isn't it time for you to leave?

Help us fight the abyssal?

Sajor scoffs loudly.

Not a chance. No matter how curious I or my team might be, we're not gonna follow some specter of an ancient race to the site of an ancient evil to do whatever it is you said they want.

That sounds like a terrible idea, especially since I've got my team's payday in hand. I'm not gonna trade it for an early grave.

What do you know about the Shattering and Abyssals?

Sajor shrugs.

Not much. The Shattering happened, Abyssal entities attacked, and most people in the world died.

Kazra specifies:

In truth, historians don't know a lot about the events of the Shattering, and not much survived. However, that doesn't mean it didn't happen. The signs of the destruction can be found everywhere, it's just that no records survived.

Sajor nods.

Yep, and what records of the time did survive read like horror stories, not historical accounts. Honestly, if even a quarter of that information about Abyssals is true, then only certain death awaits for anyone that decides to mess with them.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The Area Map for @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.dH8d3daTaRNOWLrt] depicts the entirety of the Shent Water Temple; it is discovered during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon] Quest.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.dH8d3daTaRNOWLrt inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Helkas is a peaceful settlement whose only threats tend to come from natural disasters, errant pickpockets, and opportunistic attacks from hungry monsters of the nearby Forest of Stone. However, the party's arrival in this frontier town with the Strayhearth Caravan is a remarkable occasion, and with it comes a memorable encounter — one colored by the furtive villains of the larger campaign to come.

Illumination

Exterior sections of the Area Map are illuminated by the bright light of the sunlight during the day, and are lit with dim light at night — cast from the moons and a multitude of smaller light sources (braziers, firelight, and small lanterns). Interior sections of the map are lit by these numerous light sources, the majority of which shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet.

Terrain

The interior and exterior locations of the map primarily consist of normal terrain, with relatively few exceptions. A few meaningful elevation changes (described below) result in impassable sections of the map, which must be traversed using specific points of ingress and egress.

Elevation

The area map of Helkas has three distinct levels of elevation:

Below Ground [-40 Feet]

The entrance to @UUID[.2Nm18ITo5StmzIt0] is situated below ground level at -40 feet of elevation. Descending to the mine entrance is accomplished by using the @UUID[.z5cVgeR8y4X4LZrU]. Characters who arrive in town can enter this area directly via the southwestern corner of the map.

Ground Level [0 Feet]

The central tier of the town includes most of its featured locations of interest and is situated at ground level (elevation 0). The area is entered from either the southern edge or the western edge of the map.

Upper Level [+50 Feet]

The upper tier of the town is situated at +50 feet of elevation above ground level and is connected by @UUID[.8AIpnYThUYH91wG9]{The Boneway}, which helps define the rim of the cliff that overlooks the central section of town at ground level. A 10-foot-wide wooden stairway on the eastern edge of town allows easy access to this area. Characters who arrive in town can arrive directly in the upper level, entering via the northeastern or northwestern corners of the map.

Enemies

Helkas is ordinarily a peaceful town and there are no enemies or hazards that are generally present.

Dusktide Destruction

Specifically during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.YfJF8Z5XAXFcKmiU]{Dusktide Destruction} Event, the ordinarily peaceful scene of Helkas is brutally attacked by malevolent adversaries.

Fleeing

Should the party need to flee the area, they may do so by retreating toward any of the open edges of the map that would allow them to withdraw from the town, although doing so will abandon the town of Helkas to be ransacked by the Otherhood aggressors.

Resting

During the attack on Helkas, it is not possible to rest except when explicitly specified in the event text. Otherwise, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.c9BRPEfFfUlgNQyz]{The Cragside Tavern} offers affordable rooms where the party can stay in modest comfort.

Leviathan Mine.name: Leviathan Mine
Leviathan Mine.text:
The ground opens up here to reveal a subterranean sprawl conjoined with the skeletal remains of the ancient Leviathan. It's clear that the residents of Helkas use this as one of the primary ways to enter the local mine. Even from here, you can spot signs of the strange, arcane ores that lurk within, identified by traces of their remarkable lambent radiation.

The massive earthen cavity here serves as one of Leviathan Mine's primary entrances, and is accessible by way of a steel and timber lift connected to the ground level near @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.BmnjRCSCsWNZAIyO]{Manfryd's Anvil and Stone}.

During normal working hours, this area is usually overseen by the mine's gregarious foreman, Hode Cinderhaft (Lawful Neutral, Arcturian Fej, he/him). For more information about Hode Cinderhaft, refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.Na9n2GuCfvplomyb]{Overview}.

Strange Excavations

Leviathan Mine is the source of several rare arcane components — one of which is unique to Helkas, while another can only be harvested during the lunar conjunction known as Dusktide. This strange enchanted mine is sometimes referred to as "The Jewel of Helkas," and is responsible for the frontier settlement's enduring prosperity.

The items mined here include:

  • @UUID[Item.V4v7cCEilDA0q2xK]{Dreth Sap}

  • @UUID[Item.ISmlHk1P0U5poOgY]{M’abb Salts}

  • @UUID[Item.6f2sudRdy1XTrJqN]{Steelmarrow}

Any character who examines the mine's interior and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] or [[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check is able to recall most of the properties of these arcane materials, and is aware of their role as rare ingredients in various crafting recipes.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] and [[/knowledge crafts]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

Game State: Dusktide Rising

While Helkas is under siege during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event, Leviathan Mine is abandoned and its standard inhabitants are nowhere to be found.

Mine Elevator.name: Mine Elevator
Mine Elevator.text:
This rickety wooden elevator descends from the ground into the dark bowels of the Leviathan Mine below. Its aged timber, while sturdy and secure, creaks and shudders as the trusty lift moves beneath the rigid tension of steel chains and hempen ropes.

This aged elevator allows characters to move from "Ground Level" to "Below Ground," as described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.cg6gbAmk1PzpdUIX]. It takes the elevator one full turn to move from one level of elevation to another.

The Boneway.name: The Boneway
The Boneway.text:
The colossal skeleton of some long-dead, wormlike creature spans the entire settlement, wrapping its way up and around Helkas like a gruesome shawl. When the light hits them just so, these ossified remains seem to glitter with a strange, preternatural sparkling.

A crude but reliable railway has been installed upon the spine of the serpentine skeleton, enabling the transport of heavy ore to and fro with relative ease.

The Boneway is the colloquial name for this lengthy, exposed portion of the Leviathan that encircles the center of town. Equipped with a meager railway line, most of the flesh of this section of the dead Leviathan has been stripped clean — leaving nothing but petrified bone and craggy earth in its stead.

Helkas Green.name: Helkas Green
Helkas Green.text:
This verdant courtyard is marked by the presence of a spiral arrangement of gray stones, both large and small. Vibrant festival banners are tethered to a pole at the coil's center, and the magenta leaves of nearby aithus trees float by at the behest of a rollicking mountain wind.

Helkas Green is the colloquial name bestowed on the settlement's central courtyard area, which is open to the public at all times. This plaza — defined by the cobblestone paths that wind their way through and around its viridescent expanse — is bordered on all sides by various homes and businesses, and is used by the people of Helkas (and travelers alike) for private and public gatherings.

Manfryd's Anvil and Stone.name: Manfryd's Anvil and Stone
Manfryd's Anvil and Stone.text:
The sound of crackling hearthfire fills this oblong pentagonal building that sits at the southwestern edge of the Green. Multiple anvils and forges decorate this one-room smithy, which appears to see more than its fair share of action.

The forges here at Manfryd's Anvil and Stone are owned and operated by the prodigious blacksmith/stoneworker Manfryd Grimm (Chaotic Good, Arcturian Kivahr, he/him). In tandem with a traditional coal-heated forge, Manfryd utilizes a special Gloamstone forge powered by arcane Duskflame, which serves as a valuable asset during the precarious crafting of Steelmarrow armaments.

Arms & Armor

Manfryd Grimm sells a wide array of the Weapons and Armor found on the associated @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000] tables. Manfryd maintains a modest supply of @UUID[Item.6f2sudRdy1XTrJqN]{Steelmarrow}, but he reserves this rare material for his own crafting rather than wholesale exchanges.

Additionally, a character can purchase Manfryd's services as a Hireling for 2 gp per day.

Game State: Dusktide Rising

While Helkas is under siege during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event, Manfryd's Anvil and Stone is closed for business and its standard inhabitants are nowhere to be found.

The Last Satchel.name: The Last Satchel
The Last Satchel.text:
Situated beneath an overhang of the Leviathan's bones, this small occultist's shop is bedecked with a wide array of components, reagents, concoctions, and curiosities.

An aged wooden sign that hangs above its threshold designates this place as "The Last Satchel," and you can't help but scrutinize the strange and interesting wares that line its cluttered shelves.

The shelves of The Last Satchel are lined with an array of occult wares and arcane materials, including novel spell components developed by proprietor Lorettia Ben-Wren (Chaotic Neutral, Waerd Human, she/her) from the extracts of Leviathan Mine. Lorettia is a patron of her own alchemical arts, and is known for keeping late hours at the shop while studying her reagents with unfettered focus.

For more information about Lorettia Ben-Wren, refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.Na9n2GuCfvplomyb]{Overview}.

Items & Equipment for Sale

The Last Satchel sells a wide array of material spell components and alchemical ingredients, including modest amounts of the following crafting components and specialty items:

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAcid0000000]{Acid}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAntitoxin00]{Antitoxin}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagComponentPo]{Component Pouch}

  • @UUID[Item.V4v7cCEilDA0q2xK]{Dreth Sap}

  • @UUID[Item.xFxXSYlm4CVRXRo8]{Hydroxol Gills}

  • @UUID[Item.ISmlHk1P0U5poOgY]{M’abb Salts}

  • @UUID[Item.XewoieHSHYTb5C0t]{Spider-cap Mushroom}

  • @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.causticPhial0000]

  • @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.antitoxin0000000]

  • @UUID[Item.V4v7cCEilDA0q2xK]{Dreth Sap}

  • @UUID[Item.xFxXSYlm4CVRXRo8]{Hydroxol Gills}

  • @UUID[Item.ISmlHk1P0U5poOgY]{M’abb Salts}

  • @UUID[Item.XewoieHSHYTb5C0t]{Spider-cap Mushroom}

Game State: Dusktide Rising

While Helkas is under siege during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event, The Last Satchel is closed for business and its standard inhabitants are nowhere to be found.

Glinthome.name: Glinthome
Glinthome.text:
The rustic features of a modest temple lit by crystal lanterns scintillate with divine radiance. This sanctuary is marked by several distinct furnishings, including four worn wooden benches, a reliquary of sacred tomes and tools, and a shrine that resembles a library desk more than an altar. The smell of juniper tea lingers here along with the faint sound of celestial chimes.

This modest temple is dedicated to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}, the Elder Goddess of Magic. Lit by arcane braziers of cold Duskflame, this humble place of worship is decorated with an array of Steelmarrow embellishments, and serves as an inviting sanctuary for the people of Helkas. It also provides its caretaker, the tender-hearted cleric Briannon Frost (Lawful Good, Arcturian Wirrun, she/her), with a sense of individual purpose.

Healing Services

A character can hire Briannon's divine spellcasting services as a Hireling for 2 gp per day; she can heal either 5 Wounds or 5 Madness at a cost of [[/award -1gp]]. The kind devotee of Spectra always puts half of her earnings back into the church, and sleeps well at night thanks to this selflessness.

Game State: Dusktide Rising

While Helkas is under siege during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event, Glinthome's doors are closed and its standard inhabitants are nowhere to be found.

The Armarium.name: The Armarium
The Armarium.text:
Wares ranging from dried spices to fresh produce (and everything in between) line the shelves of this general store, alongside stacks of trade goods and bundles of adventuring gear.

Here and there, small art pieces carved from the glittering bones of the mine's eponymous Leviathan decorate the building's wooden walls, hung next to sketched illustrations of the great city of Ordain (and even farther destinations).

This graciously-outfitted general store is owned by the shrewd entrepreneur Cordayne Kohle (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, he/him), one of Leviathan Mine’s key stakeholders and a skilled broker for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}. The Armarium is stocked with nearly anything a traveler of the Forest of Stone could need for a safe and successful expedition. Cordayne minds the store most of the day, along with his assistant shopkeep Thaddeus (Neutral, Arcturian Human, he/him), a sleepy-eyed teenage @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol] with plenty of bills to pay.

For more information about Cordayne Kohle, refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.Na9n2GuCfvplomyb]{Overview}.

Items & Equipment for Sale

The Armarium sells most of the Weapons, Armor, Tools, and Adventuring Gear found in the associated @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000] tables. This well-stocked general store also has modest amounts of the following crafting components for sale:

  • @UUID[Item.V4v7cCEilDA0q2xK]{Dreth Sap}

  • @UUID[Item.6f2sudRdy1XTrJqN]{Steelmarrow}

  • @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{White Inkaro Pearl}

The Armarium offers a 20% discount to members of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher} and their allies.

Game State: Dusktide Rising

While Helkas is under siege during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event, The Armarium is closed for business and its standard inhabitants are nowhere to be found.

The Cragside Tavern.name: The Cragside Tavern
The Cragside Tavern.text:
The front room of this charming alehouse is furnished with six tables and two bars for its revolving supply of patrons. Smells of hearty stew and spiced cobbler linger in the air, and the tavern's hearth crackles with a syncopated rhythm that almost sounds like music amidst the din of the town outside.

The aptly-named Cragside Tavern is a charming watering hole that caters first and foremost to travelers and the local working-class. Maintained by the lively barkeep Eveline Doss (Neutral Good, Arcturian Human, they/them), the Cragside is a place where people from every corner of Aterica can rub elbows with the storied laborers of Leviathan Mine.

For more information about Eveline Doss, refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.Na9n2GuCfvplomyb]{Overview}.

Goods & Services

The Cragside Tavern provides an array of@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbServices00000]{Food, Drink, and Lodging} food, drink, and lodging options that caters to the lifestyles of the poor, the wealthy, and everyone in between. This scrappy inn also has modest amounts of the following local items for sale:

  • @UUID[Item.4mIj4qrLgMompEZG]{Arcturian Liquor}

  • @UUID[Item.DEqm5CXzHdgN4xkH]{Nothrin Meat}

Game State: Dusktide Rising

While Helkas is under siege during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event, The Cragside Tavern is closed for business and its standard inhabitants are nowhere to be found.

Council Hall.name: Council Hall
Council Hall.text:
A sign above the doorway labels this proud wooden edifice as "Council Hall." Certainly, this multi-chambered meeting place must host the settlement's Town Council when they meet, as evidenced by the historical pomp of its decoration and the relative quietude found within.

The rooms which the public see here are kept impressively clean and organized.

Council Hall serves as the meeting place for the settlement's five-person volunteer Town Council, a group of unpaid elected officials that meet semi-weekly to discuss matters of local importance. The various chambers here show signs of regular use by the Council and local citizens of Helkas alike, who are allowed to use the northernmost meeting room as a gathering place (if the proper requisition forms are appropriately filled out, of course).

The town magistrate Sadri Zhalimorne uses the southernmost chamber here as her office, and can be found here at various times throughout any regular work week.

@Embed[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]

Game State: Dusktide Rising

While Helkas is under siege during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event, the doors of Council Hall are closed and its standard inhabitants are nowhere to be found.

Boneway Stairs.name: Boneway Stairs
Boneway Stairs.text:
This sturdy wooden stairway ascends to a sidewalk lining the Leviathan's ossified remains, where a railway crowns the ancient creature's skeletal form.

The Boneway Stairs connect the eastern edge of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.MRrbXWcRm5QNSZnL]{Helkas Green} on the Ground Level with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.8AIpnYThUYH91wG9]{The Boneway} on the Upper Level, and must be used if a character wishes to traverse the terrain quickly while changing elevation.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The Area Map for @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas} depicts the central section of town, including a few of its most prominent locations. This area serves as the scenery for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event in the Chapter 1 Main Quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai]{The Winding Trail}.

  • If desired, the party can also explore this Area Map during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq]{Dusktide Revelry} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.YfJF8Z5XAXFcKmiU]{Dusktide Destruction} Events, which are each initially configured for their own dynamic Vistas.

  • Additional information about the various buildings of central Helkas (and their inhabitants) are located in the Gameplay Details section of this walkthrough.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2 inline]

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The Area Map for the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.hxHaYXXkGDsZ8cGv] depicts a small section of the Dripstone Biome where numerous waterfalls converge and a powerful Abyssal entity is presently trapped.

Generally, the party would explore this area while undertaking the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.tJfhxYBC1weqR6K1]{An Ancient Battle} Event of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over the Moon} Quest. However, it is possible they could encounter this area independently, in which case they can still face and battle the Writing Whisperer found here, but without some additional context to understand its presence.

Difficulty

The combat encounter in this area is designed for a Level 2 party. If the party has not yet reached Level 2 or is low on resources, provide clues that foreshadow the danger level, giving the players a chance to turn back if they wish.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.hxHaYXXkGDsZ8cGv inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The following gameplay features apply to the Writing Grave area unless specifically stated in a sub-location description.

Illumination

The exterior areas of this map are exposed to direct sun and moonlight, and follow typical expectations for outdoor areas.

Terrain

This area is broken up into various stone steps that descend toward the pool where the waterfalls collect. Transitioning between these terraces or moving through the pools of water is &reference[difficult terrain] difficult terrain.

Elevation

The elevation difference between terraced levels of this map is negligible such that — from a mechanical perspective — the entire area may be treated as zero elevation.

The cliffs surrounding the perimeter of the area are several hundred feet tall and impossible to climb without substantial effort, training, or equipment.

Enemies

This area contains a single notable adversary, the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Writhing Whisperer}. Details about this combat encounter are presented in the @UUID[JournalEntry.iHDQeYHNXuIrJvqc.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Waterfall Nexus} page.

Hazards

Tainted Ground

The ground is badly tainted by otherworldly Abyssal energies, making it somewhat hazardous to rest here. While the party is generally safe for the short period they are present here, prolonged exposure to the energies will begin to have an effect on their minds.

Characters that complete a Short or Long RestRecovery or Rest in this area must make a [[/save charisma 16]] Saving Throw withstand the hazard of the [[/hazard 4 willpower psychic harmless]]{Tainted Ground} or or suffer a single effect from the @UUID[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X]{Minor Abyssal Madness} table upon the conclusion of their rest.

Waterfall Nexus.name: Waterfall Nexus
Waterfall Nexus.text:
The knee-deep water surrounding the mound in the center of this space is brackish, and an acrid smell overcomes your senses. You feel a tingle of anticipation as you inch closer — unbeckoned excitement that seems to pull you forward.

Moving through this area can be hazardous.

Treacherous Terrain

The water in this area is knee-deep and constitutes Difficult Terrain. Creatures that become &Reference[prone] @Condition[prone] within the water are submerged and cannot speak or breathe.

This area is @UUID[JournalEntry.iHDQeYHNXuIrJvqc.JournalEntryPage.SOoDEXNc3JJ0iitb#hazards]{Tainted Ground}, and unsafe for the party to remain in for a lengthy period.

The party must decide whether to do battle with this foe, negotiate with it, or flee.

Speaking to the Abyssal

Conversing telepathically with the Abyssal is deeply unpleasant and inescapable, as the being can insert its words unwanted into the minds of any creatures it senses nearby. It can transmit words, distant emotions, faint images, and even imagined sensations.

An Abyssal Offer

Parties willing to unleash this Abyssal entity into the world will be handsomely rewarded, with each character receiving a unique feature gaining a unique talent. If the party accepts this deal, see @UUID[.#aiding-the-whisperer]{Aiding the Whisperer}.

The @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Whisperer} can naturally sense the thoughts and emotions of creatures around it. While it finds mortal minds simplistic and noisy, it can quite easily sift through them to find things to use. Consider having the Whisperer appeal to the interests, fears, wants, and goals of the party to help its bid for release. It doesn't change the nature of the offer, but it can make it more tempting.

Peering Into the Abyss

The Abyssal is an @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.T0hhbtqHNVaMrmf9]{Abyssal Monster}, @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.inscrutable00000], and immune to any attempt or effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts.

Manipulation is quintessential to the nature of this creature, however, the Whisperer does tend to be truthful. It only selectively omits details or twists the truth when to avoid harming its chances of becoming free.

Any character may attempt an [[/skill insight 30]] a [[/skillCheck deception 30]] check to ascertain the Writhing Whisperer's intentions.

A character that fails this check senses the creature wants to end its detainment — to be free, to explore, to wander, and not be trapped in one place, wallowing in ancient rot.

A character that succeeds on this check senses that the Whisperer wants to be free of its binding — to roam, to explore, and be free. It has been trapped for thousands of years, and yearns to break loose.

  • Result of 35+: The Whisperer not only wishes freedom, but to seek out other mortal beings and pluck at their thoughts like so many strings on a lute.

The Whisperer opens any discussion by reiterating its offer of power. It wants nothing but to be free, and is prepared to grant a portion of its own power to make this happen. If the party asks what exactly they are being offered for setting it free, the Whisperer struggles to conceptualize it, communicating the following:

An unsettling feeling of amusement tries to take root in your mind. You realize that the sensation is this creature's giddy laughter, mixed with deep contempt.

"If you agree. If you help. I will give what all want, crave, and need — strength."

It seems to ponder the word, and alternatives.

"Strength... knowledge… growth… expansion… improvement…"

"You are lesser… release me, and I will make you… more."

The party can speak with the Whisperer to learn more about it, though such knowledge may not be especially comforting, as it is a truly alien creature.

What are you?

You feel a flurry of thoughts blooming in your mind, concepts forming and being discarded as a frustration not your own grows in your head.

"I am what the void beyond is made of. Mortal words cannot describe the totality of nothingness. I am the non-light beyond the Weave."

The trickle of thoughts and feelings stop and crystalize.

"Names — there are none for us. Your primitive minds would know us by emotion alone."

"Fear."

"Sorrow."

"Despair."

"Death."

Each word is accompanied by a sudden stab of its associated emotion.

What do you want?

The concepts that return to you are simplistic and primitive:

"Hunger… recovery… regrowth…"

You sense that the creature is weakened, perhaps significantly so, and that it desires time or opportunity to heal.

About the Shattering?

The creature remains silent for a time. A sensation like dismissal weaves through your minds. The Whisperer's voice forms in your head:

"Ember’s destiny... threads you cannot weave together. Minds too small... grasping at shadows… you cannot even see the light that casts them."

"No. Not your concern."

"Do not ponder... lest you unravel."

What happened here?

The thoughts that return to you are straightforward:

"Hunting… the prey… it resisted… animal… animal! Much death."

You feel unbidden excitement swell within you:

"Crushing… breaking… grasping and tearing!"

About the Shent? About Mioroth?

You feel a sensation of ennui, as if the question failed to take hold.

"Is it dead? Or will it yet be?"

Fighting the Whisperer

Should the party confront the Whisperer in combat, it will no longer negotiate and will not hesitate in its attempts to destroy them.

A feeling of desperate rage invades your minds, inciting a fear that makes your blood run cold. The Whisperer seizes the sword with its many tentacles and begins to strain against it, shimmers of magic rippling through the old, tarnished steel. You hear its pained voice in your head:

"Oblivion… always they seek oblivion!"

Impaled Foe

At the beginning of combat, the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Whisperer} is affected by the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.ActiveEffect.zxB53n7RxNZPleui]{Impaled} condition, which causes it to be &Reference[restrained]makes it immobile and less able to Dodge. However, the Whisperer remains dangerous, and is capable of fighting at full capacity despite being pinned in place.

Whisperer Tactics

The Writhing Whisperer is intelligent, and well versed in fighting mortals. It focuses on drawing enemies closer to it using its various abilities so that it can hold them in place and whip them to death with its tendrils.

Intensely cruel, the Whisperer attempts to keep wounded foes from fleeing to safety, or healers from reaching wounded and downed allies in need of rescue. It fights without regard for its own safety, determined to kill its foes and escape — or die trying.

The Whisperer uses its@UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.yxlzyXTpsEf4QiI9]{Grasping Form} ability to grapple nearby enemies. It can use this ability on already grappled enemies to further Restrain them.

  1. It makes two @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.lfUDtJ8hdeULQzqa]{Shadow Tendril} melee attacks, preferring to attack Restrained and Prone targets first. Alternatively, it can use its @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.uZ5ttJPT5L2MwDmx]{Psychic Sting} ranged attack for distant foes.

  2. It has two Bonus Actions it uses on its turn to hinder its enemies. Its @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.ItwLU9dQYy9xDqkp]{Extend Form} feature allows it to place a @UUID[Actor.UXpL07GsaMzGCUVh] on the battlefield, or reposition existing ones as it needs. It can also use its @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.FEJ4hGkg3cbLUp9i]{Drag Victim} ability to keep Grappled enemies from getting too close or too far away.

  3. The Whisperer has two Legendary Actions it uses between its turns to control the battlefield and keep enemies inside its reach. It uses the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.KQRvDGowc6ihejLu]{Abyssal Whip} to grab and pull distant enemies closer, and its @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.SzwWnAgr25vDeHKu]{Abyssal Whispers} which deals damage and forces them to use their Reaction coming closer.

The Whisperer has several primary tactics that it employs:

  1. Deal with enemies who keep their distance using @Action[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN abyssalWhispers] and @Action[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN abyssalWhip] to force enemies closer.

  2. Summon @UUID[Actor.UXpL07GsaMzGCUVh]{Writhing Whisperer Tendrils} using @Action[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN extrudeTendril] to apply pressure from multiple angles and create opportunities for @Condition[flanked] attacks.

  3. Grasp enemies using @Action[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN graspingForm], holding them @Condition[restrained] at a distance where they can be attacked by the Whisperer but not attack it in return.

The Whisperer is desperate for freedom and will risk anything to escape its current predicament. If it becomes @Condition[broken] or is at risk of death, it may attempt to flee the area if escape seems possible, otherwise it will fight to the death, creating an area of @Action[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN abyssalRemains] upon its demise.

Breaking Free

Once the Whisperer is reduced to under half its Hit Point maximum under half its total Health it will successfully rip itself free of the Shent blade that impales it. When this happens, disable the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.ActiveEffect.zxB53n7RxNZPleui] active effect and read the following:

A soundless, psychic scream rocks the battlefield as the Whisperer rips itself free of the blade, its amorphous form tearing open as a result. The Abyssal creature slumps briefly to the ground, and the air is filled with psychic static from this being's suffering as an ancient wound is ripped open anew.

"If I am to die… let us share the experience."

You can feel its attention fixate upon you once again.

Once the Whisperer is finally slain, read the following aloud:

With the final blow against the Whisperer landed, its form shudders and buckles into itself as through being pressed upon by an immense weight. Ripples of psychic screams emanate from it, sensations of fear, hatred, and pain following immediately after.

Then the creature quickly unravels, turning into a viscous, oil-like substance that is all but impossible to collect or get hold of. In its wake is nothing but silence.

Over the Moon Quest
