If exploring this area as part of the [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer]] Event in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over the Moon} Quest, return to the Event page and proceed from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.tJfhxYBC1weqR6K1#the-whisperer-destroyed]{The Whisperer Destroyed} section of gameplay.

Aiding the Whisperer

If the party wants to entertain the idea of helping the Whisperer, the solution to its problem should be fairly obvious: a massive sword is driven through its body and needs to be pulled out. However, if the party needs guidance, the Whisperer can offer it, albeit cryptically.

A mixture of frustration and anticipation ripples through your mind.

"Draw the sliver of corpse-made steel from this eternal vessel. Let this form return to that of un-binding. The sword… the faceted shard-shackle… bound with cosmic energies that are anathema to this vessel."

Removing the Sword

The sword is huge, and deeply sunken into the earth. It can be extracted with twenty minutes of physical effort, made shorter with appropriate tools, such as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagShovel00000]{Shovel}. The Abyssal will not attack or harm anyone attempting to remove the blade, but it is too weakened to meaningfully assist.

Destroying the sword may also be an option if it is subjected to concentrated attacks. The sword has AC 14, 20 Hit Points, resistance to Force damage, immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and vulnerability to Thunder and Acid damage. Care should be taken when targeting the blade. If the Whisperer is struck — even unintentionally — it will immediately attack the party, tolerating no carelessness from what it considers to be lesser life forms.

If the party frees the Whisperer from beneath the ancient blade, read the following aloud.

As you sword loosens from the earth, the Whisperer slips free. A ripple of relief and unbridled glee crawls into your mind, followed by a sensation of gratitude.

As promised. Power. Strength. More than your simple mortal frames. Strength to endure what petty and irrelevant trials await your short, meaningless lives.

Tendrils of blackness snap out, piercing your forehead as the Whisperer's mind joins with yours. Power surges through your body. You feel your mind being broken apart, spread too thin, and folded over like parchment as this being begins to work parts of you into new shapes. Your muscles ache, your heart races, your lungs refuse air and you feel for a moment like death would be relief. Then all goes black.

While the characters are momentarily unconscious, they receive an infusion of Abyssal potency.

Psychic Backlash

Assisting the Writhing Whisperer causes a backlash of psychic energy to affect the entire party. Each character must succeed on a [[/save charisma 16]] Saving Throw. On a failure, face [[/hazard 6 psychic willpower morale harmless]]{Abyssal Madness}. If affected, Abyssal energies suffuse the character's body and they become permanently afflicted by one random effect from the @UUID[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X]{Minor Abyssal Madness} table.

Abyssal Infusion

A party that chooses to release the Writing Whisperer gains the @UUID[Item.YGRKaXVCulhVb5yD]{Abyssal Insights} feature. They can use this feature once per day, and as their attunement with the Abyss grows, so does the feature. Characters that successfully save against the psychic backlash above may elect to refuse the feature if they so choose.

After receiving or rejecting this granted boon, the characters regain their senses.

You awaken on your back, soaked through with the brackish water of this grave. There is no sign of the Whisperer, only the vacant remnants of the giant blade that pinned it to the earth.

Over the Moon Quest

If exploring this area as part of the [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer]] Event in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over the Moon} Quest, return to the Event page and proceed with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.tJfhxYBC1weqR6K1#the-whisperer-released]{The Whisperer Released} section of gameplay.

Aftermath

The party may want to look over the corpses in the nexus before or after dealing with the Whisperer. There is not much to be found, but examining the remains can confirm suspicious or provided simple insights into the events the unfolded here.

Old Bones

A successful [[/skill medicine 16]] [[/skillCheck medicine 16]] on the dead giants makes it clear that they have been dead for thousands of years. There's hardly anything to work with or glean from them, though it is strange how the corruption or rot in this space has not seeped into them like everything else.

With a successful [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check while examining the ground you can plainly see signs of the local plants growing along but not past the line of corrupted earth. More interesting, you can see how the old, dead growth piles up, leading you to believe the taint spread over time rather than appearing all at once.

With a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check you note numerous rusted, broken, discarded Shent weapons and artifacts in the area around the central mound. They are all corroded and weather beaten beyond use, and many are likely to crumble if disturbed, but they could prove valuable to historians.

Spending some time gathering these items yields @UUID[Item.aVCYxp700VbOw0BL] which are both useless and worthless on their own, but could be valuable to a collector of antiquities.

Giant Gems

One @UUID[Item.y6lXtFPEDoPA71c6] and one @UUID[Item.yl5MGytX6I9edRCy]{Chipped Spinel} can be pried from the crossguard of the great sword using a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.V5UAjT3ed6sDNtgm] or other suitable toolafter a successful [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check. Doing so takes about 20 minutes of work.

Terraced Pools.name: Terraced Pools
Terraced Pools.text:
Character with [[/attunement emberAbyss]] feel a heightened connection to this place, experiencing the following:

As you near the nexus of the waterfalls, you can feel a roiling, twisting sensation in your chest. It extends out of your body, crawling down your limbs like a thousand invisible insects. After a moment, the feeling subsides… but in its place is the lingering sensation that you are perceived. Something knows you are here.

Then proceed with the normal area description:

As you take in your surroundings, you realize that you are surrounded by death in many forms, from the stark line where living plants turn rotten in tainted earth, to the numerous corpses of large humanoids that must be remnants of the Shent.

All round them the corroded remains of armor and weapons poke out of the centuries of dead growth, making it evident that you are standing on the site of a one-sided massacre that claimed the lives of numerous warriors.

At the middle of the crater-like depression is a huge, tarnished, and rusting Shent sword. Much too large for any mortal of Ember to use, half its length is driven into the earth. Pinned through by the ancient steel is an unsettling, almost amorphous creature that writhes around the corroded blade, grasping at it like any wounded thing might.

Considering the Creature

The creature pinned beneath the ancient blade is a Writhing Whisperer, a terrible Abyssal monster that first appeared during the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear}.

@Embed[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]

The party may attempt to identify what manner of creature this is.

The Abyssal Interloper

The Writhing Whisperer is beyond the ken of most mortals of Ember, its kind not having been witnessed for centuries, if not millennia.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 30]] [[/skillCheck arcana 30]] check identifies the creature.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge abyssal]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Upon an unlikely success, the character recognizes the attributes of a "Whisperer," a terrible monster mentioned in accounts of great horror during the aftermath of the Shattering. They recall that such creatures are likely to manipulate and twist one's own thoughts, should the mind be left unguarded.

As soon as a member of the party is within 120 feet of the Whisperer, it becomes aware of them due to its ability to sense thoughts and communicate telepathically. Being perceived by the Writhing Whisperer causes the party to immediately be assaulted by intrusive telepathic contact.

Looking upon the being in its totality causes your mind to recoil. It is not of this world… and after a moment too long looking at it, the mass becomes aware of you in return.

Its voice reaches out to your mind like a long, bony finger pressing into your forehead. Its voice is like oil and sand in your mind, sliding over it and grinding against your very thoughts.

"Mortals … sharp minds … gifts … we offer."

The words, if they can be called such, are awkward, as if lacking total familiarity with their meaning.

"A gift … we provide … for mutual gain."

The voice continues sliding its way through the recesses of your mind.

"Approach … release … reward … receive."

The intrusion stills as if awaiting some response.

Abyssal Intrusion

First contact with the Writhing Whisperer has an immediately deleterious effect on the minds of the party. They must make a successful [[/save charisma 16]] Saving Throw withstand the [[/hazard 4 willpower psychic harmless]]{Abyssal Intrusion} as the Whisperer makes telepathic contact with them and begins to weave itself into their minds for easy communication. Characters who fail to resist this effect immediately incur a single effect from the @UUID[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X]{Minor Abyssal Madness} table.

The Whisperer is a being of absolute evil, but it will honor a pact made in exchange for its release. It is impossible for the characters to discern this, however, due to the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.T0hhbtqHNVaMrmf9]{Abyssal} @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN.Item.inscrutable00000] nature of the creature.

Assessing the Environment

The party may also want to examine — from a distance — the massive blade driven through the Whisperer, which it can do without provoking the creature.

Pinning Steel

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who makes a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notes that the blade appears to have been hastily carved with numerous magical symbols and runes, many of which appear to be blackened and burnt. In addition, there are two very large red gems in the crossguard of the sword. These could be valuable if removed and appear decorative, rather than tied to the sword's magic.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check while examining the sword and its runes surmises that the markings are of numerous magical fields, though mostly Evocation and Abjuration . They were built around preserving the steel and holding the monster in place. However, many of the runes are burned out, and it likely won't hold forever.

As soon as the party approaches the creature or otherwise takes action against it, proceed to the encounter described on the @UUID[JournalEntry.iHDQeYHNXuIrJvqc.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Waterfall Nexus} page.

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

Travel through Yakoshta Mine does not have a required order or direction — characters can make their way through the mine however they see fit, using either the bridges and passageways on the edges of the map or the mining carts that make their way through the center. As they do, they can:

  • Rescue miners under attack and clear the mine of small oozes.

  • Find evidence of the contaminant that is affecting the oozes.

  • Uncover details of Jasper's plan for the mine.

  • Defeat the Giant Luminous Ooze in the Excavation pit by battling it directly or destroying it with explosives.

Illumination

The Kaleidoscope crystals throughout the mine provide dim illumination. These crystals have been cut back, which counteracts the immediate effects of disorientation normally found when exposed to @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal} — the party is not affected unless they spend a Long Rest Rest within the mine or they break the crystals apart.

Within each cavern, unless indicated, the light of the kaleidoscope crystals is supplemented by magically lit lanterns that hang from hooks on the walls. These lanterns provide 15 feet of bright light and an additional 15 feet of dim light. Upon both mine carts is affixed a lantern which produces 15 feet of bright light and an additional 15 feet of dim light.

Terrain

In general, the mine has normal terrain. Climbing over barricades or climbing up or down to a different vertical level counts as difficult terrain.

Elevation

Within the tunnels, ceilings are 30 feet high.

Deadly Falls

The bottom of the chasm is 300 feet below the tracks that run above it. A fall from this height is almost certainly fatal. A character that falls from a platform into the chasm has a final opportunity to save themselves from falling by succeeding on a [[/save dexterity 13]] saving throw [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] . If successful, the character grasps a nearby handhold and hauls themselves back to safety, becoming &Reference[Prone] @Condition[prone] instead. On a failure, the character falls to their death and their body is unrecoverable except by magical means.

Less Deadly Falls

At your discretion, you may allow for a character that falls to instead take [[/damage 1d8 bludgeoning]] damage as they break their fall on a stray piece of scaffolding.tumbling below and breaking their fall with a [[/hazard 5 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Scaffolding Impact}.

Mine Carts and Tracks

Throughout the mine are two lines of mine track, each with an operable mine cart. Each cart occupies a single 5 foot square and can hold one creature of medium size or smaller or can be filled with items equivalent to a 5 foot cube in size and weighing less than 1000 pounds.

Operating the Cart

Each mine cart is an ​ Interactable Object. As the Gamemaster, you can cause the cart to move forwards, backwards, or stop by clicking on it using the interaction tool.

  • A Left-Click causes the cart to move forwards or to stop moving if it was previously moving backwards.

  • A Right-Click causes the cart to move backwards or to stop moving if it was previously moving forwards.

When a cart begins moving, any appropriately sized character who occupies the same grid space as the cart may be designated as a passenger. This character will travel with the cart until stopped.

Visualizing the Tracks

As the Gamemaster you may visualize the current track layout by activating the ​ Tracks Visualization toggle in the Canvas Controls toolbar on the left side of the interface.

Operating the Tracks

Each track switch is an ​ Interactable Object. As the Gamemaster you can click on a track switch to toggle it to its opposite position. Note that the southern-most switch is inoperable unless its lever is recovered.

Kaleidoscope Crystals

If characters wish to extract a @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal} from one of the caverns, either use as a source of light or to break as a method of briefly distracting one of the luminous oozes, they must break it off of the cavern wall/floor. Breaking the crystal from the wall requires either a successful [[/check dexterity 14]] or a successful [[/check strength 18]] [[/skill athletics 14]] check while using a suitable tool (pickaxe, hammer, etc.) to rip it from the cave wall.

In either case, failure results in some portion of the crystal shattering, causing the release of magical energy that immediately inflicts a @UUID[RollTable.CW4O54YLtXBarVjz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal Effect}.

Alchemical Contaminant

The contaminant is leaking down into the @UUID[.xm50UssrvERyHUig]{Glowing Ore Pit} from above, as noted in the readaloud for that section of the mine. A pure sample of @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0]{Aedir Construct Fluid} can be taken by using a vial to collect it from the overlook above the ore pit. Elsewhere, the contaminant has been partially digested by the oozes and instead yields@UUID[Item.jnqAVPfmdEzxuLaA]{Vial of Luminous Goo}.

The Giant Ooze

The @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07]{Giant Luminous Ooze} in @UUID[.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit} can be defeated in two ways:

Heroes may face this adversary directly in battle, potentially with the aid of @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozelings}, @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystals}, or @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flasks} which can provide some assistance.

Alternatively, a clever party may trigger a deadly explosion using the @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU] found in the @UUID[.6OAhqzuyGkUvdWf6]{Supply Cache}. The steps necessary to accomplish this plan are detailed in @UUID[.oYxMXI3OD4YPUfxz]{Ooze Go Boom!}.

Loading Zone.name: Loading Zone
Loading Zone.text:
A mining cart has been toppled, spilling its metal ingots on the floor. Three miners are using the cart as an impromptu barricade, as gold and silver glowing oozes advance on them, slowly but relentlessly. As you enter, one of the miners calls out in your direction.

Sellen, is that you? You have to get us out of here!

Three @UUID[Actor.DRXKaLp3lhEQuKoD]{Arcturian Miners} — Shel, Trianda, and Gravin from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl.JournalEntryPage.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2#battle-at-the-loading-dock]{Battle at the Loading Dock} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl.JournalEntryPage.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2]{Saving Jasper} Event — are hiding behind the wagons in the corners of the room while a trio of oozes advance on their position.

@Embed[Actor.Jhymp0ntXyx78Gx3 inline count=2]

@Embed[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE inline]

Ooze Tactics

The oozes are hostile — all three converge on the party as soon as any are engaged in combat. They focus their attacks on the party, ignoring the lesser threat of the miners cowering in the corner.

The oozes are hostile — all three converge on the party as soon as any are engaged in combat. They focus their attacks on the party, ignoring the lesser threat of the miners cowering in the corner.

  • The Silver Oozes advance aggressively, striking out with their @UUID[Actor.Jhymp0ntXyx78Gx3.Item.yPo0LseLmDBKYiNq]{Electrified Pseudopod} whenever it is available.

  • The Gold Ooze behaves more erratically, using its @UUID[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE.Item.UXWVxVkQsinqYPdn]{Stretch} and @UUID[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE.Item.b7l42H3vQGu9mka2]{Split} actions to increase in size and multiply in number.

The oozes are hostile — all three converge on the party as soon as any are engaged in combat. They focus their attacks on the party, ignoring the lesser threat of the miners cowering in the corner.

  • Both types of oozes have the exceptional ability to @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeMultiply0000] or @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeSubdivide000], but a limited Focus pool with which to perform these actions. Oozes favor use of Subdivide if they are near full Health, and will use Multiply if they become wounded.

  • The Silver Oozes advance aggressively, striking out with their @UUID[Actor.Jhymp0ntXyx78Gx3.Item.2AEiIP3Q06gvY2O1]{Electrified Pseudopod} whenever it is available.

  • The Gold Ooze behaves more erratically, using its @UUID[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE.Item.oozeBewilderingG] to sap the willpower and morale of its attackers.

Frightened Miners

The miners are well-hidden on a ledge in the corner of the room behind an impromptu barricade created by a mining cart and are not intended to be part of initiative order, though they can be added in as a group if the party needs additional support. They avoid direct combat, but three remaining @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flasks} which they may toss over the barricade at the oozes given an opportunity to do so.

After the Battle

The cavern is a mess, full of the aftermath of the battle — wood and metal and ooze bits spread across the ground, which the surviving miners quickly begin working to set right. The cavern itself is large and open, with a silver symbol painted on one of the walls that vaguely resembles a mining cart.

Archways from the cavern appear to lead deeper into the mine, towards a tunnel in one direction and a creaking bridge in the other. An empty mining cart sits on tracks that wind their way into the mine’s dimly-lit depths, while a second set of tracks has been ravaged by someone or something — it is missing a large chunk of its tracks and there is no cart in sight.

Quest Progression

Refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl.JournalEntryPage.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2#battle-at-the-loading-dock]{Battle at the Loading Dock} in the event entry for conversation and information learned from surviving miners.

Exploring the Mine

There are four exits from this cavern further into the mine, though not all are usable:

  • A passageway leads into further tunnels towards @UUID[.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb]{Jasper's Office}

  • The upper (blue) mining track is destroyed and the gap cannot be traversed. For more, see @UUID[.GtpDWpInS0unttZW#blue-mining-tracks]{Blue Mining Track}.

  • The lower (red) mining track has a mining cart on it and can be used with or without the cart. For more, see @UUID[.GtpDWpInS0unttZW#red-mining-tracks]{Red Mining Track}.

  • A bridge leads across to the Excavation Pit, but it has been severely damaged and leads to a rockfall on the other side. For more on player options, see @UUID[.0LXzxGaXrMFhFREp#entrance-bridge]{Entrance Bridge}.

Old Ore Pit.name: Old Ore Pit
Old Ore Pit.text:
This largely empty space has been fully mined out, but there are a few piles of ore that appear ready for transport. Silver paint on the side of a crate of pick-axes reads "In Emergency, Break Crystals!"

Two miners are wielding pickaxes against a copper-colored ooze with the same glow and aggressive behavior as the oozes you encountered at the Loading Dock. One of them uses the pick-axe to break open a Kaleidoscope Crystal. As soon as the crystal shatters, the copper ooze stops in its tracks and moves its pseudopod towards the object, giving the second miner the opportunity to land a killing blow.

With the ooze dead, the first miner glances inside a bag they are carrying, as if reassuring themselves that whatever was inside the bag is still there.

As party members enter the room, they encounter a pair of miners who have together held off a single @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ]{Luminous Copper Ooze}. The ooze has now dissipated into @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ.Item.XIZ8BkDMSwgsDrZp]{Copper Flakes}.

Valka (Chaotic Good, Arcturian Hulg'run, she/her)

A young Hulg'run who is shorter than most of the others and has tufts of moss growing out of splits in the rock of her body, perhaps suggesting some Thornling heritage, is carrying the large bag. It contains the wheel from the junction. She wanted to protect it from any ooze damage, but will give it to the party with a successful [[/check charisma 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, if they mention being sent by Sellen, or if they make it clear that they are trying to save Jasper.

Danith (Lawful Neutral, Arcturian Hulg'run, he/him)

A Hulg'run whose face includes geometric spikes that might resemble piercings on another humanoid, is catching their breath.

Exhausted Miners

Valka and Danith are eager to leave the mine at once, but will answer a few brief questions before leaving. If asked how to reach a certain part of the mine they will gladly share directions with the party.

If pressed for information about the operations of the mine or Jasper's activities, they try to leave but with a with a successful [[/check persuasion 12]][[/check persuasion 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] or[[/check intimidation 13]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 13]] check they will cooperate.

If cooperative, they will share the following information:

  • Breaking a @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal} will temporarily mesmerize nearby oozes, it can be risky for whomever breaks them open though.

  • They removed the crystals from this room, but more can be found around the mine - the closest location for them is in the @UUID[.wmq1IA9LGtRNGrtq]{Mine Cart Loading Station}.

  • It's unclear who wrote the sign about using the crystal, but signs point towards Jasper.

  • Valka took the @UUID[Item.Sbw2OnVAq9Om5qpa]{Yakoshta Junction Wheel} to protect it for Jasper who seemed think the elevator mining cart could help against the oozes.

The Junction Wheel

The miners can be persuaded to hand over the @UUID[Item.Sbw2OnVAq9Om5qpa]{Yakoshta Junction Wheel} as long as the party is honest in their intentions to use it to help rescue Jasper and other miners.

Otherwise, they will only hand over the wheel with a successful [[/check persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] or[[/check intimidation 13]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 13]] check. If this check is failed, they refuse to hand over the wheel and run for the exit.

How did you hold off the ooze?

Just followed the sign on the floor and broke some of the Kaleidoscope Crystal with our pickaxes — got them to stop what they were doing and stare long enough for us to get our hits in.

Will any crystal work?

No idea, but you can try — luckily they're all over the place here. If you're looking for a bunch, check the room right to the south of us, where we usually load up the ore cards. But don't forget, messing with them can mess you up a bit, so maybe only use when you really need then?

Who painted the sign?

Couldn't say for certain but it does look a bit like Jasper's handwriting. No time to check though — even with the crystals we barely stayed alive. Time to get out of here.

What is in the package you're carrying?

Wheel for the junction down the road. Didn't want the oozes messing it up. Before Jasper ran off, he was muttering something about the mining cart and the elevator, so I'm keeping it safe for him. Or I was, anyway. Now I've gotta save my own hide.

If party members investigate or are curious about the painted sign, they can determine the following information.

The Anonymous Painter

A character who [[/check perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check notices that the paint came from a can of silver paint and brush that sits near the painted sign. The handle on the brush has a J on it for Jasper.

If the party has been to @UUID[.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb]{Jasper's Office}, they can easily tell that the handwriting on the floor matches his without a check.

If the party has been to the @UUID[.OVPUBZvPbZpksFnS]{Ooze Pool}, they can match the paint used on the floor with the paint on the wall in the Ooze pool with a successful [[/check investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check.

Jasper's Office.name: Jasper's Office
Jasper's Office.text:
The simple wood and iron desk at the back of the room is overflowing with papers, including a calendar, a series of ledgers filled with numbers, and page after page of the same set of large hand-drawn symbols.

Other than the papers, a desk, and a chair, the office is somewhat unremarkable. Any character who takes a moment to Search the room can locate the following:

  • Any character surveying the room can note the silver symbol of a desk on the back wall. It closely resembles the style and size of the symbol found in the @UUID[.yewfxh4f49fcF4gJ].

  • An @UUID[Item.U1wR5yJCfnazn9Tm]{Annotated Yakoshta Mine Map}, which provides a general layout of the mine labeled with track switches and rooms.

  • @UUID[Item.fMN0eZmpDvHmxNLG]{Jasper's Key Ring}

  • @UUID[Item.ISKt2Wp3SrpdmwNA]{Jasper's Notebook}

Hidden Valuables

Those who further search the room with a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skill awareness 14]] check notice a glimpse of red in the corner. Characters who succeed on a [[/check investigation 14]] check and upon further investigation can determine that there is misplaced clutter in that same corner that appears to be blocking something from view.

Digging through the clutter results in discovery of a small @UUID[.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb#the-locked-box]{Locked Box}.

Jasper's Keys

The large ring of keys in Jasper's office includes keys of all shapes and sizes, making it difficult to tell which is which, but include the following:

  • Four large keys, which appear a bit sooty.

  • Six medium-sized keys, some more worn down than others.

  • One small key, warm to the touch.

The keyring includes keys for all locked doors or objects in the mine including the Elevator Key and Storage Key, although neither key is labeled.

Finding the Right Key

Characters looking to discern one key from another can make a successful[[/skill history 12]] [[/skill society 12]] check to compare the keys to well-known shapes and sizes or a successful[[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skill awareness 12]] check to look for physical evidence of what each key might be. If characters are comparing a specific lock with the keys, they @Advantage[2] on the check.

With a success, characters know that the large keys are used in the mine, the medium-sized keys are used by banks and trading houses to secure valuables when lending money, and the small key is likely for a small personal lockbox.

Jasper's Notebook

It's clear from the entries in Jasper's notebook that he has been trying to decipher some sort of symbol — after several attempts with cryptic notes, one is clearly circled. It is the same as the symbol found at the bottom of the ooze pool in the Forest of Stone.

The notebook also contains notes on the aftermath of the earthquake. Two entries in particular catch your eye. The first reads:

"Must clear the rubble in the Excavation Pit before we can start repairs. Will order some more Blast Flasks. This will cut into profits. Must tell Sellen."

A second entry, scribbled in an excited hand reads:

"Blast Flasks arriving shortly. Just in time. Ooze attacks are bad enough without exits being blocked. Will lock it up and tell folks to be careful … last thing we need is some kind of chain reaction."

Deciphering the Symbol

With a successful [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skill arcana 13]] check of the symbol or [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skill awareness 13]] check to fully examine the notes, party members can determine that the mark attracts oozes to it. Those who speak [[/language pathward]] can read it without a check. Those who found the symbol in the ooze pool have advantage on this check.

The Locked Box

If discovered, the locked box is simple and constructed from stone. It has a rudimentary key hole and a rune inscribed on its top. Any party member who is fluent in [[/language pathward]] or succeeds on a [[/skill history 12]] [[/skill society 12]] recognizes the symbol as a symbol of warning or danger.

The lock is simple and can be opened by anyone proficient with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools} capable of using lockpicks. Party members without thieves' tools lockpicks can attempt to unlock the box using improvised tools and succeed on a [[/check dexterity 13]] [[/skill stealth 13]] check. Anyone who has identified Jasper's Personal Key may use it without a check. If opened with the key, the trap is not triggered.

It's A Trap

Once the lock is opened, the rune on the box begins to glow and hiss. It is a trap tied to the box that can be disarmed with a successful [[/check dexterity 14]] check using Thieves' Tools [[/skill science 14]] or [[/skill arcana 14]] check . If the rune is not disarmed, it triggers and all those within 10 feet of the box must make a successful [[/save dexterity 14]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d6 force]] damage from a powerful burst of magical force as the box explodes. [[/skill athletics 14]] check or suffer the [[/hazard 4 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{exploding box}.

If opened, the box contains @UUID[Item.sA6BUDpNnyssQ7nK]{Jasper's Diary}, and three jars - one filled with a glowing liquid, one filled with a gold-colored liquid, and one filled with a silver-colored liquid. The gold and silver-colored liquids are easily identified as @UUID[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE.Item.umj9X4CHGROfPz5I]{Pooled Gold} and @UUID[Actor.Jhymp0ntXyx78Gx3.Item.ONCtE8DcGhiVHltt]{Liquid Silver} respectively.

Luminous Evidence

The glowing vial of liquid is a @UUID[Item.jnqAVPfmdEzxuLaA]{Vial of Luminous Goo}, which is unidentified except by characters who have seen the contaminant in the mine, encountered the sickly Suarrok and inspected its vomit, have [[/knowledge alchemy]], or make a successful [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]].

  • A successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check allows a character to notice a small symbol on the vial that matches a symbol on the @UUID[Item.U1wR5yJCfnazn9Tm]{Yakoshta Mine Map} labeled as the @UUID[.xm50UssrvERyHUig]{Glowing Ore Pit}.

Supply Cache.name: Supply Cache
Supply Cache.text:
This small niche in the rock is less a cavern than an opening, only large enough for one or two people to stand inside. Whatever was once stored here is mostly gone, with only spare items left, strewn across the floor as if they were thrown around in a hurry, and a large trunk with an exclamation point on it near the back wall.

This small area has supplies that have been placed midway through the map for miners to use as needed. The area has been undisturbed by the oozes directly, but is a mess, as miners grabbed things from it to defend themselves as needed. Items that are still left in the supply area include:

  • @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ.Item.oFkmR4GWboLHhAfJ]{Potion of Healing} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingElixir000]

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.eTNc8XPtvZNe3yQs]{Potion of Flying}

  • @UUID[Item.b1Xe9Rnie8zRsXus] (which can be fed to the friendly oozes)

  • A locked @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU]{Crate of Blast Flasks}. An image of Blast Flask is painted on the crate.

  • On top and beside the crate are 3 loose @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flasks},

  • A pickaxe

  • A sign in/sign-out sheet. An @UUID[Item.U1wR5yJCfnazn9Tm]{Annotated Yakoshta Mine Map} is affixed underneath the sign-in sheet and is noticed with a[[/check investigation 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12 passive]] .

Blasting Crate

The locked @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU]{Crate of Blast Flasks} can be unlocked with the Storage Key from Jasper's Key, or by picking the lock using Thieves' Tools and a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 13]] with a set of lock picks and a successful [[/skillCheck stealth 13]]check. It can also be pried open using a pickaxe or other miner's tool with a successful [[/skill athletics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check.

If unlocked, the crate is filled with Blast Flasks and there is a sign on the underside of the lid, which reads:

Use individually for small issues. Larger detonations require direct supervision by Jasper.

Heavy Load

Moving the crate is difficult for any single character as it weighs 150 pounds. Two characters can share the load, but as a result both move at half speed and cannot use their hands for any other action.

Characters with [[/skill insight 14 passive]] or succeeding on a [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]]check recognize that the crate is an appropriate size to be loaded on a mine cart, which is probably how it was transported to this supply cache originally.

Ooze Pool.name: Ooze Pool
Ooze Pool.text:
This small niche would be empty if it wasn't for the oozes — large numbers of them have gathered here and appear to be peacefully co-existing. They do not have the glow of the metallic oozes that you've seen, seeming closer in temperament to Tauric's ooze Squish, and they are circled around a long cylindrical object made of metal that appears to have a black painted handle on one end. A symbol is painted on the wall in silver paint.

Oozes are congregated here, but they appear friendly, and do not glow like the oozes that have attacked the party thus far. These @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozelings} can be recruited if the characters have learned how to befriend them from Tauric in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl.JournalEntryPage.T8Yz3kDaxX3jUo8t]{Stone Life}. If attacked, the oozes here simply flee, squeezing into crevices in the rock and disappearing into the stone.

The Missing Lever

The cylindrical object that the Oozelings are congregated around is the @UUID[Item.YlYgsMKgXjmYdEaH]{Yakoshta Blue Track Lever} that was removed from the switch on the southern end of the @UUID[.GtpDWpInS0unttZW]{Blue Track}, which connects the @UUID[.xm50UssrvERyHUig]{Glowing Ore Pit} to the @UUID[.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit}.

As long as the characters do not demonstrate any hostility, the Oozelings do not attempt to stop them from taking the lever.

Jasper has been conducting experiments here, intentionally exposing the Oozelings to small doses of the Alchemical Contaminant.

Alchemical Contaminant

If any of the Oozelings are exposed to @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0]{Alchemical Contaminant}, they begin to glow and slowly transform. After one minute passes, roll a [[/gmroll 1d6 # Ooze Transformation]] and consult the following results to see what sort of ooze they transform into:

  • Result of 1 or 2: @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj]

  • Result of 3 or 4: @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ]

  • Result of 5: @UUID[Actor.Jhymp0ntXyx78Gx3]

  • Result of 6: @UUID[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE]

The transformed ooze immediately attacks.

The symbol upon the wall is recognizable and similar to others found elsewhere in the mine.

An Attractive Symbol

The normal symbol found on the wall in the mine has been painted over with a new symbol, which appears hastily painted. If the party investigates it, they can discover the following:

  • The symbol was painted within the last day or two.

  • The symbol matches the one found in the Ooze Pool in the Forest of Stone.

  • The symbol matches the symbol in Jasper's notes in his office.

  • The symbol has been painted with silver paint matching the paint found in the Old Ore Pit.

The party can attempt to decipher the symbol if they have not already. With a successful [[/check investigation 13]] or through appropriate deduction they determine that it is meant to attract oozes to this location.

Befriending the Oozes

If the party has learned of the process to befriend an ooze, they can befriend an @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozeling} here by removing it from the pool with a successful [[/skill animalhandling 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] check then feeding it something in their possession (such as@UUID[Item.b1Xe9Rnie8zRsXus]). Only one Oozeling may be acquired per character.

Junction.name: Junction
Junction.text:
Vertical and horizontal tracks meet at a circular platform with two concentric rings. Between them is an empty slot in the floor.

This junction appears to be a rotating platform that would allow mine carts to change the orientation of their travel. A strange looking socket stands empty just nearby as if expecting something to be placed within.

Further to the east, a large elevator cage with something vaguely blue inside.

The Missing Wheel

Any character with [[/knowledge machines]] or who makes a successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] check can intuit that the empty socket is designed to accommodate a control rod or wheel of some sort.

If characters have acquired the @UUID[Item.Sbw2OnVAq9Om5qpa]{Junction Wheel}, they can reattach and use it without a problem. If not, the junction is unusable.

Operating the Junction

The Junction Wheel is an Interactable Object. As the Gamemaster, you may interact with the wheel socket while the Interactables Layer is active to replace the @UUID[Item.Sbw2OnVAq9Om5qpa]{Junction Wheel}.

Once the Junction Wheel is replaced, you may interact again to rotate the junction. This switches the orientation of the @UUID[.GtpDWpInS0unttZW#blue-mining-tracks]{Blue Mining Tracks} to run either north-south or east-west.

If the blue mine cart is on the junction when it is rotated, the cart will rotate with the platform.

There are two reachable clusters of @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal} embedded in the walls here, which can be removed using the @UUID[.EI0ruUcoxyqYcehr#taking-a-kaleidoscope-crystal]{Taking a Kaleidoscope Crystal} rules.

Glowing Ore Pit.name: Glowing Ore Pit
Glowing Ore Pit.text:
The steady sound of dripping echoes through the cavern, as a glowing orange liquid drips from the top corner of one of the stone walls onto a large puddle on an overlook in the corner. Some of the liquid has begun to slowly leak down into the floor of the pit, where two oozes that glow with the same intensity battle a group of rat-like creatures who slip in and out of a crevice in the wall.

When one of the small creatures knocks a piece of kaleidoscope crystal from the wall near the crevice, it breaks. The oozes in the room momentarily pause in their attack and move towards the crystal, giving the rats chance to dash into the walls and leaving you alone with the two glowing oozes.

The party can enter this pit of glowing ore from three possible directions:

  • A ledge 15 feet above, reachable via the @UUID[.D4sqNCnQfsZcSxME]{Cavern Bridge}

  • Ground level, reachable via the @UUID[.GtpDWpInS0unttZW]{Blue Track}

  • A ladder up from the wooden platform at the south end of the @UUID[.GtpDWpInS0unttZW]{Red Track}

A @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ]{Luminous Copper Ooze} and a @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj]{Luminous Iron Ooze} occupy this chamber, and will engage the party in combat as soon as the characters are spotted.

The Overlook

Unless they are directly attacked, the oozes do not notice the party while they are up on the ledge and they can move freely.

A dripping rivulet of contaminant can be found here, in pure form.

Pure Contaminant

The flow of contaminant glows orange and bubbles. A character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 13]] or [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] or [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check can determine that the substance is not biological or magical - it is more akin to poison, though it appears viscous and rippling with some sort of contained energy.

Anyone who touches the contaminant with their bare hands takes [[/damage 1d10 lightning]] damage experiences [[/hazard 6 fortitude health electricity]]{Electrochemical Shock}and is thrown back 10 feet (if this throws them off the ledge, they may take further fall damage and can trigger the ooze fight if the oozes are still present).

The contaminant can carefully be collected in a container with a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 13]] [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check, a failure on this check results in contact with the contaminant, causing the effects described above. Additionally, a character may make use of a spell like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.Utk1OQRwYkMkFRD3]{Mage Hand} a spell such as @Spell[kinesis.influence] .

Successful extraction of the fluid yields a single vial of @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0]{Alchemical Contaminant}.

Ground Level

The two oozes will direct their limited attention to the crystal that's fallen here, enabling the characters to sneak around the perimeter of the room with a successful [[/check stealth 8]] check. As soon as the oozes become aware of the characters, they'll move to attack.

@Embed[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ]

@Embed[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj]

Ooze Tactics

The Luminous Iron Ooze proactively seeks out opponents who are wearing or wielding metal, and uses its @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.M9zZ2880tT8qONrT] and @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.axNcdP72e20FRJBk] trait to pull enemies closer and, if possible, disarm them.

The Luminous Copper Ooze takes advantage of @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ.Item.6mhO90U7AYY3TfCr]{Self-Soothing} to extend the duration of combat if it is threatened.

Both types of oozes have the exceptional ability to @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeMultiply0000] or @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeSubdivide000], but a limited Focus pool with which to perform these actions. Oozes favor use of Subdivide if they are near full Health, and will use Multiply if they become wounded.

The Luminous Iron Ooze proactively seeks out opponents who are wearing or wielding metal, using @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeMagneticDisa] to disarm them of their equipped weaponry.

The Luminous Copper Ooze focuses on direct attacks, reacting with their ability to @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ.Item.oozeCorrodeWeapo]{Corrode Weapons} as a natural defensive mechanism against incoming attacks.

The oozes fight to the death, even if their Morale is Broken.

Raising the Stakes

This is meant to be a straightforward combat, as there is a larger battle in the room ahead — but if you want to threaten the party more, after the first round of combat, a @UUID[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE]{Luminous Gold Ooze} emerges from the contaminant pool on the right side of the room. The Token for this ooze defaults to hidden in the Scene, and can be revealed by toggling its visibility state from the Token HUD.

A few small pieces of@UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{ Kaleidoscope Crystal} are located in this room and can be broken to use against the oozes, though doing so will trigger a @UUID[RollTable.CW4O54YLtXBarVjz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal Effect}.

Contamination

After the battle, any party member can clearly see that the glowing contaminant is dripping down from somewhere above the mine and pooling in a corner of the room.

Identifying the Source

With a successful [[/skill nature 15]] or [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] or [[/skillCheck awareness 15]]check, characters can tell that the leak is coming through cracks in the rocks above the mine, and attempting to block a specific outlet is unlikely to be helpful. The leak must be stopped wherever the source is above.

This contaminant is murkier than the pool on the ledge above or the contaminant dripping down, as it has mixed with the oozes, and only the combined @UUID[Item.jnqAVPfmdEzxuLaA]{Vial of Luminous Goo} can be collected here.

Excavation Pit.name: Excavation Pit
Excavation Pit.text:
A mammoth ooze, bigger than any that you've previously encountered, sits in the center of the railroad track. Nearby, a cart filled with ore is overturned and the walls are cracked with damage — though whether from the creature or the recent earthquake is unclear.

The ooze feasts hungrily upon the unrefined ore spilled from the cart, gathering chunks in with pseudopods that are lined with crystalline spikes. As it gluts itself upon metallic morsels it pulses and engorges, growing further in size!

In the distant corner of the room, you see the small hunched shape of a lone miner with their back pressed against the far western wall of the cavern. The figure meets your eyes and wordlessly gestures, exuding an obvious sense of panic.

Ooze Go Boom!

If the party has enacted an @UUID[.oYxMXI3OD4YPUfxz]{elaborate plan} to feed a mine cart of explosives to the Giant Ooze, this is the moment upon which the success of their plan hinges. If the mine cart is successfully laden with explosives, the ooze will hungrily latch upon it and begin feasting - exposing itself fully to the earth-shattering detonation which soon follows.

Oozesplosion!

The @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU]{Crate of Blast Flasks} explodes in a 15 foot radius, requiring every creature in the area to makea [[/save dexterity 17]] saving throw taking [[/damage 20d6 fire]]{20d6 Fire Damage} on a failure and half that amount on a success. a [[/skillCheck athletics 17]] or they are caught in [[/hazard 60 fortitude health fire]]{The Explosion}

Any character within a 40 foot radius of the blast must also succeed on a [[/save constitution 15]] check or they are deafened are @Condition[deafened] by the blast for 1 hour. Unless he is already incapacitated, @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper} sees the cart coming and successfully dives for cover.

Ooze Onslaught

Otherwise, as soon as the party enters the Excavation Pit from any direction, they immediately encounter a giant ooze which becomes aware of them and moves to attack!

@Embed[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07]

Giant Ooze Tactics

The giant ooze combines several traits of its smaller brethren!

  • Like the Iron Ooze, it is @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07.Item.6wb5ExliBRNPOBqt]{Magnetic}

  • Like the Silver Ooze, it has a recharging @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07.Item.rZI6OligU6NFy0wt]{Electrified Pseudopod}

  • It possesses the self-healing ability of the Copper Ooze with its capacity to @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07.Item.JyNWqqOBfkTcwOCy]{Absorb Oozes}

  • It has the self-replicating capability of the Gold Ooze with its capability to @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07.Item.VOrm71kQgFhMNiYA]{Spawn Oozes} as a lair action.

The Giant Ooze will act defensively, using its bulk and reach to threaten any character that gets nearby. It will spawn oozes every round, generally allowing them to act independently until it becomes desirable to re-absorb them for self-healing.

  • Like the Iron Ooze, it is @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07.Item.oozeMagneticDisa]{Magnetic}

  • Like the Silver Ooze, it has a recharging @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07.Item.oozeElectrifiedP]{Electrified Pseudopod}

  • It possesses the natural defense of the Copper Ooze with its capacity to @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07.Item.oozeCorrodeWeapo]{Corrode Weapons}

  • Like the Gold Ooze it has the ability to disorient and assault the willpower of its opponents with the @UUID[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE.Item.oozeBewilderingG} ability.

  • Like other oozes, the Giant Luminous Ooze also has the @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeMultiply0000] and @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeSubdivide000] abilities, making use of Subdivide if it is near full Health, and Multiply if wounded.

The Giant Ooze will act defensively, using its bulk and reach to threaten any character that gets nearby. It will spawn oozes every round, generally allowing them to act independently until it becomes desirable to re-absorb them for self-healing.

Managing the Battle

Because of the Giant Ooze's ability to create more oozes and self-heal gain size and subdivide into smaller threatening parts, the longer this fight goes on the more likely it is to turn against a low-level party.

If the tide of battle starts turning against the heroes, Jasper will yell and distract the ooze to temporarily gain its attention. He may suggest that the party retreat and get explosives to deal with the Ooze instead of taking it on in direct combat.

Aftermath

@Embed[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7 inline]

After the battle, Jasper briefly steps forward to talk, as described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl.JournalEntryPage.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2#after-rescuing-jasper]{After Rescuing Jasper}. After a brief exchange, Jasper directs the party to meet him back in Yakoshta to speak further.

The back exit to the excavation pit leads back to Yakoshta, but is currently blocked by rubble. If the characters have leftover explosives, they can clear it - otherwise they may need to backtrack towards the @UUID[.yewfxh4f49fcF4gJ]{Loading Zone}.

Clearing the Exit

The blocked exit to the mine is composed of two 10-foot long sections of rubble that span the width of the path.

These sections can be cleared with the @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flasks} or through by any party members who have pickaxes with a successful [[/skill athletics 13]] [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] for the first section and [[/skill athletics 15]] [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] for the second section.

If party members choose to use their hands, or any improvised tools, they have @Advantage[-2] on each of these checks.Any party member with proficiency in @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.skUih6tBvcBbORzA]{Mason's Tools} can clear the first section issue and has @Advantage[2] on the check for the second section.

On a failed check, the rubble falls forward onto the party - anyone within 10 feet of that section must make a successful[[/save dexterity 13]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check or get caught in the [[/hazard 3 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Falling Rocks}.

Once cleared, the sloping path leads back into the cavern and out to Yakoshta.

Mine Cart Loading Station.name: Mine Cart Loading Station
Mine Cart Loading Station.text:
This stone platform is the last walkable space before the mine tracks that head off into the dim light of the chasm ahead of you. A few older piles of materials that have been run over by the ooze during its attacks are on either side. They are roughed up but mostly intact. A few Kaleidoscope Crystals embedded in the walls provide a slight shifting glow.

A few old scraps of ore and supplies lie in a pile near the tracks, in disarray. Traces of copper ooze can be seen on the remaining supplies.

Jasper's Hypothesis

If characters make a successful [[/skill perception 12]] or search the pile and succeed on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check/skillCheck awareness 12 check, they find a scattered pile of @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ.Item.XIZ8BkDMSwgsDrZp]{Copper Flakes} and a note that reads:

OOZES = PROFIT? Check value of copper flakes in Helkas!

Any party members who have been to @UUID[.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb]{Jasper's Office} can recognize the note as being in Jasper's handwriting.

There are four @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystals} embedded in the wall here, which can be removed if the party desires, using the @UUID[.EI0ruUcoxyqYcehr#kaleidoscope-crystals]{Kaleidoscope Crystals} rules.

Elevator.name: Elevator
Elevator.text:
You step closer, inspecting the contents of the surface-to-shaft elevator. Inside, you spy a mine cart with blue paint on both sides, separated from you by a locked grate. The grate appears to be secured via a locked panel with a keyhole in the center, and there is a faint aura of magic around it. A note affixed to the grate reads:

BEWARE: Oozes have been tearing through this grate, so I've added a bit of juice to the lock that will make them think twice before trying it again. If you need to get through, see me for the key or you will regret it.
Jasper

The elevator has been magically warded to stop the amorphous oozes from entering between the cracks.

Warded Door

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] or [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check can confirm that the door has been magically warded against entry.

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} spell or similar will remove the ward. character with the @UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]{Recognize Spellcraft} talent can make a successful [[/skill arcana 15]] check to disable the ward.

  • The elevator can be safely opened with the Elevator Key from the Ring of Keys found in @UUID[.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb]{Jasper's Office}.

Any character who makes an attempt to open the door without the key while the ward is active must must make a successful[[/save dexterity 14]] saving throw, taking [[/damage 1d12 force]] damage on a failed save or half with a success [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check or face [[/hazard 7 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Deterring Ward} .

If the ward on the door has been dispelled, the lock can be picked with a successful[[/skill sleightofhand 14]] check using @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.woWZ1sO5IUVGzo58]{Thieves' Tools} [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] with a set of lock picks.

If the party has Jasper's Keys, but does not know which one is correct, they can identify the correct key with a successful [[/check 12 investigation]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check to match a key to the keyhole or with use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify} spell@UUID[Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]{Recognize Spellcraft} talent to determine which key has been enchanted to disrupt the magical ward.

Once the door is open, the party may access and use the blue mining cart that was locked inside, and may use the elevator at any time to return to the surface near @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta}.

Ooze Go Boom!.name: Ooze Go Boom!
Ooze Go Boom!.text:
One way for the party to resolve the presence of the @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07]{Giant Luminous Ooze} in the @UUID[.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit} is to use the @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU]{Crate of Blast Flasks} intended for clearing the collapsed southern passage. The giant ooze is known to devour the contents of mine carts in the area, a predilection which can be used to bait it into a deadly explosion.

Puzzle Clues

There are several clues the party can discover for how to use the explosives in this way.

  1. The miners at the @UUID[.yewfxh4f49fcF4gJ]{Loading Zone} are using individual explosive flasks as weapons and mention that there is a larger stash. If the party talks to Jasper from across the bridge, he notes this as well.

  2. The notes in @UUID[.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb]{Jasper's Office} reveal that a shipment of powerful explosives was delivered to be used in clearing the collapsed passageway of the southwest cavern.

  3. The surviving miners in the @UUID[.ZVl3AnWEXMhsm3UA]{Old Ore Pit} can confirm the location of the explosives in the @UUID[.6OAhqzuyGkUvdWf6]{Supply Cache} and provide the control rod needed to operate the @UUID[.8RAoBSwmaWf2ZT8h]{Junction}.

If the party is suitably inquisitive about the potential use of explosives to combat the Giant Ooze, you are encouraged to provide additional clues which reinforce the steps necessary to accomplish the solution.

Rigging the Trap

Utilizing this solution requires several specific steps:

  1. The @UUID[.GtpDWpInS0unttZW]{Blue Track Mine Cart} is needed to transport the explosive powder. The blue track cart is initially locked within the @UUID[.LuKUKowZNKDGl5dM]{Elevator}, the key to which is located on a large ring of keys in @UUID[.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb]{Jasper's Office}.

  2. @UUID[.8RAoBSwmaWf2ZT8h]{The Junction} needs to be rotated with the blue cart on top of it it so that the cart can reach the other section of track. Rotating the junction requires recovering the @UUID[Item.Sbw2OnVAq9Om5qpa]{Yakoshta Junction Wheel} from the survivors at the @UUID[.ZVl3AnWEXMhsm3UA]{Old Ore Pit}.

  3. The @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU]{Crate of Blast Flasks} from the @UUID[.6OAhqzuyGkUvdWf6]{Supply Cache} must be loaded onto the blue cart.

  4. The Missing Switch is required to switch the final track leading into the @UUID[.xm50UssrvERyHUig]{Glowing Ore Pit} from the east side. This switch was taken by the friendly oozes in the @UUID[.OVPUBZvPbZpksFnS]{Ooze Pool}.

  5. The makeshift barricade blocking the entrance to the @UUID[.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit} must be cleared so the cart can proceed into that area which contains the Giant Luminous Ooze.

Explosive Results

If the party have successfully retrieved the blue track cart, loaded it with explosives, restored the missing switch lever, and cleared the makeshift barricade — they can send the explosives-laden cart down the track into the Glowing Ore Pit where the Giant Luminous Ooze will hungrily grab it, causing its own downfall as described in the @UUID[.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit}.

This strategy allows a clever party to eliminate the Giant Luminous Ooze without needing to confront it directly in combat.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.XytBBChWK9D5ccOD] depicts a small section of the larger Yakoshta Mine, in its current deepest and most active section, centered around Jasper the mine supervisor's office and the active Excavation Pit. This section is also the portion of the mine that is currently under attack by oozes.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.XytBBChWK9D5ccOD inline]

Mining Tracks.name: Mining Tracks
Mining Tracks.text:
Suspended wooden railways weave and cross throughout the gleaming cavern ahead. Several tracks are attacked to the cave ceiling far above by rope or cables while others are affixed precariously to the rock walls that frame a seemingly bottomless chasm.

Blue Mining Tracks

The blue mining tracks are the upper set of tracks. They have been damaged by the earthquakes and ooze attacks, but portions of the tracks are still viable, either to walk on or to use the mine cart on.

When characters enter the mine, the blue mining cart is sitting in the @UUID[.LuKUKowZNKDGl5dM]{Elevator} that leads back up to surface near @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta}, but the cart cannot be removed without the Elevator Key from @UUID[.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb]{Jasper's Office}.

The Missing Lever

A lever to the southern-most track switch, between the @UUID[.xm50UssrvERyHUig]{Glowing Ore Pit} and the @UUID[.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit} is missing. Until it is located and restored into place this switch is inoperable.

Red Mining Tracks

The red mining tracks are the lower set of tracks. They have been largely untouched by the damage to the mine and are mostly viable to either walk on or use the mine cart on, though there are a few sections that are inoperable. When characters enter the mine, the red mining cart is at the bottom of the ladder down from the @UUID[.yewfxh4f49fcF4gJ]{Loading Zone}.

Mine Cart Operation

Each cart occupies a single 5 foot square and can hold one creature of medium size or smaller or can be filled with items equivalent to a 5 foot cube in size and weighing less than 1000 pounds.

The front of the cart holds a stone panel against the front wall and an activation lever marked with three symbols. One symbol depicts a wheel with an arrow through it, when activated the cart begins moving forward. Another is marked with an X, when activated this brings the cart to a stop. A third symbol is a wheel with an arrow opposite to the first, which causes the cart to move in reverse.

Operating the Cart

Each mine cart is an ​ Interactable Object. As the Gamemaster, you can cause the cart to move forwards, backwards, or stop by clicking on it using the interaction tool.

  • A Left-Click causes the cart to move forwards or to stop moving if it was previously moving backwards.

  • A Right-Click causes the cart to move backwards or to stop moving if it was previously moving forwards.

When a cart begins moving, any appropriately sized character who occupies the same grid space as the cart may be designated as a passenger. This character will travel with the cart until stopped.

Track Switch Operation

Each track's current destination is controlled by track switches along the rails. Party members who wish to switch the track's direction must locate a switch with a successful [[[/skill perception 14 passive]] or with a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skill awareness 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill awareness 12]] check or by using the @UUID[Item.U1wR5yJCfnazn9Tm]{Yakoshta Mine Map}.

Visualizing the Tracks

As the Gamemaster you may visualize the current track layout by activating the ​ Tracks Visualization toggle in the Canvas Controls toolbar on the left side of the interface.

Operating the Tracks

Each track switch is an ​ Interactable Object. As the Gamemaster you can click on a track switch to toggle it to its opposite position. Note that the southern-most switch is inoperable unless its lever is recovered.

Each Switch is associated with a particular junction and can be manipulated into one of two positions that alternates the direction of the junction the switch is associated with.

Disrupted Switches

As result of the ooze attacks, many of the levers have been damaged or made somewhat dangerous. Each time a party member attempts to redirect a switch, roll on or select from the table below to determine any issue with the switch.

@Embed[RollTable.ZXxfy0RaAx3rJdRW inline]

Waterfall Bridge.name: Waterfall Bridge
Waterfall Bridge.text:
The long wooden bridge is missing half of its planks and the rope that stretches from one side of the chasm seems frayed. It shifts, slowly, back and forth, creaking as it does, though it is not immediately apparent where the sound is coming from. On the far side of the bridge, rock has crumbled onto a landing, blocking off the sight of anything beyond it.

The entrance bridge has been partially destroyed by the recent earthquake. If characters step onto the bridge, the creaking becomes stronger and is accompanied by the sound of cracking. The mine supervisor, Jasper, who is located on the other side of the bridge, immediately calls out in a loud whisper from behind the pile of rocks.

Hello? Whoever that is, please don't come any closer. The bridge isn't stable.

Characters can speak to Jasper from their current location in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl.JournalEntryPage.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2#a-conversation-with-jasper]{A Conversation with Jasper}.

Calamitous Crossing

If, despite the warnings and Jasper's request that they not, the party attempts to continue across the bridge, one of the ropes snaps, sending the bridge lurching to the side. Anyone on the bridge when this happens must make a successful [[/save dexterity 14]] saving throw [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] or they end up hanging from the rope over the chasm below - they can be pulled up by someone else on the bridge, or get back to the safety of the cavern with a successful [[/skill athletics 12]]{brute strength climbing} or [[/skill acrobatics 12]]{swing from the rope} [[/skill athletics 12]] check. If both checks fail, the character may choose to take a level of &Reference[exhaustion] gain the @Condition[exhausted] condition to slowly pull their way back up.

Cavern Bridge.name: Cavern Bridge
Cavern Bridge.text:
The long rope bridge spans the chasm below. You dare a glance downwards and see the twinkling lights of kaleidoscope crystals descending until the light recedes entirely from view. You surmise that a fall from here would allow you time to contemplate your mistakes before meeting a tragic end.

The cavern bridge is fully operable. It stretches between the back end of the @UUID[.ZVl3AnWEXMhsm3UA]{Old Ore Pit} and the upper overlook to the @UUID[.xm50UssrvERyHUig]{Glowing Ore Pit} and can be used without incident.

Makeshift Barricade.name: Makeshift Barricade
Makeshift Barricade.text:
If the party plans to use the mining cart and explosives to detonate the giant ooze, they will need to send it into the @UUID[.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit} from here. This involves two challenges — replacing the track switch and clearing a makeshift barricade.

The Missing Lever

The track switch here is stuck sending carts north or east, instead of into the Excavation Pit to the west. Switching the track direction is impossible because the @UUID[Item.YlYgsMKgXjmYdEaH]{Yakoshta Blue Track Lever} is missing.

The lever is located in the @UUID[.OVPUBZvPbZpksFnS]{Ooze Pool}, having been taken there by friendly @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozelings} worried about growth of the @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07]{Giant Luminous Ooze} that currently inhabits the Excavation Pit.

Any character with [[/skill perception 15 passive]] or that makes a successful [[/skill perception 13]] check[[/skill awareness 15 passive]] can see a pile of debris on the tracks ahead blocking the cart's path.

A tangled pile of metal and bits of kaleidoscope crystal sits in the center of the tracks. It is covered with goo that trails into the next room as if something dragged it this way and then dropped it in its path.

Debris on the Tracks

If the cart is sent between the @UUID[.xm50UssrvERyHUig]{Glowing Ore Pit} and the @UUID[.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit} without the debris being cleared, it crashes to a stop against the barricade.

For the cart to continue, the debris must be cleared. Unless done cautiously, this process may create noise that alerts the @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07]{Giant Luminous Ooze} in the room beyond.

Any character that succeeds on an [[/skill athletics 11]] [[/skillCheck athletics 11]] check can successfully clear the debris. That character must also succeed on a [[/skill stealth 11]] [[/skillCheck stealth 11]] check if they wish to avoid alerting the Giant Luminous Ooze.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.bfORKMRfuaOgMbUt] depicts the entirety of the quarry lab location when it is discovered during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100]{Ancient Paths} quest event.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.bfORKMRfuaOgMbUt inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Illumination

The area here is near pitch black, only very faint lights emanating from the ancient bones and skulls of long dead Giants can be seen through the oppressive gloom.

Terrain

The area has a number of stepped levels, but these are relatively easy to climb and only require an additional 5 feet of movement to scale. Climbing these is not entirely without risk as the rocks can be sharp and slick from the moisture of the fog.

Dangerous Ground

The entire repurposed quarry is in a state of disarray, and there are numerous dangerous situations unfolding across the entire facility. Parties attempting to go in quietly may have a hard time due to the long sight lines and large numbers of enemies in the area.

To their advantage, the relative chaos incited by scuttling the base means that enemies might not immediately realize they have a band of intruders even if they do spot the party.

Elevation

The ceiling of the pathways above is far beyond the reach of any player character, likely in the many hundreds of feet. Levels of the quarry are 20ft apart, posing a small risk of injury for characters that fall, and the sheer stone walls of most of the quarry lack hand holds, making climbing between levels difficult without a natural climbing speed.

Collecting Evidence

Most of the evidence the party needs to acquire for the investigation can be found in @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.clq12qbRqtMJctZr]{Chemical Storage}, @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.yAtJNWC3l4EpgcE2]{Compound Lab}, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.wAH9sTRTgMQAfmXC]{Testing Platform}.

Enemies

This quarry is filled with multiple members of the Mutagist faction on all levels. The denizens of this lab are actively attempting to destroy evidence in the lab, and are preparing to depart from the site.

  • Stopping the Mutagist Bomber in the @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.9nqK1LJd8e8T4JHa]{Entry Tunnels} prevents the Mutagists from destroying any more of the lab.

  • Several Mutated Drakes are squared off in combat against Mutagist Vivisectors in the @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.h3qjYKf4g01QiTsy]{Creature Pens}

  • The party can encounter Kalasak the Cutter, overseer of the laboratory in @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.yAtJNWC3l4EpgcE2]{Compound Lab}.

  • On the lowest level the party will find a challenging opponent in the @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls]{Mutated Ultra Drake} that has been kept by the Mutagists.

Resting

It is not possible to rest in quarry area until the party has scoured the site of hostiles, driving off or defeating any enemies first.

Fleeing

Should the party need to flee the area, they may do so by retreating from the quarry interior toward the entrance tunnel they arrived at, or the cave cliff. Mutagists will not pursue them beyond the immediate area the map covers.

Entry Tunnels.name: Entry Tunnels
Entry Tunnels.text:
In the gloom, you can see the roughly dug out walls of this tunnel, streaks of bioluminescent moss growing here and there, casting the narrow passage in an eerie light. A rusting metal bridge crosses over swiftly flowing water. A haze of swirling spores fill the tunnel, pouring from the caps of numerous large mushrooms growing on the walls.

Strange Growths

Examining the mushrooms with a successful [[/skill nature 18]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 18]] yields insight into the bright yellow ones: glowing, brightly colored, and likely highly poisonous as a result. Their production of spores is prodigious, and the sole cause of the tunnel being choked with the haze.

A successful [[/skill survival 18]] [[/skillCheck medicine 18]] knows that some sort of face cover will protect you from the spores, though it'll be impossible to avoid spores coating your equipment. The party will want to keep an eye out for growths in your pack after being here.

No Fun Fungi

Characters passing through the haze of spores need to succeed on a [[/save con 15]] constitution saving throw or suffer the &reference[poisoned] condition for 10 minutes. Characters passing through the haze of spores suffer [[/hazard 3 fortitude morale poison]]{Airborne Contaminanats} for each turn they spend in the fog.

Any sort of face cover that prevents inhaling the spores allows characters to navigate the area without having the make a saving throw.

Exiting the Tunnel

Emerging from the tunnel, the space opens up quickly to reveal a cavernous quarry with structures and catwalks running between them, all suspended over a pit flooded by running water. The cliff-side path continues on north, and the entrance to a wooden structure sits nearby to the east.

The gaps of the quarry are spanned by suspended catwalks made of rusting metal, the mechanisms to move them obscured by the darkness above. From here you see no obvious controls, but there must be a way to move them.

Lab Explosion

As you take in the quarry lab you spot movement on the other end of the quarry. A figure stands before the entrance to a building, reaches into a pouch on their belt, and throws the object into the structure. A moment later there is a sudden flash of light and a resounding boom which rattles the entire cavern.

Flames and smoke begin erupting out of the windows, while a stream of some bright purple fluid spills down through the floor of the suspended structure, bubbling and smoking on the stone a level below.

The figure is a @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg]{Mutagist Bombardier} and they appear in front of the @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.78nULLak2f7mZ7x8]{Destroyed Lab} after having just destroyed it.

Now outlined by the blazing fire issuing from the destroyed lab, the figure turns and begins running across a catwalk, heading your way. As they go, you see them pull another vial off their bandolier and shake it, causing it to glow violently in their hands.

The Bombardier begins moving for the @UUID[.clq12qbRqtMJctZr]{Chemical Storage} room to blow it up next. The party can attempt to intercept them, potentially saving the room.

However, if the party is too slow, the space will be destroyed as well.

Equipment Area.name: Equipment Area
Equipment Area.text:
The equipment area is a chaotic sprawl of crates and boxes scattered about, some toppled and others hastily pried open. Inside the adjoining space, you find the remnants of packs, containers, and essential items like medicine, all bearing marks of a hurried search.

Evidence of a ransack is clear, a palpable disorder that leaves little untouched and little of value. Only a few brooms, hand tools, and pieces of protective gear remain.

Searching The Leftovers

Searching the items left behind yields numerous small items such as leather aprons, @UUID[Item.VKRNoILxt0VdiUIH]{Protective Goggles}, steel plated boots, and a @UUID[Item.1IvYsX3zT2KxGRNq]{Protective Mask}.

Volatile Chemicals

A successful [[/check intellect 16 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck science 16]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki] while examining the bottles of chemicals recognizes the presence of volatile compounds that are not only explosive but highly corrosive.

The party can collect five @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.Sx5E6utixHdAbGNb]{Acid (vial)} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.causticPhial0000].

Unattended Compounds

Examining the syringe of chemicals with a successful [[/check intellect 16 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck medicine 16]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki] check recognizes that the components listed on the bottle in the pouch alongside the syringe are all very dangerous.

Beyond that it's unclear what they would do in concert with each other without also being able to study notes on the compound and how it was made and what the mixture ratios were.

Alternatively, a successful [[/check intellect 14 tool=pois]] check An additional [[/skillCheck science 14]] or [[/skillCheck 14 medicine]] check notices a list of numerous dangerous compounds scribbled on the bottle in the pouch accompanying the syringe. Every single one is incredibly dangerous, and would make this a deadly compound if injected.

Two doses A dose of @UUID[Item.fg5EQMoBcsXYEGjv]{Alchemical Toxin} can be claimed here.

Chemical Storage.name: Chemical Storage
Chemical Storage.text:
Storage Destroyed

If the party doesn't get to the lab in time, the mutagist bombardier will blow it up, destroying everything inside and turning the room into a hazardous space.

Shattered lab glassware litters the floor, with spilled fluids staining the wood flooring in various hues and emitting noxious vapors. Destroyed shelves lean precariously, some barely standing, others dripping with chemicals left to freely mix amidst the shattered glass vessels.

The air is dense, filled with a murky, caustic gas that assaults the eyes and nose immediately, and sets lungs afire with even the faintest breath.

Navigating The Fumes

Caustic Clouds

Characters passing through the damaged storage areas are &reference[blinded] and if they breathe, will begin choking, inflicting the &reference[suffocating] condition.

They must succeed on a [[/save con 16]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d6 acid]] damage. Failing the save by 5 or more causes the blinded and choking conditions to persist for one minute after leaving the space.

Characters passing through the damaged storage areas are @Condition[blinded] and if they breathe, will begin choking, suffering [[/hazard 3 fortitude morale poison]]{Noxious Fumes} for each round they remain in the gas.

Characters with @UUID[Item.VKRNoILxt0VdiUIH]{Protective Goggles} avoid the blinded condition while in the fumes, while characters wearing a @UUID[Item.1IvYsX3zT2KxGRNq]{Protective Mask} don't suffer the blinded or choking conditions caused by the gasses.

Storage Intact

If the party is able to intercept the bomber and stop them from destroying the chemical area, they will be able to explore it and find useful information.

Lab glassware lines the walls, resting on wooden shelves covered in labels and tags. Tables bear flasks and jars of fluids and powders of all colors, and the air makes your eyes burn lightly from the barely contained fumes.

Investigating The Shelves

Volatile Chemicals

This storage area is highly reactive and can easily be destroyed if the party is not careful. Actions that break, scatter, or spill the chemicals causes the lab to explode. This includes use of bombs, grenades, fireballs, and similar concussive spells or weapons.
