If the storage room is set off, all creatures inside take [[/damage 6d6 acid]] damage and the room's description and start match the above Storage Destroyed section.

Rare Stock

Character with the [[/knowledge alchemy]] knowledge or making a successful [[/check intellect 14 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki] notes that the alchemical compounds here are highly volatile, reactive, and rare. It would take considerable connections and wealth to acquire some of these items.

Upon hearing this, Ankarist makes a @UUID[Item.3KVOnp7wj7vPJ18k]{List of Chemicals} to be turned in as evidence. The party can also claim some of the @UUID[Item.zfv8g0NUFtDKpmWL]{Rare Chemicals} stored here for use or evidence later.

Gravel Chute.name: Gravel Chute
Gravel Chute.text:
The metal plates creak and groan underfoot, sinking slightly as weight is placed upon them as you enter this space. Heavy rusted metal floors and walls surround you, their surface pockmarked and corroded by time.

Dual pullies hang ominously over two large metal plates. At first it looks like a lift, but after a moment you realize they seal off a shaft that descends to the lower level. A net and heavy rope sway slightly with a rhythmic creak overhead.

The air here carries a musty odor of rust and pulverized stone.

Falling Hazard

Characters stepping onto the central platform of the chute will feel the metal give way, dropping them into the chute. The fall is 40 feet, dealing [[/damage 4d6 bludgeoning]] damage on impact and cause the fallen to suffer a [[/hazard 12 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Perilous Impact}. This also moves them to the middle level of this scene.

Dormitory.name: Dormitory
Dormitory.text:
The dormitory is a compact, utilitarian space with two rooms shared by the area's occupants. Rusty-framed beds and a lone hammock are set up with no regard for privacy, while footlockers rest at the base of each sleeping arrangement.

The space could easily accommodate eight occupants, or three times as many if they were rotating their sleeping shifts. By the look of things, part of this space was in the midst of being searched or ransacked, with personal belongings packed or raided. It's hard to tell which.

@Embed[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F count=2]

@Embed[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]

Off Duty Dangers

A group of 2 @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F]{Mutagist Scouts} and 1 @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]{Mutagist Vivisector} can be found here packing their things and discussing the orders to abandon the lab.

A stealthy party can take them by surprise if they manage a successful [[/skill stealth 14]] [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] group check where at least half the party succeed. Otherwise they will attack on sight.

The Mutagists engage in melee combat directly, since the fighting area is tight. If possible, they will attempt to control the door into the dormitory, or the doorway between rooms as this allows them to fight only one enemy at a time.

Personal Effects

While a collection of personal effects, belongings, clothing and equipment can be found here, none of it is noteworthy or has any particular value.

Destroyed Lab.name: Destroyed Lab
Destroyed Lab.text:
Fire and smoke fills this destroyed lab space, making it hard to examine the contents. Through the heat and haze you can make out a massive vat spilling green ooze out onto the rusted metal floors, and pouring through holes down to the lower levels.

All else in this spare are tables and shelves scattered with the remnants of lab distillers and filters, glassware, vessels and more destroyed by the explosion.

The resulting fire and smoke are laced with chemicals that cause your skin to inch, eyes to water, and lungs to burn.

Caustic Clouds

Characters passing through the destroyed lab are &reference[blinded] and if they breathe, will begin choking, inflicting the &reference[suffocating] condition.

They must succeed on a [[/save con 16]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d6 acid]] damage. Failing the save by 5 or more causes the blinded and choking conditions to persist for one minute after leaving the space.

Characters passing through the destroyed lab are @Condition[blinded] and if they breathe, will begin choking, suffering [[/hazard 3 fortitude morale poison]]{Noxious Fumes} for each round they remain in the gas.

Characters with @UUID[Item.VKRNoILxt0VdiUIH]{Protective Goggles} avoid the blinded condition while in the fumes, while characters wearing a @UUID[Item.1IvYsX3zT2KxGRNq]{Protective Mask} don't suffer the blinded or choking conditions.

Alchemical Fire

Touching any of the flames deals [[/damage 1d6]] damage as well.

The flames can also cause [[/hazard 3 fortitude health fire]]{Minor Burns}.

Hazardous Salvage

A successful [[/skill perception 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16]] check while in the lab notices that two doses a dose of @UUID[Item.fg5EQMoBcsXYEGjv]{Alchemical Toxin} can be claimed here.

Otherwise, nothing in this lab survived the explosion, and there is nothing that can be saved. Additionally, it is impossible to examine this lab while it is on fire and filled with smoke.

Fire Management

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or making a successful[[/check intellect 14 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki] know that this is an alchemical fire, and won't be easily extinguished. In fact, they will likely burn for hours unabated, and water would be completely ineffective.

Instead, to extinguish these flames, soil, sand, clay and dirt must be used. The quarry has ample amounts of this, and scattered tools, but the time necessary to move enough earth would considerable and cause the characters to be exposed to the fumes the entire time.

Creature Pens.name: Creature Pens
Creature Pens.text:
Four sturdy pens line the back wall, floor to ceiling, each enclosed by heavy steel gates. They look as through they could easily contain large, powerful creatures without issue.

Examination tables stand ready with an array of tools and vials of mutagen. Overhead, stark lighting illuminates the space, casting long shadows that dance across the steel bars and surgically precise equipment.

@Embed[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9]

@Embed[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki count=2]

@Embed[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8 count=3]

Dungeons & Drakelings

As the party enters the pens they encounter one Mutated Pallid Drake and two Mutated Pallid Drakelings that were either released or escape from their cages.

They are locked in a struggle with three Mutagist Vivisectors, who are clearly losing.

All creatures in this fight start out hostile, and if the party attempts to save the Vivisectors, siding with them to fight the dragons, they will either immediately turn on the party in an attempt to kill them, or flee, attempting to regroup with and alert others in the lab area.

Examining The Space

The four pens are each ten feet wide and fifteen feet long, with iron walls separating the occupants. Rusting grates underfoot allow the waste from the occupants to filter to some reeking space below, while beds of rotting hay provide nesting materials. Racks of rancid meat sit against the walls.

Opposite the pens is a large, mostly barren work area featuring two tables, chains, and some scattered tools. The diamond patterned metal plates underfoot are rusted and stained by all manner of residues and spills that defy quick identification.

Unpleasant Accommodations

Each of the pens feature heavy bolt locks for securing the occupants inside, and chains for keeping the them held in place. The pens stink of animal waste, molding hay, and rotting meat but otherwise contain nothing of interest or value.

Workspace Items

The workspace features a handful of useful items which can be claimed including a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.p2zChy24ZJdVqMSH] @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.chainMail0000000] and leather aprons used to protect the workers from animal bites. A black leather @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.QKTyxoO0YDnAsbYe]{Whip} whip can also be found on the floor here.

On the table are two doses is a dose of @UUID[Item.fg5EQMoBcsXYEGjv]{Alchemical Toxin} and a complete @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.il2GNi8C0DvGLL9P]{Poisoner's Kit} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki].

Rare Stock

Character with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or making a successful [[/check intellect 14 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki]check notes that the far wall features numerous rare alchemical compounds. It would take considerable connections and wealth to acquire some of these items.

Upon hearing this, Ankarist makes a @UUID[Item.3KVOnp7wj7vPJ18k]{List of Chemicals} to be turned in as evidence. The party can also claim some of the @UUID[Item.zfv8g0NUFtDKpmWL]{Rare Chemicals} stored here for use or evidence later.

Same Info, Two Sources

The rare chemicals and chemical list items are identical to those found in the @UUID[.clq12qbRqtMJctZr]{Chemical Storage} area if the party manages to save it from being destroyed. The party doesn't need to collect both.

Outer Cliff.name: Outer Cliff
Outer Cliff.text:
The secluded cliff juts out from the cavern wall, offering a precarious vantage point and the remains of a long broken, corroded bridge. From this elevated position, the expanse of a cavern unfurls, the luminescent glow of the pathways strange life visible in the otherwise abundant darkness.

Possible Passages

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check notices a shift in the air currents here, and a quality in the air itself. It seems likely that there is an exit at the end of this great cavern, though you'd have to be able to fly to find it.

This might be how some of the drakes got out.

Gravel Pit.name: Gravel Pit
Gravel Pit.text:
The gravel pit is dimly-lit, filled with gravel that crunches noisily underfoot, and stony dust sent swirling through the air with even the smallest movements. Scattered throughout are rotten bones, both animal and humanoid, fouling the air here with their stench. A sturdy gate of rusting iron bars and heavy metal lock controls access to this space.

Examining the Remains

With a quick glance, there are the remains of numerous dead creatures, many buried under layers of gravel and dirt, among them are humanoid remains.

A successful [[/skill investigation 16]] or [[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] check is needed to parse through the remains. Doing so reveals the presents of bones belonging to small drakes, humanoids, dogs, what might be a small yarnac, and several small reptiles. Many are old and rotten, and ripped apart with signs of being gnawed on.

Characters hoping to get into or out of the pit will need to contend with the gate.

Opening the Opening

To bypass the lock on the door a successful [[/check dexterity 14 tool=thief]] [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000] is necessary. Accessing the lock is easily done from either side.

Conspicuous Marks

A [[/skill perception 12 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12 passive]]or better notices that the area around the door, and the iron bars themselves bear the marks of claws and teeth, as though something quite large had tried to dig its way into the pit on more than one occasion.

Eastern Quarry.name: Eastern Quarry
Eastern Quarry.text:
The east quarry is a chaotic mixture of abandoned work and untended equipment. Among layers of dust and rubble lie rock slabs and long neglected and rusting tools used to make them. The only object which looks remotely new is a wooden crane standing silently nearby.

Going Down

The crane can be used to lower one or more creatures to the flooded pit below, or raise them up. Doing so requires at least one character to work the crane from this level, however.

Old Tools

Aside from being a good source of rust and splinters, the old tools are so corroded and worn that they wouldn't even be worth keeping to sell as scrap.

Alchemical Spill.name: Alchemical Spill
Alchemical Spill.text:
A green substance bubbles and sizzles here, the vapor it emits is acrid, swirling with noxious fumes that burn the nostrils, suggesting danger even from a distance. More of the vile compound drips from the destroyed lab overhead.

Unfortunately this spill stands between the stairs and the rest of the quarry.

Toxic Barrier

Any character that touches or begins a turn already touching the slime spill suffers [[/damage 2d4 acid]] damage.

Characters passing through the dangerous vapor but not touching the slime (such as jumping or flying over it) can attempt a [[/save con 14]] saving throw to hold their breath, but failure results in taking [[/damage 1d6 acid]] damage.

Characters that touch or begin a turn already touching the slime spill suffer [[/hazard 4 fortitude health acid]]{Mild Acid Burns}.

Characters passing through the dangerous vapor but not touching the slime (such as jumping or flying over it) suffer [[/hazard 3 fortitude morale acid]]{Exposure to Acidic Vapors}.

Hazardous Spill

The chemicals are leaking from a destroyed lab overhead, the hole in the floor of the structure indicating some sort of explosion and subsequent corrosion of the metal by this chemical.

Characters with the [[/knowledge alchemy]] knowledge or making a successful[[/check intellect 14 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki] check note that this chemical is highly corrosive, pitting the stone anywhere it splashes, but isn't so corrosive that it's continuing to eat down into the stone.

Waterfall Crossing.name: Waterfall Crossing
Waterfall Crossing.text:
A cascade of water sweeps thought a channel in the stone, filling the air with mist and leaves the rocks underfoot are slick with a sheen of moss and moisture, presenting a treacherously slippery crossing. The unending rush of water floods the lower level, and creates an overwhelming roar that reverberates off the stone around you.

Slippery When Wet

The waterfall is moving too quickly to easily walk through. Characters attempting to wade through the waterfall must make a successful[[/check strength 14]] [[/skill athletics 14]] check or be swept off their feet and thrown into the water of the lower level.

Characters attempting to make a running &reference[long jump] across the waterfall need to cover a total of 15 feet to successfully clear the water.

Additionally, the 5ft of stone on either side of the waterfall is slippery, and serves as difficult terrain. This imposes a [[/check athletics 10]] check to successfully clear the slippery stone when jumping, and a further [[/check dex 10]] check to stay on one's feet when landing on the other side.

Characters can attempt to make a running jump across the waterfall, but will need to cross a distance of 20 feet in order to land safely, as 5 feet of stone on either side of the water are very slippery and loose. To successfully clear the distance requires a [[/skillCheck athletics 16]], but anyone who does not critically succeed gracelessly slips on the other side, suffering an embarassing but otherwise harmless [[/hazard 1 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Slip and Fall}.

Critical failure results in the jumper either misjudging their landing or falling significantly short of their target, the result is the same: they are swept away by the water and thrown into the water below.

Western Quarry.name: Western Quarry
Western Quarry.text: The west end of the quarry is home to a massive rock slab and never a pair of unfinished tunnels that terminate pointlessly in the dark. Old, abandoned tools rot in the darkness here, the metal pitted and ruined by the moisture in the air. A few old wheel barrows rot quietly, their wood bloated and warped after years of neglect.

Compound Lab.name: Compound Lab
Compound Lab.text:
Work in Progress! While this combat should come pre-configured in the scene for the Repurposed Quarry - Middle area, there is a chance that the actors have been cleared. For Early Access you may need to add the actors to the compound lab for this encounter.

The required actors are listed in the encounter below.

Wooden posts rise to meet the ceiling, remnants of the walls between them still visible in places. This hastily expanded workspace is filled with complexly arranged glassware brimming with strange alchemical mixtures. Four separate arrangements methodically distill, filter, stir, and transforms compounds for unknown reasons.

Behind them all, a desk, strewn with an assortment of books and papers that hold the promise of more information. To its immediate right a window looks out upon a churning waterwheel, its motion driving something unseen elsewhere.

@embed[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC]

@embed[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8 count=3]

Head of Studies

Kalasak is the overseer and director of this lab, and a dangerous individual in his own right. Upon first encounter he attempts to reason with interlopers, drawing them into a sense of safety, or at least reducing their vigilance. He is accompanied by three (3) @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]{Mutagist Vivisectors} that follow their overseer's lead.

However, once he sees an opening, Kalasak attempts to use his @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.jUtdYUnWW6X2VTrr]{Poison Needle} on an unwitting foe, and then turns his @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.BhYnUUBoU3ESkl1B]{Scalpel} on any other enemies.

Kalasak can also use his @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.52wAxR0OWeXJg0JD]{Prepare Vial} ability while adjacent to one of the tables of alchemical compounds to prepare a special attack to be used against his enemies.

He knows that failure to defend this lab and subdue the invaders will mean certain death for him, and as a result he has nothing to lose if defeat is looking likely. He fights ferociously, and without mercy.

If Kalasak is reduced to 0 HP his @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.7H1pkhJqO2mmm8mQ]{Fatal Contingency} immediately activates, preventing him from being stabilized, and removing any chance of interrogating his corpse via magic.

Dangerous Suspensions

There are four tables with different alchemical compounds loaded into them. Kalasak can use these to grab and throw vials of dangerous chemicals. These tables can also be smashed, causing them to spray dangerous compounds and shards of glass in all directions.

The glassware on the tables have an AC of 10 and 10 HP. When destroyed all creatures within 5 feet must succeed on a [[/save dex 15]] or suffer [[/damage 1d4 piercing]] and additional damage based on the color of the setup destroyed:

  • The Yellow setup deals an additional [[/damage 1d6 lightning]] damage

  • The Green setup deals an additional [[/damage 1d6 acid]] damage

  • The Blue setup deals an additional [[/damage 1d6 cold]] damage

  • The Orange setup deals an additional [[/damage 1d6 fire]] damage

Once a setup has been destroyed, Kalasak can't benefit from it to concoct an alchemical attack.

Before combat begins, Gamemasters should use the "Apply Toxin" or "Apply Poison" action as Kalasak secretly prepares to poison the unaware party.

Once he sees an opening, Kalasak attempts to use his already poisoned @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.g5d4FVRguB2bZY0A]{Cutter} on an unwitting foe, before turning the blade on any other close proximity enemies.

Throughout this combat, Kalasak makes liberal use of the alchemical workbenches in the small room to hurl available alchemical concoctions at the party. He knows that failure to defend this lab and subdue the invaders will mean certain death for him, and as a result he has nothing to lose if defeat is looking likely. He fights ferociously, and without mercy.

If Kalasak becomes Dead his @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.7H1pkhJqO2mmm8mQ]{Fatal Contingency} immediately activates, preventing him from being stabilized, and removing any chance of interrogating his corpse via magic.

Dangerous Suspensions

There are four tables with different alchemical compounds loaded into them. Kalasak can use these to grab and throw vials of dangerous chemicals. These tables can also be smashed, causing them to spray dangerous compounds and shards of glass in all directions.

GMs can use the following explosives from Kalasak's Backpack, but these are designed to reflect him throwing them from the proximity of each specific work bench.

  • @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.eM912khd1lngJdZB]{Alchemist's Fire}

  • @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.JG96q4OK5arsfuLP]{Caustic Phial}

  • @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.RP0MTlQoFArng2u9]{Electrocharge Ampoule}

  • @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC.Item.XKhLmAYd7O8xMmhC]{Frostdrop Phial}

Both Kalasak and the Party can choose to destroy the tables with a successful [[/skillCheck athletics 12]] by flipping the table or hurling an object into it to knock it over. Doing so causes the table to explode in a shattering of glass spraying compounds in a 5 foot blast, those affected suffer [[/hazard 2 fortitude health piercing]] from glass shards and [[/hazard 2 fortitude morale poison]] damage Once a setup has been destroyed, Kalasak can't benefit from it to concoct an alchemical attack.

If any of the workbenches survive the combat, the party can loot up to 2 of the bombs the bench provided, any others aren't in usable condition.

Alchemical Accounting

As long as the tables aren't destroyed, ransacking their collections of vials and bottles yields a collection of @UUID[Item.zfv8g0NUFtDKpmWL]{Rare Chemicals} per table.

Kalasak's desk holds various items:

  • A personal journal containing @UUID[Item.TGq3jsR9CvUuO2db]{Kalasak's Observations}.

  • A stack of @UUID[Item.b7tDeiRVqesPXrzC]{Experiment Reports}.

Mixing Room.name: Mixing Room
Mixing Room.text:
The mixing room hums and clatters with activity as the waterwheel outside turns steadily, powering the mechanism within.

Two large tanks, each positioned in opposite corners, dominate the room, their contents swirling under the influence of the waterwheel's transferred energy. These vessels rest on substantial, weathered iron tables adorned with an array of lab glassware and chemicals.

Notebooks, their pages open, reveal complex formulae etched in hurried hand, a testament to the ongoing alchemical experimentation.

Curious Compounds

The following items can be found here:

  • Stock and supply ledgers which yield a @UUID[Item.3KVOnp7wj7vPJ18k]{List of Chemicals} utilized in the laboratory.

  • A book containing numerous @UUID[Item.fg5P8yxtKHc0fUu1].

Testing Platform.name: Testing Platform
Testing Platform.text:
The testing platform is a massive block of stone twenty feet by twenty feet, standing starkly above the churning water, and only accessible by a bronze ramp.

At its center, a drakeling lies motionless on an examination table, its body connected by a series of tubes snaking from a tank of bubbling chemicals just next to it. Nearby, a complex glass apparatus orchestrates the flow of blood and chemicals within interconnected tubes and vials for some unknown purpose.

Surgical tools

The numerous tools here are well made, and well used, stained with the accumulated blood of numerous creatures. You doubt they were ever cleaned.

Blood Distiller

The complex collection of vials, tubes, mixers, and boilers is completely incomprehensible in purpose. Characters with the [[/knowledge alchemy]] knowledge or making a successful [[/check intelligence 14 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki] can determine that the array appears to be processing partially congealed drake blood into a substance for testing.

Dead Drakeling

A badly afflicted drakeling is strapped to the steel table here, and is long dead.

A successful [[/skill medicine 15]] [[/skillCheck medicine 15]] check determines that much of its blood having been pumped out of its body. Additionally, numerous incisions have been made across its body to remove tumors, explore seeping wounds, and examine organs.

Drum of Ooze

Characters with the [[/knowledge alchemy]] knowledge or making a successful [[/check intelligence 14 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki] notice that this is the same volatile chemical that was being utilize in the lab on the upper level.

The vat is set up to dispense samples into vials, allowing a character with the [[/knowledge alchemy]] knowledge or making a successful [[/check intelligence 14 tool=alchemist]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.alchemistsToolki] to acquire a @UUID[Item.q9PeGKDaP4NsAkEZ]{Vial of Mutagenic Medium}

Characters that examine the Examination Notes (below) also know that the purple chemical in the vat is what is a special alchemical medium. It is useless by itself, but if mixed with proper activator compounds it becomes a potent solution.

Books and Journals

A lectern holds @UUID[Item.uA95T3HphxYWqXRA]{Examination Notes} relating to this drake.

A rack nearby holds the following other documents:

  • A @UUID[Item.Xuvr7CbdXZmLLaGJ].

  • A journal containing the slab's @UUID[Item.fbER2KhZ438soBVy]{Testing Schedule}.

Flooded Pit.name: Flooded Pit
Flooded Pit.text:
Work in Progress!

While this combat should come pre-configured in the scene for the Repurposed Quarry - Lower area, there is a chance that the actor has been cleared. For Early Access you may need to add the Mutated Ultra Drake to the area for this encounter. The required actors are listed in the encounter below.

Make sure the Mutated Ultra Drake begins with the status "Invisible" or starts hidden to represent it being submerged.

The flooded pit marks the quarry's deepest point, a vast expanse now claimed by dark, swift-moving water. The reflective surface shimmers continuously under the erratic light, creating an illusion of boundless depth beneath. The sound of the cascading waterfall above reverberates through this space, adding to the sense of both confinement and expanse.

Drake Attack

The massive drake here prefers to remain out of sight for as long as it can, waiting to attack prey when they are unwary.

Characters moving through this area must succeed on a [[/skill perception 18]] [[/skillCheck awareness 18]] check to notice the presence of a massive, mutated drake lurking in the water of the flooded pit. Characters that fail are subject to &reference[surprise] @Condition[unaware] when the creature explodes from the water and attacks.

@embed[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls]

Drake Tactics

The drake is @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.LQcq5J0jLzyGwgMg]{Hyper-Aggressive} and relies on its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.RA4KljT1FHm2sPp1]{Useful Mutations} to protect it from severe injury when entering battle.

The drake is fast, capable of using its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.Z6egkpRJ2BaIEqhX]{Aggressive Rush} to quickly close distance. Combined with its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.FiijGKhZYVE6p5PG]{Twisted Leap} it can close distance at an alarming rate, and harm multiple foes in the process.

Up close, the drake uses its natural @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.KfLPMbyJZOhqwvr9]{Claws} and @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.bqO5foKPskgxHhbv]{Bite} attacks to rip apart foes.

When surrounded, the drake can use its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.gUFKr19RSTIFjrrd]{Tail Spin} to knock down and scatter nearby creatures, allowing it to escape or maneuver.

However, for all the drake's considerable power, it has limited stamina due to the ill-shaped form and heavy mutations. It can only use its Pummel, Spin, and Leap attacks once per battle.

The drake is very aggressive and its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.preternaturalins]{Preternatural Instinct} gives it a significant advantage over its prey, it relies on its substantially armored @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.wBzJjVVAz2ePthn1]{Drake Scales} to protect it from severe injury when entering battle.

The drake is fast, capable of using its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.swoopingStrike00} and @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.ruthlessmomentum] to quickly close distance and harm multiple foes in the process.

Up close, the drake uses its natural @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.KfLPMbyJZOhqwvr9]{Talons} and @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.bqO5foKPskgxHhbv]{Bite} attacks to rip apart foes, with its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.bloodletter00000] talent making these attacks particularly dangerous. The drake is ruthless, and will favor targets that are already @Condition[bleeding] (informed by @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.bloodSense000000]) and use this to fuel more actions through @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.bloodfrenzy00000].

If an opponent is for some reason unreachable, or if two or more party members cluster together, it will make use of its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.acidSpray0000000] and @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.acidSpit00000000] to punish them from a distance.

When surrounded, the drake can use its @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.tailSweep0000000]{Tail Sweep} to knock down and scatter nearby creatures, allowing it to escape or maneuver.

However, for all the drake's considerable power, it is has not been changed beyond the point of having survival instincts. If it feels its prey is too tough, or becomes @Condition[broken] it will flee, retreating back into the darkness or below the waters and out of sight. If it successfully flees, it tears loose of the @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.phkP3TCoSCIKrYEN]{Control Collar} , leaving it behind instead of the collar being found on the body as detailed below.

Explore

Examining the dead drake, you find a @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls.Item.phkP3TCoSCIKrYEN]{Control Collar}. A successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check reveals that the inscriptions and runs would have worked in concert with runes carved into the quarry walls to keep the drake in the lowest level.

  • Result of 16+ Success You notice that the runes would have leveled a shockingly powerful and likely painful psychic shock when triggered. However, the runes are largely burned out, and likely haven't functioned for quite a while.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success The amount of magical artifice needed to make something like this is considerable, and likely required it to be custom made. Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] note that while there's no clear maker's mark, the list of people who could create something of this sort is probably fairly short.

  • A further [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check regarding this would lead you to believe that the creature was eventually conditioned to remain in the quarry, even without a working collar. Likely, it was smart enough to know what would happen if it tried to breach containment, and unwilling to risk it.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the @UUID[Scene.emberBastionApex]{Bastion Apex} depicts a section of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion}. The party would arrive in this ultimate area of the bastion after navigating its prior area, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle]{Lightless Halls}.

Gazetteer Entry

@embed[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51 inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The following details describe and modify the mechanical traversal of the Bastion Apex area map.

Illumination

In the center of the Bastion Apex is an enormous orb of light, described in TODO. The Light of Lantyr creates bright light in an 80 foot radius and dim light for an additional 80 feet beyond (160 feet total). Areas of the scene which are not exposed to this light directly are treated as dim light.

Searing Light

Any character which moves within 10 feet of the Light of Lantyr or begins their turn there while in initiative order must make a [[/save constitution 15]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d8 radiant]] damage or half damage with a successful save.

Work In Progress

The mechanics caused by Searing Light will eventually be automated using Scene Regions, but for now must be evaluated manually by the Gamemaster.

Terrain

The surfaces of the Bastion Apex are treated as normal terrain unless otherwise specified.

Elevation

The Bastion Apex exists 500 feet above ground level. This spire rises far above the other buildings and fortifications of the Primordial Bastion.

The fortified walls and crennelations surrounding the apex perimeter are 20 feet tall, and the great Light of Lantyr hovers 30 feet in the air above the surface of the Apex.

The stairs on each side of the apex descend 20 feet to platforms which open to the spire interior which is not depicted in this Scene.

Apex Summit.name: Apex Summit
Apex Summit.text:
Interactive Elements

This scene has several interactive elements:

  • The Orb of Lantyr itself (GM only)

  • 12 Light Barrier Towers (GM only)

  • 4 Light Crystal Turrets (Player controlled)

Left click on these elements while the Interaction tool is active to open a dialog with options for how to interact with them.

The Orb of Lantyr

The orb itself has three interactive states:

  1. Defenses Inactive (the initial state)

  2. Defenses Active (when Luxaroth activates them)

  3. Destroyed (if the orb is destroyed)

When defenses are activated, the light barriers around the arena become active, blocking movement. The Light Crystal Turrets also become usable at this time.

If the Orb is destroyed, the entire arena goes dark, all barriers come down, and the turrets are no longer operable.

Light Barrier Towers

There are twelve Light Crystal Towers surrounding the platform of the Bastion Apex. Each tower has three interactive states:

  1. Repaired (their initial state)

  2. Damaged

  3. Broken

Towers that are damaged will become broken in the subsequent round of combat (as described below).

Work In Progress

At this point in Early Access, the interactive elements described above for the energy turrets are not yet functional. They will be added in a future update.

Meeting the First Giant

A vast orb of glowing radiant energy hovers 30 feet in the air above the surface of the Apex. It emits light so intensely that looking directly at it for more than a few moments is blinding.

The intense light from the brilliant orb of Lantyr above is nearly blinding when looking directly up at the Bastion Apex. All details of the immense structure are washed away in yellow and white light. Before you can take another step, a booming voice rings out, breaking the silence.

KURAS VUNRUNAC-TAR

Whoever understands Pathward to some extent realizes that this person is speaking an incredibly archaic and primordial variant of the language, and anyone who holds the Sun Star also hears:

HOLD STRANGERS

@Embed[Actor.d0mSoQozEIKozWVe]

Convincing Luxaroth

Luxaroth is somewhat wary of the party, having never seen such creatures before and lacking knowledge of their intentions. He possesses the ability @UUID[Actor.d0mSoQozEIKozWVe.Item.auUAIcbJJxXCNkRj]{Radiant Sense} and can tell if any of the party members before him are influenced by the Abyss, regardless of deception rolls or attempts to hide such things.

Anyone who can speak [[/language pathward]] or anyone holding the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} can communicate with Luxaroth directly. If that is their intention, they will need to succeed on a [[/check per 13]] check, likely explaining to Luxaroth that they are here to help. Anyone with [[/knowledge shent]] has @Advantage[2] for this check. Failing this check does not mean Luxaroth will attack the party, but he remains wary and will not lower his guard.

If there is a Cleric or follower of Lantyr in the party, no checks are required, as Luxaroth recognizes a fellow adherent of the light and immediately becomes friendly and warm towards them and the party as a whole.

However, if the party includes anyone who possesses Abyssal Attunement or holds Abyssal items, will need to succeed on a [[/check per 18]] check instead and must explain to Luxaroth that, despite the corruption, they are still here to help. Failing this check does not automatically result in Luxaroth attacking the party; whether he does so is ultimately up to the GM's discretion, depending on the levels of Abyssal influence within the party, as well as whether anyone is evil or purposely lying to Luxaroth to betray him later.

Talking with Luxaroth

The party can now converse with the Avatar of the First Giants, whose true name is Luxaroth. Luxaroth is an ancient being, a huge and intimidating figure who has no fear of the party. He speaks in a great booming voice and will even laugh as he speaks if he is sufficiently pleased by the party's questions or responses. During the following conversation, he provides additional basic information:

  • He will reveal that he is an Avatar and no longer truly corporeal, though he was once made of flesh and bone. He is now tied to the Orb of Lantyr above his head, and if it were to fail, he would fade into nothingness. He is not responsible for his current state; rather, he was bound to the orb by his fellow giants long ago. So long, in fact, that he has no concept of time or what age of the world he currently exists in.

  • He informs the party that he is called a Giant, a follower of a deity called Lantyr. Though he has never seen her true visage, he has followed her through the device above his head, which he calls the Orb of Lantyr. He once had a deep and close relationship with the goddess, but over many thousands of years, the orb's powers have waned, eventually cutting off this connection entirely.

  • He has never seen creatures like the party and has no idea where they came from; he is fascinated to learn about the current cultures if the party tries to explain the world above and the goings-on of the Arctus Plateau and Ordain.

  • He has stood watch over this section of the Pathways since an event he calls the Unveiling among his own people, where they fought each other over knowledge of the Abyss. This is something he will not speak more of as his eyes darken and sorrow flashes across his face for a moment.

  • When the Orb of Lantyr was fully powered, he could roam far from its light as he was still connected through its radiance despite the distance, but now he can't venture far from its light.

If the party asks how they can help repair or protect the Orb of Lantyr:

"Your heroism and compassion do you credit, young ones; you may have already brought the Orb's salvation with you, though you knew it not. I sense an item within your possession, a relic of the light that once lay below this tower that I could not claim myself. Within it lies enough radiant energy to empower the Orb above; all you have to do is lay it down before the orb or stand close to it so that the absorption can begin."

It should be clear that Luxaroth is fairly removed from current affairs but has some ancient knowledge that he is happy to share, depending on whether the party has convinced him they are friendly. If not, and Luxaroth remains wary, they may attempt to try again using various methods or tactics to convince Luxaroth by rolling a [[/check per 15]]. On a failure, nothing happens, but on a success, Luxaroth opens up a little.

If asked for additional information on various topics, Luxaroth has some direct responses for the party, detailed below.

Regarding First Giants:

My people called themselves Giants. We built much of what you see before you; beneath the world and within us flowed the energy of creation itself. Long did we labor, shaping the paths, guiding the waters, holding back the lifeblood, and settling the destructive forces of chaos. We were guided by... well, a being who ultimately abandoned us, but for a long age, he gave us great knowledge and purpose.

Regarding the Abyss

DO NOT SPEAK OF IT.. it is a terrible and unspeakable evil. My people learned of it long ago, and it caused our entire civilization to collapse upon itself. Do not underestimate the power of knowledge and of learning too much, little ones.

Regarding the Unveiling:

The end of my people, the end of everything, when darkness broke free and infected my kin, my friends, and my family. Our cities erupted in chaos and death as Giants fought Giants. You would be wise to learn from our mistakes and our failings. I only rest easy with the knowledge that some of my kind fled to the surface to escape the darkness; I hope they found a better world.

Revealing the fate of the Shent is something that Luxaroth will be deeply affected by.

So again, my people fall, paying for our ancient folly.. I lament the end of my kind, but our fate was written in stone long ago.

Regarding the Bastion:

I was told it was once a happy place, filled with laughter and glimmering lights but I came here later, after.. the blood had stained the stone. I lived and grew up in the light of the Heart itself but this bastion of light became by task and my burden. I followed my goddess in life and throughout the ages of the world I will do all that I can to safeguard this world against the evils from beyond.

Regarding the Orb of Light above:

The only thing holding back the deep darkness, the void of evil, and the monsters with claws and shining eyes. I have been guarding it for so long that I always thought it would shine for eternity, but over time, I began to notice its radiance fading, extremely slowly at first. However, a single drip of water, over a long enough period, will carve its way through a mountain. Restoring its power will not only safeguard this section of the world for another age, but it will also allow me to act freely once again; I will be able to roam and combat distant evils wherever I find them. Which I have no shame in admitting, would fill my soul with wrathful joy.

Once the party has spoken with Luxaroth, with the knowledge that Abyssal monsters are rapidly approaching, read the following and roll initiative afterwards:

Luxaroth turns to you and readies his massive blade, swinging it around his body with blinding speed and experienced ease. His words then bellow from his mouth, shouting above the rising cacophony of monstrous snarls and rending stone.

"READY YOURSELVES LITTLE HEROES, I WILL RAISE THE BARRIER BUT IT WILL NOT HOLD THEM LONG."

Luxaroth then raises his arms and clasps his blade with both enormous hands. As he does so, a great burst of power explodes outward, striking the towers at the edges of the Apex. With newfound life and energy, a radiant, glowing barrier of light springs forth between the towers, expanding upward to envelop the entire area in a dome of protective light. As on cue, the monstrous host begins emerging from below and begins to spring forth from the stairs and climbing the outer walls of the Bastion tower. With some even flying upward from the dense fog and whirling across the air itself. They recoil slightly at the sight of the barrier before throwing themselves into a destructive frenzy, attacking both the barrier and the outer structures of the tower with abandon.

Repairing the Orb

With the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} in their possession, the act of repairing the Orb of Lantyr is relatively simple and only requires the presence of the character holding the item. Over time, radiant energy leaks from the Sun Star and is absorbed by the Orb of Lantyr above.

After [[x]] number of rounds of combat, the Orb of Lantyr is restored to its full power, radiating powerful energy across the Fogbound Caverns and re-establishing a direct link to the Elder Goddess Lantyr. This is how the combat and encounter on top of the Bastion Apex ends and has nothing to do with the health pool of the Orb of Lantyr itself. The objective for the party in this encounter is too simply hold off the Abyssal host for as long as possible.

The radiant energy transfer begins as soon as the conversation with Luxaroth ends, and the light barrier is raised. You may read the following after initiative is rolled:

A wispy, cloud-like beam of pure yellow and orange energy begins to flow from the Sun Star relic, traveling upwards into the orb above. A rhythmic pulsing sound and a deep hum of energy start to ring out simultaneously.

Around the apex there are scattered four defensive emplacements where large golden crystals sits ato ancient and complex mechanisms.

Radiant Energy & Spells

Any player character with radiant spells may wish to spend their actions during combat to speed up the process of empowering and repairing the Orb of Lantyr.

This is technically feasible, and expending an action to cast a spell would decrease the number of rounds of combat by 1. However, the challenge lies in approaching the Orb of Lantyr while taking intense radiant damage and also being close enough to the Orb itself, which is floating 25 feet in the air above the Apex. Ultimately, it's within the GM's purview to allow any creative actions that would enable characters to reach and empower the orb during the combat encounter in addition to the Sun Star.

The Flow of Battle

This encounter is large, complex, and potentially challenging to run. There are plenty of fun elements and moving pieces, but the general flow has a tempo that needs some explanation before things begin in earnest. A great deal of this combat revolves around managing the influx of monsters at the edges of the combat as the barriers around the edges of the Apex fail. Ultimately, by the end of the encounter, the party may feel like they are about to be overwhelmed completely, as most of the barriers will have fallen and many monsters will be inside, attacking the orb, Luxaroth, and the party itself. The party can still win even if they are all unconscious, just as long as they held off the Abyssal host from the orb long enough.

  • Monsters attack the Light Barrier towers at the end of each round, damaging one at a time. Which tower is damaged is the GM's decision. With a tower damaged, there is a visual indication for the party regarding which barriers will fail in the following round.

  • Once a tower is destroyed and a barrier has fallen, all the Abyssal Monsters gathering outside that section of the map move forwards and attack the party, the Light Crystal Turrets, Luxaroth, and the Orb of Lantyr itself.

  • Each type of Abyssal monster shares initiative with all others. For example, when it's the Abyssal Eyes' turn in the initiative order, all the Abyssal Eyes move and act. Each type of Abyssal monster has various targets, which are detailed below.

  • The overarching objective for the Abyssal host gathered at the Apex is to destroy the Orb of Lantyr before it can be empowered in [x] number of rounds.

Orb of Lantyr Tactics

The Orb of Lanytyr does not have any kind of sentience or sapience and has no tactics other than to float passively 25 feet above the Apex. Its only feature is @UUID[Actor.pLe1VlhFsHnNqaYL.Item.osvAXIKWCFvnWRcK]{Burning Sun}, which constantly deals damage to anything that moves too close, including those trying to stand under it.

Light Energy Turret Tactics

There are four Light Energy Turrets within the scene, each positioned around the @UUID[Actor.pLe1VlhFsHnNqaYL]{Orb of Lantyr}. These ancient defense platforms can be used by the party to protect the Orb during the battle, but they can be destroyed. They are non-sentient and non-sapient constructs and do not act independently; instead, the party can use a bonus action to activate their [Light Beam] features and target a section of the Apex.

Note: The [Light Beam] damage does affect any creature, and thus it will hit the player characters and deal extensive damage.

Work In Progress

At this point in Early Access, the interactive elements described above for the energy turrets are not yet functional and will be added in a subsequent update.

Actors vs. Interactive Elements

The Orb of Lantyr and the four Light Energy Turrets are Actors because they can be targeted and attacked by the Abyssal monsters in the scene. However, the Light Barrier Towers are interactive elements as they are broken and destroyed as part of the flow and tempo of the battle, and cannot be targeted by the Abyssal Monsters specifically.

Fighting the Host of Monsters

Combat begins as soon as initiative is rolled. During the first round, the Abyssal monster will be outside the barrier and unable to attack directly. This gives the party one round to cast spells and prepare. They will also be able to see where the first tower has been damaged and where the Abyssal host will attack first.

@Embed[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM]

Abyssal Eel Tactics

These small Abyssal Monsters can move forwards quickly and use their 60 feet of fly movement to head directly for the @UUID[Actor.pLe1VlhFsHnNqaYL]{Orb of Lantyr}. On their turn, they will deal damage to the Orb but die in the next turn due to the Orb of Lantyr's [Burning Sun] ability. Most of the Abyssal Eels will not be drawn towards the party or Luxaroth, unless they lie directly in front of their path towards the Orb, in which case, they attack whatever is directly in front of that route.

@Embed[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE]

Abyssal Echo Tactics

The Abyssal Echoes have similar tactics to the Abyssal Eels and will head towards the @UUID[Actor.pLe1VlhFsHnNqaYL]{Orb of Lantyr} using their 40 feet fly speed. However, unlike the Abyssal Eels, the Echoes will purposely target party members in the general area within 30 feet of them, as long as there are at least two echoes near each other. They will try to use @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.gHXWVaidho85zB1L]{Pack Tactics} to their advantage and swarm players or Luxaroth. In addition, if there is a Crystal Light Turret in their path, they will try to destroy that as a priority target as well.

@Embed[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ]

Abyssal Eye Tactics

The Abyssal Eyes will stay as far away from any of the party members as they can while remaining in range of the @UUID[Actor.pLe1VlhFsHnNqaYL]{Orb of Lantyr} with their @UUID[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ.Item.lNrBkcszQBheNyP1]{Eye Blast}. They will not target party members, nor Luxaroth or the Crystal Light Turrets at all, and will focus all their attention on the Orb.

@Embed[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A]

Vhismara's Claw Tactics

As every Vhismara's claw claws its way up the stairs, or the outer edge of the tower, they will immediately seek out and target Luxaroth during the encounter. If enemies surround Luxaroth, they will instead try to move towards and attack party members or the Crystal Light Turrets. As these creatures cannot fly, they cannot harm the @UUID[Actor.pLe1VlhFsHnNqaYL]{Orb of Lantyr}.

Orb Restored

After [X] number of rounds, the Orb drains radiance from the Sun Star and is fully restored. When this occurs, read the following:

The rhythmic pulsing sound and deep hum of energy from the orb reach an almost overwhelming peak. With a blast of thunderous sound, a wave of golden yellow light bursts forth and washes over the Apex. As it crashes into the monsters still flowing upwards and around the tower, they explode with dazzling brilliance and fade into nothing. The screeching sounds and noise of battle cease, and a deep, comforting hum now rings out across the fogbound Caverns as the Orb is fully restored.

Abyssal Remains

Typically, when Abyssal monsters are defeated, they leave behind a miasmic black ooze with their @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.5ww5bC5eQN2D45gC]{Abyssal Remains} feature. This does not occur when the orb destroys the host, as the power of the Light is powerful enough to destroy the remains utterly. They simply disappear, and any remains that were left upon the Apex from monsters killed during the course of the battle are also swept away.

Resting on the Apex

If the Orb was destroyed during the encounter skip the dialogue below and head back to the event page of @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.LyNcEPtA6HA1XvQZ]{Shining Obelisk}, there is nothing further for them on the Apex. Though no doubt @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A]{Nadin} will be excited by this outcome. The party can rest upon the now dark Apex, but it is bleak and increasingly cold as the hours roll by.

If the Abyssal host has been defeated, Orb of Lantyr restored, the party can relax and rest. If Luxaroth is still active he will offer to use his renewed powers to teleport the party away the Bastion and back to the edge of the Fogbound Caverns. They may continue to talk with Luxaroth about subjects that still interest them. Luxaroth will be overjoyed by this outcome and will promise to aid the party if they need help in the future. Once the party is ready to depart, read the following.

With the light above restored to full power, it shines like a new burning sun above you. Though it is warming and bright, its energy is calming, radiant, and somehow measured, as if held back by an unseen hand. The gigantic avatar that fought alongside you beams with renewed energy and joy, turning to you as you prepare to depart.

"An auspicious day, little heroes. I have not felt the light this keenly since days long past. Let the evils from beyond despair at my unleashed wrath in the days to come! Go with my blessing and the blessings of my goddess... oh yes, that's right... my goddess sends her own regards and wants me to inform you that you find another friend in the glittering white city above, in a nook hidden behind dusty tomes.

Hah, yes, her words, not mine, I have no idea what that means. In any case, as I said, go with my blessing, little heroes. You are champions of the light now, and may it guide your hands in the days to come."

When ready, refer back to @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.LyNcEPtA6HA1XvQZ]{Shining Obelisk} for the next steps in the quest event narrative.

Lower Platforms.name: Lower Platforms
Lower Platforms.text:
The immense stone stairs of the obelisk-like tower zigzag internally until, just before the apex, they open into the open air, revealing the dim, gloomy expanse of the Fogbound Caverns below.

Stairways of Stone

As the party enters the scene, they appear on the lower platforms, just out of sight of the higher Apex area. They are not immediately obvious to Luxaroth, who is standing under the Orb of Lantyr. If they wish, the party can attempt to wait, observe, and study their surroundings for a time before moving forward.

The shadows cast by the Orb of Lantyr above the Apex allow you to move up the stairs just ahead while remaining concealed from the immense figure standing resolutely beneath it.

Observing from the Shadows

If the party decides to roll stealth in an attempt to remain hidden. All characters must succeed on a [[/check stealth 15]] check. This allows them to passively observe the scene before them in more detail before conversing with @UUID[Actor.d0mSoQozEIKozWVe]{Luxaroth}. With more time the players can take in the environment more clearly and see the following.

  • In any other environment, the Apex would be windswept and cold, but inside the Pathways, despite its height, the tower here is oddly still and silent without wind. Looking down over the short stone wall surrounding the stairs, the omnipresent fog is thick and motionless; the ground and the rest of the bastion are barely visible.

  • There does not appear to be anything living on top of the bastion, no plants and no animals whatsoever.

  • The massive orb of light floating above the tower is radiant and nearly blinding. However, when observed over several minutes, its light emissions are not as consistent as you thought, and tiny flickers in its output are clearly visible. le.

Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] or anyone who successfully [[/check arcana 13]] will intuitively understand that the magic used to create the Orb of Lantyr is fading. While it may have once been a mighty and much more powerful artifact, most of the warding, spellcraft, and magic surrounding it is weathered by immense age.

Rushing Host

If the party enters the scene, and they have not remained hidden, or once they have remained hidden for a time read the following:

Behind you, the silence around you is broken by the rushing sound of cold wind. Although no air actually moves around you, a deep chill settles upon your body as if the area is becoming engulfed in something. Behind you, deep within the tower that you just climbed, you can hear horrific sounds of claws scratching and rending deep into the stonework. This is accompanied by more sounds of many, if not hundreds, of monsters, as the chittering, snarling, and barking mix with the sounds of rushing movement. As the noise continues to grow, you realize that a host of creatures is moving upwards towards the apex of the tower upon which you now stand.

Fall Damage & Outcome

The party at this point cannot leave the tower and descend safely, unless they wish to jump off the top of the Apex. This route is possible but inadvisable. Characters who attempt to jump will face massive fall damage, as the tower is nearly 200 feet tall. If anyone does jump they will suffer [[/damage 20d6 bludgeoning]] damage as a result when they land.

Characters with spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.pub0OWVEB71XQx1n]{Feather Fall } or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.yfbK8gZqESlaoY5t]{Fly} would still take some damage from the attempt as they would be unable to see the ground beneath them and could smash into unseen buildings and dangers in the deep fog around the tower. In this case, characters would need to roll a [[/save dex 15]] as they fall, suffering [[/damage 6d6 bludgeoning]] if they fail the check as they smash into things during the descent.

Its safe to assume that any party that does decide to do this, suffers the [Broken Orb of Lantyr] outcome as the fight above does not go well without their aid. You can head back to the @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.LyNcEPtA6HA1XvQZ]{Shining Obelisk} at this point and read Aftermath section.

Most parties at this point will likely conclude that heading back the way they came is no longer possible. They can attempt to understand a little more about the sounds behind them or even attempt to move down the stairs.

Snarling in the Deep.

Attempting to learn more about the sounds behind them, any character who succeeds on a [[/check perception 13]] check or has [[/knowledge abyssals]] knows that the sounds coming from behind them are similar to the sounds of the monsters they encountered in the Lightless Halls or elsewhere in the Fogbound Caverns. These are the sounds of many @UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A]{Vhismara's Claw} clawing at the stone and @UUID[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ]{Abyssal Eye} pushing against one another in a great host and possibly some unknown monsters as well. They are climbing the stairs quickly, but the characters are not immediately in danger and have some time to prepare; however, an assault by a great force is inevitable.

Wall of Darkness

If anyone from the party attempt to move down the stairs, in order to confront the monsters on the stairs or in an attempt to flee read the following:

As you attempt to step foot upon the stairs leading down a wall of darkness seems to slam into you body, you recoil with pain as the combined force of the darkness below seems to prevent your escape.

That characters and any that attempts to head down the stairs must roll [[/save con 14]] suffering [[/damage 1d8 bludgeoning]] if they fail. If they succeed the check they cannot push past the wall of darkness in front of them but take no damage.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the @UUID[Scene.emberLightlessHa]{Lightless Halls} depicts a section of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion}. The party would arrive in this area of the complex after venturing through other sections of less notable ruins and chambers.

Gazetteer Entry

@embed[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51 inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Non Linear Route

To reach the final boss encounter in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.x39WFCk54eXGA5JV]{Sealed Chamber}, the party must first activate and open the central door in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.orVcdj9VxumYSiT2]{Bastion Antechamber}. This door cannot be opened until all light bowls within the antechamber have been lit using the@UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} (an item found in the East Wing's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.NQYLVd3qv4YvwGuA]{Runekey Altar} room).

Filling all four light bowls in the antechamber not only unlocks the Sealed Chamber, but also lights the southern light channel and gives access to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.0B4Yde6z0sLb0h1b]{Statues of Remembrance} room. Once the Statues of Remembrance puzzle is unlocked, parties will be able to access the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.3yPEI2VvrOAbxNPZ]{Treasure Room} next to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.111T8HXHnIo7nXjn]{Void Bridge}.

Illumination

A powerful Abyssal Darkness has taken over this section of the Primordial Bastion, shrouding large portions of it in magical darkness. A @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} can be recovered from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.NQYLVd3qv4YvwGuA]{Runekey Altar} and carried by one of the characters to create a mobile light capable of countering the Abyssal Darkness. Areas which are affected by neither Abyssal Darkness nor a Sun Star are treated as mundane darkness.

Abyssal Darkness

Any character who remains in Abyssal Darkness for longer than 6 seconds, or begins their turn in Abyssal Darkness when in initiative order, must make a [[/save intelligence 15]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d8 psychic]] damage.

Within Abyssal Darkness, mundane light sources are nullified and visibility is entirely negated unless the darkness is counteracted by a @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star}.

The Abyssal Darkness can be temporarily countered via use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.BP3GCwa66IAw1yTG]{Daylight} spell, but this spell is not powerful enough to dispel the effect darkness permanently.

Work In Progress

The current implementation of Abyssal Darkness is not entirely complete, but is partly functional. Non-magical light sources in this area do not function, and characters do not benefit from vision modes like Darkvision.

Only magical light sources which are configured with Priority of 1 or higher will supersede the ambient darkness which is present throughout this area.

The Sun Star can be used at certain fixed positions within the Lightless Halls to fill empty Light Bowls. Once active, Light Bowls, and anything they flow through, including Light Channels across the floor of the halls and Light Sconces on the walls, create bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light in an additional 10-foot radius.

Terrain

The hallways of the Lightless Halls are treated as normal terrain unless otherwise specified.

Elevation

All floors of this area exist at the same elevation. Ceilings in the Lightless Halls are 50 feet high unless otherwise stated.

There are several areas where the floor opens into a void below. There is no specific depth of this void as the expanse below is magical and fathomless in nature.

Void Stasis

Any character which falls into the void beneath the Lightless Halls is immediately affected by the &Reference[paralyzed] condition and teleported into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.Okk4y4H2ASNCP7Ev]{Containment Chamber} where they remain paralyzed for 24 hours.

This paralysis can be negated via use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.F0GsG0SJzsIOacwV]{Lesser Restoration} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} spells.

East Hallways.name: East Hallways
East Hallways.text:
Gamemaster's Note

This hallway has two states – dark, as it is when characters first enter, and illuminated, which occurs after characters have filled the light channels in this section of the bastion.

The Dark Hallway

The looming hallway in front of you is completely dark, and an overwhelming sense of scale and foreboding envelops you as you try to peer into the gloom. The corridor stretches far beyond the reach of your light source, at least 30 feet wide and towering 50 feet high, with a ceiling that appears to merge with the shadows above. The walls, crafted from massive stone blocks, are mostly pristine, but throughout the hallway, pieces of the wall have crumbled onto the floor.

A First Glance

Characters may use a [[/check perception 14]] check to take an initial look at the hallway.

  • With a success, characters can tell that some of the darkness of the hallways is unnatural, requiring more than a conventional or simple magical light to illuminate.

    • With a successful [[/check arcana 15]] check or [[/knowledge abyssals]], they recognize it as a form of abyssal darkness.

  • With a success of 3 or more, they also notice grooves in the floor that extend the length of the hallway.

    A pattern appears to run through the floor, but some lines within it are cut more deeply, like veins, as if something once ran through them.

Investigating the Hallway

Characters who examine the hallway as a whole can discover the following:

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 15]] check or [[/check nature 15]] check, characters can determine that the crumbled pieces of wall were damaged by some kind of attack or act of violence. They did not crumble naturally.

    • If characters experienced the event [[/eventState fallAgainDestruction]], they can see that the damage is similar to whatever damaged the Shent pillars.

  • With a successful [[/check arcana 15]] check, characters know that the pristine nature of the walls outside of the damage is a sign of some sort of primordial magic power, which is holding the place together despite its age.

    • If characters experienced the event [[/eventState fallAgainVoidspan]], they can tell that the magic they are sensing is similar to what they encountered on the Voidspan bridge.

The Illuminated Hallway

The channels of light beneath your feet stretch through the hallway like a life line, warm and humming beneath your feet. While you cannot see all the way into the depths of the structure, the hallway glows with more warmth than it did before, seeming to beckon you deeper into the bastion.

Runekey Altar.name: Runekey Altar
Runekey Altar.text:
The large chamber is illuminated by intensely glowing barriers that stretch across the room and reach all the way to the ceiling above, blocking access any further into the room. Below your feet lie large primordial runes meticulously inscribed onto stone panels. Along the walls, a series of stone stelae adorned with smaller runic symbols seem to have been placed deliberately to match the panels on the wall.

The Light Barrier

Investigating the Light Barrier

The light barrier feels solid to anyone who approaches it, as if it is an impenetrable wall. With a successful [[/check arcana 16]] check, characters know that the barrier of light is of an ancient primordial magic of almost unimaginable power.

  • Result of 20+. You recognize this to be a permanent @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplWallofForc]{Wall of Force} which cannot be countered except through use of powerful high-level magic.

If characters touch the light barrier while it is active, they hear a sizzling sound in their ears and feel a compulsion to back away.

Though nothing appears to happen, the sizzling sound of burning feels like it drills into your ears, and you smell the faintest whiff of smoke. You feel an overwhelming urge to stop, first whisper-quiet against your eardrums and then louder and louder and louder.

If characters stop what they are doing upon feeling this compulsion, there is no lasting effect. If they continue in their course of action, they must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 16]] saving throw or they feel a deep desire to leave the wall along and get away from it, as if they gained the &Reference[Frightened] condition.

The Runekey Puzzle

Examining the Stone Panels

The stone floor panels in front of the party appear different than any of the stone around them, each etched with its own symbol. Characters who take a closer look at the panels can learn the following. Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on the checks.

  • With a [[/check nature 14]] check, it is clear that the stone of the panels is of higher quality than the stone that surrounds it, as if designed to stand the test of time. It is the same type of stone as the slabs on the wall, with are each carved with a single symbol.

  • With a [[/check history 14]] check, or if they understand [[/language pathward]], characters recognize the runes as being in a language similar to Pathward. Given the age of the Bastion, it is likely that Pathward evolved from this language.

  • With a [[/check arcana 14]] check, characters can sense intense magical energy coming from the panels on the floor and have a strong sense that they are used to disable the light sensor.

Any stone panel touched by a character immediately glows. If touched again, the glow dims. If multiple panels are touched, but are not in the correct order, the panels blink once all seven have been activated and then go dark.

The light from the panels flashes and then fades. It seems as if something has not yet been activated correctly.

Interactive Rune Puzzle

To solve each of the two rune puzzles in this chamber, players (or the GM) must activate the runes in their correct logical sequence to complete the phrases described below.

Each phrase is a sequence of seven runes, and if completed in the incorrect order the puzzle will automatically reset. If completed in the correct order, the runes will remain illuminated and the magical barrier of light will disappear.

Using Blind Rolls

We recommend using blind rolls for skill checks made during this puzzle so that players do not know whether they have successfully or unsuccessfully interpreted each glyph. This lack of meta-information will improve the roleplaying experience of solving the puzzle.

The First Puzzle

Investigating the Stone Stelae

The only clue as to the meaning of the runes in the panels are engraved stone stelae on the side of the room, which characters notice without a check.

The stone stelae are engraved with symbols and drawings that hint at their meaning. You see several of the runes from the floor of the chamber replicated on the images, as if waiting to be interpreted and understood.

Characters succeeding on a [[/skill arcana 18]] or with [[/knowledge rituals]] can understand that the runes on the floor must likely be invoked in a specific order which serves as a type of passphrase.

Deciphering the Glyphs

Players may reference the stelae on either side of the chamber to translate each of the runes which appear upon the floor. The table below provides the definitions of each glyph in left-to-right order. For example the meaning of the first glyph on the left is "Eternal". It is possible to either imperfectly or incorrectly translate each glyph.

To attempt deciphering a specific glyph, a character must make a skill check against a DC of 15 using the skill described for each glyph in the table. Specific knowledge areas can substitute for this roll and instead count as an automatic success. A character may only attempt deciphering each individual glyph a single time.

  • Result below 5. The character incorrectly interprets the the Incorrect meaning of the glyph.

  • Result between 5 and 9. The character is unable to decipher the glyph.

  • Result between 10 and 14. The character discerns the Approximate meaning of the glyph.

  • Result of 15+. The character discerns the Exact meaning of the glyph.

Characters with [[/language pathward]] or [[/knowledge shent]] make these skill checks with @Advantage[2].

The First Keyphrase

The puzzle is correctly solved by activating the following runes in the order 2-5-7-6-1-3-4 producing the following phrase in ancient Pathward.

Unknown beyond the Weave causes eternal world destruction.

A character who succeeds on an [[/skill investigation 25]] check may deduce the correct sequence using subtle clues in the ligatures of each glyph which imply how they are intended to connect.

Once all runes have been activated in the correct order, the runes begin to glow more brightly and the light barrier in front of the party dissipates.

For a moment, the light of the barrier in front of you glows more strongly, matching the rapidly brightening glow of the etched panels at your feet. As the panels continue to shine light, ever more brightly, the barrier before you dims and fades to nothing, with a faint gentle whisper which you instinctually understand to mean:

The abyss beyond the Weave will destroy everything that Ember is.

The Second Puzzle

Beyond the first light barrier, the party encounters a second set of runes on the floor and second light barrier in front of them.

Ahead of you, on the floor, sits a raised set of engraved stone platforms, nearly identical to the ones that glow behind you. In front of them, another barrier of light stretches across the chamber, but beyond it you can see a dais that holds something on it that glitters and sparkles in the light.

Deciphering the Glyphs

Without a check, characters can see that the Stelae in this section of the room appear to be nearly identical, though age has worn away symbols in the markings on each.

This puzzle is solved using the same mechanics and rules as the first where characters can discern the meanings of the following glyphs in left-to-right order.
