The Second Keyphrase

The puzzle is correctly solved by activating the following runes in the order 5-6-2-1-3-7-4 producing the following phrase in ancient Pathward.

Search Lantyr's light, protect future life dreams.

A character who succeeds on an [[/skill investigation 25]] check may deduce the correct sequence using subtle clues in the ligatures of each glyph which imply how they are intended to connect.

As before, the light barrier pulses powerfully, harmonizing with the rhythm of the ancient glyphs. The barrier fades away, leaving behind a gentle whisper which you understand to mean:

The guiding the light of Lantyr will shelter our bodies and shield our dreams.

The Sun Star

The Sun Star

The artifact protected behind the puzzles and light barriers in this room is one of the First Giant's last great creations, the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star}. This item is a portable device that contains immense radiant energy capable of holding back Abyssal energy and darkness. It is a key item that is required for the remainder of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle]{Lightless Halls} and also the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkBasApex]{Bastion Apex} ahead.

When the party reaches the ornate stone altar in his room, read the following:

Before you stands a massive stone altar adorned with exquisite carvings and patterns. Now that the light barriers have been deactivated, you can clearly see a glittering object radiating intense energy sitting atop the altar.

With a successful [[/check arcana 15]] check or the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify}, characters know that this is an item of magic that brings light to abyssal darkness.

The Sun Star can be carefully picked up from the altar at any time. Only one person can hold the Sun Star at a time.

Examining the Altar

Characters who take a closer look at the altar, whether before or after picking up the Sun Star, and succeed on a [[/check history 15]] check, find a pattern in the inscriptions that they recognize from ancient texts: "light of sun."

If characters have identified a similar inscription on the Stone Bowl at the end of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.111T8HXHnIo7nXjn]{Void Bridge} or elsewhere in the area, they know it is the same inscription without a check.

Work In Progress

Application of the light generated by the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} is not yet automated for the character which acquires it. As the Gamemaster you must configure that character's token to emit light with the following configuration:

  • Dim = 30 feet

  • Bright = 15 feet

  • Attenuation = 1.0

  • Luminosity = 1.0

  • Color = #fedb90

  • Alpha = 0.5

  • Priority = 1 (this is important!)

Void Bridge.name: Void Bridge
Void Bridge.text:
A large stone bridge stretches across this room, with a deep channel carved into the floor in its center. On the far side, a stone bowl can be seen in the gloom. Looking down below the bridge, you initially see only darkness and a deep black void, but as your eyes adjust, you can see that the void itself is actually glittering with a multitude of small sparkling lights.

This room is primarily a combat encounter. Once the party reaches the middle of the bridge, the Abyssal eyes attack, and initiative is rolled.

@Embed[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ]

Abyssal Eye Tactics

The four Abyssal Eyes in this room are waiting in ambush and have hidden themselves in the darkest, distant corners of the room. The party cannot discover them until they choose to reveal themselves, which is when the party reaches the middle of the bridge. The Abyssal Eyes will position themselves and use their @UUID[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ.Item.lNrBkcszQBheNyP1]{Eye Blast} action to try and push players off the bridge.

They will also avoid moving closer to the bridge itself and try to stay away from melee range attacks.

Void Space

If any party member falls off the sides of the platforms or is pushed during a combat encounter, they fall down and into the glittering void of lights at the bottom of the chamber. They end up in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.Okk4y4H2ASNCP7Ev]{Containment Chamber}.

Stone Bowl

An unlit stone bowl rests on a polished pedestal, its surface etched with intricate, faded patterns. A narrow channel, carved into the stone floor, snakes away into the shadows, and its path can be followed easily by following the lighter stone trim.

Once the party has defeated the Abyssal Eyes in the chamber, they can approach the Light Bowl and investigate. It is too heavy to lift or move in any way.

Investigating the Stone Bowl

Characters can use the following checks to learn more about the stone bowl. Any character with [[/knowledge artifacts]] has @Advantage[2] on all checks. If characters have previously encountered a Light Bowl, they recognize this as the same item.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 15]] check, if characters have solved the puzzle of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.NQYLVd3qv4YvwGuA]{Runekey Altar}, they can tell that that the inscriptions on the bowl are similar to those on the altar found beneath the Sun Star.

  • With a successful [[/check history 15]] check, they can identify one of the ancient markings inscribed on the bowl, which means "light of sun." If they previously identified this marking on the altar, they know this without a check.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 15]] check, they notice a connection between the bowl and the channels carved into the floor.

    This large stone bowl appears to be an empty vessel connected to the deep channels that run along the floor. With a close look into the shadows, you discover that the bowl has an extremely small hole in the bottom center that leads to the channels below.

Filling the Light Bowl

Any character who carries the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} and comes within 5 feet of the Stone Bowl feels a calming glow emanate from it.

The sun you hold within your hands seems to pulse with energy as you approach the bowl, glowing even brighter than it did before and seeming to illuminate the bowl's very center. That glow fills the bowl, then flows down along the channels in the floor, lighting up the room with what almost seems like sunlight.

The energy from the Sun Star fills the light bowl and flows along its corresponding channel on the floor, opening any doors or obstructions. No checks, rituals, or other mechanisms are required to fill an empty bowl.

Interactive Object

The bowl here, and others elsewhere in this dungeon are interactable. The Gamemaster can use the interaction tool to activate them when the appropriate conditions, described above, are met.

Obvious Door

The door here cannot be opened until the party effectively completes the rest of the area. They will need to solve the puzzle in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.0B4Yde6z0sLb0h1b]{Mural of Volcanic Glass} room, which can only be reached once all four light channels have been lit. However, they can study the obvious hidden door in front of them in an attempt to understand how to open it. If anyone walks across the short Light Bridge that appears after they fill the Light Bowl, read the following:

The Light Bridge ends abruptly against a solid stone wall. There are no mechanisms, keyholes, or visible ways to open what is clearly a route into another passageway.

Attempting to study or investigate the wall reveals nothing more.

Containment Chamber.name: Containment Chamber
Containment Chamber.text:
Gamemaster's Note

If characters fall into the starry void at any point during their exploration of the Lightless Halls, they are transported into this room and have the &Reference[Paralyzed] condition for 24 hours due to Void Stasis. This paralysis can be negated via use of the Lesser Restoration or Dispel Magic spells.

The first time that a character is teleported to this room, read or summarize the following:

Darkness. Stars. Fading light. Flailing arms. A sheen of cold across your skin like sweat, but dry and cool as ice. Sensation after sensation passes over your body, and when they end, you are here, in this empty stone room, unable to move.

If characters look around further, or enter from the outside, they see a basic empty room:

This small room seems unremarkable at first glance, empty and devoid of any detail except for the floor, which holds a beautiful carved stone circle of runes that seem to catch the light as you glance at them.

The Inscribed Circle

The symbols of the circle have been carved deeply into the floor and look as if they have been there for eons.

  • With a successful [[/check history 15]] check or [[/knowledge rituals]], characters can identify the symbols as runes, likely used in a magical ritual of some kind.

    • If characters studied the stone bowls or altars within the bastion, they know that the script is similar without a check but cannot decode it.

  • With a successful [[/check 15 arcana]] check, characters know that this is the end point of a teleportation circle. It is meant as an endpoint and cannot be used to send anyone to a location.

The Way Out

There is a stone lever on the inside of the door, which is clearly visible but otherwise unremarkable. Any checks to determine more about it reveal that it is a simple stone lever.

Pulling the lever opens the door to the Containment Chamber and gives any character inside access to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.Ua62jsQGbeCJyBUS]{East Hallways}.

Bastion Antechamber.name: Bastion Antechamber
Bastion Antechamber.text:
The hallway opens up into a vast chamber. To the north is a massive chained door, while in the corners and slightly offset from the walls stand four towering pillars. Each pillar is connected to the channels that run along the floor, which snake their way up to large inert crystals. An ornate, large stone bowl rests at the southern end of the room, seemingly unconnected to any other channels on the floor.

The Four Pillars

Examining the PIllars

If anyone studies or examines the pillars in the room, they learn two things:

  • The top of the pillars holds a large inset crystal that is connected to the light channels on the floor.

  • The pillar is adorned with reliefs of energy, swirling through the twisting Pathways. The carvings seem to depict Giant figures traversing dangerous bubbling lava. The figures hold back boiling, fast-flowing waters while making their way through and across the world below.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check inv 18]] while examining a pillar also discover a hidden compartment in the base containing a single @UUID[Item.pv01rzzDf9aztI6H]{Giants Comfort Stone}.

Activating the LIght Pillars

Each light pillar becomes active once the party has filled the light bowl that connects to it via the appropriate channel in the floor. Once all four pillars are active, the crystals on the pillars activate. The chains on the Northern door retract into the ceiling above. This door can now be opened.

Interactive Object

Additionally, once all four pillars of light are active, the large crystal in the south side of the room may be activated to direct another light beam southward towards @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.0B4Yde6z0sLb0h1b]{Mural of Volcanic Glass}.

South Hallways.name: South Hallways
South Hallways.text:
Gamemaster's Note

This hallway has two states – dark and illuminated. It becomes illuminated once all four light pillars in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.orVcdj9VxumYSiT2]{Bastion Antechamber} have been lit.

The Dark Hallway

The dark corridor stretches beyond the reach of your light source, winding between massive stone block walls that show signs of ancient damage.

If characters have not activated the light bridges in the hallway, they will quickly come to a dead end as the corridor floor stops abruptly ahead of them.

Ahead of you, the corridor comes to an abrupt halt, revealing only a large empty void ahead.

Bridging the Gap

To bridge the gap in the corridor, characters must illuminate the South Hallway. Due to the ancient magic in this place, any attempts to go across the void by other methods, including flying, fail, plunging characters into the void below. They emerge in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.Okk4y4H2ASNCP7Ev]{Containment Chamber}.

The Illuminated Hallway

With light filling the channel in the floor, a soft glow fills the hallway.

A Dark Rock

Anyone with a [[/skill perception 15 passive]] or higher notices in the very corner of this hallway, tucked away and barely noticeable, is a strange, dark rock. Any character can attempt to investigate the rock and make a [[/check inv 19 check]] or a [[/check nat 18 check]] reveals that it is an inert monster called an @UUID[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM]{Abyssal Eel}. Those with [[/knowledge abyss]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

If anyone in the party touches the inert Abyssal Eel, it immediately activates and bites down on the hand or finger of whoever touched it, dealing [[/damage 1d4 piercing]]. The party should then roll initiative and enter into combat.

@Embed[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM]

Abyssal Eel Tactics

The Eel is not supposed to present any real danger to the party, as it is alone and extremely weak. It will likely die quickly, but while alive it will attempt to @UUID[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM.Item.khM6Zq5owrqd9fIo]{Bite} whoever is closest to it.

Void Space

If any party member falls off the sides of the platforms or is pushed during a combat encounter, they fall down and into the glittering void of lights at the bottom of the chamber. They end up in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.Okk4y4H2ASNCP7Ev]{Containment Chamber}.

Mural of Volcanic Glass.name: Mural of Volcanic Glass
Mural of Volcanic Glass.text:
A glittering light bridge stretches across the room to a plinth on the other side, where a beautiful mural made of volcanic glass awaits. Flanking the light bridge are a number of massive statues of Giants, standing as if on guard against intruders. Their features are set in grim and unyielding expressions with downturned mouths and their eyes are fixed upon the bridge itself.

The statues in this room are more than decorative; they guard the mural and require anyone crossing the light bridge to the mural to show proper deference. If characters do not figure out how to proceed correctly, they will trigger a violent response from the guarding statuary.

A Hum of Warning

If characters approach the beginning of the light bridge, the statues begin to hum with magical energy, which can be heard indistinctly by most members of the party. Any character with [[/skill perception 15 passive]] hears the faint humming sound and feels energy against their skin.

As you step toward the light bridge, you can hear a whisper of a hum in the air, everywhere and nowhere, but it tingles with energy against your skin.

A successful [[/skill arcana 16]] check reveals that the hum is a form of arcane energy that resonates from the statues that line the light bridges. Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

As characters move further onto or toward the light bridge, the sound grows in volume, becoming louder and louder. It only subsides if they back away from the bridge or proceed with their hands clasped and heads bowed in deference.

Observing the Statues

The statues here are eternal guards who watch over the room and the path towards the mural ahead. Characters can learn the following by observing them. Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on all checks.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 15]] check, characters notice that the statues have different expressions but the same three things in common: all have their hands clasped and their heads bowed.

    • With 17+ result: Characters know from the statues' positioning that they must clasp their hands and bow their heads to cross the bridge safely.

  • With a successful [[/check insight 15]] check, characters get the sense that the statues are watching and judging to see what anyone approaching the light bridge will do.

Light Blast

If any character attempts to walk across the Light Bridge without bowing their heads and clasping their hands together, read the following:

The eyes of every statue spring to life, blazing with an intense light. Powerful light beams streak out and blast the bridge in front of you.

Any characters on the light bridge takes [[/damage 1d4 radiant]] and must also make a [[/save dex 16]] saving throw, taking [[/damage 2d8 radiant]] on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. All characters on the light bridge are also pushed 10 feet toward the edge of the Light Bridge that is closest to them. This may send them over the edge.

Void Space

If any party member falls off the sides of the platforms or is pushed during a combat encounter, they fall down and into the glittering void of lights at the bottom of the chamber. They end up in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.Okk4y4H2ASNCP7Ev]{Containment Chamber}.

The Volcanic Mural

The panel at the end of this room is a massive mural of interlocking panels of primordial volcanic glass depicting renditions of Giants, the Pathways, and a towering figure even greater than the figures around them. If anyone approaches and begins studying the mural in front of them, read the following:

A huge mural of incredibly detailed figures and pictograms stands before you. The stones of the mural appear to be made of a glittering black volcanic glass that holds no runes or markings, as if it was formed separately from the stonework around you. The mural holds a mix of images — figures performing rituals with their faces illuminated by ceremonial fire, a central towering figure that makes its way through an ethereal landscape, smaller figures being guided through twisting passages of water, fire, and air.

The puzzle in front of the party is a complex mechanical lock that seals the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.3yPEI2VvrOAbxNPZ]{Treasure Room} door in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.111T8HXHnIo7nXjn]{Void Bridge} chamber. The party must piece together several aspects of ancient First Giant lore in order to solve the puzzle.

Studying the Volcanic Mural

Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 15]] check or have [[/check perception passive 17]] can see faint lines in the mural, as if it is arranged from separate pieces, and a keyhole in the center of the mural, below the feet of the center figure.

Characters who study the mural in detail and succeed on a [[/check investigation 17]] check can see that the mural is mounted on a circular rotating mechanism that consists of interlocking panels that can be rearranged in any desired sequence. If they have [[/knowledge machines]] or [[/knowledge subterranea]], they have @Advantage[2] on this check.

ucceed on a [[/check inv 17]] or a [[/check slt 13]] check. If they have [[/knowledge subterranea]], they have @Advantage[2] on this check. If successful, read the following:

The mesmerizing mural is not one image - it is six! The central figure appears set in place, but the other five images appear to have gaps between them that would allow them to be pulled out of their current position and placed in a new order. There are also five large crystals embedded in the mural in a circular pattern around the central panel — one for each of the movable pieces. The crystal in the panel at the bottom right corner of the mural glows ever-so-slightly.

The Mural Panels

To solve the mural puzzle, characters must place the story told by the mural in the correct order. Each piece of the mural can be investigated independently.

The Five Panels

When characters enter the room, the panels are arranged in the order 2-3-4-1-5 and the crystal in the 5th panel is glowing at half brightness. Panels may be moved by switching them with each other. Once all five panels are set:

  • When a crystal glows at half-brightness, it is in the right order, but one or both of the panels next to it are in the incorrect order.

  • When a crystal glows at full brightness, it is in the right order and both panels next to it are also in the correct order.

The notes below will indicate the position that each panel begins in, as well as where it should end up to be in the correct final order and checks that characters can do to learn more about it.

The Glowing Orb

This panel depicts swirling energies and elements, a chaotic blend of fire, water, earth, and air combined in a cosmic dance. In the center, a glowing orb is surrounded by powerful figures that appear to represent the forces of life and the elements.

This panel represents The Creation of the World. It begins in fourth position. Its correct placement is in first position.

Robed Figure In The Mist

Crafted with intricate detail, this panel portrays a solitary cowled figure cloaked in a deep half robe, with massive, elongated arms emerging from swirling mist. Energy radiates from beneath the hood, and they stand with hands open in supplication.

This panel represents the Birth of the Cowled Figure. It begins in first position. Its correct placement is in second position.

Characters can tell without a check that the figure in this panel is the same figure that features in the center of the mural.

Figures of Stone and Earth

This panel features the central cowled figure in the process of creating smaller humanoid figures from the stone and earth around them. Although much smaller, these figures are still colossal in their own right.

This panel represents the Making of the Giants. It begins in second position. Its correct placement is in third position.

Many Passageways

In this panel, the twisting shapes of the Pathways are clearly visible as the cowled figure and its creations craft passageways and tunnels beneath the earth. These pathways have faint energy lines that emanate from them like a lifeforce. Around the edges of the panel are scenes of trade and communication, of cities growing and civilization spreading.

This panel represents the Shaping of the Pathways. It begins in third position. Its correct placement is in fourth position.

A City Grows

This panel portrays a magnificent city in its prime, with grand structures crafted from blocky shapes reminiscent of the structure you are standing in, but its heights defy the laws of physics. Sections of the buildings float in the air, and towers twist and spiral into a sky, all within a massive domed chamber next to a radiating orb of power and energy.

This panel represents the Crafting of the Forgotten City. It begins in the fifth position, which is its correct placement.

A Secret Compartment

With the panels properly aligned and the crystals activated, a secret compartment opens, revealing a key shaped like a winding path. Players must insert this key into the central keyhole in the mural.

As the key is inserted, the chamber begins to rumble, and a deep grinding sound starts to build. The grinding sound intensifies and resonates throughout the halls, drowning out everything else, its sound like the relentless scraping of stone against stone. Small stones and debris fall from above as stone slabs shift, and finally, a deep booming sound rings out from somewhere else within the bastion. When the final echo of the boom ends, the halls are silent once again.

Sealed Chamber.name: Sealed Chamber
Sealed Chamber.text:
Behind the once-sealed door, the sprawling interior chamber is large enough to bring a slight chill in the air. In its center, a large empty platform of stone is connected to each doorway by a shimmering bridge of light that passes over the glittering void space below. The room seems as if it must have some purpose, and there is the scent of something sour in the air, but whatever it is — or was — is impossible to make out from the entrance.

Delayed Attack

The creature Gohema does not reveal itself until the entire party is standing on the central column in the middle of the chamber, at which point it immediately attacks and combat begins.

Work In Progress

The arena in which the Gohema is encountered will eventually be obscured from view until triggered at which point it will become visible along with the boss itself. This is not yet automated and is left to the Gamemaster to narrate in a way that is clear to the players.

Observing the Chamber

Characters who attempt to study the empty chamber before combat begins must succeed on a [[/check inv 18]] check. If they have [[/knowledge abyssals]], they have @Advantage[2] on this check. If successful, they sense abyssal energy in the area, though they do not know the cause.

The chamber here is empty; disconcertingly so, as an aura of Abyssal energy suffuses the area like a shroud. This may have been a place once crawling with monsters, and it has stained the very stones with corruption.

Fighting Gohema

As soon as initiative is rolled, the following actors appear within the scene.

  • 1x @UUID[Actor.Q5iudLrTvVX7AeFF]{Gohema's Head}

  • 1x @UUID[Actor.KGGDusyPn6kV7iT0]{Gohema's Tail}

  • 3x @UUID[Actor.JG5w7JLygXq3siN5]{Gohema's Tendril}

  • 3x @UUID[Actor.V9gGkZh1H06sA0VF]{Gohema's Eye}

These actors can appear randomly at first; their movement and positioning throughout the following encounter are covered under their tactics below. None of the individual appendages can move onto the platform where the party stands or outside the chamber due to their @UUID[Actor.V9gGkZh1H06sA0VF.Item.C7JonU2HEnAikqsa]{Gohema Part} feature.

@Embed[Actor.Q5iudLrTvVX7AeFF]

Gohema's Head Tactics

Gohema's Head remains close to the central column in the chamber, remaining connected to the platform so that it can reach party members with its @UUID[Actor.Q5iudLrTvVX7AeFF.Item.QCznVUiE09rWkHyF]{Bite} and @UUID[Actor.Q5iudLrTvVX7AeFF.Item.nVcaXOAkZh02PWWe]{Slam} actions.

If the head is successfully reduced to 0 HP, the head goes through @UUID[Actor.Q5iudLrTvVX7AeFF.Item.wvz9TVLwT9Tn65cI]{Death Throes} and all other parts of the body are reduced to 0 HP.

@Embed[Actor.KGGDusyPn6kV7iT0]

Gohema's Tail Tactics

Gohema's Tail remains in close proximity to the party and attempts to either hit characters @UUID[Actor.KGGDusyPn6kV7iT0.Item.tU4LnrQNrUHPJs4o]{Ram} action (potentially throwing them off of the platform in the process) or use its @UUID[Actor.KGGDusyPn6kV7iT0.Item.vR1uGmhaWFv6nQDy]{Spiked Slam} action to stun them.

Early on in the combat, the tail will also use its @UUID[Actor.KGGDusyPn6kV7iT0.Item.o716uO3NK7pTyh6h]{Entrench} to make itself difficult to target and enable it to use @UUID[Actor.KGGDusyPn6kV7iT0.Item.fpXFL1FjsGfLCXUW]{Reactionary Slam}.

@Embed[Actor.JG5w7JLygXq3siN5 count=3]

Gohema's Tendril Tactics

Two of Gohema's Tendrils stay in proximity to Gohema's Head at all times, using @UUID[Actor.JG5w7JLygXq3siN5.Item.RdSBejxsVvc2hTEz]{Defensive Shielding} whenever possible to take damage from the party. Any remaining tendrils target characters that are on the edge or have fallen off of the platform, using @UUID[Actor.JG5w7JLygXq3siN5.Item.kAf04t7aI2x7VuCK]{Lash} to attack.

@Embed[Actor.V9gGkZh1H06sA0VF count=3]

Gohema's Eye Tactics

While Gohema's Eyes will initially be visible to the party, they immediately attempt to hide using @UUID[Actor.V9gGkZh1H06sA0VF.Item.OQIo0HlzAyr3ADGL]{Veiled Coward} and move to new locations in the chamber with@UUID[Actor.V9gGkZh1H06sA0VF.Item.eRz0R372tIvYIYo5]{Flesh Fusion}, focusing on places that the party will not expect and will provide them maximum cover.

Flesh Pit

Any characters thrown off of the bridge or platform onto the ground below discover that the bottom of the chamber is made up of flesh. Read or paraphrase the following:

What appeared to be the bottom of the chamber is actually a grotesque expanse of flesh, pulsing and shifting underfoot. Each step sinks slightly into the soft, gelatinous surface, making movement feel sluggish and laborious.

Movement is halved while standing upon the flesh of Gohema at the bottom of the chamber. In addition, every time a character moves across the surface, they must make a [[/check con 15]] check or they are &Reference[Restrained] until the beginning of their next turn.

After the Gohema's head reaches zero hit points, the entire creature is defeated; all of its appendages in the chamber are also reduced to zero hit points, and the encounter ends.

Area Map Complete

Once Gohema has been defeated, the party can now refer back to the quest event @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.mGkNxDXrFEXIyAag]{Lightless Halls} for further details and rewards. The party can either leave this section of the bastion completely or attempt to unlock the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.3yPEI2VvrOAbxNPZ]{Treasure Room} by exploring the remainder of the area.

Searing Steps.name: Searing Steps
Searing Steps.text:
Beyond the two large drops into the void that cut across this chamber, a large stone bowl rests on a simple dais as if it is waiting for you. Facing it, on the last solid piece of ground before the first gap in the floor, the inert channel that runs into this room ends at a raised crystal in front of you.

Work In Progress

This challenge will be partially interactive and automated. These interactive elements are not yet implemented in Early Access. They will be added in a later patch, but until then gameplay is dependent upon the Gamemaster to describe the elements of this hazard and enforce its mechanical effects.

Crossing the Gaps

The party will initially face a simple challenge: jumping, floating, or flying over the 10-foot gaps in this chamber to reach the unlit stone bowl and fill it with light using the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star}. However, as they do so, several things happen simultaneously.

A Flaming Battle

Once a character cross the first gap and step onto the middle platform, four Abyssal Eyes in the room activate and combat begins. Immediately, the twin flamethrower traps on the central platform activate.

Twin Flamethrowers

On each turn, both flamethrowers turn clockwise by one turn and shoot out a burst of flame that measures 10-feet long by 5-feet wide.

  • Any character within range of the flame must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw.

  • If a single character is within range of the flame, they take [[/damage 2d6 fire]] on a failed save and have damage on a success.

  • If multiple characters are within range of a single flame, the character closest to the flame receives the above damage. Any additional characters take [[/damage 1d8 fire]] on a failed save and no damage on a success.

  • If the abyssal eyes are in range of the flamethrowers, they are subject to the same damage (and can be used to block the main brunt of the flame as noted above).

@Embed[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ]

Abyssal Eye Tactics

The four Abyssal Eyes have hidden themselves in the darkest distant corners of the room to wait in ambush. No character can sense or discover them until the party reaches the middle of the platform and they choose to reveal themselves.

During their attack, the Abyssal Eyes will position themselves and use their @UUID[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ.Item.lNrBkcszQBheNyP1]{Eye Blast} action to try and push players off the platforms into the void, push characters into the flamethrower blasts, and avoid melee combat by pushing any attacking melee characters out of range.

@Embed[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A]

Vhismara's Claw Tactics

Both of the claws in this room remain in wait until a character steps onto the platform containing the light bowl at the far end of the room. Once active, they attempt to remain hidden, crawling across the ceiling using @UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A.Item.C4OPhsuEKHXDlTP0]{Spider Climb} until they can jump down, attack, and attempt to grapple the closet character with @UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A.Item.X3J5Woy9xmvuWsxZ]{Clawed Fingers}. If Vhismar's Claw is able to grapple a character, it immediately attempts to use @UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A.Item.kXUe0a2GpMHkfUon]{Pinning Hold}.

Void Space

If any party member falls off the sides of the platforms or is pushed during a combat encounter, they fall down and into the glittering void of lights at the bottom of the chamber. They end up in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.Okk4y4H2ASNCP7Ev]{Containment Chamber}.

Investigating the Stone Bowl

Characters can use the following checks to learn more about the stone bowl. Any character with [[/knowledge artifacts]] has @Advantage[2] on all checks. If characters have previously encountered a Light Bowl, they recognize this as the same item.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 15]] check, if characters have solved the puzzle of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.NQYLVd3qv4YvwGuA]{Runekey Altar}, they can tell that that the inscriptions on the bowl are similar to those on the altar found beneath the Sun Star.

  • With a successful [[/check history 15]] check, they can identify one of the ancient markings inscribed on the bowl, which means "light of sun." If they previously identified this marking on the altar, they know this without a check.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 15]] check, they notice a connection between the bowl and the channels carved into the floor.

    This large stone bowl appears to be an empty vessel connected to the deep channels that run along the floor. With a close look into the shadows, you discover that the bowl has an extremely small hole in the bottom center that leads to the channels below.

Filling the Light Bowl

Any character who carries the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} and comes within 5 feet of the Stone Bowl feels a calming glow emanate from it.

The sun you hold within your hands seems to pulse with energy as you approach the bowl, glowing even brighter than it did before and seeming to illuminate the bowl's very center. That glow fills the bowl, then flows down along the channels in the floor, lighting up the room with what almost seems like sunlight.

The energy from the Sun Star fills the light bowl and flows along its corresponding channel on the floor, opening any doors or obstructions. No checks, rituals, or other mechanisms are required to fill an empty bowl.

Bisected Flamelock.name: Bisected Flamelock
Bisected Flamelock.text:
This vast chamber almost entirely drops away into the void below. A central stone platform sits in the center, with four spokes connecting to alcoves and jutting platforms around the edges of the room. Sitting atop a slightly different colored stone pedestal in the middle of the central platform is an inert stone bowl.

Work In Progress

The final description and rules for this puzzle are not yet completed as they are waiting for automated elements to be implemented so they may be described accurately.

This challenge will be partially interactive and automated. These interactive elements are not yet implemented in Early Access. They will be added in a later patch, but until then gameplay is dependent upon the Gamemaster to describe the elements of this hazard and enforce its mechanical effects.

Void Space

If any party member falls off the sides of the platforms or is pushed during a combat encounter, they fall down and into the glittering void of lights at the bottom of the chamber. They end up in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.Okk4y4H2ASNCP7Ev]{Containment Chamber}.

Filling the Light Bowl

Filling the light bowl in this room is more challenging than in the others, and it requires the party to light all the bowls around the room for the central bowl to remain lit.

If anyone attempts to study the empty light bowl, characters must succeed on a [[/check inv 15]] check. If they have [[/knowledge artifacts]], they have @Advantage[2] on this check. If successful, read the following:

This large stone bowl appears to be an empty vessel connected to the deep channels that run along the floor. After careful study, you discover that the bowl is different from the others and has no hole in the bottom.

Once the party has the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star}, they can use its energy to fill the light bowl here, which then coalesces into the air and creates a beam of light that travels towards the crystal on the platform edge to the north, lighting the channel on the floor.

Light-Locked Door.name: Light-Locked Door
Light-Locked Door.text:
A formidable door stands at the end of the ancient hallway. Towering above you and wrought from two massive slabs of stone, unbelievable strength would be required to open it manually.

Examining the Door

Characters who attempt to open the door using an athletics check automatically fail. They can also learn the following:

  • With a successful [[/check inv 13]] check, characters know that the door cannot be opened by brute force alone.

    The Door here is firmly locked, and any attempt to open it is futile as the massive slabs of stone are not susceptible to brute force.

  • With a successful [[/check arc 13]] check, characters can sense a faint magical aura in the crystals on the door, connected to the channels along the floor. Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on the check.

    Not only is the door completely locked and resistant to any form of brute force attempt to open, but the unlit crystals embedded in its surface emit a faint magical aura from an unknown magical school, connecting to the channels along the floor.

Light Lock

The door here will unlock once both beams of light from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.wwNLCv9TF8Fqohj5]{Stone Bowl} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.111T8HXHnIo7nXjn]{Void Bridge} are activated.

Treasure Room.name: Treasure Room
Treasure Room.text:
The room before you is a glittering, hidden treasure chamber, embossed and detailed with extravagant golden carvings and relics. On either side, in the north and south alcoves, two ornate chests made of stone and hammered gold are positioned between two colossal statues of unknown creatures, roaring with their fanged mouths wide. The chests are far too heavy to move, even with powerful magic, as are the statues, which likely weigh several tons. Scattered around the chamber are several large, heavy gold coins, each weighing a considerable amount on their own.

Northern Golden Chest

Anyone attempting to open the massive Golden and stone chest finds that it is tightly locked, with a large, giant-sized keyhole on the front. The chest can be opened with a successful [[/skill slt 16]] check using Thieves' Tools. Anyone with [[/knowledge machines]] has @Advantage[2] on the check.

Once open, the chest contains:

  • [[/award 80gp]] worth of massive pristine First Giant coins.

  • Five large gemstones, including 2 Amethysts, 1 Topaz, 1 Opal, and 2 Onyx.

  • 2x @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.gTRFQLdVD1gsKtPi]{Potion of Growth}.

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.dsjke4vPPsc9gsxH]{Elemental Gem of Fire}

Southern Golden Chest

Anyone attempting to open the massive Golden and stone chest finds that it is tightly locked, with a large, giant-sized keyhole on the front. The chest can be opened with a successful [[/skill slt 16]] check using Thieves' Tools. Anyone with [[/knowledge machines]] has @Advantage[2] on the check.

Once open, the chest contains:

  • [[/award 1000sp]] worth of massive pristine First Giant coins.

  • Five large gemstones, including 1 Ruby, 1 Topaz, 1 Opal, and 2 Onyx.

  • 2x @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.L887NdWEP5NqHCrQ]{Potion of Greater Healing}.

Golden Coins

There are a number of massive golden coins scattered across the floor in this chamber. Anyone attempting to pick any up discovers that time has not been kind to the unprotected metal, as they crumble into worthless flakes.

Brazier Nook.name: Brazier Nook
Brazier Nook.text:
This large alcove leads to a locked stone door. This door is unadorned and unremarkable — there do not appear to be any crystals upon the surface, and the door is not connected to the channel on the floor. It is flanked on either side by two unlit metal braziers that appear well-polished despite their age.

Ceremonial Fires

Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 14]] check can see runes engraved on each of the braziers. With a successful [[/check history 14]], characters can identify the runes as being associated with fire magic in ancient texts.

Examining the braziers with a successful [[/check arc 14]] reveals that they are receptacles that absorb and channel fire magic, likely opening the doors. Anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] has @Advantage[2] on this check.

The party must light the two braziers at same time using any combination of tools or magic they possess, including lit torches or spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.udsLtG0BugXHR2JQ] or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.EOmsUcFQJTfG2oio]{Fire Bolt}. Once both braziers are lit, read the following:

The runes on the braziers glow brightly and seem to burn with an inner fire, causing the door to click and unlock. With a burst of energy, the fire magic blasts from the braziers, but it does not burn; instead, a warm feeling of healing energy washes over you.

All characters within 10 feet of the braziers gain temporary hit points equal to the character's proficiency bonus, as the warmth of the flames invigorates them.

The Chained Door.name: The Chained Door
The Chained Door.text:
Before you stands a truly massive stone door, made from a single block of stone. Its carved and patterned surface is reinforced with large, heavy chains forged from a dimly glinting dark metal. There is no lock on the chains themselves, which disappear into holes in the ceiling and floor. Their presence suggests that the door is not merely a passage onward but is sealing something within. Behind the chains, the door is adorned with four large crystals embedded deep within its weathered surface that connect to four corresponding channels in the floor.

This utterly colossal stone door is twenty feet across, five feet wide, and nearly fifteen feet tall. As a single slab of stone, it weighs approximately 90 tons. The fact that something like this exists as a door is only possible through mastery of extremely powerful magic.

Examining the Chained Door

Examining the chained door with a successful [[/check inv 14]] check yields the following information:

Behind the chains, a detailed depiction of two giants have been carved into the stone of the door. The giants seem to shift slightly as you study them more closely, moving their massive arms together as if to bar entry. Not only is this door firmly locked, but its size, weight, and scale suggest very few forces in the Ember cosmos could open this with brute force.

Examining the light-locked door with a successful [[/check arc 16]] check yields the following information, with [[/knowledge rituals]] receiving @Advantage[2] on the check.

The unlit crystals embedded in the surface of the door emit a faint magical aura from an unknown magical school, connecting to the channels along the floor. The chains are made of an unknown metal that is crisscrossed with tiny, almost invisible runes. They are emitting intense abjuration magic.

Light Warding

If any characters attempt to strike the door or break the chains physically or magically by any means, read the following:

As the seemingly solid and immobile chains twist and writhe like rope, a flash of intense light blasts forth in a wave around the door.

Any characters within 15 feet of the Chained Door must make a [[/save dex 17]] saving throw, taking [[/damage 2d8 radiant]] on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. They are also pushed 10 feet away from the door and knocked prone.

Light Lock

This door remains locked until all four beams of light which connect to it are simultaneously illuminated. Once all four of the channels on the floor are filled, the chains disappear into the ceiling and the door is unlocked.

Deadly Encounter Beyond

If the party is wounded or low on resources at this point, it would be prudent to either indirectly or directly suggest that they consider resting before continuing further - the battle beyond is designed to challenge a level 4 party with their full resources available.

Stone Altar.name: Stone Altar
Stone Altar.text:
A huge, seemingly empty stone altar sits to one side of the otherwise-empty antechamber, its far exit blocked by a thick stone door. The edges of the altar are embossed with glimmering ancient gold and exquisite patterns and carvings, but its purpose is unclear at first glance.

The party will not immediately have time to study the altar in front of them, once they enter the room, initiative is rolled as the Vhismara's Claw springs down and surprises the party from the ceiling.

@Embed[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A]

Vhismara's Claw Tactics

The claw in this room has been hiding in effective stasis for untold years, clinging to the ceiling using its @UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A.Item.C4OPhsuEKHXDlTP0]{Spider Climb} feature. Once combat starts, it attacks the party and attempts to grapple the weakest or lightest looking character with its@UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A.Item.X3J5Woy9xmvuWsxZ]{Clawed Fingers}. If it succeeds, it attempts to pin and kill them using @UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A.Item.kXUe0a2GpMHkfUon]{Pinning Hold}.

Examining the Altar

Characters who examine the altar see the following:

The stone altar is a beautifully carved centerpiece of the room, yet nothing rests upon its surface. Depicted across its sides are a series of intricate details showcasing giant figures moving throughout the pathways and worshipping under light rays emanating from an orb.

With a successful [[/skill inv 16]], they also learn that the altar likely depicts location from somewhere else in the Pathways, possibly near the Heart of Ember. If they have [[/knowledge subterranea]], they have @Advantage[2] on this check.

While at first glance, the orb and the rays coming from it likely show the Bastion where we currently stand. Showing about the rays coming from the orb feels oddly out of place. This altar may instead be depicting somewhere else in the Pathways entirely, and this may be a scene showing the Heart of Ember itself.

Stone Bowl.name: Stone Bowl
Stone Bowl.text:
An unlit stone bowl rests on a polished pedestal, its surface etched with intricate, faded patterns. A narrow channel, carved into the stone floor, snakes away into the shadows, and its path can be followed easily by following the lighter stone trim.

Investigating the Stone Bowl

Characters can use the following checks to learn more about the stone bowl. Any character with [[/knowledge artifacts]] has @Advantage[2] on all checks. If characters have previously encountered a Light Bowl, they recognize this as the same item.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 15]] check, if characters have solved the puzzle of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle.JournalEntryPage.NQYLVd3qv4YvwGuA]{Runekey Altar}, they can tell that that the inscriptions on the bowl are similar to those on the altar found beneath the Sun Star.

  • With a successful [[/check history 15]] check, they can identify one of the ancient markings inscribed on the bowl, which means "light of sun." If they previously identified this marking on the altar, they know this without a check.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 15]] check, they notice a connection between the bowl and the channels carved into the floor.

    This large stone bowl appears to be an empty vessel connected to the deep channels that run along the floor. With a close look into the shadows, you discover that the bowl has an extremely small hole in the bottom center that leads to the channels below.

Filling the Light Bowl

Any character who carries the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} and comes within 5 feet of the Stone Bowl feels a calming glow emanate from it.

The sun you hold within your hands seems to pulse with energy as you approach the bowl, glowing even brighter than it did before and seeming to illuminate the bowl's very center. That glow fills the bowl, then flows down along the channels in the floor, lighting up the room with what almost seems like sunlight.

The energy from the Sun Star fills the light bowl and flows along its corresponding channel on the floor, opening any doors or obstructions. No checks, rituals, or other mechanisms are required to fill an empty bowl.

Interactive Object

The bowl here, and others elsewhere in this dungeon are interactable. The Gamemaster can use the interaction tool to activate them when the appropriate conditions, described above, are met.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This Side Quest can be undertaken by any party that explores the southern section of the Forest of Stone. This might happen during Chapter 1, but the Events of this Quest can also be experienced later in the game.

Difficulty

"Ooze Control" is designed for a party of Level 1 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 1 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point} upon successful completion of the [[/eventState oozeControlMine]] Event.

The southern @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} in the Forest of Stone are permeated with magnificent @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} that shimmer with prismatic color. This area is home to a small group of mostly Hulg'run miners who are using the abandoned shell of a Shent mining operation as the grounds for a renewed settlement and mining effort named Yakoshta.

The Yakoshtans are assisted in their work by the friendly oozes in the area which they use as helpers and companions. But all that has changed of late, as the oozes have begun attacking the miners without warning. The change in the ooze's behavior is due to an alchemical fluid leaking into the mine from the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost} on the bluffs above.

The party is enlisted by the settlement leader @UUID[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]{Sellen} to rescue miners trapped by the aggressive oozes. Within the mine, they discover clues as to the origin of the contamination but will have to undertake a dangerous trek in order to neutralize it at its source. Opinions differ on how best to resolve this problem, introducing a conflict between local ooze enthusiast, @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]{Tauric}, and the profit-driven supervisor of Yakoshta Mine, @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper}.

The party will be drawn into the midst of this disagreement which will escalate when matters within the local mine grow hazardous and require the party's intervention. The party's choices will help the Yakoshtans determine how to move forward and whether to prioritize ecological preservation or opportunity for profit.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]{Tauric}

  • @UUID[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]{Sellen}

  • @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper}

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]

  • @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ]

  • @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj]

Overview.soverview:
Nestled within the southern reaches of the Forest of Stone is Yakoshta, a small encampment of miners. These prospectors have built a mine and a community in the footprints left behind by the Shent, an ancient culture of giants which dwelt in the region long ago.

Life in the mine is aided by oozes in the vicinity who are friendly and helpful to the miners—individual members of the encampment can even bond with them as if they were pets. Recently, though, the oozes have changed — they are larger, have a slight glow to them, and are aggressive, attacking the miners without warning. If the reason behind the ooze's sudden transformation from helpful pets to dangerous monsters is not discovered quickly, Yakoshta will have to be abandoned.

In "Ooze Control" you will investigate a troubling change in the behavior of the oozes at Yakoshta and seek out the source of this trouble. You will explore the treacherous mines in the depth of the Kaleidoscope Caverns to overcome puzzles and adversaries to understand the source of the trouble which affects the hapless miners.

Good Ooze, Bad Ooze.name: Good Ooze, Bad Ooze
Good Ooze, Bad Ooze.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this combat event, party members travel through one of the Kaleidoscope Caverns, unaware that dangerous oozes lie in wait. Party members can:

  • Survive an attack by aggressive @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ]{Luminous Copper Ooze} and @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj]{Luminous Iron Ooze}.

  • Meet @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]{Tauric}, a young Hulg'run who was also attacked by the oozes.

  • Consider Tauric's proposal to accompany him back to the settlement of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta}.

A Distant Glimmer

Characters can see a glint of metal in the distance, but only faintly. It stands out from the reflection of the Kaleidoscope crystals — brighter and smaller, like a beam of light reflecting off of a metal object just out of sight.

What the party does not know is that both the piles of iron and the heap of gold coins are oozes, using their @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ.Item.KO8oVBIr5ydmPzfv]{False Appearance} @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.falseAppearance0] trait. It is impossible for the party to identify that the glimmering scraps are oozes due to this false appearance.

Investigating the Glimmer

Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 12]][[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check can identify the following:

  • Two piles of iron scraps arranged in neat stacks that reflect light from the kaleidoscope crystals. Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] discern that they are in good condition and could be used for crafting or repairs.

  • A small heap of copper coins. It looks as if someone was gathering copper coins and then either forgot about them or had to vacate the area in a hurry, leaving them behind. Any characters with [[/knowledge trade]] can estimate the pile as being worth approximately 1gp1 gold in value.

Ooze Ambush!

Once a character comes within 20 feet of any of the three oozes, all three reveal themselves and combat begins. Unless the party was reasonably wary of the glimmer or prepared themselves for an attack in some way, they begin combat &Reference[surprise]{Surprised} @Condition[unaware] .

@Embed[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ]

@Embed[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj count=2]

Ooze Tactics

The Luminous Oozes are aggressive and unintelligent. They converge directly upon the party without particular consideration of tactics.

Iron oozes proactively seek out opponents who are wearing or wielding metal. The use their @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.M9zZ2880tT8qONrT] and @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.axNcdP72e20FRJBk] trait to pull enemies closer and, if possible, disarm them. The copper ooze takes advantage of @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ.Item.6mhO90U7AYY3TfCr]{Self-Soothing} to extend the duration of combat if it is threatened.

Both types of oozes have the exceptional ability to @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeMultiply0000] or @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeSubdivide000], but a limited Focus pool with which to perform these actions. Oozes favor use of Subdivide if they are near full Health, and will use Multiply if they become wounded.

Iron oozes proactively seek out opponents who are wearing or wielding metal, using @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj.Item.oozeMagneticDisa] to disarm them of their equipped weaponry.

Copper oozes focus on direct attacks, reacting with their ability to @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ.Item.oozeCorrodeWeapo]{Corrode Weapons} as a natural defensive mechanism against incoming attacks.

The oozes fight to the death, even if their Morale is Broken.

Contaminated Pool

Prolonged exposure to the oozes and their internal contaminants has left the large pool in the center of the cavern dangerously electrified. Any character that steps into or starts their turn within the large pool nearest to where the oozes appeared must make a [[/save dexterity 13]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d8 lightning]] risks harm from the [[/hazard 4 electricity fortitude]]{Electrified Pool}. The pool, while dangerous, is too watered down for its contents to be useful, if collected.

After the Fight

After the party's encounter with the oozes, a small figure emerges from behind one of the kaleidoscope crystals.

A statue-like figure rises, slowly, from behind one of the large purple crystals. He is trembling as he steps out into the cavern's purple light, then rushes towards you, stumbling as he runs and waving his hands frantically back and forth.

@Embed[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]

If the party defeated the hostile oozes:

Oh thank you … thank you so much! I thought Squish and I were absolutely done for! And I suppose without your help, we might still be.

If the party has avoided the ooze fight, Tauric instead attempts to usher the party out of the caves, saying:

Did you see any oozes running about? We just saw some sliding around the cave — better get out of here before they come back!

The Hulg'run quickly introduces himself as @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]{Tauric}, and his @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozeling} companion as Squish. He then asks the party for their help getting home.

@Embed[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v label=Squish]

Tauric's Information

Tauric is happy to talk about any and everything he knows as long as the party is there to keep them safe. Key information that Tauric is ready to share during this conversation:

  • He needs the party to take him to Yakoshta, the settlement outside of the Yakoshta mining operation.

  • His oozeling companion, Squish, is not dangerous. The miners had a friendly relationship with local oozelings like Squish, treating them like pets.

  • A new type of large glowing ooze is attacking everything in sight. These are the oozes that attacked the party.

  • There may be more information about what is happening with the oozes at nearby "Ooze Island."

For detailed responses, see below.

Where are you from?

It's not far. Yakoshta Mine, maybe you've heard of it? It's supposed to be one of the best up-and-coming mining operations in or around the Arctus Plateau. Or at least that's what Sellen says. And since she's in charge, what she says goes.

Why are you here?

Before I ran in here to get away from them, I was trying to figure out what makes these new oozes different over at what I call Ooze Central—it's usually filled with friendly oozelings like Squish. Want to swing by on the way back to Yakoshta? I can show you how oozes are supposed to work, and maybe something there will help explain what's making the oozes so angry.

I know everyone thinks of oozes as these killing machines, but in Yakoshta, oozes are our little buddies — they help us in the mines. When these larger glowing oozes started attacking, I just had to know why. I was checking things out at the old ooze pool nearby when this group attacked and drove me in here.

About these hostile oozes?

I have no idea! They appeared a few weeks ago out of nowhere, driving the regular oozes away and attacking everyone they run into. They're bigger than our normal oozes and glow all weirdly and there's no way to reason with them. I've tried talking to them, singing to them, everything, and it doesn't matter. They just want to fight.

About your ooze?

Squish is one of the only regular oozes left — these new glowing ones are different. They're mean and they're big and they ran off or killed most of the regular oozes. I do my best to protect Squish from harm, and in return, Squish watches over me sort of like a …a watch ooze! With everything going on, you should consider getting a protective ooze pal of your own. You can't be too careful these days!

About Yakoshta?

We've been out here for a couple of years. Sellen was the one who came up with the idea of mining in one of these old abandoned mines carved out by the giants who used to live in the area — the Shent. Sometimes I wonder if they had giant oozes hanging out with them, but I haven't been able to find any evidence of it in the ruins around here.

Recent changes?

Nothing specific that I could put my finger on, but Squish and I wander a lot, so I don't keep up with what goes on at the mine that much. Sellen would know more—she's back at the settlement and I'm sure she'd love to meet you, even if it's just to thank you for keeping me out of trouble.

As Tauric speaks, the ooze changes position, but is always somewhere on his body, whether draped around the neck like a scarf, wrapped around the arm like a long bracelet, or shifting from shape to shape in its shoulder perch.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Tauric recommends that the party head out of the caves, and set camp. In fact, if they head to the old ooze pools, they might be able to gather some answers about what has made the glowing oozes so aggressive along the way. If the party agrees, proceed there.

If the party is in a hurry, or resting wouldn't be appropriate, Tauric still recommends making their way to the ooze pools to investigate. However, the Yakoshta settlement is only a few hours away, and Tauric is heading that way regardless.

  • If the party heads to the ooze pools first, they will encounter the [[/eventState oozeControlPool]] event.

  • If the party heads to Yakoshta directly, they will encounter the [[/eventState oozeControlCamp]] event.

  • If party members choose to go elsewhere to explore the Forest of Stone, Tauric decides to make his own way back — when the party reaches Yakoshta, he is there.
Good Ooze, Bad Ooze.soverview: While crossing through the Kaleidoscope Caverns, the party is attacked by a small number of Luminous Copper and Iron Oozes. After the oozes are dispatched, they meet a Hulg'run, Tauric, who was hiding from the oozes along with his pet oozeling, Squish. Tauric asks the party to escort them back to the small encampment outside of Yakoshta mine and fills the party in on the oozes' recent aggressive behavior, which may force Tauric and his fellow miners to abandon Yakoshta in the near future.
Good Ooze, Bad Ooze.sexposition: As you weave your way through the crystal formations that jut out from the cavern's walls and around the strange glowing pools of liquid on its floor, light glints off of something shiny and metallic in the distance.
Good Ooze, Bad Ooze.ssummary: We made it through a cave filled with strange glowing oozes! According to Tauric, the Hulg'run we met, the nearby mine has been suffering from recent attacks by these oozes, and no one knows why.

Stone Life.name: Stone Life
Stone Life.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, Tauric shows the party a strange stone basin which he calls @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.pf1eWchM2qV0iMtb]{Ooze Island}, where tiny oozelings are known to gather. In this event, the party can:

  • Learn how the Yakoshta miners domesticated oozes in the past in @UUID[.T8Yz3kDaxX3jUo8t#a-chat-with-tauric]{A Chat With Tauric}

  • Locate ancient symbols that provide a clue as to why the ooze gathered here in @UUID[.T8Yz3kDaxX3jUo8t#investigating-the-island]{Investigating the Island}

  • Attempt to befriend an ooze of their own in @UUID[.T8Yz3kDaxX3jUo8t#befriending-an-ooze]{Befriending an Ooze}. If successful, they gain a single @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozeling} as a companion.

A Chat With Tauric

@Embed[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]

Tauric can't contain his enthusiasm at seeing an oozeling, even briefly. As the party arrives to the island, read or paraphrase the following:

Squish, do you see that? It's an ooze like you! They're not all gone!

Tauric gathers Squish in his hands. It swirls around his wrist in response like an elaborate bracelet. Tauric turns to you and explains.

Used to be, if you came to this island, it would be full of oozelings hanging out in that and you could make friends with them if you wanted to. Now that little one we just saw seems to be all that's left and these new angry glowing oozes are lurking around instead. I hate seeing this place so empty, but maybe there's a clue here about what happened.

Tauric is happy to discuss the island and oozes further. He is especially encouraging of party members who might want to befriend an ooze here, as he thinks everyone should have a friend like Squish.

What is this place?

It's where we make friends with the oozelings. Or did, before these new ones started attacking. I don't know why they come to this little island, but it's been happening since before our mining group arrived here. Don't know what I would have done without this place, honestly. I'm not too great at mining, but I am Yakoshta's chief ooze-ologist. Which is why I thought maybe I could figure out what's been going wrong.

What special things can oozes do?

We've been feeding the oozes metal dust for the last year or so- they change based on what you give them. Iron ones get magnetic, like moving toolboxes, copper can heal injuries, silver keeps away rats and spiders with their electricity zaps, and gold can stretch out and do two things at once. Now that I think about it, maybe these new oozes ate something that don't agree with them?

Why would we want to make friends with an ooze?

Everyone should want to be friends with an ooze. Look at how cool they are! But if you're like Jasper and want to get practical about it … a little extra alertness from an oozeling companion goes a long way.

How do we befriend an ooze?

Depends on what you want from it. If you just want a buddy, you can try feeding it some of the heartmoss growing everywhere around here, or entertaining it — Squish and I really bonded over battle poetry.

Anything else we can learn here?

Usually if you're walking through here, you're surrounded by oozes, but with the basin empty, you might be able to see something that would normally be hidden away. I have always wondered why the oozes come here in the first place, but I haven't been able to figure it out.

Investigating the Island

Tauric has been trying to figure out if there's anything to learn about the change in the oozes from the island, but has come up short so far. He encourages the party to check it out for themselves.

The Abandoned Basin

Characters with [[/check perception 14 passive]] or who succeed on a [[/check perception 12]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notice cuts in the stone at the bottom of the empty stone basin. They can discover the following about the marks using the associated checks:

  • [[/check nature 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] The marks are not natural — they were intentionally carved into the rock.

  • [[/check history 12]] [[/skillCheck society 12]] The way that the marks are cut into the stone is typical of the carving techniques of the Shent culture that once lived in the Arctus Plateau. The Shent are believed to have used runes as part of their magic system.

  • [[/check investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] The marks form a pattern that appears to be symbols of some kind, though it is not fully clear what those symbols are or do. One faintly resembles an ooze, while another could be the shape of a large hand

  • [[/check arcana 12]] [[/skillCheck arcana 12]] The markings are definitely of a rune that has some magical ability. With a result of 15 or greater critical success, or use of a spell to identify magic, the runes can be identified — they attract oozes to the area and provide a calming environment for them.

Runic Symbols

If party members point the markings out to Tauric, he realizes that he has seen them before — the mine supervisor, Jasper, has been making a study of them for reasons that he has not yet revealed. Before leaving the area, Tauric copies the symbols down as part of his study of oozes.

If anyone touches one of the symbols, it emits a low hum and an ooze appears, making its way towards the center of the basin. If touched more than once, the symbol hums again but no further ooze appears.

Befriending an Ooze

Tauric suggests that the ooze that ran away when the party came to the island could be found and befriended - it's just scared and likely hiding somewhere nearby. He isn't used to having to track oozes down but notes that they like being sung to and will sometimes come out in search of their favorite food, heartmoss.

Finding an Oozeling

The party can attempt to track the ooze or lure it out of hiding. Both are made easier if characters spot and follow the trail it left, which is different than the normal dust and dirt in the area.

With a successful [[/check survival 12]] or [[/check perception 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] or [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check, characters can see the difference between where the ooze went and the regular dirt and grass around it and determine which area of the island it has disappeared to.

Once an oozeling has been located, the characters may attempt to befriend it using one of the following methods:

Tame the Oozeling

Physically grabbing the oozeling requires deft hands and special quickness. To grasp the oozeling a character must succeed on a successful [[/check sleightofhand 13]] [[/skillCheck stealth 13]] check or it flees to a different location. Once it has been grabbed, it can be soothed with a successful [[/check animalHandling 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check, otherwise it squirms away and flees.

Sing to the Oozeling

The party may attempt to lure out an ooze in hiding by succeeding on a [[/check performance 13]] [[/skillCheck performance 13]] check, which results in the oozeling crawling out from its hiding spot and wriggling forward curiously, as if dancing to a song. If the performance is maintained, the oozeling will crawl into the hands of whichever character is singing.

Feed the Oozeling

If the party sprinkles heartmoss on the path, the oozeling will crawl out from its hiding spot to investigate the delicious mossy treat. If the ooze's feast is interrupted, it will attempt to flee unless otherwise corralled. After eating, the ooze contentedly affixes itself to the nearest rock with a powerful natural adhesive. The ooze becomes complacent for a time, but prying it free from the rock can only be achieved with a successful [[/check athletics 13]] [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check.

Use the Ancient Runes

If the party intuits to use the magic of the ancient Shent runes carved into the stone basin, as described in @UUID[.T8Yz3kDaxX3jUo8t#investigating-the-island]{Investigating the Island}, the ooze voluntarily emerges from its hiding place and crawls into the hands of whoever activated the runes.

If the party successfully locates and befriends an ooze, they gain an @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Oozeling} as a companion. Tauric warns that oozes like to be near familiar places, so it may not stick with the party if they get too far from the Forest of Stone, even after bonding.

@Embed[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]

The party may only befriend a single oozeling in this way. If their previously befriended oozeling perishes or disappears, they may return to this location after 24 hours have passed and repeat the process to acquire another.

The first time an oozeling is befriended, whichever character in the party played the most significant role in gaining its trust advances one of their attunements as described below:

Primordis Attunement: Tame the Oozeling

A character who befriended an oozeling by tracking and taming it advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 oozeControlPoolTame]] at the conclusion of the event.

Heart Attunement: Sing to the Oozeling

A character who befriended an oozeling by singing to it advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 oozeControlPoolSing]] at the conclusion of the event.

Mayis Attunement: Feed the Oozeling

A character who befriended an oozeling by luring it with heartmoss advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 oozeControlPoolLure]] at the conclusion of the event.

Signara Attunement: Use the Ancient Runes

A character who befriended an oozeling by activating the ancient Shent runes advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 oozeControlPoolRune]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once Ooze Island has been thoroughly explored, Tauric suggests that the group head back to Yakoshta lest they run into any more dangerous glowing oozes.

Next Steps

Tauric asks party to accompany him the rest of the way back to @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta}, leading to the events of [[/eventState oozeControlCamp]] .
Stone Life.soverview: At a large basin that was once the site of an ooze pool, Tauric shares some information about how oozes are created and gives the party the opportunity to take a frightened ooze in the area and transform it into a friend. While the basin only allows for one ooze to be befriended in this way, it also reveals some markings that may help in better understanding the creatures.
Stone Life.sexposition: You spot a large circular basin at the center of the island that appears to be marked with ancient runic symbols along the inside rim, just below the water line. As you survey the basin, a tiny translucent ooze stirs within the water and swiftly makes its way towards a narrow channel in the rock nearby. Before you know it, the tiny oozeling slithers to the other side of the island and vanishes into the undergrowth, leaving nothing but the rustling of heartmoss in its wake.
Stone Life.ssummary: We accompanied Tauric to a now-empty island that was once filled with oozes to learn more about how the Yakoshta miners turn local oozes into allies.

A Miner Matter.name: A Miner Matter
A Miner Matter.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, party members reach settlement of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta}, returning Tauric to his home. They can:

  • Learn more about the recent ooze attacks on the settlement and the attached @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.XytBBChWK9D5ccOD]{Yakoshta Mine}.

  • Agree to go into the mine and rescue miners trapped by the oozes.

Meeting Sellen

A middle-aged Hul'grun woman, @UUID[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]{Sellen}, strides towards the party from between the stone buildings of the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta} encampment, quickly covering the ground between them. As she approaches, read or paraphrase the following:

The hul’grun strides towards you, hand extended, but her body is in a fighter’s stance, ready to either greet you or brawl with you, depending on what the situation calls for.

Welcome friend! At least, I hope you're a friend. Right now, Yakoshta doesn't need any more enemies.

The party's introduction to Sellen changes depending on their encounter with Tauric.

If the party has Tauric with them:

Tauric and Sellen greet each other warmly. Tauric introduces her to the party as his sister Sellen, leader of this encampment, and asks her if she will give the party a silver ingot as a reward for getting him safely home. Sellen is not happy that he has been wandering off again but is grateful to the party for returning him safely to Yakoshta. She gives the party a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.tradegoods.Item.9t5X9HG9ou6YMSdJ]{silver ingot} silver ingot worth [[/award 5sp]].

If Tauric made his way back to Yakoshta on his own:

The party receives no reward, but he is happy to see the party, saying:

You made it here! Squish and I barely got back to Yakoshta in one piece — I was worried you were done for!

He asks the party what they have been doing since they left him and introduces them to his sister Sellen as capable adventurers.

If the party has not encountered Tauric:

Sellen introduces herself directly and asks if the party has run into her brother Tauric, who has wandered off while she was dealing with her current crisis.

Talking with Sellen

@Embed[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]

Sellen is very willing to discuss her current situation. As she talks, other members of Yakoshta encampment begin walking up, listening intently and occasionally chiming in in agreement. Culturally, the group is all Arcturian, and most are of Hulg'run ancestry, though there are a few Thornlings and Kivahr in the group as well.

Sellen's Perspective

Key information that Sellen may share during this conversation:

  • Until recently, the Yakoshta miners have been working steadily and productively, with the help of friendly oozes who seem to be native to the area. Recently, though, the oozes have changed and begun attacking.

  • Before these attacks, the miners had a friendly relationship with the oozes and used them in the mines as helpers, but these oozes are different. In fact, the oozes used to be the mine's secret weapon for efficient extraction of materials, but this new type of ooze they've been dealing with is big and angry, and impossible to work with.

  • Oozes began attacking the miners a few weeks ago, shortly after an earthquake. The ooze attacks have been increasing in intensity since. It hasn't been anything they couldn't handle to this point, and Sellen is confident that Yakoshta has things under control with a few new safety protocols in place. There's some rising concern that that might not be the case for much longer.

  • So far nobody has died, or even gotten that badly hurt, but the risk is certainly there if things keep escalating. The mine foreman, Jasper, has been warning that something needs to be done.

For detailed responses, see below.

About the mine?

We've only been mining here a few years, though I know it's hard to believe that with everything we've built here. Didn't hurt that we started with some good structure in the mine thanks to the Shent who used to live in this area, even if they were a few times our size. It's been pretty smooth sailing too, at least until recently.

About the miners?

We're a pretty close group. I know there are a few among us who think we could be moving faster and digging deeper, but we need to be careful. If we'd been digging willy-nilly when that earthquake hit a few weeks back, someone might have been hit by the rock collapses in the mine — as it is, we still need to build a few things back.

Recent issues?

We've always had oozes around this area. Friendly ones. But after that earthquake a few weeks ago, something changed. Like the ground moving shook the sense out of them. At first it was one or two oozes attacking, and we could mostly keep them in line in the mine or chase them out of the encampment, but it seems like their numbers are growing just like they are. If this keeps up, we may have to shut the mine down. I've put new safety protocols in place, but I can't just put my people at risk and Jasper has folks riled up about the danger.

Before the earthquake?

The oozes were different. Smaller. Friendly. And if we fed them the right bits of metal, useful. Some could have tools stuck to them to make things easier to carry. Some kept the rats out of the mine. But if this is what happens after, it 100% wasn't worth it.

Who runs the mine?
