Jasper is my right hand in the mines - keeps the operation running smoothly so I can focus on attracting traders, getting new workers out here, and all of that. We don't always agree on the right way forward — I'm a little more cautious and he's a bit of a dreamer — but nobody works harder than him in those mines. I've been meaning to make him take some rest but I'd have an easier time convincing the rocks to mine themselves. He's convinced he knows a way out of all this trouble.

Trouble in the Mines

At some point, a crisis occurs in the mines, and people come running to Sellen for help. The party will inevitably get caught up in this, and Sellen will look to the party first for help, as they are far better equipped to deal with the dangerous oozes in the mines than her own workers.

If the party opts to long rest Rest in Yakoshta, consider using this crisis to mark the end of their rest, the commotion causing them to be roused from bed to see what is going on.

From a distance, you can hear loud overlapping voices ringing from the back of the encampment. You can't make out every word but some are clear — rescue, danger, help.

As you go to investigate the source of the rising commotion, you find a handful of miners gathering around Sellen, all yelling and arguing with each other and trying to get Sellen's attention while she struggles to get a clear answer out of anyone.

As the voices begin to rise in volume, Sellen grabs a hammer from her belt and begins to strike the stone near her. The sound of her iron hitting rocks rings out over the din, and drives the crowd to silence. Her voice rings out loudly over the crowd:

Calm down, calm down! Yelling isn't going to fix anything. We need to know what's going on, then we can figure out what to do.

She points her hammer at one of the workers, who stands up a little straighter as he answers:

It's those slimes again, Sellen. This time they've got a couple of groups trapped. We need to get all the miners out of there!

Sellen nods.

Don't worry, we will. And I think these folks here may be just the ones to help us.

A Miner Task

Sellen is is willing to pay 40@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.tradegoods.Item.9t5X9HG9ou6YMSdJ]{silver ingots} silver ingots (worth [[/award 200sp]]) if the party clears the mine of oozes and rescues the trapped miners. If they helped Tauric, he vouches for them and she raises the amount to 45 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.tradegoods.Item.9t5X9HG9ou6YMSdJ]{silver ingots} silver ingots (worth [[/award 225sp]]).

What can we do?

You look like you're packing a little more equipment and experience than most of my miners — do you think you could go in and help get them out? I'm happy to pay you for your trouble. I can offer 40 silver ingots.

If the party helped Tauric, he immediately asks for them to receive a little more:

After everything they've done for me, Sellen, is that enough?

Sellen shrugs, then nods.

45 ingots then. Just help my miners!

Where are the miners?

I don't think they're that far in - according to Feldin here, the miners can hear shouting if they stand at the entrance, but they're yelling a lot about Jasper, so he may be hurt or further inside.

Any advice?

Hopefully you don't have to go too far in to rescue the miners trapped in there, but if you do, safest way to avoid falling a few hundred feet is to stick to the carts. They'll always get you where you need to go…eventually.

What about Jasper?

He may be able to help. He's sure there's some way to fix or stop the oozes and been working on it non-stop. If you can help him figure out what it is, maybe we could put this whole issue behind us and focus on the work that keeps Yakoshta going.

Concluding the Event

If the party agrees to help, Sellen escorts them to the mouth of Yakoshta mine and thanks them for their help. She offers them a miner's kit to help them on their way, which includes a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.qMzHmlmha8qMDnEF], @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.X5knPtrQAT8GePJ4]{Miner's Pick}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.ytlsBjYsZ7OBSEBs]@UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lantern000000000], @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingElixir000], and a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.pickaxe000000000].

Tauric also bids farewell to the party — he doesn't want to put Squish in any danger — but he will be waiting in Yakoshta to see what they've found.

Next Steps

The party heads towards @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.XytBBChWK9D5ccOD]{Yakoshta Mine} to save the besieged miners in the subsequent event, [[/eventState oozeControlMine]].
A Miner Matter.soverview: After arriving to the Yakoshta encampment and meeting its leader, Sellen, the place falls into chaos — oozes have trapped some of the miners within the mine, including her second in command Jasper. Sellen offers the party a reward if they can free the group.
A Miner Matter.sexposition:
All around you the settlement bustles as you make your way in. You spy groups of miners cleaning off the grime of their latest shift, while others drink and eat. Looking over all of it is a Hulg'run woman with a clipboard, calling out shift changes and warning those heading into the mine to remain alert in case of trouble.

The moment she spots you approaching, she wraps up her instructions, telling the miners to stay in groups and take breaks as they need to, then heads briskly in your direction.
A Miner Matter.ssummary: Shortly after meeting the leader of the Yakosha mining encampment, Sellen, word came from the mine that angry oozes have trapped some of the miners, including her second-in-command, Jasper. Sellen asked us to help them get free.

Saving Jasper.name: Saving Jasper
Saving Jasper.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration and combat event takes place in @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.QzTFDTll3HhEdQru]{Yakoshta Mine} where the surviving miners struggle to fend off dangerous metallic oozes. Along the way the party can:

  • Rescue miners under attack from oozes.

  • Explore the mine and discover clues to the contaminant affecting the oozes.

  • Defeat a @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07]{Giant Luminous Ooze} and rescue the supervisor, @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper}.

Area Walkthrough

The party begins in the @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.yewfxh4f49fcF4gJ]{Loading Zone} and is immediately engaged in combat against attacking oozes.

In addition to the details provided in the area walkthrough, there are three key moments during exploration of the mine where event-specific gameplay should occur:

  1. After the party has defeated the oozes near the mine's entrance in @UUID[.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2#battle-at-the-loading-dock]{Battle at the Loading Dock}.

  2. If the party talks to Jasper from across the bridge in @UUID[.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2#a-conversation-with-jasper]{A Conversation with Jasper}.

  3. After the party has defeated the giant ooze at the heart of the mine in @UUID[.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2#after-rescuing-jasper]{After Rescuing Jasper}.

Battle at the Loading Dock

As the party proceeds forward, they immediately encounter combat in the @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.yewfxh4f49fcF4gJ]{Loading Zone}. Three miners are trapped in a corner of the room as oozes advance on them, armed only with a few @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flasks} from a planned clearing of a blockage further into the mine.

While the three rescued miners will fill the party in on what they know, they're most concerned that their supervisor @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper} be rescued as quickly as possible and urge the party to go further into the mine to help him. The miners are:

Shel (Neutral Good, Arcturian Hulg'run, they/them)

A short Hulg'run with arms that appear to be a bit longer than necessary and has a tiger-eye coloring to their skin, begins counting up the ingots and taking inventory, marking up a slightly chipped tablet recovered from the rubble.

Trianda (Neutral Good, Arcturian Thornling, they/them)

A Thornling who resembles a green bramble bush with red leaves as ornamentation. They are compact in size and concern themselves mostly with repairing the broken crates and inspecting the wagons, wielding a hammer and nails with ease.

Gravin (Neutral Good, Arcturian Hulg'run, they/them)

A slightly taller Hulg'run with a rounded stomach, who appears as if they are carved out of green and brown marble, begins putting things into neat piles.

No Survivors

If one or more miners has died during combat, the remaining miner(s) will still answer questions as indicated below but are gathering the belongings of the fallen. If all three have died, Jasper yells out from his position across the bridge to try to find out what happened in @UUID[.s52TmvVMwOFyVlV2#a-conversation-with-jasper]{A Conversation with Jasper}.

With Trianda under a wagon making repairs and Shel attempting to focus on their count, Gravin takes the role of speaking to the party and is happy to answer any questions they have. If asked, the miners will also provide the players with any @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flasks} that they still have.

The Trouble In Yakoshta

The key information that the miners have to share is:

  • The ooze attacks on the mine are getting worse every day.

  • The mine supervisor, Jasper, is trapped on the other side of the now broken bridge near a giant ooze. He refuses to leave the Excavation Pit area until it is dealt with.

  • To get deeper into the mine, characters can travel by foot past Jasper’s office (which holds supplies) or use the working mining cart to cross the center mining cavern.

  • There is another exit to this section of the mine, but it has caved in. The miners were planning to clear it with Blast Flasks when the oozes attacked.

What happened here?

Oozes happened. They attacked. Again. These oozes came from deeper in the mine, where Jasper is. I know he's the supervisor and he thinks he can figure out how to keep these oozes under control, but if he's wrong, he's gonna need help. Immediately.

What were you throwing?

Blast Flasks. Like tiny explosions in a bottle. Been using them to try to clear the places in the mine where the rock has collapsed. Grabbed a few from the supply cache when we saw the oozes coming — there might be some left if you need an extra weapon.

Where is Jasper?

From what we can hear, Jasper is just across that bridge there — it hasn't been crossable since the earthquake a few weeks back, but it usually leads right to a ledge overlooking the current Excavation Pit. He was down there working when the oozes attacked — probably crawled up to the ledge to stay safe and do some more ooze research.

Jasper's research?

Since the oozes started attacking, Jasper's been convinced he can figure out why. He keeps saying that once he's finished whatever he's always scrawling down in his office, the mine will never be the same. Whatever that means. Almost as ooze-crazed as Tauric, if you ask me.

Sign on the wall?

Lets you know where you are, but we use it for the mining carts more than anything — those same signs are at all the track junction switches so you know where the cart's headed once you hit one. Jasper's got maps of the whole mine stashed in his office, just up this tunnel — gives them out whenever a new miner joins. The switches might a bit turned around from all the attacks though.

Directions further in?

Usually the blue tracks up here lead right to the Pit that Jasper's hiding above, but between the earthquake and the oozes, there are a bunch of broken sections. It might be more solid further on in the mine, near the junction — you can get there on foot. Looks like the red tracks below are still working, though, so you can either take those through the mine or walk through the tunnels past Jasper's office.

About the mining carts?

They're pretty simple. Couple of symbols inside each cart — one that sets it to moving at a nice steady pace and one that brings it to a stop. Jasper and Sellen were the brains behind that. They based the symbols on some giant old carvings.

Exploring The Mine

Encounters in Yakoshta

As the party explores the mine, they can take several different paths, with potential encounters that include:

  • Discovering what is happening to the oozes through the records in @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.gUZhrUKdF5Ypmjsb]{Jasper's Office}, an encounter with friendly oozes in the @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.OVPUBZvPbZpksFnS]{Ooze Pool}, and an encounter with two dangerous oozes in the @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.xm50UssrvERyHUig]{Glowing Ore Pit}

  • Talking to a pair of exhausted miners recovering from an ooze attack in the @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.ZVl3AnWEXMhsm3UA]{Old Ore Pit}

  • Finding a way to use explosives to blow up the Giant Ooze at the center of the mine (as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.oYxMXI3OD4YPUfxz]{Ooze Go Boom!})

A Conversation with Jasper

The Trapped Supervisor

During the conversation with the miners, any party member with [[/check perception passive 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] can hear the sound of panicked movement from behind the miners, in the next cavern. They can choose to investigate by crossing the @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.0LXzxGaXrMFhFREp#entrance-bridge]{Entrance Bridge} to the south.

Jasper, the mine supervisor, is trapped behind rubble on the other side of the damaged bridge and is calling out for help!

@Embed[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7 inline]

If the party succeeds in hearing Jasper's cries, or otherwise attempts to cross the bridge, read or paraphrase the following:

Hello? Can you hear me? I'll assume you can hear me and I'll hope you're turning back around.

The voice from the other side of the rockfall is gravelly and hushed, but can be clearly heard despite the pile of rocks in front of you.

My name is Jasper and normally I run this mine for Sellen with maximum efficiency and minimum trouble. But of course, as you can see, we are in a situation that is far from normal. One where I could use the help of adventurers like you.

Jasper speaks in hushed tones and tries to keep it brief in order to avoid catching the attention of the Giant Ooze located in the Excavation Pit below him.

Are you okay?

I'm fine. Hope everyone else is too — I could hear the commotion from here. Luckily, the larger ooze specimen hasn't spotted me, which is giving me the opportunity to make some new observations, but I don't want to be here forever and I don't know how long I can stay hidden.

How can we help?

If you make your way through the mine, you can reach the Excavation Pit and engage the thing. Just be ready — it's consuming everything that comes in here. That's what's made it so big — gorging on ore cart after ore cart.

How do we get to you?

You can walk part of the way through the tunnels, and the mining tracks should connect the rest. Some parts might be damaged by the ooze, but from what I heard of that battle, you'll find a way.

Can we get you from here?

I don't think trying to get through this rockfall is a good idea. I thought about having the miners on the other side of the bridge try to get their Blast Flasks over here to clear the rubble, but the rocks are unsteady on this side and I think an explosion might bury me. It would certainly bring the ooze up this way and across the bridge, doing even more damage to the mine. Better to contain it where it is.

What caused this?

I'm not absolutely certain but I do have some theories. Once I'm away from this ooze, I'm happy to share my ideas…and an opportunity.

After Rescuing Jasper

Once the giant ooze in the Excavation Pit has been dispatched, read or paraphrase the following:

A Hulg'run of medium height stands on the ledge above the pit, smiling. He tips his head in your direction and gives you a small salute. He has a gray color similar to some of the rocks scattered between the glowing crystals of the cave, but his skin is studded with jewels that set him apart from the other Hulg'run of the settlement.

If you spoke to Jasper from the bridge:

Great work! Sellen did well, sending you down here. And now that that thing is gone, see what it has left behind? With a few safety precautions, ooze farming can make Yakoshta rich. If you can help me get Sellen and that ooze loving brother of hers to understand my vision.

Otherwise, if this is your first time encountering Jasper:

Great work. Sellen must have sent you this way, right? The two of us may not agree on everything, but this I truly appreciate. And look at what the creature has left behind — refined metal that can easily be sold in trade. With a few safety precautions, ooze farming could be the future of Yakoshta — I can't be the only one who sees it.

If the party is cunning enough to utilize the resources available in the mine to save Jasper, each of the characters may be affected by the following Primordis Attunement reinforcement:

Primordis Attunement: Blast the Ooze

If the party used the @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU]{Crate of Blast Flasks} to defeat the Giant Luminous Ooze with a deadly explosion, each character in the party advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 oozeControlMineBlast]] at the conclusion of the event.

Alternately, if the party doesn't use the mine's resources and saves Jasper using their own inherent talents, each of the characters may be affected by the following Ragen Attunement reinforcement:

Ragen Attunement: Direct Assault

If the party defeated the Giant Luminous Ooze using their own combat abilities, each character in the party advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 oozeControlMineDirect]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Jasper is eager to discuss the future of the oozes with you, but equally as eager to get out of the mine. He scrambles down into the main @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK.JournalEntryPage.0kFeSW2kHgr0muXo]{Excavation Pit} and heads back to Yakoshta, asking the party to meet him at "Day's End," the settlement's normal gathering point.

The party can leave the mine and head back to the settlement when they are ready to depart.

Next Steps

Upon returning to @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta}, the party will debrief with Sellen and reconnect with Jasper in the [[/eventState oozeControlUpdate]] event.
Saving Jasper.soverview: After battling the oozes advancing on a group of cornered miners near the entrance of the mine, the party learns that the mine supervisor, Jasper, is trapped deeper inside, unable to make his way back to the entrance from the ledge where he's hiding from an even larger ooze. As they make their way towards the threat, the party can learn more about what caused the oozes to begin attacking in the first place and possibly figure out a way to even the playing field in their fight against the creatures.
Saving Jasper.sexposition:
As you enter the mine proper, moving from the rough ground of the Kaleidoscope Caverns into a stone passageway, alarmed voices echo in the distance:

Someone! Please! Help us!
Saving Jasper.ssummary: We made our way through Yakoshta Mine to free the miners trapped by the ooze attack and discovered that whatever has been changing the oozes appears to be coming from above.

Ooze Foes.name: Ooze Foes
Ooze Foes.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party can attempt to find out what happened to the Yakoshta settlement, which has been destroyed. While they find no one alive, the remnants of what is left suggest a community overrun by dangerous unchecked oozes.

Event Prerequisites

This event may occur 60 days after [[/eventState oozeControlUpdate]] if the party does not otherwise intervene. This event may also occur if the party provides Jasper with the requested alchemical agent in [[/eventState oozeControlJasper1]] by choosing [[/eventState oozeControlJasper1 gave]].

The Abandoned Settlement

Characters can search through the rubble of Yakoshta looking for any clues as to what happened here. Broken furniture, dishes, and other implements are scattered across the ground.

A Metallic Mess

Bits of metallic substance can be found throughout Yakoshta on the ground and upon the sides of buildings:

  • A successful [[/check 13 nature]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] check confirms that it is identical to the bits of metal left behind by the metallic oozes the party has previously faced in combat.

  • Characters can track the path of the substance with a successful [[/check 15 survival]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check and determine that the oozes came out from the mine and through the center of town.

  • There is not enough metal in any of the piles to sell or gather.

There is no sign of survivors, but further inspecting the town for clues can turn up more evidence of what happened here:

Squished

The party may make a [[/check perception 12]] [[/skillCheck medicine 12]] check to identify clues towards what happened here:

  • Result of 12+: You spot a drawing of an ooze that looks very similar to Squish, crumbled up on the ground and a dusty gem, in the middle of the road. Any character who has spent time with Jasper can identify it as one of the ones embedded in his skin.

  • Result of 17+: You identify smashed glass vials that appear to belong to a set. With a successful [[/check medicine 14]] check you identify their spilled contents as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.ytlsBjYsZ7OBSEBs]{Potion of Healing}. Nothing salvageable remains.

  • Success: You spot a drawing of an ooze that looks very similar to Squish, crumbled up on the ground and a dusty gem, in the middle of the road. Any character who has spent time with Jasper can identify it as one of the ones embedded in his skin.

  • Critical Success: You identify smashed glass vials that appear to belong to a set. With a successful [[/skillCheck science 14]] check you identify their spilled contents as a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingTonic0000]. Nothing salvageable remains.

With a successful [[/check investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check, among a spread of other papers, a note can be found which reads:

They say the oozes are under control, that we don't need to leave this place, but I'm not sure. Sometimes I think I —

The note ends abruptly, with the final line trailing off of the page.

The Overrun Mine

An Abundance of Oozes

If the party is determined or foolish enough to enter @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.XytBBChWK9D5ccOD]{Yakoshta Mine} they find it entirely overrun with oozes, specifically:

  • @UUID[Actor.mziAGiva2J2ZTaAQ]{Luminous Copper Ooze}

  • @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj]{Luminous Iron Ooze}

  • @UUID[Actor.Jhymp0ntXyx78Gx3]{Luminous Silver Ooze}

  • @UUID[Actor.TprbfwcD8fp17XWE]{Luminous Gold Ooze}

  • @UUID[Actor.gxxM2B5tZiFFiW07]{Giant Luminous Ooze}

It is left to the Gamemaster to determine the number and location of these oozes. No sign of survivors exists within, nor are there any further clues about what might have happened.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

There are no further steps in this quest - Yakoshta is lost and can no longer be visited as anything more than a memorial to the past.
Ooze Foes.soverview: The party returns to Yakoshta only to find it in ruins. The settlement is abandoned and has been mostly destroyed by oozes that now rampage through the area. A preliminary investigation can turn up some evidence of what exactly happened, but the area is mostly destroyed and there is no sign of any survivors.
Ooze Foes.sexposition:
Something has happened to Yakoshta. As you approach the wall meant to protect the settlement from the creatures of the Forest of Stone, you pass a trail of items that must have been lost or discarded in some kind of frantic escape - a single shoe here, scattered notebook pages there, a pickaxe with a broken handle.

On the other side of the wall, next to the shattered dinner plates and broken swords and half-empty packs, chunks of rock lie spread between the buildings, some eerily similar to the hands and arms you once saw raised here in celebration. Between them, here and there, are bits of metal that resemble what you found inside of the glowing oozes you fought in the mine.
Ooze Foes.ssummary: We revisited Yakoshta and found it in shambles. It seems likely that the oozes overwhelmed the settlement and it is unclear if any of the miners we met made it out alive.

Ooze Friends.name: Ooze Friends
Ooze Friends.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, the party can see what's been happening in Yakoshta since they left. Tauric is thrilled to show off the ways that the oozes and miners are working together, Sellen presents the party with a gift in honor of the mine's new prosperity, and the party learns that Jasper has gone off in search of his fortune elsewhere.

Event Prerequisites

This event occurs in Yakoshta at least 30 days after [[/eventState oozeControlJasper1]] if the party sided with Tauric by choosing [[/eventState oozeControlJasper1 withheld]]. This event cannot occur if [[/eventState oozeControlAbattoir]] has already transpired.

Reunion with Tauric

@Embed[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]

Tauric's yell of greeting brings attention from across Yakoshta, with miners shouting huzzahs and cheering the party's return. Both he and Sellen are thrilled to see the party again and show them what has become of Yakoshta since the group helped the settlement, with Tauric focused on how things are going with the ooze and Sellen on improvements to the mine. Jasper, though, is nowhere to be found.

Tauric's Ooze Updates

Tauric is now spending more time in the Yakoshta settlement than wandering the Forest of Stone with @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN.Item.Plo1AYVyoOLb4I6C]{Squish} @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN.Item.eehWLP7PnRUq58VH]{Squish}, as the two of them are helping to attract oozes to the area.

What's new?

Yakoshta is better than ever! You could say things are totally oozetacular! It's such a good thing you came along, things could have been so much worse for me and Squish. We're working hard to make the oozes part of our operation here, and making new friends along the way!

Where's Jasper?

He left not long after you did. I tried to hash things out with him, but I just don't think we're ever going to see eye-to-eye on things. I'm not sure where he went but Sellen probably knows.

Checking in on Sellen

@Embed[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]

Sellen's Reward

Sellen will give the party [[/award 50gp]] [[/award 5gp]] as a bonus thank you gift for clearing the mine and cleaning up the alchemical leak. The mine has been thriving since the party left, and she believes that she has them to thank for its prosperity.

What's new?

The attacks by the oozes made us realize how useful they could be as allies. With Tauric's help, the oozes have become a more closely integrated aspect of our mining program. They are learning to help us transport ore and explore crevices that we were previously unable to mine. Oh … also they are excellent at keeping the mine clear of pesky crevvets!

Where's Jasper?

Ah… well. Jasper was really frustrated by not getting his hands on that alchemical fluid. He became obsessed with finding new opportunities for research. Jasper left Yakoshta some time ago to seek out some other sources of it. He's still hatching some scheme to somehow turn it into a fortune. We haven't heard from him since.

I know Jasper caused us a lot of trouble — but I do care about him. If you happen to see him, please make sure he's okay?

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

There are no further steps in this quest - Yakoshta is saved and will provide a welcome refuge or trading ally for the party should they ever choose to visit again.
Ooze Friends.soverview: If the party returns to Yakoshta after enough time has passed, having cleaned the alchemical leak and refused to give Jasper any of the alchemical agent, the mine is full of friendly oozes and thriving. Jasper has gone off to seek his fortune elsewhere, but Sellen is thrilled to thank the group in the person and give them an additional reward.
Ooze Friends.sexposition:
Yakoshta seems more full of workers than it was on your last visit. Workers and oozes. In the space between the clustered buildings, miners walk next to iron oozes holding metal toolboxes, green and blue oozes that remind you of Squish sit on cliff edges, and Tauric sits in the middle of the settlement with Squish resting on his shoulder. As soon as he spots you, he springs up from his position on the ground and rushes towards you for a hug, yelling as he does:

They're back! The heroes of Yakoshta are back!
Ooze Friends.ssummary: We revisted Yakoshta and found it thriving, with the miners and oozes living together in harmony, though Jasper has decided to leave and pursue his passions elsewhere.

Flying Predator.name: Flying Predator
Flying Predator.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, party members see a flying predator get unexpectedly and violently ill. They can:

  • Attempt to identify the flying predator as a @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]{Suarrok Juvenile}

  • Examine the gelatinous goo regurgitated by the predator

  • Potentially discover that this goo contains bits of ooze and an unknown substance.

A Distressed Predator

The creature has left behind two silvery-gray gelatinous puddles - each about a foot in diameter - as well as a few scattered bits of goo. The puddles are in fact the remains of a @UUID[Actor.Jhymp0ntXyx78Gx3]{Silver Luminous Ooze} and @UUID[Actor.CgyBkgjUKZaN83xj]{Iron Luminous Ooze}, made indigestible after being contaminated by a toxic leak in nearby Yakoshta mine. The remains have mixed together with the creature's caustic digestive fluid, turning them into a gray gelatinous goo.

About the Creature

A successful [[/check nature 12]][[/skillCheck wilderness 14 passive]] or check [[/knowledge monsters]] recognizes that this creature is likely a @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5], a flying predator that has been spotted in this region in the past.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: You recognize that this creature was an adolescent and that Suarrok can grow to be huge in size when fully grown. Battle against even a juvenile Suarrok could be deadly, but facing a fully grown adult would likely be disastrous.

Sickening Goo

The puddles are in the direct path of the party, but are only about an inch deep and can easily be avoided. Characters may wish to take a closer look at the goo to figure out what it is made of. The possible results of investigation are described below, but doing so could prove hazardous.

Caustic Slime

The digestive fluid within the puddles of goo is acidic to the touch. If any member of the party touches the gray slime directly they must make a [[/save dexterity 13]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d8 acid]] damage risk taking damage from [[/hazard 4 reflex acid health]]{Caustic Slime}.

The Regurgitated Substance

Characters with [[/check perception 14 passive format=long]] or who succeed on a [[/check perception 12]] checksucceeding on [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] can notice that there are three different substances mixed together in the puddle of goo.

Investigation of the substance with a successful [[/check medicine 14]][[/skillCheck medicine 14 passive]] check can understand that it is something that the creature ate and has reacted badly to, rather than evidence of some other sickness.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success - You identify that the natural substance that the creature ate looks like the partially digested remains of an ooze. It was recently eaten, suggesting its source must have been within a few miles of your current location.

A character with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or with a successful [[/check arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14 passive]] check correctly deduces that the acrid nature of this substance is due to some toxic substance that was ingested alongside the organic material.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success - The alchemical substance is the source of the acrid smell and any damage done by the puddles. It is dangerous to the touch and likely the reason that the creature threw up.

Collecting Samples

If party members attempt to touch or collect the substance, they face the hazard described above. The substance can be carried in any standard vial (resulting in @UUID[Item.jnqAVPfmdEzxuLaA]{Vial of Luminous Goo}).

Concluding the Event

The cave system that Agraband mentioned to the party is located to the south of the party's current location. A small group of frontier miners live there who could perhaps help clear the blockade obstructing the caravan's progress.

Next Steps

The party should continue moving south, looking for either a path around the rockfall that is blocking the caravan or someone who could help them to clear it.
Flying Predator.soverview: As the party moves south, they come across a terrifying flying monster that lands in front of them, begins retching violently, and throws up onto the ground. The beast screeches in anger, then flies off towards the north, leaving behind small puddles of slime. If the party investigates, they can determine that these puddles are the remains of at least two oozes.
Flying Predator.sexposition:
As you make your way through the broad and lush canyon to the south, a sudden breeze comes from above and the light around you dims for a moment. With a thud, a large winged creature lands its pale gray body in your path, breathing heavily as it staggers towards you and taking heavy steps with its large razor-sharp claws. The creature's singular eye at the center of its angled forehead regards you momentarily with sinister intention.

The beast rears back its head and coughs - once, twice, three times - ending each cough with a violent shake of its head and gnashing of its teeth, before retching something out of its stomach and regurgitating it onto the ground. The creature sniffs at the mess, then bares its teeth, growls, and screeches in a piercing cry, launching itself into the sky and heading north.
Flying Predator.ssummary: A large flying beast landed in front of us in the middle of the road - the creature threw up an odd glowing substance, then flew off again.

Alchemical Decisions.name: Alchemical Decisions
Alchemical Decisions.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, the party must let the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta} miners know about their decision following their encounters in the spypost. The characters can:

  • Inform @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]{Tauric} and @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper} whether they cleaned up the @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0] contaminating the mine.

  • Decide whether to preserve any for Jasper's experimental use.

  • Decide whether to inform Tauric about the neutralizing @UUID[Item.QwzYLBnZ1PjLFEuI]{Alchemical Silver}.

Event Prerequisites

This event may only occur after the party has completed [[/eventState signalIntentTower]] in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberSignalInten] quest.

Feuding Hulg'run

The two hulg'run greet you and quickly broach the subject of your excursion.

@Embed[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]

@Embed[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]

Jasper looks you with an eager grin:

Well … it looks like you managed to get plenty done without us. Did you find the source of the contamination?

Tauric interjects with obvious concern:

We were worried about you, but I'm also worried about the oozes. What's going to become of them? Can they be healed?

The two stop talking over each other for just long enough to make clear that they want to hear your account of what has happened.

Continuing Contaminant

If the party did not neutralize the contaminant by dispensing the alchemical silver, both Jasper and Tauric are dismayed to hear this news.

Common Ground

Jasper and Tauric do not agree on much, but both believe that the party should have cleaned up the alchemical fluid.

  • While Jasper is happy that the continued leak may give him access to the alchemical fluid, he is concerned that letting it flow naturally down to the mine will turn too many oozes into dangerous creatures before he has figured out a way to restrain them.

  • Tauric is upset both because this will hurt Sellen's dreams for the mine and because he believes that the luminous oozes are being corrupted from their natural friendly state by the contamination.

Both Jasper and Tauric tell the party that they believe Yakoshta will not survive long if the contamination continues.

Jasper looks concerned to hear the news:

I know you may have felt that leaving the leak as is was doing me a favor, but I won't be able to start my ooze farming if I'm constantly being terrorized by oozes I can't yet control. While I appreciate you not getting rid of any chance of progress the way that Tauric wanted, I wish you'd chosen differently.

A dismayed pallor has overtaken Tauric's granite face:

I don't understand. If you're here - weren't you able to find a way to help us? I saw how good you were in a fight back when we met, and everyone in Yakoshta is talking about how brave you were in the mine. I just knew you'd be able to save oozes like Squish from being contaminated and turned into one of those horrible creatures. What happened?

Jasper nodes in agreement with Tauric — for once — and proclaims:

I'll be honest with you. If the oozes continue to attack, I fear we'll have to leave Yakoshta before I discover anything useful that can help save the mine.

Tauric averts his eyes with a look of resignation and disappointment:

I'll tell Sellen that it doesn't look like things are going to change for us. I know she'll be disappointed. As for Squish and I, we go where she goes, but I don't know that we'll ever find another place like this one.

Cleansed Contaminant

If the party cleaned up the contaminant, Jasper and Tauric are glad to hear of this positive development.

Both Tauric and Jasper hold large coin bags that appear to have some weight to them - your reward for clearing the contamination from the mine, no doubt.

Jasper exclaims as you approach:

We figured you'd be coming down soon, I was attempting to collect some more of the substance leaking into the mine when it turned to water in my hands!

Tauric interjects:

Yeah, before you could use it to create your horrible ooze mining factory … so just in time.

Jasper scoffs and looks at you plaintively:

That's not up to you, Tauric, and you know that. I only hope that these brave adventurers have decided to do the right thing.

Tauric, staring at Jasper, resolutely confirms:

So do I, Jasper. So do I.

Jasper and Tauric are each holding half of the party's reward of [[/award 500gp]] [[/award 50gp]] which Sellen asked them to deliver as a thank you for cleaning up the contaminant.

As for what happens next, Sellen has heard both Jasper and Tauric's arguments about what to do now, but is focused on making up for lost time in the mine and killing any remaining corrupted oozes in the area. As the ones who handled the threat, it's up to the party to decide what happens now.

Jasper Makes His Case

Jasper's Argument

Jasper believes that the alchemical fluid is the future. If it could be used to change the oozes, it could be used for so many other things. He believes that the oozes could be a way to discover new forms of science and discovery, and that their sacrifice would be worthwhile "for science." He is willing to offer the party a cut on any future discoveries.

If it is mentioned to him, Jasper claims that he is also interested in the @UUID[Item.QwzYLBnZ1PjLFEuI]{Alchemical Silver}, but characters who succeed on a [[/check insight 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15 passive]] check know that he is likely to ignore it because he doesn't see a way for it to make him immediate profit.

Why do you want the Alchemical Fluid?

I know that Tauric thinks I am hard-hearted, but we use animals and plants around us every day to benefit ourselves. With the alchemical substance in hand and the leak taken care of, we could make progress not only in ooze mining, but in other ways - we must look to the future, not become sentimental over the things of the past.

What can you offer?

I promise that I will use Yakoshta Mine as a place to study this alchemical compound and what it could do and be. Will that mean using the oozes? Yes. But anything that I discover in the process, I promise that you will benefit from. Personally and materially.

Sweeten the deal?

What if I promise to only experiment on some of the oozes. Would that help?

With a successful [[/check insight 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] check, the party can tell that he thinks he would only experiment on some of the oozes, but he wouldn't be too broken up if he couldn't keep his promise.

Tauric Makes His Case

Tauric's Argument

Tauric believes that working with the oozes is not only the best way forward for the mine, but the safest and the kindest. Why would the party condemn a creature like Squish to a life of anger and pain? He has nothing to offer the party immediately, but believes that he can find a way to learn things from the Oozes about Ember and promises to share anything he discovers.

Tauric is intrigued by the idea that the @UUID[Item.QwzYLBnZ1PjLFEuI]{Alchemical Silver}, if mentioned, could potentially save the oozes, but is somewhat reluctant to use it. Characters who succeed on a [[/check insight 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15 passive]] check can tell that he would rather avoid all alchemical compounds and feels guilty that his part in discovering how oozes change when exposed to metals has now put them in danger.

Why do you want the Alchemical Fluid destroyed?

When I met you, I knew you were helpers. You helped me. You helped Yakoshta. Now I need you to help the oozes. Maybe that alchemical stuff you found could help someone someday but we know that it is hurting the oozes now, and I know that Jasper will use it to cause little oozes like Squish pain and suffering. Will you let that happen?

What can you offer?

I think that the oozes know more about Ember than any of us might, and if I find a way to communicate with them, I'll share it with you. But more than that, you'll be on the side of life. Isn't that where you want to be?

Sweeten the deal?

Tell Squish! Tell him what you are doing to his face! If you can do that, nothing I say will matter.

Siding with Jasper

It's up to the party to decide what to do with the @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0]. They can give it to Jasper, as the overseer wishes, so that he can conduct profitable experiments into the future of ooze mining.

[[/outcome gave]]

As you hand the vials of orange fluid to Jasper, he smiles, broadly but awkwardly, like his face isn't quite used to the expression.

You won't regret this, my discoveries have the potential to change all of Ember.

Tauric adds:

And a high chance of getting us all killed, starting with all the innocent oozes you're sacrificing for your idea of science.

As he turns to follow Jasper, Tauric slowly and sadly shakes his head, clutching his ooze tightly against his chest. As the two walk away you hear Tauric mutter:

I know. I thought they were different too, Squish…

If the party sides with Jasper, they'll each be affected by the following Luxarum Attunement reinforcement:

Luxarum Attunement: Side with Jasper

If the party gives the @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0]{Aedir Construct Fluid} to Jasper, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 oozeControlJasper1Jasper]] at the conclusion of the event.

Siding with Tauric

The party can withhold the fluid from Jasper and respect Tauric's wishes to protect the oozes. They can also, if they decided to collect some, give Tauric some of the @UUID[Item.QwzYLBnZ1PjLFEuI]{Alchemical Silver}, which can help against any alchemical spills in the future, and may be able to change the more dangerous oozes friendly again, though there is no way to tell at this time.

[[/outcome withheld]]

As Jasper realizes that you have not brought him any of the alchemical agent to use in his studies, his frown deepens and he shakes his head sharply.

Sentimentality over progress. Every time.

Tauric, on the other hand, is thrilled. He somehow manages to clap, tip his head, and yelp in glee all at the same time, then holds his hands out. Squish makes its way down his arm and into the palm of its hand, where it reshapes itself into a very rough but recognizable image of your party, posed as heroes.

You're heroes, and Squish and I will make sure you're remembered that way!

With a final bow of the head, Tauric turns and heads back towards Yakoshta. Jasper grunts and follows, still shaking his head from side to side and muttering about the future.

If the party sides with Tauric, they'll each be affected by the following Heart Attunement reinforcement:

Heart Attunement: Side with Tauric

If the party withheld the @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0]{Aedir Construct Fluid} from Jasper, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 oozeControlJasper1Tauric]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has made their decision, there is nothing more to be done for now except to depart Yakoshta once ready.

Next Steps

While the party's choice has no immediate effect other than the reactions of Tauric and Jasper, they may encounter the consequences of their actions in downstream events.

  • If the party destroyed the Alchemical Fluid, when returning to Yakoshta some time later they will encounter the [[/eventState oozeControlFriends]] event.

  • If the party gave the Alchemical Fluid to Jasper, when returning to Yakoshta some time later they will encounter the [[/eventState oozeControlAbattoir]] event.
Alchemical Decisions.soverview: After the party has discovered the source of contamination in the Aedir Signalpost, they return to Yakoshta and confer with Jasper and Tauric who each advocate for different visions for the future of Yakoshta. There is no way to appease them both, and the party must decide what path to support.
Alchemical Decisions.sexposition:
Following your expedition into the ancient Aedir Signalpost, you trudge back into the small town of Yakoshta. There are some miners milling about, but the town feels subdued. Shortly after you arrive, two familiar faces appear as they emerge from behind a nearby building. Striding silently side by side, Tauric and Jasper both appear determined as they walk towards you. The match each other step for step and talk animatedly as they move in your direction. You overhear the tail end of their conversation.

… but Jasper, we can't!

Jasper, the mine overseer, looks non-deterred by Tauric's plaintive objection and replies.

I'm going to ask them, I know they will see reason and do what is best for Yakoshta!

The two hulg'run approach looking at you expectantly.
Alchemical Decisions.ssummary: We parted ways with the Yakoshta miners after a final meeting with Jasper and Tauric to let them know what we decided to do about the alchemical agent that has been leaking into the mine.

A Miner Update.name: A Miner Update
A Miner Update.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event occurs just after the party has just exited the mine, having successfully cleared it of oozes. They can:

  • Report back to Sellen on what was found in the mine in @UUID[.Cj0tXDbslrRH2vhl#updating-sellen]{Updating Sellen}

  • Learn about Jasper's ideas for ooze farming in @UUID[.Cj0tXDbslrRH2vhl#jaspers-plan]{Jasper's Plan}

  • Hear Tauric's disagreement with this approach in @UUID[.Cj0tXDbslrRH2vhl#taurics-objections]{Tauric's Objections}

During these conversations, the party learns that the source of the contaminant must be in the hills of the Forest of Stone directly above the mine, but that the way up is blocked due to the recent earthquake.

Updating Sellen

@Embed[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]

Sellen is thrilled that the party has saved the miners and defeated any oozes in the cavern, immediately offering them the promised reward of silver ingots ([[/award 200gp]] [[/award 200sp]] if the party came to Yakoshta alone, [[/award 225gp]] [[/award 225sp]]worth if they accompanied Tauric), but she still fears that the mine and settlement may be in danger.

Sellen's Worries

Sellen is concerned that the party's actions helped in the short-term, but the mine is still in danger as long as the contaminant is not stopped at its source. Given the information Jasper has shared with her, Sellen is sure that the contamination is coming from the hills above the mine, but she doesn't know how to get there.

She can share any of following:

  • Jasper told her about the substance coming into the mine (in the Glowing Ore Pit) that appears to be the reason that the oozes have turned aggressive. If the substance isn't contained, the ooze attacks are likely to start again and threaten the mine.

  • Jasper believes he has a way to contain the dangerous oozes within the mine, but Sellen doesn't trust it. Jasper has always had big plans, and they don't always pan out.

  • Sellen is a little worried about the morale of Yakoshta — between Jasper's ambitions and the attacks, she's worried that her miners may leave in search of work elsewhere.

With a successful [[/check insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check, the party can confirm that Sellen is primarily concerned about the safety of Yakoshta and is giving them all the information she currently has. She trusts the party's expertise and opinion.

Clearing the Caravan

If the party asks Sellen for help with the plight of blocked the @UUID[Actor.emberStrayhearth]{Strayhearth Caravan}, she is reluctantly willing to provide the heroes with a @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU]{Crate of Blast Flasks} suitable for clearing away sections of collapsed rock in exchange for the party's pledge to seek out and resolve the true source of the contamination after the caravan makes it safely to Helkas. The party can assure Sellen of their commitment to that cause in one of the following ways:

  • With success on a [[/skill persuasion 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] check, the party may sincerely pledge to honor this agreement.

  • With success on a [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check, the party can convincingly lie or equivocate about their intentions.

  • With success on a [[/skill intimidation 16]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 16]] check, the party can remind Sellen about the extent of disaster that would have occurred without their intervention, convincing her to provide the Blast Flasks without any firm commitment in return.

What's bothering Sellen

From what Jasper's told me, there's something leaking into the mine that seems to be causing the oozes to attack. What's to stop it from turning more oozes into these dangerous things? We need to stop it at its source or Yakoshta is doomed.

The threat to Yakoshta

We barely got out of the mine alive with your help — I don't want my miners dodging ooze attacks with no support. And even if we did find a way to contain them or defend ourselves better, the mine really needs a big win that lasts, or some of the miners will head somewhere else for work. Especially with everything Jasper's been saying.

Jasper's Plan

Jasper's always been impatient, but giving him this supervisor position has made it worse. I thought that inner fire would help him oversee the mine, but he's always coming up with some big scheme to make us all rich and it isn't helpful. If everyone's dreaming big, it's hard for them to be satisfied with the work in front of us.

Source of the Contaminant

Jasper knows more about where exactly the contaminant is coming from, but I'm pretty sure it'll be in the hills above us in the Forest of Stone. I'm happy to offer another reward if you'll go up there and get rid of whatever is causing the leak.

Helping the Strayhearth Caravan?

Well … I supposed you stuck your neck out to help us in the moment of our need. You say the caravan is trapped behind collapsed rubble that blocks the road?

I could be convinced to send you off with a crate of Blast Flasks if you promise me that after you make it to Helkas, you'll try and get to the bottom of where this contamination is coming from. If you can solve this situation for us long-term, it would mean a lot to Yakoshta and to me.

Sellen rubs her temples and looks as if she's having second thoughts, but she meets your eyes and asks:

Do I have your word?

Jasper's Plan

As the party speaks with Sellen, Jasper and Tauric approach, deep in an argument.

Hushed but angry voices cut through the huzzahs of the crowd as Tauric and Jasper approach. Tauric holds Squish tightly in his hands and loudly whispers:

@Embed[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]

@Embed[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]

As they grow closer, Tauric exclaims heatedly:

I can't believe you would even suggest this in front of Squish. Cover your ears, buddy.

Jasper shakes his head and picks up his pace, gesturing in Sellen's general direction as he does.

It's not up to you or Squish to make policy. You have to let Sellen decide.

Jasper approaches the group to talk. He wants the party to find the source of the contaminant leaking into the mine and bring it to him so that he can stockpile and study it. This will allow him to start something he calls ooze mining.

Jasper's Ooze Mining Proposition

Jasper explains the following:

  • He believes that he can attract oozes to the mine using the rune developed by the Shent.

  • If the miners give these oozes both metal and contaminant, they will turn into the dangerous luminous oozes, but this can be done in a pit designed to keep the oozes contained and the miners safe.

  • When the miners need metal, they can "process" one of the luminous oozes and collect what it leaves behind — pure metal.

  • Tauric may be friends with Squish, but the oozes have shown that they are willing and able to turn on the miners — this is the time for pragmatism, not sentiment.

With a successful [[/check insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check, characters can tell that Jasper has a secondary, self-interested motivation for this idea.

  • Result of 19+: You sense that Jasper is intensely focused on the profitability of the mine — for reasons that may go beyond simple greed. He seems to have an urgent need for the money, but is trying hard to hide that urgency behind talk about the viability of the town as a whole.

  • Discovery of @UUID[Item.sA6BUDpNnyssQ7nK]{Jasper's Diary}: You know that Jasper needs the mine to become more profitable so that he can get a greater share of the profits to pay off urgent debts.

Jasper is sure that the substance leaking into the mine will be found in the cliffs of the Forest of Stone. He believes there is a safe path up to them, but doesn't know where.

Ooze mining?

Did you see the metal left behind by that ooze creature? The leak that made it larger and more dangerous also seems to have multiplied the amount of metal found in its body. We've been using oozes for a while in the mine, feeding them small bits of metal dust to make them more useful to us. But the amount we can scavenge after they've been stopped from attacking? That's truly impressive.

What is your plan?

All we have to do is create metal oozes, use whatever is leaking down here to make them transform in a place we can control them, and we have a metal-producing machine. Instead of mining the ore, we mine the oozes. If you can stop the leak but bring me more of whatever that substance is, I can get started on the safety precautions here — proper storage for the substance, a containment system for the transformed oozes, and whatever else would be necessary to keep the workers of this mine safe.

Effect on the oozes?

Tauric's ooze may look cute, but the transformed oozes were quick to attack us. Even if we only kill in self-defense while attempting to mine them, I'm sure we'll have plenty of metal at our fingertips. To be completely honest, I'm not sure if we should trust them for more than that, no matter what Tauric and 'Squish' say about it. I'm sure you understand.

Getting oozes?

Were there oozes by that Shent symbol I put up in one of the empty caves? That confirms it! I've been fairly sure that the symbol attracts them, but I was attacked before I could be positive. If it does work, ooze mining will be even better. We take them from that area, give them the metal from oozes we've already processed, and the ooze mine becomes a self-sustaining system.

Why do this?

We aren't supposed to be here at Yakoshta forever. From everything Sellen said when she brought us here, this mine is meant to be a way to build capital, create larger mines, maybe even compete with Trading House Cevher in Ordain. But none of that happens if we aren't making enough profit to survive.

What's in it for you?

I won't lie — I've had my eye on another piece of adornment in Helkas, once I get the funds together. But I'm not the only one. Some of us would love a little more luxurious city living and a little less camping out in the middle of a forest. Even Hulg'run can get sick of being surrounded by stone.

Source of contaminant?

With where the leak is coming from, the source must be up in the hills above us — I think the earthquake jarred something loose in all those piles of rock. Tauric might know more — he loves wandering around the Forest of Stone with that ooze of his.

Tauric's Objections

The more that Jasper speaks, the more upset Tauric becomes, but he attempts to keep himself under control as he speaks, offering to help the party find the contaminant if they agree to clean it up and keep it away from Jasper.

Tauric's Plea

Tauric deeply opposes ooze mining, and will share the following:

  • Jasper's idea for ooze mining is unethical — it tricks the oozes into coming closer to be friends, forces a transformation on them, and then kills them for the ore they produce.

  • The right thing for the party to do is to find the leak, stop it from coming into the mine, and destroy any contaminant left.

  • He may know a way up to the section of the Forest of Stone that the contaminant is likely coming from, but he will only tell the party if they promise not to give it to the Jasper, ending the ooze mining plan.

With a successful [[/check insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check, characters can tell that Tauric feels as if he and Squish are personally under attack.

  • Result of 19+: You sense some guilt. Tauric doesn't contribute much to the mine as he enjoys hanging out with Squish and wonders if his lack of effort has brought the mine to a place where Sellen might entertain the idea of Jasper's plan.

Convincing Tauric to Help

Tauric agrees with Jasper and Sellen about the origin of the leak, and he's sure he knows where it is.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check persuasion 13]] [[/skillCheck persuasion 13]] or [[/check intimidation 15]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 15]] check is able to convince Tauric to help (by either convincing Tauric they won't hand the contaminant over to Jasper, or by threatening to let Yakoshta fall to the ooze invasion by moving on).

Once adequately convinced, Tauric shares that the location can be found near a small lake, which he offers to mark for the party. He notes that there's a large pile of rocks blocking it the path, which will have to be cleared if they want to move forward.

Why not ooze mining?

Think of Squish here, minding his own business with the other oozes, when he's lured into a trap, force fed some kind of poison, and then killed so his insides can be sold. I don't care how much more money the mine can make that way — it's just plain wrong.

What about the town?

It'd be wrong to do this to the oozes regardless of what that would mean for our town, but I really don't think our survival hinges on poisoning the creatures of Yakoshta. In fact, who knows what further havoc that could wreak on the local ecosystem, and what danger that might put us in?

Anyway, if my time with Squish has taught me anything, it's that the oozes can be our friends and allies. We can still mine this area the same way people mine anywhere else on the Arctus Plateau — Jasper's so-called plan to "save the town" is really just greed.

Source of contaminant?

Squish and I walk around a lot while everyone else is deep in the mine, so we've seen a thing or two.

There is a path up to the bluffs high above Yakoshta that you can find. The trailhead is a couple miles south of Helkas. It's a treacherous climb, but the views up there are spectacular. I've not ever seen anything up there that seems like it could cause this, though.

Concluding the Event

With the immediate threat to Yakoshta resolved — at least for now — the party can continue on their journey. They should keep in mind that the long-term fate of the settlement likely depends on finding a more permanent solution to the contamination which is pushing the local oozes into uncontrolled aggression.

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a Milestone Point, potentially advancing them in level. Refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Player's Guide: Milestone Progression} for details on how character advancement works in Ember.

Subsequent Quests

The immediate gameplay of this quest is now concluded, but the story of Yakoshta continues in the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberSignalInten] Quest, in which the party can discover the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost} and the source of the contamination affecting the mine.

Next Steps

If the party resolves the contamination in [[/eventState signalIntentTower]] then it is possible to return to Yakoshta and make a choice that determines the lasting fate of the town in the subsequent event [[/eventState oozeControlJasper1]].

If the party does not ever deal with that contamination, at least 2 months from now the terrible events of [[/eventState oozeControlAbattoir]] will befall the people of Yakoshta, resulting in the destruction of the settlement.
A Miner Update.soverview: The relieved miners of Yakoshta are concerned with getting to the source of the contamination that has transformed the oozes, which must be in the cliffs of the Forest of Stone above the mine. While they agree on its probable location, all three have different motives. Tauric wants to destroy the substance and protect the oozes. Jasper wants to collect it to use the oozes as mining sources. Sellen wants the leak stopped so that her people can stay safe.
A Miner Update.sexposition:
A mood of celebration is in the air in Yakoshta as word spreads that the oozes have, at least for the moment, been defeated, and the main square is filled with overlapping cheers and song. In the midst of all the excitement, Sellen greets you with a strong handshake and a smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes. She leans in and says:

Something tells me our troubles are not yet over.
A Miner Update.ssummary:
The Yakoshta miners don't agree on what should be done with the contaminant leaking into the mine, but with their help, we know where to go next in order to search for its source.

Jasper wishes to use the leaking material to transform oozes into metal-absorbing minions, greatly increasing the efficiency of the mine. Tauric opposes this plan, advocating instead for the contamination to be cleansed, protecting the oozes. The settlement leader, Sellen wishes to ensure the safety of the mine for those who work there.

Wayward Sampler.name: Wayward Sampler
Wayward Sampler.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This event only happens if [[/eventState oozeControlIntro]] did not occur. In this social event the party can:

  • Meet @UUID[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]{Tauric} and learn about recent troubles in @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.XytBBChWK9D5ccOD]{Yakoshta Mine} and the surrounding region.

  • Learn about the local ooze ecology and how they have been recently changing.

  • Choose to follow Tauric back to the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta} settlement.

Talking with Tauric

@Embed[Actor.QazTcy7eZuSYcDmN]

The Hulg'run excitedly introduces himself and his pet oozeling, @UUID[Actor.LUptsqBgGJVWcg9v]{Squish}, then asks the party for their help getting home. He's seen enemies in the area and is worried about safe passage. Tauric is happy to talk about any and everything he knows as long as the party is there to keep him (and, as importantly, Sqiuish) safe. He often includes Squish in the conversation as though the two speak a common language.

As Tauric speaks, the ooze changes position, but is always somewhere on his body, whether draped around the neck like a scarf, wrapped around the arm like a long bracelet, or shifting from shape to shape in its shoulder perch.

Talking with Tauric

Tauric introduces himself explaining:

I'm from Yakoshta, home of the famous Yakoshta Mine - one of the best up-and-coming mining operations in or around the Arctus Plateau. Or at least that's what Sellen says. And since she's in charge, what she says goes.

  • Characters with [[/skill insight 13 passive]] or [[/skill history 13 passive]] [[/skillCheck society 15 passive]] or [[/skillCheck deception 15 passive]] realize that Yakoshta and its eponymous mine are — in fact — not famous.

  • If asked, Tauric explains that @UUID[Actor.0w10EA6SDwRS3VK8]{Sellen} is his older sister and the leader of the Yakoshta settlement and mining operation.

Tauric requests the the party escort him to Yakoshta. If they do, Tauric will ensure the party is given a modest reward. If asked what he's doing wandering around outside of town, he'll explain.

I'm really more of a wanderer than a miner. I think that exploring the Forest of Stone is far more fun than being holed up in a cave. Besides, Squish likes to get out in the sun! Recently though … well, I've been trying to figure out a bit of a mystery.

Tauric continues to explain in more detail if asked by the party.

What mystery?

For a long time the local oozes were very relaxed and sometimes even downright friendly, like Squish! However, lately, local oozes have gone from friend to enemy in no time at all, and nobody is sure why.

In Yakoshta, oozes are little buddies - they help in the mines and are more like pets than monsters. At least that's how it used to be until these new glowing gold and silver and copper oozes started attacking.

Aggressive oozes?

They appeared a few weeks ago out of nowhere, driving the regular oozes away and attacking everyone they run into. They're bigger than the normal oozes and glow, and there's absolutely no way to reason with or tame them. I've tried feeding them, talking to them, singing to them, and it doesn't matter. They just want to fight.

Can we help?

Tauric looks surprised for a moment as if the thought had not occurred to him, and then he beams at you with excitement.

Absolutely! I know that Sellen would want to meet you, she knows more about all this and she would definitely want extra help solving this mystery. The mine's been having trouble running consistently cause of the attacks, and that's only going to cause more problems for us down the line.

The hulg'run looks at you hopefully.

Would you come with me? Its several miles from here, but we'd be ever so appreciative!

Invitation to Yakoshta

For a more detailed conversation with Tauric, refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl.JournalEntryPage.HMQ1xNfO48AtwhjJ#after-the-fight]{"After the Fight"} section of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl.JournalEntryPage.HMQ1xNfO48AtwhjJ]{Good Ooze, Bad Ooze} event. The answers he provides there are the same set of information he would share here.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished speaking with Tauric, they can move on.

Next Steps

Tauric is happy to travel with the party to one of two places, Yakoshta where Tauric lives or the nearby Ooze Pools.

  • At @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT] the party will encounter the [[/eventState oozeControlCamp]] event.

  • At the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.pf1eWchM2qV0iMtb] the party will encounter the [[/eventState oozeControlPool]] event.

If party members choose to go elsewhere to explore the Forest of Stone, Tauric decides to make his own way back. When and if the party reaches Yakoshta, they will reunite with him there.
Wayward Sampler.soverview: As the party travels into the southern pass in the Forest of Stone they encounter a Hulg'run with a slime companion, who is all too happy to chat with them.
Wayward Sampler.sexposition:
As you round the corner of one of the many meandering channels of the Dripstones into a clearing, your eye catches motion as you observe a statue-like figure with skin the color of cool granite crouched down over a pool of glimmering liquid. The individual is facing away from you, and you witness the figure collecting some of the substance inside a small flask.

Just after doing so, the figure turns around to reveal a young Hulg'run whose bright eyes meet yours. His stony features light up with excitement and he gives a sprightly wave and begins ambling towards you.
Wayward Sampler.ssummary: We met a Hulg'run named Tauric from the local Yakoshta Mine while traveling in the southern canyons off the main trunk of the Verdant Paths.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This Side Quest can be undertaken by any party that explores the northern section of the Forest of Stone. This might happen during Chapter 1, but the Events of this Quest can also be experienced later in the game.

Difficulty

"Over the Moon" is designed for a party of Level 1 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 1 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point} upon successful completion of the [[/eventState overMoonTemple]] Event.

For centuries into possibly millennia the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.WG5PhLJbJ3Dvi4AP]{Ancient Shent Gate} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet]{Forest of Stone} has remained sealed, whatever secrets waiting beyond them left to sit undiscovered for as long as any living being knows. In fact, there are few in the world who even wonder what lies beyond, because the stone gates are an obscure piece of history at best.

However, in this quest the party will encounter the Fulgurite Blades, a band of adventurers aligned with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, who are planning to open these gates and see what lies beyond. The party will soon find themselves invited to explore the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones}, running afoul of dangers and lost history the likes of which few have seen and fewer still can remember.

The party will find ancient Shent ruins and battle with strange beasts and elementals. They will also find evidence of the Shattering, an event that nearly destroyed Ember; this destruction was only avoided by the efforts of ancient civilizations like the Shent.

Worse still, at the end of this quest they will come face to face with one of the last remnants of that invasion. The party there must decide whether they will finish what the Shent started, or give in and listen to its enticing whispers, and offers of power.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu]

  • @UUID[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28]

  • @UUID[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR]

  • @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj]

  • @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk]

  • @UUID[Actor.xaHxpBSNjhe8eonQ]

  • @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V]

  • @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS]

  • @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty]

  • @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]

  • @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J]
Overview.soverview:
In the northern part of the Forest of Stone is a colossal doorway thousands of years old. For as long as anyone can remember it has remained closed, keeping the lands beyond secured against curious souls and their ilk. However, a band of dogged adventurers are determined to unravel the secret to opening the doors and finding out what lies beyond. Will you help them?

The Fulgurite Blades are trainees of the Anachraenum — a guild of adventurers, explorers, and treasure hunters. Looking to make both a name for themselves and some coin from new discoveries, the Fulgurite Blades have been camped out before the massive stone entry to a section of the Forest of Stone for days. They are just about done deciphering the magics and passphrases that are needed, but they lack a clear picture of what awaits them, or extra backup in case things get hairy. Luckily, you're in the area.

In "Over the Moon" you will travel through an ancient section of the Dripstones, exploring waterlogged terrain, battling strange creatures, and discovering remnants of the ancient Shent and their final moments on Ember. In the wake of their destruction, their temples and mines were left abandoned, and numerous creatures from beyond Ember have taken up residence in them. Alongside the Fulgurite Blades, you'll gain insights into the past, and make decisions about Ember's future.

Curious Party.name: Curious Party
Curious Party.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event informs the party of the presence of other adventurers in the northern @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.TB9sbU2LNziZKZWD]{Forest of Stone} area, including a sect of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw] known as the @UUID[Actor.emberFulgrBlades]{Fulgurite Blades}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Examine a notice left by Fulgurite Blades in an attempt to decipher its age and origin.

  • Survey the local area to determine precisely where the Anachraenum group might be, with details pointing toward the Fulgurite Blade camp encountered during @UUID[.Xtmd5E8yiRsnnS6X], located two miles due east.

An Archaeological Claim

Examining the parchment below the banner yields a little more information.

The parchment bears a watermark of the same emblem sewn upon the banner above it, its message reads:

Investigation of nearby archaeological site ongoing by the Fulgurite Blades under the auspices of Anachraenum operations. For questions or work regarding the opening of this sealed passage, see Sajor in base camp ahead.

The final sentence has been struck through with black ink and replaced with an additional note that reads:

Do not disturb unless on official business.

At the foot of the pole is a small pile of rocks that have been haphazardly splattered with some sort of dark paint or ink to create an arrow pointing east.

Official Notice

Characters with [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notice that the note and banner are new, having been placed somewhat recently.

  • A further [[/skill investigation 12]][[/skillCheck science 12]] check to examine the cloth and ink gives the character investigating it the sense that it's less than two weeks old.

With a successful [[/skill history 14]][[/skillCheck society 14 ]] check a character will conclude that the note appears to be totally legitimate with proper watermarks and stamps, including one for the Ordain city leadership.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberOrdani]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The party may wish to consider this notice and understand more about the groups mentioned.

What is the Anachraenum?

Characters with [[/skill history 15 passive format=long]] or who succeed on a [[/skill history 13]] check[[/skillCheck society 15 passive ]], [[/culture emberArcturian]], or [[/culture emberOrdani]] know that the banner belongs to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} — an order of adventurer-historians based in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}.

Anachraenum adventurers, explorers, scouts, and scholars travel throughout the Arctus Plateau and beyond in search of hidden treasure, lost secrets, and remnants of the bygone civilizations. The guild is mostly comprised of teams that take on specialized jobs and tasks together, or freelance agents who handle their Anachraenum business alone.

  • Result of 18+Critical Success: You do not recognize the name "Fulgurite Blades", but it is expected that individual adventuring groups within the Anachraenum would have their own self-styled monikers that characterize their groups' style or motivations.

If the party would like to get a bearing or try to track the Fulgurite Blades they can do so by investigating the area around the banner.

Where Did They Go?

Characters with [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]][[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] instantly spot the pile of stones forming an arrow at the base of the banner pole. It aims east into the wide canyon. Furthermore, the banner is surrounded by numerous old tracks in the mud.

A successful [[/skill survival 12]][[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] check or [[/knowledge tracking]] reveals that the group headed east, further into the canyon. Studying the footprints which linger in certain areas of soft soil you conclude that there are at least two different people in this group.

  • Result of 18+Critical Success: You know there are four distinct sets of tracks and you recognize that one of the tracks was left by a Cor'ak, as revealed by their distinctive wide footprint. Another set of tracks was left by a much smaller figure which is probably a Thornling.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has investigated the banner, they can continue their exploration of the region.

Next Steps

If the party travels north from this location, they will encounter the Fulgurite Blades within their encampment in [[/eventState overMoonLightning]].

If, instead, the party instead travels north, they will encounter the [[/eventState overMoonDoor]] event.
Curious Party.soverview: As the party makes their way northward through the Forest of Stone, they encounter an officious banner tacked to a post, denoting the perimeter of an "Anachraenum Archaeological Study Site." Meanwhile, a small pile of rocks indicates a northward direction that the characters can follow should they choose to investigate this so-called site.
Curious Party.sexposition:
Standing next to a tree is a tall wooden pole driven deeply into the ground upon which hangs a bright, new-looking banner of heavy canvas. It bears the symbol of a sextant and quill with the words:

Anachraenum Archaeological Study Site

Just below the lower edge of the banner, a piece of parchment tacked to the pole draws your eye as it silently shifts with the breeze. You notice an official-looking seal upon it, too small to read from this distance.
Curious Party.ssummary: We encountered an Anachraenum banner and a notice of an official expedition site nearby. Per the notice tacked to the banner pole, it's being run by a group called the "Fulgurite Blades", and they have a camp nearby somewhere to the east.

Sealed Passage.name: Sealed Passage
Sealed Passage.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event is a breadcrumb that informs the party of the existence of explorable areas to the north of the Forest of Stone region.
