There is nothing the party can do to open the door from this side, it is instead opened from the other side during the [[/eventState windingTrailNorth2]] event later in this quest.

In this event, the party can:

  • Discover remnants of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ] culture.

  • Investigate the doorway to glean insights into its purpose and makers.

  • Receive the hint that there is more to find on the other side of this ancient structure.

No Entry

The Shent gateway is closed and impossible to open from this side. However, events in a nearby quest will lead the party to the other side of this door, and provide them the means to open it. The doors are around forty feet tall covered in vines and rocky protrusions that could allow them to be climbed for closer inspection.

Behind Closed Doors

Examining the stone using a successful [[/skill perception 12]][[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check reveals scrapes in the stone on the ground worn long ago where hinges were cut into the stone. This was likely once a door, but the stone seems entirely fused together with no means of moving it.

Characters who inspect the runic markings with [[/knowledge rituals]] or a successful [[/skill arcana 13]][[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check recognize that numerous markings upon the stone bear archaic symbols for transmutation, divination, abjuration, and evocation.

  • Result of 18+Critical Success: The inset gems are similarly inscribed. The stone and crystals were likely enchanted to be magically sealed and warded. Without knowing the ancient spells used to perform the sealing, there is no way to unseal the door.

  • Characters who succeed on an [[/skill insight 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check note that further clues to unsealing the door might be found on the opposite side, if that area could be reached some other way.

Characters succeeding on a [[/skill history 14]][[/skillCheck society 14]] check or with [[/knowledge shent]] conclude that, based on the door's size and markings, this structure was very likely built by the Shent; a culture of giants who inhabited this region long ago. If it was constructed by the Shent, then it is likely close to three-thousand years old.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 19+Critical Success: You recall that the Shent possessed a great reverence for Ember's moons and fostered close connections to them. It's quite possible that this place is a site religious significance. Perhaps some prayer, offering, or other invocation related to the lunar cycle might be involved in the unsealing of the door.

The eye-catching crystals embedded in the door may be tempting targets for plunder.

Gem Thieves

The crystals embedded in the door are magically set and impossible to remove or damage without a force far greater than what the party can muster.

The crystals were all sourced from this region's caves and contain latent magical effects. Attempting to interact with them up close triggers one of their @UUID[RollTable.CW4O54YLtXBarVjz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal Effects} which could be inconvenient to a character clinging to a stone wall dozens of feet off the ground.

Concluding the Event

This event serves as a signpost that gameplay content is able to be found somewhere to the north.

Next Steps

To explore the content of this quest, the party will need to travel around the cliffs to access the sealed area via the [[/eventState overMoonDoor]].

Along the way to that area they will encounter the event [[/eventState overMoonCurious]] which further introduces the quest.
Sealed Passage.soverview: The party discovers a massive stone relief that resembles a doorway. There is no obvious way to open the door from this side, although the party can learn some clues and historical context that will be useful elsewhere in the region.
Sealed Passage.sexposition:
The stonework of this large cliffside edifice ranges from a muted gray to a golden brown with sections nearing a rusty red. Left to the mercy of the wind, rain, and sun, the stone has become weathered and cracked, with much of its fine detail having been lost over the countless years it has stood here.

A dark stone crescent with carved writing, nearly indecipherable from years of exposure arcs over the large, swirling patterns that decorate the central structure, with seven large crystals set among the curves. The largest crystal is a dull blue, while the remaining smaller orbs are an array of faded colors including orange, pink, purple, red, yellow, and green. These crystals, like all else here, have lost their shimmer to layers of wear and dust.

This design is bordered by two substantial square columns and a broad crown of stone decorated with six figures, each wielding staves or weapons. Their images are eroded but faintly visible, and accompanied by more carved writing or runes that are hard to make out.
Sealed Passage.ssummary: We encountered a massive stone relief that resembles a doorway inset within the cliffside on near the eastern edge of the Forest of Stone. We couldn't find any way to open it. Perhaps the mechanism for doing so is lost to time or located on the other side — if it's even a door in the first place.

Lightning in a Bottle.name: Lightning in a Bottle
Lightning in a Bottle.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event sees the party meeting the Fulgurite Blades, a band of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw] adventurers lead by the mage @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu]. In this event, the party can:

  • Meet the @UUID[Actor.emberFulgrBlades]{Fulgurite Blades} and learn why they are present and what they hope to accomplish.

  • Learn about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} organization, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} culture, or the Forest of Stone region in general.

Meeting the Blades

As you approach several sets of eyes turn your way, and a massive Cor'ak who up to this moment looked bored out of his mind, jumps up from his seat and begins walking toward you.

"Hold there, this is a private camp, 'fore you go any further, best introduce yourselves and what you want with us."

A nearby kivahr woman looks up from a piece of ruin sticking out of the grass and shrubs, her eyes moving from you to the Cor'ak. A second later her eyes fall back to her notebook to scribble something and she calls out:

"Sajor, we have visitors, and Rorhim's gotten to them first!"

The Cor'ak, Rorhim, offers a toothy grin in response.

"Not gonna hurt them, just doing my job."

At this point you notice the arrival of a tall Nir'ae woman who stands at a distance and considers you for a moment, nearby a fidgety Thornling does the same, though he is muttering something to her which she seems to ignore.

Eventually the woman who must be Sajor comes to stand with the Rorhim, and says:

"Was there something you wanted? As I'm sure Rorhim pointed out, this is an active Anachraenum field camp, so we're all rather busy."

The Fulgurite Blades are a party of four adventurers under the leadership of Sajor and her lieutenant Rorhim.

@Embed[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu]

@Embed[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28]

@Embed[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR]

@Embed[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj]

Cleric of Spectra

A character with [[/knowledge gods]] or [[/skill religion 14 passive format=long]][[/skillCheck society 14 passive]] understands that Spectra is one of the few and extremely significant Elder Gods of Ember. She is focused on the study of magic with countless shrines around the world. Spectra has many followers and she is known to empower some of them with a portion of her divine power, particularly favoring those followers who demonstrate a scholastic enthusiasm for the pursuit of knowledge. The Kivahr, Kazra, very likely wields a measure of power from her goddess.

Talking to The Blades

Sajor and the Fulgurite Blades are generally standoffish and a touch wary of strangers walking into their camp. If anyone points out that their banner had a note about looking for help, they will counter that by pointing out that part of the letter was scratched out.

They have decided that they would like to investigate the Shent door by themselves and reserve for themselves the opportunity of scouting the unbreached lands beyond.

Reluctant Conversation

This information can be learned from the Fulgurite Blades through speaking to them. They are generally standoffish; they don't want to deal with strangers nor are they looking for new friends. Any answers they give are terse and formulated to avoid followup questions.

The Fulgurite Blades are an established team, having worked together for about two years. The four of them are friends and loyal to each other.

Sajor is their leader, and she has the near unflinching loyalty of the other three. Observing the team with a successful [[/skill insight 13]][[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check, it is clear she is a very hands-off leader, and everyone has a clear picture of what their job is on the team.

Trade Opportunities

The Fulgurite Blades have a pretty well stocked camp, and are willing to trade coins for their spare rations, rope, and tools. They might even have a couple spare weapons on hand. They mostly trade fairly and are open to barter unless the party has gotten on their bad side.

Getting to Helkas

The Fulgurite Blades are only aware of the one main path through the Forest of Stone, but they suspect there might be other paths winding through the area. One such path could be on the other side of the huge door. Once the door is opened, the Party is free to have a look and see for themselves.

Who are you?

We are The Fulgurite Blades, adventurers and scholars working under the auspices of the Anachraenum.

You are scholars?

Yes, and explorers. We are cataloging the ruins for Shent knowledge and artifacts.

You left a sign?

We initially thought it would be useful to get help with uncovering and opening the doorway, but we've changed our minds. We have everything we need and we would prefer avoiding the complexity of coordinating with others. We apologize to have misled you, but your help is not required.

Help Not Wanted

A successful [[/skill insight 14]][[/skillCheck deception 14]] check gives you the sensation that they are being cagey about their reasons. While it's certainly possible they changed their minds and that's that, you're not sure it's quite so cut and dry. You'll need to dig a little to learn more.

  • A successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] or [[/skill deception 14]][[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] or [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check to coax more information out of them allows you to learn that they realized something about the door, and that perhaps the area inside has more value than at first glance.

  • Attempting to coerce the information out of the party can be successful with a [[/skill intimidation 15]][[/skillCheck intimidation 15]] check. They will acknowledge they don't want help because they don't want to share the potential riches inside. This causes the Fulgurite Blades to become unfriendly (although not outright hostile) towards you and unwilling to help or work with you going forward.

If the party offends or provokes the Fulgurite Blades they will be asked firmly to leave, with it being clearly stated that they are not welcome.

The party may ask about the Shent or the artifacts that the Fulgurite Blades are seeking. Kazra and Sajor are more interested than the other two members of the party to discuss this topic.

What are you looking for?

We are investigating Shent ruins in the area. There is a great doorway to the north and we're going to open it. The archaeological claims beyond that door are of interest to the Anachraenum and will further our reputation within the guild.

About the Shent?

The term "Shent" is used not only to describe the dominant ancestry, but also the culture. They lived over three millennia ago. They vanished almost entirely, and almost no record or history remains of them save for small references in old documents from other, equally ancient cultures.

About their artifacts?

They Shent were prolific stone carvers and built using a combination of traditional building techniques and some sort of magical transmutation to produce and shape stone without tools.

They worshiped the moons of Ember, and also had means to harness their power for things, possibly through rituals, and magically attuned locations, though few working sites or examples exist in the world.

Meeting the Blades

The party may speak with each of the members of the Fulgurite Blades individually, they each have some response although none are particularly interested in prolonged conversation.

About Sajor?

The Anachraenum is an organization where the motivated, fearless, and dedicated can make a name for themselves while also discovering more of the world and it's countless mysteries. Of course I want to make important discoveries and to be known far and wide for it!

There is nothing wrong with being ambitious and collecting accolades. If Fernis Ossa can be a celebrity of Ordain then so too can I.

About Rorhim?

Seek adventure, test my might, see the world! That's what you get with the Anachraenum, right?

I don't really care much about the history side of things, although I understand why it's important. I'd rather battle ancient Aedir constructs or cull tomb-robbing bandits than worry about the history of a clay pot.

About Leeph?

Turns out it's far easier to lift things from ancient tombs and graves that the pockets of the living. Corpses don't get angry … except when they do which is extremely bad. That's never happened to me, but I've heard stories about it. If it does happen, well … that's what we keep Rorhim around for! I'd prefer not to deal with angry people, or corpses.

About Kazra?

I am a priestess of Spectra both trained and accredited. Some of my peers might say I'm one of the god's chosen — I seek knowledge on her behalf and wield a measure of her power. I am a scholar, but we aren't always historians first. Sometimes our purpose of exploration and discovery aligns with my goals to serve Spectra. I love being a member of the Anachraenum because I can honor Spectra while doing something that I love. I think of the group here, I've been in the guild the longest — around 8 years so far. Sajor joined shortly after me.

About Spectra?

Kazra smiles, appreciative of the acknowledgment.

That's correct, I am a priestess of Spectra both trained and accredited. Some of my peers might say I'm one of the god's chosen — I seek knowledge on her behalf and wield a measure of her power.

I can't tell you for sure why Spectra chose me, which I know is somewhat ironic given her domain.

Matters of Faith

Characters that are followers of Spectra, or fellow clerics will find the Kazra is more friendly with them, but still remains staunchly loyal to her team.

Are you hiring?

Sajor shakes her head firmly:

No, we aren't taking new members into the Blades, sorry. And no, we're not in the business of escorting sightseers either. you can explore once the gate's open, but you're on your own if you do.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has had their fill of the Fulgurite Blades, and conversation with them, they are free to move on. To proceed from here, the party will need to study the door and eventually open it.

Next Steps

The party will find [[/eventState overMoonDoor]] to the north.
Lightning in a Bottle.soverview: The party encounters a campsite where the Fulgurite Blades, an Anachraenum adventuring group, are preparing to open the great stone gateway nearby. The party can learn about the group and their purpose, potentially aligning on mutual goals.
Lightning in a Bottle.sexposition:
You find yourself in a broad clearing where a cluster of tents has been set up. At first glance, it appears to be a simple travelers' camp, but a few banners and symbol-bearing tents reveal a different story. Adorned with symbols of the Anachraenum, this must be the camp advertised by the banner you found earlier.

Around the camp, you spot four figures moving about. The individual closest to you wears a pin upon their shoulder that matches the symbol on the notice: a sword formed from lightning. Presumably, this must be the encampment of the Fulgurite Blades.
Lightning in a Bottle.ssummary: We investigated the Anachraenum expedition site and met the Fulgurite Blades, a band of adventuring scholars led by Sajor. They are here studying ruins, specifically the ancient Shent gateway nearby.

Untouched Wilds.name: Untouched Wilds
Untouched Wilds.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, the party passes through the massive @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} gateway into an isolated and unexplored region of the Forest of Stone which is predominately comprised of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]. In this event the party can:

  • Meet the @UUID[Actor.emberFulgrBlades]{Fulgurite Blades} for the first time, if they haven't yet.

  • Confer with the Fulgurite blades to get some information and limited guidance from their leader, @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu].

  • Determine a course of action for how they will explore this untouched region.

Fulgurite Blades Unmet

If the party did not previously encounter the Fulgurite Blades, read the following text aloud:

A group of adventurers come jogging up behind you, clearly drawn by the sight and sound of the great doors opening. The figure at their head, a Nir'ae woman, bears a mixture of excitement and annoyance, her eyes flipping between you, the great doors, and the land beyond.

"I knew we shouldn't have waited to open the door."

She looks to her cohort of adventurers and waves them forward.

"Let's get moving, there's a lot of ground to cover, and we're not on our timetable any more. On the double, Blades, this region won't explore itself!"

As they move forward, excitedly chattering with each other about what things they might find, and what goals the might have, a kivahr woman wearing the symbols of the god Sigil speaks up:

"Not to ruin anyone's fun, but we do need to catalog our findings before we carry on."

This statement earns the kivahr a couple annoyed groans from a thornling rogue and cor'ak fighter who clearly want nothing more than to go off exploring. The Nir'ae woman watches them in silence, not interfering until the pair look her way, only then does she nod in agreement with the priestess, and gesture for them to go help.

Eventually she turns her attention back to you.

"We haven't met yet: I'm Sajor, and these are my Fulgurite Blades."

Meeting the Blades

If this is the first time the party is meeting the Fulgurite Blades, refer to @UUID[.Xtmd5E8yiRsnnS6X] for the team's descriptions, and some introductory conversation topics which can be explored.

Fulgurite Blades Met

If the party previously met the Fulgurite Blades, they rejoin the party on the far side of the now-open passageway.

The Fulgurite Blades come jogging up behind you, clearly drawn by the sight and sound of the great doors opening. Sajor leads them, and she beams a broad, impressed grin at you, the great doors, and the land beyond.

"Impressive! I was wondering how long it'd take you to figure it out."

She looks to her cohort of adventurers and waves them forward.

"Let's get moving, there's a lot of ground to cover, and we can't let our new friends here find all the interesting things!"

As they move forward, excitedly chattering with each other about what things they might find, and what goals the might have, Kazra speaks up, cutting through the din:

"Not to ruin anyone's fun, but we do need to catalog our findings before we carry on."

This statement earns the priestess a groan from Leeph and Rorhim who clearly want to go explore, but Sajor just watches them in silence, not interfering at first. Only when they look at her does she nod, silently agreeing with Kaza. Defeated, the rogue and fighter comply, and begin helping Kazra.

Conferring with the Blades

This conversation occurs just inside the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} biome, and allows the party to get some guidance and direction from the Fulgurite Blades, and get a sense of what they want to do.

What Do They Know?

Sajor and her band can only guess at what things might be in the area. It's an untouched region that's been closed off for longer than anyone's been alive. There could be all kinds of creatures and dangers lurking here, perhaps things nobody's ever seen. They are excited to see what they find, and what valuables they can claim.

Knowledge about this area?

Shent have ruins all over, so there's a good chance of finding old ruins and sites here that have lain undisturbed for millenia!

Your research?

Never you fear, we'll take extensive notes, but that's secondary to the process of actually finding something note-worthy!

On Academic Integrity

The Fulgurite Blades are more akin to treasure-hunting adventurers than dedicated historians, and that trait is likely to become much more obvious if the party asks about the attribution of discoveries, cataloging finds, and the like.

Characters with [[/skill insight 15 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill insight 13]] check[[/skillCheck deception 15 passive]] suspect that Sajor cares more about the treasure-hunting or perhaps fame-hunting aspect of her profession as she does about pure academic pursuits.

Rorhim and Leeph don't seem to be any different. Kazra however, seems to take their role as explorers and historians far, far more seriously. If anyone can be relied upon to carry out proper logging and organization of finds, it will be her.

Passage to Helkas?

This area could possibly extend to some southern route which might present a passage to Helkas or an area near to it. There is no guarantee of such a passage though, otherwise we would have taken it ourselves.

Where are you headed?

We're going to start by heading north, towards the mountain ranges where the Shent were known to live. We plan to follow the canyon walls, looking for caves and ruins.

Traveling together?

Sajor shakes her head at the topic.

Nope. You go your way, we go ours. We don't need extra people slowing us down, getting in our way, or interfering with our discoveries.

After a pause she expands this thought:

In fact I'd recommend you start heading south along the canyon walls, and see what you find while we head north. Shent carved and decorated many stones around here, so we're hoping to find something good.

Whatever direction the party takes, the Fulgurite Blades will take the opposite, avoiding travel with them. If the party decides they want to follow the Fulgurite Blades, secretly or otherwise, then they will end up traveling toward the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.dH8d3daTaRNOWLrt] which will immediately begin @UUID[.yzgUD9WX351fihbU] in this quest.

Tailing the Blades

The party may attempt to follow stealthily, requiring a group [[/skill stealth 12]][[/skillCheck stealth 12 group]] check. If any party members fail this check, the character who rolls lowest is the one detected by @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj]{Kazra}, the most perceptive of the Fulgurite Blades.

Concluding the Event

Once the party is ready to break camp, they separate from or follow the Fulgurite Blades to continue their exploration of the region.

Fulgurite Caravan

At the end of this event a caravan actor representing the Fulgurite Blades will appear on the world map. This token can be used to track where they are in relation to the party. It's recommended that you move them whenever you move the party, but that is up to your discretion.

Next Steps

While exploring the area further, the group is likely to trigger the [[/eventState dripstonesHydroxol]] event where they encounter a territorial beast. Beyond that random encounter, the party has two options:

  • The party can optionally explore north to find the crystal caverns where [[/eventState signalIntentCrystals]] takes place.

  • The party can explore south until they find the Shent water temple where [[/eventState overMoonTemple]] takes place.
Untouched Wilds.soverview: Just beyond the ancient and now unsealed Shent gate, the party reunites with the Fulgurite Blades expedition who are also eager to explore the region beyond. The party may try to team up with them or travel separately.
Untouched Wilds.sexposition:
It is remarkable how damp the air is here, how the stone glistens as though it was all recently subject to rain. The air is thick with moisture and the scent of petrichor and mineral-rich water, leaving an almost metallic taste in your mouth.

The ground is uneven and dotted with smooth rocky pools that shimmer from the scant light filtering through the dense canopy above. Mosses of vivid greens and blues cling to every surface, their colors creating a living mosaic upon the rocks.

The sounds of running and dripping water surround you, emanating from unseen cenotes and underground rivers that carve their slow paths beneath your feet. The humidity clings to your skin and if you listen carefully, the muted rush of a distant waterfall can be heard somewhere nearby.
Untouched Wilds.ssummary: We've set foot into a newly unsealed section of the Forest of Stone. This sprawling area of dripstones probably hasn't been explored for thousands of years and there's no telling what lies within. The Fulgurite Blades are also eager to explore this new area.

Lunar Awakenings.name: Lunar Awakenings
Lunar Awakenings.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event reunites the party with the Fulgurite Blades at the site of a large temple built by the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} — where they must defeat a water elemental that feats on the flow of magical energy from an archaic Shent machine. In this event, the characters can:

  • Fight the @UUID[Actor.ycJvVeKNvictpMty]{Temple Invader} and its water elemental allies: @UUID[Actor.xaHxpBSNjhe8eonQ]{Water Motes}, @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V]{Water Sprites}, and a @UUID[Actor.cIX3WXHAZ0gAXCNS]{Water Visitor}.

  • Meet the ghostly projection of the Shent sage @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth}, who will assign the party one final, dangerous task.

  • Earn a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point} following the completion of the event.

Refer to the Area Walkthrough for the @UUID[JournalEntry.dCExfRYP8KRVogO2]{Shent Water Temple} for a full description of the event's location and associated gameplay.

Opening the Temple

The party remains relatively safe until they open the doors into the temple. As soon as they do that, they will initiate a battle with the hostile elemental contained within. Proceed with the gameplay found in the area walkthrough: @UUID[JournalEntry.dCExfRYP8KRVogO2]{Shent Water Temple}. Once the elementals have been defeated and the party is ready to leave the temple, return here for the rest of the quest event's narrative below.

The Memory Remains

After the battle ends, and once the party is ready to depart the temple, a ghostly projection of a Shent Seer appears to the party.

To avoid cluttering the scene during combat, Mioroth's actor is not present in the Moon Temple scene initially. Once the party is about to see him, drag Mioroth's actor from the actor sidebar to somewhere in the scene where the party can see them.

@Embed[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]

The Shent image begins to speak in a tongue that makes no sense to your ears. Stranger still, the sounds seem to come from all directions but the one toward the figure. Eventually the words transform into ones you recognize, the sensation akin to slowly remembering something someone once told you.

Finally its words make sense:

Please, I implore you, do what we failed to: To the south of here there is a site where an abyssal creature, the Whisperer, lies weak and vulnerable. Before you leave this region, please, travel there and defeat it. Much of Ember's future safety hangs in the balance! Do so, and I will see you rewarded properly.

Speaking to Mioroth

What Mioroth Knows

Mioroth has considerable knowledge about the Shent, the Shattering, and other topics of antiquity which could prove very interesting or enticing to historians and scholars. However, Mioroth is unwilling to go into great detail about these topics since they know how rare and potentially disruptive such knowledge could be. He has no interest in turning a handful of random strangers into the foremost experts on ancient history with no regard for how that might affect their lives.

A successful a [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check check to gauge his intentions notes that while he is being honest and accurate with what he says, he is deliberately withholding information for some reason. If pressed, Mioroth might even be entirely forthcoming with his reasoning.

Mioroth is steadfast in his convictions, and cannot be persuaded to change his mind, or give up more information. However, that is not to say he doesn't have a wealth of information he can share. He is more than happy to lend small bits of insight and knowledge to the party, especially if they help him with the Whisperer.

About Mioroth

Put simply, the projection is a memory and an echo of the ancient Seer Mioroth.

Mioroth does not eat, sleep, or breathe. He will confirm that he's neither undead, or a ghost, though, if asked. However, he refuses to elaborate any further on how he came to be, his abilities, or his purpose.

About the Shent

This is where Mioroth will be most reserved. He avoids providing direct information beyond things he believes most would have learned by now:

  • The Shent were an ancient nation and culture that fell during the Shattering. The Shent built many wonders in these lands and great cities upon distant mountain peaks but they are all long gone now, he is merely a memory.

  • The Kivahr and Keth are direct descendants of the Shent, which is why the Kivahr slightly follow their physical form. The Hulg'run predate both and were created by the Shent to be servants before gaining freedom and being treated as equals.

About the Shattering

Mioroth tells of a period where the skies were rent asunder, torn open by forces unfathomable. From those gaping wounds poured forth entities of bedlam, and malignant ruin. The realms of Ember buckled under the onslaught, with many sent to early demise in pursuit of what was a narrow survival.

The Whisperer was one of those deadly interlopers, and while Mioroth doesn't know what attracted it to the area, he is haunted by how it laid waste to the Shent here, doing so with terrible efficiency. The Shent in the area only barely managed to subdue and contain it, hoping that someone else would eventually be able to come and destroy it. That obviously never happened.

About the Temple

The temple was originally built as a grand planetarium. It was one of many built across Shent lands. This one in particular was meant to chart the celestial dance of Mayis around ember, so that its cycles would be known in greatest detail. It was designed to draw power from that moon to drive it, so that the machine would never stop, which was perhaps not the best design choice.

The item that was taken from its core is a planisphere, a deceptively simple piece of equipment that was one of the oldest inventions of his people and commonly used around the world by many other cultures. It could manually track the secret motions of the sky's errant march, and was the core of the planetarium, used to project accurate images of the celestial bodies.

About the the Crystal Caves

The crystal caves were sources of stone naturally infused with magic drawn from Ember. This was a distant mining community once, and they produced gems used all across the Shent realms. While the were deleterious in their natural form, if properly carved with runes they had a myriad of uses.

The machine in the caverns was known as a "nullifier," a clever device built to suppress the maddening effects of the crystal caverns so that our people could work in them safely. It was a marvel of its time, unique, one of a kind, and destroyed by the Whisperer.

Once the party has finished speaking with Mioroth, they are free to leave the temple and carry on with their expedition.

Concluding the Event

As part of the event's conclusion, the entire party will also be affected by the following Mayis Attunement reinforcement:

Mayis Attunement: Meeting Mioroth

Once the party completes their encounter with Mioroth, each character in the party advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 overMoonLoreMioroth]] at the conclusion of the event.

Should one of the characters attempt to take the Planisphere for themselves, they will reinforce their Aura Attunement in the process.

Aura Attunement: Planisphere Claimed

Each character who attempts to take or withhold the Planisphere from Sajor (via whatever method they choose) advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 overMoonLorePlanisphere]] at the conclusion of the event.

Alternatively, if the party convinces the Fulgurite Blades to help them clear the rubble blocking the Strayhearth Caravan, they progress their Ragen attunement:

Ragen Attunement: Fulgurite Assistance

If the party acquired help from the Fulgurite Blades to clear the rubble, each member of the party gains [[/attunement emberRagen +1 overMoonFulguriteHelp]] upon the conclusion of this event.

Milestone Progression

Completing this event earns the party a Milestone Point, potentially advancing them in level. Refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Progression} section of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide]{Player's Guide} for details on how character advancement works in Ember.

Next Steps

If the party follows Mioroth's guidance, the characters must travel southward to the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.hxHaYXXkGDsZ8cGv] where [[/eventState signalIntentCrystals]] occurs.

Alternately, the party could head south and onward into the caverns in search of an alternate route to Helkas.
Lunar Awakenings.soverview: The party happens upon a Shent temple that has been overtaken by an opportunistic elemental taking advantage of the limitless power flowing through the ancient machinery. The party needs to shut down the elemental and the machine, but luckily they'll have a little help from the Fulgurite Blades.
Lunar Awakenings.sexposition: Approaching the structure you can see numerous carvings adorn the high walls —symbols and depictions of the water moon surrounded by stars and constellations you don't recognize.
Lunar Awakenings.ssummary: We discovered a huge Shent temple dedicated to the moon Mayis that had been taken over by a particularly powerful water elemental. No sooner did we dispatch it than the ghost of a Shent appeared and asked us to face down an ancient evil nearby.

An Ancient Battle.name: An Ancient Battle
An Ancient Battle.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event occurs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.iHDQeYHNXuIrJvqc]{Writhing Grave} where the party will confront an ancient abyssal creature known as the Writhing Whisperer. In this event the characters can:

  • Encounter a @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Writhing Whisperer}, a malevolent and ancient abyssal entity.

  • Do battle with the Whisperer or accept its offered bargain.

  • Interact with the Shent seer, @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth}, who appears via projection after the battle.

Area Walkthrough

The party begins in the @UUID[JournalEntry.iHDQeYHNXuIrJvqc.JournalEntryPage.PU35w1NyL7IqA36h]{Terraced Pools}. Follow the area walkthrough for gameplay and details of this area. Once the Whisperer has been either released or defeated, refer back to this event for its final resolution.

  • If the party released the Whisperer, proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.tJfhxYBC1weqR6K1#releasing-the-whisperer]{Releasing the Whisperer}.

  • If the party destroyed the Whisperer, proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.tJfhxYBC1weqR6K1#defeating-the-whisperer]{Defeating the Whisperer}.

In this event, the party faces off against a Writhing Whisperer, a terrible abyssal monster trapped here for thousands of years.

@Embed[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN inline]

Immediately refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.iHDQeYHNXuIrJvqc]{Writhing Grave} area walkthrough for gameplay details of this location and the encounter that happens here. Once the encounter is resolved, return to this event to deal with the aftermath depending on what choice the party made.

The Whisperer Destroyed

If the party opposed and destroyed the Writhing Whisperer as Mioroth asked, record the event outcome, and award attunement progression.

[[/outcome mioroth]]

Heart Attunement: Defeat the Whisperer

If the party defeats the Writhing Whisperer in combat, each character in the party advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 overMoonWhispererDefeated]] at the conclusion of the event.

Shortly after the Whisperer is slain, the projection of Mioroth faintly appears, shimmering amidst the vapor of the cascading waterfalls.

@Embed[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]

Mioroth acknowledges the heroes' effort.

Thank you for doing what we could not. We should have destroyed this creature instead of allowing it to linger for these countless years, but there were none who could take up the fight once the last of us fell.

I will reward your intervention how I am able and I plan to watch your progress to the extent that my remaining sight permits. I suspect this will not be the last time we meet.

The party can talk about any missed information or topics from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.yzgUD9WX351fihbU#speaking-to-mioroth]{Speaking to Mioroth} in Lunar Awakenings, as well as the following additional information:

What was that thing?

A Whisperer, an outsider being that slipped through during the Shattering.

What happened here?

The battle was meant to be one-sided, we had the abomination finally cornered. My people made preparations to destroy it, but we took too long, and it had found its way into the minds of our allies.

The fight was no longer on our terms, and before long all we could do was wound it and fall back. In our retreat we sealed the passes and gates, attempting to at least contain what we could not defeat.

Leaving this place?

The closest exist to the region is through crystal caves to the south. We had a stone doorway there that served as gateway to more verdant paths beyond. However, the door is sealed magically. You will need to speak the words "Hope in destruction." which will open the way for you.

Do not worry what tongue you use, the old magic was meant to recognize the meaning, not the words.

About a reward?

Yes, of course, there is a great treasure to be had in the caves to the south. During the war against the Abyss, a powerful seer of ours was grievously wounded and sacrificed herself to make sure the canyon was properly seals.

If you can find the final resting place of this mage, you can claim the ancient spell case in the remains. Be warned though, if you do go searching the gloomy corners of the caverns, beware the glints of gossamer threads in the darkness. There are many lurking dangers still.

Shent Spell Case

The corpse of the seer that Mioroth mentions can be discovered during the [[/eventState overMoonSpiders]] event in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} to the south of the ancient battle site. It only appears for parties that have helped Mioroth and learn about its existence.

Will we see you again?

Mioroth offers an odd smile.

There are many paths and many events the Shent foretold before our time on Ember was up, and I have not forgotten all I've seen. We will meet again. I cannot and will not say anything more.

The Whisperer Released

If the party aided the Writhing Whisperer and feed it from its restraints, mark the following outcome as complete and award attunement progression as described below.

[[/outcome whisperer]]

Abyss Attunement: Release the Whisperer

Whichever character was most proactive in accepting the Writhing Whisperer's sinister bargain advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +3 overMoonWhispererReleasedA]] at the conclusion of the event. Each other character in the party who allied themself with the Whisperer also advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 overMoonWhispererReleased]] at the conclusion of the event.

As your minds settle you perceive the shimmering form of a Shent seer looking down at you. His voice booms from all directions at you, fury clear in his voice:

"Fools! Greedy, short-sighted fools! You have no idea what you've done. You've unleashed an entity of pure destruction on this world! When the skies were first sundered and its ilk spilled into our lands they were nearly our doom!"

"Of all the monsters that slipped through it was not even the strongest, and yet its power sufficed to lay waste to dozens of us within minutes of its arrival, and we only managed to weaken and contain it!"

"I hope that you have not spelled the doom of this world with your actions, and that whatever dark boon it granted you was worth it… "

With this the fuming projection of the Seer shimmers out of existence, his words still echoing off the walls and in your mind.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has had its fill of the cursed battleground, and has taken everything they want from it, they can move on.

Next Steps

If the party follows Mioroth's instructions to discover a route back towards Helkas through the Kaleidoscope Caverns, they will encounter the [[/eventState overMoonSpiders]] event.

Future Quests

Mioroth will reappear in later quests, should the party continue investigating ancient areas of the world and the history of the Shent people.

  • In Chapter 2, Mioroth may be encountered near the conclusion of the @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death} quest in the [[/eventState brushWithDeathArchives]] event.

  • In Chapter 2, Mioroth may be encountered during the @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi]{To Fall and Fall Again} quest in the [[/eventState fallAgainWreckage]] event.
An Ancient Battle.soverview: The party arrives at the location indicated by Mioroth. The area is littered with the crumbling, almost fossilized bones of countless massive humanoids that could only be fallen Shent giants. At the center of this old battle site is an ancient evil trying to free itself. The party has been warned, but now must decide how to proceed.
An Ancient Battle.sexposition:
Damp grass, moss-coated stone, and ample plant life coats this space, fed by pools of water and the numerous waterfalls in the area. There is a sourness in the air though, and as the natural stone steps descend toward the nexus of falls you can see verdant green of this place turning gray and withered. The scent of rotting plants and brackish water grows harder to ignore the longer you are here.

More concerning is this sensation of… awareness and a feeling of being watched. New thoughts appear within your mind like fingers crawling up your neck and exerting pressure upon the base of your skull. You recoil as you realize these thoughts are not your own. There is something truly wrong about this place.
An Ancient Battle.ssummary: We discovered the furtive lair of an ancient evil entity spawned during the The Shattering, known simply as the Writhing Whisperer. Although this abyssal creature was weakened, it still proved itself a dangerous foe. With any luck, we've dealt with the Whisperer for good, and it will trouble the Forest of Stone no longer.

The Glint of Gossamer.name: The Glint of Gossamer
The Glint of Gossamer.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

While searching for an exit from the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns}, the party must face an ambush of crystalline spiders. In this event, the party can:

  • Navigate a hazardous arena of glittering webs.

  • Search the desiccated cadavers of long-dead Shent that @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth} told them about.

  • Survive combat with three @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J]{Young Cheliceraeth}, whose false appearance provides the element of surprise.

The Gossamer Cave

While navigating this psychedelic subterranean landscape, the characters reach a peculiar expanse of scintillating caves defined by their natural stone columns and the presence of glittering spiderwebs. The party is funneled into the cheliceraeth lair via a narrow tunnel before spilling out into a larger maze-like cavern dotted by natural stone columns.

Here and there, you spy vaguely humanoid shapes wrapped up in the glittering webbing — large skeletal forms, the size of giants — but it's apparent that no kind of living traveler has been here in ages.

Two of these clusters of webbed detritus catch your eye in particular. To your left, a set of metallic armor adorned in ancient filigree pokes out of a bulbous mass of glittering webs. Far ahead, a large skeletal figure wreathed in sparkling gossamer clutches an odd metallic cylinder. Perhaps other withered corpses lurk about this place with their own secrets to hide…

Glittering Webs

It's easy for the characters to spot the potential danger of these glittering webs, but they may be tempted to explore them after noticing treasure among the desiccated corpses.

Whenever a creature moves through a space covered in glittering webs, they must succeed on a [[/skill acrobatics 13]] skill check or become &Reference[restrained] by webbing.

Creatures who are &Reference[restrained] can spend an Action to make a [[/check strength 11]] check to escape the webbing. The effect ends if the webbing is destroyed. Each section of webbing (defined as an individual grid space) has AC 10, 5 hit points, is vulnerable to fire damage and thunder damage, resistant to radiant damage, and immune to bludgeoning damage.

Whenever a creature moves through a space covered in glittering webs, they must face [[/hazard 4 fortitude harmless]]{Glittering Webs}, if not resisted that character becomes @Condition[restrained] by webbing. Creatures who are restrained may escape at the cost of 6 Action or with a [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check.

Sections of webbing are defined according to 5 foot squares, and can be destroyed with the application of Fire or Acid damage.

Lurking Spiders

While exploring the caverns it is likely that the characters will disturb and provoke the cheliceraeth who lurk here.

  • A character becoming restrained by or destroying the webs immediately draws the attention of all 3 spiders.

  • Players who pass within 10 feet of a spider must succeed on a [[/skill stealth 13 passive format=long]] [[/skillCheck stealth 13 passive]] check to avoid detection.

  • If the party is remarkably loud, the young cheliceraeth may hear them.

If the spiders attack their ambush and tactics are described below in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon.JournalEntryPage.wJVbH6IBHx4DRRvO#cheliceraeth-ambush]{Cheliceraeth Ambush}.

The glittering webs that crisscross the cheliceraeth lair have been here for centuries, and house an array of broken egg sacs and clusters of cocooned mysteries. In addition to the skeletal remains of subterranean animals, these webs also contain a concealed array of ancient equipment and treasure from a bygone era.

After noticing the filigreed armor, the characters may wish to explore the cave's tangled network of glittering webs for other signs of loot — a sure way to attract the attention of the three cheliceraeth who dwell here.

Searching for Treasure

A total of four Shent corpses are scattered throughout the cheliceraeth lair, all of them cocooned in gem-spangled webbing. These forgotten souls were once the Sealers of the Southern Gate; now, their worldly remains are all but bones and dust, mired by glittering web. Characters can loot the corpses with a small amount of effort, but must take care to avoid getting caught in the glittering webs.

Shent Corpse A - The Shent remains to the northeast wears a set of @UUID[Item.gmpcZTsHfwZjFJot] armor adorned in ancient filigree.

Shent Corpse B - The skeleton near the center of the area holds two items of interest: a powerful @UUID[Item.qBH1HS4smbDasLGR].

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or who succeed on a [[/skill arcana 16]] [[/skillCheck arcana 16 passive]] check recognize that the case is a powerful artifact and a discovery of considerable value.

The other two remains are not easily visible, but characters with [[/skill perception 15 passive]] or who succeed on a [[/skill perception 13]] who succeed on a [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] check spot the other two Shent corpses concealed within the tangled mass of glittering webs.

Shent Corpse C - The ancient remains to the southwest cling to something obscured by grit and gossamer: an ancient @UUID[Item.0vfSw9TfHX5FRdh7] made of a curious unknown alloy.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] or [[/knowledge gods]] recognize that this holy symbol depicts the Elder God Pathwalker.

Shent Corpse D - The corpse to the southeast holds two other aged items covered in elaborate filigree: a @UUID[Item.iNWpyXTWBNflOny4] and a @UUID[Item.li4SMIYtcU7ts0hB].

Signara Attunement: Shent Scroll Case

The first character to successfully unlock the @UUID[Item.qBH1HS4smbDasLGR]{Shent Scroll Case} advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 overMoonSpidersCase]], which occurs as soon as the magic item is unlocked.

The items the party may discover here once belonged to ancient Shent giants and giantkin who served as Sealers of the Southern Gate. Characters can spend a turn to scrutinize this loot to learn more of its nature and history.

Secrets of the Ancient Shent

Characters inspecting these items who succeed on a [[/skill arcana 15]][[/skillCheck arcana 15 passive]] check recognize telltale elements of transmutation magic in the more esoteric details of the item's design.

  • If you can confirm the item's Shent origin (with one of the skill checks below), you understand it to have the Shent Malleability property.

Success on a [[/skill history 13]][[/skillCheck society 13]] check, [[/knowledge shent]], or [[/knowledge ancients]] helps you to identify the item as a vestige of the Shent, a society of giantkin and other humanoids who lived in harmonious prosperity thanks to their innovations in lunar magic and arcane artifice.

  • [[/knowledge legends]] You wonder if the filigree on the armor and equipment of the dead giants might be the insignia of the "Sealers of the Gate", a proud alliance of Shent mage-sentinels who presided over various arcane thresholds throughout Ember.

An inspection using [[/knowledge forensics]] or a [[/skill investigation 13]][[/skillCheck medicine 13]] check provides evidence that — based on wounds visible on the skeletal cadavers or damage to their equipment — the giants who perished here did so beneath the fangs of much larger versions of the crystal spiders you encountered today.

Cheliceraeth Ambush

Three @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J]{young cheliceraeth} lay in wait here disguised as medium-sized outcroppings of crystals. Combat here is inevitable. However, the party may be able to avoid a surprise attack by the trio of crystal spiders if they successfully navigate the area without disturbing the webs.

Crouching Spider, Hidden Chelicerath

The @UUID[Macro.vdaqykaKUICstUDE]{Toggle Cheliceraeth} macro allows you to reveal hidden Cheliceraeth. To use this macro, select the Chelicerath tokens on the scene, and activate the macro by clicking on it in this dialog, or in the macro hot bar at the bottom of your screen.

It will change the crystal spiders from their hidden to active appearance and vice versa.

@Embed[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J count=3]

Ambush!

The spiders are perfectly concealed by their @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J.Item.PIhVKMYm42RWdZRx] @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J.Item.falseAppearance0] trait and cannot be detected unless they move. Once they begin to move, they can be identified by characters with [[/skill perception 15 passive format=long]][[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]]. Characters who do not detect the cheliceraeth before they attack begin the ensuing combat encounter with the &Reference[surprised] @Condition[unaware] condition.

Cheliceraeth Tactics

Once engaged they will use their bonus action @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J.Item.LmMaaO9BTbNnmFQL]{Bewildering Gaze} to debilitate an opponent before attacking them. Cheliceraeth prefer attacking bewildered or restrained targets when possible, using their @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J.Item.h4GQvtF4ZpfcWR2q]{Bite} attack to subdue the target.

If badly wounded, the Cheliceraeth will seek to use @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J.Item.hM0xr7yYbxxZzHEv]{Spider Climb} to climb away from danger and hide among the crystals.

Once engaged, the cheliceraeth are intelligent enough to use their own webs as a defensive mechanism, moving through them without penalty where other creatures may become @Condition[restrained].

At range, they will fixate their @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J.Item.bewilderingGaze0] upon prey to render them @Condition[confused] before closing into melee range and subduing them completely with @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J.Item.venomousBite0000].

If their morale is @Condition[broken] they will attempt to flee, climbing the cavern walls to escape danger and hide among the crystals.

After the fight with the Cheliceraeth concludes, the party notices the corpse of a much larger Chaliceraeth underfoot. Read or paraphrase the following:

You can't help but wonder what could be responsible for all of the glittering webs in this cavern, considering the crystal spiders you just encountered weren't seen spinning webs of their own. That's when you notice the long-dead carcass of what must have been a huge-sized specimen of crystal spider, twinkling egg sacs infesting each recess of its rotted gemstone cadaver.

After the battle or during the fray, characters may be able to recall certain details about young cheliceraeth and their kin — including elder cheliceraeth and other spiders:

Regarding Cheliceraeth

Characters who have [[/knowledge legends]], [[/knowledge abyssals]], or who succeed on a [[/skill history 13]][[/skillCheck arcana 13 passive]] check are familiar with legends of the Spider Goddess, known as "The Watcher", who is responsible for the creation of all true spiders on Ember. All manner of spiders populate the living planet, and these cheliceraeth must be among the most primordial.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success or [[/knowledge rituals]] - You know the Spider Goddess is revered throughout Ember by clandestine cults of warlocks and sorcerous acolytes. She goes by several names, from "The Watcher" to the "Eyes in the Dark," and her worshippers are often allied with spiders and their arachnid kin.

  • [[/knowledge abyssals]] or [[/attunement abyss]] - You know another name for "The Watcher" — Sitheera — an Outer God who brought about the advent of true spiders during the Abyssal Shear. Sitheera's chosen speak of her monstrous feminine form — the grotesque beauty of her flowing hair made of spider's legs, and the dominating golden-green majesty of her ten glittering eyes.

Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] or who succeed on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check understand that cheliceraeth are native inhabitants of the planet's subterranea, particularly where crystals enchanted by Ember's heartblood are known to grow in larger quantities. Compared to other giant spiders, they are rarely (if ever) seen on the world's surface.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success or [[/knowledge monsters]] - You know that large- and huge-sized specimens of cheliceraeth have been documented by celebrated explorers of Ember's Pathways. These elder cheliceraeth are known to possess a potent venom and the ability to spin webs in combat. Some of the oldest specimens are rumored to be intelligent beyond normal measure, and blessed with arcane abilities greater than the bewildering gaze encountered here.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has collected the treasures here and dispatched or escaped the ambush they can proceed onward, deeper into the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} toward the ancient exit gate found in [[/eventState windingTrailNorth2]].
The Glint of Gossamer.soverview: As the party navigates a maze-like expanse of tunnels they notice the growing presence of glimmering webs. Knowing they are near to the remains Mioroth told them about, they must survive an ambush by crystal spiders, before they can claim their prize.
The Glint of Gossamer.sexposition: Your journey through the crystal-laced Kaleidoscope Caverns is slowed somewhat as you notice the growing presence of glittering webs stretching across columns of stone and crystal. Mioroth's words, his hint to watch for "the glint of gossamer" when searching for the fallen Shent Seer ring in your ears.
The Glint of Gossamer.ssummary: We encountered a menacing trio of crystal spiders while navigating the bewitching depths of the Kaleidoscope Caverns and searching for the remains of a long-dead Shent seer.

An Ancient Door.name: An Ancient Door
An Ancient Door.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party's progress is blocked by a massive Shent-constructed gateway in the cliffside that has been sealed for millenia. Finding an alternate route to Helkas via the northern pass will require the party to discern means of opening this gateway. In this event, the characters can:

  • Learn some additional lore about the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}.

  • Open a sealed gateway into a previously unexplored section of the Forest of Stone.

  • Make use of an important clue learned during [[/eventState windingTrailMoonstone]].

Examining the Area

Beside the door and some signs of recent activity, there isn’t much to find. However, a keen-eyed party should be able to piece together how to open the door if they explore for a bit.

The Surrounding Area

A character with [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or with a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notes that there is survey equipment and supplies gathered nearby. This equipment is in good order and looks relatively new. This, plus the banner makes it clear that this location has seen recent activity and study.

Characters with the backgrounds [[/culture emberArcturian]] or [[/culture emberOrdani]] or with a successful a [[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check know that the banner belongs to the Anachraenum.

The Anachraenum is an order of adventurer-historians that operate all over the region, and are based out of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}. They are an association of adventurers, explorers, scouts and scholars that travel throughout the region hunting for treasures, secrets, and remnants of the ancient civilizations that once occupied the region. The guild is mostly made up of teams that take jobs and tasks together, or freelance agents that handle things solo.

  • If the party has already encountered the banner in [[/eventState overMoonCurious]] or if they've met the Fulgurite Blades in [[/eventState overMoonLightning]] the banner can be recognized without any required check.

Studying the area with a successful[[/skill survival 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check it is possible to identify the distinct footsteps of at least four different people in the area in the last few days. The trail heads off to the south. There's another group in the area, likely camped nearby.

Several old markers, remnants of decorative structures, and sections of collapsed wall provide context clues about the cycles of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}, the flow of the seas, and the rise and fall of oceans—all under the moon. These markers lie scattered around the edges of the camp.

Studying the Door

Examination with a successful[[/skill history 12]] [[/skillCheck society 12]] check allows you to determine various things based on the result.

  • Success: The architectural style, weathered as it is, mark it as a relic of the Shent, an ancient culture of giants which collapsed after The Shattering. Though much of the structure's face has been worn away, there are aspects of the edifice around the edges that represent multiple moons and constellations in arrays, as though the wall was tracking the passage of the moon.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: It is clear that Mayis is a central aspect of this door. The core aspects of the supporting iconography are focused entirely on Mayis, and how the other moons relate to its past and future.

A successful [[/skill religion 12]] [[/skillCheck science 12]] check while studying the imagery of the door lets a character interpret the symbolism or meaning of the reliefs and inscriptions which cover the ruins.

  • Success You notice a strong theme of reverence towards the moons, with the water moon, Mayis, most prominent among them. The specific focus on Mayis feel especially significant, with several barely decipherable symbols indicating worship, reverence, or unity. Perhaps it is indicative of the presence of a site of worship beyond this door?

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: There have been modifications made to this door's imagery that evoke more significant aspects of past and future, uncertainty and hope for what is to come. While still old, they were added after the door was made.

A successful[[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] while studying the various magical inscriptions in the gate itself yields the following knowledge.

  • Success: There is extensive transmutation magic to fuse the stone to the canyon walls, abjuration to keep the stone protected, and divination magic inscribed into the door's magical runes that is capable of deciphering speech, indicating there is a spoken command word or phrase needed to open the door.

  • Result of 18+: Examining the runes on the door you can see that there are a large number of seemingly disconnected divination and transmutation runes relating to the future and fate which don't have any specific use. They appear to be decorative, yet they were added alongside the other magic runes which are connected and idly awaiting activation.

  • A character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify} spell on the door gains information equivalent to a 18+ result.

  • A character casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} on the door will note that the stone is heavily reinforced with numerous forms of magic including transmutation and abjuration. On top of that the divination magic is waiting for an activation phrase, at which point further transmutation magic will free the door to open.

  • Success: There is extensive transmutation magic to fuse the stone to the canyon walls, abjuration to keep the stone protected, and divination magic inscribed into the door's magical runes that is capable of deciphering speech, indicating there is a spoken command word or phrase needed to open the door.

  • Critical Success: Examining the runes on the door you can see that there are a large number of seemingly disconnected divination and transmutation runes relating to the future and fate which don't have any specific use. They appear to be decorative, yet they were added alongside the other magic runes which are connected and idly awaiting activation.

  • Use of the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] talent gains the equivalent of a critical success. In addition, the character will note that the stone is heavily reinforced with numerous forms of magic including transmutation and abjuration. On top of that the divination magic is waiting for an activation phrase, at which point further transmutation magic will free the door to open.

The correct passphrase to open the great door is "fate of the moons", spoken aloud. The language doesn't matter, as the door itself has divination magic meant to parse word and intent.

Failing Forward

It's All There

If the party is struggling, consider allowing [[/check intelligence 12]] [[/skillCheck society 12]] checks to to piece together the meaning. Of course, if they decoded the passphrase from the ancient moonstone earlier, they already know what they need to say.

Outside Help

External help can be used to get past the door as well:

  • The @UUID[Item.2NsZVnU1qQaC2vmo]{Merchant's Messenger} can be used to contact the caravan, allowing the party to speak to either Lyla or Clipper to get help, since they both looked at the ancient moonstone and probably remember the inscription.

  • The Fulgurite Blades who camp nearby (see the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon] quest) have a shared interest in opening the passage. Their leader, Sajor, has already figured out the passphrase, but she is waiting for her team to finish some studies around her camp before moving forward.

Caravan Assistance

Speaking to the caravan allows Lyla and Clipper to quote the stone to the party, and in this, the core pass-phrase is contained:

… shadows end by spear restrained and sealed to never rise again. Let only those who understand the fate of the moons walk its path.

Further discussion of the door and what's been found may lead them to point out:

It seems like the pass phrase is focused on the moon and its fate… and "fate of the moons" is in the old passage. Maybe try that?

Fulgurite Blade Assistance

Speaking with the Fulgurite Blades, allows the party to get the passphrase through social means rather than exploration. This requires speaking with them at their camp, or at the doors, if you prefer to have them actively exploring.

While meeting with @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu]{Sajor}, a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check causes you to notice that Sajor knows more than she's letting on. You suspect she may already have the answer, and is curious to see if you also figure it out.

  • [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15]] You can trick Sajor into revealing the solution to the puzzle. There are many ways to approach this, but for example the party might imply that they have figured it out and wish to test whether Sajor also knows the solution. On a failure Sajor is not impressed, but on success, she finds it quite funny that she was tricked into giving up the answer.

  • [[/skill intimidation 14]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 14]] You can intimidate Sajor to reveal the solution. On a failure Sajor is very unimpressed and will refuse to assist the party further. On a success Sajor will open the door and begrudgingly apologize for wasting time.

  • [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck persuasion 14]] You can persuade Sajor to reveal the answer to the puzzle. There are several valid ways to approach this. On success Sajor is disappointed you didn't figure it out, but agrees to help. On failure, she is unimpressed with the party's inability to figure things out, but reveals the answer anyway.

Opening the Gate

If the party successfully opens the gate, mark the outcome as complete and read the following aloud:

[[/outcome opened]]

A sudden, low hum vibrates through the ground as if something deep within the stone itself has awoken. You can see the intricate inscriptions on the gate begin to glow with a soft, silvery light, casting eerie patterns on the damp, moss-covered stones around you.

Slowly, the gate starts to move. The massive stone doors, despite their age and size, part with surprising ease, revealing a verdant, wild misty region beyond.

Vista Composition

The vista composition can be swapped to "Ancient Shent Door (Open)" at this time.

Signara Attunement: Uttering the Passphrase

The first character to successfully open the Ancient Door by uttering the passphrase advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 windingTrailNorthPassphrase]].

Concluding the Event

The party can now move forward, advancing to explore the area beyond.

Next Steps

With the door new open, the party can search this area of the Forest of Stone for an alternate route through to Helkas.

In order to make it through to Helkas they must travel through this area to the sibling southern gate which can be opened in the [[/eventState windingTrailNorth2]] event.
An Ancient Door.soverview: The party encounters an ancient Shent gateway, inlaid with arcane runes and lunar insignia. The closed gateway blocks further progress unless it can be opened.
An Ancient Door.sexposition:
The face of this doorway has witnessed centuries, perhaps millennia, of wear. Constant dripping of water from above cascades down small grooves and channels in the stone around it or is carried by encroaching plants. You can see signs of once vibrant colors, now dulled beneath years of unforgiving sunlight.

A dark crescent arcs over the swirling pattern of the central frame and bears glyphs of writing that are nearly indecipherable from years of exposure. Inset within the face of the door are seven large circular crystals. The largest crystal is a dull blue, while the remaining smaller orbs exhibit an array of faded colors: orange, pink, purple, red, yellow, and green. These crystals, like all else here, have lost their shimmer due to layers of wear and encroaching moss.

This design is bordered by two substantial rectangular columns made from alternating sandstone and granite, topped with a broad arch decorated with six badly eroded figures, each holding something resembling a staff or perhaps a weapon.

Half stuck in the dirt and leaning against the stone unattended is a pole with a banner bearing the symbol of the Anachraenum.
An Ancient Door.ssummary: We encountered a great Shent gateway which bars passage to the canyons beyond. It appears that someone was already in the process of investigating it, and we found an Anachraenum banner nearby.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This is the first Main Quest in Ember and serves as both a prologue and tutorial for the rest of the game.

Difficulty

"The Winding Trail" is designed for a party of Level 1 characters, who will advance to Level 2 by the time the quest is completed.

Milestone Progression

This is a Main Quest that awards 3 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the Events [[/eventState windingTrailCairn]], [[/eventState windingTrailArrival]], and [[/eventState windingTrailLeavetaking]].

Tutorial Experience

Some of the Events at the beginning of this quest are scripted and have been designed to incrementally teach players (and the Gamemaster) about Ember's various game systems. Early on, the scope of choices that players can make is somewhat limited, but this scope will gradually broaden until the players have full control over their open-world exploration.

At the beginning of the game, the party is not allowed to control the location of the Strayhearth Caravan on the Region Map. Instead, the first three Events of this quest follow a pre-established route until the party is given autonomy to begin exploration on their own.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} region has been a peaceful, rich, and welcoming land for hundreds of years, and large-scale conflicts or especially dangerous monsters have been rarely encountered. Recently, however, the region has begun experiencing upheavals and changes that have upset the status quo, and though life continues, a subtle unease and fear has begun taking root among communities and travelers. As the caravans that follow a long, winding, triangular route from the three major cities of Casla-Brava, Toraga, and Ordain continue their paths as they have always done, they have begun hiring capable adventurers and guards to protect them, just in case.

While the party is not yet aware of it, these caravans have every right to be worried as the grand machinations of the distant megalomaniac dragon Zerranyss advance and his decades-long plot to conquer the region and become its undisputed ruler unfolds. His followers and minions, some of whom are aware of deeper plans and some who are merely pawns, have become bolder and more eager to cause chaos and disruption.

A small group of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune} plots to attack the Dusktide Festival taking place in @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}, keen to steal the valuable goods and resources gathered for the event and use them to further their ends. Accompanied by sickly draconic experiments from one of Zerranyss's laboratories, the town is in great danger, and the clock has begun ticking.

Should the party become waylaid as they resolve or explore the side passages to the north and south of the main trail, there could be dire consequences for the town and a sign of the chaos that will inevitably unfold as the story continues.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]

  • @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]

  • @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]

  • @UUID[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9]

  • @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]

Overview.soverview: The story begins as the party travels with a merchant caravan through the winding ravines of the Forest of Stone. The caravan is bound for the small mining town of Helkas, bearing goods and services for the upcoming Dusktide Lunar Festival. After the collapse of a rocky spire blocks the caravan's path, the party must explore the region's winding pathways to chart a new course through the Forest of Stone.

Sheltered Campsite.name: Sheltered Campsite
Sheltered Campsite.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is the first Event of the Ember @UUID[JournalEntry.emberGameGuide00.JournalEntryPage.Ajl2mEpagPebOYJx]{Main Quest} storyline. It is currently 10:00pm on Day 0, and the story begins with a campfire tale that introduces some of Ember's lore and history. In this Event, the characters can:

  • Learn about @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering}, a major event in Ember's past.

  • Learn about @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon}, one of Ember's moons.

  • Meet @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} and @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}.

  • Understand the caravan's current objective: to reach the town of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}.

Setting the Scene

Every gameplay Event in Ember begins with an opening passage called "Setting the Scene." Blocks of text displayed in this style are called "readalouds" and are intended to be narrated aloud by the Gamemaster. Begin every Event by narrating the "Setting the Scene" text before activating and continuing with the remaining details of the Event.

Vistas

As part of this Event, players are introduced to the first @UUID[JournalEntry.emberGameGuide00.JournalEntryPage.U7QcWsGAbENffGAk]{Vista}, a special type of environment used for storytelling and social interaction. This Vista depicts the caravan's campsite in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} Biome of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.TB9sbU2LNziZKZWD]{Forest of Stone}. Let the players know that they can navigate the Vista by right clicking and dragging to pan the view of the scene.

Time Progression

Time progression is an important mechanic in Ember. At the top of the screen is a clock and calendar display that tells you the current time. Certain moments of gameplay will only occur at certain times, and actions you take throughout the world will cause time to advance with meaningful consequences. Encourage your players to take note of the current time (10:00pm on Day 0) and be aware that time progression will matter for the gameplay that they experience.

Meeting Companions

It is vital for the party to get introduced to the various traveling companions in the Strayhearth Caravan. These will be important recurring characters that appear throughout the game, so these initial introductions are essential for the story.

In order to avoid overloading the players with new information all at once, we have designed the first Events of the game to provide an opportunity to meet and converse with these companions one at a time.

  • In this Event, the party has an opportunity to talk with @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} and @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}.

  • In the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.lyrnScnD7RrvLO8a]{Giant Moonstone} Event, the party can chat with @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]{Clipper} and @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher}.

  • In the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.juhlMw4Q80puImhj]{Skies Above} Event, the party can spend time getting to know @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}.

We recommend you portray characters who aren't the subject of focus for a particular Event as being occupied with other duties at any given point in time. However, if the party is determined to meet everyone now, those character introductions can be pulled forward from later Events to occur here instead.

Player Character Motivations

If the players have yet to do so, they should determine precisely how or why their characters are traveling with the Strayhearth Caravan to Helkas, as described in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.UJLt0kE0pFZlUkJQ]{Character Creation} section of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide]{Players' Guide}.

The Caravanner's Tale

The Strayhearth Caravan consists of three massive six-wheeled wagons, a huge @UUID[Actor.6HckJyV8TKc37xNT]{Yarnac}, and various @UUID[Actor.QGpM0XLtyG7zN76l]{Rask} that serve the convoy as beasts of burden. The caravanner @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} owns and operates the enterprise with the assistance of the Signborn merchant @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]{Clipper} and a small cohort of passengers — mostly merchants or travelers — who are along for the ride.

Some of these passengers are gathered around the fire, the most remarkable of whom are a trio named @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}, @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher}, and @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}. Each is traveling toward Ordain with the Strayhearth caravan for reasons of their own.

The game begins as the wizened caravan leader, Agraband Swift, entertains the company with the telling of a campfire tale that introduces an important moment in Ember's history.

@Embed[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]

With practiced bravado, Agraband gestures toward the strange slab of rock and says:
