"Ah yes, a fragment of Akon. Can you imagine such a place when it was whole? Think of where this came from, and the enormity of events that caused its plummet to this terrestrial soil. I'm sure you all know the tale, but please sit a moment and perhaps I might weave it upon your memories anew?"

Once everyone is settled in and paying attention, Agraband begins, his voice filled with dramatic gravitas befitting the start of a grand tale.

"Long ago, the Heart of Ember, the source of creation and life, assembled the first and most-ancient pieces of our home: the world that formed around the Heart and the elemental moons which traverse the sky. Attracted by Ember's power like a spark in the darkness, the Abyss closed in swiftly to devour our fledgling realm."

"But the Heart fashioned the protective barrier of the Weave to shelter us, and no matter how desperately the Abyss clawed at it, the Weave kept us safe from the terrors beyond."

With that, Agraband gestures up to the sky and the glittering stars.

"Within our safe enclosure, Ember grew wild and ever-changing. While the Weave shielded us from threats beyond, it did not protect us from within."

"A misguided and arrogant people, at the apex of their empire's power, sought to prove themselves masters of Ember. They built a colossal tower grasping ever-higher to harness the light of Lantyr and the power of the Weave itself."

Agraband's arm stretches up, fingers just falling beyond the light of the fire.

"All of Ember shared the punishment their hubris wrought — and when the tower was broken, the moon of Akon shattered, and the Weave itself was rent asunder."

With a sudden downward motion, Agraband snuffs out the fire before him, plunging the camp into a heart-stopping darkness.

"The Abyss rushed into our world."

In the gloom you swear you can see shapes moving around the camp. Some of the travelers nearby call out in alarm, while others assure them it's merely a trick from the bard, though even they don't sound fully convinced.

Agraband lets this unease settle among the audience before continuing. With a flourish, the flames light anew, driving back the shadows and gloom of the night.

"But all was not lost, for Ember had defenders, some of them quite unlikely. Even the mighty and terrible Alar stood alongside the other elder gods and rebuffed the Abyss. Alar repaired the Weave and prevented our annihilation."

"Not all could be saved, however, for Akon was broken beyond repair and from that shattered moon emerged dragons, clever and cruel. Banished from their home, they vanished into the mountains and pathways of Ember and hid until Alar's attention was needed elsewhere."

Agraband offers a cheeky smile.

"To this day, the dragons of old Akon prowl the lands of Ember, causing havoc as they please. But fear not, the Strayhearth Caravan is of no interest to such monsters, and we know well enough to steer clear of them!"

Agraband slowly lowers his arms, letting his final words linger in the quiet of the gently crackling campfire. He pauses and absorbs the rapt attention of the company, and with a smile says:

"… and now, friends, to rest, for tomorrow will be a long day's passage. If all goes well, we should make Helkas several days ahead of schedule!"

Chatting With Agraband

After the conclusion of Agraband's tale, the caravan members begin preparing to bed down and rest, but there is still enough activity about. For characters looking to socialize more, they will spot both Agraband and Ankarist standing together talking.

The Charming Caravanner

Agraband is a friendly, chatty, and gregarious sort, always happy to talk about something, especially if it's his stories and adventures.

Agraband was an adventurer in his youth, a bard once and still, and a caravanner now. If asked about his role in the caravan, he's all too happy to explain that he's the owner and operator of the Strayhearth Caravan and that most of the wagons and animals are his. He runs all sorts of different routes, usually based on what's selling and being sold.

Any character with a [[/skill insight 15 passive format=long]], or who makes a successful [[/skill insight 13]] check,[[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] perceives that Agraband seems genuinely proud of his caravan and the entrepreneurial success he has created for himself and his companions. Characters with [[/path emberCaravanner]] recognize that Agraband runs a tight operation and identify the telltale signs of a successful enterprise.

Your background?

A look of bittersweet remembrance crosses the old raconteur's face for a brief moment as he continues.

The story of my youth is painted with tragedy. And those ill-fated circumstances carried me from Ordain, where I was born, to a small village outside of Toraga in my adolescence. From there, I stowed away on a caravan headed to Casla-Brava, and I never stopped traveling. For many years now, I'm pleased to say, "home is where the 'Hearth is!"

Your trade?

I've run this particular trade route for decades — with a few side treks, of course. The three cities of Ordain, Toraga, and Casla-Brava form a triangular trade network that encourages the steady exchange of goods throughout the Plateau. And thanks to our stellar track record, Strayhearth has managed to turn a tidy profit along the way!

A glint in the bard's eye betrays his keen sense of pride.

The route?

The northern road we travel is a fortuitous one. We'll eventually make our way to Ordain on the eastern seaboard, but first, we'll visit Helkas and participate in the Dusktide celebrations there. You chose the right time to charter passage, my friends!

Helkas and Dusktide?

Helkas is a frontier mining town at the eastern edge of the Forest of Stone, where the Arctus Plateau opens up and stretches eastward as far as the eye can see. The people who live there are hearty folk, with good heads on their shoulders. And the mine itself is something rather special — formed from the inner reaches of an ossified leviathan.

The Dusktide festival is actually a celebration of the mine's bounty of arcane resources — peculiar substances which only seem to appear or manifest during the lunar conjunction. The whole plateau benefits from these rare materials. And this legendary celebration is not to be missed!

Allies in Ordain?

As you might imagine, I spend most of my time on the road. But I do have a few good friends and family members in the city. Well, one family member to be precise — my nephew Jorey. Truth be told, after the death of my sister Selena (the boy's mother), I haven't kept in touch with him nearly as much as I should. He's a headstrong young man, full of the old Swift bravado.

As far as friends go, my dear associate Fernis Ossa is one of the most intriguing people you could hope to meet. Her work for the Anachraenum is unrivaled. After all, you don't become the champion of the inaugural Expedition Challenge without knowing a thing or two about challenges and expeditions.

Characters in the party may have some prior knowledge or understanding about the Dusktide event.

Dusktide

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 14]][[/skillCheck science 14]] check understands that Dusktide is an occasion when the spirit moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis} and the water moon of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis} reach their zenith together. During this time, strange phenomena emerge: water tends to become unpredictable, rivers may flow backwards, faster, or slower, and the seas themselves may become as smooth as glass or hungry and treacherous.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge cosmology]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]][[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check knows that Orbis can be an unpredictable force, affecting both natural phenomena and people's emotions. Anyone attuned to Mayis or Orbis would be feeling especially sensitive to the upcoming cosmological zenith.

Characters with [[/attunement emberMayis]] or [[/attunement emberOrbis]] can feel the energy of the moons growing in them, creating a tumultuous ebb and flow of emotions in heart and mind. Though mild now, the sensation will grow stronger over time.

History of The Shattering

Ankarist and Agraband are discussing the nature of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering} and the particulars of Agraband's tale. Ankarist seems to be especially interested in the topic of dragons — perhaps in part because he is a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.GRs2vgeVsDpWPqjh]{Drakon}. Characters may join their conversation, or independently consider what they know about this legend.

History and Legend

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 12]] [[/skillCheck science 12]] check knows that The Shattering marks the year-zero from which dates in Ember are now written; it also signaled both the end of the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.o5o7MQGq9nVQlIaQ]{Age of Sunlight} and the demise of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir}, a hegemony which once spanned most of the known world.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The character recalls that historians believe the Aedir sought to build a tower so tall that they could ascend high enough to commune directly with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} and harness her power. During The Shattering, both this "Sun Tower" and the moon @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.3Oywe0peo57dQT9j]{Akon} were destroyed. It's believed that this cataclysmic event gave way to The Abyssal Shear, in which massive debris from the Sun Tower and Akon sundered @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{The Weave}, allowing the unknowable energy of the Abyss to enter the world.

Agraband may provide the party with the above information himself if asked. The bard is appreciative of inquisitive listeners and is eager to share more context with anyone who volunteers an attentive ear. After the party has had its fill of socializing and talking history with Agraband, they will be encouraged to pack up for the night and get some rest. The caravan has a long day ahead of it, and Agraband needs his rest as well.

Taking A Long Rest

Long Rest

When the party is ready to rest, you may click the Long RestRest button on the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party} sheet to recover resources and advance time to the following morning.

As night settles over the caravan, the last of the activity dies down, leaving you to sit in relative peace and quiet. Here and there lanterns glimmer in the dark, and sentries sit on watch, perched high on wagon seats, looking for trouble, but little else is happening worthy of note.

The Next Day

The Strayhearth Caravan is bustling with activity as everyone prepares for the day's travel ahead. A team of wagoners readies the caravan's trio of six-wheeled wagons, attaching a hulking yarnac to each of them with tack and bridle. Travelers vie for who will get to ride on one of the mounted seats today and who will walk alongside the wagons on foot. You consider yourselves lucky for managing to secure seating thus far with regularity.

As Agraband Swift passes your resting spot, he greets you with boisterous zest:

Be roused and ready, friends, for the winding trail beckons! We won't make it to Helkas tonight, but I know a place we can camp and stay dry. With any luck, we'll be in Helkas tomorrow — a full two days early!

Another voice calls out to the caravanner:

Agraband, have you got a moment?

Agraband is joined by the Drakon fellow you've come to know as Ankarist. He motions toward the massive shard of Akon you camped beneath last night.

I took your advice and looked at the shards of Akon once the sun rose. You weren't kidding about how different they look in the daylight.

Agraband nods in agreement with Ankarist.

Quite! All the texture and smaller elements get lost in the shadow of the evening.

The party may also be curious to inspect the strange fragment of rock said to have come from the moon of Akon.

The Fragment of Akon

If a character lays their hand upon this rock, they experience the following:

You sense a distant and subtle rhythmic pulse, like the ticking of a distant clock. It is difficult to tell whether it is something real, imagined, or merely the beating of your own heart.

This character gains @Advantage[2] to a skill check of their choosing made within the next 24 hours.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill religion 12]][[/skillCheck science 12]] check understands that Akon is one of Ember's primary cosmological forces which represents the fundamental concept of Order. Theologians believe that Akon's destruction has caused, or at least coincided with, significant change to Ember over the past two-thousand years.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 12]][[/skillCheck arcana 12]] check recalls that Akon was once the home of mythical and noble Wyrms before the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear} forced a terrible change upon them. This transformation, according to legend, was the origin of Dragons, which are terrible and formidable creatures.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 12]][[/skillCheck science 12]] check can tell that whatever mechanism once operated within this fragment of rock is broken and long-since defunct, its gears and machinery twisted and overrun by verdant growth.

Use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} spell confirms that no trace of magical aura remains upon the fragment.

Use of the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] talent confirms that no trace of magical aura remains upon the fragment.

Akon Attunement: Shard of Akon

Each character who successfully investigates the Fragment of Akon by touching the ruin and succeeding on one or more of the skill checks listed above advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 windingTrailCampsiteShard]] at the conclusion of the Event.

Meeting Ankarist

Having grown curious about the party's mutual interest (or lack thereof), Ankarist engages them in what may be one of their most meaningful conversations with the Drakon to date. If one or more characters investigated the Shard of Akon, read the following aloud:

The tall, two-horned shadow of Ankarist falls across your face, drawing your attention back to your Drakon traveling companion — who has approached your group with an unmistakable look of curiosity on his face. His smoky voice is tinged with an accent from the west, and he wastes no time with formalities.

I see you have a keen interest in the Shattered Moon as well. They say the wise and ancient Wyrms once tunneled beneath its surface, but now? It's rumored to be a broken, lifeless wasteland. Nevertheless, I feel a certain … harmony with this slab of meteoric rock.

Ankarist runs his hand over the massive lunar shard once more.

This cosmic attunement of ours is a strange thing, is it not? Tell me: what "harmony" have you managed to find in the world?

Alternately, if none of the characters approached the Shard of Akon for a closer inspection, read the following:

The tall, two-horned shadow of Ankarist falls across your face, drawing your attention back to your Drakon traveling companion — who has approached your group with an unmistakable look of judgement on his face. His smoky voice is tinged with an accent from the west, and he wastes no time with formalities.

I see the Shattered Moon is of little interest to you. I myself am drawn to it. I feel a certain … harmony with this slab of meteoric rock.

Ankarist runs his hand over the massive lunar Shard once more.

This cosmic attunement of ours is a strange thing, is it not? Tell me: what "harmony" have you managed to find in the world?

@Embed[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]

Music: Ankarist's Theme

Whilst Ember's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberGameGuide00.JournalEntryPage.di2EigjQlFTSQeiU]{Audio Engine} handles the majority of audio changes, there are some instances where the GM may wish to manually trigger a change in music mid-scene. In this instance, when the party first interacts with Ankarist, play his musical theme: [[/soundscape music ankaristTheme ankaristTheme]]

The Stoic Investigator

Ankarist initially appears serious, aloof, and reserved. He stands out as a Drakon, and keen-eyed characters can note an accent and mannerisms that betray his origins as a [[/culture emberTayan]]. If asked about this, he'll confirm the party's suspicions, noting he is a first-generation Drakon from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan} Empire — although he's lived in Ordain for the better part of a decade now. It should feel obvious to the party through these initial interactions that there is a lot more to Ankarist that isn't overtly apparent.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill insight 16]][[/skillCheck deception 16]] check gleans the following:

  • Despite his stoicism, Ankarist is being honest and doesn't harbor any ill intentions towards the caravan or the party. There are simply some (if not many) things he is not going to discuss with strangers.

  • Ankarist's line of questioning about attunement isn't merely an attempt to get to know them better as traveling companions: he's curious about what cosmological forces they're aligned with (and what that ultimately means for the safety of both Strayhearth and Ankarist's allies in Ordain).

[[/culture emberOrdani]] characters can guess that Ankarist is a member of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain}, an investigative arm of Ordain's government that provides protection, intelligence, and solutions to a wide range of legal or extralegal challenges.

Your story?

I reserve my anecdotes and remember-whens for persons far more familiar to me than yourselves. But know simply that I am both a public servant of Ordain and a warrior who is true to his word.

Your travel?

You can't help but notice that the Drakon's answer is a remarkably simple one:

I'm heading back to Ordain, where I work as an investigator for the Veiled Chain. New assignments promptly await my return.

Your investigations?

I can't rightly share any details about the various investigations I've conducted or assisted with. But rest assured that the Veiled Chain is involved with multiple investigations at any given point in time. Some of our cases await arbitration from the magistrates of the Hallows, while most are simply far too sensitive to discuss. I'm sure you understand.

The party may ask Ankarist directly more about his origins or history as a Drakon, and he is happy to share some information about his experiences.

About Drakon?

A rare grin twists its way across the investigator's face.

What? Did the horns give me away?

An instant later, his stoicism returns.

I know as much of my ancestry as anyone else, I suppose. The Drakon are a relatively young people, with much to learn about Ember's unforgiving environs. And our Human cousins have done a good job of helping us along the way.

The Drakon warrior glances toward Agraband Swift with a quick look of familial appreciation.

The Veiled Chain?

We are the eyes and ears of the Ordinate, Ordain's public body of leadership. When an incident needs investigating, the Veiled Chain is responsible for bringing those unknown answers to light. I've served the Chain for nearly a decade, and in that time I've seen many a curious deed.

Drakonic Heritage

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 14]][[/skillCheck society 14]] check knows that the Drakon are an exceptionally young ancestry, only having appeared a generation or two ago, with the bulk of the population coming out of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.bG3kuSiwqMnIHSrH]{Tayan Empire}. It is unknown precisely how they are connected to Dragons, and even Drakon themselves have no useful answers. All the same, the visual connection is striking and the mystery around it compelling.

  • [[/ancestry emberDrakon]] characters and [[/culture emberTayan]] characters automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill insight 16]][[/skillCheck deception 16]] check notes that Ankarist chooses his words carefully when answering questions about Drakon origins, but it is unclear whether the investigator is being tactful or evasive.

Music: Default

Once the party has finished this dialogue with Ankarist, return to the default music: [[/soundscape music reset]]

Concluding the Event

The caravan readies itself to depart at 8:00am on Day 1 and will depart as close to that time as possible. The party may ask for a brief delay, however, Agraband won't spare more than an hour.

Player Passengers

For the first several Events of this quest, the party is accompanying the Strayhearth Caravan and the players do not have control over its travel. The Caravan's goal is to travel to the settlement of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2], arriving by the end of Day 2. However, something will transpire that makes this impossible.

Next Steps

Click the "Complete Event" button at the bottom of the screen to conclude this Event and transition to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc]{Region Map}.

From the location where the caravan begins its journey, it will travel southward until it discovers the [[/eventState windingTrailMoonstone]] Event.

Manual Caravan Progression

We eventually envision that the Gamemaster will control the caravan's location indirectly by simply advancing the world time, causing the caravan to proceed automatically upon its scheduled route.

This system is not implemented yet, so for now you must move the Strayhearth Caravan token manually along its route as described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberGameGuide00.JournalEntryPage.FuaVOESpMunFr2TZ#the-strayhearth-caravan]{The Strayhearth Caravan}.
Sheltered Campsite.soverview: The party is part of the Strayhearth Caravan traveling from Casla-Brava towards the small mining town of Helkas, but is still several days away from the town at the outskirts of the Forest of Stone. As the caravan makes camp for the night, its leader, Agraband Swift, regales the company with tales of Ember's history.
Sheltered Campsite.sexposition:
A motley band of travelers is gathered around a softly crackling campfire, resting after the day's journey. You accompany the Strayhearth Caravan, a merchant convoy bound eastward to the great metropolis of Ordain from the small city of Casla-Brava to the west. To reach Ordain, you must pass through the Forest of Stone, a chaotic region of rocky paths, canyons, and crags that winds its way eastward toward the plains beyond. The next stop on your route is the frontier town of Helkas, which will soon host the Dusktide Festival, a rare and celebrated event for the Arcturians who live there.

You are still several days from Helkas, and tonight you camp amidst the untamed wilderness. Your company has made camp under a strange rocky shelf that offers some shelter. A jagged slab of twilight stone protrudes from a nearby cliffside, wedged and motionless, providing an overhang underneath which travelers might seek refuge. You can't help but notice that the slab's texture and color are inconsistent with the natural stone of the area. Embedded within its mass, you spy faintly visible relics of ancient clockwork — twisted and weathered by centuries of exposure to the elements.

It is evident that travelers often camp in this location. The soot-stained firepit and large logs assembled around it suggest this is a common stop for caravans following this route. Assembled around the fire are several intriguing companions who travel with the caravan, but at this moment all eyes are focused on a single figure standing beside the fire. The caravan leader, Agraband Swift, is a gregarious human with a worldly demeanor and twinkling eyes. You have traveled with him now for several days and find him to be pleasant and affable. As has become customary over the several nights of the journey, Agraband prepares to regale the company with a stirring tale of legend.
Sheltered Campsite.ssummary: We traveled with the Strayhearth Caravan from Casla-Brava towards Ordain. We rested at an unusual campsite in the Forest of Stone, underneath a broken fragment of Akon. Our caravan leader, Agraband Swift, told us the story of The Shattering which caused Akon to fracture and became the genesis of many perils.

The Collapsed Cairn.name: The Collapsed Cairn
The Collapsed Cairn.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration Event introduces a complication to the caravan's travel wherein the path through the Forest of Stone becomes blocked and an alternate route forward is needed. In this Event, the party can:

  • Witness a dangerous conflict between two large creatures.

  • Form a plan with @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband} for how to proceed.

  • Venture forth independently of the @UUID[Actor.emberStrayhearth]{Strayhearth Caravan} to begin exploring the region.

  • Acquire their first @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone} point.

Battling Behemoths

The caravan halts, entranced by the strange scene unfolding above.

The two huge creatures continue their mortal struggle for a time, slamming each other against the rock and fighting for purchase against the slick stone. With a colossal heave, the bird-like creature slams down upon the draconic one and both crash into the foundation of the tower.

In a bid to escape, the dragon weaves around the tower — but not fast enough. The great one-eyed bird fires a beam of golden-red light from its singular eye, directing it right into the dragon's face. Dazed, the dragon is helpless to the final attack of the bird, which slams it against the tower with such force that the whole thing breaks free of its base and begins to topple.

Region Map Transition

At this moment, mark the Spire Collapsed outcome of this Event as complete to trigger a transition on the Region Map and a sound effect audible for all players.

[[/outcome collapsed]]

The crashing of rock assaults your ears, and for a time you lose visibility of what is before you, but as the dust clears, the strange pale drake takes flight overhead and soars off into the eastern sky. Of the other winged creature, no sign remains.

As the caravan takes stock of its surroundings, you are dismayed to realize that the natural tunnel beneath the rock archway before you is now entirely blocked by fallen rubble.

It appears that the tower struck the archway during its collapse and careened over the far side of it. Great slabs of weathered stone and sections of the cliff face now fill the underpass, blocking all but the faintest glimmer of light from the far side and undeniably halting your progress.

Embattled Monstrosities

The party may quickly consider what they know about the two creatures whose battle just caused this catastrophic landslide.

A character who makes a successful [[/skill nature 13]][[/skillCheck medicine 13]] check knows that the feathered, one-eyed creature was a fully-grown @UUID[Actor.BQ0Ba1dNhQwg0zJM] — a deadly predator known for the potent alchemical properties of its singular monstrous eye.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge dragons]] or [[/knowledge monsters]] gain @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The reptilian creature that survived the battle was likely a @UUID[Actor.M9oc24iW3qI44GZe]{Pallid Drake} — a vicious kind of lesser dragon known to stalk and kill any creature large enough to serve as a live meal.

Surveying the Damage

The party can examine the blockage to get a sense of how bad it is and how much work it'll take to clear or bypass. At first glance, without any skill checks, the passage is completely blocked, and the approach into the natural tunnel — while wide enough for a caravan — is hemmed in by small rivers on either side, which narrow the approach into the mouth of the passage.

A Rock and a Hard Place

It is clear to everyone that while the collapse can be cleared by hand, it will be slow and difficult. All of the work will be done in a dark, narrow cave: the air will be choked with dust, the light will be scant, and the space insufficient to move debris.

The caravan doesn't have any particularly specialized tools which would make clearing the debris easier. The caravan can utilize the yarnac to move some of the heaviest slabs, but most of the debris will have to be arduously cleared by hand. If mentioned to Agraband, he says:

Yes, I noted that as well. I feel foolish for not having more practical equipment that could deal with a situation like this. We'll just have to make do with what we have now.

Getting Through

A character who makes a successful [[/skill survival 14]][[/skillCheck wilderness 12 passive]] check recognizes that attempting to climb over the rubble to get to the other side is going to be exceptionally difficult. If the wrong footholds and handholds are used, causing the debris to unexpectedly shift, it could become fatal. The only way to mitigate the danger is to spend hours carefully clearing the rubble.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] automatically succeed on this check.

If the party considers beginning that work, Lyla chimes in, saying:

I really don't recommend that. A fresh boulder fall like this is likely to shift on you suddenly. Clearing it will need careful planning and a lot of heavy lifting, especially since we don't have the proper tools. We do have the yarnac, but rigging them to clear this would take more time than we have.

Precarious Rubble

The rubble is impassable as it stands. If the party attempts to circumvent the blockage by climbing, burrowing, or digging through, Ankarist quickly shouts a warning to deter them from this foolish course.

Don't be reckless. We are not in such a rush that it's worth being crushed to death.

Characters who ignore this warning and attempt to traverse the rubble must succeed on three successive [[/skill athletics 25]] skill checks. Upon each failure, the character must make a [[/save strength 18]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 2d8 bludgeoning]] damage as rocks shift and threaten to pin them in place.

Characters who ignore this warning and attempt to traverse the rubble must succeed on three successive [[/skillCheck athletics 25]] skill checks. Upon each failure, the character may suffer damage as [[/hazard 12 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Shifting Rocks} threaten to pin them in place.

It is possible to turn back at any point and return to safety without any further checks. Any character who is killed or incapacitated by this damage can be extracted from the rubble at the expense of 1 hour of rescue time.

A Tight Squeeze

A Tiny or incorporeal creature may pass to the other side of the rubble unimpeded.

Digging Through

If the characters choose to stay and help clear the rubble, they can, though this will result in them missing the Side Quests in the region which are intended for Level 1 parties. If the players are on the fence, we suggest you encourage them to scout. If they speak to Agraband about it, there is 100 10gold pieces on offer for a scouting team willing to look for an alternate route.

If the party is determined to clear the rubble rather than scouting, mark this Event as complete and advance time by 1 hour to trigger the @UUID[.vE3DuDTTrBXkUJ6T] Event.

Finding Alternate Paths

Agraband curses his luck, but after assessing the situation, he is confident that the group can clear the rubble over the course of several days. However, that amount of time runs the risk of missing the Dusktide Festival at Helkas.

As the realization of what's happened makes its way through the caravan, more and more people begin to flock to Agraband to find out what's happening next — if he has a plan, if they'll be late, and so forth. Characters looking for updates or hoping to help will find their chance here by speaking with Agraband and the others in the caravan.

A Frustrated Caravanner

Agraband intends to keep the caravan parked where it is and put everyone to work clearing the rubble. Yes, he knows it may make them late, but it is the safer option. He laments that the collapse happened where it did, because this entrance is so narrow and difficult to work with.

Agraband explains:

Honestly, I don't know much about the rest of the region. I've been down this route more than once and know that the canyon opens up substantially on the other side of the collapse. So if we can get people to the other side — you, namely — that would make clearing things easier.

If you also clear a route there, I can send additional people to help, rather than cramming everyone into the collapse on this side.

So, what do you say? I'll hire you on as scouts for Strayhearth. A nice 100 gold pieces for you to split if you agree to go look for alternate routes to the other side of the collapse!

If the party would like to get the opinions and guidance of other characters, both Lyla and Clipper may have useful leads that could help direct the party.

Getting Some Help

@UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP] and @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ] have been listening to the conversation nearby. They each chime in with the following pieces of information:

Lyla mentions an active mine in the area:

If I recall correctly, House Cevher has a small stake in a mine to the south, part of a village called "Yakoshta." I've never been there myself, but — according to the most recent shipping reports — it should be active. If you can track them down, the folks at Yakoshta Mine might have tools or blasting materials we could use. Worth a try.

Clipper says they've heard about an expedition from the Anachraenum:

Last time I was in Ordain, I sold a few trinkets to a group of Anachraenum hopefuls. They were scheming up an expedition in the coming months to the northern reaches of the Forest of Stone, in search of ancient ruins. Maybe they're in the area and can lend us a hand! And maybe — just maybe — you can find some giant-sized treasure out there while you're looking!

Ankarist counts himself out:

The caravan needs organization and strong hands. I can provide them with both. Besides, I'm not one for wilderness survival and bushcraft. I'd simply slow you down. There's plenty to do here.

Sin chimes in about her immediate goals:

A few folks were injured by stray rocks and debris during the collapse. I'm going to make sure the people and animals here are tended to. We'll need both in good health to clear the rubble quickly and make it to Helkas on time.

Agraband is heartened to hear this, and says:

This is a fine start! We'll get to work on clearing the rubble, while our scouts investigate these leads and perhaps locate some assistance. If we're lucky, we'll make it to Helkas just in time for Dusktide!

Concluding the Event

If the party agrees to scout, Agraband and Clipper discuss and agree to provide the party with one half of a @UUID[Item.2NsZVnU1qQaC2vmo] which allows them to remain in occasional contact.

Agraband says that he will check in with the party at the end of each day, but encourages the party to check in whenever they have anything to report.

Matters of Punctuality

This event marks the point that the party becomes free to travel the surrounding area. While they can take however much time they want, their ultimate goal is to get to the other side of the blockage and get the caravan moving to Helkas. If the party takes too long, they will risk missing the Dusktide Festival.

The party should be made aware of this timing, as Agraband was careful to plan his route to arrive early. This means there's a fair bit of time to find a route to the other side of the blockage and get the caravan moving.

  • The party will be early for the festival if they arrive before 4:00pm on Day 5.

  • The party will be on time for the festival if they arrive on or after 4:00pm on Day 5 but before 12:00am on Day 6.

  • The party will be late for the festival if they arrive after 12:00am on Day 6.

Milestone

Upon completion of this event, the party gains their first Milestone Point. This is not sufficient for them to reach Level 2 yet, which requires them to earn 2 Milestone Points, but this is a good moment to communicate to the players what @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Progression} is and to reinforce the mechanics for how leveling up works in Ember.

Next Steps

Upon completing this Event, the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party} gains their own active group token on the Region Map, which allows the players to move independently of the Strayhearth Caravan.

It is intended for the characters to accept Agraband's proposal to scout for an alternate route. If they do this, they will need to backtrack and explore the other routes in the Verdant Pathways. Each of the two alternate paths has a Side Quest associated with it:

  • The southern route will lead to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl]{Ooze Control} Event, which will task the party with aiding the helpless people of Yakoshta Mine by fighting a cohort of frenzied, mutated oozes (and their misguided master).

  • The northern route will lead to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon} Event, which will allow the party to investigate the ruins of the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} giants and fight a lingering Abyssal evil (among other local threats).

As noted above in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.VzlG3TTOny9a5b1M#digging-through]{Digging Through}, the party can also choose to stay and clear the rubble. If they choose to do this, mark this Event as complete and advance time by 1 hour to trigger the [[/eventState windingTrailClear]] Event.
The Collapsed Cairn.soverview: In an unfortunate turn of events, the caravan's progress is halted by a giant pillar of rock that has collapsed into the ravine, blocking the path forward.
The Collapsed Cairn.sexposition:
The caravan trundles down an uneven path that is steadily being consumed on the southern edge by a swift-flowing river traveling in the same direction as the caravan. Up ahead, the ravine is joined by a huge arch of stone that extends into a shaded tunnel. Two immense gray towers stand guard on either side of the tunnel entrance, each impossibly old and unidentifiable from this distance.

Agraband calls out:

Once we're through the tunnel up ahead, we'll be in the home stretch. The lakes and rivers are beautiful! I know a spot we can stop for —

He trails off as the echoing sound of crashing rocks and monstrous roars draw your attention upward. Weaving between the towers, two massive creatures are locked in fierce combat. One is a bird-like beast with a menacing arced head and massive wings spread wide, while the other is a sinuous dragon, its pale scales gleaming with each movement.

Both weave through the air under their own power, though the dragon seems to be at a disadvantage, and quickly finds itself slammed against the vertical stone. It unleashes a pained roar which is cut short as the bird-like creature harries it relentlessly from the air.
The Collapsed Cairn.ssummary: Our continued passage through the Forest of Stone was suddenly halted when a ferocious conflict between two winged creatures caused a giant spire of stone to topple and block the ravine through which we were meant to travel. Agraband and the caravan have begun to clear the rubble, and he has asked us to backtrack and scout for an alternative path forward.

Sickly Drakelings.name: Sickly Drakelings
Sickly Drakelings.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is the first planned Combat Event of the adventure, and the first Event which takes place within an explorable @UUID[JournalEntry.emberGameGuide00.JournalEntryPage.en6a7GXVs2Xi2yXN]{Area Map}: the @UUID[Scene.emberForestedCli] Scene. In this Event, the party can:

  • Survive an ambush by dangerous and desperate @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki]{Mutated Pallid Drakelings}.

  • Learn that these creatures are afflicted by a mysterious sickness.

These drakelings are the first evidence the party will encounter of the malevolent influence of Zerranyss and his minions, foreshadowing the main conflict of the rest of the game. For more on the antagonists of this campaign, see @UUID[JournalEntry.emberGameGuide00.JournalEntryPage.AsbGEbLFLmozVEda]{The Villains}.

Drakeling Ambush

As the party backtracks from the halted Strayhearth Caravan and the collapsed cairn, they are ambushed by a trio of Pallid Drakelings amidst the @UUID[Scene.emberForestedCli].

@Embed[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki count=3]

Ambush!

Three @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki]{Mutated Pallid Drakelings} attack the party from concealed and elevated positions. One of the drakelings (on the ledge to the southeast of the party) is initially visible, while the other two to the west are lurking above in clefts in the stone.

Characters with a [[/check perception 13 passive format=long]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] are able to spot the drakelings before they attack. If no character spots the drakelings, the party is &Reference[surprise]{surprised} @Condition[unaware] at the start of combat.

Drakeling Tactics

These pallid drakelings are feral and deranged as a result of sickly experimentation which has left them &Reference[blinded], and they will fight to the death. The Blinded condition is partially offset by the drakelings' @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.QZs1kj18rk0sW5fY]{Blood Sense}, but this limitation in their senses is an important tactical edge for the party against a trio of otherwise dangerous foes.

They favor utilizing their Climb Speed to scale rocky surfaces that would otherwise be impassable or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.9tzB6KQDTIuw1FlZ]{Difficult Terrain}. From an advantageous perch, they will use either @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.5m7JGp8UNM3cOfSz]{Pouncing Bite} to engage vulnerable targets or @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.7lbgbSpk9B4WpE9G]{Acid Spit} to harass enemies from range.

These pallid drakelings are feral and deranged as a result of sickly experimentation which has left them @Condition[blinded], and they will fight to the death. The Blinded condition is partially offset by the drakelings' @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.bloodSense000000], but this limitation in their senses is an important tactical edge for the party against a trio of otherwise dangerous foes.

Tactically, they favor scaling rocky surfaces that would otherwise be impassable or difficult terrain. From an advantageous perch, they will use either @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.pouncingStrike00] to engage vulnerable targets or @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.noxiousSpit00000] to harass enemies from range.

Once the smoke clears, the characters can examine the bodies of these strange drakelings for evidence about their draconic nature and pustulant afflictions.

After the Battle

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill nature 13]][[/skillCheck wilderness 13 passive]] check notes that these creatures are not native to this region; they are an invasive species.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge dragons]] succeed on this check automatically.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill medicine 13]][[/skillCheck medicine 13 passive]] check recognizes that the pustules and lesions on the drakelings are the likely result of some kind of contagion, disease, or alchemical influence.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] succeeds on this check automatically, and can speculate that the affliction is probably the result of a chemical reaction.

Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] recognize that the creatures' pale skin and clouded eyes are reminiscent of the characteristics found on some creatures who live deep underground.

The party may also wish to examine the bodies of the drakelings and what might be salvaged from their corpses:

The Belly of the Beast

Characters with a [[/check perception 15 passive format=long]], or who make a successful [[/skill perception 13]] or [[/skill investigation 12]] check, will notice that one of the drakelings has a humanoid finger wedged between its back teeth.

Characters with [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] will notice that one of the drakelings has a humanoid finger wedged between its back teeth.

Investigating the finger turns up a badly damaged severed humanoid finger still wearing a @UUID[Item.jrwsTQ5IqAZQvMWc]{Simple Jeweled Ring}. It has no maker's mark or inscriptions, and is worth maybe 10 gold pieces to the right buyer.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After the conclusion of this Event, the party will have a choice about which direction to travel.

  • The northern route will lead the party toward the [[/eventState overMoonDoor]] Event and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon} Side Quest.

  • The southern route will lead the party toward the [[/eventState kaleidoscopeShimmeringDark]] Event and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl]{Ooze Control} Side Quest.
Sickly Drakelings.soverview: As the heroes backtrack from the stalled Strayhearth Caravan, they are ambushed by a trio of pallid drakelings.
Sickly Drakelings.sexposition:
You backtrack westward through the steep ravine toward the large clearing that you passed earlier. As you draw closer, you recognize some of the pink and fuchsia vegetation that dots the landscape, but something about the scene isn’t quite as you remember it — perhaps it's merely the change in perspective.

As you survey your surroundings looking for landmarks, a sudden guttural hissing noise just overhead startles you into action. You look up to see a pale, serpentine form with clawed forelimbs slink to the edge of the ravine and leap down upon you from the rocky outcropping above.
Sickly Drakelings.ssummary: We survived an ambush from three pale and sickly drakelings who attacked us from above as we passed through the winding corridors of the Verdant Paths. The creatures attacked with a feral ferocity and were ignorant of fear.

Clearing the Rubble.name: Clearing the Rubble
Clearing the Rubble.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

If the party decides to forego exploration, they may instead stay with the caravan to help clear the rubble. In this Exploration Event, the characters can:

  • Labor to help clear the rubble from the Collapsed Cairn, so the caravan might continue on its journey to Helkas unimpeded.

Discouraged Gameplay

This Event involves the party spending hours working to clear rubble. This is not the intended gameplay, as it results in the party never experiencing any of the Side Quests in the area. However, the party is not committed to this, and can always leave to explore at any time before resolving this Event. Bear in mind that they won't get any of the time spent clearing rubble back, and may find themselves incapable of arriving in Helkas in a timely manner as a result.

Agraband's Insistence

Agraband attempts to not-so-subtly encourage the party to go and explore rather than sticking with the caravan to clear rubble. However, the party is free to do as they like, and Agraband won't stop them.

You know, I do appreciate the fact you're willing to help here… but I really do think your time and energy would be better spent looking for a secondary route, or getting around to the other side of this blockage. We've got plenty of people to work the mess on this side, and more hands won't necessarily help.

Clearing the Rubble

Clearing the collapsed rubble requires a cumulative total of 48 hours of work, with the participants — caravan members and characters alike — taking grueling shifts of 16 hours' work each day, which incurs 1 level of &Reference[Exhaustion] which incurs the @Condition[exhausted] condition at the end of each workday.

The participants are allotted 8 hours to Long Rest time to Rest, which clears their Exhaustion if taken. If unaided by the party, the caravan will fully clear the rubble in three days, allowing them to arrive in Helkas just barely on time for the festival.

Working Faster

If the party remains behind at the site of the collapse, they can lend further aid to the process, enabling it to progress more rapidly.

Once per work shift, the party may undertake a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.rules.JournalEntry.0AGfrwZRzSG0vNKb.JournalEntryPage.OcHhrKKzffcVi03Q#group-checks]{Group Check}, applying their various skills to make the work go faster.

A Hard Day's Work

Characters select a skill check from the list that they will roll for the group check. No more than two members of the party may attempt the same skill check. If at least half the party (rounding up) succeeds on their respective checks, they reduce the total time needed to clear the rubble by 8 hours. Failure by the group provides no reduction in work time.

  • [[/skill athletics 14]] Your ability to climb and haul stone and move materials is invaluable, allowing the work to proceed at pace and get some of the largest pieces of stone moved.

  • [[/skill acrobatics 14]] You can navigate the most precarious parts of the collapse, surveying the rubble without causing unwanted collapses or getting hurt in the process. This helps plan out excavation for the coming days.

  • [[/skill investigation 14]] You can identify load-bearing rubble and avoid dangerous hazards in the work which could cause undue injury and delays if missed.

  • [[/skill nature 14]] Your knowledge of the qualities of local flora allows you to direct efforts to harvest lumber and vines that can be used to make the work easier.

  • [[/skill perception 14]] Your keen senses allow you to work in the gloom of the tunnel without being too badly hindered by the inconsistent lighting, constantly moving shadows, and endlessly churning dust.

  • [[/skill survival 14]] Your proficiency with natural hazards proves key in preparing the workers for the grueling task ahead. This knowledge helps in keeping the workers safe during the process of clearing the rubble.

  • [[/skill medicine 14]] Your knowledge of healing techniques and basic treatment allows you to keep injuries to a minimum, manage the health of the workers, and patch up any minor wounds that do occur.

  • [[/skill performance 14]] You help bolster and inspire the workers, raising their spirits and hopes so that they can tackle the work ahead with gusto.

Each work day, the party may undertake a Group Challenge to increase the effectiveness of that day's work.

Crucible WIP

This will eventually use the Crucible "Group Challenge" system which is not yet implemented. The following rules are temporary until the group challenge can be added.

A Hard Day's Work

Characters select a skill check from the list that they will roll for the group check. No more than two members of the party may attempt the same skill check. If at least half the party (rounding up) succeeds on their respective checks, they reduce the total time needed to clear the rubble by 8 hours. Failure by the group provides no reduction in work time.

  • [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] Your ability to climb and haul stone and move materials is invaluable, allowing the work to proceed at pace and get some of the largest pieces of stone moved.

  • [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] Your keen senses allow you to work in the gloom of the tunnel without being too badly hindered by the inconsistent lighting, constantly moving shadows, and endlessly churning dust.

  • [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] You can navigate the most precarious parts of the collapse, surveying the rubble without causing unwanted collapses or getting hurt in the process. This helps plan out excavation for the coming days.

  • [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] Your knowledge of the qualities of local flora allows you to direct efforts to harvest lumber and vines that can be used to make the work easier.

  • [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] Your knowledge of healing techniques and basic treatment allows you to keep injuries to a minimum, manage the health of the workers, and patch up any minor wounds that do occur.

  • [[/skillCheck science 14]] You can identify load-bearing rubble and avoid dangerous hazards in the work which could cause undue injury and delays if missed.

  • [[/skillCheck performance 14]] You help bolster and inspire the workers, raising their spirits and hopes so that they can tackle the work ahead with gusto.

Unless the party finds an alternate route around the rubble, the Strayhearth Caravan will stay put here until the rubble has been cleared.

Better Late Then Never

Taking the Time

If the party chooses to continue on this path and clear the rubble directly, then advance the clock as they work and rest.

The expected rate of time passage should allow the party to break through the blockage in the afternoon of Day 5, allowing them to arrive in Helkas by evening. If the party succeeds on enough of its skill checks to cut down the work time, they might be able to clear the blockage fast enough to make an early arrival, but this isn't guaranteed.

Region Map Transition

At this moment, mark the Rubble Cleared outcome of this Event complete to trigger a transition on the Region Map and remove the rubble blocking the caravan's path.

Over the next several days, the grueling task of clearing the passage unfolds. The entire ordeal is marked with darkness, sweat, and dust, each breath tasting of stone and grit.

Agraband works right alongside them, his smile never waning, his presence a comforting beacon in the chaos. The sounds of labor echo through the tunnel as the caravan members toil tirelessly, their voices occasionally breaking into song or laughter to keep spirits high.

As the final chunks of rubble are hauled away and the wagons are able to clear the tunnel, a cheer rises up, reverberating through the newly opened passage. The exhausted faces of the caravan members glow with relief and triumph; their collective effort has paid off.

Finally, with the path to Helkas open once more, the exhausted caravan begins to move. Wagons creak, wheels crunching over loose stones as the group slowly resumes its journey, albeit well behind schedule, and likely to miss the bulk of the festival.

Mayis Attunement: Clearing the Rubble

If the party chooses to stay with the Strayhearth Caravan to help clear the rubble, each character in the party advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 windingTrailClearRubble]].

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

With the rubble cleared, the exhausted caravan can continue on its way. The next step is to proceed directly to @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas} and the [[/eventState windingTrailArrival]] Event. The party arrives just in time for the Dusktide Festival, depicted in the [[/eventState windingTrailRevelry]] Event.
Clearing the Rubble.soverview: The party assists the Strayhearth Caravan with the difficult work of clearing the immense blockage caused by the collapsed cairn.
Clearing the Rubble.sexposition: A veritable hill of rubble and stone debris from the collapsed cairn looms before you in the darkness. The mass is stacked nearly twice as tall as the wagons of the caravan itself, easily reaching the ceiling of the naturally formed tunnel it's blocking. If the massive weight of the stone slabs is any indication, displacing this ruinous heap of rocks is going to take you many hours, if not days.
Clearing the Rubble.ssummary: It took the entire caravan days of work, but we managed to clear away the massive heap of rubble and stone that blocked our path after the cairn's untimely collapse. With any luck, we can still make it to Helkas for the closing ceremonies of the Dusktide Festival.

Arrival at Helkas.name: Arrival at Helkas
Arrival at Helkas.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration Event occurs when the party emerges from the winding corridors of the Forest of Stone and sees their destination in the distance, the town of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}. In this Event, the party can:

  • Determine whether they arrived in time for the Dusktide Festival.

  • Learn about the key architectural and historical features of Helkas.

Matters of Punctuality

When this Event begins, you should mark in the Event Outcomes section whether the party arrived early, on time, or late; if the party reached Helkas alone, mark that as well. The recorded outcome (or outcomes, if the party arrived alone) determines which subsequent Event occurs when the party reaches the town proper.

  • Mark Early Arrival if arriving before 4:00pm on Day 5.

  • Mark Timely Arrival if arriving at or after 4:00pm on Day 5 but before 12:00am on Day 6.

  • Mark Late Arrival if the party arrives later than 12:00am on Day 6.

  • Mark Arrived Alone if the party arrives without the Strayhearth Caravan.

Early or Timely Arrival

If the party has managed an Early or Timely Arrival, read or paraphrase the following:

As you draw closer, you can see that the Dusktide Festival is already in full swing: the town is dressed in banners and streamers, a riot of color that well accompanies the happy bustle of festivalgoers. The air is rich with the scent of wood fire and roasting foods. The energy in the caravan begins to shift toward excitement, eager anticipation washing away the weariness of the road's travel.

Agraband is happy to answer some questions about the festival or the town of Helkas that the party may have.

@Embed[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]

About Helkas?

Well, Helkas is the last stop for anyone heading into the Forest of Stone, and the first for anyone leaving it. It's a combination mining town and caravan hub. The folks there are decent, hard-working, and just the right amount of weird.

Mining operations?

Ah! Well, that'd be the great, big skeleton of the leviathan the town is built in and around. Miners are carving out marrow from its bones. Bit gruesome, but valuable from what I understand.

The Dusktide Festival?

Oh, I try to be here for it every cycle, if I can. There's games, gambling, music, and more. I've been to a lot of places, and attended plenty of Dusktide festivals, but not many places celebrate it as well. Dusktide is Helkas at its best, truly.

What Next?

Well, I'm going to spend a few days in Helkas, enjoy the festival, make some trades, get supplies, and see what goods are going where. After that? We'll be moving on to Ordain. You all should take some time to rest and relax, it's been a long road. Enjoy the festival! And if you want a ride to Ordain, you know who to ask!

The other NPCs in the caravan may also have opinions.

Ankarist about Helkas?

Ankarist seems to have already collected his thoughts into a specific checklist.

First, I've got a friend in town I want to drop in on. Then, I'm going to have myself a bath and get all my clothing cleaned. After that? Ordain.

Lyla about Helkas?

Lyla looks tired, but also relieved.

I am glad we're close. I've still have to get to Ordain, but it'll be nice to take a day or two to unwind after the Forest of Stone.

Sin about Helkas?

Sin is ebullient and obviously giddy to be arriving.

I've never been to a Dusktide festival! Oh, this is exciting… I wonder if there are any Sanguinaries in attendance!

Clipper will want the loaned magic item back, if the party hasn't already returned it.

The Merchant Messenger

@UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]{Clipper} will approach the party and request that they return the @UUID[Item.2NsZVnU1qQaC2vmo] which was provided during their traversal of the Forest of Stone.

I'd like my messenger coin back now, since we're about to arrive in town. Don't want to lose track of it and have to hunt you down or something.

They laugh heartily.

I'm kidding! I wouldn't hunt you down… I'd hire someone to do it for me. But seriously, magic coin back — please and thank you!

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill persuasion 18]][[/skillCheck diplomacy 18]] check can convince Clipper of the merits of letting the party hold on to it.

Achieving an Early Arrival reinforces the Ragen Attunement for each character in the party.

Ragen Attunement: Early Arrival

If the party has an Early Arrival to Helkas, each character in the party advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 windingTrailArrivalEarly]] at the conclusion of the Event.

Achieving a Timely Arrival reinforces the Akon Attunement for each character in the party.

Akon Attunement: Timely Arrival

If the party has a Timely Arrival to Helkas, each character in the party advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 windingTrailArrivalTimely]] at the conclusion of the Event.

Late Arrival

If the party comes in with a Late Arrival, continue the description with this text:

As you draw closer, you begin to realize something is amiss.

Helkas is burning.

The town is draped in smoke flowing from numerous large fires. The bright colors of banners and streamers meant to decorate the town are only barely visible through the haze. The air is thick with the acrid stench of burning wood and cloth, and you can see people running back and forth, some carrying buckets or helping others out of harm's way.

The energy in the caravan sours instantly as fear and anxiety takes hold, wiping away the giddy anticipation there just moments ago.

The caravan members all have opinions on what they are seeing, and what they intend to do, but none are willing to delay the caravan getting to Helkas. They'll talk as the caravan rushes toward the town.

Agraband on Helkas?

Agraband intends to rush the caravan into town.

Clearly, something horrible has happened. Likely the people there will need assistance — and supplies! The Strayhearth can offer both, and so help me, we will!

Ankarist on Helkas?

Ankarist's professional demeanor sets in, and he wants answers.

First thing's first, we need to find out what happened. Was this an attack? And if so, perpetrated by whom? We follow the facts and go from there.

Lyla on Helkas?

Lyla looks troubled by this, but unsurprised.

I'd heard that there were sporadic attacks and raids happening in the area. I hope this isn't another one of them. We need to get in there, help people, and get answers if we can.

Sin on Helkas?

Sin is concerned for the people, and wants to help.

We've got to help get those fires out and tend to the wounded. Every second matters here, so best not to waste any time.

Clipper will want the loaned magic item back, just to be safe, if the party hasn't already returned it.

The Merchant Messenger

@UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]{Clipper} requests that the party return the @UUID[Item.2NsZVnU1qQaC2vmo] which was provided during their traversal of the Forest of Stone.

Not sure what's waiting for us in Helkas, but I'd like that merchant messenger coin back, just in case I need it.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill persuasion 18]][[/skillCheck diplomacy 18]] check can convince Clipper of the merits of letting the party hold on to it.

Experiencing a Late Arrival reinforces the Aura Attunement for each character in the party.

Aura Attunement: Late Arrival

If the party has a Late Arrival to Helkas, each character in the party advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 windingTrailArrivalLate]] at the conclusion of the Event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party's arrival time has been recorded, they may proceed into the town itself. The Event which occurs depends on the timeliness of their arrival:

  • If the party arrives early or on time, they experience the [[/eventState windingTrailRevelry]] Event.

  • If the party arrives late, they experience the [[/eventState windingTrailDestruction]] Event.

  • If the party journeys to Helkas independently and arrives without Agraband Swift and the Strayhearth Caravan, be sure to mark the "Arrived Alone" outcome as well.

Milestone: Arrival at Helkas

Completing this Event awards a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}. If the party did not complete one of the other Chapter 1 Side Quests, this point is likely to advance them to Level 2.
Arrival at Helkas.soverview: The party reaches the outskirts of Helkas, having discovered a pathway through the Forest of Stone — but have they arrived in time for the Dusktide Festival?
Arrival at Helkas.sexposition:
Helkas sits on the horizon, and Agraband happily calls out:

Helkas is in view! We'll be there in less than half an hour!

A few scattered cheers go up from the trailing wagons. News and glimpses of the town immediately breathe life into the caravan. Spirits buoy and chatter breaks out across the vehicles as their long, eventful journey draws to its conclusion.
Arrival at Helkas.ssummary: We made it through the Forest of Stone despite its delays and dangers, and now the town of Helkas is visible in the distance.

Dusktide Revelry.name: Dusktide Revelry
Dusktide Revelry.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this Social and Exploration Event, the characters participate in the revelry of the Dusktide Festival, where they can enjoy a few moments of communal merriment. In this Event, the party can:

  • Learn various details about the mining town of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}, including its local culture, persons of significance, and locations of interest.

  • Engage with the numerous attractions the festival has to offer.

Progression of Time

Time advances by 30 minutes for each attraction that the party chooses to engage with. This represents both the amount of time spent on the attraction itself, as well as time spent socializing with nearby characters. If the party chooses to take a rest, partake in food and drink, or simply enjoy the spectacle of the festival itself, advance time by 1 or more hours as needed.

This Event ends when the clock hits midnight (12:00am on Day 6). After this time, the various attractions of the Dusktide Festival are no longer available to the characters.

Exploring the Festival

Stepping away from the caravan, Agraband makes a grand show of announcing the festival to the disembarking travelers:

There is no fun to be had like the Dusktide festival in Helkas! Go and explore. Spread around your coin. Eat, drink, and be merry! The festival goes until midnight — after that we'll observe the moons under lantern light and shared drinks.

Tomorrow's pursuits can wait. Tonight, we celebrate!

Friendly Pursuits

If the party checks in with the NPCs in the caravan, they will all give short updates on where they'll be and what they'll be doing. However, they decline any offers of company, preferring a chance to be apart from the caravan for a little bit after sharing a long road.

Agraband will be at @UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#folk-music]{Folk Music}.

I'm going to go check in with my people here, sort out some caravan business first. Once I'm done, though, I'm going to throw myself into the festival. Follow the music — that's where I'll be!

Ankarist will be at @UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#esoteric-wares]{Esoteric Wares}.

Well, I've got an old friend who is running a stall this year. I'm going to see if I can find her once I'm settled in. I'm sure we'll run into each other out there.

Clipper will be at @UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#high-striker]{High Striker}

I have a long-standing grudge to settle with a floating stone. This year, victory will be mine!

Lyla will be at @UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#palestone-blades]{Palestone Blades}

First stop is an inn for a room. Once I get situated, I'll check out the festival attractions, maybe play a game or something. I'll keep an eye out for you.

Sin will be at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#critters-and-cakes]{Critters And Cakes}

I'm with Lyla. I'm going to arrange lodging, then I'm going to see what sort of sweets and goodies the festival has!

As the group divides to pursue their various goals, the party's attention is immediately drawn to a nearby stage, where a performance has just begun.

Lunar Legerdemain

The applause and cheers are the first things to draw your attention, followed by flashes of light and plumes of colorful smoke. Upon a raised stage near the center of town, a pair of charismatic figures deftly direct the crowd's attention between their assistants' spectacles.

These illusory tricks are an elaborate blend of combined practical and magical effect: creatures that materialize above the crowd and appear to pounce before disintegrating into a shower of sparks, dazzling rays of color rocketed into the sky beneath trails of smoke, arcs of illusory lightning that spiderweb over your head slow enough to touch — the audience's excitement reaches a crescendo as the opening act comes to a close and a tall, slender fej man steps into view, dressed in fine clothing of gold and orange that matches his features.

Suddenly, an elegant human woman draped in layers of flowing creme-colored silk calls out from the center of the crowd with a booming, magically-enhanced voice:

Azir, I think we need some volunteers for our next trick! I shall pick one, and you choose the rest!

Upon the stage, Azir smiles and makes a show of looking out over the crowd with a hand held to his brow.

Very generous of you, Orrin. I do wonder who you've got your eye on. Surely you've already picked out your assistant!

Orrin chuckles and says:

But of course! I claim Helkas' stalwart leader, Sadri Zhalimorne!

With a flourish of her flowing silken sleeves the crowd parts around Orrin, revealing a gray-skinned Altyran woman who finds herself very much put on the spot. Undaunted, she steps up to the stage, waving to the crowd as it cheers for her.

Azir offers a deep bow to Sadri, addressing her and then the crowd:

Welcome to the stage, Magistrate! Now, then, I need a few volunteers to step up, and I am so notoriously choosy! Let's see who catches my eye…

A moment later, Azir's attention lands on you all, and the performers promptly offer you a spot on the stage. The surrounding crowd wastes no time, offering support for you through waves of cheers and claps.

Someone From The Audience

You should select 1-2 characters from the party to be taken up onto the stage. If no characters volunteer, Orrin and Azir will select the characters with the lowest [[/skill sleightofhand passive]][[/skillCheck performance 0 passive]].

Assessing the Performers

Orrin (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, she/her) and Azir (Neutral Good, Ordani Fej, he/him) are exceptionally friendly and competent performers that are old hands at guiding audience members. Their natural routine is for one to speak while the other sets up the assistants, making sure the crowd is engaged and the performers are ready.

Watching Sadri, you can tell that she is clearly out of her element on stage, but is a good sport and willing to do her best for the sake of the performance. If this is the first time the party has met her, she makes sure to introduce herself @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#chatting-with-sadri]{after the performance}.

Lunar Legerdemain

Characters are prompted to help Orrin and Azir juggle a collection of three glowing magical moons that are identical in size but are of varying weight. Over the course of the performance, Orrin and Azir begin juggling the moons between the characters with increasing speed.

Any character invited on stage can do their part by making a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 13]][[/skillCheck performance 13]] check to not drop the moons. In the event of a failed check, however, Orrin and Azir utilize magic to keep the moons in alignment, joking about the "unpredictable nature of the cosmos."

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success : This character's skillful display of juggling results in them being left with all three moons for a bit as Orrin and Azir explain the history of the Dusktide conjunction and how “Ember’s moons always move when and where they’re supposed to.”

  • If Sadri succeeds at the task, the crowd cheers for her with enthusiasm and encouragement.

  • If Sadri fails at the task, she does so quickly and to the great amusement of the crowd, but does so with grace.

Characters that take part are thanked at the end of the display, and leave the stage to generous applause from the crowd.

After the performance, Sadri approaches the party to introduce herself, recognizing that they are newcomers to town.

@Embed[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]

Chatting With Sadri

If the party took part in the onstage performance, Sadri says:

Well… that was something. Thank you for sharing the attention with me up there. I'm not bad with crowds, but that was certainly unexpected. You come in for the festival, or are you just passing through?

Sadri is happy to chat with the party for a bit, and welcomes them to Helkas. If they share the news of the events in the Forest of Stone, she'll express interest and excitement about what she learns.

If the party mentions the drakes:

I've been hearing reports of these creatures appearing in the area. The local hunters and trackers haven't had any direct run-ins yet, so we don't know anything about them really. You've single-handedly given us more information than we've collected in weeks.

Afterward, she offers them [[/award 10gp]] [[/award 1gp]] for providing the town with useful information.

I make sure that Helkas rewards those who help the town, and sharing what you've discovered in the Forest of Stone absolutely counts as helping. Now, then, I do have to be on my way. Welcome again to Helkas. Please enjoy yourselves!

From here, the party is free to explore additional festival attractions or the town of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt]{Helkas} itself.

Festival Attractions

Each of the five Strayhearth Caravan characters are associated with one of the following attractions. Each NPC uses their respective activity as an opportunity to showcase a facet of their skills and personality.

Available Activities

The festival takes place in the center of town, where an array of market stalls have been arranged for the duration of the festival.

@UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#folk-music]{Folk Music}

A space is being cleared for a music performance, with an ever-growing collection of musical instruments being assembled and tuned. A show is imminent there, and a small crowd is already gathering.

@UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#palestone-blades]{Palestone Blades}

A stall of targets and stacks of throwing knives sit alongside shelves of curious hand-carved trinkets. The attraction practically begs for a deft hand and keen eye to collect one if they can.

@UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#esoteric-wares]{Esoteric Wares}

A large sign declares the presence of strange wares and magical oddities for those with enough coin. The stall owner seems to be spending more time chatting with potential customers than actually selling things.

@UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#critters-and-cakes]{Critters & Cakes}

A pen of animals sits beside a stall bearing hand=made treats. A peculiar combination, but the townsfolk partaking appear delighted.

@UUID[.3v69BVdh1iVOVMvq#high-striker]{High Striker}

The barking of this stall's owner can be heard over the din of the crowd, challenging the brave and strong to try their might at a game of High Striker. A line of would-be challengers snakes from the stall and into the crowd.

Folk Music

A motley group of musicians — professional entertainers and folk minstrels alike — gather around with their various instruments to play Dusktide songs in the town center.

With his trademark emerald lute at his fingertips, the renowned bard Raxwell Smalls conducts this charming ragtag band of locals and visitors. As the band prepares to play, he calls out:

Come, take up an instrument if you know how! All are welcome! As are tips, if you fine folks like what you hear from us!

Taking up a weathered guitar from a rest nearby, Agraband Swift joins the band, chatting with them and preparing for a spirited performance. In anticipation of the impending entertainment, a lively audience forms, with all eyes on Raxwell and his motley crew.

Jam Session

Raxwell Smalls (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, he/him) is a handsome and powerfully charming bard with aster aspects, such as glowing emerald eyes and long-clawed fingertips, which he uses to strum his lute. He and the assorted performers are friendly, welcoming, and happy to discuss the finer points of music, life in Helkas and abroad, and more.

Characters who perform with the motley band may be given a share of the tips earned from the performance; if they do well, they are invited by Raxwell to perform again. After the third successive performance, however, Raxwell kindly asks the character to make room for someone new.

Playing the Crowd

If any of the PCs play instruments, they can join the performance and get a share of the tips that come in from the audience. Alternatively, less scrupulous characters might try to liberate unattended coin from onlookers.

Any character can contribute to the performance with a successful [[/skill performance 12]][[/skillCheck performance 12]] check, earning [[/award 4d8cp]] in tips after the show.

  • Result of 17+: The character's performance is so exemplary that the crowd's generosity is measured in silver, not copper; they instead earn [[/award 4d8sp]] in tips after the show.

  • Failure: Raxwell gives the character an encouraging smile and clasp on the shoulder before quietly asking them to step off the stage.

  • Critical Success: The character's performance is so exemplary that the crowd's generosity is measured in silver, not copper; they instead earn [[/award 4d8sp]] in tips after the show.

  • Failure: Raxwell gives the character an encouraging smile and clasp on the shoulder before quietly asking them to step off the stage.

Any unscrupulous character wishing to lift some coin from the distracted crowd can do so with a successful [[/skill "sleight of hand" 12]][[/skillCheck stealth 12]] check, lifting a few light purses and coming away with [[/award 4d8cp]].

  • Result of 17+: The character instead manages to cut some weightier purses, coming away with [[/award 4d8sp]].

  • Failure: The character is caught by the locals and thrown out of the crowd. Watchful eyes make sure they don't get a second chance at causing trouble.

  • Critical Success: The character instead manages to cut some weightier purses, coming away with [[/award 4d8sp]].

  • Failure: The character is caught by the locals and thrown out of the crowd. Watchful eyes make sure they don't get a second chance at causing trouble.

Palestone Blades

The stall before you is decked with little glowing carvings ranging from tiny Leviathan statues and local monsters to stylish jewelry and stone weapons. A ruddy brown Hulg'run stonecarver with a large pair of magnifying goggles strapped to their head sits hunched over a workbench. On the bench is a glimmering stone he is carefully whittling into some new objets d'art for the festival.

A small target range occupies an adjacent stall, the finely painted sign nearby declaring one copper piece buys five attempts at a bullseye, and three hits wins a palestone carving.
