Lyla Cevher is already present, throwing knives with exceptional skill, winning a palestone bracelet just as you approach. Catching sight of you, she tilts her head toward the targets.

Fancy a little knife-throwing? Hit three bullseyes and you get one of Padragon's pretty little carvings. And if you can beat me… I'll give you a gold piece.

D'arts and Crafts

Padragon Faeldspar (Neutral Good, Arcturian Hulg'run, he/him) is incapable of speech, instead communicating with common sign language or a small slate board on which he can scribble replies. If asked about his background:

Been working with palestone almost my whole life. Used to be a miner, now a carver.

If asked about his lack of a voice, he doesn't go into much detail:

Had a tough time in my early shaping years, decided silence was best for me.

Palestone Blades

Any character wishing to win a game of Palestone Blades may do so by making three successful [[/skill dexterity 12]][[/skillCheck athletics 12]] checks out of five attempts, winning a random palestone trinket (roll once on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} table).

Additionally, any character who takes Lyla up on her challenge will compete side-by-side with her. If they outscore her, they earn her hearty congratulations and [[/award 1gp]], as promised.

Esoteric Wares

A middle-aged Signborn peddler, draped in blues and purples stitched with patterns of silvery stars, stands before a cart full of curiosities, calling out to passing locals. A brightly painted sign declares "Esoteric Wares!" with a sub-line promising each item guaranteed to be magically enchanted.

The Ordani investigator Ankarist stands nearby, chatting with the peddler about her magical items and their origins between breaks to speak with customers. They chat like old friends. As you near the cart, her spiel is aimed at you directly:

Come, friends — you have the look of someone needing more magic in their lives! Peruse these strange and esoteric wares of mine! My prices are fair, and discounts await those with the moxie to claim them!

First Impressions

Velaria Velevestrian (Neutral Good, Arcturian Signborn, she/her) is a peddler of curios and magic items. She favors characters with confidence and presence.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill persuasion 16]][[/skillCheck diplomacy 16]] check is able to convince Velaria to offer them a 10% discount on her wares.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Familiar Faces

Speaking with Ankarist, he can provide some background:

Oh, I've known Velaria for years. We first met in Ordain in the markets. I was a young investigator who was very curious about where she finds her items, and she was frustratingly vague with her answers. It took us a while to warm up to each other.

Velaria backs up this story:

The stalwart investigator here was always so exceptionally curious about me! Always hounding me about the provenance of my items, and whether or not I had proper licenses — I tell you, I was convinced he had a crush on me by the way he was always hassling me. Alas, no, he just takes his job too seriously.

Esoteric Wares

In addition to a few noteworthy pieces of standard equipment (such as finely-crafted gaming sets, musical instruments, and scented @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCandle00000]{Candles}) @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.candle0000000000]{Candles}), Velaria has a small assortment of Common magic items for sale:

  • @UUID[Item.i8Mt6fIY0O0i7yAT]{Fisherman's Hook}

  • @UUID[Item.z6nYm7YuO2LMDXyw]{Mirror of Masking}

  • @UUID[Item.Ad6dGVm6Z2C5ynbO]{Sage's Pipe}

  • @UUID[Item.rYf1ZBDsScgPKq9Q]{Moon Ring}

  • @UUID[Item.B0SoY0AmoG6yuxdy]{Hunter's Spyglass}

  • @UUID[Item.i8Mt6fIY0O0i7yAT]{Fisherman's Hook}

  • @UUID[Item.z6nYm7YuO2LMDXyw]{Mirror of Masking}

  • @UUID[Item.Ad6dGVm6Z2C5ynbO]{Sage's Pipe}

  • @UUID[Item.rYf1ZBDsScgPKq9Q]{Moon Ring}

  • @UUID[Item.B0SoY0AmoG6yuxdy]{Hunter's Spyglass}

If the party members lack adequate funds, Velaria could be enticed to accept a trade for any valuable items the characters might have found during their exploration of the Forest of Stone.

Critters And Cakes

The setup here is an odd one: a stall offering both animal feed and decadent-looking, moon-shaped cake pops sitting beside a collection of animal pens. A hand-painted sign declares the availability of "Sweet Treats and Sweeter Critters."

Smoking a pipe from a perch on a well-worn stool, the stocky and wizened vrjnhar owner watches the animals with a small smile. Before them are a collection of expertly decorated treats each fashioned after the Dusktide moons: Mayis (the Water Moon), Ragen (the Fire Moon), and Orbis (the Dark Moon).

Already in the pens, Sin Marmot can be seen gleefully speaking with the docile critters and doing her level best to endear herself to them.

Sweet Keeper

Mishi Dolan (Neutral Good, Arcturian Vrjnhar, she/they) operates the stall. This laid-back confectioner is a long-time animal lover who works as a baker in Helkas.

I mostly run the stall for the local kids, but I know everyone loves cute animals and cake… even if they pretend they don't.

Critters and Crumbs

Admission to the Petting Zoo is [[/award -1cp]]. Animal feed is available for an additional [[/award -1cp]]; a single purchase provides a character with enough animal feed for the duration of their visit.

Treats meant for humanoids can also be acquired for [[/award -2cp]] each. The cake pops are sweet, moist, and delicious. The available options are the Water Moon Mayis, which is filled with a salted caramel, the Dark Moon Orbis, which is chocolatey and a little bitter, and the Fire Moon Ragen, a strong spiced cake.

Petting Zoo

Several furry beasts are contained in wooden pens here, including a Juvenile Carnelian Salamander, a trio of playful, friendly Oozes, a domesticated Beletor Cub, a double-headed Strainbird, and a fuzzy Mosshog.

The first character to make a successful [[/skill animalhandling 13]][[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check can befriend one of the animals and earn a free confection from Mishi.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

High Striker

Through the noise of the crowd, there's a bright chime, followed immediately by cheers and clapping. You quickly spot the source: a stall where contestants take turns swinging a wooden mallet against a calibrated lever to launch a magical lodestone into the air. A large sign with letters carved out of glowing palestone declares this game: High Striker.

The previous winner walks off with an oversized leviathan doll, and taking their spot is none other than Clipper. With a look of determination, they strike the plate and send the stone shooting upward, though not far enough. Clipper watches the enchanted stone silently descend back to the striking plate with obvious disappointment. Their ethereal arms droop and begin digging through the pockets of their bag in search of another copper piece.

Meanwhile, the burly fej barker with burning yellow eyes calls out over the din:

Come one, come all! Test your might and precision! Have you got what it takes to be a High Striker?

Heavy Hitter

Hode Cinderhaft (Neutral Good, Arcturian Fej, he/him) is a foreman of the Leviathan Mine. His High Striker stall has been a staple of the festival for as long as he's had the job; he pays for the whole setup out of pocket with no concern for making anything back. If asked, he's happy to demonstrate "how simple" the game is, conveniently ignoring the skill, practice, and physique he has as a veteran miner.

Eye On The Prize

Clipper is here attempting to win the prize with all their might, but can't quite manage it. A party member can help by winning the prize themselves. Doing so is worth nothing more than Clipper's endless gratitude, and the satisfaction of seeing them united with a giant stuffed leviathan that is equal parts adorable and monstrous.

Hammer Time

For each [[/award -1cp]] a character spends, they get a single chance to see how high they can launch a feather-falling lodestone using a heavy wooden mallet against a calibrated lever. The lightly-enchanted stone chimes and glows bright orange and emits a high-pitched tone when it reaches a height of 20 feet.

Any character can drive the enchanted lodestone high enough to chime with a successful [[/skill athletics 16]][[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check. A character who successfully chimes the stone is awarded an oversized Stuffed Leviathan Doll as a prize. Losers are swiftly encouraged to play again.

Concluding the Event

While most of the town is attending the festival, several businesses are also open to capitalize on the increased foot traffic and coin flow. If the party wants to make arrangements for food, drink, and lodging — or shop for equipment and the like — consult the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt]{Helkas} settlement walkthrough.

Next Steps

Once the party has finished exploring the festival, advance the clock to 12:00am (if midnight has not already arrived). Once the clock strikes midnight, this Event ends — mark it as as complete.

Advancing time by 1 hour will cause the [[/eventState windingTrailAttack]] Event to begin.
Dusktide Revelry.soverview: Having arrived in Helkas in time for the Dusktide Festival, the party enjoys the spectacle and attractions of the settlement's special lunar celebration.
Dusktide Revelry.sexposition: As you journey into Helkas proper, you behold a wondrous display of mirth and merriment in all directions. Beneath the ossified bones of the sprawling Leviathan that made this place famous, local townspeople meander to and fro excitedly — eager for dusk to arrive. Bustling market stalls and holiday attractions fill the air with scents both sweet and succulent, along with the sounds of rural music and lively chatter.
Dusktide Revelry.ssummary: We arrived in Helkas promptly enough to enjoy the spectacle of the Dusktide Festival, a rare lunar event that is of special significance to the Arcturians who live here.

Dusktide Rising.name: Dusktide Rising
Dusktide Rising.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this Combat Event, trouble befalls the Dusktide Festival as horrible mutated drakes assault the town with a mindless ferocity. To make matters worse, a group of raiders exploit the attack as an opportunity to pillage and plunder. In this Event, the party must:

  • Survive an attack by a @UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9]{Mutated Pallid Drake} and several @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki]{Mutated Pallid Drakelings}.

  • Repel a seemingly unrelated onslaught from @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H]{Otherhood Raiders} led by @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk]{Bassa the Firebug}.

  • Protect or save as many townsfolk of Helkas as they can, including @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians} and local NPCs alike.

  • Possibly learn a mysterious clue about the coordination of the attack.

Combat Phases

This Event is divided into two combat stages. Some important notes on these phases and how initiative order should be handled are:

  • The attack begins with the @UUID[.pjYncskqemOD6c6P#drake-assault]{Drake Assault} which drives townsfolk into cover and sows chaos throughout the town. During this phase @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist} fights by your side in initiative order.

  • This attack is followed shortly thereafter by an @UUID[.pjYncskqemOD6c6P#otherhood-assault]{Otherhood Assault} wherein raiders arrive to pillage the town. During this phase @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher} fights by your side in initiative order.

  • Your other companions from the caravan are not included in the combat directly as they are instead offscreen assisting the townsfolk.

  • There are many @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians} throughout the map. We recommend not adding these to tracked initiative order. At the end of every combat round you may reposition these commonfolk to simulate the survivors fleeing from danger and the overall chaos of the battle.

It is intended for these two combat phases to occur consecutively without extensive time for recovery between them, but as the Gamemaster you should calibrate the timing to apply the right amount of pressure to the party based on how they fared during the battle with the drake.

Drake Assault

The town is under attack! The townsfolk of Helkas scramble to reach safety while you and your companions prepare a hasty defense.

Active Ally

@UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist} stands at your side to defend against the encroaching creatures and should be included in tracked initiative order.

@Embed[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9]

@Embed[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki count=4]

Drake Tactics

The large drake is aggressive but permanently &Reference[blinded],@Condition[blinded], limited only to its sharpened senses of smell and hearing. Its blindness is offset by its @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.QZs1kj18rk0sW5fY]{Blood Sense},@UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9.Item.bloodSense000000], which allows the creature to precisely sense the presence of any wounded creature. The drake favors hit-and-run attacks, using its ability to fly to quickly reach and assault prey at ground level.

While at a distance, the drake uses @UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9.Item.y5cvFcmOMEaTtMGR]{Spit Bile} to attack in the direction of voices or creatures it can sense nearby. Once it detects a wounded target, it will close the distance and use @UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9.Item.vMpXBahMVK6vX86w]{Swooping Bite} to brutally attack from above.

If the drake does not precisely sense any targets, it will fly into the proximity of possible enemies and attack indiscriminately with @UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9.Item.acidSpray0000000]. Once it senses a wounded target, it will employ @UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9.Item.swoopingStrike00] to brutally attack from above.

The drake is crazed and will fight to the death even if its Morale is @Condition[broken].

Drakeling Tactics

The smaller drakelings are also permanently &Reference[blinded].@Condition[blinded]. They lack the ability to fly, but take advantage of their climbing ability to gain high, advantageous positions from which to attack.

From a distance, they will use @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.7lbgbSpk9B4WpE9G]{Spit Bile} towards targets they imprecisely sense. Once they have identified a wounded target using @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.QZs1kj18rk0sW5fY]{Blood Sense}, they will leap to attack using @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.5m7JGp8UNM3cOfSz]{Pouncing Bite}.

They will use @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.noxiousSpit00000] toward any target they imprecisely sense. Once they have identified a target using @UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9.Item.bloodSense000000], they will leap to attack using @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.pouncingStrike00].

The lesser drakelings instinctively follow the leadership of the larger drake, using @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki.Item.packhunter000000] to attack weakened prey. Like the larger drake, their afflicted condition means they will fight to the death even if they become @Condition[broken].

Ankarist's Assistance

During this phase of the attack, Ankarist stands alongside the party and fights with them. Once the drakes are defeated, he will depart to escort a group of embattled civilians out of the area and to safety, leaving the party to hold the square and protect whomever remains.

Ankarist is a fighter-warlock loyal to a patron of defense and creation. He is a fearless warrior who interweaves spells with strikes from his greatsword, @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs.Item.urCrVk7T2Ll56fQU]{Draconfang}.

  • Ankarist will assist others by casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.Opwh2PdX4runSBlm]{Aid} to bolster the party.

  • At a distance, Ankarist will cast @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs.Item.25ylDxyDXqOblkJj]{Eldritch Blast} before closing into melee range to attack with his blade or cast a devastating @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs.Item.pNfoSePAhxJLmF83]{Searing Smite}.

  • If the fire gets out of control, he can also use @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.a3XtAO5n2GrqiAh5]{Create or Destroy Water} to douse flames on buildings or people.

Ankarist will fight until his health falls below half, at which point he will suggest a tactical retreat if risk of death becomes too great.

Ankarist is a @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs.Item.spellblade000000] empowered by a patron goddess of defense and creation. He is a fearless warrior who interweaves spellcraft with strikes from his greatsword, @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs.Item.urCrVk7T2Ll56fQU]{Draconfang}.

  • At a distance, Ankarist will hurl spellcraft like @Spell[stasis.arrow.pull], utilizing the Pull inflection to draw enemies closer to him.

  • In melee, Ankarist uses his signature strike gesture to unleash devastating blows like @Spell[flame.strike]. If engaged with multiple targets, Ankarist will use @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs.Item.swipe00000000000] to strike at multiple foes.

Ankarist will fight until he becomes @Condition[weakened] or @Condition[broken], at which point he will suggest a tactical retreat and withdraw.

Dramatic Moments

At the beginning of each combat round after the first, roll on or choose from the @UUID[RollTable.Pg0wueP9nXkrEbL6]{Helkas Drake Moments} table below and narrate the result. Each result can only happen once.

@Embed[RollTable.Pg0wueP9nXkrEbL6 inline rollable=true]

Momentary Reprieve

The last drake collapses from its wounds, its body slumping to the ground with a heavy thud. Breathless, you turn to see Sadri emerging from a nearby building, ushering a group of frightened civilians toward safety.

Ankarist spots her and strides over, his greatsword still glinting with crimson light.

I hope you're not planning to lead these folks by yourself.

Sadri laughs like she's been caught.

I was, but if you're volunteering to escort us, consider yourself hired.

She gestures for Ankarist to take the lead before looking toward you to say:

Hold the square in case more of those beasts show up. I’ll rally the town and send help as soon as I can!

With that, Sadri and Ankarist make a hasty escape, driving the group of civilians along and leaving you to keep watch over square. As an uneasy quiet settles over the area, you can hear the roars and screams of chaos elsewhere in the town, but in the dark you can barely see what is happening.

Nearby, Sin and Agraband appear and begin heading toward you, both look concerned in their own ways and are surveying the damage, but it is Sin who urges Agraband along, leading him toward you.

Good thing we arrived here before the attack. I don't know if Helkas would have been able to hold the line without you.

Agraband grimaces, as though that hadn't occurred to him. The expression is only barely visible in the dark.

Yes, very fortunate. I shudder to think what might've happened otherwise.

Sin nods, and then looks at you.

Well, I'm not here to think, I'm here to help. What can we do?

Believing the attack to be concluded, both @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} and @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} have returned to the Helkas green to provide healing and relief.

  • Sin can provide healing through the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.uUWb1wZgtMou0TVP]{Cure Wounds} spell.

  • Agraband can also cast healing, or hasten the heroes' movement with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.B0pnIcc52O6G8hi8]{Longstrider} if healing is not required.

  • Sin focuses on restoring the health of the wounded by casting @Spell[life.influence.compose].

  • Agraband focuses on restoring the morale of the party by casting @Spell[spirit.pulse].

This process of recovery is cut short as the window of time between the drakes being defeated and the next wave of attackers arriving turns out to be insufficient for anyone to do more than catch their breath, cast a few spells, drink a few potions, and check their gear.

Applying Pressure

The Otherhood Raiders plan to attack the festival during the chaos caused by the drake attack. They would not ordinarily allow time for the town's defenders to regroup or evacuate civilians. It is intended that the party does not have time to rest between encounters. If the party fared poorly against the drakes, however, you may allow the party to take a Short Rest Recover before beginning the next passage of the event.

Otherhood Assault

Suddenly you smell the stench of burning wood and cloth caught on the wind. Turning to the source, you see smoke rising between the buildings of Helkas. From all directions, raiders begin to encircle the town square. Some of them look at you, but others seem to be trying to gauge which buildings are occupied.

Sin and Agraband swiftly retreat toward safety. Agraband calls out:

We'll make sure the civilians are safe, give them your worst… and make it look good!

He has to stop and double back to grab Sin's arm, tugging her along.

Come on, Sin. Let them handle this, there are still injured folks in the tavern that need you.

Reluctantly, Sin falls back as a sinister voice cuts through the night:

Best Dusktide festival I've ever been to. Shame it'll be the last one Helkas ever sees. Burn this place to ash! Leave nothing standing!

The speaker resolves out of the darkness. He is a wild-eyed kivahr wearing scorched leather armor covered in dark metal studs, and multiple armored bandoliers packed with vials of unknown liquids. He smells of chemicals and smoke, and looks ready for a fight. With one wave of his hand the bandits close in around you, preparing to attack.

However, you are not alone. Out of the corner of your eye you see the glint of a rapier, and a figure emerging from the shadows — Lyla Cevher. Her usual mirthful countenance is fixed and grim, ready to fight.

You're welcome to try, but we're not going to make it easy.

The party, joined by Lyla Cevher, faces a sortie of nine raiders, one of whom is their leader: Bassa, "the Firebug".

Active Ally

@UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher} stands at your side to defend against the arriving raiders and should be included in tracked initiative order.

@Embed[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H count=8]

@Embed[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk]

Otherhood Raider Tactics

The Raiders attack exuberantly without particular coordination or strategy. They are generally divided into three groups of three each, the southernmost group includes Bassa, their leader.

  • The Raiders prefer attacking from a distance, using @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H.Item.56XUUzooSiJinqz1] to deal damage to defenders or set buildings on fire.

  • As they advance, the raiders may switch to wielding blades, working together to mercilessly dispatch survivors.

  • If more than 6 of the raiders are killed, their morale will be broken and the survivors will attempt to flee. They will not surrender, however.

  • The raiders initially prefer attacking from a distance, using @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H.Item.flamingArrow0000] to damage defenders and set buildings aflame. They will use @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H.Item.pinningshot00000] to stop townsfolk or heroes from fleeing.

  • As they advance, the raiders will switch to wielding blades and use @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H.Item.dualWield0000000] and @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H.Item.backstab00000000] to mercilessly dispatch survivors.

  • Raiders whose morale is @Condition[broken] will attempt to flee. If fleeing is not possible, they will fight to the death as they refuse to surrender.

Bassa the Firebug

Bassa is a pyromaniac and wishes for nothing more than to see Helkas burned to the ground. A character with [[/knowledge warfare]] recognizes that Bassa is the closest thing that passes for a "commander" of the group.

  • Bassa will use @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.0spWUpUJyWWyIWiw]{Throw Alchemist's Fire} at every opportunity and @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.NRyveQEeqURCmPph]{Fire in the Hole!} if there are any enemies grouped closely together.

  • If Bassa is forced to fight in close quarters he will do so using @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.E7YEEioV2vsMSnNX]{Multiattack}, but Bassa avoids close combat for as long as he can, instead targeting enemies and buildings with his alchemist's fire.

  • Bassa has little regard for his own safety, and he will not flee the battle. If his life is threatened, he will prioritize maneuvering into a position to maximize the damage dealt by his @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.x99CIrBGzGPrFuCH]{Death Throes} which is activated immediately upon his death.

  • Bassa will hurl @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.MxYVu3N8UXCxmXFb] every round until he has none of the volatile bombs remaining. He is reckless enough to even hurl these flasks at point-blank range, relying on the protection offered by his @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.RvR6XSJgdhdxj5ee] to protect him.

  • After hurling a bomb, Bassa will use his blade to dispatch nearby enemies using @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.backstab00000000] or @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.dualWield0000000] (after drawing his dagger).

  • Bassa is zealously committed to his cause and has little regard for his own safety. He will not flee if his morale is @Condition[broken]. If his life is threatened he will prioritize maneuvering into a position to maximize the damage dealt by his @UUID[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk.Item.deathThroes00000] which is activated immediately upon his death, provided Bassa has Focus remaining.

Lyla's Tactics

The party is supported by @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher} during this combat.

  • Lyla is a rogue and fights accordingly, positioning to take advantage of her @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP.Item.riYc8YvN0An9WxZI]{Sneak Attack} feature and using her @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP.Item.7Vxbt38jSURyWrXf]{Cunning Action}.

  • She can also periodically use her @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP.Item.gt7noeT7BkYJIYnh]{Unconventional Tactics} feature to &Reference[help] her allies in combat, and is able to do so from a range of 30 feet away.

  • Lyla will fight until she falls below half her maximum health, after which point she will disengage and withdraw to safety.

  • Lyla uses her cunning to maneuver in combat to flank enemies and exploit their @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP.Item.weakpoints000000]. She uses @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP.Item.feintingstrike00] to deal heightened damage or @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP.Item.dualWield0000000] to make multiple rapid strikes.

  • Lyla will fight until she becomes @Condition[weakened] or @Condition[broken], at which point she will disengage and withdraw to safety.

Dramatic Moments

At the beginning of each combat round after the first, roll on or choose from the @UUID[RollTable.ymRwtDng5s77gPVC] table below. Each result can only happen once.

@Embed[RollTable.ymRwtDng5s77gPVC inline rollable=true]

An Onlooker

After the final raider falls, the gleam of Orbis provides a momentary chance to identify a mysterious clue about the attack.

A Cowled Spectator

Any character with a [[/skill perception 12 passive format=long]] or who makes a successful [[/skill perception 10]] checkwho makes a successful [/skillCheck perception 12 passive]] check notices the following:

You notice, standing atop the Helkas Boneway and illuminated against the vibrant Dusktide skyline, the silhouette of an onlooker. The figure is wearing heavy cascading robes and the combination of their low cowl and the gleaming moonlight behind them completely obscures their face. As if noticing your gaze, the figure turns their shoulder and disappears beyond the arcing ridge of the Boneway's spine.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill insight 15]][[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check can tell by the figure's demeanor that they are neither a townsperson nor a raider. They seem to have been watching the bloody spectacle unfolding without directly intervening.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] automatically succeed on this check.

By the time the party reaches a position to investigate further, no trace of the onlooker or their presence remains.

The Onlooker's Identity

The onlooker mentioned above is @UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]{Serethus}, leader of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]{Mutagists} and one of the innermost circle of @UUID[Actor.TU4SxinE07hpdTwB]{Zerranyss'} malevolent cabal. He orchestrated the attack against Helkas as a field test of the mutagen being developed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.bfORKMRfuaOgMbUt]{Repurposed Quarry} laboratory.

The mutated drakes were specimens from this laboratory that Serethus transported to the region. The subsequent attack by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune} was planned by @UUID[Actor.z1Ttp0q6CAtjDphl]{Sticks} to pillage and sow discord in the aftermath of Serethus' experiment.

It is impossible for the party to learn any of these connections at this time.

Bassa's Wraith

As the battle stills and townsfolk begin to cautiously emerge from cover and safety, Bassa's corpse shudders and jolts. Suddenly, tendrils of light begin to spiral out of his corpse, followed by a spindly, translucent humanoid form. Cries of shock and fear erupt from onlookers, several of them running away.

Sin, enraptured and horrified, walks toward the corpse as the spirit bearing a faint resemblance to Bassa begins to thrash and twist around, its form warping and becoming shot through with purple threads of energy.

It grasps at its own corporeal body, and the ground around it, dragged into the air by an unseen force. The wraith's screams are tortured and desperate, then cut off abruptly as the energy making it up unravels, dissipating into nothingness.

For a moment Sin stands wide-eyed, awestruck at the event she just witnessed. Breathlessly she speaks, more to herself than anyone else:

That can't be…

What Was That?

It is immediately clear that something very wrong just happened. Any character who makes a successful [[/skill religion 14]][[/skillCheck science 14 passive]] check understands that this does not happen with the dead, and Sin's shocked reaction to it was understandable. On Ember, the dead should not rise, nor should their spirits manifest like that. Some malevolent influence seems to have been at play here.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 17+Critical Success or [[/knowledge souls]]: Seeing a spirit ripped from the body of a recently deceased person fills you with dread. This is a direct circumvention of the normal cycle of souls. No force you know of is powerful enough to do that. This is grave tidings, and something which the Cindaric sages should be alerted to, as it could be a symptom of something wrong with the natural laws of Ember itself.

An investigation using a successful [[/skill religion 15]][[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check ascertains that there is no remaining magical or unholy influence upon Bassa's remains which are now lifeless and still.

Other than the information possibly learned above, your understanding of Ember's faiths and philosophies are insufficient to tell you anything more about this. Cindaric sages would likely know more about this, and should be informed.

Sin is clearly rattled by what she saw, and needs time to process, but if prompted to explain what she saw, or if she's okay, she can give a simple response:

About Bassa's wraith?

That was … unnatural. A deviation from the cycle of souls. This opposes what both the Primalists and Cindarics understand and believe. I'm not sure what could cause that, but that should never have happened. A spirit corrupted like that is bad, not just for Helkas but for the world itself. I need to speak with the Cindarics more now than ever.

Aftermath

Once the drakes have been felled and the raiders have been defeated or driven off, the battle of Helkas is ended. The party will likely wish to examine the remains of their enemies for clues as to what happened here.

Dead Drake

Any character that examines a dead drake's corpse and makes a successful [[/skill medicine 14]][[/skillCheck medicine 14]] check reveals that this creature appeared to have been exceedingly ill during its life. It was likely in constant pain, and functionally — if not entirely — blind. You've never seen any kind of illness like this before. There are old scars that have healed over, and some especially rancid wounds on this drake that have been festering for some time. This drake was not just ill: it was chronically ill, possibly for most of its life.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who fought the sick drakeling in the Forest of Stone recognize these as the same sort, although the adult drake is a much older and larger specimen; it is a testament to the creatures' ferocity that they survived as long as they did while so sickened.

The bandits have some identifying markers on them that might be interesting.

Bandit Corpses

Any character that investigates the bandits' corpses and makes a successful [[/skill investigation 13]][[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] check notices the distinctive presence of a tattoo upon the arm of each raider. It depicts a stylized gold coin with Arcden script and glints slightly in the light.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character that examines this tattoo and makes a successful [[/skill history 14]][[/skillCheck society 14 passive]] check recognizes that the coin tattoo says "For Other Fortunes," which is a play on an old Arcturian phrase about making changes to one's life; it is a shortened version of a catchphrase often used by pirates when pledging to a new ship: "I left my life for other fortunes — may they soon become my own."

They also notice that the ink of the tattoo is moving slightly as they look at it, indicating it may have magical properties.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge seafaring]] and characters who can understand [[/language arcden]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character that notices the tattoo's magical properties and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]][[/skillCheck arcana 14 passive]] check identify the ink as a variant of "shifting ink," which is typically used to obscure documents, making them harder to decipher. The ink is not usually used on tattoos, and does not appear to have the same properties of changing the meaning of written text while on the body.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] automatically succeed on this check.

Bassa's Remains

Investigation of Bassa's corpse identifies that several pieces of their gear are badly scorched, including the crossbow bolt sticking out of their chest. Despite the scorch marks, the leather is relatively untouched. A strange marking — a tower wrapped in coils of rope — has been deeply imprinted in the material. The armor is @UUID[Item.cq5c186h243PFHXM]{Firebug's Leather} which can be retrieved from the corpse.

Any character who searches Bassa's corpse and makes a successful [[/skill perception 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check spots small pouches hidden in the gear which hold several short notes and letters written in an indecipherable code (a mysterious Otherhood cypher that will be revealed later in the campaign).

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who examines the rope coil markings on the leather and makes a successful [[/skill history 13]][[/skillCheck society 13 passive]] check identify them as an elaborate maker's mark, used by crafters to drive business their way, but cannot tell whose mark it is.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberArcturian]], [[/knowledge trade]], or [[/path emberCaravanner]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who examines the leather material and makes a successful [[/skill nature 13]][[/skillCheck wilderness 13 passive]] check identifies the material used in the gear as leaf leather, an Arcturian leather style known for being lightweight and good for stealth. This leather is used throughout the Golden Flats, but is hard to acquire outside of larger towns and cities and costs more than a petty bandit is likely to pay.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] automatically succeed on this check.

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] recognize the telltale signs of chemically treated clothing and equipment to make it fire resistant. As long as this equipment is in well-maintained order, you reason that it could afford significant capability to withstand the hazards of heat and flame.

Concluding the Event

With the battle concluded, urgent wounds tended to, and fires quenched, both the party and the townsfolk can rest and begin to recover from the ordeal.

As part of the Event's conclusion, one of the characters may also be affected by the following Heart Attunement reinforcements:

Heart Attunement: Aid the Locals

If a character acted intentionally to protect the local townsfolk during the attack, that character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 windingTrailAttackAid]]. You may choose more than one character for this advancement.

Additionally, one of the characters may be affected by the following Luxarum Attunement reinforcement:

Luxarum Attunement: Lead the Counterattack

If a character was proactive in leading the counterattack against the Otherhood Raiders and their allies, that character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 windingTrailAttackCounter]]. You may choose more than one character for this advancement.

Next Steps

At this point, the party will likely wish to undertake a Long RestRest, which is to be encouraged. Regardless of whether the party chooses to rest now or later, completing this Event will automatically transition into the [[/eventState windingTrailSmoke]] Event.
Dusktide Rising.soverview: Violence comes to the Dusktide Festival as mutated drakes descend on Helkas, joined by Otherhood of Fortune raiders set on burning the town to cinders. The party must rally to its defense, as their own lives are also on the line.
Dusktide Rising.sexposition:
The raucous celebration of Dusktide is in full sway — music, singing, and the laughter of children awake far beyond their normally appointed bedtime. Slowly at first, and then more quickly, the gleeful cries of festival-goers turn to more somber and awestruck tones as the town collects in the square to peer up at the moons of Mayis and Orbis at their apex.

This quiet reverence is short-lived when moments later the concerned voices of nearby townsfolk break through the quiet murmurs of awe:

Something just passed in front of Mayis! What is that? It … it looks like it's coming toward us!

A lifted hand and pointed finger directs your attention to a point below the moons. Your eyes are drawn to the long, twisting, snake-like form of a beast descending in the darkness directly toward the square. The beast's long, pale body is unmistakable — a drake!

Confusion and then chaos ripple through the crowd as panicked realization sets in. Ankarist immediately raises his hand, a flash of crimson light weaving itself into a great sword as Sadri turns to the crowd and yells:

Run! Get to cover! Into the tavern and council house! Block the doors and windows so they can't get in!

The crowds scatter in all directions, rushing toward any building that might protect them as the huge beast strikes the ground and issues a guttural growl, which is echoed by other, smaller drakes nearby, each one crawling down from rocks and nearby roofs. Amidst the rush of bodies, Agraband grabs Sadri and ushers her to cover as well.

Come on, follow your own advice, now! Let the heroes deal with this.
Dusktide Rising.ssummary: We helped defend Helkas from a tandem assault, first by mutated drakes, and then by a group of fire-wielding raiders intent on pillaging and burning the town to ashes. The battle was intense, but we persevered. In the aftermath of the battle, a horrible tortured wraith escaped from the corpse of the raiders' leader. Where did these strange drakes come from? Who could have wished harm on this peaceful Arcturian town? What unholy power exerted its influence on the felled raider's spirit? We are left with significant questions that demand urgent answers.

Giant Moonstone.name: Giant Moonstone
Giant Moonstone.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration and Social Event lets the party interact with an ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.40qvRRe30tQVsAiJ]{Giant's Moonstone} of the Shent giants. In this Event, the characters can:

  • Learn more about the mysterious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}, an ancient civilization of giants.

  • Learn an ancient inscription which provides an important clue: "the fate of the moons," which will be used later during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.WG5PhLJbJ3Dvi4AP]{Ancient Shent Gate}.

  • Receive a blessing of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.RkdBtFQk7STvMbV2]{Mayis}.

  • Be introduced to Lyla and Clipper, companions in the @UUID[Actor.emberStrayhearth]{Strayhearth Caravan}.

Meeting Companions

It is intended that the party spend some time during this Event meeting @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla} and @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]{Clipper} if they have not already done so.

Approaching The Obelisk

Agraband addresses you, embracing the role of tour guide:

Behold, a moonstone! The Anachraenum historians believe these pillars were each attuned to a certain lunar cycle — and they still respond to the cycle of that moon to this day. What function they performed for their ancient builders, however, is knowledge lost to time.

Lyla approaches the stone, walking around it. She is quickly joined by the Signborn who does the same, albeit walking the opposite direction. Narrowly avoiding collision, the pair stop and seem to notice each other for the first time. Lyla says:

Clipper, didn't take you for a fan of old rocks.

The Signborn offers a cheeky grin of pointed teeth, and shoots back:

Same for you!

Lyla immediately turns her attention back to the stone and says:

Actually, I studied ancient stonework as part of my training with House Cevher, but nothing we studied was ever in such good shape. It's amazing, really. The writing is in incredible condition considering the age and how exposed it is.

Lyla gestures to the deeply cut symbols and runes in the stone. She and Clipper busy themselves poring over the moonstone, and lapse into contemplative chatter about the various aspects of it.

If the party would like, they can engage Clipper and Lyla in conversation, or examine the stones directly. Lyla and Clipper's topics of conversation are provided below, and they are more than happy to assist with the examination, especially if the party lacks the skills to glean anything useful from the ruin.

Meeting Lyla

@Embed[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]

Music: Lyla's Theme

When the party first interacts with Lyla, play her musical theme: [[/soundscape music lylaTheme lylaTheme]]

The Trading Heiress

Lyla Cevher, heir to House Cevher, is clearly the wealthiest person in the caravan, judging by her clothing and mannerisms. Characters with the [[/culture emberOrdani]] or [[/knowledge trade]] recognize Lyla as a member of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher} based on the colors and icons of her clothing. If they ask about her background, she'll confirm that she's not only a member of the trading house but also the daughter of Ralton Cevher, the head of the house.

Lyla explains that she is returning to Ordain to attend to family matters. What she does not immediately reveal is that her father recently died, and she needs to be there to support her family and brother and to take over leadership of the Trading House.

Any character that makes a successful [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check reveals that she's deeply preoccupied with a thinly veiled sadness, and that there is quite a bit more going on than she's revealed. It seems reasonable, however, that she would not be perfectly candid with new acquaintances.

Your story?

A small smile flickers across the young woman's face.

For once, my reputation fails to precede me. My name is Lyla, Lyla Cevher, and I'm a member of House Cevher. The name "Cevher" often carries with it a lot of preconceptions — key among them, people seem to think I'm either a pampered princess or a rugged miner with hands covered in rock dust, while the truth lies somewhere in between. And while I can certainly handle myself among the politicians of Ordain, I honestly prefer the feeling of a sword or a tool in my hands.

She quickly taps her rapier guard at her hip, and her smile softens slightly.

In all likelihood, I'll be trying to outrun my reputation for the rest of my days. No matter what my skills or personal desires might be…

House Cevher?

Ordain has several major Trading Houses, each with its own area of expertise. House Cevher, which includes the majority of my family members as its leaders, and its many contracted workers, is focused on the extraction and distribution of rare earth materials — such as metals and stone. We're a mining house basically, and we have a long history tied not only to Ordain but also with the Arcturians of the Arctus Plateau.

Your travel?

Like you, I'm headed eastward from Casla-Brava. I was staying with my great aunt Jeramia, helping expand Cevher's mining and trade operations and learning the ropes of administration and management. I had been living in the city for about four years, but … I have to return to Ordain. Strayhearth was the first caravan I found with an empty seat. And here we are.

Business in Ordain?

Her softness disappears in an instant.

Important Cevher family business needs my attention back home.

It's apparent that Lyla doesn't wish to discuss these matters any further.

Music: Shent Ruins

Once the party's main interaction with Lyla is over, return to the default music for this scene: [[/soundscape music ancientRuins shentRuins]]

Meeting Clipper

@Embed[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]

The Energetic Merchant

Clipper is a goodhearted, curious, enterprising, and enthusiastic @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.cYMQIQFugpO79L9f]{Maziran} aspiring to mercantile greatness. If asked about why she's in the caravan and where she's headed, she shares a simple portion of her personal story, as presented below.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck deception 13]] check understands that all the chaotic energy and endless inquisitiveness that Clipper exudes is absolutely genuine and not for show. Behind all this is a thread of earnest desire to succeed which she tries not to let show too much, possibly to avoid seeming too serious.

Goods for Trade

Clipper has a wide variety of wares available to trade. They can provide any non-magical item of Common or Uncommon rarity, subject to Gamemaster approval. They can provide any common or uncommon items which are Mundane and no greater than Fine quality, subject to Gamemaster approval. Clipper will offer items at their standard list price. If the party has impressed Clipper by proving themselves heroes of Helkas during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} event, Clipper will provide wares at a modest discount.

Your story?

Me? I'm just a not-so-simple Maziran merchant, quite a long way from home. Looking for a new place to call home, I suppose.

The merchant's spectral Signborn arms begin juggling a small array of trinkets and baubles as they continue.

I like to say I'm a "purveyor of the things peculiar" and a "collector of odd curiosities." Sometimes, I even find it hard to part with my own inventory, as eclectic and interesting as it 'tis.

Your travel?

As you can see, I'm currently on the road with Agraband. He's my mentor, you know! And my best friend. Friend-tor? Anyway, he's teaching me all sorts of things that are, and I quote: "vital for a traveling merchant to know."

The Signborn merchant smiles, charmed by their own subtle impersonation of the old caravanner.

What are you learning?

Clipper's eyes grow wide with excitement.

It might be easier to describe what I'm not learning, to be honest. It's so much. But I'm not complaining, of course! This has been the journey of a lifetime, so far, and I've already picked up more first-hand experience than I ever thought possible. Well, maybe not ever … magic, lore, economics — you name it, the captain is more than eager to talk about it.

One of these days, I'll have my own enterprise like Strayhearth! And eventually, when I'm old and rickety like Aggie over there …

They nod to the wizened bard nearby, who playfully nods back.

… I'll settle down and open up my own shop. A righteously awesome place, full of every curiosity under the sun. Until then, the road life is the only life for me. You gotta love all the stories we come across. And I've managed to sell my wares pretty successfully so far.

What do you sell?

I have quite a few interesting things in stock at the moment, now that you ask! On top of your standard tools and equipment, I have a small selection of peculiar trinkets and curios. Annnd, if you're thirsty …

The merchant leans in for a whisper.

… I have a couple of potions and spirits that can heal your wounds or steel your resolve.

Examining The Obelisk

The ancient menhir is a Shent moonstone, a pillar powered by a specific lunar cycle that was once used to monitor the area and communicate with other moonstones nearby. Curious party members may wish to discover who built the relic and learn of its purpose.

Inspecting the Area

Any character who examines the menhir and makes a successful [[/skill history 13]][[/skillCheck society 13]] check recognize that the architectural style and weathered runes of this monument mark it as a relic of the Shent, an ancient culture of giants which collapsed after The Shattering. This moonstone must be at least 2,000 years old.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12 passive]] check notices that one face of the marker is sheltered by a nearby cliff and therefore markedly less weather-worn than others. Upon this face of the monolith are the trace remnants of a legible inscription which is described below.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge weather]] automatically succeed on this check.

Deciphering Ancient Words

The party may investigate or try to translate the remnant phrases engraved upon the menhir.

  • [[/skill investigation 12]][[/skillCheck society 12]] The glyphs are an inscription in some ancient runic language. Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] recognize the runes as Pathward.

  • [[/language pathward]] You recognize and are able to read some of the runes, deciphering a short phrase mentioned below.

  • Characters with adequate supplies like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.WFQS2vT8ddrFjTJg]{Parchment} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.scrivenersToolki] may capture a rubbing of the inscription for later reference.

Offered Assistance

If the party actively attempts to decipher writing on the menhir without success, @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]{Clipper} speaks up and cheerfully offers their assistance using their innate @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ.Item.UqjTVqWS418J4oEu]{Comprehend Languages} featureusing their Glyphspeak inflection granted by their @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ.Item.emberSignbornLin].

When the characters decipher the ancient runes, read or paraphrase the following:

The translated fragment from the ancient inscription reads:

… shadows end by spear restrained and sealed to never rise again. Let only those who understand the fate of the moons walk its path.

A Phrase of Power

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill insight 13]][[/skillCheck arcana 13]] finds it remarkable that the phrase "fate of the moons" is linguistically expressed in Pathward using a prominent runic glyph at the center of the inscription.

  • Characters who can read and understand [[/language pathward]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] check recollects an ancient historical account following The Shattering that tells of the Shent doing battle against terrible Abyssal forces which destroyed much of their civilization. This inscription perhaps describes such a conflict.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] automatically succeed on this check.

Characters wanting to understand the magic in the moonstone can examine the runes and magical designs, learning more about its function. Unfortunately, this is one of the last surviving stones in the area, so not much can be done with it anymore.

Moonstone Magic

Any character who examines the markings and magical runes and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 13]][[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check recognizes that this is a Shent moonstone: a pillar powered by a specific lunar cycle. The color of the crystal and symbols on the pillar make it clear that the moonstone was attuned to the water moon, Mayis. The knowledge of how to make these arcane lunar landmarks was lost with the Shent themselves ages ago.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The markings on the stone indicate it would have been able to communicate with other nearby moonstones. Additional designs in the runes indicate that the orbs also could have monitored the area around them, though what it could "see" is unclear.

Out of Service

Characters attempting to attune with, connect to, or utilize the moonstone to see how far the device reaches or if any other moonstones remain will be disappointed to find that it is the only one left in service in the area, and most of its functions have badly degraded due to its age. It is now little more than an unusual landmark upon the caravan route.

Blessing of Mayis

Characters who understand that the Giant Moonstone is attuned to the water moon of Mayis may attempt to commune with the ancient Shent artifact. When a character touches the Moonstone, read or paraphrase the following:

As you lay your hand upon the ancient monument, the azure depths of the great crystalline orb begin to swirl within, reminding you of an aqueous, otherworldly maelstrom.

The Moonstone's Blessing

Any character who touches the Giant Moonstone can attempt to commune with the ancient artifact. Characters who commune this way while Mayis is present in the sky are empowered with additional temporary reserves of energy:

  • If Mayis is Waxing or Waning, you gain +2 Temporary Hit Points.

  • If Mayis is Full, you gain +5 Temporary Hit Points.

You gain the benefits of an effect, Patience of Mayis, which grants the following benefits:

  • If Mayis is Waxing or Waning, you gain +1 Maximum Focus.

  • If Mayis is Full, you gain +2 Maximum Focus.

This effect will be provided in the Crucible system once Ember is upgraded to use Foundry Virtual Tabletop version 14.

Mayis Attunement: Moonstone Communion

Each character who successfully communes with the Giant Moonstone by touching the monument advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 windingTrailMoonstoneCommunion]] at the conclusion of the Event.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished examining the moonstone and socializing with the NPCs, they should get back on the caravan and get moving. Agraband is happy to stop, but doesn't want to lose too much time with delays.

Next Steps

The Strayhearth Caravan will continue on its journey eastward through the Verdant Paths, winding its way northward until it reaches the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.0IsGP3Ar0XvIYoMZ]{Dry Outpost}. Here, the caravan will camp for the night, triggering the [[/eventState windingTrailRestful]] Event.
Giant Moonstone.soverview: The party encounters an ancient moonstone on the path through the Forest of Stone, a relic of the Shent giants who built great wonders in these mountains.
Giant Moonstone.sexposition:
Agraband calls a halt as the Strayhearth Caravan stops to water its yarnac and allow for a momentary respite. A woman's voice rings out over the din of the caravan coming to a stop.

Is this the moonstone you mentioned, Agraband?

Agraband chuckles, turning toward an auburn-haired noble.

Indeed it is, and as promised, you'll have a chance to look it over, Lyla.

The woman does her best to temper her obvious excitement, and heads that way, joined by Agraband and an animated Signborn girl.

As he passes by, Agraband beckons for you to come along, gesturing to the strange pillar.

Care to see a remnant of ancient civilizations?
Giant Moonstone.ssummary: Along the winding pathways of the Forest of Stone we encountered a strange menhir created by giants of old, called a moonstone. Its ancient face was inscribed with weather-faded runic markings.

Skies Above.name: Skies Above
Skies Above.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Social Event provides the players with an opportunity to meet and interact with other travelers accompanying the Strayhearth Caravan. In this Event, the party can:

  • Learn some of Ember's lore by gazing at the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} on a clear night.

  • Meet Sin Marmot, a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.VHQNztu45XEHuvtY]{Strider} journeying to Ordain to join the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}.

  • Explore the old outpost, perhaps finding some forgotten items.

Meeting Companions

It is intended that the party spend some time during this Event meeting @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} if they have not already done so.

Speaking With Sin

As the quiet evening draws on, you are joined by another member of the caravan, a Keth woman with bright blue eyes and hair like charcoal.

Hello! Having a nice evening so far?

She gestures to the sky above.

I'd invite you to stargaze a bit with me, but the clouds would need to clear first. But that doesn't mean we can't talk while we wait!

@Embed[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]

Music: Sin's Theme

Whilst the party chats with Sin, play her musical theme: [[/soundscape music sinTheme sinTheme]]

The Aspiring Cindaric

Speaking to Sin, one quickly learns a lot about her: she's a druid from the wild and dangerous reaches of the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.ntef4M02D50Y8BlE]{Corebright Forest}, was born and raised among the [[/culture emberStrider]] of the region, and began learning druidic magic at an early age.

A successful [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check reveals that Sin is being straightforward and earnest. She is both excited and intimidated about this epic journey she's recently embarked upon, but is doing a relatively good job of keeping her nerves in check.

Your story?

It's a pleasure to meet you! My name is Sin Marmot. I'm a practitioner of primal magic — a druid, if you will — from the Corebright Forest, far to the west. Among my people, the Striders, I'm one of the youngest to pick up the staff, so to speak.

The young Keth casually adjusts the position of her gnarled wooden staff, and you notice the amber glow of a pyrefly within a tiny basket slung from the staff's crook.

My connection to Ember started at a remarkably young age — according to the elders — and it's always been something that's called to me. Not all of my people have this connection, and those that do often take decades to hone their talents. For me, I suppose my connection to Ember is a little bit stronger than most.

Connection to Ember?

It's a bit hard to describe with words, but for as long as I can remember, I've always felt some kind of bond with nature and the elements, something I can feel in my bones. I can hear sounds in the wilderness that others often can't, and I can almost see a current of spiritual energy in the world around us. To be honest, sometimes it feels like it's out of my control, as if Ember is speaking through me. I know it sounds kinda funny, but magic is weird like that. Basically, what started off as natural talent bloomed into something greater — something I don't always understand, but it fills me with a real sense of purpose.

Your travel?

About a year ago, a Cindaric Sage from Ordain came to my homeland, and my druidic circle in Sirewood was assigned the task of keeping him company. I learned quite a bit from that Sage, and it didn't take long to realize I wanted to know more about the Cindaric religion. So, after a few months of preparation and some hard goodbyes with friends and loved ones, I set off for the Arctus Plateau. And here I am!

Sin gazes eastward at the gloomy horizon, looking wistfully at the overcast clouds which mask the presence of the waxing moons.

I'm on my way to Corpin Sanctuary on Mial Mountain. Hopefully, they've got room for a wayward Strider like myself. I can't wait to learn more about the Heart of Ember and how the Cindaric Sages commune with it.

Cindaric Sage?

The Cindaric Sages are the Arctus Plateau's most prominent and esteemed spiritual organization. The founder of Ordain herself started the religion, which is based on a holistic relationship with the Heart of Ember. In many ways, the Cindarics are like the druids of the Corebright Forest. I still have a lot to learn about the Heart of Ember and the cosmos as a whole, and the Cindarics seem like the right folks to help me get there.

Music: Default

Once the party has finished this dialogue with Sin, return to the default music: [[/soundscape music reset]]

Stargazing With Sin

As the evening wears on, the storm desists and the sky mercifully clears, providing a brilliant view of the heavens overhead as the clouds dissipate.

Sin's glittering eyes turn upward again to check on the darkened sky, as they have several times over the last little while. This time, though, Sin gestures upward with a flash of excitement.

There we are, clear at last. Look, the night sky is incredible, right? I never tire of it. The skies out here don't look that different from the skies that I grew up with, which is a comfort while being so far from home.

Stargazing

This is an ideal moment to introduce the party to the @UUID[Scene.emberCosmos00000]{Cosmos} map and discuss its major elements. We recommend you switch to it for some of this scene, especially while it is being discussed with Sin.

At this point, the moon @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis} is waxing. It will eventually become full on the eve of the Dusktide festival in Helkas, where the party is bound.

Lunar Influence

[[/attunement emberMayis]] As your eyes settle on Mayis, you can feel the faint push and pull of its endless waves. Within a few heartbeats, the tides of the great water moon have begun to connect with you, and an invasive cold washes over your body — as if being submerged into the depths of the very ocean. The moment is fleeting, gone in the blink of an eye, but it stands out as one of the strongest connections to the world or its lunar bodies you've ever experienced.

[[/attunement emberRagen]] As you stare at the roiling form of Ragen in the sky, you can feel a stinging sensation in your chest. You've felt it before, a sharp pain like a red-hot spark searing your skin. But this time, you don't flinch. As you observe the crimson glow of Ragen overhead, you feel a fiery warmth spread throughout your limbs. This burning sensation is pleasant but brief, and although that initial spark has subsided, a warmth lingers in your mortal flesh for a short time to follow.

[[/attunement emberOrbis]] Standing beneath the chaotic glow of Orbis, you can feel the pull of the waxing spirit moon in your mind and heart. As your eyes affix themselves to the moon's pale glow, the connection is immediate — a tingling sensation spreads throughout your limbs, and every varied emotion you've felt today washes over you, like the disturbed silt of a placid lake. Your mind roils with joy, excitement, agitation, curiosity, and many other emotions you can barely control. Just as it feels like you might lose yourself to it, this cosmic link grows taut and snaps like a bare strand of thread. As your connection to Orbis subsides, you notice your ears ringing, and your chest is tight with the fading sensations of furtive emotions.

Lunar Lore

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 13]][[/skillCheck science 13 passive]] check knows that all the moons have a similar influence on the world and its people — some feel the pull more keenly than others, but most everyone feels it at one point or another.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge cosmology]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The character recalls that each moon is home to elemental beings, or failing that, beings that are made of or heavily linked to the energies of that moon. In the case of Ragen, it's fire elementals; for Mayis, water elementals; and for Orbis, chaos spirits. These beings can be encountered all over Ember, drawn to places that resonate with their moons, and become especially common when those moons are at their apex.

Any character who succeeded on the previous check, further considers the elemental influence of moons, and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 15]][[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check understands that while lunar elementals are generally dangerous, they have a long history of being neutral to or sometimes even helpful to the people of Ember. Water elementals of Mayis have been known to share knowledge with ancient civilizations, and the legends say that the first settlers to the Arctus Plateau were aided by ancient fire sages of Ragen. Orbis' beings are less helpful, due to their deeply chaotic nature.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge elementals]] automatically succeed on this check.

Back to Ember

When the party is finished contemplating the stars with Sin, you should return to the @UUID[Scene.vistaForestedCli] to continue the event.

Investigating the Homestead

After a bit of quiet between you and Sin, the druid's attention drifts to your surroundings.

Have you rooted around the old dry outpost yet? You never know what sorts of things are lurking under old stones and floorboards. Well, aside from the bugs. There are always bugs. But sometimes there are other things…

Sin pops up and walks toward the old, dilapidated building, waving you along.

Characters who investigate the outpost more thoroughly can find a few clues:

A Dilapidated Outpost

Any character who investigates the outpost and makes a successful [[/skill investigation 13]][[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] check notices evidence that another group has camped here fairly recently: some burned logs near the fire pit are not fully turned to coal, and a refuse pit behind the outpost has discarded food scraps that are not yet rotten. You have not encountered other travelers along the road, but these signs make clear the region is not without inhabitants.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success or [[/knowledge forensics]]: The character notices a swollen floorboard that is slightly out of place. Investigating it, they find a small pouch of old and tarnished coins totaling [[/award 25sp]] [[/award 2sp 50cp]].

Once the party has finished searching, Sin finds something for the party.

Lifting a slat of wood and peering into the pile of rotting paper, Sin calls out:

Hey, look at this!

Fearlessly, she shoves her hand into the mess and pries out a worn, mildew-coated leather binder, along with a small collection of bugs which are quickly dispatched from her arm with a brisk shake.

A moment later she's flipping through the pages, scrunching her nose at what she finds.

Looks like some diagrams and recipes from a hunter. Here, you should take this! I've never seen a hydroxol before, but if you run into one, the notes could be useful!

She claps the moldy old folder closed and holds it out to claim.

Sin offers the @UUID[Item.f0aDRnZVqg5cFmk2]{Moldy Recipe Folder} to the party. It contains some curious crafting recipes that the party could try making if they can find the creature noted within.

What's a Hydroxol?

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill nature 12]][[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] check knows that hydroxols are gigantic, naturally territorial amphibious omnivores that nest in watery, secluded places.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: These creatures could probably be found in this region, in the especially watery areas of the Dripstones.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has concluded exploring or conversing with other members of the caravan, they can rest to prepare for their continued journey.

Next Steps

Upon completion of this Event, the party may complete a Long RestRest.

Like the previous day, the caravan departs at 8:00am on Day 2, and is bound for the settlement of Helkas. If all goes well, the caravan would arrive by about 6:00pm that evening.

The travel will not transpire as expected, and instead the party will be interrupted by the events of [[/eventState windingTrailCairn]] partway through the day's travel.
Skies Above.soverview: The party camps for the night in an old outpost frequented by caravans, which provides meager shelter from the moisture and unpredictable weather of the Forest of Stone.
Skies Above.sexposition: After a day of challenging travel through the ravines and ledges of the Verdant Paths, you and your band of weary travelers are relieved to arrive at the humble outpost. Your passage through the Forest of Stone has been damp with rivulets, falls, and cenotes that permeate the air with heavy moisture. The accommodation is modest, but it does offer sufficient space for the wagons, the yarnac, and the travelers of the Strayhearth Caravan to rest weary limbs, dry sodden garments, and refill hungry bellies.
Skies Above.ssummary: We camped overnight in a small outpost used frequently by caravans and travelers passing along this path. Its dilapidated structures were long-since abandoned, but it provided welcome shelter.

A Promised Exit.name: A Promised Exit
A Promised Exit.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration Event allows the party to find a shortcut back to the Strayhearth Caravan: a locked and ancient door nestled deep within the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns}, south of the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.dH8d3daTaRNOWLrt]{Shent Moon Temple}. In this Event, the characters can:

  • Examine the ancient doors, parsing out the secret passphrase needed to open them: "Hope in Destruction" (which can also be learned from the Shent Sage @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth} after the [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer]] Event).

  • Exit the Dripstone canyons and continue on their journey to reunite with Agraband Swift and the Strayhearth Caravan.

The Sealed Doors

The ancient gate here is locked by powerful enchantments, and much like the other door can only be opened using the proper passphrase. Characters that try to use "Fate of the Moon" here will find that nothing happens, but they will be on the right track.

Examining the Gate

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 12]] [[/skillCheck society 12]] check recognizes that the architectural style and weathered runes of this monument mark it as a relic of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}, an ancient culture of giants which collapsed after @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering}. The figures depicted on the crown are recognizable as Shent rebuking something in their midst while others flee, some carrying objects in their arms. The shape and darkness of it seem to represent the invading force of the Abyss during the time of the Shattering.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: You recognize an aspect of sacrifice, survival, and perseverance in the face of adversity. The figures depicted across the top of the doorway are facing evil, possibly sacrificing themselves so that others can escape to safety. This would track given that the Shent were eradicated as a result of the Shattering.

Any character who studies the imagery of the door and makes a successful [[/skill religion 12]] [[/skillCheck science 12]] check notices a strong theme of reverence toward the moons in the reliefs and inscriptions — the water moon Mayis is most prominent among them. The figures across the top of the door seem to have been added afterward. Given the prominence of Mayis on this door, much like the others, you suspect that this door was not originally meant to block entry, but to mark the presence of a moon temple or similar significant lunar element in the region.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: You recognize that this door was built with significant iconography of self-sacrifice, heroism, struggle, and protection. It seems that the figures on the door were giving all they could to rebuke some greater evil for the sake of others.

Any character who examines the runes and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 12]] [[/skillCheck arcana 12]] check notices several magical symbols carved into the stone, but they appear to be inert. At first they appear wholly decorative, but further investigation reveals interlocking runes of transmutation, divination, and abjuration. Their purpose is unknown, however, aside from the abjuration runes meant to protect the structure from outside influence. Examining the runes in even greater detail, you understand that many of them were never connected to the others and only meant to be decorative, and are all variants of destructive evocation runes. However, their presence masks rather intricate magical formulae that does serve a purpose. When activated by a command word which should be detected by the divination runes, the door's transmutation magic would manipulate a large area around the door, possibly freeing it to open.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: Strangely, like before, the active magic was embedded in a large amount of destructive runes. Yet the actual magic there has nothing to do with it. More accurately, it is deliberately hidden in the destruction.

A character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify} spell on the door gains information equivalent to a 17+ result of your choice.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} reveals an aura of Divination and Transmutation magic surrounding the gate; it is waiting for something to activate it.

A character with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] will note that the stone has active divination magic waiting for something, inert transmutation magics meant to do something when activated, and is heavily reinforced in the form of transmutation and abjuration wards.

Characters may also notice that there are runes of Pathward carved into the door, and as with the Shent moonstone they encountered several days ago, they may want to decipher the text.

Ancient Inscriptions

Characters who can understand [[/language pathward]], or those who cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplComprehend] make use of the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.versatileTransla]], are able to read some of the runes, deciphering the phrase below.

The translated inscription reads:

We fight for Ember until the last. We are not lost. We do not know despair. Purpose in oblivion, hope in destruction.

Opening the Door

A character who speaks the inscription aloud triggers the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.lPBtTwjSZNbtNqs5#concluding-the-event]{door to open} upon saying the words, "Hope in destruction."

Failing Forward

Just Like Last Time

If the party is struggling, consider allowing [[/check intelligence 12]] [[/skillCheck science 12]] checks to piece together the meaning. The above investigation should leave the party with two key aspects: Hope and Destruction. More specifically: hope in destruction. This is the door's passphrase.

Outside Help

  • Contacting the caravan will result in Lyla and Clipper prompting the party to look for a phrase of passage like the previous door. Though, this does require them to understand [[/language pathward]] or use a spell to understand languages first talent to translate the text.

  • If the party helped @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth} by defeating the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Writhing Whisperer} during the [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer]] Event, the Shent sage has already provided the exit phrase, "Hope in destruction" (in which case you should remind the party that they already know the answer).

Whispered Words

If the party chose to side with and release the Writhing Whisperer, one or more of the characters receives a harrowing flash of memory left from the residual psychic energy of the Whisperer's telepathy:

Your vision briefly distorts; for a moment, your body as you know it is gone, replaced by a countless number of limbs reaching and grabbing and pulling your form through crystalline caves at breakneck speeds. You see the glare of daylight through a great stone doorway, but it is narrowing by the second.

Shent cowards rush through the closing door, as others turn, preparing to face you. You are too slow — the fools have delayed you! — and as the great stone door collides, you hear one of the Shent bellow:

"Hope in destruction!"

The stone shimmers as a pulse of magic washes over it, fusing it with the rest of the caves, locking you inside. You lash out in a rage, but are met with the sting of Shent spears and magic so ferocious that it makes you recoil in pain and fear.

The memory unravels with a particularly strong hit, and your senses return with you on your knees, body shaking, and head ringing with pain.

Concluding the Event

After you utter the passphrase, the entire door shutters and roars to life. The massive polished gems glow brightly, their surfaces reflecting the faces of the moons they represent. The stone slabs break apart and slide open, letting in air and light from the region beyond.

Next Steps

After opening the sealed Shent door, the party can return to the Verdant Paths of the Forest of Stone. At this point, the party may wish to use their @UUID[Item.2NsZVnU1qQaC2vmo] to contact the caravan.

From here, they need to backtrack west to help the Strayhearth Caravan clear the blockage in the [[/eventState windingTrailHelp]] Event.
A Promised Exit.soverview: Traveling through the crystal caverns to the south of the greater Dripstone canyons, the party happens upon an ancient door like the one they encountered when entering the area. With the right passphrase, they can open it and continue onward.
A Promised Exit.sexposition:
You behold a familiar door at the far end of the web-strewn cavern, an enormous threshold that appears untarnished by the ravages of time, despite the lingering dust of ages and the glittering webs that crisscross its giant-sized expanse.
