Seven crystal orbs set into the stone gleam from the ever-shifting light of the cavern, each reflecting colors and patterns that remind you of the many moons of Ember.

The crown of the door features six finely detailed figures, their sharp faces looking skyward and each bearing staves or weapons. A dark stone arrowhead pierces down between them.
A Promised Exit.ssummary: We encountered an ancient door marked with seven crystal orbs fashioned into the likeness of Ember's moons. After uttering an arcane passphrase, the door opened, allowing our sought-after egress from the crystal caverns.

Lending a Hand.name: Lending a Hand
Lending a Hand.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this Exploration Event, the party clears the rubble and gets the Strayhearth Caravan moving again. They can:

  • Help clear the remaining rubble and rejoin the caravan.

  • Be rewarded by Agraband for their assistance.

While the party was away, Agraband and the rest of the Strayhearth Caravan spent their time methodically clearing the passage of rubble. They made good progress, but as predicted, the work was slow and difficult. Now that the party has returned, they can work together to clear the remainder of the blockage.

The Path Reopens

Blasting Free

If the party has secured a @UUID[Item.VCZEiWaAI3jHiDLU]{Crate of Blast Flasks} (either from Sellen in the [[/eventState oozeControlUpdate]] Event or from the depths of @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK]{Yakoshta Mine}), then these explosives can be used to rapidly clear the remaining blockage. Advance time by 1 hour and then proceed.

Fulgurite Assistance

If the party secured the assistance of the @UUID[Actor.emberFulgrBlades]{Fulgurite Blades} during the [[/eventState overMoonTemple]] Event, they are present on the far side of the blockage where they have been assisting the caravan to clear the rubble. Between Sajor's potent spells and Rorhim's powerful strength, most of the remaining work has already been completed, allowing the party to rapidly clear the remaining rubble from this side. Advance time by 1 hour and then proceed.

Manual Labor

In the absence of blast flasks or other methods of easily clearing the rubble, the required work involves several hours of hard labor, but no skill checks or challenges await the party. Instead, the work progresses rapidly and without any issues. Advance time by 4 hours and then proceed.

A Caravan Reunited

Regardless of which method was used to clear the remaining rubble, read the following aloud:

As you clear the last of the rubble and make contact with the work crew, there's a cry of excitement. The gap through the rubble opens enough to let in light and air; Agraband's face appears in the gap, covered in dust and sweat, but bearing a happy smile.

"Good to see you all again!"

He turns back to yell their success to the rest of the workers, and a cheer echoes back. Before long, the path is widened enough for the wagons of the caravan to trundle through, and the remaining work of navigating them through the newly excavated pass proceeds with high spirits.

Before long, you and the Strayhearth Caravan have embarked again on the winding trail toward Helkas — and the Dusktide Festival.

Mark the following outcome as complete to trigger a transition of the Region Map and remove the debris blocking the caravan's path.

[[/outcome cleared]]

Payment as Promised

If the party reminds Agraband about his promise of payment in exchange for assistance, he promptly offers the party [[/award 100gp]] [[/award 10gp]] as promised.

If the party does not ask, Agraband approaches the party to provide payment when they next take an opportunity to rest.

If the Fulgurite Blades were involved in helping to clear the rubble, they bid the party farewell; they are returning to the Dripstones to engage in further exploration.

Sajor nods toward you curtly and says:

Well, that's our end of it. It's certainly been interesting. You've turned out to be more capable than I initially expected… but only just.

Perhaps we will cross paths again if you make your way to Ordain. With a few more discoveries like these —

She taps the satchel at her side containing the Shent Planisphere.

— the Fulgurite Blades will be the talk of the city!

Concluding the Event

Depending on when the blockage is cleared, the caravan will take time to rest before pushing on toward their destination of Helkas.

If it is 12:00am on Day 5 or earlier:

Agraband is relieved and reminds the party that there is still plenty of time to reach Helkas for the festival. He proposes taking a Long RestRest to recover from the strenuous work clearing the rubble and to get moving early the following morning.

If it is later than 12:00am on Day 5:

Agraband insists that there is no time to spare, and they must press on toward Helkas or risk missing the festival entirely. The caravanner spurs the caravan into action and they proceed onward to Helkas without resting.

Next Steps

Once the caravan is moving again, it proceeds on toward the town of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas} and the [[/eventState windingTrailArrival]] Event.
Lending a Hand.soverview: The party returns to the Strayhearth Caravan after having explored one of the paths in the region. Approaching it from the opposite side, they can assist and expedite the clearing work needed to get the caravan moving again.
Lending a Hand.sexposition:
You approach the gathered rubble of the fallen stone pillars, noting that progress has been made in your absence. Perched upon one of the stones is a small rat, which suddenly shifts and morphs into Sin Marmot. She waves cheerfully as she spots you.

"We were wondering when you'd turn up! I said, they probably just had some sort of adventure on the way."

She hops off the rubble and dusts off her legs.

"So then Agraband sent me through a gap we cleared to go look for you. Unfortunately, I wouldn't know where to start looking, so I just held down the rocks here and decided to see if you'd turn up."

She offers a broad but cheeky grin.

"And here you are!"
Lending a Hand.ssummary: We arrived at the far side of the tunnel blockage, and set to clearing it. The work was hard, but we've gotten the Strayhearth Caravan moving again toward Helkas.

Ravine Outlet.name: Ravine Outlet
Ravine Outlet.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this Combat Event, the party is set upon by an ill and disoriented predator, which attacks in a typically vicious but haphazard manner while spitting up an odd substance. In this Event, the party can:

  • Battle a sickened @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]{Suarrok Juvenile}, routing or killing it in the process.

  • Examine the monstrosity and determine precisely why it might be sick.

A Familiar Foe

The party may have encountered this creature before:

  • This suarrok is the sickened creature in the [[/eventState oozeControlPredator]] Event.

  • If the party hasn't yet killed the suarrok atop the Aedir Signalpost in the [[/eventState signalIntentTower]] Event, then this is that specific creature. Otherwise, this is merely another suarrok juvenile that exists in the region.

Suarrok Ambush

The party is attacked by a juvenile suarrok. This strange monstrosity is likely familiar to the party by now, having been encountered at least once in the area during the events of other quests. This one in particular is ill from having eaten a corrupted slime.

@Embed[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]{Suarrok Juvenile}

Deranged Behavior

This creature's attacks don't completely make sense — it switches targets frequently and seems to favor aggression over any sort of practical attack strategy. After its turn in combat, the Suarrok hacks and coughs, spitting up a glob of glimmering goop. If it is flying when it does this, reduce its height by 10 feet, forcing it to land if necessary.

Suarrok Tactics

If healthy, a suarrok would employ tactics to protect itself from harm while hunting down the weakest prey it can hunt.

The suarrok uses @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.T2ZNQKTKt3TyWvYg]{Searing Stare} to inflict the &Reference[blinded] condition on the enemy that is most directly threatening to it.

It then relies on @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.z0zk5kCBd8tSuH64]{Flyby} and the 10-foot reach of its attacks to harass the party without becoming pinned down.

The suarrok uses @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.searingStare0000] to inflict the @Condition[blinded] condition on the enemy that is most directly threatening to it.

It then relies on @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.swoopingStrike00] and @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.rakingTalons0000] coupled with its @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.elusiveFlight000] capability to viciously attack weak foes without becoming engaged.

Survival Instinct

If the party previously battled, but did not kill the suarrok in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost}, it will fight to the death here — maddened at being displaced from its nest.

Otherwise, once reduced to below half its Hit Point maximum, if it is @Condition[weakened] or @Condition[broken], the suarrok attempts to flee, flying off in a southeastern direction in a swerving and uneven path. If it escapes, combat ends, and the creature does not come back.

In the immediate aftermath of the battle, characters can take a closer look at the creature's spit, and if they defeated it, the carcass.

A Familiar Foe

Any character who experienced the [[/eventState oozeControlPredator]] Event can tell without a check that the creature is similar to the one they saw throwing up earlier.

Otherwise, any character who makes a successful [[/skill nature 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12 passive]] check recognizes that this creature is likely a @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5], a flying predator that has been spotted in this region in the past.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge monsters]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 15+Critical Success : You recognize that this creature was an adolescent and that suarrok can grow to be huge in size when fully grown. Battle against even a juvenile suarrok could be deadly, but facing a fully grown adult would likely be disastrous.

Investigating the Goo

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]], or who makes a successful [[/skill perception 11]] check,who makes a successful [[/skillCheck awareness 11 passive]] check can see that there is an odd glint to the bird's gooey spit.

  • Characters who are familiar with the alchemical contaminant (whether from @UUID[JournalEntry.rycatIw6IR9KlRhK]{Yakoshta Mine}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn]{Aedir Signalpost}, or their encounter with a similar predator elsewhere in the Forest of Stone) do not need to do the below checks for information they are already aware of.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14 passive]] check can understand that it is something that the creature ate and has reacted badly to, rather than evidence of some other sickness.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success : You identify that the natural substance that the creature ate looks like the partially digested remains of an ooze. It was recently eaten, suggesting its source must have been within a few miles of your current location.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14 passive]] check correctly deduces that the acrid nature of this substance is due to some toxic substance that was ingested alongside the organic material.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success : The alchemical substance is the source of the acrid smell and any damage done by the puddles. It is dangerous to the touch and likely the reason that the creature threw up.

The substance in the spit is too dissolved to feasibly collect.

If the party managed to defeat the suarrok without it escaping, they may directly examine the body.

Examining the Body

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14 passive]] check reveals that the creature looks healthy, with no markers of disease, illness, or injury prior to those inflicted in the fight. The most likely answer is that the creature was poisoned by something it ate, as evidenced by the goo it was coughing up.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill survival 14]][[/skillCheck wilderness 14 passive]] check can harvest some ingredients from the felled suarrok, including @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.pUoE64EAvEMIlCuN]{Suarrok Plumage} and a @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5.Item.JEpb6xmdPXNUXHmy]{Suarrok Eye}. On failure, however, the damage to the suarrok from battle has rendered these components unrecoverable or worthless.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has driven off or defeated the suarrok, they can continue on their journey. At this point, the party may wish to use their @UUID[Item.2NsZVnU1qQaC2vmo] to contact the caravan. Their next stops are either:

  • Returning to the Strayhearth Caravan in the [[/eventState windingTrailHelp]] Event.

  • Leaving the caravan behind by proceeding directly to the [[/eventState windingTrailArrival]] Event.
Ravine Outlet.soverview: In a natural chokepoint between the southern Dripstones and the Verdant Paths to the north, the party is beset by an illness-addled Juvenile Suarrok, the same great bird-like creature they encountered previously upon their journey. The creature must be driven off or defeated.
Ravine Outlet.sexposition:
A piercing sound cuts through the air from above as a looming shadow passes overhead. A large, bird-like creature swoops into your path, wings outstretched and its singular eye gleaming with menace. It lands on the ground before you, loosing out a threatening screech before its long neck involuntarily convulses and heaves up a glob of glimmering liquid.

Undeterred, the avian monster regains its composure, shrieks again, and lunges towards you with unbridled fury!
Ravine Outlet.ssummary: On our way out of the southern canyons we encountered a monstrous avian creature that seemed sick, vomiting up befouled ooze as we did battle with it.

Dusktide Destruction.name: Dusktide Destruction
Dusktide Destruction.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Social and Exploration Event occurs in the aftermath of the Otherhood attack on Helkas described in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event. This Event only occurs if the party was delayed in reaching Helkas and arrives later than 12:00am on Day 6, at which point the attack has already happened in the party's absence.

The town has been badly damaged and the party encounters the survivors trying to pick up the pieces. In this Event, the party can:

  • Examine the scene for clues, learning about the presence of the drakes and bandits.

  • Speak to the caravan members and learn their opinions on the attack.

Surveying The Destruction

The majority of the damage done to Helkas was through arson, with numerous fires being set across the town, resulting in large swaths of it burning to the ground. In terms of casualties, that is a more varied situation, with the dead and injured either being caught in fires or attacked by the invaders.

A Town In Ruin

Those approaching the scene notice the presence of a dead raider lying in the burned-out ruins of a shop, and the remains of a large drake laying in an alley next to a pair of townsfolk.

Any character who examines the scene and makes a successful [[/skill perception 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check reveals three elements at play in the attack:

  1. A monster attack (alternatively recognized using [[/knowledge monsters]]).

  2. A bandit raid (alternatively recognized using [[/knowledge crime]]).

  3. Arson and resulting fires (alternatively recognized using [[/knowledge forensics]]).

Any character who recognizes the elements above and makes a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 14]] check comes to the reasonable assumption that the attacking raiders likely used the monsters as a vanguard to soften the town's defenses before entering themselves.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] recognize the stench of accelerants and spot a few broken containers that would be used in the creation of alchemical fire. The fires would have been incredibly hard to stop when initially set due to how stubbornly such chemicals burn.

The Dead Drake

Once the party has finished surveying the destruction in general, they may wish to examine the defeated drake, which when alive was described as follows:

@Embed[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9 readaloud="This large, serpentine creature is covered in pale white-green scales with a prominent flared tail adorned with ragged, green frills. Its draconic head is set with long horns tipped in the same pale green hue, and halfway down its body are more wide, damaged frills. The Drake's eyes are a cloudy white, hinting at blindness, and its body is marred by unsettling yellow pustules emerging from ragged wounds.\nThe drake lies still on the ground, its long, coiling body covered in pale white-green scales and numerous wounds. Its large draconic head rests against the earth, cloudy white eyes staring vacantly at nothing as blood and saliva trickle from its slack maw, pooling on the ground. Midway down its body, wide, damaged frills hang over several arrows sunk deep into its side, and a broken spear juts from its belly. Numerous unsettling yellow pustules also mark its haggard form, their appearance separate from the wounds it suffered in battle."]

Dead Drake

Any character that examines a dead drake's corpse and makes a successful [[/skill medicine 14]][[/skillCheck medicine 14]] check reveals that this creature appeared to have been exceedingly ill during its life. It was likely in constant pain, and functionally — if not entirely — blind. You've never seen any kind of illness like this before. There are old scars that have healed over, and some especially rancid wounds on this drake that have been festering for some time. This drake was not just ill: it was chronically ill, possibly for most of its life.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character that examines the corpse's wounds and makes a successful [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] check confirms that this creature died from the collective wounds it suffered while battling the townsfolk. The fatal blow was likely the broken spear jammed into its gut.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who fought the sick drakeling in the Forest of Stone recognize this as the same sort, although the adult drake is a much older and larger specimen; it is a testament to the creatures' ferocity that they survived as long as they did while so sickened.

The Dead Raider

The presence of a dead bandit may also draw their attention, complicating their picture of the attack. While alive, this individual would have been described as follows:

@Embed[Actor.Geaj9bagPJdTicsk readaloud="These remains are what little is left of a wild-eyed fellow wearing scorched leather armor covered in dark metal studs and armored bandoliers packed with vials of unknown liquids. A strange marking — a tower wrapped in coils of rope — has been deeply imprinted in the material. Much of this raider's remains are strangely untouched by the flames despite laying in the midst of a burned out structure. Upon closer inspection their bloodstained, and ripped robes do show some scorch marks."]

Bandit Corpse

Any character that investigates the bandit's corpse and makes a successful [[/skill investigation 13]][[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] check notices the distinctive presence of a tattoo on their arm. It depicts a stylized gold coin with Arcden script and glints slightly in the light.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character that examines this tattoo and makes a successful [[/skill history 14]][[/skillCheck society 14 passive]] check recognizes that the coin tattoo says "For Other Fortunes," which is a play on an old Arcturian phrase about making changes to one's life; it is a shortened version of a catchphrase often used by pirates when pledging to a new ship: "I left my life for other fortunes — may they soon become my own."

They also notice that the ink of the tattoo is moving slightly as they look at it, indicating it may have magical properties.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge seafaring]] and characters who can understand [[/language arcden]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character that notices the tattoo's magical properties and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]][[/skillCheck arcana 14 passive]] check identifies the ink as a variant of "shifting ink," which is typically used to obscure documents, making them harder to decipher. The ink is not usually used on tattoos, and does not appear to have the same properties of changing the meaning of written text while on the body.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who examines the rope coil markings on the leather and makes a successful [[/skill history 13]][[/skillCheck society 13 passive]] check identify them as an elaborate maker's mark, used by crafters to drive business their way, but cannot tell whose mark it is.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberArcturian]], [[/knowledge trade]], or [[/path emberCaravanner]] automatically succeed on this check.

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] recognize the telltale signs of chemically treated clothing and equipment to make it fire resistant. As long as this equipment is in well-maintained order, you reason that it could afford significant capability to withstand the hazards of heat and flame. Unfortunately, the gear was utterly destroyed.

Speaking To Survivors

The party may wish to speak to other surviving townsfolk, however the opportunity to do so does not seem immediately appropriate.

Though there are many dead, the survivors are acting with determination and resolve to protect what is left of the town and its people. Townsfolk are milling about, ferrying water to quench fires and medicine for the wounded wherever it is most needed. You notice an altyran woman with a steeled expression coordinating most of the activity. She looks too busy and at too critical a juncture in her work to interrupt her now, but you take note that she is likely a local leader.

Firsthand Accounts

By speaking with other survivors, the party can learn the following details of what transpired.

  • The town was attacked just at midnight during the height of the Dusktide Festival. Prior to the attack, the festival had proceeded as expected without any remarkable deviations from the norm.

  • At first, a group of drakes appeared, attacking the townsfolk, and driving them indoors. A few of the local defenders fought desperately to scare them off or kill them. The defenders managed to kill one of the larger drakes, but it killed half a dozen people in the process.

  • At some point the fires began, and with it the bandits showed up. They took advantage of all the townsfolk being holed up inside to escape the drakes. This forced people to either sit in burning buildings, or rush out to face drakes and raiders.

  • The raiders seemed to know about the drakes, and were careful to avoid getting in their way. They didn't seem to be working directly together, however.

The town magistrate, Sadri Zhalimorne, is fully occupied with organizing the response to the attack. The party can observe her from a distance, but it is not possible to engage her in conversation at this time.

@Embed[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]

Thoughts From The Caravan

Once the party has surveyed the scene, they would be likely to share thoughts with their traveling companions from the Strayhearth Caravan for further insights or ideas on what may have happened.

Agraband

Agraband pauses from unloading belongings from his carts and meets your gaze with a steady but sorrowful expression.

I've never seen an attack like this directly on a town like Helkas. Yes, there's history of feuding groups in the Arctus Plateau, but never something as brazen as this. Strange things are brewing, and the clouds on the horizon seem to get bigger with every passing footfall.

I recommend you stick together and put your skills to use investigating and standing against this rising tide of chaos. In my experience, the world never fixes itself. It's up to us, those of us who can, to do something and make a difference.

In the meantime, I'm going to unload whatever supplies I can that will be put to good use here. Clipper and I will see to getting them into the hands of those who need them most.

Clipper

Clipper surveys the scene of Helkas' desolation with a frown, idly twirling a coin back and forth across the knuckles of their ethereal hand.

It's awful what has happened here at Helkas. In my experience, whenever something terrible like this happens, it ultimately comes down to someone, somewhere, who profited from it. Some people are just bad, but most of the time there's a reason. Most of the time, that reason is hard coin. If you want to do something about what happened here, start by asking yourselves, "Who is better off because Helkas was attacked?"

Lyla

Lyla appears distant, her expression reflecting worry about both current and past events. She remains deeply lost in thought until the sound of your approach jolts her back to awareness.

I've been hearing about attacks and disruptions on the Arctus Plateau, but this attack on Helkas is brazen. Helkas partners with House Cevher to some extent. For someone to be willing to subject it to such violence is unthinkable. Never mind the drake attacks, which are entirely new.

I was already worried about the state of things here in the Arctus Plateau, but I can't just let this stand. I think it's time that I start doing some more digging, try to see what's going on here.

Ankarist

Ankarist pores over the fallen attackers, the ruins of buildings, and the patterns of combat in the ruined spaces of Helkas like they still hold secrets for him to find. Beyond this there is a simmering frustration in his posture and movements.

I can't believe we weren't here — what wretched misfortune that we were delayed upon the road!

These events confirm some suspicions that I and my superiors have been exploring for several months now. There are strange new dangers emerging in the Arctus Plateau, and a degree of coincidence in their actions that is alarming. I must think on this for now and figure out what it means, and more importantly what to do next.

Sin

The young druidess looks personally harmed by the violence visited upon Helkas. The suffering of its people has seemingly rooted deep in her chest and grown into a powerful compassion which drives her to help all in her path. Yet there is something else in her eyes, something haunted and troubled beyond this violence.

It seems clear to me now — more than ever — that we need the Cindaric Sages. Terrible events like this cannot be allowed to happen so close to their seat in Ordain. They must be informed, or perhaps they already know and are setting plans in motion to help the people and set everything straight!

A grim look passes over Sin's usually innocent face.

I heard an extremely disturbing rumor that one of these raiders, at the moment of their death, exhibited some sort of spiritual corruption by which their soul was twisted and pulled forth from their body as a gruesome specter. Could such a thing have actually happened? Something like that would be an unnatural affront to the cycle.

Concluding the Event

All of the party's companions share the sentiment that they should spend some time looking around town for further clues.

Next Steps

Having arrived late to discover the brutal aftermath of the attack on Helkas, the party can now spend time investigating in more detail what happened here.

To continue the Quest, advance time by at least 1 hour or, if more suitable, a Long RestRest. A more thorough investigation of what transpired here occurs in the following Event, [[/eventState windingTrailSmoke]].
Dusktide Destruction.soverview: If the party arrives in Helkas after the Dusktide Festival, they discover that the town has been brutally attacked by fell drakes and mysterious raiders seemingly acting in concert. The town has been crippled by this attack, but the survivors are able to share some information on what transpired.
Dusktide Destruction.sexposition:
Where you expected to find a scene of celebration and frivolity, instead smoke hangs in the air around Helkas. It lingers in the gutted remains of scorched buildings, some of which still burn despite the townsfolk's best efforts. Bodies lie in the streets, their wounds ragged and bloody, adding another layer of horror to the scene.

In the town square, a hastily built infirmary churns with activity as the town council coordinates actions to help the injured and organize response teams to put out other fires. The faces of the townsfolk are grim and fixed, only shifting into momentary alarm when a new band of travelers arrives with unknown intentions.
Dusktide Destruction.ssummary: We arrived in Helkas after the Dusktide Festival only to discover that the town was brutally attacked by both monsters and raiders. We were too late to defend the town, but we investigated the scene and learned some initial clues about what transpired.

The Smoke Clears.name: The Smoke Clears
The Smoke Clears.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

All groups experience this Event regardless of whether they were present for the attack in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} Event or arrived afterwards in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.YfJF8Z5XAXFcKmiU]{Dusktide Destruction} Event.

After the immediate peril of the attack has subsided, the party can try to aid the town, speak with survivors, and consult their allies. Ideally, this Event occurs several hours after the attack or the following morning. The exact timing is flexible depending on what actions the party takes or when they arrived in Helkas. During this Event, the party can:

  • Speak with the town magistrate, @UUID[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]{Sadri Zhalimorne}, to receive a reward for their heroics.

  • Receive a request from Sadri to look into the safety of other nearby groups who may be in danger or also targeted in the recent attack.

  • Discuss the attack further with the companions in the Strayhearth Caravan and learn of what they intend to do next.

Talking to Sadri

Though there are many dead, enough survivors remain to eventually stabilize and rebuild Helkas. Chief among the survivors is the magistrate of Helkas, an altyran woman named Sadri Zhalimorne.

@Embed[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U readaloud="In the aftermath of the attack, Sadri is both distressed and deeply preoccupied with her duties. There is an air of grim determination about her, though the pain in her eyes is unmistakable."]

If the party was present for the [[/eventState windingTrailAttack]] Event.

We've never experienced anything like this before, much less during the Dusktide Festival. Who could possibly have wished to harm the people of Helkas? Those are questions for some other day. For now, we mourn and rebuild. We are tough folk. It will take a lot more than this to break our spirit.

Thanks to your heroics, these raiders and monsters only managed to wound our town, not raze it. If Agraband's caravan hadn't arrived when it did, then things could have been a lot worse.

We need as many supplies as we can get to prevent further damage and begin to rebuild — but we can spare whatever basic items you need for your continued journey. You put your lives on the line for this town, and we won't have it said that the people of Helkas were ingrateful.

Sadri will provide the party with up to [[/award 50gp]] [[/award 5gp]] worth of whatever basic items they need, whether that's healing kits, clothing, basic arms and armor, rations, or other supplies. They put their lives on the line for the town, and the town will see them paid back for it.

For their heroism during the assault, Sadri also names the party members as honorary "Stewards of Helkas", and bestows upon the characters a special ceremonial weapon — @UUID[Item.6rydBIZu93yNKdpd]{Duskmaw's Bite}. If no characters in the party have proficiency with Martial Weapons, the weapon offered is instead @UUID[Item.DJoeW6BgYarxKaKx]{Duskmaw's Gavel}. @UUID[Item.DJoeW6BgYarxKaKx]{Duskmaw's Gavel}. If no characters in the party have training with Heavy weapons, Sadri instead offers the @UUID[Item.6rydBIZu93yNKdpd]{Duskmaw's Bite}

If the party was absent and arrived in the [[/eventState windingTrailDestruction]] Event.

Perhaps it's a bit selfish of me to say, but it's a shame you folks weren't here sooner. Our little town might have fared better with some armed adventurers at our sides.

We've never experienced anything like this before, much less during the Dusktide Festival. Who could possibly have wished to harm the people of Helkas? Those are questions for some other day. For now, we mourn and rebuild. We are tough folk. It will take a lot more than this to break our spirit.

Thoughts on the attack?

I find it strange that the drakes and raiders came so close together, but I don't have time to worry about that right now. There are fires to put out, injured to heal, and bodies to bury before investigation can begin. It will take a lot more than this to put us down, though.

What now?

We rebuild. It will take a lot more than this to put us down.

Once it appears that the party has no further urgent questions for Sadri, she broaches a topic that has been concerning her since the attack.

Sadri's Request

Sadri is full of determination and resolve, but she is deeply concerned for other groups she knows of nearby in the Forest of Stone:

I don't know if you came across them while you were traveling, but there are miners out in Yakoshta and a group of Anachraenum explorers in the Forest of Stone. In light of recent attacks, I feel it's vital that we take steps to find out if they are okay or not. I don't have anyone to spare right now, but I'm prepared to hire you to go out there and check on them. I'll pay you for information on the status of both groups.

Sadri offers a further reward of [[/award 10gp each]] [[/award 1gp each]] in exchange for confirmation that the miners at @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta} and the Anachraenum expedition at the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.WG5PhLJbJ3Dvi4AP]{Ancient Door} are safe.

[[/outcome sadriRequest]]

Recommended Progression

Sadri's request to backtrack to the Forest of Stone is the recommended and canonical path for the party to take next. This allows the party to obtain the additional milestones needed to reach Level 3 before beginning Chapter 2.

It is possible for them to refuse, however, instead continuing onward to the [[/eventState windingTrailLeavetaking]] Event, although this will make the early gameplay of Chapter 2 somewhat more difficult.

Talking To Ankarist

Ankarist looks troubled by events, but behind his outward expression of concern there is an unmistakable fire as he is busily investigating the corpse of one of the felled drakes.

@Embed[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs readaloud="Ankarist pores over the fallen attackers, the ruins of buildings, and the patterns of combat in the ruined spaces of Helkas like they still hold secrets for him to find. Presently, Ankarist is busy examining the corpses of the slain drakes. Ankarist looks troubled by events, but behind his outward expression of concern there is an unmistakable fire."]

The Felled Drakes

The party can join Ankarist in investigating the body of the largest slain creature.

Any character that examines the corpse and makes a successful [[/skill nature 15]] or [[/skill survival 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check reveals that its physiology, pallid flesh, and milky eyes suggest that it likely developed and acclimated to an underground environment.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge dragons]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character that makes a successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check notices something that had escaped Ankarist's notice: a chunk of plant-like matter lodged underneath one of the drake's talons.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character that inspects the plant matter and makes a successful [[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check identifies the material as Lunderwort, a giant mushroom variety which only grows deep beneath the surface.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge plants]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character that speaks with Ankarist and makes a successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13 passive]] check intuits that the drakon is forming a plan and will act upon it soon.

Your thoughts?

These events confirm some suspicions that I and my superiors have been exploring for several months now. There are strange new dangers emerging in the Arctus Plateau, and a degree of coincidence in their actions that is alarming.

What now?

My plans must change. I was bound originally for Ordain, but this requires immediate investigation. The drakes in particular are an emerging menace which could be related to another investigation. I will be traveling north, to Skybrush, to seek the cavernous origin of these dragons.

Can we help?

It may be a long and difficult road — but your company would be welcome should you wish to join me. I would be glad of the reinforcement; these creatures are dangerous and the shadowy forces creating or controlling them likely more so. If you're interested in coming with me, I'll be leaving in a day or two.

Ankarist plans to take a few days to help the townsfolk, rest, and resupply. In the meantime, the party is afforded time to follow up on Sadri's request.

Talking To Lyla

Lyla is actively helping to coordinate the response and talking with townsfolk about what happened. The party may choose to join her.

@Embed[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP inline readaloud="Gathered with local leaders, foremen, and merchants, Lyla is speaking in a clear, firm voice, giving suggestions for repairs and administrative affairs. Yet watching closely, she is resting one hand on her rapier nervously, fiddling with its guard. The group scatters as you approach, and she brings her attention to you fully."]

Your thoughts?

I've heard about attacks and disruptions in the Arctus Plateau, but this attack on Helkas is without a doubt the most brazen incident I'm aware of. Never mind the drake attacks, which are entirely new. It seems there are plenty of new troubles to welcome me back.

Other troubles?

She sighs deeply and looks at you with deep pain in her eyes.

My father died… recently. That's part of the reason I'm heading home. His death was sudden, and I will have to take over running House Cevher. I also need to look after my younger brother. I know I should head back to the city as soon as possible, but I need to see what's happening in the Plateau and with some of our other operations. I'm sure my brother would understand.

What now?

I need to get to Ordain, but after this attack, I'm going to take a detour first. An old friend of mine lives a day's travel to the south, and they are… well… let's just say they are eminently knowledgeable about all manner of topics, and I could use their advice.

Can we help?

You're very capable adventurers, and I would welcome the help in figuring out what's happening here. These raiders may seem like simple bandits, but I fear there is something more sinister at play here. With your help, we can find out who they are, why they attacked Helkas, and what they have to do with the other troubles. I'm going to take a few days to help out here and pull together some supplies, but then I'll be on my way. If you're interested in coming with me, you're most welcome.

Lyla's Thoughts

Any character who speaks with Lyla and makes a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] check can ascertain that something more is bothering Lyla. If pressed, she will elaborate:

Something about this entire attack feels wrong, but more than that — it feels like it's just the beginning. I'm getting worried about the state of things here in the Arctus Plateau. I think it's time that I start doing some more digging, try to see what is going on here.

They can also intuit that there is more to Lyla's acquaintance than she is admitting. If pressed, she sheepishly admits:

Well, I don't like talking about it in these terms, but my friend is Sigil. He tends to keep a low profile, but he is… well, a Shard God, even if he doesn't act like one. He dwells in a place called Oldcraft Lodge by the shores of Lake Jinro to the south.

Characters who make a successful [[/skill religion 16]] [[/skillCheck society 16 passive]] check know the basic reputation of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE]{Sigil} as a Shard God of scholastic learning, research, and knowledge.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge gods]] and characters with [[/path emberShardGodDevotee]] automatically succeed on this check.

Like Ankarist, Lyla plans to take a few days to help the townsfolk, rest, and resupply. In the meantime, the party is afforded time to follow-up on Sadri's request.

Talking To Sin

The party notices that Sin is obviously exhausted by the ordeal, both physically and emotionally. She wears the distress of the attack plainly on her features, but the characters can also tell that the tenacious Keth druid is as determined as ever.

@Embed[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv inline readaloud="In the aftermath of the attack, Sin busies herself moving from one injured citizen to the next, offering food, water, bandages, and words of encouragement. The young druidess looks personally harmed by the violence visited upon Helkas. The suffering of its people has seemingly rooted deep in her chest and grown into a powerful compassion which drives her to help all in her path. Yet there is something else in her eyes, something haunted and troubled beyond this violence."]

Your thoughts?

Sin replies with great conviction.

It's clear to me more than ever that the Cindaric Sages are exactly where I need to be, and who I need to speak to about the specter. Not only are they the best hope to aid these struggling people, they would be the ones to shed some light on that apparition and what it means. I will be certain to tell the Sages what transpired here, and they will know what to do.

What now?

I'm going to head to the nearest Cindaric enclave. Sadri told me about a place called Corpin Sanctuary to the east. It's an outlying enclave of the Sages on the top of Mial Mountain. I've got to let them know what happened here at Helkas so they can send aid.

More importantly though, I need to talk to them about what happened to the bandit leader. Hopefully they have something more to tell me about this. From what I have gleaned from the locals, spirits rising from corpses has happened more than once in the area. If it's becoming more commonplace, then that could be a sign of something way worse brewing.

The bandit's death?

If Sin directly witnessed Bassa's death:

Earlier, during the raider attack, I saw a spirit erupt from the chest of a dead bandit, then transform into a specter before being ripped away by some unseen force. According to the locals, this isn't the first time it's happened, either.

If Sin heard about it secondhand:

I heard an extremely disturbing rumor that one of these raiders, at the moment of their death, exhibited some sort of spiritual corruption by which their soul was twisted and pulled forth from their body as a gruesome specter. Could such a thing have actually happened? Something like that would be an unnatural affront to the cycle.

Either way, Sin is deeply concerned about what this means:

This might be a sign of something far worse brewing in the region, something corrupting the natural order of things. It's clear to me more than ever that the Cindaric Sages are exactly where I need to be. They are the best hope to aid these struggling people, and I must inform them about the issues with the restless dead if they don't already know.

Unnatural Death

Any character who speaks with Sin and makes a successful [[/skill religion 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15 passive]] check agrees that the dead should remain dead, and any instances of their spirits manifesting, or rising as specters, ghosts or worse — animating — are signs that something is horribly amiss. Alerting the Sages would be wise.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] automatically succeed on this check.

Can we help?

I'm a little nervous to travel on my own, not knowing the region and all. If you wanted to come with me, I'd be glad to walk at your side. You were headed toward Ordain anyway, weren't you? Well now you have another good reason to go; these folk need help and we can make sure they get it! I'm going to leave in a couple days, once I've done all I can to help the folk here myself.

Though Sin wants to remain in Helkas and help the townsfolk, she also recognizes that now more than ever she needs to make contact with the Cindaric Sages. Not only can they send aid to Helkas, she needs to inform them about rumors and concerns that have been going around the town, and coming in with travelers: strange things are happening with the dead. Like the other companions, Sin will delay their departure until after aid has been provided to the people of Helkas, taking several days to provide whatever assistance they can before heading onward.

Talking To Agraband

@Embed[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw readaloud="Agraband looks a touch haggard and affected by the events that struck Helkas. He stands upon the green at the center of town, providing encouragement and comfort to the wounded or frightened townsfolk."]

Thoughts on the Attack?

Any character who speaks with Agraband and makes a successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] check notices that Agraband is more keenly affected than he outwardly portrays. This suggests that the old bard wasn't ready for his tales of daring and adventure made manifest in front of him today. If asked about it, he laughs it off:

It's a long time since I was in a fight like that. Good show!

Agraband has been mulling over how to turn it into a story worthy of the events that unfolded here today. Agraband looks at you with pride and gloats:

The more I think about what happened here, the more I'm certain this needs to be captured in a grand tale. This was important! It was a key moment in the history of Helkas, and someone ought to record it.

I was right about you. I could see the sparks of greatness in you as soon as we departed Casla-Brava! You are proper heroes in the making, with plenty of fascinating adventures ahead, I'm sure!

What Now?

Agraband isn't planning to leave Helkas immediately. He does have some shipments and contracts to fulfill in Ordain, but he has time before he needs to get moving again. For now, he's going to help the locals sort out the damage, lend a hand where he can, and collect accounts from people here.

You should head on without old Agraband. Now that we're out of the Forest of Stone, you don't really need my guidance anymore. Head for Ordain, if that's still your destination, or venture out into the unknown and see what you find! There's a rising tide of chaos in the Plateau lately, and you can probably help make a difference!

Agraband bids the party farewell with wishes for luck and fortune:

If you do end up in Ordain — look for me around the markets of the Main Plaza. I hope to run into you again and hear about what adventures you've gotten up to!

Talking To Clipper

@Embed[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ readaloud="In the aftermath of the attack on Helkas, Clipper is taking cues from Agraband and helping the locals however she can. However, unlike her mentor, this help doesn't prevent her from collecting a little coin for her help, even if it earns her a look or two from the locals."]

Thoughts on the Attack?

Any character who speaks with Clipper and makes a successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] check notices that Clipper doesn't seem terribly fazed by the events here. Asking Clipper about it confirms that suspicion.

Suffering and violence are a part of the world. If you let it affect you deeply, then you are just suffering alongside them. Better to keep some distance while offering help where you can!

If asked about why they're charging for their goods and services, they point out:

Just because times are tough doesn't mean I should put myself in dire straits as well! I'm not heartless though. I'm charging far less than I normally would.

What Now?

Clipper plans to head off in search of new opportunities. They don't know exactly what direction yet, but they'll search for whatever is out there to be traded, bought, studied, and sold again!

Agraband is staying here, so I'm off on my own for now. Time to search for new opportunities — whichever way the winds decide to carry me. What direction that will be… remains unknown … but I'm excited to see what is out there to be found, traded, bought, studied, and sold!

If we're lucky, we'll cross paths again, because I know you'll have interesting stories and items to trade, and I look forward to both!

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished talking to the townsfolk and their companions, they're free to move on. They have two choices at this point:

  • They can accept Sadri's request and backtrack to the Forest of Stone to confirm that the miners at Yakoshta and the Anachraenum expedition are both unharmed. If the party accepts Sadri's quest, be sure to mark the "Sadri's Request" outcome as completed.

  • They can press onward with Ankarist, Lyla, and Sin — departing Helkas together and moving toward the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.wL4CB6fnuy0XJziF]{Leavetakings} Event that concludes Chapter 1. Once the party is ready to depart Helkas eastward toward Ordain, follow the steps described below.

Regardless of which path the party is now following, you may mark this Event as Complete; however, if the party decides to travel toward Ordain, be sure to take note of the actions listed under @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.fFtsG83gvrlyz3KY#departing-together]{Departing Together}, which are necessary to unlock the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.wL4CB6fnuy0XJziF]{Leavetakings} Event that concludes Chapter 1.

[[/outcome departed]]

Departing Together

When the party is ready to depart Helkas for Ordain, take the following specific actions:

  1. Mark the "Departed Helkas" Event outcome as completed.

  2. Add @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}, @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher}, and @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} to the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party} caravan.

  3. You may remove the @UUID[Actor.emberStrayhearth]{Strayhearth Caravan} from play.

  4. Begin traveling along the eastern road towards Ordain. The [[/eventState windingTrailLeavetaking]] Event will occur after crossing the first bridge or upon the party's first Long RestRest.
The Smoke Clears.soverview: In the aftermath of the attack on Helkas, the party can speak to the townsfolk and their allies and determine what to do next.
The Smoke Clears.sexposition:
The immediate urgency of the attack on Helkas has faded, but the air lingers thick with the acrid scent of charred wood and smoke, mingling with the cries and murmurs of wounded townsfolk. Despite the destruction, a palpable sense of relief weaves through the town in the aftermath of the attack. Helkas was spared a far worse fate thanks to the dogged efforts of its defenders.

Groups of rescuers move through the rubble, tending to the injured with makeshift bandages and salves, their faces a mix of exhaustion and gratitude. Buckets of water are passed hand-to-hand, dousing the stubborn embers that threaten remaining structures. In the town square, a hastily built infirmary buzzes with activity as the town council coordinates actions to help the injured and organize response teams to put out other fires.
The Smoke Clears.ssummary: In the aftermath of the attack we spoke with various people from the Strayhearth Caravan and the town of Helkas. There's not much for us to do in town, but its magistrate, Sadri Zhalimorne, has tasked us to seek out others in the region who may be in danger.

Leavetakings.name: Leavetakings
Leavetakings.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Social Event occurs on the road east of Helkas where the party has traveled alongside their Strayhearth companions of Ankarist, Lyla, and Sin. If following the road, this Event will occur specifically when reaching hex s.3208.2880. If departing from the trail, this Event will occur whenever the party next takes a Long RestRest.

The time has come for the three friends to now go their own ways and the party must make a pivotal choice about which companion, if any, to accompany further. In this Event, the party can:

  • Enjoy a final meal with the friends before parting ways.

  • Learn of Ankarist's plan to seek out the legendary Mythspire Observatory.

  • Learn of Lyla's plan to visit the Shard God Sigil in search of knowledge.

  • Learn of Sin's plan to journey to the Cindaric enclave of Corpin Sanctuary.

Ultimately, the party must make a final choice about which path to follow. This decision will dictate the majority of gameplay they experience in Chapter 2.

Exclusive Choices

It is intended that groups playing Ember do not experience all of the content the game has to offer. This is the first moment in the game where the players must choose one plotline to explore in detail at the expense of others.

Before Parting

The party stops to rest, taking a moment to share a brief meal and exchange farewells as their paths diverge. The party and their companions take some time to reminisce and solidify their newfound friendship before parting ways.

Ankarist's Test of Wit

Ankarist tests the party's wit with a series of riddles.

Any character who listens to Ankarist's riddles and makes a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check can answer each of them correctly, impressing the drakon.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] and characters with [[/path emberAcademyDropout]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who counter-challenges Ankarist with a riddle of their own and makes a successful [[/skill deception 18]][[/skillCheck deception 18]] check stumps the drakon.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] and characters with [[/path emberAcademyDropout]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Lyla's Test of Taste

Lyla asks everyone about their favorite foods. She talks about a few of the best dishes she’s had during her travels and how they differ from what’s served at her favorite restaurants in Ordain.

Any character who speaks with Lyla and makes a successful [[/skill insight 14]][[/skillCheck diplomacy 14 passive]] check can tell that Lyla is subtly attempting to assess both how adventurous they are and how familiar they are with Ordain.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] automatically succeed on this check.

Lyla loves the spicy fish stew found in Storsa’s Strand, which she thinks is more flavorful than the Ordain variety, and wonders what might be in their famous recipe. Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 15]][[/skillCheck society 15]] check can impress Lyla by guessing at the ingredients; later, they can work with her to try to recreate some of the taste by adding spice to the current night's meal.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] automatically succeed on this check.

Lyla is looking forward to a dish of Fried Kintavi Leaves at the Ordani restaurant Shine, which she greatly missed while away. Characters with [[/culture emberOrdani]] may know the savory appetizer or the restaurant; alternatively, they can share their own Ordani favorites, creating a stronger connection with her.

Sin's Test of Nature

Sin shows off her animal impersonation skills using@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.aL1F8fvYLtNzUbKu]{Speak with Animals} ,[[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]], challenging the party to identify birds as she imitates their calls. She starts with easily recognizable calls but then tests the party with a range of obscure avian sounds from the depths of the Corebright Forest.

Any character who listens to Sin and makes a successful [[/skill nature 17]] check are able to identify most of the birds that Sin imitates, impressing her greatly.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] and characters with [[/path emberPrimalistDisciple]] automatically succeed on this check.

Characters who match Sin's own spellcraft with their own usage of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.aL1F8fvYLtNzUbKu]{Speak with Animals} [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] can carry on a full conversation with Sin, crafting a duet of birdsongs that resonate across the plains.

Resolved to their separate paths, each of the Strayhearth companions makes a final appeal to the party in the hopes that they will remain in their company.

Ankarist's Investigation

@Embed[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]

Music: Ankarist's Theme

Whilst conversing with Ankarist about his next steps, play [[/soundscape music ankaristTheme ankaristTheme]].

Ankarist presents the group with a summary of the evidence he has collected about the origin of the drakes that attacked Helkas.

The creatures are biologically draconic, without question, and their physiology is most similar to that of Vile Dragons, which are especially despicable creatures. Their blinded eyes and pale skin suggest that they grew up in lightless environments, such as caves or in the Pathways. However, it might also be an effect of whatever is making them ill.

My superiors in the Veiled Chain are already tracking several incidents regarding sightings of similar creatures emerging from the cavernous Pathways in the Plateau, which reinforces the theory that they originated somewhere beneath the Arctus Plateau.

The closest entrance to the Pathways that I am certain of is nowhere near where we are now — the creatures must have come from somewhere else. I have a contact nearby in the Rustvar Valleys hamlet of Skybrush, a Kivahr named Liestra Grann. She deals in antiquities and is knowledgeable about all manner of ruins, tombs, and caverns in the area.

The party can consider the evidence Ankarist has presented.

Considering the Evidence

Any character who considers Ankarist's evidence and makes a successful [[/skill medicine 14]] or [[/skill survival 14]][[/skillCheck medicine 14]] or [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check can reasonably conclude that Ankarist's hypothesis regarding the origin of the drakes seems reasonable.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] or [[/knowledge dragons]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who recalls information about the Pathways and make a successful [[/skill survival 15]][[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check concludes that it's likely there are other places nearby that would allow the drakes to exit the Pathways, and would lead to their den or nest.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge tracking]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who considers the most likely place to find an entrance to the Pathways and makes a successful [[/skill nature 16]][[/skillCheck wilderness 16]] check recalls that the Wedgelands to the north are a natural place to find a fissure or passage that could reach down into the Pathways.

Ankarist urges the party to accompany him on this quest:

Ankarist gazes at the horizon to the north. In the distance you see the dramatic peaks of the Wedgelands protruding out from the plains like spiked teeth against the sky.

No doubt it will be a long, tough trip, and I'd be glad to have some allies at my back. These creatures are dangerous and I'm not relishing the idea of going into the Pathways alone. There's plenty more than drakes to worry about there. I could use the backup.

Your story?

I spent my youth in the Tayan Empire, getting mired in politics and scheming. Ultimately that life was not for me, and I left in search of something different. I found a different calling and a different purpose that led me to Ordain, where I have lived now for many years. It turned out that the Veiled Chain had need of my particular mixture of skills and I found myself well suited to the work.

The Veiled Chain?

The Veiled Chain is one of the branches of government in Ordain. It's the investigative arm responsible for resolving some of the most severe issues that the city faces. We get involved in cases where community enforcement of laws fails or is incapable of handling the situation.

Your interest in dragons?

Enough to know they are bad news. I saw the carnage they are capable of firsthand during my time in the Tayan Empire. I'm not sure which are more dangerous, wild ones or those bound in service to the Empress. In either case, wherever dragons appear, bloodshed swiftly follows.

About your magic?

I suppose you could say I have a knack for sorcery, and I've picked up a few tricks here and there. Mostly things to help with my work. Most non-magical crime can be solved by the Ordani community without getting the Veiled Chain involved, but when there's a dangerous spellcaster in play it's important to understand a bit of arcana. I've put one or two outlaw mages in Spellbreaker Tower myself.

Ankarist's Power

Any character with a [[/skill insight 18 passive format=long]] or who make a successful [[/skill 16 insight]] checkwho makes a successful [[/skillCheck deception 18 passive]] check senses that Ankarist is not being entirely forthcoming about the nature of his arcane capabilities.

The true source of your power?

Ankarist scowls and his expression darkens slightly.

I suppose my explanation didn't fully satisfy you.

He shakes his head wistfully before a vaguely approving smile softens his expression.

You show the instincts of an investigator!

This is a private matter, and it's nothing that need concern you or that will affect our time together. I will share with you, however, that I have a patron who has been valuable in cultivating my capabilities. I'll speak no more of it now, but perhaps if we journey together I will have opportunity to confide in you further.

Main Quest Themes

If the party joins Ankarist, they will embark upon the Main Quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100], which will take them north to Skybrush, Mythspire Observatory, and the subterranean Pathways below. This quest is a great fit for groups who enjoy dungeon exploration and combat against formidable adversaries.

[[/outcome ankarist]]

Lyla's Mentor

@Embed[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]

Music: Lyla's Theme

Whilst conversing with Lyla about her next steps, play [[/soundscape music lylaTheme lylaTheme]].

Lyla entreats the party to join her as she investigates the bandits. She's convinced that there's something bigger at work and would welcome the help to figure it out.

I just don't understand. Why attack Helkas? Why the Dusktide Festival? Right now the only thing I know for certain is that this isn't some isolated group of brigands attacking whatever they see. Something more sinister is at play.

I know we haven't been traveling together that long, but I've seen the way you handle yourself, and I'm about to put myself right in the middle of something. I'd love for you to come with me and help me figure things out. When we get to Ordain, I'll compensate you for your trouble.

Luckily, we have a few leads to work with, and I know where to go to sort them all out. Oldcraft Lodge. Sigil — yes, that Sigil, the god of books — knows more about what's happening in the Arctus Plateau than anyone else I know. He's a dear friend and was always kind to me in the past, almost like a mentor, and we could all use some direction right now.

Lyla continues to share several clues that she gleaned while investigating the bodies at Helkas.

The Coded Instructions

Several of the bandits were carrying instructions written in code, but something about the ink they were written in makes it nearly impossible to break. If decoded, the notes could lead to the bandits' leader.

This was a coordinated attack. The bandits had to know what to do, where to go, and when to strike. These notes they were carrying probably have those instructions, but I can't break the code — probably something to do with this odd ink they're written in. Sigil may well know more about that — his whole expertise as a Shard God is things that are written down.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]][[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check knows that the ink used is probably shifting ink, a type of magical ink used by some thieves and spies to make codes harder to decipher. Codes written in shifting ink usually require something special to be done in order to decode them, which only those who carry the coded message know.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] and character who can understand [[/language cant]] automatically succeed on this check.

The Leather Markings

The bandits' leather gear had distinctive markings of a tower with a thick rope wrapped around it that likely point back to whoever crafted it. If Lyla can figure out whose mark it is, they could find the bandits' supplier.

I made a sketch of the markings on the bandits' gear. Most of them had the markings on them, and the leather was expensive. Someone is supplying it. I'm sure we can figure out who.

Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] know that the markings indicate that the person who crafted this leather is in a town on or near the Elenain River.

The Strange Saying

Several of the bandits had tattoos on them of a stylized gold coin with Arcden script that reads, "For Other Fortunes." It's possible that the saying has an origin or significance that could lead to their base of operations.

Then there are these tattoos that several of the bandits had. These strange gold coins. They used the same ink as what was in their notes, but this time the text was fully readable. "For Other Fortunes." I'm just not sure why it's significant. But don't worry — with Sigil's help, and yours, I know I can puzzle it out.

The party may have already deciphered the origin of the phrase while examining the bandit corpse in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.pjYncskqemOD6c6P]{Dusktide Rising} or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai.JournalEntryPage.YfJF8Z5XAXFcKmiU]{Dusktide Destruction} Events. However, its significance won't become clear until later.

Lyla's Motives

The party knows that Lyla is returning to Ordain because of her father's recent death, however they might suspect there is more to the story.

  1. Rumors of attacks in the area have spread through the caravan, but this is more organized than any she has seen before.

  2. The odd drakes are concerning, but she plans to focus on the bandits.

  3. She's been away from the Arctus Plateau trying to learn new skills to modernize House Cevher's business practices and to boost her own confidence.

  4. She has returned to the Arctus Plateau on her way to Ordain because of her father's recent death.

Any character who considers Lyla's motives and makes a successful [[/skill insight 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14]]check knows that there is something else about her return to Ordain that is on Lyla's mind.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who presses Lyla for more information and makes a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]][[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check persuades her to share what is weighing on her.

Why do you care?

I know I've been away for a few years in Casla-Brava, but an attack on a town so closely associated with my own house? It should be unthinkable — it's in everyone's best interests to keep trade flowing. If someone thinks they can target a place so closely tied to House Cevher, I need to know who they are and why.

What's on your mind?

To be honest… I'm heartbroken over my father's death. I should have been there with him these last few years. I suppose it doesn't matter now, though, and it's my responsibility to be the future of the House. But I can't shake the feeling that if I were home in Ordain, I could have stopped this from happening.

The least I can do now is figure things out and show my father that my time away was worth it. All I can do now is honor what he cared about most — House Cevher's success.

Lyla and Sigil

If parties want to know more about Sigil, or Lyla's relationship with Sigil, she's willing to share.

  • Sigil is known as the "god of books," a Shard God dedicated to knowledge who maintains a large arcane library at Oldcraft Lodge.

  • Lyla spent many days at Oldcraft Lodge in her youth when her father was attending to House Cevher business in the Plateau. Sigil looked after her and served as a mentor and teacher, as a favor to her father Ralton, though Lyla doesn't know why the two were friends.

  • Sigil is very welcoming but also sometimes very confusing. If the party can't follow everything he says, they are in good company.

Any character who considers what they know of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.q1ZQkDuvlTY1lzaE]{Sigil} and makes a successful [[/skill religion 16]][[/skillCheck society 16]] check recalls the basic reputation of the Shard God as one of scholastic learning, research, and knowledge.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge gods]] and characters with [[/path emberShardGodDevotee]] automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who reads into Lyla's words and makes a successful[[/skill insight 14]][[/skillCheck deception 14]] check intuits that Lyla is being honest about her relationship with Sigil and thinks of him fondly.

Who is Sigil?

When I first met Sigil, I thought he was a little… crazy? The amount of information and knowledge that he's able to collect and study all at once is incredible, and it lets him make connections between things that seem unrelated in a way that no one else can. He's just a little difficult sometimes, and has an odd way of conversing with others. With any luck, he'll at least have a clue as to why these bandits struck Helkas.

Relationship with Sigil?

I spent long days throughout my childhood at Oldcraft Lodge; he was my teacher and mentor. It took me some time to understand him, but once I was able to keep up, he gave me a place to rest and a book to read. Trade in the Early Days of Ordain & the Fall of House Komric. That book led to another, then another, and another. He gradually became a mentor and a dear friend. I'm glad I'll get to see him again.

Sigil's help?

With so much information rattling around in his head, Sigil sometimes loses track of what he's saying or goes off on tangents, and his mind seems to whirl around and around. The important thing is not to let it fool you. In the end, he usually has exactly what you need, even if it takes him a little while to find it.

Main Quest Themes

If the party decides to journey with Lyla, they will embark upon the Main Quest @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu], which will take them south to Oldcraft Lodge, Arcturel, Nain, and Seawall. This quest is a great fit for groups who enjoy political intrigue and subterfuge.

[[/outcome lyla]]

Sin's Pilgrimage

@Embed[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]

Music: Sin's Theme

Whilst conversing with Sin about her next steps, play [[/soundscape music sinTheme sinTheme]].

Sin Marmot is disturbed by the attack on the Dusktide Festival and the unsettling evidence of necromancy that surfaced in the aftermath. She appeals to the party to accompany her eastward to Corpin Sanctuary and Ordain, where she can deliver news about the events in Helkas to the Speaker at Cindarin Temple.

Sin Marmot looks tired, as though sleep has been elusive. However, she appears relieved to see you, and very obviously has something on her mind. After taking a moment to collect her thoughts, she speaks quietly.

Normally, when a person dies on Ember, their spirit travels to a plane of death called the Spiritlands, where they awaken to experience an afterlife. Spirits shouldn't be appearing outside the Spiritlands after death, and they certainly shouldn't be transforming into specters. It was like something snatched the spirit out of a body before it could move on naturally.

I've traveled a long way to get here, and there are plenty of miles left in these little feet of mine. I'll get to Corpin Sanctuary and Ordain just fine on my own. All the same, though, I think that you should come with me. Wild creatures and unsavory people are matters of concern, to be sure, but this … this is something bigger. Something unnatural, and something truly wrong.

Sin looks eastward with a troubled stare, and then smiles as if she has momentarily set her concerns to rest.

And to be honest, I would very much like to have some companions for the road. It's a big world out there, and it's best to have friends with whom to share the trail. You are still planning to go to Ordain, aren't you?

Matters of Life and Death

Sin is willing to discuss matters of Ember's soul cycle with the party in more detail.

Any character who speaks with Sin and makes a successful [[/skill religion 15]][[/skillCheck society 15]] check can confirm this effectively summarizes the understood cycle of life and death. Something subverting that natural order is absolutely cause for concern.

[[/culture emberLumek]] characters know that their homeland is under direct siege by legions of the undead commanded by powerful beings that are able to raise and control them. The Lumek dedicate many resources and lives to fighting this expansion. The incident in Helkas could be a sign that necromancy is spreading, or a new source of undeath has appeared.

Any character who considers this unnatural phenomenon and makes a successful [[/skill arcana 16]][[/skillCheck arcana 16]] check recalls that the only school of magic capable of capturing spirits or animating the dead is Necromancy. Such spells are not taught by reputable sources; Necromancy is openly reviled in most places, and often outright illegal. Furthermore, the ability to wield such magic takes great arcane prowess — or an immense source of external power.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] or [[/knowledge undeath]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 20+: Critical Success: Necromancy is abyssal in nature, horribly corruptive — not only for the user, but to Ember itself. The magic is as close to innately evil as anything can be.

Undeath?

Normally it just doesn't happen, it's not the natural order of things. However, I asked around a bit, and apparently that's not the first time people have seen something like this happen, and it's even more common in other places in the region… so there's clearly something going on, and it's not at all good.

What happened?

We don't know much. A spirit emerging from a corpse, thrashing, wailing, then dissipating. It almost looked like a spirit being ripped out, or destroyed. I don't know what caused it or what the source was. That's all beyond me.

From what I understand, which is not a lot, normal magic can't really do that. It takes special knowledge and forces to control the dead and manipulate souls, which makes this whole situation that much more concerning!

Sin's Intentions

Any character who reads into Sin's words and makes a successful [[/skill insight 14]][[/skillCheck deception 14]] check senses that Sin is deeply concerned with the safety of Ember and its people. She believes with ironclad conviction that the Cindaric Sages can help, and that they will have answers for what is happening.

[[/culture emberStrider]] characters or those with [[/knowledge souls]] or [[/knowledge undeath]] can likely empathize with Sin's concern. Any part of the natural cycle being subverted or broken is dangerous; it can lead to the collapse of other systems, changes in the natural order which might not be correctable, and could result in disaster.

Your beliefs?

I grew up in the Corebright, was inducted into the Primalists at a young age, and was one of the few that went beyond just communing with nature and actually harnessing the Growth, which is what they called the power flowing from the Core of the world. I was able to connect with the Corebright itself, and that left me with the sensation that there was some deeper connection I could forge, but the Primalists don't know how to do that. They don't focus on the Core, just how nature is affected by it.

Why the Cindaric Sages?

I met a traveling Cindaric Sage who was visiting the Corebright to learn about how the Primalists viewed and connected with the world there. Naturally, he and I worked and traveled together often. He had endless questions for me, and I picked his brain on a daily basis.

He often spoke of connection to the Heart of Ember itself, and how the Lifeforce flowed from it. This is basically identical to what the Primalists believe, but the Sages engaged in a tireless pursuit of connecting to and understanding the Heart of Ember. They go beyond just the world that grows around us, and focus on the source of it all.

That's what I was after. Once it became clear I'd learned all I could from my friend, I set out for Ordain to see if the Cindaric Sages can teach me more about Ember and its Heart.

Cindarics and Primalists

Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] understand what Sin is talking about and can contribute their own understanding of the subject. The concept of Lifeforce is nearly identical for the two faiths, but they focus on different aspects of it.

Main Quest Themes

If the party decides to escort Sin, they embark upon the Main Quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1], which will take them east to Corpin Sanctuary and the metropolis of Ordain beyond. This quest is a great fit for heroic groups who want to do good, confront evil, or reach Ordain as swiftly as possible.

[[/outcome sin]]

Concluding the Event

Before completing this Event, the party must make a decision about which path to follow, marking one of the Event outcomes at the expense of the others.

Forging your own Path

If the party chooses to forge their own path, there is plenty in the world for them to find, although they will miss out on some of the game's iconic gameplay and milestone progression. Accompanying one of the Strayhearth companions is encouraged.

[[/outcome none]]

Next Steps

The next steps after this Event depend on the choice the party has made. It is recommended, especially for groups playing Ember for the first time, to travel with one of the companions as the narrative and experience will be richer.
