  • With Ankarist, the party will begin Chapter 2 with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100]{Ancient Paths} Main Quest.

  • With Lyla, the party will begin Chapter 2 with the @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu]{An Old Friend} Main Quest.

  • With Sin, the party will begin Chapter 2 with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1]{Crumbling Sanctuary} Main Quest.

If the party chose to travel separately, they will not experience these Main Quests, but there are numerous Chapter 2 Side Quests to encounter as well as opportunities to reunite with each companion at a later point.

Milestone

Completing this Event awards a Milestone Point, likely advancing the party to Level 3.
Leavetakings.soverview: After departing Helkas with their traveling companions, Ankarist, Lyla, and Sin, the party reaches a fork in the road where their paths must diverge. The party must make a pivotal choice about which companion, if any, to accompany further.
Leavetakings.sexposition:
As you put several miles of travel between yourselves and the settlement of Helkas, the coiling tendrils of smoke which marked the aftermath of the attack disappear against the horizon, which gives way toward the endless golden landscape of the Arcturian heartland.

Lyla stares at the horizon to the south, seemingly lost in thought, as she contemplates the tangled mystery which called her back to her home after so many years away.

Eyes fixed on the eastward trail before you, the diminutive figure of Sin strides forward with determination. The fabric of their half-mask ripples in the breeze and their gait suggests a mixture of trepidation and excitement at the prospects of the open road ahead.

The distinctive silhouette of Ankarist, who scouted the road ahead, is illuminated against the northern horizon. The Drakon spots your approach and beckons you to join him.
Leavetakings.ssummary: We shared a final meal with Ankarist, Lyla, and Sin before heading our separate ways. We made a choice about which path to follow, each of our companions resolute to pursue answers about what happened in Helkas.

A Sticky Situation.name: A Sticky Situation
A Sticky Situation.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This standalone event set in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} occurs when the characters are moving at a fast or reckless pace, and puts them face-to-face with two monstrous arachnids. In this standalone event, the party must:

  • Avoid damage and disorientation as they tumble down into a overgrown gulley during a sudden landslide.

  • Survive an untimely attack from two @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV]{Sitherian}, who lair in a small cave nearby.

  • Search the cave for assorted loot from previous victims of the predatory arachnids.

This event takes place on the @UUID[Scene.emberForestedCli]{Verdant Paths} area map.

The unstable earth beneath the party's feet gives away causing the group to tumble down a small embankment into a gully.

Tumble in the Rough

Each character must succeed on a [[/save Dexterity 15]] to avoid taking [[/roll 1d3]] points of bludgeoning damage face a [[/hazard 4 reflex bludgeoning]]{Minor Rockslide} from the sudden but sloped fall. Any character who fails this save by more than 10 also gains the &Reference[prone] @Condition[prone] condition.

While they've already spied one of the creatures, there are a total of two @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV]{Sitherian} here: the initial assailant in the cliffside cave to the southeast, and another hidden Sitherian among the foliage to the northwest.

Arachnid Attack!

Characters with [[/skill perception 17 passive format=long]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] are able to spot the hidden Sitherian to the northwest, who will attempt to engage the party unseen. While the Sitherian remains hidden, it has advantage on attacks against enemy characters who fail to detect it.

Sitherian Tactics

The two arachnids are hungry and eager to attack the party.

They will target the characters they perceive as the greatest threat with their @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.U0Ydv7sK1ImlRpFD]{Web} attack, rapidly closing in to @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.SuRAERXystPvC7Ci]{Bite} those they manage to restrain or any characters who otherwise engage them in melee combat.

Sitherian are relatively intelligent creatures, and will readily gang up on a targets they deem worthy of a quick take-down. At the start of combat, the two monstrous beasts are positioned to be able to close in on the party via a pincer attack, and will use this positioning - including strategic elevation and the @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.L7pVyyloHg1QFI2A]{Spider Climb} feature - to their advantage.

If one of the Sitherian is killed, the other will attempt to retreat from combat using the Disengage and Dash actions if its hit points drop below 10.

They will attack the character deemed the most vulnerable or who poses the greatest threat, rapidly converging to use their @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.venomousBite0000], working together to gain the benefits of @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.packhunter000000].

If additional challenge is desired, the Gamemaster can rule that the Sitherian have created some sections of webbing using @UUID[Actor.TxHL5k4PNCu9NvXV.Item.webSpinner000000] prior to the beginning of combat.

If either Sitherian becomes @Condition[broken] or if their companion is killed, they will attempt to retreat from combat and preserve their lives. They will utilize the rugged terrain and their ability to quickly climb to escape from harm.

If the characters think to search the small cliffside cave during the battle, they may find a few accoutrements that could prove useful to them during combat. Otherwise, the dank lair of these Sitherian awaits scrutiny after the fight.

Dank and strewn with aged webbing, this small cliffside cave appears to be the private lair of the large arachnid beasts who just attacked you. The fragmented skeletons of several smaller creatures hang suspended in the webs, and there is a pervasive odor of musky decay here. Your skin crawls with apprehension during each moment you spend amidst this dismal shelter.

Exploration Topic Title

Any character who takes the time to search the cave will spot some @UUID[Item.XewoieHSHYTb5C0t]{Spider-cap Mushrooms} growing from rotted webbing and decaying molted husks of the Sitherian who dwelt here. A successful [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check allows a character to harvest [[/roll 1d3+1 #Mushroom Samples]] usable samples of the rare ingredient.

The first character to succeed on a [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check while searching the cave will also locate the desiccated corpse of an ill-fated humanoid in the webbing, with the following items to be found upon it:

  • A mold-covered but still effective @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPotionofHea]{Potion of Healing} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingTonic0000]{Healing Tonic}.

  • [[/roll 1d2]] random results on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot} Table.
A Sticky Situation.soverview: While traveling quickly along the Verdant Paths, the party happens upon an ill-timed landslide, which deposits the characters within a small gulley marked by extensive foliage and a small, covert cave. As the characters collect themselves and assess damages from the fall, they're beset by the ravenous creatures that calls the cave home - two predatory, eight-legged Sitherian with eyes hungry for humanoid flesh.
A Sticky Situation.sexposition:
As you make your way through the overgrowth of the Verdant Paths, you suddenly notice the distinct sounds of cracking stone and crumbling earth before the ground gives way beneath your very feet. In an instant, you find yourself pulled downward amidst the gravel and detritus of a landslide, which deposits you into a small gulley a few dozen feet below the road you were on.

You look up to notice a small cave mouth yawning at you from the cliffside to the southeast. The amber glow of ten beady eyes emerges from the dark hollow, followed by the hideous body of a large eight-legged creature. The arachnid's inhuman eyes are obviously set upon you, and it scurries forth from its dark rimrock den with hungry intention.
A Sticky Situation.ssummary: As we made our way through the Verdant Paths at a rushed pace, we found ourselves besieged by the sudden hazards of a landslide, which deposited us into an overgrown gulley. Before we knew what was happening, two monstrous arachnid beasts attacked us with their venomous fangs at the ready.

Time for a Swim.name: Time for a Swim
Time for a Swim.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This standalone event occurs while the characters are traveling the aqueous expanse of the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} at a fast or reckless pace, and presents them with an immediate set of skill challenges that will determine whether or not they become hurt and/or lost. In this event, the party can:

  • Attempt to avoid bludgeoning damage wrought by the rough, preternatural currents of the biome's magical "quickwater."

  • Try to stave off a level of Exhaustion that might occur from being swept up in this untimely slipstream.

  • Determine if they've been thrown off-course by this untimely encounter, and precisely how much.

Slipstream Hazard

The characters must immediately struggle to avoid being pummeled by the preternatural currents of the quickwater's slipstream. Each character must succeed on a [[/save constitution 15]] saving throw, taking [[/roll 1d4]] bludgeoning damage on a failure. withstand the [[/hazard 4 fortitude bludgeoning]]{Raging Slipstream}}. Any character which fails to resist this hazard must also succeed on a [[/skill athletics 17]] check or suffer 1 rank of &Reference[exhaustion] also suffers the @Condition[exhausted] condition.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge seafaring]] have advantage on this check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge seafaring]] avoid exhaustion even if they are affected by the hazard.

Swept Off Course

The untimely deluge of the quickwater may have impeded the party's journey, forcing them to spend time recovering from the torrent. The extent of this inconvenience is determined based on how effectively the group withstood the hazard of the chaotic slipstream.

  • If less than half the party was affected, the characters spend 1 hour recovering from the maelstrom.

  • If more than half, but not all of the party was affected, the characters spend 2 hours recovering.

  • If the entire party was affected by the maelstrom, they lose 4 hours recovering from the ordeal and the party is forcibly relocated to a hex adjacent to the current one in a direction approximately opposite their intended path of movement.

Gathering Quickwater

Characters who manage to withstand the torrential Quickwater and who have the wherewithal to collect a sample of the arcane deluge can attempt to do so with a successful [[/skill survival 15]] [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] check and a suitable container for capturing the elusive liquid. On a success, the character harvests [[/roll 1d2]] vials or doses of @UUID[Item.Va3es1V2Xf624fmd]{Quickwater}.
Time for a Swim.soverview: While rushing their way through the Dripstones, the party happens upon a stream of arcane quickwater, which snatches the characters up in its forceful currents. The party members must call upon their wits and athletic abilities if they wish to avoid exhaustion while being thrown off-course by the untimely incident.
Time for a Swim.sexposition: Rapidly making your way through the Dripstones, you become acutely aware of a sound on the horizon - a white noise like the roar of a distant ocean. Suddenly and without warning, an incredible swell of water laced with dazzling arcane energies bursts through the canyon from seemingly out of nowhere and rushes straight towards you, catching you up within its preternatural flood. You're carried away on this impromptu current before you can do anything to stop it, tossed to and fro by its savage wash.
Time for a Swim.ssummary: As we journeyed through the Dripstones at a rapid pace, we found ourselves caught up in some kind of preternatural deluge. It took all our might and resolve to avoid being completely waylaid by the sudden and powerful flow of the unpredictable arcane waters.

Shattered Expectations.name: Shattered Expectations
Shattered Expectations.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This standalone event set in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} can occur if the party is moving at a fast or reckless pace, and presents the characters with an immediate set of skill challenges that will determine whether or not they become hurt and/or lost. In this event, the party can:

  • Attempt to avoid the piercing damage wrought by the shattered crash of a massive chunk of @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal}, previously suspended like a stalactite from the roof of the cave.

  • Try to stave off the psychic maladies associated with such close proximity to the volatile impact.

  • Determine if they've been thrown off-course by this untimely encounter, and precisely how much.

As soon as you finish the readaloud, the characters are in mortal danger from the torrent of crystal shards hurled outward by the stalactite's impact, and must react accordingly.

The Crystal Stalactite

The party must immediately react to avoid being hit by the shards of arcane mineral that are flung far and wide by the shattered crystal stalactite. Each character must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d4+1 piercing]] damage avoid [[/hazard 6 reflex piercing]]{Exploding Shards} as the crystal shards rip their skin and gouge their flesh.

Characters who sustain damage from this hazard are affected by the chaotic resonance of the crystals and must also succeed on a [[/save Constitution 17]] saving throw withstand the [[/hazard 0 willpower psychic]]{Psychic Resonance} caused by the crystal shards or roll once each on the @UUID[RollTable.CW4O54YLtXBarVjz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal Effects} table.

Following the stalactite's seismic impact, the party members can take a moment to observe their surroundings. However, the characters must also assess whether or not the event has thrown them off course - an outcome that becomes more likely based on whether or not some of them were hit by the crystal shards.

Surveying the Scene

After the stalactite's impact, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check while searching the nearby area is able to locate [[/roll 1d2]] @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystals} worth looting among the shattered detritus.

Following the crystal stalactite's untimely impact, the characters must determine whether or not it has directly impeded the route of their journey.

Bewildered Reorientation

The party must nominate one member to be their decision-making guide, that character must succeed on a [[/skill survival 18]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 18]] check to prevent the party from becoming disoriented in the aftermath of this event. Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] gain @Advantage[2] on this check.

The degree of failure on this check determines precisely how far the party is thrown off-course by the incident:

  • Failure: The party loses 2 full hours recovering their bearings, during which the characters must carefully navigate a crevasse that has opened up where the crystal stalactite hit the ground. Advance the world clock by the appropriate number of hours.

  • Result of 13 or below Critical Failure: The party loses 4 full hours recovering their bearings and the party is forcibly relocated to a hex adjacent to this one. Manually move the party token in the approximately opposite direction of their intended direction of travel.
Shattered Expectations.soverview: While traversing the Kaleidoscope Caverns, the characters hastily stumble upon a peculiar cave where the sound of their movements is prodigiously amplified by the acoustic shapes and preternatural essence of the arcane, crystal-laden hollow. Due to the party's negligence, they must react quickly to avoid the hazards wrought by this untimely encounter, which can both trouble their minds and set them off-course if they're not careful or skilled enough to avoid the dangers.
Shattered Expectations.sexposition:
Gathering your bearings, you realize you've stumbled into a cave with a rather peculiar shape - one that seems to prodigiously amplify sound, including the noise of your very footsteps. Before you know what's happening, a massive stalactite made from the kaleidoscopic crystal that makes these caverns famous comes crashing down from the ceiling right in front of you.

The enormous slab of jagged, lucent mineral hits the ground of the cave with a ferocious impact, sending sizable fragments of nacreous crystal flying this way and that. You'll have to act fast if you wish to avoid the immediate threat of evisceration from these errant kaleidoscopic shards.
Shattered Expectations.ssummary: We encountered a strange cave within the Kaleidoscope Caverns, where our hasty pace of travel subjected us to hazards we might otherwise have avoided altogether - including a fallen stalactite of kaleidoscopic crystal that shattered upon impact, hurling fragments here and there while unleashing a wave of mind-altering aracane energy.

Dripstones Menace.name: Dripstones Menace
Dripstones Menace.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event occurs semi-randomly while traveling through the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.kURCAMxlrH49hTJJ]{Dripstones} biome. During this event, the party can:

  • Encounter a @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk]{Hydroxol}, a formidable adversary.

  • Harvest some useful crafting ingredients if they defeat their foe.

Hydroxol Attack

The party are assaulted by a Hydroxol that emerges from a nearby pond with intent to protect its territory. If the party stands and fights the Hydroxol, they may be able to extract some valuable resources from its carcass, and a few useful items from its belly.

@Embed[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk]

Hydroxol Tactics

In combat, the Hydroxol is aggressive and fearless, only attempting to retreat if it becomes badly wounded, falling below half of its maximum hit points, while also outnumbered.

When entering combat, the Hydroxol rushes toward the nearest target it can perceive, using its @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk.Item.6PuULfBzy5vpBSFI]{Charging Chomp} to try and secure an early, free @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk.Item.xoX7rTPs8lllsLag]{Toothy Bite} on an unprepared target.

If successful, the Hydroxol will attempt to drag grappled foes into deep water while using its@UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk.Item.xoX7rTPs8lllsLag]{Toothy Bite} action to harm its foe. It does this because not only can it fight more easily underwater due to its natural swim speed, it also knows that most land-bound prey, such as humanoids, will drown if held underwater long enough. Since it can breathe water, it can stay submerged indefinitely.

If its charge is unsuccessful, the Hydroxol will use its @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk.Item.t2KRGzsjV4Wwp0wj]{Tail Slap} and @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk.Item.xoX7rTPs8lllsLag]{Toothy Bite} to soften up and grapple foes. If possible, it will use its Tail Slap to propel itself out of danger, while also dragging off a grappled foe.

The Hydroxol is aggressive and territorial. It will fight to the death unless it's Morale is broken, in which case it will flee upon falling below half of its maximum Health.

The Hydroxol will rush towards the nearest target it can percieve, using @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk.Item.restrainingChomp] to attempt and restrain the target, making it vulnerable to its deadly @UUID[Actor.OIMVi8FSI66sSMVk.Item.thrash0000000000] attack.

If it has a target Restrained it may try to disengage and drag the target away into the water where it is at an advantage due to its ability to swim. The Hydroxol knows that most land-bound prey will drown if held underwater long enough, so it is likely to submerge with its prey.

Fight or Flight

Both the party and the Hydroxol will fight unless either attempts to retreat. If the Hydroxol is cornered and unable to escape, it will fight ferociously to the death.

If the party chooses to flee, the Hydroxol will give chase but not past the edges of the Scene. If the party flees the area the Hydroxol returns to its den. If the party was attacked while resting, this has likely forced them to leave certain belongings behind.

Once the party has defeated the Hydroxol, they can spend some time investigating and studying the corpse of the slain beast.

Identifying the Hydroxol

Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] or succeding on a [[/skill nature 12 passive format=long]][[/skillCheck science 16 passive]] check know some information about these giant amphibians.

  • [[/skill nature 12 passive]] or successful [[/skill nature 12]] knows these beasts are called "Hydroxol", are naturally territorial omnivores that nest in watery, secluded places. They can get quite large, and prefer to drag prey into deep water, drowning them there if possible.

  • [[/skill nature 15 passive]]: Hydroxol are especially drawn to places with greater connections to the water moon Mayis or locations suffused with elemental water magic. In such places they can grow even larger, rarer Gray Hydroxol.

  • Success: These beasts are called "Hydroxol", are naturally territorial omnivores that nest in watery, secluded places. They can get quite large, and prefer to drag prey into deep water, drowning them there if possible.

  • Critical Success: Hydroxol are especially drawn to places with greater connections to the water moon Mayis or locations suffused with elemental water magic. In such places they can grow even larger, rarer Gray Hydroxol.

It Ate What?

A character who investigates the body of the defeated Hydroxol and makes a successful [[/skill perception 12]][[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check notices some oddities inside the creature's semi-translucent belly. The party may cut the beast open find various items in its guts.

  • Roll three times on the @UUID[RollTable.fC3Hy8YyGAyZBpQ4]{Hydroxol Stomach Contents} table to determine which items are found within the cadaver.

Hydrophobic Hides

Any character with [[/skill nature 14 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 12]] check [[/skillCheck wilderness 13 passive]] knows that a Hydroxol corpse contains numerous organs and other parts that can be harvested as valuable crafting ingredients.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] or [[/knowledge monsters]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The following items can be harvested from a single Hydroxol:

  • @UUID[Item.BFhtfhlLY1QnNkAb]{Bioluminescence} (x4) which is processed into colorful, luminous paints, dyes and inks.

  • @UUID[Item.xFxXSYlm4CVRXRo8]{Gills} (x2) which are an ingredient used to create water breathing potions.

  • @UUID[Item.RKXdPKeVE5nMOI0r]{Hide} (x1) which may be used to craft waterproof equipment like packs, cloaks, and tarps.

Whether the party stands and fights, or flees from the territorial beast, they are able to continue on with their exploration of the region.
Dripstones Menace.soverview: As the party makes their way south through the lush Dripstones, across bubbling streams and crashing waterfalls they are attacked by a large, territorial Hydroxol.
Dripstones Menace.sexposition: Emerging from one of the large pools is perhaps the largest amphibian you've ever seen, a blend between salamander and something else. Wide, webbed feet slap against the stone heavily as it closes the distance, eyes fixed on you. Its huge mouth slowly opens as it barrels towards you, revealing a man-sized gullet and numerous sharp teeth.
Dripstones Menace.ssummary: While exploring the region beyond the newly opened Shent gate, we encountered a large, hostile amphibian with glowing gills and stripes down its long body.

Shimmering Dark.name: Shimmering Dark
Shimmering Dark.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration event allows the party to encounter the mind-altering magical effects prevalent in the Kaleidoscope Caverns. In this event the party can:

  • Discover a treacherous new biome, the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns}.

  • Collect unique crystals that form here which could be interesting, useful, or dangerous.

Cavern Exploration

The crystals of the kaleidoscope cavern are mesmerizing, but spending too long in their presence can have a mind-altering effect on those who travel nearby. As the cavern's magical effects take hold, read or paraphrase the following:

Each time you blink or turn your head, the light from within the violet crystals seems to shift, creating a hypnotic effect that makes it difficult to concentrate on anything else. As your vision focuses in on the shimmering swirl of light you feel increasingly woozy as countless dots of light infiltrate your field of view and can't be shaken off.

Crystal Calamity

Characters encountering this event will find the crystal caverns have begun to influence their perceptions. Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] immediately suspect that the crystals formed in this place are not entirely natural.

Any character who can see the light emitted by a cluster of kaleidoscope crystals must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 13]] saving throw. On success, the character suffers no ill effects aside from minor disorientation. On failure, a character benefits from scrambled senses, suffering disadvantage on perception checks until they finish a long rest. In addition, they also suffer one of the following effects which persist until the successful completion of a long rest.

Any character who can see the light emitted by a cluster of kaleidoscope crystals must face [[/hazard 4 willpower psychic morale]]{Kaleidoscopic Disorientation}. If this hazard is not resisted, the character additionally suffers from one of the following effects which persist until the successful completion of a Rest.

@Embed[RollTable.CW4O54YLtXBarVjz inline rollable=true]

After facing this test, the characters are immune to the effects of the kaleidoscope crystals for 24 hours.

Taking a Kaleidoscope Crystal

If characters want to take a @UUID[Item.ejlcKptrojvNqenz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal}, they must break it off of the cavern wall or floor. Liberating a crystal from where it is embedded in the cavern wall requires either a successful [[/check dexterity 14]] check while using a suitable tool (pickaxe, hammer, etc.) or a successful [[/check strength 18]] checka successful [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check to extract it from the cave wall.

Attempting this check and failing causes the crystal to shatter, generating an immediate release of magical energy that immediately inflicts a @UUID[RollTable.CW4O54YLtXBarVjz]{Kaleidoscope Crystal Effect} to anyone who is not already immune to the effects.
Shimmering Dark.soverview: As characters enter the mysterious Kaleidoscope caverns, they find themselves drawn to the shifting prismatic light cast by its reflective crystals, which is strengthened by any light they bring into the caverns. The glittering light intrigues, but hides a danger - those who spend too long in the presence of the arcane crystals may fall prey to one of their mind-altering effects.
Shimmering Dark.sexposition: As you step into the cave, the swirling pattern created by crystalline reflections changes and the air moves slightly as if somehow whispering a secret. Flickers and flashes of light dance through the cavern like ripples in water. Some of these flashes rush overhead, or circle you briefly before dying out, but each time they pass by you're left feeling slightly light-headed.
Shimmering Dark.ssummary: We encountered the mysterious and captivating reflective crystals of the Kaleidoscope Caverns.

Pollen Storm.name: Pollen Storm
Pollen Storm.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This standalone event occurs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.fNE3VZ5BvQXtS0BN]{Verdant Paths} as a result of the region's dynamic weather, and happens no matter what pace the party has set for their travel. In this standalone event, the characters can:

  • React to the sudden arrival of a pollen storm, a manifestation of Ember's preternatural wonder and relative unpredictability.

  • Avoid the pollen storm's allergens, or else suffer the effects of them.

  • Experience one of a few brief encounters if they manage to avoid the storm.

This event takes place on @UUID[Scene.emberWorldRegion] Region Map. It is guaranteed to occur when the party first encounters a Pollen Storm and will not reoccur for at least 24 hours.

The pollen storm arrives thoroughly and with haste — whether the party is prepared or not. The characters must respond immediately to this environmental threat, which can have a negative impact on their short-term health (both mentally and physically). And if the characters act quickly enough, the untimely circumstances could prove to be nothing more than an inconvenience (if not the opportunity for a chance discovery as well).

Environmental Mechanics

Any area confronted with a pollen storm is subject to the following mechanical considerations:

  • The area is &Reference[Lightly Obscured].

  • Ranged attacks have @Advantage[-2] when the target is 100 or more feet away.

  • Characters who don't succeed on the requisite saving throws are subject to the hazardous effects of the pollen itself (see "Pollen Contamination" below for details).

  • The area is lightly obscured, impairing the vision of those within it.

  • Ranged attacks have @Advantage[-2] when the target is 100 or more feet away.

  • Characters who don't succeed on the requisite checks are subject to the hazardous effects of the pollen itself (see "Pollen Contamination" below for details).

Detecting & Avoiding the Storm

If one or more characters has a [[/skill perception 15 passive format=long]], or succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] successful [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] check, the party is able to detect the storm early enough to make an active attempt to avoid it, granting them [[/roll 2d5]] turns to act before the cloudburst of pollen is upon them.

  • Characters with [[/attunement mayis]], [[/knowledge tracking]], or [[/knowledge weather]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The party can also react to the imminent threat by participating in one of the Pollen Storm Encounters detailed below, which they discover while observing the storm.

Roll on (or choose from) the following table to determine what kind of encounter awaits the party when they react to the imminent threat of the pollen storm.

@Embed[RollTable.sHwxW6X0dfd6wIwt inline rollable]

Surveying the Pollen Storm

The characters can spend one or more turns in an attempt to assess the storm's nature and the potential threat it poses to the party.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check is somewhat familiar with the Arctus Plateau's infamous pollen storms, and can provide some insight into their behavior and effects: the pollen can be damaging to one's intelligence, and is outright poisonous if inhaled or via orificial contacted in large quantities.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberArcturian]], [[/knowledge plants]], or [[/knowledge weather]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The character is familiar with some of the natural lore pertaining to these storms, including the speculation of regional scholars — some of which posits that the pollen is inexplicably produced by Ember itself to pacify the creatures who roam its surface from time to time.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check knows the actual @UUID[Item.fJD7Nz7WyUPKlVTz]{Storm Pollen} itself to be a potent material component in certain illusion magic, as well as a common ingredient in a few Arcturian crafting recipes.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]], [[/knowledge crafts]], or [[/knowledge plants]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Result of 21+: The character is able to safely harvest [[/roll 1d3]] doses of @UUID[Item.fJD7Nz7WyUPKlVTz]{Storm Pollen} during the course of this encounter.

Protective Measures

Adequate methods of protection from the storm pollen include:

  • The Aquatic Adaptation feature of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAlterSelf0]{Alter Self} spell (modified by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.tKjaIifZVvGYJe1G]{The Weave} itself to allow for various environmental anomalies).

  • A suitable breathing mask or apparatus like an @UUID[Item.uwW2RbYhM3SQ6yTy]{Arcturian Respirator}. Alternately, an improvised mask provides @Advantage[2] on saving throws made to withstand the pollen.

  • A timely dose of @UUID[Item.jF7AO6nnqIhFZ6oI]{Dustweed}, which acts as an antidote to the pollen.

  • A suitable breathing mask or apparatus like an @UUID[Item.uwW2RbYhM3SQ6yTy]{Arcturian Respirator}. Alternately, an improvised mask provides @Advantage[2] on hazard checks made to withstand the pollen.

  • A timely dose of @UUID[Item.jF7AO6nnqIhFZ6oI]{Dustweed}, which acts as an antidote to the pollen.

Pollen Contamination

Characters who inhale or make orificial contact with storm pollen must succeed on a [[/save constitution 16]] save to withstand its effect, which includes the following based on the result:

  • The character has @Advantage[-2] on Intelligence skill checks and saving throws.

  • Result of 6 or less: The character is &Reference[Poisoned].

The negative effects of the pollen last for a duration of [[/roll 2d4 hours]] and can be cured by taking a &Reference[Long Rest] or by targeting the afflicted character with either the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLesserRest]{Lesser Restoration} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplProtection]{Protection from Poison} spells.

A character can only be affected by this pollen contamination once per day.

Characters who inhale or make orificial contact with storm pollen must face [[/hazard 8 fortitude morale harmless]] to withstand its effect, which includes the following based on the result:

  • The character has @Advantage[-2] on all Knowledge skill checks and is @Condition[staggered].

  • Critical Failure: The character also begins a coughing spurt and suffers [[/hazard 4 fortitude severe]].

The negative effects of the pollen last for a duration of [[/roll 2d4 hours]] and can be cured by taking a Rest, by targeting the afflicted character with @Spell[life.touch], or by consumption of an @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.antitoxin0000000].

A character can only be affected by this pollen contamination once per day.

Read the following aloud the first time one or more characters become afflicted with the pollen's negative effects:

Particles of this curious pollen make their way into your system, and you find your senses warped by the strange allergen. As your eyes itch and your wits narrow, the world around you becomes ever-so-slightly more difficult to comprehend.

Concluding the Event

The Pollen Storm event concludes once the characters have either successfully avoided the storm or endured its negative effects. Although the weather condition itself can endure (and potentially repeat), each character can only be affected by this pollen contamination once per day.
Pollen Storm.soverview: A menacing pollen storm sweeps through the area, and the party must react accordingly or else suffer the untimely consequences of this preternatural, allergen-laden wind.
Pollen Storm.sexposition: You find yourself immersed within a cloudburst of pink pollen, which rains down upon the area with the feathered descent of delicate snowfall. These pastel motes of microscopic grains form a carnation-colored miasma that floats above and throughout the nearby terrain with flustering ease. A powdery blanket of the substance begins to cover every surface in sight, and a confrontation with this pernicious weather is close at hand.
Pollen Storm.ssummary: We encountered a pernicious pollen storm while traversing the region, a pink miasma full of sense-altering allergens.

Grassland Artifice.name: Grassland Artifice
Grassland Artifice.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event allows the characters to encounter the agrimage Moriah Foxhaven, whom they've found roaming the Golden Flats with her caravan of beast-riding companions. In this event, the characters can:

  • Meet Moriah Foxhaven, an Arcturian agrimage from Steed's Point who is known for crafting wondrous items like the Grassland Talisman.

  • Procure a Grassland Talisman from Moriah, which will protect them from Jurtak poison while they traverse Steed's Point.

The Wandering Agrimage

With guidance from Rattletrap, the party can locate a roving agrimage on the plains westward of the Eastern River to procure a Grassland Talisman, which should help the characters as they explore the Jurtak-infested reaches of Steed's Point.

The sun-kissed agrimage @UUID[Actor.t98dgswBccdv1dHQ]{Moriah Foxhaven} lives amongst a group of beast-riding nomads, and is known to fashion these talismans with her arcane craft. Moriah and her companions are happy to welcome the party into their camp for a while if their intentions are pure and their gold or barter is worthy.

@Embed[Actor.t98dgswBccdv1dHQ]

Meeting the Agrimage

Moriah Foxhaven and her community of beast-riding wanderers are used to meeting all sorts of folk on the dusty path to here and there, so the appearance of the party should come as no surprise to the unnamed band of rovers.

Headstrong and heartfelt, Moriah is quick to strike up conversation with the characters when they arrive, and is willing to discuss the following:

  • The @UUID[Item.dixDloUZsbCXhNbj]{Grassland Talisman} and how it might help the party survive the poisonous Jurtak attacks they've been warned about.

  • More about herself and her beast-riding companions.

  • A brief history about the rise and fall of Steed's Point, with discourse about its most prominent denizens — including Rattletrap, Kali Andrella, and Bertron Steed.

  • A short introduction to agrimagic.

About yourself?

I'm just a traveler, like yourselves. One who has seen more than her fair share of hardship in too short an amount of time. So I put my agrimagic to good use by cultivating this little community of ours and helping the good people of the Golden Flats when I can.

About Agrimagic?

Agrimagic is an Arcturian tradition I've always studied with pride, not simply because it runs in the family, but due to some longing I've felt since youth. My sorcery stems from Ember itself, and I'm fortunate to be able to give a little magic back to the world from time to time.

Steed's Point?

It started with an earthquake. Then the Jurtak came. Soon, a well-meaning but misguided agrimage — one considerably more powerful than myself — summoned scores of gore birds to stem the saurian tide. Steed's Point was caught up in the fray, and that's how I lost my hometown. I abandoned Steed's Point before it got too dangerous to leave.

The Grassland Talisman?

Nobody deserves to die from the venom on a Jurtak's blade. Thanks to Ember's bounties, I've managed to weave a special magic that wards against the deadly toxin. A Grassland Talisman will certainly help you mitigate the mortal threat of Jurtak poison. But it's magic is fleeting, and it won't save you from a Jurtak geomancer's umbral sorcery.

About Jurtak?

The Jurtak are foul and verminous creatures that hail from the deepest, lightless depths of Ember's Pathways. These aberrations are motivated by little more than sheer cruelty and their carnivorous appetites.

The Grassland Talisman

The so-called @UUID[Item.dixDloUZsbCXhNbj]{Grassland Talisman} is a peculiar magic item fashioned by Moriah Foxhaven, utilizing her skills as an agrimage to ward its wearer against the potent poison used by the Jurtak.

Moriah Foxhaven charges a sum of 50 gp for the consumable item, but can be persuaded to lower the price.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill per 15]] check is able to convince Moriah to sell the item at a discount for 40 gp.
Grassland Artifice.soverview: The party tracks down the wandering agrimage Moriah Foxhaven, who is known for crafting a wondrous item known as a Grassland Talisman. This talisman is rumored to be an effective ward against the deadly poison of the Jurtak that inhabit Steed's Point.
Grassland Artifice.sexposition: You spy a caravan of beast riders on the amber plains ahead, with humanoids mounted atop a half-dozen yarnac and other gentle beasts of burden. They amble slowly across the Golden Flats in graceful harmony with each other and the very land they stride upon.
Grassland Artifice.ssummary: We met the roving agrimage Moriah Foxhaven, from whom we procured a Grassland Talisman. The wondrous item should provide us with a measure of protection against the deadly Jurtak poison we'll encounter in Steed's Point.

Rending Teeth.name: Rending Teeth
Rending Teeth.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event takes place on the Fogbound Caverns area map using the Lake of Whispers composition. The party finds themselves surrounded by a large number of @UUID[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM]{Abyssal Eels}. They can either:

  • Recognize that the monsters have limited senses, and can be navigated around with the party being detected.

  • Survive combat with the ravenous swarm.

The event begins with the party in the center of the Area Map in a small depression, having been silently surrounded by Abyssal Eels as they moved through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.jgf4ySVqus9CYidy]{Fogbound Caverns}. Initiative is not rolled immediately as the eels have limited perceptive capabilities.

@Embed[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM count=16]

Assessing the Situation

The party can reach the other side of the area and safely escape if they realize that the Abyssal Eels are not actively hunting them nor moving in their direction.

With a successful [[/skill prc 17 passive]], [[/skill prc 15]], or [[/skill inv 15]] check, characters notice that the Abyssal Eels are ignoring the party and have not changed course or begun moving in any particular direction.

  1. Result of 17+ While the Eels are ignoring the party, characters can tell that they are clearly aggressive predators, with small scraps of living matter stuck in their jaws. They also react sharply to any movement from each other, seeming to have a hair trigger to attack.

  2. Result of 19+ By studying the Abyssal Eels closely, characters observe that they only react to movement within a very small area around them, roughly 10 feet, and can see for an additional 20 feet. It might be possible to zig-zag between them and navigate through the area without them sensing the party if they move with stealth.

With a successful [[/skill nature 17]] check, characters are aware that Abyssal Eels, while dangerous, rely on nearby movement to find their prey. Characters with [[/knowledge monsters]] or [[/knowledge abyssals]] have advantage on this check.

  • Result of 19+ Characters know that the perception limit for Abyssal Eels is 30 feet. If characters remain outside of that limit, or succeed in moving stealthily within that limit, they can get by the group without triggering combat.

Evading the Eels

The party can evade the eels by hiding from their rudimentary senses, but the eels' constant movement makes this difficult. To sneak by without getting the eels' attention, the party must succeed on a group stealth check of [[/check stealth 15]] (if half or more of the group succeeds, the group succeeds on the check).

If the party has knowledge of the eels by succeeding on either of the more difficult checks above (those requiring an outcome of 19 or greater), they have advantage on the check as they stay ahead of the eels' predicted movements.

Abyssal Eel Tactics

If the party attacks one of the Abyssal Eels or they move within the Abyssal Eel's blindsight (30 feet) without succeeding on a Stealth check, a combat encounter begins as the eels swarm into a feeding frenzy. When combat begins, the party should roll initiative. Abyssal Eels are added to initiative order as a single entity.

The encounter with the Abyssal Eels may quickly become overwhelming and chaotic, as they will try to occupy the spaces of each other and of the player characters using @UUID[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM.Item.ZvIQhj4sTuFAQYFm]{Frenzied Swarm}. The Abyssal Eels are voracious, swarming, predatory monsters with no regard for their own self-preservation; they fight to the death.
Rending Teeth.soverview: As the party moves through the Fogbound Caverns, they suddenly realize that they are surrounded by Abyssal Eels floating silently in the nearby darkness. The party must either carefully navigate through the Abyssal Eels, avoiding detection, or fight their way through the vicious swarm of creatures.
Rending Teeth.sexposition: The chilling silence of this area is interrupted by the soft sound of a ripple of movement upon the fog-shrouded air. You assess the environment nearby and perceive the faint silhouettes of snake-like shapes floating around you in the dense air. You realize with alarm that these shapes are on all sides, moving slowly within the roiling mist. Thankfully, they seem to be unaware or unbothered by your presence … for now.
Rending Teeth.ssummary: We encountered a large number of floating Abyssal Eel-like creatures that didn't seem to sense us, even when we moved relatively close to them.

Corrupted Depths.name: Corrupted Depths
Corrupted Depths.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event can occur while traversing the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.CPBGxUJqmL8o4XsG]{Lake of Whispers} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.jgf4ySVqus9CYidy]{Fogbound Caverns} section of the Pathways. In this event the party can either:

  • Hunt some of the strange @UUID[Actor.Va3xPZVUrdOTb73X]{Corrupted Kezus Jelly}'s as the swarm the party

  • Move on quickly after recognizing that the jellies are not interested in the party.

This event is repeatable, but on a cooldown so it cannot happen for several days after it has been encountered.

The event begins with the party floating across the Lake of Whispers upon the water vehicle they possess as they move through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.jgf4ySVqus9CYidy]{Fogbound Caverns}.

@Embed[Actor.Va3xPZVUrdOTb73X count=6]

@Embed[Actor.P4mkMkXH6KK6WBoz count=1]

The jellies are not immediately hostile, so the party can choose whether to take the first move or simply investigate.

Light in the Depths

The party can decide that the jellies pose no danger to them, and they can move on without engaging in combat. This can end the encounter quickly.

A [[/check prc 17 passive]] or successful [[/skill prc 15]] or [[/skill inv 15]] check will notice that the jellies are ignoring the party and floating through the water without any apparent purpose. They react to the passing of the water vehicle but are not aggressive or hostile.

  1. Result of 16+. By studying the jellies closely, you realize that they are aware of the party but are not aggressive, leaving them alone will result may be the best course of action.

  2. Result of 17+. These jellies do not appear to be entirely natural creatures, or perhaps they may have been once, however, their colors and glowing markings seem to suggest some kind of Abyssal corruption.

A successful [[/skill nature 15]] or check or [[/knowledge crafts]] or [[/knowledge alchemy]] will notice that the jellies are rare creatures that if they were harvested for parts would produce @UUID[Item.skuFL0758trQ2HTB]{Kezus Jelly} which is highly valuable and even more so when refined into@UUID[Item.ntA6Zk1Qj7ZPwt9m]{Kezus Ointment}. The party can decide whether attacking the jellies here is worth the risk!

Kezus Jelly Tactics

If the party attacks one of the jellies, combat begins. The jellies will turn red — indicating their aggression and anger — and attack as a group.

The encounter with the jellies is straightforward, as they all move toward the water vehicle that the party is floating on as a single entity. They target the party members or characters randomly but will switch their attacks to anyone in the water if they fall in.
Corrupted Depths.soverview: While traversing the Lake of Whispers, a fog-shrouded section of the Pathways, the party encounters strange luminescent jellies rising from the fathomless depths.
Corrupted Depths.sexposition: The lake is silent aside from the rhythmic creaking of your makeshift raft and the flutter of its canvas sailcloth. At the periphery of your vision, however, you notice tiny pinpricks of faint light in the water growing gradually brighter and larger in size.
Corrupted Depths.ssummary: We encountered strange glowing jelly-like creatures which dwell in the depths of an underground lake in the fog-shrouded Pathways.

Dangerous Descent.name: Dangerous Descent
Dangerous Descent.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration Event can occur while traveling into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.tuopdqO2JSeH1LeU]{Splinter Canyons} from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}. In this Event, the party can:

  • Demonstrate their wilderness survival skills by preparing for and charting a course down the perilous cliff face.

  • Potentially overcome one or more hazards.

Stages of Descent

The canyon wall is 360 feet tall. The party must complete three stages of descent in order to reach the canyon floor; each stage represents approximately 120 feet of movement and takes approximately 1 hour. The stages of descent are:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.Ih0y4k6zcqLvYWBl#stage-1:-charting-a-course]{Stage 1: Charting a Course}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.Ih0y4k6zcqLvYWBl#stage-2:-making-the-descent]{Stage 2: Making the Descent}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.Ih0y4k6zcqLvYWBl#stage-3:-reaching-the-canyon-floor]{Stage 3: Reaching the Canyon Floor}

Each stage represents a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.rules.JournalEntry.0AGfrwZRzSG0vNKb.JournalEntryPage.OcHhrKKzffcVi03Q#group-checks]{Group Check} — if at least half of the characters succeed, they proceed to the next stage of descent without incident. If over half of the characters fail, however, roll on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.Ih0y4k6zcqLvYWBl#climbing-hazards]{Climbing Hazards} table. After resolving the hazard, the party proceeds to the next stage.

Making Preparations

Before embarking on the journey, the party may describe any preparations they're making for the climb. Appropriate tools, equipment, magic, or other precautions may grant @Advantage[2] or automatic success on a relevant roll, per the Gamemaster's discretion.

Such preparations may include: rope, pitons, climbing gear, anchored vines, magical flight, or any other sensible method of descent.

Stage 1: Charting a Course

Stage 1: Chart a Course

The characters must first identify a safe path down the canyon wall with a group skill challenge. Every member of the party must make one of the following tests:

  • A successful [[/skill nature 14]] check to clamber down the thick vines cascading down the cliff face.

  • A successful [[/skill perception 14]] check to carefully edge across a series of narrow ledges and shallow footholds that pockmark the cliff face.

If the group check is failed, roll on the @UUID[RollTable.xtUlzhr0LusL2Xkc]{Climbing Hazards} table.

Stage 1: Falling

Characters that fall from the effects of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.Ih0y4k6zcqLvYWBl#climbing-hazards]{Climbing Hazard} fall 360 feet, taking ([[/damage 20d6 Bludgeoning]] damage) and landing &reference[Prone].

Stage 2: Making the Descent

Stage 2: Making the Descent

The characters must next traverse the most dangerous portion of the climb with a group skill challenge. Every member of the party must make one of the following tests:

  • A successful [[/skill athletics 16]] check to use their strength and leverage, performing the heavy lifting across difficult stretches and securing handholds for their companions.

  • A successful [[/skill acrobatics 16]] check to use their agility and balance to trailblaze nimbly across narrow ledges, ensuring a steady footing for their companions.

If the group check is failed, roll on the @UUID[RollTable.xtUlzhr0LusL2Xkc]{Climbing Hazards} table.

Stage 2: Falling

Characters that fall from the effects of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.Ih0y4k6zcqLvYWBl#climbing-hazards]{Climbing Hazard} fall 240 feet, taking ([[/damage 20d6 Bludgeoning]] damage) and landing &reference[Prone].

Stage 3: Reaching the Canyon Floor

Stage 3: Reaching the Canyon Floor

The party must succeed on a final [[/skill survival 16]] group check to withstand the grueling demands of the extended descent to safely reach the canyon floor below.

If the group check is failed, roll on the @UUID[RollTable.xtUlzhr0LusL2Xkc]{Climbing Hazards} table.

Stage 3: Falling

Characters that fall from the effects of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.Ih0y4k6zcqLvYWBl#climbing-hazards]{Climbing Hazard} fall 120 feet, taking ([[/damage 12d6 Bludgeoning]] damage) and landing &reference[Prone].

Climbing Hazards

@Embed[RollTable.xtUlzhr0LusL2Xkc inline rollable]

Concluding the Event

Once the party has reached the floor of the Splinter Canyons, they're free to continue on their journey.
Dangerous Descent.soverview: While traveling along the edge of the Splinter Canyons, the party is confronted with a difficult choice: brave a perilous climb down the cliff face, or seek a safer ingress elsewhere at the expense of time.
Dangerous Descent.sexposition: Up close, the descent into the Splinter Canyons is steeper than it first appeared. Curtains of vine sway against broken stone, and the rattle of rock and small puffs of dust mark places where the cliff face is already giving way. You may be able to climb down, but doing so safely will require preparation and care.
Dangerous Descent.ssummary: While descending into the Splinter Canyons from the Golden Flats, we undertook a perilous climb down the cliff face. Though the journey was fraught with danger, we eventually reached the canyon floor below.

Strange Thornlings.name: Strange Thornlings
Strange Thornlings.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event sees the party encounter a small group of strange, afflicted Thornlings bearing a colony of psychic fungus. The fungus, which identifies itself as the Sporix, feeds on plants and absorbs their life energies. It has recently expanded to take control of some Thornlings that were exploring the depths. The party can:

  • Fight the afflicted, destroying them.

  • Attempt to make contact with the Sporix colony.

  • Let them pass without interference.

A Rare Encounter

This event will only ever trigger once, currently. While there may be more Sporix-based events in the future, right now this is the only instance of this sickness appearing in the current chapters. If you would like them to reappear, and become a minor plot point, you are free to.

They can be encountered growing on other plants, including other fungus, and should only be encountered underground in the Pathways, and always far from sources of light.

What Are The Sporix?

The Sporix is a semi-sentient magical fungus that grows in the darkest, dampest regions of the Sinkhole Depths. These fungus colonies specifically target plants, working their way into the core of the afflicted plant. Once embedded, the fungal colonies take over the plant and begin consuming its life force until the host withers and dies.

Thankfully, the Sporix have not managed to spread very far, as it is only well suited to dark, damp regions. The fungal weakness to heat and light makes it hard for them to survive anywhere light touches, and greatly limits the spread of colonies.

Parasitic Fungus

Mechanically, Sporix colonies function like a disease which is capable of afflicting any plants on Ember, including Thornlings. Narratively speaking, the Sporix is a parasitic fungus not unlike the cordyceps fungus on earth.

While most plants can be inflicted easily, Thornlings are much more difficult, and must already be weakened by sickness, starvation, or fatigue to be susceptible. In most cases, player characters will be in no danger. We have no provided any mechanics or saves to resist the Sporix since it's assumed player Thornlings won't be at risk.

Curing the Affliction

The Sporix colonies are highly resilient, and spread quickly. If caught early, the small colonies could be surgically cut out of the host's body, but once it takes hold, the afflicted being needs powerful magical intervention. Only @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.WzvJ7G3cqvIubsLk]{Greater Restoration} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3okM6Gn63zzEULkz]{Wish} are capable of undoing the damage the Sporix colony has done to the host once afflicted.

Fighting the Afflicted

@embed[Actor.PO4036qpja149J7E count=9]

The Sporix afflicted Thornlings are not initially hostile, and don't attack unless provoked first. There are nine of them all told, and they are easy to spot since they are glowing and make no attempt to conceal themselves. Though some are armed and armored, none of their equipment appears to be in good, usable order.

Favored Prey: Thornlings

If the party has a Thornling, all nine Sporix hosts become hostile the moment any one of them perceives the non-afflicted Thornling, and attack. The Sporix colony that has taken control of them wants nothing more than to spread itself to other Thornlings and resorts to violence as its primary method of doing so.

Sporix Host Tactics

Thornlings serving as a Sporix Host have little to speak of in the way of tactics: they rush enemies and attempt to punch, kick, and bite them until they stop moving. They attempt to prioritize other unafflicted Thornlings if they are aware of any, but are careful enough not to kill them. They need the Thornlings alive.

While they do attack mindlessly, they are coordinated, and focus on whatever they perceive to be the greatest danger. They also have a faint sense of self-preservation and attempt to flee if @Condition[broken], @Condition[weakened] or if more than half their number have been defeated.

Examining the Afflicted

Rare Insights

Sporix are not well documented or well understood, and they have only been witnessed a few times; they are more myth than reality. Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] may have heard rumors of the Sporix, but have never seen them or heard any credible accounts before now.

Characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] that examine the thornlings will recognize that they are not undead, at least not as one traditionally understands them to be. Furthermore, characters with [[/knowledge soul]] recognize that these thornling souls are likely trapped in their bodies, stuck between life and death, not unlike undead.

Characters wtih [[/knowledge abyssals]] might suspect that these beings are abyss tainted, but examining them reveals no such telltale signs. That doesn't rule out the presence of such a taint, just that it's not manifesting in usual ways.

Invasive Growths

A successful [[/skill medicine 12]] [[/skillCheck medicine 12]] while examining one of the afflicted reveals that the Thornlings are still alive, but barely. Their flesh and foliage are withered and ill-colored, giving the appearance of death or undeath, though that is not actually the case.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success The fungus growing out of them has split open their skin and looks to be coming from deep within them. These wounds combined with the clear signs of long-term malnutrition indicate to you that these afflicted may die out in the next week or so. Short of surgery to remove all the fungus, clean, and then seal the wounds, you haven't the faintest idea how you could actually save them. You’re not even certain that such an invasive procedure wouldn’t prove fatal by itself.

Strange Behavior

A successful [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skill diplomacy 15]] check while watching the afflicted Thornlings reveals that they all seem to react to certain stimuli in unison, leading you to believe they might all be sharing their senses, or connected to each other.

  • A further successful [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skill arcana 15]] check, with this insight, leads you to suspect leads you to suspect the fungus may actually be some sort of psionic colony capable of bridging minds.

Magical Diagnosis

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.2skfDtglk1mGrb3l]{Detect Poison and Disease} Use of @Spell[life.sense] reveals the presence of an invasive fungal growth that has found its way into the target's nervous system. The fungal infection is directly controlling them, and has suppressed most of their higher mental functions.

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} Using magic to read the surface thoughts of the afflicted hears only a dim whisper of numerous little reactive impulses, sentient but hardly intelligent. Digging deeper discovers that the minds of the thornlings are all but lost, and in their place is the fungal growth that has taken over.

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.2VXGS206tuChoeXy]{Speak with Plants} Using [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] does allow for more direct communication (see below) but is not strong enough to issue commands. The fungal growth controlling the Thornlings is already smart and more resistant than any mundane plant.

Failed Treatments

Targeting the afflicted with any other form of healing or restorative magic is effective. Rather than restoring lost hit points, it instead causes the afflicted considerable pain and turns them hostile to the source of the magic.

Communicating with the Sporix

Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.2VXGS206tuChoeXy]{Speak with Plants} Using the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] wildspeakerallows a character to converse with the fungus directly. Doing this reveals that the fungal growth is known as the Sporix. If contacted, they have very little say and are single-minded:

We are the Sporix. We are of the rot and darkness of Ember. We spread to grow, and grow to exist. The Thornlings are ours now. They are ideal. Most plants cannot walk. These ones are ideal. We will find more of them and multiply.

Once the afflicted Thornlings have been defeated or examined, the party may continue their travels. Since the Sporix-afflicted Thornlings are wandering aimlessly, they are never in the same place twice.
Strange Thornlings.soverview: The party encounters a group of Thornlings acting strangely and covered in glowing fungus. This brush with the strange reveals a dangerous affliction brewing in the darkness of the Sinkhole Depths.
Strange Thornlings.sexposition: You see a strange, shifting glow in the darkness around you, and it is coming closer. It doesn't take long before you hear shuffling footsteps and see the diminutive shapes of Thornlings coming your way. Strangely, each and every one of them bear glowing mushrooms sprouting from their bodies.
Strange Thornlings.ssummary: While traveling through the Pathways we encountered some strange Thornlings afflicted with an ominous, glowing fungus, which seemed to rob them of personality and thought.

In The Behemoth's Wake.name: In The Behemoth's Wake
In The Behemoth's Wake.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This repeatable Exploration Event can occur while traveling through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}. In this Event, the party can:

  • Discover a destroyed site recently laid waste by a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} behemoth.

  • Examine the ruined site, possibly uncovering clues about the strange subterranean creature responsible.

  • Recover a small trophy or other remnant of the creature if they successfully identify it.

This Event can repeat, but will not reoccur for at least 24 hours after each incident.

Randomization Procedure

To run this Standalone Event, follow these steps:

  1. Determine what kind of site the characters discover in ruins by rolling on or choosing from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.56wHKxcvf0ImvWqU#golden-flats-ruins-table]{Golden Flats Ruins} table.

  2. Determine what kind of Pathways behemoth recently passed through the area by rolling on or choosing from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.56wHKxcvf0ImvWqU#pathways-behemoth-encounters-table]{Pathways Behemoth Encounters} table.

  3. Use these results to describe a specific scene of destruction shaped by both the place itself and the creature responsible; have the characters @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.56wHKxcvf0ImvWqU#surveying-the-ruins]{survey the ruins}.

If desired, the tables used for this Event may be generalized for broader use elsewhere, whether to depict a behemoth's passage after the fact, or, at the Gamemaster's discretion, to foreshadow or accompany a direct encounter.

Under Development - Early Access

This event is currently in development and may be missing some important pieces of gameplay, such as actors for the beasts, crafting components, and other aspects that may make it difficult to play through.

Determine what kind of site the characters discover in ruins by rolling on or choosing from the table below:

@Embed[RollTable.xM7VkCEwSl7DZC8L inline rollable]

Determine what kind of Pathways behemoth recently passed through the area by rolling on or choosing from the table below:

@Embed[RollTable.EhmbWLCrjPdkdXRO inline rollable]

The characters should not be told the behemoth's identity outright. Instead, they may infer it by examining the physical aftermath of the destruction and interpreting the creature's likely behavior. Refer to the sections below for gameplay details on the combination of ruin and behemoth that were selected.

Ruined Farmstead

The walls of this farmhouse have been split open, its roof sundered and strewn across the golden grasses. A partially devoured human corpse lies outside. Insects writhe on its surface.

Trapped Cat

A frightened cat is stranded atop a tilted beam or broken roof section, hissing at anyone who gets too close.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill animalhandling 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] check convinces the cat to come down over the course of 10 minutes.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] succeed on this check automatically.

Collapsed Granary

This timber-and-brick granary has been cleft in twain, one side burst open into a swell of loose grain and shattered wood. The partially devoured remains of a yarnac lie bloody on the ground.

Injured Beast

A second @UUID[Actor.6HckJyV8TKc37xNT]{Yarnac}, still tethered to a post and grievously injured, lows weakly as the characters approach.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] check can stabilize the Yarnac over the course of 30 minutes.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] gain @Advantage[2] on this check.

Broken Aedir Watchtower

The weathered remains of an old Aedir watchtower lie in fresh ruin, its frame reduced to a heap of fallen stone blocks.

Fallen Signal Bell

Amid the rubble lies a weathered bronze signal bell, still fixed to part of its cracked mounting — and clutched in the hands of a crushed cadaver. It can be worked loose and recovered, though doing so without further collapse requires care.

Any character can attempt to retrieve the signal bell over the course of 10 minutes with a [[/skill athletics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check. Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] gain @Advantage[2] on this roll.

On a success, the character retrieves the signal bell, which is worth 25 gp 3gp. On a failure, the character still retrieves the signal bell, but the rubble pile collapses, causing [[/roll 2d6]] Bludgeoning damage and trapping the character and the character suffers [[/hazard 6 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Minor Crush Injuries}. The character can be extricated over the course of 1 hour.

Shattered Irrigation Terrace

This stretch of farmland has been violently torn asunder, its irrigation channels collapsed and the cultivated furrows churned to thick mud.

Slain Farmers

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]], or who makes a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check while examining the terrace, discovers the bloated and mangled remains of several farmers buried in the mud. Nothing of value is on their person.

Surveying the Ruins

The party can inspect the ruins of the scene to learn about what happened here.

Examine Physical Clues

Any character with a [[/skill investigation 16 passive format=long]], or that succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 14]] a successful [[/skillCheck wilderness 14 passive]] check while examining the scene, gains some insight into the creature's Physical Clues as described in the relevant behemoth table entry. Use these clues in conjunction with the destroyed site result to describe the aftermath.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge monsters]], [[/knowledge subterranea]], or [[/path emberMonsterHunter]] have @Advantage[2] on this roll.

Infer Behavioral Clues

Any character with a [[/skill insight 16 passive format=long]], or that succeeds on a [[/skill insight 14]] a successful [[/skillCheck diplomacy 16 passive]] check while examining the scene, gets an overview of the creature's Behavioral Clues as described in the relevant behemoth table entry. Use these clues in conjunction with the destroyed site result to describe the creature's likely behavior.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge monsters]], [[/knowledge subterranea]], or [[/path emberMonsterHunter]] have @Advantage[2] on this roll.

Outcome

If the party successfully identifies both the creature's Physical Clues and Behavioral Clues, they learn the name of the creature, and also discover that creature's Aftermath Loot as described in the relevant behemoth table entry.

Katherim

The katherim is a towering, six-legged grazer, broad-shouldered and heavy. Its immense weight can ruin fields, walls, and structures simply by passing through them. Though not wantonly destructive, it is stubborn, powerful, and difficult to divert once it has set its course.

Physical Clues

Six deep prints appear in a paired sequence, often sunk deepest at the front where the creature bears most of its weight.

Behavioral Clues

A katherim tends to lumber toward sources of food and water, crashing through obstacles instead of avoiding them; the destruction it wreaks is often incidental to its single-minded goal.

Aftermath Loot

A tuft of katherim hair, torn from its body by another animal — likely the result of a @UUID[Actor.ZuWduzUSGS6i4NZm]{Gore Bird Swarm}, with whom the katherim share a symbiotic relationship. A character with Proficiency in @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulWeaversToo] that is a capable [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.tailoringNovice0]] can knit the hair into a small charm, such as a bracelet, worth 25 sp 25 cp .

Encounter Loot

See the creature's Actor for harvestable materials and other loot.

If the characters successfully identify the katherim from the clues it has left behind, mark the following outcome as complete:

[[/outcome katherim]]

Avir

Avir are enormous pack-hunting birds, lean and vicious, with hooked beaks, powerful legs, and sharp vision.

Physical Clues

Multiple sets of three-toed tracks, deep talon punctures, and tears in wood or thatch; any carcasses present show signs of precise tearing.

Behavioral Clues

Avir prefer to drive prey in different directions, separating the slow and maiming others to prevent them from escaping. They seem to delight in the chase, prolonging death for as long as possible.

Aftermath Loot

[[/roll 1d4+1]] long, dark avir feathers, streaked with blood. A character with Proficiency in @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulWeaversToo] can sew the feathers into a small charm, such as a bracelet or necklace, worth 25 sp.

Encounter Loot

See the creature's Actor for harvestable materials and other loot.

If the characters successfully identify the avir from the clues they have left behind, mark the following outcome as complete:

[[/outcome avir]]

Garganthus

The garganthus is a pale, hulking reptilian creature with a long prehensile tail, many pearlescent eyes, and massive clawed limbs built for impossible bursts of speed.

Physical Clues

Damage appears most heavily on vertical surfaces, with deep claw gouges high on structures or stone faces. There are only intermittent signs of its presence on the ground, as though the creature preferred to leap; long drag marks suggest the use of a long tail.

Behavioral Clues

Despite its size, the Garganthus moves like a stalking predator, favoring sudden changes of height and direction over a direct charge. Much of its destruction is generated from pouncing atop things, rather than striking them head-on.

Aftermath Loot

A fragment of the garganthus's claw, worth 25 sp, which can be wielded as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepDagger0000].

Encounter Loot

See the creature's Actor for harvestable materials and other loot.

If the characters successfully identify the garganthus from the clues it has left behind, mark the following outcome as complete:

[[/outcome garganthus]]

Urkon

The urkon is an ill-tempered and brutish beast of massive proportions, given to direct charges and explosive violence. Wherever it passes, the earth looks rent apart.

Physical Clues

The ground is gouged by broad tracks that overlap in straight lines, like furrows torn by many plows. Any stone it contacts is likely covered in spiderweb cracks, and timber objects are pulverized into splinters.

Behavioral Clues

An Urkon will repeatedly charge the same structure or creature from different angles until its rage is sated, often leaving signs of repeated impacts.

Aftermath Loot

A fragment of the urkon's tusk, worth 25 sp, which can be wielded as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepDagger0000].

Encounter Loot

See the creature's Actor for harvestable materials and other loot.

If the characters successfully identify the urkon from the clues it has left behind, mark the following outcome as complete:

[[/outcome urkon]]

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished surveying the ruined site and gathering any information they can glean from the aftermath, they're free to continue on their journey.
In The Behemoth's Wake.soverview: While traveling through the Golden Flats, the party comes across a ruined site recently devastated by a Pathways behemoth. By examining the aftermath, they may piece together what kind of colossal creature passed this way.
In The Behemoth's Wake.sexposition: The golden grasses ahead have been trampled flat; they bow toward a scene of ruin. Whatever passed through here did so with terrible force, leaving only wreckage in its wake — violence on a scale no ordinary beast could inflict. The marks of destruction are still stark and unmistakable. By examining the ruined site, you may be able to discover what passed this way.
In The Behemoth's Wake.ssummary: While traveling through the Golden Flats, we came across a site recently devastated by a behemoth from the Pathways. We examined the wreckage for signs of the strange creature responsible.

Arcane Maelstrom.name: Arcane Maelstrom
Arcane Maelstrom.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This standalone event takes place while the party travels at a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Reckless} pace through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}, where sudden supernatural upheaval is often a way of life. In this standalone event, the characters can:

  • React to the sudden arrival of an arcane maelstrom, which threatens to rob the party's spellcasters of their spell slots and magic items of their charges.

  • Survive the chaos of the maelstrom's magical energy field.

This event takes place on @UUID[Scene.emberWorldRegion] Region Map, and its probability is dependent upon the party's regional travel speed.

While traversing the Golden Flats with some rapidity, the party encounters a hazardous arcane maelstrom: a chaotic, weather-like phenomenon that channels one (if not several) of Ember's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0DQdqtsLn3M1ZZA2]{Magical Forces} into a localized storm, infused with the raw magic of the Cosmos.

This supernatural vortex is not only physically dangerous, it acts as a mystical siphon, drawing magic energy from whatever sources lurk nearby (including the spell slots of spellcasting characters, and the charges inherent to magic items). If the party acts quickly enough, they can avoid the maelstrom and its tumultuous woes.

Roll on the Golden Flats Arcane Maelstrom table to determine precisely which type of arcane maelstrom the party must contend with.

@Embed[RollTable.m32hCNk1pEk6GImw rollable inline]

In addition to the rolled result, each Arcane Maelstrom has the following properties

Arcane Siphon

  • Any spellcasting character caught in the maelstrom loses [[/roll 1d4]] spell slots, starting with and descending from their highest level spell slot.

  • Any magic item caught in the maelstrom loses [[/roll 1d4]] charges if it is an item with charges. Otherwise, the magical effects of the item are dispelled for [[/roll 1d4]] hours.

Information on how characters can spot and avoid the maelstrom is detailed below.

Navigating the Hazard

Avoiding the Maelstrom

Each character that has a [[/skill perception 17 passive format=long]], or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] check, is able to detect the arcane maelstrom early enough to make an active attempt to navigate it safely, granting them @Advantage[2] on any ability checks or saving throws made to survive or avoid the hazard.

  • Characters with [[/attunement orbis]] have @Advantage[2].

Observing the Maelstrom

People of Ember, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau} in particular, have come to understand arcane maelstroms as an intermittent way of life. While these supernatural hazards aren't omnipresent phenomena, it's rare for a native Arcturian or Ordani to be altogether unfamiliar with them.

Any character who succeeds on either a [[/skill history 12]] or [[/skill nature 12]] check is aware of the potential dangers of arcane maelstroms, and understands that these unavoidable tempests are known to appear haphazardly throughout the region, with little rhyme or reason to their arrival.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberArcturian]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge weather]] have @Advantage[2].
