  • Result of 17+: The character is aware of an arcane maelstrom's ability to strip spellcasters and magic items of their potential (including the respective loss of spell slots and charges).

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check is able to identify some of the maelstrom's abstruse magical properties, and has a bonus round to brace against its uncanny impact.

  • Characters with [[/attunement orbis]] or [[/knowledge weather]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Result of 20+: If the character is a spellcaster, they only lose half of their lost spell slots as detailed in "Properties of the Maelstrom" above.

Surviving the Maelstrom

Each character that has a [[/skill perception 17 passive format=long]], or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] check, is able to detect the arcane maelstrom early enough to make an active attempt to navigate it safely, granting them @Advantage[2] on any ability checks or saving throws made to survive or avoid the hazard.

  • Characters with [[/attunement orbis]] have @Advantage[2].

While the arcane maelstrom cannot be avoided altogether (enveloping the party in mere moments) characters can mitigate its disastrous effects using skill checks, equipment, and other methods.

  • Any character who casts either the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCounterspe]{Counterspell} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} spell with the maelstrom as a target is able to help a number of characters equal to their Charisma modifier automatically succeed on any saving throws associated with the maelstrom's features (minimum of 1 character; including, but not limited to, the spellcaster).

  • Items such as a Dampening Stone provide @Advantage[2] on saving throws associated with arcane maelstroms, and reduce the damage done to the attuned character by a total of [[/roll 1d4]] per charge spent to do so.

  • Skill checks related to a particular type of maelstrom are listed in the rollable table with the maelstrom's description.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished navigating the area where the arcane maelstrom appeared, the characters are free to continue on their journey.
Arcane Maelstrom.soverview: The party happens upon a hazardous arcane maelstrom while recklessly traversing the Golden Flats, and must contend with their dangerous proximity to this calamitous event, lest they succumb to its chaotic metaphysical wrath.
Arcane Maelstrom.sexposition:
As you make your way through the sweeping landscape of the Golden Flats, a commotion begins to stir around you. The ground beneath your feat starts to rumble with a heavy vibration not unlike the trembling of an earthquake, and the terrain begins to fragment like shattered glass — creating a lattice of cracked earth all about you.

Before you know it, the ground starts to swirl around a funnel at the midpoint of this emerging calamity, which appears to be some kind of arcane maelstrom. A small storm of supernatural energy encompasses this malevolent vortex, which threatens to swallow you into its spiraling center!
Arcane Maelstrom.ssummary: We encountered a hazardous arcane maelstrom while traveling the Golden Flats — a dangerous vortex of chaotic magic and wild supernatural effusion.

Sanguinary Salutations.name: Sanguinary Salutations
Sanguinary Salutations.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Social and Exploration Event can occur during the day while traveling through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd]{Golden Flats}. In this Event, the party can:

  • Meet Eliren, a Sanguinary druid, and speak with her about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries'} history and philosophy.

  • Examine creatures recently transmuted by an arcane maelstrom, assist Eliren with her observations, and potentially contribute a useful insight to her work.

If the characters approach Eliren, read or paraphrase the following:

The young woman startles at your approach, but quickly recovers with a warm smile.

Greetings!

She withdraws her hands from the yarnac's chest and gives them a few brisk shakes. Then she extends one — still bloodied and coated in a strange, milky film — toward you in greeting.

My name is Eliren. On behalf of the Sanguinaries and myself, I offer you good tidings. With whom do I have the pleasure of speaking?

Eliren, the Wandering Sanguinary

Eliren (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, she/her) is a @UUID[Actor.BOAxA70Msi7JJVjL]{Sanguinary Druid} tasked by @UUID[JournalEntry.FYP2Af9bY4B9lSqi.JournalEntryPage.TWR1OsUB0LIrt4CJ]{Avwynn Taol} with studying the effects of arcane maelstroms on the creatures of the Golden Flats. Kindly, soft-spoken, and patient, she is more than willing to engage the characters in light conversation about her current task (see "Eliren's Task" below) and the Sanguinaries' history and philosophy.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skill deception 13]] check confirms that Eliren is speaking sincerely, and believes what she says to be true.

What are you doing out here?

"I'm studying the aftermath of a recent arcane maelstrom. These poor creatures were caught in its path, and I mean to learn what I can from what remains of them."

Eliren's smile never dims, though her attention keeps drifting impatiently back toward the carcasses and specimen jars nearby.

Who are the Sanguinaries?

"We seek to nurture life, wheresoever it may be found. There are many who mistrust us… and not always without reason. The Cindarics, for their part, have painted us as radicals since the schism. And, regrettably, there are elements within our organization who would prove them correct. We do not claim them."

A trace of guardedness enters her expression; she is braced for suspicion. She wipes her still-bloodied hands reflexively on her robe.

How does your work here relate?

"These creatures were transmuted into unnatural forms. If their bodies were so violently remade, what then became of their spirit? And what happens to that scarred energy after death? It is my task to determine whether these maelstroms pose a threat beyond what we can see."

Her smile dips momentarily at the weight of her own words.

Eliren's Task

Several creatures lie before Eliren, each mangled and grotesquely transmuted by the maelstrom's effects. When the characters arrive, Eliren has only just begun dissecting the yarnac, systematically removing its organs and preserving them in pickling jars for future examination. The creatures are:

  • The @UUID[Actor.6HckJyV8TKc37xNT]{Yarnac}, its hide flayed and replaced by a translucent, sticky film

  • A @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Bird}, its wings fused together by a brittle crystalline lattice

  • A Tiller Bird, its beak and talons overgrown and curled inward

Eliren's primary concern — and one she will not voice out loud to the characters at this juncture — is whether these transmutations have altered the creatures' Lifeforce. If their Lifeforce was scarred, it may pose a threat to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.0anKTKgOav9sXox1]{Heart of Ember}. Unfortunately, she has no way of proving this one way or another; for all her careful study, the question remains as philosophical as it is scientific.

Helping Eliren

Eliren gratefully accepts another pair of eyes (and hands). Any character who spends at least 1 hour examining the transmuted remains alongside Eliren can attempt one of the following checks:

  • [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skill arcana 13]] The character finds that residual Transmutation magic still clings to the remains, but not evenly; some parts of the creature are more deeply altered than others.

  • [[/skill medicine 13]] [[/skill medicine 13]] The character discovers that the transmutations occurred suddenly, rather than over time; the uneven distribution of alteration suggests spontaneity.

  • [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skill wilderness 13]] The character realizes that the transmutations appear to warp the creature's most vital adaptations: the yarnac its hide, the gore bird its wings, and the tiller bird its beak and talons.

Regardless of whether the characters succeed on a check or not, Eliren is grateful for the assistance, and bids farewell — she stuffs the pickling jars into a large satchel and begins walking in the direction of Ordain. Once Eliren departs, the characters may scavenge the creatures' crafting components.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished speaking with and assisting Eliren, they're free to continue on their journey.
Sanguinary Salutations.soverview: While traveling through the Golden Flats, the party encounters Eliren, a friendly Sanguinary druid studying the effects of arcane maelstroms on the Biome's local fauna. Her grim work offers the characters a rare chance to learn more about both the Sanguinaries and the strange forces reshaping the region.
Sanguinary Salutations.sexposition: Ahead, a young Ordani woman in a simple red robe kneels over the remains of a yarnac, her hands buried deep within the creature's chest cavity. Her gaze is set unwaveringly ahead as she focuses on her work. Nearby, several pickling jars and neatly arranged surgical tools glint in the grass; within some of the jars float pale, unrecognizable masses of flesh.
Sanguinary Salutations.ssummary: While traveling through the Golden Flats, we met Eliren, a friendly Sanguinary druid studying the effects of arcane maelstroms on the local wildlife. Her work offered a rare glimpse into the Sanguinaries' beliefs and unpredictable magical phenomena wracking the region.

Flash Flood.name: Flash Flood
Flash Flood.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration Event can occur while traveling through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.tuopdqO2JSeH1LeU]{Splinter Canyons} on any river-adjacent hex or hex containing a river. In this Event, the party can:

  • Demonstrate their wilderness survival skills by withstanding a deadly flash flood.

The flash flood occurs over the course of 10 minutes, affecting all hexes inside the Splinter Canyons and escalating in intensity every 5 minutes. This event is more likely to occur if the party is traveling at a Fast or Reckless pace. Once the Event has occurred, it cannot occur again for at least 48 hours.

Flood Stages

The party must survive two stages of flooding:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.k7VCz1HvCj134l0e#stage-1:-rising-waters]{Stage 1: Rising Waters}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.k7VCz1HvCj134l0e#stage-2:-canyon-rapids]{Stage 2: Canyon Rapids}

Each stage represents a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.rules.JournalEntry.0AGfrwZRzSG0vNKb.JournalEntryPage.OcHhrKKzffcVi03Q#group-checks]{Group Check} — if at least half of the characters succeed, they proceed to the next stage of flooding without incident. If over half of the characters fail, however, roll on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.k7VCz1HvCj134l0e#rushing-water-perils]{Rushing Water Perils} table. After resolving the hazard, the party proceeds to the next stage of flooding.

At the beginning of each stage, the party may describe any tools they're utilizing to aid them.

Preparedness

Appropriate tools, equipment, magic, or other precautions may grant @Advantage[2] on a relevant roll or an automatic success, per the Gamemaster's discretion.

Such preparations may include: pitons, magical flight, floatation devices, spells such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplControlWat]{Control Water}, or any other sensible method of withstanding rushing water.

Stage 1: Rising Waters

The river in the crevasse swells, drawing even with its banks. Though the waters look calm, they are rapidly intensifying by the minute. Even now, rivulets begin pooling beneath you and spilling through well-worn channels toward the canyon walls. It won't be long until the entire canyon is overcome by white-foamed rapids.

Stage 1: Rising Waters

The characters must react to the rising floodwaters before they overtake the canyon floor with a group skill challenge. Every member of the party must make one of the following tests:

  • A successful [[/skill investigation 16]] check to pull themselves onto firmer footing, secure a handhold, or brace themselves against a perpendicular surface to withstand the oncoming surge.

  • A successful [[/skill survival 16]] check to stay ahead of the spillover, darting across slick ground before the flood closes around them.

If the group check is failed, roll on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.k7VCz1HvCj134l0e#rushing-water-perils]{Rushing Water Perils} table.

Stage 2: Canyon Rapids

The river picks up speed, roaring through the canyons as a churn of white-foamed wrath; the water has swelled all the way to the canyon walls. It fills the canyon with a deafening rush. Branches, debris, and a few small, unlucky beasts caught in the flood's path are dashed against the cliff face and vanish beneath the white, borne swiftly to their deaths.

Stage 2: Canyon Rapids

The characters must struggle to survive the canyon rapids without being swept away with a group skill challenge. Every member of the party must make one of the following tests:

  • A successful [[/skill athletics 18]] check to use their strength to cling to vines, roots, or stone outcroppings, withstanding the torrent by brute force.

  • A successful [[/skill acrobatics 18]] check to move with the rushing water rather than against it, keeping their footing or timing their movements to avoid debris, sudden drops, and the worst of the current.

If the group check is failed, roll on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.k7VCz1HvCj134l0e#rushing-water-perils]{Rushing Water Perils} table.

Rushing Water Perils

Drowning

A character that is forced beneath the water from the effects of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.k7VCz1HvCj134l0e#rushing-water-perils]{Rushing Water Peril} begins to &Reference[Suffocation]{Suffocate}. The number of minutes the creature Suffocates is determined by the table result.

@Embed[RollTable.vFVfKkgss4m5xp5s inline rollable]

Concluding the Event

The flash flood rapidly subsides, allowing the characters to regroup, recover, and continue on their journey.
Flash Flood.soverview: While traveling through the Splinter Canyons along the river, the party is overtaken by a sudden flash flood that threatens to sweep them downstream — or drown them where they stand.
Flash Flood.sexposition: You feel a tremor in the earth, a deep vibration, like something breaking free. Seconds later, a geyser of steaming water erupts from beneath the river upstream of your position. Then another. And another. One by one, a cascading line of superheated geysers disgorges its contents into the Splinter Canyons. You can do nothing but watch as the water begins to rise with startling speed.
Flash Flood.ssummary: While traveling through the Splinter Canyons along the river, we were overtaken by a devastating flash flood that filled the entire canyon. We managed to survive by strength and wit, but the ordeal did not leave us unscathed.

The Giants' Span.name: The Giants' Span
The Giants' Span.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration Event can occur while traveling recklessly through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands}. In this Event, the party can:

  • Investigate a crumbling remnant of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} empire: an ancient shelf road, cut into the mountainside above a ravine.

  • Inspect the ruin for a safer path, attempt to cross it, or lose time by turning back and going around.

Circumventing the Span

The characters may circumvent the giants' span by retreating into an adjacent hex in the opposite direction of their destination and moving around the hex in which this Event triggered. Make a note of where this Event triggered as the location of the giants' span; the characters face the same decision upon entering this hex in the future.

Inspecting the Span

Before the party attempts to cross the giants' span, they may inspect its construction for a safer path.

Inspecting the Span

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 20]] or [[/skill investigation 20]] check while examining the giants' span identifies a prevailing architectural pattern evident in the stone: the wider outer shelf is badly degraded, but a staggered inner line of intact flagstones suggests a loadbearing path.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]], [[/knowledge subterranea]], or the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.origins24.Item.phbsptStonecunni]{Stonecunning} feature have @Advantage[2] on this roll.

Identify the Origin

Characters with [[/knowledge shent]], [[/knowledge ancients]], or Proficiency in [[/skill history]] identify the shelf road as a deliberate feat of Shent engineering; they recognize the visage as a Shent giant, and can estimate its age and that of the shelf road as approximately 3,000 years old.

Eye of Black Pearl

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]], or who makes a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check while examining the carved visage from afar, discovers that some kind of jewel gleams within one of its eye sockets. The gleaming jewel is a large black pearl worth [[/award party 200gp]].

To recover the black pearl, a character must:

  • Reach the base of the visage (60 feet along the shelf road).

  • Climb 30 feet by making a successful [[/skill athletics 16]] check — on a failure, roll on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.spCqEKBrDKN3sOyD#climbing-hazards]{Climbing Hazards} table, and apply the result to the climbing character only (not the entire party).

  • Make a successful [[/skill strength 12]] check to dislodge it from its stone setting. If the character fails this check by 10 or more, the black pearl pops out, falls, skips off the shelf road, and vanishes into the ravine below.

[[/outcome identifiedOrigin]]

Falling

A character that falls from the effects of a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.spCqEKBrDKN3sOyD#climbing-hazards]{Climbing Hazard} while attempting to retrieve the black pearl falls 30 feet onto the shelf road, taking ([[/damage 3d6 Bludgeoning]] damage) and landing &reference[Prone]. This immediately triggers the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.spCqEKBrDKN3sOyD#crumbling-shelf]{Crumbling Shelf} hazard for [[/gmroll 1d4]] randomly selected characters as described below.

Crossing the Span

Crossing the Span

The shelf road is 120-feet-long, 5-feet-wide, and lies 120 feet over the ravine below. At intervals of 30 feet, the party must make a [[/skill dexterity 14]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.rules.JournalEntry.0AGfrwZRzSG0vNKb.JournalEntryPage.OcHhrKKzffcVi03Q#group-checks]{Group Check}: if at least half of the characters succeed, they proceed without incident. If over half of the character fail, however, [[/gmroll 1d4]] randomly selected characters are subjected to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.spCqEKBrDKN3sOyD#crumbling-shelf]{Crumbling Shelf} hazard.

  • Characters that identified the architectural pattern while @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.spCqEKBrDKN3sOyD#inspecting-the-span]{inspecting the span} have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Crumbling Shelf

Description: The shelf road suddenly crumbles under the character's feet, leaving them grasping at the side of the cliff face for support.

Effect: The character must make a successful [[/save strength 16]] save or take [[/damage 1d6 Piercing]] damage from sharp rocks and suffer one level of &Reference[exhaustion]. Any character that fails by 10 or more must also make a successful [[/check athletics 12]] check or fall 120 feet into the ravine below, taking ([[/damage 12d6 Bludgeoning]] damage) and landing &reference[Prone]. Any character who succeeded on the initial save (or was not subjected to the hazard at all) may take the Help action to grant @Advantage[2] to one character making this check.

If this hazard occurs three or more times, the entire shelf road crumbles into the ravine after [[/gmroll 1d4]] days, and the hex becomes impassible.

[[/outcome acrossTheShelfRoad]]

Ragen Attunement: Across the Shelf Road

If the party cross the shelf road, they advance their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 theGiantsSpanCrossed]] at the conclusion of the event.

Climbing Hazards

@Embed[RollTable.xtUlzhr0LusL2Xkc inline rollable]

Concluding the Event

Once the party has crossed the giants' span or decided to circumnavigate it, they're free to continue on their journey.
The Giants' Span.soverview: The party reaches an ancient shelf road carved into the mountainside by the mighty Shent. The old route is the most direct path forward, but it is visibly failing. The party must decide to brave the giants' span or circumvent it at the expense of time.
The Giants' Span.sexposition: What was once a broad shelf road has narrowed to a tapering ledge of cracked slate and weathered stone. Loose shale chips skip from the cliffside and vanish into the ravine below. Above, a massive visage looms carved into the mountainside; its features are worn smooth and split by age, but the eyes remain deep-set beneath a moss-covered brow, and seem to follow your every step. The way forward may be treacherous, but circumventing it would cost you time.
The Giants' Span.ssummary: While traveling across the Wedgelands, we came upon a crumbling shelf road carved into the side of the mountain, looked over by an aged, formidable visage.

Shent Observatory.name: Shent Observatory
Shent Observatory.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Exploration and Combat Event can occur while traveling through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CgqmvuJ1NLfqaO3I]{Rustvar Valleys}. In this Event, the party can:

  • Investigate a ruined observatory once used by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} to study cosmological forces, and later repurposed by Arcturians as a barrow.

  • Realign its rusting instrument to reveal a treasure cache.

  • Fend off a group of undead warriors that rise to defend the site.

Exploring the Observatory

The observatory lies in ruin atop a stone outcropping. A broad stepped platform dominates the site, crumbling around a mechanism half-buried in mossy rubble.

Identifying the Ruin

Characters with [[/knowledge shent]], [[/knowledge ancients]], or Proficiency in [[/skill history]] identify the site as a ruined Shent observatory, and can estimate its age as approximately 3,000 years old.

[[/ancestry Arcturian]] characters, characters with [[/knowledge ancients]] or [[/knowledge rituals]], and characters with Proficiency in [[/skill history]] identify markers — burial niches and engraved funerary script — that suggest the site was used, or later repurposed, as a barrow by early Arcturian settlers. They can estimate the age of these markers as approximately 1,000 years old.

Characters who make a successful [[/skill arcana 16]] check recognize the engraved funerary script as ritualized @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGentleRepo]{Gentle Repose} spells, though their magic has long since faded.

[[/outcome identifiedRuinShent]]

[[/outcome identifiedRuinArcturian]]

When a character inspects the stepped platform, read or paraphrase the following:

The faded stepped platform is scored with weathered carvings, though much of it still lies beneath rubble and overgrowth. The lengths of metal jutting from its surface sway with the wind, and their slow movement sends a faint grinding sound through the stone.

Investigating the Stepped Platform

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] check while examining the stepped platform determines that the rusting metal arms were once part of a larger astronomical mechanism. Most still rest in deliberate relation to the carvings on the stone, but one has long since slipped from its proper alignment.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge cosmology]], characters who can understand [[/language pathward]], and characters who @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.7C7QyYxzFxvFC3cQ#identifying-the-ruin]{identified the ruin} as an observatory automatically succeed on this check.

Restoring the Mechanism

A character who understands the stepped platform's function may attempt to force the unaligned metal arm into alignment by making a [[/skill athletics 16]] check. On a failure, the arm groans and shifts, but does not lock into place. On a success, the mechanism settles into place with a heavy clunk, a hidden compartment grinds open at the base of the stepped platform, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.7C7QyYxzFxvFC3cQ#rising-skallith]{interred dead stir to life}.

If the characters attempt to move the arm three separate times and fail each time, the arm snaps off but jams partially into place, forcing the hidden compartment halfway open and triggering the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.7C7QyYxzFxvFC3cQ#rising-skallith]{skallith encounter}. The cache can then be excavated over the course of 1 hour using appropriate tools, such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulMasonsTool]{Mason's Tools}.

The Funerary Cache

Inside the hidden compartment lies a sealed funerary cache placed there by ancient Arcturian settlers: a collection of ritual objects once used to prepare and honor the dead. The cache is a large, lacquered wood chest that contains the following:

  • A bronze funerary mask with severe expression, covered in verdigris and wrapped in stiff linen cloth (worth [[/award party 200gp]]).

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll00]{Spell Scroll} of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGentleRepo]{Gentle Repose}, featuring the same funerary script present on the ruins.

  • A bronze urn engraved with ancient Arcturian ritual symbols and covered in verdigris, containing trace amounts of foul-smelling oil (worth [[/award party 25gp]]).

  • An ancient Arcturian @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesFine]{Funerary Ritual Garb}.

  • A linen bundle of 20 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCandle00000]{Tallow Candles}, rancid with age.

  • Dried herbs that crumble at the touch.

[[/outcome funeraryCacheFound]]

Signara Attunement: Funerary Cache Found

If the party discovers the funerary cache, they advance their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 funeraryCacheFound]] at the conclusion of the event.

Rising Skallith

When the mechanism locks into place, read or paraphrase the following:

The metal arm settles into alignment with a deep, grinding scream. For a moment, nothing happens. Then a deeper groan rattles through the ruin; dust spills from the seams cut through the stonework, and old niches grind open, exhaling air that smells of death. Something buried here is beginning to stir.

@Embed[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV inline]

@Embed[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy inline]

Skallith Numbers

There are 4 @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} and 3 @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy]{Skallith Warriors}.

Skallith Tactics

As undead, the skallith prioritize the closest enemy they can see, with no regard for tactical optimization beyond what weapon can strike their target.

Fight or Flight

The skallith fight until destroyed.

If the party chooses to flee, the skallith pursue, but not past the edges of the Scene.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has defeated the skallith and finished exploring the Shent observatory, they're free to continue on their journey.
Shent Observatory.soverview: The party discovers a crumbling observatory left behind by the mysterious Shent, later reappropriated by early Arcturian settlers as a barrow. Investigating the observatory's ruined mechanisms may reveal a hidden treasure, but doing so risks awakening the interred dead.
Shent Observatory.sexposition: A scatter of broken stone crowns the rise ahead, overgrown with brush and thorned vines. At the center stands a broad, stepped ruin of faded rock, surrounded by smaller squat structures that lean at odd angles; several have fallen into rubble at the base of the outcropping. Lengths of rusting metal jut from the central platform, and narrow seams divide the stonework in careful lines, as though sections of the ruin were made to open. Whatever purpose this place once served, it has stood empty for a very long time.
Shent Observatory.ssummary: While traveling through the Rustvar Valleys, we discovered a ruin perched atop a rocky outcropping.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.IVArj8xHt94eRY9g] depicts the entirety of the Aedir Digsite, otherwise known as the Jekeroka Villa location when it is discovered during the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1]{The Expedition Challenge} quest event @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.8CFcW8ez6IW1WNV4]{Manufactured Trial}.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.xWbqvB7nm4SZuXTd inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Illumination

The exterior of the digsite has no illumination other than the natural light from Lantyr. There are no lights from the digsite revealing the presence of a structure at night. However, if the party encounters the digsite at night, they will see @UUID[Actor.GA8VFWysoIYfNWCL]{Adelyne Goss} illuminated by a lantern.

Inside the dig site, the interior is lit by ancient Aedir magical lamps that cast bright light for 5 feet and dim light for 10 feet. Additionally, the main chamber of the dig site has a magical elemental energy bubbling quietly and emitting a magical blue light across the room.

Terrain

The area is broken up into several rooms, all branching away from the @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Main Chamber} one, of which, the @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.OOkUnAlIm6zEls20]{Meditation Room} is blocked behind rubble and must be cleared by the party before they can gain access.

Elevation

The ceilings of this villa are 30 feet high, and the entire structure is mostly flat with little change in elevation. There are stairs leading up to platforms within @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Main Chamber} and stairs leading into the @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.OOkUnAlIm6zEls20]{Meditation Room}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.RPTscR0MVmIA9B7P]{Librarium} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.iRj07rPeLl15VAVY]{Workshop}. All of these level changes are 5 feet.

Within the @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Main Chamber}, there are several pits that drop down into the swirling magical elemental energy; these pits are 10 feet deep.

Main Chamber.name: Main Chamber
Main Chamber.text:
As you step through the entrance into the main chamber of the dig site, you notice the air around you is cool, but an ancient energy seems to hum just below the surface. Your footsteps echo softly against the pale stone floor, and while the chamber is large with tall ceilings, your eyes are drawn to the large pits of elemental energy that bubble gently at the center of the room. The surface of this elemental energy shimmers with deep blues and turns black around the edges. Around the walls, intricate patterns and strange golden lamps pulse softly, casting delicate shadows that dance in time with the light from the magical energy coming from below. The craftsmanship is astonishing, and it’s clear this place has been both preserved and well-maintained by the Anachraenum.

Magical Elemental Energy

Within the main chamber are a number of pits that drop into glowing blue energy, which looks strangely like blue lava. Creatures that fall ten feet into this elemental energy are not submerged, but instead stand on top of it. However, they take [[/damage 3d10 fire]] damage. The intense heat and volatile nature of the energy cause immediate and searing pain. The character also takes an additional [[/damage 1d10 fire]] damage at the start of their turns if they are in combat, as the energy continues to burn until they climb out.

Anyone who wishes to investigate the elemental energy can learn the following:

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} or rolls a [[/check arcana 14]], or if a character has [[/knowledge elementals]], they recognize that this energy is strange. It is a deeply magical substance and one that seems to be powering the site, but it has not faded over the millennia and curiously continues to draw power from an unknown source, though likely, given the magical signature, that it is tied to several different elemental moons.

  • Any character with [[/knowledge aedir]] finds the substance fascinating to some degree, as there are notes and myths surrounding this substance being present in other Aedir ruins. Perhaps this might be the original source of the energy?

Polished Aedir Stone

With a [[/skill prc 12 passive]] or successful [[/skill prc 12]] check, it is obvious that the interior stonework within the chamber is substantially more preserved than the exterior. In fact, the stone still has an element of shine and polish to it, as if it is cleaned regularly. The only marks appear to be from regular travel of muddy boots leading from the door into the site.

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 14]], they discover that the stone is slightly magical in nature, at least in terms of preservation.

Strange Rubble

On the left side of the chamber, when the party enters, are two small heaps of rubble blocking the space into the room on the left, leading to the @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.OOkUnAlIm6zEls20]{Meditation Room}.

Deliberate Challenge

The Anacharsnum has placed these rubble piles to simulate what a blocked room might look like and how a band of adventurers would handle clearing the way.

  • If a character attempts to study the rubble with [[/check inv 12]], or has [[/knowledge subterranea]], they discover that the stone has been stacked together deliberately and seems to be held together by a hard-set glue or binding agent of some kind.

A character with a successful [[/check str 14]] will easily break apart the rocky rubble, and the glue will crumble, revealing the room ahead.

A Prepared Encounter

The four Anachraenum Aetherials in the main chamber have been programmed to attack only after the three switches in the other rooms have been pressed. Until then, they remain invisible, as all four have had invisibility cast upon them by @UUID[Actor.GA8VFWysoIYfNWCL]{Adelyne Goss}, and cannot be seen. In the event that any character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSeeInvisib]{See Invisibility}, the combat encounter begins immediately, and the party skips finding the switches in the other rooms. Otherwise, after the party has flipped all three switches in the other rooms and return to the @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Main Chamber}, read the following:

With small magical whines as if they are powering up, strange purple machines appear from nothing within the main chamber. They shudder and twist in the air as the central core turns and focuses directly on you.

@Embed[Actor.Lw8HeAY64cjHnuQq]

Anachraenum Aetherial Tactics

The Anachraenum Aetherial's are extremely simple creatures that do not have any sentient or cognitive capacity to think. they merely do what they have been programmed to do by members of the Anachranum who have access to them.

In this combat encounter, they have been programmed to attack and use their @UUID[Actor.Lw8HeAY64cjHnuQq.Item.OnYsxWrpQdSjwSy8]{Laser} action on thier turn to attack members at random.

If they are in melee range with a party members, the Aetherial will move away and try to gain a maximum distance of 40 feet regardless of attacks of opportunity.

Studying the Aetherial's

After the encounter, the party may attempt to investigate the small constructs, and they discover the following:

  • With a successful [[/check inv 13]], any character can determine that the Aetherial's are being powered by a magically infused @UUID[Item.hMeljYMb7OxbfNKv]{Iolite} which they can pry away and keep.

  • A successful [[/check arc 15]] or anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] determines that these strange little constructs have been created by an extremely competent and powerful arcane mage, with a level of technology approaching the Aedir but still somewhat unrefined.

The Challenge Key

At the end of the encounter with the @UUID[Actor.Lw8HeAY64cjHnuQq]{Anachraenum Aetherial}'s the hidden chest at the top of the stairs in the main chamber appears magically. Inside is the @UUID[Item.SAm2oCDjRdZggcot]{Trial Challenge Key} that the party needs to continue.

Meditation Room.name: Meditation Room
Meditation Room.text:
The small chamber is surrounded by polished stone walls decorated with glowing small Aedir glyphs that illuminate the space with a calming radiance. On the far wall, a raised dais holds a large, intricately woven cushion and several empty candle holders. Beside the cushion is a note. written in common, it appears to have been written by the Anacharanum rather than using an ancient Aedir script, and it reads:

To gain what was sought by those who before,
Speak the truth of what you adore.
It’s found in a places, both warm and bright,
Where shadows dance in the softest light.

Meditation and Reflection

This is the chamber where Jekeroka meditated rather than sleeping during his time at the villa. The party must solve the riddle to proceed.

With a [[/skill prc 13 passive]] or successful [[/skill prc 13]] check, it is obvious that the glyphs are Aedir in nature, and anyone with [[/knowledge aedir]] or who reads Aedir can understand what they say, which is that this was once a room where an Aedir Mage meditated and spent time considering arcane advancements. Nothing else is mentioned, and the graphs seem more meant for reflection and gaining a passive understanding of magic in a peaceful way.

A successful [[/skill arc 14]] check reveals that the glyphs are also powered by the elemental energy within the main chamber and have been active since the Shattering, a truly astonishing feat of magic.

Solving the Riddle

The riddle on the note is relatively simple: anyone who speaks the word 'Knowledge' hears a small click while in the room, and a hidden compartment opens in the dais, revealing a small switch. I the party is struggling to answer the riddle, ask the party members to roll an [[/check insight 12]]; those who succeed are able to figure out the correct answer. Once the switch is pushed, nothing seems to happen immediately, but the challenge with this room is over.

Librarium.name: Librarium
Librarium.text:
Inside the small room, stone shelves line every wall, holding hundreds of crumbling scrolls, many in various stages of decay. The ceiling like the other rooms curves inwards and comes together to a central apex above. The air is thick with dust, and the strong smell of old parchment fills the space. Magical lights flicker in alcoves, casting an uneven glow over a central table, which is covered with cracked charts and what appear to be heavily aged maps.

Concealed Darts

The Anachraenum has trapped the shelves within the room. Anyone who does not say they are being extremely careful with the crumbling scrolls on the shelves must make a [[/check slt 15]]. On failure, a small, thin dart spring from a hidden tube on the shelves and hits the character for [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] damage. The character must then roll a [[/check con 16]] or they lose their vision for 1 minute, gaining the Blinded condition.

Any character with a [[/skill prc 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill prc 16]] check can spot the small dart tubes concealed among the scrolls, and can disarm them by carefully picking them up.

Revealing the Hidden Switch

As the party advances into the room and looks down, alongside the crumbling charts and maps on the central table is a freshly written note, written by the Anachraenum. It reads:

Within this room is a hidden switch. Follow the clues carefully to reveal its location.

The players must examine the scrolls and maps for clues. Each player can make an [[/check int 14]] to study the contents of the table. A success reveals among the papers on the table is a detailed map of the @UUID[.]{Librarium} with certain highlighted areas that correlate to wall markings.

  • Result of 15+: Scrawled annotations on the map mention Towards the watchful eyes.

Any character who succeeds on either a [[/check inv 14]] or a [[/check perception 14]] while examining the walls of the chamber can locate several eye symbols drawn by the Anachraenum, which all appear to be looking upwards towards the ceiling.

If a character stands upon the table or finds another way to reach towards the central apex they find a switch in plain view. Once the switch is pushed, nothing seems to happen immediately, but the challenge with this room is over.

Jekeroka's Ledger

While the Anachraenum has spent many years researching the villa, they have not found all of its secrets and still have many unanswered questions. The party may be able to uncover something new during their investigation in the Librarium and discover a few details of the Aedir Magi Jekerokawas up to in this villa.

A Unique Discovery

While sifting through the crumbling scrolls, the party has the opportunity to uncover a ledger detailing Jekeroka's discoveries that even the experienced scholars of the Anchraenum missed. Despite its age, they can read about the Magi's insights into the use of elemental energies from the various moons of Ember to create their strange Elemental Flux. If any character during the course of their investigation in the villa succeeds on one of the investigation checks with a result higher than 18. Read the following:

Although you are sure you are on to something regarding the switch, it seems among the maps of the villa itself is a odd void or gap in the annotations where you would have expected a scrible to occur, the map of the villa on the table seems to be a preserved original, so this damage doesnt seem to be the work of the Anachraenum.

Anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] realizes that they might be looking at a hidden clue, and casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMending000]{Mending} on the map might repair the text.

Once mending is cast, the map annotation returns, and it points to a hidden compartment on one of the walls. A simple [[/check slt 11]] over the wall in question reveals a small nook where @UUID[Item.8F7cuYr7pgDOaSej]{Jekeroka's Ledger} has sat for over two and a half thousand years.

Workshop.name: Workshop
Workshop.text:
Within this small room, dust motes float in the light of magical orbs attached to the nearby walls. Stone workbenches are scattered throughout, covered in rusted tools and broken remnants. Perhaps the room once held far more mechanisms, but the Anachraenum seems to have cleared the area of the more complete inventions.

Anachraenum Pressure Plates

The room is covered in a thick layer of dust, which at first probably doesn't seem very peculiar to the party. However, anyone with a [[/skill prc 12 passive]] or a successful [[/skill prc 12]] check can see that this dust has been scattered intentionally. Any character who stops and attempts to brush aside or investigate the dust layer with [[/check inv 13]] discovers that across the room are a number of pressure plates disguised and incorporated into the original floor to the degree that they are almost seamless.

Triggering the Traps

If any character steps on a pressure plate without noticing, the trap is activated. Upon triggering, a mechanism within the walls activates, causing small darts to shoot from hidden alcoves. The character must then roll a [[/save dex 15]] or take [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] damage.

Finding the Switch

The switch in this room is not hidden and lies on the table on the southern side. Anyone who reaches the table and manages to avoid the traps is able to clearly see it and press it. Once the switch is pushed, nothing seems to happen immediately, but the challenge with this room is over.

Exterior.name: Exterior
Exterior.text:
Players may wish to stop and examine the exterior stone work of the digsite and the Anachraenum supplies around it and you can read them the following:

The stone works of the ruin suggest that it was once embedded or even hidden within the side of the cliff, but the Anachraenum likely excavated it at some point. The smooth stone pillars surround a metal-looking door that is firmly sealed shut.

Inspecting the Digsite

If anyone from the party investigates the stonework and succeeds on [[/skill inv 14]] check, or they have [[/knowledge aedir]], they know that the structure here was built by the Aedir Empire. Additionally, anyone who has completed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl]{Ooze Control} recognizes that the style here is reminiscent of the flickering tower.

The nature of the stonework is clearly Aedir in character, as it appears smooth, timeless, and made of a material that seems to have grown and been molded rather than hewn and placed. Famously, the Aedir built many of their structures using magic similar to the shape stone spell, but more refined and on a larger scale.

  • Result of 16+ yields the following information.

    The site is ancient, but the door and stonework are in very good condition, hinting at the physical preservation of the site, as well as a faint, lingering magical quality in the stone itself.

  • Result of 18+ and with those [[/attunement emberCora]] yields the following information.

    You notice that the door of the structure was once sealed with a magical ward of some kind, though its lingering effects have long since disappeared. Your hand seems to resonate with energies from Cora as it passes over the metal alloy.

Cliffside Construction

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill sur 12]] check or [[/skill sur 12 passive]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] or have [[/knowledge subterranea]] recognize that the digsite itself was buried at some point, either intentionally or across a large enough part of the cliff collapsed, but it was unearthed again, likely by the Anachraenum, some years ago for study.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

This area map shows the exterior grounds of Oldcraft Lodge and three interior rooms within the lodge.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.sdIjbPRNIsJ3ApcU inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

Ordinarily, the goal of any characters passing through Oldcraft Lodge is to speak with Sigil and gather any information they can from the refugees in the area, who are clustered in encampments outside of the lodge.

Illumination

Outside of Oldcraft Lodge, the lighting matches the current time of day in the world. Campfires provide dim illumination in a 30 foot range around them during the night. Inside of Oldcraft Lodge, lighting provides bright illumination unless otherwise noted.

Terrain

Oldcraft Lodge has normal terrain throughout, unless otherwise indicated.

Elevation

The indoor spaces of Oldcraft Lodge generally have 40-foot ceilings.

The Group of Wagons.name: The Group of Wagons
The Group of Wagons.text:
In the center of a group of wagons, two women are working to bring packages down — one is slender, short, and tan with cross-cropped hair and singe marks on her Arcturian clothing, while the other is broader-shouldered and pale, with shoulder-length hair that has been awkwardly cut and a bandage around her waist. A young Hulg'run boy sits nearby, tossing a stone from one gray chiseled hand to the other at a rapid, almost frantic pace.

Special Delivery

The woman in the bandages, Tay, does all the talking, while her companion breathes heavily and lapses into a coughing fit every now and then.

You like the capable kind… feel like giving us a hand over here? If you want to grab and move boxes, that would be great. Or we can handle it, if you can keep an eye on Vilby here. And I wish there was something any of us could do about Laria's cough.

Characters can lift the boxes down from the wagon with a successful[[/skill strength 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check.

  • On a failed check, the boxes begin to tumble to the ground. Characters involved in the lift must succeed on a[[/save dexterity 15]] save or they take [[/damage 1d2 bludgeoning]] damage as boxes fall on them. Laria and Tay then focus on clean-up and cannot share any useful information.

  • On a failed check, the boxes begin to tumble to the ground. Characters involved in the lift must face[[/hazard 2 reflex health bludgeoning]]{Tumbling Boxes}. Laria and Tay then focus on clean-up and cannot share any useful information.

Characters can cure Laria's cough with a successful[[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14]]check, by giving her a healing potion, or by casting a healing spell. With her cough cured, she redoubles her efforts, and the women are able to finish taking the boxes down in no time.

If characters try to talk to Vilby, they find him unresponsive, focused on tossing the stone back and forth between his hands. With a successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check, characters can tell that he is worried about something or someone.

If asked about his worries, Vilby doesn't respond, but stops tossing the stone. Laria chimes in between coughs:

One of his best friends escaped the fire that burned down our little village, but went in a different direction, toward Corpin Sanctuary. I hear they're turning folks away there, so the family will probably head this way next, but Vilby worries about who they'll meet on the road, don't you Vilby? That's why he's got that stone — ready to defend us if he needs to.

  • With a successful [[/skill performance 14]] [[/skillCheck performance 14]] check, characters can tell Vilby an engaging story about heroes defeating monsters and bandits, keeping him focused.

  • With a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, characters can persuade Vilby that everything will be okay and he will see his friend again soon.

If characters fail the check, Vilby gets bored and begins to wander off. Laria prevents him from leaving, but her attention is now split, making it impossible to get more information from the pair.

Once the boxes are successfully taken care of, Tay shares a bit about their journey, which took them to Arcturel not too long ago:

After our village burned at the hands of these horrible bandits, we thought to settle in Arcturel. Mining work is steady work and we don't mind the labor. Plus a town built into a hole in a ground seems like it might be a safer place right now. But something was off there.

People were disgruntled, accidents breaking down elevators and people getting sick just from drinking their favorite brew. From what I heard, it was House Cevher's fault, but blame doesn't keep Vilby safe and it seemed like things were getting worse, so we headed this way.

Tay doesn't have any further details — all she knows is that things were going wrong in Arcturel and the locals believe it is House Cevher's fault.

The Dancing Flames.name: The Dancing Flames
The Dancing Flames.text:
From a distance, the campfire appears to dance, twisting and turning as if a large group of people is dancing, leaping, and twirling together. Two travelers are warming themselves by the glow, one is dressed in a bright multicolored patchwork coat, while the other wears plain gray leather that highlights the fiery streaks beneath her skin.

Speaking With The Performers

As you approach the pair of travelers, the woman in brown nods at you, then mutters under her breath. Her companion sighs.

Don't mind Gilara. She's just convinced that our troupe of performers being set upon by bandits is somehow all my fault.

Gilara mutters something else, though it is hard to catch the words over the crackling of the fire. Whatever it is, she seems serious about it.

Perturbed Performers

With a successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]], the players can hear some of what Gilara is muttering – the words “fire” and “fortunes” come through loudly enough to be heard. If asked, both Kilson and Gilara are familiar with the phrase “For Other Fortunes,” which they heard used by a suspicious merchant who approached them for supplies and a group of bandits who stole those supplies from them a few days later.

With a successful [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check, characters can tell that both Kilson and Gilara feel guilty about what happened to them, though Gilara's guilt is mixed with anger. The pair were part of a traveling group of performers attacked by bandits while traveling to Helkas from the south.

Gilara and I are all that is left of Mischief and Mirth. I was on the mirth side. Comedy, color, a few cantrips. Things were going great until the bandits attacked us. And it might have been my fault.

Kilson can share the following:

  • The bandits seemed especially interested in an alchemical flame retardant Gilara uses in her “walking through fire” act. If players took a sample of the alchemical substance used by the bandits, they can confirm that it is the same substance.

  • Kilson bragged about the substance a few days before the attack to a merchant in a long cloak. Gilara did not trust the merchant, who claimed to be working for someone called the Captain and was heading towards Arcturel. persuasion

Gilara will only speak about what happened with characters who make a successful [[/skill intimidation 15]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 15]]or [[/skill persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check.

  • Gilara knew that the merchant was not to be trusted and wishes Kilson had listened to her. He gave her a bad feeling and she was glad to hear that he was headed in a different direction, towards Arcturel.

Kilson's Guilt/Kilson's Mistake

I'm all about making people happy, so when the merchant showed up, I wanted him to know what we had to offer. I may have bragged a little bit about the flame repelling gel that Gilara developed to help with her "walk through fire," but I thought the man was trustworthy. I should have listened to Gilara and kept my words about her supplies to myself.

The Strange Merchant

Gilara never liked him, and he did ask a lot of questions. All I really remember is that he wore a long black cloak and said he was working for someone called the Bonny Captain. I wouldn't have thought of it again except for two things: for someone claiming to be a merchant, he didn't buy anything, and everything he asked about was taken by the bandits a few days later. By that time he was probably halfway to Arcturel.

Entrance Path.name: Entrance Path
Entrance Path.text:
As you walk along the path to Oldcraft Lodge, you can hear the lively sounds of bustling campsites nearby—pots clang, people chat around campfires, and eat simple meals or go about daily tasks. The aroma of cooked fish and bread drifts through the air. Ahead, the grand lodge stands prominently at the cliff's edge, overlooking Lake Jinro.

The party can stop to look around outside Oldcraft for a time, but none of the people nearby pay them any attention. There is already too much going on, and plenty of wandering refugees coming and going from the area.

If the party does want to wait a moment, you can tell them that they can see two women unloading a wagon to the right and start @UUID[JournalEntry.tZhj2UzXEN4cw4nl.JournalEntryPage.aMiF6rTOg2uqploy]{The Group of Wagons} if they head over. Or if they look to the left, they can see a few people around a campfire that seems to be dancing and crackling @UUID[JournalEntry.tZhj2UzXEN4cw4nl.JournalEntryPage.NMJ8jEloVgvXilFH]{The Dancing Flames} if they head in that direction.

If the party decides to move onwards towards the lodge instead, the doors to the lodge itself are partially open, and you can begin @UUID[JournalEntry.tZhj2UzXEN4cw4nl.JournalEntryPage.6uhp2gZV0rwNUgoG]{Portal Room}.

The Storage Room.name: The Storage Room
The Storage Room.text:
A pair of refugees stands arguing in the center of the room. As you walk towards them, they do not appear to notice your presence, continuing their conversation, which has apparently turned into an argument about the food sacks in front of them.

Keffie, you idiot, we need to ration these; we can't just take a few. These will be needed for the next season!

The Squabbling Farmers

The farmers do not notice the party's presence at first, but even when they do, they will not acknowledge it and continue their argument, or if they do, they seem to be ignoring it in favor of continuing their discussion. With a successful [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check, characters know that the best way to get their attention is either to contribute something to the discussion or by invoking Sigil's name. Characters can get the scholars' attention by:

  • With a successful [[/skill persuasion 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]]check the character convinces Keffe that Sigil has a plan for food. And they don't need to use anything in here.

  • Or with a successful [[/skill intimidation 13]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 13]] check the character can scare them both into realizing that their shouting is destabilizing Sigil's concentration, and he might kick them out of his lodge.

A Strange Reward.

Once the argument is settled, the farmers feel sheepish. They can't give you gold (they have none), but they give you a@UUID[Item.6P7Qy2PFsBDerDlX]{Suspiciously Large Carrot} that they have been saving. They assure you that it's perfectly safe eat despite it glowing slightly yellow.

Sigil's Living Room.name: Sigil's Living Room
Sigil's Living Room.text:
Although the exterior of the Oldcraft Lodge is relatively unassuming, as soon as you step inside the main room from outside, you are immediately dazzled by a chaotic cacophony of sights and sounds. Bright yellow and pink motes of magic dance in the air, casting an enchanting glow around the space. Mystical runes are casually scattered in piles across tables and shelves. The room is filled with books of all sizes, colors, and ages; some sit half-open, while others have torn pages now lying in piles. Tall bookshelves line the walls, packed with more books and scrolls, and colorful rugs adorn the polished hardwood floor.

Standing near a large, comfortable-looking chair is a figure who appears to radiate magic in gentle waves. After only a few moments, the effects of his magical aura subside, and he turns toward you with a puzzled expression on his face.

A God of Books

The man standing in the room is the Shard God Sigil. He is a friendly yet confusing being, and conversations can be difficult to understand as he attempts to follow random trains of thought. If the party includes a Cleric of Sigil or follows Sigil in some way, they recognize him immediately.

@Embed[Actor.qmMlHizvtjCYKjCR]

The figure slightly tilts his head, looking at you for a brief moment before his eyes dart down towards your equipment, and he offers a warm smile before instantly changing to a frown. He begins speaking in a warm, melodic voice that reminds you of a wizened and wise grandfather.

Stop, please. You are new.

Don't step on the yellow runes. The resonance is... brittle today, and you are heavy.

No, no, three and a half—the displacement is negligible, but the boots are muddy.

Why are you vibrating? Oh, it’s your heartbeat. Far too fast. Slow it down, please.

There is food in the kitchen to your left.

Without any other explanation, he returns to the tome he was reading on the stand next to him, and small golden runes begin to move around it in odd, mesmerizing patterns.

Speaking with Sigil

Sigil views the world very differently from others, seeing it as a grand machine where each detail is observable, capable of being recorded, understood, and analyzed. He is often hyper-focused on a topic, at least until he gets distracted, which happens several times within a minute. He is also highly sensitive to sensory inputs, and slight changes in his surroundings are distressing and unwelcome. He doesn't look at faces; he examines belts, boots, or the magical aura around a player's head. When stressed, he speaks in highly informative yet wildly confusing bursts or in incredibly short, clipped sentences.

If any character makes a successful [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check, they will immediately see that Sigil is tightly controlling his magical aura, but it is immense. The character will see a glowing aura surround him for a few moments as it flickers and waves around him like a storm. His aura is neither damaging nor blinding, and it feels warm without affecting the overall temperature.

The party can ask Sigil any number of questions; some of the most likely are listed below in the Q&A sections. They can continue this conversation for as long as they wish, during which time he provides some additional information:

  • He is not all that fond of leaving the safety of his lodge, where he has many powerful wards and spells laid out meticulously to protect him from any dangers, although he does sometimes visit his good friend@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.CBreAnaMxOim355U]{Steelsong}.

  • He loves books and research above all other topics, and he can absorb boundless amounts of information. The issue is making sense of the smallest details, and he will candidly admit that he loses track of all kinds of things quite often.

  • He doesnt like to be touched, and if anyone gets too close to him, he might physically flinch or create a small magical hand to gently push them back to a "correct" standing distance.

Clerics or Followers of Sigil

If anyone in the party is a follower or even a cleric of Sigil, he stops and blinks rapidly after the initial greeting. His tone becomes even more relaxed, and he smiles broadly.

"Oh! Oh, it's you! I recognize those arms! Your aura is... noisier than I remember. More 'adventurous.' It’s messy. But your presence is.. calming. I hope you are doing… well?

Sigil will then attempt to ask his follower about their scholarly studies and what new information they have to share. If the party members launch into detail, Sigil will become almost giddy, and a fresh book will appear out of the air, and he will begin scribbling constantly. He will constantly interrupt, asking for more details about small, insignificant elements such as what color the sky was during the battle, or how the weapon smelled.

Note: While Sigil is a Shard God and wields a considerable amount of magical power, he is not someone who can solve the party's problems with a wave of his hand. Both because he doesn't want to get involved and because he is actually quite cowardly. He is happy to answer questions, but his answers often need some deciphering.

Are you a god?

Yes, yes, a Shard God to be precise, or at least that's what you all call us. I prefer Ascendant God as it's more accurate. Oh, and godhood is a misleading metric of power before you ask. A storm is powerful, but it cannot thread a needle. Incidentally, you will likely be pleased to know that you are asking an interesting question.

Don't you have a magical library?

No.

There is a long pause as he continues reading his book before twitching slightly, as if realizing he was being too blunt.

Ah! I mean, yes, but it is currently closed because I have some delicate instruments inside that I don't want disturbed. The gate there would lead you in. Please come back again later; the door will be open, I'm sure.

Why are you helping these refugees?

Because the alternative is distressing… I may not be able to help with battles, fighting, and the like. I find that kind of thing quite frightening, but allowing anyone to be extinguished by bandits or hunger is... wrong. If I have the capacity to help the people of the Plateau during this crisis, I will do so. Besides, the children brought me a flower yesterday. It had exactly five petals. Perfect symmetry.

The Ad-Hoc Kitchen.name: The Ad-Hoc Kitchen
The Ad-Hoc Kitchen.text:
A small kitchen near the front entrance of the lodge looks as if it has been the scene of a great feast, though a closer look at the food reveals that the food is mostly small items that carry well on the road - pieces of fruit, hand held sandwiches, and bundles of supplies that refugees can take with them as they go.

There is little of interest in this room apart from some leftover food on the counters and tables. If the party is lacking rations or supplies, they can gather 3 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagRations0000]{Rations}. @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rations000000000]

The Mote Chase.name: The Mote Chase
The Mote Chase.text:
As you step outside the lodge, you can see several Light Motes, floating around nearby, weaving between tents, hovering over the campfires, fluttering over the refugees' heads. For the most part, no one seems to be reacting to them, and some of the refugees bat them away with free hands as if they are bothersome flies.

Chasing the Light Motes

The newly spawned Light Motes x6 are not aggressive towards the party, Lyla, or any of the refugees. Before setting off, Lyla will say the following:

You don't need to hurt them if you don't want to! Just try to soothe them, and they will disappear!

Initiative begins, and Lyla joins the chase to disperse the motes. She will not actively harm them and instead attempts to use the peaceful approach detailed below.

  • The Aggressive Approach: A character can make a melee or ranged spell attack against the mote. On a hit, the motes only have 1 hp, and you don't need to roll damage 3 health. They simply "shatter" into harmless light.

  • The Peaceful Approach: A character can attempt an [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] or [[/skill animalhandling 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check to calm the mote. On a success, they trill with a soft tune and disappear. On a failure,they flash and teleport 60 feet in a random direction use their @UUID[Actor.dohbTGwgummsG9g7.Item.luminousTransit0] to reposition to a different location . Including over the water of the lake nearby… it's recommended that you place them in the most difficult places for the party to reach.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the Chamber of Agaseros depicts a three-level subterranean sprawl that serves as the scenery for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1]{The Expedition Challenge} quest event known as [[/eventState anachraenum1Gauntlet]].

  • This map depicts three distinct sections of the area: the @UUID[Scene.emberChamberAga3]{Entrance Level}, the @UUID[Scene.emberChamberAgas]{Main Level}, and the @UUID[Scene.emberChamberAga2]{Reservoir Level}.

  • There is a single method of entry: a main gate located south of the @UUID[.OX99OJy9EkqeJkcw]{Chamber Foyer}, off the edge of the map. The party begins the encounter in the foyer.

  • Additional information about the Archive's arcane locks and the rotating mirrors that control them are located in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.tEZnHQOPALaXewgH]{Gameplay Details} section of this walkthrough.

Since the Chamber of Agaseros is a smaller location within the mile-wide hex that comprises the Ordani district of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0]{All-Fable Keep}, the Gazetteer Entry below contains information about the neighborhood as a whole.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0 inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Illumination

The Chamber of Agaseros has a number of light sources throughout its three floors. The primary sources of light are Arcane Lamps on many of the walls. These lights cast 40 feet of dim purple light and 10 feet of bright light.

The chamber also holds floating light sources that wander the larger spaces of the rooms and can be found across all three floors. These floating lights are illusory in nature as they can pass through the Arcane Barriers and doors. The Floating Arcane Lights cast 20 feet of dim light and 10 feet of bright light.

On the first floor, within the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.73Me8QItEoDdn7Hd]{Skull Spider Lair}, there are many green ceremonial candles. These cast 2 feet of dim light and 0.2 feet of flickering bright green light.

In addition, several areas emit light sources due to various passive effects. These areas include the acid pits, which cast 15 feet of dim light and 10 feet of bright light. Meri's Garden has a few scattered red lights that vary in intensity and brightness. The glowing lava light in the steam room cast 15 feet of dim light and no bright light, and the coals cast 5 feet of dim light and 3.4 of bright light.

Terrain

The Chamber can repair itself and also move its various rooms around, like the internal mechanics of a great clock. These changes occur over many years, so it will not look any different if the players attempt to access it again. However, for the Expedition Challenge, the Chamber has been specifically configured to challenge new members of the Anacharenum. This means that floors, walls, and any other surface are typically smooth, clean, and repaired, and only a few loose debris items like pebbles, dust, and webs can be found.

Only @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.P8Z0iEJY9ynLiJEW]{Meri's Garden} is treated as difficult terrain and even the water within the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Main Reservoir} at the bottom of the chamber is usually calm and unmoving.

Elevation

The ceilings of the Chamber of Agaseroes are quite tall, at nearly 30 feet. This is true across the Chamber except within the Central Column Room, which has a height of 120 feet. This means that between the levels, there is a height of 40 feet.

Across all three floors, there are parts of the room that dip down into lower sections by 10 feet, and each one is filled with various substances or unique floor types. These include:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.73Me8QItEoDdn7Hd]{Skull Spider Lair}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.P8Z0iEJY9ynLiJEW]{Meri's Garden}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.t8Gjl8S1JLuQ3YMD]{Steam Room}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.QEjec5lQgvAeliDe]{Acid Challenge}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.GVwJOrx4XFTcyhTa]{Acid Foyer}

Additional Gameplay

Fulgurite Blades

Once they reach the chamber that holds the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.51O9wkvqzzHQ32wk]{Arcane Engine}, the characters will encounter the @UUID[Actor.emberFulgrBlades]{Fulgurite Blades}, a rival party of adventurers who are also undertaking the Expedition Challenge.

The party may or may not have previously encountered the Fulgurite Blades as part of the [[/eventState overMoonCurious]] event during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon} Chapter 1 side quest.

The Fulgurite Blades are currently stuck trying to repair the enchanted mechanism as part of the challenge, and further details on the confrontation between these two parties can be found in the Arcane Engine room description.

Sealed Runic Doors

All the Runic Doors in the Chamber are made of nearly 2 feet of solid bronze and operate through a combination of magic and machinery. None of them can be opened without finding the corresponding color switch, which requires the party to traverse the room's challenges in the correct order.

Forcing the doors open in any way is not possible and would require high-level dispelling magic as they are incredibly resistant to physical force and magical attacks, including spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplHeatMetal0]{Heat Metal} which has no effect on the thick bronze.

Main Reservoir.name: Main Reservoir
Main Reservoir.text:
As you descend the narrow, worn stairs, the air grows noticeably cooler, and you can hear the faint rippling sounds of water lapping against the stone walls. Standing on a small platform, a vast reservoir of water surrounds you in the gloom. The dim light from distant lamps casts shadows across the room, revealing the expansive water that seems calm and unmoving at first glance. As you look around, you notice several stone platforms jutting out across the water, all covered with a multitude of pipes, ranging from small to average size, and even one so thick someone could stand on it. You also see several large arcane runes glowing faintly at the edges of the outer stone platforms.

Empty Room?

The final boss encounter with the six heads of the @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU]{Vespian Hydral} does not happen until they have completed the last challenge in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.t8Gjl8S1JLuQ3YMD]{Steam Room} on the second floor and touched the Ornate Pedestal. Once this occurs, the Hydral is ready to attack, and the encounter in this room can begin. However, the Hydral only attacks once the entire party is standing on the central column in the middle of the reservoir at the bottom of the column, at which point it immediately attacks and combat starts.

A Possible Enclosure

Characters who attempt to study the empty reservoir before combat begins must succeed on a [[/check inv 18]] check. If they have [[/knowledge monsters]], they have @Advantage[2] on this check. If successful, they can deduce that this chamber may currently host some creature, or may have done so in the past.

The Hydral's Ambush

As soon as initiative is rolled, the following actors appear within the scene.

  • 6x @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU]{Vespian Hydral}

These actors are arrayed around the central platform and the bottom of the column. Their movement and positioning throughout the following encounter are covered under their tactics below. None of the individual heads of the Hydral can move onto the platform where the party stands or outside the reservoir due to their arcane nature.

@Embed[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU]

Vespian Hydral Tactics

The @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU]{Vespian Hydral} fights as a single creature, using its many @UUID[Actor.AoUvCijym6p374Qt]{heads} to menace the area it occupies. It acts on one initiative count, and all of its heads share actions, reactions, and resources. The Hydral’s main body lurks near the central column, repositioning its active heads to control nearby platforms, walkways, and swimmers.

The Hydral positions its heads to threaten as many adventurers as possible. It uses @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU.Item.eW51XST21x8IuTSM]{Arcane Bite} on any creature that moves within reach of an active head, and constantly shifts head positions to deny enemies a safe approach. When foes cluster or line up on narrow terrain, it unleashes @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU.Item.ZjoOhwCLAalMTYGg]{Steam Breath }to catch as many as possible—especially if it can knock them into hazards or off precarious ledges.

If a creature engages the Hydral in the water or strays too close to an active head, the Hydral may use @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU.Item.7FsgTbATDfMzngf7]{Whirlpool} to grapple and pin that target. As its heads are incapacitated, the Hydral loses flexibility and offensive power, so it spreads its remaining heads to maximize control of the chamber.

Water Reservoir

Characters thrown off the central platform and into the water discover that the water appears calm, but it has a strong underwater current just under the surface. At the start of each of the characters' turns while in the water, they must make a [[/save str 12]] to resist being pulled into the current. On a failure, they are pulled 15 feet towards the center of the reservoir and back towards the central column.

After the Vespian Hydral reaches zero hit points with its @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU.Item.kmc2805VhJrDgeZ2]{Shared Health}, the creature is defeated, and all the remaining heads disappear.

Area Map Complete

Once the Vespian Hydral has been defeated, the party can now refer back to the quest event @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.qeERNVDf7uz1QloT]{The Wayfinder's Gauntlet} for further details and rewards.

The party can leave the Chamber at this point, or they can attempt to unlock the secret boss @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.yfDYJAVs5OGrA4Kn]{Matrix of Agaseros}.

Reservoir Control Room.name: Reservoir Control Room
Reservoir Control Room.text:
The walls of this small room are covered with large bronze pipes sprawling across dark, ancient stone, slick with moisture and adorned with intricate carvings of flowing water. In the middle of the room is a large square ring of arcane runes embedded into the stone floor, glowing with a vibrant purple hue, and within the center is a large basin of crystal-clear water.

Secret Optional Route

This room is currently inaccessible in Early Access. Its contents will become a secret route that is unlocked by finding and activating hidden mechanisms in the chamber, discovered in various rooms throughout the area map.

Barrier Control Room.name: Barrier Control Room
Barrier Control Room.text:
Within this small room, more of the large bronze pies line the walls, but the primary focus seems to be a strange central console that dominates the space, covered in dials and levers, each meticulously covered in tiny runes and symbols.

Secret Optional Route

This room is currently inaccessible in Early Access. Its contents will become a secret route that is unlocked by finding and activating hidden mechanisms in the chamber, discovered in various rooms throughout the area map.

Fossil Display.name: Fossil Display
Fossil Display.text:
This small room appears to be a display chamber, with a large fossil skeleton of a long-dead hunting creature displayed directly across from the doorway. Several small glass cases line the walls to the left and right, but they seem to be empty.

An Empty Display

Those who further search the room with a successful [[/check inv 16]] notice that one of the cases has a @UUID[Item.y6lXtFPEDoPA71c6]{Big Spinel} lying in the corner.

Antechamber.name: Antechamber
Antechamber.text:
This small antechamber appears to be empty except for a small desk against the far wall. Made of dark wood, it is covered in notes and pieces of loose paper. To the left and right, two thick bronze doors are set into the walls. Each seems to be missing any gems or complicated mechanisms for unlocking them, and they seem to match the entrance door, able to be opened with a simple touch.

Another Lonely Desk
