The desk in this room contains several notes that detail further arcane studies and experimentations by Agaseros. Anyone who chooses to search the desk discovers a curious scrap: @UUID[Item.M5JsrbSI8tqM2NJF]{Journal of Agaseros: Page 6}.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check arcana 15]] check while studying the Journal is able to reveal the following:

  • Agaseros was intensely interested in creating arcane machines that could outlive him.

  • He attempted various methods to achieve his goals and traveled across the world to investigate strange arcane phenomena.

  • Characters with [[/attunement signara]] or [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2].

Rare Book Collection.name: Rare Book Collection
Rare Book Collection.text:
As you enter the small room, you see that the walls are lined with dark oak shelves, sagging slightly under the weight of countless books and scrolls. In the center of the room, five rare books rest on ornate stands. Each book appears to be a masterpiece in its own right, bound in luxurious or rare materials.

A Dangerous Collection

Within the room lies a number of rare books, the challenge within is to refrain from touching any of them, and instead the party needs to identify where all of the books came from in Ember. Speaking the answer out loud is enough to solve the puzzle.

Bestiary of Jurin

This book sits upon the stand to the north-west.

The cover is a deep jungle green, crafted from smooth leather that feels supple to the touch. Embossed across the front is an intricate design of intertwining vines and leaves. Large deep claw marks run across the book's length and have cut deep enough to rip out some of the paper inside.

The answer is Leviathans, or Jurin. Anyone with [[/knowledge leviathans]] recognizes that book immediately, otherwise, a successful [[/check nature 14]] check reveals the answer.

The Chained Sorrows

This book sits upon the stand to the west.

The cover of this book is dark, weathered, and worn. It is covered with locked chain links that prevent it from being opened. Under the chains, in the center of the cover, a striking image of a large, singular, glowing red eye.

The Abyss, or the Red Eye. Anyone with [[/knowledge abyssals]] recognizes that book immediately, otherwise, a successful [[/check arcana 14]] check reveals the answer.

Chronicles of the Lost

This book sits upon the stand to the south-west.

The cover of this book is midnight blue, resembling a star-filled night sky. The edges are painted with ancient runic symbols that seem to flash and sparkle like stars.

The answer is Shent, or Giants. Anyone with [[/knowledge shent]] recognizes that book immediately, otherwise, a successful [[/check history 14]] check reveals the answer.

Codex of Luxarum Myths

This book sits upon the stand to the south-east.

This large tome appears to be bound in luminous, shimmering gold that attracts the eye from any angle. The front cover is decorated with celestial motifs, and a large spear is easily visible on the front, shining like the sun itself.

The Answer is Luxarum, or Celestials. Anyone with [[/knowledge celestials]] recognizes that book immediately, otherwise, a successful [[/check religion 14]] check reveals the answer.

Compendium of the Watcher

This book sits upon the stand to the north-east.

This book seems to be strangely alive, featuring a stark black and red cover, textured to resemble worn, ancient stone. Across its cover are several small green eyes that seem to watch anyone as they approach.

The answer is the Watcher, or Spiders. Anyone with [[/knowledge subterranea]] recognizes that book immediately, otherwise, a successful [[/check nature 14]] check reveals the answer.

Sealed Collection

The rare books within the room cannot be opened, nor can they be removed from their stands. This is because a very powerful ward lies upon them. If anyone attempts to touch, remove or open one of the books, read the following:

As you try to touch the book, a faint sigh, like wind, can be heard for the briefest moment before a loud crack explodes around your hand, and red flashing lines appear over the cover in a shield.

The character suffers [[/damage 2d6 lightning]] damage from the magical shield, akin to a magical burn, and cannot avoid the damage in any way.

Anyone who wishes to investigate the books can learn the following:

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} or rolls a [[/check arcana 18]], or if a character has [[/knowledge rituals]], they recognize the wards cast over the books is perhaps some of the more intense and powerful you have come across in the chamber so far and it would be nearly impossible to remove it without high level dispelling magic.

Blue Pedestal

Completing the challenge here reveals a pedestal, which appears from nothing in the center of the room.

Interactivity

A player character can interact with the blue pedestal without investigating it. Doing so unlocks the two Blue Runic Doors on the 1st floor.

Blue Runic Pedestal

The pedestal in this room is not trapped, nor is it a complicated device. It merely unlocks any blue door within the Chamber, and interacting with the gem on its surface is enough to unlock the door. It's likely the party may find this suspicious, however, so there are a few clues on the pedestal to hint at its benign nature.

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 13]], they discover that the pedestal is connected by a thin magical thread to somewhere else in the chamber.

  • Anyone attempting to investigate the pedestal cannot find any traps or anything suspicious, but if someone rolls a successful [[/check inv 18]], they discover that the pedestal is not dangerous, and placing their hand on the gem is safe.

  • Anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] can somewhat read the runes, and they are runes of unlocking rather than anything dangerous.

Disturbed Library.name: Disturbed Library
Disturbed Library.text:
Stepping through the door, you find a ruined library that seems to have been overturned and attacked by some sort of creature, or perhaps by an explosion or whirlwind that recently tore through the room. The shelves appear to be leaning precariously forward in places, their wood cracked and splintered. The floor is littered with crumbling books and pages, some torn or ripped apart.

Life finds a way

Once the party enters the room by only a few steps, they are ambushed by the six @UUID[Actor.DchsMYAWBOV6NrCm]{Animated Rune Tome}'s that lie hidden in the room.

@Embed[Actor.DchsMYAWBOV6NrCm]

Animated Rune Tome Tactics

As combat begins, add only one or two tomes to the combat tracker and reveal them to attack the party. As combat continues, keep adding tomes in between player turns until all six of the tomes have been revealed.

The tomes are mindless, aggressive, and simple, but are able to cast spells from thier pages.

  • They will attmept to cast @UUID[Actor.DchsMYAWBOV6NrCm.Item.PSaVtZ6KS9CS7vZw]{Ray of Enfeeblement} at the start of the combat at each party member.

  • They will also attempt to cast @UUID[Actor.DchsMYAWBOV6NrCm.Item.eXPmnAWu83AY8ouJ]{Darkness} or @UUID[Actor.DchsMYAWBOV6NrCm.Item.9B3xzMyTx5SA3l7o]{Fog Cloud} around themselves to prevent them from being targeted by the party.

  • Their main attacks will be @UUID[Actor.DchsMYAWBOV6NrCm.Item.y6tHGL71IJTz3fe4]{Ray of Frost} which they can cast as if they are 5th level and the ray deals 2d8 damage instead.

The books have no concept of self-preservation and will not attempt to flee once injured, but if engaged in melee, they will use @UUID[Actor.DchsMYAWBOV6NrCm.Item.Hgg1HT5HCk5j4iVw]{Blink} to teleport elsewhere in the room. Once a book is defeated, it reverts to an intact book form that is badly damaged, and investigating reveals nothing of value.

A Lost Library

Within the room are many ruined books and notes, but nothing much that the party can uncover or find useful.

  • However, anyone who chooses to rummage through the papers and designs comes across @UUID[Item.yuHNL4jw00dFqaR2]{Journal of Agaseros: Page 8}.

Skull Spider Lair.name: Skull Spider Lair
Skull Spider Lair.text:
This dim chamber is suffused with a surreal, otherworldly light that emanates from hundreds of black candles that burn with a soft green flame. A mighty bronze grate covers a deep basin at the center of the chamber, and the entire room is covered in thick webs and large, silky cocoons. As disconcerting as this scene might be, something even more alarming emerges from the shadows at the northern end of the room …

@Embed[Actor.9VIz2g2agKz7Bl3T]

The spider in this room is an ancient creature that was captured hundreds of years ago and trapped in the chamber, but it eventually became accustomed to its new life and became friends with the mage Agaseros.

With a series of soft, almost husky clicks and taps of its mouth pincers, the creature begins to speak in a raspy, low voice.

What an unexpected surprise.. tik tik.. mortals have found my little home again. What can I do for you then.. tik tik..

Talking with Ix'erax

The party can converse with Ix'erax, during which time she provides additional information:

  • Ix'erax is a Giant Skull Spider, and she calls herself a Child of the Watcher. She reveals that all spiders are children of the Watcher. She doesnt, however, comment on who exactly the Watcher is other than her mother and Goddess.

  • She has been in the Chamber for 241 years, 7 months, and 14 days. She remembers clearly the day she was captured and how much rage, anger, and fear she felt for being humiliated in such a way.

  • These days, she very much enjoys her life in the chamber and spends much of her time using her magic to scry on Ordain and record events in her vast memory. She makes it clear that she can see many events unfolding in the city above and is deeply fascinated by the passage of time and the world.

If the party asks about the mage Agaseros, Ix'erax seems to grow quiet for a moment.

He was... one of a kind... tik tik... You mortals are often short-sighted and filled with immediate wants and needs. He was far wiser and had such skill with arcane magic. He was also kind, and even though I hated him deeply at first for capturing me, over time, we came to understand each other. I taught him many secrets, and he shared his own knowledge with me.

If asked about Skull Spiders, Ix'erax will slowly respond with the following information

My kind, or at least my direct kind of spiders, are typically known for their voracious hunger. We tend to be driven by our hunger above all other concerns. I would suggest… that if you ever meet another one of my kind, you run… tik tik…

If the party asks for her help or information on subjects directly related to their ongoing quests, Ix'erax will shudder for a moment and begin to laugh.

I am a watcher, not someone who gets involved in the affairs of mortals. I see no reason for me to help you other than to say.. be wary of the dark.

Ix'erax's Motives

A successful [[/skill insight 14]] check suggests that Ix'erax is completely friendly and unconcerned by the presence of the party. She is a wise character and clearly knows a lot about the world and even recent events in Ordain, but she has no intention of sharing any secrets and comes off as slightly smug and self-assured.

  • Result of 20+: Ix'erax believes the party is important somehow, and her eyes and tone give away more than her words, and she is watching them with some interest.

Any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} spell on Ix'erax receives nothing back but a vast void of nothing.

Now now, none of that.. tik.. tik..

Making Accusations

If the party accuses Ix'erax of being an agent of evil dark powers or a servant of the Abyss, she will not respond immediately and instead simply reveal that she is connected to the Abyss and monsters in the dark but not evil, and has little interest in the destruction of some fascinating world.

If the party asks about the Abyss directly.

I lament that you know that term. But it is too late now. It is not the place you believe it to be. These things are always far more complex when you look at them closely. For most, it is a realm of utter evil, and it is true that it has brought many powerful beings low. But I would not cement your minds on its morality just yet.

Fighting Ix'erax

Combat with Ix'erax is not the intended outcome of this event, as Ix'erax does not instigate such conflict and has no intention of seriously fighting the party.

It is not unlikely, however, that the mere presence of Ix'erax, her persona, comments, and appearance will compel the party to attack her as obviously evil or malicious.

Ix'erax Tactics

Combat with @UUID[Actor.9VIz2g2agKz7Bl3T]{ Ix'erax} will be short, as the party will have only 2 rounds to attack her. During this time Ix'erax will defend herself and she tries not to attack the party. In fact, she will do her best to remove herself from the fight by using her @UUID[Actor.9VIz2g2agKz7Bl3T.Item.H3fRdyUdlHCcubw6]{Spider Climb} ability to climb towards the ceiling.

After 2 rounds of combat, unless the party has somehow killed her during this time, she will use her@UUID[Actor.9VIz2g2agKz7Bl3T.Item.nStVV4sNaWgaqAhW]{Dark Doorway} to teleport away from the encounter.

It's possible that the party can kill Ix'erax during these two rounds, and should this happen, she will not leave behind any treasures or loot, nor will she appear again.

Acid Foyer.name: Acid Foyer
Acid Foyer.text:
As you step into the small, dimly lit room, your senses are immediately assaulted by a pungent, acrid scent that hangs thick in the air. In the center of the space, a pit of glowing green acid bubbles ominously below a grate that only seems to cover most of the pit. Some worrying gaps on either side are large enough for something or someone to fall into the acid itself. Floating above the grate is a small construct that seems familiar.

Acid Basin

The pit in this room is 15 feet deep, but 5 feet of its depth contains a violent, intensely glowing green acid, so it appears to be 10 feet deep from above.

Any character who falls into the pit suffers [[/damage 3d10 acid]] damage. The acid also counts as difficult terrain if anyone tries to swim or move through it. Characters who find themselves within the pit during combat take an additional [[/damage 3d10 acid]] damage each turn they stay in the acid.

Characters can attempt to climb out of the pit with a [[/check acr 13]] check. If they fail a check outside of combat, they slip back into the acid and take a further [[/damage 3d10 acid]] damage for each attempt.

A strange Introduction

The small single Aetherial in this room is set with a stay command. It does not attack anyone who enters the room. However, when the party enters the room itself, read the following:

The small construct doesn’t seem to respond to your movements for a few moments, but with a small ping, the device begins emitting a message in a shrill little voice.

Welcome. Hello!
Please continue through the chamber at your own pace. Unlock each door by completing room challenges in order!
… bzz.. Thank you!

@Embed[Actor.Lw8HeAY64cjHnuQq]

An Empty Room

The Aetherial will continue to hover in the room, and has little interest in the party. It cannot be talked to and does not react to anything the party attempts.

  • A successful [[/check arc 15]] or anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] determines that these strange little constructs have been created by a highly competent and powerful arcane mage, likely the aformented mage Agaseros with a level of technology approaching the Aedir but still somewhat unrefined.

Aetherial Tactics

If the party decides that the little construct has to be destroyed for some reason, it will react to defend itself. Once combat begins, it will not move from its position but will fire its@UUID[Actor.Lw8HeAY64cjHnuQq.Item.OnYsxWrpQdSjwSy8]{Laser} at whoever attacked it first.

The creature is basically mindless and has no self-preservation instincts. It will stay where it was stationed until it is destroyed.

Northern Alcove.name: Northern Alcove
Northern Alcove.text:
This small antechamber is bereft of details and is mostly empty, with a single lamp glowing on the northern wall and two thin hallways flanking the lamp that continue onward.

Trap Signaling

Any character that moves through the space and attempts to pass through the two small hallways, either side of the lamp, will encounter pressure plates of bronze inset into the floor. Anyone rushing blindly ahead will step onto the plates and hear a small "click," but nothing happens.

  • With a [[/skill prc 15 passive]] or successful [[/skill prc 15]] check within the alcove, a character will notice the plates ahead of time.

  • Investigating the plates with a successful [[/check inv 14]] or anyone with [[/knowledge machines]] discovers that the plates are actually not connected to anything.

Acid Challenge.name: Acid Challenge
Acid Challenge.text:
The stench coming from the green glowing room ahead is as close to a putrid sulfur mixed with burning dead bodies as you could imagine, and the intense smell begins to burn your eyes and nose before you even enter the room itself. The centerpiece of the room is a massive pool of bubbling acid, its surface shimmering with a sickly green hue. The acid churns and bubbles ominously, sending up occasional wisps of thick gas into the surrounding air.

Surrounding the pool are several platforms made of thick bronze grates and gears elevated above the acid by thick chain wire, strung taut across the gaps and fixed to the ceiling high above.

Gem of Curiosity

Under and above the central bronze platform is a circular mechanism that surrounds four bronze arms that carefully hold a large purple gemstone. The colour of the stone is almost completely washed away by the glow coming from the acid, but it remains a tempting target.

Investigating the gem with a [[/check inv 18]] check reveals that there is a mechanism under the gem linked to the bronze arms and that triggering something unknown. Only a successful [[/check slt 20]] can safely remove the gem without triggering the trap.

If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 17]], they discover that the gemstone is linked to hidden arcane runes that are hidden upon the walls. The runes are not decipherable, but anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] knows that the runes are likely summoning magic.

Acid Basin

The pit in this room is 15 feet deep, but 5 feet of its depth contains a violent, intensely glowing green acid, so it appears to be 10 feet deep from above.

Any character who falls into the pit suffers [[/damage 3d10 acid]] damage. The acid also counts as difficult terrain if anyone tries to swim or move through it. Characters who find themselves within the pit during combat take an additional [[/damage 3d10 acid]] damage each turn they stay in the acid.

Characters can attempt to climb out of the pit with a [[/check acr 13]] check. If they fail a check outside of combat, they slip back into the acid and take a further [[/damage 3d10 acid]] damage for each attempt.

Shades of Agaseros

The Shades of Agageros in the room do not technically exist until the party attempts to remove the gem from the central platform. If they decide not to mess with the gem, then the Shades do not appear at all.

@Embed[Actor.MNWRuR4oQQP7EUgD]

Interactivity

During the fight, the Shades can attempt to unpin the wires holding the four platforms along the walls of the Acid Challenge room. This is controlled by the GM during combat, one per round by rolling a public [[/roll 1d20]] and on the result of a 15+ reading the following:

One of the Shades seems to flick the wrist of one of its arms at the wires holding the platforms up. With a loud, cracking sound or metal snapping and shearing, the wire breaks free and the platform collapses into the acid with a heavy splash.

Anyone on the platform that is falling can roll a [[/check acr 16]] to jump out of the way and try to land on another platform or reach one of the edges. You can choose a platform at random, or specifically choose to target the platforms holding the PC's.

Shades of Agaseros Tactics

The Shades are effectively manifestations of the Chamber itself, and they do have a simple kind of intelligence. This means that during combat they recognize that the party members are here to be tested, and killing them is not part of the test (at least most of the time).

Their simple intelligence allows them to target weaker members of the group; however, such as the ones healing or when casting spells, they might target the characters with low resistance ability scores like wisdom. In this combat encounter, they use @UUID[Actor.MNWRuR4oQQP7EUgD.Item.mkteIUTW1B27Icqy]{Arcane Beam} the most and try to move around the room, floating above the acid.

If they are in melee range with a party members, the Shade will move away regardless of attacks of opportunity. Once a Shade is defeated, it disappears and does not leave a body to investigate or study.

Trap Maze.name: Trap Maze
Trap Maze.text:
Ahead of you is a narrow and dimly lit passage that seems to swallow the light. The smooth stone walls seem to close in around you, and the path ahead twists and turns without end.

The maze within the chamber is fairly simple, with several traps laid throughout to ambush the unwary. The party will have to move carefully around each corner to reach the other side safely.

Interactivity

During the exploration of the maze, the party will encounter two kinds of traps.

  • Bronze pressure plates that activate darts set into the walls

  • Thin, taunt wire across corners that activate blade traps in the walls.

Dart Trap

The pressure plates are scattered throughout the maze, mostly in the longer sections of the hallways.

A character who succeeds on a [[/skill prc 14]] check who is close enough to see the pressure plate clearly can notice it on the floor ahead. The small opening for the darts on the ends of the hallways cannot be seen.

  • The plate can be disarmed with a successful use of [[/skill dex 13]] Thieves' Tools.

The Dart Trap is triggered when 10 or more pounds of weight are applied to the pressure plate. When the trap is triggered, several darts fly across the hallways from the nearby wall.

  • Any character who is within the area of the trap immediately or at the start of a subsequent turn must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 18]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] damage or half damage on a successful save. Anyone who fails the check gains the &Reference[poisoned] for [[/roll 1d4]] minutes

Spinning Blades Trap

The wires that activate these traps are scattered throughout the maze, across various corners.

A character with a [[/check prc 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill prc 16]] check who is close enough to clearly see the wires can notice them and the thin wall seams from which the spinning blades would issue.

  • The wire can be disarmed with a successful use of [[/skill dex 16]] Thieves' Tools.

The wire is broken when 3 or more pounds of weight are applied across it. When the trap is triggered, several whirling blades erupt from the nearby wall directly on top of the corner section.

  • Any character who is within the area of the trap immediately or at the start of a subsequent turn must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw or take [[/damage 2d6 slashing]] damage or half damage on a successful save.

Meri's Garden.name: Meri's Garden
Meri's Garden.text:
Before you even round the corner, you can start to smell a strange, almost otherworldly scent wafting through the air. As you step into the open, you're stunned to discover a vibrant burst of plants deep within the otherwise mysterious stone walls of the chamber. Strange red plants tower above you; their shapes are odd, extreme, and flutter as if being affected by a wind you cannot feel. Some have luminescent petals that pulse gently, while others have tendrils reaching out as if to playfully tease you. The ground is a tapestry of soft moss, fallen red leaves, and dark, hard roots.

This is the garden of the strange Fae entity known as Meri, who was once a friend and advisor of sorts to the mage Agaseros. Once the party steps out into the garden, read the following:

One of the large flower bulbs begins opening its big red petals, and a soft, glowing figure emerges, stretching its little arms with a loud yawn. It then turns and gasps softly as it sees you.

More visitors! Oh, it's so lively here again recently! What fun!

The figure speaks in a voice similar to a small child's, with a touch of utter excitement, and you see it fluttering its little flower wings as if overwhelmed with happiness.

My name is Meri! I'm from Primordis and... Oh! Yes, that's right! I'm supposed to challenge you. Hmm, let me see... Oh, yes! Here are the rules: you must find the real me within the garden to unlock the door over there. I'll give you a hint: I'm one of the flowers! You have as much time as you like, of course, but wrong answers are punished! Good luck!

With a flash of mist, magical dust, and pollen, the little creature vanishes, leaving you wondering if you perhaps imagined the last few moments. Then, you hear a soft giggle coming from somewhere in the garden in front of you.

@Embed[Actor.XNywYg2moKGYYgqB]

Interactivity

During the exploration of the garden, there are seven plants that could be Meri. The party can walk up to each one and try to decide which one is Meri by interacting with it. However, six of the flowers are traps and will burst into pollen dust and create a magical effect. Meri herself is actually hidden in the far north-western corner.

Suspicious Flowers

As the players step into the garden, another soft giggle echoes around them, and it's clear that Meri is somewhere nearby, watching and waiting to test the party's wits.

The party can attempt several different methods to locate Meri by trying to figure out which flower is her. When they approach a suspicious-looking flower, they can investigate to see if it is the real Meri.

  • With a successful [[/check inv 17]] check, on a suspicious flower, a character realizes that it is glowing and fluttering, but it's not giggling or twitching and therefore likely not the real Meri.

  • Anyone with [[/knowledge fey]] can roll a [[/check nature 14]] and upon success, realizes that the flower in front of you is not strange enough to be Meri.

  • With a successful [[/check arcana 17]] check on a suspicious flower, will reveal that the magic around it is mostly some kind of Fae illusion designed to make it look more suspicious and magical than it really is.

Flower Trap

Anyone who interacts with a suspicious flower that is not Meri, activates a trap instead as the flower bursts into magical pollen.

Each creature within 10 feet must make a [[/save con 14]] Constitution saving throw. anyone that fails takes [[/damage 3d6 poison]] and is gains the &Reference[poisoned] condition until the end of its next turn.

In addition, each player within a 10-foot radius must also make a [[/save wis 14]] saving throw. If they fail, that player is charmed, believing that the flowers and garden around them are the most beautiful thing they have ever seen. They are compelled to defend it, and will target and ally, or party members closest to them, and attack them with a single melee action before snapping out of their confusion.

A Quick Exit

Once the party finds Meri among the other suscipisus flowers she appears back in her normal form and you can read the following:

Well done! That was quick! It's so lovely to have playthings again down here!

Meri then waves her hand, with a loud clang, you hear the door to the south unlock and slide open.

Good luck, playthings! I'm sure we will meet again!

With a sound like a flute being blown, Meri begins floating higher, and little petals start flying around her, then with a pop, she disappears.

Talking or Fighting with Meri

It's not possible within the scope of this event to talk to or fight Meri, at least this is not intended. However, Meri does have a stat block, and the party might try to attack her in some way. If this happens, she will likely simply escape, and the door can then be unlocked. Meri will appear again at a later date!

Maze Alcove.name: Maze Alcove
Maze Alcove.text:
A single light shines ahead within a small square room.

A Lonely Desk

Within the room is a small desk, with pictures, designs, and diagrams of the traps littered across the maze, in addition to several scraps of notes and papers with thoughts and ideas.

  • Anyone who chooses to rummage through the papers and designs comes across @UUID[Item.sMBWeOQnyciMziJ8]{Journal of Agaseros: Page 3}.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check arcana 15]] check or [[/knowledge machines]] can identify the bulk of the designs as prototypes and would not be helpful in disarming the traps in the maze.

    Result of 16+ You manage to find the correct design for the spinning blade traps and are able to more easily disarm them now that you understand how they work. Anyone attempting to disarm the Spinning Blade Traps gains a +2 to their skill check to disarm them.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check inv 15]] check while looking through the designs can spot a few scattered notes on the table, likely used as component pieces in magical works, but they are too faded and mysterious to decipher.

Arcane Engine.name: Arcane Engine
Arcane Engine.text:
As you step through the Blue Runic Door, several aspects of the room strike you at once. The first is that there is a crackling arcane machine at the far end emitting a burst of furious-looking electricity, while the second is that you are not alone in the room, and it would seem the Fulgurite Blades have made it this far into the chamber as well. They have turned to level you with flat stares of surprise.

Inside the room are the four Fulgurite Blades who have made it this far into the chamber but appear to be either stuck on this particular challenge. Once both parties have recovered from the shock of seeing each other here. Read the following:

Sajor holds up a hand as if to stop you from coming any closer.

Okay, this is just weird. What are YOU doing here?

The rest of the blades seem to be on high alert with weapons drawn and are starting intently between Sajor and you.

@Embed[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu]

@Embed[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28]

@Embed[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj]

@Embed[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR]

Fighting the Blades

If the party has previously made rivals of the Blades, then combat between the two groups is all but guaranteed. If the party has the New Rivals Outcome from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.HAkKGbslLkfoFqNO]{Lightning Strikes Twice} then in the next moment, Sajor shouts:

Enough of this! Get them!

Fulgurite Blades Tactics

The fight between the party and the Blades will likely be very intense, as the Blades are an experienced team that has fought many foes together and are capable of an excellent level of teamwork.

Sajor

Is the most deadly of the group and can use a number of high-level spells, including @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu.Item.zsNZCMgQ1sq7051U]{Lightning Bolt} which she will cast on the outset of the fight.

She will also use @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu.Item.DV8VmPuQ1URGPkif]{Haste} on Rorhim in her following turn.

She will use @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu.Item.FMvdJm8DmNN2idUi]{Counterspell} as much as she can stop the player party from casting any high-level spells, as well, and she knows the difference between a low-level and high-level casting.

Rorhim

Will not charge headlong into the fray, instead he will guard his teammates and move to a position to block the players' parties' access to his more vulnerable members. On the other hand, once he is engaged with another melee combatant, he loses his cool slightly and begins attacking with fervour.

Leeph

Leeph will immediately attempt to hide in the shadows of the room with their @UUID[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR.Item.93TfWPoMzBoaneMx]{Cunning Action} ability. They will use @UUID[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR.Item.frhxADwLETnOdKl8]{Sneak Attack} over and over again from the shadows using their hand crossbow to attack anyone that can't seem them.

Kazra

Is the second most powerful team member, and as the cleric, she will focus on staying back and casting @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj.Item.S835C3xtdWDAhpgn]{Cure Wounds} and @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj.Item.45dVk3RJw1bgKtjC]{Healing Word} as much as possible on Rorhim.

If she has a moment and Rorhim seems to be in good shape, she will cast @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj.Item.g25aztkMoSz5OCkg]{Spiritual Weapon} or @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj.Item.QLyF10gZ0Ruu5CZV]{Sacred Flame}.

None of the Blades have so far in the challenge used thier @UUID[Item.jggar2bndAvZthdS]{Frozen Tear} item given to them by Eveis the Star Mage. If the party reduces a member to zero hit points, the tear activates, and they are safely enclosed in a frozen shell until Eveis comes to collect them.

Fulgurite Death

It is not intended that the Blades are killed by the party in this encounter, and the Frozen Tear should protect them from the party. However, it is possible for the party to potentially get around this somehow, if so, make a very large note for the following questline [TBD].

Working with the Blades

If the party has previously made friends of the Blades then comabt here is unlikely. If the party has the Friends with the Blades Outcome from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.HAkKGbslLkfoFqNO]{Lightning Strikes Twice} then in the next moment Sajor Says:

Okay, okay, let's all calm down. We don't need to be dramatic here.

General Information

The Blades will talk with the party about their experiences with the Challenge so far. Sajor will admit begrudingly that they are not stuck on the current challenge and are in fact tired, and running low on steam. Though it is hard for her to admit to the party, she allows them to go ahead of them to the next room while the rest of the family recoup their energy. A successful [[/check insight 14]] check reveals that Sajor is telling the truth and allow she is personally deflated by this result she has made her mind up.

  • Sajor will reveal that the challenge here was very difficult and involved making sure the rods for lighting were aligned, and then they had to charge up the arcane engine on top of the gears with spells to unlock the pedestal nearby.

  • If anyone at the party asks about the Blades wanting to win the challenge. Sajor will say:

    Of course we did, but ultimately, whether we win or just finish the challenge at this stage, it is material that we will still become full members. Which is what I really wanted in the end.

Green Pedestal

Regardless of whether the party defeated the Blades in combat or they were able to talk to them, at the back of the chamber is the already revealed Green Pedestal.

Interactivity

A player character can interact with the Green Pedestal without investigating it. Doing so unlocks the Green Runic Door on the 2nd floor.

Green Runic Pedestal

The pedestal in this room is not trapped, nor is it a complicated device. It merely unlocks the green door within the Chamber, and interacting with the gem on its surface is enough to unlock the door. It's likely the party may find this suspicious, however, so there are a few clues on the pedestal to hint at its benign nature.

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 13]], they discover that the pedestal is connected by a thin magical thread to somewhere else in the chamber.

  • Anyone attempting to investigate the pedestal cannot find any traps or anything suspicious, but if someone rolls a successful [[/check inv 18]], they discover that the pedestal is not dangerous and placing your hand on the gem is safe.

  • Anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] can somewhat read the runes, and they are runes of unlocking rather than anything dangerous.

Banner Room.name: Banner Room
Banner Room.text:
Stepping into the room, you see four thick pillars, each intricately carved with runes and symbols. Hanging around them are several Anachraenum banners featuring the bladed compass symbol, shining with their own inner light. Against one wall, a large stone pedestal commands your attention. Its surface is engraved with more arcane symbols, suggesting it was once a focal point for a display.

Interactivity

A player character can interact with the yellow pedestal without investigating it. Doing so unlocks the Yellow Runic Door behind them.

Yellow Runic Pedestal

The pedestal in this room is not trapped, nor is it a complicated device. It merely unlocks any yellow door within the Chamber, and interacting with the gem on its surface is enough to unlock the door behind the party. It's likely the party may find this suspicious, however, so there are few clues on the pedestal to hint at its benign nature.

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 13]], they discover that the pedestal is connected by a thin magical thread to the door behind them.

  • Anyone attempting to investigate the pedestals cannot find any traps or anything suspicious, but if someone rolls a successful [[/check inv 18]], they discover that the pedestal is not dangerous and placing your hand on the gem is safe.

  • Anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] can somewhat read the runes, and they are runes of unlocking rather than anything dangerous.

Yellow Runic Door

Anyone who walks up to the Bronze door can attempt to investigate it with a variety of different checks.

  • With a [[/skill prc 12 passive]] or successful [[/skill prc 12]] check, it's clear that the surface of the door is smooth, except for banding lines of reinforcing bronze. Similar to some of the other doors, but this one has a number of yellow gems glinting softly upon its surface, and there is no slot to place your hand.

  • With a successful [[/check inv 14]] check, or anyone with [[/knowledge machines]] realizes that the large double door is made of solid bronze, likely weighing several tons. The mechanism is likely complex, and you can see some of the rotating gears that will allow the door to slide into the wall.

Blue Runic Door

Anyone who walks up to the Bronze door can attempt to investigate it with a variety of different checks.

  • With a [[/skill prc 12 passive]] or successful [[/skill prc 12]] check, it's clear that the surface of the door is smooth, except for banding lines of reinforcing bronze. Similar to some of the other doors, but this one has a number of blue gems glinting softly upon its surface, and there is no slot to place your hand.

  • With a successful [[/check inv 14]] check, or anyone with [[/knowledge machines]] realizes that the large double door is made of solid bronze, likely weighing several tons. The mechanism is likely complex, and you can see some of the rotating gears that will allow the door to slide into the wall.

Matrix of Agaseros.name: Matrix of Agaseros
Matrix of Agaseros.text:
With a soft grinding sound, the door slides open, revealing a large chamber hiding one final secret, the heart of the Chamber itself, the Matrix of Agaseros. The dark stone shell, covered in massive runes, emanates a rhythmic, powerful light from its shining core that seems to breathe, expanding and contracting like a living entity. The light swirls in mesmerizing patterns, casting ethereal shadows that dance along the walls. The arcane energy here flows from the Matrix in currents, occasionally sparking and crackling like electricity.

Secret Optional Boss

This room is currently inaccessible in Early Access. Its contents will become a secret boss that is unlocked by finding and activating hidden mechanisms, discovered in various rooms throughout the area map.

Steam Room.name: Steam Room
Steam Room.text:
As you step inside, the sudden rise in temperature hits you like a wall. The air is thick with sweltering steam that instantly causes you to overheat. The walls and floors seem to be glinting with a thin layer of moisture, and the stone is darkened and discolored by the heat. At the center of the room is a large bronze grate covering an open pit of softly bubbling molten rock that glows with an intense red glow. The lava churns and bubbles gently, sending up bursts of steam and the occasional hiss as it interacts with the surrounding air.

Surrounding the pit, each of the seven walls features a large basin filled with glowing coals, and pipes along the walls appear to be filled with water that occasionally drips on the coals or expels steam of its own to keep the room pressurized.

A Test of Endurance

Once all the party members are within the room, the door behind them closes and then seals shut. The challenge within is fairly straightforward, the party must survive 1 minute in the Steam Room.

Once the door is sealed, begin a combat encounter and have the party roll initiative. Over the next ten rounds, they must make a series of increasingly complex checks and attempt to counter the rising heat in the room as best as they are able. While sealed within the room, the party cannot leave through any means, abilities, or spells, including teleportation magic.

The spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplElementali]{Elementalism} is helpful in a very minor way and allows a character to direct the flow of the steam slightly. Unfortunately, this only gives a single character in the party mild relief and +1 to their constitution checks while in the room.

The spells @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSleetStorm]{Sleet Storm} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIceStorm00]{Ice Storm} can be used, but this spell has no effect on the lava basin in the middle of the room, merely creating more steam as the sleet evaporates. The spell can douse one of the basins fully if it is centered upon it, which grants the party a slight reprieve and a +1 bonus to any Constitution checks for the entire party.

The spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplControlWat]{Control Water} can be used to try to redirect the flow of water from the steam pipes. This has a tangible effect on the amount of steam buildup in the room and the rising levels of heat, and the party gains a +2 bonus to any constitution checks they need to make while in the room.

Every round, each member of the party must attempt the following checks and saves in order.

1st Round

The heat is oppressive and begins to affect a character's ability to think clearly. They must roll a [[/save con 11]] and on a failure, the character suffers @Advantage[-2] on all ability checks for the next round due to fatigue.

2nd Round

As the steam vents erupt unpredictably, the characters must avoid the steam escaping from the nearby walls with a [[/save dex 17]] save. A failure results in [[/damage 1d6 fire]] and @Advantage[-2] on the next environmental hazard in the room.

3rd Round

Characters can attempt to stand firm against the steam and resist the heat with a [[/check ath 13]] check. On a failure, they inadvertently take too many deep breaths of steam and begin choking, giving them a level of exhaustion.

4th Round

Everyone in the party has a brief moment to regain their breath as the steam seems to die down for a few seconds. The party can all roll a [[/check med 14]] and is successful, regaining [[/heal 1d4]] hit points.

5th Round

As the steam in the room thickens and the weight of the heat becomes nearly overwhelming, the party must make a [[/save con 16]] save, if they fail, each character receives one level of Exhaustion.

6th Round

Characters can try to identify a particular spot around the room that might help in avoiding damage. Success with a [[/check inv 15]] allows them to gain @Advantage[2] on a single following check related to environmental hazards in the room.

7th Round

Steam erupts violently from the lava basin in an explosion that catches the party off guard. Everyone must make a [[/check dex 18]] or become Blinded for 1 minute.

8th Round

Players can attempt to find another safe place between the steam pipes by identifying hot spots and the patterns of the eruptions with [[/check sur 20]]. On a failure, they accidentally stumble into a highly saturated area, suffering [[/damage 2d10 fire]] and [[/damage 2d10 force]] as they are engulfed in boiling steam and knocked prone for the next round.

9th Round

Characters who are proficient in arcane knowledge can attempt to manipulate the magical energies of the chamber to create a temporary shielding barrier against the heat. Success with a [[/check arc 18]] check from any character provides the entire party with fire resistance for the next round, as their understanding of the magic in the room helps to create a protective aura.

10th Round

As the heat reaches its peak, pressure builds in the room, and random steam jets erupt violently. The party must make one final [[/save con 16]] save, and if they fail, each character takes [[/damage 3d10 fire]] as the steam in the entire room begins to scald the party.

Once the rounds are over, the steam and heat in the room suddenly disappear, and the temperature returns to normal. As the thick steam clears, the party finds an ornate-looking pedestal in the center of the room.

Ornate Pedestal

Interactivity

A player character can interact with the orante pedestal without investigating it. Doing so releases the Hydral in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Main Reservoir} with a resounding roar sound that echoes around the chamber.

Orante Runic Pedestal

The pedestal in this room is not trapped, nor is it a complicated device. It merely unlocks the final boss, and interacting with the gems on its surface is enough. It's likely the party may find this suspicious, however, so there are few clues on the pedestal to hint at its benign nature.

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 13]], they discover that the pedestal is connected by a thin magical thread to somewhere else in the chamber behind them.

  • Anyone attempting to investigate the pedestals cannot find any traps or anything suspicious, but if someone rolls a successful [[/check inv 18]], they discover that the pedestal is not dangerous and placing your hand on the gem is safe.

  • Anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] can somewhat read the runes, and they are runes of unlocking rather than anything dangerous.

Chamber Foyer.name: Chamber Foyer
Chamber Foyer.text:
Inside the chamber itself, you begin to feel a buzzing charge infuse you, as if you're walking into some kind of magical nexus. However, the scene before you is entirely ordinary, and the small room seems to be a simple foyer or entrance, with several chairs, carpets, and crates filled with tools and items against the walls. Against the far wall, a large bronze door is embedded in a complex magical mechanism.

The unassuming room serves as both a storage area for simple items and a preparation area where people can return to rest or prepare themselves for the challenges ahead.

Simple Storage

Some members of the Anachraenum and even the Fulgurite Blades (Who are currently within the Chamber in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.51O9wkvqzzHQ32wk]{Arcane Engine} room) carry supplies down into he chamber and leave them in this room. The party may have done the same and wish to leave some of their supplies here to return to, or they may wish to look through what is currently here that might help them.

However, the contents of the room are stuffed into crates at random with some old and broken equipment among the more useful supplies, and the party will have to spend some time here to gain anything valuable. A successful [[/skill inv 13]] check allows a character to roll on the Chamber Supplies table. Alternatively, if the party wishes to spend an hour rummaging through the supplies here, they can pick what they need from the table instead.

@Embed[RollTable.FC0w13XLKrdZBhEC inline rollable]

Bronze Door

Anyone who walks up to the Bronze door can attempt to investigate it with a variety of different checks.

  • With a [[/skill prc 12 passive]] or successful [[/skill prc 12]] check, it's clear that the surface of the door is smooth, except banding lines of reinforcing bronze. It is also clean and in excellent condition. In the very center is a protruding circular impression of a hand. Anyone who places thier hand upon the door finds that the door slides open.

  • With a successful [[/check inv 14]] check, or anyone with [[/knowledge machines]] realizes that the large double door is made of solid bronze, likely weighing several tons. The mechanism is likely complex, and you can see some of the rotating gears that will allow the door to slide into the wall.

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 16]], they discover that everything within the room is infused with magic to some degree. The amount of arcane energy in the air is almost overwhelming and can cause a painful reaction if a caster is not careful. Anyone who casts a spell in this room must roll a 1d20, [[/roll 1d20]], including Detect Magic. On a result of 1, they suffer a reduction to their constitution by 1 for 25 hours.

Overwhelming Magic

If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 18]], they discover that everything within the room is infused with magic to some degree. The amount of arcane energy in the air is almost overwhelming and can cause arcane magic to amplify spells if a caster is not careful. Anyone who casts a spell in this room must roll a 1d20, [[/roll 1d20]], including anyone who casts Detect Magic to discover this.

  • On a result of 1, the spell fails to cast and the caster suffers [[/damage 1d6 force]] and suffers a reduction to their constitution by 1 for 24 hours.

  • On a Result of 20, the spell is cast one level higher.

Shrine to Spectra.name: Shrine to Spectra
Shrine to Spectra.text:
Dominating the room on the northern side is a colossal statue of Spectra, the elder Goddess of magic. Carved from the same stone as the rest of the Chamber, the statue stands majestically against one wall, towering over the room at least twice the height of a person. Her form is gracefully poised, draped in ethereal robes with mirrored hands, outstretched as if in the moment before casting a spell. The floor of the shrine is scattered with hundreds of unlit candles, and nothing moves within the room, which is eerily silent.

Magical Devotion

The room presents a challenge based on the parties' deviation, or at least their ability to uncover what devotion might be in the context of Specta, the elder Goddess of Magic. They must interpret the teachings of Spectra through both arcane knowledge and divine understanding.

  • If a character rolls a [[/check insight 12]], they might believe that the challenge involves lighting the candles in the room. This can be done, but it does not lead anywhere.

  • Anyone attempting to investigate the statue can roll a [[/check religion 15]]. On a success, they are suddenly overcome with insight, allowing them to tap into a divine aspect of magic. This gives them the idea to kneel before the statue and draw an arcane symbol into the air. A further [[/check arc 12]] or anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] determines that the statue needs to have a spell cast directly at its outstretched hands.

  • If there is a follower of Spectra in the room, these checks are made easier by adding +3 to every roll.

Once a party member casts a spell at the hands, it doesn't matter which spell as long as it creates a tangible effect that can appear within the room. A magical sound is heard, and the challenge is complete.

Cyan Pedestal

Completing the challenge here reveals a pedestal, which appears from nothing in the room.

Interactivity

A player character can interact with the cyan pedestal without investigating it. Doing so unlocks the Cyan Runic Door on the 1st floor.

Cyan Runic Pedestal

The pedestal in this room is not trapped, nor is it a complicated device. It merely unlocks any cyan door within the Chamber, and interacting with the gem on its surface is enough to unlock the door. It's likely the party may find this suspicious, however, so there are a few clues on the pedestal to hint at its benign nature.

  • If a character casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} and or rolls a [[/check arcana 13]], they discover that the pedestal is connected by a thin magical thread to somewhere else in the chamber.

  • Anyone attempting to investigate the pedestal cannot find any traps or anything suspicious, but if someone rolls a successful [[/check inv 18]], they discover that the pedestal is not dangerous and placing your hand on the gem is safe.

  • Anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] can somewhat read the runes, and they are runes of unlocking rather than anything dangerous.

Central Column Chamber.name: Central Column Chamber
Central Column Chamber.text:
A massive chamber lies before you, with a massive central column reaching up towards a vaulted ceiling high above. Looking down, however, you can also see that the column descends into the depths below, where you can see the faint glimmer of water. The surrounding walls, etched with arcane runes, are pulsating slowly and faintly with energy, and the hum of infusing magic is even stronger here than in the entrance foyer.

The column in front of you has two bronze platforms sticking out from the center and is currently allowing you passage toward the middle. Three doors lie across from you on the other walls, all of which seem to be sealed shut.

Interactivity

The party must rotate the central column, ascend and descend, and attempt to access the different rooms of the Chamber, following the path laid out and completing every room and its challenges in order. However, it is possible to interrupt this careful order, depending on whether the party is able to gain access to the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.CZyyf1rAApgv3siK]{Barrier Control Room}.

In the middle of the Central Column structure, there is a small bronze lever with an arcane rune. Players can interact with the lever here to rotate the entire central platform, including the two protruding bronze elements, 90 degrees clockwise.

Rotating Platforms

Within the Central Column Chamber is a large vertical pillar stretching all the way upward nearly 100 feet from the bottom of the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Main Reservoir} through the first floor and ending on the second floor of the chamber.

On both the second and first floors, the central column has independent sections that can rotate 90 degrees clockwise once the lever is pulled on the central column itself. On these floors, platforms extend from the central column sections and connect to several doorways and entrances.

Any character that walks over to the central column notices the following immediately:

The stonework of the column is smooth and unmarked, and seems to have been recently cleaned. There appear to be stairs here in the middle, and on the column itself, there is a small bronze lever with a shimmering arcane rune above it.

If a character attempts to investigate the lever, a successful [[/skill inv 15]] check or anyone with [[/knowledge machines]] or [[/knowledge rituals]] discovers that the entire column is likely capable of rotating once the lever is pulled.

Jumping or Falling

The massive central chamber has lots of vertical space, and the party might think it's possible to skip the stairs on the central column and try to jump down to the first level or the ground floor of the chamber. However, this is prevented by Arcane Barriers.

Arcane Barriers

Within the Central Column Room are two Arcane Barriers, which are 5 feet below and underneath the rotating platforms on the second and first floors. These barriers prevent the party from descending or ascending without turning the Main Column and using the stairs to traverse the chamber. They prevent anything from passing through them, including any attempts to teleport between the barriers, as well as using any class features or spells.

Any character with a [[/skill prc 14 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill prc 12]] check notices the following:

While the darkness of the chamber makes it difficult to see, a lattice of arcane energy spans the entire room here — a nearly-invisible barrier that seems to prevent access between the different floors of the complex.

In the event that a character falls onto or chooses to jump onto these barriers, they suffer [[/damage 4d6 lightning]] damage and are magically thrown back to the previous position. They are also &Reference[Paralyzed] for [[/roll 1d4]] minutes

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

This area map showcases the grounds and interior of the two-level Marlstone Manor, both before and during the annual Marlstone Gala.

The map appears in two events:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY]{Casing the Joint}, which gives the party the opportunity to get the lay of the land and determine the missing Funar Cevher's location while posing as staff planning for the gala.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.jalZUo8LGHwnn7B4]{The Marlstone Gala}, where they attempt to pull off a rescue of Funar Cevher in the middle of the gala by using their access as guests.

Physical differences in the map between the two events are minor and generally restricted to decor and the number and type of guests present, but gameplay may differ based on what is present and available to the party.

This map is adjacent to the Lantern Roads map, which depicts the nearby Lantern Roads neighborhood and the secret dungeon underneath the manor.

Gazetteer Entry

The most prominent mansion in Marlstone due to its impressive height, Marlstone Manor has had other names over the years as it passed between different owners, but most eventually fell on hard times. Local superstition says that naming it anything other than Marlstone Manor brings bad luck to the owners. The manor is famous for its glass panels, which avoid fully blocking the views of any other building while catching the eye with their impressive water features. The building also plays host, every year, to the Marlstone Gala, an event where the powerful and influential mix and mingle while showing off the latest fashions.

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

This area map is used ast least twice within the Disgraced House quest, once when the party scouts it in , and once during the Manor. As needed, rooms in the manor's area walkthrough may have a Pre-Gala section (used in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY]{Casing the Joint}) and At the Gala section (used in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.jalZUo8LGHwnn7B4]{The Marlstone Gala}). If these are not indicated, the room remains the same for both events.

Illumination

Lights in most rooms of Marlstone Manor are bright, though there are unoccupied rooms that may have dim lighting as noted.

Terrain

All terrain within Marlstone Manor is normal terrain, unless otherwise noted.

Elevation

Ceilings in Marlstone Manor are generally 40 feet high, unless otherwise noted.

Manor Access

As the party moves through Marlstone Manor, they may have Open, Restricted, or Forbidden access to a room. Open rooms can be accessed without raising suspicion or requiring checks, unless the party is doing something that would independently raise suspicion, such as breaking into a locked safe.

Exploring Restricted Manor Rooms

Restricted Rooms are rooms that characters have no reason to be in. During scouting, this is dependent on the characters' role, while during the gala, it is generally static unless there is a special circumstance noted.

Characters whose role is restricted from the room must succeed on a [[/check stealth 17]] check to sneak into the room.

  • If they succeed, they enter the room with no consequences.

  • If they fail, guards are summoned. They must succeed on either a [[/check persuasion 17]] check or a check related to the room (as noted on the area walkthrough) to explain themselves.

    • If they succeed on the check, they are able to leave without consequence.

    • If they fail the check, they gain a level of suspicion.

    • If they fail the check by 3 or more, they gain an additional level of suspicion.

  • After failing a stealth check on a restricted room, the stealth DC for that room increases by 1. This penalty stacks.

Exploring Forbidden Manor Rooms

Forbidden Rooms are rooms that no characters have cause to be in, no matter what their role is. They operate similarly to restricted room, with the following differences:

  • Characters must succeed on a [[/check stealth 19]] check to sneak into the room.

  • A failure increases the stealth DC by 2.

Characters also have a limited amount of time within the room. After 2 checks have been made within the room, a member of staff will enter to check on the room. Characters must immediately exit and make a [[/save charisma 18]] saving throw.

  • If the save is successful, they can leave without consequence.

  • If they fail the save, they gain a level of suspicion.

Gardens.name: Gardens
Gardens.text:
Access to the Gardens

Access to the Gardens varies. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

  • Pre-Gala: Open to Gardeners and Decorators, Restricted for Kitchen Staff

  • During Gala: Open to Guests

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

Pre-Gala

Gardeners are busy straightening up the many hedges, grasses, and flowers found outside the Manor, attempting to perfect them as best they can before the gala. Though most seem harried, an older man in well-worn Ordani garb appears as if he has been here countless times before, humming to himself as he spritzes water on a flower border.

The older gentleman is the gardener Tavro. Characters can speak to him in the event @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#questioning-the-staff]{Casing the Joint}.

At The Gala

The gardens are in full bloom, as if the gods themselves wanted this night to go perfectly. Even in the dimmer light of evening, their beauty is hard to ignore, drawing the eye away from areas of mundane shadow.

Janix Mance prefers to stay outside of the Manor, hiding in the gardens while waiting for the party to arrive.

Distracting the Guards

Party guests are allowed in the gardens, but Janix must remain hidden. In addition to any aid with stealth checks that the party might provide, they can keep him out of sight from the guards by causing a distraction away from where Janix will be copying the key to grab the guards' attention.

  • With a successful [[/check deception 18]] or [[/check 18 intimidation]] check, or [[/knowledge intrigue]] characters can start a heated argument with another guest.

  • With a successful [[/check athletics 18]] check, knock over one of the braziers, lighting some nearby flowers on fire.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 18]] check or [[/knowledge machines]], identify the lever that feeds the fountains. It can be disabled with a successful [[/check 18 sleightofhand]] check, causing the water to begin to back up within the fountain.

If characters pull off more than one of these distractions (or a similar distraction at the GM's discretion), or succeed by 3 or more on their check, the distraction is enough to lure one of the two guards within the @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.6pccfZZYqVECcekQ]{Guardhouse }outside.

Guardhouse.name: Guardhouse
Guardhouse.text:
Access to the Guardhouse

Access to the Guardhouse is forbidden to all at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor. See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

The guardhouse connects directly to Lantern Road through the@UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.9fHLs3vOjSlfTmfQ]{Marlstone Manor Entrance}. It is not significantly different before or during the gala.

Two guards sit inside a simple guardhouse, surrounded by nothing other than a simple table and chairs. They stare idly into the distance until the ring of a small chime from outside, when both rise from their seats and head into the gardens beyond the guard station, heading in opposite directions.

Fooling the Guards

The party can convince the guards to go out of the guardhouse and into the gardens by duplicating the tone that signals them to go on duty.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check, characters hear the chime well enough to be able to duplicate it.

  • Characters will need a way to make the noise of the chime - with a successful [[/check performance 16]] check, characters can throw their voice and mimic the sound. They gain @Advantage[2] on this check if they use a musical instrument with which they are proficient. They may also use a spell that creates sound, such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMinorIllus]{Minor Illusion} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplPrestidigi]{Prestidigitation}.

Persuading the Guards

With a successful [[/check deception 19]] check, the party can claim that the guards have been called away to patrol elsewhere, or that the party is also made up of guards and will replace them. The guards will then leave, allowing characters to move through.

Fighting the Guards

The guards in the guardhouse are @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Wandren Patrollers} dedicated to preventing the party from passing between Lantern Roads and Marlstone Manor - one guard will block the entrance opposite the one that the party entered through, using their @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F.Item.PVF1Y5P02LAH2z0V]{Paralyzing Poison }and @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F.Item.tzf4esLNwPFMYhgC]{Slowing Serum} to stop the party from exiting quickly. If they are nearing death, they will throw @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F.Item.bJdYjc1RC0cwMKDa]{Choking Fog Dust} in the room, even though they will be affected as well.

The other guard will go for help, though they will move at a normal pace so as not to alert the guests or staff about the problem. If they reach another guard before being subdued, the party is either kicked out (if scouting the manor) or detained in an upstairs room (if at the gala).

Veranda.name: Veranda
Veranda.text:
Access to the Veranda

The Veranda is open to all at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor. See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

The long white stone veranda overlooks the Manor's well-manicured gardens and provides one of the best views of Ordain in the city. Wherever you stand on the walkway, Ordain's spires and white stone buildings draw the eye, in part due to the soft glow of the tiles, which have been designed to gently mimic the lighting of the sky above.

Foyer.name: Foyer
Foyer.text:
Access to Foyer

The Foyer is open to all at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

Two large stone pillars frame an open doorway into the gala beyond, carved with a design of curved symbols with inlaid gold that glint ever so slightly as you move your eye, creating a sense of both luxury and movement, as if the road to Wandren were paved in gold.

Pre-Gala

After characters receive their instructions from Jalla Difae in the Casing the Joint event (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#getting-into-marlstone-manor]{Getting into Marlstone Manor}), she will shoo them along if they remain in the area. Once they are done with all scouting, though, they can be paid for their efforts before they leave.

Jalla Difae, the gala's organizer, remains in the center of the room in front of a large wooden table filled with lists and supplies, directing traffic and looking over papers.

Done with everything on your list already? If not, get to it. If so, thank you. I'll get you your payment and you can be on to the rest of your day.

Getting Paid

Characters are paid based on their role, and must return their assigned tools in return.

  • Gardeners return @UUID[Item.VLOb3sWUKIuuWUdG]{Gardener's Toolbelt} and receive [[/award 2gp]]

  • Decorators return @UUID[Item.W2XdDc2U3gBjtz1i]{Decorator's Satchel} and receive [[/award 3gp]]

  • Kitchen staff return@UUID[Item.OddoS1q37rUnCB2P]{Apron of Many Pockets} and receive [[/award 1gp]]

Jalla can be convinced to pay [[/award 3gp]] to Gardeners and Kitchen Staff with a successful [[/check persuasion 18]] check. If the check succeeds by 4 or more, she will pay [[/award 5gp]] to all present.

At the Gala

A greeter in House Wandren attire, welcomes each new face that comes into the foyer, directing them to the arched doorways to each side of the main foyer. Behind them, strains of music and dancing lights seem to draw you into the large room behind them.

Welcome, welcome! To the left, through the sitting room, is the coat room, you can see Hephiss Wandren's artwork in the gallery to the right, and of course the ballroom is straight behind me. If you need anything else, please let me know.

This room is primarily a place to pass through. If asked, the greeter has nothing else specific to say, but will direct characters to any of the following rooms - @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.NgXe2ukpymWe1ngw]{Sitting Room}, @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.mLzBFHXratqh3i0p]{Gallery}, @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.iWKrFcc0tCQyaCRa]{Veranda}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5mLybogUBaWRwnGx]{Hall Bathroom}.

Sitting Room.name: Sitting Room
Sitting Room.text:
Access to Sitting Room

Access to the Stting Room is open to all at all times (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is nearby.

Pre-Gala

Chairs are still being arranged and side tables cleared, with staff working hard to ensure that the room is ready for the party.

At the Gala

The sounds of laughter and conversation fill the air as guests share drinks and catch up with old friends. A few friendly debates cut through the noise, primarily about the quality of the band, along with occasional mentions of Trading House Cevher in tones of voice that fall somewhere between self-satisfied and judgmental.

The party may listen in to additional topics of conversation in this room without a check. To find what they overhear, roll on the table below.

@Embed[RollTable.5fFp7ntWIsXbLUrI inline rollable]

Gallery.name: Gallery
Gallery.text:
Access

See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

  • Before the Gala: Open to Decorators, Kitchen Staff; Restricted to Gardeners

  • During the Gala: Open to Guests

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. Note: this is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

Pre-Gala

The benches in the center of the room have been set less for conversation than observation, centering around the large sculpture in the center of the room and a set of smaller paintings that line the walls.

The Small Door

There is a small door in the back of the room - characters who have access to the room can enter it without a check, finding the @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.H8J0fQi753A3O33I]{Gallery Storage Closet}.

Examining the Paintings

Hephiss has a number of paintings, most of Ordani landscapes, each with a note about her. Characters who spend 10 minutes examining the paintings and have either [[/knowledge arts]] or succeed on either a [[/check insight 16]] or [[/check investigation 16]] check to see their commonalities and themes have advantage on persuasion checks made while speaking with Hephiss.

The paintings include the following:

  • Streets of Virtue and Vice: A series of three paintings depicting crowds walking through the streets of Ordain from the same vantage point - one done at sunrise, one at midday, and one at sunset. The note reads "Those who claim to be virtuous in the light are often something else when Lantyr looks away."

  • On Plateaus: A pair of paintings, one of a river in the Arctus Plateau and the other of a ship sailing the Destine River. The note reads "In the words of the brilliant artist Indigo Ray, pllateaus have their beauty, but they are always best left behind."

  • Wanderings: Portraits of various Ordani individuals, all in the middle of an action, from juggling balls to building Marlstone Manor. The note reads "Always in motion, always towards the top." Any character who succeeds on a [[/check history 16]] check, or who has [[/knowledge trade]] knows that these are past members of House Wandren.

During The Gala

Lights on the wall spotlight the paintings on easels beneath them, drawing the eye towards them and away from the large sculpture in the center of the room. Under each painting, a small sign reads "Art by Hephiss Wandren." In the back corner of the room, a rope has been set up, calling attention and blocking access to the door that sits behind it.

The Small Door

There is a small door in the back of the room, blocked by a rope meant to dissuade guests from reaching it.

  • Characters can open the door without being seen with a successful [[/check stealth 17]] check, leading them into the @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.H8J0fQi753A3O33I]{Gallery Storage Closet}.

    • On a failure, they are shooed away from the door. They can repeat the check, but the DC increases by 2 per check.

    • After the third failure, they are escorted from the room and gain 1 point of suspicion. They cannot retry the check.

Grand Hall.name: Grand Hall
Grand Hall.text:
Access to Grand Hall

The Grand Hall is open to all at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

Pre-Gala

As the crowning achievement of Marlstone Manor, the decorative stone pillars, large sloping staircase, and intricate wall panels will be the centerpiece of the Marlstone Gala, held every year beneath its high arched ceiling. Now, though, the rooom is urrently very much a work in progress, with flower clippings, bits of ribbon, and other decorative pieces spread across the floor between the hard-working decorators. Well, mostly hard working. One woman appears to be mostly watching while pretending to get work done.

The woman in question is the decorator Erisa Wandren, who the party can speak to in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#questioning-the-staff]{Casing the Joint.}

During The Gala

The soft tones of the music, balls of lights dangling from a lattice high above, and flowers, which almost overflow the boxes they sit in along the landing above in a an explosion of color, combine to create a sense of magic in the grand hall - somehow it seems even larger than it did before the gala, and yet there is a sense of welcome and camaraderie that floods the room.

Hephiss' Study.name: Hephiss' Study
Hephiss' Study.text:
Access to Hephiss' Study

Access to Hephiss' Study is forbidden at all times.See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. Note: this is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

There is no significant difference between Hephiss' Study before the gala and during the gala.

A guard stands at the edge of the well-appointed study, leaning against the wall in a stance of feigned relaxation that looks much less like a casual member of the staff and more like they are determined to keep any nosy visitor out.

Beyond them, a large desk sits in the middle of the room. Hephiss' desk, most likely. There is enough of her signature black and gold decor and the smell of the smoky perfume she favors to make you nearly certain that this is her dedicated office.

Entering The Study

Evading the Guard

This room is forbidden to outsiders. Characters that wish to cross the guard's line of sight must either succeed on a [[/check stealth 19]] check or persuade the guard that they are in the room for a reason with a successful [[/check persuasion 18]] check.
