Characters may increase their chances of stealth by distracting the guard - if any of the below succeed, the DC of the stealth check decreases by 2:

  • Using a cantrip or spell that creates noise or generates a light (such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDancingLig]{Dancing Lights}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMinorIllus]{Minor Illusion}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplPrestidigi]{Prestidigitation})

  • Throwing an item far enough away from them to draw the guard's attention with a successful [[/check athletics 17]] check.

  • Using an item that creates provides cover, shields their appearance, or clears the room (like @UUID[Item.JKWt3ZZKBaEvNbw1]{Choking Fog Dust} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgDustOfDisappe]{Dust of Disappearance}).

  • If an item or spell is chosen that does damage to the guard, they alert the rest of the staff and the guards become more watchful, raising the suspicion level for the entire party.

@Embed[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]

Confrontation with the Guard

Guards in Marlstone Manor will avoid direct combat, fleeing to alert others and detain the party. At most, they will use their @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F.Item.bJdYjc1RC0cwMKDa]{Choking Fog Dust} to stop the party's movements while they leave in search of help.

If the guard flees the room before being subdued, the party has been caught. If they are scouting the manor (in Casing the Joint), they are escorted from the manor and the event ends. If they are at the gala (in Marlstone Gala) they are brought to Guest Bedroom 2 and locked away.

Searching the Study

Characters who have avoided or subdued the guards can explore the study, using the rules for @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{forbidden access}. They notice the large wall safe without a check.

The Wall Safe

If characters wish to open the wall safe:

  • The safe is secured with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplArcaneLock]{Arcane Lock} - it cannot be opened unless the spell is suppressed (via @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplKnock00000]{Knock}), disrupted (via @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDisintegra]{Disintegrate},@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{ Dispel Magic}, or similar), or bypassed using the password "Indigo," the name of Hephiss Wandren's favorite artist.

  • Once the Arcane Lock spell is suppressed or inactive, the safe can be opened with a successful [[/check dexterity 19]] check with @UUID[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR.Item.IPNtmXU99URbaqNk]{Thieves' Tools} or with @UUID[Item.tFVP9iFAgD0zEhtV]{Hephiss' Keys}.

The wall safe's contents vary:

  • Before the Marlstone Gala, it contains the following:

    • A coin box containing [[/award 60gp]]

    • A vial of @UUID[Item.pyKB2u54RkGyCbdu]{Withering Flesh Poison}

    • An@UUID[Item.ntC2qNGj6cVNF8H6]{unlit torch} (in truth, a torch belonging to the celestial creatures the Kynryth)

    • A draft copy of the article found in @UUID[Item.nCdyFX3dY14CFRpA]{Overheard In Ordain: A Stitch In Crime} with additional details about the murder

  • During the Marlstone Gala, it contains all of the above and @UUID[Item.VB4pcl6EWcXObLco]{Juro Wandren's Ledger}

Hephiss' Desk

Characters can look through the papers on Hephiss' Desk for anything of interest without a check. Most of the papers are daily ledgers and plans for the gala, with two exceptions:

  • A list of members of House Wandren. Several have been crossed out. Juro Wandren's name is on the list with a question mark next to it. Vitt Wandren's name is underlined.

  • @UUID[Item.n1z4ZEHdDXTb2zTH]{ Gala Security To-Do List}. If the party sees this list before the party, only the first item has been checked off. If they see it at the party, all but the last item have been checked off.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
Access to Kitchen

Access to the Kitchen varies. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

  • Before the Gala: Open to Kitchen Staff, Decorators, Restricted to Gardeners

  • During the Gala: Restricted to Guests

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result within Marlstone Manor.

The air is full of the smells of a good meal, already wafting up from the many prep tables filled with vegetables, meats, and herbs. Cooks move between these prep stations, the cook fire, and the many dishes that will serve Marlstone Manor's guests tonight, focused on their tasks as they move from folding one thing to stirring another. Between the cooks, barrels filled with varied liquids are being added to cookpots on one side of the kitchen and poured into glasses to be served to guests on the other.

Entrances and Exits

With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check, characters notice the top edge of a door to the gardens in the back of the kitchen. If they choose to go in the direction of the door, they must succeed on a [[/check stealth 18]] check to avoid catching the chef's eyes. Characters without an Apron of Many Pockets have @Advantage[-2] on this check.

  • With a success, characters make their way to the door, which is unlocked by jammed shut. Characters can open it with a successful [[/check athletics 16]] check to force it open by using strength or a successful [[/check sleightofhand 16]] check to jimmy it open. Once opened in this way, it remains ajar, providing a direct route between the gardens and the kitchen.

  • With a failure, the chef stops the character and asks them to quickly chop some vegetables at the back corner before "going on their break." Characters can attempt to talk their way out of the task, succeeding on a [[/check persuasion 16]] check. If they fail to convince the chef, they must either complete the task or leave the kitchen.

    • To chop the vegetables, characters need to succeed on a [[/check sleightofhand 15]] check. On a failure, they cut themselves, taking [[/check 1d4 slashing damage]].

Workshop.name: Workshop
Workshop.text:
Access to Hephiss' Workshop

Access to Hephiss' Workshop is forbidden at all times. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result within Marlstone Manor.

Artifacts of all shapes and sizes lie scattered across wooden tables and under magnifying glasses — many half-dismantled or gouged by the tools that sit nearby. Along the edge of the room, wrapped packages sit waiting, some fully enclosed and some partially ripped open, thelr contents spread out beside them as if someone has been searching them for one thing in particular.

Searching the Workshop

Though there are many artifacts and partially deconstructed machines within the room, none appear to be of any value.

Sketches among the pieces show a diagram of a creature with multiple tentacles with questions on it, including "How many segments in a single arm" and "tripod legs provide speed and balance??"

Library.name: Library
Library.text:
Access to the Library

Access to the library is restricted at all times, but the doors to it are closed, not locked. They can be easily opened without a check.See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. Note: this is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

There is no significant difference between the library before the gala and during the gala.

Books line the shelves that wrap around the room. Each section is orderly, with everything neatly labeled and organized — making it easy to notice if anything is out of place. The only exception is the large desk at the back of the room, whose surface holds a stack of paper and books left open, as if the person reading them might wander back in at any moment.

The Library Desk

Characters can make a cursory search of the desk in the library without a check, finding the following:

  • A note that reads: Hephiss - the new system is ready, but it only works if the books remain in the right place. Use the phrase from the catalogues for the book that you want and it will be retrieved for you. Please do not retrieve yourself - trust me, you won't enjoy it.

  • A book titled "Unexpected Alchemy: New Uses for Familiar Extract," which is opened to a page titled "Beyond the Bath (C)," which details the following items:

    • Cloud Oil, which is known for the way it makes the user feel as if they are floating while bathing, contains Nimbus Water, collected from the Nimbus Pitcher Plant, and can be used to make airborne steam and scents spread across a room.

  • A blank piece of notebook paper with indentations on it where someone has pressed onto the page.

    • With a successful [[/check investigation 16]] check, [[/check history 16]] check, or [[/knowledge intrigue]], characters know that the indentations could be read by rubbing it with charcoal (which can be found in the Lounge fireplace, on the desk in Hephiss' study, and in several artisan's tools (Calligrapher's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Painter's Tools).

    • If revealed, the charcoal imprint has a library passphrase on it, which retrieves a book when spoken out loud — Radiance Rewarded, which retrieves the book "Luxarum: Realm of Holy Beauty."

    • "Luxarum: Realm of Holy Beauty" is an old text that has been partially faded. Characters who read through it learn that the beings from the inner realm Luxarum are often known as Celestials because of their use of radiant fire as a source of magic and life.

Using the Library Catalogue

A note by the hand-bound catalog books reads:

Hephiss, I have been adding to the collection as you requested. You are nothing if not thirsty for knowledge. In addition to the book on alchemy, you may enjoy the artifacts guide and the history of the manor - it's had several colorful inhabitants!

Use the passphrase and the book will be retrieved for you. A system you may wish to use yourself for anything you may want to hide away - I've added a guide to the shelf.

Characters can flip through the library catalogue at their leisure, but must succeed on a check to find a worthwhile book and learn its passphrase. Available books are:

  • A History of Marlstone Manor (requires a successful [[/check history 17]] check or [[/knowledge intrigue]] to learn the passphrase "The Walls Have Memories").

    • Reading the book reveals that there were once tunnels beneath the manor that connected to a room in the first floor's East Wing.

  • Great Artists of the Arctus Plateau (requires a successful [[/check history 17]] check or [[/knowledge arts]] to learn the passphrase "A Painters Pride")

    • The book is very well worn, revealing that Hephiss Wandren is a fan of the arts. One page, in particular, featuring the artist Indigo Ray, who is known for his self-portraits, is particularly dog-eared.

  • Passphrases and You (requires a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check or [[/knowledge intrigue]] to learn the passphrase "This Is Not A Passphrase")

    • Reading the book reveals that passphrases can be used to hide and reveal doors that might not otherwise be found, and should relate to a person's hobbies and interests.

Defensive Shelving

With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check while looking at the library shelves, or with [[/check perception 18 passive]], characters can see a slight shimmer in the air around the outside of the library shelves, caused by a defensive field meant to protect the books from unnecessary disturbances.

  • Characters who succeed on an [[/check arcana 17]] check, or who use Identify, know that the bookshelves are warded from being touched directly and will emit force energy towards anyone who attempts to remove a book.

  • If characters attempt to physically remove a book from the library shelf, they must immediately make a [[/save dexterity 17]] saving throw. On a failure, they take [[/damage 1d6 force]] damage and are forcibly pushed backwards 20 feet. On a success, they are unaffected, but are unable to remove the book.

    • If a character is pushed backwards into a wall or solid object, the sound alerts a Guard, who enters the library immediately - as it is a Restricted area, characters must succeed on a [[/check persuasion 17]] check or [[/check history 17]] check to convince the guard they are in the library in good faith. On a failure, they gain a level of suspicion. On a failure of 3 or more, they gain 2 levels of suspicion.

Coatroom.name: Coatroom
Coatroom.text:
Access to the Coatroom

Access to the Coatroom is open to all at all times. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is nearby.

Pre-Gala

Coats and jackets fill the hangers of the room. Most are everyday fare, likely belonging to the staff who are working to prepare the house for the gala.

A Quick Search

Characters who search through the coat room and succeed on a [[/check perception 15]] check find a discarded @UUID[Item.OddoS1q37rUnCB2P]{Apron of Many Pockets}.

At the Gala

An array of coats, jackets, and scarves have filled the room, taking up every hanger spot. Between the vibrant colors, soft fabrics, and occasional stuffed pockets, the room looks like a display case of cutting-edge fashion and casual luxury.

In their Pockets

This is a high-traffic staff room, but pickpockets may find something of value.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check, characters can identify a pocket with something in it that's worth taking. If they fail the check, any pocket they attempt to take something from has only worthless items.

    The coat pockets are filled with items that take up a lot of space but have no real value - old marbles, a crumpled up handkerchief, the pit of a fruit still damp with saliva.

  • If they succeed on the check, the character can attempt to take from one of the following, receiving the item in parentheses if they succeed in taking the item:

    • A pocket that sags down as if weighted with something heavy (a coin pouch with [[/award 6d10gp]] )

    • A pocket with the top of a closed bag peeking out of the top (a pouch of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgDustOfDisappe]{Dust of Disappearance})

    • Something round that sloshes when you move by it (a bottle of TBD)

    • Something that glints just a little in the light (a@UUID[Item.tFyeCSvVP5TJ5Bib]{Gem-Encased Petal})

  • To take an item, characters must succeed on a [[/check sleightofhand 17]] check, or they are spotted by the staff. Once spotted, characters must succeed on a [[/check deception 16]] check to explain themselves or they gain a level of suspicion.

Hephiss' Downstairs Bathroom.name: Hephiss' Downstairs Bathroom
Hephiss' Downstairs Bathroom.text:
Access to Hephiss' Downstairs Bathroom

Access to Hephiss' Downstairs Bathroom is restricted at all times. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result within Marlstone Manor.

The bathroom, while small, holds a few bottles of perfume made of delicately colored glass.

Art Studio.name: Art Studio
Art Studio.text:
Access to Art Studio

Access to Art Studio is restricted at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

Easels have been haphazardly scattered around the room, and between them, flecks of paint look as if they have been thrown from one side of the room to the other. The paintings themselves all seem to be of the same three subjects over and over again - a metallic monster with waving tentacles, Hephiss herself, and an oddly coherent beam of light.

Servants' Office.name: Servants' Office
Servants' Office.text:
Access to the Servants' Office

Access to the Servants' Office varies. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

  • Pre-Gala: Open to All

  • During Gala: Restricted to Guests, Open to Staff

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

Pre-Gala

Staff come and go through the office, usually stopping only briefly to pick up a paper or drop off a note for another member of the staff. With as many exits and entrances as the room has, the door may shut occasionally, but it rarely stays that way for long.

Notes on the Table

Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 17]] check or who search through the papers and notes on the table find a Map of Marlstone Manor that indicates that the following rooms are forbidden to both staff and guests - Hephiss' Library (West Wing), Hephiss' Study (West Wing), Hephiss' Workshop (West Wing),

  • If characters succeed on the perception check by 3 or more, they notice a small note stuck to the back of the paper, which reads as follows:

    Not surprised the Workshop is on the forbidden list. I snuck in there to check it out and it's full of weird trinkets and diagrams I can't figure out. I don't think anyone saw me, but now there's a guard posted up in the study next door, so who knows?

At The Gala

Two of the Manor's guards sit in quiet conversation. As you enter, they barely look up, barking out a few words before going back to their discussion.

You're in the wrong place - bathroom is across the way.

Dealing with the Guards

The reaction of the guards to the party depends on if and how they exit the room:

  • If the party leaves by one of the doors to the lounge, they pay the party no mind.

  • If the party leaves by the servants' entrance and do not appear to be servants or guards, they stop the party and redirect them to the lounge exit doors. The party can convince the guards to let them through their chosen exit with a successful [[/check 17 persuasion]] check, a [[/check 17 history]] check to feign interest in the house's architecture, or a similar check at the GM's discretion.

If the party does not exit the room, the guards confront them, demanding that they leave.

  • With a successful [[/check persuasion 18]] or [[/check intimidation 18]] check, the party can convince the guards either that they are needed elsewhere (causing the guards to leave the room), or that the party should be allowed to stay.

  • With a successful [[/check sleightofhand 18]], characters can steal a @UUID[Item.dfPMi9RnFWXuLuLj]{Staff Key} from either of the guards.

Storage.name: Storage
Storage.text:
Access to Storage

Access to Storage varies. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

  • Pre-Gala: Open to all staff.

  • Gala: Open to staff, restricted to guests.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result while in Marlstone Manor.

Dining Room.name: Dining Room
Dining Room.text:
Access to Dining Room

Access to the Dining Room is open to all at all times (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is adjacent to this room (in a room directly above, below, or next to it).

  • With an additional charge of the rod, the party can determine that Funar is below the dining room.

Pre-Gala

Though the largely empty wooden dining table that dominaates the room looks far from ready to host any kind of formal meal, staff have clearly been assigned to make the room presentable, whether they're the gardeners adding floral displays to the side tables, kitchen staff polishing glasses from a side cabinet, or decorators ensuring that all sconces and candelabras are lit.

At The Gala

Soft light from the room's candles flickers across a mostly-empty room, dancing against the polished surface of the empty dining table and suffusing the leaves of the flowers on the room's side tables.

Staff Bathroom.name: Staff Bathroom
Staff Bathroom.text:
Access to the Staff Bathroom

Access to the Staff Bathroom varies. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

  • Before the Gala: Open to Staff (Kitchen Staff, Decorators, and Gardeners)

  • During the Gala: Restricted to Guests, Open to Staff

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result within Marlstone Manor.

Function dominates over form in the staff bathroom - the tiles are plain, the fixtures are basic, and the lighting feels somewhat harshly bright, as if someone is watching to make sure no one is taking anything they shouldn't be.

A search of the staff bathroom finds the cupboards bare. If there was anything to take here, it has long since been stolen.

Hephiss' Downstairs Closet.name: Hephiss' Downstairs Closet
Hephiss' Downstairs Closet.text:
Access to Hephiss' Downstairs Closet

Access to Hephiss' Downstairs Closet is forbidden at all times. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result within Marlstone Manor.

This room appears to contain a closet, but in reality hides the door to the staircase that leads down into Wandren HQ. It remains the same pre-gala and during the gala. Instead, the room changes based on character actions as noted below.

If Door Is Hidden

Though this appears to be a closet like any other, the objects all appear slightly out of place in a way difficult to put your finger on, and the smoky scent of Hephiss Wandren's perfume is thick in the air despite its relative emptiness.

Discovering the Door

Characters may suspect that there is a doorway in the closet, but it will not appear without a trigger being pressed in Hephiss' Bedroom. Before the doorway appears, party's can confirm its position with the following:

  • With a successful [[/check 18 investigation]] check, characters notice that there is a significant amount of space unaccounted for behind the closet wall.

  • If characters capture or question the guard stationed in Hephiss' study, they can reveal that there is an entrance in the closet.

  • With an Identify or Detect Magic spell, characters can determine that the wall leading down to the vault is behind an illusion spell triggered from elsewhere.

  • If characters strike the walls of the closet with an axe or similar object and succeed on a [[/check strength 18]] check, the tool embeds itself as normal in all walls except for the wall that is also a door, which is made of metal. On hitting the metal wall, it clangs and bounces off, though the wall appears the same.

If Door Is Revealed

Where a wood closet wall once stood, an intricate metal door is in its place, covered with symbols and images that stand out not just in this manor, but in this city, and maybe Ember as a whole. Towards the bottom of the door, in the middle of etchings, where a key might go, is a thick metal cover that appears bolted into place.

Investigating the Locked Door

Characters who succeed on a [[/check history 17]] check, have [[/knowledge celestials]], or who know [[/language harmos]] know that the door is covered with writing in Harmos. Those who know the language can read that it is a blessing that is meant to give the door strength and allow through only those who share the right words.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 17]] check can see a slight sheen on the door, as if there is a substance painted on it, and smell a slightly acrid smell. Those with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/knowledge crime]] can identify the scent and sheen as belonging to @UUID[Item.TwsLk1KC8SqDbL8G]{Thieves' Lament}.

Removing the Keyhole Cover

The entire door has been painted with @UUID[Item.TwsLk1KC8SqDbL8G]{Thieves' Lament}, and will burn and mark anyone who touches it physically. It is also trapped - anyone who touches it must make a [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw. On a failed save, they take [[/damage radiant 1d4]] damage. On a successful save, they take half-damage and hear a whisper.

As you pull your hand back from the jolt, a voice whispers, as if from within your ears - "use your words, Hephiss"

The damage of the door trap increases by one size of die each time the door is touched within the same hour, using the pattern noted below. The voice can give additional hints as noted.

  • First touch: [[/damage 1d4 radiant]]

  • Second touch: [[/damage 1d6 radiant]]

    Use the passphrase ,Hephiss. Here's a hint - two words long.

  • Third touch: [[/damage 1d8 radiant]]

    Really, Hephiss? Begin with the end of your favorite artist's name, as if Lantyr beats down on you.

  • Fourth touch: [[/damage 1d10 radiant]]

    That's going to leave a mark. Just like your favorite flowers, and the second half of your phrase.

The trap can be disarmed with a spell that negates its magic (Disintegrate, Dispel Magic, etc), but the keyhole cover remains in place.

Revealing the Keyhole

The keyhole can only be revealed by using the correct passphrase, "Ray Lanterelle." Once spoken, the keyhole cover disappears, and the door can be opened using @UUID[Item.tFVP9iFAgD0zEhtV]{Hephiss' Key} or the @UUID[Item.oGApwdmiQ9EoVL4G]{Copy of Hephiss' Key}.

Lounge.name: Lounge
Lounge.text:
Access to the Lounge

The Lounge is open to all at all times. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result within Marlstone Manor.

The carpet in this room is more well-worn than in other areas, as if it sees a more consistent amount of a foot traffic than other sections of the manor. The chairs and couches here are set up for conversation around a glowing hearth, with small spots around the outside of the room that are designed for entertainment — a piano, a game board, a bookcase with its books arranged by color rather than subject.

Pre-Gala

With gala prep in full stride, the lounge is well-trafficked, with decorators working to set out games and accessories designed to give the room a sense of warmth.

At The Gala

Quiet conversation and gameplay can be found throughout the space, with small groups discussing news of the day, their favorite outfits of the evening, and whether House Wandren will benefit from the recent change in the Ordinate. The fire nearby glows at low levels, leaving a layer of ash at the front of the fireplace, prevented from entering the room by a small grate.

The party may listen in to the topics of conversation in this room without a check. To find what they overhear, roll on the table below.

@Embed[RollTable.5fFp7ntWIsXbLUrI inline rollable]

Breakfast Room.name: Breakfast Room
Breakfast Room.text:
Access to Breakfast Room

Access to the Breakfast Room varies. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

  • Before the Gala: Open to Kitchen Staff, Decorators, Restricted to Gardeners

  • During the Gala: Restricted to Guests

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is nearby.

Pre-Gala

Light pours into the room from its bay window, highlighting the fine furnishings and plush rug, but most of the staff in the area are using it as little more than a throughway between the kitchen and the rest of the manor.

At the Gala

In the evening light, the Breakfast Room are dim and still, its large window providing little in the way of illumination. From the dimly lit tables and benches, muffled sounds of activity and vague shouts about food and service can be heard through the thick wooden door.

Entrance Plaza.name: Entrance Plaza
Entrance Plaza.text:
Access to Entrance

The Entrance Plaza is open to all at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

Pre-Gala

A mosaic of tiles at the edge of the road marks the entrance of the plaza that leads into Marlstone Manor. A couple of gardeners tend to the abundant red grasses and flowers nearby, evening some out in preparation for the upcoming event and clipping others to be displayed inside, while a pair of decorators work on straightening out a decorative fabric awning.

The workers in the front are intent on their work - there is nothing else to find here, and characters will be urged to go inside to speak to Jalla Difae if they need anything. In addition, the barriers around the sides of Marlstone Manor are impassable.

At The Gala

Now lit for a party, the entrance plaza seems to glow and the faint sounds of music and conversation float through the air from inside. Guests occasionally come and go, but remain intent on their own thoughts and pay you no mind.

There is nothing of particular interest to be found in the front entrance plaza. The barriers around the sides of Marlstone Manor remain impassable.

Hephiss' Bathroom.name: Hephiss' Bathroom
Hephiss' Bathroom.text:
Access to Hephiss' Bathroom

Access to Hephiss' Bathroom is forbidden at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

This relaxing bathroom is filled with luxury items and a large central tub for unwinding. The labels on the various elixirs and salves draw the eye, though it isn't immediately apparent what any of them do.

A Bathroom Full of Ingredients

The bath products here can be used in some formulas to create poisons, smoke bombs, etc.

Hephiss' Chambers.name: Hephiss' Chambers
Hephiss' Chambers.text:
Access to Hephiss' Chambers

Access to Hephiss' Chambers is forbidden at all times. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result within Marlstone Manor.

Delicate gray silks arch over a the bed in the center of the room - it, like the rug in the middle of the floor, the large mirror at the side of the room, and the dressing desk by the rear curtained window, is decorated with the patterns and colors that Hephiss Wandren is known for, and carries the faintest hint of the smoky perfume she's long been known to wear.

Pre-Gala

The Lady of the House

Hephiss is in her chambers during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY]{Casing the Joint}. If the party enters the room, she immediately demands to know why there are there.

What in the name of all that is — this room is strictly forbidden to staff. Who told you that you could come up here? And did you force your way in? I demand an explanation.

The party (or a single character, if they have separated) must immediately succeed on a [[/check persuasion 19]] group check - if half or more of the group succeeds on the check, the party succeeds as a whole.

  • If the party succeeds on the check, Hephiss is not happy, but allows characters to return to their duties. Their suspicion level is raised by 1.

  • If the party fails the check, Hephiss has them escorted off the grounds immediately, ending this event.

At The Gala

A Magical Panel

The panel that must be pressed to reveal the door on the floor below is part of Hephiss' dressing table.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check 15 perception]] check or who have [[/check 17 perception passive]] note the large mirror on one side of the room, which has a note affixed to it - a copy of Hephiss' @UUID[Item.n1z4ZEHdDXTb2zTH]{Gala Security To-Dos}. On it, she has added a note - press after you dress! - and a few doodled curlicues.

    • Characters who succeed on a [[/check investigation 15]] check know that the note indicates a panel in the bedroom that reveals the door.

    • Characters who search the room and succeed on a [[/check perception 17]] check see that the panel on the desk has the same curlicue panel as was used in the note.

  • The panel is magically attuned and can be located using @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} or similar spells.

If characters push the panel, it clicks loudly.

With a resounding click, the panel depresses, and an image appears on its surface as if it were being carved into the patterns in the wood before your eyes - an ornate door in a small room, leading to parts unknown.

Hephiss' Closet.name: Hephiss' Closet
Hephiss' Closet.text:
Access to Hephiss' Closet

Access to Hephiss' Closet is forbidden at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

This closet holds clothes similar to those that you have seen Hephiss Wandren wearing in the past, but appears to have nothing else of interest.

Greenhouse.name: Greenhouse
Greenhouse.text:
Access to Greenhouse

Access to the Greenhouse varies. See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.

  • Before the Gala: Restricted to Gardeners and Decorators, Forbidden to Kitchen Staff

  • During the Gala: Restricted to Guests

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details.

  • Funar Cevher is nearby.

The plants here are of a wider variety than those showcased elsewhere in the manor from their rainbow of vibrant colors to the differing shapes of their leaves and petals - some feather-like, some resembling large bells, and others like stars bursting forth from the ground. Though the air is still and quiet, a bag and tools on a bench in the center of the garden look as if they have only been resting there for a moment.

Exploring the Gardens

Characters can open the gardening bag and explore the garden without a check

  • If they look in the bag, they find a book of flowers, titled Beauty in Bloom: Floral Notes from Near and Far. While the book is readable, some of its pages appear more well-read than others. With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check, characters can identify a page on Lanterelles as the ones that are the most worn.

  • If they explore the garden, they can note which plants are most dominant and getting the most love with a successful [[/check nature 17]] check or [[/knowledge plants]], identifying the most well-loved plant as the Lanterelle.

  • If the party has seen Lanterelles elsewhere on the grounds, they can find the name of the flower in the Beauty in Bloom book or on a label on the flower bush, without needing a check.

Guest Bedroom 1.name: Guest Bedroom 1
Guest Bedroom 1.text:
Access to Guest Bedroom 1

Access to Guest Bedroom 1 is restricted at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

A generic-looking bedroom, though oddly it has only high and narrow windows, as if it was designed to hold things in instead of giving guests a way to look out.

Makeshift Holding Cell

If the party gains too much suspicion during the Marlstone Gala (as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.jalZUo8LGHwnn7B4#access-and-suspicion]{Access and Suspicion}), they will be brought to this room to be held until after the gala ends, with their equipment brought separately to @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.63LU4iUxlEldLhae]{Guest Bedroom 2}.

This clears their suspicion level, bringing them back to no suspicion.

Getting Out of the Guest Bedroom: The Windows

The Guest Bedroom is subject to an anti-magic field - spells do not work within its boundaries.

Though the windows are towards the ceiling. characters can attempt to reach the windows and climb out. Each window is located 25 feet off of the ground.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check investigation 16]] check while looking around the room can see that the desks or table can be used to get further up and out of the window.

  • Characters who are able to get high enough, via the ability to fly, or clumbcan climb out of the window successfully by succeeding on a [[/check acrobatics 17]] check. Only characters of size Small or smaller are small enough to fit through and can make the attempt.

    • If the check is failed, the character tumbles through the window and lands outside on the balcony, taking [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] and [[/damage 1d6 slashing]] damage.

Getting Out of the Guest Bedroom: The Door

The room in which the party is restrained is not far from where guests at the party are enjoying a quiet conversation.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check, characters can clearly hear the sounds of talking on the other side of the door.

  • With a successful [[/check strength 17]] check, characters can bang on the door loudly enough for the guests outside to hear them.

    • With a success of 3 or more, characters break through the door lock and the door swings open into the hallway.

  • Once characters have made it through the door, the guests around them will question their presence. Characters can convince the guests that they are there for good reason with a [[/check persuasion 16]] check. If they fail the check, one of the guests informs the guards that they are snooping around, and their newly cleared suspicion level raises to low.

Guest Bedroom 2.name: Guest Bedroom 2
Guest Bedroom 2.text:
Access to Guest Bedroom 2

Access to Guest Bedroom 2 is restricted at all times. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

A fairly generic guest bedroom, which is much less lush that Hephiss' and appears a bit claustrophobic.

Items In Storage

If the party has been detained in Guest Bedroom 1, all of their inventory has been placed in Guest Bedroom 2.

Retrieving Seized Items

The room can be entered from the makeshift stairway on the West Wraparound Balcony, or via the door. If entered via the door, characters must either succeed on a [[/check stealth 17]] check to enter without any of the party guests knowing or on a [[/check deception 17]] check to convince the strangers that they have good reason to go into the off-limites room.

Antechamber.name: Antechamber
Antechamber.text:
Access to Antechamber

Access to the Antechamber varies. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.5MKbu1BthiAQEyaf#manor-access]{Manor Access} for more on access levels.)

  • Pre-Gala: Open to Decorators, Restricted to Gardeners and Kitchen Staff.

  • Gala: Open to Guests.

Locating Funar Cevher

See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY#locating-funar-cevher]{Locating Funar Cevher} for details. If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is in the vicinity. This is the baseline result when using the Locator Rod in and around Marlstone Manor.

Pre-Gala

Though it is open to the floor below, there are spots in this hidden nook where i almost seems as if you are in your own small corner of the manor, hidden away from prying eyes. Nearby, you can hear run a faint murmur from the room to the west, though the words are indistinct.

Listening In

If there are staff in the room, characters can move close enough to the door to Hephiss' Bedroom to eavesdrop, or distract them as follows:

  • With a successful [[/check deception 17]] check, the party can tell the staff they are needed elsewhere or there is an emergency.

  • Any character carrying an item that might cause a stain can spill it on a member of the staff with a successful [[/check sleightofhand 17]] check.

With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check, characters who are standing against the wall can identify the voice as being Hephiss Wandren and hear a few words - tonight, experiment, and Funar.

  • With a successful [[/check insight 17]] check, the party has the sense that the words are being said in a self-congratulatory manner.

  • With a success of 3 or more, characters can hear all of what Hephiss is saying.

    You're going to wow them all tonight, Hephiss. And tomorrow, back to the experiments. You will figure out what he knows and use it to your advantage. And maybe something you create could be the way to get rid of that pesky Funar.

At The Gala

Two pairs of strangers whisper in a corners of the room, as if on a date in the middle of a party, but while the couple at the back of the room lean towards each other with affection, the one standing by the door gesture angrily in each other's direction, locked in some kind of private war.

The Bickering Couple

The couple standing by the door to Hephiss' bedroom are deep in an argument about whether to go down to the lower level and dance. With a successful [[/check persuasion 17]], the party can join the conversation, steering them towards either a calm resolution to go dance (clearing them from the room) or a fierce argument (using them as a distraction).

At The Gala

If the party is in full swing with no major incident, guests gather here in groups for quieter conversation.

Though the music from the band below can still be heard here, it is slightly hushed, and snatches of conversation can be easily picked out from the various small groups of Ordani dignitaries sitting around the small tables, mostly about the general quality of other people's attire, whether the Hallows is up to the new challenges in the city, and whether anyone will dare to tell Hephiss Wandren that she's really not that great an artist.

If the party has caused a major physical disruption (fire, smoke, stampede, etc.), the crowd reacts in panic:

You can hear gasps and small yelps from the crowd on the veranda as they back away from the main floor, voices overlapping and growing in volume. Though it is hard to pick out individual words in the chaos, the sentiment is clear - worry, confusion, and concern about what might happen next.

The guests on the veranda have grown quiet, their conversations dropped to little more than a whisper, as everyone leans towards the nearby voice as if it will help them hear what exactly is happening more clearly.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

This area walkthrough provides a guide of the "Toothbreaker Hideout", a landmark located within @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.0RX8vLjKjRjf3JSj]{The Concourse}, which is encountered during the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1]{The Expedition Challenge}.

In the below gazetteer entry for The Concourse district, this location is described as the "Concourse Hideout".

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.0RX8vLjKjRjf3JSj inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The following gameplay features apply to the Toothbreaker Hideout area unless specifically stated otherwise in a specific room description.

Sound

The Waterworks feature a constant low roar of flowing water, cascading waterfalls, and echoing sounds that resonate through the tunnels. As a consequence, hearing in this environment is more challenging. The Toothbreakers talk loudly and boisterously to each other, and the hubbub of their conversations further drowns out other sounds.

  • Sounds of combat can only be heard within 30 feet of their origin, and they are muffled completely beyond the stone walls of a room if its doors are closed.

  • Characters in this area have @Advantage[2] to any [[/check stealth]] skill check to avoid being heard.

  • The verbal components of spells can be enunciated quietly enough such that they do not attract attention.

Alarm Bells

The Toothbreakers use a rudimentary system of alarm bells to alert each other to any trouble throughout the hideout. Scattered throughout the complex are wall-mounted bells that, if rung, emit an audible alarm that is heard by other Toothbreakers within a 60 foot radius who have a direct line of hearing towards the source of the alarm, and by Toothbreakers within a 30 foot radius otherwise.

  • Ringing one of these alarm bells during Combat requires using an Actionspending 3 Action.

  • An alarm bell can be silently disabled outside of Combat to render it unusable.

Interactive Element

The alarm bells are interactive objects which are usable by the Gamemaster. They can be rung or disabled according to the party's actions!

Illumination

The exterior areas of the map are exposed to direct sun and moonlight and follow typical expectations for outdoor areas.

Most interior areas of the waterworks are illuminated by torches or lanterns which create bright or dim light. In some larger chambers, apertures in the ceiling high above permit external illumination to shine through, creating additional areas of dim light. Otherwise the waterworks are un-illuminated and entirely dark.

Terrain

Areas of solid floor within the waterworks are treated as normal terrain. The water of the canals moves slowly and the canals are 10 feet deep, within the canals standard rules for swimming apply.

Flowing Currents

During combat, any creature that does not have a Swim speed and begins its turn in the water of the canals (either at the surface or submerged) is immediately moved 10 feet in the direction of the flowing current. This movement may provoke attacks of opportunitycause unsafe disengagement.

Keys and Locked Doors

Several different denominations of keys that restrict access within the hideout:

  • @UUID[Item.DtffHxTR7BB6ogGT]{Toothbreaker Security Key}

  • @UUID[Item.g1iWZuiQq4snjmmZ]{Toothbreaker Prison Key}

  • @UUID[Item.okV1Ejy1uuRz7LvP]{Toothbreaker Planning Key}

  • @UUID[Item.YksTyoJCNfAj7oN5]{Toothbreaker Throneroom Key}

  • @UUID[Item.hqyjHK9tr04V7F2Y]{Raster's Keyring}

Elevation

The interior of the waterworks is mostly flat ground (elevation 0), the staircases depicted are cosmetic and do not cause mechanically impactful changes in elevation. The surface of the canals is mechanically level with the stone floors and they are 10 feet deep.

Several canals flow towards an outlet into a deep central cistern. The water within that central cistern is 100 feet below.

The Central Cistern

A creature that is pushed or conveyed by the water towards the edge of the cistern may make a [[/save str 14]][[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check to grasp a secure handhold and avoid being swept over the brink. Creatures falling from the waterworks into the cistern take only half the normal falling damage that would occur from a fall of 100 feet.

There is no direct method for a character who has fallen into the cistern to return to the Waterworks aside from following a labyrinthine network of lower tunnels out of the complex and returning to an accessible entrance. This process consumes 1 hour of time.

Two of the canals outlet into great waterfalls that cascade down to the exterior city 200 feet below.

Exterior Waterfalls

A character that is pushed or conveyed by the water towards the precipice of an exterior waterfall may make a [[/save strength 14]][[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check to grasp a secure handhold and avoid being swept over the brink.

Creatures who fall from this height suffer the full effects of falling damage from a height of 200 feet.

Enemies

This area is the base of operations for the Toothbreaker gang and is full of their members. At most times, the following enemies are encountered here in the provided approximate number:

  • 30 @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thug}

  • 4 @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI]{Toothbreaker Scaletamer}

  • 8 @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]{Scalemaw}

  • @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn}

Significantly Outnumbered

Because of the large number of adversaries in this area, an uncontrolled assault is likely to be deadly. The party would be well advised to use stealth or guile to avoid direct confrontation where possible.

Resting

It is not possible to take a Long Rest within this area without being detected. A Short Rest is only possible in a few specific rooms which mention this as part of their location details.

Fleeing

Should the party need to flee the area, they may do so by retreating to the main @UUID[.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4], the @UUID[.3KktScTw3O1mplzH], or via the@UUID[.srnlviYxNr0FAcHl]{Canals} to the north or southeast of the map, or in truly desperate fashion by jumping out of one of the waterfall outlets to the south of the area.

Captured

If the party is subdued in combat, they may awaken from an unconscious state as captives held within the cages of the @UUID[.OC1tIVg2iiqHZGFg]. Raster and his gang will use captives for sport as fighters in the @UUID[.L15tw2cLjKIAlbup]{Cistern Bloodring}. A party that finds themselves in such a dire circumstance may attempt a desperate escape or hope for allies to come to their rescue.

Enemy Tactics

The enemies in the hideout typically employ the following tactics in combat.

@Embed[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB inline]

Toothbreaker Thug Tactics

In combat, the @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thugs} will switch between their @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB.Item.DovJBdPuoeJcB3ba]{Greatclub} and @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB.Item.UOAm2cIykoDiodsL]{Light Crossbow} depending on the situation, preferring crossbow shots unless their enemy is engaged.

When confronted in melee combat, the Toothbreakers will rely on their strength and athleticism to Grapple their targets, rendering them vulnerable to the @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB.Item.vehfoYMQQ1dmMEPM]{Gang Grappler} feature they all share.

@Embed[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI inline]

Toothbreaker Scaletamer Tactics

The more powerful @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI]{Toothbreaker Scaletamers} fight in a similar way to their lesser gang-mates, but are more dangerous because of their superior weaponry and their @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI.Item.p8LeNEEKXR84EII7]{Multiattack} feature. The Scaletamers will always use @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI.Item.LeyAV8wshu8bnqql]{Command Scalemaw} on their turn if there is a Scalemaw nearby to direct.

If the tide of combat turns against the Toothbreakers and they become @Condition[broken], they will tactically retreat and seek out allies to reinforce them or raise the alarm to call for help.

@Embed[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs inline]

Scalemaw Tactics

The Scalemaw here are well trained and will prefer attacking any target that a Scaletamer has designated with their @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI.Item.LeyAV8wshu8bnqql]{Command Scalemaw} feature. Otherwise they will attack the nearest adversary, particularly favoring any target that is close to water.

The Scalemaw attack viciously with @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs.Item.jphDRpn2W5GcC6sM]{Multiattack}, and if succesful with their @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs.Item.oBEQdx6fnOgy15s3]{Bite} attack will immediately utilize @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs.Item.JR9bbX56sLneTNhd]{Abduct} to retreat with that creature in tow. If they can reach water they will submerge with their grappled foe.

Scalemaw are ferocious and will not retreat from combat even if they seem to be in mortal perileven if they become @Condition[broken].

Tactical Options

There are a few special tactical options that the party may employ against the Toothbreakers which are useful for Gamemasters to be aware of before playing this area.

Mutagenic Serum

The Scalemaw react badly to the @UUID[Item.O59rdBzHOc7VJypf]{Gleaming Distillation} which can be obtained from the Bar. If this serum is injected into a Scalemaw via syringe, it will send them into a prolonged berserk state, turning them against their Toothbreaker Scaletamers.

Raster's Allergy

Raster has a severe allergy to @UUID[Item.cmwF3TBL4CpMKgsK]{Mudflisk}, a bottom-dwelling shelled fish that lives in Ordain's canals. It is possible to learn about this allergy from a healing house document in @UUID[.LHzFS3kEmRrHwfh2].

Mudflisk can be obtained elsewhere in Ordain or by draining the @UUID[.1H1fv6fUFK0T82s8]. Raster's meal being prepared in the @UUID[.eNBWoxp3VTQLf6HY] can be poisoned with Mudflisk, causing Raster to asphyxiate.

Raster's Habits

Raster sleeps from 1am to 9am in his locked bedroom. Otherwise he is found in his throne room. While in his chambers he is vulnerable. Chambers can be accessed by picking the lock or breaking down the damaged northern wall.

Challenging Raster

Raster can be challenged to single combat in the Bloodring if the party is victorious in each of the other Bloodring battles.

Canal Path.name: Canal Path
Canal Path.text:
A narrow footpath here overlooks a large canal that flows southwest from Koto Springs into the River Destine at the boundary between The Concourse and Flotsam districts.

Foot traffic seems rare along this path, and you notice signs of neglect where mounds of refuse have accumulated over the course of time. Periodically, a gondola or other small vessel passes by on the waterway, but their passengers do not pay you any heed.

Further down this path, the stone embankment is marked by the presence of a lonely culvert, but rusted metal bars prevent entrance. No placard or sign suggests any particular purpose of what lies within.

Locked Gate

A locked gate of metal bars prevents access into the tunnels via the culvert here. It is possible to see through it, although there is no source of light in the tunnel beyond, nor is there any sound of activity.

This gate is opened using a @UUID[Item.DtffHxTR7BB6ogGT]{Toothbreaker Security Key}. A copy of this key is carried by each of the @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI]{Toothbreaker Scaletamers}, and an additional key can be found on the table in the @UUID[.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4]{Security Checkpoint}.

  • The lock can be picked quietly through a successful [[/tool dc=16 ability=dexterity tool=thief]] check[[/skillCheck stealth 16]] check with thieves' tools.

  • The gate can be forced open with a successful [[/skill athletics 19]][[/skillCheck athletics 19]] check. Use of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCrowbar0000]{Crowbar} or a similar method of leverage grants @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Characters with [[/skill insight 13 passive]][[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] or [[/knowledge machines]] recognize that attempts to force the gate open will be loud as the metal is rusted and its screeches are likely to echo throughout the passageway.

Application of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagOil00000000]{Oil}, use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGrease0000]{Grease} spell, use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSilence000]{Silence} spell, or other similar techniques can be used to quiet the sound and avoid alerting the nearby guards.

Application of oil or other lubricant can be used to quiet the sound and avoid alerting nearby guards.

Alerting the Guards

If the gate is forced open without using precautionary measures to suppress its sound, the two @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thugs} in @UUID[.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4] are alerted and call for backup. They prepare for possible attack, but do not leave their checkpoint or unlock its door. If 10 minutes pass without further incident, they will send a scout out through the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.mUkF6TYfwreAm7ho]{Culvert Entrance} to investigate.

Distant City.name: Distant City
Distant City.text:
The sprawling cinnabar rooftops of Ordain spread out to the south. Powerful waterfalls cascade out of the waterworks, plummeting two-hundred feet to splash into the headwaters of a new canal system below.

There is an atypical quiet to the city here. The rooftops show obvious signs of disrepair and an unexpected scarcity of lights flicker in their windows.

Despite this, there is great beauty in this view. From an elevated position, you can see clearly across the expanding cityscape — its plateaus and valleys roll into the distance as the crowning dome of the Ordinate rises to meet your eye in the center of the sweeping urban vista.

If a creature or character were to be swept over the edge of the waterfall to plummet towards the city below, they would suffer likely-fatal damage.

Exterior Waterfalls

A character that is pushed or conveyed by the water towards the precipice of an exterior waterfall may make a [[/save strength 14]][[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check to grasp a secure handhold and avoid being swept over the brink. Creatures who fall from this height suffer the full effects of falling damage from a height of 200 feet.

Concealed Dock.name: Concealed Dock
Concealed Dock.text:
The canal water slows to a lazy ebb as it laps against the moss-covered timber of a furtive wooden dock. An over-laden rowboat is tied to the southwestern corner of the dock, where it bobs quietly with the constant sloshing of water.

On the north side of the docks, a small wooden chair leans back against the wall with someone slumped inside its rickety confines. A table next to the chair is decorated with a smoking pipe and a few empty glass vials.

A Sleeping Sentry

A solitary @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thug} is asleep at his post here. Any loud noises or physical disturbance within the area will awaken him, but he otherwise sleeps soundly due to the sedative effects of a Mutagenic Serum that he recently consumed.

Raising the Alarm

If the guard is awoken and alert to intruders, he will immediately ring the alarm bell on the wall in this area to alert the Toothbreakers in the @UUID[.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4]{Guardroom} and @UUID[.g97R0OPGQueRR4Jt]{Interrogation Room}.

Sneaking Through

The party can move through this area without waking the sentry provided they succeed on a group [[/skill stealth 10]][[/skillCheck stealth 10 group]] check.

Characters with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who succeed on a [[/skill perception 12]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notice the gleam of a brass key dangling from the guards belt. This is a @UUID[Item.7ooLqw3jKJ9aUm20]{Toothbreaker Storage Key}, which opens the locked door to @UUID[.zQskvNsAOLJfPkYX]{Contraband Storage}.

  • A successful [[/skill sleightOfHand 13]][[/skillCheck stealth 13]] check allows a character to steal the key off the thug's belt without alerting him.

Characters who succeed on an [[/skill investigation 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check to inspect the guard's post notice several empty or broken vials. on the round table or wedged between dock planks below. Some are fully dried of whatever contents they previously held. It seems clear that this guard is a habitual consumer of whatever substance is packaged in these vials.

  • Characters should be invited to roll a [[/skill investigation]][[/skillCheck society]] check to identify the substance, but success is impossible unless the party has completed [[/eventState chain2Headwaters]] and discovered the distilled blaze being manufactured there.

The Loaded Boat

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.phbmobRowboat000]{Rowboat} that is tied to the dock here is loaded with a mundane assortment of wares: foodstuffs, common adventuring supplies, and a footlocker full of empty glass vials that seem used.

Storage Door

The western door to the adjoining storage room is locked, and can be opened with the @UUID[Item.7ooLqw3jKJ9aUm20]{Toothbreaker Storage Key}.

Additionally, the lock can be picked by succeeding on a [[/tool thief ability=dexterity 13]][[/skillCheck stealth 13]] check, or the door can be forced open with a successful [[/skill athletics 15]][[/skillCheck athlestics 15]] check.

Contraband Storage.name: Contraband Storage
Contraband Storage.text:
This cluttered chamber is packed to the brim with a chaotic assortment of spoiled goods and ramshackle equipment, stacked around the room in a haphazard fashion. A large shelf on the northern wall — which at one point offered some hope of organization — has collapsed, its wood utterly rotted from the pervasive moisture in the local air. It's evident that this room sees regular use, but no effort has been made to restore order here for quite some time.

Searching the Storage

Any character who searches the room and succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]][[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check is able to locate an unlocked lockbox on top of a crate, containing six @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPotionofHea]{Potions of Healing} wrapped tightly in burlap.

  • Result of 18+Critical Success. The character notices a second lockbox among the wrecked shelving, which contains 3 @UUID[Item.hMeljYMb7OxbfNKv]{Iolite} gemstones and [[/award 200sp]].

Safe Resting

Although it sees regular use, this room is only visited occasionally by the Toothbreakers, and as-needed. Furthermore, it can be locked from the inside, making it one of the few safe places in the hideout where the characters can benefit from an uninterrupted Short RestRecovery.

Northern Hallway

When exiting this chamber via the southernmost door, the characters will overhear the following muffled dialog coming from behind the closed door of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.g97R0OPGQueRR4Jt]{Interrogation Room} across the hallway:

As you make your way into the hall, you notice the muffled sound of a masculine voice behind another door to the south.

… you should have told us sooner, but now it's too late, dear Fen. Far too late.

A second, high-pitched voice interrupts the first with a panic-stricken tone:

No! Wait! I can still be …

Panic turns to pain as the second voice screams out with unmistakable agony from some unknown source. This wailing continues unabated for several seconds until a wet gargling overtakes it, and all falls conspicuously silent.

Aside from the obvious ramifications of this exchange, the party is unable to deduce anything further without opening the door to the @UUID[.g97R0OPGQueRR4Jt]{Interrogation Room} itself.

Interrogation Room.name: Interrogation Room
Interrogation Room.text:
The chamber before you presents a horrific scene … A rusty cage hangs from a gibbet near the southern wall, suspended by chains. An ichor-stained table near the center of the room is decorated with instruments of torture. And a dead man is bound to a wooden chair, covered in his own blood and vomit.

Behind the chair, a Toothbreaker clad in decorative bone armor leans over this ill-fated prisoner, torture tools firmly in-hand. Furthermore, a large reptilian beasts lurks at the victim's feet, sniffing hungrily at the air as its four crimson eyes survey the blood-soaked corpse.

There are two primary circumstances in which the party will find themselves in this room. Most likely they are trespassing in the hideout, in which case they will be treated as interlopers and attacked. Alternatively, they may have been taken prisoner by the Toothbreakers and sent to Kierelin for the painful extraction of information. In either case, combat here is highly likely.

@Embed[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI label="Kierelin the Interrogator"]

@Embed[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]

Fighting the Interrogator

Kierelin is a @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI]{Toothbreaker Scaletamer}, and is accompanied by a highly-trained @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]{Scalemaw} companion. They follow the tactics described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#enemy-tactics]{Enemy Tactics}.

Kierelin's Key

Kierelin is in possession of the @UUID[Item.g1iWZuiQq4snjmmZ]{Toothbreaker Prison Key}.

This room is sufficiently isolated, and has no alarm bell. It's unlikely that combat here will alert other Toothbreakers in chambers nearby. If the characters take a closer look at the interrogator's recent victim in the chair, read the following aloud:

The victim in the chair appears to be a human man whose once-fashionable garb is badly torn and thoroughly sodden with blood. A multitude of wounds confirm the obvious: this man is dead following his torture at the hands of the Toothbreakers.

The Tortured Victim

Any character who examines the body with a successful [[/skill medicine 12]][[/skillCheck medicine 12]] check is able to conclude that the man is very recently deceased; the body is still warm, and the blood in some of his wounds has yet to coagulate.

  • Result of 17+Critical Success You identify that among the cuts, and lashes the cause of death was a final deep laceration to the side of the neck.

Any character who succeeds on an [[/skill perception 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check is able to spot a necklace tucked beneath the victim's tunic. The necklace features a small silver medallion, upon which is embossed a large key with butterfly wings:

  • The symbol is that of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows} which can be recognized by a character with [[/culture emberOrdani]] or a successful [[/skill history 15]][[/skillCheck society 15]] check.

The tortured victim was named Eltien Fen, a representative of the Hallows that was subsequently captured and interrogated by the Toothbreakers. More information about Eltien's identity and purpose is contained in the letter found in the @UUID[.BQ9jCeU6YqinlEf8]{Tea Room}.

Being Interrogated

Should a narrative need arise for the Toothbreakers to interrogate the party, you might involve Kierelin in that gameplay sequence.

Rules are not provided for how such a sequence would transpire, and the themes involved are delicate ones — themes you should only explore using caution with transparent consent from all players at the table.

Guardroom.name: Guardroom
Guardroom.text:
This squat, semi-circular chamber appears to be a fortified chokepoint that those who enter the hideout must pass through. A semi-permanent barricade flanks the thick metallic door, which is securely bolted in place. A square table on the far side of the room is strewn with food, papers, weapons, and other clutter. Meanwhile, a large metal bell on the southern wall gleams in the torchlight.

Toothbreakers

There are two @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thugs} stationed as guards in this room at most times.

Raising the Alarm

If there is any sign of trouble, the guards will immediately ring the alarm bell, alerting their allies in the @UUID[.6SwFTuVrUIds5FBO]{Barracks} nearby.

Guardroom Clutter

If the characters search the room, they'll find meager food and drink on the table here, along with a few miscellaneous items scattered about:

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepDagger0000]{Dagger}

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepHeavyCross]{Heavy Crossbow} and 12 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbamoBolts00000]{Bolts}

  • [[/award 6gp 7sp 4cp]]

  • An envelope stamped with a wax seal, already opened and empty of contents. The seal bears the iconic symbol of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows} which can be recognized by any character with [[/culture emberOrdani]] or with a successful [[/skill history 15]][[/skillCheck society 15]] check.

The letter was brought here by Eltien Fen, a representative of the Hallows. Eltien was captured after his arrival, and is currently being brutally interrogated in the @UUID[.g97R0OPGQueRR4Jt]{Interrogation Room}. The missing contents of the letter can be found in the @UUID[.BQ9jCeU6YqinlEf8]{Tea Room}.

Barracks.name: Barracks
Barracks.text:
This makeshift barracks is lined with several bunks and weapon racks. A pair of mess tables in the center of the chamber are covered with a cluttered assortment of food, personal effects, and games of strategy.

Unless the party members are being escorted through this area as guests or prisoners, they'll be treated as trespassers and immediately attacked by the trio of Toothbreaker Thugs who dwell here.

@Embed[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB count=3]

Toothbreakers

The Toothbreaker Thugs here follow the tactics described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#enemy-tactics]{Enemy Tactics}.

Raising the Alarm

An alarm bell is mounted just outside the barracks in the western hallway towards the @UUID[.L15tw2cLjKIAlbup]{Cistern Bloodring}. If under attack, the Toothbreaker Thug nearest to the door will break away to ring the alarm. which will draw the attention of all their nearby allies in the Bloodring as well as in the @UUID[.idxgwrjrPr9wBh4V]{Planning Room} to the south.

Once combat in this room has concluded, the party may wish to investigate it's contents.

Toothbreaker Plunder

Spending a minute to search the room reveals the following items of interest:

  • An assortment of 12 mundane weapons.

  • Loose coin including [[/award 7gp 24sp 36cp]]

  • A pair of mundane Scalemaw Boots crafted from cured Scalemaw leather, sized for a Kivahr wearer. The boots are in good condition and worth [[/award 15gp]].

Locked Door

The southern door to the @UUID[.idxgwrjrPr9wBh4V]{Planning Room} is locked. It can be unlocked by the Toothbreakers inside the room or from the outside using a @UUID[Item.okV1Ejy1uuRz7LvP]{Toothbreaker Planning Key} which is in possession of Vaafo the Scaletamer in @UUID[.TP5eHaP4OD2xBHaw]{Scalemaw Training} or using Raster's keyring. The lock can be picked with a successful [[/check tool=thief dc=25]][[/skillCheck stealth 25]] check.

Prison.name: Prison
Prison.text:
Four cruel gibbet cages are arranged around the room, their rusted bars reflect a dull gleam in the flickering torchlight. A befouled washtub sits in the center of the room and the scene is presided over by a solitary Toothbreaker guard who sits upon a bench against the western wall. An alarm bell is mounted to the wall just overhead and leather whip is coiled at the guard's feet.

Imprisoned

It is possible the party arrives in this area as a result of being imprisoned. If so, take a moment to position each character inside one of the vacant cages.

Each cage is locked by a secure metal padlock. The @UUID[Item.g1iWZuiQq4snjmmZ]{Toothbreaker Prison Key} opens these locks, which is in possession of Kierelin the Interrogator in the @UUID[.g97R0OPGQueRR4Jt], Ukkfal the Ringmaster in the @UUID[.L15tw2cLjKIAlbup]{Cistern Bloodring}, or on the master keyring of @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn} himself. The guard in this room does not have the keys.

Forced to Fight

Each day, the characters are withdrawn from the cages and pitted in a sequence of fights in the @UUID[.L15tw2cLjKIAlbup]{Cistern Bloodring}. See that location page for details on those staged fights. As long as the prisoners are compliant, they are provided with rations and allowed to rest in between these battles.

Escaping

Characters held in this prison are detained indefinitely until they escape or perish. Specific rules are not provided for how the party might escape, it is up to the characters and the Gamemaster to improvise a suitable gambit by which to obtain their freedom.

Without adequate tools, it is not possible to pick the lock of the cage, however a character could attempt to force the cage open with a successful [[/skill athletics 25]][[/skillCheck athletics 25]] check.

Non-Compliance

If the party attempts escape, is particularly provocative towards the guard, or does not comply with the guard's instructions they will be denied rest and rations, leading to escalating &Reference[exhaustion]@Condition[exhaustion the longer they remain imprisoned.

If the party enters this area not as prisoners, they immediately provoke the Toothbreaker guard to sound the alarm.

Prisoners

If the player characters are not prisoners here, the cages are instead occupied by other captives that the Toothbreakers have abducted. The three prisoners in clockwise order from the north-west are:

  1. Sleger Endrik, an Arcturian human woodworker (he/him).

  2. Vytho Whitecrest, a Cascilian human sailor (he/him).

  3. Muse Kindry, an Ordani human ceramicist (she/her).

The prisoners are in varying states of malnutrition and sleep deprivation. They are each terrified of the Toothbreakers and their Scalemaws and will not attempt escape unless the party can assure them that the Toothbreakers between the Prison and the exit have been eliminated.

  • Characters with [[/skill insight 15 passive format=long]][[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] notice that all four prisoners are human which is statistically unusual given the cosmopolitan makeup of Ordain.

  • If asked, the prisoners speak of another captive who was brought through recently, an Ordani named Eltien Fen who was taken away hours ago and has not returned.

Prisoner Knowledge

The prisoners — as written — know little else of value to the party, but they can be a useful mechanism for handing out hints to the players if you want to direct their attention towards any element of gameplay in the hideout.

Feel free for the prisoners to have witnessed or overheard something that could be useful to the players.

Flow Control.name: Flow Control
Flow Control.text:
This circular room initially seems to surve little purpose aside from facilitating access between areas, but upon entering you notice water running through a chute in the middle of the floor and two large metal wheels connected to pipes on the southern wall.

Sluice Controls

The two wheels to the south of the room control the sluice gates north of this room and underneath @UUID[.TP5eHaP4OD2xBHaw]{Scalemaw Training}. The valves are kept in the open position as the Toothbreakers have no reason to inhibit the flow of water through the hideout.

If the party wishes to close these valves, either purposefully or simply out of curiosity regarding their function they may do so. They are both rusted and partially stuck from years of disuse. Turning each valve requires a [[/skill athletics 18]][[/skillCheck athletics 18]] check.

  • Attempting this check regardless of the outcome emits piercing screech that alerts enemies in adjoining areas unless both doors to this room are closed.

  • Application of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagOil00000000]{Oil}, use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGrease0000]{Grease} spell, use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSilence000]{Silence} spell, or other similar techniques can be used to quieten the sound and avoid alerting the nearby guards.

  • Application of oil or other lubricant can be used to quieten the sound and avoid alerting nearby guards.

Interactive Element

The flow control valves are interactive objects which are only usable by the Gamemaster since a check is required to turn them. When both wheels are turned, the water from the western canal will drain!

If both sluice controls are activated, then the water flow from the north and northeast is stopped and the @UUID[.1H1fv6fUFK0T82s8]{Western Canals} will empty. Read the following aloud:
