After a tremendous screech of protest, the sluice gates shut with a heavy thunk and the sound of turbulent water subsides. The inflow of water from the north slows to a crawl, and then a trickle, and then solitary drips as the chute beneath your feet becomes drained of water.

Draining the Western Canals

Emptying the canals is not especially useful to the party, but it does have two potential benefits:

  • It exposes a hidden @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]{Scalemaw} who is swimming within the canal water there.

  • It provides an opportunity to collect @UUID[Item.cmwF3TBL4CpMKgsK]{Mudflisk} from the silt in the canal bed, if the party is aware to look for it.

Investigating the Drainage

Toothbreakers who notice that the canal has been drained will recognize that it is unusual and make their way towards this area to investigate the cause. If they encounter the party they will be immediately hostile, otherwise they will restore water flow after approximately 10 minutes of diagnosing the issue.

Scalemaw Training.name: Scalemaw Training
Scalemaw Training.text:
This octagonal room reverberates with the constant churning of water through a sluice beneath its stone floor — a floor covered in matted straw that smells sodden and unclean.

The chamber is decorated with numerous training dummies mounted on pivoting bases, partially suspended from the ceiling by chains. A stout metal cage at the northern end of the room appears large enough to hold a rask, and a feeding trough nearby is nearly full of raw meat and offal. The smell of this fleshy matter is rancid enough to sting your nostrils and turn your stomach.

An alarm bell is mounted on the southern wall, next to an open passage that compliments the closed doors leading east and west.

@Embed[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI label="Vaafo the Scaletamer"]

@Embed[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]

@Embed[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]

Fascination With Scalemaws

If the party arrives under escort from the Toothbreaker Thugs serving as the @UUID[.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4]{Guardroom} guards, Vaafo will reluctantly interrupt his training activities to speak with the characters and indulge their feigned fascination with Scalemaws.

During the conversation, the party must succeed on a [[/skill deception 15]] group[[/skillCheck deception 15 group]] check or Vaafo will see through their feigned interest.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberWaerd]], [[/knowledge beasts]], or [[/knowledge monsters]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

If the party is successful, Vaafo will demonstrate a few tricks that showcase his rapport with the Scalemaw. Soon enough, Vaafo will suggest that the party feed the beast with a knowing smile in his eye.

  • Characters with [[/skill insight 15 passive format=long]][[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] can correctly infer that Vaafo expects this feeding to go poorly and is eager to see whether or not the visitors provoke the Scalemaw.

A character who is feeling brave can feed the Scalemaw with a successful [[/skill animalHandling 17]][[/skillCheck survival 17]] check.

  • If successful, Vaafo is impressed and allows the party to linger, eventually losing interest in them as he returns to training the beast. Vaafo suggests they head down to the bar for a drink, but does not escort the group — granting them some momentary freedom to explore.

  • On a failure, Vaafo intervenes before the Scalemaw attacks, but will insist that it's time for the party to leave. If they refuse or resist, Vaafo will immediately doubt their ruse and become hostile.

Vaafo's Key

Vaafo is in possession of a @UUID[Item.okV1Ejy1uuRz7LvP]{Toothbreaker Planning Key}, which can be taken from his body or pickpocketed during his Scalemaw training demonstration with a successful [[/skill sleightOfHand 20]][[/skillCheck stealth 20]] check. Failure on this check results in Vaafo immediately becoming hostile to the party.

If the party arrives to this area without a Toothbreaker escort, or if they antagonize Vaafo during conversation, the brash Scaletamer becomes hostile and attacks.

Toothbreakers

Vaafo and his allies follow the tactics described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#enemy-tactics]{Enemy Tactics}.

Raising the Alarm

An alarm bell is mounted on the southern wall of this room. If provoked, Vaafo or his Toothbreaker Thug ally will move quickly to ring the alarm.

Collapsed Quarters.name: Collapsed Quarters
Collapsed Quarters.text:
There are several rooms off a narrow canalside hallway that have collapsed into from rubble, their ceilings partially caved in. The rubble is slick with moisture and overgrown with vines and mushrooms which thrive in the damp climate of the waterworks. No light or sound comes from within and it seems clear that the Toothbreakers do not frequent this area.

Hidden Stash

The northern collapsed room is only accessible by traversing the rubble through the southern side. If explored, the party discovers a footlocker stashed amidst the rubble. Inside the footlocker is the following treasure:

  • [[/award 42gp 17sp]] in loose coin.

  • One set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulLeatherwor]{Leatherworker's Tools}

  • Four yards of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.tradegoods.Item.jad5oFMDv21mPvJP]{Silk}

  • A leather quivver containing 10 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgAmmunition12o]{Arrow +1}

Safe Resting

This area is one of the few in the hideout that affords the opportunity to benefit from an uninterrupted Short RestRecovery.

Coming Through!

The weakened wall on the south side of the room can be broken through, with a succesful [[/skill athletics 17]][[/skillCheck athletics 17]] check, opening a hole and spilling debris out into @UUID[.LHzFS3kEmRrHwfh2].

Raster's Throne Room.name: Raster's Throne Room
Raster's Throne Room.text:
This large chamber has been turned into a throne room with a large trestle table down its center. Situated at the western end of the table, the throne itself is constructed from several heavy stone slabs and is adorned with bone and leather ornamentation.

On the southern wall, two large windows look out over the rolling Ordain cityscape, its tapestry of crimson rooftops stretching into the horizon.

Locked Doors

The doors to Raster's Throne Room are locked. Two @UUID[Item.YksTyoJCNfAj7oN5]{Toothbreaker Throne Room Keys} can be found throughout the hideout: one held by Taamsin the Mastermind in the @UUID[.idxgwrjrPr9wBh4V]{Planning Room}, and another in the possession of Raster himself.

@Embed[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]

@Embed[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB count=2]

@Embed[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs count=2]

Raster Thorn

Raster is found here at nearly all times. Outsiders are not often invited to this area as guests, so any incursion into the throne room is almost certain to be treated as a hostile act. If attacked, Raster will immediately brandish weapons and welcome the unexpected challenge.

In combat, Raster moves quickly into melee range to deal brutal strikes (using @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.HXGtjDOvjB1SWgWC]{Multiattack}) with his weapon @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.rMFRvxQdVU7rGj7l]{Spinebite}, which are especially damaging due to his @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.xREXwthThbqpCwSi] feature. If unable to reach melee range, he is tactically astute enough to switch to his @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.dx2ultd9nRLKteSV]{Heavy Crossbow}.

Raster is a Scaletamer, so he will use @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.4twFLDdtibtWmFQ3]{Command Scalemaw} each round to command one of the two Scalemaws which occupy the room. Furthermore, he will be actively on the lookout for one of his Toothbreaker Thug allies to grapple a target so he can exploit his @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.tUgROiRhSkqRHLKM]{Gang Grappler} feature.

When attacked in melee combat, Raster will utilize @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.9cdCelMBZLuK0FWM]{Trap Weapon} against any target capable of making multiple attacks per round. Raster's unquenchable pride prevents him from fleeing from combat; he will fight to the death, even if his life is threatenedMorale is @Condition[broken].

Raising the Alarm

There is an alarm bell on the eastern wall. When combat begins, one of Raster's Toothbreaker Thug allies will move to ring it.

Locked Vault

The door to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.jt4R9vhM3lOFxRMn]{Raster's Vault} on the western wall is locked. The only key is on @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.UHZgyAMxxL3uszH2]{Raster's Keyring}. Alternately, the lock can be picked with a successful [[/check tool=thief dc=25]][[/skillCheck stealth 25]] check.

Cistern Bloodring.name: Cistern Bloodring
Cistern Bloodring.text:
The grand central atrium of the Concourse Hideout is a huge vaulted chamber, the ceiling is nearly 100 feet overhead whic descends into darkness as water cascades from a concentric ring of waterfalls into the depths of the cistern below. In the center of the chamber, a platform stands upon a column of rock, connected by three bridges.

Upon the platform is built a ramshackle arena, tiered wooden bleachers surrounding an octagonal roped ring. Lights are strung overhead to illuminate the arena. An assortment of Toothbreakers or their guests lounge upon the bleachers, calling out encouragement to the combatants who battle in the ring.

Unless the party has been invited into this area as guests or they are escorted as prisoners, they will be treated as trespassers and immediately attacked. There are a large number of Toothbreakers in this area and the arena is overseen by one of Raster's Scaletamer lieutenants named Ukkfal.

@Embed[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI label="Ukkfal the Ringmaster"]

Ukkfal's Key

Taamsin is in possession of the @UUID[Item.g1iWZuiQq4snjmmZ]{Toothbreaker Prison Key} which can be taken from his body or pickpicketed during the chaos of a Bloodring fight with a successful [[/skill sleightOfHand 20]][[/skillCheck stealth 20]] check. Failure on this check immediately turns Ukkfal hostile.

If a character is a combatant fighting in the Bloodring, they can attempt a [[/skill performance 15]][[/skillCheck performance 15]] check to theatrically distract Ukkfal. If this check is successful, the above pickpocket check can be made with @Advantage[2].

Bloodthirsty Spectators

Parties that are invited guests of the Toothbreakers are free to mingle here, spectate on fights, and place bets on their outcomes. Gambling on the Bloodring fights is coordinate in the @UUID[.vlTZOAz7ZlzaTapN]{Bar}.

Bloodring Spectators

The various Toothbreakers here are largely intent on watching the action, but they can be engaged in conversation. Characters succeeding on a [[/skill persuasion 14]][[/skillCheck persuasion 14]] check can glean one of the following pieces of information per attempt.

@Embed[RollTable.hJECLPJNTcYVXoYU rollable inline]

If the party fails this check three times, the Toothbreakers communicate their displeasure to Ukkfal who demands that the party "shut up, or leave".

Toothbreakers

If provoked into combat, the Toothbreakers here will follow the tactics described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#enemy-tactics]{Enemy Tactics}.

Raising the Alarm

The nearest alarm bells to the Bloodring to the east across the bridge towards the @UUID[.6SwFTuVrUIds5FBO]{Barracks}, in the @UUID[.OC1tIVg2iiqHZGFg]{Prison} to the northwest, or in the @UUID[.mQtOym1uGiG7xt5L]{Sparring Alcove} to the southeast.

Forced to Fight

If the party has been taken captive and forced to fight in the Bloodring, the following rules apply.

  • The party must fight in a sequence of blood-sport contests within the arena. For each of the following four fights the party may volunteer a fighter otherwise Ukkfal will select combatants at random.

  • No character may participate in consecutive rounds unless there is no other option. Each challenge has certain special rules that are clearly explained by Ukkfal at the start of the round. Breaking the rules of the encounter is grounds for disqualification.

  • Damage dealt during these fights is not non-lethal and may kill or render unconscious the combatants. The Toothbreakers do not care if fighters lose their lives.

  • If disqualified, the combatant is subdued by Ukkfal and the spectating Toothbreakers. This either leads to a full combat encounter or if the combatant does not resist, they are returned to their prison cell with1 hit point0 Health.

  • There is only sufficient time between fights for the party to perform a short restRecover.

Fight 1 - Bareknuckle Scuffle

In this challenge, a combatant must face off against a single @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thug}. Rules for this fight are:

  • You may wear no weapons, armor, or other equipment.

  • Use of spells or magical abilities is prohibited.

Unarmed Strikes

Ensure that the character has the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbUnarmedStrike]{Unarmed Strike} feature added to their character sheet which is likely their only viable means of attacking.

Fight 2 - Tag Team

In this challenge, a pair of combatants faces off against a pair of @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thug}. Rules for this fight are:

  • Each combatant is provided with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepClub000000]{Club} which is their only permitted weapon. No armor or other equipment is permitted.

  • One combatant on each team must remain outside the ropes while the other combatant remains inside the octagon. As a free action on their turn, a combatant may "tag out" enabling their ally to enter the arena at the beginning of their next turn.

  • Combatants outside the ropes may attack enemies they can reach.

  • Use of spells or magical abilities is prohibited.

Fight 3 - Burnished Hand to Hand

In this challenge, a single combatant must face off against a captured @UUID[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA]{Burnished Hand Protector}. Rules for this fight are:

  • Both combatants may use their full set of equipment.

  • Spells or magical abilities are permitted.

Fight 4 - Scalemaw Duo

In this challenge, a pair of combatants must face off against @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI]{Vaafo the Scaletamer} and a trained @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]{Scalemaw}. Rules for this fight are:

  • All characters may use their full set of equipment.

  • Spells or magical abilities are permitted.

If the party was not victorious in all four challenges, Raster does not view them as worthy adversaries and pays them no attention. The party is left in the prison cages to be turned over as test subjects to @UUID[Actor.8jqTLAW121XrQiTN]{Kaftor Brenk} and the mutagists. They must devise their own means of escape.

Challenging Raster

If the party is victorious in all four of these challenges, Raster Thorn himself challenges the strongest — defined as the character with the greatest Strength attribute — among the party to a direct battle. The challenge is scheduled to take place "tomorrow", and the party is afforded time to long restbenefit from a Full Rest.

@Embed[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]

Raster Thorn

Raster fights using the tactics described in @UUID[.ZEEz2PVd0uRJHL5j].

  • The assembled Toothbreakers recognize that this battle is a traditional Waerd contest of might and martial acumen and they do not interfere.

  • If the party interferes with this duel by taking any action, then the Toothbreakers also join the battle, resulting in an all-out skirmish between both sides.

Defeating Raster within the Bloodring constitutes a shocking and legendary victory for the party. The assembled Toothbreakers watch in stunned silence and take no action to retaliate or stop the party from leaving afterwards.

Raster's Quarters.name: Raster's Quarters
Raster's Quarters.text:
This rectangular room is well cared for and furnished more intentionally than the rest of the hideout. Several prominent trophy skulls line the walls, and the decor — while not matching — produces the cozy feeling of a woodsman's cottage.

The door to this chamber remains locked at all times. @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn} possesses the only key.

Raster's Bedtime

Raster sleeps here from 1am to 9am each day.

If the party seeks to ambush Raster while he sleeps, it is possible for them to break through the adjoining well from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.BBTYndMN9GabSvyO]{Collapsed Quarters}, following the rules described there. Raster employs tactics in combat described in @UUID[.ZEEz2PVd0uRJHL5j].

Risky Resting

The party can risk resting here, if they do so outside of the sleeping hours described above.

The party will doubtless be interested to inspect or plunder Raster's personal belongings.

Raster's Belongings

Upon cursory inspection, the room contains several minor treasures including:

  • [[/award 12gp 14sp]] in loose coin

  • Two finely crafted @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepDagger0000]{Daggers}

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepBattleaxe0]{Battleaxe}

  • One six-foot long Varrol tusk in a display case that weighs 40 pounds and is worth [[/award 120gp]] to an interested merchant.

  • One spare @UUID[Item.YksTyoJCNfAj7oN5]{Toothbreaker Throneroom Key}.

With a thorough and successful[[/skill investigation 13]][[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check the party can find the following additional items of interest scattered around the room:

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfWater]{Potion of Water Breathing}

  • @UUID[Item.VWz9VtVER2QKO1VQ]

  • @UUID[Item.DLOAmiz9ULLPGcjV]

  • @UUID[Item.8lGsP5iqMh6hWg0W]

  • @UUID[Item.5zqHEkFq2a6NANIP]

Filthy Bathroom.name: Filthy Bathroom
Filthy Bathroom.text:
The opulence of this once-proud bathroom chamber has faded, replaced by the squalor of its stained floor and mildew-covered fixtures. If the rank odor here is any indication, this restroom is over-used and under-cleaned. Nevertheless, a grand window on the southern wall overlooks Ordain's endless cityscape with an air of forgotten dignity.

Risky Resting

The party can attempt to rest here, but the endeavor is a risky one. Roll [[/gmroll 1d4]], and on a result of 1, the party's rest is interrupted by a @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thug} entering the chamber to relieve themselves.

Toilet Interrogation

If the party happens to catch a Toothbreaker using the commode, they may seize this opportunity to interrogate this particular thug away from the scrutiny of their criminal allies.

The unfortunate gang member can be interrogated while in this vulnerable circumstance with one or more successful [[/skill intimidation 14]][[/skillCheck intimidation 14]] checks. Each successful check results in the party learning one piece of information from the table below:

@Embed[RollTable.hJECLPJNTcYVXoYU inline rollable]

Planning Room.name: Planning Room
Planning Room.text:
The erudition of this large square chamber feels out of place among the relative squalor of the hideout's other rooms. Surrounded by more than a half-dozen rickety chairs, a huge table at the center of the chamber is decorated with an assortment of maps, plans, and other accoutrements; and three smaller tables line the perimeter of the room like desks, each of them covered in some kind of functional clutter.

There are three Toothbreakers Thugs here, led by one of Raster Thorn's ringleaders, a Toothbreaker known as Taamsin the Mastermind.

@Embed[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB count=3]

@Embed[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI label="Taamsin the Mastermind"]

If the party was escorted here by the guards in the @UUID[.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4]{Guardroom}, they must speak with Taamsin to convince him of their pretended purpose.

Business Propositions

"The Mastermind" is more cunning and insightful than his peers, so convincing Taamsin that the characters are prospective partners or informants for the Toothbreakers is a challenging act of deception.

To persuade the lieutenant of their cause, the party must succeed on a group [[/skill deception 20]][[/skillCheck deception 20 group]] check.

  • Before making this check, characters may attempt a [[/skill persuasion 20]] or [[/skill performance 20]][[/skillCheck persuasion 20]] or [[/skillCheck, performance 20]] check to charm Taamsin. Success provides @Advantage[2] for the subsequent Deception check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]], [[/knowledge trade]], or [[/knowledge intrigue]] are better suited to crafting a proposition and have @Advantage[2] on the Deception check.

  • Taamsin will accept a bribe of [[/award -100gp]] or greater which counts as an automatic success on the Deception check for that player. If the party attempts to bribe Taamsin with any lesser amount, he takes the money but it counts as a failure towards the group Deception check.

If Taamsin can be deceived, he will arrange for the party to meet with @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn} to discuss matters in the @UUID[.BQ9jCeU6YqinlEf8]{Tea Room}, where Raster receives visiting dignitaries.

Taamsin's Key

Taamsin is in possession of a @UUID[Item.YksTyoJCNfAj7oN5]{Toothbreaker Throneroom Key}.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill sleightOfHand 20]][[/skillCheck stealth 20]] check is able to pick Taamsin's pocket to purloin the key. Failure on this check immediately turns Taamsin hostile.

If diplomacy fails, or if the party is caught trespassing in this area, then combat is inevitable.

Toothbreakers

The Toothbreakers here follow the tactics described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#enemy-tactics]{Enemy Tactics}.

Raising the Alarm

There is no alarm bell in this room directly. As long as the party keeps combat contained to this room, it is unlikely to alert other Toothbreakers.

There are two nearby alarms, however: one in the hallway to the north near the @UUID[.6SwFTuVrUIds5FBO]{Barracks}, and another in the small @UUID[.mQtOym1uGiG7xt5L]{Sparring Alcove} to the west. If opportunity allows during combat, one or more Toothbreakers will move away to attempt raising the alarm.

When the room is cleared of Toothbreakers, the party may loot it's contents.

Planning Room Treasure

In addition to the equipment possessed by the Toothbreakers themselves, this room contains:

  • An assortment of 10 simple melee weapons stored in racks around the room.

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepHeavyCross]{Heavy Crossbow} and 13 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbamoBolts00000]{Bolts}

  • 8 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepJavelin000]{Javelins}

  • One set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbgstDice000000]{Dice}

  • One @UUID[Item.hMeljYMb7OxbfNKv]{Iolite} gemstone and loose coin including [[/award 8gp 12sp]]

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgEmeraldElemen]{Elemental Gem (Emerald)}

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplInvisibili]{Scroll of Invisibility}

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithA]{Scroll of Speak with Animals}

Evidence of Criminality

Should the party wish to take legal action against the Toothbreakers for their crimes, an abundance of evidence can be found in this room to satisfy the requirements for prosecution via the Veiled Chain.

For the party to take action here, they would need to gather some of the papers and other elements laid out on the table, then bring them to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.ThsrAwMhXhmowirO]{The Hallows} and the Veiled Chain. This is beyond the scope of the intent for this questline, but it would enable the Veiled Chain to move openly and divisively against the Toothbreakers gang. However, it's likely that the party will have already solved the problem by defeating Raster Thorn at this point.

Tea Room.name: Tea Room
Tea Room.text:
The hideout's dangerous atmosphere fades away as you step into this large octagonal chamber, delicately illuminated by the green glow of four glass lamps and striations of soft natural light that beam down from the city overhead. Reflecting off the cerulean waters that surround the room's central platform, the light dances on the chamber walls and ceiling with a dreamlike calm, as tranquil and soothing.

The circular stone platform that dominates the chamber is connected to the rest of the room via a set of metal walkways. An ornamented table made of wrought iron sits in the middle of this platform, decorated with the remains of a tea set and a glass hookah. A smaller table occupies the southern edge of the platform, covered in the scattered pieces and checkered board of a half-forgotten game set.

You notice something else by the foot of the central table: a discarded sheet of paper containing a neatly-scrawled list of dates and names.

Searching the Tea Room

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill history 15]][[/skillCheck society 15]] check or who have completed the [[/eventState rubyGroveTales]] event recognize the crimson fluid in the tea set as @UUID[Item.7HAtpZN663UP1KBN]{Ruby}, a rare concoction brewed in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.i8a6VBrxUsZ2PaHo]{Talei} to the north of Ordain. However, the tea has gone cold and has lost it's potency; drinking it has no lingering effects.

Characters with [[/culture emberWaerd]] or who succeed on a [[/skill performance 13]][[/skillCheck performance 13]] check recognize the game as "Bastion", a contest of strategy popular among Waerds.

  • Result of 18+Critical Success - You recognize the game state of the board is such that the team controlling black pieces is positioned to inevitably win the game should play have continued.

A Rat in the Hallows

Raster's most recent tea party guest was Eltien Fen, a Hallows agent-turned-informant who met a gruesome end in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.g97R0OPGQueRR4Jt]{Interrogation Room}.

If the characters examine the paper note at the foot of the wrought iron table, they'll notice:

The note contains a table of dates, times, and names — strange looking names, at that. A curious symbol is scrawled next to many of the entries: a horizontal ellipse with a diagonal slash through its center.

Characters who succeed on an [[/skill investigation 16]][[/skillCheck awareness 16]] check ascertain that the names are codenames used to anonymize an individual and the records seem to be a history of observation, marking the dates and times where an event occurred.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/path emberNightwatch]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

What Happened With Eltien?

Eltien Fen (LE, Ordani Human, he/him), a corrupt bureaucrat who served in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows} as an informant for Raster Thorn, recently delivered the news that Toothbreaker operations have been under active surveillance by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} for several weeks. Raster did not take this revelation well, and viewed Eltien's failure to provide adequate counter-intelligence as a fatally unforgivable one.

Meeting with Raster

If the party persuaded Taamsin to arrange a meeting with @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn}, that meeting occurs here. Raster is accompanied by Taamsin, three Toothbreaker Thugs, and one Scalemaw — which swims in a slow, constant circle around the platform.

It's presumed that the party has arrived to this point under false pretenses, and that they have no actual business with Raster. However, it's also possible that certain groups may wish to continue their ruse. Doing so requires success on a group [[/skill deception 25]][[/skillCheck deception 25 group]] check.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberWaerd]] have @Advantage[2]on this check.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberTayan]] suffer @Advantage[-2] on this check.

Otherwise, it is assumed that the party has used their ruse with Taamsin to separate Raster to a more vulnerable position in order to attack, which occurs at this time.

@Embed[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]

@Embed[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI label="Taamsin the Mastermind"]

@Embed[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB count=3]

@Embed[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]

Raster De-Thorned

If the party fights Raster Thorn in this location, he and his Toothbreaker allies follow the tactics described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#enemy-tactics]{Enemy Tactics}. Raster and his allies will fight to the death.

If Raster is defeated, consult the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.ZEEz2PVd0uRJHL5j] page for information about Raster's personal belongings and the party's next steps.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
This trapezoidal room is illuminated by the firelight of a large brick oven on the slanted southwestern wall. An array of savory scents fills the chamber, including the delicious fragrance of seasoned meat and roasted potatoes, some of which decorate a small table at the room's center.

A lone Toothbreaker thug stands before the oven. Immersed in their culinary duties, this cook fastidiously spices a rack of meat as they rotate it above the oven's embers, seemingly unaware of your presence.

A single @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thug} works as a cook in this kitchen chamber.

Focused Barbecue

The cook is focused on tending their barbecue. Characters who move through the room can avoid detection with a successful [[/skill stealth 13]][[/skillCheck stealth 13]] check.

Raster's Meal

The food on the central table is being prepared for @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn}.

  • Characters with [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check[[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notice a scrap of paper on the table which lists a scribbled food order annotated "for Raster".

Poisoning Raster

If the party has learned of Raster's deadly @UUID[Item.cmwF3TBL4CpMKgsK]{Mudflisk} allergy from the healing house notes in @UUID[.LHzFS3kEmRrHwfh2] they can attempt to poison this meal by adding Mudflisk into the food. If the party has other forms of poison, they could add this to the food to produce an effect, however, adding Mudflisk is a guaranteed method of killing the Toothbreaker leader.

The cook is cautious to not keep any Mudflisk anywhere near the kitchen, so the party would need to procure a source elsewhere. Mudflisk can be easily obtained elsewhere in Ordain or by scouring the basin of the @UUID[.1H1fv6fUFK0T82s8] after it has been drained.

  • Adding Mudflisk to the food requires a successful [[/skill sleightOfHand 15]][[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check to do so without alerting the cook.

  • If Mudflisk is added to the food without the cook becoming aware and if the party is able to retreat from the room without raising suspicion, the cook will proceed to deliver the meal to Raster when it is finished (within the next hour).

  • If Raster has no reason to suspect the food is poisoned, he eats it and shortly thereafter is affected by &Reference[suffocation]. Each time that Raster gains a level of &Reference[exhaustion] from this suffocation, he may make a [[/save con 19]] saving throw to end the effects and avoid further suffocation. If Raster does not succeed on this sequence of saves he will die once his Exhaustion level reaches 6.

Raising the Alarm

There is no alarm bell in this room, but there is one up the stairs to the north in the @UUID[.mQtOym1uGiG7xt5L]{Sparring Alcove}. If the Toothbreaker Thug here becomes aware of enemies, they will run towards the north stairs calling out for help in an attempt to ring this bell.

Rushing Chute.name: Rushing Chute
Rushing Chute.text:
One-Way Water

Characters who enter the water in the grid space next to this chute are sucked into the rushing water and deposited seconds later in the canals of the @UUID[.BQ9jCeU6YqinlEf8]{Tea Room} to the southeast. Characters are momentarily submerged by the water:

  • Any flames they are carrying are extinguished.

  • [[/ancestry emberFej]] characters must make a saving throw against Exhaustion.

If a character is pulled into the chute, read the following aloud:

You draw closer to a narrow chute on the wall, where you feel a quick tug on your lower body as you're suddenly swept up in a rapid flow of water to the southeast. Before you know it, you're pulled down and away through the subterranean torrent, emerging moments later into a different section of the hideout's lazy canals.

Northern Canals.name: Northern Canals
Northern Canals.text:
After following a meandering network of canals through the Concourse waterworks, you reach a landmark that suggests you have found the Toothbreaker Hideout at last. The canal before you diverges — one side flows southwest into a gated culvert, while the other fork gains speed as it flows downhill towards a cavernous opening to the south of your current position.

Before the water reaches that southern opening, it flows beneath a rusted metal walkway that appears overgrown with canal weeds and creepmoss.

Flowing Water

Some sections of the canals here contain rapidly-flowing water, and the characters cannot remain stationary within them. This is one such section. As the characters begin moving southward, they are carried onwards by the flowing current.

Outside of combat, this is simply a narrative flourish. Refer to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#terrain]{Flowing Currents} rules for additional details about movement during combat.

Canal Walkway

Once the party reaches the metallic walkway that spans the canal — which affords them an opportunity to exit the water — they can overhear the following muffled conversation, coming from "somewhere" to the east (the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.g97R0OPGQueRR4Jt]{Interrogation Room}).

As you mount the metallic catwalk, you notice the muffled sound of a masculine voice behind a door to the east.

… you should have told us sooner, but now it's too late, dear Fen. Far too late.

A second, high-pitched voice interrupts the first with a panic-stricken tone:

No! Wait! I can still be …

Panic turns to pain as the second voice screams out with unmistakable agony from some unknown source. This wailing continues unabated for several seconds until a wet gargling overtakes it, and all falls conspicuously silent.

Aside from the obvious ramifications of the exchange, the party is unable to conclude anything further without opening the door in the @UUID[.g97R0OPGQueRR4Jt]{Interrogation Room} itself.

Bar.name: Bar
Bar.text:
On the far western side of the central cistern, a pair of connected circular chambers house a simplistic but cozy bar area. The rooms are illuminated gently by flickering torches and the tables here are covered with mugs, tankards, cards, dice, and other amusements.

You spy a chalkboard that features gambling odds for those seeking to wager on fights taking place in the cistern bloodring.

Rest and Relaxation

If the party is in this area without having antagonized the Toothbreakers, they can chat with some of them.

Characters attempting to extract information from a Toothbreaker at the bar can do so by succeeding on a [[/skill persuasion 14]][[/skillCheck persuasion 14]] check which gains one of the following pieces of information per attempt.

@Embed[RollTable.hJECLPJNTcYVXoYU rollable inline]

If the party fails this check three times, the Toothbreakers communicate their displeasure to Ukkfal who demands that the party "shut up, or leave".

Bloodring Gambling

Characters may gamble on fights occurring in the @UUID[.L15tw2cLjKIAlbup]{Cistern Bloodring}, wagering up to a maximum of [[/award 10gp]] per fight. All fights have even odds and pay double-or-nothing. One hour of time passes between every fight.

  • If a character loses a bet on the Bloodring, they gain @Advantage[2] to their next persuasion attempt to extract information.

  • If a character wins a bet on the Bloodring, they have @Advantage[-2] to their next persuasion attempt to extract information.

If the party investigates the southern room of the bar and inspects the countertop table on the southwest side they notice an unusual collection of vials and alchemical materials.

A crate of glass flasks sits next to a suspended carafe of simmering liquid that is kept warm by a burning flame underneath. The viscous surface of the liquid glistens like liquid metal. Next to the vials on the counter are several syringes that seem to be used for injection of the substance.

Mutagenic Serum

The Toothbreakers have a source of @UUID[Item.O59rdBzHOc7VJypf]{Gleaming Distillation}, provided to them by @UUID[Actor.8jqTLAW121XrQiTN]{Kaftor Brenk} and the Mutagists.

The Toothbreakers here are possessive over the substance, but their greed makes them willing to part with samples in exchange for a fee of [[/award 50gp]] per vial.

The party may attempt to persuade the Toothbreakers for a better deal, a character who succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 16]][[/skillCheck persuasion 16]] check is given a free sample of the substance.

  • Result of 21+Critical Success: Every member of the party is given a sample.

Consumption of the @UUID[Item.O59rdBzHOc7VJypf]{Gleaming Distillation} via intravenous injection has the following effects:

  • It produces a momentary exuberance and empowering effect in Humans which is thrilling (and potentially addictive) to experience.

  • It produces deleterious and nauseating effects on Drakon who are repulsed by the experience.

  • Other ancestries experience momentary lightheadedness followed by several hours of languor accompanied by minor hallucinations.

  • If injected into a @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]{Scalemaw} it causes them to become enraged, ignoring all commands and attacking whatever creatures are closest by.

Consumption of the serum by drinking makes the imbiber sick and affected by the &Reference[poisoned]@Condition[poisoned] condition for 24 hours.

Culvert Entrance.name: Culvert Entrance
Culvert Entrance.text:
You spy something partially submerged in the flowing water of the canal: a semi-circular culvert, 10 feet in diameter. Water flows inward, and you can see the faint flickering of a light somewhere down the tunnel, but it seems impossible to discern details of this light source through the gloom.

Culvert Access

Entering the culvert requires characters to pass underneath the stone walkway of the canal path. To facilitate this transition visually, a Scene Region is placed outside the culvert entrance. When tokens move into this Scene Region they are prompted with the option to teleport through the culvert into the water on the other side.

Characters who enter the water and swim through the large culvert enter an underground area.

You move with the water fifteen feet into the culvert and come face to face with a heavy metal portcullis which is descended, blocking further progress. Holes in the gate are too small to squeeze through.

You peer into the gloom beyond and perceive a small interior dock where a rowboat is moored. Two flickering torches illuminate the chamber.

Leaning backwards in a partially-reclined chair against the north wall of this interior chamber is a motionless figure, their head tilted slightly back and their breathing slow and steady.

Locked Portcullis

The portcullis is controlled using a lever next to the sleeping guard in the @UUID[.3KktScTw3O1mplzH]{Concealed Dock}. Its mechanism cannot be finessed open and it can only be raised using its intended control lever or via the application of brute force.

The portcullis may be lifted with a successful [[/skill athletics 20]][[/skillCheck athletics 20]] check, and an ally who has a Strength score of at least 16 provides advantage5 provides +2 Boons to this roll. The portcullis can also be raised using the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLevitate00]{Levitate} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplTelekinesi]{Telekinesis} spells.

A character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]]an [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check notices that the portcullis is well-maintained and shows signs of frequent use. It can most likely be lifted quietly.

Scalemaw Kennels.name: Scalemaw Kennels
Scalemaw Kennels.text:
This room is dimly lit by a single flickering torch and it is tightly packed with three large cages, each outfitted to contain a single Scalemaw.

Restraints, whips, a feeding trough, and other training implements are scattered around the room.

Each of these two rooms are similarly equipped and each contain a single caged Scalemaw.

@Embed[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]

Scalemaw

If freed or provoked the creature attacks following the tactics described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#enemy-tactics]{Enemy Tactics}.

Notable Treasure

There is nothing in these rooms that would be described as treasure, but they do provide an opportunity to inspect the Scalemaws in relative safety.

Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] or those succeeding on a [[/skill nature 16]][[/skillCheck medicine 16]] check know some lore about the Scalemaw and that they were likely captured in the wilds of the Lowland Kingdoms and transported to Ordain by ship.

Distillation Warning

Characters with [[/skill perception 15 passive format=long]] or who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] notice a scrap of paper that has fallen to the ground beside a wooden stool. The paper reads:

Vaafo — finished my investigation and came to give you the news. Weren't here so I'm leaving a note.

Looks like one of the lads took a dare to stick Vesk with that new serum they're serving at the bar. Beast went absolutely berserk and tore the place up. The new kid is dead, good riddance, and Vesk dragged another down into the canals.

I've seen her eyes in the water but feck if I know how we'll get her out of there. I don't want to be the one to tell Raster, so I'm letting you have that job!

— Fal

Characters with a successful [[/skill insight 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check infer that "Vesk" is a Scalemaw that somehow went berserk from being injected with something. The person who did it is dead and the Scalemaw escaped into the canals.

  • Characters with [[/path emberCrownApothecary]] or [[/knowledge alchemy]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Berserk Scalemaws

The substance being described is @UUID[Item.O59rdBzHOc7VJypf]{Gleaming Distillation} which can be obtained in the @UUID[.vlTZOAz7ZlzaTapN]{Bar}.

If the Scalemaws here or elsewhere in the hideout are injected with the substance, requiring a successful attack roll using an improvised weapon, they will go berserk. While berserk the Scalemaws will attack any creature that is nearby including their own handlers or other Scalemaw.

Sparring Alcove.name: Sparring Alcove
Sparring Alcove.text:
This circular alcove is lit by the flames of a single torch ensconced on the southern wall, and appears to be some sort of modest sparring or training room. A lone Toothbreaker warrior assaults a combat dummy in the center of the chamber with kicks and unarmed blows, shouting loudly with each new strike. Indeed, the clamor of this martial performance is so loud and intense, the thug seems oblivious to your initial approach.

Focused Training

The training thug is focused on his martial exercises. Characters who approach and move into the room can avoid detection with a successful [[/skill stealth 13]][[/skillCheck stealth 13]] check.

Toothbreakers

There is a solitary @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thug} in this room practicing martial arts.

Raising the Alarm

This room contains an alarm bell, which the Toothbreaker Thug will ring if they become aware of any interlopers.

Locked Door

The door to the @UUID[.idxgwrjrPr9wBh4V]{Planning Room} is locked.

Two corresponding @UUID[Item.okV1Ejy1uuRz7LvP]{Toothbreaker Planning Keys} can be found elsewhere in the hideout: one is in the possession of Vaafo the Scaletamer in @UUID[.TP5eHaP4OD2xBHaw]{Scalemaw Training}, while another is currently held by @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn} himself.

Western Canals.name: Western Canals
Western Canals.text:
Water flows freely here through a broad canal that is 10 feet wide and deep. The underground passageway ripples with a pale blue hue as the canal flows southward towards a circular interchange. To the west, a walkway borders the canal opening to several rooms, some of which appear to be fully collapsed while others have doors.

Cutting off the Flow

The flow of water here can be disabled by turning the valves in @UUID[.YORL610CzFdhixD5]{Flow Control}.

If the canals have been drained, read:

The broad canal here is emptied of water, its flow having been restricted by a pair of large sluices further upstream. The bed of the canal is grimy and full of silt, mud, and puddles of lingering water.

Mudflisk Source

If the canals are drained, it's possible to harvest @UUID[Item.cmwF3TBL4CpMKgsK]{Mudflisk} from the canal bed with a successful [[/skill investigation 13]][[/skillCheck survival 13]] check.

@Embed[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs label="Vesk"]

Enraged Scalemaw

One of the Toothbreaker's trained Scalemaws is loose and patrolling this section of canal. This Scalemaw has become enraged and volatile after being exposed to @UUID[Item.O59rdBzHOc7VJypf]{Gleaming Distillation}. Scant details of that exposure are documented in @UUID[.tqM3BjyoxFoRI00n]{Scalemaw Kennels}.

As long as the canals are full of water, Vesk is hidden and able to attack from stealth unless detected by a character with [[/skill perception 15 passive format=long]][[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]].

The Scalemaw is named "Vesk" and will attack any character or creature without provocation that passes through this area. Raster Thorn and other Scaletamers are not able to pacify the creature, but they have the skills to avoid it's aggression.

Raster's Vault.name: Raster's Vault
Raster's Vault.text:
The conduits and flooring of this small chamber suggest it was once used as a bathroom, but the copious piles of coin and other eye-catching baubles piled up here suggest that it's been converted into a vault for the storage of prized possessions. Light cascades through a large window on the southern wall, causing the treasured belongings stored within to scintillate with alluring brilliance.

Locked Vault

The door to the east is locked, and the only key is located on @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh.Item.UHZgyAMxxL3uszH2]{Raster's Keyring}, in his possession. Alternately, the lock can be picked with a successful [[/check tool=thief dc=25]][[/skillCheck stealth 25]] check.

Raster's Treasure

Plundering the vault yields a substantial amount of treasure, including:

  • Loose coin totaling [[/award 1732gp]]

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfClimb]{Potion of Climbing}

  • One @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfGrowt]{Potion of Growth}

  • One @UUID[Item.tqrxlS34PL1EmCaN]{Fine Jeweled Ring}

  • The @UUID[Item.P9rd4LUaklq6N0Pm]{Bust of Avilla}

Security Checkpoint.name: Security Checkpoint
Security Checkpoint.text:
This dingy passage turns left and terminates abruptly at a metal door, eight feet high and completely solid aside from a narrow metal eyeslit that is currently closed from the other side.

Discarded bottles and rags litter the stone floor in front of this rather unwelcoming and nondescript threshold. Taking a moment to listen, you hear no audible sound from within — save for the ambient thrum of flowing water that seems to reverberate through the walls.

Security Door

The security door here is equipped with a heavy iron crossbar, which makes it nigh impossible to open from the outside while secured in this way. The door also features a traditional lock that uses a key, but while the Toothbreaker Hideout is occupied, the guards within keep this crossbar in place.

  • The locked door is not possible to pick open or otherwise finesse.

  • The locked door can be forced open with a successful a [[/skill athletics 30]][[/skillCheck athletics 30]] check, which loudly bashes it inwards, tearing the door free of its hinges and crashing into the room beyond. Any attempt to force open the door, whether successful or not, immediately causes the @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thugs} in the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4]{Guardroom} to raise the alarm.

Most groups that seek entrance into the Toothbreaker Hideout via this route will have to socially negotiate a reason for entrance with the guards inside the adjoining @UUID[.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4]{Guardoom}.

Talking Your Way In

A devious or persuasive party may be able to talk their way into the complex. A knock on the door is greeted with a gruff response:

Leave now if you don't want to get hurt. Badly.

The party has only a brief moment to either leave or provide a compelling reason for entry, otherwise the Toothbreakers begin firing crossbow bolts through the open eyeslit of the door. Some topics that could be of interest to the Toothbreaker guards include the following (if not similar topics that the Gamemaster is willing to entertain):

Bloodring Betting

If the party has knowledge of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.L15tw2cLjKIAlbup]{Cistern Bloodring} and establishes that they wish to bet on fights, one or more characters must succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 15]][[/skillCheck persuasion 15]] check to convince the guards that they are enthusiastic gamblers who are unbothered by the depravity of the underground arena.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/path emberUnderworldMechanic]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

If the check is successful, the guards will demand an up-front entrance fee of [[/award -50gp]] as a tithe to the gang. If the check is failed or the entrance fee unpaid, the guards will insist the party leave or respond with violence.

If the party enters in this way, they are escorted by the guards to the @UUID[.L15tw2cLjKIAlbup]{Cistern Bloodring} to meet Ukkfal the Ringmaster.

Scalemaw Fascination

The party can claim to be zoological enthusiasts who are fascinated by Scalemaws. The Toothbreakers are susceptible to this ploy because of the pride they have in their companion creatures, and they are willing to indulge the party's curiosity if one or more of the characters succeed on a [[/skill animalHandling 16]][[/skillCheck survival 16]] check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] or [[/path emberPrimalistDisciple]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

If the party enters in this way, they are escorted by the guards to the @UUID[.TP5eHaP4OD2xBHaw]{Scalemaw Training} area to meet Vaafo the Scaletamer.

Business Proposition

The party can pretend to have a business proposition for the gang that would result in a substantial payday or other advancement of the Toothbreaker's agenda. Such a proposition could also include compromising information about adversarial organizations like the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} or the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}.

One or more characters must succeed on a [[/skill deception 15]][[/skillCheck deception 15]] check to seem convincing enough to deserve the attention of their supervisor.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]], [[/knowledge trade]], or [[/path emberNightwatch]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

If the party enters in this way, they are escorted by the guards to the @UUID[.idxgwrjrPr9wBh4V]{Planning Room} to meet with Taamsin the Mastermind.

If negotiations go poorly or the party chooses to provoke the guards, combat will erupt between the two chambers.

Fighting Your Way In

As long as the security door remains closed, the @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thugs} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.5pEpoZGkQBEj15W4]{Guardroom} will remain there and fire crossbow bolts through the eyeslit of the door. If the party does not retreat or demonstrates any capability to be a threat, these guards will immediately sound the alarm, summoning more Toothbreakers Thugs to reinforce the chokepoint.

See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberToothbrkWlk.JournalEntryPage.qwl1wP5cuWdhiNP8#enemy-tactics]{Enemy Tactics} for a description of their tactics.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the @UUID[Scene.emberForgCistern] depicts the above and under ground area where discovered as part of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness} quest events.

Environment

Situated beneath the city of Ordain, this ancient ruin predates the streets above by at least a thousand years. The passageways and chambers are fashioned from heavy blocks of black basalt, some shaped with magic, others by hands long vanished from the world.

Threaded throughout these ruins is a much newer incursion: a sprawling laboratory, its structures awkwardly fixed into and cutting through the ancient halls and rooms without regard for their history.

Alchemical lanterns have been bolted to the old stone, the lighting they provide seldom covers any area well, leaving shadows to cluster thickly at the edges of the harsh and uneven glow.

Ecology

Very little grows in these ruins, and all the lifeforms found within are invasive, having eaten or driven off whatever used to reside within.

Lore

Previously studied by the Anachraeunum of Ordain, any secrets it once held have been long discovered and cataloged, the records collecting dust in the All-Fable Keep's many archives.

The location was built by the Sedyri people thousands of years ago, possibly after their exodus from their homeland, possibly to serve as an outpost, or even a private home.

In truth, this structure's original purpose is not known to historians and only a collection of educated guesses and speculations are available.

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The following gameplay features apply to the Forgotten Cistern area unless specifically stated otherwise in a specific room description.

Enemies

This area is the base of operations for a Mutagist field experiment and is full of their members. At most times, the following enemies are encountered here in the provided approximate number:

  • 7 @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]{Mutagist Vivisector}

  • 2 @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg]{Mutagist Bombadier}

  • 7 @UUID[Actor.SaHU3uIIGCPqJ2eV]{Mutagist Excisor}

  • @UUID[Actor.8jqTLAW121XrQiTN]{Mutagist Kaftor Brenk}

There is also a nest of drakes in a collapsed portion of the map, among their number are:

  • 5 @UUID[Actor.se8S6JjsgSo5BJPt]{Pallid Drakeling}

  • @UUID[Actor.M9oc24iW3qI44GZe]{Pallid Drake}

  • @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG]{Radiant Ultra Drake}

Significantly Outnumbered

Because of the large number of adversaries in this area, an uncontrolled assault is likely to be deadly. The party would be well advised to use stealth or guile to avoid direct confrontation where possible.

Resting

It is not possible to take a Long Rest within this area without being detected. A Short Rest is only possible in a few specific rooms which mention this as part of their location details.

Fleeing

Should the party need to flee the area, they may do so by retreating to @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.kl5v0uMnJfpSSYCW]{Sunken Entrance} and swimming out, or by taking the stairs near the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.VolfUdkggxrYy0yq] which lead to the sewers which the party can use to return to the surface.

Truly desperate parties may attempt to take the flowing water tunnel located just off the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.TN5mwsKCSascCYgj]{Corpse Dump} which will dump them out into the Destine river, though not after a harrowing, barely controlled swim through a lightness underwater passage.

Captured

If the party is subdued in combat, they may awaken from an unconscious state as captives held within the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.tE9dJSnT8E3sCy26]{Rusting Cages}.

The Mutagists will take any Human characters to be experimented on, strapping them to chairs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.ueNNLiX5LWT5TdW3]{Injection Room}, though they may be able to escape before anything heinous can be done to them.

Sound

The cistern feature a constant low rumble of liquids coursing through pipes overhead, machines whirring, and flowing water, all of which resonate through the hard stone halls of the ruins. As a consequence, hearing in this environment is more challenging. Mutagists also wear masks, which further hinders their ability to speak loudly and clearly, forcing them to huddle together to speak effectively.

  • Sounds of combat can only be heard within 40 feet of their origin, and they are muffled completely beyond the stone walls of a room if its doors are closed.

  • The great stone doors scattered throughout the ruins create a substantial amount of noise and vibration when opening or closing, which will alert any creatures within 20 feet of them.

  • Characters in this area have @Advantage[2] to any [[/check stealth]] skill check to avoid being heard but have @Advantage[-2] to any [[/check perception]] skill check that relies on hearing.

Illumination

While most lab areas are decently lit in a yellow-orange bright light, these lamps are sparse, and fade into dim light everywhere else. In some places, either torches or old magical light sources provide dim illumination — enough to navigate by, but obscure fine details.

Terrain

Rubble and collapsed sections of the ruins, as well as the various bodies of water on this scene serve as &reference[difficult terrain] for characters moving through such spaces.

Hidden Doorways

There are several ancient stone doors which begin open and hidden in the halls between the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.YwkTdemCTyPN7NgH]{Extraction Lab}, @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.ueNNLiX5LWT5TdW3]{Injection Room}, @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.fULaKmDeZAqiJe1R]{Living Area}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.8vLylrPmKWnZvDRw]{Chemical Outlet} rooms.

They can be operated by any [[/ancestry emberAshka]] character that uses an object interaction to trigger the magical mechanisms. These doors are made of heavy, magically reinforced stone with an AC of 18 and 60 hit points once closed.

There are also two gemmed doors on either side of the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.iZvNkRCJPialiP0T]{Glowing Cistern} that require specific items to open, but can be operated by an creature. These doors are magically warded and sealed, and cannot be opened any other way.

Elements Under Development

The various hidden doorways will have interactive elements in future updates. For now the secret doorways can be manipulated manually.

Elevation

Unless otherwise stated, most ceilings are 10ft high. Rooms that have overhead pipes have about 2ft of that space consumed by these fixtures, functionally reducing overhead ceiling height to about 8ft.

In the marsh area the water is 3-4 feet deep in most places, which would places most tokens in-scene at -3ft to -4ft elevation when in the water. This should put most medium creatures at waist deep, but may fully submerge smaller creatures.

Inside the ruins, most water is 5ft deep. While in the main cistern area, this increases to 15ft deep.

Bridges, platforms and walkways are at ground level (elevation 0) unless otherwise stated.

Other Effects

The air is choked with the reek of rotting flesh, caustic chemicals, sewage, and stagnant air. The stench is not only unpleasant, but burns the airways of living creatures. Any perception checks that rely on the sense of smell are made with @Advantage[-2] as a result.

Additionally, characters begin coughing audibly if they fail any such check by 5 or more unless they are wearing a protective mask or do not need to breathe. This can potentially be heard by other characters up to 30 feet away.

Sunken Entrance.name: Sunken Entrance
Sunken Entrance.text:
Four ancient basalt pillars rise out of the shallow marsh, their surfaces weathered and pitted by countless seasons. Muck and clinging moss coat their bases, while faint carvings, almost erased by time, are still just visible from the right angle.

Ancient History

Spending time studying the ruins as the party travels allows for a [[/skill history 18]] check. If successful, the character realizes the ruins belong to the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.4RM8MIiCDWMFv2yr] culture, and vastly predate the city built over top them.

Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] have @Advantage[2] on this roll.

Setting the Pillars

You see four ancient basalt pillars standing together, rising out of the marshy water. Their dark faces are pitted and softened by time, but still bear collections of intricate carvings that seemingly refuse to yield to the ravages of time and elements.

The forms cut into the stone are easily identifiable as symbols for fire, ice, earth, wind, and many more. They are laid out in such a way that none have prominence over the others.

Examining the Symbols

Each of the pillars have three symbols, and none of the symbols are shared between pillars. Counterclockwise from the northernmost pillar, the following symbols appear:

  • Pillar one: earth, wind, fire,

  • Pillar two: rain, earth, steam

  • Pillar three: water, ice, stone

  • Pillar four: magma, snow, air

Examining the symbols with a successful [[/skill history 16]] considers that if the ruins are Sedyri in nature, which they are, then their settlements often had prevalent themes of fire and water. Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Result 20+ Another significant element of the Ashka culture were coastal settlements, and volcano iconography. Perhaps they might be represented in the symbols somehow.

Activation Sequence

These symbols need to be activated on their respective pillars to open the way forward: fire, water, magma, steam.

Note that the order doesn't matter, but the combination represents the core water and fire elements, and what you get when they are combined. Magma is not only referential to the Ashka history, but represents a form of liquid fire.

Scrutinizing the Pillars

Examining the pillars with a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] check recognizes spell work carved into the stone around the symbols, with divination and evocation elements being prominent. It's possible these symbols react to being touched, and need to be activated in a specific way.

  • Result of 16+ The character notes that there is a faint charm effect included in the stones, and is meant to affect the viewer, but what it's meant to do beyond that is unclear.

Ancestral Magic

A character with the [[/ancestry emberAshka]] will find themselves strangely drawn to these symbols, as though something about them resonates with their very blood.

They can make a [[/skill insight 14]] check while examining the stones. On success they intuit one of the symbols they need to activate. They can do this multiple times, but the DC increases by +2 each time they successfully intuit a correct symbol, first time included.

Elements Under Development

The sunken entrance puzzle and hidden doorway will have interactive elements and animations in future updates, but don't presently match the written text and events that unfold.

Opening the Passage

The four symbols glow brightly and briefly then fade out. A moment later the water stirs, and bubbles roil up to the surface as stone slides away below you, revealing an passage of stairs that descend into darkness.

The path almost certainly leads into some greater structure beyond and below, but accessing it will require some swimming.

Soaked Through

Characters taking this passage will need to swim for about 25 feet, most should be able to do so safely, but they will be soaked through in the process, potentially ruining any items that shouldn't be gotten wet, like books, paper, food, and the like.

This also renders things like torches unusable until dried.

Contamination Hazard

As the water is tainted by disease, rot and chemicals, eating any food exposed to the water requires a [[/save con 14]] or inflicts the &reference[poisoned] condition for an hour.

Entering the Secret Lab

Guided by the vile fluid underfoot, you follow the winding tunnels until the passage opens into an enormous underground cistern. The air here is warmer, clearer, and a haze of unnatural smoke lingers in the air overhead.

Ahead, slow flowing water reflects the glow of shuttered lanterns which hang from walls of metal and wood that form makeshift structures. Aside a few of the structures are rusting iron cages, and large vats of bubbling emerald fluid.

A secret lab, right below the very streets of Ordain!

Storage Room.name: Storage Room
Storage Room.text:
You enter a room cramped with storage containers, its low ceiling and narrow dimensions made tighter still by the ranks of crates, barrels, and bulging sacks that crowd the space. Every available surface has been put to use holding a container or stack of items.

The air is heavy here with the stink of mildew and damp old wood.

Underfoot, the floor has been covered with uneven wooden slats, many of which have softened and warped from the constant damp, leaving patches darkened with rot.

Stolen Effects

The store room contains crates of clothing and items that appear to have belonged to Ordani locals. These can be searched with a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check locates and identifies some @UUID[Item.UV5JlTJP1cR2LdqR]{Personal Effects}. These items can be gathered up and taken as evidence, or as treasure to be sold later.

Packed but Worthless

A quick search reveals nothing of value in the various containers, just bundles of spare vials, cases of needles starting to rust, assorted copper pipe fittings and patches, lengths of buckled leather restraints, and more packed away in no apparent order.

Narrow Passage

A narrow passage stretches into the darkness here. Small and tiny creatures can move through this space comfortably, but medium sized creatures will need to squeeze through.

While squeezing through a space, a creature must spend 1 extra foot for every foot it moves, and it has @Advantage[-2] on any physical rolls and saving throws it makes. Attack rolls against the creature have @Advantage[2] while it’s in the smaller space.

The passage connects the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.YPxglJqSXdjyn8gv]{Storage Room} to the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.fULaKmDeZAqiJe1R]{Living Area}.

Living Area.name: Living Area
Living Area.text:
You step into a long chamber that's been transformed into a makeshift living space. Four cloth tents fill much of the room, with a stockpile of barrels and sacks behind one in a corner. A campfire burns against one wall, casting uneven light and filling the room with a faint haze of acrid smoke and lazily drifts out of a hall toward the east. Pipes hang overhead, fixed to the ceiling and cutting through ancient stone.

Arcane Adversaries

The @UUID[Actor.SaHU3uIIGCPqJ2eV]{Excisors} here attempt to attack from range, avoiding close combat where possible. However, their @UUID[Actor.SaHU3uIIGCPqJ2eV.Item.sQ966YV5oMsRE6ln]{Arcane Burst} proves perfectly functional in close range as well.

In terms of spellcasting, they all have mage armor cast (which is automatically applied to their AC) and use @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRayofEnfee]{Ray of Enfeeblement} to weaken the strongest enemies on the field.

If injured they utilize their @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplVampiricTo]{Vampiric Touch} spells to recover some lost hit points while harming their foes.

Fire Support

The @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg]{Bombardiers} in this area attempt to hang back, choosing to @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg.Item.mMbzqmbN9L9egRJ0]{Throw Alchemical Grenades} at grouped targets. If engaged in melee combat, they are competent with their @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg.Item.XEofQHpIhzptXqJG]{Axe}, and will defend themselves violently.

Melee Specialists

While their allies hang back, the @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]{Mutagist Vivisectors} choose to get up and personal when fights break out, using their @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8.Item.uby0paUKaSDsJh3b]{Hollow Stiletto} with their @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8.Item.I6BPISTi52a2MniF]{Poison Vial} to harm their enemies.

Unhappy Campers

Examining inside the tents, you find nothing of value, just bedrolls on scattered hay, small bundles of clothing, the odd journal filled with scratchy observations and meandering complaints about being stuck in the lab, and the prevalent smell.

A successful [[/skill investigation 16]] check while examining the clutter concludes that about ten people use this space, sharing tents and sleeping in shifts as they can, and that the people in the lab are rotated out in shifts, indicating they likely have a safehouse elsewhere in the city.

Assorted Items

Searching the tents and piles of bags behind them yields few sets of @UUID[Item.4D3pE4WYXm3kmUps]{Mutagist Clothing} which can be used by a character to disguise themselves as a @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]{Mutagist Vivisector}.

Characters can also find @UUID[Item.UV5JlTJP1cR2LdqR]{Personal Effects} likely stolen from the victims of the lab. These can be taken as evidence or for later sale to a willing and suitably unscrupulous merchant.

Narrow Passage

A narrow passage stretches into the darkness here. Small and tiny creatures can move through this space comfortably, but medium sized creatures will need to squeeze through.

While squeezing through a space, a creature must spend 1 extra foot for every foot it moves, and it has @Advantage[-2] on any physical rolls and saving throws it makes. Attack rolls against the creature have @Advantage[2] while it’s in the smaller space.

The passage connects the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.YPxglJqSXdjyn8gv]{Storage Room} to the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.fULaKmDeZAqiJe1R]{Living Area}.

Chemical Outlet.name: Chemical Outlet
Chemical Outlet.text:
The black basalt of the old structure ends at a curved stone dock overlooking a cavern river. Here, several thick pipes jut from the wall, gushing forth torrents of luminous green chemical into the water nearby. The chemicals paint the low ceiling and walls with shifting patterns of ghastly green light and fill the air with a choking stench that makes breathing painful.

Rickety wooden walkways, built with little care, hug the cave walls and disappear into the darkness beyond.

Dangerous Dumping

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or making a successful [[/skill medicine 12]] check know that the volume of chemicals being dumped into this water stream would likely end up in city's water supply. This almost certainly would make people incredibly sick if consumed.

Shutting it Down

A quick [[/skill perception 12]] check confirms that there are no valves or other means of shutting down the chemical flow here. Searching elsewhere in the labs may provide a way to stop the flow. Nothing can be done here.

Scattered Effects

Discarded in the corner is a pile of clothing and @UUID[Item.UV5JlTJP1cR2LdqR]{personal effects}, most of them blood stained and showing signs of damage. These can be collected as evidence or treasure for later sale.

Corpse Dump.name: Corpse Dump
Corpse Dump.text:
This circular chamber stinks of death and corrosive chemicals. At the center, a broad, stone-rimmed well collects foul water, its surface tinted green by a constant flow from a large overhead pipe that dumps a stream of glowing, acrid fluid into the basin.

Against wall a heap of shrouded bodies lies is piled up, leaking rancid fluids into the already tainted water supply. Opposite the bodies is a beautiful relief standing in contrast to the grisly scene around it.

Awful Runoff

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or making a successful [[/skill medicine 12]] check recognize that combination of rotting bodies and runoff chemicals are immensely toxic and either one of them alone could account for the sickness taking hold in the city. Together, they almost guarantee it.

Hidden Doorway

On the far wall of the room there is a hidden door behind a stone relief. The party can study it, but won't find a way to open it until later in the dungeon.

The stone relief is of an Askha figure with their hands cupped at chest level, holding an orb. Their robes have decorative elements that flow like water, and a ball of flame rests in their hands. They stand on cracked, uneven ground that looks like cooled lava, and they are surrounded by billowing clouds.

A blue gem fixed and fused with the stone above glows with a dim blue light.

Empty Slot

Characters with a [[/skill perception 12 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 14]] notice that there is an indent in the wall beside the relief, circular, and faceted, like something is meant to slot into it.

A successful [[/skill arcana 14]] notes that there are small divination symbols inside the depression, indicating it might react to something being placed into the slot.

Sealed Door

Any of the Sedyri elemental emblems will work to open this door. They can be acquired elsewhere in the dungeon.

If characters slot any elemental emblem into the space aside the door, the stone wall slides upward, revealing stairs to the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.iZvNkRCJPialiP0T]{Glowing Cistern}.

Injection Room.name: Injection Room
Injection Room.text:
Five medical chairs dominate the space in this small chamber, their cracked leather surfaces stained dark by old blood and fouler wastes. Two of the chairs still hold occupants, a pair of emaciated corpses, one sitting upright with sightless eyes, the other slumped forward in its restraints.

At the back of the room, the black basalt wall bears a relief of ancient Ashka, the artful carving a jarring contrast to the filth and horror surrounding it.

Medical Investigation

A successful [[/skill medicine 14]] while examining the corpses reveals both have died very recently. Ragged puncture wounds cover their limbs, the marks of numerous injections forced through the skin in haste or disregard.

Their drawn faces and wasted bodies show there was nothing that could have saved them short of arriving days earlier.

Discarded Clothing

The stained, soaked clothing underfoot has already been picked of any valuables, but the style is distinctly Arcturian, most of it rugged and clearly hand-made.

Ashka Relief

The stone relief is of an Askha figure with their hands cupped at chest level. Their robes have decorative elements that flow like water, and a ball of flame rests in their hands. They stand on cracked, uneven ground that looks like cooled lava, and they are surrounded by billowing clouds.

Empty Slot

Characters with a [[/skill perception 12 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 14]] notice that there is an indent in the palm of the Askha figure, like they were once holding something.

The indent is plain, with no magical or mechanical attributes that any character can find.

Beaten to the Punch

There once was a Sedyri elemental emblem in this statue, but it was taken by the Mutagists some time ago, and is now in the hands of Mutagist Kaftor Brenk, the lab's overseer.

Extraction Lab.name: Extraction Lab
Extraction Lab.text:
This room is packed with heavy metal slabs, each perched upon a tilting pedestal and deeply stained by old, darkened blood. On one table, the body of a man lies beneath a coarse burlap sheet. His outline is thin and unmoving.

On the wall behind the body are a row of three large vats filled with shimmering liquids. Each stands connected to the snarl of pipes and hoses which lead to gauges and meters that provide readings without explanation.

Tables of alchemical tubes, sit here and there, each brimming with vials and canisters of fluids, some brown as old blood, others glimmering with suspect green light.

Arcane Adversaries

The @UUID[Actor.SaHU3uIIGCPqJ2eV]{Excisors} here attempt to attack from range, avoiding close combat where possible. However, their @UUID[Actor.SaHU3uIIGCPqJ2eV.Item.sQ966YV5oMsRE6ln]{Arcane Burst} proves perfectly functional in close range as well.

In terms of spellcasting, they all have mage armor cast (which is automatically applied to their AC) and use @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRayofEnfee]{Ray of Enfeeblement} to weaken the strongest enemies on the field.

If injured they utilize their @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplVampiricTo]{Vampiric Touch} spells to recover some lost hit points while harming their foes.

Fire Support

The @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg]{Bombardiers} in this area attempt to hang back, choosing to @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg.Item.mMbzqmbN9L9egRJ0]{Throw Alchemical Grenades} at grouped targets. If engaged in melee combat, they are competent with their @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg.Item.XEofQHpIhzptXqJG]{Axe}, and will defend themselves violently.

Melee Specialists

While their allies hang back, the @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]{Mutagist Vivisectors} choose to get up and personal when fights break out, using their @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8.Item.uby0paUKaSDsJh3b]{Hollow Stiletto} with their @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8.Item.I6BPISTi52a2MniF]{Poison Vial} to harm their enemies.

Dead Body

The victim is covered in numerous needle marks, many of them old and partially healed. It's hard to tell how long the victim was held here, but since the numerous needle marks appear to show signs of infection, it was likely over the course of several days at least, if not much longer.

A successful [[/skill medicine 14]] check while examining the body reveals information based on the result.

  • Result of 14+ Notes that many of the injection show signs of infection and tearing. The process was almost certainly arduous, and painful, and given the relatively fresh state of the corpse, was only concluded a day or two ago.

  • Result of 16+ The sites of the injections lead you to believe that they underwent numerous cycles of being injected and drained of their fluids, and as far as you can tell, their death was a result of blood loss.

Alchemical ritual

A mixture of biomagic and alchemy is underway on this corner table, small-scale tests of transforming one fluid to another.

Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] note that there are reagents and implements marked with sigils and runes tied to practices of biomagic and transformative rituals meant to manipulate living beings.

Examining the circles of magic with a successful [[/skill arcana 16]] check leads you to believe it's trying to enhance or empower some effect within the fluid. To what end is unclear. Characters with either of the above knowledges have @Advantage[2] on this check.

A Phantom Pain

Characters making a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] check recognize that the magic at play here is primarily illusory in nature, and mind-affecting, specifically. Without closely analyzing the magic to get specifics, the general function is to create hallucinations or visions and incite feeling and pain and fear in what amounts to magical torture.
