  • Result of 16+ The alchemical process at work is attempting to isolate something in the compound, something which apparently only occurs in humans.

Characters with knowledge [[/knowledge rituals]] or [[/knowledge alchemy]] have @Advantage[2] on the above check.

Flow Valve

A large flow valve on the wall here can be used to cut off the chemical supply to this area. Doing so causes all the dials and gauges here to show a drop in flow rate and pressure, and cut off this area from circulating more chemicals through it, but has not stopped the rest of the pipes in the area.

Supply Shelves

Examining the shelves stretched across the far south wall, you find bottles of chemicals, racks of unused restraints, bundles of syringes, and rows of canisters marked by both unreadable sigils and more recent handwriting. Nearly everything here is of plain, merciless purpose: tools for containing, injecting, and extracting, unused and waiting their turn.

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] recognize many of these chemicals as being used to transmute and manipulate biological matter.

Tank Room.name: Tank Room
Tank Room.text:
Emerging from the water, you find the stone passage rises on a gradual slope into a broad chamber carved from ancient basalt, the walls glossy from long exposure to water.

Dominating the space are a pair of massive brass tanks set to one side, their surfaces mottled and tarnished, and their presence not part of the original construction. A series of pipes stretch out overhead, going in all directions.

The air is thick with the sharp reek of chemicals and rotting flesh.

Stirring Up Trouble

The two large tanks swirl with liquid, both leaking a caustic green chemical from their bases, letting it pool in the group and gaps of the ancient stone underfoot.

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or [[/knowledge alchemy]] recognizes that these machines are moving liquids between the tanks, separating them in some way, and sending the filtered chemicals into one pipeline, and sending the runoff elsewhere.

The construction is slapdash and crude.

Main Flow Valve

A large flow valve sits attached to a huge overhead pipe above. Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] suspect this is a main flow valve.

Turning it requires a successful [[/check str 16]] check, and causes all the pipes to shudder and groan, but doesn't stop the machines.

A successful [[/skill investigation 15]] while looking over the machine notes there is no actual way to full stop the chemical dumping process, the Mutagists built it without such features, seemingly unconcerned about how much chemical they dump into the water supply.

Perhaps that was their goal.

Glowing Cistern.name: Glowing Cistern
Glowing Cistern.text:
The space opens into a vast, oval-shaped chamber, flanked by eight towering pillars on either side, each cut from a single block of black basalt. Down every pillar, curtains of glowing water stream continuously, their cold blue light bathing the entire cavern in a gentle, uneven luminescence.

A broad stone bridge stretches out above the cistern itself, its flagstones slick with mist and lit from below.

On both sides of this bridge, makeshift laboratories and chemical stockpiles crowd the arc of the chamber, their mismatched walls of timber and metal out of place amid the grandeur. Casks and crates spill over with volatile compounds, their sharp tang mixing with the cool damp of the glowing reservoir below.

Mutagist Occupiers

This area is filled with a handful of Mutagists, and there is no way to gain entry to the area without alerting them, as both stone doors in the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.TN5mwsKCSascCYgj] and @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.oM4NQm4Al5sWt4D0] create loud rumbles and vibrations that alert the nearby enemies.

Also, as soon as fighting breaks out on either side of the cistern, the other side's Mutagists with rush in to assist.

Water Pillars

The massive pillars are the source of the magical water here, by the looks of things. Examining them up close with a successful [[/skill arcana 15]] confirms this through the presence of numerous transmutation and evocation symbols carved into the stone among the other decorative elements.

It's unclear what the magic is doing beyond simply infusing the water with magical energy.

Characters that have a proper vessel on-hand can take a sample of the @UUID[Item.9GIJHWhbH0GmztLC]{Infused Water} if they want to.

Fighting Kaftor

Arcane Adversaries

The @UUID[Actor.SaHU3uIIGCPqJ2eV]{Excisors} here attempt to attack from range, avoiding close combat where possible. However, their @UUID[Actor.SaHU3uIIGCPqJ2eV.Item.sQ966YV5oMsRE6ln]{Arcane Burst} proves perfectly functional in close range as well.

In terms of spellcasting, they all have mage armor cast (which is automatically applied to their AC) and use @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRayofEnfee]{Ray of Enfeeblement} to weaken the strongest enemies on the field.

If injured they utilize their @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplVampiricTo]{Vampiric Touch} spells to recover some lost hit points while harming their foes.

A Cut Above

Kaftor Brenk also has access to a few unique abilities that make him especially dangerous. Firstly, if engaged in close combat he can use his @UUID[Actor.8jqTLAW121XrQiTN.Item.dxWWIcMBtQkqGOwX]{Draining Swipe} to not only recover hit points, but harm his enemies.

He can also use his action to consume a powerful alchemical compound and @UUID[Actor.8jqTLAW121XrQiTN.Item.dHy3xwkfVvXqB2bY]{Trigger Blaze}, giving him his action back, and enhancing his performance.

While he can only do this four times, he also has granted himself a unique @UUID[Actor.8jqTLAW121XrQiTN.Item.S1I7j30qvy0Lrbmr]{False Ember Blaze} which will trigger, saving him from death, which is not something his Ancestry can normally do.

Fire Support

The @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg]{Bombardiers} in this area attempt to hang back, choosing to @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg.Item.mMbzqmbN9L9egRJ0]{Throw Alchemical Grenades} at grouped targets. If engaged in melee combat, they are competent with their @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg.Item.XEofQHpIhzptXqJG]{Axe}, and will defend themselves violently.

Rusting Cages.name: Rusting Cages
Rusting Cages.text:
You step into a half-collapsed chamber, three rusted iron cages stand in the dark here, each easily large enough to hold a person or two. The bars are mottled brown and red with age, streaked with trails of orange where water has run across the metal. A faint, sour smell lingers in the cool air, mingling dust, old iron, and something less pleasant.

One of the cages is open, the heavy door hanging slightly ajar. The other two are locked shut with rusty padlocks. As you enter, you spot movement in one of the cages.

Speaking to the Prisoners

Prisoners

Two of the cages contain haggard looking humans that are barely dressed, and look badly wounded, though one appears to be far worse off than the other.

The prisoners are two humans:

Ror'ry (Ordani human, he/him)

Dressed as Ordani native, this young man is disheveled, his fine robes stained and torn. He looks exhausted and frightened, his concerned gaze often flicking over toward the man in the cage opposite him. He is a merchant in the city, and related to the man in the other cage, who is his uncle.

Micke (Arcturian human, he/him)

An old Arcturian man, his simple garb is stained and torn, hinting at rough treatment and captivity. His body is riddled with swollen, red marks, hinting at numerous injects at the hands of the Mutagists. He leans on the bars of his cage, barely standing, a cold hatred in his eyes. He is an inventor from the plateau, and specializes in making constructs.

How were you captured?

Ror'ry explains:

My uncle Micke was coming to visit me in the city after some troubles out in the plateau damaged his farm. We were out shopping one evening, and got jumped by masked figures in black cloaks and armor. We were knocked out and woke up here.

What have they done to you?

They've been injecting us with substances and then draining our blood. I've only had it done to me once. It makes your blood burn, and fills your mind with nightmarish visions. It's like a bad dream, and it gets so bad you black out, then wake up back in the cage.

Ror'ry gestures to the man opposite hime.

They've done it several times to my uncle, I'm not sure he'll survive another. You've got to get us out of here.

What do you know about the people here?

Nothing, really. I'm sorry, they are all masked, and they barely talk to us, don't feed us…. there used to be more people here. Some humans like us, a kivahr man, a nir'ae woman. They dragged them off into the ruins behind us.

Ror'ry shudders.

There's something back there, in the darkness, I could hear it attacking them. Their screams were echoing off the stone, it was the worst thing I've ever heard… then just stopped all at once.

Can you get out of here yourself?

I probably could, yes, but my uncle looks like he can barely stand. I think you're going to have to help us, or clear the way first…

Examining the Prisoners

A successful [[/skill medicine 14]] check is necessary to examine the prisoners. They have both been subjected to multiple injections of unknown chemicals and given nothing resembling medical treatment.

Ror'ry's wounds appear to be minor, and he is in relatively good health, likely thanks to his youth. Micke however, has undergone maybe half a dozen injection cycles, has multiple infected wounds on his arms, and is running a severe fever.

Treating the Uncle

He can be stabilized with a successful [[/skill medicine 18]] check and use of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagHealersKit0]{Healer's Kit}. However,

While healing magic and potions will restore his hit points, he is badly poisoned, missing blood, and has endured several days of torture, he needs to be taken to a hospital if he is going to have any hope of survival and recovery.

Additionally, due to his injuries, he can only move at half his speed, and cannot defend himself. Luckily, his nephew is more than able and willing to help move him, but that leaves the both of them vulnerable if attacked.

No Easy Way Out

Parties that want to get the prisoners out of the ruins safely will need to first clear a safe path to the Glowing Cistern, which will allow them to get to the stairs located on the eastern side of the bridge.

Ror'ry and Micke are too weak to utilize the sunken passage by themselves, but a dedicated party with the right spells and items could extract them from the dungeon via that route if they are willing to expend the resources to do so.

Their Only Hope

It should also be noted that leaving them for the Chain to rescue will result in their deaths due to other events that are forthcoming in this quest. While the party has no way of knowing this, they should be reminded that these men are witnesses and can provide testimony if saved, and leaving them behind is a risk.

Examining the Cages

Corroded Confinement

A quick inspection reveals the locks are flimsy and worn. A character can pick any of the cage locks with only a [[/tool thief 8]] check. With a little strength, even forcing the cages open is possible with a successful [[/check str 14]] check, though the noise would likely draw attention.

Nesting Drakes

Nesting Drakes can be found in the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.PfzZhymWKN7Wom4h]. Forcing open the cages, or making too much noise will wake them, and put them on alert. However, they are used to Mutagists being in the area, and don't come to investigate initially.

Drake Den.name: Drake Den
Drake Den.text:
Cast in deep, dark shadows from the fading light of wall-mounted gems, a hollowed-out depression is heaped with stones and half-decayed remnants of some long-eaten meal.

Nesting Drakes

3 x Drakelings can be found sleeping here. A stealthy party will not alert them immediately, but attempting to pry the emblem free of the nearby relief or making too much noise wakes them without fail.

Ancient Relief

The party may want to examine the relief in greater detail, attracted by the glowing object fixt to it.

Against the wall is a stone relief of an Ashka figure clutching something to their chest. In their hands, fixed into the stone, is a glowing disk that seems to contain an active flame.

Glowing Relief

A successful [[/skill perception 14]] or [[/skill investigation 12]] concludes that the gem disc is not part of the relief, and should be easy enough to pry free with any sort of flat tool, be it prybar or dagger.

If done, the party gains a @UUID[Item.MDqjK89thWlmYBTI]{Sedyri Fire Emblem} which will be useful elsewhere.

Collapsed Ruins.name: Collapsed Ruins
Collapsed Ruins.text:
You find yourself in a tangle of ruin that has partly collapsed, with heaps of black rubble and blocks forming irregular walls and choking old corridors. Deep gouges and ragged burrows slice through the fallen stone, evidence that something immense and neither human nor tool-wise clawed or forced its way through long after the chamber's original builders vanished.

The loosened earth and stone feel unstable in places, and every small sound echoes off both solid basalt and recent scars in the rock.

Here and there glowing blue crystals fixed to the wall or sticking out of panels of stone glimmer, casting light, whatever magic held within them not quite run out yet.

Light Crystals

Fused with the stone, these intricately carved crystals are infused with magical energy that causes them to perpetually glow with blue light. There are a few of these @UUID[Item.yryDDtKeZBEJWtDi]{Fading Light Gems} sitting loose on the floor which can be claimed, if desired.

A successful [[/skill arcana 16]] check notices the subtle magical inscriptions hidden among the decorative elements in the gems, indicating the high-level of precision and capacity with magic the builders had.

However, given their age, none of them are glowing as brightly as they once did, and likely won't emit light for much longer.

Burrowing Occupants

A successful [[/skill survival 15]] identifies the markings of a larger creature with heavy claws not meant for burrowing. However, despite this, the ruins have been extensively hollowed out to allow for easy movement between the collapsed chambers.

Cistern Stockpiles.name: Cistern Stockpiles
Cistern Stockpiles.text:
Against the wall pallets crowd the floor, each laden with wooden crates packed tight with vials of emerald-green chemical giving off a faint light.

Alongside the stock, two tables sit, one brimming with a mixture of alchemical and magical implements, while the other two hold materials in support of whatever it is doing.

The air here bites with the tang of distilled chemicals and dust. At the far end, stone stairs rise steeply toward some route out of the depths, possibly to the city above.

Mutagist Contingent

Several Mutagists occupy this area.

Dangerous Minions

For combat with Kaftor and his minions see @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.iZvNkRCJPialiP0T#fighting-kaftor]{Fighting Kaftor}on the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.iZvNkRCJPialiP0T]{Glowing Cistern} page.

Searching the Area

Searching Ritual Table

A mixture of biomagic and alchemy is underway on this corner table, small-scale tests of transforming one fluid to another.

Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] note that there are reagents and implements marked with sigils and runes tied to practices of biomagic and transformative rituals meant to manipulate living beings.

Examining the circles of magic with a successful [[/skill arcana 16]] check leads you to believe it's trying to enhance or empower some effect within the fluid. To what end is unclear. Characters with either of the above knowledges have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Searching the Alchemy Table

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] recognize this setup as a rather advanced alchemical filtering and mixing station. It's taking numerous inputs and creating a new combined compound with specific mix ratios.

Nearby notes and diagrams detail the formulas at play, but it's not clear that the chemicals are or what the final goal is.

Searching the Document Table

The table is laden down with a collection of @UUID[Item.tl96BcMoSGOB5xUS] which details what the Mutagists were trying to do here. Inscrutable to anyone not properly versed in [[/knowledge alchemy]], the content is so dense that it would take months of study by an expert to make sense of what they were doing.

There are numerous crates here packed with chemicals. The sheer volume of them makes cataloging and searching them an impossibility.

Examining the Crates

Dozens of crates large and small hold a countless number of alchemical components, compounds mutagens, samples, and more. There are too many to properly catalog or search.

These will need to be left behind for the Veiled Chain to come pick up later.

Imports and Exports

Resting on one crate is a logbook that details the items coming in and out of this lab. Taking a few minutes to examine them, a worrying discovery is made: up to a week ago the lab was only importing materials, but then began exporting small batches of something initialed as "B.R."

The logbook does not list the source or destination for these shipments. This @UUID[Item.jF5hT7KEgTQ7fViy] can be taken as evidence.

Leaving the Area

The stairwell to the south of this area leads up into the sewers, and then into Ordain itself.

Meandering Exit

A party taking this exit will find themselves traveling out of the ruins into a disused section of the city sewers. After an hour of walking they then emerge from a city works access point in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.D0AAT8TNsytqy7Hm]{Quarry Run}, above ground.

Refinement Lab.name: Refinement Lab
Refinement Lab.text:
Heavy wooden slats shore up the uneven stone floor as this area opens into a intricately arranged and immaculate laboratory, fitted carefully into the ancient space here and overlooking the glimmering waters of the cistern.

Rows of shelves bear books, magical reagents and materials arranged in a determined order. Stacks of crates near the walls overflow with pristine glassware, awaiting use.

Here, two alchemical machines whir quietly, both filled with liquids being processed into glowing compounds that drip into waiting bottles below.

At the center, a large, battered desk is strewn with diagrams and scattered notes. Among the chaos, a single bottle of iridescent, multicolored fluid sits, glimmering with blue and yellow hues.

Mutagist Contingent

The overseer of this lab can be found here, sitting at his desk, working.

@embed[Actor.8jqTLAW121XrQiTN]{Mutagist Kaftor Brenk}

Deadly Overseer

For combat with Kaftor and his minions see @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.iZvNkRCJPialiP0T#fighting-kaftor]{Fighting Kaftor}on the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.iZvNkRCJPialiP0T]{Glowing Cistern} page.

Searching the Area

Supplies Shelves

This cabinet and shelving unit is packed with all sorts of reagents, spell components, and spellcasting materials. No specific list exists for the contents, but a spellcasting character that is looking for a component can probably find it here as long as the component's price is 25 gp or less.

Bookshelves

The shelves are packed with a collection of log books, papers, notes, and journals details the ongoing process that the Mutagists have been working on here.

A character with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/knowledge rituals]] recognizes that in the broadest of terms they are trying to develop a method of extracting rare ember energy from humans.

The most recent entries into this collection indicate that they achieved success, and now have a means to extract and refine what they are calling "Blaze Residuum" which can be injected into humanoids to induce an Ember Blaze effect, or Drakes to create a highly resilient mutant with similar powers.

The key articles of this collection can be taken to form a bundle of @UUID[Item.Eflvgt6PX2gK3x0Z]{Kaftor's Research Logs} which can be turned over as evidence later.

Examining the Machines

The whirring machines are slowly processing alchemical compounds into a gleaming solution that changes colors seemingly at random. The vials are presently empty but for the barest of drops, and the process seems remarkably slow.

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/knowledge machines]] recognize that these devices are very delicate, very precise, and likely had to be hand-built for the Mutagists.

Searching Kaftor's Desk

Searching the Desktop

Among all the notes and vials and tools scattered across the desk, the only item of note is a single bottle of some unknown, @UUID[Item.Nu8WVcxl15LQrPjR]{Shimmering Liquid}. Its color appears to primarily be gold, but it changes to red, pink, purple and blue seemingly at random.

The bottle bears a handwritten label:

Batch #4, Purity: 97%

Searching the Chest

The chest under the desk is locked, requiring a [[/tool thief 18]] check to successfully open. Inside the chest is 100 GP, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potion of Healing}, @UUID[Item.P1zvwO3O5PRdwiXR]{Kaftor's Spellbook}, and a letter addressed to Kaftor Brenk (see below).

[[/award 100gp]]

A Worrying Missive

Also in the chest is a @UUID[Item.ycDGxabfXRXn12at]{Concerning Missive to Kaftor}

Letter to Kaftor Brenk

The letter reads:

Overseer,

I understand your frustration, you are right: hands are tied for now, and that will not be changing immediately. I expect you to make do with what resources you do have, and would prefer you be prepared for what comes next.

Eventually you'll have a fresh supply of test subjects and assistants to work with. The influx of refugees from the west has been beneficial to recruitment efforts being made by our allies in the city.

I will be sure you get the resources you need to do your work. You need only be patient.

Wisdom and cunning guide you.

Connection to Serethus

Serethus uses the phrase "Wisdom and cunning guide you." when the party is breaking up after Ill Tidings. It's a connection that keen characters (and their players) might notice.

Marshy Grounds.name: Marshy Grounds
Marshy Grounds.text:
The land flattens out into a sprawling wetland at the foot of a roaring waterfall, its thunder echoing distantly across the basin. Water laps against slick rocks and muddy banks, the rhythmic sound only broken by the constant crash of water far overhead. Mist curls through the reeds, lending the air a chill weight.

As the wind shifts you catch the sudden stench of decaying plants and stinging chemicals. You trace the scene to its source, and find a grim sight: oily ribbons of some sickly green swirling on the surface of the waters, and rotting reeds everywhere the oil collects along the banks.

Finding the Source

Locating the source of the alchemical runoff requires some time spent searching and at least one successful check from the following options: [[/skill perception 14]], [[/skill nature 12]], or [[/skill investigation 16]].

On success the party discovers an old stone culvert.

  • A character with [[/knowledge legends]] or who makes a successful [[/skill history 14]] check additionally notes that this stone is much rougher, older, and darker than what's used in Ordain. This may be the remains of some partially submerged ruins.

Caveway.name: Caveway
Caveway.text:
Haphazard wooden walkways, built from warped planks and crude supports, wind their way above a channel of slow-moving water. The slats lashed and nailed to half-submerged beams sunk into the water, and laid across natural stone jutting up, creating a dubious path through the area.

Below, the water moves silently, carrying streaks of shimmering green fluid along its surface to parts unknown. The echoing mutter of water dampens your ability to hear much else beyond it.

Sedyri Alcoves.name: Sedyri Alcoves
Sedyri Alcoves.text:
Along the far wall of the chamber, four shallow alcoves are set into the deep black basalt, each one crowned by a weathered stone relief depicting an Ashka figure. All four snake-folk extend empty hands upward, as though holding something aloft.

The floor is strewn with the remains of several unfortunate souls, their bones shattered and gnawed, splintered, with not a shred of flesh remaining on them. Deep claw marks run through the dust beneath the alcoves, warning against careless trespass.

@embed[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG]

Radiant Resident

A nesting @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG]{Radiant Ultra Drake} can be found here. It immediately notices the party approaching unless they succeed on a group [[/skill stealth 17]] check with at least half the characters succeeding on their checks.

If alerted, it attacks.

Blazing Assault

The Radiant drake is incredibly fast, and prefers hit-and-run tactics when possible. Its @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG.Item.nvSPL1xSfF3PVueT]{Hyper-Aggressive} feature helps secure a high initiative score, and its @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG.Item.Z6egkpRJ2BaIEqhX]{Sudden Rush} legendary action lets it close in on distant targets swiftly.

When enemies are out of sight it can use it @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG.Item.9tDpbACzOw6zHqNe]{Blood Sense} to track wounded prey, setting up for its next attack, preferring to attack from blind spots and flanks.

It uses its @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG.Item.d65Nrn8arvuG365k]{Speed Burst} action to relocate and get out of harm's way, and if surrounded, has a @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG.Item.FiijGKhZYVE6p5PG]{Radiant Blast} legendary action to harm everyone nearby, though it can only do this once, and so reserves it until needed.

When reduced to 0 hit points for the first time it also activates its @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG.Item.po7u7tjNtk1X63Jv]{Final Blaze} ability, gaining an immediate turn, and also triggers its @UUID[Actor.qFtenjgNpzAPRBBG.Item.Z6egkpRJ2BaIEqhX]{Sudden Rush}.

Searching the Area

Examining the Remains

A successful [[/skill investigation 16]] or [[/skill medicine 14]] check determines that the bones are relatively new, not more than a few months or weeks old. Given that no shreds of equipment or clothing remain, it's likely the Mutagists were feeding dead bodies to the creatures here.

Examining the Reliefs

Around their feet are words in an ancient script. Characters that understand the ancient [[/language scor]] recognize these are the words: fire, water, steam, lava. The rest of the text here indicates these a resonant aspects of the Ashka spirit, and the means by which they move forward.

A successful [[/skill arcana 16]] recognizes foundational magical symbols for divination and transmutation, but they are idle. It's likely that these are part of a magical activation sequence, but what it does is unclear.

Examining the Glowing Door

An ornate wall bearing a relief of an ancient Ashka can be found on the southern wall at the top of some stairs. The Ashka's hands are clasped together.

Unlike the wall encountered in the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.TN5mwsKCSascCYgj]{Corpse Dump} area, there is nowhere for an object to be slotted into the door.

A successful [[/skill investigation 15]] check while scrutinizing the relief notes an elemental motif. Their robes have decorative elements that flow like water, but a ball of flame rests in their hands. They stand on cracked, uneven ground that looks like cooled lava, and they are surrounded by billowing clouds.

Opening the Door

Elements Under Development

The alcove puzzle and hidden doorway will have interactive elements and animations in future updates. For now the secret doorway can be manipulated manually.

The party needs to slot the four elemental emblems into the alcoves to activate the door and open the way to the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.iZvNkRCJPialiP0T]{Glowing Cistern} beyond it.

Activating the Alcoves

A successful [[/skill investigation 15]] check while scrutinizing the reliefs will notice thematic elements in each of them that hint at what element each figure embodies.

A character that has studied an alcove knows what element should go into it. The alcove elements from north to south are:

  • Fire

  • Water

  • Magma

  • Steam

Slotting an emblem into an alcove requires an action if in combat, and the order that they are placed is not important, only that the emblems be placed into the right alcoves.

Recurring Sequence

This is the same order as the pillars in the marsh, and likely the same order that the emblems were recovered in the ruins. Players that notice this pattern should be allowed to try their hunch, and be rewarded if they are right.

Once the emblems are slotted in, the door will activate, and rise up into the ceiling.

The emblems in the alcoves all pulse with energy then a deep thump shakes the ground, causing stones to tumble off of piles along the walls.

Across the room the stone wall bearing the relief of the elemental Ashka rises up into the ceiling, revealing a passage into another area.

Secluded Grave.name: Secluded Grave
Secluded Grave.text:
This cramped, half-buried chamber is half choked by rubble, the floor and one wall leaning inwards from some long-past collapse.

On the wall, a stone relief can still be made out depicting an Ashka bearing a long blade, turned with menace against an attacker who has been almost entirely destroyed by the collapse. The cross guard of their blade seems to be missing a piece.

Resting by the far wall, a simple funeral cairn of weathered stones marks the final resting place of some being.

Disturbing the Dead

If disturbed, the crumbling armor and bones shelter a circular crystal that contains water in its surface, or appears to.

The party can collect a @UUID[Item.tIzvjmEdvn1Y8sT2]{Sedyri Water Emblem} here.

The body is also wearing a @UUID[Item.Z4JfuPeLCKFCFAHO]{Scaled Hood} which is in pristine condition, despite the considerable age of the remains. Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] or [[/knowledge ancients]] recognize this as a magically infused item made by the ancient Sedyri.

Missing Emblem

A successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check while looking over the relief notes that the Ashkan warrior's armor has a fire motif.

If the party places a @UUID[Item.MDqjK89thWlmYBTI]{Sedyri Fire Emblem} into the relief's cross guard, something happens elsewhere in the ruins. Read or paraphrase the following:

The emblem lots into place and for a brief moment flames leap across the blade of the relief. A moment later you hear a heavy thud and the sound of falling rocks elsewhere in the ruins. The shock of it causes the emblem to shake loose of the cracked relief, and fall to the floor.

Moving Parts

Placing the emblem in the cross guard caused another relief in the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.pJ1iuJ9EFYeC2lW3] to move, revealing more items.

Rudely Awakened

If the party has not alerted or defeated any of the drakes in the ruins yet, they will all be awakened and put on alert. Though they won't know where to look for the party, a fight is almost guaranteed now.

Crumbling Corner.name: Crumbling Corner
Crumbling Corner.text:
Once part of a larger space, only a small section of wall and toppled supporting stone remains unburied, with the rest crushed under untold thousands of pounds of debris.

Against the wall a cracked relief of a mountain can be seen, most of its wall mounting destroyed, and scattered on the floor.

Nesting Drake

A fully grown Drake can be found here. It is sleeping, and a stealthy party will not alert them immediately, but getting too close or making noise nearby will wakes them without fail.

Ancient Relief

The party may want to examine the relief in greater detail.

Multifaceted Art

A successful [[/skill investigation 12]] concludes that the relief can't be rotated as it currently is, the damage to the surrounding structure of it has jammed it, and the stone itself is immobile.

A successful [[/skill arcana 14]] check while examining the stone notes that there are transmutation and evocation symbols carved into it. It seems likely that something can be done to magically release and turn the relief. However, there are no obvious controls present.

Rotating Relief

If the party placed a flame emblem into the cross guard of the sword in the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.EWTztq1w09YNjJVL] room, the relief's description changes.

Use the description appropriate to the status of the relief.

Initial Position

Against the wall is a stone relief of a great mountain, jagged and forbidding. Despite the age and damage, the detail work is astounding, and features numerous small details including mountainside towns, and a jungle city at the base of the mountain.

Fire Emblem Rotation

Against the wall is a stone relief of a shattered mountain, the peak of it a gaping vent. The detail work is incredible, with an ornately decorated eruption column coming from the mountain, streams of what must be lava flows, mountainside settlements in their paths, and a jungle city at the base.

Emblem Slots

Easily mistaken for damage, a passive [[/skill perception 12 passive]], successful [[/skill perception 14]] or [[/skill investigation 12]] notes that there are two circular spaces where objects could be fitted into the relief.

The first space is at the vent of the volcano, and the second is in the center of the jungle city.

Rotating the Relief

The relief is meant to accept the fire and water emblems. If the party slots those reliefs into the proper slots — fire in the vent, water in the city — the relief will rotate.

Read or paraphrase the following when that happens:

For a brief moment you watch as fire blooms in the volcano, lava flows down the mountain, and smoke roils out of the vent. Then the whole relief rumbles and shakes before rotating to reveal a new relief.

This reveals the third rotation as detailed below.

Steam Emblem Rotation

The stone relief reveals a harrowing sight: the mountain is destroyed, the settlements on its slopes are gone, and the city at its feet is now portrayed as intricately detailed ruins shot through with flows of lava that glows with a radiant light, and the stone itself seems to ripple and swirl with a haze like smoke or steam.

Fixed to the relief are two emblems, one filled with swirling gray mist, the other glowing lava.

Extracting the Emblems

The party can safely pull the emblems out of this relief. Doing so yields both the @UUID[Item.ix0HqAua2qfSBtyT] and @UUID[Item.o0q9xp29V8HHHj7S].

A moment after they are claimed the relief will spin back around, revealing the previous relief, allowing the party to reclaim the other two emblems they had initially.

Deciphering Sedyri Lore

Ancient History

Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] knows that the reliefs depict events that supposedly occurred thousands of years ago and relate to the rise and fall of the Sedyri.

A successful [[/skill history 22]] check (characters with [[/ancestry emberAshka]] have @Advantage[2]) know that the details of the Sedyiri culture and history are not well documented, mostly surviving on in Ashka communities around the world. One common element across them all are events and tragedies relating to a catastrophic volcanic eruption.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

This area map covers two distinct regions - the Lantern Roads section of Ordain, and the bottom dungeon level of the Marlstone Manor, which is labeled Wandren HQ. The map is used in two events - the party scouts it during @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.ZPv1VeLAtINtz3gv]{Revealed by Lantern} and then makes their way through the dungeon in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.jalZUo8LGHwnn7B4]{The Marlstone Gala}.

  • When scouting Lantern Roads, the party's goal is to make their way from the southern public section of the map to the restricted northern section, thus creating a path they can use during the early section of the Marlstone Gala heist.

  • During the heist itself, the party can rescue Funar Cevher from the dungeon, confront Hephiss Wandren, and escape from the dungeon back through Lantern Roads.

This map is adjacent to the@UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU]{ Marlstone Manor} map, which depicts the ground floor, second floor, and grounds of the manor that the dungeon sits beneath.

Gazetteer Page

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.oDf89SFPmQOwbe2d]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

  • While within Lantern Roads, a gate blocks easy transit between the southern and northern halves of the neighborhood, with parties needing to make their way to the north in order to find a secret entrance to Marlstone Manor. There are several ways to either directly attack or bypass this gate, as noted in the event @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.ZPv1VeLAtINtz3gv]{Revealed by Lantern}.

  • In Wandren HQ, the party will enter from Marlstone Manor above, with the goal of freeing Funar Cevher, which requires the coordination of three different switches within the dungeon, as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.91Ck26XHcgMCo88E]{Not All Who Wandren}.

  • Once the party has accomplished their goals in Wandren HQ, their easiest exit path is to leave through Lantern Roads, exiting the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.Kvdbta9WN7XnIr2l]{Sealed Entrance (A)} and emerging in the Shadowbox section of Lantern Roads.

Illumination

Outdoor spaces within Lantern Roads match the illumination of the daylight around them. Unless otherwise stated, all inside spaces have bright lighting.

Within Wandren HQ, the floor has a gentle glow, providing bright lighting unless otherwise indicated.

Terrain

Unless otherwise stated, all terrain within Lantern Roads and Wandren HQ is normal terrain.

Elevation

The map of Lantern Roads includes several elevations, with characters able to travel at ground level and across rooftops. Within Wandren HQ, ceilings are 30 feet high.

The Beacon Brigade

Members of the Beacon Brigade, a gang running a protection and smuggling racket out of Lantern Roads, are scattered throughout the area as guards and sentries. Each time they are encountered, the party has the choice to sneak by the Brigade, persuade members that they are not a threat, or fight them.

Avoiding the Beacon Brigade

With a successful Stealth check when out of a Beacon Brigade member's line of sight, characters can use the Hide action to conceal themselves, becoming temporarily Invisible.

  • Invisibility ends automatically if characters make a sound, come within the line of sight of an enemy, make an attack roll, or cast a spell with a Verbal component.

  • If a character successfully becomes invisible, the result of their stealth check is the DC of any check to perceive them. When anyone who is invisible comes with 5 feet of a Patroller or 10 feet of a Watcher, the Brigade member automatically rolls a Perception check against that DC.

Characters can use a spell or a physical effect (throwing an item, projecting their voice) to distract Brigade members as follows:

  • Patrollers are distracted by any successful cantrip, a successful [[/check 17 performance]] check for a character to throw their voice, a successful [[/check 17 athletics]] check to throw an item far enough away to make a sound, or any similar action at the game master's discretion.

  • Watchers are distracted by any successful Level 1 spell, a successful [[/check 19 performance]] check, a successful [[/check 19 athletics]] check, or any similar action at the game master's discretion.

Fooling the Beacon Brigade

Whenever a member of the Beacon Brigade is encountered, the party can try to convince them that they are either lost or should be allowed to pass. The difficulty of the check differs based on the Brigade member's role.

  • With a successful [[/check persuasion 18]] check, characters can convince a Patroller that they're on official Brigade business and can be let through. For a Watcher, they must succeed on a [[/check persuasion 20]] check.

    • Any character with [[/knowledge crime]], or who is carrying a @UUID[Item.Z0pd4LVjVusTBvqY]{Courier Bag} has @Advantage[2] on the check.

    • If characters show the Brigade member their @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}, they automatically succeed on the check.

    • If characters bribe the Brigade member with either [[/award -10gp]] or an item of Uncommon rarity or rarer, they lower the DC of the check by 3, but the Brigade member keeps the bribe even if the check fails.

@Embed[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]

@Embed[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk]

Beacon Brigade Tactics

Beacon Brigade members favor using their items to attack. Patrollers often throw @UUID[Item.JKWt3ZZKBaEvNbw1]{Choking Fog Dust} to incapacitate targets before striking. Once engaged in melee combat, they immediately use an action to fill their Hallowed Dagger with a poison and strike.

Beacon Brigade Watchers help to find hidden enemies and direct Patroller attention by using their @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk.Item.e7jBM8stpBBfK46e]{Spotlight Shot} to light up areas in the distance. Patrollers who are within range of one of the spotlights will move to subdue any enemies revealed by the light as soon as they can, even if this means disrupting a previously planned action.

The Guards in Wandren HQ

Strange Guards with Strange Torches

All human guards within Wandren HQ are secretly Celestial creatures If hurt or injured, they change shape into the form of strange celestial creatures called @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR]{Kynryth}.

Defeating a Kynryth gives characters access to a lit @UUID[Item.5ABf86cbSTOxtMcs]{Kynryth Torch}, which is used to activate the switches needed by the party to rotate the make their way into the Central Chamber.

Holding Cells.name: Holding Cells
Holding Cells.text:
Metal walls divide this small prison into smaller holding cells, each large enough to fit a single captive. Beyond the smell of sweat and stink, there is the distinctive scent of acrid smoke, as if someone or something within these walls was set aflame.

Opening Funar's Holding Cell

The door to Funar's Holding Cell is much less well protected than the main door to the holding area. It can be opened or destroyed if the party does any of the following:

  • Break the lock with pure strength with a successful [[/check strength 18]] check. If this attempt is made unarmed/without any tools, it is made with @Advantage[-2].

  • Pick the lock with a successful [[/check sleightofhand 17]] with Thieves' Tools.

  • Secure a key from the desk in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.lG34JIEVsTljNQ2S]{Holding Cells Antechamber}

The Empty Holding Cells

The remaining holding cells are mostly (but not all) empty. They can be quickly scanned without a check to determine if there is anything of value.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.FCyzU6d0xvP857xU]{The Bare Holding Cell}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.Mpdi2qnl0ztfOdEe]{Cell with a Scratched Wall}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.PcjhmdjTXypzGM8q]{Cell with a Half-Dressed Skeleton}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.B5MR72gI1i4NNP22]{Cell with Gnawed Remains}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.gkI6hYkQSbUHOs44]{The Cell with Empty Chains}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.VrzOTZDO6rEedMHj]{The Cell with a Stained Floor}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.PzmW9oo1Hjf1afp9]{The Scorched Cell}

Stairway Entrance.name: Stairway Entrance
Stairway Entrance.text:
Locating Funar Cevher

If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is adjacent to this room (in a room directly above, below, or next to it).

  • With an additional charge of the rod, the party can determine that Funar is in a room next to this room.

The dark stone of the spiral staircase exits into a narrow hallway whose smooth glowing floors and hum of activity promise something completely different than the elegant manor that sits above.

This stairway connects Marlstone Manor and Wandren HQ. Once used by characters, it remains unlocked until Hephiss appears in the facility in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.91Ck26XHcgMCo88E#a-final-battle]{A Final Battle}, at which point it is locked and cannot be used as an exit.

Central Chamber.name: Central Chamber
Central Chamber.text:
Locating Funar Cevher

If the party uses the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod} in this area, they find that Funar Cevher is adjacent to this room (in a room directly above, below, or next to it).

  • With an additional charge of the rod, the party can determine that Funar is in a room next to this room.

When Entering The Chamber

Beneath the glassy floor at the edge of the chamber, metal gears move with a relentless rhythm that is interrupted only by a faint and consistent thumping sound. The curve of the large metal dome in front of you, by contrast, sits absolutely still, shielding nearly everything in the chamber ahead from your view.

Investigating the Chamber

Characters who inspect the chamber learn the following:

  • The Metal Gears in the Floor: With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check, characters notice that only some of the gears around the edge of the room are turning.

    • With a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check or [[/knowledge machines]], they can tell that the turning gears are attached to something outside of the central chamber.

  • The Sound of Thumping:

    • Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 15]] check, or who have [[/check perception 17 passive]] can clearly hear a thumping sound, like someone banging on a wall, coming from outside of the chamber.

      • If they succeed on the check by 3 or more, or has [[/check perception 20 passive]], they can pinpoint the origin of the sound as coming from near the Western Entrance of the Central Chamber and hear muffled shouting beneath the thumping.

The Metal Domes

The primary object within this chamber is the set of nested metal domes in the center. Characters can only see the outermost of these when they enter.

The walls of the dome seem to glow from within, producing a faint golden light that you can feel as much as see, as if some slight vibration has settled on your skin and begun worming its way in.

Investigating The Outer Dome Wall

The Outer Dome wall has been coated in @UUID[Item.TwsLk1KC8SqDbL8G]{Thieves' Lament}, an alchemical substance that burns those who touch it and scars the hands.

  • Characters who use the Identify or Detect Magic spell find no evidence of magical properties in or around the wall. Spells cannot travel through the dome to the interior walls.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 15]] check or have [[/check perception 17 passive]] can see a slight sheen on the metal where the substance was painted on.

    • Characters who succeed on a [[/check nature 18]] check, or who have [[/knowledge alchemy]] know that it is an alchemical substance of some sort. It has soaked into the wall and cannot be removed for further study.

If characters strike the wall, they can hear a faint echo without a check:

The sound of your strike echoes from the other side of the wall, as if there is some emptiness on the other side of it, but it soon fades into the background hum.

Touching the Outer Dome Wall

If characters put their hands against the wall, they are subjected to the effects of @UUID[Item.TwsLk1KC8SqDbL8G]{Thieves' Lament}.

If characters walk around the dome, they find the opening in the Outer Wall without a check.

The wall ends in a small opening marked by a deep groove in the floor. On the other side, only a few feet away, is another metal wall. It looks similar to the first, but there is a faint sizzling in the air around it, as it if is charged with some kind of energy.

Investigating The Middle Dome Wall

Characters who succeed on a [[/check arcana 17]] check, or who use the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} (or a similar spell), know that the wall has been magically altered to give an electric shock to anyone who touches it and that it is being fed by magical energy from a source nearby.

If @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic}or a similar spell is used on the wall, it loses its hum and has no negative effects when touched, but this only lasts for 10 minutes. After that time the wall is armed again.

Touching the Middle Dome Wall

If the middle wall of the dome is touched while it is active, it immediately crackles with energy and discharges a bolt of electric energy. Whoever is touching the wall must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d6 lightning]] damage.

As the energy courses through you, sending a jolt of pain through your body, an image comes to your mind - fire, as glorious as the sun, being held in the hands of a powerful creature.

If characters align the first two rings, the inner ring is exposed. If characters approach it while it is still closed, it hums with power.

The hum in the room intensifies as you draw closer to the inner ring of the metal — unlike the others, there is no glow, but you feel a heat beneath your own skin, as if the vibration wants nothing more than to melt you down and remake you.

Investigating the Inner Dome Wall

Dangers of the Inner Dome Wall: Characters who succeed on a [[/check arcana 18]] check, or who use the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} (or a similar spell), know that the wall has been magically altered to send radiant energy at anyone who passes through its opening into the center of the chamber.

The Vibration in the Air: The feeling of a vibration in the air is a combination of the machinery and the use of celestial energy.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 15]] check or [[/knowledge machines]] , characters know that some of the vibration in the air is from the metal gears that power the facility, but not all of it.

  • With a successful [[/check arcana 16]] check or [[/knowledge cosmos], characters know that there is a magical energy in the air that contributes to the vibration and that the source of the magic is different than that typically found and used on Ember.

Touching The Inner Dome Wall

When characters pass through the opening of the inner dome, they must make a [[/save constitution 16]] saving throw - on a failure, they take [[/damage 1d6 radiant]] damage from the dome wall.

Aligning The Chamber Rings

The positioning of the domes within the Central Chamber is controlled from switches in the Wandren HQ Training Room, Construction Room, and Blessing Room, as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.91Ck26XHcgMCo88E#reaching-the-central-chamber]{Reaching The Central Chamber} .

The Inner Chamber Revealed

Once all three rings are aligned, characters can enter the inner chamber:

Inside of the interlocking metal shells is a tangle of machinery that looks as if it has come to life within its metallic cocoon, with thick golden vine-like cords all grasping in different directions, extending like arms from a curved metal control station along the inner chamber wall. Between them, the table is covered with levers and etched glowing tiles, which emit plumes of light in a rhythmic pattern that seems as if it must have some meaning.

But all of this is the backdrop. In the center of the metal circle, within a silver metal band on the floor that even the intertwined cords won't touch, a creature is suspended in a beam of silver light.

Investigating the Inner Chamber

The console in the center of the inner chamber is divided into four sections, each with a glowing panel in its center that is etched with a single word in a language other than Common or Arcden and surrounded by various buttons and levers.

Characters who take a closer look can determine the following:

  • With a successful [[/check history 16]] check, [[/language harmos]], or [[/knowledge celestials]], they know that the writing on the console panels is in Harmos, the language used by the Tyraphem who dwell in the inner plane of Luxarum.

    • Any characters who know [[/language harmos]] can read the writing - the panels read "Hold."

The Beam of Light: Characters who succeed on a [[/check arcana 16]] check, or who use the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} (or a similar spell), can identify the beam of light as a field of imprisoning magic generated from a Holding Ring built into the center of the floor.

  • If characters succeed on their arcana check by 3 or more, or if they have [[/knowledge celestials]], they can tell that this magic has its source in the inner realm of Luxarum, where the Tyraphem dwell.

A Prismatic Beam

The edge of the beam of light operates similarly to a Prismatic Wall - any character who touches it must make a [[/save constitution 16]] saving throw.

  • Regardless of the result of the check, they are pushed back 10 feet.

  • If the saving throw fails, they also take [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage from the concussive force.

If characters attempt to go inside of the beam of light or speak to the creature within it, it immediately speaks to them. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.91Ck26XHcgMCo88E#meeting-the-prisoner]{Meeting The Prisoner}).

Investigating the Console

Characters who look closely at the Console can discover the following:

  • Light flashes in the panels in each section of the Console in a different pattern. With a successful [[/check investigation 16]] check or [[/knowledge machines]], characters see that the lights all pause for a moment at the same time in each cycle.

  • If characters touch a single panel, it holds its glow for a few seconds, and then begins repeating its cycle.

    The panel glows a little more brightly for a moment, then begins to fade.

  • If characters touch two or three panels at the same time, they glow more strongly.

    The panels all glow for the same amount of time, becoming brighter still, and they feel almost warm beneath your touch.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check investigation 17]] check can determine that pressing all four console lights at the same time will deactivate the central cage.

Stasis.name: Stasis
Stasis.text:
Large metallic creatures sit at the edges of the wall, a faint glow beneath their arms. They do not stir as you enter the room, but the gears beneath your feet appear to move faster.

The husks in thhis room will not move or take action unless a party member comes within 5 feet of them.

@Embed[Actor.VyWFhpROA1S5Icsg count=2]

The Kynryth Husks

If characters previously encountered a Kynryth Husk, they recognize this as the same creature. If they have previously encountered a @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR]{Kynryth}, they recognize that this creature is nearly identical.

  • With a [[/check perception 15]] check or [[/knowledge monsters]], characters notice that the husks are missing the flame that is typically found within the center of a Kyrnyth body.

  • With a [[/check history 16]] check or [[/knowledge celestials]], characters are aware that this is a celestial creatures, and that most celestials are a combination of a metal carapace and a radiant flame that provides sentience. Without it, the creature can move and attack, but is limited in its actions.

If the party comes within 5 feet of either Kynryth Husk, it attacks.

Kynryth Husk Tactics

Kynryth husks strike at whatever is closest to them, switching targets if their current target moves out of range, They show no real signs of strategy, but can still do damage with their @UUID[Actor.VyWFhpROA1S5Icsg.Item.4jpxd2WvMWh9On5A]{Tentacle Grab} and @UUID[Actor.VyWFhpROA1S5Icsg.Item.kQPuyDqQxBjgA1iY]{Tentacle Swipe}.

If given Radiant Flame by a Tyraphem or another Celestial Creature (via the Kynryth's @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.tk64nySGm5puF89S]{Share Flame}, for example), they transform via@UUID[Actor.VyWFhpROA1S5Icsg.Item.QVvYNvVlia62c7V5]{ Receive Flame} into full @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR]{Kynryth}.

Assemblyworks.name: Assemblyworks
Assemblyworks.text: Alcoves along the walls, filled with wires, feel as if they are waiting for something to occupy them. The answer may be at the back of the room, where a partially-constructed metallic creature sits motionless, as if waiting for a command.

Construction Room.name: Construction Room
Construction Room.text:
Metal tables covered with wires and cords and tools line the wall of the room. It has seemingly been abandoned, though there is a wheel protruding from a back wall, and as you draw closer you see a hint of movement out of the corner of your eye.

With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check or [[/check perception 18 passive]], characters see the movement of one of the three creatures hidden among the objects on the table. These are@UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{ Skithers}, who immediately attack.

@Embed[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0 count=3]

Skither Tactics

If the party detected the Skithers before the attack, the Skithers are surprised. If they did not, the party is surprised.

Once battle begins, the Skithers attempt to stay close together to take @Advantage[2] of their @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.UaSFbeDp4UQqHs4j]{Pack Tactics} ability, but will block the exits to the room if they can. Skithers primarily attack directly using @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.kIbBwGuzxy7FN4xT]{Rend}, but if the party is confined in a tight space, will use @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.hZGnt69Mp5meOQlq]{Self Sacrifice} to damage the party with a dying action.

Each Skither may use @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.BcQr384uRlEgdb3r]{Tyraphic Sending} to send a message to the Aburyx located in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.H35C2AzPnmV9gxJM]{Training Room}, but will avoid this action until they are at half-health or lower.

Characters who have previously encountered the Skither, or have [[/knowledge celestials]] know that Skithers are often used to assemble and care for machines on Luxarum, the inner realm inhabited by the celestial Tyraphem.

Characters who search through the pieces on the table for 10 minutes, or who succeed on a [[/check perception 16]] check can find two metal sheets. They each hold a diagram and a word engraved in a language other than Common.

The Metal Sheets

Characters who examine the sheets of engraved metal may discover the following:

  • The language on the sheets is [[/language harmos]]. Characters who have seen other writing in this language in the facility, have knowledge of the language, have [[/knowledge celestials]], or succeed on a [[/check 16 history]] check know that the sheets have Harmos writing on them, used by those from the inner realm Luxarum.

    • Anyone who can read [[/language harmos]] knows that the labels for the three sheets are Assembly, Blessing, and Control.

  • The first sheet (Assembly) has pictures of many small pieces and gears on the edges of the sheet and a large metallic creature with tentacles in the center.

  • A diagram on the second sheet (Blessing) shows two of the metallic creatures - one on the top of the page and one on the bottom. In the center is a large flame. An arrow points between the top creature and the flame and then between the flame and the bottom creature.

  • The third sheet (Control) shows a flame above a wheel, and an arrow that indicates that the wheel should be turned.

The Wheel on the Wall

This wheel is identical to those found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.B76pBYkMuExLBuLz]{Blessing Chamber} and @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.mkFgusDGto1PI97p]{Construction Room} and operates in the same fashion. If characters have already operated one of the other wheels, they recognize it immediately.

Identifying the Torch Holder

Characters can clearly see the wheel on the wall, and the torch holder above it, without a check.

The metal wheel juts out of the wall as if molded from the same piece of metal. Directly above it sits a small hoop, jutting out from the same wall.

Characters who examine the hoop and succeed on a [[/check 15 perception]] check note the smooth edges, as if something has been routinely used in that slot, wearing down the edges over time.

  • With a success of 3 or more, characters also note a small amount of damage around the torch holder slot from whatever was placed in it. It is similar to the damage that would be caused by a large amount of heat.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check history 17]] check or have [[/knowledge celestials]] recognize the hoop as a torch holder that is used to hold a source of radiant fire.

Using the Torch Holder

Any torches that the characters have on them will fit into the torch holder slot, but nothing happens when they are placed.

You can hear a slight click as the torch is placed in the torch holder, and it shifts downward slightly, but there is no other effect.

The wheel does not and will not move until characters put a @UUID[Item.5ABf86cbSTOxtMcs]{Lit Kynryth Torch} in the torch holder.If characters light their own torches (or any stick of a similar size) in the radiant fire in the bowl, it becomes a @UUID[Item.5ABf86cbSTOxtMcs]{Lit Kynryth Torch}. They may also acquire one from a defeated Kynryth in the immediate aftermath of its death.

Once a proper torch has been put in the torch holder, the wheel extends from the wall.

With an audible echoing click, the wheel in the wall begins to glow, ever-so-slightly, and it extends further from the wall.

Turning the Wheel

If the torch holder has not been used, the wheel cannot be turned, but once it has extended from the wall, it is easily turned without a check. Each time the wheel is turned a quarter turn, the Middle Dome in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.BMf5Vme1UwrRNa2J]{Central Chamber} rotates, as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.91Ck26XHcgMCo88E#reaching-the-central-chamber]{Reaching The Central Chamber}, making a deep grinding noise that can be heard throughout the facility without a check.

Blessing Chamber.name: Blessing Chamber
Blessing Chamber.text:
A large flame flickers and dances from its position on the metal platform at the far end of the room, casting light that bounces off of the still metal carapaces in the room's many alcoves, a wheel affixed to a back wall, and the slowly turning metal gears below.

@Embed[Actor.VyWFhpROA1S5Icsg count=3]

The husks in the room's alcoves will not move or take action unless a party member comes within 5 feet of them.

The Chamber In Motion

Once the party reaches the center of the room, one of the alcoves activates, bringing the next Kyrnyth forward.

At first, the metallic creatures in the alcoves of the room stand still and silent, as if devoid of life or free will - the only movement in the chamber the slow turn of the gears in the channels beneath their feet. Then, slowly, one of the creatures begins inching forward, its legs unmoving as it glides across the room, moving at the same steady pace as the gears beneath it.

Gamemasters Note: Forward Motion

The Kynryth Husks in the alcove move, one at a time, along the path of exposed gears from their alcoves towards the flame, beginning with the Kynryth to the Southeast and moving counter-clockwise. If combat ensues, on each turn, move the Kynryth that is currently being transported by the gears along its path 10 feet.

  • If the husk ends its turn within 5 feet of a party member, it attacks as noted above.

  • If the husk reaches the flame at the far end of the room, its @UUID[Actor.VyWFhpROA1S5Icsg.Item.QVvYNvVlia62c7V5]{Receive Flame} feature is activated and it transforms into a full Kynryth.

If the party approaches the central platform containing the flame, a Kynryth is revealed behind it.

As the otherworldly flame on the platform across the room dances and glows, a shadow on the wall behind it writhes, its many limbs twisting and splaying in impossible directions. After a long moment, the source of the shadow steps out from behind the flames - a metallic creature, filled with the same glowing flame from the platform.

@Embed[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR]

Kynryth Tactics

The Kynryth in this room will attempt to use @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.tk64nySGm5puF89S]{Share Flame} to activate any Kynryth Husks in the vicinity as its priority, moving towards them while using its@UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.4jpxd2WvMWh9On5A]{Tentacle Grab} and @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.kQPuyDqQxBjgA1iY]{Tentacle Swipe} to clear a path.

While within 20 feet of the flame on the platform, it uses its Inner Light features frequently, returning to the flame to refill and recharge. When further from the platform, or if cut off from its light, it is more hesitant, only using @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.QVyuVvQsMOfHFmZH]{Burst of Speed} in its effort to reach the other Kynryth.

Training Room.name: Training Room
Training Room.text:
Weapons and targets of all types line the walls of this long room. A Wandren guard shows off their knife throwing, aiming at a target that is wearing the clothing of a woman dressed for an Ordani ball. Nearby, a creature whose metallic arms extend from the ball of fire in the center of their torso sits still.

The party may choose to move through the area with stealth, or face an immediate combat. Any creatures that are not defeated while in this room come to assist Hephiss Wandren during the party's final battle with her.

Moving With Stealth

The party's ability to sneak through the room depends in part on which creatures they are sneaking by and their general direction.

Creeping Up on the Aburyx

If characters enter the Training Room through its connection to the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.lG34JIEVsTljNQ2S]{Holding Cells Antechamber}, they can attempt to subdue the Aburyx before being spotted.

With a successful [[/check stealth 20]] check, the Aburyx is surprised in any combat, and is unaware of any other attempts made against to hold or subdue it until after they are attempted.

Sneaking Through The Training Room

If characters enter the Training Room through its connection to @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.2tuIUsLppUwZhDqn]{Closet 1}, they must lure the Wandren Guard in the doorway away or they will immediately be drawn into combat.

  • The guard can be lured away in a similar fashion as a member of the Beacon Brigade (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.EH0ilpRL8UoqUQQM#the-beacon-brigade]{Beacon Brigade)}.

  • If the party enters the room without fighting the Wandren Guard in the doorway, they can move through the room without the enemies noticing with a successful [[/check stealth 22]] stealth check.

Fighting The Enemies

The creatures turn towards you. Beyond them, the radiant being sitting at a small desk chuckles, with a sound like flickering flames.

Perfect. Now you can face a real challenge.

Creature Tactics

The Aburyx, Kynryth, and Wandren Patroller each have their own individual tactics.

Aburyx Tactics: The@UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{ Aburyx }prefers to keep its distance if possible, using @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0.Item.2sV9jgOZ9nL7oT2d]{Beckoning} to summon Skithers and@UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0.Item.o073sZpHxpgrYyCA]{ Reckoning} to detonate them, using them as a ranged weapon. Once it has used up both of its uses of this action, it advances on the closest creature to it for melee combat with @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0.Item.DZy1UHEEyWgMG04M]{Cleaving Light}.

Kynryth Tactics: @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR]{Kynryth} primarily uses its tentacles to strike out, using @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.4jpxd2WvMWh9On5A]{Tentacle Grab} and @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.kQPuyDqQxBjgA1iY]{Tentacle Swipe}. It uses its special abilities, @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.lq7GsU73yDlkGRmn]{Throw Fire} and @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR.Item.QVyuVvQsMOfHFmZH]{Burst of Speed}, only if cornered.

Wandren Patroller Tactics: The Wandren Patroller immediately advances forward, attempting melee combat. If it takes any damage, it transforms into a @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR]{Kynryth} on its following turn, using all of its actions to do so.

The Central Chamber Controls

Closet 1.name: Closet 1
Closet 1.text:
Boxes of mundane storage sit neatly piled, with labels reading paper, fabric, gems, and the like.

Searching the Storage Room

With a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check of the storage, the party discovers a bag of valuable gems worth [[/award 5gp]].

Closet 2.name: Closet 2
Closet 2.text:
The storage on this side of the closet feels more mechanical and otherworldly than anything else - strange gears, unexplained tools, and items that seem to vibrate just the slightest bit whenever anyone draws near.

Searching the Storage Room

A search of the storage room yields nothing of value.

Storage Room.name: Storage Room
Storage Room.text:
Boxes lay scattered across the floor of the room. Dust and spiderwebs give the sense that they haven't been touched in quite some time.

If the party encounters this room while exploring Lantern Roads, read or summarize the following:

As you make your way through the boxes, you can feel a slight hum in the air that you can't quite place the origin or direction of.

Investigating the Room

Characters who have [[/knowledge machines]] or who succeed on a [[/check perception 17]] check to listen more closely can tell that there is a machine or gears working in the distance.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check investigation 17]] check can tell that the boxes have been specifically arranged to allow for a direct route to the back of the room.

If characters make it to the back of the room, they find the door to the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.H35C2AzPnmV9gxJM]{Training Room}. This door cannot be opened.

If the party encounters this room while leaving Wandren HQ, they can open the door and move through it without a check.

Shadow Players Theater.name: Shadow Players Theater
Shadow Players Theater.text:
Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

  • Shadowbox Alleys: Going through this building gives players access to the Shadowbox Alleys. The shopkeeper and guard within the shop want to stop the party from heading in that direction.

There is no information about the rooftop route or via bluffing.

The Front Room

Large puppets and small pieces of furniture line the walls of the shop, tended to by a solitary shopkeeper. A single customer stands towards the back of the shop, near an entrance to the room beyond, staring forward, seemingly uninterested in the goods around them.

As you enter, the shopkeeper seems vaguely surprised to see you.

Oh, hello. And welcome to the Shadow Players Theater. Really more of a museum, if I'm being honest. A monument to the Shadow Players in all their glory.

The customer clears their throat, loudly, and the shopkeeper continues, releasing all of their words in a single rush of air.

But this part of town isn't what it used to be and you should probably go around and head back the other way.

The Shopkeeper and the Guard

The "customer," who is really a guard, wants the party to leave immediately. Characters who succeed on a [[/check insight 17]] check know that the customer is a guard and that the shopkeeper is supposed to keep people from going into the back.

Though the shopkeeper doesn't want to speak much under the guard's watchful eye, if characters distract or subdue the guard, or succeed on a [[/check persuasion 18]] check, can learn the following:

  • The theater was once successful, but the growing influence of the Beacon Brigade has left it empty for some time. They are also the reason that there is a guard watching over the displays.

  • Beyond the theater is Shadowbox Alley, where there are picturesque shadowbox windows that using magic and light to create moving images.

  • The shopkeeper doesn't recommend hanging around the alleys, but there is a divination shop in the area, and the shadowboxes themselves are beautiful. If characters go in through the side entrance, they may be able to head up to take a peek without alerting the guard.

The Storage Room

The storage room has old props and boxes in it, but contains nothing of real value.

The Empty Theater

Entering Via the Side Door

The side door to the Shadow Players is locked, but can be opened with a successful [[/check dexterity 16]] check using Thieves' Tools. Characters must succeed on a [[/check stealth 17]] check to avoid being seen by the store owner and guard in the front room.

Though the stage and assortment of chairs give the sense that this may have, at one time, hosted small performances or events, the stage is covered in a thick layer of dust and most of the chairs have been toppled on their sides. Only the stairs leading up to a landing above look as if they have seen any use in years.

Parties can exit through the stairs without a check. If they walk through the dusty section of the theater, they kick up a choking dust.

A Dusty Floor

The remains of Dust of Sneezing and Choking are on the ground. If characters walk over it, they must attempt a [[/save dexterity 17]] check or they suffer the effects of the Fog.

Vitt's Candy Shop.name: Vitt's Candy Shop
Vitt's Candy Shop.text:
Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

  • Shadowbox Alleys: Characters can pursue the Shadowbox Alleys path to Beacon Brigade territory by searching the vicinity of the shop. An entrance to the Beacon Brigade side of town can be found by going past or through Hettie's Divinations.

There is no information about the rooftop route or bluffing in this area.

Outside of the Shop

If there was ever a shadowbox in this picture window, a thick layer of dust prevents you from seeing anything inside. Above the dusty window frame, a wooden sign reads Vitt's Candies, but there is no indication that anyone has been in or out anytime recently.

The door to the shop is closed, but not locked.

The Beacon Brigade

A @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Patroller} guards the stairway behind the shop. They remain there and will not emerge unless party members attack or call attention to themselves. In addition to the general options available when encountering members of @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.EH0ilpRL8UoqUQQM#the-beacon-brigade]{The Beacon Brigade}:

  • Characters have @Advantage[2] on persuasion checks with the Patroller if they offer a piece of candy taken from the store.

  • If characters encounter the Patroller after exiting Wandren HQ via the Storage Room, the Patroller is surprised.

Inside of The SHop

If the party heads inside, they find the shop unoccupied.

The inside of the shop is just as dusty as the outside, with one major exception - the shop's side window has been kept relatively clean. Through it, you can clearly see a stairway headed down.

If the party hasn't yet dealt with the @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Beacon Brigade Patroller} in the stairway, they can clearly see the Patroller through the window.

Hettie's Divinations.name: Hettie's Divinations
Hettie's Divinations.text:
Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

  • Shadowbox Alleys: Characters can pursue the Shadowbox Alleys path to Beacon Brigade territory by searching the vicinity of the shop. An entrance to the Beacon Brigade side of town can be found by going past or through Hettie's Divinations.

There is no information about the rooftop route or bluffing in this area.

Outside Of The Shop

The shadows in the window of the shop are constantly in motion, creating one constellation and then another, before spelling out the words Hettie's Divinations.

Trapped Alleyway

The narrow alleyway between Hettie's Divinations and Ordani Imports contains a spike trap coated with Paralyzing Poison and rigged to alarm the Beacon Brigade.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 17]] check can detect the trap beneath the wooden floorboards.

  • The trap can be disarmed by succeeding on a [[/check 18 sleightofhand]] check.

  • If the trap cannot be disarmed, or a party member steps on it without disarming it, spikes shoot up from the ground.

    • Anyone who has stepped on the trap must make a [[/save dexterity 17]] saving throw.

    • On a failure, they take [[/damage 1d10 piercing]] damage and are inflicted with Paralyzing Poison.

    • On a success, they take half damage. In addition, the trap triggers an alarm bell that alerts any members of the Beacon Brigade within 60 feet.

Inside Of The shop

The smell of incense wafts towards you as you make your way inside the shop. It is neat and tidy and appears to be in fairly regular use, lit by various small candles and a glowing crystal ball in the center of a ceremonial table, but at the moment the chairs around it are empty.

If this is the party's first time entering the shop:

No sooner have you stepped inside the front door than a voice calls out from around a corner.

Vitt, I'm a diviner, not a miracle worker. You'll have your money next week, same as —

The voice cuts off as a Kiska woman appears from around the corner.

Oh, I'm sorry. You're not…forget all of that. Please. How may I help you look into your future today?

A Reading From Hettie

Hettie (N female kiska) will speak with the party, but only if a member of the party sis down for a reading with her.

  • She prefers to be paid in "interesting items" than cash - an item is considered "interesting" if it is worth 2 GP or more, or if it is an item of uncommon rarity or rarer.

  • She will accept 20 GP [[/award -20gp]] but anyone who pays in cash has @Advantage[-2] on persuasion checks.

  • With a successful [[/check persuasion 26]] check, she will give the reading for free.

@Embed[RollTable.rtfXAcklcMUghWSL inline rollable]

A Conversation with Hettie

Once the reading concludes, Hettie will reveal any of the following:

  • Vitt Wandren is the leader of the Beacon Brigade.

  • Vitt has been extorting her and other shopkeepers around the city for months.

  • Vitt has always been annoying, but in recent years, they've become somewhat powerful thanks to making new friends.

    • With a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] check, she will reveal that the new friend in question is Hephiss Wandren.

  • The entrance to Marlstone near Vitt's candy shop can only be opened from within Marlstone — to get to Marlstone, the party will have to go through the Brigade's territory.

  • Hettie feels uncomfortable letting the party use the entrance to Brigade territory near her shop for fear of retribution.

    • With a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] check, she can be persuaded to look the other way, but the party will still have to sneak by (@UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.3OLRx43NmH9WaSXB#sneaking-past-hettie]{"Sneaking" Past Hettie}).

Returning To The Shop

As you step into the shop again, Hettie is nowhere to be seen, though you can hear a faint humming from behind the closed door in the middle of the shop.

"Sneaking" Past Hettie
