If the party came to an agreement with Hettie, they can pass by her shop and into Brigade territory as long as they do not come within 10 feet of her, take anything from her shop, or critically fail the Hide actions. All Hide actions to sneak by automatically succeed unless the party member rolls a critical failure.

  • If the party comes within 10 feet of Hettie, takes her property, or critically fails the Hide action, she calls out:

    You're not very good thieves, are you? I'm going to call for help, but I'll take my time about it. You should be able to be to the other side by then.

    While she makes no immediate moves, Hettie does alert the Beacon Brigade (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.3OLRx43NmH9WaSXB#on-alert]{On Alert}).

Actually Sneaking Past Hettie

If the party could not convince Hettie to help them, they can attempt to sneak by her by using the Hide action with a successful [[/check stealth 17]] check. If the check is failed, she alerts the Beacon Brigade (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.3OLRx43NmH9WaSXB#on-alert]{On Alert}) and calls for the nearest Patroller. Any Patroller with 100 feet of Hettie immediately begins moving toward her to intercept the intruders.

On Alert

If Hettie alerts the Beacon Brigade that there has been a breach, the party has @Advantage[-2] on all persuasion and Hide actions while interacting with the members of the Beacon Brigade going forward.

Local Treasures.name: Local Treasures
Local Treasures.text:
Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

  • Shadowbox Alleys: Characters can pursue the Shadowbox Alleys path to Beacon Brigade territory by searching the vicinity of the shop. An entrance to the Beacon Brigade side of town can be found by going past or through Hettie's Divinations.

There is no information about the rooftop route or bluffing in this area.

Outside of The Shop

Beneath a sign that reads "Local Treasures," a large shadowbox windows displays a large silhouette of the Ordani skyline that almost seems to move, as if the city is alive with energy. The movements are constant and rhythmic, and follow a pattern, as if they reflect something in the room behind the shadowbox that you can't quite see.

Observing the Shadowbox

Inside the shop, a pair of Beacon Brigade members is putting money into bags and loading them into a nearly-full chest.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check, characters can hear the sounds of coins clinking and heavy objects being placed down inside the shop.

    • If the check succeeds by 3 or more, characters can also hear a faint murmuring between two different individuals and make out the following:

      When we're done counting this up, I'm getting a nice long drink back at the Barracks.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check, characters can take a look at the pattern of movement and tell that there are likely two individuals inside making repetitive motions.

Seeing Behind The Shadowbox

If characters wish to see what is behind the shadowbox window, they must cast light on the shadowbox from outside. This can be done using any spell that casts light, including @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLight00000]{Light}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDancingLig]{Dancing Lights}, or similar, or by lighting a conventional torch or candle.

Once the source of light is within 10 feet of the window, the party can clearly see what is happening inside, but are visible to any members of the Beacon Brigade who are inside the shop or within 30 feet of the light source.

If characters see behind the shadowbox, they observe two members of the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.EH0ilpRL8UoqUQQM#the-beacon-brigade]{The Beacon Brigade} counting money:

Where the image of the Ordani streets once stood, you can clearly see a pair of locals counting up coins and putting it in bags. The bags are being loaded into a chest, which looks as if it is almost full.

Inside the Shop

Two locals are counting money, which they put into bags in a large crate.

The Beacon Brigade

The two locals counting money are both @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Patrollers} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.EH0ilpRL8UoqUQQM#the-beacon-brigade]{The Beacon Brigade}. They will attack the party on sight.

Searching the Shop

When empty, characters can search the shop without a check.

  • The books and other small trinkets scattered on the countertops have no particular value.

  • The chest on the floor is filled with 15 @UUID[Item.kY9aP3qlK3nJDWhX]{bags of bronze coins}.

Ordani Imports.name: Ordani Imports
Ordani Imports.text:
Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

  • Shadowbox Alleys: Characters can pursue the Shadowbox Alleys path to Beacon Brigade territory by searching the vicinity of the shop. An entrance to the Beacon Brigade side of town can be found by going past or through Hettie's Divinations.

There is no information about the rooftop route or bluffing in this area.

Outside Of The Shop

The shadowbox underneath the sign Ordani Imports displays a silhouette of a ship moving across the waves from one side of the window to the other. When it moves out of sight on the far side of the window, it appears again on the near side, creating a sense that the ship is always in motion.

No one is currently inside Ordani imports.

Outside Observations

Before going inside the shop, the party can observe the following:

  • With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check, characters note the absolute lack of sound from inside the store.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check of the door, characters can see that the hinges of the door have been greased and there is no dust around them. It's likely the door has been

  • The door to the shop has been left unlocked.

  • There is a narrow passageway between Ordani Imports and Hettie's Divinations (the Trapped Alleyway, noted below).

Trapped Alleyway

The narrow alleyway between Hettie's Divinations and Ordani Imports contains a spike trap coated with Paralyzing Poison and rigged to alarm the Beacon Brigade.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 17]] check can detect the trap beneath the wooden floorboards.

  • The trap can be disarmed by succeeding on a [[/check 18 sleightofhand]] check.

  • If the trap cannot be disarmed, or a party member steps on it without disarming it, spikes shoot up from the ground.

    • Anyone who has stepped on the trap must make a [[/save dexterity 17]] saving throw.

    • On a failure, they take [[/damage 1d10 piercing]] damage and are inflicted with Paralyzing Poison.

    • On a success, they take half damage. In addition, the trap triggers an alarm bell that alerts any members of the Beacon Brigade within 60 feet.

Seeing Behind The Shadowbox

If characters wish to see what is behind the shadowbox window, they must cast light on the shadowbox from outside. This can be done using any spell that casts light, including @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLight00000]{Light}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDancingLig]{Dancing Lights}, or similar, or by lighting a conventional torch or candle.

Once the source of light is within 10 feet of the window, the party can clearly see what is happening inside, but are visible to any members of the Beacon Brigade who are inside the shop or within 30 feet of the light source.

If characters see behind the shadowbox, they see an office filled with empty desks:

No one is inside the office, and all that you can see clearly are a set of empty desks that line the walls of the room. A number of small trinkets and artifacts are scattered across them, including several large lanterns.

Inside The Shop

The shop's desks hold a number of small trinkets of no particular value, including 3 different large unlit lanterns - one in the ornate style of Ordain, one in the well-crafted but practical style of the Arctus Plateau, and one that is all sharp angles, of unknown origin. None have any particular value and all can be taken without a check. There are also a number of papers near the items, which appear to be some kind of accounting system.

Deciphering the Notes

The notes are written in what appears to be a short-hand or accounting language of some kind.

The Courier Stand.name: The Courier Stand
The Courier Stand.text:
Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

  • Shadowbox Alleys: Characters can pursue the Shadowbox Alleys path to Beacon Brigade territory by searching the vicinity of the shop. An entrance to the Beacon Brigade side of town can be found by going past or through Hettie's Divinations.

  • Bluffing: The courier bag found here can be used to convince the Brigade that the party is on official business.

There is no information about the rooftop route.

Outside of the Shop

The shadowbox window at the front of this stand clearly shows the silhouette of piles of letters and packages, underneath a sign that reads Courier Stand. Attached to the sign, on a piece of paper that has been nailed to the sign and is slightly askew, are the words "Back in 20."

No one is currently inside the Courier Stand and the door is locked.

Seeing Behind The Shadowbox

If characters wish to see what is behind the shadowbox window, they must cast light on the shadowbox from outside. This can be done using any spell that casts light, including @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLight00000]{Light}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDancingLig]{Dancing Lights}, or similar, or by lighting a conventional torch or candle.

Once the source of light is within 10 feet of the window, the party can clearly see what is happening inside, but are visible to any members of the Beacon Brigade who are inside the shop or within 30 feet of the light source.

If characters see behind the shadowbox, they can tell that the courier stand is empty, though there are supplies - letters, packages, etc - scattered around.

Letters, packages, and stamps litter a simple counter inside the shop, which is otherwise empty, but the pile of letters, half opened and half still sealed, next to an open courier bag, gives the sense that whoever was here will be back shortly.

Inside The Shop

Exploring the Courier Stand

The door to the Courier Stand is locked, but can be opened with a successful [[/check dexterity 17]] check using Thieves' Tools. The @UUID[Item.Z0pd4LVjVusTBvqY]{Courier Bag} and letters can be taken without a check. The letters include a letter addressed to Lyla Cevher. If characters open the letter, it contains @UUID[Item.JKWt3ZZKBaEvNbw1]{ Choking Fog Dust}.

Vitt's Front Room.name: Vitt's Front Room
Vitt's Front Room.text:
The furnishings and decorations of this small home seem more lush than the surroundings around them would allow for, as if they would be more at home in the luxurious environs of Marlstone than among the commonfolk of Lantern Roads. Whoever lives here is living well.

Entering Vitt's House

The doors to Vitt's House are locked, but can be opened with the @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}.

  • If characters use the Brigade Key, members of the Beacon Brigade will not stop them from entering the facility.

Characters can unlock the doors to Vitt's House with a successful [[/check sleightofhand 16]] check with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools}. If they attempt this check within 30 feet of a Beacon Brigade member, they must succeed on a [[/check stealth 18]] check or the Brigade member notices and attacks.

The Barracks.name: The Barracks
The Barracks.text:
This large building isn't just the physical center of the Brigade's section of Lantern Roads - if the sounds of whoops, hollers and snores from the vicinity, or the occasional swinging open of the door to revel a new tell you anything, it's also a place for the Brigade members to rest, relax, and restore themselves.

The Beacon Brigade

A total of 4 @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Patrollers} are stationed in and around the barracks. The Patrollers outside of the Barracks can be dealt with similarly to any other member of the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.EH0ilpRL8UoqUQQM#the-beacon-brigade]{The Beacon Brigade}, but those inside the Barracks have the additional conditions below:

  • Characters cannot persuade the Patrollers that they are in the Barracks accidentally.

  • If characters attempt to persuade the Patrollers that they are either couriers or new members of the Brigade, they are asked to share who either recruited or hired them. With a successful [[/check deception 17]] check, they fool the Patrollers in the Barracks. With a failed check, the Patrollers attack.

Searching the Barracks

There are 3 areas of the barracks that can be searched - the Main Room, the Bathroom, and the Coat Room. The party can also locate a chest beneath the bed of one of the Brigade members without a check.

Each area is successfully searched with a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check, but each search risks discovery by a new Patroller.

  • Each time the party takes a Search action on a new section of the Barracks, or if they attempt to unlock the chest, roll a [[/gmroll 1d4]] - on a 1, a @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk]{Watcher} enters the area and immediately attacks.

  • With a successful search of the coat closet, characters locate the key to the chest found in the main room.

  • The chest can be opened with a successful [[/check dexterity 16]] check with Thieves' Tools or the chest key. It contains a sketch of Darius Cevher with a red line through it and a pouch that contains [[/award 10g0]].

  • Nothing is found in a search of the bathroom.

Impromptu Jail.name: Impromptu Jail
Impromptu Jail.text:
Though this may have once been someone's living place, there are bars on the window and the door has been shut tight. Through the window, you can hear voices below you discussing the situation, one gravelly and quiet, with words coming out as half bark, half whisper, and one thin and pointed, cutting through the sounds around it like a low-pitched knife. :

You didn't take their things?

I didn't take their things yet. Moving that many infiltrators at once isn't as easy as it looks. And where were you when I needed help, hmm?

Well I'm here now. And I'd rather deal with them while they're still knocked out or groggy than when they're awake, so let's go. If we screw this up, Vitt will have our heads.

If the party is caught by the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.EH0ilpRL8UoqUQQM#the-beacon-brigade]{Beacon Brigade} at any point, and unable to get away, they are captured and moved to this makeshift prison.

Searching the Cell

If characters search the jail cell, with a successful [[/check 16 perception]] check, they find two pieces of metal - one hidden in a metal bed frame and another tucked into a pillowcase

One of the pieces of metal is long and thin, while the other curves, but they appear to be made from the same material.

With a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check, characters know that they can arrange the pieces into the shape of a @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}. Any character who is proficient with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulTinkersToo]{Tinker's Tools} has @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Characters can join the pieces to make a key with glue, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulTinkersToo]{Tinker's Tools}, or by using the @UUID[Actor.GA8VFWysoIYfNWCL.Item.N2RTPfmtwtlIglVd]{Mending}spell. Once the key has been created, it is identical to any other @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}.

The door to leave the impromptu jail, unsurprisingly, is locked.

The Front Door

The door to the impromptu jail is made of 6 inch thick wood with a metal sheet inside, which prevents magic from being cast from the other side and makes breaking through by brute force nearly impossible.

Characters must succeed on a [[/check strength 29]] check to break the door down with force.

  • The character who attempts to break the door down must make a [[/save constitution 18]] saving throw. On a failure, they take [[/damage 1d10 bludgeoning]] damage. On a save, they take half the damage.

  • The noise of breaking down the door alerts all Beacon Brigade members within 60 feet. They immediately move to investigate.

The lock can be picked with a successful [[/check dexterity 18]] check with Thieves' Tools.

  • If characters found the pieces of the Brigade Key, even if they are unable to turn them into a working key, they have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • If characters created or are carrying a Brigade Key, they can use the key to exit.

If characters leave through the exit door, it creaks loudly. They must succeed on a [[/check stealth 17]] check or they catch the attention of any members of the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.EH0ilpRL8UoqUQQM#the-beacon-brigade]{Beacon Brigade} within 60 feet.

The Barred Windows

Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 16]] check notice that the bars of the window are thick steel, 3-4 inches in diameter, and have 1-inch gaps between them. They run into the adjoining wall and would be nearly impossible to kick out or saw through.

  • Characters who succeed on the check by 2 or more notice a small amount of heat radiating from the bars. Any character who has proficiency with Smith's Tools, succeeds on a [[/check history 16]] check, or has [[/knowledge alchemy]] suspects that they were treated with an alchemical substance known as@UUID[Item.TwsLk1KC8SqDbL8G]{ Thieves' Lament}, which burns and marks the hands of anyone who touches it.

Burning Bars

If characters touch the bars of the jail, they suffer the effects of @UUID[Item.TwsLk1KC8SqDbL8G]{Thieves' Lament}, including the hand markings. Unless the marks on their hands are covered, they have @Advantage[-2] on persuasion with members of the Beacon Brigade, who know how to avoid the substance.

Guard Arrival

If players are unable to leave the jail cell, or choose not to attempt it, the two guards they overheard will arrive to take their things.

The two voices you heard before reappear, now closer than before.

You think they're up already?

Probably not. But if they are, we're taking care of it. I'm sure Vitt won't mind.

With a clicking sound, the door slowly unlocks and two members of the Beacon Brigade enter, weapons already at hand.

@Embed[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F count= 2]

Guard Tactics

The Patrollers will immediately attempt to subdue the party with @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F.Item.tzf4esLNwPFMYhgC]{Slowing Serum} or @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F.Item.PVF1Y5P02LAH2z0V]{Paralyzing Poison}. If these don't work, they will go attempt to use @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F.Item.80G6VO1CfcKHD8sR]{Hollowed Dagger} in a direct attack.

Weapons Cache.name: Weapons Cache
Weapons Cache.text:
Outside of the building

The building is locked.

Entering the Building

Characters can enter the front door by either picking the lock, breaking the door down, or using the @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}.

  • To pick the lock, they must succeed on a [[/check dexterity 18]] check with Thieves' Tools.

  • To break down the door, they must succeed on a [[/check strength 18]] check. If they use a tool, like an axe or pickaxe, this check is made with @Advantage[2].

    • The sound of breaking down the door will catch the attention of all Beacon Brigade members within 100 feet.

  • The Brigade Key can be used without a check.

Inside of the building

The building is small, but packed to the brim with weapons. Most are poorly forged pieces of steel, but there are plenty of them.

Searching the Weapons Cache

If searched, the party can find the following without a check:

  • Several @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepDagger0000]{Low-Quality Daggers}

  • Several @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmShield0000]{Low-Quality Shields}

  • Several @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBottleGlass]{Empty Vials}

If the party searches more, they can find:

  • A single @UUID[Item.T17yt107rakVynnB]{Withering Dagger}. The poison and dagger size match the weapon that killed Darius Cevher, and the handle is engraved with the letters BB.

This can be used as evidence that the Beacon Brigade killed Darius Cevher. Mark the appropriate outcome in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.ZPv1VeLAtINtz3gv#evidence-against-the-beacon-brigade]{Revealed by Lantern}.

Forgotten Rooftop.name: Forgotten Rooftop
Forgotten Rooftop.text:
The tables and the chairs at the top of this building hint that it was once a dining establishment of some sort, but now they seem to be used as nothing more than a resting place for the Watchers who keep an eye on Beacon Brigade territory below.

The sentry on this roof is a @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk]{Wandren Watcher}. They will not target the party if the party prominently displays either a @UUID[Item.Z0pd4LVjVusTBvqY]{Courier Bag} or a @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}.

Sentry Tactics

Once they have spotted their target, sentries will always attempt, first and foremost, to use their @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk.Item.e7jBM8stpBBfK46e]{Spotlight Shot} to alert others in the area to intruders, often yelling as they do.

Any @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Wandren Patroller} within 100 feet of the sentry will respond and immediately begin moving towards the area that is being spotlit.

Impromptu Roof Garden.name: Impromptu Roof Garden
Impromptu Roof Garden.text:
Unlike some of the other rooftops that have been hastily converted to sentry perches, this rooftop sports a mix of plants that look similar to those found in the rooftop gardens in the south section of the neighborhood, though the pungent odor coming from the roof's direction gives the distinct sense that these plants are favored for their poisons rather than their beauty.

The sentry on this roof is a @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk]{Wandren Watcher}. They will not target the party if the party prominently displays either a @UUID[Item.Z0pd4LVjVusTBvqY]{Courier Bag} or a @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}.

Sentry Tactics

Once they have spotted their target, sentries will always attempt, first and foremost, to use their @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk.Item.e7jBM8stpBBfK46e]{Spotlight Shot} to alert others in the area to intruders, often yelling as they do.

Any @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Wandren Patroller} within 100 feet of the sentry will respond and immediately begin moving towards the area that is being spotlit.

Terracini's Restaurant.name: Terracini's Restaurant
Terracini's Restaurant.text:
Outside of the RestauranT

Climbing to the Roof

Characters can reach the rooftop via the ladder that sits against the side of Terracini's. With a successful [[/check perception 15]] check in the vicinity of the restaurant or [[/check perception passive 17]], they spot the ladder at the back of the shop. It can be climbed without a check.

Inside the Restaurant

Between the warmth of the cookfire, the rich smells of food in the midst of being prepared and enjoyed, and the conversation between the guests at the small intimate tables around the corners of the room, Terracini's Restaurant exudes a sense of comfort from the moment you enter.

A man, wearing shadowy clothes that are a more gray and muted version of what you've seen elsewhere in Ordain seems to slightly obscure the light as he walks by.

Welcome to Terracini's, where I am Terracini, and you are already family. Please, feel free to take a look over our menu.

As he waves you over, he draws slightly closer and whispers, too softly for anyone else to hear:

And if you really are family, you may find what you need in the terrace upstairs. If not, please stay down here.

Talking To Terracini

Terracini will not readily elaborate on what he means by being family, answering all questions with generic responses. With a successful [[/check insight 16]] check, characters know that he is trying to do his best not to get in trouble with the wrong people by saying the wrong thing. He will share any of the following:

  • He is related to the famous thief Terracini, but much prefers cooking to crime. He only uses the name to drum up business.

  • The cloak he wears is modeled after Terracini's, allowing the wearer to better sneak into and out of the shadows. It is one of his most prized possessions.

  • Characters should only go to the Terrace section of the restaurant if they have business with the Beacon Brigade, though he won't stop them from visiting. If someone in the party has the Brigade Key or Courier Bag, he is impressed and they have @Advantage[2] on the checks below.

With a successful [[/check intimidation 17]] or [[/check persuasion 17]] check, characters can convince Terracini to tell them the following:

  • The Terrace section of his restaurant is often used by associates of the Beacon Brigade. He much prefers when they are jumping over rooftops or sneaking through the Shadowbox side of town, but he feels he can't refuse them.

  • If they want to get to the other side of the neighborhood, the best way through is the rooftops, though he's heard their might be a path in the Shadowbox section of the neighborhood.

If characters succeed on the intimidation check by 3 or more, they can talk Terracini into selling them his cloak - it costs [[/award 200 gp]], which will help offset the money he's losing to the gang. The cloak is an @UUID[Item.YHDYXHfw7frsoviV]{Ashen Cloak}.

Introductions

Penni Terracini, head chef. Serving up food just as good as what they make over in Restaurant Row. And before you ask, or demand money, I'm not really related to the Terracini, though letting people think you're the cousin of a famous thief does help drum up business. It's the reason I got this thieves' cloak.

Who can go upstairs

You know that the Beacon Brigade has a base on the other side of the neighborhood? Only those who are approved by them are supposed to head upstairs. I don't want to get on their bad side - who knows what Vitt and the rest of them might do. His house is right across the way from this place - I need to stay on his good side.

His cloak

It's a cloak for sneaking around - cost me an arm and a leg and dropping Terracini's name to get it. I hope I don't have to sell it, but giving away free meals isn't great for my business.

Who uses the Terrace/Beacon Brigade info

Even the Beacon Brigade likes good food, so some of their members, and associates, use that terrace. It's pretty close to their territory, so I've promised to keep regular customers away. They aren't all bad - I think the couple up there right now are some shopkeepers they're trying to wine and dine.

Still , I wish the brigade would stick to other rooftops or skulking around Shadowbox Alley.

Requires a successful [[/check 17 persuasion]] or [[/check 17 intimidation]] check.

Getting to Beacon Brigade territory

The rooftops are the only real way that I know to get over to where Vitt and his crew hang out, though I've heard there's a path through the Shadowboxes - on the other side of the abandoned theater.

Requires a successful [[/check 17 persuasion]] or [[/check 17 intimidation]] check.

Terracini's Too.name: Terracini's Too
Terracini's Too.text:
A single couple sits in the small rooftop cafe, having a hushed but intense conversation, while occasionally glancing across to the sentries on a nearby roof. The sentries stare off into the distance, seemingly paying the customers — and you — no mind.

The sentries on @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.swv9SIyv899pl11C]{Vitt's Balcony} will not react to the party unless they take a hostile action against the Terracini customers or the sentries themselves.

Listening In

Characters can eavesdrop on the nearby conversation with a combined stealth and perception check.

  • With a successful [[/check insight check]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]], the party has a general sense that their conversation is about trying to sneak into Beacon Brigade territory.

  • With a successful [[/check stealth 15]] check, parties can get close enough to the couple to hear a small amount of their conversation. They will need a [[/check perception 18]] check to listen in clearly.

    • If the party succeeds on their stealth check by 3 or more, they only need a [[/check perception 16]] check to hear clearly.

The couple is having a conversation about whether they should try to find out more about the Beacon Brigade by sneaking across to the other side of the neighborhood.

They claim they just want to use our store to hold a few things, but I'm not sure it's quite so innocent. I say we go over there and learn more about them. I'm pretty sure all we have to do is bring a lamp to that secondhand store and they'll let us through.

The Terrace Gardens.name: The Terrace Gardens
The Terrace Gardens.text:
Characters may first encounter the Terrace Gardens at Ground Level (while walking by the streets below) or at Rooftop Level (having ascended one of the other rooftops and walked over).

Ground Level

Reaching the Terrace Gardens

Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 16]] check or [[/check 16 nature]] check notice the overgrown vines that can be climbed up to the Terrace Gardens. The vines can be climbed by any character with a climbing speed, but are filled with thorns.

Climbing the Vines

Any character who attempts to climb the vines must succeed on a [[/check 17 sleightofhand]] check to put their hands carefully down in the right places without being stabbed by the thorns. Characters with [[/knowledge plants]] or who succeed on a [[/check nature 17]] check have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Anyone who fails the check takes [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] damage from the vine's thorns.

Rooftop Level

These well-landscaped gardens, while currently unattended, have signs scattered throughout identifying several local and foreign plant species known for their calming scents and colorful blooms. Signs at the edge of the two walkways that extend to nearby rooftop read:

Explore at your own risk.

Characters interested in taking the rooftop route to the Northern section of Lantern Roads can proceed from this rooftop towards either @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.qiBZJ0T4dHxtDZWJ]{Terrace Gardens: The Wild Side} or @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.A0x1R29zmbLYX0QT]{Terracini's Too}

Terrace Gardens: The Wild Side.name: Terrace Gardens: The Wild Side
Terrace Gardens: The Wild Side.text:
The flowers and plants in this section of the rooftop garden are a bit wilder and more colorful, as if they were taken straight from a distant land and placed here for your enjoyment. A sign along the walkway reads:

For those who prefer a bit of excitement with their relaxation, take a walk on the wild side. Carefully.

Characters wishing to take the rooftop route to the Northern section of Lantern Roads may continue along the walkway to @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.JaEG0UmTydMKt0yO]{Lookout Point}.

Examining the Plant Life

Characters can learn the following about the plants in this section of Terrace Gardens. Any character with [[/knowledge plants]] has an advantage on all checks.

  • With a successful [[/check nature 16]] check, characters know that the particularly bright coloring of the plants indicates that they may be toxic. The colors warn animals away who might et them.

    • If characters succeed by 3 or more, they know that these are Red Nettlers, plants which spray nettles at anyone who comes too close to them, but can be bypassed with stealth.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check, or if characters have [[/check perception passive 18]]. they hear a rustling in the leaves.

  • With a successful [[/check stealth 16]] check to move carefully through the Red Nettles, characters can pass without incident. If they fail the stealth check, see Flying Nettles below.

Flying Nettles

The first time that a character comes within 5 feet of a Red Nettle plant without stealth, all characters within 30 feet of the plants must make a [[/save dexterity 17]] saving throw as it sprays nettles in their direction. Any character that fails the saving throw takes [[/damage 1d4 piercing]] from the sharp nettles.

Terrace Gardens: Nature's Glory.name: Terrace Gardens: Nature's Glory
Terrace Gardens: Nature's Glory.text:
The plants on this rooftop smell less floral and more herbal, and their colors while beautiful, are somewhat muted. Though they don't grow particularly tall, any attempts to see Lantern Roads from here are blocked either by the rock to the side or the taller and brighter flowers on the adjacent rooftop.

A sign on the garden reads:

Not all beauty is worn on the outside. These herbs are favorites not just because of the way they look, but also what they can do.

Characters wishing to take the rooftop route to the Northern section of Lantern Roads may continue along the walkway towards @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.JaEG0UmTydMKt0yO]{Lookout Point}.

Fresh Herbs

Characters can learn the following about the plants in this section of Terrace Gardens. Any character with [[/knowledge plants]] has an @Advantage[2] on all checks.

  • The herbs in this section of the garden can be used for healing or for poison. With a successful [[/check nature 17]] check, characters can identify which is which. If they fail on the check, any attempt to take herbs from the garden results in them grabbing a poisonous plant and taking [[/damage 1d6 poison]] damage from the contact poison.

  • Characters who can identify the herbs can remove them safely with a successful [[/check 16 sleightofhand]] check. Any character with proficiency with an Herbalism Kit can use the herbs to create 1 Healing Potion or dose of antitoxin.

Lookout Point.name: Lookout Point
Lookout Point.text:
This small hideaway nook, generally accessible only through the Terrace Gardens, offers an incomparable view of all of Lantern Roads. Below, lights flicker and shadowbox scenes play out as locals and tourists walk back and forth, though many appear to avoid the roads that lead to the northern half of the neighborhood, a place shrouded in secrets.

The vantage point offered from this location gives characters a clear view of the rooftops that lead from the public section of Lantern Roads to the Beacon Brigade section north of the gate.

Crossing the Gap

Characters can make their way to @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.swv9SIyv899pl11C]{Vitt's Balcony} by either climbing or jumping over the rocky outcropping between them.

  • Characters who wish to climb must have a climbing speed and must succeed on a [[/check acrobatics 17]] check to keep their grip during the slippery climb.

  • Characters who wish to jump can attempt a [[/check perception 16]] check or [[/check nature 17]] to gauge the distance and slipperiness of the rock before jumping. If they succeed, they have @Advantage[2] on the [[/check athletics 17]] check to jump across.

Characters who fail either the jump or the climb checks fall hard to the ground below, taking [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage.

Second Light.name: Second Light
Second Light.text:
Filled with odds and ends, the goods in the shop Second Light appear to be arranged haphazardly, with no particular rhyme or reason to where they go. Still, each time someone new enters the shop, they seem to know exactly who to see and what to do, placing their items on the counter and murmuring something to the shopkeeper before walking past her, taking an item from a back counter, and exiting through the back door.

As if she sees you watching, the shopkeeper smiles, maybe a little too brightly, and waves in your direction.

Welcome to Second Light, where old goods shine just as brightly as new ones. Whether you're looking for secondhand goods or have something to sell, let me know if you need anything - fair prices always offered!

Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

Characters seeking to get to the northern part of Lantern Roads can bluff their way through to the other side by following the procedure noted in Revealed by Lantern:

  • Bring a source of light for sale to the pawn shop

  • Say the phrase "Have a bright day"

  • Pick up the correct Brigade Key from the table and use it to exit.

There is no information about the Rooftops or Shadowbox Alleys readily available.

Observing the Procedure

Each customer who makes their way through Second Light brings in an item, speaks to the shopkeeper, and walks indirectly to the back door.

  • Characters can look at the recent items on the counter without a check — they include a broken lantern, candle, and torch stick. With a successful [[/check investigation 16]] check, characters know that the item brought to the shopkeeper must be something that generates light.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check, characters can eavesdrop on the conversation between customers and the shopkeeper . If the check is failed, it can be retried, but they must first attempt a [[/check stealth 16]] check.

    • If they succeed on the check, they have @Advantage[2] on their next perception attempt.

    • If they fail on the check, the shopkeeper questions why they're standing so close to her other customers. They can either back away, raising the DC of the perception check by 2, or explain their position with a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] or [[/check deception 16]] check.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 18]] check, characters can see that the customers who leave through the back are picking up keys from one of the back tables, which they use to unlock the back door.

Selling to the Shopkeeper

The shopkeeper introduces herself as Luma and encourages the party to look at many of the small items that she has for sale, or to sell something of their own that they no longer need.

  • If characters offer any item that does not generate light, Luma offers them one-quarter of its cost. With a successful [[/check persuasion 17]] or [[/check intimidation 17]] check, she will raise her offer to half of the initial cost.

  • If characters offer an item that does generate light, she asks if Vitt sent them. Their answer does not matter - if they do not say "Have a Bright Day" during the conversation, she offers cash for the item as above.

    • If characters do say "Have a Bright Day" or if they succeed on a [[/check intimidation 24]] check to bully Luma, she offers them "something priceless" in return for the item - suggesting that they pick up their reward and leave through the back. Characters who do not understand what she means by this can convince her to explain with a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] check.

Using the Back Exit

The party can easily take one of the keys on the back table without a check - it is a Brigade Key, which opens the back door to the shop. If parties attempt to go through the the back door without the key, Luma acts unconcerned, offering to open the door herself, but sends a silent alert to the Beacon Brigade, who now attack the party on sight.

Shadowbox Souvenirs.name: Shadowbox Souvenirs
Shadowbox Souvenirs.text:
Believed to be one of the oldest buildings in Lantern Roads, this is one of the few that does not use light in its large picture window, opting instead for a display of swirling shadows. Despite its somewhat foreboding facade, it holds only a small souvenir shop, whose shadowcasters throw shadowy tableaus at the wall. The owner, Dolin Aveun, greets you as you enter the shop.

Welcome to Lantern Roads, home of shadows and light. Feel free to browse and let me know if you need anything!

Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

Characters seeking to get to the northern part of Lantern Roads can find information on three potential routes through observation and their conversation with shopkeeper Dolin Aveun.

  • Rooftop Route: Dolin mentions that the Brigade uses the rooftops to cross the area. If party members enter the shop, they can find a direct connection from the upstairs section of the shop to the adjoining rooftop of @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.9Qqs212yQN0Rp8vx]{Terrace Gardens: Nature's Glory}.

  • Shadowbox Alleys: Dolin alludes to thieves and troublemakers that spend time in Shadowbox Alleys.

  • Bluffing: Dolin gives any characters who ask about the Brigade a lantern, which he believes to have something to do with the Brigade's vetting procedure. He usually gets the used lanterns back from nearby shop Second Light.

Speaking with Dolin Aveun

Dolin Aveun is eager to have customers and will readily make conversation with the party about his shadowboxes. He will share the following:

  • He sells miniature shadow boxes, which are replicas of some of the famous shadowbox display windows in the neighborhood. Like the windows, they are lit from within, but if a light is shone on them from outside, the scene in the box changes.

  • There are still shadowboxes up for display in Shadowbox Alley, but there are often shady people skulking around in the area - he avoids it if at all possible.

If asked about the Beacon Brigade, Dolin immediately hands the party a lantern from beneath his desk without an explanation. If asked about the lantern, he won't explain why he handed it over. With a successful [[/check 17 persuasion]] or [[/check 17 intimidation]] check, he shares the following:

  • The Beacon Brigade usually uses the rooftops to get around, but sometimes they come to him looking for lanterns, which are part of their way of identifying new members.

  • He doesn't know what they do with the lanterns, but usually sees the lanterns at Second Light, the secondhand shop, where he buys them back from the owner, Luma Texini.

Just In Time.name: Just In Time
Just In Time.text:
Timepieces of all kinds line the walls and shelves of this small shop, whose Signborn shopkeeper is hunched over a small handheld timepiece beneath a magnifying glass, using all of the arms he has available in an attempt to wind it. Though he appears deep in concentrated work, he looks up as soon as you enter, fixing you with a assessing gaze.

Ah, new customers - who look very good at taking care of themselves. I'm Fozil Dalm. May I ask what brings you to Lantern Roads? I hope you're not part of that horrible Beacon Brigade that's taken over half our neighborhood. You'd tell me if you were, weren't you?

Getting to the North of Lantern Roads

Characters seeking to get to the northern part of Lantern Roads can find information on three potential routes from their conversation with shopkeeper Fozil Dalm (see below).

  • Rooftop Route: Fozil suspects that the rooftops are used to move goods but has no real proof.

  • Shadowbox Alleys: Fozil is sad that the Shadowbox Alleys area has been largely abandoned, though he has seen people coming and going from that way.

  • Bluffing: Fozil believes there's some way into the Brigade area having to do with the Pawn shop, but he hasn't figured it out.

A Conversation with Fozil Dalm

It is clear, even without a check, that Fozil Dalm wants something from the party. With a successful [[/check insight 15]] check, the party knows that the shopkeeper is desperately eager to uncover secret members of the Beacon Brigade gang.

In truth, Fozil Dalm is an associate of the Veiled Chain, one of the investigative bodies of Ordain, and a bad liar. He looks at the door frequently, as if worried someone will come in and interrupt the conversation and speaks with a too-loud whisper. As long as the party assures him that they are not with the gang, he will answer any of the following:

  • The Beacon gang has become a nuisance, bothering innocent shop keepers for protection money and moving ill-gotten gains through the neighborhood. They've erected a gate in the middle of the neighborhood that they hide behind.

  • Fozil blames the gang for the decline in shops on the western side of the neighborhood, called Shadowbox Row, though he does sometimes see suspicious folks headed in that direction.

  • Fozil is fairly sure that the gang uses the rooftops to get past their gate without anyone seeing their movements, though he doesn't know how. He thinks it may involve the Pawn Shop, @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.oAliNrQngO8rEGpg]{Second Light}, though he hates to think the shopkeeper Mindeva has anything to do with it.

  • Fozil will pay [[/award 5gp]] for any proof of Beacon Brigade activity in the neighborhood, which he plans to take to the Veiled Chain.

Marlstone Manor Entrance.name: Marlstone Manor Entrance
Marlstone Manor Entrance.text:
This set of stairs leads directly up to the @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.6pccfZZYqVECcekQ]{Guardhouse} at the back of Marlstone Manor.

Ascending to Marlstone Manor

As you ascend the winding set of stairs, Marlstone Manor grows larger and larger in your vision, until it is just ahead of you, with only a small squat building between you and the building's back entrance.

Descending from Marlstone Manor

Marlstone Manor fades into the background behind you as you descend the stairs towards the warm steady light of Lantern Roads.

Vitt's Balcony.name: Vitt's Balcony
Vitt's Balcony.text:
Though the table and chairs on this rooftop almost look as if they could belong to another elevated dining establishment, the two well-armed sentries at each corner give it a sense of casual foreboding.

The Beacon Brigade

Two @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk]{Watchers} are stationed on the balcony, though their focus is on the ground in front of them. These Watchers can be dealt with similarly to any other member of the @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.EH0ilpRL8UoqUQQM#the-beacon-brigade]{The Beacon Brigade}, with the following additional conditions:

  • Characters cannot persuade the Watchers that they are on the Rooftop accidentally.

  • Characters who carry the Courier Bag will not be attacked, but are asked to turn over their letter and leave immediately. If they do not, they are attacked.

  • Watchers attacked from behind are surprised.

Entering the Locked House

While most of the doors to Vitt's House are locked, characters who take a close look at each can find an unlocked door on the southern side of the locked house. With a successful [[/check stealth 20]] check, or if characters are already invisible, they can enter the home without alerting either of the Wandren Watchers on the nearby roof.

Vitt's Back Room.name: Vitt's Back Room
Vitt's Back Room.text:
As you enter their bedroom, Vitt Wandren seems unsurprised, and a little amused.

It takes a lot of guts to break in here. I wonder what they'll look like splashed all over my walls.

Vitt Wandren Tactics

Vitt Wandren is an aggressive combatant who uses a @UUID[Item.cBuw0vLTJ8e2qAhO]{Gem of Shielding} worn around their neck to protect themselves from @UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz.Item.UdrAVLjQ8HhdwuLx]{Choking Fog Dust} and @UUID[Item.igL8TTHfJplOo4TA]{Slowing Dust}, which they throw to affect the party before attacking with their @UUID[Item.T17yt107rakVynnB]{Withering Dagger}. The destruction to their own home seems unimportant to them.

If the @UUID[Item.cBuw0vLTJ8e2qAhO]{Gem of Shielding} is removed from Vitt, they lose their protection from the effects of their own weapons and will resort to traditional combat using their knife and bow.

Vitt's Key

After Vitt is defeated, the party can search their belongings - with a successful [[/check perception 16]] check, they find a key in one of Vitt's pockets. It is similar to the @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}, but slightly more ornate.

Vitt's Key will work as a substitute for the @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}, and opens the locked chest in their back room. If parties do not have they key, they can pick the lock of the chest with a successful [[/check dexterity 17]] check with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools}. If the party has a @UUID[Item.NMufWIxDYBCZZQEM]{Brigade Key}, they have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The safe contains:

  • 100GP [[/award 100gp]]

  • A list of names, with initials next to them in parentheses. Several have been crossed off, including Darius Cevher. The initials next to Darius' name read HW. This can be used as a piece of evidence to clear Funar's name. Mark the appropriate outcome in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.ZPv1VeLAtINtz3gv#evidence-against-the-beacon-brigade]{Revealed by Lantern}.

Searching Vitt's House

With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check while looking through Vitt's House, characters notice the outline of a doorway along the back wall.

Other than the faint line in the shape of a doorway that cuts through the wall, there are no other indications of a door - no handle or hinges or obvious way to open it.

In truth, the wall in front of the door is a visual illusion - characters can see through the illusion with a successful [[/check 16 investgation]] check while examining the door more closely, or by physically touching where the door will be, as they can feel the true door beneath the illusion.

Holding Cells Antechamber.name: Holding Cells Antechamber
Holding Cells Antechamber.text:
A metal desk covered with small items sits empty in what is otherwise a bare room. Opposite the desk, a sign on the wall is written in bold lettering in a language other than Common. Beneath it, in a different hand, is the word Containment.

As you step into the room, you can hear a muffled voice from behind a wall:

Hello? Can you hear me? This is Funar Cevher of House Cevher, and I request your immediate assistance on two urgent matters. I must get free of this imprisonment, but more importantly, I need to get a message to my sister Lyla - she may be in grave danger!

If Lyla is with the party, she reacts immediately:

Lyla sighs, deeply, and brings her hand to her heart.

Funar, thank the Nineteen! What happened?

Whether or not Lyla is present, the conversation with Funar continues in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.91Ck26XHcgMCo88E#freeing-funar]{Freeing Funar}.

Exploring the Room

The etched sheets of metal on the desk are primarily written in [[/language harmos]]. Characters who go through them can find the following without a check:

  • A piece of paper written in a combination of Harmos and [[/language common]] with a list of names that includes several people with the last name Wandren and Funar Cevher.

    • If Lyla is with the party, or if characters either succeed on a [[/check history 16]] check or have [[/knowledge politics]], they know that that these are some of the old guard of House Wandren, who might have been political rivals of Hephiss Wandren.

    • If characters know [[/language harmos]], the remaining papers are notes about the prisoners, most of which detail them being enemies of Hephiss.

  • A sketched map of the facility with a picture of the key in the upper corner - the sketch is rough, but has three markings on it - one in a room directly to the south of the room the party is in, and one generally in the Northeast and the Southeast. Each marking has a line to it, connecting it to a drawing of the domes in the center of the facility.

    • With a successful [[/check investigation 16]] check, the party can decipher that the marking is a combination of a lever and a flame.

  • A small key. It does not match the door to the holding cell area. If the party describes the key to Funar, he will confirm that it appears similar to the keys to the individual holding cell cells.

The Locked Door

It is hard to tell, at first glance, that the piece of metal in front of you is a door at all. There's no knob, keyhole, or other indication of any kind of how it might be opened.

The Locked Door

Though Funar is certain that the door to the holding cells is locked, the party may wish to take a closer look:

  • Anyone who succeeds on a [[/check 15 arcana]] or [[/check 15 nature]] check can tell that the metal of the door has a faint glow to it that is magical in nature.

    • Anyone who uses @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} (or a similar spell) can tell that the door is magically controlled from elsewhere and repels anyone who touches it.

  • Anyone who touches the door is thrown backwards 10 feet. @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} has no effect on the door. @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDisintegra]{Disintegrate} gets rid of the protection on the door, but there is still keyhole or unlocking mechanishm.

    • The door underneath the protection has AC 24 and Hardness 6.

A Bare Holding Cell.name: A Bare Holding Cell
A Bare Holding Cell.text:
This holding cell is completely empty, with only the faint smell of cleaning solvent providing any evidence that someone was ever held within in its walls.

One of several @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.krAbLyAdPcc554Z9]{Holding Cells} in the Wandren HQ facilities.

Cell with a Scratched Wall.name: Cell with a Scratched Wall
Cell with a Scratched Wall.text:
Tally marks have been etched into the wall. Though they are even and deep in the uppermost corner, the marks get fainter and shakier as they go, until the final mark trails off before it has even been fully chiseled.

One of several @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.krAbLyAdPcc554Z9]{Holding Cells} in the Wandren HQ facilities.

Cell with a Half-Dressed Skeleton.name: Cell with a Half-Dressed Skeleton
Cell with a Half-Dressed Skeleton.text:
The skeleton in the center of this cell is wearing a set of clothing that has not yet been destroyed by the teeth of rodents or the wear and tear of time.

The Skeleton's Clothing

Characters who succeed on a [[/check history 17]] check, have [[/knowledge fashion]] or [[/knowledge trade]], or are [[/culture ordani]] can easily recognize the colors and fabrics associated with House Wandren. The skeleton likely belongs to a House Wandren member.

One of several @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.krAbLyAdPcc554Z9]{Holding Cells} in the Wandren HQ facilities.

Cell with Gnawed Remains.name: Cell with Gnawed Remains
Cell with Gnawed Remains.text:
The bones of the skeleton in this cell are covered in fresh gnaw marks, as if they've fallen prey to a nest of rats or crevvets.

One of several @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.krAbLyAdPcc554Z9]{Holding Cells} in the Wandren HQ facilities.

The Cell with Empty Chains.name: The Cell with Empty Chains
The Cell with Empty Chains.text:
The chains on the wall of this cell seem to be placed awkwardly, crossing over each other in an X that seems like it should have collapsed by now instead of laying flat against the wall.

The Mysterious X

The X in the chains is being held there by a thin set of thread that's difficult to see from a distance, but can be noticed if:

  • Characters succeed on a [[/check perception 15]] check.

  • Characters attempt to touch or move the chains in any way.

The X is laying against the wall on top of one brick in particular. With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check, characters can notice that there is a small gap around the brick. If they touch the brick, they also find that it moves, though it only moves sightly, as if stuck.

The Marked Brick

The brick marked by the X can be removed using one of the methods below. If characters use a tool (such as a pickaxe) or substance (such as grease, or a substance that dissolves brick and concrete) to aid them, they make the check with @Advantage[2].

  • Characters succeed on a [[/check strength 16]] check to push it out.

  • Characters succeed on a [[/check sleightofhand 16]] check to wiggle it out effectively.

Removing the brick reveals a small hollow - it contains 2 GP [[/award 2gp]] and Diary of a Prisoner (this can also be used as evidence against Hephiss Wandren).

One of several @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.krAbLyAdPcc554Z9]{Holding Cells} in the Wandren HQ facilities.

The Cell with a Stained Floor.name: The Cell with a Stained Floor
The Cell with a Stained Floor.text:
The dark pattern of stains on this floor could possibly be dirt or blood or something else altogether, but they've been faded to the point of being unreognizable.

One of several @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.krAbLyAdPcc554Z9]{Holding Cells} in the Wandren HQ facilities.

Vitt's Office.name: Vitt's Office
Vitt's Office.text:
Paper-filled desks line the walls of the room, nestled between bookshelves whose books have well-worn spines. On one of the, a ledger is opened and a chair pushed back from the desk, as if whoever was writing in the ledger stepped away for only a moment and will soon return.

With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check, or [[/check perception passive 18]], characters can hear someone humming quietly in the next room.

Searching Vitt's Office

Characters can search Vitt's office, though they must be careful not to alert the Brigade leader.

  • To do a superficial check, characters must succeed on a [[/check stealth 16]] check to avoid alerting Vitt and a [[/check perception 16]] check to find the items they seek. If they succeed on both, they find:

    • The Brigade's books, which include a list of shopkeepers that the Beacon Brigade is regularly collecting money from and where the money is going, including "20% to HW" - while this is not proof of anything, Lyla is likely to be interested.

  • To do a deeper search (looking for papers shoved into books and in open desk drawers, characters must succeed on a [[/check sleightofhand 17]] check to avoid alerting Vitt and a [[/check investigation 17]] to check to find the items they seek. If they succeed on both, they find:

    • A sketch of Darius Cevher's shop, Threadforge, with notes of entries and exits. A clock, drawn on top, is set to 3:00 PM, believed to be the approximate time of the murder. This is a clear piece of evidence of the Brigade's involvement in his death and a way to clear Funar's name. Mark the appropriate outcome in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.ZPv1VeLAtINtz3gv#evidence-against-the-beacon-brigade]{Revealed by Lantern}.

Vitt Alerted

If characters alert Vitt, the Beacon Brigade leader immediately enters the room and attacks. The party is surprised by the attack and Vitt enters with their Gem of Shielding already active.

Vitt Wandren Tactics

@UUID[Actor.qyuqbNfU3VFUhPWF]{Vitt Wandren }is an aggressive combatant who uses a @UUID[Item.cBuw0vLTJ8e2qAhO]{Gem of Shielding } around their neck to protect themselves from the substances that they either throw or shoot with their bow, many of which do damage over a large area and make movement difficult. The destruction to their own home seems unimportant to them.

They take @Advantage[2] of their enemies' @Advantage[-2] during this time to make close-up strikes with their @UUID[Actor.qyuqbNfU3VFUhPWF.Item.HpDvpcOoO5hRcMCI]{Club} and avoid taking damage from their enemies.

If the Gem of Shielding is removed from Vitt, they lose their protection from the effects of their own weapons and will resort to traditional combat using their club and bow.

The Scorched Cell.name: The Scorched Cell
The Scorched Cell.text:
A pattern of singe and scorch marks covers the floor and walls, and the bars on the cells show signs of having been bent from the inside.

The damage to these cells was created when the Tyraphem prisoner Yllis attempted to escape.

A Meaningful Pattern

Characters who succeed on a [[/check investigation 17]] check can see a clear pattern within the scorch marks. It appears to be a message, but is written in a language other than Common.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/check history 16]] check can identify the language as Harmos, a language used on Luxarum. Any character who knows [[/language harmos]] can identify it without a check and translate it as "They Will Pay."

One of several @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls.JournalEntryPage.krAbLyAdPcc554Z9]{Holding Cells} in the Wandren HQ facilities.

Locked Gate.name: Locked Gate
Locked Gate.text:
A large metal gate cuts through the center of the Lantern Roads neighborhood. On the south side, pedestrians and locals walk between establishments, lit by the many lanterns that help to give the neighborhood its name. To the north, the streets are much more empty, and those who walk behind it appear armed.

Direct Assault

If the party attempts to directly break through or unlock the door, they are swarmed by members of the Beacon Brigade - two @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk]{Sentries} and three @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Patrollers} converge.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the Ordain Burial Grounds depicts the interior chambers of a Cindaric Crematorium as well as an exterior expanse of the overgrown cemetery itself, which will serve as the scenery for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders} quest event known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments}.

  • This map represents one small section of the Burial Grounds, and focuses on the Cindaric Crematorium that comprises most of the map's interior.

  • There is a single method of entry to the Crematorium: the @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.o7M5PtYDgiJ9ASOZ]{Cindaric Threshold} situated outside the facility, near the center of the map.

  • Additional information about the various mausoleums of this section of the Burial Grounds and the locks that contain them are located in the Gameplay Details section of this walkthrough.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.cvUD3Rj9MLXLwpAb inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The Ordain Burial Grounds are a quiet and solemn place, and this particular section hosts a facility where the venerable Cindaric Sages perform sacred cremation rites for the deceased. It also serves as the stage for an epic encounter with a vampiric Corpuleth and a legion of skeletal minions — who've been gathered here at the behest of the mysterious Blood Baron known as Amelia Naxan.

Objectives

At the behest of the shard goddess Sionia, the party has been sent to the Burial Grounds in search of the cadavers of one or more undead creatures — which are scheduled for timely incineration in the cemetery's Cindaric Crematorium. If they wish to learn more about the rising undead threat in the region, the characters must:

  • Venture into the Cindaric Crematorium, a dungeon-like facility where Cindaric funerary rites are conducted, culminating in a large magma pit where bodies are laid to eternal rest via ceremonial cremation.

  • Observe the quest's prime mover — the necromancer @UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan} — for the first time, before she disappears in a dramatic flash.

  • Survive a brutal battle against a hulking, blood-drinking @UUID[Actor.IWpoD9AvSVfLFdad]{Corpuleth} and dozens of @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} and @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]{Crumbling Skallith} minions.

  • Escape the Burial Grounds with the physical remains one or more undead creatures, to be used in Sionia's forthcoming investigation.

These enemies do not populate this area map outside of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments} event featured in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders}.

Repopulating Minions

If the party leaves the Burial Grounds for any reason before the battle with the Corpuleth and the Skallith is finished (before the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments} event has concluded), they'll return to find the location inundated with replacements.

All Skallith will respawn on the map prior to the party's return, along with [[/roll 1d2+1]] @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy]{Skallith Warriors}, who take their place throughout the various mausoleums leading up to the Cindaric Crematorium.

Illumination

Braziers located throughout the Burial Grounds exterior burn with magical firelight and inkaro pearls, and are regularly tended to by the various lamplighters and Cindarics assigned to work here. These braziers shed bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet.

Similar sconces and braziers light the interior Cindaric Crematorium section of the map. Additionally, the magma of @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.JozGvLULBUbiPaJf]{The Aperture}'s pit sheds light throughout most of the innermost chamber, with a radius of bright light for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet.

Terrain

The exterior sections of the map are littered with gravestones, statues, and foliage. As a result, the general landscape of the Burial Grounds counts as difficult terrain, other than areas such as mausoleum interiors, the Cindaric Crematorium facility, and the cobblestone path that winds its way through the graveyard.

The flagstone floors of the Cindaric Crematorium are crafted from slabs of dark basalt, hewn from the quarries and subterranea nearby. The ground here should be treated as normal terrain unless otherwise noted. The interior walls of the Crematorium are crafted from similar stone.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.o7M5PtYDgiJ9ASOZ]{Crematorium Gate} and the similar door that leads from the @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.KVuVtYIMeLG4UfDi]{Antechamber} to the Funeral Hall are made of an adamantine alloy, and are locked. The two metal doors on the east and west edges of the Funeral Hall are unlocked and made of solid reinforced steel, as are the two smaller portcullis in the eastern and western Antechamber hallways — which are opened and closed by operating levers located nearby.

The walls and floors of the map's various exterior mausoleums are made of white marble, unless otherwise noted. The mausoleum doors are made of reinforced steel.

Graveyard Tracks

Any character who searches the Burial Grounds exterior for tracks and succeeds on a [[/skill survival 13]] check is able to locate the presence of sandaled and booted footprints along the various cobblestone walkways here. These tracks are easily identified as those of the Cindaric Sages and lamplighters who work here.

Elevation

The ceilings within the interior section of the Cindaric Crematorium are 20 feet high, unless otherwise stated. The bespoke ceilings of the smaller mausoleums outside are detailed in each of their respective sections of the area walkthrough.

The uneven landscape of the Burial Grounds exterior features slight elevation changes, but these slopes and inclines are too minuscule to make a difference.

Preparation Chamber.name: Preparation Chamber
Preparation Chamber.text:
The sweet smells of lavender, jasmine, and incense mask the subtle scent of rot in this octagonal chamber lined with mortuary slabs and medical accoutrements. If the wash basin on the southern wall and the reverent arrangement of the corpses here is any indication, this must be some kind of staging room, where the newly deceased are disrobed and cleaned before the embalming process begins.

Cadavers are brought to this Preparation Chamber for the first step of processing here at the Crematorium. Bodies are stripped of their clothing and equipment, which is temporarily stored on shelves against the eastern wall. A wash basin and a nearby utility table adjoin the southern wall, which contain everything the Cindarics need for this step of the funerary rites.

If the characters take a closer look at one of the corpses, read the following aloud:

You lean in to examine the corpse, which appears to be an Ordani citizen who met an untimely fate of one kind or another. Based on the relative lack of decomposition, it seems as though some spell or alchemical reagent is keeping the bodies in stasis.

Exploring the Prep Chamber

If the characters decide to search the room, they'll find the following:

  • The corpses of 3 ordinary Ordani citizens, who appear to be unconnected to the party's investigation. The stone slabs they're laid upon are cluttered with incense burners, half-burned sticks of incense, water jugs, cloth sheets, and other miscellaneous debris.

  • The shelves on the eastern wall contain an array of personal effects (recently collected from one or more of the corpses here in the room): one outfit of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesFine]{Fine Clothes}, one outfit of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesTrav]{Traveler's Clothes}, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagScholarsPac]{Scholar's Pack}, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepShortsword]{Shortsword}, and a mundane @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbhsyAmuletworn]{Amulet} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}.

  • A clean water basin on the southern wall, accompanied by various towels, pitchers, soap, and cleaning salts.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check is able to notice or locate the following:

  • The incense here hasn't been lit for a few hours, but ashes remain settled on the mortuary slabs from an earlier session.

  • The water basin doesn't appear to be attached to a water source of any kind, and the water is remarkably clean.

Any character who examines the corpses for details must succeed on a [[/skill medicine 13]] or [[/skill investigation 13]] check to determine the following:

  • 2 of the corpses here appear to have been the result of natural causes (old age and terminal illness), while the third looks like a fatal concussion (likely accidental).

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

A successful [[/skill arcana 13]] check confirms a few details:

  • The corpses are currently benefitting from the effects of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGentleRepo]{Gentle Repose} spell, one of Ember's "sacred" Necromancy spells.

  • The water in the basin is sourced from permanent versions of spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCreateorDe]{Create or Destroy Water} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplPurifyFood]{Purify Food and Drink}.

Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell reveals an aura of Transmutation magic on the water basin and an aura of sacred Necromancy on the corpses.

Embalming Room.name: Embalming Room
Embalming Room.text:
This wide chamber seems to have two vaguely distinct sections, each defined by its own precise stage of the embalming process. Mortuary slabs at the south end of the room appear tarnished with the crimson stains of bodily fluid, while a single stone slab to the north contains a full-prepared corpse wrapped in a traditional Cindaric funeral sheet. A clean water basin adorns the western wall; and shelves positioned around the room are decorated with all manner of tools, balms, components, and reagents.

This chamber serves as the facility's Embalming Room, where individual corpses are prepared for cremation according to sacred Cindaric rites. Younger sages work at the south end to prepare bodies with ritualistic ointments, salves, and wrappings, while veteran sages complete the final touches at the station to the north.

A large steel door is located on the eastern wall at the northern end of the chamber. This threshold is unlocked, and can be controlled with a lever on each side.

Exploring the Embalming Room

If the characters decide to search the room, they'll find the following:

  • The corpses of 2 ordinary Ordani citizens, who appear to be unconnected to the party's investigation. The stone slabs they're laid upon are cluttered with incense burners and half-burned sticks of incense.

  • The shelves on the walls contain an array of incenses, herbs, spell components, salves, unguents, perfumes, and alchemical reagents. At your discretion, spellcasters in the party can loot material components they might need for various spells.

  • A clean water basin on the western wall, accompanied by a solitary jug.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check is able to notice or locate the following:

  • The incense here hasn't been lit for a few hours, but ashes remain settled on the mortuary slabs from an earlier session.

  • The water basin doesn't appear to be attached to a water source of any kind, and the water is remarkably clean.

  • The first character to succeed on this check finds 2 vials of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagHolyWater00]{Holy Water} and enough components to assemble a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagHealersKit0]{Healer's Kit}.

Any character who examines the corpses for details must succeed on a [[/skill medicine 13]] or [[/skill investigation 13]] check to determine the following:

  • The corpse at the south end of the room appears to have been the result of a drowning. Meanwhile, the corpse at the north end of the room is too obscured by its funeral wrappings to be fully examined.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

A successful [[/skill arcana 13]] check confirms a few details:

  • The corpses are currently benefitting from the effects of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGentleRepo]{Gentle Repose} spell, one of Ember's "sacred" Necromancy spells.

  • The water in the basin is sourced from permanent versions of spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCreateorDe]{Create or Destroy Water} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplPurifyFood]{Purify Food and Drink}.

Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell reveals an aura of Transmutation magic on the water basin and an aura of sacred Necromancy on the corpses.

Chamber of Remembrance.name: Chamber of Remembrance
Chamber of Remembrance.text:
This sizable circular chamber is lined with marble benches, and features a plinth at its center atop a rectangular dais. Surrounded by half-burned candles and tiny relics, this appears to be an offering space, where mementos have been left behind to honor the dead.

Known as the Chamber of Remembrance, this room serves as a gathering place for friends, family, and associates of the recently deceased, where they're encouraged to leave something behind for the dearly departed. Anyone and everyone who wishes to honor the deceased can sit here in attendance of the sacred ceremony.

Exploring the Chamber

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 13]] or [[/skill history 16]] check is aware of the room's precise purpose and the procedures that accompany it.

  • People gather here to leave a memento or personal effect on the plinth in honor of the recently deceased. These mementos are typically collected after the cremation and relocated to a reliquary elsewhere in the Burial Grounds.

  • An effigy of the recently usually decorates the plinth during the ceremony — from carved busts of wood or stone, to illustrated and illusory likenesses.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Looting the Mementos

Although it would be considered ethically unsavory, any character who attempts to loot the plinth is able to find [[/award 1d6sp]] loose silver pieces and at least one item of interest.

  • Roll [[/roll 1d2]] times on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} Table.

  • Characters caught stealing personal effects and mementos from the Cindaric Crematorium are subject to prosecution by the Cindaric Sages themselves and agents of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}.

Chamber of Communion.name: Chamber of Communion
Chamber of Communion.text:
The stone slab at the center of this room is marked with intricate carvings and lavish embellishments, denoting a place of honor or status. The marble benches arranged around this stone table are positioned close to it, suggesting the act of observance and an overt air of intimacy.

The Chamber of Communion is a room where the close friends and family members of a dead person can gather around their fully-prepared corpse for an intimate moment of last goodbyes.

Exploring the Chamber

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 13]] or [[/skill history 16]] check is aware of the room's precise purpose and the procedures that accompany it.

  • Intimate friends and family gather here to say goodbye to the physical remains of the recently deceased.

  • This stage of the funeral can last one to three hours prior to the cremation ceremony (if not longer), but is typically limited to a single hour of observance.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 15]] check while examining the slab is able to identify the table's carvings as the litany of a Cindaric prayer written in [[/language arcden]], meant to protect a soul on its metaphysical journey to Mortolis.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] and [[/knowledge souls]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Chamber of Reflection.name: Chamber of Reflection
Chamber of Reflection.text:
This small round chamber has room for little more than the etched marble slab and two stone benches that occupy it. Perhaps its' just the relatively meager size, but somehow this room feels more solemn and lonely than the rest.

Once the friends and family of the recently deceased have had ample time for observation and remembrance in the @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.RYoIAnVfBBwlJc6V]{Chamber of Communion}, the body is brought here to the Chamber of Reflection for temporary staging prior to the actual cremation. Meanwhile, the funeral attendees pass through on their way northward to the @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.JozGvLULBUbiPaJf]{Funeral Hall}.

A large steel door is located on the western wall at the northern end of the chamber. This threshold is unlocked, and can be controlled with a lever on each side.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 13]] or [[/skill history 16]] check is aware of the room's precise purpose and the procedures that accompany it.

  • This smaller circular chamber serves as a final staging area for the fully-prepared embalmed corpse, which is brought here from the @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.RYoIAnVfBBwlJc6V]{Chamber of Communion} immediately prior to the cremation ceremony.

  • The benches here are for the comfort of the deceased's partner or next-of-kin, who may attend the body through the rest of the procedure if they choose.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 15]] check while examining the etched slab is able to identify the table's carvings as the litany of a Cindaric prayer written in [[/language arcden]], meant to protect a physical body from the corruption of undeath.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] and [[/knowledge undeath]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Funeral Hall.name: Funeral Hall
Funeral Hall.text:
This massive chamber is lit by the soft, orange glow of the colossal magma pit that lies far, far below the scorched stone platform raised above its center.
