Lined with a dozen marble benches and a guard rail for viewers, this grand hall plays host to the final stage of Cindaric cremation ceremonies — when a fully-prepared body is lowered into the molten liquid that seethes with fiery rage deep beneath the Burial Grounds.

At the southern end of the room, two shallow alcoves are crammed full of half-burnt candles as petty, final offerings for the deceased. And a collection of six robed statues lines the walls to the east and west — effigies of notable Cindarics who look upon the fire-lit scene with eternal reverence.

The key feature of this enormous Funeral Hall is the 120-foot-deep magma pit that it's built around — known to some as the Heartblood Maw — which facilitates the final step of the Cindaric funerary rites: the cremation itself.

Congregants are invited to gather here after passing through the Chambers of Remembrance, Communion, and Reflection accordingly; and funeral-goers are known to both sit on the marble benches and stand near the edge of the pit itself during the ceremony. "To each their own," as the sages are fond of saying.

The door to the south usually remains closed and locked until the closing of the cremation ceremony, when attendees exit the facility arm-in-arm.

Exploring the Funeral Hall

Any character who searches the Funeral Hall is able to spot the following details:

  • While a few of the candles in the alcoves to the south are lit, most of them have either burned down to nubs or have grown cold with disregard.

  • A couple of loose @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.odV5cq2HSLSCH69k]{Prayer Books} of various faiths are scattered about the hall, forgotten beneath a stone bench here or there.

  • A lever is situated on the northern edge of the central, circular platform above pit. (See "Operating the Platform Elevator" below).

The Candlelit Alcove

Any character that succeeds on a [[/skill religion 12]] understands that people of various faiths are known to light candles here and leave a small offerings according to their respective god’s traditions. This small ceremony is often accompanied by a temporary divine boon.

  • Any character who takes 1 turn to light a candle and leave their own offering instantly becomes the target of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplBless00000]{Bless} spell.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] or [[/knowledge gods]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The Six Sages

Any character that succeeds on a [[/skill history 14]] or [[/skill religion 14]] check recognizes the statues on the curving eastern and western walls as effigies of famous Cindaric Sages throughout history.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 16+: Cindaric effigies like these are sometimes known to be enchanted with beneficial magic to ease the troubled in times of distress.

Once per day, each of these 6 statues can be activated to radiate the effects of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCalmEmotio]{Calm Emotions} spell in a 15-foot radius for a duration of 1 minute.

  • This effect is activated when a character touches the statue's Cindaric holy symbol and says the command phrase "By Adonia's Grace."

  • These words are etched in [[/language arcden]] across the statue, cleverly hidden in decorative patterns (successful [[/skill perception 13]] check to spot while searching the statues).

A successful [[/skill arcana 15]] check confirms the following:

  • The statues are enchanted with some sort of spell-like effect.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell reveals an aura of Enchantment magic on the statues.

The Heartblood Maw

If and when one of the characters attempts to survey the edge of the fiery magma pit that dominates this chamber, read the following aloud:

You can feel the soft, steady blast of heat before you even reach the edge of the massive pit at the rear of this enormous chamber, which appears to stretch down into the earth for more than a hundred feet. Down below, magma roils with constant fiery chaos. The Heartblood of Ember itself … radiant, magnificent, and pure. A headlong tumble into this gaping maw would mean certain death.

Operating the Platform Elevator

A lever at the northern end of the platform controls the central elevator, which can be lowered into the magma 120 feet below. The mechanical elevator is quite slow, and travels 10 feet up or down per turn.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 15]] check is aware of the platform elevator's purpose:

  • During a Cindaric funeral's final moments, a fully-prepared corpse is traditionally lowered into the magma by a senior sage after being placed on the stone slab at its center. Occasionally, another person of interest or a close family member will perform this solemn task.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] or [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Falling into the Maw

Any character who falls into the Heartblood Maw (without managing to somehow escape) dies a sudden, fiery death as they're submerged in the pit's molten magma — a demise more painful than they ever imagined.

House Cevher Mausoleum.name: House Cevher Mausoleum
House Cevher Mausoleum.text:
Carved from an array of semi-precious stones, the various grave markers and statues surrounding this pear-shaped mausoleum bear the familiar names and faces of deceased members of House Cevher, Ordain's famed Trading House. A placard above the door labeled "HOUSE CEVHER" confirms the stately crypt's ownership, and the seams around its heavy iron doors provide the barest glimpse of the half-dozen graves that lurk inside.

This mausoleum is one of many such tombs owned by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}, and contains the remains of various Cevher personalities who predate or abstain from the Cindaric faith.

Locked Doors

The two iron doors to the mausoleum are locked, and can be opened with a @UUID[Item.Jljq6rNYRuNljRJi]{Burial Grounds Skeleton Key} or a successful [[/skill tool=thief 18]] check.

The ledger stones in this pear-shaped mausoleum live up to the name posted on the placard outside. Rather than the traditional white rock you see throughout the cemetery, these grave markers appear to be made of various semi-precious stones — agate, rose quartz, and moonstone among them. This crypt seems well-attended, as evident by the somewhat recent footprints that track through here, and the lambent inkaro pearls of the braziers.

Exploring the Mausoleum

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] check is able to identify this mausoleum for the monument it is, and is also aware of the following historical context surrounding the edifice.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] or [[/culture Ordani]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • The corpses interred here are the remains of eight family members of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}, Ordain's dynastic Trading House. The ledger stones mark the graves of family members lost during a plague of Crimson Cough several generations ago, including the geologist Druna Cevher and her twin children, the famed warrior Lelynd Cevher, and others.

  • Result of 18+: The easternmost stones here comprise the graves of a two House Cevher cousins, Erna and Ora, who were known for their innate divination abilities.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 16]] check is able to identify the ledger stones of Erna and Ora Cevher as unique substitutes for arcane foci with a special function.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Once per week, an arcane spellcaster who uses these ledger stones as an arcane spellcasting focus can cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDivination]{Divination} spell, whether they know the spell or not.

  • A character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} spell to examine the ledger stones automatically succeeds on this check.

The two sconces on the southern wall each contain one @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{White Inkaro Pearl}. These have been replaced recently by the Lamplighters who work the Burial Grounds to facilitate forthcoming visitations from House Cevher descendants.

Sarcophagus Contents

Both of the sarcophagi here are locked. The sarcophagus on the western wall contains the mortal remains of Druna Cevher and the following:

  • A tarnished @UUID[Item.vM7lkAcMJG2d8CiG]{House Cevher Signet Ring}.

  • A dusty @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagMagnifyingG]{Magnifying Glass} with the initials "D.C." etched into the wooden handle.

The sarcophagus on the southern wall contains the remains of Lelynd Cevher and the following:

  • A suit of bronze @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmChainMail0]{Chain Mail} coated in a patina of verdigris.

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepLongsword0]{Longsword} with a faceted garnet set into the pommel, worth a total of 50 gp.

A successful [[/skill tool=thief 20]] check is required to pick the locks on the sarcophagi. Alternately, a character can force the heavy sarcophagi lids open with a successful [[/skill strength 25]] check.

Trapped Sarcophagi

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the mausoleum is able to notice the telltale signs of matching mechanical traps on the two locked sarcophagi here.

  • A subsequent [[/skill investigation 15]] or [[/skill arcana 17]] check confirms the nature of the trap: tiny holes in the stone floor surrounding each sarcophagus seem to be connected to tiny conduits, which likely emit or expel some kind of substance from an unseen reservoir or extra-dimensional space beneath the mausoleum.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

Each trap can be disarmed with a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 16]] check. Failure results in triggering the trap, and the trap can be triggered indefinitely.

If character attempts to open one of the two sarcophagi without first disarming the trap, all characters inside the mausoleum must succeed on a [[/save constitution 18]] to avoid taking [[/roll 2d6]] poison damage and 1 level of Exhaustion from a strange poison mist that seeps into the chamber via the tiny holes in the floor.

Tomb of Spectra's Chosen.name: Tomb of Spectra's Chosen
Tomb of Spectra's Chosen.text:
This octagonal mausoleum is surrounded by statues of robed humanoid figures tattooed with esoteric sigils. Three adamantine doors seal this tomb away from the outside world, and its spired rooftop stands out as the tallest edifice in this section of the cemetery. However, no placard or sign reveals this curious mausoleum's name or ownership.

This mausoleum is known as the Tomb of Spectra's Chosen, and serves as the final resting place of nine of the elder goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra}'s most loyal and storied acolytes.

Locked Doors

The three iron doors to the mausoleum are locked, and can be opened with a @UUID[Item.Jljq6rNYRuNljRJi]{Burial Grounds Skeleton Key} or a successful [[/skill tool=thief 18]] check.

The interior confines of this mysterious crypt are adorned with nine ledger stones encircling a tenth, larger grave at the center of the chamber. The half-melted candles surrounding this central ledger stone appear to burn with perpetual light, as if the wax itself is arcane and unmoving. The soft sound of ethereal chimes lingers here, emitted from some unseen source within the tomb's arched ceiling or shaded eaves.

Exploring the Mausoleum

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] check is able to identify this mausoleum for the monument it is, and is also aware of the following historical context surrounding the edifice.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge gods]] and characters who worship Spectra have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • The corpses interred here are the remains of ten notable acolytes of the shard goddess Spectra. Half are persons of historical significance in Ordain, while the rest hail from various corners of Ember.

  • Spectra is known to bless her chosen acolytes with special boons of arcane prowess that might otherwise be outside their abilities. Some of the dead here weren't simply mages; they include clerics, warlocks, and arcane warriors as well.

  • Result of 18+: The large ledger stone at the center of the mausoleum belongs to a famed Cor'ak scholar-mage known as The Rebus, whose legendary enchantments and illusions within the Anachraenum's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0]{All-Fable Keep} endure to this very day.

Characters with a [[/skill perception passive=long 13]] or who succeed on a [[/skill perception 15]] check are able to spot curious arcane symbols hidden with the patterns on each of the nine ledger stones.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 12]] check is able to identify these symbols as the icons of seven arcane traditions — with the taboo school of necromancy the only missing symbol.

  • Result of 17+: Some of the symbols and written characters etched upon the central ledger stone can be identified as arcane writing equal to three spell scrolls. The spells include: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSilentImag]{Silent Image}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplNystulsMag]{Arcanist's Magic Aura}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSuggestion]{Suggestion}.

Any arcane spellcaster who succeeds on a [[/skill sleightofhand 15]] is able to transfer the symbols to a parchment via a charcoal grave rubbing or a comparable technique; these rubbings can eventually be transcribed into an arcane spellcaster's grimoire, but they cannot be used as spell scrolls.

Trapped Ledger Stones

Any character who attempts to unearth, damage, or deface the graves here is subject to the effects of a special @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplBefuddleme]{Befuddlement} spell trap, and must succeed on a [[/save intelligence 20]] saving throw to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplBefuddleme.ActiveEffect.KjjRlnccDwmAY7gG]{Befuddled}, taking [[/roll 2d12]] psychic damage on a failure instead of the standard 10d12. All other effects of the Befuddlement spell behave as normal.

Anrak Mausoleum.name: Anrak Mausoleum
Anrak Mausoleum.text:
This L-shaped sepulcher houses three ledger stones marked with the characters of a foreign language. Moss-laden and musky, this monument appears somewhat harried by the ebb and flow of weather conditions here on the Burial Grounds hillside.

This small mausoleum is dedicated to the famed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.1WoH2TVw0gngrgWL]{Kessian} pilgrim known as Tula Anrak, who helped establish the Temple of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.XUn8UELVkQmnCI78]{Temple Ward}.

Exploration the Mausoleum

The text etched on the ledger stones and in other places here is written in [[/language solical]], the native tongue of Tula Anrak and her celebrated adventuring party — the Dawnstriders.

  • Any character who can read these etchings will learn that this is Tula Anrak's crypt, but know relatively little about the pilgrim herself.

  • The etchings also tell the story of a grand mythical narrative, when @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.8PNpme2Ot0zfHLBH]{Lantyr} gifted his chosen priests various sacred relics to fight a formidable darkness during the time of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering}. Although these relics were lost to the ages, legends say the elder god's priests were permanently blessed with a measure of Lantyr's divine energy.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 15]] check is familiar with the legends of Tula Anrak and the Dawnstriders.

  • Legends say Tula Anrak was responsible for introducing several essential scriptures of Lantyr's tenets to the Arctus Plateau, in addition to her founding of the temple in Ordain.

  • Result of 18+: Some legends say Tula's body itself was blessed by Lantyr, and that her bones radiate the Sun's divine energy from the depths of her stony tomb.

  • [[/culture Kessian]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge gods]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Blessing of the Energy Moon

Characters with a [[/skill religion 13 passive format=long]] or who succeed on a [[/skill religion 15]] check understand the Anrak Mausoleum's ability to channel divine magic via the power of Lantyr, the ever-burning Sun.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]], [[/knowledge gods]], and [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who spends 5 minutes praying to Lantyr at the Anrak Mausoleum and succeeds on a [[/skill wisdom 15]] check gains the ability to cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDaylight00]{Daylight} spell once during the next 24 hours, regardless of their class.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Regardless of whether or not they succeed on this check, characters with [[/attunement Lantyr]] also gain one temporary level of Attunement, which lasts for 24 hours.

Prestyn Mausoleum.name: Prestyn Mausoleum
Prestyn Mausoleum.text:
The interior walls of this circular crypt are decorated with an elaborate relief that depicts a fantastic scene: an armored warrior equipped with a mighty glaive lands the killing blow against a terrible draconic creature wreathed in phantasmagorical death. A solitary stone sarcophagus sits at the center of this open-air mausoleum, which exudes a sense of stoic loneliness here by itself.

This mausoleum honors the legendary Kelmezian dragonslayer Rhydel Prestyn, and is accurately rumored to hold a solitary finger of the Shattering-era champion in a reliquary sealed within its impenetrable lone sarcophagus.

Exploring the Mausoleum

The sarcophagus here is made of an ancient stone reinforced with powerful magic. It cannot be opened by any means known to humanoid kind.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] check is somewhat familiar with the legend of Dragonslayer Prestyn, and of the various reliquaries that host his holy remains.

  • This mausoleum is said to hold Prestyn's left ring finger, which was severed by the Dragonslayer in an attempt to remove a cursed ring. According to the tales, no one alive has ever seen the relic.

  • Result of 18+: Certainly everyone knows that the various crypts and mausoleums that pay tribute to Rhydel Prestyn are ensorcelled with supremely potent magic to protect their sacred contents. Only a fool would attempt to rob or defile them.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check while searching the mausoleum finds a warning etched in [[/language arcden]] along the steps of the threshold:

Let whosoever attempts to open this reliquary hold fast to damnation, lest they be descendants of Prestyn himself. Prove yourself elsewhere, pup.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check is able to notice the powerful traps and wards placed on the mausoleum (see "Phantasmal Killer Trap" below).

Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell reveals the presence of powerful Illusion and Abjuration magic.

The first time a character attempts to open the sarcophagus at the center of the mausoleum, read the following aloud:

The marble sarcophagus feels surprisingly hot to the touch, and the smell of ozone fills the air for a brief moment as a bolt of static shock licks at your fingertips. A feeling in your gut compels you to pull away from the stony, rune-marked coffin before something worse happens.

Subsequent attempts to open the sarcophagus are met with folly.

Phantasmal Killer Trap

Those foolish enough to attempt to vandalize or loot the contents of the mausoleum's sarcophagus become the target of a powerful illusion spell, which causes the various figures depicted in the relief on the wall to seemingly come to life and attack the would-be grave robbers.

Any character who ignores the warning and attempts to open or damage the sarcophagus (or the monument at large) must succeed on a [[/skill wisdom 20]] saving throw or become the target of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplPhantasmal]{Phantasmal Killer} spell (Spell Save DC 20).

  • This effect lasts for [[/roll 1d4+1]] rounds. For this duration, the character can attempt the [[/skill wisdom 20]] save at the end of each of its turns.

  • Additionally, an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAntimagicF]{Antimagic Field} appears at the center of the chamber, with a radius of 20 feet and a duration of 1 hour. Other magical effects of the mausoleum itself are immune to this particular antimagic field.

Lamplighter's Rest.name: Lamplighter's Rest
Lamplighter's Rest.text:
The walls of this wide open-air mausoleum are remarkably well-kept compared to a few other structures nearby, as evident by the lack of mildew and mossy overgrowth. A soft breeze stirs through the arches of this proud edifice, labeled honorably by a bronze plaque as "Lamplighter's Rest."

This mausoleum serves as the final resting place for the worldly remains of a handful of venerated lamplighters, noble souls who once served Ordain as caretakers of the Burial Grounds.

Exploration the Mausoleum

Four ledger stones are set into the marble floor of the mausoleum. They surround a large sarcophagus at the building's center.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 15]] check is able to identify this mausoleum for the monument it is, and is aware of the following historical context surrounding the edifice:

  • Some of Ordain's first Lamplighters are buried here, including a trio of Cindarics who served as the original Lamplighters of the Burial Grounds.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who takes a moment to search the mausoleum will discover the following:

  • The ledger stone situated in the northwest corner of the mausoleum appears to be the newest among the group, and is decorated with some recent offerings and mementos from an admirer or loved one. These items include two blue roses, a @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{White Inkaro Pearl}, and a set of edge-worn @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbgstDice000000]{Dice}.

Examining the Sarcophagus

The sarcophagus at the center of the mausoleum is unlocked, and contains little more than the dusty bones of an unknown Lamplighter and tattered burial rags.

Ashvale Mausoleum.name: Ashvale Mausoleum
Ashvale Mausoleum.text:
The exterior of this squat mausoleum is somewhat austere compared to other structures of the cemetery. The tomb's solitary door appears made of some kind of bronze alloy, and a placard beside it labels this edifice as the "Ashvale Mausoleum."

This mausoleum serves as the final resting place for a handful of celebrated @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} soldiers who dutifully served the Cindarics in recent centuries.

Locked Door

The heavy bronze alloy door to the mausoleum is locked, and can be opened with a @UUID[Item.Jljq6rNYRuNljRJi]{Burial Grounds Skeleton Key} or a successful [[/skill tool=thief 18]] check.

Inside the mausoleum's dank interior, you spy six ledger stones overlooked by four stone statues of heavily-armored warriors. At the rear end of the crypt, a large sarcophagus dominates the chamber, silent and stoic in the shadows.

Exploring the Mausoleum

Six ledger stones are set into the marble floor of the mausoleum, and a large sarcophagus occupies the building's rear. The four stone statues of armored warriors are crafted to resemble Burnished Hand soldiers from its earliest days.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] check is able to identify this mausoleum for the monument it is, and is also aware of the following historical context surrounding the edifice.

  • Signifiers of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} culture are present here among the architectural embellishments — particularly upon the blades and armor of the four statues, and the mausoleum's stained glass windows.

  • The mausoleum is named after the historical "Old Ashvale" district of Ordain, where Lower Ashvale stands today, a neighborhood where the interests of the Cindaric Sages and their Burnished Hand allies are paramount.

  • Result of 18+: The Burnished Hand soldiers interred here were known as the Ashvale Six, and each was a formidable legend in their own right. Before their time as Burnished Hand protectors, the Ashvale Six were famed monster hunters, and fragments of their tales are told from here to the Tayan Empire.

  • [[/ancestry Oaken]] and [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The Cursed Sarcophagus

The sarcophagus at the eastern end of the chamber is locked and contains a solitary item, a rare and antique book of ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} myths known as @UUID[Item.PMXHbh24YAH3THNA]{Predators of the Prowling Death}.

Any character who takes a moment to Search the mausoleum must succeed on a [[/skill perception 11]] check to notice a sentence etched into the stone lid of the sarcophagus, written in [[/language hardac]]:

What is Ember's greatest legacy?

This is a riddle to uncovering the pass phrase capable of disarming the magic trap that's been placed on the sarcophagus lock: "Resolution" (or, alternately "Resolve"), referring to the @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.PA5iwFx87WR65pXa]{Resolute Legacy} cultural feature.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check are able to discern the pass phrase after cross-referencing their collective knowledge.

  • [[/ancestry Oaken]] and [[/path MonsterHunter]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

A successful [[/skill tool=thief 18]] check is required to pick the lock. Alternately, a character can force the heavy sarcophagus lid open with a successful [[/skill strength 25]] check.

Cursed Sarcophagus Trap

Any character who succeeds on either a [[/skill perception 16]] or [[/skill arcana 14]] check while searching the sarcophagus is able to notice the telltale signs of an arcane trap on the locking mechanism.

  • The first character who opens this sarcophagus without first speaking the pass phrase "Resolution" (alternately "Resolve") or dispelling the magic trap becomes the target of a special @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRemoveCurs]{Bestow Curse} spell's Curse Ability activity. All characters within 20 feet of the sarcophagus must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 20]] saving throw or else have @Advantage[-2] on Wisdom ability checks and saving throws for a duration of 10 days.

  • The spell also magically stains the characters with a metallic bronze dye, intended to identify them as grave-robbers to the Cindarics and Burnished Hand in Ordain. The dye has a duration of 10 days, and it can only be removed using a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} spell.

Crematorium Gate.name: Crematorium Gate
Crematorium Gate.text:
Dark stone steps ascend to a shallow alcove cut into the craggy hillside, where a large metallic gate marks the entrance of an underground facility. Made of a reinforced adamantine alloy, the massive door is decorated with the diamond-shaped sigil of the Cindaric Sages, and looks nigh impenetrable — with no a handle or keyhole in sight.

This adamantine gate serves as the only entrance to the Cindaric Crematorium facility, and is sealed with both mechanical and magical locks.

A @UUID[Item.LE30SP15s4dnCFnb]{Cindaric Crematorium Key} is needed to open the Crematorium Gate without triggering the stun trap associated with it (see below).

Surveying the Crematorium Gate

The Crematorium Gate is crafted from a unique, magically-reinforced adamantine alloy. It has 200 hp, an AC of 25, and a Damage Threshold of 30.

Any character with a [[/check prc 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill prc 13]] check while searching the door is able to spot the locking mechanism, which is hidden at the center of the Cindaric sigil.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • The door can be opened with successful [[/skill tool=thief 30]] check or with a @UUID[Item.LE30SP15s4dnCFnb]{Cindaric Crematorium Key}.

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplKnock00000]{Knock} spell has no effect on this lock.

  • Result of 16+: The character is able to notice the telltale signs of a magical trap on and around the lock.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] check is able to verify this gate as the entrance to the Cindaric Crematorium, where sacred funerary rites are conducted by the Cindarics for the people of Ordain.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters automatically succeed on this check.

A successful [[/skill survival 13]] check reveals the presence of sandaled and booted tracks passing in and out of the gate via the alcove here, which are easily identified as the footwear of the Cindaric Sages who work the Burial Grounds.

  • Result of 15+: The latest tracks are roughly 6 to 12 hours old.

Magical Stun Trap

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check is able to detect the telltale signs of a magical trap on the door. Alternately, the trap can be found with a successful [[/skill perception 16]] check.

Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell will reveal the presence of Enchantment magic on the Cindaric sigil that decorates the adamantine gate.

Any character who attempts to open the Crematorium Gate without using the @UUID[Item.LE30SP15s4dnCFnb]{Cindaric Crematorium Key} becomes the target of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplPowerWordS]{Power Word Stun} (Spell Save DC 30) with a duration of [[/roll 1d4+1]] minutes.

The Spell Save DC for @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} when targeting the Crematorium Gate is 30.

When the characters open the door for the first time, read the following aloud:

The intricate lines of the Cindaric sigil flash with a blood-orange arcane brilliance just before the heavy adamantine door starts rising up into a recessed area of the rock. A hallway greets you on the other side, decorated with a narrow throw rug that extends directly from your feet to another lustrous door on the opposite end of the antechamber.

Antechamber.name: Antechamber
Antechamber.text:
This wedge-shaped antechamber acts as a modest and unassuming foyer for the facility that lurks beyond. The sconces on the walls here burn with perpetual arcane firelight, which casts its flickering radiance on a large metallic door to the north.

This simple Antechamber is sparsely decorated, and serves as a straightforward junction for ambulation during ceremonies and rituals — when people other than the Cindaric Sages themselves are visiting the facility.

Funeral Hall Gate

This adamantine gate serves as the forward entrance to the @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.JozGvLULBUbiPaJf]{Funeral Hall} section of the Cindaric Crematorium facility, and is sealed with stout mechanical locks.

A @UUID[Item.Jljq6rNYRuNljRJi]{Burial Grounds Skeleton Key} is needed to open the Crematorium Gate without the benefit of Thieves' Tools (see below).

During ceremonial events, when the friends and family of the deceased gather to pay their respects, this gate remains shut until the sacred rites are concluded — at which time it is opened by one of the Cindaric Sages for accessible passage.

Meanwhile, smaller steel portcullises are located to the east and west. These grated thresholds are unlocked, controlled with levers to each side, and are used by the Cindaric Sages to guide foot-traffic control during ceremonial gatherings.

Surveying the Funeral Hall Gate

The Funeral Hall Gate is crafted from a unique, magically-reinforced adamantine alloy. It has 200 hp, an AC of 25, and a Damage Threshold of 30.

Any character with a [[/check prc 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill prc 11]] check while searching the door is able to spot the concealed locking mechanism.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Failed attempts at spotting the locking mechanism can be repeated once per five minutes.

Locked Door

The Funeral Hall Gate lock can only be opened with a @UUID[Item.Jljq6rNYRuNljRJi]{Burial Grounds Skeleton Key} or a successful [[/skill tool=thief 25]] check.

Ruined Mausoleum.name: Ruined Mausoleum
Ruined Mausoleum.text:
The foundation of this forgotten mausoleum has sunk deep into the earth, and its timeworn walls are streaked with cracks. It seems a massive shift in the terrain here has rendered the crypt's dark interior entirely unreachable.

The walls of this crumbling mausoleum are impenetrable by most means. Even if someone could reach the interior, they'd find it effectively empty or full of rubble and rampant overgrowth.

Examining the Ruined Mausoluem

Any character that succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] or [[/skill nature 15]] check can deduce that the notorious earthquakes of the region have been unkind to this structure during some previous seismic upheaval, and are responsible for its ruination.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This main quest occurs during Chapter 2, and begins if the party [[/eventState windingTrailLeavetaking lyla]] at the end of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai]{The Winding Trail}. If the party chose not to, they can still rejoin Lyla at a later time, in which case they start the "An Old Friend" quest partway through, via the [[/eventState otherhood1Reunite]] event.

Once any of the Chapter 2 main quests have been completed, it is no longer possible to access this quest (as Lyla has independently reached Ordain without the party's assistance).

Difficulty

The "An Old Friend" quest is designed for a party of Level 3 characters. It begins upon leaving @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}. If the party did not thoroughly explore the Forest of Stone and its respective Chapter 1 side quests, they may still be Level 2. They can either press forward and expect to advance to Level 3 upon obtaining their next milestone point, or they could be encouraged to backtrack and explore further.

Milestone Progression

This is a Main Quest quest that awards 3 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the [[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel2]], [[/eventState otherhood1Escape]], and [[/eventState otherhood1Ordinate]] Events.

The party begins this quest immediately after deciding to accompany @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher} on her quest to uncover who is behind the bandit attacks at @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}. With a few leads to follow up on — the shifting ink used in the bandits' notes, a style mark on the leather worn by the bandits, and an odd phrase on their tattoos — Lyla heads to Oldcraft Lodge to get information from her friend @UUID[Actor.qmMlHizvtjCYKjCR]{Sigil}, a Shard God known for his knowledge. There, he informs her that the Entire Arctus Plateau has been disrupted, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel}, another settlement affiliated with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher}, has been troubled recently. The issues may be related.

In Arcturel, a series of unfortunate incidents turns out to have an exceptionally surprising cause. @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Kilner}, a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem} from the Inner Realm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.pPU6VZV7WFubtcSR]{Luxarum}, was sent to Arcturel along with several Celestial creatures to defame House Cevher. After an intense confrontation, the party uncovers the instructions given to Kilner that implicate another Trading House, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{House Wandren}, as well as the bandits that Lyla is already tracking down. As the party leaves Arcturel, Lyla tracks down an old childhood friend, @UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren}, in the small village of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fBPE6UWg6EOO2WFH]{Nain}, who suggests that the problems facing House Cevher are even greater than Lyla fears, urging Lyla to return to Ordain as soon as possible. Despite the advice, Lyla decides one more stop is needed, as the information gathered so far points to the nearby port of Seawall. On entering @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.X1FzWfTYfe7JfD3P]{Seawall}, the truth becomes clear: Seawall has become a secret bastion of a group called the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood}. The Otherhood's leader @UUID[Actor.z1Ttp0q6CAtjDphl]{Sticks} explicitly and brazenly blames House Cevher and the other Trading Houses of Ordain for many of the Arctus Plateau's recent troubles. The party is soon uncovered, and they must flee Seawall for Ordain by ship.

Once Lyla reaches @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Mnh1EGR4ir1wpumM]{Ordain}, though, her troubles are not over. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{The Ordinate} makes a stunning public declaration, proclaiming that @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher} is responsible for the earthquake that many believe started the current problems facing the region twenty years ago after a long investigation. They remove House Cevher's seat, and Lyla narrowly avoids imprisonment while the Ordanite decides what punishment to inflict on her house. Worse still, her uncle has been murdered, and her @UUID[Actor.E701HRk9vreXMUhl]{brother} is missing, leaving Lyla and House Cevher's future uncertain.

Related Quests

This is the first quest in the overarching Otherhood of Fortune storyline which includes:

  1. @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu]

  2. @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1]

  3. @UUID[JournalEntry.mytyUKL7PyABLVRp]

  4. @UUID[JournalEntry.iw9aRpGjVc3iLv7E]

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher}

  • @UUID[Actor.qmMlHizvtjCYKjCR]{Sigil}

  • @UUID[Actor.z1Ttp0q6CAtjDphl]{Sticks}

  • @UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren}

  • @UUID[Actor.K9E6i8i8bO3dViwg]{Salara, Queen of Scales}

  • @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Kilner}

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H]{Otherhood Raider}

  • @UUID[Actor.VRyq5hmqCTUY2ZYO]{Otherhood Brigand}

  • @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{Skither}

  • @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR]{Vorg}
Overview.soverview:
With the town of Helkas still smoldering from the aftermath of the attack, Lyla Cevher's path is unclear. On one hand, she needs to return to Ordain as planned, but now she is determined to uncover why the town was attacked in the first place and whether her family's holdings on the plateau are under threat. Though she has been away from the Arctus Plateau for several years, Lyla still has friends in the area who can help her track down the bandits and learn why they chose Helkas as their target.

If you choose to accompany Lyla, you begin your journey with a visit to the absentminded Shard God Sigil, who has turned his home, Oldcraft Lodge, into an impromptu settlement for refugees. The information Lyla learns there does not put her mind at ease. It is clear that the attack on Helkas is part of some grander plan designed by whoever organized the bandits.

In "An Old Friend" you will journey with Lyla Cevher as she makes her way through the Arctus Plateau, visiting several House Cevher operations, attempting to discover who or what is behind the bandit attacks and what they hope to accomplish. Along the way, you will: visit Arcturel, a mining town built in a giant chasm in the ground; meet a god and one of Lyla's disruptable friends from her childhood; make your way to the city of Seawall on the coast that could hold the key to understanding what the bandits want … if you can find a way to get the information without getting caught.

A Friendly Reunion.name: A Friendly Reunion
A Friendly Reunion.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social and exploration event, Lyla and the party members ask for help and information from the Shard God Sigil. Sigil gives them additional leads to pursue the bandits and alerts them to a crisis in Arcturel.

In this event, the part begins on the region map, approaching Oldcraft lodge and attempting to speak with Sigil before accidently trigging a magical accident. The scene then changes to the @UUID[Scene.emberOldcraftLod]{Oldcraft Lodge} area map as the party has to track down several @UUID[Actor.dohbTGwgummsG9g7]{Light Motes} before Sigil will talk to them.

In this event, the party can:

  • Strategize about the clues they have in hand, which could lead them to the identity of the Helkas bandits.

  • Track down and soothe @UUID[Actor.dohbTGwgummsG9g7]{Light Motes} on the are map of @UUID[Scene.emberOldcraftLod]{Oldcraft Lodge}.

  • Speak with Sigil and ask him about the bandits and any other problems currently affecting the Arctus Plateau.

  • Optionally, speak with the refugees at the improvised campsite and learn more about the chaos unfolding in the Arctus Plateau.

Outcome Note

Parties receive @UUID[Item.r659n05meW0ZMGY9]{Coded Bandit Instructions} from Lyla during this event. They will have several opportunities to decode the instruction over the course of the quest, including in this event. If characters decode the instructions later in the quest, return to this event to mark it as a completed outcome and award the attunement point noted below.

A Greeting From Svala

Before the party decides to move into the lodge and speak with Sigil, they can optionally decide to wait and speak with Svala, who greeted the characters when they arrived.

@Embed[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb]

Speaking with Svala

Svala Bronwen is a confident Vrjnhar from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} and a peerless warrior and wanderer. Having endured many trials, she is keen to prove herself in the Arctus Plateau. Instead of trekking across the plateau searching for the "cowardly" bandits, she plans to gather clues from the refugees and stay alert, hoping the bandits might be foolish enough to attack Oldcraft Lodge. Although she typically hunts monsters, after learning of the people's plight in the regions, she is taking her duty as a warrior very seriously and plans to rid the plateau of thier blight.

She is glad to pause and chat with the party about fighting techniques and her larger goal of traveling the world to encounter deadly monsters, and she sings grand songs about her adventures.

The tail was hooked, the sting was red,
But Svala's axe found the monster’s head.
One swoop, one strike, the beast did fall,
Now its pelt hangs high in the Kalvard's hall!

If the party wants to talk to specially about the bandits that attacked Helkas, she has the following to say:

The bandit group is attacking locations across the Arctus Plateau, apparently at random. They have seemed more organized in their attacks in recent months. A few of the people who have arrived have been calling the bandits a strange name, I think it is "Otherhood". Not that it makes much difference to me, I'll split them apart all the same!

If the party asks about Sigil, she smiles and says:

Don't let his odd speech fool you; he is one of the most intelligent gods I've ever met—so much knowledge! It has been a pleasure to meet him.

Reviewing The Plan

As you step forward towards the large door of Oldcraft Lodge, Lyla stops you and beckons you to come closer so she can speak privately.

I brought us here to talk to Sigil, but it is far more crowded than I expected. I suspect that Sigil may be a little… distracted. So we should review what we have and focus on what we need to discuss with him.

The Clues At Hand

As the party stands close to the door, Lyla reminds the party about the clues found on the bandits in Helkas:

  • Coded Instructions to the Bandits. Lyla gives the party the @UUID[Item.r659n05meW0ZMGY9]{Coded Bandit Instructions} to attempt to decipher.

    • The party can try to decode the instructions at any time, but will need help — they can ask Sigil later on in this event or use a note found in the Arcturel Mine during [[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel2]]. Once the instructions are decoded, give the party members the @UUID[Item.4gnpLU3NcyXylMHB]{Decoded Bandit Instructions}, mark the outcome below, and mark the Primordis attunement point.

  • Leather Markings. Lyla has sketched the markings on the leather worn by the bandits, which could reveal either where they are from or who supplied them with gear. She reminds the party that this is the second question they should ask Sigil.

  • Tattoos. Several of the bandits had the phrase "For Other Fortunes" tattooed on them along with ropes. It likely has some hidden meaning that could point the party towards the bandits' origin or purpose and Lyla reminds the party that this is the third question they should ask Sigil.

Primordis Attunement: Bandit Instructions Decoded

When the party manages to decode the Coded Bandit Instructions, each character advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 otherhood1LodgeDecoded]] at the conclusion of the current event.

[[/outcome decodedBanditNote]]

Speaking with Sigil

Once the party has gone over the questions they need to ask Sigil with Lyla, then they can proceed inside, and you can read the following to the party:

Although the exterior of the Oldcraft Lodge is relatively unassuming, as soon as you step inside the main room from outside, you are immediately dazzled by a chaotic cacophony of sights and sounds. Bright yellow and pink motes of magic dance in the air, casting an enchanting glow around the space. Mystical runes are casually scattered in piles across tables and shelves. The room is filled with books of all sizes, colors, and ages; some sit half-open, while others have torn pages now lying in piles. Tall bookshelves line the walls, packed with more books and scrolls, and colorful rugs adorn the polished hardwood floor.

Standing near a large, comfortable-looking chair is a figure who appears to radiate magic in gentle waves. After only a few moments, the effects of his magical aura subside, and he turns toward you with a puzzled expression on his face. When he spots Lyla, his face lights up with joy, and he moves forward quickly. He begins speaking in a warm, melodic voice that reminds you of a wizened and wise grandfather.

Oh, OH! My dear little glowbug, welcome, welcome! The calluses on your hands... are they from a pickaxe or a sword? No, a rapier—ahh, the one on your hip. And your footprint... it’s heavier now. More certain. You've finally stopped dragging your left heel when you're nervous. Oh my dear, there is sadness in your eyes; it is so heavy... oh. Your father, that's right, I am so sorry.

Sigil stops in front of Lyla and slowly extends his arms to offer her an embrace, which doesn't seem like this kind of inmate contact comes easily to him. Lyla appears shocked at first but then willingly leans in, and they embrace for a few moments. When they part again, Sigil looks both pleased with himself for his efforts but also concerned for his once student at the same time. Lyla meanwhile dashes away tears that had been gathering in the corner of her eyes.

It's so wonderful to see you, Sigie. I wish I could spend more time catching up, but unfortunately, we have some urgent questions for you.

@Embed[Actor.qmMlHizvtjCYKjCR]

Before any questions can be asked, however, the Lodge seems to vibrate slightly and you can continue reading the following:

Before any further conversation can occur, an odd ringing sound can be heard in your ears. Suddenly, with a loud bang, several glowing yellow runes on the floor flash brightly, and multiple small Light Motes burst into existence. The swarm surrounds you and Sigil, who clenches his fists, frowning with a twisted mouth. Then, the motes burst through the door and scatter outside.

Sigil begins muttering under his breath.

So loud, where are they coming from! Light, Dark, Shadow, balance disturbed. Perhaps a new catalyst?

He turns back to you and Lyla, his hands now clasped together tightly.

Please, my dear, and your friends, if possible, deal with those things. I won't be able to concentrate on anything for hours. Endless disruptions, oh, OH, they are trampling over the wards!

The Mote Chase

At this point, the party transitions to the area map of @UUID[Scene.emberOldcraftLod]{Oldcraft Lodge} and can should follow the area walkthrough @UUID[JournalEntry.tZhj2UzXEN4cw4nl.JournalEntryPage.yXGyRKMat0SH0vCw]{The Mote Chase}.

Event Specific Area Walkthrough

The flow of this event is as follows.

  1. Speaking with Lyla and then Sigil on the region map (Optionally speaking with Svala)

  2. Transistioning to the area map of @UUID[Scene.emberOldcraftLod]{Oldcraft Lodge} and following @UUID[JournalEntry.tZhj2UzXEN4cw4nl.JournalEntryPage.yXGyRKMat0SH0vCw]{The Mote Chase}.

  3. Returning to this @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.6XGCgWBOeHH6HVlT]{A Friendly Reunion} and finish speaking with Sigil.

  4. Optionally: While the players are on the area map of @UUID[Scene.emberOldcraftLod]{Oldcraft Lodge} they may wish to look around and speak with refugees but the writing in @UUID[JournalEntry.tZhj2UzXEN4cw4nl.JournalEntryPage.6uhp2gZV0rwNUgoG]{Sigil's Living Room} is for anyone coming across Oldcraft Lodge without Lyla for the first time.

A Calmed Mind

Once the Light Motes in the @UUID[JournalEntry.tZhj2UzXEN4cw4nl.JournalEntryPage.yXGyRKMat0SH0vCw]{The Mote Chase} have been soothed. The party can return to Sigil and ask him their three questions about the bandits and any other topics they might have in mind.

Returning to the chaotic living room inside the lodge, Sigil appears visibly calmer, his soft smile has returned, and his hands are now resting on a book stand in front of him. He turns to look at Lyla and the party as they enter.

Very good! Thank you, glowbug, and friends, of course! Now it appears the vibrations have stopped. Yes, only two and a half percent remaining. Excellent. Oh yes, questions you said, it's likely I have answers.

A Conversation with Sigil

Lyla will begin speaking with Sigil. She is excited and out of breath after dealing with the motes, but she is able to accurately explain the events that led the party to Sigil. She talks about the attack on Helkas, the strange bandits, and drakes. She goes on to say the whole thing was too organized to be some random coincidence and suggests that Sigil's help could be useful in figuring out who or what is behind it.

Sigil nods along, listening with his head tilted, and begins tapping his finger slowly on the book in front of him.

Drakes? Oh, that's not good news. With two or four arms? Don't tell me, it's two. Even worse news. Helkas attacked? Another assault then; many of the refugees outside have been talking endlessly about these things. Fires, death, and destruction—it's not something I get involved in if I can help it.

Lyla gently interrupts the digression with a small cough.

I do have three questions that you may be able to help us with!

As the conversation continues, the question and answer blocks below can be used to create a conversation between Lyla and Sigil, or to have Sigil answer questions from the party. Sigil knows the following generally:

  • The Helkas attackers are likely part of a new group of organized bandits on the Arctus Plateau, called the "Otherhood." but he doesnt know much about them.

  • Lyla’s old friend, Juro Wandren, has helped Sigil obtain supplies from the village of Nain. Lyla will be visibly shocked at the news, but doesn’t say anything at the mention.

  • Sigil has been hearing odd rumors from Arcturel and believes something has gone wrong there as well.

  • Sigil doesn't know anything about the leather markings on the bandit's gear offhand, but a book about the markings may be on the shelf nearby or on the floor; he isn't entirely sure.

The mind of a shard good is nearly impossible to fully comprehend. With a successful [[/skill insight 24]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 24]] check, characters learn only that he is incredibly fond of Lyla and is giving her all of the information he's aware of. In fact, he is likely only going so far with this level of information because she is with the party.

The Shifting of the Ink

If the party asks about the @UUID[Item.r659n05meW0ZMGY9]{Coded Bandit Instructions} Sigil will nod enthusiastically while looking at it.

Ah, yes, a word, a phrase! This is shifting ink. It's often used in the smuggling circles and underworld to avoid the attention of authorities, and makes codes nearly impossible to break unless you know how to decode it - put it near a flame or say the right phrase while holding the paper. Something like that.

Decoding the Bandit's Message

To decode the message left by the bandits, characters must hold the paper in their hands and say the words "For Other Fortunes." If they do this, they receive @UUID[Item.4gnpLU3NcyXylMHB]{Decoded Bandit Instructions} in place of @UUID[Item.r659n05meW0ZMGY9]{Coded Bandit Instructions}. Mark this outcome complete in the @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.6XGCgWBOeHH6HVlT]{A Friendly Reunion} quest event.

Receiving the Text

To get the book they need about Arcturian leather working, the party must find a specfic book among the many books lying on the floor of Sigil's living room. As they search for it, Sigil will proudly remark that the books here represent his current "daily reading" and that his arcane library contains hundreds of times more tomes, scrolls, and books.

As the party searches they pick up all manner of interesting books, such as:

  • Ask Me Nicely: How to Get What You Want from Oakengarde to Oshclaw

  • Pleas and Thank Yous: Etiquette for Prisoners and Guards

  • Be Nice and Keep It Moving: Agraband Swift's Guide to Politeness

  • Handcrafts and How Do You Dos: Making Friends on the Arctus Plateau

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 17]] [[/skillCheck awareness 17]] check is able to uncover the book. The DC goes down by 1 each time this check is made.

Once they correctly identify the book, characters receive "Arcturian Leatherworking Marks: A Historical Perspective," which details a pattern in the bandits' leatherwork markings that indicates they are likely Ordani. Any character with [[/knowledge trade]] or [[/knowledge seafaring]] can narrow it down to two cities: Seawall and Ordain.

Are you a god?

Yes, yes, a Shard God to be precise, or at least that's what you all call us. I prefer Ascendant God as it's more accurate. Oh, and godhood is a misleading metric of power before you ask. A storm is powerful, but it cannot thread a needle. Incidentally, you will likely be pleased to know that you are asking an interesting question.

Don't you have a magical library?

No.

There is a long pause as he continues reading his book before twitching slightly, as if realizing he was being too blunt.

Ah! I mean, yes, but it is currently closed because I have some delicate instruments inside that I don't want disturbed. The gate there would lead you in. Please come back again later; the door will be open, I'm sure.

Why are you helping these refugees?

Because the alternative is distressing… I may not be able to help with battles, fighting, and the like. I find that kind of thing quite frightening, but allowing anyone to be extinguished by bandits or hunger is... wrong. If I have the capacity to help the people of the Plateau during this crisis, I will do so. Besides, the children brought me a flower yesterday. It had exactly five petals. Perfect symmetry.

What Sigil Knows About The Bandits

Hmm. Bandits. Outlaws, Thugs. Pirates. Such unpleasant people are the reason that so many poor people have been driven from their homes. I hear the group is called the "Otherhood" . I'm unclear how headgear is related to banditry. Aside from that, most of my information comes from the recently arrived travelers and Juro Wandren. A friend of yours Lyla, yes?

Who is Juro Wandren?

A delightful complex fellow, a bit of darkness and light all in one person. He was nice to talk to. He has been helping. Getting goods for the refugees somehow. He has mentioned this Otherhood multiple times. I suggest asking him directly what he knows — he is currently working in Nain, though he also lives in Ordain.

Troubles in Arcturel

Down and down it goes, mining for ores and pearls. Trade is down. Seventy percent reduction, painful and disruptive. No other information, I'm afraid. I would strongly recommend going yourself to see.

Bandits' Leather Markings

I think there is a book somewhere around here, perhaps on that shelf there. OH, no, over there in that pile.. or perhaps I left it outside on a bench? It's not completely up to date, but helpful, I'm sure.

The Phrase "For Other Fortunes"

"For Other Fortunes." An old pirate expression, originating in Kessia several hundred years ago. Or possibly from the city of Crown. Seems to be an expression about taking others' fortunes for your own. Seems like the kind of thing that a bandit group might be attracted to, especially if they had some pirates in their midst.

Once Sigil has answered all of the party's questions, the conversation ends.

Sigil's words trail off, staring into the space in and around you before he jumps slightly and returns to his book and starts to hum in an off-tune tone. Lyla smiles wryly in his direction, then turns toward the door.

It was so nice to see you again Sigie, I think we will leave you to it. There is much I need to take care of.

At the sound of her voice, Sigil refocuses on her. Throughout the entire conversation, Sigil has appeared distracted, with his voice being soft and distant, as if he was only giving a small fraction of his attention. But when his eyes meet Lyla's, they shine with an almost brilliant golden glow, and his expression is stern. The air in the room grows heavy, as if a great weight suddenly settles on everyone. His voice remains perfectly steady and firm.

You will endure, my dear. There is much ahead that will test you, but you are stronger than you could possibly imagine. I know the resonance of your soul better than I know my own wards. If the darkness grows too thick, I am here, and I will answer. Trust yourself and those around you who have proved their worth.

Lyla does not respond, merely nodding while her eyes shine in surprise and gratitude.

Concluding the Event

The party can remain in the lodge to rest, set up outside, or spend time speaking with the various groups at the lodge. When ready Lyla is ready to head to her next destination: Arcturel.

Lyla sighs heavily as she begins to pack up her gear for the road.

I can't get what Sigil said about Arcturel out of my head. Something's going on there and the settlement's no more than a day's ride. If we're going to help save House Cevher from whatever is happening on the Plateau, we need to start there.

Next Steps

Lyla proceeds to Arcturel. If the party goes with her, they trigger [[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel1]]. If they go elsewhere, she will travel with them as long as they don't go too far off course, but may eventually return to her original route.

If the party separates from Lyla, they can catch up with her again in Seawall in [[/eventState otherhood1Seawall]] or in Ordain at the end of the Act in [[/eventState otherhood1Ordinate]].
A Friendly Reunion.soverview: Lyla and the party arrive at Oldcraft Lodge to speak with the Shard God Sigil, her former mentor and friend, about their pursuit of whoever sent the bandits to attack Helkas. Oldcraft Lodge has become a gathering place for refugees, who can provide the party with additional information about the mounting unrest in the region.
A Friendly Reunion.sexposition:
A large sprawling campsite fills the area in front of Oldcraft Lodge, with many wagons and carts nearly weighed down by the number of items they're carrying. Around and among them, visitors of all backgrounds are loading and unloading goods, setting up tents, or going abotu their daily lives, and settling around campfires. As you get closer, a Vrjnhar woman steps forward and waves to you in greeting.

Welcome, welcome to Oldcraft Lodge. I am Svala Bronwen, daughter of Bronwar. I'm guessing by the look of you that you're less refugees in need of help and more adventurers looking for a resting place... either way, please make yourselves at home.

Lyla moves forward and smiles before bowing her head slightly.

Greetings, Svala. My name is Lyla Cevher, and I am here to speak with Sigil, I'm an old friend of his. Is he in the library or out in the living room?

Svala smiles in return and motions you forward, her posture relaxing.

Ah, of course. Welcome, Lyla! Sigil mentioned you; he's in the living room out front.
A Friendly Reunion.ssummary: We met the Shard God Sigil in the middle of a library that has become a gathering place for both scholars and refugees. While there, we got information from Oldcraft Lodge that should bring us one step closer to figuring out what is going on with these Otherhood bandits..

A Smuggler Extraordinaire.name: A Smuggler Extraordinaire
A Smuggler Extraordinaire.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social and exploration event, the party can:

  • Ask the locals about the bandits, and where to find Lyla's old friend @UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren}.

  • Talk to @UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren} on the @UUID[Scene.vistaGoldenFlats]{Vista: Golden Flats} to get information about the current situation with the bandits and their connection to the city of Seawall, as well as House Wandren's involvement in the Arcturel scheme.

  • Obtain forged documents from Juro to help them gain entry into the nearby city of Seawall.

Lyla's Mood

Before attempting to ask about Juro Wandren by talking to the local villagers, the party can stop and ask Lyla if there is anything wrong, and if the party is paying close attention to her, you can read the following:

Lyla appears visibly flustered, and her nervousness is obvious. She has her hand once more on the guard of her rapier at her side and has her mouth tightly pressed together.

Lyla's Uncertainty

The party might be curious about Lyla's uncertainty, which is clearly evident. If they wish to understand more, they can ask her directly or try to gauge her mood. When asked why she's nervous or if she's excited to see Juro Wandren again, she says the following:

I… well… Look, we haven't seen each other in a long time—years, in fact, and I'm sure he's a different person now. I remember him being vibrant and curious about the world, and he also had a mischievous streak that I always found refreshing and, honestly, very funny. I hope he's glad to see me and able to help.

If anyone in the party wishes to delve deeper, they can make a [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] check, And on success, they study Lyla for a moment, observing her mannerisms and face. It's clear that she's not exactly worried about the meeting with her old friend because she's afraid or fearful; instead, she seems to be flustered, and her cheeks have turned slightly pink.

Asking about The Locals

Nain is a very typical Arcturian village; its streets are quiet and almost tranquil, and there is a softness and a sense of relaxed atmosphere everywhere you look. However, the villagers don't seem very welcoming. None of the villagers are openly hostile, but you do get the sense that the few nearby are silently judging you.

Nearby Locals

There are several locals near the party that they can walk over and attempt to talk to. It's entirely possible that a few bad rolls will make the villagers defensive, and they will refuse to tell the party any information that will reveal where Juro is.

The first person the party can ask is Elowen. An older woman is sitting on a nearby porch, mending a thick, woolen coat. She doesn't look up at first as the party approaches, but she stops her needle mid-stitch. She looks at the party's armor, then at the weapons on their hips, her eyes narrowing with a weary sort of defiance.

Juro? We don't have many by that name here. Just folk who mind their own business.

A Character who succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 18]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 18]]check lean into their good intentions or mention helping refugees which mollifies Elowen. She'll suggest trying the Kapen street back to the main road, Juro has a little overhang there. Only one character can attempt to persuade Elowen, and any other attempt fails. If anyone tries intimidation tactics, she immediately rises and heads inside her house without another word.

The second person the party can ask is Rorphen, a burly man hauling a crate of salted fish. He drops the crate with a heavy thud as the party approaches. Rorphens voice is like grinding gravel. He wipes sweat from a scarred brow.

This isn't a town for sightseeing, and we've had enough bandits passing through lately. If you're looking for someone to rob, you’ve picked the wrong time and the wrong village.

A Character who succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 19]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 19]] check lean into their good intentions or mention helping refugees. which mollifies Rorphen. He'll suggest trying the Kapen street back to the main road, Juro has a little overhang there. Only one character can attempt to persuade Rorphen, and any other attempt fails. If anyone tries intimidation tactics, he immediately rises and heads down the wharf without looking at the party again.

Following a Lead

If the characters say the wrong thing to any of the local Nain villagers, which is very easy to do, they may be at a loss on how to proceed, but as they wait, you can read the following as a child named Merinda Chip, who had been listening to the party and Lyla nearby, very obviously begins to sneak away. She crouches low to the ground and "sneaks" around some crates near the wharf.

The party must make a successful [[/save wisdom 15]] saving throw [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check. If they have [[/knowledge crime]], the check is made with @Advantage[2]. If successful, they realize that Merinda seems to be sneaking away from them and likely attempting to warn Juro. Even in a failure, the party senses that the little girl is acting oddly, and it might be interesting to follow her.

A character can visually track Merinda with a successful [[/skill perception 12]] or [[/skill survival 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] or [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] , but must succeed on a [[/skill stealth 12]] [[/skillCheck stealth 12]] check to successfully follow her through Nain. On a failure of either check, the character loses sight of her among the crates, barrels, and houses.

If the party succeeds, they slowly follow Merinda through Nain and eventually reach a side street and an overhang where Juro has set up a few small market stalls in the shadows. Merinda then whispers to Juro for a moment before running off. Juro meanwhile doesn't seem alarmed and waits calmly for the party.

If the party completely loses track of Merinda and no one can follow her through the streets, she eventually makes her way to Juro on her own and tells him that there are people looking for him. At that point, Juro peeks out from a side street and sees Lyla, waving excitedly for her to come over.

Lyla!? Is that you! Over here!

A Talk With Juro

As you approach the tarp stretched between several posts beside one of the village buildings, you are taken aback by what appears to be a vast array of trinkets. Some items glint in the light, while others resemble exotic weapons or tools. Among the beads, charms, and necklaces, there are also several ancient relics, books, pieces of clothing, and mismatched boots. The person responsible for the collection stands with hands on hips, grinning widely so that his Wirrun features are stretched into a jubilant expression. He looks directly at Lyla with bright eyes, clearly unable to hide his excitement.

Ly! What on earth are you doing here! I thought you would be in Ordain by now!

Lyla meanwhile, seems to relax as she realizes Juro is pleased to see her and begins chatting to Juro as if the two have never been apart.

I would have been, but with all this bandit absurdity, I had to investigate myself. I think the old itch to get things done came over me again. How have you been though? You're looking well!

@Embed[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]

A Happy Reunion

Lyla and Juro start talking among themselves before introducing the party. Since Lyla is with the party, Juro is more than happy to chat with the party about any topic they want to ask about.

Lyla and the party can fill Juro in on what they have learned so far in their search for the bandits who attacked Helkas. The conversation can either be between Juro and Lyla, or led by the party, but Juro is willing to share the following. A successful [[/skill insight 18]] [[/skillCheck deception 18]] check makes it clear that Juro isn't saying everything, but he isn't willing to reveal any more of what he knows. This is not because of any malicious intent, but rather because of his own caution in saying too much.

  • The bandits, who call themselves the Otherhood, are based in Seawall.

  • The Trading Houses and Ordain itself are unpopular in Seawall. These days, Juro limits his time in Seawall as a known member of House Wandren.

  • Juro is willing to forge a letter that will help the group get into the city, but he can't help with any kind of disguise. Depending on what the party has done so far, the letter's quality will vary, as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.kNE6TGVnWWevjLe9#forging-otherhood-papers]{Forging Otherhood Papers}.

  • Juro had heard that trade with Arcturel was bad, but didn't have any details, and wasn't involved enough with House Wandren at the moment to know why their name was found on papers held by the creature in the Arcturel mine. He suggests asking Hephiss Wandren in Ordain, the leader of his house.

  • If asked about the clues that the party has found so far, Juro suggests that they all point to Seawall.

Juro's Shop

Juro would have a few items to sell, which at this time are not officially listed. His stock changes frequently, but if the party asks, he has a few select items for them to purchase.

The Otherhood Bandits

Oh, I've heard of the Otherhood, though it seems like they came out of nowhere. One day it's a rumor, then a few isolated incidents, and now it feels like it's all building up to something. I try to keep my nose down, whatever you may think of my relationship with the law…

He stops to wink at Lyla, who smiles softly.

I don't support anyone who goes around burning down farms and kicking puppies, though; that's just evil. I do know where you should go to find out more, though. Seawall. Though you may not make it past the front gate without my help.

Getting Into Seawall

The Trading Houses are currently less than welcome in Seawall, though I have no idea what it is they think we've — they've — done. Unfortunately, Ly, you scream House Cevher. Even if you changed your name, there's a chance someone might know you. I'd suggest going incognito. I'm not great with disguises, but if you need paperwork that makes you seem like you are Otherhood affilated, I can help.

Forged Papers

To be honest, I want to know more about what's going on in Seawall as much as anyone else! Plus, I know better than to get in front of Lyla Cevher when she's made up her mind to do something. All I ask is that you let me know whatever you find out. And maybe owe me a favor in the future. I will say that despite my skill, how good this will be is going to depend on materials. What do you have on hand?

Arcturel and House Wandren

As a trader of all kinds of items, I do keep tabs on what's happening in the plateau, and I'd heard there were some troubles in Arcturel, but that's all I know. I really don't see House Wandren getting involved in small local issues, but if they are, you should look into it in Ordain. Hephiss Wandren is still in charge, last I heard from the Wandrens I trade with in the city — she would know more. Though with this Otherhood everywhere, I'm sure she has her hands busy.

Juro's tone and mannerisms make it clear that he doesnt have a very high opinion of Hephiss.

Clues So Far

Everything you've found has the mark of Seawall on it. That leather marking? There's a leather worker in Seawall who uses that. And the ink that you mentioned, the shifting ink? I'm running low right now, but I get it delivered to me here via a contact in Seawall's Gray Market. I don't know if the place will have all the answers you need, but I'm sure some of them are there.

Forging Otherhood Papers

While Juro is more than willing to forge documents for Lyla and the party, he wants their help in gathering the right materials — paper, shifting ink, and knowledge of the bandits' catchphrase. The more they have, the better the forgery will be.

Juro takes a quill out from somewhere you can't quite see, as if he made it appear just by thinking about it. As he speaks, he gestures to a stack of papers on a nearby table.

A good forgery doesn't just come out of thin air. You want to start with the right materials. Ideally, we'll need some paper used by the bandits, a pot of shifting ink, and some language that sounds realistic. You got any of that?

The Proper Ink

To forge the message, Juro can supply of @UUID[Item.sWmD7INuv2mMZABt]{Shifting Ink}. Characters can provide him with the ink if they have any. If they do not have ink, Juro will grin and say he would be willing to part with some of his own in return for a little gold, or perhaps something they have found on the journey.

I know! I should be generous, but this stuff is hard to come by, I'll use my own supply for 200 gold, a pretty fair price to be honest, or perhaps you have an item you can trade for instead?

The party can hand over the gold to Juro, or they can attempt to give him a magic item they no longer need.

Characters who succeed with a [[/skill persuasion 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]]check convince Juro to take an uncommon item. Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] automatically succeed.

Characters who succeed with a [[/skill persuasion 16]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 16]]check convince Juro to take a common item. Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Scraps of Paper

Juro needs a sample of the type of paper used by the bandits to recreate it. If the party has any of the following, they can use it, but they will lose the item, which Juro uses to make new paper: @UUID[Item.TqEcWF022MWZQIIC]{Recruitment Flyer}, @UUID[Item.r659n05meW0ZMGY9]{Coded Bandit Instructions}, @UUID[Item.hFBEeNSQct3Tgkhc]{A Message To Tantrin}, or @UUID[Item.4gnpLU3NcyXylMHB]{Decoded Bandit Instructions}.

If characters don't have paper that works, or don't want to give up what they have, Juro suggests finding a recruit in Nain and taking their recruitment letter.

The villagers here have been trying to run potential bandits out of Nain, but the Otherhood still tries to sneak through. I'm sure you can find one if you look hard enough. Maybe back by the wharf where you came in. If you can find them and pick their pockets, you might find a recruitment flyer.

Characters can acquire the paper in the wharf by first identifying a potential bandit, with a [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check to spot the tattoo or leather armor of the bandit in question. Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] or [[/knowledge crime]] have @Advantage[2]. Once identified, they can:

  • Pickpocket the target with a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check. If characters weren't able to shrug off the crowd's earlier accusations, they have @Advantage[-2] on this check. On a success, characters acquire a @UUID[Item.TqEcWF022MWZQIIC]{Recruitment Flyer}. On a failure, the target spots them and calls them out, agitating the crowd and preventing a second attempt.

  • Convince the target to give them a flyer with a successful[[/skill persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]]check. On a success, characters acquire a @UUID[Item.TqEcWF022MWZQIIC]{Recruitment Flyer}. On a failure, the target is unconvinced and begins to move into the crowd.

A Catchy Phrase

If characters share the phrase"For Other Fortunes," Juro tells them that there is more to it, but adds it to the document.

For Other Fortunes, yeah. It's half of it. But it's a call and response kind of thing. I think the forgery works a lot better if you have both the call and the response. I wish I knew more, but we can get by without it. All I'm sure about is that it has something to do with hands. Keep your ears open in Seawall - if you can figure it out, you might fit in better.

Putting It All Together

The quality of Juro's forgery depends on how many items the party was able to acquire.

  • If they acquired both paper and ink, it is a pristine forgery.

  • If they acquired only one of the two, it is a quality forgery.

  • If they did not provide Juro with anything, it is a poor forgery.

Use the outcome boxes below to indicate the forgery quality.

Mayis Attunement: Pristine Forgery

If the party manages to obtain a pristine forgery from Juro, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 otherhood1SmugglerPristine]] at the conclusion of the event.

Cora Attunement: Decent Forgery

If the party manages to obtain a decent forgery from Juro, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 otherhood1SmugglerDecent]] at the conclusion of the event.

Ragen Attunement: Rudimentary Forgery

If the party manages to obtain a rudimentary forgery from Juro, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 otherhood1SmugglerRudimentary]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome pristineForgery]]

[[/outcome qualityForgery]]

[[/outcome poorForgery]]

Whatever the precise quality of the document (be it pristine, decent, or rudimentary), Juro hands over the @UUID[Item.uAc4sQKtoJbSjqfQ]{Forged Recruitment Papers}.

Juro waggles an eyebrow as he hands you the forged document. He shares a look with Lyla as he does, and his expression suggests no small measure of concern.
