It really is nice to see you again, Ly. It looks like your time away has been good for you, and you're definitely in good company. I'll be packing things up here soon. I'm needed back in Ordain. If you need any help, come and find me, and good luck in Seawall.

Lyla nods in return and smiles.

Of course, thank you so much for helping the refugees and us with supplies. You have a heart of gold under all that thievery.

Juro looks shocked for a moment, his hand flying to his chest, but he then smiles and winks at her.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

It is clear that the source of information about the Otherhood is somewhere in Seawall. Armed with the information you need, the party and Lyla head for the port city, reaching the gates in [[/eventState otherhood1Seawall]].
A Smuggler Extraordinaire.soverview: Upon reaching the settlement of Nain, Lyla and the party encounter Juro Wandren, a childhood friend of Lyla's, who has some information about the bandits.
A Smuggler Extraordinaire.sexposition:
Lyla navigates through the Nain's sleepy, strangely quiet streets, making her way past the locals who narrow thier eyes and cross their arms as you pass. Lyla stops when she reaches the riverbank wharf where a few merchants ply their wares. She scans the area, with an unsure look on her face, looking back and forth between carts and small shops.

I'm not sure where Juro would be; he's likely tucked himself away somewhere… Let's ask around to see if any locals know.
A Smuggler Extraordinaire.ssummary: We connected with Lyla's childhood friend, the smuggler Juno Wandren, who helped us figure out a way into Seawall.

Unhappy Accidents.name: Unhappy Accidents
Unhappy Accidents.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, the party attempts to determine what has been going wrong in Arcturel. Zodi Trask, the liaison to House Cevher from Arcturel, can give an overview of the issues happening in the city — contaminated drinks, mechanical failures, and travel accidents — but doesn't know how any of these issues came about. Characters can ask around to find out more details from locals. They include:

  • Rallyhome server Felisa, who complains about the contamination of the popular local brew Karal in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-bad-brew]{Investigating the Bad Brew}.

  • Expert mechanic Rennerie, who can share what she knows about a string of broken machines that have injured mineworkers in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-mechanical-breakdowns]{Investigating the Mechanical Breakdowns}.

  • Merchant Hob Karell, whose riding lizards have recently begun dropping passengers and goods, causing trade slowdowns and injuries, in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-sluggish-steeds]{Investigating the Sluggish Steeds}.

  • Local gossip Tantrin, who blames every issue happening in Arcturel on House Cevher, in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#rallyhome-rumors]{Rallyhome Rumors}

The party only needs to investigate one of these issues to be led to the next event, Unwelcome Diversions, where they can uncover direct evidence of the sabotage. Lyla splits off from the party after an initial conversation with Zodi and can be used to update the party on one or both of the investigations they did not pursue.

What's Wrong In Arcturel

Arcturel has been the victim of sabotage by a Tyraphem named Kilner, who was sent to the sinkhole city with the goal of disrupting trade and discrediting House Cevher, using his @UUID[Item.l2Oc7eBtvb9rsNus] to appear to be a friendly traveler or merchant.

All of Kilner's attempts at sabotage have had the side benefit of clearing the area around the Level 3 Mine, a mine in Lower Arcturel that Kilner is using as a home base — the nearby distillery, lizard stables, and repair shop have all been successfully taken out of commission, and the mine has been shut down. Kilner has been building a device within the abandoned mine to create and amplify ground shakes, though its purpose is unclear to the party at this time.

Entering Rallyhome

Under the cap of what might be one of the largest mushrooms to ever exist, a large seating area is filled with tables and chairs, many made of unexpected materials, like discarded pipes and interlocking pickaxes. Above, in the remaining gray petrified flesh of the mushroom cap, a colony of smaller luminescent mushrooms has taken up residence, shedding a faint glowing light on the locals eating, drinking, and sharing news below. As you enter, Lyla points across the room at a tall kiska man in work clothing sitting in front of a pile of maps and diagrams.

There's Zodi! From what I've heard, he's a real leader of the people, came up through the ranks to become the foreman and main House Cevher contact, which isn't easy, given all of our regulations about who can represent us in our mining interests.

You're welcome to come with me to meet him. Or gather information on your own — either way, I know we'll get to the bottom of what's going on.

Gamemaster's Note: Zodi's Current State

If the party has begun the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book Of Tales}, but has not yet met Zodi Trask, Amalthea has told them that he is beginning to turn to crystal. While this is true, the condition is currently in its early stages and hidden by his clothing. He will not mention it front of Lyla and shrugs off any questions about it as less important than the current situation.

If the party completed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000.JournalEntryPage.uJnjxdP2OBD4pSKa]{The Crystal Quarryman} in The Book of Tales, Zodi is either fully crystal or fully human. In either case, he greets the party warmly but focuses his attention on questions from Lyla.

A Conversation with Zodi

Though Zodi is putting a brave face on for Lyla, the settlement is obviously overwhelmed and Lyla's showing up is unexpected. He greets her hesitantly.

Lyla? Lyla Cevher? I’d heard you were off somewhere doing your own thing, but I see you’re back on the Plateau and checking in on our little settlement. I know that the last shipments have been a little behind schedule, but I’m sure we can catch up once we get a little bit of luck on our side and get the new mine open. No need to worry about anything, whatever you've heard.

Zodi claims that everything fine, but a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check reveals that he is deeply worried and needs help. With a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, he will reveal the following:

  • There have been a few small issues going on in Arcturel, which Zodi believes that people are making too much of a big deal about - a few more machines have broken down than normal, there's something wrong with Hob Karell's lizards, and the town's famous local brew, Karal, is making people sick.

  • The most recent issue is the closing of the mine on Level 3 - the ground started shaking there recently, among other strange incidents, and Zodi closed it for safety. He's trying to figure out a new location in that level of Arcturel, which has unusually rich iron deposits.

  • Individually, the issues are nothing, but there are whispers that Cevher is to blame for all of it, many of which are being spread by Tantrin, a local “reporter” who is little more than a glorified gossip. Zodi isn’t sure where Tantrin is getting his information.

  • If the party wants to learn more, they can:

    • Speak to one of his former workers, Felisa, who now works in Rallyhome as a server and whose adopted family makes the brew (@UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-poisoned-brew]{Poisoned Brew}).

    • Check in with his most-trusted repair person Rennerie in the corner of Rallyhome to figure out what's been going wrong with the machines (@UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-mechanical-breakdowns]{Mechanical Breakdowns})

    • Track down Hob Karell, who is currently drowning his sorrows, about his issues with his steeds (@UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-sluggish-steeds]{Sluggish Steeds})

    • Talk to Tantrin, whose "news of the day" appears to put the blame on the Cevhers (@UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#rallyhome-rumors]{Rallyhome Rumors})

If the party is with Lyla at the end of this conversation, she chooses to pursue one of the leads they are not following and asks them to check in with her to compare notes when they are done. If the party plans to pursue all leads, she offers to work with Zodi on trying to repair House Cevher's image and asks for them to update her when they've learned more.

We can probably get more done if we split up a bit. I want to talk to Zodi about some business details, but I'll try to follow up on one of the leads when I'm done. Let's meet back here in a few hours, hopefully swap some notes.

What's happening in Arcturel?

Honestly, it's not really worth talking about. Sounds much worse than it is. There have just been a few small issues. Tiny things really. Other than the mine on Level 3 closing, that is.

What's happening in Arcturel?Successful PersuasionSuccessful Diplomacy

Okay, maybe it's more than a couple of things. There's the people who got sick from drinking a tainted version of our most popular drink, Karal; the issues with the machines breaking down; the closing of the mine on Level 3; a few small injuries from machines breaking down. It feels like there’s something in the air. Even the lizards that folks use around here for steeds aren’t working right now. But that’s just luck for you, right? I’m sure it’ll turn around any day now.

The mine closing:

Much as folks complain about House Cevher operations, they don't give us enough credit for doing what's right. I could've kept the mine open after things started shaking down there, but instead I took precautions and shut things down. The way the wind whips around down there, feels like we might've hit some pocket of instability or weakened some part of the tunnel, but I don't know. Luckily, there's other places to dig in Arcturel, so I'm leaving it alone, but it's slowed down trade until we can find a new location.

House Cevher's connection:

It's all just rumors. Trust me, there’s nothing that the trading house has done to cause machines to break or something toxic to get into the Karal casks or lizards to stop climbing the way they should. A lot of that mess is coming from Tantrin - fancies himself a news trader, but all he really shares is gossip that he gets from who knows where.

Who to talk to for more:

If you want to know more about the Karal of it all, Felisa’s your best bet. She used to work in the iron mine on level 3, but with it closed down, she’s tending tables here. Hob’s the one to talk to about the lizards. Think he's looking for ideas on how to fix them over at the bar. As for the repairs, you'll find my name on all the repair slips, but I really reply on Rennerie over there in he corner to let me know when the machines are out of whack. Just avoid Tantrin — don't know what I ever did to him, but to hear him tell it, if you sneeze it's because House Cevher gave you a cold.

Rallyhome Rumors

In lieu of speaking to Zodi, the party can attempt to gather information on their own by keeping their collective ears to the ground. As they make their way through Rallyhome, they are greeted by Tantrin, who shares what he knows about the the settlement.

One moment, you are walking through Rallyhome alone. The next, a young man appears in front of you as if out of nowhere, a patchwork cap on his head and a proffered drink in his hands. At first glance, he appears to be little older than a teenager, awkwardly blocking your path forward, but when he speaks his voice is deep and his words pour out in a practiced flow that might make a bard jealous.

Hello, friend. It's always good to have newcomers in the area. These days, with everything House Cevher's put us through, we're lucky to get more than a merchant. But I'm sure you wouldn't want to know about our troubles. Unless, of course, friend, you want to keep yourself safe with information from reliable sources.

Tantrin's Tidbits

Tantrin is eager to talk about what he knows and will share the following:

  • The karal is not safe to drink, ever since House Cevher got mine dust inside of the distillery barrels. The Waterborne family is furious about it. Felisa Waterborne, who is currently clearing drinks, knows all about it.

  • House Cevher machines have been breaking apart and injuring people, likely because they don't put any effort towards real repairs. Rennerie, in the corner of the bar, can confirm.

  • House Cevher may have poisoned Hob's riding lizards so that they can force everyone to use the elevators and charge for them. Hob might know more.

  • It's good that the mine is shut down — if Cevher kept it open, it was likely to collapse and kill someone. It still could, given how badly it was constructed, though Zodi won't admit it.

With a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check, characters can tell that there's something Tantrin is holding back, about where he gets his information.

With a successful [[/skill intimidation 14]] or [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] or [[/skillcheck intimidation 14]] check, characters can get him to confess that he's getting all of his information from an inside source — someone who used to work in the mines. They're fairly new to town, but they know a lot about what's going on. Tantrin usually meets this source by going to the Dives and waiting for them to arrive with information - they're tall and always wear a distinctive black cloak.

The Karal

If anyone offers you a glass of karal, make sure not to take it. Somehow the Cevher mine got all their dust into the barrels, and now you get sick on so much as a sip. Sad, really - it's normally so good. Ask Felisa, over there clearing the tables. She trained as a distiller and everything.

The Faulty Machines

Hope you didn't have any trouble on the escalators coming down. Lot of machines have been breaking around here. Worst ones are those mining rigs Cevher uses. Barely bother to repair them. And I heard that when the parts get old, they take from other machines - like the elevators - to repair them. Rennerie over there in the corner says she doesn't know about it, but I'm not sure.

The Riding Lizards

Normally, I'd tell you to enjoy a trip on a riding lizard, get a close-up view of what it's like to go down into the sinkhole, but they've been falling asleep on the job and nearly killing whoever's on them in the process. I'm not sure if this is true, but I heard that Hob thinks Cevher is poisoning them so they can force everyone to the elevators and charge for them. Any way to make money from us everyday folk, I guess.

The Closed Mine

It's usually not so busy up here, but Zodi finally shut down the level 3 mine. I heard it was rocking and rolling down there, making odd sounds and everything. Probably dug in the wrong place. Cevher is always making mistakes like that.

Source of Intel

When I said I had reliable "sources" for the information? It's more like one source. But he's rock solid, somehow knows everything House Cevher is up to. All I have to do is go down in the Dives when he signals and wait for him to contact me. I don't know his name, but he's so well informed, and pretty well dressed. Always wearing a nice black cloak.

Rallyhome Rumors

If the party chooses to listen in on the conversations in Rallyhome, they overlap, making it difficult to tell where one conversation starts and another one ends, but the party can determine the following:

  • With a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check to identify who might be worth talking to about their troubles, characters spot a middle-aged human woman who is clearing drinks from the tables around Rallyhome, her arms loaded down with cups and plates. She mutters to herself as she moves from one table to the next. The party can attempt to speak with her about her problems to find out more (@UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-bad-brew]{Investigating the Bad Brew}).

  • With a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check to eavesdrop to nearby conversations, characters can tell them apart. Most are focused on the problems with Hob Karell's riding lizards, which keep passing out in the middle of crawling up the sinkhole walls. Everyone wants to get them moving again so that trade can move more easily through the city, but Hob has given up on a solution and is currently drinking his troubles away. The party can find him at the bar to start @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-sluggish-steeds]{Investigating the Sluggish Steeds}.

  • The locals are reluctant to speak directly about their problems, but with a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, characters can convince them to share that local equipment has been failing, both in the mines and around Arcturel. Rennerie, a keth woman sitting in the corner of the bar going over paperwork, might know more. The party can check in with her to begin @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#investigating-the-mechanical-breakdowns]{Investigating the Mechanical Breakdowns}.

Investigating the Bad Brew

A middle-aged woman with dusty hands passes through Rallyhome on a regular rotation, collecting glasses from tables and picking up any pieces of errant trash from the floor. Her steps are heavy against the floor and her smile does not reach her eyes. As she stomps by, you can her the distinct sound of muttering, though you can't make any specific words out other than "mine" and "level 3."

Waterborne Illnesses

If asked about her frustrations, or about the mine, Felisa takes a seat at the party’s table.

Are you sure you wanna know? I saw you walked in here with one of the Cevhers. I can tell by the way Zodi sat straight up and paid attention. I know he's the people's foreman, but no one wants to look like they're slacking off in front of the boss. Probably won't even tell her about what's going on with the Karal, but I will. You just be sure to pass it on.

Felisa is all too eager to talk about the problems with Karal, a popular and common beverage in Arcturel that is said to raise the overall wellbeing of those who drink it, and shares the following:

  • Everyone loves Karal in Arcturel, which is primarily made by the Waterborne family.

  • She suspects that the karal was intentionally poisoned and thinks that House Cevher was somehow responsible. Tantrin, at least, seemed sure of it.

  • There are still large kegs of Karal in the distillery that could be contaminated, but Sevali, leader of the Waterbornes, has locked it up while she decides what to do with it. If someone could get past her locks and get a sample, it could be used to find what really happened.

  • If asked, Felisa can read some of the shifting ink message, making out the words "drakes," "cloaked man," and "Arcturel." She notes that a merchant with a cloak came through town recently.

With a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]]check, characters know that Felisa is telling the truth, and that she is likely going to quit her job very soon. With a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check or [[/knowledge intrigue]], characters can convince her to share what she knows about the Waterborne locks - the handle to the distillery is rigged so that it shocks anyone who tries to open it. Characters have @Advantage[2] on checks and saves with the Waterborne locks.

What Karal Is

It was the Waterbornes who came up with the idea of using some of the water from deep down in the sinkhole to make a drink, and even they didn't realize how popular it would be. Until it started making people sick, anyway. And I mean really sick. Pale faces, coughing up their guts, shaking and shivering. Luckily it wore off pretty fast. Which is what made me think it was less illness and more poison. I heard someone say something from the mine could do that.

Who Is To Blame

Folks are saying that something from the closed-down mine leaked into the Karal barrels, something about House Cevher providing old rusty pipes, but if you ask me, someone working for the Cevhers poisoned the brew on purpose. They want to keep us in the mines, away from any work they can't control. No offense to your friend there, but that's what people are saying. Tantrin has a source and everything, so it's what I'm going with unless there's some proof that's wrong.

Where to Get More Information

There's still Karal in the distillery, aging in barrels, and Sevali still hasn't decided what to do with it. Does she throw it away just to make everyone feel better? Do the Waterbornes try to figure out what made everyone sick? For now, Sevali's got the whole place locked up tight. Probably hoping everyone forgets about it. Get past her locks, though, and you can test it for yourself, maybe find out the truth.

The Clues Found at Helkas

No fancy leather or phrases about fortunes here. Mostly just folks working hard. But that ink? The Waterbornes use it sometimes to protect the Karal formula, though they'd never admit it. I'm no expert, but I think I can make out a few words: drakes, cloaked man, and Arcturel. There was actually a man in a cloak here recently — a merchant — but I can't see how he would be involved in anything needing a code.

To find out more about how the Karal brew, characters can get a sample from the locked up distillery in Lower Arcturel. But first, they are approached by Lyla for an update in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#determining-next-steps]{Determining Next Steps}.

Investigating the Sluggish Steeds

The keth merchant, Hob, sits in front of Rallyhome's bar, ordering up drinks for anyone who passes by and can "put some vigor back into the hearts of my lazing lizards!" He is surrounded by eager advice givers, whose remedies range from playing fast-paced music in the lizards' stable area to sending one of the Lamplighters who keep the local Inkaro pearls glowing to commune with their spirit. He does not appeared to be cheered by their help, though it does not stop him from paying the tab.

Hob's Despair

Hob immediately offers the party a drink if they help him figure out what is wrong with his steeds, though he warns them not to try the karal, which has made several people in the area sick.

Hello there friend! You don't happen to be an expert in the lethargy of lizards, do you? I need some sort of help or Arcturel is cursed and all is truly lost! Hob, hobbled by fate! Korell corralled! I'm here for any answers, and if you figure it out, your next drink's on me.

Hob is happy to tell his story of woe, sharing the following:

  • Hob Korell has always known that there was more to life in a stable than horses, and coming to Arcturel has given him the opportunity to expand. The riding lizards, which he brought from miles and miles away, are one of his finest achievements, but now they keep falling asleep mid task.

  • Several people have almost plummeted to their deaths because the lizards have gone to sleep while in the midst of climbing up the sinkhole walls.

  • Hob has tried everything to try to get the lizards to pep up, but nothing has worked and it is stressing them out. Some have blamed House Cevher for the problem, believing that they've targeted the lizards for some reason, but Hob doesn't know and doesn't care. All he wants is for someone to check on his riding lizards and figure out what to do. He will give the party[[/award 10gp]] [[/award 1gp each]] if they can get the lizards fixed.

  • If asked about the clues that the party has, the only one he has information about is the leather pattern, from his days traveling and procuring unusual steeds — he's fairly sure it's from a port city, like Seawall or Ordain.

With a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check, characters know that Hob feels guilty and partially responsible for the state of his lizards. After a successful [[/skill intimidation 14]] or [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 14]] or [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, or if they have [[/knowledge beasts]], he will confide that he somehow misplaced some of his normal lizard lamps shortly before things started going wrong and couldn't replace a set that unexpectedly broke. He was able to get some new ones from a visiting merchant in a very dapper cloak, but worries that they aren't quite the same.

Who Hob Is

But wait, I should probably introduce myself! I'm Hob Korell, procurer of unconventional steeds. Or at least I was! And good at it too. My riding lizards have been the talk of Arcturel since I brought them here as hatchlings. They can climb in and around the sinkhole carrying goods, ferrying tourists, and bringing joy to the lives of all who lay eyes on their beautiful green fins. Or they could. Now they just sleep. Been like that for half a season!

What's Wrong with the Lizards

You might think sleeping lizards isn't a bad thing. After all, everything alive sleeps eventually. But these lazeabout laggards are falling asleep on the job! Mid-crawl! One dropped an entire haul of ore, and another one almost dropped a family on its head! I can't have that.

Fixing the Lizards

I've tried everything, but after being poked and prodded and fed this and told that, the lizards starting to get stressed out at the very sight of me! Me, their favorite person in the whole world! Maybe you could go down and see how they're doing, figure out if there's any way to fix this? I've got a stablehand down there, but she doesn't know any more than I do.

This all sounds silly to be worked up about, I know, but with all the machines breaking around here, this was one way folks knew they could move things around and now it's stopped in its tracks. Maybe it is something about the Cevher mine upsetting the balance of things in Arcturel. Or Zodi's poisoning them? That doesn't seem likely, though I do hear whispers. I don't know. I just know things need to change. Soon.

The Existing Clues From Helkas

Fancy leather with a pattern? Yeah. I've seen that before, when I was off trying to bring my lizards across the ocean, not that they seem to appreciate it now. There was a leatherworker in one of the port cities who used it, but I can't remember which one.

Hobs' Guilt (After a Successful Check)

I keep thinking it's all my fault. If I hadn't misplaced all the lamps and had to replace them — the lizards loved those lamps. Kept everything just the right temperature. I was able to get new ones from that merchant who came by a little while back in the very warm-looking cloak, but I think the lizards know the difference and it's completely thrown them off.

To find out more about what happened to Hob's Lizards (and check in on his behalf), the party will need to go to Lower Arcturel to visit his stables. But first, they are approached by Lyla for an update in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#determining-next-steps]{Determining Next Steps}.

Investigating the Mechanical Breakdowns

The keth woman sits in a corner of Rallyhome, focused on the papers in front of her, her grip on the piece of charcoal in her hand so tight that it seems like it might snap at any second. She writes notes and makes small drawings, then crosses them out, or crumples up the nearest parchment and tosses it on the table into a growing pile of papers.

Rennerie's Failings

Rennerie is trying desperately to figure out what has gone wrong with the machines she's worked on and tries to keep things brief.

If you need a repair, I'm not the person to ask right now. Everything I touch seems to fall apart. I'm surprised this chair hasn't collapsed underneath me.

She explains that she does most of the repairs for the elevators and mines 2 and 3 for House Cevher, but recently all of her repairs are coming apart.

I've been working repairs for House Cevher mines since I was old enough to pick up a wrench, and I've never had so many disasters. Maybe I'm losing my touch? Or spent too much time working on my art and not enough time staying up to speed? I did get sick from a bad batch of karal, but the problems started before then, about a season ago. If I don't figure out what's going wrong, someone is gonna get hurt and I'll be stuck making chairs and tables.

Rennerie is reluctant to share anything more. Any character with [[/knowledge crafts]] can see that the chair she is on is handcrafted from metal pieces. If characters compliment the work (either sincerely or with a successful [[/skill deception 13]] [[/skillCheck deception 13]] check), succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, or have [[/knowledge machines]], she will share the following:

  • There have been three bad accidents so far - a digger had pieces fly off of it and cut people nearby, an elevator plummeted halfway down the sinkhole before someone stopped it with magic, and a walkway nearly collapsed. She had done some sort of repair on each of them a few days before the issue, but she can find nothing wrong with the pieces.

  • Any rumors about House Cevher slacking on repairs are just that — rumors.

  • Rennerie has noticed some weakness in the metal pieces that she used after the accident, but she could swear they were fine before she used them. She'd appreciate if the party went and looked at her tools and materials to see if she'd done anything wrong.

  • Rennerie has been hearing odd metallic sounds down in the Dives — whirring and clacking. Normally she would dismiss it as the signs of work, but it has happened even when no one was in the mine, and usually just before something fell apart.

  • If asked about the clues the party has, Rennerie has never seen the ink or leather markings found at Helkas, but she does recognize the phrase "For Other Fortunes" — the merchant who sold her some of her new metal glue used the phrase. He tried to get her to say a phrase back, but she doesn't remember it other than that it involved using her hands.

What's Happening

First the digger comes apart, and pieces cut up everyone nearby, then an elevator nearly drops to the floor of the sinkhole, and then a walkway starts come apart at the hinges. And if that wasn't bad enough, I'd done repairs on each of them not long beforehand. No one blames me yet — they say the tools sent by House Cevher just aren't up to standard — but I'm sure that'll change soon enough. Plus, it doesn't explain the odd metal. Or the sounds.

The Odd Metal

I took a look at the metal bits that were left behind after each accident and the metal did seem sub-par. Chalky almost. I left it down at my shop, Wrestful Repairs, because I'm not sure what to make of it all. You're not from around here, so maybe you'll see something I missed before I have to give up on repairs altogether!

Creepy Sounds

I've been hearing things down in the Dives. Clicking. Whirring. At first I thought it was the Waterbornes, but then the distillery shut down, and then I thought maybe the mine, but I'd hear it even when I was in there doing repairs after hours. Maybe it was some kind of warning sign? Every time I'd hear it, something would break soon after.

House Cevher

Tantrin running his mouth again? He's convinced Cevher's to blame for everything, but I do good work, and when things got weird in the mine, Zodi cleared out. I don't know why he's still spreading those lies.

The Party's Clues

I don't know anything about weird ink or leather. That phrase though — for other fortunes? There was a merchant here a while back, before things started going wrong around here - sold me metal glue and a few other bits and bobs. He used that phrase. Struck me as kinda odd, especially because he kept insisting that I say something about my own hands back, like some kind of code. I don't remember anything else about him, though, or what the rest of that code was. Sorry.

To find out more about what might have caused the mechanical breakdowns, the party will need to check out the chalky metal left behind in the repair shop in Lower Arcturel. But first, they are approached by Lyla for an update in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW#determining-next-steps]{Determining Next Steps}.

Determining Next Steps

Back at Rallyhome, Lyla is eager to share her updates and to hear what the party has learned. She has either followed one of the leads that the party didn't pursue or (if the party chose to split up and pursue all three) is working with Zodi to find a way to repair House Cevher's reputation and wants an update.

Lyla's Updates

Lyla can update the party on any of the paths they did not pursue:

  • The Bad Brew: Most or all of the supply of karal in Arcturel has gotten contaminated and has been making people sick. No one knows why, and the Waterborne family has been reluctant to open the casks left in the distillery to find out how deep the problem goes. The party could try to discover the truth.

  • The Sluggish Steeds: Hob Korell wants someone to check in on his sluggish lizards — Lyla has heard that their tiredness is somehow House Cevher's fault (though no one knows why) and would like the party to figure out if there might be another cause.

  • The Mechanical Breakdowns: The recent failures of safety with equipment that is either provided by or maintained through the resources is upsetting. According to the main maintenance person, Rennerie, all protocols were followed, but the metal they used did seem a bit brittle after the accidents and there have been odd sounds coming from the area. They'd love someone to go down and see if there's something they did wrong.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party heads down to the lower level of Arcturel to follow up on the leads generated in [[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel2]]. Lyla accompanies the party throughout their time in Arcturel, even if the party decides to investigate the side quest @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3]{Glitter in the Dark}.

To trigger the next event, move the Party Token to Elevation -1, which will transition to the current location of Lower Arcturel in the Pathways section of the region map.
Unhappy Accidents.soverview: The party and Lyla Cevher make their way to Arcturel, where there have been a number of issues that are beginning to disrupt trade and lower morale.
Unhappy Accidents.sexposition:
You match pace with Lyla as she navigates through the tradeway, waving away trinkets offered by merchants. The road itself seems to be made of thick plates of banded metal, making each step ring out slightly from the impact. Above you, cloth signs on makeshift wooden poles clutter both sides. Two nearby platforms - one with gears and chains beneath it, the other floating as if on a cushion of air - have been blocked off by ropes and signs indicating maintenance or repair.

We should track down Zodi Trask — mine foreman and House Cevher liaison — to find out what's going on around here. Let's head to the local gathering spot, Rallyhome. If he isn't there, someone should know how to get hold of him.
Unhappy Accidents.ssummary: We discovered that a number of unfortunate incidents have been happening recently in Arcturel, all of which are being blamed on House Cevher. To investigate further, we will need to go further down in the Arcturel sinkhole.

Gated Community.name: Gated Community
Gated Community.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social and exploration event, the party reaches the gates of Seawall, which are well-guarded.

In this event, the party can:

  • Either talk their way past the Seawall guards or sneak past.

    • Gain a suspicion rating of 0, 1, or 2. Which affects their time in the rest of Seawall.

Either task becomes simpler if they gather resources or information from those waiting in line, use the crowd to create a distraction and divert some guards' attention, or do both. The party's choices determine whether they gain full access, limited access, or manage to sneak into the city. Refer to the outcomes section to select the correct outcome.

Talking Your Way In

Seawall is a large city, and unlike the nearby Ordain, it is well fortified with strong gates and high walls. Its walls cannot be scaled without attracting attention from the guards and other waiting travelers, and the two entrances to the city pass by guard stations. The guards are strict, questioning each traveler who seeks to enter the city, but they rotate regularly, so the party may make the attempt more than once.

As you draw closer to the front of the line, Lyla begins shifting her weight from one foot to the other, and once again her hand rests idly on her rapier's guard. She turns to whisper to you.

Listen… getting into Seawall is going to be no easy matter. The place has always been well fortified, but do you see how many travelers the guards are simply turning away? Maybe we should talk to some of them, see if they have any tips that will help us through?

Talking Your Way In

If the party decides to proceed to the front of the line, the guards question their reasons for entering Seawall.

Again, I ask, are you here to rail at fortune, or do you come to find your own?

The party can convince the guards that they should be allowed into Seawall with a successful group [[/skill persuasion 20]] or [[/skill intimidation 20]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 20]] or [[/skillCheck intimidation 20]] check (if half or more of the group succeeds, the entire group succeeds). If the party is with Lyla, and she is not in disguise, they automatically fail the check.

There's something about you, miss….what did you say your name was again? I'm sorry, but you just don't strike me as the Seawall type.

The DC of the persuasion and intimidation checks can be affected by the party's actions, dropping by 1 for meeting any of the following conditions:

  • The party has @UUID[Item.uAc4sQKtoJbSjqfQ]{Forged Recruitment Papers} from Juro Wandren.

    • If the party has a Pristine Forgery, the check to enter Seawall is also made with @Advantage[2].

    • If the party has a Rudimentary Forgery, someone in the party must succeed on a [[/skill deception 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15]] check to explain its quality. On a failure, the guards do not believe the forgery and confiscate the forged papers.

  • The guards are distracted (see "Creating a Distraction" below).

  • A member of the party is wearing an article of clothing associated with the Otherhood (see "Gathering Intel & Looking the Part" below).

  • Hiding among the various members of the crowd as they enter (see "Hiding In The Crowd" below).

  • A member of the party uses the phrase "For Other Fortunes." (see "Gathering Intel" below).

On a successful group check, the party gains full access to the city. While the party enters Seawall using this method, it doesn't mean they have passed the gates entirely unnoticed; either a guard, the people entering alongside the party, or locals inside the gates see them and start spreading the word.

If the party fails the check, they are denied access to Seawall. They may attempt the check again, but unless they convince the guard that they are newcomers to the gate (via the use of a disguise via a Disguise Kit, borrowed clothing, or a spell or magic item that changes their appearance), they roll with @Advantage[-2]. If the party succeeds on a repeat trip to the gates, they are given only limited access to the city.

Luxarum Attunement: Full Access

If the party manages to gain full access to Seawall, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 otherhood1SeawallFullAccess]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome fullAccess]]

Mayis Attunement: Limited Access

If the party tries repeatedly and eventually gains access to Seawall, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 oozeControlPoolLure]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome limitedAccess]]

Sneaking Your Way In

If the party instead attempts to sneak past the guards, they can try to sneak around the sides of the busy line and slip inside unseen. However, this does have consequences in the following events.

Sneaking Into Seawall

The party can sneak past the guards with a group [[/skill stealth 20]] [[/skillCheck stealth 20]] check (if half or more of the group succeeds, the entire group succeeds). The DC of this check can be affected by either of the following, each of which lowers the DC of the check by 2:

  • The guards are distracted (see "Creating a Distraction" below).

  • The party is hidden within a larger group of travelers (see "Hiding in the Crowd" below).

If the party fails the check, they are denied access to Seawall and may not reattempt the stealth check. They may attempt to talk their way into Seawall, but unless the guards believe they are a different party (via the use of a disguise via a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulDisguiseKi]{Disguise Kit} , borrowed clothing, or a spell or magic item that changes their appearance), they roll with @Advantage[-2].

While the party can sneak into Seawall using this method, this does not mean they have passed the gates completely unnoticed, and either a guard, the people entering alongside the party, or locals inside the gates might spot the party entering and start spreading the word.

Primordis Attunement: Sneaking In

If the party manages to successfully sneak into Sewall, each character advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 otherhood1SeawallSnuckIn]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome seawallSneak]]

Access Options

While the party might succeed on their first try without planning, they can also pause to discuss the best way to get inside. Some of the following options make both @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.ilKtljJ27OgYT3Y4#talking-your-way-in]{Talking Your Way In} and @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.ilKtljJ27OgYT3Y4#sneaking-your-way-in]{Sneaking Your Way In} easier.

Gathering Intel

The party can attempt to use the line of travelers waiting to get into Seawall as a resource that increases their chances of making it past the guards and into the city. To learn some ways for getting past the guards, the party can chat with those waiting in line.

With a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check while looking at the line of travelers, characters identify a family of four who have made their way to the front before and might have information to share about the guards.

You've seen these four before. At least once. Being turned away at the gate. That hasn't stopped them, though, as they are back in line, wearing slightly odd-fitting clothes. Maybe they know something you don't.

With a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, characters spot a confident young person who stands out as being confident about their chances of getting into the city.

Others may look nervous, shifting back and forth from one leg to another, but not the wiry human with the bow on their back and a gleam in the eye. If there's a secret to getting past the guards, it seems like they know it.

If characters attempt to ask other travelers in line about the guards, they receive no useful information.

The Family of Four

The matriarch of the family, Isei Velz, has noticed that those who are wearing leaf leather like the Otherhood does are getting through. Her family traded some of their belongings for a pair of leaf leather gloves and suggest the party do the same.

This isn't our first time near the front of the line, but we've never actually spoken to the guards. Just done a bit of observation over the last day or so. See these gloves? Leaf leather. Very pricey, really. But it's what the Otherhood wears. Every time I see someone who has gone right to the front and been let in without question, they've got on something like this. There are some folks who have it in line, if can spot them and have something to trade.

The Confident Traveler

The young traveler, Garrius, is convinced that saying "For Other Fortunes" when answering the guards will make a difference.

It's all about saying the right thing, if you know what I mean. Use the words that they use and they'll think you already belong. A whisper of "For Other Fortunes" and I'll be inside the walls. I'm sure of it.

Looking the Part

If the party has the @UUID[Item.l2Oc7eBtvb9rsNus], Lyla will request to wear it, as her face may be known by those familiar with House Cevher. If the party declines, or does not have the item, Lyla will need alternate clothes before entering the city. In addition, the party can use any clothes they procure to create a disguise of their own.

  • Stealing an Outfit: With a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]]check, the party sees clothes on a wagon whose driver isn't paying much attention to them. They can sneak up on the wagon with a successful [[/skill stealth 14]] [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] check and steal a set of clothing from the wagon with a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 14]] [[/skillCheck stealth14]]check. If they are caught stealing, they only gain limited access to Seawall, even on a success at the gates.

  • Buying an Outfit: Characters can offer to purchase a spare outfit from one of the travelers waiting in line. The going cost is 40 gp 4gp for a simple outfit and 100 gp 10gp if the outfit includes some item made with leaf leather. With a successful[[/skill persuasion 14]] or [[/skill intimidation 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] or [[/skill intimidation 14]] check, the cost drops to 30 gp 3gp and 80 gp 8gp gp. If the check succeeds by 3 or more is a critical success, it drops to 20 gp 2gp and 60 gp 6gp.

  • Convincing Someone to Give Up An Outfit: Characters can convince someone in line to give them some clothing with a [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check. If they have [[/knowledge trade]] or [[/knowledge crafts]], they can note someone who has clothes that they might be willing to part with and have @Advantage[2] on the check.

Hiding In The Crowd

The party can attempt to blend in with one of the larger groups of travelers to avoid catching the eyes of the guards completely by finding a large enough group with a successful [[/check investigation 14]][[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check and slipping into the group with a successful [[/skill stealth 14]] [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] .

Creating a Distraction

The party can attempt to create a distraction in order to sneak past the guards more readily. This could be a magical effect that would catch the guards' attention, starting a fight as noted below, or any other improvised distraction by the party.

  • Starting a Physical Fight: With a successful [[/skill investigation 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16]] check, characters can spot groups that are standing close enough together that a good shove might knock them out of alignment and cause those waiting to crash into each other. To pull off the maneuver, they must succeed on a [[/skill acrobatics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check or the ensuing tangle of carts and travelers fails to cause a chain reaction.

  • Starting an Argument: With a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, the party can spot Higel, a traveler who is not taking the wait well and could be easily drawn into a fight.

    They see all of us waiting out here, but do they care? Bad enough that bandits are driving folks out of their homes, but now everyone is acting like we don't belong? I was a mayor, I'll have you know. Of a very small village, but still. Why should I have to wait at the back of the line?

    Higel can be drawn into an argument with those around him in line with a [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check to make some loud declarations about mayors and lines that will enrage him.

Concluding the Event

Suspicion Rating

During this event, the party gains a Suspicion Rating of either 0 or 2. A higher level will limit what they can access in the following event of @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C]{Simmering Discontent}.

  • If the party succeeds the first time in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.ilKtljJ27OgYT3Y4#talking-your-way-in]{Talking Your Way In} they can enter Seawall with a Suspicion Rating of 0.

  • If the party succeeds any other time in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.ilKtljJ27OgYT3Y4#talking-your-way-in]{Talking Your Way In} they enter Seawall with a Suspicion Rating of 2.

  • If the party decides to sneak into the city instead of @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.ilKtljJ27OgYT3Y4#sneaking-your-way-in]{Sneaking Your Way In}, they enter Seawall with a Suspicion Rating of 0, they are penalized for failing checks in the following events.

Next Steps

The party enters Seawall and proceeds to gather information about what is going on with the Otherhood in [[/eventState otherhood1Simmering]].
Gated Community.soverview: The party arrives at Seawall, a fortified town controlled by the Otherhood of Fortune, and receive an unfriendly welcome.
Gated Community.sexposition:
A long winding line of travelers stands between you and the stone gate that protects Seawall. Some are refugees, carrying many of their belongings as they look for a safe place to rest.

At the end of the road, two guards scrutinize each traveler as they arrive. The Kivahr on the left has a booming voice, and the words "What is your business here in Seawall?" echo through the sea air over and over again as you come closer to the front of the line. Their companion on the right, a human of average height, seems almost diminutive in comparison, but as you near the gates, you can hear their words on the breeze.

Are you here to rail at fortune, or do you come to find your own?
Gated Community.ssummary: We became part of the long line of those waiting to get into Seawall and had to figure out a way to get past the strict guards.

Simmering Discontent.name: Simmering Discontent
Simmering Discontent.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is a social and exploration event, the party can chat among thesmevesl on the best route forwards to contiue their investigation and explore the upper section of Seawall known as Tower Crags.

In this event, the party can:

  • Find the leathermaker who made the bandits' outfits to learn more about them

  • Talk to the tattoo artist responsible for the For Other Fortunes tattoos.

  • Befriend the locals to learn about whats is happening in the city.

  • Find and listen to Sticks, the Provost of Sewall, as he is giving a speech.

During the event, the party may attract suspicion from the locals. As suspicion grows, it becomes harder to gather information, and the event may end prematurely if they are attacked by residents who want them to leave town immediately.

Suspicion in Seawall

Now that they are in Seawall, the party can follow up on some of the leads that they have gathered about the bandits, otherwise known as the Otherhood, but the party's options for following up on these leads is based on the outcome of @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.ilKtljJ27OgYT3Y4]{Gated Community}. Before moving any further into the city, Lyla stops the party and says the following:

Lyla clenches her fists as she turns to you, her face scrunched in determination, clearly intent on figuring out what is happening here.

Alright. The city is definitely different from what I remember. Not at first glance... but there's an air of fear, paranoia, and fervor here that I can't quite put my finger on. Be careful, friends; we should try not to upset the locals and see what we can uncover.

All-Access Pass

Suspicion Level 0

Parties that received full access to the city begin with a suspicion level of 0. They can explore any location in the city outside the fort, which is restricted even for locals. This includes @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#investigating-the-leathermaker]{Pejil's Custom Leathers}, the@UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#tattoo-artist-of-the-sea]{Inktop} and @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#a-rowdy-experience]{The Old Door Inn}.

Limited Access

Suspicion Level 2+

Parties that have limited access to the city and begin or gain more than 2 Suspicion Rating are limited in thier choices of locations to visit. They can only explore @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#investigating-the-leathermaker]{Pejil's Custom Leathers} and the@UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#tattoo-artist-of-the-sea]{Inktop}. If they try and access the Old Door Inn, they are laughed at and thrown out onto the street, as the locals have passed word aroudn that they are suspicous. They can attempt to enter by succeeding on a group [[/skill stealth 15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]]check (if half or more of the group attempting the check succeeds, it is a success). On failure, they are still unable to enter, and their Suspicion Rating increases by 2.

Sneaking Around

Suspicion Level 0

Parties that snuck into the city can explore any location and begin with a suspicion level of 0, but have a chance of raising local suspicion whenever they fail a check. On a failed check of any kind within this event, roll a [[/roll d4]]. On a 1, the level of suspicion on the party raises by 1.

Suspicion in Seawall

While in Seawall, characters can take actions that increase the suspicion that falls on the party, raising their suspicion level in the process.

  • With a suspicion level of 5 or more, the party is considered suspicious. All charisma and wisdom social skill checks are made with @Advantage[-2].

  • With a suspicion level of 8 or more, the party is considered unwelcome. End all party activities and begin @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#an-address-to-the-crowd]{An Address to The Crowd}.

Aura Attunement: Finding Your Own Path in Sewall

If the party manages to raise their suspicion level enough to become unwelcome in Seawall, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 bookTalesMoonChildAura]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome unwelcomeSeawall]]

Exploring Seawall

If the party doesnt have any clear direction, Lyla gives the following as possible options for investigation: checking out the shop of the leathermaker who made the bandits' clothing, finding the tattoo artist who inked the "For Other Fortunes" tattoos, and listening in to locals who may have information about what's happening in Seawall.

Visiting The Leathermaker

Lyla:

Juro Wandren mentioned a leatherworker in Seawall. Pejil. If he isn't the one who made the leaf leather armor worn by the Helkas bandits with this pattern on it, I'm sure he knows the identity of the crafter who did. His shop's right by the Ancient Tower, if we want to investigate further.

The party can head directly to his shop for @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#investigating-the-leathermaker]{Investigating the Leathermaker}.

Finding The Tattoo Artist

Lyla:

Keep an eye out for those For Other Fortune tattoos. If we can figure out who made them, we might be able to figure out exactly how to use that phrase to get the rest of the information that we need. I'm sure someone around here knows who they are.

Characters can ask anyone around them where to find the tattoo artist, but will immediately be asked why they wish to know. With a successful [[/skill deception 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15]] check, they successfully lie about their reasons for wanting to find the tattoo artist. On a failure, the local refuses to tell them and suspicion of the party goes up by 1. Characters may also look around Seawall for the symbol used on the tattoo — with a successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck perception 15]] check, they spot a sign on a signpost with similar art work that points them to the tattoo artist Lejiki.

Once the party has found Lejiki's location, they can proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#tattoo-artist-of-the-sea]{Tattoo Artist of The Sea}.

Listening to the Locals

Lyla:

The last time I was here, my father warned me about visiting a particular place—the Old Door Inn, hidden under the shadow of the Ancient Tower in its basement, if the rumors are to be believed. If we're looking for information from some of the most undesirable people in the city, that might be a good place to start.

If the party has full access to Seawall, or snuck into the city, they can proceed directly to the Old Door Inn for @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#a-rowdy-experience]{A Rowdy Experience}.

Investigating the Leathermaker

The leatherworking shop is tucked into an alley next to the Ancient Tower. It appears small and unassuming, easily overlooked by those not specifically searching for it. Inside, a bald man with a long gray beard works diligently in a room filled with leather samples. He is hammering a design into a piece of leather stretched on a worktable with one hand, while sketching in a small design book with the other. Throughout, he hums a surprisingly complex tune casually.

Welcome to Pejil's Custom Leathers. I'm Pejil. I'm a bit swamped, but let me know if there's anything you need.

Talking to the Leathermaker

Pejil is focused on the task at hand and not much of one for idle conversation, answering any questions with a short response and then returning to his humming. With a successful [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check, characters can tell that Pejil is stressed. He has a lot of work to do and not very much time — his only real outlet of calm is his singing.

  • With a successful [[/skill performance 15]] [[/skillCheck performance 15]] check, characters can harmonize with the current tune that Pejil is singing, which brings a smile to his face and makes him pause long enough to speak to the party.

  • With a successful [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]]check, characters can identify the song he is humming, "By the Banks of the Elenain," and comment on it. He then pauses and will speak to the party.

If the party talks to Pejil, he will share any of the following:

  • He has been working non-stop creating armor for the locals. It isn't the fine craft work he thought he'd be doing, but he wants to make sure those he knows and loves are safe. He's a bit anxious about the speech that local leader Sticks will give later today, but always feels reassured after listening to "The Captain."

  • He doesn't know anything about a grand plan for the Otherhood, but he's familiar with the term as most of his clients recently call themselves the "Otherhood Crew". Seawall is a great place to live, though, and he's paid a fair wage, so he will continue doing what he's doing without asking too many questions.

  • He hasn't really had a chance to look back at his head count and number of outfits ordered, though he keeps it in his record book, but the number has grown greatly over the last season or so. Recruiting must be up.

Snooping in the Shop

A number of fine leather garments have been laid out across the shop.

  • With a successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check, characters can see the pattern that Pejil is currently hammering into the leather from across the shop.

    • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]], or who make a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] or [[/skillCheck arcana 15]]check, can confirm that it is the same pattern as the one worn by the bandits.

The small book that Pejil is writing in appears to contain records and notes about whatever project he is currently working on, though it is difficult to tell from a distance.

  • Characters can examine the book more closely by getting close to Pejil with a successful [[/skill stealth 15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check. While within range of him, characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check can see that the number of pieces of armor needed appears to be growing exponentially.

    If the stealth check fails, characters must succeed on a [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check to convince Pejil they weren't spying, or they are kicked out of the shop and suspicion level of the party increases by 1.

  • Characters can take the book with a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check, giving them the opportunity to examine it more directly. They learn that the number of Otherhood recruited is indeed growing exponentially. A note in the book also reads "Let me know if you need any extra hands in here again - I know this is a lot of work for one person and I should have some more qualified bodies soon enough. - Sticks"

    If a character fails the check, they must succeed on a [[/skill deception 16]] [[/skillCheck deception 16]] check to explain what they were doing, or they are kicked out of the shop and the suspicion level of the party increases by 1.

Tattoo Artist of The Sea

A signpost for a tattoo shop called the Sea Liner directs you to the edge of the plaza overlooking the docks below. Inside, a small Keth is drawing the city skyline with a variety of colorful inks from his pots, including a stunning golden ink that shimmeringly shifts on the canvas.

Sorry, no tattoos today. I've been spending so much time inking others that I've forgotten what it means to ink for myself. Today I just want to relax and enjoy the view.

Lejiki has an array of inks that he is currently working with, including 3 different gold shades. They may be shifting ink, though it would require some investigation to confirm.

The Artist At Rest

If characters speak to Lejiki, they can ask him about his art, though he is reluctant to talk while he is working. For each question asked, characters will need to succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]]check. If the check is failed twice during the conversation, Lejiki stops speaking altogether and asks the party to leave the shop. The suspicion level of the party increases by 1. While speaking to the party, Lejiki can reveal the following:

  • He prefers art to tattoo work, especially because he has been asked to create the same tattoo over and over.

  • The tattoo he has been asked to repeat is ropes around arms, wrists, and legs, or the ancient tower itself, sometimes with the words "For Other Fortunes" under it. This is a phrase he hears often in Seawall, along with its customary reply, which he is not supposed to repeat. If characters a have succeeded on the check by 3 or more have critically succeeded , he will reveal the response phrase, "With Our Own Two Hands."

  • The ink he uses in his tattoos is a particularly beautiful shade of gold that is really meant for messages, but he can't get enough of. He's convinced Sticks to let him have enough to do his art. If the party is familiar with Shifting Ink or a character succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check, they can confirm that he is using Shifting Ink for the artwork.

A Rowdy Experience

You follow the sound of laughter and merrymaking to The Old Door Inn. The entrance appears to be a large open double door leading into a dark room directly beneath the Ancient Tower. It seems to be a very busy location, as Seawall locals are constantly entering and exiting, with loud laughter, the clanking and clashing of metal mugs or glasses heard everywhere, and a raucous song playing at a ridiculous volume, desperately trying to be heard above the noise. Three burly bouncers stand at the doorway, and although they don't seem to be stopping anyone, they are taking their jobs seriously, scanning people's faces and clothes as they pass.

An Unruly Crew

The party may not be able to enter the Old Door Inn, depending on thier Suspicion Rating. (see "@UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.QWhkNXVOw6CAox1C#suspicion-in-seawall]{Suspicion in Seawall}" above).

Once they are inside, the Inn is a cacopony of noise, with locals dancing on tables and the entire cavnerous room is teeming with people. The locals at the Old Door Inn are talking loudly about all manner of topoic, some about legens and myths, or the seasons changing or swapping tales about their various exploits. As the party tries to situate themselves they are best by a loud group of locals who shout at them to share soem stories.

You there… hic.. What about you lot! What merry tale can you share with me lads!

The party is unfortunately trapped as the gang of locals surrounds them on all sides. With a successful [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check or [[/knowledge intrigue]], characters have a sense of the kind of story that will excite the group and have @Advantage[2] on the checks that follow.

  • With a successful [[/skill performance 15]] [[/skillCheck performance 15]] check, characters can spin a story that is so exciting that no one pays attention to the particulars.

  • With a successful [[/skill deception 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15]] check, characters can lie about their exploits on the Arctus Plateau. Any character with [[/knowledge crime]] has @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • With a successful [[/check persuasion 15]][[/skill persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check, characters can get out of telling a story by convincing someone else to tell the tale instead.

If characters successfully tell the tale, they are welcomed by the group around them, who reveal the latest passcode to the phrase For Other Fortunes: With Our Own Two Hands.

Oi, you lot are alright in my book! HAH! I almost missed my last mission because of that blasted ink shifting this way and that. I know Sticks wants everyone to be cautious, but it just makes life so damn difficult!

If characters fail the check, the locals are unimpressed by the story and believe that the party is lying to them. The party's Suspicion Rating increases by 3.

An Address to The Crowd

Once the party has collected all available information or if they have become Unwelcome in Seawall, a loud bell rings throughout the city.

Without warning, a loud clanging can be heard coming from the Ancient Tower above. The sound reverberates throughout your body, and you feel a flash of pain in your ears. Then it strikes again, and once more. On the third strike, you hear loud clapping and cheering as the sounds of people moving toward the Ancient Tower and the plaza in front of it can be heard.

As you follow the crowd, you find yourself looking up at the steps of the Tower, where a tall, broad-shouldered Kiska dressed in exotic furs steps out and spreads his arms wide as a greeting. Based on the murmuring you hear from the crowd, it’s clear this must be Sticks, the Provost of Seawall.

@Embed[Actor.z1Ttp0q6CAtjDphl]

With a booming voice that conveys authority but still feels as if he's speaking to each person in the crowd individually and personally, Sticks addresses the crowd.

HAHA! Thank you all, loyal friends! How kind you all are! I wish that I had better news to report, but seeing your faces in the crowd makes my heart lighter and my burden lighter.

As you know, our attempts to make our living on Plateay, we call home, have remained stalled by the refusal of the listless Trading Houses and the weak wills of the Ordinate in Ordain. But I'm pleased to report, thanks to your bravery, we now know the truth: House Cevher has been creating the earthquakes that hurt our cities and crops, on purpose, simply to enrich their own pockets!

Loud booes and jeers break out among the crowd, swelling in fury, before Sticks raises his hands, urging for calm.

Yes, unfortunately, it is true. I understand it’s shocking, but I personally saw the evidence in documents stored deep inside the tower that we will soon reveal to the world! However, don’t worry — we will find a way to fight back and reclaim the Plateau from these villains soon. Though Other Fortunes may be their tool, we will take it back ourselves!

A rousing call of "For Other Fortunes" and "With Our Own Two Hands" breaks out in the crowd, and for a moment, Lyla simply stares her mouth slightly open in disbelief. before squaring her shoulders, whispering in your direction.

I may have been gone a few years, but there is no chance that House Cevher is doing any of that. And from what he's saying, he's behind everything the bandits have done in the Arctus Plateau. He might even be the leader of the Otherhood itself. Whatever "proof" he has? We find it and expose it.

As you whisper quietly among yourselves, you notice some locals nearby pointing in your direction and pushing their way through the crowd. Several armed and armored figures start to converge on you. With a yelp, Lyla grabs your arm and hisses out a warning.

Looks like it's time to make ourselves scarce! Follow me!

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party follows Lyla as she leads them down the nearby stone stairways to Stone Haven. This is one move on the region map to the lower area of Seawall and the next event in the quest, [[/eventState otherhood1Flare]].
Simmering Discontent.soverview: The party enters Seawall and investigates the political situation, only to discover the city is fully under the control of the Otherhood and their leader Sticks.
Simmering Discontent.sexposition: Seawall's gates lead into a spacious plaza surrounded by numerous side streets and shops. The towering ancient Aedir, which serves as a garrison for the city guard, dominates the skyline, while the lower parts of Seawall extend beneath it. An lively rhythm permeates the area, composed of merchants' overlapping calls, footsteps, carts on the stone streets, and seabirds' cries from the docks below the cliffs, echoing in the distance.
Simmering Discontent.ssummary: We have gained more insight into Seawall's situation. It is evident that Sticks, the leader of Seawall, is antagonistic toward House Cevher and probably responsible for much of the Otherhood's activities on the Arctus Plateau. He asserts that he has proof that House Cevher intentionally causes earthquakes, but this evidence is kept hidden in the Ancient Tower in Seawall.

Warning Shout.name: Warning Shout
Warning Shout.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social and exploration event, the party is confronted by Otherhood members who have become aware of their presence in the city. Lyla is eager to avoid combat, instead urging the party to stay hidden as long as possible, and if that fails, they need to find a ship to flee the city.

In this event, the party can:

  • Evade Otherhood members as they attempt to track down and capture the party.

  • If ambushed, the party can knock out rather than kill Otherhood members to keep things quiet

  • Meet Salara, the Queen of Scales, a local legend that Lyla is familiar with.

As they try to find a way out of the city, this event triggers a frantic attempt to escape Seawall before getting captured.

Hunted & Harried

The party races through Seawall, following Lyla as she attempts to find a way down to the docks.

Lyla hurries alongside, stopping every few minutes to peer down side streets, trying to remember the way to the nearby docks.

It's been years since I was last in the city, and back then, I had my father to guide me. We used to pass through this area on our way to Arcturel or when I visited Sigil at his lodge. The place has become even more abandoned and derelict than it was before. No wonder the people here follow someone like Sticks; I imagine he's been promising them he can fix all of this.

Ambushed Among the Debris

As the party makes its way down to the docks, they may be assaulted by Otherhood groups that have been sent to track them down and capture them.

Improvised Attack

As the party races through the crumbling slums of Stone Haven, they must roll a group [[/skill stealth 15]] [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] check (if half or more of the group attempting the check succeeds, it is a success). On failure, they are spotted by the Otherhood, who jump them from nearby side streets. Lyla holds up her hands as the Otherhood bursts into the group and urgently half-whispers:

Wait! Don't kill them! It will draw more attention, and they will use it to further their cause!

Only three Otherhood members jump the party, and they can be dealt with in any non-violent manner the party can think of, including some of these options below.

  • Tripping the bandits using nearby ropes or long strands of rotting cloth with a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck investigation 14]] check to determine the proper place to put the rope and successful [[/skill athletics 14 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check to hold onto the rope as the Otherhood pulls against it, taggling them in the debris nearby.

  • Throwing a tarp, a larger piece of rotten cloth, or other kinds of debris over the Otherhood with a successful [[/skill athletics 15]] [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] check, causing the bandits to tumble and fall to the ground.

  • Hit them on the head with a piece of debris nearby, like some rocks, sagging wooden beams, or planks, or some actual rubbish with a successful [[/check dexterity 15]] for accuracy and [[/check strength 15]] for strength [[/skillCheck athletics 15]].

  • Make any additional attempts that they come up with on their own at the GM's discretion (any associated checks should be DC 14 or DC 15).

A Cowards Path

While it is not recommended, if the party chooses to ignore Lyla's warning and attack the Otherhood directly, they may do so, but things likely won't go as planned since none of the Otherhood are eager to fight head-on. You can describe a party member successfully landing a hit on any of the Otherhood; but as soon as this happen all three immediately use their actions to flee, crying out as they go.

With the Otherhood either restrained nearby or running off, Lyla continues to urge the party forward.

I'm sure reinforcements are on the way! You saw the size of that crowd with Sticks. We can't take on the entire city. We've got to get out of here on a ship before we're completely surrounded!

The Queen of Seawall

Before the party can make it to the docks they run across none other than Salara, the Queen of Sclaes, a legendary local figure that Lyla remembers from her visits to Seawall years ago.

Rounding a corner, you spot a large building nearby among the crumbling houses. Just beyond it are the docks themselves, but before you can move any further, a tall figure emerges from the double doors. She seems to be fixating on you intently, and with a flick of her wrist, she beckons you over, calling out with a commanding tone.

Over here, please!

Beside you, Lyla blinks in shock before muttering in disbelief.

Oh, Screaming Sockets.. I don't believe it… I think that's the Queen of Seawall…

With a quick shake of her head, she rushes over to the building, beckoning you to follow.

@Embed[Actor.K9E6i8i8bO3dViwg]

As you enter the building, the interior is not only well-maintained but also pristine. Silks, large soft cushions, delicate treasures, and various trinkets seem to shimmer from every corner. Salara herself glides over to a soft, luxurious-looking couch and sits down, her gaze calm and steady, accompanied by a slight smile on her face.

Well, well, Lyla Cehver, the talk of the town. It's been so long, my dear.

The Queen of Scales.

Lyla begins to talk with Salara. She is friendly but slightly cautious, keeping her hand near her rapier as she converses with the commanding woman before her. She briefly explains her purpose for coming—identifying the bandits who attacked Helkas—and mentions that they now believe Seawall, along with the newly acquired information about Sticks and the Otherhood, was likely responsible. Additionally, Lyla shares her shock and confusion over Sticks blaming House Cevher for the earthquake twenty years ago, which feels like a distant memory to her.

Salara's light smile doesn't leave her face, and her eyes are glittering with intensity. Once Lyla is finished, she speaks slowly, each word soft and smooth.

I see. Well, my dear Lyla, I imagine you will need to get back to Ordain as quickly as possible. I will, of course, offer my help. And no, before you ask, I don't want any coins; I think I'd rather have a favour from you. Agreed?

Lyla crosses her arms and sighs quietly before nodding her head.

The conversations between Lyla and Salara end, and instead, Salara turns to her, eyes burning with curiosity. The following information and the questions and answer blocks can be used for Salara to answer questions from the party. Salara knows the following information in general.

  • Salara is a broker, merchant, and accountant. She is also known for offering bounties on disreputable beings, malicious monsters, or for tracking down missing persons or items. In reality, she might be one of the most well-informed and unscrupulous individuals you'll encounter.

  • She does "work" for sticks and the Otherhood, or rather their relationship is one of mutual benefit. Salara has many friends and a great deal of influence n Seawall and Sticks is happy for her to continue her own operations. In return Salara gives Sticks and the Otherhood information, thoug she slyly admits that doesn't always give them accurate information.

  • Salara is helping Lyla because of her father, Ralton Cevher, who Salara once worked for and respected. In fact Salara and Lyla know each other but the nature of that relationship seems to be somewhat secret, or at least neither seems willing to elaborate further.

  • She knows of a ship that is about to depart the docks and she urges Lyla to get on it, before she is captured by the Otherhood.

  • She is very interesed in the aprty and seems to make a visual note of the way they dress and hold themselves. She makes a point of asking them very directly that should they require work in the future she has several lucrative jobs and contracts they might be interested in.

Salara is clearly a powerful figure, and Lyla seems to know more about her than she's willing to reveal at this time. If anyone in the party tries to talk with her and learn more about her state of mind, they may roll a [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check. Characters learn that she is extremely calculating and very difficult to read. She could be leading them into a trap or genuinely trying to help, but it is almost impossible to figure out.

Who are you?

Salara slowly blinks her slitted eyes, her smile widening.

I assure you, no one of any consequence. I try to stay informed about what’s happening in the Arctus Plateau and have several contacts across the region.
