Mainly, here in Seawall, I am a merchant and an accountant, offering my services to any businessman or woman who needs help balancing the books, so to speak.

She pauses, bringing her hands together to interlink her long fingers in front of her.

I also provide contracts based on the information I receive or from my contacts, for the adventuring type — various tasks, missions, and bounties that come my way. All extremely dangerous, but also very lucrative at the same time…

Do you work for the Otherhood/Sticks?

Yes, of course. At least Sticks likes to think so, and I oblige him. He is extremely vicious when crossed, but he knows I have my own influence. It's better for us to work together here in Seawall. I don't get in his way, and he doesn't interfere with me; plus, he pays handsomely for information.

Her slight smile tightens.

Though just between us, I don't approve of his Otherhood all that much, and all this chaos is bad for business. I sometimes give him information that isn't entirely… accurate.

How do you know Lyla?

Oh, her poor father was such a dear. I once worked for him, when we were both much younger, of course. I was sorry to hear of his death. Ive known Lyla since she was a baby, though it's been many years since we've had the chance to… reconnect.

Contracts and Bounties?

Straight to the heart, something I find most enjoyable! While I offer my services to ships, captains, and merchants, I collect information more than I am interested in coins and accumulating wealth. To that end, I am often approached by individuals who require my help in facilitating solutions.

That's where your kind come into the equation. Avoiding types, usually members of the Anachraenum, looking to make some extra coin, etc. If you're interested in what kind of contracts and bounties I have to offer, we should talk privately another time.

With that, she slowly and very obviously winks.

How do we get out of here?

One of my contacts is about to set sail, or rather, he is attempting to. His ship, the brigantine trader Flywind, is currently a bit stuck because of delays. The Otherhood keeps postponing payment. However, the captain, who is an old friend of mine, can likely be convinced to accompany you just to free his ship.

As the conversation with Salara winds down, read the following.

So, my dear, it seems our brief reunion is at an end. They are still hunting you outside, and you have some distance to travel before you can catch the ship. Remember, it's the small brigantine, with a captain dressed in a long black cloak.

Oh, and your wonderful bodyguards are welcome to return anytime. I suspect the Otherhood is more after Lyla than you right now, so you should be able to go back to the city. Just be cautious and avoid announcing yourselves.

She then reaches inside her long coat and pulls out a small, ancient-looking black coin.

If you do have any trouble, show this to anyone in Seawall, and they will leave you alone. Now, off you go, time is ticking after all!

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party needs to head to Gray Harbour to find the ship Salara was talking about. The next event @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.0mk0tXazHpTyU6x1]{Dash Away All} has the party desperately trying to outrun a whole host of the Otherhood, and they need to move fast!
Warning Shout.soverview: The party and Lyla rush down into the Stone Haven, trying to throw off pursuit by members of the Otherhood who have discovered her identity. They are ambushed but quickly manage to throw off pursuit thanks to the unlikely aid of a local legend.
Warning Shout.sexposition: As you rush through the crowded streets of Stone Haven in the lower part of Seawall, distant shouts and the ringing of bells can be heard in the distance. As you pass the jam-packed houses on either side, it's clear that the area is practically a slum with rotting wood, crumbling stonework, and an atmosphere of decay lingering around every corner.
Warning Shout.ssummary: We were chased through the streets of Stone Haven in Seawall by the Otherhood before we came across Salara, the Queen of Scales. She told us about a nearby ship just about to depart, which we could use to leave the city and make our way to Ordain.

Fallen House.name: Fallen House
Fallen House.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event occurs on a Vista scene depicting the Ordinate. The party either arrives with or meets up with Lyla, who discovers that the situation in Ordain for House Cevher has gone from bad to worse.

At this event, the party can:

  • Ask nearby officials about what's happening, gaining insight into the proceedings happening ahead.

  • Meet important figures in the city of Ordain, including every member of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate}.

  • Discover that @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher's} seat on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordainte} held by Ralton Cevher has been stripped away from Lyla, and House Cevher is under investigation for the major earthquake that hit the Arctus Plateau twenty years ago.

  • Receive a reward for their efforts from Lyla.

Arriving at the Ordinate

Depending on the party's choices, they may have arrived at the Ordinate on their own or with Lyla.

Music: Lyla's Theme

When the party reunites with Lyla, play [[/soundscape music lylaTheme lylaTheme]]

If the party arrives with Lyla:

The clerks and officials rushing through the Ordinate don't pay you or Lyla any mind, but several members of the Trading Houses and Hallows glance at Lyla with their eyes widening in recognition. They then give Lyla a wide berth, going out of their way to avoid eye contact. One word among the murmured oddities is repeated over and over in whispers as people step out of Lyla's path: "A full session." Something is happening within the Council Atrium. Soon.

As you make your way onwards, Lyla is quiet, her eyes are wide, speaking softly only to say:

Something is terribly wrong; everyone is treating me like some kind of ghost. Half of me wants to turn around and run. I'm glad you're here with me.

If the party arrives alone/without Lyla:

No sooner have you stepped a few feet onto the steps of the Ordinate than a cracking voice can be heard behind you as someone says, "You're here?. You turn, and you see Lyla Cevher staring at you with wide eyes.

If you came for me, thank you. I'm not sure what is going on, but something is terribly wrong; everyone is treating me like some kind of ghost. Half of me wants to turn around and run. No one will speak with me — about the bandits, about Arcturel, about anything — and I can't reach anyone in my family. There's been talk of a main session, and I need to take my seat on the Ordinate Council. Will you.. accompany me inside?

Music: Default

Once the party has finished this dialogue with Lyla, return to the default music: [[/soundscape music reset]].

An Uncoming Storm

If the party wants to stop for a moment to question some of the people around them, they can ask Lyla to wait while they quickly try to figure out what is happening.

Furtive Rumors

The party can attempt to pull aside a clerk, scribe, or a low-ranking member of one of the other Trading Houses, or someone representing the Hallows or a Cindaric Sage. They will not be pleased at first, but any Characters who have [[/skill insight 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill insight 13]] check [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15 passive]] are able to calm them long enough to ask them what's going on.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]], or [[/knowledge politics]] will automactically be able to see that the people rushing towards the building are as confused as you are about whats going on but it seems that this "Full Session" everyone is whispering about means that the Atrium is filled with over a thousand people and a major surpise announcemnt is about to happen.

A successful [[/skill intimidation 18]] or [[/skill persuasion 16]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 18]] or [[/skillCheck diplomacy 16]] check reveals that something major was uncovered recently about the origins and culprit of the massive earthquake that ripped across the Arctus Plateau twenty years ago.

The Main Council Atrium

As the party makes their way inside the massive Council Atrium, you push past the crowds gathered and make your way towards the central dias where the Ordinate Council sits in session.

Load the Ordinate Atrium Vista and then read the following:

The large chamber is filled with people, with hundreds congregating on the main floor around the dais and more in the alcoves above. Members of the Veiled Chain, dressed in their rarely seen distinctive black leathers and attire, are maintaining a barrier between the crowd and the council members sitting at the curved table at the far end of the dais.

Lyla attempts to sit in the empty seat at the far end of the table, but the Veiled Chain members block her. She attempts to speak, but a loud clang of a staff striking the flagstones echoes through the chamber, silencing all the murmuring voices and conversations.

SILENCE.

The speaker, a member of the Ordinate, stands holding a long, ornate staff and dressed in long white and gold robes, while all other members remain seated.

There has been much discussion and deliberation about the topic we are about to address today. I thank everyone here for their patience. The issue today concerns the devastating earthquake that occurred twenty years ago and that I'm sure everyone here was affected by. For many years, we had assumed the earthquake was a natural, unavoidable phenomenon, and no one person or group was responsible.

With great regret, I must inform the city that the Council has recently learned that this is not true.

Murmurs and whispers spread among the people gathered around the chamber, and a few loud gasps can be heard echoing throughout, before the speaker slams her staff onto the stone once more.

SILENCE… I will have order!

She pauses as her firm voice reverberates around the now silent room once again.

Due to the nature of our discovery, I regret to inform you that there is a change in the Ordinate Council. By unanimous vote, House Cevher has been removed from its position and is under formal investigation for its egregious actions that have endangered our great city. While the investigation is underway, the House's funds will be seized and held by the Ordinate, and all members of House Cevher with authority will be questioned to determine their culpability in a number of egregious actions.

Suddenly, Lyla's voice rings out in response.

What are you talking about!? Are you claiming House Cevher is responsible for the earthquake twenty years ago? That's ridiculous! Where's your proof that our House has done anything wrong? I am Lyla Cevher, and I demand some answers!

A wave of collective gasps and shock seems to push back the crowd as people step away from you and Lyla. The woman in gold and white only turns her head slightly toward Lyla and then signals with her free hand to one of the Veiled Chain members. He quickly walks forward and hands Lyla a sealed letter.

Lyla shakes her head desperately, attempting to remain standing as she rips open the seal and quickly reads the letter. After only a moment, she gasps, dropping it to the ground. And the Ordinate speaker speaks in a ringing voice once again.

You ask for proof? You already have it! Our city is peaceful, yet your uncle, Darius Cevher, has been working with dark forces to bring about our ruin. He appears to have been betrayed and murdered for his foolishness, likely by the same corrupt forces he was trying to summon into our city! And your brother is missing. Could he be the murderer? Or just another victim of your family's vices? What do you say to that?

But Lyla has nothing to say. The personal shock is too overwhelming for her as she gazes dimly at the letter on the floor. Though she nearly crumples with it for a moment, she steadies herself—as if she has steel in her spine—and, holding her head high, with tears streaming down her cheeks, she speaks to the gathered people and the council.

I say that it is time for me to mourn, not answer questions.

With that, Lyla storms from the chamber.

A Dark Place

The party can stay in the chamber, but doing so only reveals that the council is leaving and the crowd seems to be melting away. Several clerks are tripping over themselves to head towards the antechambers with notes, and several people can be seen running for the doors to spread the news.

The party can follow Lyla to the steps of the Ordinate where she stands with a breeze that has whipped up her hair, and she is wiping her tears from her face.

I'm afraid that was not what I expected at all. I suppose the plots against my house are not just bandits attacking our mines.

Reading Lyla

A successful [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skill diplomacy 12]]check sees clearly that Lyla is deeply hurt and on the verge of breaking down, but she is holding it together.

Thank you for your help. I need to take a breather. I will fight this and clear my house's name, but I need to find my brother and figure out what's going on. I'll return to my office for the time being, but I suspect I'll need your help in the days and weeks to come.

Can we do anything to help?

Lyla doesnt smile, and tears well up in the corners of her eyes.

Probably, yeah. I need to try to take a breath, so please, I need some space. I'll reach out soon, and I would be glad to have your help.

What about our compensation?

Oh, of course, give me a moment. I have some with me right now.

If the party achieved [[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel2]] they receive a [[/award 100gp]] [[/award 10gp]].

If the party achieved [[/eventState otherhood1Depths]] they receive a[[/award 250gp]] [[/award 25gp]].

Lyla remains on the Ordanite step after you finish speaking, as people keep rushing out of the building. They avoid her as if she were cursed or ill, some sneering or giving her angry looks.

I will head back to Quarry Run to think. My house has, or rather had, some issues, so I'll try to reorient myself. Thank you for all you've done for me.

With that, she slowly walks away and disappears into the crowd after a few moments.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Subsequent Quests

This event concludes the "An Old Friend" quest, but Lyla's journey will continue during Chapter 3 with the @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1]{Disgraced House} quest.
Fallen House.soverview: As the party reaches the Ordinate, the seat of power in Ordain, they discover the Ordinate Council in chaos as scandalous accusations are made against House Cevher, and Lyla narrowly avoids arrest by members of the Veiled Chain.
Fallen House.sexposition: The grand government building of the Ordinate is bustling with activity as clerks, officials, and scribes actively rush about, some literally running into the building, while many carry stacks of papers and books with odd scraps falling unnoticed onto the floor. No one seems to linger, and various members of the Trading Houses, Hallows, and a few Cindaric Sages are quickly walking toward the public Council Atrium. Meanwhile, an odd murmur of hushed voices, tinged with fear and surprise, spreads among the figures.
Fallen House.ssummary: Lyla was devastated by the news that her uncle has been murdered, especially coming on the heels of House Cevher being publicly removed from the Ordinate.

Strange Depths.name: Strange Depths
Strange Depths.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this combat event, the party continues their attempt to escape Seawall and are forced to defend themselves against an unleashed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan} that is being controlled by the Otherhood.

During this event, the party will

  • Experience ocean combat and repair their commandeered ship as they flee.

  • Evade the pursuing @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.OPfBWA2N4EY974Wi]{Leviathan} Jerracksis and fight it off at it attack their ship

  • Learn more about Leviathans and discuss the impact of thier investigation in Seawall.

Leviathan Attack

Work in Progress! This event uses the @UUID[Scene.emberOcean000000]{Ocean} scene. This is temporary. In later updates, the event will feature a full Leviathan combat scene. For the time being, this event can be run on the region map.

As the party flees the docks of Seawall, they are quickly overtaken by the Leviathan Jerracksis unleashed by Sticks. Jerracksis, a youthful, serpent-like Leviathan, is mostly aquatic but is an extremely fast and lethal creature, not to mention larger in size than the ship the party is on. Sticks is manipulating it using a strange magic, leading the Otherhood members to believe he possesses god-like powers, and one of the main reasons they follow him without question.

As soon as the party takes a breath, read the following:

The shouts of the Otherhood members echo behind you as your ship sets sail. Strangely, no other ships appear to be casting off or trying to follow. Along the docks, you see the Otherhood cheer and raise their fists. Across the water, they start chanting the same name repeatedly, accompanied by a rising, deep thump of drums.

JER-RACK-SIS, JER-RACK-SIS, JER-RACK-SIS!

Even as the chants fade and the docks recede into the distance, the strange drumming remains clearly audible, along with the whimpers of several terrified crew members. One of the three on the boat grips the gunwale so tightly that his knuckles turn bone white, while another has his head in his hands. The third, without hesitation, lets out a scream and jumps over the side into the awaiting waves.

You don't understand! We… we have to get out of here, he's unleashed it!

The captain you convinced to come along, whose name you still don't know, lets out a long, hearty laugh and doesn't look behind him as he maintains the steady course. As you look back, you see a shape in the water rapidly approaching.

A very… very large shape.

LOOKS LIKE WE'VE DONE IT NOW!

As the captain finishes his bellow, a titanic crash lurches the ship to one side as a massive beast explodes out of the water next to you. It is easily twice as long as your vessel, and its movements displace water in such great volumes that it nearly capsizes you all at once. Only the skillful efforts of the captain and the natural buoyancy of the ship keep you from utter disaster. Water rains down from the creature's large scales as its baleful gaze twists in the air, staring at you with golden, burning eyes. You cling to the rigging and rails to avoid toppling into the heaving waves.

The captain bellows over the chaos:

TO ARMS! YA POX -RIDDEN BALLAST! Fight the thing off while I keep us steady! OH! and try NOT TO GET EATEN!

The captain's voice continues to boom out commands as he laughs over and over again.

WIP: Early Access

The below combat section is an event recently revised to reflect the intended design for this encounter, but it is not yet prepared for play. Expect future changes to introduce the mechanics of this combat encounter in a fully functional manner!

The Escape from Jerracksis

While the party has escaped from the Otherhood in Seawall, they are being relentlessly pursued by Jerracksis across the bay outside the city. They have little hope of killing the creature as it currently stands and must continue to flee, rolling initiative at the conclusion of the above read-aloud.

Thankfully, the unnamed captain keeps the ship steady and maintains its course. During the combat with Jerracksis, the captain cannot take any damage, and the ship continues in a straight line. The terrified crew takes no action as they cling to the ship.

As Jerracksis swims closer to the ship, it can take several actions that the party needs to defend against or attempt to repair as a consequence with their own actions during their turn. The party will also need to actively attack Jerracksis, as while the damage is not enough to kill the creature, it will drive it off and end the chase.

Jerracksis Actions

The Leviathan Jerracksis makes three initiative rolls, representing attacks by its head, body, and tail. This means it takes three actions each round, following the sequence of the initiative rolls in between the rolls made by the party. On its turns, roll on the table below to decide which action it performs for each of the three initiative rolls.

1d3

Jerracksis Actions

1

Smash - Jerracksis slams his body into the side of the ship, dealing 1 Ship Damage, and every character must make a[[/skill athletics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check or they are knocked prone

2

Venomous Spray - Jerracksis rears its head out of the water and spits acidic bile onto the deck. It deals no ship damage, but sets a small fire as the bile ignites upon contact with the wood. Creates a 10ft circle of fire that deals [[/damage 1d6 fire]] damage to anyone in that space and anyone that end their turn in it.

3

Bite - Jerracksis lunges forwards and bits a massive hole in the side of the ship, allowing water to rush in and dealing 1 Ship Damage

Ship Health

The ship has a maximum of 10 health points. Due to the actions taken by Jerracksis, if the ship's health drops to zero, it will be shattered, causing the party, captain, and frightened crew members to be thrown into the water. They will then need to find their own way to land as Jerracksis swims away, satisfied.

Ship Actions

A player character can perform one of these actions on their turn, replacing their usual combat options. As the combat begins, inform the party that these actions can be taken on their turn instead of attacking the Leviathan. Many of these actions are also commands that the captain yells amid the chaos as the ship desperately tries to leave the bay.

  • Plug That Hole! The character runs over to the hole in the ship made by Jerracksis and stuffs it with tar and canvas, then tries to secure it with wood and nails lying on the deck. Make a[[/skill strength 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check.
    Result: On success, heal one Ship Damage; on a failure, the hole was too big to repair, and the damage remains. The Ship cannot be repaired above its maximum health of 10.

  • Clear the Deck! The characters run to put out the fires made by the Venomous Spray. Make a [[/skill sleightofhand 13]] [[/skillCheck stealth 13]] check.
    Result: On success, the fire is removed from the deck.

  • Where's it heading?! The character must move around the ship using their entire movement speed on their turn, attempting to spot the creatures' heading. Make a[[/skill perception 16]] or [[/skill investigation 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16]] check.
    Result: On success, the character works out where the creature is heading next, and the next two attacks made against it gain advantage. On failure, Jerracksis slips beneath the water and disappears for a moment.

Escaping the Leviathan

As they attempt to escape, the party must attack Jerracksis to drive it away. To end the combat, Jerracksis has 90 hit points. When the party deals this amount of damage, the creature retreats, slipping underneath the ship and returning to the waters around Seawall.

A narrow escape

Once the party is clear of danger, they may want to discuss what just occured and after a few tense moments after the combat ends, read the following:

Looking back, the Leviathan's long form recedes into the distance as it appears to swim back toward Seawall. It seems your efforts were worth little, and most of your attacks didn't seem to bother it much—perhaps it experienced the pain like a sting from some insect and decided you were far enough from the city it safeguards, but it's hard to tell.

The captain on the tiller doesn't move from his post but turns to regard you with a grin.

A grand old escape, and you all seemed to account yourselves well eh! What's the heading, onwards to Ordain?

What Was That?

After the combat ends, the captain reveals himself as Captain Razor Blackwood, captaining the Flywind. He is a former member of House Bastilla who is now retired. He maintains his own ship to transport rare goods between the Waerd city of Wick and Ordain. He stopped in Seawall to smuggle a recent shipment of weapons, for which he was promised a substantial purse. Unfortunately, the Otherhood kept delaying payment, causing him increasing frustration.

I think I won't be dealing with those "Otherhood" types anymore; they seem unfriendly, and not in a good way. Plus, they swindled me out of a pretty penny for my last haul…

Speaking with Lyla

During the combat, Lyla tried to help as much as she could, but she is now lost in thought. The party can try to talk to her, but she only responds with the following:

It's all quite overwhelming. This Otherhood is gathering near the city, and they appear to hold a grudge or vendetta against my house. I will need to seek help from the other Trading Houses, but I can't shake the feeling that I am in over my head. As soon as we get to Ordain, I'm heading to the Ordinate to tell them what has happened.

Although Lyla is not in the mood to talk, during the journey Captain Blackwood is happy to chat with the party about all sorts of topics and has a lot of knowledge about the oceans of Ember and ships.

Was that a Leviathan?

Yeah, it was… though I’m not sure why my reckless crew was so worried; it was just a young one. If you don’t know, though, Leviathans are massive creatures said to be as old as the world itself. They are generally reclusive creatures, choosing to avoid settlements, but many are territorial, aggressive, and violent. It is believed that Leviathans are intelligent and immortal, and they wield power on the same level as the Shard Gods in many cases.

He stops to think for a moment and rubs his short beard.

What's more important is how these Otherhood folks are controlling it…

What will you do when we get to Ordain?

Hah! I'll have to go retrieve some of my savings from my old estate and get this old ship back in shape. I'll probably stick around for a while and try to wrangle a new crew... this one seems a little useless... but if you need my services in the future, you can come and find me.

He winks at the party, and his toothy grin is somehow infectious.

Concluding the Event

Moving On

Once the party escapes from Jerracksis, they are able to sail on to Ordain without any further problems. Essentially, they can either make their way into the city from the sea or stop to climb the nearby cliffs in an attempt to reach the city by land and leave the ship behind.
Strange Depths.soverview: As the party leaves Seawall aboard a commandeered ship and heads toward Ordain, they are pursued by a massive creature attacking from beneath the ocean waves.
Strange Depths.sexposition: With the chase through Seawall finished and the ship heading out of the city, Lyla takes a deep breath as she looks at the gathered Otherhood shouting insults at her and the party.
Strange Depths.ssummary: We narrowly escaped the teeth of a massive aquatic leviathan unleashed on us as we tried to flee from Seawall. Fortunately, we managed to evade the creature and started heading to Ordain with Lyla.

Unwelcome Diversions.name: Unwelcome Diversions
Unwelcome Diversions.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration and combat event, each of the leads found by the party in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.nEGURPRHh6stkdPW]{Unhappy Accidents} has led to the Lower Arcturel, and this event takes place on the area map of@UUID[Scene.emberArcturelLow]{Arcturel Lower}.

In this event, the party can explore the area map and investigate the following:

  • Get a sample of the brew that has been sickening the locals by breaking into the distillery.

  • Figure out what has been making the repairs fail by looking at the repair shop.

  • Try to figure out what is wrong with Hob Korell's lizard steeds at his stables.

  • Confront the Tyraphem @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Kilner} in the locked area.

The text in this event should be used to play out encounters rather than using Area Walkthrough for the following locations:

  • Distillery

  • Stables

  • Repair Shop

  • Apothecary

Once the party enters the mine area, you can then follow the @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu]{Area Walkthrough}. This is because this event is directly tied to the quest and Old Friend, whereas the area map could be used as a generic map for parties to explore outside the quest.

A Glimpsed Cloak

While the party is walking through the area map, they can catch glimpses of the Tyraphem @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Kilner} watching their progress. Any time a character makes a successful [[/skill perception 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16]] check outside of the mine, they see a cloak out of the corner of their eye.

Just at the edge of your vision, you see a piece of dark fabric, sweeping around a nearby corner, as if someone just moved out of your field of view.

If characters make a successful [[/skill survival 18]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 18]] check, they can identify where the figure disappeared and follow the direction back to the door of the mine. This may mean they skip some of the other clues and investigations and jump straight into the confrontation with Kilner.

Investigating the Distillery

The metal door to the distillery is closed, and there is no sign of life or activity through the one window in the center of its frame. A sign, taped to that window with an impressive amount of adhesive, reads "Closed for Internal Processing."Beneath these words, in smaller handwriting, are the words, "If you believe our karal is to blame for your current illness, please see Apothecary Arvoda for treatment."

A final scrawled note, which is accompanied by a skull and crossbones, as well as a lightning bolt, is taped up next to the keyhole above a simple metal knob.

Entering the Distillery

The distillery door is locked. It can be unlocked with a successful[[/skill sleightofhand 14 t00l=thief]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] check requiring @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000]{Lockpicks} , but opening the door triggers the a trap (see Do Not Enter below).

Alternatively, characters can smash through the glass with a successful [[/skill athletics 22]] [[/skillCheck athletics 22]] check. On a failure, a piece of glass flies off of the window — the character who made the attempt must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 14]] or they take [[/damage 1d10 piercing]] damage from the flying glass [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] to leap out of the way or suffer [[/hazard 6 fortitude health piercing]]{Shattered Glass Fragments}.

  • Characters who make a successful [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check or have [[/knowledge crafts]] can identify the window material as double-spun glass, which is extremely difficult to break unless hit at a weak point and sprays pieces of glass at anyone who tries.

  • Characters who make a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]]check to examine the window can see minute cracks underneath the adhesive that is attaching the "Closed for Internal Processing" sign to the window.

  • Characters who target the window's weak point can smash through the glass with a successful [[/skill athletics 17]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check with @Advantage[2]. Due to this targeting, no glass sprays if they fail the check.

Characters may attack the window with spells or attack actions. When attacked in this manner, the window has an AC of 13 and 20 HP, shattering when it reaches 0 HP, but sheds fragments of glass with each successful hit. If a hit succeeds, all characters within 10 feet of the doorway must make a successful [[/save dexterity 15]] or they take [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] damage from the glass spray

Do Not Enter

The door to the distillery has been rigged with an electricity trap, triggered by anyone who attempts to pull on the metal handle. If characters try to use the knob to open the door, they mustmake a successful [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw or they take [[/damage 1d10 lightning]] damagemake a successful [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] to leap out of the way or suffer [[/hazard 6 fortitude health electricity]]{Electrical Discharge} . The trap can be triggered multiple times, with no reset time required.

Characters that make a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, or who use Find Traps or a similar ability a spell or talent to locate traps, spot a tiny sliver of metal in the gap between the edge of the door and the door frame, which seems out of place. This is the trigger to the trap.

To disable the trap, a character must make a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 14]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] check, a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.disarmingToolkit] grants +2 Boons for this check. . On a success, the trap is disabled. On a failure, the trap is disabled, but triggers one final time in the process.

Once inside @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.QpHwyxq7yJZGhjFY]{Waterborne Family Distillery}, characters can easily take a sample of the brew aging in the barrels without a check using one of the vials or glasses located on the tables in the distillery.

The karal pours into the container with a pleasant fizzy sound and a rich earthy smell, but there is something else in the air as the liquid fills the glass — something ever so slightly off.

Tainted Brew

Characters who take a sample from the barrels acquire @UUID[Item.Pwr7R7tZOhltCXiB]{Suspicious Karal}.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check, or have [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/knowledge machines]], can identify the toxin in the brew as @UUID[Item.4bmOJe7s9TwbHbvC]{Concentrated Ore Dust}. Unlike regular mine dust, this has been alchemically altered to be more toxic.

  • If characters cannot identify the substance, or wish to know more about it, they can ask Apothecary Arvoda of @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.yObJp4josnr70zog]{Arvoda's Elixirs}.

The party can examine the barrels for signs of tampering.

  • With a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]], characters identify a small section of the wood at the top of the barrel with different grain than the wood around it.

    • Characters can remove this wood either with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.8NS6MSOdXtUqD7Ib]{Carpenter's Tools}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.xKErqkLo4ASYr5EP]{Woodcarver's Tools} any number of tools, such as @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.crowbar000000000], @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.hammer0000000000], or some of the tools typically contained in a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.fletchersToolkit] or @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.smithsToolkit000], or a successful [[/skill 15 sleightofhand]] check, revealing a large hole in the top of the barrel with perfectly smooth edges, as if the section was surgically removed by a metal tool.

    • Characters who make another successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check can spot wood dust from the wood on the ground. With a successful [[/check investigation 14]] or [[/check survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check, they can follow it to the barrels at the back of the room, which hide the entrance to the mine that leads to @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.o06g8caWK9wvMvSR]{The Storage Room}.

Investigating the Stables

A wave of heat washes over you as you step into the stables, muggy and thick, and somehow everywhere, with no clear origin point other than the large glowing lamps that beat down onto a group of reclining lizards. The young stablehand seems not to feel the heat, barely looking up from the rhythmic work of scooping and tossing straw in the middle of the enclosure as you enter the shop.

If you're here for a Jobri ride, you may have to wait a little bit. They're resting. And if you're here to try to get a free drink out of Hob by fixing whatever's wrong with 'em, go for it. You won't be the first.

The young stable hand Kaol (Chaotic Neutral, Arcturian Human, he/him) returns to his absentminded work. If asked any questions, he shrugs — he doesn't know what's wrong with the lizards, and he isn't in the mood to guess.

The Jobri Pen

The 3 @UUID[Actor.T6YcptpxcCLx4yLx]{Jobri} here appear to be fine, if sleeping soundly. Any attempts to rouse them have no effect. If the party attempts to get them to wake up, the stablehand just chuckles.

They've been sleep a while — don't think they're getting up any time soon. At least this time they aren't falling asleep mid-climb, but still, something about them is just off.

  • With a successful [[/skill animalhandling 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check, characters know that something is bothering the Jobri that is external to them — something in their environment is causing them to sleep. Characters with knowledge of [[/knowledge beasts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • A character that makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} spell [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] talent , or similar abilities, knows that there is a spell originating in the heat lamp that is causing the Jobri to sleep. Two of the heat lamps are, in fact, @UUID[Item.dnzX0TSncwz6EbK4]{Lazing Lamps}.

  • The Lazing Lamps can only be disabled magically — this can be done using @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} or a similar magical effect. The Lazing Lamps can only be disabled magically — this can be done using [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.counterspell0000]] against a Control rune with an Aura gesture and a willpower defense of 16.

  • The lamps can also be physically removed from the room, though they are extremely hot to the touch. Any character who attempts to remove a lamp without using gloves, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.KndVe2insuctjIaj]{Smith's Tools} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.smithsToolkit000], or magical means (Mage Hand or similar) must make a successful [[/save constitution 15]] check when touching the lamps or they take [[/damage fire 1d10]] damage [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] when touching the lamps or suffer [[/hazard fortitude health 6 fire]]{Mild Burns}.

  • Characters who use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.SleYkHovQ8NagmeV]{Locate Object} spell magic capable of locating an object can locate a Lazing Lamp found within @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.o06g8caWK9wvMvSR]{The Storage Room} in the mine.

If characters remove or disable the @UUID[Item.dnzX0TSncwz6EbK4]{Lazing Lamps}, the stable hand Kaol asks what is happening or what they are doing, but makes no effort to stop the party.

  • Kaol will freely tell the characters that the heat lamps are new, procured from a merchant recently after the heat lamps all malfunctioned and the replacements went missing.

  • Kaol suspected that someone from the mine took the heat lamps but has no idea why.

Investigating the Repair Shop

Pieces of metal are scattered across one of the repair benches alongside a number of tools and jars of unknown substances. Above them is a sign that reads "Cevher Repairs." Notes in and around the metal may have once been in some kind of order but have been scattered around the room. As you enter, a clank echoes through the room, followed by the distant sound of whirring, humming through the floor. A moment later, the sounds disappear, leaving only silence.

A Mechanical Echo

The sound of clanking and whirring can be heard intermittently in Wrestful Repairs. At the GM's discretion, or after the party makes 2 checks, the sound returns. Characters who make a successful [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check can tell that the noise is coming from the eastern wall (which is the wall closest to the mine). If characters are standing in one of the two rooms that are adjacent to the mine, they have @Advantage[2] on this check. Characters who hear the sound and have [[/knowledge machines]] can tell that it is being caused by a machine of some type.

The Odd Metal

Any character that has [[/skill perception 16 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] of the repair shop can see dust between the pieces of metal, of the same gray color as the metal.

If any character picks up a piece of metal from the bench, a flaky dust falls from it onto the floor.

Where your hands touch the metal, small bits of flaky gray dust float down to the ground. They're almost too tiny to see, but where they glint slightly in the light, their silvery color matches the metal in front of you.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/knowledge machines]], or who have proficiency with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.KndVe2insuctjIaj]{Smith's Tools} have the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.smithingNovice00]] or [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.alchemyNovice000]] talent know that this kind of effect is caused either by something physical that has been applied to the metal or a natural weakness in the material, as opposed to a spell. They also have @Advantage[2] on further checks on the metal.

    • Characters who make a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check, or who use a tool on the metal find that the bulk of the metal is strong, but the edges are flaky.

    • Characters who make a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check can see residue on the edge of the metal pieces and on the edges of several tools nearby. It has a distinctive acrid smell to it.

    • Characters who succeed on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check can identify the substance as the secretions of the boreworm, a metal-burrowing bug. The substance can also be brought to the apothecary, Arvoda, for identification.

    • Once characters have identified the substance, they can detect the same acrid smell elsewhere in Wrestful Repairs with a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check. It is primarily found in a small vat that has the word "glue" written on it in blocky handwriting — this substance is, in fact, @UUID[Item.qvLD88iUi3FBdkdc]{Metal Crumbler}. The handwriting does not resemble any other handwriting found within the repair shop.

On The Record

Rennerie's records have been scattered all around the bench. Characters who take the time to go through the papers and succeed on an [[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck science 12]] check find one paper that seems like it might be relevant.

I know people are saying that the mine is odd these days, and Zodi has pulled everyone back to the front, but I'm excited to get in there and get the excavator working! Maybe I'll try that new sample glue I got. Like that merchant said, you can never have enough supplies!

Characters can locate the vat of glue referenced in the note without a check. With a successful [[/check perception 13]] check or [[/check perception passive 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] they can smell an acrid smell in it that seems out of place. As above, the vat of @UUID[Item.qvLD88iUi3FBdkdc]{Metal Crumbler} can be identified as a metal weakening agent with a successful [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check.

Mayis Attunement: Leads Investigated

If the party manages to investigate all three of the primary leads in Lower Arcturel, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 otherhood1Arcturel2Leads]] at the conclusion of the event.

Asking the Apothecary

Haggling with Emelyn Arvoda

Arvoda will answer questions for the party about poisons, potions, and alchemical substances, but she wants to be paid for her expertise. With a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check, characters know that while she is very concerned with her bottom line, she is knowledgeable and confident in her answers.

Don't tell me. You drank the bad karal. Or got thrown from some ornery lizard? Though now that I think about it, you look less like locals than adventurers. Adventurers with a lot of questions on their tongues.

Happy to help with anything you need, though you will need to make a purchase first. Or donate to the Dives Merchant Association, if you'd prefer. Nothing under 5 gold per question, please, or it will be difficult to make time for anything but small talk.

For each substance that the party wants information about, they must either purchase an item or donate [[/award -5gp]] [[/award -1gp each]]to the apothecary. With a successful[[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]]check, she will lower the cost of getting an answer to [[/award 1gp]]. Any character with [[/knowledge trade]] has @Advantage[2] on this check.

Arvoda's Identifications

Arvoda can help with any of the following:

  • The sample of @UUID[Item.Pwr7R7tZOhltCXiB]{Suspicious Karal} from Waterborne Distillery, which she identifies as being contaminated with @UUID[Item.4bmOJe7s9TwbHbvC]{Concentrated Ore Dust}. She notes that this kind of concentrated ore dust must be created. On its own, a mine would not generate enough dust to create this effect.

    A thick grayish gloop that resembles congealing paste, found in Wrestful Repairs, which is @UUID[Item.qvLD88iUi3FBdkdc]{Metal Crumbler}.

As the party leaves Arvoda's for the first time, she stops them in their tracks:

"Wait," the apothecary says, as you turn to leave. "Now, I'm not in the business of giving away free information, as you know, but these are odd times, and I certainly don't want any unnecessary harm to come to any of my customers. So, between us, an odd man came here not too long ago, asking about whether I thought the mine was cursed and if I was worried about working so close to it. Decided then and there to stay put. Seemed like he was trying to warn me off, and I don't like being managed. I didn't get anything else from him, but last I saw, he was headed toward the mine, cloak trailing behind him."

Abandoned Mine

With all roads leading to the abandoned mine, the party can keep investigating the area further, though they will have to unlock the door first.

Entering the Abandoned Mine

The party will have to unlock the mine's gate in order to enter. The lock can be only be unlocked with a successful[[[/skill sleightofhand 16 t00l=thief]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 16]] check requiring @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000]{Lockpicks} .. However, the nearby mine door is weaker — it can be unlocked with a successful [[/check dexterity 14]] check with Thieves' Tools [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] using a Lockpick or pried open with a successful [[/skill athletics 14]] check [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check using a crowbar or other prying tool . If characters apply @UUID[Item.qvLD88iUi3FBdkdc]{Metal Crumbler} to the door, they have @Advantage[2] on the this check.

If the party cannot find a way to break into the mine, they may visit Zodi Trask, who has relocated to @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.rh4RdGCvghwWvPgR]{Zodi Trask's Apartment} and ask for the key. He is reluctant, but can be convinced to give it up with a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check.

Area Walkthrough

Once they enter the mine area, the party's progress can be tracked using the @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu]{Lower Arcturel} area walkthrough. The party's time in the mines ends with their battle against Tyraphem Kilner and a search of his belongings for information about the issues occurring in Arcturel.

If the party members search Kilners belongings thoroughly, they may come across his notes, @UUID[Item.AYDgFBnsqMR51Uqt]{Kilner Notes}, which mention a way to decode the @UUID[Item.r659n05meW0ZMGY9]{Coded Bandit Instructions} found on the bandits in Helkas.

Decoding the Bandit's Message

As mentioned in @UUID[Item.AYDgFBnsqMR51Uqt]{Kilner Notes}, to decode the message left by the bandits, characters must hold the paper in their hands and say the words "For Other Fortunes." If they do this, they receive @UUID[Item.4gnpLU3NcyXylMHB]{Decoded Bandit Instructions} in place of @UUID[Item.r659n05meW0ZMGY9]{Coded Bandit Instructions}.

If parties successfully decode the message, mark the "Decoded the Bandit Instructions" outcome in @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.6XGCgWBOeHH6HVlT]{A Friendly Reunion} as complete.

Cora Attunement: Disable the Device

If the party manages to disable the device found in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.eApuNVjHrvwXGB8C]{The Hub}, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 otherhood1Arcturel2Device]] at the conclusion of the event.

Signara Attunement: Discover the Hidden Room

The first character who manages to discover the hidden room in @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.EW7J3f5ABR3CoOQc]{The Last Pit} advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 otherhood1Arcturel2Device]] at the conclusion of the event.

Signara Attunement: Defeat the Aburyx

If the party manages to defeat the Kilner in combat, each character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 otherhood1Arcturel2Device]] at the conclusion of the event.

After the Mines

After Kilners has been defeated, Lyla will mention they should check back in with Zodi to tell them of what they have uncovered. When the party reaches Zodi's apartment, the foreman is anxiously pacing back and forth and immediately gestures for you to sit.

Updating Zodi Trask

Zodi immediately wants to know what the group has discovered and if it can help right things for House Cevher and the residents of Arcturel. He is both shocked and relieved to find out that it appears that some creature was behind the recent troubles in the city.

So all of the things going wrong? They were all on purpose? The bad karal? Hob's lizards nodding off? The machines breaking? I guess I'm glad to know that I'm not somehow the worst liaison that House Cevher has ever had here, but it feels like there was some kind of organized campaign to ruin what happened here.

Lyla (if present) agrees wholeheartedly.

Between this and the attack on Helkas, someone appears to have House Cevher in their sights. But my friends and I stopped them here and we'll stop them again. I just need to figure out who's behind it all, and why. At least I know where to go next, though. There's clear evidence of House Wandren's influence here. I hear that my old friend Juro Wandren is in the village of Nain. I'm sure he's not involved in this, but his house appears to be connected so hopefully he can shed some light on things.

Zodi wishes the party luck and invites them to stay in Arcturel as long as they'd like. If desired, this can provide an opportunity for an onramp to the event @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3], which also takes place in Arcturel.

You do what you need to do. We'll be okay here. Now that that creature has been dealt with, we here in Arcturel can pick up the pieces, and we'll keep an eye out for any other odd happenings. We're sturdy folks and we don't mind labor. Not that you have to go, of course. Feel free to stay here and rest — my home is your home.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

Lyla will proceed from Arcturel to Nain to follow up on the evidence that she has found in the sinkhole city that links to House Wandren in [[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]] and attemept to get help from her old friend @UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren}.
Unwelcome Diversions.soverview: With several businesses in the Arcturel's lower levels facing unexpected trouble, the party can investigate what is happening with any or all of them, with each discovery leading them toward the abandoned mine nearby.
Unwelcome Diversions.sexposition:
As you descend slowly and jerkily in an elevator toward the bottom of the sinkhole, the ornate carved wood, bridges, and banded metal give way to plain metal walkways covered in rust and grim. The air feels a bit flatter, and the light is dimmer. Nonetheless, you can still hear people working and living their lives, with the glow of mushrooms on the cavern walls providing strange, almost ethereal illumination.

As you step out onto one of the walkways, you notice several shops and locations nearby. Lyla steps forward, visibly more on edge than usual, her hand firmly gripping the hilt of her rapier.

Okay, we should take a look around and find out more about what happened in the mine and the troubles Zodi mentioned. Where should we start?
Unwelcome Diversions.ssummary: We investigated the odd happenings in Arcturel and tracked them down to a defunct mine that had become unexpectedly occupied!

Dash Away All.name: Dash Away All
Dash Away All.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this combat event, which takes place on the@UUID[Scene.emberSeawallAlle]{Seawall Alleys} area map, party must make their way to an awaiting ship and flee Seawall before they are captured. Though combat is likely, it is fairly unwinnable in the long run, and the party must eventually run or fall.

Note: In the combat tracker, a single raider and brigand stand in for the group as a whole in initiative order.

Otherhood Pursuit

@Embed[Actor.VRyq5hmqCTUY2ZYO]

@Embed[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H]

As the area map loads, the party realizes they must navigate a winding path filled with Otherhood members. They could try to stand their ground, but Lyla consistently urges them to run as the number of Otherhood members increases. While escaping through Seawall toward the docks, they are actively chased by Otherhood Raiders and Brigands.

An Unending Chase

While fleeing through Seawall for the docks, the party is actively pursued by Otherhood Raiders and Brigands. However, their numbers are too great to overcome, and the party must flee rather than stand their ground. The chase challenge has three parts: Distance to Destination, Otherhood Proximity, and Chase Actions.

Chase Actions

To get closer to their destination, and evade the Otherhood the party must make a series of group skill checks. The party can use any of these actions during the chase:

  • Run For It! The party runs full tilt. Make a group [[/skill athletics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check.
    Result: On success, move 1 steps closer to the Destination and move the Otherhood 2 steps further away. On failure, move 2 steps away from the destination, and move the Otherhood closer by 1 step.

  • Follow me! The party leaps down a level, runs across rooves, jumps through stalls, or other rough terrain. Make a group [[/skill acrobatics 14]] [[/skillCheck athletics 14]] check.
    Result: On success, move 1 step closer to the Destination and move the Otherhood away by 1 step. On failure, move only 1 farther from the Destination, or allow the Otherhood to move 1 step closer (the party chooses).

  • This Way! The party spots a shortcut or pathway toward their destination. Make a group [[/skill perception 14]] or [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check.
    Result: On success, move 2 steps closer to the destination. On failure, move only 1, closer to the destination and move the Otherhood closer by 1 step.

  • Hide! The party tanks a risk and hides nearby, hoping their pursuers run past. Make a group [[/skill stealth 16]] or [[/skill deception 16]] (the party decides) [[/skillCheck stealth 16]] check.
    Result: On success, move the Otherhood 2 steps away. On failure, move the Otherhood closer by 2 steps.

  • Improvise! The players can suggest an action not listed here, such as knocking over stalls, causing distractions, throwing out money, and similar. Discuss how this would affect the chase, and determine a group check that makes sense for the action.

Distance to Destination

During this chase sequence the Party is attempting to get to a ship to escape. The distance to this vessel is marked by a scale: In Reach - In View - Nearby - Close - Distant. To get onto the boat, the party must be In Reach of it.

Otherhood Proximity

The goal of this chase is to keep the Otherhood as far away as possible while getting closer to the party destination. During this chase sequence the Otherhood pursuers have the following distance states:

  • In Reach - The Otherhood is about to grab you!

  • In View - The Otherhood can see you, and you can see them.

  • Nearby - The Otherhood is just one corner away, and will be in view momentarily.

  • Close - The Otherhood knows where you are and is closing in quickly.

  • Behind - The Otherhood has fallen behind but knows what direction you went.

  • Searching - The Otherhood has lost sight of you and isn't sure where you are. You have a little time to move freely.

Escaping or Getting Caught

If the Otherhood gets to the "In Reach" proximity step and the party fails another chase action, they are captured and must fight their way out. For this encounter, they have to brawl with 4 x @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H]{Otherhood Raider} and 2 x @UUID[Actor.VRyq5hmqCTUY2ZYO]{Otherhood Brigand} on the @UUID[Scene.emberSeawallAlle]{Seawall Alleys} map. If they succeed, they can resume running, and the Otherhood start in the "Behind" distance step.

To escape the Otherhood, the party needs to get into the "In Reach" distance step for their destination and the Otherhood needs to be "Behind" or "Searching."

Escaping Seawall

Depending on how things go in the above sequence, the party can either jump onto the ship with Lyla:

You dash aboard the awaiting ship described to you by Salara. Its captain stands there for a moment with his head tilted to one side. He then turns and notices the Otherhood swarming toward you and his hip, and he grins widely.

Aha! You've kicked the hornet's nest, I see! Time to leave, lads!

He then begins bellowing orders, and the ships seem to launch away from the Gray Harbour Docks with a shudder. Cries for the crew to stop from the Otherhood approaching fall on deaf ears as the ship's sails catch the wind and drag the vessel further from the docks. Otherhood yell at each other and point at the ship. Some run off, likely to warn their leaders, while others hurl fading insults as you make your escape.

Lyla exhales, relieved, but winded.

Didn't think we were going to make it there… now let's just hope they don't come after us.

Akon Attunement: Sail with Lyla

If the party chooses to set sail for Ordain with Lyla, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 otherhood1EscapeLyla]] at the conclusion of the event.

Or in the unlikely event that the party decides to let Lyla go on her own:

You rush Lyla onto the docks and then turn to face the Otherhood. You are quickly overrun by their numbers, but they are too late to stop Lyla's ship from escaping. As the vessel retreats toward the sea, you are tied up and dragged off.

After some rough handling and questioning, it's determined that you're not especially valuable or interesting. You're "fined" all of your carried coin, and any other particularly valuable items you're carrying, and unceremoniously kicked out of the city.

One particularly burly Otherhood goon growls at you:

Stay out of Seawall. If we ever see you back in here, we'll take more than your valuables.

As they slam the gates shut, your weapons are thrown from the walls and rain down with a horrible clatter. Otherhood scoundrels jeer and mock you from atop the walls, well out of reach and far from repercussion.

Aura Attunement: Stay Behind

If the party chooses to stay behind while Lyla sets sail for Ordain on her own, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 otherhood1EscapeStay]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

If the party continues to Ordain with Lyla, mark that outcome. As the party moves out of the city on the region map, the event[[/eventState otherhood1Depths]] triggers. If the party separates from Lyla, that should be marked as well. The party will connect with Lyla again in Ordain in [[/eventState otherhood1Ordinate]].
Dash Away All.soverview: The party attempts to make it to the ship that will take them away from Seawall to Ordain.
Dash Away All.sexposition:
After leaving Salara, you hurry quickly towards the docks and the awaiting ship she promised. You hear voices shouting over the din of the city. Cries of "over here" and "they went this way" growing louder by the second. Lyla glances around her as you begin to match her pace, turning your hurried walking into a jog.

I think we can fight our way out of this. Our best bet is to head for the ship and get out of here!
Dash Away All.ssummary: We ran to escape the attack by the Otherhood, trying to make our way to the ship to escape Seawall.

Traveling with Lyla.name: Traveling with Lyla
Traveling with Lyla.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event can occur during a rest at any point during Chapter 2 if @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher} is a member of the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party}. In this event the party can:

  • Discuss the current situation with Lyla and learn her thoughts.

  • Ask Lyla for her opinion about characters the party has met along the way.

  • Get to know Lyla better by understanding her story.

This event can occur multiple times while traveling with Lyla and provides the party with an opportunity to learn about the House Cehver heir, her story, and her opinions on the current situations.

Thoughts on Events

Lyla can share her thoughts on some of the recent events that the party has encountered while on this quest.

Oldcraft Lodge[[/eventState otherhood1Lodge]]

It's wonderful to be back at the Lodge—I remember spending long days in his hidden, arcane library while my father visited the mines in Arcturel. It's a shame he's closed those doors, but I suppose he's trying to avoid losing himself in reading for a few years while so much is going on outside.

Sigil never fails to put a smile on my face, and he's always been such a sweetheart. He's always been buried in his books, though, so I was pleasantly surprised to see him actively helping those refugees! He has a lot of potential to help those around him, so I'm glad he's putting his powers to good use.

Arcturel Investigation[[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel1]]

I shudder to think about what might have happened in Arcturel if I hadn't been there to learn what was going on. More sabotage? What would people think of my house and our reputation? This is what I worry about the most. I need to take charge, but there's so much going on I can't possibly control it. I was just lucky you were here with me this time.

Kilner[[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel2]]

That thing.. in the bottom of the mine? It was honestly terrifying, like something from an old story brought to life. Why would it be trying to harm my house? I'm deeply afraid there is even more at stake than I thought, and it makes me terrified that my house is being deliberately targeted. There is more going on here than some simple trade dispute or local act of sabotage.

The "Otherhood"[[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]]

Desperate times make people do horrible things. I could have never imagined that bandits and outlaws on this scale would be terrorizing the Plateau. Their leaders are surely guiding them toward a bad end, but I can't help but wonder if we in Ordain bear some responsibility for the chaos out here and could help more. But for the Otherhood to become this much of a movement in just a few short years? Everywhere I look, something else seems to deepen this web, and I don't like where it is leading.

Seawall[[/eventState otherhood1Simmering]]

Everything seems to come back to Seawall. How can a place so close to Ordain be so antagonistic to the Trading Houses, The Ordinate, and normal Ordani? It seems like someone is working very hard to cause chaos. It's also strange that no one seems to have noticed. Something needs to be done soon to improve relations among all of us in the Trading Houses and Seawall, or there will be more violence on the Arctus Plateau. After fleeing Seawall, though… and seeing how angry everyone was, I don't think I'd ever be able to get through to them.

The Sea Serpent[[/eventState otherhood1Depths]]

I think that creature was a Leviathan or something similar. You hear about them, but this is the first time I've ever seen one. I thought people always exaggerated their size... I believe it might actually be helping or somehow under the control of the Otherhood, which is another scary thought. I would do everything to avoid running into it again, and I'll try to warn others to stay away from the waters around Seawall.

Thoughts on Characters

Though Lyla is not a gossip, she's happy to share her assessment of significant NPCs that the party has encountered.

Agraband

Who doesn't love a good story? Which means loving a good storyteller as well, of course. While I was away, it was storytellers like Agraband — and even Agraband himself, once or twice — that kept me feeling like I knew what was happening in Ordain. Though he's been telling big stories while on this road, so often gossip and storytelling often go hand in hand.

If I'm being honest, pat of me wants to ask him if he has any stories of House Cevher back in the day. Maybe my father got up to some hjinks in his youth that he never had a chance to tell me about? I'd love to see those paired with Agraband's flair for the dramatic.

Clipper

A fun spirit. And a useful merchant to find while traveling. I hope to run across them again — there is never a lack of need for important items. Especially in these troubling times.

Ankarist

I keep wondering if I remember Ankarist from Ordain. In truth, he might have escaped my notice, despite his distinctive looks. Then again, it's always hard to spot investigators of the Veiled Chain sometimes; they seem to blend into the background. He appears to be a dour yet dependable person, and I wish him luck in his own investigation. Truly.

Sin

A charming little companion, I don't think I've ever met someone from the Striders before; they seem quite interesting! She appears amazed by everything around her, and I think it's lovely that she's enamored with the Cindaric Sages. It's a good reminder of the importance of the Cindaric Sages to the people. Too often, I forget all they do and how they can be a comfort to those seeking their way.

Sigil[[/eventState otherhood1Lodge]]

I can't think of a better mentor and friend. I have so many fond memories of him teaching me random things from his vast library; he was always so patient. A little scatterbrained though. I still have the first book he ever gave me in my pack, Trade in the Early Days of Ordain & the Fall of House Komric. It was one of many he patiently read to me, and seeing him again was a blessing.

Zodi Trask[[/eventState otherhood1Arcturel1]]

He has tried his best, and he seems to be well-loved in Arcturel, but I worry about everything that has happened there. I hope that he is able to right the ship now, but I'll need to check in with him often.

Juro Wandren[[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]]

Juro and I were close once. I was born into one Trading House, and he stumbled his way into another. When my father found out we were friends, he was angrier than I had ever seen him. Still, Juro and I were young, and we both liked creative solutions to problems. I hadn't spoken to him in many years, but I hoped he could help, and I hope I can trust him now. He does like to hide in the shadows, though, so I hope I'm not proved wrong in the future.

Sticks[[/eventState otherhood1Simmering]]

I don't know where that villain came from, but he seems to hate the Trading Houses and Ordain. He was accusing House Cevher of causing earthquakes and hurting people! Nonsense. And all while he seems to be the one riling up people in the Arctus Plateau and sowing chaos. His silver tongue is dangerous, though; a lot of innocent people are caught up along with the bad, and he could easily cause a crisis in the future.

Salara[[/eventState otherhood1Ship]]

Truthfully, despite her otherwise obvious flaws… Talking to Salara felt a little like home. That insistence on rules being rules is classic House Cevher, but so is applying the rules with a bit of heart. If you're clever, you can leave just enough of a loophole in a regulation for those with good intentions to squeeze through and those with bad ones to trip on. And something tells me that the Queen of Scales is plenty clever. I just hope she's clever enough to stay clear of this Otherhood nonsense.

About Yourself

If characters would like to know more about Lyla, she's happy to share some of her past.

Your story?

I suppose I'm not that important in the grand scheme of things. I've never felt like I belong in this position, but if you must know... In Ordain, I'm Lyla Cevher, the eldest daughter of Kalton Cevher, who was the head of House Cevher, one of Ordain's famous Trading Houses. I'm on my way back to the city because... well, my father is dead and...

She pauses and takes a long, deep breath.

That means I'm now the head of House Cevher, at least I will be once I get back to the city and assume the title and all the responsibilities. I used to have big dreams about one day finding new paths for House Cevher, paths that would make us stronger than ever before with my father's help after he retired. Now I'm going to have to work it out on my own.

House Cehver?

House Cevher is a Trading House focused on ores, mining, and stonecraft, a bit of metal refinement, and the like. To the outside world, they're one of the great Trading Houses of Ordain, a vital link for Ordain and the Arctus Plateau beyond. And that's all true. Not to mention that they're my family. Literally. The problem for me is that my father has always led the house with one foot in the past. Ive always wanted to shake things up a bit, but I trusted him to keep the ship steady.

Why you were away?

I felt that I needed experiences that were hard to come by in Ordain. My father suggested I go and stay with my distant great aunt Jeramia in Casla Brava. I've been there for about four years now, and I was planning to come back next year... but then everything changed.

Your father's death?

Death can happen at any moment… yet I never expected it to happen this way. He wasn't old or sick; we only spoke through magic a month ago. When I heard he died, I was… devastated. We've occasionally argued about trying new mining techniques and changing traditional methods, but we've always stayed close. I feel immense guilt for not being with him in his final moments. I hope he knew how much I loved him.

Your plans?

I need to return to the city, officially assume the position of head of the house, and ensure my brother, Funar, is well. I also owe it to my father to protect House Cevhers' interests, regardless of our current troubles or future challenges. He may not be here to see it, but I will make my father proud. I'm confident of that.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event may repeat at your discretion when the party rests next. Feel free to use any of the questions and answers here outside the context of this event if you feel they are appropriate to mention during other situations.
Traveling with Lyla.soverview: As the party makes their way through the Arctus Plateau, they may wish to speak to Lyla Cevher about her past, recent events, and/or those the party and Lyla have met along their journey. This event provides the opportunity for the party to relax and talk to Lyla to get her take on the events of the adventure.
Traveling with Lyla.sexposition:
The fire roars at your campsite as Lyla puts the last of the logs on the pile, dusting off the glove on her right hand. She stares solemly at the campfire for a moment before glancing your way.

Another day, another night. To think I'll soon be in Ordain again.. but first, we should eat something. It is never good to rest on an empty stomach, after all.

The words are similar to those she speaks again and again, as she seems to wistfully enjoy the calm nights around the fire, and somehow dreads her return to the city she calls home. She begins pulling provisions from her pack and encouraging you to do the same, as her eyes light up with mirth as she describes each item as if it is decadent cuisine prepared by famous chefs instead of road rations. You're not sure if she does it to amuse herself or to try to keep her own spirits up, but it's become part of the routine.

Ah yes. Portable air-cured victuals and life-giving seeds.

She means meat sticks and nuts, which she divides up among the party if they have nothing to eat themselves, with exaggerated hand gestures as if delivering food on a porcelain plate, before settling down at the foot of the fire.

Before we dive into our amazing feast, anything on your mind?
Traveling with Lyla.ssummary: We spent some time catching up with Lyla around the campfire.

Reuniting with Lyla.name: Reuniting with Lyla
Reuniting with Lyla.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event gives the party an opportunity to reconnect with @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla} in the small village of Nain if they separated from her during the Leavetakings event at the end of The Winding Trail.

Once they meet up with Lyla, the party can:

  • Learn about the meeting with @UUID[Actor.qmMlHizvtjCYKjCR]{Sigil} in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.sdIjbPRNIsJ3ApcU]{Oldcraft Lodge}

  • Learn about the discovery of Celestials in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel} and the plot to disrupt House Cevher Operations.

  • Lyla shares her thoughts on her investigation with the party, after which the group can proceed together to Nain and the @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu.JournalEntryPage.kNE6TGVnWWevjLe9]{A Smuggler Extraordinaire} event.

A Surprise Meeting

When Lyla leaves Helkas to begin her investigation of the bandits, the party knows that she intends to visit Oldcraft Lodge. As her journey takes her through the Arctus Plateau, there are a few opportunities for them to learn of her travels, but the party can reunite with her in the small village of Nain. This can happen deliberately; if the party is looking for Lyla, they might have come across clues or visit Oldcraft Lodge, where Sigil directs them towards Nain. Or they may come across her randomly, and they have an opportunity to reconnect.

@Embed[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP readaloud="Though Lyla's clothing shows some more marks of travel and her pack seems a little lighter than the last time you saw her, she is still bright and focused."]

Music: Lyla's Theme

When the party reunites with Lyla, play [[/soundscape music lylaTheme lylaTheme]]

What Lyla's Learned

The party can fill Lyla in on what has happened to them during their travels so far, and Lyla is shocked by the scale of the troubles affecting the region. After a moment to compose herself, or if pressed, Lyla recaps what she learned in Oldcraft Lodge and Arcturel about the bandits.

My investigation began with Sigil at Oldcraft Lodge, where I found a large group of refugees and displaced families recovering outside. They were in terrible shape, but Sigil was doing his best to help them. While there, I asked around about the bandits and was able to learn a few things. The bandits that attacked Helkas are part of a larger organized group called the Otherhood. I don't know exactly what they want, but they seem determined to make House Cevher an enemy, and they harbor no love for any of the Trading Houses. They also appear intent on causing chaos in the region.

Sigil advised I visit the mining town of Arcturel to the south, where I discovered a plot by a strange celestial creature named Kilner to disrupt my family's operations. In the aftermath, it seems like the plot wasn't random and might have been connected to this Otherhood group.

I must admit, this all feels very overwhelming, and I don't know if I'll be able to uncover the true plan without some more help. So, I'm here to see if an old friend who has some... well, let's just say disreputable connections might have some information I wouldn't be able to find on my own.

Lyla is happy to provide a summary of what she has learned about the three clues that she decided to investigate back in Helkas.

Oh, and there were those three clues from the bodies of those Bandits back in Helkas that I managed to find some answers for at Oldcraft Lodge.

  • The Coded Instructions: Lyla partially decoded the instructions given to the bandits. They mention a cloaked figure, who she located in Arcturel, trying to sabotage House Cevher operations, and someone, a leader figure, who is referred to in the notes as the "Bonny Captain".

  • The Leather Markings: Lyla found a book on leather markings in the Oldcraft Lodge and confirmed the information with merchants in Arcturel. She's fairly sure that the leather markings come from either Seawall or Ordain.

  • The Strange Saying: The phrase "For Other Fortunes," found on some bandits as Tattoos, is a code used by the Otherhood to identify themselves — it is half of a call-and-response, but she's not sure what the other half might be.

What do the Coded Instructions say?

I couldn't fully decode the bandit instructions, but I understood the essentials. A cloaked figure was sent to Arcturel to sabotage House Cevher’s operations. While there, I found out that this figure was actually a strange creature from Luxarum. I learned about these beings from Sigil long ago, and I think the name is Tyraphem. This particular creature was somewhat weak for something from the Inner realms, and I have no idea why it would target my house’s operations. For now, it remains another mystery.

What about the Leather Markings?

The markings and icons suggest that the bandits are probably connected to either Seawall or Ordain. I think Seawall is more likely because the markings clearly show a large ancient tower, which is a distinctive feature of Seawall. Luckily, this is probably the next stop after Nain, so I will look into it further there!

The Strange Phrase tattooed on their arms?

I discovered in Arcturel that this is a phrase these bandits and this group called the Otherhood of Fortune use as a secret phrase among their members. "For Other Fortunes" might just be the first part of the codeword, though, and I wasn't able to find out the response.

The Otherhood of Fortune

I believe they are more organized than I initially feared, and they appear to have a sinister plan in motion that targets not only my house but much of the Arctus Plateau. They seem to be exploiting other events to spread chaos and unrest, but I don't know what their ultimate goal is.

What is Seawall?
