You might not be familiar with it, but Seawall is considered the only other genuine city near Ordain. It’s smaller and located to the east of Nain. The governing body of the Ordinate has paid it little mind, and it’s seen as somewhat of a backwater. Sometimes, trade ships avoid paying official taxes and duties at Ordain docks by heading to Seawall instead, hoping to negotiate a better deal. Despite that, it's a nice place, blending elements of Ordani and Arcturian traditions. I recall the people being very friendly, though a bit annoyed by Ordain and the Trading Houses the last time I visited.

Related Quests

Before continuing on, the party may choose to undertake @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book Of Tales}, a side quest that starts in Nain. Lyla doesnt mind if the party chooses to do this first if the party wants to meet up with her later when she meets Juro.

If the party is not yet at least level 3, you may wish to strongly suggest the party investigate this side quest before continuing onward.

Music: Default

Once the party has finished conversing with Lyla, return to the default music: [[/soundscape music reset]]

Pursuing the Leads

Once the party has asked Lyla enough questions about her exploits, they can decide to embark on other quests, such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000]{The Book Of Tales} or move on to meet up with Sin or with Ankarist. Lyla will continue her investigations alone if she has to, and will find her old friend Juro in Nain and ask for his help.

However, if the party seems willing, then Lyla will say the following:

Lyla gazes at you with her eyes narrowing slightly, her hand moving to the guard of her sword, not as a threat but as if she's considering you more carefully.

You know, I could really use some more help. My previous offer still stands—if you'd like to accompany me, there are still many questions to answer. I've also heard rumors from people here in Nain that Seawall has become more dangerous lately. I can compensate you for your efforts, and perhaps we can work together to uncover more about this bandit group.

Before moving on to Seawall, let's stop by another familiar face here in Nain. He's likely to be glad to see us and could help clarify some of the rumors.

The party can then head off to meet with @UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren}, and Lyla joins their group.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

If the party decides to go with Lyla, she joins the party, and you can complete this event. When ready, you can begin the next event in the quest [[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]], which also occurs within the town of Nain.

To trigger [[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]] automatically, advance time in the game world by at least one hour.
Reuniting with Lyla.soverview: The party, which separates from Lyla at the end of the Winding Trail in chapter 1, finds that she has traveled to Nain while investigating who was responsible for the bandit attack in Helkas. The party meets her here, and she shares her discoveries so far from her visits to Oldcraft Lodge and Arcturel.
Reuniting with Lyla.sexposition:
As you enter the sleepy village of Nain, the sound of running water over the nearby watermills initially drowns out a distant yell. However, as you turn your head, you see Lyla Cevher waving with her gloved right hand as she approaches you, her expression warm and a gentle smile spreading across her face.

Oh, it's lovely to see you again! And your timing is perfect — I'm getting closer to figuring out just who was behind the attack on Helkas.
Reuniting with Lyla.ssummary: We reconnected with Lyla in Nain, where she caught us up on what she's found while traveling on her own.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This main quest occurs during Chapter 2, and begins if the party [[/eventState windingTrailLeavetaking ankarist]] at the end of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai]{The Winding Trail}. If the party chose not to, they can still rejoin Ankarist at a later time, in which case they start the "Ancient Paths" quest partway through, via the [[/eventState chain1Reunite]] event.

Once any of the Chapter 2 main quests have been completed, it is no longer possible to access this quest (as Ankarist has independently reached Ordain without the party's assistance).

Difficulty

The "Ancient Paths" quest is designed for a party of Level 3 characters. It begins upon leaving @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}. If the party did not thoroughly explore the Forest of Stone and its respective Chapter 1 side quests, they may still be Level 2. They can either press forward and expect to advance to Level 3 upon obtaining their next milestone point, or they could be encouraged to backtrack and explore further.

Milestone Progression

This is a Main Quest quest that awards 3 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the [[/eventState chain1Guardian]], [[/eventState chain1Laboratory]], and [[/eventState chain1Hallows]] Events.

Ankarist and the party set out from @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas} on a quest to uncover the origins of the drakes and investigate strange occurrences in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz]{Pathways} that might be connected. To achieve this, Ankarist must first consult his friend and local expert, Liestra Grann, who resides in the small hamlet of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush}. Here, Liestra reveals the presence of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.RWj91gQguWOQcflB]{Mythspire}, an ancient ruin that serves as an entrance to the regions deep below the surface. However, she warns Ankarist that he's not the only one looking to find the ancient ruin, and it is well protected by an ancient guardian.

Upon reaching the Mythspire Observatory, the party must navigate its crumbling ruins and overcome a formidable guardian to gain access to the Pathways beneath Ember. Success will lead them into this strange underworld full of dangers and secrets, many of which point them toward something lurking in the darkness. The party ultimately arrives at an abandoned quarry that has been transformed into a twisted laboratory and is actively being destroyed by its creators to hide their actions. With time running out, the party must quickly collect evidence before it's all destroyed and the lab's occupants escape.

Regardless of the outcome, Ankarist must eventually return to Ordain to report to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}. Whether the party gathers ample evidence or only firsthand experiences, the result remains the same: they reveal the existence of an ominous plot, and a conspiracy that may threaten all of the plateau.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]

  • @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]

  • @UUID[Actor.0nC7b7MaX6OLbjoR]

  • @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC]

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B]

  • @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd]

  • @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]

  • @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F]

  • @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]

  • @UUID[Actor.FvGSOm4GOl73LaU9]

  • @UUID[Actor.04OTivhcgPIxJPki]

  • @UUID[Actor.wdPmtkdBiNBBjBls]

  • @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC]
Overview.soverview:
In the wake of a fraught journey to Helkas, and deadly assault on the mining town by never-before-seen dragons, questions lingered: Where did these new dragons come from? Why are they attacking caravans and towns? More importantly, why did the drakes attack Helkas in concert with humanoid raiders? Are they working together or was it simply coincidence?

Ankarist wants answers, and as a seasoned investigator of the Veiled Chain, he has the means and drive to get them. Following up on leads about drakes emerging from caves and caverns all across the Arctus Plateau, and now having come face to face with the vile creatures himself, he sets out to follow a hunch — they must be coming from somewhere underground — and the Pathways beneath Ember are as good a place to start looking as any. However, he'll need to call on some friends, and make a perilous sojourn into Ember's mountains before he gets close to the truth underfoot.

In "Ancient Paths" you will travel with Ankarist to troubled mountain towns, climb windswept cliffs to long forgotten ruins, and enter their crumbling halls in pursuit of rumored passage to the deep realms beneath the surface of Ember. There, you'll walk the timeless caverns where giants once tread, collecting evidence that will reveal the truth about the origin of the strange new drakes appearing on the surface of Ember. Ancient Paths has two dungeons to explore, a vast underground region to discover, and countless enemies standing between you, Ankarist, and the truth about recent events.

Guardian of Myth.name: Guardian of Myth
Guardian of Myth.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration and combat event takes place on the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.RWj91gQguWOQcflB]{Mythspire Observatory} area map, and involves briefly exploring the ruins before engaging in a social encounter with an ancient guardian which has a high chance to turn violent.

The party can:

  • Explore the Mythspire Observatory ruins.

  • Encounter an ancient @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC]{Mythspire Guardian}.

  • Learn the fate of the previous exploration party that came this way.

Area Walkthrough

The party begins at the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.5dFJV5vlH4m74GK5]{Mythspire Approach}, and can freely explore many of the locations listed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.JcGOyaCzImvAie1Z]{Mythspire Observatory} Area Walkthrough. Gamemasters should be aware of some event-specific gameplay that can occur during the exploration of the ruin:

  1. The @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.ocCJdT25yJggk3Ft]{Projection Room} and @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.1P4nZJztxyPruSsW]{Maintenance Balcony} can give the party some insight into the purpose of the observatory.

  2. Once the party reaches the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.uQdyUS2DDyiaeu62]{Central Room}, they are confronted by an ancient guardian that they must either placate or fight.

Exploring Mythspire

This event begins in the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.5dFJV5vlH4m74GK5]{Mythspire Approach}, outside the exterior doors of the ruined tower. From this point onward, refer to the area walkthrough for the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI]. Once the @UUID[Actor.aHW8ke4RHwx2uYsC]{Mythspire Guardian} has been dealt with and the passage into the Pathways has been opened, return here to conclude this event and record resulting outcomes.

Aura Attunement: Mythspire Discovery

If the party manages to discover Mythspire Observatory without directions from Liestra Grann, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 chain1GuardianDiscover]] at the conclusion of the event.

The party may advance certain attunements depending on how they approached the encounter with the Mythspire Guardian.

Akon Attunement: Befriend the Mythspire Guardian

If the party chose to befriend the Mythspire Guardian, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 chain1GuardianBefriend]] at the conclusion of the event.

Abyss Attunement: Destroy the Mythspire Guardian

If the party chose to fight and kill the Mythspire Guardian, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +2 chain1GuardianFight]] at the conclusion of the event.

Once the party has fully explored the ruin and activated the @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.G7YQat34HVQ6tspr]{Ancient Lift} to descend into the pathways, they advance their attunement further.

[[/outcome unlocked]]

Signara Attunement: Ancient Lift Activated

If the party manages to activate the Ancient Lift to the Pathways, each character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 chain1GuardianLift]] at the conclusion of the event.

The party must commit at this point whether to continue with Ankarist or to depart the investigator to continue on his own.

[[/outcome ankaristJoined]]

[[/outcome ankaristLeft]]

If the party decides to Join Ankarist, he says:

Ankarist appears pleased that he'll have backup going into the pathways.

Excellent, glad to have you along. Not only because I didn't want to go into the Pathways alone, either. You've been excellent allies so far, and I am grateful that you're going to be at my side here. From what I understand of the pathways, it's a rather massive region, with plenty of dangers. Not the place for solo adventurers, by any means.

Let's get moving as soon as you're ready.

If the party decides to leave Ankarist, he says:

Ankarist seems a touch disappointed that he won't have backup going into the pathways, but doesn't let it get the better of him.

I'll be honest with you, I was hoping that I wouldn't have to go into the Pathways on my own. Should you change your mind, though, you know where to look for me. Whether you can find me in the pathways though, that's another thing. From what I understand of the pathways, it's an expansive region.

Anyhow, safe and swift travels until we meet again.

Concluding the Event

Once this event is marked as complete the party will be automatically moved underground to the Pathways. From this point onward the party will be in the Pathways region which is separate from the rest of the Arctus Plateau. However, they can still use the Mythspire lift to transition back to the surface if needed.

Milestone Progression

Completing this event awards a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone} point, potentially enabling the party to advance in level.

Next Steps

With the passage opened, the party continues their pursuit of the source of the Drakes underground until they encounter [[/eventState chain1PathwaysCamp]].
Guardian of Myth.soverview: Arriving at the Mythspire Observatory, the party must navigate the crumbling ruins within, and avoid the ire of an ancient and dangerous guardian to find the passage into the Pathways beneath Ember.
Guardian of Myth.sexposition:
Cold air swirls around the crumbling remains of this ancient structure, the unyielding howl of it threatening to deafen you at times. The yawning maw of the entrance looms before you, meant for beings many times larger than you. The ancient stone doors lay toppled on the ground, one in, one out. Beyond the threshold you can see a mixture of shadows and light.

Ankarist takes a breath, steeling himself.

Let's head inside. If we're lucky, we'll be in the pathways in no time. If we're unlucky… well.

He doesn't finish that thought, preferring to head for the entrance instead.
Guardian of Myth.ssummary: We located the Mythspire Observatory and made our way to its base, locating the exit to the pathways. However it appears we were not the only ones seeking this route, and found several dead adventurers whose identity is suspect.

A Strange New World.name: A Strange New World
A Strange New World.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event allows the party to prepare themselves for their journey into @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{The Pathways} in pursuit of Ankarist's lead. They can do the following:

  • Scout the area to get some early leads.

  • Discover the remains of a recently used camp at the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100.JournalEntryPage.3hWpCOzbjeNswxCY#not-the-first]{Overlook Campsite}.

  • Converse with @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist} to get an idea of what to do next.

  • Potentially make camp to rest, if desired.

Not The First

Here, a collection of carefully arranged stones form a fire pit as the heart of what was must have been a camp. All around it the packed earth and stacked stones bears the hallmarks of a space used as a camp many times over.

Ankarist paces the area slowly, looking at the ground, then kicks over a rock he unearths a small stash of garbage haphazardly buried and hidden.

Looks like this camp was used recently. Week or so, I think.

If the players want to investigate the old camp, they can! The party should be prompted to speak with Ankarist before too long, as he wants to confer with the group and form at least a basic plan before they set out.

Ankarist's Plan

Ankarist recommends they scout the immediate area first, and see if they can pick up any early trails or leads. This also lets them get a quick feel for the area, so they don't stumble into any unwanted problems. After that, they can decide what to do next.

Investigating the Overlook Campsite

Those who have [[/skill perception 12 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12 passive]] or higher can easily see that the camp was large enough for a group about their size, with three or four tents.

A successful [[/skill survival 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check reveals that the camp was carefully cleared, the firepit was properly smothered, and refuse collected. Whoever camped here was a competent scouting team.

  • Success The camp has been abandoned for some time, as the various humanoid footsteps and pieces of buried garbage are a couple weeks old, as Ankarist suspected. However, numerous smaller creatures have since passed through or have tried to root out anything edible in the discard piles.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success There are heavy footsteps encircling and entering the camp space, they appear to be substantially newer than any others, and they are humanoid but not any you recognize. Large and reptilian, they are certainly not the tracks of simple beasts, and they came in numbers some time after the camp was abandoned.

A successful [[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck science 12 passive]] check confirms nothing untoward occurred in this camp. It appears it was used briefly and then abandoned. There are no signs of violence or distress here.

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check spots a @UUID[Item.IfkFvTVJMdqCOwF6] fallen into a bush, sitting next to a pack of rations that have been raided by local wildlife. The logbook is muddy and stained with moisture, but could still yield useful information.

Regarding the Jurtak

A successful [[/skill history 17]] [[/skillCheck society 17]] check yields the following information on the Jurtak: They are a secretive lizard people that live in the pathways, nothing is known about their culture, nor any settlements they have built. In all accounts they have been hostile to strangers, and are broadly considered dangerous denizens of the region.

The players may also want to scout the immediate area, as suggested by Ankarist.

Tracking the Tracks

A successful [[/skill survival 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] check reveals the presence of numerous trails through the area. The higher the result of the check, the more the character can discern.

  • Success There are numerous tracks through the area, two humanoid groups came through, as well as a high volume of animals, and something exceptionally large, which seems to have grazed on trees and mushrooms as it went. The humanoid tracks are clearly bipedal, one group consisting of about four people wearing boots, and a group of four or six barefoot with reptilian feet. The booted group came through some time ago, and the reptilian group followed later, but both sets of trails are old.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success The humanoid tracks should be relatively easy to follow, but the reptilian tracks trail off into the overgrowth and are quickly lost in the rocky soil and plant life which help mask their passage.

Spending some time examining the location with a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check takes stock of the biome. This place is lively, filled with numerous species of plants that are bioluminescent, and have developed the ability to survive without sunlight. There is a large amount of fungus, mold, and slime growing alongside grasses, plants, and even trees, off of them seemingly unaffected by the lack of natural light.

Concluding the Event

This area is relatively safe to camp, with ample space to set up and some left over materials to use from a previous group. If the party is especially beat up or out of resources from the encounter in the Mythspire, or previous encounters, he will recommend that the party make camp and rest before striking out.

Next Steps

Once the party is ready to begin exploring, they should strike out into the Pathways with Ankarist. As they explore, they will likely encounter more of the clues they're looking for in [[/eventState chain1Traps]], [[/eventState chain1Scouts]], and [[/eventState chain1Thornling]].

It is also possible for the party to leave the pathways and return to the surface ruins, however, Ankarist urges against this, as he wants to continue exploring and chasing the lead before the trail grows any colder.
A Strange New World.soverview: The party first arrives in the Pathways below Mythspire Observatory. From here they are able to scout the area, pick up some clues, rest, and prepare for their expedition into the Pathways proper.
A Strange New World.sexposition:
Caught in grandeur of the sight before him, Ankarist lets slip a glimmer of childlike wonder as he looks at the Pathways unfolding below.

I've only ever read of the pathways. I thought they were just a bunch of tunnels, not whole underground spaces like this.

After a moment he refocuses, and turns to address you.

Okay, next step is diving into that wilderness and looking for leads. As far as I can tell the drakes are coming from down here, and per Liestra it sounds like we're not the only people looking for a way in. Something is going on with the Pathways.

I'll be honest: I don't know how long we'll be down here, but I am going to get to the bottom of things. You don't have to come with, this is more my crusade than yours, but, I'd certainly appreciate having the backup.
A Strange New World.ssummary: We arrived at an overlook with a commanding view of the Pathways, and found evidence that explorers are active in the area.

Impossible Skin.name: Impossible Skin
Impossible Skin.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event allows the characters to find the shed skin of a massive dragon. In this event, the party can:

  • Find the @UUID[Item.WVX86Em0iiDYYTto]{Molted Dragon Skin} itself, and investigate clues that reveal its relationship to the drakes.

  • Discover a shrine to the skin, and evidence that someone was recently here venerating it.

  • Learn that sections of the skin were being cut and scraped by people.

Skin Of Evil

Near the head of the molt is what appears to be a makeshift shrine captures the eye, a curious assortment of offerings and melted candles sits forgotten in the dark. On the side of the molt lies the remnants of an abandoned work site, where tools and scraps of hide are left forgotten.

Underfoot, layered footprints crisscross the area, most faded, mapping the paths of countless visitors to this area.

Who Are You Wearing?

This shed skin belongs to the main villain of the story, Zerranyss, and if the party encounters said villain while wearing his shed skin, it will be noticed.

If he is masquerading as someone else, he will likely express curiosity about where they got their peculiar materials from. If it is during the final confrontation, he will likely take their fashion choices very personally and target the offending characters.

This will be addressed in later quest events and encounters as appropriate.

Examining The Skin

The dragon skin is massive, stretching for hundreds of feet, and easily large enough for the whole party to walk through. The beast it came from was already massive before it shed, and is only larger now.

  • The hide and scales are a pale white color with faint shades of green.

  • The spine of this dragon appears to be lined with large blades or fins.

  • The dragon's head sports ten large frills coming out of the back of its head and jaw, each one sporting faint green coloring.

  • Its head seems to have eight eyes, some larger than others, and clustered together.

Draconic Insights

Characters with [[/knowledge dragons]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

A character making successful [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check notes that the skin is months, possibly years old, and was at one point accompanied by a considerable layer of dried substances like blood, sweat or pus on the inside of the skin, which also spilled out onto the ground. The shedding process was likely violent and unpleasant for the dragon.

  • Result of 18+ Critical SuccessThere is evidence on the ground and on the inside of the skin indicating that this substance has been scraped off in large amounts. Whoever did it was fairly thorough, and the majority of the remaining substance is soaked into the ground and impossible to gather.

A character making a successful [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check notes the resemblance between this dragon and the smaller drakes encountered above ground. The two creatures seem to have only a few differences, such as the number of eyes and the placement of frills along the body on the drakes instead of along the spine.

  • Result of 18+ Critical SuccessThe size of the dragon's skin and configuration of the frills indicates that this was an adult vile dragon, and one that was likely centuries old, if not older, and likely at the upper size limits of its kind.

Regarding Dragons

The party is unlikely to know much about dragons at this point, but has run into several drakes. Luckily, Ankarist knows a bit about them, and can lend some insight into what they are seeing here. While Ankarist is not an expert on dragons, it is something that he has spent significant time reading about, and so he is more well versed than most people. He can provide some insights and theories if asked.

What do you know about dragons?

There are three kinds: Carnal, Cruel, and Vile Dragons. They are all different in appearance, temperament, and ability. However, they all share the same general traits: They are massive, exceptionally dangerous, wield powerful magic, and very rare.

Encountering a dragon in the wild is often the prelude to widespread destruction and death. So the fact that we're seeing evidence of one in the pathways should be cause for concern.

Do all dragons shed?

I don't know, actually. This is the first instance of a shed dragon skin I've ever seen or heard of. I intend to collect a sample to share with some Anachraenum contacts, they'd certainly be curious to see it, and to learn that some of these beings shed their skins like other reptiles.

What kind of dragon is this?

This skin appears to belong to a "Vile" dragon, known for their long serpentine bodies. I suspect that the drakes might be related to these kinds of dragons, given their shape. It could be that they are juvenile dragons, which I doubt, but I'm not sure. They do share the same general form, though.

What is special about vile dragons?

According to what I have read, vile dragons are known to be especially cruel and single-minded in their drive to accumulate power, and will do whatever they feel is warranted to achieve that goal. What form that power takes varies, there were some that supposedly craved knowledge, while others wanted treasure.

I also think they might be the only dragons that can be bartered and reasoned with, but I don't know how any scholars would have learned that fact specifically.

Who worships dragons?

Dragons wield immense power, and it would be easy enough to view them like a deity or power worthy of awe and respect. Though, I don't think that shrine was only for venerating the dragon, but seemed to be aimed at a select few deities inside the Nineteen.

Looking Over The Shrine

A successful [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] while examining the shrine notes that it is built to venerate an eclectic mix of gods, including Janar, Lanespear, Malae, Obrisire, Steelson, Sionia and Sigil, all gods found within @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.J8wfDAZmky3f5VvV]{The Nineteen}. A stone bowl at the center is filled with burnt parchment, perhaps where offerings or prayers are given. It contains only ash.

  • Result of 18+ Critical SuccessThe gods present in this shrine are related in curious ways, such as Janar, Lanespear and Obirsire for hunting and survival, and Malae, Sionia, Steelsong and Sigil for herbalism, research, and invention. Put together, this seems to be a shrine that serves two purposes, or two groups: hunters, warriors and beast wranglers looking for skill and protection, and scholars or inventors looking for guidance and inspiration.

Examining the shrine with a successful [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] notes that this shrine was used recently, within the last few days. The faint tang of burnt herbs lingering in the air. A small, half-empty flask sits conspicuously among the offerings, its cap removed, the liquid, blood, still fresh within. Someone, not long ago, paid a visit to this shrine.

Looking at the ground and making a successful [[/skill survival 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check reveals that the ground around the shrine bears fresh scuffs and footprints. These prints are only a few days old by the looks. Oddly they appear out of nowhere and vanish abruptly.

Characters looking over the footprints can glean a little info, and perhaps some extra.

You notice that there is a pretty well worn trail that the humanoid footprints are following. You are confident that you could follow this trail and they would likely lead you to their origin, or fairly close to it at least. The trail isn't new, so it likely hasn't been used in a while, but it's still clear enough to follow.

Tracking the Trails

A successful [[/skill survival 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] notes that there are humanoid and bipedal reptilian tracks all over this area. The oldest of the tracks are the booted humanoids who seem to have walked up and down the area more than once, likely examining it like you are now.

  • Success. The reptilian tracks are substantially newer, having cross through this area. They don't seem to have stayed for long before moving on in a totally different direction that the humanoid prints.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success You notice that there are some booted prints here that are far fresher than others, only a day or two old by the looks of them. Strangely, they just appear and disappear, having no clear entry or exit point. Either the person can fly, or they teleported in and out.

Examining the work area reveals that harvesting work was underway to take large pieces of the hide off the molt.

Sitting here in the darkness is a collection of dirty, rusted tools. Saws and shears left in the dirt, or laying on ragged scraps of hide. Alongside them are a few coils of frayed rope, the discarded ends of greater lengths.

Signs of Work

A successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check while examining the tools notes that they are all rusted and dulled, ill suited to the work being done with them. Their time sitting here on the ground has only worsened their condition, making them entirely useless now.

Characters skilled with Leather Working tools a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.tailorsToolkit00] or succeeding on a [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check recognize that the work to cut down sections of dragon hide were inexpertly done, leaving large sections of the hide ragged. Given the amount removed, it probably took a few days of work.

Examining the cuts in the hide with a successful [[/skill investigation 16]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 16]] check estimates that they took out probably fifty square feet of hide from the molt. This is a sizeable amount, and given how ragged the cuts were, it probably wasn't for use as a textile.

If characters want to harvest this rare resource, they can, and doing so is easy enough to accomplish if they have a sharp object and the proper skills. The tools on the ground are not suitable to this work, so the party will need to provide their own.

Harvesting The Skin

It is possible for characters with proper tools to harvest sections of the dragon skin for use later. Character proficient with and making a successful [[/skill survival 14 tool=leatherworker]] check [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] with a@UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.tailorsToolkit00] can collect one unit of @UUID[Item.WVX86Em0iiDYYTto]{Molted Dragon Skin}. This takes about half an hour to do, and there is enough good skin to collect up to 6 pieces of dragon skin if characters are willing to spend the time.

Characters without proper tools can make do with a sufficiently sharp cutting implement (such as a dagger or axe) but must make a successful [[/skill survival 16]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 16]] check to collect a unit of dragon skin. However, because the cuts are awkward, this damages the skin, reducing the available harvestable units to 3 max.

This skin is can be utilized by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.OGYBWQ543Pa241o1]{Gathering and Crafting} system to create unique items such as armor and accessories with special properties.

Concluding the Event

The party is now closer than ever to the origin of the Mutagists, even if they aren't entirely certain who it is they are chasing. From here they should have enough information to find the base of operations where these people are staging from.

Next Steps

So far the clues they should have run across are the journal in [[/eventState chain1Traps]], the knowledge from Kern gained from helping him with [[/eventState chain1Rescue]], and the trail found here by the skin. All together it should give them enough direction to find the Mutagist base and begin the [[/eventState chain1Laboratory]].
Impossible Skin.soverview: While exploring the ancient Pathways, Ankarist, and the party encounter the shed skin of a massive creature, a dragon.
Impossible Skin.sexposition:
As you proceed into the lair something astonishing emerges from the darkness —a colossal draconic visage frozen in time, its mighty scales ashen and ethereal in the muted glow. At first, terror threatens to grip you, until clarity reveals its truth: an immense, hollow shell, discarded and abandoned. It stretches across the chamber, lifeless yet horrible to behold.

Beside you, Ankarist steps forward, a rare glint of wonder illuminating his expression. He murmurs with a mixture of amazement and uncertainty:

It looks like a dragon, doesn't it? But I can't recall dragons ever shedding their skin. I wonder if we just never knew they did?

The lair is dead quiet, Ankarist's movements echoing off bare stone in the cavernous space. It seems that the vibrant life of the Pathways refuses to come into this place. Only luminous moss and slimes brazenly growing across the ceiling have dared to breach it, and now bath the scene in the faintest of blues and yellows.
Impossible Skin.ssummary: We encountered a truly massive shed skin of a dragon in the pathways, and found that we were not the only ones to take an interest in it.

Empty Laboratory.name: Empty Laboratory
Empty Laboratory.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration and combat event involves the party raiding a @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH]{Repurposed Quarry} that is serving as the home base for an arm of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]. In this event the party will need to:

  • Discover who the people here are, and what they goals are, uncovering the existence of the Mutagists.

  • Defeat the Mutagists and Drakes found in the location, so they don't escape to cause harm elsewhere.

  • Collect useful information from the various facilities and labs which can be used to further Ankarist's investigation.

Area Walkthrough

The party begins in the @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.9nqK1LJd8e8T4JHa]{Entry Tunnels}, which poses a hazard through its poisonous atmosphere. In addition, though the party has no way of knowing it, the Mutagists are in the process of destroying the lab to remove evidence of their actions.

Ankarist's Plan

Ankarist, eyes sharp and focused, looks toward you.

Seems the chaos has masked our arrival so far, but what could have them all riled up like this? We should take advantage of this while we can. If you've got any suggestions on what we do, now's the time to speak up.

What's your plan?

Ankarist grimaces slightly.

I don't really have one, to be honest. We need to collect any evidence we can get out hands on, and ideally not die in the process. I'm hoping that the chaos will help cover us, but I suspect fighting's inevitable.

What should we collect?

We need to secure anything that's useful to the investigation: documents, materials, reports, records, log books, journals, anything that we can use to learn more about this operation.

Are we sneaking in?

We can try, but given how chaotic things sound, I don't know who long we'll be able to keep it up. Still, getting the jump on the people inside will give us better odds. However, be ready to start moving fast if things fall apart completely.

Chaotic Approach

Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]], [[/path emberAnchoriteMarine]], [[/path emberFlameguardMilitia]], or [[/path emberImperialConscript]] know that the chaos ahead will mask their approach initially, and could let them get the jump on the first few encounters if they are careful about their approach. However, things could devolve quickly, leaving people out of position and exposed if they aren't careful to stick together.

Dangerous Environment

Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/path emberCrownApothecary]] recognize the scent of dangerous chemicals in the air, and suspect deadly hazards could be in play. Covering one's face would help avoid breathing in deadly fumes. It is likely they have such protective equipment inside the party can acquire on the go.

Are we taking prisoners?

Generally speaking I try not to kill people unless I absolutely have to, so, yes if we can. However, I recognize we're not really set up to take many prisoners, I have two pair of manacles on me, so I can use those. I'm sure we can scavenge some rope in there, if we need.

Entering The Lab

Refer to the Area Walkthrough for the @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH]{Repurposed Quarry} which contains this event's scene game play. After completing the area, return here.

Kalasak's Fate

With the lab cleared of hostiles, mark the outcome based on the fate of Kalasak the Cutter:

[[/outcome killed]]

Ragen Attunement: Kalasak Killed

If they party manages to slay Kalasak in combat, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 chain1LaboratoryKilled]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome captured]]

Cora Attunement: Kalasak Captured

If they party manages to capture Kalasak in combat, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 chain1LaboratoryCaptured]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome escaped]]

Abyss Attunement: Kalasak Escapes

If Kalasak escapes the party's clutches, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 chain1LaboratoryEscaped]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

With the lab scoured, its occupants defeated, captured, or routed, there is little more to do than wrap up, and head out.

Ankarist's Next Step

Ankarist is ready to return to Ordain to report to his superiors. What they've learned here in the lab complicates things substantially, but also gives them leads to follow. Before they can do that though, they need to find a way out of the Pathways, so that is his next plan of action.

In the interest of expediency, if the party has not already concluded that there must be a way back to the surface near the lab, Ankarist can point out:

We came a long way to get here, and by a route they occupants of this lab hadn't opened yet. That's a long way to bring supplies, and I didn't see any evidence of heavy traffic like we'd see from caravans or supply trains.

Given how well supplied this place was, there has to be a way to the surface nearby. Rather than retracing our steps out of here, let's see if we can find the entrance to the pathways the locals were using.

All that is left is for the party to return to the surface, and a convenient exit from the pathways exists near the quarry lab.

Milestone Progression

Completing this event (by shutting down the lab) awards a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone} point, potentially enabling the party to advance in level.

Next Steps

The party can return to the surface and continue the quest in the subsequent [[/eventState chain1Emergence]] event.

If, for some reason, the party insists on returning to Mythspire Observatory's base to travel to the surface instead, they risk missing the next event. Ankarist would advocate strongly for pressing on and heading directly to Ordain. If the party does backtrack, they may travel to Ordain via some other route, moving directly to [[/eventState chain1Hallows]].
Empty Laboratory.soverview: Ankarist and the party discover a long abandoned quarry nestled deep within the Pathways. Presently in the throes of being abandoned, the party must scramble to secure evidence and information before it's all destroyed.
Empty Laboratory.sexposition: This quarry is alive with frenetic hustle, with unintelligible voices echoing off the stone. The acrid tang of chemicals and smoke is thick in the air, pricking at your eyes and clinging to your clothes. The sounds of scrambling denizens come and go, punctuated with faint growls and keening roars of creatures.
Empty Laboratory.ssummary: We reached the underground laboratory where the drakes that attacked Helkas came from. We managed to secure some evidence of the operations, but the masterminds behind it escaped.

Grim Findings.name: Grim Findings
Grim Findings.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event occurs on a Vista scene depicting the Hallows area of Ordain. The characters to reconnect with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.dNRnUUfnB5gWCGKf]{Veiled Chain} at the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.ThsrAwMhXhmowirO]{The Hallows}, where they'll reveal what they've learned while traveling with @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}. In this event, the party can:

  • Meet important figures from the Veiled Chain, including @UUID[Actor.m7bwxaSeiblzYyJw], the leader of the Veiled Chain, and @UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb], a highly skilled mage, scholar, and ally of the Veiled Chain.

  • Lay out the evidence they've gathered, gain insights from other NPCs, and establish important social connections in Ordain.

  • Receive a reward for their efforts.

Formal Introductions

After an indeterminate stretch of time Ankarist finally reappears, his features apologetic as soon as he makes eye contact with you. Saying nothing, he leads in a trio whose presence feels painfully official.

In the group, a gray-skinned Fej with veins of blue embers simmering under their skin, and eyes to match. Behind them, a majestic Drakon whose purple horns sweep round his head, and wearing robes decorated with jewels and bronze fabric.

They all immediately settle into seats, and Ankarist facilitates introductions. He indicates the Fej first.

This is Shaar, head of the Veiled Chain.

Shaar offers a silent nod in recognition, but says nothing. Ankarist then gestures to the Drakon.

This is Serethus, fellow investigator and resident expert in mystical matters. Probably no better spellcaster in the city.

Serethus offers a wide, toothy smile and scoffs.

Certainly there are better, I am only remarkable because my skills and knowledge are accessible.

Shaar then breaks their silence.

So, let's speak about what you found in the pathways... we're going to go over our findings based on the evidence you recovered, and make sure this aligns with what you saw and observed. If you have anything to add, please don't hesitate to do so.

@Embed[Actor.m7bwxaSeiblzYyJw]

@Embed[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]

Discussing the Evidence

The following sections provide topics that Shaar, Ankarist and Serethus will discuss. The amount of information they have is based on the amount of information the party managed to recover from the underground lab. If the party wants to add their own insights and theories, they should be encouraged to, and Ankarist can be used to add onto those responses or correct false/wrong information.

Grading the Evidence

There are three grades the party's evidence collection can have: poor, good, and excellent, based on how much information they collected. The more evidence they have, the better a picture of events the Veiled Chain will have. There's a maximum of 18 points of evidence the party can collect, and they need 8 points of evidence to achieve "good" status, and 16 points of evidence reach "Excellent."

The following things contribute to their evidence score:

  • Gain +1 Evidence for each of the following items claimed from the Pathways scouts: @UUID[Item.IfkFvTVJMdqCOwF6]{Muddy Logbook}, @UUID[Item.7N5eUSASdq2PeO6t]{Scout Journal}, @UUID[Item.sig9x24pnisGbTaZ]{Alchemical Grenade}, @UUID[Item.5ySHUOLM0IgfNGlQ]{Pathways Scout Map}

  • Gain +1 Evidence if the party collected a unit of @UUID[Item.WVX86Em0iiDYYTto]{Molted Dragon Skin} from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100.JournalEntryPage.EdHIloOfkT9xTCwc]{Impossible Skin}.

  • Gain +1 Evidence for each of the following items taken from the laboratory: @UUID[Item.fg5P8yxtKHc0fUu1]{Mutagenic Formulae}, @UUID[Item.uA95T3HphxYWqXRA], @UUID[Item.TGq3jsR9CvUuO2db], @UUID[Item.Xuvr7CbdXZmLLaGJ] , @UUID[Item.fbER2KhZ438soBVy], @UUID[Item.b7tDeiRVqesPXrzC], @UUID[Item.q9PeGKDaP4NsAkEZ], @UUID[Item.3KVOnp7wj7vPJ18k], @UUID[Item.zfv8g0NUFtDKpmWL].

  • Gain +1 Evidence if they captured at least one @UUID[Actor.kxOh8R1rpCls67e8]{Mutagist Vivisector} or @UUID[Actor.6wPOcXeGsGN1uPBg]{Mutagist Bombardier} alive.

  • Gain +1 Evidence if they captured @UUID[Actor.FJFtoeSh014tPlJC] alive.

  • Gain +1 Evidence if they [[/eventState chain1Emergence studied]] where they emerged from the pathways.

Tally the party's evidence score, and then mark the appropriate outcome.

If the party's total evidence score is less than 8, they achieved Poor Evidence Collection.

[[/outcome poor]]

Abyss Attunement: Poor Evidence

If the party manages to collect very little useful evidence, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 chain1HallowsPoor]] at the conclusion of the event.

If the party's total evidence score is 8 or higher, they achieved Good Evidence Collection.

[[/outcome good]]

Aura Attunement: Good Evidence

If the party manages to collect a moderate amount of useful evidence, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 chain1HallowsGood]] at the conclusion of the event.

If the party's total evidence score is 14 or higher, they achieved Excellent Evidence Collection.

[[/outcome excellent]]

Mayis Attunement: Excellent Evidence

If the party manages to collect extensive useful evidence, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 chain1HallowsExcellent]] at the conclusion of the event.

Laboratory Findings

The following discussion pertains to the laboratory and what its purpose was.

What was the lab producing?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist glances at his notes and then says:

Far as we can determine, they were producing large amounts of alchemical compounds and shipping them to locations unknown. It clear they are part of a larger operation, but to what extent we're not clear.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist glances at his notes and then says:

Far as we can determine, they were developing mutagenic compounds and testing them on Drakes then shipping the tested compounds to locations unknown. It clear they are part of a larger operation, receiving regular shipments of base chemicals from somewhere, likely Ordain itself, along with Drakes to be experimented on.

Serethus nods, adding:

The volume of compound they were moving into that location is impressive, and doing so without anyone noticing is doubly impressive… the dire implications not withstanding, of course. Operating a lab of that size would not be inexpensive.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist glances at his notes and then says:

Looking at the recovered records, the lab was established so that Kalasak could fun experiments on drakes being shipped in from elsewhere, with the intention being to create a mutagen that made the drakes stronger and more resilience. They had some level of success, because they shipped finished mutagenic compounds and mediums right before we arrived.

Serethus nods, adding:

I should like to note that they are clearly part of a larger operation, as running such a large lab would come with considerable expenses. Zealots aside, they were receiving regular shipments of base chemicals from somewhere, likely Ordain itself, along with Drakes to be experimented on. The volume of compound they were moving into that location is impressive, and doing so without anyone noticing is doubly impressive… the dire implications not withstanding, of course.

Who was supplying the lab?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist nods at you.

Good question, we don't know, yet. We're assuming that the chemicals were coming out of Ordain, so we're going to start looking at smuggling and black market channels and see what shakes out.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist nods at you.

That's the key question. They clearly had someone funding their operation, and providing them materials. We have some chemicals and materials we can investigate for leads, but a lot of this is going to end up being us shaking down local smugglers and black market operators to see what falls out.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist taps a folder.

The answer to that is in the evidence we recovered. We have lists of names, chemical shipments, and contacts that are related to supplying the lab. With that information in-hand we can start following specific leads and seeing what connections exist. Without that evidence we would have been stuck shaking down local smuggling rings, which rarely goes well.

One name we have which stands out is a figured known as "Professor Bleak" who seems to be in charge of operations on a grander level. If we can figure out who they are, we can unravel everything else.

Why were they shutting the lab down?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Shaar says:

They were either tipped off that someone was coming, or they completed their work.

Ankarist nods.

I think the timing was coincidental, but we're not sure about why the lab was being scuttled.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Shaar says:

It seems as though they completed their work, and the timing with your arrival was purely coincidental.

Ankarist nods.

I think that's correct, and documents recovered indicate they were shipping large volumes of materials out of the lab just prior to scrapping everything.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Shaar says:

They completed their work, and were destroying the evidence. It's possible they knew you were coming, but more likely the timing was purely coincidental.

Ankarist nods.

Correct, as far as I can tell. They were shipping large volumes of materials out of the lab just prior to scrapping everything. Kalasak was ordered to scrap the lab and destroy anything that wasn't being shipped out by his superior, someone named "Professor Bleak" whom we're looking into.

Sadly we don't know who or where they are, or where everything was sent, but we are looking into it.

Mutagist Findings

The following questions specifically cover the Mutagists as a faction, and what their aims are.

Who are the Mutagists?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist lets out an exasperated sigh, his frustration clear.

The short answer is: a threat. They appear to be a collection of absolutely amoral healers and alchemists that have dedicated themselves to a line of unethical pursuits to achieve well… we're not sure. The scale and complexity of the operation in the lab we found hints they are very well funded. Sadly we just don't know anything else right now.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist casts a grim glance down at his notes, then looks back at you.

The short answer? A threat. They are a well connected, well funded, and worryingly clandestine network of amoral scholars and alchemists that have dedicated themselves to a line of unethical pursuits to create a new breed of drakes for some unclear reason.

This was only one part of a much larger operation, and one that seemingly established under our noses without anyone being the wiser.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist casts a glance at his papers then fixes his eyes on you.

Given all the documents you and I recovered, we know they are a well connected, well funded, clandestine network of scholars and alchemists that have dedicated themselves to the breeding and enhancement of a new line of drakes, possibly as weapons, or as part of some larger scheme.

We know they are headed by a figure known as "Professor Bleak" though this is an assumed name. The lab we found was only a small part of a much larger operation, and we have strong suspicions there's another lab in Ordain itself, but don't know where… yet.

Who do the Mutagists work for?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Serethus offers a shrug and an unhelpful statement of:

Who's to say? Perhaps nobody. They seem to be a bunch of crackpots working in a pit.

Ankarist interjects, countering with:

Given the scale of support they had with incoming supplies? Doesn't seem small.

Serethus smiles, the expression somewhat patronizing.

As an alchemist I can tell you that bulk chemicals are cheap, and you can always pay someone to leave a wagon somewhere if you pay them well enough. We simply lack any evidence that this is bigger than the lab you found.

Shaar cuts in:

I believe Serethus is right, to an extent, they clearly have allies, but until we have evidence of that, we can't say to what extent. Not yet, at least.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Serethus offer a contemplative hum at the question, then says:

They may not work for anyone, but there are certainly no shortages of bodies to join their cause. I know far too many frustrated academics, and frustratingly amoral alchemists than I like to admit, and someone offering them a chance to work unbidden would be quite tempting.

Ankarist adds:

Given the level of supply in that lab, it's safe to assume they have no shortage of allies in the area, likely in Ordain itself. We have some files and evidence that can hopefully help us track down names, and hopefully find a source of their funding.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Serethus offer a contemplative hum at the question, then says:

Well, there is this "Professor Bleak" figure, whom Kalasak answered to. Seems that they are the one calling the shots and deciding what gets done. However, I don't know anyone by that name in any of my circles.

Ankarist adds:

That's my thinking, yes, we need to find this Professor Bleak figure, they are almost certainly head of this organization. Also, given what we found in that lab, they clearly have a sizable operation under their control. We need to find threads to pull, and see if we can unravel the tapestry. Luckily, we have files with names and suppliers which hopefully help us track down names, and hopefully find a source of their funding.

Ankarist nods at that, clawed fingers stroking his jaw.

That is most fortunate, and I have to admit I'm morbidly curious about who your turn up in your investigation. I know a great many of frustrated academics, and frustratingly amoral alchemists.

Someone offering them a chance to work unbidden would be quite tempting, especially since many of them end up ostracized from more mainstream scholarly organizations, or chafing badly by the confines they are forced to work within.

Drake Findings

Shaar will also want to know about the Drakes. They just had an attack on Helkas, and it's possible there may be more in the future, so they want to know what kind of monsters they are dealing with.

What are the drakes?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist answers that:

As far as we can tell they are offshoots of vile dragons, we have no idea if they are naturally occurring or not.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist answers that:

As far as we can tell they are offshoots of vile dragons, probably the one whose molt we found in the pathways. It's unclear if they are migrating into the region from elsewhere, or were always present and are just now emerging, or how many there are.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist answers that:

As far as we can tell they are offshoots of vile dragons, probably the one whose molt we found in the pathways. Documents from the labs indicate they were being bred for the lab's use. So they aren't natural to this region, but if they are present now we can expect them to crop up more. We're planning to send out warnings to locals.

Serethus adds:

Rather fascinating, isn't it? The creation of an entirely new species of creature based on another. I believe only Ember itself has done such a thing before.

Ankarist frowns at that.

I'd find it more interesting if they weren't attacking settlements.

Serethus clears his throat.

Well yes of course, goes without saying.

Where did the drakes come from?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist speaks up first:

The short answer is: the lab in the quarry. It's unclear if they were being trapped in the pathways, or grown, but they were certainly being contained and experimented on there, and likely escaped. However, there's no record of these drakes in the region up to this point, so they may have been introduced from elsewhere, or might be newly spawned.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist says:

Initially it seemed like they were being trapped in the Pathways, but evidence suggests they were being brought in from some external location to be experimented on. The precise location is unknown, but it's clear they aren't naturally occurring in the pathways.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist says:

Evidence points to the Drakes being a bred or engineered sub-type of vile dragons, likely spawned from material taken from the molted dragon skin we found in the pathways. They were being shipped in from elsewhere, extensively studied and tested by the personnel in the quarry lab, then released into the wild.

Why are the drakes ill?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Serethus clears his throat and says:

Well, that's quite simple actually! They were being injected with alchemical solutions of varying designs and compositions for some unspecified reason. This was causing them to go blind, develop wounds and pustules and so forth.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Serethus speaks up, saying:

Rather straightforward answer, that: The drakes were undergoing extensive mutagenic treatment, seemingly to correct some inborn issue with them, or to enhance them. This was causing them to go blind, develop wounds and pustules and so forth, since the mutagenic compounds were all experimental and highly toxic. However, it does seem they achieved success eventually.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Serethus speaks up:

Rather fascinating answer for that, actually! It seems that the Drakes have inborn maladies and weaknesses that leave them physically weaker and malformed, possibly related to the process by which they are spawned.

Given findings in the laboratory, it seems that the rather extensive testing being done there was aimed at enhancing their physical prowess and resilience.

This had been going on for months, and that early versions of the mutagen were causing outright death in the earlier subjects, and they only recently stabilized the formula before you arrived.

Why did the drakes attack Helkas?

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Ankarist shrugs slightly.

Their presence alongside the raiders seems like nothing more than good timing. We're not sure why, beyond possibly just being an animal attack.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Shaar speculates:

Given the lab was releasing drakes into the wild, it seems plausible to me that Helkas was attacked simply because the Dusktide Festival drew their attention. They don't seem to be connected to the raiders at all.

With [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] the collected investigators have the following insights:

Shaar breaks their silence:

To see how the creatures perform, nothing more, nothing less. There might have been other ulterior motives, or other agendas with the Otherhood raiders, but for this lab's part, it was just to see how effective they were. It's possible these are intended to be weapons in the long term for their own operations, or to be given out to allies, such as the raiders.

Concluding the Meeting

Shaar looks to Ankarist and says:

I think we can conclude this debriefing, Ankarist. See to it that rewards are handed out for the assistance, and then follow up on the leads we discussed previously.

Ankarist nods at Shaar.

Absolutely will do, Shaar.

Shaar offers a faint smile to Ankarist, which is then directed to you.

Thank you for your assistance in this. If the Chain has further need of you, we will be in contact. Be well.

With that, Shaar lingers only long enough to collect goodbyes from you and Serethus, and then leaves. A moment later Serethus speaks up, saying:

I should take my leave as well, cunning and wisdom guide you, friends.

In short order you are left with Ankarist, who says:

Like Shaar said: thank you for the help. I don't know that I could have done it without your assistance. As for reward, I'm going to have someone pay you some gold on your way out. It might not be much, but I'd rather you not leave entirely empty handed.

Will you need more help?

Ankarist lets out a small laugh.

Probably, yeah. I don't need your help right this moment, so you should go spend your reward money, see Ordain, relax a bit. If something comes up, and I expect it will, I'll reach out and we'll get back into the field.

If the party achieved [[/eventState chain1Hallows poor]] they receive a [[/award 100gp]].

If the party achieved [[/eventState chain1Hallows good]] they receive a [[/award 250gp]].

If the party achieved [[/eventState chain1Hallows excellent]] they receive a [[/award 500gp]].

Concluding the Event

After the party has left the Veiled Chain offices they are once more free to pursue whatever interests they have.

Milestone Progression

Completing this event awards a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone} point, potentially enabling the party to advance in level.

Subsequent Quests

This event concludes the "Ancient Paths" quest, but Anakrist and the Mutagists will return during Chapter 3 with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness} quest.
Grim Findings.soverview: Ankarist reports back to the Veiled Chain in the Hallows district of Ordain, sharing the discovery of the nefarious Mutagists, and learning that this isn't the only threat faced by the city.
Grim Findings.sexposition:
The Hallows bustle with an energy that is simultaneously invigorating and laden with expectancy. Ushered through several halls featuring vibrant murals of life within Ordain you are eventually lead to a far more subdued space. Simple chairs and a singular wood table with the symbol of Ordain in the center sits below a broad tapestry depicting the city as it would have looked four hundred years ago.

Before leaving you there Ankarist tells you:

I've got to alert my superiors, but I'll be back shortly with them, and we'll get your account of things.

As you sit here, time marches on, longer perhaps than you might have expected to wait. You can hear movement and discussion outside the meeting space, but none of it meant for you, not yet.
Grim Findings.ssummary: We reported our findings on the underground lab to the Veiled Chain and attended an extensive debriefing with Ankarist, the Chain's leader Shaar, and one of their allies, Serethus. Our evidence has been officially filed, and we were rewarded for our efforts.

Mapping the Myth.name: Mapping the Myth
Mapping the Myth.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event focuses on an encounter with the pawnbroker @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann}, who is a long-time contact and associate of Ankarist. In this event, the party can:

  • Learn about current events in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush}, including its local quest @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death}.

  • Learn about a passage into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} via the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.RWj91gQguWOQcflB]{Mythspire Observatory}.

  • Learn a bit about how Liestra and Ankarist know each other.

Meeting Liestra

Leaned against the wall of the consignment shop is a towering Kivahr woman who immediately notes your presence. She tucks a jeweler's loupe and a trinket into a pocket, and pushes off the wall, coming up to her full height.

Well, well, well, look who it is! You Veiled Chain really do know about everything, don't you?

Ankarist looks to be at a loss momentarily, which Liestra catches. She grunts, and gestures to her shop, pushing the door open.

Let's chat inside.

Liestra is not without manners, and will go around learning everyone's name, showing them around the shop, and asking a few questions of them and Ankarist. In return she offers a bit about herself.

@Embed[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]

Polite Company

Liestra is keen to find out where everyone is from, and how they came to meet their mutual pal Ankarist. She's also happy to share details about herself, and the story about how she met the investigator. Ankarist, however, would like to focus on the task at hand.

Reading Liestra

A successfull [[/skill insight 15]][[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check or a character with the [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/knowledge crime]] knowledge suspects that while Liestra is large of frame there is a certain deviousness to her. She is more capable of subtlety than she appears, and hides it behind plenty of bluster.

How did you meet Ankarist?

I met the good inspector in Ordain, got into a bit of trouble and needed a hand. He was right there to save the day and get me out of a tight spot. Turns out I do not have the lithe frame of a burglar!

Ankarist clarifies:

You were attempting to steal items from the Lorando Collection and got caught. Not exactly the most auspicious beginning for a friendship. All I did was make sure you got a fair hearing.

Liestra takes the story a bit further:

Lot more than that, Ankarist, and you know it. If you weren't a good man, you'd have taken that wannabe merchant-lord's offer to look the other way while he killed me for breaking into his manor. I'm actually glad you caught me and took me to the Hallows. I wouldn't bet on most in the Chain being so upright as you.

Ankarist offers a faint, dissenting grumble but says nothing as Liestra wraps up:

Anyway, after that I got out of Ordain, and ended up here in Skybrush. Been running this pawnbroker for years now, and mostly deal in local artifacts found by Anachraenum passing through. Specialty is Shent artifacts, which I ship off to a couple collectors in the region. Those are my real money source these days, everything else is small time.

Scanning the Long Haul

A successful [[/skill perception 14]][[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check or having the [[/knowledge artifacts]] knowledge reveals that most of the free-standing items around the Long Haul seem like unremarkable, but practical, wares. A mix of salvaged and some newer-looking items. You do spot, however, several items artifacts around the store, but a subset of them which are secured away behind a locked display case.

  • A further [[/skill history 15]][[/skillCheck society 15]] confirms that these items are of Shent origin, and their people populated this region in ancient times. Magically and technologically sophisticated, their relics and artifacts could certainly be valuable to collectors or researchers.

Getting Liestra's Help

Ankarist wants to know about a way into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}, and suspects that Liestra knows of one. She absolutely does, and is happy to share that information, though it does come with a request first.

Ankarist looks between you and Liestra, then clears his throat before speaking.

I really would like to find the way to the Pathways, and I suspect that's the sort of thing you have information on. Would I be correct in that suspicion?

Liestra flashes a quick smile at that.

You would be, yes, but I'm not going to make getting the info easy.

Ankarist's expression sours ever so slightly, though he doesn't look surprised. Liestra continues:

You know me Ankarist, I'm happy to provide you information, always am. But this time I've got a condition: I want you to help Skybrush resolve its current problems. It's why I thought you were here in the first place.

Ankarist's brows rise at that, not quite surprised, but certainly not expecting that answer. He goes to open his mouth, but Liestra doesn't let him speak, instead she seems to predict his response:

Look, I just don't like how messy things have gotten in town. The current chaos is bad for business, and, besides, this is my home now, Ankarist. I don't like seeing the locals turning on each other. They're good people up here, and they might end up doing things they regret. I want things to go back to normal.

Ankarist lifts his hands, half in defeat, half in a soothing gesture to Liestra. His tone is softened a touch, betraying some genuine care for a friend.

I understand. You don't need to convince me, Liestra. Besides, on the way in I noticed things felt off. What can you tell us about the situation?

Liestra's shoulder relax, her relief palpable.

Well, the short and long of it is that there's been some murders in the town. Nasty ones too. One of the victims was pregnant, which is just… awful. So, naturally everybody's up in arms and wanting justice.

You know, Ankarist, I'd wager that Constable Valaston could use the help of an actual Veiled Chain investigator. Poor bastard's barely barely holding things together right now.

Local Law

Characters with the path of [[/knowledge politics]] suspect that the constable in a frontier town like this is capable of enforcing local law and dispensing justice, but perhaps out of their depth when it comes to a complex murder investigation.

Where should we start looking?

I recommend talking to some of the other locals who probably know the latest news. I've been keeping busy here lately, so I don't know everything going on. Hit up The Roost and talk to the regulars there, guaranteed well of gossip those bunch.

In fact, if you're sticking around, why don't we all head over to The Roost together? We can throw a few back and you can "interrogate" the locals!

Changing Quests

Once the party has met with Liestra, the party may choose to investigate the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death} first, at her request. This is a side quest that is set primarily within Skybrush.

If the party chooses to do this, you can mark this event complete and begin the @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death} events. Once that quest is complete, you'll want to return to this one to continue with Liestra's Directions below.

Ankarist's Interest

Generally speaking, Ankarist favors doing this first, as he does not like the idea of leaving a murder unsolved, especially if the locals need help which he can offer.

If the party is not yet at least level 3, you may wish to strongly suggest the party investigate this side quest before continuing onward.

Liestra's Directions

Where There Is A Way

If the party helped Skybrush resolve its issues ([[/eventState brushWithDeathAftermath]]) or someone makes a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]], [[/skill intimidation 15]] or [[/skill deception 17]][[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]], [[/skillCheck intimidation 15]] or [[/skillCheck deception 17]] check to convince or coerce Liestra into coughing up the location, she will reveal the presence of Mythspire Observatory. Though if the party does use intimidation, Ankarist will intervene if they are particularly aggressive or threatening.

Coercion and Consequence

If the Party uses intimidation, but were not explicitly threatening of violence, after they have left the shop Ankarist will take them aside for a gruff expression of distaste for their choice of approach:

Are you proud of how you handled that? Not only was that unnecessary, you risked the investigation. Did it occur to you that your act of coercion might have just made her shut down?

Ankarist won't belabor the issue, though, merely express his disappointment before trudging on toward their destination.

If they were particularly threatening, Ankarist intervenes — but doesn't hesitate to take advantage of the opportunity to exploit the coercion.

"That's not necessary. I want to pursue this as much as you, but this isn't the way to do it."

Turning his face toward Liestra, Ankarist proffers a simple but direct: "Sorry, Liestra," before turning back toward the party and adding "She doesn't need to be threatened— she knows as well as anyone that some people might construe her refusal to assist us as impeding our investigation. I am sure she doesn't want to end up on the wrong side of this."

While Ankarist wouldn't have chosen intimidation, successfully pursuing his quarry is foremost in his mind, and if his connection to Liestra is already hurt by the act of coercion he may as well be sure to get the information he's after by redirecting the party's successful threat.

Liestra says the following about the Mythspire:

Liestra moves to a shelf, and shifts a few scrolls aside before grabbing a larger roll of parchment.

You know… it's passing into peculiar that you aren't the first group I've provided these directions to recently. What is the sudden fascination everyone has with Mythspire?

Liestra lays out the parchment, unfurling a map of the local area as Ankarist cocks his head slightly at her question.

I'm investing something that caught my attention. Why, have others been asking about it?

Liestra weighs the map down with a couple items nearby, and then looks at Ankarist.

Yeah, I recently helped a group of Anachraenum explorers find the location… that was only a few weeks ago, in fact. Said they were trying to map entrances or something. Weird bunch, never did come back. Not that I was expecting them to. But yeah, two groups in as many weeks.

She taps the map.

Anyway, it's right around here, six miles northeast of here. Aim for the highest peak in that direction, you can't miss it. Be prepared though, a creature inhabits that ancient ruin, an ancient guardian of sorts.

It's not aggressive, just weird. It asked me lots of questions about myself and the outside world, why I was poking around the ruins, so on. I don't think it's dangerous, but it's very old, and was not used to visitors. So my advice would be to tread cautiously when you get there.

Hearing about the Mythspire, the party may know a thing or two about it.

Unraveling the Myth

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill history 15]][[/skillCheck society 15]] check have heard legend of the Mythspire, an ancient Shent ruin somewhere in the Wedgelands. However, its location was never confirmed, and nobody looking for it ever came back.

An [[/skill arcana 16]][[/skillCheck arcana 16]] check suggests that if the location was Observatory it would be built somewhere with an unobstructed view of the night sky and that it would likely be upon a summit that stands solitary from, or higher than, other neighboring peaks.

If the party wants to ask about the previous group of adventurers, they can. Though Liestra doesn't know it, these were a group of scouts attached to the very group that Ankarist and the party are out here chasing.

Previous Party

If asking Liestra about the party that came through town, or asking locals, it's possible to glean some small pieces of information. A successful [[/skill investigation 13]][[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] check reveals the following information. Liestra recalls more clues the better the party rolls on this check:

  • Success. They smelled ununsual like a tannery. The odor was noticeably unpleasant to be around. They were curt but not rude, it was clear they were in a hurry and focused on getting up into the mountains fast.

  • Critical Success. They were traveling light for an Anachraenum expedition, and didn't really go into detail about what they were doing. Liestra offered them to resupply before their journey and they declined, despite seeming to have few supplies. One of their company had badly stained and damaged hands that looked as if they had been burned or scarred with pock-marked flesh. A character with [[/path emberCrownApothecary]] realizes that Liestra's description sounds like a sort of chemical burn.
