  • Success. They smelled ununsual like a tannery. The odor was noticeably unpleasant to be around. They were curt but not rude, it was clear they were in a hurry and focused on getting up into the mountains fast.

  • Critical Success. They were traveling light for an Anachraenum expedition, and didn't really go into detail about what they were doing. Liestra offered them to resupply before their journey and they declined, despite seeming to have few supplies. One of their company had badly stained and damaged hands that looked as if they had been burned or scarred with pock-marked flesh. A character with [[/path emberCrownApothecary]] realizes that Liestra's description sounds like a sort of chemical burn.

Luxarum Attunement: Directions to Mythspire

If the party manages to obtain directions to Mythspire Observatory via their dealings with Liestra Grann, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 chain1MapDirections]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished socializing and gathering information they can depart the Long Haul and decide what to do next.

Related Quests

Before continuing on, the party may choose to investigate the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death}, a side quest that is set primarily within Skybrush. Generally speaking, Ankarist favors doing this first, as he does not like the idea of leaving a murder unsolved, especially if the locals need help which he can offer.

If the party is not yet at least level 3, you may wish to strongly suggest the party investigate this side quest before continuing onward.

Next Steps

Once the party has gotten the directions from Liestra, mark the "Directions to Mythspire" outcome complete. From that point on the party can head directly onwards towards @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.JcGOyaCzImvAie1Z]{Mythspire Observatory}, located 6 miles north east of Skybrush in ⬢ s.3195.2889. This quest continues in [[/eventState chain1Guardian]].
Mapping the Myth.soverview: Ankarist and the party arrive at the remote hamlet of Skybrush to track down a contact, Liestra Grann, a Kivahr antiquities dealer who may know the location of Mythspire.
Mapping the Myth.sexposition:
As Skybrush moves past you, the scarce few denizens out on the streets watch you warily. Paying them no mind, Ankarist leads you onward until you pass into a quieter section of the settlement. There he turns to you, his brow is furrowed with concern:

Something seems off here. While I'd never describe Skybrush as a lively or welcoming as town, the people aren't usually this avoidant. We need to ask Liestra about this. We'll find her at the Long Haul, which is just up this way.

With that, he continues with a determined stride, leading you to a modest, yet well-kept building adorned with a weathered wooden sign that reads "The Long Haul" as promised.
Mapping the Myth.ssummary: We met up with Ankarist's contact Liestra in Skybrush. She helped point us toward a possibly entry to the Pathways: toward the Mythspire Observatory in the mountains. However she asked us to look into the local troubles in return.

Emergence.name: Emergence
Emergence.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event allows the party to interact with a powerful illusory aura. Characters that resist the effect are able to study it, learning that it was put in place to ward off the area from intruders. This event occurs on the region map without a specific area map or vista to depict it. In this event, the party can:

  • Confront the fear caused by the arcane mirage over this place.

  • Examine the spellcraft for clues.

  • Discuss next steps with @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}.

Urge To Flee

This area is blanketed in a powerful illusion spell that incites unease and fear in anyone that enters it. The party is not immune to this effect, and must make saves to resist it.

Malignant Aura

As soon as the party begins this event and steps foot in the quarry they need to make a [[/save wisdom 14]] saving throw or become &reference[frightened] @Condition[frightened] and unwilling to explore the area. Sensing that something horrible happened here, they are compelling to make their way out quickly.

On a successful save, however, they realize that the fear is stemming from a magical source. Upon realizing this, the sensation fades, as does the horrifying nature of the plants and trees. In truth, the area is just abandoned and overgrown, but not inherently befouled.

Fleeing the Site

If the entire party fails their saves, or the party decides to leave without investigating the site, they can speak to Ankarist in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100.JournalEntryPage.prpxzrAkwJ89HGz4#where-to-now?]{Where to Now?} section after having retreated to a safe area just beyond the site (the party token doesn't need to move, as the hex encompasses an area far larger than the quarry itself). Should the party decide to return to the site to explore it, they will need to make saves again.

Rallying Your Allies

It is unlikely that the entire party will succeed on their save, and some characters will be overwhelmed by a desire to flee. Characters that succeed on their saving throw can attempt to rally their friends, telling them the effect isn't real. When they do this, they can repeat their saving throw, possibly seeing through the illusion.

Characters that have succeeded on their save to resist the aura can attempt to examine the area and identify the nature of the effect, though there is not much to learn.

Magical Examination

Walking around the area and making a successful [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] locates several large flat stones that have been carved with illusion magic symbols. They are likely radiating the magic that makes up the effect, and they are laid out around the collapsed mine's perimeter.

Examining the stones with a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]]check determines some key elements about these warding stones:

  • Success They are all part of a larger spell that is generating a powerful illusory aura that affects anyone entering the area. The warding effect is a mixture of the exceptionally powerful @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.f38w5rd9SgdmWc6F]{Mirage Arcane} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.GJ2WYm3SQFR0winH]{Antipathy/Sympathy} spells, creating an area that is uniquely unnerving to everyone that enters it. This would require an exceptionally skilled spell caster to create.

  • Result of 18+ The warding is built in a specific way to exclude a number of people. You suspect that the crew working in the lab in the pathways were able to come and go freely without being overrun with the area's magical fear effect.

  • Success They are all part of a larger spell that is generating a powerful illusory aura that affects anyone entering the area. The warding effect is a mixture of the exceptionally powerful Illusion magic designed to create an area that is uniquely unnerving to everyone that enters it. This would require an exceptionally skilled spell caster to create.

  • Critical Success The warding is built in a specific way to exclude a number of people. You suspect that the crew working in the lab in the pathways were able to come and go freely without being overrun with the area's magical fear effect.

Characters that cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} and have the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] talent can examine the area and find that it has been warded with a powerful illusion spell the creates not only the illusory terrain, but the aura of unease. It is an exceptionally powerful spell. The energy for the area is spilling out of numerous warded stones around the collapsed mine's perimeter.

Casters that use @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.Mzh95utKDPIrjiH8]{Detect Evil and Good} will note that this region has not been magically consecrated or desecrated. Rather, whatever the effect is here is, it's not divine, or the work of someone wielding divine magic. It's a false sensation of evil, and a very convincing one at that.

Casters skilled with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeSoul00000000]] or [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeOblivion0000]] will note that this region has not been magically affected with any sort of consecrating or desecrating forces. Rather, whatever effect is here, it is not divine, or the work of someone wielding divine or abyssal magic. It's a false sensation of evil, and a very convincing one at that.

Powerful Illusions

While there is no way for the party to learn who cast this spell, as the gamemaster you should be aware that @UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]{Serethus}, the secret head of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]{Mutagist} cabal, placed a series of powerful spells on the area to ward off curious parties, prospectors, and adventurers that might investigate the site and locate the hidden entrance to the Pathways, and with it, the underground lab.

Where To Now?

Once the part is done with the collapsed mine, whether they fled it, or studied it and then left on their own, they will need to decide what to do next. Luckily, Ankarist has a plan. He wants to head back to Ordain and report in, and wants the party to come with.

Onward to Ordain

Ankarist wants to report in to his superiors at the Hallows in Ordain. They've learned a lot on this journey, and he needs to get it into the hands of his team so they can put more people to work investigating the issue.

More importantly, Ankarist wants the party to come with him and share what they've seen and done with the Veiled Chain. That way his report will have extra weight, and they can get this case taken seriously from the get-go.

What are you planning to do next?

Well, I need to transport all of the evidence we collected from this site back to my people at the Veiled Chain. From there, I start the long process of figuring out what it all means, finding new leads to follow, and mapping out connections in the evidence.

However… we will need to reach the surface again first. So let's focus on that.

If the party completed the [[/eventState chain1Laboratory captured]] outcome then Ankarist adds:

I also need to get our captive back to the Veiled Chain offices so that he can be properly questioned about what his people were doing here.

Will we be paid for helping you?

Of course, I'll make sure that the Veiled Chain rewards you for assisting in a dangerous operation. I'm not sure how much it'll be exactly, but I'll make sure your help is recognized and compensated. We'll have to get to Ordain first, though.

What do you think was happening in the lab?

They were clearly experimenting on the drakes, but I'm not sure to what end, as alchemy is a bit beyond me. The Chain has alchemists and scholars it can call on who should be able to lend better insight into the evidence than I can, though.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished talking to Ankarist, they can move on.

Next Steps

The party now needs to head for Ordain, head for the Hallows, and report to Ankarist's superiors in the Veiled Chain in the [[/eventState chain1Hallows]].
Emergence.soverview: Ankarist and the party emerge from the Mythspire Pathways back into the Arctus Plateau at the outskirts of the Bloodwoods north of Ordain.
Emergence.sexposition:
As you navigate the rise out of the Pathways the air grows lighter and the strange, rhythmic sounds of the unseen creatures fade behind you. Eventually, you find yourselves at the mouth of the cavern, stepping onto the rough-hewn steps that spiral upward, guiding you towards the surface.

The path is littered with rubble and half-drowned in creeping mosses, and gives way to a desolate mining pit that yawns beneath a dreary sky. The pit's perimeter is fringed with broken lift pulleys, and rusting rail tracks snake haphazardly around deep scars carved into the earth. Once industrious, the land now lies abandoned, claimed by gnarled vines of black wood lined with serrated thorns, and skeletal trees whose naked branches claw at the dark sky.

Yet, it's not the silence and unseemly growth that unnerves you — it’s the oppressive aura that hangs heavy over the pit, a palpable malignance that settles like mist along the jagged terrain. A lingering intuition warns of danger as if unseen eyes observe your every move, waiting, watching. The air itself to hum with a sinister resonance, tickling more primitive parts of your mind that beg you to run for safety.
Emergence.ssummary: We emerged from the Pathways into the dilapidated and collapsed ruins of an old stone quarry. The site was shrouded in a dreadful and forbidding aura. We departed the site with Ankarist, who is intent to return to Ordain.

Crackpot in the Caves.name: Crackpot in the Caves
Crackpot in the Caves.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event allows the party to interact with the ancient and eccentric Kern, a powerful druid who lives down here in the Pathways. This event is depicted in the "Overgrowth" composition of @UUID[Scene.emberVistaPathMT]{Vista: Mycelian Expanse}. The party here can:

  • Attempt to get information out of @UUID[Actor.0nC7b7MaX6OLbjoR]{Kern}.

  • Take on a request from Kern to deal with some local @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.tLSBe3kfPlvqmnH2]{Jurtak} thieves and save his "friend"

  • Learn about his "friends" @UUID[Item.TZ7nKfZrAhT7qY96]{Kryz} which is actually just an inanimate crystal, and @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B]{Big Liz} which is actually a gargantuan lizard living nearby, though Kern won't portray either as such.

The Gamemaster should be aware that Kern is an immensely powerful druid who does not behave in a way that might suggest that to the party at this time. To Kern, the party (and the Jurtak, and indeed the Baradom) are truly not a threat and his interactions with them should be somewhat obtuse and playful. Kern is peaceful because he is powerful enough that he can choose to be.

Who?

@Embed[Actor.0nC7b7MaX6OLbjoR]

The old thornling sweeps his little mushroom walking stick through the air, causing a large curtain of glowing ivy to reshape itself into a door way. Inside it is a warmly lit home built into a natural cave.

He gestures for you to come along, as he quickly heads inside and begins setting a table which appears to be made from a large, flat-capped mushroom. On that table is an array of cups shaped from hardened mushrooms, and and pot of pungent tea.

Come over, sit down, drink tea!

He pours himself a cup, the earthy smell of boiled mushrooms hitting you immediately.

Just One Cup

Kern treats the party like they are old friends, and Kern will be insulted if at least one person doesn't drink tea with him. The tea is awful, comprised on bitter leaves and chunks of dried mushroom. It tastes like sour dirt and mold, yet the aftertaste is somehow worse, and doesn't improve with time. Kern doesn't seem the least bit bothered by the flavor.

A character can suppress any natural, reflexive reaction to the horrible taste of the tea by making a successful [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check or [[/save con 12]] saving throw suffer the effects of [[/hazard 4 poison fortitude morale]]{Disagreeable Brew} after they drink it. This can be counted as a poison for the purposes of claiming advantage on the save.

From here on out the party can speak with Kern, possibly learning about him, and getting a quest to rescue a friend in need.

Speaking to Kern

Kern is very egotistical, and likes gifts and being given respect. He expects that everybody knows who he is, and that his legendary status as a druid has reached every corner of Ember. Naturally, nobody in the party has ever heard of Kern, but that doesn't prevent the party from lying.

As long as the party doesn't insult Kern, and acts like he is as important as he thinks, Kern will remain friendly and cooperative.

Befriending Kern

Despite the ego and oddness of Kern, he is a truly powerful druid that would be a useful ally to have later on. It is possible to befriend Kern a handful of ways, and doing so is wise.

  • Playing into Kern's ego, and pretending he is a mighty and famed druid, being polite, humoring him, and being sociable goes a long way to earning Kern's support.

  • Helping Kern rescue his friend when he requests the party's help contributes immensely to getting on Kern's good side, especially if the party carries out the rescue without raising any issues with the details about it.

Kern's Knowledge

  • Kern is happy to warn the part of "creepies" lurking in the darkness with their sharp weapons and hungry jaws. Attempting to coax more information from Kern reveals that these are the "Jurtak" a large group of wandering hunters that kill and eat anything that's not a plant.

  • Kern also alludes to the "nasties" which have been seen in the pathways, long, wormy lizards that can fly, and are covered in boils. He says they are sick and he's never seen one last very long. If asked, he doesn't know where they come from (Note: this is a lie).

Kern is unwilling to share everything he knows with people who aren't his friends, and friends have tea together, he believes.

Who are you?

Kern replies immediately with:

I told you: Kern!

Ankarist issues a soft sigh.

Yes, but, we don't know who you are beyond your name.

Kern scoffs loudly.

Everyone knows who Kern is! Legendary Kern, greatest of them all.

Ankarist asks:

Greatest of who specifically?

Kern grows briefly serious and leans in conspiratorially and speaks quietly:

All've 'em.

What are you doing down here?

Livin'! At least when I remember to.

I've forgotten a time or two, took me a bit to remember again.

He points his walking stick your way.

Don't forget if you can avoid it!

What's in this tea?

It's a mix, buncha things that won't kill you, mostly. I could make a nicer tea, but only once.

Self Neutralizing Poison

Characters making a successful [[/skill nature 14]] or [[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] or [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] check suspect that this tea is a blend that is both poison and antitoxin, making it safe to consume if preserved right. Kern is either a master herbalist, or the luckiest thornling in the Pathways.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Kern's Troubles

After the party has spent some time talking to Kern, he will decide it's time to foist a mission upon them.

Kern raises the dainty mushroom cup to his brambly lips, inhaling the acrid aroma coming from it. He takes a sip, swishing the tea thoughtfully before savoring the taste with a content sigh. But quickly, his demeanor changes, grave and reflective, as though the very memory weighs down his shoulders.

It's a cruel world sometimes, isn't it?

He muses, swirling the tea in his cup.

Imagine this: just out for a delightful walk, minding our own legendary business, when my good friend, another druid of extraordinary repute, finds himself swiped away by the creepies. Such nerve they have!

What are creepies?

Those scaled hunters, the creepies, they creep around the caves and act creepy, and look creepy. If you saw them you'd say 'those must be creepies' and you'd be right!

He points a knobby finger at you.

The creepies are very aggressive and mean, if you see them, you should kill them on sight. Nobody will miss them, except the other creepies, who might want revenge, but if you can kill one, you can kill more than one!

Kern places the cup down, eyes narrowing with determination. Then, as if struck by a brilliant idea, he leans forward.

But you, yes, you marvelous adventurers, why… you could come to the rescue! Picture it: immortal, unkillable, but definitely needing a hand, my friend gets rescued by you! It could be the grandest tale of all! And who better to lend a hand than those hand picked by the equally mighty and probably immortal Kern?

With an expectant smile, Kern waits for the group to realize the grand opportunity he's offering. Ankarist hesitant speaks up, skepticism evident in his voice:

I don't know… your friend sounds like they are fine, and you're clearly powerful enough to handle this adventure on your own. We really should get back to our search…

Kern nods once, though it doesn't seem like he's listening, as he cuts in immediately:

Oh, well, of course a favor for one such as me, aside from being quite the feather in your caps would also come with a reward! I happen to know where to find the big dragon in the tunnels, and where all the little nasties like it are coming from.

He waggles the big, leafy brows of his and Ankarist utters an annoyed groan, realizing that Kern actually has useful info.

What Is Actually Going On Here?

Kern is being intentionally obtuse, likely because he's not entirely all there, but possibly because he's just messing with the party. Regardless, here's the plain situation:

  • Kern's friend "Kryz" is a large crystal that is important to Kern. Why is unclear, but the ancient Druid wants it back, and has also projected a personality on it. As stated above, Kern might not be all there anymore (if he ever was).

  • This crystal was stolen by local Jurtak, and while searching for it, Kern made contact with "Big Liz" which is actually a very large, very old @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B]{Baradom}. Kern is able to speak with her via druidic powers the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] talent, she is not otherwise capable of speech.

  • At some point Big Liz actually ate the thief that stole the crystal, and has since excreted their remains (and the crystal). A group of Jurtak are presently in and around her den looking for it. While Kern is more then capable of dealing with a bunch of Jurtak, he is lazy and wants to see how the Party handles themselves.

What happened?

Kern clucks disapproving.

It was terrible. My friend Kyrz was captured by the creepies while I was out on a walk. He lives with me, by the way. Used to live in a cave, but got tired of being alone. Anyway, they came with their bone weapons and mouths full of teeth, raided my home, and ran off with Kryz!

Who is your friend?

Kryz! A powerful, immortal, ancient and reputable druid just like me!

If Kryz is so powerful, do they need help?

Well, you see, Kryz is a softy and wouldn't lift a finger to harm others. Not even big, awful creepies.

Where do we find your friend?

They ran off toward Big Liz's place. Of course Big Liz has been complaining about the creepies hanging around her home lately, setting traps and being annoying. They won't leave her alone, and probably have some nasty little den nearby or something. You should search around there.

I even asked her if she'd seen Kryz recently, and you know what she told me? She said that they were dragging Kryz around while out harvesting their traps near her place.

I can give you directions when you leave.

Who is Big Liz?

Well, Big Liz is big, first of all, obviously.

Second of all, she is one of my oldest friends. She might even be older than me! Maybe. I'm not sure.

Either way, third of all, Big Liz likes to be left alone.

The party isn't required to go rescue Kryz, but, Ankarist acknowledges that Kern my have useful knowledge, and Kryz might be a bit easier to work with.

Concluding the Event

The party needs to decide if they want to help Kern and go rescue his friend, or if they want to continue on their own.

Next Steps

If they choose to assist Kern and rescue Krys, they can proceed to [[/eventState chain1Rescue]].

If the party has already encountered the Jurtak trap clearing in the [[/eventState chain1Traps]] event, they may have enough information to find the Mutagist lab already, otherwise, this might prove their best option to move forward.
Crackpot in the Caves.soverview: As the party explores the Pathways, they encounter a wizened and extremely aged Thornling named Kern. He is a particularly eccentric character who can be quite helpful if the party handles him correctly.
Crackpot in the Caves.sexposition:
As your group navigates the vastness of the Pathways, you begin to notice an odd rustling and faint chortling behind you. Ankarist, with a mixture of wary annoyance signals for everyone to halt. His eyes, sharp and discerning, scan the shadows.

We can hear you, you know.

His voice booms out, cutting through the harmonious murmurs of unseen creatures, causing them to still briefly. In that silence a voice responds with unexpected honesty:

No ya can't! Wait—dammit!

The contradiction catches Ankarist off-guard, his brow furrowing in confusion, and replies:

Okay, well, now we know for certain you're there, and I don't like being followed. Come on out and make yourself known.

With a resigned huff out steps a small, bushy figure, a thornling who was utterly indistinguishable from his surroundings just a moment ago.

Looking from face to face you can tell the wizened thornling is waiting for recognition to set in. When it becomes clear that none of you know who he is, he throws his gnarled arms out and declares:

It's me, Kern!
Crackpot in the Caves.ssummary: We met a truly strange and wizened thornling named Kern down in the pathways. Kern asked us to recover his friend Kryz who was abducted by some aggressive wandering hunters.

Cruel Traps.name: Cruel Traps
Cruel Traps.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event the party stumbles upon a patch of traps, and find the most recent victims of them. These victims belong to the group they are chasing, and will provide further clues. This event is played on the "Trapped Clearing" composition of @UUID[Scene.emberVistaPathMT]{Vista: Mycelian Expanse} where the players can visualize and investigate the area and its potential hazards. In this event, the party can:

  • Investigate the traps and corpses.

  • Examine the area surrounding the killing grounds.

  • Discover a @UUID[Item.7N5eUSASdq2PeO6t] among the remains of the scouts caught in the traps.

Drawing closer, you see a huge ten-legged reptile trapped within the massive iron jaws of some horrible trap. Its body is limp and beginning to rot. All round it are other signs of death, rotting carcasses now more bone than beast, and the remnants of traps sprung, the victims missing.

Close by lay two dead humanoids, their bodies badly wounded and stripped of their equipment, which is strewn about them both. Their blood has been spilled, the deep red a stark contrast against the otherwise blue tones of the Pathways.

Each of the bodies is held in place by the teeth of steel traps previously hidden in the brush. Ankarist utters a grim sound as he surveys the scene.

Best not to assume there aren't more traps, I don't want to get caught in whatever killed those two.

He gestures to the two humanoids.

But I do want to get a look at them.

The party can choose to hang back, or accompany Ankarist into the area. The investigator moves slowly and carefully, avoiding any traps underfoot, but is single-minded and doesn't call them out to the party if they come with, expecting them to fend for themselves.

Dangerous Ground

There are still numerous active traps in this area that are expertly hidden, and the party should take care to avoid them. Characters with a [[/skill perception 16 passive]] automatically spot the snares and traps before stepping on them.

Otherwise, characters that are actively looking for more traps as they move must make a successful [[/skill perception 14]] check to avoid running into one and triggering it. Characters that fail this check (or don't watch their step) suffer [[/damage 2d4 piercing]] damage as the trap goes off, driving metal teeth into their leg and rendering them &reference[restrained] until released.

A successful [[/check str 15]] is necessary to extract a character from a trap. Each failed check deals 2 piercing damage to the trapped creature. Sprung traps can also be dismantled with appropriate tools (see Disarming Traps below).

There are still numerous active traps in this area that are expertly hidden, and the party should take care to avoid them. Characters with a [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] automatically spot the snares and traps before stepping on them.

Otherwise, characters that are actively looking for more traps as they move must make a successful [[/skillCheck perception 14]] check to avoid running into one and triggering it. Characters that fail this check (or don't watch their step) suffer [[/damage 2d4 piercing]] damage as the trap goes off, driving metal teeth into their leg and rendering them @Condition[restrained] until released.

A successful [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] check is necessary to extract a character from a trap. Each failed check causes the trapped victim to suffer the trap's [[/hazard 2 fortitude health piercing]]{Sharp Teeth}. Sprung traps can also be dismantled with appropriate tools (see Disarming Traps below).

Characters that spot the traps may attempt to disarm them. Doing so is not without risk, but if successful, disables the traps in the area, and nullifies the above hazard.

Disarming Traps

The traps can be disarmed in a number of ways, and takes some time to accomplish.

The most difficult way is without any tools, making a [[/skill sleightofhand 17]] [[/skillCheck stealth 17]] check. However, characters with proper tools and associated proficiency can do the work much more easily.

A successful [[/skill sleightofhand 15 tool=thief]] or [[/skill sleightofhand 15 tool=tinker]] check while using said tools is sufficient to clear the traps quickly and somewhat easily.

A successful [[/skillCheck stealth 15]] or [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check can be made to use a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.disarmingToolkit] while using said tools is sufficient to clear the traps quickly and somewhat easily.

Failure on any of these checks results in one of the traps triggering while the character is working, potentially injuring the character doing the work. If someone is already a victim of the trap, this risk is negated. See the above hazard section for how to resolve a triggered trap.

No matter the method, successfully clearing all the traps yields four @UUID[Item.Ivc8UplVymXNZTne]{Sharp Hunting Traps}. These traps are much heavier, and far more dangerous than typical hunting traps.

Examining the Area

Caught in the Traps

Investigating the bodies yields the following information:

  • With a Successful a [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check, it is apparent that the lizard creature was killed by the trap. It looks like it has been dead for quite some time, and aside from struggling in vain to extract itself from the rusty teeth of the trap, was otherwise left alone.

  • With a Successful a [[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] check, The bones of numerous unidentifiable creatures lay scattered around this area, some of them showing signs of being scavenged, others butchered by crude weapons.

  • With a Successful a [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check,The two humanoid corpses look like they were stripped of their equipment, and violently attacked. However, a good portion of their belongings remain piled nearby, including some vials and a @UUID[Item.7N5eUSASdq2PeO6t].

Characters will want to examine the journal, as will Ankarist. It will yield them useful information about the two dead men, and what they were doing, confirming the presence of some sort of base or working area in the Pathways. This is a major clue that Ankarist is looking for.

Examining the Journal

The journal belongs to one of the dead men, and suffered some damage due to the natural moisture in the environment, causing much of the ink to run. However, many passages remain legible.

The last page is scribbled with shaky writing and reads:

Damn the jurtak. They came and moved our traps, set them specially for us. I told Kalasak that they wouldn't tolerate us poaching their kills and messing with their hunting grounds. We could've just let them alone, but no, Kalasak had to be right, didn't he? Tell Kalasak I told him so.

Well now Erd's dead, and I can't stand on my leg. I'm sure those accursed lizard men will be along soon, and if the bleeding doesn't get me, they will.

I hope they choke on my guts.

Tracking the Poachers

The journals detail this particular team and their patterns. There is one immediate takeaway anyone reading the journal can immediately pick up on:

  • The journal gives a basic rundown of the direction the pair will take, a map of trap locations that this particular team would rotate through. Using this, it's possibly to work out where the scout teams were coming from: They have a camp somewhere several miles southeast of here, on the other side of the bridge.

With this, the party can figure out the path the pair of dead men took to get here, which in turn lets them figure out how to backtrack to where they came from. It's not a precise location, but it will get them close!

No roll is required to decipher the path the poachers took. The party or Ankarist simply needs to take a few minutes examining the journal to get a feel for their travel patterns and work out where to go next.

Journal in Detail

The party may want to dig into the journal further, and they are free to do so, though it will take some dedicated reading time to parse through all the entries and pull out anything of value. It's not something they can do with a single skill check or action, rather, it should be done during downtime.

Journal Deep Dive

If a character spends some time poring over the journal during a long rest Rest, they can glean some additional information from the pages:

  • The scout teams are coming out and setting traps to catch local animals, then taking them back to a camp somewhere beyond the "great bridge." Why isn't explicitly stated, but they've been doing it for quite some time, and there's some indication it was for food.

  • Some of the teams were actively poaching Jurtak hunting grounds and trapped spaces as well, making sure to avoid taking game that died from the Jurtak poison. There was some fear that poisoned carcasses were making the drakes sick.

  • Sporadic entries detail work in a lab of some sort, meetings with someone named Kalasak. It references pens, creatures, feeding schedules, alchemical handling notes, and more, all centered around developing and testing some formula called "the mutagen."

  • There are numerous entries present that complain about being sent to collect materials and animals by the lab director. It seems that the author strongly objected to sending lab personnel out to collect animals, and argued for the scout teams to take that work on themselves to avoid anyone dying unnecessarily.

The party may also want to examine the dead and their belongings, they can do this if they like, collecting a few insights for their time.

Investigating the Remains

A successful [[/skill sleightofhand 17]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check to survey the area yields the presence of an @UUID[Item.sig9x24pnisGbTaZ]{Alchemical Grenade}, a ,@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potion of Healing} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rallyingElixir00] and an assortment of coins. Also, if not already examined, a @UUID[Item.7N5eUSASdq2PeO6t] lies nearby.

  • The @UUID[Item.sig9x24pnisGbTaZ] matches remnants of glass and brass spotted in the Mythspire Observatory, and was possibly what was used to badly wound the guardian there. It seems to contain a viscous chemical under pressure.

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potion of Healing} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rallyingElixir00] is only notable because its maker's mark shows it was made in Ordain. There appear to have been two other potions as well, but they were smashed at some point and it's impossible to learn more about them.

  • The coin is spread out across two coin purses, amounting to [[/award 5gp 128sp 35cp]]

  • If the party now examines the journal, see the above exploration entry of the same name to find out what it contains.

A successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] while examining the scene leads one to believe that whoever raided the corpses, these Jurtak, were only interested in simple, useful items: rations, material, armor, weapons. They left behind money and potions, perhaps having no use for them, or not understanding their value.

A successful [[/skill medicine 13]] [[/skillCheck medicine 13]] check while examining the bodies reveals that the deer-like creature was undisturbed, the fungal snake was carved up after death, as were both men.

In particular, the postmortem wounds on the men were to remove large chunks of muscle and several organs. The cutting was fast and crude, and makes it look like they were butchered for food.

A successful [[/skill survival 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] examination against the traps reveals that they would have been nearly impossible to spot if you didn't have some warning of their presence.

The party may confer with Ankarist if they like, he has the following to say about the traps and dead scouts:

Ankarist grimaces at the scene.

I don't want to be too glib about this, but, these people agitating the Jurtak ended up being a boon for us. With the journal we should be able to figure out where these scouts came from. This will either give us more leads to follow, or if we're lucky, lead us to the source of these scouts.

Either way, we should get moving, if only to avoid being here when the Jurtak come to check on their traps.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished examining the camp, they can continue exploring. The party simply needs to continue on their way through the tunnels, now guided by the journal of the dead harvester. Ankarist remains with them, eager to get to the bottom of this mystery.

Next Steps

If they have not already, the party can gather more clues in [[/eventState chain1Scouts]], and [[/eventState chain1Thornling]] which they may discover while exploring the area.
Cruel Traps.soverview: The players discover a small clearing within the Pathways’ foliage, lined with dangerous traps. The remains of several creatures in this area provide useful information, and a lucky break in Ankarist's investigation.
Cruel Traps.sexposition:
As you venture deeper into the cavern, the ethereal luminescence of the leaves casts shifting shadows across the floor. It reveals a grim tableau just beyond a thick cluster of gigantic stalks. From your vantage point, you can see what appears to be a killing ground where numerous creatures were recently slain. This patch of the cavern is eerily silent, as though the dreadful scene has stilled even the air.

Ankarist's focus immediately sharpens, and he moves toward the bodies.

Let's have a look, but stay sharp. Last thing we want is to get jumped by whatever did the killing.
Cruel Traps.ssummary: We found two dead bodies in some very deadly traps while exploring the Pathways. A journal on the bodies gave us a lead toward their home base. Ankarist wants to head that way next.

Rocky Rescue.name: Rocky Rescue
Rocky Rescue.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event sees the party engaging in a skirmish with a band of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.tLSBe3kfPlvqmnH2]{Jurtak} warriors and hunters who were responsible for kidnapping @UUID[Actor.0nC7b7MaX6OLbjoR]{Kern}'s friend named Kryz. In this event the party will do the following:

  • Do battle with a group of Jurtak, possibly getting the drop on them as they agitate a massive @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B] in its den.

  • Recover Kern's friend "Kryz", which turns out to be a large, once-magical crystal of unknown origin. With it, the party can decide to return it to Kern for info, or keep it for themselves.

  • Receive information from Kern about recent events in the area, and points of interest that may be relevant to the party's investigation in the Pathways.

@embed[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B]

@embed[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd count=2]

@embed[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud count=4]

Examining the Situation

If the party wants to examine the massive Baradom and the Jurtak messing with it, they certainly can. Events won't begin to unfold immediately, so the party has a brief window to size up both sides of the brewing conflict.

The Baradom

This is almost certainly "Big Liz" that Kern mentioned, in fact it's probably short for "Big Lizard," which is extremely fitting. This creature is absolutely gargantuan and covered in armor thick enough to ward off siege engines.

A successful [[/skill nature 16]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 16]] check allows a character to know a bit about the nature of the Baradom based on the result.

  • Result of 16+. The character knows about the Baradom's behavior as provided by the creature's biography section.

  • Result of 18+. The character has knowledge of the Baradom's behavior and lore as provided by the creature's biography section.

  • Success. The character knows about the Baradom's behavior as provided by the creature's biography section.

  • Critical Success. The character knows about the Baradom's behavior and lore as as provided by the creature's biography section.

Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.aL1F8fvYLtNzUbKu]{Speak with Animals}Using the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] talent allows the caster to communicate with the Baradom. It confirms that it knows Kern, that it is called "Big Liz" by him, and is a she. She prefers to be left alone, but sometimes Kern brings food, so he gets a pass.

The Jurtak

Examining the Jurtak before combat begins may yield some insight into them and their tactics. A successful [[/skill nature 16]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 16]] check allows a character to get a sense for the Jurtak based on the result.

  • Result of 16+. The character recognizes that the Jurtak are being bold in their actions with the Baradom, but are likely to scatter the moment it moves to defend itself.

  • Result of 18+. The character has knowledge of the Jurtak's general behavior as provided by the creature's biography section.

  • Success. The character recognizes that the Jurtak are being bold in their actions with the Baradom, but are likely to scatter the moment it moves to defend itself.

  • Critical Success. The character has knowledge of the Jurtak's general behavior as provided by the creature's biography section.

The Jurtak are curious creatures, sleek, intimidating, monstrous, but still humanoid. Up to this point the party has likely never encountered the Jurtak before, and they remain something of a mystery.

A successful [[/skill history 16]] [[/skillCheck society 16]] check allows a character to know a bit about the history of the Jurtak based on the result.

  • Success. The character knows about the Jurtak have been a growing danger in the Pathways for as long as history has been recorded about the underground passages. They don't really have a society of any kind, no government, no known settlements, no written or spoken language of any kind. They are organized and intelligent however, just utterly hostile to anything in their path.

  • Result of 18+. The character knows that there is speculation that they might have been part of a larger society that was partially destroyed in the shattering. These remnants of the original people are completely unwilling to interact with other peoples or cultures in a peaceful way. All attempts to make contact with them as ended in disaster. Why this is remains a mystery.

  • Success. The character knows about the Jurtak have been a growing danger in the Pathways for as long as history has been recorded about the underground passages. They don't really have a society of any kind, no government, no known settlements, no written or spoken language of any kind. They are organized and intelligent however, just utterly hostile to anything in their path.

  • Critical Success. There is speculation that they might have been part of a larger society that was partially destroyed in the shattering. These remnants of the original people are completely unwilling to interact with other peoples or cultures in a peaceful way. All attempts to make contact with them as ended in disaster. Why this is remains a mystery.

Fighting the Jurtak

If the party attacks the Jurtak, or after a few minutes of watching the Jurtak harass the Baradom, it takes offense and begins to defend itself. Narrate the following:

Finally having had enough of the prodding and poking, the creature utters a deep, rumbling growl, and begins to shift. Great muscles muscle tense and ripple under its heavy plates as it looms to its full, imposing height. Some of the jurtak fall back, but a few brazen warriors stand their ground, menacing it with spears and lobbing javelins to no effect.

In response the armored beast lunges forward, knocking over one of the jurtak, then spins, whipping the other with a massive tail. Before either jurtak can manage to rise the gargantuan beast crushes one with a slam of its armored head, then snaps up the other in its huge jaws.

The few remaining Jurtak look on warily while the creature chews on the jurtak in its jaws. The sound of the jurtak's bones snapping and crunching echo off the nearby stone. The remaining hunters and warriors hiss at the one digging through the piles of dung, seemingly urging them to work faster.

A moment later there's a joyous hiss as Jurtak pries free a large, ominously glowing crystal. Wiping the muck from the gem the Jurtak holds it aloft for the others to see. As they do this you note that it has... a primitive face painted upon its gleaming surface.

Ankarist lets out a frustrated groan.

Kryz. As in Kryz-tal. We're saving his pet rock.

The sound of Ankarist's voice causes the remaining Jurtak to turn and fix their many predatory eyes on you. It's at this moment the gargantuan creature charges both the Jurtak and you, sick of interlopers in its den!

Encounter Overview

The fight consists of four @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]{Jurtak Warriors} and two @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd]{Jurtak Hunters} and one @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B]{Baradom}. When the encounter begins, select one of the Jurtak to carry @UUID[Item.TZ7nKfZrAhT7qY96]{Kryz}. This should be the priority target for the party, since if they escape, so, seemingly does their hope of recovering the crystal.

Baradom Tactics

While the Jurtak are immediately hostile, the Baradom is a neutral combatant, only attacking creatures that get within 10 feet of it. It uses its @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B.Item.uOUMciIcoRPUaR0s]{Bite}, @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B.Item.i1DUN4J0I0SEdhZS]{Tail}, and @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B.Item.3hAh2udSD9RZ7FUg]{Headbutt} attacks against any creatures that are in reach, and uses its @UUID[Actor.GQdcb1RP9JquOC6B.Item.eZS1qRdxtb8WBWBx]{Gnash} on grappled enemies.

Note that the Baradom is immune to most kinds of mundane damage, and very likely cannot be harmed during this fight. It should be treated more as an environmental hazard than a full combatant, attacking any creatures that end their turn too close to it, or which attack it.

Jurtak Tactics

The Jurtak Warriors fight by hurling their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.4IcLr9x1vwEaz7JS]{Crude Javelins} while closing distance. Once in close range they use their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.TIJUbDlyqjxfKyrH]{Wicked Pikes}. If enemies bunch up, and the ability is charged, they'll use their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.WewF6d4OX0PjEE2j]{Acid Spit} to hit multiple enemies.

The Jurtak Hunters fight from a distance, using their @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.PR4gST1hHcztH2wO]{Grotesque Longbows} to rain arrows down on foes, ideally from high ground. If engaged in close combat, they can use their @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.wpOzOHCF1MjHKNrE]{Claw} until they can get free. If it's charged, they will use their @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.n69PG3VfnsGk06Fu]{Lunging Assault} against foes, especially if cornered or when a nearby enemy appears especially vulnerable to attack.

All Jurtak start combat with their first weapon attack coated in their @UUID[Item.qrzBBvBtYQa1AT0n]{Jurtak Poison}. They reapply it before attacking if they can spare the action to do so, and aren't being engaged by combatants in close range.

The Jurtak Warriors fight by hurling their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.4IcLr9x1vwEaz7JS]{Crude Javelins} before equipping their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.TIJUbDlyqjxfKyrH]{Wicked Pikes} while closing distance. Once in close range they rely on their pikes and the extended reach those pikes grant to full effect. If enemies bunch up they'll use their @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud.Item.acidSpit00000000]{Acid Spit} to hit multiple enemies.

The Jurtak Hunters fight from a distance, using their @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.PR4gST1hHcztH2wO]{Grotesque Longbows} to rain arrows down on foes, ideally from high ground. If engaged in close combat, they will @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.Uru5KAdSUxlY8j7u]{Bite} and @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.ed4om1cGLz4ZOZkc]{Claw} and until they can get free. If it's available, they will use their @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd.Item.lightWeaponTrain]{Lunge} against foes, especially if cornered or when a nearby enemy appears especially vulnerable to attack.

All Jurtak start combat with their first weapon attack coated in @UUID[Item.qrzBBvBtYQa1AT0n]{Jurtak Poison}. They reapply it before attacking if they can spare the action to do so, and aren't being engaged by combatants in close range.

If @Condition[broken] or @Condition[weakened] the Jurtak will break and flee. If the Jurtak carrying Kryz is still alive and successfully flees, the party cannot recover the crystal.

If the Jurtak carrying the crystal manages to flee from the battle, narrate the following:

With the red crystal raised triumphantly over its head, the Jurtak bolts around the edge of a rocky outcropping, disappearing from view. With it goes any hope of recovering Kern's friend. In the distance there is a faint scuffling sound, and a shriek abruptly cut short. All that remains is to finish up here and find Kern to deliver the bad news.

From this point onward the party's only remaining goal is to defeat the Jurtak.

Kern Still Wins

Unbeknownst to the party, Kern arrived while they engaged the Jurtak in order to be on hand when Krys was recovered. While the Jurtak prepared to escape, he positioned himself in a place that would require it to flee past him and unceremoniously rendered the Jurtak unconscious as it ran past, reclaiming the crystal.

Rescuing Kryz

Once the Jurtak are defeated, assuming the the party can recover @UUID[Item.TZ7nKfZrAhT7qY96]{Kryz}, and examine it, as well as examine the dead Jurtak, if they want to.

[[/outcome rescued]]

Examining Kryz

Kryz is obviously a large crystal with a face painted on it. It is gently glowing with some inner light or energy, and the crystal is warm to the touch.

With a successful [[/skill arcana 17]] [[/skillCheck arcana 17]] check you know that it's not uncommon for crystals to be found that hold magic stemming from Ember itself. This could be a powerful source of magic for the old druid, and why they want it back. Alternatively, it's a vessel for magic, or, maybe more worryingly, a soul. Perhaps Kryz is trapped within?

On a successful [[/skill history 17]] [[/skillCheck society 17]] check you know legends and stories tell of powerful crystals from the heart of Ember. These crystals were used to turn mortals into gods. It is possible, albeit slim, that this is one such crystal. This raises perhaps a more concerning notion: is Kern a new shard god?

With a successful [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 17]] check you know that Ember produces powerful crystals full of life and creation magic strong enough to shape the world and make gods. While there's no way to tell if this is one such crystal, it does seem to match the pattern.

Examination Via Magic

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} reveals that the gem is radiating weak magic of every school in equal measure.

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify} reveals that this crystal is thousands of years old and holds powerful creation magic from Ember itself. However its potential power has greatly diminished and it is worthless.

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} has no effect on the crystal.

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} reveals no presence of mind or thought in the crystal.

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.W4Qx5z0id6da0vqg]{Legend Lore} conjures an image of a much younger Kern painting a face on the crystal. You sense this was long, long ago, hundreds of years ago. In the vision the gem glowed much brighter.

  • Characters with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] can thoroughly examine the crystal during a Rest to determine that while the gem is radiating magic energy of varying kinds, the energy is very weak and has likely long been depleted past the point of worth.

  • Use of @Spell[control.sense] or @Spell[soul.sense] quickly determines that there is no presence of any consciousness within the crystal.

  • Any attempts to use [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.counterspell0000]] automatically fail.

  • A capable [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.enchantingJourne]] or [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeweavingJourn]] knows that this type of crystal is thousands of years old and holds powerful creation magic from Ember itself. However its potential power is greatly diminished and it is worthless.

Looting the dead Jurtak doesn't yield much. Their weapons, while dangerous, are crude and meant for their hands. Only someone desperate would want to utilize them. They have no monetary value at all.

Returning To Kern

Returning the Kern is very simple, as Kern will be nearby waiting for them! As far as the party should be able to discern, the old druid simply followed them. How he did so unseen is a question that will remain unanswered, but Kern is immensely powerful, so it would not have been difficult for him.

If the party has not [[/eventState chain1Rescue rescued]] because the Jurtak with the crystal escaped, narrate the following:

You spot Kern sitting nearby, safely removed from the skirmish, but still able to watch it. In his hands is a large crystal with a face painted onto its facets. Kern is carefully rubbing the crystal with a piece of cloth, and sitting at the old druid's feel is the body of a Jurtak, the very one that ran off with the crystal.

It was a good thing I was here, you almost lost Kryz! Luckily we make a very good team, and I used your distraction to execute my expert rescue plan and save Kryz.

Shame you didn't save Kryz, because I'd have given you information, and boy-oh-boy do I know things now!

Convincing Kern

If the party wants to convince Kern that they helped with the rescue and as a result deserve information, they can do so with either a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] or [[/skill deception 14]] check. Doing so causes Kern to treat the party as though they successfully saved and returned Kryz, allowing them to proceed to "Getting Information From Kern."

If the party [[/eventState chain1Rescue rescued]] and chooses to return Kryz to Kern, set the following outcome:

[[/outcome returned]]

If the party is stubborn and refuses to return Kryz, Ankarist speaks up:

Ankarist pinches the bridge of his nose, his voice and posture betraying his growing frustration with this diversion.

Can we just hand over the crystal? I don't want to waste any more time arguing with Kern, or wasting our collective time here. I'd rather we hand over the thing and move on. We've got bigger things to deal with, and this diversion has only cost us time.

Kern nods in silent agreement, and gestures for you to hand over Kryz.

Keeping Kryz

If the party wants to keep Kryz, they can convince Kern with either a successful [[/skill persuasion 18]] or [[/skill deception 18]] check. If successful, read the following text:

Kern's scraggly, overgrown brow scrunches up in consternation, but after a moment he sighs and says:

All right, fine, sure, yes, okay, whatever, you can keep Kryz with you. Honestly, some time apart would be good for us. I don't like having freeloaders in my home anyhow, and Kryz certainly isn't doing anything to help there.

Just make sure you take good care of Kryz, with daily polishing, and no keeping them in a sack like some common gem. Consider buying a velvet lined box, so they can travel like an uncommon gem!

Kern dabs his eye with a woody knuckle, becoming wistful as he stares at the crystal.

And you come back and visit, okay?

He look at you.

You can come back too, though. If you bring Kryz. Now go before I get too sad and lonely and then die from that loneliness and you have to spend all day digging a grave to bury me!

From this point on the party may keep @UUID[Item.TZ7nKfZrAhT7qY96]{Kryz}, and can continue on their way. However, because Kryz was not returned to Kern, he will refuse to share any knowledge he has.

If the party [[/eventState chain1Rescue returned]] to Kern, narrate the following:

Kern throws his hands up, rustling noisily as he does.

Kryz, you're safe!

Kern's enthusiasm to see his "friend" again dampens sharply when he sees the state of the crystal.

Oh wow, and covered in crap. Well… it's good to see you again regardless.

He turns his attention to you.

You have my thanks! I knew you were the right picks to rescue my dear friend! In return I'll tell you what I know. You know, now, not what I didn't know before you saved ole Kryz. Because I didn't know anything then.

I do know now, though.

Ya know how it is!

Ankarist makes a low, exasperated sound, but says nothing.

Getting Info from Kern

If the party

From here the party can learn some useful information about the local Mutagists, which Kern calls the "nasties," not to be confused with the "creepies" which are the Jurtak.

Kern sits on a rock with a sigh, and rests his walking stick over knobby knees.

There's a big bunch of nasties living in an hold in the ground. The hole used to belong to other people long ago, but they left, and the nasties just came in and took over.

The nasties released those sick snake dragons, too. Or… maybe they escaped? I am not sure, but I am sure that they look like the big dragon that used to live down here. Smaller, of course, but just as mean.

Anyway, you want to head into the north-eastern corner of the pathways around here, look for the old hole in the dirt where old people took rocks, but now nasties do their business.

Who are the nasties?

Don't know. They got all them goggles and bottles and things, and I don't let them see me. They live in the hole where the snake-dragon things are coming from. They are nasty and cruel to creatures here.

What do you know about the snake dragons?

They looked real sick every time I saw them. All covered in wounds and dripping pus all the time out of bubbles and boils.

Kern wretches slightly.

Terrible creatures. They always died quickly, which is sad. Seemed like they were in pain the whole time. The Nasties would come and pick up their bodies, drag them back to the hole.

At first they died fast, but after a while they took longer to die and didn't seem so sick.

What do you know about the old dragon?

That one was big, and mean and awful. I don't know anything about it except that it lived in a hole. I always stayed well away from it, and made sure it never saw me. I might be invincible, immortal, and all-powerful, but I don't want to get swallowed alive by a dragon.

Anyhow, it eventually left, no idea where it went or why, and I'm just fine with that!

Cora Attunement: Returning Kryz

If the party manages to return "Kryz" to Kern, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 chain1RescueReturn]] at the conclusion of the event.

Finders Keepers

If the party is stubborn and refuses to part with Kryz, Kern will do all he can to reason and intimidate the party to avoid combat breaking out.

For his part, Ankarist doesn't want to waste any more time arguing with Kern, or wasting their collective time. He'd rather just hand over the crap-caked crystal and call it a day. They've got bigger things to deal with, after all.

If the party ignores this guidance, and gives Kern no other recourse, the druid will bring some very formidable magic and wild shapes to bear on the party. Though he won't kill the party, he's not above beating them unconscious and taking his "friend" if necessary.

Aura Attunement: Keeping Kryz

If the party chooses to keep "Kryz" for themselves, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 chain1RescueKeep]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party now has information enough to go directly to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.bfORKMRfuaOgMbUt] that holds the [[/eventState chain1Laboratory]] quest event. Though this location is anything but empty when they arrive.
Rocky Rescue.soverview: The party arrives at the last known location of the "creepies" (Jurtak) that kidnapped Kern's friend Kryz. They won't need to do much to save Kern's friend, but the encounter won't be what they are expecting.
Rocky Rescue.sexposition: As you navigate through the pathways the sound of muffled grunts and hisses lead you to a dim cavern. A group of Jurtak jab their bone-tipped spears into the thick, slumbering hide of a massive Baradom, their sharp eyes gleaming with anger. A little ways off, other Jurtak root around piles of rancid dung, dragging out discarded remnants and tossing them aside with disdain.
Rocky Rescue.ssummary: We found the Jurtak den where Kern's "friend" was taken. Turns out it was a large crystal with a face painted on it. We've recovered it, and returned it to the weird old druid. In return, they told us where to find the people we've been tracking down here.

Missing Scouts.name: Missing Scouts
Missing Scouts.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration and social event invites the characters to explore the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.FJNYRa0cGLlizwYY]{Mycelian Expanse}, where they'll discover a makeshift camp used by a group of @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F]{Mutagist Scouts}. Although unoccupied, this camp shows signs of recent use. In this event, the party can:

  • Investigate the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]{Mutagist} camp for details about the scouts that occupy it.

  • Find a map detailing other key events they could encounter in this area.

  • Encounter a group of Mutagist Scouts posing as members of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}.

  • Inadvertently alert the Mutagists to their investigation.

Investigating the Camp

Cold Camp

A successful [[/skill stealth 14]] [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] check leads you to believe that this camp was very specifically laid out to be hard to spot while traveling nearby trails. You're not even sure you could spot it from above unless you knew what you were looking for.

A successful use of the [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] skill notes the firepit still holds a few smoldering coals buried under the ash and burned fuel. While it's impossible to tell precisely how long ago the fire was used, it wasn't more than a day or two if the pit is still warm.

Examining the camp area with a successful [[/skill survival 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]]check finds numerous footprints belonging to a group that recently left.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success You can tell that there were 3-4 people in this camp, given the distinct gaits, boot shapes, and impressions they made.

A successful [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check notes that the camp has collections of fungal wood, plant fronds, bags of mushrooms and other edibles on offer.

  • Result of 18+ Critical SuccessThe amount of useful and edible materials here is far more than the camp occupants would need. They are likely collecting resources meant for another location.

Unattended Bags

The following items can be found in the camp:

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.f4w4GxBi0nYXmhX4]{Rations x 10}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.Gflnp29aEv5Lc1ZM]{Cook's Utensils}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.YwlHI3BVJapz4a3E]{Playing Cards Set}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.8NS6MSOdXtUqD7Ib]{Carpenter's Tools}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.H8YCd689ezlD26aT]{Backpack x 2}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.mQVYcHmMSoCUnBnM]{Bucket x 2}

  • @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rations000000000]{Rations x 10}

  • @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.cooksToolkit0000]{Cook's Toolkit}

  • @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.expandedToolbelt]{Expanded Toolbelt x2}

  • @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.fletchersToolkit]{Fletcher's Toolkit}

  • @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.travelJug0000000]{Travel Jug x2}

  • @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rope000000000000]{Rope x 4}

  • Two backpacks.

A Useful Map

Attached to one of the backpacks, sealed up in a protective case is a fairly detailed @UUID[Item.5ySHUOLM0IgfNGlQ]{Pathways Scout Map} of the immediate area. Along with the camp itself, this map details numerous locations in the area, and paths to or from them.

The scout map item description contains a number of locations that can be explored if the party choose to use it as a reference point.

Once the party has finished exploring the camp, or once some time has passed, continue to Returning Scouts below.

Returning Scouts

Laughter and voices cut through the air, followed by the sound of approaching footsteps. A quick glance in the direction of the noise reveals movement and several figures coming toward the camp.

Ankarist looks to you and silently gestures for you to indicate what the next move is.

@embed[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F count=6]

Hiding from the Scouts

The group needs to succeed on a [[/skill stealth 14]] [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] group check with at least half the party succeeding to avoid being spotted. If successful, the returning scouts remain unaware of the party. They can be observed, ambushed, or avoided as the party needs.

If the party fails, see Scouts Confronted below.

Avoiding the scouts

A group of adventurers walk into the camp carrying bundles of fungus lashed together with rope and a few carcasses of strange animals plucked from the wilds. With a hint of frustration one of them speaks:

Well that was a bust, we'll rest here for a bit, then go check the other areas.

Another adventurer speaks up, glancing back at their comrade:

I'm telling you, the Jurtak probably got them. They've been really active around here lately, and I think the last couple teams managed to completely piss them off by poaching their hunting grounds. We'll be lucky if we find any trace of them. We should just load up and head back to the lab.

Though none of the others say it, there's a ripple of grudging agreement that moves through the rest of the adventurers.

Addressing the Scouts

If the party decides against hiding and instead chooses to meet the scouts directly, or if they are found by the scouts when they search the camp, use this description:

One of the adventurers goes into full alert, and calls out:

We've got company!

Hands go to weapons, and the adventurers turn to face you, taking defensive stances. However, they don't immediately enter combat, instead choosing to parley.

Mind explaining why you're skulking around our camp? We're not expecting visitors, and not keen on raiders. So talk or walk, strangers.

The scouts are not immediately hostile, but are very suspicious at the beginning of this exchange. They won't immediately resort to violence without a reason, giving the party a chance to talk their way out of the situation, but combat remains a real possibility depending on party actions.

Who Are These People?

The scouts are clandestine agents that belong to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn], and are out in the Pathways collecting resources for the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.bfORKMRfuaOgMbUt]{Repurposed Quarry} which houses a secret Mutagist lab.

They are wary of strangers in the area, and will be careful not to let slip their true nature or mission in the Pathways, instead they style themselves as Anachraenum adventurers on commission to pull resources out of the Pathways. This isn't untrue, as most of them are active members of that guild, and that is their job. The lies are in the omissions.

Refer to the @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F]{Mutagist Scout} biography page for further details on these scouts.

Speaking with the Scouts

If the party has chosen to address the scouts peacefully, they will have questions for the party, and the party will be able to ask them questions as well. However, the wariness of the scouts needs to be managed to avoid causing a fight to break out.

Scout Wariness

As they interact with a party their wariness will increase. Failing a skill check for Persuasion, Deception, and Intimidation increases wariness by 1. If they become too wary of the party, they may attempt to warn their base of operations ahead of time.

The scout's wariness and bearing to the party is rated as follows:

  • 0-1 Wariness: The party is viewed as weird but harmless. The scouts do their best to get send them on their way quickly as possible.

  • 2-3 Wariness: The party is viewed as suspicious, but doesn't warrant direct action unless they refuse to leave. The scouts will plant to report them once done with their work here.

  • 4-5 Wariness: The party is now highly suspect, and the Scouts will begin scrutinizing anything they say, and pick at any holes in their story so far. They will plan to leave in the next hour or two report back to their superiors immediately.

  • 6+ Wariness: The party is clearly a threat to the Mutagist operation and needs to be reported quickly. Four of the scouts break off without explanation, and leave the camp immediately, heading for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.bfORKMRfuaOgMbUt]{Repurposed Quarry}.

Lying to the Scouts

A successful [[/skill persuasion 12]] or [[/skill deception 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] or [[/skillCheck deception 12]] check can convince the scouts that the party is just a bunch of fellow explorers that found the camp by mistake, or that the party doesn't want any trouble or mean any harm.

Intimidating the Scouts

Only a successful [[/skill intimidation 20]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 20]] will effectively intimidate the scouts and make them grudgingly accept the presence of the party. The DC is especially high because the scouts have the @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F.Item.yxflqWmjBtyp9GJp]{Steadfast} feature and are not easily frightened by much.

Questions for the Party

The scouts want to know the following things:

  • Who are you? The Scouts are almost guaranteed to have no idea who the party is, so any answer is viable here. However, if Ankarist outs himself or is introduced as a Veiled Chain investigator, that will increase their wariness by 1.

  • What are you doing in the Pathways? Almost any answer will work. However, mention of investigating the Drakes, chasing strange bandits, or hunting down leads on the origins of either, or similar, will increase their wariness by 1.

    • How'd you get down here? There are only so many ways down into the Mycelian Expanse, and the scouts know them. If they are honest about using the Mythspire lift, the scouts will acknowledge they knew of the route, but not how to get in. Attempting to lie about how they got into the Pathways will raise wariness by 1.

    • Did you run into an adventuring team around Skybrush? These scouts are aware that a team went topside to find a way down, but don't know what happened to them. Getting information on their fate could help reduce wariness by 1.

    • Is the way up open now? This is purely information collection, and has no impact on bearing on their wariness.

  • Have you seen any other travelers down here? The scout team is aware they've lost people down here. If the party mentions the bodies found in Cruel Traps, the scout team will note that's who they're looking for, and will need to get those bodies buried.

The party may also ask questions of the scout team, but need to be careful as the wrong questions could raise suspicions.

What are you doing down here?

We are down here collecting rare reagents, plants, animals, artifacts and the like for contacts in Ordain. It's not really a formal expedition so much as a bunch of Anachraenum just trying to make some coin and build reputations.

Are you with the Anachraenum?

We sure are, actually.

The scouts present their personal Anachraenum badges and insignia, allowing you a moment to look at them up close.

Part of the Club

A successful [[/skill investigation 12]] check confirms that these are authentic Anachraenum seals, badges, and insignia proving they are members in good standing.

What's this camp for?

There's several teams. We all mostly work together and share knowledge. That's what this camp is for. We stockpile things, talk about finds, so forth. Sure, we might make less than if we hoarded our finds, but, this way involves way less squabbling over rights to territory and finds.

Why are there multiple Anachraenum teams in the area?

We're all working for the same patron on the same scouting job.

A successful [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck society 12]] may lead one to wonder why there are multiple teams of adventurers down here. Characters with the [[/culture emberOrdani]] know that usually Anachraenum only work in teams of 3-5 people unless it's an official/sponsored expedition.

A question?

A narrated quote answer.

Additional out-of-character information.

Have you seen anyone out of place or suspicious down here?

Aside from you? Hard to say.

There's all sorts of weird things down here, and weird people coming through the Pathways. We're not aware of anyone particularly, but it's a big space. You might try heading down south into the fog-shrouded areas of the Pathways, there's plenty of ways topside there, and places to hide out.

Sensitive Matters

If the party asks about any of the following, they will immediately increase the scout team's suspicion of the party:

  • The presence of Drakes in the upper region, and their attack on Helkas.

  • People utilizing poison or alchemical weapons, such as those in the Mythspire ruins.

Players with [[/skill insight 14 passive]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14 passive]]or making a successful [[/skill insight 16]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 16]] check recognize that there was a negative reaction to the topic, and that they know more than they are letting on. Pursuing this topic increases their wariness quickly (see above) and will cause further tension to form in the group of adventurers.

Fighting the Scouts

If the party manages to provoke the scouts during a social confrontation, ambushes them, or is caught while investigating the camp, a fight will break out. The scouting team consists of four scouts.

Scout Tactics

The Mutagist scouts are coordinated skirmishers used to working together to take down larger prey. They rely heavily on focused fire and flanking through use of @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F.Item.7JsK5lmgBSG7TpUj]{Coordinated Attack} and@UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F.Item.OE8y8otGDFop6Fzt]{Team Tactics} respectively. They are vicious and unforgiving, and will use @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F.Item.BezG6ZXGpeoa9iqE]{Paralyzing Shot (Heavy Crossbow)} to disable a target so that they can all focus on the weak link.

The Mutagists are not fearless zealots that will fight to the death, however. If reduced below 50% health they or if it seems they will not be victorious in the fight, they will attempt to flee, regroup, and set up to ambush the party later. See "Following the Scouts" below.

The Mutagist scouts are coordinated skirmishers used to working together to take down larger prey. They rely heavily @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F.Item.precisionshot000]{Precision Shots} on specific targets and focused fire directed by @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F.Item.tactician0000000]. A single scout will shout out a target to focus, and the others will rally to attack it to maximize the benefit of the Tactician's call.

They are vicious and unforgiving, and will use @UUID[Actor.dDzLM6gOY0EKzF1F.Item.RdlBYuJjXOtbwksk]{Apply Paralytic} to add a paralyzing effect to their crossbow shots in order to disable a target so that they can all focus on the weak link.

The Mutagists are not fearless zealots that will fight to the death, however. If they are @Condition[broken] or seems they will not be victorious in the fight, they will attempt to flee, regroup, and set up to ambush the party later. See "Following the Scouts" below.

Ragen Attunement: Mutagist Scouts Attacked

If the party chose to attack the Mutagist scouting party, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 chain1ScoutsConfronted]] at the conclusion of the event.

Following the Scouts

It is possible for the party to trail the team from their camp if they want. Unless they are made wary and suspicious enough to immediately report back to their superiors, they will travel to the location of [[/eventState chain1Traps]], then eventually head to the Mythspire Overlook, and up into the observatory.

If the team was made to feel especially wary and suspicious they instead will begin heading for the [[/eventState chain1Laboratory]]. However, it's not possible to follow them all the way there, as the party will likely encounter other events that will distract them, causing them to lose sight of the scouts.

In either case, when the party follows the scouts, mark this event complete, and then guide the party token toward the next relevant location.

Staying Hidden

The group needs to succeed on a [[/skill stealth 14]] [[/skillCheck stealth 14]] group check with at least half the party succeeding to avoid being spotted as they travel. If successful, the team remains unaware of the party. They only need to make this check once per day.

If the party fails at any point, the scout team becomes aware they are being followed. In response, the scout team scatters, causing the party to lose their trail. At your discretion, the team is not encountered again, or, the party is ambushed by four Mutagist Scouts while the remainder continue on to inform the lab.

Primordis Attunement: Mutagist Scouts Avoided

If the party stays hidden from the Mutagist scouting party, each character advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 chain1ScoutsAvoided]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has finished with the camp and the scouts, they can continue exploring.

Next Steps

These scouts are connected to the larger Mutagist group operating in the region.
