The party might try to follow the scouts, or they might have guessed based on what they've learned that they need to find the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH]{Repurposed Quarry} in order to conclude their investigation.

If the party have not encountered [[/eventState chain1Traps]] , [[/eventState chain1Thornling]] or [[/eventState chain1Dragonskin]] they may need to gather a little more information first.
Missing Scouts.soverview: The party locates a semi-permanent camp used by local scouts. Though it's initially abandoned, signs point to recent activity. There may be useful information here, or an opportunity for the patient.
Missing Scouts.sexposition:
Tucked beneath the expansive canopies of colossal mushrooms and glowing fungi sits a small camp partially obscured by clusters of undergrowth and carefully relocated plants. A collection of makeshift shelters crafted out of local flora help mask the camp's location, making it difficult to find if one doesn't know where to look.

Inside the camouflaged perimeter is a cleared space of packed ground with piles of materials, and a fire pit of stone filled with twisted and charred remains of fungal wood. While the camp is obviously empty, it does not look abandoned.
Missing Scouts.ssummary: We located a scout camp in the Pathways, and gleaned as much information about the scouts that were using it as we could. Using a map left behind by the scouts we now have a possible base of operations to investigate, and intend to head that way next.

Reuniting with Ankarist.name: Reuniting with Ankarist
Reuniting with Ankarist.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event occurs when the party arrives in the town of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} to reconnect with @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}. To do this they will need to locate his contact @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann}, whom they were told about when departing Helkas.

Once they meet up with Ankarist they can:

  • Learn about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.RWj91gQguWOQcflB]{Mythspire Observatory} and Ankarist's exploration of it.

  • Learn a bit about @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann} and her connection to Ankarist.

  • Learn about the ongoing issues in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} which Ankarist has agreed to help with.

Talking to Mattock

The Fej that greets the party is Mattock (Neutral Good, Fej, he/him), who had been on his way to the town's tavern (The Roost). The party knows that Ankarist was coming to contact a Kivahr woman named @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann} to get information, but they don't know where to find her here in Skybrush. If they decide to take the opportunity to ask Mattock, he has this to say:

Ah yeah, Liestra, she runs the Long Haul.

He turns and points, orienting you.

Head just up that way. Can't miss it unless you're blind. That's my good deed for the day, I'm gonna reward myself with a drink. See you about.

Satisfied with himself, he nods and trudges off without a bit of ceremony, leaving you to your own devices.

The party can then head off in the direction given, this leads them to Long Haul, a shop owned and operated by Liestra Grann, and where they'll find their investigator.

You approach a round, two-story building bearing a finely painted sign:

Long Haul

Just through the doors you see rows of racks, floor to ceiling shelves, and display cases in between, all packed with items old and obscure. From art, to old tools, clothing, and odd pieces of decorated stone, the shelves hold something for everyone.

However, you aren't given much time to browse before you hear a voice call out:

Welcome to the long haul, you selling or buying today?

Your attention is pulled to a tall, muscular kivahr woman bearing a friendly smile.

Polite Company

As soon as the party tells Liestra they are looking for Ankarist, she goes into the backroom and fetches him. After that, she is keen to find out where everyone is from, and how they came to meet their mutual friend Ankarist.

Reading Liestra

A successful [[/skill insight 15]][[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check or a character with the [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/knowledge crime]] knowledge suspects that while Liestra is large of frame there is a certain deviousness to her. She is more capable of subtlety than she appears, and hides it behind plenty of bluster.

Liestra and Ankarist

I met the good inspector in Ordain, got into a bit of trouble and needed a hand. He was right there to save the day and get me out of a tight spot. Turns out I do not have the lithe frame of a burglar!

Ankarist clarifies:

You were attempting to steal items from the Lorando Collection and got caught. Not exactly the most auspicious beginning for a friendship. All I did was make sure you got a fair hearing.

Liestra takes the story a bit further:

Lot more than that, Ankarist, and you know it. If you weren't a good man, you'd have taken that wannabe merchant-lord's offer to look the other way while he killed me for breaking into his manor. I'm actually glad you caught me and took me to the Hallows. I wouldn't bet on most in the Chain being so upright as you.

Ankarist offers a faint, dissenting grumble but says nothing as Liestra wraps up:

Anyway, after that I got out of Ordain, and ended up here in Skybrush. Been running this pawnbroker for years now, and mostly deal in local artifacts found by Anachraenum passing through. Specialty is Shent artifacts, which I ship off to a couple collectors in the region. Those are my real money source these days, everything else is small time.

Ankarist's Update

Music: Ankarist's Theme

While Ankarist updates the party, play [[/soundscape music ankaristTheme ankaristTheme]].

Speaking with Ankarist, he has the following update for the party:

Passage into the Pathways

I got the relevant information from Liestra: access to the Pathways is possible through an ancient site called the Mythspire. I have already traveled to it and located the access point leading down into the Pathways. It entails a rather long ride on an ancient Shent lift.

The passage beyond the lift is extensive, and I deemed it prudent to return to the surface and resupply before proceeding further. An added benefit: I was able to wait and give you time to catch up, which I'm glad paid off.

About theMythspire

An impressive location, thousands of years old and still standing strong. It used to hold extensive machinery and was some sort of orrery, but also a historical site or pilgrimage location.

If things ever calm down enough that I can get some free time, I would enjoy exploring the ruins in detail. For now though, we'll be passing through.

I also ran into the guardian, and some dead adventurers. Things went poorly for both of them.

Adventurers and the Guardian

While I was here, Liestra mentioned that she had previously assisted a group of adventurers working on behalf of the Anachraenum. Regrettably, I found what remained of them — scattered and dismembered throughout the lowest level of the Mythspire.

There was an ancient guardian there that was responsible for their deaths. However, the guardian itself was provoked to violence when they poisoned it, and succumbed soon after I arrived.

The entire affair leaves me uneasy. The poison they used was highly corrosive — unlike anything I am familiar with, and not the sort of thing I've known Anachraenum teams to carry.

More worrying still, the bodies of the fallen were exhibiting signs of unnatural reanimation. It appears that the guardian kept killing them until they had been sufficiently destroyed and couldn't rise any longer.

I'm not sure how any of this aligns with out investigation, if at all, but it's worth noting to you, at least.

Departing for Mythspire and the Pathways

Before we head off to the Mythspire Observatory, we need to deal with something in town. As you no doubt noticed, the locals are rather on edge.

There have been a series of murders in Skybrush, one of the victims was with child, which has understandably placed the entire community on edge and demanding justice. Constable Valaston is the sole law here, and it's clear the burden is becoming too much for him. Liestra thinks that some outside assistance would be of benefit here and I am inclined to agree.

I did tell Liestra I would help, and I wouldn't feel good about leaving the town in the current state. So, we should speak with the locals. Liestra recommended we start with The Roost, the town’s tavern and social hub. With any luck, those gathered will be willing to talk.

After that, we can sort out our supplies, gear up, and return to the Pathways.

Related Quests

Before continuing on, the party may choose to investigate the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death}, a side quest that is set primarily within Skybrush. Generally speaking, Ankarist favors doing this first, as he does not like the idea of leaving a murder unsolved, especially if the locals need help which he can offer.

If the party is not yet at least level 3, you may wish to strongly suggest the party investigate this side quest before continuing onward.

Music: Default

Once the party has finished conversing with Ankarist, return to the default music: [[/soundscape music reset]]

Reaching the Ancient Lift

Once the party arrives at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.RWj91gQguWOQcflB]{Mythspire Observatory}, they can navigate the ruin to follow the path of Ankarist's investigation into the Pathways below.

Optional Exploration

If you and your players want to explore the Mythspire area you can load the @UUID[Scene.emberMythSpUpper] scene and let them explore, but the elevator to the lower area is already unlocked, the Guardian has long since perished, and the ancient lift has been unlocked, so there is no actual gameplay for the players at this point.

Descending Into the Pathways

The party reaches the pathways by descending the great stone lift discovered by Ankarist in the lower levels of Mythspire Observatory. If the party takes the time to explore that map, you can perform this transition using the interactive elevator described in @UUID[JournalEntry.7rsDfaBhJux44VQI.JournalEntryPage.CecLJBaIh4oKCvR8]{Ancient Lift}.

Alternatively, to skip this area map exploration and transition directly into the Pathways section of the Region Map, adjust the Elevation of the party token to -1, which will cause the party to descend into the pathways.

Once the party begins their descent into the Pathways, read the following aloud:

A great stone circle thirty feet wide rests in the center of the space, with multiple concentric rings of ornately decorated stone making up its internal area. Numerous magical runes can be seen scattered through the cracked and worn stone, all of them glow with mystical energy. A singular glowing rune hangs in the air in the center of this space.

With a sweep of his hand, the rune fades out and begins turning as a deep, resonant hum signals the start of the platform's descent. It sinks slowly at first and then picks up speed, ancient magic guiding it into the earth. Runes along the lift's edge glow steadily, passing by in a predictably rhythm, their light dancing off the walls as they do.

Minutes pass, yet the lift carries on, moving steadily downward. The air grows warmer, and the color and texture of the stone changes over time, as you descend through more and more layers of Ember's crust.

Finally, the lift slows its descent, and then comes to a smooth halt with a final, magical hum that reverberates through your core. Before you, a massive passage winds into the darkness ahead.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has descended into Pathways they will find they have only one way forward.

Next Steps

The party must continue their journey deeper into the pathways until they encounter the [[/eventState chain1PathwaysCamp]] event.
Reuniting with Ankarist.soverview: The party arrives in Skybrush, looking for Ankarist by way of his contact there, a Kivahr by the name of Liestra Grann. She can point them in the direction of the investigator, and they can get an update on his ongoing investigation.
Reuniting with Ankarist.sexposition:
As Skybrush moves past you, the scarce few denizens out on the streets watch you warily. The sensation of being watched and unwelcome is a strong one as the number of eyes on you grows. Yet, for all the wariness, none of the locals allow themselves to linger in your path save one, a broad shouldered, dusty and deeply scarred Fej man.

He scoffs at the empty streets then looks at you.

Take my word, strangers, Skybrush's better'n this most days. You lookin' for somethin' particular?
Reuniting with Ankarist.ssummary: We reunited with Ankarist in Skybrush, and got an update on recent events. He's agreed to help his contact Liestra with some issues in town, and we have be asked to assist. Once done with that, we'll be heading on toward the Mythspire Observatory and the Pathways entrance below it.

Traveling with Ankarist.name: Traveling with Ankarist
Traveling with Ankarist.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event can occur multiple times while traveling with Ankarist and provides the party with an opportunity to learn about the investigator, his story, and his opinions on the current situation.

This event can occur during a rest at any point during Chapter 2 if @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist} is a member of the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party}. In this event the party can:

  • Discuss the current situation with Ankarist and learn his thoughts.

  • Get to know Ankarist better by understanding his story.

Thoughts on Events

Skybrush and Liestra

I have only visited Skybrush once before. It is a remote settlement, and the conditions there are demanding. The community is cordial, though I would not choose such an isolated environment for myself; I learned early in life that I prefer less remote surroundings.

In Skybrush, my contact is Liestra Grann. She deals in antiquities, and her business with Shent and Aedir artifacts has earned her connections among collectors and the Anachraenum alike. She is well informed about local excavation sites and ruins. If there is an entrance to the Pathways nearby, she is likely to be aware of it.

Liestra's Story[[/eventState chain1Map]]

It is largely accurate.

We, the Chain, identified a gang of thieves planning to steal a nobleman's private collection, and identified anyone we could. Somehow word got out and most of the crew abandoned their associates, leaving Liestra and a few others to get caught red handed during the robbery.

The nobleman did try to bribe me to look the other way. I'd seen his kind before, thinking his power and influence and money meant he could have and do whatever he wanted.

I decided to deny him what he sought, since I couldn't otherwise confront him. So, I personally delivered the burglars to the courts and did what I could to ensure their cases received all due fairness — no more, but no less than justice required.

Liestra took that as a sign I liked her, and made a point of tracking me down to thank me for saving her life. After that she just sort of lingered, and ended up helping me track down the people who betrayed her to the Chain. Somewhere along the line there we became friends.

Mythspire Observatory[[/eventState chain1Guardian]] or [[/eventState chain1Reunite]]

It's an impressive place, I can only imagine what it was like in its heyday. I do wonder where some of the upper framework of the orrery went. There wasn't enough debris on the lower levels to account for all the overhead collapses.

I'm also always astounded by how much of the old Shent and Aedir ruins still stand after how long it's been. Something about the magic used to make the stone, I suspect, since they use the same sort of transmuted stone as seen in Aedir ruins.

It's a different stone, yes, but similar striation in the exposed stonework means they used similar magical processes. It makes me wonder if they shared their techniques at some point, or developed the same methods independently.

The Guardian[[/eventState chain1Guardian]] or [[/eventState chain1Reunite]]

I've never seen anything like it before, and I find it strange the creature was abandoned for so long in Mythspire, and seemingly forgotten. I respect it though, a timeless defender, always vigilant, always dedicated. It deserved better.

I wish there was something we could have done for it. I think it might have been a great ally and source of knowledge. However, that acid it was afflicted with goes beyond anything I've seen before. It's clearly toxic to living beings beyond simply necrotizing the flesh.

The Pathways[[/eventState chain1PathwaysCamp]]

I read quite a lot about them before, they are broken up into various regions: Mycelia Expanse, Fogbound Caverns, the Sinkhole Depths, so on. They're all a little different, but broadly the same: overrun with fungal life, filled with strange creatures, and home to countless dangers.

It's a thrill getting to see them for myself, though I don't really have the freedom to just wander around and sightsee, much as I'd like to. There's still an an investigation to conduct, after all.

Dragon Skin[[/eventState chain1Dragonskin]]

That was a Vile Dragon's skin. If you want a good point of reference, they are like the Drakes we fought but many magnitudes worse, and much larger. Since we encountered the Drakes I've been wondering if they were related. Finding the shed skin feels like a confirmation my hunch was right.

Given the age of skin and the state of things around it, I think that the creature moved on some time ago, so I doubt we're in any real danger. If it is in the area however, well, we'll do our best to avoid it.

The Mutagist Laboratory[[/eventState chain1Laboratory]]

That site dates back to when Ordain was first being built. They cut deep into Ember to find a good source of the white stone the city uses. While the quarry was sizable, I doubt it was the main site the city's stone came from.

If I recall, the construction of Ordain required multiple quarry sites working in tandem, this one may have been a latter era site, or it might have been abandoned when it flooded.

Regardless, repurposing it into a hidden base was very smart, it's large enough to allow for expansion, and very well hidden. Once the location gets reported to the Chain I'm sure they'll go tear the place apart and extract every last secret the quarry has.

Thoughts on Characters

Agraband

He is a much better bard than a merchant, and clearly prefers leading people in song to leading wagons through dusty back roads. However, the realities of commerce are often more profitable than music, and everyone has debts.

I cannot claim to know him well, but he has a reputation for reliability. There are certainly less trustworthy choices when it comes to reaching your destination. When I was preparing to return home and investigating caravan routes, Strayhearth’s company came highly recommended.

Clipper

From my observations, Agraband appears to be gradually entrusting Clipper with much of his network — contacts, routes, and even having them undertake certain responsibilities while in transit. It resembles a deliberate succession.

I would not be surprised to see Strayhearth’s caravan someday operating under Clipper’s leadership. Whether that aligns with Clipper's wanderlust, I couldn't say.

Lyla

She has always been regarded as a significant figure in Ordain, even during her absences to administer far-flung operations. As the daughter of House Cevher’s patriarch, her position is nearly equivalent to nobility, a status shared by her siblings as well. However I believe she chafes against that, and the yoke of expectation placed on her as a result.

She's unlike other emissaries of her station. Her demeanor is less formal, her conduct less restrained, and her willingness to do things herself isn't what is considered customary among her peers. I prefer her approach, and can respect someone who wants to get their hands dirty doing the work, rather than delegating from afar.

Sin

Sin strikes me as someone guided by optimism, with perhaps a certain naivete regarding the realities of organizations and their motives. Placing absolute trust in a group one knows little about rarely ends well.

Sins intentions are utterly sincere, and the desire to do good should not be underestimated, but such openness can leave one vulnerable — to exploitation or to commitments they may later come to question.

It is a disposition I respect, and one that more people could benefit from having.

Liestra[[/eventState chain1Map]]

Liestra’s instincts tend toward opportunism, though I have never doubted the sincerity of her intentions when she states them plainly. She is resourceful and always seeking an advantage — a habit born of hardship, I suspect, rather than malice.

Her decisions are sometimes questionable, and her preference for discretion can create complications. Even so, she has made a consistent effort to improve, and her actions are often motivated by genuine goodwill.

That willingness to do better, in my estimation, deserves recognition.

Kern[[/eventState chain1Thornling]]

The idea of a solitary druid surviving within the Pathways for an indeterminate length of time is unsettling in itself, and requires cunning, power, or secrets that far outstrip our own. I have no desire to challenge someone capable of such endurance.

Kern is unpredictable and undoubtedly dangerous; on that much, I have no doubts. I find much of what he says difficult to verify, and I am certain he does not require our assistance at all. However, I do not believe he poses a threat to us unless provoked — and I have no intention of testing that theory. Discretion, in this case, seems the wiser course.

Kryz[[/eventState chain1Rescue]]

If you’re asking for my opinion on “Kryz,” I’ll be clear: I do not ascribe personhood to a large inanimate crystal, painted face or otherwise.

That said, it is worth noting that the Jurtak were unusually invested in recovering this particular stone. That alone raises questions about its significance and properties. My unease about Kern’s request was not unfounded, clearly. There were signs that something was amiss, even if I could not articulate them at the time.

Kalasak[[/eventState chain1Laboratory]]

If I am being as generous, Kalasak was a danger that needed to be contained, permanently and without exception. Those who conduct experiments on living beings without regard for suffering or dignity, forfeit any claim to sympathy. I have encountered others of his kind — methodical, remorseless, treating sentient life as little more than raw material.

Death might be too good for them, and no justice would feel truly sufficient otherwise.

Bringing an end to his work cannot undo his crimes, but it does ensure he cannot inflict further harm. For that, at least, there is some small satisfaction. His death leaves us with unanswered questions, though the records and notes he left behind may reveal more in time.

About Yourself

Your story?

I spent my youth in the Tayan Empire, getting mired in politics and scheming. Ultimately that life was not for me and I left in search of something different. I found a different calling and a different purpose that led me to Ordain where I have lived now for many years. It turned out that the Veiled Chain had need of my particular mixture of skills and I found myself well suited to the work.

The Veiled Chain?

The Veiled Chain is one of the branches of government in Ordain, it's the investigative arm responsible for resolving some of the most severe issues that the city faces. We get involved in cases where community enforcement of laws fails or is incapable of handling the situation.

Your interest in dragons?

Enough to know they are bad news. I saw the carnage they are capable of first-hand during my time in the Tayan Empire. I'm not sure which are more dangerous, wild ones or those bound in service to the Empress. In either case, wherever dragons appear, bloodshed swiftly follows.

About your magic?

I suppose you could say I have a knack for sorcery, and I've picked up a few tricks here and there. Mostly things to help with my work. Most non-magical crime can be solved by the Ordani community without getting the Veiled Chain involved, but when there's a dangerous spellcaster in play it's important to understand a bit of arcana. I've put one or two outlaw mages in Spellbreaker Tower myself.

Ankarist's Power

Characters with [[/skill insight 18 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 18 passive]], who make a successful [[/skill insight 16]] or [[/skill arcana 16]] [[/skillCheck deception 16]] or [[/skillCheck 16 arcana]] check sense that Ankarist is not being entirely forthcoming about the nature of his arcane capabilities.

The true source of your power?

Ankarist scowls and his expression darkens slightly.

I suppose my explanation didn't fully satisfy you.

He shakes his head wistfully before a vaguely approving smile softens his expression.

You show the insticts of an investigator!

This is a private matter, and it's nothing that need concern you or that will affect our time together. I will share with you, however, that I have a patron who has been valuable in cultivating my capabilities. I'll speak no more of it now, but perhaps if we journey together I will have opportunity to confide in you further.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event may repeat at your discretion when the party rests next. Feel free to use any of the question and answer responses here outside the context of this event if you feel they are appropriate to mention during other situations.
Traveling with Ankarist.soverview: The party stops for a rest while traveling with Ankarist, providing an opportunity to learn more about the enigmatic Drakon investigator.
Traveling with Ankarist.sexposition:
With dusk bleeding into night, camp has settled into a subdued rhythm. Bedrolls are set, boots are pulled off tired feet, and the smoky aroma of a dying fire lingers in the air. Ankarist sits near the edge of the firelight, back straight, journal in hand.

Silently, and swiftly he commits ink to page after page, the tip of his quill softly scribbling, each catch and scrape of it blending with the cracks and pops of the flame beside him. Between pages his attention lifts to the camp, to you, with a kind of calm vigilance that is less suspicion than habitual scrutiny.

Eventually his note taking ends and he tucks away his journal, fitting the quill neatly alongside it. Only then does he address you. As always, his tone is that of someone who weighs every word, who prefers accuracy over embellishment.

I find conversation is best had when the work is done, notes are taken, and thoughts are collected. It leaves the mind clear, and ensures distractions are few. So, if there’s any matter you wish to discuss — questions, theories, concerns — this would be the ideal time.
Traveling with Ankarist.ssummary: We took a respite from our travels to camp, finding the opportunity to discuss our current situation with Ankarist and learn more about our investigator companion.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This main quest occurs during Chapter 2, and begins if the party [[/eventState windingTrailLeavetaking sin]] at the end of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWindingTrai]{The Winding Trail}. If the party chose not to, they can still rejoin Sin at a later time, in which case they start the "Crumbling Sanctuary" quest partway through, via the [[/eventState cindaric1Reunite]] event.

Once any of the Chapter 2 main quests have been completed, it is no longer possible to access this quest (as Sin has independently reached Ordain without the party's assistance).

Difficulty

The "Crumbling Sanctuary" quest is designed for a party of Level 3 characters. It begins upon leaving @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}. If the party did not thoroughly explore the Forest of Stone and its respective Chapter 1 side quests, they may still be Level 2. They can either press forward and expect to advance to Level 3 upon obtaining their next milestone point, or they could be encouraged to backtrack and explore further.

Milestone Progression

This is a Main Quest quest that awards 3 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the [[/eventState cindaric1CorpinArrival]], [[/eventState cindaric1Attack]], and [[/eventState cindaric1Temple]] Events.

Crumbling Sanctuary will take the party on a grand adventure as they discover the machinations of an evil necromantic plot, one that threatens to upheave the very Cindaric faith itself. After their alliance with Sin Marmot in Helkas, the characters will join the young druid on a westward pilgrimage to Corpin Sanctuary and the city of Ordain. However, this trip will prove far from idyllic.

An encounter at a pillaged farmstead known as Dradley Grange will reveal the presence of marauding forces within the Arctus Plateau, and serve as the party's first clues since Helkas that unrest is troubling to the region. Subsequently, the party comes face to face with a small mob of reanimated corpses while they attempt to ford the ruins of Keeper's Crossing on the River Elenain, followed by a scuffle with a group of raiders from the Otherhood of Fortune — suggesting that several forces are at work to bring ruin to the people of the Plateau.

Once Sin and the party make it to Corpin Sanctuary, they'll meet the respected Cindaric Sages and find themselves caught in the middle of an intriguing scenario. This plot involves a necromancer named Evesso, who has clandestinely infiltrated the Cindarics in an attempt to gain access to rare occult relics and the ancient tombs beneath Mial Mountain. If the party is unable to prevent Evesso from raising the dead, at least they can help stop him from destroying the Sanctuary … or can they?

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]

  • @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb]

  • @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]

  • @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]

  • @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]

  • @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]

  • @UUID[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]

  • @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]

  • @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4]

  • @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H]

  • @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]

  • @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]

  • @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy]
Overview.soverview:
In the aftermath of tragic events at Helkas, Sin Marmot ventures eastward towards Ordain with intention to pledge themselves to the Cindaric Sages. The first step upon this journey is a stop at the outlying Cindaric enclave of Corpin Sanctuary, a tranquil retreat atop Mial Mountain in the center of the Golden Flats.

Sin is determined to do what they can to assist the people of the Arctus Plateau, and has utmost faith that the Cindaric Sages represent the right path towards accomplishing that. On the path towards Corpin Sanctuary events take a malevolent and concerning turn with new evidence of undeath affecting the region. Moreover, undeath is not the only menace that affects the plateau. Ongoing attacks by mysterious raiders, perhaps related to the ones who attacked Helkas, have ravaged farms and homesteads. These attacks create an exodus of refugees seeking shelter and safety.

In "Crumbling Sanctuary" you will travel with Sin Marmot across the Golden Flats, accumulating evidence of mounting local troubles. You will visit a remote and tranquil mountain monastery where you will meet Cindaric Sages who are, themselves, struggling to grapple with these problems. The peaceful facade of Corpin Sanctuary, however, belies an inner rot which threatens to destroy the enclave from within.

Harrowed Crossing.name: Harrowed Crossing
Harrowed Crossing.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event tasks the party and their ally @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} with crossing the River Elenain, where the grand stone bridge of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.YR30CBfcusmmL38D]{Keeper's Crossing} has collapsed. In this event, the characters can:

  • Look for clues regarding the bridge's destruction.

  • Discover undead @UUID[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4]{Sodden Corpses} lodged among the debris here, who lurch to life and attack.

  • Ford the river while fighting to survive the undead ambush.

The Collapsed Bridge

All manner of waterlogged detritus has piled up amidst stones near the ruined bridge, from fallen trees to scattered rocks, forming the humble beginnings of a few small ersatz dams. The haphazard scene here comes as an unexpected surprise for Sin and the party, who may investigate the ruins before they attempt to cross the river.

Unkept Crossing

Any character who attempts to search the area can determine the following information using the associated skill checks:

  • [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] The character is familiar with Keeper's Crossing and the history of both its architecture and its demise nearly twenty years ago at the hands of an earthquake.

  • [[/knowledge crafts]] The character is familiar with the Arcturian stonework here, and can validate the sturdy nature of the masonry. Something like an earthquake or demolition would have been necessary to topple this bridge, and no signs of manmade wrecking can be found.

  • [[/knowledge trade]] The character is well aware of the former importance of this bridge for trade, particularly when it came to Ordani imports and exports.

  • [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]]The character is able to confirm the relative safety of the crossing points that span the river along the southern edge of the ruined bridge, which have been supplemented with makeshift bridges made of rope and timber.

  • [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]]The character is able to determine that falling into the rapidly-flowing river could prove hazardous. Catching onto one of the ersatz dams or bridges might be the only way to prevent being washed downstream for the better part of a mile.

If the characters fail to assess the southern crossing points for themselves, Sin will eventually stumble onto her own successful Wisdom (Perception) Awareness check while surveying the scene, and promptly relate some findings to the group.

Fording the River

Once one or more of the characters have moved far enough to reach the halfway mark to the eastern bank, a mob of Sodden Corpses rises from the waterlogged detritus to attack. Read the following aloud:

The southbound water rushes by your feet as you ford your way towards the eastern shore. Your footing remains steady as driftwood and detritus lightly strike your ankles, but you notice something else among the shadows of the ersatz dam to the northwest: a bloated human face with milky white eyes and horribly jaundiced skin.

Just then, a sallow humanoid hand reaches out of the water at your feet, followed by the harrowing visage of a rotten and waterlogged carcass. Before you can blink, nearly a dozen of these humanoid corpses lurch to life around you!

@Embed[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4 count=10]

Sodden Corpse Tactics

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check is able to avoid becoming &Reference[Surprise]{Surprised} by the 10 Sodden Corpses that emerge from the water to attack.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] check is able to avoid becoming &Reference[Surprise]{Surprised} by the 10 Sodden Corpses that emerge from the water to attack.

The Sodden Corpses will quickly attempt to surround the closest enemies, with up to 3 of them ganging up on an individual character to use their @UUID[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4.Item.wt7JeYS3195qJdRK]{Slam} attack while making use of their @UUID[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4.Item.JrAWwwyOAKUxp9LH]{Stench} feature.

Sodden Corpses who aren't close enough to move into melee contact with a character in the span of one round will use their @UUID[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4.Item.wZzApolzz4lp41Ft]{Pestilent Retch} action while closing in, targeting multiple characters if possible.

The Sodden Corpses will quickly attempt to surrounded the closest enemies, with up to 3 of them ganging up on an individual character to use @UUID[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4.Item.legsweep00000000] and try to drag them down. Attacks made against these shambling dead rupture the @UUID[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4.Item.repugnantPustule] that cover the creatures, spilling horrid corruption into the air.

Sodden Corpses caught out away from the fight will make use of @UUID[Actor.7JfHWWicvgKFvOL4.Item.acidSpit00000000] to deal corruption damage and try to spread the @Condition[decaying] condition to as many targets as possible while they try to close the distance.

River Combat Hazards

The torrential southbound waters of the River Elenain continue to rush by as combat unfolds. The especially difficult terrain here requires sure footing and careful progress if the characters wish to avoid falling into the water.

Any character who loses 10 hp or more from attacks by Sodden Corpses while standing on one of the rocks or bridges that comprise the southern crossing must succeed on either a [[/skill acrobatics 11]] or [[/skill athletics 11]] [[/skillCheck athletics 11]] check. Any character who moves more than their walking speed in a single round must also make this check. Failure results in the character falling into the rapids and being swept downstream a total of [[/roll (1d3+1)*10]] feet.

  • Movement downstream is made at double speed for all creatures (characters travel up to 10 feet downstream for every 5 feet they move while swimming).

  • Movement upstream is quartered for creatures without a swim speed (characters only travel 5 feet for every 20 feet they move while swimming).

  • Movement upstream is halved for creatures with a swim speed (characters only travel 5 feet for every 10 feet they move while swimming).

Characters who wish to swim upstream against the current (which flows in a southeasterly direction) must succeed on a [[/skill athletics 15]] [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] check to progress. If a character fails this check by 10 or more, they are washed downstream an additional [[/roll (1d3)*10]] feet.

  • Climbing out of the river at one of the rocky cliff faces on either bank requires a [[/skill athletics 13]] [[/skill athletics 13]] [[/skillCheck athletics 13]]check.

  • Characters who attempt to climb back onto the rope and timber bridges that span the southern crossing make the same check with @Advantage[2].

Washed Away

Characters who are swept downstream by the rover current are channeled towards the Sodden Corpses stationed at the dam near the southeastern edge of the map. Once a character reaches this dam, they are able to grab onto the dam itself with relative ease. However, the character must succeed on a [[/skill athletics 11]] [[/skillCheck athletics 11]] check or a [[/skill acrobatics 11]] check at the beginning of each of their turns to hang on .

Characters can also choose to let the current wash them further downstream, outside the bounds of the area map.

  • Any character that allows the river to carry them downstream must succeed on a [[/save dex 15]][[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw to avoid taking [[/damage 3d6 bludgeoning]] [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] check or they suffer being [[/hazard 10 fortitude health bludgeoning]]{Dashed Against the Rocks} before they wash up nearly two miles downstream to the southeast on the shore of hex 3210.2892.

  • Characters who leave combat will remain outside of initiative order until a) all party members have washed downstream, b) the sodden corpses have been defeated in combat, or c) the remaining characters have successfully reached the eastern bank of the river.

If the party defeats the Sodden Corpses in combat, the characters may take time to inspect the remains for information about their origins and how they might have reached Keeper's Crossing.

A proper inspection of the Sodden Corpse cadavers requires a bit of diligence as the rapids persist. Skill checks associated with this task can be made using the &Reference[Help] help of other characters, despite occurring outside of combat .

Examining the Unholy Remains

It is clear that these corpses are highly unnatural and abhorrent evidence of some unholy power. Characters who succeed on a [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check understand that some power has interposed itself between these deceased and the natural cycle which would convey their souls to the Bonelands. Characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] or [[/knowledge souls]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

A successful [[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] check reveals forensic evidence that these people died of various causes; some of the deaths were the obvious result of violence, while others seem natural or otherwise elusive. Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check conclude that the bodies were swept downriver, until they became ensnared in the rocks, debris, and rapids present at this crossing. Characters with [[/knowledge tracking]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Searching the bodies with a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check locates some minor valuables among the remains. Roll once on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Arcturian Corpse Loot} table.

The encounter with the undead here at Keeper's Crossing is highly concerning for Sin Marmot, who is eager to share her thoughts with the rest of the party. As the characters examine the corpses or retreat from the scene, Sin speaks up:

Obviously taken aback by the encounter with the shambling waterlogged corpses, Sin pulls down her face mask and looks you sternly in the eye.

Two and a half decades on Ember and I've never seen anything quite like that before. Something foul has brought these poor souls back to life. Mark my words, this is not the Influence of Sockets at work. We must hasten our journey to Corpin Sanctuary. Surely they'll have answers, won't they … ?

Troubling Developments

The aftermath of the encounter here provides a moment for conversation with @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin}, who is noticeably shaken since the party's fight with the Sodden Corpses.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] check is able to determine that Sin feels out of their depth following the fight, and that Sin's claims of inexperience with these matters are honest and accurate.

Sin is eager to compare notes and opinions with the characters about what happened here, including:

  • Their history as a druid and aspirations to join the Cindaric Sages (if they didn't previously discuss them during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.41dlrDZuVo04zQJT]{Traveling with Sin} event).

  • Thoughts regarding the origins of the various Sodden Corpse cadavers, including who these people might have been before their original demise.

  • The necessary role of clerics of all faiths in Ember's emerging battle against necromancy.

  • The nature of the Sodden Corpses compared to legends and accounts of other kinds of undead, like spectral apparitions.

Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] or [[/knowledge undeath]] who participate in the conversation and attempt to bolster Sin's resolve or courage (or their very decision to join the Cindarics) gain one point of Inspiration.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After defeating or fleeing from the Sodden Corpses, the party can continue onwards to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh]{Corpin Sanctuary} and the [[/eventState cindaric1CorpinArrival]] event.
Harrowed Crossing.soverview: The party encounters a treacherous river crossing on their way to Corpin Sanctuary with Sin Marmot. When they attempt to traverse the River Elenain at Keeper's Crossing, the characters discover the bridge has been destroyed by the calamity of a semi-recent earthquake. As the characters ford the river with Sin at their side, they're attacked by a mob of soggy reanimated corpses that appear to have washed downstream with the current.
Harrowed Crossing.sexposition: You survey the ruins of Keeper's Crossing in search of an alternate method of traversing the fast-flowing river. To the south of the collapsed stone bridge, a makeshift trail descends towards the water, and you spy a narrow set of switchback paths that climb the eastern bank on the far side.
Harrowed Crossing.ssummary: The stone bridge at Keeper's Crossing was destroyed, perhaps during one of the storied earthquakes that have rocked the Golden Flats. We managed to ford the river, but were waylaid by a mob of sodden, undying corpses that were caught up in the detritus. These undead creatures present further evidence that necromancy is on the rise throughout the Arctus Plateau, and that our journey to see the Cindaric Sages at Corpin Sanctuary is more urgent than ever.

Corpin Arrival.name: Corpin Arrival
Corpin Arrival.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event details the party's arrival at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh]{Corpin Sanctuary}, a mountainside enclave of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}. They're welcomed by its leader, @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}, and have an opportunity to meet and discuss current events with various other characters at the sanctuary. In this event, the characters can:

  • Chat with Mira Wavehorn and debrief her on the attack at Helkas.

  • Share a meal with the Cindaric Sages and meet an enigmatic visitor to the Sanctuary named @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}.

  • Participate in an evening ceremony led by another sage named @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso}.

  • Be provided with @UUID[JournalEntry.CAKZTyo0U5gluaaH.JournalEntryPage.rVvKMBpvZ5knWvwe]{Dormitory} rooms where they may stay overnight.

  • Heed the call to adventure after a mysterious note is slipped beneath their dormitory door.

Area Walkthrough

This event takes place on the Corpin Sanctuary area map, and much of its gameplay is linked to locations in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS]{Corpin Sanctuary} area walkthrough, which describes all of the individual locations which can be explored inside the area map.

During this particular event, the party shouldn't be permitted to freely explore the sanctuary. Instead, they're guided to specific locations by their hosts, in the order described below. The party will have adequate opportunity to freely explore the area in the subsequent event, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.4rR7KxEbu3RXbzuQ]{Corpin Investigation}.

A Welcome Respite

The party arrives at Corpin Sanctuary, an enclave of the Cindaric Sages nestled in the crags of Mial Mountain, situated a day's travel west of Ordain. The party is welcomed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.WHdKr6CkT5xF7lqr]{Entry Courtyard} by the enclave's leader, Mira Wavehorn.

@Embed[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]

Meeting Mira

Mira ambles with the party in the Entry Courtyard with a desire for them to explain their visit in adequate detail, and isn't afraid to use small talk to coax information out of them. Topics that Mira is quick to bring up in conversation while meeting the party include:

  • The party's background and any affiliations they might have.

  • A brief history of Corpin Sanctuary and the Cindaric order itself.

  • The mission of Corpin Sanctuary as a refuge for lost and displaced peoples, which has been impacted and hampered by recent events.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check indicates that Mira is scrutinizing whether or not the party are refugees themselves, and is apprehensive of those who might take unsavory advantage of the Sanctuary's graces.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check is familiar with Mira's role and responsibilities as a Cindaric Sage and the leader of Corpin Sanctuary. Characters with [[/path CindaricAdherent]] have @Advantage[2].

If the characters ask Mira for shelter at the Sanctuary (or a reward for their intel from the encounters at Helkas and Keeper's Crossing), one of them must succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check with the following possible results:

  • Success: Mira is willing to offer the party room and board for a night or two as they rest up and decide their next course of action. She's also happy to offer the party a modest reward for their findings in the form of a [[/award 10gp]] per character, taken from the Sanctuary's tithe box.

  • Result of 18+: Mira takes the party's accounts of their undead encounters very seriously, and also provides them with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.ytlsBjYsZ7OBSEBs]{Potion of Healing} to assist with any similar encounters in the future.

  • Success: Mira is willing to offer the party room and board for a night or two as they rest up and decide their next course of action. Mira is also happy to offer the party a modest reward for their findings, in the form of a [[/award 1gp]] per character, taken from the Sanctuary's tithe box.

  • Critical Success: Mira takes the party's accounts of their undead encounters very seriously, and also provides them with a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingElixir000] to assist with any similar encounters in the future.

If the characters fail to persuade Mira, Sin eventually steps forward and shares professes their own dream to join the Cindaric Sages. Mira's opinion of the party softens, and she invites Sin and the party to stay for the evening (if not longer). Additional dialogue options with Mira are listed below.

About Corpin Sanctuary?

Corpin Sanctuary was built long ago to establish a satellite location for Cindaric initiatives, removed from the commotion of urban life in Ordain. The people of the Golden Flats and beyond are always in deserving need of charity, and — out here on the mountain, in our quiet little enclave — we pride ourselves on a more … intimate connection with Ember through the land itself. But we do share the same goals as our cohorts in Ordain. We're just a bit more rustic.

Regarding the Undead?

Make no mistake, these undead creatures you speak of suggest a greater threat to the natural order of Ember and the sacred heartblood that flows within it. The Soul Cycle is the wheel upon which our very cosmos turns, and these threats of restless souls and abyssal incursions are most troubling. Worse yet, you aren't the first allies of the Cindaric order to share word of these kinds of calamities. And I fear you won't be the last.

A Warm Meal

After meeting with Mira, the party is ushered into the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.R5WXCmGHIT6K7Z7e]{Refectory} where they can join some of the other sages and visitors in a meal. The characters are invited to sit at a table with a Maziran scholar who is also visiting the sanctuary, who introduces herself as "Av". This is Avwynn Taol, the leader of the mysterious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinaries}, who takes great effort to keep her identity a secret at this time.

As Mira ushers you into the refectory, you can't help but notice another outsider seated here, a gregarious femme clad in the robes of a Maziran scholar. She smiles to greet you as one of the sages saunters over with a basket of knotted bread, its golden crust adorned with candied currants and aromatic spices. Another sage waltzes in and briskly sets enough places for all of you to join this stranger at the table, where a kettle of hot tea and a pitcher of fresh-squeezed pomegranate juice sit ready to quench your thirst.

@Embed[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]

Meeting Avwynn

As the party sits down to a meal with Avwynn, she will regale them with anecdotes about her youth in Mazira and her exploits throughout the Arctus Plateau. Her methods of storytelling and overall demeanor lend an air of mystery, even slight mistrust. Subjects of this conversation with Avwynn include:

  • Her immigration to Ordain via the ship of an Akazean freebooter named Captain Kree.

  • Her family's history as esteemed Spirit Sages of Lunarai.

  • The tale of a Cor'ak sorcerer king who owes her a life debt.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check recognizes some of the historical references that Avwynn mentions during her screed.

  • They're familiar with Maziran Spirit Sages and their pivotal role in conflicts with the Tayan Empire.

  • They're learned in the history of the Maziran Kingdoms and their Cor'ak origins.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check recognizes some of the arcane references that Avwynn mentions throughout the conversation.

  • The aptly named Spirit Sages of Mazira are known for their ability to commune with the dead.

  • Cor'ak descendents of the early Mazirans were known to dabble in the study of eldritch magic.

Meanwhile, characters who succeed on a [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check can sense that Avwynn is not being entirely forthcoming about her travel or reasons for being at Corpin Sanctuary.

Additional dialogue options with Avwynn are listed below.

Avwynn's History with Arcane Magic:

Indeed, I was born with a natural talent for sorcery. But the primal magic that flows through Ember's heartblood is the true language of my soul. I am merely the latest in a proud dynasty of spellcasters, and — like my ancestors before me — I let the spirits guide me. Yet, the spirit that guides me is the spirit of Ember itself.

Avwynn's Thoughts on Corpin Sanctuary:

Although it lacks the refinement of the Cindarin Temple in Ordain, the Sanctuary certainly has its charms. In fact, I do prefer the open mountain air and the steady earth at my feet. And after all, a building is just a building. Ember provides for those that hold its promise.

Evening Ceremony

After the meal, the entire group of sages here escorts the party members up the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.9aygktOAMoTJoeBf]{Cliffside Path} to the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.Jj4lbzMBB7OBFM05]{Sanctorum Entrance} and into the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.FvJRLzLclby5Uini]{Sanctorum}. Within the Sanctorum, the group observes an evening ritual led by @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso}, one of Corpin Sanctuary's senior sages. Avwynn Taol stays behind to languidly continue her meal before retiring to her chamber.

Evesso is, in fact, a malevolent necromancer in disguise, whose insidious plans involve a secret elevator beneath the Sanctorum. This plot will advance during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.4rR7KxEbu3RXbzuQ]{Corpin Investigation} event, but Evesso's ruse is rather effective for now.

@Embed[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]

As you make your way into the large Sanctorum, you quickly take note of an eccentric Cindaric standing on the dais who appears to be leading this evening's ceremonial communion. He holds a crystal reliquary hewn from a solid piece of quartz with rough, natural edges, whose interior glows with soft amber brilliance.

Each of the other sages takes their place on the blanketed floor, seated cross-legged as if for meditation. Sin Marmot takes their place alongside Mira, and offers you an inviting look to do the same. The Cindaric on the dais speaks …

Welcome, sages and siblings alike, to this most honorable occasion. Tonight, we witness the end of one cycle and the beginning of another.

The other Cindaric sages around you begin chanting a low and soft phrase you can't quite distinguish, as if spoken in a primordial tongue from the dawn of time.

The Cindaric Ritual

Any character who wants to participate in the ceremony can do so with a successful[[/skill religion 14]] or [[/skill performance 16]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] or [[/skillCheck performance 16]] check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] or [[/knowledge souls]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Characters who participate in the ceremony gain one point of Heart Attunement, as described below.

Any character who make a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check can sense that Evesso is hiding something, and that the way he conducts the ceremony has an air of disingenuous performance to it.

  • Result of 19+ Critical Success: The character can sense a hint of curiosity in Evesso's glances towards the party members and Sin, particularly towards any allies that happen to be arcane or divine spellcasters.

After a moment, Evesso continues.

These sacred pyreflies have completed their last lunar cycle. They have lived, propagated, and now gather here to make their own journey into the beyond. We take these creatures into our souls, renumeration for the absence of their own. The heartblood beats eternal.

The sages continue their chant as the speaker opens the lid of the crystal reliquary. As he does, a luminous host of a dozen aged pyreflies slowly drifts from the vessel and into the open air of the Sanctorum. Each of these tiny bioluminescent insects floats towards one of the sages, as if drawn to the chant. With hands cupped to cradle a pyrefly as it lands, the sages finish their chant as the light of each pyrefly slowly fades.

Seated next to you, Mira speaks as she regards the deceased pyrefly in her palm.

I witness your passing, and honor your essence.

To your surprise, she ingests the dead pyrefly with a solemn and deliberate swallow. The other sages follow suit, speaking the same phrase before swallowing their own pyrefly. Mira looks to you with a smile, and Sin holds her cupped hands out in wistful anticipation.

Whether or not the characters participate in the ceremony themselves, Evesso concludes the event as he consumes his own pyrefly. The congregation is left to indulge in idle chat and meditation.

Heart Attunement: Ritual Participants

Each character who successfully participates in the Cindaric ritual advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 cindaric1CorpinArrivalRitual]] at the conclusion of the event.

A Place to Rest

Once the evening ceremony has concluded, a Cindaric Sage escorts Sin and the party to the dormitories and provides them with two @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.g5ZhafC273TnlsRm]{Empty Dormitory} chambers which they can share. The characters can choose between themselves how to divide the two rooms.

As the party settles in to rest, a shift in the narrative occurs when a note to Sin is slid beneath the door by an unseen stranger. Characters in the same room with Sin are the first to notice the note. When the moment is right, read the following aloud:

Just then, you see a small piece of folded parchment slide beneath the dormitory door. Even from here, you can see the handwritten text inked upon its top fold:

To: Initiate Marmot.
For your eyes only.

A Passed Note

As the party is preparing to rest for the evening, a mysterious @UUID[Item.sgtcxR29Zf7ukZyP]{Note to Sin} is slipped beneath the door of the dormitory where Sin lodges.

The note's interior reads:

Heed my words, for they are astoundingly true. There is a necromancer lurking among the sages here at Corpin Sanctuary. As outsiders, it seems you and your party are the most capable to investigate this dangerous affair. Most importantly, your intentions here seem noble and just.

Please, rid the Sanctuary of this invader, for all our sakes. And be careful to avoid suspicion — the eyes of the necromancer are everywhere.

The note is written anonymously and conveys the accusation that there is a necromancer lurking among the sages at Corpin Sanctuary. As outsiders with seemingly noble intentions, the author of this note wishes for the party to closely investigate the sanctuary and its sages.

Any character who wishes to scrutinize the note can do so, and notices the following with a successful [[/skill investigation 11]] [[/skillCheck awareness 11]] check:

  • The handwriting is unfamiliar to everyone in the party.

  • The ink is remarkably fresh.

If the characters open the door to look for whomever might have left the note, there is no sign of them, nor can any footsteps he be heard retreating from the empty corridor.

If a character casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLocateCrea]{Locate Creature} spell in an attempt attempts to use magic to identify the letter's owner, their effort falls short. Unbeknownst to the party, the original owner of the letter (Avwynn Taol) is protected from divinations by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.aU62xVUBYkAQWIHv]{Nondetection} spell against magical divination.

After receiving this note, Sin wishes to confer with the party.

Sin's Suspicions

Sin Marmot is relatively unfamiliar with the actual practice of necromancy, and solicits the characters for conversation about the note's revelation and whether or not it has ties to their previous encounters with undead. Sin is also eager to discuss:

  • Who could possibly be a suspect, based on the people the party has met since arriving — including the Cindaric Sages and visitors alike.

  • The relationship of Corpin Sanctuary to the Cindaric Temple in Ordain, and what kinds of strains might currently be affecting it.

  • Her trust in the Cindaric Sages as an organization, and the honest desire to keep the charitable order safe from those who might befoul it.

After some discussion about their collective thoughts and suspicions, Sin establishes a plan with the party to begin an investigation in the morning following a long (if watchful) rest vigilant Rest.

Concluding the Event

Milestone Point

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

Once the party is ready to rest, mark this event as complete. Perform a long rest or Advance Time to trigger the subsequent event [[/eventState cindaric1Investigation]].
Corpin Arrival.soverview: Sin Marmot and the party arrive at the Corpin Sanctuary, a remote enclave of the Cindaric Order located roughly one day's travel west of Ordain. Following a warm welcome by the Cindaric Sages, the characters will begin to learn about the traditions of their esteemed order — and the challenges they currently face.
Corpin Arrival.sexposition:
As you approach the entrance to Corpin Sanctuary, Sin gazes upon the place with an intense measure of reverence and awe. The impressive stone steps of the enclave's entrance ascend toward a great oaken doorway that exudes a remarkable sense of history and tradition. Your ally offers you a smile and says:

We made it this far, I suppose it's time for me to become introduced with the sages … I also wouldn't say no to a hot meal, if there are any to be had!

Just then, the doors open to reveal a Kiska femme clad in the burgundy robes of a Cindaric Sage. Her smoky voice addresses you with a measure of overt officiousness, apprehensive of your arrival.

Welcome to Corpin Sanctuary. And please don't be startled; being perched upon a mountainside has its advantages. I hope your hike up the hill wasn't too strenuous, and that your journey to our doors has been kind. Please, come in. And tell me: what brings you to our little enclave?
Corpin Arrival.ssummary: We traveled with Sin to Corpin Sanctuary, a Cindaric enclave on Mial Mountain a day's travel west of Ordain. We were welcomed by the sages with open arms, but our suspicions mounted when details about a necromancer began to surface — rumored to lurk somewhere amongst the Sanctuary's peaceful confines.

The Blockaded Bridge.name: The Blockaded Bridge
The Blockaded Bridge.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social and exploration event, the party is halted upon arriving at the Ordani Skywalk by a squadron of Burnished Hand who rebuff their progress. In this event the party can:

  • Learn why travel across the bridge has been recently restricted, and figure out how to get past the blockade.

  • Encounter a company of Lumek warriors, captained by Luna Kerrowrath who seek to cross from Ordain towards the Arctus Plateau, but are denied.

Halted Passage

The Main Bridge of Ordain is restricted by order of the Ordinate in response to heightening unrest from bandit raids, mysterious creature attacks, and rumors of undead in the Wedgelands. The guards here are stopping travelers to question them and ensure that they pose no risk to the safety of Ordani citizens.

As you size up the crowds, you identify three groups butting up against the blockade — a collection of refugees arguing with a bunch of Sages and Ordinate personnel, a checkpoint of Hallows and Veiled Chain inspectors holding up a train of merchants, and lastly two squads of soldiers locked in a heated argument as a few exasperated city officials watch things unfold.

It looks like you won't be able to just walk into Ordain today.

The party will need to investigate these groups if they want to gather more information and get past the blockage.

The Refugee Problem

A Cindaric Sage speaks up toward a crowd of murmuring refugees, the lot of them growing quiet and attentive.

Good folk, hear me! We have done all we could today to admit your number. We have reached the limit of what the city can bear —

The crowd's discontent immediately rises, the murmur returning, with a few frustrated shouts raising above the din. The Sage holds out their hands, attempting to placate them.

Please understand that we are working as hard as we can to admit everyone, and allow them to pass, but right now the city is focused on merchants and keeping the supply chains running. We beg you understand, and show us patience in these most trying times!

The crowd's displeasure turns into open, angry disdain, but it never grows past yelling and complaints, as a handful of Trade House guards step forward to shield the Sage, and dissuade the refugees from getting too upset.

Nearby you a short human man throws his hands up, and begins to complain, eventually turning to you.

Unbelievable! Least they could do is bring us some bedrolls, or food. Bad enough sitting here another day, but sleeping on stone too? Can you believe this?

Fed Up Farmer

If the party interacts with the fellow arguing with the ordinate, he'll introduce himself.

Oh, hey, where are my manners! I'm Stohb, Stohb Krunder. This is my wife Kiona, and these are my children Vinda and Jidds. Looks like we're all in the same boat. Sorry to say you're gonna be stuck waiting alongside us.

If the party lets Stohb keep chatting, or asks for his story, he'll happily share it.

Used to run Krunderfield Farms in the Golden Flats, at least until the damned raiders came through and burned it to the ground, twice! First time the got the and mill, second time they got the fields, which eventually got the house…

Anyway! We're headed up to Redrak Fields to meet up with my brother Sterhb. He runs Krunderfield Ranch with the rest of the family there. I figure we can fold into his operations until we're back on our feet.

If the party asks about the backed up refugees and why everyone's stuck, Stohb can only offer his view of things.

Can't rightly say. We've been here two days and they keep telling us that they'll let us in once things calm down, but there's nobody leaving the city, just coming in. Don't really know how anything's going to change. Frankly, if things don't get moving fast, I'm not sure I'll be able to afford to get us to Redrak.

If the party offers Stohb some money, or gets his family through the blockade, he thanks them profusely.

You're too kind! I'm afraid I don't have any way to repay you, but know you've got my eternal gratitude! If you're ever out round Krunderfield Ranch past Redrak, stop by, I'll at least see that you get a nice meal.

Cindaric Stoppage

If the party speaks with the Sage that made the announcement, they can glean some insights into the situation:

Ah, most sorry, perhaps you missed the announcement: the way into the city is closed until tomorrow. However if you wait until the next dawn, we will be admitting more refugees in. We presently are prioritizing those with skills that can directly impact food production, magic healing, and the like. If you or anyone you know fits that measure, speak with the Trade House representative when they are here tomorrow. They arrive midday and leave be early afternoon.

[[/culture emberArcturian]] and [[/culture emberOrdani]] characters know that the city should be more than capable of handling the influx of people into the city, and this blockage is highly unusual.

Meanwhile, characters with [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/knowledge trade]] know that while the Temple's resources are not infinite, it absolutely has the clout and resources to make sure all these people are fed and comfortable.

If the party points out this discrepancy to the Sage, he attempts to offer a deflection:

Not quite so any longer! Things have become difficult in Ordain. Much of the Golden Flats has begun flooding into the City, either passing through to Redrak, or cramming the city's inns and streets with refugees. Not only that, but with the falling production in the Flats, food is only coming in now by ship or from Redrak, and grain only grows so fast.

So no, the city can't support all the refugees right now.

If the party asks about the narrow application window, the sage doesn't seem to see the issue and makes excuses:

Yes, well, the Trade House is very busy, they can only spare so many people for so long. They are doing the best they can, I assure you.

[[/path emberCindaricInitiate]] characters are able to speak with the Sages handling the refugees, and talk their way in. They will let the initiate's entire party though as well. The sage motions for the guards to move.

Let them through, they are with the Temple, move aside!

If the party would like to convince the sage to let more people through (such as Stohb and his family) then a successful [[/skill persuasion 16]] [[/skill diplomacy 16]]check is necessary.

The Ordinate Checkpoint

Trade House guards form a checkpoint as Hallows inspectors move down lines of wagons, looking through goods and items. Alongside them, Veiled Chain investigators speak to merchants, and collect reports. The entire scene feels less chaotic than anywhere else along the bridge, but there is an air of agitation among the waiting caravans used to moving freely across the grand Skywalk.

A Trade Guard walks down the rows of carts and people, calling out:

Clear the central lane! Clear the central lane! Travelers on the right, merchants on the left. Be prepared with manifests, Trading House badges, and other merchant identification! If you are are shipping food or perishables, speak up!

She moves past you, barely sparing a glance. The line trundles along slowly, foot traffic and the odd mounted traveler moving past you on the right. Every now and then a caravan gets cleared to move forward, prompting carts to take the central space and head on down the bridge.

Orderly Processes

If the party chooses to wait in line and access the city via the traveler's entry line, it takes a while to be seen, but eventually they are met with a Veiled Chain investigator and watched by a Burnished Hand soldier. The questions begin mundane, asking if anyone in the group is ill, injured, diseased, or similar.

Eventually, the questions expand to ask if they have had any run-ins with bandits, noticed any identifying marks or symbols on them, and where they were encountered. This is further expanded to cover monsters, and then the undead.

They are also asked to turn over any clearly corrupted, abyssal, or necromantic artifacts they have, as they are being confiscated by Ordinate law to help protect the people of the plateau.

If the party wishes to lie their way though the checkpoint either to avoid giving accurate info, or to hide items that would be taken, the group must must succeed on a group [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skill deception 14]] check to fool the investigator. On success the party is cleared through and given no further questions. Failure tips the investigator off that there's something amiss, and may result in their packs being searched.

However, if the party answers truthfully about their encounters, and hands over any items, their names will be told the following:

Sounds as though you've had an eventful time of it. I'll be entering your names in a record for the Veiled Chain in case we need to follow up with more questions. You're not in any trouble, but we might need more details as we continue looking into things.

They'll then be allowed to cross the bridge and enter the city.

Smuggled Inside

It is possible to hide in a caravan about to move through the blockade, which requires the party to make a group [[/skill stealth 14]] [[/skill stealth 14]]check. If at least half the party succeed, they are not discovered, and can ride the wagon into the city. Otherwise they are found, and kicked out.

The Detained Lumek

As you approach the group of armored warriors their voices become clearer over the general din and chaos around the blockade. A burly Kivahr man throws his hands up in response to something a Lumek woman said just before you arrived.

You can't just go stomping across the plateau looking for the undead. You need to take your soldiers to the Ordinate, meet with the council, and work with everyone else. I don't know what part of that is unclear!

The Lumek woman sneers, eyes flaring with fire.

Unacceptable! I can't believe the Sages, Ordinate or you Brass cowards can stand by and debate how and where and why we should be acting while the undead are growing in the region. I knew I shouldn't have come to this city.

The Burnished Hand officer bristles.

First of all, Flameguard, we're the Burnished Hand, second of all we're not cowards, and finally —

The pair devolve into arguing once more as a nearby Ordinate official tries to interject to no avail. Eventually the Burnished hand falls silent, crossing his burly arms over his chest, and the Lumek woman stomps back to her waiting soldiers while radiating frustration.

It's only then that a nearby Ordinate official takes note of you.

Sorry, the Skywalk is presently restricting traffic through this area, if you're with the refugees, you want to find the Sages, and if you're a merchant or general traveler, the Ordinate have a checkpoint that will sort you out. This is a separate issue.

On the Ordain side of the bridge, the party encounters a company of Lumek discussing with a regiment of Burnished Hand. The Lumek wish to venture out into the Wedgelands and confront the rumors of undead head-on. The Burnished Hand are insisting that they return to Cindarin temple and discuss their plans with the Speaker.

@Embed[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]{Luna Karrowrath}

Burnished Officer

Asking the Burnished Hand officer what's going on, his answer is straightforward:

Look, the help is welcome, but these Flameguard come in here, stomping around, causing more chaos, it doesn't improve things. I understand they have probably killed more undead than us, but this isn't their war, it's ours. They can work with us, or they can get lost.

Ordinate Official

Asking the official what is going on, she gives a brief overview:

This whole blockade is a massive joint venture to address everything going on in the region by first collecting information, and making sure that the city doesn't take on more refugees than it can handle. It's heartbreaking to hold up people on the skywalk, but the spike in people coming over the bridge lately due to monster and bandit attacks has begun to strain the city.

Reading Luna

Luna is not especially difficult to read, as her zealous nature and drive is always on display. A successful [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skill deception 12]] check leads you to believe she is not only being forthright and honest, but strongly believes everything she says.

The Flameguard Company

[[/path emberFlameguardMilitia]] characters suspect that this may be Luna Karrowrath, the champion of Lumé, a legendary warrior that was responsible for slaying a powerful necromancer who laid siege to her home city. The fact she's here could be a very bad sign, but there's probably nobody better qualified for the task of hunting undead.

If the party asks what she knows about the the undead in the region, she has a certain answer:

You mark my words: there is something out there in the plateau that is causing this, and if it's not found and stopped immediately, this place could start looking like my homeland real fast, and I don't have much faith in the Ordinate's ability to defend itself.

Asking why she doubts the Ordinate, her answer is a simple, but dramatic one:

The locals can't handle some bandits and monsters, what hope do they have against the undead?

Risen dead are relentless, and their masters know that time is always on their side. Every fight is one of attrition, but only for you, they only grow stronger over time, each loss you suffer adding to their ranks. Worse, fighting the dead takes a toll. It breaks a person's spirit having to stare into the lifeless eyes of friends and family as you cut down their undead shells again and again.

A successful [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skill diplomacy 12]]check sees a thread of deep, personal hurt in that statement. Luna's battle against the undead has left her with scars that reach into her very spirit, and a brief, haunted look in her eye confirms her mind went somewhere else briefly.

Heading Into Ordain

[[/path emberFlameguardMilitia]] characters can easily convince Luna to vouch for the party, allowing them into the city. If asked, she'll nod and say:

Hey, Ordinates, Burnished Hand … here are the reinforcements we've been waiting for. More Flameguard for the hunt! We're going to send them into the city to get settled and resupply. Any objections?

The Ordinate official and Burnished hand officer appear skeptical but seem unwilling to say anything.

Bypassing the Blockage

If the party is accompanied by Sin bearing an invitation to Cindarin temple they are permitted to pass without issue. If the party is journeying alone they must answer some questions before being allowed to proceed.

Sinvitation

If the party is accompanied by Sin bearing the burnished hand documentation from Steros, or if the party obtained a copy for themselves, they are permitted to pass without issue. Otherwise, they will need to go through the Ordinate checkpoint, and answer some question.

However, a party that wants to by pass the blockage entirely has some other ways to do about it, though none are guaranteed to work.

Useful Connections

[[/path emberCindaricInitiate]] characters are able to speak with the Sages handling the refugees, and talk their way in. They will let the initiate's entire party though as well. (See "Cindaric Stoppage" above).
