[[/path emberFlameguardMilitia]] characters can speak with Luna, and get her to vouch for the party, taking them back into the city. (See "Heading Into Ordain" above).

Sneaking Past

It is possible to hide in a caravan about to move through the blockade, which requires the party to make a group [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skill deception 14]] check. If at least half the party succeed, they are not discovered, and can ride the wagon into the city. Otherwise they are found, and kicked out.

If the party wants to wait until the following day, they can hide among refugee groups being ushered across the bridge, which requires the party to make a group [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skill deception 14]] or [[/skill stealth 14]]check. If at least half the party succeed, they are not discovered and get over the blockage safely. Otherwise they are spotted by Ordinate personnel and sent back the way they came.

Alternate Routes

The party may attempt to go around the bridge, either by land or sea, but it will present a sizable detour. The canyon itself is not easily gotten into except from specific locations along its edges, so the party will be looking at hours of travel before they are on the other side. However, no one will stop them from doing this, and it only costs them time.

Akon Attunement: Orderly Passage

If the party manages to traverse the blockade in an orderly fashion, advance each character's [[/attunement emberAkon +1 cindaric1BridgeOrderly]] at the conclusion of the event.

Orbis Attunement: Deceptive Passage

If the party successfully deceives the the Burnished Hand to traverse the blockade, advance each character's [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 cindaric1BridgeDeceptive]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Secret Passage

If the party successfully sneaks past or through the blockade, advance each character's [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 cindaric1BridgeSecret]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once the party is across the blockade, they can carry on toward Ordain.

Next Steps

After successfully traversing the bridge, whether by permission, force, or guile, the party may continue onwards towards Ordain and the [[/eventState cindaric1Temple]] event which concludes this quest.
The Blockaded Bridge.soverview: The Burnished Hand have established a blockade upon the Ordani Skywalk, the great bridge connecting the Arctus Plateau to the city of Ordain beyond. These militia restrict access to the city, permitting only those with official business to pass.
The Blockaded Bridge.sexposition:
The steady flow of traffic seems to have become backed up here, a seeming impossibility until you draw closer and realize that a hasty blockade of momentous size has been erected right through the center of the Skywalk. The blockage spans the full width of the Skywalk and is comprised of a haphazard collection commandeered caravan wagons, Cindaric Sages, Burnished Hane fighters, Trade House guards, Hallows personnel, and even a handful of Anachraenum members.

It seems that Ordain has scrounged up everyone it could to stop anyone from passing over the canyon, and the gathering masses are anything but pleased about it.
The Blockaded Bridge.ssummary: We ran into a massive blockade on the Ordani Skywalk, and had to find a way past it.

A Sage Welcome.name: A Sage Welcome
A Sage Welcome.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event introduces the party to the great @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.GlbJezRw2ecnVIsx]{Cindarin Temple} of Ordain and its residents (whether they decided to travel alongside Sin Marmot or not). In this event, the characters can:

  • Visit the hallowed Cindarin Temple in the heart of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}.

  • Meet several influential leaders of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, including @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} and @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith}.

  • Witness @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} make their formal pledge to join the legendary druidic order.

  • Discuss the various troubles that have been affecting the Arctus Plateau.

A Reunion with Sin

Music: Sin's Theme

When the party reunites with Sin, play [[/soundscape music sinTheme sinTheme]].

If the party has arrived at Cindarin Temple in Ordain independently of Sin Marmot, they'll encounter each other at this time, as the characters first make their way into the temple's inviting sanctuary. Read the following aloud immediately after you've finished "Setting the Scene."

Before you make it very far, the familiar voice of Sin Marmot echoes throughout the sanctuary. You turn to see your Keth friend eagerly bounding from the recesses of the large entry chamber to greet you.

Well, aren't you all a sight for sore eyes! I'm so glad you made it. This place is amazing. I can't wait for you to meet everyone. So tell me … what did I miss!?

@Embed[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]

Sin's Journey

The party has a few moments before meeting the Cindaric Sages to catch up with Sin about their respective travels to Ordain. Sin will tell the characters about any events of this quest that they missed — including an encounter with sodden undead at Keeper's Crossing, the plight of the Otherhood-hassled refugees, and the Burnished Hand's investigation of Corpin Sanctuary.

If the characters manage to convey a tale about their own heroism in the face of undead threats (such as during @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush with Death} et al.), Sin is awarded one point of Heroic Inspiration to use as the party (or the Gamemaster) sees fit.

Alternately, if the party has arrived at Cindarin Temple with Sin, the characters can take a moment to discuss the grandeur of the sanctuary and their plans to meet the Sages here before they proceed.

Music: Default

Once the party has finished this dialogue with Sin, return to the default music: [[/soundscape music reset]].

Exploring Cindarin Temple

Once the party has had ample time to catch up with Sin (whether or not they've arrived here at the temple together), they will become acquainted with the leadership of Cindarin Temple.

As you linger in the sanctuary's antechamber, you become acutely aware of the enchanted grandeur on display deeper within. Long, sonorous chimes ring out from every corner of the temple, where Cindarics ritualistically meditate over bronze bowls that "sing" as the sages interact with them. Meanwhile, magical light sources — from inkaro lanterns to ever-burning torches — shed their soft amber luminance all about you.

One sage in particular takes note of your group, a spectral-armed Signborn scholar, who saunters over to join you with a cordial greeting.

Welcome to Corpin Sanctuary, friends. I am Lilla Arien, who some call the Second Sage. What brings you to our most holy abode?

@Embed[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]

@Embed[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]

Meeting the Sages

@UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} invites the party to join her on a short tour of the Cindarin Temple facility's pubic spaces, culminating in a meeting with the Steward to the Holy Speaker, @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith}.

Lilla and Vinarith are eager to hear what Sin and the characters have to say about their journey here — particularly when it comes to encounters with undead foes, Otherhood of Fortune agents, and the Sanguinaries of the Bloodwoods.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skill diplomacy 15]]check is able to detect a small amount of trepidation in Sin's demeanor, as if the druid is looking for the right time to mention their desire to join the ranks of the Cindaric Sages here.

  • If one of the party members speaks for Sin or compels their ally to speak their mind to the Sages, that character gains one point of Heroic Inspiration.

  • Lilla will eventually note Sin's trepidation for herself, and will ask the young Keth what's on their mind.

Once Sin's ambitions have been exposed, the temperament of the Cindaric Sages here shifts from mere hospitality to one of exuberance and support. Lilla Arien shows particular interest in aiding the young druid on her journey, while Vinarith excuses himself to take care of official Cindaric matters.

Following the elucidation of Sin's goal to join the Cindarics, a look of pride crosses Lilla Arien's face, marked by a wry smile and tinged with an acute element of curiosity.

We are fortunate to have such passion for the Heartblood in our midsts. If this compulsion to join the Cindaric Sages has any truth to it, you are certainly most welcome here, young Sin Marmot. Our order could only benefit from the unbridled enthusiasm you display, alongside your riveting evidence of skill (however anecdotal it may be).

Sin is overjoyed with satisfaction, grinning ear to ear as she looks to you for casual approval. Lilla continues, procuring a scroll and quill from her satchel with the enchanted weightlessness of a mage hand spell. The animated quill begins scrawling something on the scroll as the parchment unfurls in front of her.

If your aim is true, we can begin the proceedings, and foster your initiation three days hence — after you've had ample time to read and comprehend our scriptures. Your friends are welcome to come and go as they please, but our facilities here only provide for our sages and initiates, when it comes to food and lodging.

If this is your first time in Ordain, the city's vast amenities should provide a most-welcome distraction from your toils and troubles. This letter of introduction should grant you hospitality when it is most needed.

Lilla's scroll floats towards your party, hovering mid-air for you to grab at your leisure.

And with that, I have other duties I must attend to. It has been a most sincere pleasure, my new friends. Sin, please make yourself comfortable and one of the other sages will be with you shortly to help you get settled. Good day to you all, and may the light of the Heartblood illuminate your way.

Sin's Initiation

The party will be invited to return to the temple at a later time, but the characters are dismissed for now. They can continue to explore Ordain while Sin settles in to begin their training.

Sin Marmot beams with pride as the Second Sage retreats into the facility to complete her tasks. Your group idles beneath the amber lights of the temple's sanctorum, where a statue of Adonia — the city's founder and the first Holy Speaker — stands proudly in a pose of vigilant benevolence. After a moment, Sin speaks to you with a bittersweet hesitation in their voice.

I hate to say goodbye again so soon, but it looks like I have a few things to take care of on my own. Have fun in the city! And don't do anything too exciting without me. As thrilling as the next three of days will be, I have to say I'll miss your company. See you on the other side?

Concluding the Event

With that, the characters must say goodbye to Sin Marmot for the next three days as their druid ally settles in at Cindarin Temple. A summons for Sin's formal initiation is forthcoming, and the party is free to explore Ordain as they see fit in the meantime.

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Subsequent Quests

This event concludes the "Crumbling Sanctuary" quest, but Sin's journey will continue during Chapter 3 with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders} quest.
A Sage Welcome.soverview: The party arrives at the great Cindarin Temple in the heart of Ordain, home of the Cindaric Sages. Sin Marmot introduces themselves to the Sages and meets some of their most influential members. The party comes to understand more about several emergent troubles facing the Arctus Plateau as they meet the Cindaric Sages for themselves.
A Sage Welcome.sexposition: The doors to the mighty Cindarin Temple are flanked by two guards clad in lustrous bronze mail, who seem to be soldiers of the Burnished Hand stationed here to provide security for the faithful. These bright-eyed sentinels regard you with a curt smile and a quick nod as you cross the threshold into the majestic temple sanctuary.
A Sage Welcome.ssummary: We journeyed to the storied Cindarin Temple in Ordain, where we met with various leaders of the famed Cindaric Sages. We were fortunate enough to witness and support Sin Marmot's introduction to the benevolent order, who accepted the young druid with open arms; an initiation ceremony is scheduled three days from now. With the saga of Corpin Sanctuary behind us, and Sin's imminent acclimation to the Cindarics, the sprawling city of Ordain awaits our discovery.

Corpin Condemned.name: Corpin Condemned
Corpin Condemned.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event introduces the party to @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver} of the Burnished Hand, who has arrived at Corpin Sanctuary to issue an edict of condemnation against the monastery's sages. In this event, the characters can:

  • Learn about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} and their accusations.

  • Discuss the matter with Steros Kraver, @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}, and others.

  • Provide evidence to Steros that either implicates or exonerates both Mira Wavehorn and the Sanguinary @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}.

  • Choose to side with either Steros or with Mira, who will present the party with a duly-earned reward for their efforts.

The Burnished Hand Arrives

As the party investigates the sounds of war horn and marching feet, they encounter a platoon of well-armed soldiers — two dozen Burnished Hand Protectors, led by the warrior Steros Kraver. At the behest of the Holy Speaker, these militant protectors have arrived from Ordain to take command of Corpin Sanctuary, with or without Mira Wavehorn's cooperation.

You arrive at the Sanctuary gates to witness the imminent arrival of a small war force of well-armed soldiers, clad in heavy bronze mail polished brighter than the sun. The crest on their shield bears the somewhat familiar image of a symmetrical crimson hand with roots like a mighty oak. A handsome white-haired warrior with a mighty greataxe leads this stalwart platoon. He surveys the Sanctuary from afar with an air of contempt and disappointment.

@Embed[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA count=24]

@Embed[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]

Enclosing Hand

If the party members wish to determine how familiar they are with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} and their historical ties to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, the following skill checks can provide some perspective on what they know:

[[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] The character has knowledge of the Burnished Hand's history as protectors of the Cindaric Sages, and that they both have significant holdings in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}.

  • Result of 15+ Success: The character is familiar with additional details about the Burnished Hand, such as their residence at the Rusted Fortress on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CVV5b22IksTdg7hy]{Bura Island}, and their adherence to ritualistic @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.k7bsL7HRGcz4P314]{Oaken} technique. Early generations of the Burnished Hand included @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.0YvoRkcs1BxtRiQz]{Vrjnhar} warriors and clerics amongst their ranks.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The white-haired warrior that leads this group is known as Steros Kraver, and his reputation with his greataxe is nearly as large as the massive axe itself.

With a successful [[/skill insight 13]] or [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] a character can easily intuit that these soldiers are aggressively prepared for conflict, and maintain a battle-readiness despite the current lack of an immediate threat. The leader in particular seems poised to deliver some kind of order or proclamation. It's apparent that some of the soldiers are ready for a fight, as evident by the hands on their sword hilts and the alacrity of their battle formation.

[[/path emberCindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on all of these checks, and also possess a basic understanding about the role the Burnished Hand plays in lending protective aid to the Cindarics during times of war and natural disaster.

Alternately, characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] or [[/knowledge warfare]] can readily take note of the vintage quality and elaborate craftsmanship on display with the arms and armor of these soldiers. There is a distinct non-Arcturian aspect to the designs and adornments of the bronze armor, which seems to hail from a different continent during a previous age — perhaps Oaken in origin.

If the party fails to identify the Burnished Hand and is completely ignorant of their role, Sin Marmot may offer some insight of their own:

Sin whispers beneath their mask.

The Burnished Hand! From what I know, they protect the Sages in times of trouble … but we already handled things here. Better late than never, I guess …

Once the party has had ample time to survey the approaching battle force of Burnished Hand soldiers, these militant interlopers close the distance to arrive at the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.WHdKr6CkT5xF7lqr]{Entry Courtyard}, where they gather in eager anticipation. Steros Kraver steps forward to address the Sages and their guests:

The soldiers arrive at the rocky promontory that adjoins the Sanctuary courtyard, where they congregate in formation. Their white-haired leader steps forward with determination as he procures a scroll from a satchel at his side. He unfurls the parchment and begins to read its proclamation aloud:

By order of the Holy Speaker of Ordain, Corpin Sanctuary and its custodians have hereby been accused of the following transgressions … dereliction of duty, gross negligence of the needy and afflicted, the instigation of dissent against Cindarin Temple, and the provision of safe harbor for necromancy.

Mira Wavehorn, as the leader of Corpin Sanctuary, how do you answer for these misdeeds?

Mira shrugs off the trepidation of the other Corpin sages and strides forward to meet the white-haired warrior. They exchange heated words, which you struggle to make out against the incessant howl of morning mountain wind.

Proclaimed Condemnation

The party can attempt to listen in on Mira's conversation with Steros, but any attempts to join in at the moment are first met with trepidation from Mira, who politely turns the characters away with a simple gesture and a shake of her head.

Any character that makes a successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check is able to recognize the heavy tone of the conversation, including an unmistakable air of stern officiousness that surrounds Steros. Mira stands resolute in her defense of the Sanctuary, emphatic and hopefully defiant as she explains the situation at Corpin to the militant interloper.

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] allows characters to hear some aspects of the muted conversation, including the following details:

  • The Holy Speaker's disappointment with the current state of affairs, and a condemnation of Mira's abilities as a leader.

  • A brief interrogation about what transpired here, and how the undead gained access to the Sanctuary.

  • Mira's explanation about what happened.

  • Mira's defense of the Sanctuary and her gratitude for the timely arrival of the party to Corpin.

Any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} spell @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.telecognition000] to read Steros or Mira's mind is able to discern this information as their surface thoughts. Deeper probing reveals the following:

  • Mira's emotional state is a mix of worry and self-doubt, and the very fate of Corpin Sanctuary looms large in her mind.

  • Steros' emotional state is full of concern and hesitation, and the purported tombs below the Sanctuary loom large in his mind, along with the stern edicts of the Holy Speaker.

An Interview with Steros

After the conversation with Mira, Steros requests to meet the party to interview them about what happened here at Corpin Sanctuary. The party can choose to either hide or reveal this information as they see fit, including what they know about Mira Wavehorn and the Sanguinary Avwynn Taol.

After a moment of conversation, Mira lowers her head in defeat, noticeably shaken by this unforeseen encounter. The white-haried warrior glances your way with equal measures of suspicion and curiosity before he strides confidently to meet you.

I understand you played a pivotal role in what happened here. My name is Steros Kraver, of the Burnished Hand. By edict of the Holy Speaker of Ordain, I have some questions for your party that need answers. Good answers.

Meeting Steros

Steros solicits the party for answers, which can easily result in an interrogation rather than a conversation (depending on how the characters handle it). Steros is initially somewhat hostile to the group, and will only soften his attitude at the party's behest. Success on the following social skill checks can affect the warrior's disposition towards the characters:

[[/skill deception 13]] [[/skillCheck deception 13]]The character is able to deceive Steros into believing that their agenda (whatever it may be) is allied with the aims of the Burnished Hand.

[[/skill intimidation 13]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 13]] Steros is impressed by the character's brash demonstration of authority and confidence.

[[/skill persuasion 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] The character appeals successfully to Steros' curiosity and righteous code of ethics.

[[/check insight 13]] A casual air of understanding that surrounds the character puts Steros at ease.

Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} spell use of @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.telecognition000] reveals that Steros' emotional state has shifted from concern and hesitation to curiosity. Meanwhile, the purported tombs below the Sanctuary loom large in his mind, along with the stern edicts of the Holy Speaker, and the possible motives of the party members themselves. Any character who successfully probes Steros' mind gains @Advantage[2] on the skill checks listed above.

Kraver's Inquest

Steros has three main questions for the party, which they can answer with either the truth or a lie. Characters who succeed on one or more of the skill checks during "Meeting Steros" above gain @Advantage[2] on skill checks made to deceive Steros.

Any character who attempts to deceive Steros with a lie during this inquest must make a successful [[/skill deception 15]] [[/skill deception 15]] check to adequately convince the warrior about the veracity of their ruse. Otherwise, he remains skeptical until they tell him the truth.

Regarding the Necromancer:

Tell me of this necromancer. Who were they, and how did they infiltrate the Sanctuary? Furthermore, how did they gain access to the ancient tombs below?

  • If the party tells the truth about Evesso, Steros and the Cindaric leadership launches an additional inquest into how the necromancer managed this clandestine operation. Mira Wavehorn is held responsible for the folly. If Evesso survived the encounter, the necromancer becomes a known fugitive in the eyes of the Burnished Hand and Ordain's various protectorates. Wanted posters and bounties for Evesso's capture are quickly disseminated throughout the plateau.

  • If the party successfully lies about Evesso, Steros starts to maintain a list of suspects (including Sin and the party members themselves), and reluctantly considers Mira Wavehorn to be a potential aide to the necromancer's cause.

Regarding the Sanguinaries:

The Holy Speaker suspects that the Sanguinaries, our enemies to the north, have a vested interest in the downfall of the Cindarics. Did you find any evidence of Sanguinary activity during your stay here?

  • If the party tells the truth about Avwynn, she loses her ability to blend in among the Cindarin Sages and other Ordani society without the benefit of a disguise.

  • If the party successfully lies about Avwynn, she eventually hears word of their benevolence and subsequently invites them to consider a future alliance with the Sanguinaries.

Regarding Mira Wavehorn:

Mira Wavehorn has consistently fallen short of her expected duties in the face of disaster. Tell me, do you find Sage Wavehorn to be a competent leader here? Was this calamity a result of her inactions? The people of the Arctus Plateau rely on your testimony.

  • If the party vouches for Mira, Steros will reluctantly allow her to maintain some of her leadership duties at Corpin Sanctuary for the time being. As soon as she smoke clears, Mira rewards them with a @UUID[Item.SVX7oYsEn5fz40yU]{Cindaric Writ}, which can be used to grant access through the Burnished Hand blockades located at the Ordani Skywalk or at Ordain's outer gates. (see "Corpin Farewell" below).

  • If the party condemns Mira's leadership, Steros relieves her of all immediate duties and strips her of her informal title as the Sanctuary's leader. Steros promptly rewards them with a @UUID[Item.7hJfKeIw9g2ob3w6]{Burnished Seal}, which can be used to grant access through the Burnished Hand blockades located at the Ordani Skywalk or at Ordain's outer gates.

Event Outcomes

Before concluding this event, be sure to mark either the Avwynn Secret or Avwynn Exposed event outcome, depending on whether or not the party provided evidence to Steros of Avwynn's presence and affiliation as a Sanguinary.

Additionally, mark either the Mira Protected or Mira Condemned event outcome, depending on whether the party supported Mira and refuted the Burnished Hand's charges or condemned Mira and attested to her shortcomings.

Cora Attunement: Mira Protected

If the party chooses to protect Mira Wavehorn from the Burnished Hand's inquest, advance each character's [[/attunement emberCora +1 cindaric1CorpinCondemnedMiraProtected]] at the conclusion of the event.

Luxarum Attunement: Mira Condemned

If the party chooses to condemn Mira Wavehorn's leadership, advance each character's [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 cindaric1CorpinCondemnedMiraCondemned]] at the conclusion of the event.

Ragen Attunement: Avwynn Exposed

If the party chooses to expose Avwynn Taol's secret identity as a Sanguinary, advance each character's [[/attunement emberRagen +1 cindaric1CorpinCondemnedMiraCondemned]] at the conclusion of the event.

Mayis Attunement: Avwynn's Secret

If the party chooses to help conceal Avwynn Taol's secret identity as a Sanguinary, advance each character's [[/attunement emberMayis +1 cindaric1CorpinCondemnedMiraCondemned]] at the conclusion of the event.

Corpin Farewell

After the interview with Steros, he orders the party to leave Corpin Sanctuary before the Burnished Hand seals the entire facility. The characters also have a brief moment to chat with Mira Wavehorn before departing. Depending on whether the party protected or condemned Mira during their interview with Steros, the Sage's reaction will be appreciative or disdainful.

If the party protected Mira, she now provides them with a @UUID[Item.SVX7oYsEn5fz40yU]{Cindaric Writ} so they can move freely past Burnished Hand blockades — like those located at the Ordani Skywalk or at Ordain's outer gates.

Meanwhile, Sin Marmot has their own thoughts on what has transpired here. As the party prepares to leave, Sin provides some perspective on their ruminations.

Sin's Reckoning

Needless to say, Sin's once-proud effort to meet and join the Cindaric Sages has been met with unexpected tribulations, not the least of which is the timely advent of a pernicious necromancer (who may or may not have escaped justice during the previous night's battle).

Sin shares the following thoughts and considerations as the party prepares to leave Corpin Sanctuary:

  • It's a shame that Mira Wavehorn is facing such condemnation from the Cindaric leadership and their allies in the Burnished Hand. She was a good leader, and doesn't deserve this scorn.

  • Evesso must have been plotting and scheming about his necromancy in great secrecy to have gone unnoticed among the other Cindarics for so long. Perhaps there are other necromancers who were in league with the Ashka occultist.

  • The party should be careful about presuming too much about the Holy Speaker's attitude about Corpin Sanctuary and the other sages. He doesn't seem to be as benevolent as the stories from Sin's youth have suggested.

  • Can a difference me made by joining the Cindaric Sages after all? Despite all of the doubt and oversight that Evesso's plot has introduced, Sin maintains a steady hope for the future of the beloved druidic order.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After concluding their discussion with the Burnished Hand, the party and Sin may leave Corpin Sanctuary to continue their journey towards Ordain. The road ahead will lead them to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.NbPaM0jLKENCCQFQ]{The Ordani Skywalk} and the events of [[/eventState cindaric1Bridge]].
Corpin Condemned.soverview: As the party and their allies at Corpin Sanctuary recover from the harrowing undead attack, militant forces of the Burnished Hand arrive, led by the warrior Steros Kraver. And though the Burnished Hand normally serves as their protectors, the Sages of Corpin Sanctuary face accusations of negligence from the military order, now bolstered by reports of local dissent and a woeful escalation of the undead threat. Sin Marmot and the party must intervene if they wish to help steer the fate of the Cindarics in the wake of this troublesome development.
Corpin Condemned.sexposition:
The sun rises upon Corpin Sanctuary, shedding light upon a grisly and disquieting scene. Sages toil in silence as they separate the deceased from scattered remnants of skeletal undead. Mira Wavehorn leads this solemn effort, providing guidance to healers who tend the wounded. She glances towards you with a look of determination in her eye.

Just then, the relative calm of the scene is cut short by the blaring sound of a war horn in the valley below. As it echoes up and through the rocky mountain crags, the sonorous tone is met by the rhythmic march of booted feet. It seems a small army has come to Corpin Sanctuary. Mira's look of resolve gives way to one of concern.
Corpin Condemned.ssummary: A military force known as the Burnished Hand arrived at Corpin Sanctuary, captained by a warrior named Steros Kraver. He issued an edict from the Holy Speaker in Ordain, accusing the Cindaric Sages here of a gross negligence that has compromised the safety of the entire Arctus Plateau. We were questioned during an inquest, and provided our own perspective on the events that transpired here. This whole affair could be catastrophic for the sages of Corpin Sanctuary. Only time — and a trip to Cindarin Temple in Ordain — will tell.

Ambushed Refugees.name: Ambushed Refugees
Ambushed Refugees.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this combat and social event, the party and Sin encounter a beleaguered caravan of refugees who are actively under attack by predatory raiders. In this event, the characters can:

  • Join the fray, either defending the refugees or siding with the attackers.

  • Hang back and watch the raiders finish their assault against the refugees.

  • Learn the first-hand story of the refugees and their plight.

  • Investigate clues regarding the identity of the attacking raiders.

Caravan Under attack

The Vrjnhar warrior who fights among and for the refugees is @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb]{Svala Bronwen}, and she readily identifies the party as allies if they choose to assist. (If they hesitate, she beseeches them for aid).

The enemy raiding party consists of @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I]{Gafto the Howler}, @UUID[Actor.XuMfLf3hzG6IUUrC]{Shimz Shimring}, and a cohort of 10 @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H]{Otherhood Raiders}. Combat begins as soon as the encounter starts. Sin Marmot is unwilling to stand aside and let these people die.

Grouped Initiative

Given the size of this encounter, we recommend you use group initiative for the raiders and refugees, rather than having each raider and refugee enter combat as an individual actor.

When this event triggers, you will find two hidden combatants in the combat tracker, one for the Refugees, and one for the Raiders. When one of these groups have their turn start, resolve the actions of all creatures of that type before moving on.

Svala, Gafto and Shimz all have their own initiatives, as should the characters in the party itself.

@Embed[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb]

@Embed[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I]

@Embed[Actor.XuMfLf3hzG6IUUrC]

@Embed[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H count=10]

Otherhood Raider Tactics

The Raiders are fairly coordinated, with two leaders (Gafto and Shimz) directing them. Their goal is to surround and subdue or kill the refugees before taking everything they own.

The Raiders prefer attacking from distance, using @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H.Item.56XUUzooSiJinqz1]{Fiery Shot} @UUID[Actor.ewmcsEVqxwFWu46H.Item.flamingArrow0000] to deal damage and set the terrain on fire, controlling where people can safely go.

If both leaders or more than half the total raiders are killed, their morale breaks and the remaining raiders attempt to flee. If cornered, they throw down their arms and surrender.

If both Gafto and Shimz are killed , or more than half the raiders are killed or @Condition[broken], their morale breaks completely and the remaining raiders attempt to flee. If cornered, they throw down their arms and surrender.

Gafto's Tactics

Gafto is a violent maniac with little regard for their own safety.

At the start of each of their turns they gain temporary hit points via their @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.6q9UnQosoKI555R8] feature and use their enhanced speed and @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.oeY6A4eCYcmWHUKZ] nature to rush directly into combat, swinging their weapons wildly with intent to maim and kill.

Their @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.a1Rcf4Nlo9lxgHcD] feature is used often, giving their attacks advantage, heedless of the danger that puts them in.

At the beginning of combat on their very first turn Gafto activates @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.berserker0000000] and relies almost exclusively on making aggressive use of @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.dualWield0000000] to pummel opponents with @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.VUz5g6rvisPp6EER] and @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.d7Yf0agimIVB7Kj9]. Their reckless approach to combat is made somewhat safer by their @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.thickskin0000000].

Gafto knows their reckless aggression puts their opponents on edge, and leverages that to shatter the morale of their opponents and back them down using @UUID[Actor.Q3oQouScXmmHlE2I.Item.emberZephLineage].

They have no sense of mercy, and kill anyone that puts up resistance or is too slow to escape their reach. Gafto will not retreat from combat, nor will they surrender.

Shimz's Tactics

Shimz is a spellcaster first and foremost, and leans on her spells to hinder movement, deal damage, and keep Gafto alive while they charge headlong into battle. However, if pressed in close-combat, or once out of spells, she is a perfectly capable ranged and melee fighter.

She has a greater sense of self-preservation that Gafto, and if the fight is beginning to go badly, she'll slip away as quickly as possible, using her spell to vanish, if possible.

Shimz is the calm counterbalance to Gafto's rage. A spellcaster first and foremost, Shimz leans on her magic to bolster her allies, especially Gafto, while hindering her opponents. Shimz makes steady use of @UUID[Actor.XuMfLf3hzG6IUUrC.Item.inspireheroism00] and @UUID[Actor.XuMfLf3hzG6IUUrC.Item.extolldeeds00000] to bolster the morale of the raiders and drive Gafto's frenzy, while using @UUID[Actor.XuMfLf3hzG6IUUrC.Item.bard000000000000] to mock and demoralize their opponents. As opportunities arise, she may use @Spell[illumination.arrow] to hurl radiant bolts at unsuspecting targets.

Shimz has a greater sense of self-preservation than Gafto. If the fight is beginning to go badly, she'll slip away as quickly as possible, casting @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.invisibility0000] at the first opportunity to aid her hasty retreat.

Svala's Tactics

Svala is a powerful, fearless warrior that is more than happy to carry her weight in the coming fight. She focuses on keeping the refugees safe when possible, and targets any raiders that look like they'll go after a refugee first.

In combat she uses her @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.HbLLAloQKHZk5ChR]{Focused Resilience} bonus action to give herself temporary hit points, and @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.ix6rLxambHqmp4Od]{Powerful} feature (when charged) to make her attacks pack extra punch.

She is strongest in melee combat, surrounded by enemies where she can use her extra reaction granted by @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.ykjjFnmX4jyhFK9Q]{Peerless Warrior} to make good use of her @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.P5Mn7sDI2hs6bwSH]{Counter Attack} and @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.jsHMkRxGqRe498dg]{Beard Guard} reactions.

Svala will not hesitate to insert herself between the refugees and the raiders, making use of @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.intercept0000000] to close ground and shield them.

In combat Svala relies on engaging with her Battleaxe and makes a dangerous foe due to @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.cadence000000000], following up on successful hits with a @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.shieldBash000000] to punish her opponents, and will make liberal use of @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.disarmingstrike0] to establish tactical superiority. Svala is nothing if not resilient, and will lean on @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.secondwind000000] and @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.steadfast0000000] as needed in order to counteract physical or morale damage as necessary.

If Svala is pressed heavily and finds her reserves of strength taxed, her @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.emberVrjnharLine] should keep her supplied with Action Points and let her stay in the fight. Svala is at her most dangerous when pressed in melee combat and surrounded by enemies, making use of the engagement bonus she receives from @UUID[Actor.BrJJDYKDkq4A7LUb.Item.holdfast00000000]

Refugee Reactions

The refugees are all @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians}, unarmed, and unwilling to fight.

At the end of a round (on Initiative Count 0) the Refugees act. They will always attempt to get as far away from the raiders as possible without completely leaving the scene, as they are unwilling to abandon their friends, family, and belongings.

If they can move safely, they use the &reference[Dash] action to augment their normal movement. Otherwise, if they are engaged, or would be attacked as part of their movement they use the &reference[Disengage] action first. If cornered or unable to get to safety any other way, they use the &reference[Dodge] action to avoid harm.

At the end of each round, all refugees not engaged in combat will do their best to flee, expending all their available action points on movement. If they are engaged or would be attacked as part of their movement or if they are cornered, they will make use of the Defend action in order to gain what meagre protection they can. Once they realise that Svala and the Party are trying to protect them, they will try to take paths that use their valiant protectors to give them safe passage away from the raiders.

In the aftermath of battle there is time for investigation.

Heart Attunement: Refugees Saved

If the party manages to successfully save all of the refugees, advance each character's [[/attunement emberHeart +1 cindaric1RefugeesSaved]] at the conclusion of the event.

Abyss Attunement: Refugees Slain

If the party allows the refugees to die at the hands of the raiders, advance each character's [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 cindaric1RefugeesSlain]] at the conclusion of the event.

Interrogating the Raiders

If any of the raiders were captured alive they can be interrogated.

Resentful Raiders

If the party manages to capture any raiders alive, they can be interrogated for information. They inherently don't want to die, and are willing to cooperate if there is a chance they will survive. A successful [[/skill intimidation 14]] or [[/skill persuasion 18]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 14]] or [[/skillCheck diplomacy 18]] check is sufficient to convince them to talk.

They can speak about their raiding and intentions:

Refugees have been coming through for a while, we jump them, rob them. If they put up a fight, well, we kill a couple until the fight leaves them. Easy pickings, hardly any danger to us until today.

If asked why they are raiding, the answer is simple:

Need money to survive, right? That simple. Besides, a revolution takes money. The Queen of Scales sets expectations, and the Captain gets irate if we fall short for too long. Gotta keep everyone happy so we don't lose our heads.

Following up on the Queen of Scales and Captain are, they are reticent to say much:

They are the heads of the fight against the Ordinate. You won't get anything else from me. I won't help the Ordinate or their dogs.

Asking what the "revolution" or fight against the Ordinate triggers a tirade:

The corrupt leadership of the Ordinate and their secret police ruin the lives of common folk, and we're exposing the truth that the people of the plateau aren't actually safe. The government doesn't care about them, and it can't stop us!

A successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14]]check determines they are absolutely earnest, and have a genuine contempt for the Ordinate.

[[/culture emberOrdani]] characters or those who have [[/knowledge trade]] or [[/knowledge politics]] understand that the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune} is a violent political movement full of radicals, who believe that the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate} and Trading Houses are utterly corrupt and need to be torn down. It's not precisely known who leads them, and their numbers have been growing over the last few months.

Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge trade]] know that these Otherhood Raiders have been growing bolder by the week, raiding travelers, trade caravans, even attacking settlements (like Helkas). They are always unpredictable in terms of methods and brutality, but they are becoming more and more widespread.

Under the Surface

Characters using @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.telecognition000] while questioning the raiders can glean additional insights from the minds of the raiders.

  • When the Queen of Scales is mentioned, you get a flash of a market, and an ominously tall drakon or ashka figure.

  • When the Captain is mentioned, you get a flash of a larger than life, heroic, humanoid sea captain with white hair.

  • When asked about their base of operations, you get images of a large city on the coast, and it's certainly not Ordain.

The Dead Tell No Tales

If the party didn't manage to capture any raiders, but wants to use @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.I2LUSF5ogc7Bj62e] some manner of [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeSoul00000000]] magic to question the corpses can learn the information above. Using this magic in front of Svala and the refugees unsettles them greatly as necromancy is broadly feared and reviled.

Talking with the Refugees

If any of the refugees survived, the party can talk with them.

Tending the Wounded

If the refugees survive the combat, they likely have wounded and ill, many already in a poor state before the attack. The party can treat them with a successful [[/skill medicine 13]] [[/skillCheck medicine 13]] check and some time. Magic that heals or removes disease works as well, and a few casts will handle most of the ill or injured.

The refugees have nothing to give in return but their gratitude.

Rescued Refugees

If the party speaks with any surviving Arcturian refugees, the characters can learn a few rumors about various dangers on the road that have mounted over the last few weeks:

  • These weren't the first bandits the small caravan has spotted on or off the road, but they managed to avoid detection before now.

  • Several villages and homesteads across the Plateau are dealing with their own calamities, whether manmade, natural, or worse.

The refugees' origins:

Several of us hail from Skybrush, in the Rustvar Valleys, and others joined along the way. A few homesteads and farms, where times were tougher than usual. We've been making our way east for days now, a bit aimlessly I have to admit.

A successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14 passive]] check against the refugees leads you to believe that they are earnest about their troubles.

The survivors aren't sure where to go, but they do have several options:

Well, Nain would be safest but the Corpin Sanctuary might be closer, but there's no promise of help there if the rumors are true. We could also head for the Oldcraft Lodge, but the roads aren't getting any safer and there's no guarantee we'd even get halfway there given how things have been going so far.

Hearing that, Sin is confused and incredulous, arguing with the refugees:

What? That's impossible, the Sages work to help the people of the plateau both physically and spiritually. Why would you not get help from them at their Sanctuary? You should absolutely make your way there, they'll help you!

The refugees respond:

Maybe they would, but we know what we've heard. They are apparently turning people away from the Sanctuary, and that doesn't surprise us much. Support from the Sages has been thin outside of Ordain lately. Seems like they've got their own problems and we're no longer worth they time. Maybe we ought to head for Nain…

Directing the Refugees

The party can make a [[/skill persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]]check to convince the refugees to go wherever you think they should go: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fBPE6UWg6EOO2WFH], @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh], or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.sdIjbPRNIsJ3ApcU].

Concluding the Event

Event Outcomes

If the refugees were killed, record the Refugees Slain outcome as having occurred. Otherwise, record the event outcome that most closely matches what the survivors plan to do next.

Next Steps

After rescuing the refugees, joining the raiders, or simply watching events unfold the party and Sin can continue on their journey towards Corpin Sanctuary and the [[/eventState cindaric1CorpinArrival]] event.
Ambushed Refugees.soverview: The party and Sin encounter a beleaguered caravan of refugees who are under attack by predatory raiders. The characters must leap into the fray with some measure of haste if these refugees are to be saved.
Ambushed Refugees.sexposition:
The faint shouting of voices and clashing of metal drifts above the Plateau's soft breeze somewhere up ahead. Approaching the direction of this clamor, you spy a small train of three wagons that appear to be under attack. Two separate groups are gathered about the central wagon: one appears to consist of panicked Arcturian commonfolk, while the other — their assailants — seems to be a loosely-organized group of bandits.

In a moment of desperation, a young Arcturian dashes away from the wagons in a desperate attempt to escape the highwaymen. A volley of arrows is quickly let loose by some of the raiders, and the moment is heavy with dire anticipation … Just then, a Vrjnhar warrior emerges from the crowd of arcturians, catching the arrows on her heavy wooden shield with gusto. She cries out to the others:

Don't talk, run, all of you! I'll hold these bastards off as long as I can!
Ambushed Refugees.ssummary: We came across a group of refugees who had been ambushed and were under attack by nefarious raiders. We had to quickly decide whether and how to intervene.

Corpin Investigation.name: Corpin Investigation
Corpin Investigation.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event challenges the party with an investigation at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh]{Corpin Sanctuary}, where they'll search for evidence regarding the accusations found in the mysterious note left for @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} the night before. In this event, the characters can:

  • Attempt to intuit who authored the @UUID[Item.sgtcxR29Zf7ukZyP]{Note to Sin}.

    • Search the sanctuary for evidence of suspicious activity or wrongdoing.

    • Find evidence that @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn} has been turning away refugees.

    • Find evidence that @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol} is not a simple visitor, but is actually a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinary}.

    • Find evidence that @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso} is involved in eldritch rituals utilizing forbidden arcana.

  • Witness the enclave's revelation that the central dais of the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.FvJRLzLclby5Uini]{Sanctorum} is, in fact, an ancient elevator that descends into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} below.

Area Walkthrough

This event takes place on the Corpin Sanctuary area map. Unlike the previous event, the characters now have the freedom to explore the area on their own. Consult the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS]{Corpin Sanctuary} area walkthrough for full details about the areas they can explore and the evidence they can find.

Planning an Approach

Before commencing the investigation, the party must confer with Sin and plan the next course of action. This could happen anywhere, but is most likely to occur in one of the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.g5ZhafC273TnlsRm]{Empty Dormitories}.

Sin's Suspicions

Sin will admit to a lack of experience in clandestine investigations such as this, and volunteers to follow the party's lead. However, Sin is rather concerned that this investigation could damage their prospects with the Cindaric Sages — a group Sin is still very intent on joining.

The characters must align with Sin on a plan. To do so, they must succeed on one of the following skill checks to assuage Sin's trepidations and concerns for the Cindaric order:

[[/skill arcana 12]] [[/skillCheck arcana 12]] Sin's emergent understanding of necromancy is guided by the character's own acumen regarding the magical arts. Characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] have advantage on this check.

[[/skill deception 12]] [[/skillCheck deception 12]] The character uses a "little white lie" or some other method to trick Sin into believing that the necromancer poses no threat.

[[/skill insight 12]] or [[/skill persuasion 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] The character senses the earnestness of Sin's concern, and is able to offer the proper words of encouragement. Sin's resolve is bolstered by the character's persuasive call-to-action.

[[/skill religion 12]] [[/skillCheck society 12]]Sin is adequately convinced of her personal duty to take up the task, lest the Cindarics fall into ruin. Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] have advantage on this check.

Once Sin has been duly motivated, the party members can start their investigations in earnest (in any order they please). Sin will accompany the first character to succeed on their skill check unless otherwise instructed or compelled.

Investigating Mira

If the party has any suspicions about @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}, they may investigate her activities. The crucial clues for this investigation are found in @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.OnKJslXqG9NYJCI6] and @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.bS6ktM9Gelrxpi6T].

Mira's Mandate

Once they identify the location of Mira's office and private quarters, they can search each location for clues about the Cindaric leader's current activities.

@UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.OnKJslXqG9NYJCI6]{Mira's Office} contains a @UUID[Item.MB5aIlZdYZgJdZwM]{Letter from Sigil}, which makes it look as if Mira is independently turning away refugee aid.

@UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.bS6ktM9Gelrxpi6T]{Mira's Chamber} contains a @UUID[Item.NOQ9M9ktPU35XtHU]{Letter from Lilla Arien}, which clarifies that Mira is reluctantly following instruction provided to her by a superior in Ordain.

Interrogating Mira

If the characters wish to question Mira more directly, they can find her in the Refectory during the morning, in the Sanctorum during midday, in her Office during the afternoon, in the Entry Courtyard during the early evening, and in her Chamber during the late evening.

As the designated leader of Corpin Sanctuary, Mira will only entertain polite questioning that probes into Cindaric matters up to a certain point. She remains protective of the Sanctuary and its residents, as well as the Cindaric order itself. Mira can, however, elucidate the following:

  • Her history as the leader of Corpin Sanctuary for the past decade, and a scant few details about her personal life.

  • How Corpin Sanctuary's mission to harbor refugees of the Arctus Plateau has been compromised by unstable politics and edicts from Ordain.

  • The basic details Avwynn's visitation to the Sanctuary as a scholar of note.

  • Evesso's appointment to the Sanctuary nearly six months ago by the Holy Speaker himself.

Additionally, any character that casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} spell @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.telecognition000] is able to read Mira's thoughts.

  • Mira's surface thoughts include her duties for the day, which include sending a letter to the Holy Speaker.

  • Mira's emotional state is tinged with well-measured anxiety, and the plight of Arcturian refugees looms large in her mind.

Event Outcomes

If the party discovers that Mira has been following instruction to deter refugees from remaining at Corpin Sanctuary, mark the Evidence on Mira outcome as completed.

[[/outcome evidenceMira]]

Investigating Avwynn

If the party has any suspicions about @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}, they may investigate her activities. Investigating Avwynn requires the party to shadow her movements from an unobserved position, taking note of what she does during the day.

Shadowing Avwynn

After early breakfast in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.R5WXCmGHIT6K7Z7e]{Refectory} and morning tea in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.WHdKr6CkT5xF7lqr]{Entry Courtyard}, Avwynn will return to @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.wKUy9cRpOOKniHe5]{her chamber} to retrieve a satchel full of writing supplies and @UUID[Item.Y3Z5Xq6TtwPVE8IP]{her journal}.

Avwynn subsequently carries her journal to the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.7GOn0qf5bnkNFOJK]{Meditation Pavillion}, where she spends time discretely transcribing her thoughts. After an hour, she hides the journal in her room before joining other sages in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.FvJRLzLclby5Uini]{Sanctorum} for a sacred reading.

Reading Avwynn's Journal

Once they know what to look for, the party can break into @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.wKUy9cRpOOKniHe5]{Avwynn's Chamber} and read the contents of @UUID[Item.Y3Z5Xq6TtwPVE8IP]{Avwynn's Journal}. Any character who spends at least 5 minutes studying this journal is able to learn about its contents — which reveal Avwynn's identity as a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.8QFohLx6nyCxr82B]{Sanguinary}, posing as a scholar of renown to investigate the Sanctuary's practices firsthand.

Avwynn's Chamber also contains a @UUID[Item.AgmNUa9um9RGlEoP]{Black Aspen Wand}, which savvy characters may recognize as an arcane focus often used by Sanguinaries.

Interrogating Avwynn

If the characters wish to question Avwynn more directly, they can find her in the Refectory during the morning, in the Entry Courtyard during midday, in the Meditation Pavilion during the afternoon, in the Refectory during the early evening, and in her Chamber during the late evening.

As an outsider with suspicions of her own, Avwynn is fairly nonplussed by the party's investigation as long as they remain cordial and/or complimentary to her ego and her cause. She does, however, keep her identity as the leader of the Sanguinaries a close-guarded secret. Avwynn can elucidate the following:

  • The basic details of her visitation to the Sanctuary as a scholar of note.

  • Her history as an affluent Maziran scholar and her extensive travels throughout the continent of Aterica.

  • A casual mistrust of the pomp and circumstance affecting the Cindaric Temple in Ordain and a condemnation of the bureaucracy that restricts them.

Additionally, any character that casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} spell is able to read Avwynn's thoughts. characters that use @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.telecognition000] to penetrate Avwynn's mind may learn the following:

  • Avwynn's surface thoughts include apprehension about Evesso's pyrefly ritual, which she was able to observe from a clandestine spot near the Sanctorum Entrance.

  • Avwynn's emotional state is a mix of curiosity and contempt, and the questionable agenda of the Cindaric order (as a whole) looms large in her mind.

Event Outcomes

If the party discovers that Avwynn is a Sanguinary, rather than the traveling scholar that she claims to be, mark the Evidence on Avwynn outcome as completed.

[[/outcome evidenceAvwynn]]

Investigating Evesso

If the party has suspicions about @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso}, they can investigate the sage's activities. The crucial clues to Evesso's true malignant nature are found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.eDlvJHr6FhKhY8ji]{Library}, in @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.F5mVhRRToX0Z8QMz]{Evesso's Chambers}, and in the hidden @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.jPYv3Z4n7vOswB7z]{Profane Altar}.

Evesso's Darkness

To fuel their speculation regarding Evesso's dark nature, the party can first discover the @UUID[Item.kc2AKDWVnHLTY3Z8]{Letter of Introduction}: a poignant document in @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.OnKJslXqG9NYJCI6]{Mira's Office} that describes how Evesso came to join the ranks of the Corpin Sanctuary sages under unusual circumstances.

If the characters don't come to the notion on their own, Sin suggests they search Evesso's Chamber for evidence that points towards necromantic activity (or other suspicious behavior).

Signs of Necromancy

Evesso's Chamber seems extremely normal at first glance. However, it contains two important clues that point towards Evesso's true intentions:

  • @UUID[Item.5sDslKMjZXB18yNm]{Evesso's Note}, scrawled with an arcane sigil and a mysterious sequence of numbers.

  • A secret door to the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.jPYv3Z4n7vOswB7z]{Profane Altar}, which can only be opened if the characters unravel the mystery of Evesso's Note.

To unravel the mystery of Evesso's Note, the characters can do the following:

  1. Confirm the arcane sigil on the note is the same as the arcane sigil on the secret door.

  2. Investigate the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.eDlvJHr6FhKhY8ji]{Library} for @UUID[Item.wlTZjyyW8K69yf56]{Nineteen Nights in Haxim}, a book alluded to via the first number written in Evesso's Note.

  3. After finding the book, consult the page, line, and word that respectively correspond to the next three numbers mentioned in Evesso's Note. The 5th word on the 16th line of the 53rd page — "malediction" — is the password to the secret door in Evesso's Chamber.

  4. Speak the password at the secret door in Evesso's Chamber to open it and reveal the Profane Altar.

The Profane Altar unambiguously identifies Evesso as the Necromancer, as a thorough examination will confirm. And the presence of other suspicious accoutrements (including the secret door) only further supports whatever argument the party is prepared to make.

Destroying the Profane Altar

The @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.jPYv3Z4n7vOswB7z]{Profane Altar} can be destroyed or consecrated via one of the methods indicated in the area walkthrough.

If the characters manage to destroy the Profane Altar before their conflict with Evesso in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.JN1mTKPlSA0WKizP]{Sanctuary of Death} event, the necromancer loses his @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx.Item.kuKhl8K4JSGWsJAi]{Profane Blessing} feature.

Interrogating Evesso

If the characters wish to question Evesso more directly, they can find him in the Refectory during the morning, in the Library during midday, in the Entry Courtyard during the afternoon, in the Sanctorum during the early evening, and in his Chamber during the late evening.

Evesso is, in fact, the villain the characters seek, and will attempt to maintain his deception at all costs. The information he offers is elaborate, truthful, and full of misdirection. Evesso will elucidate the following:

  • His history as an esteemed ritualist and a student of arcana, which has been a great boon to the Cindarics since his induction many years ago.

  • How Corpin Sanctuary's mission to harbor refugees of the Arctus Plateau has been compromised by unstable politics and edicts from Ordain.

  • His appointment to the remote Sanctuary nearly six months ago by the Holy Speaker himself.

Additionally, any character that casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} spell is able to read Evesso's thoughts. characters that use magic to penetrate Avwynn's mind may learn the following:

  • Evesso's surface thoughts include the Sanctorum, and the architecture of Corpin Sanctuary.

  • Evesso's emotional state is calmness colored with apprehension, and a heightened suspicion about the party's motives looms large in his mind.

Event Outcomes

If the party discovers that Evesso has been practicing forbidden necromantic rites using the Profane Altar, mark the Evidence on Evesso outcome as completed.

Additionally, if the party chooses to destroy the Profane Altar, mark the Profane Altar Destroyed outcome as completed.

[[/outcome effigyDestroyed]]

[[/outcome evidenceEvesso]]

Heart Attunement: Profane Altar Destroyed

Any character who participates in the destruction or consecration of the Profane Altar advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +2 cindaric1InvestigationAltarDestroyed]] at the conclusion of the event.

Abyss Attunement: Attuned to the Altar

Any character who attunes to and uses the Profane Altar advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 cindaric1InvestigationAltarUsed]] at the conclusion of the event. This advancement only occurs once.

Signara Attunement: Evesso's Truth

If the party manages to discover the truth of Evesso's identity as a necromancer, advance each character's [[/attunement emberSignara +1 cindaric1InvestigationEvesso]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Sanctuary Elevator

Once the party has had ample time to pursue the leads they deem worthy for investigation, the narrative is driven forward by Evesso himself — who opens an ancient elevator to the Pathways beneath the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.FvJRLzLclby5Uini]{Sanctorum} floor. Created millennia ago during the foundation of Corpin Sanctuary, this clandestine elevator opens offscreen during a dramatic moment of deus ex machina guided by you, the Gamemaster.

When the time is right, read the following aloud:

Just then, the entire Sanctuary begins to shudder as a low, stony rumble reverberates throughout each chamber and shakes the very mountainside. Dust and grit falls from the ceiling as this calamity persists for about ten seconds, after which time the whole place grows remarkably silent and still. Moments later, the panicked voices of Cindaric sages rise to greet the uncomfortable calm.

At Sin's insistence, the party rushes to the Sanctorum to investigate what happened. Here, they discover the gaping aperture of the elevator standing open wide as the platform descends to fathomless depths. @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira} is also here, attempting to maintain order among the chaos. However, there is currently no sign of either @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso} or @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn} — who both seem to have disappeared.

Mira's Confession

Mira confesses that she knew of this elevator, but that it was a closely held secret for Cindaric leadership and that she thought no other sage at Corpin Sanctuary knew of its existence.

  • When pressed for more information, Mira engages a hidden control gem and causes the elevator to rise back to the surface, its platform empty.

  • Mira and Sin both agree that there is only one course of action: the party must descend the elevator to ascertain what exactly is below and what has happened.

Concluding the Event

When the party is ready, the elevator to the Pathways — and a further investigation into Evesso's machinations — awaits.

Event Outcomes

Once the Sanctuary Elevator has been opened and returned to the surface using Mira's control gem, mark the Pathways Opened outcome as complete, which will allow the next events in the quest to proceed.

Next Steps

After the Sanctuary Elevator is unlocked, this event can be marked as completed and the party can use the elevator to descend into the Pathways. Upon arriving in the Pathways, the subsequent event [[/eventState cindaric1Pathways]] will begin.

Alternately, if the party finds some other route down into the Pathways, they may advance indirectly to the [[/eventState cindaric1Temple]] event.
Corpin Investigation.soverview: The party mounts an investigation at Corpin Sanctuary in search of truths behind a startling accusation — that a wily necromancer maintains covert operations here, hidden somewhere among the ranks of the Cindaric Sages.
Corpin Investigation.sexposition: The morning sun rises over the Golden Flats from the east, cascading upon the slopes of Mial Mountain as it washes the walls and balconies of Corpin Sanctuary in amber light. You awaken refreshed, perhaps grateful for the opportunity to rest in relative comfort after several days of difficult travel. Your mind quickly recalls the mysterious note addressed to Sin, and its ominous allegations that necromancy lurks somewhere beneath the sanctuary's tranquil surface.
Corpin Investigation.ssummary: We examined the disturbing possibility of necromancy being practiced within the tranquil halls of Corpin Sanctuary. Our investigation yielded several important clues — but was cut short when someone activated an ancient elevator built into the very foundation of Corpin Sanctuary itself, unearthing a lost entrance to forgotten depths below.

Pillaged Farmstead.name: Pillaged Farmstead
Pillaged Farmstead.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event challenges the party to collaborate with @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} when they encounter a burned and ransacked farmstead at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.GgMWDvWX0zKrnEOs]{Dradley Grange}. Once the fires are quelled, a brief investigation follows — for clues regarding the arsonist's identity and what precisely became of the farmers who lived here. In this event, the party can:

  • Help Sin extinguish the raging fire.

  • Investigate the incinerated scene for clues.

  • Befriend a juvenile Rask which managed to escape the conflagration.

The Grange Ablaze

You follow Sin towards the main farmhouse, which is nearly subsumed by the roiling blaze. Despite the intimidating heat, Sin strides forward with a look of determination behind her mask, which she raises in protection against the surging smoke and ash. A glimmer of magic appears in the druid's open palm as she begins shaping the flames and redirecting the conflagration; but given the size of the fire, it's readily clear she'll need some help.

Fighting the Fire

Each party member must assist Sin in combating the fire if the blaze is to be stopped.

  • Cantrips like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.udsLtG0BugXHR2JQ]{Prestidigitation} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.SbSvZKkJASyk8jKo]{Druidcraft} (which Sin casts in this moment) Usage of [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeFrost0000000]] (like @Spell[frost.ray] which Sin casts in this moment) can be used to slowly curtail the blaze if used repeatedly for 10 minutes.

  • Water can be rapidly hauled from the farm's well or dirt can be thrown to choke the fire with a successful [[/check athletics 15]] [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] check. Success on this check has comparable effectiveness to the use of a cantrip.

  • Leveled spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.a3XtAO5n2GrqiAh5]{Create or Destroy Water} can control the fire more quickly, but not rapidly extinguish it. Use of a leveled spell lessens the time required to curtail the blaze by 5 minutes per spell level consumed. Higher-level spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.7fFHlBk3UNX8gPKL]{Control Water} can instantaneously extinguish the fire.Usage of the Frost rune by a spellcaster with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.FrostProficiency]] can instantaneously extinguish the blaze.

Checking for Survivors

A character might choose to rush into the burning buildings in search of survivors who can be saved. Any character that enters the farmhouse or guest house while the fire still rages must withstand the following hazards resulting from the blaze:

  • [[/save constitution 15]] to withstand the smoke and heat. On a failure, the character suffers [[/damage 3d6 fire]] damage (or half-damage on a success).

  • [[/save dexterity 15]] to avoid a falling support beam that threatens to crush anyone beneath. On a failure, the character suffers [[/damage 1d8 bludgeoning]] damage and is &Reference[restrained], requiring a [[/save dexterity 13]] escape check. This escape check may be repeated, and the character suffers an additional damage for each turn they are restrained in this way (see "No Time to Waste" below).

  • A successful [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] or [[/skillCheck science 15]] will allow the character to use some ingenuity to cover themselves or their face with a wetted blanket or cloth before charging in, to better withstand the smoke and heat. On a failure, the character instead suffers [[/hazard 10 fortitude health fire]]{The Burning Flames}.

  • [[/skillCheck athletics 15]] to avoid a falling support beam that threatens to crush anyone beneath. On a failure, the character is struck by [[/hazard 5 physical health bludgeoning]]{The Falling Beam} and is @Condition[restrained]. Escaping the fallen beam requires a successful [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check. This escape check may be repeated if they fail, but the character suffers additional damage for each turn they are restrained in this way (see "No Time to Waste" below).

Characters who enter the building must succeed on a [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] check to verify that there are no people within (living or dead). On a success, they also notice a @UUID[Actor.D0Ws1Flk2fF48bBf]{Rask Juvenile} trapped within the wreckage, pinned down by collapsed furniture and cowering from the blaze (see "The Frightened Rask" below).

@Embed[Actor.D0Ws1Flk2fF48bBf]

The Frightened Rask

The Rask Juvenile can be rescued using one of the following methods:

  • A successful[[/check animalHandling 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check allows a character to entice the Rask Juvenile to leap over or through the burning flames.

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.hDOENzjuj5WpLq7B]{Animal Friendship} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.aL1F8fvYLtNzUbKu]{Speak with Animals} spells [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] can be used to reassure the Rask Juvenile and convince it to leap to safety without the need for a skill check.

  • A successful [[/skill athletics 18]] [[/skillCheck athletics 18]] check allows a character to grapple the Rask Juvenile and haul it away to safety. Failure results in the frightened creature's escape and continued peril.

No Time to Waste

If a character lingers inside the house by becoming restrained or by tarrying unnecessarily (defined by GM discretion), they suffer[[/damage 1d4 fire]] damage [[/hazard 2 fortitude health fire]]{The Relentless Flames} every 6 seconds until they perish or exit the building.

Through the party's efforts, the flames that once engulfed the farm are eventually quelled, and only smoldering ashes and singed beams of timber remain. There is no immediate danger of the fire spreading any further; but despite the group's heroic efforts, the main farmhouse has been lost to the blaze.

Primordis Attunement: Magical Assistance

Any character who used magic to reduce or extinguish the flames advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 cindaric1PillagedMagic]] at the conclusion of the event.

Ragen Attunement: Check for Survivors

Any character who did not hesitate to rush into the fire to check for survivors advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 cindaric1PillagedSurvivors]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Rescued Rask

If the Rask Juvenile was rescued from the flames, the party can attempt to communicate with it.

Calming the Rask

Any character who succeeds on a a [[/skill animalHandling 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] check is able to calm the Rask Juvenile. Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The Rask Juvenile will befriend the character as an animal companion and join the party as a non-combatant ally.

  • Use of cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.hDOENzjuj5WpLq7B]{Animal Friendship} spell use the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] talent Sin or another character can successfully befriend the Rask Juvenile, achieving the same result as above.

What the Rask Knows

Once the Rask Juvenile has been calmed, Sin or one of the characters can cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithA]{Speak with Animals} spell use the [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] talent to learn precisely what happened:

  • The smell of fire and the sound of stampeding cattle were the first signs that something was wrong. The bashful Rask — ironically named Springer by Egon Dradley's nephew Cade — was caught behind a fallen timber and left behind.

  • Strange humanoids brought the fire with them. Carrying torches and barrels of oil, these strangers were clad in golden cloaks and armed to the teeth.

  • As the fire rapidly spread, the strangers took advantage of the ensuing chaos to ensnare the people who lived (and visited) here. The people of Dradley Grange were bound and gagged, hauled away to places unknown.

If Springer was befriended, mark the following outcome as completed:

[[/outcome companion]]

Heart Attunement: Rask Befriended

Whichever character manages to calm and befriend Springer the Rask advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 cindaric1PillagedRask]] upon the conclusion of this event.

Searching the Rubble

Once the fires have been dealt with, the party can also search the farmstead for items or information of interest.

Exploring the Farmstead

A general search of the farmstead grounds reveals scant items of interest, including @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.Y9S75go1hLMXUD48]{Brewer's Supplies}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.ap9prThUB2y9lDyj]{Weaver's Tools}, and [[/roll 1d3+1]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.f4w4GxBi0nYXmhX4]{Rations} Brewer's Supplies, Tailor's Tools, and [[/roll 1d3+1]] Rations per character in undamaged produce.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] is familiar with the general details and history of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.GgMWDvWX0zKrnEOs]{Dradley Grange}, and can confirm the suspicious nature of the fire and the curious lack of local residents when the party arrived.

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check reveals some specifics about the scene: it's clear that the farm has been ransacked and looted as well as burned, the fire has spread farther than it seems like it should on its own, and nearly a dozen booted footprints can be spotted around the farmstead grounds.

A successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] or [[/skillCheck science 14]]check suggests that the fires were manmade, and that the accident here is the direct result of arson. Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Concluding the Event

After helping Sin with the fire, the party can continue on their journey towards Corpin Sanctuary.

Next Steps

If they have not already encountered them, the party may yet cross paths with the brigands responsible for this fire in [[/eventState cindaric1Refugees]].

Further along the road towards Mial Mountain, the party must attempt to cross the river at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.YR30CBfcusmmL38D] where they will experience the perils of [[/eventState cindaric1Crossing]].

Upon arriving at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh]{Corpin Sanctuary} the party will next encounter the [[/eventState cindaric1CorpinArrival]] event.
Pillaged Farmstead.soverview: The party journeys to the Dradley Grange farmstead while traveling with Sin Marmot on her quest. When they arrive, the farmhouses and adjoining fields have been set ablaze by marauders, and the characters must unravel what little clues remain at the scene of the crime if they wish to determine who's responsible.
Pillaged Farmstead.sexposition:
A plume of dark smoke coils against the horizon and the acrid smell of smoke fills your nostrils as you approach the farmstead, which appears to have been engulfed in a conflagration of flames and destruction. The main farmhouse burns with ferocity, its thatched roof fully enveloped by the blaze, and the smaller buildings struggle to stand resolute against the advancing inferno. You quickly notice an assortment of smaller fires in nearby fields, where bales of hay and dry crops have also been kindled.

As the alarm in her eyes gives way to purpose, Sin Marmot wastes no time before rushing in towards the scene.
Pillaged Farmstead.ssummary: We ventured to the Dradley Grange farmstead, which was set ablaze in a clear act of arson. The farmhouse and guest house were too far gone to be saved, and we couldn't locate any sign of the people who lived there.
