If nothing else, this encounter was a troubling indication of burgeoning lawlessness within the Arctus Plateau.

Sanctuary of Death.name: Sanctuary of Death
Sanctuary of Death.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event finds the party returning to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh]{Corpin Sanctuary} on the trail of the necromancer @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso}, who leads a skeletal horde of undead minions on a rampage of death and destruction against the Cindarics. In this event, the party can:

  • Return to Corpin Sanctuary via the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.FvJRLzLclby5Uini]{Sanctorum's} secret elevator.

  • Join in combat against Evesso's undead minions - including @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith}, @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]{Crumbling Skallith}, and @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy]{Skallith Warriors} — while protecting the Cindaric Sages here from mortal peril.

  • Fight their way through a horde of skeletal undead to reach Evesso in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.WHdKr6CkT5xF7lqr]{Entry Courtyard} for a climactic showdown, which culminates in a wizardly stand-off at the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.7GOn0qf5bnkNFOJK]{Meditation Pavilion}.

  • Learn from @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn} and the other sages about what transpired here in the party's absence.

Orchestrating Combat

This event returns the characters to the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS]{Corpin Sanctuary} area walkthrough, and requires the party to move procedurally throughout the sanctuary, purifying it of undead and saving Cindaric Sages along the way.

Although the entirety of Corpin Sanctuary is connected and relatively small, this event requires you to help set and maintain the pace of action as the characters make their way from the Sanctorum to the Entry Courtyard, and potentially further. The various "scenes" of this action sequence are presented below according to their location. When the party has finished one scene, a prompt will help you move them along to the next.

The characters begin in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.FvJRLzLclby5Uini]{Sanctorum} after riding the elevator back to the sanctuary, followed by a conflict in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.XNmFfrViLKfVJiM8]{Dormitories}, then onto the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.R5WXCmGHIT6K7Z7e]{Refectory} via the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.GakdE5GfBYX8o7IM]{Winding Stairs}, before the first stage of their head-to-head combat with Evesso in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.WHdKr6CkT5xF7lqr]{Entry Courtyard}. This first stage of the encounter with Evesso will potentially lead them to a second that culminates at the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.7GOn0qf5bnkNFOJK]{Meditation Pavilion}, thanks to a handy Dimension Door spell from the necromancer's grimoire.

Regarding Initiative

Once initiative has been rolled, the characters will stay in initiative order throughout the entire event, until they have defeated or routed Evesso in combat. Enemies throughout the Sanctuary roll for initiative as soon as they're encountered in combat.

The Cindaric Adherents and various forms of Skallith (Crumbling Skallith, standard Skallith, and Skallith Warriors) have been grouped together according to their respective types, and will act on the same initiative order as any creature that shares the same name. Three "dummy" tokens have been placed invisibly upon the area map to account for this feature.

Sanctum Onslaught

Initiative is rolled immediately at the start of this combat event, after "Setting the Scene" has been read aloud. The characters begin combat from their places on the elevator at the center of the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.FvJRLzLclby5Uini]{Sanctorum}. Two types of undead creatures are currently present in this conflict, Skallith and their decrepit counterparts known as Crumbling Skallith.

@Embed[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]

@Embed[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY count=17]

Undead Tactics

Seventeen @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]{Crumbling Skallith} and one @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} await the characters here in the Sanctorum. When the fight begins, these skeletal undead will rush the characters as soon as possible to meet them in melee combat.

Crumbling Skallith who are close enough for melee attack will assault party members with their @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.HlBtohCA4riOhLP8]{Shortsword} attack. Meanwhile, Crumbling Skallith who are too far away for melee will attack ranged enemies and enemy spellcasters with their @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.NcZO9zhRtSwciqVn]{Shortbow} attack.

The lone Skallith will face off with the party member with the largest amount of hit points, using its @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV.Item.kyVnnafBYvgq61vA]{Shortsword}.

Seventeen @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]{Crumbling Skallith} and one @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} await the characters here in the Sanctorum. When the fight begins, these skeletal undead will rush the characters as soon as possible to meet them in melee combat.

Crumbling Skallith who are close enough for melee attack will assault party members with their @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.GTdwaJh0HBtSjJsq]{Shortsword} attack. Meanwhile, Crumbling Skallith who are too far away for melee will attack ranged enemies and enemy spellcasters with their @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.cMtoQfBsquZLuRCJ]{Shortbow} attack.

The lone Skallith will face off with the party member with the largest amount of hit points, using its @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV.Item.5kUOFYEzyBSJTf3O]{Shortsword}.

Dramatic Moments

At the beginning of each combat round here in the Sanctorum, excluding the first, one of several Dramatic Moments occurs. Each moment can only happen once. At the beginning of each round, roll on the Sanctuary of Death Moments table and narrate the result.

@Embed[RollTable.4qgFacrDbWU2hYEv inline rollable=true]

Once this group of Skallith and Crumbling Skallith in the Sanctorum has been defeated in combat, read the following aloud:

Just then, a voice calls out from the Dormitories to the north, where the sound of combat rings through the halls. It's the familiar voice of Mira Wavehorn, wrought with fury and distress.

Back! Back to the shadows, you loathsome creatures! You have no purchase here!

Dormitory Danger

Spurred on by @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}'s outcry, the party must now head north to the Dormitories, where they'll encounter the sage herself and another wave of Skallith and Crumbling Skallith. When the characters arrive, Mira is fending off a siege of skeletal undead from the doorway to @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.bS6ktM9Gelrxpi6T]{Mira's Chamber}.

You arrive to see a corridor full of skeletal undead, who clatter over each other as they claw their way towards Mira Wavehorn's chamber. Near the end of the hall, the sage stands defiant in the threshold, fending off the attack with a measure of desperation. A light returns to her eyes when she sees you've joined the fray.

Help! We have wounded here! I can't hold them off forever!

Mira looks over her shoulder into the chamber, surveying something — or someone — she's desperate to protect.

Undead Tactics

4 @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} and 8 @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]{Crumbling Skallith} line the hallway here on both sides, with 3 of the Skallith leading the charge into Mira's Chambers. When the party arrives, many Skallith and Crumbling Skallith will turn to face the characters in melee combat, while the Skallith closest to Mira will continue to attack her in the doorway.

Most of the Skallith and Crumbling Skallith here will opt to use their @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.HlBtohCA4riOhLP8]{Shortsword} @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.GTdwaJh0HBtSjJsq]{Shortsword} attacks in melee combat, resorting to @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.NcZO9zhRtSwciqVn]{Shortbow} @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.cMtoQfBsquZLuRCJ]{Shortbow} attacks if separated from enemies for a protracted amount of time.

Mira's Tactics

Mira uses the &Reference[Dodge] action during combat while maintaining her position in the doorway to keep the enemy from advancing.

Mira spends her time blocking the doorway and making use of the Defend action, occasionally activating a @Spell[life.aura] to make it unpleasant for the Skallith to consider approaching her.

If the characters attempt to talk to Mira during combat, she let's them know the following:

  • A wounded @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherent} is hanging on for dear life inside Mira's Chamber.

  • Evesso was seen retreating towards the Refectory with a mob of undead minions in tow.

Dramatic Moments

At the beginning of each combat round here in the Dormitories, excluding the first, one of several Dramatic Moments occurs. Each moment can only happen once. At the beginning of each round, roll on the @UUID[RollTable.4qgFacrDbWU2hYEv]{Sanctuary of Death Moments} table and narrate the result.

Once the group of Skallith and Crumbling Skallith here in the Dormitories has been defeated in combat, read the following aloud:

Mira shouts out to you as anther set of bones clatters morbidly to the floor.

Evesso … Evesso has brought this upon us! We must stop him! Make haste to the Refectory. I have some dire healing to do, but I'm right behind you.

You take note of another sage in Mira's chamber, their garments marked with a dark crimson stain from a rusty stab. As the life retreats from the sage's eyes, Mira rushes to heal them. She places her hands upon the wound as they begin to glow with holy light before regarding you once more.

Make haste! The fate of the Sanctuary hangs in the balance …

Rumble in the Refectory

After the encounter with Mira in the Dormitories, the characters must make their way to the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.R5WXCmGHIT6K7Z7e]{Refectory} by way of the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.GakdE5GfBYX8o7IM]{Winding Stairs}.

Stairway Combat

4 @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]{Crumbling Skallith} can be found traversing the Winding Stairs on their way to the Refectory. When the characters appear, these Crumbling Skallith immediately turn to face them in combat.

The two Crumbling Skallith furthest to the south with start with ranged @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.NcZO9zhRtSwciqVn]{Shortbow} attacks, while the two Crumbling Skallith to the @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.HlBtohCA4riOhLP8]{Shortswords}.

The two Crumbling Skallith furthest to the south with start with ranged @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.cMtoQfBsquZLuRCJ]{Shortbow} attacks, while the two Crumbling Skallith to the north will rush forward with their @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY.Item.GTdwaJh0HBtSjJsq]{Shortswords}.

After the brief encounter on the Winding Stairs, the characters can proceed to the Refectory, where a larger host of undead enemies wreak havoc — including a Skallith Warrior.

The once-inviting scents of the refectory have been replaced with a scene of carnage and the smell of death. Several skeletons ransack and pillage the refectory, upending furniture and hacking plates of meat with rusty swords. It seems you've become the target of this mindless havoc, as the malevolent creatures turn to face you. One of them appears quite threatening, adorned in corroded armor and armed with an ancient blade.

@Embed[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy]

Refectory Combat

1 @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy]{Skallith Warrior} is flanked by 1 @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} and 3 @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]{Crumbling Skallith} here in the Refectory. When the party arrives, they immediately turn to face the characters in combat.

Once this sequence of combat begins, the Skallith Warrior will target the character with the largest number of hit points or a spellcaster with its @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy.Item.jVTG4lWAPQLUUw8r]{Frightful Glare}, whichever poses the greatest immediate threat. A ranged @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy.Item.tNvNUSlYUNrgXaum]{Handaxe} attack is at the ready for any spellcasters who maintain concentration throughout the battle, but the Warrior will quickly engage the party member that poses the greatest threat in melee combat, using @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy.Item.hv2VKXXqOgxZ4Gl4]{Multiattack} each round with its @UUID[Actor.nOQXMU5Yd25LJgIy.Item.HMgoB5RKn1VGkuz2]{Longsword}.

Dramatic Moments

At the beginning of each combat round here in the Refectory, excluding the first, one of several Dramatic Moments occurs. Each moment can only happen once. At the beginning of each round, roll on the @UUID[RollTable.4qgFacrDbWU2hYEv]{Sanctuary of Death Moments} table and narrate the result.

Once the group of skeletal undead here in the Refectory has been defeated in combat, read the following aloud:

With a sudden gust of wind full of pink leaves and ill portent, the doors to the entry courtyard blow wide open. You quickly become aware of another presence to the south, heralded by the swell of arcane light and the sound of esoteric chants.

Evesso, the necromancer, awaits you in the courtyard, flanked by skeletal minions. He moves his arms in arcane gesticulation as a nimbus of purple vapor flows into his hands, bolstering the evil wizard with a necromantic facsimile of life.

Confronting the Necromancer

@Embed[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]

Evesso's Tactics

Evesso is accompanied here in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.WHdKr6CkT5xF7lqr]{Entry Courtyard} by a @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} and two @UUID[Actor.uDSTYr44WgaeBCFY]{Crumbling Skallith}.

Evesso has cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.7e3QXF10hLNDEdr6]{False Life}False Life spell upon himself just as the party becomes aware of his presence in the entry courtyard, gaining a total of 8 temporary hit points.

After 2 rounds of combat, Evesso casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.A4RsPuSvB9wFtz1j]{Dimension Door} spell to relocate himself onto the roof of the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.7GOn0qf5bnkNFOJK]{Meditation Pavilion}. The characters must wage ranged combat against the necromancer, or close the distance and meet him in a final confrontation atop the Pavilion.

Evesso has prepared for the eventuality that he may need to defend himself. His approach to combat at this stage involves doing everything in his power to delay or distract the party long enough to reposition himself. Ordering the Skallith to attack and engage the party to delay them. He has also prepared a magical ritual at this location to teleport himself to the top of the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.7GOn0qf5bnkNFOJK]{Meditation Pavilion}, and will take the special action in the first round to do so.

Once atop the Pavillion, Evesso makes steady use of @Spell[death.ray] and @spell[soul.arrow] to harry the party. If the Skallith are defeated and Evesso has not been directly engaged in combat atop the pavillion, he will attempt to use @Spell[death.conjure] to raise two new Skallith to protect him and keep the party at bay.

Dramatic Moments

At the beginning of each combat round here in the Entry Courtyard, excluding the first, one of several Dramatic Moments occurs. Each moment can only happen once. At the beginning of each round, roll on the @UUID[RollTable.4qgFacrDbWU2hYEv]{Sanctuary of Death Moments} table and narrate the result.

The Necromancer's Retreat

Once Evesso's hit points drop below 20 hp, he will attempt to escape combat by leaping dramatically from the roof of the Meditation Pavilion, intent on casting the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.pub0OWVEB71XQx1n]{Feather Fall} spell on himself as he plummets safely to the valley below.

If it looks as though Evesso may be killed or he is @Condition[broken] he will attempt to flee by dramatically hurling himself from the roof of the Pavillion toward the valley below, using his @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx.Item.XVukwAxLNHAUEz2q] to safely descend.

Event Outcome

Following the encounter with Evesso, record the appropriate outcome noting whether the necromancer was killed or whether he escaped.

Cora Attunement: Evesso Killed

If the party manages to kill Evesso during the event, advance each character's [[/attunement emberCora +1 cindaric1AttackEvessoKilled]] at the conclusion of the event.

Abyss Attunement: Evesso Escaped

If the party allows Evesso to live or escape, advance each character's [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 cindaric1AttackEvessoEscaped]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aftermath

After the battle has transpired and the smoke begins to clear, Sin urges the party to check in with @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira}, who aids the injured from the relative safety of the sanctuary's @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.zJl2ZxpXGLzOVr3b]{Kitchen}. This scene provides the characters with a chance to debrief with Mira and discuss precisely what has transpired here, along with the opportunity to receive a reward for their help.

Just Rewards

To demonstrate her appreciation for the party's intervention, Mira rewards the characters with a set of @UUID[Item.9cLLMuxK2Wwx7VTx] that belonged to her former boatswain — a rambunctious Cascilian bard named Daragan. a small chest containing [[/award 50gp]] collected from the surviving Cindarics.

Post-Mortem with Mira

Although Mira is extremely thankful for the party's aid, she remains somewhat distracted. Her mind is elsewhere as she tends to the injured and surveys the damage that's come to Corpin Sanctuary.

Any character with a [[/skill insight 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill ins 13]] check can ascertain that something is bothering Mira, as she exudes an subtle air of anxiety and distant concern.

  • Characters with [[/attunement heart]] have @Advantage[2].

Any character who also succeeds on a [[/skill intimidation 16]] or [[/skill persuasion 13]] check is able to convince Mira to share precisely what is bothering her: she's anxious about the imminent arrival of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand}, a military order whose aggressive oversight may upend the already tenuous situation at Corpin Sanctuary — particularly in regards to what the senior leaders of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.GlbJezRw2ecnVIsx]{Cindarin Temple} in Ordain have to say about it.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberCascilian]] or [[/path CindaricAdherent]] have @Advantage[2].

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

In the aftermath of the battle of Corpin Sanctuary, the Cindarics and the party must take time to recover, tend to their wounds, and gather the bodies of the dead. You can now mark this event as compete and then advance time by at least 8 hours, allowing ample time for a long rest.

Advancing time will automatically trigger the subsequent event, [[/eventState cindaric1CorpinCondemned]], which occurs the following day.
Sanctuary of Death.soverview: The party returns from the Pathways to Corpin Sanctuary, only to discover that a dreadful host of animated dead has arrived in their absence. Led by the necromancer Evesso, this cadaverous mob of skeletal creatures wreaks havoc on the Sanctuary and the Cindarics that call the place home. Once they're confronted with this horrible scene of carnage and destruction, the party must join in the fight, defeat the undead horde, and put an end to Evesso's necromantic plot before he escapes.
Sanctuary of Death.sexposition: A scene of absolute horror awaits you as the ancient elevator rises and grinds to a halt at the center of the Sanctorum. Even from here, you can see the look of abject terror on the face of a Cindaric Sage as he's torn apart by a small mob of reanimated humanoid skeletons. The sage screams in agony as some skeletons drive rusted blades into his flesh, while others rip the very skin from his bones. With their prey defeated, the skeletons turn their hollow gazes your way and begin scuttling across the stone flor of the Sanctorum to greet you.
Sanctuary of Death.ssummary: After our exploration of the Pathways tombs, we returned to Corpin Sanctuary to find the place under siege from Evesso and a skeletal horde of undead minions. A battle ensued, during which the horde was defeated and Corpin Sanctuary was saved from Evesso's malevolent scemes. Mira Wavehorn has subsequently grown concerned about the imminent arrival of The Burnished Hand — a militant group with historical ties to the Cindarics, whose advent threatens to upend political matters at Corpin Sanctuary even further.

Shadowed Depths.name: Shadowed Depths
Shadowed Depths.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party emerges from the Corpin Sanctuary Elevator into the massive underground environment of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.FJNYRa0cGLlizwYY]{Mycelian Expanse}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Search for clues of any necromantic activity.

  • Search for signs of passage by the missing sages, Evesso and Avwynn.

Evidence of Passage

This should be a short event that serves as an introduction to the Pathways biome and its environment.

Examining the Area

A successful [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]]check after taking some time examining the location allows one to take stock of the biome and gather some info about it: This place is lively, filled with numerous species of fungi and plants that are bioluminescent, and more importantly have developed the ability to survive without sunlight. There is a large amount of fungus, mold, and slime growing alongside grasses, plants, and even a few oddly colored trees seemingly unaffected by the lack of natural light.

A successful [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check while examining construction of the area yields some insights: The stone is properly ancient, bearing the hallmarks of ancient Shent architecture and stone shaping.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success Closer examination of some stranger elements in the stone work appear to predate the Shent. If you are right, these structures were built by the ancestors of the Shent and then added to some time later. The original stonework may be over four thousand years old.

Signs of Travel

A successful [[/skill survival 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] check reveals the presence of fresh tracks through the area. The higher the result of the check, the more the character can discern.

  • Result of 12+ Kicked over rocks and some trampled grass reveals a path recently taken eastward, but the trail quickly dries up.

  • Result of 14+ Not much farther ahead the splattered, glowing residue of a couple trampled mushrooms betray a haphazard run through the underbrush, likely meant to throw off pursuers and save some time. Following the path left behind becomes almost trivial as a result.

  • Result of 16+ Given the size and distance of the tracks and other markers alongside them, you suspect that the person responsible may have had a tail, or was dragging something along with them. Since the damage to the surrounding fauna isn't extensive enough to indicate something being dragged, it's more likely that this is a mark of Evesso's passage through the area.

  • Success Kicked over rocks and some trampled grass reveals a path recently taken eastward, but the trail quickly dries up. Not much farther ahead the splattered, glowing residue of a couple trampled mushrooms betray a haphazard run through the underbrush, likely meant to throw off pursuers and save some time. Following the path left behind becomes almost trivial as a result.

  • Critical Success Given the size and distance of the tracks and other markers alongside them, you suspect that the person responsible may have had a tail, or was dragging something along with them. Since the damage to the surrounding fauna isn't extensive enough to indicate something being dragged, it's more likely that this is a mark of Evesso's passage through the area.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill survival 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] is able to spot one particular oddity: a dead pyrefly, perched atop a bare spot of stone.

  • A further [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] skill check recognizes that these creatures wouldn't be down in the Pathways.

  • A further [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] leads one to deduce that the pyrefly likely got carried down here by one of the Sages, quite possible Evesso, who was recently overseeing the Cindaric ritual revolving around them in the sanctuary above.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After concluding their investigation, the party ventures forth, eventually discovering the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.bzaRoELCYlqc2Prb]{Hypogean Ossuaries} and the [[/eventState cindaric1Ossuaries]] event.
Shadowed Depths.soverview: Using the ancient elevator hidden beneath Corpin Sanctuary, the party descends deep into the subterranean Pathways, where they discover a vast otherworldly landscape unlike anything on Ember's surface. After taking in the enormity of this incredible new environment, the characters can follow scant clues southeast of here, leading them even deeper into the dim reaches of the Mycelian Expanse.
Shadowed Depths.sexposition:
The sound of the elevator's descent is all consuming, the ancient stone scraping against the walls the entire way down, as through the whole machine were entirely out of alignment. Chunks of stone dance around your feet with the vibrations, and new ones flaking off the surrounding walls to join the party around your feet as the platform continues down.

Eventually the cacophony subsides and you are faced with a landing that extends out into a considerable darkness. The air here is rich with the scent of fungus and rot, and in the distance you can make out the aura of a faint blue glow.

Sin remarks:

The energy here is so different. I don't think I've ever been this close to the Core of the world before.
Shadowed Depths.ssummary: After riding the massive elevator beneath Corpin Sanctuary to its destination, we found ourselves immersed in a vast subterranean landscape known as the Pathways. A brief search led us to discover a curious trail that leads southeast of here, deeper into the lightless depths, where our answers must await.

Emptied Tombs.name: Emptied Tombs
Emptied Tombs.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party discovers the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.bzaRoELCYlqc2Prb] within the pathways and learns a disturbing truth, that the ancient burial vaults have been emptied and there are signs of some profane necromantic ritual. In this event the party can:

  • Inspect the scene of an ancient burial site to discover evidence of active necromancy.

  • Parley with @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}, who approaches them from the shadows.

  • Learn details of an imminent attack on Corpin Sanctuary by the necromancer @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso} and his army of raised minions.

Investigating the Area

Grave Trouble

A character with [[/skill arcana 14 passive]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14 passive]] notes that a number of candles and offering bowls have been moved into a spot which has been prepared as a magic ritual site. It's very likely that magic was cast here recently, but how recently and of what nature precisely will require closer inspection.

A successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check while examining the area notes that these tombs were disturbed over a long period of time. Whoever was removing the remains from their resting places likely did so across several visits. This plan has been in the works for a while, probably weeks, maybe months.

Scanning the ground with a successful [[/skill survival 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] check notes the presence of tracks leading out of the ossuaries. A large number of humanoids gathered in a central area and then began marching westward. The amount of trampling and damage done to the surroundings was the work of a large number of people.

  • Result of 14+ Critical Success The tracks are fresh, they likely left only a few hours ago. The footsteps look haphazard and clumsy, and don't seem to be moving fast. If you left right now, you might be able to catch up with them, but it was take a few hours at least.

Left Behind

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notices a writhing figure in the dark, gaunt and humanoid, and sprawled on the hard stone.

If anyone in the party approaches the writhing figure, read aloud the following:

An ancient skeleton of frail, shattered bones and paper-thin skin lays on the stone here, grasping fruitlessly toward you as pale light glimmers within the empty sockets of its skull. Its body is broken and incomplete, unable to rise or move itself no matter tireless its efforts are.

The air around it tastes sour, not just from the ancient stink of rot, but from something worse, something which makes your skill crawl and triggers some small urge to flee in the back of your mind.

Old Bones

There is no danger presented by this withered old skeleton, it cannot move or attack, but is a portent of danger to come. Characters wishing to destroy it have @Advantage[2] on their attack as it is considered &reference[prone] @Condition[prone]. It has an AC of 8 and 1 hit point It has effectively 1 health and will be destroyed if it receives any damage. Destroying it releases a burst of harmless but intensely unpleasant corruption energy.

Rising Evil

A successful [[/skill arcana 12]] [[/skillCheck arcana 12]] check reveals the obvious: magic was used to raise the dead, and this one was too weak to carry itself. However, the presence of this magic is deeply concerning.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success The skill and power to raise a whole tomb's worth of dead would be considerable, especially if it was done all at once. It's possible there were multiple necromancers carrying this task out, or perhaps worse: one exceptionally gifted necromancer.

Characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] recognize this as a skeletal minion, which are often employed in large numbers as fodder, distractions, and support for even greater adversaries. An entire tomb of skeletons would serve that purpose fantastically.

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.I2LUSF5ogc7Bj62e]{Speak with Dead} spell Use of magic to attempt to communicate with the dead is utterly ineffective when used on this being, it is like who they once were has been erased, and they can only speak nonsense.

Characters may want to examine the ritual site nearby to understand what they are dealing with.

Examining the Ritual

At the center of the tombs is the site of a profane ritual which still ripples with volatile abyssal energy and necrotic power.

A Dark Lure

Characters feel a powerful draw to approach the ritual site as something dark and alien stirs in their chest. A [[/save wisdom 14]] saving throw [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] resists the lure, but failure results in the compulsion taking hold, causing them to approach the center of the ritual. Examining the ritual site results in the character experiencing both Up Close and Dangerous and Abyssal Murmurs as described below.

Abyssal Murmurs

It is necessary to step into the ritual space to examine its components and remnants. Entering the ritual space causes one to become afflicted with abyssal whispers for as long as they stand in the area. These whispers tease out the character's guilts, hatreds, and most destructive qualities, trying to draw them to the fore. Leaving the area causes the voices to fade immediately.

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.Mzh95utKDPIrjiH8]{Detect Evil and Good} spell detects that this area has been magically desecrated and is permeated with evil.

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} spell identifies the Necromancy school immediately.

  • Use of [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeSoul00000000]] detects that this area has been magically desecrated and is permeated with evil.

  • The [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] identifies that the magics used here are typically used in conjunction with necromancy.

Up Close And Dangerous

A successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check while looking over the ritual site notes the presence of several chalk symbols and discs of melted wax carved with glyphs on the ground. These symbols are from a school you're not especially familiar with, but can safely deduce are of the necromancy school.

  • Result of 16+ SuccessThe ritual here was enacted recently, maybe a few hours ago at most. It was elaborate and powerful, and built unlike any ritual you've ever seen before. It would have channeled an immense amount of energy. Unfortunately whoever created it was careful to destroy key aspects of its design, so you have no idea how you could replicate it.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success The ritual appears to have been drawing power from somewhere. You're not sure if it was from Ember itself, or somewhere beyond, but there are evocation and conjuration elements that lead you to believe it was connecting to and pulling energy from something. That would account for the remarkable power the ritual would have been capable of.

Inspecting the volatile ritual site requires a successful [[/save wisdom 15]] [[/skillCheck Arcana 15]] to resist the remnant abyssal energies in the area. Success inflicts [[/damage 1d4 psychic]] damage subjects the user to [[/hazard 2 willpower health void]]{{Beckoning of the Void}} from a growing pressure in the character's mind. This sharp headache may also cause nosebleeds or burst blood vessels in the eyes but is not fatal.

Characters that remain in the aura for longer than the time spent examining the ritual may need to repeat this save check at your discretion. This should not exceed more than once every 10 minutes, and the save check DC increases by 1 for each consecutive save check after the first.

Characters that fail are afflicted with the Abyssal Murmurs described above for the next two days, even after leaving the site. Giving into their darker, more destructive urges proposed by these murmurs causes the whispers to persist for another day.

At your discretion, if a character spends more than a week with the murmurs their Abyssal Attunement may increase ([[/attunement emberAbyss +1 cindaricOssuariesAbyssalMurmurs]]). After a while the murmurs will fade out, or perhaps worse, the character stops noticing them.

Banishing Evil

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.XZhdgVK3cLoxNCQl]{Remove Curse} spell can be used to remove the Abyssal Whispers effect from an afflicted character.

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} spell can be used to unravel the remnant magics here, weakening the abyssal presence to the point that it can't harm anyone inside its influence, though the whispers still remain for those within it.

The Abyssal Whispers effect can be removed from an afflicted character using [[/counterspell rune=control gesture=aspect inflection=negate dc=14]], and a character with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] can take some time while others Recover to unravel the remnant magics here, weakening the abyssal presence to the point that it can't harm anyone inside its influence, though the whispers still remain for those within it.

Heart Attunement: Evil Banished

If the party manages to dispel the necromantic magic that lingers here, advance each character's [[/attunement emberHeart +1 cindaric1OssuariesCleansed]] at the conclusion of the event.

Abyss Attunement: Undeathly Curiosity

If any character tries to learn the details of how the necromantic ritual was performed from the perspective of curiosity or interest in its power, advance that character's [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 cindaric1OssuariesRitualCuriosity]] at the conclusion of the event.

Studying the Ossuaries

The event should begin with an exploration and investigation of the ancient tombs.

Historical Holdovers

This location appears to match the hallmarks of ancient Arcturian burial styles. However, the location of it is strange, as the Arcturians weren't known to live underground, though they would have been in this region. These graves are somewhere around a thousand or two years old, and possibly even older.

Tombs like this have been discovered all across the plateau, mostly in cave formations, and only above ground. This may be the first one ever discovered in the pathways.

Arcane Oddities

Examining the large lamps scattered around the ossuaries requires a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check and reveals that they all still burn brightly with blue and purple light stemming from a flame contained in their glass bells. These flames are likely variants are eternal flame spells, but producing significantly larger flames than most. Creating flames that size likely took a considerable amount of gem dust for each.

Note: Each of the lamps is nearly four feet tall and weigh upward of 20 pounds, while they can be moved and carried, they are much too heavy and unwieldy to ever serve as normal lanterns.

Religious Remnants

Characters can examine the burial holes and their stone covers, the hanging grave markers, and the carved shrine stones, assessing their religious significance.

Studying the burial holes and their stone covers takes a bit of time and a successful [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check. On success, you note that the covers are all carved with various symbols that range from flowers to sewing needles.

  • Result of 14+ Success These hanging markers resemble traditional Arcturian death markers, albeit in a much more crude form. There are signs the cave was once decorated with dozens of these hanging markers, but the natural materials making them up rotted away long ago.

    The hanging marks that remain each have wooden rings with stone medallions bound within. These in turn have braided necks that then turn into long strings of ribbon, paper, or cloth. Those that exist here have been stained by mold and rot and are largely impossible to derive anything useful from.

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success You recognize the carved symbols on the covers look like old depictions of spirits. They also bear resemblance to traditional Arcturian grave markers, which might be where the modern symbols originally derived their design.

Characters with [[/tool woodcarver]] proficiency [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.fletchingNovice0]] recognize that careful effort was made to carve the outer wooden rings, and each one is unique. Some contain symbols or sequences of images depicting people doing things, while others hold what might be writing.

Characters with [[/tool mason]] proficiency [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.smithingNovice00]] recognize that both the large shrine stones and the stone medallions in the hanging markers were hand-made, likely with crude tools. While the large shrine stones are nothing more than stone loops with little ornamentation in most cases, the small marker medallions have all manner of varied and unique markings that likely spoke to qualities of whoever they were meant to commemorate.

Hidden Watcher Revealed

While investigating the site of the ossuaries, Avwynn, who has been shadowing the party through the pathways steps out of the shadows and wishes to talk.

Good Intentions

Avwynn has no interest in fighting the party and if they become hostile or attack her, she falls back to safety and tries to reason with them from the shadows, under the cover of a greater invisibility spell. If it's clear that the party has no interest in conversing with her, she'll fall silent and just observe the party from afar, trying to get a sense for what their intentions are.

@Embed[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]

Reading Avwynn

Avwynn is an inherently difficult character to read as she is well versed in deception and manipulation. Even in failure she appears to be entirely genuine and truthful.

It takes a [[/skill insight 17]] [[/skillCheck deception 17]] to successfully read Avwynn, which leads a character to believe she is being truthful, but is naturally evasive. She has an agenda, and she is pursuing it, but it doesn't seem to align with the abyssal influence or necromancy witnessed here.

The Secretive Sanguinary

Avwynn will initially work to convince the party that she is not responsible and - in fact - was the one that passed the note under their dormitory door to enlist the party's aid:

Before we dive into combat let me start off by saying I'm the one that slipped that note under your druid's door. I was trying to get you onto the necromancer's trail from the outset. I followed you down the elevator to lend a hand, but it looks like we were both too late.

If the party already learned that Evesso is the necromancer, they may be more trusting of Avwynn initially. If they ask her to confirm that, or if she knew, she confirms it:

Yes, that's correct. I've been suspicious of him for a while, but failed to get anything concrete. I was hoping that nudging you would put enough pressure on him for a mistake to occur. Instead, here we are.

You're not going to catch him, even if you leave right now, but you should still head back immediately, and try to save anyone you can. Plus, destroying the undead would be good for everybody, and Ember itself.

Arcane Conference

Avwynn is a skilled spellcaster, and can help confirm suspicions about the ritual if they ask.

The short answer: Necromancy ritual. The dead were raised, likely with the help of some Abyssal entity on Ember, and in so doing the world became a little more corrupted. While it's worse to raise the recently dead, animating the long-dead has equally detrimental impacts on Ember.

If the party asks her to elaborate on the detrimental effects:

Short answer: think of it like walking rot. A little bit of mold on your food can be cut off and you're fine, but leave it sit long enough and it'll take over the whole fruit. These old undead are the spot of mold, and you need to go excise them.

If they mention or ask about the Abyssal energies around the ritual:

Right, that's to be expected. Raising the dead is the domain of the Abyss and empowers its presence on Ember. Using necromancy is incredibly dangerous for everyone and everything involved. It warps the mind and spirit of the caster, can harm anyone that comes to close to the left over abyssal energies, and directly harms Ember itself.

Avwynn's Intentions

Asking what Avwynn's next move is, or why she can't get involved gets a vague response:

Simply put: I'm not really someone the Sages want to deal with. I'm from a splinter faction of the sages that broke with the doctrine pretty sharply. If they knew I was just walking through one of their sanctuaries I'd be in trouble, as would anyone that let it happen.

Characters that success on a [[/skill history 16]] or [[/skill religion 18]] [[/skillCheck society 16]] may suspect that Avwynn is part of the Sanguinaries, an religious order the broke from the Cindaric Sages long ago and were branded as heretical doomsayers and maniacal cultists.

If someone asks Avwynn if she's a Sanguinary she'll have a good chuckle, and confirm it:

That's right, good catch. We and the sages share the same theological goals, at least publicly, but have taken entirely different roads in how we pursue them. Don't let them fool you into thinking we're a bunch of crazy doomsayers, the truth is pretty far from that.

If asked to elaborate on the truth:

I'd love to get into the cultural, theological, and ideological differences between my religion and the one it broke from, but we both have far better things to be doing. You need to get back to the Corpin Sanctuary, and I need to report back to my people and get some things in motion.

Primordis Attunement: Avwynn Revealed

If a character in the party identifies that Avwynn is a Sanguinary, advance that character's [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 cindaric1OssuariesSanguinary]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once done speaking with Avwynn she departs, leaving them to carry on.

Next Steps

After concluding their investigation, the party needs to rush back to the Corpin Sanctuary elevator, and try to stop the undead force moving toward the Cindarics there. This leads to the [[/eventState cindaric1Attack]] event.
Emptied Tombs.soverview: The party explores the Pathways and finds a site where in forgotten times the dead were ceremonially entombed. This is followed by a disturbing revelation as the party discovers that these ancient ossuaries were recently exhumed and emptied of their remains.
Emptied Tombs.sexposition:
Up close, these ancient tombs have been completely ransacked. Shattered stone covers litter the ground, and the discarded shreds of corpse shrouds sit in piles in various places, yet aside from a few bones there is no sign of the numerous dead once interred here.

Worse yet, there is an uneasy sensation in the air which makes your skin tingle and muscles tense in reflexive response to some unseen danger. A faint, but repetitive, scratching sound comes from somewhere in the dark. The longer you stand in this nearly silent ossuary the more you start to hear whispers coming from the shadows.
Emptied Tombs.ssummary: We explored the Pathways beneath Corpin Sanctuary. To our surprise, we discovered ancient Arcturian tombs known as the Silent Ossuaries, where we encountered evidence of necromancy before a chance meeting with the enigmatic Avwynn Taol.

Traveling with Sin.name: Traveling with Sin
Traveling with Sin.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event can occur multiple times while traveling with Sin and provides the party with an opportunity to learn about the Cindaric aspirant, her story, and her opinions on the current situation.

This event can occur during a rest at any point during Chapter 2 if @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} is a member of the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party}. In this event the party can:

  • Discuss the current situation with Sin and learn her thoughts on the matter.

  • Get to know Sin better by understanding her story.

Thoughts on Events

The Farmstead[[/eventState cindaric1Pillaged]]

It's a shame about what happened to that little farmstead. It looked like it was such a nice and idyllic place before it was pillaged and razed to the ground. Those folks deserved better. Hell, the crops deserved better. And the fact that no survivors were found … it's an ominous occurrence, to be sure.

We'd see our fair share of woodland raiding parties in the outskirts of the Corebright, but wanton destruction of nature like we found at the farmstead is something the Strider people would never suffer lightly. It's either aimless chaos, or someone was sending the farmers at the grange a very strong message.

The Refugees[[/eventState cindaric1Refugees]]

It's unfortunate that Arcturian bandits feel emboldened to attack people so openly on the road like that. We're lucky that the refugees had someone as skilled in combat as Svala Bronwen in their group, otherwise it might have been an even grislier scene than the one we encountered. I hope we made the right choice in where to direct the survivors. Those people deserve some peace after what they've been through.

As for the raiders themselves, we should keep our eyes peeled and ears open for any would-be assailants as we continue our journey to the east. They seem like an organized group, and we don't need any surprises of our own.

Undead[[/eventState cindaric1Crossing]]

Those bloated things we encountered at Keeper's Crossing were wholly unnatural, rotten in body and spirit alike. What a fright! I'd like to hope it was an isolated incident, but the phantom in Helkas suggests otherwise … and that minor apparition was nothing compared to this!

Corpin Sanctuary[[/eventState cindaric1Investigation]]

The Sanctuary seems like such a quiet and peaceful place, it's hard to believe someone would want to upset that. But, I suppose it being built above a secret passage to the underworld kind of paints a different picture. The place is full of history; I just hope none of it bites us in the rear.

That said, the Sages have all been rather nice, haven't they?

The Pathways Ossuaries[[/eventState cindaric1Ossuaries]]

That was a cold and dark place I don't think I'd ever care to visit again. I know my work with the Core of the World will eventually take me further into the lightless depths of Ember's Pathways, but those Ossuaries were stained with evil. And whoever is using that place for ritual magic can't be good news.

It was rather convenient, though, for Avwynn to reveal herself as an ally. And I do mean that in a good way … I remain a tiny bit suspicious of her methods and motivations, but we can use all the help we can get get against the rising threat of necromancy.

Corpin Sanctuary Attack[[/eventState cindaric1CorpinCondemned]]

That was a dark day for the Cindaric Sages. I suppose it was a historical moment to be a part of, but I can still hear the raspy voices of those skeletal creatures … and I shudder when I think of the look in Evesso's eyes when he commanded his minions to do his evil bidding. It was all so awful, like some kind of nightmare made real. I could go the rest of my life without ever seeing something to terrible again.

To think, he was studying ancient necromancy in the ruins beneath the Sanctuary all along. My gut tells me this isn't the last of it. First Helkas, then Keeper's Crossing, now this. If anyone can offer proper guidance in times like these, it's the Speaker at Cindarin Temple.

Thoughts on Characters

Agraband

Agraband Swift is one of the kindest folks I've ever met. And so knowledgeable! Sure, every bard has a story to tell, but Agraband has a head full of 'em. I do love listening to his songs, and wondering what it would be like to travel some of those old Aterican roads he often sings about.

Clipper

Clipper was a wonderful companion to have on the road from Casla Brava to Helkas, and Agraband is lucky to have them in the Strayhearth fellowship. And while I haven't got much gold to speak of myself, it does seem as though Clipper has amassed a curious collection of continental wares that are well worth the coin.

Ankarist

Ankarist is a bit dour, if you ask me. Are all criminal investigators in Ordain so … sullen? And his affinity for that sword of his goes beyond a normal warrior's pride. I'd say there's more to that surly Drakon than he'd care to admit.

Lyla

Lyla seems to have a lot of responsibility on her shoulders, especially for her age. As young as I am, I can't really imagine what life would be like with that much … burden. I hate to put it like that, really I do, but if I had to worry about the concerns of House Cevher politics and society on top of my innate concerns for the safety of the natural world and its creatures, my little Keth head would pop.

Sin winces, as if Lyla herself were there with you.

Sorry, Lyla! I'm just being honest. Politics are simply too … political.

The druid laughs in self-awareness at her awkward moment.

Svala Bronwen[[/eventState cindaric1Refugees]]

That Svala was something to behold! She handled some of those raiders with proper grit, I tell you. What a fighter! Her ferocity reminds me of some of the Strider warriors I grew up with in the Corebright, where a certain familiarity with combat is crucial — and often the only thing that keeps you from becoming a woodland predator's next meal.

Mira Wavehorn (Initial Impression)[[/eventState cindaric1CorpinArrival]]

Mira seems to me like an inspired choice to lead the Sages at Corpin Sanctuary. Her background as a naval captain certainly affords her an interesting level of experience, and it must have been some remarkable transition for her … leaving that freewheeling life of open-sea adventure to become a Cindaric Sage, dedicating her days to a singular purpose. That's a kind of commitment I can look up to. And she seems pretty fun.

Mira Wavehorn (Revised Impression)[[/eventState cindaric1CorpinCondemned]]

The chaos here at Corpin Sanctuary is a sign of something, but I'm not altogether sure it's a sign of Mira's inability to lead the Sages here. Steros and the Burnished Hand have come to Mial Mountain to bring strength; Mira still harbors a compassion that is crucial to the way I see the world. I hope the Order is fair with their final decision regarding her fate as the head sage at the Sanctuary.

Avwynn Taol (Initial Impression)[[/eventState cindaric1CorpinArrival]]

Avwynn is quite remarkable, isn't she? So tall, beautiful, and confident. I look forward to hearing more about her endless supply of ancient Maziran myths and legends. Sorcerers have always been intriguing to me. Magic channeled from the earth? That I can understand … Magic from my very blood, or the stars, or wherever it comes from? Truly wild stuff, if you ask me.

Avwynn Taol (Revised Impression)[[/eventState cindaric1CorpinCondemned]]

By all accounts, Av's tall tales and outsider nature made it seem like she could have been a candidate in our search for the necromancer. It turns out, she's just an eccentric like us, with similar interests about the fate of the world — and how to stop it from prematurely arriving. We're lucky to have her on our side for now. We need all the help we can get.

Evesso (Initial Impression)[[/eventState cindaric1CorpinArrival]]

Evesso seems to be a real master of Cindaric traditions. The kind of scholar that you'd expect a reputable place like Corpin Sanctuary to have on hand. A proper historian. It's a shame we only have a day or two to learn firsthand about some of the Cindaric legends and lore he's collected in his travels.

Evesso (Revised Impression)[[/eventState cindaric1CorpinCondemned]]

A necromancer in our midsts … and I even looked up to him for a moment. I feel betrayed by his lies, and somehow responsible for not spotting his treachery sooner. I'm eager to talk about this with the Speaker in Ordain, and find out how and why such a scoundrel would be able to infiltrate the Cindaric Order, so that it may never happen again.

Luna Kerrowrath[[/eventState cindaric1Bridge]]

Luna Kerrowrath seems a bit too zealous for me, and a bit angry enough at the world to properly earn her surname. A hard life will harden a good person.

About Yourself

Your story?

I'm from a treetop town in the Southern Corebright Forest known as Sirewood, which is situated among the verdant hinterlands of the Briar Peaks. A great place to grow up, if you ask me — surrounded by incredible living signs of the supernatural world, but also safe enough from the primeval leviathans that prowl the forest on all sides.

My talents for druidic magic kicked in when I was pretty young, and I was inducted into the Primalists on my seventeenth birthday. I'm one of few Primalists that can actually harness the Growth, rather than just commune with it, so I started harnessing. After connecting to the Corebright itself, I knew there was something more; something greater than myself. Then, one day, a traveling Cindaric named Atticus came through Sirewood, and my world got a whole lot bigger.

So here I am … in search of someone or something that can help me focus and refine that connection to the Core of the World. And if I'm lucky, maybe I'll take that deeper connection back home one day.

The Primalists?

The Primalists are an ancient organization of druids that live among the Striders of the Corebright Forest. Thanks to our metaphysical connection with the natural world, we're able to become one with it by casting spells or transforming ourselves into various beasts of Ember. I've spent nearly a quarter of my life in service of the Primalists and their local efforts. And while the Primalists are a noble group — responsible for safeguarding the Corebright wilds, sometimes with their very lives — I feel a lingering responsibility to something greater.

There is more to this life than nature magic. And please, don't mistake my words or intentions … the Corebright is, and always will be, sacred to me. But how can we protect the forest if we don't look out for the world around it?

Cindarics and Primalists

Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] have a shared understanding of Sin's philosophies and can offer their own understanding of the subject to the conversation. The concept of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.1jb9zDsRFMXo7Je0]{Nature's Lifeforce} is nearly identical for the two faiths, they simply focus on different aspects of it.

The Cindaric Order?

Growing up, I knew nothing of the Cindaric Sages or their benevolent order. Then, one day about two years into my training as a Primalist, I met Atticus and everything changed. This traveling Cindaric stopped in Sirewood on a westward pilgrimage to Akazea . While he was with us, he shared everything my young mind could absorb about the Cindaric Order, their benevolent philosophies, and their mission to safeguard the spiritual integrity of Ember and its people.

From what I understand, the concept of Lifeforce as the Cindarics describe it is the very same as how Primalists view the Core of the World and its relationship to nature. I was eager to learn more. And when Atticus left Sirewood on his western passage, I found myself longing to find out precisely what the Sages have been up to all this time.

I'd like to do my part … and I'm more than a little curious, to be honest. Souls are such wonderful, inscrutable things. Undoubtedly, the Sages of Corpin Sanctuary and Cindarin Temple have much to teach me about the Heart of Ember.

Your journey?

After setting out from Sirewood, I made my lonely way east to Alavai, where I chartered passage on a ship to the Cascilian port of Hoist. From there, I traveled overland to Caxko and into the service of a frivolous group of adventurers who called themselves the Joyriders (with whom I spent a marvelous few weeks exploring the Dustlands). Fortune eventually led me to the company of Agraband Swift and the Strayhearth Caravan in Casla Brava, and the rest is history.

My path takes me further eastward, to Corpin Sanctuary on Mial Mountain, and then on to the great city of Ordain — where Cindarin Temple and the tutelage of the Speaker awaits. The Arctus Plateau and all its wonders are still quite new to me. If didn't mention it, the value of your companionship on this long and winding road is immeasurable, my friends.

Hopes for Ordain?

All I know of Ordain is what I learned from Atticus and what I've picked up on the road. I understand it's a marvelous place made of majestic white stone, full of the splendors of the modern world. I'm eager to see Cindarin Temple for myself, if only to see how it's different from the Verdant Sanctuary in Sirewood. And I've heard tale of a remarkable neighborhood known as Orchard Lanes, where the fruit is apparently so delicious it drives the local way of life.

More than anything, I actually hope the Cindarics and the other people of Ordain are accepting and have a place for a Primalist druid like me in their city. After all, I am an outsider, born of a place far removed from the metropolitan sensibilities of Ordain. Ultimately, I'd like to find out that this connection I feel isn't mine alone.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event may repeat at your discretion when the party rests next. Feel free to use any of the question and answer responses here outside the context of this event if you feel they are appropriate to mention during other situations.
Traveling with Sin.soverview: The party stops for a rest while traveling with Sin Marmot, providing an opportunity to learn more about the sociable Keth druid and the wanderlust that brings her to the Arctus Plateau.
Traveling with Sin.sexposition:
After the minute chores of making camp are finished, you find yourself in the genteel company of Sin Marmot, who regards you with an inviting look of curiosity. She wastes no time procuring an array of accoutrements from her knapsack, which she carefully assembles into a proper arrangement before her.

Among these personal affects, you notice an assortment of seeds in miniature jars, an owl's-feather quill, a tiny bottle of dark green ink, and a small notebook bound in cloth. Opening the notebook, Sin reveals a small collection of pressed flowers and flattened leaves, which she delicately lays out one-by-one on a handkerchief.

Don't mind me! Just jotting some things down in my nature journal while I have a free moment. The Arctus Plateau has so many wonderful species of plants to discover, and my journeys can sometimes be … absentminded. So I collect my specimens for catalogue later. And it looks like "later" is right about now!

The druid flashes you a cheeky grin before her countenance turns to an inquisitive one.

But enough about me. It's been a long day. What's on your mind?
Traveling with Sin.ssummary: Taking a respite from our travels to camp, we found the opportunity to discuss our current situation with Sin and learn more about this gregarious druid companion.

Reuniting with Sin.name: Reuniting with Sin
Reuniting with Sin.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event can allows the party to catch up with @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.HgE4i0dWTP2ipKmh]{Corpin Sanctuary}, following an extended period of separate exploration of the Arctus Plateau. In this event, the characters can:

  • Meet Corpin Sanctuary's dedicated leader, the former sea captain known as @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}.

  • Learn about Sin's journey to Corpin Sanctuary on Mial Mountain, including a trio of memorable events along the way.

  • Learn about the key denizens of Corpin Sanctuary and Sin's various opinions of them.

  • Find out about a strange note that was passed under Sin's door, and its bold claim about a furtive necromancer hiding in the midsts of the Sages at Corpin Sanctuary.

A Welcome Respite

The party arrives at Corpin Sanctuary, an enclave of the Cindaric Sages nestled in the crags of Mial Mountain, situated a day's travel west of Ordain. The party is welcomed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.WHdKr6CkT5xF7lqr]{Entry Courtyard} by the enclave's leader, Mira Wavehorn, along with their companion Sin Marmot.

@Embed[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]

Sin regards the characters as favorable companions on the road to Ordain. No matter how long it's been since their last encounter, she greets the characters like a long-lost friend.

@Embed[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}

Meeting Mira

Mira ambles with the party in the Entry Courtyard with a desire for them to explain their visit in adequate detail, and isn't afraid to use small talk to coax information out of them. Topics that Mira is quick to bring up in conversation while meeting the party include:

  • The party's background and any affiliations they might have.

  • A brief history of Corpin Sanctuary and the Cindaric order itself.

  • The mission of Corpin Sanctuary as a refuge for lost and displaced peoples, which has been impacted and hampered by recent events.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]]check indicates that Mira is scrutinizing whether or not the party are refugees themselves, and is apprehensive of those who might take unsavory advantage of the Sanctuary's graces.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]]check is familiar with Mira's role and responsibilities as a Cindaric Sage and the leader of Corpin Sanctuary. Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] have @Advantage[2] on this skill check.

If the characters beseech Mira for shelter at the Sanctuary, one of them must succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check. If successful Mira is willing to offer the party room and board for a night or two as they rest up and decide their next course of action.

  • Failure: If the characters fail to persuade Mira, Sin eventually steps forward and vouches for the characters. Mira's opinion of the party softens, and she invites the party to stay for the evening (if not longer). Additional dialogue options with Mira are listed below.

On Corpin Sanctuary?

Corpin Sanctuary was built long ago to establish a satellite location for Cindaric initiatives, removed from the commotion of urban life in Ordain. The people of the Golden Flats and beyond are always in deserving need of charity, and — out here on the mountain, in our quiet little enclave — we pride ourselves on a more … intimate connection with Ember through the land itself. But we do share the same goals as our cohorts in Ordain. We're just a bit more rustic.

Regarding Undead?

Make no mistake, these undead creatures Sin speaks of suggest a greater threat to the natural order of Ember and the sacred heartblood that flows within it. The Soul Cycle is the wheel upon which our very cosmos turns, and these threats of restless souls and abyssal incursions are most troubling. Worse yet, you aren't the first allies of the Cindaric order to share word of these kinds of calamities. And I fear you won't be the last.

After the party has had a chance to meet Mira and gain their proverbial footing, they are free to catch up with Sin about her journey to Corpin Sanctuary. Before departing to attend to her duties, Mira assigns the party lodging with Sin in one of the Sanctuary's @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.g5ZhafC273TnlsRm]{Empty Dormitories}.

Mira takes her leave, and the party is free to wander the Sanctuary grounds with Sin as they see fit. The only areas that are considered off-limits are the Sages' private quarters in the @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.XNmFfrViLKfVJiM8]{Dormitories} and @UUID[JournalEntry.maDMFsfifjKH0sjS.JournalEntryPage.OnKJslXqG9NYJCI6]{Mira's Office}.

The Druid's Journey

Music: Sin's Theme

While the party catches up with Sin, play [[/soundscape music sinTheme sinTheme]].

Catching Up with Sin

Sin details her journey to Mial Mountain for the characters, including:

  • her discoveries at the Pillaged Farmstead,

  • her encounter with the Ambushed Refugees,

  • and the undead terrors of the Harrowed Crossing, where she survived a harrowing fight with sodden undying corpses that could spew a putrid and dangerous vomit.

Sin also updates the party on her thoughts about the notable denizens of Corpin Sanctuary:

  • @UUID[Actor.GXxXO20NBaIKBxEu]{Mira Wavehorn}

  • @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}

  • @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx]{Evesso}

Finally, Sin introduces the secret note that was passed under her Dormitory door the previous night: the @UUID[Item.sgtcxR29Zf7ukZyP]{Note to Sin}.

Dialogue options for these various topics are presented below.

About the Farmstead

A few days after we parted company, I came across the smoldering remains of a pillaged farmstead known as Dradley Grange, a couple of miles west of the River Elenain. By all accounts, the farm houses and fields had been ransacked before they were razed to the ground. And there were no signs of survivors. I hate to think of what might have happened to those folks, but I have a few suspicions …

About the Ambushed Refugees

A day later, while heading southeast towards the river, I encountered a group of Arcturian refugees who were displaced from the village of Skybrush and a few scattered homesteads. As luck would have it, this impromptu caravan of migrants was beset by a raiding party of well-trained highwaymen just as I was happening upon it. Thanks to my timely arrival and the swift axe of a friendly warrior named Svala, we were able to drive off the bandits — bandits who, I might add, seemed a bit too organized for my tastes.

About the Harrowed Crossing

The perils of my journey came to a head at Keeper's Crossing, where the ruined bridge held a few surprises I won't soon forget … While fording the turbulent river, I was attacked by nearly a dozen undead corpses. Evil creatures bloated with rot and sodden with river water. Those foul things could spew a noxious puke that necrotized flesh and bone. Truly horrible stuff. I barely escaped with my life, and it will be too soon if I ever see one of those putrid faces again.

Mira Wavehorn (Initial Impression)

Mira Wavehorn seems to me like an inspired choice to lead the Sages at Corpin Sanctuary. Her background as a naval captain certainly affords her an interesting level of experience, and it must have been some remarkable transition for her … leaving that freewheeling life of open-sea adventure to become a Cindaric Sage, dedicating her days to a singular purpose. That's a kind of commitment I can look up to. And she seems pretty fun.

Avwynn Taol (Initial Impression)

Avwynn Taol is quite remarkable, isn't she? So tall, beautiful, and confident. I look forward to hearing more about her endless supply of ancient Maziran myths and legends. Sorcerers have always been intriguing to me. Magic channeled from the earth? That I can understand … Magic from my very blood, or the stars, or wherever it comes from? Truly wild stuff, if you ask me.

Evesso (Initial Impression)

Evesso seems to be a real master of Cindaric traditions. The kind of scholar that you'd expect a reputable place like Corpin Sanctuary to have on hand. A proper historian. It's a shame we only have a day or two to learn firsthand about some of the Cindaric legends and lore he's collected in his travels.

The Curious Note

Music: Tension Builds

As Sin reveals the note, change reset the music to default and switch the mood to tension: [[/soundscape music reset]], [[/soundscape mood=tension]].

Sin saves the most important information for last. Once she's caught the party up to speed about her journey to Corpin Sanctuary and her first impressions of its inhabitants, she quietly shares the most actionable information at hand: the contents of the @UUID[Item.sgtcxR29Zf7ukZyP]{Note to Sin} passed beneath her Empty Dormitory door.

If possible, Sin directs the party to a quiet spot of the Sanctuary or back to the Dormitories for relative secrecy (far away from the prying eyes and ears of potential suspects).

A look of trepidation crosses Sin's face before she speaks, much more timidly than usual.

Someone slid this beneath my dormitory door last night.

Sin holds out a small piece of folded parchment. Even from here, you can see the handwritten text inked upon its top fold:

To: Initiate Marmot.
For your eyes only.

The Passed Note

The note's interior reads:

Heed my words, for they are astoundingly true. There is a necromancer lurking among the sages here at Corpin Sanctuary. As outsiders, it seems you and your party are the most capable to investigate this dangerous affair. Most importantly, your intentions here seem noble and just.

Please, rid the Sanctuary of this invader, for all our sakes. And be careful to avoid suspicion — the eyes of the necromancer are everywhere.

The note is written anonymously and conveys the accusation that there is a necromancer lurking among the sages at Corpin Sanctuary. As outsiders with seemingly noble intentions, the author of this note wishes for the party to closely investigate the sanctuary and its sages.

Any character who wishes to scrutinize the note can do so, and notices the following with a successful [[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check, that the handwriting is unfamiliar to everyone in the party and that the ink is still quite fresh.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

If a character casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLocateCrea]{Locate Creature} spell in an attempt to identify the letter's author, their effort falls short. Unbeknownst to the party, the original owner of the letter (@UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}) is protected from divinations by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.aU62xVUBYkAQWIHv]{Nondetection} spell.

If a character uses magic to attempt to identify the letter's author, their effort falls short. Unbeknownst to the party, the original owner of the letter (@UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}) is magically protected against attempts at divination.

Sin has her own opinions about the origins of the note, and wishes to immediately confer with the party:

Sin's Suspicions

Sin Marmot is relatively unfamiliar with the actual practice of necromancy, and solicits the characters for conversation about the note's revelation and whether or not it has ties to their previous encounters with undead. Sin is also eager to discuss:

  • Who could possibly be a suspect, based on the people the party has met since arriving — including the Cindaric Sages and visitors alike.

  • The relationship of Corpin Sanctuary to the Cindaric Temple in Ordain, and what kinds of strains might currently be affecting it.

  • Her trust in the Cindaric Sages as an organization, and the honest desire to keep the charitable order safe from those who might befoul it.

After some discussion about their collective thoughts and suspicions, Sin establishes a plan with the party to begin an investigation in the morning following a vigilant long rest Rest.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has had adequate time to speak with Sin and catch up about their respective journeys to Corpin Sanctuary and the impending investigation, they're ready to begin their inquiries in earnest.

Next Steps

Sin and the party can remain in Corpin Sanctuary to start collecting evidence and clues about the furtive necromancer during the events of [[/eventState cindaric1Investigation]].
Reuniting with Sin.soverview: After traveling on separate paths for a while, the party reunites with Sin Marmot at Corpin Sanctuary, a conclave of Cindaric Sages built upon the craggy slopes of Mial Mountain. Here, Sin reveals the presence of a strange plot at the Sanctuary, made evident by a strange note slipped under her door the night before.
Reuniting with Sin.sexposition:
As you approach the entrance to Corpin Sanctuary, you're struck by an overt sense of reverence and awe — if not your own, then of the noble Sages who attend to this peaceful and wayward place. The impressive stone steps of the enclave's entrance ascend toward a great oaken doorway that exudes a remarkable sense of history and tradition.

Just then, the doors open to reveal your druid companion Sin Marmot, who wears an exceptionally wide smile on her face today. She stands beside a Kiska femme clad in the burgundy robes of a Cindaric Sage. This woman's smoky voice addresses you with a measure of overt officiousness, apprehensive of your arrival.

Welcome to Corpin Sanctuary. And please don't be startled; being perched upon a mountainside has its advantages. I hope your hike up the hill wasn't too strenuous, and that your journey to our doors has been kind. Please, come in. Sin has told me much of your journeys together.

Sin offers a few excited words in salutation of her own.

I'm so glad you made it! I knew you were right behind me all along. And you look as marvelous as ever. Didn't I tell you they were a feisty team?

Your druid companion looks up to the Cindaric Sage, who obliges her with a smile.

Indeed you did. Come, friends! Settle in and make yourselves comfortable.
Reuniting with Sin.ssummary: We reconnected with our friend Sin Marmot at Corpin Sanctuary, where she caught us up to speed on her journey thus far. Sin also revealed a curious note to us that she received the night before we arrived. The note, written by an anonymous author, suggests a necromancer has secretly been operating at the Sanctuary for some time. We have an investigation on our hands if we wish to discover who this so-called necromancer actually is (and what they have in store for the Cindarics).

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This side quest occurs during Chapter 2 as the party arrives in Nain to witness the legendary storytelling of Amalthea Stonecraft firsthand. There are no prerequisites for this quest and it can be undertaken at any time, although it is certain to be encountered if traveling with Lyla while undertaking the @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu] quest.

Difficulty

The "Book of Tales" quest is designed for a party of Level 3 characters, although the finale of the quest, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000.JournalEntryPage.7WywAnBMYYu13Ay5]{The Moon Child of Lake Jinro}, may prove difficult for a party that is not yet Level 4.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 2 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the [[/eventState bookTalesVortest]] and [[/eventState bookTalesReturn]] Events.

The Arctus Plateau's most accomplished storyteller, an Aster bard named @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft}, is nearing the end of her years and needs help finishing her latest collection of local legends. Her job for the party seems rather simple: visit four different citizens of the Golden Flats and transcribe their unique stories. But the party will discover most of these tall tales to be remarkably true, and will eventually find themselves at the center of Amalthea's grand and magical narrative.

Presented somewhat like a collection of short stories, this quest takes the party on a tour of the Golden Flats (and beyond) to meet various persons of interest; along the way, they’ll obtain detailed glimpses into Arcturian life and culture via these esoteric NPCs and their local folklore. Appropriately, "The Book of Tales" functions a bit like a collection of standalone events rather than a serial narrative, culminating in an epic moment of metatextual storytelling involving the party members and a magically-transmogrified version of the quest-giver.

After handing the party a hardbound manuscript full of blank pages, Amalthea sets them off to pursue the narratives as they see fit; and once they set out from Nain, the characters must gather the four stories on Amalthea's list before uncovering a fifth and final tale. During this finale, the party travels west to discover "the Moon Child of Lake Jinro"— a mysterious creature that turns out to be none other than Amalthea Stonecraft herself, reborn in a new adolescent body through some strange metaphysical process of Ember.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft}

  • @UUID[Actor.wI4zsTgX2eIy4VtQ]{Rattletrap, the Rickety Man}

  • @UUID[Actor.t98dgswBccdv1dHQ]{Moriah Foxhaven}

  • Eb Hargrove

  • Gabi & Brandt Hargrove

  • @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask}

  • @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0]{Corvana Vortest}

    Dangers & Enemies

  • Jodessa Cort

  • @UUID[Actor.ZuWduzUSGS6i4NZm]{Gore Bird Swarm}

  • @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]{Jurtak Warrior}

  • @UUID[Actor.m86FIWDHh47htZNy]{Jurtak Geomancer}

  • @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK]{Signaran Assassins}
