  • @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Juvenile Garganthus}
Overview.soverview:
Rumor has it that the Arctus Plateau's most celebrated storyteller — an Aster bard named Amalthea Stonecraft — lives in the riverside settlement of Nain, and that her stories have a strange way of changing the lives of those who hear them. Some say the famed orator invites raconteurs to visit her in Nain to tell their own tales. But whatever their reason for stopping by the Stonecraft estate, the party is in for the surprise of several lifetimes when Amalthea sets them off on an adventure unlike any other.

Once they've proven their mettle in conversation, the characters are hired by Amalthea to travel throughout the Golden Flats to gather four local legends for her latest — and likely final — book of Arcturian folklore. These folk tales include: the story of a sentient construct in the forgotten village of Steed's Point, the disappearance of a rural adolescent who collects parchment boats, the hermetic plight of a Signborn wizard who's led a lifetime of secrecy, and the saga of an Arcturel quarryman who's rumored to be afflicted with a strange crystalline curse.

"The Book of Tales" will take the party on an investigative journey to four distinct corners of the Golden Flats. Once they collect all four of the stories assigned by Amalthea Stonecraft, the characters will escort Lady Stonecraft herself to a lunar shrine at Lake Jinro for a surprising finale of legendary proportions.

The Moon Child of Lake Jinro.name: The Moon Child of Lake Jinro
The Moon Child of Lake Jinro.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat and exploration event features a climactic battle that pits the party against a @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Juvenile Garganthus}, a powerful Pathways predator that has recently reached the surface world via a tunnel beneath the @UUID[JournalEntry.5sSPjtjFWhTo8dmZ]{Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine}. In this event, the characters must:

  • Help the storyteller @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft} complete her 80-year cycle of Aster reincarnation at the height of the Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine's winding precipice.

  • Explore the ancient ruins of the Lunar Shrine for evidence of its historical and modern significance.

  • Protect a younger, reincarnated Amalthea from a deadly assault by a Juvenile Garganthus.

The Storyteller's Ritual

Once the party reaches the island near the center of Lake Jinro, they must ascend to the Lunar Shrine situated at the top of the location's hilly terrain. There, Amalthea can channel her magic through the Shrine's standing stones and complete her process of reincarnation.

The characters have ample time to converse with Amalthea as they move toward the island's precipice (see "More Info From Amalthea" below). However, when Lady Stonecraft finally begins her ritual, a Juvenille Garganthus arrives just in time to spoil the ceremony (see "Attack of the Juvenile Garganthus" below).

Full details about this location and its associated encounters are available in the @UUID[JournalEntry.5sSPjtjFWhTo8dmZ]{Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine} area walkthrough.

More Info From Amalthea

Amalthea invites the party to a moment of preparation before the group ascends the hill to the Lunar Shrine.

The famed storyteller is reluctant to over-explain the events that are about to take place, and is quick to suggest that the mystery itself is somehow a necessary component to the reincarnation ritual. If the characters wish to press Amalthea for more information about what precisely is happening in this moment, they can certainly try.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill per 15]] check are able to pry the following information from Amalthea as she approaches the Shrine proper:

  • She has a vague recollection of returning to this place on several occasions throughout her lifetime.

  • She suspects the Lunar Shrine is somehow able to focus the power of Ember's moons into a magical force that affects her Aster physiology.

  • Her manuscript is a mysterious key to it all, and only by transcribing a certain number of stories — including stories told and collected by others — can she complete the fated process of her reincarnation.

The Ritual Begins

Read the following aloud as Amalthea and the characters reach the island's overgrown precipice.

Amalthea takes her place upon the dais at the center of the standing tones. Closing her eyes, the aged storyteller starts performing a series of somatic gestures while orating the rest of her tale. Fragments of arcane phrases weave in and out of the narrative, and you hear the bard mention things like "the Moon Child" and "a grand return" among her esoteric chants.

The stone menhirs begin to swell with arcane brilliance and the wind stirs with uncanny excitement as the storyteller continues her tale.

Discerning the Storyteller's Ritual

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check arc 11]] while observing Amalthea's ritual of rejuvenation is able to tell that she has called upon the magical power of the stone menhirs to focus her bardic and innate spellcasting abilities.

  • Result of 13+: There's no doubting this metaphysical occurrence has something to do with Amalthea's rare nature as an Aster.

  • Result of 15+: Amalthea's apparent attunement to Orbis, the Spirit Moon, seems to be a factor in the ritual's potency — as evident by the Orbis-related birthmarks that glow upon her skin during the ritual's zenith.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check nat 15]] check is able to deduce that the magic of the Lunar Shrine is both natural and supernatural in nature — a synthesis of worldly and otherworldly enchantments channeled through the primeval materials used in the shrine's construction.

Characters with [[/attunement emberOrbis]] are able to decipher the interplay of the Lunar Shrine with Amalthea's ritual, and understand it to be a part of a supernatural order laid out by Ember itself.

Once the characters have had a brief moment to observe Amalthea's ritual in action, their moment of wonder and amazement is cut short by the appearance of a rampaging Pathways predator.

Attack of the Juvenile Garganthus

Lake Jinro has recently become the domain of a @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Juvenile Garganthus}, which leaps into combat when the characters least expect it.

An encounter with the Garganthus here is inevitable, and the party must protect a vulnerable Amalthea Stonecraft from this malicious Pathways predator as she completes her ritual.

When the timing feels appropriate, read the following text aloud:

Just then, as the arcane pageantry of Amalthea's ritual begins to reach a fever pitch, the earth below your feet rumbles and the trees nearby shudder in response. Before you can blink, a huge creature leaps from below to take its own place on the island's grassy precipice…

Consult the "Garganthus Attack!" section of the @UUID[JournalEntry.5sSPjtjFWhTo8dmZ.JournalEntryPage.CUBZWXArz36FtriO]{Ancient Lunar Shrine} location journal for full details about the encounter with the Juvenile Garganthus.

Completing the Ritual

Once the Juvenile Garganthus has been defeated in combat, Amalthea resumes her arcane rites.

Unwavering in the face of the monster's brutal attack, Amalthea appears more focused than ever, and before you know it the entire precipice of the island is enveloped in a blinding flash of bright white light. Your eyes adjust to reveal a most incredible sight: a young child — no more than five — now stands where the aged storyteller once stood, draped in oversized garments.

And much to your amazement, this child unmistakably bears the countenance and plumage of Amalthea Stonecraft, albeit in a much younger body. She regards you with a distinct look of familiarity that confirms your suspicions before producing her manuscript and scribing upon its page once more…

What's old was new once more, and I stood young again on the novel edge of a recognizable shore. Away to Nain, if we may; that place where the rivers run wild as imagination.

The young author appears lost in thought, as if struggling to maintain a grip on the here and now. You wonder if a night in her own bed back in Nain might be the best course of action, and can't help but detect a singular innocence on young Amalthea's face.

The characters will discover that "Moon Child of Lake Jinro" hinted at in Amalthea Stonecraft's manuscript is none other than Amalthea herself, reborn in a younger body through some strange metaphysical process of Ember.

From here on out, Amalthea is effectively a 5-year old instead of an 85-year old, but her stat block and bio otherwise remains the same. She has been rejuvenated by the magical effects of her uncanny ritual and its effect on her unique Aster physiology.

About the Ritual:

I apologize for the mystery and the pageantry, my friends. But it seems the spectacle itself is part of the magic's power, along with your observation of it. The moons move in mysterious ways. I cannot thank you enough for your guidance and protection.

Regarding the Garganthus:

I'm not exactly sure what that monster is … or was. But tales of subterranean creatures escaping the Pathways are not altogether unheard of. Especially since the great quake. Perhaps it was attracted to the magic of the standing stones. Let's just hope it was bad timing and not an ill omen of things to come.

What next?

Next, I journey back to … where is it I'm from, again? I seem to recall a river, and the most wonderful speaking statues …

The Lunar Menhirs

If any characters take the time to commune with one of the six lunar menhirs here at the shrine, they can strengthen their attunement to the moon associated with that particular standing stone.

Akon Attunement: The Akon Stone

Any character who successfully communes with the shrine via the Akon Stone advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 bookTalesMoonChildAkon]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aura Attunement: The Aura Stone

Any character who successfully communes with the shrine via the Aura Stone advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 bookTalesMoonChildAura]] at the conclusion of the event.

Cora Attunement: The Cora Stone

Any character who successfully communes with the shrine via the Cora Stone advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 bookTalesMoonChildCora]] at the conclusion of the event.

Mayis Attunement: The Mayis Stone

Any character who successfully communes with the shrine via the Mayis Stone advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 bookTalesMoonChildMayis]] at the conclusion of the event.

Orbis Attunement: The Orbis Stone

Any character who successfully communes with the shrine via the Orbis Stone advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 bookTalesMoonChildOrbis]] at the conclusion of the event.

Ragen Attunement: The Ragen Stone

Any character who successfully communes with the shrine via the Ragen Stone advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 bookTalesMoonChildRagen]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

The party is set to guide Amalthea back home to Nain, where they'll help the reincarnated storyteller reacquaint herself with her hazily-recollected past.

Next Steps

Once the Juvenile Garganthus has been defeated and the ritual complete, the party must escort the reborn Amalthea Stonecraft — now the five-year old "Moon Child" of Lake Jinro — back to the safety of her home in Nain. There, the characters can help her rediscover a lifetime of memories during the events of @UUID[.33XTuShe8mUGNyUI]{The Turn of a Friendly Page}.
The Moon Child of Lake Jinro.soverview: Utilizing clues that emerged from Amalthea Stonecraft's arcane manuscript, the party has escorted the storyteller to the Lunar Shrine of Lake Jinro. Here, they must help Amalthea complete the uncanny rites of her unique Aster reincarnation, and protect her from the deadly attack of a monstrous Pathways predator known as a Juvenile Garganthus.
The Moon Child of Lake Jinro.sexposition:
Amalthea scrawls furiously in her manuscript as she steps onto the island shore. The words on the page begin to illuminate her face with arcane splendor. And as you listen, the legendary storyteller starts to narrate this forthcoming tale she transcribes…

The Storyteller had been here before. She'd seen the towering stonework of the Shrine's ancient menhirs, had smelled the musky odors lapping at the water's edge, had felt the promise of something new. Here and now, with her companions at her crooked back, the aged Storyteller struggled to deny the fateful tug of curiosity that pulled her towards the top of that lonesome hill.

And once more, she gave herself permission to explore the alluring unknown.

Amalthea looks back to you with an innocent grin, and asks:

Well… are you ready?
The Moon Child of Lake Jinro.ssummary: We escorted Amalthea Stonecraft to an ancient Lunar Shrine on an island in the middle of Lake Jinro, where she completed her strange rite of reincarnation. During the rites, we were attacked by a huge Pathways predator known as a Juvenile Garganthus, who seemed curiously out of place on the surface of Ember.

The Crystal Quarryman.name: The Crystal Quarryman
The Crystal Quarryman.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and combat event involves a surreptitious meeting in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel} with @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask}, a Kiska miner whose fateful encounter with a Luxaran relic has curiously started transmogrifying his physical form into a crystalline one. In this event, the characters can:

  • Locate @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.rh4RdGCvghwWvPgR]{Zodi Trask's Apartment} in lower Arcturel's "The Dives" district, where they can meet the so-called crystal quarryman himself and discuss the nature of his strange affliction.

  • Scrutinize the strange @UUID[Item.ysL3KPZFVsOZG5yF]{Uncanny Relic} responsible for Zodi's transformation — a celestial device that Zodi himself strangely can't perceive — in an effort to determine how to reverse the crystallization effect.

  • Defend themselves from a surprise attack by a quintet of @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{Skither} spies, who've been sent to observe Zodi before retrieving the device for its creator — the Tyraphem known as @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Aburyx}.

  • Help restore Zodi to his original organic form using the Uncanny Relic itself, at which time they can transcribe the quarryman's tale in the @UUID[Item.p5m9fgcCoUVlThf7]{Stonecraft Manuscript}.

An Incident in Arcturel

Unless the characters have met Zodi Trask during a previous visit, they will need to gather information throughout the sinkhole town about the Kiska quarryman and his whereabouts — the Dives district of Lower Arcturel.

The party is most likely aware of Amalthea's plot hook from @UUID[.CBSwfaeBVs7j08kd]{The Stonecraft Summons} and little else: "Zodi Trask is rumored to be undergoing a most strange transformation — one that is turning him to solid crystal. Find out how his perilous situation came to be."

The characters need to find Zodi Trask, analyze the strange alien source of his transformation, and extract a cure from it. If they can solve the relic’s conundrum, the characters gain the insight to reverse the crystallization process.

In Search of Zodi Trask

The following skill checks allow the party to gather various information as they search Arcturel for details about Zodi and his plight. The characters must succeed on two of the skill checks listed below in order to locate Zodi's home apartment in lower @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel}, and one of these checks must be a Charisma skill check.

Rather than simply resolving these skill checks, you may want to extrapolate them into dialogue-driven scenes with assorted NPCs of Arcturel. Feel free to award advantage to certain characters for particularly inspired roleplaying or dialogue choices.

[[/skill inv 13]] Characters who succeed on a general investigation check while snooping about town are able to discern that Zodi Trask is a well-liked member of the community who dwells in the lower district of Arcturel, also known as "the Dives."

  • Result of 15+: The character is able to drum up more specifics, including the approximate location of Zodi's apartment in the Arcturel Dives.

  • Result of 17+: An informant is able to confirm Zodi's presence at his home apartment and relate vague rumors about the quarryman's condition, along with the speculation of its cause.

[[/skill his 15]] Characters who are more familiar with Arcturel and its local history may already be aware of Zodi Trask based on his reputation as a gregarious foreman for House Cevher's mining operations here. Someone at the mine or in town should be able to provide more information.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on this check.

  • Any character who succeeds on this check has advantage on Charisma checks made to gather information within Arcturel.

[[/skill ins 13]] Characters who attempt a vibe check while searching for information about Zodi Trask find that people are legitimately concerned about the foreman, who is considered to be one of the more ethical and good-natured citizens of Arcturel. Despite his overtly commercial Trading House affiliation, Trask is known to be a "man of the people" with an open heart and a lot of grit.

  • Result of 17+: It stands to reason that a hands-on craftsman like Zodi Trask would be afforded an apartment somewhat close to the mine itself, where proximity to daily operations might be advantageous for House Cevher and Zodi himself.

  • [[/culture emberArcturian]] characters have advantage on this check.

[[/skill deception 13]] Characters who manage to successfully deceive the locals into divulging information are able to learn the specific location of Zodi Trask's apartment in the Dives district.

  • Result of 16+: While they haven't seen Trask himself, his most observant neighbors have noticed a strange pallid glow emanating from the dark interior of his apartment from time to time.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] have advantage on this check.

[[/skill persuasion 13]] Characters who manage to successfully persuade the locals into divulging information are able to learn the specific location of Zodi Trask's apartment in the Dives district.

  • Result of 16+: The characters are warned about arousing the suspicion of Trask's neighbors while investigating his apartment. Dives dwellers are said to be on edge about the disappearance of such a prominent member of the blue collar community.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] have advantage on this check. Any character who offers a bribe of 15 gp or more also has advantage on this check.

[[/skill intimidation 13]] Characters who manage to successfully intimidate the locals into divulging information are able to learn the specific location of Zodi Trask's apartment in Lower Arcturel.

  • Result of 16+: The characters are warned about a rumor suggesting Zodi was exposed to a rare supernatural disease in the mines. Some say the foreman already lies dead in that Dives apartment of his, while others maintain he's disintegrated altogether.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge warfare]] have advantage on this check. characters have advantage on this check.

Once the party members have succeeded on two of these skill checks, including at least one Charisma check, they are able to pinpoint the precise location of Zodi Trask's Apartment in lower Arcturel — which is his last known location aside from deeper in the mines.

For more specific dialogue that citizens of Arcturel might offer during a conversation, consult the replies below.

Regarding Zodi Trask:

Zodi Trask has a reputation for showing on time and delivering the goods — traits that have earned him a rather notable position as a local foreman for House Cevher. He's an invaluable part of Ordain's mining operations in Arcturel.

When Zodi stopped showing up to work a couple of weeks ago, Cevher's enterprises began to suffer, and word spread quickly about his disappearance. Attempts to check on him at home have been unsuccessful, and he didn't leave a single word with anyone about a potential departure.

About Zodi's Situation:

Some say Zodi was been stricken with a strange affliction, and that's why he's either disappeared or gone into hiding or both. Rotten lungs from the mines or some madness from the depths … Who knows? Could be anything, as close as we are to the Pathways and gods knows what lurks in 'em.

What Really Happened

Unbeknownst to the people of Arcturel, the @UUID[Item.ysL3KPZFVsOZG5yF]{Uncanny Relic} was planted in the mine by the celestial known as @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Aburyx} — a subordinate of the Tyraphem @UUID[Actor.fcK7WLaLCCcMP9oL]{Pyix} — who placed it there for the very purpose of its discovery.

The Uncanny Relic is an arcane catalyst, created to enact unpredictable change on whoever it comes into contact with; and Zodi Trask is the unfortunate soul who made contact. Aburyx seeks to not only study the effects of the Relic on humanoids of the Arctus Plateau, but wreak havoc among House Cevher's mining operations in Arcturel as well. Fundamentally, the Uncanny Relic is capable of afflicting living humanoids with a potent curse known as the Relic's Touch, which transmutes the cursed humanoid's flesh into a glassy esoteric substance.

Zodi experienced a his own fateful encounter with the Uncanny Relic rather recently when working the House Cevher mines. Uncovering the relic from a lode of alloyed silver, Trask was exposed to its curse and immediately fell victim to its alarming transmogrification — which started turning his physical form to one of pure crystal. The essence of his original Kiska features remain, but his hands and feet have become as stony and translucent as the edges of a nacreous diamond.

And it seems this abstruse crystallization is on the verge of spreading; as a result, Zodi has quickly and resolutely retreated to the solitude of his home apartment in fearful anticipation of what's to come. Furthermore, Zodi can no longer perceive the Uncanny Relic itself, which presents a strange conundrum for the quarryman and anyone who dares to help him. The Uncanny Relic is currently located in the rear workshop section of Zodi Trask's Apartment.

Meeting Zodi Trask

Once the party locates @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.rh4RdGCvghwWvPgR]{Zodi Trask's Apartment} in lower Arcturel, they can survey the local area for signs of the quarryman himself. Soon enough, they'll discover evidence that the crystalline transformation has started spreading to Zodi's surroundings, and that a strange otherworldly relic is responsible — a relic Zodi can no longer perceive.

When the characters finally investigate the home apartment of @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask} in Arcturel's Balconies, read the following aloud.

The isolated apartment before you would be relatively unassuming if it weren't for the occluded window on its front door, which appear to have parchment handbills plastered upon it from within. Following closer inspection, these wax-covered papers appear to be a mix of old news sheets and mining requisition forms.

If what the locals say is true, this should be the dwelling of Zodi Trask, the quarryman in Amalthea Stonecraft's tale — and someone has taken efforts to hastily conceal the apartment's interior. Your attention drifts towards an iron knocker affixed to the front door, shaped like an inverted pickaxe.

Salutations and Introductions

@UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask} actually lurks inside the apartment bedroom in silence, well out of sight and succeeding on nearly every attempt to hide.

The characters can knock on the door to get Zodi's attention, but they must mention either their quest for Amalthea Stonecraft or their affiliation with House Cevher in order to convince him to talk — let alone open the door and let them enter.

Once the party has convinced Zodi to parley with them through the closed door, read the following aloud:

A baritone voice with an Arcturian accent speaks to you from the other side of the thick wooden door, streaked with anxiety that almost sounds of cracked glass.

If I told you what awaited you on the opposite side of this door, you might not be so eager to open it. So tell me, friend … who are you and what …

The voice cracks a bit, as if under pressure.

What are you doing here?

Entering the Apartment

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 14]] check, a [[/skill intimidation 16]] check, or a [[/skill persuasion 14]] check is able to convince Zodi to open the door and let the party in.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on these checks.

  • Characters who are proficient in Intelligence (Arcana) also have advantage on these checks.

The characters automatically succeed on these skill checks if they tell Zodi a quick recap of a tale they've previously written in the @UUID[Item.p5m9fgcCoUVlThf7]{Stonecraft Manuscript}.

If @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher} happens to be with the party, she'll let the party attempt to convince Zodi before demanding his compliance herself, at which point he'll quickly open the door and rush the characters inside.

If the party decides to force their way into Zodi's apartment, a successful [[/skill dexterity 18]] check using Thieves' Tools is required to pick the lock on the apartment's front door. Alternately, the door can be bashed in with a successful [[/skill athletics 20]] check (which might also draw the attention of Zodi's neighbors or other citizens of Arcturel).

As Zodi opens the door, the characters can finally take full stock of his physicality.

@Embed[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]

As the party enters Zodi's apartment, the quarryman is sure to shut the door behind them, which promptly draws attention to the crystalline transformation afflicting his hands.

Something peculiar draws your attention as your host closes the door behind you. Both of his hefty stoneworker hands appear to have turned to solid crystal, shimmering and nacreous like some arcane silicate. His digits sound like crackling glass as he moves them with slow precision, and you hear a similar hyaloid quality to his footsteps as he ushers you into the front room.

About His Condition:

It's hard to explain. My hands, my feet, they're … changing. Becoming crystal, like some horrible gemstone. It hurts, and I can feel it spreading. I can feel it in my throat … creeping like a cold chill …

You notice the crystalline sheen of Zodi's hands, and consider how delicate they look compared to his furred skin. Just then, a look of pain crosses the quarryman's face as the crystal spreads, streaking up his arm like a flash frost on a cold winter night.

What Happened:

I don't rightly know. It was a few days ago, at least. I remember heading into work, but came home feeling sick.

Zodi takes stock of his translucent hands and feet, and expresses a look of acute disquietude.

Something's happening to me. I'm all messed up. I've been hiding here ever since. I don't want anything to happen to anyone, and I can't risk spreading it any farther than it's grown …

Examining Zodi's Condition

After Zodi allows the party to enter his apartment, they can study the effects of his condition and attempt to locate the otherworldly relic that's responsible for it — the @UUID[Item.ysL3KPZFVsOZG5yF]{Uncanny Relic}, which is located in the northeastern workshop of Zodi's Apartment.

The longer the characters spend with Zodi, the more difficult it becomes for him to talk — the Relic's Touch is taking hold before their very eyes. By the time they move onto their examination of the relic, Zodi grows weary of struggling to speak, and will only utter short phrases.

[[/skill arc 13]] Zodi's transformation is in-progress and incomplete, but is certainly of an arcane nature. The cause for this magical transmutation must be very powerful, and no known arcane or divine spells comes to mind that could be directly responsible.

[[/skill med 13]] The glasslike transformation is most concentrated at Zodi's extremities, including his hands and feet, along with his mane of hair. Certain internal organs also seem to be affected, including Zodi's tongue and throat, his stomach, and other unseen innards. The crystalline transformation is obviously progressing, and Zodi Trask is in mortal peril if something isn't done to stop or reverse the condition.

The @UUID[Actor.MJfOzwa6uawHDhHA.Item.iCaiYRPxSxowvFJa]{Detect Magic} spell will reveal a strong aura of transmutation magic surrounding Zodi's entire body, with his glasslike extremities appearing most brightly.

Attempts to reverse Zodi's condition using the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} spell, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.XZhdgVK3cLoxNCQl]{Remove Curse} spell, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGreaterRes]{Greater Restoration} spell, or similar magic proves to be ineffective — Zodi Trask can only be saved from the encroaching doom of the Relic's Trouch via the power of the Uncanny Relic itself.

Locating the Uncanny Relic

No matter what they say to Zodi or what questions they ask him, he is able to perceive the Uncanny Relic. He also cannot remember finding it, and struggles to remember that it even exists. The characters must discover the strange item for themselves.

[[/skill perception 13]] The character spots a soft pearlescent glow beneath the cracks of the closed door to Zodi's office in the northeast corner of the apartment, or they can hear a soft metallic drone coming from within.

[[/skill investigation 13]] The character is able to follow a trail of tiny crystal growths around the apartment, starting from the front door and terminating at a larger concentration near the closed door to Zodi's office. Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on this check.

Inside the office, the desk that holds the Uncanny Relic is bathed in the dim nacreous light that it sheds, and is surrounded by scattered moss-like growths of crystal and silicate.

Analyzing the Relic

The characters can attempt to analyze the Uncanny Relic for its properties and try to determine how they might use it to reverse the transmutation that has taken hold of Zodi Trask. Furthermore, the Relic can be neutralized so that no further harm can be done.

[[/skill inv 13]] or [[/skill prc 13]] There seems to be an inherent connection between Zodi and the Uncanny Relic; the Relic emits a low hum that grows in frequency the closer Zodi gets to it in physical proximity. Furthermore, the transmogrification seems to be spreading to Zodi's apartment; the door knob, the door jamb, and several footprints throughout the place are covered in tiny crystalline growths that seethe with soft arcane lambency.

[[/ancestry emberAltyra]] and [[/culture emberTayan]] characters and those with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or [[/knowledge celestials]] characters have advantage on skill checks made to examine the Uncanny Relic.

[[/skill arc 13]] A modicum of training in Arcana is able to reveal the magical essence of the Uncanny Relic, although its properties and true nature remain mysterious.

  • Result of 16+: Those more versed in the ways of the arcane can discern that the Uncanny Relic most likely holds the key to reversing the strange transmutation that affects Zodi Trask, despite (or perhaps because of) being the source of it.

[[/skill nat 15]] A well-rounded understanding of the natural world confirms that the Uncanny Relic is not native to terrestrial Ember, and must hail from some otherworldly place like one of the Inner Realms.

  • Result of 18+: A more learned naturalist is able to accurately ascribe a Luxaran origin to the relic.

Signara Attunement: Luxaran Influence

If the party manages to successfully connect the Uncanny Relic (or Zodi Trask's condition) to the Inner Realm of Luxarum, each character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 bookTalesQuarrymanRelic]] at the conclusion of the event.

Celestial Interlopers

As the party begins to examine the Uncanny Relic, they are attacked by a group of Luxaran celestials, who have been observing Zodi in secrecy nearby.

Celestials Attack!

A scrappy group of 5 @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{Skither} keep watch over Zodi and the Uncanny Relic throughout the course of the event: one in the workshop, one in the bedroom, and three in the front room. As the characters begin to unravel the mystery of the relic and its effect on @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi}, these celestials will intervene at the most dramatically appropriate moment in an attempt to abscond with the relic.

You spy something out of the corner of your eye: a small metallic creature lurks in the dark recesses of the apartment's clutter, seeming to appear out of nowhere. Before you know it, four more of these odd interlopers appear. Combat is afoot as these intruders pivot their attention towards the relic!

@Embed[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0 count=5]

Skither Tactics

Utilizing their @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.zJEEHoXmsC6vgnz1]{False Appearance} trait, one or more of the Skither will attempt a surprise attack against the character nearest to the Uncanny Relic in an effort to take the relic from them. Successful escape would include flying away into upper Arcturel and beyond, well out of capture range.

During the heat of battle, the Skither will make use of @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.UaSFbeDp4UQqHs4j]{Pack Tactics} and their @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.kIbBwGuzxy7FN4xT]{Rend} attack to swarm the party member who holds the Uncanny Relic, or whoever poses the greatest threat to their mission.

It's unlikely these Skither will make use of their @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.hZGnt69Mp5meOQlq]{Self Sacrifice} ability to trigger @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0.Item.bXttKphal9Z1FHk5]{Dying Burst} — as their mission is to extract the Uncanny Relic — but they can resort to these measures if the moment is desperate enough.

Preventing Escape

If a Skither manages to grab the Uncanny Relic and break away from the party to such an extent that is seems escape is imminent, Zodi himself is granted a special legendary action: Zodi uses his @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58.Item.JSaiQr46w5LKIwo8]{Nimble Leap} before making a desperate ranged attack against the Skither with an improvised weapon. This attack is made with advantage, and the Skither drops the Uncanny Relic in the same square.

Failing this, an @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturian} from Arcturel can step in to distract the escaping Skither long enough for the party to intervene.

The Quarryman's Tale

Zodi Trask encountered the Uncanny Relic while digging one day and claimed it for himself, totally ignorant of the dire consequences of the uncanny artifact’s powerful Luxarum paradigms. With the Skither dispatched, the party can find a way to destroy the item and revert Zodi back to his normal form.

Restoring Zodi's Physical Form

Once they find the Uncanny Relic and deal with the Skither intruders, the party can attempt to destroy the strange magic item.

A successful [[/skill arcana 13]] or [[/skill investigation 13]] check reveals the following: the Uncanny Relic is a wondrous item of a most fragile nature, created to resemble a precious otherworldly gemstone, and can be destroyed with a concentrated effort. Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or [[/knowledge subterranea]] have advantage on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill athletics 15]] check can destroy the Uncanny Relic with a heavy blow.

As soon as the Uncanny Relic is destroyed, Zodi Trask's bizarre transformation to crystal is halted, and his normal fleshy form slowly returns to its original state.

Zodi Trask's voice returns when the characters manage to restore his physical form via the Uncanny Relic, at which time he can relate the narrative of his tale.

At once, the Uncanny Relic starts floating in the air just before emitting a brilliant luminance that streaks outward in blinding striated beams. The relic slowly begins to spin, and quickly gathers speed, eventually moving so quickly that it starts folding in on itself in a strange display of metaphysical improbability.

With a flash of light, the Uncanny Relic vanishes before your very eyes, and the only signs of it that remains are the crystalline extremities of Zodi Trask, who holds his hands aloft in amazement as the glasslike transformation recedes. You watch as the color and texture of fur return to the quarryman's flesh, and he breathes a belated sigh of relief before addressing you with gratitude.

Who knew a hard day's work could be so hard?

Trask unslings his trusty pickaxe, and traces his thumb down the wide steel blade with a self-knowing nod.

I suppose you want to know how all of this happened … I assure you, it's nearly a mystery to me. The day began like any other. Our latest assignment involved the excavation of a newly-discovered lode of silver and gemstones in House Cevher's deepest holdings. I found the relic that very first morning on the new site, hidden in a vein of silver alloy. It was almost as if the thing was calling to me, begging me to hew it from the rock, with my bare hands if necessary ...

As soon as I touched that accursed, otherworldly stone, I felt something come over me. Some dangerous, unseen force was at work, and I knew in my heart it spelt doom for the people around me. So I hustled the weird relic back to my apartment just in time to keep it secret and safe. The next morning, the transformation had taken hold. My fingers were solid crystal, just as you saw them earlier. In the days that followed, the crystalline curse spread further and further. It's a miracle you intervened when you did. I dare say I was well on my way to becoming a permanent fixture.

And what led me here? A lifetime of taking initiative; and of doing what's right. Stone-shaping is in my blood, part of my lineage. And something about this weird little sinkhole town always felt like home to me. The nights are long here, and sometimes these people need a strong hand to guide them through the darkness. It feels good to have a sense of purpose. A place to make a difference. But I guess, as far as this whole … curse, is concerned … I'd say I was in the wrong place at the right time.

I hope my story satisfies your assignment, friends. It's the only one I've got.

Cora Attunement: Zodi Trask's Tale

If the party manages to successfully record Zodi Trask's Tale in Amalthea's Manuscript, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 bookTalesQuarrymanTale]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once Zodi Trask's tale has been written into the Stonecraft Manuscript, the characters can hear the soft music of Amalthea's driftwood wind chimes stirring on the breeze.

Next Steps

If the party has other stories to collect for the Stonecraft Manuscript, they will need to do so next.

Once all four stories have been gathered and transcribed into Amalthea's enchanted book, the narrative events of @UUID[.h3qAMVVRjXYZrEP3]{The Manuscript Awakens} will occur.
The Crystal Quarryman.soverview: The party journeys to the sinkhole city of Arcturel to learn the story of Zodi Trask, a House Cevher mining foreman who became the target of a strange curse while working in the quarry one fateful afternoon. It seems Zodi Trask is turning to solid crystal, and the characters must help break the curse after surviving an attack from an otherworldly cadre of small Luxaran celestials.
The Crystal Quarryman.sexposition: The glimmering lights of Arcturel's lustrous fungi and inkaro lanterns — reflected and refracted through countless mineral growths throughout the sinkhole — remind you of Amalthea's story of the so-called Crystal Quarryman, who resides somewhere within the town's twisting subterranean sprawl.
The Crystal Quarryman.ssummary: We investigated the mystery of the "Crystal Quarryman" of Arcturel, a miner named Zodi Trask who had come into contact with a dangerous Luxaran relic. After repelling an attack from a malicious group of celestials, we were able to use the power of the strange relic to reverse Zodi's transformation to solid crystal before it was too late.

The Signborn's Secret.name: The Signborn's Secret
The Signborn's Secret.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration and combat event invites the party to explore Vortest Tower, the remote dwelling of the Signborn mage @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0]{Corvana Vortest}, in search of her story for Amalthea Stonecraft. In this event, the characters can:

  • Reach Vortest Tower and uncover the otherworldly secrets of the strange facility, including a method of journeying to Signara via the tower's powerful Daemos enchantments.

  • Explore @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.cHJSlRXSX9wvV7br]{Vortest Tower} for Corvana Vortest and clues about what happened to her.

  • Discover a group of Signaran assassins, fiendish creatures known as @UUID[Actor.MaUAJFmggmFalVeK]{Jahud}, who've been dispatched to Ember on a mission to slay Corvana and steal the @UUID[Item.Qy8YeWMH8PmAxyS5]{Orphic Reliquary} she protects.

  • Learn about Corvana's clandestine mission to protect the Orphic Reliquary for her liege, the Daemos known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.3ZDcyUW0ydYE84rj]{Nalgomith}.

Exploring Vortest Tower

In pursuit of the completion of Amalthea Stonecraft's Book of Tales, the party journeys to Vortest Tower at the southeastern edge of the Golden Flats. Here, they'll discover a rather deserted tower antechamber, where they must search for clues and the eponymous Signborn mage: the elusive Corvana Vortest. A full description of The Vortest Tower location can be found on the @UUID[JournalEntry.tdpdWJgLONFmRPKI]{Vortest Tower} area walkthrough.

The Signborn's Tale

Once the party has successfully routed the Jahud attack and saved Corvana Vortest from an untimely fate, they have a moment to explain their mission from Amalthea. As long as the characters are straightforward in the description of their quest and the details associated with it, Corvana sees no reason to relate her tale as a reward for the party's heroic efforts.

Read the following aloud when the characters ask Corvana to tell her tale:

The Signborn mage regards you with a moment of curious hesitation before her eyes drift to the arcane manuscript at your side, the volume of stories you've been collecting for Amalthea Stonecraft.

Your selflessness deserves a reward. And you clearly have a greater purpose, if that tome you bear is half as enchanted as it seems.

Corvana steadies herself and stows her implements while surveying the scene around you. A foul ichor seeps from the Jahud corpses onto the glassy floor.

These Jahud didn't arrive here on a whim. They came in search of a powerful Signaran artifact that resides here in the confines of the tower's interdimensional pocket, something I've been charged to protect since birth.

The Signborn mage produces something from the folds of her robes: an octahedron made of alloyed silver and nacreous crystal, which shimmers with otherworldly iridescence. The artifact floats in the palm of her hand as she continues.

This is the Orphic Reliquary, a sacred vestige of my liege, the Daemos Nalgomith. It contains venerated knowledge acquired through countless eons of study and experimentation. Its secrets are unfathomable, and its possibilities endless. It holds the very history of my people.

Like all Signarans and their kin, I am descended from one of the sixteen Daemos who rule the realm of shadow from places unseen. Nalgomith is my sovereign and liege, and it is by Nalgomith's will that House Vortest has endured, with purpose. Like my parents, and a handful of generations before them, I am sworn to protect the Orphic Reliquary from those who might corrupt its knowledge for their unsavory purposes. Since birth, I have honed my sorcery and my studies to prepare for the inevitable: a day when the minions of Kerastes would arrive to take the Reliquary by force. Indeed, the Jahud are foul creations of Kerastes, the Clandestine Arbiter, and were sent here to slay me and abscond with the Reliquary.

Fortunately, you intervened. And the Orphic Reliquary continues to elude the grasp of the ill-intended. But we must remain vigilant, friends — the minions of Kerastes are as relentless as the Daemos themself.

My life has been quite a solitary one, until now. I hope this account of mine is sufficient for your storytelling. Perhaps now that we've made an example of these assassins, other would-be interlopers will take heed and keep Vortest Tower out of their petty schemes. Or perhaps I'll find a new place to hide the reliquary. Time, and the fascinations of Nalgomith, will tell.

Signara Attunement: Corvana Vortest's Tale

If the party manages to successfully record Corvana's Tale in Amalthea's Manuscript, each character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 bookTalesVortestTale]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once Corvana Vortest's tale has been written into the Stonecraft Manuscript, the characters can hear the soft music of Amalthea's driftwood wind chimes stirring on the breeze.

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

If the party has other stories to collect for the Stonecraft Manuscript, they will need to do so next.

Once all four stories have been gathered and transcribed into Amalthea's enchanted book, the narrative events of @UUID[.h3qAMVVRjXYZrEP3]{The Manuscript Awakens} will occur.
The Signborn's Secret.soverview: The party visits the remote dwelling of a Signborn mage named Corvana Vortest, in search of her unique tale of inheritance from the Inner Realm of Signara. Once they reach Vortest Tower, the characters will be transported to a pocket of Signara via the tower itself, and must make their way through this otherworldly facility to rescue the Signborn mage from a band of fiendish assassins.
The Signborn's Secret.sexposition: Remarkably, there's no immediate sign of the eponymous Signborn mage. There is a curious and utter calm to this place, which is haunted by the silence that occupies it. If the infamous Corvana Vortest is here, she's nowhere to be seen.
The Signborn's Secret.ssummary: We visited the tower of the Signborn mage Corvana Vortest. After being transported to a confined pocket of Signara, we encountered a band of fiendish assassins known as Jahud, who were sent to Ember by their Daemos lord in an attempt to kill Corvana Vortest and abscond with a powerful Signaran artifact. Fortunately, we managed to turn the tide of the attack — sparing the Signborn mage from a dismal fate and learning her story along the way.

The Boy Who Collected Boats.name: The Boy Who Collected Boats
The Boy Who Collected Boats.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration allows the party to pursue the story of young Eb Hargrove, a boy who has a proclivity for finding parchment boats on the riverbank riddled with archaic messages. In this event, the characters can:

  • Visit the Hargrove Farmstead, where Eb lives with his mother and father, Gabi and Brandt Hargrove — only to discover that the boy has just recently gone missing.

  • Inspect the Hargrove Farmstead for clues about the missing boy's whereabouts, focusing on: toys scattered in the front yard, the location of Eb's favorite fishing spot, and the confines of Eb's bedroom.

The Hargrove Farmstead

With little more than Amalthea's prompt in-hand, the party must set out for the Hargrove Farmstead, approximately four miles north of Nain on the eastern bank of the river. Once the characters arrive, they'll find out young Eb is missing, and the Hargroves could use some timely help finding him.

No matter the time of day, the Hargroves can be found in the yard woefully lamenting the loss of their son. When the characters decide to approach the farmstead, read the following aloud:

As you survey the farmstead, the frocked woman takes note of your arrival and assuredly makes her way towards you. Drawing near, she looks back to the sullen man hoeing the field for a brief second before mustering a flimsy smile.

Well, you look like a capable group. And thirsty. We've got plenty of clean water in the well, and hospitality for those that deserve it. The name's Gabi Hargrove. So, what brings you all the way out here?

A glint of hope drifts to the woman's tired eyes as she awaits your introduction.

Once the party explains their reason for visiting, the woman continues:

As soon as you mention the boy's name, Gabi's eyes alight with a spark of hope.

Ebdan Hargrove is my everything, friend. His little eight year-old smile can melt the hardest heart, and his silver eyes are brighter than the dawn. You've never met a child with more enthusiasm about these changeful fates of ours. Eb's been the light of our lives ever since he came into this world, and it will be a cold day on Ragen before I give up on him.

You'll recognize my Eb by his tawny hair and his silvery-gray eyes. And he loves the color red. He was wearing a red tunic the day before he disappeared. You see … five days ago, we woke up to find Eb gone, missing along with a few of his things and an old rucksack. Someone had pillaged the pantry as well. His little footsteps led out to the river and … that was it.

The young mother is overcome with emotion, which she stifles a bit before continuing.

He's always been a good swimmer … News must travel quickly for you all to have arrived so soon. And for that we are very grateful.

Meeting the Hargroves

Brandt Hargrove (LG, Arcturian Human, he/him) remains speechless during the party's visit, overcome with anxiety and grief about the helplessness of his son Eb's disappearance. His wife Gabi Hargrove (CG, Arcturian Ashka, she/her) is eager for answers, however, and will welcome the party into their household if there's any chance the characters will help find the missing boy.

Gabi offers the party a round of water to quench their thirst, and invites them to join her on the porch or in the front room to discuss the plight of young Eb's disappearance.

Gabi and Brandt are both relatively ignorant about the cause of Eb's vanishing, but they're both anxious to see their boy return home safely. While Brandt remains overtly silent, Gabi has the following information to share and recapitulate:

  • Eb has been missing for five days.

  • Life on the farm is simple, but easy. Eb has never wanted or needed for anything.

  • Eb's favorite pastime included folding parchment boats that he'd send downriver, and collecting the parchment boats of other children that live upstream — from places like Storsa's Strand and various homesteads along the river.

  • If the party wants to explore the Hargrove Farmstead for clues, the characters should focus their investigative efforts on three locations in particular: the Toys in the Yard, Eb's Fishing Spot, and Eb's Bedroom.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill ins 12]] check or casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} spell is able to confirm the veracity of Gabi's claims.

Once conversation has been exhausted, Gabi officially solicits the party for their help with locating Eb. In exchange for their services, she's willing to offer them the only meager wealth the family has: a @UUID[Item.EV4Na2YgLh0ELDId]{Fluorite Bracelet} heirloom worth 25 gp and as many crops as the characters can carry (treat as @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3.Item.AdIhK3nCeK5AlzQa]{Rations}).

About Eb's Paper Boats:

As long as I can remember, children on the river have sent parchment boats scrawled with wishes and other messages downstream towards Nain. My own nan taught me how to fold boats when I was about five; and she was my age when she learned the pastime.

Eb loved collecting boats that didn't find their way all the way to the falls in Nain, and he loved sending his own downstream. I wish he was out there putting one in the water right now…

About the Hargroves:

Brandt and I settled here on the farm about ten years ago, after we inherited this plot of land from my family. He's a good man, a good provider; even if he doesn't have much to say at a time like this.

Neither one of us has any extended family to speak of, none that we keep in touch with, so Eb brought a lot of life to this little house. And it's too damn easy to notice when it's gone.

Gathering Clues

If the party decides to help the Hargroves locate Eb, Gabi invites them to take a look at anything around the farmstead they might consider useful, including: the Toys in the Yard, Eb's favorite riverside Fishing Spot, and the contents of Eb's Bedroom.

The scattered array of toys in the farmstead yard invites scrutiny, but offers very little conclusive information about Eb's disappearance.

Toys in the Yard

Characters who take the time to examine the yard will locate a variety of rustic toys and playthings befitting an adolescent boy of eight: a collection of stone and glass marbles, a small army of tiny wooden soldiers, and a weather-beaten hobby horse.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill inv 12]] check comes to the conclusion that these toys have simply been neglected or dismissed, but don't point towards any other evidence.

Eb's favorite fishing spot down near the water's edge offers some vague indications about the series of events that led to Eb's vanishing.

Eb's Fishing Spot

Characters who take the time to examine the fishing spot will be able to find some rustic, child-sized fishing gear that's been cast aside: a rod and a tangled reel with no hook or lure, a small wooden bucket full of driftwood snags and polished river stones, a fishing net that's been patched a few times too many.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill sur 14]] check is able to notice a few sets of weeks-old Eb-sized tracks that travel to and from the waterfront towards the farmstead's front door. The newest set of tracks, however, journeys to the river's edge and disappears — as if Eb was either pulled into the current, or waded directly into the water of his own volition.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill prc 13]] check or a [[/skill inv 13]] check is able to locate a @UUID[Item.paNbwhjOgqXKTOuw]{Tiny Copper Key} in a hollowed out rock near the fishing gear. Casting the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.SleYkHovQ8NagmeV]{Locate Object} spell on the key are directed towards the lockbox in Eb's Bedroom (see below).

Eb's bedroom is the location of the definitive clues that will point the party in the right direction to find the missing boy.

Eb's Bedroom

Characters who take the time to examine Eb's bedroom will discover (alongside a standard array of adolescent furniture and toys) an overstuffed satchel full of parchment boats of various sizes and make. Most of them are blank and a few are scrawled with famous Arcturian nursery rhymes or expressions of well-wishes.

A [[/check perception 15 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] check allows a character to locate a loose floorboard in Eb's room, which can be easily pulled away to reveal a hidden compartment containing Eb's Lockbox. Alternately, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill inv 13]] check can locate the loose floorboard while knocking on the hollow compartment.

  • Eb's Lockbox can be opened with the @UUID[Item.paNbwhjOgqXKTOuw]{Tiny Copper Key} found at Eb's Fishing Spot. The lockbox can also be opened with a successful [[/check dex 13]] check by any character using thieves' tools or with a successful [[/check str 18]] check.

Eb's Lockbox contains a secret stash of three parchment boats, each of them marked with crudely-scrawled writing. @UUID[Item.EPqMu6ou5XyYZlFW]{Parchment Boat 1}, @UUID[Item.5cAdWNe21wMMOXiZ]{Parchment Boat 2}, and @UUID[Item.dVL91wTuVWAqqgus]{Parchment Boat 3} appear to be crafted from handwritten letters, featuring the same handwriting, and detail a curious story:

  • Closer inspection of these three hand-scrawled missives reveals a narrative… via these three notes, a young girl named "Jo" claims to have found a cave upriver where a society of children has formed. Hidden away from the scrutiny of adults, this "Calloway Cove" is a paradise for the lonely and forgotten children of the Plateau, who lack the friends or siblings to provide true companionship at a young age. Furthermore, Jo claims that the cave halts the aging process, and that the children who live there will never grow old.

  • By all accounts, it seems these letters compelled Eb to follow their guidance to locate this so-called cave a few miles upstream.

The text of these three special parchment boats from the secret stash of Eb's Lockbox is presented below for convenience.

@UUID[Item.EPqMu6ou5XyYZlFW]{Parchment Boat 1}

Hello. My name is Jo. I'm ten years old. I grew up in Storsa's Strand. But now I live in Calloway Cove. It's special here. There are no adults to tell us when to wake up or when to go to sleep. Nobody makes us wash our ears, and nobody tells us what to eat. My new brothers and sisters take care of me here. I hope you have a special place, too!

@UUID[Item.5cAdWNe21wMMOXiZ]{Parchment Boat 2}

Hello! My name is Jo and I live in a special cave by the river, which we call Calloway Cove. I've only been here for a few weeks. Some of the older kids say that they've been here for years and never get older. I don't know if I believe them, but everybody else seems to. There are lots of kids here and we all take care of each other. We don't need adults. They don't understand.

@UUID[Item.dVL91wTuVWAqqgus]{Parchment Boat 3}

Hello! My name is Jo and I'm looking for friends to join us in Calloway Cove. I'm ten years old and we have our own city here, where we make all the rules and nobody ever tells us no. Baxon says the water here is magic, and that we'll never get sick or old if we keep drinking it. Bax is my friend, so I believe him. But I miss my family sometimes. I guess it's okay to make a new family, isn't it?

Concluding the Event

Once the characters have located the three parchment boat letters in Eb's Bedroom and are satisfied with their investigation, they can proceed northwards along the river to find this so-called "Calloway Cove" and the missing boy himself.

Gabi invites the party to return as soon as they have any information (or if they simply need of rest and sanctuary).

Next Steps

The party must journey two miles northward, where they can discover the hidden riverside lair of the kidnapper Jodessa Cort during the narrative events of @UUID[.SDdk5RvBu514GicD]{Down by the River}.
The Boy Who Collected Boats.soverview: The party journeys to a farmstead north of Nain, where an adolescent boy named Eb Hargrove collects parchment boats inscribed with what seem to be the centuries-old wishes of long-forgotten children. Unfortunately, young Eb appears to have gone missing, and the party must help locate the boy for his worried parents before they can hear his curious tale.
The Boy Who Collected Boats.sexposition: You spy a solitary farmstead nestled on a grassy hillside just a stone's throw away from the banks of the Eastern River. A scattered array of children's toys decorate the overgrown yard, and a sullen Arcturian man aimlessly weeds a small field next to the farmhouse with a chipped garden hoe. A frocked woman on the opposite end of the property stares at the horizon upstream — her eyes intensely squinted in solemn scrutiny or consideration. The silence here is almost deafening.
The Boy Who Collected Boats.ssummary: We ventured to the Hargrove Farmstead north of Nain in search of young Eb Hargrove and his peculiar collection of parchment boats. When we reached the farmstead, Eb was nowhere to be found, and his parents were distressed about their missing boy. Fortunately, clues we found in the boy's room and near the river bank have steered us towards a cave upriver, where we hope to find out more information regarding Eb's disappearance.

The Rickety Man.name: The Rickety Man
The Rickety Man.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event featuring social and combat elements allows the party to solicit @UUID[Actor.wI4zsTgX2eIy4VtQ]{Rattletrap, the Rickety Man} for his personal story to add to the Stonecraft Manuscript. In this event, the characters can:

  • Be tasked with a special errand from the absent-minded Rattletrap after prompting him with a special question from Amalthea Stonecraft.

  • Explore the ruins of @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr]{Steed's Point} to gain Rattletrap's favor by fetching an out-of-reach heirloom, surviving combat with killer Jurtak along the way.

  • Learn about Rattletrap's true origins and the source of his curious sentience.

Rattletrap's Mission

The characters will most likely encounter Rattletrap in the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.X6okKjJy1vST39Cg]{Steed's Point Fields}, where they'll be able to ask him the question mentioned by Amalthea Stonecraft: "how he came to be." This will trigger the start of "The Rickety Man" quest event, and lead to the following social interaction.

You notice a shift in the Rickety Man's body language as you finish your question. The construct grows silent for a brief moment before turning to you with an arresting sense of curiosity. Despite his static countenance, Rattletrap's newfound enthusiasm is unmistakable.

What's this? You want to know how Rattletrap came to be? Then you must learn about the greatest smithy the Plateau has ever seen…

The Rickety Man appears lost in thought for a second, then addresses you once more.

But sometimes, this dusty ol' brain of mine has trouble rememberin'. Maybe if you fetch me something peculiar that might help me recall the way things were… a special keepsake. If only I could remember where it was…

The Construct's Quest

The party will need to help @UUID[Actor.wI4zsTgX2eIy4VtQ]{Rattletrap} recall the basic elements of this "keepsake" he mentioned, including its current location: @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.nxcYkQrl7JRWmD3R]{Steed's Smithy} in the northwest corner of town.

After his initial remarks above, Rattletrap can be steered towards the following points of conversation:

  • Exactly who the statement "the greatest smithy the Plateau has ever seen" refers to.

  • Precisely what the "special keepsake" mentioned could be.

  • The hazards of Steed's Point and the invasive species that have brought it to ruin.

After issuing the call to find the keepsake he can't quite remember — a magical tool known as the @UUID[Item.kmShhWv8eU9cHwfx]{Shardsteel Hammer} — Rattletrap will ultimately advise the party to steer clear of the cruel Jurtak warriors and hunters who prowl the overgrown streets of Steed's Point, testifying to the efficacy of their deadly poison.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill ins 13]] check is convinced of the veracity regarding Rattletrap's account of Steed's Point and its ongoing threats.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/check his 15]] check is well-versed in the history of Steed's Point and its inhabitants. They know about the founder, Bertron Steed, and his notoriety as a talented smithy. They're also well-aware of the scourge of Gore Birds and Jurtak that were part of the village's downfall.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/check nat 16]] check is familiar with the basic qualities of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.tLSBe3kfPlvqmnH2]{Jurtak}, including their extensive use of poison, their subterranean origins, and the savagery of their hunting tactics.

  • [[/culture emberArcturian]] characters and those with [[/knowledge crafts]] or [[/knowledge souls]] are able to quickly confirm the fact that Rattletrap is no ordinary Woven Construct, as reflected by the expert quality of the craftsmanship and/or sapient wit on display.

Rattletrap can also point the characters towards the grassland artifice of Moriah Foxhaven — an agrimage that roams the plains west of the River Nain. She is rumored to have developed a potent ward against the Jurtak poison, and may be able to provide the party with material aid in the form of her so-called "Grassland Talisman."

About The Smithy:

Yours truly was created by the great Bertron Steed, the intrepid founder of this village and the most talented smithy to ever swing a hammer. Steed can work wood and steel in perfect tandem, you see. A craftsman like no other, full of grit and ambition. The kind of fella you want to be around, to learn from, and to impress. A leader, with a good heart. I often wonder where the old man is now… it's been a terribly long time. Terribly long, indeed.

>About The Keepsake:

Now, that's a good question. My memory ain't quite what it used to be, you see… I suppose it has something to do with Bertron? I suppose it's special enough to recognize when you see it.

Why Not Fetch It Yourself?

I learned long ago to keep to my field. The Jurtak won't bother messing with me out here in the field, but they'll tear these old wooden limbs up faster than a summer wildfire if I roam too far into their territory. You all look to be made of sterner stuff than ol' Rattletrap, and you came this far for my story, so I reckon' you'll do the job better than anyone else.

About the Jurtak:

Those scaly, six-eyed monsters are good at eatin' meat and causin' a fuss, and not much else. I'm lucky I don't have to worry about the poison they seem to pour on everything, but you might not be so fortunate, my friends. You may want to consider arming yourselves against the venom with some kind of protection. Have you heard of a Grassland Talisman?

The Grassland Talisman:

There's an agrimage who roams the Golden Flats west of here, a beast rider who travels with a group of like-minded drifters. Her name is Moriah Foxhaven, and they say she can forge a charm that protects its wearer from the Jurtak's poison. Seek her out before you dive headlong in to the bramble and get yourself roasted on a Jurtak spit.

Find Moriah, and tell her Rattletrap sent you. That might be your best bet for surviving a trip to Steed's Smithy. I'd hate to lose more friends; it's awful lonely here sometimes.

Once the characters have gathered enough information, they must make their way east and then north through Steed's Point to reach their destination: @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.nxcYkQrl7JRWmD3R]{Steed's Smithy}.

Exploring Steed's Smithy

Characters familiar with Steed's Point will be well aware of its dangerous denizens, including the @UUID[Actor.ZuWduzUSGS6i4NZm]{Gore Bird Swarms} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.tLSBe3kfPlvqmnH2]{Jurtak} raiders that prowl the ruined village's overgrown grounds. The presence of these predatory species makes it difficult for live humanoids to traverse the village without the furtive cover of stealth or magic.

Whether or not they leave and return to Steed's Point with the aid of Moriah Foxhaven's @UUID[Item.dixDloUZsbCXhNbj]{Grassland Talisman}, the party must explore Steed's Smithy and locate Rattletrap's special keepsake known as the @UUID[Item.kmShhWv8eU9cHwfx]{Shardsteel Hammer}. Originally owned by Bertron Steed himself, this hammer is the key to activating Rattletrap's reluctant memory — and the secret tale of his curious origin.

Mayis Attunement: The Grassland Talisman

If the party chooses to leave Steed's Point in order to retrieve a Grassland Talisman before they continue, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 bookTalesSteedsPointJurtakTalisman]] at the conclusion of the event.

Heart Attunement: Jurtak Eliminated

If the party manages to successfully rid Steed's Point of the invasive Jurtak, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 bookTalesSteedsPointJurtak]] at the conclusion of the event.

Rattletrap's Tale

Once the characters return to the Steed's Point Fields with the Shardsteel Hammer in hand, they can offer it to Rattletrap to magically jog his memory and hear the secret tale of his creation. As the Rickety Man relates his story, one of the characters must transcribe the tale in the Stonecraft Manuscript (if not recall it from memory later).

Rattletrap reacts to seeing the hammer as soon as the party presents it:

Well, isn't this a sight for sore eyes.

Rattletrap's statuesque countenance appears fixated on the hammer as you produce it for him. He reaches forward to grab it, and once the keepsake is in his wooden hands, you see it glow with a scintillating arcane brilliance that lights up the construct's face.

This, my friends, is the Shardsteel Hammer, an invaluable tool used by the late Bertron Steed.

The Rickety Man looks off to an overgrown patch of dirt in the northwest corner of the field, a tract you've previously overlooked until now. There, a human skeleton barely peeks out from beneath the tall grass, and a realization comes to you that Bertron Steed met his untimely end right here.

I can tell you my story, now that I remember it. You know me as Rattletrap, but I was once a man. And Bertron Steed was my name.

When I first settled this place, I found something in the bedrock below the land my smithy still stands on — a crystal shard of impossible brilliance, a magical treasure I kept hidden away, unable to decipher its secrets.

This construct body you see before you now was my dearest companion; a tireless assistant I forged to help me work the shop. I named him Rattletrap, and our accomplishments were many. That is, until the gore birds and the jurtak came.

Making our final stand here in the field against a band of jurtak hunters, I held that crystal shard aloft in the hopes that its magic would somehow turn the tide. And in the aftermath of a great arcane blast, I discovered that my soul — the soul of Bertron Steed — had been somehow grafted to the fabricated body of my dear friend Rattletrap.

I believe the sheer impossibility of that moment is what led me to forget who I really was. Who I really am.

Bertron looks over to his skeletal remains with a distinct air of remorse.

I suppose it isn't easy to admit our own mortality, even if we manage to escape it.

He looks to you once more.

So, that's the story of The Rickety Man of Steed's Point. And I must admit, I'm glad to have heard it myself.

Aura Attunement: Rattletrap's Tale

If the party manages to successfully record Rattletrap's Tale in Amalthea's Manuscript, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 bookTalesSteedsPointTale]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once Rattletrap's tale has been written into the Stonecraft Manuscript, the characters can hear the soft music of Amalthea's driftwood wind chimes stirring on the breeze.

Next Steps

If the party has other stories to collect for the Stonecraft Manuscript, they will need to do so next.

Once all four stories have been gathered and transcribed into Amalthea's enchanted book, the narrative events of @UUID[.h3qAMVVRjXYZrEP3]{The Manuscript Awakens} will occur.
The Rickety Man.soverview: The party journeys to a ruined village known as Steed's Point, where a unique Woven Construct known as Rattletrap is rumored to possess an uncommon sentience. Once they arrive, the characters find Steed's Point overrun by swarms of gore birds and jurtak raiders, which must be routed or avoided if the party is to gain the Rickety Man's favor by fetching a long-lost heirloom at the far-end of the village.
The Rickety Man.sexposition: A humanoid silhouette ambles through the overgrown field that marks the southwest perimeter of Steed's Point; a curious sight to behold, considering the village's abandoned nature. This gaunt humanoid figure swings a rusty scythe overhead, which adds a methodic thrashing sound to the bed of noise here — a chorus of ramshackle eaves flapping in the wind, dominated by a squawking cacophony of gore birds perched further to the north.
The Rickety Man.ssummary: After fetching a special heirloom to learn Rattletrap's origin story, we transcribed the tale of the Rickety Man of Steed's Point in the Stonecraft Manuscript.

A Song for Lady Stonecraft.name: A Song for Lady Stonecraft
A Song for Lady Stonecraft.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event introduces the party to the legend of the famed Arcturian storyteller @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft}, and serves as an adventure hook for the Book of Tales. In this event, the characters can:

  • Encounter a roving band of bohemian vagabonds known as the Grass Road Revelers, whose resident bard sings a most peculiar song.

  • Listen to the bard Oona Tilelle's ballad about the storyteller Amalthea Stonecraft and the enchanted nature of her tales.

  • Chat with Oona and her companions to gain more information about Amalthea Stonecraft and her home town, the riverside trade hub known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fBPE6UWg6EOO2WFH]{Nain}.

The Bohemian Camp

This small encampment of bohemian vagabonds is rather inviting to the party if the characters approach with a friendly disposition themselves. Calling themselves the Grass Road Revelers, they're comprised of a motley but charming crew of foreign travelers and Ordani expatriates.

The young raconteur Oona Tilelle (CG, Waerd Human, she/they) serves as the troupe's de facto leader, thanks to her relentless charisma and far-traveled sensibilities. As the characters approach, read the following aloud:

As you make your way into the camp, the woman tuning the kithara looks up and greets you with a curious and welcoming smile. Her light gray eyes suggest a Lowlands heritage, a detail all but confirmed by the Wyrdic stitching and trinkets that decorate her loosely-fitted garb. She strums a chord and begins singing an enchanting song…

The tales of Lady Stonecraft, believe them if you may,
believe them if you care to find your own along the way.
Believe them if you feel a certain stirring in your heart.
Believe them 'cause the Lady is a master of her art.

The tales of Lady Stonecraft are said to ring with truth,
From wedding bells to coffin smells and recklessness of youth.
From waking dreams and wanderlust of childhood fantasy,
to Ember shards to broken hearts and all that's in between.

We're on the road to Nain again to hear the Lady tell!
We're on the road to Nain my friend, so join us for a spell.

The rest of the troupe joins in for a second round of the chorus, which they conclude with a triumphant cheer. A wry grin crosses the bard's mouth before she speaks.

They've been practicing that bit for weeks. My name is Oona Tilelle, these are the Grass Road Revelers, and we appreciate your patronage.

With a wink, the young raconteur motions to an open kithara case at her feet, where a few loose copper and silver coins are scattered for inspiration.

Some of the characters may already be familiar with the legends of Amalthea Stonecraft, who is famed throughout the Arctus Plateau for her epic and affecting stories.

The Bard's Tale

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 14]] check is somewhat familiar with Lady @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft}, the famous storyteller of Nain. She is known to be a wise Aster decorated with the feathers of a bird, and her stories are said to inspire thousands the world over.

  • Result of 17+: The character is well-read when it comes to Amalthea Stonecraft's fantastic tales, or has been exposed to several via oral storytelling. Indeed, they likely have a favorite story from her vast body of work that occasionally comes to mind.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arc 15]] check can readily confirm that there is nothing magical about Oona's song, but can also reasonably speculate that Amalthea Stonecraft is capable of arcane spellcasting in her own right (if the legends about her stories are true).

The Grass Road Revelers have provisions for trade and warm company for those who wish to keep it.

Friendly Conversation

If one or more party members agree to tell the raconteurs a brief tale of their own, Oona and the rest of her troupe have the following information to share:

  • The brief history of the "Grass Road Revelers" and how they came to be the adventuring troupe they are. The first three met each other one night about five weeks ago in a tavern in Casla Brava, and they haven't looked back ever since. A hopeful but aimless group of raconteurs, the six of them roam the Arctus Plateau in search of stories, songs, and experiences to add to their collection.

  • The Revelers are slowly making their way to visit Amalthea Stonecraft, the legendary storyteller from Nain — a wordsmith whose stories are said to be so powerful, they change the lives of those who read and hear them.

  • If the party was unaware, Nain is built upon the banks of an enchanted river and serves as an important trade hub for the Arctus Plateau.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill ins 13]] check is self-assured that Oona's account of Lady Stonecraft is one that she earnestly believes in. It feels as though she has very little reason to mislead the party about her enthusiasm for the famed Amalthea Stonecraft and her celebrated storytelling acumen. [[/culture emberArcturian]] characters have advantage on this check.

Region Map: Nain

If the party hasn't discovered @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fBPE6UWg6EOO2WFH]{Nain}, it becomes visible on the Arctus Plateau Region Map as soon as they learn about the settlement from Oona. Check the box for the "Nain Discovered" outcome at the top of the page.

Who are you?

Me? I'm just a kithara player from Casla Brava with a few songs to sing. Long story short, I left my rather war-torn family behind to myself find a new one.

She gestures toward her companions.

And these mad lads will certainly do. The first three of us met each other one night about five weeks ago over several flagons of ale, and we haven't looked back since. Now, we simply wander the Plateau in search of stories and songs and friendly hearts.

About Amalthea?

My whole life I've been told that the world has never known a greater storyteller than Amalthea Stonecraft. And with each new story I hear, I tend to agree. Her stories are said to be so powerful, they actually change the lives of those who hear and read them. But, like most things in life, you have to see it to believe it — so we're headed to Nain to visit Lady Stonecraft and find out for ourselves.

About Nain?

They say the waters are never calm in Nain, which is built on the enchanted shores of the Eastern River at the edge of a gorgeous waterfall. The bustling trade hub is even said to be adorned with talking statues that orate Amalthea Stonecraft's stories to passers by on the street. A sight to see, if ever there was one.

A favorite tale?

When I was six years old, my dear old nan read me a book I've treasured ever since: "The Fourteen Fables of Fortigard." There isn't a day that goes by where I don't remember one of those silly fables. And they always seem to come to mind at the right time. Isn't it funny how childhood stories can stick with you for so long?

Concluding the Event
