The Grass Road Revelers are happy to host the party for a day and an evening, after which time they pack up camp and set off on their own — towards Nain, of course, but with a few unknown stops along the way. They politely refuse any offers from the party to join up for travel, citing their need to tie up loose ends before reaching the storyteller's hometown themselves.

Next Steps

With Nain newly indicated for the players on the Arctus Plateau Region Map, they must decide whether or not to investigate the veracity of Oona Tilelle's song by visiting the famed riverside town themselves. If the characters have yet to hear of Nain, this may strike them as an interesting reason to visit the peculiar cliffside settlement.
A Song for Lady Stonecraft.soverview: The party encounters a roving band of vagabonds while traveling the Arcturian wilderness. A young bard in the group sings the song of a storyteller named Amalthea Stonecraft, whose collections of tall tales have a way of changing the lives of those who read them.
A Song for Lady Stonecraft.sexposition:
Sounds of revelry meet your ears as you take notice of a small camp on the road ahead. Drawing closer, you regard a group of two tented wagons and a half-dozen troubadours whose weather-worn bohemian clothing and travel gear betray them as vagabonds.

Two of these gregarious travelers prepare onion stew over an open fire, while another duo trades playing cards in a friendly game of chance. Meanwhile, an older fellow quietly reads a dog-eared book in the shade. And a striking young woman with a tangled mane of curly hair tunes the six strings of her kithara as she prepares to pluck a tune.
A Song for Lady Stonecraft.ssummary: We encountered a roving band of bohemian vagabonds who called themselves the Grass Road Revelers. A bard among them named Oona Tilelle sang us a whimsical ballad about a legendary storyteller from Nain named Amalthea Stonecraft, whose tales are rumored to be enchanted.

The Storyteller of Nain.name: The Storyteller of Nain
The Storyteller of Nain.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event allows the party to meet the famed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ZLHE7Cv3tPV1Spik]{Aster} storyteller @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft}, who will set them off on a quest of mythic proportions. In this event, the characters can:

  • Learn more about Amalthea from one of many enchanted storytelling statues that are installed throughout her hometown of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fBPE6UWg6EOO2WFH]{Nain}.

  • Visit Amalthea's home, where they will meet the renowned storyteller and learn about her forthcoming manuscript, her history as a fabulist, and a her life as an Aster.

  • Take on a quest from Amalthea to track down four different Arcturian citizens and transcribe their personal stories in the manuscript.

Nain's Orating Statues

While traversing the streets of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.fBPE6UWg6EOO2WFH]{Nain}, the party discovers one or more enchanted storytelling statues featuring the likeness of a local legend — @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft}, the region's foremost author on folklore and myth.

The statue proceeds to orate a most fantastic tale for you, involving the whimsical story of a local pauper — a helpless romantic — who found a curious bottle while fishing one day. After uncorking this wayside cruet, it seems the fisherman was magically pulled inside, and found himself living blissfully on the beaches of a miniature island. They say he lives there still, awaiting the fateful day when his one true love will find the same bottle washed upon her own lonely shore. The statue concludes by addressing you directly once more…

So be careful with precisely whose bottles you open, my friend, and remember this lovelorn tale as you float amidst life's tumultuous seas.

And with that, the statue returns to resolute stillness.

After they listen to the statue's tale, the party can inspect the stone effigy for additional information.

Investigating the Statue

Any character who inspects the statue will notice an inscription etched in Common at the base of the pedestal it sits upon:

The Stonecraft Estate calls, if you have stories to share.

A [[/check perception 15 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] check allows a character to notice that there are words actually inscribed in the stone book held by the statue:

Find your fate in the stories of Lady Stonecraft.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill his 14]] check is somewhat familiar with Lady @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]{Amalthea Stonecraft}, the famous storyteller of Nain depicted by the statue. She is known to be a wise Aster decorated with the feathers of a bird, and her stories are said to inspire thousands the world over.

  • Result of 17+: The character is well-read when it comes to Amalthea Stonecraft's fantastic tales, or has been exposed to several via oral storytelling. Indeed, they likely have a favorite story from her vast body of work that occasionally comes to mind.

A successful [[/skill arc 15]] check is required for a character to accurately speculate the traditions of magic associated with the statue's enchantment, and can reasonably speculate that Amalthea Stonecraft is capable of arcane spellcasting in her own right (if the legends about her stories are true).

After relating a brief tale, the magical statue issues another proclamation: intrepid adventurers are encouraged to visit Amalthea's estate to meet with the author herself.

Once they've finished examining the statue, the party can choose whether or not to track down the so-called Stonecraft Estate where the famed storyteller of Nain resides among a library of her works.

Locating the Stonecraft Estate

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill inv 13]] check or a [[/skill per 13]] check is able to track down the address of or directions to the Stonecraft Estate, an aged two-story house near the center of town cluttered with countless books and historical records.

If any of the characters has an explicit history with Nain (as mentioned in a written backstory or conversation with the GM), they already know where the Stonecraft Estate is located, and can direct the party towards Amalthea's book-strewn residence themselves.

The Stonecraft Estate

If the party follows up on the statue's solicitation, they may encounter Amalthea at home and take up her quest.

Once the characters reach the Stonecraft Estate, read the following aloud:

An impressive two-story house of historical Arcturian design is nestled here at the end of a cul-de-sac in the middle of town. A handsome bronze placard mounted on the outer wall labels this sagging edifice as Stonecraft Estate.

Past the wall's rusty gate, you can see piles of books through the home's dust-clouded windows, and weeds crowd the overgrown flower bushes that decorate the front lawn boxes. Driftwood wind chimes sing their inviting songs from the estate's front porch, and a lantern at the front steps shines a warm, welcoming light upon the yard.

As you regard the unmistakable charm of this place, the front door swings open by itself, as if it were calling you to enter.

If the characters decide to enter:

Lit by candle and lamplight, the front room of the Stonecraft Estate is an amalgam of library and museum, rather than what many would consider to be a proper foyer. Various maps, trinkets, and contraptions are surrounded by countless books, diagrams, and scrolls. The place smells of apple cider, and you could spend forever here.

A moment later, the lady of the house appears:

@Embed[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3]

This must be Lady Stonecraft, the legendary storyteller of Nain. She addresses you with the sincere familiarity of an elderly auntie.

Welcome home, my young friends. I've been waiting for you for quite some time. And here you are! My name is Amalthea Stonecraft, and I invite you to consider a friendly solicitation… a job, if you will. With payment, of course, should it please you. But please, make yourselves comfortable.

As you settle in and begin to consider her words, Amalthea continues.

The time has come for my latest manuscript, the Book of Tales, featuring a collection of local legends — narratives as unique as the Arcturians who were born to tell them. And I need your help collecting these legendary tales.

Like divinations themselves, my reputation as an oracle often proceeds me. I need to hear these stories told by someone who doesn't know what to expect. And as you can see, I have quite a few years behind me; I need a group of able raconteurs to travel a bit faster and a bit farther than these old bones might allow. Truth be told, I require fresh perspectives and fleet travelers to bring this new manuscript to life.

But first, tell me a tale about yourselves! I have my suspicions you'll make a fine group of storytellers.

The Storyteller's Quest

Following a round of introductions and pleasantries, Amalthea petitions the party to visit four citizens of the Golden Flats to transcribe their tales for her latest book of Arcturian folklore. Each of these citizens harbors a story they have yet to tell, and the characters must coax these stories out of each of them. The proposed stories include:

  • @UUID[.hJn9ofVtP4DxSTLe]{The Rickety Man} of Steed's Point. Journey to @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr]{Steed's Point}, where a sentient construct made of wood and vine named @UUID[Actor.wI4zsTgX2eIy4VtQ]{Rattletrap} keeps watch over a doomed village. Ask him how he came to be.

  • @UUID[.CfrTzEDg60aXGsRo]{The Boy Who Collected Boats}. Head to the Hargrove Farmstead north of Nain, where a young boy named Eb Hargrove has mysteriously disappeared from his front yard. Find the boy and learn his tale of lost and found.

  • @UUID[.QwGONBUR04vwnj8k]{The Signborn's Secret}. Travel to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.cHJSlRXSX9wvV7br]{Vortest Tower}, where a Signborn mage named @UUID[Actor.4RXpGeP2FzdAxzw0]{Corvana Vortest} navigates a clandestine situation. Learn the secrets of her solitude.

  • @UUID[.uJnjxdP2OBD4pSKa]{The Crystal Quarryman}. Visit the Kiska quarryman @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask} in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel}, who is rumored to be undergoing a most strange transformation — one that is turning him to solid crystal. Find out how his perilous situation came to be.

As a reward for the party's efforts, Amalthea offers up a choice of one of the following uncommon magic items and promises to immortalize the characters in one of her tales: a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.44XNWmMGnwXn7bNW]{Pearl of Power} or a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.2veAOEyfbDJuxR8Y]{Ring of Warmth}.

A [[/check insight 15 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill insight 13]] check allows a character to confirm the veracity of Amalthea's intentions.

Amalthea is willing to offer up information and her perspective on a variety of subjects that she deems appropriate, including:

  • The precise location of each of the stories they must gather (indicated on the Arctus Plateau Region Map).

  • General details about Nain and its surrounding environs.

  • A brief history of her time as a professional storyteller, and her various accomplishments throughout the years.

  • Specific and general advice for the party in a mentorship capacity.

More About Amalthea:

In my youth, I'd wander the Plateau gathering myths and fables from Casla Brava to Caste, speaking to any outlander I could spend a free moment with. And if I couldn't journey far enough to find the adventure I was looking for, fate often brought it to my own doorstep in the form of a rare book or a far-off traveler. Everyone has a yarn to spin, my dears, and my life has been spent weaving a most colorful blanket.

About Aster:

I see you've noticed my plumage. These violet and indigo feathers of mine are a resplendent gift from the Heart of Ember. As you can imagine, life as an Aster can bring with it many unexpected wonders and revelations; and I'd wager you or someone you know has been touched by the grace of Ember themselves.

Why Not Gather Them Yourself?

As you can see, I have more years behind me than ahead. And these old bones aren't as spry as they once were. Fate simply whispered your names in my ear, and then you came. I'd be a fool to not seek your timely assistance and nurture the fabulist within each of you. After all, who will tell these tales when I'm gone?

Where Should We Begin?

Go where your hearts lead you. You're the storytellers now. Make them your own. But I can certainly set you on the path of whatever tale you fancy most.

Tell Us Another Tale:

Have you ever heard the story of the Wintermaned Huntsman and the Hearthfire Grove? Long ago, there lived a Wirrun Huntsman whose deft arrow could pierce the center of a copper piece from six-hundred feet. No quarry could outpace him, and no prey could escape.

One day, this Wintermaned warrior spied the most intriguing game he'd ever seen on the hunt, an elegant four-horned stag with a brilliant coat of crimson fur. The Huntsman followed the stag for many a mile, until the beast retreated into a curious grove of burning trees. But rather than relent in the face of mortal peril, the Wintermaned Huntsman betrayed his own body to keep up the chase. They say he hunts that stag among smoke and cinders to this very day, immolated but alive, and that the grove can only be seen when desperation runs high on a moonlit night.

It seems the price we pay to serve our passions can be rather steep.

Accepting the Call

If the party agrees to take up Amalthea's quest, she presents them with a @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3.Item.jdxSEP3RliniOZrY]{Pouch} containing an @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3.Item.yczOxQz060CRoXty]{Ink Pen}, 2 @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3.Item.zntVQCZMcRDYenyH]{Ink Bottles}, and a blank leather-bound tome full of blank pages: the @UUID[Item.p5m9fgcCoUVlThf7]{Stonecraft Manuscript}.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill arc 16]] check are able to discern something vaguely magical about the manuscript, but the properties are abstruse and obscure.

  • Any character who casts the @UUID[Actor.MJfOzwa6uawHDhHA.Item.iCaiYRPxSxowvFJa]{Detect Magic} spell to inspect the manuscript is able to detect the telltale auras of Enchantment and Divination magics on the tome. Unfortunately, the @UUIDCompendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} spell can't offer any additional insight or information about the manuscript's inscrutable arcane nature.

Concluding the Event

Amalthea will entertain the party as long as the characters have questions to ask or time to listen to her tales, but she presses a small amount of urgency upon the players if they linger for very long.

Next Steps

The four points of interest for the locations associated with each of the four tales are indicated on the Arctus Plateau Region Map. The characters are free to choose which of the four stories to explore first, and so on.

No matter what order the party pursues the stories in, the clue that leads to the finale featured in @UUID[.7WywAnBMYYu13Ay5]{The Moon Child of Lake Jinro} is presented after completion of the fourth story.
The Storyteller of Nain.soverview: The party is hired by the renowned storyteller Amalthea Stonecraft to visit four citizens of the Golden Flats and transcribe their tales for her latest book of Arcturian folklore.
The Storyteller of Nain.sexposition:
While navigating the cobbled streets of Nain, you draw close to a life-sized marble statue of an aged Arcturian woman holding a stone quill to the pages of a stone manuscript. Countless feathers are carved like a mantle upon the statue's lapidarian garments, and the bookish woman's eyes seem to almost twinkle with life as the sculpture begins to move. A friendly femme voice escapes the statue's unfastened mouth.

New to Nain, dear stranger? Then join me for a spell, and hear this story I have to tell!
The Storyteller of Nain.ssummary: We met with the famed Aster storyteller Amalthea Stonecraft in Nain, where she solicited us to take up a quest. Presenting us with a blank manuscript, Amalthea has tasked us to visit four Arcturians and transcribe their own stories in the book.

Down by the River.name: Down by the River
Down by the River.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration event allows the party to rescue young Eb Hargrove and confront the kidnapper Jodessa Cort, who has lured Eb and a handful of other children into a life of indentured servitude. In this event, the characters can:

  • Explore the riverside terrain north of Hargrove Farmstead for signs of the secluded cave referred to in the Parchment Boat Letters — known as Calloway Cove.

  • Confront Jodessa Cort and loosen her hold on the kidnapped Arcturian children of Calloway Cove.

  • Escort a rescued Eb Hargrove back to the Hargrove Farmstead and into the welcoming arms of his worried parents.

The Riverside Cave

If the party follows the clues mentioned in Eb's secret Parchment Boats, they can locate the source of these curious letters: a kidnapper who lairs in a cave north of Nain. Here, at the so-called Calloway Cove, the characters can unravel the plot of the kidnapper Jodessa Cort and convince her to release the runaway children.

The closer you get to the dark hollow you noticed in the eastern rock face, the surer you become that it is indeed the mouth of some small cave. Vines and ivy are draped across this shaded opening, which is only a stone's throw away from the water's edge.

Outside the Cave

This cave mouth is indeed the threshold of the lair of Jodessa Cort, the kidnapper who sent the parchment boats downstream for little Eb Hargrove (and others) to find. An inspection of the area can confirm the party's suspicions. For more information about Jodessa, see "Confronting Jodessa Cort" below.

A [[/check insight 14 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill insight 12]] check allows a character to notice that the concealment provided by the ivy and vines draped across the cave mouth has been enhanced with a net of man-made camouflage netting.

  • Result of 15+: The character can detect the faint sound of animal noises or young voices echoing from within the cave.

  • Result of 18+: The character is also able to notice the slight smell of a campfire or torchlight emanating from within.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill sur 14]] check is able to locate several distinct sets of humanoid footprints leading in and out of the cave to the waterfront. The size of these footprints are diminutive enough to be those of small-sized adult humanoids or younger medium-sized humanoids.

Once the characters journey into the cave, read the following aloud:

A narrow passage behind the unsuspecting cave mouth leads further into the earth, and winds its way steeply downward towards the faint sound of muffled chatter and crackling firelight. As you draw nearer to some large underground cavern, you spy the distinct decoration of a camp or makeshift hideaway. A half-dozen bedrolls are circled around a central fire pit, occupied by several adolescent children — their faces dirty and full of hardship. These kids appear to be sorting through a variety of stolen goods as they inspect a purloined stack of purses, satchels, and rucksacks.

A thirty-something Arcturian woman stands above these youths, gesticulating in protest and admonishing the children with a stern reprimand. Clad in a tight gray jerkin and a collection of colorful scarves, sashes, and bands, this overseer bears a distinctly roguish affectation. Her words are as harsh and biting as the rocky stalactites that decorate this musty cavern.

I told you to stick together, didn't I? I told you to avoid strangers, didn't I? Then why have you been talking to strangers, my loves!? Do you seek to destroy the sanctity of this place we call home? Where your hateful parents can never hurt you? The Cove is our sanctuary. You are safe here. You are wanted here. The outside world doesn't want you or love you. You know this. Who really loves you?

There is a brief moment of uncomfortable silence before a few children mutter in reluctant response:

Jodessa loves us.

The woman grows angry.

I can't hearrr you! Who loves you!?

The children reply, adamant with faux enthusiasm.

Jodessa loves us!

Satisfied, the woman responds with an air of dismissal.

That's right, my loves. Jodessa is the only one who cares about you …

Inside the Cave

The party arrives just in time to hear Jodessa Cort (NE, Arcturian Human, she/her) address 4 Adolescent Thieves and eight-year-old Eb Hargrove (CG, Arcturian Human, he/him). Jodessa is a cruel but charismatic leader of this gang of misfits and runaways; a would-be footsoldier of the Otherhood, she is athletic and formidably competent — but quite obviously outmatched by the party and their resources.

The characters can sneak to avoid detection by Jodessa if they decide to venture into the cave. If they manage to catch the kidnapper by surprise, the party will gain an upper hand for their negotiations.

  • Each character must make a [[/skill stealth 15]] check if they attempt to sneak. If half or more of the party members succeed on this check, the overall attempt to sneak up on Jodessa's camp is successful.

A [[/check insight 15 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill insight 13]] check allows a character to notice one particular child among the adolescents: a boy with tawny hair and silver eyes wearing a red tunic. This, of course, is Eb Hargrove.

If the party succeeds on their group Stealth check to surprise Jodessa, read the following:

You stealthily make your way closer and closer to the makeshift camp at the bottom of the cave. By the time the adolescent thieves turn their eyes to greet you, it's too late for the woman to notice you for herself. This roguish Arcturian gang leader spins around with a look of utter surprise on her panicked face.

If the party fails their group Stealth check, read the following:

The woman pauses for a moment and raises her right hand. With a snap of her fingers, this roguish Arcturian gang leader sends the children scurrying for weapons and cover in various nooks and crannies around the camp. She raises her voice in mockery before turning slowly to greet you.

Well, well, well. It looks like we have company, my loves! These awful people mean to hurt you or take you away.

A snide grin crosses the woman's face as she draws a wicked short sword from its sheathe and addresses you directly.

You wouldn't want to hurt the children, would you?

Confronting Jodessa Cort

Jodessa has been grooming the Cove's coterie of adolescent thieves, and the parchment boats are simply one of her odious recruitment methods.

If the party wishes to save Eb Hargrove and the other children from Jodessa's devious influence, they must succeed on a Skill Challenge wherein characters must succeed on their choice 3 or more of the 6 skill checks listed below. Characters have advantage on these checks if the party managed to avoid detection and surprise Jodessa (see "Inside the Cave" above).

[[/check athletics 15]] The character is able to effectively flex their physical superiority over Jodessa, and she begins to question the prospects of her victory.

[[/check deception 14]] In one way or another, the character is able to convince Jodessa that harboring the adolescents will result in her demise. Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge politics]] have advantage on this check.

[[/check intimidation 14]] The character is able to bully or dishearten Jodessa enough for her to question the likelihood of her survival. Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] have advantage on this check.

[[/check medicine 13]] The character is able to identify a small outbreak of a common caravan sickness known as the Red Cough among two of the Adolescent Thieves, which adds an element of anxiety to Jodessa's temperament. Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] or [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on this check.

[[/check persuasion 14]] In one way or another, the character is able to convince Jodessa that giving up this kidnapping scheme is more profitable than maintaining it. Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on this check.

[[/check slt 15]] The character is able to reposition themself to a more tactically advantageous spot in the cave, which undermines Jodessa's standard security methods. Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]] have advantage on this check.

Once the characters have succeeded on 3 of these skill checks, Jodessa will drop to her knees and lay down her arms as she surrenders to the party. A mere thug in service to the crime syndicates of Nain and Seawall, she's willing to offer a small amount of information in exchange for her prompt freedom.

If the characters fail, Eb Hargrove himself will join the attempt to confront Jodessa — adding 1 or more successes as needed by the Gamemaster.

Ragen Attunement: Jodessa Bullied

Each character who uses their skills of Athletics or Intimidation to force Jodessa Cort's surrender advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 bookTalesRiverBullied]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Jodessa Deceived

Each character who uses their skills of Deception or Sleight-of-Hand to force Jodessa Cort's surrender advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 bookTalesRiverDeceived]] at the conclusion of the event.

Cora Attunement: Jodessa Convinced

Each character who uses their skills of Persuasion or Medicine to force Jodessa Cort's surrender advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 bookTalesRiverConvinced]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Kidnapper Surrenders

When Jodessa Cort finally submits to the party's confrontation, she drops to her knees and offers a confession, along with a limited amount of information about her criminal operation here in Calloway Cove.

Jodessa's Confession:

Wait, wait! I surrender! Please … Whatever you think of me, it took a lot of hard times in low places to wind up where I am today. I'm not proud of who I am sometimes, but I manage to survive. And I gave these kids some leadership when they needed it most. So please. Let me live another day.

You can take the kids, send 'em home, whatever; I'll just crawl back to the rock I was hiding under and we can forget this ever happened. You obviously have everything under control.

About Jodessa's Operation:

If I tell you anything about who I usually work with, they'll kill us both. But I can tell you're not going to take "no" for an answer, so I'll just let you know that Nain and Seawall have plenty of fences for people with hot merchandise and scarcely any scruples.

Working out of this cave seemed like a great way to avoid the hustle and bustle while still making ends meet. Once or twice a week, we'd head down to Nain and liberate a few purses from their owners. It worked so far; but I'm done.

Regarding The Adolescent Thieves:

These dumb runts were just looking for a place to belong. I can relate. It's a cruel world for all of us born between a rock and a hard place, you know? They didn't know any better. But maybe they learned a thing or two about living while they were here.

If I had someone like me when I was their age, somebody to look up to and learn from, I could have been somebody special. I was good to these kids. Mark my words.

Rescuing Eb and the Others

Once the party has successfully subdued Jodessa via the Skill Challenge in Confronting Jodessa Cort, they can liberate the gang of 4 Adolescent Thieves from their misguided servitude.

Furthermore, the party can influence the gang's decision regarding their next steps: the Adolescent Thieves can either stay here in Calloway Cove, or they can disperse and return to their various settlements or homesteads of origin.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check dec 13]] check or a [[/check per 13]] check can sway the gang's collective decision one way or the other.

Eb Hargrove joins the party no matter what, and is eager to return to the Hargrove Farmstead and into the waiting arms of his parents. The characters must escort him safely home in order to transcribe his tale for the Stonecraft Manuscript.

Looting the Hideout

If the characters decide to loot the hideout after defeating Jodessa, they can search tent that served as the gang leader's private quarters. A locked footlocker inside ([[/check dex 13]] check to open) contains [[/award 25gp]], a bottle of @UUID[Item.jnKYsmCYNNP21aYF]{Seawall Brandy}, and a random @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinket}.

Additionally, any character who decides to search the stolen goods the Adolescent Thieves were sorting when the party arrived can roll [[/roll 1d2]] + 1 times on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot (Arctus Plateau)} table and [[/roll 1d2]] times on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} table to determine what they find, along with 2 @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3.Item.eLDl92MlNqpgYL2M]{Backpacks} and [[/award 3d8sp]] in a soft leather @UUID[Actor.VBHt7Uwke7GZ1OV3.Item.jdxSEP3RliniOZrY]{Pouch}.

Orbis Attunement: Runaways United

If the party manages to convince the runaways to stay united, each character advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 bookTalesRiverUnited]] at the conclusion of the event.

Akon Attunement: Runaways Disbanded

If the party manages to convince the runaways to disband, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 bookTalesRiverDisbanded]] at the conclusion of the event.

Eb Hargrove's Tale

After the characters safely escort Eb Hargrove home, he’s able to relate the full tale of his recruitment by Jodessa Cort and a first-person account of his liberation at the hands of the party. As Eb relates his story, one of the characters must transcribe the tale in the Stonecraft Manuscript (if not recall it from memory later).

Before you even reach the Hargrove Farmstead's sprawling front yard, you notice Gabi and Brandt Hargrove rushing out the front door to greet you. Eb breaks into a run and closes the distance, before Gabi reaches down and grabs the boy in a longing embrace, tears of joy streaming down her rosy cheeks.

As you join the family, young Eb is already spinning a yarn for his folks about what really happened out there in Calloway Cove …

I'm sorry for leaving without saying goodbye, mama. Really, I am. I didn't mean to make you cry. I just had to find out if the story on the boats was true. This girl named Jo said there was a city of kids who needed friends like me, and promised us that we'd live forever, but it was all a bunch of lies. She was just a nasty liar. And she made us lie for her, and steal for her, and do all sorts of nasty things. Am I a bad person, mama?

The Hargrove boy bursts into tears of guilt as his mother comforts him.

No, baby. You're not a bad person. You simply got taken advantage of by someone who knew better. But you promise me right now Ebdan Hargrove. Promise me you'll never leave my side again without first saying goodbye.

Eb looks up with determination.

I promise, mama. Dada. I won't let you down. But I have to tell you about the other kids I met! I don't think they were bad people either.

The boy continues his tale as his family looks on with newfound contentment and renewed appreciation for the simple life.

Concluding the Event

Once Eb Hargrove's tale has been written into the Stonecraft Manuscript, the characters can hear the soft music of Amalthea's driftwood wind chimes stirring on the breeze.

Next Steps

If the party has other stories to collect for the Stonecraft Manuscript, they will need to do so next.

Once all four stories have been gathered and transcribed into Amalthea's enchanted book, the narrative events of @UUID[.h3qAMVVRjXYZrEP3]{The Manuscript Awakens} will occur.
Down by the River.soverview: In search of young Eb Hargrove, the party ventures north of the Hargrove Farmstead in the hopes of finding the elusive "Calloway Cove" mentioned in Eb's parchment boat letters. Once they find the riverside cavern, the characters must confront the kidnapper Jodessa Cort if they plan to free Eb Hargrove and a gang of other runaways.
Down by the River.sexposition: After an exhaustive search of the area, you spy a dark hollow in the rocky outcroppings that line the eastern bank of the river. From here, it looks like little more than a fissure or animal den, but a closer investigation should confirm whether or not this is the so-called "Calloway Cove" mentioned in the letter you found.
Down by the River.ssummary: We journeyed north of the Hargrove Farmstead in search of young Eb Hargrove, where we eventually found a riverside cave that served as the headquarters of Jodessa Cort — a kidnapping cutpurse who held Eb and several other runaways under the sway of her malicious influence. Thankfully, our fateful encounter with Jodessa led to the safe release of Eb and the other children.

The Turn of a Friendly Page.name: The Turn of a Friendly Page
The Turn of a Friendly Page.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration event requires the party to help Amalthea Stonecraft remember who she was prior to her reincarnation in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000.JournalEntryPage.7WywAnBMYYu13Ay5]{The Moon Child of Lake Jinro}, and serves as the finale for The Book of Tales. In this event, the characters can:

  • Search the confines of the Stonecraft estate for three or more keepsake items that will help young Amalthea recollect her memories.

  • Listen to Amalthea's final contribution to The Book of Tales: the story of her reincarnation as the Moon Child of Lake Jinro.

Amalthea's Homecoming

Whether or not the characters escort young Amalthea home from Lake Jinro, the Book of Tales only concludes once the party returns to Nain and visits the Stonecraft estate. There, they must explore the contents of the house in search of three or more keepsakes that will help jog Amalthea's hazy memory.

Skill Challenge: Locating Amalthea's Keepsakes

The lifetimes of information that Amalthea once knew will slowly return to her; but before they do, the party must help the Moon Child discover a few of her most treasured possessions — keepsake items that serve as psychic anchors to the many existences she has previously known.

The party must succeed on at least 3 of the following skill checks as a part of this Skill Challenge. As the characters present each keepsake item to Amalthea, her eyes alight with greater recognition, and she has a pointed anecdote or reaction to share.

[[/check arc 13]] The character is drawn to a wondrous item on a cluttered and unassuming bookshelf, a Wooden Mask that Amalthea once used as an arcane focus during her earlier days as a bard. The face of this lightly-enchanted mask can alter slightly according to the wearer's mood or performance.

  • [[/culture emberOaken]] characters and Bards have advantage on this check.

[[/check his 13]] The character recognizes the title of one of Amalthea's earliest works, a collection of epic Arcturian poems titled "Songs of the Windswept Reach."

  • [[/culture emberArcturian]] characters have advantage on this check.

[[/check inv 13]] The character discovers evidence of which pigments Amalthea favored among her collection of inks, which can be corroborated in the handwriting of several of her most recent tomes and manuscripts.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] or [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on this check.

[[/check prc 13]] The character spots a pair of Signaran reading spectacles that Amalthea has used over various centuries, particularly during her elderly years.

  • [[/culture emberRailen]] characters have advantage on this check.

[[/check per 13]] The character is able to draw forth a clue from Amalthea herself to locate one of her most prized possessions. If persuaded to talk, Amalthea speaks of a stitched-up raggedy doll made in her own likeness, which can be found on a windowsill in her bedroom. This tiny effigy was a keepsake from Amalthea's first generation on Ember, and was gifted to her by a dear friend.

  • [[/culture emberArcturian]] characters have advantage on this check.

[[/check slt 13]] The character is able to amuse young Amalthea with card tricks using a deck of her own oracle cards, which is easily found nearby. The moment of frivolity conjures up countless memories of the joy she's given to other young ones throughout the years.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] and Bards have advantage on this check.

The Moon Child's Tale

Once three keepsake items have been presented to Amalthea, read the following aloud:

A curious wind sweeps through the room, causing flames to flicker and parchment to flutter. The timeless assortment of curiosities that decorate this place seem to nearly come alive as they stir in the breeze and swell with arcane lambency. As this magical gust subsides, a familiar light returns to young Amalthea's eyes, along with the confidence of recognition.

My dear friends. What a road we've travelled together. The generosity of your guidance is immeasurable, but I'll begin by thanking you for helping me find myself amongst the detritus of my cluttered home. Each time I take the journey to Lake Jinro, I must try a bit harder to recollect what came before.

Like all Aster, I was born to Ember with strange and unique blessings. My feathers and bardic talents are only part of my boons, as you've seen with your own eyes. I live to be reborn, every eight decades, and have lived on Ember for several generations. I am not invincible; my body is still a fragile and mortal vessel. But thanks to the power of Ember's moons, the ritual shrine at Lake Jinro, and my own precautions, I have lived to see many tales of the Golden Flats be told — including your own.

A new day dawns, and another page is turned. Along with the stories you've collected, "The Moon Child of Lake Jinro" marks the final story in The Book of Tales. Well done, my dears. Now, care for a cup of tea?

Concluding the Event

And with that, The Book of Tales is complete. Amalthea Stonecraft, newly reacquainted with her history and surroundings, is poised to once again assume her role as the Arctus Plateau's preeminent storyteller.

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

This quest is now concluded, but the party may have further interactions with some of the characters encountered here during other quests:

  • In @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu]{An Old Friend} the players will work with Zodi Trask to further investigate the Luxarum influence in Arcturel.

  • In @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM]{Thorny Predicaments}, the party can explore Rattletrap's relationship with their family more deeply.
The Turn of a Friendly Page.soverview: The party returns to the home of Amalthea Stonecraft in Nain, where they help the Moon Child of Lake Jinro — the reincarnated Amalthea herself — become acquainted with a life she's never known. The characters must search the house with Amalthea to locate her most treasured possessions, which will help her remember precisely who she was prior to her latest rebirth. Once the spark of remembrance ignites Amalthea's memories, she can reward the characters for their help assembling the eponymous Book of Tales.
The Turn of a Friendly Page.sexposition:
The cluttered front room of the Stonecraft estate is markedly quiet and darkened compared to your first visit. The Moon Child of Lake Jinro — young Amalthea Stonecraft herself — steps forward from the shadows and produces an oil lantern, which she lights with flint and steel. She quickly surveys the curio-littered chamber before speaking:

This place seems rather familiar to me. As if it were home. I'm sorry I can't quite remember … Where are we? And who, exactly, am I?

A look of stark curiosity crosses young Amalthea's face as she patiently awaits your elucidation.
The Turn of a Friendly Page.ssummary: We met with Amalthea Stonecraft at her home in Nain, where the reincarnated "Moon Child of Lake Jinro" had to be reacquainted with her memories. After we helped her locate several pieces of personal memorabilia, the wizened mind of the Aster storyteller returned to its full capacity — albeit in a child's body. With any luck, she'll repeat this arcane process eight decades from now, and Amalthea's stories will endure for countless generations to come.

The Manuscript Awakens.name: The Manuscript Awakens
The Manuscript Awakens.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event occurs once the party has collected the four stories assigned by Amalthea Stonecraft and transcribed them in the Stonecraft Manuscript. In this event, the characters can:

  • Witness a story begin to write itself upon the blank pages of the magical Stonecraft Manuscript.

  • Follow the Manuscript's instructions to meet Amalthea on the shores of a mysterious island in the northwest reaches of Lake Jinro, a large body of water located west of Nain.

The Self-Writing Story

Scrutinizing the Manuscript's Tale

A successful [[/skill arc 15]] check allows a character to confirm that the magical display of self-writing that just occurred is intrinsic to the book's enchantments and not the result of some outside force or illusion (aside from Amalthea Stonecraft herself).

Any character who previously noticed the writing inscribed on a statue's stone book during @UUID[.CBSwfaeBVs7j08kd]{The Stonecraft Summons} can recognize the silver handwriting that just appeared in the Manuscript as being the very same.

  • Likewise, a successful [[/check intelligence 14]] check allows a character to recall having seen this same handwriting on various tomes and parchments in Stonecraft Manor when the party first met Amalthea.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check his 14]] check is familiar with Lake Jinro and its location on the Arctus Plateau region map. Otherwise, the party must gather information about the Lake's precise location (see "Finding Lake Jinro" below).

  • Result of 16+: The character has heard of an ancient shrine dedicated to Ember's moons that's said to adorn an island near the northwest corner of the lake.

  • A successful [[/check inv 13]] check following a successful History check allows a character to accurately deduce that the "isolated shores" in the Manuscript most likely refers to one of the two islands located in the lake's northwest reaches.

With this newfound information in hand, the party must now travel to the @UUID[JournalEntry.5sSPjtjFWhTo8dmZ]{Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine} to further their quest.

The Journey to Lake Jinro

Finding Lake Jinro

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check inv 13]] check or a [[/check per 13]] check while interacting with the populace of an Arctus Plateau settlement is able to drum up information about the precise location of Lake Jinro and the two islands that dot its central reaches.

Once the characters have traveled to Lake Jinro and reached the large island within it, read the following:

You notice a familiar amethyst-plumed figure standing on the southeastern beach of this large Lake Jinro island. As you get closer, you're greeted by the warm smile of Amalthea Stonecraft, who seems to be waiting for you on this lonely shore.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party must travel to the @UUID[JournalEntry.5sSPjtjFWhTo8dmZ]{Lake Jinro Lunar Shrine} where they will encounter the events of @UUID[.7WywAnBMYYu13Ay5]{The Moon Child of Lake Jinro}.
The Manuscript Awakens.soverview: Following the party's completion of Amalthea Stonecraft's mission to transcribe four Arcturian tales in her manuscript, the magical book itself begins manifesting a fifth and final task for the characters: meet Amalthea on the shores of an isle upon Lake Jinro with the manuscript in hand.
The Manuscript Awakens.sexposition:
As you place the final punctuation on the fourth story in the Stonecraft Manuscript, you can almost hear the wind chimes from Stonecraft Manor sounding at the edge of your perception. The manuscript drifts away from your hands, hovering before you as luminous silver words begin scribing themselves on the next blank page — as if written by some unseen hand.

This arcane prose is written in the Common tongue, and tells a story of its own.

With all four narratives in hand, Amalthea's newfound companions would be called to a place where inspiration runs deep, where the storyteller herself would be waiting for them. By the isolated shores of Lake Jinro, where a half-forgotten monument to Ember's moons stand ready and waiting to hear Amalthea's recitation… the story of a lifetime.
The Manuscript Awakens.ssummary: We heeded the magical call of the Stonecraft Manuscript to journey to the large island upon Lake Jinro, where Amalthea Stonecraft curiously awaited us on the southeastern shore.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This side quest occurs during Chapter 2 as the party follows clues leading to a foreboding and fog-shrouded section of the subterranean Pathways. There are no prerequisites for this quest although it is likely to be encountered if the party is traveling with Ankarist while undertaking the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100] quest.

Difficulty

The "To Fall and Fall Again" quest is designed for a party of Level 3 characters, although the finale of the quest, @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.LyNcEPtA6HA1XvQZ], may prove difficult for a party that is not yet Level 4.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest quest that awards 2 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the [[/eventState fallAgainShadows]] and [[/eventState fallAgainApex]] Events.

The quest has its origins in the distant past, in the history of the Giants — a chronicle that takes place over a vast duration of time, dating all the way back to the earliest days of the Age of Beasts. The first primeval Giants encountered the malevolent influence of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.06I8t0GPggrMVnGV]{the Abyss} long ago (ultimately leading to their downfall), and the survivors fled their Pathways homes to settle in the Giants Mountains that span the continent of Aterica. These people began to change, establishing a culture significantly different from their origins, and would eventually become known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}.

Unfortunately for the Shent, the Abyss and its rapacious denizens never forgot (or forgave) their cosmological meddling. When the @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.51sxCdwRrdffEBgK]{Abyssal Shear} that followed @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{the Shattering} ripped apart the Weave two and half thousand years ago, the Shent were ruthlessly targeted above all other mortals to be destroyed by servants of the Outer Gods and their Abyssal magic. However, the Shent — as seers and prophets of great power — had foreseen their own demise, and had taken numerous steps to safeguard their knowledge in an effort to protect the world. One of the Shent, a Giant named @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth}, built a machine that he imbued with his own mind and memories. And while Mioroth died along with his people, his resolve and ability to protect the world against the Abyss endured.

There are many routes that may bring the party into the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.jgf4ySVqus9CYidy]{ Fogbound Caverns} within the Pathways, but once there, they encounter not only the influence of the Abyss, but something far older and more terrifying than anything they've encountered before. The true scale of the threat is revealed at the end of the quest, both within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion}, and later, in Ordain, where they have the opportunity to speak with the Elder Goddess @UUID[Actor.xCPKIKhMrVO6iljg]{Spectra} and have their worst fears confirmed.

This quest follows on from some of the story and lore points surrounding the Abyss and continues the story of the character@UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth} laid out in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon}.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth}

  • @UUID[Actor.xCPKIKhMrVO6iljg]{Spectra}

  • @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A]{Nadin}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.dapPg66vgvLnwgcp]{Vhismara}

  • @UUID[Actor.bEMPCjG9mFc1d93U]{Issa Sunsword}

  • @UUID[Actor.GuuohJfDx6gifCH5]{Kendral Lowd}

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.IZ1XuA12PN7L7DYE]{Pale Whisperer}

  • @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE]{Abyssal Echo}

  • @UUID[Actor.Q5iudLrTvVX7AeFF]{Gohema}

  • @UUID[Actor.z8lCnghb89oIEWAZ]{Abyssal Eye}

  • @UUID[Actor.gWb5gxg6o3AAYOiM]{Abyssal Eel}

  • @UUID[Actor.pLe1VlhFsHnNqaYL]{Orb of Lantyr}

  • @UUID[Actor.NbrSVEybVKU3MEW5]{Light Energy Turret}

  • @UUID[Actor.d0mSoQozEIKozWVe]{Luxaroth}

  • @UUID[Actor.rtMzEH7llUgEtV9A]{Vhismara's Claw}

Involved Locations

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]{Storsa's Strand}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion}

Overview.soverview:
An ancient attack. A mysterious body. A whisper in the night. Something is changing deep in the Pathways beneath Ember that has begun to affect the lives of those on the surface — and (as luck or fate would have it) this mysterious phenomenon has also attracted the attention of powerful forces locked in an age-old struggle.

In the midst of these larger-than-life events, one family has suffered an unthinkable loss. A child has fallen in the darkness of the Pathways, another to the anguish of trying to find her. Their father now lives a simple life, but even his daily existence is tainted by the effects of the corruption that has begun to make its way up from the deep.

In “To Fall and Fall Again,” the party's journey will lead them into the Pathways deep below the surface of Ember, toward a light in the darkness — facing monsters, temptations, and archaic powers along the way. As the characters explore a network of subterranean ruins that have stood for ages, they can learn some of the secrets of the ancient people who built them, uncover the power that still remains hidden deep within, and confront a corruption as old as time.

Shining Obelisk.name: Shining Obelisk
Shining Obelisk.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration and combat event, the party reaches the top of the Bastion Obelisk, where they find a huge figure standing vigil before a large, glimmering light. The glimmering light, the Orb of Lantyr, is an ancient artifact that repels the Abyss. It is guarded by an ancient being, @UUID[Actor.d0mSoQozEIKozWVe]{Luxaroth}, that has somehow maintained a form through his connection to the orb that hovers above him.

  • Once the party finishes talking with Luxaroth, the stairways begin to swarm with Abyssal Monsters as they relentlessly attack the party, Luxaroth and the Orb itself.

  • The party must repair the Orb of Lantyr while monsters attempt to break through the barrier created by its power. They are likely aided by Luxaroth in this battle.

  • The party may find themselves fighting the Luxaroth instead, depending on their choices and how much Abyssal Attunement they have accumulated.

In this event, the characters can:

  • Gain 1 point of Heart or Abyss Attunement — depending on whether they choose to repair or destroy the Orb of Lantyr (each character).

  • Gain 1 point of Cora or Luxarum Attunement — depending on whether they choose to defeat Luxaroth in combat or befriend him (each character).

Climbing to the Apex

Area Walkthrough

Refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkBasApex]{Bastion Apex} for a complete walkthrough of the area, which takes place on the @UUID[Scene.emberBastionApex]{Bastion Apex} area map. This includes exploration of the area, the main combat encounter, investigation and skill checks, and other details not contained here.

While at the Apex of the Bastion, the party must choose whether to repair the Orb of Lantyr Relic or help destroy it. Depending on the party's decision, this may also mean confronting and defeating @UUID[Actor.d0mSoQozEIKozWVe]{Luxaroth}. Luxaroth may also be defeated independently of the decision to repair the orb.

The Aftermath

Once the party has completed the encounter at the Apex of the Primordial Bastion, a number of different events may occur. While these mostly determine the way that the party leaves the Fogbound Caverns, they can also have repercussions in the future.

[[/outcome RepairedOrbLantyr]]

The Light Restored

If the party repairs the Orb of Lantyr Relic and aids Luxaroth, the Avatar of the First Giants uses his renewed power to magically transport the party to the beginning of the Fogbound Caverns (Hex 3205,2888). This is the shortest route out of the caverns, and the party may not wish to enter the area again. Thankfully, with the Orb of Lantyr shining brightly once more, Abyssal monsters and energies gradually begin to die back and fade over the next several weeks and months. If the party decides to leave the area this way, while it may be the quickest route, they may not learn of the diminishing Abyssal influence for some time.

Heart Attunement: Orb Repaired

If the party manages to successfully repair the Orb of Lantyr, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 fallAgainApexRepaired]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome DestroyedAvatar]]

Luxaroth Gone

With the Avatar seemingly gone, whether destroyed or recovering magically, the party will not be able to count on his aid again and have to make their way back through the Fogbound Caverns on foot.

As the party makes their way back, any character that has [[/knowledge abyssals]] or succeeds on a [[/check nature 14]] check can confirm that the biome and area around them are slowly losing some of the Abyssal energies, and the omnipresent fog and feelings of wrongness are beginning to fade. Likely, this will take some weeks or months.

Cora Attunement: Luxaroth Defeated

If the party defeats Luxaroth in combat, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 fallAgainApexDefeated]] at the conclusion of the event.

Luxarum Attunement: Luxaroth Befriended

If the party chooses to ally themselves with Luxaroth, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 fallAgainApexBefriended]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome BrokenOrbLantyr]]

Overwhelming Darkness

With the Avatar destroyed alongside the Orb of Lantyr Relic, the light is now completely gone in the Fogbound Caverns, and darkness has fallen entirely. The party will not be able to count on the aid of Luxaroth ever again, as he is truly gone, and they must make their way back through the rising danger of the unbound Fogbound Caverns on foot.

As the party makes their way back, any character that has [[/knowledge abyssals]] or succeeds on a [[/check nature 13]] or [[/check arcana 13]] check can confirm that the biome and area around them is becoming even more infused with Abyssal energies. The fog grows thicker, and attacks by monsters in every hex they pass through will also increase. In the long term, the darkness here is likely to spread even onto the surface of the Arctus Plateau.

Abyss Attunement: Orb Destroyed

If the party chooses to help destroy the Orb of Lantyr, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 fallAgainApexDestroyed]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

The quest is effectively over after this event. However, if the party aided Luxaroth, he will have directed them to the "quiet nook" in the shining city above. There, in the event @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.gJZicCkQfXe0XzYN]{Magic Incarnate}, they will meet someone who may shed more light on the events here and assist them further in the coming struggles.

If the party destroyed the orb, they will not have learned anything about the final event or where to find it, and thus will have to encounter @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.gJZicCkQfXe0XzYN]{Magic Incarnate} naturally as they traverse the city of Ordain.
Shining Obelisk.soverview: The party reaches the apex of the colossal ruins of the Primordial Bastion, a structure as old as the world itself, which still stands tall deep beneath the world. Depending on the choices they made and their Abyssal Attunement, they can either aid or are attacked by an ancient giant memory, an ancient hero still protecting the heart of the bastion. They are then confronted by hordes of Abyssal monsters as they attempt to repair an ancient glimmering relic of Lantyr.
Shining Obelisk.sexposition: The immense dark obelisk towers overhead, a glimmering orb of light at its apex. A series of interconnected stairways, crafted from massive stone blocks, wind their way upward at the base of the tower. Despite an overwhelming sense of age, like the rest of the Bastion, the structure remains in pristine condition.
Shining Obelisk.ssummary: We finally reached the top of the immense structure in the Fogbound Caverns and discovered an ancient relic of Lantyr. We also found a manifestation of a primordial Giant guarding it. Abyssal monsters attacked us in waves until we were able to repel them and repair the artifact. This was only a stopgap measure, however, and the artifact only protects this very small area of the Arctus Plateau from the horrors of the Abyss.

Twisting Shadows.name: Twisting Shadows
Twisting Shadows.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event is meant to urge the party towards the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion} and open up this southern section of the Mythspire Tunnels.

The region map opens up automatically upon accepting this event as the area opens up ahead. Additionally, the party can:

  • Investigate the nearby twisted rocks.

  • Investigate the thick ankle-deep fog that is surrounding their feet.

  • Investigate a corpse found within the fog.

Hazards of the Shadows

Almost any action the party takes as they move into this area is going to cause some degree of mental anguish. Prolonged investigation occurs at the party's own detriment.

Fingers of Rock

The rocks are oily, black, and horrifically twisted and blackened as if set alight by some ancient fire. If a party member attempts to investigate the strange twisting black rock around them by touching it, they must succeed on a [[/save wis 14]] save. Should they fail, they must roll upon the Minor Abyssal Madness table below.

Encroaching Fog

The fog gathering between the party members' feet is not immediately dangerous, even to individuals who are not wearing shoes or footwear. If a party member reaches down to touch the fog with their hand of fingers, they must succeed on a [[/save con 12]] save. If they fail, they must roll upon the Minor Abyssal Madness table below.

Roll on the following table to determine which effect grips the player's character.

@Embed[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X inline]

Note: The effects upon the party as they travel towards the Primordial Bastion can be more extreme depending on your taste. This area is supposed to be an anathema to living things of Ember and should be made to feel increasingly bad as they move forward. You can, therefore, refer back to this section of the event and ask players for further checks as they move forward.

Investigating The object

If parties approach the large object they see in front of them, it is immediately clear that it is a body of a young kivahr woman wearing armor.

Investigating the Area

Characters may look around the area with a Search action using either [[/check perception 14]] or [[/check investigation 14]] checks, but curiosity this close to the creeping fog has its dangers. If they fail on the check, roll a [[/gmroll d4]]. On a 1, the character who failed becomes fascinated by the fog around them and has a hard time refocusing on the task at hand. They must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 15]] saving throw or they reach out to touch the fog as if compelled and must roll on the Minor Abyssal Madness table above.

Characters who succeed on the Search action find a small metal box, which is locked. With a [[/check perception 14]] check or [[/check perception 16 passive]], characters can see that the metal is the same as that of the armor the body is wearing. The box can be opened with a key found on the body nearby or with a [[/check sleightofhand 14]] check with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.woWZ1sO5IUVGzo58]{Thieves' Tools}. Inside the box is [[/award 2gp]] in small coins and a journal, @UUID[Item.ZITQWWtflbUSIL9M]{The Final Days of Daelin Lowd}.

A Fallen Corpse

The body is positioned on one of the rocks as if it were sleeping, but there is no movement. Whoever this was is dead. The party can learn the following from the body. Anyone with [[/knowledge forensics]] has advantage on all checks:

  • With a [[/check perception 13]] check, or [[/check perception passive 15]], it is clear that the armor she is wearing was iron, but it has been coated with an odd silver patina, as if the fog itself painted over her body.

  • With a [[/check history 15]] check or [[/knowledge warfare]], characters know that the armor is handcrafted and was likely made somewhere on the Arctus Plateau in and around the Rustvar Valley area.

  • With a [[/check arcana 15]] check, it is clear that the body has been preserved from decay magically for some time, though that magic has now worn off.

  • With a [[/check medicine 15]] check, characters know that the body is positioned as if she was sleeping when she died. Her cause of death is not clear beneath the heavy armor she is wearing.

  • With a [[/check investigation 15]] check, characters can find a @UUID[Item.8L9rrnzA8fLIpCdP]{Lowd Ring of Eternal Rest} on a chain around the neck of the body, tucked into the armor. A small key also hangs on the chain.

The armor on the body is heavy and has almost fused to the body over time, but it can be taken off, gingerly, with a successful [[/check sleightofhand 15]] check. However, on touching the body, character's fingers become coated with fog. Whoever succeeded on the check must also succeed on a [[/save con 14]] saving throw or they take [[/damage 1d6 necrotic]] damage.

After removing the armor, characters can examine the body underneath. It is apparent without a check that the body has taken some damage underneath. Anyone who succeeds on a [[/check medicine 15]] check or has [[/knowledge forensics]] knows that the body died from the effects of a crushing blow. The death likely occurred over time. With the armor removed, characters can spot the @UUID[Item.8L9rrnzA8fLIpCdP]{Lowd Ring of Eternal Rest} and a small key hanging on a chain on the body without a check.

A Final Ring

If characters have seen the @UUID[Item.8L9rrnzA8fLIpCdP]{Lowd Ring of Eternal Rest} on Aberin Lowd's body or in the possession of Kendral Lowd, they can confirm without a check that it is the same ring. With a [[/check arcana 14]] check or an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify} spell, it is clear that this ring has protected the body for a time by casting the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.n4JDcFKe5ikzYmAc]{Gentle Repose}.

Final Words

With a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.I2LUSF5ogc7Bj62e]{Speak with Dead} spell, the corpse can reveal the following information in response to questions:

  • Her name was Daelin Lowd.

  • She was with her family when they were attacked and she was separated from them.

  • She tried to find her way back to the surface but failed. She tried to find her way into the Bastion, which feels like a place of some safety, but could not.

  • She documented what she could of her last days in a journal stored in a metal box nearby.

  • She hopes her family made it back to Storsa's Strand.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

The party may continue moving toward the Primordial Bastion in the distance, proceeding through the newly-opened sections of the map.
Twisting Shadows.soverview:
Within the Pathways the party enters an area that seems to twist and turn. Strange otherworldly effects flash across their vision, and even the rocks themselves are twisted, blackened, and purple.

This is an emanation of the Abyss, and the party must tread this ground extremely carefully. As they enter the area, they must pass checks and fortify thier minds against the maddening effects around them. As they enter the area, however, not only does the biome change, but it opens up the Pathway section, and they can see a colossal structure in the distance.
Twisting Shadows.sexposition:
Nightmarish twisted rocks thrust outwards as you move slowly southwards, becoming denser and increasing in size until they seem to surround you like the gnarled fingers or talons of giant monsters beneath the ground, clawing for escape.

The colossal stalactites hanging from the distant ceiling drip with a viscous, dark liquid, pooling on the ground in small puddles that steam and disappear into a thick ankle-deep fog. The bright glowing mushrooms of the area behind you are now eerie, faint, and deathly pale, casting a ghostly light that barely pierces the suffocating gloom. The air becomes dense and heavy with a chilling silence that hangs like an oppressive shroud, broken only by distant echoes and almost imperceptible whispers. The only respite you can find is a dim light in the sky in the distance, which seems to promise warmth and safety, even as it flickers on and off in the darkness.

Ahead of you, illuminated by the glow of the mushrooms around it, something large and heavy is curled on the ground. It seems out of place, and what light there is in this place glints from something metal in or on it.
Twisting Shadows.ssummary: We entered a deeper, darker section of the Pathways, where the stone itself seemed to react to our presence with a malicious and unsettling intent. A thick fog blanketed the ground here, and faint whispers could be heard in the eerie silence.

Discordant Whispers.name: Discordant Whispers
Discordant Whispers.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event has a low chance of triggering anywhere in the Arctus Plateau after the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon} is completed, with a much higher chance of happening at night.

Each time the event triggers, select a Minor Whisper to be heard either by a specific character or the party as a whole, using the options below, which reflect potential choices made, items acquired, and quest events experienced by the party, each triggering specific whispers.

In some instances, multiple options are given — the choice of whispers is left up to you as the GM.

The specific origin of the whispers is still under development, but will be a powerful force within the world of Ember.

Quest-Related Whispers

These whispers directly relate to quests and quest events that the party has experienced. They should be heard by the party as a whole.

A harsh hiss of a whisper swirls around you like a malevolent breeze, faint but impossible to ignore.

Quest Whisper Triggers

Past events that trigger quest whispers are listed below. If an X is next to the listing, the party did not trigger this outcome. If a checkmark is next to the listing, the party triggered the outcome and can be given the appropriate whisper:

  • [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer mioroth]] in the quest Over the Moon

  • [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer whisperer]] in the quest Over the Moon

  • [[/eventState fallAgainDestruction survives]] in the event Absolute Destruction

  • [[/eventState fallAgainDestruction dies]] in the event Absolute Destruction

  • [[/eventState fallAgainDescent entered]] in the event Savage Descent

  • Experienced the event [[/eventState fallAgainVoidspan]]

The text used by the whispers for each is listed below.

[[/eventState overMoonWhisperer mioroth]] (two options):

  • Mioroth's pets. Do you know the power you could have had? Too late…too late for all of you…

  • You did not want our whispers…and cast your lot with Mioroth…you'll pay for your mistake in blood and bone…

[[/eventState overMoonWhisperer whisperer]] (two options):

  • Power in your blood…glory in your heart.. Be grateful for the gift you have been given…

  • The whispers gather strength…the strength within your veins…go forth and tear the world apart with all your newfound power…

[[/eventState fallAgainDestruction survives]] (two options):

  • Saving Issa Sunsword…how generous…how brave…how delicious when one day soon you stumble on her bones…

  • Issa Sunsword…saved one day…is it worth the price you'll pay?

[[/eventState fallAgainDestruction dies]] (two options):

  • Poor Issa Sunsword…turned to dust…a glimpse into your future…will your screams be nearly as delicious..

  • Issa Sunsword fought for light…but shadows always find you…and now the shadows hunger for your blood…

[[/eventState fallAgainDescent entered]] (two options):

  • You think you are so strong…crawling down into our depths…stepping deep into a trap that will rip you limb from limb…

  • Yes…come closer…further down…walk among our Pathways where you're close enough to touch…

Examined the echoes of a past battle in [[/eventState fallAgainVoidspan]]:

You see a victory…on a lost and lonely bridge…ask the wizard if the win was worth the price he paid

Item-Related Whispers

These whispers are based on items in a character's inventory, and should be heard only by the character currently carrying the item in question.

The raspy whisper seems to come from everywhere around you, scratching at your eardrums as if begging to be let in.

Item Whisper Triggers

Items that trigger whispers are:

  • @UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas}

  • @UUID[Item.3kcd1E5aXjMi1NhB]{Bleak Archive Relic}

  • @UUID[Item.vSmAlffTDmiGnvVN]{Wraith Bane}

  • @UUID[Item.ysL3KPZFVsOZG5yF]{Uncanny Relic}

  • @UUID[Item.3qOjY12SUpQXz96v]{Defiled Journal}

The text used by the whispers for each is listed below.

Has the Finger of Nethehepticas (two options):

  • A finger in your pocket…a way to touch our power…a way for us to scratch and claw our way into your veins..

  • Glory to Nethehepticas…glory to one who carries him…when you are nothing more than bone…who will carry you…

Has the Bleak Archive Relic (two options):

  • Are you tired…weary weary weary…your very bones are cursed to hold a fragment of our power…

  • A relic in your pocket…a heaviness in every step…the light that burns your eyes and skin…is only the beginning…

Has the Wraith Bane:

You think the sword of giants old will save you from our reckoning? They fell to dust…and like them…you will soon be ash and bone…

Has the Uncanny Relic:

Uncanny pain…within your flesh…a sleep that never comes…they call it curse but it is but a preview of our power…

Has the Defiled Journal (two options):

  • The journal drips with ink…like a wound that never heals…like Aberin's wounds, in the end.

  • Poor poor Aberin…lost to the whispers in the night…but you're still listening, aren't you…are you ready to be next…

Character Option Whispers

These whispers are based on character options, including attunement and ancestry, and should only be heard by the specific character they apply to.

The whispering voice in your ear is hushed and raspy, its growled words burrowing deep into your eardrums.

Character Whisper Triggers

Character Options that trigger whispers are:

  • [[/ancestry emberHuman]]

  • [[/culture emberKessian]]

  • [[/attunement emberAbyss]]

  • [[/knowledge abyssals]]

The text used by the whispers for each is listed below.

Human Ancestry:

  • A human. So easy to corrupt…so fun to break….

  • A human. You think yourself resistant to the whispers of the night. Step by step…bone by bone…we'll shape you to our liking…

Kessian Ancestry

Kessian, your people bleed their useless lives on distant desert sands…one day we will feast on all your dust…

Attuned to the Abyss:

  • You have chosen wisely…you know the feel of power…we will bring you glory beyond measure…

  • You have answered the call of the deep….attuned to death and glory…let us feast together on the power you have found…

Has knowledge of the abyss:

  • You think you know all there is to know of the abyss? Dream of us tonight and wake up bleeding.

  • Each time you think of the abyss, it sees into your heart…the echo of your screams will be delicious….

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

There are no immediate next steps for the party - the whispers are simply a consequence of the decisions they have made thus far.

This event can be experienced multiple times and will continue to be in effect until @UUID[.A5AegdhUty9ISa1P]{Snarled Promises}, @UUID[.ypLaBcokRunTKLXA]{Smouldering Shelter} or @UUID[.HKClyq74TIjeZSJ8]{Phantasmal Waters} triggers later in the Quest.
Discordant Whispers.soverview: As the party continues to explore the Arctus Plateau, they will sometimes hear incredibly faint whispers in their minds. The voice is hideously painful and grating, often causing headaches or migraines.
Discordant Whispers.sexposition: A thin breeze whips past your face, and you shudder as a chill passes over you. You hear an incredibly faint whisper in your mind as if something utterly terrifying and alien has chanced across your path by some trick of fate and now focuses upon you with curiosity and hunger.
Discordant Whispers.ssummary: A faint whisper of some horrific alien entity passed over our minds; it spoke in a strange, jarring voice that gave us painful headaches and left us feeling ill.

Savage Descent.name: Savage Descent
Savage Descent.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party must make their way through a perilous route down into the Pathways. Along the way, they face a number of skill checks and challenges, including:

  • Finding their way past a barrier meant to keep out curious travelers.

  • Withstanding individual mental and physical challenges.

  • Resisting one final urge to turn back.

In this event, the characters can:

  • Gain 1 point of Akon Attunement if they manage to bypass the barrier using arcane magic (each participating character).

  • Gain 1 point of Ragen Attunement if they manage to bypass the barrier using the divine magic of Lantyr (each participating character).

  • Gain 1 point of Orbis Attunement for traversing the borehole (each character).

Several of these challenges are posed by a whispering voice similar to the one the players may have encountered in Discordant Whispers. As is noted in that event, the specific origin of the whispers is still under development, but will be a powerful force within the world of Ember.

Note: This event is easier for any member of the party who has [[/attunement emberAttunementAbyss]] or holds a @UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas}.

A Barrier Of Darkness

As the party begins to make their way through the passageway, they reach something that prevents them from moving forward any further - a barrier of darkness.

No sooner have you moved into the rapidly dimming light than something in front of you pushes back against your forward progress. It is thin and mildly damp, like the skin of a clammy hand, but stretches across the entire gap in front of you with an shadowy darkness that you can't see through.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check perception 14]] check or has [[/check perception 16 passive]] can see markings in the dirt in front of the barrier.

Though you can see nothing through the dark barrier, there are markings in the dirt in front of it - faint, and hard to see in the dim light, but intentional. The arrows and symbols have worn away slightly, but there is enough that you might be able to understand what they indicate, including the initials "A.L.," etched deeply but shakily into the ground like a signature.

The markings on the ground were made by Aberin Lowd, who found a small entrance through the skin of darkness.

Aberin's Notes

A character who succeeds on a [[/check investigation 22]] can follow in Aberin's footsteps, finding the gap that he went through into the quarry.

  • If any member of the party is carrying the @UUID[Item.3qOjY12SUpQXz96v]{Defiled Journal}, they can use it as a comparison with the markings, lowering the DC of the check by 2.

  • With a successful [[/check survival 15]] check, the character can determine which marks were made at which time, making them easier to read clearly and lowering the DC of the check by 2.

  • This section of the borehole is dimly lit. If characters generate light (by using a torch, casting a spell, or the like), they can see the markings more clearly, gaining advantage on the check.

Characters can also make their own way into the borehole by learning more about the barrier and/or attempting to break through.

Investigating the Barrier

  • With a successful [[/check arcana 15]] check or [[/knowledge abyssals]], the party knows that the wall in front of them is a form of abyssal energy that functions similarly to magic.

  • A portion of the barrier can be brought down by @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} if the spellcaster succeeds on a DC 14 check with their spellcasting ability. The gap created is narrow, as if the dispelled magic was mixed with something more powerful.

  • If characters touch but do not attack the barrier, they hear a soft whispering sound in their ears and begin to feel nauseated. Characters who remain in contact with the barrier must make a [[/save constitution 15]] saving throw. On a failure, they take [[/damage 1d10 necrotic]] damage.

  • Any character who has equipped an item of Lantyr or Spectra (such as @UUID[Item.O9mOxNLmw5XBGIiP]{Lantyr's Flame}, @UUID[Item.sFMqeMvy84TK0Kc1]{Spectra's Blessing}, or the @UUID[Item.kgaaBDUOYewux0Sn]{Sunalin Shield}), can pass through the barrier, which hisses as it is repelled from them and leaves behind a narrow gap.

Akon Attunement: Bypass the Barrier with Arcane Magic

Any character who manages to bypass the barrier with a arcane magic (such as the Dispel Magic spell) advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 fallAgainDescentArcane]] at the conclusion of the event.

Ragen Attunement: Bypass the Barrier with Divinity

Any character who manages to bypass the barrier with a divine relic of Lantyr (or similar magic) advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 fallAgainDescentDivine]] at the conclusion of the event.

Thick Skin

If characters strike at the barrier with force, it strikes back as noted below. After two attempts to force their way through, characters are able to create a narrow gap in the darkness that they can pass through.
