  • A melee weapon attack: Unless the weapon deals radiant damage, some of the darkness comes off on the weapon, coating it. Until the next long rest, attacks with this weapon are made with disadvantage. At that long rest, the character carrying the weapon must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 14]] saving throw. If they fail, they must roll on the @UUID[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X]{Minor Abyssal Madness} table.

    If the weapon used deals radiant damage, the barrier sizzles as it weapon cuts through it. There is no ill effect on the weapon and the barrier is cut through on a single strike.

  • An unarmed attack: Some of the darkness comes off of the barrier, coating any body part that came into direct contact with the barrier and clinging to it. The character affected must make a [[/save constitution 16]] check. On a failure, they take [[/damage 2d6 necrotic]] damage and gain the poisoned condition. On a success, they take half damage and are not poisoned. The barrier seems somewhat thinner beyond the point of contact.

  • A ranged weapon or magical attack: The attack bounces off of the barrier and targets the attacker. That character receives the full brunt of the attack, but the barrier sizzles and releases plumes of smoke at the point of impact. It smells faintly of charred meat.

Once the characters create or find an opening in the barrier, they can proceed into the borehole through the narrow gap.

The gap in the barrier is a narrow gash, torn through the veil of darkness. On the other side, a dim passageway leads forward and around a corner, narrow enough that you'll need go one by one, sideways, through its winding twists and turns, which may hold untold dangers.

Characters can choose to continue into the Shrouded Borehole, or choose to find another path into the Pathways.

[[/outcome entered]]

[[/outcome back]]

Traversing The Shrouded Borehole

As characters step into the Shrouded Borehole, they are immediately separated from all other members of the party and subjected to their own individual trials. Any character who is carrying the @UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas} or has [[/attunement emberAttunementAbyss]] has advantage on all individual checks, including their individual rolls within group checks. The broader group does not otherwise benefit.

Shrouded Borehole Challenges

Roll or select from the roll table below to determine the challenge each character faces. All character challenges end with them emerging into a misty room, described in @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}.

@Embed[RollTable.smFuXT0GQ6ur8Lkr inline rollable]

Choking Air

You round the corner into a dark circular cave of a room, the air around you warm and thick enough to choke on. If anyone else is in this place with you, you can't see or hear them, and there is nothing within arm's reach. As the air grow thicker and harder to breathe, a voice giggles and whispers into your ear.

You don't think about the breaths you take…until you feel them quicken…shorten…burn…

Breathing is nearly impossible in this room, as if the air itself is antithetical to life. Even ancestries that do not breathe air feel their life force being cut off bit by bit, with no way forward.

Choking On The Air

The character must immediately make a [[/save wisdom 16]] saving throw.

  • On a success, they have the will to move forward despite the choking effects of the cavern. With a successful Search made with either a [[/check perception 18]] check or [[/check investigation 18]] check, they find and use the exit, emerging in a misty room (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

    If the Search fails, the character may attempt it again, but after 2 failures they collapse from lack of air and gain 1 level of exhaustion, waking in a misty room (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit})

  • On a failure, they take [[/damage 1d6 psychic]] damage and hear the voice whispering once again:

    You tremble as your pathetic body begins to break down…but death would be too easy…not as much fun. Will you face your doom now…or will you suffer from it later…choose…choose…you must choose…

    If the character chooses to face their doom now, they take [[/damage 1d6 psychic]] and 1 level of exhaustion. If they choose to suffer from it later, they must roll on the @UUID[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X]{Minor Abyssal Madness} table. At the end of either choice, they lose consciousness from lack of breath, waking in a misty room (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

Grasping Hands

You round the corner into a cavern empty of everything but a scattering of small thin bones. Suddenly, a cold wind blows through the room, sweeping several bone fragments toward you. Where they knock into each other, they conjoin, forming grotesque mockeries of hands with long sharp fingers and joints that twist in ways they shouldn't, and begin crawling in your direction. When the wind blows again, it carries a voice with it.

What are you willing to leave behind…to make your way below…

The hands target the character's belongings, attempting to take an item of Common value (or of the GM's discretion) in the character's possession.

Attacking the Hands

Any individual hand can be kicked apart with an action or hit, but as soon as it does, the cold wind blows again and the hands re-form in their last position, striking out at the character in the process.

The character must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw or they take [[/damage 1d6 slashing]] damage. The DC on this check increases by 2 each time it is made and the hands do damage on a larger die, moving to [[/damage 1d8 slashing]], then [[/damage 1d10 slashing]], and so forth.

The bones break apart, but the chill wind returns, bringing them back where they came from, where they scratch and grab at your pockets and pouches once again, blows sharper than before.

Walking Through

To make their way through the passageway to the other side, characters must succeed on a [[/check acrobatics 18]] check to weave their way through the hands without being grabbed. With a successful [[/check nature 16]] check or [[/knowledge forensics]], they have advantage on the check.

  • On a success, they make their way through and exit the area, emerging in a cavern filled with mist (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

  • On a failure, or if the party takes any other action, the hands scratch at them as they exit, dealing [[/damage 1d6 slashing]] damage, and attempt to take an Uncommon item from them. The character must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw to pull the item back, losing the item on a failure as the hands scuttle off with it into the darkness.

    Will you be able to face what's next…without your little treasure…take it back now if you dare…

    Characters can attempt to retrieve their item from the scuttling hands, but must succeed on a [[/check 16 sleightofhand]] check to grab the item back. If they first succeed on a [[/check perception 14]] check to determine which of the fast moving hands is holding their item, they have advantage on the sleight of hand check.

    On a failure of the sleight of hand check, the hands pull the item under the ground and scratch at the character, who takes [[/damage 1d6 slashing]] damage. Any further attempts they make to retrieve the item are handles as in Attacking the Hands above.

Once characters leave the room, they emerge in a misty cavern (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

Heavy Steps

As you round the corner, you emerge in a long narrow passageway. The air here is heavy on your shoulders, pressing you down towards the ground, which is rocky and hard, studded with rough sharp rocks. Though there is no one in this passageway with you, you can feel the weight trying to bring you to your knees and push your body down into the ground beneath your feet. Along with the weight comes a whisper in your ear:

How slow you are…how bent and broken…crawl your way through if you can…

Characters have difficulty making their way forward as the air presses them down, attempting to force them to crawl across sharp bloodying rocks.

Heavy Weights

Any character in this area must immediately make a [[/save strength 18]] saving throw. On a success, they move forward despite the weight, remaining upright. On a failure, they are forced by the weight onto their knees, taking [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] and must crawl forward across the sharp rocks of the floor (see The Bloody Rocks) below.

As characters continue making their way through the passageway, whether on their feet or while crawling, the voice speaks again:

You think you are so strong…but there are many types of weight…do you feel your failures weighing down your shoulders? You are nothing. Nothing at all…

Characters immediately feel an internal weight that they must push through.

As the voice speaks, memories come to you unbidden. Every word of disappointment anyone has ever spoken to you. Any final screams of death from those you have failed to save. Any choices you have made that you are not sure were right. All of them add to the weight on your shoulders now as the whisper continues to echo — failure, nothing, weight.

Characters must make a [[/save 16 wisdom]] saving throw. On a success, they stagger forward at their current height (remaining standing or crawling). On a failure, they are pushed down, either from standing to crawling, or from crawling to dragging, taking [[/damage 1d6 piercing]] and face the sharp rocks of the floor (see The Bloody Rocks) below.

Once characters have dealt with the consequences of both weights, they emerge in a misty cavern (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

If characters succumb to either the mental or physical weight of the passageway, they are pushed down. Characters who are walking begin crawling and characters who are crawling begin dragging themselves forward.

Crawling Through the Bloody Rocks

As the crawl begins, the the voice speaks to the character again:

Crawling like a child…do you feel like a child? Frightened like a child?

The character must make a [[/save 16 wisdom]] saving throw or they gain the frightened condition and immediately bolt for the end of the passageway, automatically failing all remaining checks.

Characters who are not frightened can avoid further immediate damage by carefully weaving their way through the maze of sharp rocks with a successful [[/check survival 15]] or [[/check perception 15]] check. On a failure, or if they are frightened and cannot make the check, they take an additional [[/damage 1d6 slashing]].

If characters avoid being pushed down further when the voice speaks to them a second time, they can crawl forward the rest of the way without incident, emerging in a misty cavern ((@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

Dragging Over the Bloody Rocks

Characters who have been pushed from crawling into dragging themselves forward are confronted by the voice once again.

You drag yourself forward, bit by bit…leaving your blood behind. How sad you are…how…tiring…

Characters take [[/damage 1d6 slashing]] damage and take 1 level of exhaustion, before emerging into a misty cavern (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

Painful Echoes

You round the corner into a small cave whose black glassy walls seem partly melted, the rock caught in the middle of dripping down the sides of the cavern and frozen in place, creating odd bulges and lumps. As you enter, a single drop of murky water hits the ground, echoing loudly. But where sound would normally cease, this sound reverberates, bounding between the melted walls and growing in volume until it threatens to drill into your ears with its power. In its place, a very quiet whisper reaches your ear, less heard than felt, as if it has crawled its way up through your body.

What do you have to say for yourself now…will you say anything at all?

Escalating Sound

Any sound made by the character (a word spoken out loud, a loud footstep, etc.) bounces off of the walls and becomes louder and louder until it is a percussive attack of a sound.

Characters can make their way through the cavern silently by succeeding on a [[/check stealth 16]] check. On a failure, the sound that they make bounces through the room and hits them at full volume. They must succeed on a [[/save constitution 16]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d6 thunder]] damage.

As characters make their way through the cavern, they are affected twice by the whispering voice of the borehole. In either case, a failure causes them to make a sound.

  • The First Trial: Characters are subjected to intense fear as the voice speaks to them.

    You claim bravery…but I see your soul…and you will scream in terror…

    The character must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 15]] saving throw or they gain the frightened condition and flee towards the exit, making sound that echoes back and forth. They must succeed on a [[/save constitution 16]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d6]] thunder damage. If they have already taken thunder damage, this save is made with disadvantage.

  • The Second Trial: Characters are subject to intense joy and glee.

    Do you feel the glee…how delicious it is to feel you suffer…

    The character must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 15]] saving throw or they begin to giggle, uncontrollably, and the giggles bounce back and forth off of the walls. They must succeed on a [[/save constitution 16]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d6]] thunder damage. If they have already taken thunder damage, this save is made with disadvantage.

Once they have made it through both trials, the characters exit the area into a misty cavern (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

Dark Dreams

As you round the corner, you enter a cavern that is pitch black, as if no daylight has ever been seen here. You are hit with an overwhelming urge to sleep, your eyes becoming heavier and heavier and your body racked with exhaustion.

Lulled to Sleep

Characters must make a [[/save wisdom 16]] saving throw or they are inflicted with the effects of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.KhwiSi9fwVfUPtku]{Sleep} spell cast at a level equivalent to the character's level. They are affected even if they would normally not be affected by this spell (they are immune to being charmed or are undead).

If the character falls asleep as a result of the Sleep effects, they must immediately roll on the @UUID[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X]{Minor Abyssal Madness} table and gain 1 level of exhaustion when they wake.

If the character succeeds on their save, the voice speaks to them again:

You do not wish to sleep? Heed these words…sleep now…or suffer later…

Characters may choose to sleep, suffering the penalty above. If they do not, they must succeed on a [[/save constitution 15]] saving throw or they take [[/damage 1d8 psychic]] damage. In addition, on a failure they have lingering fatigue. The next time they take a long rest, they must succeed on a [[/save wisdom 15]] saving throw or they gain 1 level of exhaustion when they wake.

Once characters have either resisted the effects of the exhaustion or fallen asleep, they can leave this cavern and move into a large space (@UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG#a-misty-exit]{A Misty Exit}).

A Misty Exit

You emerge in a large open space, reunited in this place of swirling darkness. The edges and shape of it are hard to make out through the shadowy mist that roils and curls in front of your eyes, whispering indistinctly in voices that sound both distorted and familiar. Before you can take a step, a now-familiar voice speaks to you all as a suddenly fierce breeze batters your faces:

Still here…fools…you have one last chance…turn back…turn back…

Ahead of you is a faint purple light, eerie but steady. Behind you is the light of the land you left behind, safe and calm,

The entire party emerges in an open misty cavern, reunited after their individual trials.

Pushing Through

To leave the cavern, the party must resist the entity's entreaties to turn back and head toward the purple light. They succeed on a group [[/check 24 wisdom]] check (if at least half the party succeeds, the entire group succeeds). This check is made easier as follows:

  • If any character came through their trial with no damage, the DC of the check is reduced by 3.

  • Any character who shares their experience with the rest of the party makes their check with advantage.

  • If any member of the party stops here for a short or long rest, they make the check with disadvantage.

  • Any member of the party who attempts to step forward can make a [[/check athletics 15]] check. On a success, they move closer to the exit and the DC of the check is reduced by 2. Each characters can only make this check once.

If characters succeed on the wisdom check, they exit into the purple light of the Pathways, leaving the voice behind:

Success…or so you think…but now the real fun begins…

If characters fail the wisdom check as a whole, but any member of the party succeeded on their roll, that character may attempt to convince the rest to keep going into the pathways with a successful [[/check 15 persuasion]], [[/check deception 15]], or [[/check 15 intimidation]] check. If they succeed, they persuade the group to leave.

If the character attempting to convince the others to continue forward fails, or no one passed the initial check to resist the voice's calls to turn back, they turn to the safe place behind them. The voice speaks one last time:

Weak…as we thought…leave this place at once!

All characters take [[/damage 1d6 psychic]] and [[/damage 1d6 necrotic]] damage before stumbling out of the cavern and find themselves back where they started, outside of the Shrouded Borehole on Ember's surface.

Orbis Attunement: Through the Borehole

Any character who successfully traverses the borehole advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 fallAgainDescentThrough]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome pathways]]

[[/outcome back]]

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party emerges in the Pathways, triggering @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.fVJBgl3XH6lCPdEy]{Twisting Shadows}
Savage Descent.soverview: The party uncovers a small borehole, and it's unclear if the tunnel descending into the depths is naturally occurring or created by something or someone. They can attempt to travel down this tight, claustrophobic passage into the Pathways but will be challenged by progressively challenging mental hazards.
Savage Descent.sexposition: Among the rocky hillsides a small gorge cuts into the nearby stone ahead. The jagged walls rise steeply, and sunlight fails to penetrate through the narrow opening above, casting dark shadows along the ground that dissolve into a deep darkness the further you peer ahead. The air here is stagnant and thick with tension, and it feels as if someone is watching.
Savage Descent.ssummary: We discovered a small claustrophobic route down into the Pathways. As we made our way forward, we were separated and given vicious challenges by a voice from within the passage. Eventually, we made our way through, emerging in a large dark cavern.

Absolute Destruction.name: Absolute Destruction
Absolute Destruction.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and combat event takes place in the @UUID[Scene.emberRustvarMoun]{Rustvar Valleys} area map using the "Giant Ruins" composition.

The party comes across a Paladin of Lantyr from Kessia, @UUID[Actor.bEMPCjG9mFc1d93U]{Issa Sunsword}, studying the remains of the gashed pillar. As she invites the party to help her determine the nature of the damage, Abyssal Echoes emerge from around the party and attack.

Whether or not she succumbs to her injuries, Issa suggests that something is entering the Arctus Plateau from the Pathways and that it will continue to attack unless it is stopped at its source.

In this event, the characters can:

  • Gain 1 point of Abyss or Luxarum Attunement — depending on whether or not Issa Sunsword is killed during the fight with the Abyssal Horrors (each character).

A Greeting from Issa Sunsword

The woman turns toward you.

My apologies for speaking without showing you my face. Lantyr knows that all things are done best in the light, but this pillar troubles me enough to have drawn me into gazing at its shadows. This is a troubling stain upon the Arctus Plateau and one more place to shine Lantyr's light. Tell me, do you also walk her path?

Characters with [[/knowledge gods]] or who succeed on a [[/check 13 religion]] or [[/check 13 history]] check know that Lantyr, in addition to being the cosmic body known commonly as The Sun, is an Elder Goddess and that worship of her generally involves reverence for the light, energy, radiance, and life, as well as hatred of all things twisted by evil and monsters.

Unless the party attacks Issa or claims to be working with forces that opposed Lantyr, she wishes them well on their quest and is happy to share her own:

  • Issa has been traveling across the surface world of Ember rooting out and fighting corruption and evils on her own for several years.

  • Issa is from the southern continent of Kessia, miles away from the Arctus Plateau, where the worship of Lantyr is common and the threat of monsters is ever-present. Long ago, Kessia was a place where the Aedir built massive cities and entire kingdoms, but the Shattering ravaged the land, transforming most of the continent into the vast Obsidian Desert. According to many Kessians, only Lantyr's divine help saved what remains of the continent.

  • Issa hopes that figuring out what the Shent pillar said will explain why it was so brutally attacked. She suspects that it might be a marker of a location in the Pathways beneath the surface of Ember.

On a successful [[/check wisdom 14]] check, characters know that Issa is being forthright about what brings her to this place.

  • Result of 17+. You sense that Issa hopes to convince you to join her in worship of Lantyr and that she is prepared to attack if it turns out they have any association with the corruption that Lantyr opposes.

Issa's Quest

Like many others from my homeland of Kessia, I have committed myself to the service of Lantyr, whose light graces us daily and whose divine wisdom has shaped my long journey here. Unlike those who battle the monsters my goddess despises in the expansive sands of Kessia's Obsidian Desert, she has led me here, fight by fight, to a land across the ocean from my birthplace. While you may not concern yourselves with the darkness as we do, this place is no less threatened by the creatures it corrupts.

Kessia

Our ancient texts say that my homeland of Kessia was once a paradise, with lush vibrant jungles filled with thriving cities, powerful armies, and wondrous magics. But when the Shattering ripped apart the sky, our land was destroyed, broken, and twisted beneath our feet. Only Lantyr saved Kessia's people, and even she could do so much against the evils that sprang forth. Rich land became endless black and purple deserts, with only stones like this one left as markers of what once was.

I fear that this could happen to your land too. If Kessia was harmed by ambition, Aterica and the Arctus Plateau may someday fall to ignorance. Remember, just because you do not see the monsters shifting below the surface does not mean they aren't coming.

What Brought Her Here

I believe this stone was left here by the Shent giants. They fell against the darkness during the Shattering but they were strong enough and wise enough to leave knowledge behind. I suspect many evil monsters make it a point to destroy Shent relics where they can, leaving nothing for future mortals to learn from. Perhaps there is something from this marker they've left behind, though it has suffered greatly in some ancient attack.

The Ancient Stones

Characters who succeed on a [[/check history 15]] check know that the ancient pillar was placed here by the Shent, an ancient ancestry of giants that was wiped out during the time of the Shattering.

  • Result of 17+: The Shent were targeted for destruction by creatures of corruption and destruction who descended on Ember after the Shattering.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check investigation 15]] check or have [[/knowledge warfare]] can tell that the damage to the stones is ancient. It also shows signs of targeting. Something or someone purposefully attacked the stones in a coordinated assault.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check religion 15]] check or have [[/knowledge rituals]] have a strong feeling that the pillars were a part of a Shent ceremony of some kind, but the purpose of the ceremony has been lost to time.

Translating the Runes

Many of the runes on the ancient pillar have been damaged by whatever creature damaged it, but Issa thinks she can make out the Pathward words for Sun and People. The rest has either been destroyed or worn down over time.

Here, this is the the Pathward symbol for sun. It is similar to a mark we use at some of our holy sites in Kessia, passed down from before the Shattering. And I believe this is the sign for people. Maybe people of the sun? I wish there was more I could see, but it is good to mark where it is — some believe that these pillars marked nearby entrances to the Pathways beneath Ember's surface.

Characters with [[/language pathward]] or [[/knowledge shent]] can confirm the runes Issa has found and know that Pathward is written as combinations of symbols that can be combined to create a greater meaning.

A Sudden Attack

Before the party can investigate further, the circumstances on this mountain ledge suddenly change.

For a moment, the wind slows to stillness. When a faint breeze returns, it carries the smell of smoke, bile and rot. Behind the pillar, a shadow appears, forming seemingly out of thin air to advance on Issa Sunsword. The paladin has her sword out in an instant.

Monstrous echoes of darkness! They will cower soon enough before the power of Lantyr!

As she turns to face the threat, another one of the creatures forms behind her, joined soon by another and another.

Stand against these horrors!

Five Abyssal Echoes appear from thin air amidst the shadows cast by the great pillars.

@Embed[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE count=5]

Abyssal Echoes Attack!

The Abyssal Echoes focus their initial attack on Issa Sunsword, immediately moving to within range of her and keeping each other close. If choosing between targets in the party, Abyssal Echoes will target Spellcasters or anyone who is either carrying a holy symbol or has an attunement to Lantyr.

Abyssal Echo Tactics

Abyssal Echoes typically swarm their targets, taking advantage of Abyssal @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.gHXWVaidho85zB1L]{Pack Tactics} and their flying speed, then use @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.P6VruIOK3ctYTiZ2]{Malignant Slash} to attack. Anyone who casts a spell during a fight with the echoes is quickly targeted by @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.cMDpGjHKzXd2im33]{Swallowed Screams}, to prevent them from using spells with a verbal component.

When Echoes are low on hit points, they may attempt to position themselves so that their death blocks their targets into a corner, as they melt into a residue that can be harmful to anyone to who touches it.

Issa Sunsword's Words

During this battle, there is a high probability that Issa will be hurt or killed. During the battle, she shares what she knows, and may say any of the following on her turns.

Initial attack:

How are there so many of them?

During the attack:

They come from below! The Pathways of legend are filled with horrors!

If Issa dies:

Find these creatures where they lurk and stop them, before they corrupt your lands as they did Kessia!

After the Attack

If Issa died in content, the party can search her body for information.

Issa's Items

Issa Sunsword's shield has broken in two, but her sword, @UUID[Actor.bEMPCjG9mFc1d93U.Item.T4N1c8jjKCSdI7Zv]{Lantyr's Blade} can be taken by anyone in the party. If the person who takes the sword has [[/attunement emberAttunementAbyss]] or is carrying an item of the abyss (such as the@UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas}), the sword burns them as they grab the handle, dealing [[/damage radiant 1d6]] damage.

Abyss Attunement: Issa Sunsword Died

If Issa Sunsword dies during the fight with the Abyssal Echoes, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 fallAgainDestructionDied]] at the conclusion of the event.

If Issa survives, she moves on to her next adventure, but wishes the party well.

A Sacred Calling

Issa thanks the characters and prepares to head off into the Arctus Plateau

Thank you so much for your help. Much as I walk my path with Lantyr alone, I am so grateful for the times that she puts companions in my path. I wonder if we have met because you will find where these things came from and stop them. If you have the chance, please take it. I believe they have come up from the Pathways below the surface. I do not know a way down there, but if you find one, perhaps you can track them down and end this threat.

Issa plans to continue on her own, following a ray of sunlight that she sees in the distance, which she believes is a sign from Lantyr.

I see a glow of light in the distance that I must follow, but that is my journey. May Lantyr bless you on yours.

Luxarum Attunement: Issa Sunsword Survived

If Issa Sunsword survives the fight with the Abyssal Echoes, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 fallAgainDestructionSurvived]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event serves as a breadcrumb and introduction to the rest of the @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi]{To Fall and Fall Again} quest. There are no immediate follow-up steps, but the party will discover more information about what has happened here by exploring and investigating the Pathways or by visiting the hamlet of Storsa's Strand where the @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.kcVbK4QwEsG0XYOG]{Strand of Fate} event occurs.
Absolute Destruction.soverview: The party discovers a damaged Shent pillar while exploring the recesses of a deep valley. This ancient stone ruin has been torn into by deep, rending claw marks. A Paladin of Lantyr named Issa Sunsword greets the party as the examines this damage, explaining that she is tracking abyssal activity in the Arctus Plateau. Before she can share much more, abyssal creatures appear attacking both her and the party.
Absolute Destruction.sexposition:
Between the towering peaks of the Wedgelands, the valley deepens into a nook of wildflowers and weathered standing stones in a rough circular pattern. All are covered in large runes, but one stands above the others, its once-polished stone roughened by time and marked by deep wide carvings. It is only when you move closer that the jagged edges of some of the cuts can be seen — these are not carvings but gashes, torn into the stone by an unknown force that has nearly ripped it apart.

But you are not the only ones drawn to the pillar. A figure in golden armor stands in front of the pillar, nearly dwarfed by its size, turning her head from one direction to the next as she carefully examines the gash marks in the stone.

As you step toward her, her voice rings out, echoing across the small valley.

Be on your guard, travelers. This is not the sort of damage caused by storms or beasts. This is something much worse.
Absolute Destruction.ssummary: We discovered a destroyed Shent Pillar that seamed to be a marker of some kind, through most of its inscribed runes were heavily worn and weathered. A fellow adventurer examining the pillar came under attack from monstrous creatures and believed they had come from the Pathways beneath the surface.

Strand of Fate.name: Strand of Fate
Strand of Fate.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, characters visit Storsa's Strand, which is awaiting news of a missing town member, Aberin Lowd. If the party knows of Aberin's death from @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.SiGM3D6clt3XH978]{Tormented Threads}, they can inform his father Kendral Lowd. While in town, they can also:

  • Potentially convince Kendral Lowd to give them the location of a nearby entryway to the Pathways that Aberin was studying before he died.

  • Meet the residents of Storsa's Strand, who are friendly but have been feeling a general sense of weariness and malaise for some time. (This feeling is caused by the abyssal energy that is leaking into the area through the Shrouded Borehole that Aberin was attempting to use to reach the Pathways and wedged open, though there is no way for the town to know this.)

  • Visit the local shrine to Lantyr for comfort.

  • Gain 1 point of Cora or Primordis Attunement — depending on whether they provide proof of Aberin's fate or not (each character).

The Missing Son of Storsa's Strand

The fish-carrying villager who stopped the party is Verdal Fain, who believes the party has come with news about the missing Aberin Lowd.

A Short Conversation with Verdal Fain

Verdal wants to speak with the party but can only talk for so long while balancing the crate that they're carrying. With a successful [[/check athletics 15]] check, the party can help them with their current task, allowing for a longer conversation. Characters can also convince Verdal to stop and put the crate down with a successful [[/check 15 persuasion]] check. On a failed check, or if a check isn't attempted, Verdal can only share the following:

  • If the party knows and shares that Aberin has died, Verdal is crushed. They knew Aberin, and though Aberin had problems, hoped for the best. They suggest telling Aberin's father, Kendral, who works by the docks.

I feared that this might happen, I did. Aberin just isn't the same as he was when we were in school together and worried something might happen to him. One of the only things I've really felt at all lately. His father's here in town - a fisher just down there at the docks. You'll have to tell him. After everything he's been through, I hope it doesn't break his heart.

  • If the party does not know anything about Aberin, Verdal apologizes for interrupting their journey. The town is worried about Aberin, who is the son of Kendral Lowd, a local fisher who has "already lost so much."

I'm sorry. I shouldn't have assumed. You're probably here to try the fish stew. Though they jtaste like much these days. Whole town's just a little worried about Aberin Lowd. Mostly because of everything his father's been through. He won't talk about it — just wants to talk about fishing — but he's lost so much already that I was hoping for good news. Thought it might lighten the mood around here a little.

A Longer Conversation with Verdal Fain

If the party helps or convinces Verdal to be part of a longer conversation, they can learn the following:

  • Aberin Lowd is the son of the Lowd family, a group of adventurers who would go on dangerous expeditions. After his sister Daelin died on one of them, he got strange and started mumbling about passageways to the deep.

  • When Aberin started losing touch with reality, he was sent off to Corpin Sanctuary for healing. Everyone thought he was fine, until a letter from the sanctuary arrived — Aberin left to make his way home a few weeks ago. No one has heard from him since.

  • Town morale has been low recently, but that started before Aberin left town. Seems like there is something in the air dragging everyone down.

  • The main attraction in town is the Far From Home, where Chef Tama Tyne serves up the town's famous Fish Stew, served in edible bowls. The stew seems a bit bland to Verdal, but then everything seems a bit bland to them these days.

  • The structure in the center of town is the town's shrine to Lantyr, which they keep burning at all times and is the only thing that seems to boost spirits.

Aberin:

Aberin Lowd. One of the adventuring Lowds. At least they used to be. Nowadays only Kendral's left, fishing at the docks like he didn't have a whole different life once. Sad story, really — daughter Daelin disappeared somewhere down below the surface of Ember and Aberin went just about crazy trying to get her back. That's why he left Storsa's Strand.

Aberin's Disappearance:

There was something Aberin was looking into, some way to get down to where his sister Daelin disappeared, and it started playing tricks with his mind. Kendral sent him to Corpin Sanctuary for help, figured he'd get what he needed there. Until word came down that Aberin left, said he was headed back this way. That was weeks ago, and the world's a dangerous place these days.

Life in Storsa's Strand:

Not much to tell about Storsa's Strand. Days come, days go. You keep your head down and do what needs to be done. Mood in town's been low recently. Since before Aberin left. Don't know what it is, but no one seems able to shake the feeling that your steps are heavier and the food is blander and everything looks a bit dim.

The Inn:

Far From Home's known more for the fish stew that Tyne serves up than its room and board, but I'm sure there are a few rooms available. Just know — if you walk through the doors of the inn, Tyne will make you try some of the stuff. It all tastes the same to me, like liquid dust, but she swears she's putting seasoning on it.

The Burning Flame in Town:

A shrine to Lantyr. About the only thing that really puts a smile on folks' face around here. Grabbing one of the torches can fix just about anything for a moment, though it didn't do much for Aberin in the end.

Meeting Kendral Lowd

@Embed[Actor.GuuohJfDx6gifCH5]

Kendral is generally kind, but prefers keep his answers short and sweet and is focused on getting back to his fishing. He can confirm that he used to be an adventurer but now focuses on fishing, which is safer.

Making Conversation

Kendral is reluctant to speak about anything other than fishing, especially if it relates to the Pathways, his life as an adventurer, or his family. If asked about the odd feeling in the town or Sielle Kraddock's hope that he'll investigate it, Kendral dismisses it strongly.

I used to be the type to think about things like that. Always off trying to make the world better. Only I made my own life worse in the process.

If asked about his family, or Aberin, he will only say that he hopes Aberin will return someday.

I'm the only Lowd left in town these days. Used to think Aberin would come back one day, healed from whatever's troubling his mind, but even the healers at Corpin Sanctuary couldn't help him, so he may be lost forever.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check insight 14]] check can tell that he is both guilty and afraid - he fears that sharing what happened to Aberin will somehow lead others to follow in his path.

Aberin's Fate

Kendral will speak about Aberin with any character who tells Kendral about his son's death and provides an item of proof, including @UUID[Item.FAIY0mM4FxU52CK9]{A Note For Pa}, the @UUID[Item.3qOjY12SUpQXz96v]{Defiled Journal}, or an @UUID[Item.8L9rrnzA8fLIpCdP]{Inscribed Ring of Eternal Rest}. He is saddened but not surprised.

I should have known it would come to this, I suppose. Ever since that horrible night. I lost my daughter in the Pathways beneath the surface, but I lost my son too, overcome with this obsession with finding her.

Characters who know of Aberin's death but have no proof must succeed on a [[/check persuasion 17]] to speak with Kendral about Aberin, while characters who do not know of Aberin's death must succeed on a [[/check persuasion 18]]. He will share the following:

  • Kendral was trained as a wizard by the Anaechranum and once adventured in the near-mythical pathways beneath the surface alongside his wife Jai, a cleric who worshiped Lantyr, Aberin, and Aberin's sister Daelin.

  • On one trip, Kendral and Jai were separated from both of their children. Daelin was permanently lost to the family, while Aberin returned. After that event, Kendral stopped adventuring, and Jai left Storsa's Strand for Ordain, but Aberin became obsessed with getting back to the Pathways and finding Daelin.

  • Aberin found what he thought was a way down to the Pathways, the Shrouded Borehole, but trying to get to the Pathways began driving him mad. Kendral is aware of the location to this entrance, but does not want the party to attempt to find it.

  • Aberin went to Corpin Sanctuary in an attempt to get better and no one has heard from him since. Recent reports from the Sanctuary say that he left the place, but he hasn't been heard from since. Kendral believes that his son is dead, though he hopes he is wrong.

Kendral does not want to share the location of the Shrouded Borehole, but can be convinced by characters who succeed on a [[/check persuasion 17]] or [[/check intimidation 17]] check, marking the location on the characters' map. Characters with [[/knowledge abyssals]] or who told Kendral of his son's death have advantage.

Cora Attunement: Proof of Aberin's Fate

If the party chooses to reveal the details of Aberin's fate to Kendral, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 fallAgainStrandFate]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Aberin's Fate Untold

If the party chooses to withold the details of Aberin's fate from Kendral, each character advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 fallAgainStrandUntold]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Lowd Family:

There was a time when it was the four of us — me, my wife Jai, Aberin, my daughter Daelin. Traveling into those dark spaces beneath the surface of Ember, trying to understand them and bring them Lantyr's light. I have always favored the goddess Spectra myself, but my wife was dedicated to Lantyr, and for a while the group of us seemed unstoppable. Then we had a bad night, and Daelin was lost. And so was Aberin, in his own way.

Aberin's Obsession:

After his sister died down in the Pathways and his mother went to Ordain to rededicate herself to the temple of her youth, I thought Aberin and I would be able to support each other here. Give up adventuring. Live a slower, safer life. But he kept wanting to go back. Get back down below. Find her body. Say his last goodbye. Even found a cave near here that leads that way. But going through it? He couldn't figure out how, and each time he came back he'd left some piece of himself behind. Ended up tearing him apart so badly he went to Corpin Sanctuary for healing.

Kendral's Daughter/Aberin's Sister:

Daelin was strong, bright. Smart as a whip, just like her mother. And devoted to Lantyr. It's why we settled here — the whole town is about Lantyr, but don't worry, they're welcoming. Didn't mind an old Spectra follower like me setting up and living here as long as I did right by the community. Maybe they take pity on me — only took one wrong battle with those inky shadows in the pathways and I lost Daelin and my wife and now Aberin, and…and everything.

Aberin's Current Location (If not aware that Aberin has died):

I was hoping Aberin would stay in Corpin Sanctuary for a bit, but last I heard he checked himself out and went back to searching for a way into the world beneath the surface. I'd love to say that I expect to see him back here one day, but I have a feeling he's lost to me now.

[[/outcome convinced]]

Exploring Storsa's Strand

If the party wishes to learn more about the town of Storsa's Strand, they can visit the Far From Home Inn, investigate the large bowl of fire, or speak to the woman who is now lighting her unlit torch sticks from the communal flame, Sielle Kraddock.

Sielle Kraddock's Lost & Found Artifacts

Sielle is the daughter of the infamous Quag Kraddock, who had a knack for pulling odd items out of the deep. She's trying to clear out some of the finds he kept in his Kraddock's Dock after Quag's recent death in the lake. She will attempt to get the party to buy her items first and foremost.

You're interested in my curious artifacts, are you? They're a legacy from my father, Quag Kraddock. Always pulling odd things out of the lake. House is filled with them now so I'm trying to sell a few - any interest in buying?

To determine what Sielle currently has for sale, roll 3 times on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} treasure table. She charges 10sp for all items.

Sielle is happy to talk to the party if they buy an item from her, talk to her about her sales with [[/knowledge trade]] or speak with her about her devotion to Lantyr with a successful [[/check religion 14]] check or [[/knowledge gods]]. She knows the following:

  • Her father felt an odd energy in the area in the weeks before his death, which he felt was coming from outside of the town, somewhere close. Sielle believes that this energy may have been the reason that her father's boat capsized in the lake and is responsible for a general feeling of malaise in the town.

  • Sielle suggested that Kendral Lowd investigate the odd energy, as members of his family have long been unofficial protectors of the town, but he worries that it will go wrong. If the party thinks they can talk him into it, he's at the docks.

  • Sielle is hoping that by keeping the flame of Lantyr lit, the town will be protected from whatever is in the air.

Sielle's Items/Sielle's Father:

I don't know which of these things is worth anything at all. My dad was the artifact expert. Had a sense for things beyond the ordinary. Sometimes I think it's what got him killed — he was too good a fisher to just fall out of his boat, but he'd been talking about an odd feeling in the air. It's still here, I think. Don't you feel it?

Energy in the Town:

Something is off. Been like this since before Aberin left for Corpin Sanctuary. Things don't taste the same, we haven't had our regular festival. My dad…he felt it. Used to be the kind of thing you'd ask a Lowd to take care of, but Kendral's not the same these days.

Kendral Lowd:

Only member of the Lowd family left in Storsa's Strand. Used to be him and his wife Jai and the kids, Daelin and Aberin. Daelin and I were about the same age. When she didn't come back after one of their expeditions, whole family tore apart. Bad for them and bad for us too - Storsa's Strand has always had a Lowd family member looking out for it, and now the whole town just feels sad.

Worshipping Lantyr:

We have always worshipped Lantyr here. How can you look upon her glowing beauty and not feel warmed from within? I only hope that she will keep us safe now.

Aberin Lowd:

I liked Aberin. A lot. Not sure what happened to him there in the end. Just couldn't get over Daelin's death, I guess. The whole family hasn't been the same. I think it's the reason Kendral won't investigate whatever it is that's settled on the air here. Afraid of losing more. I get it. I just wish someone would figure out what's going on around here.

Investigating the Bowl of Flame

The first time that any character approaches the flame, they feel a sense of warmth fill them, unless they are carrying an item of the abyss or have [[/attunement emberAttunementAbyss]].

  • Any character carrying an item of the abyss (the @UUID[Item.3qOjY12SUpQXz96v]{Defiled Journal}, the @UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas}, etc.) feels it grow hot within their bag and takes [[/damage 1d6 fire]]. With a [[/check arcana 15]] check, characters know that the shrine has some sort of divine magic that is anathema to abyssal attunement.

    A fierce heat begins to radiate from the object of the abyss that you carry with you, as if it is a ball of flame, leaving burns on your skin.

  • Any character who has [[/attunement emberAttunementAbyss]] is prevented from getting too close to the flame. As they approach the ball of fire they are repelled, taking [[/damage 1d6 force]] damage. With a [[/check arcana 15]] check, characters know that the shrine has some sort of divine magic that is anathema to abyssal attunement.

    As you move toward the dancing flame, you hit what feels like a wall of force and are thrown backward.

Characters with [[/knowledge gods]], who succeed on a [[/check religion 13]] check, or who succeed on a [[/check history 15]] check know that the bowl and torches comprise a shrine to Lantyr, an Elder Goddess of Light and Life whose physical form is the celestial body commonly known as the sun. Shrines of this type are open to all, and those who wish to honor Lantyr can do so by lighting one of the torches and opening themselves to the warmth of the sun.

The first time that any character does this, they receive the benefits of the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.8dzaICjGy6mTUaUr]{Bless}. Any character who is under the effects of a curse has that curse removed, as if targeted by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.XZhdgVK3cLoxNCQl]{Remove Curse} spell, and characters. If characters light the torch a second time, they feel the warmth but do not receive the mechanical benefit.

A feeling of warmth fills your body, lifting your spirits. The warmth does not seem to come from the flame ahead of you, but from deep within your heart.

Characters can return the torch sticks to the nearby bowl, or take one (but only one) with them. if the party takes more than one, only one will stay lit, becoming @UUID[Item.O9mOxNLmw5XBGIiP]{Lantyr's Flame}. Any additional torch sticks are simply @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.BnOCLuNWhVvzHLjl]{Torches}.

The Far From Home Inn

The party may choose, if they wish, to visit the Far From Home Inn. It is mostly empty.

The inn is brightly decorated, but pretty much empty of anyone other than a vrjnhar who stands behind a large countertop cooking fish in a series of large silver skillets over a carved box that spurts out fire at regular intervals. The air is almost chokingly thick with the smell of spices. As you enter, the chef drops a handful of something red into one of the skillets and turns your way without skipping a beat.

Come for the famous spiced fish stew? Hopefully you'll actually be able to taste what I'm trying to do here, unlike everyone else in this town.

Maximum Spice

If a character chooses to taste the fish stew at any point during their conversation with Chef Tyne, the chef is thrilled and offers a bite free of charge. It is spiced aggressively, with enough heat on it to burn the mouth.

Any character who tastes it must make a [[/save constitution 14]] saving throw. On a failure, they are burned by the spices and take [[/damage 1d4 fire]] damage. Characters with [[/ancestry emberVrjnhar]] or [[/ancestry emberFej]] have advantage on the save.

Talking to Chef Tyne

The vrjnhar introduces herself as Chef Tama Tyne, and invites the party to try a sample of the fish stew. If no one in the party will taste the food, she's hurt and offended and busies herself with trying to come up with a new recipe, ignoring any further attempts at conversation. She can be persuaded to speak with the party even after a refusal with a successful [[/check persuasion 18]] check. Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on this check.

Characters can lie about their enjoyment of the meal with a successful [[/check deception 15]] check, attempt to identify an ingredient and talk about it with a successful [[/check 14 nature]] check, or attempt to change the conversation entirely to local matters with a [[/check 14 persuasion]] check.

With a success on any of the three, Chef Tyne will share information about Storsa’s Strand. With a failure, Tyne turns away from the group and returns to cooking, mumbling about the palates of the people in the village.

Chef Tyne can share the following:

  • She has a higher spice tolerance than most, but feels as if she is overdoing her attempts recently as she tries to get any reaction from the locals, who seem to have no real sense of taste anymore.

  • She arrived in Storsa’s Strand only about a season ago, having been recruited by the previous chef of Far From Home. Tyne thought it would be a good opportunity, but the chef she replaced complained about having lost their ability to really enjoy food, and she is noticing a similar effect.

  • The issues with the food predate Chef Tyne's arrival, but according to the previous chef, they started around the time that one of the locals had to be sent to Corpin Sanctuary after losing touch with reality. Tyne believes the last name of this unfortunate local was Lowd, probably related to the fisher Kendral Lowd, who works on the docks and is one of her fish suppliers.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

If the party successfully got the location of the Shrouded Borehole from Kendral Lowd, they find and can attempt to use it in @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.vUgwYCf14LUD3zDG]{Savage Descent}. If not, they will have to find another way into the Pathways, but can follow up with the residents of Storsa's Strand at the end of the quest.
Strand of Fate.soverview: The party arrives at the small hamlet of Storsa's Strand, a sleepy fishing settlement on the shores of Lake Mithra. They need to uncover more details about the fallen adventurer, Aberin Lowd, by finding his father. If they convince him to help, they can learn of a mysterious passageway nearby that leads down into the Pathways.
Strand of Fate.sexposition:
As you make your way into the small town, it sounds quiet. Too quiet. There's a lack of breeze and a heaviness that settles on your shoulders that seems unnatural - a stillness in the air that holds more tension than peace.

Other than the feeling of weariness and malaise, the town is a typical Arcturian hamlet, filled with modest homes and an inn called the Far From Home that proudly advertises "FAMOUS FISH PIES - NOW WITH MORE SPICE!" on a wooden sign. The only oddity is a very large earthen and metal bowl filled with flames that seem to dance more than they crackle.

A young woman walks towards the bowl of flame almost reverently, unlit torch in one hand and softly glowing bag of items in the other. Nearby, a villager struggles with a heavy crate of fish. While both keep their heads somewhat down and shuffle more than they walk, the struggling villager does their best to raise a hand in greeting while keeping the crate balanced on their shoulder.

Hello travelers and welcome to Storsa's Strand. Have you come with news about Aberin?
Strand of Fate.ssummary: We reached the small hamlet of Storsa's Strand, following the journal we found on Aberin Lowd's body. We managed to convince his father, Kendral Lowd, a local fisherman, to tell us where we could find the Shrouded Borehole, located in a cave in the mountains next to the hamlet.

Snarled Promises.name: Snarled Promises
Snarled Promises.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is a social event that introduces, for the first time, an Outer God, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.dapPg66vgvLnwgcp]{Vhismara}. This particular entity is known by many different names but should be called the Snarling Voice in all interactions with the party.

  • This event triggers if the party moves towards the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion} location.

  • During this event, if any party members attract the voice's attention, they receive the @UUID[Item.UzWm9Z3Pk71idDmY]{Beast Mark}. This will impact their interaction with @UUID[Actor.d0mSoQozEIKozWVe]{Luxaroth} while within the Primordial Bastion and with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2xYjHyT4HVr6CiIC]{Spectra} at the end of the quest in @UUID[.gJZicCkQfXe0XzYN]{Magic Incarnate}.

  • Characters can reconnect with Mioroth if they [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer mioroth]], but only for a moment.

Voice from Beyond

While interacting with an Outer God would typically break a mortal's mind, the Snarling Voice is a faint manifestation of Vhismara's true power. While it might cause some immediate damage, the voice can't do lasting harm to any of the party members at this time.

Howling in the Darkness

The Snarling Voice that rips into your mind seems to echo within and around you, and there is a howling in the distance, as if a great pack of wolves hovers nearby. The voice snarls once more, dripping with menace.

Strange little creatures.. hurrying this way and that, so curious, so... delicious…

As the words linger in your mind, the voice falls silent and a profound sense of terror claws at your brain. Although the voice has finished speaking, it has not departed and appears to be awaiting a response.

Understanding the Snarling Voice

The main choice that the party must make is whether to speak to the Snarling Voice or avoid the conversation. While the party does not have the ability to truly comprehend the voice, they can discover the following:

  • With a successful [[/check arcana 16]] check, they sense that there is something beyond the mundane about the Voice, but it is not any form of magic or power that they are familiar with and is deeply corrupted.

  • With a successful [[/check insight 16]] check, they know that the Snarling Voice is interested in them, and might be willing to offer power or knowledge, but at a great cost.

  • With a successful [[/check history 16]] check, they know that others have had encounters with similar voices in the past and describe being "marked forever" by the experience.

Speaking with the Snarling Voice

If characters choose to speak with the Snarling Voice:

  • Vhismara is an Outer God, and their voice in any character's mind is bad… very bad. It causes a great deal of pain and mental anguish; the longer that the conversation continues, the more the characters' health can be damaged and/or levels of exhaustion can be gained. In addition to the damage and exhaustion listed below, you may wish to

  • Characters pursuing an evil playthrough or attempting to amass Abyssal attunement may wish to converse with the voice for longer in an attempt to gain knowledge or power. This would be considered an acceptance of Abyssal evil. As a result, the party cannot engage with Mioroth in @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.A5AegdhUty9ISa1P#mental-shielding]{Mental Shielding}, even if they [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer mioroth]].

  • If the party asks the Snarling Voice directly what it wants from them, read the following:

    Nothing.. everything! Yes.. everything you have… the veil is so very thin here.. a window into the hidden ones little world.. She thinks she is beyond me, safe.. but she IS WRONG!

    I see it clearer now, I have her scent, I prowl through the darkness, ever searching.. oh how I love to hunt.. scents, smells.. HUNGER.. oh how I hunger.. I smell such delights from.. oh.. from you.

All party members who speak to the Snarling Voice must immediately make a [[/save con 18]] or take [[/damage 2d8+5 psychic]] damage. In addition, whoever asked the question immediately receives the @UUID[Item.UzWm9Z3Pk71idDmY]{Beast Mark}. All other party members must also succeed on a [[/save wis 16]] or they receive the @UUID[Item.UzWm9Z3Pk71idDmY]{Beast Mark} as well.

  • If you wish to roleplay further, the Snarling Voice can and will answer any questions posed by the party, but its responses make little sense — the only commonalities are its sense of hunger, and its deep fascination with the party members.

Ignoring the Snarling Voice

If the party members decide not to speak with the entity, try to run from it, dispel it, or otherwise attempt to ignore its voice, you may read the following. This is the only way to truly avoid any meaningful consequences, and if the party refuses to speak to the entity, they will not be marked.

A chilling snarl followed by a hoarse, insane howl of laughter can be heard as the voice drifts away from your mind; "next time, perhaps" you hear finally, and the presence disappears, leaving behind a furious headache and foreboding sense of dread that persists for hours.

In addition, if players [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer mioroth]], skip to @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.A5AegdhUty9ISa1P#mental-shielding]{Mental Shielding} below.

Mental Shielding

This section of the event can only be completed if the party [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer mioroth]] and chooses not to engage with the Snarling Voice.

The Snarling Voice howls and rages; the force of its attention brings you to your knees, and the vast darkness seems to swallow you as great fangs close in around you. Just as all seems lost, a vast echoing chime breaks the hold over you and the darkness retreats in a rushing torrent. The Snarling Voice that had latched onto your mind howls with rage as it fades away, replaced by a great calm that settles upon you.

"Ahh, my friends... what a terrible place to be.

@Embed[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw readaloud="Miroth's memory fades into view, but this time he is far from serene. His image flickers in and out of existence and a deep frown lines his face. Both of his hands are clenched into fists, as if maintaining his presence in this place requires significant effort."]

Talking with Mioroth

Mioroth's memory fades into view, though his image is flickering and his once calm demeanor is now harried and concerned. If the party asks what is wrong, read the following:

I cannot maintain myself here for long; this area of the world is rife with corruption, and it takes all my efforts to shield you at this time. I compel you, dear heroes, to carry on towards the ancient seat; there, perhaps, the light may grant me some respite to talk with you again.

A successful [[/skill insight 15]] check suggests that Mioroth is not only greatly worried but seems to be in pain. It is unclear whether this is due to the effort to shield the party members' minds from the voice or something else entirely.

Mioroth's image fades quickly, leaving the party members with no opportunity to ask additional questions.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

As the voice dissipates, or Mioroth's image fades, the next step is to approach the Primordial Bastion ahead and discover what lies within during the @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.mGkNxDXrFEXIyAag]{Lightless Halls} event.
Snarled Promises.soverview: As the party travels toward the structure within the corrupted section of the Mythspire tunnels, an insidious, snarling voice enters their minds, promising them great power and riches. If the party previously encountered and sided with the character Mioroth in the Over The Moon quest, they can encounter the figure again here.
Snarled Promises.sexposition:
As you trudge towards the massive structure ahead, a feeling of utter terror and panic washes over you, as if a predator has just caught your scent. The light from the Bastion above seems to flicker, and in an instant, its glow appears extinguished. Darkness flows around you like a wave, and you feel like you have been suddenly transported to another place entirely, a black glitters realm of stars and an empty void of nothingness, even though your feet remain in the caverns. A low, impossibly deep guttural growl resonates among the twisting rocks.

Ahh, what have we here... a creature of flesh?

The creature snarls its words eagerly, as if savoring each one with deep pleasure. You can feel an alien power twisting against your senses and trying to corrupt your mind, so evil and vast that it takes your breath away.
Snarled Promises.ssummary: We encountered the Snarling Voice in the deep, blackened and Abyssal corrupted area of the Pathways. Its whispered words were so utterly.. wrong.. that will felt deep pain from even hearing its words.

Magic Incarnate.name: Magic Incarnate
Magic Incarnate.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this Social event, the party can explore the Librarium and encounter the Elder Goddess Spectra herself, a surprising encounter with a being as old as the cosmos and with much to say regarding their encounters with the Abyss on their journey to Ordain.

  • Spectra will be interested in the Party's encounter with @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Writhing Whisperer} from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon} quest.

  • Spectra will give the party more complete information about the Abyss if they completed the @UUID[.LyNcEPtA6HA1XvQZ]{Bastion Ruins} event from the @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi]{To Fall and Fall Again} quest.

  • Spectra will also speak briefly about the@UUID[JournalEntry.skQcdBxw8K0AS7hv]{The Bleak Archive} from the @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush With Death} quest.

Chapters 3 & 4.

This event is currently placed at the end of the Fall and Fall Again questline. It ties up a few loose ends and answers some lingering questions. However, it's likely this event will eventually be part of a breadcrumb for the next quest in the Abyssal storyline called Terror Below.

Roaming the Librarium

The party can explore the Librarium of Spectra, perhaps intending to find an acolyte or follower, or they might rummage through the stacks of books in search of answers.

Researching Subjects

The Librarium is filled with knowledge from across Ember, some of which is ancient, dating back to the founding of the city, while some of its books and scrolls are even older, having been brought here from distant lands. For any scholar or researcher in the party, it offers a treasure trove of information. However, it is also poorly organized, and spending any amount of time here can lead to hours slipping away quickly and without warning.

Many scholars and researchers can be found crammed into corners, and some are happy to engage in conversation with the party, albeit briefly. They mostly specialize in arcane and obscure subjects, but the party may uncover one or two who share relevant and interesting information that may assist them. Within the Librarium the Players can search for specific knowledges. This section does not need to be a one time event, and the players may wish to return here another time to research again.

Aedir Research

Any character who succeeds on on a [[/skill investigation 16]] or a [[/skill history 16]] specifically looking for Aedir knowledge unearth the following, characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have advantage on this check.

  • The Aedir were present on the Arctus Plateau beyond a few outposts. According to legends, they even built a strong vibrant city upon the headwaters of one of its major rivers.

  • Result of 19+: In the first section of a battered journal, a long-dead member of the Anachraenum Mirrium Jorcurlos, details their discovery and the exact location of an Aedir lost city said to be far to the south of the Forest of Stone. They followed the river that drains from the area toward the ocean. However, most of the journal is faded due to water damage.

  • Result of 24+: The latter section of the journal of Mirrium Jorculos is more accurate and while most of the pages are blank the location is said be:

    Carved into a great crescent cliff of stone, it is nestled atop the waterfalls of the river Herelion.

Gods Research

Any character who succeeds on on a [[/skill investigation 15]] or a [[/skill religion 15]] specifically looking for God knowledge unearth the following, characters with [[/knowledge gods]] have advantage on this check.

  • Many gods of the Nineteen, whom the people of the Arctus Plateau worship, are said to visit the great city of Ordain in disguise. Some of them have favorite spots where they like to spend time among their followers or take in the city's metropolitan airs.

  • Result of 18+: The character encounters a priest of Katu, studying weather phenomena and charts. He informs the party that ancient Katu and his small family of Shard Gods reside upon a floating island, which for the last several hundred years has been discreetly anchored off the southeastern Arctus Plateau, far from any trade routes, roads, or well-traveled paths.

  • Result of 20+: The priest of Katu accidentally lets it slip that the Shard Goddess Raineka adores Ordain and spends most of her time in the city; her favorite spot is... Then the priest realizes that perhaps he should not share such information with strangers and hurries off.

Magical Research

Any character who succeeds on on a [[/skill investigation 13]] or a [[/skill arcana 13]] specifically looking for Magical knowledge unearth the following, characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on this check.

  • Ordain has always been a city surrouned by magical forces, but the Ordani people have never been great wizards and there is no academy or place where wizards specifally gather together expcet in this very building. But they are few and far between.

  • Result of 19+: The character finds a battered and tired looking Wizard nestled deep into some books and while initially wary if the character is also a wizard and succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 15]] check the now friendly wizard teaches them the spell @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ImlCJQwR1VL40Qem]{Arcane Eye}.

  • Result of 24+: The character assists the weary wizard for one hour. During this time, they develop an unusual rapport, and if the character also succeeds in [[/skill insight 16]], they gain insight into the nature of magic and the intricate, interwoven fabric of reality. The wizard, who reveals themselves to be none other than the Star Mage Eveis Brightstone in disguise, teleports away, leaving behind a scroll of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.fVbCxFRaORalHB20]{Scrying}.

Shent Research

Any character who succeeds on on a [[/skill investigation 14]] or a [[/skill history 14]] specifically looking for Shent knowledge unearth the following, characters with [[/knowledge shent]] have advantage on this check.

  • The Forest of Stone and the Wedgelands of the Arctus Plateau contain many ruins from the Shent culture. However, these ruins represent only a fragmented fraction of the culture as a whole and are the remnants of distant outposts on the periphery of a civilization that controlled nearly the entire remote Shana Mountains.

  • Result of 18+: The character meets a scholar who is convinced by a rumor that there is an ancient Shent ruin hidden somewhere in the mountains above the Bloodwoods, north of Ordain. Many seek its treasures, but it has yet to be found. The scholar is searching for more information and no additional clues.

  • Result of 22+: The character learns that a specific magical incantation is needed to reach the Shent mountaintop temple of lore. Though they don't quite discover the incantation, they discover among magical writings a page containing fragments related to the ruin, and a hidden message that reads:

    Under moon, under sun, the fire burns brightest, basking stone in radiant light.

Once the party has investigated the Librarium with some satisfaction, read the following.

Navigating through the overwhelming stacks of books and strange arcane devices, you come across a hidden alcove in the back of the building, where a large stained crystal window casts red, blue, and dazzling orange light across the chamber. In the centre of the room stands an awe-inspiring figure of myth.

A Cosmic Being

The woman standing among stacks of books is the Elder Goddess Spectra. She is a friendly, approachable entity, and while she may not hold every answer, she is eager to help and answers as many questions as she can, albeit with some cryptic responses. If the party includes a Cleric of or followers Spectra, they recognize her immediately.

@Embed[Actor.xCPKIKhMrVO6iljg]

While her dazzling appearance and aura clearly indicate that Spectra is a being of great power and influence, her presence in this dusty, tucked-away library is somewhat surprising. Nonetheless, she speaks to you all with warm and flowing tones, as if she has known you your entire lives.

Why, greetings! As canny and vibrant a group of eager young heroes as I ever saw! I see from your apparel that you are all adventurers of keen minds and some skill. What brings you to this little library today?

Speaking with Spectra

Spectra comes across as an excitable, earnest, and bright person who is genuinely happy to meet the party. She has vast knowledge of many different subjects, from magic to creatures, history, science, and people. However, she tends to babble a little bit, and it's somewhat difficult to get a straight answer from a direct question.

If any character succeeds on [[/skill arc 11]] check, they will likely experience something of an explosion in the person's mind as the raw power emanating from the entity in front of them rocks them backward with unbelievable force. Her passive aura is not damaging, nor blinding, and it feels warm without causing any issues with characters' overall temperature.

Spectra appears earnest and upfront, but it's very hard to read her intentions. A successful [[/skill ins 20]] check notes that while she is honest and forthcoming with her answers, she will not reveal sensitive information to the party, either because she wants to protect them or because she doesn't quite understand their motivations just yet.

The party can continue their conversation with Spectra for some time, during which time he provides additional information:

  • She often appears here in this library, as it is a lovely place to read and relax where no one bothers her without a desire to discuss interesting topics. Her presence here is kept somewhat secret; at least, no one tends to advertise it. But she often moves around the world and may not be here the next time the players require her aid.

  • Spectra adores those who can practice magic and has nothing but kind words to say to them.

  • She is even friendly with evil characters to some extent, and although it's clear she knows of their nature, she tends not to be too dogmatic. Even if a character is clearly a necromancer or a caster of dark magic, Spectra doesn't skip a beat.

She greets any Cleric of Spectra with excited and warm regards, bearing on giddiness, and will jump up and give them a warm embrace, asking if they have been doing well.

"Oh my dear, it is lovely to see you again! I hope the world has been kind. How are you faring? Are you eating well? What is this you're wearing? Isn't it lovely!"

Note: While Spectra is an Elder Goddess and an extremely old and powerful being created during the creation of the Cosmos itself, she is not a particularly active participant in events and she is not omniscient. She is more of a passive observer that can be irritatingly cryptic at times. She is friendly and happy to chat with the party about the arcane nature of reality if they wish to get into specifics, and will be particularly fascinated with Wizards and Sorcerers, but she tends to push people towards seeking the answers themselves if asked direct questions.

Are you really the Elder Goddess Spectra?

Oh yes, in the flesh! Ordain is such a wonderful location for experimentation and analysis, with all these lovely records and extensive research into… hmm, well, it's mostly clothing, design aspirations, and different ways to write trade agreements while maintaining favorable and profitable positions within the political landscape of the city. But isn't that fascinating!

About the troubles in Ordain

Ahh I have not been paying attention really, has something been happening in the city recently then?

About Magic

Ah! Yes! I am the Goddess of Magic, and all facets of the arcane flow through me! Magic is like a hidden thread entwining the forces of our cosmos, woven into the fabric of reality, accessible only to those who dare to seek its elusive embrace! It is the dance of unseen forces, carefully coaxing motes of energy from spaces hidden, the whispers of ancient knowledge, and the art of shaping the very essence of existence. Magic is both a key and a lock, a bridge and a chasm, a riddle waiting to be unraveled! Even I will never truly master the arcane; it's simply unattainable, but that's part of the fun.

Spectra will then wink at the party and tap her fingers together playfully.

About the Abyss

Spectra closes the large book in front of her and sighs heavily.

Regarding the most pressing matter, yes, you have indeed encountered the influence of the Abyss. I can sense it on you, and it's not a good sign at all. I'm sure you have many questions, but please understand that while I will endeavor to provide you with the information you seek, I cannot offer you extensive knowledge of the Abyss.

She pauses and taps her finger against the cover of her book slowly. The nature of the Abyss itself is not only a source of unimaginable power and a rabid, uncontrollable ability to destroy everything it touches, but it is also an insidious force that seeks our utter annihilation. Giving it attention, attempting to understand it, and so on, merely feeds it and draws it closer to our world. While the Abyss may have touched you in various ways, the more you know, the greater the danger, and the more likely you will be destroyed or driven insane.

About the Writhing Whisperer from Over the Moon

Ever since the Abyssal Shear, there have remained monsters of the foulest, more evil kind hidden in the darkest corners of our world. This thing you speak sounds to be like an entity from the Abyss itself and left alone; it would cause untold destruction in time.

About the Shattering

It is not a subject I wish to discuss; it is not a fond memory, but suffice it to say the Cosmos suffered greatly until my sister stepped in.

About Alar (Her Sister).

Spectra will tilt her head backward and smile.

My sister is a treasure! I saw her only a century ago and she looked determined and as willful as ever! I believe she was investigating something about the Shattering, but we didn't talk about the matter for long.

About the Bleak Archive

That place was older than you know; the Shent were wise to lock some of those things away. I always liked the Shent; they had a great handle on things.

About the Bastion

There are ages of this world that extend far longer than the times before the Shattering. While the Shent, whom I'm sure you know, were an ancient culture that lived in the mountains to the north, the Giants themselves originally came from below. Although they are not quite as old as I am, they once shaped what you call the Pathways and encountered the Abyss, battling its influence to their ultimate downfall. The Bastion is one of their remaining legacies, still standing after all this time.

If the party was able to work with the Luxaroth and save the Bastion, Spectra will say this:

Your actions within the Bastion are highly admirable, if not heroic, and I believe you may be exactly what this world needs to confront the horrors of the Abyss. If you wish, I will impart a blessing to you. It will remain active indefinitely and will provide you with a small protective ward against the Abyss in your future adventures.

Spectra's Blessing
