Should the party accept Spectra's Blessing, each party member is given a permanent new feature called @UUID[Item.sFMqeMvy84TK0Kc1]{Spectra's Blessing}.

About the Snarling Voice

Spectra will peer carefully at the party.

That... is something you should ignore. I cannot stress enough that speaking more about this, or giving it any further attention, is damaging to reality itself.

About the Beast Mark

Spectra stares at it for a while, seeming to gather herself slightly, and for the first time in the conversation, she appears entirely at a loss for words. After a moment, she sighs and looks away. As I said, giving Abyssal entities attention is extremely perilous, and no, I cannot remove that from you. Doing so would only fuel that thing's attention further and likely draw attention onto me, which... well, it would not be good. The only person who can remove that from your flesh is my sister, Alar. You'd best seek her out soon, and please don't talk to voices in the darkness, for Ember's sake…

The party can finish their conversation with Spectra at any time; it is ultimately up to the GM whether she appears here again outside of quest events, as she tends to teleport around the world a fair amount.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once this quest is finished, there are still mysteries to uncover regarding the Abyss, as well as many unanswered questions. As the party progresses through the main story and the following side quests, much more will be revealed…
Magic Incarnate.soverview:
The troubling encounters with the Abyss and the warnings of growing danger in the region are unsettling, but with the vague directions to find someone who can help in the Scholars Nook district, the party arrives to discover whoever this person might be and seek their wisdom.

Here, they encounter the Elder Goddess Spectra herself. Spectra is one of the few who listens, understands the party's concerns, and is equally worried. She gives the party her blessing and more information about the Abyss depending on which quests and events the party has completed up until now. She informs them that she is distantly aware of further Abyssal influence in the Arctus Plateau, and the threat is far from over.
Magic Incarnate.sexposition:
Navigating through the Scholars Nook district of the city, the party comes across a grand yet clearly old and somewhat dilapidated building with a large faded name written across the mantle above the large double doors. The "Librarium of Spectra" has seen better days, but the occasional scholar or robed officiant passes before you, head down and buried in papers or books.

Inside, the Librarium is secluded and mostly empty, where loud sounds are muffled, turning into soft whispers. A few scribes, scholars, or worshippers can be seen reading intensely among the books. The pervasive smell of old musty paper lingers as heavily in the air as the drifting motes of dust, visible through sunbeams from the windows.
Magic Incarnate.ssummary: We encountered the Elder Goddess Spectra herself within the Libarium of Spectra in the Scholar's Nook of Ordain! She was able to give more information about our terrible encounters with the Abyss.

Phantasmal Waters.name: Phantasmal Waters
Phantasmal Waters.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event occurs if the party attempts to cross the Lake of Whispers which sits in the middle of the Fogbound Caverns to reach the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion} on its southern bank.

  • As they cross the deep waters, they are attacked by the @UUID[Actor.IZ1XuA12PN7L7DYE]{Pale Whisperer} and its many tendrils, which combine to create a larger and more powerful variant of the Writhing Whisperer from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon}.

  • Unlike the previous Whisperer, this monster is not interested in communication or dialogue with the party. It attacks immediately, surging from the water and surprising the party.

  • The characters can gain 1 point of Heart Attunement if they defeat the Pale Whisperer in combat (each character).

The entity within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.CPBGxUJqmL8o4XsG]{Lake of Whispers} is an ancient and lingering Abyssal monster that notices the party as soon as they enter the lake, as its telepathic ability lets it sense the minds of beings around it.

A Pale Whisperer

Characters with [[/attunement emberAttunementAbyss]] feel the oncoming attack before the Pale Whisperer breaks the surface; this is not enough time to prepare, but it may give them a split-second warning. Read or paraphrase the following once the area map is revealed.

The calm, dark waters of the lake explode around you as writhing tendrils reach out for the wooden edges of the raft. You feel a roiling, twisting sensation in your chest, and as you recoil in horror, a bulbous, milky shape rises out of the water beside you, accompanied by the sensation of a thousand invisible insects crawling across your skin.

@Embed[Actor.IZ1XuA12PN7L7DYE]

@Embed[Actor.zLzpZYINc9KHFrTd count=3]

Abyssal Intrusion

If this is the first time the party has made contact with a Whisperer, the encounter has an immediate deleterious effect on the minds of the party. All characters must make a [[/save wis 16]] saving throw as the Whisperer makes telepathic contact with them and begins to weave itself into their minds. On a failure, the character suffers a single effect from the @UUID[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X]{Minor Abyssal Madness} table.

If the party encountered the @UUID[Actor.fvLM77PBiD61hcLN]{Writhing Whisperer} in the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOverTheMoon]{Over The Moon} read the following additional text.

The creature before you appears to be a more formidable or perhaps more mature variant of the impaled being you found in the Forest of Stone. While the similarities are striking, this one moves with a sense of malice and shows little interest in engaging in elaborate conversation.

If the party spends any action or time trying to identify the Whisperer they will be unable to learn anything of note, the being defies all attempts to identify or understand it.

The Writhing Interloper

Neither Arcana, History, nor Religion are helpful in identifying the Writing Whisperer. It is beyond the ken of most mortals of Ember, and its kind have not been witnessed by mortal eyes for centuries, if not longer.

Fighting the Whisperer

The dark water of the Lake of Whispers is a challenging environment for any party member, and it is more than deep enough to swim in. Throughout the encounter, it's likely they will fall or be pulled into the water. Although cold, the water itself inflicts no penalty apart from the normal disadvantage on melee attacks for anyone without a swim speed.

Whisperer Tactics

The Whisperer is intelligent, and well versed in fighting mortals. It focuses on drawing enemies closer to it using its various abilities so that it can hold them in place and whip them to death with its tendrils.

The Whisperer uses its @UUID[Actor.IZ1XuA12PN7L7DYE.Item.cqmNO2NcN1Iso0Zr]{Abyssal Whip} ability whenever it's available, attempting to drag creatures close. If it can, it will attempt to whip and drag creatures before attacking with its @UUID[Actor.IZ1XuA12PN7L7DYE.Item.SmEqi818eKoBWt1v]{Shadow Tendril} so that it has advantage when it does.

Its @UUID[Actor.IZ1XuA12PN7L7DYE.Item.i2727Xttc3fllgRG]{Abyssal Whispers} legendary action can be used to draw enemies closer, and should target the farthest enemies on the battlefield. Its guaranteed damage is also effective at downing already weak enemies, and the Whisperer is intelligent enough to target weak and dangerous enemies.

The @UUID[Actor.IZ1XuA12PN7L7DYE.Item.SWwrvPuTbWvYwuyt]{Grasping Form} legendary action is useful for holding nearby enemies in place. This is especially useful if the Whisperer has dragged primarily ranged combatants such as rangers or casters into close range. It also prevents wounded characters from fleeing to (relative) safely.

The encounter also includes 3 @UUID[Actor.zLzpZYINc9KHFrTd]{Pale Whisperer Tendril} s. These are connected to the main body of the Whisperer underwater but can move and act independently, each with their own initiative. These smaller tendrils have only a single attack action and a basic goal to attack the closest creature.

Once the Pale Whisperer has reduced to zero hit points it slips back into the dark waters of the lake. There may be some questions regarding its actual death, as the party will not be able to investigate its body. In fact, the Pale Whisperer is not dead and has simply retreated for the time being. It will sink deep into the Pathways to regenerate and will appear again elsewhere another time.

Heart Attunement: Slay the Whisperer

If the party manages to defeat the Pale Whisperer in combat, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 fallAgainWatersWhisperer]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Having survived attack by the Pale Whisperer, the party may continue their journey south towards the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.mGkNxDXrFEXIyAag]{Lightless Halls} event that occurs there.
Phantasmal Waters.soverview: If the party attempts to directly traverse the space between the entrance to the southern Mythspire Tunnels and the Primordial Bastion, they will have to enter the waters of a lake within the Pathways. This will prove a dangerous choice as long tendrils emerge to drag party members into the depths of the waters.
Phantasmal Waters.sexposition: The small makeshift raft you've had to build to cross the lake seems dwarfed by the inky blackness of the water around it. The dark waters of the lake are nearly deathly still, with no ripples from the wind or movements in the air. It appears that the lake drops into utter darkness. While it seems as if some kind of current is circulating from further down beneath the surface, only the faint splashing and quiet movement from your own actions can be heard over the silent and extremely unsettling waters.
Phantasmal Waters.ssummary: As we crossed the dark waters of the lake in the heart of the Fogbound Caverns, we were attacked by a pale terrifying monster. Its thick, tentacled arms tried to drag us down into the depths below.

Smoldering Shelter.name: Smoldering Shelter
Smoldering Shelter.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is a social event with potential combat that introduces the party to @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A]{Nadin}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Choose to accept Nadin's offer to turn off the Light at the top of Bastion. In return, Nadin offers gold and a powerful relic, promising that it will boost the power of anyone who holds it.

  • Fight Nadin, though she will vanish upon reaching 0 hit points and is likely to overpower the party. If she defeats them, she will leave them unconscious rather than attempting to kill them.

  • Gain 1 point of Ragen Attunement for defeating Nadin in combat (each character).

Studying the Tent

Characters can stop and investigate the tent before entering or choose to leave without heading inside.

The tent before you is a strange structure, one that appears to be ancient, with unsettling designs and fading rippled red and black patterns weathered and worn by uncounted years. A thick black smoke rises from the top of the tent and fades quickly in the darkness above. Softly burning red braziers are scattered outside, lying carelessly in places with deep dragging furrows in the ground leading from the tent entrance.

@UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A]{Nadin} calls the Smouldering Tent home, but this tent is not a permanent fixture of the Fogbound Caverns. Instead, it is a wondrous magical artifact in its own right, capable of moving through space to distant locations whenever Nadin wishes.

What the Characters See

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 14]] or [[/skill arcana 14]] check while studying the tent notices the following. Characters with [[/knowledge abyssals]] or [[/knowledge artifacts]] have advantage on this check.

  • The tent is exuding Abyssal energies and magic and feels deeply wrong.

  • The fabric is clearly old and has seen better days. It has been torn and weathered by great age.

  • There is something magical and near undetectable in the smoke flowing from the top of the tent. This same smoke trails along the ground like a slow tide, coming from beneath the tent and its entrance. Whatever effect the smoke is causing does not appear to be dangerous at first, but you likely shouldn't breathe it in for too long.

  • Result of 17+: The tent has not been in this part of the Fogbound Caverns for very long. While the fabrics are worn and old, the ground around the tent has been recently disturbed, and a faint aura of conjuration magic hums around the tent like a shroud. It's clear that the entire tent is, in fact, magical in some way and may even be a singular magical artifact.

Reveal the following to party members who succeed on [[/skill perception 16]] skill check:

As you linger near the tent, the coughing and hacking noises become clearer. It's a dry, rasping sound that makes you feel uneasy, as it seems both uncomfortable and painful. Whoever or whatever is inside the tent is likely humanoid, as amidst the dry coughs, you hear a low murmur- either they are conversing with one another or someone is talking to themselves.

A successful [[/skill arcana 16]] check of the braziers around the tent reveals that they are exuding an extremely faint magical energy. The magic is not abyssal in nature — at least not entirely — but you detect residual signs of conjuration magic. Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on this check.

Smouldering Black Smoke

When a character spends more than 10 minutes breathing in the black smoke within 5 feet of the tent or directly inside, they begin to suffer adverse effects on their health. Characters other than Nadin or Abyssal monsters must make a [[/check con 16]] saving throw, taking [[/damage 1d4 poison]] on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one, with a minimum damage of 1. Creatures that fail the saving throw additionally become poisoned for one minute and develop an uncontrollable dry cough.

Keeping track of the exact time of this hazard is optional. Instead, the GM may choose to inflict this upon the characters randomly or once they have spent significant time within the smoke talking to Nadin.

Meeting Nadin

If the characters choose to enter the strange structure, describe the following:

The interior of the tent is stifling and hot, filled with more of the thick black smoke that stings your eyes and is almost overwhelming to inhale. A dark, rich wooden floor is strewn with a collection of red patterned rugs, rags, and piles of crumbling and ancient manuscripts. Across the walls, suspended from thick black chains, are several blackened, spiked weapons that seem twisted with cruelty and capable of inflicting great pain. These weapons seem to be part of a personal collection, all crafted by the same disturbing artisan. At the center of the tent is a large black brazier, with ever-burning red coals burning within, glimmering through the smoke. A hunched figure stands, shrouded at the back of the tent, facing you.

@Embed[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A]

The woman's rasping voice cuts through the smoke, landing not only in your ears but also in your mind.

Ahh.. a merry band of adventurous types I see, stumbling around…

She pauses to cough and hack into the air, her figure twisting as if in great pain, and her limbs tremble with the exertion. But she recovers quickly and finishes.

In the dark…

Her mouth twists into a strange, unsettling smile and she turns her head slowly to regard each of you.

Did my curious abode pique your unending curiosity perhaps?

She laughs with a loud, rasping cackle, and her long-fingered hands twitch and curl before closing into tight fists. She seems to wrestle with control over her own actions.

So now lovelies, by all means, ask for my story, my wisdom and the blessings of my dark goddess.. I will answer you truthfully and reveal so many wonderful things to you…

Talking with Nadin

The party can continue their conversation with Nadin, during which time she provides additional information:

  • Nadin is a follower of a goddess known as the "Red Eye," guided by her will. She has devoted her entire life to this deity and doesn't remember her age or origins. Deeply committed to this entity, she regards her chosen goddess with adoration but is not actively trying to persuade her party members to follow the "Red Eye."

  • If asked about her appearance or mask, Nadin will respond that she can see the party using the eye on her hand and that she is not blind. If questioned about her ancestry or whether she is human, Nadin simply laughs and exclaims, "Certainly not!".

  • Nadin is very careful with her words and refrains from providing the players with additional names or terms that might cause them long-term mental harm. She avoids saying the word "Abyss," preferring to use "Dark Beyond." Although Nadin is aware of many dangerous Abyssal monsters nearby, she does not share any details with the party, as she wants them to confront and test themselves against such horrors.

  • If the players point to the weapons hanging from the chains on the tent's walls, Nadin will gesture toward them and remark that they are hers, acquired long ago from a friend for whom she "did a favor."

  • If asked about her tent, Nadin will confirm that it is not merely a tent but a magical artifact in its own right—something she deeply treasures as her home. She notes that it has its own temperament and is rather sensitive to loud voices, advising the party not to shout.

If the party ask want she wants from them or why she is here in the Fogbound caverns, read the following:

Ah, to the heart of the matter then. Yes, I'm here now, but I was elsewhere. I came to investigate the fading light of the Bastion… It has stood eternal for millennia, but it’s beautifully dim now!

In fact, that brings up a rather exciting… cough… opportunity. If you examine that old dilapidated ruin for me, explore its ancient, lightless halls, climb to the apex of the tower, and ensure that the blasted light is dimmed permanently… you will discover a fitting reward when we meet again. I shall offer you treasures, such as gold, of course, and even more thrilling, a relic of my own—something I guarantee will bring you more power, glory, and joy than anything else in this world… what do you say, lovelies?

If the party agrees to her terms, Nadin offers the characters [[/award 100gp]] and a powerful dark relic when they meet again in exchange for "turning off the lights." Though Nadin does not specify what this relic reward is, her eyes dart to one of the many black weapons on the walls of her tent.

[[/outcome accepted]]

If pressed for additional information, Nadin has some direct responses for the party, detailed below.

Nadin's Motives

A successful [[/skill insight 17]] check suggests that Nadin is serious and forthcoming in her intentions. Although she appears unhinged and profoundly affected by Abyssal energies or powers, which makes her seem very suspect, she is not lying to the party but rather concealing certain things for their own sake.

  • Result of 20+: Nadin is deeply fascinated by the party and seems strangely interested in them; she has no intention of harming anyone.

Any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} spell on Nadin is met with inconclusive results, a swirling tapestry of confusing images that are impossible to read.

If the party ultimately refuses Nadin's offer and chooses to leave, Nadin watches them depart with a grin. She has no desire to stop the party or desperately try to convince them. Nadin is confident she will approach the party again with other offers.

Making Accusations

If the party accuses Nadin of being an agent of evil dark powers or a servant of the Abyss, she will not deny it. In fact, she will grin and confirm that she is exactly as they say, but that doesn't mean she is their enemy. Nadin is refreshingly blunt about her own character, and the party might see this as an opportunity to attack her; in that case, they should skip directly to the Fighting Nadin section below.

The Abyss

The "Dark Beyond", as I call it, is a deeply mysterious place, home to ancient creatures and wondrous magic. I have studied it all my life and have even ventured into its depths on several occasions. However, it is not a place for the faint-hearted, and the experience has taken a great toll on me. I lament its dark and terrible reputation, for truly it can be monstrous, but there are aspects within that are so wondrous and filled with such beauty that it brings me to tears.

Her "Dark Goddess"

My wonderful teacher, my dark beauty, and the one I worship above all things. She is caring, compassionate, and filled with love. She exists within the dark beyond and is a being that I believe is simply misunderstood by some others. I follow her desires and goals without question, and she leads me here and there to carry out her will. What I do greatly depends on her, but she called me here to watch and learn most recently.

The Bastion

It's been there since ancient times; not even I know when it was built or what its true purpose ever was, but it's stubborn and enduring, I'll give it that. It should be a crumbling pile of rocks by now, yet it's filled with ancient secrets and treasures. Delving into its depths will surely be profitable, and to be honest, I'm rather curious about many of its aspects myself.

The Light

That "thing" is deeply wrong. A LIGHT?! in the middle of the lovely darkened pathways of this world. Silly, useless, irritating. Thankfully, it's been fading for years and finally seems to be giving up, but it would be dear to turn it off permanently, either by destroying it or flicking off the switch. I would be very grateful, as would my dark goddess, of course. It will plunge this area back into darkness, yes, but that is its natural state, and everything drawn to it will fade away, I suspect.

If the party leaves the Smouldering Tent peacefully, read the following:

As you move away from the tent and leave it behind you a faint hum can be heard. Within moments, the sound twists and quickens into a whining screech of metal on metal. With a thunderous crack, the blackened smouldering tent behind you vanishes in a flash of crackling light, leaving you alone in a cold, dark depression within the caverns, faint echoes reverberating around you.

Fighting Nadin

Combat with Nadin is not the intended outcome of this event, as Nadin does not instigate such conflict. She is curious and calculating, viewing the party as unwitting pawns to achieve her own goals and those of destruction and chaos. Even if the party provokes her, is rude, or is generally hostile toward her, she will not attack unless weapons are drawn and someone tries to hurt her.

It is not unlikely, however, that Nadin's persona, comments, and appearance will compel the party to attack her as obviously evil or malicious.

Nadin Tactics

@UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A]{Nadin} is calculating and careful during combat, at least to some extent. She will test the party and will try to gauge weaknesses or strengths. This might mean she randomly switches targets to attack the strongest martial character before turning to attack a healer or a mage. When she does attack, she will focus both @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.e4ciJOjCfRQ04a7d]{Gleeful Smash} and@UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.M5hNywzF6xRLJMiK]{Crimson Ray} on that one target for an entire turn.

Nadin will use her legendary action @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.Lo5Ar51DZ8PzHyNK]{Teleport} to move behind or next to characters in the party, attempting to hide from or stay behind more challenging party members.

She will also use @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.2d1ffJD6z7uG4AYe]{Innate Spellcasting} to cast @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.FmarGWklAAr42eDX]{Blindness/Deafness},@UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.sRB2yvl3kiTpt75F]{Confusion} and @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.bupUckHC92tDgV6p]{Fear} spells on characters she wants to remove temporarily from the fight in order to focus on someone else in the party.

It's nearly impossible to stay hidden from Nadin as her passive perception is very high, and she has @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.DcZ8kQJm4Ew7ZAr6]{Keen Senses}. If anyone in the party attempts to hide from her magically, she will cast @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.bffjgFEVhPXBqXkI]{See Invisibility} and target that character next.

Nadin's damaging abilities do not do lethal damage, as she will control herself just enough to stop her from landing lethal blows. However, once someone is knocked unconscious, she will happily pull a part of their spirit from their body and use her @UUID[Actor.0HebXoiBWhsTBH0A.Item.Umpd3dz5hGoTYDFc]{Create Abyssal Eye} feature. This may lead to a snowball effect where the party is quickly overwhelmed.

It is not possible to kill Nadin during this encounter, as she, along with her tent, teleports away if she reaches 0 hit points. This is unlikely to occur, as the battle is in Nadin's favor. She is both more powerful than the party and intentionally holding back, as her true intention is to observe and corrupt the party, not destroy them. Nadin will deliberately leave the entire party unconscious rather than killing them outright during their battle. If this occurs, the party naturally awakens after [[/roll 1d4]] hours on empty ground within the Fogbound Caverns. If the party does manage to overwhelm Nadin somehow, read the following:

Nadin's form shudders, her face splits open into a wide, cruel smile before she hacks into her palm. As she does, the tent around you begins to hum slowly with a strange sound. Within moments, the sound twists and quickens into a whining screech of metal on metal, and the patterns of the tent's fabric around you start to swirl in increasingly rapid movements. The air thickens with black smoke, and Nadin turns, straightening to her full height, as any semblance of combat, wounds, or ailments vanishes from her form. Her smile widens even further, horrifically stretching the skin as she softly whispers:

What a charming little group you all are… until we meet again, lovelies.

With a thunderous crack, Nadin and the blackened smoldering tent vanish in a flash of crackling light, leaving you alone in a cold, dark depression within the caverns, with faint echoes reverberating around you.

Ragen Attunement: Nadin Defeated

If the party defeats Nadin in combat, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 fallAgainNadinDefeated]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After the interaction with Nadin, whether peaceful or hostile, the party may be further compelled to reach the Bastion deeper within the caverns and the @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.mGkNxDXrFEXIyAag]{Lightless Halls} event which occurs there.

Nadin herself will not appear again to reward the party for some time, but she is a character who will play a role in further quests later in the game.
Smoldering Shelter.soverview: The party encounters a strange, seemingly inhabited structure in the middle of the Fogbound Caverns: a large red tent housing an even stranger figure within—the disturbing form of Nadin, a follower of the Outer God, Sha-Xotha.
Smoldering Shelter.sexposition: In a small gully hollowed into the stone before you, a blackened red tent sits in the darkness, its tattered fabric surrounded by fog. Thick black smoke curls in lazy whispers from underneath its edges and rises from a hole in the top, leaving and dry and bitter taste that lingers in your mouth. An almost imperceptible coughing can be heard coming from within the tent that trails off into silence.
Smoldering Shelter.ssummary: We encountered a strange woman deep in the Fogbound Caverns living in a red tent that had seen better days. She was not entirely lucid, and when she stretched out her hand, a crimson eye could be seen in the center of her palm.

Tormented Threads.name: Tormented Threads
Tormented Threads.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event and on-ramp to the Fall and Fall Again Quest, characters can examine the fallen body of the adventurer Aberin Lowd. In this event, the characters can:

  • Discover a request from Aberin to tell his father about his death and the location of his body.

  • Find evidence that Aberin spent time at Corpin Sanctuary to be healed from a growing madness caused by his adventures.

  • Locate a record of Aberin's travels, a @UUID[Item.3qOjY12SUpQXz96v]{Defiled Journal}, which radiates abyssal energy. Characters can use it to learn more about what Aberin faced, but will suffer consequences from the abyssal energy contained within it if they touch it or interact with it.

  • Gain 1 point of Abyss Attunement if they attempt to loot the Defiled Journal (one character).

This event has a much higher chance of happening if the party found @UUID[Item.HLuTRoOpNSmD3PTW]{Aberin's Medical Records} in Corpin Sanctuary.

Investigating the Overhang

If the party makes any movement towards the overhang, they immediately see the body of Aberin Lowd, slumped over against the rock face, and the message he scratched in the rock beside him.

As you step closer, the source of the glint is clear – a body of a young adventurer slumped against the rock, the metal of the breastplate gleaming slightly as it catches the light. It is hard to tell much about the body from a distance - whoever it is, they look to have been dead for some time, though their body is well-preserved and clearly of a kivahr. A book bound in an inky-black leather sits in front of the body in a patch of dark withered grass, and words have been cut into the rock above the adventurer's head: Tell Pa I’m Sorry. -AL

Examining the Body

A cursory examination of the body doesn’t reveal what happened to the adventurer. With a closer look, characters can learn the following.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 15]] check, characters can spot folded paper tucked into the adventurer's armor and a ring, the @UUID[Item.8L9rrnzA8fLIpCdP]{Inscribed Ring of Eternal Rest}.

    • One of the sheets is @UUID[Item.FAIY0mM4FxU52CK9]{A Note For Pa}, which asks whoever finds it to let Kendral Lowd in Storsa's Strand know that he is dead and where his final resting place is.

    • Another is a torn piece of paper from Corpin Sanctuary. If characters have seen @UUID[Item.HLuTRoOpNSmD3PTW]{Aberin's Medical Records}, they can identify it as a torn piece from that record. It lists dates from two seasons earlier and a series of treatments, all unsuccessful.

  • With [[/knowledge crafts]] or a successful [[/check history 14]] check, characters recognize the armor and clothing that the adventurer is wearing. It shows influences from both the Rustvar Valley and the Golden Flats, and likely comes from somewhere near the intersection of those 2 regions, close to where the party is now.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 15]] check, characters can see an ink-like blackness on the tips of the finger bones of the corpse, in the same color as the journal in front of them.

Aberin's Final Words

If parties use @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.I2LUSF5ogc7Bj62e]{Speak with Dead}, the corpse gives only mutters incoherently, but the following words and information can be discerned from what they say: Daelin, Storsa's Strand, and Borehole. Other than that, all they do is speak of is a light in the sky and apologize to Pa.

I tried to get back to the light in the sky, to find the way, to crawl through. I'm sorry Pa, I tried to find her. I did, I did. Through the borehole. Find Daelin. Go to that place and the light in the sky but no light on the ground and the darkness inside and I'm sorry, I'm sorry Pa.

The Mysterious Journal

If characters move closer to the journal, the decay on the withered grass beneath it seems to move slightly.

The grass around the book begins to shift slightly as you approach, and a thin plume of smoke that smells of rot curls up from underneath its covers.

Examining From A Distance

From a distance, characters can figure out the following. Characters with [[/knowledge abyssals]] or who have Abyssal Attunement have advantage on these checks and know without a check that this is an object of the abyss.

  • On a successful [[/check 15 arcana]], characters know that whatever is causing the book to smoke is not an effect of magic. It is something deeper.

  • On a successful [[/check 15 nature]], characters can tell that the grass immediately around the book is more than dead - it seems as if it has been permanently drained of all life.

  • On a successful [[/check 15 perception]], characters can make out the words on the front of the book, which say, in [[/language arcden]], "An Account of Aberin Lowd."

Direct Contact

Interacting with the journal directly causes ill effects.

  • Any spell used to interact with the journal (such as Mage Hand) immediately ceases on contact with it, as if forcibly rejecting it, and deals [[/damage 1d6 force]] to the caster.

  • If characters touch the book with an object, they find themselves unable to hold onto it, dropping it immediately onto the ground.

  • If characters touch the book with their hands, they feel a thick rot coat in the back of their throats as if they were choking and cannot breathe normally. If they put the book down, the effect stops, but if they pick it up again, they feel the choking once more. Any character who touches the book also gains a vulnerability to necrotic damage that lasts until their next long rest.

Your throat swells from the inside, as if some shadowy hand from within your own flesh squeezed tightly against your airway, slithering long fingers into your gut and clenching. Every effort you make to take in breath is a struggle, the air turning into a thick choking smog that grabs at your tongue and twists in your throat, as if it wants to make you speak its name.

Within the Journal's Pages

If characters hold and read the book despite the feeling of suffocation, they gain the following knowledge, but take a level of exhaustion from the effort. This knowledge can also be found in the @UUID[Item.3qOjY12SUpQXz96v]{Defiled Journal} in a series of entries:

  • Aberin Lowd once traveled with his sister, Daelin, his wizard father Kendral, and his cleric mother Jai through the Pathways, trying to bring the light of Lantyr and the wisdom of Spectra to the darkest corners of the Arctus Plateau.

  • On one particular trip, Aberin was on watch, but became distracted by a flickering light in the sky in the distance. While watching it, he wandered further from their camp than he intended, drawn back only by his sister's screams. Terrified, he fled instead of returning to help fight. When he made it back to Storsa's Strand, his sister was missing, presumed dead in the Pathways.

  • Wracked with guilt for his distraction and cowardice, Aberin pledged to either find his sister's final resting place or rescue her if she was trapped in the Pathways, but could not find a way back down.

  • Aberin was eventually driven mad by his continued attempts to reach her through a place he called the Shrouded Borehole, his mind so lost to the abyss that even Corpin Sanctuary could not help him. At this point, his journal stops making sense and is covered only with sketches and symbols and question marks.

Abyss Attunement: Defiled Journal Looted

The first character who attempts to take permanent possession of the Defiled Journal advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 fallAgainThreadsJournal]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event leads the party directly to the small hamlet of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.VmrcB6qB9wLVF9Sk]{Storsa's Strand}, where they can inform Aberin's father Kendral about his fate.
Tormented Threads.soverview: The party comes across the body of an adventurer lying beneath a rock ledge next to a journal that oozes with abyssal energy. The adventurer, Aberin Lowd, has a note that asks for his locket to be returned to his father in nearby Storsa's Strand. Looking through his journal is risky, but if parties manage it, they tell of his attempts to travel into the Pathways through the back of a cave called the Shrouded Borehole.
Tormented Threads.sexposition: As you pass a large collection of rocks surrounded by soft golden grasses, you spot a glint of metal against a pile of green clothing. Whatever waits there, it rests in the shadows of one of the rocky overhang, as if waiting or seeking shelter, but it does not move, still as the grave.
Tormented Threads.ssummary: We found the body of a dead adventurer named Aberin Lowd under a rocky overhang. Near her in the grass is an extremely unsettling journal that seemed to ooze with some kind of sinister aura.

Bastion Wreckage.name: Bastion Wreckage
Bastion Wreckage.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration and social event, the party can take a moment to breathe and investigate the damaged chambers before them, now feed from abyssal darkness. In this event the party can:

  • Study the bastion's inner chambers in detail to learn more about the First Giants and their history.

  • Encounter the ancient Shent Giant @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth}, who both warns the party of dangers to come and pleads with the party to help the restore and safeguard the light above. Mioroth during this event is deeply worried. Its clear the abyssal influence here is a terrible strain on him.

If the party has completed [[/eventState brushWithDeathArchives]] or [[/eventState overMoonTemple]], they have previously encountered Mioroth. Guidance is provided whether or not this is the case.

The chambers here were once the main living section of the Bastion, filled with a thriving civilization, before they were disrupted by war. If the party chooses to investigate around them, read or paraphrase the following text:

Between the twisted and broken ancient walls and piles of rubble around you, you have the sense that a terrible battle once occurred here, many centuries ago. Whatever happened in this place, much of it has been lost to time — bodies, weaponry, or sign of the people or creatures that fought against one another have long been ground to dust and drifted away.

Investigating the Chambers

Characters who investigate the ruins around them can determine the following. Characters with [[/knowledge abyssals]], [[/knowledge monsters]], or [[/knowledge forensics]] have an advantage on all checks.

  • With a successful [[/skill investigation 16]] check, characters can tell that the damage in the area was not all caused by the monsters of great power whose handiwork they have seen in the damage to the bastion elsewhere.

    • Result of 22+: Characters unearth the @UUID[Item.CIha88j0QaJvF247]{Skull of Merliota} artifact in the rubble.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 15]] check, characters can see damage marks on the stone. Characters who succeed on a [[/check history 15]] check or who have [[/knowledge warfare]] know that the stone was damaged by a large mace or club of some kind.

  • With a successful [[/check arcana 16]] check, characters can sense the use of magic here in the past.

    Truly ancient magic was unveiled here in eons past, and its lingering effect can still be felt. While most of the energies here feel dark and twisted, you are able to feel strong radiant energy as well, as if the corrupt entities were confronted with a power infused with a radiant light.

    • Result of 19+: Characters know that fire has melted some of the magical stone, suggesting the use of a powerful spell by a mage with great power

Flickering Memory

Once the party has finished investigating the ruins around them, a ghostly projection of the Shent Seer @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth} appears. Read or paraphrase the following text:

@Embed[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw readaloud="As the light flickers between the ruins and casts long shadows across the shattered halls around you, a form appears, bathed in radiance. This massive figure looms over you even as he sits with his legs crossed. Semi-translucent and seemingly constructed out of energy, strands of light and shadow evaporate off him constantly, forming flickers that fade in and out of existence. He is clearly distressed, exhibiting a worried expression, and his hands are balled into fists as if he is concentrating hard on maintaining his presence here."]

If the party has previously interacted with Mioroth in [[/eventState brushWithDeathArchives]] or [[/eventState overMoonTemple]] (and if, in [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer]] , they [[/eventState overMoonWhisperer mioroth]]), read the folllowing:

Mioroth's image is clearly far removed from previous interactions, and he appears deeply concerned.

Dark times are upon us, my friends, and I have little time. I can stay here only as long as the light above endures, but we may be at a tipping point. You must hurry ahead and assist the one who guards the relic of Lantyr. Repairing it will once again safeguard this part of the world. I must ask for your help once more in combating the evils of this world and beyond.

If this is the party's first interaction with Mioroth read the following instead:

The Shent image begins to speak in a tongue that makes no sense to your ears. Stranger still, the sounds seem to come from all directions but the one toward the figure. Eventually the words transform into ones you recognize, the sensation akin to slowly remembering something someone once told you.

Finally its words make sense:

This is a dark place you find yourselves in, heroes. My name is Mioroth and I must ask you for your aid in combating evil. Above you lies a relic of ancient days, a relic that hold back the powers from beyond. I must ask you to repair and aid the one who stands guard. Much of Ember's future safety hangs in the balance! Do so, and I will see you rewarded properly.

The Light Above

If the party asks Mioroth more directly about his request, read or paraphrase the following.

As far as I know, there are two great forces in this world that resist the destructive powers of the Abyss. The first is the Lifeforce of our world, the power imbued within Shard Gods and, in small amounts, within every creature or person, including yourselves. The second is Light, a blinding radiance of energy that repels the darkness of abyssal energy. The tower of this bastion holds aloft an ancient relic of Lantyr herself, yet it is fading. Without an external force to repair it, I fear it will break, and this part of the world will fall even further into the clutches of the great enemy.

He will also share the following information about the general area if asked. Full answers are detailed below:

Regarding the Abyss:

That term is best left unsaid. My people knew the dangers of even learning more about the space beyond our world. It also laid low the very first Giants who dwelt within the Pathways here and built this very structure. Alas, what happened after the making of the world marked my kind, and though we thought we escaped to the surface and built our culture anew, it happened once again as the Shent fell to darkness during the events you know as the Shattering.

Regarding the Beast Mark or the Snarling Voice:

I will not speak more of it, other than to say that it is a vast and terrible evil. You would do well to ignore it if you can and make every attempt to remove its attention from you if you have gained it. Only destruction and annihilation await those who dwell too deeply or try to uncover more about that… thing.

Regarding the Bastion:

It was built long before my time, though I know it was once a place of joy and celebration. A settlement I believe on the edge of a great path that led deep into the heart of the world. It became a battleground, however, where the first Giants fought one another in a great civil war triggered by the unleashing of dark powers and knowledge. It then became a bastion against the darkness and stood firm for uncounted years until very recently.

Regarding the one above:

He is a hero, a being not so different from myself, an echo of a once glorious people. Unlike me, however, he is not a memory or a ghost; while the light shines, he can act and defend it. Be wary of him, for he will tolerate no evil in his presence, but he is a resolute defender of all that is good in this world and a steadfast ally.

Regarding his flickering form:

My being and form are of no consequence at this moment. Though should you succeed here, I suspect you may once again be able to aid me, this time more directly. My existence is under threat from the rising darkness, just as this place is. While I still have some time, the darkness at my own door is growing beyond my ability to control.

Learning From Mioroth

Mioroth has considerable knowledge about the past, especially the Shent and the Shattering, but he is unwilling to go into great depth.

Mioroth's Information

During their conversation, Mioroth can reveal the following. With a successful [[/skill ins 14]] check, characters now that he is being honest, but is deliberately withholding information, and that he might reveal more if pressed.

  • He feels immense pressure to maintain his form in this space, as the Abyssal energies and darkness here significantly limit him and interfere with his ability to appear before you. The strain will become overwhelming soon, and the party has only a limited opportunity to ask him any questions.

  • He is a Shent Giant, different from the first Giants who built this structure. His people arose later, after emerging from the Pathways and building great cities in the mountains. While he can manifest in this place now, the events that transpired here in ages past are things he has only heard about in myths and legends. He has little firsthand knowledge of what occurred.

  • Mioroth does not eat, sleep, or breathe. If asked, he will confirm that he's neither undead, or a ghost, though, but refuses to elaborate any further on how he came to be, his abilities, or his purpose.

Learning About The Shent

When it comes to the Shent, Mioroth avoids providing direct information beyond things he believes most would have learned by now:

  • The Shent were an ancient nation and culture that fell during the Shattering. The Shent built many wonders in these lands and great cities upon distant mountain peaks but they are all long gone now, he is merely a memory.

  • The Kivahr and Keth are direct descendants of the Shent, which is why the Kivahr slightly follow their physical form. The Hulg'run predate both and were created by the Shent to be servants before gaining freedom and being treated as equals.

  • The Shent were wise, peaceful seekers of truth and worshipped the moons and cosmos of Ember. They also held great power of foresight and studied the Sea of Stars to such an extent that they foresaw the Shattering coming many hundreds of years before the events ultimately occurred.

Mioroth cannot be persuaded to change his mind or give up more information.

Concluding the Event

At the end of the conversation, Mioroth offers the party a place to rest before moving forward that is relatively intact and safe from attack, which they can use for a short or long rest. He then fades away, wishing them good fortune. He believes that once the orb has been fixed, they will surely meet again.

Next Steps

Whether the party has decided to take Mioroth's warning to heart, has accepted Nadin's offer and is committed to destroying or switching off the light above them, they move on to @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.LyNcEPtA6HA1XvQZ]{Shining Obelisk}.
Bastion Wreckage.soverview: As the party leaves the Lightless Halls and continues to move through the Primordial Bastion, they come across devastated and destroyed chambers, many of which seem to have been literally torn apart by colossal claws and collapsed into rubble. The light coming from the orb on the massive obelisk above glimmers through the ceiling, casting rays of light across the walls and floors. Here, the party encounters the Shent Giant Mioroth, but something is wrong with their image and they are desperately concerned with what is happening.
Bastion Wreckage.sexposition: In the ceilings and openings between the chambers above, the glimmering light of the orb on top of the central obelisk has seemingly banished the omnipresent darkness around you. In the dim light, you can see the way this area has been ripped apart. The impossibly hard and unmarred stone that seemed so resistant to age and damage elsewhere lies broken and smashed in heaps of rubble and debris, entire walls have collapsed, and the floors have been torn apart. Deep claw marks can be seen on the stone, as if a colossal rampaging beast were let loose in this area.
Bastion Wreckage.ssummary: As we passed through the bastion, we observed horrific damage to the structure and chambers. The Giant Mioroth then appeared and warned us about the failing Orb of Lantyr above, and that we must do everything we can to repair it. Mioroth also warned us that the strength of Abyssal forces in the region has been growing day by day and that something unknown is causing a buildup of dark and powerful energy in the area.

Lightless Halls.name: Lightless Halls
Lightless Halls.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is an exploration and combat event that takes place in the @UUID[Scene.emberLightlessHa]{Lightless Halls} area map.

This event is a large sprawling dungeon experience, set in the first area of the Primordial Bastion. The party must make their way through to the endpoint and unlock a huge fortified door to progress. In this event, the characters can:

  • Find a @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} by exploring the first part of the dungeon. This magic item holds back Abyssal Darkness, allows the party to light the channels in the dungeon, and unlocks the door to the enormous central chamber.

  • Survive the area's hazards, including various light-based and abyssal energy traps.

  • Fight off any Abyssal monsters that emerge from the darkness.

  • Gain 1 point of Signara Attunement for solving the Runekey Puzzle within the Lightless Halls (each character).

  • Gain 1 point of Heart Attunement for successfully cleansing the Gohema's abyssal remains (each character).

Ancient Beyond Measure

The structure of the Primordial Bastion is truly ancient, a towering stone edifice from the time when the world of Ember was being formed. Despite its age, the structure is in good condition, remarkably unblemished by the ravages of time.

The Bastion At First Glance

Before the party enters the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.Pp9sfdw0pK2GbV51]{Primordial Bastion}, and at any time while within the structure, they can investigate the building around them. If they succeed on a [[/skill perception 16]] skill check, reveal the following:

The breathtaking scale of the stones and structures immediately catches your eye; they were clearly crafted by Giants much larger than any you have ever encountered. A profound stillness surrounds you, a heavy silence that feels even more intense than the caverns behind you, but it is not entirely gloomy. There is a sense of calm, resolute fortitude woven into the atmosphere. Furthermore, you observe that no flora, such as plants, grows on the stones of the Bastion; not even a thin layer of lichen, moss, or fungi, as if the stones themselves are utterly sterile.

Taking a Closer Look

If anyone from the party investigates the stone blocks of the Bastion and succeeds on a [[/skill inv 14]] check, they know that the structure here is very different from anything they have encountered so far in the world. Anyone with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] has advantage on this check.

There is something very different about the nature of the stonework here: a seamless style of interconnecting blocks suggests a mastery of construction techniques, with most of the stone blocks likely weighing 100 tons, and some of the larger crossbeams twice or three times that weight. This was not created by the Shent, nor the Aedir, nor any known culture recorded by scholars.

  • Result of 17+ yields the following information.

    The huge stone blocks that makes up the structure are not really stone at all, and appear to be some kind of impenetrable metallic alloy. It is resistant to any damage you try to inflict upon it, even when using your full strength to strike it or attempting any magical attack.

  • Result of 20+ yields the following information.

    As you run your hands along the structure walls and clear away some of the dust upon the floor, you can feel damage on the strange alloy — deep, thin, almost imperceptible slashes that remind you of claw marks. There is no way to tell exactly when or how this damage occurred.

With a successful [[/skill arc 14]], characters detect an extremely faint magical aura coming from the structure itself. Anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] or [[/knowledge stars]] has advantage on this check.

  • Result of 16+ yields the following information.

    Whoever created this structure must have done so with magical aid; the stonework and materials exude a faint aura of enchantment. You can also sense that the structure is extremely old and surprisingly appears to withstand the passage of time without any degradation or fading of its magic. The structure feels warm to the touch; however, you do not sense any evil or malice, in fact, it feels natural, calming, and resolute.

Entering The Bastion

Once the party heads inside and begins to explore the Primordial Bastion, the full area walkthrough can be found here @UUID[JournalEntry.emberWalkLightle]{Lightless Halls}. One the party reaches the Inner Chamber and defeats the boss monster Gohema, return here for the next steps.

Signara Attunement: Solve the Runekey Puzzle

If the party manages to successfully solve the Runekey Puzzle, each character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 fallAgainHallsPuzzle]] at the conclusion of the event.

A Beast of Flesh and Darkness

After the massive monster has been destroyed in the inner chamber, its remain leave a stain on the stone around it similar to other Abyssal monsters that the party has faced. While it is not really possible to destroy these remains, the characters may attempt to do so, which yields the following effects.

Cleansing the Beast's Remains

Attempting to cleanse, destroy, or purge the remains of this Abyssal monster is a noble pursuit, but in the end, only something extraordinarily powerful can remove such a potent and magical entity from the world.

  • If characters attempt to consecrate the Abyssal remains by casting either the @UUID[Actor.fuL7YqC7eENDtHeJ.Item.BE6ec6v5AVnSxz2R]{Bless} spell or the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.xmDBqZhRVrtLP8h2]{Protection from Evil and Good} spell using the remains as the target (the remains count as a willing creature for the purposes of this spell), there is no effect.

  • If a cleric uses their @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.classfeatures.Item.r91UIgwFdHwkXdia]{Channel Divinity} ability with Divine Spark within 30 feet of the remains read the following:

    For a moment, nothing happens as the Abyssal Stain in the room seems to resist the energy. Suddenly, with a terrible echoing snarl of anger that reverberates loudly around you, the darkness retreats and fades further into the cracks of the stone. As the flesh remains melt further into thinness, receding from the godly power of lifeforce, you now see a glinting armband revealed in the darkness.

  • If characters attempt to use the @UUID[Item.mXk3nqy8QaqFVlQf]{Sun Star} by pouring some of its essence onto the remains. While this does not eliminate the stain, the darkness appears to recoil for a moment. All creatures within 30 feet must succeed on a [[/save dex 14]] saving throw or take [[/damage 2d8 necrotic]] damage as the remains burst apart, scattering stonework and flinging Abyssal matter and shards across the room.

Heart Attunement: Cleanse the Abyssal Remains

If the party manages to successfully cleanse Gohema's remains, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 fallAgainHallsCleansed]] at the conclusion of the event.

Band of Primordial Life

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check perception 14]] check or has [[/check perception 16 passive]] can see the @UUID[Item.YOuSwPClrmMdDAL5]{Band of Primordial Life} among the dark remains on the floor of the chamber.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill arc 15]] check are able to determine the magical nature of the Band of Primordial Life without needing to cast @UUID[Actor.MJfOzwa6uawHDhHA.Item.iCaiYRPxSxowvFJa]{Detect Magic} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify}, and are aware that it is a wondrous item, but can determine little else. Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] have advantage on this check.

  • Result of 18+: The bands, style, and runic lettering correspond to the Primordial Bastions, and this item was evidently consumed by the Fleshy Beast but was originally forged by the First Giants. It is deeply connected to the life energies of the world and is likely a treasure beyond reckoning for many.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Having made their way through the Lightless Halls, the party can move forward into the next area of the Primordial Bastion, advancing on the region map and triggering @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.PX0lktv1PWrPRMSR]{Bastion Wreckage}.
Lightless Halls.soverview: The party enters the massive structure of the Primordial Bastion and must make their way through the shadowy chambers on the lower levels, filled with traps, puzzles, and ambushing Abyssal monsters. Eventually, the party unlocks the way forward through a large fortified door, and they continue onward into the next area.
Lightless Halls.sexposition: The immense blackstone buildings and chambers of the complex stretch out before you — vast, unsettling, and surprisingly intact. As you approach the open entrance gate, a deep, unnatural darkness obscures any further details about the yawning void within. While this may have once served as a settlement or bastion for defense, the titanic edifice appears to have weathered countless years without any noticeable faults or cracks. It's also in far better condition than you would have expected — it does not appear to be ruined or worn by time, except for a thick layer of dark gray dust that covers what you can see of the floor ahead.
Lightless Halls.ssummary: We entered the first section of the Bastion Structure in the Fogbound Caverns, where we encountered terrible shadowy monsters and managed to unlock an ancient fortified door that led into the section beyond.

Torn Veil.name: Torn Veil
Torn Veil.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event on the Voidspan Bridge onboards players into the Fall and Fall Again questline if they have been traveling with Ankarist or reached the Pathways from the Mythspire Observatory. In it, players can see the echoes of a battle between a powerful wizard and cleric against the corrupting forces of the Pathways.

  • This battle took place between Kendral Lowd (a wizard currently living in Storsa's Strand), his then-wife Paravi (a cleric currently living in Ordain), and several Abyssal creatures. Following in their wake leads the party toward the nearby Fogbound Caverns.

  • Players who encounter this event after completing the majority of the questline in the Fogbound Caverns can gain additional insight into the life of Kendral Lowd before the loss of his family.

  • The effects of the battle have been partly shrouded by an unknown force. The nature of that exact force, and who is behind it, are still in development and will be revealed as part of future content.

  • Gain 1 point of Signara Attunement for managing to fully "recreate the battle" during their analysis of the scene (each character).

Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 15]] check or have [[/check perception 17 passive]] know that what they are seeing is real. Their vision has been altered by an unknown source, but what they are seeing is legitimately in front of them.

There is no way to stop the change in the characters' vision. @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.15Fa6q1nH27XfbR8]{Dispel Magic} and other anti-magic spells have no effect on the shift.

Shifting Vision

Before moving forward, characters can attempt to learn more about what has happened to them. Characters with [[/knowledge abyssals]] or [[/knowledge undeath]] have advantage on the checks below.

  • With a successful [[/check nature 16]] check, characters can tell that the change in their vision has not been caused by anything physical or natural.

  • With a successful [[/check arcana 16]] check, characters know that their shifting vision has been caused by an abundance of necrotic energy in the area.

    • Characters who succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence (History) check know that this amount of energy is highly unusual but sometimes found in places where either many creatures of the Abyss or one particularly powerful creature was destroyed, leaving a stain upon the world. This includes sites from the time of the Shattering where creatures from the abyss are known to have attacked Ember. This has been weaved together with echoes of powerful magical abilities to create a powerful lingering effect.

    • Characters who succeed on a [[/check survival 16]] check can sense where this area of necrotic energy is located. It hangs over the bridge, extending from one side to the other.

The Battle At The Bridge

A closer examination of the bridge can reveal what happened during the past battle.

Recreating the Battle

Characters can determine what happened on the bridge with a successful [[/check investigation 22]] check. Each success on one of the checks below lowers the DC of this check by 1. Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]] or [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on the checks.

On a success, characters know that a battle happened on the bridge between a creature of the abyss and a pair of combatants — a cleric of Lantyr and a wizard. The abyssal creature was mostly defeated and slunk across to the far side of the bridge.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 14]] check or [[/check perception 16 passive]], characters can tell that there are three different types of damage on the bridge.

    • With a successful [[/check arcana 15]] check, characters can tell that one set of gouges was created by a spellcaster casting both Fire Bolts and Magic Missiles. The blast marks are greater on the southern side of the bridge, suggesting that more creatures came from that direction.

    • With a successful [[/check religion 15]] check, characters can see that the pattern of the second set of gouges forms a protective symbol associated with acolytes of Lantyr. They are focused in the center of the bridge, as if presenting something from crossing over.

    • With a successful [[/check nature 15]] check, characters know that the third set of gouges are a set of claw marks from a large creature. More of them are located on the southern side of the bridge, suggesting more creature sin that direction.

  • With a successful [[/check survival 15]] check, characters know that the creature that left the gouges on the bridge was injured and backed away toward the far end of the bridge). The injuries were likely fatal to the creature.

Signara Attunement: Fully Recreate the Battle

If the party manages to fully recreate the battle by succeeding on 5 of the skill checks above, each participating character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 fallAgainVoidspanRecreate]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

If parties decide to explore the Fogbound Caverns and follow the path of the injured creature, they can proceed into the area, triggering @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.fVJBgl3XH6lCPdEy]{Twisting Shadows}.

If not, there are no direct follow-ups, though members of the party may be subject to whispers that allude to the events on the bridge if they trigger @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi.JournalEntryPage.R6Zuhq9eNi6m6zg8]{Discordant Whispers} during their travels.
Torn Veil.soverview: As the party moves across or discovers the Voidspan bridge for the first time, they momentarily see through a veil that seems to hide deep gouges in the ancient stonework and hints of a battle with some terrible foe that occurred here in the not too distant past.
Torn Veil.sexposition: As you cross the awe-inspiring bridge before you, a chill wind rushes up from below, followed by an unearthly echoing snarl. Before you, the bridge shifts slightly, as if you are seeing through a veil with a new set of eyes, revealing sets of long, deep gouges in the stonework across the length of the bridge.
Torn Veil.ssummary: We uncovered a strange magical veil laid upon a place called the Voidspan Bridge, deep in the Pathways. As we investigated, we discovered that a terrible battle took place there only a few years ago, with magical effects still swirling around it and a trail heading to the south.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This side quest occurs during Chapter 2 and begins once the party crosses paths with the aspiring agrimage, Edivel Sprout. There are no prerequisites for this quest and it can be undertaken at any time, although it is likely to be encountered if traveling with Sin while undertaking the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1] quest.

Difficulty

The "Thorny Predicaments" quest is designed for a party of Level 3 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest quest that awards 2 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the [[/eventState canyonsSideBridge]] and [[/eventState canyonsSideBlessing]] Events.

The party can begin this quest in a few different ways — they may cross paths with @UUID[Actor.hLvc42ruEEclRBCZ]{Edivel Sprout} as the aspiring agrimage attempts to get an errant spell under control, meet a pair of lost travelers who point them in the direction of the "seed settlement" Brevin, or stumble upon Brevin on their own. Each of these on-ramps eventually leads them to the pivotal event that kicks off the quest in earnest — Edivel's fall into the canyons as the result of an earth tremor.

If the party frees Edivel from where they are trapped at the bottom of the canyons, helping them escape the swiftly rising waters, the young wizard asks for help on their quest to learn the vineweaving spell they were trying to perfect when they fell. Edivel is convinced that the earthquakes have damaged Brevin's bridge and that this spell will help restore it.

To help Edivel, the party must venture through the creature-laden @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.FByC8hRZtRuAJgA8]{Bramble Gully} to retrieve the right spell component, get Edivel's spellbook back from a would-be brigand, the @UUID[Actor.qW0lhTVZLQknOayq]{Canyon Crawler}, and find the originator of the spell that Edivel is trying to learn, famed agrimage @UUID[Actor.FAWXlZTU8syDdRFy]{Kali Andrella}. Finding and talking to Kali is easier said than done, as she is barricaded in her home in the ruins of Steed's Point in the midst of traps, wandering jurtak, and aggressive gore birds. When not fighting the dangers of Steed's Point or the Canyons, characters have the chance to use persuasion and charm, first to set the Canyon Crawler on a more positive path, and then to help Kali Andrella decide if she should leave Steed's Point so that her mind is clear enough to help train Edivel.

With their primary mission with Edivel complete, the party returns with the agrimage to Brevin, where the bridge has indeed been compromised and is dragging the entire town into the canyon. With the vine weaving they've learned, Edivel is able to help, while the party provides support in dealing with varying crises caused by the rapid shifts of the town. Whether or not their combined efforts succeed in saving the Brevin bridge, their efforts catch the attention of the shard god Aythorn, who gives them a boon after blessing the town.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.HUIhXv1i0eywY5Q5]{Aythorn}

  • @UUID[Actor.hLvc42ruEEclRBCZ]{Edivel Sprout}

  • @UUID[Actor.FAWXlZTU8syDdRFy]{Kali Andrella}

  • @UUID[Actor.wI4zsTgX2eIy4VtQ]{Rattletrap}

  • @UUID[Actor.qW0lhTVZLQknOayq]{Carmin}

  • @UUID[Actor.AJuixWYxgoyEo3tf]{Triss Carpel}

  • Leini and Karao, a pair of Kithil adventurers

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.qW0lhTVZLQknOayq]{The Canyon Crawler}

  • @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Birds} and @UUID[Actor.ZuWduzUSGS6i4NZm]{Gore Bird Swarm}

  • @UUID[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl]{Gumtoads}

  • @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd]{Jurtak Hunter} and @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]{Jurtak Warrior}

  • @UUID[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE]{Ketral}

  • @UUID[Actor.sUYwQ8KqdxqyQOCV]{Sarracenias}
Overview.soverview:
At the edge of the deep and treacherous chasm known as the Splinter Canyon sits the small town of Brevin, a "seed town" that was grown instead of built and hopes to attract visitors to see its many natural marvels. Chief among them is the Brevin Bridge, a new vine and grass bridge that will cross the canyon and shorten the trip to the city of Ordain from the northern Arctus Plateau.

But not everyone is ready to celebrate. A young Thornling wizard who aspires to be a legendary agrimage is away on the Arctus Plateau, trying to master a complex spell from once used by one of their heroes. They are sure that if they get it done in time, they can earn a blessing from the shard god Aythorn, who is coming to celebrate the bridge unveiling. Then a sudden earth tremor during their pursuit of a spell component lands the Thornling at the bottom of the Splinter Canyons, whose waters are beginning to surge. Even worse, they are now convinced that without the spell they have yet to master, Brevin's bridge might suffer the same fate.

In "Thorny Predicaments" you will journey through the Splinter Canyons to help the aspiring agrimage gather what they need for their spell, dealing with the local creatures, environmental hazards, and unexpected attacks. Eventually, your journey leads you to an unexpected location - an abandoned town that has been overrun by monsters and whose remaining resident may hold the key both to the spell's success and the opportunity to save Brevin from a terrible fate.

Planting a Seed.name: Planting a Seed
Planting a Seed.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social and exploration event, characters are introduced to Edivel Sprout, a young aspiring agrimage, and can help them clear the path forward, which has been blocked by a slowly moving brambled hedge. In this this event the party will:

  • Get to know Edivel Sprout, his background, and why he's attempting to wrangle hedges.

  • Find out how the hedges came to be and why their presence is a problem.

  • Figure out how to move the hedges without destroying them, or if inclined, destroy them for good.

A thornling steps out from behind the hedge, dragging their partly-torn cloak behind them.

I'm so sorry, travelers! My spell appears to have gotten away from me. But no fear, Edivel is here! I know I can figure this out. Probably.

Actually … maybe you can help?

@Embed[Actor.hLvc42ruEEclRBCZ]

Edivel explains the situation at hand:

My name is Edivel, Edivel Sprout!

I was trying to figure out a vine weaving spell, to debut at the upcoming Brevin bridge blessing ceremony, and something went wrong. I waved my hands and said the words and suddenly the hedge in front of me was … well … doing this.

While the hedges are not an immediate threat, he wants to figure out what happened and take care of things:

I don't think this … whatever it is is trying to hurt anyone, but it is blocking the path, and it's my responsibility. There must be some trick to undoing it right?

Gathering Information

The brambles are the tangled mass of five awakened hedges that are incapacitated due to Edivel's faulty spell, though he isn't ware of this. Edivel is pretty sure that the spell can somehow be undone, but they haven't yet been able to figure out what exactly happened.

Edivel's Ambling Brambles

Characters can gather information about the situation with the checks below.

Edivel used a spell from their spell book. They can be persuaded to share the page in question with a successful [[/check persuasion 14]] or [[/check intimidation 14]] check.

Any character with the [[/knowledge plants]] can convince Edivel without a check.

The spell page reads "Vine Weaving" and has a series of complex drawings on it that seem to indicate ingredients and hand movements, along with a series of words. Several of the original drawings are half rubbed off of the page, though, and have been drawn over with more recent ink work and several question marks in the margins.

  • Any character that succeeds on a [[/check insight 14]] check, can deduce that Edivel was guessing at some of the spell and aren't sure if they figured it all out before casting. Edivel will also admit this if asked directly.

With a successful [[/check nature 15]] or [[/check perception 15]] check, characters can determine that the bramble is made up of five intertwined hedges. If successful, Edivel immediately realizes that they must have somehow awakened the hedges, though they don't understand why the hedges haven't attempted to communicate.

Of course! I was thinking of this as one creature, but it's at least three or four. And they look pretty impossibly tangled too. But why haven't they done anything more..interesting?

Characters who succeed on a [[/check arcana 15]] check know that the bramble has been magically awakened. If they have seen the spell in Edivel's spell book, they have advantage on the check. If successful, Edivel immediately realizes that this effect will last for 30 days and there's no way to use Dispel Magic on it. They don't understand what exactly they have awakened, though.

Oh, I see! I meant to have them weave, but somehow it made them wake. If I remember what Eamon Mariflor said in their correspondence class, that means thirty days of hedge aliveness and no way to dispel it. Usually I thought Awakened things had a bit more life though. This one just seems to wander.

Characters who study the behavior of the creature and succeed on a [[/check 15 investigation]] or [[/check 15 survival]] check conclude that all the brambles can do is move forward. If successful, Edivel immediately realizes that the creature is incapacitated, though not what it is.

You're right! This hedge thingy isn't doing much. Must be suffering from incapacitation. Bad on the battlefield, bad for the bramble. Not that it hurts them or anything. They just can't do much more than walk.

As long as characters have succeeded on at least one check, Edivel uses the information they uncover to come up with a plan to get the brambles out of the road by creating a magical fence.

I think I see what's happening now.

Five hedges, all tangled together, awake enough to move but not do much else. I don't think they'll hurt anyone, but it's not good to have them blocking the road.

I know what to do - I'll whip up a couple of post stones! They're pretty basic agrimagic, made to stop animals from wandering too far off from a farm. Sort of like an invisible fence. And that I know how to do.

While I get them ready, can you herd the brambles over to the left side of the road?

Redirecting the Brambled Hedge

The brambles can be redirected with a variety of following spells or approaches, or through other means which the Gamemaster approves.

Herding Brambles

With a [[/check nature 14]] check, characters know that a small amount of damage should get the brambles to move without killing them. They are also aware that hedges are afraid of fire and will move away from it.

  • Any contact with the brambles that does under 30 damage will get the brambles to move 10 feet away from the source of the contact.

  • Any fire, whether directly created or magical (via @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.MUO1uYN7JR1hm4dR]{Thaumaturgy}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.eCPQuQkIabFKTl9u]{Produce Flame}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.udsLtG0BugXHR2JQ]{Prestidigitation}, or similar) will cause the brambles to move 10 feet away.

  • Characters may use spells that directly move the brambles without harming them permanently as long as they do under 30 HP of damage (which destroys the bramble), such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.WTbOQBsarsL1LuXJ]{Thunderwave} or similar.

Once the characters have gotten the hedges to move 10 feet, Edivel's plan succeeds and they are corralled off by the side of the road, delighting Edivel.

That's perfect! They should be safe over here. And I'll come check on them, don't worry. In between tracking down what I need for my next try, that is.

Heart Attunement: Hedge Redirected

Any character who participates in redirecting the brambled hedge to bypass it advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 canyonsSideSeedRedirecting]] at the conclusion of the event.

Destroying the Brambled Hedge

Edivel is resistant to the hedge being attacked. If a member of the party readies a spell against it or raises a weapon, they attempt to block the hedge, saying:

Hey, you don't have to do all that - it's not the hedge's fault it got like this and it's not hurting anyone. I want to put it back, not blow the whole thing up.

Despite this protestation, Edivel won't prevent the party from doing damage to the hedge.

Characters can easily destroy the brambles, which have an armor class of 10 and 30 HP. If characters do this, Edivel is very unhappy about it, and characters have disadvantage on any charisma checks with Edivel or in their presence for 1 week.

You killed it. I was hoping you wouldn't do that. I mean, if I hadn't made it come to life to begin with, it would be fine now. I feel terrible.

Ragen Attunement: Hedge Destroyed

Any character who participates in destroying the brambled hedge to bypass it advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 canyonsSideSeedDestroy]] at the conclusion of the event.

Introducing Edivel

Gamemaster's Note

To represent the success at clearing the brambles, change the Vista Composition from Brambled Crossing (Blocked) to Brambled Crossing (Cleared).

With the bramble taken care of it, Edivel thanks the party for their help.

Thanks so much! I'm so glad you stopped to help. Though you must wonder what I'm doing out here hurling spells around.

Edivel's Ambitions

Edivel wants to be a great agrimage, like the ones they grew up idolizing. This walking hedge is a result of their latest attempt at agrimagic. Edivel is mostly self-taught - they are a wizard, but most of those around them who use magic are druids, so they've been collecting spells and information wherever they can find it.
