A successful [[/check insight 15]] check reveals that there is something about the situation that Edivel is holding back because they think it’s embarrassing.

  • If asked, Edivel denies it, but with a successful [[/check persuasion 14]] or [[/check intimidation 14]] check, they admit that they didn’t have all the components to cast the spell and made some substitutions, which may have caused the issue.

  • Edivel has figured out what to do next - they mistook one of the spell components and can get another one from Bramble Gully in Splinter Canyons.

The current spell Edivel is working on is a copy of a spell that was being developed by the famed agrimage Kali Andrella before her disappearance in the aftermath of the fall of Steed's Point. The page is a third-hand copy retrieved by a friend of theirs, Carmin, and is somewhat faded, so they may have cast it incorrectly.

Edivel has been pushing themselves hard because the shard god Aythorn, whom they deeply admire, will be at Brevin to preside over the opening of the new bridge. They really want to figure out the spell they’re working on and use it to impress Aythorn. If the party offers to help or accompany Edivel going forward, they don't think it's necessary but won't turn it down.

What were you doing?

Agrimage in training, soon to be the pride of Brevin, once I figure a few things out. Most of the folks in Brevin are druids, and I learn better from a book, so I'm putting my version of it together on my own.

About agrimagic?

Agrimages work with the land to make farming it easier. Could be anything from enchanting the soil to make the crops grow faster to weaving straw together into a ladder, to creating a fence made of flowers that keeps pests away. Agrimages tend to be a bit more focused on using spells to enhance everyday life.

We're not druids though, they harness nature's power, we're a traditional school of magic.

I know that may not sound like much compared to turning into a bird and everything, but agrimagic can mean a lot to people. There's stories of whole towns that wouldn't have gotten off of their feet without the help of someone like Kali Andrella.

About Kali?

Kali Andrella is only one of the greatest living agrimages on the Arctus Plateau.

At least I think she's still living.

No one's heard from her in a few years, but the spell I'm working from is a Kali Andrella original. Got it from my friend Carmin, who copied it from a paper they saw, so it's kind of third hand, but I'm sure it's pretty close to the real thing.

About Brevin?

Have you heard of Brevin? We're one of the new seed cities that's grown from the ground up instead of built. The druid who put it together, Moss Rivethun? Another agrimage legend.

Anyway, one of the big things we've been growing recently is a bridge, right across the Splinter Canyons, to make travel to Ordain easier if you're coming from the North. It's a big deal. So big that the shard god Aythorn's sent word that they are going to come and give a blessing.

A shard god. In my home town!

Which is why I'm practicing. Naturally I had to come up with something to impress, right?

About Aythorn?

I'm sure you've heard of Aythorn. Of all the shard gods, they're the one who tends to show up the most in the world.

Some say it's because they're full of mischief, or 'cause they just became a god not too far back, but I like to think they just enjoy keeping an eye on us and making sure we do well. And I'm going to do well by them.

Once I figure this all out.

What's next?

There's only so well a spell to go if you're not using the right components, right? Looking at the way these vines twirl around, I realized exactly the flower I need to match the sketch here in my book. And I know where to find it - Bramble Gully.

Getting there will mean a little climbing at the top of Splinter Canyon, but nothing I can't handle.

Can we help?

Edivel waves a hand dismissively.

Oh, don't worry about me! Between this cloak, my tough skin, and the kindness of strangers, I always find a way to make it through.

Hey, maybe I'll see you at Brevin? The bridge celebration ceremony is going to be amazing. Especially when I show off the final version of this spell!

Concluding the Event

As long as the party did not kill the hedges, Edivel is willing to mark the location of Brevin on their map. Mark the outcome Location of Brevin as completed if this occurs. This will reveal the location of Brevin to the players on the Region Map.

[[/outcome brevin]]

Next Steps

The party may choose to travel with Edivel on their quest, which brings them towards the Splinter Canyons and triggers @UUID[.Rkbb3FUjqyPdDLJx]{The Fall's Gonna Kill You}, head to Brevin to check out the upcoming celebrations in @UUID[.2Ve19KR8g04QGtSc]{Natural Wonders}, or proceed on their own through the Plateau, possibly encountering the travelers in @UUID[.onZv5ABkPkXMrrBz]{Revelers on the Road}.
Planting a Seed.soverview: When the party's path is blocked by a mass of moving vines, they turn out to be the work of Edivel Sprout, a Thornling wizard and aspiring agrimage who is attempting to master a magical vine weaving technique. They're hoping to impress the shard god Aythorn, who is coming to their village to give a blessing at the opening of a new bridge.
Planting a Seed.sexposition:
Around a bend, a large hedge of brambles blocks the path, stretching across the entirety of the road through the Arctus Plateau. Slowly, it begins moving forward, creeping in your direction as its branches grow more and more tangled. As it lurches in your direction, a small voice comes from behind it.

Oh no, that isn't what I intended at all — hello? Hello, if you can hear me, don't move. I can fix this, I know I can.
Planting a Seed.ssummary: We encountered a young Thornling, Edivel, whose attempt at mastering agrimagic had gone a bit awry. They're on the hunt for a mythical spell developed by the talented agrimage Kali Andrella, which they hope to show off at an upcoming festival in Brevin.

A Rising Tide.name: A Rising Tide
A Rising Tide.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party help Edivel from the agrimage's current position, trapped in the Splinter Canyons as the water rises. They can:

  • Locate Edivel in the Splinter Canyons in @UUID[.vnRwvPy99V7Z0HiK#finding-edivel]{Finding Edivel}

  • Help the agrimage get free from where they are trapped at the canyon floor in @UUID[.vnRwvPy99V7Z0HiK#freeing-the-agrimage]{Freeing the Agrimage}

  • Find a safe place above the rising water to figure out what to do next in @UUID[.vnRwvPy99V7Z0HiK#getting-to-safety]{Getting to Safety}

Once Edivel is free and the party is safe, the grateful thornling asks the party for help with their quest to recover their spellbook and master a new vine-weaving technique that could help Brevin's new bridge in @UUID[.vnRwvPy99V7Z0HiK#edivels-ask]{Edivel's Ask}.

Canyons Vista

The Canyons Vista for this scene has a more dramatic water surge than noted in the text - it will likely change in future.

Finding Edivel

Characters can't see Edivel from their position in the Canyons, but they can narrow down where the Thornling is.

Edivel's Location

Characters can locate Edivel's location by searching the canyons with a successful [[/check investigation 20]] check. Doing any of the following checks beforehand lessens the DC of the check by 1:

  • A successful [[/check perception 18]] to narrow down the origin of Edivel's echoing voice. If characters speak to Edivel again and/or get the thornling to call out to locate the echo, they have advantage on this check.

  • A successful [[/check survival 17]] check to look for signs of Edivel's fall and use it to figure out their likely trajectory after falling. If the party saw Edivel fall in @UUID[.Rkbb3FUjqyPdDLJx]{The Fall's Gonna Kill You}, they have advantage on this check.

  • A successful [[/check nature 17]] to narrow down what is around Edivel, if the party asks the thornling to identify any landmarks around them. Edivel doesn't have much information to share:

    I'm not sure - these rocks all start to look the same to me, if you know what I mean. I guess I'd say I'm between two larger peaks, in one of the more shadowed areas to the Ordani side. I wish I'd paid more attention when my buddy Carmin was trying to teach me tracking, I can tell you that.

If the party succeeds on their investigation check, they quickly locate Edivel in the canyons. If they fail the check twice, or don't attempt it, they eventually find Edivel, but face an obstacle during their search - roll on the Canyon Catastrophes table below for the obstacle.

@Embed[RollTable.xtUlzhr0LusL2Xkc inline rollable]

Freeing the Agrimage

Once the party reaches the agrimage, they find that Edivel is, in fact, stuck in place.

Edivel comes into sight as you round one of the Splinter Canyons' many winding corners, their foot wedged deeply into a narrow crack in the middle of the rock. "My heroes," the agrimage says, waving at you all and gesturing to their trapped foot.

Thank you so much for coming down to help! Usually, I can get myself out of trouble, but this time I was actually starting to worry about ending up under water.

The Waters Rise

From this point on, the party faces the rising water levels of Splinter Canyons. Each time the party does a check, roll a [[/roll d4]] and consult@UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh200.JournalEntryPage.k7VCz1HvCj134l0e#stage-1:-rising-waters]{Rising Waters}, going no higher than level 5.

Freeing Edivel

Characters can assess Edivel's current condition with a successful [[/check medicine 17]] or take a closer look at the crevice the agrimage is stuck in with a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check.

  • A success on either gives them advantage on any attempts to help Edivel move. With a success on both, they have advantage and the DC of all checks to help the thornling move lowers by 1.

Characters can carefully remove Edivel's foot with a [[/check sleightofhand 17]] check to free Edivel or pull Edivel free with a successful [[/check athletics 17]] check.

  • If either check fails, Edivel is wrenched loose and takes [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] and they can only move at half-speed until healed and all water level checks should be made as if with disadvantage (roll for the water level change twice and choose the lower number of the two for the effect).

Getting to Safety

Edivel may be free, but the waters have continued to rise, blocking the path that the party took down to the canyons.

Thank you for coming to my recue, friends! Now maybe I can help you. I 'm not sure how you got down here, but if it's back that way, there's no good way through. But don't worry - I've got a way out of here that keeps all of our feet dry.

Edivel gestures to a rock at the edge of the still-rising waters.

If we can get up there, we should be safe from the water for now - it never gets up that high. Once we're above the water, I can thank you properly, and maybe you can help me figure out what to do next?

Climbing the Rocks

The characters can use the below checks to attempt to get to an outcropping located 20 feet above the rising water. As above, the water levels continue to rise.

With a successful [[/check survival 17]] check, characters can use their knowledge of the terrain to find a series of handholds they can use to climb up, and can bypass any other checks to reach the outcropping. Characters with a climbing speed have advantage on this check.

Characters may use any spells that will lift or propel them out of the water, or that will help them to make the climb, such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.KJRVzeMQXPj8Gtyx]{Spider Climb}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.MRxldJd6C4bsBo3O]{Levitate}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.yfbK8gZqESlaoY5t]{Fly}.

Characters who climb without handholds or other assistance must attempt a [[/check athletics 16]] check to make the climb. Any character who uses a climbing tool has advantage on the check.

  • On a success, they begin pulling themselves out of the mud and water, and must succeed on a [[/check acrobatics 15]] check to stay steady as they climb. If the acrobatics check is failed, they fall, taking [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage, making the rest of the climb without incident.

  • On a failure, they must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 17]] to attempt to grab onto something as they slip back down to the water and mud below. If the save is failed, they take [[/damage 1d10 bludgeoning]] damage. If the save succeeds, they take half the damage. They make the rest of the climb without incident.

Edivel's Ask

Once the party has safely made it out of the canyon waters, read or paraphrase:

You clamber up onto a slightly higher section of the canyons - still far from the Golden Flats above, but safely away from the water that has rushed into the bottom section of the canyons. No sooner have your feet touched the ground than Edivel grins.

You were amazing back there! Real adventurers, like in the stories. And just when I need help - if I don't figure out how to make my vine weaving spell work, Brevin could be in serious trouble.

Edivel's Request

Edivel wants the party to accompany them as they attempt to master their vine weaving technique. They can share the following information:

  • They lost their spellbook, which drifted downstream. It is enchanted so that they can locate it, but they want to make sure they stay safe in the process.

  • They need a specific flower from Bramble Gully, an upstream section of the canyons that used to hold the Thornling community that moved to Brevin.

  • They need to master the vine weaving technique now because they believe the earthquakes may have weakened the still-growing bridge that Brevin is opening in an upcoming celebration - their technique might help shore up any damage.

  • They believe that Brevin's Steward, Triss Carpel, will reward the party if they help Edivel - Triss has a soft spot for them.

What do you need?

As you can maybe tell, I have a bit of a habit of getting myself into trouble… and usually I get back out again! Eventually, anyway.

Usually I'm not in any hurry, but now? I need to figure out my vine weaving technique before Brevin unveils the bridge, and that means getting my spellbook back from downstream and the flower I need for the spell from upstream.

If you're with me, I might have a shot to get it done in time.

How does this help?

If you'd asked me before I fell down here, I would've said I wanted to impress Aythorn, show off how good an agrimage I can be.

Now though? I'm worried that these earthquakes might cause trouble with Brevin's new bridge, and maybe even Brevin itself. Maybe I'm wrong, but if I'm not, I need to do something right?

About Bramble Gully?

I used the wrong flower for the spell the last time I tried it - it's one of the reasons it went all wrong. Luckily, Bramble Gully's got tons of different flowers - the Thornlings who used to live there were big on flower displays and they left most of them when they moved on to Brevin. I know what I need will be there.

About the Spellbook?

The spellbook got away from me when I fell. I've got about 10 enchantments on it, so it should be safe and I can track it, but I still have to head downstream to pick it up and hope no gumtoad's stuck to it or anything like that.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The water has reached its peak and is now beginning to pick up speed. The party can decide to go upstream to find the flower that Edivel needs in Bramble Gully, leading to @UUID[.wayoxatxc7P06K0t]{Growing Pains}, or head downstream in search of the Thornling's spellbook, leading to @UUID[.q3RclLggX8rF6npb]{Supplies and Demands}.

Either way, they may must face the waters during their travels, making their way through the canyons in @UUID[.QmC0z4DS80SLsqD2]{Fighting the Current}.
A Rising Tide.soverview: The party locates an injured Edivel in the Splinter Canyons, which have begun filling with water due to the recent earthquake. The water is calm, but threatens to submerge Edivel if they can't get free.
A Rising Tide.sexposition:
You hear Edivel's voice before you see them.

Friends? Friends, is that you! I could use your help here if you can - my foot is stuck in a crack and the water's really starting to rise.

Their voice echoes as it bounces off of the canyon walls, making it hard to pinpoint exactly where it is, but two things are certain - it is coming from somewhere ahead of you and it is getting increasingly hard to hear over the sound of water rising into the canyons from points unknown.
A Rising Tide.ssummary: We helped Edivel get free before they were swallowed up by the rising waters in the canyons. They've asked them to accompany them as they try to master a spell that could help Brevin's new bridge stay stable.

Revelers on the Road.name: Revelers on the Road
Revelers on the Road.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, characters run into a pair of travelers, Karao and Leini, who have gotten turned around trying to find Brevin. In this event the party will:

  • Help the pair get their bearings and figure out the way to Brevin.

  • Learn a little bit about the travelers.

  • Experience a tremor, and learn that they are becoming more common in the Arctus Plateau.

Speaking to the Travelers

Karao (kithil kivahr, he/him)

Calm, and reserved, Karao tends toward introspection and carefully considered action, contrasting with Leini's enthusiastic desire to act first and think never. He seems to have an infinite well of patience, and often serves as as a moderating force for Leini's impulses.

Leini (kithil keth, she/her)

Possessing a mind prone to wandering into often nonsensical tangents, Leini is eccentric to put it mildly. She makes no effort to explain how her thoughts flow from one to the next, but is happy to share them with any stranger she meets in her travels.

If a character is [[/culture emberKithil]], Leini is especially excited to see a fellow kithil adventurer. Her response varies based on time of day.

If it is night:

Of course! I should have known a fellow kithil would be basking in the moonlight the way that we are.

I know that part of going off Sunning is to experience other cultures that live under the harsh gaze of Lantyr before settling down, but we try to do as much traveling under the moons as we can, even now.

You seem much more experienced, though - not just off Sunning for a season like we are before heading back to your village but adventuring full time. Any way you can help us?

If it is day:

A fellow kithil!

You look too experienced to just be Sunning the way we are, getting your time out under Lantyr's punishing light in order to learn from other cultures before returning to a sensible kithil village to live under the moonlight.

Perhaps you're better at keeping track of where you are under Lantyr's gaze, can help us find our way?

The pair of Kithil are Sunning, a kithil tradition of going out to explore the world during the daylight before returning to settle down for nocturnal life in a kithil village.

Reading the Kithil

An [[/skill insight 15]] check confirms that the two are simply lost and have no negative feelings towards nor pose danger for the party. Speaking to the pair, they can share the following:

  • They are heading to Brevin for the celebration of its new bridge. Leini will be helping a friend, Temi, with her shop, while Karao is hoping for a blessing from Aythorn, who will be in attendance.

  • Shortly after crossing the Ordani Skywalk, they were waylaid by a mysterious robber calling themselves the Canyon Crawler, who demanded they leave most of their supplies and map behind.

Where are you going?

Karao gestures vaguely in a direction, seeming unsure where to point.

We're trying to find Brevin.

I don't know if you've heard of it, but it's one of those settlements grown from seeds, and they're getting ready to unveil a vine bridge that stretches all the way across the Splinter Canyons.

Leini here is helping her old friend Temi with her shop during the event, but I'll be keeping my eye out for Aythorn - they're known to give out blessings at special occasions, and who wouldn't want to be blessed by a shard god?

If we get there in time.

Getting lost?

Leini explains:

It happened so fast. We weren’t more than mile or two away from the Ordani Skywalk, on this side of the Canyons, when someone we didn't even see swooped up out of nowhere and attacked us.

Lucky they didn’t try to kill us.

You were attacked?

Karao nods, and says:

They didn’t seem too interested in doing real damage, honestly. Just threw out a bunch of threats and grabbed at our feet with vines until we agreed to leave our stuff behind. Including our map. And called themselves…what was it, Leini? The Canyon Crawler? So keep an eye out.

Finding the Path

Without a map, Karao and Leini don't know where Brevin is exactly, but they know that it has a bridge that will be going across to Ordain, so it must be near the Splinter Canyons. They just don't know how far north.

The Way to Brevin

Characters who have the [[/eventState canyonsSideSeed brevin]] can mark it on the travelers' map, and give them effective directions. Alternatively, a character with [[/knowledge trade]] can easily give the travelers directions from where they are. Otherwise, characters can use any of the following checks to help the strangers figure out the direction of Brevin:

  • A successful [[/check nature 16]] check while surveying the land nearby would reckon that a seed city could viably grow in the northern region of the Splinter Canyons.

  • A successful [[/check history 16]] check would know a bit about the seed cities, including that Moss Rivethun created one for a community of Thornlings in the northern section of the Splinter Canyons edge.

  • A successful [[/check survival 16]] check while looking at the dirt map that the travelers have drawn allows a character to compare it to the landmarks nearby and make an educated guess about Brevin's location.

If characters succeed on any of these checks, they successfully give Karao and Leini the information they need. They can also mark the location of Brevin on their own map.

If characters are able to help Leini and Karao, the two are grateful and begin gathering their stuff to head in that direction. If they are not able to help the pair, Leini and Karo thank them for the effort - they're sure that they'll figure it out or stumble over Brevin eventually.

A Sudden Tremor

As characters are leaving, or at any point at the GM's discretion, a minor earthquake moves through the area.

Triggering the Tremor

Mark the Minor Tremor outcome of this event as completed to trigger the earthquake tremor effect.

The ground shakes slightly, as if it was being tugged back and forth and up and down, jolting the two travelers and shaking you from below. Wherever you try to place your feet, the ground seems to move away from them, and only your own balance and the things around you are there to try to keep you steady. The two travelers from Ordain look much worse for wear, jerking back and forth as they try to keep their feet.

A Minor Shake

Characters must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw to stay upright during the tremors, or they are thrown to the ground and take [[/damage 1d4 bludgeoning]] damage.

In the aftermath of the shaking Leini peers over at the map scrawled into the dirt and says:

At least our map is still standing! It's probably time for us to use it and get moving, before things start shaking again.

Karao dusts off their legs and picks up their bag.

Agreed, these tremors always leaves my legs wobbling. Feels like the last few years they've been getting more and more common. I was hoping we'd be done with all the quakes and shakes, but apparently not.

Well, thank you for your help, we're going to be off! Safe travels!

Leini waves and begins walking off, Karao following after a moment later.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party can either head to Brevin, triggering @UUID[.2Ve19KR8g04QGtSc]{Natural Wonders}, or go off on their own, likely eventually triggering @UUID[.Rkbb3FUjqyPdDLJx]{The Fall's Gonna Kill You}.
Revelers on the Road.soverview: A pair of adventurers who have gotten somewhat turned around after falling prey to a robber are heading to the upcoming bridge blessing celebration in Brevin and need help finding their way. While the party is talking to them, a minor earthquake tremor affects the area.
Revelers on the Road.sexposition:
A small camp has been set up by the side of the road. Two travelers — one tall and gray, the other small with a tattoos on their arm and a mask covering their face — have drawn a rudimentary map in the dirt right at the edge of the road.

The taller traveler says, just at the edge of your earshot:

I'm sure it's north, Leini

The shorter one replies:

I'm not saying it's not … I'm just saying it's also west. North and west.

Spotting you, the shorter traveler turns and waves.

Hello there! Name’s Karao. This is Leini. Quick question, do you know the way to Brevin?

Karao gestures to the ground.

As I’m sure you can tell from our attempts at a dirt map, we’re a little bit lost.
Revelers on the Road.ssummary: We ran across two lost travelers and felt a minor tremor shake the ground of the Arctus Plateau.

Growing Pains.name: Growing Pains
Growing Pains.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this combat event, the party must make their way to the spell component @UUID[Item.FXNnFGmbtvZrJEhq]{Everbloom} (a colorful flower found on an Everblooming Hedge) on the far side of the area while confronting two sources of danger:

  • Gumtoads and Sarracenias, which lurk within the center of Bramble Gully.

  • Ketral and Cave Wasps, found upon the rocky slopes or within cavernous areas.

Note: The Everbloom can sometimes be difficult to spot on the map - it is an all-white flower in the Southeast section of the map, immediately below the ledge with the broken wheel.

The Path Through the Canyons

The bush containing Everbloom that Edivel needs to reach is on the far side of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.FByC8hRZtRuAJgA8]{Bramble Gully} from where the party begins, and cannot be reached by returning to the Golden Flats above.

The Way Forward

Edivel immediately offers a path forward.

I know this looks impossible to get through, but there's a path. We stay in the middle of the Gully, winding through all these plants, and we should find a way up to that ledge. If we're lucky, it's a quick walk. If we're unlucky…well, that's why I asked you all to come along.

They can also share the following:

  • There are dangers on the path ahead, mostly in the form of creatures that may attack in Bramble Gully. If characters ask about these dangers, they have advantage on perception checks while in the Gully.

  • The flower is called an Everbloom, and can be used as a spell component when others won't work. Edivel is sure this will make their spell a success.

  • Edivel can't guarantee that their spell will save Brevin, but believe it could be of help if the earthquakes continue to rock the region.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check insight 16]] check can confirm that Edivel is being truthful, telling the party everything they know about the flower and the region. They are nervous, but only about something going wrong with the plan.

Dangers of the Gully?

Oh, there's plenty here that might want to kill you. Gumtoads jumping down from the canyon walls, ketral trying to take a finger off while you're climbing, plants with an appetite. Just the kinds of things adventurers are ready to tackle, right?

The Flower?

The flower is called an Everbloom. From the Everblooming bush, naturally. Despite the name, they're not the easiest to find on the Plateau, which is too bad - their petals can work in spells that normally require very hard-to-get ingredients. It's exactly what the vine weaving spell needs.

Why doe the Flower Matter?

The Everbloom flower on that hedge over there is the flower that I need to make the vine-weaving spell work. I don't know that it will save Brevin exactly, but with these earthquakes, any spell that can pull things together is a good thing.

Crossing the Garden Path

The Garden Path is a relatively flat area made up of leafy bushes and grasses punctuated by sprays of colorful flowers and vines that snake partway up the canyon walls.

The area ahead of you is broad and flat, though it is hard to tell exactly how level the ground is beneath the intertwining greenery of the bushes and flowers. Above, the canyon rock is still a muted brown, but there are traces of color where vines and flowers have grown partway up the rocks, rustling slightly where they sit against the canyon wall.

The movement of the vines on the canyon walls is due to the presence of 2 Gumtoads, each perched on a different low outcropping. Further in the gully, a third Gumtoad waits. In addition, there are 2 Sarracenias hidden among the plants on the ground.

Scouting Ahead

Characters are aware of the Gumtoads' presence with a successful [[/check perception 18]] check or [[/check perception passive 20]].

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check perception 21]] or [[/check perception 23 passive]] are also aware of any Sarracenias within 20 feet of them.

@Embed[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl count=3]

Gumtoad Tactics

The Gumtoads in Bramble Gully attack any creature that moves within range of their tongue attack (30 feet). If they see a creature moving 30-60 feet ahead of them, they will attempt to close the distance by jumping toward the target with their @UUID[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl.Item.l8RRmBpiSWIRuBiS]{Standing Leap}. If choosing between targets, Gumtoads favor creatures of Small or Medium size, which they believe are easier for them to grapple.

Once Gumtoads have selected a target, they use their very long @UUID[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl.Item.WOcK6z5h1ECL6R4N]{Barbed Tongue} to grab at members of the party - once the gumtoad has successfully used it to grapple a target, they can either pull the creature toward them with @UUID[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl.Item.laJHkd0m3K64Xoje]{Tongue Pull} or propel themselves onto the target from a distance with @UUID[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl.Item.h5MpYXeaYVqM66DY]{Tongue Boomerang}.

@Embed[Actor.sUYwQ8KqdxqyQOCV count=2]

Sarracenias Tactics

Sarracenias will attack any creature that is not currently grappled by or attached to another creature, and is within the 15-foot range of its Grasping Vines. Sarracenias prefer not to move if at all possible; if creatures move out of their range successfully, they will stay where they are instead of pursuing their prey.

The Sarracenias primarily uses its @UUID[Actor.sUYwQ8KqdxqyQOCV.Item.pAgu3mfoRsKNaqdR]{Grasping Vines} to drag creatures into its digestive sacs. The Sarracenias has several sacs, and can @UUID[Actor.sUYwQ8KqdxqyQOCV.Item.gmiMgXolwS0aFNfC]{Engulf} a new creature every other round.

Climbing to the Ledge

Once on the far side of the canyon, Edivel points out the location of the bush they need on a low outcropping and suggests carefully climbing up:

Almost there! There's the Everbloom flower, on the ledge above. I think there are enough handholds that we can make our way up.

Up close, you can see that the canyon wall is less a single rock than a collection of outcroppings and crags, rough spots and smooth, small crevices and deep crevasses. In this section of the wall, in particular, enough pieces of rock jut out to form handholds that seem to lead up to the ledge you need to reach.

Scouting Ahead

A pair of Ketral sit in the path of the characters' ascent, ready to attack. Characters spot them with a successful [[/check perception 19]] check or [[/check perception 22 passive]].

@Embed[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE inline count=2]

Ketral Tactics

Ketral will only attack creatures who come within 5 feet of whatever position they currently hold, but attempt to anticipate where creatures will move next; once a creature is within 40 feet of them, they will burrow through rock and ground to move into the creatures' most likely path without being seen.

Ketral work in packs, with one or two members of the pack situating themselves in a crack or crevice in a stony wall and striking out with their @UUID[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE.Item.JBuH0p4HvHV7673g]{Bite} or @UUID[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE.Item.kb6XyDZbNSKNpJFA]{Claws} in a @UUID[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE.Item.1hN2GE3d5Cd2ohIg]{Surprise Attack}. If the moon Cora is at its height, these attacks are more dangerous, as noted in @UUID[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE.Item.P2kQQ12YqyFA4lWZ]{Lunar Attack}.

Additional Ketral wait in a nearby cavern; if their prey chases them into the cavern, they can take advantage of their @UUID[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE.Item.uRIWxtdOWXqP2oVV]{Pack Tactics}, working together with others of their pack.

@Embed[Actor.v6ty5QZydZmZ7hrb]

Cave Wasp Attack

If characters explore the northern cavern of Bramble Gully, a swarm of cave wasps attacks from the darkness. While not particularly powerful, a Swarm of Cave Wasps, immediately surrounds and extinguishes all sources of light with @UUID[Actor.v6ty5QZydZmZ7hrb.Item.6MjuFYBkOHPDKpLu]{Light Eater}, then attack anyone in the party who is in its immediate path.

Upon the Ledge

Once the party has made it to the top of the outcropping, they reach the bush needed for Edivel's spell and can retrieve the @UUID[Item.FXNnFGmbtvZrJEhq]{Everbloom} without a check.

If characters wish, they can examine the Everbloom for themselves as well. With a successful [[/check 15 nature]] or [[/check 15 arcana]] check, they can confirm that this is the flower known as Everbloom, and know that it can be used as a substitute for other components in lower level spells that require a material component. It has no known harmful or toxic properties.

"We made it!" Edivel says, as they begin the careful work of picking up discarded flowers from around the bush's base and placing them in one of their cloak's pockets.

I knew we would. Or I hoped we would, anyway. And don't worry, I've got plenty - we won't need to go through all of this again. All I need to do now is figure out how to use it.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Depending on the route the party has taken in the quest, they may be headed to do any of the following:

  • Seek out Edivel's spellbook in @UUID[.q3RclLggX8rF6npb]

  • Travel to Steed's Point in search of information about Kali Andrella's spell in @UUID[.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu]

  • Return to Brevin with both Kali's advice and Edivel's spellbook in tow in @UUID[.yWP8ZAyLMGIWpaRU]

To leave the Canyons, characters should ideally exit up into Steed's Point from the canyons below.
Growing Pains.soverview: Bramble Gully, the valley containing the flowers that Edivel needs is overgrown and teeming with creatures. The party will have to safely make their way through in order to get the spell component that the aspiring agrimage needs.
Growing Pains.sexposition:
Making your way through the dense overgrowth of flowers and plants in this area is likely to be a challenge - the narrow and winding paths between them seem to lead to dead ends and their scents fill the air, creating a heady mix of perfume that seems to make your head spin and your vision wobble.

"There!" Edivel exclaims, pointing across the pungent landscape to a particularly striking orange tipped bush dotted with purple flowers.

That's the flower I need to save Brevin.
Growing Pains.ssummary: We helped Edivel retrieve the particular flower from Bramble Gully that they need for their vine-weaving magic.

Supplies and Demands.name: Supplies and Demands
Supplies and Demands.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration and social event, with optional combat, characters are attacked by the Canyon Crawler, an initially unseen adversary who strikes at them with environmental attacks. The attacks, which function similarly to traps, give characters the opportunity to either locate the Canyon Crawler's lair or survive long enough to draw the villain out for a direct confrontation.

Once the party finds the Crawler and unmasks their identity as a childhood friend of Edivel's, the party can attack the brigand, but only by deeply upsetting Edivel. Their other alternative is to talk to the would-be bandit, who can potentially be persuaded to change their ways and return to Brevin.

Once the situation with the Crawler is resolved, Edivel becomes interested in a wand Carmin was carrying, which they believe means they need to go to Steed's Point to get answers.

Geysers

The circular openings on the ground throughout this scene indicate the location of the geysers. Currently there is no geyser animation, so this will need to be theater of the mind.

The unseen voice continues to make demands:

You are now in the domain of the Canyon Crawler.

If you wish to survive your time here, you will pay me a fee: either fifty gold, each, or an item of true value.

Place your choice on the ground in front of you and I will let you walk away from here unharmed. Refuse, and you shall feel my power.

Oh, and leave the spellbook. That is mine.

You have two minutes to decide - either make the right choice or feel my wrath!

Assessing the Situation

The party cannot see the Canyon Crawler, but they can determine a few things about this adversary from their voice alone.

A character that makes a successful [[/check 17 perception]] check can tell that the echo of the Canyon Crawler's voice is not natural and is being enhanced, likely via magic cantrip.

A further successful [[/check 17 arcana]] check surmises that this would either be with a Thaumaturgy or Minor Illusion spell, putting the Crawler within 30 feet of the party.

Edivel is determined to get their spellbook back and immediately refuses to hand anything over to the Canyon Crawler.

You are not going to take my spellbook," Edivel says, taking their wand out and bobbing it in the air as if waiting for a fight. "And you will see that we did not come unprepared."

Laughter echoes all around you in a bitter coughing bark. "You think to taunt me with your power, adventurers? I have power of my own. Let me show you all that I can do!"

Canyon Crawler Attacks

The Canyon Crawler reveals several "powers," one at a time, announcing their power before striking, like a parody of a villain. This also gives the party options for tracking down their hidden location.

Striking from the Shadows

Place the party and Edivel into a tracked Combat encounter. At the beginning of each round of combat, the Canyon Crawler remains hidden and performs one of the following actions which you may choose:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.q3RclLggX8rF6npb#water-geyser]{Water Geyser}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.q3RclLggX8rF6npb#grasping-vines]{Grasping Vines}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.vnRwvPy99V7Z0HiK]{A Rising Tide}

On the players' turn, they can spend their action trying to locate the Canyon Crawler.

Each time that the Canyon Crawler strikes, the party has an opportunity to find and confront them. They can use any of the following methods:

Locating The Crawler

The party can directly investigate the area for signs of the Crawler's location, finding a clue that reveals them on a successful [[/check investigation 22]] check.

The party can search for tracks in the area revealing a path to the Crawler's position on a successful [[/check survival 22]] check.

With a successful [[/check perception 24]] check, the party can pick out the Canyon Crawler's real voice underneath the magical facade and use it to pinpoint their location. Each time the Crawler speaks, the DC of this check goes down by 2.

Each effect has a specific range, which can be pinpointed with a successful [[/check arcana 24]] check, giving a sense of how far the Crawler can be from the party's current position. With each new effect, the DC of this check goes down by 2.

Alternately, the party may try to fool the Canyon Crawler into thinking that their demands are being met to draw them out.

Fooling The Crawler

If characters want to fool the crawler into emerging from their hideout, they will need to leave some items of value (or that appear to be items of value) as instructed. If a character leaves an item or collection of items that are collectively worth at least 100 gold pieces, the Crawler will be satisfied with the offering.

  • If the items left are not truly valuable, the character leaving them must succeed on a [[/check deception 18]] or [[/check sleightofhand 18]] to trick the Crawler.

Once their items are placed, the party must "surrender" either verbally or via their body language. The Crawler commands the party to depart the area, leaving the offerings behind. The party may attempt to deceive the Crawler into thinking they have withdrawn using either a [[/check 18 deception]] or [[/check 18 stealth]] check.

  • On a success, the Crawler comes out as soon as the party is out of sight to collect the goods left behind. If the party successfully lures out the Canyon Crawler, proceed to the final section of this event, @UUID[.q3RclLggX8rF6npb#the-canyon-crawler,-revealed]{The Canyon Crawler, Revealed}.

Water Geyser

Watch as the water rises from the depths to sweep you away! Can you make the power of Mayis itself bend to your commands as I can!

Water erupts from the edge of the river left in the center of the canyons in a spout that streams up from the surface and curves toward you with full power.

Geyser

A geyser of water erupts from the center of the water-filled crevasse towards a member of the party within 30 feet. Whomever is targeted must succeed on a [[/save 15 strength]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d4 bludgeoning]] and be pushed 15 feet away by the force of the blast. If their movement ends against solid rock, they take an additional [[/damage 1d4 bludgeoning]] damage and fall prone.

Ketral Attack

The first time this attack is used, the geyser disturbs the nearby rocks, causing a single @UUID[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE]{Ketral} to emerge and join the combat encounter.

Locating the Source

The gushing water is caused by an @UUID[Item.yEMw3gyVWsrAuuSK]{Endless Fountain Stone}, which the Canyon Crawler has placed beneath the edge of the water in the Canyons. An acute party member can see a magical glint in the light as the stone is activated with a successful [[/check perception 22]] check.

  • If the Fountain Stone is noticed, its function is understood to any party member who succeeds on a [[/check arcana 22]] check or uses the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3OZnNhunvRtPOQmH]{Identify} spell.

Grasping Vines

Nowhere you stand is safe. Behold as even the plants in the ground respond to my power!

On the still-damp ground, weeds begin to sprout around you, grasping at whatever is around them as if they were the fingers of the dead, looking to hold on to whatever part of you they can grasp.

Entangling Vines

Weeds and roots form a 20-foot square at a location of the Crawler's choosing requiring each creature in the area to make a [[/save strength 15]] saving throw or become &Reference[restrained].

Any character that succeeds on a [[/check arcana 16]] check recognizes the effect as originating from the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.gMrWeG8fMDPRFiVe]{Entangle} spell.

Sarracenias Attack

If any character is successfully restrained by the effect, a single @UUID[Actor.sUYwQ8KqdxqyQOCV]{Sarracenias} emerges from a small cave in the nearby rock and slowly moves towards the restrained character to devour them.

Falling Stones

See how the canyon itself tears itself apart to crush you? You will never know peace unless you give me what I want!

The vines on the canyon's wall seem to double in size, growing new shoots and leaves and getting thicker than before. As they grow, they dislodge rocks from the canyon walls, which tumble down from above.

Rocks Fall

A cascade of large rocks crash down towards the party. Two of these rocks are close enough to pose a significant threat, each creating a 10-foot radius impact somewhere of the Crawler's choosing. Any creature within the area of effect must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d12 bludgeoning]] damage.

Gumtoad Attack

Affixed to each of the falling rocks is a single @UUID[Actor.7dENUBzy6ZXlZVxl]{Gumtoad} which joins the combat encounter. Each toad is initially &Reference[stunned] for 1 round by the fall, but after recovering its senses will attack any character nearby.

The Crawler Revealed

If characters reach the Canyon Crawler in their lair, they find a young Thornling in the back of a cave, surrounded by items, including a @UUID[Item.t5SrnNauNSwFjZgy]{Speaking Horn}, which they hold to their lips:

"Do not enter this cavern." The voice booms, but in the dim light you can see its origin - a young Thornling, not much older than Edivel, speaking into a carved horn. This close, you can hear the Thornling's normal everyday voice a second before whatever they say comes booming into your ears as if by magic - thin and shaky.

Before you can speak or confront the Crawler, Edivel gasps and points in the other Thornling's direction.

Carmin? Is that you? What are you doing? Someone could have been seriously hurt!

If the party has lured the Canyon Crawler outside of their lair, Edivel recognizes them immediately.

In the distance, a Thornling emerges from around a corner, carrying a bag of items and waving what looks to be a fallen branch in your direction. Before they can speak, Edivel gasps and points in the newcomer's direction.

Wait, I know who this is! It's Carmin! Carmin, I know you've been getting all those 'be a bandit like the Otherhood of Fortune' ideas in your head, but this is ridiculous! Someone could have been killed!

A Fallen Friend

Carmin is unapologetic about their actions so far, helped by the @UUID[Item.ykX3uNQVRC6tXWhh]{Shielding Pin} that they are wearing, which can repel most direct attacks, at least temporarily.

Of course it's you, Edivel. My old friend. Probably spent more time tracking down that spellbook than you ever did trying to hang around with me. But don't worry, nobody's been harmed, not really. I'm just having a little fun, like that shard god you're always going on about, god of tricks and traps, or whatever. And you're way too attached to that spellbook anyway. Or you were. Now it's mine!

Edivel is incensed at the characterization of the shard god.

Aythorn would never try to hurt anyone. They're about bringing people joy even when things are hard. The way that agrimages do.

Carmin is unconvinced.

Agrimages. Again. Well, while you were off filling up your spellbook with lost spells, I was figuring out how to use the things they make for something a little more interesting. Want to see what else I can do?

Edivel shakes their head and turns to the party.

Carmin used to be so great, but those Otherhood lies have twisted their ideas. Please, don't hurt them?

Convincing Carmin

As Carmin prepares to attack again, the party can attempt to intervene and prevent a fight by convincing the Thornling that they won't win in a direct battle and should stand down with a successful [[/check persuasion 20]]. The DC of this check can be lowered by 1 with success on either of the following checks:

  • Carmin can be flattered with a successful [[/check deception 16]] check

  • Carmin can be threatened with a succesful [[/check intimidation 16]] check

  • Carmin can also be persuaded using spells to induce them to stand down, such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.zMAWdyc8UVb37BK4]{Suggestion } or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.eS7XnnApoxRxYXPs]{Charm Person}.

If successfully persuaded, Carmin agrees to stand down, although they are sulky about the outcome:

Fine, you never wanted to have any good fun anyway, Edivel. Not anymore. So keep your silly spellbook. Plenty of other travelers on these roads I can "make friends" with. How else am I going to get nice gear like this?

Otherwise, Carmin will attack, committed to their path of banditry!

Fighting Carmin

If Carmin is attacked by the party at any point before they exit, Edivel will refuse to participate in the attack. Edivel spends each turn in combat taking defensive or protective actions and attempting to persuade both the party and Carmin to stand down.

Carmin's Tactics

Carmin attacks haphazardly, using their @UUID[Item.ykX3uNQVRC6tXWhh]{Shielding Pin} to protect themselves. Carmin lacks any significant combat capabilities, and instead will rely upon his @UUID[Actor.qW0lhTVZLQknOayq.Item.kgsEaCr2NRTptrG2]{Handcarved Vine Wand} and pre-placed @UUID[Item.yEMw3gyVWsrAuuSK]{Endless Fountain Stone} to threaten the party as described above.

Reconsidering Life Choices

Once Carmin is either persuaded to stand down or forcibly subdued, Edivel — and possibly the party — will demand that they divert from their criminal path. Carmin intends to continue as the Canyon Crawler, but may be convinced to give up banditry altogether with a successful [[/check 22 persuasion]] check. The DC of the check lowers by 1 for each of the following successes:

  • A [[/check intimidation 17]] check to threaten to find Carmin and destroy them if they continue their robbing spree.

  • A [[/check insight 17]] check to realize that Carmin simply wants to be famous and important and convince them accordingly

  • A [[/check performance 17]] check to tell a stirring tale of why Brevin needs them more than they need to continue being the Canyon Crawler.

If effectively persuaded, Carmin agrees to return to Brevin and to stop robbing travelers.

Okay, okay. Maybe those Otherhood folks aren't the best to listen to anyway. And if Brevin's in trouble, they'll need the Canyon … Crusader. Canyon Crusader to the rescue, I like the sound of that.

If the party does not succeed in talking Carmin down, they suddenly smash an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.CvzjhUy9ekRieR1A]{Eversmoking Bottle} upon the ground and vanish into the resulting haze, their voice lingering behind as they go.

See you around, old friend.

Heart Attunement: Carmin in Brevin

If the party manages to convince Carmin to give up their life of banditry and settle in Brevin, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 canyonsSideBridgeBrevin]] at the conclusion of the event.

Orbis Attunement: Carmin the Bandit

If Carmin chooses to continue their life of banditry, each character advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 canyonsSideBridgeBandit]] at the conclusion of the event.

Luxarum Attunement: Carmin Killed

If the party kills Carmin during this fateful encounter, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 canyonsSideBridgeKilled]] at the conclusion of the event.

A Final Clue

With Carmin either gone or no longer a threat, the party can recover @UUID[Item.zgIxSMrCtlJe09in]{Edivel's Spellbook} and the @UUID[Item.GIghIDXB62nPaaKT]{Handcrafted VIne Wand} that was in Carmin's posession. Most of the remaining items in Carmin's pile of goods are useless, including their @UUID[Item.ykX3uNQVRC6tXWhh]{Shielding Pin}, which has burned out and become mundane.

Edivel is thrilled to get their spellbook back but is most intrigued by the wand, which features an intricate woodcarving technique and might be related to the type of vine magic that they are trying to master.

Examining the Wand

Edivel asks the party what they make of the wand. Characters can notice the following:

  • With a successful [[/check history 16]] check, characters can tell that this is a somewhat older version of the agrimage symbol, indicating that it might be from an older or more traditional agrimage.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 16]] check, characters notice initials carved into the side of the wand - "KA".

  • If Carmin has been convinced to give up their ways, the party can ask where they got it. Carmin tells the party that the person they took the wand from was said to have been given it by a great agrimage in Steed's Point.

Either through success on these checks, or through Edivel's independent realization, Edivel is convinced that the wand previously belonged to Kali Andrella - a renowned agrimage who used to live in the now-ruined town of Steed's Point.

Concluding the Event

Edivel is convinced that the wand is an important clue and wants to travel to Steed's Point to learn more.

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

This event should lead the party towards @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr]{Steed's Point}, where they encounter the quest event @UUID[.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu]{A Dying Art}.

To leave the Canyons, characters should ideally exit up into Steed's Point from the canyons below.
Supplies and Demands.soverview: The party's attempt to retrieve Edivel's spellbook from where it washed downstream leads them into a fight with the Canyon Crawler, a brigand who attacks from afar. A defeat of the Canyon Crawler reveals them to be Carmin, a childhood friend of Edivel's using stolen magical items for their attacks. Edivel recognizes one of the items — it belonged to famed agrimage Kali Andrella and could lead the party to her whereabouts.
Supplies and Demands.sexposition:
There! The spellbook - I see it!

Without Edivel's charm on the spellbook, it might have been impossible to spot, but the young agrimage heads toward it without hesitation, following the slight glow among the stones and mud at the sides of the canyon. The land has been tossed and shaken by the recent rapids, but the waters are finally calm again, leaving behind a slowly burbling stream in the canyon's center crevasse.

Just as Edivel reaches out for it, the book moves, as if dragged somehow by the dirt beneath it, rocks and soil holding tight to it as it shifts away from Edivel's reaching grasp. As Edivel comes closer, it moves again, and then again, as if drawing the agrimage away from the rest of the group.

You might as well give up.

A voice rings out from an unseen location in the canyons all around you.

That spellbook - and anything else you have - now belong to me.
Supplies and Demands.ssummary: We recovered Edivel's spellbook from the Canyon Crawler, who turned out to be Edivel's childhood friend Carmin. Subduing them led us to a potential location for agrimagical expert Kali Andrella, who may be at Steed's Point.

A Dying Art.name: A Dying Art
A Dying Art.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this event, characters make their way through Steed's Point. The location details and gameplay of the travel through Steed's Point can be found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr]{Steed's Point Area Walkthrough}.

Along the way, they will likely encounter Rattletrap in @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.X6okKjJy1vST39Cg]{Steed's Point Fields} and can question him about what he knows about Kali.

Once characters make their way to Kali Andrella's cottage in the center of town, the event transitions from combat and exploration to a social event. In this event, the characters can:

  • Find out why Kali is still in Steed's Point.

  • Help her decide what to do next.

  • Get Edivel the training they need to be able to help Brevin as an up-and-coming agrimage.

Encountering Rattletrap

If the party speaks to Rattletrap in Steed's Point Fields, he will engage in general conversation with the party, as noted in the area walkthrough. He can also share a few extra pieces of information specific to this quest in response to Edivel, as follows:

A Conversation with Rattletrap

Rattletrap is willing to share the following in response to additional questions from the party or Edivel:

  • Rattletrap believes that Kali Andrella is in the cottage in the center of the town and that she knows he is there — her traps do not trigger when he passes. Still, he has not seen or spoken to her since the town's fall and isn't sure how to get her attention.

  • Rattletrap thinks Kali has remained in Steed's Point because she also has a connection to his creator, Bertron Steed, who Kali saw as a father figure. He believes she has a strong drive to protect this place, even with so little of it left.

  • Rattletrap knows Kali's daughter, Moriah Foxhaven, but Kali and Moriah parted on somewhat bad terms. She hasn't been seen since before the fall of Steed's Point.

Kali's Location?

I remember Kali. Hard woman to forget. Used to go all over the Plateau solving problems with a handful of seeds, a newly carved wand, and a smile. Pretty sure she's still here, same as me, tucked into that house wrapped in thorns in the middle of town. Can't prove it or anything, but this whole place is full of the kind of nasty hedge bits that I think I remember she was good at, and they always leave me alone. Maybe that's her way of saying hello?

Contacting Kali?

Maybe bring her something she wants? Or make your way to her door and ask nice? There's some winding hedges to the north that I think lead right to her. If you're trying to hurt Steed's Point, she'll cut you down where you stand, but if not — she might welcome the company.

Why is Kali still here?

Maybe she's like me, feels some kind of tie to the place? Or to Bertron? He's who this whole town was named after, Bertron Steed. Feels like if we all leave, we lose the last piece of him. Whatever her reason is, I'm sure she's doing good - those hedges come out with their thorns out whenever the gore birds or jurtak get too close to the middle of town, like she's protecting it.

Kali's Daughter?

Kali likes to think she's all alone in the world, but I know her daughter's out there somewhere. Moriah Foxhaven. Always with the hundred questions. Why is the grass golden? How come I can talk but the rattle man can't? Guess back then, I couldn't. I'd forgotten about that. Pretty sure she left before everything went wrong with Steed's Point - she and her ma had different ideas about how she should be living her life.

Meeting Kali

@Embed[Actor.FAWXlZTU8syDdRFy]

Once the party has reached Kali, they may speak to her generally about Steed's Point as noted in the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEbYuYfF12qoN6Xr.JournalEntryPage.jCEAfUatFe6LoEnE]{Kali's Cottage} area walkthrough. When there is a pause in the conversation or party questions, Edivel interrupts:

While Edivel appears to listen at least somewhat attentively to Kali's answers, they begin squirming as she continues to speak, finally blurting out, in a rush of words:

I'm sorry Kali Andrella I don't mean to interrupt your talk but I'm Edivel and I really need your help with vineweaving or else I think Brevin could end up just like Steed's Point. We're growing a bridge of vines to go across the canyons but I think the recent shaking of the earth might throw off what the druids have done so far - from everything I've heard, they have to be very precise to make the bridge grow properly.

Kali looks the young agrimage up and down, and smiles slightly, the vines at her fingertips reaching toward them as she does, then slowly nods.

Brevin, you say? I don't know it, but what you're saying about the bridge sounds right - some vineweaving might be good to have in case of trouble. And when the earth shakes, it often means trouble. It was the shaking earth that gave the jurtak a way out of the depths to attack Steed's Point, destroy most of my home. And now I have to figure out what to do about it. Once I've done that, I'd be happy to help you out.

The Situation At Hand

Kali is focused on deciding what to do next about her situation in Steed's Point — until she does, she can't be of any help to Edivel. She can share the following, but always comes back to her big decision. With a [[/check insight 15]] check, characters know that Kali legitimately wants to help them, but can't focus until she figures her own situation out.

  • The vineweaving technique is a tricky one, hard to master on your own. Edivel will need training from her or another agrimage to learn it. They will also need a colorful flower found in Bramble Gully, Everbloom.

  • The @UUID[Item.GIghIDXB62nPaaKT]{Handcarved Vine Wand} is indeed something she made. She used to make several magical items and trade them to those who visited Steed's Point.

  • Kali is willing to train Edivel, but only after she decides whether she wants to stay in Steed's Point or leave it. Until then, she's focused on her decision.

Full answers below.

The Vineweaving Technique?

Not surprised the vineweaving isn't going well, it took me a while to master it myself. I'm sure I could give you a few pointers, though. Something tells me you'd pick it up pretty fast. I just don't really have the time to teach you yet. Big decisions to make.

The Vine Wand?

That definitely looks like one of mine, though it's been a few years since I carved for someone else. Used to make things like this for other agrimages or wizards looking to hone their craft, but with no one to trade with, I've almost forgotten a few of these techniques. I'll hold on to this, see if I can learn something from it one way or the other. No matter what I decide, this could come in handy.

Helping Edivel?

It's not that I don't want to help — I absolutely do. But it's hard to focus and teach when you're still figuring things out for yourself. Stay here in Steed's Point or leave it behind? I just can't quite figure out which would be right.

Helping Kali Decide

With the party waiting for her to decide, Kali asks for help deciding what to do next.

You seem to be a pretty determined group. Remind me of my baby girl, Moriah, wherever she is these days. And since I know you want me helping this young agrimage, maybe you can help me in return. I've been going back and forth for a while now about whether I should stick things out here or go back into the world, and sometimes it's good to get out of your own head. I'll lay it out for you and then you tell me: what do you think I should do?

Decisions, Decisions

If the party wants to convince Kali one way or another, they must succeed on a [[/check persuasion 26]] check. Whether they attempt to convince her to stay or go is up to the party. For each argument they successfully make or piece of information they share to sway Kali, whether pro or con, the DC of the check lowers by 1.

Why Leave

Kali lays out her reasons for going:

My baby girl's out there, like I said, and she has no idea her mama is holed up here. If I leave, I could go find her, maybe make up for lost time. And while I get along fine here for now, it might be nice to hear some voices other than my own, see the sights I used to when I traveled all over the plateau. Until you all got here, I don't think I realized just how much I missed that. Only problem is, if I leave, who will keep this place from being destroyed once and for all?

With a successful [[/check insight 17]] check, characters know that they can push her toward leaving if they figure out what would be the right place for her to go next, can lead her to her daughter, or can convince her that Steed's Point is fine without her. They can do any of the following to convince her to go (each success lowers the DC of the persuasion check to convince her by 1), or make an attempt at the GM's discretion (all attempts DC 18):

  • Giving Kali the @UUID[Item.vLYGD46oaA7xcXXC]{farewell note} from Moriah (found in the Ruined House in Steed's Point), which gives a lead towards Moriah’s whereabouts near the Eastern River.

  • A successful [[/check 18 performance]] check to talk up the wonders of the Arctus Plateau outside of Steed’s Point. Any character who has [[/knowledge politics]] has advantage on this check.

  • A successful [[/check 18 arcana]] or [[/check 18 deception]] check to convince Kali that Steed’s Point will survive without her if she sets up the right agrimagical items before she leaves. Any character who has [[/knowledge crafts]] has advantage on this check.

  • A successful [[/check 18 intelligence]] check to determine that Nain would be a good place for Kali to resettle. Any character who has [[/knowledge trade]] has advantage on this check.

Why Stay

Kali also gives reasons for staying:

I know it seems like I've already decided to stay, seeing as I've been here for a while now, but I still feel like I did right after the battle, when Bertron was on the ground and folks were running for the hills, and all I could do was call down gore birds to fight the jurtak and protect what was left with the hedges in the ground. If I was really staying, I'd do it differently. Rebuild, add security, try to keep the jurtak away. I just don't know if it's better to try to build back or to leave it all behind.

With a successful [[/check insight 17]] check, characters know that they can push her toward staying by emphasizing the legacy of Steed's Point that would be maintained or convincing her that Steed's Point can be rebuilt. They can do any of the following to convince her to go (each success lowers the DC of the persuasion check to convince her by 1), or make an attempt at the GM's discretion (all attempts DC 18):

  • A successful [[/check deception 18]] or [[/check intimidation 18]] check to convince Kali that the jurtak can be easily taken care of, giving Kali time and space to rebuild. If the party has cleared Steed's Point of all enemies or has [[/knowledge monsters]], they have advantage on this check.

  • A successful [[/check history 18]] check to emphasize the importance of Steed's Point as an agrimagical wonder that will be lost if Kali is not there to carry it on. Any character with [[/knowledge plants]] has advantage on this check.

  • A successful [[/check survival 18]] check to come up with plans to rebuild Steed's Point as a vibrant part of the landscape. Any character with [[/knowledge trade]] has advantage on this check.

Kali's Final Decision

If the party succeeds on its persuasion check, characters successfully convinces Kali to either leave Steed's Point forever or commit to rebuilding it. If they fail, she decides to continue weighing the matter.

  • Kali is Convinced to Stay and Rebuild: Kali decides to rebuild Steed's Point, with the party bidding goodbye in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu#fond-farewell]{Fond Farewell}.

  • Kali is Convinced to Leave: Kali decides to go to Nain, where she has a good friend, and settle there, leaving Steed's Point to fall but giving her a chance to live her life and possibly gather resources to rebuild it. The party can head out as she gathers her things in @UUID[.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu#helping-kali-pack]{Helping Kali Pack}.

  • Kali Can't Decide: Kali decides to focus on the here and now and dig into her life in her cottage, staying in the safety of its walls while she decides what's best. The party can leave her to it in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu#leaving-kali-behind]{Leaving Kali Behind}.

Staying In Steed's Point

Kali thanks the party for their help in getting her to decide to stay in Steed's Point:

You're right. Steed's Point needs me. But not like this, like a scared child cowering and waiting to make up their mind. If I ever want Steed's Point to be more than this, I need to come out of hiding and start fixing this mess It'll take some time, but it's worth the doing.

Kali reaches into her pocket and retrieves the handcrafted wand that Edivel gave her, presenting it to them with a flourish.

And Edivel Sprout, that town of yours, Brevin, it's also worth the saving, Edivel. So I'll teach you a little of what I know, and you can hang onto this wand. Just in case you need it. Now let's get some vineweaving in that spellbook of yours.

In addition to giving Edivel Sprout the @UUID[Item.GIghIDXB62nPaaKT]{Handcarved Vine Wand}, she offers the party a gift: a @UUID[Item.KQVMGcQAEqHRs8RC]{Reaching Vine} which she has crafted over her time in Steed's Point.

Taking a Stand

If asked, Kali shares the following about her plans:

  • She plans to spend more time in and around Steed's Point outside of her cottage, working to fix the place up.

  • She looks forward to talking with Rattletrap more and thinks that together they might be able to fight back the jurtak and gore birds, but at the least she will invite him to her cottage.

  • She wants to get the word out to Moriah that she can be found in Steed's Point and asks the party to tell others, though she wants Moriah only to visit if she can do it safely.

Expanded answers follow.

Kali's Plans?

I'll protect Steed's Point, like I have been, but I can't just protect it for me. I want to drive these creatures out, build the place back to what it used to be. Think I got a little too comfortable just being within these walls. And don't worry, Edivel - if the jurtak or those gore birds try to mess with me, they'll learn some of the new agrimagic tricks I've been developing with all my free time. Can you say exploding roots? In a year or so, I'll have that one perfected, can teach it to you.

Relationship with Rattletrap?

I knew Rattletrap was out there, but the way you talk about him, like he was actually speaking back to you? That's something new. I'll admit, I'm curious to know what happened there, and even more than that, it would be nice to have someone else to talk to, maybe reminisce a bit about the way Steed's Point used to be.

Relationship with Moriah?

I wonder what Moriah thinks happened to me. I tried to get word out when Steed's Point fell, was hoping she might come in and turn the tide, but the message never got out. I wonder if you might spread the word a bit, up in Brevin or wherever else you go in the Arctus Plateau, let her know I'm here and she's always welcome back. I'd say as long as she can make it here safely, but Moriah always knew how to take care of herself.

Kali remains in Steed's Point, but can be found in varying locations around the settlement.

Mayis Attunement: Kali Rebuilds

If Kali is convinced to stay and rebuild Steed's Point, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 bookTalesMoonChildMayis]] at the conclusion of the event.

Leaving Steed's Point

Kali thanks the party for their help in getting her to actually make the move to Nain and leave Steed's Point behind.

You're right. I've been living in the past. And staying here doesn't bring Bertron Steed back, or make my daughter come home, or fix any of the broken homes around this place. I have a friend in Nain — think I might head there for a bit, maybe get some folks to help me come back and build something new. That's what Bertron would've done.

Kali reaches into her pocket and retrieves the handcrafted wand that Edivel gave her, presenting it to them with a flourish.

And since I'm starting fresh, I'll leave this old wand with you, Edivel, hope that it does you a bit of good. And don't you worry, I'll teach you a bit of the vineweaving to go along with it. If the rest of you don't mind waiting for just a moment, I'll get Edivel here up to speed.

In addition to giving Edivel the @UUID[Item.GIghIDXB62nPaaKT]{Handcarved Vine Wand}, Kali also offers the party a gift — a @UUID[Item.KQVMGcQAEqHRs8RC]{Reaching Vine}, which she won't need in Nain.

A New Beginning

If asked, Kali shares the following on her plans going forward:

  • She plans to reconnect with an old friend in Nain and possibly get others in Nain to come back with her to Steed's Point to revitalize it in the future.

  • She worries what will happen to Steed's Point without her there, but is cheered by the idea that at least Rattletrap will be around to let her know if she is needed.

  • She wants to get the word out to Moriah that she can be found in Nain and asks the party to share the info with those they see during their travels.

Full answers below.

Kali's Plans?

I used to get around the Plateau a lot, so I should still have a few friends in Nain. Gonna look up my old pal Zenodora — see if she's still running her General Store. And if she isn't…let's just say I got a long list of folks who'll probably be happy to see me. I'm gonna need 'em all if I want to get a group together to come back this way and reclaim Steed's Point for the future.

What Happens to Steed's Point?

I'm not sure. I've been keeping an eye on things, but then so has Rattletrap, I suppose, so maybe nothing changes at all. Or maybe the jurtak run the whole thing over. My guess is that either way Rattletrap stays around here, so if things get too bad, he can let me know.

Relationship with Moriah?

It would be nice to see Moriah after all this time. I tried to get word out when Steed's Point fell, was hoping she might come in and turn the tide, but the message never got out. I wonder if you might spread the word a bit, up in Brevin or wherever else you go in the Arctus Plateau, let her know I'm heading to Nain and she might want to come visit.

Kali relocates to Nain.

Cora Attunement: Kali Resettles

If Kali is convinced to relocate to Nain, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 canyonsSideCrafterResettles]] at the conclusion of the event.

Kali Undecided

Kali thanks the party for trying to help her make a decision, even if it wasn't a successful effort:

Harder decision than it seems like, I know. But you've given me a few new things to think about, so I appreciate that. And as a thank you, I suppose I can take a little time to teach Edivel a few tricks of the vineweaving trade. Just talking it all out a bit helped me get a bit of focus, so don't worry, you're getting my best.

Kali beckons an exhilarated Edivel over and opens their spellbook.

Don't worry — it won't take too long. And if you want to come back and visit, you're welcome anytime.

Staying Put

If asked, Kali shares the following about her plans:

  • She will continue weighing whether to stay or go, but will remain in the cottage in the meantime. With her new supplies, she may be able to turn the tide against the jurtak one day.

  • It would be great to see Moriah, but it isn't safe for her to visit. She asks that if the party sees Moriah, they let her know that Kali is okay, but to stay away.

Full answers below.

Kali's Plans?

I'm not quite sure what I'll do, but with these new supplies, I won't need to figure it out for a while, can stay here and weigh things out. Who knows, maybe I'll get the better of the jurtak one of these days.

Relationship with Moriah?

I tried to get word out to Moriah when Steed's Point fell, but it never got to her. I'd like her to know I'm okay. Not going anywhere, at least not for now. Doubt she was planning on coming by, but you tell her to stay back until this place is a little safer. I can take care of myself.

Kali remains permanently in Steed's Point.

Orbis Attunement: Kali Undecided

If Kali remains undecided about her fate, each character advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 canyonsSideCrafterUndecided]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Whatever Kali decides, the party can head back to their next steps in the quest - either retrieving the flower that Edivel needs in @UUID[.wayoxatxc7P06K0t]{Growing Pains} or heading back to Brevin for the celebration in @UUID[.yWP8ZAyLMGIWpaRU]{Bridging the Gap}.

The impacts of Kali's decision will be felt in downstream events later in the campaign:

  • If Kali goes to Nain, parties may encounter her in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.e8T6ACfUEzwMgxGB]{Next Year In Nain}.

  • If Kali rebuilds, parties can see the effects in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.EuiLwch7KTh32EpJ]{The New Steed's Point}.

  • If Kali hasn't made a decision, parties can check in on her in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.NXQyM1vHizHyFdR6]{Kali On The Fence}.
A Dying Art.soverview: The party investigates the overgrown ruins of Steed's Point, which Edivel is convinced show the influence of Kali Andrella. They believe a powerful artifact of the legendary agrimage must be in the center of the village, but it is in fact Kali herself, who has barricaded herself in her home in the center of the village, surrounded by defensive hedges. Once the party has reached Kali, they can help her make the decision to either relocate to Nain or participate more fully in rebuilding Steed's Point.
A Dying Art.sexposition:
No sooner have you reached the clump of ruined buildings that was once Steed's Point than Edivel goes running, intent on examining a hedge with a combination of yellow, green, and purple leaves that move back and forth ever so slightly, as if warning, or beckoning, or both.

You see this purple here?

Edivel lifts one of the purple leaves with their finger , seeming to miss how it curls back in a near-flinch.

This color leaf is a Kali Andrella signature. Even if she isn't here, there must be something powerful of hers still here in this village that can help me… and Brevin of course. There's no way we'll get straight through one of these hedges, but there may be a path around somewhere in the ruins. If we-

Edivel's voice is interrupted by the sound of metal clanging to the west, followed by a sound somewhere between a whisper and the wind. Without missing a beat, Edivel bolts off toward the sounds, calling over his shoulder:

Must be the voice of Kali, showing us the way! C'mon!
A Dying Art.ssummary: We braved the dangers of Steed's Point and met the legendary Kali Andrella, who was holed up in the center of the ruined village.

Next Year In Nain.name: Next Year In Nain
Next Year In Nain.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

This is an event that happens after some time has passed since Thorny Predicaments. It gives the party an opportunity to catch up with Kali now that she has moved to the larger city.

@Embed[Actor.FAWXlZTU8syDdRFy]

Too Busy To Chat

If the party declines her request, moving on with their quest, she addresses them as they leave:

As you continue on your quest, focused on the task ahead of you, Kali calls out again to the crowd.

Look at them – so polite, not wanting to cut in front of the crowd. Probably off to do great deeds somewhere else on the plateau. Deeds we could use in these troubling times. Let’s send them off with a fond farewell.

Kali leads the crowd in a rousing round of applause that seems to have a bit of her magic in it, raising your spirits as you head off on your next adventure.

A Little Help From Your Friends

Thanks to the gratitude of the crowd and Kali’s magic, the entire party has advantage on their next skill check, as if they had the benefits of the Help action.

Catching Up With Kali

If the party goes up to see Kali, they find her at a makeshift stand in a small garden.

The sign announcing Kali’s presence hangs above a wooden stand that might seem plain if it wasn’t surrounded by plants and flowers, as if a garden sprung to life wherever Kali had decided to settle. On the stand sits a large jar filled with a combination of small trinkets, jewels, seeds, and coins. As you approach, she rises and steps away from the stand into the midst of the plants around it, where a small ring of tall reeds provides a small amount of privacy from the waiting line.

It’s wonderful to see you again, my friends. Here, come talk with me a moment before I get back to all my newly adoring fans.

The Survivor of Steed's Point

Kali is happy to tell the party what she's gotten up to since leaving Steed's Point. She shares the following:
