  • Zenodora, who runs Zenodora's General Goods nearby, was thrilled to see her and just as thrilled about hyping up her story to drive people to her store nearby. Kali answers questions, helps those she can, and sends anyone who needs something simple to Zenodora's store.

  • She felt a little guilty at first for calling herself the Survivor of Steed's Point, but at least it's gotten people talking, and she's been collecting donations of goods for the revitalization of Steed's Point from the people she helps.

  • One day, Kali plans to return to Steed's Point and build it back again, but in the meantime it's nice to be out in society again and she's glad that her story can inspire.

Full answers below.

Kali's New Store?

You like the shop? Zenodora's idea, really. She's been in Nain for years, has a General Goods store, so she usually knows the mood of folks in town. And the last few seasons, they've been jumpy. Rumors of bandits and living corpses and beasts running wild. Having someone like me here helps folks feel more secure - if I could survive Steed's Point, they can survive whatever life throws their way. Most folks just want advice, but I get to make a few magic items too, grow my garden. Not a bad life altogether.

Relationship to Steed's Point?

I haven't forgotten about Steed's Point. I'm not just a survivor of it, I'm part of its legacy. See that jar there? When folks come up to talk, if they want, they can leave something that'll help regrow Steed's Point. Some give money, or supplies, but I think my favorite are the seeds. Things we can replant there one day, after things settle down on the Plateau. I can't wait.

What's New With You

Kali is also thrilled to hear any news from the party. She reacts generally positively to anything they say, but has an especially positive reaction to any of the following:

  • If the party met Moriah, she is excited that her daughter is doing well and vows to get word out through those who travel through Nain of her new location. She's enthusiastic about potentially seeing Moriah soon.

  • If the party saved Brevin, she is pleased, though not surprised. She thought they'd be able to do it. She also shares that she has been in correspondence with Edivel, helping the young agrimage to continue to develop their craft.

  • If the party knows that Rattletrap is Bertron Steed, she is surprised, and worried that she left him alone in Steed's Point. She vows to increase her efforts to go back and make Steed's Point what it once was, or at least to go check on Rattletrap from time to time.

Full answers below.

If they've met Moriah:

My girl. I'm glad she's okay - thanks for letting me now. I hope you told her I moved here to Nain - not that I expect her to drop everything and come this way, but I hope one day she'll come and see her ma. We could be like oil and water sometimes, but after everything that's happened, it's a good time to have family around.

If Brevin was Saved:

I knew you all would do it. That Edivel certainly was determined, and with your help keeping them out of trouble, they were bound to make sure that Brevin kept thriving. Good work! I've been sending them a few other tips and tricks over the last couple of months, where I can. Better to keep their hands busy learning agrimagic than running off causing trouble, especially these days, when there are more dangers on the Golden Flats than ever before.

Rattletrap is Bertron:

Really? You're not kidding with me? I guess that explains why Rattletrap stayed around Steed's Point for so long the way I did. Probably still there now. I should visit, see what he remembers. See if he's angry I left. See if he's angry I couldn't keep the jurtak from running us over and out of our homes. Better angry than dead, at least.

The way he fell to the jurtak? It weighed on me, and now it weighs a little less.

Thank you.

Another Fond Farewell

With their talk complete, Kali offers the party something to help their future adventures and travels. Generally, she gives a single portion of @UUID[Item.FKsd5PGexRuqn264]{Growing Thorns} to the party, but if the party brought her specifically joyful news, she gives them an additional item.

  • If the party met Moriah, she offers a pouch of Throwing Stones, which have the properties of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.SqTtbBCfiEsmZ36N]{Beads of Force}.

  • If the party saved Brevin, she adds an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.i89okN7GFTWHsvPy]{Herbalism Kit} and an @UUID[Item.FXNnFGmbtvZrJEhq]{Everbloom}, which she has begun cultivating after getting a seed sent to her by Edivel.

  • If the party brought news of Rattletrap, she offers a @UUID[Item.Qg2cqy4rAf4YSBx0]{Healing Potion} and a trinket she found while clearing out Steed's Point that reminds her of him. Roll on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} table for the item at hand.

Kali wishes the party a final goodbye and good luck on their journey, acclaiming them to the crowd.

Farewell, my friends! Everyone, please, give these adventurers the well wishes they so deserve!

As the crowd cheers you on, you head off to your next adventure with lighter feet, as if the crowd itself is lifting you up with a little sprinkling of magic.

Concluding the Event

A Little Help From Your Friends

Thanks to the gratitude of the crowd and Kali’s magic, the entire party has advantage on their next skill check, as if they had the benefits of the Help action.

Next Steps

This ends the general quest line. The party is free to explore Nain or head elsewhere in search of new adventures. They can also buy alchemical or herbalist goods from Kali going forward, with a 20% "friends of Kali" discount.
Next Year In Nain.soverview: The party finds a resurgent Kali living in Nain and raising funds and resources to rebuild Steed's Point.
Next Year In Nain.sexposition:
You see the line before you know what it leads to – people waiting, mostly patiently, for something in the distance. From what you can hear in the overlapping murmurs of those lined up, most have a question or problem that they’re looking for help with, and many are holding seeds or plants or flowers in their hands. As you pass the line, you can hear one word repeated over and over: survivor. It is not until you see the sign that it all comes together: Kali Andrella, Renowned Agrimage, the Survivor of Steed’s Point.

Kali sees you the moment you see her and stands, beckoning you closer and announcing to the crowd.

These are the adventurers I spoke of! The ones who braved Steed’s Point to bring me news of the outside world. Please, friends, come up and say hello!
Next Year In Nain.ssummary: We ran into Kali Andrella in Nain, where she is thriving and making plans to rebuild Steed's Point with resources and supplies from her new home.

Bridging the Gap.name: Bridging the Gap
Bridging the Gap.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

In this exploration event, Brevin is being pulled by its waterlogged bridge into the Splinter Canyons. While Edivel goes to help the druids, the party must provide support for the town by helping with a series of emergencies.

Once the final fate of the bridge is known, Aythorn appears, beginning a conversation that continues in the next event.

Edivel immediately pinpoints the shouting as coming from The Root, Brevin's central town square. They are concerned that Brevin may be under attack and take off running for the center of town, as rumors have spread about the attack on Helkas and they fear the worst. When characters arrive, the place is in chaos.

In the center of town, a crowd has gathered on the large trunk at the heart of Brevin, standing on it as they point off in the direction of something you can't yet see. Suddenly, the platform shifts, creaking and cracking as it jolts closer to the edge of the canyons and throws several Thornlings to the ground.

A voice calls out, cutting through the crowd.

This is what I mean! If we don't cut the bridge loose now, we're going to lose the whole town!

The voice belongs to Triss Carpel (Arcturian, Thornling, they/them), Steward of Brevin, who quickly approaches the group, heading straight for Edivel. Triss is thrilled to see that Edivel is okay.

Reunion with Triss

If the party has already met Triss in @UUID[.2Ve19KR8g04QGtSc]{Natural Wonders}, they are grateful Edivel was found:

You found Edivel! Wonderful. We could use some good news right now. If we don't do something soon, the whole town is going to plunge into the canyons!

Meeting the Steward

If this is the party's first time in Brevin, Triss is grateful that someone made sure they got back home safely:

Edivel! I was about to send out a search party. At least you're okay, but I don't know if Brevin is going to be. The bridge fell, and it's dragging the whole town into the canyons! Maybe these travelers with you can help us? I’m Triss Carpel, by the way. Steward of Brevin. Though this isn’t exactly what I signed up for when I took the job!

Trouble in Town

Triss updates the party on what is currently happening to Brevin:

  • Brevin was getting ready to unveil their new vine bridge when the entire town began sliding into the canyons. The slide is being caused by the vines of the bridge, which were dislodged by the earthquake. They are hanging down into the canyon and weighing down the city.

  • Because Brevin is a seed city, the entire city is interconnected at its roots - the vines are a real danger.

  • The druids are attempting to coax the vines back into place, but are running out of time. They are attuned to the vines, so what they need is support.

Characters may have some knowledge of the situation as well.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check history 16]] check know that the seed cities are completely interlinked. If the vines cannot be fixed, the only way to stop them from dragging the city into the canyons is to cut them loose.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check nature 16]] check know that if the druids can get the vines to reach across the canyons, it will fix the problem.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check insight 16]] check can confirm that Triss is telling the truth, but is somewhat understating the problem - the city is in definite danger of being destroyed if the vines are not fixed soon.

Full answers below.

The Situation at Hand?

All those recent earthquakes shook the vines loose from the formation that the druids coaxed them into and now they're all just hanging down into the canyons below, weighing down the rest of the town. I don't want to lose the bridge, but it's pulling all of Brevin down into the canyons, and we can't lose everything we've nurtured here!

Seed City Interconnection?

Seed cities are amazing because the whole place grows together and everything is interconnected, but there's one big issue. What affects one part of the city affects us all. Those vines are linked into the roots of this town and it's dragging all of us into the canyons below.

Fixing the Problem/The Druids?

The druids are connected to those vines and they can get the bridge to stretch back across, but they need to do it fast and not get distracted from their mission. Otherwise it won't matter what the bridge does - we'll need to cut it free or all be smashed to pieces below!

Once Triss has finished explaining the situation, Edivel decides to take action.

Edivel immediately straightens up to their full height and gestures at their spellbook with the hand holding their wand.

Triss, I can help! I met Kali Andrella – the Kali Andrella -and she taught me a new vineweaving technique. I think I can use it to reinforce the vines that have fallen.

I'm sure the druids are working on getting the vines into a better position again, but this can buy them some more time. Please, let me try! And maybe my new friends can help you with things here in the meantime? They’ve already gotten me out of a lot of trouble!

Triss looks a bit skeptical, but slowly nods.

Edivel, check in with the druids at the bridge. The rest of you, you're with me. We need to get everyone out of danger!

Brevin Emergencies

As Edivel heads off to try to help with the vine weaving, Triss asks the party to keep Brevin safe – if there are any emergencies, it can take time and energy away from those trying to save the bridge.

Emergency Situations

Roll [[/gmroll 1d6 # Brevin Emergencies]] on the Brevin Emergencies table below to find the issue that the party must attempt to solve. Once it has either been successfully dealt with or failed, roll again. Each time the party finishes their attempt at a task, Brevin slides a bit closer to the canyons.

  • If the party successfully convinced Carmin to change their ways and head back to Brevin, the former brigand can successfully complete one task as the Canyon Crusader, giving the party an automatic success.

  • If the party helped the revelers on the road find their way to Brevin, they get the help of Leini and Karao on one check, giving them advantage.

The Final Outcome

  • If the party succeeds on three emergencies, Edivel and the druids pull off a final fix and the bridge is saved!

  • If the party fails to complete three total emergencies, Brevin's efforts fail and the bridge is lost!

@Embed[RollTable.8qfnSy3vQeLqMhdB inline rollable]

Frozen in Fear

A small huddle of Thornlings stands on the far side of the trunk platform in the center of the Root. Each time the town shifts, they are pulled closer and closer to the edge of the canyon, but they seem frozen in place, even as those around them yell to them to move. If they aren't moved soon, they could topple over the edge.

Assessing the Situation

With a successful [[/check medicine 17]] check or [[/check arcana 17]] check, characters know that the afflicted locals are not under an enchantment or spell, and are physically able to move.

  • A successful [[/check insight 16]] check determines that the group is frozen in fear.

The locals can be convinced to move with a successful [[/check 18 persuasion]] check or a spell that removes the frightened condition, like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3MYDjS6k9IYL0aTj]{Calm Emotions}, moving themselves out of danger.

If the party's attempt succeeds, the party is able to get the group to calm down and remove themselves from danger.

If the party's attempt fails, a pair of Brevin's druids divert from their other work to create hedges from the ground that physically move the frightened group away from the canyon's edge.

Dangling at the Edge

A scream comes from the edge of the Splinter Canyons. One of the druids who was working on stabilizing the bridge has fallen and is now dangling over the edge of the canyons, slowly losing their grip on the small bit of vine that they are currently holding on to.

Assessing the Situation

The party can pull the dangling druid up with a successful [[/check athletics 18]] check, or by using a spell capable of supporting their weight. If the check fails, the druid begins to slip.

If the party's attempt succeeds, the druid is saved by the party.

If the party's attempt fails, a few of the other druids redirect one of the vines from the bridge to grab their fallen comrade and bring them back to the top of the canyons.

Toxic Tonics

A powerfully bitter scent wafts through the air, accompanied by the sound of coughing and retching in the distance. A cart with a sign reading Temi’s Tonics has overturned and a few Thornlings in the area are doubled-over nearby.

Assessing the Situation

Characters can confirm that the noxious smells and sounds of sickness are coming from the overturned cart without a check. With a successful [[/check perception 18]] check, they see shattered bottles from the cart, whose liquids are leaking and mingling.

  • With a successful [[/check 18 nature]] to understand the winds and approach from the correct direction or [[/check 18 investigation]] to observe the pattern of the sick Brevinites and adjust their movements accordingly, characters can approach the overturned cart safely. Characters can also disperse the smell with a spell that clears the air (@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.FSMy6VAjDnXY9vWz]{Gust of Wind} or similar).

  • Any character who fails to avoid the fumes must succeed on a [[/save constitution 16]] saving throw or they take [[/damage 1d8 poison]] and have the poisoned condition.

  • To clean up the broken glass, characters must succeed on a [[/check 16 sleightofhand]] check to avoid cutting themselves — on a failure they take [[/damage 1d8 piercing]] damage.

If the party's attempt succeeds, the party successfully cleans up the tonics quickly, clearing the air and ensuring that the spill does no more damage.

If the party's attempt fails, the mix of tonics soaks into the ground, further weakening Brevin's roots.

Staking the Ground

Triss yells from across the trunk in the center of Brevin, where she has collected a pile of large wooden stakes whose roots are growing and curling even as they lie in front of you.

We use these root posts to reinforce trees as they grow – they may be able to counteract the weight of the vines. Can you drive these two in at the edge of the trunk here? I’ll handle the other side. Just pick a spot that feels right!

Assessing the Situation

Characters can find the best place to drive the stakes into the ground with a successful [[/check 18 nature]] check to tell where the trunk needs to be stabilized or [[/check 16 investigation check]] to observe what Triss is doing on the other side and follow her lead.

If characters know where the stakes should be placed, they successfully drive them into the ground with a [[/check 18 athletics]] check for each stake, with advantage. If they do not know where to place the stakes, each stake requires a [[/check 19 athletics]] check.

If the party's attempt succeeds, the stakes go into the ground easily and Triss shouts their thanks to the party for helping to slow down the movement of the town off of the cliff.

If the party's attempt fails, the stakes break and cannot be used. Triss runs to bring them to the druids, who are able to mend the stakes and give clearer directions about where they should go.

Animal Stampede

At the end of another jolt toward the canyons, the sound of a commotion and animal calls can be heard in the distance.

"They're loose!" someone calls, as a small herd of pavelins run into the center of town. The shaggy four-legged creatures are small, but their crowns of horns and diamond-sharp hooves can be dangerous if they run into or over a bystander. Already, the group has begun galloping around the outskirts of the town center, causing those in their path to jump back or step closer to the canyons edge.

Assessing the Situation

With a successful [[/check animalhandling 17]] or [[/check investigation 17]] check, the party knows that the out of control herd is being led by a pair of pavelins and has advantage on checks to stop the herd.

The leading pair can be stopped by physically grabbing them, requiring either a [[/check stealth 18]] or [[/check 18 acrobatics]] check to time the grab and a [[/check 18 athletics]] check to hold on. They can also be calmed with a successful [[/check 18 animalhandling]] check or a spell like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.hDOENzjuj5WpLq7B]{Animal Friendship} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.aL1F8fvYLtNzUbKu]{Speak with Animals}.

If the party's attempt succeeds, the herders catch up to the group and round them up, taking them off of the party's hands.

If the party's attempt fails, the townsfolk call down to one of the druids working on the bridge, who comes up and gets the herd calmed down.

Panic Attack

Friends, can you help? We've got a situation here!

Even in the middle of the chaos, Edivel's voice cuts through the clamor, but it is soon drowned out by another - an older thornling holds a sharp blade above their heads and is waving it wildly, hacking at parts of the ground around them with no apparent rhyme or reason.

You heard Triss - we need to cut it all free now! Or we're all going to die! Just like the people of Helkas!

Assessing the Situation

With a successful [[/check insight 17]] check, it is clear that the older Thornling is in a complete panic and will not easily be reasoned with until they are unarmed. While still holding the blade, they can only be persuaded to stop their cutting with a successful [[/check 23 persuasion]] check with disadvantage or a spell of 3rd level or higher.

Disarming the older Thornling requires success on a [[/check 18 sleightofhand]] check. Anyone who fails this check must also succeed on a [[/save 16 dexterity]] saving throw to avoid the Thornling's wild swings or they take [[/damage 1d8 slicing]] damage.

  • Once the Thornling has been disarmed, they can be persuaded to break off their attack with a 2nd-level spell like Calm Emotions, a successful [[/check 18 persuasion check]], or a stirring tale of the party's heroics in Helkas with a [[/check 17 performance]] check. If none of these checks succeed, the party may physically restrain the Thornling using any equipment they have on hand and a [[/check 15 athletics]] check.

If the party's attempt succeeds, the Thornling stops their attack and goes off to calm themselves down.

If the party's attempt fails, one of the Thornling's wild swings severs a part of the roots of the town that provide its support, immediately accelerating the speed of the slide of the town.

Brevin Bridge Outcomes

Depending on the party's actions, Edivel may or may not have been able to work with the town's druids to save the bridge.

If the bridge was successfully saved:

A cheer echoes through the air from the canyons edge, and Edivel quickly comes running back, high-fiving and celebrating with other locals around them.

We did it! Mostly the druids here — they know the vines better than anyone — but the vine weaving that Kali taught me? It helped, took some of the pressure of them so they could get the vines back in line and we could fix them back to the ground the way they should be. And all you did here around town? It meant we could focus, do our work together as one. And there you have it — the Brevin Bridge, just the way we promised. I only wish Aythorn was here to see it.

Akon Attunement: Bridge Saved

If the party manages save the bridge from destruction, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 canyonsSideCeremonySaved]] at the conclusion of the event.

Alternatively, if the bridge was lost:

"We're doing the best we can, but we have to cut it loose!" Triss' voice cuts through the noise again, followed by a sawing, ripping noise, as if something has been wrenched out of the dirt. The ground around you shudders one more time and then stops, followed by a distant echoing splash. Soon, Edivel reappears, walking toward you with slumped shoulders.

We did everything we could. The druids were amazing, getting the vines to work to form the bridge, and my vine weaving really helped, but the earth shaking has just done too much damage and we weren't able to stay focused on the work with so many things going on. The town is safe, though, right, and that's something. I hope Aythorn isn't too disappointed.

Abyss Attunement: Bridge Lost

If the bridge is ultimately destroyed, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 canyonsSideCeremonyLost]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

In either case, the party continues to meet Aythorn in the next event, @UUID[.focT6KUUgQVhn8lc]{Aythorn's Blessing}.

Next Steps

@UUID[.focT6KUUgQVhn8lc]{Aythorn's Blessing} immediately follows this event. To trigger the event, advance time forward by 1 hour.
Bridging the Gap.soverview: Back in Brevin, Aythorn is due any moment, but the vines of the living bridge have been damaged by the earthquake and are hanging down into the canyons free, dragging the parts of Brevin that they are anchored to toward the canyons. Edivel attempts to help using their new vine-weaving ability while the party helps to keep the town together. Aythorn, who witnessed Edivel's heroism offers them a blessing, and can offer the party one as well.
Bridging the Gap.sexposition:
At first glance, Brevin appears ready for a celebration. Flower garlands and decorative foliage are everywhere, and phrases like "Welcome to Brevin" and "Greetings Aythorn" appear on the hedges in splashes of floral color, as if the land itself welcomes your arrival.

Then you hear the shouts. Not the happy yells of celebration and joy, but panicked voices reacting and overlapping coming from the middle of town. Something is wrong here.
Bridging the Gap.ssummary: We tried to intervene to help Brevin as its new bridge threatened to drag it into the canyons, with the help of Edivel, who behaved so heroically that they received a blessing from the shard god Aythorn.

Natural Wonders.name: Natural Wonders
Natural Wonders.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, characters meet the Steward of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.qJlz7IOwWve46sLq]{Brevin}, Triss Carpel, and can do the following:

  • Learn that Edivel, an up-and-coming agrimage, is missing in action, whether or not the party has previously met the agrimage.

  • After an Earthquake, pledge to find Edivel and stop them from doing anything foolish to try to prove themselves at the bridge opening ceremony.

Concern for Edivel

@Embed[Actor.AJuixWYxgoyEo3tf]

As you take in the scene, a willowy Thornling runs towards you, a garland of flowers in their outstretched hands.

Welcome to Brevin! Please, have a garland! I'm Triss Carpel, the Steward of Brevin. Have you come for our bridge blessing celebration?

Brevin Steward, Triss Carpel, is worried about the missing local, Edivel, and hoping the party ran into the young Thornling during their journeys. The Steward can share the following:

The Worried Steward

An [[/check insight 16]] check confirms that they're worried about Edivel’s safety and sees them as a surrogate younger sibling to watch out for.

Brevin is currently preparing for a Bridge Blessing ceremony, which will include a visit from the shard god Aythorn.

Edivel Sprout, who promised to unveil a new marvel at the event, is nowhere to be found. The Steward is worried that Edivel may have gotten into some trouble - they can be foolhardy as they search out what they know.

  • If the party has met Edivel, the Steward is somewhat reassured but still concerned.

  • If the party saw Edivel fall into the ravine, the Steward is worried that they might be attacked by something in the canyons.

The Steward is willing to offer a reward of two @UUID[Item.tFyeCSvVP5TJ5Bib]{gem-encased flower petals} for Edivel's safe return.

About Brevin?

We’re not your average Arcturian town! Everything you see around you is grown from seeds, not built by hand. It took a lot of work and time cultivating this town into what you see before you, but we think it's been worth the effort.

Bridge ceremony?

That's right! A celebration to mark the opening of a new bridge, made of vines, grown across the Splinter Canyons.

Things aren’t usually quite this hectic, but Aythorn has sent word that they’re making an appearance at the event, so we have to make sure Brevin is looking its best for the Shard God.

About Aythorn?

Yes! One of the few roaming Shard Gods that people may run into! Aythorn is a very tall and colorful Thornling that likes to hand out blessings and pranks to travelers. From what I understand, you can always tell when they are about if you start seeing colorful flower petals appear out of nowhere.

Few of us have actually met Aythorn here in Brevin, so it's kind of a big deal they are coming!

Edivel is Missing

Say, this might be a long shot, but have you seen a young Thornling on your way here? His name is Edivel, he's an aspiring wizard, very enthusiastic, but still green. I haven't seen him in a bit, and he has a knack for getting himself into trouble, so I'm just a little worried right now.

You haven't run across him have you?

If the party hasn't completed [[/eventState canyonsSideSeed]], and notes that they haven't run into Edivel yet, then Triss' response is:

Triss' shoulder slump a touch upon hearing you haven't met him yet.

Well, that’s just a little worrying. I do hope he's okay. Thornlings are pretty hardy as a rule, but Edivel’s the type to try a spell for flame resistant plants by charging into a bonfire.

Could I ask you to search the area and see if you run into him? If you do, tell him to come check in. I'd really appreciate it. I just hope he hasn't wandered off to the Splinter Canyons again…

If the party has completed [[/eventState canyonsSideSeed]], and tells Triss they've seen Edivel, she says the following:

Triss looks immediately relieved.

Oh wonderful, at least he was okay last time you saw him. It sounds like they might have gone off on some fool headed quest though… do me a favor, would you? Go see if you can find him, and send him back here. I could use the extra help, and I'd feel a little less anxious if he was accounted for.

If the party completed [[/eventState canyonsSideFall]], and saw Edivel fall into the canyon, they can inform her of this, and get the following response:

Triss throws her hands up in exasperation.

Of course! I've told him to steer clear of the canyons, but that Sprout never listens.

Would you go get them? Normally, I'd send someone to go help them, but we're all hands on deck here trying to make the place look nice for Aythorn.

Besides, there are a lot of dangerous creatures in the canyons and none of us are quite as suited to the task as you. We thornlings are tough, but that only gets you so far.

Where to start looking?

Splinter Canyons, naturally. Edivel says it's a good place to practice magic without danger of harming anything important. Problem is that it's plenty dangerous on its own, what with the dangerous creatures, shifting rock and floods.

Any reward?

Sure, if you bring Edivel back home I can reward you for your trouble with a couple of @UUID[Item.tFyeCSvVP5TJ5Bib]{Gem-Encased Petals} which would be worth some gold in Ordain, or could be made into some very fine jewelry, if that's more your style.

A Sudden Shake

As the party begins wrapping up their conversation with Triss or begins to head off to other tasks, another tremor hits the area.

The ground rumbles beneath your feet, but it feels distant, as if something is stopping the disturbance from touching you. Around you, the buildings shake ever so slightly, their woody forms swaying like trees in a strong wind, but none seem damaged.

Triss exhales with reliefe.

Every time one of those tremors hit I'm glad we grew this place sturdy.

Tremors common here?

Steward Carpel shrugs slightly.

Common enough. They're worse in the canyons though, so watch your footing if you end up in there.

Best way into the canyons?

Triss gestures for your map.

I don't know all the ins and outs, but I can mark the easiest way in that I know of…

The Steward notes the best ways into the Canyons on your map before handing it back.

Now, this doesn't mean the way won't be dangerous, just less so.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

If the party already completed @UUID[.Rkbb3FUjqyPdDLJx]{The Fall's Gonna Kill You} and agree to go looking for Edivel, they will next encounter Edivel in @UUID[.vnRwvPy99V7Z0HiK]{A Rising Tide}

Otherwise, if the party has not yet run into Edivel, the next encounter will be @UUID[.Rkbb3FUjqyPdDLJx]{The Fall's Gonna Kill You} in the splinter canyons.
Natural Wonders.soverview: In Brevin, Steward Triss Carpel is overseeing the preparation for the bridge blessing ceremony, but Edivel, who promised a surprise for the festivities, is nowhere to be found, and they're getting concerned. Worried that Edivel might be in trouble (or having heard from the party about the thornling's fall into the canyons), the Steward asks the group to find the young thornling.
Natural Wonders.sexposition: In the heart of Brevin, past the saplings that hide the outline of small doors and fountains shaped by flower stems, a large trunk-like platform sits in the middle of a clearing, surrounded by the bustle of merchants and traders wheeling small wooden carts. Many of these impromptu stands are decorated with leaves or branches, carved to look as if they, like the rest of Brevin, grew from the ground they stand on.
Natural Wonders.ssummary: Brevin is in the middle of preparing for an upcoming celebration and one of the participants is missing. With the recent earthquake making the Splinter Canyons more dangerous, the town's Steward has asked us to track them down.

The Fall's Gonna Kill You.name: The Fall's Gonna Kill You
The Fall's Gonna Kill You.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, characters encounter or reunite with Edivel at the edge of the Splinter Canyons and see him fall into them. This is intended as a call-to-action to the rest of the quest.

Talking to Edivel

@embed[Actor.hLvc42ruEEclRBCZ]

If the party completed [[/eventState canyonsSideSeed]] and has met Edivel, they recognize him immediately, and he recognizes them, saying:

Edivel offers an energetic wave of his hand.

Hi friends! I hope your travels have been going well! Did you know there used to be a climbable path over to the Bramble Gully down there? Recent shakes have caused a bunch of the rock to fall away down there. I bet you could do it with the right climbing gear or spell, though…

Otherwise, the young Thornling enthusiastically introduces himself:

The figure at the edge of the cliffs waves as you come near.

Hello! I'm Edivel Sprout, Agrimage Wizard! Who are you?

The party can speak to Edivel here, covering the topics below, as well as any found in @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.YH9lcSrNRH5C3ZwC]{Planting a Seed}.

If the party previously completed [[/eventState canyonsSideBrevin] then this is the thornling that @UUID[Actor.AJuixWYxgoyEo3tf] sent them to find.

Triss is looking for you in Brevin.

Oh, yeah, I should probably check in with her and make sure everything's okay. They have a whole big event they are preparing for. But I do want to see if I can get to the bramble gulley first…

If you go back to Brevin, let Triss know I'm fine and will head back soon.

If the party attempts to persuade Edivel to return early, or attempts to subdue him, proceed immediately to @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.Rkbb3FUjqyPdDLJx#cliffside-collapse]{Cliffside Collapse} below.

Cliffside Collapse

Triggering the Tremor

While you are reading or preparing to read the narrative of the next section, mark the Earthquake Tremor event outcome as completed which will cause an earthquake animation to occur!

During that earthquake animation, delete or hide Edivel, which will make it appear as if he fell over the cliff during the tremor.

[[/outcome tremor]]

As the party heads towards Edivel, the ground shakes again.

Suddenly the ground shudders, a rolling sensation passing through the earth underfoot. The ground shudders and sways so strongly that you have to plant your feet to avoid falling over. At the same time you hear a loud crack and see Edivel suddenly lurch backward, crying out in surprise, before vanishing over the side of the cliff. Before you can intervene, a broad section of the cliff gives way and falls into the canyon after the thornling.

After a moment the shaking stops and it is silent.

You hear Edivel's voice, softly groan.

Ow.

There's a pause then he calls up at you:

Don't worry! I'm okay!

If characters head to the edge of the Splinter Canyons, they see Edivel below.

As you peer down into the steep canyons, Edivel's voice comes echoing out of it, from a place you can't quite make out.

Hello!? The rocks broke my fall, and nothing else! I am stuck down here though… If you could lend a hand that would be really great! If you have a moment!

Reaching Edivel

If characters wish to follow Edivel directly into the canyons, they must climb down.

Finding Edivel

A character with [[/skill perception 16 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 14]] notices that Edivel has landed on a rocky outcropping a hundred feet down. Luckily, there are ample grip points that would make climbing down possible, if risky.

Descending Into the Canyons

To descend the cliffs, characters must make a [[/skill athletics 15]] check. On success they are able to descend up to half their movement speed toward Edivel before repeating the skill check. Characters with a climb speed, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClimbersKit]{Climber's Kit}, or similar item may automatically descend without needing to make a check.

On a failure, they encounter a hazard from the Canyon Catastrophes table below.

Climbing Aids

Characters that make a successful [[/skill survival 16]] or [[/skill nature 14]] notice some old roots jutting out from the freshly exposed canyon wall. Using them would provide @advantage[2] on a character's first check to descend the cliff.

The Easy Way

If characters previously completed [[/eventState sideCanyonsBrevin]] then they know of a route given to them by Triss Carpel that will let them head into the canyon safely. This bypasses the need for the above climbing checks, and allows them to reach Edivel in 20 minutes, and without incident.

@Embed[RollTable.xtUlzhr0LusL2Xkc inline rollable]

Orbis Attunement: Hazardous Descent

Any character who first reaches the canyons by surviving a hazardous descent advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 canyonsSideFallHazards]] at the conclusion of the event.

Cora Attunement: Hazard-Free Descent

Any character who first reaches the canyons while bypassing any and all hazards they encounter advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 canyonsSideFallHazardFree]] at the conclusion of the event.

Mayis Attunement: The Easier Path

Any character who first reaches the canyons via Triss Carpel's directions or the House Cevher mines advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 canyonsSideFallEasier]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the characters make their way into the canyons they must free Edivel from the threat of rising water in @UUID[.vnRwvPy99V7Z0HiK]{A Rising Tide}.

Note: To move the token into the canyons, the GM must make the movement using the Unconstrained Movement tool — the party will not be able to move themselves there.
The Fall's Gonna Kill You.soverview: Edivel is on the edge of the canyons when a tremor causes them to fall. They are injured in the canyons with the waters rising and call out for help.
The Fall's Gonna Kill You.sexposition:
Ahead of you, the Splinter Canyons cut a large gash through the land that goes on for miles. On the near side is the lush flat land of the Arctus Plateau that you have become accustomed to. On the far side, in the distance, the city of Ordain gleams on the horizon.

Nearby you spot a small thornling in a red cloak pacing along the edge of the cliff, an open book in their hands. The contents of the tome seems to have utterly consumed their attention, and it's not until you draw closer they notice you.
The Fall's Gonna Kill You.ssummary: We saw a young Thornling, Edivel, tumble into the Splinter Canyons. While they landed without doing serious damage to themselves, they're now stuck down there and could use some help.

Fighting the Current.name: Fighting the Current
Fighting the Current.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party makes their way through the Splinter Canyons, either heading north toward Bramble Gully or south in search of Edivel's spellbook. Whichever way they go, they face the increasingly dangerous rapids of the Splinter Canyons — which they can face head on or try to avoid by climbing above them through the Canyons' rocky ledges.

Region Map Update

In the future, the region map will change to show flowing water that matches the event text noted here.

Seeking Safety

Edivel surveys the surroundings, then turns to face you, worry evident in he features, despite his best efforts to remain positive.

Okay, so, I'm not an expert adventurer or anything, so if you've got a better idea, say so, but I think we're either going to need to pick our way across the cliffside, or, cross the rapids. I don't really like either option, but staying here isn't any better.

Thoughts?

Surveying the Options

Characters with [[/skill survival 16 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill survival 14]] check note that there are dangers to both routes: if they make their way across the cliffs they will be at the mercy of falling rocks, unstable ground, and possibly territorial creatures riled up by recent events. If they decide to brave the rapids the threats are fewer, but no less dire, as debris in the water and a general drowning risk will be constant threats.

Climbing the Cliffs

Planning an Approach

Before setting off, members of the party can use their knowledge to make the group's progress easier:

  • With a successful [[/check perception 18]], any character can note places where the ground is uneven or slippery and avoid them. The entire party has advantage on the survival check to traverse the cliffs.

  • With a successful [[/check nature 17]], any character can note the location of vines and grasses on the cliffs that provide sturdy handholds. The entire party has advantages on dexterity checks and saves.

If the party chooses this path, they find the following:

You walk behind each other, weaving along the narrow path as it takes you above the canyon floor. The ground is slippery and the height makes every step a precarious one, but the true danger is less from what is ahead of you than what hangs from above, as showers of pebbles make it clear that pieces of the ledges overhead could fall at any moment.

Traversing the Ledges

To make their way through the ledges, the party must succeed on a a sequence of four challenges listed on the Climbing Hazards table below. These are group challenges - for all checks and saves, the entire party makes a roll. If at least half the group succeeds, the whole group succeeds. If not, the whole group fails.

Roll on the table below four times and challenge all members of the party to deal with each encountered obstacle.

@Embed[RollTable.9ZEoRuZnTju4xO1O inline rollable]

Cora Attunement: Climbing the Cliffs

Any character who successfully navigates the Splinter Canyons by climbing the cliffs advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 canyonsSideCurrentCliffs]] at the conclusion of the event.

Facing the Rapids

If the party chooses this path, or ends up in the rapids as the result of a fall, they find the following:

The water picks up speed, tossing and turning its way through the canyons as a rushing, surging river. Rocks and pieces of fallen carts caught in the water's path are dashed against the sides of the canyon as if they were nothing more than twigs and pebbles, and the echoing water almost roars as it slams its way between the canyon walls, as if it had a voice of its own.

Braving the Currents

To make their way through the currents, the party must make movement checks, which differ based on whether the party is going north (moving against the current) or south (moving with the current).

These are group challenges — for all checks and saves, the entire party makes a roll. If at least half the group succeeds, the whole group succeeds. If not, the whole group fails.

Any party member with a swim speed (whether innate or granted by an object or spell) has advantage on all checks while their swim speed is active.

Swimming Against the Current (North)

If the party is heading north, against the current, they must succeed on two [[/check athletics 16]] movement checks to summon the strength to move forward against the powerful rapids.

  • If they succeed on a check, they stay afloat, but must deal with one of the dangers from the Canyons Rapids Peril table below.

  • If they fail on a check, they must succeed on a [[/save strength 15]] saving throw or they are pulled fully into the water, taking [[/damage 1d8 bludgeoning]] from its pressure against their bodies. On a successful save, they take half damage. Whether or not the save was successful, they must reattempt the movement check.

If the party fails a movement check twice in a row, or at the GM's discretion, they are unable to make their way through the currents and must try going above instead, via @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.QmC0z4DS80SLsqD2#climbing-the-cliffs]{Climbing the Cliffs}.

Swimming With The Current (South)

If the party is heading south, against the current, they must succeed on two successive [[/check acrobatics 16]] checks to summon the strength to move forward against the powerful rapids.

  • If they succeed on a check, they stay afloat, but must deal with one of the dangers from the Canyons Rapids Peril table below.

  • If they fail on a check, they must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw or they are tossed by the rapids into the side of the canyons, taking [[/damage 1d8 bludgeoning]] from the impact. On a successful save, they take half damage. Whether or not the save was successful, they must reattempt the movement check.

If the party fails a movement check twice in a row, or at the GM's discretion, they are unable to make their way through the currents and must try going above instead, via @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.QmC0z4DS80SLsqD2#climbing-the-cliffs]{Climbing the Cliffs}.

@Embed[RollTable.vFVfKkgss4m5xp5s inline rollable]

Ragen Attunement: Facing the Rapids

Any character who successfully navigates the Splinter Canyons by facing the rapids advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 canyonsSideCurrentRapids]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has overcome this challenge, they will have either made their way towards Bramble Gully and the @UUID[.wayoxatxc7P06K0t]{Growing Pains} event, or south in search of Edivel's spellbook and the @UUID[.q3RclLggX8rF6npb]{Supplies and Demands} event.
Fighting the Current.soverview: With the currents in the Splinter Canyons picking up speed, the party must try to make their way to their next location either by braving the rushing waters or trying to stay above them on a precarious cliff walk.
Fighting the Current.sexposition:
Edivel points down to the rushing water below you, which has spilled over the banks of the canyon and reaches to the steep walls, twisting and turning between them with ever-growing speed.

Well… my spellbook fell down there. On the upside, it's enchanted, so the water won't hurt it, but the downside is, I think it was washed downstream. I'm going to need to get it back…
Fighting the Current.ssummary: We found a path through the treacherous surging water of the Splinter Canyons and navigated our way upstream with Edivel in tow.

The New Steed's Point.name: The New Steed's Point
The New Steed's Point.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

This is an event that happens after some time has passed since Thorny Predicaments and is an opportunity to catch up with Kali and see what she has done to rebuild Steed's Point.

@Embed[Actor.FAWXlZTU8syDdRFy]

Catching up with Kali

Kali is in the midst of working, but happy to see the party.

Kali walks toward you, but somehow never stops working, her dancing motions somehow divided between pruning a thorny edge, casting a spell in its direction, and setting goods out on an impromptu table made of wood scraps to her side.

Don’t mind me. Just keeping my hands busy. Figured out a few new defenses against the jurtak in case they’re foolish enough to show their faces around here again. Hopefully with them run off, folks will feel comfortable enough to come by and buy some of what we have for trade.

If the party completed @UUID[JournalEntry.emberNainSide000.JournalEntryPage.hJn9ofVtP4DxSTLe]{The Rickety Man} in the Book of Tales quest, and Rattletrap is still alive, the sound of metal clanging can be clearly heard near by.

A loud metal clang from in the distance brings a smile to Kali's face.

That’s Rattletrap. Or Bertron. I go back and forth on what to call him nearly as much as he goes back and forth on what to call himself. We're still not fully sure how he survived inside of Rattletrap, but I do know this. – he’s still the heart and soul of Steed’s Point, and he’s even gotten back into doing some smithing, though I keep him far away from the fire. Surviving death one time is more than enough. Thanks for your part in bringing us back together.

The Revival of Steed's Point

Kali is happy to tell the party what she's gotten up to since leaving Steed's Point. She shares the following:

We still have a lot to do to make Steed's Point anything like what it used to be. And in some ways, it can't be the same and we'd be fools to try. Can't bring back everyone lost, can't undo what time has done. What we can do is build back, make this a place folks feel safe visiting, trading, and sharing stories. With everything going on in these parts right now, travelers need a place they can think of as a safe resting place. And if those Otherhood or anyone else tries to come take it away again, they'll see just how strong we are.

Kali wants to put Steed’s Point back on the map in a good way and has started making magic items and other sundries available to travelers. She’d appreciate if the party spread the world that Steed’s Point is safe again.

As you can see, I'm doing my part to attract the right sort, putting together a few items that folks will like and trying to make the place hospitable. If you can tell those you meet that Steed's Point is a safe place to land, I'd appreciate it.

If the party has completed the "Grassland Artifice" standalone event, and Moriah is alive, she updates the group on her daughter's whereabouts.

You just missed Moriah. Still got the wanderlust in her feet. I’d almost blame her for it if I didn’t know I’m the one who probably gave it to her. But now Steed’s Point is on her travels, and she brings us things from near and far to help build this place back up. Feels like we’re mother and daughter again, ready to take on the world.

Kali has also kept up to date on the party's activities. If they saved Brevin, she congratulates them.

I had no doubt you and the young agrimage would be able to set Brevin to rights — you're a capable group of adventurers if I've ever met any.

Regardless of the outcome of Brevin, she has kept up a correspondence with Edivel.

In case you're wondering how that Edivel is doing, I'm keeping an eye on them from afar as best I can. Last I heard, they'd had an unfortunate incident with some cave wasps and came back to Brevin lit up like a starry night, but they're getting better at agrimagic too. They'll be a force to reckon with one of these days. Eventually.

Items For Sale

With their talk complete, Kali is open for business as a seller, with a few items for trade.

First One's Free

As a thank you for all they have done for her and for Steed's Point, Kali will allow the group to take one item for free from the following list. With a successful [[/check persuasion 20]], the party can convince Kali to part with one additional item at no cost.

  • @UUID[Item.FKsd5PGexRuqn264]{Growing Thorns}

  • a pouch of Throwing Stones, which have the properties of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.SqTtbBCfiEsmZ36N]{Beads of Force}

  • an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.i89okN7GFTWHsvPy]{Herbalism Kit}

  • an @UUID[Item.FXNnFGmbtvZrJEhq]{Everbloom}

  • A @UUID[Item.Qg2cqy4rAf4YSBx0]{Potion of Healing}

In addition, Kali will throw in a bonus item for each of the following conditions met.

  • If the party saved Brevin, she gives them an additional @UUID[Item.Qg2cqy4rAf4YSBx0]{Potion of Healing} and a @UUID[Item.a5aQZkftctSTDDNC]{Potion of Climbing}.

  • If the party completed Grassland Artifice and she has been reunited with Moriah, she shares some of the knowledge that Moriah has brought from her recent travels, clearing the fog of war from an area TBD.

  • If the party helped Rattletrap, she gives them a new tool from his smithing shop, a @UUID[Item.VWcCUckiQG1vFmum]{Temp Tool}, which they can use in an emergency if needed.

As the party departs, Kali wishes them well on their next adventures and offers an incentive to return.

As you turn to exit Steed's Point, Kali waves you off while simultaneously checking over her remaining goods.

Thank you all for visiting! You're welcome back any time, and while I can't always give away my goods, you'll always get the Kali Andrella discount for Friends of Steed's Point. I hope you take advantage soon! And since you helped me, I hope you'll take a little help of your own.

She smiles and waves in your direction as a warm breeze sweeps around you and it feels for a moment as if someone's steady hand is on your back, pushing you forward as you head into your next adventure.

Concluding the Event

A Parting Gift

Thanks to Kali’s magic, the entire party has advantage on their next skill check, as if they had the benefits of the Help action.

Next Steps

This ends the general quest line. The party is free to return to Steed's Point in the future to purchase items at a 20% discount.
The New Steed's Point.soverview: The party returns to Steed's Point and catches up with Kali Andrella, who has begun rebuilding the town.
The New Steed's Point.sexposition:
At first glance, Steed's Point looks unchanged from your last visit - there are still thorny hedges winding through its center, and many of the buildings seem as if they have seen better days. But where before the settlement seemed abandoned other than the lonely construct Rattletrap, now there are signs of life. Planks have been nailed over the holes in some of the walls, and some of the former gaps in the roofs have been stuffed with new thatch. As you step into the settlement, the thorns seem to melt away, and Kali steps out from behind a freshly-painted door, carrying a basket filled with goods.

Welcome to Steed's Point - we're so glad you came to vi—

Kali stops talking as she sees you.

Oh, friends! I didn't see you there! So glad you came back for a visit.
The New Steed's Point.ssummary: We visited Kali Andrella in Steed's Point and saw the rebuilding work she's done in the area!

Aythorn's Blessings.name: Aythorn's Blessings
Aythorn's Blessings.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

In this social event, the party meets the shard god Aythorn, who is visiting Brevin to celebrate the new bridge. Whether or not Brevin succeeded at saving the bridge, Aythorn is excited to see the seed-grown town and gives it a blessing of prosperity, but their response to the party differs based on the outcome of @UUID[.yWP8ZAyLMGIWpaRU]{Bridging the Gap}.

The vista composition remains on "Brevin Festival" by default but can be swapped to "Brevin Festival, Bridge Complete" if the party saved the bridge.

@Embed[Actor.HUIhXv1i0eywY5Q5]

The Arrival of Aythorn

Aythorn moves to the center of the platform at the heart of Brevin, seeming to float as much as they walk, trailing flower petals as they go.

Characters who succeed on a [[/check religion 15]] check, have [[/knowledge gods]], or are of [[/culture emberArcturian]] know that Aythorn is the god of eternal mischief and happiness during times of trouble, and that it is widely believed that the flower blossoms they leave behind are a sign of either luck or trouble - often both.

Characters can pick up one of the blossoms in Aythorn's wake with a successful [[/check sleightofhand 16]] - it immediately dissolves into air on their fingertips, but leaves them with a sense of calm and beauty. They gain the benefits that would come from taking a short rest.

As Aythorn reaches the large platform at the heart of Brevin, ignoring any chaos and clutter they pass along the way, they turn to address the still-growing crowd.

Do not worry about the chaos, my friends – to be honest, I like a gathering that isn’t too set in its ways, and a place whose people come together to strive against the dangers of the unexpected. In truth, I have been looking forward to my visit here for some time - a city that grows from the ground was too much of a temptation for me to resist, and it is somehow even lovelier than I'd imaged.

From this point, Aythorn's conversation shifts slightly based on the outcome of the bridge.

A Fallen Bridge

In the end, new vines will grow, and long after the bridge has become commonplace, you will remember all that you have done here today. But long speeches are for other gods. What if, instead, I give you one more thing to remember?

A Completed Bridge

I am sure that you are tired from your many efforts here today, but you are to be commended for all you have accomplished. In many ways, this is exactly how I hoped to find you all — giving your all for each other. Nectar cider all around! And, if you're up for it, I'll give you one more thing to celebrate!

In either case, Aythorn provides a blessing for the town.

A Blessing for Brevin

Aythorn spreads their arms wide, and a rain of blossoms falls on the city, some in the colors of flowers you've seen before and some in impossible shades of silver and gold.

I bless this town with a bit of luck, at least for a time. The things you've misplaced may suddenly be found. The love you seek may unexpectedly find you. The flowers you plant will be that much brighter and the bonds you make that much stronger.

The murmuring in the crowd grows louder until it threatens to become a full-throated cheer. But before the noise can overpower them, Aythorn clears their throat, and the town grows quiet again.

But I will be watching - anyone who uses their luck to harm another while within Brevin will find small misfortunes following them as soon as they step outside of its gates - holes in their shoes, being caught in the rain, accidentally sitting down right in a patch of crawleaf or on top of a pricklebush. So use your luck well. Lest it run out.

And with a final flourish of their hand, Aythorn bows and walks into the excitedly milling crowd.

Any player character who observes Aythorn bestow this blessing is overcome with feelings of positivity and possibility, gaining the benefits of Inspiration. In addition, all skill checks made within the Brevin city limits are made with advantage.

Leaving Brevin

Farewell from Edivel

As the party prepares to depart, Edivel bids them goodbye and gives them 2 @UUID[Item.tFyeCSvVP5TJ5Bib]{Gem-Encased Petals}.

Thank you all for your help! I am so glad our paths crossed back on the Plateau. Couldn't have done this all without you. There's no real way to repay you, but we'll try. Triss — Steward Carpel, that is — gave me these gems to pass on to you for helping to keep me out of trouble. You can keep them or spend them, whatever works for you!

Edivel can share any of the following:

  • Whether or not the bridge was saved, Edivel's work alongside the druids of Brevin made them feel more a part of the community than ever before.

  • While they plan to continue their study of agrimagic, they now feel that they have a mentor in Kali Andrella and can learn from her while staying safe in Brevin. They are going to focus on figuring out a way to keep the ground and those on it steady during earthquakes.

  • The party is welcome to visit them in Brevin anytime.

  • If the bridge was destroyed, they reassure the party that a new one will be built and eventually there will be a bridge across the Splinter Canyons between the Arctus Plateau and the outskirts of Ordain.

Edivel's Plans?

I've been wandering around the Plateau for a long time trying to figure out agrimagic, and I'm still going to figure it all out, don't you worry, but working along with the druids on the bridge? Reminds me that there's a lot I can do closer to home. Probably less dangerous too. And this way you know where to find me - come back anytime!

Learning Agrimagic?

Kali and I magicked up a little something so we can talk once in a while, and she can give me ideas on what I can learn next. With her as my teacher, I'm going to be a great agrimage, but more than that, I want to figure out some way to keep folks steady on the ground in the middle of all these earthquakes - maybe something with magic and roots and even a bit of that sticky stuff on those gumtoads in the canyons.

The Brevin Bridge?

With everything we all went through to get the bridge up, I just hope people use it. Aythorn's blessing should help - who doesn't want to visit a lucky town!

The loss of the Brevin Bridge?

Don't worry about the bridge. I was sad to see it fall into the canyons too, but the druids are already at work on a new one, and with our new luck. I'm sure it'll be done in no time!

Aythorn's Boon

As the party departs Brevin, Aythorn appears in front of them.

You smell the faintest hint of grass and forests, flowers and dew, and then Aythorn stands in front of you, almost larger than life.

The Shard God's Boon

Aythorn commends the party on facing the many dangers of the area to help a stranger.

I have been following a bit of your adventures through the Arctus Plateau. I will admit, the sight of a Thornling falling end over end into a canyon first caught my attention - and between us, I may have helped to smooth their path to the canyon floor just a little. But you? You are what truly intrigues me.

Aythorn is impressed by the party's willingness to help Edivel, and offers them a boon that will help for the days to come, which they believe will bring more danger.

In recent days, strife and trouble seem to be multiplying. Even the ground shakes in anger. And yet you helped a stranger, kept them safe long enough for them to follow their dream. I believe there is more to come for you, and will offer you a small boon, if you choose to accept it.

Heart Attunement: Aythorn's Blessing

If the party accepts Aythorn's blessing, their, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 canyonsSideBlessing]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

This ends the Thorny Predicaments quest for the moment, though the party can run into Kali Andrella in Nain at a later date in @UUID[.e8T6ACfUEzwMgxGB]{Next Year In Nain} if she was convinced to leave Steed's Point in @UUID[.KyrjXxjCEDQRXuuu]{A Dying Art}, or visit her again in Steed's Point if she remained there, in either @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.EuiLwch7KTh32EpJ]{Fond Farewell} or @UUID[JournalEntry.jcQpIeQ0gpD4UsHM.JournalEntryPage.NXQyM1vHizHyFdR6]{Kali On The Fence}, depending on the circumstances of her remaining in Steed's Point.
Aythorn's Blessings.soverview: Aythorn, who has arrived to the Brevin bridge celebration, offers their commentary and blessings, which differ based on the state of the bridge at the end of the previous event.
Aythorn's Blessings.sexposition:
Flower petals float in on the breeze and begin to swirl, circling in and among each other as they gain speed, as if they were dancing to a tune you can't quite hear, moving faster and faster until they transform into a large Thornling with an easy smile and an aura that hums with Ember's power.

Aythorn.

Even if you didn't feel the magic in the air or recognize the shard god in front of you, the excited whispers that ripple through the crowd would make it unmistakably clear.

"I'll give you this much," the shard god says, their voice somehow a mix of babbling brook, the echo of laughter, and a rustle of leaves, but still ringing out clear and strong. "You throw an unconventional party."
Aythorn's Blessings.ssummary: We met the shard god Aythorn, who offered us, and the town of Brevin, a blessing.

Kali On The Fence.name: Kali On The Fence
Kali On The Fence.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

This is a social event that happens after some time has passed since Thorny Predicaments and is an opportunity to catch up with Kali in Steed's Point. While visiting Kali, parties can:

  • Get a helpful item from her in trade for information about the world

  • Attempt to convince her to either rebuild Steed's Point or resettle in Nain

A Friendly Reunion with Kali

@Embed[Actor.FAWXlZTU8syDdRFy readaloud= "Kali sits in much the same place as she was when you left her. While she appears calm, there is something in the way she twists her hands together and occasionally furrows her brow that suggests a bit of unease."]

Catching Up With Kali

If asked, Kali is happy to share what she's been up to.

You know, I’ve had a couple of visitors since I last saw you – I assume you’ve spread the word about me. Or Edivel Sprout has. Whoever it was, I thank you. Not too many are willing to brave the jurtak and the gore birds for little ol' me, but the occasional traveling adventurer has managed to fight their way in, ask me to explain a spell or two. I've even started preparing a few healing kits and supplies they can take back with them into the world. Least I can do. They keep the place clear of creatures, and it's nice to occasionally hear from someone outside of my own head. Makes me think that maybe I should rebuild this place for real. Or settle in Nain. Still can't quite make up my mind.

Kali is eager to hear about what's going on in the outside world and invites the party to tell her something about their recent adventures.

Now I'm not sure what brings you here, but I'm not letting you leave without telling me a bit of what's going on out there in the world. What have you been up to since you left here?

She generally responds positively to anything the party says and gives them a @UUID[Item.Qg2cqy4rAf4YSBx0]{Healing Potion} at the end of the conversation, with the following exceptions:

  • If the party has news of Moriah, she is thrilled, and offers them a handful of something new she's been cooking up, Throwing Stones, which have the properties of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.SqTtbBCfiEsmZ36N]{Beads of Force}, as a thank you for the news.

    Moriah? Really? How's she looking? Is she eating? Did she say she was going to visit? Sorry, don't mean to overwhelm you with questions. I'm sure I'll reconnect with her at some point. But knowing that she knows about me and that we might see each other again some day soon? That's worth a lot, even if I'm not quite sure how we'll get along this time. I'm not sure I can pay you back, but here's a little something I've been whipping up, in case it helps you on your travels.

  • If the party knows that Rattletrap is Bertron, she's intrigued, and offers them an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.i89okN7GFTWHsvPy]{Herbalism Kit} as a thank you for the news.

    That sounds like a wild story. Something from an Amalthea tale. Might be worth going out there and hearing it from Rattletrap … or should I say Bertron … for myself. Though I don't know how Bertron would feel about me, what he'd think about what this place has become. Maybe one day I'll find out. In the meantime, here. Take one of these herbalism kits for the road - you never know when it'll come in handy.

  • If the party saved Brevin, she's happy to hear it, and offers them a second @UUID[Item.Qg2cqy4rAf4YSBx0]{Healing Potion}.

    I knew you all could do it. I'm glad that what I taught Edivel did its part. That young agrimage is promising - might be a legend of their own one day. And I'm sure you had a part to play in keeping them safe, so here's something extra for your packs, as a thank you.

Convincing Kali

Making Their Case

If desired, the party can attempt to convince Kali to leave Steed's Point, though she is reluctant to talk about her current decision-making process.

I'm happy to have you here, and you're always welcome to visit, but I'm in the middle of some things and don't have time to talk through every thing I'm weighing while I figure out what's next. And since you don't have any desperate agrimages with you needing training, I'm inclined to take my time figuring things out. If do appreciate you, though, so if you have an argument to make, I'll listen.

To convince Kali, the party must succeed on a [[/check 26 persuasion]] check. This check can be affected as follows:

  • If the party brought Kali new news of Moriah, they have advantage on the check if persuading her to leave.

  • If the party brought Kali news of Rattletrap having the spirit of Bertron Steed, they have advantage on the check if persuading her to stay.

  • If the party successfully saved Brevin, the DC of the check lowers by 3 regardless of whether they are persuading her to leave or stay.

If the party successfully convinces Kali to leave for Nain, she begins packing up her goods and equipment.

You're right. It's time to leave this place. Gonna head to Nain, look up my old pal Zenodora - see if she's still running her General Store. And if she isn't … all I need is little space and the right ingredients and I'll make a life for myself, no problem.

If they convince her to rebuild, she begins preparing for that.

You're right. With all the little bibs and bobs I'm making for travelers, I'm already starting to put Steed's Point back on the map. Why not go all the way? I'm going to start fixing this place up. If you come back in a season or two, it'll be a whole new place.

If they fail to convince her, she bids them farewell.

I hear what you're saying, but I'm just still not sure. And there's no rush to decide these days. Until I do, you're always welcome here. Good luck on your travels.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This ends the quest line. Parties are free to continue exploring the Arctus Plateau.
Kali On The Fence.soverview: The party returns to Steed's Point to find it generally unchanged. Kali still waits to make her decision, but is happy to hear news of the outside world. If desired, the party may attempt to get her to make a choice.
Kali On The Fence.sexposition:
Steed's Point is much the same as you left it - filled with broken buildings and winding thorns. Here and there, a glimpse of claw or beak or blood on the ground reveals the continued presence of the jurtak and gore birds, even if none come close enough for battle. A clang of metal in the distance is likely Rattletrap, continuing his tending of the crops. Ahead of you, what was once a tangled mass of vines and thorns parts, shrinking back on itself to reveal a doorway - the direct route to Kali.

You step through into her home, where she sits, still tending her indoor garden.

Hello there, adventurers. I am not surprised to see you have returned, it is hard to resist the charms of Steed's Point, even now.
Kali On The Fence.ssummary: We visited Kali Andrella in Steed's Point to say hello, and to see if she'd come any closer to a decision about whether to leave the ruined settlement or try to rebuild it.

Rumors in Rock Bottom.name: Rumors in Rock Bottom
Rumors in Rock Bottom.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration event allows the party to continue their investigation into the Renegade Construct's so-called murder of Kellan Lorde by visiting the scene of the impact in Rock Bottom — a tent town that resides below Arcturel on the sinkhole floor. In this event, the characters can:

  • Gather rumors from locals about the scene of the impact, where Kellan Lorde and the Renegade Construct are said to have hit the ground after their perilous fall.

  • Investigate the scene of the impact itself for forensic evidence and signs of the Renegade Construct's survival.

  • Encounter a mushroom farmer named @UUID[Actor.BU1Vzjo20Q4CUjTK]{Ifton Shepp}, a retired artificer who aided the constructs before sending them on their way.

The Itinerant Spelunkers

If the party approaches the itinerant spelunkers — a human @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.O3ABqI55Ir1du1Xa]{Scout} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.archetype.Item.archetypeScout00] named Thura and a Kiska @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.J8xjoG4Dxb8WkHtV]{Veteran} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.archetype.Item.fighter000000000] named Beet — the characters will be able to quickly learn about the "final" location of the crime scene, where Kellan and the Renegade Construct fell to the sinkhole floor, along with a few generalized pieces of information about Rock Bottom itself.

You take a closer look at the rambunctious wine-swilling duo on the boardwalk. An aged Kiska soldier lovingly cradles the wine bottle like a newborn babe, while a younger human next to him tries to playfully snatch it away. This tawny-haired young man is clad in loose Arcturian leathers, and his Kiska companion wears mismatched pieces of Lowland splint mail. These two bleary-eyed revelers strike you as accomplished subterannean scouts, despite their current state of reckless abandon.

What the Spelunkers Have Seen

If the party mentions their investigation to Thura (Chaotic Neutral, Arcturian Human, he/him) and Beet (Chaotic Neutral, Arcturian Kiska, he/him), the itinerant spelunkers are willing to share some information, culminating in general directions to the scene of the impact:

The young scout shoots you a swift glance at your mention of the Renegade Construct, a look marked by equal parts curiosity and recognition … "Well, there's a giant crater in the boardwalk a stone's throw away from here, if that's what you're talking about," he says.

The Kiska takes a swig from the wine bottle and offers a few words of his own without looking up:

"Cevher and Silver Beam sent a search team down to check it out, but their findings were … what did they call it, Thura?"

"Inconclusive."

"That's right. 'Inconclusive'. Like every mystery in Rock Bottom."

Thura the scout snatches the bottle and takes a big draught of his own. "All the same, we're happy to point you kind folks towards the crater. And it goes without saying …"

The Kiska interrupts: "But he'll say it anyway."

"A donation would certainly help your cause." The young scout flashes a black-toothed grin in salutation.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check suggests that Thura and Beet are being sincere with the party.

Characters who succeed on a [[[/skill deception 13]], [[/skill persuasion 13]], or [[/skill intimidation 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]], [[/skillCheck deception 13]], or [[/skillCheck intimidation 13]] check are able to compel Thura and Beet to reveal more, as indicated below. Any character who offers a "donation" of at least 5 gp (or another bottle of wine) automatically succeeds on these Charisma checks. Additional information includes:

  • Mutual suspicion about Silver Beam and House Cevher operations in the Sinkhole Depths.

  • A general distrust for the authority of House Cevher in Arcturel. Zodi Trask is an amiable enough fellow, but he's a puppet of Trading House industrialism.

  • An explanation of Rock Bottom's ramshackle culture of wayward travelers and lost causes.

If the characters don't speak with the spelunkers but choose to look around Rock Bottom for themselves, they can still locate the scene of the impact; it just takes a short while longer.

Exploring the Scene of the Impact

Any character who spends 30 minutes to search Rock Bottom and makes a successful [[/skill perception 15]] or [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check is able to locate the scene of the impact without assistance.

The scene of the impact is recognizable as a section of wooden boardwalk marked by splintered wooden planks surrounding a large hole. The fragmented wooden planks are stained with blood, and the impact appears to have left a nearly 10-foot-wide shallow basin.

Characters can examine the impact site for clues and other details:

[[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] The character can spot heavy gouges in the wooden boardwalk near the impact that match the hard angles of a Chessman's chassis, along with an indentation in the ground beneath the boardwalk that roughly matches the outline of an adult humanoid. Gallons of blood appear to have seeped into the earth below.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: A loose scattering of components that could be from a Chessman construct (small bolts, nuts, and wires) can be found trailing away from the impact site to the northeast, towards Ifton Shepp's Mushroom Farm.

[[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]]The character is able to confirm the site as the location of an impact from a humanoid and a construct, via the splinter patterns in the boardwalk, the splash patterns and directional splatter of blood, and a rough estimate of the parabolic approach vector of the falling victims.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The loose scattering of components that trail off to the northeast towards Ifton Shepp's mushroom farm appear to match the materials used in the manufacture of Chessmen.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on this check.

[[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] The character is familiar enough with Arcturel and Rock Bottom to know that this impact site is recent enough to match the timeline of events surrounding the accident in Lower Arcturel.

Once the party has had enough time to search the scene of the impact, they can continue their investigation by following leads to the mushroom farmer Ifton Shepp, who cultivates a farm nearby.

The Mushroom Farmer

If the party decides to approach the mushroom farm, they'll meet some of Rock Bottom's most interesting characters — the disgraced artificer @UUID[Actor.BU1Vzjo20Q4CUjTK]{Ifton Shepp} and his @UUID[Actor.aXNNESwMlzmcTccK]{Woven Construct} companion named Totter. Not only does Ifton Shepp have a past that's intertwined with Vartholomew Chess and the Silver Beam Consortium, his recent run-in with the Renegade Construct makes him a person of significant interest.

You survey the earthen sprawl of a modest mushroom farm that occupies a lonely corner of this derelict tent town. A field of edible greencaps and sprite-stools grow here in lush abundance, tended by a squat construct made of rustic timber, who brandishes a spade with stoic proficiency.

A few small tents conceal what are likely the dwelling and storage areas of whoever lives here, and you regard a few crates of newly harvested mushrooms nearby. A tiny wisp of smoke trails up from what must be a cook's fire pit inside, as the hearty smell of mushroom stew also suggests. The wooden automaton continues in its work, undeterred and nonplussed by your arrival.

The characters have a moment to visually inspect the area before meeting the mushroom farm's residents.

Surveying the Mushroom Field

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check is able to notice a few details of interest:

  • The character catches a brief glimpse of someone inside the tent, looking out at the party through a darkened flap, but briefly illuminated by the fire pit inside.

  • One crate among the mushroom crates is stocked full with what appears to be lumber.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: The person inside the tent was a cloaked human with a masculine silhouette. The lumber in the crate resembles loose or replacement parts for the wooden construct that works the field.

Any character who makes a successful [[/skill history 17]] [[/skillCheck society 17]] check knows the tale of an ex-assistant of Vartholomew Chess named Ifton Shepp, who took residence in Rock Bottom after the two artificers had a falling out. Rumor has it that Shepp runs a mushroom farm nearby. Perhaps this is that very farm.
