  • Characters who succeed on this check gain advantage on skill checks made to observe and influence Ifton Shepp (see "A Conversation with Ifton Shepp" below).

A successful [[/skill survival 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check allows a character to locate some curious tracks at the perimeter of the farmyard. Since it doesn't rain here in Rock Bottom, the soil is rarely upturned.

  • There are heavy booted footprints here that don't match the footprint of the wooden construct that works in the field. It's possible they match the humanoid inside the tent, but it's hard to say. The depth of the tracks suggests that whoever left them is quite heavy.

  • The tracks appear to head eastward into the Sinkhole Depths, and there are more outgoing tracks than incoming ones.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success: There are four distinct sets of tracks that look remarkably similar, recognizable from each other by their age and the most minor of physical inconsistencies. The oldest tracks are several months old, while the newest seem to have been left here a week ago or less.

If the party approaches the wooden construct or the tents, or after they've surveyed the area for a few minutes, they'll be promptly greeted by the mushroom farm's owner — the semi-retired artificer known as Ifton Shepp.

The wooden construct looks up toward the sound of booted footsteps on the boardwalk. You follow its gaze to see someone emerging from the darkened tent, a cloaked humanoid whose cautious yet comfortable body language suggests an utmost familiarity with this place. He approaches you, and speaks:

Hello, travelers. I see you've met Totter.

He glances toward the construct, who looks up with a shrug of benevolent indifference, before sizing you up once more.

You seem to be a bit lost. Or do you simply seek the finest mushrooms the Depths have to offer? I'm afraid there's little else for you here. And while I usually sell my wares in bulk, it seems like a fine day for exceptions.

@Embed[Actor.BU1Vzjo20Q4CUjTK]

A Conversation with Ifton Shepp

The hermetic mushroom farmer known as Ifton Shepp is one of Rock Bottom's most well-known and self-reliant citizens, known to keep the company of his construct companion Totter and few others. Once the characters reveal their intentions about the investigation, Ifton Shepp has the following to say:

"Well, they say everything hits Rock Bottom sooner or later … The name's Shepp. Ifton Shepp. And yes, I've heard about this 'renegade' Chessman and the accident upstairs. They say the miner didn't survive the fall, and as far as we locals can tell, there wasn't much left to find.

So, while it's been nice meeting you all, I have some mushrooms to feed. If you don't mind, I'll respectfully bid you a farewell."

The lonesome mushroom farmer turns back to his field.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check suggests that Ifton Shepp is hiding something from the party.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: Ifton Shepp keeps glancing towards the crate of body parts and the wooden construct, as if they've occupied his thoughts since you mentioned the Renegade Construct.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 15]], [[/skill persuasion 15]], or [[/skill intimidation 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]], [[/skillCheck deception 15]], or [[/skillCheck intimidation 15]] check is able to compel Ifton Shepp to reveal more information, some of which is detailed below.

  • A character who presents a @UUID[Item.F6nv7SQCf2xSYxcR]{Chessian Souvenir} to Ifton Shepp automatically succeeds on these checks.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] and [[/knowledge subterranea]] have advantage on these checks.

  • [[/ancestry emberAltyra]] characters have disadvantage on this check.

The information Ifton Shepp provides includes the following:

  • Not only did the Renegade Construct come through here, Ifton Shepp provided direct assistance to the damaged automaton before sending them on their way.

  • The "Renegade Construct" has a name, and their name is Hew.

  • Hew has gained sentience, most likely through the strange Inkaro Pearl that was found inside the construct's chassis, dubbed an @UUID[Item.IcaaecvWdzTXxXz5]{Entropic Pearl}. Shepp still has one of these Entropic Pearls to offer the party for inspection, but the rest were cast down into a bottomless refuse crevasse on the southern edge of town.

  • Hew is one of four Chessmen that Ifton Shepp has assisted over the course of the past several months. They've relocated to a camp several miles to the east.

  • Ifton Shepp shares his philosophical thoughts about Hew and the other Chessmen (known as the "Downsiders"), which include support for their autonomy as sentient creatures. Whatever caused their awakening, the Downsiders deserve the same rights as other people of the Arctus Plateau.

  • From time to time, Shepp has spotted Silver Beam crewmen (including constructs and humanoid alike) hauling scrap into Arcturel from the Sinkhole Depths. He couldn't be sure, but it seemed as though they were hauling these materials from the east.

The curious Inkaro Pearl:

When Hew crawled out of that crater in the boardwalk, he was busted up and his brains were scrambled. So I brought him back to the farm and went to work. The first thing I did was replace the pearl in his chest … the one I pulled out was a sickly green color, tainted by gods knows what. The most curious thing about this is that I pulled similar inkaro pearls out of the other three constructs. So something's adding up, I'm just not sure what.

The other constructs:

"Chamberlain" was the first one to come through a few months back. Snuck down the shaft of his own accord, worried about what would happen if Silver Beam ever found him, or found out about his … awareness. A confusion plagued the poor fellow, until I replaced his inkaro pearl. Then "Lucent" snuck into Rock Bottom a few weeks later, followed by "Rider" — on the back of a lizard no less. "Hew" was the most recent Chessman to visit the farmstead. And I dare say, the four of them didn't strike me as hostile or threatening. They just seem to want a fair shake, and a chance at something special.

About the Construct Camp:

I don't know much about it, nor would I tell you if I did. Those Chessmen deserve their peace. But Chamberlain came back once or twice to let me know he'd found a place to settle in for a moment, somewhere a few miles to the east, tucked away from the prying eyes of Silver Beam goons.

Ifton Shepp's past:

In a former life, not too long ago, I worked closely with Vartholomew Chess, crafting Chessmen with my very hands for the good people of Arcturel. But times change, and times grew tough. So I took an offer to work for Silver Beam on the construction of their facility. Little did I know, I was being used to sabotage my mentor. Not only did they headhunt his most skilled assistant, they extorted me for designs and information. I sold my soul for a chance at financial freedom, and I ended up losing almost everything along the way. So now, it's me and Totter against the world. Helping out the Downsiders seemed like the only way to make up for my checkered past. But then again, things wind up in Rock Bottom for a reason.

The Entropic Pearl

This is likely the party's first direct encounter with an @UUID[Item.IcaaecvWdzTXxXz5]{Entropic Pearl}, a corrupted variant of a standard @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{White Inkaro Pearl} that has been crafted by the quest's antagonist Larissa Toth. No matter their original purpose, Entropic Pearls serve to sabotage the Chessmen very constructs they empower — and the Downsiders were each spiritually awakened by the chaotic magic of the Entropic Pearl.

Any character who is familiar with a regular Inkaro Pearl immediately notices the strange and novel aspects of an Entropic Pearl when they first see it. [Recap of description of Entropic Pearl from item here].

Finer details can be gained through examination, as follows:

[[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] The character identifies carbon burns on the pearl that confirms its previous use in the chassis of a Chessman construct. Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

[[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] The character is able to notice several layers of esoteric symbols traced into the surface of the pearl, rather than just the overt layer on top, suggesting a process of multiple augmentations. Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

[[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]]The character is able to confirm the novel aspect of the Entropic Pearls, which haven't been seen elsewhere on Ember. Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] and [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

[[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] The character recognizes that the Entropic Pearl deviates from the subtle supernatural qualities of standard Inkaro Pearls and is a manmade or man-altered material. Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] have advantage on this check.

[[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] The character recognizes the esoteric symbols traced on the surface of the pearl as Luxaran in origin. Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] have advantage on this check.

Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ghXTfe7sgCbgf1Q8]{Detect Magic} spell reveals a strong aura of Transmutation magic on all Entropic Pearls.

Additionally, those who have [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeOblivion0000]] or [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]] can readily identify the presence of Oblivion magic on all Entropic Pearls.

Signara Attunement: Entropic Pearl Details

If the party manages deduce at least 3 of the 5 "finer details" listed above, each character who participated in the deduction advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 arcturelSideBottomPearl]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Gathering Evidence: Entropic Pearl & Used Chessman Parts

Important evidence can be gathered here that can be used in support of Hew the Renegade Construct's exoneration. If the characters loot an @UUID[Item.IcaaecvWdzTXxXz5]{Entropic Pearl} or the @UUID[Item.pDQcjL6w2oLswE1N]{Used Chessman Parts}, record the appropriate Event Outcome. This physical clue plays a major role in the forthcoming [[/eventState arcturelSideEvidence]] event.

Next Steps

The party is free to explore the rest of the Sinkhole Depths for clues, gathering information during the events of [[/eventState arcturelSidePool]], [[/eventState arcturelSideCamp]], and [[/eventState arcutrelSideScrapyard]] if they have yet to do so.
Rumors in Rock Bottom.soverview: The party journeys to the rough-and-tumble Arcturel suburb known as Rock Bottom, which resides on the floor of the city's infamous sinkhole. Here, they can search for clues about the corpse of Kellan Lorde and the missing Renegade Construct. Before they leave, the characters can meet an enigmatic local with a lot to say about the matter — a semi-retired artificer named Ifton Shepp, who aided the Renegade Construct in his escape.
Rumors in Rock Bottom.sexposition:
As you look for immediate signs of a crime scene, you can't help but notice that the atmosphere here in Rock Bottom is thick with languid aimlessness, and the scant denizens of this rough-and-tumble tent town go about their business with little to no regard for your group.

Scanning the dim expanse, you spot a few immediate points of interest, including a pair of itinerant spelunkers sharing a bottle of wine on the boardwalk, and a small mushroom farm attended by a wooden construct. It's quiet here, but you draw little attention as you pass — as if Rock Bottom has seen its fair share of surprises, and then some.
Rumors in Rock Bottom.ssummary: We journeyed to Rock Bottom below Arcturel, where we investigated the scene of the Renegade Construct's impact after the fall. After speaking with a local hermit named Ifton Shepp, we gained some insight regarding the Chessman's fate, and learned about a remote location in the Sinkhole Depths where the Chessman and its allies have made camp.

Surface Matters.name: Surface Matters
Surface Matters.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and combat event introduces the party to the local tensions between Chessmen constructs and humanoids in Arcturel. In this event, the characters can:

  • Choose whether or not to intervene during a hate crime against a Chessman construct and its owner, a young Arcturian forager named Torra.

  • Listen to various rumors, including stories about the missing Renegade Construct and Arcturel's current economic troubles.

  • Learn about a couple of persons of interest that reside in Arcturel's Upper and Lower districts, who might provide key insights into the rumors at hand.

Torra (Chaotic Good, Arcturian Human, she/her) is a scrappy forager who collects herbs, spell components, and random salvage from the upper reaches of Arcturel and the wilderness beyond the sinkhole brim. Her @UUID[Actor.0xDU0k3l8V4movO8]{Chessman} companion — a refurbished model she's lovingly named "Rusty" — serves her dutifully and without malfunction.

Arcos (Chaotic Neutral, Arcturian Human, he/him) is a lanky but handsome scoundrel who loves to stir up trouble when he isn't drowning his misdirected woes in ale at the local tavern. Armed with a bucket of paint, he's joined by 6 other unarmed mob members during this loosely-coordinated effort to harass Torra and her Chessman construct.

Treat Torra, Arcos, and the other mob members as @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians}. One of the unnamed mob members is armed with a knife, while another carries a second bucket of red paint.

If the Party Intervenes

If they party decides to intervene, they must coerce Arcos and the assembled mob into standing down from their assault, which is readily accomplished via the skill checks featured below.

Defusing the Mob

Any character who makes a successful[[/skill deception 15]], [[/skill persuasion 15]], or [[/skill intimidation 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]], [[/skillCheck deception 15]], or [[/skillCheck intimidation 15]] check is able to convince the mob to stand down.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]], [[/knowledge machines]], or [[/knowledge warfare]] have advantage on these checks.

  • Characters who brandish lethal weapons also have advantage on Intimidation checks against the mob.

Alternately, any character who targets the mob with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.3MYDjS6k9IYL0aTj]{Calm Emotions} spell is able to immediately cause them to become indifferent to Torra and her Chessman.

Additionally, if a character targets the mob's leader Arcos with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.eS7XnnApoxRxYXPs]{Charm Person} spell, they gain advantage on Deception and Persuasion checks used to defuse the mob.

Alternatively, characters capable with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeControl00000]] may be able to use it creatively to calm the crowd individually or as a group.

If the party manages to defuse the situation, read the following:

Having been robbed of their pointless ire, the various members of the mob begin to slowly back away from the scene. Some of the ne'er-do-wells look almost ashamed of themselves, while others remain notably suspicious. Nevertheless, Arcos and the thugs begin to retreat. Propriety has won this day, and the teenage girl wastes no time before cleaning the crimson stains from her beloved construct before addressing you:

Thanks. That got a little scary there for a minute. I really appreciate you showing up when you did … While you're here, care to take a look at my wares? I have trinkets for sale, with fair prices for altruists like yourselves. And I could use the coin to have my Chessman detailed.

She continues wiping the red paint away from the nooks and crannies of the construct's chassis. Meanwhile, you take note of the market stall behind her, stocked with a curious array of fresh herbs and Arcturian trinkets.

Ragen Attunement: Protected Torra's Construct

If the party manages to successfully protect Torra's construct Rusty from the mob, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 arcturelSideSurfaceProtect]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome protected]]

Speaking with Torra

The characters are now free to chat with Torra, who is happy to provide the following rumors and information:

  • The reason for the mob's confrontation and the red paint. A Chessman construct owned by House Cevher is said to have gone haywire and killed a miner in the Dives a few weeks back. The incident has rattled many of the locals, particularly those who already had a tenuous hold on their emotional state — like the down-and-out or the displaced.

  • A brief history of her time as a young forager. 17 years young and orphaned at an early age, Torra has made a good go of her career as a forager and scavenger of Arcturel's surrounding environs for a couple of years now. She's well-known among frequent travelers for her rotating collection of esoteric trinkets for sale.

  • The basics about her Chessman companion named Rusty. Torra found Rusty's damaged body in a garbage heap two years ago during one of her early outings, partially dismembered and fried from lightning damage. After dragging him out of the mess and gathering suitable replacement parts, she managed to put the Chessman back together with the help of a few locals. They've been inseparable since.

  • A job lead. Zodi Trask of House Cevher is looking to hire investigators for an official inquiry regarding the cause of the fatal Chessman incident. He can be found in Rallyhome when he isn't attending the mines in Lower Arcturel.

A successful [[/skill insight 11]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 11]] check validates the honesty of Torra's claims from her perspective, which by all accounts seems to be a measured and educated one (especially compared to Arcos' mob).

  • Result of 16+ Critical Success: Torra obviously has something to prove, both to others and herself. Her history as an orphan has contributed to her standoffish nature as a loner; she'd never consider diplomacy as a way to deal with the mob, favoring a display of strength instead.

Torra's Trinkets

If the party wants to offer Torra their patronage, each character can spend 5 gp for one of Torra's Trinkets, which can be randomly selected via the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} table.

Additionally, Torra has a selection of herbs for sale, many of which can be used for spell components. Her prices are firm, and a lot of the funds go towards repairing Rusty on a regular basis.

If the Party Stands By

If they party decides to stand idly by, they will witness the following exchange:

You stand back to watch the scene unfold without intervening. The teenage girl and the greasy-haired thug exchange a few more hushed words before the girl spits in the assailant's face. Before you can blink, the young man pushes her to the ground as the rest of the mob rushes in with tools and clubs to pummel the Chessman.

A moment later, the mob staggers back, sated. As the dust clears, you notice the Chessman has been battered enough to be broken. The girl sits alone, sobbing at the senseless violence, powerless to do anything about it. As the mob disperses, the greasy-haired youth approaches you with a look of smug satisfaction on his face.

She should have listened to reason. Everyone else in Arcturel knows those Chessmen can't be trusted.

Orbis Attunement: Didn't Protect Torra's Construct

If the party chose to stand by while Torra's construct Rusty was attacked by the mob, each character advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 arcturelSideSurfaceStoodBy]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome destroyed]]

Speaking with Arcos

The characters are free to chat with Arcos (or another member of the mob), who is willing to provide the following rumors and information:

  • The reason for the mob's confrontation and the red paint. A Chessman construct owned by House Cevher is said to have gone haywire and killed a miner in the Dives a few weeks back. The incident has rattled many of the locals, particularly those who work in and around the constructs, like lower Arcturel miners and inkaro pearl farmers of the Sinkhole Depths.

  • The basics about Chessman constructs, from a very biased perspective. The famed constructs were designed by the artificer Vartholomew Chess, who lives in Upper Arcturel. Despite their ubiquity, Chessmen are becoming more and more dangerous and unpredictable. Arcos and other locals view the Chessmen as liabilities in terms of the safety and livelihood of the citizens of Arcturel.

  • A job lead. Zodi Trask of House Cevher is looking to hire investigators to track down the missing Renegade Construct to ensure it doesn't kill any other citizens of Arcturel. Trask can be found in Rallyhome when he isn't attending the mines in Lower Arcturel.

  • A brief history of his time in Brimtown. Arcos moved to the surface after being displaced from mining work by a Chessman in Lower Arcturel. Instead of digging for ore, he now spends his days as a cut-rate guide or sellsword. If the party wants to hire him for 5 gp a day, he's willing to join up with them (but his promises far outweigh his efforts).

A successful[[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check confirms the honesty inherent in Arcos' perspective, but does hint at the ignorance and bias that drives his actions. He doesn't seem to be an outright bad person, but bad circumstances have probably led him to make bad decisions.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: There is likely some incident from Arcos' past that has already corrupted his pride and sense of self, and his aggression against Rusty and other Chessmen is probably the transference of that previous pain.

Based on how friendly the characters are to Arcos, he can potentially be a point of contact in Brimtown for the party moving forward — although his rather bohemian and chaotic lifestyle means his appearances are less than consistent, and his haughty mindset exceeds his work ethic at every turn.

Brimtown Rumors

After their encounter with Torra and the mob, the characters can optionally spend time gathering additional rumors in Brimtown before proceeding to Upper Arcturel.

Gathering Additional Information

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check is able to track down one of the following rumors via conversation with locals:

  • A few locals speak of inkaro pearl shortages, opting to use oil lanterns, candles, or torchlight to illuminate their dwellings at night while the local resource grows notably scarce for the first time in recent memory.

  • Rumor has it that the Renegade Construct in Lower Arcturel wasn't the only Chessman to start acting up. There isn't any hard evidence, but stories are floating through town about other constructs that have gone missing rather than malfunction. Maybe it's just thievery or hearsay. Times can be tough, after all.

  • They say the Sinkhole Depths are crawling with all sorts of strange, carnivorous creatures. If you journey too far from Rock Bottom, be sure to steer clear of the bone effigies left by the Jurtak, or you may never see the light of Lantyr again.

  • Rumors abound regarding the Silver Beam Consortium, a group of Railen engineers and businessfolk who have made some impressive strides over the past months when it comes to their industry and holdings. Members of the Brimtown Watch claim that shipments to and from the Silver Beam headquarters tend to come at night, when the rest of the city is at rest.

  • Caravaners who've camped at Brimtown in recent weeks have spoken in hushed voices of a growing concern for House Cevher's ability to consistently supply certain goods like inkaro pearls, shadestone, adamantine, silver, and precious gemstones.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After they pass through Brimtown, the party can continue towards the tavern known as Rallyhome in @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv]{Upper Arcturel}, where they'll meet with the quest-giver @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask} during the events of [[/eventState arcturelSideTradeway]].
Surface Matters.soverview: The party arrives at Brimtown, Arcturel's surface-side suburb, where visitors to and from the sinkhole city are treated to a glimpse of the settlement's rough-and-tumble lifestyle. Here, the characters witness an impromptu conflict between a group of locals and an unassuming Chessman construct, whose owner is caught in the middle of the potentially dangerous situation. The party must decide whether to intervene and prevent these tensions from escalating, or to stand back and watch the scene play out on its own.
Surface Matters.sexposition:
A troubling scene near a market stall catches your eye as you make your way through the dusty streets of Brimtown: a teenage girl stands defiantly between a surly mob of Arcturians and an aged humanoid-shaped construct made of copper and steel. The construct, marked by burnished edges and mismatched replacement parts, has been doused in a large splattering of red paint that resembles a gout of fresh blood. Meanwhile, two members of the angry mob have empty buckets in their hands, stained with the same vermillion pigment that paints the construct.

The teenage girl stares into the eyes of the assailants and shouts:

You rock heads better keep your damn hands off my construct.

The mob's leader, a roguishly handsome twenty-something with long greasy hair, retorts with a sneer:

This Chessian trash can't be trusted! If you were smart, you'd scrap this thing before it kills somebody. Just say the word and we'll do it for you right now …

The mob stirs with excitement as the girl rolls up her sleeves in dissent.

You'll have to go through me first!

Outnumbered seven-to-one (excluding the construct), she plants her feet and raises her fists, ready for a fight.

Who wants to lose a few teeth today, huh!? Come on, I'm not afraid of you idiots! Who's first!?

The tension is so thick you could cut it with a knife — which you actually spot hanging in the hand of one of the toothless assailants towards the back of the mob. If anyone has anything to say about this anxious situation, they'll need to act fast.
Surface Matters.ssummary: While making our way through Brimtown near the sinkhole's surface edge, we saw a group of locals attempt to harass and intimidate a Chessman construct and its owner. We learned more about the rising tensions in Arcturel surrounding constructs and their fallibility, along with various details about the city itself.

Presenting the Evidence.name: Presenting the Evidence
Presenting the Evidence.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event tasks the party with presenting the evidence they've gathered to Zodi Trask and Larissa Toth, and provides a branching-out point for the conclusion of the quest's narrative. In this event, the party can:

  • Journey to Lower Arcturel for a semi-public meeting with Zodi Trask and Larissa Toth, along with Lucent (if the characters decided to absolve the Downsiders of their erroneous crimes) or Hew (if they decided to condemn the Downsiders and side with Silver Beam).

  • Present the evidence they've gathered throughout Arcturel and the Sinkhole Depths, whether in support for or against the Downsiders.

  • Convince Zodi Trask about the veracity of their claims, one way or another.

  • Decide upon their next steps and determine the overall event outcome in the process.

Arranging a Meeting

"Presenting the Evidence" presumes the party has gathered enough information to support an argument for either exonerating or condemning the Renegade Construct known as Hew. With evidence in hand, the characters journey back to Lower Arcturel to meet with Zodi Trask, who has been patiently awaiting an update.

The characters conveniently reunite Zodi during a moment of contemplation in Lower Arcturel, a stone's throw from both his apartment in the Dives and the scene of the so-called crime.

Prelude to an Inquest

The party must approach Zodi Trask with their intentions of presenting the evidence and formalizing an inquest about the case of the Renegade Construct. Trask explains the following to the characters:

  • A fair inquest will require both parties to meet on neutral ground. Trask nominates this very spot as a location for the arbitration.

  • During the inquest, Trask will hear the party's argument and review their evidence, which will be weighed against testimony from the plaintiff Larissa Toth (as corroborated by other locals of Arcturel).

  • The Chessman dubbed Hew will either be released or decommissioned based on Trask's ruling.

Once the party members have agreed to Trask's terms, he'll ask them to gather here again at this spot in two hours, along with Larissa Toth and other key witnesses.

  • If the party plans to exonerate Hew and the Downsiders, Lucent will join them as a key witness. The other Downsiders will remain behind in Rock Bottom, well out of sight of their Silver Beam enemies.

  • If the party plans to condemn Hew and the Downsiders, any surviving Chessmen will remain in (or escape to) Aberin's Folly to begin fortifying their camp.

Timely Preparations

The characters now have two hours to prepare for the inquest. Advance Time by 2 Hours once the party's preparations are complete.

The Inquest Begins

Two hours later, the party gathers once more with Zodi Trask in Lower Arcturel, this time with Larissa Toth in attendance. Since Silver Beam has their own missing Chessman and a vested interest in the entire ordeal, Larissa is insistent upon hearing the so-called evidence for herself.

The air is thick with anticipation as you make your way to the catwalk outside Hob Korell's stables, where Zodi Trask and Larissa Toth survey the scene of the crime — the precise spot where Kellan Lorde and the Renegade Construct tumbled to their doom. Beyond these two officials, the twinkling lights of lower Arcturel scintillate in the darkness as far as the eye can see, and the clamorous din of the sinkhole city echoes with a relaxing ceaselessness.

Larissa Toth glances up as you approach, surveying your party with measured aplomb.

They're here.

Zodi Trask turns to greet you.

Welcome back. I assume you've met the esteemed Larissa Toth.

The Railen executive nods in your direction as Trask continues:

It seems the time has come to stand and deliver. Tell us, what information have you found about the Renegade Construct?

Larissa Toth speaks once more:

Indeed, the people of Arcturel have a right to know if a killer lurks among them. What news, friends?

The Party's Evidence

The party must present their evidence to Zodi Trask and Larissa Toth, whether in favor of exonerating the Downsiders or condemning them to an unfortunate fate. As part of this presentation, the characters will also be tasked with various skill checks, as described below.

Exonerating the Downsiders

In order to convince Zodi Trask of Hew's innocence, the party must present at least 3 pieces of the following evidence in support of Hew and the Downsiders' exoneration:

  • One or more @UUID[Item.IcaaecvWdzTXxXz5]{Entropic Pearls}, particularly those removed from the Chessmen by Ifton Shepp.

  • A piece of @UUID[Item.VOsnsStt2vkRPce0]{Chessman Scrap Metal} from the Scrapyard bearing the Vartholomew Chess trademark.

  • Celestial Remains from the encounter with the Vorg and Skither at the Scrapyard.

  • The @UUID[Item.mkkNU0Hfdio8EVbp]{Inkaro Pool Mandate} obtained from the Inkaro Pools.

  • @UUID[Item.ZQs3ejY6m150wKs7]{Silver Beam Schematics} obtained from either the Scrapyard or the Silver Beam @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.tgGJNYt0wynV4PIV]{Side Offices}.

  • Information gained from personnel at Silver Beam HQ via the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.ppWAAEul0QHtm4er]{Detect Thoughts} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.spell.Item.telecognition000] spell.

  • Verbal testimony from Lucent.

The characters must also succeed on 1 or more of the following skill checks:

  • [[/skill persuasion 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] To convince Trask that Hew and the Downsiders aren't responsible for their malfunctions.

  • [[/skill intimidation 18]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 18]] To convince Trask that Silver Beam currently poses the greatest threat to Arcturel.

  • [[/skill deception 18]] [[/skillCheck deception 18]] To trick Trask into believing that a piece of irrelevant evidence is pertinent to Hew's absolution.

  • [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] To impress upon Trask the extent to which the Inkaro Pearls must have been tampered with by a spellcaster with intent.

  • [[/skill performance 15]] [[/skillCheck performance 15]] To rousingly convince Trask about the sheer weight of the evidence that's been presented.

Condemning the Downsiders

Alternately, in order to convince Zodi Trask of Hew's guilt, the party must present at least 1 piece of the following evidence in support of Hew and the Downsiders' condemnation:

  • An account of the Downsiders camp at Aberin's Folly, with physical evidence of the discarded @UUID[Item.pDQcjL6w2oLswE1N]{Used Chessman Parts} found in Rock Bottom.

  • The large Riding Lizard that was stolen by Rider during his escape, which can be found at Aberin's Folly and returned to Hob Korell (who promptly recognizes the missing steed).

  • An account of the disastrous Jurtak raid that occurred at the Inkaro Pools, with physical evidence of the encounter (such as a Jurtak item or bodily remains).

  • The erroneous and misleading testimony of a false witness.

The characters must also succeed on 2 or more of the following skill checks:

  • [[/skill persuasion 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] To convince Trask that Hew and the Downsiders are responsible for their malfunctions.

  • [[/skill intimidation 18]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 18]] To convince Trask that the Renegade and other Chessmen currently poses a great threat to Arcturel.

  • [[/skill deception 18]] [[/skillCheck deception 18]] To trick Trask into believing that a piece of irrelevant evidence is pertinent to Hew's castigation.

  • [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]]To adequately impress upon Trask the inscrutable nature of Inkaro Pearls.

  • [[/skill performance 15]] [[/skillCheck performance 15]] To rousingly convince Trask about the sheer weight of the crime as it was witnessed.

Orchestrating the Inquest

Since several NPCs are directly involved in this social encounter, here's some advice to keep the conversation going. If you find the parley is drifting too far from the matter at hand, use the personal motivations of each of the key NPCs as pivot points for the conversation:

  • Don't waste time. Time is money, and Larissa Toth has very little to waste with antics in Lower Arcturel.

  • Give everyone a chance to speak. Zodi Trask is a representative of the people's will, and the people of Arcturel believe in fair justice.

  • Remember the real victims. Lucent is quick to offer words of confirmation and support for any of the party's arguments. Alternately, a Lower Arcturel bystander could have something to say that paints a clearer picture of the accident.

One of two scripted moments will occur once the criteria for "Exonerating the Downsiders" or "Condemning the Downsiders" has been fulfilled, based on the party's actions.

Downsiders Exonerated:

Larissa Toth's eyes narrow with derision as you provide your closing statements, as if she's well aware of the unsavory shadow this evidence has cast upon her precious Silver Beam Consortium.

After a moment of protracted silence, Zodi Trask speaks with unfaltering authority:

It seems to me that the evidence is quite clear: these tainted inkaro pearls have something to do with the malfunctions, rather than the construct's programming or a fault of their maker's. The bad pearls are to blame. Furthermore, it stands to reason we have a lot to learn about these awakened Chessmen. They're not mere automatons any more. I dare say, this evidence also suggests that Silver Beam hasn't been entirely forthcoming about certain operations …

Larissa Toth shoots the quarryman a scornful gaze and offers him a disrespectful sneer:

I dare say the evidence is threadbare at best. These vigilantes you've hired are as reckless as Chess and his constructs. Silver Beam has nothing to do with the malfunction of these automatons, and this slander against my company simply won't stand. I deny these feckless allegations, and plan on launching a new investigation of my own.

She looks over your group with disdain.

Our business here is done. Good luck cleaning up the mess, Trask. I have my own problems to deal with. Now, if you'll excuse me …

Toth snaps to attention and storms off, leaving you in the gregarious company of Zodi Trask, whose skeptical gaze follows the Railen executive as she skulks away to the elevator. Once she's out of earshot, Trask speaks to you under his breath:

If I didn't know any better, I'd say that arrogant was hiding something. Care to help me find out?

Akon Attunement: Against the Consortium

If the party chooses to exonerate the Downsiders, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 arcturelSideEvidenceConstructExonerate]] at the conclusion of the event.

Downsiders Condemned:

After a moment of silence, Larissa Toth speaks up:

I think we've seen enough. It's quite evident that the Renegade Construct acted of its own volition, and that these Chessmen can't be trusted to maintain the safety of Arcturel's people. Silver Beam is suspending all activity of our Chessian models, effective immediately. And we'll be recommending that the rest of Arcturel do the same. Our town is in your debt, friends.

She offers you a respectful nod. Meanwhile, Zodi Trask scratches his chin as equal measures of doubt and relief cross his furry face:

If only we'd have seen it coming sooner, we could have pulled the bad constructs from active duty and spared Kellan Lorde his untimely fate. At least the city can find some closure in all this. But ol' Varth is going to have a hell of a time trying to move his product from now on.

Toth quickly offers a word of caution:

If things don't change, Master Trask, I fear Vartholomew Chess is only going to have more problems on his hands, as more Chessmen continue to malfunction and more accidents continue to happen.

Finally, Trask looks to you with unmistakable appreciation:

You've nearly earned your reward for a job well done. Now, are there any loose ends we should worry about?

Akon Attunement: Against the Constructs

If the party chooses to condemn the Downsiders, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 arcturelSideEvidenceConstructCondemn]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aftermath

In the wake of the inquest, one of two downstream events will take place: @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3.JournalEntryPage.NcFW8EXnMRdFekac]{Storming the Consortium} or @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3.JournalEntryPage.mQ5njChi8ZdTvRSN]{Checkmate for Chessmen}. Before those events begin, the characters have a moment to gather their thoughts and discern the intentions of their allied NPCs.

Trask's Plan

In order for Zodi Trask and House Cevher to launch a formal complaint against Silver Beam on behalf of all of Arcturel, the party must infiltrate Silver Beam HQ to gather one last piece of irrefutable evidence that connects Silver Beam to the Entropic Pearls and the ongoing malfunctions of Chessmen.

Toth's Vengeance

If the party has yet to do so, Larissa Toth tasks them with raiding the Downsiders encampment at Aberin's Folly and either the capture or execution of the Renegade Construct. Toth would prefer a clean slate, and is willing to offer a bonus if all four of the Downsiders constructs are executed or dismantled.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

If the party decided to exonerate Hew and the Downsiders, the characters will proceed to the events of [[/eventState arcturelSideFinale]]. We recommend not starting the 'Storming the Consortium' event until the party is ready to go. At the top of that event, the characters will find themselves downstairs at the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.hPNx5zJWyySGYFjE]{Glimmer Lounge} in Upper Arcturel, where Chamberlain and the other Chessmen will help the party scrutinize their plans in the moments before the final assault against Silver Beam.

Alternately, if the party decided to condemn the Downsiders, the characters continue the saga in [[/eventState arcturelSideCheckmate]], where they'll be poised to assault the hideout at Aberin's Folly from the camp's outskirts.
Presenting the Evidence.soverview: With evidence in hand, the party regroups with Zodi Trask in Lower Arcturel to plan a meeting with Larissa Toth. Their goal: condemn or exonerate the Renegade Construct known as Hew.
Presenting the Evidence.sexposition: The iron chains of the elevator squeal and clank as the lift grinds its way to a halt in Lower Arcturel. The people of the Dives appear to go about their business as usual, including Zodi Trask, who you can spot leaning on the northern catwalk. Trask's attention vacillates between locals nearby and the wide, sweeping city of Arcturel itself, which glitters in the dark like some magnificent geode. The quarryman seems lost in thought, and taps his foot with a measure of restlessness.
Presenting the Evidence.ssummary: We met with Zodi Trask and Larissa Toth in Lower Arcturel, where we presented evidence in favor of our stance on the Downsiders and whether or not they represent an existential threat to the sinkhole city.

Storming the Consortium.name: Storming the Consortium
Storming the Consortium.text:
Against the Consortium

This combat event challenges the party with the exploration and infiltration of the Silver Beam Headquarters in Upper Arcturel, where they must obtain evidence of Larissa Toth's insidious plan to undermine House Cevher, Vartholomew Chess, and other denizens of Arcturel. In this event, the characters can:

  • Join the Downsiders in the Underbelly nighclub at Glimmer, where they'll receive a report from Chamberlain about the Silver Beam facility and its security protocols.

  • Plan their precise method of infiltration.

  • Set out to infiltrate the Silver Beam headquarters and secure the evidence necessary to bring Larissa Toth to justice: @UUID[Item.otPv3LhRyg5KHh1u]{Larissa Toth's Memory Shard}.

The party begins this event in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.hPNx5zJWyySGYFjE]{Glimmer Lounge} of Upper Arcturel's Underbelly, alongside the Downsiders: @UUID[Actor.XK20zaizyZOLGmsl]{Hew}, @UUID[Actor.1ZEi2D4j2RbKDc9x]{Rider}, @UUID[Actor.OYdqWs17RvL7ntbf]{Lucent}, and @UUID[Actor.iOyLbOiGrqMY49QI]{Chamberlain} — who is particularly suited to provide a few clear details about the Silver Beam facility and its inhabitants.

A Brief from Chamberlain

Prior to his awakening, Chamberlain served the Silver Beam Consortium under the iron fist of Larissa Toth and her Railen engineers. Fortunately for the party, this time of servitude has provided the Chessman with an intimate understanding of the Silver Beam facility, its various hazards, and its personnel. Before the characters set off from the relative safety of the Glimmer Lounge, Chamberlain is able to share the following details:

  • Larissa Toth is assisted by 4 Silver Beam Engineers and 4 Silver Beam Guards. At any given point in time, one Guard patrols the upper floor, one Guard patrols the lower floor, and 2 Guards are stationed in the Security Room.

  • Silver Beam Servitors are stationed at the facility, but Chamberlain can't verify the total number, since he's been gone for nearly a month. There were at least two working models on the floor before Chamberlain escaped.

  • Alarm buttons are located throughout the facility that enable lockdown protocols: one in the Silver Beam Foyer, one in the Director's Office, one in the Security Room, and one in the Cubicles downstairs.

  • Multiple elevators at the rear of the facility provide freight access to the Dives below.

  • Although the party is unaware of the specific evidence they're looking for, Chamberlain is quick to explain that Larissa Toth keeps the most sensitive documents related to the Consortium's efforts in her executive office.

Planning the Approach

If they've yet to do so, the characters must now plan the method of ingress for their infiltration of the Silver Beam headquarters. We've detailed some possible infiltration methods below for the characters to consider, categorized as one of two main avenues of approach: The Stealth Approach and The Direct Approach.

Gameplay for this event is intended to follow the motivations, proclivities, and instincts of the player characters, rather than rely on the guidance of the NPCs. If the party members struggle to devise a method of infiltration on their own, refer to the appropriate section below to offer them some guidance.

The Stealth Approach

If the characters choose to sneak their way into the Silver Beam headquarters, the following methods of entry are potential options for them:

Tradeway Deceptions

Characters can attempt to bluff their way from the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.5IHmzA71p0Fd8F4l]{Silver Beam Foyer} to the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.r3qQuNmGgOfkPzpo]{Director's Office} via a series of successful Deception checks. Spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.eS7XnnApoxRxYXPs]{Charm Person} or Suggestion can temporarily assist these efforts.

A successful [[/skill deception 18]] [[/skillCheck deception 18]] check is required to deceive any @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7]{Silver Beam Guard}, @UUID[Actor.vyN7FNbPEw6KsuGw]{Silver Beam Engineers}, and @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians} on duty in the facility, who are on high alert following Larissa's previous meeting with Zodi and the party.

  • Check once per question asked or lie told.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] have advantage on these checks.

  • Characters wearing @UUID[Item.LZAFIWKck47hrjRt]{Silver Beam Uniforms} also have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Underbelly Deceptions

Some of the characters can don Silver Beam uniforms in an attempt to deceive their way through the facility. 2 extra Silver Beam Guard uniforms can be found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.AbndV9j7m2yUX5On]{Silver Beam Barracks}.

Stealth via the Tradeway

Spells such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.A3q2gTNqG6fvNGrv]{Disguise Self} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.1N8dDMMgZ1h1YJ3B]{Invisibility} can help the characters infiltrate unseen or unnoticed.

Spells or items that offer an illusory appearance or make the character invisible can help the characters infiltrate unseen or unnoticed.

Stealth via the Underbelly

Characters can use a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.tfDxZIKDpOkz6pbx]{Grappling Hook} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.ugzwHl8vYaPu2GNd]{Climber's Kit} @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.grapnel000000000] to span the platform from the Glimmer Lounge to the Silver Beam catwalks. A single Silver Beam Guard patrols this sector in 5-minute shifts. Each character must succeed on a [[/skill acrobatics 13]] or [[/skill athletics 13]] [[/skillCheck athletics 13]] check in order to cross quickly enough to avoid being seen.

Additionally, characters can purchase a @UUID[Item.9mc77JtFfWVHz8GQ]{Potion of Jumping} from @UUID[JournalEntry.PWK8ADZy5RgbwBAu.JournalEntryPage.yObJp4josnr70zog]{Arvoda's Elixirs} that can assist the effort when it comes to spanning the gap between Glimmer and Silver Beam.

Primordis Attunement: The Stealth Approach

If the party chooses the Stealth Approach for their infiltration of the Silver Beam HQ, each character advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 arcturelSideFinaleStealth]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Direct Approach

If the characters choose to physically force their way into the Silver Beam headquarters, the following methods of entry are potential options for them:

Bravado via the Tradeway

Characters can force their way into the Silver Beam facility via the Silver Beam Foyer by taking advantage of the element of surprise. The obsequious Receptionist (Lawful Evil, Railen Altyra, she/her) stationed here is poised to push the red security button, but can't act quickly enough to seal the front door if the party coordinates their movement. Treat the Receptionist as an @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturian}.

Once each of the PCs make their first moves, roll for initiative, including the foyer's Receptionist — who will immediately push the Red Button twice on her turn. See @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.Xi8DSOxh18XVrkep#activating-alerts]{Activating Alerts} for the effects of pressing the button.

Bravado via the Underbelly

If a Silver Beam Guard is alerted during the course of an unsuccessful "Stealth via the Underbelly" attempt (see above), or if the party brazenly attempts to span the gap from the Glimmer Lounge without attempting to sneak, the Silver Beam Guard on duty will engage as soon as the characters are spotted.

Once the characters are spotted, roll for initiative. The Silver Beam Guard on patrol will call for help during the first round of combat, alerting the Silver Beam Guards at the Barracks. One of these Guards will join the encounter on the catwalk while the other Guard will move upstairs to alert the rest of the Silver Beam facility.

Ragen Attunement: The Direct Approach

If the party chooses the Direct Approach for their infiltration of the Silver Beam HQ, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 arcturelSideFinaleDirect]] at the conclusion of the event.

Point of No Return

If the alarm is sounded at any point in time while the characters are infiltrating the Silver Beam headquarters, the entire facility is placed on alert, per the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv]{Gameplay Details} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv]{Arcturel Upper} area walkthrough.

Silver Beam Security Protocol

When the Silver Beam headquarters is placed on alert — whether via the Red Button alarm located in the Silver Beam Foyer or by word of mouth — all Silver Beam enemies in the area roll for initiative to join the initiative order. The various enemies will behave as follows:

  • The @UUID[Actor.vyN7FNbPEw6KsuGw]{Silver Beam Engineers} move to activate any inactive Silver Beam Servitors.

  • The @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7]{Silver Beam Guards} maintain a suppressing fire against the advancing party with their @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7.Item.WXLInWVw8GPitrtc]{Light Crossbows}.

  • The Receptionist in the Silver Beam Foyer retreats from the scene into the Upper Arcturel Tradeway, never to be seen again. Any other commonfolk in the area retreat as well via the Elevators into Lower Arcturel.

  • Once activated, the @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU]{Silver Beam Servitors} here will start off by targeting enemies at range with their @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU.Item.SxFwLo6u8W2vmDzG]{Net Throwers}. After a volley of nets, the Servitors will move into offensive positions, utilizing their Lightning Discharge against any adjacent enemies before attacking with their @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU.Item.UZMTD9JjMM9SsAfL]{Arm Blades} and @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU.Item.glj95eRlM5lIDQYE]{Charged Claws}.

  • @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth} will stand back to utilize her array of spells to bolster the Silver Beam forces, guiding the Silver Beam Servitors, Guards, and Engineers as she sees fit — notably leaning on the @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W.Item.X9pxVeiSymKHPyfD]{Blindness/Deafness} spell to target enemy spellcasters, saving @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W.Item.YcJvpZfJfp81S8Ea]{Counterspell} for the most dramatic or strategically advantageous moment. She'll use @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W.Item.3ikUaU4uJ45r6nmO]{Fire Bolt} liberally throughout the battle. As soon as the party poses any kind of threat to Larissa, she'll retreat into the confines of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.r3qQuNmGgOfkPzpo]{Director's Office} and activate the 4 Silver Beam Servitors located therein.

The Sentinel Arrives

On the 3rd round of combat, an unseen @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE]{Silver Beam Sentinel} arrives via the Western Elevator to confront the players. Any Silver Beam Engineers nearby will move to support the Sentinel with @UUID[Actor.vyN7FNbPEw6KsuGw.Item.gWWQ4TOhfdeNMmEX]{Field Repairs}.

A highly-aggressive technological nightmare, the Silver Beam Sentinel will attack enemy characters with no quarter, targeting the most powerful enemy in an attempt to incapacitate them quickly with its @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE.Item.Gtsf1CCGi8o5USpz]{War Machine} bonus actions: @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE.Item.0r1QxUULnKl4LQ4D]{Flamethrower} and @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE.Item.gMQ7ijGFBHRInzv5]{Magic Missile Pod}.

When the Silver Beam headquarters is placed on alert — whether via the Red Button alarm located in the Silver Beam Foyer or by word of mouth — all Silver Beam enemies in the area roll for initiative to join the initiative order. The various enemies will behave as follows:

  • The @UUID[Actor.vyN7FNbPEw6KsuGw]{Silver Beam Engineers} move to activate any inactive Silver Beam Servitors.

  • The @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7]{Silver Beam Guards} maintain a suppressing fire against the advancing party with their @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7.Item.WXLInWVw8GPitrtc]{Crossbows}.

  • The Receptionist in the Silver Beam Foyer retreats from the scene into the Upper Arcturel Tradeway, never to be seen again. Any other arcturians in the area retreat as well via the Elevators into Lower Arcturel.

  • Once activated, the @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU]{Silver Beam Servitors} here will start off by targeting enemies at range with their @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU.Item.Nor3GNdILjRXPnXG]{Nets}. After a volley of nets, the Servitors will move into offensive positions, utilizing their @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU.Item.lightningBurst00]{Lightning Burst} against any adjacent enemies before attacking with their @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU.Item.UZMTD9JjMM9SsAfL]{Iron claws} and @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU.Item.chargedClaw00000]{Charged Claws}.

  • @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth} will stand back to utilize her array of composed magic to reinforce the attacks of other Silver Beam forces from a distance, ordering the Silver Beam Servitors, Guards, and Engineers as she sees fit — notably leaning on the Control rune to target already engaged enemies and weaken their resolve, while reserving attention to any noticeable enemy spellcasters in order to lean heavily on Counterspells. She'll otherwise use @Spell[flame.arrow] and @Spell[illumination.ray] liberally throughout the battle. As soon as the party poses any kind of threat to Larissa, she'll retreat into the confines of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Exq8U5xEyk6B5JKv.JournalEntryPage.r3qQuNmGgOfkPzpo]{Director's Office} and activate the 4 @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU]{Silver Beam Servitors} located therein.

The Sentinel Arrives

On the 3rd round of combat, an unseen @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE]{Silver Beam Sentinel} arrives via the Western Elevator to confront the players. Any Silver Beam Engineers nearby will move to support the Sentinel with @UUID[Actor.vyN7FNbPEw6KsuGw.Item.fieldRepairs0000]{Field Repairs}.

A highly-aggressive technological nightmare, the Silver Beam Sentinel will attack enemy characters with no quarter, targeting the most powerful enemy in an attempt to incapacitate them quickly with its @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE.Item.flamethrower0000]{Flaming Spray} and @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE.Item.arcaneProjectile]{Fire Arcane Projectiles} actions.

Dramatic Moments

Once the Sentinel arrives, at the beginning of each combat round, one of six @UUID[RollTable.lo3A3bXG6GGdCszd]{Silver Beam Sentinel Moments} occurs. At the beginning of each round, roll on the table below and narrate the result. These moments can occur more than once, and continue until the Sentinel is destroyed or otherwise defeated.

Reinforcements!

If the characters happen to make short work of the Silver Beam forces and you find additional reinforcements are necessary for a balanced or challenging combat sequence, the two elevators here can deposit even more Silver Beam reinforcements to the battle. Mixed groups of [[/roll 1d2]] Silver Beam Servitors, a Silver Beam Engineer, and [[/roll 1d2]] Silver Beam Guards can arrive every other round.

Early Access

The elevators in this map will eventually be interactable and provide the ability to bring forth reinforcements like the Silver Beam Sentinel or additional guards in dramatic fashion. Until that interactivity is added in a later update, we rely on the Gamemaster to provide an evocative description of the elevator's arrival.

@Embed[RollTable.lo3A3bXG6GGdCszd inline rollable=true]

Confronting Larissa Toth

This event culminates when the characters encounter Larissa Toth, who is likely to behave in battle according to the following tactics.

Larissa Toth Tactics

If and when combat in the main chamber of the Silver Beam Headquarters becomes too perilous for Larissa Toth, she'll retreat to the confines of the Director's Office for a final showdown with the party.

When she first enters the chamber, Larissa will activate the 4 Silver Beam Servitors located on the pedestals here and take a defensive position behind the room's furniture. Any surviving Silver Beam forces in the facility at large will be commanded to fall back to the Waiting Room to flank Larissa's pursuers.

If she has yet to do so, Larissa will activate her @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W.Item.DlXPVPhJQuYbGU28]{Tyraphic Transformation} once she reaches the office. Once reinforcements arrive, Larissa will settle into a defensive position and prepare to hurl spells at the most vulnerable targets while the servitors act as a front line to distract the party.

Retrieving the Evidence

The unidentified evidence the party seeks is contained in @UUID[Item.otPv3LhRyg5KHh1u]{Larissa Toth's Memory Shard}, which can be found in Larissa Toth's personal inventory. Alternately, the characters can attempt to extract a "confession" from Larissa herself, but the Railen transmuter will not afford the party this information willingly.

Larissa's desk also contains various accoutrements that reveal her occupation as a transmuter, including her research and rare components for the Luxarum incantation known as The Diagram Transcendent.

Signara Attunement: Transcendent Discoveries

The first character to adequately loot Larissa's desk and take possession of her research for The Diagram Transcendent advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 arcturelSideFinaleDiagram]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level. This milestone is mutually exclusive with the [[/eventState arcturelSideCheckmate]] event which cannot be earned.

Next Steps

With Larissa's confession and/or her Memory Shard in-hand, the party is free to return to Zodi Trask for the [[/eventState arcturelSideHomecoming]] event, which will result in the exoneration of Hew and the other Chessmen.
Storming the Consortium.soverview: The party infiltrates the Silver Beam headquarters in Upper Arcturel in search of evidence that will implicate Larissa Toth and the Consortium for their alleged wrongdoings. This raid will result in a final confrontation with the Railen transmuter and her league of metallic minions.
Storming the Consortium.sexposition:
You find yourselves huddled in the dim seclusion of the Glimmer Lounge, where the Downsiders are gathered in support of your clandestine efforts. The Chessman known as Chamberlain arranges a stack of decorative crystals and nightclub paraphernalia to mock up a miniature map of the Silver Beam offices, eager to explain the ins and outs to you before you set off.

Looking out the balcony, the Silver Beam headquarters seems to loom especially large over Upper Arcturel this day. Your mission to observe and report on the facility is at hand, but the precise method of infiltration is up to you. And the appointed time is nigh.
Storming the Consortium.ssummary: We infiltrated the Silver Beam headquarters in Upper Arturel, where we found evidence of Larissa Toth's illicit mission to undermine House Cevher's trade efforts and the reputation Vartholomew Chess' famed constructs. We should report back to Zodi Trask with these findings.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This side quest occurs during Chapter 2 as the party is drawn by rumor or circumstance to the mining settlement of Arcturel. There are no prerequisites for this quest and it can be undertaken at any time, although it is certain to be encountered if traveling with Lyla while undertaking the @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu] quest.

Difficulty

The "Glitter in the Dark" quest is designed for a party of Level 3 characters, although the finale of the quest, either @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3.JournalEntryPage.NcFW8EXnMRdFekac]{Storming the Consortium} or @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3.JournalEntryPage.mQ5njChi8ZdTvRSN]{Checkmate for Chessmen} may prove difficult for a party that is not yet Level 4.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 2 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point upon completion of the [[/eventState arcutrelSideScrapyard]] Event, and a second upon completion of one of the mutually-exclusive [[/eventState arcturelSideFinale]] or [[/eventState arcturelSideCheckmate]] Events.

Whether they reach @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel} on the heels of rumors about the Renegade Construct or of their own accord, the characters are promptly requisitioned by @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cevher} upon their arrival to investigate a local matter of utmost importance. A miner named Kellan Lorde was recently killed during a questionable incident with a @UUID[Actor.0xDU0k3l8V4movO8]{Chessman} construct during routine operations in The Dives district of lower Arcturel. The construct promptly disappeared, and escaped somewhere into the sprawling subterranean city or into a furtive corner of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.SZq6RXsfxKownAN6]{Sinkhole Depths}, where it remains "dangerously" at-large.

The party must investigate the crime and track down the malfunctioning Chessman, known as the "Renegade Construct" to most of the citizens of Arcturel and @UUID[Actor.XK20zaizyZOLGmsl]{Hew} to his compatriots. Along the way, they'll meet several of Arcturel's noteworthy denizens, including the famed artificer @UUID[Actor.nnTbrW4RdzudxxMT]{Vartholomew Chess} (the Hulg'run responsible for making the Chessmen) and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.y7o8dKT1yxdnh2Pz]{Silver Beam Consortium} executive @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth} (a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.y4WHE3TEr6Of13SL]{Railen} transmuter who lurks at the heart of the quest as its secret villain).

What the people of Arcturel don't know is that Hew's malfunction is actually a supernatural awakening caused by Larissa Toth's own arcane tampering — a detail the Railen executive is desperate to conceal from public understanding. In an attempt to sabotage House Cevher and Chessian operations in Arcturel, Toth has weaponized various Chessmen with a chaotic transmutation ritual known as The Diagram Transcendent. Indeed, a total of four awakened Chessmen lurk in the Sinkhole Depths away from prying eyes; and it's up to the party to determine whether the deeds of these constructs (nicknamed the Downsiders) merit their destruction or their autonomy.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.Rh7z2eruwwhFlG58]{Zodi Trask}

  • @UUID[Actor.gGNpwLWttuHPZF1W]{Larissa Toth}

  • @UUID[Actor.XK20zaizyZOLGmsl]{Hew}

  • @UUID[Actor.OYdqWs17RvL7ntbf]{Lucent}

  • @UUID[Actor.1ZEi2D4j2RbKDc9x]{Rider}

  • @UUID[Actor.iOyLbOiGrqMY49QI]{Chamberlain}

  • @UUID[Actor.nnTbrW4RdzudxxMT]{Vartholomew Chess}

  • @UUID[Actor.BU1Vzjo20Q4CUjTK]{Ifton Shepp}

  • Nodrick Stolas

  • Calandra

  • Hob Korell

  • Eolas Hathwick

  • Zirca Bronzebellow

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.0xDU0k3l8V4movO8]{Chessman}

  • @UUID[Actor.mGxrffI6CI7Dd5rU]{Silver Beam Servitor}

  • @UUID[Actor.r1L9EyeHna2sm8tE]{Silver Beam Sentinel}

  • @UUID[Actor.vyN7FNbPEw6KsuGw]{Silver Beam Engineer}

  • @UUID[Actor.6NOp0fdZPcSnGzO7]{Silver Beam Guard}

  • @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{Skither}

  • @UUID[Actor.eOeEoqatnUz1TOVR]{Vorg}

  • @UUID[Actor.AnhHlAMP5rsnH7wZ]{Mootap}

  • @UUID[Actor.oannEhbJhuyf19Qd]{Jurtak Hunter}

  • @UUID[Actor.ZcHPxGsFjhqfXvud]{Jurtak Warrior}

  • @UUID[Actor.m86FIWDHh47htZNy]{Jurtak Geomancer}
Overview.soverview:
Rumors are sweeping through the Golden Flats about an unsolved crime in the sinkhole city of Arcturel, a place where lawlessness has a loose foothold and lost things are seldom found. It seems one of the ubiquitous constructs used for manual labor in Lower Arcturel's industrial sector went haywire and killed an innocent bystander, and now the murderous automaton is missing — having fled the scene of the crime to places unknown in or around the Sinkhole City itself.

Naturally, a pall of paranoia and civil unrest has settled on the various districts of Arcturel, whose citizens live in mounting fear of the errant "Renegade Construct" and its homicidal tendencies. In an effort to stem this tide of turmoil, House Cevher and other businesses of Arcturel have teamed up to hire some outside investigators to track down the missing construct and mete out some proper recompense. Enter the party, who may very well discover a new definition of justice before Arcturel's score with the Renegade Construct is settled.

"Glitter in the Dark" will task the party with tracking down the so-called Renegade Construct and examining the mysterious events that surround the incident with the deceased citizen, a miner named Kellen Lorde. This investigation will lead the characters from the upper reaches of Arcturel to the darkest subterranean corners of the Sinkhole Depths — where the party will come face-to-face not only with their quarry, but with their very sense of right and wrong.

Concerned Merchants.name: Concerned Merchants
Concerned Merchants.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event introduces the party to a group of merchants that have recently visited the sinkhole city of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel}, where a "renegade construct" is purported to have murdered a human being. In this event, the characters can:

  • Meet the merchants Doran Styme and Nevel Rux, the gregarious leaders of the "Rux Brothers" caravan, and join them for a free meal.

  • Learn about the caravan's recent visit to Arcturel, where rumors abound about a murderous Chessman construct on the loose.

  • Purchase various goods and services from the merchants, if desired.

Approaching the Caravan

If the characters approach the caravan with any amount of caution, propriety, or stealth, they can easily overhear a couple of the merchants engaged in conversation — who earnestly discuss their most recent venture to the infamous sinkhole city of Arcturel. These are Doran Styme (Lawful Neutral, Arcturian Human, he/him), a squat leather trader in his late forties, and his older "brother" Nevel Rux (Chaotic Good, Arcturian Human, he/him), a reedy jewel merchant in his early fifties.

As the characters approach, read the following:

Nearing the encampment, your attention is drawn to the cook, a squat human merchant dressed in Arcturian fineries who sprinkles some kind of aromatic herbs from a small jar onto the spit-roasted meat. A taller man clad in similar garb accented by countless rings, bracelets, and necklaces joins the shorter fellow with a pouch full of his own seasoning — which he sprinkles on the meat despite protestation from his associate.

Moons help us, Nevel, you're going to ruin the recipe!

The taller fellow retorts:

Pish posh, Doran. You'll never form a proper bark without enough pepper. Now stand aside and let a real artist cook.

Doran keeps a close eye on his tall friend, who offers a liberal dusting of spices to the meat. The short merchant continues:

I know you better than that. You're just in a hurry to use those spices you picked up in Arcturel. So be it! But if you ruin that roast, you will never hear the end of it, Nevel. I promise you!

Just then, these two would-be gourmands notice your group. They greet you with a polite smile and a hurried wave that beckons you to join them. Stepping forward, you notice a banner on the wagon behind them that reads: "Rux Brothers, Est. 2495."

Meeting the Merchants

As the rest of the caravan members go about their business in the background, Doran and Nevel are eager to become acquainted with the party — not only for the company, but for the timely chance of an unexpected sale.

An Invitation to Supper

The merchants quickly introduce themselves as the Rux Brothers, although they are brothers in name alone. Treat them both as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.monsters.Actor.GlaCGcgIP6YjBjGc]{Nobles} @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians}.

  • Doran Styme (Lawful Neutral, Arcturian Human, he/him), a squat leather trader in his mid-fifties. Weathered and well-traveled, Doran greets people with a hearty laugh and warm voice. The gregarious merchant is pragmatic and patient, always willing to find the best solution after weighing options.

  • Nevel Rux (Chaotic Good, Arcturian Human, he/him), a reedy jewel merchant in his early sixties. A few years Doran's senior, Nevel acts as the assertive and pontifical "big brother" in the relationship and is quick to offer his so-called expert opinion on nearly everything.

After introductions, the Rux Brothers invite the party to join them for a complimentary meal, which consists of the seasoned meat from a large Nothrin shank and a salad of mixed greens, dried fruits, and candied nuts. Doran and Nevel offer up a variety of anecdotal information during the meal, including:

  • Their history together as entrepreneurs of the Arctus Plateau.

  • Their recent visit to Arcturel, along with rumors about a haywire Chessman accused of murder and the failing trade practices of House Cevher.

  • Tantalizing descriptions of the origin of their wares, which include various weapons, armor, tools, rations, and trade goods. And while they've recently collected a fair amount of Inkaro Pearls from Arcturel, that inventory is spoken for, and the nacreous arcane orbs are not for sale.

  • Advice for the journey to Arcturel, including some basic resources available to visitors.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck deception 12]] check is able to confirm the validity of Doran and Nevel's claims, and have no reason to mistrust their account of the sinkhole city and its plight.

The "Rux Brothers"

Doran

I met this old buzzard at the schoolhouse in Nain when we were just boys. Those days, my diminutive stature earned me more than a few taunts from the other children; so you can imagine my surprise and appreciation when the tallest kid in school started standing up for me.

Nevel

Indeed. I saw a little brother in Doran back then. And so, my brother he became. As the years went by and we stumbled from adolescence into adulthood, we decided to chase our fortunes and glory together on the open road as merchants of the wide Plateau. And it's been a fun ride ever since. Though we are brothers from different mothers, we are siblings all the same.

Doran

Still, I remain convinced: the banner would look better if it read "Styme Brothers" instead!

Nevel dismisses this claim with a cheeky grin before sipping a draught of wine.

Yes, Doran. I'm sure you do …

Arcturel

Doran

Ah, yes. The Glittering City. Those of you unfamiliar with Arcturel should know that it is built among the walls of a massive sinkhole that stretches from the surface village of Brimtown to the rough-and-tumble planks of Rock Bottom in the Pathways below. There's no other city in the world quite like it.

Nevel

It is truly an intriguing place — that is, if you can manage the incessant dust and rust that comes along with it. Perhaps your intrepid troupe would have some insights to offer the troubled locals regarding their so-called Renegade Construct.

Renegade Chessman

Doran

Certainly, you've seen a Chessman in your travels. They happen to be the most prized automatons on the Arcturian market these days. An ingenious Hulg'run fellow named Vartholomew Chess is responsible for their exceptional design. This is the first time I've heard of a Chessman falling short of its expectations; they're rather remarkable machines, if you ask me.

Nevel

Truly, the modern Inkaro trade thrives because of the workforce these tireless constructs provide. And as you can imagine, a complication for the pearl industry is a complication for the entire Arctus Plataeau. Hopefully, this haywire Chessman is an isolated incident. House Cevher has enough problems on their hands these days without faulty automatons killing innocent citizens when they least expect it.

House Cevher

Nevel

In all my decades, I've known House Cevher to be a competent and conscientious partner. As one of the Plateau's most esteemed jewel merchants, I consider my alliance with the Trading House to be a rather necessary one. I grow concerned whenever I hear of troubles within House Cevher's operations. And it seems they're having a little trouble in Arcturel these days.

Doran

No doubt. Rallyhome was full of rumors about impending issues, from the case of the Renegade Construct to a mounting unrest among the House Cevher miners. It seems like they're having a bad season. But I don't grow too concerned for the Trading Houses — they have all the resources they need to bounce back from a little slump. I'm sure they'll be just fine …

What the Party Already Knows

One or more of the party members may already be familiar with the sinkhole city of Arcturel. If the players ask or the characters would otherwise know, consider the following skill checks:

[[/skill history 12]] [[/skillCheck society 12]] The character is familiar with the general history of Arcturel and its location near the southern edge of the Golden Flats. Among various details, the character understands Arcturel to be governed by a syndicate of business owners, they know of Arcturel's relatively lawless nature, and its status as the region's only source of Inkaro Pearls. Characters with [[/knowledge subterranea]] or [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on this check.

  • Success - Other than Inkaro Pearls, Arcturel is a source of a wide variety of rare resources and raw materials (both magical and mundane), and House Cevher has maintained a foothold on this industry for most of Arcturel's storied history. Furthermore, the inventor of the Chessmen constructs — a gifted artificer named Vartholomew Chess — lives in Upper Arcturel's "Balconies" district.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The character is familiar with Arcturel as a haven for adventurers and would-be profiteers, and knows of a talented Vrjnhar bard named Gullivhar Paras who frequents a tavern in Upper Arcturel known as Rallyhome. They say the Oaken bard knows anything and everything about what happens in the sinkhole city, so he may serve as a potential point of contact.

[[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] The character is aware of the importance of Inkaro Pearls to the Arctus Plateau, and knows that these nacreous orbs are harvested from dangerous creatures called Mootaps, which lair in pools of arcane water within the Sinkhole Depths.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge monsters]], [[/knowledge subterranea]], or [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on this check.

Trade with the Rux Brothers

If the characters are interested in buying or selling any goods, Doran and Nevel are eager to trade with the party on behalf of the rest of the caravan.

Goods & Services

The Rux Brothers caravan is currently stocked with ample goods gathered from all over the Arctus Plateau, and can supply the characters with the following in exchange for their standard prices:

  • Any light or medium armor, up to a quantity of 4 each.

  • Any simple or ranged weapon, up to a quantity of 4 each.

  • Any martial weapon, up to a quantity of 2 each — excluding glaives, greatswords, halberds, lances, pikes, tridents, blowguns, and hand crossbows.

  • A wide variety of Adventuring Gear, Tools, and Trade Goods.

  • Most spell components that cost 1 gold piece or less (at your discretion).

Doran and Nevel are also willing to spend up to 400 gp to the party in exchange for any used goods the characters wish to sell them, but will only offer half of each item's original purchase price.

  • Each character can convince the Rux Brothers to pay full price for their own used goods with either a successful [[/skill deception 15]] or [[/skill persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15]] or [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check. Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on these checks.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Following their encounter with the concerned merchants, the party can journey to Arcturel to find out more about the so-called Renegade Construct that is rumored to be on the loose. Once the characters reach the surface-level Arcturel suburb known as Brimtown, they'll encounter the events of [[/eventState arcturelSideSurface]].
Concerned Merchants.soverview: While traveling the Golden Flats, the party encounters a small merchant caravan making their way from the infamous sinkhole city of Arcturel. The gregarious merchants offer the characters a free meal, some samples of their wares, and a selection of the region's most recent gossip — including the peculiar story of a haywire construct who killed an ill-fated miner in Arcturel's Dives.
Concerned Merchants.sexposition: You spy a caravan of a half-dozen carts and wagons parked ahead, attended by a small group of humanoids and their beasts of burden. Several jittery rask bound about the camp with playful abandon, while the caravan's noble yarnac engage in active rest and relaxation. Judging by the scattered array of mercantile goods that some of the humanoids sort through, you'd wager this convoy is made primarily of Arcturian merchants and their wares. The smell of savory food wafts from a small fire pit at the encampment's center, where one merchant attends a large cut of seasoned meat roasting on a spit. The scene is a lively and inviting one.
Concerned Merchants.ssummary: We encountered stationary caravan of traveling merchants, who invited us into their camp. Along with their hospitality and a selection of their wares, these merchants offered rumors about a Renegade Construct accused of murder in the sinkhole city of Arcturel.

A Troubled Tradeway.name: A Troubled Tradeway
A Troubled Tradeway.text:
Gamemaster's Summary
