  • The Harrowed Townsfolk are also willing to provide basic details about Skybrush itself, including various points of interest and a key few personages.

A successful [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck deception 12]] check allows characters to confirm the veracity of the Townsfolk's tale; the truth behind their plight seems unmistakable.

  • Result of 17+ Critical success: There is no hiding the dread and trepidation in the Townsfolk's eyes, and your gut tells you that Valence himself feels downright haunted. There is a thinly-veiled sorrow to this exodus, signifying the loss of home and sanctity.

Suggested dialog with Valence can be found below, including his reaction to questions about the young girl's Moon Blossom as described in 'Signs of Strife' above.

Who are you?

My name is Valence, friend. And these are my people. I make my coin as a carpenter, and this axe at my side is sharp enough to split a jurtak's skull — so please, kindly help us keep the peace and we'll be well on our way.

About Skybrush:

It pains us to say goodbye to a place we've known so long… our village in the trees, where the wind chimes sing and a dappled sun dances above the proud ruins of ancient giants. But that whimsy is gone, replaced by the lingering threat of a gruesome death. Good riddance, I say. And Gods take whatever evil came to Skybrush!

About the young girl's flower:

Deera has always had a special fondness for the outdoors. She takes after her mother in that regard.

The elder nods towards a headstrong Arcturian woman seated in the wagon beside the girl. After a brief moment of thought, he regards you once more.

Those cerulean anemones grow in and around Skybrush, but I'm no gardener. If you're lucky, that's the last one of those little flowers you'll ever see, friend.

Efforts to gather information elsewhere about the incident in Skybrush are relatively fruitless, compelling the characters to explore the harrowed settlement for themselves.

Concluding the Event

Once the characters have satisfied their curiosity with the Skybrush refugees, the party is ready to venture forth. With the location of Skybrush newly indicated on their map, the party can travel towards that remote treetop village to investigate the unsavory rumors of a killer in the town's midst.

Next Steps

This quest begins in earnest when the party arrives at Skybrush themselves, in the [[/eventState brushWithDeathSkybrush1]] event.
Flight from the Dark.soverview: The party encounters a group of harrowed commonfolk on the road: expatriates from nearby Skybrush headed eastward to the lakeside haven of Storsa's Strand. These troubled townsfolk speak of murder and ill-omens, which they're desperate to escape.
Flight from the Dark.sexposition: You find yourself approaching a procession of three wagons on the broken valley road. A half-dozen humanoid commoners drive this tiny caravan forward at a swift pace, and an elder among them looks back over his shoulder with curious regularity — eyes hidden by his low-worn cowl.
Flight from the Dark.ssummary: We encountered a small caravan of townsfolk from Skybrush, who claim to have fled the treetop village in the advent of a dangerous murderer and thinly-veiled portents of doom.

The Situation in Skybrush.name: The Situation in Skybrush
The Situation in Skybrush.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration event that welcomes the party to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} where multiple murders herald the rise of some evil force. This event is depicted in @UUID[Scene.emberVistaSkybru]{Vista: Skybrush}, where the characters can:

  • Encounter a local washerwoman named Gurty Holdstone who offers words of warning in @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.nYENxoxsgZ78PDwc#the-lurking-fear]{The Lurking Fear}.

  • Visit The Roost, Skybrush's neighborhood watering hole, where a grizzled mine worker named Mattock can provide information about the murders in @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.nYENxoxsgZ78PDwc#the-word-about-town]{The Word About Town}.

  • Visit an accused murderer named Qory Hult in the Blockhouse jail and survey his deranged state in @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.nYENxoxsgZ78PDwc#the-agitated-prisoner]{The Agitated Prisoner}.

  • Follow up with a visit to Qory Hult's home, where additional clues wait to be found in @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.nYENxoxsgZ78PDwc#the-scene-of-the-crime]{The Scene of the Crime}.

  • Discover clues throughout these encounters that will point the party towards a reclusive artist named Gedron Tath.

Before undertaking this event, you may wish to read through @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.MyxkUsLNydK7zTBE]{Revealing the Mystery} to understand the truth of events before players begin their investigation.

The remote treetop settlement known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} has fallen under hard times and ill omens as a mysterious curse of undeath plagues its inhabitants. The citizens of skybrush are a mixture of stalward mining folk and proud lumber workers and are ignorant of the curse's sinister origin — the wraith of a Varùn warlock entombed deep in the Skybrush hinterlands. With any luck, the timely arrival of the party might help turn the bleak tide for this shadow-haunted frontier town.

Although many people of Skybrush are going about their daily business, something clearly troubles these rural folk, who regard the party with a healthy mix of curiosity and suspicion. Skybrush is cloaked in a palpable sense of dread, and the party's first encounter will point them towards the presence of a larger threat.

The Lurking Fear

As you make your way through Skybrush, a local washerwoman meets your gaze. This elderly woman appears intently alert, and speaks up with righteous admonition.

"You sure picked a bad time to visit Skybrush, strangers! There's a murderer on the loose in our humble town, and another killer's been locked up in the local gaol. Keep your eyes open, especially at night! Foul deeds are afoot…"

Her gaze lingers in your direction, as if silently inviting you to engage her in further conversation.

A Friendly Warning

This remonstrative washerwoman is Gurty Holdstone (Neutral, Arcturian Human, she/her), who is known throughout Skybrush for her overtly cautious nature. If the characters would like to know more, Gurty is all-too-eager to oblige them, although she indulges in a fair amount of unnecessary dramatic flair. Gurty has the following information to offer:

  • The first murder that happened was the killing of Branos Erekos by his brother Dereth, who's gone missing after the incident. Mr. & Mrs. Erekos are in mourning, and aren't taking visitors at this time. Gurty recommends giving them a day or two for bereavement.

  • The second murder involved a young miner named Qory Hult who supposedly killed his wife. Qory is being held at the local gaol situated in The Blockhouse.

  • Gossip and rumors are never in short supply at The Roost, Skybrush's communal tavern in the treetop Canopy district.

  • Other than occasional attacks from local wildlife, Skybrush has never been a place for trouble or mortal terror. The people here are hard-working, and like to celebrate the fruits of their labors with good times and hearty celebration.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] check find Gurty's cautious information suitably trustworthy. She has nothing to hide.

The Word About Town

Whether the party follows Gurty's advice or not, the Roost (situated in the Canopy district) stands out as one of the most suitable places to gather basic information. Considering the relatively subdued dispositions throughout Skybrush, this treetop watering hole is by far the liveliest venue in town.

This potentially serves as a first point of contact with Liestra Grann, the town's resident pawn broker and an influential ally of the Anachraenum. Although she doesn't offer much in the way of information at this time, Liestra invites the party to ask further questions while they're perusing the wares in her shop across town: The Long Haul.

@Embed[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R label="Liestra Grann"]

Rumor Mill

At The Roost, there is always talk of local happenings. If the party visits this treetop tavern with queries about Skybrush's recent disturbances, they can meet a few locals.

A handful of NPCs frequent the Roost, including @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann}, Danton Shain, Shax the Seeress, and Hadras. At this time, however, they're more concerned with escaping their woes than educating outsiders.

One grizzled citizen in particular is eager to share everything they know; this is Mattock (Neutral Good, Arcturian Fej, he/him) a scar-striped Arcturian mine worker who's seen more action than most of Skybrush. Mattock's rumors include:

  • Seemingly out of nowhere, the young bard Dereth Erekos lost his mind and killed his brother Branos in cold blood. There were no witnesses, just evidence from the scene of the crime. After the incident, Dereth fled town hasn't been heard from since. Their poor parents are completely absorbed by fear and sorrow.

  • Three nights later, a fellow mineworker named Qory Hult went mad and slaughtered his wife and their unborn child in the most gruesome display of violence the town has ever seen. Qory is currently locked up in the town gaol, and doesn't seem to remember what happened. He claims he had nothing to do with it, but the blood on his hands suggests otherwise.

  • Many townsfolk want swift mob justice for these atrocities, but the Town Council likes to do things by the book. An imminent inquest is needed to assess Qory and Dereth's culpability.

  • Stranger still, both of these incidents were the subject of paintings from a local artist — an eccentric loner named Gedron Tath who lives outside the city limits. The strangest part is that Tath painted these 2 scenes at least a week before they happened. Was it precognition or premeditation?

  • As for Kel Kornan: she lives nearby in the Canopy district, but hasn't been seen about town for several days.

If the characters press the subject of Qory's wife Veera and their unborn child, Hadras will speak up to confirm the following:

  • Veera's bloody corpse was laid to rest in a ceremony Hadras himself, burned to ash according to ancient rites.

The Agitated Prisoner

Gurty Holdstone and Mattock present the party with information that should point them towards The Blockhouse, where a local miner has been imprisoned for the crime of killing his wife and child. Here, they can speak with the accused as well as the town's constable.

Optional Area Map

If you wish to further build suspense at this stage of the investigation, you may use the @UUID[Scene.emberArcturiJail]{Arcturian Jail} area map for the party's conversation with Qory. This map will be used again later during the subsequent [[/eventState brushWithDeathSkybrush2]] event when Qory is overcome by his curse.

Interrogating the Accused

Qory Hult (Chaotic Good, Arcturian Human, he/him) is afflicted with early onset of @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}, and has been locked up in the Blockhouse gaol after he murdered his wife and child during a state of magical confusion. His belongings, including the murder weapon (an ancient @UUID[Item.w7jXkPu7MheM6bkw]{Rune-Marked Arrowhead}), are locked up in Constable Mica Valaston's office nearby.

Qory is available for questioning from the confines of his cell, and has the following information to offer:

  • Qory maintains that he is innocent, and doesn't remember anything of his wife and child's murder. He came to and was surrounded by blood and their warm corpses, ancient Varùn Arrowhead in hand.

  • The Rune-Marked Arrowhead is something he found while working the mine.

  • He's suspicious of Gedron Tath's macabre paintings and is certain they have something to do with the grim occurrence. Qory assures the characters that this is no mere coincidence, and begs them to seek answers from Tath on his behalf.

Characters who have [[/skill insight 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill insight 13]] check [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15 passive]] are able to confirm the veracity of Qory's confessions, and his suspicion of Gedron Tath seems sincere.

  • Result of 18+ Critical success: Qory seems afraid for more than his life; it's as if his very soul is on the execution block. More curiously, his story about the Varùn Arrowhead rings false.

A successful [[/skill intimidation 18]] or [[/skill persuasion 16]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 16]] or [[/skillCheck diplomacy 16]] check is needed to gain a further confession from Qory about the true origin of the Arrowhead, which he admits was purchased from a local shop as an inevitable gift for his son — an investment for the future that he could barely afford on a miner's salary, and something he was sincerely afraid to boast about.

Nearby the gaol where Qory is held, the party may encounter the local constable.

@Embed[Actor.cvyDEZu7WvSDLzAo]

Meeting the Constable

Constable Mica Valaston is the local authority in law enforcement, and maintains a Blockhouse office adjacent to the gaol. The constable speaks with a smoky femme voice and greets the party politely but with a hint of skepticism.

Constable Mica Valaston, at your service. I see you've found your way to Skybrush. So tell me: what brings you here, of all places?

This cynical Arcturian gendarme can offer the party the following information:

  • Mica doesn't fully know what to make of the situation, but they do know that Qory was found at the scene of the crime with the murder weapon and his family's blood on his hands.

  • Before the incident, Qory was a relatively unremarkable citizen, known to appreciate his privacy and the simple rewards of family life. He doesn't have any best friends, aside from his deceased wife. Mica expresses an amount of sympathy for the young man, and laments the squandered potential of his lost family.

  • Veera Hult's corpse was laid to rest in a ceremony led by the priest Hadras, burned to ash according to ancient rites.

Qory Hult's belongings are being held in an iron-bound evidence chest sealed with a formidable lock. If the party is upfront with their intentions, Mica has no problem letting them see the contents to assist their investigation, but only under direct supervision.

A successful [[/skill persuasion 18]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 18]] check is required to convince Mica to allow the party to take the Varùn Arrowhead with them to assist their investigation. Given the extreme suspicion surrounding this remarkably macabre case, Mica can't be bribed.

Akon Attunement: Convince the Constable

The first character who manages to successfully convince Mica Valaston to let the party take possession of the Varùn Arrowhead advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 brushWithDeathSkybrush1Mica]] at the conclusion of the event.

If the characters fail to convince Mica Valaston of their efforts or wish purloin the contents of the iron-bound evidence chest, they can attempt to pick the lock.

Acquiring the Evidence

A successful [[/check dexterity 18 tool=thief]] check [[/skillCheck stealth 18]] check using @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.lockpicks0000000]is required to pick the lock, which is built into the iron bindings of the chest itself. The contents of the evidence chest include Qory Hult's belongings:

  • A @UUID[Item.ZwCcNTFuiYAug3ET]{Cloak Pin} adorned with the House Cevher Mining Guild insignia

  • A dusty gray cloak marked with lovingly-stitched repairs (sentimental value only)

  • A pair of modern Arcturian Bracers (worth [[/award 2gp]] [[/award 2sp]])

  • An ancient @UUID[Item.w7jXkPu7MheM6bkw]{Rune-Marked Arrowhead} (the murder weapon)

Luxarum Attunement: Steal the Evidence

The first character to successfully steal the Rune-Marked Arrowhead from the evidence chest advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 brushWithDeathSkybrush1Evidence]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Scene of the Crime

The party can also visit Qory Hult's bloodstained home to investigate the scene of the crime. Here, they can speak with a meddlesome neighbor while examining the home itself for additional evidence.

Surveying the Hult Estate

The characters can find a few clues if they decide to search Qory Hult's home for information.

Outside, characters with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passwive]] will notice @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} blooming outside the Hult home. Alternately, any character who makes a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check will be able to spot the scattered presence of these lambent cerulean flowers about the exterior.

Although Veera Hult's corpse has been cremated, the interior still harbors evidence of the murder where bloodstains cover the front room, the overturned furniture indicates clear signs of physical struggle.

A successful [[/skill medicine 14]] [[/skillCheck medicine 14]] check will confirm the veracity of the forensics to date: a sharp weapon was used to puncture Veera's jugular vein, and she died of rapid exsanguination.

The Haunting of Hult House

As the characters search about Qory Hult's home, they're approached by an elderly woman with an unmistakable look of inquisitiveness on her wizened face. This nosy neighbor is Mrs. Estweather (Neutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/her), and she's eager to share a few salacious details.

  • There was a "perverted artist" named Gedron Tath hanging around who created a painting that caused a fight within the household.

  • The Hults never had any real fights to speak of, so Qory's behavior is curious in addition to the outright shock of the situation.

  • Veera's body was burned quickly after passing, although this is a customary funerary rite.

A successful [[/skill persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check, a successful [[/skill deception 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15]] check, or a bribe of [[/award 5gp]] [[/award 5sp]] or more convinces Mrs. Estweather to reveal that Veera had grown increasingly suspicious of her husband's behavior in the week that followed the art's arrival.

Some dialog responses from Mrs. Estweather are presented below:

What do you know?

I can tell you're looking into things here — nobody listens to me about anything but I know a thing or two, you mark my words!

Qory and his wife Veera had an argument about "that perverted artist" Gedron Tath's "sick joke of a painting" just a week ago. Qory was somewhat amused at the time, and Veera most certainly was not; while Mr. Hult was eager to dismiss the art as fantasy, his wife was notably suspicious of the grim imagery and ultimately offended by it.

Veera's fate?

It's a shame the beautiful young woman's body had to be burned so quickly, but rites are rites. And Hadras, as quiet and eccentric as he is, is a fine enough holy man for Skybrush.

Concluding the Event

Investigation of any of the scenes described in this event may very well compel the characters to return to a previously encountered scene. No matter the order of their investigations, the discovery of the artist Gedron Tath's implied involvement is paramount to the party's next steps.

[[/outcome gedronEvidence]]

Primordis Attunement: A Suspicious Artist

If the party manages to deduce that Gedron Tath is their most prominent lead (and devises a plan to visit his remote estate), each character advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 brushWithDeathSkybrush1Gedron]] at the conclusion of the event.

Clues gained from conversations with Mattock at The Roost, Qory Hult at the Blockhouse, and Mrs. Estweather at the Hult home should inevitably lead the party a mile from town to investigate the remote domicile of Gedron Tath — an eccentric illustrator and sculptor who purchased a cursed Varùn Ring from Liestra Grann.

Next Steps

The party's investigation will take them to [[/eventState brushWithDeathHill]] to investigate Gedron Tath.

If the characters were commissioned by Kadrick Pond in [[/eventState brushWithDeathOrdain]] to search out Kel Kornan, they can locate her treetop domicile in Skybrush — but there is no sign of the House Cehver contact at this time. Further details about Kel will be revealed later in [[/eventState brushWithDeathSkybrush2]].
The Situation in Skybrush.soverview:
The party reaches Skybrush, a lonely mountainside settlement with a reputation for its exports of rare lumber and ancient giantkin artifacts. The sense of dread that hangs about the place is palpable, and several clues throughout town point towards the presence of a larger threat.

Although many people of Skybrush are going about their daily business, something clearly troubles them as they regard the party with a healthy mix of curiosity and suspicion.
The Situation in Skybrush.sexposition: Passing through Skybrush, you can't help but note how the dour faces of depressed townsfolk look upon you with remarkable disdain, as if they somehow hold contempt for the vibrancy you've brought here with you. The people here seem lonely, bitter, and afraid; but a few hopeful expressions that peek out from darkened windows and shaded doorways break up this sullen monotony.
The Situation in Skybrush.ssummary: After reaching Skybrush, we gathered information throughout town by speaking with a few locals. Two citizens have been accused of gruesome murders here, including the missing bard Dereth Erekos and a jailed mine worker named Qory Hult. We investigated the gruesome crimes and it is clear that some strange malevolence has afflicted the people of this remote town.

Where Evil Lurks.name: Where Evil Lurks
Where Evil Lurks.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is an exploration and combat event that challenges the party to explore the shadow-haunted interior of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CS82h91RP59553vr]{The Bleak Archive}, an aged Shent repository of Abyssal relics and pre-Shattering antiquities.

In this event, the characters can:

  • Explore the Bleak Archive for the source of @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment} curse that afflicts Skybrush.

  • Survive the area's hazards, including various mechanical and magical traps, along with the evil minions of the wraithlike warlock @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd]{Tethra Shùl}.

  • Combat Tethra Shùl herself in an attempt to put an end to The Bewilderment and the Abyssal scourge that has come to Skybrush.

  • Recover a forbidden Abyssal artifact from Tethra Shùl known as a @UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas}.

  • Entreat with a spectral memory of the Shent Sage known as @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth}.

Exploring the Bleak Archive

Once the party reaches The Bleak Archive, they must find a way inside and explore its tenebrous reaches for signs of The Bewilderment's furtive origin. A full description of The Bleak Archive location can be found in @UUID[Scene.emberBleakArchiv]{The Bleak Archive} area walkthrough.

Signara Attunement: Mirror Puzzle Solved

If the party manages to reach the Bleak Archive's @UUID[JournalEntry.skQcdBxw8K0AS7hv.JournalEntryPage.TfjCELA7w5tj5ybN]{True Vault} by successfully solving the mirror array's puzzle of sealed chambers, each character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 brushWithDeathArchivesMirrors]] at the conclusion of the event.

Ragen Attunement: True Vault Breached

Although the Bleak Archive's True Vault can't normally be reached by any way other than solving the mirror array puzzle, this is a game of exceptions.

If the party manages to reach the True Vault by some method other than solving the mirror puzzle (including the use of spells or spell-like abilities), each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 brushWithDeathArchivesBreached]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Warlock's Legacy

Once the party reaches the Bleak Archive's Inner Sanctum, they must contend with the wraithlike warlock @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd]{Tethra Shùl} in mortal combat. After Tethra Shùl has been defeated, the characters must destroy or consecrate her worldly remains to loosen The Bewilderment's hold on Skybrush.

Cleansing the Wraith's Remains

Once Tethra Shùl has been defeated in combat, her worldly remains must be destroyed or consecrated via one of the following methods:

  • Destroying the Remains. Characters can destroy Tethra Shùl's worldly remains by inflicting 33 hit points of additional magical damage to the remains. If the remains are destroyed, all creatures within 30 feet must succeed on a [[/save wis 15]] saving throw or take [[/damage 2d4 necrotic]] damage and [[/damage 2d4 psychic]] damage. Characters who take damage this way are subject to the effects of a @UUID[RollTable.YktgyhNcShUVGd6X]{Minor Abyssal Madness} until they have completed 7 Long Rests.

  • Consecrating the Remains. Characters can consecrate Tethra Shùl's worldly remains by casting either the @UUID[Actor.fuL7YqC7eENDtHeJ.Item.BE6ec6v5AVnSxz2R]{Bless} spell or the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.xmDBqZhRVrtLP8h2]{Protection from Evil and Good} spell using the remains as the target (the remains count as a willing creature for the purposes of this effect). Alternately, a cleric can use their @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.classfeatures.Item.r91UIgwFdHwkXdia]{Channel Divinity} ability to Turn Undead within 30 feet of the remains to consecrate them (roll Wisdom save using Tethra Shùl's stat block).

Tethra Shùl's worldly remains are imbued with a persistent enchantment from @Spell[spell.death.aura.influence].

  • Destroying the Remains. The remains can be destroyed by dealing 33 points of magical damage to the remains. If the remains are destroyed, all creatures within 30 feet experience [[/hazard 4 fortitude health corruption]]{Necrotic Wave} and [[/hazard 4 willpower morale void]]{Abyssal Screams}. Characters who take damage this way are subject to the effects of a .

  • Dispelling the Remains. The remains can be dispelled using a ritual to counterspell the effect, through [[/counterspell rune=death gesture=influence inflection=negate dc=16]]. Dispelling the remains effectively consecrates them for the purposes of the Consecration outcome.

    • The nature of the enchantment can be recognized with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]].

    • Attempts to dispel using the Life rune gain +2 Boons.

    • Attempts to dispel using the Death rune suffer +2 Banes.

Heart Attunement: Warlock's Remains Consecrated

If the characters cleanse the Bleak Archive by consecrating Tethra Shùl's remains, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 brushWithDeathArchivesConsecrated]] at the conclusion of the event.

Cora Attunement: Warlock's Remains Destroyed

If the characters cleanse the Bleak Archive by destroying Tethra Shùl's remains, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 brushWithDeathArchivesDestroyed]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome cleansed]]

Once the worldly remains of Tethra Shùl have been cleansed, read the following:

The physical remains of Tethra Shùl begin to shudder and crack as beams of light shoot forth from tiny fissures in the wraithlike warlock's malevolent skull. After a brief crescendo, the remains disintegrate in a blinding flash, and the undying spellcaster is no more.

You can't help but think of the treetop hamlet and the curse that has afflicted it. The people of Skybrush will no doubt wish to know about your triumph here this day.

Inert Relics

Once Tethra Shùl's remains have been properly dealt with, both the curse and the enchantments laid upon the 5 Varùn Relics become inert and the items lose their potency. These items are still of interest to collectors, but are now non-magical and only worth 25% of their original stated value:

  • @UUID[Item.w7jXkPu7MheM6bkw]{Rune-Marked Arrowhead}

  • @UUID[Item.tft5aeUE51jyKoqX]{Rune-Marked Band}

  • @UUID[Item.59gxtjjpznto4p2x]{Rune-Marked Knife}

  • @UUID[Item.OJRVuMrUlSAM3soe]{Rune-Marked Sash}

  • @UUID[Item.s2rgATaIZi2879IM]{Rune-Marked Vial}

The Finger of Nethehepticas

The party must also decide whether or not to retrieve the @UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas} from among the wraithlike warlock's remains. Their decision to loot this accursed relic will have a noteworthy effect on gameplay to come.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check is able to determine the magical nature of the Finger of Nethehepticas without the benefits of a @UUID[Actor.MJfOzwa6uawHDhHA.Item.iCaiYRPxSxowvFJa]{Detect Magic} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} spell and its categorization as a wand without the need for [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]], but they can determine little else.

  • Result of 16+ Success: The wand is clearly an item of great power. Its accursed nature also becomes apparent, but the actual effects and properties of the curse remain inscrutable.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success: The character recognizes the Abyssal nature of the wand, but its properties remain inscrutable.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 17]] [[/skillCheck society 17]] check has heard a handful of legends and rumors regarding ancient artifacts crafted from the remains of godlike beings, and this strange eldritch relic seems a likely candidate.

Alternatively, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check is able to determine the otherworldly nature of the wand's origin, but its Abyssal identity remains elusive.

Abyss Attunement: Strange Relic

The first character to take possession of the @UUID[Item.KIRSWcFMZoW52CpM]{Finger of Nethehepticas} advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 brushWithDeathArchivesRelic]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Shadow of Tethra Shùl

If the party fails to destroy or consecrate Tethra Shùl's worldly remains, the effects of the Bewilderment continue to plague the citizens of Skybrush and anyone who comes into contact with the cursed Varùn artifacts.

Once one-hundred days have passed, Tethra Shùl will rise from the grave to inhabit the Bleak Archive once again.

A Departing Word

As the party exits the Bleak Archive via the Main Gallery, the arcane spirit of the Shent Sage @UUID[Actor.vJTrFC4smlGimCqw]{Mioroth} appears to the characters to share a word of warning.

A Final Visit from Mioroth

Whether or not a character interacts with one of the Crystal Relics or the Alloyed Clockwork here, the spectral memory of Mioroth appears near one of these esoteric items.

Mioroth addresses the characters directly as soon as he arrives. Read the following aloud:

As you make your way through the Main Gallery, the semi-translucent memory of the Shent Sage Mioroth appears once more, appearing close to a nearby gemstone in a fluttering brilliance of arcane light.

Ebbok Zhùr is no place for the faint of heart, and whatever wounds you wear — be they scars of the body or mind — shall serve in remembrance.

As you depart, remember what you take with you. The Abyss and its minions leave a stain that once marked may forever remain.

He looks to you with the calm interest of a scholastic mentor, as if waiting for an inquiry or the solicitation of rare advice.

A Parting Conversation with Mioroth

The characters have a few moments to beseech the Sage's memory before they depart. Mioroth can readily offer the party information on the following topics:

  • On the Abyss: The Abyss is an infinite realm beyond the Weave that contains otherworldly creatures of terrible power.

  • Regarding Tethra Shùl: The Abyss can be a source of power for the peoples upon Ember, the kind of power that comes at a price. The Varùn warlock named Tethra Shùl was a servant of these dark powers via her eldritch otherworldly patron.

  • About the Finger of Nethehepticas: The dark wand known as the Finger of Nethehepticas is an accursed artifact of unknown power, with direct ties to the Abyssal Horror of its namesake.

  • On Nethehepticas Itself: Nethehepticas is an Abyssal Horror whose insidious schemes have troubled the people of Ember for centuries, and will continue to do so if allowed to go unchecked.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 16]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 16]] check are able to convince Mioroth of the veracity of their cause, and may elicit some additional help from the Sage (at the Gamemaster's discretion).

Once the characters have completed their exchange with Mioroth, he bids them farewell before his apparition dissipates with a fluttering of arcane light.

Our fates are one. Moons guide you; and may the waxing light of the Six lead us to brighter futures. I will call upon you yet again, when the time and need are right.

Concluding the Event

Milestone Point

Completion of this event rewards a Milestone Point.

Next Steps

After Tethra Shùl's defeat and her remains have been cleansed via destruction or consecration, the party must journey back to Skybrush to inform the locals of their efforts and tie up the loose ends of their investigation, as detailed in the events of [[/eventState brushWithDeathAftermath]].
Where Evil Lurks.soverview: The party finally reaches the Bleak Archive, a forgotten Shent repository where profane pre-Shattering artifacts have been interred for centuries untold. Here, they must survive the vault's hazards and defeat the wraithlike warlock known as Tethra Shùl, the perverse origin of the Bewilderment curse that afflicts Skybrush.
Where Evil Lurks.sexposition: If the legends told by Liestra Grann are true, this lonely place is the forgotten Shent vault known as The Bleak Archive, where Dereth Erekos found the accursed Varun relics. With any luck, the solution to the plight in Skybrush lurks somewhere inside.
Where Evil Lurks.ssummary: We explored a forgotten Shent vault northwest of Skybrush known as the Bleak Archive, where we encountered and defeated the wraithlike Varùn warlock known as Tethra Shùl.

The House on Lonely Hill.name: The House on Lonely Hill
The House on Lonely Hill.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is an exploration event that occurs on the region map and invites the characters to survey the home of a third suspect in the recent Skybrush murders.

This event can only occur after the [[/eventState brushWithDeathSkybrush1 gedronEvidence]] evidence has been acquired in the preceding event. In this event, the characters can:

  • Investigate home of the artist Gedron Tath who was implicated as a person of interest in the recent murders.

  • Witness Tath's horrific self-immolation during the onset of the ancient eldritch curse known as @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}.

  • Discover five macabre artworks illustrated by Gedron Tath that ominously depict the various murders in Skybrush.

  • Acquire of the accursed Varùn artifacts, potentially becoming afflicted by the curse itself.

Clues gained during the party's first trip to Skybrush should inevitably lead them a mile south from town to investigate the remote domicile of Gedron Tath (Chaotic Neutral, Arcturian Kivahr, he/him) — an eccentric illustrator and sculptor who purchased a cursed Varùn Ring from Liestra Grann. Here, they'll encounter more than they bargained for, and gather telling evidence about the grim forces motivating the situation in Skybrush.

Approaching the Homestead

While limited information can be gained from examining the exterior of Gedron Tath's home studio, this initial moment also serves to slow down the party's approach and nurture an air of suspense as they ponder what could be happening inside.

Inspecting the Mural

If the party takes a closer look at the mural that decorates the exterior wall, they can easily discern that it was painted by Gedron Tath himself — who apparently signs his last name upon his work using esoteric, stylized strokes.

Observant or knowledgeable characters may be able to discern more:

[[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] You're somewhat familiar with the artistic works of Gedron Tath, having seen one of his originals on display during your travels. The esoteric autograph on the mural is unmistakably Tath's signature.

[[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] Based on the faded tones of the pigments and the weathered erosion at the edges, you suspect this expressionistic mural was painted at least several months ago.

[[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] You recognize the expressionistic elements of the mural as depictions of Ember's six moons as well as the three Inner Realms of the Cosmos. Despite the abstruse, almost mythical nature of the imagery featured here, you can identify the creatures as various entities associated with positive themes of wisdom and protection.

Where the Moon Blossoms Grow

Characters with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] will readily notice scattered @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} blooming outside Tath's home.

Tath's Immolation

The party has arrived at Gedron Tath's isolated home studio just in time to witness his baleful metamorphosis into a @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendor} under the evil dominion of the wraith Tethra Shùl. However, in anticipation of his hideous change, Gedron Tath has decided to take his own life to spare himself a gruesome undying fate. Once the party's investigation of the exterior is complete and they begin to survey what's going on inside, read the following aloud:

As you draw nearer to the painted Arcturian edifice, you're able to discern someone inside while peeking through an open window. A hairless Kivahr male adorned in a loose paint-spattered tunic kneels on the floor. Facing away from you, this figure — who you assume to be Gedron Tath — appears to be fidgeting with something in his unseen hands. A low-burning candle flickers nearby.

After a brief moment, the man slowly turns his head to look at you, revealing an expression of abject fear upon his face. His skin is remarkably pale, and you can almost see him stifle a macabre smile as he gazes intensely in your direction.

The Kivahr holds the candle in a trembling grasp, and illuminated beneath its subtle glow you perceive the reflected sheen of some liquid that coats the artist like a veneer of oil. His smile lingers for a moment as he presses the candle to his chest — resulting in a sudden and horrible conflagration of flame and black smoke as the man immolates, burning himself alive in front of your very eyes.

You Are Too Late

The party has arrived in the very moment that Gedron Tath has taken his life, and is effectively powerless to stop him from burning alive. If they rush in to save the immolated artist, his unconscious form slumps to the ground in a dismal blaze.

Since Tath's body has already succumbed to the baleful transformation of @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}, no means of healing mundane nor magical will return him to consciousness. The characters were too late to save him, and all that remains is Tath's smoldering corpse, an ancient Rune-Marked Band worn like a bracelet on his left arm, and a studio full of curious and macabre artworks.

The Troublesome Trinket

The solitary remnant remaining on Tath's immolated corpse is a strange stone and metal bracelet worn upon the artist's left arm. This item is initially unidentified, but is the @UUID[Item.tft5aeUE51jyKoqX]{Rune-Marked Band} which was obtained in trade from Liestra Grann.

The Varùn Ring is not only a curious magic item, it is the party's most substantial evidence to date regarding what's actually happening in Skybrush. Naturally, the characters may be compelled to acquire and attune to the Ring — a process which will unavoidably afflict that character with @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}.

A Conversation with Tath's Corpse

Because Tath was able to take his life before the transformation into a Horrendor was complete, his charred remains are an eligible target for the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.I2LUSF5ogc7Bj62e]{Speak with Dead} spell magical methods of communication with the dead. If the party attempts to communicate with Gedron Tath in this way, the deceased artist is able to croak out a few pointed answers from the sooty confines of his burnt throat. Tath's corpse is able to relate aspects of the following information, should the characters ask suitably related questions:

Tath is a loner who generally kept to himself. He only journeyed into town for supplies or to peddle his art.

Kept to myself … only went to town for supplies or to sell pieces.

He had nothing to do with the deaths of Branos Erekos or Veera Hult, and knew Qory Hult by reputation only.

Nothing to do with the deaths. Knew Branos not. Cared for Veera.

The "inspiration" for the macabre paintings on display in the studio came to Tath in dreadful nightmares. These dreams portrayed an ill-omened alignment of the moons, alongside a doomed Skybrush and a mysterious otherworldly voice full of portent.

Saw it in dreams … the doom that comes … for me too now.

The dreams came to Tath after he started wearing the ancient Varùn Ring as a bracelet, which he purchased from Liestra Grann.

Started once I wore the ring. The giant's bauble. A pretty thing.

Tath killed himself to spare the other citizens of Skybrush from the dangers of his horrible transformation into a Horrendor — something he anticipated via the grim self-portrait in his studio.

I knew what was coming. Painted it. I chose a different path.

Body of Work

Once the literal and figurative smoke clears, the party can survey the interior of Gedron Tath's home studio for additional clues related to the incident at hand.

Tath's home also serves as his studio, and is decorated with an array of recent artworks of a macabre and disturbing nature. Painted in a surrealistic style, Tath's art depicts eerie scenes and images that apparently presaged the recent atrocities in Skybrush and foreshadow the encounters of quest events to come.

Five notably gruesome art pieces are on display here:

The Prisoner

A masculine figure clutches the bars of a jail cell. You recognize the face of the man as Qory Hult, whom you met in Skybrush, but his unhinged countenance is corpselike and hideous.

This portrait depicts Qory Hult whose affliction by the Bewilderment progresses even as the party investigates this very scene. It is clear to all characters that this depiction of Qory is far more horrific than the visage of the man you spoke to previously.

[[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck science 12]] The fresh tones of the pigments and the relative lack of dust on the parchment suggest these images are somewhat new compared to other artworks in the studio. Surely, this illustration can be no more than a week old.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: It appears Tath used his own blood for one of the pigments used in these paintings, which has dried to a dark shade of crimson-brown.

The Palanquin

A mid-forties Kiska woman languishes proudly atop a grotesque litter of humanoid bones, her finger curled around a trailing strand of sinew as if a practiced diversion.

This is a future image of Kel Kornan who is currently experiencing early onset of The Bewilderment.

If the party is seeking Kel on behalf of Kadrick Pond, a character with [[/skill insight 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill insight 13]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 13 passive]] recognizes the Kiska from the description you were given.

The Artist

You behold a portrait of a Kivahr with a sinister and rotted disposition taking over one half of his face. Notes surround the portrait scrawled in blood with maddened haste.

This is a self-portrait of Gedron Tath, the scrawled notes demonstrate the artist's rapid descent into lunacy and the intrusive thoughts of an unnamed "Master".

[[/language abyssal]] You recognize some of the lunatic scrawlings on the portrait as Abyssal script. These characters appear to refer to the aforementioned "Master" as an entity known as "The Night Terror".

The Conflagration

A diorama of a small cottage, its furniture in disarray and walls blacked by scorch marks and peeling. A slumped figure lies in the center of the room, horribly burned and surrounded by a mound of ash and dust.

The scene depicted in this portrait matches exactly your current vantage point of the home before you - including details you are certain would have been impossible to predict.

This painting is the result of Nethehepticas' dream that showed to Gedron Tath one of the possible paths which lay before him and ultimately the path which the artist chose to take.

The Archive

The final painting depoicts a set of double doors to some mysterious stone edifice. The entrance flanked by two statues of celestial hounds carved from moonstone. A pair of luminous eyes of a tenebrous entity loom ominously overhead, as if watching you approach.

This painting depicts the entrance to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CS82h91RP59553vr]{The Bleak Archive}. Gedron Tath has not visited this place himself, but was shown a vision of it by Nethehepticas, urging him to go there and join the other Horrendor in service to Tethra Shùl.

[[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] According to its craftsmanship, the double doors and the surrounding moonstone decoration appears to be ancient Shent or Varùn in origin.

[[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] The landscape surrounding the mysterious stone doors and their stone edifice is reminiscent of the neighboring Wedgelands.

Should the party take the paintings with them, the artworks may prove valuable as clues. However, relatively few citizens of Skybrush will respond to these perverse images with open minds.

Concluding the Event

Whatever the outcome of the party's encounter with Gedron Tath, the most reasonable course of action is a continuation of the investigation in Skybrush.

Next Steps

With Tath's artworks in hand, the party must travel back to town to further unravel the mystery of the trouble in Skybrush in [[/eventState brushWithDeathSkybrush2]].
The House on Lonely Hill.soverview: The party investigates the remote homestead of Gedron Tath, an eccentric artist whose macabre paintings have implicated him with the grim occurrences in Skybrush.
The House on Lonely Hill.sexposition:
You spy an isolated Arcturian homestead situated on a lonely hillside. This squat stone edifice is relatively unremarkable, aside from the intriguing presence of an expressionistic mural painted across its outer walls. Marked by strokes of faded black and white pigments, this mural — which wraps around the entire building — appears to depict the cosmos of Ember itself. Six moons hover within a field of stars, and abstract images of countless mythical creatures linger at the peripheries of what must be portrayals of the Inner Realms.

Although this place is quiet and pervaded by solitude, you notice a subtle flicker of lantern or candle light in one of the darkened windows.
The House on Lonely Hill.ssummary: We scouted the remote homestead of an eccentric painter named Gedron Tath for clues about the Skybrush murders. When we arrived, Tath took his own life in a horrible conflagration of lantern fire. His studio was also decorated with five macabre paintings, some of which curiously portray the recent incidents in Skybrush.

Loose Ends.name: Loose Ends
Loose Ends.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration event takes place in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} after the party's fateful encounter with Gedron Tath. In this event, the characters can:

  • Discover the transformation of Qory Hult into an undead Horrendor which happened while the party was away.

  • Investigate the home of Dereth Erekos and speak with his surviving family members, who are newly open to visitation.

  • Visit the home of Dereth's girlfriend Revelry Wyst, whose brusque father Hescott Wyst offers a few pieces of new information.

  • Get paid a visit by Revelry Wyst herself, who is eager to share her side of the story about Dereth's macabre predicament.

  • Visit the home of House Cevher's Kel Kornan, who is in the final days of her fight against the onset of The Bewilderment.

  • Deal with the passage of time in their absence, which may have allowed for additional exchanges of the accursed Varùn artifacts.

  • Follow a trail of evidence to track Dereth's westward path from town.

The party has several avenues of investigation. The most important of these are the aforementioned encounters with the Erekos family and Dereth's betrothed Revelry Wyst. Ultimately, your goal as the Gamemaster is to shepherd the party's investigation until they have the information they need to begin following Dereth's trail westward out of town.

Remaining Clues

As the party returns to Skybrush after visiting the home of Gedron Tath, they will have several clues to follow-up on:

  • The prisoner Qory Hult was depicted in baleful form in one of Gedron's paintings.

  • The party may be seeking Kel Kornan on behalf of Kadrick Pond or because of the subject of one of Gedron's paintings.

  • The party may wish to interrogate the family of Dereth Erekos, or his paramour Revelry Wyst.

  • Look for clues regarding the provenance of Varùn artifacts which seem to be a common thread.

Guiding the Investigation

As the party gets settled in Skybrush and takes on additional events and encounters, their various visits back to the treetop settlement are likely to be a bit open-ended. As GM, you may have to improvise a bit more than usual during this quest. Here are a few pointers to help keep you on track:

  • Allow the characters ample time to follow leads and investigate Skybrush in their own way, but be mindful of moments when the narrative stalls out due to confusion or dead ends. Don't be afraid to interject with one of the several NPCs at your disposal to keep things moving along; after all, Skybrush is their town and the party is just visiting.

  • Always keep track of where each of the 5 Varùn artifacts are at any given time. If you know where the artifacts are you can determine when, how, and how quickly The Bewilderment is spreading.

  • When in doubt regarding the sequence of events that preceded the party's arrival or the effects of the curse itself, consult the @UUID[.MyxkUsLNydK7zTBE]{Revealing the Mystery} and @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment} appendices for more details.

Offering Hints

If at any point during the investigation, the party seems stuck - request the players to roll a [[/check investigation 16]] or [[/check insight 16]] check. On a success, provide a hint framed from the perspective of something they realize or remember.

The Unholy Prisoner

Qory Hult died in his Blockhouse gaol cell while the party was away, and has just recently completed his baleful transformation into a Horrendor under the distant control of Tethra Shùl.

Where the Moon Blossoms Grow

Outside the Blockhouse, characters with a[[/skill perception 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check will notice a scattered growth of @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} gathered about the exterior.

Area Map - Arcturian Jail

This particular passage of play will benefit from use of the @UUID[Scene.emberArcturiJail]{Arcturian Jail} area map, enabling you to play out the combat encounter with @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr] at a tactical level. Since this Area Map occurs within the middle of an event, its usage is not automated and you should activate it yourself at the appropriate moment.

You enter the squat gaol of the Blockhouse to see Qory Holt leaning against the rear wall of his cell, hands splayed to either side. As if suddenly aware of your presence, the man twists his head unnaturally around — at an almost impossible angle — and smiles at you with the rictus visage of a pallid corpse.

@Embed[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr inline]

Qory Transformed

Qory Hult has become an undead @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendor} mere hours before the party's arrival, but his imprisonment has prevented him from causing too much harm.

If the party attempts to question the Qory, he ridicules them in [[/language common]] and [[/language abyssal]] from behind bars. His taunts include the following:

  • Descriptions of how he might wreak havoc in Skybrush after escaping his gaol cell.

  • A deranged account of the murder of his wife that landed him here in the first place.

  • Personal insults to the characters, including but not limited to their Flaws.

Characters who can understand [[/language abyssal]] or who can cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.4dSvfvTy2ZIJ3K4k]{Comprehend Languages} spell or that consume an @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.omniglotDecoctio] can make out a serious of cryptic phrases that Qory mutters beneath his breath:

The Bleak Seed grows within you.

You may sunder my flesh but you'll never escape the Bewildering Night.

The shadows of Ebbok Zhùr await.

Qory is imprisoned behind bars and cannot leave the cell, but he is not actively &Reference[Restrained]. A cunning or resourceful party should not have difficulty subduing him. A formal combat encounter is likely not necessary, but depending on the players' actions you may call for initiative rolls if desired.

Horrendor Tactics

If a combat encounter is required, Qory will gleefully @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.CFHyyTtMRhrwaJ51]{Multiattack} any character that gets within 5 feet of the bars and use @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.gldnENV6nrtpTlkH]{Cunning Escape} to disengage and retreat beyond reach.

If the characters are prudent enough to maintain a safe distance, Qory will assail them with @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.Vna5GyoBUJhBtV1f]{Gruesome Mockery} each round.

If a combat encounter is required, Qory will gleefully pummel any character that gets within 5 feet of the bars with unarmed attacks, and use his nature as a @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.skirmisher000000] to disengage and retreat beyond reach.

If the characters are prudent enough to maintain a safe distance, Qory will assail them with a steady stream of mockery, making use of @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.diversionist0000] to batter their Focus each round.

As one of the @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.restlessDead0000], Qory is difficult to permanently defeat.

Meeting the Erekoses

The family of both the victim Branos Erekos and the accused murderer Dereth Erekos have opened their doors for visitors while the party was away. Zereth and Demetria Erekos are somber and not overly welcoming of strangers, but they will accept the party into their home as long as they are not antagonistic.

Their home is a sullen one, marked by drab stillness and oppressive quietude. The only joy here is found in the brief tail wags of the Erekos family pet: a cat named "Tommen".

Where the Moon Blossoms Grow

Outside the Erekos house, characters with a[[/skill perception 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] check will notice a scattered growth of @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} gathered about the exterior.

Speaking with Mr. & Mrs. Erekos

Dereth's mother and father are stricken with grief, but are still able to answer a few questions about the young bard and his brother Branos.

  • They weren't present at the time of the incident.

  • The brothers, younger Dereth and older Branos, had a remarkably loving relationship until this tragic incident took place.

  • Dereth spent most of his free time writing songs for his girlfriend Revelry Wyst. In fact, he'd recently earned enough coin to purchase a new lute with which to sing his ballads.

    Unbeknownst to the Erekos family, Dereth purchased the new lute from the pawn broker Liestra Grann with his spoils from The Bleak Archive as described in @UUID[.MyxkUsLNydK7zTBE]{Revealing the Mystery}.

  • Dereth liked to write his songs while looking upon Skybrush from the hills nearby to the northwest. And music could be heard from his room nearly every day.

  • If the characters offer any form of assistance or consolation, Mr. & Mrs. Erekos invite the party to inspect Dereth's room for clues.

Speak with Animals

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.aL1F8fvYLtNzUbKu]{Speak with Animals} spell[[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.wildspeaker00000]] talent allows the party to communicate with Tommen the cat, who has one extra clue worth mentioning: Dereth cut his brother down with a strange stony blade before fleeing the Erekos home in a panic.

The Diary of Dereth Erekos

If the characters search Dereth's room while visiting the Erekos home, they'll find two major clues:

A dusty old lute sits discarded and neglected. It hasn't been played in weeks.

  • A successful[[/skill performance 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check identifies telltale clues that this was — at one time — a beloved possession. For Dereth to leave it behind by choice would be surprising (unless it's somehow no longer his favored instrument).

Near the bedside rests @UUID[Item.jlmAciSoBLtSdIaB]{Dereth's Journal} of song lyrics and diary entries. Any character who spends at least 10 minutes studying the journal reveals details concerning series of dreams in which Dereth encountered a dark, manipulative entity from a tenebrous nightmare realm.

  • A successful[[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]]] check understands that these dreams are similar to the types of premonitions that the artist Gedron Tath might have experienced. If a character has experienced one of these dreams themselves in @UUID[.O1u2YfjEcHhFRezW]{Night Terrors}, the check is made with @Advantage[2].

Meeting the Wysts

If the party visits the home of Dereth's girlfriend Revelry Wyst, they'll find the Wysts are very apprehensive after Dereth's act of violence and subsequent disappearance.

Speaking with Mr. Wyst

Revelry's father Hescott Wyst is reluctant to accept home visitors, and will only entertain inquiries from the most persuasive of characters.

  • One detail Hescott Wyst eventually parts with: a few nights before the murder, Dereth showed up to sing Revelry a new song with a shiny new lute and a bouquet of lambent flowers in hand. "Fancy flourishes for a pauper like the Erekos boy…"

If the characters entreat Hescott Wyst's professional services as an apothecary and inquire about the strange blue flowers that are growing about town, he relates the following:

  • These curious "Moon Blossoms" are new to Skybrush, and their novel properties are unknown.

  • Hescott is willing to study and identify the properties of one of the @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} over the course of an evening in exchange for 5 gold pieces. The party must come back a day later for results — during which time, the effects of The Bewilderment may progress.

A Visit from Revelry Wyst

If the party asks around town for signs of Dereth Erekos, they don't uncover many immediate clues; but their ambition eventually pays off when Revelry Wyst approaches the characters somewhere in public (such as The Roost, or near a public marketplace).

Revelry's Confession

Free from her father's overprotective scrutiny, Revelry is eager to share her side of the story.

  • According to the young muse, Dereth Erekos is the most kind-hearted soul she's ever met, and he couldn't possibly be responsible for the killings.

Any character whomakes a successful [[/skill persuasion 12]] or [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skillCheck persuasion 12]] or [[/skillCheck deception 14]] check can coerce Revelry into sharing a few more private details:

  • Dereth liked to write songs for her from the tranquil confines of a small hillside grotto west of Skybrush.

  • Although she's never had any reason to be skeptic of Dereth's behavior, Revelry does seem to harbor some suspicions about the new lute he'd been seen with. With all of their plans for the future on one hand — and Dereth's meager financial means on the other — the lute strikes her as a remarkably frivolous purchase.

The Return of Kel Kornan

Asking around town about a Kiska with the description of the subject of Tath's painting results in locals pointing the party in the direction of Kel Kornan, the stone broker.

If the party wasn't tasked with finding her directly via @UUID[.wUIrn2Jd1CksCRew]{Locating Kel Kornan}, discovery of the painting in Gedron Tath's studio and subsequent investigation about town may lead the party to the home of Kel Kornan, an experienced stone and timber broker for House Cevher.

Where the Moon Blossoms Grow

Outside Kel's home, characters with a[[/skill perception 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] will notice a scattered growth of @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} about the exterior.

The Verge of a Curse

Although she purchased a cursed @UUID[Item.OJRVuMrUlSAM3soe]{Rune-Marked Sash} from Liestra Grann, Kel simply hasn't succumbed to the full effects of The Bewilderment — yet. But it's only a matter of time.

  • If questioned about the murders in Skybrush, Kel is honestly ignorant; and it doesn't occur to her to voluntarily mention the Rune-Marked Sash or how she procured it.

  • Kel has never met Dereth Erekos, Qory Hult, or any of their kin; she simply lives in a different social strata than these "unfortunate young men."

Characters who succeed on a[[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check can confirm the Varùn origins of the vintage sash that Kel wears as a novel part of her everyday apparel. If this connection is made, Kel will explain how she purchased the rune-marked sash from the pawn broker Liestra Grann a few days prior.

Kel Kornan has been suffering from the invasive dreams of Nethehepticas for weeks. A successful [[/skill persuasion 15]] or [[/skill deception 15]] [[/skillCheck persuasion 15]] or [[/skillCheck deception 15]] convinces her to share more info with the party about this particular detail. Kel's fractured account of her past weeks suggest the onset of some kind of dementia.

A Job for House Cevher

If the party came to Skybrush on behalf of Kadrick Pond, Kel is in possession of the missing consignment, but she's oblivious to the lapse in time and her responsibilities — perverse side effects of her own dreams of Nethehepticas.

A Bewildering Scene

If the party members spend enough time in Kel Kornan's presence, the Confusion effects of The Bewilderment may occur before their very eyes. Roll a Wisdom saving throw for Kel using [[/gmroll 1d20 + 2 # Wisdom Saving Throw]]. On a result of 15 or less Kel becomes afflicted by @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.9hQXdMSmerkTsHDe]{Confusion}.

If the party members spend enough time in Kel Kornan's presence, the Confusion effects of @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment} will occur before their very eyes.

Enduring Evil

The Curse Abides

Each time the party ventures out of the Skybrush city limits and returns, someone in town falls under the sway of @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment} while they're gone. The effects of this curse will manifest in either confused murders or their own accidental suicides.

No matter the cause of their demise, these cursed citizens become @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendors} all the same); and as long as the party fails to reach Tethra Shùl's inner chamber within the Bleak Archive and destroy or consecrate her worldly remains, the malevolence of her curse endures.

Qory Hult is the first citizen of Skybrush to perish while the party is away. Additional points of contact with the accursed artifacts include the following:

  • @UUID[Item.tft5aeUE51jyKoqX] The party likely found this during their encounter with Gedron Tath. If they didn't take the ring, Mica Valaston will add it to the evidence locker in their office at the Blockhouse gaol.

  • @UUID[Item.w7jXkPu7MheM6bkw] Qory Hult's murder weapon in the Blockhouse gaol is likely the first artifact to change hands.

  • @UUID[Item.OJRVuMrUlSAM3soe] Currently in the possession of Kel Kornan, who is already cursed by the item.

  • @UUID[Item.s2rgATaIZi2879IM] Located in @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann's} pawn shop The Long Haul, this item is a prime target for petty theft by an unscrupulous citizen of Skybrush.

  • @UUID[Item.59gxtjjpznto4p2x] The party will find this accursed weapon during their forthcoming encounter with @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z]{Dereth Erekos} in [[/eventState brushWithDeathDereth]].

The second time the party returns to Skybrush after a jaunt outside of town, there are at least 2 additional outbreaks of The Bewilderment to contend with. The rate at which the curse continues to proliferate should be determined by the party's relative advancement and associated class levels.

Plot Armor

As the Gamemaster you should feel empowered to afflict any citizen of Skybrush with the deadly curse except for @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann} who is an important character in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100]{Ancient Paths} quest and also makes an important appearance later in [[/eventState brushWithDeathDereth]]. A narrative explanation for why Liestra does not succumb to the curse is that she does not have any sense of ownership over the Varùn artifacts and therefore is not succeptible to their effects.

Concluding the Event

After gathering enough clues from Skybrush and its residents, the characters must track the trail of @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z]{Dereth Erekos} from Skybrush westward into the valley.

Signara Attunement: Dereth Evidence

The first character to successfully deduce that the Moon Blossoms and the grotto west of Skybrush are the party's most valid leads advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 brushWithDeathSkybrush2Evidence]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome derethEvidence]]

Once the party has obtained sufficient evidence to resolve themselves to this plan, mark the "Dereth Evidence" outcome of the quest and read the following aloud:

Your investigations in Skybrush have proven fruitful, and evidence compels you to strike out for the southwestern perimeter of town in search of the trail left by Dereth. As you approach the perimeter of town, you begin notice a scattered trail of the luminous blue Moon Blossoms that winds its way towards the outskirts of the vale.

The party can continue exploring the valley west of Skybrush to discover additional evidence connected to the bard's trail.

Concluding the Event

With new clues in hand, the party must set out on the heels of Dereth Erekos to find the inspired mountainside grotto spoken of in his diary and by his betrothed, Revelry Wyst.

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

Following the path left by Dereth will lead the party to discover the [[/eventState brushWithDeathTrail]] event, or alternatively they may stumble upon Dereth's location directly in the [[/eventState brushWithDeathDereth]] event.
Loose Ends.soverview: The party returns to Skybrush after a trip away from the troubled settlement. Unbeknownst to the characters, the horrors of Tethra Shùl's curse have ravaged the town while they were away. It's time to gather more clues if they wish to track down the true culprit of these calamitous events.
Loose Ends.sexposition: Somehow, Skybrush seems even more desolate than when you left it. The sounds of local wildlife have gone woefully silent, and a sullen wind stirs through the pines. Unbeckoned, your mind evokes the image of Qory Hult's horrific face pressed between the bars of the Blockhouse Gaol.
Loose Ends.ssummary: We returned to Skybrush, where we gathered additional information about the bard Dereth Erekos and his girlfriend Revelry Wyst. Clues have compelled us to seek an inspired mountainside grotto somewhere west of town where Dereth wrote songs for his beloved.

The Bard's Trail.name: The Bard's Trail
The Bard's Trail.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is an exploration event that leads the party west and eventually northward from Skybrush on a hunt for @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z]{Dereth Erekos}, a young man wanted for the murder of his brother Branos. In this event, the characters can:

  • Follow a trail of lambent @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} that will eventually lead towards Dereth's current location: a small mountainside grotto to the northwest, marked by a loose circular gathering of ancient stones.

  • Encounter an interesting landmark along the way that points the party in the right direction: a scarecrow in an overgrown field that's been mangled by a haphazard blade.

The Mangled Scarecrow

The scarecrow that stands watch over this small overgrown field, located nearly two miles southwest of Skybrush, has recently been cut down by a large blade in what appears to be a random act of vandalism.

What the Characters Find

A closer inspection of the scarecrow indicates that it was haphazardly cut in half by a hefty blade of some kind. The straw innards are strewn about in disarray, and trinkets have been left behind — including a rusty iron helmet and a splintered wooden spear.

  • [[/knowledge forensics]] and [[/knowledge warfare]] characters notice that the strikes seem undisciplined as if driven by passion more than technique.

A character with [[/skill perception 15 passive]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] check allows characters to spot boot tracks that match Dereth's boots.

  • A successful [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check is required to ascertain that these tracks weave beyond the scarecrow and head up into the foothills of the mountains to the northwest. This check can be repeated once per character per short rest Rest.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge tracking]] have @Advantage[2] for this check.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party must continue exploring the valley north of Skybrush to locate Dereth's next stop in the [[/eventState brushWithDeathFlowers]] event to the northwest.

They may possibly miss that next clue and instead discover Dereth himself in the [[/eventState brushWithDeathDereth]] event further north.
The Bard's Trail.soverview: In search of the missing bard Dereth Erekos, the party follows a scattered trail of luminous Moon Blossoms into the valley west of Skybrush. Clues the party has collected point in the right direction, but they'll need to explore the surrounding hinterlands to find the precise location on their own. Along the way, they discover a scarecrow that has been suspiciously mangled by some unknown assailant.
The Bard's Trail.sexposition: Beyond the southwestern edge of town, you trod through an overgrown field, long-abandoned by whichever citizens of Skybrush have neglected it. The withered vines of sporadic gourds crunch beneath your feet as you spy a scarecrow among the dense growth of tall grass. This effigy — dressed up in the rags of an Ordani conscript — appears torn or cut down, and hangs from its splintered wooden stake like some wounded drunkard.
The Bard's Trail.ssummary: We followed the trail of Dereth Erekos into the hinterlands west of Skybrush where we discovered an overgrown field harboring potential clues — a scarecrow that had been recently defaced, and an adjoining set of tracks that continued to the northwest.

Delivered from Evil.name: Delivered from Evil
Delivered from Evil.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event serves as the conclusion for "A Brush with Death," and chronicles the party's return to Skybrush with news of their triumph and the hopeful dissipation of the terrible curse that afflicted the town. In this event, the characters can:

  • Speak with constable Mica Valaston about the culpability of Tethra Shùl's curse.

  • Speak with the surviving Erekos family and Revelry Wyst about what really happened to Dereth.

  • Interact with various citizens and businesses of Skybrush to put the townsfolk at ease and increase the standing of the party's reputation.

This event describes the "good" ending to this quest. If Tethra Shùl isn't defeated and her remains aren't consecrated or destroyed, the state of Skybrush as described in the Enduring Evil section of @UUID[JournalEntry.iBzd1B4Zp2dE7ddM.JournalEntryPage.sKrSRRNlbfJ4eonr]{Loose Ends} persists — eventually leading the town to terrible ruin.

Counsel for the Constable

Once they've destroyed or consecrated Tethra Shùl's remains, the party must return to Skybrush with an account of the events they experienced — lest the treetop hamlet continue to live in fear of The Bewilderment. The most important point of contact for this effort is constable Mica Valaston, who is the town's only hope for order amidst the chaos (aside from the characters themselves).

A Reward from Valaston

Mica Valaston is eager to hear a full account of the party's excursion to The Bleak Archive and what transpired there.

If the characters fail to present substantial evidence of their deeds, a successful [[/skill persuasion 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check is required to convince the constable of the veracity of their claims.

Should the party manage to present enough evidence to relieve the innocent citizens of Skybrush from further implication, Mica offers them with a small donation of[[/award 50gp]] [[/award 5gp]] from the town's public coffers.

Mica Valaston can also help facilitate the sale of property within town, including the recently vacated homes of Qory Hult and Valence, the Harrowed.

A Visit with Mr. & Mrs. Erekos

The party may wish to visit the grieving Erekos family to deliver news of their son's demise. If they do, Zereth & Demetria Erekos are eager to find some resolution to their open-ended sorrows.

Furthermore, Revelry Wyst has been spending more time with the Erekos family in recent days, and can be found grieving with them during this particular encounter.

A Family Bereaved

If the characters are delicate with the manner in which they share the news of Dereth's ultimate demise, the Erekos family is eager to offer them the following tokens of appreciation:

  • A dusty @UUID[Item.Pxu2HNJreTBnqI5w]

  • A family heirloom. Roll once on the @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets} table.

However, in the midst of credible rumors that have already started to circle about town, a successful [[/skill dec 14]] check is required to convince the Erekos family that Dereth had nothing to do with the curse that came to Skybrush.

Aura Attunement: Accept the Erekos Heirloom

If the party accepts the Erekos family's heirloom as part of their reward, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 brushWithDeathAftermathAccept]] at the conclusion of the event.

Akon Attunement: Refuse the Erekos Reward

If the party refuses the Erekos family's heirloom as part of their reward, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 brushWithDeathAftermathRefuse]] at the conclusion of the event.

A Village Indebted

The party may be able to put a large number of Skybrush townsfolk at ease by visiting The Roost to spread hasty word of their heroic exploits.

News for the Roost

As news of the party's victory at The Bleak Archive spreads throughout Skybrush, Mattock and the other patrons of The Roost are eager to celebrate with them. The characters drink and eat here for free for their first night back in town.

From here on out, the characters have advantage on any skill checks made for Downtime Activities at the Roost, including all Charisma (Performance) checks.

Luxarum Attunement: Local Notoriety

If the party members revel in their newfound notoriety with the locals of The Roost, each character who does so advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 brushWithDeathAftermathNotoriety]] at the conclusion of the event.

Orbis Attunement: Local Humility

Each character who humbly refuses the benefits of their newfound notoriety advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 brushWithDeathAftermathHumility]] at the conclusion of the event.

If the party managed to aid @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann} during the course of [[/eventState brushWithDeathDereth]], the characters may wish to visit her at The Long Haul for the barter and trade of errant artifacts.

In the Grann Scheme of Things

Liestra is extremely grateful for the party's assistance at the mountainside grotto, and is happy to offer them a 10% discount on goods purchased from her at The Long Haul. Additionally, she gifts them a complimentary @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potion of Healing}Their choice of @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingElixir000] or @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rallyingElixir00] during their first transaction of 50gp 5gp or more.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After the party brings word of their exploits at The Bleak Archive back to Skybrush, the events of "A Brush with Death" are concluded and the quest is complete.

If Kel Kornan has survived the ordeal in Skybrush, the party may report back to Kadrick Pond if they were tasked to locate her, receiving the payment negotiated upon in [[/eventState brushWithDeathOrdain]].

Related Quests

If the party is traveling with Ankarist on @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc100]{Ancient Paths}, he would recommend making Mythspire Observatory the next destination now that the situation in Skybrush is resolved.

@UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas} and the malign influence they exert over this region will appear later in the main quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr3].
Delivered from Evil.soverview: After defeating the wraithlike warlock Tethra Shùl and cleansing her worldly remains from The Bleak Archive, the party returns to Skybrush to settle the mystery for its troubled citizens once and for all.
Delivered from Evil.sexposition: The sullen silence that pervaded Skybrush since your arrival has been replaced by tranquil sounds of repose. Birdsong drifts through the twisted boughs of the settlement's gravelbark pines, and a wistful fluted melody floats upon the mountain wind. A feeling of hope has once again settled on this place, whose people no longer fear the bewildering dark.
Delivered from Evil.ssummary: We rid Skyrbush of the furtive evil that bewitched it from the dark confines of The Bleak Archive. With any luck, the curse known as The Bewilderment will no longer trouble the Arctus Plateau and its people.

Revealing the Mystery.name: Revealing the Mystery
Revealing the Mystery.text:
Recent History

One week ago…

An enterprising young bard named Dereth Erekos, eager to win the heart of his beloved Revelry Wyst (and the approval of her family), ventured deep into the hills northwest of Skybrush in search of rare Shent relics that might turn his financial tides. Dereth's heedless quest for fortune and glory led him to plunder a forgotten Shent vault known as The Bleak Archive — where the wraithlike apparition of an evil Varùn warlock named Tethra Shùl has lurked for centuries untold.
