And curiously, the young bard was lured to this place by a recurrence of strange dreams and a trail of luminous blue flowers that lined his inconspicuous pathway into the lore-haunted hinterlands.

A frightened and astounded Dereth absconded with a handful of 5 relics from the tomb's antechamber, each of them cursed by the Varùn warlock's enduring betrayal. When he returned to Skybrush — newfound fortune and a bouquet of Moon Blossoms in hand — Dereth unwittingly brought doom and undeath along with him.

Any humanoid who claims and possesses one of these 5 stolen Varùn treasures becomes afflicted with a loathsome curse known as @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment}, which drives them mad before killing them outright. After death, the unfortunate victim of the curse becomes and undead creature known as a @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendor}, and serves as an immortal minion to Tethra Shùl and her otherworldly patron — the Abyssal Horror known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas}.

The citizens of Skybrush who've already come into contact with the accursed Varùn relics find themselves the targets of a woeful fate. Meanwhile, the strange moon blossoms bloom wherever the curse has taken hold. Perhaps a group of heroes will arrive in time to help the harrowed innocents of Skybrush survive…

Tracking the Curse

The first time the party arrives in Skybrush, @UUID[.jw0mOUcqhJPRajUY]{The Bewilderment} has already taken hold. There are 4 initial victims of the curse:

  • @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z]{Dereth Erekos}, who killed his brother Branos during a moment of magical confusion. Dereth fled the scene of the crime and currently presides over the mountainside grotto northwest of Skybrush where the events of @UUID[.nhl7heVSpb4FphFW]{The Abandoned Lute} take place. Dereth has fully transformed into a Horrendor.

  • Qory Hult, who killed his wife during a moment of magical confusion before getting arrested by constable Mica Valaston. Qory is currently locked up in the Blockhouse Gaol in town, and is in the process of becoming a Horrendor. The party should encounter Qory sometime during @UUID[.nYENxoxsgZ78PDwc]{The Situation in Skybrush}.

  • Gedron Tath, who lives a solitary life at his remote home studio, located one mile south of Skybrush. Gedron is cursed but has yet to become involved in a violent accident. His death via self-immolation will occur just as the party arrives at his home to experience the events of @UUID[.oohsyHFttpyI8Cju]{The House on Lonely Hill}.

  • Kel Kornan, who has retreated from her life of local commerce to hide away as The Bewilderment takes hold of her mind. The party won't encounter Kel Kornan until their second visit to Skybrush (after they meet Gedron Tath), during @UUID[JournalEntry.iBzd1B4Zp2dE7ddM.JournalEntryPage.sKrSRRNlbfJ4eonr]{Loose Ends}.

Each time the party ventures out of the Skybrush city limits and returns, someone in town falls under the sway of The Bewilderment while they're gone — and has likewise accomplished either a confused murder or their own accidental suicide (perhaps by falling from one of the settlement's treetop catwalks).

No matter the cause of their demise, these cursed citizens become Horrendors all the same); and as long as the party fails to reach Tethra Shùl's inner chamber within the Bleak Archive and destroy or consecrate her worldly remains, the malevolence of her curse endures.

Qory Hult is the first citizen of Skybrush to perish while the party is away. Additional points of contact with the accursed artifacts include the following:

  • @UUID[Item.tft5aeUE51jyKoqX]{Rune-Marked Band} The party likely found this during their encounter with Gedron Tath. If they don't take the ring, Mica Valaston will add it to the evidence locker in their office at the Blockhouse gaol.

  • @UUID[Item.w7jXkPu7MheM6bkw]{Rune-Marked Arrowhead} Qory Hult's murder weapon in the Blockhouse gaol is likely the first artifact to change hands.

  • @UUID[Item.OJRVuMrUlSAM3soe]{Rune-Marked Sash} Currently in the possession of Kel Kornan, who is also cursed by the item.

  • @UUID[Item.s2rgATaIZi2879IM]{Rune-Marked Vial} Located in @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann's} pawn shop The Long Haul, this item is a prime target for petty theft by an unscrupulous citizen of Skybrush.

  • @UUID[Item.59gxtjjpznto4p2x]{Rune-Marked Knife} The party will find this accursed weapon during their forthcoming encounter with Dereth Erekos in @UUID[.nhl7heVSpb4FphFW]{The Abandoned Lute}.

The second time the party returns to Skybrush after a jaunt outside of town, there are at least 2 additional outbreaks of The Bewilderment to contend with. The rate at which the curse continues to proliferate should be determined by the party's relative advancement and associated class levels.

Where the Moon Blossoms Grow

Beds of strange flowers blossom wherever someone has died after becoming afflicted by The Bewilderment. These @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} resemble small anemones and radiate a dim light at night. Few people have noticed the coincidence, but locals remain suspicious of the curious lambent buds nonetheless.

Once the party notices this concurrence, spotting the lambent flowers becomes easier for them, and is a definitive clue for locating the secluded tomb of Tethra Shùl in the Skybrush hinterlands.

Locating Kel Kornan.name: Locating Kel Kornan
Locating Kel Kornan.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is a social event that occurs on the region map somewhere in Ordain. This event steers the party towards the remote treetop village of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} which has mysteriously fallen prey to an evil curse. In this event, the characters can:

  • Meet Kadrick Pond of House Cevher, who hires the party to investigate a disappearance in Skybrush.

  • Learn about the missing individual, Kel Kornan and gather limited information about Skybrush.

A Job for House Cevher

While traversing the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.D0AAT8TNsytqy7Hm]{Quarry Gate} district in Ordain, the party is approached by Kadrick Pond (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him), a delegate of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{House Cehver}, with a mission most important.

The gentleman coughs slightly and inclines his head in your direction, seemingly keen to discuss business.

Well met. I am Kadrick Pond, of House Cevher. Perhaps you've heard of me? Nevertheless, let's put the small talk aside…

Your own reputations precede you, and Cevher is in need of some rather clandestine reconnaissance services. A modest reward and fine standing with the Trading House await you if both time and interest are available for this task.

Shall we discuss the matter further, with proper discretion?

Kadrick Pond crosses his arms in pragmatic anticipation, obviously awaiting your word.

Speaking with Kadrick Pond

After his initial speech, Kadrick Pond awaits a response from the characters. And while he keeps House Cevher trade secrets rather close to the vest, he's happy to answer most questions the party might have about the job at hand. He makes the following details readily available:

  • The Trading House has lost contact with one of their most seasoned hires: an experienced stone and timber broker named Kel Kornan. Kornan has served House Cevher from her home in Skybrush for years.

  • House Cevher has a wide array of investors that depend on timely transactions and the prompt exchange of goods, and Kel's absence of communication has grown troubling for the Cevher bookkeepers.

  • Located several miles northwest of Ordain, Skybrush is well known for its precious stone quarries; but the frontier town also has a reputation for rare artifacts culled from the timeworn ruins of the Varùn giants nearby.

  • House Cevher is willing to pay the party a modest[[/award 100gp]] [[/award 10gp]] if they're able to locate Kel Kornan and provide a report of her condition. If the characters take up this job and fail to deliver information back to House Cevher in Ordain, their reputation with the Trading House may be compromised.

  • A successful [[/skill persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check or a character with [[/knowledge trade]] will convince Kadrick Pond to contribute an additional [[/award 50gp each]] [[/award 5gp each]] from the House Cevher coffers as payment.

A successful [[/skill insight 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] check provides characters with some understanding about Kadrick Pond's intentions. He seems to trust the party's ability to carry out this recon job; and while there is a measure of importance to the mission, Pond doesn't seem to consider Kornan's disappearance a world-changing event.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: You can tell Kadrick Pond is used to keeping secrets from others, and there's no short supply of them here. But you don't feel any unsettling intentions from him aside from a certain fear the unknown; and Kornan's disappearance seems more important than he leads on.

The characters can ask around the city for information about Kel Kornan and Skybrush, but aside from basic details about the distant settlement, available information is scarce:

Gathering Information

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 15]] check is able to gather additional basic details about town regarding @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} and its most influential residents.

Concluding the Event

Once the characters have gathered the desired amount of information from Kadrick Pond or Ordain at large, they are ready to venture forth. The party's reputation with House Cevher now depends on whether or not they eventually deliver information about Kel Kornan's whereabouts. The must travel to the settlement directly to learn more.

Next Steps

The party can begin that investigation when they reach Skybrush themselves, in the [[/eventState brushWithDeathSkybrush1]] event.
Locating Kel Kornan.soverview: The party is discreetly tasked by Trading House Cevher to find out what happened to one of their most experienced brokers, a citizen of Skybrush named Kel Kornan who's mysteriously lost contact.
Locating Kel Kornan.sexposition: A gentle hand taps you on the shoulder as you make your way through Quarry Gate's cluttered cobblestone streets. You turn to see an apprehensive fellow patiently lingering behind you, clad in the austere fineries of an Ordani businessman. If the emblem on his cloak is any indication, this anxious gentleman is a member of Trading House Cevher.
Locating Kel Kornan.ssummary: We were hired by Kadrick Pond of House Cevher to find out what happened to one of their most experienced brokers, a citizen of Skybrush named Kel Kornan who's mysteriously lost contact with the esteemed Trading House.

Night Terrors.name: Night Terrors
Night Terrors.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event which occurs anywhere in the world and is played on the region map reinforces the mysterious curse affecting the town of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} and its inhabitants.

  • This event only occurs after the party has visited Skybrush.

  • Experience one of four random dreams riddled with nightmarish portents and visions of doom.

  • Uncover thinly-veiled allusions to Skybrush in these dreams, including vague details about a few of the town's inhabitants.

The Stuff Dreams Are Made Of

During a Long Rest Rest, one or more unsuspecting party members are beset by a strange and supernatural nightmare. This surrealistic jaunt is actually a remote manifestation of the psychic malevolence of an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nChUneUkEF2XBgxc]{Abyssal Horror} known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas}, who slumbers in a forgotten tomb somewhere in the Wedgelands.

The existence of Nethehepticas is entirely unknown; these nightmares are merely the first signs of a gradual awakening that might lead to the Horror's return. Unbeknownst to both the party and the citizens of Skybrush, the awakening presence of Nethehepticas is responsible for the outbreak of a great many undead manifestations in the region.

Whom Doth Dream?

The character with the highest [[/check charisma 0 passive]] score [[/skillCheck awareness 0 passive]] skill is the first to experience the nightmare. During further long rests to come — this event may recur — each time being experienced by a different party member in descending order.

A Solitary Experience?

Consider whether you wish to take the affected player aside and convey the material of the dream to them in private. This is not required, but can produce interesting roleplay moments.

Characters will naturally be confused by their nightmarish experiences, and may attempt to seek answers. A few of these details may be closer at hand than they realize, however vague they might seem.

Roll on the table below to determine which nightmare the character experiences.

@Embed[RollTable.Vl44RuVdUgscbv2r inline rollable=true]

1. The Crawling Catacomb

Torchlight kept you safe as you wandered the surreal subterranean landscape of some shadow-haunted catacomb, lined with endless ossuaries and scuttling darkness. The skulls of countless skeletons there seemed to glare at you with ill intent, yet the allure of some unknown treasure kept pushing you further and further into the shaded corners of this macabre and meandering place. The sinister whispering of some evil voice taunted you as you navigated the winding corridors, and the last thing you remember before waking is the gaze of two luminous crimson eyes and the rank smell of sepulcher rot.

Analyzing the Nightmare

[[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] The surreal expanse of the subterranean landscape was adorned with telltale signs and symbols of illusion and divination magic. This nightmare felt more vivid than any dream you've ever experienced.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: You also recall the vile signs of otherworldly eldritch magic lurking among those tenebrous dead-end halls, in both the menacing taunts of the skeletons and the baubles they clutched in their bony hands.

[[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] You can feel in your very soul that this was no mere dream, and that the places depicted in that nightmare landscape are somehow real. You're inspired to seek this place out.

  • Result of 19+ Critical Success The dream feels to you like a warning on some level as much as it may be an overt call-to-action.

[[/skill history 15]] or [[/skill religion 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] The burial rites in the dream appeared archaic and old-fashioned, and resembled certain consecration rites performed by the disciples of a legendary Shent sage known as Heroth, the Harrow-Hearted.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success: In addition to his arcane prowess, Heroth was known to be a war priest of the Elder God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets}, and stood proudly and successfully against many Abyssal incursions of the ancient past. This proximity to the Abyss came with rumors about Heroth's corruption — rumors staunchly denied by his disciples and allies.

[[/culture emberKithil]] You recognize the architecture of this place shares common elements with centuries-old Shent designs.

[[/language abyssal]] Although you can't make out very many specifics, you can identify some of the dark, foreboding speech from the dream to be Abyssal in origin. One phrase in particular stands out amidst the noise:

Away to Ebbok Zhùr.

2. The Ruined Village

You dreamt of climbing an impossibly tall tree in a mountaintop forest. The bark scraped the flesh of your hands raw as if it was petrified stone. Perched high above, you looked down upon the rocky ruins of some ancient village — its crumbling foundations splayed out in the shape of a gruesome humanoid skull. An impossibly sinister voice in the deepest baritone rang through your ears as you struggled to hold on for dear life; the words, while unclear, were remarkably menacing.

Analyzing the Nightmare

[[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] In addition to the central skull shape, some of the ruins below you were arranged into images that resembled the arcane symbols for illusion and divination magic. This nightmare was more vivid than any dream you've ever experienced.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: You vaguely remember the repugnant signs of otherworldly eldritch magic scrawled upon the massive tree you climbed.

[[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] You can feel in your very soul that this was no mere dream, and that the places depicted in that nightmare landscape are somehow real. You're inspired to seek this place out.

  • Result of 19+ Critical Success: The dream feels to you like a warning on some level as much as it may be an overt call-to-action.

[[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] You associate the imagery of the mountainside treetop village with a storied Rustvar Valley settlement known as Skybrush, which is indicated as a point of interest on the region map. You're familiar with Skybrush and its role in Arctus Plateau commerce as a source of gravelbark pine and rare giantkin artifacts of the ancient Shent and Varùn.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: You recognize a phrase from the sinister whispering: "Ebbok Zhùr", which you know to be a Shent landmark of some kind.

[[/culture emberKithil]] The peculiar alignment of the moons reminds you of an ancient fable about an ill-fated Keth who became obsessed with a Giant's wardrobe.

[[/language abyssal]] Although you can't make out very many specifics, you can identify some of the dark, foreboding speech from the dream to be Abyssal in origin. One phrase in particular stands out amidst the noise:

The Night Terror beckons the brave.

3. The Giant's Footsteps

The silhouette of some shade-haunted giant ambled on the horizon, and you felt compelled to follow. Yet, no matter how fast you ran, you couldn't keep pace with the plodding giant, whose massive strides carried you both to a mountainside forest at the edge of the world. Eventually, you caught up with your mysterious quarry; and as the giant turned to face you, its expression was no more than a pitch black nothingness. A damnable voice whispered from within, muttering unspeakable truths in an otherworldly tongue.

Analyzing the Nightmare

[[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]]You recall the giant's use of arcane sigils and somatic choreography, recognizing elements of both illusion and divination magic. This nightmare was more vivid than any dream you've ever experienced.

  • Result of 18+: You also recognize the loathsome signs of otherworldly eldritch magic in some of the nightmare's imagery that followed in the giant's wake.

[[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] You can feel in your very soul that this was no mere dream, and that the places depicted in that nightmare landscape are somehow real. You're inspired to seek this place out.

  • Result of 19+: The dream feels to you like a warning on some level as much as it may be an overt call-to-action.

[[/culture emberKithil]] The peculiar alignment of the moons reminds you of an ancient fable about an ill-fated Keth who became obsessed with a Giant's wardrobe.

[[/skill history 17]] [[/skillCheck society 17]] You recognize the Giant from the dream as one of the ancient progenitors of modern Giants and their kin.

[[/language abyssal]] Although you can't make out very many specifics, you can identify some of the dark, foreboding speech from the dream to be Abyssal in origin. One phrase in particular stands out amidst the noise:

The Sleeper walks in Skybrush.

4. The Cerulean Bloom

You recall endless hillsides of luminous blue flowers that resembled small anemones. Their pale cerulean glow cast a pall on everything around you, including the faces of dozens of nameless commoners who seemed to appear from nowhere. As you beheld their forlorn expressions, each countenance transformed into a grim specter of skeletal rot. Doomed whispers of doleful fates crawled forth from their hollow mouths, alongside a cryptic utterance like the voice of the netherworld itself.

Analyzing the Nightmare

[[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] The flowers seemed to grow in patterns that unmistakably resembled the symbols for both illusion and divination magic. This nightmare was more vivid than any dream you've ever experienced.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: You also recognize the loathsome signs of otherworldly eldritch magic in some of the nightmare's imagery, from the sight of spectral undead to the sound of cosmic incantation.

[[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] You recognize the lambent blue anemones as @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms}, which are native to certain areas where the magical leylines of Ember's moons run deep.

[[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 14]] You can feel in your very soul that this was no mere dream, and that the places depicted in that nightmare landscape are somehow real. You're inspired to seek this place out.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The dream feels to you like a warning on some level as much as it may be an overt call-to-action.

[[/culture emberKithil]] The peculiar alignment of the moons reminds you of an ancient fable about an ill-fated Keth who became obsessed with a Giant's wardrobe.

[[/language abyssal]] Although you can't make out very many specifics, you can identify some of the dark, foreboding speech from the dream to be Abyssal in origin. One phrase in particular stands out amidst the noise:

The Bleak Seed has been sewn.

Concluding the Event

The lack of finite information should compel the party to seek additional details about the place featured in the recurring nightmares, taking them closer and closer to Skybrush. Precisely how and where they find this information is up to them.

With the rest of the Arctus Plateau at their disposal, it's only a matter of time before the characters are able to identify the location of their nightmare dreamscape.

Next Steps

This event may recur when the party takes a long rest again. Continue repeating this event until each party member has experienced one of the dreams.

The clues in these dreams may draw the party to Skybrush where they will encounter [[/eventState brushWithDeathSkybrush1]].

The dreams will end once Tethra Shùl is defeated in [[/eventState brushWithDeathArchives]] and their presence is cleansed.
Night Terrors.soverview: One or more of the party members experiences the surreal events of a particularly troubling nightmare. This unsettling dream depicts morose imagery, featuring a mountainside treetop town and a mysterious, loathsome evil lurking among its rural denizens.
Night Terrors.sexposition:
You surrender to the curative unconsciousness of a much-needed long rest, although this particular slumber is far from restful for one of you. Instead of tranquility and relief, this interlude brings calamity and strife as you whittle away eight treacherously somnolent hours.

Visions of a treetop mountainside village inhabited by spectral citizens linger at the edge of your memory, along with a curious and foreboding alignment of the moons. Your mind races to remember the fevered chaos that brought you to wakefulness…
Night Terrors.ssummary: One of us experienced a rather fearful dream about a doomed mountainside village haunted by a strange evil. Perhaps there's more to this nightmarish story than meets the eye.

The Ballad of Dereth Erekos.name: The Ballad of Dereth Erekos
The Ballad of Dereth Erekos.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event which occurs on the region map can happen in any settlement or town and introduces the party to the remote treetop village of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush}, which has mysteriously fallen prey to an evil curse. In this event, the characters can:

  • Hear a mysterious song from Larka Hex,which tells the story of a star-crossed bard named @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z]{Dereth Erekos} and the doom that came to his village.

  • Gather limited information from Larka about Skybrush and its inhabitants.

A Song of Skybrush

Larka Hex (Neutral Good, Arcturian Signborn, she/her) is a silver-tongued Arcturian bard whose catalogue of tall tales from Signara have helped form the basis of countless ballads. Larka travels the Arctus Plateau looking for opportunities to exchange stories and compose new songs. In this very moment, while the characters are in attendance, a familiar tune that Larka plays is interrupted by a strange psychic event.

Larka begins singing with haunted detachment, as if the music she plays is not her own, and her despondent words weave a tale of sorrow…

In Skybrush, where the moon blossoms grow
and the wind in the mountains blows cold,
dreams a girl of her lover so 'lone,
of the bard who awaits to atone.

No honeyed words save him this day,
whose brother himself did he slay;
and reason may ne’er find a way
for Skybrush to weather the fray.

Oh Dereth, young Dereth, wherever you roam
Lurks the ghost of your brother,
where the moon blossoms grow.

As the last chords of the sullen melody refrain, Larka appears bewildered and lost.

After singing absentmindedly of Skybrush and the doomed saga of Dereth Erekos, Larka is willing to engage with the characters, however befuddled she may be.

Speaking with Larka Hex

Larka has no memory of having played the new song, let alone having written it. It's as if she received the song directly from some unknown transmitter and manifested it into the physical world. After a few moments of rest, she's back to normal.

Larka can offer the characters the following information:

  • She's never heard the name "Dereth", but is somewhat familiar with the "moon blossoms" that grow among the Skybrush hinterlands. In fact, she's never actually been to Skybrush herself.

  • Charming ghost stories abound throughout the Arctus Plateau, but this tale of a bard who killed his own brother is new to her.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] check allows characters to get a good read on Larka's reaction to this predicament. She seems a bit more confused than anything, having no recollection of the song or having played it. If the characters are already familiar to her, she is welcoming; on the other hand, she may be somewhat baffled by the concern of relative strangers.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: You can sense a fear behind Larka's eyes that even she seems unaware of, as if strange and unseen forces are pulling the strings. This ignorance suggests an innocence to Larka's involvement in this beguiling occurrance.

Larka's absent-minded song recurs once each day at a random time until the characters decide to investigate Skybrush for themselves.

Concluding the Event

With the location of Skybrush newly indicated on their map, the party can travel there to investigate the sullen story of Dereth Erekos and whether or not it has any truthful merit.

Next Steps

This quest begins in earnest when the party arrives at Skybrush themselves, in the [[/eventState brushWithDeathSkybrush1]] event.
The Ballad of Dereth Erekos.soverview: Motivated by strange and unseen magic, the minstrel Larka Hex begins singing a curious, forlorn tune about a doomed bard in a treetop village called Skybrush. The party plays witness to this out-of-body experience and learns the sullen tale of young Dereth Erekos.
The Ballad of Dereth Erekos.sexposition: The mood shifts at the behest of a sullen song that slowly meets your ears. The Signborn minstrel Larka Hex appears to have transitioned from the lively traditional tune she was playing to a forlorn melody in a minor key.
The Ballad of Dereth Erekos.ssummary: Larka Hex began playing a strange, forlorn tune about a doomed bard in a treetop village called Skybrush. It's as she had an out-of-body experience, and this music she played was not her own.

The Bewilderment.name: The Bewilderment
The Bewilderment.text:
Characters who take ownership of one of the Rune-Marked Varùn Artifacts from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CS82h91RP59553vr]{The Bleak Archive} become cursed by The Bewilderment.

The cursed nature of these items is revealed only when an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} spell is cast on them. Exerting a distinct feeling of ownership towards a Rune-Marked item immediately curses you until you are targeted by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.XZhdgVK3cLoxNCQl]{Remove Curse} spell or similar magic; removing the Rune-Marked item from your possession fails to end the curse.

The cursed nature of these items is revealed only when scrutinized with [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.recognizespellcr]]. Exerting a distinct feeling of ownership towards a Rune-Marked item immediately curses you until the curse is removed with a [[/counterspell rune=control gesture=aspect inflection=negate dc=16]]. Removing the Rune-Marked item from your possession fails to end the curse.

While you are cursed by the Rune-Marked item, you suffer from the confusing effects of The Bewilderment and experience the recurring @UUID[.O1u2YfjEcHhFRezW]{Night Terrors} of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VXFOxdzzDefX5dQ8]{Nethehepticas}.

Taking Ownership & Becoming Cursed

The triggering condition for this curse is unusual. Touch, inspection, or other cursory exchanges with an afflicted artifact will not trigger it, but the curse immediately comes into effect as soon as a character views such an item as belonging to them.

For example, @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann} is surprisingly unaffected because the antiquarian has no wish to possess the artifacts, only to sell them to a collector. It is Liestra's unfortunate customers who become inevitably afflicted by The Bewilderment.

The Bewilderment

While cursed, at the start of each hour the character must make a [[/save wisdom 16]] saving throw or become affected by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.9hQXdMSmerkTsHDe]{Confusion} spell for 10 minutes.

Additionally, each morning after the character becomes cursed, they must make another [[/save wisdom 16]] saving throw. Upon failing this saving throw for the third time, that character will inevitably die of terrifying shock [[/gmroll 1d12 # Hours]] hours later. Immediately upon their death, the character becomes a @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendor} controlled by the Gamemaster on behalf of @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd]{Tethra Shùl} or their otherworldly master Nethehepticas.

While Cursed, at the start of each hour the character faces [[/hazard 6 willpower morale psychic]]{Creeping Confusion}, and if they do not pass the hazard they enter a brief state of delusion.

While in this state of delusion, the character may:

  • Forget the names of friends and allies, or important details of quest events

  • Set out walking in a direction other than the one they intend to move

  • Become dissociated, staring into space and no longer moving until someone jostles them out of their reverie

  • Trail off in the middle of sentences, forgetting that they had been speaking

  • Begin humming a tune the party might recognize as @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo.JournalEntryPage.Ea9QwROqcr4kJoLK]{The Ballad of Dereth Erekos}

Additionally, each time the bearer of this curse awake from a Rest they must face [[/hazard 4 willpower morale severe]]{Lost Dreams}. The third time this hazard deals damage, that character will inevitably die of terrifying shock [[/gmroll 1d12 # Hours]] hours later. Immediately upon their death, the character becomes a @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendor} controlled by the Gamemaster on behalf of @UUID[Actor.fzbl7UQ5W82mFnbd]{Tethra Shùl} or their otherworldly master Nethehepticas.

Once cursed, this curse may only be removed with a [[/counterspell rune=control gesture=aspect inflection=negate dc=16]].

The Abandoned Lute.name: The Abandoned Lute
The Abandoned Lute.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is an exploration and combat event that leads the party even further away from Skybrush on their hunt for @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z]{Dereth Erekos}.

In this event, the characters can:

  • Reach the end of the trail of lambent @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} that lead towards Dereth's current location: a small mountainside grotto, marked by a loose circular gathering of ancient stones, where the characters will find Dereth's broken and abandoned lute.

  • Survive a fateful encounter with Dereth himself, who has transformed into an undead @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr]{Horrendor} under the control of the wraithlike warlock Tethra Shùl.

  • Discover and aid the injured pawn broker @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann}, who has narrowly survived her own encounter with Dereth after woefully attempting to supersede the party during their manhunt.

A Discarded Instrument

The final stop along the bard's trail into the hinterlands is a small mountainside grotto marked by a loosely circular gathering of ancient stones. Here, two miles northwest of Skybrush, the party finds Dereth's cast-aside lute.

A bright pinpoint of reflected light catches your eye. Something small and shiny among the rocks seems to be out of place here, and compels you to investigate further. Drawing near, you see the fractured remains of what must have been a lacquered instrument made of fine hardwood.

What the Characters Find

The instrument appears to be a lute, and was obviously quite shiny and new before it was recently bashed upon the nearby rocks.

[[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] The broken instrument matches the description of Dereth's lute as indicated by Hescott Wyst and @UUID[Item.jlmAciSoBLtSdIaB]{Dereth's Journal}.

A successful [[/skill survival 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] check allows the characters to locate Dereth's boot prints once more, and the long earthen groove of a heavy sword tip being dragged along behind them to the northwest.

Mountainside Grotto

Intermittent growths of Moon Blossoms lead you towards the foothills, where you discover a grotto marked by a bed of these lambent cerulean anemones and a circular arrangement of ancient stones. These short menhirs appear to be marked with archaic carvings, and jut out from the rocky landscape like an enormous hand reaching up from the rugged earth.

Upon investigating the grotto, the party is attacked by @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z]{Dereth Erekos} — who is no longer human but is now a particularly formidable horrendor who wields the @UUID[Item.59gxtjjpznto4p2x]{Rune-Marked Knife} as if it were a broadsword.

@Embed[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z inline]

Dereth's Tactics

Dereth will attempt to take the party by surprise, attempting to use stealth to take the party unawares. Failing that, Dereth will attempt to draw one of the characters closer to him by taking advantage of their curiosity — promising answers to the mystery of Branos' murder.

Once in range, Dereth will attack gleefully and without remorse using a combination of @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z.Item.CFHyyTtMRhrwaJ51]{Multiattack}, @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z.Item.nEQn0MrUk3y9quJf]{Gruesome Mockery}, and @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z.Item.ninUf05hSjEl7faH]{Cunning Escape}.

Dereth attacks to the death and will not answer any questions the party asks except with misderection, mockery, or malice. Note that @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z.Item.qOy6o1qXTKOkYCXQ]{Undeathly Fortitude} makes Dereth exceptionally difficult to fully defeat.

Once in range, Dereth will attack gleefully and without remorse using a combination of repeated focused attacks and @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.diversionist0000] to mock the party and deprive them of Focus. Dereth will rely on his abilities as a @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.skirmisher000000] to disengage and retreat beyond reach.

Dereth fights to the death and will not answer any questions the party asks except with misderection, mockery, or malice. Note that @UUID[Actor.e67w5IOBScYtJKXr.Item.restlessDead0000] makes Dereth difficult to fully defeat.

When the Smoke Clears

After the party defeats Dereth in combat, they may loot his body for clues. These include:

  • The @UUID[Item.59gxtjjpznto4p2x]{Rune-Marked Knife}, which is at least the 3rd Varùn artifact the characters have encountered since visiting Skybrush.

  • A leather pouch containing [[/award 250gp]] [[/award 25gp]].

  • If the characters haven't already found @UUID[Item.jlmAciSoBLtSdIaB]{Dereth's Journal}, they find it here.

A Grann Entrance

Once the party has had ample time to survey the area in the aftermath of their encounter with Dereth Erekos, they are approached by @UUID[Actor.BJ0TzuQIdpqKTm5R]{Liestra Grann}, who has followed them from town at a breakneck pace in an effort to warn them about a fresh revelation of hers…

Thanks to the magic of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLegendLore]{Legend Lore} spell scroll, Liestra has learned the location of the Bleak Archive and its involvement with the origin of the curse. The precise timing of Liestra's arrival is somewhat up to the players and the decisions they make following the encounter with Dereth in the Mountainside Grotto.

Dramatic Timing

The moment of Liestra's arrival is a delicate narrative beat, particularly when it comes to the kind of suspenseful gameplay "A Brush With Death" aims to capture. Here's our advice regarding the approximate timing of her appearance:

  • Best Case Scenario. The most optimal time for Liestra to arrive, in terms of dramatic impact, would be when and if the characters take a short or long rest Rest after their encounter with Dereth — particularly during the moment they decide to take a closer look at the Rune-Marked Blade (or another Varùn relic).

  • Most Likely Option. A more convenient moment would be Liestra's precise arrival to the Mountainside Grotto as soon as the party has finished inspecting Dereth's remains after the battle.

  • If All Else Fails. If the party's exploration somehow outpaces your preferred timing, simply have Liestra arrive when it suits you. After all, the tone and intentions of her message are ultimately more important than the timing.

Whatever the actual timing, feel free and be prepared to augment the readaloud text below with a prefacing phrase that helps root Liestra's arrival in the precise moment during your own campaign.

When the moment is right, read the following aloud:

Just then, a voice cuts through the harsh rustling of mountain wind…

Be careful with that relic, my friend. You'll never believe from whence it came.

You turn to see the weary face of Liestra Grann. Sweat drips from the Kivahr merchant's troubled brow, and her trademark grin has been replaced by an exhausted grimace. Her hands seem to tremble as she produces a rune-marked antique from the folds of her garments. Her eyes betray a potent fear, but her sense of purpose is unmistakable.

Liestra extends the relic for you to see, and you behold an oversized vial carved from cerulean crystal, adorned with strange runic markings and stoppered with a cap made from some curious alloy. The markings on this relic are unmistakably similar to the ones found on the rune-marked blade wielded by Dereth Erekos. Liestra continues:

Pardon my intrusion, but I've made an important discovery — one that sheds light on this dismal situation in Skybrush. The news I bring is imperative, and I beseech you to listen…

Dereth Erekos came to me one week ago with a collection of Varùn relics he'd found while ambling somewhere up in the mountains. As is my custom, I made sure to identify each item before agreeing to take them off the young bard's hands for a handsome price. I purchased four of these oversized antiques from Dereth, including a sash, a ring, an arrowhead, and the vial you see now. It seems young Erekos kept the knife for himself.

You see, I'd been saving a scroll of Legend Lore for a rainy day. And as I considered the untimely fates of Qory Hult and Gedron Tath, my conscience got the better of me. I realized that rainy day was finally upon us…

These relics hail from a forgotten Shent vault north of here, known as the Bleak Archive. The sages who constructed it long ago built it to contain a variety of relics and antiques that have been corrupted by dark forces from beyond The Weave. Indeed, traces of the Abyss itself are said to linger in the lightless halls of the Archive. According to legend, a Varùn warlock named Tethra Shùl led a raiding party to the Bleak Archive and never left. Somehow, against all odds, Dereth brought these Varùn relics back to Skybrush from that loathsome place — a vault that predates the relics themselves.

Liestra takes a moment to gauge your reaction to her tale.

Liestra's Tale

Liestra has the following information to offer about the Varùn relics in addition to the details presented in her readaloud above.

  • Liestra purchased 4 of the Varùn relics from Dereth, who had found them while exploring the hinterlands north of this grotto. Liestra offered Dereth the laquered hardwood lute and a very modest amount of coin in exchange for the relics — indeed, the very same lute that was found splintered and destroyed here in the grotto.

  • Spell scrolls of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} that were used to discern the nature of the relics didn't yield any conclusive results.

  • After Liestra claimed them from Dereth, 3 of the Varùn relics were sold to their respective owners within a week — a Varùn Arrowhead to Qory Hult, a Varùn Sash to Kel Kornan, and a Varùn Ring to Gedron Tath. (For more details, consult the "Tracking the Curse" section of the @UUID[.MyxkUsLNydK7zTBE]{Revealing the Mystery} appendix).

  • When pressed about where he found the relics, Dereth described a "giantfolk tomb" nearly two miles northeast of the grotto. Liestra's research has revealed this place to be @UUID[JournalEntry.skQcdBxw8K0AS7hv]{The Bleak Archive}, a vault supposedly constructed by the Shent giants who inhabited these mountains and valleys long, long ago.

  • Liestra purchased 4 of the Varùn relics from Dereth, who had found them while exploring the hinterlands north of this grotto. Liestra offered Dereth the laquered hardwood lute and a very modest amount of coin in exchange for the relics — indeed, the very same lute that was found splintered and destroyed here in the grotto.

  • Magical and non-magical attempts to discern the nature of the relics didn't yield any conclusive results.

  • After Liestra claimed them from Dereth, 3 of the Varùn relics were sold to their respective owners within a week — a Varùn Arrowhead to Qory Hult, a Varùn Sash to Kel Kornan, and a Varùn Ring to Gedron Tath. (For more details, consult the "Tracking the Curse" section of the @UUID[.MyxkUsLNydK7zTBE]{Revealing the Mystery} appendix).

  • When pressed about where he found the relics, Dereth described a "giantfolk tomb" nearly two miles northeast of the grotto. Liestra's research has revealed this place to be @UUID[JournalEntry.skQcdBxw8K0AS7hv]{The Bleak Archive}, a vault supposedly constructed by the Shent who inhabited these mountains and valleys long, long ago.

Whether or not the characters believe Liestra's story, she urges them to investigate the Bleak Archive themselves for a solution to the curse that plagues Skybrush.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

With Dereth's Notes in hand and guided by additional directions from Liestra Grann, the party must journey northward to search for the location of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.CS82h91RP59553vr]{The Bleak Archive} and the events of [[/eventState brushWithDeathArchives]].
The Abandoned Lute.soverview: In search of Dereth Erekos, the party encounters the remote mountainside grotto where the young bard was known to compose his ballands. Lurking amidst the cavern is the now undead remnant of Dereth himself. The character battle the dread Horrendor that Dereth has become and encounter an unexpected friend, Liestra Grann.
The Abandoned Lute.sexposition: Intermittent growths of Moon Blossoms lead you towards the foothills, where you discover a grotto marked by a bed of these lambent cerulean anemones and a circular arrangement of ancient stones. These short menhirs appear to be marked with archaic carvings, and jut out from the rocky landscape like an enormous hand reaching up from the rugged earth.
The Abandoned Lute.ssummary: Our search for Dereth Erekos led us to a mountainside grotto northwest of Skybrush where we encountered Dereth himself, twisted into a monstrous undead creature. After defeating Dereth in battle we encountered Liestra Grann, the antiquarian and shopkeeper from Skybrush, who tracked us down with further clues about the origin of the Varùn artifacts.

Trampled Florescence.name: Trampled Florescence
Trampled Florescence.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This is an exploration event that leads the party further away from Skybrush on their hunt for @UUID[Actor.H0WMbdJx0yELum4z]{Dereth Erekos}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Encounter a remarkable concentration of @UUID[Item.ihthfY7X30HnAVcH]{Moon Blossoms} that will point the way further north towards Dereth's current location.

Bed of Moonflowers

As the party follows the trail further north through the valley west of Skybrush, they may notice themselves walking in tandem with wild growths of the luminous Moon Blossoms. Keen-eyed characters will spot several trampled sections of flower bed that clearly indicate a western progression of movement.

What the Characters Find

With a [[/check perception 15 passive format=long]] or a successful [[/skill perception 13]] check, a character notices a faintly trampled path through the cluster of blossoms.

  • A successful [[/skill sur 14]] check is required to locate the trail of Dereth's booted tracks among the flower bed, which lead northward deeper into the valley.

  • A successful [[/skill nature 16]] or characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/knowledge plants]] recognize that this extreme concentration of flowers has created a subtle pollen cloud and that the air is full of tiny spores.

There is something unusually serene about this location despite the grim troubles which underscore your current quest. The rugged pastoral beauty of the Rustvar Valleys is in full display here and the crisp air of these hinterlands coupled with the mazy smells of the wildflower meadow leave you wishing for time to rest and take in the majestic scene.

Dream a Little Dream

If the characters spend at least 10 minutes in this location but do not voluntarily decide to take a long rest, they find themselves involuntarily setting down their packs and reclining amidst the wild meadow.

Each character is so transfixed by the scene that they do not notice others in their company drifting off into a gentle sleep. Each party member must make a [[/save wisdom 13]] saving throw or fall asleep. Characters who succeed on this saving throw fall into a daydream instead, unaware of the dozing of others. This torpor lasts for [[/gmroll 1d4 # Hours of sleep]] hours.

Each character is so transfixed by the scene that they do not notice others in their company drifting off into a gentle sleep. Each party member faces a [[/hazard 2 willpower morale psychic]] , and if they fail to resist, they fall asleep. Characters who succeed on fall into a daydream instead, unaware of the dozing of others. This torpor lasts for [[/gmroll 1d4 # Hours of sleep]] hours.

At first the dreams are pleasant, but any sleeping character who has not yet experienced a nightmare of Nethehepticas eventually experiences one of the dreams described in the @UUID[.O1u2YfjEcHhFRezW]{Night Terrors} event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party must continue exploring the valley on the heels of the bard's trail, which will eventually lead them to discover the mountainside grotto to the north and the event [[/eventState brushWithDeathDereth]].
Trampled Florescence.soverview: The party continues to search for Dereth Erekos, following the scattered trail of moonflower blossoms in the hinterlands north of Skybrush. The party encounters a fresh clue in the form of a remarkable bed of lambent cerulean Moon Blossoms that has been suspiciously trod upon by an interloper.
Trampled Florescence.sexposition: You encounter a thick bed of Moon Blossoms that cover the ground here like a soft cerulean blanket. The growth is so dense, you struggle to keep pace with the trail that you followed out of Skybrush. And the delicate tranquility of this place is unmistakable compared to the stark wilderness nearby.
Trampled Florescence.ssummary: During our search for Dereth Erekos, we found a remarkable bed of lambent cerulean Moon Blossoms that had been suspiciously trod upon by an interloper. This clue suggested that someone, possibly Dereth, had ventured this way recently.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This main quest occurs during Chapter 3 amidst the great city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, and is intended to begin when the party receives @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.AqCu9AhqOyEJmqiw]{A Cevher Summons} a few days after the events of [[/eventState otherhood1Ordinate]].

Unlike the events of Chapter 2, each of the Chapter 3 main quests can occur simultaneously, although the characters must manage their time accordingly for various encounters and events to proceed with certain measures of success.

Difficulty

The "Disgraced House" quest is designed for a party of Level 5 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Main Quest that awards 3 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the [[/eventState otherhood2Threats]], [[/eventState otherhood2PreHeist]], and [[/eventState otherhood2Aftermath]] Events.

Point of No Return: The Marlstone Gala

The [[/eventState otherhood2Gala]] Event serves as a point of no return for certain Chapter 3 Main Quests. Once the characters complete this Event, they can no longer continue or complete the Events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness}.

Lyla Cevher asks for the party to join her at House Cevher headquarters, where she is reeling from the death of her uncle Darius and the disappearance of her brother Funar. In his untimely absence, Funar is being blamed for the crime — and Lyla's first priority is to clear her sibling's name. She asks the party to investigate the scene of the crime and use a locator rod that is attuned to a pin she and her brother both wear to find his location. The characters discover evidence that the murder was carried out by a gang known as the Beacon Brigade, based in Lantern Roads; they also find out that Funar is being held in the neighboring Marlstone district, in the home of Hephiss Wandren, the head of House Wandren. Coincidence? Likely not.

After a tense visit from Hephiss, the party realizes that the Wandren matriarch alone holds the keys to Funar's prison — and that the upcoming Marlstone Gala is the perfect time to steal them. They'll have to recruit an alchemist who can copy the magically-warded keys by doing a dangerous favor, convince Lyla's old friend Juro Wandren to get them on the list, and scout both Lantern Roads and the Marlstone Manor to secure themselves a safe path in and out. On the night of the gala, the party must attempt to steal Hephiss Wandren's keys, have them copied, and find a way into her well-guarded lair where Funar is being held prisoner. As they go, they'll discover the real power behind the plot against House Cevher, and may even end up with an ally whose power can help them defeat it.

Related Quests

This is the second quest in the overarching Otherhood of Fortune storyline, which includes:

  1. @UUID[JournalEntry.CHLiPiU0Bx9Pdevu]

  2. @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1]

  3. @UUID[JournalEntry.mytyUKL7PyABLVRp]

  4. @UUID[JournalEntry.iw9aRpGjVc3iLv7E]

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher}

  • @UUID[Actor.OOO380zs3xZYG9PI]{Hephiss Wandren}

  • @UUID[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren}

  • @UUID[Actor.E701HRk9vreXMUhl]{Funar Cevher}

  • @UUID[Actor.gBXPA4AerLzwSbi6]{Janix Mance}

  • @UUID[Actor.u6ntYVVPwHy97AGH]{Projection of Pyix}

The ball also provides an opportunity for other past characters to make an appearance and catch up with the characters.

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Wandren Patroller}

  • @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk]{Wandren Watcher}

  • @UUID[Actor.qyuqbNfU3VFUhPWF]{Vitt Wandren}

  • @UUID[Actor.ZMLyUZaK76soqKx0]{Skither}

  • @UUID[Actor.yqcFzCs8eJXXNKiR]{Kynryth}

  • @UUID[Actor.69yCeDhDktOWW5O0]{Aburyx}

  • @UUID[Actor.8PiFttcf0tJV0joE]{Ketral}

  • @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]{Suarrok Juvenile}
Overview.soverview:
In the wake of her uncle Darius' murder, the disappearance of her brother Funar, and the expulsion of Trading House Cevher from the Ordinate, Lyla Cevher is determined to right the wrongs done to her family and repair the damage to House Cevher's good name. But she can't do it alone. Lyla reaches out to the party for help — to investigate the murder, track down her brother's whereabouts, and find who or what is behind the assault on all things Cevher.

After examining the scene of the crime, tracking Funar Cevher's current whereabouts, and learning more about the head of a rival Trading House, the place to help Lyla accomplish all her goals is clear: the annual Marlstone Gala, an event where the who's who of Ordain comes out to see and be seen. Together with Lyla and any allies they can recruit, the party will have to pull off a heist, right beneath the enemy's nose.

No heist is guaranteed to be easy, especially not under the bright lights of Ordain. The party must scout the location, find a way into the party, use the glitz and glamour as a cover to move throughout the massive Marlstone Manor, and progress into its hidden and dangerous depths. Along the way, they can uncover not only what is truly happening to House Cevher, but also what lies beneath the glittering surface of one of Ordain's most exclusive occasions.

A Cevher Summons.name: A Cevher Summons
A Cevher Summons.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, the party is brought a message from@UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{ Lyla Cevher}, who wishes to see them at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.h9ObbNZE3wenJ4pu]{Trading House Cevher} headquarters in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.D0AAT8TNsytqy7Hm]{Quarry Run} to discuss the recent murder of her uncle Darius.

  • During this event, the party can speak with the messenger about the circumstances of the murder and the current state of the House Cevher (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.AqCu9AhqOyEJmqiw#the-talk-around-town]{The Talk Around Town})

The Talk Around Town

If the party wishes, they can ask the messenger about the current situation with House Cevher.

What the Messenger Knows

The messenger, Hanslo Rey (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him), doesn't intend to chat for long after delivering his warning, but with a successful [[/check insight 15]], the party knows that the messenger is a bit of a gossip and loves to share what he knows.

Characters can convince him to speak longer with a tip of [[/award -2sp]] or greater, a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] or [[/check intimidation 16]] check, [[/knowledge intrigue]], or [[/knowledge politics]].

Lyla's Current Situation

I'm sure you heard, but Lyla's brother is the one who killed Darius Cevher, the fabric maker down in Gossamer. Bloody business. The brother, Funar? He's run off, hiding from the authorities. I wonder if Lyla's gotten wind of where he is and is trying to sneak him out of town. She's been gone for years, I think - what a welcome home. I almost feel bad for her, Cevher name and all.

House Cevher's Past

Should have known that Cevher would be the one involved in something like this. They always claimed not to have been the cause of the Stonehollow Quake a while back, but it started in one of their sites and killed a whole lot of people. Since then. I've been waiting for the next disaster. This, though - this is a disaster of a whole 'nother sort.

Funar's Guilt

Of all the Cevhers that would kill someone, I never would have guessed it was the Funar kid. Didn't know him much, but delivered to him now and again. Very shy and quiet, but I guess it's always the quiet ones.

House Cevher's Future

House Cevher may be in a bit of trouble. Everyone relies on them for stone and metal, but after the earthquake and this scandal - folks are remembering that they aren't the only merchants in town.

Concluding The Event

With nothing more to say, the messenger heads off to their next job, leaving the party with Lyla's letter and invitation.

Next Steps

When and if the party wants to meet with Lyla, they can proceed to the House Cevher Tradeway in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.D0AAT8TNsytqy7Hm]{Quarry Run}, triggering @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.SiKrlbgifaPCGobw]{Family Business}.
A Cevher Summons.soverview: The party receives a message from Lyla Cevher, asking them to meet her to talk about House Cevher's current predicament. The messenger can bring the party up to speed on some of the troubles facing the Trading House.
A Cevher Summons.sexposition:
Ordain is a city with its own rhythm and pace, a drumbeat of color and sound and perpetual motion, but somehow, among all the many people in its bustling streets, a messenger finds you, Arriving as if out of nowhere, he holds a letter in his hand a smile pasted on his face, bowing his head as he waits for you to read the neatly lettered note.

I must speak with you. Please come to the House Cevher Tradeway in Quarry Run. There is more to my uncle Darius' murder than what they say, but I need your help to prove it.

-Lyla Cevher

As you finish reading, the messenger studies you for a moment, then leans in and lowers his voice.

You're new in town, right? Might want to be a bit careful about who your friends are.
A Cevher Summons.ssummary: We received a message from Lyla Cevher asking us to meet her in the House Cevher Tradeway in Quarry Run to talk about the murder of her uncle, Darius. The gossipy messenger who delivered the note strongly alluded to the troubles that House Cevher faces in the wake of this horrible murder, but Lyla believes the crime is more complex than the powers that be would have the city believe and wants our help to prove it. She's asked us to meet her in the House Cevher Tradeway to discuss.

Finding Funar.name: Finding Funar
Finding Funar.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

Lyla suggests in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.SiKrlbgifaPCGobw]{Family Business} that the party use her @UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod } to find the general location of her brother Funar, as detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.LIQ5fMBwNgnnIFLA]{Searching for Funar}.

This social and exploration event begins once the party has tracked Funar Cevher's location to the Marlstone district of the city. The locator rod leads them to Marlstone Manor, where they can:

  • ask a few routine questions of the guards at the gate (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.7sf7FVZyd5yoWmYM#a-chat-with-the-guards]{A Chat with the Guards})

  • learn that staff will be allowed on the grounds of the Marlstone Manor to help prep in advance of the upcoming Marlstone Gala

Note: characters should not enter the manor grounds at this time (see @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.7sf7FVZyd5yoWmYM#investigating-the-manor]{Investigating the Manor} below).

Investigating the Manor

Gamemaster Note: Entering the Manor

The party will have the opportunity to scout Marlstone Manor in later quest evens at length. As a result, it is important that players do not enter the manor now, as it will make the running of the quest much more difficult. The obstacles below are designed to be a deterrent, but add to them as needed to deter a creative party.

If they would like, the party can do some initial scouting of the manor.

Do Not Enter

The entrance to Marlstone Manor is blocked by a large gate and staffed with guards who are well-equipped to defend the grounds if needed.

Any character who casts Detect Magic can note the presence of magic in and around the gate. With the Identify spell, characters know that the gate is warded with a spell that alarms if anyone comes too close and delivers a powerful burst of force energy.

  • Any attempts to sneak by the gates automatically fail.

  • If characters attempt to touch the gates or cross them without permission, they must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 22]] saving throw or take [[/damage force 3d6]]. Each time this defensive feature activates, the DC of the saving throw increases by 2 and the damage increases by 1d6 - the gate resets after 1 hour without being activated.

A Chat with the Guards

Talking To The Guards

The guards will answer a few questions about the Manor, noting that the only easy way to gain entrance is to be part of the staff for the upcoming Marlstone Manor gala.

  • With a successful [[/check persuasion 18]] or [[/check intimidation 18]] check, the party can convince the guards to give them information about when and where staff is showing up for the event.

  • If the party accuses the guards of holding Funar, they are offended, throwing the party off of the grounds. They are unaware of Funar being held here and have no information to share on the matter.

Whose manor this is

You must be new around these parts. No matter. Marlstone Manor has been one of the jewels of the Wandren Trading House for years. Whoever's running the house moves into the place and puts their own stamp on it, though it hasn't changed hands in a while. Hephiss Wandren has this house and the Trading House firmly in her grasp.

Speaking to Hephiss Wandren

Hephiss isn't here. And she's not one to come out and greet random strangers at the front gates either. If you need something from her, go on and send a messenger. Or see her at the Marlstone Gala. If you're invited, that is.

Getting access to the grounds

Sorry, no can do. I've heard of some of the previous Wandren heads doing open tours of the Manor, but Hephiss Wandren prefers her privacy. Only time she'll be opening up her house is for the gala. If you want a peek inside, you'll need an invite. Or to be one of the folks helping to prep the place. There's a call going out for cooks and gardeners and the like sometime soon.

The upcoming event

The Marlstone Gala's the biggest see and be seen event in town. I'm not always one for a fancy occasion, but I'm trying to get guard duty that night so I can walk the gardens, see what they look like when they're all lit up for a party. Good thing staff get first pick of assignments, right?

Getting into the gala as staff (requires successful [[/check 18 persuasion]] or [[/check 18 intimidation]])

No guarantees, but from what I hear, if you show up here two days before the gala and look halfway competent, you should be able to get the job. Good luck.

Funar Cevher is inside!

Excuse me, what? I'm not sure what you're talking about, but you need to go talk about it somewhere else. Get a move on, now. Go!

Luxarum Attunement: Befriend the Guards

If the party chooses to befriend the guards to learn more about Funar's whereabouts, each participating character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 otherhood2FindingFunarBefriend]] at the conclusion of the event.

Ragen Attunement: Befriend the Guards

If the party manages to offend the guards during the attempt to learn more about Funar's whereabouts, each participating character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 otherhood2FindingFunarBefriendOffend]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding The Event

Next Steps

Once the party has located Funar and gotten any information they can from Marlstone, they must also investigate the scene of the crime of Darius Cevher's murder (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.YBxOyEZ4eN4jEobu]{The Death of Darius} ) to learn more about who committed it.

If both tasks are done, the party should report to Lyla at the House Cevher Tradeway in Quarry Run, triggering @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.zSpPVloL1lGDom9T]{Veiled Threats}.
Finding Funar.soverview: Having canvassed the city of Ordain tracking the location of Lyla's missing brother, Funar Cehver, using a magical rod attuned to his direction, the party arrives at Marlstone, the district where they believe he is being held.
Finding Funar.sexposition:
According to the locator rod, Funar Cevher is somewhere in this district, which is filled with grand houses and a single winding street. The street leads up to the grandest of these estates, distinguished enough to have its own name on a sign at the gate — Marlstone Manor. As you near the gate, the locator rod shifts slightly as its inset jewel switches from gray to blue. Funar Cevher must be somewhere on the grounds. Before you can move close enough to investigate further, a guard behind the gate waves in your general direction.

This is private property - not open to visitors. Is there something else we can help you with?
Finding Funar.ssummary: With the help of the Locator Rod given to us by Lyla Cevher, we tracked her brother Funar's location to the opulent Marlstone Manor, where we were stopped by the guards. The manor isn't generally open to the public, but if we want to rescue Funar, or find any proof that he is on the property, we will need to find a way inside.

The Death of Darius.name: The Death of Darius
The Death of Darius.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party can:

  • Make their way into Threadforge, Darius Cevher's shop, which has been locked up by the Veiled Chain for an investigation that appears to have stalled.

  • Investigate the clues at the scene of the crime at Darius Cevher's shop (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.YBxOyEZ4eN4jEobu#investigating-the-crime-scene]{Investigating The Crime Scene}), which include:

    • Bloody papers and thread, which include a powder found in an envelope that would have incapacitated Darius and an appointment with Funar Cevher — well after the time of the murder.

    • A large quantity of money in Darius' desk that was easily accessible but ignored by his killer — contradicting the belief that Funar killed Darius for money.

  • Free the stabbed mannequin from the floor, allowing it to reenact the last moments of Darius Cevher's life (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.YBxOyEZ4eN4jEobu#the-stabbed-mannequin]{The Stabbed Mannequin}).

In @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.SiKrlbgifaPCGobw]{Family Business}, Lyla provided the party with the most recent known information about Darius' murder, found in the form of an article in local gossip rag Overheard in Ordain - @UUID[Item.nCdyFX3dY14CFRpA]{A Stitch In Crime}. They can refer to this at any time as a reminder of the "official" investigation.

Work In Progress: Future Vista

In the future, this event will take place in an Interior Vista representing Darius Cevher's destroyed shop. Currently, the event will instead take place on the region map, using theater of the mind.

Entering The shop

Outside Observations

Before entering the shop, characters can attempt to determine how long it has been since anyone was in the shop by:

  • Succeeding on a [[/check dc 17 investigation]] check to note how much thread dust is on the windows.

  • Succeeding on a [[/check dc 19 history]] check to note how much the ink in the letter has faded.

  • Noting the lack of footprints in the threadfall on the ground with a successful [[/check perception 17]] check.

All three indicate that the shop has been untouched for at least the last 2 weeks. If there was an investigation, it appears to have stalled.

A Simple Lock

A lock has been placed on the door of the shop. It can be removed/disabled by any of the following methods:

  • A successful [[/check dexterity 16]] check with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools}.

  • A successful [[/check strength 21]] check to break through the locked door.

  • A successful [[/check perception 16]] check or [[/check passive perception 18]] to notice that one of the windows is open. The window can be entered without a check.

Once characters enter the shop, read or paraphrase the following:

It is clear that something violent happened here. Papers and spools of thread are scattered across a wooden worktable, some spattered with red droplets that are likely blood, the wooden fabric racks propped against the wall are half-askew, and in the center of the room, wearing a finely tailored jacket, a patchwork fabric mannequin is sprawled on the floor with a knife in the middle of its chest. Behind the worktable, a glowing outline on the floor of sprawled legs seems to indicate that the body was found on the far side of the shop.

The Scene Of The Crime

There are several places in the shop that the party can investigate to try to learn more about the murder.

A Quick Look Around

Without a check, parties can see the following:

  • Fabric On The Floor: A crumpled piece of fabric in the center of the floor, stained with an unknown substance.

  • The Body Outline: An outline indicating the position of Darius' body when it was found.

  • Papers and Spools of Thread: Bloody papers and spools of thread, strewn across Darius' work table.

  • Broken Fabric Racks: Broken wooden fabric racks leaning against the wall.

  • The Stabbed Mannequin: A cloth construct on the ground with a knife embedded in its chest

If characters cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic}, the only magical effects are found on the cloth construct mannequin itself.

Fabric On The Floor

At first glance, the crumpled fabric on the floor appears to have been dyed a brownish-crimson, though the similarly colored stain on the rug beneath it may indicate something more sinister.

  • Any characters with [[/knowledge forensics]], [[/knowledge crime]], or who succeeds on a [[/check nature 16]] check knows that the fabric and the stain underneath it are both blood.

  • Any character who examines the stain beneath the body and succeeds on a [[/check nature 18]] or [[/check investigation 18]] check knows that the blood soaked into the rug for some time, indicating the body was likely laying in this spot for some time, far from where the body was found. Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on this check.

Outline Of The Body

The clear outline of sprawled legs can be seen from the doorway, with the rest of the outline coming into view as you draw nearer, hidden initially by his working desk. According to the outline, his body was discovered behind his desk, next to a still overturned chair. This matches what you've heard about the murder — that Darius was sitting or standing behind his desk when he was stabbed.

  • Any characters with [[/check perception 15 passive]] or who succeed on a [[/check perception 17]] check can see that the rug behind the desk appears undisturbed, with no traces of blood, and is covered in a powder of some kind.

    • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]], [[/knowledge crime]], or who succeed on a [[/check arcana 17]] check can recognize the powder by smell and vision - it is the remains of @UUID[Item.JKWt3ZZKBaEvNbw1]{Choking Fog Dust}, sometimes used by criminals and thieves to disable their victims.

Papers and Threads on the Table

Papers and spools of thread are scattered across the table. Many have drops of blood in or around them. The blood is concentrated on the papers and thread on the near side of the table, while the far side is covered in dust. Underneath both, scattered across the table, are coins.

  • With a successful [[/check 17 investigation]] check, characters know that Darius was stabbed while standing in front of the table, spraying blood on the objects closest to him. Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on this check.

  • With a successful [[/check perception 17]] check, characters can see that the substance on the far side of the desk is more than dust - it's residue from a powder.

    • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]], [[/knowledge crime]], or who succeed on a [[/check arcana 17]] check can recognize the powder by smell and vision - it is the remains of @UUID[Item.JKWt3ZZKBaEvNbw1]{Choking Fog Dust}, sometimes used by criminals and thieves to disable their victims.

  • If desired, the party can collect the coins from the desk, gaining [[/award 4gp]] in small coins.

Fabric Racks Against The Wall

Wooden racks are propped against the wall in an odd position - one has a scrap of silver fabric on it that looks as if it was dipped in a dark brown dye, while the other one is empty but obviously broken.

  • The dyed fabric: With a successful [[/check medicine 16]] check or [[/knowledge forensics]], the party knows that the dye on the silver fabric is dried blood. The fabric was laying in the blood for several hours before it was moved onto the rack.

  • The broken fabric rack: With a successful [[/check nature 16]] or [[/check investigation 16]] check, the party knows that the fabric rack would have only broken with a sudden crash. It was likely lifted up and put against the wall after the confrontation that killed Darius.

The Stabbed Mannequin

The patchwork mannequin sprawled across the floor like a body, a long metal knife stuck through its chest and into the floor below. As you approach it, it moves, raising a hand with silk and burlap fingers, clutching at the knife handle as if it wants to set itself free.

Without a check, the party can see that the knife has gone through the mannequin and is pinning it to the floor.

Examining the Mannequin

The mannequin is made of pieces of fabric of all shapes, sizes and colors, stitched together in bundles. Though it is made only of fabric, it is tough and can’t be pulled through the knife.

  • Characters who succeed on a [[/check arcana 16]] check or have [[/knowledge crafts]] know that this is a fashion construct, usually created over the course of a designer's career out of the scraps they have saved over the years.

  • They also know (as does anyone who casts @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify}), that these constructs are attuned to whoever creates them and are have the magical ability to repeat up to 30 seconds of another person's motions on a loop - designers use them to capture customers' movements and design properly flowing garments.

Examining the Knife

If the party takes a closer look at the knife, they notice a fingerprint on it without a check.

A small circular smudge mars the surface of the otherwise clean metal handle of the knife — a fingerprint, or what's left of it.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 17]] check or with [[/knowledge forensics]]. the party knows that the fingerprint was smudged while the knife was wielded. Whoever the fingerprint belongs to likely stabbed Darius, and then used the knife to pin the mannequin to the ground.

Removing the Knife

The knife can be pulled out of the floor with a successful [[/check athletics 15]] check. Once the knife is removed, a foul stench rises from the construct where it was pierced.

A foul scent rises from the hole in the center of the fabric where the knife pierced it, and the edges of the hole in the fabric are devoid of all color, as if it has been sucked out of the neighboring thread.

Characters can try to identify the fumes. With a successful [[/check nature 16]] check, [[/knowledge alchemy]], or [[/knowledge crime]], they know that they are the end result of @UUID[Item.pyKB2u54RkGyCbdu]{Withering Flesh Poison}, which is designed to rot the flesh but can also disintegrate non-living objects.

If a character touches the knife, they are affected by the poison and must succeed on a [[/save constitution 16]] saving throw or take [[/damage necrotic 1d6]].

Once the knife is removed, the fabric construct immediately gets up and begins moving:

The fabric construct rises and walks to a spot behind the central table in Threadforge, which is still filled with scraps of paper and fabric. It makes an action with its hands over the table as if grasping something, then begins violently shaking and stumbling into the center of the room. Before it can take more than a few steps, it jolts forward, spins around, and jolts backwards, falling to the ground in the position it was in when you arrived. Immediately, it rises again, walks to the spot behind the central table and repeats the entire sequence.

Deconstructed Crime

If the party watches the construct, they see it make three distinct movements — motioning with its hands, shaking and stumbling, and jerking forward and back.

  • The Action With Its Hands: Characters who succeed on a [[/check sleightofhand 16]] check to recreate the motion the construct is doing or a [[/check investigation 16]] check to try to match the motion to something on the table know that Darius was likely opening a piece of paper. If characters have found the dust-filled envelope on the work table, they know that the motion was to open this envelope.

  • The Shaking And Stumbling: Characters who succeed on a [[/check performance 16]] check to recreate the construct's movements or a [[/check medicine 16]] check to look for any physical causes know that this is likely a coughing fit. If characters have found the @UUID[Item.JKWt3ZZKBaEvNbw1]{Choking Fog Dust} residue, they know that it causes these effects.

  • The Jolting Forward and Backward: Characters know, without a check, that the violent jolting is caused by the stabbing itself, indicating that Darius was stabbed twice, first in the back and then in the chest.

  • The Repetitive Action: Characters who succeed on a [[/check arcana 16]] or [[/check investigation 16]] check or have [[/knowledge crafts]] know that the construct is repeating the last actions that Darius experienced. The only thing stopping it from going through this sequence earlier was the knife that pinned it to the ground.

Mayis Attunement: Freeing the Mannequin

The first character to remove the knife in an effort to free the mannequin advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 otherhood2DariusFreed]] at the conclusion of the event.

Signara Attunement: Thorough Investigation

If the party manages to successfully identify all 5 of the clues here, each participating character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 otherhood2DariusClues]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding The Event

Next Steps

If the party has discovered the location of Funar, they should proceed to see House Cevher HQ to fill Lyla in on what they have found.
