@UUID[Actor.HUIhXv1i0eywY5Q5]{Aythorn}

Of course I wouldn't miss this for the world. I love a good party — and the flowers here are beautiful!

Aythorrn will wax poetic about the beautiful decorations - and suggest that the party might be more lively if a subtle breeze were to blow the flower petals across the room in time to the lively music.

@UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]{Cherish Ellerie}

It took me a lot of work to get an invite — luckily I know one of the members of the ensemble, who was able to sneak me in. I love talent, and I've heard Hephiss has a very unique art collection.

Cherish will quickly mention Ordain as a great city for the arts and talk up the importance of Trading House Salva, which focuses on the arts and on fashion.

@UUID[Actor.X2nmQ7Ewt14lSR6g]{Eamon Mariflor}

You ought to see the parties in Redrak for last day of harvest. This is nice, but doesn't hold a candle to our celebrations.

Eamon Mariflor encourages everyone he speaks to to visit the red grass heartland, Redrak Fields, and will claim that it is not facing the same problems with dissension or violence as other parts of the Artcus Plateau.

@UUID[Actor.XrFDJNn1Fa7hopqR]{Eveis Brightstone}

Before you ask, yes, it can be quite difficult to fit through some of the doors here, but I'm always so glad to be invited to these kinds of events. Ordain is such a welcoming and lovely city!

Eveis is difficult to speak to alone for too long, as others come up to her frequently to welcome her or thank her for her protection of the city. She takes the compliments graciously and downplays her role, turning conversation instead to the city's wonderful mix of different peoples and cultures.

@UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa}

Oh gosh, I can't seem to get a breather here, so many faces and people to talk to! I would love to talk more, but I'm swamped!

Though Fernis is often on the move at the party, she's interested in any stories of adventure that the party might have, as they help to quell her wanderlust. She especially wishes she had been able to help when Helkas was attacked.

@UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien}

I don’t rub elbows with aristocrats very often myself, but occasions like these do help you see how the other half lives, so to speak. The normal, working-class folks of Ordain keep me and my sages rather busy.

Lilla is more brusque than she might be otherwise, concerned about some illness in the north of the city that the Sages of Ordain must deal with - it feels to her like life has recently been one crisis after another.

@UUID[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]{Luna Karrowrath}

You call this a party? My good friends, there isn’t nearly enough open flame here to label it a proper celebration. If you truly want to see a good time, spend an evening of revelry with me and my Flameguard.

Luna Karrowrath came to the party mostly out of curiosity, and primarily brags about the excitement of the Flameguard - she keeps the conversation relatively short as she is planning to leave early.

@UUID[Actor.DxLuKBTSF9dDzEbG]{Ournesta Brel}*

House Bastila has interests across the plateau and beyond. What better place than here to make the necessary connections?

Ournesta loves talking trade and can recommend some good shops in the city in return for any business contacts the party may have made, especially if they are reachable by sea.

*Note: Ournesta Brel does not currently have a full portrait.

@UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND]{Redfiend Loris Tezran}

This little gathering is very quaint, is this typical for Ordain do you think?

Redfiend Loris Tezran loves the Tayan Empire and thinks it is the best place on Ember. He frequently asks leading questions about local customs that seem designed to make the Empire look great and everywhere else seem provincial.

@UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]{Serethus}

You know, I've attended these sorts of affairs all across Ordain, for every House and organization, and few have the gilded glory of a Wandren affair!

Serethus is boisterous, and loves to tell stories of times that the Veiled Chain helped to save the day in Ordain. He often ends these accounts by claiming he said too much and then promptly jumping into the next one.

@UUID[Actor.m7bwxaSeiblzYyJw]{Desham "Shaar" Phos}

I wouldn't call myself a party person, but there's always something interesting to see at these sorts of events.

Shaar is much more of a watcher than a talker, and tends to respond to questions about the Veiled Chain or their life in brief sentences, while speaking for longer if any observations are made about others around them.

@UUID[Actor.qmMlHizvtjCYKjCR]{Sigil}

Knowledge isn't just found in the books — it's found in the world around us. I have been taking copious notes. And who knows? Perhaps I will throw a gathering like this for the many peoples of the Plateau who have been seeking refuge at my Lodge.

Sigil has heard that Hephiss Wandren has an extensive library and is intrigued by what might be in it. He's also quick to defend House Cevher to anyone who will listen, and believes they should still have a seat in the Ordinate.

@UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith}

It is good to be among those who help make our city what it is — when we gather like this, I think of all we can do together.

Vinarith enjoys making connections, and will ask the party about their interests and attempt to come up with another party guest whose company they might enjoy.

A Conversation with Hephiss Wandren

While Hephiss is busy hosting, she projects the energy of calm and control. With a successful [[/check insight 16]] check, the party knows that despite this, she is worried about what the guests might destroy in her house.

  • With a success of 3 or more, characters notice her looking towards the front door. Whatever she is worried about is likely in one of the front rooms - the @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.eUMzGYjT63M9UV3g]{Foyer}, @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.NgXe2ukpymWe1ngw]{Sitting Room}, or Gallery.

If characters have visited the Gallery, read Great Artists of the Arctus Plateau in the Library, or have [[/knowledge arts]], and speak to Hephiss about her artwork, they have advantage on all persuasion checks with Hephiss during the course of this conversation.

Hephiss doesn't have much time for the party, but she is willing to discuss the following:

  • The layout and history of the house. With a successful [[/check history 16]] check, the party can connect with her about architectural details and she will reveal that there's a hidden door somewhere on the first floor.

    I've always wanted one of those libraries where you pull a book out to reveal a secret door. Sadly, this place doesn't have that, but the secret door it does have is at least close enough that I can still smell the book binding.

  • Her artwork. Characters who have seen Hephiss' artwork in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.mLzBFHXratqh3i0p]{Gallery} and either have [[/knowledge arts]] or succeed on a [[/check deception 16]] check can flatter Hephiss about her artwork, getting her to confess that she has more artwork that she wasn't comfortable showing. She gives them directions and a temporary key to the@UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.npPq56DCS4tAURkp]{ Art Studio}, which becomes an Open room for the party for the next hour.

    I'm so glad you enjoyed my work. I've been working on some more complex pieces , but they didn't seem quite right for this environment. I'd be curious what you thought of them - I usually don't show my work in progress, but for a fellow artist? You can find it upstairs - it's locked up of course, but I always have a few extra keys around for those who appreciate the arts.

  • Tinkering. Characters who know of Hephiss' love of tinkering from visiting her Workshop can speak with her about tinkering with artifacts. Hephiss is willing to speak about this to anyone with [[/knowledge machines]] or who succeeds on a [[/check persuasion 16]] check, but they must first succeed on a [[/save charisma 17]] saving throw - on a failure, Hephiss knows the party was in her workshop and their suspicion level rises twice.

    Tinkering? What an interesting topic. But I must know - what made you think I was the one to talk to about it?

Copying Hephiss' Keys

It is up to the party how they wish to take Hephiss' key, but creating a distraction will make the job easier by lowering the DC of checks and/or giving the opportunity to make them with advantage.

Creating A Distraction

The party can pick whichever way they might think is best to create their distraction. The better they do at the distraction, the easier it is for the stealing the key challenge to proceed below.

Distractions can be either major or minor. While there is no limit on how many the party can start at once, after two consecutive distractions they gain a level of suspicion with each additional distraction.

  • Social Distraction: Start a fight, create a scene, get a loud conversation

    • To distract a person socially, characters must first determine what might rile them up with a successful [[/check insight 17]] check. If they know the person in question from a previous event, the DC of this check is lowered by 2.

      • If characters succeed on the insight check, they can start a fight with a successful [[/check intimidation 16]] check, begin an in-depth conversation with a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] check or using an appropriate [[/check history 16]] or knowledge check, or stage a dramatic scene with a successful [[/check performance 16]] check. On a success, they create a minor distraction. On a success by 3 or more, they cause a major distraction.

      • If characters fail the insight check, they may still attempt the above, but they make their check with disadvantage, and a failure to create the social distraction raises their suspicion level.

  • Physical Distraction: Knocking something over, starting a small fire

    • To create a physical distraction, characters must first determine where would be the appropriate place to stage their distraction with a [[/check 16 investigation]] check. They may use their heist points, or any items they have brought with them, in creating the physical distraction, but must succeed on a [[/check 16 stealth]] or [[/check 16 sleightofhand]] check or they are spotted in the vicinity of the distraction and gain a level of suspicion.

    • Whether the distraction caused is major or minor is at the gamemaster's discretion.

  • Magical Distraction: Casting any spell that creates a physical effect could create a distraction.

    • While casting their spell, characters will need to be careful not to draw attention to themselves in the process. If the spell is made using a physical gesture, for example, they must succeed on a [[/check 16 stealth]] check to find an out of the way place to cast the spell or succeed on a [[/check sleightofhand 16]] spell to make the gesture unobtrusively.

    • Whether the distraction caused is major or minor is at the gamemaster's discretion.

Stealing the Key

Either Lyla or a member of the party can steal the key from Hephiss Wandren with a successful [[/check sleightofhand 23]] check, which is modified by the following:

  • If the party has caused a major distraction, they have advantage on the check. Any additional major distraction lowers the DC of the check by 2.

  • For each and every minor distraction that the party causes, they lower the DC of the check by 1.

  • If a member of the party is currently engaging Hephiss in conversation, her distraction lowers the DC by an additional 2.

If the party fails to steal the key, they may retry the check, but they gain a level of suspicion for each attempt.

Getting to Janix Mance (and Back)

The party must make their way through the area map to Janix Mance, who is stationed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.OLD5SnNvjPB6nOfU]{Gardens}. This is primarily an area map challenge, with a few wandering guards and rooms with a variety of access levels. The party can determine the best way to make it to Janix and back as suits them. Once they reach him, he will begin to copy Hephiss' Keys.

A Talk with Janix

Janix reveals that the key alone won't get them into the safe - they'll need to reveal the door. Hephiss isn't carrying anything else on her, so the key to this must be elsewhere in the house and can be searched for.

Returning the Key

This is a fairly simple stealth/sleight of hand check to get the key back to Cevher and close the loop, with a few options. Each check, if successful on its own, will be enough to return the key. If a check is failed, the party may try another check, but a second failure will gain a level of suspicion.

  • Stealth: With a successful [[/check stealth 17]] check, the party is able to get close enough to Hephiss Wandren to easily place the key.

  • Sleight of Hand: With a successful [[/check sleightofhand 17]] check, the party does a reverse pickpocket to place the key in Hephiss' pocket.

  • Social: With a successful [[/check deception 17]] check, the party pretends to have found the key and returns it to Hephiss without incident.

Juro's Ledger

Juro and the Ledger

If the party wishes, they may attempt to retrieve Juro's ledger, which is located in Hephiss' Study on the first floor.

  • If the party retrieves the ledger, Juro is extremely grateful and promises to reward them at some future date. With his mind clear, he is also able to aid the party on any social checks that happen in his vicinity.

  • If the party does not retrieve the ledger before returning the key to Hephiss, Juro confronts them after this task is done, asking when they intend to retrieve it. With a [[/check persuasion 18]] or [[/check deception 18]] check, characters can convince Juro that they are on their way to get it.

    • If the check fails, Juro storms off to retrieve the ledger on his own. He is swiftly caught, and his prior conversation with the party is noted, raising the party's suspicion level by 1.

Getting To Funar

The party likely knows where Funar is based on their recon, but there's room here to find him if they don't.

Confirming Funar's Location

Funar is being held in a vault at the bottom level of the Manor, near the entrance to the Wandren hideout.

The party can determine Funar's location by using the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{ Locator Rod}. The result of using the Locator Rod can be found at the top of each room in the area walkthrough.

Getting Into Wandren HQ

To get into Wandren HQ, parties must do the following:

  • Discover that @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.kwFKceeBEoe8hpwq]{Hephiss' Downstairs Closet} is hiding the entrance to the vault.

  • Push the button in @UUID[JournalEntry.BCFHYDhO5nm7BhDU.JournalEntryPage.1W6MgyHIKhQ9m8cz]{Hephiss' Chambers} to reveal the door in the closet.

  • Learn the passphrase to remove the keyhole cover. The passcode is "Ray Lanterelle," a combination of Hephiss Wandren's favorite artist's name and her favorite flower. The door itself gives hints as to the passcode, though other hints can be found around the manor.

  • Use the copy of Hephiss' keys to open the door.

Concluding The Event

Next Steps

Once the party uses Hephiss' keyring to enter the basement level of Marlstone Manor, where Wandren HQ is located, they immediately proceed to the next event, @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.91Ck26XHcgMCo88E]{Not All Who Wandren}.
The Marlstone Gala.soverview: Lyla Cevher and the party infiltrate the Marlstone Gala, one of Ordain's preeminent social events, to rescue her missing brother Funar and steal a copy of Hephiss Wandren's magical keyring.
The Marlstone Gala.sexposition:
The gala is every bit as sparkling as Lyla claimed that it would be, filled with drinks and laughter and festive music. But you aren't here simply to enjoy the stories and atmosphere and company. You have a heist to pull off, and only the rest of the night to do it. As you make your way into the Great Hall, passing underneath the twinkling lights, Lyla walks toward you, a smile on her face.

Hephiss does know how to throw a party. Now all we have to do is take her keys, get Janix Mance to copy them, and find wherever she's managed to stash Funar. All while looking good, of course. Unfortunately, I'm not going to be as much help as I wanted to — with all the attention that House Cevher has gotten, lots of eyes are on me. But that hopefully gives you the space you need to pull off this heist.
The Marlstone Gala.ssummary: We used the cover of the Marlstone Gala to make our way through the Marlstone Manor, uncovering a secret entrance to a floor below the main manor. This must be where Funar is being held.

Aftermath.name: Aftermath
Aftermath.text:
Gamemaster's Guide

This brief social event gives the party the ability to recap after the events of the Marlstone Gala. This event may vary from party to party, but gives your party the opportunity to catch up after escaping the manor.

The Crew's Next Steps

Lyla's primary focus is in bringing the evidence she has gathered to the Ordinate. Other members of the crew also have plans, if they survived the events of the night intact. The party may speak with them here to figure out their next steps.

Lyla's Plans

Lyla is focused on bringing the evidence of what House Wandren has become to the Ordinate, but is happy to bask in what the group has accomplished and will mention the following:

  • House Wandren is in a bit of disarray after the death of Hephiss Wandren, but is pretending that everything is okay. It is still unclear who will take over going forward.

  • Lyla is going through all the information you all found during the heist and its lead-up. She believes she has enough to get House Wandren removed from the Ordinate and House Cevher restored.

  • If Yllith, the captive Tyraphem prisoner found in Wandren HQ, survived ([[/eventState otherhood2Wandren survived]]), they have left Ember, but promised to return with information about what Pyix might be planning.

  • With Funar's help, Lyla will be taking her father's old position as one of the leaders of House Cevher. It isn't the position she sought, but she thinks it will give her the opportunity to do some real good.

Funar's Plans

Funar is both grateful and embarrassed by everything that happened - he had a lot of time to think while in the holding cell under Wandren HQ and though he has always wanted to lead House Cevher, believes that Lyla has shown she has what it takes to be the leader of the House. He plans to help her bridge the gap between the more traditionalist members of the House and the flexibility that the current times call for.

Juro's Plans

Whether or not the party returned Juro's ledger to him, Hephiss Wandren's death means that he is safe from any of her manipulations. He has no desire to be the new head of House Wandren, but will be sticking around Ordain to try to make the house a respectable one again, if that is even possible.

  • If the party did return Juro's ledger, he is especially grateful and promises to lend the group a hand in the future if needed.

Janix's Plans

Janix enjoyed the challenge of key copying on the fly and is interested to see what else he can do with the replicating mold he developed to help the party. He welcomes them to visit him in his shop anytime if they need anything going forward - he's always happy to help.

Concluding The Event

Next Steps

This scene ends the current arc of Lyla and House Cevher focused series of quests. The next section of this quest will begin when Lyla is ready to bring her evidence to the Ordinate.
Aftermath.soverview: The party regroups with Lyla Cehver in her office to plot their next moves.
Aftermath.sexposition:
It hasn't been long since the Marlstone Gala, but already the rumors about what happened at the event have begun to filter through the streets. As you walk from Quarry Run into Lyla Cevher's office, House Cevher appears to be abuzz with new activity and a fair amount of relief. The house may be under siege, but at least it has begun to clear its name. Lyla, though, does not appear to be resting on her laurels. She has even more papers on her desk than before, several of which have the word Wandren written somewhere on them.

I know what you're thinking. I should probably enjoy the success of the night. But what we saw of House Wandren? It has to be stopped. And I'm the one to stop it.
Aftermath.ssummary: With the gala behind us, we gathered with our team once again. Despite all that we uncovered, the future for House Cevher is still hazy and we have much to learn about the broader plan that the celestial creatures we glimpsed might want with House Cevher, Ordain, or Ember.

The Insider.name: The Insider
The Insider.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social and exploration event, the party must recruit Juro Wandren to be part of Lyla's heist plan. Juro is amenable to putting the party on the Marlstone Gala guest list, but first the party must:

  • Complete a challenge in the Hallows that shows either their stealth, persuasion, or political skills in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.y76bbpKFTkrAgm8j#juros-challenge]{Juro's Challenge}.

  • Either agree to Juro's demand to recover an item that he believes is stashed within Marlstone Manor, or convince him that they will in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.y76bbpKFTkrAgm8j#a-final-request]{A Final Request}.

A Meeting WIth Juro

The party has seen Juro during his visit to Lyla's office, but may have also have met him in the past, depending on their choices in Chapter 1. If they completed [[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]] and met him during the event, he greets them warmly:

Juro smiles as you approach with a look of recognition.

Lyla's friends, of course. I'm glad you made it safely to Ordain. Something tells me you're looking for another favor, but Lyla's note wasn't fully clear. What's going on?

If he has only met them in this quest, he is kind, if more distant:

Juro looks at you appraisingly as you approach.

From the descriptions that she gave, you must be Lyla's companions. Her note wasn't fully clear about what you need from me. What's going on?

Sharing The Plan

The party's goal, as set by Lyla, should be to get Juro to add them to the guest list of the Marlstone Gala. Once they make that ask, he conditionally agrees to the plan if they meet his demands in@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.y76bbpKFTkrAgm8j#juros-challenge]{Juro's Challenge}.

With a successful [[/check insight 16]] check, characters sense that Juro is more amused by their questions than anything, but there is some worry below the surface. They also know that his affection for Lyla will keep him from betraying her.

  • Juro is visiting Ordain on the request of Hephiss Wandren, who has asked several questions about his meetings with Lyla before she arrived in the city.

    • If the party did not complete [[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]]: He and Lyla briefly crossed paths in Nain.

  • The Marlstone Gala is a big deal - a place to see and be seen - but also a bit boring. Juro would love something exciting to happen there.

  • Juro and Lyla have a complicated relationship, but they go back for years and he'll always have her back. He doesn't elaborate on what happened in their past, focusing instead on the here and now.

  • Lyla's heist plan sounds like fun, and adding to the party to the guest list should be easy enough. Usually Hephiss approves of each guest to the gala, but she's been distracted recently.

  • If asked, Juro's worries have to do with recent changes in House Wandren. He doesn't want to speak much about it, but with a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] check, will reveal that a lot of Wandren seems on edge and most of the associates he would normally ask are out of town with no sign of returning soon.

If the party does not ask Juro about being added to the guest list, or you want to cut the conversation short, he can mention it unprompted.

Is that everything? Lyla's note wasn't 100% clear, but it seemed like it might have something to do with the Marlstone Gala.

What Brings Juro to Ordain - ([[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]]) Completed

Hephiss Wandren suddenly requested my presence not long after you all left me in Nain. She claims she's taking an interest in the next generation of House Wandren, I know a fishing expedition when I see one — something Lyla found during her travels has got Hephiss more than a little on edge.

What Brings Juro to Ordain - ([[/eventState otherhood1Smuggler]]) Not Completed

Ah, Lyla told you I'm not a big fan of the big city? I don't mind it too much, but I prefer the Plateau, where no one's keeping much of an eye on what I'm doing. The only reason I'm even in Ordain is that Hephiss Wandren suddenly requested my presence after I crossed paths with Lyla - she was tracking down information on the Helkas bandits in Nain and I gave her a hand with some very official-looking papers. I'll say this, Hephiss asked a lot more questions about Lyla than my business dealings. I'm not sure why, but I think she's more than a little spooked.

The Marlstone Gala

The Marlstone Gala is basically the event of the year in Ordain if you care about fashion and power. Or at least that's what people say. There are plenty of stories about deals beinng made and people making themselves known, but to be honest, nothing really big has happened there for years. The fashion is great, but every year I hope there's a screaming match or a construct gets loose or someone throws a drink.

Relationship with Lyla

Lyla and I go way back, but I'll let her tell those stories. Though she probably won't give me enough credit. Sure, I was a bit of a fool in my younger years, but honestly - break a few rules and some folks never look at you the same way again . I'll say this, though - then and now, I've always got her back. Always.

Lyla's Heist Plan

Lyla always was good at coming up with something. The plan seems like it'll work — as long as I don't tell Hephiss, that is. Don't worry, the secret's safe with me. I'd choose Lyla over most folks in the city, and with Hephiss as the other option…she's not exactly on my good side at the moment. As for adding your names, that's easy enough. We'll just call you the Heroes of Helkas. No one knows exactly what happened there, so no one will ask any questions, and Hephiss is too distracted to care.

Relationship with Hephiss Wandren

Hephiss and I have generally gotten along in the past, but all these questions she has about what I've done and what I know about Lyla? I don't like it. Not to mention —

Juro appears to consider saying more, but stops himself.

Meet my challenge and I'll tell you all about it.

Juro's Worries

Folks in House Wandren have a tendency to come and go a bit, but right now more are gone than most. Something about it seems wrong. I wonder if it has anything to do with the way Hephiss has been acting…but we can talk more about that after I make sure you're up to snuff.

Juro's Challenge

Juro is willing to work with the party, if they can prove that they are actually up to the task.

Juro smiles and gives you a single sharp nod.

Before I put you on the guest list, I want to make sure you'll be able to pull this off. After all, if things go wrong, my name's going to be on the line. I'll even give you two options - heist something very small or show me you can fit in among the high society types.

The Smallest Heist

Juro explains what he wants done.

A small heist. Of course, this should be easy for you. Much easier than what you have planned for the gala. All I want is for you to get me a free piece of fruit from that stand right there. Up to you how you do it, I only care that you do it.

Parties can:

  • Steal an item. With a successful [[/check stealth 17]] check, a party member can get close to the stand without being seen. They gain an advantage on the check to steal. With a successful [[/check sleightofhand 17]] check, the party successfully takes the item. If they fail on the check, they are caught, and have disadvantage on any check to convince the shopkeeper to let them have the item.

  • Convince the shopkeeper. With a successful [[/check nature 16]] check or [[/knowledge trade]], a member of the party knows a bit about the type of fruit that is for sale, and has advantage on the check to persuade the shopkeeper to give it up. With a successful [[/check persuasion 16]] or [[/check intimidation 16]] check, the party receives the item.

  • Fool Juro. If the party wishes, they can buy the item, but attempt to convince Juro that they got it for free. They'll have to be sneaky in buying the goods, using a [[/check stealth 17]] check, and succeed on a [[/check deception 16]] check to speak convincingly to Juro about it.

Standing Out In The Crowd

Juro explains the challenge, which uses three movable NPCs within the scene: Hallows Passersby A, B, and C.

Fitting in the crowd can be a hard thing, but it helps if you know who should be in the crowd to begin with. See that gentlemen in the green wrap eating a handheld bun, the spellcaster with the staff in the red robes, and the woman in gray looking at the vases? One of them will absolutely be at the gala, and other two would never make it past the door. Tell me who gets in and the challenge is won.

If the party is at a loss, they can ask Juro for help. With a successful [[/check persuasion 15]] check, he will agree to give them one hint about each.

The party can observe the following about each:

The Gentleman in Green

Juro's hint: "Remember, at the gala, it's all starts with the outfit."

  • With a [[/check 16 perception]] check, characters can see that the detailing on the cloak is intricate, but there are a few small spots of dirt and plant material. With a successful [[/check investigation 15]] check, characters know that the dirt and plants suggest recent travel.

  • With a successful [[/check history 16]] or [[/knowledge arts]] they know that the design of the cloak is Arcturian, not Ordani, suggesting a visitor from the Arctus Plateau.

It is unlikely they have the power or influence to be invited to the gala.

The Gesturing Wizard

Juro's hint: "Some outfits are less about how they look than what they represent"

  • Without a successful [[/check arcana 16]] check or [[/check religion 16]] check, the party recognizes the distinctive robe or staff of a member of the Cindaric Sages, a local religious group that does good works throughout the city.

  • With a successful [[/check investigation 16]] check, or [[/knowledge arts]], they know that while the robes look lovely, they're older and don't fit quite perfectly — they may have been handed down from another member of the order.

It's likely that they are a local initiate of the sages, not someone getting ready to go to a gala.

The Woman by the Pottery Stand

Juro's hint: "The clothing is important, but it's not just the look - it's also the materials. Any ideas what hers might be whispering?"

  • With a successful [[/check history 15]] check or [[/knowledge arts]], characters know that the woman is wearing current Ordani fashion.

  • Her outfit includes some silken, leather, and metal accessories - character with [[/knowledge trade]] or who has proficiency with tools related to one of these items (@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulSmithsTool]{Smith's Tools,} @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulLeatherwor]{Leatherworker's Tools,} @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulWeaversToo]{Weaver's Tools}) can identify them as high-end materials.

  • Those who succeed on a [[/check investigation 16]] check can see that her leather belt is embossed with a symbol. Anyone from Ordain, succeeds on a [[/check 14 history]] check, or has [[/knowledge trade]] can identify the symbol as one common in Trading House Bastilla.

The woman is an Ordani of some wealth who is affiliated with a Trading House, and thus likely invited to the gala. If the party successfully identifies her, Juro is impressed.

The party only needs to complete one of Juro's challenges in order to move forward. Once they do, he agrees to participate in the heist if they promise to help him with one small favor (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.y76bbpKFTkrAgm8j#a-final-request]{A Final Request}).

Juro smiles and nods at you, looking genuinely pleased at your success

I had a feeling you could do it. Consider yourselves invited to the gala. That is, if you me a favor.

Primordis Attunement: Fruit Stolen

If the party manages to successfully steal the fruit for Juro, each character who participates advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 otherhood2InsiderStolen]] at the conclusion of the event.

Luxarum Attunement: Shopkeeper Convinced

If the party manages to convince the shopkeeper to give them the fruit, each character who participates advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 otherhood2InsiderConvinced]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aura Attunement: Juro Fooled

If the party manages to fool Juro into helping them, each character who participates advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 otherhood2InsiderFooled]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome recruited]]

If the party fails one challenge, they may attempt the other. If they fail both challenges, Juro won't add them to the list…unless they promise to do him a favor, without telling Lyla(@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.y76bbpKFTkrAgm8j#a-final-request]{A Final Request}).

Juro shakes his head wryly.

This isn't the Arctus Plateau anymore - you have to be a lot more subtle here in Ordain. And if I vouch for you, it'll be me that Hephiss comes for if you get caught. I'm sure you can find your own way into the gala, and I promise if you do, I won't blow your cover. Unless, that is, you'd be up for doing me a favor?

A Final Request

Juro's Ledger

Whether or not he trusts the party, Juro has one last ask - there is a ledger of his activities that Hephiss Wandren is "holding" for him and he wants it back, especially if Hephiss might end up being implicated in some crime.

If I'm going to put you on this guest list, I need something from you in return. Hephiss took my ledger from me when I got into town — it has all of my contacts and records in it, including some that the Hallows would probably frown at. She says it's for safekeeping, but I think it's to keep me in line. I need you to find where it is, take it, and bring it back to me. And don't tell Lyla, please. I don't want her worrying about it - or me.

Juro will not put the party on the guestlist without this promise, but they can lie to him about their intentions with a successful [[/check deception 16]] check. Parties that succeeded on one his tests have advantage on this check. On a successful [[/check insight 15]] check, they can confirm that he appears to be telling the truth, though he may be underplaying the value of what is in the ledger.

If the party refuses to help Juro, or is unsuccessful in lying to him, he refuses to help, though he promises not to expose them if they make their own way to the gala.

[[/outcome refused]]

Concluding The Event

Next Steps

If the party has not yet completed all of the preparation events below, they can proceed to any incomplete event to continue with this phase of preparation.

  • Found a hidden route through @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls]{Lantern Roads} into Marlstone Manor [[/eventState otherhood2Lantern]]

  • Recruited Janix Mance in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.dNI3A44TwJO1kevp]{Stonework Hollow} in [[/eventState otherhood2Key]]

  • Spoken to Juro Wandren in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.ThsrAwMhXhmowirO]{The Hallows} in [[/eventState otherhood2Insider]]

  • Scouted the Marlstone Manor in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.uVodk7tLiG3pZMTq]{Marlstone} in [[/eventState otherhood2Casing]]

Once all of the above have been completed, they should proceed to the House Cevher Tradeway in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.D0AAT8TNsytqy7Hm]{Quarry Run} to prepare for the ball in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.hUIBGXTjsQrrD1e1]{Set In Motion}.
The Insider.soverview: With only Lyla's invitation to the gala secured, the party meets with Juro Wandren to get on the guest list. He's willing to help, but only if the party proves their mettle and promises to takes something from the Marlstone Manor for him in return.
The Insider.sexposition: The Hallows, as always, is bustling with activity - some buying, some selling, some relaxing, and some simply passing through. Juro Wandren is in the middle of the crowd, surveying some of the wares that are being displayed in the center of the walkway, but looks up as you approach, beckoning you over.
The Insider.ssummary: We met with Lyla's old acquaintance Juro Wandren to persuade him to add us to the guest list of the Marlstone Gala. Never one to do something for nothing, he put us through our paces, asking us to prove that we'd fit in once we were at the gala and promise to retrieve a ledger from a safe hidden somewhere in the house.

Family Business.name: Family Business
Family Business.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event,@UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{ Lyla} meets with the party in the House Cevher Tradeway in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.D0AAT8TNsytqy7Hm]{Quarry Run} in the wake of the trading house's fall from grace. The party can:

  • Learn about the House Cevher 's current state of affairs from Lyla - her uncle was murdered, her brother is the prime suspect, and the other trading houses have seized the opportunity to remove House Cevher from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.ZR5KWPkEpxPchi53]{Ordinate}, leaving Lyla unsure of who to trust.

  • Agree to help Lyla by finding her brother Funar's current location in Ordain and investigating her uncle Darius' death at his shop in Gossamer.

@Embed[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP readaloud="Lyla retains her noble bearing, but appears deep in thought as she stands in the center of the room, foot tapping idly against the ground. There is a sadness in her eyes, but also a sense of determination."]

As you enter the room, Lyla looks up and smiles, though the expression quickly dissipates into one of steely determination.

Thank you for coming. Unless you've been absolutely ignoring the news, I assume you know the state of things? My poor uncle killed, my brother being blamed and nowhere around to defend himself, and House Cevher taken out of its seat on the Ordinate based on rumors and lies. To think that anyone would kill a man who only wanted to make beautiful things over what's probably some political dispute? I keep thinking - if only I'd gotten here sooner to stop it somehow. But I can't change the past.

What to do going forward, on the other hand? That I have a pretty good handle on.

The Current Situation

Lyla's Losses

Lyla is devastated at what she has lost, but that sadness is being covered with determination. A successful [[/check insight 16]] check reveals that she is taking action to keep herself from despair. Any talk of her emotions is quickly replaced with her thoughts on what she can do about the situation.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge politics]] , or who succeed on a [[/check history 16]] check know that the most likely culprit for this kind of action is one of the trading houses. Lyla doesn't want to believe they would be capable of it, but agrees.

Darius' Murder

I can't believe Uncle Darius is gone. He cared much more about making cloth than anything having to do with house politics, and yet I'm afraid that his murder is all about Cevher and not about him. How could it be? He was such a kind man. Nobody would want to harm him.

Funar's Disappearance

Everyone - and by everyone I mean the other Trading Houses - are spreading lies about my brother, who wouldn't hurt a fly. I know he's still in the city…we each wear an earring that gives us a sense of how far apart we are…and the fact that he hasn't reached out must mean that someone's got him. I need to find him and save him from whatever's going on. That's why I need your help.

The Removal of House Cevher from the Ordinate

I'm not sure who was behind House Cevher losing the Ordinate seat. House Bastilla holds the seat now, and they certainly aren't afraid to break the rules. But according to what I've heard, the deciding votes were from House Wandren and House Lilifeld. Ultimately, I'm not sure I can trust any of them. Whoever is behind it, we need to figure this out on our own. That is, if you'll help me.

Likely Culprits (requires [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/check history 16]])

I grew up alongside the members of other trading houses — I would hate to think that one of them could be behind this. But you're right. Who else could it be? They seem to be the only ones who truly benefit.

A Call To Action

Lyla's Ask

Lyla is determined to fix things for her family and asks the party for their help to find Funar and solve the murder.

Darius' Murder

Lyla gives the party an article containing the popular understanding of how Darius was murdered, which happened in his shop in the Gossamer district, Threadforge -@UUID[Item.nCdyFX3dY14CFRpA]{Overheard In Ordain: A Stitch In Crime}. According to her sources, the investigation has stalled and the shop is still closed up. She suggests that they investigate themselves and see if they can find any information that the investigators either missed or have yet to discover.

Finding Funar

Lyla wears an earring attuned to an identical one worn by Funar. While it doesn't give her his exact location, he must be within 20 miles of her current location, which includes most of Ordain. She has used her earring to create a @UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{Locator Rod }that should be able to track him more closely, but it only has 10 charges - once all are gone, the party must return to Lyla to recharge it. Once it's within 200 feet of him, the jewel on the Locator Rod will switch colors.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge politics]], or who previously identified the trading houses as possibly causes of House Cevher's troubles, have the sense that Funar Cevher is being kept alive near one of the trading house centers. Lyla agrees and names a few of the major trading house districts:

    • House Lilifeld:@UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.s7O0qBepuI89HKUU]{Lilifeld Station}

    • House Bastilla: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.BzNFGWAEOwRwrQDp]{Coinwealth Heights}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.OGwqwpjpXueYnloV]{Ember's Bounty}

    • House Wandren: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.uVodk7tLiG3pZMTq]{Marlstone}

    • House Salva: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.FhanWf8srQnOOAud]{Gossamer}

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]], or who succeed on a [[/check history 16]] check, can identify districts in Ordain that might be good for hiding people away. If asked, Lyla agrees with the list as possible starting places:

    • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.giaDQErIafhgueop]{Fallbrook} - known for its underground tunnels

    • @UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls]{Lantern Roads} - has extensive back alleys

    • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yiPc8r3jvLlp3PJf]{The Harborage} - used to move goods to and from the docks, including late at night

Locating Funar

As I said, I know that Funar is in the city because of my earring. I've used that to create this Locator Rod, which you can activate to send you in the right general direction. See how the jewel in the center is gray? That means Funar is somewhere in the city, but nowhere nearby. The rod will pull you in towards Funar each time you use it, and when you're within 200 feet or so, the stone will turn to blue — Funar's favorite color.

Would you mind moving around the city and seeing what you can find? If you run out of charges, just bring it to me and I can use my earring to recharge it. I'd join you, but I need to spend some time on Trading House affairs - right now, I seem to be the only one holding the Trading House together.

Solving Darius' Murder

Darius' shop was locked up tight by the Veiled Chain, who claim to be investigating it, but it's clear they've put it on the back burner. I'm convinced there's evidence they're overlooking about the case, if they've even looked at all. Could you go in and investigate on your own? If I do it, they'll assume I'm biased, but anything that you find, we can follow up with. Rumors are flying in the meantime - this ridiculous article gives a good rundown of the general "facts" that everyone is talking about.

Restoring House Cevher

Helping Funar and avenging Darius are important, but I'm responsible for more than just myself. I care about the house as a whole. And this isn't an isolated incident. There have been several strikes against House Cevher recently. We need to figure out who it is and stop their plans. But only after Funar is safe and we've struck back against whoever killed Darius.

Where to Start (requires [[/knowledge politics]])

If a trading house is behind this, Funar might be around one of the their stronghold districts. House Lillifeld has Lillifeld Stations, Wandren is in Marlstone, Bastilla has Coinwealth Heights and Ember's Bounty, and Salva dominates Gossamer, where Darius was murdered. I'd definitely start with one of those.

Where Else to Start (requires [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/check history 16]])

There are definitely some districts that would be easier for whisking someone away — or hiding them — Fallbrook has all those underground clubs, Lantern Roads is known for its alleys and tunnels, and there are always ships coming to and fro at the Harborage moving boxes.

Concluding The Event

With her conversation with the group finished, Lyla turns back to her work, asking the party to fill her in when they know something new.

Next Steps

The party can either:

  • Head to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.FhanWf8srQnOOAud]{Gossamer} District to investigate Darius' death at his shop Threadforge in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.YBxOyEZ4eN4jEobu]{The Death of Darius}

  • Attempt to narrow down Funar's current location by moving through the city using the Locator Rod (details on running this search in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.LIQ5fMBwNgnnIFLA]{Searching for Funar}. Once they have located him in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.uVodk7tLiG3pZMTq]{Marlstone} district, the event @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.7sf7FVZyd5yoWmYM]{Finding Funar} begins.
Family Business.soverview: Lyla asks the party for their help finding her missing brother Funar and clearing his name in the death of her uncle Darius.
Family Business.sexposition:
Precisely chiseled blocks of white stone extend from floor to ceiling along the long open walkway that runs through the center of House Cevher's Headquarters, connecting hallways that echo with activity — down one, you can hear the clanging of metal on metal, and down another, the heavy footsteps of a group deep in conversation.

Though you were welcomed warmly at the gate and directed to the office Lyla is using as her own, the place seems consumed by worry and gossip, even in the middle of a trade day. Here and there, members of the trading house cross the hallway in front of you, but no one seems in the mood for conversation, and you hear the names Funar and Lyla more than once, echoing from around corners in hushed whispers.
Family Business.ssummary:
We met with Lyla Cevher, who believes that her brother Funar is being framed for her uncle's murder. Though Funar has disappeared, making him an easy scapegoat for the crime, Lyla is convinced that whoever murdered Darius also kidnapped her brother in order to pin the crime on him.

Lyla asked us to track down Funar's current whereabouts in the city using a Locator Rod attuned to a piece of jewelry he never goes without and to do our own investigation into Darius' murder at the scene of the crime — Darius' shop Threadforge in Ordain's Gossamer District.

Veiled Threats.name: Veiled Threats
Veiled Threats.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social and exploration event, Lyla and the party go over what they found at Darius Cevher's shop. As they begin to come to some conclusions about who is responsible, Hephiss Wandren appears. Lyla asks for the party's help in figuring out what the true purpose of the visit is, asking them to hide and listen in. As they do, the characters can:

  • Stay hidden to be able to observe Hephiss' actions during the conversation.

  • Notice the sound of Hephiss' elaborate key ring, which inspires Lyla's idea for a heist.

  • Share their observations with Lyla, who uses them to come up with a plan to expose Hephiss and get her brother back.

Putting the Clues Together

Sharing the Clues

Lyla generally believes that what the party has found is promising, and has her own thoughts to share about the information.

  • Money was scattered across the desk.

    The rumors say that Funar killed Darius for his money. If money was left behind, that helps to prove his innocence - and it means that this wasn't a random robbery.

  • The killers used a special dust to choke Darius.

    Dust? That sounds familiar. I've been hearing that a new local group has begun using dust as a way to incapacitate people - Beacon, I think they're called. I can ask around, find out more.

  • Darius was stabbed twice, in the back and then in the chest.

    Stabbed in the back. Of course. Cowards. But that helps prove Funar's innocence - if Darius was fighting with Funar the way everyone claims, he wouldn't have turned his back on Funar.

  • There was a withering poison on the knife blade.

    A withering necrotic poison. You don't see that every day. I can ask around, find out who's been using that method in any other crimes.

  • The body was likely moved from where it fell. A blood pool in the center of the room is far from where the outline of the body is located.

    Someone is trying to frame Funar. Plain as day. And whoever it is, they aren't getting away with it.

As the party finishes this conversation, a messenger enters the room.

No sooner have you finished talking than a messenger appears, sweaty and out of breath.

Lyla, you have visitors. Including the head of House Wandren, Hephiss. They're only a minute or two behind me. Thought you'd want to know.

An Unexpected Guest

An Incoming Visitor

Though there isn't much time, Lyla quickly updates the party - the head of House Wandren is Hephiss Wandren, a powerful force in the city of Ordain. Lyla can share the following:

  • It's not clear why Hephiss Wandren is visiting. She could be coming to pay her condolences, but she was never particularly close with Darius Cevher. It seems like a ruse.

  • If the party found Funar's location ([[/eventState otherhood2FindingFunar clue1Funar]]), Lyla is especially concerned about what Hephiss' intentions might be, and thinks that Hephiss knows exactly where Funar is and will be trying to throw her off.

  • Lyla doesn't know Hephiss well - Lyla was once close friends with Juro Wandren, who also belongs to House Wandren, but Juro had a somewhat distant relationship with Hephiss. She and Juro are on decent terms now, but she doesn’t quite trust him or House Wandren.

  • There are rumors that since Hephiss gained control of the house, it has become more secretive, secluded, and dangerous.

Lyla would like the party to hide in the room behind a dividing screen. out of sight, and see what they think of Hephiss during the meeting, so she doesn't miss anything.

Vista Composition

The vista composition can be swapped to "House Cevher HQ (hiding)" if the party chooses to hide.

Lyla quickly hurries to the door to peer down the hall, hand on her sword hilt. As she stares out, she takes her hand down and straightens her back instead.

Here she comes. You should be able to avoid her knowing you're here as long as you don't make too much noise behind that folding screen. If she figures it out, she'll leave without sharing any good information.

Just as Lyla opens the folding screen and ushers the party behind it, two people appear at the doorway of Lyla's office — Hephiss and Juro Wandren.

@Embed[Actor.OOO380zs3xZYG9PI]{Hephiss Wandren}

@Embed[Actor.BuOnSzuKysdVLzwz]{Juro Wandren}

During Hephiss Wandren's conversation with Lyla, the party can take the following actions, as desired, but must remain out of sight throughout Hephiss' visit:

Determine Hephiss and Juro's Motives

Characters who wish to learn more about Hephiss or Juro's motives can:

  • Observe Juro and Hephiss through the screen by succeeding on a [[/check stealth 18]] check to get close enough to the screen to peer through the gaps.

    • Any characters who succeeds, and who has [[/check 18 perception passive]] or succeeds on a [[/check 16 perception] check sees Hephiss attempting to hide or downplay a set of keys that she wears on her wrist.

  • Make a [[/check insight 20]] check on the character they targeted at any point during the conversation to get a better sense of what the character is truly thinking. Any character with [[/knowledge intrigue]] has advantage on this check. Hephiss and Juro's true thoughts are noted within @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.zSpPVloL1lGDom9T#the-conversation-begins]{The Conversation Begins} below.

During the conversation, at the GM's discretion, or if a stealth check is failed, Hephiss may hear a sound from behind the screen, telling Lyla that she wants to know what is behind the screen. Any character who is currently looking through the screen must make a [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw to avoid being detected. If they fail, they have the following recourses:

  • Lyla can dissuade Hephiss from investigating further by dismissing her concerns. This only works once.

  • The party can redirect Hephiss' attention by creating a distraction (see Create a Distraction below). This can work more than once but risks the party's overall chance of discovery.

  • If Hephiss is not dissuaded or distracted, she discovers the party and ends the conversation (see Party Discovered) below.

Create a Distraction

If the party is at risk of being discovered, or wishes to end a line of conversation, they can cause a distraction. This can be accomplished as the party sees fit, including:

  • Use of Mage Hand, Prestidigitation, or another spell with a visual or auditory effect.

  • Sliding an object across the room from under the screen. Characters must succeed on a [[/check athletics 16]] check to slide it far enough that it draws Hephiss' attention away from the screen — on a failure, the object draws Hephiss' attention instead and any character who is currently observing her must make a [[/check stealth 16]] check to maintain their position. If they fail, Hephiss notices as if the initial stealth check had been missed.

Primordis Attunement: Party Hidden

If the party remains hidden throughout the conversation between Hephiss and Juro, each character advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 otherhood2ThreatsHidden]] at the conclusion of the event.

Party Discovered

Hephiss Wandren is uninterested in having her conversation with unexpected guests listening in. If the party does not hide, she sees any member, or their actions bring them to her attention, she immediately ends the conversation and leaves, saying:

I'm sorry, I came for a private conversation. Just you, me, and your old friend here. I can see you're busy, though, and I'd hate to think of uninformed ears listening to what we have to say. Please accept my condolences, and if you're up for it, I'd welcome you to attend the Marlstone Gala. Alone, of course. It's at my home, and I can't let just anyone through my doors.

Abyss Attunement: Party Discovered

If the party is discovered by Hephiss during the course of the conversation, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 otherhood2ThreatsDiscovered]] at the conclusion of the event.

The Conversation Begins

As Hephiss and Juro enter her office, Lyla greets them politely.

Hephiss Wandren. And Juro. Fancy seeing you here. To what do I owe the pleasure?

Condolences and Invitations

Hephiss begins by extending her condolences to Lyla. A successful [[/check insight 17]] check while within range reveals that she seems irritated at Darius Cevher's death, as if she wanted it to yield more than it did.

First, I apologize for not having reached out to you sooner, but I wanted to extend the deepest condolences of all of House Wandren on the lost off your uncle Darius. I have always been a fan of his work with threads and metals, and I regret that he will be unable to make this year's Marlstone Gala, where we always look forward to seeing his work. You are of course welcome to come in his stead. As long as you promise not to stab anyone.

Juro adds his sympathies. On a successful insight check within range, characters know that he is indeed sorry for Lyla's loss.

Yeah, Ly, I'm sorry. Darius was a good guy. Whoever did this, it can't have had anything to do with the kindness of his heart.

Hephiss sighs. (A successful insight check reveals that Hephiss is trying to get Lyla upset on purpose, possibly to learn something, though it is not clear what.)

Yes, who knows what would have motivated Lyla's brother Funar to become a killer. I never would have thought he could have done such a thing, but with him on the run, it's clear that his guilt must have gotten the better of him. I hope you know that the removal of House Cevher from the Ordinate is likely only temporary, to give you a chance to recuperate from this time of tragedy. Though House Bastilla is filling the seat admirably.

After a silence, Lyla replies.

How thoughtful of you to make that determination for us instead of burdening us with the decision.

Lyla then coughs, taking the opportunity to whisper to the party.

I'm ready for this conversation to be over, but is there anything you think I should ask?

Additional Questions

If the party has any topics that they want to be discussed, they can attempt to whisper Lyla to continue the conversation along those lines. Characters can do this by using a spell that allows for information to be communicated non-verbally or physically passing a note to Lyla without Hephiss noticing (requiring a [[/check 19 stealth]] to succeed). Alternatively, they let the conversation end naturally. Topics could include:

  • Why is Hephiss Wandren here now? Hephiss insists that she simply wants to pay her condolences, but has been busy with internal house business and did not want to disturb Lyla right away while she was grieving. An insight check reveals that she came when she felt it was strategically important. Juro also seems skeptical of her answer.

  • Why is Juro accompanying Hephiss? Juro just got to town and wanted to meet up with Lyla right away to give his condolences. An insight check reveals that this is true, but also that he was forced to come on this particular trip. Hephiss has some leverage on him.

  • Why are they accusing Funar of Darius' death? Hephiss claims not to know much about the situation - she says she's gotten her information from the local paper Overheard in Ordain, which has a source within the investigation. An insight check reveals that she is lying — it's more likely that she is the paper's source of information than the other way around, and she definitely knows more about where Funar is.

  • When will House Cevher be returned to the Ordinate? Hephiss reiterates that House Cevher was removed to avoid them having to deal with politics during a tragedy and claims that making another change too quickly would cause dissension during a time when stability is needed. An insight check makes it clear she never plans for House Cevher to return to the Ordinate.

  • If the party has located Funar (([[/eventState otherhood2FindingFunar clue1Funar]]), what does she know about Funar's current whereabouts? Hephiss seems surprised at the question — she claims to believe that he ran away from Ordain because of the shame of killing his uncle. While answering the question, she fidgets, briefly exposing a ring of keys on a bracelet that is normally hidden by her sleeves. An insight check reveals worry that Lyla knows more than she should.

Full answer text is below.

Once characters have no more questions for Lyla to ask or actions they wish to take, she wraps up the conversation.

Thank you for your kind words, but I do need to deal with a good deal of House business, Hephiss. You understand. Thank you again for coming by!

Why is Hephiss here?

I am sorry it has taken me so long to reach out to you. I wanted to give you time with your family before burdening you with an additional guest.

Why is Juro here?

Nothing more than a coincidence. I happened to run into him while heading in this direction and thought you might be interested in seeing a familiar face.

Accusations of Funar

I've always liked Funar, though he's never said much to me. I wouldn't suspect him at all, but with his disappearance and the evidence that's been shared in Overhead in Ordain, it seems clear he did it. I take no comfort in this fact, but I think it is good to face it head on.

Returning Cevher to the Ordinate

Let's give it some time. Your father understood how things worked in the Ordinate, but without him, and with Funar on the run, we thought it might be best to give the House a bit of a chance to recover. In truth, from what I've heard about the troubles on the Arctus Plateau, you may have your hands full. I wish you all the best with it, of course.

Funar's Whereabouts

What an odd question. I have no idea, though I had heard he'd fled the city. Probably guilty from what he'd done. I'm so sorry Lyla - I hope you don't feel too guilty that he changed while you were away. How could you know that going off to do your own thing would lead to you coming back to two deaths in the family?

Debriefing With Lyla

A Brief Debrief

With Hephiss and Juro's departure, Lyla is ready to debrief.

They're gone. That was…unpleasant, though I'm not sure Juro's heart was fully in it. Also, did you notice what was going on with Hephiss' wrist? I think she has a set of keys on there. If she has Funar trapped somewhere in Marlstone, we'll have to get a hold of them.

If the party succeeded on any insight checks, they can share the results with Lyla, which confirm what she suspected - even if she didn't do it herself, Hephiss Wandren is involved in what happened to Darius.

  • Given the evidence that the party found in Darius' shop, Lyla that a group in Lantern Roads, the Beacon Brigade, was responsible for Darius' death. They favor poisons, dusts, and other items in their work, which lines up with the evidence the party found. The group is also loosely associated with House Wandren, which now makes Lyla fairly sure they're the ones responsible.

  • If the party did not locate Funar in [[/eventState otherhood2FindingFunar clue2Funar]], Hephiss' appearance at Cevher HQ has convinced Lyla that he is somewhere in the mansion. She recharges the@UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{Locator Rod} and asks the party to hold onto it for the right moment.

Lyla's Plan

Music: Lyla's Theme

As Lyla reveals her plan, play [[/soundscape music lylaTheme lylaTheme]].

The Heist in a Nutshell

The invitation to the Marlstone Gala that Hephiss brought with her has given Lyla an idea - the gala is the perfect place to search for Funar's exact location in the manor and get Hephiss' keys from her while she's distracted. Her plan has two phases — preparation and execution — each of which will need the party's help.

I think Hephiss just overplayed her hand. That invitation to the Marlstone Gala? I'm sure she just wants to rub my new circumstances in my face, but I think it's the perfect time to turn the tables on her. Why not use it to search the place, take her keys, and sneak off with Funar?

A [[/check insight 15]] check reveals that Lyla is slightly nervous, but overwhelmingly convinced that she can pull it off with the party's help. With a success of 2 or more, it is clear that she will make an attempt to do this with or without the party, but is much less confident of being able to do it on her own.

The overarching plan works as follows:

  • The party attends the Marlstone Gala, sneaking a renowned artificer onto the grounds on their way into the event. Lyla is sure that Hephiss' keys won't be easily copied, but the artificer, Janix Mance is an expert on magically warded keys.

  • Hephiss Wandren offered Lyla an invitation, but the party members will need to get their own invitations, convince the artificer to participate, and find a hidden way for the artificer to get in before the ball begins.

  • Once at the gala, the party creates a distraction and steals Hephiss Wandren's key, which they sneak to the artificer to copy for them. They then return the key to Hephiss Wandren with the House Wandren leader none the wiser.

  • The party leaves the event early and sneaks through the manor, where they find and release Funar Cevher, look for evidence of who truly killed Darius Cevher, and try to find evidence to clear House Cevher's name.

Lyla suggests they focus on what needs to be done before the day of the gala and can regroup just before the gala begins when they've gotten the early pieces in place.

In order to pull this off, we'll need to have everything in place before the Marlstone Gala begins. I have some work to do here, so I'm counting on you to recruit the rest of the team and do some scouting. You up for it?

Lyla asks that the party keep her informed via signal stone or coded message and meet her at House Cevher HQ on the night of the gala ready to go. She trusts they will get everything done in the meantime.

Recruiting Juro Wandren

As you know, Juro's not my favorite person in Ordain, but we go way back, and he still owes me one. Which he isn't going to want me to collect. I'd love if you could find a way to convince him that it'll be in his best interest to get you on the list for the Marlstone Gala. Juro seemed like he felt for me when he was here, but he's never given a favor without making a production out of it.

Recruiting Janix Mance

Janix Mance is the best artificer in Ordain, hands down. And he's got a pretty straightforward view on life - do something for him and he'll do something for you. My sources say he's been complaining about an infestation of some kind keeping him away from some of the materials he needs in the old quarry. I'd bet if you offer to take care of it, he'll be on board, and he'll know exactly how to copy Hephiss' keys.

Scout Marlstone Manor and Lantern Roads for a hidden way in.

Juro should be able to get all of us onto the guest list after your heroics elsewhere on the Arctus Plateau, but we'll have to sneak Janix in. Which means finding a good route in. I'm pretty sure there's a way to the Marlstone Manor through the back alleys of Lantern Roads that we can use the night of the event. If you can disrupt things for that horrible Beacon gang that killed Darius in the process, I'd love it.

It would also be good to get the layout of the manor itself so we know what we're up against. With all the party prep, my guess is that a lot of laborers are coming in and out. You may be able to use that to your advantage.

See if you can figure out the quickest way between the main gala floor and where Janix will be waiting, taking note of guard stations and the like. The more we know, the better off we'll be.

Concluding The Event

Next Steps

If the party chooses to proceed with the plan, they need to make the following preparations, which can be done in any order.

  • Recruiting Juro Wandren to gain easy entry into the Marlstone Gala in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.ThsrAwMhXhmowirO]{the Hallows} in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.y76bbpKFTkrAgm8j]{The Insider}

  • Recruiting Janix Mance, who can copy Hephiss' keys, in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.dNI3A44TwJO1kevp]{Stonework Hollow} in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.3f1UcZFeprts8D9L]{To Copy A Key}

  • Finding a hidden route through@UUID[JournalEntry.pUGB4qMJlbbVU6ls]{ Lantern Roads }into Marlstone Manor in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.ZPv1VeLAtINtz3gv]{Revealed by Lantern}

  • Scouting Marlstone Manor in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.uVodk7tLiG3pZMTq]{Marlstone} to figure out the lay of the land in @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY]{Casing the Joint}
Veiled Threats.soverview: Lyla gets an update from the party that points to House Wandren as the culprits in House Cevher's current troubles. An unexpected visit from the head of House Wandren gives the party a chance to eavesdrop…and Lyla the opportunity to come up with a plan.
Veiled Threats.sexposition:
As you wind your way through House Cevher's headquarters toward the office that Lyla has claimed as her own, the mood seems a little lighter. As far as you know, nothing has changed, but if the murmured conversations in the hallways and the hopeful smiles of some of the traders you pass in the hallls are any indication, your visit to Darius Cevher's shop hasn't gone unnoticed. As you make your way into Lyla's office, she looks up from her papers and nods in your direction.

Perfect. Your timing couldn't be better. I hear you've been to Threadforge — did you find anything to clear Funar in Darius' shop?
Veiled Threats.ssummary: After sharing what we found out about Darius Cevher's murder with Lyla, we eavesdropped on an unexpeted visit from the leader of House Wandren, Hephiss Wandren, who seemed to be checking up on what Lyla knows about Darius' death and Funar's disappearance. The incident helped Lyla figure out a plan of attack, which centers on the upcoming Marlstone Gala. She's asked us to take on a few tasks to prepare — scouting Marlstone Manor, finding a way through the adjacent Lantern Roads district, and recruiting some associates who can help make the plan a success.

Searching for Funar.name: Searching for Funar
Searching for Funar.text:
When to Use This Reference

In the @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1]{Disgraced House} quest event titled @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.SiKrlbgifaPCGobw]{Family Business}, Lyla Cevher asks the party to find the location of her brother, Funar Cevher, giving them a @UUID[Item.psLBUt4fyHfURaOC]{Locator Rod} attuned to the earring that he is wearing.

Characters may use the Locator Rod to search for him from any location on the Ordain region map, at any time, but will need to complete the search to trigger the event @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.7sf7FVZyd5yoWmYM]{Finding Funar} and proceed with the quest.

When characters use the Locator Rod to search, refer to the instructions below to direct them.

Using the Locator Rod

The Locator Rod has two modes — distance tracking and proximity tracking — and has 10 charges. When searching on the region map, it is set to distance tracking and its inset jewel is gray. Characters can use it with an action at any time, using one of the charges. Once all 10 charges have been used, they must return to Lyla so that she can recharge it.

Funar Cevher's Location

Funar is located in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.uVodk7tLiG3pZMTq]{Marlstone} (coordinates 3208.2905). Each time the party uses the Locator Rod, give them the name of the hex that brings them closest to Marlstone from their current location. After 10 tries, they must return to Lyla Cevher to recharge the item.

  • When the Locator Rod is activated, it indicates the general direction where Funar can be found.

  • Let the characters know which hex adjacent to their own is the closest to Funar ("the locator rod pulls you towards this hex adjoining Ordani district.") If the party is a fair bit away and multiple hexes seem equally adjacent, you may pick one using your best judgment or substitute a general direction ("the locator rod indicates that Funar is somewhere to the south")

When the party reaches Marlstone (the hex where Funar is located), the event @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.7sf7FVZyd5yoWmYM]{Finding Funar} triggers.

Further Use of the Locator Rod

When the party returns to Marlstone, either to scout the manor (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.Hg1HjuxWR7BzzXhY]{Casing the Joint}) or to attend the Gala (@UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1.JournalEntryPage.jalZUo8LGHwnn7B4]{The Marlstone Gala}), they move within 200 feet of Funar, activating the Locator Rod's proximity mode. The inset jewel turns to blue and the Locator Rod uses sounds to indicate how close the party is to Funar, as detailed in the item entry and those events.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This Main Quest occurs during Chapter 3 amidst the great city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, and is intended to begin when the party is approached by @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} during [[/eventState anachraenum1Acquaintance]]. Alternately, the party may begin the Quest via the [[/eventState anachraenum1Hall]] or [[/eventState anachraenum1Scholar]] Events.

Unlike the events of Chapter 2, each of the Chapter 3 Main Quests can occur simultaneously, although the characters must manage their time accordingly for various encounters and Events to proceed with certain measures of success.

Difficulty

"The Expedition Challenge" is designed for a party of Level 5 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Main Quest that awards 3 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon completion of the [[/eventState anachraenum1Concourse]], [[/eventState anachraenum1Gauntlet]], and [[/eventState anachraenum1Closing]] Events.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} hosted the first Expedition Challenge ten years ago, as a way to test new adventurers' skills but also to bring the city of Ordain together. The winner, @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa}, and her party became overnight celebrities, and their successes in the field after delving into an ancient skyhold the following year placed her in an interesting position among her fellow adventurers. Many began to view her as the natural successor to the current Guildmaster Veron Longspear, and she took on several responsibilities in All-Fable Keep. Her party, the Skywarders, disbanded, and Fernis began leaving the city more and more under the direct orders of the guildmaster. However, a year ago, Veron Longspear was killed under mysterious circumstances while Fernis was visiting the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.IOBQMGUigqxn3UkM]{Kithil} city of Luen. Upon her return, she was deeply concerned that something sinister was brewing in the city and that she could not fully trust other members of the Anachraenum. While the other members offered her the position of guildmaster, she ultimately refused, and the untested @UUID[Actor.FYprIclhoDOI8FI4]{Arcos Sarinland} took over in her place. Plans to host another Expedition Challenge are underway, and Fernis has begun formulating a plan to investigate and uncover the truth behind Veron's death and the growing troubles in the city.

This year's Expedition Challenge is expected to be a grand affair, challenging the mettle of various new adventuring parties and finding new blood for the ranks of the Anachraenum. The adventure challenge expedition consists of three smaller challenges that can be completed in any order, both within and outside the city, with the goal of acquiring a key from each. Once all three keys have been obtained, the party can undertake the final challenge: the dangerous and mysterious Chamber of Agaseros within All-Fable Keep itself.

The party will be pitted against other teams of adventurers that will appear periodically throughout the challenge to apply pressure on the party; however, they are not intended to be present during the completion of the challenges themselves. The winners of the Expedition Challenge are those who complete all three smaller challenges and reach the end of the Chamber of Agaseros in the fastest time. However, all parties are magically tracked by the Anachraenum guildmaster, Arcos Sarinland, and loremistress Adelyne Goss. No matter where a party places in the challenge, all are given the option to join the Anachraenum at the end, unless they repeatedly demonstrate that they are not Anachraenum material. All parties who finish the challenge will be given the choice of a gold reward or a chance to select a minor magical item from the guild's archive. However, if a party wins the challenge overall, they will be given an even larger reward and the chance to pick magical items from the restricted section of the archive.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa}

  • @UUID[Actor.FYprIclhoDOI8FI4]{Arcos Sarinland}

  • @UUID[Actor.XrFDJNn1Fa7hopqR]{Eveis Brightstone}

  • @UUID[Actor.GA8VFWysoIYfNWCL]{Adelyne Goss}

  • @UUID[Actor.pgpa26YQys5VDwNu]{Sajor Velex}

  • @UUID[Actor.dYGD1p1ui2gE9d28]{Rorhim Iron-Cask}

  • @UUID[Actor.nHiypQMDLV9IvTyR]{Leeph}

  • @UUID[Actor.kHu4Tvu4hKIEAbKj]{Kazra Steelshift}

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.n3MAXRLTxENVeDWB]{Toothbreaker Thug}

  • @UUID[Actor.I4omhcBZxC8PP9jI]{Toothbreaker Scaletamer}

  • @UUID[Actor.WgXxUcogizL8D5Rh]{Raster Thorn}

  • @UUID[Actor.zCaW2IABpatj2TDs]{Scalemaw}

  • @UUID[Actor.XNywYg2moKGYYgqB]{Meri}

  • @UUID[Actor.9VIz2g2agKz7Bl3T]{Ix'erax}

  • @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU]{Vespian Hydral}

  • @UUID[Actor.MNWRuR4oQQP7EUgD]{Shade of Agaseros}

  • @UUID[Actor.DchsMYAWBOV6NrCm]{Animated Rune Tome}

  • @UUID[Actor.Lw8HeAY64cjHnuQq]{Anachraenum Aetherial}
Overview.soverview:
Shortly after the party reaches the glittering city of Ordain and begins exploring the metropolis, they are approached by the famous Anachraenum adventurer Fernis Ossa, who has been keeping track of their exploits in the Arctus Plateau. Fernis is impressed by the party's skills and convictions, but more importantly, she has a task and request for the party that no one else in the city can complete.

Fernis reveals that two years ago, the Guildmaster of the Anachraenum died under mysterious circumstances. Since that time, changes among the Anachraenum organization have left Fernis feeling troubled. To discover what happened, she needs outsiders to join the Anachraenum and help her. A timely opportunity to do this presents itself in the form of the upcoming "Expedition Challenge", a spectacular celebration and test for aspiring Anachraenum members to prove their adventuring mettle.
