They can try to talk to the Anachraenum organizers or other groups of challengers, or they can take time to ponder the meaning of these clues. The solutions to each clue are described in the "Next Steps" block at the bottom of this event.

Talking to Associated Characters

The party might speak with others, groups, or with Eveis, Fernis, or Adelyne to learn more or discover some key piece of information about the location of the Keystone Challenges. Unfortunately for the party, all of these characters stay incredibly tight-lipped and the learn nothing from them.

The First Challenge Clue

The party can consider the first challenge clue:

Where distant waves serenade against the towering stone, Lantyr's descent bathes golden grasses with her lambent glow. There, tower-builders carved a noble dwelling in the earth. Not stranded nor abandoned, a key for those who breach its hall and prove their worth.

Characters with [[/culture emberArcturian]], [[/knowledge seafaring]] , or who succeed on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check recognize that "distant waves cascade against towering stone" sounds like the dramatic bluffs of the Sarin Strand.

  • With a further [[/skill deception 14]] [[/skillCheck deception 14 passive]] check, a character realizes that "not stranded" may be a subtle caution that the location is not in the Sarin Strand, but perhaps nearby.

Characters with [[/skill insight 13 passive format=long]] [[/skillCheck science 13 passive]], [[/knowledge cosmology]], or [[/path emberCaravanner]] recognize that "Lantyr's descent bathes golden grasses" must mean an area of the Golden Flats to the west.

Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] or who succeed on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14] check recognize that "the tower-builders" refers to the ancient Aedir, suggesting the clue is found within some Aedir structure or ruin.

Characters with [[/check perception 14 passive format=long]] or who succeed on a [[/check perception 12]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notice that the Salt Breakers are leaving and you overhear Blister Brass excitedly mutter something that sounds a lot like "The Strand!".

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success : You clearly hear Blister exclaim "that ruined digsite in the bluff over the Strand!"

The Second Challenge Clue

Be not offended when forced to wander through thorny twists of this meander. Descend below the auric plains to tread where waters fill the gorge. Brave the onyx monster's ground with maw agape to to paths unknown. Giants marked the yawning way and there your key waits to be found.

Characters who have completed [[/eventState canyonsSideGrowing]] will immediately recognize "thorny twists of this meander" as potentially referencing the brambles of the Splinter Canyons.

Characters succeeding on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check or who have completed [[/eventState canyonsSideCurrent]] recognize "descend below the auric plains to tread where waters fill the gorge" as likely referencing the Splinter Canyons to the west of Ordain.

  • Result of 19+ Critical Success : You note that the periodic water surge that fills the Splinter Canyons originates from the northern reaches where its central crevasse is deepest.

Characters with [[/knowledge monsters]] or [[/knowledge subterranea]] surmise that "brave the onyx monster's ground with maw agape to to paths unknown" may likely refer to a creature's lair in a cave mouth or subterranean entrance.

Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] or who succeed on a [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] check identify "Giants marked the yawning way" as perhaps an ancient waystone of the Shent or other giant culture.

A character with [[/skill insight 15 passive format=long]] [[/skill awareness 15 passive]] recognizes the references in the clue to "paths" and "way" and surmises that the clue may have something to do with the Pathways.

The Third Challenge Clue

Destine's finger stretches out through mesmerizing sanguine boughs. Seek our quarry where falls its head, your challenge lies beside our winter stead. Some here may know it well. Guard your minds but bare your knowledge and find the key through wit or courage.

Characters with [[/knowledge tracking]] or who succeed on a [[/skill survival 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] know that "Destine's finger" likely refers to the River Destine or one of its tributaries while "mesmerizing sanguine boughs" likely refers to the Bloodwoods north of Ordain.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success : The phrase "falls its head" could reference the river's headwaters, a waterfall, or both.

Characters with [[/skill insight 15 passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 passive]] and who completed [[/eventState chain1Emergence]] pick up on the use of the word "quarry" in the clue and know that there is an abandoned "quarry" to the north of the city.

The clue "some here may know it well" indicates that other Anachraenum members are familiar with this location. If the party asks Adelyne, Fernis, or other veteran Anachraenum members about this clue, with a successful [[/skill persuasion 15]] [[/skillCheck persuasion 15]] check they will reveal that the party should "seek Krator's Hall" but provide no further information.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success : The person asked will provide deeper information about @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.gurjrg1XS8TNG9fd]{Krator's Hall} and hints towards its precise location.

Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] or who succeed on a [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check consider the phrase "Guard your minds but bare your knowledge" as implying some sort of test of intellect.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has ascertained whatever information they can about the provided clues, they may depart All-Fable Keep and begin pursuing the available leads.

Next Steps

The party now has three options and three locations to visit in order to gather the Challenge Keys. There’s no time limit for collecting these keys, and they don’t need to be obtained in any specific order.

  • The objective of this first challenge is found in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.IVArj8xHt94eRY9g]{Jekeroka Villa} and the @UUID[.8CFcW8ez6IW1WNV4]{Manufactured Trial} event.

  • The objective of the second challenge is located in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.oGk7VMdbmgB4tEKw]{Bramble Maze} and the @UUID[.3GwzjZKooj0gxatv]{Amazing Brambles} event.

  • The objective of the third challenge is located in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.gurjrg1XS8TNG9fd]{Krator's Hall} and the @UUID[.zgWKNYcDPuNbjPkw]{Hidden Campsite} event.
The Challenge Begins.soverview: In this event, the party arrives at All-Fable Keep and finds the main hall swarming with activity with various adventuring groups and Anachraenum members all assembled to initiate the challenge. The guildmaster of the Anachraenum, Arcos Sarinland, delivers a welcoming address, and the groups of challengers are equipped with instructions and items necessary to undertake the forthcoming challenges. The party is provided with initial clues for where to find the three challenge keys necessary to unlock the final gauntlet in the Chamber of Agaseros deep beneath All-Fable Keep itself.
The Challenge Begins.sexposition: As you step into the main hall of All-Fable Keep, you become immediately enveloped by a buzz of excitement and energy. The vast room is alive with the chatter of excited adventurers and you begin to distinguish various groups that are clearly teams ready to participate in the upcoming Expedition Challenge. Some of the teams are clad in the distinctive garb of Anachraenum trainees, already sporting the symbol of the bladed compass, while others wear fresh, eager faces and have likely traveled to Ordain for the first time. Amidst this vibrant scene, your attention is drawn to the mesmerizing figure of a otherworldly creature levitating off the ground at the far end of the hall.
The Challenge Begins.ssummary:
We met several other competing parties in All-Fable Keep and the resident Star Mage of Ordain, Eveis Brightstone, who gave us a magical item each. Afterward the guildmaster of the Anachraenum, Arcos Sarinland, appeared and announced "the second Expedition Challenge has now begun"! We have been given three clues to find the three Keystone Challenges and retrieve the Challenge Keys.

Where distant waves serenade against the towering stone, Lantyr's descent bathes golden grasses with her lambent glow. There, tower-builders carved a noble dwelling in the earth. Not stranded nor abandoned, a key for those who breach its hall and prove their worth.

Be not offended when forced to wander through thorny twists of this meander. Descend below the auric plains to tread where waters fill the gorge. Brave the onyx monster's ground with maw agape to to paths unknown. Giants marked the yawning way and there your key waits to be found.

Destine's finger stretches out through mesmerizing sanguine boughs. Seek our quarry where falls its head, your challenge lies beside our winter stead. Some here may know it well. Guard your minds but bare your knowledge and find the key through wit or courage.

Other parties are also searching for the Keystone Challenges so there is some urgency for us to retrieve these keys as quickly as possible.

Manufactured Trial.name: Manufactured Trial
Manufactured Trial.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event takes place within the @UUID[Scene.emberJekerokaVil] area map. The area is a pre-configured and carefully constructed challenge by the Anachraenum to test a party's skills and abilities. In this event, the characters can:

  • Encounter @UUID[Actor.Lw8HeAY64cjHnuQq]{Anachraenum Aetherials} designed and programmed to test the party's combat skills.

  • Survive various traps and hazards scattered throughout to test the parties' awareness.

  • Solve a devious puzzle which will test the parties problem-solving abilities.

Scene

For the descriptive and exploration gameplay about the area itself, refer to the Area Walkthrough: @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9]{Jekeroka Villa}

Ruins of the Sun

The ruins of the villa are in relatively good condition, and there are a number of Anachraenum crates, barrels, and tools scattered around the entrance. Some seem to be sealed crates containing remaining objects of significance from inside, ready to be shipped back to All-Fable Keep. The party can speak with Adelyne Goss here, but she makes the situation and the task ahead quite clear, and as the party approaches, you can read them the following:

Adelyne sits in a relaxed pose, but also with a certain level of discomfort as she shifts her position every so often. She is clearly annoyed, perhaps more than usual, with a frown upon her face so deep that her eyebrows are nearly crossed, and she impatiently taps her finger against her chin.

Wonderful... you lot. It's hot and I'm far too busy. This is a task I'd rather leave to someone else. Can you all hurry it along, please!

Talking with Adelyne Goss

Adelyne Goss is as terse and short-tempered as ever, and she is not particularly pleased to be outside All-Fable Keep, overseeing one of the challenge sites. But Arcos asked her, and she relented for the sake of her friend and to make sure the Expedition Challenge moves along swiftly.

Aedlyne is not here to assist the groups, either physically or by revealing what may be inside in any detail. However, if the party asks, you can read the following.

No, I won't be giving you any help whatsoever. I'm here merely to observe and ensure no one dies. If anyone appears to be in real danger, I will step in, but you won't get any information from me about what's inside. Only that it's been prepared in a way to test your dungeon delving abilities, so take that as you will.

The party might have been friendly with Adelyne and may try to convince her to reveal something. Characters who succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 18]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 18]] learn that the area inside is relatively small but each room has a different challenge that they have to overcome.

  • Result of 20+ The party learns that another group has recently entered the digsite, and for some reason Adelyne doesnt seem to be worried about it. Which suggests that they are still in there, or they failed and are currently awaiting rescue inside their frozen stasis fields from the @UUID[Item.jggar2bndAvZthdS]{Frozen Tear}.

  • Critical Success. The party learns that another group has recently entered the digsite, and for some reason Adelyne doesnt seem to be worried about it. Which suggests that they are still in there, or they failed and are currently awaiting rescue inside their frozen stasis fields from the @UUID[Item.jggar2bndAvZthdS]{Frozen Tear}.

If anyone wants to know more about the Aedir nature of the ruin specifically, they can ask Aedlyne about the digsite, and you can read the following:

Adelyne's tone shifts slightly as her interest in the history of this location becomes clear. "The Anachraenum has determined that this digsite was once known as Jekeroka Villa, and it was once the ancient home of one of the powerful Magi of the Aedir Empire. He likely lived on the Arctus Plateau before the events of the Shattering. We know the builder pursued magical experimentation, and the elemental energy he produced and created is still powered by a connection to distant and mysterious magical forces."

Entering the Digsite

Once the party heads inside and begins to explore Aedir Digsite, the full area walkthrough can be found here @UUID[JournalEntry.dZZJwSWRMaOemjc9]{Jekeroka Villa}. Once the party has completed the area map, they receive the key they need from the chest and can carry on to the next location.

Signara Attunement: Jekeroka's Ledger

If the party manages to find Jekeroka's Ledger while exploring the Villa, each character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 anachraenum1VillaLedger]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

With the@UUID[Item.SAm2oCDjRdZggcot]{Trial Challenge Key} in hand, the party can now either move on to the other two sites and collect the remaining keys, or if this is the final key they need, they can head back to All-Fable Keep in Ordain.
Manufactured Trial.soverview: In this event, the party finds the Aedir Digsite, more commonly known as Jekeroka Villa. The ancient site has long been cleared out and researched by the Anachraenum, but for the Expedition Challenge, the site has been prepared with various manufactured trials. After talking with Loremistress Adelyne Goss outside, they can enter and complete the various trails within and retrieve a Challenge Key!
Manufactured Trial.sexposition: As you approach a tall cliffside overhang, you notice a variety of crates, barrels, and tools surrounding the entrance to an ancient-looking door embedded into pale stonework. The strange-looking designs are clearly reminiscent of Aedir construction. As you move closer, you spot a figure sitting in the shadows outside the entrance, Loremistress Adelyne Goss was reading a hefty tome, but she notices your approach, leveling you with a withering stare.
Manufactured Trial.ssummary: We successfully completed the trial set up by the Anachraenum and recovered the Trial Challenge Key for the Expedition Challenge.

Amazing Brambles.name: Amazing Brambles
Amazing Brambles.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event challenges the party's capacity to traverse dangerous environments and tests their skills in navigation and wilderness survival. In this event, the party can:

  • Employ their skills and abilities to withstand difficult natural elements.

  • Discover the lair of a deceased @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Garganthus}.

  • Find a totem constructed by the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.Z8Nm4rnjqG3BJHSd]{Varún} and the @UUID[Item.3vbsNwylLdTUFA8q]{Maze Challenge Key} hanging from it.

  • Learn of a hidden route between the surface to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways} below.

Group Skill Checks

The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.3GwzjZKooj0gxatv#traversing-the-maze]{Traversing the Maze} section of this event involves a sequence of group skill checks @UUID[Compendium.crucible.rules.JournalEntry.CrucibleSkills00.JournalEntryPage.skillChecks00000]{Group Skill Checks}. The party's progression through the maze will depend on the success or failure of each group skill check.

Abandoning the Event

If, at any point, the party is thwarted by the challenge of navigating this area they may leave. In this case simply abandon the event which will allow the party to re-attempt it at a later time.

Penetrating the Maze

The first group challenge the party will face involves breaching the perimeter of the area.

The labyrinthine warren of brambles here is near impenetrable. You can only hope that if you get past the outer-most shell you will reach terrain that is not so actively suffocated by the massive vines.

Penetrating the Thorns

Perform a group skill check requiring [[/skill athletics 16]] or [[/skill acrobatics 16]] [[/skillCheck athletics 16 group]] to breach the outer maze of brambles.

  • Characters who are [[/ancestry emberThornling]] automatically succeed on their check.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberOaken]] or [[/path emberPrimalistDisciple]] have advantage on this check.

  • Use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplBlight0000]{Blight} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplTreeStride]{Tree Stride} spells can automatically succeed on this challenge, counting as a Critical Success for the entire party.

The outcome of this challenge is determined via the rules for group skill checks with the following results. Unless otherwise stated by the result, the party moves onwards to the next challenge.

Success

You locate a section of thorns that is sufficiently pliant for you to squeeze through by force or by contorting your body through its aperture.

The party is successful in bypassing the thorny barrier.

Critical Success

You locate a section of thorns that is sufficiently pliant for you to squeeze through by force or by contorting your body through its aperture. As you proceed through the winding corridors beyond, you come upon a small clearing within which grows a large and unusual plant.

The party benefits from a Success but also refer to the "Nimbus Pitcher" section below.

Failure

You force your way through the perimeter of thorns with clumsy effort, the countless briars snagging on your equipment and tearing at your skin. The passage, although short, is exhausting and leaves you bloodied.

The party forces their way through the perimeter, but at some cost. Each member of the group gains one rank of &Reference[exhaustion] and must succeed on a [[/save 16 con]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 2d10 piercing]] damage

Critical Failure

You spend an hour trying to force or squeeze your way through the perimeter of thorns. It is a clumsy effort and the countless briars that snag on your equipment and tear at your skin are both damaging and demoralizing. The perimeter of thorns is impregnable and you are forced to retreat to the plateau upon which you started and reconsider your approach.

The party suffers the consequences of Failure but is also unable to make progress and must repeat this challenge. The party may simply attempt the check again, or if they can devise some alternative stratagem for bypassing the perimeter of thorns the Gamemaster may allow it.

Nimbus Pitcher

If the party achieved a Critical Success on this challenge, read the following:

Along the path you clear you discover a small clearing containing an unusual plant - a thriving tangle of purple flowers and deep pitchers hanging from sturdy vines. These pitchers appear to contain effervescent moisture and appear to be perpetually emitting steam, although they generate no perceptible heat.

Characters with [[/knowledge plants]] or who succeed on a [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check recognize the plant as a "Nimbus Pitcher", a rare flora with properties that are valuable to alchemists.

With a successful [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check the party can harvest five @UUID[Item.B81IadxxOQtLpyKt]{Nimbus Pitchers} from the plant. Characters possessing an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulHerbalismK]{Herbalism Kit} may instead perform a [[/check tool=herb dc=14]] check with advantage.

Ragen Attunement: Utilizing Strength

Any character who uses Strength to successfully penetrate the maze advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 anachraenum1BramblesStrength]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aura Attunement: Utilizing Dexterity

Any character who uses Dexterity to successfully penetrate the maze advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 anachraenum1BramblesDexterity]] at the conclusion of the event.

Akon Attunement: Utilizing Magic

Any character who uses magic to successfully penetrate the maze advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 anachraenum1BramblesMagic]] at the conclusion of the event.

Avoiding Gore Birds

The second group challenge tests the party's ability to avoid notice from a flock of gore birds which roost upon the canyon cliffs.

As you continue navigating the treacherous environment, you see upon the canyon cliffs above you a huge flock of birds. Their excrement has bleached the rocks and their nests are wedged into any cranny that affords even an inch of space upon which to precariously balance. You recognize these birds as carrion eaters and fear they might be emboldened enough to attack living prey in numbers.

Carrion Flock

Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] or who succeed on a [[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck medicine 15 passive]] check recognize these creatures as a @UUID[Actor.ZuWduzUSGS6i4NZm]{Gore Bird Swarm}.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success: You realize that the swarm could be distracted through the careful placement of food scraps or shiny objects that would capture their attention and aid in the party's passage.

The party must utilize stealth or guile to move through the area without being detected by the flock. Perform a group skill check requiring [[/skill stealth 18]] or [[/skill animalHandling 18]] [[/skillCheck stealth 18 group]] to pass through the area unnoticed.

Success

You narrowly escape notice by the birds, hearing a great cacophony from behind you as you leave their domain.

The party is successful in eluding the birds.

Critical Success

You effortlessly escape notice by the birds, sneaking past them silently and entirely undetected. As you weave your way through the brambles you stumble upon the ravaged body of a giant figure.

The party benefits from a Success but also refer to the "Gored Giant" section below.

Failure

Your attempts to elude notice by the birds are unsuccessful. No longer afforded the luxury of subtlety you have to flee the cacophony of hungry cries that swell through the canyon behind you. Several outlying wings of the massive swarm reach you and rip at your exposed skin.

The party is unable to avoid detection. Each party member must make a [[/save 16 dexterity]] saving throw, suffering [[/damage 6d4 slashing]] damage or half damage on a successful save suffers damage from the [[/hazard 12 reflex slashing]]{Swarming Talons}.

Critical Failure

The flock of birds easily detects you and soon you are swept up in a bewildering maelstrom of flapping wings, raking talons, and vicious bites. You are forced to flee as a cacophony of hungry cries that swell through the canyon behind you in pursuit.

The party suffers the consequences of Failure and also becomes disoriented as they lose their sense of direction. Every member of the group will have Disadvantage on the fourth challenge, "Rediscovering the Path".

The Gored Giant

If the party achieved a Critical Success on this challenge, read the following:

You stumble upon the body of a giant, its bones picked clean and bleached by the sunlight that passes daily overhead. The remnants of its equipment, broken armor, an enormous bone-spiked club, and tattered cloth are strewn about the clearing.

Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] or who succeed on an [[/skill history 16]] a [[/skillCheck society 16]] check recognize that the equipment and remains here are unlikely to be those of a Shent, and are more likely those of a Varún, a surviving culture of giants who are genealogical cousins to the ancient Shent.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill medicine 22]] [[/skillCheck medicine 22]] check identify that the giant likely died from terrible wounds sustained to its back, where the ribcage is broken and its bones are scored by deep gouges.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage to this roll.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill investigation 15]] an [[/skillCheck awareness 15]] check identify a leather pouch discarded to the side of the body which contains an unidentified @UUID[Item.YbwW1bsZi0NdOmQU]{Varun Moonmedal}. This particular medal is attuned to Cora.

Withstanding Noxious Plants

The third group challenge tests the party's ability to withstand the delirious fumes of noxious plants.

The canyon before you narrows and you notice that on both sides affixed to the rock are the rotund forums of globular plants that seem to almost breathe as they slowly increase and decrease in size. With every exhalation, a small puff of spores or pollen spout forth from a hole near the top of the plant. It seems there is no alternative way forward.

Noxious Plants

Characters with [[/knowledge plants]] or who succeed on a [[/skill nature 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15 passive]] check identify that these plants are called "Chokebellows", notorious for how their fumes can cause temporary (or permanent) suffocation in creatures who inhale them.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success: You suspect that you could safely move and breathe in the area between exhalations of the plants fumes if you timed your approach carefully. If the party reaches this realization, they have advantage on the skill checks required by this challenge.

The party must utilize stealth or guile to move through the area without being detected by the flock. Perform a group challenge requiring [[/skill perception 15]] [[/skillCheck awareness 15 group]] to to carefully time their movements between "breaths" of the nearby plants.

  • Characters who are [[/ancestry emberHulgrun]], [[/ancestry emberAltyra]], or who otherwise have immunity to the &Reference[poisoned] @Condition[poisoned] condition automatically succeed on this check.

  • Use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplWindWall00]{Wind Wall}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGaseousFor]{Gaseous Form}, or other comparable spells can count as a success on this check for one character.

Success

You carefully time your movements through the growth of plants, taking brief moments to exert yourself and breathe between exhalations of the plants fumes. Your progress is slow and your lungs burn by the end, but you make it to the other side without incident.

The party is successful in traversing the hazard.

Critical Success

You expertly time your movements through the growth of plants, balancing your physical exertion with opportune windows to breathe. Your progress is slow, but you reach the far side without incident. From the safety of a plateau on the far side of this hazard, you appreciate a clear vantage point of the maze of brambles which helps reinforce your sense of direction amidst the confusing warren.

The party benefits from a Success but also gains advantage to the skill check required by the final challenge, "Rediscovering the Path".

Failure

You attempt to time your movements between exhalations of the plants, but you quickly become overtaken by the burning of your lungs and the persistence of the miasma. You cannot avoid inhaling some of the fumes and the breath is sucked away from your lungs. With the help of your allies you press onwards to the far side but feel the burning effects of the choking vapors.

Each character must make a [[/save 18 constitution]] saving throw, suffering [[/damage 4d6 poison]] damage or half damage with a successful save [[/hazard 12 fortitude poison]]{Chokebellow Fumes} .

Critical Failure

Your attempt to time movements between exhalations of the plants are short-lived as you are rapidly overtaken by the burning of your lungs and the persistence of the miasma. You inhale the fumes and the breath is ripped from your lungs. Through some grace or fortune you crawl you way to the far side but your vision swims and you feel distinctly unwell.

The party suffers the consequences of Failure and every member gains the &Reference[poisoned] @Condition[poisoned] condition until the completion of a long rest. Unless removed, this condition imposes disadvantage on the subsequent skill checks in this event.

Rediscovering the Path

The final group challenge requires the party to maintain their overall sense of direction and avoid getting turned around and lost during their ordeal.

You approach the far end of the canyon where you think awaits your eventual destination … but wait … that spur of rock, that distinctive spiral of bramble, have you been here before? The overhanging rock occludes your view of the sky and your sense of direction falters.

The Bewildering Maze

Perform a group skill check requiring [[/skill survival 16]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 16 group]] to ascertain your bearings.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge tracking]] or [[/path emberCaravanner]] have advantage to this check.

  • Use of spells like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAugury0000]{Augury} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLocateObje]{Locate Object} can enable the casting character to automatically succeed on their own check.

  • Use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplFindthePat]{Find the Path} spell results in the party automatically achieving a Critical Success on this challenge.

Success

You reorient yourself and press onwards, passing through the tangled warren into a spacious enclave at the end of the narrow canyon.

The party has completed the challenge and reached the Garganthus Den at the end of the maze.

Critical Success

You swiftly reorient yourself and press onwards, emerging from the tangled warren into a spacious enclave at the end of the narrow canyon. As you gaze upon the space before you, the light overhead highlights the rock face of the canyons with a spectacular bloom of radiant color, you feel invigorated knowing that you have weathered the maze and reached its terminus.

The party benefits from a Success but also each member of the party gains Inspirationmay reduce Madness by 10.

Failure

The brambles surround you on all sides and you lose confidence in your progress. None of the multitude of routes before you look like clear passageways towards the clue you seek within this maze. Hours of frustrating trial and error pass until you stumble as if by chance into a spacious enclave at the end of the narrow canyon. Relief and exhaustion mingle together in your mind.

Advance time by 4 hours and every member of the party gains one rank of &Reference[exhaustion] the @Condition[exhausted] condition .

Critical Failure

The brambles surround you on all sides and you lose confidence in your progress. None of the multitude of routes before you look like clear passageways towards the clue you seek within this maze. Hours of frustrating trial and error pass until you stumble out onto a rocky shelf. It takes a moment for recognition to dawn on you that this is the exact point from which you began your exploration, now many hours ago.

The party suffers the consequences of Failure and also is returned to the beginning of the Bramble Maze. They must either abandon the challenge or re-attempt it, beginning again from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.3GwzjZKooj0gxatv#penetrating-the-maze]{Penetrating the Maze}.

The Garganthus Den

You gaze ahead into the terminus of the canyon that you spent strenuous hours traversing. Before you is a round depression, enclosed on all sides by sheer stone cliffs that reach towards the distant sky overhead. In the center of this depression you see a totemic pillar standing proudly, and slumped near its foot the large dark form of some creature. Behind the creature's body, you see an opening in the ground that descends into darkness.

The totem itself is constructed from thick sections of thorny vine surrounded and reinforced by the cleaned ribcage bones of an enormous creature. The bones are lashed together in bunches which surround the central vine, creating a bone-encircled pillar that stands nearly five feet in diameter and twenty feet tall. Hanging from the totem are some scraps of pale cloth upon which have been painted runic markers in a variety of colorful paints.

At the foot of the totem, a monstrous figure slumps motionless. It's hide glistens black, almost perfect onyx interspersed with bulging purple veins and vivid cyan spines. The creature's side has been torn open exposing the chest cavity of its carcass.

A glint suddenly draws your eye — halfway up the bone totem dangles a bunch of metal keys fastened around the totem with a leather cord.

A Varún warrior created a totem here to commemorate their defeat of the Garganthus as the conclusion of their ritualistic pilgrimage and hunt.

A Totem of Conquest

Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] or who succeed on an [[/skill history 16]] a [[/skillCheck society 16]] check recognize the totem as being Varún in origin, a surviving culture of giants who are genealogical distant relatives of the ancient Shent.

  • Characters who previously discovered and identified the body of the Varún in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.3GwzjZKooj0gxatv#avoiding-gore-birds]{Avoiding Gore Birds} have advantage on this check.

  • Result of 21+ Critical Success: You recall a fragment of lore that some adolescent Varún warriors undertake a rite of passage within which they are assigned to travel by themselves towards some distant land where they must locate and hunt a formidable monster which inhabits the local wilderness.

Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] or who succeed on a [[/skill medicine 16]] [[/skillCheck medicine 16]] check notice countless tiny pock-marks in the bones which have been picked completely clean. You suspect that the gore birds encountered previously were drawn to this carcass and have made short work of the exposed remains.

The Felled Garganthus

Characters with [[/knowledge monsters]] or who succeed on a [[/skill nature 18]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 18 passive]] check recognize the felled creature as an @UUID[Actor.sE0B84CcdGKguNVI]{Adult Garganthus}. A gargantuan reptilian creature whose formidable aspect evokes a sense of primordial savagery.

  • Result of 23+ Critical Success: You have heard tales that Garganthus Hide is a precious material utilized by some of Ember's finest leatherworkers to create equipment that is prized for it's durability, flexibility, and light-neutralizing properties.

  • An attempt to skin the remains of the Garganthus to harvest its hide require a successful [[/skill athletics 25]] [[/skillCheck athletics 25]] check. A character with@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulLeatherwor] may instead perform a [[/tool tool=leatherworker dc=25 ability=strength]] check with advantage. On a success, the player is able to harvest two units of @UUID[Item.6MkixQ3Kud91T4ng]{Garganthus Hide}.

The Challenge Key

Hanging from the bone-covered totem is a bundle of @UUID[Item.3vbsNwylLdTUFA8q]{Maze Challenge Keys}, one of which is required by the party to progress in the Expedition Challenge. It does not require any noteworthy effort to retrieve, however as soon as the first character in the party touches one of the keys, read the following aloud.

As your fingers make contact with one of the gleaming keys, you feel a sudden flash of power emanating from the Frozen Tear and a glimmer of magic leaps from the tear onto the bundle of keys covering them in a momentary lattice of glowing permafrost.

Any attempt to remove or destroy any of the other remaining keys is thwarted by a field of magical stasis that surrounds the bunch of keys. Eveis Brightstone has planned ahead and the Frozen Tear that each party member carries doubles as a passkey, allowing that party member to obtain one - and only one - of the challenge keys. If desired, each member of the group may retrieve one single key from the bundle.

Once the party has retrieved the challenge keys, they are interrupted as described below:

No sooner have your fingers closed around the key and withdrawn it from the totem when you hear a cascade of rock pebbles and crunching footfalls descending the scree behind you, in the direction from which you entered the area. You turn instinctively to see a pair of figures making their way down towards you.

One stands tall with the posture of a Wirrun, but with a flamboyant mane and tail of remarkable pink fur like that of a Kiska. The other is a stout Thornling, their head crowned by the magnificently broad cap of a blue mushroom.

One of your rivals in the Expedition Challenge, the duo called "Mug and Cap" approach. Mug, limping slightly but seemingly undeterred, greets you with a jaunty wave.

Woulda beaten you here if it weren't for those stinking fume blasters … Oh well, you might have won this leg, but the race is still up for grabs.

Rival Group

The party's response to the arrival of Mug & Cap could range from amicable to antagonistic. If the party tries to be friendly, there is a chance to persuade Mug & Cap to share information about the challenge clues.

With a successful [[/skill persuasion 22]] [[/skillCheck persuasion 22]] or [[/skill intimidation 20]] [[/skillCheck intimidation 20]] check, they can be convinced to share the solution to the first Challenge Clue, revealing their knowledge of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.IVArj8xHt94eRY9g]{Jekeroka Villa} and its location.

  • Failure: If this check is failed, they will lie and instead describe@UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.isjEWrS8Qv8gq8A2] as the clue's location. A character who succeeds on an [[/skill insight 16]] a [[/skillCheck deception 16 passive]] check realizes they are lying.

They party can ask about the third Challenge Clue, to which Mug & Cap confess they have not yet figured it out. Success on an [[/skill insight 16]] [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] check concludes that they are being forthright in this regard.

To Paths Below

Behind the felled creature's body, a cavernous aperture drops into darkness below. There are precarious shelves and ledges of rock that ring the sinkhole offering the possibility of descent while simultaneously alluding to the danger inherent in such an attempt.

Once the party has completed this event, the Bramble Maze becomes a permanent connection point that the party can use to descent into the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}, emerging within the great subterranean lake of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.FJNYRa0cGLlizwYY]{Mycelian Expanse}.

Pathways Entrance

To descend from here into the Pathways, return to the Arctus Plateau region map and change the party token elevation to -1 to enter the Pathways layer.

Concluding the Event

Once the party have traversed the maze and retrieved the @UUID[Item.3vbsNwylLdTUFA8q]{Maze Challenge Key} they require, mark the following outcome as complete and conclude the event.

[[/outcome complete]]

Next Steps

If the party have yet to complete other challenges, their next steps are:

  • The objective of this first challenge is found in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.IVArj8xHt94eRY9g]{Jekeroka Villa} and the @UUID[.8CFcW8ez6IW1WNV4]{Manufactured Trial} event.

  • The objective of the third challenge is located in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.gurjrg1XS8TNG9fd]{Krator's Hall} and the @UUID[.zgWKNYcDPuNbjPkw]{Hidden Campsite} event.

If all three keys have been acquired, the party can return to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0]{All-Fable Keep} and enter @UUID[.qeERNVDf7uz1QloT].
Amazing Brambles.soverview: In this event, the party finds the Bramble Maze, a hidden Anacharnum Challenge, within the Splinter Canyons west of Ordain. Throughout the challenge, the party will be confronted by increasingly difficult survival and exploration challenges and skill checks that will test their ability to explore dangerous environments.
Amazing Brambles.sexposition:
As you navigate the winding paths of the Splinter Canyons, light from above filters through jagged rock formations, casting long shadows on the ground. The air is thick with a scent similar to rain, and vibrant plants cling stubbornly to life among the sheer rocks around you.

You squeeze through a particularly narrow passage and find yourself looking into a ravine full of giant brambles. Thick vines, wicked thorns, and dense underbrush frames the way like teeth in the mouth of some ancient beast. You recall the clue that Arcos Sarinland provided:

Be not offended when forced to wander through thorny twists of this meander. Descend below the auric plains to tread where waters fill the gorge. Brave the onyx monster's ground with maw agape to to paths unknown. Giants marked the yawning way and there your key waits to be found.

You suspect you have found the location of one of the Expedition Challenge trials.
Amazing Brambles.ssummary: We traversed a formidable Bramble Maze within the depths of the Splinter Canyons to find one of the Challenge Keys required to progress in the Expedition Challenge. The key was hanging from a strange giant totem near a sinkhole which descended into the darkness of the Pathways far below.

Hidden Campsite.name: Hidden Campsite
Hidden Campsite.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event takes place in the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.gurjrg1XS8TNG9fd]{Krator's Hall} location in the@UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QmrljlMl1VocfxAo]{Wedgelands} to the north of Ordain. In this event, the party may choose to explore or investigate several things at once, and the sections within this event are not supposed to be linear.

In this event, the characters can:

  • Investigate the shelter of Krator's Hall, which has been sealed off to the public by the Anachraenum.

  • Encounter the Well of Orbis, an inscrutable landmark that will not only test the party's knowledge of history and lore, it will challenge their skills of insight and deduction.

  • Earn the @UUID[Item.WUeU31rhRz7YQCO1]{Well Challenge Key} by enduring all 4 Well of Orbis Echoes and answering their questions about Ember's ancient histories — including those of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.zkmWSB32y8Fbc4UL]{Orbis}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent}, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.4RM8MIiCDWMFv2yr]{Sedyri}.

The Overgrown Hall

If the party first decides to investigate the large abandoned lodge, read the following:

As you approach the massive doors of the hall, a large, heavy lock catches your eye. It's clear that the structure itself seems to have been locked up and secured, as all of the windows have solid-looking shutters covering them, and peaceful stillness covers the surrounding area.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/check perception 14]] check or has [[/check perception 16 passive]] can see that several of the windows and the wood paneling of the door have a number of old light scratch marks.

Investigating the Door

  • With a successful [[/check arcana 15]] check or [[/knowledge rituals]], the character recognizes the lock is of a magical nature, but only to enhance its durability, the lock itself does not appear to be magically trapped. Touching the lock does nothing, and no magical spell appears to disuade entry.

  • If someone attempts to pick the lock in order to gain entry, they must succeed on a [[/check slt 16]] check, and the lock falls open with a click, the door can be opened safely.

  • Any character who has [[/knowledge tracking]] understands that the creatures that left the marks on the doors and windows are likely small animals and not something particularly dangerous.

Breaking the Door or Lock

If characters strike the door or lock with force, the magic infused into the lock will respond in kind. Allow the character to make an attack roll against an AC of 13, and let them roll for damage with whatever weapon or spell they are using to break the door or lock. Then, describe how the lock shudders and begins to glow with a magical light for a moment, and the character must succeed on a [[/save dexterity 15]] saving throw or they hit with exactly the same damage that was just inflicted upon the door or lock.

Ultimately, gaining entry into the lodge proves to be a frustrating experience, and if the party seems determined to see what lies within, read the following:

Stepping into the hall, you see that the single large room is devoid of anything notable. The emptiness feels slightly oppressive, with the echoes of your footsteps amplifying the silence that surrounds you. Unfortunately, while the area may sometimes be used by the Anachraenum, only a few small empty cots for bedding rest along one side, and a kitchen area with bare countertops sits on the other side. A small faded note lies pinned to one of the walls that reads:

Please lock the door after you. Thank you!

The Well of Orbis

As the party approaches the pool of shimmering water to the side of Krator's Hall, they realize that this is where the true challenge begins. Next to the pool is a sign written by someone from the Anachraenum, it reads:

Well Challenge for the Expedition Challenge. Successful answers to the Well's questions will result in the acquisition of the Key.

As you stand there pondering the meaning of these words, you notice that the waters of the pool begin to stir with soft movements that catch your attention.

Well of Orbis Echoes

Roll or select from the roll table below to determine the challenge that the party faces.

@Embed[RollTable.qijerRjXzHlsY6Sj inline rollable]

Origin of the Well

The Well of Orbis is an extremely strange and esoteric object. It possesses a degree of knowledge of its own but does not seem to be alive and can be directed by the Anachraenum with questions for the Exhibition Challenge, yet it remains entirely unknown to the Anachraenum overall, with only vague hints that the small pool may be connected to the moon of Orbis.

Any character who has [[/attunement orbis]] finds the pool comforting and resonates with it oddly, but experiences no other tangible effect.

1. Legacy of Destruction

In an instant, a massive fireball appears over the water and explodes outward, casting a wash of vibrant reds and oranges across the shimmering surface. The heat seems palpable, tingling against your skin, but as you brace for the impending impact, you realize that the force is merely an illusion. The force of the explosion fades into silence, revealing the ghostly remnants of a broken tower flickering in the air, ethereal and shimmering like a mirage.

This section is based upon the parties' knowledge of the ancient Aedir Empire. If the party cannot answer a question or answers incorrectly, then move on to the next question or proceed to scoring if all the questions have been asked and answered.

Aedir Knowledge

Anyone within the party with [[/knowledge aedir]] immediately recognizes that the Well of Orbis is showing a simple version of the Shattering and is likely going to ask questions about the Sunfire Empire.

As the characters stand before the pool of water, a strangely dispassionate voice speaks in a monotone:

Question: When did the Aedir Empire end?

Anyone in the party who answers correctly, with the current precise date in years, which is 2523, or saying two thousand five hundred and twenty three years ago, hears a small ping and a quiet, almost imperceptible sigh. Anyone succeeding on a [[/check insight 12]] will be able to link both the current date and the end of the Aedir Empire together automatically.

Second Question: How did the Aedir achieve military supremacy?

The answer to this question may be hard, but if anyone within the party answers Constructs or advanced magical technology, they hear a small ping and a quiet, almost imperceptible sigh. If anyone has [[/knowledge aedir]], they know the answer to this question automatically, as it is fairly well-known information. Otherwise, anyone succeeding on a [[/check history 15]] will remember learning about this at some point. The party may also have first-hand knowledge of the Aedir's military power if they have completed the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl]{Ooze Control} and will also be able to know this information automatically based on thier encounter with an Aedir Construct.

Third Question: With whom did the Aedir ally themselves during the war?

This final question is very difficult to answer, but anyone who answers, Celestials, or the forces of Luxarum, hears a small ping and a quiet, almost imperceptible sigh. Only someone with [[/knowledge aedir]] may attempt a [[/check history 18]], and upon success, they recall that the Aedir were said to have allied themselves with a faction from Luxarum during a tumultuous period known as the Forsaken War.

Scoring Success or Failure

Answering any question correctly gives the party a single point, which the GM should keep track of. These points should not be revealed to the party until the final section @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.zgWKNYcDPuNbjPkw#a-key-from-chaos]{A key from Chaos}. However, upon completing this echo and answering all the questions, determine whether the party answered all the questions correctly or not, and read the corresponding response from the voice.

  • If the party managed to answer every question, the voice within the Well of Orbis imparts a piece of sage advice:

    It's important to understand the hubris of the Aedir, and it's easy to see the lessons regarding the dangers of excessive pride and the responsibility that accompanies power.

  • If they get it wrong, everyone in the party must make a [[/save 14 wisdom]] saving throw. On a success, they are able to remain standing and suffer no ill effects. On a failure, they are pushed to the floor and knocked prone for a moment, taking [[/damage 1d6 psychic]] damage and a fierce headache rips through their minds. The voice within the Well of Orbis then says:

    You are as foolish as the Aedir. It seems you will once again fail to understand their arrogance, and those who do not learn from history are doomed to repeat it.

2. Dragged Under

As you stand before the shimmering surface, a disturbance ripples through the water. Suddenly, massive pale hands surge forth from the depths with surprising speed. The skin stretched across the blackened, elongated bones is glittering and translucent, and beneath the surface, you can glimpse that the hands come from a nothingness. The hands spring forward, attempting to grab hold of you.

These hands are a strange, somewhat physical illusion, linked to the ancient history of Orbis. They are effectively the well itself, attempting to rebel against the commands and instructions of the Anachraenum and have a deep malice to harm those standing around the pool.

Avoiding the Hands

Anyone within 15 feet of the pool (which is likely every party member unless otherwise implicitly stated) must succeed on a [[/save strength 15]] saving throw. If they succeed, they break free from the initial hold. If they fail, they are dragged towards and then into the water of the pool.

At this stage, while this may not be a traditional combat encounter, rolling initiative is encouraged to help break down the individual actions for the party members and assist with some of the mechanical actions they might take.

While any character is struggling in the water, the remaining party members can attempt to help them.

  • A party member can attempt to physically pull their companion back using ropes, their own strength, or with some other aid. A successful [[/check athletics 16]] allows the affected player to make another [[/save strength 15]] saving throw with advantage.

  • A character outside the pool may attempt to analyze and counter the magic of the well with a [[/check arcana 16]], and anyone with [[/attunement orbis]] succeeds automatically. Success allows the affected player to gain a +2 bonus to their next save against the spectral hands.

  • On their turn, any character within the pool can make either a [[/save strength 15]] or a [[/save dex 15]] in order to break free themselves.

Anyone from the party can attempt to attack the hands; however, their attacks are strangely insufficient and seem to pass through the hands no matter what the party tries.

If any character is still restrained after two turns and remains within the pool, they must roll on the chaotic visions table below. If the party works together and succeeds in pulling them out or counters the magic in some way, the player escapes with the knowledge that the well holds more secrets than they realized.

@Embed[RollTable.hq4wuqdGRm4KrxQY inline rollable]

3. The Ending of the Stars

Flashes of light dance above the shimmering surface of the pool, illuminating the scene with vibrant hues of azure and gold. As if guided by an unseen hand, these bright orbs begin to weave together in a delicate pattern that resembles a twinkling constellation. Stars of varying sizes and brightness pulse in rhythm, but suddenly, without warning, the entire constellation is engulfed, snuffed out by a deep, dark void, and only a deep darkness remains.

This section is based upon the parties' knowledge of the ancient Shent. If the party cannot answer a question or answers incorrectly, then move on to the next question or proceed to scoring if all the questions have been asked and answered.

Shent Knowledge

Anyone within the party with [[/knowledge shent]] immediately recognizes that the Well of Orbis is showing a simple version of the Shattering as it relates to ancient stargazing Giants and is likely going to ask questions about the Shent.

As the characters stand before the pool of water, a strangely dispassionate voice speaks in a monotone:

Question: What was the Shent's primary writing language?

Anyone in the party who answers correctly, with Pathward, or says magical runes, hears a small ping and a quiet, almost imperceptible sigh. Anyone succeeding on a [[/check history 12]] will be able to remember several times when they encountered Shent ruins previously and saw runes on them.

Second Question: Where did the Giants originate

These questions may be hard unless the party has completed @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi]{To Fall and Fall Again}, but the answer is the Pathways. If anyone has [[/knowledge shent]], they know the answer because this is considered where the Shent came from before they started building their kingdom in the mountains. Otherwise, anyone in the party can attempt a difficult [[/check history 19]], and if successful, they will remember learning about this at some point.

Third Question: What destroyed the Shent?

This final question is very difficult to answer, as the majority of characters may think that the answer is the Abyss, but the true answer is actually Abyssal Horrors specifically. However, the party may not have come across this information unless they have completed @UUID[JournalEntry.gUbcqJg4YBHbqjyi]{To Fall and Fall Again}. Only someone with [[/knowledge shent]] may attempt to roll a [[/check history 20]]. If successful, they recall this specific piece of information, but nothing else about Abyssal Horrors is revealed.

Scoring Success or Failure

Answering any question correctly gives the party a single point, which the GM should keep track of. These points should not be revealed to the party until the final section @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.zgWKNYcDPuNbjPkw#a-key-from-chaos]{A key from Chaos}. However, upon completing this echo and answering all the questions, determine whether the party answered all the questions correctly or not, and read the corresponding response from the voice.

  • If the party managed to answer every question, the voice within the Well of Orbis imparts a piece of sage advice:

    The Shent were once wise and knowledgeable, but they carried with them a terrible weight of ancient folly. They learned too much, which ultimately led them to their doom.

  • If they get it wrong, everyone in the party must make a [[/save 14 wisdom]] saving throw. On a success, they are able to remain standing and suffer no ill effects. On a failure, they are pushed to the floor and knocked prone for a moment, taking [[/damage 1d6 psychic]] damage and a fierce headache rips through their minds. The voice within the Well of Orbis then says:

    Just like the Shent, you have learnt much but also nothing.

4. Depths Revealed

Bubbles rise from the pool as a large fire seems to form under the water. Steam escapes in gentle wisps, curling upward and enveloping the area in a deep mist. Within the shroud, your senses heighten, and you glimpse beneath the waters a vast underwater city, its once-grand structures now languishing in decay.

This section is based upon the parties' knowledge of the ancient Sedyri. If the party cannot answer a question or answers incorrectly, then move on to the next question or proceed to scoring if all the questions have been asked and answered.

Sedyri Knowledge

Anyone within the party with [[/knowledge legends]] immediately recognizes that the Well of Orbis is showing a stylised version of the sunken city myth and will likely ask questions about the Sedyri.

As the characters stand before the pool of water, a strangely dispassionate voice speaks in a monotone:

Question: Who is more ancient, the Sedyri or the Aedir?

Anyone in the party who answers correctly, with the Sedyri, is correct, and they hear a small ping and a quiet, almost imperceptible sigh. Anyone succeeding on a [[/check insight 12]] will be able to remember that this was noted by several scholars throughout the Expedition Challenge.

Second Question: What two elements did the Sedyri venerate?

The answer to this question is difficult, but if anyone within the party answers Fire & Water, they hear a small ping and a quiet, almost imperceptible sigh. If anyone has [[/knowledge legends]], they know the answer to this question automatically, as it is fairly well-known information.

Third Question: What island is said to contain ancient intact Sedyri ruins?

This final question is very difficult to answer, but anyone who attempts it, as no one in the party has likely heard the answer yet, except possibly from a conversation with Fernis Ossa. The correct answer is the mistbound island of Kadisos. Anyone with [[/knowledge legends]] may try a [[/check history 17]] and if successful, they recall learning about this trivia in a tome that discusses the myths and legends of the ancient Sedyri.

Scoring Success or Failure

Answering any question correctly gives the party a single point, which the GM should keep track of. These points should not be revealed to the party until the final section @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.zgWKNYcDPuNbjPkw#a-key-from-chaos]{A key from Chaos}. However, upon completing this echo and answering all the questions, determine whether the party answered all the questions correctly or not, and read the corresponding response from the voice.

  • If the party managed to answer every question, the voice within the Well of Orbis imparts a piece of sage advice:

    The Sedyri were once a vibrant, dynamic, and implacable culture, experiencing many periods of growth, collapse, and resurgence. They have withstood the test of time for untold millennia... perhaps they can do so again.

  • If they get it wrong, everyone in the party must make a [[/save 14 wisdom]] saving throw. On a success, they are able to remain standing and suffer no ill effects. On a failure, they are pushed to the floor and knocked prone for a moment, taking [[/damage 1d6 psychic]] damage and a fierce headache rips through their minds. The voice within the Well of Orbis then says:

    The Sedyri fell, sinking into the depths of the world, and their people are scattered and lost, just like you are.

A Key from Chaos

With a loud ping, the well’s ethereal light begins to fade. The soft glow that once illuminated the surroundings now casts long, unsettling shadows that twist and writhe along the eerie stone walls of the gorge. You can feel the now familiar yet unsettling voice slithers through your mind, weaving its way into your thoughts like dark tendrils of smoke.

We are finished.. heroes.

The Challenge Key

If the party answered six or more of the questions correctly, they hear the following and the @UUID[Item.WUeU31rhRz7YQCO1]{Well Challenge Key} appears from nothing in front of them.

Knowledge can be a great gift, a weapon in the right hands, one that will serve you well in the trials and challenges to come. Congratulations..

If the party instead answered fewer than six questions correctly, they hear the following and the @UUID[Item.WUeU31rhRz7YQCO1]{Well Challenge Key} also appears from nothing in front of them.

Despite your clear lack of knowledge, if you have the bravery to carry on, that is still an admirable trait and worthy of reward. Knowledge is important, but so is the will to carry on.

Orbis Attunement: The Challenge Key

Any character who helped the party acquire the Challenge Key advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 anachraenum1WellKey]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

With the @UUID[Item.WUeU31rhRz7YQCO1]{Well Challenge Key} in hand, the party can now either move on to the other two sites and collect the remaining keys, or if this is the final key they need, they can head back to All-Fable Keep in Ordain.
Hidden Campsite.soverview: The party discovers Krator's Hall in the Wedgelands north of Ordain and not far from the Bloodwoods. Here, the party finds a location that the Anachraenum typically uses for training Wayfinders in survival skills, but it has been specifically set up instead to focus on the mysterious Well of Orbis, which also resides at the site. The party will be challenged with a number of puzzles and skill checks testing their knowledge of the history and lore of Ember.
Hidden Campsite.sexposition: The towering structure ahead attracts your attention, and this can only be Krator's Hall, that Arcos Sarinland spoke of, and the location for one of the Expedition Challenges! Just beyond the hall, your gaze is drawn to a shimmering pool of water, its surface sparkling with a soft, white magical energy. Encircled by glowing stones, the well casts a gentle light, illuminating the dark corners of the gorge surrounding it.
Hidden Campsite.ssummary: We successfully completed the puzzles set up by the Anachraenum and recovered the Well Challenge Key for the Expedition Challenge.

The Wayfinder's Gauntlet.name: The Wayfinder's Gauntlet
The Wayfinder's Gauntlet.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event takes place within the Chamber of Agaseros, a mysterious area created hundreds of years ago and powered by powerful arcane magic and esoteric technology. This massive arena in the lower levels of All-Fable Keep was made to train Anachraenum guild members in a variety of combat and exploration techniques, but is generally off-limits, given how dangerous it can be.

In this event, the characters can:

  • Battle various creatures, such as the @UUID[Actor.Lw8HeAY64cjHnuQq]{Anachraenum Aetherial}'s, many @UUID[Actor.MNWRuR4oQQP7EUgD]{Shades of Agaseros} and a final encounter will a huge @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU]{Vespian Hydral}.

  • Survive a variety of traps and hazards, along with moving platforms that can make navigation extremely difficult.

  • Compete directly with the Fulgurite Blades in their efforts to reach the final chamber.

Scene

For the descriptive and exploration gameplay about the area itself, refer to the Area Walkthrough:@UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ]{Chamber of Agaseros}

The Testing Chamber

The small antechamber in front of the Chamber doors is not particularly interesting, made of stone floors and typical white Ordani brick walls. However, the door in front of the party is mesmerizing in its complexity and art of magical construction.

The party can speak with Eveis Brighstone here, but she makes the situation and the task ahead quite clear, and as the party approaches, you can read them the following:

Greetings heroes! I hope you are hale and healthy!

She seems to be genuinely pleased that you succeeded with the three previous tasks, as her usually reserved demeanor has changed to one of genuine excitement and pride.

Congratulations are in order as I see you have managed to gather all three of the keys! They are required to open the Chamber door ahead, but I would warn you to be cautious when approaching the doors themselves. Hold out the keys ahead of you, and they should open without issue.

Talking with Eveis Brightstone

Eveis is outside the Chamber to provide those entering with some measure of safety. She will warn the party as they enter that the Chamber is extremely dangerous and while it has been prepared for the Expedition Challenge to some extent, the Chamber has a mind of its own in a way and it will try to kill the party if they are careless and try to push ahead too quickly.

If the party tries to ask Eveis for help, or for information on the Chamber, she will refuse and answer:

I'm afraid not, dear ones, you must attempt this challenge on your own.

The party might try to convince her to reveal something. Characters who succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 20]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 20]] learn that the area inside is particularly challenging and involves conquering a series of increasingly dangerous challenges.

If anyone in the party or everyone has already used up their@UUID[Item.jggar2bndAvZthdS]{Frozen Tear} item given to them by Eveis, she will say the following:

Unfortunately, the Frozen Tear would have likely been very useful inside the Chamber, but I imagine it served you well before. That is why I am here, and if you fall, I will try to intervene at the last moment. Doing so means you'll have to start over from the beginning of the Chamber, and I will need to reset its challenges.

The Chamber Door

The party can investigate the door and anyone with [[/knowledge rituals]] realizes that the magic used here is quite extraordinary. Not only is the chamber door a masterpiece of magical construction, but there are layers upon layers of runic symbols from various cultures, all used to bind and contain immense magical power.

Characters who succeed on [[/skill inv 18]] check realize that the Chamber Door is used regularly and has been recently opened due to the long marks on the floor and disturbed dust pushed to both sides.

Magical Resonance

Examining the magical runes floating around the door in greater depth can be achieved by anyone with the [[/knowledge rituals]] in addition to a successful [[/skill arcana 17]] [[/skillCheck arcana 19]] and yields the following information based on the result.

  • Result of 14+ This door was created by a mortal and not some greater being. There are mistakes, although minor, in the construction that suggest the magic contained here is unstable.

  • Result of 18+ With [[/knowledge aedir]] or [[/knowledge shent]] or [[/knowledge cosmology]]], how this magical chamber remains active after all these years is a mystery, but studying it more closely you can see that it not only uses Shent, Aedir runic symbols, but also seems to use strange symbols that suggest it connects and draws energy from the moons and inner realms as well.

  • Success. This door was created by a mortal and not some greater being. There are mistakes, although minor, in the construction that suggest the magic contained here is unstable.

  • Critical Success. With [[/knowledge aedir]] or [[/knowledge shent]] or [[/knowledge cosmology]]], how this magical chamber remains active after all these years is a mystery, but studying it more closely you can see that it not only uses Shent, Aedir runic symbols, but also seems to use strange symbols that suggest it connects and draws energy from the moons and inner realms as well.

Runic Explosions

The doors of the chamber are highly tuned and if any member of the aprty appraoches without holding out the three keys and attmepets to touch teh door itselfdirectly they must make a [[/save dexterity 14]] saving throw or suffer [[/damage 1d8 lightning]] damage risk taking damage from [[/hazard 4 reflex lightning health]]{Runic Explosion}.

Entering the Chamber

Entering the Chamber

When the party is prepared and committed to enter the Chamber of Agaseros, mark the outcome below which will trigger a Scene transition that moves the characters into the area map for this event.

Area Walkthrough

A full room-by-room walkthrough of all three levels of the Chamber of Agaseros is provided in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ]{Chamber of Agaseros} journal. As the Gamemaster you should start by briefly reviewing the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.tEZnHQOPALaXewgH]{Gameplay Details} which apply to all levels of the chamber.

The party will begin their exploration in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.OX99OJy9EkqeJkcw]{Chamber Foyer}.

[[/outcome entered]]

The party's objective within the Chamber of Agaseros is to complete the gauntlet and defeat the @UUID[Actor.N33UoQCnyZc3tYTU]{Vespian Hydral} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1Fy8k7745vkwIofJ.JournalEntryPage.RiVzSitNZsn7qsQp]{Main Reservoir}.

Luxarum Attunement: Completing the Challenge

If the party manages to defeat the Fulgurite Blades in addition to the chamber's challenges, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +2 anachraenum1GauntletTotalVictory]] at the conclusion of the event.

Alternately, if the party is defeated by the Fulgurite Blades after they complete the chamber's challenges, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 anachraenum1GauntletPartialVictory]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has completed the area map, they have completed the Expidition Challenge itself and the reminaing task is to head back to the main hall of of All-Fable Keep in the event @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.O42tiNiFefHiNMiZ]{Closing Ceremonies}.
The Wayfinder's Gauntlet.soverview:
The party returns to All-Fable Keep with all three Challenge Keys from the locations they've completed for the Expedition Challenge. They can now venture below All-Fable Keep and find the locked door to the Chamber of Agaseros, where Eveis Brightsone is outside. Her presence is curious, but she insists she is merely observing and offers the party some cryptic hints, suggesting they may not be the only party attempting the Chamber at this time.

Once inside, the party must face some of the most dangerous and even deadly challengers they've encountered so far. It seems the Anachraenum is not holding back, and as they progress, they realize they are competing directly with the Fulgurite Blades, who are also within the chamber at the same time, and only one team can win the Expedition Challenge!
The Wayfinder's Gauntlet.sexposition: As you traverse the dimly lit corridors beneath All-Fable Keep, traveling downward for what feels like an eternity, an overwhelming magical presence begins to pulse ahead of you, washing over your body in waves. You emerge into a vast chamber, your breath catching as you behold the massive doors of the Chamber of Agaseros. The doors loom before you, casting a vibrant and intense purple glow throughout the area. Large runes twist and dance across the surface of the doors, and you feel the energy in the air itself. Standing just next to the doors, you spot once again the large floating figure of Eveis Brightstone, who is studying your arrival in turn with a wide smile of greeting.
The Wayfinder's Gauntlet.ssummary: We successfully defeated the fearsome Vespian Hydral created by Agaseros and finished the Expedition Challenge!

Closing Ceremonies.name: Closing Ceremonies
Closing Ceremonies.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This event takes place upon the parties return from the Chamber of Agaseros. Whether or not they won first place or the Fulgurite Blades managed to win instead, the party can speak to @UUID[Actor.FYprIclhoDOI8FI4]{Arcos Sarinland} in the main hall of All-Fable Keep. Here, the guildmaster congratulates the party and awards them full membership in the Anachraenum.

Scene

@UUID[Scene.emberVistaOrdInt]{Vista: Ordain Interiors}

Speaking with Arcos

With the Expiston Challenge over, the party can now speak with Arcos to receive their rewards, including full membership into the Anachraenum guild of scholars and adventurers, money, and their choice of magical items that Arcos offers them.

@Embed[Actor.FYprIclhoDOI8FI4]

Arcos steps forward, clasping your hands in his, and beaming widely.

Well done indeed! I hope the Chamber was a trial worthy of your talents but not too deadly in the end, hmm?

He pauses and looks at you all again, though you notice that while his mouth is still smiling, a knot of almost imperceptible worry is written across his face.

I think you more than deserve the rewards you were promised; here, let me give you these.

He digs through the large pockets of his coat for a few moments and then pulls out a handful of shiny glinting objects. He then hands you an Anacharaenum Medallion before stuffing the rest back into his coat.

With this, you are now full members! You can access the archives below to research information, conduct your own studies, and borrow some of the relics and artifacts we hold in our collection.

Each member of the party receives an @UUID[Item.fdy47m1duEeHMYJa]{Anachraenum Medallion} from Arcos, in addition, he hands one member a heavy pouch of gold coins[[/award party 300gp]].

Speaking with Arcos Sarlinland

In the aftermath of the Expedition Challenge, Arcos is worried about many things, and while he is pleased the party succeeded, he has learned that they are working with Fernis in some capacity. This makes him suspicious of the party overall, and he doesn't fully trust them. A successful [[/skill insight 15]] check reveals that he's preoccupied with something as well, and that there is quite a bit more going on than he is willing to talk to the party about.

He is also worried about the results of the Challenge. Whether or not the party won or came in second, he knows that out of all the groups attempting, only the Fulguraite Blades, the Salt Breakers, Vortera, and the player party succeeded in conquering the Chamber. Mug & Cap went missing during the Keystone Challenge events, while Lanterns Road all perished in the Chamber of Agaseros before Eveis could save them.

Archive Rewards

If the party asks Arcos about the rewards that they were promised, Arcos will jump slightly and respond with:

Oh! My apologies, why of course! Here, let me show you!

Arcos then goes on to explain that the party may each pick one item from the @UUID[RollTable.iSC4eHqYFCubhfPM]{Amaranthine Archives Artifacts} roll table, or receive 1 item at random. The party may only look at the unidentified sections of these items, and the full breadth of the item is not revealed to them until they receive the item itself.

This might feel slightly unfair to the party, but Arcos assures them that if they are not happy with the item they have chosen, they can return the relic to the Archives and receive another one from the display list at any time, for a small fee.

A successful [[/skill insight 18]] check reveals that Arcos finds the idea that the party receives magical items with little knowledge about their full abilities hilarious, and he is making every effort not to grin.

Full Members of the Anachraenum

If the party asks Arcos about what's next and what the guild expects of them, Arcos will respond slowly at first, but you can read the following:

Nothing. You may go where you please, study, and explore at your own leisure. Of course, as full members, you now have access to the archives. There, you may come across some key snippets of information that could lead you to lost treasures and objects of historical significance. Should you make a find, please return to the keep, and we shall buy these from you to add to our collection!

Oh, and if you're looking for something I might have a lead on, I may ask you to investigate something in a nearby location soon. I'm not sure if you've come across or have any knowledge of the Crumbling Spire out in the Golden Flats, but I recently came across some new information. We might soon be able to open its fabled locked entrance doors and access what's waiting inside!

After the party has finished speaking with Arcos, he thanks them once again and excuses himself. Many other things hold his attention, and you can read the following:

Well then, I'm sure I shall be seeing you all very soon! Please come and see me if you have any further questions, but I must get back to my administrative duties! Well done once again!

He then hurries from the hall with a brisk gait, humming slightly to himself.

The Investigation Truly Begins

After the party receives their rewards and Arcos hurries off, they will notice Fernis emerging from the shadows nearby. Having overheard the conversation, she is both deep in thought and happy to see that the party succeeded in completing the Expedition Challenge. You can read the following:

@Embed[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]

As you begin to leave the hall, you notice a shape emerge from next to one of the wooden beams along the side of the main hall.

Well met friends, I trust the final challenge was not too arduous, hmm?

Fernis winks at you and smiles broadly, before a shadow seems to flicker across her features for a moment.

Now that the challenge is over, we can begin our investigation. I’m sure that you will agree that something is happening both here within the Anachraenum and within the city at large. While I am focused on my guild, I’m not blind to the rising number of chaotic events, and I fear that Orodain is heading toward a climatic event that we are ill prepared to face. Together, I hope we can uncover the truth of things.

Speaking with Fernis

Fernis is ecstatic with the party upon their completion of the Expulsion Challenge and welcomes them into the Anachraenum with open arms. She is also pleased that now she can progress her own investigation into the death of the previous Guildmaster, Veron Longspear.

Patience is Key

Fernis will go on to explain that while she has some ideas on where to start her investigation, she also needs the party to be patient.
