She believes that Arcos will have no choice but to come to the party for help in the following days, as she has heard rumors that something massive has been uncovered.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill per 13]] check[[/skillCheck society 15]] are able to convince Fernis to share one detail about her hunch, which is that the Crumbling Spire in the Golden Flats may, after thousands of years, be close to opening. This may mean that one of the largest and most important locations related to the Aedir Empire will be able to be explored outside the Starshield continent itself and would provide a treasure trove of knowledge and wealth. A prize that many within Ordain would likely kill for.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party has now finished the Expedition Challenge questline, and while they have succeeded in their goal to join the Anachraenum and become full members so that Fernis can progress her internal investigation, Arcos now sees the party as reliable enough to head out into the field on a critical mission to the Crumbling Spire. This quest leads directly onto the Crumbling Spire questline, which takes place in Chapter 4.
Closing Ceremonies.soverview:
The party completed the Chamber of Agaseros and now returns upward to All-Fable Keep. Here they find Arcos Sarinland, who is beaming with delight. He provides the party with Anachraenum medallions, symbols of their full membership into the Anachraenum guild, and reminds them that they can now access all the facilities within the keep, including the restricted section!

Fernis Ossa is also present and eager to talk with the party now that they have become full members. She tasks them with keeping a low profile but hints that her investigation can now proceed with their help. The next stage involves investigating the legendary Crumbling Spire in the Golden Flats.
Closing Ceremonies.sexposition: You step into the main hall of All-Fable Keep, the echoes of your footsteps bouncing against the walls. Soft light streams in from the high windows, casting dappled patterns across the polished stone floor and illuminating the banners and tapestries of the Anachraenum overhead. Arcos Sarinland stands at the center of the hall and, upon seeing you, he approaches you with open arms, his energy contagious. "Welcome back!" he exclaims, showing his wide Keth smile, his voice rich with pride. "You’ve done wonderfully in the Chamber below, congratulations, I couldn't be more proud of you all!"
Closing Ceremonies.ssummary: We successfully completed the second Expedition Challenge of the Anacharaenum and became full members! Fernis is extremely impressed, and her investigation into the death of her mentor and previous guildmaster can proceed with our help.

Troublemaking Duo.name: Troublemaking Duo
Troublemaking Duo.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event, the party encounters . They are a mischievous pair who can provide the party with some information about the challenge. In this event, the party can:

  • Meet a duo of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.MsiM0222IPxjGTQQ]{Waerd} adventurers named "Mug" and "Cap" who are traveling to @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain} to participate in the upcoming Expedition Challenge.

  • Learn some details about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum} organization and the Expedition Challenge.

  • Perhaps be tricked by the duo into misunderstanding the stakes of the challenge.

Portrait & Vista WIP

Mug & Cap are getting an upgrade to full characters with actor bios and portraits and this event will change to a vista encounter in the future.

Meeting Mug & Cap

Surveying the Duo

Any character with [[/culture emberWaerd]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check recognizes that both of these characters are from the Waerd culture and have extensive Waix Tattoos that are especially focused on battle and hunting prowess. It's likely that the duo are experienced and deadly monster hunters.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success: You have encountered Waix tattoos before and know that Waerds Tattoo themselves ritually throughout their lives, recording important events, successful hunts, or battles they may have taken part in to their own bodies as intricate patterns and symbols.

A character with [[/ancestry emberKiska]] or [[/ancestry emberWirrun]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check recognizes the striking combination of mixed ancestral traits that the taller figure exhibits, with the lean physique of a Wirrun but the luxurious glowing mane of a Kiska.

The party can choose to stop and talk to the two arguing figures, and if they do, read the following:

The two figures turn toward you, and you notice that the taller one is a Wirrun with a mix of Kiska traits, notably a magnificent blue glowing tail and more humanoid facial features, while the smaller is a small Thornling wearing a large blue cap. Both are covered in striking tattoos and sport a number of curved, wicked-looking weapons strapped to scale mail made from what appears to be a creature of some kind.

Oh, who are you then?

The Thornling speaks in a voice similar to a small child's and looks at you quizzically before tilting their head, awaiting an answer.

Well, clearly they are adventurers like us, Cap, I mean, look at them..

The taller figure is also staring at you intensely, with his hands hovering near the sharp-looking short sword at his belt. The Thornling, however, seems more at ease and immediately perks up, hurriedly replying.

Oh, well, of course! Where are our manners? We are Mug and Cap! Fearsome adventurers from Oshclaw, are you heading to Ordain for the Expedition Challenge as well?

Talking with Mug & Cap

The party can engage Mug (Neutral, Waerd Kiska + Wirrun, he/him) and Cap (Neutral, Waerd Thornling, they/them), a pair of @UUID[Actor.mNKKDsvvNi8f0Pel]{Anachraenum Adventurer}, in conversation, during which they can provide additional details about themselves or about the Expedition Challenge which are described below.

A successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check infers that Mug & Cap are friendly, yet not entirely truthful, and there is a small glimmer of wariness that underpins the words they choose.

  • Result of 19+ Critical Success: Mug & Cap are not hostile and are not interested in fighting the party, but they would very much prefer less competition in the Expedition Challenge and are trying to scare the party off.

Any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectThou]{Detect Thoughts} spell on Mug & Cap immediately realizes that they are deliberately lying to the party to scare them away from the event, as the duo sees the party as competition.

If the party accuses Mug & Cap of lying to them or trying to mislead them, the duo will sheepishly apologize. They don't have ill intent and were trying to scare the party off, which they will openly admit and attempt to smooth things over.

The Expedition Challenge?

Oh! The Expedition Challenge is an event run by this guild in Ordain, you see, called the Anachraenum. You compete with other groups or teams in super deadly challenges and win gold and the location of some secret dungeon that the Anachraenum keeps hidden if you win. We heard about the last one, five years ago, and the winner... what was her name... Fernos, Fernas, Fern... something or other! She became rich and famous afterward, I think… Anyway, when we heard they were going to run another one this year, we got on the next boat!

The Anachraenum

The Anachraenum is simply the fancy name for the Lore Hunters guild! It's like this big organization of archaeologists, explorers, treasure seekers, and adventurers who travel around the world, exploring ruins and discovering treasure. Their home base is in Ordain, and they have this massive castle called the All-Fable Keep where they keep all the stuff they find!

We've never been to Ordain before but have heard tales of the adventuring Anachraenum in our homeland. They are all about treasure seeking, monster slaying, and all-round exploration which suits us perfectly.

Your travel?

Didn't ya hear us before? We are from Oshclaw!

We've been traveling across the Arctus Plateau for several weeks, left from Toraga. Its been pretty quiet, too quiet, too boring compared to the Lowlands. It's so peaceful here, ugh.

We did get to kill a rampaging monster about two weeks ago, some kind of giant two-legged bird. Nothing fun like that recently, though.

As the party leaves Mug & Cap, read the following:

As you and your party turn away from Mug and Cap, the argument between the two begins again, each fervently trying to gain the upper hand. Gradually, however, it fades into the background behind you, and the sounds of the Golden Flats and the rustle of nearby grasses rises once more.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event introduces the party to the existence of the upcoming Expedition Challenge and to one of the groups of adventurers who will be participating in it.

  • The party can travel to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0]{All-Fable Keep} and investigate the challenge directly in the @UUID[.kelVZv24HBN9yfK2]{An Upcoming Challenge} event.

  • The party can gain sponsorship to enter the challenge themselves after meeting @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.vkXY7W6Z7z1p6clq]{An Auspicious Acquaintance} event.
Troublemaking Duo.soverview: As the party explores the Golden Flats biome, they have a chance to encounter an adventuring duo named Mug and Cap from the Waerd city of the Oathclaw. These two troublemakers are on their way to Ordain after traveling overland from Toraga and they are bubbling with excitement to join the upcoming Expedition Challenge.
Troublemaking Duo.sexposition: Amid the gentle breeze and the ambient sounds of the surrounding flats, you suddenly hear shouting and what appears to be a prolonged argument nearby. As you approach you notice two figures, a tall figure with a magnificent mane and tail of glowing fur accompanied by a stout mushroom-capped Thornling standing beside a large boulder. Neither seem to have noticed you, as they are deeply engrossed in their confrontation.
Troublemaking Duo.ssummary: We met the lively adventuring duo called Mug and Cap in the Golden Flats, who were questionably useful in answering our questions. Apparently, they are bound for Ordain and are looking to join an event called the Expedition Challenge.

Scholar in Need.name: Scholar in Need
Scholar in Need.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event introduces the party to the Ordani scholar Losten Vax, a participant in the upcoming Expedition Challenge. Losten has stopped here to research and translate an ancient ruin he's uncovered. In this event, the characters can:

  • Meet Losten Vax and learn about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.lRAxRZ4doNSLC6zw]{Anachraenum}'s Expedition Challenge.

  • Learn about the Cinderspar pillar and the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.4RM8MIiCDWMFv2yr]{Sedyri} culture that created it.

  • Investigate the ruins for themselves.

Meeting Losten Vax

From a Distance

If the party wishes to study this stranger from afar, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] an [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check is able to notice the following:

  • The stranger is intently inspecting the surface of the peculiar stone, frequently referencing the contents of the book they're carrying.

  • The stranger's garb is remarkably fashionable for such remote environs.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 13]] [[/skillCheck society 13]] check is able to readily identify that this stranger's garb originated in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}.

  • Characters with [[/culture emberOrdani]] automatically succeed.

As the party passes by or approaches the figure, read the following aloud:

The figure on the hill appears to be Human, and they are holding a book in one hand as they peer intently downwards at the black rock with a frown upon their face. Their clothing is immaculate with long hemmed trousers, a thick waistband of shimmering red cloth, and a delicate floppy-looking hat to shade their eyes from the sun.

He turns to you as you approach, his eyes springing fearfully to your appearance and weapons, and his hand reaches down to the small dagger he wears on his waistband.

Wait, stop right there … who are you!

He does not back away and stands his ground, but it's clear that he is extremely wary of you and could bolt at any second.

Talking with Losten Vax

Losten Vax (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, he/him) is an intellectual and perpetually nervous scholar. Before talking with Losten, the party must succeed in calming him down and earning some measure of trust. This can be achieved in a number of different ways including:

  • A successful [[/skill persuasion 13]] or [[/skill deception 15]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 13]] or [[/skillCheck deception 15]] check manages to calm his fears and realizes that you are not bandits or anyone attempting to steal from him after all.

  • A character with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or [[/knowledge legends]] or who succeeds on an [[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check can notice something interesting in what Losten is investigating and express curiosity, which diffuses the situation.

  • A character with [[/path emberObsidianAntiquary]], [[/path emberAcademyDropout]], or who succeeds on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check can persuade Vosten of their own scholastic interest in discovery.

Losten is Spooked

If the party does not succeed in calming Losten, the event ends as the scholar disappears.

With a small sound, like the chirping of a bird, this timid-looking scholar, now even more afraid, does not spare you a second glance as he slams his book shut and runs down the hill, disappearing into the grasses of the flats and quickly vanishing from sight.

Losten is Calmed

If successful in persuading and calming Losten, then you can read the following:

Oh, thank goodness! I thought you might have been bandits! My name is Losten Vax, and I’m a trainee with the Anachraenum. I found this strange ancient stonework on my way back to Ordain to participate in the upcoming Expedition Challenge, but I can’t for the life of me figure out which ancient culture it’s from!

The party can continue their conversation with Losten Vax, during which time he can provide additional information about himself and the Expedition Challenge with responses to common questions provided below.

The Expedition Challenge

The Expedition Challenge is the second event run by the Anachraenum; the first was held five years ago and was won by Fernis Ossa. Participating in the event grants full membership into the Anachraenum guild immediately, along with a pouch full of gold and the chance to borrow one of the guild's artifacts from the archives. You can compete alone or in teams, drawing in people from all over the region and even beyond! It's very exciting, and although I may not be much good at fighting or combat parts, I hope to find some like-minded souls to join up with in the city!

The Anachraenum

The Anachraenum is also known as the Lore Hunters guild by many! It's a large organization of archaeologists, explorers, treasure seekers, and adventurers who travel around the world, exploring ruins and discovering treasure. Our main base of operations is in Ordain, known as the All-Fable Keep, where we store and catalog the artifacts and knowledge we find in the Amaranthine Archives.

I'm what's called a "trainee", but I have mostly spent the last few years staying close to Ordain. I'm trying to make a breakthrough which will gain me more esteem in the eyes of my peers.

The Black Stone

I'm not really sure what it is. It clearly seems infused with some kind of magic and appears very old, yet I can't find any references linking black stones like this to any culture I know in the region that would make sense. Unless it's Sedyri, but I only know that they were an ancient ocean-faring culture from long before the Shattering.

Your travel?

I was in Helkas recently, but I left a few weeks ago to head towards Ordain. I had hoped to stay for the Dusktide Festival, a big celebration they have every year or so, but I was worried I'd be late and so I departed before the festival started. It was a shame to miss it.

Travel together?

No, I prefer to journey on my own — and I already have a few friends in the Anachraenum who I've promised to join with for the challenge ahead.

The Sedyri Ruins

The party can try to study the black rock themselves, but they probably won't learn much. It is an extremely weathered and ancient stone, but they might learn a few details.

Examination of the stone with a successful [[/check history 15]] [[/skillCheck science 15]] or by someone with [[/path emberObsidianAntiquary]] or [[/knowledge legends]] recognizes that this is indeed a black stone typically crafted by a very mysterious culture called the Sedyri. Records, myths, and legends state that they were known for creating durable black stone structures using magic, fire, and water through a strange process similar to quenching metals in water.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success: You recognize that this ruin is made of a material famously associated with the ancient Sedyri that they called Cinderspar. The material itself is extremely durable and can withstand weathering and the passage of time for many thousands of years. It is also very light and is constructed through the precise injection of near-boiling water via magical means into melted volcanic stone, creating bubbles of compressed water within the rock. The pillar is likely between 10,000 and 100,000 years old and predates even the Aedir Empire.

Examining the stone carefully and with a successful [[/skill arcana 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] yields only a small glimmer of understanding that this stone would have crumbled to dust long ago and is only being held together with faint remnants of abjuration magic.

Signara Attunement: Ruins Identified

Any character who successfully identifies the Sedyri ruins advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 anachraenum1ScholarRuins]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event introduces the party to the existence of the upcoming Expedition Challenge and to one of the adventurers who will be participating in it.

  • The party can travel to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0]{All-Fable Keep} and investigate the challenge directly in the @UUID[.kelVZv24HBN9yfK2]{An Upcoming Challenge} event.

  • The party can gain sponsorship to enter the challenge themselves after meeting @UUID[Actor.A2SrOhUvUVuV7os0]{Fernis Ossa} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAnachrnArc1.JournalEntryPage.vkXY7W6Z7z1p6clq]{An Auspicious Acquaintance} event.
Scholar in Need.soverview: The party encounters a young Anachraenum scholar named Losten Vax who is deeply engrossed in translating a Cinderspar pillar, a magically infused black rock created by the ancient Sedyri culture thousands of years ago. While the pillar's weathered surface has little interesting information, studying it will reveal some details about the ancient Sedyri.
Scholar in Need.sexposition: As you travel through the soft grasses of the Golden Flats, you see in the distance a low rise or mound. At first, nothing seems to be out of the ordinary, but silhouetted against the sky you spot a humanoid figure standing with a book in hand at the summit of the hill itself. As you move closer, you recognize that this stranger is standing in front of a square rock that is almost pure black in color and shimmering with a slightly luminous quality.
Scholar in Need.ssummary: We encountered a timid scholar named Losten Vax, a trainee member of the Anchraenum who was studying an extremely weathered pillar of a lost culture called the Sedyri. We managed to help them in their research, and they revealed some information on an event happening soon in Ordain called the Expedition Challenge.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This side quest occurs during Chapter 3, and can begin any time after the party arrives in Ordain.

Difficulty

"Spreading Sickness" is designed for a party of Level 4 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 3 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon successful completion of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200.JournalEntryPage.K991Ggiwrd9PbadG]{Secondary Sources}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200.JournalEntryPage.Byl5asdRp3YzqNrL]{Missing Persons}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200.JournalEntryPage.oWBdpAjAyc4fAFlH]{Unhallowed} Events.

Point of No Return: The Marlstone Gala

The [[/eventState chain2Meeting]] Event serves as a point of no return for certain Chapter 3 Main Quests. Once the characters complete this Event, they can no longer continue or complete the Events of @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1]{Disgraced House} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders}.

Summoned to the Hallows to once more join forces with Ankarist to work on a investigation of critical importance. A new, dangerous sickness has appeared in Ordain, and already threatens the lives of dozens of citizens, and Veiled Chain now relies on the help of the party to make the difference. However, this problem is not as simple as it seems, and old enemies lurk in dark, forgotten places within Ordain.

Armed with leads across several city districts, the party searches for weaknesses in the city’s infrastructure, interviews healers about a new illness afflicting forge workers along the waterways, and eventually discovers a dangerous contaminant flowing through the mighty Destine River and threatening to poison all of Ordain.

The investigation takes them deep underground to ancient ruins that predate Ordain, where they uncover old foes — the Mutagists — at their usual tricks. They find human experimentation, deadly new Drake variants, and a harrowing plan to harvest Ember energy from human bodies.

Yet another layer of intrigue awaits when they return to the surface: someone is inciting Ordain’s common folk and refugees, turning them against the city. With a violent uprising brewing, the party must go undercover to find the movement’s core and shut it down before things spiral out of control.

Overview.soverview:
During their time in Ordain, the party is duly summoned to the Hallows to once again join forces with Ankarist of the Veiled Chain. Their mission: to investigate a new and dangerous sickness that has appeared in the city. This situation is of critical importance, and the characters must learn of a new, dangerous sickness that has appeared in Ordain. Already spread thin due to other issues in the city, the Veiled Chain now relies on the help of the party to make the difference where they can't. However, this problem is not as simple as it seems, and old enemies lurk in dark, forgotten places within Ordain.

Vetted by Ankarist and proven by their previous actions, the party is given the autonomy to conduct their investigation as they see fit. The Chain is stretched thin, and Ankarist will conduct his own investigation while the party chases down their leads. Will the party make the right choices? Can they find every clue needed to stop the plots of foes hidden in Ordain’s alleys and parlors, or will they find themselves in over their heads?

In “Spreading Sickness,” the party is drawn into a troubling web of plots meant to destabilize and destroy Ordain from within. As their investigation unfolds, they begin to uncover a deeper conspiracy that seeks to manipulate, kidnap, and turn the people of Ordain against each other. Allies are few, support is thin, and danger grows in every shadow and alley as the party draws closer to the source the spreading sickness.

An Unexpected Requisition.name: An Unexpected Requisition
An Unexpected Requisition.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event sees the party receiving a request to meet from @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]. In short, the party:

  • Is contacted by a city courier and given a letter.

  • Receives instructions in the letter on how to reach Ankarist.

  • Can speak to the courier, though the courier knows little.

Taking the Letter

As you take the letter, the courier pulls out a notepad and pencil, makes a note about the delivery, and wishes you a good day. Then they head off to their next delivery.

The party can stop the courier to ask questions, but the courier knows little and will leave promptly afterward.

Who hired you?

I work for the city. I was assigned this message along with a bunch of others. This one did come directly from a Veiled Chain source though, if you go by the stamp on the envelope. Hopefully you’re not in any trouble!

How did you know where to find us?

The courier holds up a note for you to see, but not long enough to read the text on it.

I was given delivery instructions. The Chain seemed to know where to find you, which isn’t a shock. They watch everything and know who’s coming and going. Honestly, I doubt there’s much that happens in the city they don’t know about.

Opening the Letter

Examining the Envelope

The envelope is stamped with both a Veiled Chain symbol, and a symbol of the Hallows, with a number scribbled on the corner.

Characters with [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/culture emberOrdani]] know that the Hallows handles post in the city free of charge. The ink stamps indicate several things: the official Veiled Chain and Hallows stamps show that both organizations handled the documents directly. The Hallows stamp is common on city post. The number is for record-keeping, as the city handles thousands of messages a day.

Reading the Letter

The message within is handwritten, from Ankarist:

I hope this message finds you well,

I received word that you had arrived in the city, and your timing couldn't be better. There is a strange sickness affecting the people of Ordain, and I suspect it may be related to our previous cases I've worked.

As the Veiled Chain is light on manpower, and I need help, I would like to hire you on to assist with the investigation. Come to the Hallows and go to the entrance to the Underfoot. Then follow the directions below to reach me.

-Ankarist

The attached directions are a series of turns and landmarks for traversing the Underfoot.

Characters that have either [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/culture emberOrdani]] or who make a successful [[/skill history 14 passive]] know that Ordain was built over existing ruins and ancient pathways. The Hallows is home to the Underfoot, a network of tunnels and chambers rumored to hold secret meeting places and underground structures if one knows which turns to take.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has read the letter, they can head toward the Hallows to meet Ankarist.
An Unexpected Requisition.soverview: The party receives an official summons from a city courier instructing them to report to the Veiled Chain’s headquarters in the Hallows. A public-safety investigation is at hand.
An Unexpected Requisition.sexposition:
A city courier wearing the Hallows badge comes into view. They scan the street, and their gaze settles on you. They check a card in their hand and seem to confirm you’re the one they’re looking for. Moving toward you, they pull a sealed envelope from a shoulder bag.

Hello. I have an official message for you from the Veiled Chain. Instructions say to open it immediately.

They hold the envelope out, waiting for you to take it.
An Unexpected Requisition.ssummary: We have been summoned to meet with Ankarist and the Veiled Chain in the Hallows as soon as possible. He has some urgent issue, and provided us directions on how to reach the meeting point.

Ill Tidings.name: Ill Tidings
Ill Tidings.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event sees the party meeting with @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}, @UUID[Actor.m7bwxaSeiblzYyJw]{Shaar} and @UUID[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]{Serethus} to go over what information they have about the current illness, and to hand out assignments to the party. During this event the party can:

  • Learn about the sickness that is spreading through the city.

  • Learn that there's also a missing person's case ongoing.

  • Get guidance and suggestions on where to go from Serethus.

The Briefing

@embed[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]

@embed[Actor.m7bwxaSeiblzYyJw]

@embed[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]

If needed, Ankarist gives the party brief introductions to the people at the table:

Shaar

Shaar is the head of the Veiled Chain, an expert in forensics, and likely has the best eye for detail in the city. They are overseeing this meeting and will stand by to lend further aid if needed, but they won’t be part of the main investigation.

Serethus

Serethus is the resident expert on magical rituals, spellcraft, and alchemy. Like you, he is not a member of the Chain, and is attached to lend his expertise. Serethus has ideas on where to start, and I've got plans to assign those leads so we can divide efforts and cover ground rapidly.

Once the party is ready to get into the briefing, Ankarist begins:

Ankarist addresses you directly, as the others seem already up to speed:

In the past month or so a number of illnesses have stricken the city. While not itself an issue, and not even a Veiled Chain concern, the same illness keeps turning up, and the source is never determined. This is strange, and what drew our attention.

It's always the same thing: presents as wasting sickness, with headaches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, so forth. However, it never responds to typical medical treatment. While it does eventually run its course and vanish, it's remained a medical oddity.

As of this month, it's back, and worse than before. Rather than appearing in a few isolated cases and then vanishing, it has struck a good number of people, which means we might have a chance to track it to the source.

About the Illness

A successful [[/skill medicine 14]] check confirms that the illness does indeed sound like a wasting sickness, which usually stems from tainted food and water. It should be relatively easy to treat with bed rest and fluids, but will keep spreading if the source isn't found.

Any leads on a source?

Ankarist says:

We have only gotten reports on the spike in the illness, not its distribution. That is something that needs to be established though. Maybe that's something you can determine as part of your assignment. If we know where the sick are most concentrated, we can probably find a source.

A foreboding Interruption

Once the first part of the above briefing is done, read aloud the following:

As you you are discussing the situation, another agent from the Chain approaches, drawing Shaar's attention. They step aside to speak quietly for a moment, then Shaar returns to the group and interrupts:

Ankarist, something's come up with the missing person's case. I'm going to follow up on that information now. Report in when you have something Ankarist.

Ankarist nods.

We can take it from here.

Serethus nods as well, saying to Shaar:

Indeed we can! Wisdom and cunning guide you.

Offering an appreciative nod in response, Shaar steps away, leaving the spreading sickness in the party's hands.

From this point, the briefing can continue.

Serethus' suggestions

Serethus looks to Ankarist.

May I?

Ankarist nods.

Go right ahead.

Serethus offers a broad smile, and addresses you directly:

I believe it prudent to cast a wide net, in the hopes of catching more fish, or in this case, information. I would advise you to begin in Lower Ashvale, Lilifeld Stations and the Burns. These locations give you the best chance of finding the source, as it targets the food, health and industry of the city.

If there are no viable leads, then that at least helps rule out a few sections of the city!

He falls silent, and waits, as if expecting questions.

Why Lower Ashvale?

It has the largest healing house in the city.

He says this as though it were answer enough, but a moment later continues:

Speak to the healers there and see what they know about the illness. They might have some insight into this disease and how to treat it. If we are lucky, they might even know where to begin looking for a source!

I'll note: the symptoms do seem similar to wasting sickness, which is dangerous but treatable.

Why Lilifeld Stations?

Well, violence and unrest in the flats has put more pressure on Redrak to deliver grain to feed the city. The increased need to produce food might have resulted in them being less stringent about their standards.

That is not to say that Redrak is trying to poison us, just that it could be a cause!

To that end, visit the stations during operating hours, speak to foreman Tadrick Soles, and ask to examine the grain silos. Also look over any produce coming in from Redrak.

It might be poisoned, or worse, spoiling. If the city's food supply is tainted, the city could be in real trouble.

Why The Burns?

Serethus grimaces slighty.

This is a bit unpleasant to say, but, Janix Mance, a well known figure in the arts of Alchemy, is always trying to push the limits on process and method in the forges and workshops around the Burns. Such innovation is vital, but it can lead to recklessness and unforeseen consequences.

It's… possible that he may have introduced something into the local smithy ecosystem which would account for illness coming out of the Burns. The smoke from the burns travels far with just a little breeze, and could be making people ill all over.

Ankarist's Assignments

Seemingly satisfied, Ankarist straightens up, grabbing a notebook off the table, and tucking it away.

All right, I have a couple contacts in the Ordinate I want to talk to about this, to see if I can turn up some new leads or get a better overview of things.

While I'm doing that, I want you to follow up on Serethus' leads.

Serethus speaks up:

While I'm no means a mighty adventurer, I nonetheless would like to attend the investigation with the team, and lend my expertise where possible! In fact, we should begin with Lilifeld Stations, I want to see the state of the food coming into the city, last thing we need is a sick populace!

Ankarist nods to Serethus.

Fine with me.

In response, Serethus beams a toothy grin and grabs his things.

Excellent, I have some things to tend to right now, but I'll meet you at Lilifeld Station tomorrow, bright and early! This shall be most exciting.

As Serethus leaves Ankarist looks at you.

Any questions?

To Ankarist: Do we have to start with the Lilifeld Granary

No, you don't, however Serethus seems to think that's a good place to start. Make sure you go during daytime hours so you can speak to the foreman, and get access to records if you need them.

To Ankarist: When should we report in?

I'll be chasing down my own leads, and won't be back here for a bit, so there's no point having you report back in after each location is cleared. Instead, report back once you've checked out all three locations and can provide a broader overview of your findings.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once questions have duly been answered, the party is cut loose to go investigate, while Ankarist heads off to chase down his own leads. The party should proceed to one of the districts noted by Serethus. It's recommended they start with Lilifeld Station, but they can start with any location they like.
Ill Tidings.soverview: The characters meet with Ankarist, and meet Shaar, the leader of the Veiled Chain, to discuss recent events in the city and set a plan to investigate the source of a spreading illness afflicting the people of Ordain.
Ill Tidings.sexposition:
You follow the instructions on Ankarist’s note, taking several turns and walking down dimly lit stone hallways until you reach a well-appointed chamber filled with desks and chairs, and shelves of ledgers and scrolls. A handful of staff work at their stations, writing reports, reviewing files, or speaking in low voices.

At the center of the room is a large table where several people are gathered, Ankarist among them. As you enter, they look up at you, and Ankarist speaks:

You're here. Good, just in time. Let's get started.

He gestures for you to approach the table, where the group studies a map of the city.
Ill Tidings.ssummary: We met with Ankarist, Shaar, and Serethus at the Veiled Chain headquarters to discuss an issue with a spreading sickness in the city. We were assigned three locations to investigate: Lilifeld Stations, Lower Ashvale, and The Burns.

Looking Into Lilifeld Station.name: Looking Into Lilifeld Station
Looking Into Lilifeld Station.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event sees the party visiting the Lilifeld Granary, a landmark and key location found in the Lilifeld Stations district. Here, the party can interact with the locals, meet some key figures, and examine the facilities. They can also:

  • Meet a visiting dignitary from Redrak Fields: Eamon Mariflor

  • Investigate the newly upgraded and warded grain silos meant to keep the city's food safe.

  • Discover any bouts of illness in the area, gaining additional insights and leads.

Daytime Hours

Note that this event is intended to take place between dawn and dusk, and will only appear during that period. This event will not occur at night.

Meeting Serethus

If the party arrives the morning after @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200.JournalEntryPage.BT7XU3X6zdUlC6N4] then Serethus is waiting. Use the following readaloud. If the party arrives midday or later, adjust his greeting for the time of day.

If the party arrives the same day as Ill Tidings, or investigates another location first, then Serethus is not present, and the event continues without the readaloud. In that case, his part in any of the events the follow should also be ignored.

@embed[Actor.0XaohuZ6O3yijRTb]

As you approach the center of the station's chaos, you spot Serethus coming your way.

Good morning!

Pleasure to see you again. I see the foreman is already engaged, and the stations are as busy as ever. Let's not waste any time, and get our investigation started!

He immediately walks off toward the group, clearly expecting you to follow.

A Round of Introductions

@embed[Actor.X2nmQ7Ewt14lSR6g]

@embed[Actor.RLFMnPbPwqW4SEKr]

Eamon Mariflor

I am Eamon Mariflor, head of the Agrimage Consortium in Redrak. I’m visiting to make sure everything is in good order. With the increasing demands on our fields, I want to make sure all the links in the supply chain are strong. I’d heard that Lilifeld just finished upgrades on their silos with some impressive new magic, and I decided to come see them for myself.

Del Kalais

I am here specifically to escort Eamon around and make sure he stays safe. Not my usual assignment, but everybody else is busy with other things lately. I don't mind being a tour guide though, there's plenty to see in Ordain beyond big, magical grain silos!

Tadrick Soles (Ordani Human, he/him)

Tadrick Soles, manager here at the Lilifeld Granary. I keep the whole site running, and have been in charge for over a decade now if my memory serves me! Anything that happens here is done with my oversight.

Serethus (if present)

Serethus, a pleasure, I am but a humbler academic and spellcaster. I endeavor to make myself useful to anyone in need, and consults with organizations across the city, including the Veiled Chain, which is why I'm here today!

Inspecting the Silos

Tadrick invites the party to join the inspection tour of the granary. He’s certain that everything is safe and secure. Read the following aloud when the party moves on to inspect them:

The empty silo is cavernous and resonant, the great, rounded walls reflecting every noise made. Evenly spaced inside, and rising all the way to the darkened ceiling, is a series of carefully carved magical sigils, each one faintly glowing with magic.

Nearby, Tadrick explains:

House Lilifeld just completed an extensive upgrade on all the silos here in the granary. This includes improved seals and transfer chutes, as well as specially designed wards that actively protect and preserve the stored food. It was extremely expensive, and we only just finished getting the last of the main silos upgraded.

Why upgrade the silos?

Purely out of an abundance of caution. With Golden Flats’ supply dropping due to regional troubles there, Redrak Fields is taking on more of the production burden. This puts more pressure on a single source of our food.

Todrick gestures toward the silo.

So, while the expense is great, keeping the stores safe means we have one less weak link in an already taxed logistics chain.

What do the wards do?

Tadrick holds up two fingers.

Two things: they passively purify any grain flowing into them and, once sealed, they produce a preserving field that lets us keep the food longer, reducing spoilage. They were specially designed for House Lilifeld

Eamon says:

You can bet I’ll try to convince your House to part with those designs; we could use the same wards on our silos.

Tadrick offers a friendly chuckle and nod in response, saying:

I think you'll have an easy time of that; we need to make sure the supply lines are secure from origin to destination.

Anyone been sick recently?

Todrick nods, crossing his arms.

Yes, actually. I had to send a few people to the healing house in Lower Ashvale. They were vomiting and had fevers.

Del pipes up:

Were they anywhere near the food stores?

Todrick shakes his head sharply.

Gods, no! I run a tight operation here. We don’t let anyone who is sick go anywhere near the food stores or handle any transfers. Not worth risking it. We’ve also been watching for anyone else not feeling well, but that initial wave of illness seemed to be it.

Examining the Silos

Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] or [[/knowledge machines]] or making a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check knows that the silos have been expertly built, and are exceptionally sturdy. The locks on the seals are also precisely built and fitted so that nothing unwanted can get in.

Examining the Wards

Studying the wards requires a successful [[/skill arcana 16]] and reveals that the wards were expertly made, powerful, and narrowly focused on two tasks: purifying the contents of the silo, and halting decay of any organic matter inside.

  • Result of 18+ The magic at play appears to be a clever mixing of magical elements typically found in spells like purify food and water and gentle repose. Together they would ensure that everything stored inside remains safe.

Investigation Takeaways

The party should conclude that the grain is not contaminated, and not at any risk once stored. Furthermore, any tainted grains going into the silos would be purified and made safe.

They should also walk away with the following info:

  • The party can follow up on investigations at Lower Ashvale to speak with the sick.

Parting Ways

Once the tour is complete, the group begins to break up.

As the tour comes to an end Eamon turns to Tadrick:

This has been enlightening, Tadrick, thank you for your time! If you're available later, I'd very much like to talk to you in depth about the wards you're using.

Tadrick smiles brightly, nodding back.

Of course, I would be happy to. Unfortunately it can't be today, I've got a fair bit to tend to before my day is over. Perhaps tomorrow?

Eamon seems agreeable, and offers his hand, which Tadrick takes straight away.

Tomorrow, then. For now, good day, all!

With that, Eamon and Del offer you farewells and take their leave. Tadrick looks to you and asks:

Was there anything else you needed for your investigation? If not, I will be on my way.

If the party has any questions they want to ask, they have a chance now. Refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200.JournalEntryPage.F12OXjjdUfs8FMZe#inspecting-the-silos]{Inspecting the Silos} for possible questions and answers.

Serethus' Distraction

If Serethus is present, he will take this time to delay the party by trying to get them wrapped up in busy work.

Serethus speaks up:

Yes, actually, they want to look through all your intake and storage records for the last six seasons. The warding efforts are all well and good, but there are people sick and dying in Ordain, and if it's possible someone's tampered with your grain, they need to find it.

Tadrick winces at the prospect.

That's going to be a lot of records, it'll take hours to pore through.

Serethus gently clasps his hands together.

And the Chain is dedicated to doing whatever's necessary to keep the people of Ordain safe, and I'm sure house Lillifeld will do the same.

Tadrick deflates slightly and nods.

Yes of course, I'll get you the necessary access…

The party will be taken to the granary offices and given access to hundreds of files, scrolls, folders, and log books that cover the steady inflow and outflow of food from the granary stations. This work will take hours to complete, and perhaps predictably, Serethus won't be helping.

Are you going to help us?

Serethus offers an apologetic smile.

I am sorry, friends, I simply cannot. I have classes to teach, students to tutor, clients to consult for. If only I had the time, I would help. Fortunately, the city has you to rely on. I am sure you'll find the cause of this trouble!

Why do this?

Serethus wants to waste the party's time so that he has time to muddy the investigation further. Additionally, the longer they spend on this task, the more time the Mutagists have to carry out their experiments unhindered.

The party doesn't have to do this task, and a wise party would recognize that it's a potential waste of time.

If the party agrees to do the work, they can, but they won't find anything useful.

Examining the Records

It takes 72 hours or work to examine the records in full. Each character studying the records contributes to getting this work done. For example, a party of four that studies for an hour would reduce the work time by 4 hours to 68 hours remaining.

Access to the records is provided by Tadrick, and the work can be done across multiple days if necessary. Since the records are all in order, and Redrak's agricultural production is not beset by issues, the records prove entirely uneventful.

We're Wasting Our Time

The party can stop doing this research at any time, there is no penalty for doing so, and no benefit to finishing it.

Akon Attunement: Met with Serethus

If the party completes the investigation at Lilifeld Station with Serethus present at the scene, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 chain2LilifeldWithSerethus]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aura Attunement: Missed Serethus

If the party completes the investigation at Lilifeld Station without Serethus, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 chain2LilifeldWithoutSerethus]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After the characters explore the granary, they’re free to continue their investigation elsewhere. They should proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.86owx3lgvm2zLyv4]{Lower Ashvale} or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.u94YePH6zyrQFuP2]{The Burns} next.
Looking Into Lilifeld Station.soverview: The party arrives at Lilifeld Stations in eastern Ordain, where they investigate reports of tainted grains and sick storehouse workers at one of the district’s landmark institutions: the Lilifeld Granary.
Looking Into Lilifeld Station.sexposition:
The Lilifeld Granary is buzzing with activity as you arrive. Carts loaded with sacks of produce, trailed by wagons bearing huge barrels of grain, move across the broad plaza in front of the grain stores and silos. Cranes hoist loads from vehicles as workers get them into place for storage.

In the midst of this chaos, you spy a trio of figures talking and gesturing at their surroundings. One of them appears to be a member of House Lilifeld, judging by the symbols emblazoned on his leather apron and on the shoulder of his green work shirt.

The middle-aged man has the air of a foreman or manager as he chats amicably with a keth man with exceptionally long gray hair and a slender signborn man with purple horns.
Looking Into Lilifeld Station.ssummary: We visited the Lilifeld Granary at Lilifeld Station like Ankarist asked. There we met the granary manager, Todrick, and the head of the Rekdrak Agrimages. Together we inspected the newly upgraded granary silos, and determined the city food supply is safe. However, some ill workers were sent to the healing house in Lower Ashvale recently.

Ill in Lower Ashvale.name: Ill in Lower Ashvale
Ill in Lower Ashvale.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event covers the party’s ongoing investigation into the source and cause of a growing sickness in the city. Since the city’s sick often end up here, there is a good chance the healers have insight into the illness. Here, the characters can:

  • Study case files and glean additional information about the illness.

  • Speak with the healers at the house and get their accounts of events.

  • Learn that the situation may be more dire than initially reported.

Discussing the Disease

The receptionist places a hand on a stone affixed to her desk and says:

Malinda to the front desk, please. The Veiled Chain is here to ask about the spreading sickness.

The gem glows and goes dark, flaring with light a few moments later. At the second flash, the receptionist smiles at you and says:

She'll be right down!

After a few minutes of waiting you spot a dark-haired woman approaching, her uniform as pristine as that of every other staff member here, but adorned with more elaborate designs of gold and red, making her her seniority in the healing house clear.

Stepping up to you, she wastes no time:

I'm Malinda Felgon, one of the chief healers of this house, and the one overseeing the sickness you're here to investigate.

Please come with me.

She begins walking out of the foyer, past rooms filled with the sick and healers attending them, and speaks to you the entire time:

I’m not surprised the Chain is already on this. I wonder who tipped them off... not that it matters. You've got eyes everywhere. Anyway, about the sickness:

We've been doing our best to keep the afflicted comfortable and alive, and the overall outlook is positive for all of them. We're not expecting anyone to die, since all the patients were in generally good health to begin with. We believe they will recover with sufficient bed rest and fluids, but that's only the start of it.

The veteran staff have been talking about the situation, and we're seeing a rise in Wasting Sickness cases coming in here and in other healing houses around the city.

This could be the real problem: We believe there's a real risk of an epidemic if this isn't dealt with immediately.

What's the epidemic risk?

Since vomiting and diarrhea are common symptoms, there’s serious concern that these symptoms increase transmission, spreading it to others, who in turn spread it themselves.

We have been seeing a steady rise in the number of cases here. I've also been in contact with other healing houses around the city and they've noted new cases as well. If this continues, the number of inbound patients would rapidly outstrip available potions and magical healing capabilities.

It's not a winnable fight without finding the source.

Epidemic Insight

Characters with [[/skill medicine 14 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill medicine 16]] check know that these symptoms can contaminate food and water, can easily spread illness through contact, and persist on surfaces for quite some time.

What do you know about the illness?

It presents as an affliction of the bowels, or wasting sickness. Common symptoms are headaches, nausea, vomiting, hot flashes, diarrhea, and dizziness. It's not contagious, but contact with a patient's discharge can spread it.

It response to typical wasting sickness treatments: Bed rest, fluids, and fever management at the most basic level, with restoration magic for more sensitive cases.

Where are the sick coming from?

The ill coming in are primarily from the north of the city, with most of the patients we have coming specifically from The Burns. If there's a source, it's probably around there. However, I'm not sure what you'd want to look for. It could be tainted food, tainted water, or something else.

Can we speak with or examine the patients?

No.

Not unless you're an accredited healer recognized by the healing house network, or have a signed order from the Hallows. Access to the patients is limited to staff only.

Why can't we speak to the patients?

Malinda sighs and holds up two fingers.

Two reasons: Rules, and safety.

First, rules states only healing house staff may directly interact with patients, and guests are limited to family and only during visiting hours.

Second, these people are sick, some of them in delicate conditions. Letting a bunch of investigators traipse through the healing floors not only risks their safety, but your own.

So, if the Veiled Chain wants direct access, they will need to request access through the Ordinate, by way of the Hallows.

Studying the Disease

Another healer arrives and approaches Malinda, waving her aside to speak privately. Judging by his uniform, he is a junior member of the house. After a brief exchange, Malinda nods, dismisses him, and turns back to you.

I have to assist with something on the floor, but before I go I want to give you access to all the medical reports we have on this affliction. Maybe you and the Chain will spot something we didn’t, or use what we’ve learned to find the source.

Come with me.

She leads you to an office, stopping briefly to collect several leather binders of reports and papers from a secure room before settling you in a quiet office.

These are diagnosis and treatment reports, test results, everything that I can legally let you see without a magistrate's orders or healer's accreditation.

Leave the files and reports here when you're done, I'll put them back later.

There's stationary in the cabinet on the far wall if you need to take notes.

Two Different Problems

There are two elements at play: alchemical toxicity, which is the primary issue, and wasting sickness, which has arisen as a secondary symptom of the toxicity buildup in the city.

The alchemical toxicity lies at the core of this medical mystery. It is an unsourced contamination building up in the afflicted and poisoning them. Its symptoms are deceptively similar to wasting sickness: stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, sometimes diarrhea, dizziness, and weakness. Treatment requires the afflicted to process the toxins out of their bodies naturally or by way of restoration spells.

The wasting sickness afflicting the people of Ordain is mundane and is actually a secondary symptom of the alchemical toxicity. Its symptoms are well understood: diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, fever, and dehydration (GM’s note: it’s dysentery). Transmission occurs when the sick contaminate their environment. Treatment is simple: clean water, simple foods, and keeping their strength up while they rest.

The first pile of records is a collection of diagnostic reports for all the incoming patients with the current malady. There are several dozen of them.

Diagnosis Records

The first batch of reports are for groups of forge workers, smiths, and artisans arriving arriving from the Burns. They all exhibited the following symptoms:

  • Stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, sometimes diarrhea, dizziness, and weakness.

  • Use of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectPois]{Detect Poison and Disease} confirms the afflicted as carrying disease contagions connected to their bodily excretions, and identifies them as a source of a toxin, as though they are venomous.

  • Bowel movements have a distinctly green tinge.

  • The sickness is observed to be infectious by way of exposure to the vomit and excrement of the patients.

All diagnostic reports that follow are either for additional patients arriving from the rest of the city (including additional waves from the Burns), or patients falling ill while inside the healing house already. They all exhibited the following symptoms:

  • Diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, fever, dehydration.

  • Use of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectPois]{Detect Poison and Disease} confirms the afflicted as carrying disease contagions connected to their bodily excretions.

  • The sickness is observed to be infectious by way of exposure to the vomit and excrement of the patients.

Malinda also provided a stack of treatment records for patients which may lend some insight into how the healers have been responding to the illness, and how that illness has been responding to their efforts.

Treatment Records

Treatment reports on the initial patients that arrived from the Burns:

  • Weakness, dizziness, and delirium does not respond to basic treatment, indicating that it may not be stemming from dehydration, but some other unknown issue.

  • Healers observed that patient's sweat and tears leave a powdery residue on their skin.

  • Recovery time is slow, fastest (non-magical) recovery time being 19 days with early signs of recovery only presenting after 10+ days in most cases.

  • Use of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplProtection]{Protection from Poison} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAntitoxin00]{Antitoxin} have proven effective at reducing symptoms and aiding in recovery, but do not cure the affliction.

  • Use of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLesserRest]{Lesser Restoration} will fully remove the illness.

Treatment reports on all other patients with this malady include:

  • Weakness and dizziness responds to treatment quickly, indicating it may stem from dehydration, which is to be expected.

  • Typical (non-magical) recovery time is 14 days with bed rest, light food and water. Immediate improvement shows as early as 4-7 days.

  • Use of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLesserRest]{Lesser Restoration} has no effect on the illness.

Once party has finished looking over the medical reports, they can begin to piece together the nature of the illness, and get some indication of what is going on.

Analyzing The Data

Poring over the files takes several hours of work, which can include a short rest. During this time, a character needs to succeed on a [[/skill medicine 16]] check to glean additional information. Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] have advantage on this check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] know that improperly handled alchemical compounds can cause many symptoms similar to what's noted here, presenting as a mundane illness that refuses to respond to treatment.

  • Result of 16+ The epicenter of this malady seems to be the Burns. However, the initial cases are clearly different from all following cases. It is clear that there's a primary malady, and a secondary illness stemming from it, likely a typical affliction of the bowels, or wasting sickness.

  • Result of 18+ The illness sourced from the Burns seems to be stemming from some intrinsic source of infection or sickness in the patient. In many cases it almost seems like more of a poison or other implanted toxin. The patients don't seem to recover until their bodies have processed it out.

Investigation Takeaways

The party should conclude the following:

  • The illness is sourced from the Burns, and whatever the initial patients from there had was somehow different from the wasting sickness that's spreading in its wake.

Mayis Attunement: Analyzing the Data

If the party manages to successfully analyze the data, each character who participates advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 chain2AshvaleData]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After the characters finish asking their questions and reviewing medical data, they're free to continue their investigation elsewhere. They should proceed to the Burns or Lilifeld Stations next, though the investigation here should more strongly indicate the Burns as the next stopping point.
Ill in Lower Ashvale.soverview: The party visits the healing house in Lower Ashvale to learn more about the illness and people afflicted by it, in hopes of finding more clues to its source.
Ill in Lower Ashvale.sexposition:
The healing house of Lower Ashvale is a tall, regal structure, with numerous windows, and several floors. As you move past the entrance you see halls stretching out in all directions, lined with doorways into rooms where patients wait for healers to tend their ailments.

Just inside you are greeted by a young receptionist seated behind a desk, her pristine clothing accented with the crimson-and-gold symbols of the Cindaric Order.

She smiles politely as you approach.

Hello, welcome, how may I direct you?
Ill in Lower Ashvale.ssummary: We visited the healing house in Lower Ashvale and spoke with one of the head healers there, Malinda Felgon, who answered our questions, and provided their case files to study. We have determined that the illness seems to be coming from the Burns.

Sickness in The Burns.name: Sickness in The Burns
Sickness in The Burns.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event covers the party's ongoing investigation into the source and cause of a growing sickness in the city. Since the city's ill end up here, there is a good chance the healers may have some insight into what the illness is. Here the party can:

  • Speak with Janix Mance and learn what he knows about the situation.

  • Potentially locate the source of tainted water that is afflicting the area.

  • Deal with some local looters trying to take advantage of the situation.

Speaking with Janix

@embed[Actor.gBXPA4AerLzwSbi6]

If the party previously met Janix and completed [[/eventState otherhood2Key]], his greeting changes somewhat:

Janix lifts his machine-hand in greeting, and grins broadly upon seeing you.

Well, well, I was just thinking that it would be extremely fortunate if a band of adventurers turned up to start setting things right. Who knew I had oracular abilities!

He gestures to the area around him.

I'd welcome to you to the hardest working district in the city, but as you can see, the Burns isn't doing so great right now. Bouts of illness have shut down several forges, shops, a restaurant or two. Lots of people are ill right now, and probably not the best place to be hanging around.

So! Are you here of your own volition or did the city send you to look into things?

Otherwise:

Janix lifts his machine-hand in greeting.

Well met, I'm Janix Mance. I operate a forge here, the Burnside Arms. I'd like to say that I'm known far and wide for my work as a forge master, but if you've never heard of me, that says all it needs to.

He gestures to the area around him.

As you can see, the Burns isn't doing so great right now. Bouts of illness have shut down several forges, shops, a restaurant or two. Lots of people are ill right now, and probably not the best place to be hanging around.

Unless of course, you're here on behalf of the city, at which point you're just who I want to talk to.

What happened to your arm and leg?

Janix lifts his hand and flexes it, looking over the metal digits.

Oh boy, that's a story for another day. Short version is this though: fire elementals are amazing allies to have in a forge, as long as you don't let them get too carried away.

How many other people are sick?

Quite a few, actually. Every shop in the district has someone sick right now, and it's been continuing to spread despite our best efforts. I'd say, at this point, everybody knows someone that's caught some sort of affliction of the gut lately.

The worst of them were taken to healing houses, obviously, the rest of the sick are staying home, drinking fluids and recuperating.

Is your forge affected?

Not directly, actually. I've got an apprentice out sick, and a few of them have sick family members, but we've so far managed to avoid the worst of it. I'm not entirely sure why, could be the wards I have in the place to manage air purity, or could be that I'm closer to the Smokerie. I couldn't tell you for sure.

How long ago did the sickness set in?

Few weeks now, maybe months. It was scattered at first, a few people ill here and there, some workers out sick for a day or two. It started to pick up though, and is pretty widespread now.

Have the Hallows of Cindarics come to help?

Yeah, we've got a couple visiting Sages who are tending the ill, casting magic where they can. It's helping, but the number of sick is more than they can manage. Plus the sick aren't getting better, and even the ones that get healed end up sick a few days later.

Persistent Sickness

Characters with a [[/skill medicine 14 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill medicine 12]] check suspect that the source of the illness must be persistent in the Burns for people to catch the sickness again after recovering. This also means that the source is widespread, not localized.

Do you know the source?

I have suspicions, but no hard proof. I would look at the Red Iron forge up the way. One day the whole work crew there came down with the sickness, all at once, and so bad that we had to pile them into a boat and rush them to Lower Ashvale.

I have the key to the forge if you want to look around.

Have you changed anything recently?

Nope, nothing so far. I checked through all my most recent fuel batches, oil stocks and forge additives too. Nothing out of the ordinary. So whatever the cause is, it's not coming from anything I'm supplying people.

Besides, I work with all the materials myself, every day. If it was the cause, I'd be sick, too.

Reading Janix

Janix is being honest and forthright. A successful [[/skill insight 12]] confirms this, and yields further insight: the kivahr alchemist is more concerned about this illness than he lets on. His words are reassuring but there are threads of doubt beginning to fray along the edges of his social mask.

Raising Serethus' Concerns

If the party wants to raise Serethus' concerns about Janix being the source, they can.

Have you introduced any new compounds in the area?

What? Wait, are you accusing me of this? No. I work with the Hallows to help make sure the forges in the city all follow a roughly equal set of safe working conditions so people don't get hurt. That includes anything new that enters widespread use in the city forges.

Serethus seems to think you might have been responsible.

Janix scoffs loudly.

Serethus. Of course. I don't really care what some wannabe alchemist says about me, though I don't appreciate him slandering my name. Obviously I'm not the one responsible, if I was, why would I be willing to help you on your investigation?

Do you know Serethus?

Janix scrunches his nose out of reflexive distaste.

Not well, I know he's from pretty far off and a very competent spellcaster, but I couldn't tell you anything concrete about his story, and I definitely don't care to. I do think he needs to stick with magic, and leave alchemy to the experts, though.

Routing the Looters

As you approach the forge you see a small group of people trying to find a way into the building. Some are testing the windows, a few are trying and failing to pick the door. However, their sentry spots you and calls out:

We've got company!

They all slide clubs and knives from their coats, and size you up. The number advantage they have is clear, and seems to have made them bold, but none of them look to be well armored or heavily armed.

@embed[Actor.jZBVgCb2P61F9SrT]

Ne'er Do Wells

A group of 8 @UUID[Actor.jZBVgCb2P61F9SrT]{Ordani Ruffians} will attack the party. Their tactics are simple: they try to distribute themselves evenly across all combatants, and refuse to fight one-on-one if they can help it.

No Help At All

Janix Mance immediately falls back to a safe distance until the fighting is over, and refuses to engage in combat. He cannot be convinced or cajoled into fighting by any means.

Mild Violence

The Ruffians will flee if more than half their number are defeated, and if the party actually kills a Ruffian, rather that simply knocking them out, they will begin to flee as soon as they lose the advantage of numbers in the battle.

The Ruffians aren't looking to kill anyone, so in the off chance that they are victorious, they will take bags, valuables and weapons from the party, but nothing that they can't just grab and run away with.

Does the Burns usually have this sort of problem?

Janix shakes his head.

Well, Ordain has its unseemly sorts, same as anywhere else, and they are always looking for easy paydays. However, the break-ins only really only started happening after people got sick and stopped coming to work around here.

As soon as people are better these ruffians will move on.

Searching the Forge

Janix guides you to the shut down forge, the shutters and doors closed tightly. He takes a heavy key and unlocks one of the gates, lifting it up to grant access to the building. Inside, it appears that the forge was simply abandoned in the middle of a work day.

Couple people came through, doused all the fires, made sure nothing would burn down, but otherwise everything's been left as-is. Be warned: there's probably still puke and worse on the ground in places, so watch your step.

Janix doesn't come in with you, but instead hovers at the entrance as he tucks the key into a belt pouch.

All right, well, I'll leave you to it, and just be waiting outside until you're done. I'm not going to risk my own health, but hopefully there's something to find in here. I'll lock it back up when you're done.

Inside the dark forge space there's the stink of acids, oils, coal and burnt wood, alongside the stench of iron and human waste. Eyes cast down to the floor easily spot sources of the stink, spattered and dripped here and there.

Contaminated Containers

A character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] check notices a barrel and several buckets sitting against a wall next to a water pump fixed to the wall, the iron pipes descending into the ground. Looking at them, there an obvious sheen on the water, not unlike soap or oil collecting on the surface.

  • Result of 16+: The character also notices that there are several drinking cups sitting on a shelf nearby the barrel and buckets, they also are coated with the strange, oily sheen.

  • Result of 18+: The character also notices numerous troughs and barrels around the forge likely used for quenching metals, all of these have a mixture of oil and a green film collecting on their surface.

  • Result of 20+: The character also notices a powdery gray residue on most everything in the forge. At first it looks like ash, but it is too uniformly spread out to be, and looks as though it was applied while wet and dried to the surfaces.

If the party completed [[/eventState chain2Ashvale]] then they should know they are looking for sources of alchemical hazards, and automatically succeed on the base roll above, but may roll with advantage to locate further sources and clues.

A character with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] or who makes a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check posits that the water is contaminated, and that the workers here were drinking said water, dousing themselves to keep cool, and vaporizing the chemical in the quenching troughs. It's no wonder they fell violently ill.

Well: There's Your Problem

Characters that test the wall by pumping water notice that it has a slightly sickly green tinge to it. Upon seeing this, it is safe to assume that the whole district's water supply is likely contaminated.

  • Characters with [[/skill medicine 12 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill medicine 14]] check believe this is probably why the locals aren't getting better. If the water's tainted, they're only going to keep getting sick, or end up getting sicker over time.

  • Characters with [[/skill investigation 12 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check would suspect that the source of the contamination is likely from the Destine river, and as a result, the source of the contamination might be upriver somewhere.

Signs of Sickness

Examining the vomit in the forge doesn't yield any particular insight into the illness, beyond what the workers last ate before falling ill. However, a character with [[/skill medicine 12 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill medicine 14]] check notices that the vomit appears to have been thin, possibly containing mostly water. It's likely that the forge workers had been drinking large amounts of water while on the job, probably to offset the volume of sweat caused by the heat in the forge.

Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectPois]{Detect Poison and Disease} immediately allows a character to notice the water as a primary source of toxicity. More than that, though, there is a mild haze of toxicity on every surface of the forge area.

After the party examines the forge, they may want to look for other wells or water sources in the area, and Janix, who is still nearby, will offer to show them. They can also ask Janix more questions.

Where does the district get its Water?

Well, most people pump the water from the river directly. Since the district is close to the headwaters, there's not much concern about city contaminants. A few pump water from the ground, though the aquifers are fed from the river, too.

If the water's contaminated though, that'd explain why people are falling ill.

Testing the Waters

Locating another well in the district is easy with the help of Janix Mance, who is more than happy to guide the party to it. If tested, the water is also contaminated, though the water is not as obviously green, meaning the contamination is weaker here.

A character with [[/skill investigation 12 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] would note that this well is further from the waterfront, leading them to suspect that the source of the contamination is likely from the Destine river.

Up A River

Examining the Destine river is inconclusive, as the speed and volume of the water is too great to examine it up close. However, if the party draws water from the Destine, they'll note it does have the same strange sheen.

Samples of Sickness

The party may have chosen to take samples of the water from the forge barrels, either of the wells, or the Destine river itself, gaining a @UUID[Item.RU3MhSlxzxQbBo6Q]{Tainted Water Sample} in the process.

This sample is contaminated with an unknown alchemical compound, and if examined while @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectPois]{Detect Poison and Disease} is active, is revealed to be a source of an unknown toxin.

Testing the sample requires an hour and use of [[/tool alchemist 14]] and reveals a collection of dangerous chemicals that nobody should be consuming. The chemicals can be compiled into @UUID[Item.aHME2RsZUIbpaQlx]{Water Sample Results}.

What's Going On?

  • Workers are drinking the alchemically tainted water frequently due to the heat of the forge area.

  • Workers are dousing themselves in water to stay cool during the work day, coating themselves in the toxin.

  • Workers are exposed to steam which coats them and which they inhale during quenching.

  • The tainted water is coming from local wells that draw from the destine directly.

Why is there no tainted water further downriver?

  • The dilution in the Destine makes it a non-issue. The Burns is clearly close to the source!

  • The city's filtration systems are taking care of a good amount of the toxin in other places (Ankarist is looking into this, and it will come up later.)

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After the characters finish talking to Janix Mance and examining the shut down forge, they should report back to Ankarist at the Veiled Chain headquarters.
Sickness in The Burns.soverview: The party explores the soot-stained district known as the Burns in search of answers about the pervasive sickness afflicting Ordain. Here, they obtain a promising lead from the famed artificer Janix Mance of Burnside Arms.
Sickness in The Burns.sexposition:
An odd stillness pervades the streets as you walk through the Burns, as if most of the district has packed up and gone home early. Looking down side streets and into shop windows, you notice a theme: signs declaring temporary closure due to sickness.

Up ahead, a rare sign of life: a small crowd has gathered around someone addressing them with calm authority. As you draw closer, you see a tall, powerfully built Kivahr man with one arm and one leg replaced by glowing bronze limbs. He is surrounded by a group of locals, many of them smudged with soot and forge grime.

The Kivahr man calls out:

It's very simple: The sick, whether that's you or someone in your house, need rest and clean water. If they don't show improvement in a day or two, then it's time to get to a healing house.

There's an edge of unease in the crowd, the kind that lingers after too many unanswered questions. Someone calls out:

Janix, we can't sit on our duffs all week hoping to feel better. What happens if this doesn't go away?

The man at the center, Janix, replies:

It will. I've informed the Hallows and the Cindarics, they know something's going on here. Besides, you only get one life, and there'll always be more work for the Burns. The city needs us.

The crowd grumbles and begins to disperse, leaving you with the kivahr man. His glowing eyes settle on you.

Hail! Sorry to say, most shops around here are closed, if you're looking to buy.
Sickness in The Burns.ssummary: We traveled to the Burns district and carried out our investigation there. We met a forgemaster named Janix Mance who helped us investigate a local forge where a large number of people fell ill. Inside we found badly contaminated water, and determined that most of the well are also pulling in contaminated water.

Hazardous Headwaters.name: Hazardous Headwaters
Hazardous Headwaters.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event sees the party discovering and infiltrating a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.frzH0bjzUvkqliSn]{Mutagist} laboratory hidden in ancient ruins under Ordain. In this event, the characters can:

  • Locate victims of a kidnapping ring, and greater machinations of the Mutagists and their allies.

  • Discover the macabre experiments of the mutagists and the results of them.

  • Stumble upon ancient ruins belonging to the long dead Sedyri people.

Challenge Level

This event is balanced for a level 5 party. A group of level 4 heroes can be successful but will need to employ careful strategy. If the party is not yet level four, it would be advised for them to seek other challenges and revisit this event later.

Area Walkthrough
