The initial exposition of this event takes place on the region map until the party chooses their preferred approach to the hideout. Once that choice has been made, gameplay transitions to the "Forgotten Cistern" Scene where the central gameplay of this event transpires.

Once inside the scene, a complete room-by-room description of its environment and the gameplay that occurs there is detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h] area walkthrough. This area has several special rules and gameplay expectations, so it is advisable to review the @UUID[JournalEntry.mGWhbkZnbXZZTu3h.JournalEntryPage.Z2krOyo0nPTwiEQe]{Gameplay Details} page either before or during the party's exploration of the location.

After investigating the districts of Ordain for the source of the sickness, the party in concert with Ankarist now have enough information to make an educated guess on the origin of the contaminant: the Destine basin.

With Ankarist reassigned to another task, the party has been left to handle this leg of the investigation themselves. They've been asked to collect evidence, and try to find the source of the poison seeping into the water.

They are about to find more than that by quite a bit.

Shutting Down the Lab

Raiding the Lab

The party will ultimately want to do the following to consider this event complete:

  • Defeat or capture the Mutagists and their Drakes.

  • Find and save any victims of the Mutagists in the area.

  • Confiscate or document the alchemical materials and machinery being used by the Mutagists.

  • Collect any evidence that would help shed light on the goals and operations of the Mutagists as a whole.

Luxarum Attunement: Mutagists Killed

If the party kills the Mutagists during their raid of the lab, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 chain2HeadwatersKilled]] at the conclusion of the event.

Cora Attunement: Mutagists Captured

If the party captures the Mutagists during their raid of the lab, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 chain2HeadwatersCaptured]] at the conclusion of the event.

Heart Attunement: Victims Rescued

If the party manages to successfully rescue the kidnapped victims during their raid of the Mutagist lab, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 chain2HeadwatersVictims]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After invading the Mutagist Lab and discovering the furtive origins of the toxicity, and evidence that there is something more afoot. The party must return to the Veiled Chain headquarters in the Hallows to share their findings.
Hazardous Headwaters.soverview: The party explores the waters feeding into the River Destine of Ordain in search of the source of its contamination. What they find instead is the entrance to a hidden alchemical laboratory where a group of vile Mutagists has been conducting unsavory experiments on captured humanoid subjects.
Hazardous Headwaters.sexposition:
The land flattens out into a sprawling wetland at the foot of a roaring waterfall, its thunder echoing distantly across the basin. Water laps against slick rocks and muddy banks, the rhythmic sound only broken by the constant crash of water far overhead. Mist curls through the reeds, lending the air a chill weight.

As the wind shifts you catch the sudden stench of decaying plants and stinging chemicals. You trace the scene to its source, and find a grim sight: oily ribbons of some sickly green swirling on the surface of the waters, and rotting reeds everywhere the oil collects along the banks.
Hazardous Headwaters.ssummary: We located and raided a secret Mutagist base hidden under Ordain. While we defeated several Mutagists, and seized worrying evidence of their plans in the city, the head of the lab managed to destroy the bulk of their records before escaping. We need to report back to the Veiled Chain immediately.

Missing Persons.name: Missing Persons
Missing Persons.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event involves the party reporting back to the Veiled Chain about their findings during Hazardous Headwaters, only to be handed a new assignment to investigate a group actively agitating the people of Ordain and refugees coming in from the Golden Flats. The characters can:

  • Report on what they found in the hidden Mutagist lab and turn in any evidence they have.

  • Learn about the agitators attempting to turn the populace of Ordain against its leadership.

  • Get their next assignment in the city.

Vista Under Development

A scene representing the Veiled Chain headquarters is planned, in the meantime, the event will show the Hallows vista, which is where the entrance to their hidden operations can be found.

Reporting the Lab

Reportable Evidence

If the party turned in any of the following items they can achieve the Outcome: Recovered Mutagist Records & Materials:

  • @UUID[Item.tl96BcMoSGOB5xUS]

  • @UUID[Item.jF5hT7KEgTQ7fViy]

  • @UUID[Item.Eflvgt6PX2gK3x0Z]

  • @UUID[Item.Nu8WVcxl15LQrPjR]

  • @UUID[Item.Nu8WVcxl15LQrPjR]

If the party found the @UUID[Item.ycDGxabfXRXn12at] and turned it in, they can achieve the Outcome: Reported on Mutagist Allies.

If the party recovered and turned in at least one of the bundles of @UUID[Item.UV5JlTJP1cR2LdqR]{Personal Effects} that could be found in the forgotten cistern they can achieve the Outcome: Turned in Victim Personal Effects.

For their efforts, the party is paid a [[/award 75gp]] for each bundle they turn in (a higher price than what the valuables would likely command if sold).

Signara Attunement: All Outcomes

If the party manages to complete all outcomes (recover the Mutagist records, report on the Mutagist allies, and turn-in the personal effects of the victims), each character advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 chain2MissingOutcomes]] at the conclusion of the event.

Once the party is done giving their report, read this aloud, or paraphrase it:

Shaar reaches out a delicate finger and taps their nails on the map near where you found the lab.

The fact this lab was run under our noses raises numerous very concerning questions. We'll send investigators to scour the location for any further evidence, and secure the location.

However, that's going to be the end of your work there, we need to move you to a new task.

Shaar addresses Ankarist:

Get them up to speed on the situation with the refugees and fliers, then get after the assignment I gave you.

Ankarist nods in acceptance as Shaar steps away. The head of the Chain pauses, regarding you again for a moment.

Good work finding that lab. Shutting it down will save numerous lives, and hopefully set back these Mutagists and whatever they are trying to achieve. Perhaps you can replicate this success on your next assignment.

With that said, Shaar steps away, leaving the hall directly.

Update on Missing Persons

Ankarist watches Shaar go then looks to you.

First of all, like Shaar said: good work. I don't like that the Mutagists have turned up again, and especially don't like that they are in Ordain now. However, Shaar and I will send a team to clean up the lab and gather whatever evidence you left behind.

In the meantime, I'm putting you on another task…

Ankarist shifts some papers about, setting a flier down on the table in front of you. In bold text it proclaims:

THE CINDARICS HAVE LET US DOWN

The following text bemoans the state of the city, the sickness in the burns, refugees being turned away from temples, people being left to sleep on the streets with nowhere to go.

Ankarist slides another flier to sit beside it, featuring the same style and same bold text, this time stating:

THE HALLOWS IS INEFFECTIVE

The text below it points out that refugees coming into the city are choking the skywalk, slowing down commerce, that they are being preyed upon by criminals and unscrupulous merchants, that the Hallows and the courts are doing nothing to make the Trade Houses and Cindarics address the issues in Ordain, or beyond.

Both fliers end the same way:

We will not suffer their indifference. We will not be subordinate. We will unite and be heard.

Ankarist cross his arms over his chest and exhales out of clear frustration.

These have been circulating through the city, specifically through refugee-heavy areas. It's causing agitation in the city, especially among the refugees coming in from the golden flats. I don't need to tell you that we don't need more issues piled on top of the one's we've already got.

Do the fliers have a point?

Ankarist grimaces as his eyes move to the fliers.

I hate to admit it, but, yes they do. The city is usually quiet, but with the influx of refugees, the rise of banditry in the flats, and now the illness? On top of all this, the Cindarics seem scattered. They aren't doing nothing, but they could be doing more.

That's before we even get to the issues inside the city lately: Crime's spiked: burglaries, assaults, theft. This also means court volume's spiked. The Hallows has a lot to keep under control, and the city doesn't have a dedicated peacekeeping force.

Using the Anachraenum and Burnished Hand is hardly ideal, either. A bunch of armed historians and monster hunters aren't the sort of people you send to keep peace in a city.

Ankarist waves a hand at the fliers.

This isn't what we need right now, but it's not like there's no truth to it…

Where are the fliers coming from?

Ankarist lifts his shoulders in a small shrug.

We haven't tracked down the source yet. Any time we send investigators out to find the source they come back empty-handed. These fliers are being made somewhere and handed out by a group of people, that much we are sure about.

They must know how to identify our agents, which raises some unpleasant questions about operation security, but that's a problem for the Chain's upper echelons.

He taps the fliers.

This is the current concern.

What can the party do to help?

You're not officially part of the Chain, and we're banking on you not being a known quantity to whoever is agitating the populace. You're going to head out into the city and see if you can figure out who the source is and where they are operating out of.

Where should investigations begin?

Ankarist indicates two locations on the city map:

We've identified two hotspots where the fliers are turning up a lot: Foxlairs or Palisade Cross. Hit them both, see what you can find.

Why Foxlairs?

The refugees coming in from the flats are bringing their pack animals and livestock in droves, and they need somewhere to put them. Foxlairs has numerous stables, they are going to be here in large numbers. Expect the agitators to be handing out fliers there.

Why Palisade Cross?

Palisade Cross has a lot of low-cost housing and several large inns, usuually it's where incoming sailors from the docks end up, but the refugees have flooded the area as of late.

Secondarily, it's home to a sizeable population of lower income Ordani, and they are likely feeling the pinch with the city's resources being stretched thin. If I were looking to agitate the city populace, I'd also be targeting them.

Should we shut this operation down?

Short answer: yes.

The longer answer is that the Chain's getting spread thin with things going on, so we don't have the assets to run strict oversight on this, plus, we're concerned out presence would compromise you. So… you'll be on your own for this investigation.

You need to figure out where these fliers are coming from, and shut down the source. Confiscate the materials they are using, disable any machines or duplication magic they are using, and capture anyone involved.

These people are actively turning the city populace against its own government. If left unchecked, they could destabilize the city, and the last thing we need are riots in the streets.

What new assignment are you on?

Sorry, that's been deemed need-to-know, and it's not something I can divulge. I can guarantee you that it's important, and related to everything else going on.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

Once the party has finished talked to Ankarist, and has a clear picture of what to do next, they can move on to either Foxlairs or Palisade Cross to investigate the source of these fliers and the agitators trying to destabilize Ordain.
Missing Persons.soverview: The party returns to The Hallows to report their findings about the Mutagist Lab to Ankarist and the Veiled Chain. Ankarist presents a discovery of his own, and Shaar tasks the party with locating additional information about a disgruntled civilian group known as the "Subordinate."
Missing Persons.sexposition:
You step into the chamber of the Veiled Chain, the underground office buzzing with activity, as people carry on conversations around the perimeter of the room, and move files between workstations. At the center of the motion are Shaar and Ankarist, both fixated on documents, both wearing looks of concentration.

As you get close their eyes divert to you, and Ankarist speaks:

Welcome back, did you find the source of the contamination?
Missing Persons.ssummary: We reported the existence of the Mutagist lab to Ankarist and Shaar with the Veiled Chain who are going to secure it. However, we've been asked to investigate the source of some propaganda meant to agitate the city's poor and refugee populations, turning them against the Ordinate.

Agitation in Foxlairs.name: Agitation in Foxlairs
Agitation in Foxlairs.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event tasks the party with a trip to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.cGtlD2sG0mv9j0ll]{Foxlairs} district, where they must confront the as-yet-unidentified agitators that have been sewing civil unrest among the locals. Once they meet the agitators in question, the party members must decide how they want to proceed. In this event, the characters can:

  • Eavesdrop on the agitators to glean more information about their motives.

  • Either help the agitators or attack them, earning their trust or forcing a confession in the process.

Scanning the Crowd

The party will likely want to examine the crowd, and see if they can spot anything of note. The discarded flyer will be the most immediate thing, but the agitators are also in plain view if they look more closely.

Forgotten Fliers

Characters with a [[/skill perception 10 passive]] notice a flyer resting on the ground, stained with mud (and worse). It has the same style as the other fliers previously seen. This one's headline boldly declares:

THE CITY DOESN'T WANT YOU HERE

The rest of its text is too stained to make out.

Wranglers and Refugees

Characters making a successful [[/skill perception 14]] check notice that several people in the crowds carrying fliers matching the style of those previously seen, but the source of them isn't immediately obvious.

  • Result of 16+ Tracing the fliers as they move through the crowd, and seeing where they are missing in the hands of others, you're able to locate their source: A pair of unassuming citizens stopping people to talk to them briefly before handing out fliers taken from a satchel slung across their respective chests.

The agitators in questions are:

Sura (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

Sura's a short, lean woman dressed to blend into the crowds of other Ordani. Her garb is colorful and well made, but not so eye-catching that she'd ever stand out in the crowds she's weaving through. She is wearing gloves and is effortlessly careful not to touch anyone or anything unless she has to.

Larz (Lawful Evil, Arcturian Human, he/him)

Larz is a tall, skinny fellow with a large nose and sunken eyes. He is deeply tanned from years spent outdoors, and has sunken eyes likely stemming from one too many sleepless nights. He is dressed similarly to the other refugees in the area, wearing rugged clothes meant for farming and travel, not leisurely urban life.

Speaking With the Agitators

Observing the Agitators

To successfully spy on the agitators, a successful group [[/skill stealth 12]] check is necessary. The ample crowds and animals make this relatively simple, and as long as the party doesn't do anything to draw attention to themselves, they'll be able to trail the agitators.

Watching them allows a few things to become clear:

  • Neither Sura or Larz cross paths while handing out fliers, intentionally avoiding each other to cover more ground. Since they are actively talking to people in the crowd, approaching them directly would not be strange.

  • Neither of them appear to be armed or armored in any obvious way, nor do they appear to be spellcasters.

  • While they are wary of their surroundings, and watching the crowds, they are watching for authorities, not random civilians in the crowd. It might be relatively simple to pickpocket them.

  • Every now and then they break away from the crowds to meet up and talk. These meetings are always brief, lasting only a minute or two, and represent the best chance the party has to ambush them.

To get close to the agitators without drawing their attention, the party will need to exercise a bit of caution and deception.

Playing the Part

A successful [[/skill deception 14]] or [[/skill performance 14]] allows a character to appear like any other member of the crowd, acting agitated and desperate. Doing this allows them to move toward the agitators without drawing attention.

Alternatively, a successful [[/skill persuasion 16]] check allows the party to directly approach the agitators and convince them that the party is curious about the movement and interested in knowing more.

Once the agitators have been contacted, they can be spoken with to gain insight into the movement, and what's going on in Foxlairs.

Talking Politics

Interacting with either of the Agitators provides this information directly:

  • Larz and Sura are members of a growing movement of Arcturian and Ordani citizens that have grown tired with the elitism and detachment Ordain shows to its own people inside and outside its walls.

  • They are handing out a new flyer. This flyer proclaims:

THE CITY DOESN'T WANT YOU HERE

It goes on to detail that the Ordinate, Hallows, and Trading Houses don't have an interest in helping the refugees. They won't ever dedicate enough resources to help everyone, and now that they aren't producing food and livestock in the flats, they are even less useful to the city.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] recognize this is an inflammatory half-truth that can be easily defended with little effort. For a group of stressed, distracted refugees, any nuance is likely to be lost.

Isn't this misleading and inflammatory?

Not at all! What about it is either of those things? The people of the flats are here because situations outside the city got out of control: banditry, disease, monsters. But why?

Ordain has the Trading Houses which all operate in the Golden Flats and have hundreds of thousands of gold tied up in those operations. They can't keep bandits at bay or hire mercenaries?

Ordain has the Anachraenum and Burnished Hand they could pressure into helping protect the countryside too! Instead, one's out collecting knick-knacks for the rich, and the other's locked in a grudge match with the Cindarics.

Is there some larger action planned?

Yes, actually! Right now we're just getting people informed and interested in the movement. A greater collective action is in the works, and when that time comes, we'll be able to get the people together and really do something.

Is there some way we can help the movement?

Actually, now that you mention it, yes. There's a rich noble that bought up a bunch of the stable space to keep locals from being able to use it, and it's sitting empty! I want to do something about that. Or, more accurately, I want you to do something about it.

Why would they do that?

I don't know, it seems needlessly cruel, doesn't it?

They waggle the flyer in their hand.

Like the paper says: there are people in the city who don't want the refugees here. I don't think I really care why, the end effect is the same — making people suffer.

Have you tried talking to the stable boss?

I have.

He's not going to budge on the space since it's all paid for. However, you might be more convincing than me! Go change their mind, and get those stable spots opened so that the refugees here have somewhere to put their animals.

Helping the Agitators

Talking Stable Space

A successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] convinces one of the stablehands to talk about the situation here, and they point out that a wide swath of the stables has been rented out by a rich noble. They aren't at liberty to say who, but it has cut into available spaces, the remainder are going fast.

Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] and [[/knowledge intrigue]] know that it would be hard argue with a standing reservation, especially since the stable boss could keep raising the prices with demand, knowing the reserving party would have to pay for it.

  • A further [[/skill insight 12]] check leads a character to suspect that whoever put the reservation for the spaces in has a lot of money to burn, and doesn't care about how much this stunt will end up costing them.

Characters may want to speak to the stable boss directly, they can request that chance via any of the stablehands.

Nathira Jessos (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

The spry, gray-haired Nathira Jessos is the latest in the line of children running the Jessos Station here, and she is the one grappling with the influx of new people and animals to deal with. She might not want to admit it, but the rush is very good for business, and Nathira likes it when business is good.

Nathira turns to face you as stablehands direct animals to open spots in the stables behind you. She looks you up and down and immediately looks annoyed at having her work interrupted.

Yeah? What do you want? I'm a little busy today.

Reading Nashira

A successful [[/skill insight 14]] check allows a character to get a general read on Nashira's personality while talking to her.

Generally speaking, she is honest but abrasive. Nashira doesn't seem to be a bad person, but is clearly motivated by profit, and probably has a hard time looking past that.

Why aren't you helping the refugees?

I'd like to, but I'm not running a charity. Taking care of all these animals isn't cheap, nor is paying all my people. If the refugees can pay, and I have room, I'll make sure their animals get taken care of. It's not personal.

Who reserved all the stable space?

Sorry, we don't divulge client information to strangers. You'll need orders of inspection from the Hallows, and I know we're not doing anything worth their attention right now.

If the party points out they are here working for the Veiled Chain, Nathira's response develops further:

Nashira's scowl deepens.

All right, well, in that case you can go get the Hallows to send an inspector here with a signed order to inspect my work records, like I said. Then I'll divulge that information.

I have a lot of respect for the work the Chain does in the city, but there's rules for a reason, and I'm going to have to ask that everyone follows them. You included.

Could we pay you to release the stables?

Potentially, yes. I'd accept fifty thousand gold to bump the current hold on the spots, then you can use them. Anything less than that, and I can't justify the loss of profit and reputation I'd suffer.

Convincing Nathira

Nathira can be convinced to open the stable slots with one of several successful checks including [[/skill persuasion 16]] check to, [[/skill deception 16]], or [[/skill intimidation 14]] from a character in the party.

Generally speaking, appealing to her sense of goodness and the potential goodwill and fame helping the refugees would garner will be more effective than anything else. In that same vein, Nashira is worried about profit and reputation, and any direct threats made to them will work to coerce her into complying.

Mayis Attunement: Helping the Agitators

If the party chooses to help the agitators, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 chain2FoxlairHelp]] at the conclusion of the event.

Reporting Success

Returning to either Sura or Larz, the party can report on their success.

If the party previously completed [[/eventState chain2Palisade]] by assisting the agitators there, then they say this:

Looking genuinely surprised at your success they shoot you a smile.

I'm glad you turned up to lend a hand. I honestly didn't think we'd see any success here.

Say, I think I've heard about you. You helped out with some issues over in Palisade Cross, if I recall.

Listen, we're gathering like-minded folk, potential allies, and supporters in the Verocorte estate in a few days. Come after midnight, we'll have three lanterns by the side gate located on Kelekin Alley if we're meeting. Use the passphrase "I won't be subordinate." to get in.

Hope to see you there!

Otherwise, they have this to say in response:

Looking genuinely surprised at your success they shoot you a smile.

That's very impressive! I didn't think that the stable boss would open up the spots again. You're clearly an ally worth keeping around.

You know… we've got people all over the city that need help. Palisade Cross, for example, has been a real mess lately with fighting and people getting detained. You might be able to do some good there, too.

I'd love to stick around, but I need to be on my way. Thank you again for your help here.

Unexpected Results

A successful [[/skill insight 14]] check against Sura or Larz notes that they are actually somewhat disappointed that you were successful since the stables turning away the refugees was technically good for their cause and gave more fuel to their anti-Ordinate rhetoric.

Attacking the Agitators

The party may choose the direct approach, here are the relevant skill checks and details for such an event:

Easily Approached

A party looking to ambush either Sura or Larz can do so easily. They do not put up much of a fight, and can be subdued without combat. They aren't looking to die for their cause (not yet at least), aren't armed or armored, and are not expecting a fight. They quickly surrender when faced with violence, especially where there's a risk they'll die.

Deniable Assets

Sura and Larz have been hired for this work, but aren't connected to the rest of the

Questioning Sura and Larz yields the following information:

Who are you working for?

Brynna Verocorrt, a rich noble who lives in Fallbrook. She wants agitate the locals against the Ordinate, and bring about social change.

What is the next step?

We're going to start handing out fliers for a rally in Fallbrook, gather up everybody, and get them to agree to join a new city-wide reform movement!

When is this meeting?

In a few days, after sundown.

Where will the meeting be held?

There's an old theater in Fallbrook, the Bronze Rask, they are hosting it there.

The password to get in is: "I Won't Be Subordinate" given at the door.

Ragen Attunement: Attacking the Agitators

If the party chooses to attack the agitators, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 chain2FoxlairAttack]] at the conclusion of the event.

Looting the Agitators

If the party kills Sura and/or Larz, picks their pockets, or robs them they can find the following items of interest:

Robbing the Agitators

A successful [[/skill sleight 16]] check is necessary to lift items from the bags of either Larz or Sura. Failure by 5 or more results in the targeted agitator becoming wary of the party, and going to meet with their counterpart to warn them.

Shared Inventory

These items are carried by both Larz and Sura.

Planning Letter

This letter is about the upcoming meeting:

We're still putting together the details, but if anyone asks you: yes we're planning a proper rally. There's going to be a meeting in Fallbrook at the old theater that Brynna's bought out. Timeframe is in the next week or so.

Once this is set in stone we'll start gathering people up.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] might suspect that a noble or merchant of means and influence is backing this movement. Why is a mystery, but political intrigue and ideological fights are not uncommon in the halls of power.

Foxlair Note

The Jessos Station in Foxlairs is a good place to hand out fliers and build buzz for the movement. Someone with deep coffers paid to reserve a bunch of stable space to keep the refugees out, and the Jessos family is so profit oriented they will be hard pressed to do the right thing if it costs them coin.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] recognize that someone is feeding the movement inside information, and is likely embedded in the city's merchant community.

Spare Fliers

THE CITY DOESN'T WANT YOU HERE

It goes on to detail that the Ordinate, Hallows, and Trading Houses don't have an interest in helping the refugees. They won't ever dedicate enough resources to help everyone, and now that they aren't producing food and livestock in the flats, they are even less useful to the city.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] recognize this is an inflammatory half-truth that can be easily defended with little effort. For a group of stressed, distracted refugees, any nuance is likely to be lost.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event is completed when the party either collects evidence from the pair of agitators here, or earns their trust by helping them out with the stables lodging issue. Once they have done so, they can go to the other district to investigate that location.

Parties that looted materials directly from the agitators can skip investigating both locations and move to the Midnight Meeting event, as they have enough material and information to find it.
Agitation in Foxlairs.soverview: The party investigates the Foxlairs, one of Ordain’s districts, for information about agitators spreading inflammatory propaganda meant to rile up locals. They'll need to identify the culprits, and decide how to deal with them.
Agitation in Foxlairs.sexposition:
The wide paved street is dotted with the leavings of animals great and small, filling the air with the stink of rotting hay, and animal waste. Wagons trundle by in both directions, piled high with bundles, and pulled by teams of beasts. Some of them carry goods, others carry the lives of people fleeing the Golden Flats.

All the traffic seems to coalesce around a large stable surrounded by a swirl of commotion. Here, clusters of harried refugees, flustered locals, and stablehands jockey to be heard and coordinate movement of animals into and out of the stables. Every so often, a voice rises above the din: a stable boss shouting names, or a farmer bargaining for a safe stall.

There is an air of tension here, the agitation bubbling up into the animals which snort, stamp, and shift restlessly as their handlers attempt to find food and shelter for them. The agitation ripples through the gathering, hinting at tensions that go well beyond mere overcrowding.
Agitation in Foxlairs.ssummary: We investigated the agitators in Foxlairs, and got leads that will help us track down the source of the propaganda fliers they are handing out.

Midnight Meeting.name: Midnight Meeting
Midnight Meeting.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event is a trap and an ambush. While the assembled civilians are the primary targets, the party is an expected arrival that the assembled enemies are prepared to deal with once and for all. In this event, the characters can:

  • Survive an ambush by the Wandren Tracer known as @UUID[Actor.UVncdPqmzpZLwGvK] and her @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.C7ArtlQkeNgne3Ej]{House Wandren} allies.

  • Discover the identities of the various Mutagist conspirators throughout the city.

  • Learn that an attack is being launched on the Veiled Chain while they are at the meeting.

Point of No Return (Chapter 3)

This event serves as a point of no return for certain Chapter 3 main quests. Once the characters complete this event, they can no longer continue or complete the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.GEuq75fq1VfNBud1]{Disgraced House} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders}.

Challenge Level

This event is balanced for a level 5 party. A group of level 4 heroes can be successful but will need to employ careful strategy. If the party is not yet level four, it would be advised for them to seek other challenges and revisit this event later.

Area Walkthrough

This event's gameplay transitions to the "@UUID[Scene.emberBronzeRaskT]{Bronze Rask Theater}" scene where the this event transpires. A complete room-by-room description of its environment occurs there is detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim] area walkthrough. Text related to this event's core narrative is retained in this event and should be referenced alongside the walkthrough.

This area has several special rules and gameplay expectations, so it is advisable to review the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB]{Gameplay Details} page either before or during the party's exploration of the location.

Spotting the Ambush

Danger in Plain Sight

Characters need to make a successful [[/skill perception 15]] check to notice that there are people in the crowd who are paying more attention to them than the speech. Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] have advantage on this checks.

They will have three chances before Brynna finishes her speech to the crowd, and springs the trap. Characters that fail all three checks don't notice that they are being surrounded by potential threats, and will be surprised when combat begins.

Characters that succeed on at least one roll suspect something is off and are not surprised.

Brynna's speech

Brynna begins her speech to the gathered people:

@Embed[Actor.UVncdPqmzpZLwGvK]

Brynna stands before the crowd.

Thank you for coming, tonight is going to be a important turning point in the fate of Ordain, and I think you can all feel it.

This city used to be great once, it used to look after its people, it used to care about more than its nobility and coffers. Once, the Hallows keep order, the Cindarics kept us fed and healthy, and the Trading Houses made sure we had work.

Now? None of that. The Ordinate and its Veiled Chain, it's secret agents want to control us, watch us, make sure we don't step too far out of line. The city doesn't care about you, especially if you can't give something back to it.

The party should be given their first chance to spot danger here. They should also be prompted to take actions if they have any.

Readaloud paragraph text.

The Cindarics promised healing, but there’s sickness festering in the burns and no sanctuary in their temples. You’re left to sleep on cold cobblestones, because the stables and inns won't make room for you or your livestock.

You're forced to watch your loved ones suffer because the city’s too busy catering to the rich and powerful.

The Hallows say they are working for the good of all of Ordain, but what have they done? Crime and misery are beginning to choke the streets, thieves and merchants bleed everyone with impunity. They let you suffer, ignored and voiceless.

The party should be given their second chance to spot danger here. They should also be prompted to take actions if they have any.

Arcturians, when you fled the flats, when you brought your children and elders looking for shelter, did the city welcome you with open arms? No! Everything is rations, every little piece of help and aid they hand out is carefully measured to keep you wanting more.

It's bad enough you're here, displaced, suffering, but I hear them blaming you for the loss of crops and livestock, as though you wished for bandits, and sickness and monsters to destroy everything you and your families worked for!

She paces before the gathering, voice growing fierce.

We will not suffer their indifference. We will not be manipulated and used! We will not be silenced! We will not be subordinate. We will unite and be heard. It's time the city listened to those it thought could be ignored.

The party should be given their third and last chance to spot danger here. They should also be prompted to take actions if they have any. After the next narrative block the combat begins.

Hunter or Hunted?

Depending on how the party handled events to get here they will have a slightly different narrative block and encounters ahead of them.

Part Used Direct Methods

If either [[/eventState chain2Foxlair gatheredInformation]] or [[/eventState chain2Palisade gatheredInformation]] are true the party used overt methods to gather information, and the conspirators know the party is coming. Use the Cover Blown narrative block and enemy composition.

Party Remained Discreet

If both [[/eventState chain2Foxlair assistedAgitators]] and [[/eventState chain2Palisade assistedAgitators]] are true then the party chose discretion and haven't shown their hand yet. They'll still get caught in the ambush, but no special plans have been made for them. Use the Cover Intact narrative block and enemy composition.

Cover Blown

She stops to look over the crowd.

To those of you who want to join our cause directly, who want to take direct action, and place themselves on the front line of this fight, join me on the stage so we might stand together!

A small group of people move up to the edge of the stage to stand with Brynna. She smiles down at them, leaning down to shake a few hands before turning back to the crowd.

To the rest of you: I promise you that this won't end until we band together… and as for the Veiled Chain and their spies among us…

She locks eyes with you directly.

Don't think that we haven't be watching the watchmen. Your days of skulking through the spying on the people of Ordain are coming to an end!

Several people in the crowd around you throw back their hoods, and draw steel, angling their weapons at you.

@embed[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14]

Orbis Attunement: Cover Blown

If the party manages to blow their cover, each character who participates advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 chain2MeetingCoverBlown]] at the conclusion of the event.

Cover Intact

She stops to look over the crowd.

To those of you who want to join our cause directly, who want to take direct action, and place themselves on the front line of this fight, join me on the stage so we might stand together!

A small group of people move up to the edge of the stage to stand with Brynna. She smiles down at them, leaning down to shake a few hands before turning back to the crowd.

To the rest of you: I promise you that this won't end until we band together… but you'll still have a chance to play your part for the good of Ordain.

Primordis Attunement: Cover Intact

If the party manages to maintain their cover, each participating advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 chain2MeetingCoverIntact]] at the conclusion of the event.

Springing the Trap

Immediately after she says this a pair of armored, gas-mask wearing figures walk out onto the stage carrying bombs. A moment later they ignite and throw the bombs into the crowd, the projectiles sputtering and hissing as they fly. Both go off immediately, dispersing blasts of gas which stings the eyes and burns the throat!

You watch as some people begin to wobble on their feet and fall over, hitting the ground in heaps and going still. Others double over, coughing and trying to cover their faces.

As the crowd begins to panic and attempt to escape the smoke you see armed fighters pouring into the room to corral the crowd as the grenadiers prepare more bombs to subdue the crowd.

@embed[Actor.lB0MpcO3fI3sbOww]

@embed[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]

Once the fight begins, refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.sU8YWzkfl82nM0R6#encounter-details]{Encounter Details} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim]{The Bronze Rask Theater} area walkthrough.

After the Fight

Once the encounter has been completed, refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.sU8YWzkfl82nM0R6#searching-the-aftermath]{Searching the Aftermath} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim]{The Bronze Rask Theater} area walkthrough if the party wants to search the area. However, if the party wants to immediately leave to check on the Veiled Chain, they can, and this is a reasonable decision.

The party can return to the theater at a later time to resume searching the area if they want. The location will be deserted, with any dead bodies removed, and the doors locked once again. However, discoverable items will remain.

Abyss Attunement: Brynna Escapes

If Brynna Verocorrt manages to escape during or after the conflict, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 chain2MeetingCoverBrynnaEscapes]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the fight has ended, and the party is ready to move, they should report back to the Veiled Chain about the events that transpired here.
Midnight Meeting.soverview: The party heads to Fallbrook to attend a clandestine meeting located in the Bronze Rask theater. The true intentions of the agitators will be discovered here, but only after the party walks into a trap of Mutagists, and House Wandren thugs.
Midnight Meeting.sexposition:
Night settles over Fallbrook, but the district doesn't rest. The streets still teem with people coming and going, wagons and carts trundle over stone, while ferries and barges dock and depart from the waterfront nearby. All seems normal, but as you watch the sun vanish behind the skyline you can feel an odd electricity in the air. Something is happening tonight and it seems all of Ordain is aware of it.

Before long, you find yourself traversing the broad avenue of Kelekin Alley, a side-street lined with various shops and townhomes. Here, you spot a weathered alloy statue of a majestic four-legged beast perched above an otherwise unremarkable edifice: The Bronze Rask Theater.
Midnight Meeting.ssummary: We narrowly escaped an ambush set by Brynna Verocorte in the historic Bronze Rask Theater. Sadly, the leader of the organization escaped, but not before revealing that the Veiled Chain will soon be no more. We're returning to the headquarters now, uncertain of what we'll find.

Unhallowed.name: Unhallowed
Unhallowed.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event is a dramatic conclusion to the events of Spreading Sickness, and marks a dark turn for the party and their allies. The Veiled Chain will be badly set back by this betrayal, and its leadership rendered out of action for a while. The party's options are limited, but significant:

  • Save Shaar and Ankarist from imminent death.

  • Get the survivors medical assistance.

  • Put out fires and save vital documents.

Assets Under Development

A version of the Veiled Chain headquarters depicting the damaged state is planned but not yet complete. In the meantime, the event will show the undamaged version.

Speaking to Serethus

I had hoped the ambushes and traps I set would have been more effective. You are all proving to be frustratingly resilient. I assume that Brynna is dead, of course.

A pity. She had potential. Bright mind, keen intellect, drive and dedication to a cause greater than her. People who could have changed the world if they hadn't been murdered in cold blood… and you do so love your murder.

But, it doesn't matter. You are always just a little to late, aren't you? Always just behind us. You ruined the quarry lab, but not before we finished the mutagenic compound. You turned the cistern lab upside down, but not before we sent off our first shipments of stable residuum.

Now… well...

Serethus gestures to the death and destruction around him.

And with the Chain broken, you'll never catch up.

Who are you working for?

Giving you a name would only risk the security of our operations, and you've done enough damage as it is. I will say this though: their identity will be revealed when the time is right, and not a moment sooner.

Why are you doing this?

Serethus laughs.

All will be revealed in time, you just need to survive long enough to see it.

How can you do this?

It's quite easy, if I'm to be honest. I serve something greater than a city, or its government. I have become part of something greater, something truly world changing. The pain, suffering, and death are regrettable, but necessary for progress. Eventually you will see, and you will understand.

Ankarist Attacks

Ankarist pushes himself to his feet, calling his sword to hand as he rises, but he is too slow, too weak to best Serethus, who catches his wrist in a clawed fist, and twists the investigator's arm until his hand opens, and the blade clatters to the floor.

I admire your tenacity, Ankarist. But you need to learn when you've been beaten. You and your friends had to survive the traps and turn up before I could finish my work here and gotten away cleanly!

Serethus strikes Ankarist in the stomach, driving the man to one knee. Ankarist coughs a spit of blood then says:

I figured you out, so did Shaar. You aren't as clever as you think.

Serethus sneers, the anger clear as day on his features, though they twist into a cruel smile as a thought occurs to him. Without flourish he produces a syringe filled with green fluid from his robes.

Then let me send a message to the survivors, Ankarist: Survival isn't always the triumph one might think.

Serethus grabs Ankarist by the horn, and wrenches his head to the side, exposing his neck. With a swift stab, he drives a needle into the man's throat and presses the contents of the syringe into his body.

Ankarist screams in pain and doubles over, hands grasping at the side of his neck, as though me might claw the poison from it if he tries hard enough. The investigator is quickly lost to convulsions, and collapses on the floor.

Serethus Exits

Serethus turns calls out:

Time's up, we need to go!

In response, five figures appear from side rooms and passages, each of them carrying items, cramming books and papers into bags, or wiping blood off of weapons. By the look of their equipment, they are Mutagist and Wandren agents.

One speaks up:

We've destroyed what we can't take, but lost two in the fighting.

Serethus motions for his agents to gather around. As they do, his attention turns back your way, and he offers a smug, satisfied smile.

This is where we part ways. I am sure we will meet again. Until then, may cunning and wisdom guide you.

With another gesture and invocation of magic he and the agents at his side vanish in a flash of magical light. A moment later the wall of magical force collapses, granting access to the rest of the chambers.

Rescuing the Chain

Trapped Chain Members

Several rooms in the Veiled Chain have had fires set in them, and to make matters worse, these rooms have injured and dying members of the Veiled Chain trapped inside, incapable of extricating themselves without help.

A character (or party as a whole) trying to save people needs to accrue three successful [[/skill athletics 14]] checks to get everyone out safely.

Should a character (or party) accrue three failures before they get the necessary successes the fire and smoke grows too extreme to make any further attempts, dooming anyone left inside.

Characters failing a check by 5 or more must also make a saving throw against the Fire Hazard (see below).

Firefighting Assets

The danger of these rescue efforts can be partially mitigated with proper resources or spells. All of the following things provide Advantage to rescue rolls made by characters or groups:

  • The water barrel (See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200.JournalEntryPage.oWBdpAjAyc4fAFlH#looking-for-help]{Looking For Help} above) can be used three times.

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCreateorDe]{Create or Destroy Water} as part of a rescue attempt.

  • Casting @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbProtectionFro]{Protection from Energy (Fire)} on a character.

Fire Hazard

Characters that fail a rescue attempt by 5 or more must make a successful [[/save con 14]] or [[/save dex 14]] saving throw (the player chooses which). Failure deals [[/damage 1d6 fire]] damage.

Searching the Halls

Characters searching the halls for anything useful will need to make a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check, and as a result finds a water barrel and buckets which provide advantage on attempts to fight fires and rescue people trapped in burning rooms. This barrel can be used three times in this way before it's expended.

A higher roll will uncover additional items:

  • Result of 14+ also finds a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagHealersKit0]{Healer's Kit} in a cabinet in a ransacked side room. It has 5 uses in it, and is sufficient to stabilize the dying so that they'll survive long enough for help to arrive.

  • Result of 16+ also finds a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potion of Healing} which can be used to save a dying person.

Assisting Ankarist

What's Afflicting Ankarist?

Ankarist is &reference[poisoned], and &reference[incapacitated] due to a powerful mutagenic compound. Nothing short of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLesserRest]{Lesser Restoration} will clear these effects and remove the poison effect.

However, removing the poisoned state does not remove the alchemical and biomagical effects of the mutagenic compound. These have already begun to take root, and nothing the party has access to can stop its effects, not yet!

Examining Ankarist

A successful [[/skill medicine 13]] check reveals that Ankarist is badly poisoned and incapacitated by intense pain and muscle convulsions, but is otherwise stable.

  • Result of 16+ You also note that there is already discoloration forming around the injection site. This discoloration can also be seen seeping into his veins, darkening them.

Examining the Vial

Characters studying the syringe of poison must succeed on a [[/skill investigation 15]] or [[/skill medicine 15]] check to discern the nature of the chemical. Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] have advantage on this check.

  • Result of 15+ The syringe appears to be one taken from the cistern lab, and thus the dosage was meant for humanoids, not drakes. This is fortunate, since a larger dose would likely have been instantly fatal.

  • Result of 18+ The lot number written on the label dates this mutagen from the later days of the quarry lab experiments. This means the compound was one of the more stable variants, so it shouldn't kill him in the long run, but he may suffer from physical mutations which might be worse than death.

Worrying Implications

The collected evidence and research about Mutagist efforts in the region should lead the party to expect something is happening to Ankarist internally. Since he's a Drakon, and has some distant connection to dragons and drakes, he is likely going to suffer some similar, horrible fate.

  • Research data about the mutagenic compounds created the mutated drake, which suffered horrible physical deformities as the mutagen changed it.

  • Most of the early tests on the drakes killed them after lengthy, painful periods of illness and suffering.

  • Injecting humanoids with the mutagen was almost always immediately fatal.

Looking For Help

Searching the Hollows

A character wanting to return to the Hallows knows that it will take ten minutes to do so, effectively removing them from the scene, and making it impossible to assist in saving others in any way.

However, in trade, they encounter Shaar and a team of Chain members already rushing back to the headquarters, and the group can move together.

Shaar's Arrival

Once Serethus has departed, Shaar will arrive a short time later. This should be at least ten minutes, to give the party time to attempt rescuing people, and putting out fires, but can happen sooner at your discretion. When Shaar arrives, read the follow aloud:

You hear movement nearby, and as your attention shifts that way you see a group of Veiled Chain agents rushing into the headquarters, with Shaar leading them. She issues orders rapidly, and the agents begin fanning out to grab the injured, rescue materials, and put out fires.

Shaar quickly takes note of your presence, and moves toward you.

Where were you?

Chasing down leads on a conspiracy against the Hallows and Veiled Chain. Based on the state of things, we were all being led into traps meant to keep us busy while the conspirators dealt with the Chain H.Q… unfortunately, it seems they were successful.

Ankarist speaks up:

My lead was also a trap, but it was easy to avoid. When I realized they were distracting us I rushed back, and ran into Serethus and and his people ransacking the place.

Who is targeting the Chain and Hallows?

Serethus, The Mutagists, and House Wandren. What we don't know yet is how they are all connected, or what they are trying to accomplish.

What do we do now?

Save what and who we can, bury the dead, and move our operations to a more secure location, and take stock of the damage. We won't know what they stole and destroyed until we compare our files to case records.

After the Chain is up and running again, we start tracking down Serethus and the Mutagists, and figure out what to do about House Wandren.

Can we afford to wait?

It's not entirely a choice, the Chain won't be able to work at full capacity until things are put back in order, and fielding agents without proper backup and resources is only going to cost us more people. We won't stop watching and investigating, but recovery is the priority.

Concluding the Event

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

With Consecution Hall in tatters, the party has no course of action until the Veiled Chain has had time to recover. There are other quests and plots in the city that they can focus to in the meantime. Unfortunately for Ankarist, the bizarre effects of the mutagen are only beginning.
Unhallowed.soverview: The party returns to Consecution Hall in the Hallows to find the Veiled Chain headquarters ransacked and violated by Mutagists and the Otherhood. Serethus, evidently a Mutagist and a turncoat, injects Ankarist with a strange mutagenic reagent before escaping through a teleportation circle to destinations unknown. The party and the surviving investigators are left to pick up the pieces and save the dying.
Unhallowed.sexposition:
You move swiftly down the familiar halls leading to the Veiled Chain’s meeting chamber, but a wrongness hangs in the air as you draw closer. The usual quiet order of the halls feels unnatural, too quiet, as though the faint din of activity has ceased.

As you round the last corner, the scene inside the chamber stops you cold. Desks and chairs are overturned, reports strewn across the blood-smeared floor. At your feet, a dead agent in golden robes lies sprawled and still, a blade inches from his outstretched hand.

Across the room you see a half-dozen more bodies lie unmoving among the wreckage, and near the center of the room, Ankarist is slumped to his knees, clutching the hilt of a dagger lodged deep in his side. Towering over him stands Serethus, his fine robes spattered with blood.

At the sound of your approach, Serethus snaps his head toward you, eyes narrowing. With a sharp motion and a muttered incantation, a dazzling, translucent barrier leaps into existence and fills the space between you, humming with power and blocking any hope of quick rescue.
Unhallowed.ssummary: We arrived at the Veiled Chain headquarters too late to stop Serethus' attack. Shaar was grievously wounded, Ankarist was injected with some unknown mutagenic compound, and several other members of the Chain were killed. We have no further leads, and all investigation has come to a halt for now…

Crowds in Palisade Cross.name: Crowds in Palisade Cross
Crowds in Palisade Cross.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event tasks the party with a trip to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.ZOL7UfagZwmQvKzO]{Palisade Cross} district, where they must confront the as-yet-unidentified agitators that have been sewing civil unrest among the locals. Once they meet the agitators in question, the party members must decide how they want to proceed. In this event, the characters can:

  • Eavesdrop on the agitators to glean more information about their motives.

  • Either help the agitators or attack them, earning their trust or forcing a confession in the process.

Scanning the Crowd

The party will likely want to examine the crowd, and see if they can spot anything of note. The detained people will be the most immediate thing, but the agitators are also in plain view if they look more closely.

Refugees and Rebels

Characters making a successful [[/skill perception 14]] check notice that several people in the crowds carrying fliers matching the style of those previously seen, but the source of them isn't immediately obvious.

  • Result of 16+ Tracing the fliers as they move through the crowd, and seeing where they are missing in the hands of others, you're able to locate their source: A pair of unassuming citizens stopping people to talk to them briefly before handing out fliers taken from a satchel slung across their respective chests.

The agitators in questions are:

Drayk (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

Drayk's a short, stocky fellow missing an arm, with the empty sleeve pinned to his side. He has the look of a grizzled old sailor, permanently weathered by the sun and wind. His clothing is clean but plain.

Jahash (Neutral Evil, Arcturian Kivahr, he/him)

Jahash's tall, burly, and well past his prime. Long gray hair frames a weathered face and crooked nose that's been broken at least once. He moves with an obvious limp, and a rounded, puffy ear all but confirms this old fellow was a brawler of some sort once.

Speaking With the Agitators

Observing the Agitators

To successfully spy on the agitators, a successful group [[/skill stealth 12]] check is necessary. The ample crowds and animals make this relatively simple, and as long as the party doesn't do anything to draw attention to themselves, they'll be able to trail the agitators.

Watching them allows a few things to become clear:

  • Drake and Jahash never cross paths while handing out fliers, intentionally avoiding each other to cover more ground. Since they are actively talking to people in the crowd, approaching them directly would not be strange.

  • Jahash's bad leg means he doesn't move too much from his spot, and only wanders periodically.

  • Neither of them appear to be armed or armored in any obvious way, nor do they appear to be spellcasters. Given their age and injuries, it appears neither of them would be able to mount much of a defense if they were forced to fight.

  • While they are wary of their surroundings, and watching the crowds, they are watching for authorities, not random civilians in the crowd. It might be relatively simple to pickpocket them.

  • Every now and then Drayk wanders over to chat with Jahash. These meetings are always brief, lasting only a minute or two, and represent the best chance the party has to ambush the both them.

To get close to the agitators without drawing their attention, the party will need to exercise a bit of caution and deception.

Playing the Part

A successful [[/skill deception 14]] or [[/skill performance 14]] allows a character to appear like any other member of the crowd, acting agitated and desperate. Doing this allows them to move toward the agitators without drawing attention.

Alternatively, a successful [[/skill persuasion 16]] check allows the party to directly approach the agitators and convince them that the party is curious about the movement and interested in knowing more.

Once the agitators have been contacted, they can be spoken with to gain insight into the movement, and what's going on in Palisade Cross.

Talking Politics

Interacting with either of the Agitators provides this information directly:

  • Drayk and Jahash are members of a growing movement of Arcturian and Ordani citizens that have grown tired with the elitism and detachment Ordain shows to its own people inside and outside its walls.

  • They are handing out a new flyer. This flyer proclaims:

THE CITY DOESN'T WANT YOU HERE

It goes on to detail that the Ordinate, Hallows, and Trading Houses don't have an interest in helping the refugees. They won't ever dedicate enough resources to help everyone, and now that they aren't producing food and livestock in the flats, they are even less useful to the city.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] recognize this is an inflammatory half-truth that can be easily defended with little effort. For a group of stressed, distracted refugees, any nuance is likely to be lost.

Isn't this misleading and inflammatory?

Hardly. This city's flooded with Arcturians that got nowhere to go, nothing to their name, and the city's got nothing to offer them. All they're gonna do it bring the banditry, disease and monsters to us.

If the Trading Houses and Cindarics can't be bothered to look after us in the city, what makes you think they'll be bothered to help all these new outsiders?

Even the Burnished Hand here are arresting locals and detaining refugees rather than dealing with the problems outside the city.

Is there some larger action planned?

Yes, actually! Right now we're just getting people informed and interested in the movement. A greater collective action is in the works, and when that time comes, we'll be able to get the people together and really do something.

Is there some way we can help the movement?

Yeah, you can distract the Burnished Hand nearby, and give the detained people a chance to escape.

It's a load of crap they even got held, anyway. There was a disagreement between a couple refugees and some locals, and it blew up into an argument. Some of those bronze bullies were coming by, and decided to intervene.

Problem is, they detained everybody, and are threatening to drag them off to the Hallows. There's no reason for any of that, but they aren't listening to reason.

Why would they do that?

They are probably trying to make themselves into the city's guard force, if I had to bet. Rather than just being a band of monster hunters. Why else would they be getting into everyone's business and acting like they wield the law?

Have you tried talking to them?

Sure! They told me to take a hike unless I wanted to be lumped in with the rest of them.

Helping the Agitators

Characters wanting to help the people being detained will need to speak with the Burnished Hand officer.

Kabiro Klark (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

The burly, steely-eyed Burnished Hand officer is straight-backed and severe. The is a career monster hunter, practically having grown up in the Burnished Hand. He is loyal to them to a fault, and considers his duty to the Burnished Hand and the Arctus Plateau a calling.

Reading Kabiro

A successful [[/skill insight 14]] check allows a character to get a general read on Kabiro's personality. Generally speaking he's a career military man, or as close as a Burnished Hand warrior gets to being one. He takes himself, his position, and his duties incredibly seriously.

  • Result of 16+ He comes off as humorless, and stubborn, but seems to mean well.

Idle Hands

A successful [[/skill insight 14]] while watching the rest of the Burnished Hand warriors allows a character to notice that with the chaos of the crowds going on around them, their attention is split and scattered. It would be relatively easy to distract them.

Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] have advantage on the above check and also know that they could easily rile up the crowds to draw more attention, giving the detainees a chance to scatter.

Mayis Attunement: Helping the Agitators

If the party chooses to help the agitators, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 chain2PalisadeHelp]] at the conclusion of the event.

Riling the Crowd

A successful [[/skill persuasion 15]], [[/skill deception 14]] or [[/skill intimidation 16]] check can be used to incite the crowd to action. Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] have advantage on this check.

Depending on what the party chooses to do, and how they direct the crowd, this can have several different outcomes:

  • Directing the crowd's ire at the Burnished Hand for detaining people will result in violence. Stones and punches may be thrown, and the armored warriors will be forced to defend themselves. The ensuing skirmish with the angered crowd will result in them retreating from the area.

  • Directing the crowd's ire or attention toward the Hayren Arms (such as claiming they are offering first-come-first-served rooms) causes the crowd to rush the hotel, practically bowling over the Burnished Hand in the process, forcing them to redirect their attention, allowing the detainees to escape.

  • Inciting the refugees and locals to fight causes the Burnished Hand to try and break up the scuffles, creating a diversion necessary for the detainees to dissolve into the crowds, though some of them may decide to join the brawl.

Orbis Attunement: Riling the Crowd

If the party chooses to rile up the crowd, each character advances their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 chain2PalisadeCrowd]] at the conclusion of the event.

Trampling Hazard

If the party incites the crowd to violence, they will need to make a successful [[/skill acrobatics 14]], [[/skill athletics 14]], or [[/skill intimidation 14]] check to avoid being shoved around, attacked, or trampled by the crowd. Failure results in [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage, while failure by 10 or more results in [[/damage 1d8 bludgeoning]] damage.

Reporting Success

Returning to either Drayk or Jahash the party can report on their success.

If the party previously completed [[/eventState chain2Foxlairs]] by assisting the agitators there, then they say this:

I was watchin' from here, glad to see those bronze-headed thugs don't get to push locals around anymore. Anyway, thanks for the help.

Now, I'm pretty sure that I've heard about you. You helped out some refugees in Foxlairs, and stuck it to some bastard nobles trying to throw their weight around. Or at least that's what I heard. I respect that!

So here's the deal: We're gathering like-minded folk, potential allies, and supporters in the Verocorte estate in a few days. Come after midnight, we'll have three lanterns by the side gate located on Kelekin Alley if we're meeting. Use the passphrase "I won't be subordinate." to get in.

Be there. You're gonna like what you hear.

Otherwise, they have this to say in response:

Looking genuinely surprised at your success they shoot you a smile.

I was watchin' from here, glad to see those bronze-headed thugs don't get to push locals around anymore. Anyway, thanks for the help.

Now look, I don't meant to volunteer you or anything, but there are people like us all over the city that need help. Foxlairs for example? Whole lotta refugees needing somewhere to put their animals, and local merchants don't wanna let them. You might be able to unjam things there. Just saying.

Anyhow, I'd love to stick around, but I need to be on my way. Thanks again for the help here.

Attacking the Agitators

The party may choose the direct approach, here are the relevant skill checks and details for such an event:

Easily Approached

A party looking to ambush either Drayk or Jahash can do so easily. They do not put up much of a fight, and can be subdued without combat. They aren't looking to die for their cause (not yet at least), aren't armed or armored, and are not expecting a fight. They quickly surrender when faced with violence, especially where there's a risk they'll die.

Deniable Assets

Sura and Larz have been hired for this work, but aren't connected to the rest of the plot in any significant way.

Questioning Sura and Larz yields the following information:

Who are you working for?

Brynna Verocorrt, a rich noble who lives in Fallbrook. She wants agitate the locals against the Ordinate, and bring about social change.

What is the next step?

We're going to start handing out fliers for a rally in Fallbrook, gather up everybody, and get them to agree to join a new city-wide reform movement!

When is this meeting?

In a few days, after sundown.

Where will the meeting be held?

The old Bronze Rask threater, in Fallbrook. They are hosting it there.

The password to get in is: "I Won't Be Subordinate" given at the entrance.

Ragen Attunement: Attacking the Agitators

If the party chooses to attack the agitators, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 chain2PalisadeAttack]] at the conclusion of the event.

Looting the Agitators

If the party kills Drayk and/or Jahash, picks their pockets, or robs them they can find the following items of interest:

Robbing the Agitators

A successful [[/skill sleight 16]] check is necessary to lift items from the bags of either Drayk or Jahash. Failure by 5 or more results in the targeted agitator becoming wary of the party, and going to meet with their counterpart to warn them.

Shared Inventory

These items are carried by both Drayk and Jahash.

Planning Letter

This letter is about the upcoming meeting:

We're still putting together the details, but if anyone asks you: yes we're planning a proper rally. There's going to be a meeting at the Bronze Rask theater in Fallbrook, organized and paid for by Madame Verocorte. Expect that in the next week or so.

We'll start gathering people up soon.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] might suspect that a noble or merchant of means and influence is backing this movement. Why is a mystery, but political intrigue and ideological fights are not uncommon in the halls of power.

Foxlair Note

I want you two to hand out fliers in Palisade Cross, around the inns and apartments. Start with Rylo's Rooms. From what we've heard, it's choked with refugees from out of town, and is a good place to hand out fliers and build interest in the movement. There's almost certainly going to be tensions there between locals, visiting merchants, and refugees, which will help our messaging.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] recognize that this movement is very smartly tapping into displaced, desperate, and unhappy refugees that aren't receiving proper support from the city.

Spare Fliers

Their belongings include some spare fliers. All of them have the same leading line in bold font:

THE CITY DOESN'T WANT YOU HERE

It goes on to detail that the Ordinate, Hallows, and Trading Houses don't have an interest in helping the refugees. They won't ever dedicate enough resources to help everyone, and now that they aren't producing food and livestock in the flats, they are even less useful to the city.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] recognize this is an inflammatory half-truth that can be easily defended with little effort. For a group of stressed, distracted refugees, any nuance is likely to be lost.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event is completed when the party either collects evidence from the pair of agitators here, or earns their trust by helping them out with the Burnished Hand. Once they have done so, they can go to the other district to investigate that location.

Parties that looted materials directly from the agitators can skip investigating both locations and move to the Midnight Meeting event, as they have enough material and information to find it.
Crowds in Palisade Cross.soverview: The party investigates Palisade Cross, one of Ordain’s districts, for information about agitators spreading inflammatory propaganda meant to rile up locals. They'll need to identify the culprits, and decide how to deal with them.
Crowds in Palisade Cross.sexposition:
The air is heavy with the smell of sweat, road dust, and pack animals. The narrow street ahead is a sea of bodies, pressed shoulder to shoulder in places. These groups chatter noisily, parents wrangle children, friends yell after friends, and locals barter with refugees, the collective shouts and murmurs merging into a relentless wave of noise.

The groups filter toward a sprawling inn ahead — Rylo’s Rooms — perhaps the largest inn the city has to offer. As you make your way closer you spot a line of Burnished Hand warriors in gleaming bronze armor detaining a small group of locals and refugees for some unknown infraction.

A restless knot of refugees and locals alike shout and argue with the Burnished Hand leader, and tension hangs thickly in the air. Despite the chaos, the inn itself looms, its broad doors hanging open, and banners welcoming all comers, while inn staff stand out front trying to control the flow of visitors.
Crowds in Palisade Cross.ssummary: We investigated the agitators in Palisade Cross, and got leads that will help us track down the source of the propaganda fliers they are handing out.

Secondary Sources.name: Secondary Sources
Secondary Sources.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event allows the party to bring all their evidence to the Veiled Chain and receive their next assignment from Ankarist. While discussing things with him, the party can learn:

  • What Ankarist has been up to, what he's learned, and what he's doing next.

  • What their investigation has contributed to, and what it all means.

  • Where the party needs to go next.

Reporting on Lilifeld Station

Agricultural Concerns

The party can provide insight into operations at Lilifeld Stations, speaking to the level of preparation, safety and security on display with the grain stores, establishing at a basic level that the grain supply to the city is not tainted.

A successfull [[/skill arcana 14]] check notes that the wards the party was shown were well designed and more than capable of keeping any stored grains or other food stocks safe.

  • Result of 19+ Notes that the designs were particularly well implemented, easy to check and maintain, and layered well so as to have long-term redundancy. House Lilifeld planned it out well.

  • A character with [[/knowledge rituals]] has advantage on this check.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check notes that the visiting dignitary from Redrak was interested in getting the ward designs from House Lilifeld for use in their silohs as well.

  • A result of 18+ Notes that the dignitary expressed interest in making sure Redrak Fields was able to meet Ordain's needs and not lose as much stock to spoilage, and given how well the foreman and he got on, there's a good chance the deal will go through.

Pointless Busywork

If the party [[/eventState chain2Lilifeld examinedRecords]] as Serethus suggested, then they can also confirm that there are absolutely no issues with any shipments coming in from Redrak, nor any discrepancies in handling and storage.

Ankarist's Response

With the Golden Flats supply issues lately I'm glad we can still rely on Redrak Fields to feed the city. If both faltered things could become dire very rapidly. I understand that Del Kalais was there as well, he mentioned seeing you.

If the party [[/eventState chain2Lilifeld examinedRecords]] he also adds:

I appreciate your thoroughness on looking through the records, but I don't know that was the best use of time. Be that as it may, it's good to have that insight. I'll make sure it gets entered into the report.

Serethus' Response

If the party [[/eventState chain2Lilifeld missedSerethus]] at Lilifeld Stations he says:

Had you all actually agreed to meet me when I'd asked, perhaps I could lend some insight into what was seen! I'll endeavor not to take it personally, as we are all working toward the same end, and you still clearly did the work, but I do not appreciate being left in the lurch.

Otherwise he says:

I would largely concur that the situation at Lilifeld Stations is stable… however I think it critical the Veiled Chain should consider dedicating a team or two to regular inspections to ensure that House Lilifeld is upholding the thoroughness displayed for the visiting diplomat and investigators.

If the party did not [[/eventState chain2Lilifeld examinedRecords]] as Serethus suggested he will add:

Also, I suggested that your team should look into the last six season's worth of records for discrepancies. Since it seems they ignored that advice, perhaps you can spare another team to do so.

Ankarist takes a moment to consider that and then says:

I will put the recommendation on the final report, but we're too thinly spread for that right now.

Reporting on Lower Ashvale

Medical Inquiries

The party can provide a report on what they learned from the healing house in Lower Ashvale. They note that the sick are numerous but not overwhelming, none have died, and all should make a full recovery soon.

A successful [[/skill medicine 13]] check notes that while the patients are not too numerous right now, and the illness is not inherently deadly, it's contagious enough that it could begin spreading. If necessary, restorative magic can be used.

  • Result of 18+ If the disease is allowed to spread far and wide enough it could easily overwhelm the capacity of the Cindaric healing houses across the city. Long-term care of large volumes of patients is not what most of them are built for.

If the party [[/eventState chain2Ashvale medicalRecords]] successfully they can report on the disease more directly.

A successful [[/skill medicine 13]] check summarizes that the illness causes severe nausea and dizziness, sweating, vomiting, and weakness. However, treatment requires very little more than clean water and bed rest. However, it is spreadable through contact, especially if there is a lack of hygene.

  • Result of 18+ Notes that there are two illnesses at play, one due to alchemical exposure, and one stemming from it as a secondary illness. They have very similar symptoms, with only slight variations between the two, which results in them being mistaken for a single malady. The alchemical malady is harder to cure because the alchemical exposure needs to be resolved first.

Ankarist's Response

Well, it's good that nobody has died yet, but I am increasingly concerned about the risk of this spreading. Wasting sickness can easily get out of hand. I'll make note of this, and hopefully the Hallows can help the Cindarics get out ahead of it.

If the party [[/eventState chain2Ashvale medicalRecords]] successfully he adds:

Good investigative work, that distinction matters. We might have caught yourselves fighting two illnesses like they were one, never attacking the source.

Serethus' Response

So very good of the Cindarics to see to the ill. I am glad that they are keeping our city healthy. I think we should excise caution, perhaps caution the Hallows to quarantine the districts and search all the forges and water walls around the Burns. Time consuming, but the last thing we want is more outbreaks…
