  • @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.vCvZonF9atZIhDL7]{Ashvale Mausoleum}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.KVuVtYIMeLG4UfDi]{Antechamber}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.WmAwEcsFQtuKXOYC]{Chamber of Remembrance}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.AyE5UzznZQTARBwr]{Embalming Room}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.sVpTIjK8G8bhJloG.JournalEntryPage.JozGvLULBUbiPaJf]{Funeral Hall}

Each of the 5 Ken Crystals must be placed at least 50 feet away from the other crystals. If a character attempts to place Ken Crystals too close to each other, they won't vibrate with arcane energy until the proper distance has been traveled.

Whenever a Ken Crystal is successfully installed, it becomes wreathed in a dark nimbus of divination and illusion magic before disappearing from plain sight — seemingly vibrating out of our reality and into another, altogether unseen one.

The first time one of the characters attempts to install one of the Ken Crystals in the Burial Grounds, read the following aloud:

As you speak Sionia's command phrase, the crystal shard begins levitating from your hand and thrums rapidly with arcane energy. Space and time pulse around the ken crystal as it begins vibrating out of the visual spectrum. A moment later, it's as if the crystal has dissolved into the very fabric of reality here, where — invisible to the naked eye — it will await the Lonely Goddess' remote command.

Event Outcome: Eyes for the Deathbinder

Once the characters have successfully installed all 5 of Sionia's Ken Crystals in the Burial Grounds, check the "Eyes for the Deathbinder" Event Outcome at the top of the page.

Mayis Attunement: Eyes for the Deathbinder

Any character who successfully installs one of Sionia's Ken Crystals advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 cindaric2BurialGroundsEyes]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once the party is ready to depart the Burial Grounds, two downstream events await them: @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.KdqZ2BHPEi1Rh9tf]{Spirited Revelations} at the Numinous Shrines, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.d2HewHlB5nO1S5hQ]{Speaker Silenced} at Cindarin Temple. The former will provide them ample opportunity to follow up with Sionia about the undead remains they've collected, while the latter will propel the entire order of Cindaric Sages into a most uncertain and tumultuous future.

Sin is particularly interested in what Sionia has to say about the undead creatures the party has recently faced, and is eager to follow up with the Shard Goddess. The encounter at Corpin Sanctuary remains a solemn surprise, no matter which event the characters happen to trigger first.

Next Steps

Once the undead here in the Burial Grounds have been defeated, the party must collect one or more samples of undead remains for delivery to Sionia, who awaits them in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.aLXuhuWQdislrPnJ]{Numinous Shrines} for the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.KdqZ2BHPEi1Rh9tf]{Spirited Revelations}.
Grave Assignments.soverview: On behalf of Sionia, the party journeys to the Burial Grounds northeast of Ordain, where they must explore the catacombs for remnants of the recently slain undead. If the party can extract the remains of the creatures they fought in Westgate and Lower Ashvale, Sionia can use her divine necromancy to study them further. But the characters are in for a lethal surprise: a malicious undead hematophage lurks in the catacombs, feasting on the macabre evidence, ready for the party's arrival with a horde of undead minions at hand.
Grave Assignments.sexposition:
The air of the Burial Grounds is thick with anticipation as you navigate your way among the mossy gravestones and monolithic vaults. The lamps are lit, but no cemetery workers can be seen wandering the premises. It's remarkably quiet here. And solemn. And still.

After several minutes of careful plodding, you spot a familiar silhouette on the horizon. Your ally Sin Marmot stands at the ready, stoically waiting for your arrival, her cloak gently flapping in the breeze.
Grave Assignments.ssummary: We ventured to the Cindaric Crematorium beneath Ordain's hallowed Burial Grounds in search of the cadavers of recently slain undead. What we found there was gruesome and astonishing: a menacing undead hematophage was feasting on the corpses, stirred on by its devious master — an enigmatic necromancer who vanished in a terrible crimson mist. Our battle with the Corpuleth and its retinue of Skallith minions was fierce, but we emerged victorious thanks to a timely appearance by our friend Luna Karrowrath.

Numinous Rendezvous.name: Numinous Rendezvous
Numinous Rendezvous.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event allows the party to meet @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gT5S5ncAEUvkYYYg]{Sionia}, the Shard God of necromancy, and learn about her specific thoughts regarding the rising undead threat. In this event, the characters can:

  • Locate @UUID[Actor.jzrNvlGQHpoSkkIU]{Sionia} at her own shrine within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.aLXuhuWQdislrPnJ]{Numinous Shrines} district.

  • Speak with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard God} about her recent observations regarding necromancy and the undead, and how these phenomena relate to an undefinable change in Ember's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle}.

  • Share information about their own experiences with the undead, leading to a clandestine mission from Sionia for which they are most qualified.

  • Receive @UUID[Item.TS35W4W7SwFaMCP3]{Sionia's Blessing} before they head into the potentially dangerous environs of the Burial Grounds.

The Shrine's Riddle

In order to beckon Sionia from her idle activity, nearby and out of sight, the party must solve the shrine's relatively simple riddle: "The Deathbinder's Armaments" refer to the material spell components for Necromancy spells, which will metaphysically call the shard goddess' attention when left upon the stoney floor of her shrine.

The Summoning Rite

Characters with [[/skill passive arcana 15]] or who succeed on a [[/skill arcana 13]] check understand the shrine's riddle, and know that the correct offerings here are material spell components for Necromancy spells (including Spellcasting Foci featuring Sionia or Necromancy iconography, enchanted items with auras of necromancy, et al).

  • Characters with [[/knowledge gods]] or [[/knowledge undeath]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • Clerics, paladins, and warlocks whose spellcasting is powered by Sionia or other necromancy automatically succeed on this check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on this check.

Alternately, character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 15]] check is able to surmise what the inscription on the flagstone is referring to.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge gods]], [[/knowledge rituals]], or [[/knowledge undeath]] have advantage on this check.

Characters who fail these skill checks can attempt them again once per hour by gathering information from locals, researching via books and scrolls, etc.

Once the party solves the shrine's riddle, Sionia appears from another undisclosed location nearby.

Meeting Sionia

When one of the characters places a suitable offering on the inscribed flagstone, the shard goddess Sionia appears once more. Read the following aloud:

You place the offering on the floor of the unassuming alcove, and for a moment you consider the notion that you might be wasting your time. In a flash, the materials are enveloped in a ghostly flame, and the flagstone is barren once more.

A somewhat familiar female voice greets you from behind.

That which is given is returned.

You turn to see the alluring woman from the Temple of Sockets, her hand outstretched, palm open — containing the very item you left on the alcove floor. She hands the offering back to you with a look of studious curiosity.

You seek an audience with the "Deathbinder," do you? Well, here I am.

She gestures at herself and her surroundings with sardonic humility.

Tell me, what business do we have?

@Embed[Actor.jzrNvlGQHpoSkkIU]

A Conversation with Sionia

Although she recognizes the party from the brief encounter at the Temple of Sockets, Sionia is most likely unaware of their involvement with the incidents with the undead creatures in Fallbrook and Westgate. (News travels quickly enough in Ordain, but fame and notoriety take time). If the party wants to solicit Sionia for her advice about the rising undead threat, they must adequately convince her that their mission is a worthy one.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 13]] or [[/skill deception 18]] check is able to convince Sionia that the party's goals are worthy of her time and attention.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge souls]], [[/knowledge undeath]], or [[/attunement Orbis]] have advantage on these checks.

  • Characters can re-attempt this check each time they offer Sionia a new anecdote about one of their previous encounters with the undead (whether earlier in the campaign or an explicit part of the character's background and history).

  • Clerics, paladins, and warlocks whose spellcasting is powered by Sionia or other necromancy automatically succeed on this check.

  • Additionally, characters who have any loose item, keepsake, or component from the @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} the party encountered during @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.JN1mTKPlSA0WKizP]{Sanctuary of Death} automatically succeed on this check.

Once the characters have adequately convinced Sionia of the veracity of their cause, she's willing to discuss the matter beyond surface-level issues and simple pleasantries. Topics of discussion include (but are not limited to):

  • The events that led the party here to begin with, including the subject of their conversation with Conaris Haid. Knowledge is power, as far as Sionia is concerned.

  • A brief history of Sionia's advent to the Arctus Plateau, and why: to conduct her own investigation about the rising undead threat.

  • The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle}. Sionia explains in detail how this cosmic process ordinarily works, and provides evidence that it's currently malfunctioning. There are three major pieces of evidence in support of Umbra's theories:

    • Sionia's reanimations have been stronger than usual of late, but there have also been elements of unpredictability, even for such a powerful necromancer as the Deathbinder herself.

    • Sionia has encountered corrupted shards of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.O9EH9dLsKfdv3oif]{Heart Crystals}. These hazy shards seem to have absorbed latent energies from beyond Ember, and react accordingly around undead creatures and places of necrotic power.

  • Details about various lesser undead that have been seen throughout the plateau. Sionia is particularly keen on categorizing any creatures the party has encountered thus far.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check can readily tell that Sionia's point of view about these matters is authentic, and feels as though she's been confident and trusting throughout her interaction with the party.

Additional conversation points are detailed below, in Sionia's own words.

Who are you?

"I am Sionia, a shard-bearer who some have come to know as the Deathbinder. Others know me as the Lonely Goddess, or even the God of Necromancy. But you may call me Sionia. My life as a so-called shard god has been a relatively short one by Ember's standards, and my concerns are largely the same as they were prior to my ascension. Ultimately, my past is unimportant. It is our actions that define us, don't you agree?

I've come to the Arctus Plateau in search of answers about the mounting threat of suspicious necromancy in the region. Ordain is far from the Moiran wastelands to the west, and it troubles me to consider what kind of cosmic unrest might be at the heart of this matter."

About the Soul Cycle:

"All living creatures on Ember — from the lowest beast to the oldest shard god — have Souls. Souls are motes of Lifeforce from the Heart of Ember, joined with a physical body at birth. When a mortal creature dies naturally, both their Spirit (which is the accumulation of their life experiences) and their Soul (the spectral, metaphysical essence of the being) leave their body and drift toward the Spiritlands.

Someone or something is interrupting the Soul Cycle. And I'm eager to find out who or what."

Regarding Necromancy:

"You're already quite aware of how welcome I was at the Temple of Sockets …

Most of us are told since birth that necromancy is inherently evil — an instrument of chaos and malevolence and darkness. But this, like many notions of our time, is a half-truth. Like any tool, necromancy is as good or as evil as the one who handles it.

My philosophy is simple: souls are the domain of Sockets, and are the immutable stuff of the Cosmos; but the physical remains we leave behind are nothing more than terrestrial matter. Just as a transmuter can shape flesh to stone with ethical consideration, necromancy can transform death into a semblance of life. Flesh and bones are as clay to the skilled necromancer. The clay itself is not evil, nor is the art of shaping it."

The Looming Undead Threat:

The shard goddess regards you with a measure of concern.

"Your party's encounters with the restless dead aren't the only evidence of this looming threat or its magnitude. My own reanimations have been suspiciously unpredictable of late, and the dead speak with troubled voices these days. This is surely a sign of things to come."

Once the party breeches the subject of what to do next, Sionia takes command of the conversation with a light display of magic.

With a wave of her hand, Sionia conjures the apparition of a sprawling cemetery with Ordani architecture, full of overgrown grave markers and mausoleums. The image zooms in on a massive doorway in one corner of the cemetery, marked with a large Cindaric symbol on the front.

Our task is clear. You must journey to Ordain's Burial Grounds north of the city, where the Cindarics are known to deposit the mortal remains of the dead following certain embalming rites. Bring me the corpses of these undead creatures you encountered in the city before the Cindarics incinerate them according to their sacred ceremony. With the bones or flesh of these curious undead creatures in-hand, I can try to deduce their origin through magic and ritual of my own.

The goddess looks to you with a measure of regret in her eyes.

I would go myself, if not for the solemn pact I've made with Conaris Haid and the Temple of Sockets. You see, I'm allowed to practice my magic in the city, but I've been forbidden to enter the Burial Grounds for any reason whatsoever. And considering how tenuous my alliance with the church is, I aim to maintain this accord."

Sionia dismisses her illusion and presses her hands together in thought.

What say you? Is this macabre task within your capacities?

About the Burial Grounds:

"Most of the Burial Grounds are open to the public, with few exceptions: the Cindaric Crematorium where the undead corpses can be found is normally off-limits. However, your ally Sin Marmot can most likely acquire the credentials you need, along with precise directions to the Cindaric facility.

The Burial Grounds are generally a welcoming place, where the mortal remains of adherents to all faiths of Ember can be found. The rise of the Cindaric religion in recent centuries has slowed the need for physical expansion of the cemetery, thanks to their funerary practices — which involve an elaborate cremation ceremony high above a pit of subterranean magma.

The cemetery is attended by a cohort of priests and acolytes of various faiths, with a heavy Cindaric presence for obvious measure. With any luck, your clandestine journey to the crematorium facility will be an uneventful one."

Viable Undead Remains:

"The description of the creature you encountered in Westgate bears striking similarities to certain minions of the Moiran Blood Barons. But the only way to be sure is to get a closer look at the corpse, so that I might examine it with magic and artifice.

As for the entity you fought in Fallbrook, it sounds somewhat novel and wholly new to me. The implications are murky and rather vast until I can investigate the remains with my own eyes.

Bring back whatever remains you can from either corpse — something from both, if possible. Bones, flesh, organs … whatever you can retrieve and safely escort back here to me without arousing suspicion."

Sionia has a parting gift for the characters to make their potentially-dangerous journey to the Burial Grounds less deadly.

The Lonely Goddess raises her hands, which dance on the air with inscrutable arcane gestures. Threads of magic flow out of her fingertips and individually towards your chests, and you feel an oncoming surge of divine inspiration.

One more thing before you go: a blessing to help bring you back safely, so that we might put this nightmare to rest.

It seems the shard goddess has granted you some kind of divine and esoteric boon, one you perhaps hope you'll never have to use.

Sionia's Blessing

Each character should add the @UUID[Item.TS35W4W7SwFaMCP3]{Sionia's Blessing} feature to their character sheet at this time, to be removed once the feature has been used.

Additionally, each character gains one point of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.AQ1oTG7jHy5kZuN9]{Heroic Inspiration}.

A Secondary Objective

The party may assist Sionia with a secondary task if they choose, and will be justly rewarded if their efforts are successful. Before the characters depart, she turns to them with the additional offer.

Sionia begins gesticulating, and five scintillating crystal shards manifest before your very eyes, swirling before the necromancer goddess in a slow and hypnotic dance.

One more thing … Conaris said I couldn't step foot in the Burial Grounds, but he never said I couldn't scry upon them. If you wish to earn my favor, scatter these special crystal shards around the Burial Grounds — indoor and out — so that I might keep an eye on that measurably important corner of the world from afar.

Simply hold each crystal aloft when you've found a suitable spot for it and speak the words:"Eyes for the Deathbringer." You will know the proper places for them when you're in their midsts. Do we have an accord?

Sionia asks the characters to install a series of scrying devices throughout the Burial Grounds so that she might monitor the area from afar. She has a measure of respect for Conaris Haid, despite his madcap ramblings and misguided dogma, and doesn't want to dishonor the pact she's made. However, current events are a sign that her watchful guidance can often be helpful (even if she can't physically be there herself).

After you accept the shard goddess' offer, the five crystals float gracefully through the air to hover in front of you, ready for the taking.

Then it's settled. You have everything you need. Now, make haste, and find us some lovely specimens, if you please.

The wind stirs, sweeping dust from the street into your watering eyes. As your vision clears, it's plain to see that Sionia no longer stands before you, vanished like the breeze itself.

The characters are free to take up these 5 @UUID[Item.G4v6oL4DTZ3ZPBZ5]{Ken Crystals} and add them to their inventory.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party must journey to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.cvUD3Rj9MLXLwpAb]{Burial Grounds} northeast of Ordain for the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments}, during which they'll search for the remains of the undead creatures they encountered at Westgate and Fallbrook.
Numinous Rendezvous.soverview: The party journeys to the Numinous Shrines district for a visit with Sionia, so they might learn more about her radical theories about the nature of undead in the region. If the characters can provide her with certain assurances, the Shard God has a task for them that will involve an expedition to Ordain's Burial Grounds in search of undead remains.
Numinous Rendezvous.sexposition:
One corner of the Mall of The Nineteen is remarkably staid compared to the rest — an alcove where a shrine should be is decorated with silence and neglect rather than candles, charms, and offerings. There is a sullen feeling about this forsaken place, and the air here feels measurably cool compared to the rest of the neighborhood.

A phrase is inscribed on the flagstone where you'd expect to find an altar, etched in Common:

THE DEATHBINDER'S ARMAMENTS
AVAIL THE LONELY GODDESS
Numinous Rendezvous.ssummary:
We traveled to Ordain's Numinous Shrines district to speak with the Shard God Sionia about the rising undead threat. Sionia has tasked us with an important mission: journey to the Burial Grounds northeast of Ordain on a clandestine search for the remains of the undead creatures we encountered in Lower Ashvale and Westgate. With these undead remains in-hand, Sionia can learn more about their origins.

But we must hurry: the remains are being prepped for cremation according to traditional Cindaric purification rites. If we have time and interest, we can also install a handful of scrying devices for Sionia, who is prohibited from visiting the Burial Grounds by Conaris Haid and his acolytes.

Helping Hands.name: Helping Hands
Helping Hands.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event invites the party visit Veneration Hall, the headquarters of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} in Ordain, and learn more about the militant organization (while being covertly interrogated by the Burnished Hand’s stoic leader Steros Kraver). In this event, the characters can:

  • Journey to Veneration Hall in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.86owx3lgvm2zLyv4]{Lower Ashvale} (at least one day after @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.ni5ibLbO93pU3Frt]{Sagacious Initiation}) and explore the garrison’s limited public areas, gathering whatever details and information they may.

  • Meet with the venerated warrior @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver} to learn more about the Burnished Hand, including somewhat propagandized associations with the Cindaric Sages and potential recruitment options.

  • Choose to avoid suspicion by obscuring their motives from Steros and other Burnished Hand members, or otherwise reveal their true intentions.

  • Meet a low-ranking @UUID[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA]{Burnished Hand Protector} as they leave, who solicits the party to perform a wellness check on their behalf in the neighboring @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.giaDQErIafhgueop]{Fallbrook} district.

Early Access Work in Progress

This event is intended to use an Ordain Interior vista configured for Veneration Hall, which is unavailable at this time. The interior scene must be imagined for now.

Gaining Entry

The Burnished Hand Protector stationed outside the entrance of Veneration Hall is a brash young solider named Tolus (LN, Ordani Kivahr, he/him), who must be adequately convinced or persuaded if the characters wish to gain entry to the semi-private facility. However, the party can't actually fail this test of social skill, and the characters will ultimately gain entry one way or another.

As you step towards the threshold, the young warrior looks down his chiseled nose at your group with no small measure of apprehension. It's clear this armored sentinel takes the duties of his station seriously. He addresses you before you have a chance to speak:

Welcome to Veneration Hall, home of the Burnished Hand and its Protectors. Please state your business. The barracks are closed to outsiders.

@embed[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA]

Providing Credentials

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 13]], [[/skill deception 15]], or [[/skill intimidation 17]] check is able to convince Tolus that the party's invitation by Steros is authentic.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] and [[/knowledge politics]] have advantage on these checks.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters automatically succeed on these checks.

Alternately, any character who targets Tolus with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCharmPerso]{Charm Person} spell automatically succeeds on these checks.

Additionally, the party may use their growing infamy to gain entrance. Any character who relates a rousing story about a previous encounter with an undead creature automatically succeeds on these checks. Appropriate encounters include:

  • the Skallith horde from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.JN1mTKPlSA0WKizP]{Sanctuary of Death} event at Corpin Sanctuary

  • the Vampyre Spawn encounter during @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy}

  • the Sodden Corpses of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.2expJELjYHucAyKl]{Harrowed Crossing} event

  • the encounter with Tethra Shùl and her Horrendors in @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush with Death}

  • any other appropriate encounters.

Once Tolus the Protector has been suitably convinced, he opens the massive front gate and invites the characters to enter.

Primordis Attunement: Entry via Deception

Any character who uses their skills of Deception to gain entry to Veneration Hall advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 cindaric2HandsDeception]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aura Attunement: Entry via Magic

Any character who uses magic to gain entry to Veneration Hall advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 cindaric2HandsMagic]] at the conclusion of the event.

Luxarum Attunement: Entry via Infamy

Any character who uses their infamy to gain entry to Veneration Hall advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 cindaric2HandsInfamy]] at the conclusion of the event.

A Meeting with Steros

Following their successful entry, the characters are escorted through Veneration Hall to the office of @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m]{Steros Kraver}, who they likely encountered at Corpin Sanctuary and Cindarin Temple. This meeting is both an opportunity for Steros to estimate the party's capabilities as potential recruits for the Burnished Hand, and a chance for him to gauge their overall intentions as persons of interest in the looming undead threat.

As another sentinel takes his place, Tolus ushers you on a brief tour into the depths of Veneration Hall, a spacious edifice marked by the smell of musk and metal alongside sounds of combat training and lively music.

Moments later, you find yourselves entering the modest office of Steros Kraver, who sits behind a large wooden desk decorated with maps, scrolls, and folded parchment. His bronze helmet serves as an ersatz paperweight as a light breeze sweeps through the room, rustling the desk's accoutrements with regularity. The commander smiles when he sees you, with looks of recognition and satisfaction on his handsome face, like a man who just won a friendly bet.

I see you've accepted my offer for a visit to Veneration Hall. Welcome to our humble abode. Make yourselves comfortable. We have water for refreshment, and plenty of room for company. So tell me: how does a motley group of slayers like yourselves get involved in so many entanglements with undead creatures? Word of your accomplishments travels fast. And I'd like to know if you have what it takes to wear the bronze plate and take arms against enemies of the Cindarics.

A Meeting with Steros

Steros Kraver is interested in getting to know the characters, their capabilities, and their motivations. And while he presents an element of good faith, he's also quite curious about how and why the party has been involved in the series of events to date regarding the looming undead threat.

After the characters are given an opportunity to regale the commander with stories of their previous exploits, additional topics of conversation include:

  • The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.QahIpRl4OYbZ8KiM]{Burnished Hand} and their role as stewards of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} and the great city of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}.

  • A brief account of Steros Kraver's own history and his rise to the rank of commander of the Burnished Hand.

  • The importance of the Cindaric Sages and their faith.

  • The looming undead threat and what it means for Ordain and the Arctus Plateau at large, along with the need for new recruits to stem this unholy tide. Steros is curious about the potential roles the characters could play in his organization, whether at home or afield.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check is able to confirm the veracity of Steros' interest in the capabilities of each party member, and his earnest desire to see if they're a good fit for the Burnished Hand.

  • Result of 16+: There is an element to the commander's inquiry that suggests an ulterior motive. Nothing nefarious, just something hidden beyond the charismatic keen of his steely eyes.

Any character who targets Steros with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectThou]{Detect Thoughts} spell is able to sense feelings of ease and anticipation, and knows that the safety of Ordain looms large in the commander's mind.

If the characters attempt to confront Steros for this light ruse, the commander will readily and happily admit his agenda. Indeed, who wouldn't want to know more about such famed and capable slayers of the undead — particularly when one is the commander of the Burnished Hand. Steros views it as his solemn duty to protect the Hand and the Cindarics they serve, and will to to any lengths necessary to uphold this righteous duty.

Additional conversation points are detailed below, in the commander's own words.

About the Burnished Hand:

The commander proudly knocks on the iconography of his breastplate with a soft fist.

"The Burnished Hand is everything to me. When I needed direction, I found it here. When I asked for a reason why, the order answered. We are the open hand in times of need, and the closed fist in times of trouble. Together with the Cindarics, we seek to keep the Heartblood of Ember pumping pure and strong, for an eternity to come.

That's a long time, my friends. And we need good soldiers and honest protectors for the long road ahead."

Opinion of the Cindaric Sages:

"The Cindarics are Ember's chosen protectors. I truly believe that. Something inside each one of them stirs them to devote their very lives to the Heartblood and its ceaseless flow. We're lucky to have such custodians in our time. The Cindarics toil so that generations of Ordani and Arcturian people can thrive. It's a beautiful thing, and it deserves to be protected at all costs."

Opinion of Jon Vastil:

With a deep breath, a quick sigh of pride escapes the commander's nostrils.

"Jon Vastil is a good man with a kind heart. He's also got a rather sharp mind for his age, and manages to keep my office fairly busy. As you're well aware, we've had to take on some fairly sizable operations lately, from the march on Corpin Sanctuary to an increased street presence throughout the city. These edicts come from the Holy Speaker himself, with my counsel of course; but his edicts are fair. Jon Vastil has guided the Cindarics for the better part of a century, and the old man deserves every ounce of respect he's afforded."

Opinion of Vinarith:

The commander proudly knocks on the iconography of his breastplate with a soft fist.

"The Steward is a capable and learned Sage in his own right. In fact, Vinarith's divinations have helped us prognosticate more than one of these undead encounters, but not with the swiftness or precision needed to stop them. He takes after the Holy Speaker quite a bit, and has done much to refine the modern image of the Cindarics among younger initiates. When it comes to veteran sages, Vinarith knows his way around the temple, and is recognized by many of the city's residents as one of Ordain's brightest sons. I look forward to working with him more often."

Opinion of Lilla Arien:

"The Second Sage is a lovely woman, if a bit sheepish. Her matronly kindness precedes her, and she's a valuable asset to the order. I must admit, we don't often share much in terms of conversation, and I doubt we have too many things in common aside from Ordani pride and an adherence to the Cindaric faith. But she's a lovely woman all the same."

Examining the Area

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] check while actively observing Steros and his office during the meeting is able to notice the following:

  • The maps on the desk detail various sections of the Arctus Plateau, including a swathe of the Wedgelands to the northwest and the Bloodwoods north of Ordain. Reveal the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.i8a6VBrxUsZ2PaHo]{Talei} points of interest to the players.

  • Many of the folded parchments on the desk consist of official communication to and from Cindarin Temple, marked with the seal of the Holy Speaker.

  • The chambers of Veneration Hall are well-kept, but the eaves are dusty and the corners are dingy, which suggests a cleaning routine that overlooks the smallest details. It seems the soldiers of the Burnished Hand prefer to spend their free time on practical matters like training and leisure.

Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell draws attention to the commander's @UUID[Actor.voKZyf0ZE8EBY27m.Item.AaZY0FHTbjDVcrhM]{Vicious Greataxe} mantled on a weapon rack nearby, along with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll00]{Spell Scroll} of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplIdentify00]{Identify} and two @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll00]{Spell Scrolls} of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplComprehend]{Comprehend Languages} on the desk.

Once the party has had ample time for conversation with Steros, read the following aloud:

With brusque alacrity, Steros stands and dons his helmet.

Well, friends, that concludes our time for now. I look forward to additional consultations in the days and weeks to come. But for now, I have business at the Rusted Fortress that requires some timely attention. Please, return at your leisure to discuss an alliance with our group once you've had ample time to give it some serious consideration.

The brash young Tolus appears once more, ready to escort you back to the front gate of Veneration Hall. Your egress is swift and without incident.

One Last Thing…

Following their meeting with Steros, the party is approached by a lower-ranking Burnished Hand Protector with a concerned request for them. This is Vance (CG, Arcturian Human, he/him), a typically lighthearted solider who is currently upset by circumstances beyond his control — a fellow protector hasn't reported in for duty in a few days, and Vance wants to perform a wellness check on his friend without alerting any official parties or his commanding officers.

As you linger on the street outside Veneration Hall for a brief moment, you're approached by another Burnished Hand Protector with a look of concern in his eyes. The man beseeches you with a rural Arcturian accent, his voice measured and hushed.

I'm sorry to bother you, but I could really use your help. The stories of your exploits precede you. And I'm in dire need of some reliable assistance …

The young solider leans in to whisper more softly.

… Assistance that is better left a secret. I can pay you in advance, for just a few hours of your time.

The Protector’s Plea

If the party is willing to hear his plea, Vance pulls them aside from the main thoroughfare to disclose the precise nature of the plight at hand:

  • Burnished Hand protectors are assigned daily-to-weekly shifts in various districts of the city as well as stations at the Rusted Fortress on Bura Island. Vance's best mate Ordan was scheduled to relieve Vance here at Veneration Hall three days ago, and Vance doesn't want to get his closest friend in trouble if he can help it.

  • Ordan keeps an apartment in the neighboring Fallbrook district. If the party is willing to perform a wellness check on Ordan, Vance will pay them [[/award 50gp]] pieces in advance for their effort.

  • Ordan was seen returning from his shift at the Rusted Fortress by a few other locals, but he wasn't seen leaving his apartment.

  • Vance and Ordan have been best friends since childhood, the kind of pure and honest camaraderie that is often hard to find.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 11]] check can determine that Vance's words are authentic, and that his concern for Ordan and his livelihood are sincere.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 15]] check is able to convince Vance to offer the party a little more reward for their effort, which takes the form of a jewled heirloom @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepDagger0000]{Dagger} worth 25 gp.

Additional conversation points are detailed below, in Vance's own words.

About the Burnished Hand:

"I'm proud to serve with the Burnished Hand. The pay is good, and I sleep well at night, even if the hours are long. It feels good to help protect the city."

About Steros Kraver:

"Steros is a bit of a hard-ass, but he always means well. One thing's for sure: he won't take kindly to finding out that Ordan's derelict of duty, even if he's only been shitting his brains out in Fallbrook for the past three days."

Why are you so concerned about Ordan?

"Ordan likes to drink. And he loves to fight. This isn't the first time he's screwed up a shift; but if he keeps this up, it just might be his last. We go back pretty far, Ordan and me. Hell, I joined the Burnished Hand because of that brazen fool. And I'll be damned if he gets kicked out before I do. So it would mean a lot to me if you could just drag him back to work without a fuss."

Once the party accepts Vance's offer, he provides the characters with precise directions to Ordan's apartment in Fallbrook, which the party can find with total ease.

Concluding the Event

After their encounters at Veneration Hall, the party can follow up on their investigation with a visit to the Fallbrook home of the missing Burnished Hand Protector, Ordan. There are no formal plans in place by Steros to recruit the characters at this time, although he's happy to keep the conversation going in the days and weeks to come.

Next Steps

If the party wishes to follow up on Vance's task, the characters must journey to the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.giaDQErIafhgueop]{Fallbrook} district for the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.HKGCsBtXR0tfedkJ]{The Derelict Protector}, wherein they'll encounter the errant Ordan — who has somehow become an undead creature himself.
Helping Hands.soverview: The characters are invited to Veneration Hall in Ordain’s Lower Ashvale district for an audience with Steros Kraver of the Burnished Hand, who has taken an interest in the party’s involvement at Corpin Sanctuary and elsewhere. Characters with the particular interest or skills can partner with the Burnished Hand as potential recruits, but Steros is actually using this moment to subversively gather intelligence on the party and their motives.
Helping Hands.sexposition: You arrive at Veneration Hall, an impressive stone edifice whose columns, walls, and balustrades are elaborately decorated with an aged bronze plating that matches the amber-hued armor of the exalted soldiers who dwell within. A Kivahr warrior clad in the order's model russet plate mail stands in attendance before the front threshold.
Helping Hands.ssummary: We met with Steros Kraver of the Burnished Hand in Ordain’s Lower Ashvale district. While leaving Veneration Hall, we were approached by a Burnished Hand Protector named Vance who beseeched us to check up on a fellow Protector who has been missing for a week. We must head to the neighboring Fallbrook district in search of a Protector named Ordan if we wish to honor Vance's plea for assistance.

Speaker Silenced.name: Speaker Silenced
Speaker Silenced.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event occurs in the wake of the party's fight in the Burial Grounds, and allows them to present their findings to @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.GlbJezRw2ecnVIsx]{Cindarin Temple}. However, grave tidings of the utmost magnitude await the characters when they arrive. In this event, the characters can:

  • Learn about the death of the Holy Speaker @UUID[Actor.KQ9uGdZu6zDlM66n]{Jon Vastil} alongside their ally @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}.

  • Speak with Lilla Arien and other Cindaric Sages about everything that has transpired.

  • Help Lilla formulate an early hypothesis about why and how this undead uprising in the Arctus Plateau is happening, and what the Cindarics can do to stop it.

Debriefing The Second Sage

@UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien}, @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}, and other Cindarics including @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith} are gathered here in the Cindarin Temple sanctuary for an impromptu wake of Jon Vastil.

After Vinarith exchanges his pleasantries, the party can speak with @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} about everything that has transpired — from their encounter in the Burial Grounds (and Sionia's related thoughts), to the death of the Holy Speaker and the future of the Cindaric Sages. @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} is part of this exchange, although her participation is markedly reserved.

Lilla Arien takes a deep breath before turning her full attention to your group.

Initiate Marmot tells me you've had quite an excursion to the Burial Grounds, but she was reluctant to share all of the details until you arrived. Please, let's step away from the crowd to discuss things with a bit more discretion.

The Second Sage motions you towards a quiet corner of Cindarin Temple, where your narrative might go unheard by the sorrowful throng gathered here for the Holy Speaker.

A Conversation with Lilla

Even though the day is painted with grief, Lilla Arien is eager to hear what became of the party's journey to the Burial Grounds north of Ordain. After the characters have had a chance to relate their story, the Second Sage informs them about the matters at hand facing the Cindarics:

  • Lilla expresses her own grief at losing Jon Vastil, who was like a father figure to her, despite how overlooked she's felt in recent months.

  • Lilla emphasizes how troublesome the timing is for such a tragedy. The Cindaric order has already under mounting pressure and scrutiny due to various conflicts in the region, including lingering earthquakes a surplus of refugees, errant monster attacks, civilian disappearances, and now — most notably — the looming undead threat.

  • The sages will soon call a council to order that will determine who shall assume the role of the new Holy Speaker. Lilla is confident that she's first in line for the position, given her history with the Temple and her expert tutelage at the foot of Jon Vastil.

Sin Marmot is remorseful during the course of the exchange, and leaves most of the talking to the rest of the party members — chiming in only when necessary or appropriate.

Additional conversation points are detailed below, in Lilla Arien's own words.

Regarding Jon Vastil's Death:

"The Speaker was a good man. My favorite teacher, and — despite our differences in age and station —one of my best friends. I haven't known many people of Ember to be as wise and sincere as he. I imagine I will think of him every day for the rest of my life. He leaves some large shoes to fill. I hope whoever is chosen to walk in those shoes is ready and willing and able."

About the Necromancer, Amelia Naxan:

"I'm unfamiliar with this Amelia Naxan, although tall tales of the Moiran wastelands are told far and wide throughout the Plateau. Based on your description of her, I'd say she's a formidable adversary, if she's actually responsible for your encounter in the Burial Grounds. It's certainly a lead worth following."

About the Corpuleth:

"This hematophage you describe sounds like a most loathsome creature. Truly an accursed being. You've done the city of Ordain and the Heart of Ember a great service by slaying the bloodthirsty brute before it could do more harm."

About the Skallith:

"These skeletal creatures sound like the same restless dead you encountered at Corpin Sanctuary. I'm no expert in the ways of arcane magic, but I'd wager the same necromancy that brought those decrepit bones to life on Mial Mountain is also responsible for the horde you fought in the cemetery. We simply need to confirm who summoned them, and how."

Regarding Sionia's Hunch:

"I'm no shard god, but I'm inclined to believe what Sionia has to say, particularly when it comes to addressing such accomplished fate-spinners as yourselves. Perhaps her pilgrimage will lead to some revelations. But in the meantime, we'll have to fend for ourselves. This developing situation grows more desperate each day. We can't afford to wait for the Deadbinder to save us."

About the Undead Threat:

The Second Sage takes a moment to measure her thoughts as an unmistakable wave of concern washes over her.

"It seems your encounters in Westgate and Fallbrook weren't isolated incidents. These are dark times, my friends. The city is no stranger to calamity, but this escalation of undead activity is beyond the pale. First Corpin Sanctuary, now Ordain. What's next?"

You all share the weight of the moment as Lilla considers what to say.

"The days to come will present us with a new Speaker, and with that new leadership, I pray … a sense of direction. We can't stand idly by as these soulless monsters unravel the very fabric of the Arctus Plateau."

The Second Sage musters a tiny smile.

"Adonia wouldn't stand for it, now would she?"

Once the party (or Lilla) breeches the subject of what to do next, @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith} joins the group once again with a few final words of his own (for now).

A tall shadow cascades across the floor as the holy steward Vinarith joins your group once more. His countenance is earnest and staid, but full of assurance. He clears his throat and speaks with measured sincerity.

My friends, it pains me to say that the Second Sage is needed elsewhere. We have several matters throughout the temple that require her foremost attention.

Vinarith looks to Lilla with a nod of recognition, as if subtly endorsing her capabilities. He continues.

As we prepare to convene our council to discuss the Holy Speaker's succession, I invite you to stay in close touch throughout the days to come. You are never strangers here. Please remember that, and consider us fast friends. Now, if you'll excuse us.

The steward puts his hand on Lilla's shoulder and draws her close for a hushed consultation. The Second Sage waves you goodbye and offers you a smile of resignation. Sin Marmot gives her own farewell — a short salute, and a forced smile.

Sadness lingers here in Cindarin Temple. And outside, the city of Ordain awaits with all its distractions, frivolous and fateful alike.

Concluding the Event

Milestone Point

Completing this event (by attending the wake of Jon Vastil) awards a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially enabling the party to advance in level.

Next Steps

If they party has not yet visited Numinous Shrines in the wake of their encounter in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.KdqZ2BHPEi1Rh9tf]{Spirited Revelations} event awaits them the next time they travel to that hex.
Speaker Silenced.soverview: The party returns to Cindarin Temple expecting to share their dire findings with Lilla Arien and the others, only to find out that the circumstances within the Cindaric Order have changed in a most dramatic and significant way. The Holy Speaker Jon Vastil has died from natural causes, and the other Cindaric Sages must assemble an impromptu council post haste to determine who will succeed him. However, before this council of sages congregates, the characters have a brief moment to chat with the Second Sage about their encounter in the Burial Grounds — and what it means for the city of Ordain.
Speaker Silenced.sexposition:
As you make your way through the front halls of Cindarin Temple, there is a noticeable change in the atmosphere of this normally warm and welcoming place. A somber tone hangs thick in the air today, and there seems to be less activity than normal at a glance.

Entering the sanctuary, it becomes all too clear why the mood has changed so significantly. Upon the dais where Cindaric leadership is accustomed to giving their addresses to the adherents, a glass coffin bearing the cadaver of the Holy Speaker Jon Vastil sits surrounded by flowers, candles, and offerings.

The Holy Speaker is dead. And various people have gathered here for a wake.

Your ally Sin Marmot stands next to Lilla Arien nearby. She places a small hand on Lilla's back to offer the Second Sage some kind of comfort in this trying time. There aren't many dry eyes in the sanctuary today, and Lilla is no exception. Just as they meet your gaze, a hand falls upon your shoulder, followed by the solemn voice of Vinarith, Steward of the Holy Speaker.

As you can see, Jon Vastil — our beloved Holy Speaker — is no longer with us. Time has taken its inevitable toll, and the Speaker has a new journey ahead. We who remain are honored to carry his legacy, and will do so until the end of our own days.

Vinarith regards the other sages in your circle with a simple nod of understanding.

A private ceremony for the Speaker will commence on the morrow. In the meantime, please commiserate with us as your faiths allow. I'm sure Jon would have admired the company. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have quite a few anxious sages to speak with today …

As the Holy Steward steps away, a small chorus of Cindarics gather near the dais. They begin singing a sad song, an Ordani dirge handed down for centuries, since the time of Adonia. A tune that fills your heart with freedom and longing and the cloying regret of "goodbye."
Speaker Silenced.ssummary: We returned to Cindarin Temple to deliver news of our exploits in the Burial Grounds to Lilla Arien. To our surprise, we arrived to find out that the Holy Speaker Jon Vastil has died of natural causes. We shared our revelations about the undead uprising with the Second Sage amidst this solemnity before leaving the Cindarics to mourn the loss of their beloved leader. According to the Lilla, a senior council of sages will soon assemble for a private succession meeting. It seems we'll have to simply wait and see to find out what's in store for the Cindaric Sages and their benevolent order.

A Conflagration of Lumé.name: A Conflagration of Lumé
A Conflagration of Lumé.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event allows the party to gain insight about the looming undead threat from the champion of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.w5XsGfNsSEJnr1yd]{Lumé} known as @UUID[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]{Luna Karrowrath}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Explore the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.jBVzQi6wRjMew0Es]{Performer's Plaza} district of Ordain, where they'll meet Luna Karrowrath and her cadre of @UUID[Actor.8ICWlEOQZFXd1rJP]{Flameguard Crusaders} at a bonfire gathering.

  • Compete with the Flameguard Crusaders in a test of skill with ranged weaponry.

  • Learn a brief account of the history of undead in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.UXitezaq69A5JVmd]{Aterica} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WA0f1FgKpas0Ycc4]{Arctus Plateau}.

  • Participate in the communal bonfire ceremony, which intends to bless the Flameguard before they set off on a crusade to the shadow-haunted @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.iQhYX8QCmDyBnhHP]{Barrows}.

  • Speak with and spot other denizens of the Arctus Plateau who happen to be attending the event, like the mysterious Sanguinary @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}.

The Lumek Bonfire

If the party wishes to discuss the intricacies of undeath with Luna Karrowrath and her Flameguard allies, they must locate the so-called champion of Lumé among her people, a courteous but protective group of foreigners from the Lumek lands west of the Arctus Plateau. Known for their shared lifelong mission to eradicate the scourge of undeath wherever they find it, these warriors may have insight for the party — if the characters can ingratiate themselves with the outsiders first.

The Lumek bonfire at Performer's Plaza is a gigantic pyre of open flame, and is attended by 24 @UUID[Actor.8ICWlEOQZFXd1rJP]{Flameguard Crusaders} and their leader @UUID[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]{Luna Karrowrath}, along with a half-dozen Ordani citizens who appear to be allies and confidants of the foreign group.

The characters must gain the favor of one of the Flameguard warriors, who will subsequently introduce them directly to Luna.

@embed[Actor.8ICWlEOQZFXd1rJP count=24]

Surveying the Scene

If they desire more information, the party can examine the bonfire from afar before they approach. The following skill checks can provide some additional details.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 12]] check is somewhat familiar with the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.f52WC5ZzNSK0yKOz]{Lumek} culture, and had heard of the righteous @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.flameguardMiliti]{Flameguard} and their holy mission to fight the undead. The character is knowledgeable of the Lumek's war against the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.s9Mpdp3AdicS1W24]{Moiran} @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.ZMHd8i0tOkhfOiKK]{Blood Barons} north of the Firelands.

  • Result of 17+: The character is familiar with Luna Karrowrath as a person of import in Lumek society, and has heard about some of the champion of Lumé's exploits.

  • [[/ancestry Lumek]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] have advantage on this check.

  • [[/path FlameguardMilitia]] characters automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 11]] check is well-versed in the origin story of the shard goddess Lumé and her holy mission against the undead.

  • Result of 16+: The character recognizes this celebration as one of the famed Lumek bonfire ceremonies, which they may have heard about or seen before. These bonfires are known to honor the shard goddess Lumé and her holy quest to vanquish the evil of undeath.

  • [[/ancestry Lumek]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] or [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on this check.

  • [[/path FlameguardMilitia]] characters automatically succeed on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 12]] can sense that while the Lumek warriors celebrating here tonight are a cautious lot, their attention is mostly focused on the celebration itself and the various actions that support it. They appear mostly at ease, absorbed in the moment, and supremely confident.

  • Result of 17+: The carefree nature of this moment feels hard-won from such a hardy group of slayers as these Lumek warriors gathered today. There is a distinct focus to the revelry.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]] and [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 18]] check is able to spot one warrior that stands out from the rest on the opposite side of the bonfire, nearly hidden by the throng of revelers. This battle-scarred warrior exudes an aura of experience, and still wears some of her plate armor — a steel alloy covered in esoteric symbols. This is Luna Kerrowrath, absorbed in conversation with a few of her closest Flameguard allies. The moment seems unapproachable without some dramatic interruption.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]] have advantage on this check.

Once the party decides to approach the Lumek for conversation, read the following aloud:

As you draw closer to the bonfire, a few of the Lumek revelers look up to see who might have the audacity to join their group. And then another. And another. And suddenly you feel the weight of dozens of scrutinizing eyes upon you. But the music and the dancing doesn't stop. And the party rages on.

One of the Fej warriors stands to greet you as you pass, a mug of ale held firmly in his meaty right hand. There is an unmistakable air of sass in the bald fellow's voice.

You lost, friends?

Another Lumek warrior stands to join him, a Vrjnhar woman with exquisite tattoos of fire on her face.

Maybe they've finally found their way. These folks look like good company to me, Iskar.

She addresses you directly with a grin on her otherwise intimidating face.

And you don't want to make me a liar, now do you?

Meeting the Flameguard

If the party wants to meet with Luna Karrowrath, they'll need to first ingratiate themselves with the other Flameguard Crusaders who've assembled here for the bonfire.

The two Crusaders who stand to greet the party are Iskar (CN, Lumek Fej, he/him) and Thala (CG, Lumek Vrnjhar, she/her), and they are willing to exchange a few pleasantries with the characters if the party is suitably reverent to the moment. Thala and Iskar are most willing to discuss the following:

  • The nature of the bonfire as a ceremony in service to the shard goddess Lumé, the Flame Warden, which they celebrate so that it might bless them on a crusade ahead.

  • The ongoing war between the Lumek Flameguard and the Moiran forces of undead.

  • Current affairs in Ordain and the Arctus Plateau.

An Audience with Luna Karrowrath

If the party asks for an audience with Luna Karrowrath, they'll have to convince Thala and Iskar (or another Firebrand) that they won't be wasting the champion of Lumé's time.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 15]], [[/skill intimidation 20]], or [[/skill persuasion 13]] check is able to convince Thala or Iskar to introduce them to Luna.

  • [[/path FlameguardMilitia]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge undeath]], [[/knowledge rituals]], or [[/attunement Ragen]] have advantage on this check.

  • Characters who adequately describe their encounter with Luna during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.eZB70NxqEPY68Jbw]{The Blockaded Bridge} also have advantage on this check.

  • Clerics or paladins who use a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagHolySymbolV]{Holy Symbol} of Lumé as their divine spellcasting focus also have advantage on this check.

Alternately, any character who targets Thala or Iskar with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCharmPerso]{Charm Person} spell automatically succeeds on these checks.

Additionally, any character who relates a rousing story about a previous encounter with an undead creature automatically succeeds on these checks. Appropriate encounters include:

  • The Skallith horde from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.JN1mTKPlSA0WKizP]{Sanctuary of Death} event at Corpin Sanctuary

  • The Vampyre Spawn encounter during @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy}

  • The Sodden Corpses of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.2expJELjYHucAyKl]{Harrowed Crossing} event

  • The encounter with Tethra Shùl and her Horrendors in @UUID[JournalEntry.pod4PApXHuZgXwHo]{A Brush with Death}

  • Any other appropriate encounters.

After the characters have successfully convinced the Flameguard Crusaders that their motives are valid, they're granted an audience with Luna Kerrowrath, the Flame Warden's venerated champion.

As the party approaches Luna Kerrowrath at the opposite side of the bonfire, read the following aloud:

The gregarious crusader grabs you by the shoulder and steers you through the crowd of her merry-making cohorts, who regard you with a mixed array of amusement and incredulity. Within a moment, you stand before a makeshift dais, upon which is seated an impressive Fej paladin clad in rune-covered armor.

Thala leans in to speak something into the armored woman's ear. The battle-scarred Fej takes a sip of her ale, smiles a curious smile, and beckons your group to join her. As soon as you're close enough, she addresses you directly with a voice as smoky as the night sky above the plaza bonfire.

Thala tells me you wish to discuss the scourge of the Evernight? Well, that is certainly a story with which I am most familiar …

The Lumek warriors around you scoff and chuckle with grim jocularity.

But tell me: what do you adventurers have to offer the Flameguard? This is a sacred night, and we must be selective of the company we keep. Assurances don't come quickly in my line of work. I need more than idle tales of boogeymen on your road to the big city.

The armored captain stands and finishes her last sip of ale. She reaches down to a pile of javelins nearby, and holds one aloft. With a flash in Luna's eye, the tip of the missile becomes wreathed in a nimbus of flame.

I'd like to see you prove your worth before I seat you at my table. Choose your champion. A test of mettle is in order tonight. The Flame Warden is watching. Are you ready?

@embed[Actor.GcHER06gTFCwQzOr]

If the party members want to continue their tête-à-tête with Luna, they'll need to participate in her impromptu contest of fortitude and ranged skill. However, for better or worse, only one of the player characters will compete in this Lumek challenge.

A Test of Skill

As part of the ceremony, the Lumek warriors partake in tests of skill and strength, inviting the party to challenge themselves by joining the trials. This event presents a way to learn about - and hopefully establish a rapport with - the Lumek Firebrands who will return as allies in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr3].

With her flaming javelin in one hand, Luna grabs a curious stuffed sack and leads you to an area at the perimeter of this section of the plaza. She reaches into the sack and produces a misshapen skull, humanoid but vaguely deformed with fangs.

We encountered these foul wretches north of Nain along the river. Undead shamblers, hungry for flesh. Now, they're kindling for the Flame Warden's fire.

Luna tosses the skull to Iskar, who's taken place closer to the bonfire. The bald warrior tosses the undead skull, and — in the blink of an eye — Luna hurls the flaming javelin with lightning-fast precision. The missile skewers the skull and sends it hurtling into the bonfire, where it crackles and sparks like dry moss. Luna turns to you and holds out another flaming javelin.

I'd like to see you prove your worth before I seat you at my table. Now, choose your own champion. A test of mettle is in order tonight. The Flame Warden is watching.

Skulls for the Flame Warden

The party must appoint one character to accept Luna's challenge to hit a skull with a ranged javelin attack and send it flying into the bonfire, all while the heat from the burning javelin threaten to burn the character's arm.

The character who takes up the javelin — known as the party's champion — must succeed on a [[/save con 15]] or else take [[/roll 1d4 fire]] damage each turn they hold the javelin.

The target skull has an AC of 15, and has 1 hp.

The party's champion has 3 chances to hit the skull. If the party's champion fails to hit the skull, Luna Karrowrath will humor the party with a brief conversation, but the characters will fail to win the favor of the Flameguard this day.

If the party wins the skull shooting challenge, Luna congratulates the party and invites them to participate in the ceremony. Read the following aloud:

The skull pops and crackles like a kindling in the bonfire, and the crowd of Lumek warriors cheer in unison to celebrate your steady aim. Luna strides forward and touches her forehead to yours, muttering a prayer to her goddess:

By the Hearthslayer's hand. The Flameguard could use an aim like that against the legions of the Everdark. Welcome to the party, friends. Please, eat, drink, and be merry! Lumé commands it!

Before you know it, Lumek revelers are jamming food and drink into your hands, and the ceremony swirls around you like a beautiful storm of song and dance and firelight.

Event Outcome: Lumé's Blessing

If the party's champion succeeds during the Flameguard contest of skill and mettle, the characters gain a temporary boon from the shard goddess Lumé. Mark the "Lumé's Blessing" Event Outcome above.

Akon Attunement: Lumé's Blessing

The party's champion succeeds during the Flameguard contest of skill and mettle, they advance their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 cindaric2BonfireBlessing]] at the conclusion of the event.

If the party fails to win the skull shooting challenge, Luna admonishes the party's lack of skill and champion spirit, but she invites the party to watch the ceremony and share in the bounty of food and drink that is being enjoyed this evening. Read the following aloud:

A few muffled jeers make their way through the crowd as Luna strides forward and puts a hand on your shoulder.

It seems the Hearthslayer's hand does not guide you this evening, friends. Perhaps you don't have what it takes to run with the Flameguard. But fear not, you're still welcome at my table. Please, make yourselves comfortable and enjoy the simple rewards this night has to offer.

Before you know it, Lumek revelers are putting food and drink into your hands, and the ceremony swirls around you like a beautiful storm of song and dance and firelight.

The Ceremony Begins

With Luna's contest of skill and mettle out of the way, the party can enjoy the bonfire ceremony and the amenities it has to offer. During the celebration, they'll be able to continue their conversation with Luna about the rising undead threat.

A Conversation with Luna Karrowrath

Once the festivities begin, Luna Karrowrath is more than willing to share additional information about the Flameguard and their mission against the undead scourge of the Moiran Blood Barons. Some conversation points include:

  • A brief history of her triumphs and tribulations as a champion of the shard goddess Lumé.

  • An account of her company's journey to Ordain, and the trials they've faced along the way.

  • An explanation of the bonfire ceremony, which is intended to grant favor to their impending journey to the Arcturian Barrows, where they are avowed to confront the rising undead menace in the region.

Whether the party's champion managed to succeed at the contest of skill and mettle or not, Luna invites the characters to take up arms with the Flameguard and pledge their assistance to the company of Firebrand warriors on their mission to the Barrows.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] is able to confirm the authenticity of Luna's narrative, and finds the champion of Lumé to be a remarkably honest person in general.

Event Outcome: Pledged Assistance

If the characters choose to pledge their assistance to Luna and the Flameguard in the days to come by offering to aid them on their quest to the Barrows, mark the "Pledged Assistance" Event Outcome above. The party's loyalty to the Flameguard's cause will reward them with help and opportunities of their own from time to time.

Ragen Attunement: Pledged Assistance

If the party pledges their assistance to Luna and the Flameguard, each character advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 cindaric2BonfirePledged]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aura Attunement: Withheld Assistance

If the party refuses to assist Luna and the Flameguard, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 cindaric2BonfireWithheld]] at the conclusion of the event.

On the Peripheral

Throughout the course of the Flameguard ceremony, the party will have a few opportunities to notice moments and persons of interest among the crowd.

Characters with a [[/skill passive perception 13]] or who succeed on a [[/skill perception 15]] check are able to notice a familiar face among the crowd: @UUID[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]{Avwynn Taol}, whom they most likely met at Corpin Sanctuary during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr1.JournalEntryPage.FvDSH3rhzyh3So2K]{Corpin Arrival}.

However, as soon as one or more of the characters notice Avwynn at the edge of the plaza, in the blink of an eye she's gone. A quick investigation or pursuit yields no results; wherever she went, she's well beyond the party's reach at this time.

@embed[Actor.cDvmtfES2GwAl0vH]

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

There is no downstream event following this one. If they have yet to do so, the party is free to learn more about the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} of Ember by visiting the Temple of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.XUn8UELVkQmnCI78]{Temple Ward} district of Ordain for the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.ydYEFz46NhoJZqHs]{Bickering Priests}.
A Conflagration of Lumé.soverview: Per a suggestion from Lilla Arien, the party travels to the Performer's Plaza district of Ordain to meet with the Lumek warrior Luna Karrowrath. This storied champion of the shard goddess Lumé may have some insight for the characters about the undead creatures they encountered in Westgate, Fallbrook, and elsewhere. But in order to win Luna's favor, the characters must compete against her Lumek Flameguard in a test of skills and participate in a bonfire ceremony honoring the Flame Warden, Lumé.
A Conflagration of Lumé.sexposition:
The flickering shadows of firelight and the rhythmic sound of a dozen drums guide you to an interesting corner of the plaza, where a group of spirited warriors have gathered in evening celebration around a massive bonfire. Clad in loosely-fitting garments of black and red, these erstwhile combatants have laid down their arms and taken up accoutrements of revelry instead. Some pound the drums, while others dance around the fire with inspired abandon.

Judging by their ashen skin and dangerously close proximity to the bonfire, many of these revelers appear to be Fej, but representatives of nearly every ancestry can be seen among them — clad in similar garb, sporting flame iconography. A large feast is in the works; smaller fire pits roast savory game, while a head cook mans a large cauldron full of some immaculately spicy stew or casserole. Certainly, these must be the Lumek Flameguard warriors you seek at Lilla Arien's behest.

But the scene isn't precisely an inviting one; outsiders seem few and far between among this convocation of bacchanalian foreigners, who eye your uninvited party with suspicion.
A Conflagration of Lumé.ssummary: We ventured to Performer's Plaza in an effort to meet with Luna Karrowrath, the champion of Lumé, who had few words of wisdom for us regarding the looming undead threat. After a friendly competition of skill and ranged accuracy, we participated in a bonfire ceremony to honor the Lumek goddess. This ritual is purported to bless the Lumek Flameguard on a grand crusade that soon awaits them — a march into the dismal Barrows along the plateau's northern coast, where undead servants of evil are said to brood and plot their evil revolt.

Spirited Revelations.name: Spirited Revelations
Spirited Revelations.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration event occurs in the wake of the party's fight in the Burial Grounds, and allows them to present their findings to @UUID[Actor.jzrNvlGQHpoSkkIU]{Sionia} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.aLXuhuWQdislrPnJ]{Numinous Shrines} district. In this event, the characters can:

  • Speak with Sionia about the encounter at the Burial Grounds during @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments}.

  • Help Sionia analyze the undead remains they collected from the Cindaric cremetorium.

  • Earn a potential reward for their clandestine placement of Sionia's five @UUID[Item.G4v6oL4DTZ3ZPBZ5]{Ken Crystals}.

Post Mortem

The party returns to @UUID[Actor.jzrNvlGQHpoSkkIU]{Sionia} at the Numinous Shrines district following their deadly encounter in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments}. At the Mall of The Nineteen, the characters will present undead remains to the shard goddess for scrutiny, along with their first-hand account of the harrowing battle and their unholy assailants.

After the characters have presented Sionia with the evidence, read the following aloud:

Sionia helps you lay the undead remains down upon the hard flagstone floor of the mall, and kneels to situate herself slightly above them. As the shard goddess begins waving her hands in arcane gesticulation, an ectoplasmic mist of strange occult energy starts seeping out of the remains and into her fingertips. Her eyes glow bright with arcane power as she throws her head back with ecstatic dread.

The Deathbinder speaks, but the ethereal voice you hear is one of multitudes.

The shade of the Everdark grows long. But our threat is strangely close at hand. These remains are riddled with a dark necromancy, more loathsome than any magic I've yet seen. Beyond Varun malediction … beyond the ghosts of Sunfire sorcery … our threat is furtive and unknown. A darkness beyond our sight.

Sionia's Examination

Using esoteric magic, the shard goddess conducts a brief investigation of the undead remains.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check is able to assist Sionia with her efforts during the investigation, and gains advantage on their next [[/knowledge undeath]] check.

The Shard God's Analysis

Sionia is able to share various pieces of information with the players during her examination of the undead remains. Such details include (but are not limited to):

  • What precisely happened during the party's encounter at the Burial Grounds (if they've yet to tell her).

  • The nature of the various undead remains that may have been retrieved:

    • @UUID[Actor.j3B9TkGTc23Q6Ina]{Vampyre Spawn} remains.

    • @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb]{Harrower} remains.

    • @UUID[Actor.IWpoD9AvSVfLFdad]{Corpuleth} remains.

    • @UUID[Actor.l7LyzJ2PD2C4o6MV]{Skallith} remains.

  • Sionia's emerging theory about what might be going on: some force, element, or entity is causing a surge of necromantic energy in the Arctus Plateau and beyond.

  • Sionia speaks reluctantly of the Lumek Flameguard, and their quest to rid the Barrows of any undead threats they might find, but recognizes the serendipity of this alliance.

A successful [[/skill arcana 15]] check confirms the veracity of Sionia's arcane findings, as far as the character can tell.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] and [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] believes Sionia's account of her findings to be authentic (according to her knowledge, at least), and is able to sense an element of concern behind the shard goddess' all-knowing eyes.

  • Result of 16+: Sionia is hiding something beyond simple concern, but the specific details of that "something" remain elusive. She is calculating something, perhaps her next move.

Additionally, if the party learned the name of the necromancer @UUID[Actor.CDnkeyHq8Nb9Lzeb]{Amelia Naxan} and shares this information with Sionia, the shard goddess will relate some of her own personal history with the Blood Barons and her scorn for the Lumek.

About the Vampyre Spawn:

"This is unmistakably a creature of the Moiran wastelands. And based on your accounts of the various encounters between Westgate and the Burial Grounds, it seems the large hematophage you found feasting on the undead corpses was actually the cause of the poor fellow's original demise. This spawn was the offspring of the Corpuleth, as you call it."

About the Harrower:

"Whatever foul necromancy turned this Burnished Hand warrior into a withered revenant, it is a novel and curious magic — the likes of which we haven't seen. I regret that I know little else about the form and function of this … soot-handed harrower."

About the Corpuleth:

"Despite its overt similarities to the vampyres of the Moiran wastelands, this brutish hematophage is quite unlike any creature I've encountered or studied in my several centuries on Ember. It seems novel horrors such as this are part of whatever loathsome endgame is afoot."

About the Skallith:

"Skallith have been known to the Arctus Plateau for centuries, but their likes have not been seen since the time of The Shattering. Powerful necromancy is required to activate such a large cohort of undead soldiers in so quickly a time."

About the Mysterious Necromancer (Amelia Naxan):

"The Blood Barons are a scourge of the living planet, and their foul necromancy is characterized by the opposite of everything I represent — corruption, subjugation, and outright cosmic profanity. Amelia Naxan is among the worst of their ilk, and her acumen with the dark arts of necromancy is perhaps only rivaled by my own."

Once the party breeches the subject of what to do next, Sionia speaks.

A rustle of wind punctuates a brief moment of silence before the shard goddess speaks again.

Our tasks are clear. I must go abroad to learn more about the unseen powers at play. You must travel with the Flameguard into the shadow-haunted Arcturian Barrows, where their undying boogeymen await your scrutiny — and your blade. If this necromancer you speak of is nearby, those murky lowlands are as good a prospect as any …

Fare thee well, adventurers. And keep your heads about you.

With a smile and a wink, the shard goddess becomes one with the ghostly mists that perpetually surround her and coalesces into the form of a phantasmal raven that takes flight. Up and away she flies, into the starlit sky.

The Shard Goddess is fascinated, and muses what the implications of this finding might be for the long-term sustainability of the cycle of souls. Sionia tells the party they must travel to the Barrows, pursue this Necromancer, and learn more if they can about what is happening.

Eyes for the Deathbinder

If the party managed to successfully complete their secondary objective by secretly placing Sionia's @UUID[Item.G4v6oL4DTZ3ZPBZ5]{Ken Crystals} throughout the Burial Grounds, the shard goddess rewards them at this time.

The shard goddess casts a watchful gaze about your group.
