I can see you no longer carry the ken crystals. I presume your attempt to place them throughout the cemetery and the Cindaric crematorium were successful?

About the Ken Crystals:

"The ken crystals are simple but effective tools for divination. From their watchful vantage points, I'll be able to keep an eye out for errant necromancy in the cemetery. The city can't afford another incident like the one you described."

Event Outcome: Sionia's Reward

Characters who successfully install Sionia's 5 Ken Crystals in the Burial Grounds receive their own @UUID[Item.G4v6oL4DTZ3ZPBZ5]{Ken Crystal} as a reward, as well as the future favor of the Lonely Goddess. Mark the "Sionia's Reward" Event Outcome at the top of the page.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

If they party has not yet visited @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.GlbJezRw2ecnVIsx]{Cindarin Temple} in the wake of their encounter in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.d2HewHlB5nO1S5hQ]{Speaker Silenced} event awaits them the next time they travel to that hex.
Spirited Revelations.soverview: The party returns to the Numinous Shrines district to share their Burial Grounds evidence with Sionia, who conducts a brief examination of the undead remains using her arcane powers. With scant revelations at hand, the Shard Goddess of Necromancy decides to set off for regions unknown to further her esoteric investigations.
Spirited Revelations.sexposition:
You return to the lonely alcove in the Mall of The Nineteen, where the empty shrine of Sionia is currently attended by the shard goddess herself, kneeled in silent thought or meditation among the weather-worn residual offerings. She speaks as you approach:

Welcome back, adventurers. And not a moment too soon. Tell me of your journey to the Burial Grounds. What have you brought for me?
Spirited Revelations.ssummary: We returned to Sionia at the Numinous Shrines with the undead remains we collected at the Burial Grounds. Following a brief investigation, the shard goddess was taken aback with our findings, and has now set off on her own to investigate these matters further. We must share what we have learned with Lilla Arien and the other Cindarics.

Lost in the Stacks.name: Lost in the Stacks
Lost in the Stacks.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration event presents the party with a series of skill challenges in the Old City Library of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.iphMPgtJv5eQjGaR]{Scholar's Nook}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Make their way past the Old City Library front desk and into the lower stacks of the basement level.

  • Locate their ally @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}, who has been trapped in a sticky cocoon of parchment moth silk, and free the young druid from her tenacious situation.

  • Receive a magical summons from the Second Sage @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien}, who has a new assignment for Sin (alongside an invitation for the party's help).

Early Access Work in Progress

This event is intended to use an Ordain Interior vista configured for Scholar's Nook, which is unavailable at this time. The interior scene must be imagined for now.

The Front Desk

The front desk of Old City Library is supervised by a single @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherent} at all times. An obsequious adherent named Magda Mosswell (LN, Ordani Hulg'run, she/her) is the desk clerk on duty when the characters arrive for this encounter.

The party has two main methods of passage past the front desk and into the lower stacks, where Sin Marmot awaits their timely (and covert) assistance: socializing with Magda for permission, or sneaking by undetected. If the characters choose to approach the front desk directly, read the following aloud:

As you step towards the front desk, you find yourself meeting the judicious gaze of the Cindaric clerk on duty here. This stoney young woman casts a discerning glance at you above the lenses of her reading glasses, her head tilted down at her work.

Can I help you with something?

Navigating the Front Desk

Due to so-called "renovations" in the basement and sub-basement areas of the library, the lower stacks are currently off-limits to visitors. Magda will protest the party's ingress unless they have the means to convince her.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 15]] or [[/skill persuasion 15]] check is able to gain permission from Magda to search the lower stacks despite of the renovations in progress.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters and [[/path ObsidianResearcher]] characters have advantage on these checks.

  • A character wearing the robes of a Cindaric Sage or Cindaric Adherent also has advantage on these checks. A character can substitute a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulDisguiseKi]{Disguise Kit} as a convincing facsimile.

Characters who fail this check must succeed on an additional [[/skill deception 13]] check to avoid triggering the suspicions of the desk clerk, which could raise unwanted awareness of Sin Marmot's predicament.

  • If the characters fail this Deception check more than 3 times, they may still proceed to the lower stacks to rescue Sin, but Lilla Arien and the other Cindaric Sages will be informed of the initiate's failure here at Old City Library. Check the "Library Demerit" Event Outcome above.

Alternately, the party can attempt to bribe their way past Magda. Any character who offers the obsequious front desk clerk a tawdry romance @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Book} to satisfy her appetite for salacious fiction will be granted entry.

  • An item such as this can be found in one of the many book shops scattered throughout Scholar's Nook.

Sneaking By

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill stealth 16]] check is able to sneak past the front desk clerk without being detected or arousing suspicion.

  • An allied character can use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.5S8i59qskkd9GGcJ]{Help} action to cause a distraction elsewhere in the library, including (but not limited to) a prolonged conversation with Magda.

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.MQIZ1zRLWRcNOtPN]{Invisible} creatures have advantage on this check, but must still make an effort to sneak due to the relative silence here.

If the characters fail this check or choose to simply storm their way past the front desk, they may still proceed to the lower stacks to rescue Sin, but Lilla Arien and the other Cindaric Sages will be informed of the initiate's failure here at Old City Library. Check the "Library Demerit" Event Outcome above.

Primordis Attunement: Sneaking Past Magda

Each character who manages to successfully sneak past Magda at the front desk advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 cindaric2StacksSneak]] at the conclusion of the event.

Luxarum Attunement: Bribe Magda

Any character who manages to successfully bribe Magda with an appropriate Book advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 cindaric2StacksBribe]] at the conclusion of the event.

Into the Lower Stacks

Once the party has successfully navigated the front desk, they can proceed into the lower stacks located in the library's basement level. Here, @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} has been trapped inside a cocoon by a colony of oversized parchment moths, who have invaded the stacks for their seasonal nesting.

The party must locate Sin among the various cocoons scattered throughout the lower stacks and release her from her silky imprisonment — hopefully without raising a fuss and alerting the other Cindarics upstairs.

You furtively make your way into the lower stacks of the Old City Library, descending quietly down a worn wooden stairway into the building's basement level. A musky, earthen scent hangs in the air, and you can't help but notice the familiar flittering of a tatterwing moth as it floats down past you from behind.

The further you go, the more the origin of the musky odor becomes apparent … the nooks and crannies of the lower stacks are covered in a messy blanket of mulberry silk and keg-sized cocoons. You quickly spy a half-dozen giant moths crawling about this cluttered space and hanging from the ceiling, no doubt the furry engineers of this silk-spun calamity. Meanwhile, countless smaller moths flutter about the room without a care in the world.

Sin Marmot is hidden somewhere in that tangled mass, and it's high time to find and free her — without causing a ruckus.

The medium-sized Parchment Moths are oversized cousins to the tatterwing moths the characters are accustomed to, and pose no physical threat to the party or their allies.

Exploring the Lower Stacks

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] check or [[/skill investigation 15]] check while searching the room is able to locate one cocoon that stands out from the rest — a Sin Marmot-shaped husk that contains the party's missing ally.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] have advantage on this check.

Alternately, magic can help the party locate Sin Marmot among the silky morass.

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell can be used to locate @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv.Item.36Uxa6kffGZaxxoj]{Sin's Pyrefly Staff}, which radiates a mixed aura of illusion and abjuration magic.

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectThou]{Detect Thoughts} spell can help pinpoint Sin's location, but will not locate her outright, and provides advantage on Perception and Investigation checks used to find her.

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLocateAnim]{Locate Animals or Plants} spell or the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLocateObje]{Locate Object} spell can be used to find specific items such as Sin's equipment or plant-based spell components the character might be familiar with.

  • Additionally, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithA]{Speak with Animals} spell will allow a character to communicate directly with the parchment moths themselves, who will reveal Sin's location following a successful [[/skill persuasion 13]] check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 14]] check is familiar with the ecology of parchment moths and their closest kin, and know the medium-sized beasts to be docile and friendly creatures — despite their taste for aged parchment and book bindings.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] have advantage on this check.

Helping Sin Escape

Once the party locates Sin among the crowded silken expanse, they must free the young initiate from the cocoon that envelopes her.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill strength 15]] check is able to pry open the cocoon wide enough for Sin to escape.

  • A character who fails this check must succeed on a [[/skill stealth 15]] check to avoid alerting the Cindarics upstairs with a loud commotion — such as a fallen bookshelf, a fumbled piece of equipment, or the sudden fluttering of parchment moths. They may still rescue Sin from the lower stacks, but Lilla Arien and the other Cindaric Sages will be informed of the initiate's failure here at Old City Library. Check the "Library Demerit" Event Outcome above.

  • If an allied character uses the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.5S8i59qskkd9GGcJ]{Help} action to assist with this skill check, both characters must succeed on the above Stealth check to avoid detection.

When Sin Marmot is finally free of restraint in the parchment moth cocoon, read the following aloud:

Before you've even finished, your Keth companion is crawling her way out of the cocoon with a massive grin on her face.

You came! My sincerest thanks are yours forever. I started thinking I might never see the light of Lantyr again! I'm too young to die in a moth's cocoon. What would my gran say?

Sin emerges from her confinement and surveys the silky, moth-covered mess that blankets the lower stacks with a sigh of resignation.

Guess I still have a bit of cleaning to do!

A Message from Lilla Arien

Once Sin has been freed from her silken imprisonment in the moth cocoon, the characters can eventually make their way back upstairs and exit the Old City Library with little to no conflict or obstacle. However, there's one more encounter in store for them before the day is due: a message arrives from Lilla Arien on the wings of a lone Pyrefly, featuring a timely new assignment for Sin in another part of town.

The process of cleaning the silk from your garments is a sticky and cumbersome one, but — with a little due diligence — you and Sin eventually find yourselves entirely free of the viscid stuff.

Just then, another winged creature floats in on the wind to join your group. As a lone pyrefly curiously makes its way into the fold, Sin instinctively holds out her palm, where the luminous insect lands with the softest touch. The voice of Lilla Arien emanates from the pyrefly, who is apparently serves as some kind of magical envoy for the Second Sage.

Initiate Marmot, I hate to pull you away from your duties at Old City Library, but a situation is developing that could use your timely attention. One of our fellow Cindarics has died under mysterious circumstances, and I'd like your help with an official autopsy of the poor fellow's cadaver. Your druidic magic and investigative acumen have been valuable assets for the order, and I think this is a great opportunity to prove yourself to the sages. But you must make haste and maintain secrecy. We don't need to spread panic among the other initiates, and this is a delicate matter, best solved by a small team of specialists like yourselves.

Meet with Menedaeus at the rear door of Traveler's Rest in Westgate, tonight at the stroke of midnight. Menedaeus has been a trustworthy and capable aide to me for years, and will tell you everything you need to know. Good luck, Sin. And may the moons guide you.

With that, the tiny pyrefly takes flight and drifts off and away on the breeze.

A Timely Assignment

Sin is eager to wrap up any loose ends here at Old City Library before heading out to prepare for the clandestine autopsy at Traveler's Rest later this evening. She'll say goodbye to the characters for now, while making plans to join them later. Other topics of conversation might include:

  • Sin's reaction to getting snared and restrained in the parchment moth cocoon.

  • Everyone's suspicions about the forthcoming midnight encounter in Westgate.

  • The best way to leave Old City Library without causing a fuss.

Concluding the Event

Event Outcomes

If the party managed to help Sin Marmot escape her sticky situation in the lower stacks without alerting Magda at the front desk or the other Cindarics here, check the "Library Accolade" Event Outcome at the top of the page.

If the party alerted one or more of the Cindarics at Old City Library during the attempt to save Sin, check the "Library Demerit" Event Outcome instead.

Next Steps

The party must venture to the Traveler's Rest healing house in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.nS7kj8wZ5eFq6pcy]{Westgate} before the strike of midnight. There, during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy}, Sin Marmot will help them gain backdoor entry so they might investigate the curious corpse of a deceased Cindaric.
Lost in the Stacks.soverview: The party visits Sin Marmot amidst the stacks of the Old City Library in Scholar's Nook, where the young Cindaric initiate has become trapped by the very colony of moths she was assigned to safely remove. The characters must clandestinely make their way into the lower stacks of the library, locate Sin, and free her from a bothersome predicament — without alerting any of the other Cindarics to their chicanery.
Lost in the Stacks.sexposition:
The musty smell of parchment assaults your senses as you step through the massive wooden doors of the Old City Library, an exalted athenaeum run by the Cindaric Sages, where countless historical texts are stacked high and low among the facility's seemingly endless shelves.

A few Cindaric adherents study their tomes and scrolls in abject silence throughout the library's sprawling chambers, but these studious sages pay you no heed as you spy the front desk clerk — an attentive young Hulg'run scholar with multiple ledgers and one tawdry novel laid out on the work surface before her.
Lost in the Stacks.ssummary: We visited Sin Marmot at the Old City Library in Scholar's Nook, where she'd become trapped by an overgrown colony of arcane parchment moths. After making our way to the lower stacks, we managed to free Sin from her amusingly troublesome situation. On the heels of this endeavor, we received a somewhat urgent message from the Second Sage Lilla Arien, who requests our presence for a clandestine autopsy at Traveler's Rest in Westgate.

The Derelict Protector.name: The Derelict Protector
The Derelict Protector.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event pits the party against a new undead adversary within the confines of a small Ordani town house. In this event, the characters can:

  • Investigate the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.giaDQErIafhgueop]{Fallbrook} apartment for signs of the derelict protector derelict Burnished Hand Protector named Ordan.

  • Survive a quick and brutal combat scenario with Ordan, who has become a loathsome undead creature known as a @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb]{Harrower} following his apparent death.

  • Choose whether or not to reveal the truth of what happened here to the Burnished Hand (including the protector named Vance) and/or the Cindaric Sages.

This event will occur on the @UUID[Scene.emberOrdainFlats]{Ordain Flats} biome area map, using the "Apartment Block" composition.

Early Access Work in Progress

This event uses an Ordain Flats biome area map for the Derelict Protector's townhome apartment. This particular composition of the Ordain Flats area map does not (yet) have any Walls defined for its buildings. This is a known limitation that will be resolved as we switch our biome-specific area maps to use Scene Levels in Foundry VTT version 14.

Outside the Apartment

Examining the Apartment Exterior

Characters with a [[/check prc 16 passive format=long]] or characters who search outside the apartment and succeed on a [[/skill perception 13]] check are able to notice the following:

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] and [[/knowledge crime]] have advantage on this check.

  • There is no sign of foul play outside.

  • Footprints of the same booted foot can be found around the front threshold, leading to and from the door.

  • The subtle yet distinct odor of carrion rot lingers on the air.

  • Result of 16+: The character can spot @UUID[Item.VG4JppXHfTFrMwHj]{Ordan's Key} hidden above the top jamb of the door's stonework, and can hear the faint sound of flies buzzing.

A successful [[/skill survival 13]] check is able to date the most recent booted footprints leading to the front door as roughly four days old. Any other footprints are impossible to place based on their age, worn from time and weather as they are.

Any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectEvil]{Detect Evil and Good} spell while searching the apartment's exterior is able to sense the location of the @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb]{Harrower} inside, who is seated in the dark towards the rear. It's particularly easy for the character to sense Ordan this way while looking through the glass windows and the front door.

Locked Door

The front door to Ordan's apartment is locked. A successful [[/check dex 18]] check using Thieves' Tools is required to pick the lock, which can also be unlocked via @UUID[Item.VG4JppXHfTFrMwHj]{Ordan's Key} (found above the door jamb).

Inside the Apartment

Once the party gains access to the apartment interior, they have a brief moment to survey the scene before their encounter with Ordan the @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb]{Harrower} begins.

The first thing you notice as you step into the darkened apartment is the fetid smell of rotten flesh, followed by the sound of a soft, staccato buzzing. Your eyes drift to a limp form on the floor — the withered cadaver of a large dog, desiccated and swarming with house flies. The scene here is a gruesome one, marked by motionless heat.

Before you have a chance to search the apartment any further, a brittle voice croaks out from the back of the room, where an armored figure is seated in the dark. The table before them is decorated with rotten, abandoned food.

I don't recall summoning any visitors to my home this evening … but you'll suffer all the same.

The armored figure you presume to be Ordan stands to reveal his countenance. No longer human, the derelict protector has become something apparently new and entirely accursed. The abrupt sound of a longsword leaving its sheath is the last thing you hear before battle erupts in the confined apartment.

@embed[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb]

Harrower Tactics

The Harrower will most likely lead with a @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb.Item.hV3Vsy935wi8AOsK]{Multiattack} salvo of ranged @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb.Item.SBC9LE11MPeBvxE7]{Oblivion Beam} or melee @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb.Item.PKMiiEMs0C1hTvl9]{Thanatic Blade} attacks.

If and when adversaries close in for melee, the Harrower will target the strongest among them with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplBestowCurs]{Bestow Curse} spell, followed by a @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb.Item.4DVP9Pg8NqMVJcAb]{Withering Touch} attack.

As far as other @UUID[Actor.iL5MWjykxIcApZAb.Item.nAcXB3eIabfT7RK1]{Spellcasting} is concerned, bold or haughty characters will quickly become the targets of the irksome Harrower's @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCommand000]{Command} spell, and enemies who attempt to bolster their abilities with their own magic will become the swift targets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic}.

The Harrower fights gruesomely to the death, and as unfairly as possible.

Innocent Bystanders

The @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani} and @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians} placed on the area map are not intended to participate in this combat encounter, unless you deem their involvement a suitable measure for your game. Once combat begins, any innocent bystanders such as these will run away from the conflict as soon as they become aware of it.

If the combat somehow lasts for more than 10 rounds or spills out into the city at large, you can choose to have 1 or more @UUID[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA]{Burnished Hand Protectors} arrive to help contain the battle and put the minds of other locals at ease.

Examining the Corpse

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 12]] check while searching the corpse of the Harrower is able to confirm it as the worldly remains of Ordan, the Burnished Hand Protector they were sent to check up on — confirmed by etchings on his longsword as well as personal accoutrements around the apartment.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on this check.

  • Result of 15+: There are no apparent wounds on the corpse aside from those inflicted by the party and its vile, withered hand. Whatever strange and accursed force was the cause of this morbid transformation remains a distinct mystery.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 16]] or [[/skill nature 16]] check can confirm the nature of the Harrower's corpse as an undead creature, recently risen from the grave.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] and [[/knowledge forensics]] have advantage on this check.

  • Result of 19+: The loathsome monster slain here today displayed qualities and attributes quite unlike any undead creature in recorded history.

Any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell to examine the corpse notices a dissipating aura of Necromancy magic, which grows less intense by the second.

Despite the previous conclusion of @UUID[.pKU5q3dMnM5DmNpH]{Helping Hands}, the party is free to return to Veneration Hall in Lower Ashvale to share news of their encounter here with Vance, Steros, or the other Burnished Hand Protectors.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Should they desire more information, the party can seek counsel with the Second Sage @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} at Cindarin Temple during the recurring event known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.Z1HSFqailGvSKc7q]{Sage Advice}.

If the party has completed both @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.HKGCsBtXR0tfedkJ]{The Derelict Protector} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy}, their next visit to visit Lilla Arien will direct them to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.jBVzQi6wRjMew0Es]{Performer's Plaza} for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.0vgrOompFkSYPv71]{A Conflagration of Lume}.
The Derelict Protector.soverview: The characters journey to the Fallbrook district of Ordain to investigate the case of a derelict Burnished Hand Protector named Ordan, who has failed to report for duty at the Veneration Hall barracks for a few days now. During their examination of the Protector’s apartment, the party is attacked by Ordan himself — who is no longer human, but has turned into a vile undead creature the likes of which no one in the city has seen before.
The Derelict Protector.sexposition: The directions from Vance are simple but adequate, and lead you right to the front door of a small town house here in Fallbrook, nestled in the lonely byways of a quiet neighborhood street. There is an air of stillness about the place, which seems bereft of the lively activity you're used to seeing in this part of town. The door is closed, the windows dark … not much to speak of without a closer look.
The Derelict Protector.ssummary: We journeyed to the Fallbrook district of Ordain to perform a wellness check on an errant Burnished Hand Protector known as Ordan, who hasn't shown up for his guard duties at Veneration Hall in nearly four days. While investigating Ordan's town home, we encountered the solider himself; no longer a living humanoid, the protector had turned into some grotesque undead semblance of his former self. Our fight with this creature was relatively brief but intense.

A Message from Sin.name: A Message from Sin
A Message from Sin.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event serves to propel the party towards the narrative of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.4gdHjAh6pDmB652r]{Lost in the Stacks}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Receive an invitation from @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} to visit her at the Old City Library in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.iphMPgtJv5eQjGaR]{Scholar's Nook} district.

  • Gather information about Scholar's Nook prior to their visit.

This event is designed to occur wherever the characters might be when the requisite amount of time has passed, rather than at a specific location. The readalouds have been constructed accordingly, but feel free to make any necessary adjustments to suit the party and the moment.

A Curious Visitor

When the Tatterwing Moth arrives, the party has a brief moment to observe the creature directly and begin making some deductions about its peculiar nature and intent.

Identifying the Moth

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 11]] check is able to identify the tatterwing moth as native to the Arctus Plateau. Tatterwing moths are known to inhabit forest, grassland, swamp, and subterranean biomes, but are relatively scarce in urban environments.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] have advantage on this check.

Characters with a [[/skill animalhandling 11 passive]] are able to notice that the behavior of the moth is peculiar and uncanny, as if it was being motivated by an outside influence.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 13]] check is able to recognize a magical gleam in the moth's eyes and traces of a latent supernatural aura, details that signify the moth's role as an arcane (or perhaps druidic) familiar.

Sin's Message

The tatterwing moth carries a message from Sin Marmot: she's trapped within the library vaults beneath the Old City Library, and she needs the party's discreet help to escape. After all, she doesn't want to earn any demerits in her new role as an initiate of the Cindaric order.

After the characters have had a moment to survey the curious scene, continue with the following readaloud:

The moth speaks with a tiny whisper of a voice, but you can hear its words quite plainly if you focus your attention and lean in to listen.

Salutations, friends! Believe it or not, this is your old pal Sin Marmot speaking. But this isn't actually me, here and now. I'm still in Scholar's Nook, and I need your help.

I'm stuck in the lower stacks of Old City Library, and I'm afraid to reach out to the other sages. I just started my training, and the last thing I need is a demerit for a bad job. If you can find it in your hearts, please come to Scholar's Nook and make your way to the lower stacks by any clandestine means necessary. That's all I can say for now. It's getting hectic over here. Please hurry!

With that, the special gleam in the moth's eye disappears and the tiny creature flutters off and away with the wind.

Identifying the Moth's Magic

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 13]] check can determine the following details.

  • Druids have advantage on this check.

  • The character is able to surmise that Sin is using some bespoke primal magic to communicate via the moth, rather than the shapechanging abilities she's also known for.

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell reveals traces of Illusion and Conjuration magic, but the aura is vague.

Gathering Information: Scholar's Nook

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill charisma 13]] or [[/skill investigation 13]] check is able to round up some conversation about the Scholar's Nook district from a local Ordani citizen. Highlights include:

  • [[/path emberCindaricInitiate]] characters have advantage on this check.

  • The Old City Library is also known as Tomehold, and is famed for the countless books that line its dusty shelves.

  • The five Coalescents who run the Old City Library are an eccentric group of Cindaric Sages, and rumor has it that they're all collectors of antiquity, with a friendly streak of competition among them.

  • If you're in need of a low-level spell scroll, the folks at The Secret Shelf can help.

Concluding the Event

This quest event is relatively brief, and the characters are Sin's only recourse if she hopes to escape her unfortunate predicament.

Next Steps

The party must travel to the Old City Library in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.iphMPgtJv5eQjGaR]{Scholar's Nook} district of Ordain, where Sin Marmot awaits them for the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.4gdHjAh6pDmB652r]{Lost in the Stacks}.
A Message from Sin.soverview: The party is whimsically approached by a special tatterwing moth, which is actually a bestial envoy for their ally Sin Marmot. Sending a message via the moth's supernatural whispers, Sin entreats the characters to join her at the Old City Library in Scholar's Nook to assist her with a timely task at hand.
A Message from Sin.sexposition: A swift breeze sweeps through your vicinity, carrying with it a familiar mossy scent that you can't quite place. On its heels, the soft, fluttering sound of a tatterwing moth can be heard. Indeed, you see such a tiny creature drift into the area from seemingly nowhere, and waft its way ever-so-closer to one of your shoulders, where it comes to a gentle rest.
A Message from Sin.ssummary: We were approached by a curious visitor: a tatterwing moth that carried the voice of our ally Sin Marmot. Following an exchange of pleasantries, Sin invited us to visit her at work in the Old City Library, which can be found in Ordain's Scholar's Nook district.

Sage Advice.name: Sage Advice
Sage Advice.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event allows the party to seek counsel with the Second Sage @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} several times throughout the course of the quest by reconnecting with her at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.GlbJezRw2ecnVIsx]{Cindarin Temple}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Speak with Lilla Arien about the various quest events leading up to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.0vgrOompFkSYPv71]{A Conflagration of Lume} to learn her perspective on the matters at hand and the respective characters involved.

  • Take advantage of Cindarin Temple's other amenities during their visit.

Event Repetition

"Sage Advice" is a repeating event, and is configured to activate whenever the party returns to Cindarin Temple at this point. As a result, you may find yourself having to ignore repeat pop-up windows for this event when they occur from time to time.

Character Advancement

The characters will have the opportunity to advance during the course of their visits with the Second Sage. This moment occurs the first time the party checks in with @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} after they've completed both @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.HKGCsBtXR0tfedkJ]{The Derelict Protector}.

Milestone Point

Completion of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.HKGCsBtXR0tfedkJ]{The Derelict Protector} events rewards a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone} point, potentially enabling the party to advance in level, but only after the characters have reported this progress to Lilla Arien.

During this same visit, Lilla will suggest two courses of action for the party: stop by the forthcoming Lumek bonfire ceremony in Performer's Plaza to meet with Luna Karrowrath and her Flameguard warriors, and visit the Temple of Sockets in Temple Ward to speak with the high priest Conaris Haid. These two leads will hopefully provide the characters with more answers about the mystery at hand.

During this particular encounter with Lilla Arien, be sure to read the following aloud:

The Second Sage holds her chin in speculation for a brief moment before speaking.

These two distinct encounters with the undead start raising some serious concerns about the origins of these entities and its potential impact on the city. My knowledge of these things is limited … perhaps you should seek the counsel of a few people in the city more informed about the ways of the undying.

Tomorrow night, Luna Karrowrath — the infamous champion of Lumé — will be hosting a ceremonial bonfire for her Flameguard warriors in Performer's Plaza. Seek her out, and ask her about the Blood Barons. Perhaps she can enlighten you regarding what became of our friend Ardus Tohl.

As for the harrowing, withered soldier once known as Ordan … perhaps that old lunatic Conaris Haid can help you. Be sure to visit the Temple of Sockets in the Temple Ward to speak with the high priest. He can tell you more about the Soul Cycle, and the ways in which it has been broken. But be warned — the dodgy old fellow has a wandering mind and a rather short temperament.

None in the city are more qualified than these two in matters of the soul. Or its enemies.

Lilla's pointed instructions here are distinct from her general opinions about the Lumek and the Temple of Sockets, which can be found below in their respective sections.

Next Steps

Once Lilla has made the party aware of these two leads, the characters can investigate the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.0vgrOompFkSYPv71]{A Conflagration of Lumé} and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.ydYEFz46NhoJZqHs]{Bickering Priests}.

Visiting Lilla Arien

It's relatively easy for the party to track down @UUID[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]{Lilla Arien} whenever they return to Cindarin Temple for her counsel (unless otherwise dictated for your narrative). The Second Sage can often be found in the sanctuary, the refectory, the library, or her private chambers.

Learnings from the Second Sage

Lilla Arien is a well-learned, well-liked individual in Ordain, and her reputation for kindness and empathy often precedes her. Throughout the party's many interactions with the Second Sage, they should find her to be an approachable and helpful ally — fully aligned with their quest to solve the mystery lurking at the heart of the rising undead threat. (Of course, any of the party's agendas outside of this are up to your discretionary judgement).

General conversation points that Lilla is prepared to discuss include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Sin's current progress during her training as an initiate.

  • If any of the player characters are a [[/path CindaricAdherent]] themselves, Lilla takes an similar interest in their progress as well.

  • The party's overall wellness — physically, mentally, and spiritually.

  • Day-to-day affairs of the Cindaric Sages (omitting any potentially sensitive information, of which she is generally unaware).

  • The current task at-hand for the party's larger quest to investigate the rising undead threat.

  • Details about various aspects of the city of Ordain, including specific information on select districts, how and where to find standard amenities, persons of interest, and more.

Unless otherwise indicated, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check is able tell that Lilla Arien point of view is consistently authentic. More often than not, the Second Sage has nothing to hide.

@embed[Actor.Sxbbvc7gq0WhbuXq]

Other prominent Cindarics, such as @UUID[Actor.KQ9uGdZu6zDlM66n]{Jon Vastil} and @UUID[Actor.Gw2LWZ2e1MU6KuIY]{Vinarith} are unavailable for counsel or conversation during these intermittent trips to visit Lilla Arien. During these visits, access to the Temple's more private areas is rather limited. Once the party is ready to leave, they may go about their business in whatever fashion they choose.

The Secret Autopsy

About the Victim, Ardus Tohl:

The Second Sage exhales with a sigh of regret.

"Ardus Tohl was a good man, and well on his way to becoming a good sage. It's hard enough to find adherents who embrace our path of servitude, let alone those who would eagerly perform their duties in the droll environs of a cemetery. This affliction of his, whatever it was, is certainly a shame.

Ardus kept a dormitory here at the temple. Once his body was discovered, a thorough examination of his chambers was conducted, to no avail. It's difficult to say precisely when or where the mysterious affliction took hold. But his body was cold and as pale as a sheet when we found him."

About the Vampyre Spawn:

"It's as if Ardus Tohl had become infected with some terrible, monstrous curse or disease to become such a fiend before your very eyes. Far to the west, in the wastelands of the Moiran Blood Barons, there are creatures such as this … feral, blood-drinking cutthroats whose humanity has been corrupted its very core. Did this creature wound any of your party, by any chance? I'd hate to see you ravaged by some unseen poison or illness. Please, let me take a look at you …"

The Derelict Protector

About the Protector, Ordan:

"I don't know much about this young protector named Ordan, or the station he keeps within the Burnished Hand. Fallbrook is a lovely neighborhood, however, with ample housing for those of comfortable means. I believe the Hand pays their protectors well. And the soldiers certainly earn it. No doubt the young man earned himself some rest as well."

Thoughts on the Burnished Hand:

"The Burnished Hand is the sword arm of the Cindaric Sages. A group of tireless warriors who help protect the Cindarics and the entire city from a variety of would-be problems. Whether it's defending the city from outside attack, providing muscle for emergency relief, or the simple security details here at Cindarin Temple … the Burnished Hand have proven themselves to be invaluable allies in our ongoing struggle against the encroaching chaos of the Sheer."

Opinions of Steros Kraver:

"Steros is a proud man, but (I believe) he lacks the haughty pompousness of less-dignified fellows. He is a very capable leader of the Burnished Hand, and charismatic at that. Here at Cindarin Temple and during official ceremonies, he's all business. But he seems to be more grounded among his soldiers, and their world of bronze armor and endless combat training. I certainly hope to get to know him better in the years to come. He's a good friend to the Cindarics, and one of our best resources when the going gets tough."

About the Harrower:

"It seems as if Ordan was beset by some terrible evil to become a withered creature such as this. In all my years I've never heard of such a menace, even amidst the tall tales from out of the west of the Moiran wastelands and their inhuman armies. This was no vampyre you encountered, but something else altogether. Something insidious, to be sure. We should share news of this novel entity with the inner council of Sages, and Steros Kraver himself."

A Conflagration of Lumé

Regarding Luna Karrowrath:

"Songs are sung of Lumé's champion from here to the Cascilian Republic. She is known to be a beacon of light in the hopelessness of dark, and serves as a potent figurehead for her people and the Lumek Firebrands she leads into battle."

On the Lumek Flameguard:

"The Lumek are known far and wide as formidable warriors, and one of the best hopes Ember has against the encroaching threat of the Moiran Blood Barons. Thanks to the Flameguard, the Barons are confined to their lightless wastelands, and the rest of Ember can sleep well at night knowing that sunlit lands like the Arctus Plateau are safe."

Bickering Priests

Regarding Sockets:

"The elder god of death is known to nearly all of us, whether we realize it or not. His domains are that of death, rebirth, and souls. I've yet to meet the Lord of the Bonelands, but from what I understand he's a rather cantankerous old fellow who loves a good laugh. No wonder his high priest here in Ordain is a stubborn madman as well. Souls are heavy things, I suppose, and a light heart must surely be needed to carry them through the ages of eternity.

If you've yet to meet any priests of Sockets on your journeys so far, they're actually fairly common throughout the Arctus Plateau. We have a grand temple to Sockets here in Ordain, situated in the middle of Temple Ward."

Regarding Sionia:

The Second Sage purses her lips with a measure of hesitation.

"Not much is known about the Lonely Goddess, other than her prodigious wizardry and her penchant for reanimation. But anyone who would tread on the sanctity of the Soul Cycle — shard god or otherwise — is someone to be carefully minded."

Opinions of Conaris Haid:

The Second Sage cracks a sardonic smile.

"The High Priest of Sockets is a very unserious man. One who's devoted his life to a rather serious cause. The old codger acts like a fool, raving and drooling from time to time, but I imagine there's more to these bouts of madness than it seems. I'm not sure whether Sockets chose Conaris to serve him, or if Conaris was drawn to the Keeper of Souls by his own accord. But those two are a match made in Primordis, that's for sure."

Numinous Rendezvous

Sionia's Plan:

The Second Sage regards you with a measure of concern.

"It may already be too late to retrieve those corpses from the Burial Grounds, but there's a chance they haven't been prepared or cremated yet. You'll need to make haste to the cemetery if this plan is to bear any fruit … rotten or otherwise."

Regarding Shard Gods and Other Deities:

"The shard gods are curious entities, each of them disparate, with their own interests and areas of concern. Various deities of The Nineteen are worshipped openly by the people of Ordain, although we Cindarics tend to hold a more secular point of view. Certainly, there are faithful among us here at Cindarin Temple; but dedicated service to the protection of Ember's Heartblood is paramount — and must supersede our individual faith in any god. All things serve the ever-beating Heart of Ember."

About the Burial Grounds:

"The Burial Grounds are built atop an overgrown hillside estate northeast of town, and play home to graves and monuments for people of every Arcturian and Ordani faith. Cindaric funeral practices differ from more archaic faiths, in that we prepare the dead in a special ceremony before their eventual cremation.

Sionia's plan to retrieve the undead corpses seems like a reasonable one, and it's a shame we didn't think of it sooner. The Cindaric Crematorium where the bodies will be found is near the center of the graveyard's cluttered sprawl. Follow these simple directions to find your way, and always heed the groundskeepers."

Lilla hands you a tiny scrap of paper with a map of the Burial Grounds sketched upon it, which presumably will lead you directly to the Cindaric facility you seek.

Other Topics

About the Soul Cycle:

"The Soul Cycle is a curious phenomenon, but it is a process that steers the fate of every person on Ember, whether they know it or not. When we're born, a tiny piece of the Heart of Ember coalesces into our soul before journeying to the surface, where it joins with our physical bodies; and when we die, our souls leave our bodies and journey to the Bonelands, where Sockets himself holds sway over the fate of each soul.

But honestly, this is a matter best discussed with the priests of Sockets themselves, who know a great deal more about it than myself. You can always find the high priest and his disciples at the Temple of Sockets in Temple Ward, alongside sanctuaries to several other faiths."

Thoughts on the Cindaric Order:

"We are the custodians of Ember's light, and the healers of the living planet's Heartblood. For centuries, the Cindarics have kept a light burning in the advent of darkness — a darkness we've kept at bay for so very long, and one we will continue to fight. Alongside the goodly adherents of Sockets and other gods, we strive to protect the ever-changing world of ours from the chaos that might destroy it. The great city of Ordain is our most treasured protectorate, and each Cindaric feels the weight of their station when they walk through the grand halls of Cindarin Temple, where the great Adonia once prophesied the very age we live in. I've given the Cindarics my life, and thy've given me a grand and righteous purpose in return."

Opinions of Jon Vastil:

"The Holy Speaker has been like a father to me for many years. He's a good man. A wise leader. And a kind soul. He is the very heartbeat of the Cindaric faith. There is a calm in his spiritual guidance that feels … comfortable, and right. And pure. I trust him with my very being, and would lay down my life for him, should it ever come to that. That's how much he means to me."

Opinions of Vinarith:

A slight wrinkle dances across Lilla's brow, which she fails to hide.

"The steward is a remarkably capable sage, and is very well-liked among the sages and adherents here. Jon Vastil himself is certainly fond of Vinarith, who has been like a personal attendant to the speaker of late. Indeed, it's become harder and harder to schedule a meeting with Jon without Vinarith's inclusion; but the Cindaric faith is one of holistic collaboration. Even if he can be a bit … erudite, Vinarith is undeniably successful with his recruitment efforts and is extraordinarily well-studied in the history of the Cindarics and the lore of the Soul Cycle. We're lucky to have him."

Opinions of Sin Marmot:

The Second Sage smiles.

"Initiate Marmot is an extraordinary addition to the ranks of the Cindaric Sages. Her enthusiasm for life and her zeal for discovery are valuable assets for a Cindaric, who is expected to give back to Ember as much as they take from it — physically and metaphysically alike.

Furthermore, Sin's spellcasting aptitude exceeds that of a standard adherent of her age, and I'm sure these talents will take her far in life. Her benevolent magic will no doubt be a boon to many people. We're grateful that you helped her reach Ordain safely, despite your trials and tribulations. I won't hesitate to say she belongs here at Cindarin Temple, among like-minded healers and dreamers. And so you, my friends."

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

After each subsequent quest event, the party is free to return to Cindarin Temple to speak with Lilla Arien at their relative leisure. Sage Advice will no longer be available after the characters have started the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.CdrrKWXIJazJgTJ7]{Grave Assignments} event.
Sage Advice.soverview: After their encounters with undead creatures in Westgate and Fallbrook, the characters reconnect with the Second Sage Lilla Arien at Cindarin Temple for information and advice pertaining to the quest events at hand. Lilla is receptive of the party's request for help, and invites the characters to return to the Temple at their leisure whenever they require additional guidance.
Sage Advice.sexposition:
A few familiar faces greet you as you traverse the grand halls of Cindarin Temple — sages and initiates who've come to know you as allies of the Cindarics and one of their most promising new members. Before you know it, you're standing face-to-face with the Second Sage, Lilla Arien. The matronly Cindaric puts her idle business aside to welcome you back to the benevolent order's stately home.

Welcome back to Cindarin Temple, friends. How can I help you?
Sage Advice.ssummary: We visited Lilla Arien at Cindarin Temple, and she provided us with some helpful information regarding the Cindaric Sages and our ally Sin's advancement within the group. The beloved Second Sage has extended an open invitation to return to her, should we require additional knowledge or guidance about whatever comes our way.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for Traveler's Rest depicts the eponymous @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric} Healing House, located in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.nS7kj8wZ5eFq6pcy]{Westgate} district. In addition to its ubiquity as an everyday place of rest and relaxation for Ordani citizens, this location serves as the setting for the following quest events.

[[/eventState cindaric2Autopsy]] in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders}:

  • During The Secret Autopsy, the characters will enter the downstairs areas through the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.NRXgT7OwVzJvyUBl]{Basement Entrance} with their ally @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} at the duly appointed time.

  • Other points of entry include smaller doors attached to the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.x2EmlUaHS1npWWvO]{Library}, @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.jSsBCkof3uze0SCV]{Main Office}, @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.AdKtzErtJ57hkJpo]{Jessa's Private Quarters}, @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.obGpA59TbzuiYePx]{Guest Quarters}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.u9GZ9o0g1rOJRX4A]{Rear Storage Vestibule}, plus multiple points of access via the exterior @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.TUjtZx3pz8oPALfq]{Courtyard}.

  • Traveler's Rest is occupied at all times by various @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} and a few @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, as well as numerous patients — citizens and visitors in need of the Cindaric Order's famed healing capabilities and the amenities of the facility itself. More information about these various denizens is available in @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.vl026XRpU0CEjsHG]{Gameplay Details}.

  • Each of the Cindarics here is equipped with a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key}, capable of unlocking most of the healing house's interior and exterior doors.

[[/eventState unfinishedBusinessHealing]] in @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq]{Unfinished Business}:

  • The party will visit Traveler's Rest with their ally @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} in an effort to determine the medical details about his newfound condition as a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound} individual.

Since Traveler's Rest is a smaller location within the mile-wide hex that comprises the Ordani district of Westgate, the Gazetteer Entry below contains information about the neighborhood as a whole. Additional information about the specific areas of Traveler's Rest are featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.vl026XRpU0CEjsHG]{Gameplay Details} section of this walkthrough.

Work In Progress

This area walkthrough for the Traveler's Rest area map is a work in progress. Some location descriptions are still in development, and journals may not reflect all of the intended encounters or terrain features.

Additionally, the two different area maps of the location's two vertical levels — the @UUID[Scene.emberTravlrsRest]{Traveler's Rest Healing House} upper level and the @UUID[Scene.emberTravlrsBase]{Traveler's Rest Basement} lower level — will eventually be combined into a single, multilayer map. For now, please activate the appropriate map when necessary.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.nS7kj8wZ5eFq6pcy inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The complete area map for Traveler's Rest is currently depicted by two corresponding maps. @UUID[Scene.emberTravlrsRest]{Traveler's Rest Healing House} details the upper level of the map, and serves as the primary location of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq.JournalEntryPage.e8yFtrTYgYb5kiVE]{Swift Healing} event of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq]{Unfinished Business} main quest. Meanwhile, @UUID[Scene.emberTravlrsBase]{Traveler's Rest Basement} serves as the primary location for the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders} main quest.

Objectives

When the party arrives at the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.NRXgT7OwVzJvyUBl]{Basement Entrance} for the events of [[/eventState cindaric2Autopsy]] they'll connect with their ally @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}, who will lead them deeper into the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.ccly4nfs5DytOJ6h]{Morgue}. Once the characters settle in, they'll:

  • Meet the @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherent} known as Menedaeus, who will present them with the information to-date.

  • Survive a surprise attack from the subject of the autopsy, which is actually a newly-awakened @UUID[Actor.j3B9TkGTc23Q6Ina]{Vampyre Spawn}.

  • Prevent the Vampyre Spawn from escaping the Traveler's Rest Basement and wreaking further havoc upstairs (or beyond).

When the party arrives at the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.jSsBCkof3uze0SCV]{Main Office} for the events of [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessHealing]] with their @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound} ally @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} in tow, they'll solicit the Cindaric Sages who operate the establishment for help. Once the characters enter the healing house, they'll:

  • Make contact with a Cindaric Adherent named Sefton Smythe, who will assist the party with their immediate needs.

  • Meet the @UUID[Actor.uIDDak2Oq8Qd9Mfx]{Cindaric Sage} Thessandra Vale, who will treat Agraband's supernatural wounds to the best of her abilities.

  • Learn scant details about Agraband's mysterious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.pFxI6eScKqZbfT2Q]{Soulbound} condition while acquiring a few leads for potential next steps.

Illumination

The interiors of Traveler's Rest are illuminated by torch and lantern light, which radiate bright light for 15 feet and dim light for an additional 15 feet. The courtyard area is subject to exterior lighting and associated weather conditions.

Terrain

The terrain here resembles a typical urban landscape, with enough clutter and furniture to create intermittent spots of difficult terrain.

Most doors within Traveler's Rest are unlocked. Of the doors that are locked, a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} is necessary to open them without forced entry. Meanwhile, the Basement Entrance has a corresponding extra @UUID[Item.HOL5fmggz6d8QMd4]{Traveler's Rest Basement Key} that must be used to open it. All of the Cindarics at Traveler's Rest are equipped with the Traveler's Rest Key, while a select few (such as Jessa Aritou) have full-time access to the Basement Key.

Elevation

The ceilings within the upstairs and downstairs locations of Traveler's Rest are 15 feet high, unless otherwise stated.

Inhabitants

Traveler's Rest is inhabited by several @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} and @UUID[Actor.uIDDak2Oq8Qd9Mfx]{Cindaric Sages}, including the head sage Jessa Aritou. While they work at various positions throughout the facility, many of these Adherents can often be found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.XxQCJhQ3xhxOSjKV]{Cindaric Lodging} chamber during evening and off-duty hours. Other denizens include the following:

  • One @UUID[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA]{Burnished Hand Protector} is regularly stationed here on security detail, and spends a lot of time in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.3ZK1bmMk5WR9XON6]{Recreation} room on the eastern side of the facility.

  • Meanwhile, the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.uwR5BMezDhDx7oEc]{Infirmary} is currently occupied by four @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani} and two @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians} — patients in need of Traveler's Rest's storied healing.

  • Throughout the day, other Ordani and Arcturians tend to drop in for a variety of short consultations or healing services from the Cindarics, but the frequency of these visits is as unpredictable as the weather. Interestingly, more and more people seem to be in need of the Cindaric Order's help of late (a phenomenon that hasn't gone entirely unnoticed by the Cindarics themselves).

Morgue.name: Morgue
Morgue.text:
The cool air of this large chamber is thick with macabre suspense. Six stone slabs decorate this room, four of which are adorned with humanoid corpses. On top of the abstruse alchemical practices of the Cindarics, you suspect these cadavers are magically preserved in some kind of suspended animation, based on the lack of both visible rot and the putrid stench of the grave.

Just around a corner to the northwest, a narrow set of stairs wraps upward to the ground level of the facility, where the soft thrum of activity can be heard in the nearby distance.

This large room is the morgue of Traveler's Rest. Once a cadaver has been properly cleaned and examined, it becomes the target of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGentleRepo]{Gentle Repose} spell and is brought here, where it awaits final transport to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.cvUD3Rj9MLXLwpAb]{Burial Grounds} or another location. There are currently 5 cadavers in the morgue.

The morgue is attended by at least one @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherent} at all times. A solitary Cindaric works the night shift here, and 1-2 Cindarics can often be found working in this location during daytime hours.

Exploring the Morgue

The morgue is supplied with various tools of the trade, which can be readily spotted by the characters as they survey the area. Notable elements of the room include:

  • A desk on the northern wall, stacked with various notes and documents relating to the cadavers that have recently been processed here.

  • A shelf crammed with official documents like coroner's reports and death certificates.

  • A few piles of random equipment, loose tools, and sundry other items.

  • 4 rolled canvas body bags on a steel cart in the hallway to the east.

  • The skeletal specimen of a deceased humanoid, stored behind glass in a horizontal display case.

The first character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the morgue is able to locate the following:

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Book} on modern embalming techniques of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages}, labeled "The Vascar Papers: A Treatise on Cindaric Funerary Rites".

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Book} on traditional @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.SySGCB7QdgeKowkD]{Kelmezian} embalming techniques, labeled "Consecrations of Old Carinth".

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCantripScro]{Spell Scroll} of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMending000]{Mending}. Alternately, this scroll can be instantly located by a character using the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell.

  • Result of 18+: A Holy Symbol of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.bZ0KT1qResSwRz6f]{Thayloc} is hidden within a concealed drawer inside the desk, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbhsyReliquaryh]{Reliquary} containing TBD.

Inspecting the Cadavers

A series of successful [[/skill investigation 14]] checks are able to confirm some basic information about the cadavers currently stored here, including their respective causes of death.

  • These corpses are random Ordani citizens, and the details of their lives and deaths are relatively inconsequential to the party's adventures. You are encouraged to come up with your own details about the ancestry, gender, and cause of death of these deceased individuals.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The cadavers stored here effectively change every three days. If the characters leave Traveler's Rest and return at least three days later, the initial cadavers are no longer here, and have been replaced with different ones.

Cindaric Small Talk

The Cindarics assigned to work the morgue either love it or hate it, and conversation in this part of Traveler's Rest tends to be more droll and morbid compared to the chatter upstairs.

If the characters find themselves here in the morgue without Cindaric supervision, the Cindaric Adherents on duty will attempt to escort them upstairs and into the welcoming attention of a fellow sage.

Otherwise, if the characters have permission to be here, the Cindarics on duty in the morgue are willing to discuss the following topics of conversation:

  • Day to day duties of Cindarics assigned to the downstairs areas of Traveler's Rest.

  • The general layout of the upstairs locations of Traveler's Rest.

  • Jessa Aritou's role as the head sage, and the roles of the various Cindarics who work here under her inspired guidance.

  • Some of the recent cadavers that have made their way through the morgue.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 17]] or [[/skill persuasion 14]] check is able to convince the Cindaric on duty to share a bit more information.

  • The Cindaric mentions the presence of resources like the Holy Water in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.PbvKrGCRx0f58GRB]{Examination Room} and the barreled chemicals in @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.iLFleFu8TBuc4oJw]{Basement Storage}.

  • The Cindaric will also absentmindedly or accidentally reveal the presence of the "lost & found" chest in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.cfqA38ekYHmEO2qb]{Downstairs Vestibule} area.

  • Characters with [[/path CindaricAdherent]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Cold Storage.name: Cold Storage
Cold Storage.text:
The air of this small, dimly-lit chamber is unnaturally cold. Four recessed appliances like tall steel vaults line the southern wall; one of them stands open, revealing a humanoid body atop a metallic cart half-extended from within. While overtly morbid, this place is nevertheless highly clinical and remarkably clean.

This chamber serves as a cold storage facility here at Traveler's Rest, where the cadavers of the recently deceased can be contained without fear of spoilage.

Exploring the Chamber

The room here is sparsely decorated. It's only notable contents are the four refrigerator vaults that line the southern wall, and a matching set of size-appropriate carts made from a light steel alloy. One of these carts bears a humanoid cadaver, with a parchment tag inconspicuously attached to the right foot (see "Investigating the Cadaver" below for more information about the corpse itself).

Any character that succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check while searching the room is able to notice the following:

  • Most of the vaults here are currently empty.

  • The room itself and the steel carts appear to be cleaned with regularity, to an exceptional standard.

  • Result of 17+: A surgical knife is covertly attached to the bottom of one of the steel carts here via a simple tension clamp. Treat this knife as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbwepDagger0000]{Dagger}. Any character who uses this hidden knife to begin combat gains a +1 to initiative if using a weapon attack with it for their first action.

A successful [[/skill arcana 13]] check is able to confirm the use of magical enchantments as the primary source of refrigeration here.

  • Result of 18+: The character is able to surmise that rare @UUID[Item.gT8CtkBPcAAlmw3t]{Duskflame Powder} is likely a source component of the refrigeration methods used here.

Inspecting the Cadaver

A successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check is able to confirm some basic information about the cadaver currently stored here, including the cause of death.

  • This corpse is a random Ordani citizen, and the details of their life and death are relatively inconsequential to the party's adventures. You are encouraged to come up with your own details about this deceased individual's ancestry, gender, and cause of death.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The cadaver stored here effectively changes every three days. If the characters leave Traveler's Rest and return at least three days later, the initial cadaver is no longer here, and has been replaced with a different one.

Freezing Cold Temperatures

Any character that spends more than an entire hour in this chamber must succeed on a [[/save constitution 15]] saving throw to avoid gaining 1 level of Exhaustion. This saving throw must be repeated every three hours after the first.

  • A character cannot gain more than 3 levels of Exhaustion this way.

  • [[/ancestry Wirrun]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this saving throw.

Examination Room.name: Examination Room
Examination Room.text:
The air of this large room is marked by a melange of strange odors, from the coppery scent of fresh blood to the musky fragrance of stale incense. No doubt, these odors emanate from the countless jars, urns, and casks that decorate this clinical place. A central examination table dominates the room, surrounded by an array of tool carts and end-tables with half-opened drawers.

This chamber serves as the primary examination room whenever the Cindarics need to conduct an autopsy to determine the cause of someone's death (or other extreme ailment).

Exploring the Examination Room

The examination room is fully supplied with various tools of the trade, which can be readily spotted by the characters as they survey the area. These include:

  • Surgical equipment used for posthumous examination and embalming processes.

  • Dozens of jars, urns, and casks that contain a variety of specimens preserved in aldehydes and alcohols.

  • An assortment of journals and notes from previous examinations and autopsies.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the room is also able to locate:

  • The components of 2 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagHealersKit0]{Healer's Kits}.

  • 2 flasks of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagHolyWater00]{Holy Water}.

  • 1 flask of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAlchemistsF]{Alchemist's Fire}.

  • Result of 18+: A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll00]{Spell Scroll} of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectPois]{Detect Poison and Disease} can be found among the various scrolls and documents here. Alternately, this scroll can be instantly located by a character using the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell.

The Secret Autopsy

This chamber is the ultimate setting for the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy}, as featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders} main quest.

After the party arrives at the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.NRXgT7OwVzJvyUBl]{Basement Entrance} with their ally @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}, they'll be led to the Examination Room by the @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherent} known as Menedaeus, where they'll begin their autopsy of the late Ardus Tohl's accursed corpse — which is actually an undead @UUID[Actor.j3B9TkGTc23Q6Ina]{Vampyre Spawn} on the verge of a deadly surprise attack.

This encounter is unique to the quest, and overrides any conflicting information about the encounters described above.

For additional information about this encounter, please refer to the Event Details described in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy} quest event.

Medical Archives.name: Medical Archives
Medical Archives.text:
This neatly cluttered chamber is lined with shelves, replete with numerous books, scrolls, and tomes that appear to contain the facility's archive of medical records and reference documents. The remaining wall space is decorated with assorted medical diagrams, and a handful of dusty skeletal specimens surround the room. Meanwhile, a small desk covered in half-forgotten research occupies a space along the northern wall.

This chamber hosts the medical archives of Traveler's Rest, including current and historical records of patients, handy reference documents, timeworn Cindaric manuals, and more.

Exploring the Archives

Characters who take a moment to Search the archives are able to immediately spot the following:

  • Several volumes of patients' medical records. Many of these leather-bound tomes are sealed with permanent @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplArcaneLock]{Arcane Lock} spells, and require the password "Adonia's grace" to open, spoken in Adonia's native [[/language arcden]]. The contents of these volumes are mostly inconsequential to anyone other than the relatives of the patients or deceased people documented therein.

  • The labeled skeletal reference models that stand here in the room are the cleaned and reconstituted bones of four distinct specimens of humanoids: a human, an ashka, a keth, and a vrjnhar. A fifth, somewhat larger humanoid skeleton occupies the stone table at the center of the chamber, in a state of slight disarray.

  • The desk here sees relatively little use, if the layer of dust on it is any indication. A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Book} labeled "An Encyclopedia of Aterican Osteology" is splayed open on the desk, revealing a page that details the skeletal system of a kivahr male.

  • A hook on the wall near the Basement Entrance bears a key ring containing both a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} and a @UUID[Item.HOL5fmggz6d8QMd4]{Traveler's Rest Basement Key}.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the archives is able to locate the following:

  • The desk drawers contain a loose set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulCalligraph]{Calligrapher's Supplies} and [[/roll 1d2]] random @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets}.

  • Additional @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Books} pertaining to various subjects like Bodily Systems, Alchemical Preservation, and Taxonomy.

  • Result of 18+: The character is also able to find a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagFlask000000]{Flask}, half-full of @UUID[Item.4mIj4qrLgMompEZG]{Arcturian Liquor}, hidden above the desk inside a hollowed-out book.

Basement Storage.name: Basement Storage
Basement Storage.text:
This shadow-cloaked chamber appears to be reserved for basement storage. Packed full of various crates, chests, and barrels, it reeks of some kind of pungent chemical.

This basement chamber is utilized for the storage of assorted tools and equipment, along with various chemicals and compounds used by the Cindarics during their mortuary services.

Exploring the Storage Chamber

This darkened room is plainly packed full of tools, equipment, and consumable resources. Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the room is able to spot the following:

  • 2 barrels full of a curious chemical (formaldehyde).

  • 2 barrels full of a diluted isopropyl alcohol solution (used for cleaning), and 1 barrel full of undiluted isopropyl alcohol.

  • The contents of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagScholarsPac]{Scholar's Pack} and [[/roll 1d2+1]] random results on the @UUID[RollTable.1Osa0OB2Wi99hMyK]{Corpse Loot} table.

Hazardous Chemicals

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check is able to identify the pungent chemical smell as that of an aldehyde used for the preservation of organic tissue. The substance is fatally poisonous if ingested.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Characters with a [[/skill nature passive 12 format=long]] or who succeed on a [[/skill nature 14]] check are immediately wary of the alcohol stored here and its flammable properties. The alcohol is used for industrial cleaning rather than consumption, and is severely poisonous if ingested.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 17+: The character surmises that the undiluted barrel of isopropyl alcohol would make a powerful improvised explosive, dealing [[/roll 4d6]] points of fire damage to any creature within 30 feet of a detonation caused by an attack that does fire damage to the barrel itself.

Downstairs Vestibule.name: Downstairs Vestibule
Downstairs Vestibule.text:
This vestibule appears to serve as a storage area as well as a point of access from the upstairs locations here at Traveler's Rest. Crates full of miscellaneous equipment and barrels full of water, wine, or some other liquid are stacked here in ample supply. The wooden floors here creak beneath your feet as you take note of the low din of the healing house above.

This antechamber connects the downstairs locations to the upstairs areas via a stairway that leads to @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.AdKtzErtJ57hkJpo]{Jessa's Private Quarters}. Due to this proximity to the head sage's personal chamber (despite Jessa's friendly open-door policies with her staff), the downstairs vestibule is the least-used of the healing house's two interior stairways.

Creaky Floors

The floors of the downstairs vestibule are old and rickety, which normally adds an element of charm to the place, but is otherwise problematic for characters who wish to sneak through the area undetected.

Any character who walks on the rickety wooden planks as they move through the downstairs vestibule must succeed on a [[/skill acrobatics 15]] check to avoid the floor's loud creaking noises.

  • Failure compromises the character's ability to Hide here in the downstairs vestibule for a short time. All Dexterity (Stealth) rolls made by the character to Hide here for the next 5 minutes are made with @Advantage[-2].

Exploring the Vestibule

This intermediary chamber is stuffed full of miscellaneous wares. Characters who take a moment to search the downstairs vestibule is able to spot the following:

  • Many of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBarrel00000]{Barrels} here do indeed contain various liquids. At least 4 of them are labeled "WATER," another 3 are labeled "WINE," and 2 are labeled "HARD CIDER" and stamped with a logo of a tree that reads "SWEET RELIEFS, EST. 2483. ORCHARD LANES - ORDAIN."

  • Other sundry items stored down here include crates full of medical-grade textiles, stacks of loose tools, and other equipment.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the room is also able to notice the following:

  • The wooden chest near the northeast corner of the chamber is locked with a heavy pad lock. See "The Locked Chest" below for additional details.

  • One of the barrels contains the residue of a heavily-used supply of @UUID[Item.gT8CtkBPcAAlmw3t]{Duskflame Powder}.

  • The character can assemble enough tools from the equipment here to comprise a set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulCarpenters]{Carpenter's Tools} and a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagDungeoneers]{Dungeoneer's Pack} without the Rations.

  • Result of 18+: The character is also able to find a scattered set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools} here, culled from the various lost & found components of other tool kits. Additionally, the character can smell the Ordani Purfume located in the Locked Chest (see below).

The Locked Chest

The wooden chest here serves as the healing house's little-used lost & found, and contains various items that have gone unclaimed over the last few months. The chest itself is made of sturdy Wedgelands oak and is locked with heavy pad lock. It can be unlocked with a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key}.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill tool=thief 16]] check is able to pick the lock. Alternately, a successful [[/skill athletics 20]] check is able to damage the chest enough to open it. The contents of the chest include:

  • A bottle of Ordani @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPerfume0000]{Perfume} in a velvet @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPouch000000]{Pouch}, which can be smelled from outside the chest by any character with a [[/skill perception passive 15 format=long]].
