  • A silver @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepMace000000]{Mace} worth 105 gp, engraved with the holy symbol of the Hearthken, the shard goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.CBreAnaMxOim355U]{Steelsong}.

  • A dog-eared @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Book} of Waerd Nursery Rhymes.

  • 2 sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesFine]{Fine Clothes} and 3 sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesTrav]{Traveler's Clothes}.

  • 2 random @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets}.

Basement Entrance.name: Basement Entrance
Basement Entrance.text:
A short corridor is cut into the tall stone sidewalk here, with stairs leading down a few steps to a heavy wooden door — notably featureless, save for the sturdy steel hardware that comprises the entry's locking mechanisms.

This basement entrance is primarily used as an inconspicuous access point for the delivery of standard goods and services related to the ongoing operation of the Traveler's Rest downstairs locations, including the morgue and medical archives.

Locked Basement Door

The street-facing basement entrance to Traveler's Rest is a fortified doorway, equipped with two heavy-duty locks and a sturdy wooden crossbar on its interior side. Characters can readily see that the two outward-facing locks are made of high quality steel.

To open the basement door, it must be unlocked with both a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} and a @UUID[Item.HOL5fmggz6d8QMd4]{Traveler's Rest Basement Key}, and the wooden crossbar must also be removed (which can theoretically only be done from the inside).

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the door is able to confirm that although the door is locked quite securely, there are no associated traps.

  • Result of 18+: The character is able to confirm the presence of the sturdy wooden crossbar on the opposite side of the door, and can safely assume that this extra security measure makes lockpicking here a somewhat futile effort.

In order to open the door from the outside, both locks must be picked and the wooden crossbar must somehow be removed.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill tool=thief 15]] check is able to pick the bottom lock, which corresponds to the @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key}.

  • Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill tool=thief 18]] check is able to pick the top lock, which corresponds to the @UUID[Item.HOL5fmggz6d8QMd4]{Traveler's Rest Basement Key}.

  • The wooden crossbar can only be removed from the interior side of the door. If a character can somehow manage to gain visibility of the interior side of the door (an unlikely feat), the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMageHand00]{Mage Hand} spell is strong enough to remove the crossbar.

Alternately, the party can bash the door in with a successful [[/skill strength 30]] check. One failure is ignored. A second failure results in the prompt arrival of one or more @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} and a @UUID[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA]{Burnished Hand Protector}, who are prepared to call forth additional help if necessary.

  • Consult the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.vl026XRpU0CEjsHG]{Gameplay Details} section for additional information about how criminal activity including trespassing is treated by the Cindaric Sages and other locals.

  • Removal of the wooden crossbar lowers the difficulty of this task, requiring a successful [[/skill strength 25]] check instead.

A Cindaric Welcome

The Cindarics of Traveler's Rest use this basement entrance for the day-to-day needs of the morgue, including various ingoing and outgoing goods and services. The door stays closed and locked at all other times.

If the party attempts to knock on this door to gain entry to the basement area of Traveler's Rest, different times of day will result in the following responses:

  • During daylight hours, one of the @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} who work the downstairs locations will answer the door within 5-10 minutes of the knocking.

  • During evening hours, the door will go unanswered for an indeterminate amount of time. Characters may have to wait up to an hour for someone to arrive, and the dispositions of the Cindarics who work these locations after normal hours are comparatively inhospitable. The party is likely to draw unwanted attention to themselves if they persist in this approach.

Unless the party is here to investigate the circumstances of "The Secret Autopsy" (see below), their social encounter here is less than fruitful. The Cindaric who opens the door has the following limited conversation points for the party:

  • This basement entrance is generally reserved for deliveries and outgoing processions (when a cadaver is transferred away from Traveler's Rest to its final resting place, which may or may not be the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.cvUD3Rj9MLXLwpAb]{Burial Grounds} northeast of Ordain).

  • Visitors and patrons of Traveler's Rest are encouraged to enter through one of the main entryways, including the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.jSsBCkof3uze0SCV]{Main Office}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.x2EmlUaHS1npWWvO]{Library}, or the various @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.TUjtZx3pz8oPALfq]{Courtyard} doors.

  • Traveler's Rest is one of Ordain's famed healing houses, where the injured and the infirm can benefit from the mundane and magical healing methods of the Cindaric Sages who work here.

  • These downstairs facilities serve various mortuary needs, and are off-limits to the public. Additional questions can be answered by one of the friendly Cindarics upstairs.

At your discretion, one or more characters may attempt to get additional information out of the Cindaric with a successful [[/skill deception 18]] or [[/skill persuasion 15]] check.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Intimidation is outright unsuccessful, and results in the Cindaric immediately closing and locking the door before the characters can react.

If a Cindaric Adherent answers the door, you may read the following aloud or substitute your own social encounter:

The sound of the city is the only thing that keeps you company for a moment, a thrum of lively activity, indifferent to your interlude.

A few minutes later, you can hear the telltale sounds of the locks on the basement door unlatching, along with the sound of a heavy wooden crossbar being removed from its cradle on the other side.

The door swings outward only a few short inches, and an officious voice issues from within:

Salutations, friends. What business do you have with Traveler's Rest that isn't suited for the front desks?

@Embed[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]

The Secret Autopsy

The basement entrance here serves as the covert meeting place for the party and their ally @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot} for the inciting events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2.JournalEntryPage.GkmuCgw3qlnRGbb6]{The Secret Autopsy}, as featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCindaricAr2]{Smoldering Cinders} main quest.

When the characters arrive for this event, they're promptly greeted by one of the Cindaric Sages — who is expecting them on behalf of the Second Sage Lilla Arien. This encounter is unique to the quest, and overrides any conflicting information about the encounters described above.

For additional information about this encounter, please refer to the Event Details described in [[/eventState cindaric2Autopsy]] quest event.

Courtyard.name: Courtyard
Courtyard.text:
A magnificent stone sun dial sits near the center of this recessed courtyard, where nearly a half-dozen doors lead into various chambers of the healing house. A breeze sweeps through this area with regularity, carrying the ceaseless sounds of the city with it.

This exterior area serves as a quiet retreat where @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} can rest and contemplate amidst the open air of western Ordain.

Time and Time Again

If the characters explore this area during daylight hours, they may discover a curious aspect of the courtyard's centerpiece: the large stone sundial doesn't tell accurate time.

Exploring the Courtyard

During daylight hours, any character with a [[/skill perception 12 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 10]] check while searching the area notices that the shadow of the sundial doesn't align quite evenly with the hour markers.

A character that also succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 16]] check while examining the faulty sundial can determine the cause: the gnomon (the raised pointer that casts a shadow upon the dial) was likely designed for a different latitude.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge cosmology]] or [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Characters with a [[/culture emberRhivan]] background have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • [[/path AcademyDropout]] characters automatically succeed on this check.

  • Result of 18+: The character identifies the precise reason for this error: based on its design, this particular sundial was imported from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.emFVgDaCDq0lWY2b]{Rhivan} @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.KwSB4FIeTyPmdVRl]{Star Academy}, and seems to have never been recalibrated for orientation in Ordain (although it's obviously "close enough" by Cindaric estimates).

Once the problem is identified, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 13]] or [[/skill nature 13]] check while spending an hour working on the sundial using the appropriate tools is able to repair the broken device — aligning the gnomon within its bracket until its shadow falls accurately along the hour mark.

  • Result of 18+: The job is finished in half the time.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] or [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

As soon as the sundial is properly aligned, read the following aloud:

As you nudge the final component into place, the sundial shudders for a brief moment, vibrating with arcane energy. Just then, a dozen tiny blue orbs of magical light illuminate the numerals that line the circumference of the dial. The current hour appears to glow more intensely than the others, and an artful scrawl of lambent text appears on the side of the sundial's stoney plinth. It reads:

A gift of the Star Mages. May time always be on your side.

Just Rewards

If the party manages to repair the sun dial, the head sage Jessa Aritou is astonished by the unsolicited refurbishment, and offers the characters a [[/award party 25gp]] for their timely service.

Infirmary.name: Infirmary
Infirmary.text:
Many of the beds of this large, open-air infirmary are occupied by ill and ailing patrons of the healing house. But despite their unfortunate reason for being here, there is an overt air of calm throughout this place. A chart of dates, times, and procedures sits on a small table at the foot of each bed, and the curtains here allow a modicum of natural light to reach the room from outside.

This room serves as the main infirmary for patients of Traveler's Rest. The beds here are mostly used for short-term occupancy, but provisions for extended stays are certainly made from time to time.

@Embed[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]

Main Quest: Spreading Sickness

If the characters return during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness}, the infirmary is overfilled with people suffering from the mysterious wasting illness. They are tended to by one or two exhausted Cindaric Adherents, who aren't in the mood to answer questions. Ignore the text below until the quest is resolved.

Exploring the Infirmary

A simple Search reveals the following: each cot is accompanied by a small side table bearing a clay basin.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 11]] check notices that several of the clay basins contain traces of a herbal tincture that smells faintly of mint.

  • Result of 15+: One of the clay basins contains a full, untouched dose of the tincture. A character can carefully decant it into a suitable container.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill medicine 14]] check recognizes this tincture as @UUID[Item.g3PuMlzSD8tEIYnQ]{Cindaric Mint Tea}, a palliative draught meant to induce sleep.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge plants]] or [[/knowledge forensics]] succeed on this check automatically.

If stolen, the @UUID[Item.g3PuMlzSD8tEIYnQ]{Cindaric Mint Tea} can be given to the Burnished Hand Protector in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.3ZK1bmMk5WR9XON6]{Recreation} room for a small reward.

Cindaric Conversation

The Cindarics on duty here are busy, and are generally unwilling to engage in long conversation. However, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 12]] or [[/skill persuasion 12]] check is able to solicit some additional information, including:

  • The mint-scented tincture kept beside certain beds is a mild palliative draught, used to help patients sleep through pain or fever. It is not considered dangerous, though the Cindarics avoid giving it to anyone who needs to remain lucid for treatment or questioning.

  • The healers here see all manner of common illnesses and lingering complaints, from fevers and fatigue to infected wounds and chronic pain. Cases that prove unusually stubborn are typically referred to one of the more experienced Cindaric Sages in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.86owx3lgvm2zLyv4]{Ashvale Sanatorium}.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check confirms the relative veracity of the Cindaric healer's various conversation points, along with an honest desire to be equally helpful to all patrons (no matter their personal disposition).

Local Small Talk

The Ordani and Arcturian patients here are willing to pass the time with ordinary conversation. Common topics include the following:

  • How long each patient has been staying at Traveler's Rest, and whether their condition seems to be improving.

  • Opinions on the Cindarics' bedside manner, remedies, and food from the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.mNaKv1ypsKYSypJx]{Refectory}.

  • Local gossip based on what the party is currently experiencing; for example, if the party has discovered a mural from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0]{Local Color}, they might hear gossip about graffiti.

Can I help?

I don't know, can you? What does someone like you know about treating disease?

Bedside Manner

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill medicine 12]] check demonstrates their basic aptitude in conversation with the Cindaric attendant, who then allows them to treat patients in the infirmary.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] succeed on their check automatically.

Helping Out in the Infirmary

Once their assistance is accepted by the attending Cindaric, a character can approach a patient and attempt to diagnose their condition: roll on or choose from the @UUID[RollTable.cK0yaPfqWY4csCUx]{Aterican Diseases} table to determine the patient's condition (do not share this information with the character).

Physical Examination

The character gets an overview of any obvious exterior symptoms (rashes, bruises, etc.). A character with a [[/skill perception 16 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] check reveals any exterior symptoms that are easy to miss (if present at all).

Patient History

The character interviews the patient and gets their interpretation of their symptoms, which may or may not be entirely accurate. A character with a [[/skill persuasion 16 passive format=long]] or who makes a [[/skill persuasion 14]] check gets them to open up about symptoms they might find embarrassing or sensitive (if present at all).

Diagnosis

Once the character believes they've gathered enough information, they can attempt to diagnose the illness by consulting the @UUID[RollTable.cK0yaPfqWY4csCUx]{Aterican Disease} table and cross-referencing the patient's symptoms. In the event that their information matches more than one illness, they must choose one.

Outcome

After diagnosing the patient, the character can present their thoughts to the attending Cindaric, who will lend them their @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} in order to enter the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.ox3u0apezmYTtHA8]{Alchemy} closet and concoct a cure.

Upon returning to the infirmary and administering the cure, the patient may — or may not, if the diagnosis was incorrect — recover. If a character ever gives an incorrect diagnosis, their privileges in the infirmary are revoked.

Refectory.name: Refectory
Refectory.text:
This large refectory is organized around a broad oak table at its center, the wood stained dark in places by years of careless dining. Along the walls stand preparation counters and shelves of brass cookware. A stone hearth smolders in the northwestern corner, and the smell of cooked meat and charred herbs drifts from the embers.

This area functions as both a food preparation area and a shared dining hall. Meals are typically taken whenever they are most convenient for the Cindarics on duty and their visiting guests.

@Embed[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]

Main Quest: Spreading Sickness

If the characters return during the events of Spreading Sickness, the refectory is emptied of supplies. Ignore the text below until the quest is resolved.

Exploring the Refectory

A simple Search reveals the following: the shelves and larders here are kept in orderly condition, with simple ingredients and cookware kept close at hand so meals can be prepared quickly.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check notices a bottle of @UUID[Item.XweVxnBoA5aDhoLa]{Waterborne Whiskey} partially hidden behind a number of other bottles.

If stolen, the whiskey can be given to the Burnished Hand Protector in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.3ZK1bmMk5WR9XON6]{Recreation} room for a small reward.

A Hot Meal

A Cindaric is busy at work preparing meals for the whole lodge. They welcome the characters to sit and enjoy a hot meal if they're hungry, but are generally unwilling to engage in long conversation. However, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 12]] or [[/skill persuasion 12]] check is able to solicit some additional information, including:

  • Meals here are prepared for both Cindaric staff and any guests or patients well enough to leave their rooms. Those too weak to walk are typically served directly in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.uwR5BMezDhDx7oEc]{Infirmary}.

  • The Cindarics keep simple staples on hand at all times: broths, roasted meats, coarse breads, herbal teas, and other foods meant to be easy on the stomach.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters have advantage on these checks.

  • Result of 14+: The Cindaric decides to "share a little something extra," and retrieves the bottle of @UUID[Item.XweVxnBoA5aDhoLa]{Waterborne Whiskey}; they leave the bottle on the central table.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check confirms that the Cindaric is speaking honestly, along with a genuine desire to be warm and inviting to guests.

Cindaric Lodging.name: Cindaric Lodging
Cindaric Lodging.text:
If the crimson robes hanging around the room are any indication, this modest dormitory houses the resident Cindarics of Traveler's Rest. Seven slender beds line the chamber, each paired with a small footlocker and an iron hook for garments. This orderly space is one of unostentatious comfort, rife with the soothing scent of clean linens and aromatic teas.

This room serves as the primary bedchamber for Cindarics assigned to work at Traveler's Rest, where they're expected to tend to the ill and the infirm at nearly all hours of the day. While many sages, adherents, and initiates who work the healing house do actually live elsewhere, several of the Cindarics are provided with beds here.

@Embed[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]

Off Limits

The doors to this chamber remain unlocked, but the area is off limits: characters who are found in this area without permission (or a good reason) will be asked to leave Traveler's Rest, and may be barred from returning.

Exploring the Cindaric Lodging

A simple Search reveals the following: several of the beds are made with nearly identical precision, while others show small signs of recent use, such as a half-finished cup of herbal tea, a pair of slippers tucked beneath a bedframe, or a freshly washed robe left hanging from an iron hook to air dry.

The room's footlockers contain little of material value, consisting mostly of spare robes, linens, writing materials, Cindaric texts, and small personal effects. However, any character with a [[/skill perception 15 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the room discovers a Kingslayer travel set with carved bone pieces.

Library.name: Library
Library.text:
The air here is infused with the earthen smell of aged parchment and the congenial aroma of lingering incense. Numerous books, tomes, scrolls, and folios are stacked neatly on the shelves that line this welcoming library.

Cindarics are known for their studious application of knowledge, and this library chamber contains all the standard scholastic resources that have come to be associated with the Sages, including time-honored volumes on subjects like medicine, alchemy, botany, geology, Cindaric purification rituals, and the metaphysics of Ember.

Exploring the Library

A simple Search reveals the following: the library's collection focuses heavily on Cindaric medicine, anatomy, and the natural world, but a small shelf dedicated to Ember metaphysics stands apart from the rest.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 11]] check while searching the area also notices the following:

  • Every book bears a small brass clasp engraved with Cindaric sigils, though none appear to be locked.

  • Most volumes show almost no sign of wear, as if they have been repeatedly restored.

  • Result of 15+: The character discovers an ornate feather-shaped bookmark of silvered metal tucked inside a book on Ember metaphysics. The base is embossed with a cat's head symbol.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 18]] check is able to detect that the brass clasps are anchoring a powerful magical effect; @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} reveals a pervasive aura of conjuration magic surrounding each clasp.

Any character who succeeds on either a [[/skill history 18]] or [[/skill religion 20]] check is aware of the reason: many Cindaric libraries secure their collections with enchanted clasps that teleport misplaced or stolen books back to their proper shelf [[/roll 1d4]] hours following due date expiration. The same enchantment also periodically repairs wear and tear. If the clasp is separated from the book, its enchantment is broken.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters automatically succeed on these checks.

  • Known by all Cindarics, the secret phrase "Knowledge in the margins" suppresses the clasp's enchantment for 36 hours.

Using the Library

A character can perform a Study Action in this area over the course of a Short Rest, gaining @Advantage[2] on their next check related to a chosen area of knowledge. At the GM's discretion, they may also learn new pieces of information about the subject.

Alchemy.name: Alchemy
Alchemy.text:
This cramped alchemical workshop is crowded with blackened glassware and dried herbs strung from a timber rack. A clouded alembic rests on the workbench, surrounded by sparse but meticulously arranged supplies.

This area is used as an alchemical workshop and storage space. The Cindarics prepare medicines, tinctures, and curative draughts here before distributing them throughout the infirmary.

Locked & Off Limits

The doors to this chamber remain locked unless a surgical procedure is taking place. Each door can be unlocked with a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} or [[/skill tool=thief 15]] check; alternatively, it can be bashed open with a [[/skill athletics 22]] check.

Characters found in this area without a good reason will be asked to leave Traveler's Rest and be barred from returning.

Main Quest: Spreading Sickness

If the characters return during the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness}, the alchemical lab's supplies are completely exhausted. Ignore the text below until the quest is resolved.

Alchemical Lab

This area contains an alchemical lab and enough alchemical components to craft 1 of each of the following:

  • @UUID[Item.j6zuAbUyWDWLjBFg]{Antifungal Draught}

  • @UUID[Item.zYnZJXWZ2s2jKzEv]{Anticoagulation Tonic}

  • @UUID[Item.CZTzfRrJLOdxeS1n]{Dissolution Tonic}

  • @UUID[Item.ohX47gu4PvpL7Go5]{Heartward Elixir}

  • @UUID[Item.g3PuMlzSD8tEIYnQ]{Cindaric Mint Tea}

  • @UUID[Item.Qg2cqy4rAf4YSBx0]{Potion of Healing}

Alchemical components are restocked on the first day of each month.

Main Office.name: Main Office
Main Office.text:
The cluttered front desk of this main office is covered in parchment notes and dog-eared ledgers, and is flanked by a modest bookshelf on the north wall. An array of low wooden benches fills the front and sides of the room, and the amber glow of lantern light keeps a warm and welcoming vigil here.

This room serves as a reception and waiting area for healing house patrons. A sturdy desk sits near the entrance. Next to it, a large woven basket holds folded wool blankets for patients who must wait overnight.

Exploring the Main Office

A simple Search reveals the following: a prominent ledger rests upon the edge of the front desk. Any character who takes a moment to look at this visitor's log sees the two most recent entries, aligned beneath categories labeled "Name," "Reason for Visit," and "Notes."

Entry 1 features the current occupant of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.hrmtUDWIx7LoMinf]{Study}, as determined by the @UUID[RollTable.sJK3abcGjb6IamDp]{Traveler's Rest Itinerant} table.

[NAME]. Research.

Entry 2 features the current occupant of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.obGpA59TbzuiYePx]{Guest Quarters}, as determined by the @UUID[RollTable.sJK3abcGjb6IamDp]{Traveler's Rest Itinerant} table.

[NAME]. Temporary housing.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check while searching the room is able to notice the following:

  • A logbook of remote Cindaric assignments for various locations throughout Ordain, including the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.86owx3lgvm2zLyv4]{Ashvale Sanatorium}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.J37jJxiegQk11IcL]{Spellbreaker Tower}, and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.cvUD3Rj9MLXLwpAb]{Burial Grounds}.

  • Result of 17+: The character discovers a @UUID[Item.HOL5fmggz6d8QMd4]{Traveler's Rest Basement Key} inside the desk.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Study.name: Study
Study.text:
This narrow chamber serves as modest living quarters. A bed sits beneath a small window overlooking a quiet cobblestone street. Beside it stands a writing desk, its surface a messy sprawl of loose pages and open books.

This bedroom chamber acts as a private study area for the residents and visitors of Traveler's Rest, and often serves as guest quarters for important guests and dignitaries.

Exploring the Chamber

A simple Search reveals the following: in addition to the usual comforts provided by Traveler's Rest, the room contains a wash basin, a folded spare blanket, a water pitcher and clay cup, and an unlocked footlocker for the current guest's belongings.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 11]] check notices a few personal effects left in plain view, their exact nature depending on whoever is currently staying here (see "Who Goes There?" below); describe one or two visible items that suit that guest.

  • Result of 15+: The character also notices an additional personal belonging, keepsake, or trinket on the current guest's person. This item should reinforce the guest's possible profession, recent travels, present hardship, or reason for staying at Traveler's Rest.

Who Goes There?

Roll on (or choose from) the @UUID[RollTable.sJK3abcGjb6IamDp]{Traveler's Rest Itinerant} table to determine who is currently staying in the Guest Quarters. They readily engage in conversation, revealing the following:

  • Where they most recently came from, where they expect to go next, or what business brought them to Ordain in the first place.

  • One additional personal detail appropriate to the current guest, such as their profession, recent hardship, notable possession, or local connection.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check confirms that the guest is mostly forthright (for a complete stranger), and that their stated reason for staying here is genuine.

Recreation.name: Recreation
Recreation.text:
This cluttered room appears to have once been a guest bedroom or the like, but now bears the signs of a somewhat communal space. A narrow bed on the northern wall sits half-made. Nearby, a game board and several wooden pawns lay scattered atop a small round table, as though the players abandoned it only moments ago. A bored-looking Burnished Hand Protector greets you with a nod.

This chamber provides the residents and visitors of Traveler's Rest with a place for rest and relaxation, whether of a communal or solitary nature. More often than not, a Burnished Hand Protector from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.86owx3lgvm2zLyv4]{Veneration Hall} can be found here, having been stationed at Traveler's Rest to provide martial support for the local Cindarics.

@Embed[Actor.EHxdMeC2ys3fnWFA]

Exploring the Chamber

A simple Search reveals the following: this room is supplied with a handful of simple comforts for idle hours, including spare blankets, dog-eared books, a deck of cards, and a well-used Kingslayer set with mismatched wooden pieces.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 11]] check notices several neat rows of tally marks carved into the table's sides.

  • Result of 15+: The character also finds a folded scrap of paper tucked beneath a table leg: it lists a few favored Kingslayer opening plays in a messy scrawl. Any character who spends 10 minutes studying these notes gains @Advantage[2] on one Intelligence check made to play Kingslayer in this room.

The Bored Guard

Lucel Darrigon (Neutral Good, Arcturian Human, he/him), the Burnished Hand Protector stationed here, is starved for company, and readily engages the party in light conversation. He will not disclose sensitive information, but may reveal the following:

  • The Burnished Hand keeps a protector at Traveler's Rest to discourage trouble, assist the Cindarics in emergencies, and provide a visible reminder that patients and staff are under protection.

  • Visitors are welcome in the healing house, but certain areas — such as the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.khkwSR9UgOWenjGK]{Private Surgery} room and the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.NRXgT7OwVzJvyUBl]{Basement level} — are off-limits.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check confirms that the guard is speaking honestly within the limits of his station, and is more bored than suspicious.

Water Water Everywhere

Lucel may ask the characters to retrieve the bottle of @UUID[Item.XweVxnBoA5aDhoLa]{Waterborne Whiskey} from the Refectory and return it to him. He will also accept @UUID[Item.g3PuMlzSD8tEIYnQ]{Cindaric Mint Tea} from the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.uwR5BMezDhDx7oEc]{Infirmary} or the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.ox3u0apezmYTtHA8]{Alchemy} workshop.

In exchange for one of these substances, he palms them a [[/award party 5gp]], consumes the drink, and promptly settles in for a sound nap lasting [[/roll 1d4]] hours.

Care For a Game?

Lucel may ask the characters for a friendly game of Kingslayer. The game takes 1 hour. Any character that participates must make an opposed [[/skill Intelligence]] check against the Burnished Hand Protector's Intelligence score (10).

  • Characters that have proficiency with [[/skill sleightofhand]] or any game set gain @Advantage[2] on their check.

Regardless of the game's outcome, the guard grows more talkative: the next [[/skill Charisma]] check made to solicit information from him is made with @Advantage[2].

Operating Theater.name: Operating Theater
Operating Theater.text:
Tiered timber benches surround a central operating table, its surface scrubbed pale over years of use. Brass instruments are arranged neatly beside a clay basin stained russet by antiseptic tinctures, and the air smells faintly of iron and ammonia.

This spacious chamber serves as a teaching theater, where elder Cindarics and other specialists perform instructional operations for a congregation of students. Outsiders are permitted, but visitors are required to stay quiet during procedures (and will be asked to leave if they violate this rule more than once).

Main Quest: Spreading Sickness

If the party visits Traveler's Rest during the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness} main quest, the Operating Theater stands empty; all Cindarics are busy fighting the illness here and elsewhere in Ordain. Ignore any other encounters here until Spreading Sickness is concluded.

Exploring the Operating Theater

The Operating Theater contains nothing of interest outside of surgical demonstrations (see "Surgical Lesson" below).

Surgical Lesson

At your discretion, characters who enter this area during the day may find a precise and delicate surgery about to begin; they are welcome to take a seat amongst the students and watch. If they do, read the following:

Students settle along the tiered benches as Cindaric Adherents prepare the operating table below. One draws brass medical instruments from a basin of steaming water, laying them side by side on a ceramic tray, while another stands at the ready with clean boiled cloths. When all is prepared, the lead surgeon raises a hand for quiet and begins to speak.

Operation

Roll on (or choose from) the @UUID[RollTable.W7KjKplGCtbIZ6TA]{Surgery} table to determine which particular procedure is currently in progress.

No Interruptions

Characters who attempt to speak during the presentation are promptly shushed by a nearby student; characters who persist in being disruptive are asked to leave the theater.

Follow Along

A character who observes the operation for at least 1 hour and succeeds on a [[/skill intelligence 16]] check to follow along gains @Advantage[2] on their next [[/skill medicine]] check made to to treat a creature.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result 18+: The character also gains a point of Inspiration.

Private Surgery.name: Private Surgery
Private Surgery.text:
A single operating table sits in the center of this room, illuminated by a bright surgical lamp. Counters nearby hold carefully arranged tools, bottles, and folded cloths. A brass basin for washing instruments stands beside the table, and the sharp smell of antiseptic solutions pierces the air.

This chamber serves as the primary facility for patients in need of surgery, and is off-limits to visitors during all hours of the day unless they have express permission.

Locked & Off Limits

The doors to this chamber remain locked unless a surgical procedure is taking place. Each door can be unlocked with a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} or [[/skill tool=thief 15]] check; alternatively, it can be bashed open with a [[/skill athletics 22]] check.

Characters who are found in this area without permission (or a good reason) will be asked to leave Traveler's Rest, and may be barred from returning.

Main Quest: Spreading Sickness

If the party visits Traveler's Rest during the events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness} main quest, the Private Surgery room is unoccupied and emptied of supplies; all Cindarics are busy fighting the illness here and elsewhere in Ordain. Ignore any other encounters here until Spreading Sickness is concluded.

Exploring Private Surgery

A simple Search reveals the following: in addition to the room's surgical implements, the counters here are stocked with clean bandages, splints, brass needles, hemp sutures, and several stoppered vials of antiseptics.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 11]] check notices that one of the southwestern tables has been draped with a cloth, low enough to conceal something beneath it; a closer look reveals the corner of a small, locked medicine chest.

  • [[/path CindaricInitiate]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • The chest requires either a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} or a [[/skill tool=thief 15]] check to open. It contains the following items:

    • @UUID[Item.fg5EQMoBcsXYEGjv]{Alchemical Toxin}

    • @UUID[Item.TwsLk1KC8SqDbL8G]{Thieves' Lament}

    • @UUID[Item.ohX47gu4PvpL7Go5]{Heartward Elixir}

    • @UUID[Actor.WTvtYb0n8AGcSMPx.Item.ZpXFyzDlYr7XsbKv]{Potion of Greater Healing}

    • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll00]{Spell Scroll} based on the party's level:

      • Level 2: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll00] of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCureWounds]

      • Level 3: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll00] of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGentleRepo]

      • Level 4: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll00] of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDeathWard0]

Surgery in Progress

At your discretion, a surgery might be occurring here. Roll on (or choose from) the @UUID[RollTable.W7KjKplGCtbIZ6TA]{Surgery} table to determine which particular procedure is currently in progress.

Jessa's Private Quarters.name: Jessa's Private Quarters
Jessa's Private Quarters.text:
This cozy chamber is a curious amalgam of bedroom and study lounge, with more than enough space for a tiny gathering — a notion supported by the small couch at the foot of the bed. Ample tools, trinkets, and curios are stashed around the room, and an impressive model of Ember's cosmos serves as an eye-catching centerpiece.

This tool- and trinket-cluttered chamber serves as the private quarters of the Traveler's Rest head sage Jessa Aritou. For more information on Jessa, consult the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.pmuznacWe8MqqVYV]{Area Overview} or the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.nS7kj8wZ5eFq6pcy]{Westgate} gazetteer entry in the Ordain Gazetteer.

The kindhearted Jessa Aritou is a @UUID[Actor.uIDDak2Oq8Qd9Mfx]{Cindaric Sage} equipped with a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} and a @UUID[Item.HOL5fmggz6d8QMd4]{Traveler's Rest Basement Key}.

Locked & Off Limits

The doors to this chamber remain locked unless Jessa is present. Each door can be unlocked with a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key} or [[/skill tool=thief 15]] check; alternatively, it can be bashed open with a [[/skill athletics 22]] check.

Characters who are found in this area without permission (or a good reason) will be asked to leave Traveler's Rest, and may be barred from returning.

Exploring Jessa's Quarters

A simple Search reveals the following: the room's shelves, side tables, and cabinets are crowded with reference books, rolled charts, writing materials, tea tins, spare garments, and a careful assortment of tools and curios. Though eclectic, the chamber is orderly, and nothing here appears particularly strange.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 11]] check notices that the Ember cosmological model is not merely decorative, but articulated: the Elemental Moons have been manually aligned into a conjunction. @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi] reveals an aura of illusion magic surrounding the model.

A character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 20]] check while attempting to realign the cosmological model causes it to reconfigure itself into a small chest.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge cosmology]] or [[/knowledge stars]] have @Advantage[2] on their check.

Inside the chest is a plain silver band worth 25 gp and an ornate, leatherbound journal. Its pages contain appointment reminders, inventory notes (including items found in @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.iLFleFu8TBuc4oJw]{Basement Storage} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.cfqA38ekYHmEO2qb]{Downstairs Vestibule}), a few patient histories pulled from the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.oyEzM9ABnpfhuDsz]{Medical Archives}, and brief personal observations about patients, staff, and guests.

The chest automatically reconfigures itself into a cosmological model after 1 hour.

Basement Access

A staircase in the northwest corner of the room leads down to the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.cfqA38ekYHmEO2qb]{Downstairs Vestibule}.

Guest Quarters.name: Guest Quarters
Guest Quarters.text:
This cozy corner chamber is equipped with all the amenities of a homey bedroom, but remains sparsely decorated despite its comforting vibe.

Stocked with amenities and room to spare, this modest chamber serves as the guest quarters for short- and long-term visitors of Traveler's Rest. Guests are provided a footlocker here to store their belongings, but the small chest is unlocked (encouraging guests to provide their own).

The northern door here that exits into the streets of Ordain is locked, and can be opened with a @UUID[Item.kZwykfPodDT0n75g]{Traveler's Rest Key}.

Exploring the Chamber

A simple Search reveals the following: in addition to the usual comforts provided by Traveler's Rest, the room contains a wash basin, a folded spare blanket, a water pitcher and clay cup, and an unlocked footlocker for the current guest's belongings.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 11]] check notices a few personal effects left in plain view, their exact nature depending on whoever is currently staying here (see "Who Goes There?" below); describe one or two visible items that suit that guest.

  • Result of 15+: The character also notices an additional personal belonging, keepsake, or trinket on the current guest's person. This item should reinforce the guest's possible profession, recent travels, present hardship, or reason for staying at Traveler's Rest.

Who Goes There?

Roll on (or choose from) the @UUID[RollTable.sJK3abcGjb6IamDp]{Traveler's Rest Itinerant} table to determine who is currently staying in the Guest Quarters. They readily engage in conversation, revealing the following:

  • Where they most recently came from, where they expect to go next, or what business brought them to Ordain in the first place.

  • One additional personal detail appropriate to the current guest, such as their profession, recent hardship, notable possession, or local connection.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check confirms that the guest is mostly forthright (for a complete stranger), and that their stated reason for staying here is genuine.

Storage Closet.name: Storage Closet
Storage Closet.text:
This closet is crammed full of all sorts of supplies, including the telltale tools and equipment of the healers, surgeons, and apothecaries who work here. From wall to wall, well-used instruments and apparatuses sit beside or upon half-forgotten containers surrounded by clutter, suggesting a sense of haphazard convenience and utility.

This chamber serves as a storage closet, and contains a variety of supplies, tools, and equipment used by the Cindarics of Traveler's Rest.

Exploring the Closet

A simple Search reveals the following: the closet is full of practical supplies used throughout Traveler's Rest, including folded linens, empty chamber pots, spare tools, lamp oil, and other common necessities. Nothing stored here is especially valuable in isolation.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 12 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 10]] check notices that the shelves have been allowed to fall into mild disarray, with several items stacked out of place and a few smaller supplies in need of sorting.

Any character that spends 10 minutes reorganizing the storage closet discovers a single silver piece that had rolled beneath a shelf.

Light Work

Once the work is finished, the head sage Jessa Aritou takes notice of the unusual tidiness and conducts a personal inventory of the closet's contents, which takes [[/roll 1d4]] hours. Though slightly irritated by the unsolicited help, she offers the party a [[/award party 5sp]] for their labor — accompanied by a gentle admonishment not to touch the lodge's supplies.

Rear Storage Vestibule.name: Rear Storage Vestibule
Rear Storage Vestibule.text:
Half of this vestibule is crammed full of food stuffs — including sacks of grains, bushels of dried fruits and nuts, and barrels of water and wine — while the other half contains an assorted sundry of other items. A clear path cuts through the middle of the room, and the scuff marks on the floor near the northernmost door betray the function of this chamber as the delivery depot of Traveler's Rest.

Due to the exterior door positioned on the northern wall, this antechamber is used as a reception area for deliveries, and also serves as pantry storage for the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.mNaKv1ypsKYSypJx]{Refectory}.

Off Limits

The doors to this chamber remain unlocked, but the area is off limits: characters who are found in this area without permission (or a good reason) will be asked to leave Traveler's Rest, and may be barred from returning.

Exploring the Vestibule

A simple Search reveals the following: in addition to the foodstuffs stored here for the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.mNaKv1ypsKYSypJx]{Refectory}, the vestibule contains empty crates, wrapping twine, burlap sacks, and other mundane delivery supplies used to receive and sort incoming goods.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 13 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 11]] check notices a folded delivery manifest tucked onto a crate near the northern door. It lists a number of routine recent shipments; at your discretion, it may confirm where certain common supplies are usually stored within Traveler's Rest, as well as the contents of the locked medicine chest in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.khkwSR9UgOWenjGK]{Private Surgery} room.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the @UUID[Scene.emberBronzeRaskT] depicts the historic theater and the excavation behind it, as well as the events that transpire in the area as part of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness} quest events.

Normal Theater Use

If you want to use this theater as a place to visit for shows and portray it as an operational venue you can do so easily, but will need to ignore certain parts of the walkthrough text.

Specifically, ignore any text that relates to the Wandren and Mutagist plot as it relates to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200]{Spreading Sickness} quest event @UUID[JournalEntry.emberChainArc200.JournalEntryPage.N2kV75NY00Q4NqET]{Midnight Meeting}.

This includes the combat encounter, and placed enemies, and probably any opportunity to explore the backstage and tunnel areas of the map.

Environment

Situated in the city of Ordain, in the Fallbrook district, this multistory theater is old and regal, standing for several centuries, and has served as a center for the arts for generations of Ordani locals. The structure is made of white stone like the rest of Ordain, but features extensive wood construction inside, all of which was been relatively well maintained.

Ecology

The structure has issues with critters and insects living in the small places where one expects, but no plants or animals of note grow in this building.

Lore

Built several centuries ago, this is one of the older locations in Fallbrook. The theater has been known by several names, and has been home to hundreds of performers attempting to make a name for themselves or simply trying to entertain their fellow Ordani.

The stage has seen countless plays, concerts, and performances, and the theater's current name even stems from one such performance. The highly detailed bronze rask statue located in the lobby came to rest there as a result of a particularly impressive performance one night. A foreign noble in attendance was so struck, so delighted by the performers and their show that they gifted the troupe the immensely heavy statue as a show of appreciation.

Having nowhere else practical for the statue to go, it ended up in the lobby, and before long the theater's old name was forgotten as it was given a new moniker: The Bronze Rask.

In recent months the theater has been closed and disused, having been hired out by Brynna Vercocorte for "private use" which has displaced the local performers. The intent is to reopen the theater once Brynna's contract runs out on it, though won't be for some time.

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The following gameplay features apply to the Bronze Rask Theater area unless specifically stated otherwise in a specific room description.

Enemies

This area is currently occupied by a collection of House Wandren agents and some Mutagists on loan from the local contingent. They are gathered here for the upcoming meeting. The following enemies are encountered here in the provided approximate number:

  • @UUID[Actor.UVncdPqmzpZLwGvK]{Brynna Vercocorte}

  • 4 @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Wandren Patroller}

  • 2 @UUID[Actor.Q4dB8frYvdhTbUYk]{Wandren Watcher}

  • 2 @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14]{Wandren Tracer] (Variable)
  • 2 @UUID[Actor.lB0MpcO3fI3sbOww]{Mutagist Grenadier}

  • 6 @UUID[Actor.jZBVgCb2P61F9SrT]{Ordani Ruffian}

Nonlethal Methods

The combatants in this area are atempting to capture future prisoners, and are not striking with lethal intent. All characters and creatures reduced to 0 HP are incapacitated, but not killed or put into death saving throws.

Resting

It is not possible to take a Long Rest or Short Rest within this area due to the events unfolding.

Fleeing

Should the party need to flee the area, they may do so by retreating out of the theater and into the city streets beyond.

Captured

If the party is subdued in combat, they will be placed in a cage in the backstage area. Details for this outcome are presented in the encounter text.

Illumination

The theater is well lit with high mounted lamps and lanterns throughout. The backstage area features unique lanterns that glow with a pure white light, improving visibility in the area.

The tunnels and old passages behind the backstage area are lit unevenly by a handful of lanterns.

Terrain

Rubble and collapsed sections of the ruins in this scene serve as &reference[difficult terrain] for characters moving through such spaces.

Elevation

The theater has 20ft ceilings on the ground floor, and in the main theater room the vaulted ceiling reach up to 80ft at their highest.

In the dug out tunnels the space is a cramped 5ft in all directions, this includes the old water. The old passages and door chamber have 20ft ceilings.

Lobby.name: Lobby
Lobby.text:
As you enter the lobby you are met with a large bronze statue of a Rask standing upon a broad bronze base. Light catches on the polished ridges and intricate detail work on its muzzle and hammer-patterned fur. The metal bears no mark of abuse or age, clearly well cared for.

On either side of the lobby, ticket booths sit empty, behind the openings, shelves and cubbies wait in neat rows, now still and unused. To the left and right, stairways climb upward, and signs fixed to the newel posts point upward, plainly marking the way to the balcony.

Ahead, a pair of heavy double doors of dark wood marks the entrance to the theater proper. Brass push-plates gleam where hands have polished them smooth.

A pair of men stand in the lobby, watching you as you enter. Once the doors swing shut behind you one asks:

Will you submit like the rest?

You offer back the passphrase:

I will not be subordinate.

With that, the man gestures to the double doors, offering directions:

Take the doors into the theater, and get comfortable. There's food and drink, feel free to help yourself.

The lobby is guarded by a small team of Wandren guards.

Lobby Guards

Four @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Wandren Patrollers} guard the lobby. Two guard the main doors, and two block the stairs up to the lobby.

They are alert but not hostile unless they are provoked. When fighting begins in the theater they enter through the double doors.

There is little to see in the lobby, though the party can examine the bronze rask statue which the theater derives its name from.

The Bronze Rask

Characters with [[/culture emberOrdani]] and [[/knowledge arts]] know that the rask statue in the lobby was gifted to the theater several decades ago by a visiting noble or dignitary. Story goes that they were so impressed with the play put on here that they were compelled to give a gift, and so they commissioned a statue of their favorite animal. With nowhere else for it to go, the statue ended up in the lobby, and eventually the theater came to be known for it, which is how it ended up with its current name.

Characters without the above culture and knowledge combo must succeed on a [[/skill history 16]] skill check to know this information.

No Balcony Access

The balcony area of the theater will not be available until the release of Foundry VTT V14 and the inclusion of scene level technology. Until this time, consider the balcony closed for renovation and physically inaccessible.

A later encounter states that there are enemies on the balcony, they are instead found on the main stage for the time being.

Main Floor.name: Main Floor
Main Floor.text:
The theater hall descends in three sweeping terraces toward a central floor crowded with neatly ranked chairs. The hall holds a hush, broken only by the faint settling of old wood and creaking ropes in the rafters. The air carries the mellow scent of beeswax and polished wood.

Far above, the ceiling vaults upward, beyond the balcony overhead, past the hanging lamps that light the central space, and into the large, windowed cupola. Toward the stage, a network of ropes, beams and narrow walkways crisscross the open space.

Ahead, the stage waits, lit by gleaming gold sconces.

Encounter Details

Malevolent Main Course

Characters that ate or drank any of the food must instead make a [[/save con 16]] saving throw against a potent poison. Success leaves the character &reference[poisoned] for 10 minutes, while failure renders the character &reference[unconscious] for 1d10 hours.

Characters rendered unconscious by this poison immediately wake up if they suffer at least 1 hit point of damage from any source.

Choking Gas Bombs

The Ordani locals and Arcturian refugees in the basement will be unable to escape due to the immobilizing poison in the food and drink. Characters on the stage, like Brynna, are out of reach and remain safe as long as they stay up there.

Characters caught in the smoke must make a [[/save con 14]] to resist being &reference[blinded] and &reference[incapacitated] for 1 minute, but can repeat their save at the end of their turns. Successfully saving ends the effect.

This encounter also has a special macro to help with setup.

Group Hostility Macro

The @UUID[Macro.vVd3mpVRRCtUI0p1]{Subordinate Disposition} turns the Wandren actors and Ordani Ruffians hostile. Use this when the encounter begins and the enemies are revealed to the party.

Bad Eats

Plans and Poisons

The Mutagists are utilizing a two-part poison to subdue the party and civilians here for easy capture. The first part of the poison is in the food and drink, and has no immediate effect, but becomes activated when the Mutagists throw in gas bombs later.

The gas bombs themselves simply cause choking and partial blindness, but combined with the poison in the food, they create a powerful sleeping poison that renders most people unconscious.

For the commonfolk in the scene, this is immediately effective without saves, but the party is sturdier and will be able to make saves to resist the poison.

Encounter if Cover Intact

Crowd Control

The two @UUID[Actor.lB0MpcO3fI3sbOww]{Mutagist Grenadier} on loan to Brynna can wade into the toxic clouds without issue, and focus on placing @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagManacles000]{Manacles} on any creatures that are defeated or disabled by the poison. If engaged in combat they utilize their @UUID[Actor.lB0MpcO3fI3sbOww.Item.6gRu9IFFkvxesFfK]{Axe} to defend themselves, and avoid killing commonfolk or cityfolk. This courtesy is not extended to the party once they reveal themselves.

Riot Patrol

The largest fighting force consists of 4 x @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F]{Wandren Patrollers} that work in teams to capitalize on their @UUID[Actor.6nFbfFrRVb2lGW3F.Item.w0tpyk1wXaDk6B4W]{Pack Tactics} ability.

Their goal is to keep the crowd in the smoke so that it can do its work. The patrollers pull their attacks so as not to kill anyone, but are otherwise very rough with anyone trying to flee.

Upstage

@UUID[Actor.UVncdPqmzpZLwGvK]{Brynna Vercocorte} will hold per position on the stage and direct efforts from relative safety. However, if she's engaged in combat, she is a highly competent Wandren Tracer. Refer to the Hidden Blades section below for her combat tactics.

If half her forces are defeated by the party she will attempt to flee.

Overwatch

There are 2 x @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14]{Wandren Tracers} on the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.upXrX8Q8azmIheO9]{balcony} that begin selecting targets to fire at from above. They shoot to disable if possible.

Turncoats

The people that join Brynna and move near the stage avoid combat, but if forced to fight should be treated as @UUID[Actor.jZBVgCb2P61F9SrT]{Ordani Ruffians}. They fight using the simple weapons they carry, and attempt to surrender or flee if they are reduced to half their maximum hit points or less.

Encounter if Cover Blown

Hidden Blades

Use the above encounter, but add 3 x @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14]{Wandren Tracers} to the battle near the party. These nimble fighters use hit-and-run tactics via their @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.JKTF0NXaja99YP9N]{Cunning Action}, @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.qr0MMOlB2yqAreb0]{Nightstep}, and avoid harm using their @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.dNNI9bG6mobfYlvs]{Evasion} abilities.

They excel in close combat with @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.CjGEA68OpB1zPU0H]{Swift Stabs} from their short swords and @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.VeLwk0u9lcUuNQj6]{throwing knives}, both of which utilize their @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.d6iKYVL1LCzzYmla]{Sneak Attack} for increased damage and @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.Evy8YePEUTJaWRNV]{Limblock Toxin} to disable enemies.

They also favor dark environments, utilizing their @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14.Item.qr0MMOlB2yqAreb0]{Nightstep} ability to quickly teleport between shadows.

While these enemies are dedicated to the cause, they aren't willing to die for it, and use their speed and agility to flee the fight if either Brynna is defeated, or more than half their allies have fallen in battle.

Risk of Defeat

If The Party Fails

If the party entirely fails their saves and is immobilized, they will still have a chance to escape and turn things around. Have the party wake up in the cage found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.uzj35hSucpoZBaxm]{Backstage} area. They will be there along with some other commonfolk, and more are being brought in periodically.

The party is without their weapons and spell books (the items are nearby) but they have everything else the entered the theater with.

The heavy lock on the cage can be picked from either side of the cage, but is easier if done from the outside. A single successful [[/skill thief 16]] check is necessary to pick the lock. Attempting this from inside the cage is done with @Advantage[-2].

Alternatively, the party can wait for more prisoners to be brought in and attack when the cage is opened.

Searching the Aftermath

A Worrying Missive

A pair of letters addressed to Brynna can be found on her person once defeated. If she managed to escape they can instead be found on the writing desk found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.yRrp8TWhNsmHUQHt]{Makeup} area.

A successful [[/skill investigation 16]] determines that the paper, handwriting and ink are identical to each other. Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

If the characters still have the @UUID[Item.ycDGxabfXRXn12at]{Letter to Kaftor}, they will note it's also a match for the other two.

The First Letter

As promised, I've conferred with leadership and forwarded your proposal.

It was met with general approval, as expected. Therefore, you have clearance to send the majority of your new flock underground, after you supply the lab with sufficient human test subjects. They should be healthy and hearty, ideally.

I know you will want the most strong-backed of them, and that is fine. The lab needs survivors, not people who can fight back or rip themselves free of restraints. Sort your bodies accordingly!

Be aware that the Veiled Chain is attempting to uncover and disrupt both our operations, and are being especially tenacious in their efforts. I'm doing my best to throw them off, but expect undercover Veiled Chain operatives and hired adventurers.

I've forwarded descriptions and information on the party they have been relying on recently. Be aware of them, and make necessary preparations for their arrival.

Wisdom and cunning guide you.

The Second Letter

This letter lacks any signature or identifying marks, but is dated shortly after you raided the lab. The hand writing is identical to the first letter.

You have every reason to be concerned. The loss of the lab at the hands of the Veiled Chain has set us back substantially. However, I am personally taking steps to ensure that the Veiled Chain will no longer be a problem.

You simply need to deal with the undercover operatives the Chain has in play. Once you have done this, and the Chain is broken, we will be able to reopen the lab and continue our work with impunity.

As always,

Wisdom and cunning guide you.

Connection to Serethus

Serethus used the phrase "Wisdom and cunning guide you." when the party was breaking up after Ill Tidings. It's a minor connection that keen characters (and their players) might notice here.

Magic Armor

If Brynna was defeated in combat, a suit of magical @UUID[Actor.UVncdPqmzpZLwGvK.Item.6N2cHZD7anVMGHHN]{Studded Leather Armor +1} can be looted from her body. The leather is expertly made and died dark, and the metal studs are all a polished bronze, fitting the typical House Wandren style.

If Brynna escaped but you still want to award the party with this armor, you can place this armor on one of the other fallen Wandren fighters, or found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.1FxkcAs1EpdcswzG]{Wardrobe} area racks with a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check.

Balcony.name: Balcony
Balcony.text:
Seats line the balcony level which overlooks the whole of the theater. While not as close as the front rows, the view of the full stage is commanding, and in some ways superior. The seats are worn but well maintained here, and the slightly warm air is thick with the scent of polishing wax and oils.

No Balcony Access

The balcony area of the theater will not be available until the release of Foundry VTT V14 and the inclusion of scene level technology. Until this time, consider the balcony closed for renovation and physically inaccessible.

A later encounter states that there are enemies on the balcony, they are instead found on the main stage for the time being.

There is nothing of note to find in this upper area, however there are some archers present

Overwatch

There are 2 x @UUID[Actor.uwkC8q5jaZirnE14]{Wandren Tracers} on this balcony that are sitting together and talking. Before combat breaks out, they are not especially aware of their surroundings and easy enough to avoid.

If alerted, or when combat breaks out below, they separate and begin selecting targets to fire at.

Long Fall

The distance from the balcony to the theater floor below is 40ft, and deals [[/damage 4d6 bludgeoning]] damage to any character that jumps or falls off the balcony.

Stage.name: Stage
Stage.text:
The broad wooden stage stands in full view of both levels of the theater, with not even a curtain to provide cover. To either side of the stage props and decorations sit in haphazard piles, as though the venue was never fully reset after the last performance concluded.

There is not much to be found on the stage aside from some discarded props and tools.

Pointless Props

The various props and decorations on the stage are flimsy and cheap, worth nothing in terms of coin, and all but worthless if used in combat. At best they could serve as basic improvised bludgeons but wouldn't survive one or two uses before breaking.

Characters may notice a large trap door in the stage floor while on the stage. This trap door starts closed, but if opened, becomes a combat hazard.

Stage Fall

There is a large trap door in the stage. Spotting this trap requires a successful [[/skill perception 14]] and there is no obvious mechanism for triggering or opening it on the stage.

This trap door links to a passage that leads directly to the iron cage found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.uzj35hSucpoZBaxm]{Backstage} area.

Climbing out of the passage back up to the stage requires a successful [[/skill athletics 16]] or [[/skill acrobatics 16]] check. This is impossible if the trapdoor is closed.

Backstage.name: Backstage
Backstage.text:
The expansive backstage area encompasses the whole back quarter of the theater, and is packed with items needed to run the various performances held here. Overhead props and decorations hang from ropes and hooks, ready to be lowered when needed.

Two things are immediately strange about this space:

First, a section of stone wall has fallen inward. Pale dust veils and rubble lies on the floor and just beyond the cracked masonry gapes a dark tunnel and freshly pulverized stone.

Second, at the center of this area stands a huge iron cage. Its bars are thick and riveted to a square frame bolted straight into the wooden floor which is covered in scrape marks indicating it was dragged into place recently. A heavy lock hangs on the double door’s hasp.

This note provides an overview of the space. For detailed information on specific areas, see the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.1FxkcAs1EpdcswzG]{Wardrobe} and @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.yRrp8TWhNsmHUQHt]{Makeup} pages.

Cagey Addition

A successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check notes fresh scrapes and gouges on the floor. This would indicate that the cage was recently brought in and installed, and not a normal part of the backstage area.

The heavy lock on the cage can be picked from either side of the cage, but is easier if done from the outside. A single successful [[/skill thief 16]] check is necessary to pick the lock. Attempting this from inside the cage is done with @Advantage[-2].

Exterior.name: Exterior
Exterior.text:
You stand beneath a canopy of bright banners in red, gold, blue, and purple. Their patterned cloth stretches from building to building over white cobblestone streets worn smooth by countless steps.

The street flows around a tall, white-bricked building. Above the double doors hangs a plain wooden placard, its letters simple and firm:

The Bronze Rask Theater

The theater’s facade rises at least two stories, each course of large white bricks stacked with careful order, and capped with a roof of weather worn violet tiles. The building appears to be one of the older structures in the area, but has been well cared for over its lifetime.

The front doors are unlocked, and the party can enter at will.

A Historic Theater

Characters with [[/culture emberOrdani]] and [[/knowledge arts]] are aware that this theater has been known by several names over the years, and is one of the oldest theaters in the city, having stood for over four centuries now. It has passed through many hands, and has been home to countless acting troupes, and was renovated several times over the years. Once it was known as the City Center Theater, when Ordain was much smaller.

Characters without the above culture and knowledge combo must succeed on a [[/skill history 17]] skill check to know this information.

Side Entrance.name: Side Entrance
Side Entrance.text:
The long alley here terminates at a double door entrance at the side of the theater. A brightly painted sign declares:

Private entrance.

Cast and staff only.

Not for theater guests.

This entrance is locked, but would allow the party to enter the backstage area directly.

Locked Up

The side door features a hefty and fairly modern lock. A successful [[/tool thief 18]] check is necessary to bypass the lock. Each attempt takes several minutes.

Breached Waterway.name: Breached Waterway
Breached Waterway.text:
Water flows rapidly though this narrow, forgotten channel, the sound of it reverberating off the wet brick, and filling the space with noise. Though the water is clean and clear, the accumulated grime and mildew on the damp stone is impossible to ignore and hints that this waterway has sat forgotten and unmaintained for quite some time.

Up ahead light spills out on the stained white stone from another hole in the wall.

There is nothing of note to find in this space, but the slick, noisy environment does present its own issues characters need to be wary of.

Slippery When Wet

Moving through this tunnel faster than a walk speed requires a successful [[/save dexterity 14]] or else the character slips and falls prone.

White Noise

The flowing water is especially loud. Characters attempting to make perception checks related to hearing while inside this tunnel have @Advantage[-2].

Forgotten Passage.name: Forgotten Passage
Forgotten Passage.text:
This broad passage is built of the same white stone as the rest of Ordain, but it all seems older and worn by comparison. The floors are lined with piles of rubble, broken tiles fallen from the ceiling, and wrapped in cobwebs.

The hall is empty otherwise, with only a trio of lanterns to light the way.

Though there's nothing of value to find in the passage aside from rubble, bricks, and stone.

Old Stone

Characters that examine the passage and make a successful [[/skill history 16]] check know that Ordain is a city that was built up over centuries and features layers of passages, old streets, forgotten aqueducts and more that were built over as the city expanded.

Characters with the [[/culture emberOrdani]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Sealed Doorway.name: Sealed Doorway
Sealed Doorway.text:
This passage, half collapsed on one side, expands out into a large chamber of white stone that reaches from floor to ceiling. Each block is perfectly cut and set then polished smooth.

Time has not been kind to this space, as cracks have formed throughout the walls and ceilings, and fixtures have suffered damage from falling stone slabs. Curiously, much of the rubble has been moved aside and collected into piles.

At the end of the space a massive white stone door spans one side of this area, its face gilded with old bronze or gold metal.

Two figures in mining gear and wearing illuminated helmets stand before the massive door, idly chatting with each other. Their voices echo off the stone, words becoming indistinct in the process.

Examining the Chamber

Ancient Chamber

Characters that examine the chamber recognize that it might be the oldest stone encountered so far. A successful [[/skill history 16]] theorizes that this chamber might have been part of some of the earliest of Ordain's construction, and is several centuries old. The area has likely been long forgotten, built over and lost due to collapse.

Characters with the [[/culture emberOrdani]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Gilded Barrier

Characters attempting to open the door note that it is sealed and will not budge no matter how hard one might try. Attempting to cast portal opening spells such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplKnock00000]{Knock} are also entirely ineffective.

A successful [[/skill investigation 15]] check notes that there are no obvious or hidden mechanisms by which to open the door. It is possible the door only opens from the other side.

A successful [[/skill religion 16]] check on the gilded door recognizes an exceptionally old symbol once used by the first Cindaric Sages, meaning this door is at least as old as the organization is.

Characters with [[/path emberCindaricInitiate]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

speaking to the Miners

The miners are Donak and Karnt, they are Arcturians both, and former residents of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.9jlnhyRR3otAltgs]{Arcturel}. They were put out of work due the actions of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.y7o8dKT1yxdnh2Pz] and the events that eventually lead up to the @UUID[JournalEntry.m6P3pXWB3ssdG7o3] quest.

The miners have no interest in fighting and if threatened will surrender immediately, preferring to be taken to the Hallows rather than risk being killed by a group of armed assailants.

Unlucky Landmovers

These miners are unwitting accomplices of of Brynna Vercocorte, house Wandren and the Mutagists. They were paid to do a dubious job, and know nothing about the events going on.

They are innocent bystanders caught in this mess, and had Brynna's plans gone as expected, they would have been scooped up and captured like all the other commonfolk in the theater.

Temporary Presence

Note that if the party leaves the theater after the Midnight Meeting event without speaking to the miners first, they will be gone on any return visits.

The party may want to speak with or question the miners, the following topics are relevant to the area map.

Who hired you?

Brynna Vercocorte. She wanted us to dig through to a chamber, this one, I guess! Been working on it for weeks now, most of the time was spent trying to get through the basalt. Only just broke through a little while ago.

We've got legit work order papers and everything, not on us, but we insisted on them.

Why are you hanging around?

Brynna told us to hang tight down and that she'd be along with our payment. It's been a bit though, we were discussing if we should just go and hit her up for payment later, or something.

Are you with House Wandren?

No way! We used to work out in Arcturel, but lost our jobs after the Silver Beam consortium moved in and started buying up the mines and bringing in their own crew. We've been taking whatever rock and stone jobs come up since.

Do you know anything about the Mutagists?

Who? You mean the creeps in the masks? Nah, they've been lurking around for a bit now, we keep well clear of them. The way they look at you, it's like you're meat to be carved up, not a person.

What do you know about the chamber and door?

Nothin'. It's the same white stone as the rest of the ruins, and most of Ordain, at that. It's not local stone, so it was quarried elsewhere. Again, like the rest of Ordain.

The symbol on the door is weird, and there's no way to open it that we're aware of, not that we were asked to. But we did get curious and see, all the same.

Flyspace.name: Flyspace
Flyspace.text:
Just off of stage right, this space is sparse, featuring nothing more than a row of ropes connected to the overhead pulley system that allows stagehands to control suspended props and decorations above. The space is otherwise empty, possibly left open so that the nearby side entrance can be used to bring things in and out of the theater easily.

Characters entering the theater from the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.Vx7bbrr9qeJwqNe4] will find themselves here, and might have a chance to sneak up on an unaware enemy.

Waiting Enemy

A single @UUID[Actor.lB0MpcO3fI3sbOww]{Mutagist Grenadier} is waiting here for a signal to head onto the stage. They are bored and not paying attention to their surroundings, and could be avoided by a stealthy party.

When the time comes, they head out onto the stage to help subdue the crowd collected in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.sU8YWzkfl82nM0R6]{Main Floor} area.

Prop Drop

The ropes tied off here can be cut or untied with an action to drop hanging props on creatures in this area. This can be done three times, and the targeted creature must make a successful [[/save dexterity 14]] or suffer [[/damage 3d6 bludgeoning]] damage as the prop lands on them.

Storage.name: Storage
Storage.text:
Just off of stage left, this space holds numerous large wooden crates likely packed with unneeded costumes and props waiting for their time to shine. Set along the wall is a row of ropes connected to the overhead pulley system that allows stagehands to control suspended props and decorations above.

Not easily visible from the main floor, a mutagist agent is hidden behind the curtains here.

Waiting Enemy

A single @UUID[Actor.lB0MpcO3fI3sbOww]{Mutagist Grenadier} is waiting here for a signal to head onto the stage. They are bored and not paying attention to their surroundings, and could be avoided by a stealthy party.

When the time comes, they head out onto the stage to help subdue the crowd collected in the @UUID[JournalEntry.BJZy9DJnRXYY6dim.JournalEntryPage.sU8YWzkfl82nM0R6]{Main Floor} area.

Prop Drop

The ropes tied off here can be cut or untied with an action to drop hanging props on creatures in this area. This can be done three times, and the targeted creature must make a successful [[/save dexterity 14]] or suffer [[/damage 3d6 bludgeoning]] damage as the prop lands on them.

The party can also search the area if they want.

Prop Hunt
