The boxes are filled with all sorts of items, including costumes, stage weapons, prop jewelry, decorative items and set dressing elements. These items are all dusty and haven't seen use in quite a while.

None of the items appear to hold any particular value, and there are no notable items to be found within.

Wardrobe.name: Wardrobe
Wardrobe.text:
Along the far wall, long racks hold dozens of costumes outfits, from ornate dresses to archaic armors, and every accessory one might need in between. A nearby tailoring station allows for quick fixes and alterations.

Characters may want to dig through the racks and chests here to find items, though there is very little of value to be found.

Off the Rack

There is a broad selection of outfits, dresses, uniforms, and stage armors hanging from these racks. While all of them exhibit considerable style and care in their design, none of them appear to especially valuable or unique.

Hidden in the Chest

A character searching the various chests in the wardrobe area finds container of jewelry. A successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check finds a real piece among all the prop pieces, yielding a @UUID[Item.jrwsTQ5IqAZQvMWc] that might be worth some money if sold.

Characters will want to explore the collapsed section of wall and see where it leads.

A Hole in the Wall

The old stone of the wall has been torn out and smashed, revealing the raw basalt stone behind it.

A character with [[/knowledge subterranea]], [[/knowledge crafts]], [[/knowledge warfare]] or succeeding on a [[/skill investigation 14]] check recognizes that the wall was smashed fast and with no regard for rebuilding the wall later.

Makeup.name: Makeup
Makeup.text:
A pair of vanity tables sit ready for cast members to dress themselves up, each one covered in collections of brushes and bundles of makeup, and featuring a large mirror.

A writing desk is scattered with papers sits nearby, covered in papers, pens, and ink bottles. A small pile of letters and a scattering of written pages sit untouched on the desk as well.

The party may want to search the tables. The vanities hold nothing of note, but the writing desk may lend insight, and hold damning evidence depending on how events played out elsewhere in the theater.

Vanities

The vanity tables feature large mirrors and assorted collections of brushes and makeups. Most of them are on the older side, and probably in need of replacing.

Writ Large

The desk features various pens, quills, ink bottles and several pages of half-finished scenes for a play. A bundle of letters sits on the top of the desk next to a tray of letters. All of them appear to be addressed to the theater or their local troupe.

Characters interested in looking through the letters may find something interesting.

Fan Mail

If a character opens any of the letters, they find various letters addressed to the playwright, actors, or the theater at large. Each letter thanks them for their performances, or critiques some aspect of a play or skit. While interesting to read, there is nothing of importance to find in the letters.

Letters of Complaint

One bundle of letters are comprised entirely of missives complaining about the theater shutting down, shows being cancelled, and disappointment over the Bronze Rask being closed to the public for "private use."

Some of the letters are especially mean spirited, and all of them are addressed to the owner, one Dory Doss.

Agreement with Brynna

A character that searches the drawers of the desk will find a series of letters on House Wandren stationery. They are all addressed to Dory Doss, and goes over a long-term contract with her to purchase exclusive use of the theater.

The letters are only one side of the conversation but a successful [[/skill insight 14]] check gleans that Dory Doss was especially dogged in their negotiation with Brynna, working the price up as high as possible to ensure the theater and its displaced troupe would be taken care of during the hiatus.

Characters with [[/knowledge arts]] or [[/knowledge trade]] or making a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check recognize that the amount being paid by Brynna is likely far in excess of what this theater would normally make, and would ensure its operation long-term.

Irregular Tunnel.name: Irregular Tunnel
Irregular Tunnel.text:
The stone has been hastily chipped and broken away, the iron-hard basalt having been removed on a meandering path likely determined by least resistance rather than engineered plan.

The tunnel breaks through stone and brick into a new area up ahead.

This tunnel stands in for both of the dug-out tunnels located in this scene. Their qualities are identical, and characters studying one tunnel will note the same traits in the other tunnel without needing to roll.

Fast and Messy

A character with [[/knowledge subterranea]], [[/knowledge crafts]], [[/knowledge warfare]] or succeeding on a [[/skill investigation 14]] check recognizes that the digging was done fast and messy, with little regard for typical mining processes or good tunnel engineering.

Whoever dug this was taking the path of least resistance while still trying to aim in a specific direction. The work to excavate the tunnel that lies ahead likely took days if not weeks.

A successful [[/skill nature 14]] check notes that the stone around Ordain is basalt, a notoriously resilient stone that can be harder than iron. Digging through it could not have been easy.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the Ember's Bounty trade vessel depicts a commercial sector of the ship's main deck, where several vendors and places of business are established alongside recreational facilities and private storage. This hybrid landscape of crowded interior and exterior locations will serve as the key scenery for the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL]{Diplomatic Impunity} quest event known as @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.Fe4QZwpNc5lyppA1]{Parcels and Pirates}.

  • This map represents one small public section of the Ember's Bounty, with a particular focus on the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.kJBS8IrjMT2yaopq]{Game Room}, where the party's encounter with the pirate lord @UUID[Actor.217UQNTaajO2MIBq]{Gastern Faviyos} takes place.

  • The standard method of entry to this section of the ship is via the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.mq8SQSmhGuofdUoy]{Cargo Lift} situated near the bottom left corner of the map.

  • Additional info and mechanics regarding the various chambers of this section of the ship are located in the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB]{Gameplay Details} section of this walkthrough.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.OGwqwpjpXueYnloV inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
A naval ship so large it serves as a city district, the Ember's Bounty is known far and wide as the mobile domain of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}, and plays host to a wide variety of obtainable goods and services for the enterprising people of Ordain. The Ember's Bounty is a boisterous place, where action and opportunity lurks around every corner — and this modest swathe of the upper deck is no exception.

Objectives

The characters will journey to this section of the Ember's Bounty in search of the nefarious pirate lord @UUID[Actor.217UQNTaajO2MIBq]{Gastern Faviyos}, who has already been paid to hand over some equipment to the party for delivery to @UUID[Actor.yztzqRozoEkbiO2K]{Katerin Bastilla}. While they're aboard the famed House Bastilla vessel, the characters can:

  • Take advantage of the location's various amenities, including leisure and entertainment as well as trade.

  • Meet some of the locals and gain insight into their assorted lives, including their relative affiliations with House Bastilla and Ordain at large.

  • Meet with the chaotic Gastern and his @UUID[Actor.Ipca55bI0vc7yCLZ]{Wind Raider} allies in the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.kJBS8IrjMT2yaopq]{Game Room} to secure the equipment for Katerin, which will require a measure of negotiation (if not outright combat).

Most of the characters that populate this area map exist here with or without the presence of Gastern and his cronies. If the party wishes to revisit the area, locations and encounters remain generally the same as described within the body of this walkthrough, with the only notable exception being the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.kJBS8IrjMT2yaopq]{Game Room} — which is similar in most aspects, but no longer serves as the temporary headquarters of Gastern and his allies.

Local Rules & Regulations

By edict of Katerin Bastilla herself, the denizens of the Ember's Bounty must abide by three simple rules: no stealing, no killing, and no damaging of the ship.

Any character who breaks one or more of the three rules will be thrown overboard by 6-12 @UUID[Actor.7z8CVE7r4cQtlJKI]{House Bastilla Sailors} who arrive to the scene within [[/roll 1d2+1]] rounds. Acts of murder are likely subject to greater penalties, with individual punishments based on the specific circumstances at hand.

Characters thrown overboard are placed on a watchlist and denied subsequent entry if they attempt to board the ship in the future. The full rules for falling overboard are featured below in the Elevation section of this page.

Illumination

Interior areas of the Ember's Bounty are lit by mundane lanterns, which are situated throughout the ship at various intervals. Most of these lanterns are fueled by lantern oil, although a scattered few are known to be lit by inkaro pearls. Unless otherwise stated, these lanterns shed bright light in a 10 foot radius and dim light for another 10 feet. Meanwhile, table lamps like those in the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.kJBS8IrjMT2yaopq]{Game Room} shed their own bright light in a 5 foot radius, casting dim light for another 5 feet.

Exterior sections of the Ember's Bounty (including the exposed areas of the main deck featured on this map) are lit by moonlight, which counts as dim light (unless otherwise dictated by weather conditions).

Terrain

The hardwood floors of the Ember's Bounty are crafted from planks of Arcturian oak, cedar, and pine. The ground here should be treated as normal terrain unless otherwise noted. The interior walls of the ship are crafted from similar hardwoods.

The ship's doors are made of reinforced oak (AC 17, 25 HP, DC 16 to open), and are unlocked unless otherwise stated. When ship doors do happen to be locked throughout the Ember's Bounty — whether this deck or otherwise —the associated lock complexity most often ranges from Good (DC 15 to unlock) to Superior (DC 20), with a few higher-difficulty exceptions.

Elevation

The ceilings of the various cabins and chambers located throughout the Ember's Bounty are 15 feet high, unless otherwise stated. The northernmost flooring of the exterior deck is situated 5 feet higher than the central section of the deck, which is readily accessible via the short flights of steps that connect them.

Cargo Hold Pits

The two pits on the map depict open-air access to a large cargo deck located 40 feet below. Any character who happens to fall into one of these pits must succeed on either a [[/skill acrobatics 16]] or [[/skill athletics 16]] check to catch the railing as they tumble over it, taking [[/damage 4d6 bludgeoning]] damage on a failure.

Any characters who fall into the cargo hold this way can return to the main deck via the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.mq8SQSmhGuofdUoy]{Cargo Lift}, which takes the character a total of [[/roll 1d2 + 1]] turns. Alternately, characters with a fly speed can navigate the distance between the cargo deck and the main deck more directly.

The wooden railing that lines the edges of the ship's deck is 4 feet high. Meanwhile, the network of ropes that hang above the exposed areas of the main deck are suspended roughly 10-15 feet high above the wooden planks of the floor.

Falling Overboard

Any character who is thrown overboard immediately falls at least 60 feet into the roiling waters of the ocean below, and must succeed on a [[/skill acrobatics 15]] or [[/skill athletics 15]] check to avoid taking [[/damage 3d6 bludgeoning]] damage. On a successful check, any damage resulting from the fall is halved.

Mechanical Lift.name: Mechanical Lift
Mechanical Lift.text:
Reinforced with corroded steel hardware, this creaky wooden lift sways ever-so-slightly as it rumbles into position on the upper deck of the ship. Trademark scents of rust and sea-spray mingle with the smells of aromatic smoke and savory foods, which waft throughout the nooks and crannies of the main deck like eager visitors at a party.

This sizable elevator is constructed from timber and steel, and provides general access to the main deck from the cargo hold located 40 feet below.

Using the Lift

The lift can be manipulated by the use of a hardwood wheel located on its westernmost edge, and is powered by an intricate and mostly unseen network of pulleys and hoists.

Any character who wishes to use the lift to journey from the cargo hold to the main deck (or vice versa) must use a standard action to successfully manipulate the device. Unless otherwise stated by encounter conditions, the lift takes a full round to relocate between these two positions.

Additional lower decks of the ship can be accessed via the lift, but are relatively inconsequential to the events of @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.Fe4QZwpNc5lyppA1]{Parcels and Pirates}.

Perlin's Powders.name: Perlin's Powders
Perlin's Powders.text:
The smell of incense greets you as you step into this cozy retail cabin, which is lined with shelves full of various alchemical reagents and spell components. These curious goods — which include everything from rose petals to powdered silver — are packed into countless jars, urns, boxes, and vials, all decorated with handwritten labels.

A young Arcturian woman scrawls the latest tag on a stubby glass vial, barely peeking up above her work to address you with staccato detachment.

Welcome to Perlin's Powders. Perlin at your service! How can I help you?

Perlin Prest (Neutral Good, Arcturian Human, she/her) is the studious proprietor of Perlin's Powders, a shop that sells arcane spell components and alchemical reagents of a rather wide (and widely-sourced) variety.

Perlin's Wares

Characters who wish to purchase spell components from Perlin are able to do so with relatively little fanfare. Perlin has a matter-of-fact attitude about her inventory, and has nearly any spell component a character could need worth 500 gp or less. Additional items include the following crafting components:

  • @UUID[Item.7ltA4b7LI3KqyKfS]{Cheliceraeth Eyes}

  • @UUID[Item.NeBAxUn3WJJHrv3q]{Crag Raptor Feathers}

  • @UUID[Item.XewoieHSHYTb5C0t]{Spider-cap Mushrooms}

  • @UUID[Item.Va3es1V2Xf624fmd]{Quickwater}

If a character is persistent about an item worth more than 500 gp, Perlin is happy to offer a suggestion about where they might find it (given they actually purchase something in the process).

No matter how hard a character tries, Perlin won't budge on her prices (requiring the intervention of magic or similar methods to sway her mind).

The Armory.name: The Armory
The Armory.text:
The smell of boiled linseed oil and full-grain leather rush to greet you as you step into this elaborately-outfitted armory, which appears to feature all manner of weapons and armor on its ample shelves. A mustachioed House Bastilla sailor polishes a broadsword as you enter, nodding your way as if to say "let me know if you need something" without actually making the effort.

The simply-named Armory is the main deck's primary weapon and armor storage facility, and also caters to crew members and visitors alike with the sale of surplus (and often confiscated) goods.

The gruff sailor who usually attends this place is Hewson Elexios (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, he/him), a seasoned veteran who simply can't be bothered — by anything. Sarcasm and buffoonery are met with swift and pragmatic condemnation, often at the low cost of someone's pride.

The Armory's Wares

A wide array of weapons and armor are available for sale here, including nearly all of those listed in the corresponding @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000] tables.

Weapons and armor that are confiscated during infractions of the "Local Rules & Regulations" described in @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB]{Gameplay Details} are eventually brought here for refurbishment and resale. At least one-third of the inventory here hails from confiscated or abandoned equipment.

Barrel Room.name: Barrel Room
Barrel Room.text:
This dim and dusty cabin is stocked full of barrels, kegs, and bottles — presumably full of alcohol and food stuffs (if the lingering smell of rum and dried fruits can be trusted).

This cabin serves as the storehouse for the Game Room nearby, and is closed to the public. It's stocked full, with enough barrels full of ale, wine, and liquor to keep the main deck inebriated for a week.

The heavy oaken door is locked (AC 20, 30 HP, DC 18 to open), and can be unlocked using a @UUID[Item.zohLqrx3ZeWClKAy]{Barrel Room Key} — found nearby in the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.kJBS8IrjMT2yaopq]{Game Room} scullery.

Barrel Room Inventory

Any character who takes a moment to search the room can readily find a bottle of @UUID[Item.jnKYsmCYNNP21aYF]{Seawall Brandy} or @UUID[Item.4mIj4qrLgMompEZG]{Arcturian Liquor} they can easily abscond with. If a character attempts to take more than one bottle, they might raise the ire of crew members who spot their illicit bounty of beverages.

The Game Room.name: The Game Room
The Game Room.text:
Stepping into this large, smoke-filled cabin invites an assault on the senses. The dim glow of lantern light is painted with the hazy tint of cigar fumes and close-quarters humidity, and you find yourself drowning in a cacophony of noise — including everything from the clinking of glass and shuffling of cards, to the squeaking of furniture and the din of idle chatter. Above it all, the melodious sound of a piano dances towards you from the northern end of the room, where a moody bard plays some half-forgotten tune.

Several world-weary faces turn to examine your group as you make your way into this crowded chamber, which is packed with all manner of patrons, crew and visitors like. Sailors sit shoulder-to-shoulder with landlubbers in search of good times or easy money; and (if the far-flung accents and curious atmosphere are any indication) everyone here has a story to tell.

The Game Room is the veritable centerpiece of this section of the main deck, and provides a lush environment for patrons to while away their extra hours — with activities like eating, drinking, gaming, gambling, and the occasional musical performance taking the spotlight.

The crowd here is comprised of assorted @UUID[Actor.7z8CVE7r4cQtlJKI]{Arcturian Sailors}, @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani Cityfolk}, and @UUID[Actor.jZBVgCb2P61F9SrT]{Ordani Ruffians}, who are engaged in the Game Room's activities to varying degrees. Meanwhile, the cabin is attended at all times by a work staff that includes: a trio of Bartenders, two Cooks, and a rotating cadre of Card Dealers (all of which are Arcturian Sailors employed by @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.JOQCjyaSIPRhrEd6]{House Bastilla}).

Carousing

The Game Room is open for business 24 hours a day, and has a modest assortment of drinks and food available for purchase. The drinks are watered down, and the meals are dubious, but the prices are reasonable.

Although a variety of minstrels and performers are known to play here, the musician most commonly associated with the room's piano is a playfully sardonic bard named Robbi Mars (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, he/him).

If the party wishes to gather information, any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 15]] check is able to round up some details relatively pertinent to the task at hand in @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.Fe4QZwpNc5lyppA1]{Parcels and Pirates}, including:

  • The precise location of @UUID[Actor.217UQNTaajO2MIBq]{Gastern Faviyos} and his @UUID[Actor.Ipca55bI0vc7yCLZ]{Wind Raider} crewmen, seated at a square card table in the darkened northwest corner of the room.

  • Information about the various vendors and crewmen stationed throughout this particular section of the main deck (the cabins featured on the area map and beyond), along with details about their associated shops and services.

  • Unsubstantiated rumors pertaining to House Bastilla and various districts of Ordain (per Gamemaster discretion, based on whatever quests or events are active for the PCs at the time).

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Games of Chance

Several games of skill and chance are available to play here in the Game Room, including backgammon, poker, and dominos (among other, more regional games).

Characters who wish to engage in these games of chance can do so at their leisure. Finding an opponent is easy, as someone is always willing to play, and gambling is often encouraged (even, if not especially, when it's a match between close friends or associates).

You can allow the characters to play these games in real time if the activity suits your table. However, you should also feel free to utilize the following Gambling Skill Challenge as an approximation to expedite these supplementary moments.

  • Any character who attempts to win a game of chance must succeed on 3 out of 5 skill checks, chosen from the following list of potential checks: [[/skill deception 15]], [[/skill insight 15]], [[/skill investigation 15]], [[/skill perception 15]], [[/skill sleightofhand 15]].

  • Each skill check can only be attempted once. The player character chooses the skill for the first check, followed by the opponent's choice of the second skill check; participants continue alternating (with either the PC or the NPC choosing the skill at hand) until win or lose.

  • Betting is handled between the participants, with no oversight from the House Bastilla crew stationed nearby. Altercations, however, are dealt with per the "Local Rules & Regulations" described in the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB]{Gameplay Details} section of this area walkthrough.

Kitchen Supplies

Any character who takes the time to search the Game Room's scullery to the southeast (without getting caught) and succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] check is able to find a @UUID[Item.zohLqrx3ZeWClKAy]{Barrel Room Key}, which unlocks the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.xlo5aV0beGpvleTV]{Barrel Room} located to the west nearby.

Varlo's.name: Varlo's
Varlo's.text:
Dim lantern light cascades upon the cluttered tables of this small dining hall, where an array of hearty food has been prepared for its patrons. Your mouth waters at the smell of grilled fish and fresh bread as you linger in the doorway, and a bright-eyed server brushes past you with a steamy eel pie on his arm — piping hot and straight from the oven.

The aforementioned bright-eyed server is none other than Varlo himself (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him). Varlo the Eleventh to be precise — the youngest (and currently last) of the Varlo line.

The food offered in here Varlo's dining hall is of fairly low quality but is reliably abundant. Young Varlo is still mastering his trade, and he has a lot to learn. Quite comically, all complaints can be addressed to his father, Varlo the Tenth (who is notoriously deceased).

A burgeoning entrepreneur, Varlo is known to offer his fellow vendors aboard the Ember's Bounty vouchers for free meals, in the hopes that new customers are around every corner. Of course, the meals provided by these coupons are the cheapest on the menu.

Varlo's Wares

The meals here consist of standard Arcturian and Ordani fare, and range from Poor (at 2 cp) to Wealthy (at 3 sp). Additionally, Varlo has a small supply of non-perishable @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagRations0000]{Rations} for sale.

Boxing Ring.name: Boxing Ring
Boxing Ring.text:
A melange of blood and sweat paints the canvas of this small boxing ring, where two bareknuckle brawlers are engaged in a one-on-one boxing match. As these two pugilists wage their mock battle, a crowd of spectators cheer and jeer with reckless abandon, clutching pouches of coin in eager anticipation of a win.

The boxing ring here is run by Burl Havoc (Chaotic Good, Ordani Kiska, he/him), a professional fighter who also serves as an erstwhile boatswain for smaller House Bastilla ships. A formidable opponent in his own right, Burl is known as a Kiska of few words.

The fights here are all unarmed, and contestants brawl until one of them is knocked out. Murder is frowned upon, and offenders are either immediately thrown overboard (per the "Falling Overboard" rules described in @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB]{Gameplay Details}) or put to the sword by House Bastilla sailors. Gambling is encouraged, and nearly everyone bets.

Part of the Action: Betting

Characters can bet on matches between other boxers, with the Gamemaster running a quick nonlethal combat simulation between two NPCs. Chose any combination of two contestants from the following: @UUID[Actor.7z8CVE7r4cQtlJKI]{Arcturian Sailor}, @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani Cityfolk}, or @UUID[Actor.jZBVgCb2P61F9SrT]{Ordani Ruffian}.

The rules are simple: the first character to knock out their opponent (by reducing them to 1 Hit Point and giving them the Unconscious condition) wins.

Part of the Action: Boxing

Characters can participate in the boxing themselves if so desired, but must doff all armor and fight using unarmed, nonlethal combat with their bare hands.

The rules are simple: the first character to knock out their opponent (by reducing them to 1 Hit Point and giving them the Unconscious condition) wins.

Winners claim a small percentage of earnings from the house for each match they win, which results in an average of [[/roll 1d10]] x 10 sp per match (unless the party engages in even higher bets on the match themselves).

Secondhand Rugs.name: Secondhand Rugs
Secondhand Rugs.text:
You regard a large pile of rugs and carpets, many of which appear rather dusty and worn, with frayed edges and furtive stains. However, few of the textiles here do look remarkably clean, decorated with rare patterns from far-off places.

If anyone actually attends this motley assortment of carpets, it must be one of the spectators surrounding the boxing ring nearby. You have a feeling you'll have to grab their attention if you want to make a purchase.

The quality of the carpets and rugs sold here range from truly exquisite to remarkably terrible. The stall's proprietor, a wizened smuggler named Anton Straid (Chaotic Neutral, Cascilian Human, he/him), can usually be found paying more attention to the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.YFLxGOR5uNSmUJUA]{Boxing Ring} nearby than he does to the sale of his tattered carpets.

This absence is by design, however, since Anton also uses the location as a drop-off and pick-up location for a variety of secret deliveries of illicit goods (such as illegal shipments to and from Grevian Markos of @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.6mCDDKtMMH9wG8cT]{Everything & More}, or the smuggling of contraband components to Perlin of @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.g2ELVJBHT9RYDgGj]{Perlin's Powders}).

Anton's Wares

If the characters manage to drag Anton away from his gambling at the Boxing Ring, he is willing to sell them one of his rugs or carpets. The textiles range in price from 1 gp for the most tattered among them, to 25 gp for the most artful, imported, or exquisite.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 20]] check can tell that Anton is hiding something among his wares, as indicated by his shifty eyes and shady demeanor.

Hidden Cache

Any character who takes a moment to search the carpet piles here and succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] check is able to locate a hidden lockbox that's been stashed beneath a few of the dirtiest rugs.

Characters who wish to take the lockbox without being detected by Anton or someone else nearby must succeed on either a [[/skill stealth 18]] or [[/skill stealth 18]] check. Failure results in that character potentially being thrown overboard, per the "Local Rules & Regulations" described in @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB]{Gameplay Details}.

The reinforced lockbox (AC 20, 30 HP, DC 20 to open) can be safely opened by speaking the phrase "Anton sent me," which is furtively scrawled on the bottom of the box in Cascilian (requiring a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] check to locate), and contains the following:

  • [[/award 8pp]]

  • 2 doses of @UUID[Item.QrbcfllnppjmOSfe]{Rapture}

  • A treasure map of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.JuuKQzqfLP4R33Dm]{Lake Mithra} with an "X" marking a spot near the eastern expanse of the lake.

Opening the lockbox using physical force has a 50% chance to shatter the vials of rapture inside. If fire is involved, their is a 100% chance the treasure map is burned and becomes illegible.

Everything & More.name: Everything & More
Everything & More.text:
This sprawling cabin appears to house a well-supplied general store. All manner of baubles, curios, arms, armor, and adventuring gear can be seen lining the crowded shelves, which appear to host more clutter than the proprietors can keep up with.

The aptly-named Everything & More is the main deck's general store and pawn shop, and provides its customers with handy solutions for all kinds of equipment needs — from the mundane to the illicit, and everything in between.

The owner of this bestrewn establishment is a sagacious merchant named Grevian Markos (Lawful Evil, Ordani Human, he/him), and is rumored to be involved with a black market network that runs all the way from the deck of the Ember's Bounty to the ports of the Cascilian Republic.

Grevian is the older brother of Kasta Markos of @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.ura2nBkuotrLKse0]{Kasta's Alterations}, and feigns a certain amount of disregard for his younger sister (despite the love he actually harbors for her as his only relative).

Grevian's Wares

The shelves of Everything & More are laden with the fair- and ill-gotten gains of the ship's assorted crew and visitors, with an equal supply of new and used goods that hail from all corners of Aterica.

Per Gamemaster discretion, nearly any and all items listed in the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000] section of the game rules are available to customers in good standing with the ship. Additional items include the following:

  • @UUID[Item.KdlUUFhAnpv6YIHT]{Blast Flasks}

  • @UUID[Item.pCl2T09DRBETkkbZ]{Chasm Candles}

  • @UUID[Item.Ivc8UplVymXNZTne]{Sharp Hunting Trap}

  • @UUID[Item.6f2sudRdy1XTrJqN]{Steelmarrow}

  • @UUID[Item.KjpBoF2y1cl2Yptz]{White Inkaro Pearls}

Grevian himself seems to know a few details about every item in the store (and he makes up lies about the rest). Used goods are marked down to 80% of their listed price, but there's a 1 in [[/roll 1d2]] chance that a used good will eventually be recognized by a previous owner (who is both angry and vengeful) on the Ember's Bounty itself or somewhere on the streets of Ordain.

Froot's Discount Produce.name: Froot's Discount Produce
Froot's Discount Produce.text:
This produce stand is bedecked with all manner of fruits and vegetables, including a selection of regional favorites as well as morsels from far-off places like the Lowland Bastions and the Cascilian Republic. A gregarious-looking Thornling with a bushy beard of flower petals busies himself organizing the neatly-stacked produce as you approach.

The proprietor of this welcoming produce stand is Froot (Chaotic Neutral, Arcturian Thornling, he/him), an amiable farmer-turned-sailor who is always pushing the glorious benefits of Vitamin C onto his cohorts.

Froot's Questionable Wares

Froot's Discount Produce is stocked with a wide selection of regional fruits (sporting an even wider array of freshness, from nearly-rotten to straight-from-the-vine). And because of the questionable origins and freshness of some of Froot's wares, customers without a discerning eye or an iron-clad stomach tend to find themselves regretting a purchase from time to time.

Any produce purchased from this stand has a 50% chance of being tainted with rot. A character who unwittingly eats such rotted produce must succeed on a [[/save Constitution 13]] save or gain the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.HWs8kEojffqwTSJz]{Poisoned} condition until they finish a long rest. A successful [[/skill nature 13]] check allows a character to ascertain the questionable quality of the rotted produce.

Phestra's Boar & Grill.name: Phestra's Boar & Grill
Phestra's Boar & Grill.text:
The delicious odor of savory meats wafts up from this unsuspecting grill, where a Signborn chef turns a wild boar on a spit above an open flame. Despite the relative grime of this wayside establishment, your mouth waters in hungry anticipation.

Phestra's Boar & Grill is owned and operated by the comically acerbic Phestra Thulios (Chaotic Good, Ordani Signborn, she/they), a boisterous chef who barks at passers by with bold (and often dubious) claims about her questionably-seasoned meats.

Phestra's Sickening Wares

Phestra's Boar & Grill specializes in savory meats cooked from wild game, but her sources are often suspicious (as if carrion and diseased meat make their way onto the menu with some regularity). The squalid cuts of meat that Phestra sells are only 1 cp in cost, but they don't often agree with the consumer.

Any character who eats some of Phestra's overly-seasoned meat must succeed on a [[/save Constitution 13]] save or gain the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.HWs8kEojffqwTSJz]{Poisoned} condition until they finish a long rest. A successful [[/skill nature 15]] check allows a character to ascertain the questionable quality of the meat.

Tolan's Tiny Critters.name: Tolan's Tiny Critters
Tolan's Tiny Critters.text:
A ramshackle arrangement of tables, crates, and cages decorate this curious corner of the deck, which appears to be some kind of small creature shop. An assortment of tiny beasts reside within the cages here, including crevvets, gore birds, and trickadees. From the look of things, you can't quite tell if these creatures are intended as companions or cuisine.

Owned and operated by the opportunistic Tolan Rae (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Kivahr, she/her), Tolan's Tiny Critters profits from the sale of small and tiny beasts of Ember — including creatures both local and foreign, from all corners of Aterica and beyond. Whatever the reason for a customer's purchase, be it for food or familiar company, Tolan pays no particular heed.

At this time, however, the vendor's supply of "exotic" creatures has been depleted, leaving nothing more than common Arcturian beasts for purchase.

Tolan's Wares

Tiny Critters has @UUID[Actor.tr7jEl3CiQE1zZ7X]{Crevvets}, @UUID[Actor.EZso8riuETFlJQ8G]{Gore Birds}, and @UUID[Actor.5f6yFaP9gpprOu0w]{Trickadees} for sale at the price of 5 gp each.

Liberating the Critters

Any character who attempts to steal or liberate one or more of the eponymous critters can do so with a successful [[/tool thief 14]] check per cage, but must also succeed on either a [[/skill stealth 20]] or [[/skill sleightofhand 20]] check to avoid detection.

  • Allied characters can use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.5S8i59qskkd9GGcJ]{Help} action to cause a distraction, providing @Advantage[2] on this check in the process.

The character must also succeed on a [[/skill animalhandling 16]] check to keep the beast docile enough to escape the scene without alerting Tolan or one of her associates nearby.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge beasts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Failure on any of these checks results in detection by Tolan, and will likely end up with the characters being thrown overboard per the details in @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB]{Gameplay Details}.

Kasta's Alterations.name: Kasta's Alterations
Kasta's Alterations.text:
This small tailor's stall is attended by a young Ordani woman who busies herself mending a cloak. By the looks of it, she also has a small array of clothing for sale, with everything from urban fineries to rural comfort-wear on the modest racks.

This stall is owned and operated by the mindful tailor Kasta Markos (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, she/her), who combines traditional sewing skills with a light touch of transmutation magic to successfully ply her trade. Treat Kasta as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmCultistFanatic]{Cultist Fanatic} with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMending000]{Mending} cantrip on her list of known spells.

Kasta is the younger sister of Grevian Markos of @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.6mCDDKtMMH9wG8cT]{Everything & More}, and is no stranger to the machinations of her brother's illicit schemes (which she occasionally attempts to subvert, particularly when it suits the betterment of the community at large).

Kasta's Services

The young seamstress provides alteration and mending services, and charges a rate of 5 sp for Common Clothes and a rate of 2 gp for Fine Clothes and similar garb. If spellcasting is required, the cost for arcane @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMending000]{Mending} is 30 gp.

Additionally, Kasta has a small selection of clothing available for purchase, including the following:

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesFine]{Fine Clothes}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesTrav]{Traveler's Clothes}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagRobe0000000]{Robes}

  • A lone @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgCloakOfProtec]{Cloak of Protection}

The Smoke Hut.name: The Smoke Hut
The Smoke Hut.text:
The peculiar, spicy odor of strange smoke wafts through the air around this small tent, which is crowded by an assortment of red-eyed ne'er-do-wells that appear to be quite stoned. Beneath the tent's awning, a large octagonal table is decorated with a variety of water pipes and jars of dustweed. This smoke hut strikes you as a great place to gather some questionable information or lose track of time.

A spry, twenty-something sailor covered in Maziran tattoos waves towards your group, beckoning you to sit at the table.

Care to join us, friends? Best price on dustweed in Ordain. And the tastiest!

The young man takes a long drag off of a long-handled water pipe before flashing you a silver-toothed grin.

The Smoke Hut is a tiny venue for recreational smoking, owned and operated by the gregarious yet opportunistic Kyren Volt (Chaotic Neutral, Maziran Human, he/him), a mirthful young man who is always eager to meet a new customer or acquaintance (for whatever questionable reason). Treat Kyren as an @UUID[Actor.7z8CVE7r4cQtlJKI]{Arcturian Sailor} who can speak Common and Kaziric.

Kyren's Wares

Kyren Volt's primary goods and services include the sale of @UUID[Item.jF7AO6nnqIhFZ6oI]{Dustweed} (of which he has ample), @UUID[Item.ajjQaTDDrGOnqnHs]{Maziran Water Pipes}, @UUID[Item.erbebQcmEIdFnc9D]{Arcturian Tobacco Pipes}, and various accessories like @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagTinderbox00]{Tinderboxes} and scented @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCandle00000]{Candles}.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 13]] check are able to convince Kyren to offer them some of his more illicit wares, which include up to 6 doses of rare Maziran @UUID[Item.QrbcfllnppjmOSfe]{Rapture}.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Rumor Has It

The Smoke Hut is always rife with rumors. Characters who dare to strike up a conversation with the establishment's regular customers (including Kyren) and succeed on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check can roll once each on the @UUID[RollTable.yHfISNEnDIaz5Mlw]{Ember's Bounty Rumors} table featured below.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 15]] check is able to gather additional information, resulting in one more roll from the rumor table.

  • [[/path AnchoriteMarine]] and [[/path Nightwatch]] characters have @Advantage[2] on this check.

@Embed[RollTable.yHfISNEnDIaz5Mlw]

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the Spellbreaker Tower depicts the top seven levels of the tower including the tower's roof. This area contains a prison with escalating levels of security, and is meant to contain troubled figures who are a danger to themselves and society for various reasons including criminal ambitions.

This multi-level location serves as the key scenery for the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL]{Diplomatic Impunity} quest events @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.GvEj76wdl5vdKVWj]{Doing Time} and @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.TGOj5GcJdo3tsp85]{Breaking the Tower}.

  • This map represents only a small portion of the tower, there are potentially another eight levels beneath this area map which house citizens of ordain who are cursed or otherwise afflicted with magical maladies that require them to be quarantined.

  • Entry to this tower is chiefly achieved through the ground floor of the tower, and leads the party to the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.BMAgxL8BOc8wWqmZ]{Entry Checkpoint}. However, admittance to the upper levels is limited to guards, support staff, incoming inmates, and visitors.

  • Additional info and mechanics regarding the various chambers of this section of the tower are located in the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB] section of this walkthrough.

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.J37jJxiegQk11IcL]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Antimagic Field

The entirety of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.J37jJxiegQk11IcL]{Spellbreaker Tower} district in Ordain is shrouded in a powerful @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAntimagicF]{Antimagic Field} that emanates from the tower itself. As a result, all levels of this tower are also under this effect.

Objectives

Parties arriving here as part of @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL] (specifically the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.GvEj76wdl5vdKVWj] event) will be in the prison with the express purpose of breaking out, and taking another inmate (@UUID[Actor.WQzk939folhpYwOH]) with them.

To do this they should each have a @UUID[Item.qyuowPNcOgLKwykU] (plus one spare) hidden in the tower for them. The intent is that they will circumvent security, find a secure jump point, and leap from the tower, sailing to safety.

However, this is not the only way to escape. Alternate routes are available and explained below.

Other Escape Routes

Walking Out

Whether they fight or sneak their way out, a party that manages to get down to the first floor of the tower and take the stairwell found at the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.BMAgxL8BOc8wWqmZ] will have a clear shot to safety. Narratively they'll have to travel several flights of stairs down to do so, but resistance should be minimal at that point.

A clever party might utilize stolen guard uniforms to make this easier, and could theoretically walk right out of the prison with one of the numerous shift changes that take place every six hours.

Climbing Down

All told, the tower is about 300 feet tall. With at least 6 spools of rope (50 feet each) a party could climb down to the ground level. Since the tower has no windows and minimal guard presence outside, there is almost no risk of them being seen in the act.

However, acquiring enough rope (taken from the store rooms) is easier said than done. A resourceful party could employ bed sheets to create enough makeshift rope though, however this would take considerable time and effort to do, and the sheets would need to be sourced without drawing attention.

The other difficulty is finding a secure tie-off point for the rope. The best locations for this would be the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.3GBTxF18BAtD3lah] on level 5, or the top of the tower on Level 7.

Illumination

Interior areas of the Spellbreaker Tower are lit by mundane lanterns and braziers which are situated throughout the tower. Any light sources located in areas where inmates can access them are locked shut and require a guard key to open.

Unless otherwise noted, these light sources shed bright light in a 10 foot radius and dim light for another 10 feet.

The prison is lit at all hours, though the guards may extinguish lights in parts of the prison that aren't being used.

Exterior sections of the tower (including the exposed areas of the fifth level featured on this map) are lit by moonlight, which counts as dim light (unless otherwise dictated by weather conditions).

Terrain

The entirety of the Spellbreaker is made of extremely dense and sturdy black basalt. There are no signs of traditional masonry, and any decorative elements in the walls and floors appear to have been carved into the stone. The ground here should be treated as normal terrain unless otherwise noted.

In some places there are sections of hardwood flooring, these are built and laid over the stone flooring for purely aesthetic value. Pulling up the slats of wood only reveals more stone below.

To prevent suffocation from the extensive use of oil lanterns and braziers in the tower, all levels feature feature obscured ventilation chutes that run through the wall out to the face of the tower, allowing for easy air exchange.

The walls are made of the same material and require siege weapons to break, unless someone finds existing weaknesses to exploit. Cells feature iron bars at the entrance which are equally sturdy. Some rooms may have wooden partition walls which are not as sturdy.

Prison Doors

There are several types of doors in this prison:

Wood Doors

Found on all levels of the tower but become rarer on higher security levels where controlling movement is more important. These doors are braced with iron and use heavy, sturdy wood. They have AC 17, 25 HP, and are DC 15 to open.

Light Gates

Appearing on most levels, but commonly used on Blue Block, they are used on lower priority areas. These doors are made of iron, are sturdy, and either fixed on heavy hinges or tracks. They have AC 18, 50 HP, and are DC 16 to open.

Medium Gates

Found most checkpoints between levels and cell blocks, these are the most common gate in the tower. These doors are fixed to heavy hinges or rails and are exceptionally sturdy. They have AC 19, 60 HP, and are DC 20 to open.

Heavy Gates

Found on the central security room and the highest security cell block, these gates are made of heavy, reinforced steel bar and plating, and fixed to shielded rails. Nearly unbreakable, they have AC 20, 75 HP, and are DC 25 to open.

Elevation

The ceilings of all levels are 20 feet unless otherwise stated.

Guard Presence

There are two kinds of guards in the Spellbreaker Tower, the standard @UUID[Actor.QnYBCVJZr2dnukzz]{Spellbreaker Guard} and their heavier counterpart, the @UUID[Actor.Qd480eptt72VSjeu]{Spellbreaker Riot Guard}.

Standard guards can be found on all levels, and are generally alert while on shift. They tend to be more relaxed the lower the level is, with Levels 1 and 2 being the most relaxed, and least alert.

Generally speaking neither standard nor riot guards are interested in violence, and attempt to deescalate altercations before they come to blows. If combat does break out, guards won't kill.

Riot guards appear in only one place, Level 5, Red Block, and they are more heavily armed, with crossbows and shields. These guards are willing to use lethal force if the security of the tower and the lives of everyone inside it are at risk, such as if Red Block was to suffer a breakout. However, they don't kill unless given no other choice.

Inmate Presence

The prison is home to numerous inmates that fall into three types: The @UUID[Actor.9tOfMhRD3CuoKovh]{Blue Block Inmate}, @UUID[Actor.FaPgcwX9XXm4NqIg]{Yellow Block Inmate} and @UUID[Actor.CxGN8EVZC3pELQgs]{Red Block Inmate}

Blue Block Inmate

The least dangerous denizen of the cell blocks, these inmates are typically a citizen with a magical curse or malady that makes them dangerous to others but otherwise not likely to cause trouble while magically suppressed. Most are allowed to roam the Blue Block level with only light supervision, being locked up in the evening or if they cause trouble.

Yellow Block Inmate

Typically someone with sufficient mundane or magical skill to be very dangerous and some history of violence or danger associated with them. They might be cursed or possessed, or they might be a dangerous killer unfit for the Hallows jail. These inmates tend to be locked up around the clock for everyone's safety, but a rare few may be trusted to mingle with the Blue Block.

Red Block Inmate

Easily the most dangerous entity in the prison are these inmates. Even without magic they are resourceful, ruthless, and likely to be dangerous to others. These are serial killers, magical assassins, or otherworldly monsters that pursue their whims unbidden by the law.

Magically Suppressed

It should be noted that all of the actors provided for the prison are configured without any magical abilities since they reside in a tower that utterly suppresses them. This means it is likely that these inmates would be substantially more dangerous than their listed CRs should they ever managed to escape the prison.

Keep this in mind should any inmates escape and appear later.

Prison Hours

The prison is patrolled 24/7 with guards rotating out every 6 hours. Supplementary personnel, such as cooks and healers (all of them @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents}) are escorted inside the prison during the morning, and are escorted out before sundown.

Blue Block

Inmates on Blue Block are afforded ample time to wander, socialize and relax outside their cells, only being forced inside if they cause problems, or after sundown.

Yellow Block

Inmates on Blue Block are afforded ample time to wander, socialize and relax outside their cells, only being forced inside if they cause problems, or after sundown.

Yellow Block are occasionally let out and allowed to visit Blue Block's amenities and eat with them if they have not cause any problems in recent memory.

Red Block

Red Block inmates are never let out under any circumstances.

Intercom Panel

In each central security room there is a mechanical intercom system which allows the security teams to communicate with each other, broadcast to the floor, or trigger an alarm. Guards use this to make announcements, and call for help without raising alarms.

Alarm States

The controls for the alarms are clearly marked, and has two settings: "Local Alarm" or "Full Alert."

The local setting causes an alarm to go off across the level it's activated on, alerting the guards to a problem, and prompting them to secure checkpoints and stairwells. Guards activate a local alert if inmates become unruly, if a fight breaks out, or a similar issue arises.

The full alert setting causes an alert to go out across all levels, inciting the guards to lock down the prison, and for new guards to begin reinforcing the blue, yellow and red blocks with riot guards. Guards activate a full alert only if there is a breach in the red block, or if a full level is in riot and a risk of breakout is present.

Gate Controls

On levels 3 ,4 and 5, there are a series of colored buttons. These buttons connect to various checkpoints around the prison, and allow the guards to open the doors.

When a guard wants through a door that they can't open themselves, they enter sequence of long and short button presses. The guards in the control room respond with a flash of the button to indicate they are waiting for the second pattern, which the guard the enters.

If correct, the security operator triggers the door unlock mechanism by holding the button down. The doors lock themselves once closed, requiring the process to be repeated.

In some cases the guards in the central room can see the checkpoints directly, and make a judgement call based on that. As long as the guard is not acting strangely or in distress, they will open the door promptly.

Incorrect Gate Codes

If an incorrect first or second pattern is issued then the door won't open and one or more guards will go to verify who is at the gate.

The patterns changes every day for every level, and levels don't use the same patterns.

Handling Gate Codes

The codes are not a physical game item or piece of info for the characters to collect, and there are no rules for determining what the codes are for a day, instead it should be handled in abstract: either the party has a code for a door, or a full level, or they don't.

Finding the Codes

It is possible for characters to determine the challenge and response patterns a number of ways:

  • Observing guards, perhaps with a successful Perception check would let a character figure out a code for a single gate.

  • The central security rooms should have notebooks with the day's current challenge and response patterns.

  • Some guards may (foolishly) carry a note with the patterns for their gate or for the level, which a character might notice and be able to steal.

Central Elevator

A central elevator runs through the tower, granting access to multiple levels. This elevator can be called and controlled from any level it services, which include Level 1, Level 2, Level 4, Level 5 and Level 6.

This elevator takes a minute to travel one level, and cannot be stopped once in motion. The shaft that contains the elevator does not descend past the lowest level of this area map, and the machinery is hidden somewhere in a lower level.

The shaft is lined with stone bricks that can be climbed, however each level is automatically sealed with a medium iron gate when the elevator platform isn't present to prevent falling. Opening this gate from the inside while climbing should be very difficult and done with @Advantage[-2] under most circumstances.

Guard Mess.name: Guard Mess
Guard Mess.text:
The small dining area here is furnished with a few wooden tables, some broad and communal, others smaller, both with half-eaten meals and trays of snack foods sitting unattended.

Built into one wall is a dumbwaiter framed in stone and fitted with a light iron grate to limit access without a key. A small panel allows it to be sent to different levels.

Three Square

Meals for guards and inmates arrive via a dumbwaiter three times a day, but a small cupboard is available and tended by a pair of @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} to provide snacks throughout daytime hours.

Ups and Downs

The dumbwaiter is strong enough to move up to three Medium sized creatures at once, though not comfortably or swiftly. The elevator takes two minutes to move to a new level and makes enough noise to alert anyone within 15 feet of its arrival or departure point.

Stairwell Checkpoint 1.name: Stairwell Checkpoint 1
Stairwell Checkpoint 1.text:
You enter a broad, square chamber where two wide stairwells meet, one rising up to the landing, and the other descending. The steps are shallow and worn smooth at the edges, as though traversed by many sets of feet over the years.

Each stairwell ends at a wide landing sealed off by iron gates set into thick frames that are themselves set deeply into the stone above and below it. The gates are barred tight and held with heavy locks, with guards posted at them.

Adjoining rooms connect to this space, one filled with chests and storage crates, and the other a small space for personal searches.

New prisoners are brought in here to be searched and relieved of their belongings. Any items they entered the prison with are claimed here and stored in the chests nearby. Once their possessions have been claimed a guard checks their records and assigns them a cell block on a higher level.

Smuggled Items

Sneaking an item past the guards here may require one or more successful [[/skill sleightofhand 14]] checks. A character can only hide one item at a time, and that item must be small enough to fit in their hand.

Central Security 1.name: Central Security 1
Central Security 1.text:
Four heavy braziers throw warm light across the intricately carved floor here and paint the walls in slow, wavering shadow. Numerous windows provide extensive views of the outer halls, allowing the guards here to see everything going on outside.

Large pots occupy the corners of the room, each holding red, leafy plants with broad, waxy fronds. Their earthy scent mixes with smoke from the braziers, and bits of fallen leaf litter the floor around the planters.

Access to this room is controlled by two @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{heavy gates}.

This room features the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#central-elevator]{Central Elevator} which provides access to other levels.

Baths.name: Baths
Baths.text:
A large communal bath occupies the center of this room, its broad basin fed by a flow of hot water that keeps the air damp and warm. Along the sides sit two smaller individual baths, separated only by low stone partitions that offer little privacy. Steam hangs in the air here at all hours, while water trickles and laps against stone in a steady, echoing sound.

On-duty guards come here to bathe before or after shift before going to the barracks. While not occupied at all hours, it is visited often.

Lavatories.name: Lavatories
Lavatories.text:
This small junction chamber holds two plain doors, each marked with signs denoting one for visitors and one for inmates.

The visitors’ washroom is lined with wooden toilet stalls, their partitions offering partial cover for occupants, while the inmates’ facility features rows of bare stone toilets cut into the rock and simple bathing materials stacked close at hand.

The space leading to the washroom always has at least one guard in it if there are visitors and inmates on this level, and the rooms are checked often if someone is inside.

On-Duty Barracks.name: On-Duty Barracks
On-Duty Barracks.text:
These barracks are a cluster of connected common rooms featuring rows of wood-framed beds and accompanied by chests packed with personal belongings and clothes. The air carries the mixed smells of oiled leather, sweat, and lantern smoke.

Guards on duty are housed here. This space is more occupied during the evening hours than during daytime, but always has a few guards in it, often sleeping.

Personal Effects

Searching through the chests here will yield several outfits of common clothes, and more crucially, clean guard uniforms including belts, boots, and padded coats.

There are enough uniforms for two people, though a successful [[/skill perception 15]] check will yield two more. Wearing these uniforms allows one to pass for an off-duty guard on this level without drawing attention as the wearer is not acting suspiciously.

  • Result of 20+ You also find a set of guard keys that will open any wooden doors encountered on any level, and any cells on Level 2 or Level 3.

Storage.name: Storage
Storage.text:
This storage room is crowded with stacked crates, rough boxes, and tied burlap bags stack atop each other. Simple shelves are bowed slightly under the weight of general goods of the same type. The air is dry and dusty, carrying the mixed scents of wood, hemp, and old canvas.

This space mostly holds general goods used by the prison level, such as spare barrels of water, wine, cooking oil, lantern oil and similar. At your discretion there may be other useful items here beyond what's listed.

Useful Items

Searching the boxes here yields basic hand tools such as a hammer, saw, chisel, an axe, and a pick. There are also other useful items here like gloves, lanterns and and three 50' coils of rope.

The back wall is also damaged, which keen eyed characters might notice.

Curious Damage

Characters with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check notice a boarded up corner where the stone appears to have been damaged.

Prying the boards off requires tools (such as a prybar) or a successful [[/check str 16]] check, and both actions are noisy enough to attract attention from the adjacent room.

Success grants access to the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.SEIifGAqIsFUnSTg] beyond it.

Armory.name: Armory
Armory.text:
This armory is lined with racks and stands each crowded with ready gear. Shields are stacked in orderly rows, crossbows hang by their stocks, and quivers of bolts sit bundled in crates within quick reach.

Suits of sturdy armor stand along the walls on simple frames, each ready to be put on, while weighted clubs rest in thick clusters below.

The air is rich with the sharp smell of weapon oil, leather, and oxidized iron.

Armed and Dangerous

The racks here hold a large assortment of armors and weapons, enough to outfit upwards of two dozen characters in @UUID[Item.tpdQk2J2YD4JNdBj]{Riot Armor} with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepClub000000]{clubs}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepHeavyCross]{Heavy Crossbows}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbamoBolts00000]{ammunition} for all of them.

Gearing Up

During a crisis, standard @UUID[Actor.QnYBCVJZr2dnukzz]{Spellbreaker Guards} can come here and gear up, taking up a crossbow, ammunition, armor, helmet, and shield, becoming a @UUID[Actor.Qd480eptt72VSjeu]{Spellbreaker Riot Guard} when done.

These more heavily armored guards then move to the central elevator and head to whatever level needs help.

Library.name: Library
Library.text:
This quiet library and lounge is a split level space, with the upper area featuring a sitting area with plush chairs and hardwood floors. The lower level features a bubbling fountain surrounded by benches and the whole room is lined with shelves that are packed with volumes of every thickness.

Off duty guards can relax and read here, and often has one to two guards reading and chatting quietly.

Entry Checkpoint.name: Entry Checkpoint
Entry Checkpoint.text:
You enter a broad, square chamber at the top of the stairs. A metal gate clatters open loudly as you're ushered through into a broad space with wood floors and numerous benches. A guard manning a desk here looks up at you as you arrive.

Everyone coming into the tower from lower levels are checked in here, from new inmates to guests to guards. Visitors and inmates receive a brief, cursory search for contraband before being sent onward.

Nothing Dangerous Allowed

Characters entering the tower from this point will have relieved of any weapons and dangerous items already, all of which end up in storage crates in the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.CvHoqViz4Z26Apbn]{Intake Checkpoint} storage room.

This search is just to make sure no other dangerous items or contraband items (such as narcotics, lock picks, poisons, etc.) made it this far.

Note that inmates will be subject to another search before moving up to the next level.

Smuggled Items

Sneaking an item past the guards here may require one or more successful [[/skill sleightofhand 14]] checks. A character can only hide one item at a time, and that item must be small enough to fit in their hand.

Central Security 5.name: Central Security 5
Central Security 5.text:
The light of four braziers creates an undulating mask of shadows here as light flickers across carved floors and heavy barred windows. The central elevator here features doors on the north and west faces, both stepping out to subtle flames engraved in the stone underfoot.

A bank of levers sits against the central elevator wall, with four levels for the four checkpoints and two more levers marked as controlling the south and east hall gates.

In the south-eastern corner of the room a long corner table sits against the wall and features the collective efforts of the central security team for this level. A collection of colorful buttons fixed to copper pipes running into the wall can also be found here.

Heavies on Standby

While the stations here are manned by standard guards, like all other central security levels, three @UUID[Actor.Qd480eptt72VSjeu]{Spellbreaker Riot Guards} are always on duty here, standing by in case there's a problem in the cell blocks.

Access to this room is controlled by two @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{heavy gates}.

This room features the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#central-elevator]{Central Elevator} which provides access to other levels.

Stairwell Checkpoint 2.name: Stairwell Checkpoint 2
Stairwell Checkpoint 2.text:
You enter a broad, square chamber where two wide stairwells meet, one rising up to the landing, and the other descending. The steps are shallow and worn smooth at the edges, as though traversed by many sets of feet over the years.

Each stairwell ends at a wide landing sealed off by iron gates set into thick frames that are themselves set deeply into the stone above and below it. The gates are barred tight and held with heavy locks, with guards posted at them.

Several wooden shelves and open racks have been set along one side of the central chamber, crowded with folded prison uniforms in dull, serviceable cloth.

Here, incoming inmates are given a checkup by a waiting @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherent} before receiving uniforms here based on the cell block they are heading to. Privacy is a luxury not afforded here, sadly.

Curious Damage

Characters with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or making a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check notice a boarded up corner where the stone appears to have been damaged.

Prying the boards off requires tools (such as a prybar) or a successful [[/check str 16]] check, and both actions are noisy enough to attract attention from the adjacent room.

Success grants access to the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.SEIifGAqIsFUnSTg] beyond it.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
This cramped kitchen is packed wall to wall with baskets and crates of fresh produce, bundled herbs, and stacked cuts of meat laid out for quick use.

A few narrow worktables are crowded with boards, knives, and bowls, while pots simmer and kettles steam over squat stoves, filling the air with heat and sharp, savory scents.

The stone floor is damp and mottled with spills, and everything here is arranged for speed, with ingredients and tools kept within arm’s reach.

Cooks of the Line

Two @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} trained as cooks work here to prepare food for the other levels during the day. They use the dumbwaiter to move meals between floors when they are ready.

Ups and Downs

The dumbwaiter is strong enough to move up to three Medium sized creatures at once, though not comfortably or swiftly. The elevator takes two minutes to move to a new level and makes enough noise to alert anyone within 15 feet of its arrival or departure point.

Private Visitation.name: Private Visitation
Private Visitation.text:
This cluster of visiting rooms is divided into small, plain chambers separated by a barred window narrow enough to make passing anything larger than a finger's width impossible. Benches and simple stools sit opposite the bars, with stone tables fixed to the wall.

Visitors heading into these rooms and inmates coming out of these rooms are searched by an attending guard before they are allowed to move on.

Public Visitation.name: Public Visitation
Public Visitation.text:
Six stone tables stand in two neat rows with a seventh in the middle of them. The entire space is hemmed in by light iron bars that rise all the way to the ceiling.

Each table has space enough for four to sit together for public group visitation, and are fitted with iron shackles and chain in the event an inmate needs to be restrained here.

A security checkpoint controls passage in and out of the area, while granting the attending guards clear view of everyone inside.

Visitors heading into these rooms and inmates coming out of these rooms are searched by an attending guard before they are allowed to move on.

Inmates and groups may visit here. Inmates are only shackled if they are troublemakers, or from Yellow or Red Block, though it is rare for Red Block inmates to ever be let out of their cells.

Medical Cells.name: Medical Cells
Medical Cells.text:
The cells here are ten by fifteen foot rooms cut into the black basalt, each opening framed by light iron bars and jail door set into the dark stone. Lanterns light the rooms and halls between them.

Inside each cell is a low stone bed topped with a thin mattress and light bedding folded tight. Alongside them a small stone table and stool provide a place for occupants to sit.

The air carries a faint, sharp trace of cleaning spirits and boiled herbs, as if the medical ward sits just out of sight.

Inmates are kept here to await or recover from medical treatment.

Break Room.name: Break Room
Break Room.text:
This break room is plain but comfortable, a few rough tables and benches set here provide seating, and a collection of snacks await hungry occupants. On nearby racks some spare pieces of equipment sit, and one whole side of the room is piled with crates and sacks holding unknown contents.

Useful Items

A few shields and clubs can be claimed from the racks, similar to what the guards use.

Unattended Uniforms

Characters choosing to search through the sacks will find they are stuffed with dirty prison uniforms and bedding destined for the laundry. However, a successful [[/skill perception 14]] check yields three dirty guard uniforms.

While these uniforms lack belts, boots, gloves, and padded armor, they might be enough to masquerade as a guard from a distance. Wearing these uniforms provides @Advantage[2] on stealth checks against other guards as long as they aren't within 20 feet of the wearer.

A more complete uniform would be far more effective, but it won't be found here.

At your discretion there may be more useful items hidden here, such as rope or tools, but a Perception or Investigation check might be necessary to find them in the piles of containers.

Medical.name: Medical
Medical.text:
This medical room is a clean, spare chamber of dark stone with a few beds set out in the open, each fitted with thin mattresses, light blankets, and anchor points for shackles. The air here stings with the scent of medical salves, herbs, and spirits.

A simple desk stands nearby for an attendant, its surface kept for notes and cabinets holding basic supplies, and beside the desk two doors connect to a small treatment room with a bed and storage, and a cramped break room for the staff.

Attended all-hours by at least one @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherent} trained in medicine and a guard. Any healing provided here is mundane due to lack of magic, but medical supplies are ample.

The cabinets here hold healing supplies and tools typically found in a healer's kit, allowing for a trained character to treat wounds on themselves or another.

The amount of supplies here are sufficient for several rounds of treatment if necessary, and the treatment room is even outfitted for simple surgery if the situation calls for it.

Exercise Room.name: Exercise Room
Exercise Room.text:
A sizeable open space has been dedicated to exercise here, with painted lines, a few metal baskets, and leather balls available for play. In one corner stacks of weights sit ready to be lifted, while on the opposite end of the space a shelf of books is accompanied by chairs for inmates less athletically inclined.

A pair of single doors with signs denote lavatories for inmates should they need them. Above you the ceiling is grated, allowing for guards on the upper level to keep an eye on the inmates here.

This area is open to inmates during daytime hours, but is cleared out and locked up in the late evening. Nothing in this space is allowed to leave it if a guard is watching.

Stairwell Checkpoint 3.name: Stairwell Checkpoint 3
Stairwell Checkpoint 3.text:
Shallow steps of well worn stone meet here at wide landing sealed off by iron gates and marked with blue lines. The gates are barred tight and held with heavy locks, with guards posted at them.

Beyond the gates a large room waits, with badly scuffed wooden flooring, a shelf of reading materials, and a few couches sit against the walls in the corners for guards to use as a resting space.

This space is occupied by guards at all hours. It uses an intercom to communicate with central security who work the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#gate-controls]{Gate Controls} remotely. The @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{Prison Doors} and walls are light here.

Work in Progress

Hidden passage assets and interactivity are planned for this secret passage, and will be added in a future update.

Cracks in the Wall

A character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or making either a successful [[/skill perception 12]] check while passing through the stairwell notices that a section of the wall has suffered damage of some sort and might be exploitable with the right tools.

A chisel and hammer, or mining pick would be necessary to break open this section of wall, and there's almost no way to do it without being seen, but if done, it would create a passage through the stone.

Characters that do this would create passage to a @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.Oang2HH4knNdCV1l] outside. This passage is narrow, but easily traversed by a small creature. Medium creatures would need to squeeze through.

Blue Block Cells.name: Blue Block Cells
Blue Block Cells.text:
This block holds a row of single-occupant cells, each one broad enough to pace a few steps before meeting cold basalt. The entrances are a grid of light iron bars paired with sliding jail doors, their metal pale and worn smooth at the handle points.

Within each cell a stone bed is built into the wall, fitted with a proper mattress and ample bedding. They also feature stone desks with a stout stone stool tucked beneath, all made of a lighter gray stone not matching the tower's.

Near the back, a semi-private toilet space is set behind a short wood partition, just high enough to break the line of sight from the door without truly sealing anything off.

Cells are unlocked during daytime hours, allowing inmates to roam somewhat freely.

Central Security 3.name: Central Security 3
Central Security 3.text:
Braziers spit smoke toward the ceiling where tendrils of it disappear into pinhole vents in the corners. The unstable light dances over carved floors and numerous barred windows.

A collection of clutter comprised of sacks and crates sits piled in one corner next to a lon work desk scattered with papers and half-written log reports. Fixed to the wall above it are a series of color coded buttons on copper pipes.

Set against either side of the central elevator walls are banks of levers, six levers total, each labeled with the gate they control access to.

A pair of weapon racks are bolted to the north and south faces of the central elevator column here, their frames holding a collection of heavy clubs just like those the guards carry.

Access to this room is controlled by two @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{heavy gates}.

Central Security 4.name: Central Security 4
Central Security 4.text:
Four large braziers burn at the corners, filling the air with heat and the bitter smell of smoke. Despite their presence, the haze is light, and following its movement you see it escaping into vents in the ceiling.

Flanking the central elevator walls are two banks of levers, with two levers apiece. Each lever is marked with the checkpoint it controls. Opposite these banks are two decks covered in paperwork and log books. The west desk is fitted with a bank of color-coded buttons on copper fittings.

Access to this room is controlled by two @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{heavy gates} and features the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#central-elevator]{Central Elevator} which provides access to other levels.

Central Security 2.name: Central Security 2
Central Security 2.text:
Warm light cast by four braziers dances between the geometric patterns carved into the floor and along the stony walls. Beyond them, through barred windows, the central hall of the prison can be seen.

Set against either side of the central elevator walls are banks of levers, four total, each labeled with the gate they control access to. Along the walls opposite them are bookshelves, crates, chests, and desks littered with papers where the guards file reports and keep logs of events.

On the eastern wall a set of color coded buttons are fixed to the wall.

Access to this room is controlled by two @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{heavy gates}.

This room features the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#central-elevator]{Central Elevator} which provides access to other levels.

Sitting Area.name: Sitting Area
Sitting Area.text:
A wide swath of grated flooring stretches, with a knee-height railing keeping anyone from directly walking across it. Through the metal grating you can see the lower level of the tower with an open area dedicated to exercise and sport.

The grate here has a view of the lower level @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.MrdtNTA1dx7uMkGi]{exercise} area on the lower level, allowing guards to watch inmates from above.

Stairwell Checkpoint 4.name: Stairwell Checkpoint 4
Stairwell Checkpoint 4.text:
Two wide stairwells meet here, both ending at wide landings sealed off by iron gates and marked with yellow lines. Guards posted here keep keen watch.

Beyond the gates a large room sits with a stone fountain bubbles softly in the center of it. To one side of the room are wooden benches, and in the opposing corner a large desk where records and reports are processed for the level.

This space is occupied by guards at all hours. It uses an intercom to communicate with central security who work the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#gate-controls]{Gate Controls} remotely.
