The @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{Prison Doors} and walls are medium here.

Blue Block Gate.name: Blue Block Gate
Blue Block Gate.text:
This checkpoint consists of two light iron gates and the inner space has seating for two guards, and some furniture for them while on shift. An glowing button is fixed on a copper pipe going into the floor here and is used by the guards to communicate with the central security room.

This space is occupied by guards at all hours. It uses an intercom to communicate with central security who work the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#gate-controls]{Gate Controls} remotely. The @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{Prison Doors} and walls are light here.

Yellow Block Gate.name: Yellow Block Gate
Yellow Block Gate.text:
This checkpoint consists of two medium iron gates and the inner space has seating for two guards, and some furniture for them while on shift. A glowing button is fixed on a copper pipe going into the floor here and is used by the guards to communicate with the central security room.

This space is occupied by guards at all hours. It uses an intercom to communicate with central security who work the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#gate-controls]{Gate Controls} remotely. This area uses @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{Medium Iron Gates} and walls.

Red Block Gate.name: Red Block Gate
Red Block Gate.text:
This checkpoint consists of two heavy iron gates and the inner space has seating for two guards, and some furniture for them while on shift. A glowing button is fixed on a copper pipe going into the floor here and is used by the guards to communicate with the central security room.

This space is occupied by a pair of riot guards at all hours. It uses an intercom to communicate with central security who work the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#gate-controls]{Gate Controls} remotely. This area uses @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{Heavy Iron Gates} and walls.

Elevator Checkpoint.name: Elevator Checkpoint
Elevator Checkpoint.text:
This checkpoint consists of two iron gates and the inner space has seating for two guards, and some furniture for them while on shift. The gates connect the central elevator space and a carpeted lobby.

This space is occupied by a pair of guards at all hours, both guards have keys to the gate, as do all other guards on this level. This area uses @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{Medium Iron Gates} and walls.

Blue Block Canteen.name: Blue Block Canteen
Blue Block Canteen.text:
Behind light iron bars sits a wide canteen dedicated to feeding the inmates of this level. Half a dozen stone tables and accompanying stools provide space for two dozen people to eat at once and a central dumbwaiter seems to be the source of the meals that are served here.

Side doors lead to a pantry with serving dishes, and some lighter consumables fit for between meal snacks.

Access is free most hours from side doors connecting to the cell blocks while access via the central hall access is limited via a security gate.

Three Square

Meals for guards and inmates arrive via a dumbwaiter three times a day, but a small cupboard is available and tended by a pair of @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} to provide snacks throughout daytime hours.

Given the lower security of this level, the pantry workers and inmates are able interact fairly freely as long as no issues are created.

Ups and Downs

The dumbwaiter is strong enough to move up to three Medium sized creatures at once, though not comfortably or swiftly. The elevator takes two minutes to move to a new level and makes enough noise to alert anyone within 15 feet of its arrival or departure point.

Yellow Cells.name: Yellow Cells
Yellow Cells.text:
This block holds a row of single-occupant cells, each one broad enough to a fixed stone bed and mattress with bedding provided. The cells also feature a broad stone desk against the wall with a squad stone stool to accompany it.

All these fixtures are cut from a paler stone that doesn't match the tower's own. The toilet space is half-screened by a wood partition that provides modesty but little privacy.

The entrance to the cells are comprised of sturdy steel bars and moderately reinforced jail doors sitting in reinforced metal tracks.

Cells are locked most hours and inmates are not let out without at least one attending guard to supervise.

The halls can be secured with light metal double gates, limiting movement between individual groups of cells.

Staff Corner.name: Staff Corner
Staff Corner.text:
Secluded from the rest of the prison is a quite space with a few doors, one leads to a private lavatory for guards where they can wash and do their business, while another leads to small but comfortable break room with a couch and shelf of books.

Beyond the break room is another door, and a storage room.

This room is packed high with crates, sacks and barrels goods. It seems there is no organization or method to the madness here, and each container holds an assortment of goods, making finding anything specific here a chore.

Useful Items

Without spending much time searching this space a character can find a few spare sheets, sacks of spare inmate uniforms (Yellow Block), a few bottles of wine, a lantern, and little else of use.

Digging Deeper

A character that spends 10 minutes actively searching through the mess will find more useful items, including a 50 foot coil of rope, and a set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools}.

Yellow Block Mess.name: Yellow Block Mess
Yellow Block Mess.text:
The small dining area here is furnished with a few wooden tables, some broad and communal, others smaller, both with half-eaten meals and trays of snack foods sitting unattended.

Built into one wall is a dumbwaiter framed in stone and fitted with a light iron grate to limit access without a key. A small panel allows it to be sent to different levels.

The dumbwaiter is strong enough to move up to three Medium sized creatures at once, though not comfortably or swiftly. The elevator takes two minutes to move to a new level and makes enough noise to alert anyone within 15 feet of its arrival or departure point.

Guards Only

A place for guards to eat. Since Yellow Block feeds inmates in their cells, and has a higher on-duty guard roster (also on call for Red Block above) this space is where guards gather and relax while on duty.

Three Square

Meals for guards and inmates arrive via a dumbwaiter three times a day, but a small cupboard is available and tended by a pair of @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} to provide snacks throughout daytime hours.

Ups and Downs

The dumbwaiter is strong enough to move up to three Medium sized creatures at once, though not comfortably or swiftly. The elevator takes two minutes to move to a new level and makes enough noise to alert anyone within 15 feet of its arrival or departure point.

Surge Walkers.name: Surge Walkers
Surge Walkers.text:
A broad metal platform composed of heavily oxidized iron plates covers the area here. The scent of salt water and sea life hangs in the air and between the gaps of the platform and prison floor movement of the lower level can be seen.

Crates and barrels made of teal wood with bronze fittings sit on this platform, each marked with the symbol not typically found in Ordain, and smelling strongly of the sea.

@embed[Actor.SDSf8Oo4lloU4gVM]

Ready and Waiting

A pair of surge walkers wait here on standby. These walkers are active and capable of surveying their surroundings. A successful [[/skill perception 16]] notices this fact.

These Surge Walkers typically sit and wait for an alarm or directions from a guard to take action, but will respond to inmates that they notice in their area.

Surge Walker Tactics

These surge walkers are both configured slightly differently. One has its heavy claw equipped, while the other has a heavy spear gun on its arm. Their stat blocks reflect these differences in equipment, and modify their available tactics.

The harpoon gun surge walker uses its @UUID[Actor.SDSf8Oo4lloU4gVM.Item.6Cotyr98Sn4wdjl3]{Heavy Speargun} to make ranged attacks and favors fighting from a distance if it can, while the clawed surge walker uses its @UUID[Actor.SDSf8Oo4lloU4gVM.Item.pTCBVfXp3bXYL2xL]{Crushing Claw} and @UUID[Actor.SDSf8Oo4lloU4gVM.Item.hLjoSQ886Piu9Uh1]{Punch} to capture and subdue inmates.

In either case they can use their @UUID[Actor.SDSf8Oo4lloU4gVM.Item.MiAdarG7h8vWHPq5]{Focused Beam} to blind and injure single targets at range, or @UUID[Actor.SDSf8Oo4lloU4gVM.Item.dWudvjY4V8dEYU4q]{Blinding Blast} to disable large groups.

Unless reduced to half hit points, activating their @UUID[Actor.SDSf8Oo4lloU4gVM.Item.BP9F7XoC6AQ1EZLF]{Ortarec Core} feature, the surge walkers to not attempt to kill prison inmates.

Fights in Tight Spaces

Being large creatures, surge walkers may come across numerous places in the prison where they lack the room to fight effectively. In hallways and doorways where they lack the space to fight easily they @Advantage[-2] on their attacks.

Surge walkers can squeeze through narrow doorways, treating the space as difficult terrain when they do.

The crates sitting next to the Surge Walkers originate from the same country as the walkers themselves. The spear gun wielding Surge Walker can use these crates to rearm itself, and a desperate or opportunistic character could raid the crates for a simple weapon.

Foreign Supplies

The crates are marked:

Munitions: SW-34a Heavy Harpoons

Characters with [[/culture emberCascilian]] or [[/path emberAnchoriteMarine]] recognize the symbol of the Cascilian Republic's Military.

The metal harpoons within are heavy, and expertly made. Clearly meant to be used as ammunition by the Surge Walkers here, they can also be used by any humanoid as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepSpear00000]{Spear}. A crate holds about 12 heavy harpoons.

Dark Cells.name: Dark Cells
Dark Cells.text:
This corner of the prison is dark, the lights all snuffed out and the cells left open save for one where a single glowing cube hovers silently, emitting a strange light. The cell it resides in seems to have suffered damage, with a collection of dark stones piled in the corner behind it.

A few of the other cells feature cages large enough for a person, albeit without an ounce of comfort. The air here has a heavy, unsettling quality, and lingering too long feels unsafe.

The cells are unoccupied save for @UUID[Actor.UwzAECe3l3ioFp45]{The Cube}. Most of the cells have smaller iron cages in them. Guards don't come into this area unless they have to.

Sky Cells.name: Sky Cells
Sky Cells.text:
The cells here are sparse, mattresses lie directly on the basalt floor with bedding piled atop them and each one is missing a wall, instead they open to the sky beyond. The air here is crisp, bordering on cold, and a strong wind sweeps through the cells periodically.

The gates to these cells are ironically heavy, with thick iron bars and matching sliding doors that roll over armored rails, as if the occupant couldn't simply leap from the tower at will. Though, such a decision might surely be their last.

Falling Hazard

A character that falls or jumps from this platform without some way to land safely would suffer the maximum [[/damage 20d6 bludgeoning]] damage after falling about 250 feet.

Escape Options

This location provides a viable jumping off point for wingsuits.

This location provides a viable tie-off for rope to climb down the tower.

Red Block Mess.name: Red Block Mess
Red Block Mess.text:
The small dining area here is furnished with a few wooden tables, some broad and communal, others smaller, both with half-eaten meals and trays of snack foods sitting unattended.

Built into one wall is a dumbwaiter framed in stone and fitted with a light iron grate to limit access without a key. A small panel allows it to be sent to different levels.

Guards Only

A place for guards to eat. Since Yellow Block feeds inmates in their cells, and has a higher on-duty guard roster (also on call for Red Block above) this space is where guards gather and relax while on duty.

Three Square

Meals for guards and inmates arrive via a dumbwaiter three times a day, but a small cupboard is available and tended by a pair of @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents} to provide snacks throughout daytime hours.

Ups and Downs

The dumbwaiter is strong enough to move up to three Medium sized creatures at once, though not comfortably or swiftly. The elevator takes two minutes to move to a new level and makes enough noise to alert anyone within 15 feet of its arrival or departure point.

Stairwell Checkpoint 5.name: Stairwell Checkpoint 5
Stairwell Checkpoint 5.text:
Two wide stairwells meet here, one rising up to the landing, and the other descending. Each ends at a wide landing sealed off by heavy iron gates and marked with red lines. Barred tight with the heaviest iron locks, armored guards stand by them, ready for trouble.

Beyond the gates, the flooring changes to well-worn hardwood planks and the space it cluttered with stacks of crates, barrels, and chests. A few long wooden benches provide seating, though it doesn't seem like many linger here.

This space is occupied by riot guards at all hours. It uses an intercom to communicate with central security who work the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#gate-controls]{Gate Controls} remotely. The @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{Prison Doors} and walls are heavy here, providing maximum security.

Central Elevator.name: Central Elevator
Central Elevator.text:
Four heavy braziers throw warm light across the intricately carved floor here and paint the walls in slow, wavering shadow. Intricately carved walls pick up dancing shadows as the walls lead around toward a gated checkpoint.

This room features the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#central-elevator]{Central Elevator} which provides access to other levels.

Lounge.name: Lounge
Lounge.text:
This wide room has been transformed into a lounge with a pair of worn but comfortable couches to accommodate guards and guests, while shelves sit nearby laden with reading materials for anyone present.

A trio of fountains bubble away softly against the far wall, their waters lit by a crackling brazier while a cage with a pair of little red songbirds twitter back and forth at each other happily.

Fountain Room.name: Fountain Room
Fountain Room.text:
A huge, three-tiered fountain dominates the north wall here, a large rask's head spewing water into the basins. Lanterns fixed to the wall on either side cast warm light across the flowing water.

Doors sit on either side of the fountain, while a pair of heavy double doors sit on the other side of the room. The rest of this space is occupied with assorted barrels and storage containers.

This space mostly holds general goods used by the prison level, but at your discretion there may be more useful items hidden here, such as a coil of rope or a weapon, but a Perception or Investigation check might be necessary to find them in the piles of containers.

Work in Progress

Hidden door assets and interactivity are planned for this secret door, and will be added in a future update.

Hidden Passage

Characters with a [[/skill perception passive 18]] notice seams on the eastern wall that denote what might be a hidden doorway. However there is no clear way to open it.

Remote Entry

Searching the wall and the space around the hidden doorway yields nothing in the way of a mechanism to open the hidden doorway, indicating that it might be opened elsewhere.

Treasure Room.name: Treasure Room
Treasure Room.text:
The narrow stone passage gives way to a small room laden with golden coins, gilded vessels, and fat ingots of pure gold worth a small fortune. Even without light the gold seems to glow faintly on its own.

Curious Coinage

Examining the coins, they don't appear to be ones minted in Ordain and each feature a shrouded female figure on both faces.

Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] know that these coins were not minted by any nearby city, guild, or government that they know of.

Characters with [[/culture emberOrdani]] or making a successful [[/skill history 16]] check recognize that the figure on the coins is Avilla, the Spellbreaker, the very shard goddess that made this tower centuries ago.

Glittering in the Gold

Eight large @UUID[Item.ZrQEbleUzvMVCfSu]{Lambent Gems} can be found in this collection. A successful [[/skill nature 16]] check notes that these are a well known semi-precious stone found all over Ember and the source of the glow is not well understood except for the fact that it's not inherently magical, but a natural quality of the gemstone itself.

Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] know that these gems are commonly used in decorative light fixtures, jewelry and art pieces.

A Wealth of Weight

The total value of the hoard here is close to ten thousand gold, however the weight of the ingots and coins are considerable, making transport of the coin hard, especially for a party wearing prison uniforms and lacking proper packs and gear.

A party hoping to extract this wealth should have a hard time doing so, with the collective weight of the coins slowing them down, even if they manage to find bags and packs in the prison to carry them.

Parties hoping to glide or climb their way to safety will quickly realize the extra weight of the gold makes both routes impossible.

Warden's Office.name: Warden's Office
Warden's Office.text:
This large room is lined with four huge bookcases laden with tomes. Each one climbs to the ceiling ands towers over the rest of the room which contains a half-circle desk of ornate wood and a small seating area with chairs and a sofa. The furnishings here are simple, but of high quality.

Hidden Latches

Characters that search the room and make a successful [[/skill investigation 18]] check note that there is a hidden lever here that opens the treasure room to the south.

The Prison Warden

Warden Availability

During daytime hours the Warden of the prison can be found here, handling paperwork, and administering the prison. During evening hours there is a chance he is in the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.MuN4WTmWgAm4gvqy], but it is also possible that he's left the prison for the night. His presence is up to your discretion.

Warden Cyran Holst (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

A gaunt, quiet leader, Holst has spent nearly three decades balancing the expectations of the Ordinate, the Cascillian Republics' demands, and the needs of the Tower's inmates. His commitment to routine and fairness underlies every decision, rendering him respected by Ordinate, Cindaric, Cascillians and Veiled Chain alike. There is no aspect of operation within the tower prison levels that he doesn't know about.

Cyran Holst has been married for over twenty years to his wife Surna. He has two grown sons, one of which works in the Hallows, and the other in House Lilifeld.

He is well respected by his guard team and does his best to make sure they are well taken care of and safe, alongside the people the prison inters.

Guarded Warden

Cyran Holst should use the @UUID[Actor.QnYBCVJZr2dnukzz] actor, and has the same equipment and training as one. If attacked, he will defend himself while trying to raise the alarm with the rest of his guard team.

It is possible to interact with the Warden when he is present in his office, and inmates in the prison may even request meetings, which have a good chance of being granted.

Meeting The Warden

A meeting with the Warden of the Spellbreaker is not especially difficult to arrange for inmates within the prison. To do so, one simply needs to put in a request with any guard, and assuming that the guard forwards the request, a meeting may be granted in the next few days.

Visits are always supervised by a small team of guards, and for inmates in yellow or red block, the warden is more likely to come visit their cell directly to talk.

Not Unreasonable

The Warden is willing to consider requests that improve the quality of life and comfort of inmates without sacrificing the security of the prison. They are also willing to listen to complaints and will do their best to solve them, if possible.

However, Warden Holst doesn't respond well to being threatened and doesn't accept bribes. He is a lawful individual who has high ethical standards when it comes to operating the prison.

Warden's Quarters.name: Warden's Quarters
Warden's Quarters.text:
These private quarters are cozy and clean, the floor is spotless, and the shelves neatly organized. A collection of bottles and packages of food cover the flat surfaces, while a double bed sits in the corner.

Useful Items

The footlocker and cabinet both contain a pair of guard uniforms in good condition. They are tailored for a human, and might not fit all ancestries, but they would allow one to easily pretend to be a guard provided the wearer doesn't act suspicious.

Sundry Items

The rest of this room contains packaged foods such as candies, dried fruits, pastries, and the like. Some of them appear to be gifts, and a few have cards indicating they were given by someone named "Surna" who is quite fond of the warden and hopes to see them soon.

Clothing for Two

Searching through the cabinet, a character would notice that some of the clothing is different in style and size, likely meant for someone with a more petite frame. It is likely the warden doesn't always sleep alone here.

Guest List

The items found here are meant to indicate that the Warden has a partner in the city that sometimes stays over in the tower. If the party wants to make use of this insight, they can.

Private Bathroom.name: Private Bathroom
Private Bathroom.text: A large bath dominates the rear of the room, the water giving off a gentle haze of steam. A smaller basin sits against the opposite corner with a hand pump, and a corner lavatory with wooden partitions allows for a bit of privacy from the rest of the bath.

Display Room.name: Display Room
Display Room.text:
This room features a collection of artifacts including historic armors, weapons, books, along with alchemical and medical curios. Most of the items appear old, some of them not fit for use, but all are lovingly displayed, with many behind glass.

The vast majority of items in this space are of historical or academic value and aren't useful in the hands of the party. However, a particularly larcenous party might want to help themselves to the items anyway. The cases are locked (DC 15 to open) and sturdy enough (AC 15, 15 HP).

Museum Pieces

The arms and armor displayed here are old, and in many cases have been maintained for display, not use. The armor's leather straps and fittings are old and weak, unfit for the rigors of combat, while the blades are dull, and more useful as bludgeons.

Characters with [[/culture emberTayan]] or [[/path emberImperialConscript]] recognize some of the rifles as being early models of Tayan firearms. They are unlikely to be functional, and even if they were, there isn't any ammunition present.

Of the medical curios present, many are bottles with contents long since removed, consumed, or dried up, leaving them as nothing more than display pieces.

Bust Gallery.name: Bust Gallery
Bust Gallery.text:
Five stone busts sit on large stone plinths in this hallway, their gray countenances lit by the dancing flames of the braziers nearby. The stone plaques at their bases are each engraved with the names of the figures represented.

The busts are representations of the wardens that previously served the tower, and include the dates that they served. Each warden seems to hold the position for about twenty years before being replaced.

Map Room.name: Map Room
Map Room.text:
The walls of this room are lined with shelves, each one comprised of dozens of cubby holes and they in turn cradle rolled up parchment and vellum tied with leather stringers. In the center of the space are four tables with old, beaten maps on display.

Cartographer's Cache

Looking through the shelves you quickly realize that this room houses a large collection of old maps. Most are decades or centuries old and depict regions of the world as they were understood to exist back then.

Most of these maps are likely wildly out of date and inaccurate, giving them more value as collector's items than anything else.

Stairwell Checkpoint 6.name: Stairwell Checkpoint 6
Stairwell Checkpoint 6.text:
A singular stairwell connects to this space, its landing hemmed in by an iron gate and watched by a pair of wary guards.

Beyond the gate the room is filled with long benches like a waiting room, and a half-circle desk manned by a guard acts as a receptionist.

A single, narrow door is the only exit available into the rest of this level.

This space is occupied by guards at all hours, and all guards present have keys to open the doors here, as do the rest of the guards on this level. The @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB#prison-doors]{Prison Doors} and walls are medium here.

Crystal Cluster.name: Crystal Cluster
Crystal Cluster.text:
A huge cluster of crystals rises from a basalt mound protruding from the roof. Each crystal is a little different, and each emits a pale lavender light, though the qualities of that light, from the richness of the color to the frequency that it pulses is unique.

A loud, modulating hum rolls out from the cluster of resonating crystals, swelling and dipping like a steady, resonant chord that you can feel in your bones.

Part of the Sum

A successful [[/skill arcana 15]] surmises that this is the source of the antimagic field that permeates the city district. The lack of any spell runes, symbols, seals, or wards makes the operation of this cluster an absolute mystery.

  • Result of 20+. While this huge clump of crystals is certainly generating a powerful antimagical field, given the size of the tower, the other nearby crystals, and the way energy is moving through the space, this is likely only one part of a mechanism that might be spread out through the entire district around the tower.

A Sliver of Crystal

The crystals are unbreakable in any practical sense, and cannot be destroyed or disabled. However, a character with proper tools (such as a prybar or pick) could separate a single @UUID[Item.SWNgMezQYmqSIuhC] from the cluster.

Attempts to get more than one automatically fail, even if attempted by different characters.

Blue Crystals.name: Blue Crystals
Blue Crystals.text:
A triangular blue crystal glows within a larger triangular housing made from black basalt, its polished facets gleaming brightly.

Thin rays of arcane energy spill from its edges in straight, shimmering lines, then curl and braid as they reach outward, entwining with distant strands drawn from other matching stones set around the tower.

Where the currents meet, the air flickers with a faint, steady shimmer. Periodically these swirling eddies of energy spiral down to the large cluster of crystals at the center of the area.

Magical Intake

A successful [[/skill arcana 16]] check suspects that the crystals are feeding energy into the central crystal cluster, possibly pulling it up from the rest of the tower.

Result of 21+ Given the extensive antimagical properties of the tower, it is quit possible that these gems are part of the mechanism siphoning magic into the central cluster.

Ballistae.name: Ballistae
Ballistae.text:
A raised platform of weathered planks supports a pair of large wooden ballista, their frames thick and splintered at the edges where the wood has dried and checked. The bow-arms sit slack, cords dulled and frayed, and the winching gears are crusted with rust, seized stiff in their housings.

The ladder up is rickety and suspect, in truth the whole emplacement looks neglected and long unused.

Unused Arsenal

Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]] of succeeding on a [[/skill perception 14]] check know that these weapons have not been maintained whatsoever. Attempting to use this weapon would pose a greater hazard to the operators than their intended target.

Cages.name: Cages
Cages.text:
On this raised brick platform are iron cages sized to hold a person, but not much else. Their thick bars are set close together, but their doors hang slightly open on crooked hinges. Rust grows where rain and moisture have been allowed to gather, causing streaks of orange to paint the sides of the cages.

This collection sits fully exposed to cutting wind and open weather, offering no shelter, no warmth, and nowhere to lie down, an arrangement that would make confinement here a long, raw misery.

Each show signs that they once held occupants, though it doesn't seem like they have been used in a long time. The cages are made of light iron bars with swinging doors, all of them are unlocked.

False Prisoners

If during the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL]{Diplomatic Impunity} event @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.TGOj5GcJdo3tsp85]{Breaking the Tower} the party manages to reach the roof of the tower [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityBreakout undetected]] then theses cages will each contain a @UUID[Actor.R478CwJEwZZhibaA]{Veiled Chain Agent} posing as cage occupants and ready to jump out and join the ensuing fight with @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND]{Loris Tezran} when he arrives.

Notable Inmates.name: Notable Inmates
Notable Inmates.text:
This list represents a roster of potential inmates the party can encounter throughout the prison blocks of Spellbreaker Tower. These inmates are not present in the preconfigured scenes, but can be represented by the provided inmate stat blocks. Feel free to create your own inmates, perhaps ones connected to characters in the party, or related to their backgrounds.

Blue Block Inmates

Serce Darran

A painter of some renown who specialized in realistic depictions of Ragen and its elementals. Out of the blue she went mad and began setting buildings on fire. Turns out a quirk of her high Ragen attunement is being easily possessed and influenced by corrupted elementals. The tower suppresses her elemental powers, but not the lingering pyromaniacal tendencies. Resides in Blue block when the urges get out of control, and lives on a lower level normally.

Norban Grozburn

A spellcaster convicted on several charges of destruction of property, intent to cause mayhem, assault with dangerous magic, and arson. He was arrested after flying over the city throwing fireballs. Utterly de-fanged in the tower, he is eccentric and antisocial, but harmless.

Nemi Korill

Claims to hear the Abyss commanding her to harm people. Has assaulted half a dozen people with weapons, and critically injured several. The tower seems to suppress the voices, and she is presently serving out her sentence, but is expected to be moved into a tower community afterward.

Marrit Marrison

Cursed with poison skin so that they could never get close to anyone, they attempted to live a normal life but eventually became bitter and disillusioned and began using their poison to make people ill, nearly killing several. Presently undergoing rehabilitation in Blue Block, and is expected to be moved into a lower level community in the future.

Vrover Bindman

A former Agrimage who was convicted of mass poisoning and destruction of property after he began tainting land and the crops growing on them. He is supposedly an agent of an "earth lord" who demands all the earth be turned rancid. Though magically disarmed, he refuses to recant his cause or be rehabilitated.

Yellow Block Inmates

Taskel the Tinker

A clockmaker and artificer of seemingly limited skill, Taskel killed twelve people and mangled twice as many in the last decade with "faulty" devices that would catastrophically fail in dangeorus ways. Chain investigation into his creations determined he was sabotaging the devices intentionally to harm people. His cell is searched weekly.

Flint Karsha

A famed musician, renowned for being able to play any instrument you give him. Beloved in every city he visited, it wasn't uncommon for fans to leave town with him. Trouble was, they'd never be seen again. His killing spree was ended when he was caught trying to lead a group of fans out of Ordain. Is not allowed access to music instruments, even while magically suppressed.

Corlin Juddit

A former member of the Cindaric faith, and a healer, they turned from performing life-saving surgery to collecting organs and selling them to an unknown buyer. They refused to give up their contact, and to this day show no remorse.

Mira Silvane

An herbalist and alchemist renowned for her medicines, she was jailed after she decided to make several batches of healing potions into lethal toxins, killing half a dozen people including two prominent Anachraenum adventurers.

Red Block Inmates

Skwang the Magnificent

Former stage magician; cheerful, his state routine involved making members of the audience disappear. Sometimes they never reappeared. Arrested in Ordain for attempted murder after a Veiled Chain investigation revealed that he would kill and hide the audience members if it was his final act in a city. He has been linked to over eighteen unsolved disappearances following his shows.

The Bleak Weaver

A strange, intelligent @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J]{Cheliceraeth} spider found hunting citizens in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.D0AAT8TNsytqy7Hm]{Quarry Run}. Seemingly invincible, it was fought to a standstill at which point it became dormant. Without any way to dispatch it permanently, the Hallows ordered it stored in Red Block. The tower has not suppressed whatever force makes it immortal.

Blood Drinker

A hulking vrjnhar that refuses to speak. They seem to serve as a chosen warrior for an unknown deity or force that demands they drink the blood of the slain. Their raw strength alone makes them dangerous, let alone the potent magical abilities the tower is actively suppressing.

The Cube

This hovering, humming, carved stone cube originated from the Cascillian Republic, though its origins have never been clearly established. It radiates a purely malevolent energy and when not suppressed is capable of drawing psychic energy from nearby beings, causing them to become erratic and violent before dying.

“Mercy”

Occupying the most locked-down cell in the tower's Red Block, Mercy appears to be nothing more than a middle-aged human woman. However, their rumored abilities are numerous, and change with each source; they might be are either a supernatural assassin, a rogue archmage, a Shard god, a being from beyond Ember, or something else entirely.

Damaged Cell.name: Damaged Cell
Damaged Cell.text:
This cell appears as any other, but keen eyes will notice that the back wall has suffered some damage that could be exploited.

Work in Progress

Hidden passage assets and interactivity are planned for this secret passage, and will be added in a future update.

Cracks in the Wall

A character with a [[/skill perception 16 passive]] or making either a successful [[/skill perception 14]] or [[/skill investigation 12]] check notices that the damage and cracks in the corner of this cell are more extensive than they might initially appear.

With proper tools, like a chisel and hammer, or mining pick it's possible for a character to break away the wall and possibly create a passage through the stone.

Doing so might take hours of conspicuous work, and hiding it would be all but impossible, but if done it would create a passage to a @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.Oang2HH4knNdCV1l] outside.

Rickety Platform.name: Rickety Platform
Rickety Platform.text:
Old, half-rotten wood hangs from corroded metal struts, the slats lashed together with frayed rope long past its prime. Possibly the remnant of some older construction effort, this platform seems as though it was forgotten when world concluded and was left to the mercy of the elements.

This rickety platform connects to the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.ANDypk5PFri9k4qR] and the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.dyPqEixnw7eHjAZf] and accessing either space through the damaged wall requires tools and considerable effort to widen the gaps on either side.

Falling Hazard

A character that falls or jumps from this platform without some way to land safely would suffer the maximum [[/damage 20d6 bludgeoning]] damage after falling about 250 feet.

Escape Options

This location provides a viable jumping off point for wingsuits.

Characters might consider this a viable location to tie off rope to climb down, and a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check will come to the conclusion that the rickety platform likely would work, but it wouldn't be the most stable or reliable point.

Wall Tunnel.name: Wall Tunnel
Wall Tunnel.text:
A long, pitch black tunnel winding through the basalt stone in the walls of the tower. Its shape and length guarantee that all visible light is gone before you even reach its first bend.

The origin of this tunnel is unknown, and was covered up some time ago. It is large enough for a small creature to move through at normal walking speed, and a medium sized creature to move through at half speed. It connects @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.jyEjb9CXfSzRRZCf] to the stairwell of the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.gzphhu9XASBBI6sw] area.

Red Block Cells.name: Red Block Cells
Red Block Cells.text:
The cells here are sparse, mattresses lie directly on the basalt floor with bedding piled atop them. The air near the bars tastes of smoke and the shadows cast through the bars feels harsher against the ample bare stone.

The fronts of these cells are built for endurance: thick, heavy iron bars and matching heavy iron jail doors seated on armored rails keep the occupants in permanently, and each looks to take effort to even open.

Cells are locked all hours and inmates are not let out except under full guard.

Webbed Cell.name: Webbed Cell
Webbed Cell.text:
This cell is coated with glittering, iridescent webbing wrapped tightly over the furnishings meant for more humanoid inmates. At the center of this arachnid's nest is a large spider made of faceted crystal. It watches you from the dark with glowing eyes.

This cell is home to a unique, and deadly creature:

The Bleak Weaver

A strange, intelligent @UUID[Actor.C8POmQfke7hHRQ9J]{Cheliceraeth} spider found hunting citizens in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.D0AAT8TNsytqy7Hm]{Quarry Run}. Seemingly invincible, it was fought to a standstill at which point it became dormant. Without any way to dispatch it permanently, the Hallows ordered it stored in Red Block indefinitely. The tower has not suppressed whatever force makes it immortal.

Garden.name: Garden
Garden.text:
Long planters line the perimeter of this platform, and crimson broadleaf ferns grow up alongside decorative shrubs with golden foliage. The warm colors are contrasted with points of stark white and blue flowers.

At the center of this garden a large circular fountain bubbles away loudly, as a stone-faced status of Avila the Spellbreaker looks on to the horizon.

The Spellbreaker

This statue is a small-scale recreation of the greater visage of Avilla that appears on the tower itself. Though some artistic liberties have been taken with the rest of the spellbreaker's form which the tower's depiction doesn't provide, it effectively captures the essence of the goddess.

Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] or making a successful [[/skill nature 13]] check note that the stone is the same basalt as the tower is made of, but has distinctly different patterns, indicating it was likely quarried from the region, but not from the same body of stone as the tower.

A placard at the base notes the statue was donated to the spellbreaker prison sixty years ago, and that the sculptor wished to remain anonymous.

Shooting Range.name: Shooting Range
Shooting Range.text:
A collection of weather beaten bows rest on tables alongside quivers stuffed with arrows. All around them are barrels, bales of hay, and dummies serving as targets.

Everything about this space is geared toward recreation, not training, and likely is used by the guards to entertain themselves when not on shift.

Worthless Weapons

Examining the bows and arrows on the tables here for a moment reveals that these are cast-off weapons, low quality, and not meant to see actual combat unless one had no other options.

There are six @UUID[Item.5r5lFkbTB5A6V2Et]{Battered Shortbows} available to be claimed here, along with several hundred low quality arrows. Together, these weapons deal only 1d4 piercing damage and have half the range of a normal bow due to their low quality.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

There are no specific requirements to begin this Side Quest, and it is available to the party at the start of Chapter 1. Most groups will likely experience the full course of these events after the party reaches @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}.

Difficulty

"Signal of Intent" is designed for a party of Level 2 characters. Its preliminary Events may be encountered by Level 1 party, but the main content of this Quest will naturally occur after the characters have advanced to Level 2.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 1 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point} upon successful completion of the [[/eventState signalIntentTower]] Event.

Long ago, two disparate cultures overlapped within this section of the Forest of Stone. The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} were the predominant group, living and mining the area. The Shent were monitored and surveilled by the expansive and powerful @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Empire from a hidden signalpost in the cliffs above. In the present day, while neither culture is currently active on Ember, evidence of their history and lives can be found throughout the region.

The Forest of Stone was once an outlying boundary of both the Aedir empire and Shent civilization. People from both cultures cohabitated the area, forming an uneasy acceptance of each other. The Aedir were wary that the Shent could become enemies opposing their imperial expansion. The Shent were wary that the Aedir would attempt to conquer their peaceful and philosophical mountain realm.

An unlikely friendship emerged between a Shent student and an Aedir researcher, their mutual passion for inquiry and discovery breaking through the frosty barrier between the peoples. A preserved historical record of these ancient scholars holds the key to modern day explorers being able to uncover and breach the halls of the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost}, a military research and observation tower standing atop bluffs high above the Forest of Stone.

The party will follow this trail of clues, explore the sealed outpost, and discover how materials from its Underforge have escaped containment to threaten the safety of the town of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta} in the ravine below.

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE]

  • @UUID[Actor.nJwL6Gxdv9fU7Dh5]

  • @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v]
Overview.soverview:
High above the Forest of Stone, an ancient tower stands shrouded in invisibility and long-abandoned by the ancient Aedir architects who built it to survey the outer boundary of their expanding empire. After silent millennia, the tower's power source has failed, allowing the structure to become periodically visible and for containment mechanisms within its Underforge to fail. From the bowels of this tower leak a contamination that has transformed the behavior and capability of local metallic oozes that dwell within the prismatic strata of the Kaleidoscope Caverns below.

In "Signal of Intent" you will learn about the complex history between the Aedir and Shent, two ancient cultures whose territorial boundaries overlapped in the Forest of Stone. Discovering remembrances of the Shent will provide the key to breaching the Aedir fortification. Within this tower, a multi-level explorable dungeon, you will learn more about the history of the world-spanning Aedir and identify the root cause of problems afflicting the settlement of Yakoshta in the valleys below.

Guarded Neighbors.name: Guarded Neighbors
Guarded Neighbors.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event occurs if the party investigates a specific section of the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.1jVbIkYzmXocJ1iH]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} a few miles northeast of @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta}. By exploring this cavern the party can:

  • Discern fragmented clues about how this place was used by the ancient @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.dKvFRTSqJcJwDeAJ]{Shent} culture.

  • Discover lost recordings that describe an unlikely relationship between a Shent carver and an Aedir researcher stationed nearby.

  • Translate a sequence of murals describe calamitous events of @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.GlwUGpaqvUorPF6q]{The Shattering}.

  • Locate a hidden cache of supplies which contains some curious antiquities.

Area Map

This event is played in the @UUID[Scene.emberKaleidoCave]{Kaleidoscope Caverns} area map. There is no specific area walkthrough text.

Investigating the Pedestal

The party will likely begin exploration of this cavern by inspecting the crystal pedestal at the mouth of the cave mentioned at the conclusion of the introduction. Each of the pedestal's three sides has script in a different language.

Reading the Pedestal

The three sides of the pedestal feature script written in [[/language pathward]], [[/language towyr]], and [[/language common]].

  • Characters who know one of these languages can each recognize and read the language they know or have learned to translate without a check.

  • Characters can also read each language by using the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplComprehend]{Comprehend Languages} spell or similar [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.versatileTransla]] talent.

  • For languages that are not familiar to the characters, the language can be identified with a successful [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] check. Characters who have encountered the language before can also identify it with a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] [[/skillCheck science 15]] check to see the similarities.

One of the three languages used on the pedestal is an older version of Common. Characters who succeed on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check can confirm that this is an early version of the language that became the Common Coin (also known as Common). It is readable, but distinct from the modern language.

Each set of symbols on the pedestal translates to the same phrase:

Our journey ends here. We cannot foresee what will yet come, so we leave these words for whomever comes after.

Illuminate the past by speaking our words and telling our tale. Begin with the beginning.

Activating the Pedestal

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15 passive]] check can guess that they should speak the words "the beginning."

  • Speaking the words in either [[/language common]] or [[/language pathward]] is straightforward.

  • Speaking the words in [[/language towyr]] is difficult, as scholars do not know how to pronounce the words — characters must succeed on a [[/skill history 18]] [[/skillCheck society 18]] check to puzzle it out enough to activate the pedestal.

When the pedestal is activated:

A glow emanates from within the purple depths of the carved crystal, bathing the area immediately around it with a soft lavender light. This light reflects ever so subtly from one crystal in the cave to the next, making the images carved into the walls stand out more clearly. This is not one large overlapping image but four separate murals, each on a different surface of the cavern walls.

Seeing the Light

If the pedestal has been activated and is emitting light, characters with [[/skill perception 16 passive]] or who succeed on a [[/skill perception 14]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 16 passive]] notice a crystal near the pedestal that appears to be somewhat out of place.

The sharp lines of the crystal don't connect the way they should, as if it was somehow removed from its resting place and then wedged back, and its glow is a slightly bluer tint than the other crystals nearby.

Recording Crystals

Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or who succeed on an [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check can identify the crystal as a Recording Crystal, a magical gemstone that can be used to store spoken words and replay them in a language familiar to the listener. Only advanced mages are capable of the technique to create such crystals, but they can be activated by anyone regardless of magical talent.

  • Characters who have previously encountered such a crystal in [[/eventState signalIntentCrystals]] automatically succeed on this check.

If characters touch the crystal while concentrating on the intention for the crystal to replay its recording, a voice comes out of it:

A voice rings out from the crystal, young-sounding and bright, speaking in an exaggerated whisper.

I know. This is not a time to dawdle. This is a time to work. But my hands have made these same motions so many times and there's something to be learned from hiding a message in plain sight.

If you discover this small rebellion, feel free to assign me an extra task. Write "Chiseqi" down on your list as many times as you wish. As I have been told more than once when struggling towards a new goal, the accomplishment is generally worth the consequence.

I shall leave these notes as annotations to my carving, perhaps a small hope that our work will endure and someone may yet hear them.

Hidden Recordings

Somewhere nearby to each of the four murals in the cavern is another Recording Crystal. These crystals are placed unobtrusively to evade notice except for the keen-eyed.

  • Mural Dark: The Recording Crystal can be spotted with a successful [[/skill investigation 18]] or [[/skill perception 18]] [[/skillCheck awareness 18]] check.

  • Mural Illuminated: The Recording Crystal can be spotted with a successful [[/skill investigation 13]] or [[/skill perception 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check.

When they party investigates and discovers a Recording Crystal, the messages should be revealed in the following order, regardless of the order in which the murals are investigated.

Recorded Message 1

I am better at erasing my tracks than I thought — so far as I can tell, no one has read my last message. I quite like the idea of being able to speak into the void with no idea of who might listen - it's freeing, almost like speaking to the moons.

I can tell you that I am growing weary of the chisel, or that these crystals sometimes make my head throb, or that I'm probably more curious than I should be about the tower the Aedir Empire is trying to hide up in the cliffs. I wouldn't admit it to anyone else, but the tower fascinates me. I wish there was some way to say hello.

Recorded Message 2

I have to tell someone, and you're all that I have, so here's my small confession: I went up to the cliffs today, to try to get a glimpse of what the Aedir do on that tower. I'm not sure why I'm so intrigued. Maybe it's that the Aedir are a bit of a mystery to me - they're arrogant and powerful and they appear to be everywhere, but we Shent don't interact much with the Empire. After all, we're fairly sure they're going to break the world one day. So why do I want to get closer?

Perhaps it is curiosity, perhaps boredom, or perhaps it is an intuition that we must connect with those we distrust in order to survive this breaking world.

Recorded Message 3

I saw someone. Up on the cliffs. Orbis only knows why I've taken to going up there so frequently. Taking "walks", I say. In truth just staring at where I think the tower is, even though I lack the arcana to perceive it. There's probably a lesson in that, though I can't quite puzzle it out.

All I know is that staring is why I saw her, running through the cliffs for just a moment, glancing back over her shoulder. As if she shouldn't be there. We have that, at least, in common.

Recorded Message 4

The woman I saw? A researcher in the invisible tower, which they call the "signalpost" — more likely a "spy post", but I digress. Her name is Golarne.

We have talked together each evening beneath Orbis' shimmer. Perhaps we both know better, and yet the spirit moon has willed us forward. Golarne swears that she is only there for research, but the Empire doesn't waste an opportunity. She doesn't appear to enjoy alchemy more than I enjoy chiseling, but at least we can talk to each other and I can stop bothering you.

She even gifted me a few trinkets that I've buried near the northern mural. The world is a shaky place these days. It never hurts to be ready.

The Four Murals

There are four separate murals within the cavern, each of which is a piece of swirling line art that incorporates 3-4 runic symbols in a larger picture.

For each of the murals, the runes and the picture can be used together to determine the meaning of the drawing and hint at a phrase which activates the mural when spoken aloud. Each mural embeds within its design a number of key runes. The art to decoding each mural is to identify these runes and to utter them aloud in the correct order.

Once a mural has been decoded and activated, it begins to glow with lambent illumination, casting bright light in the immediate vicinity for 1 hour. This light does not trigger any effects from kaleidoscope crystals in the cavern.

Interpreting the Murals

Any character who can read or is otherwise familiar with [[/language pathward]], or who succeeds on a [[/skill history 14]] or [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] or [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check, recognizes these as runic symbols once used by the giants of the Shent.

For each mural, characters may attempt the following checks to assist with solving that mural's puzzle:

  • A successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check to discern how many runes are incorporated into each individual picture by separating those runes from the broader picture.

  • A successful [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check to clear away the natural decay that has affected the murals, including any heartmoss that has grown into the stone or mold that obscures the symbol.

  • A successful [[/skill arcana 16]] [[/skillCheck arcana 16]] check to interpret what the individual runes on each stone mean. Once a rune is translated on a specific stone, it remains translated for any future stones without a check.

  • Any character that knows [[/language pathward]] gains @Advantage[2] on these checks.

Signara Attunement: Decode a Mural

Decoding the murals is an act of Curiosity, rewarding characters with an increase to their Signara Attunement.

Each character that played an investigative role in decoding one or more of the murals advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 signalIntentNeighbors]] attunement upon the conclusion of the event.

The Eastern Mural

The eastern mural depicts a scene of the ancient Shent traveling a great distance into a rocky landscape.

A swirling line drawing chiseled into the cavern wall depicts group of humanoids standing around an empty vehicle, their backs to an unfamiliar line of rocky cliffs. A few of the cliffs appear to have shallow puddles on them. The cliffs are steep, but have lines that seem out of place, as if something has been traced onto them.

Decoding the Eastern Mural

This mural contains three runes: Shent, Stone, and Travel.

With a successful [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] , characters know that the landscape reflects what the Forest of Stone would have looked like thousands of years ago and that the puddles are likely natural ooze pools.

With a successful[[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check, they know that the Shent are thought to have traveled through the Arctus Plateau 2000 years ago, in vehicles that look roughly like the travel rune.

With understanding of [[/language pathward]] or a [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check, the runes can be combined to roughly mean:

“The Shent travel to the stone.”

If the word "travel" is spoken aloud within 20 feet of the mural:

The mural begins to emit a soft glow, and the runes that make up the humanoids appear to shift slightly on the wall, as if they were waving out at whoever watches them.

The Southern Mural

The southern mural depicts a scene of the Shent gazing at the sky and venerating the moons.

The lines of this drawing depict a group of humanoids standing on a rocky plain, staring at an object in the sky above them. It appears as if rays or beams are coming down from the object, touching both the humanoids and a pool in the distance. Each ray looks like a slightly different symbol.

Decoding The Southern Mural

This mural contains four runes: Shent, Stone, Reverence, and Water.

With a successful [[/skill history 14]] or [[/skill religion 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check, characters know that the Shent held deep reverence for the moons.

  • Result of 20+ Critical Success or [[/attunement emberMayis]]: You identify the circular object as the water moon, Mayis.

  • With a successful [[/skill nature 14]][[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check, characters can place the location – as somewhere in the vicinity of Yakoshta.

With understanding of [[/language pathward]] or a successful [[/skill insight 15 ]][[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check, the runes on this stone can be combined to roughly mean:

“The Shent of the stone honor and celebrate the moon and the creatures of the water.”

If the words "honor" or "moon" are spoken aloud within 20 feet of the mural:

The rays on the mural appear to glisten and glow, and light shines from the depiction of the moon above, creating moonbeam like light on the cavern around it.

The Western Mural

The western mural depicts the arrival of the Aedir and the construction of their tower on the bluffs high above this area.

In this mural, a large and imposing tower on a cliff blocks the orb in the sky. The tower surrounded by a group of faceless humanoids made of sharp, angled strokes, different from those on the other stones. They stare down at the humanoids seen in the previous stone.

Decoding The Western Mural

This mural contains three runes: Shent, Tower, Others.

With a successful [[/skill perception 14]] or [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]] check, characters can identify the tower as having been in the direction they are traveling to. With a successful [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check, characters know that the Aedir were active around this time period as well, and may be the faceless humanoids depicted.

With understanding of [[/language pathward]] or a successful [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check, the runes on this stone can be combined to roughly mean:

“The others watch the Shent."

If the word "watch" is spoken aloud within 20 feet of the mural:

The glow in this mural seems to emanate from the tower - it flickers almost like a fire, as do the faces of the humanoids surrounding it, almost as if there is something dangerous and out of control in their very presence. The crystals near the mural seem to flicker in response, casting a glowing light on the ground.

The Northern Mural

The northern mural depicts the calamitous consequences of The Shattering and the destruction of the Sun Tower.

The land beneath the tower in this mural is splintered and shattered. Glyphs appear to have been created with the jagged lines in the land. In the midst of the splintered ground, the faceless humanoids flee the tower.

Decoding The Northern Mural

This mural contains three runes: Tower, Others, Break

All characters know, without a check, that this stone references The Shattering, an event in which the Aedir broke the world.

With understanding of [[/language pathward]] or a successful [[/skill insight 15]] [[/skillCheck arcana 15]] check, the runes on this Stone can be combined to roughly mean:

"The world breaks. The others go."

If the word "break" is spoken aloud within 20 feet of the mural:

Light appears to pour out from across the mural, lighting the nearby walls and floor.

A Hidden Cache

The Shent carver Chiseqi stashed some supplies and trinkets near the northern mural in a creche between large stalagmites.

Locating the Cache

Discovering this cache unaided requires a successful [[/skill investigation 35]] [[/skillCheck awareness 35]] check in response to the party wishing to search the cavern for items of interest. The difficulty can be reduced in the following ways:

  • Knowledge of the cache's existence and that it is located near the northern mural (from listening to Recorded Message 4) reduces the DC by 10.

  • If all four murals have been decoded, the cavern is bathed in consistent illumination, further reducing the DC by 10.

Once the cache has been located, it can be easily removed from the ground. It contains:

  • Antique coins worth [[/award 20gp]] [[/award 2gp]]

  • 2 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.items.Item.ytlsBjYsZ7OBSEBs]{Potion of Healing} 1 @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingElixir000] and 1 @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rallyingElixir00] sealed within unbroken glass vials

  • A charm bracelet, whose gems can be used as a spell component or sold for [[/award 5gp]] [[/award 50sp]]

  • A carefully folded note tucked neatly at the bottom of the cache

The note is written in [[/language towyr]]. If inspected by someone who knows the language or has the means to translate it, it reads:

The ancient note is written in a scribbled and uneven hand on ancient vellum.

Chiseqi,

I wanted you to know how glad I am that we met. I remember your words and will use them to focus my task during the days ahead. It won't make the days go any faster, but I will see you beneath the stars once my work is done and I promise we will go exploring soon.

As thanks for your friendship, I invite you to see our work as I do. Trace this glyphsign upon the lens of the clarion shrine I showed you. I will hear it when you do and meet you there.

Golarne

Beneath the signature is an sketched diagram of a spiral with three diagonal lines of differing lengths cutting across its curvature.

The depicted glyph is unique, and cannot be recognized as belonging to any particular language or known spellcraft. If the party discovers this note and the associated glyphsign depicted within, mark the following outcome as completed.

[[/outcome glyph]]

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

This event provides an initial clue that establishes the later events of this quest. There is no immediate follow-up, but the information gained here will be important in the subsequent events:

  • In [[/eventState signalIntentCrystals]], the party can learn about Chiseqi's tragic fate.

  • In [[/eventState signalIntentRevealed]], the party can use the glyphsign learned here as a means of revealing the hidden tower.

  • In [[/eventState signalIntentTower]], the party will learn more about the relationship between Chiseqi and Golarne.
Guarded Neighbors.soverview: During their travels through the Forest of Stone, the party encounters a crystal-lined cavern once used by the Shent that contains a record of their time in the area. With a thorough search of the cavern, the party can find the record of a friendship between a Shent carver and an Aedir researcher, despite the standoffishness between their two peoples.
Guarded Neighbors.sexposition:
Piles of tools sit scattered throughout the cavern, each made from the same purple crystalline material as the Kaleidoscope Crystals protruding from the rocky floor. That same purple hue reflects from elaborate etchings on the cave wall around you, glittering as they reflect the meager light that reaches into the cave from outside. Each is an overlap of lines and symbols that appears to create a picture of some kind, though it isn't clear, at first glance, what the images are or mean.

By the door to the cave, one of the purple crystals is larger than the others and has smoother edges, as if it has been carved into a trilateral pedestal. Upon each of the pedestal's three sides are carved a few words or glyphs — in a different style or language on each side — including one side which appears to be an antiquated variant of Common.
Guarded Neighbors.ssummary: We found a cavern filled with murals left behind by the Shent - a window into what life was like in the Forest of Stone of the past.

Multifaceted.name: Multifaceted
Multifaceted.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration and combat event, the party discovers unsettling remnants of a destroyed Shent machine within the depths of the Kaleidoscope Caverns. Clues found here foreshadow a terrible conflict against abyssal forces, and investigation of the machine draws forth lingering malevolent echoes of abyssal energy that assault the party!

  • Discover and investigate the ancient remains of the dead Shent, possibly learning how they died so suddenly and so gruesomely.

  • Investigate the carved crystals the Shent were making, and perhaps glean some insight into what they were doing with them.

  • Study and figure out what the purpose of the strange metal machine was sitting in the middle of the caves. It appears to be Shent-made, but unlike anything seen before.

  • Survive an ambush by @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE]{Abyssal Echoes} provoked by the party's investigation.

Examining the Shent Remains

Remains of giant folk are strewn about the cavern. Some are seemingly ripped apart, others are broken where they smashed against crystals, and several were crushed by chunks of rock and crystal which seem to have fallen from overhead. Aside from these grievous wounds, the bodies seem to be remarkably intact as if undisturbed since the moment they fell.

Giant-sized tools and implements lay in their hands or nearby their bodies, hinting that they died suddenly, perhaps in the midst of work or defending themselves. Numerous crystals line the walls and lay on the ground, many of them carved and adorned with runic carvings. There are countless additional crystals strewn about that appear to be half-carved, or shattered by some hard impact. All around the corpses you can see places where the crystals were being cut from the cavern walls and carved for some purpose.

The long-rotten and crumbling remains of dead Shent can be found all over, most laying in piles of shattered crystals and stone, laying next to their tools. The party may wish to investigate the giant remains.

Examining the Dead

Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]] or [[/skill insight 14 passive]][[/skillCheck medicine 12 passive]] surmise that this destruction was very one-sided, and more of a massacre than a battle between balanced sides.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check is able to identify a few more details about these tattered remains:

  • There are no signs of scavenging or plunder that suggest the cavern has been disturbed since the event.

  • These bodies have been left here undisturbed to rot for ages. The cave likely played some role in slowing their decay, either by shielding the corpses from outside influences, or via whatever magic is present in the crystals.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The characters may wish to also investigate the ancient and broken tools strewn about the cavern.

Examining the Tools

The huge tools laying here have become corroded beyond saving, let alone use. Among their rusted number you count chisels, rasps, hammers, and picks all meant to be used in the carving of crystals. Strangely, many of these tools bear mystical symbols. Perhaps they held magic once?

A successful [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check reveals the presence of crystals bearing transmutation runes meant to make the tools sturdier, protect them from wear and corrosion, and even resize them dynamically to the user's hand. However, the crystals are cracked, cloudy, and burned out, leaving the tools to the ravages of the elements and time.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

In addition to investigating the Shent remains, the party may wish to inspect the crystal shards that were evidently being carved within this cavern.

Examining the Crystals

A successful [[/skill nature 12]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 12]] check while examining the crystals recognizes that there are numerous shattered crystals everywhere among the shards and chips that would have naturally come from shaping them. Something or someone deliberately destroyed them. It might have been the carvers, but it might not have been.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The crystals in this cavern have all regrown since being harvested, a process which would have taken thousands of years. The carvers, their tools, and these crystals must all be equally ancient.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge ancients]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Characters may attempt to ascertain the properties of these crystals. Inspection with a successful [[/skill arcana 12]] [[/skillCheck arcana 12]] check determines that these crystals were all carved in unique pattern groups and styles, each one bearing various, interlocking runes with differing magical applications. They all fall under very archaic but easily identified archetypes of evocation, transmutation, and abjuration, all meant to work in concert toward a single effect.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: The runes were actively shaping the magic in the crystals to draw out desired effects or impart specific functions. The crystals here are all either incomplete or entirely inert, the runes having burned themselves out over the years. You suspect that when they were newly made they might have made strong power sources, or useful elements of more complex magical applications. Several of the crystals present had a notably different design from the others; focused on the abjuration of illusion and mind-affecting magics. Only a few of the crystals bear these markings, and none of them were ever completed. Without a finished one to study you can't be entirely sure what their ultimate purpose was.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Examining the Ancient Machine

An ominous dome of metal attracts your gaze in the dark, and as you draw closer the sight only grows stranger: a massive machine, tarnished and splayed open like a carcass. It seems that whatever damaged the object also killed whoever was nearby it. It is splattered with long dried and oxidized blood, and a broken, skeletal corpse of a giant lays scattered at the base of the structure.

The party may wish to examine the machinery to try and ascertain its purpose. If any character in the party touches the ancient machine, interrupt their investigation and proceed to the "Destructive Echoes" section, below.

Examining the Machine

With a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check while looking at the remnants, characters can safely rule out mechanical failure. The damage the device sustained propagates inward, leaving you to surmise that the structure was attacked and the ensuing damage is what caused the subsequent failure. What's notable about this though, is that the metal is unlike simple bronze or iron, and the force and power required to punch a hole through it would therefore need to be immense.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

A successful [[/skill history 15]] /skillCheck society 15means characters know the Shent are most well known for their prolific and intricate stonework. There are few cases of Shent-built machines made of metal in recorded history, making this an exceptionally rare find, and one sure to cause an uproar with historians.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Inspecting the machine with a successful[[/skill religion 13]] /skillCheck society 13 check reveals a general absence of religious or lunar markings, which is strange. Most surviving Shent structures and items that utilize magic almost always also include some religious markings venerating or drawing from the moon. This has none of that.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Attempting to discern the purpose of the machine is likely to trigger the abyssal ambush, but such an investigation may be safely continued after that combat is resolved.

Discerning the Purpose of the Machine

Physical inspection of the great machine involves an [[/skill arcana 12]] [[/skillCheck arcana 12]] check to speculate upon its original purpose. With a successful check, you surmise this was once a machine intended to generate and project a field of magical energy. The presence of numerous shattered crystals inside the housing tell you that the cavern's crystals likely played a part in its function.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: Thorough examination of the machine, and piecing together some of the scattered pieces gives you a fuller picture of this machine's true purpose. It used archaic abjuration, conjuration, and evocation runes to move power from some sort of core to the outer regions of the machine where it resonated with numerous cavern crystals. You believe that the abjuration effect produced by the machine would have dampened the environmental effects of these caverns. It is hard to imagine the field's scale, but the extensive power of the device and the nature of its evocation runes leads you to believe that it produced a massive field that could have stretched for miles, mitigating or disrupting the disorienting effects of the Kaleidoscope Caverns within that radius.

  • The prevalence of abjuration as a major facet of the magic leads you to believe it was protecting or stopping something. When in operation it would have produced a field of energy that dampened the effects of the caverns here.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

It does not seem possible to repair the machine or restore its functionality, as it is too ancient and too devastatingly damaged.

Signara Attunement: Discerning the Machine's Purpose

Whichever character identifies the original purpose of the machine — to disrupt the disorientating effects caused by the Kaleidoscope Caverns environment — advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 overMoonLoreMachine]] upon the conclusion of this event.

Abyssal Echoes

Whenever a character physically touches the machine, interrupt their investigation with the following readaloud and subsequent combat encounter.

The ancient metal is cold to the touch and seemingly inert, and yet the grim diorama before you manifests a looming dread within the recesses of your mind. For a brief moment you can clearly imagine the moment in time when these giants witnessed the destruction of their work and the deep-voiced screams of horror as something came forth …

Your imagination is interrupted by a subtle shimmer of motion at the periphery of your vision and the exact same giant screams that you imagined now heard in truth as an echo that replays and resounds throughout the cavern.

Rising from within the ribcages of several giant remains are horrible smoke-writhed apparitions that immediately move to attack the party.

@Embed[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE count=3]{Abyssal Echo}

Abyssal Echo Tactics

The three Abyssal Echoes are distributed on different sides of the cavern, they will each initially attack the character closest to them rather than concentrating their efforts.

Once any character becomes &Reference[frightened] or &Reference[deafened], all remaining Echoes will break away from their current engagements, using their Fly speed and @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.gHXWVaidho85zB1L]{Pack Tactics} to concentrate attacks on that target.

On their turn, each Abyssal Echo will use @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.cMDpGjHKzXd2im33]{Swallowed Screams} to create fields of Silence that prevent the party from communicating or casting spells. They will follow-up with @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.P6VruIOK3ctYTiZ2]{Malignant Slash} to destroy any living creature nearby.

When an Abyssal Echo is destroyed, it dissolves, leaving behind @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.5ww5bC5eQN2D45gC]{Abyssal Remains} which creates an area of melted shadow afflicting any creature that enters it with a Cursed Vision effect.

Once any character becomes @Condition[frightened] or @Condition[silenced], all remaining Echoes will break away from their current engagements, taking advantage of their @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.packhunter000000]{Pack Hunter} to concentrate attacks on that target.

During combat turns, Abyssal Echoes use @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.swallowedScreams]{Swallowed Screams} to harass and afflict targets with @Condition[silenced], prevent them from communicating or casting spells before following up with vicious attacks using their @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.AoDrw0vw5e1R0RF8]{Shadow Talons}.

When an Abyssal Echo is destroyed, it dissolves, leaving behind @UUID[Actor.XU0Wy6EdRtuQmtOE.Item.abyssalRemains00]{Abyssal Remains} in a 4 foot radius outward from its position, any creature within the area or who enters it in a subsequent turn suffers the effects of the remains.

The Shent Carver's Remains

As the party prepares to leave the cavern, they have an opportunity to recover something useful. A final set of giant remains sitting against the cavern wall to the southeast of the machine attracts attention.

You observe the broken remains of a giant hunched in a seated position against the cavern wall to the southeast of the device. The figure's skeletal fist appears to be clutching something close to their chest. Upon closer inspection, you see a curious trilateral crystal with a distinctive blue tint, different in its oblong dimensions and coloration than the others found in this cavern. The crystal is fastened to a pendant chain, upon which dangles a distinctively shaped piece of metal that is elegant bifurcated into two twin prongs.

These are the remains of Chiseqi, the Shent carver whose memories the party may locate in the [[/eventState signalIntentNeighbors]] event.

A Carver's Demise
