Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or who succeed on an [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check can identify the crystal as a Recording Crystal, a magical gemstone that can be used to store spoken words and replay them in a language familiar to the listener. Only advanced mages are capable of the technique to create such crystals, but they can be activated by anyone regardless of magical talent.

  • Characters which have previously encountered such a crystal in [[/eventState signalIntentNeighbors]] automatically succeed on this check.

If characters touch the crystal while concentrating on the intention for the crystal to replay its recording, a voice emanates from it:

The hesitant sound of a woman's voice emanates from the crystal, her voice is high-pitched and flutters with anxiety although it carries an undercurrent of sorrow.

My dear friend, I am sorry I was not here to meet you. Orders have come. We are leaving the Signalpost. We go to the Sunwell to make a stand until a portal can extract us. This land is lost to the encroaching darkness. Return north to your haven peaks and be safe, I implore you.

Live, Chiseqi, and remember our friendship as I will cherish yours.

The message bears no indication of its author, however the party may speculate as to whose voice is recorded here. The message was recorded by Golarne, a researcher stationed at the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost}, who formed an unlikely companionship with Chiseqi in the months following The Shattering.

Attached to the recording crystal is an unidentified @UUID[Item.PXTk8eHOkgIo3Nsp]{Clarion Fork}, a device used in conjunction with certain scrying lenses to disrupt invisibility fields and reveal objects or locations concealed by ancient Aedir magi. If the party investigates Chiseqi's remains and obtains the Clarion Fork, mark the following outcome as completed.

[[/outcome fork]]

In the vicinity of Chiseqi's remains, the party can spot an additional valuable item that may be recovered.

Something Useful Remains

Characters with [[/skill perception 14 passive]] or a successful [[/skill investigation 12]] check [[/skillCheck awareness 14 passive]] notice an intricately carved shard of prismatic crystal face-up on the floor of the cavern. It is engraved with runic markings which ripple with a faint glimmer if illuminated by a source of light.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] or who succeed on a [[/skill insight 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] check infer that this shard might have been expelled from the large machine during its destruction.

  • Analysis with a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]] check suggests that the shard has unbroken and functional abjuration wards set upon it that might offer protection against something. With the application of a bit of cord or chain, it could be fashioned into a wearable pendant.

If the party retrieves this item, they obtain an unidentified @UUID[Item.cfTTrbcPgR14xc1f].

Concluding the Event

Having explored these corpse-laden caverns and the mysteries they contain, the party may continue on their exploration of the Forest of Stone.

Next Steps

The clues obtained here may not be immediately useful to the party, but they will resurface later as they explore more of the region.

  • The party can learn more about Chiseqi, the Shent carver, in [[/eventState signalIntentNeighbors]].

  • The @UUID[Item.PXTk8eHOkgIo3Nsp] can be used to reveal the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost} in [[/eventState signalIntentRevealed]].
Multifaceted.soverview: The party discovers a withdrawn cavern of prismatic crystals. In the midst of them they can find evidence that the Shent were carving the crystals, and imbuing them with magic. Even stranger is an odd machine made by long-ago giants that now sits dormant and ripped open. More questions than answers can be found here among these forgotten, broken things.
Multifaceted.sexposition:
The cavern's eerie silence is pierced only by the faint, haunting sound that seems to resonate from the shimmering crystals and the sounds you make reflecting back at you in strange ways, creating echoes that come from unpredictable directions.

As your eyes adjust, the unsettling details come into focus — dark, ominous stains mar the ethereal beauty of the cavern, and giant, moldering bones litter the ground, hinting at a violent past that lurks beneath the surface of this mesmerizing place.
Multifaceted.ssummary: We discovered a vast cave of crystals that were being cut away from the walls and carved by a ancient giants. Within the cavern was a strange machine that served some inscrutable and arcane purpose. The signs of carnage inside the cave suggested that something horrible befell these people.

The Tower Revealed.name: The Tower Revealed
The Tower Revealed.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration event, the party confronts a challenging natural obstacle, discovers an ancient ruin, and is tantalized by the appearance of a mystical tower which appears against the distant horizon. In this event, the party can:

  • Witness the brief appearance of the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost}.

  • Examine the ancient shrine which sits beside the chasm edge and enact the means to make the tower visible for longer than a fleeting glimpse.

  • Decide how best to surmount a challenging environmental obstacle.

The Flickering Tower

At some point during this event, the party's inspection of the crevasse and the shrine should be interrupted suddenly by the unexpected appearance of the distant tower.

Reveal Timing

As the Gamemaster, introduce this narrative moment whenever the party's engagement with prior clues seems to slow down or when they are at an impasse about what to do next.

Your inspection of the crevasse and the nearby shrine is suddenly interrupted as your gaze shifts reflexively upwards in response to sudden movement. The light around you seems to shift, as if unseen clouds parted somewhere in the sky overhead. In the distance, a tower appears where nothing stood a second before, jutting out of the ground like an enormous cylindrical tree of metal and stone. Its gray edifice is cracked and craggy, ravaged by nature and time, but it is still there, unmistakably looming over the ground around it. Then, as soon as it appeared, it disappears, flickering briefly between seen and unseen until it vanishes completely.

This momentary glimpse of the tower affords each member of the party a split second to try and recognize what it was that they saw.

Now You See It…

Each character is allowed to make one (and only one) attempted skill check from the following list, learning the corresponding pieces of information upon a success.

[[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]]

The shape and profile of the tower matches the signature architectural design of the ancient Aedir Empire. Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

[[/skill arcana 14]] [[/skillCheck arcana 14]]

It is unlikely that the tower itself has moved, but rather that some magic or artifice has shrouded its appearance. If the tower is shrouded using magic, it must be an exceptionally powerful invisibility field to cover such a large area.

[[/skill perception 14]] [[/skillCheck awareness 14]]

It seemed as if there was some extensive weathering or damage to the stonework on the facade of the tower, suggesting long-term abandonment or neglect.

[[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]]

The general location of where the tower appeared is likely very close to, and far above, the location of Yakoshta is in the valley far below.

Now You Don't!

The quick disappearance of the tower makes it very challenging to discern much information about it. Any character who rolls a result of 20 or greater achieves a Critical Success on their check may attempt a second check from the same list.

If the characters try and wait for the tower to appear again, it will flicker once more in exactly [[/gmroll 20d20 # Minutes]] minutes. The unpredictable timing of such appearances means that unless the party is paying constant attention, the tower's momentary appearance is likely to be missed.

Any further information to be gleaned about the tower will need to be observed upon reaching the structure, but only if the party can safely cross the intervening chasm.

The Crevasse

The party will likely wish to investigate the area and its shrine more closely before attempting to cross, however they must eventually do so in order to continue on their journey. This is a perilous enterprise, but there are several methods by which the heroes might succeed.

Traversing the Crevasse

The crevasse is 30 feet from side to side and deep enough that descending offers no hope of achieving a crossing.

  • If one character were able to cross while bearing one end of a long rope, it would be achievable to secure a rope on both sides of the chasm.

  • A character that wishes to heroically jump the distance would require a horizontal jump distance of 30 feet in order to succeed. This could potentially be enabled via the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplJump000000]{Jump} spell or the Kiska @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.cnaWBYATyGPvQtBY]{Nimble Leap} feature.

  • A character might use magical aid to cross, for example via the UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMistyStep0] spell.

  • A character with rope and a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagGrapplingHo]{Grappling Hook} can successfully throw and affix the rope to a secure object on the far side of the crevasse by succeeding on subsequent [[/skill athletics 14]] and [[/skill sleightOfHand 14]] checks.

  • If one character were able to cross while bearing one end of a long rope, it would be achievable to secure a rope on both sides of the chasm.

  • A character that wishes to heroically jump the distance would require a horizontal jump distance of 30 feet in order to succeed.

  • A character might use magical aid to cross.

  • A character with rope and a @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.grapnel000000000] can successfully throw and affix the rope to a secure object on the far side of the crevasse by succeeding on subsequent [[/skill athletics 14]] checks.

Bridging the Gap

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check notice that there is one aspen in the vicinity of adequate height and proximity to the ledge that, if it were toppled at the correct angle, might span the gap.

The party can make only one attempt to fell the tree, requiring a successful [[/skill survival 15]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 15]] check for the tree to fall at the correct angle to form a makeshift bridge.

Falling Into the Crevasse

Should any character be ill-fated enough to fall into the crevasse, they and one nearby party member may both make a desperate [[/save dexterity 16]] saving throw [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] check to attempt and arrest their fall. If neither character succeeds, the individual who fell into the crevasse disappears into the darkness below and perishes, their body is impossible to recover.

Regardless of the method used, once the party has safely navigated the crossing, mark the following outcome as completed.

[[/outcome traversed]]

Ragen Attunement: Crevasse Crossing

Whomever in the party was the first to cross the crevasse advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 windingTrailTowerCrevasse]] upon the conclusion of this event.

Region Map Change

Marking the crevasse as traversed removes an impassable boundary from the Region Map and allows the party to continue traveling towards the Aedir Signalpost.

The Clarion Shrine

The party will likely wish to investigate the circular wayshrine constructed atop a low rise nearby, overlooking the chasm ahead.

The partially-ruined structure nearby is a circular colonnade, nearly 20 feet in diameter, built upon a rise of rock overlooking the surrounding area. In the center of its enclosure is a low round pedestal with a slightly domed top covered in moss and dirt. The portions of this dome which are not covered by overgrowth have a smooth, almost glassy, surface. On one side of this pedestal is a metal rod that protrudes outward several inches like a singular spoke.

This small shrine served as a waypoint and control device for the invisibility field shrouding the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost}. Its magic could still function today, if the party is able to invoke the correct command.

Investigating the Clarion Shrine

Inspection of the shrine and the central pedestal requires some effort to clear away moss and debris which covers it. This consumes some amount of time but does not require any particular skill check. Investigation of the shrine and the pedestal reveals the following information:

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check note that the architecture of this small monument matches the design of the Aedir empire.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 19+ Critical Success: This structure seems illogical to exist in isolation and you surmise that it must represent some sort of wayshrine or marker upon the path to some other more significant destination.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill arcana 13]] [[/skillCheck arcana 13]] check note that the design of this pedestal suggests that it is likely the focal point for some spellcraft or arcane ritual.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi] @Spell[illusion.sense] spell confirms latent enchantments of illusion and divination upon the glassy lens.

  • Result of 18+ Critical Success or [[/knowledge artifacts]]: You are familiar with the concept of a Clarion Lens, an artifact generally associated with the Aedir that is designed specifically to control or penetrate certain illusions.

If the party has learned of [[/eventState signalIntentNeighbors glyph]], then they are able to recognize that this is the "clarion shrine" mentioned in Golarne's message to Chiseqi.

If the party has discovered the [[/eventState signalIntentCrystals fork]], then a character who succeeds on an a [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck science 13]] check can notice that the style of the metalwork of the @UUID[Item.PXTk8eHOkgIo3Nsp]{Clarion Fork} matches almost identically to the style of the metal spoke protruding from the pedestal here.

Revealing the Unseen

This Clarion Shrine provides the intended mechanism for revealing the Aedir Signalpost tower. The tower can be revealed in any of the following ways:

If a character strikes the @UUID[Item.PXTk8eHOkgIo3Nsp]{Clarion Fork} against the metal spoke:

A shrill and pure note rings out across the mountain highlands, cutting through the moist air. The sound is piercing, if not necessarily painful to hear. In immediate response to this tone, the cloudy lens on the pedestal before you swirls and clarifies, revealing a distinctive shape suspended within the glassy dome; a spiral with three diagonal lines of differing lengths that cut across its curvature. This glyph shines with a pale blue light and in the distance you behold the rippling motion of illusion as the distant horizon changes shape and reveals the striking silhouette of a tall tower isolated against the sky.

If a character traces the geometry of Golarne's glyphsign upon the lens:

You trace a specific sign upon the lens, a spiral with three diagonal lines of differing lengths that cut across its curvature. The smudges left by your finger upon the lens suddenly flare to life with a pale blue light. The cloudy lens swirls and clarifies to reveal the geometry of that glyph repeated in vibrant color within its glassy dome. This glyph shines with a pale blue light and in the distance you behold the rippling motion of illusion as the distant horizon changes shape and reveals the striking silhouette of a tall tower isolated against the sky.

If the party has not discovered or has access to either of these methods, the tower can be alternatively revealed through use of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSeeInvisib] spell or similar effects other means of magical detection, such as @Spell[illusion.sense]:

In the distance you behold the rippling motion of illusion as the distant horizon changes shape and reveals the striking silhouette of a tall tower isolated against the sky.

Once the party has caused the tower to be revealed, by whatever means, mark the following outcome as complete and award attunement progression depending on the manner by which the challenge was surmounted.

Reducing the Challenge

Revealing the Aedir Signalpost is intended to be a difficult challenge for a low-level party to overcome. They must either thoroughly explore the Forest of Stone to find one of the necessary methods or gain access to higher level magic that allows them to penetrate the invisibility field.

If you wish to offer an easier means of continuing this adventure, you can allow the tower's invisibility field to completely fail, either immediately or after some amount of time passes. This field is already weakened, and allowing it to fail completely will be compatible with the story that follows.

Region Map Change

Marking the below outcome causes the Aedir Signalpost to appear on the Region Map.

[[/outcome revealed]]

Primordis Attunement: Clarion Fork

If a party member was able to dispel the tower's invisibility field using the [[/eventState signalIntentCrystals fork]], they advance their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 windingTrailTowerClarion]] upon the conclusion of this event.

Aura Attunement: Golarne's Glyphsign

If a party member is able to dispel the tower's invisibility field by tracing the sign of [[/eventState signalIntentNeighbors glyph]], they advance their [[/attunement emberAura +1 windingTrailTowerGlyph]] upon the conclusion of this event.

Orbis Attunement: Alternative Solutions

If a party member is able to dispel the tower's invisibility field using some method other than the two above, they advance their [[/attunement emberOrbis +1 windingTrailTowerOther]] upon the conclusion of this event.

Concluding the Event

Having successfully crossed the crevasse and identified the location of the tower, the party may continue on in search of further answers regarding its nature.

Next Steps

If the party was able to successfully traverse the crevasse and was able to cause the Signalpost tower to be revealed, then they can continue south along the ridgeline to reach the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost} and the [[/eventState signalIntentTower]] event.

Conditions of Progression

If either outcome is not completed, the party may need to fall back or repeat the attempt. These outcomes can be retried later if the party is unable to accomplish them now.
The Tower Revealed.soverview: The party climbs the bluffs above the Forest of Stone in search of ancient secrets and reaches a broken crevasse in the earth that halts their progress. In the distance, the party catches sight of a fortified tower that intermittently appears, as if from thin air, and vanishes just as suddenly.
The Tower Revealed.sexposition:
Over the past few miles of arduous hiking you have gained altitude above the Forest of Stone and you sense the air growing slightly thinner and the terrain more rugged with every forward step. Sharp brambles pull at your ankles, slippery rock makes it difficult to walk steadily, and the earth is interlaced with narrow crevices that run through the ground.

Upon cresting a short rise your gait is pulled short as the ground before you falls away into a wide crevasse, perhaps 30 feet across. Pebbles and scree, disturbed by your footfalls, cascade off the ledge and tumble into the gap, creating an echoing clatter that rebounds off and is amplified by the chasm walls. You detect the faint metallic scent of minerals wafting from the depths.

Looking around, you notice, about 100 feet from your current position and on your side of the chasm, a circular structure of columns like a small henge or wayshrine. The structure looks old, and several of its columns have toppled or broken but it is unmistakably a notable landmark in the midst of rugged wilderness otherwise untouched by human influence.
The Tower Revealed.ssummary: While exploring the bluffs high above the Forest of Stone we discovered a strange tower in the distance, magically shrouded in a field of invisibility which caused it to phase in and out of existence. A deep crevasse separates us from our goal, but on this side of the crevasse we discovered an ancient wayshrine of some kind that may offer further clues.

Traversing the Tower.name: Traversing the Tower
Traversing the Tower.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this exploration and combat event, the party enters and investigates the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost} to investigate the rumors shared by Lorettia Ben-Wren in @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.QdZoGPgl1gEGFcQ2]{Helkas}, to find the source of contamination seeping into @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.XytBBChWK9D5ccOD]{Yakoshta Mine}, or to satisfy their own adventurous curiosity.

While exploring the tower the party can:

  • Repair the central elevator that affords access to all four levels of the tower.

  • Learn more about Aedir ambitions of the time and get hints about what they might have been researching.

  • Discover the source of the contamination in the Underforge where Aedir constructs were manufactured and empowered. Decide whether to cleanse the contamination or — if players are underway the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl]{Ooze Control} Quest and have have agreed to work with @UUID[Actor.4FErI4WjKruAtHz7]{Jasper} — collect samples for Jasper in @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.izjepwOp9OMXotTT]{Yakoshta}.

  • Defend themselves against the tower's remaining guardian, a @UUID[Actor.uXUbnrLLJ70leK6v]{Broken Aedir Sentinel}.

  • Choose whether to restore full power to the tower, preserving its Invisibility Field, or allow the tower's power source to fully wane, making the structure permanently visible.

Area Walkthrough

Upon beginning this event, and throughout the party's exploration of the tower, refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn]{Aedir Signalpost} for a complete walkthrough of the area. This includes exploration, combat encounters, investigation and skill checks, and exploration details not contained here.

Exploring the Tower

The Aedir Signalpost is the source of a leak of contaminated fluid that is poisoning the oozes in Yakoshta Mine below. The party has been asked to find and stop the leak. Once they are inside the signalpost, the character's objectives are generally the following:

  1. Repair the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn.JournalEntryPage.lETrNdT8ZjdH8X3f] or locate the hidden @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn.JournalEntryPage.jBd5CnAhQ2Zxf3o7] passage in order to access the lower levels.

  2. Defeat the Broken Aedir Sentinel that guards the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn.JournalEntryPage.ndbokyeEFn2XBDSf] and locate the source of contamination from within the tower. The contaminant is located in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn.JournalEntryPage.ndbokyeEFn2XBDSf].

  3. Cleanse, collect, or ignore the alchemical contamination, affecting downstream repercussions in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl]{Ooze Control} Quest.

Restoring Power

While in the tower, the party must make a decision about what to do with the contaminant found in the Underforge and whether to restore and activate the tower's stealth capabilities — both are tracked via the outcomes in this event.

Power to the Tower

The party may choose to restore power to the tower at by re-powering and reactivating the generator in the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn.JournalEntryPage.L9nUFFrj0MIiBec4]{Secret Basement Room} by recharging its power cells using the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn.JournalEntryPage.ndbokyeEFn2XBDSf#recharge-station]{Recharge Stations} in the Underforge. However, this can only be done if the alchemical fluid has not yet been cleansed!

Luxarum Attunement: Restore Power

If the party manages to restore power to the tower, each character advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 oozeControlTowerPower]] at the conclusion of the event.

Resolving the Contamination

Once the construct in the Underforge of the tower has been defeated, the party must take some actions to determine the final fate of the tower and the alchemical fluid which seeps downwards from it into the rock above Yakoshta Mine.

Cleansing the Contaminant

The party may choose to decontaminate the @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0] in the tower using the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn.JournalEntryPage.ndbokyeEFn2XBDSf#decontamination-station]{Decontamination Station} in the Underforge, which is filled with a mixture of @UUID[Item.QwzYLBnZ1PjLFEuI]{Alchemical Silver} and water. When this mixture is further combined with the@UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0], the fluid loses all of its toxic properties and becomes harmless.

If the party has completed this task, any character that has [[/knowledge alchemy]] or makes a successful [[/skill nature 14]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 14]] check can confirm that the liquid remaining in the vats and on the floor of the Undercroft has been rendered inert and no longer has any meaningful alchemical properties.

Claiming the Contaminant

Alternatively, the party may use sample containers found in the Decontamination Station's supply cabinet to collect @UUID[Item.IrxgsosSg8CNiaS0], either to give to Jasper as part of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOozeControl]{Ooze Control}, or for the party's own use.

Depending on what choice the party makes with regards to the source of contamination, one of their attunements may advance:

Cora Attunement: Contaminant Cleansed

If the party chooses to cleanse or claim the contaminant, each character advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 oozeControlTowerHandled]] at the conclusion of the event.

Luxarum Attunement: Contaminant Sampled

If the party collects samples of the contaminant for the purposes of further experimentation, each member advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 oozeControlTowerSampled]] at the conclusion of the event.

Abyss Attunement: Contaminant Ignored

If the party leaves the contaminant where they found it, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 oozeControlTowerIgnored]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has concluded their exploration of the Signalpost, they may depart for further adventure.

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

This marks the conclusion of "Signal of Intent", but there are some follow-up actions the party can now take:

  • If they were promised a reward for their investigation by either Lorettia or Sadri in Helkas during [[/eventState signalIntentRumor]], they may return to town to collect that reward.

  • If the party has undertaken the events of Ooze Control and completed [[/eventState oozeControlUpdate]], they may now return to Yakoshta and deliver news to Tauric and Jasper in [[/eventState oozeControlJasper1]].
Traversing the Tower.soverview:
As the party approaches the spot where the tower was last seen, it appears before them. It has been damaged by time and the recent earthquake, and is clearly the source of the contaminant in Yakoshta Mine. The party must explore the tower, figuring out how to operate its strange systems, avoiding its traps, and fighting off its natural and mechanical threats.

Eventually, they can discover the source of the contaminant — a leak deep within the basement level of the spypost. It's up to the party whether they want to fix it, and what they they want to do with the remaining contaminant.
Traversing the Tower.sexposition: Twin stone doors are mirrored on either side of the tower's facade. Each has been half-reclaimed by the natural world around them, overgrown by patches of heartmoss and reedy weeds that peek out from beneath the cracks. Otherwise the structure stands silent, permanently visible now that you are within the boundaries of its illusory field.
Traversing the Tower.ssummary: We found a way to enter an ancient tower that was once an Aedir research and signal tower high atop the bluffs to the south of Helkas in the Forest of Stone. The knowledge within could be impactful for those living and working in the region.

A Watchful Spire.name: A Watchful Spire
A Watchful Spire.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event occurs in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt]{Helkas} once at least 2 days (48 hours) have passed since the completion of [[/eventState windingTrailSmoke]]. The party meets Lorettia Ben-Wren, the eccentric proprietor of the occultist shop known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.GL1EYjzoOTsbSV5H]{The Last Satchel}, who has a bold claim about a mysterious landmark in the region. In this event, the characters can:

  • Speak with Lorettia to learn more about her warning and ask questions about what she knows (namely, the general location of the @UUID[JournalEntry.1qs2re1V3s3hDDrn]{Aedir Signalpost} southwest of Helkas).

  • Ask around town to learn if anyone else has additional information to offer.

  • Earn a modest reward from Lorettia for investigating the tower, along with the potential for greater rewards via magistrate @UUID[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]{Sadri Zhalimorne} for putting the matter to rest.

Lorettia's Concern

If the character are willing to listen to her story, Lorettia Ben-Wren (Chaotic Neutral, Waerd Human, she/her) has a potentially troubling tale to tell — one that involves the location of a mysterious tower on the southeastern edge of the Forest of Stone, which Lorettia believes to be the base of operations for the recent attack on Helkas.

A Conversation with Lorettia Ben-Wren

Lorettia is typically a passionate student of Ember's supernatural wonders, and is often eager to trade anecdotal evidence with fellow enthusiasts. Today, however, her enthusiasm is replaced with equal measures of apprehension and concern; and following the apparent rejection from Sadri for aid, Lorettia sees the characters as kindred spirits in her pursuit for answers.

During the course of the conversation, characters can attempt to discern the sincerity of Lorettia's words with a successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck deception 13]] check, which reveals her words and intentions to be true (to her, at least).

If the characters are interested in Lorettia's tale, the beleaguered occultist has the following things to say about the matter at hand:

What are you talking about?

Last night, I went foraging for radiant bog caps — they're a kind of rare mushroom that only grows under the light of the moons — and my excursion took me on a path I hadn't really ever tread before, southwest of town, down near Yakoshta. As I was gathering my things to head back to town, I caught a glimpse of something standing above the southeastern edge of the forest. A tower of some kind, tall enough to see the entire valley. And the strangest part yet: the tower disappeared nearly as soon as I saw it. But it sort of "flickered" there a moment before it was gone again, like a candle flame getting snuffed out.

Lorettia takes a quick look around to see if anyone's listening, raising her voice a bit in the process.

I know it sounds rather silly, but you must believe me when I say: I know I saw something. I'm just not entirely sure what that "something" was. But if I had to guess, I'd wager it has something to do with the recent attack. Those Otherhood raiders must be using the tower as some kind of remote headquarters. It makes perfect sense to me. I can't prove it, but something strange is afoot atop that overlook near Yakoshta.

Where is the tower?

Lorettia levels a finger towards the southern horizon, pointing nearly due south at the edge of the Forest of Stone.

Nearly ten miles south of town, east of Yakoshta. I saw the flickering tower standing high on the butte — almost tall enough to see the entire Forest of Stone at a glance. Given all the brambles and overgrowth, it's a miracle I saw anything at all. Magic is at play here. I'd bet my wand on it.

What makes you believe this?

Call it a gut feeling if you'd like, but something tells me this isn't just another Shent ruin that's yet to be discovered — nor is it a figment of my imagination. I know around Helkas I'm known to be a bit … eccentric. But my occult practices have strengthened my intuitions rather than dulled them.

The attack on Helkas during Dusktide was rather convenient, wasn't it? Don't you think there's some validity to the notion that these rogues were stationed nearby, cloaked by magic and guile?

What should we do?

If I were as formidable as the "Heroes of Helkas," I'd go investigate the situation myself. But alas, I am but a simple apothecary.

She looks over your group with a wry, encouraging grin.

After all, mysteries like these always have some kind of gold-plated reward at the end of their unraveling, don't they? All jokes aside, I'd hate to see our precious little town waylaid yet again as soon as you leave us.

Offering a reward?

I don't have much in the way of monetary reward for an endeavor like this. However, since this is a matter of public concern — whether anyone believes me or not — I'd love to make it worth your while, at least so we can get some answers and sleep well around here.

Lorettia rubs her chin for brief moment, weighing her options.

How does a ten-percent discount at The Last Satchel sound to you? I can also provide you with some consumables to help you on your way: a couple of potions, perhaps? If you wish, I can send you off with a bit of a care package to aid in the effort. What do you say?

Quest Rewards

If the party agrees to take up Lorettia's task and investigate the presence of the mysterious "flickering tower" situated on the southeastern edge of the Forest of Stone, she promptly provides the following items to aid them in their journey:

  • 2 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potions of Healing},

  • 1 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfClimb]{Potion of Climbing}

  • 1 dose of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAntitoxin00]{Antitoxin}

  • 2 @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.healingElixir000]

  • 1 @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.rallyingTonic000]

  • 1 @UUID[Compendium.crucible.equipment.Item.antitoxin0000000]

The 10% discount at @UUID[JournalEntry.emberHelkasWalkt.JournalEntryPage.GL1EYjzoOTsbSV5H]{The Last Satchel} is only available upon successful completion of [[/eventState signalIntentTower]]. Characters who wish to press Lorettia for a larger reward are met with promises of restitution if the investigation leads to any substantial results (that can be appropriately leveraged with Sadri and the other citizens of Helkas).

Aura Attunement: Encouragement

Any character who encourages Lorettia's conspiratorial outlook and agrees with her that the "flickering tower" is worth investigating advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 signalIntentRumorEncourage]] at the conclusion of the event.

Cora Attunement: Rationalism

Any character who overtly expresses skepticism to Lorettia or downplays the likelihood that the "flickering tower" is involved in the attack advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 signalIntentRumorRationalize]] at the conclusion of the event.

Word About Town

After discussing the matter with Lorettia, the party can ask around town to seek further evidence from locals about whether or not there is any truth to the occultist's claims.

Gathering Information

If the party chooses to seek out details that may corroborate or refute Lorettia's claims, the following skill checks can help them gather the appropriate information.

Any character who succeeds on a a [[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 12]] check while asking around town is able to round up a few general details from locals.

Lorettia is well-known for her absentmindedness and perpetually-distracted nature. Most folks are aware of her indulgence in mind-altering substances, and are quick to blame Lorettia's confusion about the so-called "flickering tower" on her lifestyle. Despite her flights of fancy, Lorettia is a skilled apothecary and learned occultist, whose knowledge and acumen have proven to be invaluable to the citizens of Helkas throughout the years.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success : One lone denizen of Helkas supports Lorettia's claims with a half-forgotten anecdote about a traveling merchant that came through town several moons ago, who spoke of a "illusory monument" they spotted while traveling through the Forest of Stone. No one thought much of it at the time, and the traveler's story was never investigated or taken seriously.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] and [[/knowledge trade]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] [[/skillCheck deception 13]] check confirms the relative veracity of the information that's been provided (based on how much truthful information a particular NPC actually knows).

Meanwhile, a successful [[/skill history 18]] [[/skillCheck society 18]] check introduces some skepticism from one or more folks about The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdMk2KY9vGQJUggH]{Otherhood of Fortune }operating out of the Forest of Stone via a permanent garrison, highlighting their primary involvement in the coastal town of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.X1FzWfTYfe7JfD3P]{Seawall}.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] and [[/knowledge intrigue]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Various citizens of Helkas — including the assorted NPCs the party has met throughout their adventures — have their own opinions about Lorettia and her tale. Portions of these individual accounts are detailed below. We encourage you to lean on roleplay throughout the party's information gathering process, but please feel free to combine the skill checks listed above with the dialogue featured below.

@UUID[Actor.SNU9TG0r1Jcpi62U]{Sadri Zhalimorne}

She means well, but Lorettia's attentions tend to drift, often leading her to places that indulge her unfettered curiosities. There is no tower on the hill overlooking Yakoshta. Our friends at Yakoshta would have seen it by now, let alone someone here in Helkas.

Sadri pauses and takes a breath, as if reconsidering.

I'll tell you what: if you have the time, I'm willing to pay your group an ample commission to scout the land east of Yakoshta. It's not a lot, but it's all we have for such a non-issue. And truth be told, it would be nice to soothe Lorettia's worrying. Consider it a favor for the whole town.

A Reward from Sadri

Sadri's offer of [[/award 100gp]] [[/award 10gp]] is available for the characters once they return from a thorough scout of the southeastern perimeter of the Forest of Stone, offered on good faith thanks to the party's heroic involvement in the Dusktide attack.

The first character to succeed on a [[/skill deception 15]] [[/skillCheck deception 15]] or [[/skill persuasion 17]] [[/skillCheck diplomacy 17]] check is able to convince Sadri to sweeten the deal, resulting in an additional reward of 1 unit of @UUID[Item.6f2sudRdy1XTrJqN]{Steelmarrow} for a successful scouting mission to the so-called "flickering tower" (paid upon the party's return, following a full report to Sadri and her allies).

Briannon Frost

There's no denying that Lorettia is good at what she does. And while she's one of the town's more eccentric personalities, her head and heart are full of noble intentions, as far as I can tell. Any threat to Helkas is worth investigating, as far as I'm concerned. You've already been such exemplary allies to us all, so you have my thanks — no matter the road you choose to travel next.

Cordayne Kohle

The last thing this town needs is more trouble. And it's hard to say whether or not Lorettia is the source of the trouble herself in this case. I'm afraid I just don't buy it. Helkas is the only settlement worth mentioning for miles. If there was a landmark out there near Yakoshta, we'd know about it. Somebody would have seen it. Besides, those ruffians came in on the heels of drakes — who knows what beasts of burden they have at their disposal to traverse the plateau?

If you insist on investigating the matter, I recommend you speak with Sadri before setting off. The town has its own interests, after all.

Eveline Doss

If you ask me, this whole area is full of weird shit and even weirder reactions to it. If I had the time, I'd climb up the hillside myself to settle the debate. Sounds like a mystery worth solving to me. But what do I know?

Hode Cinderhaft

I've heard a lot of fish stories while mining these hills, but this one takes the cake. Hell, if you make it out there and actually find an invisible tower standing over Yakoshta that we've somehow missed all this time, I've got a bottle of Arcturian brandy with your name on it.

Concluding the Event

After hearing Lorettia's conspiratorial concerns and asking about town, the party can make ready to depart for whatever next step of their journey awaits.

Next Steps

This event provides an initial breadcrumb leading towards the discovery of the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.Ydvl8O5s1ZRwtOAC]{Aedir Signalpost}. In order to reach the tower, the party will need to:

  • Find a navigable route up to the bluffs, experiencing [[/eventState signalIntentSunwell]]

  • Figure out a mechanism to reveal the shrouded tower in [[/eventState signalIntentRevealed]]

  • Explore the ancient structure in [[/eventState signalIntentTower]]
A Watchful Spire.soverview: Upon returning to Helkas some time after the attack at the Dusktide Festival, the party encounters a local raving about a sentinel tower high above upon the cliffs that they claim is the reason the town was attacked.
A Watchful Spire.sexposition:
A curious scene awaits you upon your return to Helkas, where the pall of the Dusktide attack still hangs in loose reminder of what transpired here. A small commotion disrupts the otherwise tranquil town square when Sadri Zhalimorne bursts forth from front door of The Last Satchel, with the shop's proprietor Lorettia Ben-Wren hot on her heels. The Waerd apothecary waves her hands in protest as she pleads her case.

Please believe me, Sadri! I know what I saw!

The Altyra magistrate turns to confront the exasperated shopkeep with a measured look of frustration in her eyes.

Lorettia, your claim is simply … preposterous. A few hundred people live here in Helkas, not including the visitors who come-and-go, and not a single one of them has ever seen a tower on the southern edge of the forest. Let's face it: this isn't the most reasonable explanation, and — please don't take this the wrong way — but you're wasting your time, and you're scaring the tourists. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a town to help rebuild.

As Sadri shuffles along towards Council Hall, you're left standing in the town square with Lorettia, who turns to regard you with a look of helplessness on her face.

Maybe you have a spare ear for a woman at the edge of her wits? I've witnessed something that requires some expert attention, and we're a bit shy on experts these days.
A Watchful Spire.ssummary: We spoke with a concerned shopkeeper in Helkas named Lorettia Ben-Wren, who made wild claims about the existence of a secret tower on the ridge south of town — which she claims is the origin of the malevolent forces that attacked Helkas during the ill-fated Dusktide Festival.

Well Enough Alone.name: Well Enough Alone
Well Enough Alone.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

South of Helkas, a route ascends between looming spires of the Forest of Stone towards a highland ridge overlooking the rocky landscape. In a large clearing near the beginning of this trail, the party discovers the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.lkzAA0iHIkGJsa5T]{Overgrown Sunwell}. This exploration event can be encountered at any time by traveling to this location for the first time. In this event, the party can:

  • Investigate the overgrown ruin and discern its original purpose.

  • Uncover clues of a terrible battle that happened here long ago when the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} made a stand against abyssal invaders.

  • Undertake a substantial project to restore the Sunwell to a functioning state by clearing the overgrowth and restoring an @UUID[Item.g55R0263jCwRPoxX]{Aedir Wellstone}.

The Ruined Sunwell

The party may be enticed to investigate the ruins of the Sunwell and the gleaming metal that they spotted.

Surveying the Ruin

Characters can attempt to place the historical context for the ruin through a [[/skill history 14]] [[/skillCheck society 14]] check. Upon success, identifying that the buried structure bears hallmark geometry associating it with Aedir design.

  • Result of 19+ Critical Success: You recognize this specific ruin to be an @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCultures000.JournalEntryPage.KwMTJoJblt96WKcI]{Aedir} Sunwell and know the lore presented in the @UUID[JournalEntry.ForestStoneGazet.JournalEntryPage.lkzAA0iHIkGJsa5T]{Overgrown Sunwell} page.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The party may survey the ruin for any clues. A successful [[/skill perception 13]] or [[/skill investigation 13]] [[/skillCheck awareness 13]] check confirms that the central monument is a singular structure with no evident entrances. You spot a section of the stonework that seems to have been violently caved in on the rear side of the structure. Some object was slammed into the stone with extreme force, fracturing it in a radial pattern around the resulting impression. At the base of the ruin near the site of this impact is one of the large flora-covered mounds that sporadically dot the landscape.

Climbing the Ruin

Some characters may wish to climb the ruin to see what can be learned from its summit. No skill check is required as the ruin has adequate handholds, made easier by the heavy vines which cover its facade.

If the party climbs to the top of the Sunwell, read the following aloud:

Atop the structure is a shallow basin, about twenty feet in diameter and nearly three feet deep. The stonework is covered in moss, but the absence of pooled water suggests either damage or an intentional drainage mechanism. In the center of the basin is as small aperture, about three inches across, that appears round but upon closer inspection is shaped from ten straight edges of equal length. Whatever the purpose of this socket, it is empty aside from an accumulation of dirt within.

The party may wish to clear one of the mounds of overgrowth to identify what is buried there.

Clearing the Overgrowth

The work is hard labor as the vines are strong and the underbrush is dense. The party may spend one hour of time to attempt a group challenge to clear the debris, with each party member rolling one of the following checks or performing one of the alternative actions:

  • [[/skill athletics 16]] [[/skillCheck athletics 16]] to clear the debris through brute force

  • [[/skill survival 14]] [[/skillCheck science 14]] to perform a controlled burn or other similar technique

  • [[/skill nature 13]] [[/skillCheck wilderness 13]] to use their knowledge of flora to identify specific vines to cut which weaken the fabric of the verdant covering to be more easily removed

  • Cast a leveled spell which is able to control the growth of plants such as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplEntangle00]{Entangle} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplPlantGrowt]{Plant Growth} Use the Ennervate action from [[/talent Compendium.crucible.talent.Item.runeDeath0000000]] to cause plants to wither and recede

The task is successful if at least half of the group members obtain a successful outcome. Upon a failure, each member of the party gains one rank of &Reference[exhaustion]becomes demoralized from the [[/hazard 4 bludgeoning fortitude morale]]{Unrelenting Vines}.

An Ancient Battleground

If the party clears enough of the overgrowth to identify what is buried underneath, read the following aloud.

You clear the clinging vines, leafy underbrush, and creeping moss away from one of the larger heaps, revealing a mound of dark earth from which protrudes the mangled and broken remnants of strange automatons. You notice heads plated with unsettling masks, powerful metal cores, and twisted limbs with finely articulated parts — all patinaed by oxidation and rust. The remains within these charnel mounds are coated in limestone deposits, grasped by taut vines, and covered in moss; like new muscle, sinew, and skin grown atop ancient metal bones.

This site was a small battleground where the remnant forces of the Aedir made a final stand against the abyssal incursion in the aftermath of The Shattering. The party may wish to inspect the remains closely.

Battlefield Archaeology

Inspecting the construct remains with a successful [[/skill history 16]] [[/skillCheck science 16]] check identifies them as Aedir automatons, constructed by the ingenious artificers of the ancient empire.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 21+ Critical Success: You identify two specific types of constructs present here, models which historians believe were called "Skirmishers" and "Sentinels". Skirmishers were lithe but mostly humanoid in form, capable of extruding deadly blades of energy from their limbs. Sentinels were hulking four-armed bipeds with an array of mechanical weaponry. Both models of construct are undeniably categorized as machines of war.

Searching for clues about what happened requires a successful [[/skill investigation 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check to reveal that the forces assembled here suffered terrible destruction at the hands of some unknown force. There are numerous construct remains, but no mortal remains nor clue about the nature of attackers is to be found.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge warfare]] or [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Result of 17+ Critical Success: You carefully consider the weaponry of these constructs and the damage to their chassis. While there is no direct evidence to support the hypothesis, it seems as if these constructs could possibly have been destroyed by their own armaments, or ones similar to them.

The Researcher's Remains

If the party investigated the construct remains, the party member with the highest [[/skill perception passive]] [[/skillCheck awareness passive]] notices an additional clue.

Behind the hulking form of one of the largest construct and nestled within a gaping cleft in its ravaged chassis you notice the telltale form of humanoid bones. The bones are badly deteriorated, but there is a recognizable shape of a body curled in a fetal position as if taking shelter or overcome with grief. Dangling from the bleached spine of the remains is a delicate chain pendant bearing the broken stump of a carved prismatic crystal. Upon the tightly coiled fingerbone of the body's left hand remains a delicately coiled signet ring.

The body here is that of Golarne, one of the Aedir researchers who was stationed at the Signalpost. It is impossible for the party to identify the remains here, but some clues may be gained enabling the party to infer her identity elsewhere.

Golarne's Fate

The crystal pendant is a broken and unidentified @UUID[Item.cfTTrbcPgR14xc1f]{Shard of Mind Grounding} which cannot be repaired by any known means. Inspection of the crystal pendant reveals no immediate clue as to its origin or purpose, however certain characters may have knowledge allowing it to be identified.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge shent]] who also succeed on a [[/skill history 15]] [[/skillCheck society 15]] check can recognize the pendant as being crafted by Shent carvers.

  • If the party retrieved the @UUID[Item.cfTTrbcPgR14xc1f]{Shard of Mind Grounding} from [[/eventState signalIntentCrystals]] they can immediately recognize this as a broken version of that item.

The signet ring is @UUID[Item.oZTYuDbSnIyy9atT] and is initially unidentified. Inspection of the ring offers only a single clue to its nature. Characters who succeed on a [[/skill perception 12]] [[/skillCheck awareness 12]] check identify an engraved glyph on the flat surface of one side of the ring.

  • Characters who understand [[/language towyr]] or have some other means of translating it can identify the glyph as the analogue of the modern letter "G", written in Towyr.

The corpse is too ancient and disintegrated for any attempts at magical communication with it to succeed.

Restoration of the Sunwell

The party may reason that the Aedir Sunwell could possibly be restored. If attempted, that work requires fully clearing away the overgrowth from the structure and restoring an @UUID[Item.g55R0263jCwRPoxX]{Aedir Wellstone} capable of powering it.

A Restoration Project

A character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 22]] [[/skillCheck arcana 22]] check understands that restoration of the Sunwell would require fully clearing away overgrowth from the structure and restoring an @UUID[Item.g55R0263jCwRPoxX]{Aedir Wellstone} capable of powering the monument.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge aedir]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Clearing the overgrowth from the Sunwell requires expending two days of hard physical labor for a group of four workers.

  • Laborers from Helkas or Yakoshta may be recruited for the project at an expense of [[/award -4gp]] [[/award -4sp]] per day.

There is no immediate clue about where to procure the necessary Wellstone.

If the party does manage to perform the necessary restoration steps now or at any later point during gameplay, revisit this event and mark the following outcome as completed and award attunement progression as appropriate.

Region Map Change

Marking the below outcome changes the appearance of the Overgrown Sunwell on the region map to reflect its now-active state.

[[/outcome restored]]

Luxarum Attunement: Sunwell Restored

Restoring the Sunwell grants [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 signalIntentSunwellRestored]] to the entire party.

Abyss Attunement: Sunwell Defaced

Intentionally destroying or defacing the Sunwell grants any character which does so [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 signalIntentSunwellDefaced]].

Sunwell Usage

If the Sunwell is restored, it will be able to be utilized once per day to direct its solar energy as part of enchantment or spellcraft. The mechanics for this are not yet implemented and will be added as a separate standalone event in a future update.

Next Steps

Having investigated the ruins of the Overgrown Sunwell and discovering any clues that were able to be identified, the party may continue their journey.

Next Steps

If the party intends to investigate the rumors of the hidden tower upon the bluffs, they will proceed south along the highland trail and encounter the [[/eventState signalIntentRevealed]] event.

If the party did not activate the Sunwell during this visit, they may do so at any later point according to the same mechanics described earlier in this event. Whenever the Sunwell is restored, whether now or at a later point, mark the [[/eventState signalIntentSunwell restored]] outcome as complete.
Well Enough Alone.soverview: The party discovers the overgrown ruin of an ancient Aedir Sunwell. Around the base of the Sunwell the party locates clues about a terrible battle that unfolded here long ago between forces of the Aedir and some opposing force which decimated them.
Well Enough Alone.sexposition: The circular structure protrudes above the lush carpet of low-lying shrubs, vines, ferns, and other foliage that blankets the ground. Spaced irregularly around the base of this protrusion are lumpy mounds of overgrowth. As your gaze passes over the environment, a chance glint of metal captures your eye as light from overhead reflects off some object shrouded within the leafy sprawl.
Well Enough Alone.ssummary: We discovered an ancient Aedir ruin in a clearing south of Helkas, a notable landmark along the ascending path towards the mountainous ridge overlooking the region.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

There are no specific requirements to begin this side quest, and it may begin at any time during Chapter 3 after the party reaches @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet]{Ordain}.

Difficulty

"Diplomatic Immunity" is designed for a party of Level 4 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 2 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 each upon completion of the [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityVisit]] and [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityBreakout]] Events.

Witness to a murder, and saddled with the responsibility of delivering a dead courier's final charge, the party finds itself embroiled in a series of increasingly dubious errands to appease the imperious Tayan Ambassador and avoid his ire.

The party will steal from the Cascillian Navy, help forge documents for the Hallows, and enter into fraught negotiation with unpredictable sea raiders. Why? All so they can infiltrate the uppermost levels of the daunting Spellbreaker Tower where a maximum security prison resides.

Once inside the party will have to concoct their escape plan, and convince a captured Tayan operative to escape alongside them. However, nothing in this quest is as it seems, and the party might not even be serving the interests of the Ambassador and the Tayans by the time they are starting their breakout.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND]

  • @UUID[Actor.yztzqRozoEkbiO2K]

  • @UUID[Actor.LxNdaYC9hKg9QSZN]

  • @UUID[Actor.WQzk939folhpYwOH]

  • @UUID[Actor.217UQNTaajO2MIBq]

  • @UUID[Actor.B5TakRnU7gZ4X3pV]

Dangers & Enemies

Cascillian Navy

  • @UUID[Actor.3BhvYUprLcgIiOZ8]

  • @UUID[Actor.TYjkxAwVLHm6dD30]

  • @UUID[Actor.aEg0dqDAyOEXxyTv]

Spellbreaker Security

  • @UUID[Actor.QnYBCVJZr2dnukzz]

  • @UUID[Actor.Qd480eptt72VSjeu]

  • @UUID[Actor.SDSf8Oo4lloU4gVM]

Spellbreaker Inmates

  • @UUID[Actor.9tOfMhRD3CuoKovh]

  • @UUID[Actor.FaPgcwX9XXm4NqIg]

  • @UUID[Actor.CxGN8EVZC3pELQgs]

Wind Raiders

  • @UUID[Actor.217UQNTaajO2MIBq]

  • @UUID[Actor.Ipca55bI0vc7yCLZ]

Local Criminals

  • @UUID[Actor.jZBVgCb2P61F9SrT]
Overview.soverview:
While traveling through Ordain, the party see a brazen assault unfold in the middle of a busy plaza. Before they can even act a stranger is cut down by a group of violent criminals. Now witnesses to murder, and realizing that the victim is a courier of the Tayan Empire, they are stuck with the dead man's last charge: a satchel full of valuable diplomatic missives.

With no one else willing or able to finish the courier's last task, the work falls to the party to deliver the sensitive documents to the Tayan Embassy that rests in the shadow of the Ordinate. However, no good deed goes unpunished, and the party quickly finds itself being strong-armed into helping the Tayan Ambassador with a series of tasks under threat of being charged with murder and espionage against the Tayan Empire!

In "Diplomatic Impunity." the party is drawn into a sprawling plot of dubious legality, forced to carry out errands under threat of punishment at the hands of the imperious Tayan Ambassador, all while working toward some greater end that they might not ever fully understand. As the events unfold, will they follow the orders given, or find ways to turn this plot against their blackmailer?

One Last Thing.name: One Last Thing
One Last Thing.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event sees the party finally getting told what is going on, what all their jobs and actions have been for, and what their final task will be. During this event they'll meet with Ambassador Loris Tezran and Katerin Bastilla and do the following:

  • Learn they'll be infiltrating the Spellbreaker Prison, why, and what that will entail.

  • Have a brief aside with Katerin, who will make them a special offer they can think about.

  • If they have been working with the Veiled Chain, sow discord and distrust between the Ambassador and Bastilla.

Katerin's commentary

If the party didn't complete either the [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityBounty]] or [[/eventState diplomaticImpunitySwordspoint]] events Katerin says:

Before we get started, I'd just like to point out that I don't appreciate being ignored. I didn't give you those assignments for my own amusement, but to make things easier down the line. Since you decided to ignore my tasks, I am looking forward to seeing how you manage what comes next.

Additional Commentary

Rather than providing prewritten responses for all the possible event outcomes from Katerin's events, we encourage you to consider how your party handled her tasks and have her comment accordingly.

She might be impressed if the party [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityBounty fought]] and his Wind Raiders successfully, or if they somehow managed to [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityBounty convinced]] without violence. She might be disappointed or amused if they [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityBounty failed]] of the wingsuits.

She may also comment on if they [[/eventState diplomaticImpunitySwordspoint failed]] of the Cascillian device out of incompetence or disinterest. She might be impressed if they [[/eventState diplomaticImpunitySwordspoint acquired]] the device, doubly so if they did it [[/eventState diplomaticImpunitySwordspoint unnoticed]].

Revealing the Plan

Katerin speaks up:

All right, it's about time Loris let you in on the grand scheme, I think.

Ambassador Tezran’s smile is functional and too polite to be real as he looks up from the documents.

Indeed. It’s time you knew the purpose of the errands you’ve been running.

He gestures to the papers. You recognize sketches from the prison dossiers the guard at Spellbreaker Tower gave you, maps of the floors, notations on the guard rotations, and a circled annotation: Yellow Block, Cell 8.

All of your recent labors, from document forgery, to procurement of specialized equipment, was to supply us for what comes next: The Tower’s prison holds one of my countrymen, a mage by the name of Toron.

He is in custody, and you’re going to correct that.

Katerin lets out an amused snort.

From the inside.

Tezran inclines his head, his annoyance masked expertly, but not completely.

Quite so. We're going to insert you into the Spellbreaker's prison levels as new inmates using the criminal personas you helped create. Once inside you're going to locate Toron, and then escape the prison, and bring him back here.

Given this revelation, the party will almost certainly have questions:

How are we getting in?

Katerin lifts her glass.

I have a secured wagon and guards that will clap you in irons and drop you off at the tower. Combined with the forged criminal records, I've arranged for arrest and court orders for incarceration. We'll hand the whole mess over to the prison and they'll take you up the tower like any other criminal.

How are we going to escape?

Katerin waves her now empty glass toward you.

Those wingsuits you collected from Gastern? Use them from the top level of the tower and you should be able to ride wind currents to anywhere within a mile or two easily. There's a spare one for Toron in the set for a reason.

She refills the glass as she continues:

You can, of course, get creative and find a different route, but that's for you do figure out. We already arranged one solution, so use it or don't.

What if Toron won't cooperate?

The Ambassador's reply is cold:

Convince him. By word or by blade. Either way he is leaving that Tower.

Why us?

Katerin says:

It was going to be Gastern and his crew of maniacs. Luckily for us you turned up with Loris' bag of documents, and immediately became the better option. Which is good because there were concerns about Gastern's reliability… and stability. I'm sure you know what I mean.

Ambassador Tezran adds:

You’re outsiders. Your names aren’t tangled in embassy reports or House ledgers. If this goes wrong, the incident ends with you, not us.

Why Toron?

Toron failed one of his missions and was captured. Were he less important I would let him rot in the prison for his failure, but he knows too much, and his presence there serves as an ongoing security risk for the Empire which I cannot allow that to continue.

What does Toron know?

That is not your concern, his extraction and safe delivery to me, however, is.

Couldn't you get him out legally?

I've tried, but the Ordinate is dragging their feet, and wasting my time with manufactured delays and layers of bureaucracy. They are attempting to hold him for as long as possible, and I'm not interested in playing their game.

What about our criminal records?

Katerin grins at that question, and speaks:

Well, there's a few tricks up my sleeves regarding that, you'll be fine. Short version is that I have enough pull within the Hallows that I can get those documents expunged for being fraudulent. The Hallows or Chain might come looking for you, they won't be able to really prove anything without legit records.

No Backing Out

At this point, if the party becomes apprehensive, Katerin steps in to make sure the party sees "reason" and doesn't back out:

When the conversation turns hesitant, Katerin rises from her seat, not threateningly, but with the ponderous certainty of a ship breaking anchor.

Now, let’s not do anything foolish. You’ve been busy for us, and in the process you’ve committed enough criminal acts to have the Hallows calling for your heads. Stolen Cascillian property, forged official records, stolen items from a foreign courier, attempted to smuggle materials into the Spellbreaker?

That's pretty bad, I'd say.

She gestures to the door.

If you want to walk away, by all means. But when the Hallows find out what you’ve done, and they will, you might not end up in the Spellbreaker, but they will put you in a cell.

Don't you need us?

You’re useful, but not irreplaceable. Besides, you've gotten everything in place already. All we'd have to do is find another team to go in and do the final part.

Aren't you implicated too?

Katerin raises a hand, showing her palm, while offering a meanspirited smile.

Oh no, our hands are clean. Yours? Not so much.

She motions to herself and the Ambassador, then past you toward the city beyond the embassy walls.

Besides, we've got enough clout and money to make whatever wild claims you spew just disappear. Ordain's a mostly upstanding city, sure, but the Ordinate don't seem to mind the dubious things all the Trade Houses get up to because it funds their little utopia.

Katerin's Offer

After the party has spoken with the pair for a bit and has asked any questions they have, there is a moment where the Ambassador is pulled away from the meeting, giving Katerin a chance to make the party a counter-offer on the prison escape.

A soft knock at the garden doors breaks through the conversation. An attendant in Tayan livery steps into view, bowing low before speaking in measured tones.

Ambassador, forgive the intrusion. A representative from the Ordinate has arrived to discuss your most recent request. They are waiting in the parlor.

Tezran’s eyes narrow, irritation barely masked. Rakavi’s tail gives a slow, sweeping flick behind him. After a heartbeat, he exhales and straightens to his full, commanding height.

Of course they are. Typical of the Ordinate to choose the worst possible moment.

He glances toward Katerin, voice turning clipped, businesslike.

Continue the briefing. I’ll be back shortly.

Without waiting for reply, the Tayan ambassador stalks off toward the embassy’s inner halls. Rakavi raises his head, the great predator giving brief consideration to following without being told, but thinks better of it and lays back down.

As the door closes, the garden falls into a hush broken only by the rustle of Katerin's clothing as she leans forward. There's intent behind her eyes suddenly, sharp as a compass point. Her voice is low and conspiratorial, the words coming swiftly:

You’ve gathered by now that he wants Toron back, and ‘back’ doesn’t mean safe. The Redfiend doesn’t forgive failure, and Toron failed him badly enough that Loris wants him retrieved... for judgment. Which, in Tayan fashion, means death.

Her voice softens, but her expression hardens.

That’s none of my business, officially. But unofficially, I don’t like playing errand-girl to executions and certainly hate to see a perfectly good mage go to waste. So here’s my side-proposal: when you escape with Toron, don’t hand him to Loris. Bring him to me instead.

Katerin sits back again, gaze sweeping across you.

You don’t have to answer now. Just remember: when the dust settles, you’ll be the ones standing with Toron. You'll be the ones who get to decide his fate: life or death. Think carefully which will matter more.

She swirls what’s left in her glass for a moment, watching the light catch it like a gold coin tumbling through water, then adds:

I'll also pay you a tidy sum for the trouble, enough to make up for burning your bridge with the Ambassador.

What will you do with him?

Make him disappear, firstly. But you mean after that, I know.

Bastilla always needs more mages. Adding someone of Toron's caliber to my network would let me add Imperial magic tricks to the fleet, and that's more valuable than seeing the man killed and buried under flagstones in Highgate.

Won't that harm your alliance?

Not really, no. The Tayans need Bastilla and its fleet to move their goods and fund their wars. Loris knows that some personal vendetta against a failed spy or whatever Toron is won't register to the Empress. He'll swallow the loss and play nice… probably.

What if we tell him about this?

You could, and I'd deny it, and he'd become paranoid and it would strain the working relationship I have with him. However, he needs me, and my ships, and as long as my crews are reliable, which they are, he will work around not trusting me.

Besides, I don't think that man has trusted many people in his life. I wasn't about to be an exception.

Once the party has finished this exchange and asked any questions they have check the Heard out Katerin outcome. After this point, the Ambassador returns.

The garden doors open once more, causing Rakavi's to head lift immediately and turn toward it. His eyes fix on Ambassador Tezran as he reappears and returns to the meeting.

Did I miss anything of significance?

Katerin shakes her head in response.

Not at all, just fielding questions and making sure the crew is properly informed. I believe they have all they need. I am ready to call my men when they are ready to go.

Loris nods.

Good, excellent. I am eager to get this operation underway.

Katerin reaches into a coat pocket and takes out a golden coin, speaking to it:

Make ready the wagons, mister Forley.

The coin barks back in a stranger's voice:

Aye, aye.

Katerin pockets the coin and looks at you.

Transport will be here shortly, if you're ready to go.

Betraying Katerin

If the party chooses to betray Katerin and tell the Ambassador about her side offer, toggle the Made the ambassador suspicious outcome, and read or paraphrase the following narrative:

The ambassador looks more annoyed than surprised by your revelation.

I shouldn't expect any different from the leader of a band of corsairs masquerading as a proper merchant navy. Let me be clear: Your mission is to bring Toron to me, and nobody else, and I do not suffer failure or betrayal gracefully. I trust you'll bear that in mind, and make the correct decision when the time comes.

Ragen Attunement: Sowing Discord

A party that chooses to reveal Katerin's offer to Loris advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 diplomaticImpunityPlanRevealedKaterin]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Schemes in Schemes

A party that chooses to keep Katerin's offer a secret from Loris advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 diplomaticImpunityPlanKaterinConcealed]] at the conclusion of the event.

Delaying Departure

If the party would like some time to prepare or wrap up other pending tasks, they can do so. This gets the following response:

Katerin sighs and a look of annoyance plays across the Ambassador's face. Katerin speaks:

I had a feeling you might want to delay things once you knew the plan. I'll have my people waiting for you on the approach to the Spellbreaker district. Head that way once you're ready, and they'll intercept you, put you on their wagons, and take you in properly.

Ambassador Tezran breaks in:

And don't tarry any longer than necessary. We have smuggled items and forged documents in play, wasting time risks them being discovered, which in turn risks this operation's chances of success.

From this point forward the party can depart, and undertake any other actions they want first. For example, they could report in with the Veiled Chain at the Hallows as part of @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.5eXgvCwkvIVCP4Xi]{Coming Clean} which would allow them to begin a counter-operation against the Ambassador.

Leaving for Spellbreaker

When the party is ready to leave for the prison, set the Party Ready to Leave outcome, and proceed with the following narrative section:

Collected out front of the Embassy you can hear the distant rattle of chain and hoofbeats growing louder, until two heavy wagons arrive, one bearing a squad of House Bastilla guards, and the other chains and manacles fit for securing prisoners. As the wagon creaks to a halt the armed contingent dismounts and prepares the second wagon to receive you.

At your side, Katerin gestures to the wagon.

On you go, let's not drag this out. If the manacles are tight it's not personal, we need things to look right.

As you board the wagon, the guards secure your ankles and wrists, the chains directly attaching to the wagon so you can't escape its confines.

Once secured, the guards clamber back onto the first wagon, and the pair set off down the street, eventually leaving embassy rise, and angling toward the great tower that looms over the whole city.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

If the party chose to head to prison directly they should be moved directly to the Spellbreaker Tower where the next event, @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.GvEj76wdl5vdKVWj] will begin.

However, if the party chose to delay departure they will need to move to the tower directly on their own when they are ready to carry out the next state of the plan.
One Last Thing.soverview: The party, having gotten everything in place, is finally going to be told what they are preparing for. Called to meet with the Tayan Ambassador Lysael and Bastilla head Katerin, they'll be given their next task: infiltrate the Spellbreaker Tower prison.
One Last Thing.sexposition:
You arrive once more at the Tayan Embassy, and are ushered through to the garden by the same attendant as before.

There, Ambassador Loris Tezran stands near a marble table strewn with papers and delicate glass decanters, his crimson finery sharp against the pale stone. Rakavi rests behind him, sharp eyes watching your every movement.

Opposite him, Katerin reclines in one of the garden’s marble seats, Her immense frame making the chair look almost dainty, a sight only amplified by the small crystal glass of white wine she turns slowly in her hand.

She gives you a small nod of acknowledgement, but the Ambassador ignores you, his attention fixed on the spread of documents before him.
One Last Thing.ssummary: We met with Ambassador Tezran and Katerin Bastilla, finally being given a picture of what the plan is: We're going to be sent into Spellbreaker Tower, the prison specifically, to find a Tayan agent by the name of Toron, whom we're going to break out with. Bastilla guards will take us to the prison when we're ready.

Parcels & Pirates.name: Parcels & Pirates
Parcels & Pirates.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this combat event the party is tasked with collecting items from a pirate captain hired by Katerin Bastilla. However, this captain isn't going to be cooperative, and will require come convincing. This event will see the party:

  • Visit the Ember's Bounty, the massive flagship of House Bastilla, and famed haven for pirates.

  • Meet Gastern Faviyos and his wind raiders, and convince him to give up the items he has.

  • Engage in combat with Gastern, if negotiations fall apart.

Area Walkthrough

This event's gameplay transitions to the "Ember's Bounty" scene where the this event transpires. A complete room-by-room description of its environment occurs there is detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT] area walkthrough. Text related to this event's resolution is retained in this event and should be referenced alongside the walkthrough.

This area has several special rules and gameplay expectations, so it is advisable to review the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB] page either before or during the party's exploration of the location.

Rules and Regs

Just aboard the ship the party is confronted by a burly sailor with a pair of swords slung from her belt. She holds out an arm, halting you briefly. Gruffly she speaks:

Rules aboard the Bounty are simple: No stealing, no killing, no damaging the ship.

Break any of these rules and we throw you overboard and will have to swim for dry land, cause you ain't comin' back aboard after.

Got it?

If the party refuses to agree to follow the rules they are told they can leave and come back once they do. They won't be let on the ship until they do. Otherwise, if the party agrees (or lies about agreeing) they are welcomed through without any further issue, and get the following narrative addition:

Inside, the ship stops feeling like a ship at all, instead you are greeted with a bustling space full of shops, distractions and vices to entice visitors.

Laughter and haggling roll together with the chiming of coin. You hear the muted strains of a band's lively performance, but can't tell from which direction it comes. Somewhere in this vessel, on this deck, is the pirate you need to speak to.

Finding Gastern

Locating Gastern should be fairly straightforward, as most named npcs should have had at least one unpleasant run-in with him or his crew by the time the party arrives. The way they talk about Gastern should leave the aprty the distinct impression that that crew is not fond of him or his Wind Raider cronies.

Asking around should reveal that Gastern can be found in the corner of the @UUID[JournalEntry.3BGopMhQSx1DW6uT.JournalEntryPage.kJBS8IrjMT2yaopq]{The Game Room} next to the stage, with some of his crew.

Speaking to Gastern
