@embed[Actor.217UQNTaajO2MIBq]

Gastern and his crew of brigands are all cocky, mean spirited, and evil in alignment. They are self-serving, and have no regard for the party, or others, and only care about House Bastilla insofar as they can pay them for work. This is why Gastern remains an outsider privateer rather than being officially welcomed into the house.

Are you Gastern?

I am. Who’s asking?

What are the items?

Kessian-designed wingsuits, each one has adjustable harnesses to fit nearly anyone. Expensive, not that we paid much for them...

Though their mask is fixed, you can hear the grin and mean spirited amusement in their words. His cronies chuckle along with him.

Can we have the package?

Sure! Just hand over five hundred gold pieces first.

You were already paid.

I was. In fact, I was paid to get them for Katerin, not you. So if you want them, you’ll pay me too. Just the cost of doing business out on the water.

Do you care that Katerin sent us?

Gastern scoffs.

Not even a little bit. Katerin can come get them herself, or you can pay me to care.

Persuading a Pirate

Gastern can be talked into handing over the crate of wingsuits with a successful [[/skill persuasion 20]] check. Otherwise he'll only hand them over if given 500 gold, intimidated, or defeated.

Negotiating Price

He can be negotiated down to 300gp with an easier, successful [[/skill persuasion 14]] check. Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] have advantage on this roll.

  • Result of 19+ Gastern will agree to drop the price to 150 Gold Pieces.

Talking Tough

The party can attempt to intimidate Gastern and his henchmen, but need to make a successful [[/skill intimidation 18]] check. Failing this check by 5 or more results in Gastern becoming hostile.

Primordis Attunement: Convincing the Corsairs

Each character who uses their social skills to persuade, intimidate, or negotiate with Gastern Faviyos to acquire the wingsuits advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 diplomaticImpunityBountyConvincedCorsairs]] at the conclusion of the event.

Fighting Gastern

The Hard Way

Gastern is backed up by a group of Windraider Pirates. Should a fight break out, they fight with their bare hands unless the party draws their weapons first. Gastern will back down if his health is reduced to half its maximum, and his pirates will stop fighting if he does.

Adhering to the laws of the Ember's Bounty, they won't kill the party if they win the fight, but will take some of their money or valuables while knocked out.

Upon defeating Gastern in combat, he yields.

Gastern throws up their hands, attempting to ward you off.

Katu's balls, all right, all right, enough! Back off. You can have the damned package, it's not worth this much trouble, and I'm certainly not dying for the old sea hag's ambitions.

We stashed them inside a dark chest with brass fittings outside, across from the smoke hut. Go get them and get lost!

Ragen Attunement: Clobbering the Corsairs

Any character who engaged in combat with Gastern Faviyos advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 diplomaticImpunityBountyClobberedCorsairs]] at the conclusion of the event.

Finding the Stash

The party may suspect that the items they are meant to pick up are somewhere on the ship, and they would be correct. The party can attempt to locate the items without needing to deal with Gastern, but they will need a little information to work with first.

Eavesdropping

A successful [[/skill stealth 16]] check nearby but out of sight of Gastern and his pirates allows a party member to listen in on Gastern's conversation with his pirates. Alternatively, a character may blend in with nearby patrons with a successful [[/skill deception 16]] check. They have disadvantage on this check if Gastern and his pirates have already interacted with the party and has seen them before.

In either case, successfully listening in reveals that Gastern has stashed the items on the ship in a nearby room. With this information in-hand, the party can search the surrounding spaces and find the stash of items, collecting them without having to persuade, pay, or fight Gastern.

Mayis Attunement: Patient Observation

Any character who successfully eavesdropped on Gastern and his band to learn the location of the stash advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 diplomaticImpunityBountyObservedCorsairs]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished with Gastern and the Ember's Bounty, they can move on to Katerin's other job if they haven't completed it yet, or move on to depositing the items at the Spellbreaker Tower if they've completed all the jobs given to them.
Parcels & Pirates.soverview: Now vetted by Katerin, the party is sent to the Ember's Bounty to acquire equipment from one Gastern Faviyos, a pirate captain hired to acquire items for House Bastilla. The items have been paid for, but Gastern is a notorious wildcard.
Parcels & Pirates.sexposition:
Your skiff rides the chop toward a colossus of a ship, a behemoth riding low under the weight of a trove you can only guess at. Narrow gangways along sides side bristle with traffic, and a small flotilla of smaller vessels bob alongside it as cargo and people move in and out.

Once your craft is tied off, a gangway is tossed over the gap between deck and dock, and you are waved aboard. Ahead, a broad hatch yawns open, offering access to the inner decks of the great vessel.
Parcels & Pirates.ssummary: We visited the Ember's Bounty, the Bastilla flagship and raucous haven for pirates and brigands in Ordain. There we met a pirate boss by the name of Gastern whom we were sent to retrieve items from. He didn't make it easy, demanding extra payment, despite having already been paid by Katerin.

Criminal Records.name: Criminal Records
Criminal Records.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this social event the party meets with Katerin Bastilla, head of the Trading House, and has a chance to get to know her before being asked to handle a handful of tasks. In this event the party will:

  • Get to know Katerin Bastilla a bit, and how she's connected to Ambassador Tezran.

  • Learn about the jobs she wants them to do.

  • Work with a clerk she employs to create some documents of a dubious nature.

Ringing the Bell

When you ring the bell, the sound rolls deep and clear, like a call across harbor water. An attendant arrives almost at once, orange and teal livery neat in the lamplight, and with a courteous incline of the head they unbar the gate.

You are expected, please follow me.

They usher you inside, and you are guided to a cool foyer that smells faintly of lemon oil and sea salt. The parlor is all dark wood and high ceilings, with heavy beams of wood stretching overhead.

The furniture is worn from use and age, but impeccably maintained. Along the walls, model ships sit on shelves, with navigational charts are on display above them.

A brass chronometer ticks with patient precision as you wait, until a moment later nearby double doors burst open and a mountain of a being strides in, their heavy footfalls shattering the quiet.

Aha, you're the band that Loris pressed into helping me with my tasks, eh? I’m Katerin Bastilla head of house Bastilla. Who all are you lot? Speak up now!

@embed[Actor.yztzqRozoEkbiO2K]{Katerin Bastilla}

Katerin's Tasks

Katerin takes a seat. A moment later the doors open and a clerk walks in, carrying a leather folder, and a scribe's case. They give you a silent nod and offer a polite greeting to Katerin, who waves them toward a table where they carefully unpack their pens, pencils, papers, and inks.

Katerin speaks while they do:

I've got some work for you. One's simple, the other two less so. The first job is helping my clerk here with some paperwork. The second and third jobs are just picking up items.

Of course, the people holding those items might not be cooperative. You'll need to get some equipment from the Ember's Bounty, and steal an item from a Cascillian warehouse in Tridents Point.

What paperwork are we doing?

Katerin waves a hand in dismissal.

Some records we'll need in the future need finalizing and you're going to furnish some details for them. It'll be the easiest of the tasks you're assigned.

What are we getting on the Ember's Bounty?

There's a privateer that I hired, Gastern Favyos, he's a bit of a wildcard, and little too much of a rogue element for Bastilla membership, but he has his uses. He was paid to acquire some equipment for me, and they are being held on the bounty, awaiting pickup.

Just make sure you follow the rules you're given, or else you'll be tossed overboard. If you are going to break the rules, at least break them after you get the wingsuits from Gastern!

What are the items?

I had him acquire some wingsuits, ingenious creations that let the wearer glide through the air rather than plummeting like a stone.

Where is the Ember's Bounty?

It's the massive ship docked off the coast of the Coinwealth harbor. You have probably seen it already. You'll need to take a boat from the waterfront out to the ship, but it has its own dock, so getting aboard is simple, and I'll make sure the crew lets you on.

What is the Ember's Bounty?

Only the largest ship that's ever sailed. It's the crown jewel and flagship of House Bastilla, and roams the seas, traveling from port to port doing business and making our presence known. It's effectively a floating town with its own market, casino, and more.

There's a lot of rare and unusual things that end up aboard the bounty that people might have trouble getting their hands on otherwise. You ought to poke around and see what's being offered when you're there.

Piratical Supership

Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] know that the Ember's Bounty is a hotbed of smuggling, and is effectively a floating black market. Rare, banned, and regulated items can be found here, though the price is often exceptionally high. It also a good place to sell items of dubious provenance.

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge politics]] know that the Embers Bounty skirts legality, operating as a trade and social hub inside Ordain's area without ever submitting itself to the laws of the city. Since the ship never officially docks in Ordain, it has never been officially searched and its cargo manifests never scrutinized. This allows it to operate with impunity, and serve as a safe haven for people looking to avoid the prying eyes of the Hallows and Veiled chain.

On a successful [[/skill history 16]] check a character knows that the Embers Bounty has been a controversial vessel for it's long and storied lifespan. It has been under the command of House Bastilla for almost as long as there have been records of the ship, and the actual origin of the ship remains an open question. It is unclear if the ship was a gift or was seized from another navy or if it was custom built for House Bastilla. Unfortunately, the story changes with the captains, and none have bee considered reliable narrators.

How do you know the Ambassador?

House Bastilla and the Tayan Empire have a shared interest: trade. They need their exports moved around the world, and their fleets are all tied up in whatever war they are fighting currently. So, House Bastilla graciously stepped up to lend a hand and a small fleet of merchant vessels, for a cut of the trade profits, of course.

Because I'm based in Ordain, Loris is my main point of contact.

Do you trust the Ambassador?

Katerin laughs!

Gods no! I wouldn't trust him as far as I could throw him. He's Tayan, and they want nothing more than conquest and supremacy over all others. Right now he and his superiors know that House Bastilla is their current best choice for trade needed to fill their war chests.

That doesn't mean we're friends, or even allies.

But I have some tasks I need done, he has some goals he wants to achieve, and working with him benefits my house.

Do you care that you're funding their wars?

So long as the Tayans play nice and pay their contracts on time the wars of the Empire don't concern me or my house. The money and trade interests of the Empires is what I care about, and right now both are very positive.

The Second Task

The second task for you is a bit more complex: You're going to head to a warehouse in the Tridents Point District on the other side of the waterfront, and pick up a Cascillian autotool device. Ideally without being seen.

Government Property

Characters with [[/knowledge politics]], [[/culture emberCascilian]], [[/path emberAnchoriteMarine]] or making a successful [[/skill history 16]] know that Tridents Point is largely occupied and patrolled by members of the Cascilian Republic, and they employ highly trained marines, combat animals and war machines. In addition to that, the Cascilians and House Bastilla are not on good terms due to clashing ideologies about magic use.

Are we stealing the tool?

Sure are! I'd recommend not being seen by the Cascilians that run the place, but if you want to break in and fight your way through, feel free. It's your ass to risk. Cascilian Marines are no joke.

What does the tool do?

Cascilians love their machines. The autotool, from what I understand, is a handheld toolbox that can do its work automatically. It's going to be very useful in the future.

Cascilian Innovations

Characters with [[/knowledge machines]], [[/culture emberCascilian]], [[/path emberAnchoriteMarine]] or making a successful [[/skill nature 16]] check know that Cascilians eschew magic for their constructs and devices, relying on a pairing of biological creatures grown around machinery, creating new biotechnology, sometimes with the capacity to carry out tasks autonomously.

What will it be helpful for exactly?

Katerin smirks.

I'm not surprised that Loris hasn't told you what you're doing yet. Unfortunately for you, I'm not going to spoil the reveal. Just know that you'll want to have it around when the time comes.

Won't this provoke the Cascilians?

If it were House Bastilla doing the robbing, sure, but it's not. You don't work for me, not officially in any way they can prove, at least.

Why are House Bastilla and the Cascilians at odds?

We didn't always used to be. The Cascilians and Bastilla were allied once upon a time, but it didn't last. Nowadays their hatred and mistrust of magic, and our willingness to utilize any magical trick or enchantment to give our ships an edge puts us on their short list of people to watch.

I think our shared history and the fact we're not pushovers keeps things from becoming an all-out war, but that doesn't mean we don't trade blows now and then.

Cascilians & House Bastilla

Characters that succeed on a [[/skill history 16]] check know that the Cascilian Republic and House Bastilla have a long and complex history dating back centuries when their fleets were allied against common enemies. However, the march of time and development of differing ideologies has driven a wedge between them.

While neither side is fully willing to commit to war with each other, creating an ongoing cold war scenario where both sides interfere with each other's operations in obfuscated and deniable ways. Unfortunately, this means that the tensions are raising, and goodwill is stretching thin. Conflict may be unavoidable in the future.

Characters with [[/culture emberCascilian]] or [[/path emberAnchoriteMarine]] know that the warehouse and most of trident point for that matter our controlled by the Republic, which means they will have Marines protecting most of the structures, and may even have warbots which are these powerful automatons loaded with weaponry and covered in armor that's all but immune to Magic.

Wrapping Up With Katerin

Once the party has finished speaking with Katerin, she takes her leave.

Katerin claps her hands loudly.

All right. Excellent, sounds like I can leave this with you. I'll leave you to sort out the document details. Once you've done the other two jobs, drop the items off with lobby guard at the Spellbreaker Tower. They'll know what to do.

Pleasure meeting you, keep the wind at your backs.

With that, Katerin strides out of the parlor. The clerk looks at you expectantly.

Ready to get started, then?

Helping the Clerk

Madame Bastilla wants me to forge some criminal records, but didn't give me any guidance on what those records should hold, and, frankly, don't have a head for these sorts of things. So if you could help me finesse the details, that would be incredibly helpful.

What I'll do is give you some questions, and you can furnish the answers.

Build-a-Brigand

For each person the clerk poses the following prompts:

  • This criminal, what name do they go by? What is their most famed alias?

  • List this person's known and suspected crimes.

  • Declare this person's level of magical ability: minor, major, or master. In addition, are they member to any guild, religion, cult, or are they a know servant to any god?

  • Does this persona belong to any gangs, outlaw forces, and if so, what position do they hold within?

The clerk takes note furiously, casting aside pages of parchment to make room for thoughts that spill from one to the next. After a moment he looks up at you and says:

This is all fantastically helpful! With these suggestions I can finish the work madame Bastilla's given me. Thank you for your help.

What are the files for?

I honestly don't know. They are forged warrants for arrest and criminal records for people that don't exist. I'm not sure what she wants these for, or why she wants them filed with the Hallows, but she doesn't pay me to ask those sorts of questions.

Why do you work for Katerine?

Because I need money to survive, and the Hallows doesn't pay as well as one would like. At least not well enough if you intend to live comfortably, and I do.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished speaking with Katerin and helped the clerk develop their forged criminal records they can go tackle one of the other jobs given to them. Optionally, they can report to the Veiled Chain first.
Criminal Records.soverview: The party is sent to meet with one of Redfiend's allies, Katerin, who intends to interview the party and take measure of their character. If satisfied, she'll give them further tasks to take care of. The party will be prompted to craft personas and criminal records suitable for entry into the Spellbreaker Tower.
Criminal Records.sexposition: The walled estate sprawls, enclosed by a high stone perimeter softened by manicured hedges and climbing jasmine. Drawing near, you see the great iron gates bear the sigil of House Bastilla: a ship’s wheel wrought in dark metal. A burnished bell hangs beside the post, the shape unmistakably nautical.
Criminal Records.ssummary: We met with Katerin Bastilla, head of the trading house bearing the same name. She is an ally of Ambassador Tezran, and gave us several tasks to pursue around the city. She also had us speak with a clerk under her employ who wanted our help crafting criminal personas for some unspecified use later.

Visiting Hours.name: Visiting Hours
Visiting Hours.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event sees the party visiting the Spellbreaker Tower to drop off the items they acquired while working for Katerin Bastilla. The contact they are speaking to is a guard in the tower, and in return they'll get a packet of info in return. This event entails:

  • Exploring the lower level of the Spellbreaker Tower and the healing house.

  • Interact with the Cindaric Sage in charge the healing house, learning about them and their position.

  • Learn about the Spellbreaker Tower and gain insight into what they are working toward in this quest.

Delivering the Items

The party can tell the guard they are making a delivery, and they will understand. The party doesn't have to namedrop Katerin Bastilla, or House Bastilla, but can if they want.

  • To deliver the wingsuits the party needs to have acquired to get the wingsuits from the Ember's Bounty. How they did this doesn't matter as long as they didn't mark the [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityBounty failed]] outcome.

  • To deliver the autotool, the party needs to have [[/eventState diplomaticImpunitySwordspoint acquired]] from the Cascillian warehouse on the docks.

If the party has no items to deliver read or paraphrase:

The guard looks at you like you've grown a few extra heads:

I was told you'd be delivering some items. If you don't have them, I can't help you. So… is there anything you want me to take?

The party can still give the guard items they want smuggled into the tower if they choose.

Otherwise they read or paraphrase this passage:

The guard takes the items off of you, and takes a few minutes relocating them into a large rucksack. They pause a moment and ask:

Anything else you want me to take?

The party can give the guard additional items to smuggle into the prison levels if they want.

What will you do with them?

Take them into the tower and stash them. Were you not informed — you know what, not my problem. If you want me to take anything, hand it over. Just understand anything magical you give me will be worthless in the tower.

Once they have handed over any items they want stashed, the guard will cinch up the rucksack and leave.

Meeting Jonico

Manning a reception desk is an older fellow with silver-streaked hair and wire-rimmed spectacles. Seeing you standing about, waiting for the guard to return he whistles at you, and gestures for you to come his way.

C'mere! Why're you just standing around in my lobby?

Your lobby?

I'm the head of the ground level, the Foundation we call it, so yes, my lobby.

Who are you?

Chief Healer Jonico Daridane, head of the Foundation, and elder sage of the Cindarics.

A Familiar Name

Charactgers with [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/path emberCindaricInitiate]] or making a successful [[/skill history 14]] check recognizes the name, and that he was once also a member of the Ordinate council but was recently replaced.

Weren't you on the Ordinate council?

Yep, sure was! Not anymore though, and I certainly don't care. It's a big popularity game these days, and I'm not the game-playing sort. I'd rather show up, do the work, and get things done.

Vinarith likes his little cult of personality and weeding out anybody who doesn't immediately agree with whatever bout of self-serving, ego-stroking soapbox he's decided to stand on that day.

Well, I was one of those weeds.

Why are you manning the lobby?

I'm giving the woman who works here a break. Besides, I'm not to good to do the low-level stuff now and again.

Don't you have other people for that?

Hey, hey, hey, I don't show up randomly in ancient ruins or whatever telling you how to do your job. So don't come into my lobby and tell me how to do mine. Also no, I don't, there was a scheduling issue.

What is the Foundation?

It's the largest Cindaric healing house in the city, and the only one where no magic is used. We specialize in healing techniques that utilize existing traditional knowledge, and newly pioneered methods to mend bodies. We also work on studying and breaking magical maladies, curses, illnesses, and the like.

Who built the tower?

Well now that's an interesting story!

The tower is some six centuries old, built by one person: Avilla. Now, it's worth noting that she was special, being as she was the first Shard God of Ordain. She shaped the tower from the very spire of ancient basalt the whole district is built on, and imbued the tower with its anti-magic properties.

As for the Foundation and apartments built into the other levels of the tower, those were established many years later. The newest addition was the prison on the upper levels, having been built a few decades ago.

For more the on history of the tower see @UUID[JournalEntry.SXu41X2NifZaSVqh.JournalEntryPage.wBfEdFXGf2pE20MF]{The Spellbreaker}. Jonico is well versed on the topic, and can speak at length about the history of the tower if asked.

What is the tower used for?

Tower's used for quite a lot, actually!

Beyond the Foundation levels you have a collection of dormitories, apartments, and communal spaces set aside for people that are suffering from magical maladies, curses, afflictions, and the like. Since the tower suppresses all magic inside itself and the district, this is a haven for people who couldn't live normal lives elsewhere.

Past that, the top levels are a prison, but that's not my domain.

Do you also oversee the rest of the tower?

Yep, that falls under purview of the Foundation healing house. We even provide healing service to the prison levels, making sure the people there are kept healthy.

Who is in charge of the prison?

Warden Cyran Holst, my counterpart here, sort of.

Who is kept in the prison?

It's a prison, so it mostly has criminals in it. But I also send people to be held temporarily if they have intermittent curses that make them a danger to other people. Prison's not my responsibility, as a note, you'd want to talk to Warden REFERENCE about how they run things.

Delivery Confirmation

If the party is still talking to Jonico:

While speaking to Jonico you noticed the guard return, carrying a thin leather satchel in his offhand. As he draws near he nods at you but turns to address the healer, saying:

Healer Daridane, if you don't mind, I need to have a word, and hand off a delivery.

He holds up the satchel, giving it a shake.

In response Jonico throws up his hands defensively.

All right then, don't mind me. I'll just leave you to your prison business, and go back to what I was doing.

At that, he turns and walks off without so much as a goodbye. The guard then looks back to you, and offers the satchel, saying:

Your shipment was received, here are the documents you're expected to deliver. Come this way, I'll show you out.

The guard gestures toward the doors, intending to escort you out.

Otherwise, if the party is done speaking with Jonico:

The guard returns, carrying a thin leather satchel in his offhand. As he draws near he nods at you and offers the satchel, saying:

Your shipment was received, here are the documents you're expected to deliver. Come this way, I'll show you out.

The guard gestures toward the doors, intending to escort you out.

The party is given both a @UUID[Item.CWa9TuNjTm4mcKLn] and @UUID[Item.DrGGBJmRls0BogyU]

Clandestine Documents

If the party chooses to look at the documents they are handed, it includes several diagrams and writeups on the prison levels of the Spellbreaker tower, as well as a report on one of the prisoners there, a Tayan spy named Toron.

Information on Prison

Like the rest of the tower and district, the prison area is devoid of magic. Spells, magic items, and some magical abilities possessed by beings cease functioning entirely. This means everything in the prison levels is mundane in nature, with the exception of some Cascillian technology.

The prison is patrolled mostly by prison guards who are lightly armed at all times. In times of riot or crisis the guards can gear up with heavier equipment from the armory. There is also a Cascilian Surge Walker machine available if things get out of hand.

Prison Levels

The prison is contained in the topmost six levels. Internally, the prison levels are broken up across multiple floors and movement between levels is highly restricted and managed through secured gates. The distinct floors are as follows:

Guard Barracks

Temporary housing for on-duty guards. Usually contains at least 8 guards at all times, up to 16 during the day. These guards are on-call to respond to issues, and rotate watch with other guards on higher levels. Guard armory is here.

Visitation/Medical

A medical ward, waiting area, visiting area, and temporary holding space is here. Newly arrived inmates may be held here, but inmates seeing visitors are also brought down here.

Blue Block

Dedicated to lower threat individuals, this is the minimum security area that allows prisoners the most freedom. Physical security is somewhat relaxed here.

Yellow Block

Yellow Block holds individuals considered highly dangerous and employs heavier security, frequent searches, and has more restricted movement.

Red Block

The uppermost and most secure level. Here, prisoners are isolated in reinforced cells under constant monitoring, and the most restrictive routines. Entry is limited to senior staff and only under the strictest protocols.

Warden's Office

The penultimate level of the tower holds the warden's office, and their personal gallery and meeting spaces. The prison levels are administered from this location.

Tower Roof

The top level of the tower is a natural garden/terrace accessible only by prison staff.

The report on Toron is far less extensive, but does specify where they are being kept and how they ended up in prison. At this point the party won't know why Toron matters, but they should be beginning to get an idea of what the mission is if they haven't already figured it out.

Report on Toron

Toron, Prisoner number 15874, is a Tayan national, human male. Their record states they are trained in martial and magical combat, intrusion, and general skullduggery. Their magical capacity is noted as being significant, and combined with their reported skillset they have been assigned to a cell in Yellow Block.

They were arrested in the Ordinate when security wards went off, alerting the evening watch to their presence. The ensuing pursuit resulted in several minor injuries and one life threatening but nonfatal injury before they were cornered and captured. They were charged and convicted of assault with a weapon, assault with intent to maim, in addition to multiple counts of espionage and theft against the Ordinate and its member entities.

They are presently being held until the Ordinate determines a proper diplomatic response to the presence of a Tayan spy in the city. The Tayan Embassy has not yet been informed of this arrest, but will be once diplomatic channels are opened.

The Waiting Courier

As you leave the Spellbreaker Tower a figure wearing a bright orange sash around their waist and a crisp double breasted coat approaches you. You quickly spot the gold ship's wheel pinned to their chest — a House Bastilla agent.

They move with you, speaking casually:

Lady Bastilla sent me to give you some further instructions, and take something off your hands.

What's the message?

She wanted me to inform you that now , since all your tasks are done, you're meant to report to the Tayan Embassy for a meeting. I'd recommend you not waste their time, and go soon as you're able.

He pauses then adds:

Before you ask, no, I don't know any details about the meeting. But I do know you're reporting to the boss directly, and not many people do that in Bastilla, let alone outside it. Don't waste an opportunity other people would kill for...

What are you taking?

She said you were overseeing delivery of sensitive documents from the tower. I was sent to get them from you, and see them on their way back to her for study. I was also told not to leave until I got them from you.

Once the party hands over the documents, the courier takes their leave, and moves with purpose. If the party chooses to follow them, their trail ends at Katerin's private estate in Coinwealth Heights, a location they won't be let back into.

Concluding the Event

Milestone Progression

Completing this event awards a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone} point, potentially enabling the party to advance in level.

Next Steps

Once the party has finished at the tower they can move on with the next steps in the quest. From this point they'll need to report back to the Embassy and Ambassador Tezran as part of @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.Ud8jlpeQoEg4MlYx], but they could also report their recent actions to the Veiled Chain via the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.5eXgvCwkvIVCP4Xi] event.
Visiting Hours.soverview: The Party is sent to deliver the wingsuits, Cascillian devices and a letter to a guard on the ground floor of the the tower. While there, they meet the Cindaric that runs the place and have a chance to learn about them, the tower, and recent events.
Visiting Hours.sexposition:
The tower rises like a judgment over the street, a monolith of stone carved with the immense cloaked visage of the Spellbreaker. The goddesses hooded gaze is cast across the city, her eyes ever watchful, as her mantle down the tower in great ripples of stone.

The air around the base feels cool and still, and the sound of the city seems to grow quieter the closer you get to the tower itself. The hush reaches its peak as you move through the doors to the base of the tower and enter the lobby of dark, polished stone. Here, banners of crimson and gold hang from the walls, their designs unmistakably Cindaric, and the air has the scent of medicinal tinctures and fresh linen.

As take in the surroundings a nearby armed guard straightens, and begins to crosses the floor with measured steps toward you. He stops at a respectful distance, posture crisp.

Sorry, can't let you go any further as the tower isn’t typically open to the public. What’s the nature of your visit?
Visiting Hours.ssummary: We visited the lowest level of the Spellbreaker Tower to drop off the various items acquired while doing tasks for Katerin. The items were given to a guard that seemed to be on her payroll. In return we were given a packet of information. While there we met the Cindaric Sage in charge of the healing house, and spoke to them about their role in the city and tower.

Breaking the Tower.name: Breaking the Tower
Breaking the Tower.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event involves the party breaking out of the Spellbreaker Tower prison. How they choose to do this is up to them, and can be as stealthy or chaotic as they choose. Regardless of the methods they use, the party will:

  • Bypass the security that locks down the prison.

  • Defeat or evade the guards patrolling the various levels.

  • Escape the tower, and take Toron toward a chosen rendezvous.

Manual Trigger

This event needs to be manually triggered via the "Initiate Event" button found at the top and bottom of this page. Once the party has had sufficient time to plan, observe, and prepare their escape you want to begin the jailbreak events detailed below.

The Veiled Chain Trap

For the Veiled Chain trap to be possible the following things need to be true as this event begins:

  • The Outcome: [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityPlan suspicious]] needs to be completed, which was done by revealing that Katerin had made the party an offer to take Toron into custody, or by some other form of manipulation carried out by the party.

  • The Outcome: [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityChain counter]] needs to be complete, which indicates that the Veiled Chain have offered a counter-plan for the party to undertake.

If both states are completed, the party then has a more difficult task ahead of them: The need to escape to the roof of the tower with Toron without raising any alarms, or causing the tower to go on alert. If they can do this, then the Ambassador will be waiting and can be captured.

Starting the Escape

The players may begin their jailbreak whenever they are ready. This can be at any time of day, wherever they are located in the prison, whether they are eating a meal, working out, or locked up in their cell. It's up to them to improvise their escape based on the resources and knowledge they've gathered.

We encourage you as the Gamemaster to simply have the guards follow their routine as normal and react to any oddities or disturbances they encounter while going about their patrols.

Since it is possible to fail an escape attempt, this event can be retried as many times as needed. See @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.TGOj5GcJdo3tsp85#failing-to-escape]{Failing to Escape} below.

Recovering the Items

It should be assumed that the party knows where to find the items they delivered to the Spellbreaker Tower, and have been able to acquire those items before the jailbreak begins, as the escape itself is intended to be the main challenge.

However, if you want to make retrieving the items part of the gameplay, you can have the guard from @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.1lXTVRoSZAapaYZW] quietly inform them where their items are stashed, and leave retrieval up to them. If you go this route, place the items in an empty cell nearby. To make retrieval harder, place the items in room they don't normally have access to, like a storage room, or a locked cell.

Resolving the Escape

There are several ways the party can escape, but the intended method is to reach the top of the tower and then leap off with the wingsuits, gliding to safety. However, a party might find another place they can leap from the tower (Red Block and the Warden's Offices are potential alternatives) but they might also choose to exit the tower by heading down the stairwell.

While we don't have prepared gameplay for escaping down the tower stairs, since most of the guard forces are concentrated on the upper levels, a party that gets past the lowest security gates could escape fairly easily. Though, reaching the point is far easier said than done.

Failing to Escape

It is possible that the party could fail to escape the tower. This results in them resetting their positions in the prison after being relieved of any items they have, including the wingsuits (if they had them on their person). These items can be found in a secured storeroom somewhere on the prison levels, allowing them a chance to reclaim them later.

Being captured and failing to escape doesn't prevent them from attempting another escape later, and is even expected. A party that fails to escape should have an easier time on future attempts because they'll know how fast guards can react, what doors they can bypass, and may even find new passages to improve their route.

Danger of Escalation

We recommend cautioning your party against using lethal force unless absolutely necessary. The prison guards default to non-lethal attacks and don't kill prisoners if fights break out, but extreme force will prompt the guards to use more force in response.

A party that kills may find themselves facing harsher treatment from guards if they fail to escape, or be locked down in a higher security (yellow block) or maximum security (red block) cell in response to their actions. Such an outcome could make future escape attempts harder.

Springing the Trap

If the party has managed to meet the criteria to spring the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.TGOj5GcJdo3tsp85#the-veiled-chain-trap]{The Veiled Chain Trap}, and arrived at @UUID[Scene.emberSpellbreak7]{Spellbreaker Tower (Level 7)}, the top of the tower, Loris Tezran will arrive moments later.

Swooping in from on high, a great crimson Ancara lands on the roof of the tower, ridden by Ambassador Tezran. The pair strike the stone with a heavy thud, the great predator absorbing most of the impact with his powerful limbs.

Loris dismounts even before Rakavi fully settles, and calls out to you:

I've decided to collect Toron myself. You've done well getting this far, but I don't think I can rely on you any further. I hope you don't hold it against me!

Now. Hand over Torn, and we'll be going.

What about us?

You have the wingsuits don't you? Jump, as your planned! If you don't, well… you're on your own, I'm afraid.

If Toron is conscious, he is resistant:

Toron shakes his head.

I think I'll take my chances in the prison, given my options.

Loris sneers.

I'm giving you an order!

Toron barks out a bitter laugh.

Then you can add insubordination to my service log. I know what failure earns me under your leadership. I'd just as soon make my way back to the Empire on my own, Commander.

Loris draws his sword.

Very well, we'll do this the hard way.

From this point forward, Toron and Loris become hostile to each other. The party may intervene, helping either side, or choose to stay out of it. However, the Veiled Chain quickly arrive:

Nearby cages pop open, a team of Veiled Chain agents posing as inmates coming view. They draw their weapons and call out:

Ambassador Tezran, Inmates of Spellbreaker Prison, stand down! You're all under arrest!

Loris looks from the agents to you, and back, processing the betrayal.

Very cunning. I didn't think a double-cross was something you could manage.

He points his blade at you.

I will show you what becomes of those that cross the Redfiend.

From this point Loris becomes fully hostile to the party, but they are joined by the Veiled Chain agents as allies.

Fighting the Redfiend

Without access to magic, Loris Tezran relies on his pure martial abilities, using his @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND.Item.y7aZsVssXjL1Mjz3]{Multiattack} to make four attacks with @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND.Item.Vjng7ukm5ZyIw3gJ]{Foolsbane}.

As a masterful swordfighter, he uses his @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND.Item.da8EcyKQS44fGYrl]{Reactive} and @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND.Item.2sZQ1TlsdQlXF7ZW]{Riposte} abilities to defend himself, and take advantage of opportunities as they appear.

His legendary actions include a @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND.Item.MW3hKRIgekK7AmjO]{Lunging Strike} and two commands he can issue Rakavi: @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND.Item.tkVpLJpFukvamRBW]{Command: Pounce} and @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND.Item.FqKF6NLj8cZ72sxK]{Command: Tail Swipe} which he needs to be able to speak to use. If Rakavi is defeated, these actions become unusable.

Loris is a ferocious fighter, but he does not have a deathwish, and will surrender if he falls below half his maximum hit points and is unlikely to win if he keeps fighting.

Additionally, if Rakavi's life is in mortal peril (such as being below half its max HP), or if the beast has been killed, he can be convinced to give up with an action and a successful [[/skill persuasion 14]], or [[/skill intimidation 14]] check.

Fighting Rakavi

Rakavi is an @UUID[Actor.wz5NmMYH7HdO32GS]{Ancara} and uses its @UUID[Actor.wz5NmMYH7HdO32GS.Item.TgcxZ2UgJq13WGHl]{Sweeping Tail} to knock over foes, followed by its @UUID[Actor.wz5NmMYH7HdO32GS.Item.0LXjHYolKn09PB6g]{Crushing Bite} or @UUID[Actor.wz5NmMYH7HdO32GS.Item.0YJ2P0CTX5Oip6X7]{Rending Claw} after.

It fights as long as Loris does, and surrenders only if they do.

Veiled Chain Allies

There are several Veiled Chain Agents hiding on the roof, posing as prisoners in cages when the trap is set. They fight to disable Loris and Rakavi, but refuse to kill either, and attempt to prevent anyone else from killing them. Their aim is to arrest Loris.

Concluding the Event

Ragen Attunement: Breaking Out

A party that fights it way out of the tower without any regard for stealth or alarms advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 diplomaticImpunityBreakoutFought]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Sneaking Out

A party that successfully sneaks out of the prison or reaches the tower roof without raising alarm or entering combat advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 diplomaticImpunityBreakoutSneaked]] at the conclusion of the event.

Ragen Attunement: Redfiend Reversal

A party that successfully defeats Loris Tezran in battle on the top of the tower advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +2 diplomaticImpunityBreakoutRedfiendBeaten]] at the conclusion of the event.

Milestone Progression

Completing this event awards a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone} point, potentially enabling the party to advance in level.

Next Steps

The resolution of this event depends on what the party has done in the prison.

If the party was working with the Veiled Chain, and captured Ambassador Tezran, then they are released from the prison and the quest concludes with this event, though they will receive some unpleasant news later via the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.jZb8BLcXdOvp0S5h] event.

If the party escaped but is letting Toron go without turning him over, then the party can escape into the city, and end the quest chain here. However, they will remain wanted by the Hallows and Veiled Chain, and risk being apprehended if they draw too much attention to themselves going forward.

Selecting a Destination

If the party intends to turn Toron over to the Ambassador or Katerin, they will need to select a destination point for their escape, moving directly into the final event of the quest.

If they take Toron to Ambassador Tezran they'll head back to Embassy Rise and get @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.MjbdRFpFkJXFed8g], if they take Toron to Katerin in Coinwealth Heights they'll get @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.kfVNJY9cm9UZttBa] instead.
Breaking the Tower.soverview: The party begins their breakout of the Spellbreaker Tower prison. They'll need to recover their stashed equipment and use it to sneak or fight their way to the top of the tower with Toron. There, they'll leap from the tower, using the wingsuits to sail to safety.
Breaking the Tower.sexposition: Life in the tower carries on around you, guards patrol between cells, peering between bars here and there, while less scrutinized inmates idle in common spaces. You find yourselves mixed in among them, waiting for a moment to arrive, the moment when your escape attempt begins.
Breaking the Tower.ssummary: We enacted our plan to escape from the Spellbreaker Tower and its prison levels.

No Good Deed.name: No Good Deed
No Good Deed.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event happens some time after the party helped capture Ambassador Tezran, and involves the party being summoned to the Hallows to have a meeting with the Veiled Chain. In this event the party will learn:

  • The outcome of capturing the ambassador.

  • What the ambassador and Tayans did in response.

  • What the party should expect going forward.

So, the good news first: I secured you a payout for your work against the Ambassador's plot. It's not much, but it's something at least. I've also made sure to have the falsified records expunged and disconnected from your names.

She places a heavy pouch on the table which jingles softly on impact. As you claim it she slides a dossier in front of herself.

Now, for the bad news.

Yeela flips open a dossier, revealing a stamped document, reports, and an unmistakable portrait of Ambassador Loris Tezran.

Okay, so. Despite our collective efforts, Loris Tezran has managed to slip out of Hallows custody, and return to his embassy. Before you ask, no, nothing stuck. Instructions came down from the Ordinate directly that he be released immediately with no charges pressed. He didn't even get a reprimand for his actions.

They close the file with deliberate calm.

Now, while insight into the Embassy is limited, we know for certain he’s not happy. You embarrassed him in front of Katerin, his underlings, the Ordinate, and more crucially: his Empress. You can expect him to hold a grudge, probably permanently, and eventually make you pay for it.

I wanted to tell so you at least knew well enough to watch your back. I'd feel bad if he managed to blindside you.

They pause, allowing the weight of that to sink in, and leave space for questions.

Yeela provides the party [[/award 1000gp]] as a reward for their efforts.

What about Toron’s fate?

That's a bit of good news, actually. He was moved to a secure off-site location where he could be handled properly. Not in the Tower, and not within Ordain’s public record. He’s cooperating, surprisingly. The Tayans won’t find him, not unless something goes catastrophically wrong.

How did the Ambassador get free?

Political pressure, mostly. The Tayan Empire leaned hard on the Ordinate, and the Ordinate blinked. Political exchanges, trade threats, diplomatic gestures, the typical song and dance.

She gestures to the dossier on the table.

The official report reads that the charges were ‘unsubstantiated and beyond the local jurisdiction of the Hallows.’

In short, the man has friends in high places.

What kind of repercussions should we expect?

Anything, really. He’s resourceful and patient. Could send assassins or spies, could twist the paperwork and create red tape in the Ordinate to cause you headaches. He might even aim to poison your reputation with rumors, turn allies against you.

The Redfiend’s grudge burns slow, but it burns until satisfied.

And Katerin?

We know she was involved, but didn't come away with anything that’ll hold up in Hallows court.

Every lead we dig into comes up clean, too clean, frankly. It's rather unnerving how good she is at covering her tracks, assuming it is her. It's possible she's got a world-class fixer on payroll, but that's just speculation.

For now, she’s just under watch while we try to root out her allies in the Hallows.

Wrapping Up

Once the party has asked all the questions they care to, the agent wraps up the meeting:

Yeela stands, signaling that the meeting is over.

Well, that’s the state of things. I'm sorry that the Chain can’t protect you from the games the Ambassador plays, but at least you've been warned. I felt you earned that much.

I’ll be in touch if anything changes. In the meantime… keep your weapons oiled, check your locks often, and don't sit with your back to a window.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished receiving their update, they are free to go on their way, and seek adventure elsewhere in Ordain.
No Good Deed.soverview: The party is informed that Redfiend managed to use his connections and clout to evade consequences and is back at his posting as Ambassador.
No Good Deed.sexposition:
Making your way to the Hallowsyou are met at the entrance by a member of the Veiled Chain who motions for you to follow, and walks you into the meeting area. The agent that guided you there is replaced by Yeela a moment later.

Welcome back, have a seat. I've got news, not much of it good.

She gestures for you to sit.
No Good Deed.ssummary: We were called in to the Hallows to meet with the Veiled Chain and informed that Ambassador Tezran was no longer in the custody of the Spellbreaker Tower. It seems that his political clout and connections and enough plausible deniability resulted in his release. We were warned to watch our backs, as Tezran would almost certainly be looking for us after betraying him.

Doing Time.name: Doing Time
Doing Time.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration event sees the party delivered to the Spellbreaker Tower and submitted to the prison as new inmates. This is where the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.h4neZftlUY3J51dw]{criminal records} they helped created will come into play, which will determine what cell blocks they are placed into.

During this event the party will:

  • Learn about the prison levels from the inside, how it works, and who is housed.

  • Meet with Toron and take steps to convince him to become part of the planned escape.

  • Prepare for the coming prison break.

Area Walkthrough

This event's gameplay transitions to the "Spellbreaker Tower" scene where the this event transpires. A complete room-by-room description of its environment occurs there is detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8] area walkthrough. Text related to this event's resolution is retained in this event and should be referenced alongside the walkthrough.

This area has several special rules and gameplay expectations, so it is advisable to review the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.tj1ZpcdX5wJ0ooRB] page either before or during the party's exploration of the location.

Entry and Processing

The party begins at the @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.BMAgxL8BOc8wWqmZ]{Entry Checkpoint} and will be moved through the prison by a group of three @UUID[Actor.QnYBCVJZr2dnukzz]{Spellbreaker Guards}, with two behind the group, and one ahead, leading the way.

A clerk sits behind a narrow window, his manner bored and brisk, leafing through pages of records you recognize your forged background.

Another fine batch of lowlifes. Excellent. Welcome to the tower. Now, let's see who we're working with today...

As the clerk goes over your files and gets things in order the guards begin to confiscate your belongings, packing them away into chests.

At this point you should have the clerk read off the offenses of each character based on the persona they helped craft. Each one of these figures was apprehended, tried before the Hallows and found guilty.

In addition to these records they should be assigned placement in one of the prison levels: Blue, Yellow or Red. Their placement depends on the level of violence in their record, and how volatile they appear to be.

Blue Block, Minimum security:

Those who are unlikely to harm anyone are held here. They are allowed free movement in the block, open recreation, and communal meals. They generally receive the least scrutiny, and are rarely subject to searches or lockdowns unless there's an incident first.

Yellow Block, Medium security:

Those with capacity harm others and history of being dangerous are housed here. They are allowed out of their cells with supervision, and as long as they behave, may have communal meals, but are locked down for even minor offenses, and subject to frequent searches every day.

Red Block, Maximum security:

Those with incredible capacity for violence or those that cannot be trusted to control themselves are locked down here. They are not let out of their cells, are constantly watched, and receive meals delivered by armed guards.

Where to Place the Party

It's recommended that you put the party in Blue Block if possible, but depending on the records they crafted, it might be more appropriate to put some of them in Yellow. We don't recommend you put any of the party in Red block to start, since that will severely limit character mobility in the prison.

Into Holding

The party is walked through the prison level to @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.CvHoqViz4Z26Apbn]{Stairwell Checkpoint 1} where they are alleviated of their items, armor, weapons, and anything else they brought with them.

The guard in the checkpoint points to the space in the center of the checkpoint.

Place your things in neat piles at your feet. You won't leave this level in anything but the clothes you're wearing. Once you've finished placing your items down, you'll be searched and moved aside.

Your items will be stored in the tower, and returned to you upon your release, minus any items that are illegal to have in the city limits of Ordain. Those will be confiscated.

Once the party has finished being relieved of their items, they are taken up another level to @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.gzphhu9XASBBI6sw]{Stairwell Checkpoint 2}

The march up the tower is not a difficult one, but the long, wide stairwells are without natural light, and the heavy stone walls make it clear nobody gets out of here easily. At each landing you spy locked gates manned by guards. Though none of them are heavily armed or armored, they look alert and focused.

Each floor is the same: a series of gates opening and closing behind you as you move higher into the tower, tackling another flight of stairs, and passing through a level crawling with guards, until finally you arrive at a landing where a Cinadric Sage and a guard wait for you next to racks of clothing.

Here, the party is given a checkup by a waiting Cindaric Adherent, who will offer them mundane medical treatment for any injuries they may have. After that, they are instructed to put on uniforms here based on the cell block they are heading to. Privacy is a luxury not afforded here, sadly.

Once the party is changed, a senior guard appears to orient you:

Welcome to the tower, from here you're about to be taken to your cells. Before we do that, we're going to go over the rules in the Spellbreaker Tower. They are very simple: No fighting. No stealing. No hiding contraband. Follow the commands of the guards promptly, and we will have no issues.

The guard paces slowly, the speech well practiced.

Meals are served the same time: morning, noon, and night, and we'll do our best to make sure everyone gets a chance to eat. If you can't make it to mess due to injury, illness or infraction, we'll make sure you're fed. Starving you is not one of the goals we aspire to here in the tower.

We wish to treat you with dignity and respect, and believe such should be given back in kind. You will be afforded as much privacy and freedom as your condition or sentencing permits. But do not test us, we will do what is necessary to ensure safety and security are maintained.

With that, the senior guard walks off, leaving you to change.

From here the party is moved up to @UUID[JournalEntry.SEmb0Fox8QAhOvK8.JournalEntryPage.dyPqEixnw7eHjAZf]{Stairwell Checkpoint 3}. Characters bound for Blue Block are sent through to an empty cell here, while Yellow block inmates are sent up another level.

Where to Place the Party

It's recommended that you place the party in adjacent cells if possible, provided they are all on the same level.

Establishing the Routine

Once the party has changed they are transferred to their cells and offered a meal if they are hungry. It's expected that you'll want to advance time at least eight hours after this point.

The prison serves food three times a day, breakfast at 9am, lunch at 2pm, and dinner at 7pm. Inmates are expected to be in their cells by 9pm. Otherwise, the characters are free to explore the prison and interact at will.

The party should be encouraged to interact with the prison, explore the area, and observe how the prison operates. Consult with the area walkthrough for the Spellbreaker Tower for how the tower operates while the party is present.

The walkthrough also includes the various inmates that can be encountered on each level, though you are encouraged to create your own colorful, strange, and dangerous characters to fill the cells as you see fit.

Time Served

From that point onward the party should speak with Toron and begin preparing for their escape. This phase might take a few hours or could take days of preparation. Both are valid, but once the party is ready the next event should be triggered.

Meeting Toron

Finding Toron is simple; the party know he is in Yellow Block, and is routinely allowed down into Blue Block during daytime hours to socialize and entertain himself due to generally good behavior. He often leaves his cell (when allowed) to eat, exercise, and otherwise spend his free time. Convincing him to join the escape however, is not. The task requires care as he expects spies, betrayal, and traps.

@embed[Actor.WQzk939folhpYwOH]

Convincing Toron

Convincing Toron to work with the party is not easy, and should not be attempted before the party speaks with him first. Saying the wrong thing could make these checks easier or harder.

Failing to persuade Toron in any of the below methods does not prevent future attempts, and a party that spends more time with him may find other ways to make him agreeable.

Persuading Toron

A successful [[/skill persuasion 18]] check can convince Toron to work with the party, though he will require the party to tell him the plan in detail so that he knows what to do.

  • Result of 23+ Toron is convinced that the party and plan has merit, and will do his best to help prepare so that the escape is a success.

Deceiving Toron

A successful [[/skill deception 18]] check is necessary can convince Toron to work with the party without divulging all the details to him. He remains skeptical of their plan, and won't fully commit himself out of concern over it going badly.

  • Result of 23+ Toron believes the party has a workable plan, and is willing to work with them, but dislikes being kept in the dark.

Intimidating Toron

A successful [[/skill intimidation 17]] check can force temporary compliance but he won't trust the party and views them as a threat, seeking to get away from them at first opportunity.

  • Result of 22+ Toron is sufficiently cowed that he will remain compliant for the entirety of the escape, but his opinion doesn't change.

How did you get captured?

I made a mistake, and my escape plan failed. Details don't matter beyond that.

We can get you out. Are you willing to work with us?

You can try to get me out, but it's a tall order. Ordain runs a tight operation here, and the tower's magic suppression is unlike anything I've experienced. I don't think there's a way past it.

If the fact the party is working for Redfiend is known, he also says:

Besides, with you being here on Loris' orders, I’d rather rot in this hole than let you turn me over to him.

What if we’re not working for Tezran?

Then you’ve got my attention. You pull this off, I’ll follow your lead... but gods help you if this is a trick.

The party expressing disdain, hatred, or dislike for the Ambassador reduces the DC of any checks to convince Toron by 4. However, expressing the opposite will make the DC increase by the same amount.

Would you be willing to go into Katerin Bastilla's custody?

The head of the trade house? I suppose that could work out okay. I assume she wants my magical knowledge, and in return I'd be hidden. Might be trading one prison for another though...

Extending Katerin's offer to Toron reduces the DC of any checks to convince Toron by 4. This can be combined with other DC reductions gained from social interactions with Toron.

If Ambassador Tezran is mentioned during any interactions, the following occurs:

The moment Ambassador Tezran’s name is mentioned, a muscle in Toron's jaw locks.

The Redfiend sent you, I assumed as much. If you expect me to just walk into his clutches, you're sorely mistaken. You'll have to drag me out of here, or kill me yourself.

Why is he called The Redfiend?

It was the Empress’s gift after what he did to the Kelmezians. He burned a city to ash to prove his loyalty. Tens of thousands dead in a single night. It cemented his position in the royal court and put his name on the lips of every noble house in the Empire.

Why would he want you back now?

Because I failed him. My failure’s a stain on his record. If he retrieves me himself, he gets to clean it publicly. Don’t think he’s doing it out of friendship or obligation as my commending officer.

You expect the Ambassador to kill you?

Absolutely, without a single doubt. I'm dead if I let you take me to him, and I wouldn't expect him to treat you any better as a reward.

His favorite place to keep his daggers is in the backs of his allies and underlings.

What's it like in the Empire?

Great, if you're on top. There's plenty of money, food, and luxury for the noble houses and their cronies. If you're born poor though you just have the factories and forges to look forward to. Or if you're unlucky, the mines and gas pits.

Ragen Attunement: Unwilling Participant

A party that coerces or forces Toron to cooperate with their plans advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 diplomaticImpunityPrisonCoercedToron]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Willing Participant

A party that convinces or tricks Toron into cooperating with their plans advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 diplomaticImpunityPrisonConvincedToron]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party is ready begin their prison break, initiate the next event in the quest: @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.TGOj5GcJdo3tsp85].
Doing Time.soverview: They party is delivered to the Spellbreaker Tower, the criminal records they helped forge being used to ensure their entry as wanted criminals. Once inside, the party can begin planning their breakout.
Doing Time.sexposition:
The clatter of iron wheels fades as your wagon grinds to a halt at the base of the Spellbreaker Tower. The Bastilla guards dismount first, handing over a packet of documents to one of the guards before they begin to unload you. A pair of armored wardens step up to assist, carrying iron shackles with heavy chains.

You are transferred from wagon to the custody of the tower guards, and taken in pairs through the immense front doors. The metallic echo of boots and chains reverberates off the bare stone in the entry hall, the space bare and cold within, holding only a clerk and desk, the both of them inaccessible to you.
Doing Time.ssummary: We were admitted to the Spellbreaker Tower prison under the guise of the false criminal personas we created some time ago. We've been placed in prison cells and are now at the mercy of the prison guards here. We need to make contact with Toron, and put our plan to escape into action soon.

One Dead Courier.name: One Dead Courier
One Dead Courier.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this combat event the party runs into a brazen attack on a courier belonging to the Tayan Empire. The party has the chance to do the following:

  • Intervene and capture or drive off the attackers.

  • Investigate the corpse of the courier.

  • Discover the courier's satchel of imperial documents.

Scene Under Development

The scene used for this event lacks walls, doors and lighting due to a technical limitation on how the scenes are configured. These limitations will be resolved in a future update.

Dealing with the Murderers

The party can deal with the band of ruffians in several ways.

Fighting the Ruffians

The group consists of 6 x @UUID[Actor.jZBVgCb2P61F9SrT]{Ordani Ruffians} armed with small weapons. They have no qualms with killing, having just murdered someone, and will fight to kill. However, their morale will break if three or more ruffians are defeated, causing them to flee.

Coercing the Killers

It is possible to convince the ruffians to surrender, or flee if that is what the party wants to do. In either case, a successful [[/skill intimidation 15]] check is necessary. If the party causes them to surrender, they can be restrained and left for the authorities to pick up after the event concludes.

Ragen Attunement: Immediate Justice

Any character who joins in the fight to subdue the ruffians advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 diplomaticImpunityCourierFoughtRuffians]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Being Reasonable

Each character who uses their social skills to coerce the ruffians into surrender or flight advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 diplomaticImpunityCourierConvincedRuffians]] at the conclusion of the event.

Dealing with the Courier

Once the killers are dealt with, the party is left with a dead body to deal with. They will likely want to begin with searching it.

Examining the Scene

The scene consists of the deceased courier, and their dropped messenger bag which is full of documents. There are witnesses and bystanders, though many have already left the area, leaving only a few scattered folk trying to go about their business.

[[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/skill history 14]] know that this sort of crime is all but unheard of in Ordain. Most of the crime the city sees is either petty theft, smuggling, and some sort of corruption. Violent crime has always been rare, and something this brazen even more so.

The courier and their bag can be examined in closer detail.

Inspecting the Courier

As one would predict, the courier is dead, and cannot be saved. Their body contains an opened envelope, and some personal effects, though none of it has any true value or relevance. Additionally, next to their body is a @UUID[Item.PaU4FVJCS77r1OJ6] filled with scrolls, envelopes, and folders.

[[/knowledge intrigue]] or [[/knowledge crime]] posits that the ruffians attacked just because the courier looked well off and was vulnerable. If they were after the documents specifically, they would have taken the bag and left straight away.

Characters with [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/culture emberTayan]] or [[/path emberImperialConscript]] recognize the uniform of a low-level functionary in the Tayan Empire. Their death could be a problem for the Ordinate, and if the documents don't get delivered, will likely hinder the local Tayan contingent as well.

Courier's Orders

Characters with [[/knowledge politics]] or [[/culture emberTayan]] or [[/path emberImperialConscript]] recognize that the opened envelope in the courier's coat bears the official crest of the Tayan Empire. Inside it is an official letter written in [[/language imperial]] and contains instructions for the courier. They were meant to deliver the satchel of missives and messages to Commander Loris Tezran in Embassy Rise in Ordain.

Characters that don't understand Imperial will still recognize a proper name: the city district of Embassy Rise. It should be simple enough to assume the documents were meant for the Tayan Embassy there.

Using Necromancy

If the courier is questioned via @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithD]{Speak with Dead}, they can provide a little information: they were sent from the Tayan Empire, they were delivering messages to the Tayan Ambassador in Ordain, Loris Tezran. They don't know what the documents contain. They don't know why they were attacked.

If asked about the cipher used on some of the letters, they know that only high ranking officials have them.

Resurrecting the Courier

The party should not have access to the necessary spells when this quest is first encountered, and thus resurrection should not be a possibility. To that effect, there is no provision in the event text for reviving the courier and how that would change events.

However, if the party waits to tackle this quest, they might have the necessary spells or items to do so. At a basic level, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplRevivify00] should always prove ineffective, as the courier will have been dead for over a minute by the time the ruffians have been dealt with. Any greater level of resurrection magic would be successful, however, the result of doing so is left to your discretion.

Refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.0RXUc08I2fOUESTL#resurrection]{Resurrection} and the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.c1aSjHNbUgDscRy7]{Soul Cycle} for guidance on how death and resurrection works in Ember.

The dropped bag beside the courier will also warrant examination.

Signara Attunement: Undeniable Curiosity

Any character who chooses to look through the bag of documents taken from the courier advances their [[/attunement emberSignara +1 diplomaticImpunityCourierExaminedDocuments]] at the conclusion of the event.

Akon Attunement: Deniable Curiosity

Any character who resists the urge tothrough the bag of documents taken from the courier advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 bookTalesMoonChildAkonResistedCuriosity]] at the conclusion of the event.

Examining the Bag

The bag contains a large number of documents, mostly scrolls, but some in envelopes and sealed folders. The bag has been dropped and trampled, leaving many of the documents inside damaged as well. Many of the wax seals on the documents are broken already due to the abuse the pack suffered.

Your Eyes Only

The documents cover a wide range of topics, though the majority of them are terse acknowledgement of prior reports, or mundane letters that talk about weather and recent events. In a few cases there are diagrams and drawings of machines or floor plans for structures relating to some sort of "Highgate project."

Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] or making a successful [[/skill investigation 18]] check know that the mundane letters are encoded in some way, and hold secret messages, but without the cipher there's no way to determine what they actually say.

Characters with [[/knowledge politics]] or making a successful [[/skill history 15]] check know that @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.jI992TwkfCqH9H8Z]{Highgate }was badly damaged in a quake some years ago, and has been the subject of extensive reconstruction efforts. It seems that the Tayan Empire is somehow involved in that effort, at least partially.

Once the party has searched the scene there is not much for them to do, but they can wait for the authorities to arrive if they want. This takes a few minutes.

Holding Out for the Hallows

If the party wants to wait for authorities to arrive, they can. Eventually a Hallows inspector will arrive to take reports and make sure the body (or bodies) and any captured culprits are dealt with.

However, when it comes to the document bag, the party is put on the spot: they can either head to the Hallows to report the bag to the Veiled Chain, and let them handle it, or they can take the bag to the Tayan Embassy, to make sure the courier's work is seen through to the end.

Mayis Attunement: Waiting for Resolution

If the party chooses to wait for the authorities to arrive so they can report the events that transpired, or hand over surrendered ruffians, each character advances their [[/attunement emberMayis +1 diplomaticImpunityCourierWaited]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has defeated the attackers and finished examining the dead courier, they can choose to visit the Tayan Embassy to hand over the wayward documents, or report the crime to the authorities in the Hallows.

If the party chooses to report the attack, the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.5eXgvCwkvIVCP4Xi] event needs to be manually triggered to do so.
One Dead Courier.soverview: The party stumbles across a Tayan Imperial Courier being attacked and killed. After the dust settles they will find the courier's bag holds a trove of letters and scrolls meant for the Tayan ambassador in Ordain.
One Dead Courier.sexposition:
Making your way through a section of the waterfront you hear cries of alarm and yelling. A moment later a local scrambles up to you, fear in their eyes.

They're killing him, you've got to help!

They turn and point to a plaza nearby where a group of armed men fight against a man in a uniform of black and red. They are trying to take something from his arms, and he is resisting to the best of his ability. A moment later one of the armed men steps up and jams a blade into the uniformed man's back.

He crumples to the ground, and the murderers begin rummaging through his coat and dropped bag for valuables.

A few scattered locals look on in frozen horror.
One Dead Courier.ssummary: We witnessed the murder of a courier working for the Tayan Empire. Their satchel of diplomatic missives and documents was left behind, and we should do something with it. We could return it to the Tayan Embassy, or leave it with the authorities at the Hallows.

Foreign Influence.name: Foreign Influence
Foreign Influence.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event involves the party meeting and being extorted by the Tayan Ambassador @UUID[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND]{Loris Tezran} who is also a special agent to the crown. In this event the following should occur:

  • The party will be pressed into service, forced to help the ambassador under threat of punishment for a crime they likely didn't commit.

  • The party will be sent to meet with another ally/contact of the Ambassador in Coinwealth Heights.

  • The party will be able to learn a little bit about Tayan culture, and the Ambassador himself.

Meeting the Ambassador

After the party states their business, and presents the messenger bag the attendant responds as follows:

Ah, that is most fortunate. We received word that our courier was in the city, but had not seen them. Please, come inside, Ambassador Tezran will want to speak with you directly.

You’re ushered through a cool, polished foyer and along a quiet corridor that opens into a manicured garden. Clipped hedges and white gravel paths frame a view of the city’s waterfront below. You’re invited to wait among marble benches, the attendant leaving you to sit in silence, yet you cannot shake the sensation of being watched.

Concealed Security

Characters succeeding on a [[/skill perception 16]] note that several of the windows above have armed guards watching the garden below. There are four of these sharpshooters in total, and they are watching the garden closely.

  • Result of 21+ Though it's hard to see from this low vantage, the guards appear to be well armed with heavy crossbows or something similar, and would be firing from raised, concealed positions with ample cover. They would have a significant.

An Obvious Deterrent

The presence of the armed guards here is meant to deter the players from choosing violence in the upcoming social encounter. While the Ambassador is a highly competent combatant himself, and has the aid of his trained mount, this is a layer of additional insurance.

Combat Diplomacy

If the party does decide to escalate to violence for any reason, the four snipers act on initiative count 20, have a [[/roll 2d20kh +6]]{Ranged Attack} with a +6 bonus and advantage from their firing position. They deal [[/damage 1d10 +4 piercing]] damage on hit. They have an AC of 18 to hit (with cover) and 35 HP.

The Ambassador Arrives

@embed[Actor.oSDaY9LSzRvxQZND]

@embed[Actor.wz5NmMYH7HdO32GS label="Rakavi" readaloud="A creature of unmistakable presence, this beast's brown plumage is broken by a vivid streak of red feathers running from his head down the length of his back to the tip of his tail. His head bears the intelligent golden eyes of a predator, and a serrated beak well suited to rip apart prey. On the shoulder of his foreleg the imperial crest of the Tayan Empire has been burned into the scales, branding him as their property."]

From the side of the building a shadow slips across the gravel as a massive winged creature stalks into view, talons clicking, its pinions rustling like heavy silk. It watches you with a predatory intensity that tightens the air.

A heartbeat later, a regal man in red and black finery joins it, every line of his attire tailored to quiet authority. He lays a hand on the side of the beast.

Calm, Rakavi, they are guests.

The beast exhales, posture easing, wings settling close to its sides as the Ambassador offers you a courteous nod.

I am Loris Tezran, Ambassador to Ordain from the Tayan Empire. I understand you've come into possession of some documents belonging to my office.

Host and Pet

Characters with either the [[/culture emberTayan]] or [[/path emberImperialConscript]] or making a successful [[/skill history 18]] check recognizes Loris Tezran as a famed commander of the Tayan Empire, and holder of the moniker "Redfiend" after his role in the bloody conquest of a Kelmezian city state some years ago.

Characters that make a successful [[/skill nature 14]] check will recognize the creature as an ancara, a predator known for its agility, ability to climb, and glide. Native to the Corebright Forest, it roams themas an apex predator. This one seems to have been trained as a war beast and has not lost its predatory edge in the slightest.

The party can engage in a bit of small talk with the Ambassador if they want, but once they hand over the messenger bag, the next part of this event begins.

Imperial Ambition
