The Ambassador lays out the documents from the bag, examining them one by one, taking note of the crushing damage and numerous broken seals on them. And air of displeasure brews around him like a storm, and eventually he looked to you, his voice taking on an edge:

You know, it is a high crime in the city of Ordain to tamper with official diplomatic documents. The seals are broken on nearly every document here, leaving me to question if they have been tampered with, or if sensitive knowledge has been gleaned about the innermost operations of my nation's diplomatic efforts.

If I were less merciful, I'd have you all detained to be put before the Hallows and tried for espionage against a foreign dignitary. However, that is messy, and time consuming, and benefits neither of us.

Instead, I'd rather you run some errands for me as compensation, then we put this whole debacle behind us.

We didn't open the documents!

So you say, but you have no proof and I have no evidence that these documents are opened by anyone other than you. You can claim unknown figures, or faceless murders carried out the act, but I see neither here right now. Perhaps the Hallows would side with you, but such cases take months to resolve, and you'd be jailed for the duration, I'd see to it.

What are the tasks?

They are very simple, and not even mine, truly. I need you to head to the Coinwealth Heights and visit with a woman known as Katerine Bastila, an important ally of mine. She has a handful of tasks she wants dealt with, and I've agreed to get her help on them. This means you. Once you've satisfied her task list, come back to me, and we'll settle up affairs.

Responding to the Ambassador

No Easy Way Out

The party is intended to be coerced into this course of action by the Ambassador. While it is possible for them to refuse to help, the offer remains open so that they can come back if they change their minds.

If the party does say no, they are able to leave without issue, and carry on with their adventure.

Elements Under Development

At present there are no repercussions for refusing to work with the Ambassador. If the party refuses they are free to go about their business and carry on their adventure unhindered. They will not be arrested or harassed unless you decide to do so as the gamemaster.

This may change in the future with additional events.

If the party threatens the Ambassador

I'm sure you've also noted that there are several guards in the windows above keeping watch over this meeting. They do not miss.

The the party has expressed recognition of his title "Redfiend" he adds:

If you know who I am, then you also know what I am capable of. Do not test me.

If the party does accept to carry out the ambassador's tasks, he responds as such:

The Ambassador sweeps the documents into the bag and stands lifting it with him

Good, very good! I am pleased you've chosen to be reasonable. Seek out Katerin Bastilla at the Bastilla estate in Coinwealth, and handle the tasks she has for you. Once you've done them all, report back here, and we can put all this ugly business behind us.

Endran will see you out.

With that, the Ambassador takes his leave, though the massive ancara, Rakavi, remains in place, watchful and vigilant.

A moment later an attendant appear, Endran you presume, and he gestures for you to follow.

This way, please.

You are walked through the embassy to the entrance, and escorted to the front gates which clatter closed behind you.

Once the party is clear of the embassy they can carry on with this quest, or return to other matters.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished being coerced by the ambassador, they should head off to Coinwealth Heights to meet the ambassador's contact. If they want, they can also report this meeting to the Veiled Chain via the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.5eXgvCwkvIVCP4Xi]{Coming Clean} event.
Foreign Influence.soverview: The party delivers the documents to the Tayan Ambassador, but their good deed is twisted around on them as the Redfiend attempts to extort them into carrying out tasks to avoid punishment for supposedly tampering with official diplomatic documents.
Foreign Influence.sexposition:
The Tayan embassy' clean lines stand before you, a two-story square of pale stone and wide, gleaming windows that mirror the sky. Standing just inside the gate a guard in red and black uniform steps forward, posture straight, the gold accents on his uniform and armor catching the light as he looks you over with professional calm.

With a crisp nod he signals inside to announce your arrival.

Visitors at the gate!

Moments later an attendant in matching colors appears, their manner warm where the guard’s is measured. In a calm, smooth voice the address you:

Greetings, how may I assist you this day?
Foreign Influence.ssummary: We returned the wayward documents to the ambassador of the Tayan Empire, one Loris Tezran. As a reward he accused us of tampering with the seals on the documents and reading sensitive data. He threatened to report us to the Ordinate directly for interfering with diplomatic communications unless we do some tasks for him and his allies.

Coming Clean.name: Coming Clean
Coming Clean.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This repeatable social event allows the party to report to the Veiled Chain, informing them about the events that occur in this quest. Reporting to the Veiled Chain allows the party to:

  • Learn about the Tayans and House Bastilla.

  • Get direction and guidance from the Veiled Chain.

  • Work toward a special ending in this quest.

Manual Trigger

Note that a party moving to the Hallows will not prompt you to activate this event as is typical for other events. This event needs to be manually triggered via the "Initiate Event" button found at the top and bottom of this page. This needs to be done each time the party chooses to visit the Hallows and report to the Veiled Chain, which they can do multiple times as the quest progresses.

Repeatable Event

This is a repeating event where the party can report to the VC about events going on in the quest. This event is available until the moment the party ends up in prison. The Outcomes provide the GM ways to track what pieces of information have been reported on, and can unlock a special ending encounter if the party commits to this path.

@embed[Actor.B5TakRnU7gZ4X3pV]{Yeela Drevvin}

Yeela is a veteran agent of the Veiled Chain with decades of service to the city under her belt. She is keen-eyed, insightful, and dedicated to keeping the city safe. She specializes in profiling subjects with the aim of predicting their actions.

In walks a human woman, Ordani by the style of her clothing, middle aged and fit. At first you mistake her for a stranger, but quickly notice the Veiled Chain crest pinned to her clothing, making her as an agent in its ranks.

Hello, I'm Yeela Drevvin, senior agent of the Veiled Chain.

Yeela takes out a notebook and pencil, sitting down as she continues:

I understand you were witness to a crime and want to make a formal report. Go ahead and do so, and please be as detailed as you can manage. The more you recall, the more we'll have to work with here.

Reporting the Courier

Well that's not good at all. I'll add this onto the pile of waterfront incidents lately. More concerning is the death of a foreign agent, which I'll need to get reported to the Ordinate so they aren't caught off guard when a diplomatic incident lands in their lap.

She sets her pencil down and leans back in her seat.

So, I'm going to offer you a reward of twenty-five gold pieces for being good, law abiding citizens.

Yeela reaches into a hip pouch and pulls out a smaller pouch that jingles audibly when it lands on the table.

And I also need to ask you a favor: Take the satchel of documents from the deceased courier to the Tayan Embassy located in Embassy Rise. I'd have one of our runners do it, but we're stretched thin at the moment.

If you come back afterward, I'll give you another twenty-five gold for your trouble.

Can't you do it?

Yeela shakes her head.

Not really, no. I've got to follow up on thus murder, get what information I can, and then report it up the chain to the Ordinate.

What if we get blamed?

Yeela scoffs at the question.

Don't be silly, just explain what happened, and offer to return the reports. You might even get a reward for your trouble. Just be polite and mind your manners. You'll be fine.

What about the murder?

We will look into it, don't you worry. The Chain isn't going to view the death of a foreign agent as a minor incident, and the Ordinate will want answers.

Is violence on the rise in Ordain?

Yeela takes a moment to consider that.

Yes and no. There are some districts where crime has increased, and some of those increases do include spikes in violence, but overall it's marginal, and not widespread.

Akon Attunement: The Rule of Law

Any character who goes along to report the crime to the Veiled Chain advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 bookTalesMoonChainReported]] at the conclusion of the event. Note: This attunement occurs only the first time the party reports to the Veiled Chain.

The next time the party can report in is after they complete [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityInfluence]] and met with Ambassador Loris Tezran.

Reporting the Ambassador

Yeela raises her eyebrow at the report as she takes notes.

Strong-arming you into service is unexpected. We know he's working angles and trying to make friends in the city, so Katerin Bastilla's inclusion isn't a surprise, especially given their ongoing trade deals.

However, I am now curious what he's after. If you're up for it, I want you to keep cooperating, and see where this goes.

You know Katerin Bastilla is involved?

We had suspicions. She's very ambitious and opportunistic, and the Tayans need money to fund their wars. Most of the major sea trade organizations in the area are wary of the Tayans, or their parent nations are under siege already, which makes creating trade deals… difficult.

Why do you want us to cooperate?

Because there is a chance that the Ambassador's plan is a threat to the city, and having you on the inside means we can find out if it is or not. If you stop working with him he'll need to find someone new, and we can't guarantee they'll come to us like you did.

After this check-in the party's next report possibility is after [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityRecords]] where they met Katerin Bastilla and got assignments from her.

Reporting Katerin Bastilla

Yeela takes notes silently for a moment before speaking.

Very interesting, very interesting. The depth of Katerin's connections is always surprising. We figured she had friends in the Hallows given how some court cases have gone in the past, but being able to brazenly falsify criminal records in the Hallows is a bit more involved.

She snaps her notebook shut.

You know the deal: Keep cooperating. See where this is headed. It seems like you're close to getting the full picture of the Ambassador's operation.

If Katerin and the Ambassador bring you in on the full plan, come update us and we'll put a plan into motion to stop them.

Don't you have enough evidence already?

Not really, no. We have your testimony, and that's valuable since it's created avenues of investigation we can pursue, but these need time to bear fruit. The more you can tell us about what they are doing, the better.

Can you arrest Katerin?

Right now, no, but this evidence and the jobs she's got you doing make that into more of a soft no that we could turn into a yes in the near future.

Can you arrest the Ambassador?

Yeela grimaces.

That's a much messier proposition. Foreign representatives have direct connection to the Ordinate, and while we can go after them if they break the law, getting charges to stick through all the political bureaucracy can be hard.

In fact, even if it does, there's a good chance they get pulled and replaced before anything comes of it.

Which is enough of a victory to some, I suppose.

The last check-in will be after the party completes [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityPlan]] and learns what the Ambassador's true intentions are. Note that they must report in before they go to the Spellbreaker Prison, since that will begin the next main event.

Starting the Counter-Operation

Yeela is silent for a long time after you give your report.

Well, that's bold. We figured the Tayans had some ulterior motives in the city, and that Toron was connected to Tayan espionage efforts, but this effectively confirms that.

She thinks for a moment.

I think we can make this plan work for us. We know that Ambassador Tezran's got a paranoid streak, and doesn't trust Katerin any more than she trusts him. Obviously we can't have you breaking Toron out, but I think we do want to have you go along with the plan. You'll be inserted into the prison, and go along with the breakout.

Knowing the Ambassador, he'll want to be nearby to ensure things go to plan, but won't risk his cover unless he has to. We need a way to force him to come to you on the tower, and if you do, we can have Veiled Chain agents waiting to capture him.

If the party [[/eventState diplomaticImpunityPlan suspicious]] then Yeela adds:

The fact that you let him know about Katerin's offer is a huge help. He's definitely not going to trust you to come to him now, and we can take advantage of that.

If you can get to the roof without raising the alarm, he'll likely come to pick up Toron directly. He'll probably want to leave you behind, but that's a sacrifice he'd be willing to make, I'm sure.

Otherwise she adds:

So, it might be a long-shot, but I'll expect that if you got to the roof and didn't have your wingsuits to escape with, he'd come in directly to pick up Toron. He'll probably want to leave you behind, but that's a sacrifice he'd be willing to make, I'm sure.

Why does it have to be without raising the alarm?

If you have to fight your way up to the roof of the tower and have guards and those Cascillian security machines chasing you he won't risk his neck. So you get to the roof and don't get swarmed, he'll take the chance.

Can't you just let us out?

Yeela laughs at that.

I wish, that would make this a whole lot simpler, but no, there's two things that make that impossible.

First one is that the Veiled Chain doesn't have direct influence or sway over the prison, and second is that knowing the warden, he won't agree to make it easier for you unless we arrive with Ordinate signed directions, which I doubt we could get.

So no, you'll have to break out on your own.

Why can't you get him in the Embassy?

It's technically foreign soil, it would take to get the Ordinate to sanction a raid on the location with the evidence we have right now. Plus, if the Veiled Chain launched a raid on the location it'd be exceptionally messy. Tayan infantry are no joke, and most of our agents aren't hardened combatants.

Characters with [[/knowledge politics]], [[/path emberImperialConscript]] or [[/culture emberTayan]] know that the Tayan Empire maintains a huge, professionally trained, and well equipped military that has seen decades of active combat, making it one of the most experienced fighting forces on Ember.

Characters that make a successful [[/skill history 14]] check know that the Tayan Empire has been in near continuous war since it formed, either through aggressive expansion of its borders, or by lending military aid to allies on more distant fronts, and as such is incredibly well versed in the art of war.

Primordis Attunement: Double Agents

A party that reports to the Veiled Chain enough that it incites them to take action against the Ambassador advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 diplomaticImpunityChainDoubleAgents]] at the conclusion of the event.

Lastly, before the party leaves Yeela has a final few words for them:

Well, I think that's it for my side. I'll have agents in place in case you pull off your side of things. Good luck in the Spellbreaker, Warden Holst runs a tight operation, getting out unseen won't be easy.

After a moment's pause Yeela adds:

Oh! Also, because you've been a huge help in all this, I'll make sure your records get cleared. As a bonus, if you swing back here afterward and look me up, I'll try to have a reward waiting. I think you've earned something for the trouble.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

The party can return to the rest of this quest's events once they have reported in to the Veiled Chain. Since this quest is repeatable, they can return to this event later in the quest to update the Chain and get further guidance and insight if they want.

Point of No Return

This event is only available up to the @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.GvEj76wdl5vdKVWj] event. Once it triggers, and the party is transferred to the Spellbreaker Tower they won't be able to report in.
Coming Clean.soverview: If the party visits the Veiled Chain to report on some recent events, they can alert them to the potential criminal actions of the Tayan Ambassador.
Coming Clean.sexposition:
You guided through dimly lit stone hallways until you reach a well-appointed chamber filled with desks and chairs, and shelves of ledgers and scrolls. A handful of staff work at their stations, writing reports, reviewing files, or speaking in low voices.

You are ushered into a side room with a table and chairs where you are asked to wait until a Veiled Chain agent can speak with you.
Coming Clean.ssummary: We reported to the Veiled Chain, and told them about recent events regarding the Tayan Ambassador. We could return to them later with further updates as we feel is warranted.

Three Point Lift.name: Three Point Lift
Three Point Lift.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This combat event sees the party breaking into a warehouse controlled by the Cascillian Republic. Once inside, the party must steal a technological device for Katerin Bastilla. The party can:

  • Infiltrate the warehouse silently, avoiding guards and confrontation.

  • Assault the warehouse, fighting their way in and out of the building.

Useful But Optional

The Cascillian autotool device will be useful later in the quest, but is not vital, and a party that fails to or chooses not to acquire this item can still continue the story. However, the prison escape where it would be useful will undoubtedly be harder without it.

Breaking the Law

At present, there are no repercussions for being identified, or fighting the guards. This may change in the future with additional events or content related to this quest, but does not exist presently. If the party leaves behind bodies, witnesses, or evidence this can be used against them at gamemaster discretion.

Scene Under Development

The scene used for this event lacks walls, doors and lighting due to a technical limitation on how the scenes are configured. These limitations will be resolved in a future update.

The event begins the party a short distance away from the warehouse in a position where the guards are unlikely to notice or suspect them. This gives the party a chance to decide on their approach, watch the guards, and set up for success.

Approaching the Warehouse

The Cascillian Marines patrolling the warehouse are members of a foreign nation, and trained soldiers. They are disciplined, watchful of outsiders, and know who should and should not be on the premises. This makes deceiving them or talking past them a fruitless endeavor.

However, if observed for a while it is possible to spot gaps in their patrols.

Military Presence

There are 7 @UUID[Actor.TYjkxAwVLHm6dD30]s patrolling the warehouse. They are commanded by 1 @UUID[Actor.3BhvYUprLcgIiOZ8] located in the warehouse office. They also have 3 Trained @UUID[Actor.aEg0dqDAyOEXxyTv]s in the water that know to alert the marines if they detect intruders.

Casing the Joint

Characters can watch the guard patrols with a successful [[/skill perception 18]] check. Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] have advantage on these checks.

  • Result of 23+ notes that the waters around the dock are also patrolled by three large sea creatures.

Entering the Warehouse

Characters that successfully watched the patrols have advantage on this skill check and any stealth checks made to avoid unalerted marines and anydrath. However, this advantage is lost if the guards become suspicious or are alerted to intruder presence.

Avoiding the Guards

At the start of this event the marines guarding this warehouse are calm, not on alert, and not suspicious of their surroundings. This gives the party the best chance to sneak in if they want to, but they need to take care, because any mistakes or signs of intrusion will put the marines on guard.

Sneaking Around

The marines are alert and watchful on their patrols inside building. Though they are all armed, none of them expect trouble, and are not initially suspicious. As a result, the marines can be avoided with a successful [[/skill stealth 10]] skill check.

If the marines notice any evidence of entry or disturbance they will be put on alert, informing their allies of the issue. At this point, the difficulty to evade them via stealth requires a [[/skill stealth 12]] and they will investigate any oddities in teams of two rather than going alone.

Anydrath Patrols

For parties that approach from the water, the Anydrath patrolling around the docks come to investigate anything they see in the water, coming within 15 feet to get a good look before rushing back to the docks to alert the marines. These Anydrath are trained by the Cascillian military, and can't be easily manipulated without using magic.

Fighting the Guards

While it's not advised that a party fight the guards patrolling the warehouse, they can. Defeating the guards lets the party claim the item with impunity, but may leave witnesses, or dead bodies that the city authorities will have to follow up on.

Combat Tactics

If combat breaks out in the or around the warehouse, and alarm is raised, the marines will quickly form up and work together to coordinate their efforts. They also call for their Anydrath companions to join the fight, likely outnumbering and overwhelming the party quickly.

Collectively the marines fight ferociously but will attempt to retreat if more than half their number are defeated, and individually Marines will attempt to flee combat when reduced to half their maximum hit points. If forced to flee, they will favor diving into the water and swimming away over running.

Marines that do flee via water can do so quickly with the help of their Anydraths if nearby.

Finding the Device

Once the party has gotten inside the warehouse, they will need to find the item that Katerin sent them to find. The placement of the @UUID[Item.xHOJWc40rhyvp7Cu]{Cascillian Autotool} in the warehouse isn't fixed, and should be handled in a way that befits the party's approach.

Finding the Desired Item

To make sure that finding the object is not overly difficult or too abstract to accomplish, there are several ways to find the item in question. Any of these methods work, and once the device is found, the party can flee.

  • Searching the Officer: If the party has infiltrated the warehouse and managed to approach the Marine Officer that is patrolling the interior of the warehouse, it could be taken from them with a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 14]] skill check.

  • Searching the Warehouse: In the party has infiltrated the warehouse unseen and wants to search the warehouse while hidden, they need to make a successful [[/skill perception 14]] check which takes a few minutes. During this search the guards will continue patrolling, risking discovery.

  • Tossing the Warehouse: If the party managed to drive off the marines, forcing their retreat, they can search the warehouse which takes about ten minutes and will yield the item in question without needing a roll.

  • Searching Bodies: If the party decided to fight their way in and defeated the marines, they should be able to find the item on the body of the Marine Officer once they are defeated.

Other Items of Interest

Searching the warehouse, or downed Cascillian Marines yields a working @UUID[Item.rq67rQSRftO407Wd]{Cascillian Rebreather}, and several @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepTrident000]{Cascillian Tridents}. The rest of the warehouse holds materials, goods, and items of use to the local Cascillians, but nothing particularly noteworthy to the party.

Ragen Attunement: To the Point

A party that foregoes stealth and takes the brazen (likely violent) route to acquiring the autotool advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 diplomaticImpunitySwordspointUsedViolence]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Nothing to Point At

A party that manages to acquire the Cascillian device without being noticed by the guards advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 diplomaticImpunitySwordspointAvoidedNotice]] at the conclusion of the event.

Aura Attunement: Avoiding the Point

A party that chooses not to engage with the warehouse and decides to ignore this event (thus failing to acquire the autotool) advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 diplomaticImpunitySwordspointSkippedWarehouse]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has completed their robbery of the warehouse they can go tackle the other job given to them by Katerin Bastilla, or if they've done all the tasks, head to the Spellbreaker Tower to drop the items off as part of @UUID[JournalEntry.7OAi8miYaunaLqgL.JournalEntryPage.1lXTVRoSZAapaYZW].
Three Point Lift.soverview: The party is tasked with breaking into a Cascillian Republic controlled warehouse where specialized materials are being kept. Katerin wants us to steal something called an "autotool" and ideally without any unnecessary bloodshed or attention.
Three Point Lift.sexposition:
The dockside opens in clean lines of white stone brick, the creak of rigging and the slap of waves against pilings echoing off the sides of nearby buildings. Ahead, an unassuming warehouse stands, built of the same timber and stone as all the other structures around it.

The only thing that makes this structure stand out are the uniformed soldiers patrol the perimeter in a measured cadence. They patrol in fixed intervals, their keen eyes sweeping the quay with practiced attention.

On the water's side of the building a small loading dock sits open, leading directly into the warehouse. A small boat bobs there, lines neatly hitched, deck in the process of being unloaded, but presently left unattended.
Three Point Lift.ssummary: We broke into and robbed the Cascillian held warehouse at Tridents Point with the goal of stealing a strange Cascillian device. The location was protected by highly trained Cascillian Marines and their war beasts.

To the Redfiend.name: To the Redfiend
To the Redfiend.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event has the party delivering Toron to Ambassador Tezran after a successful escape from the Spellbreaker Tower. They will also:

  • Learn Toron's ultimate fate.

  • Receive a reward for their work.

On the patio, at the garden’s edge, Ambassador Tezran stands with hands clasped behind his back, posture straight and still as the marble columns flanking him. Rakavi crouches nearby, restless claws brushing the gravel, leaving slow furrows as it watches you approach.

Tezran turns at the sound of your steps. His expression holds neither warmth nor surprise, but finality.

The Empire’s lost son returned to our keeping. Very good.

Toron sneers but says nothing. The ambassador gestures sharply, and two soldiers in Tayan crimson sweep out of the building to lay claim to Toron.

The soldiers seize him, shackling his arms tighter as he curses his former commander in the clipped tongue of Imperial. A fist to the gut silences him before the soldier drive him forward, past the doors of the embassy.

What will happen to Toron?

The Empire does not leave liabilities unattended, and I do not suffer failure gracefully. He will be dealt with permanently.

Is it necessary to kill him?

Every act of loyalty carries blood somewhere on it. Whether that means killing, or dying, or both.

Redfiend’s Favor

Your task is complete, the Empire is satisfied. You’ve carried out a mission worthy of commendation, though none shall ever know it.

As established prior, Katerin will see that your names are cleared of the unflattering accusations now cluttering the Hallows’ ledgers. I would remain unseen for a few days while she sees to the process, unless you want to be arrested again.

He reaches to the side table, taking a small, leather pouch and holding it out.

Your recompense for services rendered, and a token of gratitude for your discretion. You are to consider your obligations to this embassy concluded.

Rakavi’s talons click once against the stone as if punctuating the words.

Within the pouch is [[/award 1000gp]].

The Ambassador has nothing more to say at this point, and the party is encouraged to leave.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished receiving their reward, they are free to go on their way, and seek adventure elsewhere in Ordain.
To the Redfiend.soverview: The party receives payment for their work and various crimes. Depending on their choices, they may receive rewards from either Redfiend, Katerin, or the Veiled Chain.
To the Redfiend.sexposition:
The streets outside the Tayan Embassy seem quieter than usual, their usual bustle subdued. Guards at the gate stiffen as they see you coming, and there are orders barked inward as you approach. The attendant who once welcomed you here nods sharply and opens the gates just as you reach them.

Ambassador Tezran is expecting you. Please, this way.

The halls inside are as immaculate as ever, polished stone, red and black banners giving way to the verdant, secluded garden beyond.
To the Redfiend.ssummary: We turned over Toron to Ambassador Tezran, and were rewarded for our part in the Redfiend's operation. The fate of Toron is almost certainly death, though we did not witness it ourselves.

Personal Privateers.name: Personal Privateers
Personal Privateers.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event has the party delivering Toron to Katerin Bastill after a successful escape from the Spellbreaker Tower. They will also:

  • Learn what Katerin will do with Toron.

  • Get advice about dealing with the ambassador after betraying him.

  • Receive a reward for their work with Katerin.

After a short while you hear the thump of heavy footsteps leading up to the heavy doors swinging open. In strides Katerin, a grin broad enough to flash in the firelight aimed your way.

Well, my favorite band of agents finally returns, and with the man of the hour, no less!

She scoops up a glass and bottle, filling one from the other as her keen eyes settle on Toron.

You look half-dead, friend. Let’s fix that.

She sets the bottle down and slaps her hand on the table twice sharply, prompting two servants step through the doors at once.

See to this man properly: bath, clothes, meal, and a real bed, with company if he wants it. He’s done suffering the hospitality of the Ordinate and the Empire, let's show him how Bastilla does things.

Toron hesitates for just a second, sizing up the servants and Katerin before allowing himself to be lead from the chamber. Katerin watches until he’s gone, then turns back to you, her voice dropping to a more personal tone.

You did good work. I imagine Tezran’s starting to realize what's happened by now. In a few days’ time your ‘criminal records’ will quietly vanish from the Hallows’ registry.

Paperwork’s a delicate art, and I’ve paid for the best artists.

Until then, stay here at the estate. The staff don't talk and my kitchens never close. You’ve earned a damned rest.

What should we do about Ambassador Tezran?

Don’t lose sleep over it, but definitely watch your back going forward. He went to all this trouble to get Toron out of the Spellbreaker for failing a mission, he might do the same or more to get his revenge on you for this.

Katerin's Payment

Katerin sits, the chair creaking under her bulk.

As for your the coin of the matter: You’ve earned a reward, and I always pay my debts.

Then she gestures lazily toward a bronze coffer sitting on a nearby table, then begins counting off with her fingers.

You can take two thousand gold in the coffer and be on your way, or a thousand and a satchel of healing potions, half a dozen, all high quality. Or… I can pull a few strings and get you a magical trinket or two instead, something properly useful, or interesting, or both.

The kind of thing House Bastilla doesn’t sell to just anyone.

Katerin shrugs, leaning back once more, the decision clearly unimportant to her.

I don’t care which you pick, so go with what suits you best.

The party can take:

  • [[/award 2000gp]]

  • [[/award 1000gp]] and 6 x @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgGreaterPotion]{Potion of Healing (Greater)}

  • Up to two Uncommon magic items of the party's choice, subject to GM approval.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished receiving their reward, they are free to go on their way, and seek adventure elsewhere in Ordain. If they choose to remain in Katerin's estate they can stay up to three days as guests before being expected to leave.
Personal Privateers.soverview: The party receives payment for their work and various crimes. Depending on their choices, they may receive rewards from either Redfiend, Katerin, or the Veiled Chain.
Personal Privateers.sexposition:
The sprawling Bastilla estate stands ahead, the guards recognize your approach and unbar the way at once, wordlessly ushering you up the winding path to the front doors.

At the doors a well-dressed attendant greets you with a low bow and gestures for you to follow.

Madame Bastilla has been expecting you. This way, if you please.

Inside, you move through the halls at a brisk pace, your path terminating at a pair of heavy doors that swing open into a broad parlor of mahogany and brass. Here a fire burns low in the stone hearth and a nautical chronometer ticks steadily on a nearby mantelpiece in concert with the snaps and hisses of the fireplace.

In the center of the room a table sits laden with food and drink. You are ushered inside and prompted to help yourself.
Personal Privateers.ssummary: We turned over Toron to Katerin Bastilla, who has assured us that he'll vanish from sight and given chance to pay back House Bastilla for its efforts in freeing him and sparing his life. We were also told to avoid the Tayans from now on, as we've almost certainly made enemies of them. Nonetheless, we were rewarded for our part in these criminal enterprises.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

This area walkthrough provides a guide of the "Pit Trap", a popular club located within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c] district of Ordain, which is encountered during the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessSearch]] event of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq]{Unfinished Business} side quest.

In the below gazetteer entry for the Smokerie district, this location is described in the "Pit Trap" location.

Gazetteer Entry

@embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The following gameplay features apply to the Pit Trap area unless specifically stated otherwise in a specific room description.

Sound

The area around the club is quiet, but the sound of the crowds and music within leak out, and are audible as you approach. Within the club however, the noise levels rise sharply, and between the people talking and cheering, and the energetic performance of the band, the club is intensely loud.

As a consequence, hearing in this environment is more challenging. Staff and clubgoers alike talk loudly to each other, and it's only between songs that the din quiets down at all.

  • Characters in this area have @Advantage[2] to any [[/skill stealth]] skill check to avoid being heard.

  • The verbal components of spells can be enunciated quietly enough such that they do not attract attention.

Illumination

Outside the Pit Trap, the alleys and streets are lit by lanterns at night, leaving the areas brightly lit in most cases.

The mezzanine areas are bathed in a pale but bright pink light from wall-mounted sconces. The lower pit area, which includes the bar, stage, and dance floor are shrouded in dim pink link that borders on darkness.

  • Characters in the lower dance floor area have @Advantage[2] to any [[/skill stealth]] skill check to avoid being seen.

Terrain

The Pit Trap's terrain is normal in all areas.

  • The upper mezzanines are metal grating which allows tiny objects and liquid to pass through them if dropped or poured.

  • The pit areas are a mixture of stone and dark wood flooring.

Elevation

The Pit Trap is a multi-level structure and and provides multiple levels of elevation within its area.

  • The ground floor of the pit trap begins at elevation 0 and contains the outside areas, entry area, and mezzanine spaces.

  • The pit itself is -20 feet down, and accessed by metal stairwells. Guardrails on the mezzanine areas help prevent accidental falls.

  • The dancer cages are suspended at -10ft from ground level, on long chains that descend from the rafters above.

  • Above the mezzanine are the iron rafters, these are 30 feet up from the ground floor, and what the various dancer cages are suspended from. There is no convenient access to these rafters and the roof.

Inhabitants

Though they aren't hostile to begin with, the club is protected by a team of 8 @UUID[Actor.jgBUHwTKHfdPasei]{Pit Trap Bouncers} that are on-hand to resolve any issues as they arise.

  • If forced to deal with unruly patrons, the bouncer's go-to correction is to escort the offender outside the club, and not let them back in.

  • The bouncer team attempts to break up fights if they occur, but is not willing to risk their lives in combat. They withdraw from any combat more dangerous than a drunken brawl breaks out.

The club is also filled with a large number of @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani} that serve as the location's dancers, performers, bartenders, and the clubgoers visiting the location. These humanoids aren't hostile, and flee from combat if anything more than a barehanded brawl breaks out.

Front Alley.name: Front Alley
Front Alley.text:
The wider alley you arrived by gives way to smaller passages between buildings, each one choked with discarded barrels. You can see people in the shade and shadow of these alleys, all of them appearing to be club patrons taking a moment to get some fresh air before heading back into the building.

No Easy Way In

While the alleys run the perimeter of the Pit Trap's building, there are no alternate entrances for the party to find here. They must go through the front door to get in.

Gaining Access

If the characters want to explore the interior of The Pit Trap, they'll have to gain privaleged access — by any means necessary. Sneaking in to the facility is nigh impossible, so the front door is the party's only option.

What's the Password?

The party's first order of business is gaining access to the exclusive nightclub by properly entreating with the doorman, who is not easily swayed.

Marth Holbrook (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Kiska, he/him) is a dismissive and easily-offended fellow who takes his job very seriously, and he has the muscular physique to prove it. Marth will only permit club members and their guests to proceed past the front door, and requires the establishment's weekly password to enter.

  • The password this week is: "Auntie says smoke 'em if you got 'em."

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 18]], [[/skill intimidation 22]], or [[/skill persuasion 18]] check is able to convince Marth to let the party enter without too much hassle.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] and [[/knowledge intrigue]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Alternately, Marth is willing to accept a sizable bribe of 100 gp in exchange for the party's access, but they must also succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 13]] or [[/skill deception 13]] check to seal the deal. Agraband has an extra 20 gp to spare for the cause, but is otherwise cashed out for now.

Alternate Methods

If the characters fail to gain entrance to The Pit Trap via one of the methods mentioned above, they can choose instead to eavesdrop on other club patrons in an attempt to learn the coveted password.

The first character to succeed on both a [[/skill stealth 18]] check and a [[/skill perception 15]] check while hiding at least 20 feet away from the entrance is able to discern the password as another patron speaks it aloud to Marth.

  • In the event of a failure, the party can repeat this check once every 20 minutes. During this time, other patrons come and go, showing varying amounts of comical disdain for the characters if nearby.

  • A character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectThou]{Detect Thoughts} spell on Marth or one of the other patrons is able to learn the password after probing deeper into the target's mind.

Iron Mezzanine.name: Iron Mezzanine
Iron Mezzanine.text:
As you move past the entrance doors the full force of the Pit Trap is sprung on you at once. The confined space of the entrance is replaced by the sprawl of a warehouse, the clatter of heavy grating underfoot, the rattle and creak of metal cages swinging from great iron rafters, and the roar of a crowd enraptured by a live band below.

It takes you a moment to acclimate to the sudden change, as your senses attune to the darkness of the Pit below, barely lit by the unsteady light of dozens of pink lamps affixed to the walls, not a one of them strong enough to do anything but faintly illuminate the edges of the crowds that gather in the center.

Down the stairs you can see yet more patrons crowding around a bar, while across the space you can see an entire mezzanine dedicated to private seating, and the private parties with enough clout to have access to them.

Entrance.name: Entrance
Entrance.text:
Just past the double doors you can feel and hear the thrum of the Pit Trap grow louder, the intensity of it now just a pair of doors away. In this space the club staff relieve people of coats and cloaks, tucking them away in a coat room lined with racks and shelves. On the other side of the room a door leads to a cramped office where club staff talk loudly amongst themselves.

Periodically the main doors open as people come and go, each time they do the noise and chaos of the club spills out in ringing bursts.

Posted Rules

Per a large painted sign by the doors, these things will get you thrown out of the Pit Trap for the night:

  • Fighting, whether you start it or finish it.

  • Harassing the staff, band or patrons.

  • Casting spells or using magic on the unwilling.

  • Hanging from the mezzanines or trying to get into the dancer cages.

A further warning at the bottom states:

Repeat offenders will be banned.

Ignorance is not an excuse.

Private Mezzanine.name: Private Mezzanine
Private Mezzanine.text:
The iron stairs leading upward are barred by velvet ropes and watched by hawk-eyed bouncers. Only the worthy are allowed to the upper level, and they alone are arbiters of that worthiness.

Beyond them is the private mezzanine, and like the entry mezzanine opposite it, this space is comprised of metal grating on iron girders overlooking the Pit Trap's lowest point. Here, ornate wooden benches with plush cushions and decorated tables laden with food and drink rest on rich crimson carpets, each one separated from the next by standing partition walls made of paper and wood.

Important People Only

Access to this private mezzanine is at the discretion of the club staff alone, and a pair of @UUID[Actor.jgBUHwTKHfdPasei]{Pit Trap Bouncers} make accessing this area difficult unless you're on their lists.

A successful [[/skill persuasion 18]] or [[/skill deception 18]] check can allow a character to talk their way in. alternatively, a bribe of 50 gp will also get a character and their companions access to the upper level.

Forced Exit

Characters that are caught on the private mezzanine causing trouble, disturbing other patrons, or there without permission from the bouncers will be physically removed from the club and not let back in.

Bottle Service

In the event that a fight breaks out, all of the tables in the private mezzanine feature [[/roll 1d4+1]] bottles of spirits and wine can be utilized as improvised weapons.

Characters can make use of these improvised bludgeons with an action, and the intended target must make a successful [[/save dex 14]] saving throw. On failure, the target is struck by the bottle, dealing [[/damage 1d10 bludgeoning]] damage and shattering the bottle.

Private Booth Service

There is one private booth available in the private mezzanine that characters can occupy once they are past the bouncers. From this booth they can order drinks from the @UUID[JournalEntry.YRCZmeogHpxWLR91.JournalEntryPage.gvpTWsrFpMQ8NquE]{Bar}.

Additionally, they can order a bottle of spirits for the table for 100 gp, or a bottle of wine for 200 gp.

Stage.name: Stage
Stage.text:
A broad wooden dais rises a step above the floor, its boards dark as the the rest of the wood here, stained black polish countless spilled cups have tipped. A broad embroidered rug swallows most of the platform, the intricate patterns of gold and black weaving through the rich red cloth. Great pillows serve as seats for band members who attend a collection of instruments.

At the edge of the stage bodies press close; moving in time with the band's music, the roar of their collective voices rising and falling as the performance does. The air here is thick with the smell of sweat, alcohol, and smoke, and the energy is intoxicating.

Band Members Only

Access to the stage is not physically restricted, but any characters attempting to take the stage will find themselves being physically removed by a pair of nearby @UUID[Actor.jgBUHwTKHfdPasei]{Pit Trap Bouncers} who are keeping an eye on the stage.

Special Guest Appearance

Characters that approach the stage while openly carrying musical instruments might be invited to the stage to perform. If the characters accept the invite, they need to make a successful [[/skill performance 16]] check to impress the band and crowd.

If successful, they are given a random drink from @UUID[JournalEntry.YRCZmeogHpxWLR91.JournalEntryPage.gvpTWsrFpMQ8NquE]{the bar}. On failure, they are booed off the stage, being physically removed if they refuse to leave on their own.

Dance Floor.name: Dance Floor
Dance Floor.text:
The Pit Trap's central space is dim, the people here little more than silhouettes outlined by the glow of pink lamps on the walls, dancing through a thin haze of smoke. With the crush of thirsty patrons at the bar on one side and the throng of dancers crowding the stage on the other, the central space is dotted with dancers and mingling guests that have yet to be consumed by either group.

Dance the Night Away

Characters that choose to dance with the crowd must make a successful [[/skill performance 14]] check or [[/check dex 14]] check to avoid bumping into anyone or getting jostled by fellow dancers.

Failing by 5 or more results in the characters suffering [[/damage 1 bludgeoning]] damage from a wayward elbow. Due to the darkness of the venue, they can't tell where it came from.

Bar.name: Bar
Bar.text:
The long counter of the bark is a rough, dark wood burnished smooth by countless hands and drinks traveling over it. Rings of old spills stain the wood, and leave it sticky in places despite frequent wipe-downs.

A four-headed metal tap juts out of the bar's center where drinks are drawn and served as rapidly as orders come in.

Behind the counter the Pit Trap's bartenders move to a chaotic tempo set by the bodies that crowd the wood and call out orders over each other. Each demand is met by a flurry of motion and practiced precision as bottles come off shelves, drinkware is laid out, and libations are mixed.

Ordering Drinks

A chalk board listed with drinks and their prices hangs over the bar, each one overpriced by a huge margin, but still selling at a rapid pace. Prices are paid up front, each handful of bright coin glittering against dark wood swiftly replaced by a drink of unidentifiable parts and undeniable strength.

High Quality Spirits

The Pit Trap's drinks are all strong and delicious, each one expertly mixed for the patron by a bartender that tries to look like they don't care about your order. A successful [[/skill insight 14]] check notices that they take their job seriously, despite appearances.

Drink Responsibly

The Pit Trap serves strong drinks, characters can consume a number of drinks equal to their Constitution modifier without ill effect. Drinking more than that requires a successful [[/save con 14]] saving throw to avoid the &reference[poisoned] condition for the next hour.

Bottle Service

In the event that a fight breaks out, there are several drinks and bottles of alcohol on the bar which can be used as improvised weapons. Characters can take an action to use either of these improvised moves as they are within reach of the bar and there's at least one use available:

  • Throw Drink (2d4 uses). The character grabs a random drink from the bar and splashes it in a target's face. The intended target must make a successful [[/save dex 14]] or suffer the &reference[blinded] condition until the end of their next turn.

  • Swing Bottle (1d4+1 uses). The character grabs a bottle and swings it at a foe. The intended target must make a successful [[/save dex 14]] saving throw. On failure, the target is struck by the bottle, dealing [[/damage 1d10 bludgeoning]] damage and shattering the bottle.

House Offerings

The following drinks are available to order:

Snake Bite, 5 gp

A bright green, and threaded with gold, the taste is crisp, a mix of lime and sour apple with a peppery finish that numbs the throat and lips.

Rusty Snare, 5 gp

A coppery drink with orange and green flecks swirling through it. It's powerfully sweet at first, but has a metallic snap that makes your teeth hurt.

Shot of Venom, 10 gp

A single shot of pearlescent black liquid that tastes like violets and roses, with a sweet blackberry tail.

Snapped Ankle, 10 gp

A cloudy bone-white drinks with a thin red swirl of syrup at its center that tastes like sweetened milk and raspberry that hides the high proof alcohol within.

Back Alley.name: Back Alley
Back Alley.text:
The broad back alley behind the pit trap goes on some distance, the length of it filled with crates, discarded wood pallets, barrels, and packing material. Numerous doors and smaller alleys connect to this space, leading to other businesses, stores, workshops, and more. While some doors are marked with signs, many are not.

Tracking Zira

By the time the party arrives in this space Zira will have made a clean escape. No rolls should be given to attempt to find her, as her escape is intended to be successful no matter what the party does.

If the party wants to spend time looking for her narrate the following:

After a quick search you find no evidence of Zira's passage through this area. The numerous old footprints and well worn paths weaving through crates and garbage in the alley yield no insights, and not even a single creature is present to be pressed for information.

It seems that Zira managed to a clean escape for now.

Side Office.name: Side Office
Side Office.text:
A threadbare couch hugs one wall here, opposite a scarred wooden table and two mismatched chairs crammed into a corner. On the wall, a broad board of dark wood bristles with notes and announcements pinned under iron tacks. A few bottles of alcohol and accompanying glasses sit on the table, each one half full in its own way, and forgotten for the moment.

If a character decides to examine the board and the notes here, read the following:

The board is covered in all manner of notes, plans, messages, and more. The week's shift rosters scribbled in uneven script sits beside a list of band names and the dates they are booked to perform, which sits overtop half a dozen notes about people who should or should not be let in to the club.

Coat Room.name: Coat Room
Coat Room.text:
This cramped space is lined from floor to ceiling with shelves and iron rails burdened by a confusion of cloaks, capes, coats, and traveling bags. A dozen different perfumes cling to the air in thin threads, mingled with the tang of leather, and dried sweat.

Hidden Treasure

A character than spends 5 minutes searching the shelves and makes a successful [[/skill perception 18]] check will find the @UUID[Item.EbOfStUhDnCtBL2z].

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the "Kalion Stadium Underworks" depicts a three-part subterranean sprawl that serves as the scenery for the @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq]{Unfinished Business} quest event known as [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessUnderworks]].

  • This map depicts three distinct sections of the area: the easternmost Hall of Contest, the central Hall of Challenges, and the westernmost Temple of Ku'arta.

  • There is a single method of entry: via the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.C7cZROcerETNtVqJ]{Entrance Hall} located in the Hall of Contest, at the northeastern edge of the map.

  • Additional details about the various features of this area are located in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.swLcVvn5Yvu03ZXA]{Gameplay Details} section of this walkthrough.

In the gazetteer entry for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge} district featured below, this location is described in the "Grand Kalion Stadium" location.

Early Access Under Construction

The Kalion Stadium Underworks area map is a work-in-progress, and some chambers and features have yet to be fully implemented (most notably the central "Hall of Challenges" section).

Gazetteer Entry

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The Kalion Stadium Underworks are a long-abandoned and oft-forgotten network of tunnels and chambers beneath @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Grand Kalion Stadium} that once served as a series of training facilities for the arena's athletes and gladiators. Now, the bygone area serves as the clandestine headquarters of the warlock @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero} and her unsuspecting cult of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta} acolytes known as the Undaunted. Most notably, the Kalion Stadium Underworks host the harrowing conclusion of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq]{Unfinished Business} side quest.

Objectives

The Kalion Stadium Underworks serve as the setting for the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessUnderworks]] event of Unfinished Business, during which the party will attempt to confront the villain @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero} and her allies. If they wish to bring the evil warlock to justice and reunite @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} with his estranged nephew @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I]{Jorey}, the characters must:

  • Navigate the Hall of Contest while avoiding or confronting the @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted Adepts} and @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]{Undaunted Trainees} who call the place home.

  • Survive the perplexing Hall of Challenges and its curious puzzles and hazards.

  • Infiltrate the Temple of Ku'arta just in time to witness a profane ritual conducted by Zira Hestidero and her Undaunted acolytes.

Avoiding Detection

If the party wishes to navigate the Kalion Stadium Underworks without being detected by the Undaunted Adepts and Undaunted Trainees that inhabit the area, they'll need to maintain stealth from chamber to chamber.

Each time the characters enter a new chamber or corridor, they'll each need to make a [[/skill stealth 15]] check, avoiding detection on a success.

Illumination

Braziers and sconces located throughout the Kalion Stadium Underworks interior burn with magical firelight, and are tended to by the various Undaunted acolytes when necessary. The braziers shed bright light in a 30 foot radius and dim light for another 30 feet, while the smaller sconces shed bright light in a 15 foot radius and dim light for another 15 feet.

Terrain

The flagstone floors of the Stadium Underworks are crafted from slabs of gray slate, hewn from the ancient quarries of old Ordain nearby. The ground here should be treated as normal terrain unless otherwise noted. The interior walls of the area are crafted from similar stone.

Underworks Tracks

Any character who searches the Arena Underworks interior for tracks and succeeds on a [[/skill survival 13]] check is able to locate the presence of sandaled and booted footprints along the various walkways within. These tracks are easily identified as those of the Undaunted Adepts and Trainees who dwell here.

Elevation

The ceilings located within the interior chambers and corridors of the Kalion Stadium Underworks are 20 feet high, unless otherwise stated.

Entrance Hall.name: Entrance Hall
Entrance Hall.text:
This octagonal chamber bears the first light you've seen for nearly a mile while navigating the subterranean reaches beneath Grand Kalion Stadium. Despite the archaic architecture and clandestine qualities of this shadow-haunted place, you get the distinct feeling that someone has recently been here.

This large antechamber serves as the Entrance Hall for the Kalion Stadium Underworks, and is typically only trafficked by The Undaunted who call this place home. In times long gone, there might be more inhabitants here.

Avoiding Detection

If the party wishes to navigate the Kalion Stadium Underworks without being detected by the @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted Adepts} and @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]{Undaunted Trainees} that inhabit the other chambers nearby, they'll need to maintain stealth from room to room.

Each time the characters enter a new chamber or corridor, they'll each need to make a [[/skill stealth 15]] check, avoiding detection on a success.

Exploring the Entrance Hall

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] or [[/skill survival 13]] check is able to notice the presence of sandaled footprints coming to and from the area, with the most steady flow of traffic towards the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.I7WsOSHq4UVLZgrt]{Bathhouse} to the east.

Hall of Preparation.name: Hall of Preparation
Hall of Preparation.text:
Two Undaunted warriors occupy this chamber, which appears to be stuffed full of assorted weapons, armor, and adventuring gear. Based on this motley collection of equipment, you'd wager these goods were gathered from a variety of different sources.

The two athletes appear to be caught up in their task of sorting and cataloguing the assorted gear, and exchange a few words between each other without bothering to look up.

If you ask me, we're wastin' our time with this scuffed up junk. Who needs to know how to use a blasted polearm, anyway? These two fists of mine have been good enough so far.

The older warrior chimes in with a quick rebuttal:

Sure they have — good enough to get you stuck on inventory duty here with me. If your strikes were half as fast as that mouth of yours, you'd be wearing the captain's uniform by now.

They continue to go about their business, and the steady noise of clanging metal and padded leather keeps pace.

The Hall of Preparation was historically a chamber for the arming and outfitting of gladiators before combat in the arena above (or amidst other parts of the Underworks at large). These days, it serves as a staging area for loot, plunder, and additional rewards The Undaunted bring home from their various triumphs in the city (illicit and otherwise).

Advantageous Stealth Conditions

Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to sneak here and in adjoining chambers are made with @Advantage[2], thanks to the loud noise caused by the sorting work.

Exploring the Hall of Preparation

Any character with a [[/skill perception 11 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check is able to spot a few key details throughout the room:

  • Much of the equipment here seems well used and lightly damaged by battle, as if these items were culled from various encounters with an assortment of armed warriors.

  • The two Undaunted acolytes here are sorting the items and recording associated details on a couple of small notebooks.

  • Result of 18+: The character spots the seams of a secret door behind the brazier on the western wall here, but the method of opening it is completely impossible to ascertain.

Eavesdropping

If the characters decide to linger in an attempt to hear more, they can check once every five minutes on the following table (roll [[/roll 1d4]] to determine):

  1. Half of the goods here were the property of Undaunted hopefuls before they joined the cult, while the other half have been culled from private matches with enemy teams outside of the arena.

  2. While there aren't many participants, an underground fight club has popped up in Ordain, and the Undaunted are regular participants of this illicit activity.

  3. The quality of equipment here pales in comparison to some of the goods stored in the Underworks @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.bKJRzPHSiusLwmbL]{Reliquary}.

  4. Zira says the next Solar Games match is going to be one the people of Ordain never forget. It sounds like she has a trick or two up her sleeves.

Looting the Room

If the characters want to sort through the equipment here, they can find at least one of every Simple and Martial Melee Weapon listed on the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000.JournalEntryPage.z1wx4cNO7AfqyNof]{Weapon Table}, along with most Simple Ranged Weapons.

Additionally, there are several pieces of Light and Medium Armor here, with no single item exceeding a value of 200 gp, as depicted on the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000.JournalEntryPage.adlJqek4sIyJePKO].

@Embed[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]

@Embed[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]

Undaunted Tactics

The Undaunted Adept and Undaunted Trainee will leap into action at the first sign of an intruder, attempting to raise the alarm by alerting other Undaunted in the area, namely:

  • The Undaunted Trainee who cleans the monuments in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.eyUP3WMr4YNkkvHT]{Hall of Champions}.

  • The 2 Undaunted Trainees in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.Au99JvZXO8t47N3B]{Hall of Records}.

  • The Undaunted Adept in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.vtHfRHobh0WxPBrP]{Hall of Recovery}.

If cornered or threatened by the party, the Trainee may use their @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI.Item.RFWALrXc42D6Hlxj]{Reckless Movement} feature to gain a better position on the battlefield.

Meanwhile, the Adept will make quick use of spells like @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm.Item.RHMj9pksa88teGb2]{Hold Person} and @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm.Item.V2YCYYwzRDfTjxuW]{Expeditious Retreat} to turn the tide, potentially creating an avenue for the Trainee to escape and raise the alarm.

Detecting the Secret Passage

The secret door on the western wall here can be spotted with a successful [[/skill perception 18]] check while Searching the room.

Crafted by expert Ordani stonesmiths using arcane techniques, this door can only be opened using a @UUID[Item.4RHsNmK18A9mTxHK]{Temple of Ku'arta Key} or magic like the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplKnock00000]{Knock} spell (which will alert all Undaunted enemies in the Underworks).

Hall of Champions.name: Hall of Champions
Hall of Champions.text:
A lone Undaunted trainee appears to be polishing the pedestal of a large stone statue in this massive chamber, where a half-dozen monuments have been erected in the honor of ancient Ordani gladiators — legendary personalities, by the look of their collective bearing and ornamentation. The imposing statue of some particularly formidable champion dominates the central area of the room, a lightly-armored muscular warrior whose clenched fists are shrouded in hand-sculpted arcane spectacle.

This area is currently occupied by a single @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]{Undaunted Trainee}, along with the lingering phantom of @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI]{Regus Halamattrix}, the original champion of the Arena's Solar Games. The ceiling of this massive chamber is taller than most of the Underworks at 35 feet high.

Exploring the Hall of Champions

The statues located here are monuments to various champions and all-stars that have gained legendary status throughout the history of Grand Kalion Stadium and the Solar Games. Chief among them is the statue at the center of the chamber, which depicts the late Regus Halamattrix, who was the very first champion of the Solar Games.

Any character who performs the Search action while exploring the Hall of Champions is able to locate a placard beneath each statue with a small descriptor of the person being honored. Clockwise from the northeast, they read:

  • "Clotho Drax."

  • "Hannigan Stethlas."

  • "Bronn Swifthammer."

  • "Demetra the Dauntless."

  • "Zoriax of Kalvard."

  • "Ora Feyd."

Meanwhile, the statue at the center of the chamber stands larger and prouder than the rest, depicting a brawny Ordani gladiator covered in an impossible array of scars. A shiny golden plaque on the floor before the statue reads:

Regus Halamattrix. Inaugural Champion of the Solar Games.
"Death is no excuse for defeat."

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill history 15]] check is familiar with the tale of Regus Halamattrix, and how he rose to glory in the arena by winning amidst a succession of near-death experiences.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] and [[/knowledge warfare]] have advantage on this check.

@Embed[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]

Undaunted Trainee Tactics

The Undaunted Adept and Undaunted Trainee will leap into action at the first sign of an intruder, attempting to raise the alarm by alerting other Undaunted in the area, namely:

  • The 2 Undaunted Trainees in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.Au99JvZXO8t47N3B]{Hall of Records}.

  • The Undaunted Adept in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.vtHfRHobh0WxPBrP]{Hall of Recovery}.

  • The Adept and Trainee sorting equipment in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.sCHWBFuf1lYkz5WZ]{Hall of Preparation}.

The Phantom in the Statue

The statue here is haunted by the undying spirit of @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI]{Regus Halamattrix}, the first champion of the Havoc Games, who watches over this place in grim perpetuity.

Coercing the Trainee

If the party overwhelms the Undaunted Trainee here with force, they can convince him to share some information about the facility with a successful [[/skill deception 15]], [[/skill intimidation 15]], or [[/skill persuasion 17]] check. This information includes:

  • Spirits roam the halls here, and spell doom for any would-be enemies of The Undaunted.

  • Most of the Undaunted team members are gathered for a ceremony further inside the temple, past the Hall of Challenges.

  • Zira can read minds. She probably already knows the interloping party is here.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] reveals an element of truth behind the first two rumors, and a falsehood about the third.

  • Result of 18+: The Trainee can be seen looking with anxious regularity at the statue in the center of the room. But he'd sooner risk death during an attempt to escape rather than explain himself any further.

If the party chooses to physically interact with the statue of Regus Halamattrix, read the following aloud:

The statue feels strangely cold to the touch, even for the subterranean depths of the Underworks. For a brief moment, you feel as though your hand is affixed to the monument against your will. Looking up, you notice the statue's countenance moves — as if it's come to life. With a voice the sound of a low and raspy wind, the statue speaks:

Only fools would approach this unholy memorial without fear. Tell me: who dares entreat with the observer of the Underworks?

A Conversation with Regus

If the characters summon the phantom of Regus Halamattrix by interacting with his monument, the undead champion will appear the following round. Because of his hubris and enthusiasm for tribulation, Regus is willing to have a conversation with the party, albeit laden with insults and provocation. Topics include (but are not limited) to:

  • His history as the first champion of Ordain's Solar Games, and his legacy as an unkillable gladiator.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}'s clandestine influence on the people of Ordain via the violence of the arena and its contestants.

  • The sanctity of this Underworks facility as a temple to the shard god of torment, however forgotten it may have become.

  • The party's accomplishments as warriors or athletes in their own right, including their associated victories in battle.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 18]], [[/skill deception 18]], or [[/skill deception 18]] check is able to convince Regus that the party's motives are aligned with his own — resulting in a friendly disposition from the phantom (however temporary it may be). If the characters manage to turn Regus into an ally, he'll also provide them with the following information:

  • The general layout of the Kalion Stadium Underworks, including the presence of the hidden temple at the western end of the complex.

  • Details about the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.Hm9ku5muMPilfUuG]{Chamber of Bargains}, including how to entreat with Ku'arta and what the bargain entails.

  • Helpful tips for navigating the hazardous Hall of Challenges to the west.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

  • Characters who succeeded on the History check to identify their familiarity with the legend of Regus Halamattrix have @Advantage[2] on these checks (see "Exploring the Hall of Champions" above).

  • Characters who openly wear the holy symbol of a god other than Ku'arta have @Advantage[-2] on these checks.

  • Result of 23+: Regus may be convinced to intervene during battle on the party's behalf, but won't turn against another adherent of Ku'arta without adequate reason (such as defilement of the temple or betrayal of the shard god's edicts).

  • Result of 8 or less: the character instantly angers the phantom (see "Regus Halamattrix Tactics" below).

If the party manages to befriend Regus, he'll recognize Agraband as a fellow Soulbound, and reveal that aspect of his history to the characters.

Your story?

You are humbled by the presence of greatness, for I am Regus Halamattrix, chosen of Ku'arta and supreme contestant of the Solar Games. Many have suffered the humiliation of my eminence. I suspect you shall be no different, you pitiable worm.

This place?

As the city endures its ceaseless changes, the Underworks persist, forgotten but powerful in their grand design. For decades, I trained here with the likes of Ordain's finest warriors and athletes — losers and wretches all. None could thwart the might and mercilessness of Regus Halamattrix!

Zira Hestidero and The Undaunted?

The young champion may yet prove to be a powerful implement of Ku'arta, but I presume her ambitions exceed her grasp. These acolytes of her are no the spineless dredges, however, and their humble beginnings have made them strong. Many have survived the Hall of Challenges and lived to tell the tale.

Can you help us?

Mind the gauntlet to the west; the Hall of Challenges are no trifling matter. And pay heed to the Reliquary, where a weapon of mine is kept hidden: the Pellucid Glaive, a trophy from my time in the arena. Zira shields the relic with arcane glyph. Speak the words"Tormenter, guide my hands" to avoid her chicanery.

If the party befriends Regus, take a moment whenever most appropriate to interject with the following:

Regarding Agraband?

The phantom directs his gaze at Agraband as a snide grin creeps across his spectral face.

Your friend has the mark. I, too, was graced with undying purpose. My Soulbound nature was the secret of my legacy. And I dare say this damnation was worth the price I had to pay. Regus Halamattrix bows down to no lord, even the god of torment himself.

The apparition's fists crackle with translucent arcane energy as the spectral remnants of his scars seethe with lambent intensity.

If the party ends up angering Regus Halamattrix, they'll have to fight the phantom in combat — with or without the Undaunted acolytes nearby alongside him during the fray.

@Embed[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI]

Regus Halamattrix Tactics

The phantom champion is a cruel adversary who enjoys tormenting his enemies with a steady flow of taunts and denigration.

During the first round of combat, Regus will typically attempt to use his @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI.Item.jCqIBuYcpnhRQ3fr]{Horrific Visage} attack against as many enemies as possible, followed by melee combat the next round using his @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI.Item.UZjLU9UqSUzWXFoz]{Arcane Strike} and @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI.Item.sJTTZC3HWmYnUv8U]{Draining Strike}.

If Regus falls below half his HP, he'll use @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI.Item.HYrNe974uE1UMamK]{Life Drain} against an adjacent enemy or @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI.Item.chdJGVQNsjVpDGwa]{Vanish} if necessary, reappearing sooner or later in a more advantageous position on the map.

Any characters who wield especially powerful weapons or arcane implements against Regus will be targeted by his @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI.Item.A8P1ZWaltnWCbpWj]{Ghostly Telekinesis}, with Regus attempting to snatch the weapons from out of the characters' very hands.

Hall of Recovery.name: Hall of Recovery
Hall of Recovery.text:
The twin rectangular chambers here appear to be furnished for recuperation. To the south, a set of five beds is lit by calm lantern light. To the north, desks and cabinets line the dungeon walls and fountain edges, covered in a wide array of apothecary tools and arcane materials.

An Undaunted Adept lurks here among this makeshift study, replenishing the contents of a healer's kit with a stock of herbs, ointments, and fresh bandages.

The two chambers collectively known as the Hall of Recovery include a barracks to the south and an apothecary's study to the north. While some of The Undaunted use the beds here as permanent lodging, most of them are not present at this time. A lone @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted Adept} works here, accompanied by a furtive @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V]{Water Sprite} — hidden in a jar on the cabinet.

@Embed[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]

Undaunted Tactics

The Undaunted Adept is an experienced member of Zira's team, and can't be reasoned with. They'll leap into action at the first sign of an intruder, initially breaking the jar on the cabinet to release the Water Sprite before attempting to raise the alarm by alerting other Undaunted in the area, namely:

  • The Undaunted Trainee who cleans the monuments in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.eyUP3WMr4YNkkvHT]{Hall of Champions}.

  • The 2 Undaunted Trainees in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.Au99JvZXO8t47N3B]{Hall of Records}.

  • The Adept and Trainee in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.sCHWBFuf1lYkz5WZ]{Hall of Preparation}.

If cornered or threatened by the party, the Adept will make quick use of spells like @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm.Item.RHMj9pksa88teGb2]{Hold Person} and @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm.Item.V2YCYYwzRDfTjxuW]{Expeditious Retreat} to turn the tide, potentially creating an avenue for escape to raise the alarm.

When the Undaunted Adept smashes the jar to release the elemental, read the following aloud:

The Undaunted warrior reaches up to a jar on the shelf, which appears to hold some clear liquid within. He drops the receptacle to the ground and glass cascades across the Underworks floor along with the aqueous contents. However, this sheet of water on the stone floor coalesces before your very eyes into a single, living entity — a creature that aims to attack you, if its liquid "body language" is a trustworthy indicator.

@Embed[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V]{Water Sprite}

Exploring the Apothecary's Study

Any character that takes 5 minutes to Search the apothecary's study to the north is able to locate the following:

  • The fresh @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagHealersKit0]{Healer's Kit} the Adept was in the process of creating.

  • A vial of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAntitoxin00]{Antitoxin}.

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPotionofHea]{Potion of Healing}.

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the study also reveals:

  • A vial of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSerpentVenom0]{Serpent Venom}.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 12]] check while Searching the area is able to identify several material components for arcane spells stored in the containers here, and can loot [[/roll 1d2]] samples of any mundane material spell component for a spell on their spell list worth 15 gp or less.

If the Undaunted Adept failed to break the jar containing the @UUID[Actor.sVnMPbEj5P18Yo8V]{Water Sprite} during combat, it will be located here now. Fully intact, it will react to the party's presence if they linger her longer than 5 minutes, but cannot escape the jar without external assistance.

Exploring the Barracks

Any character that takes 5 minutes to Search the barracks to the south is able to locate the following:

  • 3 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBackpack000]{Backpacks} stuffed with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesTrav]{Ordani Traveler's Clothes}.

  • [[/roll 1d2]] doses of @UUID[Item.jF7AO6nnqIhFZ6oI]{Dustweed}.

  • [[/roll 1d2]] @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinkets}.

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the barracks also reveals:

  • A bottle of @UUID[Item.jnKYsmCYNNP21aYF]{Seawall Brandy}.

Hall of Records.name: Hall of Records
Hall of Records.text:
The three circular chambers here are lined floor-to-ceiling with bookshelves packed full of tomes, scrolls, and assorted bric-a-brac. The light of two ornate crystal chandeliers casts its glow upon this aged library, where two Undaunted trainees are set about the business of sorting through a large stack of books — setting some on the shelf and some others to the side.

The youngest of them speaks.

I don't know why we're wasting our time with these moth-eaten textbooks. You know we're not going to find anything.

The other trainee retorts with an air of indignation.
