Look, you know just as well as I do, if we overlook some scrap of paper with a funny sigil or a mention of the Shear on it, she'll tear our fuckin' heads off and drink wine out of 'em during the next match. Just keep lookin' … at least we're not on our knees in the Sanctum right now.

The younger athlete hastily replies.

You got that right.

These chambers have served as the Underworks library for ages, and already bore an impressive number of books and scrolls upon their shelves when Zira and her team first occupied the area. Since then, Zira's furious efforts to gather lost and eldritch lore have resulted in a recognizable backlog and overflow of new inventory.

Exploring the Hall of Records

Any character with a [[/skill perception 11 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check is able to quickly spot a few key details throughout the room:

  • Much of the literature here seems to be historical in nature, with many works on mythology of Ember and legends of the Arctus Plateau.

  • The small pile of books the trainees are stacking appears to contain several works written about Ember's moons and subterranean @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.FurLgJBcqG4ILqMO]{Pathways}.

  • Result of 18+: A tome on the lectern in the western wing is splayed open, revealing diagrams of martial arts techniques on its pages.

  • A character who spends at least 5 minutes Searching the area automatically succeeds on this check.

Eavesdropping

If the characters decide to linger in an attempt to hear more, they can check once every five minutes on the following table (roll [[/roll 1d4]] to determine):

  1. This latest batch of books was from an estate sale in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.iphMPgtJv5eQjGaR]{Scholar's Nook}, inherited from an old Nir'ae mage said to have explored the Pathways.

  2. While there aren't many participants, an underground fight club has popped up in Ordain, and the Undaunted are regular participants of this illicit activity.

  3. Zira won't let anyone in to her @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.DTsgzo5IgXJJg2YV]{Arcane Workshop}, and all sorts of rumors about regarding what she keeps in there.

  4. Zira says the next Solar Games match is going to be one the people of Ordain never forget. It sounds like she has a trick or two up her sleeves.

Looting the Room

If the characters want to sort through the bookshelves here, they can find the following:

  • Countless books, tomes, and scrolls of a mundane nature that detail a wide array of esoteric subjects.

  • 12 aged hardcover @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Books} that pertain to Ember's moons, the Pathways, various deities, and the Abyss.

Additionally, a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] check leads any character who Searches the room to discover a false book that conceals a vial of @UUID[Item.QrbcfllnppjmOSfe]{Rapture} hidden inside.

@Embed[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI count=2]

Undaunted Trainee Tactics

The Undaunted Trainees will leap into action at the first sign of an intruder, attempting to raise the alarm by alerting other Undaunted in the area, namely:

  • The Undaunted Trainee in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.eyUP3WMr4YNkkvHT]{Hall of Champions}.

  • The Undaunted Adept in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.vtHfRHobh0WxPBrP]{Hall of Recovery}.

  • The Adept and Trainee sorting equipment in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.sCHWBFuf1lYkz5WZ]{Hall of Preparation}.

If cornered, they'll use @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI.Item.zvPjS1oJgxoIs330]{Pack Tactics} to their advantage and fight until they're defeated — preferring the hand of fate to Zira's wrath.

Secret Vestibule.name: Secret Vestibule
Secret Vestibule.text:
As you emerge from the so-called Hall of Challenges, you find yourself in a shaded vestibule, decorated with a lone bench made of cold stone. A passageway to the south winds westward, dark and uninviting.

This small chamber serves as the unassuming arrival area for characters who successfully traverse the Hall of Challenges.

WIP: Under Construction

The Kalion Stadium Underworks area map is a work-in-progress, and this chamber has yet to be fully implemented.

Secret Passage.name: Secret Passage
Secret Passage.text:
A dark and narrow corridor extends into the darkness ahead, as still and silent as the grave.

This secret passage connects the temple @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.AgGSbVyJqLjTsDW9]{Armory} with the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.sCHWBFuf1lYkz5WZ]{Hall of Preparation} to the east, and is frequently used by Zira and her most experienced Undaunted allies to traverse the expanse of the Underworks while conveniently avoiding the Hall of Challenges.

Detecting the Secret Passage

The secret doors at each end of this concealed passage can be spotted with a successful [[/skill perception 18]] check while Searching the adjoining rooms.

Crafted by expert Ordani stonesmiths using arcane techniques, these doors can only be opened using a @UUID[Item.4RHsNmK18A9mTxHK]{Temple of Ku'arta Key} or magic like the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplKnock00000]{Knock} spell (which will alert all Undaunted enemies in the Underworks).

Sealed Entrance.name: Sealed Entrance
Sealed Entrance.text:
Long ago, this dead end was the site of a massive entrance to the temple here from another section of the city Underworks. Now, all that remains here of the once-proud threshold is a pile of stone rubble.

This alcove was once the main entrance to the temple, but was sealed centuries ago by the authorities of Ordain in an effort to quarantine this unholy location from the rest of the city and prevent the old acolytes of Ku'arta from rising to prominence.

Examining the Sealed Entrance

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check while searching the area is able to determine that this was once the main entrance to the temple, but it must have been sealed long ago by denizens of Ordain — the collapse is manmade, rather than the result of an earthquake or natural disaster.

  • Result of 18+: The character is able to pinpoint the age of this rubble (and the fortified stonework around it) as being from the earliest days of Ordain.

Alternately, a character who succeeds on a [[/skill nature 15]] check can determine that the collapse here was not due to natural causes.

Chamber of Bargains.name: Chamber of Bargains
Chamber of Bargains.text:
This atmospheric chamber reeks of the sickly sweet smell of some potent incense, and large runic markings on the floor pulse with intermittent arcane light. In an alcove to the north, the fragments of a shattered statue lay in ruin; to the south, a small collection of occult tomes and a ritual dagger decorate a bleak stone altar littered with half-burned candles.

This curious room is a special shrine to Ku'arta, where would-be adherents can perform a blasphemous Ritual of Bargains to receive a divine reward: a double-edged blessing, which bestows a magical impediment upon the willing recipient as well as an arcane benefit. Furthermore, Ku'arta actually speaks to those who would beseech his bargain, and this room serves as an arcane conduit for this mystical palaver.

Exploring the Chamber

A momentary Search of the room points the characters towards an altar or stone table on the southern wall, upon which rests a copy of the Manual of Pain — one of the most notable religious texts regarding the shard god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}. Also present:

  • An obsidian @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepDagger0000]{Dagger}

  • [[/roll 1d2+1]] unused @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCandle00000]{Candles}

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] check while searching the room is able to locate the following:

  • To do.

  • Result of 19+: To do.

Characters must succeed on either a [[/skill religion 15]] or [[/skill arcana 18]] check can use the obsidian dagger and other accoutrements here to initiate the Ritual of Bargains, which bestows a temporary curse on them known as the Curse of Bargains.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge gods]] or [[/attunement luxarum]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] automatically succeed on this check.

  • A character who spends at least 30 minutes reading the Manual of Pain automatically succeeds on this check.

  • A character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCommune000]{Commune} spell automatically succeeds on this check.

Characters who successfully initiate the Ritual of Bargains also have an opportunity to commune with Ku'arta himself (see below).

If a character manages to successfully initiate the Ritual of Bargains, read the following aloud:

The runes on the floor seethe with uncanny brilliance as the air swirls about you. A raspy masculine voice echoes through the chamber, emanating from nowhere, metallic and clanging with guttural malice.

Avow to me, willful seeker: who art thou to bargain with the Tormentor, and what is thine ambition?

Ku'arta's Bargain

The character must state their so-called ambition for the ritual to continue. Once they do, Ku'arta responds from his hidden sanctum on the other side of the world with one simple phrase:

Carry this blessing, and don your suffering as unholy armor, painful and resolute.

The character immediately becomes afflicted with the Curse of Bargains, which has a duration of 24 hours.

If a character responds to Ku'arta's query with an honest request to strike an arcane pact with him, the shard god will most likely oblige them. Read "A Pact with Ku'arta" below for more information about what this eventually entails. For now, the shard god will answer three questions for them, per the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCommune000]{Commune} spell.

Meanwhile, a successful [[/skill insight 13]] check offers a character all the assurances they'll need to believe this paranormal encounter was an authentic interaction with the so-called God of Torment himself.

  • Characters with [[/attunement luxarum]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Once a character has completed the Ritual of Bargains, read the following aloud:

You feel a strange sensation take hold of your body, like a flash of cold sweat and mortal panic. But somewhere behind this animal fear, you sense a distant presence, guiding your will with the ferocity of a thousand forgotten vengeances.

The Curse of Bargains is upon you.

A Pact with Ku'arta

This encounter provides characters who wish to pursue a relationship with Ku'arta as their arcane patron with an optimal opportunity to do so. However, the ultimate fulfillment of this bargain requires the character to invest at least one level in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCharClasses]{Warlock} class when they next advance in level.

Characters who make a Warlock's arcane pact with Ku'arta this way receive the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplThaumaturg]{Thaumaturgy} cantrip as a bonus to their list of known spells.

WIP: Under Construction

The Kalion Stadium Underworks area map is a work-in-progress, and this chamber has yet to be fully implemented.

Reliquary.name: Reliquary
Reliquary.text:
The sconces that illuminate this narrow chamber appear to gleam with perpetual arcane firelight, casting their warm glow on an array of glass display cases and other containers situated about the room.

This chamber serves as the temple's Reliquary, and contains a small collection of relics and antiques that are considered sacred to adherents of @UUID[Actor.0zolrBB1ci4yz4qg]{Ku'arta}.

One noteworthy relic of the original inhabitants remains: a magical crystalline glaive, which @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira} and her cohorts regard as something of a holy item given its history with previous acolytes of Ku'arta — including @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI]{Regus Halamattrix}, the first champion of Ordain's Solar Games.

Exploring the Reliquary

Any character who takes a moment to Search this room will locate the following:

  • Three urns on a stone table at the northern end of the room, which contain the ashes of @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI]{Regus Halamattrix} and two other champions of Ku'arta.

  • 6 broken relics, which can be harvested for their rare crafting components.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 18 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 16]] check while searching the area is able to notice the presence of lambent arcane marking on the chest at the center of the room.

  • A successful [[/skill arcana 18]] check allows a character to identify these marking as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGlyphofWar]{Glyph of Warding}.

  • The chest itself is unlocked, but trapped (see "Magical Chest Trap" below), and contains the @UUID[Item.NPJqphtKu5ov9MLp]{Pellucid Glaive} — a relic that Zira and her allies discovered here when they moved in.

Magical Chest Trap

The chest at the center of the room containing the Pellucid Glaive is unlocked, but is trapped with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGlyphofWar]{Glyph of Warding} spell. To avoid triggering the trap, a character must speak the password to disarm it:

Tormentor, guide my hands.

The passphrase renders the glyph inert for 10 minutes. If a character triggers the trap, they become the target of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplBestowCurs]{Bestow Curse} spell (using the Curse Actions activity for a duration of 24 hours).

The password can be discovered via two primary methods: searching the shelves of the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.LfBDELBnhykIyPrg]{Ritual Chamber}, or by successfully interrogating an @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted Adept} or @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero} herself.

Armory.name: Armory
Armory.text:
This darkened chamber is furnished with an archaic forge, its embers cold and latent for time uncounted. Piles of damaged arms and armor are stacked around in various states of disarray, with little rhyme or reason to their accumulated mess. A layer of dust has settled on this forgotten smithy, which is little more than an antechamber now.

This chamber is the ancient forge of the once-proud Temple of Ku'arta, but it has grown largely dormant in the days since Zira and The Undaunted have lived here.

Exploring the Armory

Any character who takes a moment to Search this room will readily locate an array of damaged weapons and armor, including:

  • 12 broken @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmShield0000]{Shields}.

  • 6 broken suits of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmScaleMail0]{Scale Mail}.

  • 8 broken suits of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmLeatherArm]{Leather Armor}.

  • 1 unbroken @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmBreastplat]{Breastplate}.

  • 1 unbroken suit of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmStuddedLea]{Studded Leather Armor}.

  • 1 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepShortsword]{Shortsword}.

The broken shields and suits of armor provide no bonuses to AC but can be sold as scrap for 10% of their listed price (rounded down).

Detecting the Secret Passage

Any character with a [[/skill perception 17 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] check while searching the room is able to notice a trail of footprints in the dust leading towards a section of the eastern wall.

The secret door here can be located with a successful [[/skill investigation 18]] check, which reveals the seams of the door as well as a keyhole concealed among the stonework.

Crafted by expert Ordani stonesmiths, this door can only be opened using a @UUID[Item.4RHsNmK18A9mTxHK]{Temple of Ku'arta Key} or magic like the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplKnock00000]{Knock} spell (which will alert all Undaunted enemies in the Underworks).

Temple Sanctum.name: Temple Sanctum
Temple Sanctum.text:
Lit by a scattered array of sconces, this massive oblong chamber reeks of ceremonial incense and the musk of sweat. An altar occupies an alcove at the northern end of the room, sitting atop two tiers of elevated flagstone terrain. Two large runic symbols are emblazoned on the floor here, one at the center of the chamber and one to the south — esoteric signifiers of some arcane purpose or design. Meanwhile, a curiosity sits atop the altar: a large glass jar bearing a crimson orb suspended in some murky fluid.

Eight Undaunted acolytes are gathered in a circle at the center of the room, engaged in a chorus of ritualistic chanting while they each perform a series of esoteric gestures. A few others look on with rapt anticipation, including a notable figure near the altar on the top dais: none other than Zira Hestidero herself, who conducts this macabre symphony while paying heed to the jarred orb behind her. The warlock speaks with a commanding voice to her followers, who manage to retain their concentration on whatever profane ritual is taking place.

The moment is at hand! Through diligence and the unending defeat of our enemies, we have gained the favor of our lord of suffering. Join me as we beseech the divine favor of this unholy oculus, and bask in the splendor of our becoming!

Zira turns her back to you, engaging with the strange relic on the altar. Her hands begin to perform a complex series of arcane gestures as she chants beneath her breath. All the while, the rest of the Undaunted continue their rites, absorbed by the labored esoterica.

This wedge-shaped chamber serves as the Temple of Ku'arta's unholy Sanctum, and has endured here since the earliest days of Ordain. The ceiling is 45 feet high here.

Multiphased Encounter

This combat encounter has a total of three segments that should occur during the course of action:

  • "The Party Arrives," in which the characters enter the scene. If they remain hidden, the characters will have up to 10 rounds to survey the scene. Otherwise, combat will begin as soon as they become noticed by the enemy.

  • "The Assembly Appears," in which Zira's ritual takes its first dramatic turn, as the eight Undaunted acolytes performing the ritual are absorbed into a new abberant creature, the @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su]{Grim Assembly}.

  • "Zira Absorbed," in which the ritual takes yet another dramatic turn, when Zira herself is absorbed into the grotesque melange of the Grim Aseembly's misshapen form.

If the party remains hidden when they arrive, the characters have a total of 10 rounds of gameplay before "The Assembly Appears," at which time combat begins. Alternately, combat begins as soon as one or more of the characters are spotted.

The Party Arrives

@UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero} leads the profane conjuration ceremony that is taking place here, with 5 @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted Adepts}, 4 @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]{Undaunted Trainees}, and @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I]{Jorey Swift} in attendance.

The characters may wish to examine the scene before they act (a prudent strategy if they wish to navigate the encounter with appropriate safety and efficacy).

Staying Hidden

If the characters want to survey the Sanctum without being detected by Zira Hestidero or her allies, they'll each need to succeed on a [[/skill stealth 13]] (made with @Advantage[2], thanks to the distractions of the ritual).

Failure results in that character being spotted by the enemies in the room, while other party members who succeed on the check remain hidden.

Examining the Sanctuary

Any character who takes a turn to Search the room from afar is able to notice the following without any skill checks or other considerations:

  • Even from here, the grotesque relic that accompanies Zira at the altar resembles a large crimson eye in a jar.

  • The circle is actively observed by an Undaunted Adept in the northeast corner of the central section of the room, who chants along with his allies but doesn't perform any gestures.

  • Jorey Swift is situated in the rear northwestern corner of the central section of the room, and observes the ritual with a recognizable amount of tenuous resolve, barely speaking the chant in unison.

Characters who succeed on a [[/skill insight 15]] check are also able to deduce the following:

  • The tenuous resolve on display by Jorey betrays a measurable amount of anxiousness, as if he's somewhat in over his head but too stubborn to realize it.

  • There is a slight element of deception to Zira's body language, betraying an amount of insincerity.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] or [[/skill religion 15]] check while taking the Search action is able to determine that the 8 Undaunted performing the ritual along with Zira are engaged in some kind of arcane conjuration.

  • Result of 20+: The ritual being performed here is markedly different from the ceremonies and rites associated with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}, the known patron of Zira and her Undaunted cohorts.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge gods]] or [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

@Embed[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]

@Embed[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm count=5]

@Embed[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI count=4]

@Embed[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I]

Parley with Zira

If the characters blow their cover in an attempt to speak with Zira (for whatever reason), they have one turn to ask her a question before combat begins. Some specific dialogue options for Zira are featured below.

Alternately, you can choose to allow the characters and Zira to exchange words once combat begins.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check can readily tell that Zira is up to something nefarious here today, something illicit masquerading as a traditional ceremony to her patron.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

What's happening here?

Zira regards the throng of acolytes before her and casts a quick glance over her shoulder at the strange artifact on the altar.

Rejoice! You are the sacred witnesses to a great becoming!

Jorey Swift?

Jorey is where he belongs. We're the only family he'll ever need.

Revenge for Agraband?

The old bard is little more than a nuissance. Storytellers should stick to the sidelines, lest they become the subject of stories themselves.

Alerting the Enemy

Once one or more of the characters have been spotted by Zira or one of her Undaunted allies, they have one free bonus round for parley or preparation before combat officially begins.

  • Before the end of this round, after the characters have had a chance to act, the lone @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted Adept} loscated outside the summoning circle here will move to engage the party in combat.

  • Alternately, if one or more of the characters attack Zira or one of the Undaunted acolytes, the free bonus round is simply the first round of combat.

No matter how many rounds from the original 10 rounds of "The Party Arrives" remain, combat begins following the bonus round. Proceed to "The Assembly Appears" for more details about what happens next.

Parley with Jorey

At any point during the encounter, the characters may attempt to convince Jorey Swift to abandon his association with The Undaunted and join the party alongside his uncle Agraband.

If they wish to recruit the young acolyte to their cause, the party must complete a skill challenge by succeeding on a total of 3 skill checks from the following list:

[[/skill deception 13]] The character lies to Jorey in an effort to coerce the youth to change his stance.

[[/skill insight 13]] The character takes advantage of Jorey's inner turmoil or his vulnerable situation.

[[/skill intimidation 13]] The character convinces Jorey of the party's superior might or introduces another obstacle.

[[/skill persuasion 13]] The character uses encouragement or cajolery to change Jorey's mind.

[[/skill religion 13]] The character attempts to warn Jorey about the cosmic implications of his participation here.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge abyssals]], [[/knowledge gods]], or [[/knowledge souls]] have @Advantage[2] on these checks.

  • Each time a character succeeds on one of these checks, you should indicate to them that Jorey is growing increasingly sympathetic to what they have to say.

  • Alternately, any character with a [[/skill insight 15 passive format=long]] knows precisely how many successes are needed to recruit Jorey.

If and when Jorey is successfully recruited, he'll defect to the party, joining the characters as an ally in combat. While technically autonomous, he'll take his lead from Agrband and the other party members; if desired, you can allow the players to take control of his token and character sheet at this time.

The Assembly Appears

When combat begins, read the following aloud:

The heat of battle is upon you, but Zira takes a brief moment to address the congregation.

The truth is often a terrible thing to behold. I must admit, I've been deceiving you, my friends. Ku'arta's magic could only take us so far. We have a new master now.

She gestures to the large crimson eye in the jar on the altar behind her. With a pulse of magenta light, the glass receptacle shatters outward into a thousand tiny fragments, and the imposing red eye begins to hover above the dais. A wicked grin streaks its way across Zira's face.

The Red Ruin sees you …

Just then, a shriek of pain from one of the Undaunted adepts gathered in the summoning circle arrests your attention. You look to see a vaporous arcane mist surrounding the panicked warlock, enveloping some of his extremities. Before you know it, the very flesh is torn from the adept's arm and slowly pulled into the center of the circle, where the crimson eye from Zira's relic has somehow found its way above the throng amidst a terrible arcane miasma.

The rest of the Undaunted adepts and trainees in the circle are likewise torn asunder by the strange ritual magic, their flesh and bones and viscera coalescing into a singular mass around the eye at the center of the chamber. In an instant, a new creature lurches to life before you — unmeasurably horrible and alien in origin …

Simultaneously, the bodies of the four Undaunted adepts in the circle appear to have undergone a horrible transformation of their own …

Token Reveals: Grim Assembly & Abyss-Warped Undaunted

At this time, replace the 4 Undaunted Adept tokens in the summoning circle with 4 Abyss-Warped Undaunted tokens.

Additionally, toggle the visibility of the Grim Assembly token on, and assign the Dead status effect to the 4 Undaunted Trainees in the summoning circle.

@Embed[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su]

The 4 Undaunted Adepts have also undergone a gruesome transformation, resulting in the creation of 4 Abyss-Warped Undaunted who join the fray beside the Grim Assembly.

@Embed[Actor.DX50kH8P7yh5BFh0 count=4]

Zira Hestidero Tactics

During the earliest rounds of combat, Zira will target enemy spellcasters or ranged attackers from afar with spells like @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj.Item.8SB38jhJXYCG8BSv]{Phantasmal Killer} or @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj.Item.1IfWKKgb0u5dNPHm]{Hold Person}. If necessary, she'll position herself within 60 feet of an enemy spellcaster to be able to cast the @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj.Item.W5FMqMu3NvTpU1MW]{Counterspell} spell.

If Jorey attempts to defect from The Undaunted early in the encounter, Zira may use the @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj.Item.DuD1KxoSSwGmcLiC]{Command} spell in an attempt to humiliate and control him (if not another party member, including Agraband).

Jorey Tactics

When the Grim Assembly appears, Jorey will continue to naïvely support Zira in combat until the characters manage to convince him otherwise (see "Parley with Jorey" above).

Using his @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I.Item.ehJ1OjcBjmRG67JF]{Reckless Movement} to close in for melee combat with one of the characters (with priority for warrior classes like fighters, monks, paladins, or rangers), Jorey will attempt to use his @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I.Item.9RAeXkazGgW47hnb]{Pack Tactics} feature to the best of his abilities alongside his Abyss-Warped allies.

Abyss-Warped Undaunted

These fearsome aberrations will close in for melee attacks with the closest available enemies, using their @UUID[Actor.DX50kH8P7yh5BFh0.Item.yzkhC3HSvGguuydi]{Flesh-Warped Tentacle} attack and @UUID[Actor.DX50kH8P7yh5BFh0.Item.XUG88QPvPMiUyo13]{Pack Tactics} with deadly precision.

Grim Assembly Tactics

The Grim Assembly is an inscrutable creature of abyssal origin, and its motives are the stuff of unadulterated entropy. Because this encounter is likely to be a very dangerous and challenging one, the Grim Assembly will likely distribute its attacks equally amongst the characters.

Characters who engage the Grim Assembly in melee combat will take a certain amount of priority, becoming rapid targets of its @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su.Item.VMpHGSgWScoqfGgc]{Sickening Slam} and @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su.Item.ZEAiCr0gkEHljw3i]{Grab} attacks.

Meanwhile, the Grim Assembly will use @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su.Item.CRXmrlUmT9ur8h5y]{Eye Blast} as often as possible to target as many enemy creatures as possible — with little or no attempts being made to avoid hitting allied @UUID[Actor.DX50kH8P7yh5BFh0]{Abyss-Warped Undaunted} in the process.

Once the Grim Assembly has lost half or more of its total hit points, the additional abilities of its @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su.Item.ViFCcnkQk8nb0OVr]{Multiphased} feature become active just as the "Zira Absorbed" segment of the encounter begins (see below).

Zira Absorbed

As the Grim Assembly's @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su.Item.ViFCcnkQk8nb0OVr]{Multiphased} feature activates, read the following aloud:

With another fateful blow struck against Zira's horrible conjuration, you notice a peculiar reaction from the loathsome one-eyed monster: its viscous flesh begins to shudder with anticipation as the same arcane mist you saw earlier envelops Zira herself.

A look of panic inches its way across the warlock's face as she comes to the horrible realization of what's happening. As she issues a blood-curdling scream you'll never forget, Zira's body is magically pulled towards the Grim Assembly and subsumed by its awful, misbegotten form.

Without missing a beat, the large mass of flesh continues its reckless assault, Zira's body gruesomely fused to its hideous side.

Token Reveal: Grim Assembly (Phase 2)

At this time, remove Zira Hestidero's token and replace the Grim Assembly Phase 1 token with the Grim Assembly Phase 2 token.

Grim Assembly Tactics

The Grim Assembly retains most of its tactics from the previous phase, with the addition of arcane spellcasting as part of its action economy.

Throughout the encounter, Zira's fleeting consciousness will exert itself via the Grim Assembly's @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su.Item.7BgT6T8ZlmNljgdA]{Spellcasting (2nd Phase)} spells.

Aftermath

If the party manages to defeat the Grim Assembly and its minions in combat, read the following aloud:

As you strike one final blow against the awful otherworldly creature, a myriad of boils and pustules begin forming on the fleshy surface of its tenebrous skin. Black as the night, these malevolent pocks bubble and pop, and a smoky vapor starts rising from the monster's hideous corpse. In the blink of an eye, the entire creature dissolves into an inky pool of abyssal muck.

The sanctum falls silent for a moment, heavy with grim revelation.

If the party managed to convince Jorey to defect from The Undaunted, this is likely the appropriate time for a conversation between the troubled youth and his uncle Agraband (with the characters serving as mediators).

A Conversation with Jorey

Depending on the party's actions during the course of the encounter, Jorey will be disposed to a variety of conversation points, including (but not limited to) the following:

  • How he became affiliated with The Undaunted.

  • Zira Hestidero's clandestine pursuit of eldritch power.

  • Next steps with Agraband.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check reveals the honesty behind Jorey's claims, and suggests that he feels a certain amount of fatigue from the day's events that would be served from some rest and relaxation far away from the confines of the Underworks.

Your affiliation with The Undaunted?

I never thought it would go this far. They found me at a time in my life when I needed someone, anyone, to show me the way. They just happened to show me the wrong way.

There were times when I really felt alive being part of that team. But it was all a lie. And here I am, caught between evil gods and a whole world of misunderstanding.

Zira's leadership and powers?

I looked up to Zira like a sister. A cruel but capable sister, who could hold the city in the palm of her hand if she wanted to. But it sounds like Zira wanted more than we'll ever know, and more than she could bargain for.

Agraband's situation?

A look of shame crosses Jorey's face, and he regards his uncle with a bashful appeal — attempting to clumsily bridge the gap of a decade of missing moments.

I'm sorry, uncle. I only wanted to be somebody important. I never wanted to be a villain. I never wanted this.

Event Outcomes

Due to its social elements, the results of this combat encounter can have an effect on several Event Outcomes from the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessUnderworks]] event, including:

  • Jorey Redeemed (Heart Attunemet)

  • Jorey Undaunted (Cora Attunement)

  • Jorey Slain (no Attunement)

  • Ku'arta's Bargain (Luxarum Attunement)

  • Sha-Xotha's Bargain (Abyss Attunement)

Be sure to check the appropriate Event Outcomes on the event page at the conclusion of the encounter.

Corrupted Altar.name: Corrupted Altar
Corrupted Altar.text:
The surface of this wide stone altar appears to have been discolored by some foul, purple-black ichor. Tenebrous rivulets of murky stain run down the side of the blemished rock, and you swear you can almost hear the rasp of an otherworldly whisper as you stare closely at the stygian grime.

The stone altar has been corrupted by Zira Hestidero's attempt to commune with abyssal forces beyond the veil of reality, and bears signs of her loathsome experimentations.

WIP: Under Construction

The Kalion Stadium Underworks area map is a work-in-progress, and this area has yet to be fully implemented.

Anterior Chamber.name: Anterior Chamber
Anterior Chamber.text:
The alcove channels you into to a small square chamber decorated with little more than a burnished steel turnstile at its center. Peering out through darkened archways to the north and south, it seems this room is situated on a railway of sorts, supported by the pronounced grooves on the floor below.

To the west, a similar room adjoins this one, illuminated by a solitary brazier. Farther still, you spy the silhouette of a large ballista in a third chamber alight with arcane flame.

Agraband surveys the scene and scratches his chin in contemplation.

If I didn't know any better, I'd say we must navigate this mechanized maze of malevolent chambers to proceed …

Under Construction

The central "Hall of Challenges" section of Kalion Stadium Underworks is a work-in-progress, and will eventually feature an interactable puzzle for players to solve as they navigate the map.

This puzzle is intended to begin with the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.cG03KmQ91RbQWc1w]{Anterior Chamber} and will terminate at the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.Z2ysTZfnXSZpXZrN]{Secret Vestibule}. For the time being, we recommend you connect the two sections of gameplay that occur in the Hall of Contest and Temple of Ku'arta with the readaloud below.

Starting at the edge of this massive trap-like complex, you manage to navigate a veritable gauntlet of shifting rooms and sliding chambers equipped with deadly obstacles. After several moments of adrenaline-fueled decision and encounters with esoteric hazards, you find yourself face-to-face with an alcove on the opposite side of this inscrutable mechanical sprawl, roughly a dozen chambers and one-hundred-and-thirty feet (as the crow flies) from where you began.

Acolyte Quarters.name: Acolyte Quarters
Acolyte Quarters.text:
This sparsely decorated room shows signs of recent inhabitance: the bed is unkept, and the crumbs of some recent meal linger on the bedside table.

This small room serves as the private quarters for one of Zira's Undaunted Adepts. Very few possessions can be found here, as the Undaunted maintain lives of relative freedom from the distraction of personal belongings.

Bathhouse.name: Bathhouse
Bathhouse.text:
The faint smell of petrichor accompanies the sound of lightly-running water here, where a large and inviting bath dominates the chamber. Towels and fresh linens lay draped upon wooden palettes to stay dry, and the stonework here is remarkably clean thanks to the immediate presence of the facility's aqueducts.

This chamber is the facility's bathhouse, and features a small variety of magical and technical accoutrements to ensure the good health and hygienics of the residents here.

Exploring the Bathhouse

The water that flows from the nearby fountains and basins is potable drinking water, cool and clean, piped in via ancient Ordani aqueducts from fresh water sources nearby.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 12 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] check is able to notice a button concealed among the bricks that line the bath here.

A successful [[/skill arcana 13]] or [[/skill investigation 13]] check allows a character to confirm the precise use of this button without pushing it: the button powers a slab of enchanted stone at the bottom of the bath that heats or cools the water within it.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge machines]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who takes at least 5 minutes to Search the area is able to locate the following:

  • [[/roll 1d3+2]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBlanket0000]{Blankets}, bleached white but variously stained with blood.

  • A vial of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPerfume0000]{Perfume} scented with essence of aithus.

  • A water-logged @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Book} of salacious fiction titled "The Executioner's Tales."

Ritual Chamber.name: Ritual Chamber
Ritual Chamber.text:
The lingering smell of incense and grave nitre assault your senses as you step into this macabre chamber, which appears to be decorated with a variety of occult trophies and arcane accoutrements.

This room serves as a chamber for Zira's clandestine arcane rituals, as well as her private quarters when she so desires. A collection of bleached skulls, scented ritual candles, bloodied trinkets, and profane texts are scattered about this unholy place.

Opening the Locked Doors

The doors to this chamber are locked, and can be opened with either a successful [[/skill thief 18]] check or a @UUID[Item.4RHsNmK18A9mTxHK]{Temple of Ku'arta Key}. A successful [[/skill athletics 22]] check is required to bash the doors in.

Alternately, the doors can be opened with magic like the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplKnock00000]{Knock} spell, which will alert all Undaunted enemies in the Underworks.

Exploring the Ritual Chamber

Any character who takes the Search action here will notice the following:

  • A collection of humanoid skulls, which appear aged and decrepit.

  • A strange array of components and esoteric materials are gathered here.

A successful [[/skill perception 13]] check also reveals the presence of Zira's Diary, which reveals her newfound allegiance to an entity she refers to as "The Red Ruin," which promises to offer her otherworldly power in return for her betrayal of Ku'arta.

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll3r]{Spell Scroll} of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplSpeakwithD]{Speak with Dead} is tucked into the rear fold of the diary.

  • Result of 18+: The character also discovers the password to disarm the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGlyphofWar]{Glyph of Warding} on the chest in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.bKJRzPHSiusLwmbL]{Reliquary}, which is written alongside a sketch and brief description of the @UUID[Item.NPJqphtKu5ov9MLp]{Pellucid Glaive}:

    To access to the champion's relic, you need only speak the mantra "Tormentor, guide my hands" lest a curse befall you.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check can recognize the purpose of this room as a ritual chamber, and allows for a retry of the Wisdom (Perception) check detailed above.

  • The character also recognizes that the material spell components here include incense traditionally associated with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCommune000]{Commune} spell.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on this check.

Chantry.name: Chantry
Chantry.text:
Five wooden pews face a short stone dais at the northern end of this modest chamber, where a podium overlooks the temple's dust-strewn chantry. Scattered arrangements of half-used candles decorate the dais, as well as a bookcase on the southern end of the room, where puddles of wax keep company with a neglected bookshelf full of moldering texts.

This dusty chamber serves as the temple's chantry, where recitations, prayer sessions, sermons, and ceremonies are traditionally carried out with less pomp and circumstance than the majestic @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.wWT2yqitYzTHNWaR]{Temple Sanctum} nearby.

Exploring the Chantry

Any character who takes a moment to Search the chamber here will notice the following:

  • The bookshelf to the south is stocked with a variety of workbooks lined with handwritten accounts of the lectures here.

  • A solitary tome sits atop the podium on the dais, which appears to be a chronicle of Ku'artan champions called "Fists of the Tormentor."

Any character with a [[/skill perception passive format=long 14]] who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check while Searching the chamber is also able to spot the following:

  • The sheer amount of dust on the various surfaces and accoutrements here suggests that the chantry goes largely unused compared to other chambers in the temple complex.

  • The character spots a particularly curious tome on the bookshelf titled "The Triumphs of Regus Halamattrix." Any character who spends at least 15 minutes to study this tome gains @Advantage[2] on Charisma skill checks made to influence @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI]{Regus Halamattrix} in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.eyUP3WMr4YNkkvHT]{Hall of Champions} and elsewhere.

A successful [[/skill religion 12]] check allows a character to confirm the purpose of this chamber, along with its role in the temple's ongoing practices: while the Temple Sanctum is reserved for important ceremonies, the Chantry here is a place of learning, proselytizing, and demonstration.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge gods]] and [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on this check.

Arcane Workshop.name: Arcane Workshop
Arcane Workshop.text:
This darkened area reeks of stale ash and chemical fumes, no doubt emanating from the cauldron in the middle of the chamber, which sits idly above a cold hearth. A small table next to this fireplace is decorated with an array of alchemy apparatuses, and shelves stocked with all manner of strange reagents and spell components line the entire space.

This room is Zira Hestidero's arcane workshop, where she prepares the ritual incense and other esoteric ingredients necessary for the cult's various activities in areas like the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.Hm9ku5muMPilfUuG]{Chamber of Bargains}, her private @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.LfBDELBnhykIyPrg]{Ritual Chamber}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.wWT2yqitYzTHNWaR]{Temple Sanctum}, and other locations outside the Underworks. Likewise, this place functions as an ersatz kitchen of sorts, and some of what appears to be alchemical supplies is actually jarred foodstuffs.

Exploring the Workshop

With a brief Search of the area, the party is able to locate a few items of interest:

  • 32 pints (4 gallons) of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbWaterpint0000]{Water}

  • [[/roll 1d2]] vials of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAcid0000000]{Acid}

  • [[/roll 3d4]] jars of preserved fruits (2 lbs. of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagRations0000]{Rations} each)

  • [[/roll 1d2]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagTinderbox00]{Tinderboxes}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulAlchemists]{Alchemist's Supplies}

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 14]] check while searching the room is also able to locate the following:

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAlchemistsF]{Alchemist's Fire}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagComponentPo]{Component Pouch}

  • @UUID[Item.9CmgPSRokA8ta3D1]{Improved Alchemist's Supplies}

  • Result of 19+: @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfResis]{Potion of Necrotic Resistance}

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 12]] check while Searching the area is able to identify several material components for arcane spells stored in the containers here, and can loot [[/roll 1d3+1]] samples of any mundane material spell component for a spell on their spell list worth 15 gp or less.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This Side Quest occurs during Chapter 3, and begins while the party traverses the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.rzME5gXmbZ2zvqq5]{Ordain Flats} biome of the great city of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}. There are no prerequisites for this Quest, but it must be undertaken within one week.

This Quest also presumes the characters have maintained a friendly relationship with @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} of the Strayhearth Caravan, who they encountered saw during the events of [[/eventState windingTrailSmoke]], and the narrative relies on that amicable status to proceed.

Difficulty

"Unfinished Business" is designed for a party of Level 4 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 2 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Points}: 1 Milestone Point each upon successful completion of the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessThayloc]] and [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessUnderworks]] Events.

The party's trusted friend @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} approaches them with what seems to be a relatively simple task: help him track down his estranged nephew Jorey, who's rumored to have fallen in with a rough crowd in Ordain. However, the confrontation with Jorey's new associates doesn't go quite as planned, and Agraband is killed during a fateful scuffle … or is he? Endowed with supernatural life, Agraband becomes one of the mysterious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound}: newly-dead individuals of Ember who must fulfill some great personal or cosmic duty before their souls can peacefully migrate to the City of @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.WmwoaJUw9oosRtS5]{Eternas} in the Spiritlands. Thus, with young Jorey's fate hanging in the balance, the characters must help Agraband settle his own unfinished business — lest he remain Soulbound forever (and succumb to the condition's inevitable withering).

"Unfinished Business" will lead the party on a mystifying adventure through various parts of Ordain, starting with Agraband's fateful encounter with Zira and The Undaunted in the Smokerie. Following a brief period of recuperation at @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP]{Traveler's Rest} in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.nS7kj8wZ5eFq6pcy]{Westgate}, the party must help Agraband learn more about his strange condition by speaking with local authorities — including the scatterbrained @UUID[Actor.UEN4Lxa3qDqOAS5B]{Conaris Haid} in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.XUn8UELVkQmnCI78]{Temple Ward}, and the ever-elusive @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gT5S5ncAEUvkYYYg]{Sionia}. Simultaneously, the party must help Agraband track down Jorey and learn more about the gang of dangerous misfits he's fallen in with. This course of action will take them to the Grand Kalion Stadium of Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}, where they'll initially watch The Undaunted in action on a field of simulated combat, before returning to confront Zira and her cronies in the Kalion Stadium Underworks — where a forgotten temple to Ku'arta conceals secrets untold.

Can the characters successfully uncover Zira's newfound allegiance to an outer god and unravel her malevolent plot to sacrifice her Undaunted cohorts in a rise to power? If so, they just might survive a final conflict with the warlock in her inner sanctum, alongside a flesh-warped creature of the Abyss known as the Grim Assembly (which threatens to wreak more havoc on the city than even Zira herself can imagine). And with any luck, the party can convince Jorey to turn his back on Zira's twisted schemes altogether — closing the book on Agraband's unfinished business in the process.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift}

  • @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I]{Jorey Swift}

  • @UUID[Actor.UEN4Lxa3qDqOAS5B]{Conaris Haid}

  • @UUID[Actor.jzrNvlGQHpoSkkIU]{Sionia}

  • @UUID[Actor.V12wT5KF8sosFLvW]{Helice Korsos}

  • @UUID[Actor.9AXW4Yr8ON5V6SGj]{Brackus von Tet}

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero}

  • @UUID[Actor.4Fzy8LfpwR3px7zI]{Undaunted Trainee}

  • @UUID[Actor.NmGRNpwShrNbdtYm]{Undaunted Adept}

  • @UUID[Actor.B3WggltirZtxdcEE]{Thayloc Courser}

  • @UUID[Actor.q6jhaDn9jsBWKZNI]{Regus Halamattrix}

  • @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su]{Grim Assembly}

  • @UUID[Actor.DX50kH8P7yh5BFh0]{Abyss-Warped Undaunted}
Overview.soverview:
The famed raconteur Agraband Swift approaches the party in Ordain, but this timely reunion is regrettably an unpleasant one. During Agraband's time away from Ordain, his estranged nephew Jorey — the old caravaner's only surviving relative — is rumored to have fallen in with a bad crowd, and he needs the party's help for a wellness check on the younger Swift. The task at hand is a relatively easy one: the characters will serve as a security detail for Agraband during a brief visit to Ordain's Smokerie district, where a warehouse nightclub known as "The Pit Trap" is rumored to host exclusive events. And Jorey's new gang, a competitive team of Solar Games players culled from the ranks of a neighborhood orphanage, are said to be the club's VIPs on a regular basis. Known as "The Undaunted", this team of roguish athletes are local heroes, and access to their inner circle won't be easy.

But what begins as a simple escort mission descends into tragedy when Agraband is mortally-wounded on the dance floor by an assailant. Despite the chaos of the moment, all signs point to The Undaunted's leader Zira Hestidero as the perpetrator of this heinous crime. Yet, as the smoke clears and the venue is evacuated, Agraband's death is not entirely what it seems … he lives! Driven by some unknown source, his wounds seep lambent energy. In the days that follow, the party must help Agraband come to understand the reality of his new "Soulbound" condition, which will inevitably lead them on a local hunt for Jorey and The Undaunted.

Along the way, the party will uncover sordid truths about The Undaunted and their leader Zira Hestidero — namely, that Zira is a powerful warlock of the shard god Ku'arta, and The Undaunted serve as acolytes for the God of Torment's deranged religion of violent brinksmanship. However, once they reach Zira's inner sanctum, the our heroes will discover one final and terrible secret: the intrepid warlock has turned her back on Ku'arta to serve a new otherworldly master. But the cost of this power is steep, and The Undaunted (including young Jorey Swift) are unwitting participants in Zira's horrible ascension. With any luck, the characters will help Agraband settle his unfinished business and put and end to his nephew's time with The Undaunted, sparing Jorey from the servitude of Zira's baleful pact.

The Troubled Caravaneer.name: The Troubled Caravaneer
The Troubled Caravaneer.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event takes place within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.rzME5gXmbZ2zvqq5]{Ordain Flats}, and reunites the party with their old ally @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} — who's in timely need of a security detail for a sensitive (and potentially dangerous) errand. In this event, the characters can:

  • Learn about Agraband's activity since the @UUID[Actor.emberStrayhearth]{Strayhearth Caravan}'s recent arrival to @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.g9VNrwVFUBMUOgPh]{Ordain}, along with a few details about his untold past.

  • Decide whether or not to accept Agraband's job offer, which will task them as casual bodyguards during a trip to the rough-and-tumble @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c]{Smokerie} district.

  • Learn a few minor details about what the other members of the Strayhearth Caravan have been up to (if they've yet to do so).

Strayhearth Reunited

The party is approached by their ally @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} while traversing the neighborhoods of the Ordain Flats. Despite his warm nature, the old caravaner seems troubled, and is eager to catch up with them before sharing additional details regarding a furtive plight.

@Embed[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift}

Catching Up with Agraband

Agraband is eager to hear stories from the characters about what they've been up to, and is happy to indulge a few brief tales of his own. Some of this small talk includes (but is not limited to):

  • Where the characters happen to be lodging while in Ordain, and what they've been up to.

  • A few notable Ordani landmarks, such as the many wonders of the Waterfront Bazaar in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.hKNuD0yWUAA6UmDA]{Flotsam}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.jBVzQi6wRjMew0Es]{Performer's Plaza} (where Agraband first plied his trade as a bard), and any other districts the party shows interest in.

  • A couple of brief anecdotes about Strayhearth encounters along the road to Ordain, like a timely run-in with a group of refugees from northern @UUID[JournalEntry.emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.QpeeUqr3NZMsObnG]{Skybrush}, and a brief scuffle with a small gang of bounty hunters mounted on @UUID[Actor.T6YcptpxcCLx4yLx]{Jobri}.

Additionally, the characters may be curious about what the other members of the Strayhearth Caravan have been up to in recent days (if not weeks). Even if the characters show no initial interest, Agraband himself is likely to share a few anecdotal details about various rumors he's heard regarding the sundered company — with stories about @UUID[Actor.gP1uHGhYAkJM9rIP]{Lyla Cevher}, @UUID[Actor.IGDzpiRypheZ4mWv]{Sin Marmot}, @UUID[Actor.ehBJkqqxoa7VEwSs]{Ankarist}, and @UUID[Actor.ffC4a0BFAnDg2NjZ]{Clipper} in particular.

As Agraband shares these tales of the Strayhearth compatriots, any character with a [[/skill Insight 12 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill Insight 14]] check is able to tell that the bard is keeping something from them: a source of anxiety and consternation, somewhat unusual traits for the worldly bard.

Ultimately, Agraband uses the relative scarcity of the disparate Strayhearth allies to broach a new topic of rather personal concern: a plight involving his estranged nephew, Jorey Swift. Once this shift in narrative occurs, please refer to "Agraband's Plight" below for additional details.

Your Story Since Helkas?

Our jaunt from the Forest of Stone to the marble walls of Westgate was relatively uneventful, unless we count that cadre of scurvy bounty hunters we encountered near Lake Jinro, or the group of refugees on their way from Skybrush.

The refugees had been displaced from Skybrush on account of a freak accident that had spooked a few of its citizens, a few families on the outskirts of town in particular. We offered them passage to Ordain, and they kept mostly to themselves. Proud folks, and fine people, but humbled by their circumstances.

The bounty hunters were another story altogether. Thankfully, Clipper was able to pacify their aggressive inclinations by offering them a discount on a few arcane baubles. We've no idea who they were really looking for, or why. And we didn't bother to ask.

As for me, I'm happy to spend a few days back in my hometown. After all, I have more than a few travel companions to catch up with!

The old bard gestures proudly to your group and smiles with familial recognition.

Lyla Cevher's Story?

It seems House Cevher has its hands full these days with an assortment of troubles. Young Lyla has no doubt swept up in the calamities herself, buried under paperwork and bureaucracy at the House Cevher Tradeway in Quarry Run.

Sin Marmot's Story?

I understand Sin has acclimated herself to the ways of the Cindaric Sages. Life at Cindarin Temple certainly has its perks, as opulent as the old edifice is (and as well-funded as the Cindarics can be). Perhaps I should pay the sages a visit sometime. The sacred pyreflies dance in the atrium at night, and it's a wonderful sight to behold.

Ankarist's Story?

Our friend Ankarist has been able to return to his duties for the Veiled Chain. Word about town suggests some kind of pending investigation regarding a strange illness, but I've yet to discuss it with the headstrong Drakon himself.

Clipper's Story?

Agraband looks off towards the city's western gate, where the Strayhearth Caravan awaits his inevitable return.

Clipper is holding down the fort, so to speak, stationed at the caravan with a few other company regulars. I know they enjoy the good banter and resourceful opportunities the city has to offer, and Westgate is a fine hub for such activity. Should you need any equipment or information that the city itself can't provide, I'm sure our gregarious Signborn friend would treasure a visit from you all.

Agraband's Plight

Once the party has had ample time for small talk and pleasantries, Agraband shifts the focus of the conversation to more important matters at hand.

Agraband's mood shifts as he addresses what's obviously been lingering on his mind since you met here on the street.

Truth be told, this visit isn't entirely a serendipitous one. I've actually sought you out, friends, because I need your help. However, my situation is a clandestine one, and a little privacy is in order before I relay the circumstances of my plight. Shall we?

The old bard motions towards a nearby alcove, where a few public benches are flanked by municipal decoration — hedges and statues, in particular, which seem to provide ample seclusion for your conversation.

The Caravaneer's Tale

Once they've reached a suitable spot for secrecy, Agraband explains his situation:

  • He’s journeyed to the city in search of his estranged nephew @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I]{Jorey Swift}, an audacious young man whose life has been a series of one reckless predicament after the next following the untimely death of his mother (Agraband's sister Selena).

  • It seems Jorey's latest cavalier undertaking may be the most dangerous yet: he's joined a team of daredevil exhibitionists known as The Undaunted, participants in the Solar Games of Grand Kalion Stadium in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}.

  • Reigning champions of their sport, the Undaunted are said to welcome the lonely, the outcast, and the foolhardy to their ranks — which are led by a fierce athlete known as Zira Hestidero. In recent months, the self-destructive antics of The Undaunted have started spilling into the streets of Ordain, and Agraband fears the worst for his impressionable nephew.

  • The Undaunted are known to frequent a seedy warehouse nightclub in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c]{Smokerie} district known as @UUID[JournalEntry.YRCZmeogHpxWLR91]{The Pit Trap}.

Once these details have been shared with the party, Agraband beseeches them for aid and presents them with an offer: if they'll accompany him to the Pit Trap tomorrow night as a security detail, he'll gladly pay them [[/award 50gp]] each for their trouble (in advance).

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 15]] check is able to detect the honesty behind Agraband's statements.

Enterprising characters can attempt to elicit a higher payment from their old pal. The first character to succeed on either a [[/skill persuasion 16]] or [[/skill deception 20]] check is able to convince Agraband to sweeten the deal with an additional [[/award 20gp]] each.

Additional details and dialogue regarding Jorey et al. are featured below.

More About Jorey

A look of unmistakable concern rushes to Agraband's face when you mention his nephew's name.

Jorey is my only surviving relative, and — were I here in Ordain more often — I'd like to think of myself as a surrogate father for the boy.

He briefly chuckles beneath his breath.

"Boy," I say, as if he's still a kid. The "boy" is eighteen years old this year, and is hardly a child these days. But it's difficult to abandon the innocence I've foisted upon him. He's already been through so much, especially after the loss of his mother (my sister, Selena, who passed away nearly two years ago). One year in a soot-stained hostel with no real family seems to have undone seventeen years of good parenting. And perhaps it's my fault.

Jorey deserves an easy life, full of good times and people who truly care. I don't want to see these Undaunted ruffians steal that opportunity from him. I at least want to have the conversation with him, face to face. But his team of champions is somewhat inseparable, it seems.

Your Sister's Story?

Selena was the best sister a scoundrel like me could ask for. Life wasn't easy for us as children, orphaned and alone, but at least we had each other. And while I invested what I received of our inheritance into the Strayhearth enterprise, Selena would spend her own wealth on building a family here in Ordain. But the best laid plans of mortals are wrought with ruin, and our family has dwindled once more. Selena was killed in a simple accident while I was on the road nearly a year ago.

Agraband's composure slips for the briefest of moments, the only time you've truly seen this man lose his cool since you first met.

Strange things, those accidents. While Jorey was at school, Selena slipped on the wet floor and cracked her head wide open on the kitchen floor. Gone, in a flash. Such a simple and sudden and absurd way to die. I made it back for her funeral, but — like a damned fool — I hit the road again as soon as I could. And I regret not being here for her son this past year the way she was always there for me.

The Undaunted?

I'm not much of a sports enthusiast myself, but the Solar Games are important to many folks here in Ordain — not only because they're exhilarating, but thanks to the way the games are structured using teams from various districts. The element of hometown pride is important, and the Undaunted — who mostly hail from the Smokerie district — seem to have captured the heart of the entire city with their brash antics and ceaseless victories.

Beyond that, they've gained a reputation for causing trouble in certain parts of town, including every neighborhood between Arena Ridge and their home district. Further still, members of the Undaunted are known to retire from the sport a lot quicker than athletes from other teams … for one dubious reason or another.

Their team captain is a local celebrity of sorts named Zira Hestidero, a Maziran gladiator known for her ostentatious attitudes and bombastic arcane flourishes. Ultimately, I fear this veritable scoundrel might not be the best influence on young Jorey, and I aim to find out.

Akon Attunement: Accepted Agraband's Offer

If the party accepts Agraband's offer, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAkon +1 unfinishedBusinessFriend]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome swiftOfferAccepted]]

Aura Attunement: Refused Agraband's Offer

If the party refuses Agraband's offer, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 unfinishedBusinessFriend]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome swiftOfferRefused]]

Concluding the Event

If the characters decide to help Agraband, they have a couple of hours to gather their effects for a trip to the Smokerie, where the dim lights of the Smokestack await.

Next Steps

The party must travel to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c]{Smokerie} district by midnight tonight, where they'll provide a security detail for Agraband while he confronts Jorey and his new cohorts during the events of [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessSearch]].
The Troubled Caravaneer.soverview: As the party traverses the neighborhoods of the Ordain Flats, they're approached by their associate Agraband Swift, but the timely reunion is colored by the old caravaneer's latest troubles: Agraband's estranged nephew Jorey — his only surviving relative — has fallen in with an unsavory crowd, and the wizened raconteur aims to save the younger Swift from the perils of a life in Ordain's seedy underworld. If the characters are willing to escort the esteemed bard on a wellness check to the most dangersome corners of the Smokerie district, their old friend has a few hundred gold pieces in his pocket to make it worth their while.
The Troubled Caravaneer.sexposition:
A familiar sound drifts upon the hurried din of the city, something you can't quite place at first, a musical noise that feels like it emerged from a dream — soft and ephemeral and full of life. You instinctively strain to listen as the tones of this mysterious music drift ever-so-closer, bending their way through the streets and city-goers like some unseen labyrinth. After the briefest moment, you can finally identify the sound as the dulcet tones of a six-stringed kithara, followed by a friendly voice — the gentle tenor of the raconteur Agraband Swift, who croons a lilting melody rife with whimsy.

Through happenstance we parted ways and found our lonesome paths,
but friends of truth and consequence build bridges that will last.
And lo, I quickly found myself along a wayward road,
that somehow led right back to those whose hearts I'll always know.

The old bard slings his instrument over his back with a smile, and steps forward to greet you with a warm embrace.

A sight for sore eyes, indeed! I'd recognize those silhouettes anywhere. What have you all been up here in the great city of Ordain?
The Troubled Caravaneer.ssummary: We were approached by our erstwhile ally Agraband Swift, who beseeched us to help him with a new problem on his metaphorical plate: his estranged nephew Jorey has fallen in with a bad crowd, and Agraband wants to hire us to escort him on a wellness check to the Smokerie district — where a seedy nightclub named Hell is rumored to host parties celebrating Jorey's so-called friends.

Shine On.name: Shine On
Shine On.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event occurs the first time the party takes a long rest following the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessHealing]] event, and introduces the characters to the effects of a Rank 1 Soulmark.

This event may occur anywhere in the world as long as Agraband Swift is traveling with the party. It is depicted in the "Cozy Lounge" composition of the @UUID[Scene.emberVistaOrdInt]{Vista: Ordain Interiors} vista. In the rare circumstance that the party is traveling outside of Ordain when this event occurs, you may wish to change the scene to something more geographically representative.

In this event, the characters can:

  • Wake to discover an apparition of their friend @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift}'s soul drifting away from his body, alongside an intensification of his supernatural wound: indicators of his @UUID[Compendium.ember.character.Item.emberSoulbound00]{Rank 1 Soulmark}.

  • Intervene in an attempt to prevent Agraband from suffering the worse possible outcome this Rank 1 Soulmark.

  • Try to assess the likelihood of this happening again, learning more about the practical effects of life as a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.pFxI6eScKqZbfT2Q]{Soulbound} character in the process.

Prerequisites

This event may only occur during a Long Rest Rest while @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} is a member of the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party}.

Nightmares & Dreamscapes

In this moment, the characters are timely witnesses to the first manifestation of Agraband's Rank 1 Soulmark, and can interrupt the bard's supernatural nightmare to help him stave off its negative effects.

@Embed[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw readaloud="The exuberant smile and calm demeanor one might normally expect to see on the face of this wizened Ordani bard have been replaced by a countenance tinged with angst and apprehension. A curious pale light emanates from a scar on his chest, lightly obscured by the folds of his tunic. However, despite whatever strange malady afflicts him, the aged raconteur holds his chin high with hope and expectation."]

Timely Intervention

For the duration of this quest, the mechanics of Agraband's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.pFxI6eScKqZbfT2Q]{Soulbound} nature are modeled after those of a Player Character rather than a traditional NPC. These rules are fully detailed in the Player Characters section of the Player's Guide.

As allies who are present during Agraband's nightmarish episode, the characters can attempt to intervene, providing @Advantage[2] to Agraband's associated Wisdom save by immediately taking one of the following actions:

  • Casting the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCalmEmotio]{Calm Emotions} spell with Agraband inside the area of effect.

  • Expend 1 use of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbclcChannelDiv]{Channel Divinity} (Clerics) or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbpdnChannelDiv]{Channel Divinity} (Paladins) while laying hands on Agraband.

  • Issue 1 dose of @UUID[Item.ISmlHk1P0U5poOgY]{M’abb Salts} to Agraband as an inhalant.

Alternately, if Agraband becomes the target of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDream00000]{Dream} spell, he automatically succeeds on his associated Wisdom save.

In all likelihood, this is the first time the characters have encountered a Soulbound character's Lesser Soulmark. Naturally, they may not instinctively know if they have useful skills at their disposal — or whether they can help at all. Thus, a few corresponding methods of discovery are detailed in "Bedside Manner" below.

If they act quickly, the characters can perform certain physical and metaphysical examinations to help steer them towards an action that could aid Agraband.

Bedside Manner

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check is confident in the ability of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCalmEmotio]{Calm Emotions} spell to help stem the tide of psychic episodes such as this.

  • Result of 20+: The character also trusts in the efficacy of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDream00000]{Dream} spell to attempt to counteract the Lesser Soulmarks' adverse effects.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill religion 16]] check is confident in the ability of a cleric or paladin's @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbclcChannelDiv]{Channel Divinity} class feature to help neutralize Agraband's current ailments.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge undeath]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Any character who possesses at least one dose of @UUID[Item.ISmlHk1P0U5poOgY]{M’abb Salts} and succeeds on a [[/skill medicine 16]] or [[/skill nature 16]] check is aware of the rare mineral's ability to counteract a small array of psychic and spiritual maladies.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The Bard Awakens

If Agraband is left undisturbed, his nightmares continues for the remainder of its duration, and Agraband suffers all negative effects of the Lesser Soulmark as described in the rules for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.pFxI6eScKqZbfT2Q]{Soulbound} in the Player Characters section of the Player's Guide. If the characters attempt to wake Agraband without a successful intervention, the apparition persists until he wakes of his own accord. Read the following:

Agraband Swift jumps awake with a shriek.

Wait! … Wait …

Drenched in sweat and eyes wide with fear, he struggles to catch his breath.

I beheld a nightmarish vision, a harrowing reminder of our incident in the Smokerie. Were it not a dream, I'd tell you it was as real as the very air we breathe.

Alternately, if the characters manage to successfully intervene, read the following:

Your efforts to remedy Agraband's plight appear to be somewhat successful, as you can plainly see the apparition dissipate, retreating back into the bard's sleeping body. Just then, he startles from his slumber and regards you with a measure of bewildered anxiety.

What happened? Why are you all looking at me like that?

Medical Examinaitons

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill medicine 13]] check is able to confirm that Agraband's wound hasn't changed in size or appearance since the encounter at Traveler's Rest, despite the strange luminous pulsations that occurred during his nightmare.

  • Result of 18+: By gauging the intensity of Agraband's psychic trauma (or lack thereof), the character can also successfully estimate the range of damage a Lesser Soulmark like this one could cause in the future.

A Conversation with Agraband

If and when Agraband is woken up from his troubled slumber, he's notably harrowed by the situation, but he's willing to talk about the incident as he slowly regains consciousness. Topics he's willing to discuss include (but are not limited to):

  • The imagery of the nightmare, which involved a horrific and phantasmagoric version of the incident at The Pit Trap.

  • The current state of discomfort associated with his mortal wound, which is notably minuscule and of no immediate concern.

  • Reasonable courses of action to help mitigate the damage another nightmare could cause.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check validates the honesty of Agraband's accounts.

Specific dialogue options for the aforementioned talking points are detailed below; and while Agraband is willing to discuss the issue with some measure of fastidiousness, he's also eager to have a few moments to himself, where he can collect his thoughts in silence after such a harrowing incident.

Your nightmare?

Agraband's eyes grow heavy with remembrance as he recollects the images of his dream.

We were back at that infernal Pit Trap, you and I. But the dance floor — once an oasis of revelry — was a sea of monstrous faces and endless shadows. Jorey was there on the balcony, alongside his hero, and they were carving the limbs off a young dancer like … slices of cake. The room was so hot, but I felt so impossibly cold. And as I made my way across that bedeviled room, I felt a tugging sensation behind me.

I turned to look back, and saw myself standing there, as if I hadn't moved an inch since the dream began. Just then, a horrible laceration streaked its way across my throat. And as I stared into my own eyes, horrified, I clutched at the wound in my chest. A moment later, I woke to see you standing over me. But I can still feel the chill of that shadow-haunted air …

Your wound?

Agraband runs his fingers lightly across his lambent scar, reflecting on the odd nature of it.

It's strange … even though this wound persists and sheds its curious light, I feel no pain from it. I'll never quite forget the sting of Zira's dagger, though. And the pain of Jorey's betrayal.

That's a wound I fear may never heal …

What next?

Perhaps I should stay awake for a while and collect my thoughts. Thank you for your timely assistance, friends. It seems we may want to actually lean upon the madcap wisdom of Conaris Haid, as our friends at Traveler's Rest were so keen to suggest.

I fear the High Priest of Sockets has a reputation that precedes him, however, and gaining his trust on these matters may be easier said than done.

Formal Investigations

If the party is inspired to seek answers about Agraband's apparition (as it relates to his condition or as a novel supernatural phenomenon), the traditional methods of gathering information will only get them so far. Ultimately, they'll need to make their way to @UUID[Actor.UEN4Lxa3qDqOAS5B]{Conaris Haid} at the Temple of Sockets for [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessSockets]] to find out what's really going on behind Agraband's undying nature.

Hitting the Books

Attempts to study the nature of Agraband's condition in a formal capacity can lead the characters to interesting places like the Old City Library and the Librarium of Spectra in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.iphMPgtJv5eQjGaR]{Scholar's Nook}, or the esoteric libraries of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.SeNNZfhn77kJqUl0]{All-Fable Keep}.

However, these efforts are ultimately unfruitful, as the emergence of Soulbound on Ember is a contemporary occurrence.

Word on the Street

Any character who spends at least one hour searching an appropriately busy section of town for rumors and succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 12]] check is pointed towards the various temples in Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.XUn8UELVkQmnCI78]{Temple Ward} or @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.aLXuhuWQdislrPnJ]{Numinous Shrines} districts.

  • Result of 17+: The recommendation is for the Temple of Sockets, with a personal referral for the High Priest Conaris Haid.

Concluding the Event

No matter the result of this encounter, the party is free to continue their long rest (which should be a relatively uneventful one, per GM discretion). But the threat of another soul-sundering nightmare lingers, and will continue to do so until the party has helped Agraband settle his so-called unfinished business with Jorey.

Next Steps

Due to Agraband's Soulbound condition and the nature of his eponymous unfinished business, this event has a chance to repeat each time the party takes a long rest until they complete the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessUnderworks]] event.
