The [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessThayloc]] event is now likely to take place as the characters traverse the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.rzME5gXmbZ2zvqq5]{Ordain Flats}.
Answers From On High.soverview: Per the recommendation from Thessandra and the Cindarics of Traveler's Rest, the party visits the Temple of Sockets in search of a deeper understanding of Agraband's supernatural plight. The High Priest of Sockets, a scatterbrained cleric named Conaris Haid, will certainly have some insight to share after he completes the day's ceremonies — but only if the characters can manage to navigate the cagey responses of his aloof and meandering conversation.
Answers From On High.sexposition:
A somber moment awaits you as you enter the temple sanctuary, where a small group of people are solemnly gathered around a funeral dais. The mourners look upon the scene with misty eyes, dressed in their finest dark-hued garments. A few of these sorrowers appear to be knightly soldiers clad in polished bronze armor, maintaining a stoic vigil from behind the sad-eyed civilians — tradespeople and next-of-kin, judging by the look of their young faces and makeshift funeral garb. A solitary figure dressed in the gold and crimson robes of a Cindaric Sage stands nearby, observing with reverence and intent.

Upon the dais, you spy a deceased human male clad in bronze mail like that of the the soldiers. This elderly warrior's long gray hair has been lovingly styled around his pauldrons, and a jagged silver broadsword lays at his side. Just then, a short old priest in tattered robes moves into position amidst the throng, taking an overtly ceremonial stance as he does. The mourners that aren't completely lost in their grief look towards the wizened clergyman a measure of comfort or inspiration in their eyes.

As you take stock of this austere tableau, you catch the eye of a younger priest in gray robes nearby, who sidles up towards your group before offering a few hushed words in greeting.

Welcome to the Temple of Sockets. My name is Acolyte Eston, Eston Veld. Do you know the deceased?
Answers From On High.ssummary: We journeyed to the Temple of Sockets in Ordain for a word with the High Priest, a scatterbrained cleric named Conaris Haid. After some coercion, we managed to convince the aloof clergyman to share some insights about Agraband's strange condition with us. Haid provided us with a lecture on Soulbound — humanoids whose souls cling to their mortal forms after death — and explained what this means for our friend and his so-called unfinished business with Jorey.

Game Day.name: Game Day
Game Day.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration and social event tasks the party with gathering some timely information at Grand Kalion Stadium in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}, where they'll attend a session of the local "Solar Games" featuring @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero} and the Undaunted. In this event, the characters can:

  • Gain entry to Grand Kalion Stadium, where Zira and the Undaunted are scheduled to compete against another team in the gladiatorial Solar Games.

  • As attendees, gather information about Zira and the Undaunted, including the names and locations of two people formerly tied to Zira's inner circle.

  • Collect additional rumors about Zira and the Undaunted, which may or may not prove useful throughout the investigation to come.

Prerequisites

@UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} must be a member of the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party} for this event to occur.

For Ticket Holders Only

Although they can scrounge for a modicum of information outside the stadium walls, the characters will need to gain proper access to the Solar Games by procuring a ticket for all attendees. While purchasing tickets from the box office is the most conventional route, various methods of obtaining the tickets are available to the party, as described below.

Rules & Regulations

The following set of rules and regulations guide the day-to-day business at Grand Kalion Stadium, which holds upwards of 20,000 people in its tiered seating.

  1. The cost of entry to the Solar Games is 2 gp per adult attendee. Tickets for attendees under the age of 14 are only 1 gp, and children must be supervised at all times.

  2. Weapons and arcane accoutrements must be checked at the front gate with the Security Office. Attendees are given a ticket that corresponds to the locker containing their possessions.

  3. Violence in the stands and adjoining facilities is not allowed. There is no second strike. Violators are promptly ejected by a contingency of Stadium Security staff. Treat Stadium Security as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmGuardCaptain00]{Guard Captains}.

  4. Gambling on events is not precisely forbidden, but there is no formal sportsbook maintained by Grand Kalion Stadium or its affiliates.

The Solar Games are not the only event at Grand Kalion Stadium, but they are perhaps the most popular. The Solar Games take place twice a week, on Wednesdays and Fridays, with sets of matches typically starting at Noon and 3pm.

Box Office Banter

The Grand Kalion Stadium box office is currently supervised by the excitable Holden Borios (Chaotic Good, Ordani Signborn, he/him), a kid-at-heart cashier who has outstanding rapport with younger fans thanks to his obsession with tall tales. Although common when it comes to his social status, treat Holden as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.actors24.Actor.mmNoble000000000]{Noble} in terms of stats.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 18]] or [[/skill persuasion 18]] check is able to spin a tale convincing enough to earn them a 50% discount, requiring the paltry sum of 1 gp for entry.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

  • Intimidation tactics will result in the swift arrival of two or more Stadium Security guards.

A fan of unheard stories, Holden Borios is a rather chatty clerk, and is happy to talk with the characters for a brief moment (as long as they don't hold up the line for very long). Topics of conversation include:

  • Some basic information about the Solar Games.

  • Zira Hestidero and The Undaunted, reigning champs of the Solar Games.

  • Their challengers, a team from Cutter's Lane known as "Cutter's Crushers."

  • Grand Kalion Stadium fun facts.

A successful [[/skill insight 13]] check is all it takes to confirm the authenticity of Holden's conversation points, and suggests an overall demeanor of honesty and kindness.

About the Solar Games?

A look of excitement crosses the Signborn clerks' youthful face, and his four arms begin punctuating the conversation with broadly-animated gestures.

Now, some folks prefer the simplicity of Fastball, or the majesty of the Crown's Cup. Personally, I'm a big fan of the Solar Games. The story goes, after Arcus Kalion retired, he sat down with a few of the Anachraenum's most esteemed strategists to come up with the Solar Games — which are as close as you can get to a dungeon crawl without the dungeon or its toothy denizens. No beasts, no bullshit. Just one neighborhood team versus another, running the modular gauntlet as the people's gladiators. What. A. Rush!

About the Undaunted?

Ah, yes. The champions of the realm. "The team you love to hate."

They're good at what they do, there's no denying that. Zira's just a little … aggressive, for my tastes. I look at it this way: as long as the audience is happy and nobody really gets hurt, I don't care how unsportsmanlike a match gets. Unfortunately, the Undaunted have a habit of crossing that line every once in a while. Maybe that's why the roster changes so often …

About Cutter's Crushers?

The Crushers are probably in-over-their-heads today. They're a proud bunch of athletes, raised by hard-working families in Cutter's Passage. So, just like The Undaunted, they've got something to prove out there. But the main difference between the two is that the Crushers, as brawny as they are, lack the speed — and outright brutality — that Zira's Undaunted have at their disposal. And Ned Graves, the Crushers captain, is a bit of a lout. Good guy, but dumb as a rock. Needless to say, all bets are on The Undaunted today.

He casts a look past you at the line of would-be ticket buyers, which has slowly gathered length since your conversation started.

About Grand Kalion Stadium?

Using all four arms, the Signborn clerk gestures broadly at the sprawling facility surrounding him.

"Grand Kalion Stadium is an architectural marvel, designed to host a variety of events and entertainment spectacles. With a seating capacity that rivals the largest arenas in the known world, the stadium features state-of-the-art magic and technology, including a dynamic scoreboard and sound systems that enhance the spectating experience."

At least, that's what the brochure says.

He tosses you a wink and a smile, snorting beneath his breath at the pedantic humor.

Check it out for yourselves. Only two gold pieces a head!

Scouting the Perimeter

Characters who attempt to gain more insight about their surroundings here outside the stadium can do so by spending a few moments inspecting the facade and its patrons.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check while observing the stadium exterior is able to notice the following:

  • The burgundy and gray sign that reads "The Undaunted" appears slightly sun-bleached and weather-stained. A longer look suggests it's been intermittently defaced by spiteful missiles of eggs or rotten vegetables (however expertly cleaned and maintained).

  • The sound of some kind of pre-show can be heard echoing from within the stadium, and the crowd of thousands roars with equally raucous measures of cheers and jeers each time The Undaunted are mentioned.

  • Result of 17+: The character notices a group of three @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani Cityfolk} pre-teens helping another of their ilk sneak in through the front gate by providing a worthy (and absurd) distraction.

Ticket Snatchers

Alternately, one or more of the characters can attempt to gain illicit access to the Solar Games by purloining a ticket or sneaking in.

A successful [[/skill investigation 15]] check is necessary to first identify an adequate mark (i.e. target) for ticket theft, followed by a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 15]] check to actually steal the ticket.

  • Characters have @Advantage[2] on this check if one or more allies succeeds on a [[/skill performance 13]] check to provide a worthy distraction.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill stealth 20]] check is able to sneak their way into the busy stadium without actually presenting a ticket.

  • Small and Tiny characters have advantage on this check.

  • Characters have @Advantage[2] on this check if one or more allies succeeds on a [[/skill performance 15]] check to provide a worthy distraction.

Gathering Information: Stadium Exterior

The party can attempt to gather additional information about Zira Hestidero and The Undaunted outside the stadium (along with other information relevant to the tasks at hand). However, the details available here are rather limited, as most of the informants are already located inside.

Any character who spends at least 15 minutes attempting to gather information outside the stadium and succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check is able to round up one of the following rumors (roll [[/roll 1d4]] to determine which):

  1. The Undaunted have a reputation for playing exceptionally rough, pushing their opponents (and the rules) to the limit.

  2. Zira Hestidero is known for burning bridges, and has lost a few friends on her way to the top.

  3. Cutter's Crushers are a decent team with several wins under their belts, but they play a slow and deliberate game. They're outclassed today when it comes to speed.

  4. Ned Graves is the son of a nepotistic landlord named Carson Graves, who owns several buildings in The Smokerie where The Undaunted are from.

  • Result of 18+: The character is also referred to a regular attendee of some renown inside, a local Solar Games historian of sorts named Dani Brax (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Kivahr, she/they), who might be able to provide them with better information about the two teams.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Game On!

Stepping into the stadium proper, you're engulfed by a sea of auditory and olfactory sensations — from the undulating cacophony of the crowd, to the ozone smell of magitech on the field.

At the northern end of the arena, you spy Zira Hestidero and a quartet of Undaunted adepts, who circle their positions on the starting platform like hyenas eyeballing a juicy carcass. To the south, five athletes clad in blue-and-white take their own places on a matching rostrum, shrouded in conspicuous apprehension.

A sprawling obstacle course connects these two starting platforms — rife with hazards, traps, and pedestals bearing various polearms. At the center of the arena, a luminous orb fashioned into a likeness of the spirit moon hovers above a suspended dais.

Scouting the Interior

Characters who attempt to gain more insight about their surroundings here outside the stadium can do so by spending a few moments inspecting the facade and its patrons.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check while observing the stadium interior is able to notice the following:

  • With a great deal of certainty, @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I]{Jorey Swift} is nowhere to be seen.

  • Roving Vendors weave their way through the crowd at regular intervals, offering an array of food, drink, and souvenirs (for what are sure to be inflated prices).

  • In the arena, Zira's Undaunted have already established dominance over the Crushers, one of whom is bleeding from a light head wound.

  • Result of 17+: An exceptionally loud contingency of fans clad in Undaunted team colors occupies a section of the risers on the east side of the stadium. Towards the front, a burly Kivahr woman holds court for a throng of other attendees who follow her backseat coaching with enthusiasm.

  • A character using a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagSpyglass100]{Spyglass} or similar item has @Advantage[2] on this check.

Gathering Information: Stadium Interior

If they're interested in doing so, the party can attempt to gather additional information about Zira Hestidero and The Undaunted inside the stadium (along with other information relevant to the tasks at hand).

Any character who spends at least 15 minutes attempting to gather information inside the stadium and succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check is able to round up one of the following rumors (roll [[/roll 1d4]] to determine which):

  1. The Undaunted have a reputation for playing exceptionally rough, pushing their opponents (and the rules) to the limit.

  2. Zira Hestidero is known for burning bridges, and has lost a few friends on her way to the top.

  3. Cutter's Crushers are a decent team with several wins under their belts, but they play a slow and deliberate game. They're outclassed today when it comes to speed.

  4. Ned Graves is the son of a nepotistic landlord named Carson Graves, who owns several buildings in The Smokerie where The Undaunted are from.

  • Result of 18+ or a total of 3 successes: The character is also referred to a regular attendee of some renown inside, a Solar Games historian named Dani Brax, who might be able to provide them with better information about the two teams. She always sits on the east side of the stadium on the front row.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge intrigue]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

The party can attempt to repeat this Intelligence (Investigation) check up to a total of 8 times (representing the duration of the match). When the match is over, the boisterous crowd pours out of the stadium like a flood, rife with the celebration and scorn of twenty-thousand fans.

A Conversation with Dani Brax

Once the party is successfully informed of the local Solar Games historian, they can track her down after a few moments of searching near the easternmost section of the arena's front row seats.

Dani Brax (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Kivahr, she/they) is a crude and jocular forty-something with nothing to lose other than her attention on the arena. Although she roots for several of the local teams that compete in the Games (and appreciates their disparate qualities), Dani has a perverse interest in violence, which puts The Undaunted in high (if fractious) esteem.

The first character to succeed on a [[/skill deception 15]], [[/skill intimidation 17]], or [[/skill persuasion 15]] check is able to convince Dani to share some of her insider knowledge about the Solar Games, including the following details:

  • The address of an upstart forge in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c]{Smokerie}, operated by a former Undaunted athlete named @UUID[Actor.9AXW4Yr8ON5V6SGj]{Brackus von Tet}, who went into early retirement for reasons unknown.

  • The name of Zira's estranged lover, a mystic in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.F7b8e10Thlz19yxw]{Orchard Lanes} known as @UUID[Actor.V12wT5KF8sosFLvW]{Helice Korsos}, who provides arcame spellcasting services from her home office.

  • A few details about Zira and her teammates, including some of their favorite arena tactics and Ku'arta's influence on their style.

  • [[/path ShardGodDevotee]] and [[/knowledge warfare]] characters have advantage on these checks, capable of appealing to Dani's enthusiasm for tactics and eldritch lore surrounding The Undaunted.

  • If the characters looted a @UUID[Item.eQCvpFcKsAFW8Tku]{Sash of the Undaunted} during the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessSearch]] event, they can bribe Dani with the item for an automatic success.

What do you know about Zira?

I know she's about five-foot-eight of "grade-A ass-kicker." Quite a few of us think she's the best athlete to ever run the gauntlet. I might be inclined to agree. Of course, Arcus Kalion fans might disagree. I know pretty much what everyone knows about Zira Hestidero: she's an underdog from The Smokerie who turned out to be a savant when it comes to hazard sports.

She's brutal, smart, and gorgeous. What more could you ask for in a Solar Games all-star?

The retired athlete?

The roster is a little light this season. One of my favorite players is missing, a bruiser named Brackus von Tet. I hear he set up shop as a smithy in the Smokerie on Chateau Lane, putting those big mitts of his to work forging arms and armor. A waste of talent if you ask me. No idea why he left the team, but it's a loss.

Zira's old flame?

To be clear, I think people's business is their own. But those two were a dynamite couple. Helice Korsos is a charming young woman. And Zira speaks for herself. But together? Man … Hotter than Ragen's insides. Zira loved parading her warlock girl around on game day. But that all changed a while back. Helice keeps to her shop in Orchard Lanes. Nobody's seen her around here in months, and the speculation is all reasonable, respectable stuff. Idle gossip, you know the kind. I wish them both the best.

Ku'arta's influence on the Solar Games?

What can I say? The God of Torment's patronage is a worthy addition to the lineup here. Let's face it: the Solar Games are called "The Solar Games" for a reason. Just look at how they're controlling the field out there … To the victor go the spoils, and victory is traditionally earned in this arena by wits, speed, and whatever it takes to win.

For Zira, that means a few boons from a shard god from time to time. And The Undaunted are careful to avoid breaking the rules — well … maybe not careful, but they do tend to actually avoid breaking them somehow. There's a fine line between ripe and rotten, my old man used to say. Zira likes to ride that line here in the arena. And it's damn good spectacle, if you ask me.

Concluding the Event

If the characters managed to successfully gather information about one or both of Zira Hestidero's former allies, they can follow up on those leads by investigating the respective neighborhoods of those named associates.

Next Steps

From here, the party can either visit @UUID[Actor.9AXW4Yr8ON5V6SGj]{Brackus von Tet}'s forge in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c]{Smokerie} district for [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessTeammate]], or journey to the home office of @UUID[Actor.V12wT5KF8sosFLvW]{Helice Korsos} in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.F7b8e10Thlz19yxw]{Orchard Lanes} for [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessLover]].

Each of these NPCs will have two relevant pieces of information for the party, including how to locate the secret entrance of Zira Hesitdero's subterranean hideout back here in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}.
Game Day.soverview: In search of Jorey Swift, the party journeys to Grand Kalion Stadium in Arena Ridge to gather information about Zira Hestidero and the team of brazen thrill-seekers known as The Undaunted. Here, they'll witness a sporting event where Zira and her comrades ride roughshod over the competition with a spectacular display of Ku'arta's arcane patronage. During the game, the party can scout the Stadium grounds for details about Zira and her cohorts by speaking with the locals and taking in the sights.
Game Day.sexposition:
A menagerie of sounds assails you as you navigate the streets leading up to Grand Kalion Stadium, where a cacophony of white noise roars throughout the entire neighborhood. Half of Ordain must be packed into the arena, you muse, as you take note of the absolute wall of commotion that awaits — a tapestry of cheering fans, bickering gamblers, diligent hawkers, and panhandling bards. Indeed, you can pick out the sound of at least three different melodies bouncing around the stadium exterior, where ticket holders eagerly line up for entrance through the main gate.

You spy a box office nearby, a small edifice built into the side of the arena, where a jaunty attendant barks offers to the newly-arriving patrons. Countless notices, handbills, and posters adorn the walls surrounding this enclosure. Meanwhile, a large pair of colorful wooden signs hangs above the stadium's front gate. Painted in colors of burgundy and gray, the sign on the left reads: "The Undaunted" with the phrase "Champions 2522-2523" inscribed below. And the sign on the right, marked by colors of blue and white, reads: "Cutter's Crushers," with no subscript or dates beneath.

As you gaze upon this engrossing scene of people coming and going, the voice of an announcer rises above the din inside the stadium, accompanied by the fanfare of brass horns. It sounds like the day's events are about to begin.
Game Day.ssummary: We attended a session of the Solar Games at Grand Kalion Stadium in Arena Ridge, where we saw Zira Hestidero and her Undaunted teammates win a triumphant victory against their opponents. As the game continued, we managed to track down some information relevant to our quest, including the names and locations of two former contacts of Ziras: Brackus von Tet in the Smokerie, and Helice Korsos in Orchard Lanes. Perhaps these erstwhile associates will have some details for us.

Running the Gauntlet.name: Running the Gauntlet
Running the Gauntlet.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This exploration and combat event challenges the party to explore the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl]{Kalion Stadium Underworks}, which serves as the clandestine headquarters of the warlock @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero} and her surreptitious cult dedicated to the shard god @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Explore the Kalion Stadium Underworks in search of the Undaunted hideout.

  • Either sneak past or subdue various members of the Undaunted and their minions.

  • Discover a lost temple to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta}.

  • Reveal the truth b ehind Zira Hestidero's terrible pursuit of eldritch knowledge and survive a deadly encounter with the loathsome @UUID[Actor.cTvZKcxTxhqQE1Su]{Grim Assembly}.

  • Determine the fate of @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I]{Jorey Swift} alongside the other surviving Undaunted.

Prerequisites

@UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} must be a member of the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party} for this event to occur.

Area Walkthrough

The party begins their exploration of the area in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.C7cZROcerETNtVqJ]{Entrance Hall} located at the northeastern corner of the map. Refer primarily to the details provided in that area walkthrough, although note a few key moments during exploration where event-specific gameplay occurs that is presented only on this page:

  1. In the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.Hm9ku5muMPilfUuG]{Chamber of Bargains}, the party may undertake @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq.JournalEntryPage.SIebtgR8yFa5TIxN#a-bargain-with-kuarta]{A Bargain with Ku'arta}.

  2. In the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.LfBDELBnhykIyPrg]{Ritual Chamber}, the party may undertake @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq.JournalEntryPage.SIebtgR8yFa5TIxN#a-bargain-with-sha-xotha]{A Bargain with Sha-Xotha}.

  3. After confronting Zira and her Undaunted allies in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.wWT2yqitYzTHNWaR]{Temple Sanctum}, the resolution to this story is realized in @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq.JournalEntryPage.SIebtgR8yFa5TIxN#finishing-the-business]{Finishing the Business} and @UUID[JournalEntry.Un5QH25zAdoxenmq.JournalEntryPage.SIebtgR8yFa5TIxN#eventful-goodbyes]{Eventful Goodbyes}.

Exploring the Underworks

In search of Jorey Swift, the party must explore the hidden headquarters of the Undaunted — a defunct and forgotten training facility deep beneath @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge} known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl]{Kalion Stadium Underworks}. Here, beyond monuments to fallen champions and a gauntlet designed to test the hopeful, a hidden temple to Ku'arta has gone moldering and forgotten for centuries. Until now.

If the party can survive the lair’s denizens and its handful of magical and mechanical gauntlets, they’ll arrive just in time to interrupt a profane ritual conducted by Zira in the temple's inner sanctum. A full description of the location can be found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl]{Kalion Stadium Underworks} area walkthrough.

A Bargain with Ku'arta

When exploring the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.Hm9ku5muMPilfUuG]{Chamber of Bargains}, the party may have an opportunity to strike a bargain with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.2t5fcw7ns01LpvaH]{Ku'arta} directly who has a vested interest in the resolution of this tale. If the party (or any member thereof) forms such a pact, mark the following outcome as completed and award attunement advancement.

[[/outcome pactKuarta]]

Luxarum Attunement: Ku'arta's Bargain

Any character who decided to adopt Ku'arta as their warlock patron advances their [[/attunement emberLuxarum +1 unfinishedBusinessUnderworksKuarta]] at the conclusion of the event.

A Bargain with Sha-Xotha

When exploring the @UUID[JournalEntry.slIRkmNoRi3qfYIl.JournalEntryPage.LfBDELBnhykIyPrg]{Ritual Chamber}, the party may have an opportunity to undertake a profane communion with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.VUhtOxDvWc3I7pY2]{Sha-Xotha}. Should the party (or any member thereof) establish such a pact, mark the following outcome as completed and award attunement advancement.

[[/outcome pactAbyssal]]

Abyss Attunement: Sha-Xotha's Bargain

Any character who decided to adopt Sha-Xotha as their warlock patron advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 unfinishedBusinessUnderworksShaxotha]] at the conclusion of the event.

Finishing the Business

Before concluding the quest, record the final outcome that best corresponds to the fate of @UUID[Actor.TSMrh51VyKrdMz1I]{Jorey Swift} and award attunement progression depending on which path was token.

Heart Attunement: Jorey Redeemed

If the party convinced Jorey to turn his back on the Undaunted and leave his worship of Ku'arta behind, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 unfinishedBusinessUnderworksRedeemed]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome reconcile]]

Cora Attunement: Jorey Undaunted

If the party failed to convince Jorey to turn his back on the Undaunted, each character advances their [[/attunement emberHeart +1 unfinishedBusinessUnderworksUndaunted]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome separate]]

The Death of Jorey Swift

If Jorey Swift is slain during the course of the encounter with Zira Hestidero and her minions, Agraband's business is finished all the same — but the loss of Jorey is an unfortunate circumstance that may shadow the party for years to come.

[[/outcome death]]

Eventful Goodbyes

With the existential cause of his Soulbound affliction resolved, Agraband is now free to relinquish his mortality and release the troubled spirit from his Soulmarked body. Naturally, he will want to share a few parting words with the characters (and his nephew Jorey, depending on the event's outcome).

A Final Word with Agraband

This moment of goodbyes is a somber one, with Agraband offering up a few bittersweet remembrances of significant times he shared with the party, good and bad alike.

After one final exchange between Agraband and the party, read the following aloud:

With a forlorn sigh, Agraband unslings his kithara and begins plucking a final tune, some bittersweet melody you'd swear you recognize from somewhere — but that you know in your heart to be novel to this fateful moment. Agraband's tenor is a strange but welcome sound here, where light and hope must dare to roam.

For foes and friends, a song begins, a stirring in my heart
Down roads untold, our story folds, from epilogue to start

The bard offers you a small nod and turns away, meandering as he continues to play his tune throughout the dimly-lit chamber. The light of his wound swells to an intensity heretofore unseen, enveloping Agraband in a bright and otherworldly illumination.

In a moment, he's gone, disappearing before your very eyes like the last rays of a dying sunset. But you can almost swear, if only for an instant, that the sound of that final song lingers on the wind. You wonder if it always will.

Concluding the Event

The completion of Agraband's so-called unfinished business and his subsequent demise result in the simultaneous conclusion of the event and the quest.

Milestone

Completing this event earns the party a @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, potentially advancing them in level.

Next Steps

Once the party leaves the Kalion Stadium Underworks after Agraband's death, the event is concluded and the quest is complete.
Running the Gauntlet.soverview: In search of Jorey Swift and vengeance for Agraband, the party journeys to the Kalion Stadium Underworks in Arena Ridge to explore the clandestine headquarters of Zira Hestidero's cult of Ku'arta. If they can survive the assembly of dangerous traps and Undaunted cultists who call this place home, the characters can potentially save Jorey from an untimely death at the hands of a malevolent creature of the Abyss known as the Grim Assembly. Depending on the party's actions, they can potentially convince Jorey to abandon the Undaunted, turn him further away from Agraband, or lose him altogether as a victim of the eldritch outsider's deadly wrath.
Running the Gauntlet.sexposition: After stumbling through a mile of subterranean sprawl beneath Arena Ridge, the dull marble in your possession begins to emanate a soft white light, which grows brighter the further you follow its uncanny lead. Before you know it, you find yourself at the threshold of a well-lit vestibule — an entrance hall of some kind that beckons you with burning sconces and braziers of perpetual flame.
Running the Gauntlet.ssummary: We explored the Kalion Stadium Underworks beneath Arena Ridge, where we encountered Zira Hestidero and her cult of adherents to Ku'arta. Unbeknownst to these acolytes, Zira planned to sacrifice them to a hideous creature of the Abyss — which we managed to defeat, thanks to our circumstances and wits. The completion of this task has resolved our friend Agraband's unfinished business, and his soul can now journey to Mort'oliss unhindered.

The Old Flame.name: The Old Flame
The Old Flame.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social event takes the party to the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.F7b8e10Thlz19yxw]{Orchard Lanes} district in southwestern Ordain, in search of a mystic known as @UUID[Actor.V12wT5KF8sosFLvW]{Helice Korsos}, who is said to be the former lover of @UUID[Actor.hsUL3azeNLhXi2Aj]{Zira Hestidero}. In this event, the characters can:

  • Visit Helice Korsos' home in Orchard Lanes, where the warlock of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.RPVn1KLLcutCzYcv]{Vesper} runs a small business as a spellcaster and fortune-teller for hire.

  • Gain Helice's allegiance by proving the virtuousness of their intentions, via both their conversation skills and one of the mystic's own auguries.

  • Learn two key details about the adventure ahead: the location of The Undaunted's hidden lair beneath Grand Kalion Stadium, and a tactic that can help them defeat Zira Hestidero in battle.

This encounter utilizes the "Mystic's Apartment" configuration of the @UUID[Scene.emberVistaOrdInt]{Ordain Interiors} vista.

Prerequisites

@UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} must be a member of the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party} for this event to occur.

The Korsos Connection

When the event begins, Agraband and the party have arrived at the home of Helice Korsos, a spellcaster-for-hire known for her astute divinations and abilities as an empath. Helice is also the scorned lover of Zira Hestidero, and is all-too-familiar with some of her former partner's secrets. If the characters can convince Helice that their motives are pure, the compassionate mystic may provide them with some helpful details about how to find The Undaunted's secret underground lair.

@Embed[Actor.V12wT5KF8sosFLvW]

A Conversation with Helice

The party is here in search of details about Zira Hestidero and The Undaunted, including precisely how and where to find them. However, Helice Korsos has no intention of telling perfect strangers about the peculiarities of her private life. If the characters want to learn about the mystic's past with Zira, they'll need to convince her to share her most intimate details.

Helice is used to running a business out of her home, and is willing to entertain the standard array of questions one might expect from a potential customer. Topics of such general conversation include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • The characters themselves (including Agraband) and any needs they might have for professional spellcasting services.

  • Current affairs in Ordain, with an emphasis on Orchard Lanes.

  • A brief account of her history as a spellcaster, with a focus on her current pact with the Casia known as Vesper, but including details about her time as a servant of Ku'arta.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check is confident of the honesty behind Helice's intentions, and understands the inviting warmth of this place to be an integral part of both her nature and her business.

  • Result of 18+: There is a slight element of suspicion in Helice's eyes, countered by the assurance of her body language. She feels safe, even when a group of strangers is in her home.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check is drawn to various elements around the room: the wares and components that line the shelves, the crystal ball situated on the rear table, the curious lantern overhead, and the choker that hangs upon Helice's neck.

  • Result of 19+: The lantern and the necklace of are particular interest, with subtle runes of Conjuration and Abjuration magics decorating them respectively.

  • Subsequently, a successful [[/skill insight 15]] or [[/skill investigation 15]] check identifies the necklace as a potential gift or heirloom from Zira, based on how Helice can be seen absent-mindedly touching it each time her former lover's name is mentioned.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on this check.

Additionally, any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell here in Helice's apartment is able to spot the following:

  • Most of the potions, components, and trinkets that line the shelves here subtly radiate the various auras of nearly every arcane tradition known to Ember.

  • The spherical lantern hanging overhead in the room displays the distinct auras of Conjuration and Illusion magics (see "Safety Measures" below for more details).

  • An unassuming Crystal Ball at the back of the room radiates a strong aura of Divination magic.

  • The necklace around Helice's neck radiates a strong aura of Abjuration magic. A successful [[/skill insight 15]] or [[/skill investigation 15]] check identifies the necklace as a potential gift or heirloom from Zira, based on how Helice can be seen absent-mindedly touching it each time her former lover's name is mentioned.

Down to Business

If one or more of the characters ask Helice about her relationship with Zira Hestidero, she's willing to speak on subjects that are public knowledge, but a certain amount of convincing is necessary if the characters want Helice to share the information they seek.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill persuasion 14]] or [[/skill deception 16]] or [[/skill intimidation 18]] check is able to convince Helice that their intentions are aligned with her own (perhaps by explaining the dire situation that awaits Agraband if his business remains unfinished), but they'll still need to pay homage to the spellcaster's services (see "Fortune Favors the Bold" below).

  • Characters with [[/knowledge souls]] and [[/knowledge undeath]] have advantage on this check.

  • If the characters looted a @UUID[Item.eu0SxgfFRnFVvBoJ]{Focus Stone} during the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessSearch]] event, they can present it to Helice for @Advantage[2] on these checks.

  • Alternately, the first character to mention Helice's necklace (with credible supposition of the story behind it) has advantage on these checks.

Some initial answers Helice might provide for certain questions are detailed below, and hint at pertinent information that will only be elucidated upon later.

What can you tell us about Zira and The Undaunted?

A forlorn look crosses the mystic's face, but only for a moment.

Zira. The name I'll never escape. There was a time when the sound of that name could stop by very heart from beating in my chest. But that time has passed.

From the looks on your faces, it was the rumor mill that brought you to my doorstep. But I'm afraid I haven't seen or heard from Zira in well over a year. Her team, her … thugs … are precisely what this city needs them to be: dispensable. That arena is made to grind people into pulp for the amusement of others, and it isn't what I'd precisely call a "good time."

Your history as a warlock?

Indeed. A subject worth discussing with potential customers.

Helice casually adjusts the choker around her neck and motions towards your surroundings.

Vesper's patronage has provided me with a good life, and my connection to her is strong. But I'd also like to think that my own arcane talents are worth the price they command. Life is harsh and unpredictable. Since adolescence, I've sought to lessen the burdens of others with my magic. The struggle need not be so strict and persistent. We're in this together, after all. But, a girl still needs to make a living …

I have a variety of arcane enchantments, illusions, divinations and otherwise at my disposal, if you have the coin to purchase them.

About Ku'arta as an arcane patron?

A mix of regret and discernment cloud her countenance.

In a previous life, I myself made a pact with Ku'arta, the great tormentor. But that pact has been severed for quite some time now, and we're all better for it.

About Vesper as an arcane patron?

Mother Mask can be a tireless inspiration for those who seek the comforts of her embrace; but her Primordial sponsorship comes with its fair share of … unexpectedness. Vesper is a wise, if sardonic, teacher. But then again, I suppose a warlock's connection to their patron is like any intimate relationship — full of cloying specificity and idiomatic regret.

We are all unique individuals, after all, and should be treated as such. I suppose that's part of Vesper's plan for me, the proliferation of that insight, one spell at a time.

The Undaunted's secret lair?

Helice stifles something between a scoff and a chuckle.

If you're looking for secrets about Zira's merry band of rogues, you've come to the wrong warlock. Zira's love of the arena is precisely why she has no place here.

It's massive amphitheater, built upon countless layers of old Ordain. One could get lost down there. Perhaps a divination from Mother Mask is in your near future … if you have the coin, that is.

What Helice Won't Say

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check can readily tell that Helice is holding back some information about her relationship with Zira.

  • Result of 18+: There's likely more to the topic of warlock patrons than Helice currently admits, particularly in regards to her own past with Ku'arta and Zira's current connection to the shard god.

Safety Measures: Magical Lantern Trap

The lantern that hangs overhead in the parlor here is enchanted with a darkness trap (plus a dimension door getaway). When the command word is spoken, the lantern releases the following:

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDarkness00]{Darkness} spell, with the table at the center of the room as the target.

  • The @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDimensionD]{Dimension Door} spell, with Helice as the target.

Helice uses the Dimension Door spell to teleport to a safe location nearby, like a Noticerie house or the front room of the Sweet Reliefs tavern, where she can seek the timely aid of other locals.

Fortune Favors the Bold

Helice has no intentions of sharing her most intimate secrets with the party at this time, but an element of divine intervention (via a message from her fey patron Vesper) is soon to change her mind. First, the characters must enlist Helice's standard spellcasting services — namely, by paying her for an augury or other divination. Unbeknownst to Helice and the party, this straightforward ritual will lead to a revelation.

After the characters have had a moment for pleasantries and to survey their surroundings, read the following aloud:

With a dramatic wave of her hand, Helice conjures a quartet of tiny magical lights, which dance about the room before drawing your attention to a crystal ball located on a rear table. The alluring warlock approaches the arcane relic and speaks:

If you seek answers, then answers we shall find. People travel miles upon miles for a glimpse at Vesper's divinations, and tend to leave with more insight than they brought with them. The prices of my services are standard, but charity has been known to grace this chamber from time to time.

So, what manner of spell can I weave for you? An augury perhaps, if not a pure divination?

A Reading from Helice

If the characters want more information from Helice, they'll need to pay for a professional @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplAugury0000]{Augury} from the warlock.

Helice is willing to reduce the 200 gp price of the spell for any of the following reasons:

  • The first character to succeed on a [[/skill persuasion 16]] or [[/skill deception 16]] check is able to convince Helice that this arcane reading is purely in service to their mutual goals, cutting the price in half to 100 gp. Characters with [[/knowledge rituals]] have advantage on these checks.

  • If the characters looted a @UUID[Item.eu0SxgfFRnFVvBoJ]{Focus Stone} during the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessSearch]] event, they can present it to Helice for a 100 gp discount.

  • Characters with [[/attunement primordis]] Rank 1 are favored by Vesper to benefit from the aid of her warlocks, and Helice is willing to cast the spell for a discount at 100 gp.

  • Characters with [[/attunement primordis]] Rank 2 or higher are cosmically "chosen" by Vesper to benefit from the aid of her warlocks, and Helice is willing to cast the spell for free.

  • Alternately, Helice is willing to accept a trade for a magic item of equal or greater value (with discretion).

Once the terms are settled, Helice begins her Augury ritual. Read the following aloud:

With one hand on her crystal ball, Helice begins to gesticulate with the other, weaving the somatic components of an augury spell as her bracelets jangle upon her lithe wrist. Strange arcane syllables escape her lips, carried by the timeless weight of magical words.

The lights glow dim as the crystal ball begins to seethe with a dull arcane brilliance, and Helice addresses you directly:

Through depths of inner realms we peek to walk upon the path you seek. Tell me, what course of action do you wish to divine with Vesper's wisdom?

After the augury's omen has been revealed to the party, read the following aloud:

Just then, all the lights in the parlor momentarily surge with a brief and blinding intensity before all goes dim. As your eyes adjust to the shaded room, you notice that Helice is caught in some kind of seizure or episode — her eyes roll into the back of her head and she speaks with an otherworldly voice quite unlike her own, a gravelly voice that reminds you of the roar of wildfire:

Guide this bard to paths unseen, inspired by divinity.

The normal light returns to the room, and Helice appears to casually shake off the episode with a deep breath and a knowing nod. She opens her eyes and addresses you once more.

Vesper has offered you a gift of divination. No cost is required for this spell. Tell me, what clarity do you seek as we turn to Mother Mask for answers?

Following the Augury (and her subsequent vision from Vesper), Helice offers to cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDivination]{Divination} spell for free.

Whatever the party's intentions, Agraband speaks up to recommend that they divine one of the following pieces of information during the ritual:

  • If they haven't managed to learn the location of the secret entrance from @UUID[Actor.9AXW4Yr8ON5V6SGj]{Brackus von Tet} during the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessTeammate]] event, the Soulbound bard strongly advises they do so at this time.

  • Alternately, if they already possess a @UUID[Item.IVdSScotnE5HqyPI]{Kalion Underworks Key}, Helice can ask whatever question the characters deem most important to the mission ahead.

Your falling out with Zira?

We met each other as teenagers, orphaned and alone, with hearts full of determination and heads full of daydreams. I saw something in Zira the first time I laid eyes on her. She's … immaculate. But she's also lost, adrift in her own self-righteous ambitions.

We had a few great years together. We shared everything, our hopes, our talents, even our pact with Ku'arta. Looking back now, this thing that brought us closer together would end up being the end of us. The further Zira delved into eldritch lore and forbidden secrets, the less I came to recognize the woman I fell in love with. Victory was more important to her than our relationship; conquest, at any cost. So, I drew a line in the sand, and she walked away. I said goodbye to Ku'arta, and lost my lover along the way.

It's no easy thing, turning your back on a shard god. And I'd wager this never-ending mess with Zira is part of my punishment.

What motivates Zira and The Undaunted?

Zira is motivated by one thing, and one thing alone: power. It's as simple as that. And the impressionable street rats on that team of hers are fools if they believe she holds any true care for them. Ku'arta is called the "God of Torment" for a reason — he's a sick bastard, who would drive an infant to bite its own mother's breast.

And beyond her allegiance to Ku'arta, Zira has an unhealthy obsession with lore and legends about The Shattering. She had a small collection of illicit heirlooms and antiques that she obtained through questionable means, all of which reeked of bad energy. The more of those relics she brought into our home, the more I could discern a madness in her eyes. And this is a lust no lover can satisfy, I assure you.

Where to find The Undaunted's lair?

Helice whispers an incantation while removing one of the marble-shaped gemstones from her necklace, which loses its luster before your very eyes.

The power of Vesper compels us. This stone will light your way.

A @UUID[Item.IVdSScotnE5HqyPI]{Kalion Underworks Key} is now in your possession.

Any other details?

Familiarity breeds contempt, as they say. Zira's hubris is her strongest asset, and her greatest weakness. If you can challenge to her sense of pride, you may be able to manipulate her with some measure of success.

I'd also urge you to use caution when searching any private effects of hers. My Zira loves a good trap.

Obtaining the Kalion Underworks Key

By the end of this conversation, Helice Korsos should hand over the @UUID[Item.IVdSScotnE5HqyPI]{Kalion Underworks Key} to one of the party members.

If the encounter with Helice goes poorly, you may choose to allow the party to attempt to steal the Kalion Underworks Key from her apartment (if they can manage to find it). A successful [[/skill investigation 16]] check is required to locate the locked jewelry box, followed by a successful [[/skill thief 18]] check or [[/skill athletics 22]] check to open it.

Concluding the Event

When the characters are satisfied with the level of detail they've gained from Helice (or become discouraged by their lack thereof), they're free to pursue other leads or follow up on the information they've learned here today.

Next Steps

Thanks to the newfound information from Helice, the party can now locate the secret entrance to Zira Hesitdero's subterranean hideout in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge}, kicking off the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessUnderworks]] event.

If they've yet to do so, the party can also journey to the forge of @UUID[Actor.9AXW4Yr8ON5V6SGj]{Brackus von Tet} in The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.Cbez3Zqmh9sYAp4c]{Smokerie} for [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessTeammate]], where they'll gain corresponding information about The Undaunted's hidden lair.
The Old Flame.soverview: Agraband and the party venture to the Orchard Lanes district to locate and speak with Helice Korsos, Zira Hestidero’s scorned lover from better days. If the characters can suitably convince the lovelorn mystic, she'll share some intimate details of their relationship and Zira’s troubled past — along with directions to The Undaunted's hidden lair beneath Grand Kalion Stadium.
The Old Flame.sexposition:
The cozy cobblestone streets of Orchard Lanes lead you on a roundabout journey through the charming neighborhood, where locals of all stripes linger in relative tranquility compared to some of the busier sections of town. These helpful citizens waste no time directing you to the abode of Helice Korsos, located in the northern shadow of the sagging, aged edifice known as Briarhearth. Here, a three-story townhouse appears to have been converted into apartment dwelling, and a wooden sign above the side door decorated with florid scenes of far-off Primordis reads "The Korsos Connection." A smaller sign in the window proclaiming "Open For Business!" invites you to enter.

A variety of curious odors assail you as Agraband eagerly opens the door — ranging from the crisp scent of ozone, to the soft aroma of rose petals — and you regard a welcoming parlor replete with all the accoutrements of a professional mystic. Before you have time to act, a sultry feminine voice emanates from a back room:

Please, make yourselves at home! I'll be right with you!

In a moment, the proprietor of this place joins you from a nearby room, a striking femme of mixed Human and Nir'ae features clad in loose garments and elegant baubles. If the unfettered charisma radiating from this woman is any indication, this is certainly the same Helice Korsos you seek.

Well, aren't you an assorted lot … Welcome. I am Helice. Tell me: who do I have the privilege of hosting today?

She motions for you to sit as she gathers the tools of her trade, occult items and components that must have been scattered about the room during previous sessions.
The Old Flame.ssummary: We visited the home business of Helice Korsos, a warlock of Vesper and the scorned lover of Zira Hestidero. After some conversation and a paid augury session with Helice (a formidable mystic in her own right), we gained some valuable information about how to find The Undaunted's secret lair beneath Grand Kalion Stadium in Arena Ridge.

Swift Healing.name: Swift Healing
Swift Healing.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This social and exploration event takes place at @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP]{Traveler's Rest} within the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.nS7kj8wZ5eFq6pcy]{Westgate} district of Ordain, where the party attempts to help @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} receive some timely healing after the deadly encounter in [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessSearch]]. In this event, the characters can:

  • Pay for assorted healing services from the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.yBCoSK3v86rKRqrB]{Cindaric Sages} who operate Traveler's Rest, including help for Agraband.

  • Gather some general details about Agraband's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberAncestries0.JournalEntryPage.ip4nuWevdJr8zh5q]{Soulbound} condition, including some brief research in the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.x2EmlUaHS1npWWvO]{Library}.

  • Speak with the various @UUID[Actor.uIDDak2Oq8Qd9Mfx]{Cindaric Sages}, @UUID[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]{Cindaric Adherents}, and patrons of Traveler's Rest in search of useful information.

As the encounter begins, the party will arrive through the doors to the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.jSsBCkof3uze0SCV]{Main Office} of the @UUID[Scene.emberTravlrsRest]{Traveler's Rest} area map, where the Cindaric Adherent on duty can set them on the proper course.

Prerequisites

@UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} must be a member of the @UUID[Actor.EmberParty000000]{Party} for this event to occur.

Aid for Agraband

The party escorts @UUID[Actor.IsfSfKd2S9mIJsyw]{Agraband Swift} to the nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.nS7kj8wZ5eFq6pcy]{Westgate} district, where the healing house known as @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP]{Traveler's Rest} is likely to have the medicines he needs and the professionals to administer them.

When they reach to the location, the party enters via the @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.jSsBCkof3uze0SCV]{Main Office}, where a Cindaric attendant awaits the arrival of visitors and patients in need.

@Embed[Actor.yq8SHGAgAoMg4Tla]

Cindaric Hospitality

The young Cindaric on duty here is Sefton Smythe (Lawful Good, Ordani Human, he/him), a studious-but-scatterbrained Cindaric Adherent who is well on his way to becoming a proper sage. While the party waits for the arrival of a sage, Sefton can assist them with a brief discussion on a variety of topics, included (but not limited to) the following:

  • The services provided at Traveler's Rest.

  • The role of the Cindaric Sages throughout Ordain, including their various bases of operation (like Cindarin Temple and other Healing Houses).

  • His personal journey as a Cindaric, which is actually a family legacy handed down from his father (and his father before him).

Healing Services

Traveler's Rest offers a variety of magical and mundane healing services, including an array of Spellcasting with costs as described in the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbServices00000.JournalEntryPage.mhsrVbdk7Nxzll72]{Lifestyle Expenses} section of the basic rules. Spells the Cindaric Sages are known to cast for their patrons include:

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplResistance]{Resistance}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectPois]{Detect Poison and Disease}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplHealingWor]{Healing Word}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLesserRest]{Lesser Restoration}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplProtection]{Protection from Poison}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbProtectionFro]{Protection from Energy}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDeathWard0]{Death Ward}

Lodging at Traveler's Rest under the benevolent care of the Cindarics provides the benefits of a Comfortable lifestyle at the cost of 3 gp per day.

  • Any character who takes a Long or Short Rest while lodging here gains @Advantage[2] on their next saving throw.

After roughly 3-5 minutes have passed, the party will be joined by an experienced Cindaric Sage named Thessandra Vale (Neutral Good, Ordani Kivahr, she/her), a matronly healer who tends to dish out her timely advice with a heavy dose of pragmatism.

Moments later, another Cindaric steps into the room, bringing an air of calm with her. This lithe Kivahr woman is clad in the fineries of a Cindaric Sage, and she addresses your group with the tranquil assurance of a practiced healer.

Whatever ailments have brought you here, we greet you with open arms and a readiness to serve. Tell me, how can we help you during this time of need?

Agraband dutifully stands and pulls his tunic to one side. The light from his injury spills out into the office, and the sage — at once measured and sedate — grows as wide-eyed and incredulous as young Sefton beside her.

Come with me. Let's take a closer look at you.

@Embed[Actor.uIDDak2Oq8Qd9Mfx]

The Sage's Examination

Thessandra leads Agraband and any interested party members towards the Infirmary, where she helps Agraband lay down for an examination. Sefton aids her in these efforts, while gathering a few medical accoutrements for homegirl's imminent use.

Thessandra's 15-mintue analysis of Agraband's confounding wounds is brief but thorough. Ultimately, she's able to offer very little insight into the precise cause for this rare, supernatural condition. Some key learnings include:

  • After an application of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds} spell (and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplLesserRest]{Lesser Restoration} for safe measure), Agraband's wound is effectively healed.

  • A peculiar aura of radiant magic surrounds Agraband, but it isn't nearly as potent as the nimbus of eldritch energy that would typically identify the undead.

  • With no recourse via physical medicine, Thessandra eventually posits that an alternative solution may be found among the various priests and clerics of Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.XUn8UELVkQmnCI78]{Temple Ward}.

Furthermore, because the Cindarics can't provide more substantial aid to Agraband (with measurable results), they only require a payment of 50 gp for the Cure Wounds spell. The other immediate care they provide him is free of charge.

A few specific dialogue options for Thessandra are provided below.

Your Story?

The sage continues working as she speaks, her eyes on the matter at hand.

Thessandra Vale, at your service. I've been mending wounds here at Traveler's Rest for the better part of six years. And I've never seen anything quite like this …

I make it a point to not ask our patrons too many unnecessary questions about how or why they end up in our care here, but a few details usually go a long way. If you'd like to share.

The silence lingers as she waits for any insight you might have to offer.

Agraband's Wound?

She proceeds to study the bard's injury with supreme focus.

By all accounts, this wound should have been fatal … Your perseverance is a inexplicable conundrum, Master Swift! I've mended your flesh as much as possible, and cast out any lingering poisons, but this luminous scar of yours endures — and is no doubt supernatural in its nature. I fear there is something elusive at work here that my magic can't deter.

Necromancy and Reviled Magic?

She shoots you a sharp glance, full of scrutiny.

Spells that draw upon the power of the Abyss or the corruption of undeath are abhorrent to the natural order of things. They have no place in Ordain, or elsewhere for that matter. I trust you understand the dire perils of necromancy, and the evils it portends.

Other options?

I regret we can't provide you with more explicit answers about this condition of yours, Master Swift. It sits somewhere beyond the keen of our understanding, and I've seen quite a few ailments in my time.

The presence of a radiant aura is most puzzling. Perhaps you might consider a visit to Temple Ward, where the places of worship are full of priests and clerics with greater acumen about such things. Seek out Conaris Haid at the Temple of Sockets, but mind the old fool's madcap ways.

In Pursuit of Answers

During or after Agraband's treatment, the characters can explore Traveler's Rest in search of information — whether in regards to Agraband's condition, or the lingering concern of Jorey's alliance with Zira Hestidero and the Undaunted.

Gathering Information

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check while speaking with the Cindarics or patients of Traveler's Rest can obtain one of the following pieces of information (roll [[/roll 1d4]] to determine):

  1. The Undaunted compete twice a week in the Solar Games at Grand Kalion Stadium: Wednesdays and Saturdays, during daytime hours.

  2. The Undaunted have a reputation for playing exceptionally rough, pushing their opponents (and the rules) to the limit.

  3. The competitions at Grand Kalion Stadium weren't always as civilized as they are now; bloodsport was commonplace in the arena long ago.

  4. Zira Hestidero is known for burning bridges, and has lost a few friends on her way to the top.

Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] and [[/knowledge intrigue]] have advantage on this check.

Hitting the Books

Alternatively, the party can search the various tomes located in the Traveler's Rest @UUID[JournalEntry.Qd9ePDLpB2HcMnyP.JournalEntryPage.x2EmlUaHS1npWWvO]{Library} for medical and/or spiritual answers about Agraband's condition.

Any character who takes at least 30 minutes to search the library and succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check is able to locate one of the following pieces of information, in the following order:

  1. The Elder God @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.WHj7BfBdSACYArYX]{Sockets} created Soul Transference during Creation as he believed souls should move on from their mortal lives, experience an afterlife in @UUID[JournalEntry.xqx0clu8pT4kRxAz.JournalEntryPage.Rn0WQchGPVYCTExP]{Mort'oliss}, and come to terms with their existence before finally passing on to become one with Ember itself.

  2. @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.lEqEFiYkwSvEjmVj]{Elder Gods}, certain @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.6pJu6l3a7RTzcaRM]{Shard Gods}, and the progenitor species of the Inner Realms — @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.4lTtZfLS961MjIST]{Tyraphem}, @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.nXYB7d7ZBsWV1chY]{Fiends} — possess the ability to "claim" souls.

  3. Followers and believers of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.gyNN8Hkjc23LRqsn]{Alar}'s "Eternal Soul" concept maintain that the best way to safeguard the cosmos and an individual experience is to try and live forever instead of moving on after death.

Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] and [[/knowledge souls]] have advantage on this check.

A Word with Agraband

The party will likely wish to confer with their wounded ally before making any decisions about their next steps or possible courses of action. And while Agraband is certainly concerned about his own health, he's more worried about his relationship with Jorey and what the aftermath of the party's encounter at The Pit Trap might have in store for them. Topics that Agraband might wish to discuss at this time include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Whether or not his supernatural wound was somehow caused by Zira herself.

  • Jorey's role in The Undaunted, considering the lengths Zira went to in order to keep him shielded from Agraband.

  • Agraband muses that, if all else fails, a visit to see The Undaunted at their next Solar Games competition might be a suitable course of action.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check is able to verify the legitimacy of Agraband's claims and the honesty of his intentions.

Specific dialogue options for Agraband's post-recovery conversations are detailed below, but one thing persists throughout his ongoing assessment of the situation: a pervading sense of confusion, which grows easier to manage with each new day.

Your wound?

At the mention of his wound, Agraband absent-mindedly reaches to caress the scar tissue with his fingertips, a look of contemplation streaking its way across his furrowed brow.

It's quite strange … the laceration doesn't precisely feel like any wound I've ever suffered before. It doesn't seem to hurt, at least not in a normal way. There is a dull ache, perhaps, but nothing severe.

I recall the flash of a dagger blade, then a spray of blood as Zira did the deed. As experienced as I am with the arcane, I don't recall noticing any spellcraft or similar chicanery. But then again, the ways of illicit nightclub patrons are not my own. Maybe I simply didn't get a proper look at whatever happened up there. But I wonder what other tricks this Zira Hestidero has up her sleeves …

Although the specialists here have come up short with explanations, I personally fear a curse or some other arcane malady has been foisted upon me by that comely scoundrel. I suppose time will tell.

What about Jorey?

I barely got a good look at the lad before the incident. And in the chaos of the moment, I failed to see him leave. Did you get a good look yourselves?

I wonder what I must have done to incur such wrath from the boy. Absence makes the heart grow colder, it seems.

Potential next steps?

Agraband regards his strange wound once more as he addresses you with a small measure of anxiety.

I suppose we should seek answers about this strange affliction, wherever we may find them. If the traditional Cindaric healers of Traveler's Rest can't afford us answers, perhaps an occult specialist or holy dignitary can.

Concluding the Event

Once the party has been granted enough time to scour Traveler's Rest for information, they're free to go about their business — which likely includes further investigation about Agraband's collective plights.

Next Steps

From here, the party has two key options in their pursuit of answers: they can either venture to the Temple of Sockets in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.XUn8UELVkQmnCI78]{Temple Ward} for the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessSockets]], or journey to Grand Kalion Stadium in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.yrVQQP2A4i1H2TNw]{Arena Ridge} (during daytime hours) for the [[/eventState unfinishedBusinessGame]] event.
Swift Healing.soverview: Following Agraband's deadly encounter at The Pit Trap, the party escorts the injured bard to Traveler's Rest in the nearby Westgate district, one of the most esteemed Healing Houses in town. However, conventional Cindaric remedies prove ineffectual at dealing with Agraband's strange and supernatural wound; but, with a little luck or discipline, the party might be able to gather some helpful information before proceeding (including where to look next for more direct answers).
Swift Healing.sexposition:
You tumble through the doorway to the Main Office of Traveler's Rest, where a wide-eyed Cindaric is seated behind a front desk strewn with ledgers, notes, and office supplies. This mop-headed young man regards your group with instant concern, taking a moment to gaze at Agraband's lambent wound in disbelief. Swift immediately adjusts his garments, obscuring the injury once more; and with an eager jolt, the young Cindaric jumps up from his seat and urges you to come inside, stuttering a bit from excitement as he speaks.

W-w-welcome to Traveler's Rest. Y-you look like you could use some help! Please come in, make yourselves as comfortable as possible. One of our sages will be right with you.

The young Cindaric rings a bell on the front desk with alacrity, and its chime sounds throughout the entire Healing House. He then grabs a ledger nearby, along with a quill dipped in burgundy ink, which he holds out for you to take.

My name is Sefton. Please, sign the patient's name here, and we'll make sure we get you settled in.
Swift Healing.ssummary: We took our friend Agraband to Taveler's Rest in Westgate with hopes of treating his deadly injury. However, conventional Cindaric healing proved ineffectual at dealing with our friend's strange and supernatural wound. We must look elsewhere for answers.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

This area walkthrough provides a guide to the "Redwalk Ramble" Scene. It is used in the quest @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0]{Local Color}.

It is part of the larger @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.bfpbRmmyoVF5Ize7]{Redwalk Ramble} district detailed in the gazetteer entry below.

Gazetteer Page

@Embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.bfpbRmmyoVF5Ize7]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
Objectives

The party will journey to this area of Redwalk Ramble during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] Event to confront @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar} and his menagerie of art-magic monsters.

Elevation

Elevation varies across Redwalk Ramble. Inspect the @UUID[Scene.emberRedwalkRamb]{Redwalk Ramble} Scene for details.

Illumination

Redwalk Ramble is subject to exterior lighting and weather conditions.

Ample lanterns throughout the area provide @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbExploration00.JournalEntryPage.j39OCLFX4okynRIO]{Bright Light} once the sun begins to go down.

Terrain

Treat all areas as normal terrain unless otherwise noted.

  • Several rocky walls present in the area can be climbed, but are otherwise impassable, requiring premade pathways to move up or down the natural slope of the terrain.

  • Water features present are shallow enough to walk across but do present &reference[difficult terrain] for characters that traverse them.

  • While the shops are all locked and lack interiors for character to explore, they are still present on the area map and could be entered at the gamemaster's discretion. Their doors are made of reinforced oak (AC 17, 25 Hit Points), requiring a [[/skill Strength 16]] to force open, or a successful [[/skill sleightofhand 15]] check using Proficiency in @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulThievesToo]{Thieves' Tools} to unlock.

Falar's Hallucinatory Terrain

During the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] Event, @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar} enchants several areas of Redwalk Ramble with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplHallucinat]{Hallucinatory Terrain}. The particulars of each piece of illusory terrain is explicated more fully where it appears in the text, but each illusion follows these general rules:

  • Falar has made these spells permanent — and very dangerous — by empowering them with the Lifeforce of several @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf]{Chiaroscuran Beasts}; when a beast is slain, its associated illusory terrain vanishes.

    • Because of their connection to the chiaroscuran beasts, the illusions include audible, visual, tactile, and olfactory elements, so it can turn clear ground into @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.BVb0EMYNoOk3FPYc#hex-based-exploration]{Difficult Terrain} (or vice versa) or otherwise impede movement through the area. Any piece of the illusory terrain (such as a rock or stick) that is removed from the spell's area disappears immediately.

    • Creatures with @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.be7g0q1xBAwb8drv]{Truesight} — and creatures who make a successful [[/skill investigation 15]] check to examine the illusory terrain — can see through the illusion to the terrain's true form; however, all other elements of the illusion remain, so while the creature is aware of the illusion's presence, the creature can still physically interact with the illusion.

  • The chiaroscuran beasts are immune to the hazardous effects of any piece of illusory terrain in Redwalk Ramble, and can pass through any illusory obstacles or hazards with impunity.

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} targeting the illusory terrain fails automatically, but inflicts [[/damage 1d4 Psychic]] damage multiplied by its spell level to the hazard's associated chiaroscuran beast. For example, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} cast using a 5th-level spell slot would inflict [[/damage 5d4 Psychic]] damage to the hazard's associated chiaroscuran beast.

There are five hazardous areas of illusory terrain:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.8wDjs0IVM65Lldac#hallucinatory-terrain:-overgrown-jungle]{Overgrown Jungle}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.0tTphS248DHk0L65#hallucinatory-terrain:-tomb]{Tomb}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.pF387YTaWH5kEAMs#hallucinatory-terrain:-scorching-desert]{Scorching Desert}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.9SoTYFpauLtxZYHk#hallucinatory-terrain:-lava-floe]{Lava Floe}

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.DOOdLbIqGVtB0T3a#hallucinatory-terrain:-pit-trap]{Pit Trap}

Enemies

During the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] Event, the following enemies are encountered here:

  • 5 @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf]{Chiaroscuran Beasts}, each one connected to a section of illusory terrain that they are serving as the magical anchor for.

  • 5 @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg]{Paint Globlins}, hidden in jars of paint around the area. They emerge when a character moves within 15 feet of their jar, or if their jar is shattered.

  • @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, located near the @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.9SoTYFpauLtxZYHk]{Promontory}.

Enemy Tactics

The preceding enemies typically employ the following tactics in combat.

@Embed[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf inline]

Chiaroscuran Beast Tactics

These elemental predators are each anchored to a specific piece of illusory terrain and prefer to remain inside that area, though they can leave it if necessary.

  • In melee combat, they utilize their @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf.Item.ZH8Zlr7RdgTjDN7K]{Scratch} attack to harm enemies, and prefer to attack isolated, unaware, and vulnerable targets inside the illusory terrain they are tied to.

  • When a Chiaroscuran Beast is defeated, the terrain it is linked to dissipates, returning that section of the battlefield to normal.

  • They can use their Bonus Action to enter or leave a flat surface using their @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf.Item.zPtkhxg2m4xurlhR]{Ride Surface} ability.

  • While they are merged with a surface, they can use their @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf.Item.Er1JRuePqKcELECz]{Quick Sketch} to quickly reposition without danger of being attacked, or recover lost hit points with their @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf.Item.WqUiEvNm0MdwPllb]{Redraw Form} ability.

@Embed[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg inline]

Paint Globlin Tactics

These strange elemental creatures are intensely chaotic, and revel in mess and disorder. They attack exuberantly without much coordination or strategy.

  • Once they've engaged a character in melee combat, each paint globlin will use its @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.MYOzrqDwpuizBIhz]{Clobber} attack against adjacent enemies.

  • When they die, their @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.HJQnsFvfrAFumrCY]{Death Burst} feature triggers, potentially blinding enemy combatants, which become preferred targets for other paint globlins.

  • The paint globlins will fight to the death, and will either pursue enemies outside of the immediate area or target them with ranged @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.xfAFqQSGG0QxJupA]{Glob Lob} attacks.

@Embed[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih inline]

Falar Tactics

This old, veteran mage and adventurer has been busy weaving magic into the Redwalk Ramble, and now waits on Promontory to goad the party while peppering them with magic from on high.

  • Falar is completely immune to his own illusory terrain, and can walk through it unharmed and unhindered, and the creatures on this map will obey his commands when given.

  • Falar has command of a potent @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.aVSKmjM2ObbfIzhP]{Illusory Arsenal} that allows him to create any weapon he needs for any combat situation, allowing him to attack in melee or at range.

  • As a spellcaster, he begins combat with @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.kVOsxqHFifCBGwmz]{Mage Armor} already cast on himself. When enemies get close enough to attack, he can cast @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.Bn9WPKxzheDoPV73]{Mirror Image} on himself to further enhance his defense.

  • When attacked, he can use @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.fXlTzqkWhQqOU0NL]{Shield} or @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.GZAXmUHs6QMrKVO7]{Counterspell} as a reaction to block incoming attacks and spells.

  • He will cast either @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.BN6g1RyPuCEW6xYx]{Mind Spike} or @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.PB9zHkX5yr6SVCf3]{Phantasmal Killer} on targets that are especially dangerous or persistent, favoring other spellcasters who might be able to disrupt his own spellcasting.

  • He can cast @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.fllNnUPPljr7TOhQ]{Hypnotic Pattern} to disrupt groups of enemies, but is not averse to using the spell on single targets that are especially persistent or dangerous to him.

  • Falar fights with bravado and cunning but will begin to falter when his Hit Points fall below half their maximum.
