At that point he will consider retreat, using @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih.Item.6b68s7G7qxQ9LeHR]{Invisibility} (if available) to escape from the area unseen. If cornered and presented with surrender or death, Falar will give up.

Reasoning with Falar

Parley with the old Illusionist

At any point during the encounter, the characters may attempt to convince Falar to abandon his crusade against Ordain, and surrender. If they wish to do so, the party must complete a skill challenge by succeeding on a total of 3 [[/skill persuasion 16]] skill checks.

Any of the following lines of reasoning are likely to work:

  • Ruining Varinna will cause House Salva to take away her contract, ruining her future. Falar is making her a victim of circumstances she had no part in.

  • Harming the innocent people of Ordain will only make him into a villain, and if people die by his hand the Veiled Chain will make sure you never leave the Spellbreaker Tower.

  • He clearly hasn't run out of ideas or ingenuity, there's no reason he couldn't pick himself up and start rebuilding his life properly.

  • Owning the creation of his Murals, and standing behind the message might make him a target of the Trading Houses, but he's not alone in his sentiments and distaste for them.

  • Things are difficult in Ordain, and what the city needs is someone who will fight for its people, not another problem to keep them awake at night, and these elementals are just that.

  • Mistress Caberi still remembers you, the old you, charming, gregarious, creative. You clearly left a mark on people in the city, it's not too late to recapture that.

The Flexible Approach

Players should be encouraged to use what they have learned about House Salva, Falar, Varinna, and the people of Flotsam to influence the old mage. Certain knowledges, paths, or cultures may provide advantage, and alternate skill checks to Persuasion could be viable, with a DC at your discretion.

Falar is not so far gone that he can't be reasoned with, but convincing him to stand down should not be impossible.

Main Plaza - East.name: Main Plaza - East
Main Plaza - East.text:
A curtain of thick jungle growth chokes the path ahead, uprooting the plaza's pale flagstones into rubble. Thorned, black vines lie coiled and writhing at the roots of the trees; one snaps at an insect with a whipcrack sound. A light mist obscures what lies beyond the tree line. The air is hot and wet in your throat.

This area has been transformed by Falar's illusion magic into a thick, sweating jungle. Thorned, animated vines lurk among the roots and undergrowth, snapping at anything that draws too close.

Effect Under Development

This hallucinatory terrain feature may lack a combination of walls, lighting, sounds, and similar effects. These enhancements will be added in a future update, and tied to the interactable object functionality.

Hallucinatory Terrain: Overgrown Jungle

In addition to the general rules described on the @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.RKNzA7Glmcy6kWxX#falars-hallucinatory-terrain]{Gameplay Details} page, this hazard has the following characteristics:

  • Treat the area as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.9tzB6KQDTIuw1FlZ]{Difficult Terrain}.

  • Treat the area as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.24I7GDO2vVahRan1]{Lightly Obscured} due to foliage and light mist.

  • A character who enters the hazard or who begins their turn in the hazard must make a successful [[/save dex 12]] save to avoid the animated vines or suffer [[/damage 1d6 Piercing]] damage and become @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.dqLeGdpHtb8FfcxX]{Restrained}. A character Restrained in this way can make a [[/skill strength 12]] check as a Bonus Action on their turn to free themselves; alternatively, an animated vine has AC 10 and 5 Hit Points.

Once the area's @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf]{Chiaroscuran Beast} is slain, the hazard vanishes.

@Embed[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf inline]

On a Normal Day

If the party visits this area outside the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] Event, read or paraphrase the following:

A broad sweep of pale stone lies before you, carefully ordered and paved flat. Narrow channels of water divide the plaza and draw the eye south, where a great curving promontory of stone frames the drop toward the lower grounds. Shopfronts, benches, and arches hem the space like the curtains of a stage.

This area acts as a main thoroughfare for Redwalk Ramble. At the height of activity, artists, food vendors, and street performers gather here to display their work and ply their trade.

Promontory.name: Promontory
Promontory.text:
A great mass of lava has engulfed the promontory ahead. Thick, sulfurous smoke roils above it in a choking cloud. The molten floe churns in slow eddies and whorls at the promontory's edge, threatening to pour into the lower plaza before vanishing suddenly in midair.

This area has been transformed by Falar's illusion magic into a circulating mass of lava. A foul-smelling cloud of smoke conceals the whole area.

Effect Under Development

This hallucinatory terrain feature may lack a combination of walls, lighting, sounds, and similar effects. These enhancements will be added in a future update, and tied to the interactable object functionality.

Hallucinatory Terrain: Lava Floe

In addition to the general rules described on the @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.RKNzA7Glmcy6kWxX#falars-hallucinatory-terrain]{Gameplay Details} page, this hazard has the following characteristics:

  • Treat the area as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.9tzB6KQDTIuw1FlZ]{Difficult Terrain}.

  • Treat the area as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.YkuKTIH2YaYW8lTS]{Heavily Obscured} due to sulfuric smoke.

  • A character who enters the hazard or who begins their turn in the hazard must make a successful [[/skill acrobatics 12]] check to keep their footing amidst the shifting floes or suffer [[/damage 2d6 fire]] damage.

Once the area's @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf]{Chiaroscuran Beast} is slain, the hazard vanishes.

On a Normal Day

If the party visits this area outside the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] Event, read or paraphrase the following:

The plaza narrows into a broad stone promontory overlooking the lower grounds. Its embossed masonry sits atop the natural rock like a pale crown; the water below laps audibly against the stone. From here, Ordain's crimson architecture appears to cascade toward the harbor as a russet fall.

The promontory offers Ordani citizens a clear view of both the performances taking place in the @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.DOOdLbIqGVtB0T3a]{Lower Plaza} below and the city beyond. It is a favorite spot for landscape artists working "en plein air."

Lower Plaza.name: Lower Plaza
Lower Plaza.text:
The area ahead appears as an unbroken, level plain, its chalky flagstones fitted together as a perfect jigsaw. Its seams are so fine as to be nearly invisible.

This area has been transformed by Falar's illusion magic to conceal a large pit trap beneath the appearance of solid ground.

Effect Under Development

This hallucinatory terrain feature may lack a combination of walls, lighting, sounds, and similar effects. These enhancements will be added in a future update, and tied to the interactable object functionality.

Hallucinatory Terrain: Pit Trap

In addition to the general rules described on the @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.RKNzA7Glmcy6kWxX#falars-hallucinatory-terrain]{Gameplay Details} page, this hazard has the following characteristics:

  • The pit trap is 30-feet deep.

  • A character that moves into the hazard falls 30 feet, taking [[/damage 3d6 Bludgeoning]] damage and landing &Reference[Prone].

  • A character inside the hazard can climb out using natural handholds with a successful [[/skill athletics 15]] check.

Once the area's @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf]{Chiaroscuran Beast} is slain, the hazard vanishes; creatures still inside the hazard when this occurs are ejected, landing safely with a soft thump on solid ground.

@Embed[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf inline]

On a Normal Day

If the party visits this area outside the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] Event, read or paraphrase the following:

A circle of broad, chalk-white flagstones sits in the shadow of the promontory — the performer to the promontory's audience. A shallow stream of clear water babbles beneath it to pool on the other side.

The lower plaza circle serves as a performance and exhibition space for artists, fashion models, actors, and singers; it is one of many such performance plazas dotting Redwalk Ramble.

Pavilion.name: Pavilion
Pavilion.text:
A platform of sun-bleached stone, perched atop a natural outcropping, looks over the grounds. It offers a clear view of the lower plaza circle, the gentle water, and the crimson skyline of Ordain beyond. The stones have been worn into irregular shapes by the feet of hundreds of dancers.

This raised, open-air dais serves as a public gathering place for a variety of social functions, such as wine tastings, dances, parties, and ceremonies.

Main Plaza - Central.name: Main Plaza - Central
Main Plaza - Central.text:
Five stone sarcophagi lie at the center of this darkened chamber. Four have been cracked open to reveal ashen bones; the fifth remains untouched. Strewn about the tomb are small treasures and coins that appear to glint and glimmer with mesmerizing color.

This area has been transformed by Falar's illusion magic into a lightless tomb. Illusory gold glitters within the dark, compelling the greedy and unwary to draw near.

Effect Under Development

This hallucinatory terrain feature may lack a combination of walls, lighting, sounds, and similar effects. These enhancements will be added in a future update, and tied to the interactable object functionality.

Hallucinatory Terrain: Tomb

In addition to the general rules described on the @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.RKNzA7Glmcy6kWxX#falars-hallucinatory-terrain]{Gameplay Details} page, this hazard has the following characteristics:

  • Treat the area as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.YkuKTIH2YaYW8lTS]{Heavily Obscured} due to permanent nonmagical @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixDRule.JournalEntryPage.4dfREIDjG5N4fvxd]{Darkness}; its nonmagical quality is itself part of the illusion.

  • A character that sees a piece of illusory treasure must make a successful [[/save Cha 12]] save or be compelled to spend its entire turn moving toward and examining the gold piece. A character compelled in this way becomes &Reference[Incapacitated], and repeats the saving throw whenever it takes damage and at the beginning of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A character that succeeds on their save becomes immune to this effect until they finish a Long Rest.

Once the area's @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf]{Chiaroscuran Beast} is slain, the hazard vanishes.

@Embed[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf inline]

Main Plaza - West.name: Main Plaza - West
Main Plaza - West.text:
A driving wind blurs the world ahead into a pale haze of sun-blasted sand. The plaza's streets have vanished beneath a series of rocky outcroppings, and heat shimmers in undulating waves. The sand crawls and slithers beneath the wind.

This area has been transformed by Falar's illusion magic into a scorching desert. Blasting winds drive an ever-present sandstorm, and the magical heat is punishing to any living creature caught within it.

Effect Under Development

This hallucinatory terrain feature may lack a combination of walls, lighting, sounds, and similar effects. These enhancements will be added in a future update, and tied to the interactable object functionality.

Hallucinatory Terrain: Scorching Desert

In addition to the general rules described on the @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx.JournalEntryPage.RKNzA7Glmcy6kWxX#falars-hallucinatory-terrain]{Gameplay Details} page, this hazard has the following characteristics:

  • Treat the area as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.9tzB6KQDTIuw1FlZ]{Difficult Terrain}.

  • Treat the area as @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbAppendixCRule.JournalEntryPage.24I7GDO2vVahRan1]{Lightly Obscured} due to the sandstorm.

  • Ranged weapon attacks are made with Disadvantage due to the sandstorm.

  • A character who enters the hazard or who begins their turn in the hazard must make a successful [[/save con 5]] save to withstand the desert's magical heat or suffer one level of &Reference[Exhaustion]. For each consecutive round a character remains inside the hazard, the DC increases by 2.

Once the area's @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf]{Chiaroscuran Beast} is slain, the hazard vanishes.

@Embed[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf inline]

On a Normal Day

If the party visits this area outside the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] Event, read or paraphrase the following:

A broad sweep of pale stone lies before you, carefully ordered and paved flat. Narrow channels of water divide the plaza and draw the eye south, where a great curving promontory of stone frames the drop toward the lower grounds. Shopfronts, benches, and arches hem the space like the curtains of a stage.

This area acts as a main thoroughfare for Redwalk Ramble. At the height of activity, artists, food vendors, and street performers gather here to display their work and ply their trade.

Area Overview.name: Area Overview
Area Overview.text:
Area Map Context

The area map for the Flotsam Canal Market depicts a notable subsection of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.hKNuD0yWUAA6UmDA]{Flotsam} district's famed marketplace, a popular destination for working-class patrons in search of food, leisure, art supplies, and more. This location serves as the scenery for the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] and [[/eventState localColorSketchy]] events of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest.

Since the Flotsam Canal Market is a smaller area within the mile-wide hex that comprises the Ordani district of Flotsam, the Gazetteer Entry below contains information about the neighborhood as a whole. Additional information about the specific areas of the Flotsam Canal Market are featured in the @UUID[JournalEntry.jUCq8sac06LvGlT6.JournalEntryPage.nOAOw32ALXglGRfv]{Gameplay Details} section of this walkthrough.

Gazetteer Entry

@embed[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.hKNuD0yWUAA6UmDA inline]

Gameplay Details.name: Gameplay Details
Gameplay Details.text:
The Flotsam Canal Market area map depicts a small section of the market proper, let alone the Flotsam district itself. It plays host to a wide array of commerce and social exchange, populated with all manner of Ordani locals and visitors from afar. Comprised of three vertical Levels that include the Dockside, Stoneside, and Promenade layers, the various interior and exterior sections of the area walkthrough adhere to the following mechanical gameplay features (unless otherwise stated in a specific area's description).

Elevation

The Flotsam Canal Market features a total of three vertical Levels of elevation, including:

  • Dockside. The main waterfront of the area (which includes the wooden docks themselves, the first floor interiors of buildings on the docks, and the westernmost section of the connected stone walkway), is set to an elevation of 0.

  • Stoneside. This central series of winding ramps and terraces is 20 feet high.

  • Promenade. The easternmost section of the map, which depicts a stoney promenade lined with typical Ordani edifices, is 40 feet high.

The water surface level of the area's eponymous canal is set to an elevation of -6, and is approximately 40 feet deep.

Illumination

Most of the interiors and exteriors of the Flotsam Canal Market are illuminated by lanterns, which radiate bright light for 15 feet and dim light for an additional 15 feet. Alternately, throughout the first-floor interior section of @UUID[.VfumF2r8uCyNAVhR]{The Bread Barge}, most light sources radiate dim light for a total of 15 feet.

Additionally, the exterior sections of the map are illuminated by the light of the sun during the day, and by the light of the moons at night (with visibility dependent on current weather conditions).

Sound

Sound in the area is full of white noise, including the constant lapping of water in the canal, and the chatter of idle patrons and market barkers during business hours.

Wisdom (Perception) skill checks made to hear something have @Advantage[-2] throughout the market exteriors.

Terrain

Aside from the waterway of the canal, the terrain here is manmade and considered normal terrain unless otherwise indicated (such as the difficult terrain sections of @UUID[.Q1RA3PuqlRFcpZ8w]{Merchant's Quay} or the @UUID[.0p2PutjpDrAunVck]{Cluttered Dock}).

The wooden timbers of Dockside are aged and weather-worn, but the people of Ordain keep them sanded with regular maintenance. The cobble- and flagstone walkways of the Stoneside area and the Promenade include the same white stone typical to the rest of Ordain, built upon the tiered earthen foundations common to the area.

Inhabitants

The following characters and creatures inhabit this map:

  • The Flotsam Canal Market is usually occupied by an array of various @UUID[Actor.pxvrzj4uE4tVFzYL]{Ordani} and @UUID[Actor.9plFRf3Hurd9r7ol]{Arcturians}, with a higher concentration of visitors from nearby Flotsam and other districts during daytime hours.

  • Important characters here include @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna}, @UUID[JournalEntry.jUCq8sac06LvGlT6.JournalEntryPage.Q1RA3PuqlRFcpZ8w]{Seylu}, and others.

  • During the [[/eventState localColorSketchy]] event of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest, @UUID[.Q8OllaH7mbfwDEXF]{Falar's Studio} is occupied by a group of antagonistic @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg]{Paint Globlins}.

Falar's Paints.name: Falar's Paints
Falar's Paints.text:
This modest, one-room shop obviously caters to patrons in search of high-quality paints and art supplies. Several shelves and cabinets throughout the place have Falar's eponymous wares on display, oils and acrylics with evocative names such as Leviathan Blue and Fey-Fire Red, and the wizened proprietor himself seems busy at the back with a new mixture. The gray-haired shopkeep turns to greet you with a small measure of annoyance, as if new customers are a few and far between.

Adventurers, eh? Let me guess: you stumbled into a grease trap and need a barrel of mineral spirits to clean up the gunk …

He continues stirring his pigments with the hint of a scowl.

This small Dockside paint shop is owned and operated by the retired adventurer @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, a wizard-turned-shopkeep who plays a central role in the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] and [[/eventState localColorSketchy]] events of the @UUID[..emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest.

Falar's Paints sells higher-end paints of various mediums and colors (including oils, acrylics, and watercolors), along with a modest selection of art supplies, fine wooden easels, and chemical solvents.

If the party visits Falar's Paints during the course of the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] event, they will likely have a series of questions to ask Falar to help aid their investigation. The following social and exploration blocks presume the characters are in search of information relevant to the @UUID[..emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest.

@Embed[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]

Conversation with Falar

@UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar} (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Human, he/him)

A retired adventurer and wizard who has become increasingly fed up with Ordain and what he perceives as it's numerous failings. Falar is brusque, bitter, and wants to be left alone. He has had a hard life, suffering setbacks, betrayals, and mistreatment at the hands of many people and institution in the city, and has had people he cared about suffer in similar ways. The ideal of Ordain is a lie as far as he's concerned.

Conversation topics that Falar is willing to discuss include (but are not limited to):

  • Varinna, her status as a customer, and potential suspects that might want to ruin her reputation.

  • His disdain for the local Trading Houses.

  • His apparent lack of awareness surrounding the House Salva mural from the [[/eventState localColorDrawing]] event.

  • His (flimsy) alibi.

  • His background as a paint retailer, and the qualities of his inventory.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 15]] check is able to tell that Falar isn't being entirely forthcoming when asked about his alibi or Varinna's reputation.

A few specific dialogue options for Falar are provided below.

Do you know Varinna?

Name, yeah, story, no. I don’t have time for tea with every painter in Flotsam, and they don't want to spend all day yapping at me. She buys pigments here, yes. Her coin's always good, she always buys what she reserves, and never leaves me holding product too long. Good customer.

Are you a mage or an adventurer?

I’m a paint monger. I stack jars and argue with suppliers trying to jack up prices on my pigments and oils. Adventurers wear skulls on their belts and tell stories in taverns.

He gestures to himself.

Do you see any skulls? Me neither.

What do you think of the trading houses?

Crooked comes in many cuts. Some wear silk while they do it. City would breathe easier without them leaning on every throat that tries to make an honest crown.

What do you think about the Ordinate / Hallows / Veiled Chain?

Oh, they do their best. I'm sure they do their best. I just can’t tell who “best” is for. Doesn’t always look like it’s the dockhands or the stall-minders who get the benefit.

Have you seen the mural?

Nope, haven't. I open early, close late, sleep when I can. I don’t have time to gawk at walls.

Do you have an alibi for the last few days?

Here. Or at home. Here. Or sleeping. Take your pick.

Are you an artist or painter?

I sell paint. That’s the job. Other folks make the mess and call it art. I have some doodles and examples in the shop here, you can see them yourself, judge if I'm any kind of artist.

Did you sell any magical or infused paints lately?

I sold a bunch of enchanted paints to Varinna a while ago. Go bother her. I don't decide what people do with my paint. I just make it and sell it.

Do you carry infused pigments at all?

Yep, sure do. They are costly to make, take special materials and pigments, and sell out fast. I would make and sell more of it if I could, but I'm one person.

Do you make all of your own paint?

Not all, but most everything here, yes. There's a few makers in the city I also stock when I can, but they don't make me as much money as my own mixes do.

Can we see your inventory or sales records?

Bring a writ from the Hallows and you can read my ledgers line by line. Until then, no.

Who would want to harm Varinna's reputation?

Flotsam, all of Ordain really, is full of copycats and bravado. Everyone's painting over everyone in one way or another. For Varinna to succeed someone else had to fail, didn't they?

Surveying the Scene

Any character who takes a moment to look around the shop is able to discern a few basic details:

  • Falar doesn't seem to be a particularly talented artist. His work appears somewhat rushed and predominantly lackluster.

  • Falar's art style is clearly different from Varinna's, which can be seen in@UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{ Varinna's Studio (Lower)}.

  • The paints for sale here are solely made by Falar himself. No products from other makers or manufacturers can be found.

  • One shelf of paints is labeled "Magical Hues." On the wall above it, a painting of a local Ordani street slowly and continually fades from day to night (and back again), simulating the passage of time.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check while examining the so-called Magical Hues is able to discern that subtle and precise illusion magic is being used to supernaturally shift the pigmentation of the paint.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Characters who cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell while searching the area automatically succeed.

Exploring the Shop

Any character who takes at least 10 minutes to exhaustively search the shop is able to find a few pieces of information pertinent to their investigation into the House Salva mural from [[/eventState localColorDrawing]], found inside the desk on the southern wall:

  • A stack of letters on top of the desk indicate Falar has been in contact with the Hallows. His request to appeal the ruling against House Salva has been denied yet again, and no further appeals will be heard. (This information can also be learned when meeting @UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]{Cherish Ellerie} and @UUID[Actor.i5jXHUyZCPBJDb2k]{Mistress Caberi}).

  • The desk contains several receipts of the sale and delivery of rare pigments and minerals from @UUID[..emberArctusGazet.JournalEntryPage.UkNBiAA4l5PP891p]{Redrak}, indicating that Falar's been receiving regular orders. Among these, a letter exchange of Falar asking if something weird was going on, and the reply is that Cora was full, and some of the pigments are elementally charged.

  • A title deed for this building (Falar's Paints), and another deed for a two-story building just north of here (Falar's Studio).

  • Searching his desk in here he has notes about stock, including spare stock. There's not enough room for all his stock to be here, so he's keeping it elsewhere. This is a hint that he's got another space nearby.

If the party attempts to search the shop outside of normal business hours (10am to 8pm), Falar is located at @UUID[.Q8OllaH7mbfwDEXF]{Falar's Studio (Lower)} across the dock instead, and Falar's Paints is closed for business. If the characters wish to gain entry, the locked door must be picked or bashed in (see below).

After Hours: Locked Door

If the party attempts to visit Falar's Paints to investigate outside of normal business hours (10am to 8pm), they'll find the door to be securely locked.

Any character who succeeds on either a [[/tool thief 16]] or [[/skill athletics 20]] check is able to open the locked door. Characters who make a lot of noise during their attempt to bash the door may draw the unwanted attention of other people nearby (and subsequently the ire of local law enforcement or neighborhood watch).

Falar's Studio (Lower).name: Falar's Studio (Lower)
Falar's Studio (Lower).text:
Decorated for comfort, this cozy dockside chamber appears to be an artist's public-facing office or client sitting room. Two armchairs flank a coffee table near the room's center. Close by, an artist's desk props up a canvas carefully splattered with paint, and an array of other tables, desks, and shelves line the room's perimeter. Meanwhile, a large painting hung upon the northern wall depicts an image of Ordain's waterfront, masterfully rendered using oils of the deepest hues.

Along with @UUID[.8DDGWFhzTuBFKy7w]{Falar's Studio (Upper)}, this Dockside lounge is owned and operated by the retired adventurer @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, a wizard-turned-shopkeep who plays a central role in the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] and [[/eventState localColorSketchy]] events of the @UUID[..emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest.

The sitting room here serves Falar as a parlor and showroom for potential customers, and is quite obviously set up for entertainment others. An illusory painting on the northern wall conceals a passage to @UUID[.8DDGWFhzTuBFKy7w]{Falar's Studio (Upper)} via the staircase beyond.

Exploring the Studio

A brief examination of the room reveals the following:

  • The art here is stylish, full of distinction and skill. However, the newest piece is dated several years ago. It seems the artist hasn't done any new artwork in years.

  • The desk on the western wall contains the @UUID[Item.a4mO1lO3M2wckqtJ]{House Salva Art Missives}.

  • The Ordain Waterfront painting on the northern wall depicts a scene of immigrants from all over Aterica arriving to Ordain's shores, the city's docks brimming with community and hope.

  • The table in the northwest corner of the room bears both @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulPaintersSu]{Painter's Supplies} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulAlchemists]{Alchemist's Supplies}, along with @UUID[Item.xsQ9RHVNs9wJ1ECm]{Falar's Studio Notes}.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check while examining the Painter's and Alchemist's Supplies is able to identify some curious qualities among them, including the presence of rare lunar elements that suggest an association with @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora}, the earth moon.

  • Characters with [[/attunement cora]] automatically succeed.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge alchemy]] or [[/knowledge cosmology]] have @Advantage[2].

Illusory Painting

The Ordain Waterfront painting on the northern wall is actually a permanent @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMajorImage]{Major Image} spell that conceals the stairway to @UUID[.8DDGWFhzTuBFKy7w]{Falar's Studio (Upper)}.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 15]] check while examining the painting is able to identify the telltale signs of illusion magic.

  • Characters who cast the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell automatically succeed.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge artifacts]] or [[/knowledge crafts]] have @Advantage[2].

Physical interaction with the painting reveals it to be an illusion, as things can pass through it. Any creature that takes a turn to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/skill investigation 16]] check. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image, and its other sensory qualities become faint to the creature.

Alternately, any character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDispelMagi]{Dispel Magic} spell and succeeds on a spellcasting ability check (DC 16) can suppress the effects of the painting for a duration of 1 hour.

Varinna's Studio (Lower).name: Varinna's Studio (Lower)
Varinna's Studio (Lower).text:
A spirited Ordani woman answers the door, no doubt an artist by the look of her paint-dappled clothing and pigment-stained hands. She appears somewhat fatigued from labor, but an active air of inspiration and enthusiasm hangs about her. She blows a tassel of graying hair from her eyes before addressing you:

You folks don't exactly look like my normal patrons, but I never turn away a good commission, and I could use a break anyway. So, how can I help you?

Behind her, the bottom floor of this two-story dwelling appears to host a spacious art studio. Several tables stand about the room, adorned with paints, palettes, brushes, and more — anything a professional painter might need to ply their trade.

Meanwhile, two large canvases dominate the room, which appear to feature in-progress works of abstract art. The larger piece on the eastern wall depicts a mythical clash of two heroic on Signara, while the smaller piece to the north bears the emerging scene of a pair of intertwined, passion-wrought lovers.

Along with @UUID[.HRBT4lxbapBPp1MQ]{Varinna's Studio (Upper)}, this Stoneside-level area serves as the home studio and private residence of the accomplished Ordani artist known as Varinna — who plays an important role in the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] event of the @UUID[..emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest.

The first floor of this two-story edifice is the primary studio space of Varinna's humble abode, and has multiple works on display that showcase her noteworthy talent as a mural artist, including a palimpsest of sketches and paintings on the very walls themselves.

Conversation with Varinna

Varinna (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

Grew up middle-class, was once more disillusioned about some of Ordain's shortcomings (the houses can strangle independent traders/makers out of the markets, forcing them to languish in smaller markets, like flotsam's) but has changed her tune a bit now that she's succeeded well enough to land commissioned work with Salva.

Varinna is happy to discuss her art style and history as an artist, but is initially unwilling to share more intimate details of her work and private affairs with strangers. However, she can be swayed with effort. Any character who succeeds on either a [[/skill deception 13]], [[/skill intimidation 16]] or [[/skill 13 persuasion]] check is able to convince Varinna to share some noteworthy details.

  • Characters with [[/attunement heart]], [[/knowledge crime]], [[/knowledge intrigue]], or [[/path lunarEmpath]] have @Advantage[2].

  • If the party has already completed the [[/eventState localColorFashion cherishFirst]] coutcome, they can invoke the name of @UUID[Actor.i5jXHUyZCPBJDb2k]{Mistress Caberi} to automatically succeed, relaying that she has expressed a personal interest in this attack on House Salva's image. This elicits Varinna's immediate cooperation.

Conversation topics with noteworthy details that Varinna is willing to discuss include (but are not limited to):

  • The @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{House Salva} mural from the [[/eventState localColorDrawing]] event, and her relationship with the famed Trading House.

  • Her alibi, and potential witnesses who can corroborate the details.

  • The source of the paints and materials she uses for her work, and the inspirations for her abstract style.

  • Other local artists and painters of note.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check is able to tell that Varinna has nothing to hide, and is being totally forthcoming with her explanation of the matters at hand.

A few specific dialogue options for Varinna are provided below.

What do you know about the mural?

I don’t, not firsthand. I haven’t seen it at all, and I certainly didn't paint it.

Why would it look like your style if you didn’t paint it?

I don't know! Perhaps a copycat?

Where were you when it went up?

Home. I’ve been under the weather these past few days, some sort of head cold that's left me a feeling terrible. I barely left my bed, let alone climbed a scaffold with pots of paint to work on a mural.

Can anyone confirm your alibi?

Yes, actually. Go speak to Seylu Koine, she runs the produce stand down on the docks, and is a friend of mine. She came by several times with soups and fruit and stayed to make sure I ate. She’ll vouch for me. Neighbors saw her coming and going too, I'm sure.

What’s your relationship with House Salva right now?

Currently professional. I’m contracted to do some interior murals for them in exchange for pay and possible inclusion into the house later. I won’t jeopardize that by going after them through a mural.

You used to be more critical of the trading houses.

I grew up watching friends get squeezed out of the big markets. I said plenty about it. I still think the system can grind down independents. But I’ve got a contract now, and I’m not foolish enough to bite the hand that’s feeding me, or pretend it isn’t feeding me.

Where do you buy your paints?

From Falar, mostly. He’s nearby, carries good stock, and it's all very consistent. If you look around my studio, you’ll see his labels on nearly everything.

Do you use magical or “infused” pigments?

Not yet, but I did buy some. My last order is sitting by the door, and the jars are still sealed with his wax stamp. You’re welcome to check the dates and break them open if you need to.

Would you object to us examining your studio and supplies?

Go ahead. If someone’s trying to steal my style and ruin my name, I want them identified as much as you do. Just don’t smear the charcoal thumbnails pinned on the east wall — I need those for a Salva mock-up.

Who might know your style well enough to imitate it?

There's plenty of painters in the local community, some of them far better than me, and I have my studio open all day for anyone that wants to come buy something or commission me.

Look, I’m not accusing anyone, just… if you’re after material study, my work’s out in the open most days.

Exploring the Studio

Most of the pieces are for sale, a few are already sold, they are going to modest prices, and the art is all well done. A sign on the wall notes she is not accepting commissions for the time being.

If the party has previously completed the [[/eventState localColorDrawing examinedSalvaMural]] outcome, they can study Varinna's work and likely conclude that while the styles were similar, they have some key differences. Such as Varinna's work has less bold lines and figures are portrayed slightly differently.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge arts]] automatically succeed.

  • Characters with [[/attunement primordis]] have @Advantage[2].

Wicks & Wax.name: Wicks & Wax
Wicks & Wax.text:
Candles of every shape and size adorn each surface of this dimly-lit chandlery, which is warmed with the sweet and inviting smells of scented wax. The shopkeeper, a dignified Zeph with a mask crafted of rose-colored stone, turns to greet you with a gentle tilt of her head.

You've come to the right place! Can I interest you in a new scent today?

This chandlery is owned and operated by the fledgling candlemaker Eliki Nort, and is known district-wide for the exquisite aromas associated with its wares.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Eliki Nort (Lawful Good, Ordani Zeph, she/her)

This ceremonious Zeph is a chandler of moderate skill who just stepped into the candle-making business a couple of years ago, after jumping careers from her work as a lamplighter for the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.TdFy82NoVNArBC9f]{Hallows}.

Given her somewhat recent career change, Eliki has relatively little to offer in terms of noteworthy details about locals like Varinna, Falar, and Seylu.

Goods & Services

The candles here are all handmade by Eliki, and the rest of her inventory has been sourced with care and utmost consideration for ethical concerns. Eliki's wares include:

  • Ample @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCandle00000]{Candles} of various shapes, styles, and purpose (including perfumed candles and those that burn with colored flame).

  • [[/roll 2d4]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagLanternBull]{Bullseye Lanterns}.

  • [[/roll 3d4]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagLanternHood]{Hooded Lanterns}.

  • Over 2 dozen flasks of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagOil00000000]{Oil}.

  • Blocks of wax, and other raw materials.

  • [[/roll 1d2]] @UUID[Item.pCl2T09DRBETkkbZ]{Chasm Candles}.

Haxwell Tailoring & Alterations.name: Haxwell Tailoring & Alterations
Haxwell Tailoring & Alterations.text:
A tiny brass bell above the doorway ring-a-ding-dings as you step across the threshold into this tidy little tailor shop, where a sharp-eyed seamstress busies herself close to the floor, making acute adjustments upon a garment-draped sewing mannequin. She stands from her crouched position to welcome you with a professional smile and a tilt of her head.

Welcome to Haxwell Tailoring. I'm Phoebe. How can I help you?

This Dockside tailor shop is operated by the skilled seamstress Phoebe Haxwell, who inherited the century-old business from her great aunt Vernita Haxwell, and is considered to be the best couturier in Flotsam.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Phoebe sells all manner of garments and accessories, and is always eager to take a custom orders for clothing. Her alteration services cost a total of 2 gp per hour. For a full list of the shop's current inventory, see "Exploring the Shop" below.

Phoebe Haxwell (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

This pragmatic seamstress is the proprietor of Haxwell Tailoring & Alterations, and is extremely proud of the critically-acclaimed history of her family's multigenerational business. Phoebe makes her own clothes by hand, and always has a compliment in store for a new acquaintance.

Although she's a law-abiding citizen, Phoebe isn't in the habit of providing sensitive information to those she doesn't seem worthy. Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill deception 15]] or [[/skill persuasion]] check is able to convince Phoebe to share some insights with the party.

  • Characters with [[/attunement heart]], [[/knowledge crime]], [[/knowledge intrigue]], or [[/path lunarEmpath]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Any character who "invests" at least 50 gp in Phoebe's store (via purchase, donation, or bribe) automatically succeeds.

Conversation topics with Phoebe include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Errant small-talk and gossip she's picked up from customers.

  • What she knows of the abstract artist @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna} and her associates.

  • Her relatively positive opinions of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{House Salva}.

  • What little she knows of the paintmonger @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar} and his @UUID[.fwXjPzq3KmQoIKJ0]{Paints}.

A few specific dialogue options for Phoebe are provided below.

If the party has completed the [[/eventState localColorFashion cherishFirst]] outcome, Phoebe will buy the @UUID[Item.rfXJp1hjlLUOGFsu]{Exquisite Clothes} they received as a reward for full price.

About Varinna?

She does good work. It's a bit abstract for my own tastes, but it's bold — which would explain how she caught the eye of House Salva. I hear they recently added her to their roster of artists. She deserves the recognition, and the Trading House could certainly use a little shakeup when it comes to style.

Speaking of shakeups, Varinna had a falling-out with her best friend Seylu a while back, but they seem to have patched things up; which is good, because Varinna barely leaves the house. I'll never understand the mind of a tortured artist myself.

Who's Seylu?

Seylu Koine is a produce vendor with a stall on the Merchant's Quay nearby. She runs her stall most days, with lunch breaks here and there, and an early quitting time. Once in a while we'll all grab a mug of ale and a bowl of stale olives at The Parched Lark on the Promenade, but it's been a few moons.

Regarding House Salva?

As far as Trading Houses go, it's nice to have one that caters to the family business. Some of my finest work has come about thanks to the enchanted textiles of Nix Salvar's studios. That said, it would be nice to have a few more options when it comes to my choice of suppliers. Salva knows best, right?

On that note, is anything in the shop rousing your interest? A cloak modeled after the esoteric styles of Signara, perhaps?

About Falar?

The paintmonger? I don't know him very well, aside from his sour disposition. You can see his scowl from across the canal. His paint shop has been open for years, but there was this nice little tea house there when I was young. I miss that tea house …

Exploring the Shop

Any character who spends a few moments searching the shop is able to locate the following inventory without much effort:

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulWeaversToo]{Weaver's Tools}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulLeatherwor]{Leatherworker's Tools}

  • [[/roll 1d3]] sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesFine]{Fine Clothes}

  • [[/roll 1d6]] sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesTrav]{Traveler's Clothes}

  • [[/roll 2d4]] elegant @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCostume0000]{Costumes} for a gala or ball.

These items are also currently for sale. Removing this inventory from the shop without consent, however, will eventually lead to criminal prosecution if the characters are caught.

Deela's Barberie.name: Deela's Barberie
Deela's Barberie.text:
The crisp smell of disinfectants lingers in the air of this quaint little barber shop, vaguely masking the copper scent of freshly exsanguinated blood. A mural on the eastern wall showcases a wide range of hair styles for potential customers, and a ponytailed Kiska barber greets you with a half-cocked smile, her hands wet from the daily cleaning.

Hi! I'm Deela. Have a seat. I'll be right with you.

She motions to two benches along the west wall as she finishes up the task before her, placing an array of dirty tools and accoutrements in a blood- or dye-stained sink (you're not entirely sure which).

Owned and operated by the acclaimed coiffeur Deela Danryn (with help from two junior cosmetologists), this Stoneside barberie offers haircuts, shaves, and dental work (along with occasional hedge-medicine procedures like bloodletting).

Conversation with the Barbers

Deela Danryn (Chaotic Good, Ordani Kiska, she/her)

A testament to to modern irreverence, Deela Danryn is a talented barber-surgeon who carries a lot of sway with locals of the Flotsam Canal Market — whether due to her infectious charisma, her skill with a razor blade, or both.

Conversation topics with that Deela is willing to discuss include (but are not limited to):

  • The exceptional quality of the services offered here at the barberie.

  • Various details about the Flotsam Canal Market at large.

  • Observations on @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna}, with a mention of the mural she painted here at the shop (see "Exploring the Shop" for details).

  • Observations on @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, with a focus on his poor moods.

A few specific dialogue options for Deela are provided below.

Barberie Services

The various services provided by Deela's Barberie (and their associated costs) are as follows:

  • Haircut (1 sp)

  • Dye Job (1 gp)

  • Permanent (5 gp)

  • Shave (5 sp)

  • Dental Work (1-100 gp)

  • Bloodletting (10 gp)

  • "Life-Changing Advice" (1 gp)

Any character who purchases one or more of these services gains a temporary +1 bonus to their Charisma skill checks for a duration of [[/roll 1d2]] days. A character can only benefit from this bonus once a month.

About the Canal Market?

The Flotsam Canal Market has been good to us over the years. New faces come and go, and familiar favorites have a way of sticking around.

You know, quite a few folks who work or shop in the market actually get their hair done here. In fact, if you see someone with a bad do or a lousy shave, please send 'em my way!

About Varinna?

Varinna is lovely. She's been a good neighbor, and she actually painted the style wall over there for me a few years ago. She even touches it up every once in a while, thanks to a haircut or two on the house.

About Falar?

That gray-haired paint-pusher is pretty much always in poor spirits. If you ask me, a proper cut and a shave would do the old boy some good. But he don't seem too interested.

Exploring the Shop

A mural on the eastern wall depicts a wide range of Ordani citizens with a varied assortment of hair cuts and styles, painted by Varinna as a commission a few years ago.

Any character who takes a moment to examine the art posted throughout the barber shop is able to notice @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna's} signature on the mural, which is overtly abstract in style.

Flowers by Meadows.name: Flowers by Meadows
Flowers by Meadows.text:
This structure is surrounded by numerous earthenware pots filled with bright and blooming flowers in vibrant reds, golds, and yellows. Wooden crates line the low wall dividing the promenade from the lower paths, and each one is crammed with flower pots, each one priced for sale.

Leaning halfway out of a half-door is a young human woman sipping liquid from a large mug. Bags under her eyes and a slightly unfocused look betray her lack of sleep, but as soon as you drift close enough to catch her eye she sets the mug aside and opens the door fully.

Hello, hi, welcome to Flowers by Meadows, I'm Merygold! Can I help you find anything today? We've got potted flowers here ready to go, and inside I've got plenty more cut and ready to be arranged!

This building is one of the older ones in the area, and like many of the businesses here, has changed hands multiple times. Flowers by Meadows is actually a transplant from another district, having moved here to avoid rising rent.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Merygold Meadows (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Human, she/her)

A friendly if perpetually tired looking florist who never less than halfway through a mug of over strong tea. What she lacks in sleep each night she makes up for in caffeine. She's owned this business for over a decade, but only recently relocated it to the market a year and a half ago.

Conversation topics with Merygold include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Her favorite flowers, which will always be snakevine. She loves the shape of the flowers, but they are terrible in bouquets.

  • The key to a good flower arrangement being the proper layering of textures and shapes to create something with depth and visual variation.

  • Where she gets her flowers, which is mostly from local suppliers, but she has to sometimes buy from Lillifeld, which is fine. The quality isn't always great, but it's cheaper and the flowers are abundant.

  • Her tea is a custom blend she came up with years ago, and is steeped for ten minutes at least. It's bitter enough to wake the dead, which is great, because she's half dead most days on account of her insomnia.

  • If the party asks about @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, Merygold states that she doesn't know the paintmonger personally, but her friend Tula has complained about someone of the same name. She works nights at @UUID[.VfumF2r8uCyNAVhR] and probably knows more, or has a good story at least.

  • If the party asks about Varinna, she says that she's a fairly regular customer, coming in every few days to buy arrangements to make her studio look nice. Or she was, but Merygold hasn't seen her in about two weeks.

Inside the Shop

Inside the building you can see rows of buckets filled with fresh flowers and other decorative plants, shelves burned by glass vases, and displays of pre-arranged flowers ready to be taken home.

Exploring the Shop

A character that examine the flowers or plants and succeeds on a [[/skill nature 14]] or [[/skill survival 16]] skill check will observe that they are all healthy, fresh, and well cared for.

Merygold offers an extensive collection of flowers from all over the region, grown by local farmers and brought in fresh every day for sale. Her shop offers the following:

  • Numerous types of @UUID[Item.5PLwavrpQJsSiKkz]{Potted Plant} for 10GP apiece.

  • A custom made @UUID[Item.HLasg7aNsCpk5kmI]{Fine Bouquet} made by hand from the finest flowers available for 25GP.

A character with [[/knowledge arts]] note that the arrangements on display are well crafted with a keen eye for design.

Aed's Threads.name: Aed's Threads
Aed's Threads.text:
Racks of clothing sit outside along the outer walls of this building, each one bearing a paper tag with a price and rough size. The front doors of Aed's Threads hangs open, and beyond its threshold you can see an even larger collection of racks, each one as packed with second-hand clothing as the ones in front of you.

Nearby a signaran fellow offers a wave as his ephemeral hands sort clothing onto a rack. He says:

Welcome, feel free to browse. If you're looking for anything specific, want to sell, or have questions, let me know.

Run by Aed, this second-hand clothing shop has a lot of good deals for anyone willing to dig through the racks. Everything is in decent shape, but there is nothing new or truly high-end on offer.

The party can sell the @UUID[Item.rfXJp1hjlLUOGFsu]{Exquisite Clothes} they received from Cherish as part of the [[/eventState localColorFashion]] event, but Aed will only offer coin equal to half their value.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Aed Weaver (Neutral Good, Ordani Signborn, He/Him)

Aed is a life-long purveyor of fashion and has done his absolute best to cloth the fine people of Ordain for as long as he has lived. He is opinionated, loves to chat, and believes that everybody should do their best to help everyone else, so that no one suffers alone. He is a devout follower of the Cindaric tenets of unity, cooperation, and charity.

Conversation topics with Aed include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Aed is not a member of House Salva, and quite frankly never wants to be. He considers them to be antithetical to the good taste and creative spirit of the Ordani people. It is his very strong opinion that the way they hoard textiles, and gatekeep fashion is downright criminal.

  • He was training to become a fully robed Cindaric, but accidentally discovered his love of fashion and decided that he had a higher calling in Ordain: making sure everybody had access to fine clothing.

  • If asked about Varinna, he says that he knows her well enough, since she used to be a regular in his shop before she became a sellout. She and her friend Seylu used to come thrift here every week, but that stopped as soon as she got her vaunted art commission with House Salva.

  • If asked about @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, he says that he's had a couple run-ins with the man, and none of them have been pleasant. Though he is a snappy dresser, he's more sour than a sack of lemons. Aed also thinks he heard something about Falar being a retired member of the Anachraenum, but he's not sure where he heard that.

Exploring the Shop

As long as a character is not worried about the quality or state of them, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesTrav]{Traveler's Cloths}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesFine]{Fine Clothes}, or a functional @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagCostume0000]{Costume} can be acquired here for half their normal price.

Aed also sells a few sets of worn and stained @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmPaddedArmo]{Padded Armor} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbarmLeatherArm]{Leather Armor} at half price. It's clear they've seen better days, but the deal can't be beaten.

The Parched Lark.name: The Parched Lark
The Parched Lark.text:
A sun-bleached wooden sign hangs above the front door of this small edifice. It proudly reads "The Parched Lark" atop the caricature of a fowl in bard's clothing swilling a bottle of ale. The clinking of glass mugs and the ambling din of idle chatter can be heard beyond the establishment's frosted windows, and the earthy smells of delicious alcoholic brews waft upon the salty canal air.

This dingy little alehouse is a favorite among Flotsam locals, who are known to soak up the modest tavern's shade and libations while escaping the waterway sun.

Conversation with the Barkeep

Sigurd Halfspear (Chaotic Good, Ordani Vrjnhar, he/him)

Known for his Oaken tattoos and a tendency to excitedly (and humorously) lose his place during conversation, this verbose barkeep has an ale for every mood.

Conversation topics include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Aside from the alehouse, @UUID[.Q1RA3PuqlRFcpZ8w]{Merchant's Quay} is a fine place for gathering information about locals of the Flotsam Canal Market.

  • @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna} is a fine neighbor, nice enough, has even given some of her old sketches over to sale. The party can ask to see these abstract studies, gleaning the same insight as when examining the art in her studio.

  • Observations on Falar, who is considered to be a bit of a lonely figure who's fallen out of favor with whatever audience he once had.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check is able to tell that Sigurd is an honest fellow, with nothing to hide other than the sob stories told to him in confidence by other patrons.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check while gathering information here is able to collect one of the following details from Sigurd or the alehouse patrons (roll [[/roll 1d4]] to determine):

  1. @UUID[.VfumF2r8uCyNAVhR]{The Bread Barge} makes a mean cold cut sandwich and soup combo.

  2. @UUID[.JDvHCop7yadiTY7G]{The Last Component} has some curiously esoteric wares on its shelves.

  3. @UUID[.fwXjPzq3KmQoIKJ0]{Falar's Paints} is gaining a reputation for their novel illusory paints.

  4. @UUID[.Q1RA3PuqlRFcpZ8w]{Merchant's Quay} is a terrific source of gossip and local rumors.

Exploring the Alehouse

Any character who takes a moment to examine the art posted throughout the alehouse is able to notice @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna's} signature on most of the paintings, which are overtly abstract in style.

The Sortilege.name: The Sortilege
The Sortilege.text:
The crystal doorbell above the threshold to this arcane emporium resounds with an otherworldly cascade of chimes as you step into the shop's wondrous expanse. All manner of reagents and spell components line the shelves here, and countless magical implements lay locked away in glass display cases — beckoning you to inquire about their abstruse enchantments.

A rune-scarred Wirrun mage operates the store from behind these counters, clad in a shimmering robe of dark gossamer. She addresses you with a welcoming gesture, her deep voice thrumming with sultry resonance like the purr of some great cat:

We've been expecting you.

One of Flotsam Canal Market's more esoteric destinations, this Promenade-level magic shop caters to spellcasters of all stripes — with a respectable inventory of wands, staffs, wondrous items, implements, components, and more.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Ro Chastain (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Wirrun, she/her)

This enigmatic wizard is a purveyor of spell components, alchemical reagents, and arcane implements. Known for her wry sense of humor and her proclivity for riddles, Ro Chastain is one of Flotsam's most peculiar denizens, and — as the owner of the mysterious Sortilege — is the source (if not subject) of more than one local legend.

Ro Chastain sells a broad selection of reagents and spell components for all disciplines and traditions of magic, as well as a handful of interesting magic items (see "Exploring the Shop" below).

Ro also provides @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbServices00000.JournalEntryPage.mhsrVbdk7Nxzll72]{Spellcasting Services} as a 6th level Wizard.

Conversation topics with that Ro is willing to discuss include (but are not limited to):

  • Her history as a purveyor of the arcane, and her knowledge of local arcane experts and phenomena.

  • Observations on @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, who she considers to have been a capable mage during his prime.

  • Her lack of information for (or relative interest in) @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna}.

A few specific dialogue options for Ro are provided below.

About Falar?

Falar, you say? Well, there was a time when the paintmonger was a capable mage in his own right. But those days are behind us. He came in to the shop one afternoon a few years back, and traded nearly all of his reagents and implements for gold. The deal was too good for me to pass up. And it seems Falar has traded in his wand for a paint brush.

About Varinna?

I don't know the artist myself, but her reputation among the locals is one of appreciation (when they aren't unsettled by her style or choice of subject matter, that is).

Exploring the Shop

Any character who takes a moment to survey the shop's shelves and display cases is able to notice the following items for sale (in addition to the full range of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000]{Spellcasting Focuses}):

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgCircletOfBlas]{Circlet of Blasting}

  • 6 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagComponentPo]{Component Pouches}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgGemOfBrightne]{Gem of Brightness}

  • [[/roll 2d3]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potions of Healing}

  • [[/roll 1d2]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgGreaterPotion]{Potions of Healing (Greater)}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgRingOfMindShi]{Ring of Mind Shielding}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll3r]{Spell Scroll, 3rd Level}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll2n]{Spell Scroll, 2nd Level}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll1s]{Spell Scroll, 1st Level}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgStaffOfThePyt]{Staff of the Python}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgWandOfMagicDe]{Wand of Magic Detection}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgWandOfMagicMi]{Wand of Magic Missiles}

Other items can be available to the party at your discretion.

Hadwyn's Hats & More.name: Hadwyn's Hats & More
Hadwyn's Hats & More.text:
You come across a makeshift stall bedecked with all sorts of clothing accessories — hats, gloves, scarves, bags, and everything in between. The gregarious Nir'ae merchant in attendence here seems excited to see you.

Well, well, well … your head looks a little lonely there, stranger! How about a fancy new headpiece from Servio, eh? Perhaps a scarf to keep your neck warm? Or a new belt for your britches? I can see you have the style of a true Ordani!

Whatever accessories you seek, Servio Hadwyn is at your service!

This provisional market stall plays host to the goods and services of Servio Hadwyn, a purveyor of hats and other clothing accessories.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Servio Hadwyn (Chaotic Good, Ordani Nir'ae, he/him)

This industrious thirty-something tailor was blacklisted by House Salva for speaking out against some of local their fashion market designs. Now, he's resigned to selling his own wares on the street — a concession that causes Servio a great deal of consternation to this day. He conceals this frustration with flamboyant salesmanship (but this facade can slip when no one's looking).

Conversation topics with that Servio is willing to discuss include (but are not limited to):

  • The high quality of his wares, which include all manner of clothing accessories.

  • His negative opinions of (and history with) House Salva.

  • Scant observations on Varinna.

  • Scant observations on Falar.

A few specific dialogue options for Servio are provided below.

About House Salva?

Contemptible rogues, the lot of them. I had the audacity to challenge their preposterous new designs last season, and it seems the revocation of my license was the punishment. In perpetuity, no less!

If you ask me, that street mural everyone's talking about is spot on. We've very little to gain from the Trading Houses, and everything to lose in return.

Speaking of which, I am losing precious time (and potential sales) with this conversation. Perhaps a new hat will lighten your mood?

About Varinna?

I've never met this Varinna, but her artwork is popular with the locals here. She has a Stoneside studio just around the bend, if I'm not mistaken.

About Falar?

The name doesn't ring a bell.

A paintmonger, you say? I understand there's a paint shop southwest of here on the docks; but fine art is not my area of purview. Can I interest you in some clothing accessories instead?

The Bread Barge.name: The Bread Barge
The Bread Barge.text:
The welcoming smells of fresh-baked bread and savory meats waft through the air of this permanently-moored canal boat, which plays host to a snug little bakery known as "The Bread Barge," as indicated by a loaf-shaped sign affixed above the front door. Inside, Ordani bakers come and go between satisfied patrons who feed their faces with overstuffed sandwiches and piping-hot soups. It's hard to imagine a cozier place to grab a bite to eat here on the canal.

This aged river barge has been permanently affixed to the canal docks and converted into a restaurant/bakery. The northern end of the barge, where the kitchen can be found, is located offscreen. The Dockside eatery caters to all sorts of clientele, with a particular focus on quick and affordable meals for people on-the-go — sandwiches, soups, wraps, and massive Arcturian sweet potatoes (roasted and buttered to perfection).

If the party visits The Bread Barge during the course of the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] event, they will likely have a series of questions to ask the staff to help aid their investigation. The following social and exploration blocks presume the characters are in search of information relevant to the @UUID[..emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest.

Conversation with the Staff

The restaurant and bakery are staffed by a variety of part-time folks with a wide range of experience, but the two head servers are usually on-hand during their respective working hours — and are always eager to make a good impression on new patrons. &Reference[food]{Meals} range in cost from Poor to Wealthy, but all are high quality.

Xavi Orfeld (Lawful Neutral, Ordani Kivahr, he/him)

This perpetually-groggy stargazer is the Barge's head server during daytime shifts. Although he enjoys his role here in the restaurant with a fair deal of enthusiasm, Xavi's head is always in the cosmos, thinking of far-off places and stranger realms than this.

Conversation topics with Xavi include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • His favorite facts and legends about Ember's moons and Inner Realms.

  • A list of daily specials, which always include the oversized Arcturian sweet potatoes, prepared in an interesting style du jour.

  • Details about the Bread Barge owners, who are members of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{House Lilifeld}. Rumor has it the owners (like many locals) have become increasingly dissatisfied with Lilifeld's excessive overreach in recent months.

  • If the party asks him about @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, Xavi will reveal that the paint monger breezes through the barge on occasional mornings, but rarely talks and never stays long.

Tula Jondak (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

This wry twenty-something scholar is the Barge's head server during evening shifts. By day, Tula studies Ordani law in the hopes that one day she'll save enough coin to move closer to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.1RJRU9XGC5WBm2Kq]{Assembly Hills} — where she diligently aims to serve as a magistrate of Precept Hall.

Conversation topics with Tula include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Her goal to become a magistrate of Precept Hall in Assembly Hills.

  • Her study routine, and her duties as head server here at The Bread Barge.

  • A list of daily specials, which always include the oversized Arcturian sweet potatoes, prepared in an interesting style du jour.

  • Details about the Bread Barge owners, who are members of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{House Lilifeld}. Their opinions of the Trading Houses are somewhat mixed. On one hand, Lilifeld keeps the city fed; on the other, they've allowed the wealthiest of Ordain's citizens to determine the rules of modern commerce.

  • If the party asks her about Falar, Tula will reveal that the paint monger sometimes comes here for evening meals before heading to his studio next door.

Exploring the Barge

The food is ample here, and the atmosphere is supremely relaxing — so much, in fact, that purloining some grub is a relatively easy task.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill sleightofhand 13]] check is able to steal [[/roll 1d2]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagRations0000]{Rations} worth of food. Everyone is allowed to get caught once, with merely a word of warning as the initial punishment. Repeat offenders, however, will be eighty-sixed with haste (and potentially get thrown overboard by multiple staff members and patrons).

Dockwood Books.name: Dockwood Books
Dockwood Books.text:
This canopy-covered landing appears to be some kind of used bookstore or community swap center. The dog-eared tomes and paperbacks here are all well-worn; indeed, some have missing covers, pages, or both. A quaint sign above the long wooden table to the west reads: "Take a book, leave a book!"

Similar placards can be found above several crates here, each one labeled "Donations" in the same unsophisticated scrawl. All of these receptacles are laughably full, with books stacked high on more than one, and others strewn about in half-forgotten disarray.

A lone shopkeep here takes inventory of what appears to be a new delivery of used books — a studious Ashka teenager with ink stains on his fingers. He offers you a respectful nod and glances at the various signs before getting back to his task.

Operated by the young shopkeep Sorian Harsa, this ramshackle stall is a used book store where locals of the Flotsam Canal Market can donate or trade pre-owned books. Most of the hardcovers and paperbacks here are in rough shape, and the low prices match the relative quality as a result.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Sorian Harsa (Chaotic Good, Ordani Ashka, he/him)

This bookish young shopkeep is an erudite 17-year-old who seeks to make his mark on the world — one salacious paperback recommendation at a time.

Conversation topics include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Sorian's ambitions as a storyteller, which include writing his own novels one day. He's hard at work on his first title, a novella-length piece of speculative fiction called The Conjurer's Apprentice.

  • The inventory here includes donations from nearby @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.iphMPgtJv5eQjGaR]{Scholar's Nook} and other neighborhood bookstores, along with used books contributed by locals.

  • He doesn't know Falar or Varinna personally, but is aware of their respective places of business.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 12]] check can immediately perceive the honesty behind Sorian's conversation and intentions, and has no reason to mistrust the wide-eyed young bookseller.

Exploring the Shop

Most of the @UUID[Item.5cG3moaInEtz15Xv]{Tattered Books} here are worth 5 gp each, and only provide a +1 bonus to any nonfiction topics contained within.

Any character with a [[/skill perception 14 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check while searching the stall is able to locate a few rarer @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Books} scattered amongst the inventory here, including titles like Mythic Wyrms of Old Akon, Cascilian Nights, and Tales of the Lonely Conscript.

  • Characters with [[/attunement signara]] or [[/knowledge legends]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Result of 17+: The character finds a folded @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagMap00000000]{Map} of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPathwaysGaz.JournalEntryPage.SZq6RXsfxKownAN6]{Sinkhole Depths} inconspicuously concealed within a mold-stained @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Book} called Plumbing the Depths: Atro's Guide to Subterranea. This map can be purchased along with the book at no extra cost.

Cluttered Dock.name: Cluttered Dock
Cluttered Dock.text:
This cluttered vestibule is stacked full of crates, sacks, and boxes full of assorted materials — none of which seem particularly valuable or interesting at a glance, as if this lonely corner of the market is half-forgotten by those who live and work here.

If the party visits this area prior to the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] and [[/eventState localColorSketchy]] quest events from @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0]{Local Color}, this dock is cluttered as described above. This obstruction prevents the characters from accessing @UUID[JournalEntry.jUCq8sac06LvGlT6.JournalEntryPage.Q8OllaH7mbfwDEXF]{Falar's Studio} to the north.

Alternately, if the party visits this area during the Local Color quest events, the dock is no longer cluttered, and allows the characters to access the door to Falar's Studio.

Exploring the Dock

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 12]] check while searching the area is able to perform a suitably exhaustive search, revealing the presence of raw materials, ingredients, and foodstuffs, including:

  • The main pile of clutter at the center section of the vestibule appears to be a conglomeration of scrap wood, splintered pallets, and empty storage containers.

  • The sacks to the east are stuffed with raw materials and ingredients like those used in the creation of paints, inks, and dyes.

  • The crates to the west contain a variety of art materials, including canvas textiles and wooden planks used for framing.

  • The barrels on the southern end of the dock have a capacity of 65 gallons each, and contain potable water.

Merchant's Quay.name: Merchant's Quay
Merchant's Quay.text:
The stone platform here is furnished with a handful of makeshift market stalls, which appear to offer everything from fresh produce to assorted gift-shop trinkets. And the ambitious vendors who operate these ramshackle booths go about their business with the gregarious demeanor of people who not only have a profit to turn, but a story to tell along with it.

This small dockside quay plays host to an assortment of vendors who lack a more permanent place to ply their wares. Despite a few fabric canopies and makeshift awnings, this modest jetty is mostly open to the elements, which communicates a more inviting and lively atmosphere as a result. If there's something a potential customer can't find elsewhere in the Flotsam Canal Market, Merchant's Quay is a great place to start.

If the characters are here for the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] or [[/eventState localColorSketchy]] events of the @UUID[..emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest, one of the merchants has more information regarding the artist Varinna's alibi — her best friend, the produce vendor Seylu Koine.

Merchants of the Quay

A handful of vendors use the quay as their regular place of business, and can usually be found here during normal shopping hours (and well into the evening). These merchants, their typical hours of operation, and their wares are detailed below — along with any information they might be able to share with the party.

Seylu's Produce

Business Hours: 8am to 5pm.

Seylu Koine (Neutral Good, Ordani Human, she/her)

This warm-hearted produce vendor sells fresh fruits and vegetables sourced from all corners of the region, and stoically operates her stall independently of House Lilifeld's influence. Seylu's crops are all sold at exceptionally reasonable prices, and she's considered to be a burgeoning community leader by her peers.

If the characters engage Seylu in conversation, she'll readily share the following information:

  • Her produce is sourced from local growers who operate their businesses independently of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.M2xns0qajMHS38kg]{House Lilifeld}.

  • She offers discounts for certain produce at the end of the work day. What she can't sell, she gives away to local vagrants.

Other details are sparse, however, as her independence from House Lilifeld comes at the cost of constant precaution. Any character who succeeds on either a [[/skill deception 13]] or [[/skill persuasion 13]] check is able to convince Seylu to share a few personal or noteworthy details.

  • Characters with [[/attunement heart]], [[/knowledge crime]], [[/knowledge intrigue]], [[/knowledge trade]], or [[/path lunarEmpath]] have @Advantage[2].

  • Characters with [[/culture emberOrdani]] automatically succeed.

Conversation topics with personal or noteworthy details that Seylu is willing to discuss include (but are not limited to):

  • Her negative opinions of the Trading Houses.

  • What little she knows of @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, who runs a @UUID[.fwXjPzq3KmQoIKJ0]{Paint Shop} just east of here.

  • Her opinion of her old friend @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna}, and their idealogical differences regarding Ordain's Trading Houses.

  • Varinna's alibi: she was having lunch with Seylu at the time.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check can readily detect the honesty that is an essential part of Seylu's character, and has no reason to doubt her various anecdotes and accounts.

A few specific dialogue options for Seylu are provided below.

About the Trading Houses?

I'm not a fan of their expansionist agendas and the control they seem to exert over nearly every aspect of life here. But I do what I can to make a difference in my own way, even if it's a simple matter of making sure some Arcturian farmers can get their crops to market.

Speaking of which, have you tried these moonshine melons?

About Falar?

The old curmudgeon doesn't bother with niceties when he comes and goes. His paint shop behind us is open most days, and he spends a lot of evenings in his studio space across the way. But he isn't much of a conversationalist unless you're buying something.

From what I understand, he also doesn't paint much these days. Capitalism can crush your soul, man.

About Varinna?

Seylu stifles a bit of a knowing smile.

We've known each other since we were kids. She's a lot to handle, but she means the world to me. I was pretty disappointed when I found out she's hooked up with House Salva, but I suppose a starving artist has to actually eat every once in a while.

Her friendship means more to me than politics. But we can have our moments.

Varinna's Alibi?

Seylu's brow furrows with incredulousness.

There's no chance Varinna is responsible for those murals. I was with her in her studio that day. She gets so obsessed with her work, she can't even be trusted to take care of herself. So I took her some potato and leak soup to make sure she didn't wither away into some oblong shape, like one of those feisty ladies in her paintings.

She smiles at the thought of the erotic abstract paintings in Varinna's studio.

And it's a damn good soup recipe, if I do say so.

Scooter Geary's Discount Tools

Business Hours: 8am to 7pm.

Scooter Geary (Chaotic Neutral, Ordani Hulg'run, he/him)

An intrepid adventurer on the weekends, Scooter Geary is one of Flotsam's most beloved scoundrels. His Merchant's Quay stall caters to rogues and dungeoneers, and has nearly anything an explorer might need to replenish their inventory before their next jaunt.

Scooter's wares on any given day include at least one of each item from the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000.JournalEntryPage.ibFcHkHH1icuT3l8] and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000.JournalEntryPage.GCvg8n7Q7ltSPRxe] equipment lists, along with a wide array of standard @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbEquipment0000.JournalEntryPage.fWDbFyRcjabZV9lW].

Conversation topics with Scooter include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Errant small-talk and rumors he's picked up from customers.

  • His somewhat neutral opinions about Ordain's Trading Houses.

  • He has a bit of a crush on Seylu, but this adoration is unrequited (and he's fine with that).
