  • Observations on Falar.

  • Observations on Varinna.

Scooter is an open book, with nothing to hide (other than the details of his next dungeon crawl). Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 12]] check can assess his honesty with ease.

About Falar?

Mixing paints seems like a rather boring way to make a living, but what do I know … I crawl through cobwebbed vaults for fun.

About Varinna?

She's a talented lass, and a good friend to dear Seylu over there.

You detect a hint of longing in the Hulg'run's eye as he mentiones the fruit vendor across the quay.

Maybe one of these days I'll invest a few gold pieces in one of those paintings of hers. Fun stuff. Kind of crazy and abstract, like a dustweed hallucination — not that I know what that's like or anything …

Yorm's Freshwater Grill

Business Hours: 7am to 9pm.

Narius Yorm (Lawful Neutral, Arcturian Kivahr, he/him)

This chronically-relaxed fisherman runs a humble grill at the center of the quay, which he dutifully stokes throughout the day while offering a delicious selection of local freshwater fish. A relative expert on the local waterways and a man of few words, Yorm has an absurdly brief tale to spin about every fish he's ever caught.

Yorm's wares on any given day include a modest selection of seasoned freshwater fish, caught that day by the chef himself, piping hot from the grill (count as Poor or Modest &Reference[food]{Meals}, depending on the quality of fish).

Conversation topics with Yorm include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Errant small-talk and rumors he's picked up from customers.

  • His neutral opinions about Ordain's Trading Houses.

  • Observations on Falar.

  • Observations on Varinna.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check can tell that Yorm is being forthcoming and honest with his responses.

About Falar?

He doesn't like my fish!

About Varinna?

The artist? Isn't she Seylu's girlfriend?

Good Spirits

Business Hours: 10am to 7pm.

Harden Korulios (Chaotic Good, Ordani Human, he/him)

This perpetually inebriated raconteur is a purveyor of fine wines and alcoholic spirits, including his own home-brewed Ordani table wine. Harden lovingly taste-tests each of his wares, and is always eager to trade a good story about the winding roads between here and there.

Harden's wares on any given day include [[/roll 1d2]] bottles of each of the following:

  • @UUID[Item.4mIj4qrLgMompEZG]{Arcturian Liquor}

  • @UUID[Item.yOKHQCpRHaGZSThQ]{Ordani Wine (Common)} (Double the rolled result).

  • @UUID[Item.xc6x6YcqbFHBjnFp]{Ordani Wine (Fine)} (Double the rolled result).

  • @UUID[Item.jnKYsmCYNNP21aYF]{Seawall Brandy}

  • @UUID[Item.Pxu2HNJreTBnqI5w]{Shadowcap Wine}

  • @UUID[Item.XweVxnBoA5aDhoLa]{Waterborne Whiskey}

Conversation topics with Harden include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Errant small-talk and rumors he's picked up from customers.

  • His skeptical opinions about Ordain's Trading Houses.

  • Observations on Falar.

  • Observations on Varinna.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 13]] check can tell that Harden is being forthcoming and honest with his responses.

About Falar?

Every once in a while, the old-timer will stop by for a bottle or two, but he never has much to say. A bit unfriendly, if you ask me.

About Varinna?

I'm more of a music guy myself. Not much of a fine art enthusiast, if you know what I mean. But she seems like a nice lady. Seylu over there would have more to say about it. They go way back.

Exploring the Quay

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 15]] check while searching the area finds a forgotten [[/award 1pp]] lodged beneath one of the planks atop the quay, stamped with the seal of Naloria Vale — the domain of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberBestiary000.JournalEntryPage.U39JWvasyCgtyXQI]{Casia} known as @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.RPVn1KLLcutCzYcv]{Vesper}.

  • Characters with [[/ancestry emberKiska]] or [[/attunement primordis]] have @Advantage[2].

Mysteriously, this coin (or another just like it), reappears in the exact same spot on the quay whenever one of Ember's moons reaches its zenith. Only one of these curious @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.16sqn71JsCkghaTt]{Primordial} coins is present at any given time, and the cause of this phenomenon remains an undiscovered mystery (much like the coin itself).

Cobblestone's.name: Cobblestone's
Cobblestone's.text:
The sickly sweet smell of shoe polish nearly bowls you over as you step into the front room of this cluttered shoe repair shop, where an aged Kivahr cobbler works intently to mend a sole-less boot. He greets you with a nod and a smile, his crystal spectacles gleaming in the lantern light.

Owned and operated by the talented leatherworker Brod Balehammer, this small shoe repair shop is crammed full of decades worth of tools, materials, and inventory — including more than a few single shoes that are missing a partner.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Brod Balehammer (Lawful Good, Ordani Kivahr, he/him)

On top of his unrivaled skill as a cobbler, this aged shopkeep possesses an avuncular charm that his customers tend to find well worth the long-winded stories he tells.

Conversation topics include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • Brod's six decades as a cobbler in Ordain, and the pride he has in his work.

  • His inventory (see "Exploring the Shop" below).

  • Observations on Falar.

  • Observations on Varinna.

A few specific dialogue options for Brod are provided below.

About Falar?

I've been here long enough to remember when Finnegan's tea house was on that end of the docks. Falar has been mixing his paints there now for quite some time. Come to think of it … in all these years, he's never come by my shop.

About Varinna?

She's the artist who lives down the lane, Stoneside. I run into her every once in a while down at The Parched Lark. As a matter of fact, they've got a few of her pieces on display. Sketches and studies, really. But interesting stuff.

Exploring the Shop

Multiple sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulCobblersTo]{Cobbler's Tools} can be found strewn about the shop, along with at least one set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulLeatherwor]{Leatherworker's Tools}.

A variety of mundane boots and shoes are for sale, plus one pair of each of the following (400 gp each):

  • @UUID[Item.e9JtZ5KLQSKagAEf]{Primordian Boots}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgBootsOfStridi]{Boots of Striding and Springing}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgBootsOfTheWin]{Boots of the Winterlands}

Falar's Studio (Upper).name: Falar's Studio (Upper)
Falar's Studio (Upper).text:
This zigzag chamber is unmistakably the studio of some prolific visual artist, and — judging from the abundance of paints and other materials here — an artist that specializes in the creation (or use) of novel pigments, mediums, and techniques. Over a half-dozen tables placed about the room are littered with countless jars, urns, bottles, and cans containing various oil paints and chemical solvents. Odors of alcohol and turpentine linger here, along with the earthy smells of natural pigments.

Along with @UUID[.Q8OllaH7mbfwDEXF]{Falar's Studio (Lower)}, this Stoneside-level dwelling is owned by the retired adventurer @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, a wizard-turned-shopkeep who plays a central role in the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] and [[/eventState localColorSketchy]] events of the @UUID[..emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest.

The spacious studio here serves as Falar's private workroom, and bears the trademark signs of an experienced artist. This upstairs chamber spans the length two downstairs areas (and the 10-foot canal between): @UUID[.Q8OllaH7mbfwDEXF]{Falar's Studio (Lower)} to the west, and @UUID[.VfumF2r8uCyNAVhR]{The Bread Barge} to the east.

The easternmost door here leads to the Stoneside platform via a wooden gangway that can be raised and lowered using a lever downstairs. Additionally, the illusory painting that obscures the stairway downstairs is a one-way image, and can't be seen from this side of the permanent illusion.

Interactable: Destructible Shelves

The nine shelving units in the chamber here are destructible, and can be destroyed by any character who targets them with an &Reference[attack] action (AC 15, 8 hp).

Each of the shelving units are @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.lNMkySfNYWS3EvIk#interactable-objects]{Interactable Objects}, and can be toggled between their undamaged or destroyed states via the interaction tool in the Scene Controls interface on the left side of the screen.

Upper Gangway Controls

A lever next to the door on the eastern wall controls the wooden gangway that spans the gap between Falar's Studio (Upper) and the Stoneside area of the map. This timber gangway is normally raised, but can be lowered by the characters during the [[/eventState localColorSketchy]] event.

Exploring the Studio

A brief examination of the room reveals the following:

  • The studio appears to also serve as an ersatz living area, with signs of impromptu bedding and other accoutrements.

  • The studio contains nine shelving units that cater to the storage of paint and other art materials, including at least one set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulPaintersSu]{Painter's Supplies}.

  • Several pieces of curious art here match the style and mediums of the House Salva mural from the [[/eventState localColorDrawing]] event, and also appear similar to @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna's} style.

Any character who has previously visited Varinna's Studio and succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 13]] check while examining the curious art is able to determine that the art pieces were painted to resemble Varinna's style, but that they are clearly from the hand of another artist. Some of Varinna's original art can be found nearby, no doubt used for reference during the creation of these forgeries.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge arts]] or [[/knowledge forensics]] have @Advantage[2].

Any character who spends at least 10 minutes while searching the room is also able to locate the following:

  • An inert @UUID[Item.fdy47m1duEeHMYJa]{Anachraenum Medallion} that seems to have lost its arcane potential.

  • Several invitations to wealthy galas, dated many moons ago.

  • Falar's @UUID[Item.EhupjfsvIapLdTFO]{Notes on Elemental Binding}.

Any character who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 13]] check while searching the room also discovers:

  • @UUID[Item.PwlNz4dMT6MjoCzK]{Falar's Curious Note}.

  • A @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgSpellScroll2n]{Spell Scroll} of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplNystulsMag]{Arcanist's Magic Aura}.

A character who casts the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell while searching the studio is able to locate the presence of the 5 @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg]{Paint Globlins} using their @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.YuWV6xJkkLVkzahM]{Paint Form} to hide here, but the precise nature of the creatures isn't readily apparent.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge elementals]] can identify the hidden Paint Globlins as elemental creatures.

  • Characters with [[/attunement cora]] or [[/knowledge cosmology]] can identify the latent presence of lunar magic from the earth moon @UUID[JournalEntry.emberCosmos00000.JournalEntryPage.5pD8lxiilJJXOgoa]{Cora}.

The moment one of the characters disturbs any of the paints or paintings here (including the Varinna forgeries), 5 @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg]{Paint Globlins} leap out of the forged paintings to attack the characters. Read the following aloud:

@Embed[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg count=5 readaloud="Just then, the otherworldly cackle of some small creature echoes throughout the room. Then another … Then another … Soon enough, the surfaces of five of the paintings here begin to shudder with curious arcane undulations before a small oily monster climbs its way out of each portrait. These stout creatures have stubby legs and arms, and their multicolor bodies appear to be formed from psychedelic splatters of various paints — countless hues constantly swirling around each other, desperately refusing to blend. Their maniacal eyes scan the room as they slosh forth into battle, held together by some unseen magical force, eager to mete out some punishment for your tresspass."]

Paint Globlin Tactics

These strange elemental creatures are intensely chaotic, and revel in mess and disorder. They attack exuberantly without much coordination or strategy, sometimes choosing actions that create more mess than physical harm.

During the first round of combat, at least 2 of the Paint Globlins will use their @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.xfAFqQSGG0QxJupA]{Glob Lob} attacks against potential ranged threats, while the rest of the Globlins will use their @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.D7ylQD0qJCDQZcCx]{Paint Roller} bonus action to close ranks with enemy characters.

  • They will happily plow through shelves and furniture when using their Paint Roller ability, showing no regard for the damage they will do.

  • Once they've engaged a character in melee combat, each Paint Globlin will use its @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.MYOzrqDwpuizBIhz]{Clobber} attack against adjacent enemies.

  • Paint Globlins may use their action to topple the shelves of paint onto players, dealing [[/damage 1d6 bludgeoning]] damage if they are adjacent to the shelf when it falls over.

  • When they die their @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.HJQnsFvfrAFumrCY]{Death Burst} feature triggers, potentially blinding enemy combatants, which become preferred targets for other Paint Globlins.

  • The Paint Globlins will fight to the death, and will either pursue enemies outside of the immediate area or target them with ranged @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.xfAFqQSGG0QxJupA]{Glob Lob} attacks.

Varinna's Studio (Upper).name: Varinna's Studio (Upper)
Varinna's Studio (Upper).text:
This upstairs foyer is cluttered with an assortment of art supplies. Several brushes, pots of various paints, and an array of dog-eared reference texts are scattered across the tables here — all stained with various shades of an artist's fingerprints.

Along with @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna's Studio (Lower)}, this Promenade-level area serves as the home studio and private residence of the accomplished Ordani artist known as Varinna — who plays an important role in the [[/eventState localColorArtists]] event of the @UUID[..emberLocalColor0]{Local Color} side quest.

During daytime hours, Varinna can be found working downstairs in the studio proper. She retires to the upstairs area for long rests and whenever she needs to retrieve something from the miscellaneous storage of the foyer.

Exploring the Foyer

The storage area here contains assorted tools and art materials, including 2 sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulPaintersSu]{Painter's Supplies}, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.content24.JournalEntry.phbMountsAndVehi.JournalEntryPage.NVPIUDJEdFDaErTg]{Cart}, 2 @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagLadder00000]{Ladders}, and [[/roll 1d2+1]] nonfiction @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Books} about art history and technique.

The chamber to the south of the foyer is Varinna's bedroom, and is in a constant state of half-forgotten disarray — an apt reflection of the importance the artist places on tidiness (or distinct lack thereof).

The bedroom here is inviting, yet bears the distinct air of desuetude, as if no one actually spends much time here. A stale loaf of bread lies half-forgotten on the side cabinet, and the unkempt bed looks like someone sleeps on top of the sheets rather than beneath them.

Exploring the Bedroom

Any character who takes a moment to Search the room will find [[/roll 1d2]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagBook0000000]{Books} and [[/roll 1d2]] @UUID[Item.5cG3moaInEtz15Xv]{Tattered Books}, spanning subjects from fictional romance to existential philosophy, along with a random @UUID[RollTable.BUurPyycyDIuox5L]{Arcturian Trinket}.

The locked chest on the southern wall can be opened with either a successful [[/tool thief 18]] or [[/skill athletics 20]] check, and contains 245 gp, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagPerfume0000]{Perfume}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagClothesFine]{Fine Clothes}, an heirloom @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbwepHandaxe000]{Handaxe}, and an @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagEntertainer]{Entertainer's Pack}.

Heel and Sole.name: Heel and Sole
Heel and Sole.text:
The Signborn shoemaker here makes ample use of their four hands while working this small stall, which appears to be overstuffed with quality footwear from all four corners of Ordain.

This market stall is the business place of the Signborn cobbler Narro Pinz, who provides quality repairs on top of a modest inventory of locally-designed footwear for sale.

Conversation with the Shopkeep

Narro Pinz (Lawful Good, Ordani Signborn, They/Them)

This industrious shoemaker never sits still while working the four corners of their stall, all four Signborn hands working as fast as they possibly can. Narro talks almost as fast as they work, and believes that "good enough" is the enemy of perfect.

Conversation topics include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • If asked about @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar} they notes that the old paint maker stops by occasionally to get his shoes fixed or shined. He never has anything nice to say about anyone, but Falar always tips.

  • If asked about @UUID[.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{Varinna}, they say that Varinna's art is a bit too chaotic for them. They prefer classic fantasy styles.

  • If asked about Seylu in the quay, they maintain she's very nice, and always shares her leftover fruit. She's close friends with Varinna, but their friendship hasn't always been smooth sailing, so to speak.

Exploring the Shop

Multiple sets of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulCobblersTo]{Cobbler's Tools} can be found on the various surfaces here, along with at least one set of @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbtulLeatherwor]{Leatherworker's Tools}. These belong to Narro, and are not for sale.

Narro offers shoe repair, cleaning, customization, and simple shining services. Prices range between 1 sp and 10 gp, depending on the desired service. They also sell resoled and repaired shoes for discount prices; the workmanship is of an expert quality, but the items are all mundane.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Requirements

This side quest occurs during Chapter 3, and begins while the party is traversing @UUID[JournalEntry.umX2Xt1eMUC0ECgc.JournalEntryPage.4gRSL7Tq1pgccdIW]{Ordain}. There are no prerequisites for this quest.

Difficulty

"Local Color" is designed for a party of Level 4 characters.

Milestone Progression

This is a Side Quest that awards 1 @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Point}, upon successful completion of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] Event.

While traveling through Ordain the party encounters a vibrant mural depicting the cruelty of House Salva as it lords its success, recognition and fame over the fashion and textile communities. Here they meet Cherish Ellerie, a young but ambitious member of House Salva, who is more curious about the mural than insulted. However, this art is interactive in a most dangerous way, and soon the party is beset by chaotic elementals made of magically infused paint. Having saved Cherish and their own skin, two pressing questions remain: who made this mural, and are there others like it in the city?

"Local Color" will take the party on an adventure from the working-class Flotsam district of Ordain to the high-fashion nexus of Gossamer, allowing them to see both sides of the city's artistic and textile cultures. In both locations they will speak to locals, hear their insights and opinions on the city, the government, and the Trading Houses, while also trying to figure out who is creating the unsigned and magically charged murals in the city.

With a sharp eye and good social skills, the party might just be able to figure out who is responsible, what they want, and what will be necessary to put a stop to their protests against Ordain itself. But it won't be simple: the culprit is an embittered old adventurer with an extensive set of skills and spells at their disposal, and some help from the moon of Cora. Perhaps, though, the party won't find fault in the culprit's actions, and instead will decide to let him go! A game of cat and mouse, differing perspectives, and hard choices awaits the party as they explore the city's local color.

Involved Characters

  • @UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]{Cherish Ellerie}, a project coordinator working for House Salva, and the main point of contact for this quest.

  • @UUID[Actor.i5jXHUyZCPBJDb2k]{Mistress Caberi}, the magnificent head of House Salva.

  • Varinna, an up-and-coming painter and muralist recently commissioned by House Salva. Her style is being copied in an attempt to frame her and damage her reputation.

Dangers & Enemies

  • @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar}, a retired adventurer and wizard who has become increasingly fed up with Ordain and what he perceives as its numerous failings.

  • @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg], a small mass of chaotic paint animated by unpredictable elemental energies and created by Falar.

  • @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf], large, artistically rendered creatures not unlike a large cat, animated by elemental energies and created by Falar.
Overview.soverview:
Long ago an adventurer known as Falar struck out to find success in Ordain, and for a while he did well for himself. A man of charm and intelligence, he quickly found allies, made connections to high society, and built a small fortune for himself as a purveyor of magical knowledge and tricks for other ambitious adventurers. However, every luxury and laurel that Ordain can bestow it can take away, and through a series of poor decisions, chance encounters, and soured relationships, Falar watched everything he'd spent his life building vanish overnight.

Forced to sell off his extensive magical library to pay off creditors, Falar was left with nothing to his name but a few deeds to ramshackle buildings in Flotsam. Having lost all taste for adventuring, Ordain, and magic, he retired into obscurity and was never heard of again. For many years he lived life as a simple paint monger, and even tried to rebuild himself as an artist, but Ordain has a long memory, and Falar still harbored grudges which made success difficult.

Now, years later, an anonymous artist has begun creating murals across Ordain criticizing and drawing attention to aspects of the city, its culture, and government which some might find distasteful or dubious. Their first target is the mighty House Salva, and the iron hand they use to control the vast textile and fashion industries that dominate the culture of Ordain. While this would be uncomfortable but tolerable in most situations, the artist has begun to escalate, and people may die as a result if someone doesn't intervene.

What begins with a chance encounter with a mural, a House Salva member, and some chaotic elements is a series of events that will take the party across Ordain from the working-class canals of Flotsam to the heart of House Salva's operations in Gossamer, all in pursuit of Falar as he creates a series of elementally charged murals. Will the party be able to uncover his identity, and stop him? Or will they find merit to his complaints against Ordain?

Drawing Attention.name: Drawing Attention
Drawing Attention.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this Combat Event, the party encounters @UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]{Cherish Ellerie}, a liaison of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{House Salva}, just before a pack of @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg]{Paint Globlins} emerge from a mural and attack. In this Event, the party can:

  • Get to know Cherish and learn more about House Salva and its role in Ordain.

  • Investigate the mural and its paint to learn more about its mysterious creator.

  • Encounter Paint Globlins, a strange and chaotic form of earth elemental.

This event is modestly more likely to happen during the day than at night.

Chatting With Cherish

@Embed[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]

Who are you?

Ah! So sorry, forgot my manners there for a moment. I'm Cherish Ellerie, nice to meet you. Who are you?

What do you do in Ordain?

I work for House Salva, primarily as a project overseer for various things in the trade house such as textile manufacturing and clothing production, but my main expertise is design. I've also been getting myself attached to other things, like I'm helping pick the roster for next season's style trend, and have helped arrange the Art Ramble event the last two years.

What's the Art Ramble?

Oh, it's great! House Salva brings in a bunch of artists to create murals on the walkways in the Redwalk Ramble. It's happening soon, you should absolutely come by and check it out. There'll be food, and drinks, live music, art and clothing for sale, and a sneak peek at the next season's style.

This is about House Salva?

Seems like it! House Salva's expertise is textiles, and the clothing made from them. At the top are the experts in those fields, picking the best of the year's production, guiding the markets, celebrating the best of the year's artists, and setting fashion trends across the city. It's exclusive, to be sure, and I think the artist is bitter about that.

Who made this?

I'm not sure, the style looks familiar, I feel like I've seen their work somewhere before, but I can't recall the artist's name.

Style Points

Any character with a [[/skill perception 18 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 16]] check observes that the lines and the style are very clean, indicating someone who is well-versed in creating art pieces at this sort of scale. However, without other styles to compare to, it's impossible to know more about the artist.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge arts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Wet Paint

Any character with a [[/skill investigation 16 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 14]] check notes that the paint is fresh but fully dried, meaning it's been on this wall for at least a day, if not longer. The scale of the painting indicates that there were likely scaffolds and days of work involved.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge arts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Characters that cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} notice an aura of abjuration magic radiating from the mural.

[[/outcome examinedSalvaMural]]

Globlin Attack

[[/outcome attack]]

Your conversation with Cherish is cut short as the surface of the mural ripples and several small humanoid forms made of paint fall to the ground, leaving large splats of color where they land.

That's new...

The paint creatures stand up, fix their eyes on you and Cherish, and begin to advance.

@Embed[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg]

Paint Globlin Tactics

These strange elemental creatures are intensely chaotic, and revel in mess and disorder. They attack exuberantly without much coordination or strategy.

  • Once they've engaged a character in melee combat, each Paint Globlin will use its @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.MYOzrqDwpuizBIhz]{Clobber} attack against adjacent enemies.

  • When they die their @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.HJQnsFvfrAFumrCY]{Death Burst} feature triggers, potentially blinding enemy combatants, which become preferred targets for other Paint Globlins.

  • The Paint Globlins will fight to the death, and will either pursue enemies outside of the immediate area or target them with ranged @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg.Item.xfAFqQSGG0QxJupA]{Glob Lob} attacks.

Cherish Tactics

Cherish is unarmed but not afraid to defend herself. She will retreat to safety, leaving the encounter, if her hit points are reduced to half their maximum.

  • Cherish may use @UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1.Item.WDtEi6LhW4UuuLuN]{Heroism} on herself when the fight begins to improve her odds of surviving the encounter.

  • Cherish uses her Attacks with her @UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1.Item.q3QerP5lcv81lsWo] attack against enemies in melee range.

  • Cherish can cast @UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1.Item.esA77AaqTOglB90q]{Healing Word} on injured characters to help keep them alive, or on herself if she gets too badly wounded.

[[/outcome defeated]]

Attack Aftermath

With the last globlin defeated, you have a chance to survey the area, and it is splattered with paint. Much of the mural's lower half has been ruined by the explosive demise each globlin underwent, and the ground is similarly coated with a thin, vibrant layer of paints, the colors blending into unattractive gray-brown wash in places.

Cherish looks at herself, trying to wipe paint from her face and arms, but only smearing it in the attempt.

This was a new outfit, too. It's lucky you were here, I might have been in real trouble if they caught me out here alone. Thanks for the help!

What were those?

Good question! I've never seen anything like those before. They were made out of paint, right? Maybe there's magic runes hidden in the art, or maybe the paint is magic? This isn't really my area of expertise, my sister is the spellcaster in the family.

Where would someone get magic paint?

Off the top of my head, I know there's a lot of art supplies sold in Flotsam at the canal market. I'd expect there's almost certainly someone selling it there. Certainly there are other places in the city, but I don't know them offhand.

Examining the Mural

Any character with a [[/skill investigation 16 passive format=long]], [[/skill arcana 16 passive format=long]], or who succeeds on a [[/skill investigation 14]] or [[/skill arcana 14]] check note that there are no hidden magical symbols, marks, or runes in the mural. Whatever spawned the paint globlins had to be contained in the paint itself.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge arts]] have @Advantage[2] on this check.

Examining the Paint

The splatter of paint left over from the creatures is filled with strange mineral flecks that glimmer brightly on their own. Examining the components of the paint at the source of its creation is the only sure way to know how these creatures were made.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge arts]] know that paints can often have metallic elements included to give them a glittering appearance, which this may be, and is not indicative of anything untoward.

  • Characters with [[/attunement emberCora]] sense the faintest of connection to these flecks, as though they bear a small measure of magic from the moon itself.

  • Characters that cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} notice an aura of abjuration magic coming from the mural, and conjuration magic where the globlins once stood. Both are rapidly deteriorating in the wake of the globlin attack.

Cherish Departs

Cherish fusses at some of the paint splattered on her before giving a sigh of resignation.

Okay, I'm going to go see if I can salvage this outfit. You should swing by Silver Street in Gossamer tomorrow, or whenever, and look me up. I've got my office there, and I'd like to formally reward you.


I could give you a new set of clothes to replace what you're wearing now, at least. Nice clothing too, in style, expertly made. I've got access to the good stuff thanks to House Salva.


Anyhow, hope to see you, bye!

Cherish offers a wave, and promptly sets off, leaving you with the aftermath of the fight and a few leads.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished investigating the mural and the battle's messy aftermath, they can go to Flotsam for clues about the paint ([[/eventState localColorArtists]]) or Gossamer to meet with Cherish ([[/eventState localColorFashion]]). The party will also begin encountering more murals in the city via the repeatable [[/eventState localColorCommentary]] event.
Drawing Attention.soverview: While traveling through Ordain, the party encounters a liaison of House Salva inspecting a large painted mural, and must defend her from a pack of paint globlins.
Drawing Attention.sexposition:
You see a finely dressed woman standing before the broad wall of a building, admiring a huge mural painted across the pale stone. The paint still holds a sheen, not yet dry, and the art depicts several towering figures clad in fine clothing, each admiring bolts of cloth. Gathered at their feet is a mob of smaller figures holding up their own offerings of woven textiles in the hope of being recognized. Some of these figures appear desperate to be noticed; others are bent crooked as they sob, resigned to their fate.

The woman hears your approach, glancing over her shoulder once before turning to address you more directly. She gestures to the mural and says:

Certainly not a flattering take on House Salva, is it?
Drawing Attention.ssummary: While traveling through Ordain, we encountered Cherish, a liaison of House Salva, as she was inspecting a large painted mural. As we talked, a pack of paint globlins emerged from the mural and attacked. We survived, but our clothes did not.

Mixed Media.name: Mixed Media
Mixed Media.text:
Overview

This Exploration Event takes the party to Ordain's @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.hKNuD0yWUAA6UmDA]{Flotsam} district, where they can investigate a small community of crafters, artists, and merchants for information about an inflammatory mural recently discovered in the area. During this Event, the characters can:

  • Meet and interview Varinna, an aspiring artist just recently commissioned by House Salva, and the suspected artist responsible for the mural.

  • Meet and interview Falar, an old adventurer and mage turned paint monger, the actual culprit behind the mural.

  • Interact with various locals who can provide further insight into the principal characters in this event, and their backgrounds.

Area Walkthrough

The party begins in the @UUID[Scene.emberFlotsamMark] scene where the central gameplay of this event transpires. A complete room-by-room description of the market environment and the gameplay that occurs there is detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.jUCq8sac06LvGlT6] walkthrough.

Investigating Varinna

As the party investigates Varinna and @UUID[JournalEntry.jUCq8sac06LvGlT6.JournalEntryPage.JZYlp0m4lOeAUouS]{her studio}, check the appropriate outcome boxes below.

[[/outcome metVarinna]]

[[/outcome confirmedAlibi]]

[[/outcome investigatedStudio]]

Varinna is Innocent

Varinna is not the artist responsible for the mural, and is being actively framed by another party. To learn this, the party needs to do the following:

  • Question her about her views on Salva, and where she was recently.

  • Follow up on her alibi with Seylu Koine

  • Examine her art to see if it matches the mural.

A party that does this would reasonably conclude that Varinna lacks the motive and opportunity necessary to be the culprit. If the party [[/eventState localColorFashion cherishFirst]] as part of @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.ooARWZr1voKdluXx], then they should arrive with the ability to invoke Mistress Caberi's name to force more ready compliance.

Investigating Falar

As the party investigates Falar and @UUID[JournalEntry.jUCq8sac06LvGlT6.JournalEntryPage.fwXjPzq3KmQoIKJ0]{his shop}, check the appropriate outcome boxes below.

[[/outcome metFalar]]

[[/outcome examinedPaint]]

Falar is the Culprit

The artist responsible for the mural is @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih], but this shouldn't be obvious to the party immediately. In fact, Falar does all that he can to pass himself off as a simple, disgruntled paint monger.

A party that speaks to him during this event should be expected to find him hard to deal with, bitter, and highly critical of Ordain, but not likely to be the source of the mural. His displayed art is neither good enough nor the same style, and while he lacks an alibi, he isn't the only person in the market area that dislikes Salva.

Falar's Motives

Bitter that Varinna has begun to taste success, he has started painting murals in her art style to discredit her and harm her reputation. Deep down, he wants to hurt Salva more than anything, and harbors no true ill will toward Varinna. In truth, she was the most convenient scapegoat, and if pressed later in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5], will even admit guilt over hurting her to get at Salva.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished interviewing the various characters around the market, they should head for @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.0V2KtTURXT8WaxfX]{Gossamer} to report to Cherish Ellerie on their findings in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.ooARWZr1voKdluXx].
Mixed Media.soverview: Arriving in the Flotsam Canal Market, the party chases down leads about the mural artist and possible source of the paint globlins that leapt from it. If they already visited Cherish, they will arrive with knowledge about Varinna, and a means to coerce her into cooperation.
Mixed Media.sexposition: The white stone of the market promenade stands stark against the makeshift docks and boardwalks that span the canal below. The swift waters of the Destine run slow here, channeled around the location's ramshackle landmarks: quays of earth and stone, timber structures cobbled together from repurposed wood, and a scattered array of small boats and other vessels.
Mixed Media.ssummary: We canvassed the Flotsam Canal Market, talking to the locals and learning what we can about Varinna as a possible source of the slanderous mural against House Salva.

Outside the Lines.name: Outside the Lines
Outside the Lines.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This Social Event introduces Cherish (Salva’s point-woman) and Mistress Caberi (head of House Salva, a Shard Goddess). The party will accomplish the following:

  • They will be thanked and rewarded by Cherish, and have a chance to glimpse Salva’s ethos

  • They will be given useful information for the next part of their investigation in Flotsam. Depending on when they visit Cherish, the nature of this information changes.

Cherish’s office is a gallery of labor and luxury, a mixture of fine furniture covered in samples of cloth and bolts of silk and rolling racks of fine clothing awaiting examination. The center of the space is dominated by a large table covered in papers bearing patterns and sketches of clothing.

Cherish looks up from a sketch, smiles with genuine warmth, and gestures you in.

Hello! Welcome!

She gestures to her office, and the state of things.

Please excuse the clutter, I've got a lot on right now, so things are a bit… eh, scattered.

Cherish's Gratitude

She gestures toward the racks of clothing bearing every hue and style one can imagine.

There, those racks, choose what pleases you. Consider it my thanks, and a remedy for what the paint monsters ruined.

Fine Clothing

Each character gains one set of @UUID[Item.rfXJp1hjlLUOGFsu]{Exquisite Clothes}. Keeping or reselling is at the player’s discretion.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crafts]] or Proficiency with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbtulWeaversToo]{Weaver's Tools} recognize many are hand-worked masterpieces that demanded long hours and rare skill to create. Many feature materials that were likely very expensive to procure, such as rare gems, metal fixtures, or specialty textiles.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge trade]] or Proficiency with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbtulWeaversToo]{Weaver's Tools} note that these outfits would be worth hundreds of gold to the right buyer. Coinwealth, Marlstone, or Koto Springs would be more favorable districts to sell in.

  • [[/path emberCosmopolitanFashionista]] characters realize the materials used to make these items were likely sourced through Salva’s routes and markets, allowing the trading house to profit twice over.

Where'd these clothes come from?

"Samples and trials from Ordain’s finest designers — pieces that did not make next season’s final procession. Many are one-of-a-kind. If a piece does not suit you, sell it. They do me more good in your hands than gathering dust."

Shouldn't the clothing be returned?

"No. These were granted to House Salva and placed in my care. Designers know that inclusion in our season carries a cost. The garments are payment toward a chance at favor."

Social Immobility

[[/culture Ordani]] characters, [[/path emberCosmopolitanFashionista]] characters, and characters with [[/knowledge politics]] note House Salva’s taste can begin or end a career; their word sets fashion for the city. The articles of clothing in Cherish's care all represent those who were deemed unfit for that blessing.

What does Salva do?

"We make Ordain, Ordain. From raw fiber to woven cloth to finished tapestries, garments, and flooring, Salva shepherds all of it from field to loom to market."

Market Control

[[/path emberCosmopolitanFashionista]] characters and characters with [[/knowledge trade]] recognize Salva’s near-captive market here. Most weavers and tailors must deal through Salva to sell in Ordain, or to have enough material to work at scale.

Caberi's Arrival

@Embed[Actor.i5jXHUyZCPBJDb2k]

A hush falls as the lacquered door behind you opens, and Cherish inclines her head toward the arrival. A moment later she stiffens and sharply turns to address the new arrival. When she speaks, her surprise is immediately apparent.

Mistress Caberi, hello! This is an unexpected surprise!

Caberi releases a little giggle of amusement at Cherish's awkwardness.

My dear, I heard that you encountered a bit of chaos in the streets and wanted to come visit. Ordain has had enough of grim surprises as of late, and I wanted to be sure you were okay. But first, who are your guests?

Cherish pivots to look at you and says:

Utterly fine, thanks to my guests, whom I'll let handle introductions on their own!

Caberi graces you with a smile so bright and powerful that it causes a warmth to bloom in your chest. She says nothing, instead waiting for you to introduce yourselves.

The players should be encouraged to introduce their characters before moving on.

Head of Salva

Characters with [[/knowledge politics]] or who succeed on a [[/skill history 14]] check recognize Mistress Caberi as both the current head of House Salva and the former Holy Speaker of the Cindaric Sages, a position she held over four hundred years ago.

Characters with [[/knowledge legends]] or who succeed on a [[/skill religion 15]] check recall that rumors and legends persist around Mistress Caberi, claiming that she is a being of immense power, perhaps even a Shard God. Her remarkable longevity is often cited as one of the reasons for this rumor persisting.

Speaking With Mistress Caberi

Mistress Caberi's Identity

Mistress Caberi is secretly a powerful godlike being known as the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000.JournalEntryPage.FaUiibd3k4gfrzry]{Soul of Fashion}. Reference her entry in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberDeities0000]{Deities} journal for more information.

What do you do in House Salva?

Caberi smiles brightly at the question.

"My dear, I herd visionaries toward greatness! I keep the city's looms from tangling, and make sure all within Ordain remain inspired by the efforts of House Salva! Also, many, many, many meetings."

What are your aspirations for Salva?

There is a spark of excitement in Mistress Caberi's eyes at the question.

"I have great aspirations for Salva. Long it has busied itself with all things woven, but I consider that just one thread in the great tapestry of life. I would have us weave all art together, dance and music, painting and sculpture, every thread becoming part of a bright tapestry that celebrates the act of turning inspiration into creation."

Sensing Caberi's Agenda

Characters that succeed on a [[/skill insight 14]] check intuit a sense of genuine fondness for artists, creation, and creativity. Mistress Caberi seems to hold a reverence for creation that borders on religious.

  • Result of 19+: The character notes that such an expansion holds no small measure of strategic consolidation as well. House Salva already tightly controls Ordain's fashion industry, and Caberi's plan would fold even more lucrative fields into that empire.

Meeting Before Mixed Media

If the party chooses to meet with Cherish before completing @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.Ib7kciwFbnWEqbRN]{Mixed Media}, she can lend them some insight into the artist she suspects is responsible for the mural.

Cherish’s eyes narrow thoughtfully.

"So, about the mural, I suspected that I knew the artist, so I poked around and it looks an awful lot like Varinna's style. She works in Flotsam upriver, has a little studio there. What's odd, though, is that she's currently under contract to grace several Salva walls with her art."

Don't you have people for this?

Caberi smiles.

Not in the painter’s world, no. Our own agents would stir gossip and draw attention. You, however, are new threads, unnoticed, not yet worked into the grander tapestry of Salva.

Cherish nods in agreement, adding:

The moment Salva starts officially investigating this it'll draw attention, and I'd rather not do that. I've already arranged for the mural to be removed, I don't want more people being attracted to it before it's gone.

What happens if Varinna's guilty?

Cherish, regretful but firm:

Her contracts would be ended at once, of course. She can't expect to bite the hand that feeds her and continue getting fed.

Caberi adds:

"We would likely pursue slander in the Hallows as well, since her artwork could be considered an attack against our good name and interests."

What happens if Varinna's innocent?

Caberi brightens.

Then we ask a better question — who wore her mask? The city is large, but not boundless. We will find the hand holding the brush if we but look hard enough. Or, you will, to be more precise.

Meeting After Mixed Media

If the party chooses to meet with Cherish after completing @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.Ib7kciwFbnWEqbRN]{Mixed Media}, they receive different information as Cherish has pursued her own investigation in the meantime.

Cherish moves to claim a journal off her table, and flips it open to a bookmarked page.

I thought that the mural's art looked familiar, and I couldn't figure out where I'd seen it before. I remembered that we have a couple in-progress murals on Salva properties, and turns out the art style matches! The artist in question is Varinna. Turns out that Varinna is currently on contract with us to grace several Salva properties with her art. It seems unlikely she'd bite the hand that feeds her, though, so I kept digging.


As expected, magic pigments are common in Ordain, for both paints and dyes, but one stands out: Falar. He operates a paint shop in Flotsam as well, quite near Varinna’s place in fact. He would know her style’s bones if he wished to copy them.

Caberi pipes up:

Ah, Falar, Falar, yes, I know that name. If it's who I think it is, he was an adventurer of some renown in his youth. I wonder how he ended up a paint monger in Flotsam...

Cherish looks surprised.

I didn't expect you to know him... but yes, that's all correct. I'm not sure how he ended up a paint seller, but I do think he has reason to hold a grudge: he briefly contracted with Salva some years back, but was fired.

Absolving Varinna

At this point, the party can offer any evidence they have in favor of Varinna.
If they completed [[/eventState localColorCommentary]] (examined Falar's in-progress mural) and [[/eventState localColorArtists]] (studied Varinna's art), they can point out that the styles are similar, but different in key ways.

  • If they [[/eventState localColorMixed metVarinna]] they would know she has a plausible alibi over the last several days, which is why she couldn't have been responsible.

  • If the party [[/eventState localColorMixed confirmedAlibi]] they can confirm it's true, making it unlikely that Varinna is the culprit.

Why was he fired from Salva's mural work?

From what I can tell about the records, we — House Salva, that is — couldn't agree on the murals' content. There aren't any details about what the issue was, specifically, but it seems he brought a case before the Hallows. Of course, it didn't go anywhere.

He took you to the Hallows?

He took Salva to the Hallows, yes.

Cherish checks her notes.

From what I found, he petitioned for reimbursement for time and materials spent on the project, and when House Salva denied him, he took the claim to court, but the case was dismissed by the magister overseeing it.

Caberi, candid, notes:

Salva has some friends in the Hallows. They likely saw to it the case didn't get far.

Isn't that unethical?

Caberi's gaze softens.

The Hallows' job is making sure that Ordain isn't harmed by frivolous or damaging court cases, and the Trading Houses are an integral part of Ordain. Not every quarrel deserves a hearing. If true harm had been done, the Hallows would have heard it, I'm sure.

Characters that succeed on a [[/skill insight 15]] check sense a sincere belief in civic stability buttressing House privilege.

Falar was an adventurer?

Caberi's gaze softens.

"Indeed he was. Briefly famous for a bit in his youth, too, thanks to his work as an adventurer. He was also quite fun to be around, as I recall. There was more than one dreadful gala saved by his clever little illusions. What a pity that he just disappeared into obscurity and didn't do more things of note."

Contracted Work

Once the party has finished talking with Cherish, and are ready to leave, she has a final offer:

Cherish says:

"Before you go, I want to make you an offer to incentivize resolution on this issue. That is to say: I want you to capture the culprit to be handed over to the Hallows, or uncover their identity and provide me some hard proof I can go to the authorities with myself.


You do that, and I'll make sure you're compensated for your time and effort."

How much are you willing to pay?

That depends on how things pan out. If you can find me evidence on who is responsible, or convince them to stop, I'll pay you two-hundred and fifty gold. If you can capture them, or convince them to surrender so they can be brought to justice properly, I'll go as high as five-hundred gold.

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once done speaking with Cherish and Mistress Caberi, the party needs to head to Flotsam. If this was the first stop after Drawing Attention, then they are just starting the investigation, and their next event should be Mixed Media. If they met Cherish after visiting Flotsam for the first time, then they are heading back to confront Falar, and their next event will be A Sketchy Situation.
Outside the Lines.soverview: The party visits Cherish as she requested, so she can reward them for saving her during the paint globlin attack. Mistress Caberi arrives mid-meeting, and depending on whether the party visited her before or after investigating Varinna, they receive different information that can guide their investigation.
Outside the Lines.sexposition:
You arrive at the building where Cherish's office is housed, a small, single-story structure with ample windows and a gleaming white facade. The doorman wears a House Salva pin, and after explaining you are there to meet with Cherish Ellerie, he opens the door and gestures for you to enter.

Once through the doors, you are guided down a long hall lined with doors, each marked with the names of House Salva members, until you finally arrive at Cherish's door. The attendant leaves you there and bids you a good day before heading back to his post.
Outside the Lines.ssummary: We met with Cherish of House Salva in her office, and were rewarded with fine clothing as thanks for saving her. There we met Mistress Caberi, head of Salva and a Shard Goddess, and discussed leads to pursue regarding the divisive mural we found in the city.

A Sketchy Situation.name: A Sketchy Situation
A Sketchy Situation.text:
Overview

In this Combat Event, the party discovers Falar's private studio and realizes (or confirms) that he is actually the artist behind the mural. The party will also do the following:

  • Fight a pack of paint globlins that were set in place to attack anyone that breaks into his studio.

  • Learn more about Falar's past, and the difficulties he suffered that led him to his current state.

  • Discover his next move in the city, and where he plans to carry it out.

Area Walkthrough

The party begins in the "Flotsam Canal Market" scene where the central gameplay of this event transpires. A complete room-by-room description of the market environment and the gameplay that occurs there is detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.jUCq8sac06LvGlT6] walkthrough.

Collecting Evidence

There are three major points of information the party needs to collect to complete their investigation into @UUID[JournalEntry.jUCq8sac06LvGlT6.JournalEntryPage.8DDGWFhzTuBFKy7w]{Falar's Studio} in the Flotsam Canal Market:

  • The party spends time studying the art found in Falar's hidden studio. This should let them conclude that he is trying to copy Varinna's art to frame her.

  • The party acquires either @UUID[Item.xsQ9RHVNs9wJ1ECm] or @UUID[Item.EhupjfsvIapLdTFO] (or both). This is evidence that proves Falar developed a way to lure and capture elementals, including the paint globlins. The notes themselves aren't complete, however, and can't be used by the party in any mechanical way.

  • The party finds @UUID[Item.PwlNz4dMT6MjoCzK]. This item is a direct hint for the party to head to Redwalk Ramble to intercept Falar before he seriously harms someone there. It can also be used as evidence against him later.

[[/outcome copies]]

[[/outcome notes]]

[[/outcome flyer]]

Concluding the Event

Once the party has defeated the paint globlin ambush and finished gathering evidence against Falar, they can move on.

Next Steps

With damning evidence in hand, the party should have enough information to know that Redwalk Ramble is Falar's next target, and their next destination. There, they will trigger @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5]{Matters of Perspective}, and confront Falar directly.
A Sketchy Situation.soverview: The party arrives in Flotsam to investigate Falar, the true culprit behind the slanderous mural and paint globlin attack. They will need to search his shop, uncover the presence of his hidden studio, and find the evidence within that will lead them to their final confrontation with him.
A Sketchy Situation.sexposition: As you step onto the promenade of the canal market in Flotsam, you spy several businesses with colorful signs on either side of you, with more waiting on the lower terraces that descend steadily toward the manmade waterfront below. In the distance you can see wooden walkways snaking between timber structures built over the slow waters of the Destine, some of them multiple stories high and several built out of reclaimed wood that once belonged to river barges and sailing ships.
A Sketchy Situation.ssummary: We uncovered Falar's hidden studio and made several damning discoveries within, including his work to copy Varinna's art style, the development of methods to trap elementals in paint, and his imminent plans to sabotage an art event at Redwalk Ramble.

Matters of Perspective.name: Matters of Perspective
Matters of Perspective.text:
Overview

In this Combat Event, the party moves to intercept @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar} at the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.bfpbRmmyoVF5Ize7]{Redwalk Ramble}, only to find he's already transformed a large section of the park into an illusory death trap almost guaranteed to badly harm anyone that wanders into it. In this Event, the party will:

  • Confront Falar and his elemental minions in combat, including the @UUID[Actor.UJpPT2tvWfGZJfyg]{Paint Globlin} and never before seen @UUID[Actor.hDGMA97hjsiEszDf]{Chiaroscuran Beast}.

  • Decide the fate of Falar by either killing, capturing, or siding with him.

  • Navigate numerous illusory hazards placed on the map by Falar.

Area Walkthrough

The party begins in the "Redwalk Ramble" scene where the central gameplay of this event transpires. A complete description of the park and the gameplay that occurs there is detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.M9s0Phg1hkiTWUJx] walkthrough.

Falar's Fate

Check the appropriate outcome below based on Falar's ultimate fate after the party confronts him in Redwalk Ramble. The outcome will affect the narrative in the following @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.CgidJvms1kxbKBbE] Event. The possible outcomes for Falar are:

  • Falar is killed in the fighting. He won't be able to face formal justice in the courts of the Hallows, but can no longer harm others.

  • Falar is defeated and captured. It is possible to persuade Falar into surrendering himself to the party, though it isn't easy. In either case, he can be turned over to the authorities once captured. This would be Cherish's preferred outcome, based on the meeting the party had with her in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.ooARWZr1voKdluXx]{Outside the Lines}.

  • Falar escapes. This can happen during the encounter with him as part of combat, but could also be a result of the party deciding to let him go because they sympathize with him, or agree with his cause.

Once the party has completed the encounter in Redwalk Ramble, mark the appropriate outcome below based on Falar's fate.

[[/outcome killed]]

Ragen Attunement: Falar Killed

Any character who commits to slaying Falar rather than capturing him advances their [[/attunement emberRagen +1 localColorRedwalkRagen]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome captured]]

Cora Attunement: Falar Captured

Any character who commits to capturing Falar so that he can face justice advances their [[/attunement emberCora +1 localColorRedwalkCora]] at the conclusion of the event.

Primordis Attunement: Falar Convinced

Each character who uses their social skills to force Falar's surrender advances their [[/attunement emberPrimordis +1 localColorRedwalkPrimordis]] at the conclusion of the event.

[[/outcome escaped]]

Aura Attunement: Falar Released

Any character who refuses to pursue Falar and lets him escape advances their [[/attunement emberAura +1 localColorRedwalkAura]] at the conclusion of the event.

Concluding the Event

Milestone Progression

Completing this event earns the party a Milestone Point, potentially advancing them in level. Refer to @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide.JournalEntryPage.jK1PXextPwuJuSnr]{Milestone Progression} section of the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberPlayerGuide]{Player's Guide} for details on how character advancement works in Ember.

Next Steps

Once the party has defeated Falar (or let him escape) and defeated his elemental minions, they can return to @UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]{Cherish's} office in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.0V2KtTURXT8WaxfX]{Gossamer} to trigger @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.CgidJvms1kxbKBbE]{Commissioned Work}, give her an update on what's transpired, and be rewarded for their efforts.
Matters of Perspective.soverview: Pursuit of Falar has led the party to Redwalk Ramble, where they find the old mage has transformed a large swath of the park into a death trap using illusion magic and elementals. If the party hopes to stop Falar, it will be in this moment.
Matters of Perspective.sexposition:
As you arrive in Redwalk Ramble, you are immediately faced with a strange sight: burning lava flowing out of the ground, a mass of wild jungle growing up out of the stone, and swirling stands weaving through a spat of rocky desert dominating the once placid promenade.

These foreign terrains push against your mind and perceptions. On some level, you understand they are unreal, that there is no stretch of burning desert in the center of this park, but you cannot bring yourself to disbelieve, to see past the places where tree and rock seem to become chalk-and-charcoal renderings rather than real wood and stone.

These illusions are unlike any you have seen before, and somewhere at their heart is the source: Falar.
Matters of Perspective.ssummary: We tracked down and dealt with Falar at Redwalk Ramble. His elementals are defeated, and his plan to turn the art walk event into a potentially fatal trap has been foiled. Now we need to report back to Cherish Ellerie on what occurred.

Commissioned Work.name: Commissioned Work
Commissioned Work.text:
Overview

In this Social Event, the party meets with @UUID[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]{Cherish Ellerie} again in her office found in @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrdainGazet.JournalEntryPage.0V2KtTURXT8WaxfX]{Gossamer} to discuss the end result of their work investigating the artist slandering @UUID[JournalEntry.emberOrganizatio.JournalEntryPage.kObm85VeyvnBT2XX]{House Salva}. In this Event, the party can:

  • Implicate Varinna, leaving her to take the blame for the murals and globlin attack if they choose.

  • Report on the outcome of their clash with @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar} in Redwalk Ramble.

  • Get rewarded for their efforts based on what they accomplished during prior events.

@Embed[Actor.fqzXhwQjnOuCAVz1]

Framing Varinna

The party can leave Varinna to take the blame for the murals, and suffer the consequences, even though she is ultimately innocent. To do so, the following criteria must be met:

  • The party never [[/eventState localColorArtists confirmedAlibi]] or [[/eventState localColorArtists investigatedStudio]] in Flotsam during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.Ib7kciwFbnWEqbRN] event.

  • Either the party [[/eventState localColorPerspective killed]] or [[/eventState localColorPerspective escaped]] at Redwalk Ramble during the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.HqScsjz62ZHBzCb5] event.

[[/outcome framed]]

A look of surprise crosses Cherish's face.

I have a hard time believing that Varinna would do anything like this, she seemed like a level-headed and reasonable person. Plus she had an active and quite lucrative contract to produce a mural for House Salva… but, well, without any evidence exonerating her, it looks how it looks.

With a disappointed sigh, Cherish grabs her notebook and scribbles down several new to-do tasks.

I'll go ahead and get her contract terminated, and start the paperwork on a court case against her.

She gestures toward her window with her pencil, eyes rising to you for a moment.

It's a shame, you know? I quite liked her, but Salva can't take this kind of slander lying down. At any rate, thanks for the help. The door attendant has a purse of coin for you, payment for the work. He'll make sure you get it on your way out.

You hear the door open behind you, and a quick glance back reveals a familiar attendant, waiting. He offers a smile and small nod as Cherish offers her farewell:

Stay safe out there, you never know who you can trust these days!

At this point, the party is free to depart and collect payment. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.CgidJvms1kxbKBbE#receiving-payment]{Receiving Payment} for what the party is paid for their work.

Abyss Attunement: Varinna Framed

If the party chooses to implicate Varinna with full knowledge that she was innocent, each character advances their [[/attunement emberAbyss +1 localColorCommissionAbyss]] at the conclusion of the event.

Falar's Fate

As long as the party hasn't [[/eventState localColorCommission framed]] for the murals they can follow up with Cherish on the fate of Falar, getting slightly different results based on how things resolved:

If the party [[/eventState localColorPerspective killed]] at Redwalk Ramble, Cherish responds this way:

It's good you stopped Falar before he could unleash his illusions on the public. I can't imagine how bad it would have been if people turned up to the art ramble set up as it was. Folks would have died, and that blood would have been on Salva's hands, at least partially.

She pauses a moment as a thought occurs to her, which is followed by Cherish picking up her notebook to quickly jot down a note for herself. As she writes, she mumbles aloud:

I'm going to have to make sure future events have better security...

Clapping the notebook shut she looks at you.

Anyhow, thank you! The doorman will have your payment for services rendered when you head out. It was good working with you, but I hope the next time we cross paths it will involve a little less violence.

You hear the door open behind you, and a quick glance that way reveals the attendant, waiting. He offers a smile and small nod. Cherish adds:

Take care out there, Ordain's a big, crazy place!

If the party [[/eventState localColorPerspective captured]] at Redwalk Ramble, Cherish says:

Cherish seems relieved, as though a burden was lifted from her shoulders.

I'm glad that you managed to bring him to justice without killing him. He deserves to face the full fury of the Hallows for his actions. Not only was he slandering the good names and images of House Salva, he could have gotten people killed.

She looks out the window at the Ordain skyline for a moment, and muses.

I wouldn't be surprised if they put him in Spellbreaker Tower and never let him out again. If he's lucky, maybe they'll let him have some painting supplies.

She turns and looks back to you.

Anyhow, when you head out, the doorman will have your payment for services rendered. It was a pleasure working with you, and I hope we meet again under more pleasant circumstances!

Behind you the door opens, and a quick glance that way reveals the attendant waiting. He offers a silent nod and smile.

If [[/eventState localColorPerspective escaped]] from Redwalk Ramble, Cherish states:

Cherish lets out a faintly exasperated sigh, then sweeps her hair back over her shoulder.

I'm surprised he managed to elude you! Though if he was as potent an illusionist as Mistress Caberi indicated, perhaps giving you the slip and vanishing into the city would actually be pretty trivial for him.

Still, it leaves me uneasy, with too many unanswered questions: Is he going to keep creating dangerous trap murals? Will he plan another sabotage at a House Salva event?

Hopefully not, but I'm sure the Veiled Chain are looking for him, and nobody can hide from them for long.

She waves her hands, banishing the thoughts and topic, moving on:

Anyhow, I'm sure you did your best. I'll make sure you get paid for your work up to this point. Thank you for trying at least. If Falar pops up again, I'll be sure to reach out. Maybe we'll have a second chance at getting him...

Take care out there, and watch your backs!

Behind you the door opens, and the attendant steps into view, giving you a short nod and smile as he begins waiting for you to make your exit.

At this point, the party is free to depart and collect payment. See @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.CgidJvms1kxbKBbE#receiving-payment]{Receiving Payment} for what the party is paid for their work.

Receiving Payment

As you exit the building onto the street once more, the doorman offers you a small wooden box sealed with a ribbon. It bears the House Salva crest and is particularly heavy for its size. A small note attached to it says:

Payment for valuable services rendered to House Salva.

Inside the box is an amount of gold based on the party's performance in the quest:

  • If the party [[/eventState localColorCommission framed]] or [[/eventState localColorPerspective escaped]] or they [[/eventState localColorPerspective killed]] they receive a [[/award 250gp]].

  • If the party [[/eventState localColorPerspective captured]] they receive a [[/award 500gp]].

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

With the completion of this quest, the party's interaction with Cherish and House Salva is complete for now.
Commissioned Work.soverview: With Falar dealt with, the party returns to Cherish's office in Gossamer to update her on the situation, conclude their business with her, and receive compensation for their time and effort assisting House Salva in protecting its good name.
Commissioned Work.sexposition:
A familiar attendant lets you into the Salva building, guiding you toward Cherish's door. He knocks three times, then opens the door, ushering you inward. Cherish is already moving toward you as you enter her office. With a bright smile, she greets you.

Hello, hello, welcome back!

Then, a moment later, she nods to the attendant, who closes the door, granting you privacy. Cherish's eyes shift back your way.

So, how has the investigation been going? What've you been up to? What've you discovered?
Commissioned Work.ssummary: We returned to Cherish Ellerie's office in Gossamer to deliver our final update on the investigation into the mural slandering House Salva, and the party involved in its creation. We were rewarded for our efforts and have concluded our business with the Trading House.

Color Commentary.name: Color Commentary
Color Commentary.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

In this Social Event, the party encounters one of several murals created to critique aspects of the city, its leadership, and current events. The party will have a chance to examine the mural briefly before moving on.

The mural "Work in Progress" is unique, and should be used after the party completes Outside the Lines and Mixed Media. All other murals can appear at any time.

This event becomes substantially more likely to occur after the [[/eventState localColorFashion cherishSecond]] outcome in the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberLocalColor0.JournalEntryPage.ooARWZr1voKdluXx]{Outside the Lines} event. Once [[/eventState localColorPerspective]] is completed, this event becomes progressively less likely with each passing day.

The Work in Progress

This mural should appear once the party has completed [[/eventState localColorArtists]] and [[/eventState localColorPerspective]]. It should take precedence over any other murals if the criteria for it appearing are met.

You round a corner and find a figure in the midst of painting a mural. The artist is startled, and in the natural moment of awkwardness you realize the person before you is none other than Falar. It takes only a breath for him to recognize you in turn, and a look of concern flashes in his eyes as he does.

He drops his paint and brush and begins running. You can hear him saying something as he breaks around a corner, but the words are unintelligible.

@Embed[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]

Illusory Chase

As @UUID[Actor.rOAkdqKDnEYnAKih]{Falar} begins his flight, he casts Silent Image to create a false copy of himself in an alley nearby as a distraction, then takes a different route, leaving the decoy to draw attention.

It is intended that the party won't be able to catch Falar in this event.

Chasing Falar

Any character with a [[/skill perception 12 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill perception 10]] check can pursue Falar to the end of an alley, trying to get a door open.

Characters that approach Falar in the alley should be given the following description:

As you approach Falar, he begins pacing in a circle, panic setting into his posture before glancing your way and then turning to a closed door, which he tries to open.

As you draw closer, you watch Falar fully panic, throwing himself against the door, trying to get it to budge. This is the moment you realize the truth: There's no sound or weight to his actions, he isn't looking at you, but simply in your direction, and after a moment his actions begin to repeat.

This is an illusion, and Falar's gotten away.

[[/outcome workProgress]]

Tracking Falar

Searching the area reveals a few spots of glimmering paint leading off in the opposite direction of the illusion and the mural, but they quickly stop, making all attempts to track him in the city impossible.

Predicting Falar

Any character with a [[/skill insight 16 passive format=long]] or who succeeds on a [[/skill insight 14]] check deduces that Falar will head somewhere familiar and safe. While they don't know where he lives, they do know where his paint shop is. Searching his shop in Flotsam could yield insights or provide clues into what he's doing.

  • Characters with [[/knowledge crime]] or [[/knowledge intrigue]] succeed on this check automatically.

Any character who examines the glimmering paint specks and succeeds on a [[/skill arcana 12]] check suspects that searching Falar's paint shop could lead to the discovery of components necessary to create Paint Globlins.

With Falar in the wind, the party can return to the mural to inspect it if they like.

Inspecting the Mural

The mural is only vague shapes, and has no clear image to it yet. However, the wet paint gleams brightly with latent magic.

A character that inspects the paint jars and makes a successful [[/skill investigation 14]] check notices that the containers are identical to those Falar sells in his shop, but they are labeled differently, clearly not intended for sale.

A character that makes a successful [[/skill arcana 14]] check while examining the paint notices that the jars themselves are carved with various abjuration symbols meant to contain the magic in the paint.

The Veiled Chain's Eyes

The street here is painted with shadowy figures, with bright eyes arranged in such a way that they seem to follow you as you move past the mural. Upon closer inspection, each figure bears the symbol of the Veiled Chain.

[[/outcome chainEye]]

The Burnished Left Hand

This brutal mural depicts a Burnished Hand warrior with their armored foot on the chest of a prone monster, axe raised to behead it. The creature snarls and lashes out with wicked claws, but can do nothing pinned as it is.

The art is done in mottled grays and whites, like an ancient statue, while in the foreground, in full color, a Burnished Hand warrior mimics the motion. Yet, it is an Ordani citizen he has pinned underfoot, and their expression is one of panic as they hold their arms up to shield themselves from the coming blow.

[[/outcome burnishedHand]]

The House of Criminals

A series of wanted posters are painted on the wall here, each one depicting a figure wanted for theft, extortion, racketeering, or worse. Beside the posters the wanted figures stand, each one clad in Wandren uniform, and amicably chatting with figures wearing badges of the Hallows and Veiled Chain.

[[/outcome houseCriminals]]

The Temple Fortress

This mural depicts the Cindarin Temple of Ordain as a fortress, with jagged barricades and spear walls of Cindaric Sages in crimson and gold armor, keeping hordes of Ordani from approaching. The crowds are not depicted as aggressive, but as destitute masses desperately trying to gain access to the grand temple.

[[/outcome templeFortress]]

The Unwanted Stranger

This mural depicts a group of Arcturian refugees, each one thin, haggard, and desperate in their look. They are huddled together and shielding themselves with bare arms as rocks rain down on them. The mural is situated so that the rocks have come from various windows on the building, as though the occupants themselves have cast the stones. Some of the refugees are already wounded, others lie on the ground, perhaps dead or nearly so.

[[/outcome unwantedStranger]]

The Endless Mines

This mural depicts the mouth of a mine surrounded by a crowd of mine workers, half of them injured in some way or another. A stream of bloody and battered miners are shown trudging out of the entrance, some carrying the limp bodies of other workers with them. For each miner leaving, a new figure is depicted marching inward to replace them.

[[/outcome endlessMines]]

The Warmonger's Word

The mural depicts a pair of faceless figures shaking hands and exchanging a bag overflowing with coin. One is dressed as an Ordani, in pale, flowing robes, and the other clad in the black and red uniform of the Tayan Empire. The Ordani's hands are stained by blood from the pouch of money, and a bloody dagger peeks out of the Tayan's sleeve.

[[/outcome warmongerWord]]

The Hardened Heart

This large mural depicts a crowd of Arcturian refugees huddled together around the feet of three Cindaric sages, the crowd looks up to them, some raising hands in begging gestures. The first sage is rotund in body, holding food and drink in either hand, partaking in both merrily. The second wraps a bandage around her hand as a single droplet of blood beads on a cut fingertip. Lastly, the third sage tacks a no vacancy sign up on the wall, his back turned on the crowd at his feet.

[[/outcome hardenedHeart]]

Concluding the Event

Next Steps

Once the party has finished viewing the mural, they can continue on toward their intended destination.

Chasing Falar

If the party got the Work In Progress mural, they should know to head to Flotsam to pursue Falar in [[/eventState localColorSketchy]].
Color Commentary.soverview: A rebellious artist has painted several murals throughout Ordain: pieces of social critique aimed at the powerful and influential. This is a repeatable event that occurs whenever the party discovers such a mural.
Color Commentary.sexposition: You spot a splash of color and bold lines of dark paint that contrast against the pale walls of Ordain. Moving to get a better view of it, you see a mural taking up the side of a building and depicting life in Ordain in a way you've rarely seen before.
Color Commentary.ssummary: While traveling through Ordain, we came across an interesting mural.

Voices in the Square.name: Voices in the Square
Voices in the Square.text:
Gamemaster's Summary

This repeatable Social Event can occur while traveling through Speaker's Square in the Hallows. In this Event, the party can:

  • Witness an Ordani citizen publicly air a grievance that reflects class tensions within Ordain.

  • Ask them questions after their speech to gain additional insight.

Randomization Steps

To run this Standalone Event, follow these steps:

  1. Roll on (or choose from) the @UUID[JournalEntry.emberEventsCh300.JournalEntryPage.HP2pJLrWrktw9HJg#ordain-rumors-table]{Ordain Rumors} table.

  2. Follow the entry's embedded link to the appropriate section.

  3. Read or paraphrase that section's read-aloud text, then allow the party to ask the speaker questions.

@Embed[RollTable.XongzPrSbaj6dMFd inline rollable]

Grievance: Quarry Run Justice

An older woman stands before the crowd, flanked by a few grim-faced relatives and neighbors. As she begins to speak, her voice breaks; someone gives her arm a reassuring squeeze. When she begins again, her voice carries clean over the din, more powerful than her slight frame would suggest.

"My son died in the Stonehollow Quake, along with over a hundred others in Quarry Run. They died because House Cevher wanted more from us — they died so House Cevher could fill its coffers.
